The peculiar Kāshmīrī modified a, represented in the Nāgarī character by and in the Persian character by zabar. Thus, اَدَرُن, ạdᵃrun, to be moist. The sound of this letter, which is not uncommon, has nothing corresponding to it in English. It is something between the ordinary a and the ŏ in 'hot', but is exactly equivalent to neither. ¶ This ạ usually arises from the influence of a following ᵃ. Thus, chuh kalān, he is dumb, but chuh kạlᵃrāwān, he makes dumb.

This letter represents the sound which a takes when it is followed by ⁱ. It is represented in the Nāgarī character by, and in the Persian character by zabar. Thus, اَسِ, ȧsⁱ, we. The sound of this letter is that of a short ai. Thus ȧsⁱ sounds something like aⁱsⁱ.

This is the usual short a of Hindī and other Indian languages, sounded like the a in 'America'. It is represented by in Nāgarī, and by zabar in the Persian character. When followed by ᵃ it becomes ạ. when followed by ⁱ it becomes ȧ, when followed by ᵘ it becomes o, and when followed by ᵘ̈ it becomes ü. ¶ When ya is initial or follows a vowel it becomes yĕ, and when it immediately follows another consonant it becomes ĕ, and so also does a when it follows ñ or sh. Thus, yĕmis, not yamis, biyĕ, not biya, while pōthya, books, becomes pōthĕ, myāña, mine (fem. plur.), becomes myāñĕ, and nisha, near, becomes nishĕ. Similarly, also sometimes after c, ch, and j, as explained under the article ĕ. ¶ Similarly, when wa immediately follows another consonant it becomes ŏ. Thus, dwad, milk, becomes dŏd. ¶ The vowel a at the end of a word is always pronounced as ᵃ; but, the rule being universal, it is not customary to indicate the fact in writing. ¶ In monosyllabic words ending in an aspirated consonant a has the sound of the a in 'hat', as in krakh, a noise.

An interjectional suffix used by a woman when addressing a man or woman who is a familiar or a junior. Thus, hatabā kāk-a, O father (familiarly), hatau Gana (for Gana + a), O Gana. When a woman addresses a man or a woman by his or her proper name we may use -a bāyĕ or -a bāyau. Thus, hatabā Mahādēv-a bāyĕ, hatabā Mahādēv-a bayau, or hatau Mahādēv-a bāyau, O Mahādēv. This cannot be used with words which are not proper names. We cannot say hatabā kāk-a bāyĕ, O father.

for ā 1 see a 3. This is the ordinary ā of other Indian languages, and has the sound of a in 'father'. It is represented in Nāgarī by and in the Persian character by alif. Thus, کاتھھ, kāṭh, wood. This is a very unstable letter. When followed by i or ī it often becomes ö, and when followed by u it often becomes ô. Thus, mālis, to a father, becomes mölis; the Arabic qā'im becomes köim, established; tayārī becomes tayörī, readiness, and ṭhākur becomes ṭhôkur, an idol. Before the mātrā-vowels similar changes occur. Thus, before ᵃ, ⁱ, ᵒ, or ᵘ̈ it becomes ö, as in köñᵃrāwān, to make one-eyed (from kānun, to have one eye); mölⁱ (base māl-), fathers; abögᵒrᵒ, not divided (from bāg, division); brörᵘ̈ (base brār-), a cat; and before ᵘ it becomes ô, as in myônᵘ (base myān-), my. Sometimes the ā becomes ö, even when no i or u follows, as in pönʦ, five; ös, a face.

Three forms of a suffix added to verbs, after the pronominal suffixes, if any, and giving an interrogative force. Before them the kh of a pronominal suffix does not become h, as it does before another pronominal suffix, but a final h is dropped, i, ⁱ, or ĕ becomes y, and a final u (but not ᵘ or ᵘ̈) becomes w, even when originally followed by such a dropped h. Thus, sapadi + ā becomes sapadyā, will he become? sapȧdⁱ + ā becomes sapadyā, did they (masc.) become? bŏvĕ + ā becomes bŏvyā, did they (fem.) become? chĕh + ā becomes chyā, is she? and chuh + ā becomes chwā, is he?; but korᵘ + ā becomes korᵘā, pronounced korā, was he made? and kürᵘ̈ + ā becomes kürᵘ̈ā, pronounced kürā, was she made? After a final a the termination and the suffix (with the exception noted below) together become ā; thus, kara + a becomes karā, shall I make? ¶ The rules for the use of these suffixes are somewhat complicated and are not always strictly followed. The following is the most usual custom:-- ¶ In the first person, or when immediately following a suffix of the first person, a is employed with the singular and ā with the plural. Thus, chus-a, am I (masc.)? chĕs-a, am I (fem.)? chu-m-a, is there to me? chyā (chih + ā or chĕh + ā), are we (masc. and fem.)? ¶ In the second person singular and plural, or when immediately following a pronominal suffix of the second person, the usual form employed is a. Thus, chukh-a, art thou (masc.)? chĕkh-a, art thou (fem.)? chu-y-a (pronounced chuyĕ, see ĕ), is there to thee? In the plural, contrary to the rule just stated about final a, the final a of the termination is elided, so that we have chiw-a for chiwa + a, are you (masc.)? chĕw-a, are you (fem.)? The suffix ā can also be used with the second person, but is not polite. ¶ In the third person ā is alone employed. Thus, chwā (chuh + ā), is he? chyā (chĕh + ā), is she? or (chih + ā), are they (masc.)? or (chĕh + ā), are they (fem.)? Occasionally we find a used with the feminine, as in sapüzᵘ̈a, did she become? ¶ In the feminine it is usual to substitute ay (or, after a vowel, y) for a or ā if a woman is addressed. Thus, karān chĕs-ay, am I making? (a woman is addressing a woman). If she were addressing a man she would say karān chĕs-a. Similarly, karān chy-ĕy (for karān chĕh + ay), do we make? if a woman is addressing a woman, but karān chy-ā if a man is addressed. In the second person a may be substituted for ay, so that we have karān chĕkh-ay, or karān chĕkh-a, art thou making? (in which either a man or a woman is addressing a woman). Similarly, in the second person plural we have karān chĕwa-y or karān chĕw-a, are you (fem.) making? For the third person we have karān chy-ĕy (karān chĕh + ay), is she making, or are they (fem.) making? (a man or a woman is addressing a woman). ¶ Similar negative interrogatives are nā and nay.

m. (sg. dat. acyutas), a N. of Vishnu (Viṣṇu) (Śiv. 1437).

m. a half; often signifying a portion, not exactly a half, and hence (in compounds) incomplete, imperfect; with the suff. āh of the indefinite article, aḍāh, a half (cf. K.Pr. 103). -aḍ 1 m.sg. halves, equal parts (u. w. vbs. of making, dividing, etc.). -aḍ 2 adv. half-and-half, in halves. -buḍa adj. c.g. nearly old, getting on in years (of animate creatures). -dọ̆bᵃri adv. half-hidden (of treasure buried in the ground). -digar m. the time of sunset, sunset (K.Pr. 177). -dū̃ʦhari adv. half sorted out (of a collection of things); half carded (of cotton, wool, etc.). -han f. dim. of aḍ, a little half, the half of a small quantity, or about half (K.Pr. 153). -khôrᵘ 1 adj. (fem. -khörᵘ̈), weighing half a khār or kharwār (about 48 seers). -khôrᵘ 2 adj. (f. -khörᵘ̈), half raised; hence very powerless, very weak (naturally or by disease), very puny. -khūrᵘ adj. (-khūrᵘ̈), half or imperfectly afraid; hence timid. -khashĕ adv. half-slaughtered, half-executed; hence at the point of death (of a criminal under execution). -khĕw adj. c.g. having emaciated limbs; wanting a limb, maimed (by accident) or having lost a limb through disease or from birth. Lit. half-devoured. -kôjᵘ m. a certain time; half-way to the morning meal, about 2 1/4 hours after sunrise (K.Pr. 176). -lāburᵘ adj. (f. -lābürᵘ̈), half sloping; hence moderately uneven, up and down. Cf. aḍa-lāburᵘ below. -mahanyuvᵘ m. half a man (of a man whose body is lean from illness or undeveloped, or of a woman who exhibits the qualities or virtues of a man). -mŏla adv. at half price. -mŏñjĕ adv. at a reduced price, very cheaply. -nañĕr m. half-light (as of an obscured sun or moon); the half-telling of a secret. -rāth m. and f. (sg. dat. m. -rātan, f. -röʦᵘ̈), m. half a night; f. midnight (cf. K.Pr. 176). Cf. ajĕ röʦᵘ̈ under oḍᵘ. -rātan adv. at midnight. -rātan-bögⁱ or -rātan-bögin adv. at about midnight. -rātas adv. at midnight. -rātas-bögⁱ or -rātas-bögin adv. at about midnight. -shĕholᵘ m. (in the hot season) the cool of the afternoon, when the shadows are lengthening and a breeze springs up. Cf. aḍa-shĕholᵘ below. -shĕhalĕn adv. in the cool of the afternoon. -shĕhalĕn-bögⁱ or -shĕhalĕn-bögin adv. about the time of the cool of the afternoon. -sôrᵘ adj. (f. -sörᵘ̈), half collected (of things gradually brought from one place and deposited in another). Cf. aḍa-sôrᵘ below. -sārĕ-maḍ-sārĕ f.pl. a collection of things purchased (such as fish, etc.), each of which is not very large or very small, averaging about half a seer. -ʦāri adv. merely in a half-cooked condition. -wara adj. c.g. half-old, oldish, middle-aged (of human beings). ¶ aḍa-ômᵘ adj. (f. -ömᵘ̈), half-raw, half-cooked (usually of fruit cakes and the like). -brokᵘ adj. (f. -brücᵘ̈), half-disintegrated, of tough food in the process of chewing or of things being ground on a stone or pounded in a mortar. In women's abuse also applied to another woman. -buzᵘ adj. (f. -buzᵘ̈), half-roasted or half-parched, imperfectly roasted or parched. -chônᵘ adj. (f. -chöñᵘ̈), half or imperfectly sifted (of meal, flour, etc.). -chotᵘ adj. (f. -chüʦᵘ̈), half-white, white here and there, partly white (e.g. a cow); of a dirty-white colour, not of a pure white. -chôvᵘ 1 adj. (f. -chövᵘ̈), half-cooked, imperfectly cooked. -chôvᵘ 2 adj. (f. -chövᵘ̈), half-used, of something lost or spoilt before it is used up or worn out. -cyūrᵘ adj. (f. -cīrᵘ̈), half or improperly squeezed, not properly wrung out (as wet clothes); not thoroughly split (as a beam of wood, by a saw). -dodᵘ adj. (f. -düzᵘ̈), half-burnt, not entirely consumed; half-burnt, burnt only in parts. -dŏdorᵘ adj. (f. -dŏdürᵘ̈), half-decayed; half-worm-eaten. -dogᵘ adj. (f. -düjᵘ̈ 1), half or imperfectly pounded on a stone or in a mortar (of grain and the like). -ḍokhᵘ adj. (f. -ḍüchᵘ̈), having half or an imperfect support (of some article which would over-balance without a support or which is on an uneven surface); something which is not securely resting against another firm object. -dolᵘ adj. (f. -düjᵘ̈ 2), half or imperfectly crushed or husked (of grain in a mortar); (in carpentry, of a board) imperfectly smoothed down by working with an adze or the like. -ḍongᵘ m. ground which is not perfectly level, and on which it is hence not safe to deposit anything round, or that over-balances easily. -ḍyū̃gᵘ adj. (f. -ḍī˜jᵘ̈), insecure (commonly of an unsteady base or support). -ḍyolᵘ adj. (f. -ḍë˘jᵘ̈), half loose, not properly steady (of something requiring a support); not properly bound (of a parcel or of a book, etc.). -ḍyongᵘ adj. (f. -ḍë˘njᵘ̈), not securely based, resting insecurely on its base, or resting on an insecure or unsteady basis or foundation. -gᵒhᵒ adj. (f. -gᵘ̈shᵘ̈), imperfectly ground, not in a fine powder (of sandal-wood, kuṅkuma, and the like); imperfectly polished or worn smooth. -gorᵘ adj. (f. -gürᵘ̈), half-made, imperfectly made, badly put together (e.g. a wooden or copper vessel, a pillar, or an ornament). -gosᵘ adj. (f. -güsᵘ̈), not smoothly polished. -gashĕl adj. c.g. half-melted, half-worn (of the impression on a coin or the like). -họ̆khᵘ adj. (f. -hö̆chᵘ̈), half-dry (of fruit, etc., under the sun, or of a lake, river, etc.). -holᵘ adj. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), slightly crooked (either of a thing or of a man's nature). -họ̆tᵘ adj. (f. -hö̆ʦᵘ̈), half-decayed, tainted, 'high' (of cooked food, fruit, etc.). -kāchurᵘ adj. (f. -kāchirᵘ̈), half or imperfectly husked (of grain in a mortar, etc.). -khām adj. c.g. half-raw, imperfectly cooked. -kolᵘ adj. (f. -küjᵘ̈), imperfectly speaking, not speaking clearly, mumbling with the mouth half opened. -kāñĕl adj. c.g. half lying on one side, almost confined to bed, feeble, weak. -kôrᵘ adj. (f. -körᵘ̈), half or imperfectly boiled (of milk, ghī, melted butter, etc.). -kôsᵘ adj. (f. -kösᵘ̈), half or imperfectly shaved; shaved on one side and not on the other. -köshurᵘ adj. (f. -köshirᵘ̈), half Kāshmīrī (born in Kāshmīr and brought up elsewhere); of articles, made elsewhere of Kāshmīrī stuff; of language, Kāshmīrī mixed with foreign expressions; of cloth, etc., made partly of Kāshmīrī thread. -kāyurᵘ or -kāyirᵘ adj. (f. -kāyirᵘ̈), half a pine-tree. The wood of this tree is very soft and easy to pierce; hence, weak, powerless, unresisting. -lāburᵘ adj. (f. -lābürᵘ̈), half-rising, (of uneven ground) elevated here and depressed there. Cf. aḍ-lāburᵘ above. -lĕdorᵘ adj. (f. -lĕdürᵘ̈), slightly yellow (of the complexion); partly yellow, yellow in one place and not in another. -lyokᵘ adj. (f. -lë̆cᵘ̈), incomplete, imperfect, not completed (Gr.Gr. 162). -lë̆cᵘ̈ kömᵘ̈ f. a work which is left incomplete. -mani half a maund of anything, hence a large quantity, a lot, as in K.Pr. 169. -moṇḍᵘ 1 adj. (f. -müṇḍᵘ̈), half gruel-water; any grain boiled in water, from which the water and scum are not poured off, the whole being served together. -moṇḍᵘ bata m. boiled rice so served, in a soft slimy state. -moṇḍᵘ 2 adj. (f. -muṇḍᵘ̈), not properly rubbed (of woollen clothes in the wash). -môrᵘ adj. (f. -mörᵘ̈), half-killed, half-dead. -mūrᵘ adj. (f. -mūrᵘ̈), half-husked (of grain, etc.), half-shelled (of peas, etc.). -nyūlᵘ adj. (f. -nījᵘ̈), half blue or green; (of grass, etc.) not thoroughly dried. -pholᵘ adj. (f. -phüjᵘ̈), half worn out, neither entirely new nor too old for wear (generally of clothes). -phọ̆lᵘ adj. (f. -phö̆jᵘ̈), half-expanded (of flowers); half-blown; half-opened in the morning (of flowers that close at night and open in the day). -phoṭᵘ adj. (f. -phüṭᵘ̈), half-split (of wood); incompletely sprung from the earth (of a seedling); half-expanded (of rice, etc., being boiled); not completely plunged in water, etc.; not having reached full age, before one's time (of a man, tree, etc., dying or the like). -phyôrᵘ adj. (f. -phyörᵘ̈), half-strained; that from which the cooking water has not been thoroughly strained (of grain, vegetables, etc.); unstrained generally. -pạjᵒrᵒ adj. (f. -pạjᵘ̈rᵘ̈), half hemmed and felled; (of clothes) hemmed together, but not finally felled. -pôkᵘ adj. (f. -pöcᵘ̈), incompletely cooked. -popᵘ adj. (f. -püpᵘ̈), half-ripe (of fruit, grain, etc.). -pronᵘ adj. (f. -prüñᵘ̈), imperfectly white (e.g. dirty clothes), imperfectly clear (e.g. water). -prônᵘ adj. (f. -pröñᵘ̈), half-old, neither new (or young) nor old. -shĕholᵘ adj. (f. -shĕhᵘ̈jᵘ̈), half-cooled (of something tangible that has been hot). Cf. aḍ-shĕholᵘ above. -shūrᵘ adj. (f. -shīrᵘ̈), half or imperfectly repaired. -sôrᵘ adj. (f. -sörᵘ̈), half-collected, not properly collected (usually of harvest bundles not properly stacked); half-felt, half-touched. Cf. aḍ-sôrᵘ above. -sūrᵘ adj. (pl. dat. -sōrĕn, f. sg. nom. -sūrᵘ̈, dat. -sōrĕ), nearly spent, nearly exhausted, nearly used up. -sôvᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), (of a living creature) half caused to lie down, half put to sleep; (of a post or the like) half thrown down on the ground. -syonᵘ adj. (f. -së̆ñᵘ̈), half-softened, half tender (of vegetables, etc., in cooking); insufficiently salted or spiced (of the same). -syonᵘ maḍa-syonᵘ adj. (f. -së̆ñᵘ̈ maḍa-së˘ñᵘ̈), the same. -syuvᵘ adj. (f. -sivᵘ̈), (in cooking) half or imperfectly boiled or stewed; (of birds, monkeys, or the like) half-domesticated, half-tamed. -tholᵘ adj. (f. -thüjᵘ̈), having branches half or imperfectly trimmed (of trees, creepers, etc.). -trukᵘ adj. (f. -trucᵘ̈), half-gnawed, half-chewed (of food, or of damage done by mice, etc.). -trọ̆shᵘ adj. (f. -trö̆shᵘ̈), half-hard, hence (of parched grain) requiring chewing but eatable; (of climbing plants and the like) partly dry, partly withered. -tôwᵘ adj. (f. -tövᵘ̈), half or imperfectly heated (either in the sun or by fire), of grain or of metal vessels, etc. -ʦomᵘ adj. (f. -ʦümᵘ̈), half-dry, withered but not quite dry (of something which was once green and fresh). -ʦôpᵘ adj. (f. -ʦörᵘ̈), half-selected, hence not properly sorted, imperfectly sifted (of grain and the like). -ʦôshᵘ adj. (f. -ʦöshᵘ̈), half or partly astringent in taste; half bitter-salt (as sea-water). -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), half-cut, hence (of a human being, tree, etc.) living only half his or its time, cut off before his time, dying in the prime of life. -ʦyūṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦīṭᵘ), half or imperfectly pounded to powder (in a mortar or the like). -wahôrᵘ adj. (f. -wahörᵘ̈), half or imperfectly spread out (as clothes, straw, etc., to be dried in the sun). -wūnᵘ adj. (f. -wūñᵘ̈), half, imperfectly, or badly woven. -vĕñorᵘ adj. (f. -vĕñürᵘ̈), half or imperfectly separated (especially of grass or vegetables from the husk or shell). -wushonᵘ adj. (f. -wushüñᵘ̈), half-warm, lukewarm (either by nature or from the application of heat). -wothᵘ adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), half-open (of a door, etc.). -wuṭhᵘ adj. (f. -wuṭhᵘ̈), half or imperfectly twisted (of ropes, etc.). -vĕʦhonᵘ adj. (f. -vĕʦhüñᵘ̈), half-separated; (of cotton) half or imperfectly teased out; (of literary compositions) half corrected or half explained. -wŏzolᵘ adj. (f. -wŏzüjᵘ̈), half red, light red; partly red, red in parts. -zāmotᵘ adj. (f. -zāmüʦᵘ̈), (of seeds, etc.) half-sprouted, imperfectly sprouted. -zumotᵘ adj. (f. -zumüʦᵘ̈), half worn out; (of animate beings) thin, lean; (of plants) half-dry, half-withered; (of creepers) half-dry, easily broken, flaccid; (of clothes, etc.) worn thin, easily torn. -zôvᵘ adj. (f. -zövᵘ̈), half-born; (of plants) half or improperly sprouted; (of milk) not properly or entirely curdled; (of a portable brazier or kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈) not showing signs of fire, half-lighted.

adv. then, thereafter, thereupon, therefore (both of time and of causality). Very common with interrogatives, in which case its use closely resembles that of the Hindī tō, as in the following. -kōr adv. then where? then in what direction? as if we were to say, "if it's not there, then where is it?" i.e. "it's nowhere". -kōr-kun, the same as ada-kōr. -kōra-kani adv. then whence? -kus m.an. (f.an. -kŏssa, inan. -kyāh), adj. pron. then who? then what? hence, then there is no one, or nothing; (inanimate) what else, of course. -kus-sanā, the same as ada-kus. -kus ta ada-kas, then who, and then to whom? i.e. there is no one (to give), and therefore no one to whom to give (or no one need expect anything). -kati, or -kati-sanā adv. then where? (used after a verb signifying 'to put', etc.). -kotᵘ, or -kotᵘ-kun adv. then where? then in what direction? -kūtᵘ (f. -kǖʦᵘ̈), or -kūtᵘ-sanā adj. then how much? -kǖtⁱ m.pl. (f. -kṻʦa or -kaiʦa), or -kǖtⁱ-sanā, then how many? -kĕtha, or -kĕtha-sanā, or -kĕtha-pöṭhⁱ, or -kĕtha-pöṭhⁱ-sanā adv. then how? then in what manner? -kōtāh (f. -kaiʦāh), or -kōtāh-sanā adj. then how much? -kaityāh (f. -kaiʦāh), or -kaityāh-sanā adj. then how many? -kǖtyunᵘ  (f. -kǖtiñᵘ̈), or -kǖtyunᵘ-sanā adj. then consisting of how many? then of what price? -kawa, or -kawa-sanā, or -kawa-kani, or -kawa-kani-sanā adv. then for what reason? then why? -kyāh-ō adv. then what, sir? i.e. here it is, do you want anything else? what else? of course. -kyuthᵘ (f. -kiʦhᵘ̈), or -kyuthᵘ-sanā adj. then of what kind? ¶ ada is also frequently employed with verbs expressing propriety or necessity, and is then equivalent to the Hindī tō. Thus, ada goʦhᵘ totᵘ gaʦhunᵘ, then it is proper to go there, in that case you should go there. --lagi tati bihunᵘ --, then (in that case) it is proper to settle there. --pazi tati dapunᵘ --, then (in that case) it is proper to tell (it) there. ¶ ada combined with vocative particles often expresses simply 'yes', and with an interrogative adverb simply 'no', in the sense of agreeing or refusing to do something that one has been asked to do. Thus, adā (ada + a) adv. yes (addressed to an inferior). adō (ada + ō) adv. yes, that's right (addressed to an inferior who is at a distance). ada-bā adv. yes (in addressing a male of equal rank). -biñᵘ̈ adv. good, yes (in addressing a female of equal rank). -kaṭi adv. then where? hence, in the sense of a negative, 'no.' -sö adv. good; yes, sir (respectfully addressed to a male). -kyā adv. good, yes (addressed to a person present), of course. -kyā-bā adv. good, yes (addressed by a woman to a man, or by a man to an equal). -kyā-biñᵘ̈ adv. good, yes (addressed by a man to a woman of equal rank). -kyā-sö adv. good, yes (used respectfully by a man). aday adv. good; yes (used in answer to an inferior or younger woman).
f. completion, fulfilment. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go to completion, to be completed, (of a space of time) to elapse (H. x, 8; xii, 4, 9, 11, 12).

(for aḍa 1 see aḍ), f.pl. bones, especially those of the forearm and of the shin. -sūr m. bone-ashes; a severe beating, which (metaphorically) reduces the bones to powder. -trakorᵘ adj. (f. -trakürᵘ̈), having hard or strong bones (especially those of the forearm and shin); (of a woman) one whose forearm or shin-bones are so hard that they do not easily allow bracelets, etc., to be put upon them.
f. (sg. abl. adālüʦᵘ̈), justice, the decision in a law case; a court of justice (the building).
m. one who presides in a court of justice; a judge.

adal-wadal, or adal-ta-wadal m. exchange, interchange, substitution; as adj. c.g., confused, of a contrary disposition, K.Pr. 2, 102. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to exchange. --wanun -- m.inf. to make an incorrect statement in conversation; to give incorrect instruction.
f. abusive language, attacking abusively. See also adal-badal.

m. Adam, the first man (H. iv, 2, 3; vii, 6, 7). Hence ādamī (= آدمی) or ādȧmⁱ m. a descendant of Adam, a human being. ādȧmⁱ-khāv m. a man-eater, a carnivorous animal; N. of a kind of grass (Rām. 1631). ādamī-zād m. a man, a human being (Rām. 445, 892).
adv. very little, used regarding the partial return of something deposited.
m. a period, time, term, limit of time.

in ādanukᵘ  m. (f. ādanücᵘ̈), a first-born child of a woman. -bôjᵘ m. a brother-friend (used of two men who from childhood have grown up together as brothers, but are not brothers by blood (Rām. 213)). -yār m. one who has been a friend from childhood.
m. honour, respect. -bāv m. respect shown by an inferior to a superior. -satkār m. honour, respect.
m. a support, prop; a stop to prevent a ball rolling away.
m. (sg. dat. ādatas), custom, habit, practice (cf. K.Pr. 88; 138).
m. the name of the letter a.
m. hatred, malice, desire to injure.
m. the wooden beams which support a large log when being sawn asunder (cf. ara 1).
f. the name of a well-known pargana in the Marāz part of Kashmir, commonly called 'Adavin'. See RT.Tr. ii, 471.
m. a shed or place where men and cattle assemble, or where articles are collected for sale; a stand, a station, a meeting-place; a lounging-place for idlers.
adj. c.g. and the others, and the rest, et cetera (Rām. 573).
f. the name of a well-known village about 30 miles west of Śrīnagar.
a beginning, in ādi-kāran m. a first cause.

f. a bone (cf. K.Pr. 173, 226). This is the general term, cf. aḍa and aḍyulᵘ. It is the feminine form of the latter. āḍiji-khỗkhur m. a skeleton; a main bone of a complete skeleton. -panzulᵘ m. a skeleton; a living skeleton (of one who is very lean). -trangurᵘ m. a string of connected bones (compared to a knotted string, or a rosary).
m. power, capability; office, rank, position (Śiv. 36).
m. a person in charge of anything or having power over it (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. depending on, subject to, under another's power; poverty-stricken.
adj. (f. adüzᵘ̈), not burnt (whether this is a defect or a perfection).
adj. (f. adüjᵘ̈ 1), not struck, not hit (by a blow of the fist or a hurled missile); not pounded (on a stone or in a mortar) (of spices, food, etc.).
adj. (f. adö̆jᵘ̈), not husked (as of paddy in a mortar).
adj. (f. adüchᵘ̈), having no support, of an article which will over-balance or roll away unless it has a support.

adj. (f. adüjᵘ̈ 2), not torn, not shredded (of spices, such as ginger in a mortar); not crushed (as of paddy, etc., in a mortar); (in carpentry, of a board) not smoothed (with an adze, the native substitute for a plane).
adj. (f. adöjᵘ̈), not removed, that of which the position is not changed, not put aside; not cleansed (of barley, etc., by a winnowing sieve); not removed (of a disagreeable form).
adj. (f. adümᵘ̈), not given enough air (of a furnace supplied with air by a bellows).
adv. even without thought, without taking any consideration whatever (u. w. vbs. of taking and the like).
adv. without speaking; without giving any order.
adj. (f. adürᵘ̈), not firm, not steadfast; not firmly fixed; not strong, weak; (of rain) not incessant.
adj. (f. aḍürᵘ̈), not fearing, without fear, brave.
adj. (f. adörᵘ̈), without fortitude in adversity.
adj. (f. adörᵘ̈), not put, not placed (of any material thing, or of confidence, belief, etc.); not given on loan.
adj. c.g. not distinct, not different (both of opinions and of things).
m. (sg. dat. adrakas), green ginger (Zingiber officinale). -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. a cake flavoured with ginger, the lumpy root of the ginger plant.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. aḍyōv), to become half; hence, to become lean or wasted (from sickness or old age); to persevere, be intent on the attainment of some difficult object.
adj. (f. adūñᵘ̈), not carded (of cotton, wool, etc.).
f. an untidy or worn-out turban.
adj. (f. aḍuvᵘ̈), not swept, not cleared (of a seat or the like).
adj. (f. aduyᵘ̈) non-dual; hence (of the mind) convinced of the non-duality or identity of the Self with the Supreme (L.V. 5, 65).
m. (sg. dat. adwaitas), the advaita or monistic Vēdānta philosophy (Śiv. 26). the Deity in his monistie aspect, He who alone exists (Śiv. 512, 1402, 1604).
m. the weight of 2 tōlās (about 1 ounce); literally half a wal, Skr. pala, which was equivalent to 4 dhaṭakas.
or ad-wöyⁱ m. a broker in wheat and other grains. His wife is ad-wöyⁱ-bāy.
m. a chapter or section of a book.
m. (m. form of aḍijᵘ̈ q.v., cf. also aḍa), a large bone, such as that of the leg; generally used of the bone of limb rather than of the trunk; according to El., the rounded head of a bone.
m. justice, a just decision (used principally by old-fashioned people of the rural parts or by women).
adj. c.g. vile, mean, of vile occupation.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ạdᵃrôwᵃ; 2 p.p. ạdᵃrāvyōv), to make moist or wet.
or ạdᵃrēr m. dampness, moistness, wetness.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. ạdᵃryōv), to become moist (of something which has been dry).

m. a square coin of the value of half a pice; the Hindi adhēlā. Formerly in Kashmir articles of small value were purchased with cowries. Twelve cowries were called a bahāgañ; twenty-five were called a pū̃ʦhuh; fifty or half a hundred were called ȧdⁱ-hyolⁱ; a hundred was called a hath, and was considered the equivalent of one pice. In the rural parts of the country a pice is still called hath. Cf. bahāgañ, and RT.Tr. ii, 312.
f. the opium poppy, Papaver somniferum, L. 330.
interj. alas! W. 101; afsōs lārun, to become vexed, K.Pr. 153; yih chhuh boḍᵘ afsūs, this is a great pity (Gr.M.).
m. the sun. Sg. dat. YZ. 176.
m. a knot in wood; the knot in a tree. Cf. L. 461. aga-zyunᵘ m. firewood in which there are many knots.
in āg-bāg m. checking, careful examination. Cf. ôgᵘ-bôgᵘ.
m. a master, lord, chief; cf. K.Pr. 25. -bāy f. a master's wife, a mistress; cf. K.Pr. 263.

adj. c.g. fathomless, very deep (of water); hence also, profound, earnest (of character). agādi gaʦhun m.inf. to persevere steadily, to persist till one has gained one's object;  to display causeless wrath against one who is without fault.
adj. c.g. aware, acquainted (with), cognizant (of), apprised (of); compassionate (El.).
adj. c.g. knotty (of wood). -magal adj. c.g. dirtied (said of something itself pretty, but mixed up with foreign matter, such as straw or mud).
adj. c.g. the same as agal-magal, q.v., dirtied, etc.; used specially of incorrect writing full of mistakes. Paṇḍits apply the term to copies of MSS. made by Kāyasths, which require much correc on.
m. onefold; a fractional part, or at most one, of anything. aganas-dŏgan adv. twice the right amount (usually employed with verbs of giving or bringing).
adj. (f. agạnzᵘ̈rᵘ̈), uncounted, i.e. left uncounted (in counting).
or gar گر، اگر, conj. if.
m. the name of a certain plant described as blooming in the autumn, having a strong scent, with flowers of nearly every colour, and very useful as a medicine, probably Agasti grandiflora.
f. the immediate appearance of something inquired after, information, cognizance.
adj. (f. agöjᵘ̈), not molten, not melted, still unmelted, not reduced to a liquid form (usually of metals exposed to heat).
(f. agünḍᵘ̈, dat. aganjĕ), not tied up (of bundles and the like).
(cf. غافل) adv. thoughtlessly, inadvertently, unconsciously, unintentionally (Rām. 56, 129).
m. Aghōra, not terrible, a euphemistic name of Śiva (Śiv. 48).
adj. (f. agürᵘ̈), not worked, not smoothed off, rough (of metal vessels or ornaments, earthen vessels, wooden pillars, and the like which are 'worked' by artificers).
(f. agörᵘ̈), not searched for; hence also, forgotten (usually of persons).
m. (sg. dat. ã̄ganas, and so on), the anganā or courtyard of a house; cf. L. 459, anguṇ.
m. (sg. dat. āgaras, and so on), a place of origin or source (of a river, story, etc.), cf. K.Pr. 233.

f. an order, command; permission; a decision (of a judicial officer, etc.); (honorifically) a statement, proposition. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give an order; to decide (a case). --kurüñᵘ̈ --, f.inf. to make an order; to make a proposition (honorific) (Gr.M.).
adj. (f. agᵘ̈shᵘ̈), not ground, not reduced to a fine powder (of sandal-wood, kuṅkuma, and the like); not polished or worn smooth.

a suffix added to the nominative case singular of any noun, and giving the force of an indefinite article: thus, kalam-āh, an expression; manāh (manā + āh), a prohibition. When a nominative singular ends in an aspirated consonant, the aspiration is retained even when not original. Thus, from murat, sg. nom. murath, murathāh, an image.
m. a sigh, a groan, an inarticulate sound uttered in illness, grief, etc.; sg. gen. āhukᵘ (YZ. 494). --kaḍun --, m. to sigh (ib.).
f. the pin of a plough from which the yoke is suspended or to which it is tied.
m. in ahālgaʦhun, m.inf. to be skilful in any work, to be well practised in anything, to know how to do anything.
اھل کار m. an official, a Government officer (Gr.M.).
m. (f. ahalāwüñᵘ̈), one who causes another to agree to any action.
m. mistletoe (Viscum album) (El.). It attaches itself to the walnut-tree, and its berries are said to be the favourite fruit of the bulbul (L. 81) cf. wahal.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. aholᵘ, 2 p.p. ahajyōv), to agree to any action.
thou camest to me (ākh + am) (YZ. 138, 250, 252), see yunᵘ.
pron. I; the ego (L.V. 15), a word borrowed from Skt., and used in its philosophical sense. -bāv m. self-pride, egoism (K. 513).

interj. of respect (Gr.Gr. 101) and adv. of assent, employed in the following compounds:--āhanō adv. yes, used when addressing a male of equal or lower rank; it is an expression of doubtful assent. āhanū adv. yes, addressed to a junior male of rank equal to the speaker. -bā adv. yes, addressed to an equal or superior male. -biñᵘ̈ adv. yes, addressed to an equal or superior female. -möjᵘ̈ adv. yes, addressed to a superior or very senior female. -sö adv. yes, used by a male to a superior or senior male, as in -sö karān ha-sö chuh yes, sir, he is doing it. āhanuv adv. yes, addressed to a male equal or inferior in rank. āhaniy adv. yes, addressed to a woman inferior or equal in rank.
m. pride, vanity, overweening or insolent behaviour, whether due to wealth, knowledge, or family; the conceit of individuality, belief in the independent existence of the ego (Śiv. 125, 336).
f. consciousness of one's own individuality, self-consciousness (Śiv. 1620).
m. food. --karun -- m.inf. to eat (with dat. of obj. Śiv. 4).
m. the causing of a person to be confused or agitated by terrifying him, or the like.
? conj. to eat food (only noted in L.V. 28).
f. a prayer (El.); prob. i.q. öhī (q.v.).
m. a curse, imprecation, especially an imprecation uttered by one in extreme trouble.
m. the central pin or pivot of a pair of millstones, round which the upper stone revolves.

m. the examination of a portion of a crop in order to determine the amount of the whole; appraisement of a crop. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to calculate the probable result of any work by examining a portion of it at its commencement; skilfulness in such appraisement.
f. (sg. dat. ahö̆ʦᵘ̈), offering an oblation to a deity (Śiv. 1200); an oblation.
adj. (f. ahūrᵘ̈), not returned (of a debt, or anything lent); (figuratively) of a child not yet recovered from smallpox or other similar disease.
m. condition, case, circumstances, state of affairs (Rām. 220, 252, 263, etc.).
adj. (f. ahë̆ʦᵘ̈), unfriendly, acting in opposition to anyone.
m. i.q. ohuda, q.v. (vill.). In H. i, 2, the word is used to indicate the period of a king's reign, his lifetime as a king.
m. the name of a quarter of the town of Śrīnagar, situated on the east bank of the River Jehlam (Vĕth), said to be the site of Ahalyā's maṭha or hut. Hence its name.
adj. (f. -ranyē-müʦᵘ̈), one who has become hard or obstinate by perversity or change of nature.
m. the name of a well-known district and waterfall in Kashmīr, where the River Vĕshau (or Viśōka) issues from the Kōnsᵃr Nāg lake on the north side of the Pīr Pantsāl range.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. ạhᵃryōv), to be distraught from fear, sorrow, or the like; also, to show extreme obstinacy.

This is the ai of Hindī, pronounced like the y in 'my'. At the end of a word it is often written ay, as in rŏpai or rŏpay, a rupee. It is represented in Nāgarī by, and in Persian by zabar or zēr followed by yē. Thus, اَیتھھ or اِیتھھ, aiṭh, eight. When not final, ai is often optionally pronounced as ö, as in aiṭh or öṭh, eight. Before ⁱ or ᵘ̈, ai becomes ṻ. Thus, from the base kait-, how many? we have pl. dir. masc. kǖtⁱ, sing. dir. fem. kǖʦᵘ̈. Before ᵘ it becomes ū, as in sing. dir. masc. kūtᵘ.
interj. O! W. 101. ai Khudāyĕ or ai Khudāyō, O God! ib.; ai hākh, O cabbage! K.Pr. 4.
? f. a certain plant (Rumex) which is picked and dried for winter use and much valued as a potherb (L. p. 72). Cf. obulᵘ.
f. a cardomum; pl. nom. aila (K.Pr. 30; Śiv. 577).

or öna (= ائینہ) m. a mirror, a looking-glass (Śiv. 500, 558, 1547). K.Pr. spells this word āīnah, transliterating the Pers. آئینہ. -dörᵘ̈ a door ornamented with mirrors. -gorᵘ m. a mirror-maker; a seller of mirrors. -khünḍᵘ̈ f. a piece of a mirror. -khạpᵘ̈ṭᵘ̈ f. a small mirror, of no value or use. -khôṭᵘ m. a mirror-cover, or mirror-case. -phuṭᵘ f. a broken piece of looking-glass. -wöjᵘ̈ f. a kind of finger-ring, fitted with a tiny mirror. -zömpāna m. a palanquin, the doors and other parts of which are made of mirrors of glass, crystal, or the like; hence, met., a very fragile conveyance.
m. (sg. dat. ainakas), a pair of spectacles, an eyeglass (either for improving the sight or for protecting against glare). -gara m. a spectacle case.
(? spelling), f. a certain small white fish which inhabits the smaller streams flowing into the Jehlam (L. 158) and is carried into that river when the waters are high. ? connected with aṭh 1.

or öṭh card. c.g. (dat. aiṭhan), eight, Śiv. 711 (aiṭh), 1494 (öṭh). ¶ aiṭha-bôgᵘ m. the eighth part or share of anything; adj. (f. -böjᵘ̈), divided or divisible into eight parts. -gunᵘ adj. (f. -guñᵘ̈), eightfold. -khorᵘ path m. a path or field producing eight khorᵘ, or loads of twelve seers each, or a total of ninety-six seers; a path being the area in which six seers of grain have been sown. -khôrᵘ adj. (f. -khörᵘ̈), weighing eight kharwārs, each kharwār being sixteen traks or ninety-six seers. -kūnᵘ adj. (m. sg. dat. -kūnis, abl. -kōni; f. -kūñᵘ̈, sg. dat. -kōñĕ), eight-cornered, octagonal. -kūñjal adj. c.g., id. -lobᵘ adj. (f. -lübᵘ̈), eight-pointed. -labal adj. c.g., id. -lorᵘ adj. (f. -lürᵘ̈), eight-stringed (of a necklace, etc.); eight-stranded (of a rope, etc.). -nö m. the name of the number eight (used in schools). -polᵘ adj. (f. -püjᵘ̈), weighing eight pals; producing eight pals; the produce of eight pals. A pal is one-fifth of a seer. -rongᵘ adj. (f. -rünjᵘ̈), having eight colours; of eight kinds. -rẹ̆tᵘ adj. (f. -r;ë̆ʦᵘ̈), produced in eight months. -shotᵘ adj. (f. -shüʦᵘ̈), consisting of eight hundred (of the number of threads in a cloth); costing eight hundred (rupees, etc.). -shēṭhakh f. a certain unlucky marriage (prohibited by astrology) amongst Hindūs, when the bride is born in the sixth sign of the Zodiac (or Virgo) and the bridegroom in the eighth thereafter (or Aries). -trokᵘ adj. (f. -trücᵘ̈), weighing eight traks (of six seers each). -wuhurᵘ adj. (f. -warishᵘ̈), produced in eight years, eight years old. -zongᵘ adj. (f. -zünjᵘ̈), having eight legs; met. swift, rapid in progress. ¶ aiṭhan ṛĕtan-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), produced in eight months, an eight months' child.
f. the eighth lunar day of a Hindū lunar fortnight.
m. an old, worn-out, and patched garment.
or ǖṭhyumᵘ ord. (f. aiṭhimᵘ̈ or ǖṭhimᵘ̈), eighth.
m. the condition of half-ness; hence, maimedness, the condition of wanting limbs or members; also, leanness of the body.
m. the name of a village in the Lār Pargana of Kashmīr, situated near the River Jehlam (Vĕth).
or az adv. to-day (W. 95), see az.
adj. (f. ajürᵘ̈), plain, not jewelled, not set, not mounted (of ornaments, etc.).
f. a wild plant growing on the mountains, the fruit of which is used as medicine for indigestion. The same as the Hindī ajwān (Carum Copticum). L. 330, 346, calls it ajwāin.
one of the spellings of akhāh in the Persian character (W. 34). See under akh.
m.pl. the great, grandees, people of rank (Rām. 1314, adj.).
adj. (f. akahüʦᵘ̈), very distressed, very depressed (owing to insults offered, loss of property, sickness of a dear one, or the like).
adj. c.g. timeless, eternal; as subst., N. of Śiva (Śiv. 622).
adj. c.g. without stain, spotless, unblemished (Rām. 1321).
m. (sg. dat. -nandanas), an affectionate term for an only son.
m. the name of the symbol for the number one (1) in the Śāradā character, in which it is represented by a small circle on the line, thus o = 1, o. = 10, and so on.
m. form, shape, appearance, the expression of the face. ākāra-gŏpᵃth adj. c.g. one who conceals the expression of his face, one who dissimulates.
m. a confession, admission (cf. K.Pr. 14); an agreement; a promise. --karun --, to confess; to agree to anything; to promise, pledge one's word (Gr.M.).
m. (in the Nāgarī or Śāradā alphabet) the letter a (Śiv. 1771).
m. pride, self-importance, arrogance (of one raised to a high position or affluence).

m. the sky, ether, firmament, atmosphere (Śiv. 28, 200, 468, 501, 508). ¶ ākāshĕ-gang or -gangā f. the Ganges of the sky, the Milky Way. -gath f. (sg. dat. -güʦᵘ̈, and so on), the power or act of going in the atmosphere (e.g. of birds, gods, or superhuman beings). -wönī f. a voice from the air or from heaven.
adj. (f. akatürᵘ̈), not cut in slices (of fruits, vegetables, gourds, and the like).

card. num. c.g. [in declension this verb takes the remaining cases from okᵘ. Thus, dat. akis (Śiv. 473); gen. ȧkⁱ-sondⁱ or (referring to something inanimate) akyukᵘ; ag. ȧkⁱ; abl. aki (Śiv. 64). These are all of common gender, and are used even in agreement with feminine nouns, as in akis khās kathi to one special matter], one (Śiv. 512, 543); (as an indefinite article) a, an (Śiv. 509), a certain. Cf. akhāh below. This adjective, when used as an indefinite article, often idiomatically follows the noun it qualifies, e.g. YZ. 140, Śiv. 64, 97, and Gr.M. 1427. --ȧkⁱ kyā nām akh --, once one is one, the formula of multiplication Cf. ȧkⁱ below. --akh -- adj. c.g. all, all together (as in all went together); each, one another (as in akh akis madath karun to help one another); adv. (W. 95), singly, one by one. -bari, see ekbari. --horᵘ -- m. a pair, a couple (either animate or inanimate, but more usually inanimate). --hath -- m. one hundred, a hundred. --jōra -- m., or --jūrⁱ -- f. a pair, a couple. (Although one of these words is masculine and the other is feminine, either may be employed without reference to the gender of the things composing the pair described.) --ta panüñᵘ̈ -- f. one and my own; hence extreme selfishness, allowing no one to stand in the way of one's own interest. --ta zᵃh karān -- adv. doing one and two; hence, very quickly, at once. ¶ akhāh c.g. amounting to one, just one; any one, some one; (as an indefinite article) a, an, a certain. yus akhāh, whoever. In the Persian character we often find this word spelt akāh اکاہ (e.g. YZ. 263) or akā اکا (W. 34); K.Pr. spells it akhā in 7 and akhāh in 150. --khanḍā -- c.g. about one, nearly one. ¶ ȧkⁱ kyā nām, the formula used for one in multiplication, as in akh ȧkⁱ kyā nām akh, once one is one; zᵃh ȧkⁱ kyā nām zᵃh, twice one are two (Gr.Gr. 86). ¶ aki-aki adv. one by one. -cyāli adv. in some way, in an undetermined way. -cyāli-aki adv. in some way or other, in some manner or other (the second form is the more indefinite of the two). -dŏha adv. on a certain day, once upon a time. -dŏha-aki adv. on some day or other. -laṭi adv. at one time; once. -laṭi-aki adv. at some time or other. -nata aki-laṭi adv. at some time or other, at some hour or other. -phiri adv. at a certain time, once upon a time; in one time, once. -phiri-aki adv. at some time or other. -pāri adv. from (or on) one side of any country or thing; cf. okᵘ pôrᵘ. -pörⁱ adv. on (or from) one side of any country or thing; cf. okᵘ pôrᵘ. -ranga adv. after one manner. -rĕta-aki adv. in some month or other. -samayĕ-aki adv. at some time or other. -warihĕ-aki adv. in some year or other. ¶ okuy adj. (i.e. okᵘ + emphatic y) (m.abl. akiy, Śiv. 469, 471; f. ükᵘ̈y), only one. ¶ akiy-phiri adv. at only one particular time, only once. -pörⁱ adv. on or from only one particular side. -lari adv. on one side only. -lari ta akiy shānda adv. only on one side and only on one pillow, a phrase used in imprecations, i.e. may you never turn in your bed, and may you never raise your head from the pillow, equivalent to wishing a person to die as soon as he goes to bed.
m. (sg. dat. ākhas, and so on), a scar, the mark of a healed wound, or of smallpox.
thou camest, or (Śiv. 81) he, belonging to them, came; see yunᵘ.
adj. c.g. bearing a scar, marked with a scar.
adj. (f. akharᵘ̈cᵘ̈), unexpended, unspent (of money, etc.).
adj. (f. akhūjᵘ̈), unopened, not opened, not untied.

adj. (f. akhūnzᵘ̈), not plucked (of hair or feathers); that of which the hair or feathers have not been plucked out (e.g. a fowl not prepared for cooking, or a beard, the hairs of which are plucked out by some ascetics).
f. a story of old times, a romantic legend, a historical romance, either written or recited.
m. (sg. dat. akhĕnis, and so on), lit. not eating, hence inability to enjoy or reap the benefit of what is one's own; esp. an imprecation wishing that an enemy may incur this liability.
m. the name of a village in Kuṭahār Pargana, sacred to the goddess Śivā (Dēvī). See L. 313, Śiv. 112.
adv. on one side (of anything, dat.) (H. xii, 14).
adj. (f. akŏliñᵘ̈), of low family, belonging to one of the inferior Brahmanical gōtras.

adj. untimely. Used in the following compounds. akölⁱ-marun, m. an untimely death, to die before one's time, a death during an epidemic of cholera or the like. akölⁱ-warshun m. untimely rain, rain which injures crops. akāli-pōsh m. flowers blooming out of season, e.g. a fresh bloom coming again immediately after the regular fruit has ripened; hence a child born unexpectedly to a woman late in life.
adj. (f. akünzᵘ̈), unsinged, prepared for roasting, but not singed (of a plucked fowl, an animal's head, or the like).
(f. akörᵘ̈), unboiled, (of liquids, such as milk, etc.).
adv. in the heaven, in the sky (Śiv. 246, 1146, 1396).
adj. (f. aküʦᵘ̈), of cotton, wool, etc., unspun; also spun or twisted by hand, and not in a spinning-wheel.
adj. c.g. not acting, free from work; in a religious sense, free from the bond of works as an impediment to salvation, in a state of salvation (L.V. 32, 45).
or (K. 831) akshauhĕn f. a large army (complete in chariots, elephants, cavalry, and infantry) (Śiv. 853; K. 553, 818, 831).
m. a letter of the Nāgarī or Śāradā alphabet, a syllable (Śiv. 1763-4, 1768, 1771). I.q. achur, q.v.
(f. akūrᵘ̈), not loosened in the roots, not soft, stiff, hard, firm, as the roots of hair before being lathered for shaving; from which the kernel has not been extracted (of walnuts and the like).
ord. (f. akimᵘ̈), first, first in order.

f. (pl. nom. ala 1, K.Pr. 10), a pumpkin, gourd, squash, Cucurbita maxima (El.), Cucurbita Pepo (L. 346), cf. YZ. 404. ¶ ala-bạrᵃg m. a pumpkin leaf. -byôlᵘ m. a pumpkin seed. -ḍokhᵘ m. a trellis or hedge on which pumpkin vines are supported. -dĕl m. the husk or rind of a pumpkin. -gaḍorᵘ m. a kind of gourd; with the interior extracted, the outer shell is used by religious mendicants as a water-vessel (Śiv. 593). -gaḍürᵘ̈ f. a small gourd used as a water-bottle, or for holding powder or the like. -hüṭᵘ̈ f. pumpkin-wood: a piece of dried pumpkin flesh. A kind of hour-glass shaped gourd which ripens in the autumn and is skinned. It is then cut up and dried for eating in the winter, or used as a medicine. -hacĕ wālañĕ f. pl. inf. to strip a gourd for the above purpose; hence, when a person is wearing a garment, to tear it from top to bottom. -khünḍᵘ̇ f. a piece or slice of a pumpkin. -kükᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the hard outer rind of a pumpkin. -kulᵘ m. a pumpkin vine (cf. K.Pr. 9). -kulis tula-kulᵘ m. a mulberry-tree for a pumpkin vine; hence, lengthening out a small affair by turning truth into falsehood and falsehood into truth (e.g. in a court of justice, or in a matter of business). -künḍᵘ̈ f. the globular rind of a certain gourd, which when over-ripened in the autumn is extremely hard. -kānüjᵘ̈ f. the edible tendrils of a gourd vine. -kānolᵘ m. the branches of a gourd vine. -novᵘ m. the festival of eating the first young pumpkins. An auspicious moment is selected in the summer, when the fruit first appears. -phal-hār m. eating food consisting only of cooked pieces of pumpkin, on fast days. -pōsh m. a pumpkin flower. -pōshĕ-mọ̆nḍᵘ m. spiced cakes of wheat flour and pounded pumpkin flowers, cooked in a sauce of ghī or oil. -pōshĕ-mŏ̈nḍᵘ̈ f. a similar dish eaten with curds. -thaph f. (sg. dat. -thapi), a full lump of stewed pumpkin raised by the hand for insertion into the mouth; hence, metaphorically, a mass of leaves or papers firmly stuck together. -tīl m. an oil extracted from pumpkin seeds, and used as a medicine; said to benefit the brain and blood-vessels. -ʦūr m. a process in the cultivation of pumpkins, in which the earth is turned up and the roots are cleaned. -wã̄gan m.pl. pumpkins and egg-plant fruit (baĩgan), the name of a dish in which these two are cooked together. -wörᵘ̈ f. a pumpkin garden. -wạthᵃr m. the leaf of the pumpkin vine. -zᵃlun m. the refuse--rind, seeds, etc.--of a pumpkin prepared for cooking. ¶ ȧlⁱ-ȧlⁱ khasun m.inf. to become very stout; lit., to mount like a pumpkin plant, which is slender but has large fruit. ¶ ali-ti-shāph bali-ti-shāph m. both a curse at a pumpkin and a curse at a sacrifice, cursing a person whether he is offering a service of very small value, or whether he is doing anything of great difficulty and involving self-sacrifice; hence, general dissatisfaction, of a master who is always blaming his servant, whether right or wrong, or of a servant who is always grumbling at his master.
or ala 2, an intensive prefix. See the various words below in alphabetical order.

a primary suffix added to the root of the verbs dyunᵘ, to give, and dāwun, to cause to give, with an obscene sense. Thus, dinal or dāwal, an unchaste woman, mājĕ-dinal or mājĕ-dāwal, one who commits incest with his mother, and so on (Gr.Gr. 107).

c.g. a secondary suffix forming adjectives of possession. Thus, dörᵘ̈, a beard, dārĕl (i.e. dāri + al), bearded. When added to an abstract verbal noun, that noun takes the feminine form. Thus, from thĕkun, to boast, we have thĕkiñĕl, a boaster (Gr.Gr. 120, 133).
m. a plough (sg. ag. ālan, K.Pr. 10). Cf. ala 3. āla-phyurᵘ m. the soil turned up by the second ploughing after the seed has been sown.

(for ala 1 and 2 see al 1 and 2), f. a plough. Cf. āla. -böñᵘ̈ f. the main beam of a plough (Śiv. 1531), cf. al-böñᵘ̈ (s.v.); (?) a goad (El.). -kijⁱ or -kijᵘ̈ f. a pin of a plough, to which the yoke or other part is fastened. -phāl m. a ploughshare; (by extension of meaning) a collection of articles used in husbandry, plough, bullocks, digging implements, etc., equivalent to the Hindī hal-bail. -wath f. (sg. dat. -wati), a plough-furrow.

in ala-ʦānun m.inf. to bring in trembling; to cause something fixed to totter; hence, to scare one who is weaker by a hasty move of the hand, cf. ala-ala ʦānun below. ¶ ala-ala m. unsteadiness, trembling, tremulousness. -ala aʦun m.inf. to tremble from fear, cold, or ague. -ala ʦānun m.inf. to bring in trembling, to cause to tremble, to terrify.
m. swinging, swaying (as of a child's cot or swing).
adj. (as subst., f. aladĕviñ), very stout, very fat, of a man or woman; hence, foolish, wanting in intellect.
m. a great man, K.Pr. 9, where it is opposed to malagaḍi, a base man.
f. a polite greeting, saying, "how do you do?" Cf. ölⁱ-wākh.
علیحدہ adj. c.g. pl. separate, apart (in position, form, quality, or action).
m. connexion, concern, relevancy (Gr.M.); an estate (El.). alāka-dār علاقہ دار m. the owner of an estate (El.).
m. (sg. dat. alakhas), the Invisible, N. of Śiva (Śiv. 555).
m. (sg. dat. ālakŏnḍalas, pl. nom. ālakŏnḍal), a circle, a circular mark; the inner, circular, earthenware receptacle of the kāngrī or portable brazier.
m. a proper name, used metaphorically, like our Crœsus and Dives, to mean the heir of a rich man or king; used as a respectful term when referring to such an one.

f. a banner, a flag (usually a small one), including the staff. -pōsh m. the cloth of such a flag (usually three-cornered). -tulᵘ m. the height of a flagstaff. -tulis khārun m.inf. to cause to ascend to the height of a flagstaff; hence, to render a person liable to general reproach by abusing him. ¶ alami-kūṭᵘ m. a flagstaff. -pōsh m. the same as alam- pōsh.
m. cheating, swindling (in keeping accounts and the like), embezzlement.
m. the name of a village about 16 miles north of Śrīnagar, close to where the River Vĕth (Jehlam) enters the Wŏlur Lake.
conj. (1 p.p. alanôwᵘ), to cause to oscillate, to set swinging (e.g. a cradle or a child's swing).
f. swaying, swinging (as of tree-branches); trembling, shivering of the body (from cold, etc.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. alarôwᵘ), to set in oscillation, to cause to swing (of a child's swing, or a cradle).
adj. (f. alarawüñᵘ̈), one who causes to oscillate or tremble.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. alorᵘ), to cause to oscillate or tremble; to move something from rest, to shake.

(f. alarwöñᵘ̈), very insecure, easily shaken; also, not very secure, moderately secure, of a stone or the like fixed in a wall. ¶ alarwañĕn-kañĕn adv. very insecurely, in such a position as to be easily upset, u.w. vbs. of placing or of position, etc.
m. eager desire, eager anxiety for anything or for the success of any action.
adj. (f. alatamüñᵘ̈) very ill-looking, very ugly.

f. the ceremony performed in adoration of a god by moving circularly round the head of the idol a platter containing a five-wicked burning lamp, flour, water, and incense; a similar ceremony performed on a bride and bridegroom, on the occasion of the second visit of the bride to her husband's house, and on other similar occasions.
adv. fruitlessly, in vain. Cf. alēbalē and alēpralē-kŏlēṭās. --dŏh kar-lösi -- adv. desiring to pass one's time fruitlessly.
f.pl. extreme anxiety or distress, e.g. that caused by terror, the afflictions of those we love and the absence of any means of their relief; helplessness.
m. a fire in a pit in the open, a bonfire. -ta-jĕlāv m. a great conflagration (e.g., a house on fire, or the burning of a stack of wood); hence, met., the burning of fever, etc.
m. a loud, clear, call or cry (Śiv. 1187); ālav dyunᵘ m.inf. to call, shout to a person (K.Pr. 102, Śiv. 532). -milav m. a loud, clear, call or cry; any loud, clear, sound.
f. the act of bringing a boat to or near the shore.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ālowᵘ), to wave round one's head, wave aloft, to wave (the hands), esp. in a propitiatory ceremony as described below (Śiv. 108, 1692, K.Pr. 50); to bring a boat near the shore; to row (El.). gulⁱ ālawanⁱ, m. pl. inf. to pass the hands over the head and face in order to pacify, to show affection (K.Pr. 13). ¶ ālawith conj. part. used as adv., waving an offering to a spirit of evil round the head before casting it forth, as in a ceremony for warding off a calamity. -pālawith adv. waving round the head and casting forth, as in the above ceremony.
in ālay-zālpyonᵘ m.inf. to be in the condition of an orphan child, on whom devolves all the burden of supporting a house.

f. (pl. nom. alāyĕ-balāyĕ), pleasure and pain, happiness and misery. K.Pr. 134 translates this word by 'sacrifice', in the sense of the use of the word by women whilst waving platters with lamps, etc., round a person's head, to remove all evil. Hence the words have come to mean 'offering', 'sacrifice', 'victim'. Cf. ālawun. alāyĕ-balāyĕ kaḍun m.inf. to expel by this waving, to deliver a child from infantile dangers, much as smallpox and the like; similarly, alāyĕ-balāyĕ-nishĕ rachun m.inf. to protect from calamities, as in the ceremony above referred to.

or ālaʦhī adj. (as subst., f. ālaʦhī or ālüʦhᵘ̈), lazy, idle, weary, tired. -būñᵘ̈ f. "the weary one's plane-tree", the name of a famous chenar, or plane-tree, under which pilgrims rest on the way to Jwālāmukhī. -mar m. "home for the lazy", the name of a place in the village of Khạrᵃv or Khruv, in the Vihī Pargana of Kashmīr, traditionally said to be a foundation by some merciful person for the benefit of the weary or the work-shy.
adj. c.g. idle (W. 21, where it is spelt ālaʦlad).
f. a plough, the same as ala 3, q.v. Cf. ala-böñᵘ̈ under that word.
adv. very secretly, without exciting suspicion.
adv. suddenly, unexpectedly, without cause. Cf. alēpralē-kŏlēṭās and alāṭösi.
adv. very uselessly, futilely. Cf. alēbalē and alāṭösi.
(corruption of علی تشَیُع). The term by which Sunnī Kāshmīrīs refer to Shī'a Musalmāns; a heretic. Cf. L. 284.
m. the alphabet (in the Kashmiro-Persian character) (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. weak, sick, worn to a shadow from sickness or the like.
m. a style, title of honour (Hindōstānī xitāb) (Gr.M.).
f. a certain garment, shaped like a dressing-gown, extending from the neck to the feet, and open in front. It is like the kabā (قبا), but has buttons instead of strings.
m. (sg. dat. almadatas and so on), an exclamation of encouragement.
adj. (f. alümᵘ̈), not dragged, not pulled out straight, not extended (of a rope, etc.).

adj. (f. alönzᵘ̈), suspended, hanging down. --ʦhã̄ḍun, m.inf. to seek to get a thing that is hanging out of reach (K.Pr. 10). alāndĕn-thapa karañĕ f. pl. inf. to stretch up the hand to things suspended; to grasp at a worthless support.

adj. (f. alörᵘ̈) (of vessels) not polished, (of clothes) not properly fullered; on which fuller's earth or polishing paste has been applied, but the final polishing or cleansing has not been carried out.

m. the five things commencing with the letter m formerly employed in their religious worship by followers of the left-hand Śākta sect, viz., madya, wine; māṁsa, flesh; matsya, fish; mudrā, special attitudes; maithuna, sexual intercourse; hence, in modern language, any vile and utterly impure food. -ta-mal m. anything extremely uneatable or undrinkable, or which if eaten or drunk produces illness or is indigestible; lit. "al-pal and filth".

adj. c.g. (as subst., m. sg. dat. alsēṭas), very stout (whether suitably so or not). -hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -hishᵘ̈), too stout, too fat (of an animate being or inanimate thing); hence, (of a person) a fat fool, (of a thing) unsuitable, useless.
adj. c.g. (as subst., m. sg. dat. alsrēṭas), very stout, very fat (of an animate being), hence very foolish, witless. Cf. arsrēṭh. -hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -hishᵘ̈ -), id., a fat fool.
m. the potato, Solanum tuberosum (L. 346), i.q. ôluh, q.v.
in ālū-bukhārā آلو بخارا or örᵘ̈, m. the Bukhara or Persian plum, Prunus communis (L. 348).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. alyōv), to be insecure, to shake.
adj. (f. alūñᵘ̈), not reaped (of a crop).
m. adieu, farewell. --karun -- m.inf. to make a last farewell (H. vii, 16).
? gend., a kind of woollen cloth, plain or unembroidered pashmīnā (L. 377).
adj. (f. alë̆vᵘ̈), not licked, of a dish or vessel to which some dainties are still adhering.
adj. (f. alivᵘ̈), not plastered, of the surface of the ground, or a wall.
m.pl. a kind of earring, flat and round, in the shape of the leaf of a tāl palm (Hindōstānī tarkī). -horᵘ m. a pair of such earrings. ¶ ạlᵃkan m. a single one of such earrings.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ạlᵃrôwᵃ), to cause something firm to be in movement, to shake, cause to oscillate or tremble.
or ali, a secondary suffix forming adverbs of time, as in tĕlⁱ or tĕli, then (Gr.Gr. 156).
m. that which continues both in this world and the next (as fame, etc.), said to be connected with orᵘ firm, i.e. of this life, and sorᵘ absorbed, vanished, i.e. of the next life.
f. a certain fish described as being large and handsome, but insipid as food.

f. flax, Linum usitatissimum; also the seed, linseed. Cf. L. 330. ¶ ȧlⁱshi-kã̄ḍ m. the stem of the linseed plant. -khüjᵘ̈ f. linseed oil-cake, used as a cattle food. -khal f. linseed oil-cake. -krüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kracĕ), linseed chaff, used as a cattle food, and, mixed with earth, as a wall-plaster. -koshᵘ m. the husk of linseed. -kāṭh m. the stem of the linseed plant. -phal m. linseed, as ready for sale or use. -pröjᵘ̈ f. linseed chaff, see above. -tīl m. linseed oil.
m. the act of eating, eating (a nursery word, generally used of food offered to a child being weaned).

m. human intestinal worms or entozoa, lumbricus (El.). ¶ āma-ḍī˜jᵘ̈ f. a mass of such worms. -kyomᵘ m., i.q. ām 1. -lọ̆ʦhᵘ m., i.q. āma-ḍī˜jᵘ̈-phŏkh or -phukār m. the disease, accompanied by swelling of the belly, of having these worms in the body, most commonly in children. -shöshⁱ f. excessive breathing or panting caused by this disease.

pron. suff. appended to the finite tenses of verbs, with the force of the acc. dat. or ag. sing. of the 1st pers.: me, to me, by me. If the verbal form to which it is added ends in a vowel, the a of the suffix is usually elided. Thus, karan, they will make, karan-am, they will make me or for me; korᵘ, made, koru-m, made by me, I made. When added to the 3rd sing. fut. or to the fut. impve. the a is not elided, but, together with the final i of these forms, becomes ĕ. Thus, kari, he will make, karĕm, he will make me or for me; kȧrⁱzi, you should make, kȧrⁱzĕm you should make me or for me (Gr.Gr. 183).
adj. c.g. common, general (Gr.M.); common persons, people of low birth. āmas sṻty har, a quarrel with the common people (K.Pr. 11).
he came to me, see yunᵘ.
f. a grandmother. The word is said to be common among the prostitute families of Śrīnagar (El.); an old prostitute, a bawd. Cf. am-jī.
in āma-tāv m. 'raw-roasting', half-roasting, parching (Rām. 1626). Cf. ômᵘ.

? adv. an interrogative particle, indicating a desire with doubt as to its accomplishment, equivalent to sentences such as 'will you, pray?', 'is it the case that?', 'why, pray?' or the like. Probably the same word as amā 2. -kyāsanā ? adv., i.q. amā 1, but more emphatic.
conj. but, moreover (El. and W.), (W. 100 spells it amma, with a double m as in Arabic). -pozᵘ conj. but.
m. numbness caused by contact with snow or ice, frostbite; pain in the teeth from drinking very cold water or from eating ice or snow.
adj. (f. amahörᵘ̈), not broken to pieces, not reduced to powder (of a lump of boiled rice, sugar, earth, or the like).

m. work, action; employment (K.Pr. 10). --āsun -- m.inf. to be brought into use (K.Pr. 10). --karun -- m. inf. to act; to obey (El.). --karanwôlᵘ -- m. a certain official, a taḥṣīldār, a collector (El.). cyönis wananas pĕṭh --karun -- (Gr.M.), to act upon (or comply with) what you say.
m. the state or condition of possessing a raw or unripe odour; musty smelliness.
f. change for the worse; a condition of corruption or of malodorousness.

m. (sg. dat. amānatas), depositing, committing property to the trust or care of a person; a deposit, a thing placed in charge (K.Pr. 30). amānatas khiyānath, embezzlement of a deposit (ib. 11). -cīri f. a document certifying a deposit, a deed of trust.
f. change for the worse, applied to food grown stale and beginning to be offensive.
adj. (f. amandüchᵘ̈), without shame, shameless; bold, daring, confident, audacious.

m. the receiving of anything into the mouth, usually applied to a suckling child receiving milk. -ta-grŏṭh m. putting into the mouth and swallowing (without chewing), usually applied as before to a suckling child.
f.pl. perturbation, fluster, agitation of mind, from fear or other similar cause.
f. a certain land tenure, in which the state takes its share of the actual produce of a village (L. 403).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. āmanyōv), to change for the worse; to look exhausted from fatigue or hunger; to go bad, become corrupt and malodorous (of food, etc.). ¶ āmanyô-motᵘ perf. part. (f. āmanyö-müʦᵘ̈), changed for the worse, disimproved; appearing exhausted from fatigue or hunger; become corrupt, malodorous (of food).
adj. c.g. undying (Śiv. 931, 935); N. of Śiva (Śiv. 622).
a suffix added to cardinal numerals giving indefiniteness, as in aiṭh-amara, about eight (Gr.Gr. 84).
m. a wanderer (El., who writes it ámárah).
? gend. building; a building, structure, edifice. -gar m. one who builds, a skilled builder (Rām. 131).
f. N. of the abode of the gods, esp. the heaven of Indra (Śiv. 1497, personified).

m. (sg. dat. -būtas), or ombur-būth, a certain white powder applied to the limbs by pilgrims to Amarnāth (q.v.). It is made of the gypsum rock of which the cave is composed. Its application is believed to possess great religious efficacy.

m. (sg. dat. -nāthas) or ambar-nāth, Lord of the Immortals, N. of Śiva (Śiv. 192); N. of a cave about 70 kōs east of Śrīnagar among the sources of the Sind River (Śiv. 114, 622). It contains a large block of transparent ice formed by the freezing of the water which issues from the rock. This is worshipped as a liṅga or emblem of Śiva Amarēśvara. It is a place of great sanctity, and the pilgrimage to it in the month of Śrāvaṇa or June-July attracts many thousands of people not only from Kashmīr but from all parts of India. The pilgrimage is one involving great hardships. See El. s.v., L. 41, and RT.Tr. II, 409. For a description of the modern pilgrimage, see Vigne, Travels, pp. 10 ff.
m. the mark of slight burning, or scorching, on cloth or the limbs.
adj. (f. amaṭhörᵘ̈), not levelled or straightened; hence, of a vessel or dish, etc., not hammered out.
m. the night of the new moon (Śiv. 1658).
f. a mango (the tree or the fruit) (Gr.M.).

m. a large pile (Śiv. 996) or heap of grain, earth, etc., cf. ambār. --karun -- m.inf. to heap up, make a heap. ¶ ambaras āsun m.inf. to be (a material) for piling up, to remain over and above; hence, met., to have a fresh lease of life after recovering from the point of death, or after rescue from mortal peril. --karun -- m.inf. to make to a pile, to pile anything (e.g. grain) up, to make into a pile.

in the two following. Cf. L. p. 349. -trēl f. a kind of apple, small in size and of excellent flavour. -ʦū̃ṭhᵘ m. another apple, large, round, red and white, ripening in October, and keeping in condition a long time.
f. a canopied litter, with ornamented housings, used on an elephant (Śiv. 967).
adv. at one's own free will (Śiv. 586).
adv. intentionally, deliberately; (in Ksh.) as a natural result, owing to (such and such) a cause (Śiv. 1230).
m. raw-kneedness, having weak knees, inability to walk properly (of a child learning to walk), K.Pr. 260, where it is spelt ām-kuṭ. Said also to mean incomplete, immature.
or amōb, exceeding, excessive, or adv. exceedingly, excessively.
adj. (f. amö̃ḍᵘ̈), not mingled, not mixed, not kneaded up (of flour or the like in water).
adj. (f. amö̃jᵘ̈), not cleaned, not scrubbed, not polished (of a metal vessel or the like).
adj. (f. amö̆jᵘ̈), without price, priceless, that for which a price is impossible; without price, gratis, as a free gift.
adj. (f. amüjᵘ̈), not rubbed or shampooed (of the body or a limb); not used in shampooing (of the customary oil or medicament).
adj. (f. amüjᵘ̈), undefiled, pure, free from all defilement (L.V. 64).
adj. (f. amünzᵘ̈), not churned, not fully churned (of milk, etc.); met., not fully considered, not worked out (of a story, theory, etc.).
adj. (f. amüṇḍᵘ̈, pl. amanjĕ), not kneaded (of woollen clothes kneaded under foot in water in order to soften or clean them).
adj. (f. amünjᵘ̈), not asked for; got without asking.
adj. (f. amüʦhᵘ̈), not rubbed (of oil, medicine, or the like, rubbed on the body); not rubbed, not brushed, dusty (of clothes).
adj. (f. āmüʦᵘ̈), the perf. part. of yunᵘ, q.v., come, arrived (e.g. Siv. 44); of seeds and the like, just sprouting, just appeared above the ground.
f.pl. the feeding of one bird by another, beak to beak. -mangañĕ f.pl. asking to be fed in this manner; hence, met., persistently and repeatedly asking for an urgently desired object.

m. (sg. dat. amṛĕtas and so on), ambrosia nectar, always represented as a liquid (Śiv. 15, 167, 195, 473, 501, etc.); hence, met., any particularly dainty or delicious food. amṛĕta-zal m. the water of ambrosia, liquid ambrosia, nectar (Śiv. 179).

adj. (f. amuchᵘ̈), not brought to a conclusion, not accomplished (of a day on which a fast or the like has been undertaken, but on which the final oblations, etc., cannot, owing to some rule of ritual, be performed).
m. a smell of burning or scorching cloth, especially cotton-cloth.
adj. (f. amuñᵘ̈), not pounded in a mortar for the removal of husk, not husked (of rice and other grains).
adj. (f. amūrᵘ̈), not shelled, not husked (of peas, vetches, and the like).
adj. (f. amū̃trᵘ̈), not rendered subject to charm, not charmed against (e.g. a snake); not offered to a god, etc., with the proper spell or invocation (mantra).
adj. (f. amījᵘ̈), not united, not mixed; not met with, rare, difficult or impossible to procure.
adj. (m. dat. sg. amīnis, ag. amīnⁱ, abl. amēni; pl. nom. amīnⁱ, dat. amēnĕn, ag. and abl. amēnyau; fem. amīñᵘ̈, dat. amēñi, and so on), not measured, not weighed.
f. a species of elm (Ulmus erosa and pumila) (El., who spells it amráí).
m. the name of a celebrated garden on the Ḍal Lake near Śrīnagar. It was prepared in the latter half of the eighteenth century by Amīr Khān Jawān Shēr.
m. the name of the uppermost bridge over the Vĕth (Jehlam) River in Śrīnagar. It was built by Amīr Khān Jawān Shēr in the latter half of the eighteenth century.
adv. yes, a particle of assent; cf. ã̄kār.

m. any edible grain, cooked or uncooked; grain food generally (Śiv. 969). As the first member of a compound this word often takes the form anna, see below. --karun -- m.inf. to eat food, generally used as a polite formula in addressing a superior. -kāṭh m. inferior kinds of grain such as barley, pulses, or the like, eaten by the poorer classes. -kūṭh m. (sg. dat. -kūṭas), a pile of grain; esp. a pile of grain and other food distributed to the poor at various festivals, especially at the close of the rice harvest. Cf. El. s.v. ankúṭ and L. 271. -kitȧrⁱ m.pl. a kind of rat which infests granaries. Employed in the plural, as they appear in great numbers. -pan m. a reduplication of an; grain etcetera, grain and the like; all kinds of food eaten with grain. ¶ ana-gagorᵘ m. (f. -gagürᵘ̈), a musk-rat (W. 115 connects this with onᵘ 1). -kan m. a kind of cake in the shape of a ball made up of rice, etc., and offered by Brāhmans to deceased ancestors, a piṇḍa. -mūrᵘ or anna-mūrᵘ m. a kind of grain-rat, apparently a kind of musk-rat; according to El. (s.v. anamur), a mole. -më̆ṭᵘ̈ or anna-më̆ṭᵘ̈ f. the amount of cooked grain taken into the hand at one time to put into the mouth, a gobbet of rice; hence, met., any small quantity of food, a mere mouthful. -mŏṭh or anna-mŏṭh f. a fistful of grain, such as is given to a beggar in charity; hence, met., a very small quantity of grain. -māyĕ or anna-māyĕ m. the satiety produced in an invalid by eating only a small quantity of food; the satisfaction of an invalid's hunger. -pān m. bread (El.). -prāshun m. the religious ceremony of putting rice into a Hindū child's mouth for the first time. Cf. L. 260.
f. an order, command, used in the following: -mönī f. obeying (mutual) orders, mutual respect; mutual confidence, mutual loyalty. --mānüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to obey orders; to become subject to anyone.

pron. suff. of the 3rd pers. sg. in either the acc. or the ag. case, and added to any finite form of a verb. If the verbal form ends in a vowel, the initial a is dropped. Thus, karān chuh-an, thou makest him; koru-n, made by him, he made. If the verb be in the 3rd person, an in the sense of the acc. is not used, as being substituted, as in suh karān chu-s, not suh karān chu-n, he makes him (Gr.Gr. 185). an is also used to indicate the nom. case, when the nom. represents the object of a transitive verb in a past tense, as in trôwᵘth-an, he was released by thee, thou releasedst him (Gr.M. 1057), so mŏkalôwᵘth-an (Śiv. 3).
a prim. suff. forming the pres. part., as in kar-ān doing (Gr.Gr. 104).

a primary suffix forming abstract nouns from certain verbal roots. In the case of three verbs whose roots end in ĕ (viz., chyonᵘ, to drink; khyonᵘ, to eat; and hyonᵘ, to place) the initial a is dropped, and the abstract noun is masc. Thus, cĕn, drinking. In the case of the other verbs with which this suff. is used, the abs. noun is fem. A list of these verbs will be found in Gr.Gr. 120 ff.
a sec. suff. added to some few words, giving an adjectival force with a bad sense, as dand, a tooth, dandān, having an ugly tooth (Gr.Gr. 137).
anī 1, anas, or anan, a secondary suff. added pleonastically to adverbs of place (see Gr.Gr. 155).
m. the name of a certain coin or sum of money, an anna.
adv. at a (certain) time, only used -˚, as in tami-āna, at that time.
adj. c.g. without beginning, existing from eternity (L.V. 72).
m. disrespect, contempt, rudeness offered to one to whom respect is due.
m. the Limitless Word, a mystic N. of the Deity in Yōga philosophy (Śiv. 1656).

or anum, in the following compounds. -nĕnam or anum-nĕnum adv. without due regard to proportion, unthriftily, uneconomically, without considering exact quantities, u.w. vbs. of giving, bringing, etc., giving without considering whether the gift is excessive or too little. -nĕnam-pöṭhⁱ, anum-nĕnum pöṭhⁱ, -nĕnam-pöṭhin, or anum-nĕnum-pöṭhin adv. id.
m. the occurrence of an opportunity, the right moment for doing anything, an opportunity; intentness, attention applied to any work.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ananôwᵘ) (this verb is classed by native grammarians as the caus. of yunᵘ, to come; it is really the caus. of anun 2, to bring, see Gr.Gr. 171), to cause to bring, to cause another to convey, to get brought.

m. happiness, joy, pleasure, delight; ecstatic bliss, rapture (Śiv. 15, 21, 182, 195, etc.); rest, leisure (cf. K.Pr. 187). ānanda-gan  adj. c.g. consisting of pure joy, all rapture through and through (of saints) (Śiv. 102). -sān, quietly (El.).
adj. c.g. endless, as subst. (voc. ananta), N. of Śiva (Śiv. 931).
f. the name of a certain goddess; a certain image made of boiled rice, and after consecration worshipped at the śrāddha ceremony.
f. a certain kind of boil, described as having a small white opening, and as being hard, not small, round, and very painful.
m. not eating, starvation, fasting, from famine, sickness, poverty, anxiety, or on account of a fast.
f. freedom from flurry, composure, coolness, imperturbability.

m. (sg. dat. anatas), an ornament used as an amulet, made of string formed of kuśa-grass, and worn in the sacrificial thread after the sacrificial ceremony of the anta-ʦŏdāh festival, q.v.; an armlet of silver or gold worn by men on the right arm; an ornament, usually of gold, worn by Brāhmaṇ women on the left ear.
m. one without a master, hence an orphan, a fatherless person (Śiv. 987, 1751); a poor man, one in evil plight (Gr.M.).

m. the name of a pargana of Kashmīr in the Division of Marāz. It is also called Islāmābād, after the chief town of the division, and Islāmābād itself is also called Anathnāg. The word is said to mean endless springs, the ancient name being Anantanāga (El.). Cf. RT.Tr. II, 466, and Śiv. 1162.
m. selflessness, ignorance of the nature of self (Śiv. 1850).
m. (f. anawüñᵘ̈), one who brings (K.Pr. 13); cf. anun 2.
a prim. suff. giving the force of the past conj. part. negatived, as in kar-anay, not having made. With roots ending in vowels, the initial a is dropped, as in ni-nay, not having taken (Gr.Gr. 111).
f. a present of fruit, such as walnuts and other things, sent to a woman's father's house by her father-in-law, on the occasion of her giving birth to a child.

m. either end or edge of any inanimate thing; the end or limit (of a person's greatness, existence, majesty, etc.) (Śiv. 46, 97); a boundary, limit (L. 458); the end, conclusion, or termination of any action or condition; adv. to the end, right through to the end in due order (Śiv. 120); in various idioms noted below the word 'end' is extended to mean the outer end, the exterior. Cf. anta and önth. -borᵘ m. nearness to a conclusion, getting near the end. -gŏḍ m. the end and the beginning, the beginning and the end, the alpha and omega of anything. --hĕth -- lit. having taken the end; hence, as an adv., from the beginning, from the first. -pĕṭh adv. lit. on the outside, the converse of gara-pĕṭh, q.v. under gara. Used with reference to a bride being made over to her husband's house, as contrasted with a son-in-law who lives with the bride in her parents' house. --wātun -- m.inf. to arrive at the end, to be successfully concluded; to conclude a long and successful life. ¶ ȧndⁱ adv. on the edge, outside (YZ. 40). -ȧndⁱ adv. round and round outside, as in -ȧndⁱ bīṭhⁱ yĕgyĕs they were seated round the sacrifice (Śiv. 78), -ȧndⁱ pakun or -ȧndⁱphērun, to walk ceremonially round any person or thing, keeping him or it to the right hand, as a token of reverence (cf. YZ. 89). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go outside; hence, of a missile, to miss the mark or, of a person, to act vainly or uselessly (Śiv. 22). --karun -- m.inf. to make outside; to separate from a group or collection; to despise, reject; to abandon. -pȧkhⁱ adv. outside and here, outside and inside; here, there, and everywhere; u.w. vbs. of searching, etc. --thawun --, i.q. anda thawun ab. -wati adv. by an outer way, by another way (usually with the idea of secrecy); u.w. vbs. of going, etc. -wath hë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. to take the outer way, to go away secretly. ¶ andukᵘ adj. (f. andücᵘ̈), of or belonging to the end, final, the last. --and -- m. the end of all, end, e.g. of a row or of a strip of cloth. ¶ anda-kani adv. in the end, at the end, to one side, on the outer side, close by, u.w. vbs. of placing, pointing out, and the like; apart from, free from, devoid of, māyāyĕ anda-kani, free from delusion (Śiv. 422). -kani manz-bāg adv. being on the outer side (to sit) in the middle; (of any action) going off right into the middle of things (cf. K.Pr.12). -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of or belonging to the end, edge, outer side or vicinity. -pĕṭha adv. from the end, as in counting from either end of a row. -pĕṭha önthas-tāñ adv. from one end to the other, from beginning to end, thoroughly, u.w. vbs. of investigating, searching, and the like. --thawun -- m.inf. to place outside, to hide anything away. -wand adv. from beginning to conclusion, u.w. regard to anything implying length, such as a line, a road, or the like; continually, without cessation (of time) (Śiv. 333). ¶ andā-and adv. on the edge (L. 460).
. Here insert a new sub-article. ¶ andas adv. at the end, at the edge (Śiv. 1662).
adj. c.g. blind, i.q. onᵘ 1, q.v. anda-gāsh m. light (i.e. sight) for the blind (Rām. 1103).

m. darkness, want of sunshine or other light; met., tyranny, unjust rule (cf. K.Pr. 126); as a religious tech. term, the darkness of delusion, the conception of sense, egoism (= Sanskrit ahaṁkāra) (Śiv. 3, 18); sinful delusion generally (Śiv. 59, 66, 67).

adv. and postpos. inside, within (Śiv. 766), in (Śiv. 21, 866). As postpos. it governs the dat., e.g., khābas andar, in a dream (YZ. 80); nayi andar, on the plateau (K.Pr. 156); māgas andar, in the month of Māg (Śiv. 590); nētran andar, in the eyes (Śiv. 767). --aʦun -- or --gaʦhun --, to go in, to enter. -kun- adv. to within, u.w. vbs. of placing, etc. -kūṭh m. (sg. dat. -kūṭas, and so on), the name of a village in Kashmīr some 14 miles below Śrīnagar on the left bank of the Vĕth (Jehlam). It is on the site of Jayapura, the ancient capital of King Jayapīḍa, see RT.Tr. iv, 506-11, and II, 479. -nĕbar adv. inside and outside, within and without. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come in, to enter. ¶ ạndᵃra 1 adv. and postpos. from within, from inside; from among (as in one from among several). In K.Pr. 156 it means simply 'inside'. As postpos. it governs the abl. For ạndᵃra 2 see under ạndᵃr. -kanĕn adv. inside, within. -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of or belonging to the inside, internal, interior. -nẹ̆bᵃra adv. from within and from without. ¶ ạndᵃ̇rᵃ̇ adv. from within. -ạndᵃri adv. very private (of a consultation, etc.), secretly between the parties. -ạndᵃrᵃy adv. quite within; very privately. -dam m. the name of a disease in which there is inhibition of the breath in the air passages caused by the morbid accumulation of phlegm; bronchitis, ? asthma. -kinⁱ adv. in the middle, within, inwardly (Śiv. 764); from within, from in. -tam m. darkness of in the middle; hence, fainting, or extreme pain, owing to an internal disease, of which the symptoms are not visible. -ʦūr m. a thief of in the middle; a hidden, incurable, internal disease.
adv. without connexion with, apart from, excluded from.
m. the desired result of any action; an approximation, rough calculation, estimate (Gr.M.).
adj. (f. andüñᵘ̈), fit or worthy to be ended; approaching the conclusion (of a story, action, etc.).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. andyōv), to be ended, concluded; of a lawsuit or dispute, to be decided, settled.

m. (sg. dat. andĕtis), the reciprocal giving in marriage of children, as when two persons have each a son and a daughter, and agree to marry the son of one to the daughter of the other and also the daughter of one to the son of the other.

m. entrail, intestine. Cf. ạndᵃram. Its abl. is ạndᵃra 2, hence the following. For ạndᵃra 1 see under andar. ¶ ạndᵃra-chal f. rupture or exposure of the intestines; lesion of the intestines; ? hernia. -humal adj. c.g. one who is in the habit of offering entrails in sacrifice; hence, met., very mean, miserly. -wã̄ṭh m. the chief organ in the intestine, the main bowel.

m. an intestine, entrail; the intestines, as a whole. Cf. ạndᵃr. -kūṭunᵘ m. a piece of intestine; a portion of the intestines, a gut. -lọ̆ʦhᵘ m. a lump of intestine; hence, a portion of extruded intestine, the extruded intestine in hernia. -lŏʦhürᵘ̈ f. id., but of a smaller lump. -nôrᵘ m. a tubular portion of the intestines.
m. the condition of not being cooked within, of not being cooked through and through; hence, met., indigestion.

adj. (f. ạndᵃrimᵃ), within, internal, inner (cf. K.Pr. 13); met., inner, heartfelt, sincere (of affection) (Gr.M.). The converse is nĕbᵃryumᵃ, q.v. (El. spells this andarum.) --nĕbar karun -- m. to make what is within outside, to turn inside out; to slay by evisceration.
f. the thick darkness of a clouded dark night (Śiv. 1034); clouds or a dust-storm, causing such darkness by day; met., tyranny, injustice. Cf. ö̃dⁱ.
