f. the name of a small district in Kashmīr which formerly comprised the town of Anatnāg (Islāmābād) (q.v.) and the tract immediately to its south and west. See RT.Tr. II, 467. -wörⁱ pulahorᵘ m. a kind of grass-sandals manufactured in the Añĕch District.

m. rice-water, rice-gruel; gruel of any other similar grain (cf. K.Pr. 23). -dāl f. a dish of rice-gruel and cooked pulse. -dām m. as much rice-gruel as is taken into the mouth at one time; hence, fig., a very small amount of it. -dāra m. a thin stream of rice; hence, fig., a very small amount of it. -golᵘ m. as much gruel as will fill the mouth, a mouthful of it. -hanā f. a little rice-gruel. -khorᵘ adj. (f. -khürᵘ̈), brought up on gruel, fed on gruel (of a child, etc.). -khāv adj. c.g. accustomed to eat or making a practice of eating nothing but rice-gruel (e.g. from religious motives). -mŏyā f. a small amount of gruel, a tiny dish of gruel, such as would be given to an invalid. -nôrᵘ m. the drain in a cook-room down which waste rice-water is poured. -nörᵘ̈ f. the sink or receiving-bowl of such a drain. -nyūrᵘ m. a stye in the eye. -phyorᵘ m. (sg. dat. -phĕris), a splash of gruel; met., a very little gruel. -phyūrᵘ m. (sg. dat. -phīris), a very small portion of rice-gruel. -poʦhᵘ m. the foam or froth of rice-water, used as a medicine for fever, etc. -thaph f. coagulated or congealed rice-gruel. -ṭĕkh f. a small circular drop of rice-gruel. -ṭörⁱ m.pl. gruel-eyelids, eyes running with mucus. -ṭôrᵘ adj. (f. -ṭörᵘ̈), afflicted with the above eye-disease.
and üñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, see onᵘ- motᵘ under anun 2.
m. blindness, want of sight (Śiv. 1756); met., unjust rule, injustice, tyranny.
adj. (f. anĕwözᵘ̈), not presented, not given (as an offering to a god, or to a lord, etc.).

m. a limb (not only of a living being but also of a tree, etc.); a member of the body (including such members as eyes, ears, etc.); a relation, a person related by blood, belonging to the same family. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to apply to the body, hence a certain ceremony; when a new garment is procured, the body or appropriate limb is touched by it for the first time at a lucky moment, as a preliminary to bringing it into wear. This is called 'applying them to the body'. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to put on new clothes for the first time, usually applied to putting on one's own body some one else's new clothes, so as to take the newness off them. This wards off the evil eye, etc., from their real possessor. ¶ anga-būz m. food or medicine which makes the limbs stout, nourishing food or medicine, a tonic. -dorᵘ adj. (f. -dürᵘ̈), having firm or strong limbs (generally of men or animals). -dūsh m. a fault or blemish in a person's limb or member of the body, e.g. one-eyedness, which would be, for instance, considered as a blemish in arranging a marriage with a person so afflicted. -hyūnᵘ (fem. -hīñᵘ̈), wanting a limb or limbs, or having a deformed limb or limbs (usually of a human being or of an image). -rāg m. a cosmetic, especially the lac-coloured cosmetic applied to the cheeks, etc., of a bride, rouge. -wôlᵘ m. a small permanent earring fixed for luck in the lobe of the ear, from which larger earrings or other ear-ornaments may be suspended. It is made of gold or silver. -wāṭukh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭakas, and so on), a treatment or medicine which helps to unite a broken limb.
m. granulations of a healing sore or wound. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to begin to granulate, to show signs of healing (of sore or wound).

f.pl. (for anga 1 see under ang 1), a method of ridicule, when a crowd of children or the like shout imitative sounds over and over again at a person. --wuṭhun -- m.inf. or --wuṭhañĕ -- f. pl. inf., to adopt a method of ridicule or abuse employed by low-caste people and the river population when quarrelling and abusing each other; it consists in the disputant twisting up rags into the form of a doll and showing it meaningly to the other (wuṭhun, to twist).

f. a particular astrological period, i.e. when the planet Mars (Maṅgala) is in the twelfth, first, or second sign of the zodiac from the particular sign in which the moon was at the time of the birth of a person; such periods are unlucky for that person.
f. an indecent action, thrusting the finger into a woman's privities; a slang term for swindling.
adj. c.g. English; subst.f. the English language (Gr.M.).
m. (pl. nom. ang ūr, K.Pr. 180), a grape (W. 155).
m. the state or condition of an unmarried person, bachelorhood, maidenhood.
or anahār, a prim. suff. indicating fitness, as in karanhār, fit to be done, khĕnahār, fit to be eaten (Gr.Gr. 129).
m. unfriendliness, malevolence, ill-nature, unkindness; of an action, an ill result, a result which only does harm to the doer, a disappointment.
adj. (sg. dat. an-haharis, and so on; f. an-harishᵘ̈), unwedded, unmarried, (m.) a bachelor, (f.) a maid. Cf. K.Pr. 13.
adj. (f. an-hë̆ʦᵘ̈), unfriendly, malevolent, ill-natured, unkind; of an action, having a result harmful to the doer, disappointing, of evil effect.

(for 1 see an 4), a primary suffix indicating necessity, like the Latin part. in -ndum, as in karanī, it must be made. Added to a root ending in a vowel, the initial a is dropped, as in dinī, it is to be given (Gr.Gr. 111).
m. ignorance, or want of comprehension, of the meaning of anything, failing to understand anything.
adv. like the noise of lamenting and beating breasts, lamentably.
f. want of wish, unwillingness; sg. dat. used as adv., against one's will, unexpectedly (Śiv. 19, 1215).
m. Polygonum bistorta (El.), a creeping plant, from which a drink is prepared with sugar for obstinate colds and hæmorrhages.
m. end, termination, conclusion (El.); completion, accomplishment. --sapadun --, to be completed, finished, accomplished (Gr.M.).
m. a large vessel brimful of anything.
m. Ficus carica and Ficus caricoldes. It is small and wild (El.).
m. an assembly, meeting, company, society (El.).
m. a fabulous bird, the phœnix; a rara avis, something very rare (H. ii, 2, etc.).
adv. word by word, statement by statement, u.w. vbs. of remembering and the like.
m. the hook or goad used in driving an elephant (K. 397).
m. setting one's hand for any purpose to any work, whether that work is being already performed by another or not; ability to understand the purport of any such work, acumen, comprehensive power.
or anörⁱ adj. c.g. unskilful, awkward, clumsy, inexpert; inexperienced, unpractised; ignorant, uncouth.
adj. (f. anümᵘ̈), not bent, not bowed down; not humble, not polite by nature.
adj. (f. anö̃pᵘ̈), not shining, not bright (of jewels, metal vessels, and the like).
f. the condition of one who is without a master, poverty, distress (Gr.M.).
adj. (f. anö̃ṭhᵘ̈), not fruitless, fertile (of seeds and the like); not obstinate, not hard (of character).

m. (sg. dat. añĕṭis), a cooking-pot cover, a saucepan-lid. Cf. K.Pr. 14, where it is spelt anit, and 13, where the sg. dat. is spelt anĕtis. ¶ añë˘ṭᵘ̈ f. (pl. nom. añĕcĕ), a small dish-cover, dim. of the preceding. ¶ añĕcĕ-han f. a small dish-cover or saucepan-lid.
adj. (f. anöwᵘ̈), not cleaned, not polished (of any metal article, etc.).
adj. (f. anöwᵘ̈), nameless, without a name.
adj. c.g. unread, not learned, ignorant (Śiv. 1519).
the first member of the following compound. Cf. and and önth -rostᵘ. adj. (f. -rütshᵘ̈), endless, without end, never ending. Cf. önta-rostᵘ, under.
i.q. antakaran, q.v. (Śiv. 1420) (a borrowed Skt. word).
m. inward workings, i.e. inward meditation (Śiv. 285).
f. N. of a certain magic powder that causes death to him on whom it is cast; hence --chaküñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to scatter this (on a person); met. to cause (his) death (K. 196).
m. that which is within, the inner, or hidden, meaning (of anything) (L.V. 56).
(borrowed from Sansk.), adv. within and without, through and through, entirely (Śiv. 761).
m. the Inner Restrainer, the Inner Monitor, the Supreme Spirit as guiding mankind (K. 718).
f. the festival of the Ananta-caturdaśī, held on the fourteenth day of the light half of the month of Bhādrapada, on which Śēṣa or Ananta, the Serpent of Eternity, is worshipped.

m. (sg. dat. antas) (i.q. and, q.v.), the end, conclusion of anything (Śiv. 1418, 1789; Rām. 1596, 1779). Cf. önth. ¶ anta-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), endless, without end, never ending. Cf. önta-rostᵘ, p. 35b, l. 26. ¶ ȧntⁱ (L.V. 54) or ȧntihⁱ (L.V. 33, 37, 38, 41, 61) in the end, finally, ultimately.
m. perception, understanding, experience. anubawa-bāw m. a condition in which one is capable of experiencing or understanding the merits of any person or thing (Śiv. 75).
m. favour, kindness (Śiv. 885). anugraha interj. show favour! show mercy! (Śiv. 127).
2nd sg. impve. of anun 2, with suffix 3rd pers. sing. acc., 'bring him' or 'bring it', liable to be confounded with anun, the infinitive.

or ānun conj. 1 (1 p.p. onᵘ, f. üñᵘ; 2 p.p. añōv), to bring, convey, fetch (Śiv. 194, 516, 589); to bring, conduct, invite (a person) (Śiv. 72, 89, 154); to bring forward (arguments, etc.); to bring forward, quote, borrow a story (YZ. 239); to bring forward, grant, give (Śiv. 603). tāb anun, to bring forward endurance, to endure (Śiv. 584). --nād dith --, to bring having called out, to call for, summon, send for. ¶ onᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. üñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), brought, conveyed; brought into the house, hence a slave, bondman, servant. añĕ-maʦĕ-hondᵘ ʦônᵘ-motᵘ adj. (f. añĕ-maʦĕ-hünzᵘ̈ ʦöñᵘ̈-mütsᵘ̈), the brought in one (of a bondwoman), i.e. the child of some servant, who has been introduced into a house, but who has no authority comparable with that of the children of the house; hence, met., one unworthy of authority, unfit for exercising authority.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. anyōv), to become blind, become sightless. anyō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. anyē-müʦᵘ̈), become blind, blind, without sight (Rām. 772).
f. the name of the seventeenth out of the twenty-eight nakṣatras, or lunar mansions, Anurādhā.
m. the name of small black fish with a large head. See L. 158, where it is called unyaur.
adj. (f. añūrᵘ̈), one with sight who acts as if he were blind; not careful, not provident.
m. blindness, whether caused by disease or existing from birth, or, temporary, caused by weeping, separation from one's beloved, or the like. ¶ añivⁱlad adj. c.g. afflicted with such blindness.

f. a time, round, bout, period, routine (Śiv. 8, 1160), a turn (as when men move turn and turn about or in turn). --panwār -- f. a reduplication of the foregoing, but less definitely indicating fixed periods of alternation. --wanwār -- f. id.
m. logical connexion; tenor, drift, purport; the real truth (concerning something) (L.V. 59).

f. (sg. dat. anwacĕ), alarming news. anwacĕ pĕñĕ f. pl. inf. the falling of alarming news; hence, to be in terror or panic, to be utterly distraught and panic-stricken through fear. anwacĕ ʦhunañĕ f. pl. inf. to give news calculated to make a person panic-stricken.
etc.; for most words beginning thus, see under añ-, üñ-, etc. Many English writers (including El. & W.) represent ñ by ny.
adj. (f. anë̆ʦᵘ̈), not sheared, unshorn (of a sheep, etc.).
f. the open hands placed side by side and slightly hollowed, a mark of supplication.
f. or anzonᵘ m. a species of rice, producing a white grain, soft and sweet-smelling when cooked. Cf. anzun, and L. 333.
adj. c.g. unknowing, unpractised (in an action or profession) (Śiv. 1733); unknown, unrecognized, a stranger (of a person).
m. a village in the Anatnāg (q.v.) Pargana of Kashmīr, below the temple of Mārtāṇḍa, on the bank of the Lambōdarī River.
f. the first of the four fingers, the index-finger.
f. a hen-swan; a hen-goose; see ünzᵘ̈.

adj. c.g. within and in the middle, in the centre of anything, not nearer one side than the other. Cf. anzyumᵘ-manzyumᵘ. ¶ anza-manza adv. from in the centre, from in the middle, from not nearer one side than the other. anzas-manzas adv., i.q. anz-manz.
m. the border or hem of a cloak, veil, shawl, or mantle, usually woven with a special pattern.
m. a kind of white rice, cf. anzan.
adj. (f. anzimᵘ̈-manzimᵘ̈), middling, mediocre, neither good nor bad; cf. anz-manz.
f. finishing, completion; decision (of a dispute, etc.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ạnzᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. ạnzᵃrun, q.v. ạnzᵃrāwonᵃ fut. p.p. (f. ạnzᵃrāwüñᵃ), i.q. ạnzᵃronᵃ, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ạnzᵒrᵒ), to finish or conclude (a dispute, story, etc.); to decide, conclude (a dispute or law-case). ¶ ạnzᵃronᵃ fut. p.p. (f. ạnzᵃrüñᵃ), fit to be finished; fit to be decided.
f. the last rites, the funeral sacrifice and ceremonies.
f. a virgin, an unblemished maiden.
adv. without recognizing, without heeding, without discrimination, u.w. vbs. of taking, etc.
f. a calamity, misfortune, esp. a public calamity, such as a flood, a drought, a plague, or the like; misfortune, ill-fortune (Gr.M.).
m. ridicule, derision, esp. with regard to an unfounded report, as when a report spreads abroad that a woman is pregnant, and nothing happens.
m. a certain kind of grape, considered to be the best of all (K.Pr. 43, W. 144, and El. s.v. dach).
adj. (f. apạjᵘ̈rᵘ̈), (of clothes in the making) half-sewn, not permanently sewn, tacked together.
m. causing injury, causing wrong, oppression; doing ill to one to whom gratitude is due, ill-requital.
m. disrespect, contempt (shown to some one worthy of respect).
m. one of the five life-winds in the body, which goes downwards and out at the anus (L.V. 101, Śiv. 1682). See prān 1 for particulars.
f. (sg. dat. apanöyüʦᵘ̈, and so on), treating as one's own, showing affection for any person or thing as if he or it were closely connected with oneself.
adj. c.g. transcending, infinite, a N. of the Deity (Śiv. 1659).
m. a fault, offence, transgression (Śiv. 1726); sin, vice.
f. (sg. dat. āparüñᵘ̈, and so on), the putting a morsel or gobbet of food into another person's mouth; hence, insistence upon giving an unwilling person some work.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. āparôwᵘ), to feed another person, to put food into the mouth of another person (e.g. an invalid or a child).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. āporᵘ), to feed another person with one's own hand as a token of hospitality (Śiv. 45, 1151); to put food into the mouth of another person (e.g. a helpless invalid, or a child).
m. the name of a certain disease, ? bleeding piles. Cf. apāʦukᵘ.
f. (sg. dat. āpüʦᵘ̈, and so on), a calamity, misfortune (Gr.M. 263). Cf. āphath.
m. a nonsensical, absurd, or preposterous speech, gibberish. -mapatrọ̆kᵘ m. gibberish and that kind of thing (a rhyming repetition of the preceding).
m. the time between the complete consumption of the old crop and the ripening of the new, the early autumn.
m. loss of reputation, disgrace, infamy.
m. untruthfulness, untrust worthiness, disloyalty to a promise.
m. (sg. dat. apȧzⁱyöris, abl. apȧzⁱyāri; f. sg. nom. apȧzⁱyārĕñ, dat. apȧzⁱyārĕñĕ), a liar, either habitually or on an occasion. Cf. K.Pr. 103.
m. (sg. dat. apāʦakis, but ag. and pl. nom. apāʦᵃ̇kᵃ̇), the bloody stools of dysentery; hence, dysentery. Cf. apās.
m. ignorance, want of skill; ignobility, lowness of degree, smallness of consideration; being ignorantly satisfied with too small a result from or reward for one's labour.
m. the condition of being unsplit or unbroken (of any article of wood, metal, or the like).
or āpharīn (Rām. 706, 792) interj. may there be applause! be thou praised (Śiv. 655).
m.pl. a hasty disposition, the disposition of doing things at once without reflection, precipitancy, impetuosity. aphari-thaphari adv. hastily, precipitately, impetuously, headlong, slapdash.
f. (sg. dat. āphüʦᵘ̈), a disaster, misfortune, calamity (Gr.M. 1165). Cf. āpath.
reported, rumoured, a report, a rumour (Gr.M.).
adj. (m. sg. dat. aphŏlis; f. sg. nom. aphö̆jᵘ̈, dat. aphŏjĕ), not expanded, not blossomed (of a bud or flowering tree); not blossoming (of a plant which does not bear blossoms).
adj. (m. sg. dat. aphalis; f. sg. nom. aphüjᵘ̈, dat. aphajĕ), (of clothes, etc.) not worn out; unworn, new.
adj. (m. sg. dat. aphönis, abl. aphāni; f. sg. nom. aphöñᵘ̈, dat. aphāñĕ), not made entirely void; (of a person) not utterly deprived of wealth; (of a vessel, etc.) not entirely emptied.
adj. (m. sg. dat. aphaṭis; f. sg. nom. aphüṭᵘ̈, dat. aphacĕ), not split, not broken (of anything made of wood, metal, etc.).
adv. destroyed and then scattered abroad, flung to the winds.
f. tiny pieces of gold-leaf scattered over paper, etc., as an ornament (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. pressed, squeezed out; friendless, without helper, destitute, without support (Rām. 772).

adj. (m. sg. dat. aphukis; f. sg. nom. aphucᵘ̈, dat. aphucĕ), of a stove or the like, not having the fire lit up (whether supplied with fuel or not) by blowing with the mouth used as a bellows; not set alight, 'cold.'
adj. (m. sg. dat. aphuṭis; f. sg. nom. aphuṭᵘ̈, dat. aphucĕ), (of a vessel, etc., made of earthenware, metal, etc.) not broken; not breakable, not fragile.
adj. (m. sg. dat. aphyöris, abl. aphyāri; f. sg. nom. aphyörᵘ̈, dat. aphyārĕ), not strained, not passed through a sieve.
f. an appeal in the law-courts (the English word) (Gr.M.).
adj. (m. dat. apakis; f. sg. nom. apücᵘ̈, dat. apachĕ), (of food) not cooked, not fully cooked; (of food already eaten) not digested, not fully digested.
adj. (m. sg. dat. apökis, abl. apāki; f. sg. nom. apöcᵘ̈, dat. apācĕ), uncooked (of food, etc.); badly cooked.
adj. (m. sg. dat. apŏlis; f. sg. nom. apö̆jᵘ̈, dat. apŏjĕ), not slack, firm, strong; strong, accustomed to carry burdens; strong in an argument, strong in a war of words.
adj. (m.sg. dat. apapis; f. sg. nom. apüpᵘ̈, dat. apapĕ), unripe (of fruits, crops, etc.).

adj. (m. sg. dat. apörimis, f. sg. nom. apörimᵘ̈), of or belonging to the far side or shore of anything (e.g. of a river, mountain, or the like), of or belonging to that direction as opposed to this direction. Cf. K.Pr. 15.

adj. (m. sg. dat. aparis; f. sg. nom. apürᵘ̈, dat. aparĕ), illiterate, uneducated. apȧrⁱ-achar m.pl. unread letters, hence the acquirement of knowledge without literary study; knowledge not acquired from book-learning.

or apōr (Rām. 1590) m. (sg. dat. apöris, ag. apörⁱ, abl. apāri), the opposite or far side of anything (e.g. of a river, a mountain, or the like); that direction as opposed to this direction. --tarun -- m.inf. to cross over to the far side, to cross (Śiv. 245). -yĕpôrᵘ m. the far side and the near side, the far shore and the near shore. Cf. K.Pr. 14, 240. ¶ apārĕ, i.q. apāri, q.v. (Śiv. 968). ¶ apāri adv. on the other side. -kani adv. to on the other side, on the other side (with verbs of placing, etc.). -kanyukᵘ adj. (m. sg. dat. -kanikis; fem. sg. nom. -kanicᵘ̈), of or belonging to the far or opposite side. -yĕpāri adv. on the far side and on this side, on the far shore and on the near shore. -yĕpôrᵘ adv. from the far side to the near side, from the far shore to the near shore. ¶ apörⁱ adv. from the far side (Śiv. 1460); from that direction as opposed to this direction. -kinⁱ adv. from the direction of the far side. --tārun -- m.inf. to bring over from the other side (K.Pr. 14). -yĕpörⁱ adv. from that side and from this side, from all sides. -yĕpörⁱ-kinⁱ adv. from the direction of the far side and of this side (with verbs of inquiry and the like).
adj. c.g. (as subst., m. sg. dat. apŏtras), sonless.
adj. (m. sg. dat. apayis; f. sg. nom. apüyᵘ̈, dat. apayĕ), not heated or roasted (of metals), not baked (of bricks).

m. (sg. dat. apazis), a lie, a false statement, a falsehood (Śiv. 765). Also adj. (f. apüzᵘ̈, dat. apazĕ), false, untrue; incorrect, erroneous (for m. sg. dat. cf. K.Pr. 15) (Gr.M.). -bāpār m. a course of conduct, business or trade conducted dishonestly. --dapun -- m.inf. to speak falsely, to lie, to tell lies (El.). -mapozᵘ m. a thoroughly and totally false course of conduct, practice, or action. -pozᵘ m. a mixture of falsehood and truth, a romance founded on fact. --wanun -- m.inf. to tell lies, to lie (El.). --wananwôlᵘ -- m. a speaker of lies, a liar (El.). ¶ apȧzⁱ-bāpār m. the conduct or practice of untruthful persons, the kind of conduct you would expect from liars. ¶ apozwāh-mapozwāh m. (with the suff. āh indicating the indefinite article), a mixture of truth and falsehood, in most parts true, but with some falsity. ¶ apüzᵘ̈ driy f. a false oath, perjury (El.).
m. non-manifestness, the non-display or non-declaration of some glory, fame, quality, or condition.
adj. (m. sg. dat. aprạkhᵃṭis; f. sg. nom. aprạkhᵘ̈ṭᵘ̈, dat. aprạkhᵃcĕ), not manifest, not famous; hidden, concealed.
adj. c.g. not pleased, displeased, dissatisfied: chhus tihandis sangas aprasan, I dislike their company (Gr.M.).
adj. (m. sg. dat. apröṭis, abl. aprāṭi; f. sg. nom. apröṭᵘ̈, dat. aprācĕ), not dug, not dug up, not mined.
adj. (m. sg. dat. aprayis; f. sg. nom. aprüyᵘ̈, dat. aprayĕ), (of a living being) not loved (even though deserving love), unloved; (of an inan. object) not pleasing, unpleasant.
adj. (m. sg. dat. aprinzis, f. sg. nom. aprinzᵘ̈), not sent, not dispatched, not deputed for any work.
m. an officer (corruption of the English word) (H. x, 12).
adj. (m. sg. dat. apuʦanis; fem. sg. nom. apuʦüñᵘ̈, dat. apuʦañĕ), not picked to pieces (leaf by leaf) (of flowers).
f. any oblation offered for the satisfaction of the gods or deceased ancestors (Śiv. 1430).

m. compassion, mercy, pity (K.Pr. 95; Śiv. 6, 129, 168, 192, 948; YZ. 486, 568); meanness, a mean action, a shameful act (K.Pr. 247; cf. W. 135). ¶ āra-barutᵘ adj. (f. -barᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), compassionate, merciful, whether by nature or owing to some special accidental cause. --gōmotᵘ -- adj. (f. -gōmüʦᵘ̈), gone to pity, a subject of pity (YZ. 39). -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), smitten with compassion, pitiful. -krỗtᵘ adj. (f. -krö̃ʦᵘ̈), smitten by compassion; smitten by some pain, etc., which excites compassion; worthy of compassion, in a condition which excites a feeling of tenderness (e.g. a sleeping infant). -kᵒtᵒ adj. (f. -kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), of a compassionate nature; deserving of compassion (Śiv. 113, 1473). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), void of compassion, merciless (Śiv. 334, 943), either by nature or for some special reason.

adj. c.g. helpless, without resource (owing to poverty, sickness, or the like). -dachĕ f.pl. the persistent and constant troubling of somebody in order to procure the achievement of some purpose; selfish worrying. ¶ ara anun m.inf. to cause distress to anyone directly or indirectly, mentally or physically.
in ar karun m.inf. to root up, pull up by the roots, pull up from the ground. Cf. arra.
m. a saw (Śiv. 1776). -kash m. (f. -kash bāy, his wife), a sawyer whose profession it is to cut logs into planks. L. 463 (arikash). Cf. ara 1 and ürᵘ̈ 3.

m. a secondary suffix which, added to adjectives, forms abstract nouns. It is added to the m. sg. abl. of the adjective, the final i of which becomes y. This y, with the initial a of the suffix, usually becomes ĕ. The presence of the y also causes certain changes in the final consonant of the base. Thus, popᵘ, ripe, m. sg. abl. papi, hence papĕr, ripeness; but nyukᵘ, little, m. sg. abl. niki, hence nicĕr, littleness. ¶ Some adjectives of three or more syllables take ār instead of ar. Thus wŏzulᵘ, red, wŏzajyār, redness. ¶ For further particulars see Gr.Gr. 138 ff.

m. the action of moving up and down of a saw, when cutting logs into planks; the act of such sawing, sawing (Śiv. 167). Cf. ar 3 and ürᵘ̈ 3. -aḍāv m. the wooden framework for supporting a log of wood when being sawn. -cīr m. the pulling of a saw up or down. -koshᵘ m. sawdust. -litᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a large saw (for cutting logs into planks) --wālañĕ-- inf. f. pl. to saw in piees or into planks.
m. the act of encircling, surrounding, enclosing; standing in a circle (of a number) of people (Śiv. 947); a necklace (K.Pr. 143). Cf. āru and örᵘ̈ 3.
m. the raising of any heavy object, such as a rock or a log of wood, with the aid of temporary supports, levers, or the like.

m. a rocky river, a hill-stream, or the like (Śiv. 948, 1638); the head-stream of a large river (Śiv. 1075). -bal m. the ground near a hill-stream. -göḍᵘ̈ f. a certain fish found in rapid hill-streams. -grazun m. the noise made by the water of a rocky, rapid hill-stream; met. any such noise. -hiy f. a kind of jasmine which grows by such hill-streams. -küñᵘ̈ f. the round stones or rocks found in the bed of a hill-stream. -pal m., id. -path f. land or fields situated, like an island, in the bed of a mountain stream. -pạthᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a village or collection of hamlets in such an island. -wal f. a kind of wild rose with a yellow blossom (cf. El.) (Śiv. 55, 469, 948, 1611). -wôñᵘ m. the water of a mountain stream. -wara adj. c.g. like a hill-stream, i.e., impetuous, twisted, and washing away what lies in its course; hence, of character, impetuous, crooked, and destructive of all that comes in the way.

f.pl. the hair of the border of the scalp, the border hair of the forehead. -kāsañĕ inf. f. pl. to shave the hair of the forehead, a ceremony performed upon brāhmaṇ youths on the final return home of a student from his preceptor.
m. throwing again and again, as stones to form an embankment; a bombardment, a continuous volley of cannon or musketry.
adj. c.g. Arabian, as in -gurᵘ m. an Arab horse, a horse of Arab strain.
f. adoration, worship, homage. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to worship (Gr.M.).
the form which aradāh takes in multiplication, as in zᵃh aradöhⁱ shĕyĕtrᵃh, two eighteens (are) thirty-six.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ārodᵘ, f. ārüzᵘ̈; 2 p.p. ārazôv), to worship, adore, pay homage to (esp. in order to obtain something), to conciliate; to make happy, entreat hospitably (K.Pr. 126).
m. a flaw or irregularity in the arrangement of the threads as set for weaving.
m. the pole or beam of a plough.
f. (sg. dat. aralöʦᵘ̈), a general term for a quantity of money, garments, rice, etc., collected together for distribution in charity or as free gifts.
f. a molar tooth, a double tooth. ¶ armi-chal f. a broken fragment of a molar tooth. -mūl m. the root or fang of a molar tooth.
m. a place for repose, a home of rest (Śiv. 1274).
m. peace, rest, repose. Cf. Gr.M. and K.Pr. 80.
m. commencement, beginning. -karun m.inf. to begin, commence (Gr.M.).
m. greatness, whether owing to high rank or wealth. Cf. aratöjih 2.

in the following. --kāṭh -- m. the piece of wood used for kindling fire by attrition for sacrificial purposes. -ruth m. a certain ceremony at the investing of a youth of a twice-born caste with the Brahmanical cord (yajñōpavīta).
adv. from one end to the other, completely, entirely, without a break. Cf. ar-war and ōr 1.
m.pl. procrastination, dilatoriness; hesitation, inability to make up one's mind (Śiv. 1750).
f. (sg. dat. arasīʦᵘ̈), bootless exertion, efforts great but in vain. Cf. arsēth.
adj. c.g. wearied with long-continued exertions; one accustomed or fond of attempting difficult or impossible tasks.

m. (sg. dat. arātas), nightfall, but not full night, evening. Cf. onᵘ. ¶ arātan adv. by evening-time, at even, not till evening; generally of something which should be commenced in the daytime, but which is delayed till evening; hence, after considerable delay. -bögⁱ adv. by nearly evening, by about evening (u.w. vbs. signifying arrival or the like).
m. greatness, whether owing to high rank or wealth. Cf. aram-töjy.
f. (sg. dat. arawüñᵘ̈), the act of roughening a grindstone or the like; see ārawun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ārowᵘ), to make rough, to roughen (u.w. ref. to grindstones, millstones, etc., which have worn smooth).
m. a chief or head, lord, possessor (El.).
m. a certain disease, the symptoms of which are tumours on the loins. It is described as difficult to cure.
m. a neck-shackle, a chain worn on the neck by a prisoner.
m. the name of an implement for digging, described as having a wooden handle and a wedge-shaped point, ? a spud or hoe.
f. the setting out of a forerunner, i.e. of the attendant who runs in front of his master's conveyance (derived from the next).
m. a forerunner, an attendant who runs before his master's conveyance (a corruption of the English 'orderly').
m. the lord who is half a woman, N. of Śiva in his bisexual form (Śiv. 974).
m. midnight (El., who spells it arda-rāt).
. This word also occurs in Rām. 1108g. In Rām. 1265 we have arda-rātran, adv. at midnight.
adj. c.g. possessing half a body, N. of Pārvatī or Śiva, as one-half of the conjoint bisexual form of Śiva-Pārvatī (Śiv. 114).
adv., onomat., plump, crash, bang, with the noise caused by a heavy body falling from a height.
m. good condition, soundness (of things); good health, health, healthiness (of animate creatures). Cf. Gr.M. -darĕr m. good condition and strength; good health and strength.

m. a well-known perfume compounded of several scented ingredients, such as kakkōla, aloes, musk, and camphor. Another formula gives saffron, aloes, musk, camphor, and sandal. The Sanskrit name is yakṣa-kardama.
(?) m. a person whose father is a Kāshmīrī but whose mother is not (El., q.v. for further particulars).
adv. at the wrong time, at an inauspicious time (u.w. vbs. of going, etc.).

f. a certain kind of yellow jasmine. ariñĕ-pōsh (or) m. its flower (Śiv. 54). -raṅg m. the colour of the yellow jasmine, yellow; esp. when the colour is not natural but is acquired owing to ill-health, or to becoming decayed.
f. high estimation, high repute (on the score of wealth, learning, family, rank, or the like).
f. a certain disease, piles, hæmorrhoids.
[?], the name of the first khushābā or process of weeding and working the young rice-plant (L. 463, where it is spelt aree-ʦar; cf. also 327).
m.pl. pillars, columns. arkān-i-dōlath (= ارکانِ دولت) m.pl. 'pillars of the State', grandees, nobles (Rām. 142).

m. the name of a certain tree, Rhus acuminata (Śiv. 1062); it grows in the hills, and blisters the hand that holds it. The branches of this tree droop like the weeping ash (El.). Cf. ar-khŏr and L. 76, 79, and (for its poisonous properties) 82. In 79 L. calls it Rhus Wallichii.
m. misconduct, misbehaviour; esp. of children, naughtiness.
adj. c.g. one who misconducts himself, one who is guilty of misbehaviour; esp. of children, naughty.
f. the name of the vowel ū, when non-initial, represented in the Śāradā character by the sign. Cf. ar-mǖnthᵃr.
m. longing, hankering, solicitude, eager desire for something not yet obtained (K.Pr. 13; Śiv. 160, 430, 706, 1655); disappointment, unsatisfied longing.
m. the name of the letter ṭa used in schools.
adv. for the sake of religion, as an act of piety (u.w. vbs. of giving and the like).
f. the name of the vowel ī, when non-initial, represented in the Śāradā character by the sign. Cf. ar-khǖrᵘ̈.
adj. c.g. presumptuous, ignorantly ready to undertake a task for which one has no qualifications or which one has not attempted to understand.
adj. c.g. ignorantly presumptuous, rashly undertaking a task with bad results.
m. (sg. dat. ārōgĕs, and so on), good health, freedom from disease, health (Gr.M.).
adj.(f. arünjᵘ̈), not coloured, not dyed (of cloth, etc.).
adj. (f. arüsᵘ̈), juiceless, sapless; (of a literary composition) dry, insipid.
m. a present, offering (Śiv. 169, 192, 984, 1620, 1640); -˚ as an offering to, hence out of love for (Śiv. 1697).
m. throwing or pushing down from a height.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. arpôwᵘ), to throw down; to fell, esp. (of an illness) to floor a person, to render him utterly incapacitated.
m. a vigil or wake kept on the night preceding the 'īd festival of the Musalmāns.
conj. 1 to offer (an oblation, or the like) (K. 138, 141).
m. the act of pulling, lifting, or rooting up something heavy, such as a rock or a post fixed in the ground; a lever or other implement for raising such.
m. (sg. dat. arsātas), distress owing to poverty, the possession of only very narrow means; met. incurring great trouble or difficulty.
f. (sg. dat. arsīʦᵘ̈), great exertion, great efforts directed towards some object either very difficult to obtain or impossible of attainment. Cf. arasēth.

m. the heaven, the sky. Its ablative and dative are used in the following phrases: arshĕ pyonᵘ m.inf. to fall from heaven, used of a sudden and unexpected downfall from a high position, power, or wealth. --wasun -- m.inf. to descend from heaven, of some sudden and unexpected piece of fortune, whether good or bad. ¶ arshĕs-khasun m.inf. to mount to heaven, to be filled with pride or conceit, owing to the attainment of some quality or of wealth, etc.
adj. c.g. accustomed to use great exertions, esp. at some impossible task.
adj. c.g. very stout, very fat; hence, foolish. Cf. alsrēṭh. -hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -hishᵘ̈), like one who is very fat and clumsy, a perfect fool.
f. leaf or foil of gold, silver, or mixed metal. Eaten as a medicine, as well as used for ornamentation.
m. (sg. dat. arthas), meaning, purport; aim, object, purpose riches, worldly prosperity (Śiv. 1798).
adv. that is to say, videlicet (Gr.M.).
or ārᵃtī f. a special kind of address to a god in which praise is mingled with petitions for graciousness, a litany (Śiv. 740, 1318).
m. the standing of a number of people in a circle; a circle of people. Cf. āra 1 and örᵘ̈ 3.
f. the spare cloth remaining beyond the seam when, in making clothes, two pieces of cloth are sewn together, which is only fit to be pared off and thrown away.
m. (dat. arunas), the dawn-god, the dawn.
f. the star Alcor, considered as the consort of the seven ṛĕshis or the Great Bear (Śiv. 638, 686); also N. of the wife of the saint Vasiṣṭha (Śiv. 676).
adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. arṻpas), formless, without form (Śiv. 1757).

adj. (f.aruvᵘ̈), not transplanted, not planted out (of cultivated plants, such as rice, which are grown in seed-beds and then transplanted); self-sown (of wild plants, which have grown up without such planting out).
f. (sg. dat. arūʦi), disgust, want of appetite.
adj. (sg. dat. arūʦis, but pl. dat. arōʦĕn, ag. pl. arōʦyau; fem. sg. nom. arūʦᵘ̈, dat. arōtsĕ, and so throughout), unpleasing, disagreeable (e.g. food, ornaments, expressions, etc.).

adv. from that side and from this; hence, of an indefinite area, of indefinite extent. Cf. āra-pôrᵘ and ōr 1. ¶ ara-war adv. from the far side to this side, on the whole, entirely, (of something long) from one end to the other.
f. the earth; arz ō samā ارض و سما f. earth and the heavens (i.e. everywhere) (H. vii, 26).
m. Panicum miliaceum (El.). Cf. Persian ارزن.
f. (sg. dat. arzüʦᵘ̈ and so on), earnings, gain, profit. Cf. Gr.Gr. 128.
f. a respectful representation, a written petition (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. very useless, of no use for any particular purpose. Cf. Persian ارزانی cheapness.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. orzᵘ), to earn, acquire, get, gain.
m. a proper N., Arjuna, one of the heroes of the Mahābhārata (Śiv. 739, 1734).
f. worship, adoration (of a deity) Siv. 1162).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. orʦᵘ; 2 p.p. arʦōv), to worship, adore.

m. (sg. dat. argas, and so on, exc. pl. nom.), unhusked rice or barley offered to a god, etc., at the time of worship, etc. -pōsh m. grains and flowers similarly offered. ¶ arga-pholᵘ m. a small offering of such grains, a few of such grains; also, a general term for the grains offered, whether few or great. -ʦāl m. a handful of such grain in the act of being offered (Śiv. 662).
m.pl. (dat. arᵃhākan), small, round bits of wood broken off timber floating down a river or the like.
m. (sg. dat. arᵃhaṭas), the 'Persian wheel', an endless string of earthen pots attached to a revolving wheel over a well, which go down empty and return full, and tilt the water into a trough.

m. a market gardener, a kitchen gardener, a man who keeps a garden for his livelihood. His wife is called āramĕñ. Cf. K.Pr. 13, where the sg. ag. ārᵃ̇mᵃ̇ is written ārimi. -gŏgᵃjĕ f.pl. a kind of red turnip cultivated by market gardeners, and sweeter than the ordinary kind. -hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), a superior kind of green vegetable or spinach grown by market gardeners. -hand f. a kind of Cichorium grown by market gardeners, and much esteemed as a vegetable. -wörᵘ̈ f. the garden of a market gardener (well cultivated as compared with ordinary gardens).
adv. everywhere, universal (u.w. vbs. indicating fame, repute, etc.).

m. a representation, petition, request (Śiv. 880). --karun -- m.inf. to make a representation, represent, submit, state humbly; to make a request, to make an application (Gr.M.). This word is masc. in Kāshmīrī, although fem. in Hindōstānī (W. 18).
adj. (f. arᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), not good, bad (either in character or in appearance), no good (of a sentient being); useless, no good for any specific purpose (of an inan. obj.).
adv. yes (El., who spells the word áṅs).
pron. suff. of 1st pers. sing. nom. After a vowel the initial a is elided. Thus, karyōn-as I (as) was made by him; poku-s I went (Gr.Gr. 183).
the same as ös, q.v. This is the spelling of K.Pr., e.g. pp. 145, 171, 248.

card. c.g. (borrowed from Sanskrit), eight. The eight siddhis (Śiv. 115, 519) are the eight supernatural powers acquired by Yōgins. The ashṭa-dala hṛĕday (Śiv. 519), or eight-leaved heart, is the name of a mystic diagram used in the worship of Shiva. The ashṭa-mūrti (Śiv. 519), or eight forms of Shiva, are the five elements, the sun, the moon, and the sacrificing priest. Eight forms of Shiva are classed as Bhairavas (Śiv. 986). Cf. börav.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. osᵘ; 2 p.p. asōv), to laugh (K.Pr. 48). In the past tenses this verb is construed impersonally. Thus, osu-m, it was laughed by me, I laughed; osu-n, he or she laughed; osᵘ, we laughed, and so on. ¶ asun m. a laugh (K.Pr. 260, Śiv. 788). Its abl. is asana, as in the following. ¶ asana-hanā f. a small laugh, a smile. --karüñᵘ̈ --, to smile (Gr.M.). ¶ asān-asān pres. part., laughing, laughing; hence, as adv., cheerfully, happily, joyfully, and met., very quickly, speedily (Śiv. 899, 917). ¶ ȧsⁱ-ȧsⁱ conj. part. laughing, laughing; hence, as adv., joyfully, quickly, speedily.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. ôsᵘ, pl. ösⁱ; f. ösᵘ̈, pl. āsa 2; 2 p.p. āsyōv is not used), (lit.) to sit; hence, to remain, continue, abide (Śiv. 1832); to be, to become (passim). The past tense is employed as the ordinary past tense of the verb substantive. Thus, ôsus, I was. Similarly, for all other tenses except the present, 'I am' being chhus. The present of this verb indicates condition. Thus, suh chhuh yiʦhanwôlᵘ āsān indicates that he is not only eager, but that he is in a general condition of eagerness (so Śiv. 90, 1040). ¶ The verb is also employed as an auxiliary, like the Hindōstānī thā or hōnā; thus it forms an imperfect, as in suh ôsᵘ karān, he was doing; a pluperfect tȧmⁱ ôsᵘ korᵘ-motᵘ, he had done, and other tenses, such as suh āsi karān (wŏh jāntā hōgā), he is probably doing, hargāh bŏh karān āsahö (agar maĩ karta hōtā), had I been doing, or yĕduwai mĕ āsihē korᵘ-motᵘ (agar maĩ-nē kiyā hōtā), had I done. As a verb substantive it often governs a dative of possession, then meaning 'to have'. Thus, mĕ āsi or āsĕ-m, there will be to me, I shall have; mĕ ôsᵘ or ôsu-m, I had. Gr.M., K.Pr. 114, YZ. 245. ¶ This verb has a benedictive mood, which is thus conjugated: sg. 2, āshĕkh, mayst thou be; pl. 2, āshiv, sg. and pl. 3, āshĕn (Śiv. 188, 940). ¶ In poetry the pres. part. is sometimes āsan or āsana, instead of āsān (e.g. Śiv. 1040, 1724). ¶ āsun-bāsun m.inf. being and appearance, or possibly a jingling repetition of āsun; hence, a person's possessions, property. ¶ āsan-wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), wealthy, having great possessions.

pron. dem. that (within sight or pointed to), this, both substantive and adjective. It is commonly referred to the pronoun huh, q.v., and is defective. It has no nominative, the word ath being the dative singular inanimate. It has three genders--(1) masculine animate, (2) feminine animate, and (3) inanimate (whether masc. or fem.). In most forms the masc. an. and the fem. an. are the same. When this is the case the form will be indicated simply by 'an.' The following forms occur: dat. sg. an. amis (Śiv. 809 m., 874 f.); inan. ath (Śiv. 47, 929); gen. sg. an. ȧmⁱ-sondⁱ (Śiv. 806), or asondᵘ (Śiv. 803, 813); inan. amyukᵘ (Śiv. 69); ag. masc. an. ȧmⁱ (Śiv. 45); fem. ami (Śiv. 91); inan. ȧmⁱ (Śiv. 46); abl. an. and inan. ami. No plural forms have been noted, nor any for the nom. sing. For the missing forms the corresponding forms of huh are employed. With emphatic y, ath becomes ȧthⁱ (Śiv. 1754), ȧmⁱ becomes ȧmiy (Śiv. 803), and ami becomes amiy (Śiv. 648). When this pronoun is used as an adjective there are some variations in the declension. When agreeing with an animate feminine noun the dative is ami, not amis, which is the dative of the pronoun when referring as a substantive to any animate noun, whether masc. or fem. Thus, ami kōrĕ, to this girl. When agreeing with an inanimate noun, the only dative inanimate form used is ath, which agrees with any inanimate noun in the dative singular, whether masc. or fem. Thus, ath cīzas, to this thing, ath kāmĕ, for this work (so Śiv. 164). In other cases the distinction between animate and inanimate disappears, and the adjectival pronoun agrees with the qualified noun in gender and case like any other adjective. Thus, to take the genitive, we have masc. an. amis sāhiba-sondᵘ, of this gentleman; inan. ami cīzukᵘ, of this thing; fem. an. ami kōrĕ-hondᵘ, of this girl; ami jyāyĕ-hondᵘ, of this place (so Śiv. 91). In composition awa is frequently used instead of ami and away instead of amiy. It sometimes also becomes a in composition (see Gr.Gr. 151). ¶ ami, see ab. --ạndᵃra-- adv. from in that (within sight or pointed to). --ạndᵃ̇rᵃ̇ -- adv. from inside that (within sight, etc.), u.w. vbs. of going, bringing, etc. --apāri -- adv. beyond there (within sight, etc.). --apāri-kani -- adv. towards the direction of beyond there (within sight). --apāri-kanyukᵘ -- adj. (f. --apāri-kanicᵘ̈ --), of or belonging to beyond there (within sight, etc.). --apôrᵘ -- adv. beyond that place (within sight, etc.), elsewhere than there (pointed to). --apôrᵘ-kun -- adv. in the direction of or towards beyond that place (within sight, etc.). --apörⁱ-kinⁱ -- adv. from beyond there (within sight, etc.). --apöryumᵘ -- adj. m. (sg. dat. aṭas, and so on), a flood, a rush of any liquid, generally used --˚, as in pã̄-aṭh a flood of water, rūda-aṭh a flood of rain, rata-aṭh a flood of blood. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to carry through any work (however difficult or seemingly impossible).

a pron. suff. of 2nd pers. sg. acc. as in karān chus-ath, I make thee. When, however, it is added to the 3rd person it has the force of the agent case, as in koru-th, made by thee, thou madest. As in the last example, when added to a verbal form ending in a vowel, the initial a is elided (Gr.Gr. 184).

f. (sg. dat. aṭi), a silk thread used for tying on ornaments or the like. Cf. üṭᵘ̈. ¶ aṭa-horᵘ m. the pair of silken strings by which a pair of ear-pendants are suspended from the ears so as to reach to the shoulders. -kāñĕr m. unevenness in the twisting of threads or strings. -pholᵘ (? spelling), m. the neck-thread put on a woman at her marriage (L. 263, where the word is spelt athful).

m. (sg. dat. aṭas, abl. aṭa), a market, used in the following compounds. ¶ aṭa-hār m. a crowd or collection of men or women, e.g. at a wedding or festival, or in paying a visit of condolence. -manz f. a place where four ways meet, a cross-roads; a bazaar, a wide street of shops. -wāza f. a bazaar-cook, one not engaged in regular service, but hiring himself out by the day on special occasions; a job-cook. ¶ aṭas bĕhun m.inf. to sit in the market-place; to act like a harlot, to take to playing the harlot.
c.g. (as subst., m. sg. dat. aṭas), an adjectival secondary suffix occurring in the words waĩsaṭh or wö̃saṭh, very old, and rᵃshĕṭh or, malicious (Gr.Gr. 137).

m. (sg. dat. athas, ag. athan or (usually) ȧthⁱ 2, abl. atha or (usually) athi), the hand; the forearm, including the hand (Śiv. 1462). For ȧthⁱ 1 see ath 1. W. (e.g. 18, 114) spells the sg. nom. ath, but I can find no authority for this. ¶ In the following phrases and compounds atha may be either sg. nom. or (rare) sg. abl., or pl. nom. As an exam. of atha used independently as sg. abl. we may quote nimāz atha, prayers from the hand, i.e. out of hand, gone (K.Pr. 89). --kṛĕhȧnⁱ gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the hands to become black; to work hard for an object and the result to profit some one else; to labour fruitlessly, as when one builds a house and it is destroyed when finished or comes into another's possession; or as when one serves a master diligently, faithfully, and skilfully, and only reaps dislike and disgrace as the reward. --kṛĕhȧnⁱ ta buthi saphēd -- hands black (from handling money) and white (clean) in the face; dirtying one's hand with money dealing, and making no profit out of it; handling money, and none of it sticking to the fingers. ¶ atha-ạndᵃra, from in the hand, in the following phrases: atha-ạndᵃra nērun m.inf. to issue from the hand, to pour forth in quantities from the hand (of writing, or any mechanical work). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall from the hand, to be dropped; to get out of hand, to become free or independent (of one who has hitherto been subject to a person's authority). --trāwun -- m.inf. to release from the hand, let go; to set free, let go forth (as a child from his lessons or a slave from servitude). --ʦalun -- m.inf. to escape from the hand, to fly as a bird from the hand, to be lost. ¶ atha-ongujĕ f.pl. the fingers. -bā̃bᵃr f. agitation of the hand, trembling or palsy of the hand in attempting a task with anticipation of its difficulties. -buḍȧnⁱ m.pl. old age of the hands, stiffness or clumsiness of the hands produced by old age, sickness, or the like. -bạḍᵃran f. stretching out of the hand; in a hand-to-hand combat, the mutual thrusting out of the hand, hitting out, boxing; the joining of hands by a number of people in order to cure a sick man's disease. It is believed that if mutual enemies so join hands the good object puts an end to the enmity. -bögᵃran f. dividing out (approximately) by hand (not accurately by scale and weights). -bāgay m. id. -bĕha sitting of the hand, hence slackness of a skilled hand; travelling on wooden supports held in the hand (of a cripple deprived of the use of his legs). -bahā lagun m.inf. to experience hand-sweat; hence, of a flower or a tender young bird to be injured by the sweat or the pressure of the hand. -bujĕr m. old age of the hand, loss of skill, or inability to use one's former skill in manual work. -böjᵃran f., i.q. atha bögᵃran, q.v. -bal m. strength of hand; power owing to wealth, great possessions, etc. --band gaʦhun -- m.inf. to have the hands tied, to be so busy that one has no leisure; to be reduced to poverty, to lose one's possessions. -banḍan m. mutual friendship. -brakh m. (sg. dat. -brakas), hand-crushing, the crushing of the hand with a blow from a heavy weight. -brakawana yunᵘ m. inf. pass. the hand to be crushed with the blow of a heavy weight. ¶ atha-chakh f. (sg. dat. -chaki and so on), scattering by the hand, scattering (seed or the like in sowing grain). -chikh f. (sg. dat. -chiki, and so on), sprinkling (water, etc.) by or from the hand. --chalun -- m.inf. to wash the hands, either ceremonially (e.g. before eating) or to remove dirt; to wash the hands after eating (K.Pr. 17); to wash one's hands (of hope), to be driven to despair, become hopeless, as when all one's property is destroyed, or when one loses his independence, or when one's efforts fail to produce their expected results; to wash with the hand (YZ. 232), cf. dachyunᵘ atha chuh chalān khōwaris, the right hand washes the left (K.Pr. 43). -chŏmba m. rubbing in the hands, esp. rubbing grain in the hands to remove the husks. -chọ̆nᵘ adj. (f. -chö̆ñᵘ̈), having (the contents of) the hand reduced, empty-handed; temporarily reduced to poverty. -chöñᵘ̈ f. sifting in or through the hands (and not through a sieve or by means of a winnowing basket). -chŏñĕr m. empty-handedness, temporary poverty. -caũkharunᵘ m. contraction of the hand; the shrivelling up or numbness of the hand from extreme cold, or the like. -cār m. pressing or squeezing of or by the hand. -cīr m. wringing or squeezing of or by the hand. ¶ atha-dọ̆bᵃrĕ adv. hiding or burying secretly by the hand (u.w. vbs. of placing, etc.). -dachyunᵘ adj. (f. -dachiñᵘ̈), nimble-handed, dexterous, quick of hand, usually in a bad sense, as in hitting some one, striking a child or a servant, or carrying off property; ready with the fists; nimble-fingered. -dȧchⁱñĕr m. nimble-handedness, dexterity, quickness of hand, as in the preceding. -dodᵘ adj. (f. -düzᵘ̈), having the hand burnt, either lit. or met. -dag f. pounding by the hand, kneading, working up by hand into a mass; pain, disease, or swelling of the hands. -dọ̆gᵘ m. a blow with the fist, a thump. -ḍakha m. a support for the hand, a walking-stick; supporting or steadying some globular body by the hand. --ḍạkhᵃrun -- m.inf. to support by the hand, to be used as a walking-stick or alpenstock. --ḍalun -- m.inf. the hand to pass over, to have the hand make a mistake, to make a slip of the hand, i.e. when a skilful hand for some reason or other does a thing badly. --ḍālun -- m.inf. to touch a person affectionately with the hand, to pat, stroke; to cure a disease by some holy person or a god touching the affected part (YZ. 431); to lead a person to perform a work badly or imperfectly by giving bad advice, to meddle, interfere, to spoil the execution of a work; to smoothe with the hand, to make beautiful (K.Pr. 93). -dᵃnan f. shaking out dust, water, etc. (from a garment) with the hand. --dᵃnun -- m.inf. to shake out dust or water (from a garment) with the hands. -dūnʦh f. (sg. dat. -dūnʦhi), separation by hand; taking out the contents of a package; pulling out wool or cotton so as to make it ready for spinning. -dūñᵘ̈ f. pulling out or carding wool or cotton by hand (not by a carding machine), so as to make it ready for spinning. -dorᵘ adj. (f. -dürᵘ̈), one having a firm or strong hand, or having a skilful hand, or having a hand strong in beating others. --darun -- m.inf. to have a skilful, steady hand (in writing, etc.); to have a strong or violent hand ready to strike. --dạrᵃrun -- m.inf. to gain a steady hand by practice; esp. to train the hand for theft or pickpocketing. --dārawunᵘ -- adj. (f. -dārawüñᵘ̈), one who is accustomed to stretch out the hand, a beggar. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give a hand, to lend a hand in lifting a load or the like (K.Pr. 17); to put forth the hand to steal, to steal, to misappropriate, esp. when done secretly. --düzᵘ̈ --, see atha-dodᵘ ab. ¶ atha-gŏbĕr m. hand-heaviness, esp. of a hand heavy with gifts, liberality. -godᵘ m. a hole in the hand, caused by disease or accident; met. a hand like a sieve, extravagance, wasteful expenditure. -gumonᵘ adj. (f. -gumüñᵘ̈), grey in the hand; hence, sweaty-handed; having the hands fouled by dirty work. -gumañār m. sweaty-handedness; foul-handedness. -gōmotᵘ adj. (f. -gömüʦᵘ̈), gone from the hand; gone into some one else's possession; (of a slave) freed or insubordinate, out of hand. -gömüʦᵘ̈ f. of the preceding; used in the special sense of a pregnant female (human or other) miscarrying, suffering miscarriage; cf. atha-karüñᵘ̈ below. -ganḍ m. a knot on the hand; a knuckle; a knotted rag tied round a sore hand; inability to spend one's money owing to some one preventing it; the holding together of a bundle by the hand alone, without a string, etc. -graṭa m. a hand grinding-mill (for grinding flour, etc.), as distinct from one worked by machinery. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go from the hand; to go into some one else's possession; (of a slave) to become freed, or to get out of hand, to be insubordinate. -gaʦhawunᵘ adj. (f. -gaʦhawüñᵘ̈), released (El.). ¶ atha-hüjᵘ̈, see atha-holᵘ bel. -hajĕr m. crooked-handedness, deformity of the hand; cleverness in doing crooked (lit. or met.) work. -holᵘ adj. (sg. dat. -jüʦᵘ̈, and so on), a heavy growth of hair on the hands (considered a disfigurement). -jạʦᵃl adj. c.g. having very hairy hands. -jüʦᵘ̈lad adj. c.g., id. ¶ atha-kaḍun adj. (f. -kë̃ñᵘ̈), sweaty-handed, esp. of a person who is occupied in some foul business. -kāyorᵘ adj. (Śiv. 1220). mĕ athi lyūkhᵘ -motᵘ, written by my own hand (Gr.M.); in the hand (Śiv. 1628, 1697). --āmotᵘ -- adj. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), come into the hand, got, in one's possession (Śiv. 1794). --anun -- m.inf. to bring into the hand, to bring into one's possession; to gain, esp. to regain. --āyotᵘ -- adj. (f. --āyüʦᵘ̈ --), subject to one's hand, in one's possession, or under one's power. --āyĕtan -- f. independence, the faculty of settling a matter independently. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give into the hand, make over, entrust. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take something in the hand (Śiv. 855, 860, 1211); to take money, etc., with one when going on a journey. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat with the hand (K.Pr. 17); cf. atha sṻtin and atha khyonᵘ ab. --lagun -- m.inf. to come to hand, to reach, be received, regained; to be gained as profit. --lūrᵘ̈ bĕbi khôsᵘ -- m. stick in hand and cup in the bosom; utter misery, as when a man is so weak from disease that he has to go leaning on a stick, and so poor that he has to live upon food secretly begged and received in a cup hidden in his bosom. --lūrᵘ̈karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. lit. to do clubbing with the hand; to beat a person severely with the hand (breaking his limbs and leaving him helpless). --lārun -- m.inf. to follow on the hand; hence, to be partly found (when something is lost and a part of it is got back sufficient to go on with). --na hār andakār -- m. a curse, (may there) not (be) a cowry in your hand, (and may all be) dark (to you). The phrase indicates utter misery. --nyunᵘ -- m.inf. to take in one's hand, to take with one on a journey (as a servant, or money and possessions). --pholᵘ -- m. a little grain in the hand; at a sacrifice, the grain (sesame, rice, barley, etc.) mixed with clarified butter which is ceremonially thrown upon the fire by the priest and those for whose benefit he acts. --raṭun -- m.inf. to hold in the hand; to keep under one's own control or in one's own possession; to keep (children, pupils, or servants) obedient to oneself. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain in the hand; to be under a person's control or in his possession. --sörᵘ̈ -- f. the act of gradually collecting property (esp. some one else's) (either openly or secretly) and bringing it under one's own control; hence, theft generally. --sōzun -- m.inf. to send in somebody's hand; to send in charge of somebody, to send by somebody. --thawun -- m.inf. to place in the hand; to give to some one to keep; to put into one's own hand, to take possession of. --ʦŏ̈ṭᵘ̈ lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. bread to come into the hand; sufficiency for a living to be earned from the practice of any art or craft. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come into the hand; to come into somebody's possession (K.Pr. 8, 34; Śiv. 1754); to be earned; (of something lost) to be found (YZ. 136). ¶ athukᵘ sg. gen. (f. athücᵘ̈), of the hand; cf. athacĕn, K.Pr. 17). --māz --m. the flesh of the hand; met. money earned with great labour and trouble. ¶ athan sg. ag. (rare) and (usually) pl. dat.; cf. athan phakh, a smell to (on) the hands (K.Pr. 240); dŏd math athan, rub milk on the hands (K.Pr. 137, cf. ib. 166); athan kĕth, in the hands (Śiv. 12, 1093); and athan ʦŏn hĕth, holding in his four hands (Śiv. 801). ¶ athas sg. dat. to the hand; cf. K.Pr. 88. -andar anun m.inf. to bring into the hand; hence, with great efforts to get control of something. -andar thawun m.inf. to put into the hand; to bring into one's own possession or under one's own control. -kĕth in the hand, into the hand (YZ. 242; Śiv. 543, 620). -kĕth thawüñᵘ f.inf. to place in (one's own) hand; esp. to rob, carry off, and conceal property. -manz adv. in the hand, into the hand. -pĕṭh, adv. on the hand, in the hand; there and then, at once, quickly, immediately. -pĕṭh atha dyunᵘ m.inf. to place hand upon hand (a form of promise or oath to do a thing). -sṻtin atha, hand (joined) in hand (Śiv. 1010). -zodᵘ m. a hole in the hand, extravagant expenditure; cf. atha-zodᵘ ab.
adv. throwing the arms round a person or thing and lifting him or it up; e.g. lifting up a person in a faint whose limbs are stiffened, or lifting or pulling up a heavy post.
f. estimate, calculation; an estimate of the cost of making anything; anxiety (El., who spells the word aṭkal and makes it m.); agitation arising from affection (Śiv. 1574, f.).
m. delay (in starting); delay, waste of time.
adj. (f. athüjᵘ̈), (of a tree) having untrimmed branches, unpruned.
adj. (f. aṭhösᵘ̈), not uprooted (of a pillar, post, peg, etc.); not knocked down on the ground.
m. the name of the first day of the week, Sunday. W. 106 spells the word ātwār.
f. (sg. dat. -wathi), thorough knowledge of anything.

f. the larva of the wool-moth, a worm which infests and eats wool or woollen cloth. ¶ ạthᵃri-buzy adv. (also spelt -buzⁱ), lit. dependent on the wool-worm; hence (with verbs of making, governing an object indicating something made of wool), (made) over to the wool-worm, put in a place where it is liable to be destroyed by the wool-worm. -kyomᵘ m. = ạthᵘ̈rᵘ̈. -ṭukh m. (sg. dat. -ṭukas), a hole in wool or woollen cloth eaten out by this worm.

adv. there (within sight or pointed to), u.w. vbs. of existing, placing, etc. (Śiv. 747); from there, thence (Gr.Gr. 155). wuṭhañĕ chĕs ati, the twists are there (still remaining) (K.Pr. 178, cf. 111 and 239). -barābad, adv. there, in that place (in sight), e.g. of a place pointed to on the ground or in a book, u.w. vbs. of seeing, etc. -kinⁱ adv. from there (within sight or pointed to), thence (within sight or pointed to), u.w. vbs. of bringing, etc. ¶ aticᵘ̈, see atyukᵘ below. ¶ atinukᵘ adj. (f.atinücᵘ̈), of or belonging to that place (within sight or pointed to). ¶ atithⁱ adv. there, in that place (within sight or pointed to), u.w. vbs. of placing, etc. ¶ ȧtⁱ adv. (for atiy 2, see s.v.), from that very place (within sight or pointed to). -kinⁱ adv. from that very place, even thence, u.w. vbs. of motion. ¶ atyukᵘ adj. (f.aticᵘ̈), of or belonging to that place (within sight or pointed to). atyukuy adj. (f. aticᵘ̈y), of or belonging to that very place (within sight or pointed to).
(? spelling of atil), m. an irrigation system by which villagers are bound to repair and clean irregular channels (L. 460), cf. kŏl-wān under kŏl.
adj. c.g. (m. sg. dat. atītas), very poor, indigent, deprived of all wealth (Śiv. 1751); powerless; very afflicted, miserable; a mendicant, ascetic, devotee.
adv. (for atiy 1 see ati), at that very time; for that very reason; u.w. vbs. of going, etc.

or ātmā m. (sg. dat. ātmas, Śiv. 1016, 1823), the individual soul, self, principle of life, Śiv. 473 (ātma), 776 (ātmā), 866 (id.); the Great Self, the soul of all things, Brahma (Śiv. 993, 1053); --˚ as in trayōdashĕ-ātma, having thirteen selves, consisting of thirteen (Śiv. 524). -būd m. knowledge of self (sg. ag. -būdⁱ, Śiv. 1812). -dēv m. a tutelary deity (Śiv. 1761, 1772).
adj. c.g. one who has complete knowledge of the Supreme Spirit, a perfected saint (Rām. 1683).
m. He who rejoices in His Self, or in the Supreme Spirit, a name of the Deity (Śiv. 1481).
adj. (f. atüchᵘ̈), not planed, not pared smooth (of wood, leather, etc.).
adj. (f. atöḍᵘ̈, sg. dat. atācĕ), not scolded, not taught by scolding, untaught, a boor.
adv. without being taught, ignorantly, unskilfully, without knowing how to do a thing.
adj. (f. aṭŏküwᵘ̈), not hammered (of something of copper, etc.).
adj. (f. aṭücᵘ̈), not noisily crushed with the teeth; (of a tree, etc.) not severed or split with an axe or the like.
adj. (f. atüjᵘ̈), not cooked in ghī, oil, etc., not fried.
adj. (f. aṭüjᵘ̈), not moved from its position; firm, immovable.
adj. (f.atüñᵘ̈), not thin, viscous; thick, close, dense.
adj. (f. aṭöṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat. aṭāchĕ), not dear, not beloved; not liked, unpleasing.
adj. (f. at üʦᵘ̈), not hot, no longer hot, once hot but now able to be touched, become cool.
adj. (f. atüwᵘ̈), not roasted, not parched (of grain).
adj. (f. atöwᵘ̈), not heated in fire (of metals); not dried by the sun (of crops); not parched or roasted (of grain).
or atrāph f.pl. extremities, ends, environs; outlying districts, distant countries (Śiv. 678).
m. (of food) neither wholesome nor unwholesome, neither well-flavoured nor without flavour, insipid.
adj. (f. atūjᵘ̈), unweighed; unweighable, very great, (of wealth) vast. -bĕtūlᵘ adj. (f. atūjᵘ̈-bĕtūjᵘ̈), unweighable, very vast, huge (of wealth, gifts in charity, etc.).
f. approval, assent; acquiescence, concession, admission.
m. an improper action, an action which results in repentance (whether done wittingly or unwittingly).
(f. āṭivᵘ̈), altogether unsubstantial, with no strength, substance, or firmness.
adj. (f.āṭivᵘ̈), made or composed of flour (K.Pr. 18).

f. the otto of roses or other similar flower-essence (Śiv. 1149, cf. L. 77). ¶ ạtᵃri-phīl f. name of a medicine compound of various essences used to cure colds and disease of the eyes resulting therefrom.

adv. there (within sight); here (of a place pointed to) (Gr.Gr. 154). ¶ ȧtⁱnas adv. there (within sight or pointed to), u.w. verbs of placing, etc. ȧtⁱnⁱy adv. there indeed (within sight or pointed to), in that very place (within sight or pointed to). ¶ ȧtⁱthⁱy adv. id. ȧtiy adv. id.

adv. so as to cause to wander from country to country, roamingly, u.w. vbs. of expelling or of going forth. ȧṭⁱ-ȧṭⁱ kaḍun m.inf. to expel a person so as to cause him to roam from land to land, to banish from the country; to make a person disgraced. ȧṭⁱ-ȧṭⁱ nērun m.inf. to issue forth under compulsion of roaming from land to land, to be banished from hearth and home; to become an object of disgrace.

is properly pronounced as in Hindī, but is usually hardly distinguishable from, and is freely interchangeable with, ō. Thus, or, کریون, karyōn or karyaun, he did. Before mātrā-vowels it is treated exactly like ō.
or ōtār m. the avatār or incarnation of a Hindū god (Śiv. 1793); i.q. awatār.
or ōtörī adj. c.g. becoming incarnate, one who becomes incarnate (Śiv. 625).

he came, see yunᵘ. ¶ āv-bēṭh f. coming and sitting, sitting down on arrival. -gav m. coming and going (always with reference to some person or thing other than the speaker or the subject of the sentence). Cf. K.Pr. 18. -pāv m. coming and falling; an instantaneous fall, hence a sudden death.
(m.pl. ēy; f.sg. and pl. ēyĕ), the suff. of the 3 p.p. of all verbs, see Gr.Gr. 237 ff. The final v is dropped before personal terminations.
m. indifference, neglect, disregard; disrespectful abandonment of one worthy of respect, etc.
f. (sg. dat. avë̆zᵘ̈), acting against rule, doing a thing the wrong way. ¶ avë̆zᵘ̈-kinᵘ̈ adv. in a wrong way. -sṻty adv. id.
adj. (f. avẹ̆dᵘ̈rᵘ̈), not loose, not slack; unopposed, unhindered.
adj. c.g. unmanifest, indiscrete, imperceptible (Śiv. 1752, of God).
oraviʦār m. want of consideration, heedlessness, inattention (Śiv. 1111, 1530).
adj. (v. avĕʦhüñᵘ̈), not separated, not teased out, not carded (of wool, or the like).
m. non-destruction, salvation (Śiv. 170); N. of Śiva, voc. avināshĕ, or avināshō (Śiv. 157, 1052, 1269).
m. N. of Śiva, the Imperishable (Śiv. 694).
adj. c.g. mistrustful, suspicious, --banun --, to feel mistrust (Gr.M.).
adj. (f. aviʦörᵘ̈, as if from the next), void of consideration, heedless.
adj. (f. avë̆zᵘ̈), not known, not recognized, unknown.
adj. (f. avë̆nzᵘ̈), not honoured, not revered; despised, not appreciated, used carelessly; not accepted, not obeyed; not thought about.
the form which the term. au of the ag. and abl. pl. takes when emph. y is added; as in guryavᵘ̈y from guryau (see Gr.Gr. 93).
adv. yes, that's so, so let it be. Cf. K.Pr. 18 (where the word is spelt awah) and W. 96. El. spells the word auwah.
f. (sg. dat. awüzᵘ̈), a limited time, period; space of time allotted for any purpose.
m. repeated practice of any science, art, action, or the like.
m. a fault, a bad quality (in an animate being or a thing).
or āwalunᵘ m. (sg. dat. āwalanas), a whirlpool (Śiv. 1023, 1488, 1755, 1840).

f. a prim. suff. added to verbal roots, to signify the wages for doing anything, as in lōnawañ, the wages of reaping. If the root ends in a vowel, the suff. takes the form wawañ, as in diwawañ, the wages of giving (see Gr.Gr. 129).

or (Rām. 1705) āwāra آوارہ adj. c.g. wretched, in misery (owing to disease, grief, pain, or poverty) (YZ. 60, 279, Śiv. 129). -bal m. presents given by friends and relatives to a boy's father at the ceremony when the protection of the boy by the sixty-four deities is invoked (L. 260).
conj. (1 p.p. āwarôwᵘ), i.q. āwarun, q.v.
f. a funeral pyre; cf. K.Pr. 22. ¶ āwarĕñĕ-bal, a burning ghāt, a place on a river-bank where dead bodies are burnt. -mọ̆nḍᵘ m. logs of wood for a funeral pyre.
m. the state of being encompassed, being much occupied in any business, intense application to any work.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. āworᵘ), to cover, to envelope; to obstruct; to pervade, to surround, encompass; to take possession of (K.Pr. 54, 111). ¶ āworᵘ adj. (f. āwürᵘ̈ 2), 1 p.p. covered, enveloped, etc., as above; busily engaged (in anything). -motᵘ perf. part. (f. āwü-müʦᵘ̈), id.
adj. c.g. important, necessary; necessary, needed, wanting; adv. of necessity, necessarily, certainly (Gr.M.). -pöṭhⁱ adv. with same meaning as the preceding.
adj. c.g. (as subst. m. sg. dat. awashĕkas), necessary, needful, urgent (Gr.M.).

f. state, condition, circumstances, one of the four stages of life through which a man passes (childhood, youth, manhood, and old age) (Śiv. 515), or of the four conditions of the soul (waking, dreaming, sound sleep, and final beatitude) (Śiv. 1529). bālaka-awasthā, the condition of a child, the simple nature of a child (Śiv. 887, 1379), dat. in the condition of a child, (coming to God) as a little child (Śiv. 1379).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. āwasyōv), to crumble to pieces, to be decayed, worn out. āwasyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. āwasyē-müʦᵘ̈), decayed, worn out, crumbling to pieces.

m. the avatār or incarnation of a Hindū god, i.q. autār or ōtār (Śiv. 11, 58, 851, 854, 862). --dārun -- (Śiv. 1238, 1739), or --hyonᵘ -- (Śiv. 1384), m.inf. to take an incarnation, to become incarnate.
f. (sg. dat. āwaṭhi, avēṭhi), entrance (of a supernatural being into a person), demoniacal possession, inspiration, i.q. övish.
f. (sg. dat. āwaṭhüñᵘ̈), covering, superimposing; mingling (one thing with another) (Rām. 767).
adj. (f. awüjᵘ̈), not surrounded, in the sense of not covered, not wrapped up (in cloth), not wound round (with string), not clothed.
m. food which is partly wholesome and partly unwholesome.
adv. without speaking, without saying beforehand, without giving previous notice.
adj. (f. -thürᵘ̈), not wiped clean or dry.
adj. (f. awöʦᵘ̈), not arrived, not yet arrived; not yet come to pass; not yet come to perfection.
adj. (f. awöṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. awācĕ), not joined, not united (e.g. pieces of cloth, or the component parts of a metal vessel).
adj. (f. awüvᵘ̈), unsown, not sown (of seed, or of a field); coming up unsown, self-propagated (of weeds or wild plants).

adj. (f. awüzᵘ̈), without sound, mute; (of a musical instrument) not played upon, not sounded; not capable of producing a sound (owing to some imperfection). awozu-y adv. only mutely, entirely silently (of a musical instrument).
adv. without seeing, without inspecting, without examination.
adj. (m. sg. abl. awōni; f. sg. nom. awūñᵘ̈, dat. awōñĕ), not woven, not yet woven (of a cloth); (of a string bed) not having the string network completely woven.
adj. (f. awurᵘ̈), not strung (as a necklace of pearls).
f. (for 2 see āwarun), covering; encompassing, surrounding; surrounding a person in a hostile manner. -pāwürᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. surrounding a person, e.g. for his protection, or to prevent his escaping.
adj. (f. awushüñᵘ̈), not hot, no longer hot, cooled.
adj. (f. awuṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat. awuchĕ), not twisted together (of the strands of a rope).
adj. c.g. first, prior, foremost; best, excellent (El., who spells the word auwal).
the interrogative suffix (see a 3, ā 1, ay).
they (masc.) came, and āyĕ 1, she came or they (f.) came, see yunᵘ.

or ai conjunct., if (Śiv. 165, 634), usually appended to the subject of the sentence, as in bŏ-y (bŏh + ay) karahö, if I had made. With the past cond. hay may be used instead, as in tim-hay karahön, if they had made. Its negative is nay, as in tim-nay karahön, if they had not made; su-nay (suh + nay) karihē, if he had not made (Gr.Gr. 257).

m. (sg. dat. āyĕs 1, abl. āyĕ 2), life, age, long life, the allotted term of life, esp. a healthy long life (Śiv. 1209). In Śiv. 1480 there is a pun on the dat. of this word and on āyĕs 2, q.v. ¶ āyĕ-dorᵘ adj. (f. -dürᵘ̈), long-lived; of a healthy constitution. -grāyĕ f.pl. tremor or tottering with a tendency to fall (esp. of the weakness of convalescence). -gĕv m. long-life ghī, the ghī, or clarified butter, which remains over and above after certain sacrificial ceremonies, and with which the head of the boy for whose benefit the sacrifice is performed is anointed. It is a Hindū custom and is supposed to confer long life. --pyonᵘ -- m. to ascertain the prospects of a child's length of life by means of a horoscope, birth-marks, or the like. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), possessing life, long-lived; esp. used in blessings. -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -söwᵘ̈), long-lived, destined to live long, healthy. -tan m. independence, freedom (u.w. vbs. signifying granting, etc.). -zyūṭhᵘ m. (m. sg. dat. -zīṭhis, abl. -zēṭhi; f. sg. nom. -zīṭhᵘ̈, dat. -zēchĕ), long-lived. ¶ āyĕs-tān m. the cavity supposed to be in the skull through which the soul leaves the body at the time of death; the upper part of the skull; the anterior fontanelle (El.).

pron. suff. of 2nd pers. sg. dat., and also of the acc. when the verb to which it is attached is in the 3rd person. When joined to a form ending in a vowel the initial a is elided. Examples are: chus-ay karān, I make for thee; kari-y, he will make for thee, or he will make thee (see Gr.Gr. 184).
f. prim. suff. forming abstract nouns, as in wakhan-ay, telling, from wakhanun, to tell (Gr.Gr. 128).
f. a sec. suff. used in the case of the word lūk-ay, a crowd of people, from lūk(h), people (Gr.Gr. 152).
m. family, children, household. -bār (= عیالدار) adj. c.g. having a family, possessing a large family or household (Gr.M.).
or aiyām ایام m.pl. days, times; space of time, duration, term (Rām. 132). See gardish.

m. setting anything as one would wish it, arranging according to one's wish. -dār adj. c.g. easy or ready to be grasped (of the position of a weapon, etc.). --karun -- m.inf. to hold straight, to hold a sword, staff, etc., ready for the hand; to hold a gun straight, ready to fire at the mark. Cf. āyĕwun.
she came to them, and āyōkh, he came to them, see yunᵘ.
m. the sun's course from one solstice to another.
m. (f. -hānzañ), one who is both a hunter and a boatman, a boatman who lives by fishing and catching animal gen. a forest man who lives by hunting; cf. āyirᵘ.
I (f.) came, Śiv. 86, 1480 (with pun on āyĕs 1, dat. sg. of āy 2), see yunᵘ.
f. a resting-place, support, seat, abode; used in compounds such as athi-āyĕtan, see under atha.
you came to me, see yunᵘ.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. āyowᵘ), to aim straight at anything, to aim.
they (m.) came. āyēyĕ, she came or they (f.) came, see yunᵘ.

. The dat. of āyĕʦār, āyĕʦāras, is used idiomatically to mean 'subject to', 'at the call of' (K. 531, 723). pānas āᵒ, subjection to oneself, acting on one's own authority, independent action (K. 544).
m. (sg. dat. āyĕris), a forest hunter (usually Musalmān); cf. āyĕr-hönzᵘ̈. In Śiv. 1471 the word is used to indicate the low-caste forest Bhīl hunter who befriended Rāma-candra.
or f. the town of Ayōdhyā or Oudh (Śiv. 865, 1420, 1483). -nāth, the Lord of Ayōdhyā, Rāma-candra, the famous hero and incarnation of Viṣṇu.
. Note that in Rām. (e.g. 1678, 1695) 'Ayōdyā' is spelt 'Ojudyā'.
card. c.g. (sg. dat. ayŏtas), ten thousand, a myriad.
adj. (f. āyüʦᵘ̈), dependent on, at the disposal of; subject to, obedient to. pāna-āyotᵘ, self-dependent, independent (Gr.M.).
m. force of life, long life (used in blessings).
m. the calculation of life, in a horoscope, etc.

adv. to-day (Śiv. 1105); now, at the present time (Śiv. 1287). -kāl m. to-day and the day after to-morrow, nowadays (Hindī āj-kal) (as a noun). -kāli adv. nowadays (as an adv.). -kölⁱ adv. id. -kālāh adv. to-day one time, only once to-day, doing a thing to-day only once (of eating, taking medicine, etc.). -kani adv. perhaps to-day, about to-day. -kanĕn adv. id. -pĕṭha or -pĕṭhan adv. from to-day, henceforth. --rātas -- adv. to-night (Gr.M.). --subᵃhan -- adv. this morning (Gr.M.). --shāmas -- adv. this evening (Gr.M.). -tām or -tāmath adv. up to to-day, up to now, still, yet. -tāñ (Śiv. 738, 1486, 1627, 1829), or -tāñĕth adv. id. ¶ aza-boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈, sg. dat. -bajĕ), great of to-day, a nouveau riche, an upstart. -bajĕr m. greatness of to-day, the condition of an upstart. -wôtᵘ adj. (f. -wöʦᵘ̈), arrived to-day; having acquired complete knowledge to-day; fixed for and occurring to-day. ¶ ȧzⁱ adv. even to-day, on this very day. -kāli or -kölⁱ adv. even nowadays, in these very days. -pĕṭha from even to-day, from this very day, henceforth (Gr.M.). -tām or -tāmath, or -tāñ or -tāñĕth adv. up to this very day, even still. ¶ azyukᵘ adj. (m. sg. dat. ȧzⁱkis and so on; f. sg. nom. azicᵘ̈), of or belonging to to-day. ȧzⁱki-pĕṭha adv. from to-day, henceforth. ȧzⁱkis adv. m. sg. dat. to-day then (Hindī āj tō).
prep. from (Śiv. 650), where it governs the nom.
m. punishment, chastisement (K.Pr. 75); pain, torment (Gr.M.); torture, tyranny (L. 464).
m. N. of a quarter of Śrīnagar on the east bank of the River Vĕṭh (Jihlam), below the Zaina Kadal, in which is situated the well-known Mahārāj Ganj market.
m. eternity, abl. with emph. azalay, from eternity (Śiv. 652).

. The first consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet, the twenty-third (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the twenty-sixth) consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the second consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It has the sound of the letter b in English. ¶ The Sanskrit aspirate sonant bha does not exist as a pronounced sound in Kāshmīrī. When a Hindī or Sanskrit word containing this letter also occurs in Kāshmīrī, the bh is represented by b. Thus, the Sanskrit bhavati, he becomes, is represented in Kāshmīrī by bŏvi. In the case of words borrowed directly from Sanskrit, the bh is often, but not always, retained in writing in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character. Thus, the Sanskrit word Bhagavān, a name of the Deity, appears in Kāshmīrī written in these characters both as and as, but the pronunciation is always bagawān. Similarly, the Sanskrit word bhakti, faith, becomes in Kāshmīrī bȧktⁱ and other related forms, although occasionally spelt. ¶ In the present work, whether a word is spelt in the Nāgarī character with or with, that letter will always be transliterated b, and hence words found in any native book spelt with should be looked up, in the English order, under b. Thus, will be found, in alphabetical order, under bagawān. As a rule, spellings with will not be indicated in this Dictionary, even in the Nāgarī character. The principal exception to this rule will be found in the case of proper names, in which it is most usual to preserve the in native writing. Thus, the Sanskrit proper name Bhairava, a name of Śiva, will be shown in this Dictionary as bairav .
the Persian inseparable prep., with, by, for, from, in, etc. As in bakār بکار, for use, serviceable. Cf. W. 99.
the Persian prep., with, by, possessed of, as in bā-adab, with politeness, politely. Cf. W. 99.

an interjectional suff. used in addressing males. It means literally 'brother!', and is employed as follows:--hē nārān bā, O Nārān, in addressing a priest, a person of the middle class or a servant. If he is old, hata-sö-hē... bā or hata-bā-hē... bā is used. If a woman addresses a man or a woman respectfully she says hata-bā... bā, or if addressing a familiar or junior, hata-bā... au or hata-bā... a, or when addressing persons by their proper names only, hata-bā... a-bāyĕ or hata-bā... a-bāyau. Other words are often prefixed, as in ada-bā (v. ada), āhan-bā (v. āhan), and na-bā, No, sir. Cf. Gr.Gr. 99 ff., W. 101, and L. 279. For examples of its use see K.Pr. 49, 232; Śiv. 1244.

m. a father (cf. K.Pr. 1, 43, 156, 165, 255; Śiv. 435, 1526, 1790), grandfather, or other ancestor. -wŏhav m. vulgar abuse or imprecations uttered against a person's father. ¶ baba-dag f. grief for the death of a father. -dag pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. the falling of grief for a father's death, a father's death (and the consequent grief) to occur. -dagal adj. c.g. suffering grief for such a cause. -haʦar m. the want of a father, the disadvantage experienced by a bride or bridegroom not having a father alive. -ponᵘ m. sorrow occasioned by a father's death. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), wanting a father, one whose father is dead, esp. one who is not yet grown up, and whose father has long been dead. -sāvĕr m. a father's prosperity; comfort and luxury provided by one's father who is still alive. -sāway m. id. -tônᵘ m. fatherhood; acting like a father to another's child. -yĕtīm adj. c.g. one whose father died leaving him or her a child; a fatherless child, a helpless orphan with no one to supply the place of a father.
m. a chapter, section, division of a book (El.).

f. the nipple, pap, or breast of human beings, esp. of women (Śiv. 1371); the udder or dugs of an animal. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give the breast, to apply a child (esp. a crying child) to the breast, to give suck. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take the breast (esp. of a newly-born child), to suck the paps. ¶ baba-köñᵘ̈ f. a woman or female beast suffering from obstruction of the flow of milk. -kāñĕr m. a certain disease, obstruction of the flow of milk from the paps. -korᵘ m. the breast-orb. -wāy m. a severe pain in a woman's bosom; caused by disease, or as a consequence of the unsatisfied longing of a pregnant woman. ¶ babi-tal hyonᵘ m.inf. to put to the pap, to give the pap to a suckling child. -talukᵘ adj. (f. -talücᵘ̈), one who is close to the pap; hence a suckling child; also applied to very fresh milk immediately after it has been drawn from the udder, or (in the fem.) to the stream of milk as it issues from the udder. -ṭyonḍᵘ m. the nipple of the breast of a human being or beast.

m. a father (esp. in his old age) (cf. K.Pr. 22; YZ. 79, 93, 126, 456), grandfather; old man, sir, sire (respectfully), the head of an order of monks called Calendars (Qalandar). Used principally by Musalmāns in this sense, but also, generally, by Hindus in reference to a religious ascetic; hence, a respectful title given to any pious Musalmān, as in Hājī Bāba, O Hājī, sir (K.Pr. 74). -zī m. a respectful form of address to a religious ascetic, Hindū (Śiv. 555) or Musalmān. Also used as a term of endearing address to children.
adj. f. possessing a large bosom, full-bosomed, high-bosomed.
f. a lady of respectability, one of good family. Cf. bābū and bᵃrᵃka.
(? spelling and gender), a kind of good white rice (L. 463).
m.pl. in wȧrⁱ-babar, p. 1137a, l. 16, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. bā̃barôwᵘ), to cause a person to be flurried or flustered. bā̃barôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bā̃baröwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), flustered or flurried by somebody's action.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. bã̄baryōv), to be flurried, to be flustered. bā̃baryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bā̃baryē-müʦᵘ̈), flurried, flustered.
m. a brother's son, a nephew (cf. Gr.Gr. 133).

f. action like that of a father, showing a father's affection, esp. of one who deceitfully pretends such affection.
m. a gentleman of good family, esp. an immigrant from India. In this sense it has a gen. bābyunᵘ. Generally used as a prefix equivalent to our 'esq.', and as such is not declined (Gr.M.). Cf. bābañ.

m. camomile; camomile flowers; Matricaria chamomilla (El.); Cotula anthelmintica, an indigenous medicinal plant, stomachic, and good for rheumatism (L. 75).
