or bā̃bürᵘ̈ f. fluster, flurry, agitated haste in doing anything (Gr.Gr. 122, Śiv. 633). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. flurry to occur. ¶ bã̄bᵃri-bã̄bᵃri adv. hurriedly, flurriedly. -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), hurried, flurried.
adj. c.g. (as subst. f. bā̃bᵃriladiñ), flurried, flustered; one who is by nature, or from fear or the like, easily flurried or flustered.

(often written bachih in the Roman character, as a transliteration of بچِہ), the young of any animal, e.g. W. 129 (a colt), K.Pr. 240 (a sparrow-chick); esp. a very young infant (K.Pr. 23). bāl-baca (-bacĕ), m.pl. children (Gr.M., Siv. 1051). baca-dār adj. f. possessing children or young ones; pregnant, with child.

m. (sg. dat. -baṭas), a Kashmīrī Brāhmaṇ who lives by officiating as a priest. f. the wife of a priest-Brāhmaṇ.

m. preservation, salvation, deliverance; protection, defence, refuge; guarding, screening, cloaking.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bacôwᵘ), to save, preserve, rescue, deliver, protect; to set aside, put or lay by, save, spare, leave over and above; to reserve, keep back (a part of anything): i.q. bạcᵃrun, q.v. bacôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bacöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), saved, preserved, rescued; saved, put by; kept back, reserved.
adj. (f. bacawüñᵘ̈), one who escapes or survives, one who is saved; that which is reserved, set aside, laid by, or remains over and above.

m. alms, in the following:-- ¶ bēcha-bēcha m. the condition of living on alms, the profession of a beggar; begging as a last resource. -bēcha lagun m.inf. to be so reduced to poverty as to be compelled to take to begging for alms (of one formerly rich). bēcha-bŏkutᵘ m. 'an alms brat', a child sent out to beg by some one (usually too proud to beg for himself) who lives on the alms received by it. -bāna m. a beggar's wallet or platter in which he puts the food received by him as alms. Cf. bēchanas bāna under bēchun and bēchan-bāna bel. -bata m. food received by a beggar or set apart to be given as alms, usually cooked rice. -dana m. wealth accumulated little by little, and by means of severe economy, as the result of begging. -hāra f. id. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), 'a son of alms,' a boy who, although well-to-do, out of sheer greed is fond of begging (in a way that brings disgrace) from others, and especially from people of low caste. -küṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kacĕ), the fem. of the preceding, a girl who has no hesitation in begging from people of low caste, and thus bringing disgrace on her family. -myonḍᵘ m. an alms-morsel, cooked rice given in alms. -myonḍᵘ aʦun m.inf. the alms-morsel to enter, to take to begging (of one who has once tried begging, and found it so suitable to his temperament that he takes to it as a profession). -pholᵘ m. alms-grain, a store of grain realized by begging. ¶ bēchan-bukurᵘ m. a face for alms, impudence in begging. -bāna m. a dish for alms, hence a beggar's stock-in-trade of articles used in begging; met. a habit or custom of begging. -buthᵘ m. a fate for alms (cf. buthᵘ 1); the condition of having one's fate that of being a beggar; a face for alms (cf. buthᵘ 2), impudence or audacity in begging (even when the beggar is not in need). -gara m. an almshouse, a place where alms are distributed regularly, a monastery at which there is free distribution of food. -kuṭhᵘ m. (f. sg. nom. -kuṭhᵘ̈, dat. -kuchĕ), an alms-room, hence one who makes a regular practice of giving alms. -kŏthulᵘ adj. (f. -kŏthᵘ̈jᵘ̈), a confirmed beggar; one who will not give up the profession of begging even when he has a chance.
m. the male young of an elephant, horse, or ass; a colt. The feminine is bachīrⁱ, q.v.
f. the female young of an elephant, horse, or ass; a filly. Cf. bachēra.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. bacyōv), to escape, be saved, preserved (Śiv. 1299); to be saved, spared, set aside, remain over. Cf. (f. bacyē-müʦᵘ̈), escaped, saved, preserved; remaining over and above, etc.
m. (sg. dat. bacūris, pl. dat. bacōrĕn), a young male child still in its mother's arms, a babe, a term of affection.
f. (sing. dat. bacōrĕ), a young girl still in its mother's arms, a babe, a term of affection.

or bạcᵃrāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. bạcᵒrᵒ or bạcᵃrôwᵃ), to save, preserve, cause to escape, protect; to save, set aside, keep what is over and above; caus. of bacun, q.v. bạcᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. bạcᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), saved (by some one), caused to be preserved, caused to escape; saved up, stored up (of a surplus).

adj. c.g. bad, evil, wicked, vicious, K.Pr. 163 (f. sg. nom.); inauspicious, unlucky. As m.subst. a wicked person, a bad man, K.Pr. 157, 23 (sg. dat.), 157 (pl. dat.); evil, harm (K.Pr. 242); a wild pig (L. 117). -bakhᵃtī بدبختی f. misfortune, bad luck, adversity, misery, wretchedness. -bakhᵃth بدبخت adj. c.g. (as subst. sg. dat. -bakhᵃtas), unfortunate, unlucky, wretched, miserable. --duā بد دعا m. a bad prayer, a curse, an imprecation (for gend. see W. 18) (W. 110). --hāl بد حال m. a bad condition, bad state (W. 110); as adj. in bad circumstances, in evil plight. -kār بدکار adj. c.g. acting evilly, wicked, sinful, dissolute, licentious. -körī بدکآری f. a misdeed, wickedness; profligacy, licentiousness. --karun -- m.inf. to make bad, to disable (El.). --nām بد نام m. a bad name, ill repute (K.Pr. 157); as adj. of bad name, infamous (W. 110). --nazar بد نظر f. the evil eye (K.Pr. 55). --shĕkᵃl بد شکل adj. c.g. ill-formed, deformed (Gr.M.). -ĕtikād بد اعتقاد adj. c.g. mistrustful (Gr.M.). --yunᵘ -- conj. 3, evil to come; yĕs mahanivis biyⁱ-sondⁱ bad yiyi, to what man the evil of another will come, i.e. the man who wishes evil to another (K.Pr. 242).

great, in compounds, such as the following. Cf. baḍa and boḍᵘ. Baḍ-gômᵘ m. a large or important village; the name of a well-known village about 10 miles west of Śrīnagar (cf. El.). -gömⁱ adj. c.g. of or belonging to a large or important village; of or belonging to the village of Baḍgômᵘ. Baḍshāh بڈشاہ m. the great king, used as a proper N. referring to Zainu'l-'ābidīn, the eighth and greatest of the Musalmān rulers of Kashmīr (K.Pr. 261). -shĕrwār f. a certain astrological period. A man is born under that Zodiacal sign in which the moon happens to be situated at the moment of his birth. Taking that sign, together with the one immediately preceding it and the one immediately following it, the period of 7 1/2 years during which the planet Saturn is passing through these three signs is that man's baḍ-shĕrwār. Thus, suppose a man is born under Aries, his baḍ-shĕrwār is the 7 1/2 years during which Saturn is passing through Pisces, Aries, and Taurus. -watharū m. a large rice-field (L. 463, where it is spelt bad wattru).
in the following: -bã̄d m. repeatedly urging, pressing, or insisting upon.

m. a jester, buffoon, mime, strolling player, actor, dancing-boy (Gr.Gr. 10). See L. 312 for an account of these people. --lāgȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to employ buffoons for an entertainment, to give a theatrical display with hired actors. ¶ bā̃ḍa-bēgörⁱ f. jester's forced labour (K.Pr. 200), doing a thing with an outward appearance of enjoying it, but inwardly hating it, like a professional clown acting with a breaking heart. -bāy f. the wife of a buffoon; a professional actress. -jĕshᵃn m. a banquet or festival at which there are buffoons for the amusement of the guests; with suff. of indef. art. -jĕshᵃnāh (Śiv. 1705). -kār m. the actions of a buffoon; stage-acting. -koṭᵘ m. (f. sg. nom. -küṭᵘ̈, dat. -kacĕ), a buffoon-brat, a boy-actor who dresses as a woman, and takes a woman's part in a play; (in the fem.) a buffoon's daughter, an actress, a dancing-girl, a light o'love. -pöthᵃr m. acting (in a drama); the profession of an actor.
(Persian impve.), let it be, may there be, in phrases such as āpharī˜ bād آفرین باد, may there be applause, may there be praise (Śiv. 655).

m. venereal disease, syphilis (El.); also, a noisy downward breaking of wind. --pakun -- m.inf. the breaking of wind with noise. --pĕnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. syphilis to occur; --pĕyi-y, may syphilis attack you! an imprecation (K.Pr. 147). ¶ bāda-pȧjⁱ f. the spreading of syphilis through a man's body, constitutional syphilis. ¶ bödⁱ-hath f. (sg. dat. -hüʦᵘ̈), an attack of syphilis.

adv. very much, in a great degree, very; too much, too, excessively. Although generally an adverb, this word is also not infrequently used as an indeclinable adjective, synonymous with boḍᵘ, and meaning 'great', 'much', etc. See Gr.M. s.v. --baḍ -- f. steady increase, esp. of opposition, dislike, or a disease. --boḍᵘ -- adj. (f. sg. nom. --büḍᵘ̈ --, dat. --bajĕ --), very great; greater (than something else). --buḍⁱ bab -- m. a paternal great-grandfather, sometimes a maternal great-grandfather. --bran -- m. a certain large forest tree, with a hard wood, probably a kind of elm. Cf. bran. --dabār -- (cf. Arabic دبور, the west wind), m. a wind which blows from Bārāmūlā, and drives away malaria (L. 465). --gula -- m. a certain plant; it creeps along the ground and is used medicinally as an internal styptic; cf. gula in L. 76. --gurⁱ -- m.pl. conciliation by false promises, or offering false expectations. --hihurᵘ -- m. a grandfather-in-law, a husband's or wife's grandfather, the father of a husband's or wife's father or mother. --hŏhawurᵘ -- m. the family of a wife's maternal grandfather. --hŏhawȧrⁱ-bāy -- f. the wife of the son of one's wife's maternal uncle, the wife of one's wife's cousin on the mother's side. --hash -- f. a wife's or a husband's paternal or maternal grandmother, a grandmother-in-law. --mātāmāl -- m. the home of one's mother's maternal grandfather. --mātāmāl-pokhᵘ -- m. of, belonging to, coming from, or related to one's mother's maternal grandfather. --nāñ -- f. a paternal or maternal great-grandmother. --nyôvᵘ -- m. the esculent water-lily, Nymphæa lotus. Not necessarily the white-flowered variety. --prān -- m. a kind of wild onion. --shāl -- m. or kamrāzī, the name of a violent wind blowing from Karnao (L. 465). --ṭyū̃ṭhᵘ -- m. a certain bird, described as small and black, with a very long tail. --wörivⁱ bôgᵘ -- m. the nuptial present given by a bride's parents to the bridegroom's maternal grandparents' relations. --wöryuvᵘ -- m. the home of a husband's maternal grandfather. --zag -- m. a kind of rice; pale red in colour, a good cropper. --zügᵘ̈rᵘ̈ -- f. a kind of paddy, or rice plant, producing a light-red rice. --zyurᵘ -- m. a coarse white cumin-seed, used in medicine as a stomachic. ¶ baḍāh = baḍa, with suff. āh giving sense of indef. art. Often written baḍā in the Roman character; e.g. khān baḍā, a big tray (K.Pr. 103).
m., in bã̄dakarun m.inf. to settle, establish, a bargain, etc.; to agree to, to promise.

(? بداد), in --anun -- m.inf. to oppress or bully a person by compelling to do something which he does not wish to do; to distress or interrupt some one engaged on any work by making a needless noise. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be bullied, oppressed, or distressed, as above. Cf. bēdād.
m. spottiness, a brindled, spotted, or variegated state or condition.
adj. (f. baḍahörᵘ̈), spotted, brindled, variegated, of a dirty black colour with here and there clean or white spots scattered over it.

or badᵃla بادلہ m. (abl. sg. badᵃla بادلہ, see bel.), change, exchange, alteration; recompense, return (YZ. 428); requital, retaliation, retribution, revenge; used as postpos. governing abl., in exchange for (K.Pr. 70); as a substitute for, instead of (K.Pr. 155, Śiv. 910); instead of, like, as it were (Śiv. 1243). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to exchange (El.). ¶ badᵃla بادلہ, see ab., used as adv., in exchange, in revenge, etc.; also as postpos. governing gen., dat., or abl., = badal (Gr.M., W. 97). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take revenge, to take vengeance. --karun -- m.inf. to exchange (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. bādaladiñ), afflicted with venereal disease (bād, q.v.).
f. the price of exchange, the difference paid on the exchange of articles of different value; e.g. when an old article is exchanged for a new one of the same kind.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. badalôwᵘ̈), to cause to be changed or altered; to change, alter, or vary anything, etc.; caus. of badalun, q.v. Cf. also Gr.M. badalôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. badalöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to be changed, etc.
f. (sg. dat. badaliyüʦᵘ̈), a condition of change, a changed condition, transformation (Śiv. 1704).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. badolᵘ, f. badüjᵘ̈), to be changed or altered (Gr.M.); to change, alter, vary; to be changed, transferred, removed, exchanged; to be transformed, transmuted. badolᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. badüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), changed, exchanged, altered, etc.
m. an almond, cf. bādām. -phulay f. the almond-blooming; the beauty of a garden in the early spring, in which, as is common, rows of almond-vines are in blossom.

m. an almond, i.q. bādam, q.v. Cf. El., so YZ. 478. -gūjⁱ f. an almond-kernel; met. (of a bride, or the like) a girl of good family. -shīra m. almond-juice, a milky liquid made by pounding almond-kernels in water, used medicinally as a tonic. --shīrīn بادام شیرین m. the sweet almond (L. 458). --talkh بادام تلخ the bitter almond (L. 458). -ṭyokᵘ m. the name of a tilak or mark put upon the forehead, triangular in shape but with a round base; a person marked with such a tilak (f. -ṭë˘cᵘ̈).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. bādanôwᵘ), to cause to become powerful (Gr.Gr. 175).
adj. c.g. rich, wealthy, opulent (lit. and fig.).
the Himalayan silver fir, Abies Webbiana, see budulᵘ.
adj. c.g. out of doors, outside. --karun -- m.inf. to turn out, expel, reject, repulse. Cf. El. badar, repulse.
m. setting forth, setting out, esp. if one does not expect or intend to return; (of money or the like) excess over an amount agreed upon.

m. largeness in size, e.g. of a person's arms, of a vessel. --aʦun -- m.inf. largeness to enter; hence, of the growth of plants, to grow too large in a short time, to become too luxuriant. -dār adj. c.g. possessing largeness, hence too large, e.g. of a pot, a basket, or a garment. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be too large, e.g. of a pillar which will not fit into the place prepared for it in building a house.
f. an actor's or buffoon's fee.

m. anger caused by envy at another's honour or success. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to feel rage caused by such envy; to display anger at greater respect being shown to another than to oneself on some public occasion. --karun -- m.inf. to cause another to feel such anger. --wŏthun -- m.inf. such anger to arise.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. baḍôwᵘ), to extinguish a light or a fire by withdrawing the fuel. baḍôwᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. baḍöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), extinguished (of a fire).
conj. 2 (1 p.p. baḍôwᵘ), to set out on a journey. badôwᵘ-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. baḍöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), set out, started (on a journey).
adj. (f. baḍawüñᵘ̈), one who regularly and continually increases, etc., cf. baḍun; used politely to mean one who is about to depart, or set out on a journey.
m. one, esp. a village elder, who thinks himself a great man, whether others agree with his estimate or not; a man with a good conceit of himself.
f. badness, wickedness, evil, ill, mischief, injury, misfortune. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. badness to happen, going wrong, turning out badly.
in bã̄digaʦhun (-) m.inf. 'to occur by stoppage (of the flow of blood)', i.e. the black swollen bruise caused by a blow or the breaking of a limb.
adv. to, for, or in this (Rām. 1009).
f. the profession of a bã̄ḍ or actor, etc., q.v.
f. greatness (cf. Gr.Gr. 141), esp. u.w. reference to the exercise of generosity or the like. --hāwüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to display or proclaim one's greatness by word or deed.
adj. c.g. almond-coloured, light-brown; as subst., the colour light-brown, or a cloth or other similar article dyed that hue.
f. greatness, esp. of generosity or good fame; greatness, in size or importance (K.Pr. 111). In the Roman character this word is often written baḍāi.
m.inf. to use abusive language about or to an opponent (either before his face or behind his back). Cf. Persian رد بدل.
adj. c.g. kingly royal, in bādshāhī wath, f. the king's highway (borrowed from Hindōstānī) (El.).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. baḍyōv), to become large, become big, get big (L. 461); so, bata baḍyōs, I am become big through (eating) food (K.Pr. 26); to become bigger, increase in size (K.Pr. 173, Śiv. 1462, of love); to become extended, lengthened; to grow, rise, increase in age (K.Pr. 119); to grow up, become of full age (K.Pr. 71); to swell (as a stream); to be raised, elevated, exalted (K.Pr. 33); to grow tall; to spring up fast and in quantities (of crops), to become rank and luxuriant; to rise, be enhanced (of a price, or prices gen.); to go on, set out, proceed, advance; to go out, be extinguished from want of fuel (of a flame, or fire). baḍan-wôlᵘ n. ag. (f. baḍan-wājĕñ), one who keeps increasing, who increases gradually and regularly; one who is about to set out or go ahead on a journey. baḍith āsun m.inf. having increased to be; hence, to be prosperous, in good condition, to be excellent (as a man's qualities, learning, wealth, or reputation). baḍith bĕhun m.inf. to increase and sit; hence, to give up anxiety (regarding any matter), to be at ease, without care. baḍith rōzun m.inf. having increased to remain; hence, to acquire and retain a reputation for increased greatness (of wealth, good qualities, etc.). baḍyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. baḍyē-müʦᵘ̈), increased (e.g. in age, size, wealth, extent, etc.); advanced, gone forward (on a journey); extinguished (of a flame).
or brādun conj. 3 (2 p.p. bādyōv or brādyōv), to become powerful (Gr.Gr. lv, 175).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. bôdᵘ), to afflict, cause pain to (L.V. 7).
m. (sg. dat. bã̄ḍatas), the profession of an actor or buffoon.

f. the act of increasing or making greater, or spreading abroad, anyone or anything; the act of extinguishing a flame (Gr.Gr. 121). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to increase (of anger, disease, hatred, or the like, owing to measures taken with the contrary object). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause to spread abroad, to cause to increase (esp. of anger, hatred, disease, or the like, in spite of and owing to measures taken to reduce it).

or bödripĕth m. (sg. dat. bādᵃrapĕtas), the name of a month of the rainy season, corresponding to August-September, the Sanskrit Bhādra-pada, and the Hindī Bhādō̃ (K.Pr. 128); used also as the name of groups of small boils which commonly affect people in the rainy season. bödripĕtukᵘ adj. (f. bödripĕtücᵘ̈), of or belonging to the month Bādᵃrapĕth.
m. (sg. dat. -pīṭhas), an auspicious seat; esp. a rājā's throne used on ceremonial occasions, and a god's throne in a temple or other sacred place (cf. L. 161).
f. the act of causing to increase; (of things, qualities, or acts) encouraging the growth, spreading abroad, increasing by accumulation.
m. (f. bạḍᵃrāwawüñᵃ), one who causes to increase, a cherisher (Śiv. 862).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. bạdᵃrôwᵃ), to bake bread or cakes over hot coals (Gr.Gr. liii).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bạḍᵃrôwᵃ), to cause to increase, to make larger (Śiv. 1885); (of things, qualities, or acts) to encourage the growth, to spread abroad, to increase by accumulation; to cause to grow up, bring up. bạḍᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. bạḍᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), caused to increase, made larger, etc.
or (Śiv. 1174) badrakölī m. a village where there is a temple of Bhadrakālī (RT.Tr. II, 489). El. calls it Badrigul, and states that it is in Machipor Pargana.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bạḍᵒrᵒ), caus. of baḍun, q.v., to make to increase, esp. (of a human being or animal) to nourish, cherish, bring up; atha bạḍᵃrun, to stretch out or thrust out the hand, to join in hand-to-hand combat, see atha. bạḍᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. bạḍᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), of a human being or animal, brought up, nourished up, and now of full age.

f. a loud cry in order to call persons together from a distance, a halloa; the call to prayer by the mu'aẕẕin from the tower of a mosque (K.Pr. 25, 199); the crowing of a cock (K.Pr. 176). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to call Musalmāns to prayer; to call out at the latter end of the night to waken people; to crow (of a cock). --wanüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to whisper the aẕān or call to prayer, as is done by a Musalmān pīr in initiating a disciple, or (at a birth-ceremony) in welcoming a new-born child into the world; cf. L. 270. ¶ bā̃ga-loṭᵘ m. a certain toy, a kind of peg-top.

m. a share, a portion (Śiv. 1695); hence, part, in the sense of position, as in manz-bāg in the middle part, in the middle, in the centre (Śiv. 20, 914, 1107, 1459, 1547, 1588, 1668, 1695, 1744, 1759). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to deal out shares to those entitled to them (Śiv. 1695); to divide into parts or shares, (in arithmetic) to divide (a number). ¶ bāga-hār m. (in arithmetic) division (of a number).

m. a garden (Śiv. 181, etc.; K.Pr. 56, 204; YZ. 46, 254, 407); an orchard; pl. dat. with emph. y, bāganạy (Śiv. 503). -wān m. (f. -wān-bāy, see bel.) (in El. and W. 111 spelt optionally bāgbān), a gardener, esp. a tree and shrub gardener (K.Pr. 142); in fem. a gardener's wife or a female gardener. -wönil f. the profession or trade of a gardener. ¶ bāga-babᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a kind of sweet basil grown in gardens (Śiv. 1691); see babᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 2. -bombur m. (sg. dat. bomburas), a garden-bee, a bee which frequents only gardens and does not seek wild flowers; met. a libertine, one who haunts women as a bee haunts flowers. -dörᵘ̈ f. a garden side-door, the door of a house opening into a garden. -mŏy f. a small garden. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who owns a garden, the lord of a garden. ¶ bāgukᵘ adj. (f. bāgücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a garden; produced in a garden (sg. gen. of bāg).
in bāg-ḍōra m. a bridle-rope, a long rope by which horses, etc., are tied, a halter.
postpos. governing abl., without, exclusive of, excluding, except, besides (K.Pr. 178).

m. the armpits. -canda m. the side-pocket of a coat or similar garment. -bŏy f. the stink of the armpits; the sweaty smell emanating from a man's skin and perceived by those who are close by his side. ¶ bagᵃ̇lᵃ̇ gaʦhun m.inf. to go to a person's armpit, hence to meet him privately or secretly; to go by a side-path instead of by the direct road. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come together privately, to meet secretly; to approach a person with the object of offering a bribe.
m. Vāgambara, a N. of Śiva (Śiv. 1587).

f. division, dividing into shares, i.q. bāgay, q.v., Gr.Gr. 129; fate, fortune (El. bāgnai). --nērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. sharing to issue; i.e. in dividing anything out into several shares, the shares to come out accurately. ¶ bāganayĕ-dār adj. c.g. divisible into parts, easily or naturally divided into equal parts, or such as demands subdivision on account of its quantity or the like.
m. a fistula in the pudendum muliebre or in the anus, a boil in or close to the anus. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. fistula to occur, the occurrence of an attack of the disease.
adj. c.g. (when used as subst. the f. is bagandarladiñ), suffering from or afflicted by fistula.

in bāgȧnⁱ yunᵘ m.inf. to be joined to a person in marriage, to become married to a person (Śiv. 37, of a woman); to obtain one's share allotted by fortune, to receive one's fated portion; K.Pr. 54 spells the word bāguni. Cf. bāgi yunᵘ under bôgᵘ.
in bāgar bang, m. Hyoscyamus niger (L. 74, 76).

m. oil, ghī, dripping, or other grease used in cooking; cf. Gr.Gr. 122. --karun -- m.inf. to fry in oil, etc.; to cook in or with oil, etc. -dār adj. c.g. greasy, oily, buttery (of cooked food). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without oil; anything cooked or baked without grease.
conj. 1 (1 p.p.bagôrᵘ), (in cooking) to fry, etc., in oil, etc.; to add hot oil, etc., in the process of cooking. bagôrᵘ-motᵘ adj. (f. bagörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), cooked in or with ghī, oil, etc.; fried.
adj. c.g. made of mixed metal (of pots, dishes, or the like). Cf. bö̃gurᵘ.
m. a gluttonous lazy fellow; a young fellow who eats much and won't work.
adj. c.g. adored, holy, revered, venerable (applied to a divine being), as in bhagavath-māyā, the adored Māyā, or illusory power of the divinity (Śiv. 34, 665, 1234).
or f. of bagawān, q.v. the revered one, applied as a proper name to the goddess Pārvatī in Śiv. 101, 1527.

or m. God, the Supreme Deity, the Bhagavān, or the Adorable, of India proper (Śiv. 1712); vocative bagawāna, O God! (K.Pr. 102). Commonly applied as a title to certain Hindū deities, esp. to Viṣṇu (Śiv. 6, 31, 447, 863, 1142, 1156, 1317), Śiva (Śiv. 158, 944, 1216, 1629, 1737), and the sun (Śiv. 476, 580). The f. form of this word is bagavatī, q.v.

f. dividing into shares, distributive division, i.q. bāganay, q.v. --nērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. sharing to issue; i.e. in dividing anything out into several shares, the shares to come out accurately. --bōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to consider sharing; to calculate out shares, to arrange a fair division.
f. a buggy, a kind of one-horse carriage; a carriage in general (Śiv. 1859). Cf. bagī.
m. prosperity, good-luck (Śiv. 821), i.q. bögⁱ 1 under bôgᵘ.
adj. c.g. fortunate, lucky, blessed with prosperity (Śiv. 432, 685, 687, 939, 1331, 1554, 1832).
f. a long barge with a hood like that of a buggy which covers the passenger (El.).
m. dawn of good fortune, a lucky occurrence (K. 422).
m. steam from boiling water, etc.

or bah بہ card. c.g. (sg. abl. (?) baha K.Pr. 162; pl. dat. bāhan Śiv. 523), twelve; -shĕth, twelve hundred (Gr.Gr. 84, Śiv. 738, 188). See baha. In K.Pr. 162 this numeral is in agreement with a noun in the sing.

f. (sg. dat. böshᵘ̈), the twelfth lunar day of a lunar fortnight; the name of a certain expiatory funeral ceremony, carried out at Mārtaṇḍa or other holy place, in cases of those who have committed suicide, or who have died a sudden or unnatural death. In Sanskrit the ceremony is called nārāyaṇa-bali. Ordinary funeral ceremonies terminate on the eleventh lunar day after the death. ¶ böshᵘ̈ bihun m.inf. to commence such an expiatory ceremony. -bāpār m. the actions of the twelfth lunar day, i.e. the Hindū preparations for breaking the fast of the eleventh lunar day; the arrangements for the ab. expiatory ceremony. -bata m. the food eaten after breaking the fast on the twelfth lunar day. -hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to the twelfth lunar day, or to the ab. expiatory ceremony. -vĕd f. the ritual of the ab. expiatory ceremony. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who fasts by eating only once on the twelfth lunar day, after having accomplished the Hindū fast on the eleventh. -wölⁱ m.pl. of ab. the relations of the deceased who are engaged in performing the ab. expiatory rite.
in K.Pr. 162, apparently f. sg. abl. of bah 1, twelve. K.Pr. writes bahah.

m. vapour, mist (El.). When -ᵒ, as in atha-ᵒ, the word is practically equivalent to 'sweat', v. atha. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give steam (to), to subject to the influence of steam, to steam (e.g. to give a vapour bath, or to separate papers clotted together by applying steam, etc., etc.). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat steam, hence to go bad by becoming steamy (e.g. of stored grain heating, clothes becoming musty, or the like). --lagun -- m.inf. steam to be attached; the going bad by the production of steam (as of clothes or grain packed away in a damp condition). -ṭhāna, see s.v. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. steam to come; hence (of unripe fruit, grain, etc., stored away so as to heat through absence of ventilation) to become ripe, to ripen after being plucked or reaped.
adj. c.g. and subst. m. brave, bold, valiant, courageous (W. 117); as a title, Kampanī b˚, the East India Company; cf. K.Pr. 189, 190. W. spells this word bo˙hödur.

f. a certain nominal coin, the value of the eighth part of a British pice. The latter is now used as the equivalent of the old nominal coin (representing a hundred cowries) called the hath or 'hundreder'. Bahāgañ therefore means 'a twelver' (for 'a twelve-and-a-halfer'). As sixty-four cowries now go to a pice, therefore a bahāgañ now equals eight cowries. Cf. ȧdⁱ-hyolⁱ and RT.Tr. ii, 312. ¶ bahāgañĕ-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to eight cowries; costing eight cowries.
m. a coin of the value of a bahāgañ or eight cowries; when preceded by a num., --˚, a coin worth so many bahāgañ.
adj. (f. bahāgüñᵘ̈), multiplied by twelve, twelvefold; (of a rope, or the like) twelve-stranded.

f. (sg. dat. bahāki), any distant forest on a high mountain, a mountain forest. ¶ bahāki khasun m.inf. to ascend to the mountain forest; esp. of villagers paying a visit to such a forest to inspect their herds, which it is the custom to send there to graze during the warm months of the year.

f. (sg. dat. bahali), a long stout staff used by mountaineers, an alpenstock. bahali-pāwi adj. c.g. raised above one's fellows, exalted above others (metaphorically or physically, of a person or anything inanimate).
adj. c.g. turned musty or decayed from hot damp, of anything put by in a damp state, and hence getting spoiled by the heat of damp fermentations; spoiled by damp heat.

m. an excuse, pretext, plea (Śiv. 650, 1123); pretence, shift, evasion, subterfuge; with suff. āh indicating indef. art. bahānāh (Śiv. 682). --karun -- m.inf. to make an excuse; to pretend, sham, feign; to evade, shuffle.
conj. 3, to fix (El.), perhaps incorr. for bĕhanāwun, q.v.
m. a sea, gulf; a river. mānind-ĕ bahar, like a river, going on swimmingly, prospering (K.Pr. 64).
adv. outside, without, out of doors (Śiv. 678).

m. spring, spring-time, the spring season (Śiv. 54). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. spring to come, to blossom, bloom; (of persons) to flourish, be blooming, to be happy and joyful. ¶ bahārukᵘ adj. (f. bahārücᵘ̈), of or belonging to the spring-time, vernal. ¶ bahāras-kyutᵘ adv. in the spring-time.
m. (f. baharawüñᵘ̈) = baharan-wôlᵘ, v. the prec.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. baharyōv), to be brave, show courage, to stand up to a person, not to be cowed; not to be dismayed in the face of difficulties or defeat. ¶ baharan-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is naturally brave in the face of difficulty or danger. ¶ baharyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. baharyē-müʦᵘ̈), one who has become brave or capable in the face of difficulties, etc.

m. a cover for steam, hence, met. a device or means for concealing conduct, evasive action. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. a secret to be suddenly revealed or become generally known, to be unveiled, exposed, laid upon, revealed. --rōzun -- m.inf. to be concealed, a secret to be kept.
f. the use of a vapour-bath, taking a vapour-bath, or the local use of medicated steam; the steaming of cooked food which has got cold and congealed, to render it liquid again.
card. all twelve, the whole twelve, emph. form of bāh 1. Cf. Gr.Gr. 85.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bahôwᵘ), to apply steam to cooked food (such as rice, etc.), which has become cold and a jelly, so as to liquefy it again; similarly, to apply steam to melt any solidified substance; to cleanse soiled clothes by steaming them. ¶ bahōwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bahöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), steamed, as ab.

f. (sg. dat. bahāʦi), a kind of large cargo-boat or barge carrying as much as 800 maunds. It has a straw covering, and carries grain or other goods down-stream from the villages to the city of Śrīnagar, progressing by means of a tow-rope; the crew and family live on board (Gr.M. and El.). Cf. L. 313, 381, 458. ¶ bahāʦi-hönzᵘ̈ m. (f. -hanzañ), a cargo-boatman, one of the crew of a cargo-boat (Gr.M., W. 115). The fem. indicates either his wife or a female who works as such a boatman.
in bāhi waharĕ, in the twelfth year (K.Pr. 72); cf. böhyumᵘ.
f. an account-book, an official register (Gr.M., Śiv. 1912).
f. habitual custom, habit; --ᵒ conduct like (that of so and so); as in Shēkha- bahī, the custom of the Shēkh (is to do so and so), K.Pr. 194.
(? spelling), ? m., the name of a certain soil. It is a rich loam of great natural strength (L. 319).
adj. c.g. of or belonging to the spring-time, vernal.
m. disputation, discussion, controversy, argument; altercation, wrangling, dispute (El.); cf. bē-bahs.
adj. much, many (a borrowed Skt. word) (L.V. 51).

m. (sg. dat. bahuganas), a small brazen vessel with a wide mouth. In it tea is made, rice is cooked, ghī is prepared, etc. (K.Pr. 36, where it is spelt buhogun or bhogun). ¶ bahugan-khünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -khanjĕ), a broken vessel, as ab.; a small bahugun.
adj. one who says "Oh! may I become many", an epithet of the one God, with reference to his desire to create worlds (Śiv. 1274). This word is the Sanskrit bahu syām, with the voc. part. ō suffixed.
or böhyumᵘ ord. (f. bahimᵘ̈ or böhimᵘ̈), twelfth (YZ. 416, bahimis, m. sg. dat.).

f. a kind of bracelet worn on the forearm, described as made of engraved gold or silver, and being eight or nine inches long; cf. Persian بازو. ¶ bahi-band m. a single similar bracelet; cf. بازو بند -gulᵘ m. a single similar bracelet.
in bȧhⁱ-bāhaway card. c.g. (the emph. form of bȧh 1, twelve), the whole twelve, all twelve. Cf. Gr.Gr. 85.
conj. on the contrary, nay rather.
f. a name of the goddess Durgā, the consort of Śiva (Śiv. 1498).

or bö̃s 2 m. a bamboo plant, a bamboo; a joint of bamboo, open at one end and closed at the other, used as a receptacle for liquids (Śiv. 1210). -ḍünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ḍanjĕ), a stalk of bamboo, a bamboo-stick, a straight piece of bamboo. -kalam m. a short length of bamboo, of a couple of knots only. -köñᵘ̈ f. split bamboo, used for weaving stools, chairs, and the like.

m. a couplet, distich, verse (in poetry); poetry. baita-bözⁱ بیت بآزی f. an exercise or game in schools, etc., in which one person recites a verse, and his opponent must immediately recite another verse, commencing with the last syllable of the verse just recited. The first person must then recite another verse, commencing with the last syllable of the second verse, and so on till one fails and the other is declared conqueror. The game thus somewhat resembles our 'capping verses'.

m. a share of anything; tribute, tax, toll, duty, impost, cess taken from anything. -dār adj. c.g. one who pays such a cess, the person from whom it is due; that on which such a cess is payable (e.g. a house, land, or the like). --lagun -- m.inf. cess to become payable (of some one who has not paid it before, or of something on which it has not hitherto been paid). ¶ bāja-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), he who is liable to pay cess, or that on which cess is payable.
adj. c.g. in place, proper, suitable, fit, becoming; right, just, true (K.Pr. 200).
m. a musical instrument, esp. a wind instrument.
m. devotional faith directed to a deity, the bhakti of India.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. bajôwᵘ), to cause to sound, to play a musical instrument, to cause musical instruments to be played (Śiv. 725).
a word borrowed from Hindī to signify 'o'clock', as in aki bajĕ at one o'clock; aiṭh bajĕ tām till eight o'clock; dahi bajĕ at ten o'clock (Gr.M.).
m. greatness, abs. n. of boḍᵘ (q.v.) in all its senses (Śiv. 1306, 1588, 1716); degree, rank (El.).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. bajyōv) (borrowed from Hindī, the corresponding Kāshmīrī word being wazun), to sound (of a bell or clock). kyāh bajyōv what o'clock is it? (Gr.M., El.).

f. haste, flurry, hurry. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. haste or hurry to occur, e.g. in doing anything, or in completing anything after unnecessary dawdling, or in motion, or the like. --pāwüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause haste or hurry, to urge a person to complete something quickly.
adj. c.g. (when used as subst. f. bājᵃriladiñ), one who is flurried or hurried; one who is of an easily flurried nature or disposition.
m. a fop, beau, buck, dandy (K.Pr. 55). Prob. borrowed from Hindī.
adj. c.g. one (usually a lunatic) who barks like a dog; met. of abusive language.
m. a petty shopkeeper, esp. a Musalmān huckster (L. 387).
adj. c.g. one who often cries aloud (esp. of children); a cry-baby.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. bakaladiñ), a prater; one who is ready to talk or abuse a great deal when meeting opposition, free with the tongue (Gr.Gr. 135).
adv. according to one's desire or object; agreeably to one's wish. --wātun -- m.inf. to attain one's object (YZ. 228).

adj. c.g. useful, requisite, necessary, required for any purpose (K.Pr. 51); useful, of use, of any good (of a servant, YZ. 119). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be required, needed, necessary (K.Pr. 56). --yiwawunᵘ -- adj. (f. --yiwawüñᵘ̈ --), that which comes in as useful, useful, handy; that which comes into use.

m. prating, jabbering; loquacity (Gr.M.). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. mutual abuse or mutual rude language to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to prate, jabber, gabble; mutually to pour forth abuse. --lāgun -- m.inf. to start prating, so as to inconvenience another, to start talking nonsense.
adj. c.g. talkative, garrulous, a chatterer, prater.
adj. (f. bakawünᵘ̈), one who talks nonsense, or jabbers (like a lunatic); one who pours forth abuse; one who vomits.
adj. c.g. a remaining portion, remainder, residue; left, passed over; surplus, excess; arrears of revenue, etc. (L. 407, spelt bāki), i.q. bökⁱ, q.v.

m. (sg. dat. bakas), prating, chattering. -bakh m. continuous prattle, prate, babble, chatter, talking nonsense. --dᵃnun -- m.inf. to prate excessively, to threaten or abuse inarticulately, to talk nonsense. --karun -- m.inf. to prate, to babble the same thing senselessly over and over again. --lāgun -- m.inf. to rave, be delirious, talk nonsense so as to disturb others. ¶ baka-bakh f. babbling excessively; bubbling with noise (of rice or the like being boiled). -bakh karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to babble, prate, to abuse in meaningless language. -bakh karawunᵘ adj. (f. -bakh karawüñᵘ̈), bubbling up with noise (of food being boiled). --dᵃnañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to rave, talk nonsense in anger, abuse with senseless language. --diñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to chatter in rage, to address or reproach a person inarticulately owing to anger. --dᵃnawunᵃ -- adj. (f. --dᵃnawüñᵃ --), one who threatens or abuses another in raving or nonsensical language. --diwawunᵘ -- adj. (f. --diwawüñᵘ̈ --), one who abuses another in such a rage that he talks nonsense, or speaks inarticulately, raving with anger. ¶ bakan lagun m.inf. to start copious abuse owing to being in a rage.

f. (sg. dat. bāki), lamentation with a loud voice, weeping aloud, a cry (YZ. 178, Śiv. 828); pl. bāka, loud lamentation (K.Pr. 28). -cikh f. (sg. dat. bāki-ciki), lamenting and crying out (for help or to excite commiseration). -cīkh f. (sg. dat. bāki-cīki), id. -cīkh diñᵘ̈ f.inf. to cry aloud lamentably (for help, or to excite compassion, etc.). --lāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to emit a loud cry of lamentation, etc. (YZ. 571). --thawüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to stop crying aloud, cease lamenting. --trāwüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to start lamentations, to commence making loud lamentations (YZ. 19, 33, 130, 440, 484); esp. of the formal lamentations or mourning performed at stated fixed intervals after a death. --ʦhaṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to burst out into lamentations after a period of silent grief or after recovery from fainting for grief. ¶ bāka-bākh f. (sg. dat. as ab.), loud lamentation. -bukurᵘ adj. (f. -bukürᵘ̈), having a woeful or tearful countenance. -brūrᵘ adj. (f. -brǖrᵘ̈ or -brīrᵘ̈), one who cries readily and often, a cry-baby. -buthᵘ adj. (f. -buʦhᵘ̈), having a woeful countenance. ¶ bāki wadun m.inf. to cry aloud, lament.
adv. in the house, at home; āyĕ bakhāna, she returned home (Śiv. 650).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. bākhanyōv), to have the intellect obscured or clouded (from sickness, anger, etc.), to be mistaken (Gr.Gr.). bākhanyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bākhanyē-müʦᵘ̈), having the intellect obscured, mistaken.
f. a kind of sewing, sewing with long stitches, basting, tacking. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to tack, to baste.
m. an oblation or offering made to deceased ancestors at a Hindū śrāddha.

m. a business or occupation involving much work; a wide, extensive, or complicated business. --karun -- m.inf. to apply oneself to such a business, to commence a troublesome or complicated piece of work. --lagun -- m.inf. such a troublesome or complicated piece of work to fall to a person's lot. --wahārun -- m.inf. to make complicated preparations for commencing any work.
adj. c.g. miserly, avaricious, stingy; a miser, K.Pr. 184 (spelt bakhail).
f. acting like a miser (not necessarily of a miser).
one who gives, generous; the Giver, God (K.Pr. 183); of a forgiving disposition (Śiv. 3).
adj. (f. -wājĕñ), generous; of a forgiving temperament.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. bakhᵃcôwᵃ), to give, present, make a present of. bakhᵃcôwᵃ-motᵃ past part. (f. bakhᵃcöwᵃ-müʦᵃ), given, presented, given in grant.
adj. (f. bakhᵃcawüñᵃ), one who pardons, of a forgiving nature.
f. a present, gift, donation, gratuity, reward. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give, present.
f. favour, bounty; a present; forgiveness, pardon.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bakhᵒcᵒ), to give as a reward, to grant a favour; to give, present (YZ. 401, Śiv. 704, 715, 1031, 1193); to forgive, pardon, excuse. In the Persian character this word is spelt bakhshun, بخشن bakhᵒcᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. bakhᵘ̈cᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), granted to anyone as a reward; pardoned, forgiven.
adj. (when used as subst., f. bakhᵃriladiñ), one who keeps continually repeating the same word (as a lunatic).
m. iron armour, coat of mail, a cuirass.
f. i.q. bakhᵃtara, q.v. bakhᵃtari-barᵃdār m. one who carries armour, an armoured warrior.

bakth 1, bȧktⁱ 1, or baktī f. (For bȧktⁱ 2 see boktᵘ.) In Hindū works this word is often spelt with, in the Sanskrit fashion; thus, or. The following forms have been noted in Śiv.: -bakth (Śiv. 49, 103, 625, 663, 715, 1031, 1219, 1262, 1517, 1593); bȧktⁱ (Śiv. 494, 988, 995, 1041); baktī (Śiv. 649, 663, 938, 1005, 1511, 1520); sg. dat. bükh ᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈ (Śiv. 1199, 1265, 1368, 1419, 1470, 1472, 1823); baktiyĕ (Śiv. 739, 1372); bakti 1 (Śiv. 1794); abl. bükhᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈ (Śiv. 1058, 1535, 1711); baktiyi (Śiv. 99, 992); bakti 1 (Śiv. 749, 1012, 1013, 1116, 1144, 1588, 1678, 1784). (For bakti 2 see boktᵘ.) Attachment, devotion, devotional faith rendered to the Deity; abl. baktiyi bāpath, for the sake of devotion, in order to produce devotion (Śiv. 99). bakth bōzüñᵘ̈ f.inf. (of a deity) to hear devotion, to accept a devotional prayer (Śiv. 103). bȧktⁱ-bāv f. and m. (sg. dat. baktiyĕ-bāwas), devotional faith and respect (Śiv. 188); bakti-bāv the sentiment of or disposition towards devotional faith (Śiv. 515, 525, 734, 757, 1033, 1171, 1203, 1219, 1370, 1587), or baktī-bāv (Śiv. 1001, 1683), m. (sg. dat. bakti-bāvas). bakti-bāvanā f. id. (Śiv. 144; cf. 1683). bakti-vatsal m. one who loves, or is gracious to, devotion (Śiv. 1036, 1535).
or bakth 2 adj. c.g., i.q. bạkhᵃ̇tᵃ̇, q.v. bakta-vatsal m. one who is kind or gracious to devotees (Śiv. 1204, 1675).

m. (sg. dat. bakhtas, and so on), portion, lot, fortune; luck, prosperity; success (K.Pr. 25, W. 110). --bĕdār gaʦhun -- m.inf. one's fortune to become wideawake, prosperity to come, a turn of good luck to occur. ¶ bakta-boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈, sg. dat. -bajĕ), possessing great good fortune, very prosperous. -bāganay f. fate, fortune, what is predestined. -bajĕr m. great good fortune, prosperity. -lŏponᵘ adj. (f. -lŏpüñᵘ̈), lit. a luck-jar, hence one who is comfortably prosperous on wealth not earned by his own exertions.
adj. c.g. attached or devoted to, faithful, honouring; (with regard to the Deity) full of devotional faith directed to Him, cf. boktᵘ and bakhᵃth 2.
adj. (f. bāküjᵘ̈), a grown-up person who readily laments aloud for little cause; a cry-baby.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. baktāwārĕñ), fortunate, lucky (Śiv. 35); a fortunate or lucky man.
f. good fortune, good luck, prosperity.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bokᵘ, 2 p.p. bacyōv), to prate, chatter, jabber, babble; to rave; to pour forth abuse, speak angrily (Gr.Gr.); to bark, growl (Gr.Gr.); to vomit. ¶ bakith trāwun m.inf. to vomit. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to pour forth angry abuse at a person.

or bŏkusᵘ m. the group of four outer dark-coloured calix leaves of the saffron flower. --karun -- m.inf. to mix up and squeeze together flower petals, or the like, so that they are spoilt and cannot be sorted out again.

m. power, strength, might, vigour, force (Śiv. 6, 1026, 1200, 1303, 1841); strength, stoutness (of men or things); power, influence (e.g. of an unlucky planet) (Śiv. 489). ¶ bala-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without strength, weak, feeble (whether of mind or body, of things, actions, or conduct); incompetent, unable (El.). -raʦhar m. weakness, feebleness, as in the preceding. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), possessing strength, strong (in mind or body, or of things, actions, conduct, etc.). -sôvᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), rich in strength, strong, efficacious (usually of medicines or the like). -vīr m. bold, brave, courageous, a hero; not afraid of undertaking any difficult work; a strong, mighty man (K.Pr. 249, Śiv. 1675). -vīrī f. bravery, courage (Gr.M.).

m. a mountain range, a mountain, hill (K.Pr. 240, Śiv. 701, 820, 1162, 1165, 1222, 1240, 1456, 1687, 1854); --˚ mount so and so, as in Harmŏkha-bāl, Mount Haramukha (so Śiv. 1680, 1681, 1890); (in boatmen's language) the high embankment along the edge of a river to confine the current, a 'bund' (Śiv. 1834). -bachĕ f.pl. (the singular would be -büṭhᵘ̈, cf. boṭhᵘ), a mountain range forming a boundary between two countries, a mountain frontier; sloping land at the foot of a mountain. -bachĕ lagun m.f. to reach the mountain-foot; met. to reach a secure position; to become established in prosperity; to become settled after a roaming life; to become expert or well-taught. -bachĕ lāgun m.inf. to make a person established; to set him up in life, to put him in a secure position; to settle a person in a fixed home; to cause a person to become expert or well-instructed. -pĕṭh hāwun m.inf. to show the top of the embankment; hence met. to abscond openly; to leave home openly and go to a far country, like a person out of disgust at the world taking up his abode on a mountain-top. -tal hāwun m.inf. to show the bottom of the embankment; hence met. to run along the foot of an embankment, to abscond secretly, to run away secretly to a distant land. --raṭun -- m.inf. to moor a boat along the bank; met. to come to close quarters, to answer abuse with abuse. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain on the mountain-top; met. to exhibit indifference, apathy, disregard. --thawun -- m.inf. to moor a boat to the bank. ¶ bāla-bāla adv. through mountains; hence, through woods and forests, through wild country (Śiv. 660, 1253). -pĕṭhukᵘ adj. (f. -pĕṭhücᵘ̈), of or belonging to mountain-tops; met. beyond the reach of vision, non-existent. ¶ bölⁱ-bölⁱ adv. in mountainous countries (Śiv. 889); round about, outside, externally, esp. when unnecessarily distant (u.w. vbs. of perambulating, looking at, or the like). -bölⁱ phērun m.inf. to go round, move, or act at an unnecessary distance from anything. --raṭun -- m.inf. to move a boat along the bank of a river. --thawun -- m.inf. to moor a boat to the bank; to abscond secretly. -wath f. (sg. dat. -wati), a mountain track or path; the highest amongst several roads; the high path along the top of a river bank, a towpath.

m. an offering or propitiatory oblation of portions of food, such as grain, rice, etc., offered to gods, to semi-divine beings such as fairies, ghosts, etc., or to nāgas (snake-gods), dogs, or crows, etc., to secure the cessation of any natural or supernatural impediment, disease, or the like (cf. awāra); met. food given under force majeure to some animal (K.Pr. 150). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to make such an offering. -pröpyunᵘ m. the ceremonies connected with the offering of such a propitiatory oblation.
m. a child, used in the following: bāl-baca m.pl. the children of a family, wife and children, family (Gr.M.); dat. bāl-bacĕn (Śiv. 1051).

m. a suffix forming nouns of place, either proper or common, as in Hazrat-bal, N. of a place (RT.Tr. II, 457); saba-bal, the place where a wedding dinner party is carried on; wura-bal, the place for the cooking-fires of a bridegroom's party; kō̃da-bal, a brick-kiln or a potter's kiln; graṭa-bal (K.Pr. 71), the site of a Persian wheel, a mill-house. The word is esp. used to indicate the presence of water or a place sacred to a minor deity or spirit; thus, Ganēsh-bal, N. of place (RT.Tr. II, 340); Shāradā-bal, N. of a place (ib. 279); Ganga-bal, N. of a famous bathing-place at the source of the Kashmīr Gaṅgā (ib. 407, Śiv. 1684); vĕtha-bal, any bathing-place on the River Vĕth or Jĕhlam; Mörᵘ̈-bal, a bathing-place on the River Mār (RT.Tr. II, 416); Pŏkhari-bal, N. of a well-known bathing-place (Pushkara-nāga of ib. 476); krīrⁱ-bal, a well; yāra-bal, a bathing-place, a landing-place, quay (Śiv. 178, 1683, 1686); āwarĕñĕ-bal, a place where a funeral pyre is set up; shimᵃshāna-bal, a burning ghāṭ; rāza-bal, a burning ghāṭ. The last three are always on the bank of a river. Cf. Gr.Gr. 165.

f. (dat. bāli, written bō̈̈lih in YZ. 36, 258; voc. bāli, K.Pr. 25), a girl, a maiden, approaching maturity, between sixteen and twenty years of age (Śiv. 1834, where it is met. used for 'desire'). The m. is bāla 1, q.v.

m. the forehead. Used in the following compounds: -mŏkh hāwun m.inf. lit. to show the forehead and the face; hence (of a relation or friend) to show oneself or pay a visit after a long absence. bāla-ʦandᵃr m. (voc. -ʦandra), having the moon on the forehead, a N. of the god Ganēsh (Gaṇēśa), Śiv. 9.

m. a boy or youth, between sixteen and twenty years of age (the f. is bāl 3, q.v.) (Śiv. 943, 1353, 1383, 1470, 1887, etc.); (of sheep) a wether, (L. 363, 464, see below); a N. of Śiva (Śiv. 965, 1106, 1557, 1577, 1680); as adj. c.g. young (W. 21); young, feeble (Śiv. 1253 (f.), 1684 (f.)). -kūrᵘ̈ f. a beloved daughter (K.Pr. 25). -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a castrated ram, a wether. -mujᵘ̈ f. a carrot (Daucus carota). El. spells this word balmūj. -pān m. youth, the time or condition of youth (esp. used by old people talking of their young days) (Śiv. 660, 1106, 1444, 1834, 1843). -ʦēr f. a kind of apricot. -yār m. a friend of youth, a youthful friend (K.Pr. 250), or one who has been a friend from youth, a dear friend (K.Pr. 187, Śiv. 1616).
f. N. of the goddess Dēvī (Śiv. 1180).
. Before '-kūrᵘ̈' insert '-brahmaʦörⁱ m. a perpetual Brahmacārin (see p. 121a, l. 30) vowed to life-long abstinence and chastity (K. 781)'.
m. top, upper part; adj. and adv. high (YZ. 64), lofty, elevated, exalted; before-mentioned; prep. on, upon, above; bālā-ĕ-tākh بالا طاق upon the window (K.Pr. 4).
m. the scaffolding used as a support in building the upper part of a doorway or the like, the centering of an arch.
m. violence. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to happen suddenly and violently (esp. of misfortunes, etc.).

f. (sg. dat. balāyĕ K.Pr. 237; pl. dat. balāyĕn), trial, affliction, misfortune (YZ. 64), calamity, evil, ill. This word is often spelt balāĕ, balāī, etc., as K.Pr. 2, 4, 84, 134, 183, 207, and El. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. calamity, etc., to come or befall. ¶ balāyĕ dyunᵘ m.inf. to make an offering, or offer a substitute, in order to avert a calamity or pestilence. --lagun -- m. to become an offering or substitute in order to avert a calamity, to be devoted on behalf of another; cf. balāy lagi, may thy misfortune be upon me! (W. 101).
m. phlegm -- one of the humours of the body (El.).

m. an oblation, cf. bal 2; used in the following compounds. -dān m. to offer an animal sacrifice, to make a sacrificial offering of a ram, goat, or other animal. -vĕdān m. the ceremony of offering such a sacrifice.
m. N. of a celebrated demon (Daitya or Dānava) who was humiliated by Viṣṇu (Śiv. 859). -dānav m. id. (Śiv. 704).
adv. and conj. Moreover, but, nay but, on the contrary (W. 100). Cf. bökiy.

m. (sg. dat. bālakas; abl. bālaka, Śiv. 887, 1379, 1876; pl. nom. bālakh, Śiv. 805; dat. bālakan, Śiv. 705, 1055, 1322, 1876), a male child, a boy not more than ten years of age, with suff. āh indicating indef. art. bālukhāh (Śiv. 711). (El. has both bālak and bāluk.)

conj. 3 (2 p.p. balyōv), to be convalescent, recover, get well (YZ. 184, Śiv. 1541, 1572); (of a disease) to get better, be cured (K.Pr. 109); (of a wound or the like) to heal; to be well (El.). balyō-motᵘ adj. (f. balyē-müʦᵘ̈), recovered, well, convalescent.
[sic]? gend., the acorn of the Quercus incana (El.).
f. curing, successful medical treatment of a sick person.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. bạlᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. bạlᵃrun, q.v. balᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. balᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), cured.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. bạlᵒrᵒ), to cure, to treat medically with success.
m. riot, tumult, disturbance, insurrection, rebellion, mutiny.
c.g. a rioter, one who joins in an insurrection, etc., cf. balᵃwa; in the pl., a mob of rioters.
adv. for no reason, without cause (K.Pr. 72, 111); suddenly, violently; nolens volens (ib. 203). -kĕnas adv. (u.w. vbs. of being or doing) whether, or whether.

m. the roof of a house (Śiv. 1108, 1671). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to build a roof, to roof a house. --tārun -- m.inf. to put the roof on a new house or to renew it in an old one. ¶ bāma-zang m. the sloping beams which support a roof; presents given for luck to priests and to the carpenters and masons when the building of a roof is commenced. ¶ bömⁱ-chŏkh m. (sg. dat. -chŏkas), a species of gambling, in which cowries are thrown upon the ground. -püṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -pacĕ), one of the boards which form the roof of a house; a board suitable for such a purpose.
m. the skin. --tulun -- m.inf. to raise weals (with a whip) (L.V. 101).

m. an obstacle, impediment, hindrance, interruption (Gr.Gr. 148), something which causes disappointment. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. an impediment to happen or be caused; a disappointment to happen; (of a member of a social gathering) to have one's enjoyment stopped. Cf. bamal and bamalad. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to interrupt or impede anyone by making him angry, saying unpleasant things to him, or the like.
m. a kind of deep-toned drum, a bass drum (Śiv. 1455). -zīra (= زیر و بم), m. a pair of small kettle-drums (Śiv. 1455).
adv. and prep. together with, along with. As prep. it is used with the nom. case (Śiv. 676, 810).
adj. c.g. one who interrupts or puts a stop to anything (e.g. an angry man at a dinner-party or the like), a spoil-sport; cf. bamᵃr.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. bamaladiñ), one who is subject to an impediment, esp. one who, at a dinner-party, finds himself prevented, owing to anger, from enjoying himself.
f. the occurrence of an impediment in any work, owing to some person becoming angry.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. bambarladiñ), one who is flurried or agitated; of a flurried or agitated disposition.

m. (sg. dat. bambaras), flurry, agitation (mostly used in pl.). ¶ bambar pĕnⁱ m. pl. inf. agitation or flurry to occur. --tulȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to flurry a person by hurrying him in the completion of any work. --wŏthȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. sudden pain to arise, a start (from pain) to occur, as from pricking oneself with a thorn, tasting something unexpectedly pungent, accidentally touching fire, or the like.
prep. on account (of), in pursuance (of); by means (of) (W. 99).

m. (pl. nom. bāman), a sprout, shoot, leaf-bud, blade (Śiv. 1848). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. buds to sprout, esp. from a burnt or dried-up tree or from withered seeds. Met. offspring to be born to one who has hitherto been childless.

m. the quince fruit, Pyrus cydonia (L. 76, 348). According to El. there are two varieties of quince growing in Kashmīr: ʦọ̆kᵘ bam-ʦū̃ṭhᵘ and mŏdurᵘ bam-ʦū̃ṭhᵘ, the sour quince and the sweet quince. The quince is ripe in the month of October and is of superior quality. -ʦū̃ṭhᵘ-hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -ʦū̃ṭhᵘ-hishᵘ), quince-like, quince-coloured, pallid as a result of illness. ¶ bam-ʦū̃ṭhⁱ-byôlⁱ m. a collection or mass of quince-seeds. -ʦū̃ṭhⁱ-hüṭⁱ f. (sg. dat. -ʦū̃ṭhⁱ-hacĕ), dried slices of quince; the wood of the quince-vine. -ʦū̃ṭhⁱ-kujⁱ f. a quince-vine, a quince-tree. -ʦū̃ṭhⁱ-kulⁱ m. a quince-tree (El.).
adj. (as subst., f. bamarĕñ), one who interrupts, impedes, or spoils a social gathering by a display of anger, cf. bamal (Gr.Gr. 148).

f. (sg. dat. bani, Gr.Gr. 70), a heap, a pile, a stack (K.Pr. 64, 144, 207). Cf. bọ̆nᵘ and banna. ¶ bana-gāsa m. a hayrick, a straw stack; the hay or straw composing a rick. -zyunᵘ m. a stack or pile of firewood; the wood which composes such a stack, or a piece of wood drawn therefrom.
m. an arrow (El.); Onosma macrocephala (El.); Zizyphus flexuosa (El.); Rhus cotinus (written bhān) (El.), see bana.
m. a sec. suff. signifying 'keeper', 'man', etc., as in ratha-bān, a charioteer (Śiv. 1734).
m., i.q. banna, q.v. (El.); Rhus cotinus (El.), cf. bān 1.

m. a vessel (for any purpose), basin, plate, dish, water-jar, pitcher (K.Pr. 4, 17, 25, 29, 50, 75, 87, 114, 171, 216, 221, 252, W. 132, 144, Śiv. 473, 1149, 1216; with emph. i, bāni, K.Pr. 138). -bāh m. the sweating of grain, etc., confined in a jar. -bȧhⁱ adj. c.g. sweating, fermented (of grain, fruit, etc., confined in a jar). -bȧhⁱ anun m.inf. to cause or bring on such fermentation. -bȧhⁱ yunᵘ m.inf. such fermentation to occur. -baṭha m.pl. a general term for dishes, vessels, etc. -gorᵘ m. a maker of vessels, a potter, a coppersmith; a seller of vessels of all kinds. -garath m. (sg. dat. -garatas), the shaping of earthen vessels. -han f. a small vessel, a cup (YZ. 421). -kō̃da f. a potter's furnace, the pile of combustible materials in which he bakes his earthen vessels. -kã̄dur m. (sg. dat. -kã̄daras), a large kind of jar, wrapped round with twigs cased in mud, kept in kitchens as a receptacle for articles frequently required; a china merchant (El.). -khörᵘ̈ f. the weight of carrying on a household; esp. living as a householder when one's means are narrow and one has to make a good outward show, and in such a way that out- siders do not realize the state of affairs. -khörᵘ̈ phuṭarüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to break, i.e. to give up, such a struggle for appearances owing to one's poverty becoming known cf. wati-pĕṭh bāna-khörᵘ̈ phuṭarüñᵘ̈, p. 1156a, l. 40. -khotᵘ m. a pot-cupboard, a cupboard for holding pots and pans. -kuṭhᵘ m. a dish-room, a larder, a room reserved for storing food and condiments in separate bowls, a store-room. -manḍulᵘ m. a place in a kitchen for laying out dishes separately. --phuṭȧnⁱ 1 -- m. pl. inf. (for 2 see bāna 3), crockery to be smashed. --thurȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to shape earthen vessels on the potter's wheel. -tünzᵘ̈ f. a pile of dishes or plates, one on the top of the other. --ṭhāsȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to break dishes; met. to exhibit anger, be in a rage. -wôlᵘ 1 m. (f. -wājĕñ) (for 2 see bāna 3), a maker of earthen vessels, a potter; a seller of earthen vessels. -yüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -yacĕ), a kind of large wicker or cane basket in which potters carry about their wares for sale.
m. (connected with bāna 1), the womb. --wasȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the womb to fall, or be displaced, prolapsus uteri to occur.

m. (connected with bāna 1), fate, luck, fortune (good or bad), as the result of a person's character or conduct; worthiness to have good fortune, the possession of many virtues (Śiv. 431). --barana yinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. good luck to be fulfilled, to get plenty, to become very prosperous. --phuṭȧnⁱ 2 -- m. pl. inf. (for 1 see bāna 1) luck to be broken; hence, friendship to be broken. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), luckless, miserable, of no worth (Śiv. 1216, 1475, 1550, 1554). -wôlᵘ 2 m. (f. -wājĕñ) (for 1 see bāna 1), one who is referred to as experiencing fate (good or bad) as the result of his conduct. --zānun -- m.inf. fortune to be recognized as the result of conduct.
f. Viola serpens, also called nūna-pōsh or salt flowers, as they used to be exchanged for their weight in salt (L. 74).
m. a Bāṇaliṅga, or liṅga- shaped pebble brought from the bed of the River Narmadā in India, and worshipped in Kashmīr, as in other parts of India, as a form of Śiva (RT.Tr. ii, 67 and 283).
the solar month in which an intercalary lunar month occurs; an intercalary lunar month, a lunar month in which the sun does not move to a new sign of the zodiac.

adj. c.g. one who follows the prescribed rites and obligations of the solar month in which an intercalary lunar month occurs, and not those of the intercalary month. ¶ bāna-môsᵘ adj. (f. -mösᵘ̈), of or belonging to the solar month in which an intercalary lunar month occurs; one who follows the prescribed rites and obligations of such a month.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. bananôwᵘ), to cause to be, to make, bring into existence (Śiv. 1005). This verb is caus. of banun in all its senses. Cf. banāwun.
adj. c.g. that which can be made, possible, probable (Gr.M.).
m. (sg. dat. banātas), woollen cloth, broad-cloth, usually made of camel's wool.
adj. (f. banātücᵘ̈), of or belonging to woollen cloth; composed of such cloth. The word is really the genitive of banāth, q.v.
adj. (f. banātüvᵘ̈), composed of woollen cloth.
conj. 1 (double caus.) (1 p.p. banāwanôwᵘ), to cause to be made (El.).
m. (sg. dat. banāwatas), the sudden or unexpected occurrence or result of anything (usually of loss or the like). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. sudden or unexpected loss or damage to occur.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. banôwᵘ), to cause to be or become (Śiv. 25, 705, 712); to make, form, fashion, shape, create, prepare, manufacture, construct, build, compose, invent (Śiv. 904, 914, 937, 960, etc.); do, perform; finish, complete; arrange (a sacrifice) (Śiv. 70); banôwᵘthan, thou madest him (rich) (Śiv. 703, so 1879). ¶ banôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. banöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made, completed, etc. (Śiv. 751); artificial, not natural.
adj. (f. banawüñᵘ̈), that which happens or is self-produced; that which results, the fruits of exertion.
f. a large artificial canal issuing from a lake; esp. N. of an important canal issuing from the Wolur Lake.

m. a kinsman, relation, esp. a near relation, such as father, mother, wife, or sister (K.Pr. 25, Śiv. 43, 624, 1526, 1790). Cf. bāndav. -bāndav m.pl. kinsmen and relations, both near and distant (cf. Śiv. 43). ¶ banda-wôlᵘ 1 m. (f. -wājĕñ) (for 2 see band 3), having many relations, belonging to a well-known and high family.

adj. c.g. fastened, tied up, bound (YZ. 40, Śiv. 1035); shut, closed, stopped, cut off; prevented, hindered, barred, checked (Śiv. 1801); imprisoned, caged (K.Pr. 167, 218). --ganḍȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. a kind of knot twisted up from gold, silver, or silk thread embroidered, as an ornament, upon dresses, etc. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be stopped, impeded; to become stopped by one's own slackness or laziness; to be shut up, confined, locked up. --karun -- m.inf. to stop, to impede; to shut, close; to delay a work by slackness; to shut up, confine, lock up.

m. a limb, joint, of the body or of any jointed article. The pl. is used to mean the whole body, as in bandau nishĕ, from the whole body (K.Pr. 255). ¶ banda-banda karun m.inf. to separate limb from limb, dissect, take to pieces (of anything jointed together). -dār adj. c.g. anything (esp. an ornament or the like) complete in its various sections, limbs, or parts. --kadun -- m.inf. to take to pieces, dismember. -phuṭᵘ adj. (f. -phuṭᵘ̈, f. sg. dat. -phucĕ), having a limb or joint broken (of anything possessing joints). -wôlᵘ 2 adj. (f. -wājĕñ) (for 1 see band 1), jointed, made up of separate parts jointed together. -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), a joint, a place where two limbs or sections are united.

m. a pledge given as security for a loan (K.Pr. 181). -rand m. anything offered as security, such as a pledge, a surety, or a written document. -rand karun m.inf. to give such in security. --thawun -- m.inf. id. ¶ banda-paʦh f. (sg. dat. -paʦhi), confidence, trust, reposed in, or credit given to, a person possessed of immovable property, though short of ready money. -wasth m. (sg. dat. -wastas), anything given as a pledge. ¶ bandukᵘ adj. (f. bandücᵘ̈), that which is pledged.

in the following compounds (for other compounds beginning with this word see band 1, 3, and 4). -kath f. (sg. dat. -kathi), a prudent, trustworthy reply, decision, or piece of advice. banda wanun m.inf. to make such a reply, etc.
f. servitude, service (YZ. 380); compliment, salutation, farewell. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to compliment, salute, say farewell (El.).
adj. c.g. (as subst., m. sg. dat. bandakas), anything which impedes or is an obstacle.
m. an asseveration, vow, solemn promise (Rām. 151).

m. respect, reverence; obeisance, homage, adoration. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. reverence, etc., to occur or be shown. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. an occasion for showing reverence or welcome to occur. ¶ bandana-wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is in the habit of showing reverence, of a reverential disposition; one who receives reverence, of high dignity.
(Śiv. 973) or bandanā (Śiv. 1435), m. a bond, tie, fetter. In Śiv. 1435 the final ā is prob. m.c.
m. a city street usually crowded with many passengers; a harbour, trading-town, emporium (YZ. 160, 548).

m. the arrangements for or carrying out of the cooking and preparation of a great feast given to mendicants, etc., on the occasion of a religious festival or the like; the giving of such a feast. --karun -- m.inf. to make such a great feast.
m. a relation by blood, or a connexion by marriage (Śiv. 43, 624; K.Pr. 201); cf. band 1. -bāy f. the wife of a kinsman; a kinswoman (such as a sister or maternal or paternal aunt).
m. a man whose duty is to arrest and confine criminals, a thief-catcher, a jailer. --thawȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to appoint thief-catchers, to order the arrest of an offender.
m. tying firmly, shutting up tightly, enclosing securely in a cage or the like; a certain medicine for rheumatism or the like, made up of pepper, ginger, etc.
f. the act, or state, of tying, binding, or imprisoning.
m. plan, organization, management, administration; method, order, system; a settlement (of revenue) (El.).
m. (f. banḍörᵘ̈), the manager of such a feast.

m. (sg. dat. bandūkas), a gun, musket (K.Pr. 14; W. 18 for gender). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to aim a gun, to hit the mark with a gun. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be hit by the bullet of a gun. ¶ bandūka-khār m. a gun-maker.

m. (sg. dat. bandatas), connexion, relationship, affinity (Gr.Gr. 144); the affection existing between kinsfolk. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. kinship-affection to come into being (of two unrelated persons becoming close friends). --karun -- m.inf. (of persons not related) to entertain mutual affection, like that between kinsfolk.
m. one who is in the habit of taking pledges in return for loans, a pawn- broker.
f. a kind of turban made of cloth woven from silken threads and covered with gold or silver (kalābattū), worn by the bride or bridegroom at a wedding.

m. a pledge, a deposit. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take possession of a house in exchange for a loan, to take on mortgage with possession. --raṭun -- m.inf. to receive or accept a pledge or deposit. --thawun -- m.inf. to give in pledge.
m. breaking; breaking of the voice, stammering, broken articulation (Śiv. 107, 450, 974, 1103, 1203, 1803).

f. Indian hemp, bhang, Cannabis indica (L. 67), either the entire plant or its leaves, dust, or stalks used for intoxicating purposes; also Cannabis sativa (L. 68), cultivated mainly for its fibre (K.Pr. 80); a species of millet, cf. bāzar-banga. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give bhang for consumption, to intoxicate with bhang; met. to delude a person into hostility to anyone. --gālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to melt bhang; met. entirely to remove, utterly destroy. --tulüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to lift bhang; met. entirely to consume or use up (stored food or the like). --wuḍāwüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause bhang to fly; met. to take away entirely and destroy. --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. bhang to arise; met. to be entirely consumed, used up. -yār m. a fellow-consumer of bhang, a bhang boon companion. -yārᵘ̈zᵘ̈ f. bhang boon companionship. ¶ bangi-bôbusᵘ m. a kind of firework, a kind of bomb which bursts in the air. -bōda m. fuddled or intoxicated with bhang. -ḍār m. a piece of land (generally on the bank of a river) on which bhang grows wild. -ḍṻs m. a pestle for pounding bhang. -dyolᵘ m. the bark of the stalk of hemp. -dĕli-wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -dĕli-wāṭas), roping up with hemp-bark; met. commencing any work with incomplete or improper materials (cf. K.Pr. 80). -dĕv m. one who is a slave to the bhang habit. -manz naʦun m.inf. to dance amidst Indian hemp plants (where one's dancing cannot be seen); met. to labour in vain. -ras m. bhang juice, an intoxicating drink prepared by pounding bhang leaves in water. -raz f. a rope made of hemp bark. -shōda m. a bhang sot. -shīra m. an intoxicating drink made by pounding female bhang blossoms in water. -ṭhūl m. a small egg-shaped section of the female bhang blossom; a sort of firework, a kind of bomb. -ṭūpᵘ m. the male bhang blossom. -ṭiryuvᵘ or m. the female bhang blossom.
m. the province of Bengal (Gr.M.). bangālukᵘ (gen. sg.), adj. of or belonging to Bengal (Gr.Gr. 94).
m. a terrace room, a terrace summer-house, a room open on four sides on the top of a house (Śiv. 784, 965, 1247, 1696). Cf. bọ̆ngᵃla.
(K.Pr. 25), i.q. bö̃gis, sg. dat. of bö̃gⁱ, q.v.
adj. c.g. of or belonging to Bengal, a Bengali; as subst. f. the Bengali language (Gr.M.).
or bangurᵘ adj. (f. bangᵃrĕñ or bangᵘ̈rᵘ̈), one who deals in bhang; one who is accustomed to eat or drink it, a bhang-sot (Gr.Gr. 148, and (for f.) 35, 39).
m. traffic, trade, commerce. --karun -- m.inf. to do trading, to trade, to earn money by trading.
m. waste-land, land unfit for cultivation or which has never been cultivated. --tulun -- m.inf. to bring such land under cultivation. --ʦaṭun -- m.inf. id.
m. (sg. dat. bankas), a bank (the counting-house), (borrowed from English) (Gr.M.).
f. a heap, pile, cf. ban and bọ̆nᵘ.
m. a confidant, one to whom a person confides private affairs; one who is cognisant of a person's private affairs.
adj. c.g. composed of woollen cloth; a loom-woven shawl (L.377, where it is spelt binoet).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. banyōv), to be made, constructed, built; to be created, formed, fashioned, produced (Śiv. 649, 689); to come into being, to be produced (of crops); to be prepared, got ready, be done, finished, completed; to be managed, executed, effected; to be felt, experienced (of pain) (K.Pr. 30, YZ. 196); to be composed; to be mended, repaired; to be established, set up; to be, become (Śiv. 490, 529, 544, 559, etc.); to happen, befall (Śiv. 91, 674, 829; H. vii, 22), betide (YZ. 37, 128); to be possible (Śiv. 907); to fit, come right, to be suitable (Śiv. 1228); to succeed, do well, prosper, to be made, acquired, gained. panani banana, from my own being, i.e. because I am what I am (K.Pr. 163). banyōv kath, of what is it made? (Śiv. 763); fut. pass. part. banun, that which is to be, the future, destiny (YZ. 215); banana-rostᵘ, free from fate (as in 'no one can escape from fate') (H. vii, 23). With the infinitive of another verb, banun has a potential force, as in mĕ chhuna banān parun, I cannot read (W. 86). In poetry the pres. part. is often banan, instead of banān, e.g. Śiv. 1003, 1007. ¶ banith gaʦhun m.inf. suddenly or unexpectedly to be made, accomplished, completed, etc. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to succeed, turn out well, be fortunate, to prosper. banyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. banyē-müʦᵘ̈), produced, come into being (Śiv. 447, 618); completed, finished, executed, etc.; successful, prosperous.
m. a howl. --karun -- m.inf. to howl (El.).

f. the selling of any valued property owing to the requirement of money for necessary expenditure, the selling cheaply or at a sacrifice (Gr.Gr.); the division or partition of one's own or joint property amongst kinsfolk.

or bạnzᵃrāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. bạnzᵒrᵒ or bạnzᵃrôwᵃ), to sell valued property under urgent necessity for money, to sell for small value or at a sacrifice (Gr.Gr.); to pledge such property for a similar purpose; to divide or make partition of joint family property amongst the kinsfolk (Gr.Gr.). ¶ bạnzᵒrᵒ-motᵒ or bạnzᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. bạnzᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ or bạnzᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), sold or pledged at a sacrifice or below value; divided, subjected to partition.
or bạñᵉ̆rāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. bạñᵒrᵒ or bạñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), to cause to be, to bring into being, produce (Gr.Gr. 173, 175).
the behaviour natural to a person, natural conduct.

postpos. governing abl. or abl. of gen. (K.Pr. 217); owing to, on account of (K.Pr. 63); about, concerning, for the sake of (Śiv. 583, 1448, 1487, 1862). taway bāpath, for the sake of that very business (Siv. 709); for the sake of, in order to produce (Śiv. 99); for the sake of, in order to obtain (Śiv. 101); frequently forming an inf. of purpose with abl. of inf., as in wuchana bāpath, in order to see.
f. the wife of a nephew on the brother's side.
m. a nephew on the brother's side.
m. (sg. abl. bāpāri, gen. irreg. bāpāryukᵘ K.Pr. 26), a merchant, tradesman (Gr.M.).

m. a door (K.Pr. 36, 105, 135, Śiv. 1450, 1646, 1747); (of a mountain) the commencement of the ascent (Śiv. 1176, baras tal). -tal hūñᵘ̈ or -pĕṭh hūñᵘ̈, a bitch at the door (K.Pr. 7, 65, 102); barau kinⁱ, (looking) through the doors (Śiv. 953). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to shut a door (K.Pr. 26, W. 147). --dith ȧchⁱ tōwarüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to close the door, and threaten; to get into a hidden place for safety, and then to abuse a person or brag of one's superiority to him. -hākh f. (sg. dat. -hāki), a doorpost, the side-post of a door. -hang m. the upper beam of a doorway, the lintel of a door (Śiv. 1075). -nyās the beam of wood projecting over a door, the lintel. Cf. the proverb Dai ay diyi ta bar-nyāsa-y, if God will give, then (He will give) even at the lintel. In W. 129 and K.Pr. 45 this is written bara nyāsai, and is apparently wrongly translated. -poṭᵘ m. a plank of a door, the leaf of a double door. -ʦaran f. (sg.dat. -ʦᵃrüñᵃ), a chink in a door, or between the two leaves of a double door. -ʦᵃrüñᵃnasthgaʦhünᵃ f.inf. the nose to go into the chink of a door; met. to be absolutely under a person's thumb or at his beck and call. ¶ bara 1 abl. at the door (K.Pr. 45). --aʦun -- m.inf. to enter by a door (Śiv. 448, 1132). --nērun -- m.inf. to go out by the door (K.Pr. 10), so bari nērun (Śiv. 1367). ¶ baras gã̄ṭh dyunᵘ m.inf. to apply a knot to a door, to fasten up a door and go away leaving the house empty of people (K.Pr. 76).

m. a burden, load (YZ. 420, Śiv. 1254, 1791); the amount being weighed, or to be weighed, in a scales. Cf. bōr and bôrᵘ 1; see also kār o bār under kār. yā bār Sāhibō (K.Pr. 210) = Persian bār-ĕ Ilāh, O great God! -dār باردار f. a pregnant woman. --gaʦhun --, a burden to happen; an unwished for, difficult, or impossible task to be imposed upon a person. --hĕnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to take loads; to incur, without cause, a share in another's loss; to become a partner in some unlawful or criminal act. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take a burden, to undertake a task or responsibility, to accept responsibility. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to impose a burden (YZ. 551). ¶ bāra-wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ 1), endowed with heaviness, overloaded (of a camel, etc.); difficult, or impossible to carry out (of an action).
a prefix indicating fullness or completion. See under the separate words.
m. a time, a turn. bār bār, time after time, again and again (K.Pr. 184). yĕkh bār یک بار adv. at the same time, at once, simultaneously (Śiv. 781, 912).
m. greatness; God. --Khŏdāyō, O Great God (H. v, 7). --Söhib, the Almighty (H. vii, 2, 3, 5).
a suffix used with measures of value, weight, etc., indicating approximateness, as in hār-bar, (worth) about a cowry, (worth) a mere cowry (Śiv. 1795).
f. a kind of rice, small in grain and white, mainly produced in the hill-country of Western Kashmīr, on the borders of the State of Pūnch.
m. a lamb (K.Pr. 180, W. 155) (for 1 see bar 1), a thin half-fed sheep.

f. the fruit of a certain small thorny shrub, in appearance like a small jujube-fruit, growing wild on the mountain slopes. -dŏph m. (sg. dat. -dŏpas), the shrub on which the bāra-fruit grows. -konḍᵘ m. the long sharp thorn of the bāra-dŏph (Rām. 1633). -thürᵘ̈ f. N. of a certain shrub, i.q. bāra-dŏph. -wājĕñ 2 f. a woman who collects bāra-fruit and sells it in the streets. -zāl m. a spot covered with these bāra-dŏph bushes, usually on the hill-slopes.

m. leanness, an emaciated condition, of a man or beast from sorrow, illness, etc. (Rām. 645, 686, 1020); witheredness, flaccidity, of a tree, flower, or the like (YZ. 153). Cf. bara 2. --gō-motᵘ --  adj. (f. --gö-müʦᵘ̈ --), reduced to leanness, or witheredness (of a man, tree, etc.). --gaʦhun --  m.inf. to be reduced to leanness (of a man or animal), to be withered (of a tree or flower) (YZ. 152, Śiv. 168). --karun -- m.inf. to reduce to leanness, to allow to become lean or withered by neglect (Śiv. 304, Rām. 1606).

adj. c.g. heavy, weighty. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall heavy, of some impossible or difficult task, which a person finds himself compelled to undertake. --tatun -- m.inf. the load to be hot; hence, (of some work which was undertaken hastily and must now be completed) to be without resource, to be at one's wits' end.
a corruption of barābar, q.v., see ati.
f. the act of filling to the brim.

adj. c.g. equal, coinciding, alike, all one (K.Pr. 18, 64, 79, 81, 163); of equal value (Śiv. 900); flat, level (K.Pr. 136, of the beam of a pair of scales); equal (to) (governing dat., K.Pr. 163, W. 121); (of opinions) agreeing, coinciding (Gr.M.); full, complete (Śiv. 1348); as prep. according to (El., K.Pr. 257); as adv. continually, regularly, without intermission (Rām. 746).
adj. c.g. filled to the brim.
m.pl. a married couple, husband and wife.
prep. for the sake of, on account of (W. 99). barāe Khudā برائی خدا, for God's sake, the cry of a beggar (K.Pr. 5, W. 152).
(?), m. the oak, Quercus dilatata (El.). According to L. 79 this tree does not grow in Kashmir. The spelling of the word is doubtful.

f. (sg. dat. barüñᵘ̈), a lightly-built door, such as that admitting to the ground floor of a house or water-shed or a cow-house; a doorway fitted with such a door. Cf. L. 460. hasti-baran, f. an elephant's stable-door (K.Pr. 190).
f. the N. of one of the lunar asterisms, the Sanskrit Bharaṇī.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. baranôwᵘ), to cause another to fill anything.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. baranôwᵘ), to make a person homesick, to cause him to be homesick.
(K.Pr. 39), i.q. brã̄da, abl. of brã̄d, q.v.

m.pl. a pair of uterine brothers, or a brother and sister, both uterine (YZ. 438); any number of uterine brothers or brothers and sisters (YZ. 453). -tônᵘ m. brotherhood (uterine or not), the relationship between brothers or between brothers and sisters; met. mutual affection or mutual conduct like that between brothers; relationship by blood, or even by having the same teacher.
(lit. icy), a kind of sweetmeat made of sugar and milk and having the appearance of ice.
to a door, see bar 1; I will fill for him, see barun 1.

f. (sg. dat. baröʦᵘ̈), a writing conferring immunity or exemption; by message or written document causing another to make a payment to a third party, a draft, cheque. baröʦᵘ̈ dyunᵘ m.inf. to give by a draft on another; met. to put forward another man, an animal, etc., as a substitute for oneself, in order that he may be presented as an offering to a deity, undergo misfortune, receive punishment, make good a loss, or the like; to offer another in atonement as a substitute for oneself, to make another a scapegoat. --lagun -- m.inf. to be offered by another in substitution as ab., to become a scapegoat.

m. disclosure, revelation, making some hidden thing or condition manifest. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to become manifest, esp. the spontaneous manifestation of some valuable object hitherto concealed. --lagun -- m.inf. a search for something hidden to be undertaken, e.g. of the official search for stolen property.

m.pl. reproaches, complaints, grumbling (only used in pl.) (K.Pr. 58, 59). El. spells this word bārau. --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to complain about one person to another; to lament (Ram. 939). --dāwȧnⁱ -- to scold (Śiv. 1817); to cry for help, call for rescue (Śiv. 130). ¶ bāravan aʦun m.inf. to enter upon reproaches, to start reproaching. --lagun -- m.inf. to become the object of reproaches; (also) to utter reproaches.
f. the wages for filling (e.g. for packing cotton in sacks, etc.).

adj. (f. barawüñᵘ̈ 1), one who is accustomed to fill, or is employed in filling. ¶ barawañĕ ṭās m. a certain children's game played with hollow balls of earth, which are dashed on the ground and burst with a bang (ṭās).
adj. (f. barawüñᵘ̈), one who pines in absence.
adj. c.g. given to the wind, wasted, ruined, destroyed (K.Pr. 48).
f. filled full (of beauty); hence, a woman beautiful in every respect.
