m. one who lives by parching grain; a grain-parcher (usually of maize). ¶ barbuzⁱ-bāra m. a grain-parcher's parching-pan (filled with hot sand). -bāy f. a grain-parcher's wife. -gāsa karun m.inf. to throw into disorder, scatter widely something which should be kept in an orderly manner (as a person's hair, the threads in a loom, or the leaves of a book) (like the confused pile of leaves and grass kept by a grain-parcher for fuel). -pöthᵃr m. acting or conducting oneself like a grain-parcher, the habits of a grain-parcher; met. of a fellow who handles dirty and disorderly things, such as piles of dry leaves and grass, smoke, etc. -wān m. a grain-parcher's shop or stand where he parches grain.
f. the profession, or trade, of a grain-parcher.

adj. c.g. and subst. m. holding or raising up; a bearer, supporter, carrier; -˚ as in chēri-bardār, a wand-bearer (Śiv. 1153); kharca-bᵒ, a man responsible for, or in charge of, expenditure, a head steward (Śiv. 1154); murachala-bᵒ, a fan (or whisk) bearer (Śiv. 1148).
in the following: bardāri bardāri dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to pull a person or thing towards oneself and beat him or it. --bardāri kaḍun -- m.inf. to pull a person out of his place and drive him away.
m. endurance, patience; taking goods on credit, a credit transaction. --khārun -- m.inf. to give goods on credit (Rām. 1312).
m. a leaf (of a tree or paper) (Śiv. 983, see barg 2, and El.) -hanā f. a small piece of paper (Gr.M.). -paiwand برگ پیوند m. grafting, budding (L. 458). Cf. pana-barg (Śiv. 994).
m. radiance; N. of Śiva (Śiv. 983, with double meaning, referring to barg 1). -shikhā f. N. of a mountain sacred to Śiva.

m. a descendant of Bhṛgu, see brug 1. bārgava-rām m. Rāma, the descendant of Bhṛgu, Paraśu-rāma, who is said to have wiped the Kṣatriya tribe out of existence, the sixth avatār, or incarnation, of Viṣṇu (Śiv. 860).

m.pl. small bits of the skin of the body of a living animal, such as those rubbed off by galling, or the top of a blister, etc. --tulȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to raise bits of skin, utterly to wear a person out with carrying burdens or the like, so that his body becomes raw and blistered. --wŏthȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. bits of skin to rise, to be worn out with excessive carrying of burdens or the like.
adj. c.g. confused, jumbled together, turned upside down, entangled, spoiled. barham-darham برہم درہم or darham-barham درہم برہم adj. c.g. confused, entangled, topsy-turvy (Rām. 229).

f. confusion, trouble, anarchy; utter destruction. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. utter destruction to occur, to be utterly destroyed or driven to destitution owing to the destruction of house, land, livelihood, wealth, protectors, friends, etc.
they were muddied by him, see barun 2.
(cf. برّش) f. (pl. nom. bȧrⁱshĕ), a sharp-pointed spear, lance (H. viii, 7; Rām. 872). bȧrⁱshĕ-bardār m. a lancer, a soldier armed with a lance.

adj. c.g. full (Śiv. 24), filled (K.Pr. 82, 119); governs the abl. as in ʦēnyau barith, full of pillars (Gr.M.), tīza barith, full of glory (Śiv. 919). --karun -- m.inf. to fill (El., who spells the word bȧrrit). The word is properly the conj. part. of barun 1, q.v.
adj. c.g. fixed, established, firm, unchangeable (Gr.M.).

in the following: --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to set a person in front (for almost certain death, as in a sudden attack in battle or in a sudden calamity), to dispatch on a forlorn hope. --lagun -- m.inf. to be set in front (for almost certain death, as in a sudden attack in battle or in any great disaster). --lāgun -- m.inf., i.q. barkari dyunᵘ.

m. (sg. dat. barkatas), increase, abundance, prosperity, blessing (K.Pr. 79, 150); Kāshmīrī Musalmāns use this word for 'one' in counting, instead of akh, by way of asking God's blessing on the whole transaction.
adj. c.g. rising, broken up, dismissed (of a meeting or court) (Gr.M.); removed from office, dismissed.
(?), f. a Kāshmīrī custom, the celebration of the day of a person's death (L. 258).
adj. c.g. contradictory, inconsistent. --hāwun -- m.inf. to show the reverse, to misrepresent (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. prosperous, successful, happy, enjoying long life and prosperity (K.Pr. 248).

m. trust, confidence (in a person), esp. general trust reposed in a man of good repute; credit, good repute. --tulun -- m.inf. to destroy credit (e.g. by making public a person's bad conduct, or by spreading a report as to his poverty). --wŏthun -- m.inf. credit or good repute to be lost (owing to a person becoming bankrupt or the like). --wŏthith gaʦhun -- m.f. id.

m. (H. vii, 24, barᵃm), an auger, drill, a kind of gimlet or borer worked with a string. --karun -- m.inf. to bore holes (H. vii, 24). -tujⁱ or -tujᵘ̈ f. the metal point of an auger, a drill-point. --tārun -- m.inf. to bore with an auger. -trọ̆pᵘ m. joining together by auger-holes, as when two pieces of metal or leather have holes drilled along the edges, through which string or wire is passed to fasten them together. -trŏpal c.g. sewed through drill holes (of shoes or the like, in which holes for the thread are first drilled with an auger).

or -mandiñ m. midday. ¶ bar-mandĕñukᵘ adj. (f. -mandĕñücᵘ̈), of or belonging to midday. ¶ bar-mandĕñĕn or -mandiñĕn adv. at midday (Śiv. 1756). -mandĕñĕn bögⁱ (or bögin)  adv. at about midday. ¶ bar-mandĕñĕs adv. at midday. -mandĕñĕs bögⁱ (or bögin)  adv. at about midday.
m. a man whose profession is to wind the woof in the shuttle for weaving woollen cloth.
or barpāh adj. c.g. on foot, erected, established. --āsun -- m.inf. to be set on foot, established, to be zealously engaged in any work (Rām. 573).
m.inf. to provoke, incite, persuade a person to do anything.
adj. c.g. quite full, brimful, chokeful, crammed, replete.

m. arrogance, the insolence of a low person suddenly raised to power; used in the following:-- ¶ barsas āmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), come to arrogance, arrogant. --anun -- m.inf. to bring to arrogance, to cause a person to be arrogant. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come to arrogance, to become arrogant (of a mean person suddenly elevated).

m. (sg. dat. barsātas), the rainy season; rain in general (Śiv. 1551). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat the rains; hence, to suffer from the rotting, fermenting, or mustiness which occurs to articles in the rainy season. -kāl m. the period of the rainy season (July-September). -lad adj. c.g. decayed, fermented, musty, maggoty, owing to the damp of the rainy season. --lagun -- m.inf. to decay, grow musty, infected with maggots, etc., owing to the damp of the rainy season. -zad adj. c.g. decayed, rotten, infected with maggots owing to the damp of the rainy season. ¶ barsātas-kyutᵘ adj. in, during, or at some time in the rainy season.
adj. (f. barsāvë˘ʦᵘ̈), possessing wealth and property, rich, well-to-do (Gr.Gr. 137).
f. a certain medicine used for catarrhs, made up of almond juice, cardamoms, saffron, musk, and other ingredients.
or bartāh (El. barthā), m. a husband (Rām. 323, 656, 661, bartā; 159, 756, 1641, bartāh). bartā-rüʦhᵘ̈ f. a woman deprived of her husband, one who has been abandoned by her husband (Rām. 1205).
m. the common or greater plantain, Plantago major (El.) (not the plantain-fruit or banana, the botanical name of which is Musa).
adj. (f.barücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a door. Prop. gen. of bar 1, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. borᵘ 2, for borᵘ 1, see s.v.), to fill (K.Pr. 95; YZ. 373, 374; Śiv. 24, 1169, 1345, 1784); to fill (with joy, sorrow, faith, etc.) (Śiv. 171, 925, 1587); to perform, fulfil (e.g. a hope or wish), complete; to pay (the penalty of), undergo, suffer, endure; to attain to, enjoy, experience (love, happiness, sorrow, etc.) (YZ. 252, Śiv. 1113, 1645); to feel and maintain (love, faith etc.) (Śiv. 1171, 1174); to pass (time) (Śiv. 799, 1065, 1584). --cāv, to fill a wish, to desire ardently, covet (K.Pr. 247); to fulfil a desire (YZ. 31). --gam, to suffer grief, to be sorrowful, anxious (YZ. 38). ¶ bȧrⁱ bȧrⁱ freq. part. continually filling, filling over and over again (YZ. 343, Śiv. 1079, 1400); used as an adj. very full (Śiv. 520, 1245, 1524). ¶ borᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. bürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), filled, brimful. ¶ barana yunᵘ 1 m. inf. pass. to become filled (e.g. a vessel or a river), to become brimful (Śiv. 1234, 1286). ¶ barith dyunᵘ m.inf. to fill, to fill up (YZ. 222).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. borᵘ 3; for borᵘ 1 see s.v.), to smear, daub, stain, defile, pollute (K.Pr. 121, of a wet dog dirtying people). borᵘ-motᵘ 2, perf. part. defiled, dirtied (of clothes) (Śiv. 1022).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. baryōv), to pine in absence from home or friends, to be homesick. ¶ barana āmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈--), becomehomesick. --yunᵘ 2 -- m. inf. pass. to become homesick.

a door (Śiv. 207, 1890); cf. bar 1. ¶ barañĕ-bal m. N. of a certain narrow pass or cleft in the mountain wide enough for only one person at a time, through which pilgrims pass on the way from Śrīnagar to Gangābal (Śiv. 1176, 1890); in Śiv. 1890 also used met. to signify the maṇipūra, or mystical circle on the navel, referred to in Yōga philosophy.
m. the N. of a village about seven kōs south-east of Śrīnagar. The site of the ancient Viśvaikasāra, a sacred spot said to give beatitude to those who die there; see RT.Tr. I, 192, and II, 460.
m. (sg. dat. baratas, gen. barathunᵘ, Rām. 891, 1353), N. of the brother of Rāma-candra, in Sanskrit Bharata (Rām. 5, 83, 275, 288, etc.).
m. (sg. dat. baratas), a dish or other vessel made of an alloy of several metals melted together.
or m. (sg. dat. baratas or), N. of a hill about fifteen kōs north of Śrīnagar on the pilgrim-route to Gangābal (K.Pr. 233), also called Bhutēśa; cf. buthⁱ-shēr. barata-bāl or id. (Śiv. 1890).

m. fullness, repletion (lit. and met.). --karun -- m.inf. to make fullness, to fill (e.g. anything empty, or a poor man with wealth, or a disciple with virtue, etc.). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. fullness to occur, as ab.
adj. c.g. lance-headed, fitted with an extremity like a lance.
or bö̃s 1 m. a buffalo (El.), i.q. maĩsh, q.v. The word should probably be baĩsh or bö̃sh.

adj. c.g. enough, sufficient (YZ. 185, Rām. 162); sufficient, competent (Śiv. 1712); adv. in short, in a word; very much, greatly (YZ. 77); interj. enough! that will do! hold! stay! az-bas ازبس adv. from the abundance; sufficiently; very extremely (Rām. 378). --karun -- m.inf. to stop, have done, cease, desist (Śiv. 121, 837, 1298, Rām. 198). --thāv -- interj. enough! (El.).

f. fine dust (of charcoal, cowdung fuel, or the like); fine powder (as of salt or the like). ¶ basa-nār m. powder-fire, a very hot fire of burning powdered charcoal, cf. basi- nār bel. ¶ basi-nūn m. salt-powder, the powder that accumulates from the frequent handling of blocks of salt in the course of sale. -nār m., i.q. basa-nār ab. -pholᵘ m. a collection of powder (of cowdung fuel, charcoal, salt, etc.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bāsanôwᵘ), to make a thing visible, esp. to make a thing, that is ordinarily not visible, visible on close inspection (Śiv. 1612, 1660, 1882, Rām. 1660). Cf. bāsanun and Gr.Gr. 175. bāsanôwᵘ-motᵘ adj. (f. bāsanöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made visible to close inspection.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. basanôwᵘ), to cause to dwell, to settle (a man of wandering habits) in a permanent residence (Śiv. 1784).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. basanôwᵘ), to cause a thing to become yellow; to cause it to smell fetid; to cause it to become yellow, swollen, and rotten. Cf. basanun and busun.
m. the colour of spring flowers, mustard-yellow, applied specially to garments (Śiv. 1784).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. basanyōv), to become yellow; to go rotten and turn yellow (of things); to become sick with jaundice, or shrivelled and yellow from old age or illness. Cf. busun; impers. pass. basanana yunᵘ m.inf. (in agric.), a growth of thorns to arise (Śiv. 1111, of a hedge). basanyō-motᵘ adj. (f. basanyē-müʦᵘ), spoilt by turning yellow from heat and rottenness; yellow and swollen from disease.

conj. 1 (2 p.p. bāsanyōv. The occurrence of the 1 p.p. has not been noted), to cause something invisible to become visible; to make a thing or idea visible or cognizable to another. Cf. bāsanā-wun. bāsanyō-motᵘ adj. (f. bāsanyē-müʦᵘ̈), made apparent, made cognizable (of something invisible or non-cognizable to most people, but which becomes apparent on close inspection).
m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who inhabits; a settled inhabitant.

adv. to an end, at an end, used in the following. --anun -- m.inf. to worry, harass, by putting pressure on a person, to keep him working to the end of some long and difficult work. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be compelled or have pressure put upon to keep on to the end of some long and difficult task.
in --anun -- m.inf. to distress or worry a person by insisting on his accomplishing some difficult or impossible task.
f. payment for residence, the rent of a house.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. basôwᵘ), to cause to dwell, to settle a person (esp. a newly married woman) in a new residence. basôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. basöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), one who is caused to settle; one who is compelled against his or her will to adopt a settled mode of life.
m. (f.basawüñᵘ̈), one who inhabits (a house or the like), whether regularly or temporarily, a dweller (Śiv. 737, 817, 1152, 1188, 1324, 1846).

m. (f. bāsawüñᵘ̈), that which is apparent, manifest (Śiv. 104, 512, 1325, 1525); just visible (of something hitherto invisible, but now apparent to the intellect or to the sight, by considering closely or looking keenly).

m. understanding, sense, consideration, thinking about anything (K.Pr. 91). --thawun -- m.inf. to employ consideration, to act intelligently. ¶ bāshĕ-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), wanting in consideration or not applying the understanding; adv. without consideration, carelessly. -wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), a careful, intelligent person.
m. a kind of falcon; a hawk, sparrow-hawk (Śiv. 1693).

f. the inarticulate cry of an infant (Rām. 1284, 1286); the inarticulate sounds uttered by one who is dumb (K.Pr. 93); infantile babbling (used deprecatingly of a worshipper's language in addressing God) (Śiv. 157, Rām. 1102, 1107, 1108); the inarticulate cries or chirping of birds (Śiv. 502, 1052, 1693, 1783, 1816). Cf. bōl-bāshĕ. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of a young infant) to commence to speak, to begin to say 'papa', 'mamma', etc.; met. of the Deity teaching His worshippers to address Him in right language (Śiv. 1386).
or conj. 1 (1 p.p. bôshᵘ), to speak, utter words. bôshᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bösh ᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), spoken; (of something concealed) openly spoken about, disclosed.
m. the sun; N. of Śiva (Śiv. 1163).

or m. ashes (as used in Hindū purificatory ceremonies), esp. ashes of incense and the like. Yōgīs especially smear their bodies with these, and Śiva is represented as having his body covered with them. The word is frequently employed with the suffix āh of the indefinite article, and then appears as . basm (Śiv. 878, 978, 1350, 1541, 1572, Rām. 1081); basmāh (Śiv. 503, 529, 592, 816, 894). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be reduced to ashes (Rām. 1360). --malun -- m.inf. to smear the body with ashes of incense, a religious act of purification, esp. amongst worshippers of Śiva (Rām. 389). ¶ basma-golᵘ  m. N. of the rent in the earth, to the north-west end of the Walur Lake and below Warahmūl, by which the waters of the valley escaped (El.). See RT.Tr. II, 389; Śiv. 1572. -pö̃ʦam f. the fifth (lunar day) of ashes; the fifth of the light half of Māg (Māgha). On the fourteenth day of the dark half of the month of Māg Hindūs worship Śiva, and after fasting collect ashes. These ashes are smeared on the body as a purificatory ceremony on the fifth lunar day of the following light half of the same month. -ṭyokᵘ m. a spot of incense-ashes marked on the forehead of Hindūs at the commencement of worship.
m. he who has ashes smeared upon his body; N. of Śiva (see basm) (Śiv. 161, 621, 622, 937, 1180, 1480, 1583).

m. N. of an Asŏr (Asura) or demon, called in Sanskrit Bhasmāsura. His name was originally Vṛkāsura. He burnt his own flesh to ashes as an offering to Śiva, and was restored to his original form by a touch from that deity (Śiv. 932). Cf. basm.

or bāsmath f. (sg. dat. bāsmüʦᵘ̈), a certain kind of paddy bearing a small, white, longish, and very fragrant rice (L. 332, 463), and growing near Nathipor in the Yich Pargana (El.); the rice borne by this paddy. bāsmȧti-görⁱ m.pl. a small white kind of Singāra or water-nut (gôrᵘ) (L. 354).
conj. 1 to reduce to ashes, consume (K. 740).

f. the act of dwelling, habitation, used in the following. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to settle of one's own free will, or to take up one's habitation, amongst strange folk (e.g. a newly married woman). --karawunᵘ -- m. (f. karawüñᵘ̈), one who takes to a settled life amongst people (usually amongst strangers), after leading an unsettled life.

adj. c.g. and subst.m. bound, shut, closed, fastened up, folded up, impeded; a thing shut up, a secret (K.Pr. 41, where bastih is probably a misprint for bastah, i.e. basta); cloth in which anything is folded up, a wrapper; a parcel, bundle (as of papers or books), a bale; das-basta for dast-basta دست بستہ with folded hands, engaged in prayer (Śiv. 188); kamar-basta کمر بستہ having the loins girt, in a state of readiness, on the alert, ready for action (Rām. 573). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become shut up, imprisoned; to become puzzled or perplexed, to find oneself in a dilemma (as an argument or the like); to become stopped in one's work for want of materials; to become shut (of a door), to become fastened. --karun -- m.inf. to bind (El.); to shut up, imprison; to puzzle a person in an argument, to reduce him to a dilemma; to stop a person's work by stopping the supply of materials; to shut a door, etc., to fasten up. -phurāo, m. the name of the fourth weeding and working of a rice crop (L. 463). --rōzun -- m.inf. to be or remain voluntarily shut up in a room or imprisoned; to stop working (through laziness, etc.).

f. sheepskin, goatskin, deerskin, or the like (K.Pr. 26, 84); a leather bag or sack for carrying grain, salt, flour, or the like (K.Pr. 36, bastan, pl. dat.), 99 (basti, sg. dat., cf. W. 124), 158 (bastai = basta + emph. y); a blister (El.); a beggar's wallet (El., m.); pl. met. the skin of a man, bastan andar, within the skin, in a man's natural self (K.Pr. 2). daman-basta, a bellows (K.Pr. 46). -gorᵘ m. a skin-worker, one who lives by preparing sheepskins, goatskins, deerskins, or the like for sale. -khalᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. an old crumpled piece of sheepskin, etc. --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a blister to rise from a burn or on the foot, etc. -kaṭürᵘ̈ f. a dried-up, shrivelled, sheepskin, etc.; a piece of such. -rangur m. (f. -rangᵘ̈rᵘ̈), a dyer of sheepskin, etc.; the f. is a woman who lives by this trade. --ʦhunᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take to begging (usually of a respectable person, who throws off his shame and takes to this practice). --wālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to skin or flay a sheep, goat, deer, etc.; to flay a man alive (H. viii, 6). -wālay f. the profession or trade of skinning sheep, etc.; the work of a flayer, in scraping, etc., the skins.
see basta 1 and cf. basti under basta 2.
m. a skin sack or bag for carrying paddy, etc., of the contents of about a khār (say 150 lb.); (El. bustúr) the bag in which coolies or porters carry their supply of provisions.

conj. 2 [1 p.p. bosᵘ 2, f. büsᵘ̈ (or,rarely, büʦhᵘ̈), f.pl. basa (or, rarely, baʦha) (Gr.Gr. 31), for bosᵘ 1 see s.v.; 2 p.p. basōv (or, rarely, baʦhōv)], to dwell, abide (Śiv. 674, 1646). --lasun -- m.inf. (1 p.p. bosᵘ-lūstᵘ), to dwell (and) to live long; to be a hereditary householder, to dwell from generation to generation in one place. ¶ bosᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. büsᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of persons) long settled in any house or village, an old inhabitant; (of house, village, etc.) settled, long inhabited by somebody. ¶ basan-jāy f. a dwelling-place (Rām. 1742).

conj. 2 or 3 [1 p.p. bôsᵘ, 2 p.p. bāsyōv (Śiv. 1187) or bāsōv; poet. pres. part. bāsan (e.g. Śiv. 981). This verb is usually treated as belonging to the 3rd conj., but some authorities class it as belonging to the 2nd], to become visible, become apparent, come into view (Siv. 1187, 1650); to become visible, reveal oneself (of a supernatural being) (Śiv. 1435, 1441, 1480, 1586, 1642, 1763, 1769); to become just visible on close inspection; to become cognizable to the senses (Śiv. 171, 883, 981, 1280, 1655, 1900); to become apparent, intelligible, cognizable by the intellect; to be visible, apparent (Śiv. 57, 72, 1374, 1724, 1757); to appear, to seem (Śiv. 1310, 1585, 1657). bāsana yunᵘ m. inf. pass. to become apparent, to become just visible. bāsyō-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. bāsyē-müʦᵘ̈) (for 2 see s.v.), that which has become apparent or just visible; just cognizable by thought.
adj. (f. bāsyē-müʦᵘ̈) (for bāsyō-motᵘ 1, see under bāsun), stale, not fresh (of food or news).

or bastī f. settling, settlement, taking up a fixed residence (in a new home); a settlement, village, a place where people live as a settled community (Siv. 1349). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause a person to raise or set up a family by taking a wife, setting up house, or (when childless) by adopting a son. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to definitely set up house, to adopt a settled life, to range oneself (of one who has hitherto led an unsettled life). --lagᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to set up a family, become a family man by taking a wife (of one long unmarried), or (of one who has given up the hope of progeny) to get a son at last.
m. a frequent termination of Musalmān proper names in Kashmīr, as in Tāz Baṭ, etc. It probably indicates that its owner belongs to a family originally Hindū (El., K.Pr. 13). Cf. baṭa.

m. boiled rice (K.Pr. 26, 27, 226; Śiv. 45); food (K.Pr. 59, 94, 124, 137, 145, 163, 253; W. 135, 149); diet, a meal (K.Pr. 41, 114, 159); pl. kinds of food (K.Pr. 29, abl. batav for batau; 139, batani for batanᵘ̈y, pl. dat. with emph. y); dayĕ-bata, God's food, the sacramental food eaten together by a bride and bridegroom; see day (Śiv. 1202, 1223). -bab m. a father who provides food, one who acts in the capacity of a father by supporting and supplying food to anyone. -boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈, sg. dat. -bajĕ), one who has achieved greatness by liberality in giving of food to people in general; famed for lavish generosity in distributing food. --bögᵃrun -- m.inf. to divide out cooked rice, to give helpings of food; met. to allot good fortune or prosperity to people in general, so much to each (of the Deity) (Śiv. 1510). -bagav m. a food-glutton, one who is always desirous of frequent meals and nothing else. -bajĕr m. a great reputation depending on lavishness in the distribution of food. -böjᵃran f. the division or helping of rice and other food at a dinner. -bọ̆kᵘ m. a handful of cooked rice, as much as can be taken in the palm with the fingers extended; met. any small amount of cooked rice. -bāna m. a dish for cooked food, a plate (W. 111). -brôrᵘ m. an image of a god made of cooked rice mixed with clarified butter, milk, etc. These are worshipped at the śrāddha ceremony by Brāhmaṇs of the Tāntrik order. The image may be really a rough representation, or may be a simple ball of rice, etc. -börav c.g. a rice-demon, one who is accustomed to gorge himself with food. -bôsᵘ m. a rice-belly, the stomach full of cooked rice just eaten. -bata m. "rice, rice!"; hence, famine, general inability to obtain food; starvation, inability of a single person to obtain food (K.Pr. 26). -bata lagun m.inf. famine or starvation to occur. -bath karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to be employed in preparing and distributing food at a banquet. -böʦᵘ̈ m. enough cooked rice for one person, a helping or portion of cooked rice. -dab m. 'rice-flop'; a heavy sleep immediately after the evening meal, when the digestion is only commencing. -daban adv. at bedtime (Gr.Gr. 157). -dôdᵘ m. 'food-pain', anxiety as to subsistence, the anxiety of labour for a livelihood. -dag m. 'food-smarting', id. (K.Pr. 26). -dŏgulᵘ m. a ball of cooked rice. -dāta c.g. (-dāta-bāy, his wife), one who provides food, a provider of subsistence; (of God) 'the Provider'. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to feed (tr.) (El.). -grās m. a gobbet of rice, the ball of rice in the hands which is put into the mouth at one time; an amount of rice equal to such a mouthful. -gāsh m. 'rice-brilliancy', abundance or cheapness of food. -khan gaʦhȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. 'food-pits to happen'; extreme hunger (due to long-continued want of food) to occur. -khĕv m. dinner (L. 459, battakheu). -khĕwawañ f. 'wages for eating food'; a present given by a bride's relations to her husband's people on the occasion of her first meal in her husband's house. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take food, to eat something (K.Pr. 5, 237). --khyāwun -- m.inf. to give food to eat; esp. (of the parents of a bride to the parents of the bridegroom, or vice versa) to give a feast or dinner-party on the occasion of some festival. -khyāwañ f., i.q. -khĕwawañ, ab. -kāl m. cooked rice sufficient for a single meal. -kulᵘ m. 'the rice-tree', the bread-winner of a household. -kan m. a very small ball of cooked rice, smaller even than a mouthful; a very little cooked rice. -krakh f. (sg. dat. -kraki), 'rice noise,' the outcry raised by a mob of people assembled at a feast when there is not enough food to go round, when there is confusion in the service, or other similar cause. -lŏkhᵃr f. a solid mass of cooked rice in a dish, a rice-shape (K.Pr. 27). -langȧrⁱ f. a pile of cooked rice ready for a large number of eaters. -lūrᵘ̈ f. 'food-cudgel', want of livelihood, inability to support oneself. -lūrᵘ̈diñᵘ̈ f.inf. to injure or destroy a person's means of livelihood. -lūrᵘ̈ lagüñᵘ̈ f.inf. a person's means of livelihood to be destroyed. -mar m. a storehouse for food, a rice store (K.Pr. 240). -më̆ṭᵘ̈ f. a fistful of cooked rice; a genl. term for a small amount of the same. -mŏyā f. a little boiled rice, a small amount of boiled rice (Gr.Gr. 165). -myonḍᵘ m. a mouthful of cooked rice, as much as is taken into the mouth at one time; a genl. term for a small amount of the same. -nĕnd f. a plate piled up with cooked rice for one person's eating. -nĕng f. a large pile of rice prepared for a man's single daily dinner, the night-meal, dinner. -nĕngan adv. at dinner-time, at the time of the night-meal, while at dinner (Gr.Gr. 157). -pholᵘ or -pholwā (Gr.Gr. 164) m. a single grain of cooked rice; met. a very small amount of the same (K.Pr. 4). -phȧlⁱ-pöthⁱr m. rice-grains-conduct; interested love, pretence of love for interested motives, pot-love, cupboard-love. -pāṭh m. (sg. dat. -pāṭhas), recitation of charms or prayers for food, either for people generally or for some particular person. -rôyᵘ m. King Food, a term applied honorifically on seeing some great pile of grain or a plenteous crop in the field. -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -söwᵘ̈), rich or well supplied with grain and other similar food, one whose barns are well filled. -sāvĕr m. the condition of one whose barns are well filled, easy circumstances, opulence. -sāway f. food luxuriance, plenteousness of crops, the condition of a land flowing with milk and honey, cheapness of food. -ṭīrᵘ̈ f. a mass of congealed cooked rice, a rice-shape. -wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), one who possesses much cooked rice or food (El.), one who is well-to-do; one who is accustomed to distribute food in charity or to give free dinners (K.Pr. 62). -wata m. a jingling repetition of bata, cooked rice, etc.; cooked rice and other similar articles of food, cooked rice and its usual accompaniments (Gr.Gr. 95). -wāv m. rice-wind; poverty so great that food is wanting, destitution, indigence. -wāv pyonᵘ m.inf. poverty to fall; the destitution by the death, etc., of the breadwinner of a family to happen. ¶ bȧtⁱ yunᵘ m.inf. to become arrogant on obtaining, without working for it, a great supply of food or wealth. ¶ batas pyonᵘ m.inf. to fall for food; to fall upon someone for support, as when a family's breadwinner dies and the members of the family throw themselves upon someone else for their support. --rōzun -- m.inf. to wait for food; to have one's food stopped, to be deprived of one's dinner (as is done in schools as a punishment for a naughty boy). --thawun -- m.inf. to stop a naughty child's food as a punishment, to give him no dinner.

m. (f. baṭañ or baṭiñ q.v.), a brāhmaṇ, a Kāshmīrī Hindū (all of whom are brāhmaṇs), a Kāshmīrī Paṇḍit (K.Pr. 26-8, 72, 116, 139, 147, W. 123, L. 456), the brāhmaṇ caste. According to El., s.v., the Hindūs of Kashmīr are divided into (1) Brāhmaṇ Hindūs, whose only work is to perform the Hindū worship. In short they are exclusively priestly, and number about 500 houses. (2) The Jōtish Hindūs, who study the stars for the purpose of predicting future events. They number from 100 to 150 houses. (3) The Kārkun Hindūs, who are writers, merchants, and farmers, but never soldiers. Relatively, this is a very numerous class. -bāy f. a brāhmaṇ's wife (Gr.Gr. 34). A woman of the brāhmaṇ caste is baṭañ (Gr.Gr. 38), q.v. -bôyᵘ m. a brāhmaṇ brother, a brāhmaṇ caste-fellow; a brāhmaṇ of the same rank or degree, who can eat and drink with another brāhmaṇ, with whom he is compared. -cŏbur m. (sg. dat. -cŏbaras), a young brāhmaṇ, able-bodied but uneducated. -dāy f. the servant-girl of a brāhmaṇ (usually of some lower degree in caste). -gān m. a brāhmaṇ who lives on the proceeds of his wife's adultery (K.Pr. 107); a term of abuse not necessarily implying the truth of the accusation. -hörᵘ̈ f. a sort of bird, a kind of yellow-coloured hörᵘ̈ (śārīkā, or mainā); also the name of a kind of vulture. -kūrᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kōrĕ), an unmarried girl or virgin of the brāhmaṇ caste (cf. Gr.Gr. 73). -krüñᵘ̈ f. N. of a certain wild herbaceous medicinal plant, described as low-growing, with long fine leaves from which a medicine is decocted. -koṭᵘ m. a boy of the brāhmaṇ caste; a brahmaṇ's son, a real son of a brāhmaṇ, i.e. a good brāhmaṇ (Gr.Gr. 132). -mahanyuvᵘ m. a brāhmaṇ-man, a menial brāhmaṇ who lives by acting as a cook or in other similar menial service; cf. baṭañ. -mahanivⁱ-koṭⁱ m. (f. -küṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. -kacĕ), the son (f. daughter) of such a menial brāhmaṇ. -mahanivⁱ-kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), the son of a menial brāhmaṇ, used only contemptuously. -mahanivⁱ-kār m. the menial work done by a menial brāhmaṇ. -mahanivī f. the profession or condition of a menial brāhmaṇ. -mahanivⁱgi f. the profession, condition, or means of livelihood of a menial brāhmaṇ. -morᵘ m. a brāhmaṇ's body (to be protected and kept free from defilement by obeying rules of conduct). -nĕcyuvᵘ m. a brāhmaṇ's son, generally employed in a complimentary sense of an intelligent youth. -pöṭhⁱ adv. like a brāhmaṇ, in the manner employed by brāhmaṇs, according to rule (of conduct, giving gifts, or the like). -ʦhürᵘ̈ m. N. of a certain medicinal plant, described as having small spiny leaves which creep along the ground.
in bāṭa-wã̄gūn, see bŏṭa-wã̄gun under bŏṭa.
[sic], adj. c.g. courteous (K.Pr. 30). This word has not been elsewhere identified, and if the meaning given in K.Pr. is correct there is probably some mistake in the spelling.

(Gr.Gr. 38), or baṭiñ f. a female Brāhmaṇ, a woman of the Brāhmaṇ caste (see baṭa); esp. a maidservant of the Brāhmaṇ caste, a menial Brāhmaṇī, cf. baṭa-mahanyuvᵘ, under baṭa. When employed ˚--, this word takes the form baṭᵃñĕ. ¶ baṭᵃñĕ-pônᵃ m. the condition of being a Brāhmaṇ maidservant, the making a living in such a capacity; (of anyone else) making a similar living. -tônᵘ m. the condition of a Brāhmaṇ woman; esp. the life led by any woman who is well-conducted and careful about ceremonial purity and the like. -wāza m. a man who lives by cooking only for women (esp. Brāhmaṇ women); hence, a cook who does not know his work thoroughly, an inefficient cook.
m. a button (corruption of the English word; the old word, ṭūpⁱ-pholⁱ, with the same meaning, is now superseded by this borrowed term).

adj. c.g. in straits, in difficulties; distressed, harassed, vexed. --anun -- m.inf. to worry, plague a person for something impossible or unobtainable. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be worried, distressed, have one's heart broken in trying to do something unsuccessfully.
for batanᵘ̈y, pl. dat. of bata, with emph. y (K.Pr. 139).

m. (lit. filled with wind), a certain sweetmeat of a spongy texture and hollow within (K.Pr. 28); a kind of cheap brown sugar, which comes from the Panjāb (L. 254). -khünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -khanjĕ), a piece of this sweetmeat. -worᵘ m. N. of a special variety of this sweetmeat.
prep. after the manner of, by way of (governs abl.) (Gr.M.).
f. Saturday (K.Pr. 231, W. 106). ¶ baṭawāri-dŏh adv. on Saturday. -hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to Saturday.

m. the name of a place in Kashmīr about six miles south-east of Śrīnagar. baṭawörⁱ-bāy f. a class of fish-wives who carry fish on their heads in baskets and cry their wares through the Śrīnagar markets. The fish are netted in the Vĕth (Jehlam), near Baṭawôrᵘ. baṭawāryukᵘ adj. (f. baṭawāricᵘ̈), of or belonging to Baṭawôrᵘ.
m. a certain bird, the quail.
f. (sg. dat. baṭi), a sec. suff. used in the word böjⁱbaṭh (see bôjᵘ), commensality or partnership (Gr.Gr. 145).

f. (sg. dat. bāti), a word, speech, language (YZ. 382); talk, gossip, report, discourse, news, tale, story, account (Rām. 659); thing, affair, matter, business, concern. katha-bāta, f.pl. conversation (Gr.M.).

or m. (sg. dat. bāṭas), the noise of crying, esp. the howling or yelling of a beaten or angry child, or the noisy crying of a woman. -baṭil f. id., esp. when excessive. -baṭil lagüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to start making the noise of crying, esp. of a number of grief-stricken or angry people. --lāgun -- m.inf. to commence yelling and weeping (of a beaten child or an angry woman). --wahārun -- m.inf. to commence weeping and yelling like a beaten child or angry woman, of one who is not actually beaten or angry.

f. (sg. dat. bāti), a scheme, plan, means, expedient, device, esp. for the performance of some difficult task (Rām. 471, 836). ¶ bāti anun m.inf. to point out, show; to explain, make comprehensible. --khasun -- m.inf. to become clearly manifest to the sight or intellect; (of a wished-for object) to come into sight, to become as one desires. --khotᵘ-motᵘ -- adj. (f. --khüʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), become clearly manifest to the sight or intellect; become or turned out as one desires. --yunᵘ -- m.inf., i.q. --khasun.
m. (sg. dat. bāṭhas), a thicket (of brambles or the like). Cf. böṭhᵘ̈.

m. (sg. dat. bāṭhas), the panegyrist of a king, whose duty it is to proclaim the hour of the day, his master's titles, etc., a herald. ¶ bāṭha-bāy f. a female panegyrist, as ab.; the wife of a panegyrist.
m. (sg. dat. baṭas), a warrior, a soldier; a demon, esp. a demon messenger or apparitor of Yama (the god of the nether world) (L.V. 74). See yĕm 1.

m. the condition of being crooked or bent; the condition of being dented (of some metal or wooden article distorted by a blow or the like); crookedness, distortion; met. of a man's nature. --aʦun -- m.inf. distortion to enter, distortion to occur, either lit. or fig. of character, health, or the like; breakage to occur. --drāv -- adj. (f. --drāyĕ --), that which was distorted and has become straight, straightened out, lit. and fig. as ab. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to take out distortion, to straighten out something which has been distorted, lit. and fig. as ab. --nērun -- m.inf. distortion to go forth, straightening out to occur, lit. and fig.; (of something puzzling or intricate) to be made plain and clear. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause distortion to enter; to distort, make crooked.
adj. c.g. (as subst.f. baṭhaladiñ), bent, curved, crooked, distorted (by a blow or the like); of a man's nature, sullen, suspicious.
(? spelling), adv. on the high ground, towards the hill (K.Pr. 171). Cf. boṭhᵘ 1.
f. the profession of cooking large quantities of rice, wholesale cookery. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to distribute large quantities of cooked rice.
f. the condition of being a brāhmaṇ, brāhmaṇhood.
c.g. one who through miserliness or the like is in the mean habit of living upon food given in charity by others, even though he have sufficient wealth to support himself.
f. the condition of living on food given by others in charity, whether due to greed or misfortune; any mean conduct of this sort.
(? spelling of first word), f. a wild trēl, a kind of apple (L. 349). See trēl.

(Gr.Gr. 30, 36, 58) or batukh بتخ m. [sg. dat. batakas (Gr.Gr. 58), pl. nom. batakh; f. batᵘ̈cᵘ̈ (Gr.Gr. 30, 36), or batᵃc (Gr.Gr. 66)], a drake (K.Pr. 117, W. 21, 129); (f.) a duck (W. 17). ¶ batakh-lyūṭᵘ m. a certain medicinal plant growing in marshes and watercourses and having a firm, white flower (Rām. 646); clover (L. 70, 359); cf. lyūṭᵘ, and under dã̄d, dā̃da-lyūṭᵘ. -pŏṭh f. (sg. dat. -pŏṭi), duck's gut, a certain plant, the pounded leaves of which have an intoxicating effect when taken in the form of a pill.
conj. 3 (of the sun) to shine forth (noted only in L.V. 16).
adv. with sharpness, with severity, with acrimony (Rām. 497); violently, fiercely, with fury (Rām. 376).

m. a kind of quail, cf. baṭēra. --athi lagun -- m.inf. the quail to come into the hand; the means for carrying out any desired object to be gained. --pyonᵘ -- m.f. the quail to fall; something eagerly desired to be suddenly and unexpectedly acquired, to drop from the clouds.
m. a globular metal vessel, cast in one piece, used for cooking; the baṭlōhī or lōṭā of India.
m. a small bag with divisions or folds, used for holding money, betel-nut, tobacco, etc.

m. existence, birth; worldly existence. ¶ bawa-sāgar , the ocean of worldly existence (Śiv. 14). -santāph m. (sg. dat. -santāpas), the misery, or torment, of existence (according to Hindū pessimism) (Śiv. 1870). -sar m., i.q. -sāgar (K.Pr. 243, Śiv. 14, 155, etc., Rām. 1596).

m. becoming, being; state, condition (Śiv. 1211, with pun on meaning 'market-price', see bel., 1679; Rām. 549, 1781; anubava-bāv, a condition of perception, Śiv. 75, 982; bakti-bāv, the condition of faith, a state of faith, but often equivalent to bȧktⁱ-bāv, faith and love, bel., see bakth, Śiv. 515, 525, 757, 915, etc.; brama-bāv, a condition of delusion, Śiv. 1835; dāsa-bāv, the condition of a servant, Śiv. 620, 1076; gūrⁱ-bāv, the condition of a cowherd, Śiv. 1000, 1837; nȧṭⁱ-bāv, the condition of a well-bucket, Śiv. 1818; shurⁱ-bāv, the condition of a child, Śiv. 1015); conduct, behaviour; way of thinking, feeling, sentiment, opinion (advaita-bāv, acceptance of the doctrine of monism, Śiv. 26); love, affection, devotional love shown to a deity, i.q. bakth (Śiv. 484, 531, 670, 772, 790, etc.; bȧktⁱ-bāv, love and affection, Śiv. 188; bāwāh, with suff. of indef. art., 1083); affectionate respect, consideration, honour (Rām. 84, 317), cf. ādar-bāw; power of discrimination (Śiv. 1548); a high value put upon anything (Śiv. 1808); price-current, market-rate (Śiv. 1211, see ab.); prosperity in business (Gr.M.). --baḍun -- m.inf. respect to go forward; to show pretended compliance to an order (given by a senior, a superior, a teacher, or the like). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to show respect, to rise from one's seat through politeness or respect. --karun -- m.inf. to make respect; to welcome to one's house with love and honour. --thawun -- m.inf. 'to put honour'; to respect and comply with the order or advice of an elder or superior, the instruction of a teacher, or the like. ¶ bāwa-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), wanting in love, wanting in politeness or respect, rude, genl. used as an adv. -sān adv. politely, respectfully, affectionately. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), possessing love, polite, respectful; possessing respect, respected, honoured. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -v ë̆ʦᵘ̈), loving, faithful, affectionate, or respectful by nature.
m. (sg. dat. bavishĕtas), the future, futurity (Gr.M.).

m. a kind of house; a house with rooms built round and opening into a hollow square, the house of a well-to-do person. --sọ̆mbᵃrun -- or --sọ̆mbᵃrāwun -- m.inf. to lay up a great store of household necessities, as a provision against hard times.

m. 'the habitation', N. of a sacred spring or tīrtha close to the famous temple of Mārtāṇḍa. The large basins filled by the spring are inhabited by an abundance of sacred fish. The Sanskrit name of the place was bhavana (RT.Tr. II, 466; El. s.vv. mártand and maṭan).
f. a feeling of devotion, faith (in), respect, honour directed to a god, a preceptor, a Brāhmaṇ, or the like. i.q. bakth, q.v. (Śiv. 70, 130, etc.).
m. belief, faith, confidence, trust, credit. --karun -- m.inf. to believe, etc. (H. viii, 13).
adj. (as subst., f. bawāsīriladiñ one who suffers from piles; met. a maniac, an incoherent madman.
f. (sg. dat. bāwüʦᵘ̈), showing, telling, information; a declaration of intentions, an expression of one's wishes, a giving of instructions. Cf. bāwun 1, of which it is the abs. noun (Gr.Gr. 128).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. bāwazyōv, Gr.Gr. 226), to be liked, preferred; (esp. of food) to be tasty, dainty (Gr.Gr. lv).

f. Bhavānī, N. of the goddess Pārvatī, the wife of Śiva, in her pacific and amiable form (K.Pr. 228, Śiv. 109, 494, etc.). Śiv. makes the sg. dat., etc., of this word sometimes bawöniyĕ  (496) and sometimes bawāñĕ  (79, 80, 1315). -dās m. 'servant of Bhawānī', N. of a Kashmīr worthy, regarding whom a story is told in K.Pr. 254.

m. a kind of armlet worn by women, consisting of ornamental bosses or plates of one of the precious metals strung together. ¶ bāwȧṭⁱ-gulⁱ m. one of a pair of such armlets. -horᵘ m. a pair of such armlets.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bôwᵘ; inf. abl. poet. bāwanēlogᵘ, he began to tell, Śiv. 700), to show, tell, inform, relate (YZ. 454, Śiv. 700, Rām. 292, 453, 1105, etc.); to disclose one's inner thoughts, disclose (a secret) (K.Pr. 23, Śiv. 675, 1633, Rām. 340, H. vii, 21); to confide one's secret intentions, to tell (a friend, etc.) what in one's own opinion is a proper course of conduct (Rām. 1574, 1592, 1764); to explain the meaning of anything (Śiv. 21, 480, 675, 1506, 1130). ¶ bôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. böwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), disclosed, confided (of a secret), etc.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bôwᵘ), to pour a libation of rice-milk or the like over the image of a god, or into running water at some holy bathing-place. ¶ bôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. böwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), poured in libation as above; met. (of anything not a libation) plunged in a flowing river or the like.

f. a brother's daughter, a niece on the brother's side (Gr.Gr. 133, L. 462, Rām. 138). -nŏsh m. the wife of a brother's son, a niece by marriage on the brother's side. -zāmaturᵘ m. the husband of a brother's daughter, a nephew by marriage on the brother's side.

f. a lady, mistress, as in āga-bāy, the wife of the master of a house, the mistress of a house. Cf. K.Pr. 263; Śiv. 1141, 1237, 1491, 1493. Often used as a suffix to indicate the wife of a man of a certain caste or profession. Thus, baṭa-bāy, a Brāhmaṇ's wife, as distinguished from baṭañ, a woman of the Brāhmaṇ caste.
m. a declaration, assertion, statement; explanation, disclosure, description (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to tell, relate, express; to explain, make clear (El.).
adj. c.g. (as subst., m. sg. dat. bayānakas), fearful, terrible, dreadful, formidable.

f. (sg. dat. bayöʦᵘ̈), the act of promising obedience; submission, obedience, allegiance; initiation as a disciple of a saint or religious guide. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to initiate a disciple, etc.; hence, to initiate, to teach a person what to do and what to avoid in any business or course of conduct. --wanüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to utter words of initiation; hence, to give verbal instructions as ab.

m. (in Rām. 1486, bay), fear, alarm, dread, apprehension (Śiv. 962, 1256, 1288, 1648, 1758); righteous fear, the fear of God (K.Pr. 201). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to fill with fear, threaten, scold, make afraid (e.g. a stronger threatening a weaker, a parent scolding a child, a man frightening a beast). -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), smitten by fear, terrified, frightened. -haʦar m. a state of being smitten by fear, a state of terror, a state of fright. --hāwun -- m.inf. to show terror (to another), to intimidate. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat fear, to be frightened at anything, to experience a sensation of fear. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), fearless, without fear (Śiv. 1732); not causing fear, not frightening, not formidable. --rōzun -- m.inf. fear to remain, a condition of fear previously caused (e.g. to a child or an opponent) to continue; having once experienced fear from any cause, that fear to continue for the future. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), awful, terrible. --thawun -- m.inf. to put fear, to put in fear. -ʦhaṭh f. (sg. dat. -ʦhaṭi), tossing up of fear, a sudden attack of fear, terror begotten by a mere apparition, or by the mere appearance of an enemy, etc. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), overcome with fear; in a state of terror owing to some previous fear. ¶ bayĕs-tal rōzun m.inf. to remain subject to somebody under the influence of fear, to be in a state of terror (of somebody). -tal thawun m.inf. to put under one's influence by means of fear, to intimidate.
m. an elder brother; met. any elder relation on the father's side. Cf. bôyᵘ.
adj. c.g., (of dice, or the like) lucky, one that usually gives lucky throws. Cf. bayĕth.
f. (sg. dat. bayüʦᵘ̈), a lucky throw (of dice or the like).

f. a brother's wife, a sister-in-law. Cf. böyⁱ-kākañ under bôyᵘ. ¶ bȧyⁱ-kākañĕ-tônⁱ m. the relationship of sister-in-law (brother's wife) to any person (male or female); met. conduct as such, conduct (affection, etc.) of another woman similar to the conduct of a sister-in-law.

m. playing, gambling; esp. a single play in gaming, a single throw of the dice (Rām. 1351). pŏkhta bāzāh, a winning throw, khām bāzāh, a losing throw (Rām. 298). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. a throw (of dice) to fall; met. to come together (of a number of people who will help one to carry out something just as one wishes to do it, e.g. in some domestic affair, the simultaneous arrival of a wife, sons, and friends all of whom are experienced in the matter).
m. a certain dish, rice fried with spices in ghī, oil, etc.
f. a continual frying, a general frying where a number of dishes are all being fried at the same time, owing to their all being immediately required.
m. a vessel in which things are cooked in hot oil, a frying-pan. See bazun.

m. a street with shops in it, a market, market-place, bazaar, mart (YZ. 40, 253, where the word is spelt bāzār, in imitation of Persian; K.Pr. 78, 103, Śiv. 1211, 1808). In Śiv. 1566 bāzār also occurs m.c. in the sense of market, i.e. traffic of the market. --aʦun -- m.inf. to enter the bazaar; esp. to waste one's money in bazaar enjoyments, to lead a dissolute life. -banga f. a certain food grain, a kind of millet, akin to bājrā (Panicum spicatum or P. italicum). --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause to enter the bazaar; to induce (a respectable youth) to lead a profligate life; to seduce to dissoluteness. --wuchun -- m.inf. to look at the bazaar; to ascertain the market rate of anything, to test the value of anything by comparison with the market price.
m. a cloth-merchant, draper, mercer. bazāza-wān m. a draper's shop (K.Pr. 159), cf. bazözⁱ.
(cf. بزور), adj. c.g. forcible, exercising force, mighty, powerful (Śiv. 677).
m. drapery, linen-drapery, haberdashery, the stock-in-trade of a draper. bazāzi-wān m. a haberdashery, a draper's shop. Cf. bazāz.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bozᵘ, 2 p.p. bazōv), to cook in hot oil, to fry (esp. vegetables and the like). The procedure is to plunge the articles into heated ghī and stir them about with a ladle. It is hardly the same as our frying. Cf. bazyunᵘ 1 and Gr.Gr. 117. ¶ bozᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. büzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), cooked in hot oil, fried.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bozᵘ, 2 p.p. bazōv), lit. to divide, distribute, allot; hence, to lay out money in invitations to festivals; to give away rewards or presents on birthdays and similar occasions of rejoicing; to put down the stakes in gambling; to put down money in compensation for losses, etc. -lazun m.inf. (among relations or friends) mutually to give and receive presents on the birthdays of each other's children and similar festivals. ¶ bozᵘ-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. büzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), lavishly distributed in presents, etc.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. bozᵘ, 2 p.p. bazōv), to serve, honour, revere, love, adore (Gr.Gr. liii). ¶ bozᵘ-motᵘ 3 perf. part. (f. büzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), served, revered.

m. (sg. dat. bazinis; a by-form of bazun, q.v., used as an abstract noun, Gr.Gr. 117, where the word is spelt bazyun), frying, cooking in hot oil. The articles (principally vegetables) are plunged into hot ghī, and stirred about with a ladle; met. the oil used for such cooking (K.Pr. 67, 132, bazin). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give such cooking, hence to cook in hot oil. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat such cooking; hence, to be cooked in hot oil. --lagun -- m.inf., id. ¶ bazinⁱ-dĕgulⁱ m. a kind of large earthen vessel or pot in which vegetables, etc., are cooked in hot oil. -lĕjⁱ f. id., but of small size.
m. (sg. dat. bazinis), a certain vegetable growing wild in the forest, and said to have an acrid smell.

adj. c.g. of or appertaining to the bazaar; easily to be bought anywhere in the bazaar; hence, ordinary, common; low, vulgar. --baṭa -- m. (f. --baṭañ --), a bazaar brāhmaṇ; met. one who lives a double life, outwardly polite and respectful, but inwardly deceitful and guileful. The f. is a woman of this character. --jōsh -- m. bazaar ebullition; met. external brave show of something essentially worthless.
in baʦh barüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to utter distraught lamentations, to lament incoherently (K. 286 (v.l.), 291). Cf. briʦh, ab.
f.pl. the arms (or fore-legs of a wild beast) from the shoulder to the elbow.

or, بے, the Persian privative particle, prefixed to other words, as in bē-adab, without politeness, insolent. It is equivalent in meaning to the Kāshmīrī suff. rostᵘ (q.v.). Although a Persian prefix it is also commonly employed, usually under the form bĕ, with non-Persian words, as in bĕ-bayĕ, fearless. For words commencing with this prefix see s.vv. It is often used as a mere preposition, governing another noun, and meaning 'without', as in yilm bē bahs, knowledge without argument (K.Pr. 216). Similarly, adverbial phrases, such as bē sabab, without cause, causelessly.
the name of the second letter of the Persian alphabet. Alif-bē = a b c, the alphabet.
adj. c.g. without manners, rude, insolent (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. without sense, a fool (K.Pr. 29, 107).
f. want of sense, silliness, folly.
adj. c.g. unused, not put to use (K.Pr. 88).
adj. c.g. (as subst., m. sg. dat. -antas), endless, illimitable (Gr.M.).

f. the inside of a garment in front of the body, the inner fold of the breast of a garment; the inside breast of the long gown worn by Kashmīrīs (K.Pr. 23, 29) used as a kind of pocket. The word is often used to signify generally the space between the body and the clothes. ¶ bĕbi hyonᵘ m.inf. to take into the bosom of one's dress; to take a child to one's bosom, inside one's dress, to warm it, or to console it. -nār m. fire in one's bosom. "Kashmīrīs whilst squatting on the ground in the winter time place their (portable stoves or) kāngars under their long cloak next their skin. Give a Kashmīrī his kāngar and he is perfectly happy. Hence the words bĕbi-nār come to mean without care" (K.Pr. 125). In the following it means exactly the reverse, fire in one's bosom being equivalent to discomfort or pain. -nār lalawun m.inf. to cherish fire in the bosom; to feel trouble or sorrow on account of losses or calamities affecting oneself or those near and dear. -ʦŏ̈ṭᵘ̈ f. a loaf in the bosom, met. any hidden thing which, because it is hidden, is considered to be extra good; a reputation earned for being good at one's trade or clever at one's work (which therefore gives a man a certainty of a comfortable life or a perpetual loaf in his pocket); u.w. ref. to harlots, a loaf (i.e. a means of earning one's livelihood) in one's bosom, something like the English expression "my face is my fortune", but more indecent.
f. lit. searching (for refuge) inside (another's) breast-cloth, hence fear, dread, apprehension, timidity. See bĕb.
adj. c.g. not cooked in oil, ghī, or the like. Cf. abagôrᵘ.
without disputation, without controversy; yilm bē-bahs, knowledge without argument (i.e. without exercise), K.Pr. 216.
adj. c.g. without remainder, complete, paid up in full, (of an account) balanced, settled (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. without fear, without apprehension, without anxiety (Rām. 1283).
adj. c.g. one who, when engaged in any act, does it without care and attention, and perfunctorily. Cf. bāsh.
f. the condition or state of being uninhabited (of a country, village, or house), uninhabitedness, vacancy.
adj. c.g. without fear, fearless; wanting in reverence.
? m. want of discrimination, misgovernment, anarchy (K.Pr. 223).

f. (lit. absence of foundation), non-production, e.g. of crops failing to germinate, or of profits not accruing from one's work. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to destroy utterly, annihilate (a person's entire wealth, crops, profession, or the like), lit. to cause non-existence.
m. the becoming non-existent of some article of general use, such as grain, money, or the like.
adj. c.g., i.q. bĕcôrᵘ, q.v. YZ. 408 and frequently in the Persian character; used as a subst. its dat. is bēcāras (K.Pr. 136).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. bēchanôwᵘ), to set a person to beg; hence, to reduce a person to beggary.
adj. (f. bēchawüñᵘ̈), a beggar, esp. a professional beggar, a mendicant.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. byūchᵘ), to beg, to go daily from door to door asking for alms (K.Pr. 29, 191); bēchan-wôlᵘ, a beggar (L. 458); inf. dat. bēchanas bāna, a beggar's pot in which he collects food (K.Pr. 29), cf. bēcha-bāna under bēcha. ¶ bēchani nērun m.inf. to go forth to beg; hence, to take to the profession of begging.
adj. (f. bicörᵘ̈), without means, without resources, destitute, unfortunate, wretched; a helpless person, a poor wretch.

or bīd m. separation, difference, distinction (manz, between); bīd karun m.inf. to distinguish (Gr.M.). ¶ bīda-nyāy (or -) m. the system or belief in duality, as opposed to the Vēdānta system which maintains the unity of God and the universe (Śiv. 1816). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), free from duality, non-dual; N. of God, who, according to the monism of the Vēdāntic school of philosophy, is one with universe (Śiv. 1077, 1865); one who is a follower of Vēdāntic monism, and repudiates duality of the Deity and the universe (Śiv. 1567).

f. (sg. dat. bīzᵘ̈, and so on), secret or hidden virtues or resources (of); secret, mystery. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to extract the secret; to ascertain the real reason, purport, or object of anything; to find out the real motive. --nanüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a secret to be naked, the unveiling of a mystery; the real purport or object to be discovered. --nạñᵉ̆rudotdot;ñᵉ̆ -- f.inf. to unveil a mystery, disclose the real purport or object of anything.

m. a willow, in -mushᵃkh بید مشک m. (sg. dat. -mushkas), a certain plant, the musk-willow, Salix caprea, from whose flower is produced an essential oil much used in perfumery (L. 77); Salix Ӕgyptiaca (El.).
adj. c.g. ill-shapen, ugly, ungainly; clumsy, awkward, unmannerly.

. For the article bē-dād, substitute the following. bē-dād بے داد adj. c.g. unjust (El.); as subst. m. injustice, affliction (Rām. 289, 875, 892, 939, 1704). dād-i-bēdād m. crying out for help or protection (Rām. 438). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. tyranny, or misery, to happen (to a person), to become distraught (Rām. 756, 1356, 1696).
(cf.بے دانہ) m. the fruit of a species of mulberry (cf. El. s.v túl). bĕdāna-tᵃla-kulᵃ, the special mulberry-tree which produces this fruit (see El. s.v. tulakul).

bēdār بیدار adj. c.g. awake (Rām. 889, 908, 928, 1059, 1189; K.Pr. 25, YZ. 47); wakeful, sleepless; watchful, vigilant, alert (cf. El.). --karun -- m.inf. to awaken from sleep; fig. to awaken the intellect, arouse; attract attention. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be aroused, awakened from sleep; to have the intellect aroused; to have one's attention attracted, to become alert.
in bēḍigaʦhañĕ f. pl. inf. to be ensnared, entangled, impeded.
adj. c.g. (m. sg. dat. bĕdiwatas), ugly, without beauty in appearance, dress, actions, conduct, intelligence, quality, or the like. -pöṭhⁱ or -pöṭhin adv. in an ugly manner; in a wicked way.

f. ugliness, want of beauty, badness in behaviour, dress, actions, intelligence, skill, or the like. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make ugliness, to humiliate a person by abusing him in public, when he expected to be honoured. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take such humiliation, to suffer or undergo it. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such humiliation to fall, humiliation to be experienced.
adj. c.g. shapeless, hence misshapen, ill-fashioned, ugly, clumsy; ill-mannered, ill-bred, uneducated, loutish.
adj. c.g. unprofitable, useless, vain; as adv. in vain, to no purpose, fruitlessly. --kharᵃch -- m. extravagance. --karun -- m.inf. to make in vain, misspend, waste (Gr.M.).
m. a lord, master, a Mogul title of honour (K.Pr. 145).

in bĕgā-wakhᵃth m. (sg. dat. -wakhtas), evening, the first three hours or so after sunset; cf. bē-gāh. -wakhtan, -wakhtan-bögⁱ, -wakhtas, or -wakhtas-bögⁱ adv. at evening, at some time in the first three hours after sunset.
adj. c.g. without sorrow, without fear or anxiety (Rām. 382).
adj. c.g. strange, foreign, alien (K.Pr. 146, Śiv. 1605).
f. acridity, astringency (of flavour of food).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bĕgarôwᵘ), to make acrid; intr. to be acrid. bĕgarôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bĕgaröwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made acrid (of food, etc., by smoke, burnt grease, or the like); met. made acrid in temperament, angered, estranged (by some busybody).
adj. c.g. disinterested, without selfishness, impartial; independent, indifferent.
m. acridity; met. anger due to hidden enmity.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. bĕgaryōv), to be acrid, to have the flavour of grease burnt in cooking; to cause the throat or nasal passages to have a sensation of astringency (e.g. by the smoke of burning grease). --tulun -- m.inf. to cause the sensation of acridity in the throat or nasal passages (e.g. of the smoke of burning grease, etc.). --wŏthun -- m.inf. the sensation of acridity, astringency, or throat-burning to be experienced, (e.g. from the vapour of burning grease or of burning cayenne pepper). ¶ bĕgaryō-motᵘ adj. (f. bĕgaryē-müʦᵘ̈), that which has acquired an acrid taste (e.g. by going bad).
adj. (f. bĕgürᵘ̈), acrid, astringent, throat-burning (of food). Cf. bĕgarun. -bāna m. an earthen cooking-pot, spoilt by grease or oil being often burnt in it.

f. compelling to work for nothing; pressed or forced labour (K.Pr. 17, 200). -nakha wālüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to do a thing carelessly and hurriedly (as if by forced labour). ¶ bēgāri lagun m.inf. to be suddenly and unexpectedly pressed for such service. -mahanyuvᵘ m. a person pressed into service against his will, one pressed to carry loads (for individuals or the public). --raṭun -- m.inf. to press into such service, to seize a man for such service.
m. a person pressed into service against his will for carrying loads or the like.
adj. c.g. without sin, sinless, guiltless, innocent (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. impassable (of a forest, mountain-pass, river, etc.) (Gr.M.).

or biha m. sitting down; stopping, arrest of motion; laziness in work; cf. atha-˚; a wooden or rope ring for supporting globular-shaped vessels (in which they 'sit'); the parts of a wooden spinning-wheel in contact with the ground (El.); a chair (K.Pr. 31, spelt bihĕh); cf. Gr.Gr. 122. --aʦun -- m.inf. laziness to enter; slackness in work to be exhibited, laziness to be shown. -dār adj. c.g. fitted with a ring support as ab. -drāv adj. c.g. that of which the sediment has settled, clarified, clear. -wāl adj. c.g. one who stops work and intimidates others; a lazy person who stops at home (K.Pr. 193, W. 21); of a liquid, that of which the impurities have settled as a sediment and is now clear; K.Pr. and W. both spell this word bĕhwāl. -wölī f. the lazy do- nothing of one who has stopped work and is without employment.
or bē-hāl بے حال adj. c.g. out of condition, ill-circumstanced (Śiv. 573); damaged, unserviceable, worn out; unemployed, badly off, in a bad state.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bĕhanôwᵘ), to cause to sit; to cause to perch (of a bird) (Śiv. 1694); to put down, to set down (on the ground or on a supporting stand); to cause something in motion to come to rest; to set anything in its proper place (as in a row); to calm, assuage; to press down, make flat or even; to plant (El.). ¶ bĕhanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bĕhanöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to be seated; set down, put down, etc.
or bihawunᵘ adj. (f. bĕhawüñᵘ̈), one who sits, sitting, at rest (K.Pr. 31) (spelt bihĕhwani, f. sg. nom.).
adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. bĕhayāhas), shameless, immodest, bold, impudent; as subst. a shameless person (K.Pr. 29, sg. dat.).
adj. c.g. unconscious, insensible, stupefied, delirious; senseless, stupid; senseless, fainting (Śiv. 1455, 1564), (from envy or jealousy, Śiv. 498). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become senseless, etc.

conj. 2 [1 p.p. byūṭhᵘ (Śiv. 842, 847), pl. bīṭhⁱ (Śiv. 78); f. bīṭhᵘ̈, pl.bēchĕ (Gr.Gr. 212); 2 p.p. bēchyōv (Gr.Gr. 231); conj. part. always bihith (Gr.Gr. 197), and freq. part. bihⁱ bihⁱ (Gr.Gr. 105)], to be seated, to sit, to sit down (K.Pr. 132, impve.; YZ. 409; Śiv. 842, 847, 1468, 1484, 1914); to settle, reside in a place (K.Pr. 191); to remain, continue in a place, be fixed in any position (Śiv. 730, 1690, 1797, 1821); with dat., to sit (at a thing), to remain busy (at anything) (Gr.M.); to be unemployed, idle (K.Pr. 33, m. sg. dat. of 1 p.p.); to alight, settle, perch; to subside, settle, abate; to cease motion, be stopped (of a vehicle or machine). ¶ bĕhan-jāy or -jyāy f. a place for sitting; a place where people meet to sit and converse, the reception-room of a house; a favourite place for sitting, a home (Śiv. 90). ¶ bihith conj. part. having sat (YZ. 383, Śiv. 1102, 1119); also used as an adj., seated, etc. [Gr.M.; K.Pr. 31, 87 (busy at the spinning-wheel), 145; YZ. 67, 141; Śiv. 1101, 1567]. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to sit down; to settle down; to fall in or down (of a house, wall, etc.); to cease motion, be stopped; to lose one's occupation or post, to become unemployed. ¶ byūṭhᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bīṭhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), seated, etc.; so sg. dat. of 1 p.p. bīṭhis, to an idle man (K.Pr. 33).
f. unconsciousness, insensibility, stupefaction; delirium; senselessness, stupidity.
adj. c.g. better, superior; good, excellent; preferable, advisable (Śiv. 722).
adj. c.g. out of place, ill-placed, ill-timed; unbecoming, improper, amiss; unreasonable, wrong, objectionable.
adj. c.g. lifeless, inanimate, faint, dead (El.).

adj. c.g. without work or employment, idle, unemployed (K.Pr. 29, Śiv. 17, 96), not in office; useless, worthless, invalid. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become unserviceable, be of no avail, be nullified, invalidated.
adj. c.g. unstable, unsteady, vacillating; uneasy, discomposed, disturbed in mind, anxious, disquieted, distracted (cf. Gr.M.).
f. restlessness, uneasiness, discomposure. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to disturb (El.).
adj. c.g. (m. sg. dat. bĕkastas), i.q. bē-kas, q.v.

f. foundation; root (K.Pr. 157). --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to root up foundations, to destroy, ruin (physically or met.). --nērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. destruction to occur, to be ruined, destroyed. -sumbul بیخ سنبل m. Convallaria (El.), a kind of lily of the valley. -zāfrān بیخ زعفران m. Aristotochia rotunda (El.). -zambakh بیخ زنبق m. Convallaria (El.).
. Here add as sub-article. ¶ bēkha-dōlath f. well-founded prosperity, unfailing good fortune (Rām. 330).
adj. c.g. without knowledge, uninformed (Śiv. 984); thoughtless (El.).
adj. c.g. (subst. sg. dat. bĕkhatakas), untaught, uneducated, unskilled (of men or animals).
adj. c.g. beside oneself (with joy or grief), out of one's mind (YZ. 194); in ecstasy, transported, delirious (Gr.M.).
f. alienation of mind, senselessness, delirium (Rām. 714).
adj. c.g. without rule, unarranged, irregular; without order or discipline (Gr.M.).
f. the state of being unemployed, want of employment, idleness; (of things) uselessness, worthlessness.
adj. (bĕkörᵘ̈), ugly, unpleasing, blameable (of appearance or acts).
f. want of sense, foolishness (either owing to some accidental occasion, or by nature).

or bil m. the wood-apple or bēl, Ӕgle marmelos (Śiv. 1501); the leaf of the tree, used in the ceremonial worship of Śiva (Śiv. 187, 191, 1401). bĕla-pạthᵃr m.pl. a collection of bēl-leaves, used as above.

m. embroidery, flowered tissue; (on paper or the like) gilt and painted pattern-work or flower-work. -halkörⁱ بیل حلکاری f. a kind of gilt or plaited pattern flower-border round a picture or the like.
m. a small mattock or spade (K.Pr. 71), cf. bēl.
m. (in preparing bread, etc.) a rolling-pin.
m. a sister's husband, a brother-in-law (K.Pr. 30). -ḍār m. a sister's husband (generally employed as a term of abuse).
adj. c.g. (as subst., m. sg. dat. bĕmandachas), without shame, shameless.
adj. (f. bĕmandüchᵘ̈), shameless; esp. wanting in reverence, impudent.
adj. c.g. unmeaning, senseless; without meaning, conveying no meaning or impression to the mind (K.Pr. 30).
adj. c.g. sick, ailing, ill, unwell, indisposed (K.Pr. 29, YZ. 40); a sick person, a patient (K.Pr. 251, YZ. 184). Voc. bĕmārō (K.Pr. 30). -dörī f. attendance on the sick, sick-nursing.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. bĕmāriladiñ), suffering from a long illness, an invalid.
adj. c.g. tasteless, insipid; unpleasant, displeasing.
adj. c.g. incomparable. bē-misᵃlu-mānand بے مثل و مانند, without compare and parallel, incomparable and unparalleled (Śiv. 775).
adj. c.g. not hungry, without appetite (K.Pr. 30).

f. sickness, illness, disease (Gr.M., where it is spelt bēᵒ). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. sickness to occur or arise, esp. of a long illness. ¶ bĕmāri-buḍᵘ̈ f. a severe, long-continued illness, a chronic illness. -drāv adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -drāyĕ), issued from illness, convalescent. -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), smitten by illness, an invalid, weak after illness. --wọ̆thᵘ -- adj. (f. --wö̆ʦhᵘ̈ --), risen from sickness, one who has just recovered from a long illness. --wŏthun -- m.inf. to rise from sickness, to recover from a long illness.
f. the act of reviling, abusing, insulting a person in public. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. reviling to take place, to be publicly insulted or reviled.
adj. (f. bĕmūdᵘ̈), worthy of being reviled or abused, despicable.
adj. c.g. wanting in manliness, without fortitude or virility (K.Pr. 30).

m. difference, distinction (most often found in a negative sentence, as in timan chhuna bĕn kē̃h, there is no difference between them); apartness, distinction, non-unity (Śiv. 55, 543). ¶ bĕna-bĕn f. separateness, apartness, aloofness.
adj. c.g. shameless, without shame; naked.
f. the wife of a sister's son.
m. a nephew, a sister's son. Cf. bẹ̆nᵃza.

or bind or bindu m. a drop, a spot; esp. the dot which forms the nasal symbol or anusvāra in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character (Śiv. 774). bindu-nād (Śiv. 452) or nāda-bĕnd (Śiv. 669, 1320, 1336, 1594, 1602), a term in the Yōga philosophy (see Bhāgavata Purāṇa, VII, xv, 54) for the nasal sound represented by this dot, employed in mystical formulas, as representing a phase of the Supreme; hence, met., the Supreme Being.

f. a full-sister, a sister. This word being written بنِ or بِنِہ in the Persian character is often wrongly transliterated bĕni, binih, or bĕnih (cf. K.Pr. 34, 70, 132, 182, 236; W. 16, 18; Śiv. 1445). -dinal m. one who has incestuous intercourse with his sister; a term of abuse (Gr.Gr. 107). -dil m. id. (Gr.Gr. 107). -dāwal m. id. (Gr.Gr. 107). -wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), one who has a good or noble sister; one who has many sisters (Gr.Gr. 134).
m. one who has an immoral sister; one who has incestuous connexion with his sister (Gr.Gr. 134); used as a term of abuse.
m. distinction, difference (-manz = between) (Gr.M.). --bōzun -- m.inf. to know the difference, to be able to distinguish between things of the same kind or nature.
adj. c.g. without mark or sign; without distinguishing mark; incapable of comprehension (of the Deity) (Śiv. 1599).
adj. (f. bĕnöwᵘ̈), without name, nameless, unnamed.
m. a sisters' darling, usually of one petted brother among a number of sisters.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. bĕnyōv), to be apart, separate, separated; to be separated, pulled to pieces, cut to pieces, cut off. This verb is often spelt bĕnnun. ¶ bĕnyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bĕnyē-müʦᵘ̈), separated, separate, apart; separated, in pieces, cut to bits.
m. sisterly conduct, mutual affection of two women, as between sisters. -tônᵘ m. sisterhood, the sisterly relation (including the relationship between a woman and her female cousin).

f. a sister's daughter, a niece on the sister's side. Cf. bĕnathᵃr. -zāmaturᵘ m. the husband of a sister's daughter, a niece's husband. -pônᵘ m. the relationship between a niece and her maternal uncle or aunt; met. a similar imaginary relationship between two women of different ages who are fond of each other.
f. the act of separating, dividing, or opening out.

or bẹ̆ñᵉ̆rāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. bẹ̆ñᵒrᵒ or bẹ̆ñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), to separate, divide, open out (Gr.Gr.) any thing or action which is naturally closely united. bẹ̆ñᵒrᵒ-motᵒ or bẹ̆ñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. bẹ̆ñᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ or bẹ̆ñᵉ̆röwᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), divided, separated, opened out.
adj. c.g. unlawful, against the law (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. unlawful, against the law (Gr.M.).
adj. and adv. heedless, careless, unconcerned (K.Pr. 133); careless, wanting in respect (Śiv. 536); fearless, bold, fearlessly, boldly (Śiv. 891, 1232, 1236; Rām. 844, 1388, bē-parwāh).

adj. c.g. (as subst., m. sg. dat. bĕpaʦhas), without trust, not trusting in another; not trusted by another; (of a thing or action) not considered likely to be of use or to succeed. --karun -- m.inf. to show distrust in a person, to have no confidence in a person, not to confide in him.
adj. c.g. free from care or anxiety; without solicitude, unconcerned, tranquil.
f. freedom from care, anxiety, or solicitude.
adj. c.g. one who has no spiritual guide or pīr; vicious, wicked (K.Pr. 189). With emph. y bē-pīrᵘ̈y (K.Pr. 170, 196, W. 22).
adj. (f. bĕpöcᵘ̈), not cooked, not sufficiently cooked, underdone.
adj. (f. bĕpüʦhᵘ̈), distrustful; not trusted, distrusted.

f. a fence, hedge, paling, railing, low wall (Gr.Gr. 21); the edge of a field (K.Pr. 58, 121, Śiv. 1028, 1681); a partition in a granary or the like. Cf. bēra. -büṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -bachĕ), an elevated piece of uncultivated ground between two fields.

f. an edge, a border (El.); a road- fence, hedge, paling, railing, boundary mark, partition. Cf. bēr. -gagur m. a field-mouse or field-rat. -ganḍ m. a low boundary bank between fields or gardens. -mūjⁱ f. a kind of plant, an Umbellifer, eaten by the poor in time of famine (L. 71). -mōsta f. a kind of grass (the Indian mōthā), Cyperus rotundus. It grows on field banks, and its root is used in medicine and as a perfume.
adj. c.g. sick, ill, ailing, unwell, indisposed; a sick person, a patient. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to fall ill.
(?) m. a certain kind of grass (L. 70, 359) (qy. is this really for bēran pĕṭh, on the field borders, and meaning either bēra-mūjⁱ or bēra mōsta, see bēra?).

adj. c.g. without colour, colourless; without form, formless (of God) [Śiv. 849, 1820 (of the universe before creation, "without form and void"), Śiv. 1025]; without passion, passionless (a Persianization of the Sanskrit rāga-rahita) (Śiv. 1267, 1566).
f. a kind of walking-stick with a handle across the top, like that of a crutch.
adj. (f. bē-rünjᵘ̈), i.q. bē- rang, q.v.; out of order, deranged, disarranged (L.V. 85).
adj. c.g. without employ, out of employment (L. 456).
adj. and adv. without cause, causelessly (Gr.M.).
m. unevenness; inequality, difference; want of similarity.
m. (sg. dat. bĕsātas,), a wrong moment, an unlucky time, a time which according to the rules is not propitious for any action such as setting out on a journey, a marriage, or the like.
adj. c.g. ignorant, uninformed, a stupid follow, a blockhead.
adj. (m. sg. dat. bĕshūbis, abl. bĕshōbi; f. sg. nom. bĕshūbᵘ̈, dat. bĕshōbi), not good, bad, unpleasing.
adj. c.g. without management, with no conduct of affairs, ungoverned (of a country, K.Pr. 216).
adj. (f. bĕsözᵘ̈), tasteless, insipid (of food); met. (of an action, narrative, or conduct), id.

adj. (f. bĕsümᵘ̈), uneven, rough, difficult of access; unequal, not equal (to); dissimilar (K.Pr. 206); not even, odd (of number); unequal (in character), great but mean (K.Pr. 30, spelt be-suṅmb); difficult, hard; disagreeable, painful, troublesome, vexatious.
or bē-sŏr adj. c.g. without memory, having lost one's memory; senseless, unconscious, in a faint (Gr.M.).
f. forgetting, loss of memory; unconsciousness, senselessness.
adj. c.g. faint, powerless (YZ. 84); agitated, uneasy, restless, impatient (Rām. 372, 646, 776, 1164).
adj. c.g. without discrimination, without conscience (W. 110).
adj. c.g. impartial, of no party, unsectarian (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. without order, irregular; without system (Gr.M.).
in beth-muru (? spelling), rice land requiring a fallow (L. 336). Cf. bīṭhᵘ̈.
m. (sg. dat. bēṭhas), sitting, delay. --lagun -- m.inf. delay, slowness in accomplishing something which should be finished quickly.
f. a sitting-room, a room set apart for receiving friends and conversation, a drawing-room.
adj. c.g. without traffic, without commerce (K.Pr. 216).
adv. and the rest, etcetera, and so forth. -tētri adv. id.
adj. (m. sg. abl. bĕtōli; f. sg. nom. bĕtūjᵘ̈, sg. dat. bĕtōjĕ), unweighed; esp. that which cannot be weighed, in very large quantity, immeasurable. Cf. atūlᵘ.
adj. c.g. (K.Pr. 72, W. 134); i.q. bē- wŏphā, q.v.
adj. c.g. without motive, without reason; without business, without concern; without relationship, without connexion; without tie, without connexion with worldly things (e.g. a mendicant devotee).
adj. c.g. careless, fearless (W. 21, bēwāi); adv. carelessly, fearlessly (Rām. 108, 1300).
adj. c.g. faithless, perfidious, treacherous; ungrateful (K.Pr. 72, W. 134); (as subst.) a traitor, faithless one, ingrate.
f. faithlessness, infidelity, ingratitude, treachery (H. viii, 6, 11).
f. mental pain or distress, sorrow, anguish (arising from abuse, dishonour, loss of property, etc.).
adj. c.g. without sense, ignorant, foolish, stupid; (as subst.) a fool, a blockhead (Gr.M.).
f. want of sense, foolishness, a foolish action, stupidity, folly, fatuity (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. without rations or victuals (of soldiers, etc.); without subsistence allowance, without stipend, without salary.

or biyĕ 1 adv. again, once more (Gr.Gr. 94; K.Pr. 237; Śiv. 916, 979, 980, 1341; W. 99, beyi; YZ. 15, 138; Rām. 1, 84, 85, etc.); more. Conj. and, and also, also (Śiv. 163, 799, YZ. 82). Cf. byākh. --akh -- pron. adj. one more. --kē̃h -- pron. adj. anything else. --ti -- conj. moreover, and moreover, and what's more. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come again, to return (El.). The word is properly dat. of bi, q.v.
biy, biyau, biyĕ 2, biyⁱ, biyi, see byākh.
adj. c.g. without religion, infidel (K.Pr. 239); corrupt, faithless, perfidious, treacherous, dishonest, fraudulent.
adj. c.g. without limit, endless, boundless, infinite (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. bē-yazzatas بے عزتس), without honour or dignity, disgraced; subst. m. (K.Pr. 90), i.q. bĕ-yizzatī, q.v.
adj. displeased, vexed, out of humour (Rām. 1090). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become displeased, out of humour with (e.g. with a child or a servant).
adj.(f. bĕzuvᵘ̈), without life; hence, weak, unfit for work, unable to do one's work (e.g. of a servant or beast of burden).

pron. adj. other, another. This word is not used alone, but forms the base of the declension of byākh (bi + akh), q.v. Its dat. sg. bĕyĕ or biyĕ (q.v. s.v.) is used as an adv. or conjnct. meaning 'moreover', 'and', 'also'.
m., i.q. bicĕr, but also of the hands, etc., after touching grease or greasy food.
m. greasiness, the condition of being smeared with grease (e.g. a pot which has held ghī, etc.).
m. the fringe of hair or side locks worn by young boys.
m. a certain bird, the skylark (?).

or bĕd f. in the following. --marüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a thing to turn out as one desires, to one's secret pleasure but to one's outward dissatisfaction. --mārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to interfere in some business undertaken by another, so as to make the result to suit one's own wishes.
f. a bag; wrapper, cover; esp. a large ball or wrapped up parcel of silk, valuable cloth, etc.; cf. Hindī bidrī and Persian بدرہ.
m. the Indian measure of area, a bīghā. In Kashmīr a kaccā biga contains 40 square gaz, and a pakkā biga contains 60 square gaz (El.).
in bigār karun m.inf. to set at variance, to set friends at enmity.

f. change for the worse, impairment, deterioration, corruption, vitiation, disfigurement, defacement; decline, decay; disorder, disarrangement, confusion; ruin, harm, injury, damage; blemish, stain, flaw; disagreement, discord, quarrel, misunderstanding, disaffection, rebellion, mutiny.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. bigarôwᵘ), caus. of bigarun, i.q. bigārun, q.v. bigarôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bigaröwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. bigôrᵘ-motᵘ, s.v. bigārun.

conj. 2 (2 p.p. bigaryōv), to be changed for the worse, to be impaired, deteriorated (K.Pr. 246); to take harm, be damaged, marred; to fall off, decline in beauty; to fail, miscarry; to break down; to go or turn bad; to get out of order, be disordered; to be mismanaged, bungled; to be at variance, to be estranged; to get out of temper, become angry; to become vicious; to rebel, revolt. bigaryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bigaryē-müʦᵘ̈), impaired, damaged, spoilt, etc.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bigôrᵘ), to ruin, spoil, mar, vitiate, etc.; to bungle; to break a custom; to cause a misunderstanding (between friends). Caus. of bigarun, q.v. Cf. bigarāwun. bigôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bigörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), ruined, spoiled (by some one).
(? spelling) in bih-dāna, m. seeds of the quince (L. 389).
m. the abode of the blessed, Paradise, Heaven (Gr.M.).

m. (sg. dat. bīkas), marrow, lymph, fat. ¶ bīka-bēchawunᵘ m. (f. -bēchawüñᵘ̈), a low mean beggar, who will beg for any scraps of food or rejected bits of fat, etc. -bata m. a dish consisting of rice, goat's fat, and water (El.). -chichur m. (sg. dat. -chicharas), a piece of fat meat. -dār adj. c.g. fat, corpulent; (of a piece of meat) fat, fatty. -lala f. exudation of lymph or matter from a wound. -nôrᵘ m. an intestine (of some animal slaughtered for food) surrounded by or embedded in fat.
f. things given in charity, alms (K.Pr. 31).
f. a female beggar or mendicant, esp. one who is mean and importunate. Cf. bikhörⁱ.
f. the actions or profession of a mean beggar.

m. a beggar, a mendicant, esp. one who is importunate, dirty, mean, and ill-conducted. The f. is bikhārĕñ, q.v. -bāy f. the wife of such a beggar. -koṭᵘ m. (f. -küṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. -kacĕ), a beggar's brat, the son of such a beggar, or a boy who begs on his own account. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), the son of such a beggar (without reference to the character of the son).
f. the actions or profession of a mean beggar; acting like such a beggar.
m. (sg. dat. bikshukas), a beggar, a mendicant, one who asks for alms (Śiv. 1475).
adj. (f. bīküjᵘ̈), fat, fatty, covered or inspissated with fat (of meat or the like).

m. a whetstone. --dith bihun -- m.inf. having applied the whetstone to sit; hence, to set ready for action (e.g. for a battle, for gambling, for setting out on a journey), to wait equipped. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to apply the whetstone; hence, to be handsomely dressed, well equipped.
m. a fringe of hair hanging over the forehead, worn by boys and prostitutes. Cf. bicurᵘ 1.
m. the skylark, cf. bicurᵘ 2; (according to El.) the nightingale, which in Kashmīr corresponds to the bulbul.
