m. fear, terror, dread; reverence, respect; danger, risk; bīma-sṻtin, through fear (Siv. 128). --hāwun -- m.inf. to exhibit fear, i.e. to threaten, intimidate, frighten. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take fear, i.e. from previous experience to be afraid beforehand of any person, animal, action, or the like. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to experience fear, to be afraid, terrified, panic-stricken. --rōzun -- m.inf. to be timid, shy, of a fearful disposition; to be abashed. --thawun -- m.inf. to place fear, i.e. to intimidate, threaten.
m. (sg. gen. byūmukᵘ), insurance, money paid for the insurance of goods (Gr.M.).
m. N. of a famous hero in the Mahābhārata, one of the five Pāṇḍava brothers (Śiv. 1164).
m. (sg. dat. bimasinis; f. bimasiñᵘ̈), an earthworm, i.q. buma-sin, see bum 3. The f. is a smaller, or female, worm.
m. the extreme limit of a person's resources.
or biñᵘ̈ interj. a term of address used to a woman of moderate age, or of an age equal to that of the speaker (Gr.Gr. 98). Cf. ada and āhan. W. 101 writes the word bin.
f. (sg. dat. bīñᵘ̈), the ornamented flange or wooden strip covering the crack between the two halves of a double door or window-shutters when shut.
f. a reed-pipe, pipe, flute, fife (Śiv. 1455).

m. foundation, ground, motive, beginning. Used in the following: --karun -- m.inf. to make a beginning; hence, to consider the means of accomplishing some work, such as the collection of materials, etc.
adj. c.g. seeing, one who sees (H. ii, 2).
f. a deceitful woman skilled in treachery, a treacherous Siren, a Circe.

m. N. of a wood (Sanskrit, Vṛndā- vana) near the town of Gōkula in the District of Mathurā on the left bank of the Yamunā (Jumna). It is celebrated as the place where Kṛṣṇa (Krishna), in the character of Gōpāla, passed his youth, associating with the cowherds and herd-maidens employed in tending cattle (Siv. 997, 1053, 1327, 1367, 1409, 1423).
m. the stomach, belly, abdomen. --alun -- m.inf. the belly to tremble, to be agitated, terrified. --naṭun -- m.inf. id.
f. a kind of spangle or ornament for the forehead, worn by young married women.
f. a crowd, throng, concourse. ¶ bīra-bīr f. crowding, thronging, pressing. --karüñᵘ̈ -- or --lāgüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to crowd, throng, swarm.
m. a leaf of betel (pān) rolled up with spices (see pān 2) (K. 977, 982).

m. a hockey- ball; the game of hockey. -gŏgul m. a hockey-ball. -ṭãv-ṭãv m. a position in the middle, when the right position is to one side (like a hockey-ball which is knocked from one side to another).
interj. go! avaunt! (K.Pr. 4) (the Persian imperative of raftan).

f. a small kind of earring passing through the centre of the ear, usually of gold, and ornamented with bosses. It is worn by boys. ¶ bīr-bali-horᵘ m. a pair of such ear-rings. -kan m. a single one of such ear-rings; an ear adorned with such an ear-ring. -pōsh m. a boss on one of such ear-rings.
m. a mixed mess of fried grain of various sorts, eaten as a snack in the afternoon of the long days of summer.
(? spelling), m. Picea Webbiana, the Silver Fir (El.).

m. N. of a village about 13 miles south-west of Śrīnagar, the ancient Bahurūpa, near which is a cave, into which, according to tradition, the celebrated Śaiva teacher Abhinava-gupta entered with twelve hundred disciples, and was thence translated in bodily form to Śiva's heaven (Śiv. 1894).
or adj. c.g. terrific, terrible; N. of Śiva, voc. bīshĕna (Śiv. 1209).
adj. c.g. very greedy, always haunting the kitchen.
m. a cry used to drive away a cat (K.Pr. 35).
or bisⁱlāy f. a fishing-rod. bislāyĕ-wôlᵘ m. a fishing-hook.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bitôwᵘ), to pass over; to carry out, get through any difficult business; to pass through (a country); to cause (time) to elapse, to pass (time). bitôwᵘ-motᵘ adj. (f. bitöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈),got over, carried out, passed through; (of time) spent, etc., as ab.

or biṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. bichĕ), a session, assembly, meeting, concourse (El., Gr.Gr. 13), esp. of persons assembled for some unlawful purpose, such as gambling, drinking, or the like. --lāgüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to set going, bring together, a meeting of gamblers, drinkers, or the like. --wahārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to spread out such a meeting, i.e. to make arrangements or prepare the necessary materials for a meeting of gamblers, drinkers, or the like.

(sg. dat. bīʦᵘ̈), the hole in the ground used in the game of tipcat. The 'cat', instead of being tapered at each end, is a straight peg, sloping with one end in the hole; the other projecting end is then struck with the stick.
m. a kind of petticoat (or sāṛī) made of coarse cloth.
m. one guilty of incest with his own daughter (used in abuse), a scamp (El., K.Pr. 72).
m. sg. dat. of byūṭhᵘ, see bĕhun or bihun and byūṭhᵘ.

f. (fem. of byūṭhᵘ, seated; see bĕhun and cf. K.Pr. 158, bīṭ); (of land) long uncultivated, untilled, lying fallow (El. bīṭ-zamīn); (of a woman, cow, etc.) one who does not bear children owing to some stricture or malformation. Cf. beth.
see byūṭhᵘ-motᵘ, under bĕhun or bihun.
m. a sufficiency of means (neither too much nor too little), implements, paraphernalia.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. biyĕnôwᵘ), (of cooked food) to make stale, to let get cold and tasteless; to make a person permanent in any position by dint of long occupation, to allow a person to gain a right to a post by long service.

m. staleness, the condition of cooked food allowed to grow cold and tasteless (Gr.Gr. 138); met. a long time occupied, or long delay occurring in any business. --lagun -- m.inf. delay to occur in the carrying out of anything which it was hoped to complete quickly (e.g. a marriage).

in -biyō m. a certain game played by pairs of little girls. They stand facing each other with their feet close together, and firmly holding each other's hands. Then both lean backwards as far as they can, and whirl round in a circle with their feet as pivots.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. biyyōv), to be or become stale or cold and tasteless (of cooked food), to be spoilt by being kept too long before eating (of something that should be eaten directly it is cooked); spoilt by being kept too long, so that it is dried up. Cf. byuyᵘ. biyyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. biyyē-müʦᵘ̈), stale (of cooked food); met. (of a man, woman, etc.) one for whom something (e.g. a marriage or the like) takes place long after the usual time, period, or age for such a ceremony, etc.
m. lit. imperat. 'strike', 'slay', hence slaughter; used in the following: -bēg بزن بیگ m. an executioner; an official flogger, or officer appointed to carry out sentences of flogging.
f. the act of dragging and violently hurling or thrusting something (such as a pole or the fist) down into a hole or down to a lower level. Cf. bizan.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bizᵒnᵒ), to drag and violently hurl or thrust anything (such as a pole or the fist) down into a hole or down to some lower level. Cf. bizan. bizᵒnᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. bizᵘ̈ñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), dragged and hurled down, as ab.
a poetical form of bŏh, q.v. (El.).
بوے f. odour, scent, fragrance (YZ. 9, 32; K.Pr. 89).

m. a small earthenware vessel, the size of a slop-basin (K.Pr. 139); a small hollow earthenware bomb, with a little orifice at the top. It is filled with gunpowder and other ingredients, and when ignited emits showers of sparks (Hindī, anār).
m. a man, in appearance and dress honest and respectable, who deceitfully intervenes between others for his own profit, a calumniating middleman.

f. often pronounced and written bŏchĕ or bŏchih, or in the Persian character بوچہ (YZ. 402), hunger (Śiv. 1584). -bŏcha f. telling of one's hunger, crying out for food when starving. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. hunger to be experienced, the feeling of hunger. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. hunger to be attached, the arising of a feeling of hunger (K.Pr. 71). --marüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. hunger to die, hunger or appetite to pass away owing to its long continuance. --ʦalüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. hunger to flee, one's hunger or fast to be broken by getting food. ¶ bŏchi (often spelt), sg. dat. and abl., as in bŏchi-sṻṭin (dying) of hunger (YZ. 408); putra bŏchi, in hunger (i.e. ardent desire) for a son (K.Pr. 174). bŏchi-gaṭa f. hunger-darkness, extreme hunger, starvation. -gaṭa wasüñᵘ̈ f.inf. the pangs of starvation to be felt, the experiencing of the pangs of starvation. -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), smitten by hunger, starving (YZ. 410, W. 113). -haʦar m. the being smitten by the pangs of hunger, starvation. -lĕḍ adj. c.g. conquered by hunger; hence, one who cannot stand being hungry even for a short time. --marun -- to die of hunger (K.Pr. 120). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), free from hunger; as an adv., without hunger, without being hungry, u.w. vbs. of eating and the like.
m. extreme hunger, usually employed with reference to a suckling child.
adj. (f. bŏchatᵘ̈rᵘ̈), food for the hungry; hence, a child adopted by one who has no children of his own, and to whom tender quasi-parental love is shown.
m. hunger, esp. a sharp appetite.
f. a female, esp. a cow, a long time after giving birth to a child, or after calving, who is consequently fat and in good condition, but with a diminished flow of milk.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. bŏchōv), to become or be hungry. ¶ bŏchō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bŏchē-müʦᵘ̈), hungered, ready to eat anything.
adj. (f. bö̆chᵘ̈), hungry; m. sg. dat. bŏchĕ (K.Pr. 35).
m. (sg. dat. böcis), a man, generally a Brāhmaṇ, who lives upon what he can get in the way of gifts, and is ignorant of any trade or business.
(or), m. intelligence; esp. perfect knowledge of the Self (L.V. 35).
m. (voc. bŏda, Śiv. 478), the planet Mercury. ¶ bŏd-wār f. Wednesday. Cf. bodhwār in W. 100.

m. the Buddha (Śiv. 861). ¶ bŏda-brôrᵘ m. the Buddha incarnation, the founder of the Buddhist religion, counted by Hindūs as the ninth avatāra or incarnation of Viṣṇu. -khorᵘ m. (f. -khürᵘ̈), a wise lotus; as a term of affection applied to a good, intelligent, boy or girl.

f. (sg. dat. bö̆zᵘ̈ 1, e.g. Śiv. 881), intelligence, reason, discernment, judgment, understanding, reasoning power (K.Pr. 25, 125; Śiv. 42, 46, 182, etc.). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to apply discrimination, to apply one's mind (to). ¶ bô̈zᵘ̈-brēṭh adj. c.g. (as subst. m. sg. dat. -brēṭhas), intellect-foolish, one whose intellect or sense of right and wrong has been injured or destroyed. -gāh m. intellect-brilliancy, clearness in explanation, or in seizing the point of anything. -manzar m. slowness of intellect, feebleness of intellect, unintelligence. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without intellect, stupid. -wān adj. c.g. wise, sensible (Gr.M., Śiv. 995).

adj. c.g. unintelligent, stupid (= Hindī baudh). -gaʦhun m.inf. to become stupid or a fool, owing to some mistake or forgetfulness. -küñᵘ̈ f. a foolish stone, a weight which weighs too much, i.e. more than it is supposed to weigh.
m. the name of an ancient site to the west of the Pradyumna-giri or Hāra-parvat; a well-known hill lying north of the city of Śrīnagar.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bŏḍanôwᵘ), to cause something (that does not naturally sink) to sink, to dip, immerse (Śiv. 67); to submerge, drown, flood; to lose, waste, exhaust, sacrifice, ruin. Caus. of bŏḍun in all its senses. bŏḍanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bŏḍanöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), sunken, immersed, etc., by anyone.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. bŏḍowᵘ), i.q. bŏḍanāwun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 171). bŏḍowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bŏḍüwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made to sink by some one (of something that does not sink naturally).
adj. (f. bŏḍawüñᵘ̈), one who sinks or dives; that which sinks of itself owing to its high specific gravity.
m. the lord of knowledge, N. of Śiva (Śiv. 1178).
f. the day of the new moon of the month of Bādᵃrapĕth (q.v.). Kuśa (Poa cynosuroides) grass is collected on this day and worshipped.

conj. 2 (1 p.p.bọ̆ḍᵘ; 2 p.p. bŏjyōv), to dive, to sink, drown, be drowned (K.Pr. 121; fig. Śiv. 1582); to be immersed, submerged (lit. or fig.), inundated; to be destroyed, ruined; to sink, go down (of the sun); to be at the bottom of a hole; to sink down a pipe, be carried away; to sink in sin, be a sinner; to sink in debt, be overwhelmed with debt. K.Pr. spells 1 p.p. buḍ. bŏḍan-wôlᵘ n. ag. (f. bŏḍan-wājĕñ), one who sinks, etc.; hence, anything which naturally sinks in water, or easily runs down a pipe, or anyone who is naturally prone to sin, or readily gets badly into debt, and so on. bọ̆ḍᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sg. nom. bö̆ḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, dat. bŏjĕ-maʦĕ), sunken, immersed, etc. (Śiv. 1629).
(f. büdᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 1), in --dã̄d -- m. a bull of a brown or tawny colour. büdᵘ̈rᵘ̈-gāv f. a cow of the same colour.
adj. c.g. intoxicated, senseless under the influence of an intoxicating drug.
f. the act of causing some one or something to sink, of dipping, immersing, drowning, flooding, etc. Cf. bŏḍanāwun.
f. plastering, applying a plaster of ordinary lime-plaster or of mud mixed with chaff and chopped straw.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bọ̆ḍᵃrôwᵃ), to cause to sink, dip, immerse; met. to cause to sink in sinful acts, to debauch. bọ̆dᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ adj. (f. bọ̆dᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), sunken, immersed (by some one); met. debauched, led into sin.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. böḍᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. böḍᵃrun, q.v. böḍᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. böḍᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), plastered (of a wall, etc.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. böḍᵒrᵒ), to plaster (a wall); genl. to prepare a house, make it ready for habitation (Śiv. 1065). böḍᵒrᵒ-motᵒ (f.bödᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), plastered (of a wall or the like).

adj. (f. büḍᵘ̈, sg. dat. bajĕ). (In the Roman character this word is usually written by others boḍ, but sometimes (e.g. K.Pr. 125, 128) buḍ. The f. is often written baḍ, a transliteration of بَڈ, for), great, big, large (in size) (K.Pr. 144, 168, 188, YZ. 201, L. 458, W. 20, Śiv. 859); great (in quantity or degree) (K.Pr. 125, of a pain; Śiv. 655, of favour); great, grand, imposing (Śiv. 120); great, important (K.Pr. 125); great, loud (of sound) (YZ. 571, Śiv. 725); great, superior, famous, excelling (K.Pr. 62, Śiv. 671); great, rich (K.Pr. 33); great, mighty, powerful (K.Pr. 170, W. 155, Śiv. 10, 158 (voc.), 159); great in dignity (K.Pr. 23, 24, 33, 80, Śiv. 36); great, noble, munificent (K.Pr. 33); great, chief; elder (of brothers); (pl.) one's superiors. Often used instead of baḍa (q.v.), qualifying another adj. with the sense of 'very'; in such cases it agrees with the adj. in gender, number, and case (Śiv. 427, 687; cf. Gr.M.). It appears as an adj. suff. in words such as khōʦa-boḍᵘ, very fearful, timid (Gr.M.); pāyĕ-boḍᵘ, of great dignity (YZ. 25, 240, 543; cf. baḍi pāyĕ bel.). ¶ The following forms may be noted: masc. sg. nom. boḍᵘ (boḍ, buḍ) (K.Pr. 28, 33, 62, 125, 170, 188, 239; L. 458; W. 20, 155); dat. baḍis (K.Pr. 20, 24, YZ. 240); abl. baḍi (K.Pr. 144); voc. baḍi (Śiv. 1236), baḍy-ō (YZ. 543); pl. nom. bȧḍⁱ (YZ. 25, 571); f. sg. nom. büḍᵘ̈ (baḍ) (K.Pr. 33, 80, 168, YZ. 201, Śiv. 869); dat. bajĕ (Śiv. 1136); abl. baji (K.Pr. 24). ¶ baḍi adv. greatly; with a great (voice), loudly, u.w. vbs. of speaking, teaching, and the like. --baḍi -- adv. very loudly. --boḍᵘ -- (f. sg. nom. --büḍᵘ̈ --, dat. --bajĕ --), very great, very large; greatest of all, supreme (Śiv. 580). -bagawān  m. one who is fortunate in possessing much; N. of the Deity, the All-Possessor, Śiv. 158 (voc.), 1216 (voc.). -bala-sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), possessing great might (Śiv. 1259). --dŏha -- adv. on a great day, on a festival; see boḍᵘ dŏh above. --dŏhokᵘ dŏh -- adv. id. (lit. the day of a great day). --pala -- adj. c.g. lifted up, elevated; high (of a price); high (in honour); high (in generosity); and in similar meanings. --pöṭhⁱ, --pöṭhin -- adv. in a great manner, to great extent, greatly, u.w. vbs. of giving, spending, etc. --pāyĕ -- adj. c.g. provided with much assistance, provided with ample means or materials for doing anything (cf. pāyĕ-boḍᵘ ab.). ¶ boḍᵘ dŏh m. a great day, a holiday, a festival (K.Pr. 28); a long day, a day of the spring and summer seasons, when the sun is north of the equator. --day -- m. a great god; N. of Kṛṣṇa; voc. baḍi-dayĕ (Śiv. 1383, 1487). --hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. büḍᵘ̈hishᵘ̈), greatest of all, greatest, used as a superlative of boḍᵘ. --karun -- m.inf. to make great, increase, augment (anything) (El.). --mahanyuvᵘ -- m. a great man, either owing to wealth or position. --māz -- m. beef (El.). --pahān -- m. somewhat great, a little greater (than) (Gr.Gr. 93). ¶ büḍᵘ̈ f., see ab. --jāy -- f. a great place; a place terrible through wicked, sinful practices, etc., such as a haunted burning-place or the like. --möjᵘ̈ -- f. the big mother, the senior lady of a family, who manages the household affairs. ¶ boḍuy (fem. büḍᵘ̈y) = boḍᵘ, with emph. y, even great, exactly great, verily great; K.Pr. 33 (m.), 23 (f.); Śiv. 428 (m.).

adj. (f. bö̆zᵘ̈ 2), wise, intelligent, quick to understand, esp. of children (Gr.M.). ¶ bŏdⁱ-brēṭh adj. c.g. (as subst. m. sg. dat. -brēṭhas), without intelligence, stupid. -yĕch m. a wisdom-demon, a certain yakṣa or demon believed to have possessed persons in former times, and to have turned their intellects upside down, or to have inspired them; also u.w. reference to a wise person lapsing into forgetfulness, or of a fool unexpectedly doing something intelligent.

or bodᵘ1 m. (f. bö̆zᵘ̈ 3 or büzᵘ̈), a handful of leaves, twigs, grass, etc., held together in the hand, as in hāka-bodᵘ, a bundle of spinach (Gr.Gr. 145); any similar bundle; in reaping, the handful of rice-straw cut by the sickle (L. 328, budu); used as a suffix with the numerals 100 and above, it implies plurality, as in hata-bodᵘ, by hundreds; sāsa-bodᵘ, by thousands; lachĕ- (or lacha-) bodᵘ, by hundreds of thousands (see Gr.Gr. 144). In this sense it is generally, but not always, employed in the pl. As an example of the sg. we have lachĕ-badi ranga, in a hundred thousand forms (Śiv. 1522, 20, 32, 51). For the pl. we have hata-baza wata (f.), hundreds of ways (Śiv. 1626); lachĕ-bȧdⁱ sāsa-bȧdⁱ sās dyār, wealth by hundreds of thousands, by thousands of thousands (Śiv. 952; so 952, 1436 fem., 1519, 1545, 1912). El. spells this word baud. --karun -- m.inf. to grasp stalks, twigs, grass, or the like in the hand, so as to tie up the part below the hand with a string, etc. (e.g. in making a posy); to gather up the edge of a body-cloth, etc., into the hand. --phirun -- m.inf. to tie a person's hands behind his back. ¶ badi anun m.inf. to bring into the hand; hence, with reference to some action or thing which is lost or in disorder, by diligent search or arrangement to put it in the way of accomplishment, to put in good order. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to extract from the fist; hence, in reference to any concealed thing, requirement, action, or the like, by means of arguments, etc., to make it manifest, and to wield it for one's own purposes. --khārun -- m.inf. with reference to any intricate or unintelligible thing or action, to explain it according to one's wishes.

m. a sec. suff. used with nouns of relationship, as in sŏna-bodᵘ co-wifehood; pitᵃ̇rᵃ̇-bodᵃ̇, fatherhood; böyⁱ-bodⁱ or böjⁱ-bodⁱ, brotherhood, commensality (see Gr.Gr. 144 ff.). Cf. bodᵘ 1, with which it is probably connected.

c.g. a prisoner in jail, a convict. -hāl f. (sg. dat. -höjᵘ̈ YZ. 384), a prison-house, a prison, jail (YZ. 385). -hölⁱ m. a jailor. -wān m. a jail, prison. -wān lagun m.inf. to be imprisoned, to go to jail, to be sentenced to imprisonment. -wān lāgun m.inf. to put in jail, send to jail, sentence to imprisonment.
f. the fees paid at intervals by a prosecutor for feeding a prisoner who is in jail at his suit.
f. sweet-fennel (El.); its seeds, anise-seed. -gūjⁱ f. the kernels of anise-seed, extracted by pounding in a mortar.
in bōg-bāganay f. dividing out into proper proportions, e.g. of a piece of gold for the various members of an ornament in course of manufacture. Cf. bôgᵘ.
adj. c.g. entitled to a share.
f.pl. a kind of bean, Vicia faba (= L. 330, bágláh, El. bãgla). -dāl f. a quantity of these beans husked and split; a spiced pottage made of these beans.
f. a fee or payment for dividing; the commission or perquisite kept back by a distributor.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bögᵃrôwᵃ), caus. of bögᵃrun, to get divided, to cause to be divided by some one (Śiv. 855, 969); to divide among each other, to share out (YZ. 254). bögᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. bögᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), divided, apportioned, shared out.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bögᵒrᵒ), to divide, apportion, distribute, portion out, parcel out (Śiv. 1072, 1510); to go shares in, share out, divide among each other. bögᵃrana-bôgᵃ m. a share for dividing, an extra share given to the person engaged in dividing, as a perquisite for his trouble. bögᵃrunᵃ fut. pass. part. (f. bögᵃrüñᵃ), to be divided, fit to be divided; that which is to be divided; a thing or act which is the subject of division. bögᵃran-wôlᵃ m. (f. bögᵃran-wājĕñ), a divider, an apportioner, a distributor. bögᵃrith thawun m.inf. to fix, during one's lifetime, the shares in which one's own property is to be divided amongst one's heirs; to hide shares in any property from those who are entitled to it. bögᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. bögᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), divided, apportioned; divided, shared out.

m. (sg. dat.bögis, abl. bāgi, pl. nom. bögⁱ 3), a share (K.Pr. 103); an allotment, apportionment; a share or helping at a meal (K.Pr. 38, 81); a portion or aliquot part of anything, as in aiṭha-bôgᵘ, an eighth part; (also in pl., see bögⁱ 1 bel.) lot, fortunate lot, good fortune, the betrothal presents given by a bridegroom's father (L. 268, cf. baḍa wörivⁱ bôgᵘ under baḍa). -bāgay f., i.q. bōg-bāganay, q.v. s.v. bōg. -band m. a travelling-bag or hold-all for carrying bedding, clothes, etc. --karun -- m.inf. to make a share, to share anything with some one else. ¶ bāgi āmotᵘ adj. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), come into sharing; hence of a husband (or wife) who has become partner for life with his wife (or her husband) (perf. part. of --yunᵘ bel.). -boḍᵘ adj. (f. sg. -büḍᵘ̈, dat. -bajĕ), having great good luck, prosperous, well-to-do and blessed with offspring. -bôgᵘ m. a person's full share of anything under division (K.Pr. 24); the share to which a person is entitled by his fate. -barutᵘ adj. (f. -bürᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), filled with good fortune, excessively prosperous; (of a thing) complete in all its parts or in all its good qualities; (of a vessel) completely and satisfactorily filled. --drāmotᵘ -- adj. (f. --drāmüʦᵘ̈ --), one who remains outside the distribution, i.e. one who, even though present at a distribution of food or the like, does not receive his or her share (perf. part. of --nērun bel.). -hyūnᵘ adj. (f.-hīñᵘ̈), deprived of good fortune, reduced to ill-fortune, deserted by fortune, miserable. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to expel from a common or similar employment, or from a common means of livelihood, or from a common association, or from commensality, etc. --khasun -- m.inf. to receive one's fated share of a thing. --nērun -- m.inf. to go out from a share, to be outside a distribution; i.e. not to receive one's due or expected share at a distribution, even though present. -wān adj. c.g. having good fortune, prosperous. -wönī f. the possession of good fortune, prosperity. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come into sharing, or into one's good fate; of a husband (or wife) becoming partner for life (as a result of fate worked out in former births) with his (or her) wife (or husband). Cf. bāgȧnⁱ yunᵘ. ¶ bāgyukᵘ adj. (f. bāgicᵘ̈), of or belonging to a share; of or belonging to good fortune, hence prosperous. ¶ bögⁱ 3 pl. nom. shares; good fortune, prosperity, the happening of prosperity. --karȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to make shares; to arrange in, or to divide out into, shares. --ninⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to take away good fortune; to have one's prosperity or good fortune destroyed owing to some act of folly, robbery, ill-success, failure of crops, or the like. --wŏthȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. good luck to rise up (and depart), to lose one's good luck. ¶ bögis pĕṭh wātun m.inf. to arrive upon good fortune, to arrive at exactly the right time, so as to share in the fruits of another's success.
m. the mu'aẕẕin who calls out the bã̄g (q.v.) or call to prayer (K.Pr. 25).

or bögin (for bögⁱ 3 see bôgᵘ) postpos. governing dat., at about the time of, u.w. words indicating a part of the day or night, as in shāmas bögⁱ (or bögin), at eventide; subahas bögⁱ (or bögin), at dawntide; mandĕñĕs (or mandĕñĕn) bögⁱ (or bögin), at about midday.
(for bögⁱ 3 see bôgᵘ), postpos. governing abl. (with vbs. of giving, accepting, etc.), on account of, for the sake of, in exchange for.

c.g., pron. of 1st pers. I (YZ. 19). In poetry this word sometimes takes the form bō or bū. With the emph. part. y, it takes the form bŏy (Siv. 24) or buy, even I, I indeed. So also with the conj. ay, if, we have bŏy, if I (Gr.Gr. 257), and similarly we have bŏ-ti, I also (Gr.M., Śiv. 73, 119, 988, 1608), bŏnai, not I (Gr.Gr. 22). This pronoun has no gen. sg. or pl., employing instead thereof the possessive prons. myônᵘ, my, and sônᵘ, our, qq.v. In the sg. for all cases exc. the nom. it has mĕ (Śiv. 511). In the pl. its nom. is ȧsⁱ 1 (Śiv. 984); other cases, exc. gen., asĕ (Śiv. 1284). (For ȧsⁱ 2 see asun.) ¶ As in the case of the other personal pronouns, this pron. has a series of pronominal suffixes, but only for the sg. number. It has no suff. for the pl. These suffixes can be optionally added to any finite form of a verb. The suff. of the nom. sing. is s, and of all other cases of the sg. is m. These are added directly to forms ending in vowels, but when added to a form ending in a consonant they take a as a junction-vowel. Thus pokᵘ + s becomes pokus, I went; korᵘ + m becomeskorum, made by me, I made; korun + s becomes korᵘnas, I was made by him, he made me. ¶ There are certain irregularities in adding these suffixes. The principal are: (1) A final h is dropped before them, and a final kh (the suffix of the nom. of the 2nd pers. sg. and of the 3rd pers. pl.) becomes h. Thus chhuh + m becomes chhum, there is to me, I have; korukh + s becomes korᵘhas, I was made by them, they made me. (2) Before them the term. av becomes ō and iv becomes yū. Thus karav + m becomes karōm, we shall make for me, and kariv + m becomes karyūm, make ye me, or for me. (3) When added to the 3rd sg. fut. the final i of the verb is changed to ĕ. Thus kari + m becomes karĕm, he shall make me. (4) When added to the 2nd sg. impve. they take u as a junction vowel. Thus kar + m becomes karum, make thou me. (Cf. Gr.Gr. 87, 181, 183, 257.) ¶ bŏh-tāna wanȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to tell an imaginary story, so as to gain another's confidence. ¶ asĕ, see ab. asĕ-ti pāṭhi interj. may that be my luck!, an exclamation used at seeing another's good fortune. ¶ ȧsⁱ, we see ab. ȧsⁱ gȧʦhⁱ baḍȧnⁱ interj. may we flourish! may we prosper! lit. it was proper that we should go forward. --gaʦhaw zēnȧnⁱ -- interj. may we be victorious! lit. it is proper that we should conquer. --gay asiy -- interj. indicating self-satisfaction, 'I'm the man!,' lit. we (honorific pl.) are we indeed. ¶ bō, bū, see ab. bŏy, buy, even I, I indeed, if I, see ab. bŏ-ti, I also, see ab. bŏ-nai, not I, see ab. ¶ mĕ acc. dat. ag. or abl. sg., see ab. mĕ-ti, me also, etc. (Śiv. 521, 525, 1165, 1434). mĕ-y, even me, me indeed, me only, etc. (Śiv. 544, 634, 644, 692, 724, 760, 768, 900, 901, 1257).
card. c.g. the special form which bāh, twelve, takes in multiplication by a number exceeding ten. Thus, kāh böhⁱ akh hath ta dŏyĕtrᵃh, eleven twelves (are) a hundred and thirty-two (Gr.Gr. 86).
etc. These are common spellings in the Roman character of the word bôyᵘ, a brother, q.v. (e.g. K.Pr. 34, 130; W. 18); similarly, böi or bö̂i for the nom. plur. böyⁱ.

m. the occurrence of a strong smell from the accumulation of filth, a stink. --anun -- m.inf. the coming into existence of a stink, a stink to be produced. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. stinking to come, to begin to stink, e.g. of stale food mixed and left by or in mixing medicines or the like.
f. dividing out amongst people by one not of their number, partition; sharing out amongst each other.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. böjᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. böjᵃrun, q.v. böjᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. böjᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. böjᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. böjᵒrᵒ), to divide, partition, esp. to divide out family property or food at a dinner; to share out mutually, to share amongst each other. böjᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. böjᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), divided out (by another), or shared out (by mutual agreement).

m. a partner (in business); a confederate (in gambling, etc.); an ally. sǖty-bôjᵘ m. a companion (Śiv. 169). ¶ böjⁱ-bọ̆dⁱ m. want of respect to elders, impudence. -bodᵘ m. partnership (Gr.Gr. 144, where the translation 'brotherhood' is wrong). -baṭh f. (sg. dat. -baṭi), partnership (K.Pr. 127, spelt bājbaṭ), cf. Gr.Gr. 145. In K.Pr. 107 and 224 the word is spelt bājwaṭ.
(cf. bôjᵘ) m. one who has a share (bāj) in anything; hence, one who gets such and such as his allotted share of fate, one who gains possession of (L.V. 62).

f. (sg. dat. bŏki, pl. nom. bŏka), the loin, the small of the back; (pl.) the kidneys. -tara m. the diaphragm, or muscle on which the kidneys lie, and which separates the thorax from the abdomen. ¶ bŏka hᵃnañĕ f. pl. inf. to become joyful, to rejoice; sometimes used of a swollen breast, lactation to commence. -türᵘ̈ f. the diaphragm, i.q. bŏkh-tara. -wüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -wacĕ), a kidney, so called from the lobulated kidney of many animals. -wacĕ-khỗṭᵘ m. a piece of kidney, the split half of a kidney. Cf. khỗṭᵘ.

m. a bundle (as of clothes, etc.), wallet, knapsack (K.Pr. 37, W. 154). -bahā m. sweating in a bundle, the rotting of clothes, etc., left tied up in a bundle. --karun -- m.inf. to make a bundle, a method of tying up a criminal as a punishment.
m. one who is in arrears, a debtor, esp. a debtor to the Government treasury (L. 448).
f. crisp bread or cake (like pie-crust) made of butter, milk, and flour.
adv. and conj. moreover, but, nay, nay but, nay rather, on the contrary.
f. (sg. dat. bö̆kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), prosperity, worldly bliss (K. 424, 1077).

m., i.q. bạkhᵃ̇tᵃ̇, q.v., attached or devoted to, faithful, honouring; (with regard to the Deity) full of devotional faith. Cf. bạkhᵃ̇tᵃ̇ and bakhᵃth 2. With suff. of indef. art. we have baktāh (Śiv. 1038); sg. dat. baktis (Śiv. 857); abl. bakti 2; pl. nom. bȧktⁱ 2 (Śiv. 507, 522, 663, 1257, 1525, 1888, 1893); dat. baktĕn (Śiv. 14, 103, 199, 663, 981, 988, 1007, 1058, 1424).
m. (f. bŏkᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), a child (of a human being); a whelp (of a dog).

m. the hand with the fingers extended together, so as to hold grain, flour, or the like; an open handful; a claw (El.). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to scratch with all the fingers (e.g. a person's face or at his eyes). ¶ bŏkⁱ dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to render a person inwardly unhappy by the employment of abusive words, to abuse, objurgate. --lagȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. inward unhappiness to be produced by abuse, etc.; to feel hurt by abuse; the eyes to be scorched by a bright light.

m. remainder, residue, surplus; arrears of revenue, etc. (cf. L. 407 and bākay). --thawun -- m.inf. to leave over and above; (in distributing food, etc.) to leave people without their share, or to leave part undistributed. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain over and above, to be over, be left; to remain unpaid or unadjusted, to be still due; (in a distribution) to remain without getting one's share.

m.urine. --yunᵘ 1 -- m.inf. urine to come, to commence to urinate. ¶ bōla-mīl f. a kind of ink, usually employed for writing in the Persian character. It is made up with burnt rice, beeswax, and other ingredients.

m. a mistake, blunder, slip of the hand, mistakenly doing something or touching something with the hand which should not be done or touched; heedlessness, fickleness (Gr.Gr. 23). --yunᵘ 2 -- m.inf. such a slip of the hand to occur.

m. speech, speaking word, talk, conversation, cf. būlⁱ; used in the following compounds: -bajā anun m.inf. to bring one's word aright; hence, to carry out one's wishes against those of another, to have one's way. -bōsh m. or -böshᵘ̈ f. the song of birds, f.pl. -bāshĕ (Śiv. 502, 1783); the similar sound made by an infant in arms or the sounds made by a dumb man (K.Pr. 93). ¶ bōla-paʦh f. (sg. dat. -paʦhi), belief in a word, accepting a verbal statement or promise made by a person in whom one has confidence. ¶ bōlas āmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), obstinately intent on attempting something which is left undone and which should not be done; acting perversely. --onᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --üñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), incited to carry out any abandoned work. --anun -- m.inf. to incite or persuade a person to perform a work which he has abandoned. --lāyĕna yunᵘ -- m.inf. obstinately to perform or refrain from any act, in spite of entreaties; to act perversely. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be obstinately intent on doing anything, esp. something wrong or objectionable.
m. (sg. dat. bōlānāthas), Bhōlānātha, a N. of Śiva (Śiv. 168).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bōlanôwᵘ), to teach to speak (e.g. a child or a parrot) (Śiv. 1376). bōlanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bōlanöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), taught to speak (as a child or a parrot); enabled to speak (as of a dumb person cured).
. An additional meaning is 'to cause to address, to summon, call to' (L.V. 105).
m. (f. bōlawüñᵘ̈), one who speaks; (adj.) talkative, loquacious, garrulous.

f. a kind of nose-ring worn mostly by children and suspended from the septum; usually set with a pearl or other gem. ¶ bōlāki-broḍᵘ m. a septum of the nose (i.e. a nose) to which such a ring is attached; adj. (f. -brüḍᵘ̈), (a child) wearing a nose-ring. -nĕcyuvᵘ m. a boy who wears a nose-ring; hence, a boy of about nine years of age or less.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. būlᵘ, 2 p.p. bōjyōv; conj. part. būlith; freq. part. būlⁱ būlⁱ), to speak, talk, tell, say, utter, pronounce (Siv. 439, 555, 599, 1052, 1797); to give forth sound, e.g. (of a bird) to sing, chirp, and so on according to the sound of the animal (Śiv. 181 (of birds), 1360, 1814). būlᵘ-motᵘ adj. (f. būjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), spoken, said, etc.; (in narrative, etc.) a person previously referred to, the said, the above-mentioned. bōlan-wôlᵘ m. (f. bōlan-wājĕñ), one who speaks, esp. one who speaks impudently or impertinently.
adj. (as subst., f. bōlᵃladiñ), one who by mistake does some improper or unaccustomed work, one who acts under a wrong impression.
adj. (f. büjᵘ̈), convalescent, recovered in health (Gr.Gr. 9).
m. obstinacy, determination, determined prowess. --dārun -- m.inf. to display such prowess (Rām. 1451).
for börⁱ pl. nom. of bôrᵘ 1, loads (Rām. 1041).

m. anger, cf. bomᵘ. Used in the following compounds: --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. anger to fall; hence, an outburst of anger against one's own people so as to spoil a holiday or the like; the occurrence of some anger-causing impediment on such an occasion (cf. bam 1). --ʦalun -- m.inf. anger to flee, anger to be appeased, esp. of the calming of some one usually of an angry disposition. ¶ bōma-bukurᵘ m. (f. -bukᵘ̈rᵘ̈), anger-faced, of one of such an angry disposition that his face habitually shows the fact. -dĕv m. (f. -dĕviñ), one whose anger causes impediments, e.g. a passionate child who spoils a social gathering or a game. -ʦọ̆lᵘ adj. (f. -ʦŏ̈jᵘ̈), full of silent rage, raging inwardly.
or baum m. the planet Mars; voc. bauma (Śiv. 477). -wār f. Tuesday (El., who makes it m.).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. bōmaladiñ), filled with inward wrath (on experiencing opposition, or something disliked occurring, etc.), sulky.

m. (sg. dat. bomburas), a drone-bee (El.), a humble-bee (Śiv. 1007, 1008, 1035); in phrases such as hāputh bombur, a black bear (L. 458), the word means black-bee coloured. ¶ bombura-goḍᵘ m. a bees' nest, a beehive. -gītā f. the name of a famous song of the herdmaidens in honour of Kṛṣṇa, in which his dark complexion is compared to the colour of a humble-bee (Śiv. 1007). In Sanskrit this song is called the Bhramara-gītā, and forms part of the 47th chapter of the 10th book of the Bhāgavata Purāṇa. It is a favourite subject of translation into modern Indian vernaculars. -par m. bee's-wing, the name given to the buckle of a jēgā or turban ornament.
(f. bümᵘ̈), of an angry disposition, passionate, wrathful, esp. when the fact causes annoyance to others. Cf. bōm 1 and bam 1.

adj. c.g. low, not lofty (as a room or the like) (Gr.M.). More usually as adv., below, beneath (Śiv. 966, 985, 1412, 1879). --anun -- m.inf. to bring down (El.; K.Pr. 43, spelt bun; YZ. 257). -bŏn adv. gradually lower, lower and lower (u.w. vbs. of motion, descent, etc.). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go down, descend (El.). -kun adv. towards the lower part of anything, in a lower direction, downwards (Gr.Gr. 161, K.Pr. 38). --ta hyorᵘ gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go down and up, to be tossed up and down (Gr.M.). --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to lower, let down (e.g. a bucket into a well). --wasun -- m.inf. to descend (K.Pr. 158). ¶ bŏna-hyorᵘ adv. up and down, from top to bottom; one above and the other below; upside down, topsy-turvy. -hyūrᵘ adv. id. -kani adv. down, on the ground (u.w. vbs. of putting, etc.). -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), lower, nether, under, below. -pĕṭha adv. from below, from beneath, commencing from the bottom. -shuth adv. id. ¶ bọ̆nⁱ-kinⁱ adv. below, along the bottom, along the foot (of) (u.w. vbs. of going, etc.).
adv. like, as if, as in suh bŏnā, as if it were he; korun bŏnā, as if he had done it.
. An alternative form is bŏna (e.g. Rām. 401, 542, 795, etc.).

f. a certain ornament, a glass armlet, bracelet, bangle, worn by Musalmān women (El.); El. s.v. bungir (q.v. for varieties of bracelets) says they are made of different shapes, and of various materials, such as gold, silver, brass, copper, tin, or a fine kind of clay. ¶ bọ̆ngᵃri-gulᵃ m. an arm covered with many glass bangles. -gorᵘ m. (f. -gürᵘ̈, but his wife is -gȧrⁱ-bāy), a glass bangle-maker, a bracelet-maker (El.). -wôñᵘ m. (-wāñĕñ), a seller of glass bangles, a bracelet-seller (K.Pr. 154).
f. a woman on whose arms there are many glass bangles.
m. the assistant of a merchant, a salesman.
adj. (f. bŏnimᵘ̈), lower, of or belonging to below (Gr.Gr. 161).

or bonᵘ 1 m. a heap, a pile (Śiv. 126, sg. dat.; 1199, sg. nom.; 1287, pl. dat.). Cf. ban, banna. ¶ bȧnⁱ gaʦhȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. piles to be made, a large pile or heap to grow, heap to be heaped upon heap.

f. a stick or pole with slings at each end for carrying boxes, baskets, etc., across the shoulder, a 'bangy'; a suspended rail for hanging clothes or the like. Cf. ala-böñᵘ̈ and Śiv. 1531. ¶ bāñĕ-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a person who carries baggage, etc., on such a pole.
m. a chisel for cleaving wood (El.).
f. the whole collection of pots, pans, dishes, etc., in a kitchen or the like. Cf. bāna 1.
f. a large vessel in which cowkeepers collect and store their milk. bāñĕ-dŏd m. sour milk, made by collecting and storing raw and unboiled milk till it turns sour.
m. a burden, load (Rām. 846). Cf. bār and bôrᵘ 1, and Gr.Gr. 22.
m. the plaster on a wall, usually of mud mixed with hemp, chaff, etc. Cf. bôrᵘ 2.

or bairav  m. N. of any one of eight manifestations or forms of the god Śiva (Śiv. 986); N. of one of a certain class of lesser deities who form Śiva's host. One of these is often the local godling of some locality or tract of country, and special localities protected by him are looked upon as sacred. Such a Bhairava is a very terrible deity. Cf. Śiv. 1683. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. Bhairava to happen; hence, sudden unexpected destruction to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to offer oneself as a sacrifice by committing suicide before the image of a deity; met. to become engaged in some very perilous action. -nāth m. N. of Śiva (Śiv. 976, 1552, 1894).
burdus, or borᵘ-dusᵘ m. fighting, coming to blows (of people gathered together in a house or at an assembly) (K.Pr. 85).
adj. c.g. in lŏti-börī, possessing a light weight (Śiv. 1048).
adj. c.g. (m. sg. dat. börīkas), very heavy, very difficult.
f. rain, a shower of rain. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. rain to fall, to rain; esp. of a sudden fall of rain.
adj. (f. bürʦhᵘ̈), filled, (of a garment) covered (with blood) (YZ. 126).

adj. [m. sg. dat. baratis, ag. barᵃ̇tᵃ̇, pl. dat. baritĕn (H. vi, 15); f. sg. nom. barᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈, q.v.], filled (both lit. and fig., e.g. a vessel with something material, or a man with wealth, virtue, as in srēha-borutᵘ, filled with love (Śiv. 1806), etc.); f. (of a woman) pregnant, esp. when approaching the time of her delivery.
adj. (m. sg. dat. baratis, ag. barᵃ̇tᵃ̇, f. nom. barᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), smeared, plastered, used --˚ after words meaning oil, mud, or the like.
f. wages for carrying loads, porterage. Cf. börᵘ̈.

m. a load. Cf. bôrᵘ 1. By some spelt bārī (e.g. K.Pr. 147, 166). Used in the following compounds:-- -gurᵘ m. a pack-horse. -khar m. a pack-ass; met. one who works like a pack-ass, one who, in return for the necessities of life, works entirely for another's profit, i.e. who makes over all his earnings to his master. --khārȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to cause loads to mount, to pretend to undertake a task, which one really wants done oneself, at the instigation of another, and to lay the whole responsibility on him; i.q. börⁱ khārȧnⁱ, see bôrᵘ 1. --ladȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to load burdens, to pretend to undertake some work at the instance of another, to throw the whole burden and responsibility (in case of failure) upon another, while ready to claim the credit in case of success; i.q. börⁱ ladȧnⁱ, see bôrᵘ 1. -sörᵘ̈ f. loading, the act of making up loads, and transferring them from place to place. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a man or beast actually employed in carrying a load, a porter or pack-animal. -way f. the wages of a porter (Gr.Gr. 143). Cf. börᵃway. -zyunᵘ m. firewood collected in the forest and brought in bundles for sale, as distinct from chopped logs.

m. (for borᵘ 2 and 3, see under barun 1 and 2; cf. also borᵘ-dusᵘ under bŏrdus), a large crack or fissure in a wall or the like; a hole in a wall permitting entrance (Gr.Gr. 9); a mine in a wall cut by a housebreaker. Cf. bürᵘ̈. --karun -- m.inf. to make a hole in the wall; met. to pry about and as the result reveal another's secrets. --ṭukun -- m.inf. to bore (like a rat) a hole in a wall; met. to spoil or impede another's work by calumny or backbiting him or it to his associates or helpers. --ʦaṭun -- m.inf. to cut hole in a wall, to dig a mine through a wall in order to commit housebreaking. --trukun -- m.inf., i.q. --ṭukun.

m. (dat. böris, abl. bāri), a bundle carried on the head or shoulders, load, burden (K.Pr. 34, 104, Śiv. 199, 1027, 1810, 1849, 1896); the cargo of a ship (Gr.M.). Cf. bār, bōr 1, and börᵘ̈, and Gr.Gr. 143. --khasun -- m.inf. a burden to mount, a burden to be imposed (upon a person) (Śiv. 1637). --thawun -- m.inf. to place weight, to lean upon (Gr.M.). --tulun -- conj. 1, to load, carry (El.). --tulanwôlᵘ -- m. (f. --tulanwājĕñ --), a porter (of burdens) (El.). --wālun -- m.inf. to cause a burden to descend, to relieve a person of a burden, to lighten his load (Śiv. 1506). ¶ börⁱ khārȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to cause burdens to mount, to lay or transfer a burden or (fig.) a responsibility upon anyone; esp. when doing any work, to throw the whole responsibility on someone else, under the pretence that it is undertaken on his behalf or that he is a fellow-worker or accomplice. Cf. börᵘ̈ khārȧnⁱ. --khasȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. a burden or responsibility to be transferred to, or laid upon, any person; esp. as above. --ladȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to load burdens, to put or transfer a burden or responsibility upon another; esp. to make a show of complying with another, apparently only acting under his orders, in some work which one wishes to do oneself, and thus to throw the responsibility upon him. Cf. börᵘ̈ ladȧnⁱ, s.v. börᵘ̈. --rōzȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. burdens to remain, a responsibility to be incurred or shared; esp. for a crime or its punishment. --thawȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to place loads; to pretend compliance with any order, but to leave the work to be done, or the responsibility to be undertaken, by the giver of the order.
m. the plaster on a wall, etc., made up of lime, mud, etc. (Rām. 568). Cf. bōr 2.
or bāryā  f. a wife (Śiv. 1825, bāryā).

m. pride, insolence, arrogance, haughtiness, rudeness, shown in refusing a favour or the like. --khārun -- m.inf. to cause arrogance to rise, to give a mean person an opportunity for showing arrogance by asking a favour from him, agreeing with what he says, etc. --khasun -- m.inf. arrogance, etc., to arise under the above circumstances. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. pride to come, respect for something to increase, as e.g. when something formerly easy to get has become rare; honour to come, to be attained by a person (as when he is suddenly raised in rank) (Śiv. 44, 167).
f. similarity of condition of life, similarity of fate.
f. incitement to speak, encouragement to speak, teaching to speak (of infants, parrots, etc.).
see bāh; also fem. of bôshᵘ 1 and 2.
adj. (f. böshᵘ̈), able to speak (of an infant, hitherto inarticulate); able to speak a foreign language; an interpreter, translator.

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. böshᵘ̈ladiñ), one who is undergoing (the feeling of) the twelfth lunar day, one who has kept the fast of the eleventh lunar day, and who is hence not expected to be good for much on the twelfth.
m. a flower-garden (Rām. 318). bustān afrōz بستان افروز m. Amaranthus cruentus (El.).
or bosᵘ 1 m. chaff and other refuse of grain, chopped straw, broken pod-husks, and the like (K.Pr. 204, bus). For bosᵘ 2, see basun.

m. the receptacle of the undigested food, the upper part of the abdominal cavity, from the throat downwards, containing the lungs, heart, and stomach, etc.; according to El. the stomach. --phaṭun -- m.inf. the breast to burst, a disease in which the phlegm accumulates in the lungs, etc., bronchitis or the like. --phāṭawun -- m.inf. to cause (another's) breast to burst; to annoy another by incessantly talking to, asking, advising him, and giving him no opportunity to reply.

adj. c.g. stale, belonging to the day before, or to some former time and no longer fresh. -bata m. stale cooked rice; rice cooked yesterday and consumed to-day, or cooked some hours before eating (cf. bāsi rōṭī in L. 250). -drika f.pl. stale leeches, the use of leeches, after having used eeches to extract blood on the preceding day. -rath m. (sg. dat. -ratas), stale-bleeding, i.e. bleeding a person for the second time, when he has been already bled on the preceding day.

adj. c.g. a corruption of the Sanskrit Bhāskarīya, i.e. of or connected with a certain Kāshmīrī astronomer Bhāskara (not the famous Indian astronomer of the same name). Used in the following: bösⁱ-nĕchapạtⁱr, an almanac based on Ganēśa Daivajña's work entitled the Grahalāghava, which was introduced into Kashmīr by Bhāskara. In Kashmīr, Hindū almanacs have at different times been based on the calculations contained in various Sanskrit works. The oldest authority was the Āryasiddhānta (in use from the year 665 A.D.), which was in course of time (about 1758 A.D.) superseded by the Grahalāghava. Subsequently the Grahalāghava was again superseded by the Āryasiddhānta, but some almanac-makers still adhere to the Grahalāghava. Such almanacs, based on the Grahalāghava, are now known as bösⁱ, or almanacs according to Bhāskara. See JRAS., 1912, pp. 719-21.

m. (f. bŏṭiñ, buṭiñ 1 qq.v., or bŏṭa-bāy, see bel., Gr.Gr. 38), a man of Tibet, a Tibetan; usually a man of Western Tibet or Ladāk, a Ladākī (see El., s.v. túl and tulakul). -babᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. Ladākī basil, N. of a certain medicinal plant, dark-coloured, with smooth scented leaves. -bāy f. a Ladākī woman, a Ladākin, i.q. bŏṭiñ, q.v. (cf. Gr.Gr. 38). -daturᵘ m. Ladākī Datura, N. of a certain plant; also of its intoxicating seeds, flowers, and leaves. -jath (? spelling), m. a certain medicinal plant used as a stomachic (L. 76). -khọ̆bᵘ m. a Ladāk hat, the woollen-lined hat worn by Ladākīs. -khôlᵘ m. the kernel of a kind of plum (? = the Hindī Bhōṭiyā Badām, Prunus communis) imported from Ladāk. -khorᵘ m. a kind of round-leafed grass growing in lakes, and used as fodder. -malikh m. (sg. voc. -malika), Mr. Simpleton. The Ladākīs are easily outwitted by the sharp Kāshmīris. Malik is used as a title of respect or flattery (K.Pr. 191). -phamb m. the cleaned wool of the Ladākī goat. The wool is bought by women who take it home and clean it, the coarse and coloured wool being separated from the white fine wool (kilⁱ-phamb). The latter is employed in the manufacture of shawls and pashmīna; cf. El., s.v. kíl-phamb. -poṭᵘ m. a soft coarsely-woven cloth of goat's wool imported from Ladāk. -sŏy f. a kind of nettle (Urtica) imported from Ladāk and employed as a stomachic and diuretic medicine. -tᵃl m. a kind of mulberry fruit imported from Ladāk. -ʦādar f. a large soft shawl of goat's wool imported from Ladāk. -ʦᵃnunᵃ m. a luscious kind of peach imported from Ladāk. -ʦēr f. a kind of apricot imported from Ladāk, but also grown in Kashmīr; cf. El., s.v. tséra. -wã̄gun m. a tomato eaten in Kashmīr by Musalmāns but not by Hindus (El., who spells -wāngun and also bāṭa- wāngūn). -wôñᵘ m. (f. -wāñĕñ, his wife), a Ladāk merchant who imports shawl-wool, grapes, cotton, medicaments, precious stones, etc., from Ladāk. There is a brisk trade between Kashmīr and Ladāk. -vīr f. a kind of willow, Salix sp. (its bitter leaves used as a cooling remedy in fever and as a local application for the feet, L. 76). According to El., s.v. vír, two varieties of willow grow in the valley, the musk willow (mushka-vīr) and the Ladākī willow (bŏṭa-vīr).
m. sg. nom. with suff. of indef. art. bōṭāh), a boat (corruption of English word). agna-bōṭāh, a fire-boat, a steamboat (Śiv. 1831).
f. a bottle (corruption of the English word).
adj. (f. bŏṭanicᵘ̈), of or belonging to, coming from, or born or produced in Ladāk.
i.q. brō̃ṭh, q.v. L. 460 spells this word bont, and W. 97 bonth or bront, cf. ib. bontakana.
f. the profession of a panegyrist, etc.; see bāṭh 3.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. böṭhᵒrᵒ), to prune (a tree, etc.). Cf. böṭhᵘ̈.

f. (sg. dat. bāchĕ), a single long thin dried branch or twig of a tree or creeper, esp. of a willow cut off in pollarding. Cf. bāṭh 2. ¶ bāchĕ f.pl. twigs, esp. the bundles of leafed willow branches and twigs stored for winter fodder in the forks of tree-trunks; see bel. These stores are typical features of the landscape of the country. -gyoḍᵘ m. a bunch of branches; a large mass of leafed tree branches cut in the autumn, tied together by a rope, and stored in the fork of a tree-trunk for use as required for fodder. --karañĕ -- f. pl. inf., lit. to make (i.e. cut) branches; (of willows and the like) to pollard or cut off in the autumn of every second year the young withes or osier-twigs that shoot thickly in the spring from old lopping wounds. The smaller twigs and leaves are stored as above and used as fodder for sheep and goats during the winter. The larger are cut up and sold in the bazaar for firewood. -lôwᵘ m. a branch- sheaf, a bundle of slender soft twigs cut from trees in the autumn as fodder for cattle.

m. high ground, a bank, embankment (dat. pl. baṭhĕn, K.Pr. 192); the bank of a river (K.Pr. 63, Śiv. 1755, Rām. 625, etc.); the bank round a garden, etc.; the high waste ground near the foot of a mountain. sudara-boṭhᵘ, the seashore (Gr.M.). Cf. büṭhᵘ̈ 1. --khārun -- m.inf. to lift up on to the bank from the stream of a river or from a boat, to land anything (Śiv. 1023, 1840); to put to one side, i.e. in any action or business to put aside someone who is connected with it as helper or promoter. This is the active form of the following. --khasun -- m.inf. to be lifted up on to the bank, to be put ashore from the water or from a boat, to be landed (K.Pr. 121); to be put to one side, i.e. when engaged in any action or business and on the point of success, to be disappointed by finding oneself dissociated from it by some impediment or opposition. --thawun -- m.inf. to put to the shore, to bring to the bank (of something floating on a river, etc.); to set apart, put apart from others. -tal adv. under the bank; hence, secretly, privately, u.w.vbs. of giving, speaking, assaulting, or the like. ¶ baṭhi-baṭhi adv. along the bank (of a river or field); on every bank (Śiv. 1681). --khārun -- m.inf. to make proper or fit for use (of some an. or inan. obj. originally until for use or in confusion and made useful by teaching, arrangement, purification, etc.). --khasun -- m.inf. to become fit for use, as ab. --lagun -- m.inf. id., to be, or become, naturally fit for use, as ab. --logᵘmotᵘ -- adj. (f. --lüjᵘ̈müʦᵘ̈ --), made useful, put to a proper use, esp. of something previously useless or in confusion. --lāgun -- m.inf. to bring to shore, to lay along shore (of a boat or something floating in a stream); to make useful by education, by strengthening, or putting in good order, etc.; to put to a suitable use, to employ in a suitable manner. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain on the bank, to have one's habitat on a river bank or seashore; to disregard, keep aloof from any action or business (even when one has connexion with it). --thawun -- m.inf. to bring to the bank, to lay (a boat) alongside the shore; to put to one side, to disregard an instructor in or promoter of any work by acting independently.

m. a heap of dried cow-dung used for fuel (L. 460, but). --wahārun -- m.inf. to spread out cow-dung to dry in order to convert it into fuel. ¶ bȧṭhⁱ-güjⁱ f. a fire-place full of cow-dung fuel; sufficient cow-dung fuel to fill a fire-place. -kā̃durᵘ m. (f. -kã̄durĕñ), a baker of cow-dung; hence, a man or (f.) a woman who follows a filthy employment, or an employment resulting in wearing filthy clothes, etc. -lŏbur m. a single cake of dried cow-dung. -nār m. fire proceeding from dried cow-dung, a fire of this material; a spark of burning cow-dung. -pholᵘ m. a heap of cow-dung fuel, esp. a small one (Gr.Gr. 164). -tīl m. oil of cow-dung fuel; the oil which condenses from the vapour of burning cow-dung fuel and is used as a remedial application in skin diseases, sores, etc. -tyọ̆ngul m. (sg. dat. -tyŏngalas), a spark of burning cow-dung fuel; a mere spark, a hardly apparent burning spot in cow-dung fuel. -ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ f. cow-dung charcoal; cow-dung fuel slightly burnt and then extinguished. -yôrᵘ m. (f. -yārĕñ), a cow-dung-fuel fellow, a stupid man or (f.) woman, one unable to tell or to understand the object of any course of action or who acts without consideration of preceding conditions or of consequences in the ordinary acts of life.

adj. c.g. unapparent, hidden, concealed; internal, intrinsic, esoteric; (as subst.) the inward part, secret thoughts, mind, heart, disposition of mind. ¶ bötⁱnukⁱ adj. (f. bötⁱnücⁱ), of or belonging to the unseen, to a distant country, or to a time other than the present. ¶ bötⁱnücⁱ balāyyiñᵘ̈ f.inf. a sudden calamity (such as a flood, a drought, a lightning-stroke, or a pestilence) to happen.
or buṭiñ 1 f. a woman of Western Tibet or Ladāk, a Ladākin, a synonym of bŏṭa-bāy, see bŏṭa (Gr.Gr. 38).
m. N. of a country, Western Tibet or Ladāk (K.Pr. 94). Sg. gen. bŏṭanyukᵘ, q.v.
f. a kind of large vessel of the shape of a washing-basin and made of bell-metal, employed both for cooking and for eating; a washing-basin (El.).
m. that which will be, that which is predestined, fate, destiny.
(? spelling), adj. c.g. furious (El.) crazed, crazy, demented (K. 501).
or buwan  m. the earth, the world. Usually three worlds are counted--heaven, atmosphere, and earth (cf. Śiv. 118, 159, 196, 978).
f. (sg. dat. bŏwüʦᵘ̈), excessive production or fructification, esp. of crops, fruit, plants, birds, or the like. Cf. bŏwun, of which this is the abs. noun.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. bọ̆wᵘ; impve. 3 bŏvin or bŏyin; ben. 2 sg. bŏyyĕkh, pl. bŏyiw, 3 bŏyyĕn; in Gr.Gr. this verb is taken as the model for the 2nd conj., and is conjugated throughout), to become, be (Gr.Gr. 23; the ben. is very often used in this sense in blessings, e.g. Śiv. 5, 92, 111, 658, 685, etc.); to be born; to accrue, result; to be effected, accomplished; to be committed (as sin, fault, etc.); to come to pass, take place, to happen, occur; to turn out, prove to be; to serve, answer, do; (most commonly, exc. in ben.) (of crops, fruit, etc., or of swarms of insects, birds, etc.) to be produced, spring up (Gr.Gr. 205, lvi, El., K.Pr. 47, Śiv. 1291); esp. to be produced in great plenty or swarms, to grow plenteously (K.Pr. 84). ¶ bọ̆wᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bö̆wᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), become, born, etc., as above; esp. (of crop, fruit, etc.) produced in great quantity, with great fruitfulness; happened in past time, happened before now (Rām. 1601).
f. the thigh (esp. of birds); the posterior aspect of the thigh (El. bóv). Cf. ünzᵘ̈-böwᵘ̈.

or bōy 1 f. a bad smell, the smell of anything decaying or rotten, a stink. --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give forth a stink, to stink (esp. of something rotten or decaying). --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a stink to arise, as ab. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. id.

conj. 2 (only used in the imperative and benedictive moods, and then usually referred to the verb bŏvun, q.v.). Thus, bŏyyĕkh, mayst thou be (prosperous, and so on) (ben. sg. 3): bŏyin, let him be (prosperous, etc.) (impve. sg. 3). (Cf. Gr.Gr. 247 and 252.)

m. [spelt boi, K.Pr. 34, 130, and bōy, YZ. 436; sg. dat. böyis (K.Pr. 134), ag. böyⁱ, abl. bāyi, gen. böyⁱ-sondⁱ (Rām. 509, 510, 894; cf. bāyyunᵘ bel.), voc. bāyĕ or bāyi (Gr.Gr. 99, Śiv. 1482, Rām. 1161, the bāyih of K.Pr. 29) or bāyau (Gr.Gr. 99); pl. nom. böyⁱ (Śiv. 1526, 1790; bōy of YZ. 109), dat. bāyyĕn or bāyĕn (Śiv. 41; bāyⁱan or bāyⁱen of YZ. 97, 138, 372, 452), ag. and abl. bāyyau (bāyⁱev of YZ. 84, 103), gen. bāyyĕn- or bāyen-hondᵘ, voc. bāyō (YZ. 98)], a brother, whether uterine or a step-brother, cf. böyⁱ-bārȧnⁱ bel.; met. a near relation, a clansman (Śiv. 41). When opp. to kākh, q.v., it means a younger brother, cf. bāyyun bel.; cf. also bāyĕ 1. ¶ böyⁱ-bö m. "brother ba", the name by which the letter bha is called in Kāshmīrī. This letter is pronounced ba in that language, and is so called to distinguish it from or ba proper. In the Śāradā and Nāgarī alphabets it immediately follows ba in alphabetical order. Cf. bubbö, the name of ba. -bodᵘ m. brotherhood, commensality, partnership (Gr.Gr. 144). Cf. böjⁱ-bodⁱ under bôjᵘ. -bĕñĕ f. the sister of a brother; hence, a woman who has a real brother, i.e. a brother of excellent reputation, endowed alike with virtue and with fortune. -bārȧnⁱ m.pl. a collective name for a number of uterine brothers (YZ. 438, 453, Rām. 332, 443). Cf. bārȧnⁱ. The opposite is ōra-bôyᵘ, a half-brother by the same father (YZ. 84, 97, 103, 138, 452). -kākañ or bȧyⁱ-kākañ f. a brother's (usually an elder brother's) wife, a sister-in-law (Rām. 510). -lāla m. an honorific term for one who is at once an elder brother and distinguished by virtue. -tônᵘ m. the relationship of brother, brotherhood (Gr.Gr. 143); met. brotherly conduct, respect, or affection shown by one who is not necessarily a brother. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who possesses a brother or brothers. ¶ bāyyunᵘ or bāyunᵘ adj. (f. bāyyüñᵘ̈ or bāyüñᵘ̈), of or belonging to a brother; esp. when the brother is a person specially referred to, and the word is used instead of or partially representing a proper name, of or belonging to brother, cf. K.Pr. 251, where bāyinih seems to be for bāyini, masc. sing. abl. Here the word is opposed to kākun, of or belonging to an elder brother. Cf. kākh.
m. the relationship of brother (or near relative), brotherhood, close kinship (K. 536, 898); brotherhood, kith and kin, those who are close blood relations (K. 897).
m. an arm, esp. a large, well-formed arm (Śiv. 1510).

m. liquor made from grapes, molasses, rice, barley, etc.; wine, beer. -gorᵘ m. (f. -gürᵘ̈), a dealer in or seller of this beer. The fem. indicates a female dealer; a dealer's wife is -gȧrⁱ-bāy. -gȧrⁱ-wān m. a place where this liquor is prepared or sold.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. bōzanôwᵘ; pres. part. m.c. bōzanāwan, Śiv. 1652), to cause to understand, to instruct, explain (Gr.M.); to persuade, advise (Śiv. 831, Gr.M.); to cause to hear, to tell someone about something (Śiv. 41, 691, 842); to cause to be heard (Śiv. 1389); to narrate, tell (Śiv. 1652). bōzanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bōzanöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to understand, hear, etc.; esp. (of a story, etc.) caused to be heard, told, narrated. bōzanāwan-wôlᵘ m., n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who causes to hear, a narrator, teller, informer.
m. lit. a consideration-dish; hence, the nature of one who is habitually a considerer, judiciousness, a discerning nature, habitual prudence or wisdom.
c.g. one who is by nature a good listener, judicious, discerning, prudent.

m. (f. bōzawüñᵘ̈), one who hears, a hearer (Śiv. 695), one who is by habit a good hearer, or who by habit pays attention to and considers advice offered to him (Śiv. 906); as adv. even while hearing, immediately on hearing (Śiv. 736).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. būzᵘ, 2 p.p. bōzōv; conj. part. būzith, Gr.Gr. 104; freq. part. būzⁱ būzⁱ, ib. 105), to understand (YZ. 197, 198, K.Pr. 234, W. 136); to regard, consider (Śiv. 1753), reckon; (usually) to hear, listen to (Śiv. 6, 92, 93, 113, etc.; YZ. 1, 10, 22, 31, 182, 229, 247, 260, etc.; K.Pr. 34, 234); to hear of, hear concerning (anyone or anything) (YZ. 135). būzᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. būzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), understood, heard, etc. (YZ. 455); esp. heard or known before, already heard. bōzan-wôlᵘ m., n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who understands, hears, etc.; esp. one who is by nature accustomed to consider, to act with understanding and intelligence. ¶ bōzana yunᵘ m.inf. the pass. of bōzun, to be intelligible; esp. to be visible (Śiv. 665); to be seen (Śiv. 85, 1241). This verb in the pass. rarely means 'to be heard'. 'To be heard' is generally expressed by a periphrasis, such as bōzanas andar yunᵘ, to come into hearing (Gr.Gr. 169) see also yunᵘ. ¶ būzith dyunᵘ m.inf. having understood to give; to give or divide out intelligently, so that the proper persons receive the proper shares. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. having understood to take; in taking shares of anything, to claim one's proper share. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. lit. having understood to eat; to vie with, emulate, rival, cope with, confront, withstand, oppose, resist. --nyunᵘ -- m.inf. having understood to take; the converse of --dyunᵘ, intelligently to take one's proper share in the division of joint property. --thawun -- m.inf. to consider, to understand (Gr.M.).

play, sport, game, trick; doing, carrying out any profession; gambling (Śiv. 1015, with allusion also to the following meaning); swindling; conjuring, legerdemain, magic (Rām. 905); deceit (Rām. 164, 361, 1171); illusion (Rām. 25, 1611, 1732). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give deceit, to trick, swindle. -gar بازی گر or -gār (e.g. Śiv. 1644) m. (f. -gariñ, -gārĕñ), one who exhibits feats of legerdemain or activity, a tumbler, rope- dancer, juggler, conjurer (W. 140, K.Pr. 41); one who swindles, a swindles, a swindler, cheat (K.Pr. 29, Śiv. 1644, Rām. 1317, 1785). The fem. indicates a female who does these things. -garī or -görī f. the profession or practice of conjuring; the profession or practice of swindling. -gar-pöthᵃr or -gār-pöthᵃr m. the profession of a conjurer, etc., the practice of conjuring, etc.; conjuring, legerdemain; genl. deceiving, swindling. --khĕñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to eat swindling, to be swindled (Gr.M.); met. to swindle oneself, to make a careless mistake in any action. --khārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause the stake to rise; hence, beat an opponent in gambling (Rām. 1316). --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the stake to rise; to be conquered in gambling, to lose the stake; the carrying on (of worldly affairs) to rise, (of a householder) a well-conducted worldly life to be carried on (perhaps with a side-reference to losing the 'game' of salvation, to which a worldly life is inimical). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. swindling to occur, to be cheated, swindled (in buying, selling, etc.). --pakanāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause swindling to proceed; to make a discreditable living by swindling. --paküñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. swindling to proceed; a livelihood to be made by swindling. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. carrying on to fall (to occur); the household affairs of a person to be carried on prosperously owing to his having intelligent wife and children; the stake to fall, to win in gambling; swindling to fall, swindling to become apparent, to find out that one has been swindled. --tarüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be swindled (in purchasing or the like). -tārüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to swindle (in selling, etc.). ¶ bāzĕ-pĕṭh thawun m.inf. to place upon swindling, to carry on (a business of buying and selling, etc.) in a swindling way, to conduct (a trade) dishonestly. -pĕṭh rōzun m.inf. to remain upon swindling; to habitually live in a swindling manner, to habitually practise swindling. ¶ bāzi-pöṭhⁱ  adv. swindlingly, cheatingly, dishonestly, u.w. vbs. of making, carrying out, giving, speaking, etc. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), void of swindling, honest, an honest dealer; (of things) honest, genuine, not 'made to sell'.
adj. c.g. one who avoids, shuns, is displeased with a person. Only noted in K.Pr. 145, where it is used in contrast with rözⁱ.

adj. (f. böʦiñᵘ̈), --˚ possessing so many members in one's household, used with numerals as the latter portion of a compound word, thus: du-böʦyunᵘ, having two persons in one's household; trᵃ-böʦyunᵃ, having three; ʦu-böʦyunᵘ, having four; pönʦa-böʦyunᵘ, having five persons in one's household.

m. (sg. dat. böʦᵘ̈s or bāʦas, Gr.Gr. 54), a member of a person's family, a relation; pl. a person's family, the members of a household (K.Pr. 29, 100, 124; Śiv. 1445, pl. dat. bāʦan), husband and wife (K.Pr. 59); the inner apartments of a house, the harem containing the female members of his family (El., Gr.M.); a wife (f.) (qabīla) (El., K.Pr. 43, YZ. 464). In the pl. this word is often used with a genitive of the word signifying a husband, to indicate husband and wife. Thus (H. viii, 13), pātashāha-sȧndⁱ zᵃh böʦᵘ̈, lit. the two members of the family of the king, i.e. the king and queen. -bal m. power or influence due to having many members in one's family. -bata m. family food, the comparatively coarse food eaten by the ordinary members of a large family, as distinguished from the delicate food given to old people, the head of the family, children, guests, etc. -grākh adj. (m. sg. dat. -grākas; f. nom. -grākañ), the head of a large family. -syunᵘ m. family seasoning; the ordinary oil, condiments, vegetables, etc., eaten by the ordinary members of a large family, as distinguished from superior kinds given to the senior members, guests, etc. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), the head of a large household; one who is a member of a large household. -zᵃh m.pl. the two members of a family, husband and wife (H. viii, 1). ¶ bāʦi-bāʦi adv. each member of a family one by one (used e.g. with verbs of giving, visiting, or the like). bāʦan-bāʦan adv. id.
m. a clumsy, ugly-looking fool, who speaks and listens without intelligence, and whose one object is to fill his belly; an idiot.

or brānd m. the platform or landing in front of the main door of a house, the doorstep, threshold (K.Pr. 39, abl. written barándah; Śiv. 1098, ag. brāndan). -phash m. the plastering of the threshold with cow-dung plaster, done every morning by strict Hindūs. ¶ brā̃da-khotᵘ m. a room by the platform of a doorway, a door-keeper's room. -küñᵘ̈ f. the stone step in front of the main door of a house, the threshold. -pôwᵘ m. a single step leading up to a door.
f. the condition of, or acting like, a greedy, ugly, incompetent fool.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. brādyōv), to become powerful, i.q. bādun, q.v.
m. the N. of a quarter of the city of Śrīnagar, occupying the right bank of the river between the fourth and the fifth bridges. The ancient Bhaṭṭārakamaṭha. See RT.Tr. II, 448.

(poet. sometimes spelt brugu) m. (f. bragiñ), the blue heron, Ardea cinerea, L. 126 (breg). See also Elmslie s.v. brág for particulars as to this bird. The feathers are worn by Pandits on marriage days and by soldiers when visiting the Mahārāja (K.Pr. 34, Śiv. 1815). --tulȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. (lit.) to raise herons; met. to cause the down of the body to rise and fall rapidly, like a flight of herons; hence, to scold violently (e.g. a pupil scolded by his master). --wŏthȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. (lit.) herons to rise; met. to have the down of the body rising and falling rapidly like a flight of herons; hence, to feel extreme cold, to shiver from cold. ¶ braga-phamb m. heron-cotton, i.e. the head-down of a heron, worn on the caps of the children of the well-to-do. -posᵘ m. a certain wild medicinal creeper, said to resemble a heron, and to have white leaves. -tīrᵘ̈ f. a heron-feather; (pl.) the plume feathers growing on a heron's head, worn by kings and chiefs (Śiv. 1012).
m. a flame (of fire). Cf. brēh.
Sorghum halepense (El.), the Johnson grass, Cuba grass, etc.

f. (sg. dat. -kathi), a sudden, violent, or unnatural death, caused by drowning, burning, falling down a precipice, an earthquake, or the like. -kath gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. such a sudden death to occur; met. of any sudden calamity as grievous as death.
m. (sg. dat. brahaspatas), the planet Jupiter.

m. Brahma, the one self-existent, impersonal spirit, the Absolute, the Pantheos (Śiv. 1051, 1458, 1593, 1766, 1850) (voc. brahmō, Śiv. 1415, 1424); ˚- a Brāhmaṇ, a man of the Brāhmaṇ caste; ˚- the god Brahmā, the Creator. ¶ brahma-bāv the state of identification with Brahma, (according to Pantheists) final salvation; conduct like that of a pious Brāhmaṇ. -ganḍ m. the knot which ties together the three threads forming the sacred cord worn by Brāhmaṇs; any similar knot tied on things ceremonially worn. -hatyā f. murder of a Brāhmaṇ; any equally heinous crime. -hȧtⁱyôrⁱ m. (f. -hȧtⁱyārĕñ), one who is guilty of the murder of a Brāhmaṇ or of any equally heinous crime. -hȧtⁱyörⁱgī f. the conduct of one who murders Brahmāṇs, or commits equally heinous crimes. -hüʦᵘ̈ f., i.q. brahma-hatyā (K.Pr. 102). -lōkh m. (sg. dat. -lōkas), N. of a certain division of the universe, the world, or heaven, of Brahmā. -muhūrta m. a particular hour of the day, just before daybreak. A term used only by educated Hindūs; Musalmāns use the term gazal (K.Pr. 176). -nishṭh (Śiv. 1859) or -nishṭhā (Śiv. 1770), f. absorption in the contemplation of Brahma. -rākhĕsī f. the condition or conduct of a brahma-rākhyusᵘ, q.v., or of a man who acts like one. -rākhĕsgī f., i.q. brahma-rākhĕsī. -rākhyusᵘ m. (sg. dat. -rākhisis; f. -rākhĕsañ), a kind of very terrible demon, the worst kind of demon, believed to have attained his fearful powers owing to his having managed to become a Brāhman. -randr or m. the Brahmarandhra, 'Brahmā's crevice,' the suture or aperture in the crown of the head through which the soul is said to escape at death (Śiv. 1654). -rṻph m. the form of Brahma; abl. -rṻpa, under the form of B., (acting) under the condition of B. (of Śiva, Śiv. 851, 977). -rĕshᵘ m. a Brahmarṣi, a brahmanical sage, one of a class of sages supposed to belong to the Brāhmaṇ caste. -sar or -saras m. N. of a lake in Kāshmīr passed by pilgrims on the route to the sacred Gangābal (Śiv. 1176); also used met. as equivalent to brahma-randr, q.v. (Śiv. 1891). -tônᵘ m. brāhmaṇhood. -ʦöri or -ʦörī m. a Brahmacārin, a Brāhmaṇ devoted to the study of the Vēdas and preserving the vow of chastity; a young one (Śiv. 1353); an older unmarried Brāhmaṇ versed in the Vēdas (Śiv. 1047, 1507, 1523, 1887); a name of Viṣṇu (Śiv. 1377, 1838). -zān f. (sg. dat. -zöñᵘ̈) = Sanskrit Brahmajñāna, divine or sacred knowledge, esp. knowledge of the universal permeation of the one Spirit as taught by the Vēdānta philosophy (Śiv. 451, 1738, 1891). -zanm m. birth as a Brāhmaṇ, the condition or fact of one's being a Brāhmaṇ by birth (Śiv. 1593, 1670, 1748). Cf. bröhmana-zanm, under brôhmun.

m. (sg. ag. brahman, Śiv. 131; gen. brahmā-sondᵘ, Śiv. 32, 1200), N. of a Hindū god, a member of the triad of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. He created the universe and uttered the Vēdas, at the bidding of Viṣṇu (Śiv. 31, 1115, etc). Cf. brahm. -jī m. (dat. -jiyĕs, Siv. 717, 718; ag. -jiyĕn, Śiv. 679; voc. -jiyĕ, Śiv. 485), or -juv (Śiv. 802, 1116, 1142) (sg. dat. -juwas, Śiv. 697, 848), a respectful N. of Brahmā.
or brahmānḍ m. the mundane egg from which all things were created; hence, the universe (Śiv. 32, 1660, 1727); the suture in the crown of the human head, i.q. brahm-randr, see brahm (Śiv. 1909).
m. the form, condition, or state of Brahma, i.q. brahma-rṻph, see brahm (Śiv. 1864).
m. the rapture of Brahma, i.e. the rapture of absorption into the one self-existent Spirit, Śiv. 23, 1757 (with āh of indef. art.), 1782.
m. N. of the district surrounding Āgrā and Mathurā, the scene of Kṛṣṇa's juvenile adventures. braja-wösī m. N. of Kṛṣṇa (Śiv. 1435, voc. brajawösiẏĕ).
adj. c.g. broken by a crushing blow; met. reduced to a wreck by severe disease.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. brakowᵘ), i.q. brakun, q.v. brakowᵘ-motᵘ adj. (f. braküwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. brokᵘ-motᵘ, see brakun.

m. (sg. dat. brakas), a crushing blow, a blow with a heavy weight calculated to break anything. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. lit. to eat such a blow; to be broken by a crushing blow. --lagun -- m.inf. such a blow to occur; to suffer from a crushing blow; met. of a man, to be a wreck after a severe illness. ¶ braka-drāv adj. (f. -drāyĕ), lit. issued from crushing blows; hence (of animate or inanimate objects), hardened by experiencing or making a practice of undergoing blows; inured, case-hardened, trained. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to harden by blows, inure, train. --nērun -- m.inf. to be hardened by blows; to be inured, case-hardened, trained.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. brokᵘ, f. brücᵘ̈; 2 p.p. bracyōv), to crush, pound, esp. to crush grain with a pestle, or to crunch it with the teeth; to masticate; met. to confound a man with angry abuse. brakana yunᵘ m. inf. pass. to be crushed, pounded, esp. of the hand, foot, finger, or toe; to be crushed between two hard substances. ¶ brokᵘ-motᵘ adj. (f. brücᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), crushed, pounded; crunched by the teeth, masticated; met. crushed by angry abuse.
f. crushing, pounding (as hard grains in a mortar or by crunching with the teeth); met. crushing a man by abuse.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. brạkᵒrᵒ), i.q. brakun, q.v.

m. wandering, roaming, travelling (with suff. of indef. art. YZ. 190, bramāh; K.Pr. 6, ag. braman); an error, mistake; error, delusion (Śiv. 1762, 1769, 1835, 1844); an illusion, a delusive thing (Śiv. 1049, 1570, 1578, 1754, 1788-92, 1799); swindling, cheating; giddiness, dizziness. -˚ mistaking for something, as in sarpa-bram, mistaking (a rope) for a snake (Śiv. 1818). --dyunᵘ-- m.inf. to cause to wander (YZ. 190); to swindle, cheat, defraud; esp. u.w. reference to children. --dinawôlᵘ -- adj. (f. --dinawājĕñ --), false, deceptive, deceitful (El.). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be in error, mistaken. --lagun -- m.inf. to be swindled, cheated. -tam m. swindling, cheating. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to become giddy, dizzy. ¶ brȧmⁱ nyunᵘ m.inf. to be swindled, cheated.
. Add, as a new sub-article, 'brama-wônᵘ m. a wanderer, one who roams (L.V. 26).'
(YZ. 190) = bram (q.v.) with suffix of indefinite article.
m. (sg. dat. bramarācōkas), a certain kind of demon or ghost, who dwells in waste places and misleads travellers by pretending to be a light, a will-o'-the-wisp. Cf. brahma-rākhyusᵘ, under brahm.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. bramyōv), to wander, roam; to go round in circles, to revolve; to be in error, mistaken, to make a mistake. bramyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. bramyĕ-müʦᵘ̈), in error, mistaken.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. brạmᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. brạmᵃrun, q.v. (YZ. 339, Śiv. 530). ¶ brạmᵃrôwᵘ̈-motᵘ̈ perf. part. (f. brạmᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. brạmᵒrᵘ-motᵘ, see brạmᵃrun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. brạmᵒrᵒ), to mislead, lead into error, delude. ¶ brạmᵒrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. brạmᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), misled.

m. an elm-tree (Śiv. 1286), Ulmus Wallichiana and U. sp. (L. 79), U. erosa and U. pumila (El.). L. spells this word bren and brenn, El. has both bran and bren. Cf. L. 68, 70 (its young shoots used for their fibre), 79, 80. ¶ brana-dĕl m. the elm-bark, used as a medicine for cutaneous diseases. -dyolᵘ m. the bark of the young shoots of the elm, used for making rough but strong ropes (L. 70). -sūr m. the ashes of burnt elm, which have alkaline properties and are used for making lye. -zyunᵘ m. elm firewood, used principally by Musalmāns (L. 80).
m. knock, crash, flap, the sound of striking or moving anything solid.

m. a turret; the minaret of a mosque; with āh of indef. art. brangāh (K.Pr. 143). --tulun -- m.inf. to raise a minaret; met. to swear repeatedly, to call over and over again God or one's spiritual teacher to witness.
m. the name of a pargana in the south-east of the valley of Kashmir.
f. N. of a river rising in the mountains east of Kashmīr, and watering the pargana of Brang.
adj. (f. branivᵘ̈), made of elm-wood, see bran.
f. a musty smell produced in anything spoiled by damp or kept shut up from the fresh air.
(? spelling), f. a species of elm, Ulmus campestris (El.). brāri, a certain plant: it was eaten in the famine of 1877-9 and caused many deaths (L. 71). Cf. brôrᵘ 1.

m. the going bad or musty of cooked food, milk, or the like; mustiness, a musty smell. --anun -- m.inf. to bring mustiness, to make (anything) musty by keeping it from the fresh air or in a confined place. --karun -- m.inf. to make a musty smell, a musty smell to arise. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. a musty smell to come or arise.
in brash-brash m. eating again and again without limit and without regard to propriety, greedy gluttony; see brashun.
m. a bull; met. a manly, vigorous, strong man.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. broshᵘ), to eat with champing of the teeth (as animals do); to eat greedily. broshᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. brüshᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), eaten with champing of the teeth, eaten violently; met. violently abused by word of mouth.
or brēsta f.pl. fenugreek (Trigonellum fœnum-græcum, Hindī mēthī) seeds, used as a condiment.
or brĕswār f. the fifth day of the week, Thursday (K.Pr. 220, 232, W. 106).
f. (sg. dat. brüʦᵘ̈;), a trade, profession (Gr.M.).

f. (sg. dat. brö̃ʦᵘ̈), hope, expectation; brö̃ʦᵘ̈ chĕs, I (f.) am in hope (YZ. 317). --rōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. hope or expectation to remain or continue. --thawüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to hope, expect, look for. ¶ brö̃ʦᵘ̈ rāwun m.inf. to be lost in hope, to be hopeless (YZ. 37, 251). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain in hope, to continue in hope. --thawun -- m.inf. to give a person hopes, to encourage with hope.
f. (sg. dat. brö̃ʦᵘ̈), i.q. brỗtᵘ, q.v.

f. confusion, disorder, mixing up, esp. spoiling by mixing up tender things and crushing them together. --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to crush together (flowers or similar delicate things). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of flowers or the like) to be crushed together.

f. the jujube fruit, Zizyphus vulgaris. The wood is hard and red-coloured, and is used for making better quality chairs, lintels, and haircombs (L. bre, 79, 81). ¶ brạyĕ-kujⁱ or -kujᵘ̈ f. the jujube bush. -posᵘ m. a kind of thin rice gruel given to invalids.

f. N. of a small white variety of rice (L. 463, brez). ¶ braza-görⁱ m.pl. a heap or supply of the edible kernels of a certain variety of the water chestnut (Trapa bispinosa). ¶ brazi-bata m. boiled rice of the braz variety. -byôlᵘ m. seed grain of braz rice.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. brazanôwᵘ,), causal of brazun, q.v. See Gr.Gr. 174.
f. (sg. dat. brazüʦᵘ̈), polish, brightness, sheen; (of the face) brightness, cleanliness plus beauty.
adj. (f. brazawüñᵘ̈), bright, polished; (of the face) bright, clean, and beautiful.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. brazyōv, Gr.Gr. 226), to be brilliant, to have a polish, to shine with polish; (of clothes, ornaments, etc.) to be bright, clean, well set; (of the face) to be clean and beautiful, to be bright-faced. brazyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. brazyē-müʦᵘ̈), brilliant, polished, bright, bright-faced, as ab.

f. (sg. dat. brīshᵘ̈), a flame, the flame of fire, cf. brāh. --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to raise a flame (by blowing a fire or the like). --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. flame to arise, to burst into flame, or, of a fire nearly out, to flame up on the addition of wood, oil, or the like.
m. something formidable or terrible, a huge, ugly, and terrifying form, a monster. --hāwun -- m.inf. to see a terrifying monster, ghost, etc. (Rām. 1367).
