m. sexual desire or excitement in female animals, heat, the œstrum; (of cows) bulling. --lagun -- m.inf. signs of heat to appear in a female animal. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. heat to come, sexual desire to arise in a female animal. ¶ brēshĕ-āmüʦᵘ̈ f. (a female animal) who has come into heat, or is in heat. -müʦᵘ̈ f. (a female animal) mad with heat, in full heat, wild with heat. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come into heat, to show signs of heat. ¶ brēshĕn ʦāmüʦᵘ̈ f. entered into heats, i.e. to begin the series of attacks of heat which she is destined to undergo (of a female animal who is in heat for the first time). ¶ brēshĕs aʦun m.inf. to enter into heat, to exhibit signs of a first attack of heat.
adj. c.g. frightened at suddenly seeing something terrific.
adj. c.g. (as subst. f. brēshĕladiñ) (of animals or men), desirous of sexual intercourse, in rut or heat.

adj. c.g. (m. sg. dat. brēṭhas), stupid, foolish (K.Pr. 128, 195, 215); unintelligent, ignorant. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become stupid, to be capable of some act of stupidity, generally of some person usually intelligent. ¶ brēṭha-lŏpunᵘ adj. (f. -lŏpᵘ̈ñᵘ̈), met. a stupid grain-jar; a fat fool, a big, clumsy, stupid fellow. -pŏtulᵘ adj. (f. -pŏtᵘ̈jᵘ̈), a stupid statue, an utter fool, a stolid fool.
f. the actions of a stupid man, stupidity.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. brēṭhyōv), to become stupid, be a fool (of one previously intelligent); (of greasy hot food) to be spoilt by not being eaten at the proper time, to be spoilt by being allowed to get cold. ¶ brēṭhyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. brēṭhyē-müʦᵘ̈), become foolish, clumsy (of one usually intelligent).
(?), f. the tobacco plant, Nicotiana tabacum (L. 346).

f. (sg. dat. brikhi), any acute pain of the eye, accompanied by watering, swelling, and redness. The word is generally employed as a compound, as in the following: --lagüñᵘ̈ --, --wŏthüñᵘ̈ --, or --wasüñᵘ̈ --, f.inf. such a disease to occur. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- is the equivalent of the Hindī pak jānā, and is used, not only of the eye swelling, but also of fruit, etc., ripening.
adj. c.g. suffering from eye disease, in which the eyes water and are bloodshot.
in brīm-pōsh, m. the water-lily, Nymphœa alba (El.).

f. a certain tree, Celtis australis, usually found in Musalmān graveyards and in the vicinity of shrines (L. 68, 79, 81; K.Pr. 35). Hindūs look upon it as unclean and as inhabited by the Kali Yuga or evil genius of the present age. El. gives the following variants of the name of this tree, brīmdū, brimla, and brūmīj, and calls it Celtis caucasica. ¶ brimiji-chỗṭᵘ m. the small fruit of this tree.
(? m.), rice (K.Pr. 180, W. 155). The word has not been noted elsewhere. Cf. braz.
m. N. of a tree of Kashmīr (El.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. brīṭhᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. brǖṭhᵃrāwun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 173).
in britō-britō m. the act of humbly begging, imploring; repeatedly begging and imploring.
f. lamentation, wailing. --barüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. i.q. briʦhun, q.v. (K. 312, 510). Cf. baʦh, bel.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. briʦhanôwᵘ), to cause to cry, e.g. as when some dainty or longed-for object is refused to a child. breʦhanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf.part. (f. breʦhanöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to cry, given something to cry for, as ab.
adj. (f. briʦhawüñᵘ̈), one who is accustomed to wail or cry, as when a suckling child wails for the breast, or the like.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. bryuʦhᵘ, f. briʦhᵘ̈), to weep and lament, wail, as when a child cries for some coveted object, or when it is left motherless while still a child.

m. the septum of the nose. ¶ brȧḍⁱ kaḍȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to drag the septa (i.e. the septum of the nose and other parts of the face, the nose itself, lips, eyes, forehead, etc.), to suddenly screw up the face, to have the visage suddenly contorted, as when at the point of death, or as when a suckling child is in pain or suffering from hunger, or as in disgust; so wuṭhan brȧḍⁱ kaḍith, dragging the nostrils to the lips, screwing up the face to show disgust (Śiv. 830).
m. the burning end of a lighted wick.
f. the profession or duties of a Brāhmaṇ met. the sacred books used by him as textbooks for such duties.

m. (sg. dat. bröhmanas, Śiv. 1630, 1737; pl. nom. bröhman, Śiv. 1101. As ˚- this word takes the form bröhman, see, however, brahm. A female Brāhmaṇ is bröhmüñᵘ̈, q.v., but a Brāhmaṇ's wife is bröhman-bāv), a man of the Brāhmaṇ caste (Śiv. 1118); esp. the family priest of any particular person. ¶ bröhman-bāv f. a Brāhmaṇ's wife, see ab. -kūrᵘ̈ f. a young girl (married or unmarried) of the Brāhmaṇ caste. --karȧⁱ -- m. pl. inf., lit. to do Brāhmaṇs; hence, to invite a number of Brāhmaṇs to a feast on the occasion of holidays, religious ceremonies, or the like. -koṭᵘ m. a boy of the Brāhmaṇ caste, esp. the son of a poor Brāhmaṇ who has not yet been invested with the sacred cord; a boy-Brāhmaṇ, i.e. a boy who is already, in his boyhood, familiar with the duties of a Brāhmaṇ. -küṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kacĕ), a Brāhmaṇ girl, esp. a young unmarried Brāhmaṇ girl of poor parentage. -tônᵘ m. Brāhmaṇhood. -zanm or -zarm m. birth as a Brāhmaṇ; the property of a Brāhmaṇ, consisting mainly of the few utensils and books used by him in religious ceremonies, see bröhmana-zanm, bel. ¶ bröhmana-zanm m. birth as a Brāhmaṇ, Brāhmaṇhood, i.q. bröhman-zanm ab. and brahma-zanm, see brahm (Śiv. 1754, 1879, 1897).
f. a woman of the Brāhmaṇ caste, see brôhmun.
(bronṭ, W. 97), brūnṭhⁱ, etc., see under brō̃ṭh, brū̃ṭhⁱ, etc.

m. (f. brörᵘ̈ 1), a cat (m.), a tom-cat, (f.) a pussy-cat (K.Pr. 34, 35, 64, 69, 109). Cf. byôrᵘ. --mārun -- m.inf. to attack a person with abuse. --mörith thawun -- m.inf. to establish oneself by abuse, as when a newly appointed official at once brings his subordinates under his thumb by threats and abuse immediately after his taking charge. ¶ brāri-bŏkutᵘ m. (f. -bŏkᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), a kitten. -gāsa m. a certain labiate plant, used in medicine as an anthelmintic (L. 75). Cf. brārī. -hal m. cat's embryo, the embryo of a cat voided before its full time, known to be rarely found by a human being; met. anything of great rarity. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to exhibit a movement of surprise or fear, to start. -zūn f. the pleasing moonlight in the latter half of the night and before dawn. -zūn gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. owing to being deceived by the moonlight of the latter half of the night, to wrongly imagine that dawn is near. ¶ brörⁱ-jath f. (sg. dat. -jüʦᵘ̈), cat's hair (used for fine paint-brushes, etc.). -khotᵘ m. a safe or cup- board in kitchens, etc., in which milk, butter, etc., is kept out of reach of cats. -köñī f. the cat's attic, i.e. a small attic or garret immediately under the roof, suitable for storing wood or other lumber. -kāñĕñ f. id. -mālay f. anything longed for by cats, such as milk, butter, meat, or the like; met. anything longed for by children. -māy f. the act of sitting silently and motionless, unseen by others, but watchful, like a cat; stealthiness. --pakun -- m.inf. to walk like a cat, to walk stealthily. -thaph m. (sg. dat. -thapas), plunder by a cat; plundering or carrying off by anyone in the manner of a cat, i.e. by a sudden attack after stealthy watching. -zāgay f. cat's watching; stealthy watching in order to obtain anything, after the manner of a cat.
f. a she-cat, pussy-cat; cf. brôrᵘ.

m. the upper cross-bar joining the two upright posts of the wooden contrivance for raising water from a well; cf. byôrᵘ. ¶ brörⁱ-kijⁱ f. the pin securing this cross-bar in position. -türᵘ̈ f. the pointed end of the cross-bar; cf. türᵘ̈.
f. (f. of brôrᵘ 3, q.v.), a goddess, in general, to whom any particular place is sacred.

m. a god, esp. Śiva. This word is commonly found at the end of place-names, and is derived from the Sanskrit bhaṭṭārakaḥ, the equivalent of īśvara, as in Vija-brôrᵘ = Skr. Vijayēśvara, RT.Tr. II, 464. Cf. brörᵘ̈ 2.

or bō̃ṭh, adv. (of place) in front, before (Śiv. 872, 1029, 1494); (of time) before, beforehand (K.Pr. 107); formerly; in the beginning, in olden time (Śiv. 100); first in order of events (Śiv. 1160); ˚-- former, as in brᵒ-grāy, former unsteadiness, the unsteadiness of former times (Śiv. 1133), cf. brū̃ṭhⁱ-grāy bel.; postpos. (governing dat.) before (YZ. 434, Śiv. 8, 846). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give beforehand, to advance (money, etc.) (Gr.M.). -kāli adv. in former times, formerly, once upon a time. -kāli-hondᵘ adj. (f. -kāli-hünzᵘ̈, of or belonging to former times, ancient; of or belonging to the beginning, initial. -kölⁱ adv. in former times; in the beginning. -kālyukᵘ adj. (f. -kālicᵘ̈), existing or born in former times; of or belonging to former times, old-fashioned. -kun adv. (of place) before, in front; (of time) before; forwards, in a forward direction (El.); for the future, in future (Śiv. 1756). -lāki adv. from the beginning, from the very first. -lāki-hondᵘ adj. (f. -lāki-hünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to the very beginning (either of place or time). -nam m. the front end of a boat, the prow (K.Pr. 76). --nērun -- m.inf. to go out in front, to lead a procession (Śiv. 121); path brō̃ṭh nērun, to move backwards and forwards (Śiv. 1790). --pahān -- adv. somewhat in front (Gr.Gr. 94). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come forward, advance; to act publicly, behave (Gr.M.). ¶ brō̃ṭha adv. in front, in (so and so's) presence; opposite (Śiv. 1733, 1911) (--larun, to run before a person, to meet him). -kani adv. in front, opposite; from in front (Gr.M.); cf. W. 97, bontakani. -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of or belonging to in front, opposite, present, visible. --nērun -- m.inf. to go out, or advance, to meet a guest (Śiv. 85). -pĕṭha adv. from the beginning, from the first (of place or time). -wāw m. a wind in front, a contrary wind, a head-wind (Śiv. 1632). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come in front of a person (K.Pr. 17). ¶ brū̃ṭhⁱ adv. from in front, from the vicinity (of anything); in front (Gr.Gr. 154, Śiv. 115, 1609, 1790). --āmotᵘ -- adj. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), advanced, come forward; advanced in position, rank, or fortune, etc. --anun -- m.inf. to bring forward; to advance a person in rank, prosperity, good qualities, etc.; to advance, adduce (arguments). -grāy f. lit. unsteadiness in front (cf. brō̃ṭh-grāy under brō̃ṭh); hence the outward grace, etc., of some person, as seen when walking or the like. -kāli adv. in a former time, formerly, long ago. -kölⁱ adv. formerly, long ago. -kālyukᵘ adj. (f. -kālicᵘ̈), of or belonging to a long bygone time, ancient. -kinⁱ adv. in front, before, ahead, u.w. vbs. of motion, seeing, etc.; from in front, from before (Gr.Gr. 158). -lāki adv. from the first of all, up to now or here; regularly from the beginning, u.w. vbs. of motion, taking, collecting, gaining. -pörⁱ adv. in front, opposite; from the front (Gr.Gr. 160). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come in front, come forward from behind; to advance in position, rank in life, or prosperity; to present oneself publicly, behave (Gr.M.).
adv. next year, in the coming year (Gr.Gr. 158). -kani adv. about next year. brō̃ṭhasukᵘ adj. (f. brō̃ṭhasücᵘ̈), of or belonging to next year.

m. a mistaken recognition, being misled by appearances; cf. brã̄th 2. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. mistaking one person for another to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to cause a person to be mistaken by substituting something similar to what he expects to find, to lead a person to believe that a thing is something else.

or brỗṭᵘ m. a blot or drop of ink, obscuring a writing or drawing. ¶ brö̃ṭⁱ wālȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to blot or smear with ink what one is writing or drawing, to cover with blots. --wasȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. a paper, writing, or drawing to be covered or spoiled by blots.
adj. c.g. (of a writing or drawing) blotted, smudged.

or brugu 1 m. N. of a celebrated legendary saint, in Sanskrit Bhṛgu. Sg. gen. brugunᵘ, f. brugüñᵘ̈ (Śiv. 797). ¶ brugu-lattā m. kicked by Bhṛgu, a N. of Viṣṇu, who was so treated by the saint, and expressed himself as honoured by the blow (Śiv. 797).
adv. in front. brũh brũh pakun m.inf. to keep walking in front, to precede, to go along in front of a person (H. iii, 2; cf. iii, 1 and viii, 9).

m. bending or sagging of something perpendicular owing to having to support a too heavy weight; esp. the bending or twisting of the backbone from such a cause. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to cause sagging or twisting, owing to the superimposition of an excessive burden, as in the case of a man's waist, of the trunk of a tree, a pillar, or the like. --nērun -- m.inf. such bending or sagging to occur.

or brīrᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. brīri), a certain animal, said to resemble a cat (cf. brôrᵘ) and to have a voice like that of a person crying; its presence brings ill-luck. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the occurrence of something which portends or is the cause of misfortune.

or adj. (f. brū̃ṭhimᵘ̈), of or belonging to former time, of olden time; (of a procession or the like) of or belonging to the front; (of place) of or belonging to the place before one, of or belonging to the front (Rām. 13); (of time) of or belonging to the future. Note that this word can refer both to past and to future time.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. brǖṭhᵃrôwᵃ), to make stupid, e.g. a boy naturally sharp-witted whose education is neglected or who is subjected to causeless terrors; to spoil greasy hot food by allowing it to get cold before eating it. brǖṭhᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. brǖṭhᵃröwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made stupid, etc.; (of hot greasy food) spoilt by letting get cold.

or brunzᵘ (sg. dat. brinzis), the sound caused by snapping the middle finger against the thumb; the time occupied by such a snap, an instant = the twinkling of an eye; a second (K.Pr. 176). ¶ brinzⁱ mārȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to snap the finger and thumb. ¶ brinzi-brinzi adv. at every instant, instant after instant, moment after moment. ¶ brinzĕn-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, instants; met. one who has only a few moments to live, one who is at the point of death.

f. in the following: --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to go musty, of anything kept in a confined place or away from the fresh air. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to turn anything (esp. soft or juicy food) musty by shutting it up in a confined place or pressing it together so that fresh air cannot reach it. --wasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. mustiness to descend; mustiness to be caused to any soft or juicy food or the like by leaving it shut up in a vessel without allowing access to fresh air. --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. id. (lit. mustiness to arise); met. affection or friendshi to be turned to hate owing to the mind becoming poisoned or to misunderstanding.
(written by paṇḍits) f. the earth. -manḍal m. the terrestrial globe, the earth (K. 17, 776, 850). -tal m. the surface of the earth, the whole earth as opposed to the sky (L.V. 9).
f. a bubble, esp. the bubbly foam of fermentation, etc.
f. the foam or bubbles of a waterfall or of a spring issuing from its source; the saline efflorescence drawn forth from the earth at the commencement of rain, from ant-hills and similar places.
m. the name of the letter ba, used in schools. Cf. böyⁱ-bö, the name of the letter bha, under bôyᵘ.
m. a nightingale (bulbul); bubula-rostᵘ, (a garden) without a nightingale (YZ. 46).
m. a large kind of jar used for holding grain or the like.
m. (sg. dat. bubaras and so on), a bubble.
m. (f. buchawüñᵘ̈), an animal (such as a serpent) that bites or stings; met. one whose words are sharp and stinging, a calumniator.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. buchᵘ), (of a snake, scorpion, etc.) to bite, to sting; (of a beloved's hair compared to serpents), YZ. 35, 205, 265, 507. buchana yunᵘ m. inf. pass. to be stung; hence, to be stung or terrified by the memory of some former grief, pain, or calamity. ¶ buchᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. buchhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), bitten, stung.

m. learning, knowledge, wisdom, intelligence derived from study; ocular evidence, direct perception, apprehension of the senses; knowledge, perception, understanding, apprehension (Śiv. 1812, 1850); cognizability, visibility. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. intelligence, or the critical faculty (from study, etc.) to be produced; (of something hidden) to become visible or cognizable by the senses. --karun -- m.inf. to make manifest, make visible or cognizable (of something hidden). ¶ būda-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), learned, well instructed, intelligent.
became, came into existence, the past participle of the Persian būdan, to be. With emph. y, būdạy (Śiv. 1521).

adj. c.g. old, aged, of a human being, beast, tree, etc., K.Pr. 36, 121 (sg. abl.); an old man (or woman), K.Pr. 36 (pl. dat.). Cf. buḍᵘ. --ail -- f. a kind of cardamom, bearing a large seed. --bādām -- m. a kind of almond. --brang -- m. 'an old minaret'; met. an ugly, tall, fat, silly old man. --dala -- adj. (f. --dülᵘ̈ --), a lecherous old man or woman. --drǖ̃khᵘ̈rᵘ̈ -- f. an old hag; a withered, feeble, ugly old woman. --göñᵘ̈ -- f. an old harlot, a woman, a harlot in her youth, who still endeavours to practise her profession in her old age. --khorᵘ -- m. a certain round-leafed swamp plant much valued as food for cattle. Cf. L. 71. --kulᵘ -- m. an old tree, a withered tree even though young, a prematurely old tree. --pīn -- m. the birth of a child in old age (of women or cattle). -pīnukᵘ adj. (f. -pīnücᵘ̈), a child born in the old age of its parents. --ṭaṭurᵘ -- m. (f. --ṭüṭᵘ̈rᵘ̈ --), 'an old withered'; a vile, slanderous old man or woman. --ʦhāwulᵘ -- m. (f. --ʦhāwᵘ̈jᵘ̈ --), 'an old goat'; a foolish old man, a dotard, an old man who is felt as a burden by his relations. --wāl -- m. 'old hair'; grey hair, white hair. --zaz -- adj. c.g. 'an old ancient', a very old man, even whose eyebrows and eyelashes are white.

m. (sg. dat. buḍakas), flickering, of a flame; flickering, fluttering, of breath, breathing that at one time exists and at another time is almost stopped, like the flickering of a flame. --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to give flickerings, to be at the point of extinction of a flame; to draw the last flickering breaths of a dying man.
adj. c.g. wanting sense or discrimination, one who commences to converse without discrimination.

m. a certain bird, a kind of wild duck, the gadwall, Chaulelasmus streperus, good for the table (L. 129). Probably i.q. El.'s buḍun, a bird which is said to migrate to Ladak in the hot season and to return to Kashmīr in the cold season.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. buḍanôwᵘ), to cause to grow or be old (Gr.Gr. 175).
f. sinking, becoming immersed, see wā̃ṭa-bᵒ, p. 1157b, l. 44.

m. a kind of tree, the Himalayan silver fir, Abies Webbiana. Its timber is used in house and household carpentry (L. 79, 80). El. calls this badar and búdar, and also gives budal as meaning 'fir-tree'.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. buḍyōv), to become old, to reach old age (of animals or trees, etc.), cf. Gr.M. and K.Pr. 22, 36, 65, 123, 234. --aʦun -- m.inf. to enter old age, to become old; esp. to become old before one's time, to become prematurely old. buḍyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. buḍyē-müʦᵘ̈), one who has become old; one who has become old before his time, who is prematurely old.

m. a kind of bird, said to frequent the lakes north of Kashmīr, and to be not quite so large as a goose. ¶ buḍar-kônᵘ m. a certain bird, described as shaped like a sparrow, but with a long beak and tail. It dives from a height and catches small fish. A certain distressing disease of the eyelids, accompanied by swelling.
adv. in old age, in the period of old age.

m. (f. sg. nom.buḍᵘ̈, dat. bujĕ), an old man (K.Pr. 87, 127, Śiv. 943); (f.) an old woman (YZ. 241); cf. buḍa. For exam. of buji (f. sg. ag., etc.) see K.Pr. 80, W. 142, YZ. 247, 493. -ruḍᵘ adj. (f. sg. nom. bu ḍᵘ̈-ruḍᵘ̈, dat. bujĕ-rujĕ), a jingling repetition of buḍᵘ, old people and the like, i.e. old people, the helpless, the unfortunate, and the like. ¶ buḍⁱ-bab m. a father's father, a paternal grandfather (L. 460); also used for a mother's father. -pöṭhⁱ adv. like an old man, after the manner of an old man. ¶ bujĕ-buthᵘ m. a young man who has a face like an old woman's; i.e. whose face is shrivelled and wrinkled.

f. the act of painting or stamping coloured pictures or patterns on walls, cloth, etc. --khārᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to raise painting, to apply paint; esp. to paint the face (e.g. of an actor); to paint, as a practical joke, some one who has been rude enough to go to sleep in public.

m. enjoyment, pleasure, esp. worldly pleasures, as opp. to yōg or yūg, asceticism (Śiv. 866, 867, 1377, 1458, 1714); fruition (Śiv. 1696, 1835, 1838); sexual enjoyment; experiencing, feeling, perception; advantage, pleasure, delight. --karun -- m.inf. to enjoy, etc.
adj. c.g. fond of pleasure or enjoyment, a voluptuary.
f. (sg. dat. būgüʦᵘ̈), the enjoyment, possession, usufruct of that to which one is entitled (e.g. wife, house, wealth, etc.).

adj. (f. būgawüñᵘ̈), one who enjoys, experiences, suffers, undergoes, etc.; one who is fond of enjoyment, a voluptuary; būgan būgawunᵘ, one who enjoys earthly pleasures (as opp. to an ascetic) (Śiv. 866). Cf. būgun.
adj. c.g. devoted to enjoyment or luxury, a voluptuary.
f. the wife of a servant's master, a servant's mistress; K.Pr. 263 spells the word boguni. It is fem. of bugiy, q.v., cf. Gr.Gr. 38.
m. (f. bugiñ q.v.), a master (of a servant). ¶ bugiyĕ-kūrᵘ̈ f. a master's daughter (of whatever age), the daughter of a servant's master.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. būgᵘ, 2 p.p. būjyōv), to enjoy (Śiv. 1423, 1603); to enjoy the delights of the world (as opposed to asceticism) (Śiv. 1458, 1828); to experience, suffer, undergo, to reap the fruits of one's actions in this, or a former, life (Śiv. 1795); frequently with cognate acc. pl. of būg, q.v., būgan būgun, to enjoy delights (Śiv. 1377, 1714), or to reap fruition (Śiv. 1835, 1838). ¶ būgᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. būjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), experienced, suffered, undergone, reaped (as above).
f. a gunny-bag, a sack or bag of coarse material.

m. a vendor of drugs, spices, herbs, groceries, etc.; a druggist, spicer, grocer, etc. ¶ buhᵃ̇rᵃ̇-bāy f. a druggist's wife. -koṭᵘ m. (f. -küṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. -kacĕ), a druggist's child. -phuṭᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a druggist's packet; a packet of drugs made up as a medicine; a dose or doses of medicine as it comes from the pharmacy, usually wrapped in a leaf or the like. -tônᵘ m. the trade or profession of a druggist; conduct like that of a druggist. -wān m. a druggist's shop, a pharmacy.
m. He whose necklace consists of serpent-kings, a N. of Śiva (voc. Śiv. 152).
m. old age (Śiv. 22, 1637, 1791; YZ. 519), abs. n. of buḍᵘ (q.v.) in all its meanings. --aʦun -- m.inf old age to enter, the beginning of old age.
m. foam, spray (as from a waterfall); water and spray dashed into a boat by a strong wind.
a well-bucket; a bucket for lifting water from a canal or river in order to irrigate land; cf. būkh.
m. a well-bucket; a bucket for raising water for irrigation purposes; i.q. buka 2. --lāyun -- m.inf. to lower a bucket into a well (YZ. 113).
adj. c.g. hungry, ready for one's food at meal-time; met. (of a field) thirsting for rain or (of a machine) in need of oiling.
adj. c.g. hungry, hungered, starving, famished, ravenous (of one who has not had food for a long time).
m. feverish heat, fever. --karun -- m.inf. fever to arise, an attack of fever to occur. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. a severe and sudden attack of fever to occur.
adj. (as subst., f. bukhārᵃladiñ), suffering from an attack of fever; one who is still suffering from the sequelæ of a previous attack of fever.

f. a stove or fire-place with a chimney, for warming the house, not for cooking. Only wood is burnt in it, not dried cowdung (El.). It is found in the houses of the well-to-do (K.Pr. 37, 75; W. 141, 154; Śiv. 973).

f. repetition of the same word over and over again (as by a lunatic). --dᵃnüñᵃ -- f.inf. to repeat the same word over and over again, as above. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. id. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to gabble or prate nonsensically (of a lunatic) with the object of distracting the attention of some one who is busy upon some work.

m. (sg. ag. bukᵃ̇rᵃ̇), the face, countenance; met. rudeness, gruffness, K.Pr. 252 (sg. dat.); cf. bēcha. --karun -- m.inf. to speak in unfriendly tones; to deny, refuse in an unfriendly way. ¶ bukᵃ̇rᵃ̇-dorᵃ̇ adj. (f. -dürᵘ̈), stubborn, obstinate, perverse, persistent; dissolute (El., who spells the word būkirdūr); cruel, hard, pitiless (K.Pr. 167, spelt bukuri dar, f.). -khünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -khanjĕ), insolence, obstinacy, stubbornness, wilfulness, effrontery, persistence. -wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), bold, daring, fearless, confident; obstinate, stubborn, wilful. -wothᵘ adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), irreverent, bold, saucy.
f. a mistake (Gr.M., El. also has būl m.). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a mistake to occur.

adj. c.g. heedless, forgetful, inattentive, stupid. --baṭh -- (sg. dat. --baṭas --), "Mr. Silly," a little image of a man, horse, etc., with which children play, a sugar toy (K.Pr. 18). -phrôtᵘ adj. (f. -phröʦᵘ̈), forgetful, absent-minded, one who even forgets his duties, or to eat, or to put on his clothes.
adj. c.g. of a guileless or sincere nature; N. of Śiva (Śiv. 660, 819, 887, 891, 1258, 1876).

m. (in Persia and Arabia) the nightingale; (in India) the fork-tailed shrike, Lanius boulboul; (in Kashmīr) the white-cheeked crested bulbul, Otocompsa leucogenys (L. 154, K.Pr. 161, Śiv. 181, 1025, 1046).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. bulyōv), to be forgotten; to be led away, be misled, be deceived; to forget, err, go astray, stray, mistake, go wrong, blunder. bulⁱ-bulⁱ phōrüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to be eager, longing, or agitated in the performance of anything. bulyō-motᵘ adj. (f. bulyē-müʦᵘ̈), forgotten, lost, astray; forgetful, erring.
f. (sg. dat. bōlĕ), speech, language, dialect, idiom; song or note (of birds), chirrup (Śiv. 1721), (of frogs) (Śiv. 1827).

or būm بوم, f. land, ground, soil (Śiv. 1213, abl. būmi); foundation, base, root. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to drag out the foundation; hence, met., to destroy down to the root, to cause to waste away; in the hope of receiving further favours, to persistently cling to and worry a person from whom one has once before received a favour. --nērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the foundation to come out; hence, to be destroyed down to the root, to waste away. ¶ buma-sin m. an earthworm (K.Pr. 38), cf. bima-syunᵘ. -sin bāh f. (sg. dat. -sin böshᵘ̈), the name of the twelfth lunar day of the light half of the month Māg (January-February), on which the fast of the eleventh day of that month is broken. -sin daham f. the name of the tenth day of the light half of Māg, on which a fast (consisting of only one meal in the day) is performed. -sin kāh f. (sg. dat. -sin köshᵘ̈), the name of the eleventh day of the light half of Māg, on which Hindūs fast. -sina kaḍañĕ f. pl. inf. to pull up earthworms; hence, met., to stand idle and lazy, doing nothing. ¶ bumi-path m. (sg. dat. -pathas), a wide, level plain.
m. the name of a village near the famous ruins of Mārtāṇḍa, usually called 'Bamzū' by Europeans, the ancient Bhīmadvīpa (RT.Tr. ii, 465).

or bum 1 f. the long stalk of the Nymphœa stellata, see bel. ¶ bumbi kūrᵘ̈ f. a handful or bundle of such stalks, which are intended to be dried and eaten. -lū̃ṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -lū̃cĕ), a bundle of such stalks when dried. -pōsh or bumⁱ-pōsh m. the Nymphœa stellata or water chestnut. It is a lily-like plant, growing in water with a very long thin stem, which is said to have heating qualities and is dried and eaten as a vegetable in winter. A pleasant sherbet is made from the fragrant white flowers (cf. L. 72, 345, El., and Śiv. 1809). -ʦürᵘ̈ f. a bundle of Nymphœa stalks, partly dried, and put by for consumption in winter.

or bum 2 f. (usually in pl. bumba or buma, YZ. 6, 51, 78, 208, 449), an eyebrow; pl. with emph. y, bumay or bumai, even eyebrows (Gr.Gr. 22). ¶ buma-cīrüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to contract the eyebrows, to frown. bumi-ruh m. quick movement of the brows, not indicating anger.
f. the earth (El.); soil, ground (K.Pr. 187; Siv. 1235, 1476); (in Yōga philosophy) one of the stages in the acquisition of divine knowledge, of which there are seven (Śiv. 1654).
m. a man who acts or conducts himself ridiculously, a buffoon, a comic actor.

m. an earthquake, see El. s.v. bunyul. ¶ buñilⁱ-dĕv m. an earthquake-demon, i.e. a long succession of earthquake shocks as destructive as a demon. -ʦūr m. an earthquake-thief, i.e. a violent earthquake which destroys one's house and property. -yĕṭh f. a single, solitary, earthquake-shock.

f. (sg. dat. bōñĕ), the 'chinār' or Oriental plane-tree, Platanus orientalis. (Cf. Śiv. 1285, 1819; El. s.v. buiṅ; būni or būnī of K.Pr. 7, 82, 102, 162, 173; and boin of L. 79, 81.) Its capsules are used internally as a remedy for ophthalmia (L. 75). ¶ bōñĕ-muhulᵘ tārun m.inf. to ferry over a pestle of plane-wood; hence, met. with great efforts to induce some obstinate or stupid person to enter any place. -dĕl m. the bark of the plane-tree. This is sometimes subject to a mild hypertrophy, which has many, if not all, the properties of cork (El.). Powdered it is used as a remedy for skin diseases. -shĕhulᵘ m. the grateful coolness under a plane-tree; the shadow thrown by it. -wạthᵃr m. the leaf of the plane-tree (cf. Gr.Gr. 74), where we have bōñi-wạthᵃr. ¶ bōñi-ḍūnᵘ m. the seed of the plane-tree; a kind of ear-stud, made of gold, and worn by boys. According to El. the tree never bears seed in Kashmīr; but see contra, L. 82. -hawāh m. the cool breeze wafted from plane-trees.
f. handsel; first sale for ready money early in the day (considered as a good omen and as determining the luck of the day). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make such a sale.
f. a foundation, basis, base, groundwork (Śiv. 448).
f. the hoof of a cloven-hoofed animal, such as a sheep or a goat.
m. i.q. bū 3, p. 1245b, l. 7, q.v., used in the Skt. phrase bhūr, bhuvaḥ, svar, the earth, atmosphere, (and) heaven, i.e. the whole visible universe (L.V. 9).
m. a kind of woollen garment or gown made of coarse black and white yarn.
(K.Pr. 239), i.q. birav, q.v. In W. 156 misspelt burāw.
or burdama m. (sg. dat. burdamas), a mass, or collection, of wealth or of many valuable things; wealth earned and collected.
f. an angry speech addressed to a servant or naughty child, scolding. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to scold, address angrily.
or burja m. a bastion, tower, turret (Rām. 742, 1770); any sign of the Zodiac (Śiv. 523). (The Arabic plural of this word is burūj. Hence Rām. 579 has pl. dat. burūjĕn.)
f. a kind of salad, composed of pounded radishes mixed with curdled milk (dahī), and seasoned with cumin and salt. It is eaten uncooked.

(cf. برزہ) or būrza m. the inner bark of a species of birch, Betula tartarica or (L. 79) Betula utilis, which grows freely in the mountains of Kashmīr. The bark is easily separated into thin sheets and was formerly used for manuscripts. In old times it was employed as material for rough garments, worn by hermits and the like (Rām. 201, 763, 1448, 1591), or for umbrellas (Rām. 1253). It is still largely used as a wrapping-paper and for thatching (K.Pr. 167). Cf. El. s.vv. bhojpatr and búrza, and L. 68, 418. In Śiv. 901 the bark is contrasted with silken clothes. Cf. Śiv. 1687, quoted bel. -bôrᵘ m. a load of bundles of birch-bark, roughly tied up with ropes made of birch-twigs, as brought down from the mountains for sale. -chal f. a piece of birch-bark (Gr.Gr. 162). -gë̆ḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -gĕjĕ), a bundle of birch-bark, as ab. -jāma or -jyāma m. a coat, or gown, made of birch-bark (coarse and of small value) (Śiv. 1687, Rām. 5, 182, 214). -kônᵘ m. a man whose profession is to remove the bark from birch-trees. -köñᵘ̈ f. a bundle of birch-bark for thatching. -kāyĕ f.pl. a kind of apron or petticoat made of birch-bark, esp. worn by forest hermits. Cf. Siv. 901. -lürᵘ̈ f. a house thatched with birch-bark. -më̆ṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -mĕcĕ), a short rope or wisp twisted up of bits of birch-bark. -më̆ṭᵘ̈ ka ḍüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to perform the ceremony of lustration after a Hindū mother has bathed on the sixth day after a child's birth, in which wisps of birch-bark are lighted, waved over the heads of the mother and child, and then extinguished in a jar of water. -phuṭȧjⁱ or -phuṭüjᵘ̈ f. a parcel tied up in birch-bark. -pash m. a thatch made of birch-bark. -pŏstukh m. (sg. dat. -pŏstakas,), a manuscript written on birch-bark. -pōstukh m. (sg. dat. -pōstakas), id. -pūthⁱ f. a manuscript written on birch-bark, esp. a small one. -tilim f. a piece of birch-bark (smaller than burza-chal ab.) (Gr.Gr. 163). -wôñᵘ m. a shopkeeper who sells birch-bark, brought down from the hills by the hill-men. --watun -- m. a large, thin, split-off sheet or layer of birch-bark.

m. a special kind of walnut, with a thin shell, and a kernel which is easily separated (K.Pr. 229, L. 352, burzal). This word generally appears in the plural, in the following form: burzȧlⁱ ḍūnⁱ m.pl. walnuts of a special kind named burzȧlⁱ. See El. s.v. dún.

f. a crack or fissure in wood, a stone, wall, door, etc., a spy-hole. El. spells this bȧir. Cf. borᵘ 1 and Gr.Gr. 10. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a hole to occur; met. a secret plan or the like to be revealed, as if by means of a spy.

adj. c.g. yellowed; spoilt, rotted, or damaged by exposure to extreme steamy heat (of garments, fruit, or something else naturally soft, and rendered rotten); similarly, of children, rendered delicate by such heat; (of the personal appearance) shrivelled up and yellow from old age or jaundice. (In Kashmīr people often die yellow, due to bacterial septicæmia and pyæmia. Hatō busa is a term of ridicule to a feeble, dried-up, old man.) Cf. busun 2. --āmotᵘ -- adj. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), rotted, disfigured, etc. as ab. --onᵘ-motᵘ -- adj. (f. --üñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), caused to be rotten or disfigured, etc., as ab. --anun -- m.inf. to cause to be rotten or disfigured as ab. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to become rotten, disfigured, etc., as ab.
or m. ornament, decoration, jewel; (of qualities, fame, etc.) adornment.
m. the vessel out of which the poorer Kāshmīrī Musalmāns eat. It is of clay (El.).
m. a portion of the boat called ḍōnga, situated in front of the stern mahtöbī, q.v. (El.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. busᵘ), to eat from the hollow of the hand (of sattū, grains or the like). Cf. busᵘ. busᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. busᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), eaten up (of food eaten from the hollow of the hand).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. busᵘ, f. busᵘ̈), to become yellow, to become spoilt, rotten or damaged by exposure to extreme steamy heat (of garments, fruit, or something else naturally soft, but reduced to a pulp by becoming rotten); to be attacked by jaundice, or to be shrivelled up and yellow from old age, to be swollen and yellow from pneumonia, asthma, etc. Cf. busa.
m. N. of a certain crow, who was an ardent worshipper of Vishṇu, and who recited the Rāmāyaṇa to Garuḍa.
m. a gobbet or mouthful of rice or similar food taken in the hollow of the hand formed by curving the fingers, and put into the mouth at one time.
m. a flower or sprig worked on cloth or painted on paper. -dār adj. c.g. flowered, sprigged (of shawls or cloth) (L. 375).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. būtaladiñ), devil-natured; readily angered, passionate, irascible.

or būtar āth f. (sg. dat., etc., butaröʦᵘ̈, Śiv. 495, or būtaröʦᵘ̈), the earth, the world (Śiv. 496); the earth as opposed to the sky (Śiv. 468); (usually) earth, land, ground (Śiv. 1110, 1231, 1234, 1291, 1296, 1297, 1345, 1530, 1550, 1869; Rām. 504, etc.). -prāṭanwôlᵘ m. a ploughman (El.).
m. Soul of all beings, N. of Śiva (Śiv. 1055).
f. (sg. dat. būtāvēṭhi), a condition of rage, fury, or gloomy anger, as if one were subject to possession by an evil spirit.
f. inspiration or possession by a demon or evil spirit.
m. Lord of ghosts, N. of Śiva (Siv. 1135, 1175).
m. (sg. dat. butas بتس), an idol, image, statue (YZ. 198; L. 177, but). but(h)-shikan بت شکن m. an image-breaker, an iconoclast (L. 166).

m. (sg. dat. būtas; pl. dat. būtan, Gr.Gr. 51), a kind of malignant spirit (believed to haunt deserts, deserted houses, burning ghāṭs, graveyards, cross-roads, trees, etc.), a ghost, goblin, demon (Śiv. 12). --aʦun -- m.inf. a devil to enter, i.e. a malignant spirit to enter a corpse and vivify it, or to take possession of a living person so as to render him insane or maniacal. --lagun -- m.inf. a demon to possess a person; a fit of passion to arise, e.g. in consequence of the parent of a child, a near relation, or husband not granting a wished-for treat. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to raise a devil; to put some one, esp. a woman or a child, into a rage by opposing their wishes. ¶ būta-bal m. 1 , a propitiatory oblation made to evil spirits; 2 , supernatural power obtained through the help of a malignant demon; 3 , a place haunted by a malignant spirit. -grakh f. (sg. dat. -graki), devil's ebullition; hence, the birth or production of anything animate or inanimate in excessively luxuriant quantities or swarms. -grakh diñᵘ̈ f.inf. great productiveness to take place or exist (as in the case of a numerous progeny, of crops, of wealth, etc.). -grakh lagüñᵘ̈ f.inf. id. -khᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ f. devil's nose-mucus; the distress experienced by the disgrace of failing to accomplish a wished-for purpose. -khᵘ̈ñᵘ̈gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. shame at such disgrace to occur. -khᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to cause such disgrace by refusing or withdrawing promised help or the like. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a devil's cub; one (especially a male child) of a very passionate temper, like one who is possessed of a demon. -sĕd f. (sg. dat. -së̆zᵘ̈), rendering a demon subservient by some incantation or spell, and thereby acquiring magical powers. -ʦọ̆lᵘ m. a devil's screen, i.e. one who is merely a screen in front of a devil; one who is of a sullen, morose nature, cross-grained, cantankerous, sulky. -war m. an uncontrolled nature, want of self-control, a fickle disposition. -wash f. the making a demon subject to a person by incantation, spells, etc.
m. (sg. dat. b ūtas), ashes with which devotees of Śiva smear their bodies; used --˚, as in amar-būth, q.v.

m. (sg. dat. būtas) (in Śaiva philosophy) one of the group of five tattvas, or factors, of which the apparent universe consists (Skt. bhūta or mahābhūta). They are, in Skt. pṛthirī, earth; āp, water; agni, fire; vāyu, atmosphere; and ākāśa, the sky. See the vocabulary of L.V. for further particulars (L.V. 77).
f. ugly-facedness, foulmouthedness, abusiveness, scurrility. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be abusive, foul-mouthed, scurrilous.
m. a person's lot in life, fate (supposed to depend upon his actions in a former life). Cf. bēchan-buthᵘ, under bēcha.
f. (sg. dat. bachĕ), a heap, a bank rising out of level ground. Cf. boṭhᵘ 1.

m. (K.Pr. 82, 243, spells this but, but elsewhere buth or buṭh [sic]; L. 460 has but), the face, esp. the human face (K.Pr. 36, 38, 82, 84, 105, 160, 189; Śiv. 68, 128, 1155; Rām. 258, etc.); the mouth (cf. acholᵘ); the front (of a house, etc.); the right side (of cloth, etc.); the front part, toe (of a shoe, etc.); (?) the tuck of a turban (L. 464, but); face, audacity, impudence (cf. bēchan-buthᵘ under bēcha); appearance, outward fashion; gabi buthi, a sheep in appearance (K.Pr. 63, W. 21). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give face; to come forward to undertake a task, esp. to assist some person who has to undertake the expense of a marriage or the like but has not the necessary means, by enabling him to undertake the responsibility. --hāwun -- m.inf. to show the face; hence, to scold, threaten, menace. --karun -- m.inf. to make a mouth; to refuse a request with abusive words. --ladun -- m.inf. to build a mouth; to show displeasure by twisting the features (esp. when one has suffered loss by another's action), to frown angrily. --ladith bihun -- m.inf. to sit frowning; to remain sullen and full of silent wrath at some action disapproved of. --nahāwun -- m.inf. to obliterate the face; to crush a person with abuse, esp. someone who is addressing the abuser. --phirun -- m.inf. to turn the face, to give an insolent reply (e.g. a servant to his master, or a debtor to his creditor). --payun -- m.inf. to make the face red-hot, to conduct oneself audaciously (in begging or the like). --payĕnun -- m.inf. id. --rangun --, --ranganāwun --, or --rangawun -- m.inf. to colour the face; to become mean, insignificant (of a respectable person taking to mean employment, begging, etc.). --samun -- m.inf. the face to become level; to show sudden courage (as of one who is weak, timid, or lazy, for once in a way addressing or making a request to an angry, illiberal, or very powerful person). --tarith pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall to the ground and lie motionless with the limbs spread out (e.g. from illness, or as the result of an extreme effort). --ʦọ̆kᵃrāwun -- m.inf. to make the face angry, to frown (El.). ¶ buthⁱ-boḍⁱ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈, sg. dat. -bajĕ), having a large face or mouth; one who is talkative, eloquent, loquacious; one who has attained eminence by the accumulation of wealth or the gain of a reputation; one universally honoured. -bākal adj. c.g. one whose mouth is full of sobs; (of children) one who is continually crying, cause or no cause, a cry-baby. -chaturᵘ adj. (f. -chatᵘ̈rᵘ̈), pretty-faced (esp. of children). -dag f. the buffeting of a violent shower of rain in the face of a traveller. -dār m. (f. -darĕñ), one who is in front, a principal man in a village, a leader of society. -dyār m. face-money, N. of a poll-tax imposed upon Hindūs by the Paṭhān Governor, Muḥammad 'Az̤īm Ḵẖān (expelled A.D. 1819); see L. 197 ff. -holᵘ adj. (f.-hüjᵘ̈), crooked-faced (of a man); crooked-fronted (of a house); crooked-pointed (of shoe or the like). -har f. wrangling or verbal quarrelling immediately on coming face to face (of two enemies meeting each other). -khạkhᵃr f. face-torture; hence, the pain or inconvenience caused to an old person or a cripple, etc., in uselessly going anywhere and returning, see khạkhᵃr. -khạkhᵃr diñᵘ̈ f.inf. to cause such pain or inconvenience. -khạkhᵃr lagüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to suffer such pain or inconvenience; to needlessly undergo the toil of going over a long and difficult road. -khünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -khanjĕ), steadiness of face; hence, the condition of one accustomed to endure another's abuse or insults. -kinⁱ āmotᵘ adj. (f. -āmüʦᵘ̈), madly arrogant, purse-proud, puffed up (of some mean person suddenly raised to power, wealth, or dignity); see -kinⁱ yunᵘ bel. -kinⁱ anun m.inf. to cause a person to be arrogant, etc., as ab. -kinⁱ onᵘ-motᵘ adj. (f. --üñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), one who is caused to be arrogant, etc., as ab. -kinⁱ yunᵘ m.inf. to become madly arrogant, to become puffed up, purse-proud (of a mean person suddenly raised to power, wealth, or dignity). -lab f. the cheek. -lāgay f. the occurrence of a quarrel or bad feeling, esp. between relations or friends. -lāgay gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. such quarrelling or ill-feeling to occur. -lāgay karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to wilfully start a quarrel with one's relation or friend for one's private ends. -nonᵘ adj. (f. -nüñᵘ̈), barefaced, e.g. when a child is sleeping with its face uncovered; (of a woman) barefaced, shameless, audacious; clean-faced, white-faced; (of cloth, rice-grain, etc.) clean and white externally; cf. buthi-nonᵘ bel. -phĕshĕl m. (f. -phĕshạl or -phĕshil), unlucky-faced; a man, or other m. obj., whose face it is unlucky to see the first thing in the morning, immediately on rising from bed. The f. forms imply a woman, or other f. obj., possessing the same unpleasant character; cf. phĕshil. -phyurᵘ adj. (f. -phirᵘ̈), face-turned, insolent, insubordinate, rude, ill-behaved, answering-back (of a servant to his master, a child to his parent, a pupil to his teacher). -püjᵘ̈ f. a big basket of a face; a great, round, ugly, and fierce-looking face. -prath m. a blow in the face; speaking insolently face to face to one's elder or other person entitled to respect. -tamunᵘ adj. (f.-tamüñᵘ̈), black-faced, dark-faced, having a swarthy complexion. -tamañĕr or -tamañār m. blackness of the face, a swarthy complexion; the darkening of the face caused by another's disrespect, or by shame, sorrow, or the like, a woeful countenance. -trakurᵘ adj. (f.-trakᵘ̈rᵘ̈), hard-faced; possessing the terrifying cast of countenance acquired by often giving way to anger, or by giving frequent abuse, etc. -wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), one who has face; one who is universally respected. -wothᵘ adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), lean-faced, one whose face has become thin and disfigured by disease, etc.; one who, having once been polite, is become impudent before his elders. -vyoṭhᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat. -vĕchĕ), fat-faced, having a face too fat. -zālay f. face shivering; the sense of humiliation and shame felt before an elder or other person entitled to respect when one has been doing something wrong. ¶ buthi adv. in front, opposite, u.w. vbs. of going, putting, seeing, etc. --āmotᵘ -- adj. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), come into a person's presence, arrived in front; one who has replied rudely and with contrariety to a polite remark; see buthi yunᵘ bel. -buthi m. a form of lamentation amongst women, in which they slap their own faces and scratch them with their finger-nails. -chotᵘ adj. (f. -chüʦᵘ̈), white-faced, fair-complexioned; (of clothes, grain, or the like) outside white, esp. when black, dark-coloured, or dirty within. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to put in front; (in a fight) to place something in front of one's opponent; to put up a shield, etc. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take in front; (in an address or in instruction) to take some head of the subject of discourse and bring it forward; to take another person as a helper in order to put him in front face to face with the work. --lagun -- m.inf. to appear in front, take one's stand before an opponent; to take one's stand to contradict one's elders, etc., to reply in a discussion, or to give back abuse in a verbal quarrel. --logᵘ-motᵘ -- adj. (f. --lüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), ready to contradict one's elders, etc., to reply to an opponent in a discussion, or to give insolent abuse in a quarrel. -nonᵘ adj. (f. -nüñᵘ̈), i.q. buthⁱ-nonⁱ, ab., q.v. -pĕṭha tulun m.inf. to raise from the face; to abandon shame (as of a respectable man reduced to earn his food by begging); to become bold, impudent (of a person naturally mild-tempered). -pĕṭha wŏthun m.inf. to rise from the face; shamelessness to occur (as ab.). -pĕṭhukᵘ adj. (f. -pĕṭhücᵘ̈), of or belonging to (something) upon the face (Siv. 467). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall in front or on the face; (of something belonging to a class usually considered desirable) to be considered undesirable as soon as it comes within sight; (of meeting on the road a friend, to visit whom one is making a journey) to suddenly come into sight. --thawun --m.inf. to place something before another; to offer reverently, to present a gift (from an inferior to a superior); to offer a sample or specimen of anything. --wasun -- m.inf. to descend in the face; the face to become shrunken, reduced, drawn, or thin. -wāv m. a contrary wind (Gr.M.). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come into a person's presence, to arrive in front; to give a rude reply, face to face, to an elder or person entitled to respect, to reply impudently. -zyūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat. -zēchĕ), long-faced. ¶ buthis-pĕṭh adv. on the face; before a person's face, in his presence (K.Pr. 96, wrongly written buṭhis). ¶ buthyukᵘ adj. (f. buthicᵘ̈), of or belonging to the face of any person, or surface of any thing.

f. (sg. dat. and pl. nom. bachĕ, which, e.g. Śiv. 1450, is often written bacha), a hearth, the level surface beside a kitchen fire-place on which vessels are put when taken off the fire, a hob (K.Pr. 7, 23, 163, bachhih); dārĕ bacha tröwith, having abandoned door and hearth, i.q. leaving house and home (Śiv. 1450). El. spells this word baṭh. --raṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to seize the hearth; (of some hitherto untasted food or medicine) to be suitable on account of its wholesomeness; (of a child, servant, or the like) to be suitable, to fit into one's life, owing to affection. ¶ bachi bahā dyunᵘ m.inf. to steam at the hearth; a kind of medical treatment for rheumatism of, or boils on, the leg, consisting in laying the limb on the hearth of a lighted fire in order to promote perspiration. -bŏkutᵘ m. (f. -bŏküʦᵘ̈), a kitchen cub, a greedy child always hanging about the kitchen. -brôrᵘ m. (f. -brörᵘ̈), a kitchen cat, a greedy child, esp. (f.) a greedy girl, always hanging about the kitchen. -kŏkorᵘ adj. (f. -kŏkürᵘ̈), a kitchen cock, id., but esp. (m.) of a boy. -kuʦürᵘ̈ f. a kitchen whelp, id. (of a girl).

m. N. of a sacred place in Kashmīr, near Mount Haramukh. It is passed by pilgrims on their way back from the sacred lakes of Ganga-bal, etc. It is the ancient Bhūtēśvara. See RT.Tr. i, 107; v, 55; and II, 407.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. būtīmārĕñ), i.q. būtalad, q.v.
m. (father of wailing), the heron or bittern.
f. a certain vegetable creeper which usually grows wild in the jungle; a collection of its leaves; its flower.
(K.Pr. 243), incorr. for buthisᵘ̈y, sg. dat. of buthᵘ 2, with emph. y.
f. N. of a certain nāga, or sacred spring, near Khŏnᵃmuh, and visited on the pilgrimage to the shrine of Harṣēśvara (RT.Tr. II, 459; Śiv. 930, cf. 932).
or, i.q. bŏz, q.v., but chiefly used in proper names; dashĕ-buz, the ten-armed, a N. of Śiva (Śiv. 521, 1688).
m. a snake, a serpent (Skr. bhujaga). Its gen. sing. is buzagunᵘ (K.Pr. 122) (?).

m. burning, scorching (of garments, cloth, etc.). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be burnt or scorched as above; also of the human body (esp. the belly or other part of the trunk) being burnt or scorched. --karun -- m.inf. to burn or scorch garments, clothes, or another's body.
or bōzan m. cooked food, victuals, a dish of food, meal (Śiv. 108, 1042, 1071, 1084); a feast (El., who spells the word bōzan). --karun -- m.inf. to eat, partake of food, make a meal.
m. complete disappearance (as of the simultaneous disappearance of all the company assembled in a room, or of all the contents of a pile of any articles).
m. a certain dish, the fruit of the egg-plant roasted and served with curds.

f. the wages paid for roasting or parching (grain, etc.); the small profit made by buying something and simultaneously selling it to someone else, a kind of brokerage; the commission or 'dustoorie' taken by servants. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to draw or take such commission or 'dustoorie' (lit. to deduct it from the money given for the purchase).
adj. c.g. timid, faint-hearted, a coward (Gr.M., El.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. buzᵘ, 2 p.p. buzōv), to parch or roast (esp. grain or meat over heated sand); to roast (L. 463; K.Pr. 168, buzāyih for buzāyĕ, 2 p.p. f.), to bake, cook (K.Pr. 38), fry (El. apparently, in the last sense, by confusion with bazun). buzᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. buzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), roasted, parched, as ab.

or buzy adj. c.g. a sec. suff. meaning 'dependent on', as in ạṭhᵃri-buzᵃ, dependent on the wool-worm (ạṭhᵘ̈rᵘ̈), liable to be attacked by the wool-worm; lūka-buzⁱ, dependent on people (lūkh), belonging to other people; kŏlayi-buzⁱ, dependent on a wife (kŏlay), having only one relation--a wife; ʦūra-buzⁱ, dependent on a thief (ʦūr), liable to theft (Gr.Gr. 161). -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a wretched son of dependence; one who, owing to powerlessness of voice, weakness of body, feebleness of action, want of money, or the like, takes refuge with and makes himself subject to someone who has plenty of these qualities; miserable, wretched.
f. of buthᵘ 2, at the end of an adjectival compound. Cf. bāka-buthᵘ, under bākh.

byēkh (H. viii, 1), or bēkh (H. viii, 1; xii, 4) pron. adj., c.g. [cf. Gr.Gr. 52; declined as follows: sg. dat., c.g. biyis; ag.m. biyⁱ, f. biyi; abl. biyi or (Gr.Gr. 94, 153) biyĕ; gen. an. (rarely inan.) biyⁱ-sondⁱ or bĕy-sondᵘ (f. -sünzᵘ̈), inan. (rarely an.) bĕyukᵘ (f. bĕyücᵘ̈); pl. nom. m. biy or biyⁱ, f. biyĕ or (c.g.) bĕyĕ; dat. c.g. biyĕn; ag. and abl. biyau; gen. biyĕn-hondᵘ (f. -hünzᵘ̈)], another, other, different (Śiv. 618; K.Pr. 242, sg. dat. written bĕyih); the other (Śiv. 1441); another one (pl. some), more, additional (Gr.M.). W. (34) spells this word bėyāk and (137) beyāk. -trākh pron., indef. adj., c.g. (sg. dat. biyis-triyis, and so on, like byākh), anyone else, someone else. byākhᵘ̈y adj. (declined as above with y added), altogether different; met. different from everything else, unsurpassed, beyond comprehension (K.Pr. 60). ¶ This word byākh is really an irregular compound of bi (q.v.) and akh, one. The obl. cases are those of bi, without akh, to which the emph. particle y has been added.
m. one who makes his living by interest, a money-lender, usurer.

m. (biol of L. 463; sg. dat. byölis (Śiv. 929) or bēlis; ag. byölⁱ or bēlⁱ; abl. byāli or bēli, and so on), seed-grain, seed (K.Pr. 187, 193; Śiv. 928, 1110, 1530, 1678; Rām. 617, 826, 1504, 1512); semen; insect eggs, fish-roes (owing to their resemblance to minute seeds). -kukᵘ m. the cuckoo, so called from its cry being heard at seed-time, in spring (El.). ¶ bēlⁱ-basta f. a seed-bundle, the bag or membrane containing eggs, in the case of certain insects; similar collections of granulations in disease. -dāñĕ m. seed-paddy, seed of the rice-plant reserved for sowing. -ḍūrᵘ m. lit. a seed-bed; hence, the amount of paddy-seed required for sowing the plot of ground used as a seed nursery. -düjᵘ̈ f. lit. a seed-field; a plot of unirrigated land in which spring crop (barley, wheat, etc.) or an autumn crop (mung, etc.) have been sown broadcast, and before the seeds have sprouted. -gö̆ʦᵘ̈ or byölⁱ-gŏ̈ʦⁱ f., lit. a seed-berry, a collection of seeds, etc., as e.g. the bag of eggs of certain insects, the seed-pod of a plant containing many minute seeds, the roe of a fish. -lyolᵘ or byölⁱ-lyolⁱ m. a jar in which seed-grain is soaked before sowing (see the next); met. a hole or pit packed tightly with a large number of articles. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ or byölⁱ-mŏ̈nḍⁱ f. (sg. dat. -mŏnjĕ), the root of a kind of pot-herb (? a kind of cabbage) which is planted again, and from the sprouts issuing from which seeds are propagated. -tọ̆mᵃl or byölⁱ-tọ̆mⁱl m. a certain kind of rice. Before sowing, seed-paddy is soaked in water till it begins to sprout. When the sowing is completed, any seed-grain that remains over is parched and pounded for food, and is called by this name. It is thus a kind of malted parched grain. Cf. the preceding, and byāli anun bel. -wahĕkh or byölⁱ-wahĕkh m. (sg. dat. -wahĕkas), 'sowing-Wahĕkh' (Skt. Vaiśākha), the month (April-May) in which paddy is sown. -wāph or byölⁱ-wāph m. (sg. dat. -wāpas), seed-sowing, esp. the season for sowing paddy (commencing with the sun's entry into Taurus, and continuing for forty days until the sun's entry into Gemini). -wāpas-kyutᵘ adv. in the sowing-season (as ab.), u.w. vbs. of coming, going, being born, or the like. ¶ bēli khasun m.inf., lit. to ascend by seed; to arrange, or put in rows (like rice seedlings), to set a crowd of people in rows; to put (papers, etc.) in proper order (for reading or the like). Cf. bēli-wasun bel. --wasun -- m.inf., lit. to descend by seed; to bring or select, anything in rows, i.e. one by one in proper order. Cf. bēli khasun ab. ¶ byāli anun m.inf., lit. to bring for seed; hence, to prepare seed for sowing by soaking it in water so as to cause it, to sprout. Cf. bēlⁱ-tọ̆mⁱl ab. --bihun -- m.inf., lit. to sit by seed; (a field) to be fruitful, every single seed coming to maturity. --byūṭhᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --bīṭhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), (a field, etc.) in which not a single seed has failed, but in which each has come to maturity. --kaḍun -- m.inf., lit. to bring out by seed; to sow (a prepared field). --nērun -- m.inf., lit. to go out from seed, to be completely sown (of a field). --wọ̆thᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --wö̆ʦhᵘ̈ --), (of a field, etc.) specially fitted for being sown with seed owing to the fertile quality of its soil. --yunᵘ -- m.inf., lit. to come by seed; hence, (of a field) to have been sown, with the seed which has just commenced to sprout. See bēlⁱ-tọ̆mⁱl ab. ¶ byölⁱ-dã̄d m. a seed bull, a stud bull, a bull kept for breeding. -gö̆ʦᵘ̈ f., i.q. bēlⁱ-gŏ̈ʦⁱ ab. -lyolᵘ m., i.q. bēlⁱ-lyolⁱ ab. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f., i.q. bēlⁱ-mŏ̈nḍⁱ ab. -pholᵘ m. a small quantity of seeds (Gr.Gr. 164); the total quantity of seed from a single plant or flower; a single seed. -tọ̆mᵃl m., i.q. bĕlⁱ-tọ̆mⁱl ab. -wahĕkh m., i.q. bēlⁱ-wahĕkh ab. -wāph m., i.q. bēlⁱ-wāph ab.

or byunᵘ (e.g. H. vii, 3, 14) adj. [sometimes written byonnᵘ, with m. sg. dat. bĕnis or bĕnnis, ag. bĕnⁱ or bĕnnⁱ (Gr.Gr. 26); sg. f. nom. bë̆ñᵘ̈ ], apart, separate (Śiv. 1198); distinct from, other than; various; adv. separately (Śiv. 1427, bĕnnō, m.c. for byonᵘ, 1563). -byonᵘ adv. separately, apart, variously (Śiv. 843, 1203, 1579, 1775); often used almost as an adj. as in byonᵘ byonᵘ rāyĕ (f.pl.), different opinions (Gr.M.; so Śiv. 1134, 1755). -byonᵘ gaʦhun m.inf. to be torn, torn apart; (of clothes) to be torn through being worn out. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to separate, pull to pieces. -byonᵘ karun m.inf. to separate, open out. -lë̆jᵘ̈ f. cooking and eating apart from the other members of a commensal family. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to separate out, partition (joint family property, or the like). ¶ bĕnⁱ-pöṭhⁱ or -pöṭhin adv. separately, apart; apart, privately, secretly.
m. a cat (mostly vill.). The cross-bar joining the two upright posts of the wooden contrivance for drawing water from a well. Cf. brôrᵘ 1 and 2.
adj. (f.bë̆ʦᵘ̈), one who is (esp. by birth) of feeble and emaciated body, a weakling. Cf. byuʦᵘ̈.
m. (sg. dat. bicis), a scorpion. ¶ bicⁱ-zöʦⁱ adj. c.g. scorpion-natured, malignant, malicious, spiteful, maleficent. -ṭŏph f. (sg. dat. -ṭŏpi), the sting of a scorpion; met. a secret malignant act.

adj. (sg. dat. bīṭhis; f. sg. nom. bīṭhᵘ̈, dat. bēchĕ) (1 p.p. of bĕhun, to sit, q.v.), seated, sitting; settled, settled down, fallen in (as a roof, etc.); sitting idle unoccupied, idle (K.Pr. 33); (of land) fit for cultivation or once cultivated and now fallow, cf. bīṭhᵘ̈.
perf. part. (f. bīṭhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, sg. dat. bēchĕ-maʦĕ; perf. part. of bĕhun or bihun, q.v.), seated; idle, unemployed; settled, cleared (of a muddy liquid, etc.).
adj. (m. sg. dat. biyis; f. sg. nom. biyᵘ̈), (of cooked food) stale, allowed to get cold and hence tasteless, kept over-night or for longer so that it has dried up. Cf. biyun.
adj. (f. biʦᵘ̈), emaciated, feeble. Cf. byotᵘ.

or bạhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a kind of hawk or falcon, said to be strong enough to carry off even children; the royal white falcon (El.); the corresponding Hindī word is bahrī (also fem.), the Falco calidus. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the falling of a falcon; hence, to be destroyed suddenly, or (of a healthy man or beast) to be carried off by a sudden and violent illness.

burbatan, bᵃrbatañ, or burbatañ f. a certain toy, a disc (of stone, metal, or wood) with two holes passing through it, through each of which a string is passed. It is made to revolve by twisting the double string, the ends of which are held apart, one in each hand, etc.; these are then pulled against each other.
m. a rapidly repeated sound, a whirr, buzz, like the noise of a number of birds suddenly rising at once.

m. a kind of veiling dress worn by respectable women outside their houses. It is a long strip of cloth, concealing the whole of the face of the woman wearing it, except the eyes, and reaching to the feet. --bābañ -- f. a respectable woman accustomed to wear a bᵃrᵃka in public.
f. a woman who wears a bᵃrᵃka, q.v.; esp. a woman who deceitfully wears such to disguise herself, in order to give the impression that she does so habitually.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. bᵃrᵃkôwᵃ), to force violently into an orifice, e.g. a nail; obsc. (f.inf.), to violate, have violent intercourse with a woman.

or busar f. very hot water, scalding water (Rām. 1459); rain struck by lightning (supposed to be the boiling hot fire of God; in this sense often used in curses, 'may the fire of God burn you!'). Cf. rasᵃr and sᵃsar --pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. scalding water to fall; the pain caused by the fissures in the skin resulting from contact with scalding water, lightning, or burning coals, to arise; (of a tree) scathing, fissures in the bark of a tree, or burning, to result from contact with lightning. ¶ bᵃsari-dĕv m. a scald-devil, a vessel of water or fire-brazier so hot that it splits or otherwise burns the fingers that touch it. -dĕviñ f. a scald she-devil; a fire-brazier (kāngrī) too hot to touch without causing fissures in or otherwise burning the fingers that touch it. ¶ busari-wôñᵘ m. scalding water, esp. lightning water, rain which has been made scalding hot by lightning.
or busarilad adj. (as subst., f. bᵃsariladiñ), one whose skin is scalded or fissured by burning, one who is suffering generally from burns.

. The second consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character, the sixth when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the eighth when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It has the sound of ch in the English 'church'. ¶ Its aspirate is ch چھ, the seventh consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character. ¶ A c or ch occurring in a Sanskrit or Hindī word is very frequently changed respectively to ʦ or ʦh in Kāshmīrī, which are in Nāgarī commonly written and, and in Perso-Arabic چھ and چھھ. Thus, the Sanskrit candraḥ becomes Kāshmīrī ʦạndᵃr, and the Hindī chhōṭā becomes Kāshmīrī ʦhoṭᵘ. In fact, to Kāshmīrī ears, c is ʦ followed by y, and ch is ʦh followed by y. In other words, to a Kāshmīrī, c is really cy, and ch is really chy. It thus follows that many Kāshmīrīs, when writing their own language in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, put no dot under or, when these represent ʦ or ʦh respectively; but, on the contrary, represent c by and ch by. So strongly is the y-sound heard in these two letters by Kāshmīrīs, that ca is usually pronounced cĕ, and cha is usually pronounced chĕ, ya following a consonant being always sounded as ĕ or yĕ (see article ĕ). Thus, the word caras is usually pronounced cĕras, and the word chakun is usually pronounced chĕkun. In the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, each method of writing each of these two words is equally common. In the Perso-Arabic character (in which the short vowels are generally omitted) this question of spelling hardly arises. Similarly, the word cāra is quite commonly written cyāra, and chotᵘ is equally commonly written chyotᵘ. Again, the 1 p.p. of the verb chōrun should according to rule be chūrᵘ, but we also find it written chyūrᵘ, which is liable to confusion with another chyūrᵘ, the regular 1 p.p. of the verb chīrun, qq.v. ¶ Hence, if a word commencing with cĕ, cy, chĕ, or chy is not found in this Dictionary, it should be looked up under ca, c, cha, or ch, and vice versa respectively. Important words which have been noted as actually occurring in literature under both forms are as a rule given under both, with appropriate cross-references, each in alphabetical order; but it will be understood that it would be impossible to give every word commencing with c or ch twice over, in its two different spellings.
m. a father's brother, a paternal uncle. The word is mostly used in villages or by Musalmāns. -bāba a father's elder brother; also, a father's paternal uncle, a paternal granduncle.
m. spoiling a child by showing affection or praising it even when it is naughty. Cf. cibôlᵘ.
f. crying aloud from pain, groaning; groaning in a state of prolonged unconsciousness. Cf. cicrahāray, cicarāray, and chicharahāray.
m. the cone of a fir-tree (El.).

m. a well (El., YZ. 103, 214, 396, 406); a pit (natural or artificial) (Rām. 958, 1147). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. go to a pit; hence, to have one's life made a burden by another's abuse. -ĕ zanakhdān چاہ زنخدان m. the hollow (or pit) of the chin (YZ. 214). ¶ cāhas gaʦhun m.inf. to go into a pit; hence, to fall into or commit an unworthy action.
card. four. cahār-dah چہار دہ card. fourteen.
m. face, visage, countenance; (usually) a likeness, a portrait.

cāhy, or cāy (also spelt cyāhⁱ, cyāy), f. tea (K.Pr. 39, Gr.M.). According to El. two kinds of tea are sold in Kashmīr--Suratī and Sabz. Suratī tea is like English tea, and Sabz tea is brick tea imported via Ladāk and the Panjāb. There are two ways of preparing tea in Kashmīr. For mugal cāhⁱ, five cups of water are poured upon a tōlā of tea. It is then boiled for half an hour, when more cold water is added, along with condiments and sugar, after which it is boiled for half an hour more. Milk is then added. It is now ready for drinking. The colour is reddish. The second mode of preparing tea is called shīrⁱ cāhⁱ. The tea is placed in the teapot with a little soda and water and boiled for half an hour. Milk, salt, and butter are then added, after which it is boiled for another half-hour, when it is ready for drinking. According to K.Pr. (l.c.) the salt used in the infusion of tea is called phul. It is found in the Nubra valley in Ladāk, and contains the carbonate and sulphate of soda and a little of the chloride of sodium. cāhⁱ karüñᵘ̈, f.inf. to make tea (El.). ¶ cāhi-koshᵘ m. tea-leaves which have been infused, 'tea-leaves.' -nörᵘ̈ f. a teapot (with a spout like the English vessel), the vessel in which tea is placed after it has been made (El.). ¶ cāhyāh or cyāhyāh f. a cup of tea, tea (the infused liquid) (Śiv. 1824). This is cāhⁱ with suff. of indef. art., lit. 'a tea'.

or cötany, m. (sg. dat. caitanĕs or cötanĕs), consciousness, intelligence, sensation; meton. (Skt. cētana) an intelligent being, a being possessed of consciousness, animate, as opposed to zaḍa, inanimate matter (Śiv. 1525).
m. (for 2 see cakh 1 and 2), curds, curdled milk (dahī) from which the liquid portion, or whey, has been strained.
or cã̄kar (K.Pr. 42) m. a servant, esp. a house servant, a shampooer servant, or the like.
m. a kind of Government tenant, an official who has obtained waste land on privileged terms (L. 414, 426). Cf. cakh 1.
m. (sg. dat. cakas), a plot of land (usually hitherto uncultivated) let for a fixed rent by Government; turf-clods (L. 464).

(also spelt cyākh) m. (sg. dat. cākas), a tear or rent (of cloth, leather, or the like), cf. cōkh 2; a crack (El.); as adj. broken, torn (El.); a splitting (of a rock, etc.) (Rām. 1197, 1694); met. of the heart being broken (Rām. 237, 771, 1503). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to tear, to rend (e.g. the clothes in grief, etc.) (YZ. 19, 440; Rām. 119, 266, 283, 1537). --gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. tearing to occur, to be torn; to be split (with dat. of subject, YZ. 130). --karun -- m.inf., i.q. cākh dyunᵘ ab. (YZ. 536, Śiv. 828, Rām. 156, 441, 444, 874, 1305). ¶ cāka-wüṭᵘ̈ f. a slit or slash made on each side of the lower part of a garment. -wacĕ diñĕ f.pl. inf. to give such slits, hence to slash or tear a garment from the neck to lower end.

m. enmity, opposition, strife, altercation, tumult, wrangling. -cakh چخ چخ m. babble, prating; scolding over and over again, a good continued scolding, esp. when administered to children or the like. ¶ caka-bokᵘ m. the confused noise of a number of people talking at once, a hubbub. -cakh f. the confused noise made by a number of people (esp. children) talking or abusing each other at the same time, an angry hubbub. Cf. cikra-bākar.
adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. cākas), active, alert; dexterous; sound, healthy, hale, hearty, in good spirits.

m. in cākh-bākh m. loud lamentations, cries of grief, sorrow, or pain. Cf. cikh-bākh, under cikh. -bākh dyunᵘ m.inf. to make a complaint with loud lamentations (esp. of a complaint or call for justice to an official).
(cf. چخے) m. driving away with abuse (e.g. a dog out of a kitchen). --karun -- m.inf. to drive away with abuse, as ab.
f. a kind of dagger (worn concealed on the waist).

m. a kind of charcoal used for fireworks. It is made by burning certain kinds of bark, and collecting the extinguished sparks. Children wrap it up in cloth, and swing it about after setting it on fire. Cf. Hindī cakacaundh.
(K.Pr. 55), incorrect for Hindōstānī ciknā, smooth, shining, cheerful.
m. a kind of leather stocking worn in snowy places, snow-boots.

m. a tract of country divided into village-areas, a group of villages (H. ix, 10). cakladār (= Hindōstānī چکلے دار) m. a subordinate revenue official or speculating contractor for small areas of land (L. 403, 421).
adj. c.g. sharp, quick, intelligent (esp. of a boy or girl).
(?), a certain kind of boat used by people of high rank in Kashmīr (L. 382, ʦāka-wörᵘ̈,).

f. longing, desire, urgent wish (for anything or to do anything). --aʦüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. longing to enter, to expect to get something again and again because one has already once got it easily; to be in the habit of doing anything, to do a thing easily from long practice. ¶ caki-khōr m. an eater of longing; hence, one who does a thing easily from long practice, an old servant (K.Pr. 39).

m. a sudden or unexpected happening of any conduct (such as giving and repaying, buying and selling, or the like). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. something unpleasant to happen unexpectedly (such as the arrival of an enemy, or the inconvenient demand for the repayment of a debt).
f. (sg.dat. cāli 1), beauty of form (of anything animate or inanimate) (K.Pr. 71, of a horse; so W. 139).

or cyāl f. (sg. dat. cāli 2 or cyāli), rule, practice, course, procedure, method, mode, manner; conduct, behaviour, character (Gr.M., K.Pr. 156); with suff. of indef. art., cālāh, a mode of life (Śiv. 818).
c.g. one who is good at urging others to work (with his voice only, and not by example).
adj. c.g. active, alert, nimble; expert, dexterous; clever, ingenious; vigilant; artful, cunning. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain vigilant, to keep vigilant (Rām. 1321).
m. an invoice or waybill, bill of lading, letter of advice (H. viii, 10).
(also spelt cĕmakāwun), conj. 1 (1 p.p. camakāwôwᵘ), to cause to shine, to make brilliant, polish (Śiv. 1660).
f. (sg. dat. camaki), glitter, brilliance, splendour; flash; gleam. Cf. Gr.Gr. 125.
adj. c.g. moving gracefully, swaying coquettishly; hence, stately, pompous.

(also spelt cĕmakun) conj. 3 (2 p.p. camakyōv), to shine, beam, glow, glitter, sparkle, glisten (Śiv. 1703); to shine, be pre-eminent (in character, etc., of human beings); to be prosperous, have a bright outlook, (of trade or the like), to revive (Gr.M.).
m. lit. a low caste leather-worker, but used to mean any vile person, a vile sinner, one whose conduct is sinful and vile.
f. conduct such as that of a vile sinner (see camār), a habit of causing sorrow or trouble to others.
m. conduct such as that of a vile sinner (see camār), esp. when such is performed by a person usually well-conducted.
m. Jasminum grandiflorum, J. officinale, and J. revolutum (El.).
m. a glittering leaf of metal suspended from jewellery worn on the forehead, etc., a spangle.
m. onomat. the sound made by a slap of the open hand on the shoulder or similar flat part of the body. -cañ m. onomat. a howl, such as that made by a dog when beaten.

m. the chick-pea, Cicer arietinum, commonly called 'gram' (El.). -cambēl f. anything to be eaten in grains, such as mixed peas, pulses, and the like, parched together and eaten dry. -phȧlⁱ pöthᵃr m. lit. the manner of pea-grains; hence, a condition of temporary, loose friendship, quickly made and quickly dissolved.

f. an unruly woman, a vixen, a slattern; a woman of bad character who will not obey the ordinary decencies of life. ¶ canḍa-bāpār m. habitual action such as that of an unruly woman or slattern. -müʦᵘ̈ f. a mad slattern, a woman who is such a vixen or slattern that she is as good as insane.

(also spelt cĕnda) m. a pocket (in a garment) (K.Pr. 4, 8, 18, 25, 43, 189, 201, 253; W. 135; Śiv. 1201); a purse (El.). -golᵘ m. the opening of a pocket. -gŏʦᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the bag part of a pocket, which holds the articles put into it. -ʦūr m. a pickpocket, one who steals from pockets. -ʦūrⁱ f. pocket-picking (El.).
m. (f. canḍöjᵘ̈), a man of a degraded tribe, such as a leather-worker or other low caste.
f. the actions of a canḍāl; hence (of a man of higher caste), cruel, vile, despicable, or sinful conduct.

m. a claw (of a wild beast), talon (of a bird). --yunᵘ m.inf. a claw to come (i.e. falling into someone's claw); hence, distress to arrive (esp. some causeless distress to arise through the action of a king or the like which can only be avoided or removed at great cost), tyranny to be experienced. canga-tala nērun m.inf. to issue from under the claw, to escape clear from tyranny or distress.
m. a certain musical instrument, a kind of Jew's harp (L. 307); N. of a sept in Kashmīr, whose ancestor is said to have played this instrument (L. 307).
m. N. of a village famous for its singing- and dancing-girls (El.).
m. (apparently a jingle of phanj, cf. Persian فند falsehood; see phand), statements partly true and partly false (e.g. in flattery or the like).
m. extreme haste or speed (in the performance of any action or business). Cf. capᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 1 and cār 1.
m. excessive talkativeness, vain talking (esp. when untruthful); cf. car. --karun -- m.inf. to prate excessively, use vain talking (esp. when the talking is reprehensible).
adj. c.g. one who is in the habit of using excessive talking (esp. when vain talking).
f. (sg. dat. capöʦᵘ̈), a slap with the palm of the hand, esp. on the cheek (K.Pr. 74, 156; Śiv. 873). --lāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to slap a person on the cheek; met. to swindle another out of property.
adj. c.g. quadrangular and, at the same time, long; plank-shaped.
m. the entire destruction of a living being, utter destruction.

f. (sg. dat. cã̄pi), pressing, squeezing, used in the following: cã̄pa cārañĕ f. pl. inf. to put to a certain form of torture, in which wedges of wood are placed between the fingers, which are then tightly bound together. Cf. capᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 2.
m. onomat., used in the following: capa-caph f. (Gr.Gr. 75), or caph-caph m. onomat. (sg. dat. -capas), the ugly sound made in greedily eating, as if one were a hungry dog.

f. (sg. dat. capi), false tale-bearing, slandering (esp. of a servant to his master against a fellow-servant); cf. چپ دادن to deceive. --khë̆nᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to tell false tales of, inform against, as ab. ¶ capa gaʦhun m.inf. (of an overseer or the like) to show habitual disfavour to one person or set of people and at the same time to show habitual favour to another person or set of people.

f. a necklace worn by women, composed of little ornaments in the form of the bud of the campā flower (Hindī, campā-kalī). ¶ caphkali-hoṭᵘ m. a throat adorned by wearing such a necklace. -hoʦᵘ m. a die for stamping the campā-bud beads of such a necklace. -pholᵘ m. a single campā-bud bead of such a necklace. -pōsh m. the gold setting (like a flower) in which the campā-bud beads of such a necklace are set. -roshᵘ m. a long, thick variety of the above necklace.
(= Hindōstānī چپلی) f. a slipper, a sandal (cf. L. 69).
m. a badge as a mark of office worn by official messengers or peons (usually upon the belt or head-dress).
m. one who wears a capᵃrās or badge, a peon, orderly, messenger of a court (L. 450).
f. haste, agitation, flurry; cf. capacār and cār 1. capᵃrĕ ganḍañĕ f. pl. inf. to harass or afflict a person so as to induce him to perform quickly some action (e.g. to repay a debt).
f. the wedge placed between the fingers and used in the torture called cã̄pa cārañĕ. See cã̄ph.

m. excessive talking, esp. self-conceited talk, bragging, as e.g. when a man who is not able to accomplish more than a very little, brags about his ability to accomplish something difficult, and does nothing but talk, without making a real attempt; cf. cāpar, carcar, and caral. --karun -- m.inf. to stand by and prate advice as ab.
in cār-dah, for cahār-dah (q.v.), card. fourteen (Rām. 1083).
m. quickness, speed; cf. capacār and capᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 1. ¶ cāra-cār f. extreme haste or speed in the performance of any work.

m. drawing tight; bracing; tying tightly (Gr.Gr. 124), fastening, strapping, binding; pressing upon, bearing hard upon, oppression; wringing, squeezing (cf. atha-cār under atha and cã̄pa cārañĕ under cã̄ph). --aʦun -- m.inf. squeezing to enter; harassment or urgent pressing of a person to occur in order to induce him to do something or to make him repay a debt, pay a tax, and so on; squeezing to extort payment to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to urge or harass a person to do something quickly; as ab., to squeeze for payment. Cf. capᵃri ganḍañĕ under capᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 1. --ʦānun -- m.inf. id. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. squeezing to come; oppression from violence, esp. violence to induce a person to do anything, to occur.

or cyāra چارہ m. a device, stratagem, artifice; a means of success; redress, help, resource (Śiv. 11, 69, 129, 152, 429, 1473, 1581, 1582, 1897; Rām. 264, 333, 385, etc.). -sāz m. a helper, protector (Rām. 70). -sözī f. helping, giving protection (Rām. 361).
(K.Pr. 204), cĕrāg (K.Pr. 161), cirāg (K.Pr. 189) چراغ m. a lamp, a light.
m. (sg. dat. carakhas), a wheel; hence, an instrument, machine (Gr.M.) (a variant of carkh).
adj. c.g. one who is accustomed to brag about the great things he can do, but who really can do nothing, and who only talks without giving active help. Cf. car.
m. a foot like a lotus, a foot-lotus; a polite or reverential name for a superior's or deity's foot. Borrowed from Sanskrit caraṇāravinda (Śiv. 1035).
f. a woman who after maturity resides in her father's house, and owing to her being free from control waxes fat and wanton.

m. (sg. abl. carḅa 1), fat, grease, suet, tallow (Rām. 839). ¶ carbā-bagaira (?) m. a dish composed of suet and vegetables (El.). Cf. bagôrᵘ. -ʦṻnṭh f. (sg. dat. -ʦṻnṭi), an apple of fat; hence, a plump (esp. a fat and stupid) woman. ¶ carbas tal wölinj gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. the heart to go (concealed) under the suet; hence, to show a brave face in the presence of a cause for fear.
adj. c.g. (for 1 see carb), fat, stout, plump.

f. fat, grease, suet, tallow. --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring fat; hence, self-confidence or presumption to arise in one (esp. in one who has suffered defeat and subsequently obtained assistance and materials).
m. discussion, encomium, esp. of some absent person's actions or affairs; coming into fashion, great appreciation (e.g. of something for sale which has a great many would-be purchasers).

m. in the following: carcar karun m.inf. to prate, chatter, so as to distract the attention of another from his work. Cf. car. --lāgun -- m.inf. to keep making a noise that distracts the attention of another (of children and the like).
in the following: cārcār-goyᵘ adj. (f. -güyᵘ̈), one who by nature is a prater or talker of nonsense.
m. the condition of one who habitually uses improper or unfit language; muteness, idiocy.
(? spelling), in cari-hākh, m. (L. 72) (sg. dat. -hākas), a certain warm potherb, Campanula sp.
(L. 157, charri gad), ? incorr. for chiryuvᵘ, q.v.

m. (sg. dat. carkas), turning or whirling round, esp. of some wheel-shaped object; a wheel (El.). Cf. carakh. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to walk round and round anything, esp. with one's face towards it (YZ. 247). --phērun -- m.inf. the revolution to go round; in buying and selling in the market, business to be set in motion, esp. of some traffic which had been stopped or suspended. ¶ carka phērun m.inf. to go round by a wheel, hence, circumambulation round a sacred object or temple, keeping it on the right hand (Rām. 88); to find one's brains whirling; giddiness, staggering, reeling to occur; to ride a horse in circles, to cause a horse to curvet (Rām. 1333, 1339). --phirun -- m.inf. to cause another to circumambulate, as ab., or to cause him closely to walk round oneself or another. ¶ carkas khasun m.inf. to mount the whirling; hence, to be so entangled or involved in an action or business that one can neither abandon it nor take it up, esp. when this is due to emulation or competition. The Sanskrit cakravāṭa.
f. an instrument (e.g. a peg held in a potter's hand) for causing a wheel to revolve.
adj. c.g. one who is a great talker, inopportunely and without rhyme or reason. Cf. car.
f. a charpoy, bedstead, bed (H. x, 5).

or caras (also written cĕrs and cĕras) m. 'charas', the pollen of the Indian hemp or bhang, an intoxicating drug when smoked (K.Pr. 54, Śiv. 1182, L. 67). Cf. curu. ¶ carsa-biṭh f. a company of charas-smokers. -büṭhᵘ̈ f. a place to which people resort for smoking charas. -shōda m. one who is a slave to the habit of smoking charas, a charas-sot. -wān m. a charas- shop. -yār m. a boon companion in charas-smoking.
