m. (sg. dat. cārsōyĕs چارسویس), a cross road; a market (YZ. 202).

(also written cyārun) conj. 1 (1 p.p. côrᵘ 1; f. cörᵘ̈ 1; for 3 see s.v.), to oppress, harass, worry, or dun a person in order to induce him to pay a debt, a fine, or tax. Probably the same as cārun 2.

(also written cyārun) conj. 1 (1 p.p. côrᵘ 2; f. cörᵘ̈ 2; for 3 see s.v.), to tie up tightly, draw tight, strap up; to press upon, bear hard upon; to enter in a ledger or register (Śiv. 1912) (perhaps, in this meaning, another word, cf. Hindōstānī caṛhānā). Cf. cārun 1.
m. a quadruped, esp. a cow, bull, or the like.

f. the name of the fry of a certain fish, or of a certain small fish, usually found in holes in mountain streams. The cạsh proper has a pointed head, small mouth, dark back, silver belly, and firm scales (L. 158).
m. the eye (El.; YZ. 12, 417; Rām. 59, 516, 523, etc.; in YZ. 144 the word is written cashma).
m. a spring, source, fountain (YZ. 205). --shöhī شاھی-- or --söhibī صآحبی-- m. N. of a fountain on the northern shore of the Śrīnagar city lake. Its waters are considered to be very delicious (El.).
m. the middle hour between sunrise and the meridian; the meal eaten at that hour, breakfast, luncheon (El.). i.q. kôjᵘ, q.v.
c.g. or caṭulᵘ (f. caṭᵘ̈jᵘ̈) adj. one who habitually tells false and invented stories, a liar, an untruthful flatterer. Cf. caṭh.
m. praising one person to another, eulogy, commendation.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. catôwᵘ), to praise one person to another (esp. when the praise is deserved), to eulogize, commend.

m. (sg. dat. caṭas), a statement or piece of news mixed up with false additions invented by the teller, a partly untrue story, an exaggerated statement, a lie that is partly the truth, a false rumour; cf. caṭal and caṭūrᵘ̈. -bāz adj. c.g. one who, either maliciously or in order to give pleasure, is accustomed to tell invented stories or spread false rumours. --karun -- m.inf. to make a falsehood; hence, to cause great damage (e.g. by undoing an action, or by causing loss of money). --lāyun -- m. to spread abroad false reports likely to create disturbances or other breaches of the peace.
m. (sg. dat. cāṭas), eating, devouring, in the following: cāṭh kaḍun m.inf. to be worn out very quickly (of clothes taken into wear and the like).
f. in the following: caṭōrĕ ʦaṭañĕ f. pl. inf. idly, or for one's own or other's amusement, at a time of peace to spread abroad news, esp. false news, of disturbances, riots, and the like.

f. a sum of money paid as a punishment, a fine (El.). --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take (i.e. inflict) a fine. ¶ caṭi lagun m.inf. to become subject or liable to a fine; esp. to be fined for, or charged with, another's fault.
(L. 271), the term used by Kāshmīrī Musalmāns for the fourth day after a man's death, on which day a feast is given at the deceased's house.
m. a kind of litter or sedan in which women are carried.
or cō̃kharun conj. 3 (2 p.p. caũkharyōv), to shrivel up, become withered, as the hands or feet from excessive cold, or some delicate flower from extreme heat.
f. (sg. dat. caundani), a kind of altar (K. 923).
m. eager desire, longing (K.Pr. 247), esp. to complete or carry out some work. Cf. barun 1 (YZ. 31, Rām. 747, 752).
m. a kind of loose vest or shirt resembling the qabā, but having buttons instead of strings at the neck and navel and between the two; = the Persian pairahan.
adj. c.g. one who owing to his careless nature speaks a great deal without heed to his words, mixing them up, and thus talking nonsense as if he were a lunatic; a blundering gabbler.

or cyāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. côwᵘ or cyôwᵘ), to cause to drink, give to drink (K.Pr. 64; YZ. 268, 411, 506, 527; Śiv. 15, 179, 195, 970, 1006, 1017, etc.; Rām. 427, 1174, 1395, 1522); met. to cause a person to drink (information), to slander one person to another, to inform; to irrigate (a garden) (YZ. 254). (Caus. of cyonᵘ, q.v.; another form of the caus. is cāwanā- wun. In the printed edition of YZ. this verb is incorr. spelt chāwun.) côwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. cöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ 1, for 2 see s.v.), caused to drink, one to whom drink has been given and who has drunk, (of cattle) watered; met. caused to drink (information), hence one to whom slander is told, one who is informed against another. cöwith thawun m.inf. having made to drink to put; met. to tell tales about one person to another so as to cause them to sink into his mind, to slander one person to another.
or cyāwüñᵘ̈ conj. 1 (past tenses only used in f., 1 p.p. cöwᵘ̈), to milk a cow (K.Pr. 87, cāway, I shall milk for thee; Śiv. 1368, 1837).
f. tea, i.q. cāhⁱ, q.v. cāyĕ-nörᵘ̈ f. a teapot.
or cērun conj. 1 to mount (e.g. a horse) (noted only in L.V. 14, 15).
m. a pupil, disciple, follower; esp. one of the disciples or followers in a Hindū monastery, whose duty it is to carry on the traditions and perform the ritual laid down by the founder.
m. (for gender see Gr.Gr. 120), a drink, a beverage (Sanskrit pānam in Kashmīra-śabdâmṛta, IX, ii, 41), esp. a beverage fit to be drunk in large quantities, a large draught.
m. impers. fut. part. of cyonᵘ, that which is to be drunk, bibendum (Gr.Gr. 111); hence, any potable beverage.
f. a kind of sewing, tacking two pieces of cloth together. Cf. cūrⁱ.

m. (sg. dat. cĕtas), thought (Gr.Gr. 25), perception, consciousness, wits; vigilance, caution; memory, recollection, remembrance. --thawun 1 -- m.inf. (for 2 see cyonᵘ), to impress (a story or subject) upon one's mind; to store accurately in one's memory. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to thoroughly master (a branch of learning, a story, or the like).
m. a subscription, collection, assessment for a joint purpose.

f. wages for drinking (Gr.Gr. 129); hence --˚, a present customarily given to a young wife by her father-in-law when he pays a visit to her husband's house and she offers him a ceremonial spiced drink.
n.ag. (f. cĕwawüñᵘ̈), one who is drinking, a drinker, esp. one who is accustomed to drink (Śiv. 1759); for the form see Gr.Gr. 105.
she was drunk, or they (f.) were drunk; see cyonᵘ.
m. a kind of toy, a child's rattle. Cf. chã̄ṭun.
see chakun. chã̄cyov, see chã̄ṭun. chicyōv, see chĕkun 2.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. choḍᵘ, f. chüḍᵘ̈, f.pl. chajĕ; 2 p.p. chajyōv), to release, let go, dismiss (e.g. a man or beast from confinement or from work in which he or it is engaged). choḍᵘ-motᵘ (f.sg. chüḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, pl. chajĕ-maʦa), perf. part. released, etc.

or chĕg f. sudden dispersal, rout, as when a crowd is suddenly attacked and scatters, or when a flock of birds rises and flies away on the approach of a human being (Śiv. 1860). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to scatter, disperse, drive away, as ab. --lāgüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be dispersed, scattered, driven away, routed, as ab. --ʦānüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause an assembly or a flock to suddenly scatter, as ab.
f. hurry, flurry in doing anything (so as to get it done before anyone comes or something happens).
in the following: --baṭañ -- f. a shameless brāhmaṇ woman; a woman of good caste who goes about openly in public and has no sense of modesty; an unchaste woman of good family. Cf. chōra.
m. a winnowing basket, a winnowing fan.
m. the crest of a bird.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. chakanôwᵘ), to cause to scatter (Gr.Gr. 174), see chakun.

m. the act of scattering about in all directions. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give scattering; to be scattered about in all directions; to become spread on all sides (e.g. of a flood, a conflagration, or an epidemic).

f. (sg. dat. chaki), the spreading abroad of anything usually collected in piles or heap, e.g. dust or grain; esp. the scattering abroad of seed-grain, sowing seed broadcast. Cf. chakun, atha-chakh, s.v. atha, and Gr.Gr. 125. chakh diñᵘ̈ f.inf. to sow broadcast.

or chĕkun 1 conj. 1 (1 p.p. chokᵘ; 2 p.p. chacyōv; imperat. sg. 2 chĕkh, Śiv. 1776), to scatter abroad things usually together in large numbers, to scatter, throw about (K.Pr. 117; YZ. 163; Śiv. 732, 1079, 1092, 1149, 1400, 1401, 1497, 1861; Rām. 109, 440, 778, etc.); esp. to scatter seeds, to sow broadcast. El. spells this chhikun, i.e. chĕkun 1 and 2. The causal of this verb is chakanāwun or chạkᵃranāwun; the regular causal form chạkᵃrun or chạkᵃrāwun is not used in the sense of a causal, but has the meaning of the primitive verb (Gr.Gr. 174). ¶ chakana yunᵘ m.inf. pass. to be scattered; esp. (of seeds, etc.) to be scattered abroad automatically, to be self-sown. ¶ chakith ʦhunun m.inf. to scatter abroad; esp. to throw out into the open, dust, sweepings, etc., collected in a basket. ¶ chokᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. chücᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), scattered abroad; sown broadcast.
f. a kind of song sung by women to the accompaniment of a drum and other instruments. The leader sings a phrase, which is sung in turn by the others.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. chạkᵃranôwᵃ), i.q. chakanāwun, causal of chakun (Gr.Gr. 174). See chakun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. chạkᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. chạkᵃrun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 174, 175). ¶ chạkᵃrāwana yunᵘ m. inf. pass., i.q. chạkᵃrana yunᵘ, see chạkᵃrun. ¶ chạkᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. chạkᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. chạkᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, see chạkᵃrun.
n.ag. (f. chȧkᵃrawüñᵃ), one who disperses or scatters.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. chạkᵒrᵒ), to scatter abroad, throw about things collected together, esp. of dust or of seeds scattered on the roadside or the like, and not on a field. Although in form the caus. of chakun (q.v.), this verb has not a causal signification (Gr.Gr. 174, 175). ¶ chạkᵃran-wôlᵃ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who scatters or disperses (El.). ¶ chạkᵃrana yunᵘ m. inf. pass. to be scattered about, thrown broadcast, thrown about (of dust, or of seeds scattered automatically, and self-sown, i.e. not sown on ground properly prepared beforehand). --āmotᵘ -- perf. part. pass. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), scattered, thrown about as ab. (of dust, seeds, etc.). ¶ chạkᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. chạkᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), scattered, thrown about (of seeds or the like improperly scattered on the roadside, etc., as ab.).

f. (sg. dat. chali). a bit, part, scrap, portion, fragment (Rām. 878); a crumb (Gr.M.). Frequently --˚ (Gr.Gr. 162), as in lācha-chal f. a wafer (Gr.M.). -dal m. quarrelling combined with mutual recriminations. Cf. chala-polᵘ bel. ¶ chala-bāgay f. division by partition or by breaking up into fragments. -chā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. fragment-hurry; hence, improperly to scatter about in all directions. -chā̃gᵃri adv., abl. of the preceding, (of the mind or intellect) scatteredly, in an agitated manner, distractedly. --chala karith trāwun -- m.inf. to break anything in pieces (Gr.M.). -polᵘ m. mutual recriminations and abuse, wordy warfare. -wŏgᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. causing a crowd to scatter and flee away in various directions, breaking up an assembly. ¶ chali chali gaʦhun m.inf. to be smashed, broken in pieces, to fall to pieces. --chali karun -- m.inf. to smash to pieces.

in the following: -chŏkh m. (sg. dat. -chŏkas), the washing of a great number of articles at one time, a 'washing'. ¶ chala-chŏkh f. (sg. dat. -chŏki), the act of washing, cleaning (esp. cotton clothes, see chalun). ¶ chalan-grāy f. a slight, hasty washing. -pôrutᵘ m. an opportunity or time for washing accumulated dirty clothes, 'washing-day.'
m. the dirty water left after washing anything (esp. after washing rice, etc., preparatory to cooking), washings.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. cholᵘ, f. chüjᵘ̈; 2 p.p. chajyōv), to wash, cleanse (K.Pr. 17, 40, 41, 43, 82, 112, 154; YZ. 232; Śiv. 1022, 1575; Rām. 622, 774, 1644, etc.). According to El., s.v., when cotton cloth is referred to chalun is used, but when the reference is to woollen cloth manḍun or manḍanāwun is the word employed. ¶ chȧlⁱ chȧlⁱ freq. part. washing frequently or continually; commonly used as adv. ¶ chalith chŏkith adv. (a jingling repetition of the conj. part. chalith), having completely washed. Cf. chala- chŏkh under chal 2. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. having washed to throw away; hence, (of friends who have become estranged) to wash one's hands of another person, entirely to abandon friendly intercourse. ¶ cholᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. chüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), washed, cleansed by washing (Rām. 786, clothes).

m. a mountain precipice (K.Pr. 227, Rām. 1014); a ravine, precipitous cleft (Śiv. 1627). ¶ chamba-ḍula gaʦhun m.inf. to fall over a precipice; hence, to die a sudden or untimely death. -tᵃlürᵃ f. a precipice-bee; hence, a passionate woman, ready to abuse on the slightest provocation. ¶ chambas gaʦhun m.inf. to go to a precipice; hence, to be plunged in bad company and sinful habits. -pĕṭh wasath f. living on a precipice; an insecure position, liability to destruction at any moment (e.g. a village built on a sandbank in the midst of a river). ¶ chȧmbⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to go over a precipice; hence, the sudden irresistible flood of water from a river or canal that has burst its banks.

m. a carpenter, a house carpenter (El., Śiv. 337, K.Pr. 41, 178, W. 140). His wife is chöñᵘ̈ 2, chāna-kŏlay or chāna-bāy. Of these the first is generally used as a kind of surname, added to the woman's proper name. Regarding the other two see below. As a title (e.g. Yēkar chān, Yēkar, the carpenter) the gen. of this word is chānunᵘ. ¶ chāna-bāy f. a carpenter's wife. The word is honorific, cf. chāna-kŏlay bel. -kijᵘ̈ or -kījᵘ̈ f. a carpenter's nail; the last and final nail put into a house by the builder, thus completing the work; met. in any work nearly completed the small amount remaining to be done. Kāshmīrī carpenters are constantly omitting a nail here or some work there in order that they may be recalled and get another job; this is called 'the carpenter's nail' (K.Pr. 41). -kŏlay f. a carpenter's wife. This word is non-honorific. Cf. chāna-bāy ab. and Gr.Gr. 34. -koṭᵘ m. a carpenter's son; met. a real carpenter's son, a good carpenter (Gr.Gr. 132). -ṭhas m. carpenter's bang, the noise made by a carpenter when he hits a piece of wood with the back of his adze. -ṭŏkh m. (sg. dat. -ṭŏkas), carpenter's hammering, the noise made by a carpenter when he hits an iron wedge or other similar article employed in splitting wood.
m. sifting; falling down (as powder leaking through the interstices of a sieve, of a basket, or ripe pollen from certain flower-clusters).

m. onomat. the noise made by a metal vessel or the like falling on the ground, clang, clatter; cf. chŏñ. -chakh m. onomat. (sg. dat. -chakas), clang and clatter; a kind of musical dance. The girls who dance wear bells and tinkling anklets which are sounded in time with the music and singing; cf. chŏñ-chŏkh under chŏñ. -chambᵘ̈rᵘ̈ m. a sudden and accidental death, as if it were caused by falling down a precipice. -chañ m. onomat. clash, chink, tinkle, the noise of metal to metal, e.g. of metal vessels knocking against each other, or of rings or bells on a bell-girdle.
f. wages paid for sifting flour, etc. Cf. chān 2.
f. wages paid to a carpenter. Cf. chān 1 (Gr.Gr. 142).
f. the act of sifting, esp. of flour or other similar minute powder.
f. the profession or craft of a carpenter (Gr.Gr. 143).

or chĕnun conj. 3 (2 p.p. chanyōv), to be strained, sifted; to fall from a mass (as grain falling through a hole in a basket), to dribble away; to exude (Śiv. 1008); (of a tree) to lose its leaves (Śiv. 1039, 1208); to waste away (Śiv. 1002); to be broken up into parts (of a ring of dancers, Śiv. 1010).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. chônᵘ, f. chöñᵘ̈; 2 p.p. chāñōv), to sift (Śiv. 1527); to strain, filter; to trim (Gr.Gr. xxii); to search minutely, investigate; to shake down fruit from a fruit-bearing tree. ¶ chônᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. chöñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), sifted; strained, filtered, examined, investigated; (of a fruit-tree) having had its fruit shaken down off the branches.
pl. nom. of chaph 1, 2, and 3, qq.v.
m. anything printed, such as a book, a patterned cloth, or a pattern generally.
adj. c.g. having a chip or splinter elevated from the surface, having a split point (as in a reed-pen).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. chapanôwᵘ), to cause some one to pass time, or to cause him to wait till a shower of rain is passed over (caus. of chapun 1, Gr.Gr. 174).
in chāpȧnⁱ küñᵘ̈, i.q. chā̃pȧnⁱ küñᵘ̈, see chā̃punᵘ.
m. a hut, a temporary shelter of straw and wood or the like.
f. (sg. dat. chapüʦᵘ̈), throwing away, scattering and abandoning; hence, putting up with, or making the best of, a work or a life full of pain and affliction.

f. in the following:-- -dag f. wasting time in the performance of any employer's work, by the workers pointing to each other as the proper person to do it; as when e.g. A says "it's B's work", and B says "it's C's work", and C says "it's A's work", so that in the end nothing is done. Cf. chāwan and chọ̆pᵃrāwan-dag under chọ̆pᵃrāwan.
f. (sg. dat. chã̄pi), an instrument for sealing or stamping, a seal, signet-ring; a stamp or impression made by a seal, etc., either in sealing-wax or in ink, etc.
or chĕph 1 f. (sing. dat. chapi), fine dressing, adornment, wearing jewels and rich garments. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to wear fine clothes, etc., to be expensively dressed.

or chĕph 2 f. (sg. dat. chapi, pl. nom. chapa), a sacrificial offering (cf. chapun 2). ¶ chapa-chörᵘ̈ f. sacrifice-haste, unexpectedly becoming a sacrifice in company with some one who is dying or suffering great calamity, unexpectedly sharing such a fate. ¶ chapi lagun m.inf. to offer oneself as a sacrifice instead of or on behalf of any one.

or chĕph 3 f. (sg. dat. chapi), a paring, chip, shaving, when cutting wood either with a hatchet, etc., or (e.g. a reed-pen) with a penknife; a gash or cut in shaving (L. 457 chēp). --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to raise up or elevate a splinter or shaving when cutting a stick; to put a point to a reed-pen, etc.
m. a splinter, a chip, as in pointing a stake or mending a reed-pen.
i.q. chā̃punᵘ, q.v. chā̃pȧlⁱ-küñⁱ, i.q. chā̃pȧnⁱ-küñⁱ, see chā̃punᵘ.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. chôpᵘ), to print (a book, cloth, or the like) (Gr.M.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. chopᵘ), to be hidden, concealed (Rām. 398, 978); to take shelter from heavy rain; generally, to take refuge with (K.Pr. 243), seek the patronage of any one; to endure patiently trouble or calamity in the hope of better times; to waste time, pass time unprofitably. The caus. of this verb is chapanāwun, chạpᵃrāwun, chọ̆pᵃrun 1, or chọ̆pᵃrāwun 1 (Gr.Gr. 174). ¶ chapan-jāy f. a place of shelter, a shelter under which a person waits for rain to pass over; generally, a place of refuge. -shāī f. a place of refuge (El.). chapani yunᵘ m.inf. to come for refuge, to take refuge with any one, to claim sanctuary (Rām. 475). ¶ chapith conj. part. used as adv. secretly, privately (Rām. 398, 978).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. chopᵘ), to cast into a river the remains of an offering to a deity, flowers left after a sacrificial ceremony, etc.
chāpun, or chā̃pulᵘ m. (sg. dat. chã̄panis), a sling (for casting stones, etc.) (K.Pr. 96). chā̃pȧnⁱ küñᵘ̈ f. the stone, or missile, of a sling.
or chạpᵃrāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. chạpᵒrᵒ or chạpᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. chapanāwun (Gr.Gr. 174).
f. a kind of large basket.
or chīrᵘ̈1 f. name of a certain disease, a crop of boils on the hands, feet, or back, impetigo contagiosa; also used of carbuncles.
f. a sprinkle of water, oil, ghī, or the like from the tips of the fingers, small in amount, and thrown to a distance. Cf. chir 1.
or chĕrā adv. alone, only (Śiv. 243, chĕrā).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. chorᵘ. This verb is impersonal in tenses formed from the past participles, as in K.Pr. 13, 200), to evacuate, go to stool (K.Pr. 17). chorᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. chhürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), dirtied by evacuations (e.g. a pan or commode).

or chĕta in the following (cf. chotᵘ):-- -chiran-hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -chiran-hishᵘ̈), lit. like white and yellow rice-milk, very white and clean-looking, esp. of something edible. -hôrᵘ adj. (f. -hörᵘ̈), marked or ornamented with a white pattern, esp. of a cloth or the like which has become dirty and dark-coloured, and then is given such a pattern to freshen it up. -lay f. spoiled by becoming white or being whitened (as a face by sickness or by foul air, or anything by being touched with white matter that comes off). -tᵃl m. the fruit of the white mulberry, white mulberry-fruit. -ṭyokᵘ adj. (m. sg. dat. -ṭĕkis; f. -ṭë˘cᵘ̈), having white spots on the skin, one who suffers from a leprosy that comes out in white spots.
m. a flock of sheep, etc., esp. such a flock led out for the season on to the hills for grazing.
adj. c.g. left to one side as unpleasing (of unsatisfactory things picked out of a pile and left uncared for, e.g. the bad fruit picked out of a basket of fruit and laid aside).
m. a certain weight, a chittack, the sixteenth part of a seer or 5 tōlās, approximately 2 ounces avoirdupois; anything which weighs a chittack.
m. (sg. dat. chaṭas), the weight or amount of the load of a beast of burden, such as a horse, ass, or camel.
m. (sg. dat. chatas), the thatch or roof of a house; a ceiling.

f. (sg. dat. chüʦᵘ̈ 2 or chë̆ʦᵘ̈2; for 1 see chotᵘ), injury, loss, harm, especially the loss or diminution of the original stuff incurred in the manufacture of vessels, ornaments, wooden furniture, or the like. --gāʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such loss of original material to occur. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take (advantage of) loss, to cause or get a person to work for nothing. --nakha wālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to repay loss, to work badly (of one who is compelled to work against his will). ¶ chüʦᵘ̈ (chë̆ʦᵘ̈)-pūtᵘ̈  m. a son of loss, a son born last of all in a large family (and hence unwelcome).
or chaturᵘ1 adj. (f. chatürᵘ̈ or chatᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 1), fair-complexioned, fair-skinned, fair-limbed, esp. of a child, and equivalent to 'beautiful'.

or chĕtun conj. 3 (2 p.p. chatyōv), to become white, to turn white (Siv. 1704); to be white; (of the eyes) to become white, to lose their sight (Rām. 1196). The caus. of this verb is chaʦᵃrun or chaʦᵃrāwun (Gr.Gr. 173, 175). ¶ chatyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. chatyē-müʦᵘ̈), become white, turned white, whitened.

conj. 1 (1p.p. chỗṭᵘ, pl. chö̃ṭⁱ; f. chö̃ṭᵘ̈, pl. chã̄cĕ; 2 p.p. chã̄cyōv), to pick, pick out, cull, select, sort; to discuss (rumour, news, etc.); to make public something which was known as a secret, esp. to disclose suddenly a secret anger, sorrow, or the like. chỗṭᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. chö̃ṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), picked out, selected; discussed (of news, rumour, etc.); disclosed (of anger, etc.).
m. (f. chatᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 2), a young fish, any tiny fish like a minnow or our whitebait. ¶ chatᵃrĕ f.pl. a flock or crowd of such small fish.
f. an umbrella, a parasol. Cf. chạthᵃr. ¶ chạtᵃri-bardār m. an umbrella-bearer, an official whose duty it is to carry the state umbrella over a king's head; see chạthᵃr.

f. the fine show or beauty made by new clothes when they are put on for the first time on the expiry of mourning for a father or other relation, going out of mourning. --ganḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to tie on pretty clothes; (esp. of a man's wife's relations) to put a man out of mourning by giving him a new suit of clothes, to induce (by such means) a son (or the like) to go out of mourning (for his father or the like).

m. the final cooking of rice or other cooked food, after pouring off the water in which it has been boiled. It is then heated for a short time in order to drive off the surplus moisture. This heating is called chāv. El. writes the word chhao, makes it f. and translates it 'boiling' (Śiv. 1020, 1717). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. cooking to be completed, as ab.
f. flinging, in the following:--chāwa-chāv f. a kind of gymnastic exercise, throwing a stick or the like from one to another, backwards and forwards. Cf. chāwun 1.

in the following:---dag f. wasting time in the performance of any employer's work, by the workers pointing to each other as the proper person to do it; as when e.g. A says "it's B's work", and B says "it's C's work", and C says "it's A's work", so that in the end nothing is done. Cf. chọ̆pᵃrāwan and chapāwan. -dās m. 'Mr. Shirker', one who wastes time as above, a work-shirker, a skulker.
m. the act of tucking up the skirts of a garment (as is done by villagers when working in the fields).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. chôwᵘ), to throw anything at or to another person (Rām. 923, 1433). ¶ chôwᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f.chöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), flung at another.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. chôwᵘ), to enjoy, make use of, partake of, experience (Śiv. 26, 60, 132, 181, 511, 1008, 1058, 1691, 1711, 1782, 1800, 1823; Rām. 1525, 1627, 1634, 1770); to experience (an odour), to smell (H. xiii, 3); to enjoy happiness or prosperity, to be happy, blessed. azal chāwun chuh, fate is to be experienced, one must dree one's weird (H. ix, 6). chāvĕkh or chāyĕkh ben. sg. 2, mayst thou use, mayst thou have full enjoyment of (Gr.Gr. 252). Hence, used as a subst. masc., full enjoyment, perfect bliss, equivalent to the Persian mubārakī (Śiv. 668). ¶ chôwᵘ-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. chöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), enjoyed, used, partaken.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. chôwᵘ), to embroider (cloth, etc.) (K.Pr. 260, where the inf. is translated 'jewels'. It seems really to mean 'embroidery', i.e. an embroidered garment; so W. 149).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. chôwᵘ), to complete the cooking of rice, vegetables, or the like when being boiled (K.Pr. 41); the 'completion' is done by pouring off the water, and placing the food over the fire for a short time, so as to drive away the surplus water. Cf. chāv 1 and aḍa-chôvᵘ 1 under aḍ.
(YZ. 254, 258, 527, etc.), incorr. for cāwun, to give to drink, q.v.
m. a certain kind of apple (see El. s.v. trēla).

f. the White River, N. of a certain river in Kashmīr, called in Sanskrit Śvētagaṅgā (White Ganges) or Dugdhagaṅgā (Milk Ganges). Its source is at Chütsᵘ̈-küñᵘ̈ in the Pīr Panʦāl Range to the south-west of Śrīnagar. It runs into the Vĕth (Jehlam) in the town of Śrīnagar at a place named in Sanskrit Bahukhādakēśa, still of some repute for its sanctity, and opposite the old quarter of Diddāmaṭha. Cf. chüʦᵘ̈-küñᵘ̈ under chotᵘ, RT.Tr. II, 418, and El. s.v. chatsakŏl.
f. (sg. dat. chạʦᵃrüñᵃ), the act of making white, of whitening; the condition or state of becoming white, whitening.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. chạʦᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. chạʦᵃrun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 173). chạʦᵃrāwanayunᵃ m. inf. pass., i.q. chạʦᵃrana yunᵘ, see chạʦᵃrun. ¶ chạʦᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. chạʦᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), made white, whitened, whited; caused to feel ashamed; publicly disgraced.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. chạʦᵒrᵒ), to make white, to whiten; met. to put to shame, to make ashamed, to leave without answer; caus. of chatun (Gr.Gr. 173, 175). chạʦᵃrana yunᵘ m. inf. pass. to be put to shame, to feel shame, to feel oneself disgraced.
m. (sg. dat. chēkas), a wish for good luck expressed when another puts on new clothes or ornaments for the first time.

or chikun conj. 1 (1 p.p. chyukᵘ or; 2 p.p. chicyōv), to propel liquids to a distance in one stream, to squirt; to urinate, make water (in this sense impersonal in the tenses derived from the past participle). El. gives this word the meaning of chakun, q.v.
m. a plain ring of gold, silver, or other metal, worn on the finger or toe--the Hindōstānī challā.
f. irritation, annoying or frightening a person by abusing him or worrying him; using such means to drive a person away, or make him run away.
adj. c.g. one who acts hurriedly owing to irritation, fear, or the like. Cf. chörᵘ̈.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. chyūrᵘ 1, pl. chīrⁱ; f. chīrᵘ̈ 3, pl. chērĕ 3; 2 p.p. chēryōv. For chyūrᵘ 2 see chōrun, for chīrᵘ̈ 1 and 2 see s.vv., and for chērĕ 1 and 2 see chīrᵘ̈ 1 and 2), to irritate, to worry a person by abusing him or harassing him. chyūrᵘ-motᵘ adj. (f. chīrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈; for 2 see chōrun), irritated, etc.
m. the presentation of an offering to a deity (in Sanskrit balidānam) (Rām. 1132).
f. a short sudden cry of pain (e.g. when one is unexpectedly pinched). Cf. cicrahāray, cã̄carāray, and cicarāray.
f. a woman who is fond of ridiculing others, a silly jesting woman.
m. (sg. dat. chicharas, ag. chichᵃ̇ᵃ̇, abl. chichari; pl. nom. chichᵃ̇rᵃ̇, dat. chicharĕn, abl. chicharyau), a boil, a pustule or swelling full of matter; met. a small lump of fat mutton.
f. (sg. dat. chīshᵘ̈), a sneeze, sternutation.
f. (sg. dat. chishᵘ̈), a slight accidental blow (esp. of something hard) on the edge or point of anything, a knock.
f. a very small amount of anything, as in ạshᵉ̆ka chīh, a very little love (H. vii, 30).

f. (sg. dat. chiki), sprinkling, the throwing a little water or other liquid to a distance (Gr.Gr. 125); cf. atha-chikh, s.v. atha. ¶ chika-chikh f. mutual sprinkling of water, when two persons sprinkle each other or throw water on each other as ab.
f. the act of urinating by a dog.
m. a vile man living by vile habits and with vile companions.
f. a vile, despicable mode of life or conduct.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. chyundᵒrᵒ or; this verb is impersonal in the tenses formed from the past participles), to be stupefied, esp. of the stupefied amazement caused by the attainment of more than one hoped for or expected.
m. poverty, esp. that caused by loss of wealth or savings.
f. the thin stream of milk issuing at one pull of the udder at the time of milking (Gr.Gr. 13).
f. the milk of a goat or sheep. chiri-goru m. a seller of such milk; his wife is chiri-gȧrⁱ-bāy, while a female seller of such milk is chiri-gürᵘ̈.
f. the growth of the substance of a seed (as of rice, etc.), the filling out of the husk of a seed. Cf. dŏda-chir, under dŏd.
m. a lamb, the young of a sheep (male or female), esp. when newly born. --kaṭh -- m. (sg. dat. --kaṭas --), a young male sheep, a lamb ram. -pūtᵘ m. a young lamb (male or female).
f. an oblation of rice boiled in milk, coloured yellow with saffron, etc., and offered to Vāc, the goddess of speech, on the day on which a boy commences his first studies.
m. sprinkling water on the ground (to lay dust or the like).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. chirkôwᵘ), to scatter, sprinkle (water, etc.) (Gr.M.).

m. (sg. dat. chirivis), a certain fish found in the Valley of Kashmīr, with a long snout, from 8 to 15 seers in weight, the chharū gād of El. and charri gad of L. 157. ¶ chirivⁱ-cỗṭⁱ chiryuvᵘ-chinned, one who says flattering things, one who is soft-spoken in order to carry out objects.
f. (sg. dat. chērĕ 1), i.q. char 1, q.v.

f.(sg. dat. chērĕ 2, for chērĕ 3, see chērun), a switch, stick, wand, rod, cane, walking-stick; a wand of office (Śiv. 222, 1029). ¶ chēri-bardār m. a wand-bearer, the marshal who walks before people of consequence with a wand of office to make way and keep off crowds (Śiv. 1153).
f. a woman who habitually wears cloth stamped in colours; see chiṭh.

f. (sg. dat. chiṭi), cotton cloth stamped in colours, chintz; a chintz garment (K.Pr. 28 contrasted with satin, 154, 239). chiṭi-dutay f. a chintz garment with very wide sleeves worn by Musalmān women; it is sometimes simply called dutay, q.v. (El.). -gar m. a chintz-maker (El.). -nȧrⁱwār m. a large kind of sleeve or cuff made of chintz and worn by women.

f. in the following:--chiwalayĕ nērañĕ f. pl. inf. surplusage to issue, more than sufficient to exist, e.g. when food or money is being distributed amongst a number of people after every one has been supplied, something to remain over and above; to be enough and to spare.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. chivyōv), to be intoxicated, maddened (with wine, drugs, etc. (K.Pr. 5, Śiv. 1860); to be proud, puffed up, arrogant, intoxicated with the possession of wealth or the like; to be intoxicated, in rut (of an elephant, etc.). chivyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. chivyē-müʦᵘ̈), intoxicated; arrogant (whether by nature or owing to some special cause); in rut (of an elephant, etc.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. chiwᵃrôwᵃ), to intoxicate, madden (by the administration of wine or drugs or by suggestion); to make proud.
f. a bramble; a raspberry, Rubus nivens (L. 73, El.). This word is often spelt chānch or cānc.
f. (sg. dat. chö̆zᵘ̈), hunger, desire for food; craving genl. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. hunger to come; a craving to arise (in one who is a slave to the habit) for snuff, bhang, opium, or other intoxicant.
adj. c.g. wounded, bruised (esp. of fruit or the like). Cf. chŏkalad.
adj. c.g. having a sore (Gr.Gr. 135, El.); wounded, lit. (e.g. of soldiers in a battle, or any other animate creature), or met. (YZ. 149, the heart). Cf. chŏkal.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. chŏkalyōv), to be scattered, become separate from the others, e.g. of one of a number of things floating down a river being separated by an eddy from the rest. Cf. chạkᵃrun.
f. obstinate and persistent begging for something valuable which the owner does not wish to give; cf. chŏka-phakīr under chŏkh 2. --trāwüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to beg obstinately, as ab.
f. (sg. dat. chŏkawüñᵘ̈), the act of dipping into water (as when one holds a garment by one end and dips into, and moves it about in, the water).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. chakowᵘ), to dip (a garment or the like) into water and move about the article dipped therein; to stir any liquid contained in a vessel, to churn by shaking. ¶ chŏkawana yunᵘ m. inf. pass. (of curds, water, or the like) to be shaken about in a closed, or nearly closed, vessel, to be churned by shaking.
f. persistently and obstinately begging for something (of children). Cf. chŏka- lākañ under chŏkh 2.
m. (sg. dat. chọ̆kas), slight washing (of a dish, a garment, etc.), rinsing out only with water (Gr.Gr. 123). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to rinse out with water. --trāwun -- m.inf., id.

m. (sg. dat. chŏkas), a wound (K.Pr. 17, 146, Rām. 187, 430, 529, etc.), a sore (esp. from a missile), a blow with effusion of blood (El.); met. the blow or striking of a churning stick in milk (K.Pr. 174); lōla-chŏkh (pl.), the wounds of love, pangs caused by love (YZ. 451). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to wound (esp. by a missile). ¶ chŏka-dŏd m. buttermilk churned without water. -lāgay f. wounding oneself; esp. the revengeful self-wounding done when a person is aggrieved by the action of another on whose head he intends that the guilt of causing the wound shall fall. -lākam m. a thorn-bit (for horses). -lākañ f. persistent asking for anything (esp. by children who won't be satisfied with a refusal). Cf. the next. -phakīr m. an obstinate persistent beggar, who inflicts wounds upon his own person in order to terrify people into giving him something. -phakīrī f. the conduct of such a beggar; leading the life of such a beggar.
adj. (f. chŏkᵘ̈jᵘ̈), clear and quick (of speaking, reading, singing, etc.) (Gr.Gr. 146).
adv. exactly, accurately, u.w. vbs. of speaking, answering, etc.
adv. from above (cf. bāl 1) and below, heedlessly, carelessly, u.w. vbs. of coming, etc.

or chŏmba (Gr.Gr. 122) m. a method of threshing paddy, in which the stalks are held in the hand and the heads struck against a post. This preserves the straw from being injured, as it would be if trodden out by cattle on a threshing-floor. The chúmba of L. 464. Cf. atha-chŏmb under atha. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to flog, whip (with a rod on the bare skin). --karun -- m.inf., id.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. chọ̆mbᵘ), to thresh grain, as described in art. chŏmb, q.v. chọ̆mbᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. chö̆mbᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), threshed, as ab.

m. onomat. chink, tinkle, the sound made by money in a bag, a bell-girdle, or the like; cf. chañ. -bọ̆ngᵃrĕ f.pl. bracelets (of crystal or precious metal) supplied with bells, so as to make a tinkling sound. -chŏkh m. onomat. (sg. dat. -chŏkas), i.q. chañ-chakh, see chañ. -chŏñ m. onomat. chink-chink, tinkle-tinkle, the sound of chink repeated over and over again. -dār adj. c.g. a chinker, a tinkler, that which has the power of emitting chinks or tinkles, such as a staff or a girdle supplied with rings or bells to make a chinking or tinkling noise. -ṭŏñ m. onomat. making chinks, making money (esp. someone else's) fly, squandering.
m. incompleteness, want of full weight or measure; loss, detriment (El.).
f. the art or profession of a carpenter (Gr.Gr. 142).

or chŏnnun conj. 3 (2 p.p. chŏnyōv or chŏnnyōv), to be deficient, to be below the full size, quantity, or weight (Śiv. 1212). ¶ chŏnyō-motᵘ perf. pass. (f. chŏnyĕ-müʦᵘ̈), reduced in size, quantity, etc. (e.g. of dried-up fruit, wealth, etc.).

or chọ̆ñᵉ̆rāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. chọ̆ñᵒrᵒ or chọ̆nᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), to make less, to reduce below a certain fixed quantity, to lessen (the chhenrāwun of K.Pr. 119). chọ̆ñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. chọ̆ñᵉ̆röwᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), reduced below a fixed weight or scale of quantity.

or chonᵘ adj. (f.chö̆ñᵘ̈ or chüñᵘ̈), empty, void; (of a cargo-boat) empty, in ballast (Gr.M.); empty of wealth, poverty-stricken (cf. atha-chọ̆nᵘ under atha); less than a certain amount, deficient in quantity; adv. (like the Hindōstānī ḵẖālī) only, merely. This word is generally used with emph. y, as in chọ̆nu-y or chonu-y (Śiv. 1201), and is thus spelt: chhŏnóí by El., so K.Pr. 42, chhĕnī, and 239, chhanī for chüñᵘ̈y. -nonᵘ adj. (f. chüñᵘ̈-nüñᵘ̈), empty and naked; hence, poverty-stricken. ¶ chañĕ-mŏchĕ adv. in a condition of being poor or hard up (esp. in connexion with having to provide a wedding feast or the like), u.w. vbs. of giving, etc.

f. sifting, winnowing, straining; knocking down walnuts from a tree; siftings, the resultant of sifting (e.g. cleaned or winnowed grain) (Śiv. 1532, 1533). In Śiv. 1532 chöñī is m.c. for chöñⁱ, i.q. chöñᵘ̈.
the result of sifting, the cleansed and sifted rice, flour, or whatever article is passed through a sieve or strained.
f., see chān 1, a carpenter's wife, usually employed as the latter part of a proper name, as in Zūna chöñᵘ̈, Zūna the carpentress (Gr.Gr. 37). K.Pr. spells this word chhāni, i.e. chāni.
f. the livelihood or craft of a carpenter, carpentry, esp. of one who has taken to the craft after giving up some other art (Gr.Gr. 143).
m. (sg. dat. chōpas), a machine or stamp (usually of wood) for impressing marks on heaps of grain, etc., so as to prevent the pile being broken without detection.

f. (sg. dat. chọ̆pᵃrāwüñᵃ), throwing something about so as to conceal it, hurried concealment; concealment of faults, bad qualities, etc.; causing time to pass. -dag f. causing time to pass, pretending to waste time, temporizing in order to get something done. Cf. chapāwan-dag under chapāwan and chāwan-dag under chāwan.

or chọ̆pᵃrāwun 1 conj. 1 (1 p.p. chọ̆pᵒrᵒ or chọ̆pᵃrôwᵃ), to spend (money), to expend (articles); esp. to spend extravagantly, dissipate. This verb is an irreg. caus. of chapun 1, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 174). chọ̆pᵒrᵒ-motᵒ 1 perf. part. (f. chọ̆pᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), expended, dissipated. chọ̆pᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. chọ̆pᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), id.
or chọ̆pᵃrāwun 2 conj. 1 (1 p.p. chọ̆pᵒrᵒ or chọ̆pᵃrôwᵃ), to fling away anything so as to conceal it, to conceal hurriedly; to hide, conceal (faults, bad qualities).
or chỗpᵘ m. a kind of small churning-stick, used for churning curdled milk, etc. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to churn as ab.
m. in the following:-- --lagun -- m.inf. unhealthy evacuation to occur unawares, sudden diarrhœa to occur. Cf. chôrᵘ.

m. a waterfall (an old form of chūl, q.v.). chōra-dār f. the stream of a waterfall, a torrent; chōra-dārĕ karun m.inf. to make (a person) in a torrent, to make him stream with blood, esp. to cause this by dragging him along the ground (as is done in a certain punishment).
in the following:-- -baṭañ f., i.q. chahōra-baṭañ, see chahōra, p. 159, col.a, l. 26.
m. a certain part of the female genital organ; apparently the triangular segment in front of the vagina on which are the clitoris and the meatus urinarius. The word is also used in filthy abuse.
in the following: ---chŏr or -chŏra f. agitation, distress, fluttering, quivering (from pain, sorrow, etc., like that of a fish caught in a net).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. chūrᵘ or chyūrᵘ 2, pl. chūrⁱ or chyūrⁱ; f. chūrᵘ̈ or chyūrᵘ̈, pl. chōrĕ; 2 p.p. chōryōv. For chyūrᵘ 1 see chērun), to release, loosen, dismiss, let go (Rām. 490), esp. something tied up or confined; to let go (something held); to give, give away (Gr.Gr.). chūrᵘ-motᵘ or chyūrᵘ-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. chūrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ or chyūrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈. For chyūrᵘ-motᵘ 1 see chērun), let go, etc., as ab.
m. an unhealthy condition of the evacuations, diarrhœa, etc. (K.Pr. 49), esp. of horses or cattle. Cf. chōr. ¶ chāri-könzᵘ̈ m. dahī (curdled milk) which has turned liquid, green, and sour.
f. hurry, fluster, agitation from fear or the like occurring in the performance of any action cf ʦhĕpa-chörᵘ̈, p. 1061a, l. 7.

or chyotᵘ adj. (m. sg. dat. chatis or chĕtis, and so on; f. chüʦᵘ̈ 1 or chë̆ʦᵘ̈ 1; for chüʦᵘ̈ 2 see chath 2), white [Śiv. 113, 1543, 1607, 1662, K.Pr. 42 (chotᵘ pôʦhᵘ, a white cotton coat), 116; Rām. 1502, 1614]; dāri- chotᵘ, white-bearded, a venerable person (Rām. 1600). --shīn hyuhᵘ -- adj. [f. chüʦᵘ̈ (ch ë̆ʦᵘ̈) shīnhishᵘ̈  ], white like snow, snow-white. chotu-y adv. uselessly, needlessly, unnecessarily, u.w. vbs. of coming back and the like. ¶ chȧtⁱ (chĕtⁱ) krĕhȧnⁱ ʦārȧnⁱ  m. pl. inf., lit. to select blacks and whites; hence, to be zealous in picking holes in a person's (esp. a blameless person's) character, or in harmless words or actions. ¶ chüʦᵘ̈ (chë̆ʦᵘ̈) dāl  f. white dāl, a certain dish made up of husked millets, husked beans, or similar white grains. --han -- f. 'the white little', i.e. that which remains after sorting or sifting out the dirty portion of things, such as grain or the like. --küñᵘ̈-- f. the white stone, N. of a place also known as 'Sangsafēd', marked by a white rock, from which issues the source of the river formerly known as Śvētagangā, and now as Chaʦa-kŏl, q.v. s.v. The place is to the south-west of Śrīnagar, in the central part of the Pīr Panʦāl Range round Mount Taṭakūṭī. See RT.Tr. II, 418.
m. (?), a broom of twigs, a branch of a tree used as a broom. Only noted in K.Pr. 35. The form of the sg. nom. is uncertain.

vb. subst. This verb is defective, being only used in the present tense and rarely in the imperative; it is participial in form, being liable to change for gender. Its forms are m.sg. 1 chus, 2 chukh, 3 chuh; pl. 1 chih, 2 chiwa (chiv, m.c. in H. vii, 9), 3 chih; f.sg. 1 chĕs, 2 chĕkh, 3 chĕh; pl. 1 chĕh, 2 chĕwa, 3 chĕh. The final h of the forms chuh, chih, and chĕh is added only to aid pronunciation, and is dropped before all suffixes, as in chu-na, he is not, chĕm, she is to me. When a suffix commences with a vowel the u of chuh becomes w, and the i and ĕ of chih and chĕh become y. Thus, chuh + ā becomes chwā, is he? and chih + ā and chĕh + ā both become chyā, are they (m.)? is she? or are they (f.)? ¶ In H. vii, 9 a pres. cond. pl. 2 chiv occurs. ¶ For the other tenses of the vb. subst. the vb. āsun (q.v.) is employed. ¶ Chuh is also employed as an auxiliary verb, forming, with the pres. part., a present tense, as in suh chuh karān, he makes or is making, and, with the perf. part., a perfect tense, as in tȧmⁱ chuh korᵘ-motᵘ, he has made. In such cases verbal suffixes are added to the auxiliary verb and not to the participle. There is this peculiarity, that when this occurs the suffix of the agent case of the 2nd pers. sing. is generally y, not the th used with the past tense. Thus, ʦĕ koru-th, thou madest, but ʦĕ chu-y korᵘ-motᵘ, thou hast made. ¶ As a vb. subst. chuh is very commonly used with a dative of possession, thus providing Kāshmīrī with a verb signifying 'to have'. Thus, mĕ chuh or (with suffix) chu-m, there is to me, i.e. I have. ¶ Except as stated above in regard to the agent of the 2nd pers. sing., this verb takes the usual pronominal and adverbial suffixes. Thus, chus, I am; chus-ay, I am for thee; chukh, thou art; chukh-a, art thou? chuh-an (for chukh-an) karān, thou makest him; chuh-an-a karan, dost thou make him? chwā (chuh + ā), is he? chyā (chĕh + ā), is she? chu-na, he is not; chu-nā, is he not? chu-y, he is to thee, or he is verily; chu-y-ĕ, is he to thee; chu-s, he (or there) is to him; chi-s, they (m., or there) are to him; chĕ-na, she is not; chĕ-nā, is she not? chĕ-y, she is to thee, or she is verily; chĕ-y-ĕ, is she to thee? chĕ-s, she (or there or they, f.) is to him, and so on. In H. xii, 6, chiy is used instead of chuy, he is verily. Cf. Gr.Gr. 189 and Gr.M.
m. onomat. the noise made in driving a horse, tchk (H. xi, 8).
m. (sg. dat. chūkaras), a lad, a growing boy; hence, a small person, a person of humble station. Cf. K.Pr. 42, where the sg. dat. is incorrectly written chuṅkaras, i.e..
m. (pl. dat. chūlan Gr.Gr. 51), a waterfall, cascade (Śiv. 983). ¶ chūla-wôñᵘ m. cascade water, a small mountain stream issuing from a water-fall.

in the following:---mār m. 'a dagger-striker', a kind of beggar so importunate that he will even kill himself with a dagger if his request is not complied with. Such threats are not uncommon, and invariably result in the request being granted, as a refusal would bring the guilt of murder on the head of the refuser.
chĕy, chĕyĕ; chuy, chuyĕ, see chuh.
or m. a squirt, syringe for projecting water.

pron., adv., and conj. what?; which, what; as, because; either, whether, or, even; in Rām. 573 ci is used in the sense of the Persian چون, like,--ci guldasta, (the six seasons were standing together) like a posy.

m. onomat. in the following:--cī˜-cī˜ karun m.inf. to utter repeatedly low sounds when crying, to sob. cī˜ karun m.inf. a certain sound, the short involuntary exclamation uttered, when one is suddenly and unexpectedly pinched or the like.

adj. boyish, childish, puerile, only noted in the m. abl. sg. and in the following adverbial phrases:-- ¶ cibāli cibāli karun m.inf. to show love to a child regardless of its conduct (whether it is naughty or not), to spoil a child with injudicious affection. --cibāli gaʦhun -- m.inf. (of a child) to be petted or treated with affection (even when naughty), to be spoilt by injudicious affection so that he is encouraged in naughtiness.
or cicĕ m. the bosom, esp. that of a young undeveloped girl.
f. groaning, moaning, usually the low moaning of a number of starving people, esp. children. Cf. cicrahāray, cã̄carāray, and chicharahāray.
f. a scream arising from any sudden pain. Cf. cã̄carāray, cicarāray, and chicharahāray.
m. the intoxication of youth (K.Pr. 207, of a young girl), the effervescence of spirits in a young man making him self-confident and daring.

m. a particular mode of working silk flowers on muslin or other cloth (El.); embroidery, 'chicken-work.' -dôrᵘ m. an embroiderer (El.). --kaḍȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to pick out embroidery; met. excessively and unnecessarily to test another's statements; to bring under discussion over and over again. -kār چکن کار adj. c.g. embroidered, the name of a certain kind of shawl (L. 377, chiknikár).
m. N. of a mountainous tract in the west of Kashmīr along the left bank of the Vĕth (Jehlam) between Cikōtī and Dōmēl. Immediately to its west is the British District of Hazārā.

adj. c.g. lit. 'of what use?' useless, worthless, contemptible. cikāras hyonᵘ m.inf. to be countable on an occasion of honour (i.e. of one whose character has to be considered before deciding as to the amount of respect to be shown to him); to consider mean or contemptible (used especially with reference to one who has taken a bribe and cannot be trusted).

f. (sg. dat. ciki), a shrill sound made by any mechanical means; a high-pitched cry (not necessarily loud); (pl.) met. grumbling, murmuring (Gr.M.). -bākh m. (sg. dat. -bākas), a complaint made with loud lamentations (esp. of a complaint or call for justice to an official). Cf. cākh-bākh, under cākh 3. ¶ cika diñĕ f. pl. inf. to grumble, murmur (Gr.M.). -nād m. a call or cry uttered in a high-pitched, but not harsh, voice.

f. (sg. dat. cīki), a shrill, far-travelling sound, such as that emitted by the whistle of a locomotive-engine; a scream, a screech. -bākh f. (sg. dat. bāki), weeping associated with screeches or screams (as when caused by rage or pain).

in the following: cikra-bākar f. noise, esp. the disturbing noise created by a number of children quarrelling or crying. Cf. caka- cakh under cakh 2. --hāray -- f. the noise made by a crowd (esp. of children or of birds).

m. a wooden pile, a piece of timber driven into the ground for building or strengthening embankments, etc. (Śiv. 1109); cf. cilacil. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to drive a pile or piles. cila-juvürᵘ̈ f. a wooden pillar driven into the ground for carrying a light, a lamp-post.
f. in cilacil karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to drive a number of piles close together in making an embankment, etc. Cf. cil.
m. the country commonly called Chilās, to the north and north-west of Kashmīr. It contains a celebrated shrine of Śāradā, the patron goddess of Kashmīr.
f. (sg. dat. ciliki), the manner or customary method of conducting any business. --nērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a method to issue forth, the starting of a new method of business.
f. the bowl of a huqqa, or hubble-bubble tobacco pipe, which holds the tobacco and the fire (K.Pr. 204, chilam). --cyonᵘ --, to smoke tobacco (K.Pr. 241).
(Hindōstānī چلکی), the local rupee formerly current in Kashmīr and worth about 10 ānās in British-Indian coinage (L. 236).

or cila m. a period of forty days; the forty days of Lent during which Musalmān religious fraternities seclude themselves in their cells or in their mosques, and remain at home fasting and engaged in divine worship; the fast of Lent. ¶ cilas bĕhun m.inf. to pass forty consecutive days in fasting and divine worship in a cell or mosque, etc.; to keep Lent.
adj. c.g. of, belonging to, or produced in the country of Chilās; a kind of tobacco, the plant of which has green flowers, Nicotiana rustica (L. 346).
f. a kind of earthenware dish or saucer used by Musalmāns (El. chin).
m. the country of China (Gr.M.); see cūna.
f. a large dish (El., K.Pr. 2, 6, 211, where it is spelt chin, i.e. cin).
? f. a fold, plait (YZ. 5, of hair).
cinwā m. Panicum miliaceum (El.). It is like rice in appearance, but is grown on dry land (L. 337).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. cīni), of or belonging to China (Gr.Gr. 150). --khôsᵘ -- m. a china cup (ib.); see, however, cūna.
adj. (f. -köñᵘ̈), dull-eyed, blear-eyed (e.g. from illness, or from having mean, insignificant eyes).

m. twisting, wringing; tearing by twisting or wringing (Gr.Gr. 123); cf. atha-cīr under atha, and ara-cīr under ara 1. -cār m. tearing fine cloth or the like by twisting and wringing. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to squeeze out, wring out liquid from anything, e.g. matter from a boil. ¶ cīra adv. firmly, tightly, u.w.vbs. of tying, etc.
(? spelling, L. 459, chirāgh beg), diarrhœa of cattle. ? cf. charun. Perhaps the word should be spelt chirāg or charāg.
(? spelling, L. 74, chirain), a certain tree found in Kashmīr at a high elevation, with a slightly acid berry, Pyrus lanata.
f. constipation, esp. of children. Cf. cīran 2.
m.pl. the bowels with their enclosing fat or suet. Cf. cirn.
n.ag. (f. cīrawüñᵘ̈), one who squeezes or wrings out cloth; (a cloth) which is wrung out (K.Pr. 254).

m. onomat. the chirping or twittering of small birds (esp. when a number are collected together). Cf. ciriv ciriv. --karun -- m.inf. to make a twittering; to make a low murmuring sound (of talking or weeping), esp. one which distracts the attention of another; to be peevish (Gr.M.). --lāgun -- m.inf. such a low murmuring sound to begin.
m. diversion or pleasure caused by vocal exercise, such as reading aloud, singing, or orating.
m. onomat. the chirping of sparrows. Cf. circir.
f. (sg. dat. cirki), purulent matter, pus.
(? spelling, L. 341, chirma), a certain weed, Ranunculus sp.
m. the fat surrounding the entrails, suet. Cf. ciran 2.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. cyūrᵘ, pl. cīrⁱ; f. cīrᵘ̈, pl. cīrĕ), to squeeze or wring out clothes or the like (Śiv. 1022); to squeeze together, contract (cf. bumb 2). ¶ cīrⁱ cīrⁱ hyonᵘ m.inf. to be wrung with pain from a long-standing disease difficult to cure.

f.pl. rice or other grain scalded with hot water, and then parched and beaten in a mortar. It is used for food, esp. as a viaticum when travelling. -gorᵘ m. a seller of this food. ¶ cirvĕn khasun m.inf. lit. to climb up upon (a pile of) this food; hence, met. to mount in absence of mind on to anything not intended for being mounted (e.g. stepping over a wall instead of going through the gate).

f. (sg. dat. cīrĕ, Gr.Gr. 61; for 2 see cīrun), a slip of paper, esp. one used for a memorandum, account, a lottery ticket (Gr.Gr. 60), or business acknowledgment; a document, paper used as evidence, a deed. Cf. amānath-cīrⁱ. --trāwüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to throw down a paper; esp. to cast a lottery slip or the like, when a number of names are written on separate slips of paper and mixed together, the prize-winner being drawn by chance from among them.
f. (sg. dat. cīrĕ), a certain thorny plant (Śiv. 1021).
adj. c.g. a niggard, one who, even though he have the wherewithal, stints himself and his family in the necessaries of life.
m. in ciṭha trāwun m.inf. to approve, choose, prefer.
f. a letter; a document, esp. a cheque, a bill of exchange, IOU, or other instrument acknowledging money (H. viii, 10).
m. a yellow kind of fragrant sandal-wood. -ṭyokᵘ m. (sg. dat. -ṭĕkis), a mark on the forehead made with powder of this wood.

m. any inanimate thing, article, commodity (Śiv. 1119, 1126, 1546; Rām. 152, 771, 1464, 1638); a matter, affair (K.Pr. 183); a thing of value, a valuable, precious thing: in the last sense also used with reference to animate objects with emph. y, chuna kē̃h cīzᵘ̈y, he is not any thing, he is insignificant (Gr.M.). El. makes this word f. With the suff. of indef. art. we get cīzāh (Śiv. 1650, Rām. 152, 1464).

m. a mace, a club, a stick; met. a beating (El., who makes the word f.; K.Pr. 73, 81, 85, 94, 171, 198; W. 141). In the latter sense the object beaten is put in the dative, as in hūnis cōb, beating (given to) a dog (K.Pr. 85), zamīnas cōb, beating the ground (K.Pr. 94). --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to give sticks; to administer a thrashing, to wallop, flog, birch (esp. children in punishment). --khĕnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to eat sticks; to be flogged, etc., as a punishment. -ĕ-korᵘ چوب کر m. (? spelling) a bitter root and tonic used in Kashmīr for horses, and much exported, Picrorhiza Kurroa (L. 75). -ĕ-kŏṭh m. the aromatic root of the kŏṭh plant. Its sale is a state monopoly (L. 75, 77, 83, 389, 418). See kŏṭh.
adj. c.g. quick, active; adv. quickly (YZ. 493).
m. (sg. dat. cŏbaras), a youth, a young man between the ages of 16 and 30. (cf. wū̃ṭa-cᵒ, p. 1159b, l. 41).

f. a young woman (esp. one who has not borne children) between the ages of 16 and 30, who is characterized by good looks and becoming dress. cŏbᵃri-motᵃ m. 'girl-mad', madly in love at first sight with some particular girl; lusting for a girl.

m. a ladle or spoon, made of wood when large and of bell-metal, etc., when small (El. spells this word choṅchih). --bazun -- m.inf. to wield the spoon; to hold authority or possess the power of superintendence, esp. in distributing another's food, money, etc. -mār m. 'spoon-hitting', preventing another from completing a meal or finishing a dish. --sapanun -- or --sapazun -- m.inf. 'to become a ladle'; hence, to become shrivelled or withered, as of the hand or other limb owing to cold, of the face owing to grief or loss, or of a flower, herb, or the like owing to the heat of the sun or to being broken.

m. adder's tongue (L. 72), a certain pungent herb growing wild in the forests, and used as a vegetable. It is described as having small leaves, and growing in the spring. cō̃cȧrⁱ-hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), id. considered as a vegetable.
f. an immoral woman, esp. one who receives men only in her own house. Cf. biṭh-cōd.
m. a kind of cloak reaching to the feet like a dressing-gown.
m. a kind of paddy bearing soft white rice. This rice is considered the best of all kinds, and is grown in Tēlbal on the Ḍal Lake (El. s.v. dányí and L. 333).
m. an informer, a spy; a tale-bearer, a tell-tale.

m. a square; an enclosure set apart for cooking or distributing food, the space in which a Hindū cooks and eats his victuals (the ground being first plastered with mud and cowdung); a similar place set apart for worship; a cooking-range. In the houses of the common people it is placed either in the small hall of the house or in the topmost floor (El., who spells the word chŏka). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to prepare such an enclosure for eating or for worship, to plaster the ground with mud and cow-dung as ab.

m. an impediment, in the following: cōka pyonᵘ m.inf. an impediment to fall, a stoppage or impediment to occur during the execution of some work. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to throw an impediment, to cause an impediment to occur to another in the execution of some work on which he is engaged.
(?) m. a pole for beating the mud at the bottom of a lake when collecting water-chestnuts (L. 355, chokdan). Cf. görⁱ-kôwⁱ, under gôrᵘ.

f. (sg. dat. cō̃ki), a sudden blow or bruise (esp. from something inanimate, e.g. from coming into collision with a block of wood or the like); a shock, loss in trade, etc. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause loss to another by setting an obstacle or stumbling-block in the way of his success. --lāgüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a stumbling-block to occur; loss to occur by an obstacle coming in the way of success. --khë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to suffer loss as ab.
m. (sg. dat. cōkas), a house in the form of a hollow square, with a court- yard in the centre, into which rooms on all the four sides open.
m. (sg. dat. cōkas), a long straight rent or tear in cloth or the like. Cf. cākh 1.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. cō̃kharôwᵘ), to cause to be withered or shrivelled (Gr.Gr. 170).
m. roast meat kept over from dinner and suitable for the following midday meal, equivalent to our 'cold joint'.
f. a group of four, an assembly of four persons; hence, a small assembly.

(?), N. of a Kāshmīrī tree, Euonymus sp., the spindle-tree. It is somewhat rare and grows at high elevations. Its wood is highly valued as a material for pen-boxes and for tablets in lieu of slates at school (L. 79, 82, chol). Cf. cūāl.
f. excitement, in the following: cölⁱ khasüñᵘ̈ f.inf. excitement to rise, esp. mad desire for the accomplishment of some purpose to arise in a person who cannot accomplish it without assistance.
m. an intoxicating drug made of opium and smoked in a pipe.
or conjᵘ adj. (f. cö̆njᵘ̈ or cünjᵘ̈), one who is accustomed to act without discrimination or without previous reflection.
m. (sg. dat. cōpaṭas), N. of a certain game resembling backgammon, the caupār of India (K. 811, 936, 938).

m. in the following: cŏrta karun m.inf. to stop a person's work by withholding the promised necessary materials, supplies, or other help. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to have one's work stopped by not obtaining such supplies, etc., as ab.; to be needy, necessitous.
m. the 'Persian lamb', the young of a sheep found in Central Asia. ¶ cȧrⁱ-musⁱla m. the soft woolly skin of this lamb used for making warm clothing, such as pōstīns and the like.
1 p.p. f. of cārun 1 and 2, qq.v.
adj. (f. cürᵘ̈), one who is fond of talking much, esp. of talking untruths and nonsense, a careless, heedless prater. Cf. car.

(also written cyôrᵘ) adj. (f. cörᵘ̈ 3, Gr.Gr. 12, for côrᵘ 1 and 2 and cörᵘ̈ 1 and 2 see cārun 1 and 2), one who is accustomed to conduct himself unworthily in whatever he says or does; an idiot (Gr.Gr. 12, Śiv. 1639; El. chór, f. chãr).
f. a kind of long-leafed grass growing in wet ground and used as fodder.
m. (sg. dat. cŏṭas), a fall (of a person slipping in mud, etc., and falling down).

m. (sg. dat. cōṭas; in some of the phrases below the word is fem.), a hurt, wound, bruise, blow, stroke, esp. on the lower part of the leg, from a fall, or violent contact with some inanimate object such as a stone or a log of wood; also of the blow of one inanimate object as ab. with another. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat such a blow, hence to receive a blow from an inanimate object, as ab.; met. to be hurt (of two people, etc., colliding); to suffer loss or injury by some obstacle intervening to prevent the completion of a matter. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to strike a person with a stick or the like on the lower part of the leg when he is erect or walking; to cause to trip or stumble. --lāgüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of a person erect or walking) to receive a blow from a stick or the like on the lower part of the leg; to trip, stumble.
f. (sg. dat. cōṭhi), fever recurring every fourth day, a quartan ague.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. cōṭyōv), to be pleased, satisfied (used in the old language, now mostly vill.).
f. a group of gossips, an assembly in which a number of people meet together and criticize others.

m. the chin, the lower part of the face; the mouth (El.). --holᵘ gaʦhun -- m.inf. the chin to become crooked; met. to receive a slight, or disrespect, in response to repeated requests for an urgent need. --raṭun -- m.inf. to grasp the chin; met. to stop a person as he begins to speak (by placing the hand over his mouth). --ʦaṭun -- m.inf. to cut the chin; to interrupt a person when he is speaking, by scolding, blame, or reproaches. ¶ cö̃ṭⁱ-ganḍ m. a knot on the jaw; to confine oneself, or to be confined, to one special food (e.g. owing to a vow or to sickness). -holᵘ adj. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), one who has a crooked chin, wry-chinned. -ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. a blow on the chin; met. when a person commences to speak, to stop him by the use of abusive language.
f., only used in the pl. cã̄cĕ, the lips. Cf. cỗṭᵘ, the chin. ¶ cã̄cĕ-myã̄cĕ f.pl. the corners of the lips, the right and left corners of the mouth.
f. a woman who excessively talks nonsense, a gabbler, prater, chatterbox.

f. a flat pat of soap, curd, or similar substance, bearing the impress of a man or other image; esp. a square of English soap (which usually has such a device stamped upon it), or a piece of native-made soap stamped, in imitation of English soap, with the form of an idol or other image.
f. (for 1 see cāwun), a cow that has been milked (perf. part. of cāwüñᵘ̈, q.v.).
m. (sg. dat. crāṭas), N. of a pargana of Marāz, the rice of which is esteemed excellent (El.).
m. Euonymus fimbriata and Hamiltonii (El.). Cf. col.
(?) (L. 258), the giving of presents on the fourth day after death. Cf. caudas.
f. cījᵃlā m. the ash (Fraxinus xanthoxyloides) (El.).
m. the settlement or fixing of a price between buyer and seller; the settlement or adjustment of an account.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. cukôwᵘ), to fix or settle a price (between buyer and seller), to agree to a price. cukôwᵘ-motᵘ perf.part. (f. cuköwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), having the price settled, that of which the price has been agreed upon.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. cukyōv), to be finished, completed, settled, decided (of a lawsuit, quarrel, or the like).
(?), f. a kind of barberry-tree bearing red fruit, Berberis Lycium. cuki-phal (?), m. its fruit (L. 74).
f. a square and low four-legged seat, a stool, a bench.
m. a watchman, guard, sentinel, chowkidar; a messenger (Rām. 584).
f. (sg. dat. cōlĕ), a small jacket or bodice, usually reaching down about as far as the navel.
m. boasting, gasconade, in the following: cum-kūṭunᵘ m. that which is hollow within but outwardly solid in appearance, a hollow fraud.
m. fawning, in the following: cuma-cỗṭᵘ m. one who fawns and licks, a flatterer, sycophant, fawner. Cf. cumun.
m. tongs, forceps, pincers, nippers, used principally for taking up burning coals or the like.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. cumᵘ), to show humility (to a person), to fawn upon, flatter, to implore with flattering words.

or cyūna m. (in composition this word takes the form cīnⁱ, as if from cyūnᵘ), lime. ¶ cīnⁱ-khôsⁱ m. a kind of metal cup (usually of brass) covered or ornamented with a lime-cement or enamel (probably really connected with the word 'china', see the next; in Gr.Gr. 150 the word cīnⁱ is given as an adj. meaning of or belonging to China). -pyāla m. a kind of earthenware cup ornamented with lime-cement or enamel. (The word cīnⁱ has here two meanings--one connected with cūna, lime, and the other meaning china, i.e. a cup made after the Chinese fashion.)

f. a spark, a small ruby or other gem, or a similar spark of an imitation gem (El. chaunī, i.e. caunī). --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to mark a pattern of creases along the edge of a cloth. --lāgüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to set sparks or other small gems, to fasten them in an ornament; to corroborate or confirm a statement made by another. ¶ cūni-dār adj. c.g. (of an ornament, etc.), set or studded with sparks or small gems. -gar m. a gem-setter, one whose profession is to set sparks or small gems in ornaments of gold, silver, etc.
in the following: curba bazun m.inf. to give or prepare a special titbit of dainty food just after midday, in addition to the usual morning and afternoon meal.
f. the ghost of a woman who dies in a state of pregnancy or impurity, and thus reappears as a demon; a witch, hag, beldame, vicious slut.

(? spelling) in curu-caras (L. 67, churu charras), a kind of 'charas' (see cars) extracted from the female hemp plant, and the same as the Indian gānjā. It is also called gard bang (dust bhang), and curu is apparently the same as the Hindōstānī cūrā, powdered.

f. a collection of creases in fine cloth or the like made by folding, sewing, etc., gathers, rucking, smocking, 'shirring.' Cf. cēr. cūri-bulbul m. a man outwardly prosperous but really so poor that he wants the necessaries of life. -norᵘ m. a garment, the sleeves of which are ornamented with fancy smocking.
adj. (as subst., f. cuṭhᵘ̈), young and thriving (in bodily powers), strong, vigorous.
f. a handful; a very small quantity (of grain or the like), only so much as can be taken up in one open hand.

f. a certain ornament, the cup-shaped silver bells fastened at the end of the long hair worn by girls hanging down the back. The use of this ornament is said to date from the time of Chinese domination, about a hundred and fifty years ago.
or cāñĕr m. the condition of being thine; hence, the condition of one who says "I am thine", extreme humility, extreme subserviency.

conj. 1, irreg. Śiv. 1000, 1220, 1344, 1385). For further forms see Gr.Gr. and Gr.M.], to drink (K.Pr. 102; YZ. 193; Śiv. 90, 579, 753, 1090, etc.; Rām. 557, 624, 806, etc.); to smoke (tobacco) (Gr.M., K.Pr. 241). -kyutᵘ adj. (f. cë̆ñᵘ̈-kiʦᵘ̈), anything intended to be drunk, a beverage placed ready to be drunk, something intended to be drunk and for no other purpose. For the form see Gr.Gr. 115. ¶ cĕna-bāv m. a beverage, something liquid prepared specially for drinking. -grākh n.ag.m. (sg. dat. -grākas, f. -grākañ), a drinker, one who drinks; one who habitually drinks, a man who is remarkable as a drinker, a great drinker, a hard drinker. -hār adj. c.g. anything drinkable, potable (Gr.Gr. 129); one who is able to drink a great deal, a mighty toper. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), i.q. cĕna-grākh, ab. ¶ cĕth thawun 2 m.inf. (for 1 see cĕth 2), to drink up the entire contents of a drinking vessel and to set the latter down empty.

possessive pron. (f. cyöñᵘ̈), thy. This word is used as the gen. of the personal pron. ʦᵃh, thou, q.v. ¶ cyönⁱ-sondⁱ adj. (f. -sünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to thy masculine person or object, e.g. of or belonging to thy (horse). ¶ cyāñĕ-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to thy feminine person or object, e.g. of or belonging to thy (mare).
in cyū̃-phyorᵘ m. (sg. dat. -phĕris), a tear-drop, esp. a hypocritical tear-drop forced out from the eyes to exhibit feigned sorrow or trouble.
adv. on (all) four sides, all round, in every direction (K. 1018, 1036).

. The third consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is the eighteenth (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the twenty-first) consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the twelfth consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It is pronounced as in India proper, with a sound much softer and more dental than the English d. ¶ The Sanskrit aspirate dha does not exist as a pronounced sound in Kāshmīrī. When a Hindī or Sanskrit word containing this letter also occurs in Kāshmīrī, the dh is represented by d. Thus, the Sanskrit dhanaṁ, wealth, is represented in Kāshmīrī by dana. In the case of words borrowed directly from Sanskrit, the dh is often, but not always, retained in writing in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character. Thus, the Sanskrit Dharmarāja, a name of the god Yama, appears in Kāshmīrī written in these characters both as and, but the pronunciation is always darmarāza. ¶ In the present work, whether a word is spelt in the Nāgarī character with or with, that letter will always be transliterated d, and hence words found in any native book spelt with should be looked up in the English order, under d. Thus will be found, in alphabetical order, under darma-rāza in the article darma. As a rule, spellings with will not be indicated in this Dictionary, even in the Nāgarī character. The principal exception to this rule will be found in the case of proper names, in which it is most usual to preserve the in native writing. Thus, the Sanskrit proper name Dharma-rāja will be shown in this Dictionary as darma-rāza .

. The fourth consonant in the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is the thirteenth (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the sixteenth) consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the thirteenth consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It is the cerebral ḍ of India proper, and has no corresponding sound or character in Arabic or Persian, or, indeed, in any European language. It has something of the sound of the English d in 'drum', but is properly pronounced by turning back the tongue and pressing the under surface of the tip against the palate. ¶ The Sanskrit aspirate ḍha does not exist as a pronounced sound in Kāshmīrī. When a Hindī or Sanskrit word containing this letter also occurs in Kāshmīrī the ḍh is represented by ḍ. Thus the Hindī ḍhēr, a heap, is represented in Kāshmīrī by ḍēr. ¶ In most Indo-Aryan vernaculars of the present day, including Hindī and Pañjābī, ḍ ڈ, when non-initial, is pronounced as a cerebral ṛ ڑ. This cerebral ṛ ڑ does not occur in Kāshmīrī, the pronunciation as ḍ ڈ being generally retained, even when non-initial. Thus the Hindī baṛa, great, is represented in Kāshmīrī by boḍᵘ. Sometimes, however, an original ḍ becomes a simple dental r in Kāshmīrī. Thus the Sanskrit biḍālaḥ, a cat, becomes brôrᵘ, and the Hindī ghōṛā, a horse, is represented by gurᵘ. In the dialect of the Sindh Valley, and perhaps also elsewhere in Kashmīr, r and ḍ are frequently interchanged. Thus, in a collection of Kāshmīrī folk-tales collected in the Sindh Valley by Sir Aurel Stein, the word for 'daughter' is not only the Śrīnagar kūrᵘ̈, but often, even on the same page, kūḍᵘ̈, and the word for 'to search' is both ʦhāḍun and ʦhārun. ¶ Occasionally we find ḍ optionally interchanging with a dental d, as in ḍal or dal, a leaf.

m. onomat. the lowing of a cow, a moo (K.Pr. 72, written daṅ). --karun -- m.inf. to moo (K.Pr. 72); met. to hem and haw, in the sense of denying or turning off the truth, e.g. concealing or denying the existence of something entrusted for safe custody, evading the execution of an order.

m. deception, dissimulation, feigning, hypocrisy; esp. of a criminal undergoing punishment feigning insensibility, pretended fainting, or similar device to get the punishment stopped. --karun -- m.inf. to do feigning; esp. in gambling or the like, to pretend something wrongfully, unfair dissimulation. --lāgun -- m.inf. to apply feigning; esp. to pretend to be ill in order to avoid doing any work, to malinger. --trāwun -- m.inf. (of a criminal under punishment) to pretend fainting as ab. ¶ ḍã̄ba-kã̄gᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a dissimulation-brazier; hence, the practice of dissimulation; esp. keeping quiet in the hope that something may be neglected, or that some other person may be charged with neglecting its completion.

m. a fall from a height, tumble (K.Pr. 43); the sound of a fall, flop, crash, bang (K.Pr. 227); dastāras dab, dashing one's turban upon the ground (a token of grief principally among Hindūs, K.Pr. 51); manȧṭⁱ dab, the fall (of a stone weighing) a sēr and a half, hence a punishment (K.Pr. 56); tōri-dab, the fall or stroke of an adze (K.Pr. 114, 236); dŏkᵃ̇rᵃ̇-dab, the blow of a hammer (Śiv. 1563). --bōzun -- m.inf. to hear the flop; to foresee accurately the result of any course of conduct. -dab m. the noise of footsteps, etc., in an upper story, heard in the story below. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to throw down from a height, crash to the ground (Rām. 1032); met. to abandon contemptuously any task already begun. --dāwun -- m.inf. to hurl down from a height (Śiv. 1879, from heaven to earth). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go flop, to suddenly cease (e.g. of a shower of rain, a storm, a fever, or the like). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall from a height when climbing. --karun -- m.inf. to wrestle (cf. daba-dab bel.); to cease suddenly (e.g. a shower of rain, a fever, etc.). --lagun -- m.inf. to come in contact with the ground as the result of a fall from a height, to come crash to the ground (K.Pr. 16); to stumble and fall when walking (K.Pr. 43). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall from a height; met. to fall from a high rank to a lowly position; to be knocked down by another; (of an object desired or tried for) to come into sight, success to come into view. --tārun -- m.inf. to sew in a particular way, to fell, to run and fell. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to constrain, compel, e.g. to do something impossible, to insist on a reply which cannot be given, or to give something which should not be given. ¶ daba behun m.inf. to be pressed, squeezed, or jammed down into any receptacle or on to the ground, etc. --bĕhanāwun -- m.inf. to press, squeeze, or jam down into any receptacle or on to the ground, etc. --byūṭhᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --bīṭhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), pressed, squeezed, or jammed down, as ab. -dab f. (dat. dabi-dabi), wrestling; cf. dab karun, ab. (K.Pr. 11; Śiv. 1754, dat.). -dañ m. the sudden fall, or being knocked down, of something solid. -dāñĕ m. smashing and pounding up anything suddenly, suddenly knocking to 'smithereens'. -lörᵘ̈ m. a breaking in pieces, like a cucumber falling from a height. -lörᵘ̈ gaʦhun m.inf. to be knocked down and broken, like a cucumber, as ab. (of a man's body or the stem of a tree, etc.). -lörᵘ̈ karun m.inf. to knock down and break, as ab. -lūr m. a knocking down and smashing, esp. of a lofty house levelled to the ground by an earthquake or the like. -lay  f. the heavy sleep of exhaustion after great exertion, or due to grief, illness, etc. -layĕ pyōmotᵘ perf. part. (f. -layĕ pyēmüʦᵘ̈), one who is asleep from exhaustion, as ab. -layĕ pyonᵘ m.inf. to fall asleep from exhaustion, etc., as ab. -sūr m. a certain medicine made of ashes of cowdung, pounded while still warm and mixed with clarified butter or oil. It is used as a remedy for a cough. -tronᵘ or -tryūnᵘ m. the serious injury (e.g. a sprain or broken limb) caused by a fall from a height or slipping on a muddy road. -tronᵘ gaʦhun or -tryūnᵘ gaʦhun m.inf. to suffer such a serious injury. -tronᵘ karun or-tryūnᵘ karun m.inf. to cause such a serious injury to another by throwing him down. ¶ dabas-pĕṭh dusᵘ m. a blow upon a fall; being at one's wits' end in a matter of extreme hurry and importance, e.g. the sudden arrival of a king in a distant province necessitating the immediate collection of supplies by the local Governor when such supplies are not available. pĕṭh dusᵘ pyonᵘ m.inf. blow upon blow to fall; met. a sudden, difficult, and urgent work to be imposed upon one who is already using all his energies on some other equally important and difficult business.
m. N. of a village near Shödⁱpūr (Shadipur), in Sāiru'l-mawāẓi' Pargana. Near it is a lake called Dabsar. See El. s.v. Cf. dŏb 2.
m. Typha angustifolia, a kind of bulrush (El.).
f. a covered wooden balcony outside the upper story of a house; a palace (El.). ¶ ḍaba-ḍolᵘ m. a wooden railing dividing out spaces in a room or enclosed area.

magnificence, pomp; power, vigorous authority. --karun -- m.inf. to exercise vigorous authority. --thawun -- m.inf. to assert or establish one's authority immediately on taking office. --trāwun -- m.inf. to proclaim, or spread abroad a reputation for, one's invincible powers.
m. a certain disease accompanied by boils on the chest.
m. a small round covered box or casket.
power, majesty; esp. vigorous and powerful rule due to prestige. Cf. dāba.
m. confusion, bewilderment, distraction in any business.
adj. c.g. one who shams sickness or weakness in order to escape punishment (Rām. 1785).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. dabaladiñ), dinted or damaged by a blow from a fall.
f. (sg. dat. -möshᵘ̈), a kind of vetch, dark in colour, fat-shaped, and long.

or dabanga adj. c.g. drunk, insensible from consuming bhang or the like (Śiv. 383), drunk and incapable. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become drunk or insensible from consuming an intoxicating drug (Śiv. 383), esp. of one not accustomed to it. ¶ dabanga sapazun m.inf. to become intoxicated as ab. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain or continue in a condition of insensibility as above.
m. rating, threatening (usually a subordinate or pupil). --karun -- m.inf. to abuse or threaten a person as ab.
f. a noise of trampling in a floor above, heard in the lower rooms of a house (cf. dab-dab under dab 1); angry rating, abuse.

f. (although shown as f., this-word is m. in the phrases below), a quick fall, utter destruction. --karun -- m.inf. to destroy quickly, e.g. to knock down a house with hatchets and the like. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. sudden destruction to occur; (of a human being) to be struck down when hale and hearty, to be ruined unexpectedly, to die suddenly.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dabôrᵘ), to rate, abuse, threaten (esp. a servant, child, or pupil, etc., who is prone to act improperly). dabôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. dabörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), rated, abused, threatened, as ab.
m. pressing down; force, strength, power; authority, influence, prestige.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dabowᵘ), to press down, knock down; hence, to press down to the ground (Gr.Gr.); to press down into the ground, to conceal in the ground. ¶ dabawana āmotᵘ perf. part. pass. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), crushed, pressed down (Gr.M.); knocked down senseless, senseless from falling down from a height. --yunᵘ -- m. inf. pass. to be crushed, pressed down; to become senseless from a fall, esp. from a height; to be run over (by a vehicle) (Gr.M.). ¶ dabowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. dabüwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), buried, or hidden, in the ground. dabawith thawun m.inf. to conceal in the ground.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dabôwᵘ), to press, squeeze (Gr.M.); to threaten, menace; to repress by threats, reproof, etc. dabôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. daböwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), threatened, menaced; repressed by threats, etc. daböwith thawun m.inf. to make entirely subservient by means of threats; to press, squeeze, nip (e.g. the finger between pincers) (Gr.M.).
f. a kind of practical joke, consisting in promising a person a gift or the like, which he is led to expect to be very large, but which turns out to be very small.
f. excessive threatening and abuse in order to humiliate another. Cf. dabāra.
adj. (f. ḍã̄bᵘ̈jᵘ̈), one who fraudulently wounds himself in order to accomplish some design.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dobᵘ), i.q. dabawun, q.v. dȧbⁱ dȧbⁱ thawun m.inf. to crush any articles into any receptacle and fill it in forcibly. dabith thawun m.inf. to forcibly stuff any article (such as wool or cotton) into a receptacle so as to fill it completely.
m. (sg. dat. ḍabaras), a kind of altar, made up of wooden boards, and kept inside a house or in a little erection close by.
perf. part., i.q. dabôwᵘ-motᵘ, see dabāwun.
f. a kind of large drum, used in proclamations and the like (Śiv. 1724). --wāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to play the proclamation drum; met. to widely divulge things that should be kept secret.
f. a small covered box (smaller than ḍaba 2, q.v.).

f. (sg. dat. regularly dachi, but usually written, i.e. dacha for dachĕ, cf. art. ĕ; the pl. nom. is dacha, also often pronounced dachĕ), a grape (W. 144, K.Pr. 43, Rām. 698; see El. for an account of the cultivation of this fruit in Kashmīr); the grape-vine (L. 73, 348). ¶ dachĕ or, the customary spelling of dachi, the dat., ag., and abl. sg. of dach. It is used in the following compounds: dachĕ-bạrᵃg m. a vine-leaf. -ḍaba or -ḍȧbⁱ m. a small round wooden box for holding grapes packed in cotton wool for transport. -ḍakh or -ḍokhᵘ m. (sg. dat. -ḍakhas or -ḍakhis), a grape-support, i.e. the trellis or lattice on which a grape-vine is trained. -gurun (sg. dat. -guranas), a bunch of grapes. -kŏḍurᵘ or -kuḍurᵘ m.
