(sg. dat. -kŏḍaris, ag. and pl. nom. -kŏḍᵃ̇rᵃ̇ or -kuḍᵃ̇rᵃ̇), a grape-seed. -kalam m. a grape-vine cutting, a short cutting of the grape-vine for planting or grafting. -kan m. a single grape, or two grapes growing together. -kānᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. the tendril of a grape-vine. -kurᵘ̈ f. an unripe bunch of grapes; vinegar is made from them (El.). -loṭᵘ m. the stalk, or pedicle, of a grape. -pholᵘ m. a single grape; a small collection of grapes, esp. when separated from the bunch. -püjᵘ̈ f. a large basket of grapes (YZ. 402, dachhih-paj). -pö̃purᵘ m. (sg. dat. -pö̃paris, ag. and pl. nom. -pö̃pᵃ̇rᵃ̇), N. of a certain moth. -ras m. grape-juice, used for making wine, as a medicine, or as a drink; for the last-named purpose Hindūs express the juice, strain it, and place it in the sun for four or five days; it is said to make a good drink (El.). -rāṭh or -rã̄ṭh f. (sg. dat. -rã̄ṭhi), a grape-vine, Vitis vinifera (cf. rã̄ṭhas dach, K.Pr. 155); a vineyard (El.). -tabakh m. (sg. dat. -tabakhas), a kind of earthenware case for storing grapes; two large basins are placed face to face and the edges sealed with mud; the interior is filled with the fruit. -tākh m. (sg. dat. -tākas), the posts supporting the trellis on which a vine is trained; hence, the trellis itself. -wạthᵃr m. a vine-leaf.
m. blackness, darkness, esp. of the colour of a bear or other wild animal; met. black-heartedness, hard-heartedness. Cf. dochᵘ.
or dachiñᵘ̈1 f. (sg. dat. dachiñᵘ̈ or dachiñĕ), a fee or present offered to an officiating priest or teacher, i.q. dakshinā, q.v.
m. N. of a pargana of Kashmīr situated on the right bank of the River Lẹ̆dᵘ̈rᵘ̈ (Ledar), the Sanskrit Dakṣiṇapāra (RT.Tr. II, 461); it is famous for its horses (El.).
adv. on the right (hand) (Gr.Gr. 155); in the south (Śiv. 246). --kinⁱ -- adv. from the right (Gr.Gr. 159). --pörⁱ -- adv. from or on the right (Gr.Gr. 160). Cf. dachyunᵘ 1 and 2.
m. a grain of rice first soaked and bruised and then parched, the familiar parched rice of India (El. dáchhul). ¶ dāchilⁱ-sütⁱ m. flour made from this parched rice, 'suttoo.'
m. the direction of the right hand, the right (Rām. 856); the south (Rām. 516, 1682). Cf. dakshin and dachinⁱ. ¶ dȧchⁱnyukⁱ adj. (f. dȧchⁱnicⁱ), of or belonging to the south (Gr.Gr. 151).

adj. (f. dachiñᵘ̈ 2; for 1 see dachin), right, not left (K.Pr. 43, 57; H. viii, 7); dexterous, clever, expert (cf. atha-d.); of or belonging to the south, southern, coming from the south; (of a tract of country) situated on the right hand of the sun's course. Kāshmīrīs divide land in this way into 'right-hand' and 'left-hand' country. A 'right-hand' village is better for rice-cultivation than a 'left-hand' one (L. 435). (Note, in the Persian character, and in most works by Europeans founded on Kāshmīrī written in that character, this word is usually written dachun, or dachhun, with its abl. dachani for dachini or dachĕni, owing to the persistent confusion between ĕ and i and between cha and chĕ.) Cf. dachinⁱ and dakshin.
f. the movable pole used for supporting the sloping mat-roof of a boat or the like when it is desired to raise its lower and outer edge. ḍachĕ tulañĕ f. pl. inf. to raise such a mat-roof.
or dȧchⁱñĕr m. the quality of being from or of the south, southerliness (e.g. of a wind or of a light shining); right-handedness, skill, dexterity (cf. atha-d.).

dānd m. an ox, bull, bullock (K.Pr. 69, 171, 226, 232). This is the word used in Śrīnagar; elsewhere hakhur is more common. The voc. is dã̄dā (K.Pr. 49); dā̃dᵘ̈y (K.Pr. dándai, 219), the very, or the particular ox. --trāwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to let loose bullocks; hence, to take them out from home to the field for ploughing; to let them loose for grazing, esp. in someone else's fields; at the end of a day's work, to unyoke the bullocks from the plough. --wāyȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to plough (Śiv. 1530). --wöyith thawȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to leave after ploughing; hence, met. to dig all round under walls of a room in search of treasure; (of rats) to burrow under the walls of a house. --wöyith trāwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to let go after ploughing; hence, to utterly beggar a person, even taking away what he had buried in the ground, as if he were not let go till all his land was ploughed up in the search for hidden treasure. ¶ dã̄da-brāṭh m. one who is as stupid as an ox. -bāṭh m. (sg. dat. -bāṭhas; f. -bāṭhĕñ), one whose business it is to transport goods on bullocks from place to place, a bullock-carrier. The f. is his wife. -cŏbur m. (sg. dat. -cŏbaras), a bullock-lout, a strong healthy young fellow as stupid as a bullock. -cākh m. (sg. dat. -cākas), a bullock-lout, a lusty young fool. -cākurᵘ adj. (f. -cākürᵘ̈), one who is as foolish as a bullock-driver, a loutish fool. -hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), N. of a certain vegetable eaten only by cattle. -hakhur m. a bullock-calf old enough to be used for ploughing. -hūrⁱ or -hūrᵘ̈ or (K.Pr. 10) -hŏwürᵘ̈ f. a pair or yoke of bullocks employed together on one plough (Gr.Gr. 82, where it is said to be vill.). -jūrⁱ f. a pair of bullocks, usually a match in appearance and age, fit for ploughing, etc. (Gr.Gr. 82, K.Pr. 187). -khrāv f. a kind of high patten or wooden soles used by Kāshmīrīs. -lyūṭᵘ m. (sg. dat. -līṭis, abl. -lēṭi), a kind of broad-leafed grass much liked by bulls for fodder, apparently resembling, or a kind of, clover. Cf. lyūṭᵘ and under batukh, batakh-lyūṭᵘ --pihun -- m.inf. to thresh grain by trampling it under the feet of oxen on a threshing-floor; to pound bullocks, to hit them on the hind quarters to make them go along when ploughing; met. to compel, by slapping him, an unwilling person to do any work. -phrāṭh m. (sg. dat. -phrāṭas), a bullock's scratch, a long slight furrow, e.g. for marking a boundary or starting-point, etc. -pūtᵘ m. an affectionate term used for a young bull not yet put to work; met. a stupid child. -thȧñⁱ or -thüñᵘ̈  '' f. 'bull's butter', anything impossible, like our 'pigeon's milk'. Cf. dã̄d chwā dŏd diwān, can an ox give milk? (K.Pr. 31). -wôrᵘ m. a bullock-pen, a bullock-yard, a stockyard. ¶ dā̃di-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), one who does not own an ox (K.Pr. 49). -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), one who owns an ox, the owner of an ox (K.Pr. 49).

m. user, use of anything usable, enjoyment of anything enjoyable, experience of anything. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to use, experience, enjoy (e.g. clothes, ornaments, food, or the sight of beautiful things).

m. statute, law; equity, justice; crying out for justice, complaint (YZ. 302); revenge; a part, portion; life, age. -bēdād داد بیداد m. crying out for help or justice (Rām. 438). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to dispense justice; to do justice (to), to appreciate, to give due praise (to); to weigh, reflect upon (another's words, or the like). -khāh داد خواہ m. a petitioner for justice, a complainant, prosecutor (H. ii, 5).

. Another meaning of dād dyunᵘ is 'to cry for justice, make complaint' (K. 756). Add the following. 'dād hyonᵘ m.inf. to take vengeance (K. 377, 443),' and in l. 14, '--wanun -- m.inf. to cry for justice, make complaint (K. 996).'

adj. c.g. knotty, full of knots (of sheets of birch-bark or the like). -pad m. verses that are knots (i.e. disfigurements), forged or non-original verses or sentences inserted into the matter of some authoritative book. -phĕl m. a knotty carbuncle; met. a son or daughter who is disobedient and wickedly behaved. -wāy m. knotty rheumatism; rheumatism of the joints, stiffness of the joints from rheumatism.
adj. c.g. bold, daring, fearless; (of things) tightly or firmly fastened up so that the knots or fastenings cannot be opened. Cf. ḍöḍⁱ.
f. an advance of money (made to cultivators, labourers, manufacturers, etc.). Cf. L. 418.

m. destruction of property, esp. the reduction to beggary of a weak man in his endeavours to please some important visitor, or the violent destruction of property by some superhuman means. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. destruction of property as ab. to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to destroy violently as ab.
f. a violent and continuous storm of rain.
m. N. of a fountain in the Vihī Pargana, near the village of Khruv (El.). Cf. RT.Tr. II, 459.
m. the name of the letter da, used in schools. Cf. ḍuḍḍö.
(? spelling), a fish-like insect, with hard scaly wings, which injures young rice-plants (L. 157, 331).
(? spelling) m. Rhamnus virgatus (El.), apparently a species of buckthorn.

f. a hollow tree; a hollow in a tree (H. ii, 10); a cucumber which has ripened till it is hard and dry and is no longer edible. (El. gives dadir, m. which he translates 'the edible part of a cucumber'; W. 12 has dadạr, a cucumber.)
m. N. of an extensive karēwa or plateau in Dachünpōr Pargana (El.).

or dā̃durᵘ m. (f. dã̄darĕñ), a kitchen-gardener (El.), a vegetable- and fruit-seller. The f. is a woman who herself sits in the market and sells such articles (Gr.Gr. 39). ¶ dā̃dᵃr-bāy f. the wife of a vegetable- and fruit-seller. -mujĕ f.pl. a small kind of radish, a garden-radish. ¶ dā̃dᵃ̇rᵃ̇-khāh m. a kitchen-garden.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dạdᵃrôwᵃ), to make weak, to oppress, harass another to weakness; (of grief, etc.) to reduce a person to weakness. dạdᵃrāwana āmotᵘ perf. part. pass. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), reduced to weakness by grief, etc. dạdᵃrāwana yunᵘ m. inf. pass. to become reduced to weakness by grief, etc. dạdᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. dạdᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), reduced to weakness by oppression, grief, etc.
adj. c.g. suffering from the disease of itch.
f. N. of a certain bird, a woodpecker.
f. N. of a certain cutaneous disease, itch. --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. itch to arise, an attack of itch to come on.

m. a man who is weak, powerless; one too weak to accomplish any particular work. --byucᵘ -- m. remains, savings, the little that is saved when one's fortune is lost. ¶ ḍaga ḍaga adv. (bringing) by little and little, (bringing) scraps or the leavings of a meal day by day (K.Pr. 54).

m. a mark burnt in, a brand, cautery (K.Pr. 60, Ram. 190, 203); a mark, spot, speck; a stain, dirty mark; a stigma, a blemish (Ram. 1106); the blemish (in a family), a ne'er-do-well, the black sheep of a family. --aʦun --m.inf. a stain to enter, dirty spots to come upon something white and clean (Rām. 652). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to mark, to scar; to wound, to grieve; to give a distinguishing mark to anything; to disgrace a person, to put a person to shame, on account of his bad conduct. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to brand (a horse, cattle, etc.); to apply the cautery (in medicine); to wash off a dirty mark or stain on a cloth, etc.; to suffer branding; to suffer intense pain (Rām. 203, 387, 643); to cause intense pain (Rām. 1713, 1718). --karun -- m.inf. to dip heated metal (such as red-hot iron or silver balls or nails) into water, so as to make a tonic draught. Cf. dāg-dār, s.v. --lagun -- m.inf. to be burnt; to become spotted with dirt; to be branded; to be defamed, get a bad name; to be damaged. --rōzun -- m.inf. the spot to remain; after washing out a dirty mark, traces of it still to be visible; met. of inward grief, after consolation, traces of the old grief still to rankle. --thawun -- m.inf. to stain, sully; to put a distinguishing mark on anything (Rām. 440); to vilify, defame, give a bad name to, to disgrace a person on account of his bad conduct (Rām. 688). --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause a stain to enter; to stain, put dirty spots on a clean cloth or the like. -zad داغزد adj. c.g. (as subst., f. dāga-zadiñ, see bel.), one who has a bad reputation, a reputed thief, or the like. ¶ dāga-zadiñ f. of dāg-zad ab., a woman with a bad reputation.
m. a club, mace (Gr.Gr. 10); a blow with a stick or cudgel (Śiv. 130); a walking-stick. Cf. ḍã̄guvᵘ. --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to give clubs; to give a drubbing, to flog a person as a punishment.

f. (Gr.Gr. 125), a blow (Gr.Gr. 148); esp. a blow caused to something falling from a height (e.g. to a fruit falling from a tree); patting, a series of gentle blows or pats with the hand or the like on any part of the body, shampooing; the smarting pain of a wound (K.Pr. 58); pain generally (K.Pr. 26, Rām. 1350); sorrow caused by the death of a beloved relation or friend; bata-dag, rice-pain, the pain of earning one's living (K.Pr. 26); mĕnga-dag, a pain in the temporal bone, a headache (K.Pr. 158); putra-dag, the pains of childbirth (K.Pr. 126); sūra-dag, the pain caused to the bare feet by walking in the hoar-frost (K.Pr. 26); yüḍᵘ̈-dag, stomach-pain, hunger (K.Pr. 239); dödis dag, the pain of sickness (Śiv. 1855, dagē m.c. for dagi); māzas dag, pain in the flesh (K.Pr. 152). Cf. dôdᵘ 1. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to thump; pound, triturate; to shampoo; to weave very tightly. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make smarting, to smart (of a wound, a rheumatic limb, a burn, or the skin to which an irritating ointment has been applied, etc.). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. grief to fall, grief at the death of some near relation or other loved person to befall. --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause smarting to another by a wound, a blow, or the like; to cause mental smarting by opposition, abuse, or the like. --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give rise to grief, to cause grief to a person, by killing his loved son or the like. --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. smarting to arise, smarting of rheumatism, a wound, or the like, to be felt; mental smarting from opposition or abuse to be felt. ¶ daga diñĕ f. pl. inf. to give thumps, to slap; to shampoo; to pour, as a remedy, a stream of water on a fresh bruise or wound. -makh f. (sg. dat. -maki), the employment of force or violence in order to accomplish anything (after previously trying gentler means). -makh karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to compel an obstinate person to set to work upon anything.

f. great love shown to a son, friend, or the like, intimate affection; cf. dôdᵘ 2. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take love, to feel intense sympathy with one who is loved. ¶ dagi-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), wanting in affection, not liking (anything or course of action), antipathetic; not loving (e.g. a woman to her step-children), unsympathetic; adv. , unkindly, stiffly, unsympathetically, in a critical spirit. -raʦhar m. want of kindliness, want of sympathy, want of liking (for). -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is very fond of any person or thing, loving, sympathetic.
m. (in building) a wooden vessel for carrying mud or mortar, a hod. Cf. ḍagur.
m. deceit, imposture, treachery; cheat, fraud, artifice (Gr.M.). tami-sṻty chih dagā karān, they impose upon him (Gr.M.). Cf. dagöyi.
in dāga-shālwôlᵘ, N. of a Government official, the chief of the shawl department (El.).
adj. and subst. m. deceitful, treacherous, fraudulent; a cheat, knave, impostor, traitor (Gr.M., El.).
adj. c.g. wounded by a blow, injured or spoilt (as e.g. a fruit) by a blow; suffering grief owing to the death of a loved relation or friend. Cf. dag.
adj. c.g. bruised, esp. of fallen fruit.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. dāgaladiñ), spotted, dirtied, spoilt by dirt-marks; defiled, morally fouled, of bad repute.
(cf. دغل دوست) m. (f. dagal-dūsᵘ̈), a treacherous friend, one who backbites in order to sow dissension between two friends.
or dagal-dūsī (cf. دغل دوستی) f. deceitful friendship; backbiting in order to sow dissension between friends.
f. the wife of a grain merchant. This word is non-honorific, whereas ḍã̄gar-bāy is honorific. See ḍã̄gur.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dāgowᵘ), to mark down, to note a person's or thing's character in a memorandum or the like for purposes of future identification, to note, brand, stigmatize; to enter a person's name in a document, account-book, or the like. ¶ dāgawana āmotᵘ perf. part. pass (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), one whose name has become entered as above. --yunᵘ -- m. inf. pass. to become entered by name as ab. dāgowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. dāgüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), entered by name as ab.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -dārĕñ), full of affectionate sympathy (as a father for his children, a master for his servant, etc.).
adj. c.g. branded, cauterized; scarred; marked, spotted; stained; blemished; (of water or the like) that into which red-hot iron has been dropped (to make a tonic). Cf. dāg karun, s.v. dāg.
adj. c.g. sympathetically affectionate (of a parent, husband, wife, or the like).
f. (sg. dat. dāgi-lānüʦᵘ̈), openly displayed disgrace, universally known moral foulness of any person, a thoroughly bad character.
f. deceit, fraud; faithlessness, infidelity (H. viii, 8). Cf. dagā.

conj. 1 (1 p.p.dôgᵘ, f. dögᵘ̈), to mark, to brand, to put a distinguishing mark on anything. ¶ dôgᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. dögᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, not döjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), marked, supplied with a distinguishing mark, ticked off (in a list).
or dagunᵘ (Gr.Gr. 148) m. (sg. dat. daganas), a hand-pestle for pounding vegetables, medicines, etc.; a mace, a club (Gr.Gr. 148).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dogᵘ, f. düjᵘ̈; 2 p.p. dajyōv), to pound, triturate (K.Pr. 66, 208); to hit, pound, with the fists (Śiv. 1856, dagē m.c. for dagi); to cudgel; to shampoo; to beat thin (e.g. gold leaf). In K.Pr. 208 daga fut. sg. 1 is spelt dugah, as if from a verb dŏgun, instead of dagun. Cf. dŏgawun and adọ̆gᵘ. ¶ dȧgⁱ dȧgⁱ sŏn banun m.inf. (somebody else) continually beating (someone), and that someone to become gold, i.e. by continual teaching and practice to become thoroughly competent or perfect. ¶ dogᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. düjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), pounded (of drugs, vegetables, etc., with a wooden hand-pestle); beaten thin (like gold-leaf or the like); struck, thumped, cudgelled. ¶ dagān dagān anun m.inf. pounding and pounding to bring; hence, with great difficulty, by some means or other, to bring any difficult and long-continued task towards completion. ¶ dagith thawun m.inf. to beat, drub, thump, smite (with fist or stick, all over the body).
m. (sg. dat. ḍagaras), a labourer employed in carrying mortar or the like, a hodman. Cf. ḍaga.

or ḍã̄gorᵘ m. (sg. dat. ḍã̄garas), a grain-merchant. He buys paddy from the cultivators and conveys it in large cargo boats to the city for sale. His wife is ḍã̄garĕñ, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 149 has dā̃gorᵘ, which is a misprint). Cf. dāñĕ. ḍã̄gar-bāy f. his wife. This is the term used when speaking politely.
f. a steep part in a mountain path.
adj.(f. ḍã̄güvᵘ̈), made up or composed of a club or walking-stick, as in ḍã̄guvᵘ gaz, a walking-stick yard, an approximate yard measured by a walking-stick (K.Pr. 221).
m. a coat or waistcoat padded with cotton, a quilted coat or vest.

card. (pl. dat. dahan 1, ag. dahau), ten (YZ. 93, Śiv. 199, 521, 984, 1692, 1793). Often used indefinitely for a large number; for examples see bel. -dôrᵘ adj. (f. -dörᵘ̈), ten-streamed, flowing in a copious stream; met. (of a work or the like) going forward energetically or prosperously. --dar dah -- دہ در دہ adj. c.g. ten upon ten; hence, very many, very much, copious; ten by ten, ten cubic (yards of water,--such being regarded as pure according to Musalmān law). -mashtī (? دہ مشطی), f. a kind of paper made in Kashmīr composed of three parts hemp fibre to every 177 parts of rags (L. 380). --sīrᵘ̈ -- f. presents of grain, etc., sent to a bride at intervals when living in her husband's house. Cf. daha- syūrᵘ bel. --sās -- m.pl. ten thousands, a certain weight equivalent to ten trakhs of about 11 English pounds each (L. 243); esp. materials (flesh, spices, etc.) for a great feast, to this amount. ¶ daha-gorᵘ adj. (f. -gürᵘ̈), of ten houses; hence, a square or other place surrounded by many inhabited houses. -khôrᵘ adj. (f. -khörᵘ̈), measuring ten khārs of 16 trakhs each. See daha-trokᵘ bel. -moñᵘ adj. (f. -müñᵘ̈), weighing ten man or manoṭᵘ of nearly 3 pounds each (L. 243). -mara adj. c.g. about ten, ten or thereabouts (Gr.Gr. 84). -syūrᵘ adj. (m. sg. dat. -sīris; abl. -sēri; f. sg. nom. -sīrᵘ̈), weighing ten sērs. A sēr is two-thirds of a manoṭᵘ, see ab. (L. 243). Cf. dah-sīrᵘ̈ ab. -trokᵘ adj. (f. -trücᵘ̈), weighing ten trakhs of a little over 11 pounds each (L. 243). -wuhurᵘ adj. (f. wuhᵘ̈rᵘ̈), aged ten years, ten years of age (Gr.M.). -wotᵘ m. approachable by ten roads, easily approached. ¶ dahan-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of ten, having ten owners; produced by ten, born of ten; costing ten (of anything), worth ten (Gr.Gr. 148). ¶ dahay card. only ten (Gr.Gr. 84).

m. burning, combustion, conflagration; the sensation of burning, internal heat; inflammation; ardour; heart-burning, envy, jealousy; a conflagration, a thing that causes internal pain or arouses jealousy (Rām. 153); destruction by burning, destruction (YZ. 556, K.Pr. 75). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to apply fire to, to light (the funeral pile), cremate (Rām. 443). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. envy or jealousy to arise; inward burning, inward rage to arise (Rām. 804). --karun -- m.inf. to cause envy or jealousy to be felt by any person.

f. (sg. dat. dahümᵘ̈), the tenth lunar day of either fortnight of the luni-solar month. Cf. dahomᵘ, dᵃhum, and dahyumᵘ. --kāh -- f. the tenth and eleventh lunar days, the name of a certain Hindū fast lasting three days. On the first day only one meal is taken, on the second nothing is eaten, and one meal is eaten in the forenoon of the third. --kāh karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to carry out such a fast; to fast in this way for any three days as a penance for eating impure food or the like.
f. (sg. dat. dahüñᵘ̈; for 1 see dah), the bad smell of milk or the like which has gone bad and sour.
m. a kind of musical instrument, consisting of a number of rings fixed to an iron rod crescent-shaped at one end. The rings are shaken in time to the music (El. dhehra). Cf. dukra.
card. (pl. dat. dahawȧnⁱ or dahawanī; ag. dahawȧyⁱ), all ten, the whole ten, emph. form of dah, q.v. (Śiv. 521, dat.). Cf. Gr.Gr. 85.
a place between the outer gate and a house; a privy; a spot where the house-refuse is thrown.

adj. in the following (cf. daham, dᵃhum, and dahyumᵘ): dạhomᵘ-hondᵘ adj. (m. sg. dat. dạhamis-handis; f. sg. nom. dạhümᵘ̈-hünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to, or produced on, the tenth day of a lunar fortnight.
m. (sg. dat. dahshĕtas), consternation, fear, fright, terror, dismay, dread, awe, alarm.

m. a large row or line of people (cf. dᵃhᵃrᵃ 1), a column of men, a caravan. ¶ dahari-bôjᵘ m. (f. -bājĕñ), the leader of a troop, esp. the leader of a class assembled for instruction, or of people collected together for amusement, a master of the ceremonies. -bājĕñ f. of the ab.; esp. a member of a row of women met together for singing, etc., on the occasion of a festival or the like.

m. a cry of distress, a piteous appeal; adj. (f. dahijᵘ̈), piteous, lamentable, full of distress, distressful (Gr.Gr. 146). --ponᵘ -- m. piteous grief, grief at the death of a son, husband, or the like, and of such a nature that it excites pity in another. ¶ dahijᵘ̈ dag f. a piteous blow, the extreme grief caused by the death of a loved son, husband, or the like.
or ord. (f. dahimᵘ̈), tenth (Rām. 1157). Cf. daham, dạhomᵘ, and dᵃhum. --dŏh -- m. the funeral ceremonies performed on the tenth day after a person's death. ¶ dȧhⁱmi adv. on the tenth day.
(W. 165), ḍāi (K.Pr. 80), and ḍāī, i.q. ḍāy, q.v.
m. a demon, an evil spirit hostile to the gods, a Titan (Śiv. 446, 677, 709, 856, 1392; Rām. 38, 550, 738; K. 736). See döth.
m. a bride's dowry, presents given to her and to her husband's relations (Śiv. 1675).
adj. c.g. a great deceiver; antichrist; hence, mean-hearted, miserly and shameless.
adj. c.g. patched (of a garment, cooking-pot, etc.).
m. pretended stupidity; pretending not to hear another's incitement; cf. dọ̆jᵘ.

m. a shove, push, knock, jostle, jolt, jog, shock, impact, collision; a push, a thrust (as in pushing a boat along) (K.Pr. 65); being thrust back or to one side, being pushed away, leaving off, desisting from; a blow or stroke of misfortune, affliction; loss (in trade), damage. -dakh f. (sg. dat. -dakas), shoving and pushing (as in a crowd), jostling. -ḍula m. treating with indignity, rough handling, esp. one who has lost his protector and is helpless. Cf. ḍula. -ḍula dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to give indignities, to expel or drive away with persistent contumely. -ḍula khĕnⁱ m. pl. inf. to suffer indignities, to be roughly handled, to be expelled or driven away with contumely from one's situation. --dith ʦhunun -- m.inf. 'having given a thrust, to throw'; to cause a person to desist from any action, whether he has completed it or not, to make him desist anyhow; to cause (a work) to stop, to complete a work, esp. to complete the marriage ceremonies of a girl. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to shove, push, jolt, jostle, knock against; to thrust or push away, butt against (Rām. 923, of two rams butting against each other); to inflict a blow or shock (on a person), to bring misfortune on; to thrust to one side; to put (a work) to one side, to complete (a work), esp. the arrangements for a girl's marriage. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. a thrusting aside to happen, to become hopeless of the accomplishment of any task. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to receive a shock or blow, to be pushed, shoved, or knocked, to suffer collision; to become hopeless of the accomplishment of any task. --karun -- m.inf. to thrust aside, to cause a person to desist from any work, to dismiss from employment. --lagun -- m.inf. to get a knock, shock, or jolt, etc.; to suffer loss; to meet with misfortune; to desist from any work, in hopelessness of being able to complete it. --ta ḍula lagȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. (of one who has lost his natural protector, and is hence helpless) indignity to be experienced on all sides, to be thrust about from pillar to post. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. a shock to come, to be stunned by any sudden calamity. -zad adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -zadiñ) reduced to misery by a blow of misfortune, such as the loss of one's natural protector or of one's means of support.
m. the name of the letter in the Śāradā alphabet, used in schools. Cf. ḍuḍḍö .
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. dakaladiñ), pushed about from pillar to post (of one who has lost his home or livelihood and is unable to obtain another from elsewhere). See daka.

or ḍakha (q.v.) m. (sg. dat. ḍakhas), a support, a prop; a support, a help (Śiv. 443); a stop to prevent a ball or the like rolling or falling; yūpis shup ḍakha, a winnowing-fan as a dam against a flood (K.Pr. 254). --āsun -- m.inf. a support to be; help to come, to be helped, encouraged, or propped up in any business. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to help, prop up, encourage a person in any business. --karun -- m.inf. when a boat is going along, to keep it off the bank with a punting pole. ¶ ḍakha-wörᵘ̈ f. a kind of small boat in attendance on a larger boat, for landing or bringing passengers and the like.

m. (sg. dat. ḍākas), the post (for conveying letters) (Gr.M.); a post-office. ¶ ḍāka-gara m. the post-office (Gr.M.). --munshī -- m. a post-master (Gr.M.). -pahörᵘ̈ f. a post-hut, a station at which a relay of post-runners waits and where the runners are relieved; any other similar relay-station. -wôlᵘ m. a post-runner, a postman. ¶ ḍākücᵘ̈ kirāy f. the postage of a letter (Gr.M.).
m. (sg. dat. ḍakhas), a curling lock of hair hanging behind the ears of Hindū children, a side-lock, curl, ringlet (El., Gr.Gr. 133).

m. (sg. dat. ḍākas), burnt clay, ashes, earth or clay which has been burnt by fire or parched by extreme heat. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be burnt, reduced to ashes or to dust by heat, e.g. of a house, a field, or the like. ¶ ḍāka më̆ʦᵘ̈ f. the earth round a cooking-place or the like, which is burnt and scorched by the heat. -nūn m. a kind of salt found in the hill tracts, mixed up with sand, and in colour like burnt earth. It is acrid in taste.

m. (sg. dat. ḍākhas), wiping out or devastation of a house or village, from epidemic disease or the like; utter destruction, wiping out of a country, a people, or the like (Rām. 783). ḍökhⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to be wiped out as ab.; (of anything collected in a heap) to be dissipated, scattered abroad.
m., i.q. ḍakh 1, q.v., a support, prop (K.Pr. 254, Śiv. 443). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain as a support or prop; to assist, become a helper. --thawun -- m.inf. to put a support, prop, etc.
adj. c.g. one who wears the curling lock of hair called ḍakh, q.v., curly-headed (Gr.Gr. 133).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ḍakhanôwᵘ), i.q. ḍạkhᵃrun, q.v. (H. xi, 16).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ḍakhowᵘ), to lean upon (e.g. on a stick or crutch, or against a wall). ḍakhowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ḍakhüwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), used as a support as ab.
f. a crutch, lame man's stick, or the like.
f. a pole on which the flap- roof of a boat or tent is raised and supported.
dakhun m. the South (El.). Cf. dachyunᵘ 1 and dakshin.

m. entrance, access; entering (upon), taking possession (of), possession, occupation; reach, grasp, comprehension; influence, power, authority; esp. possession by a spirit, demoniacal possession, convulsions of children; a fit of childish terror leading to convulsive attacks. --karun -- m.inf. to throw (a child) into convulsions, to terrify it. --kāsun -- m.inf. to exorcise a demon in possession of a child, to repeat charms, etc., over a child in convulsions; --gatshun -- m.inf. demoniacal possession to occur, convulsions to come on in the case of a child, to be terrified (of a child).
f. (sg. dat. ḍạkhᵃrüñᵃ), employment of a prop., i.e. using a stick, alpenstock, or crutch, when going is difficult.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ḍạkhᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. ḍạkhᵃrun, q.v. ḍạkhᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. ḍạkhᵃröwᵃ -mᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), i.q. ḍạkhᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, see ḍạkhᵃrun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ḍạkhᵒrᵒ), to lean upon (e.g. a stick, crutch, or the like); to depend upon; lūrᵘ̈ ḍakhᵃrith pakun, to walk leaning upon a stick (Gr.M.). ḍạkhᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. ḍạkhᵘ̈rᵘ̈-muʦᵘ̈), used as a stick, crutch, etc.
f. the habit of walking about like a hunchback, a doubled-up gait, hobbling along. Cf. ḍọ̆kᵘ and ḍŏkurᵘ-ḍŏkurᵘ.
adj. c.g. roofed, possessing a reed-mat roof (of a house, boat, or the like). Cf. ḍokhᵘ 2.
adj. c.g. a well-to-do householder with a large family and numerous relations.
or dakshĕ prazāpath m. Dakṣa, N. of a famous Hindū āditya or demigod, father of Umā and father-in-law of Śiva (Śiv. 33, 65, 76, 78, 124, 317, 321).
adj. southern (Śiv. 661); subst.m. the south (Śiv. 1412, 1589, Rām. 632). The south is supposed to be the home of Dakṣa (see daksh), hence a double meaning in Śiv. 661. Cf. dakhin and dachyunᵘ.
f. a fee or present paid to a Hindū officiating priest or to a teacher (Śiv. 707, Rām. 612), i.q. dachin, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ḍokᵘ, 2 p.p. ḍacyōv), to drink with a gulping noise, to gulp down a drink greedily. ḍokᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ḍücᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), drunk with loud gulps, drunk greedily.

m. (sg. dat. ḍākaras), a belch, eructation (K.Pr. 124, ḍākar). --khasun -- m.inf. belching to rise, eructation to take place (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to belch, eructate. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. belching to come, eructation to take place.

m. (sg. dat. ḍākaras), the smell of chopped or pounded radishes, potatoes, or the like, which arises from a mixed stew of vegetables and meal. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. such a smell to arise, esp. of the smell from stale food after meal-time.
f. a kind of basket, round, wide, and shallow, for holding vegetables, flowers, fruit, or the like (El. ḍákir).
f. rising ground on a road, a hill on a road. Cf. ḍȧkⁱ.
f. a hilly part of a mountain path. Cf. ḍakᵘ̈rᵘ̈.

f. split pea or pulse, used for food; the cooked porridge made from it. The best dāl is said to come from Khampur (El.). --galüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the dāl to become soft (in boiling); hence, to have an advantage, to avail; to succeed; to keep in (with), get on (with); to persuade by any means, to persuade by some means or other, to use every effort in persuasion. --paküñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the dāl to start going (through one's body); met. (of a person of cowardly disposition) to lose courage and gradually to become utterly helpless in mind and body on the receipt of bad news, real or imaginary. --ʦalüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the dāl to run away (through one's body); met. to lose one's presence of mind immediately on hearing of some terrifying news. --vĕsarañ -- f. the dāl becoming ruined (inside one); met. sudden loss of presence of mind on hearing terrifying news. ¶ dāli-baṭa m. a brāhmaṇ for porridge, a stupid lout of a brāhmaṇ, only good at eating, and with no learning. -ḍṻs m. a cudgel for porridge; met. a helpless lout, good at nothing but eating. --dĕv -- m. (f. --dĕviñ --), one who is helpless and effortless.
f. a shield (K. 447); a kind of seat offered to honoured guests (Śiv. 968).
m. a group, collection. Cf. nāḍi-dal, p. 622b, l. 5.

or ḍal 2 (q.v.) m. (sg. abl. dala 1), a young and tender leaf or shoot (Śiv. 1805, 1841); the petal of a flower; a company, party, or body (of men united together for a common object). -bādal m. obstinately upholding one's own opinion, without advancing proofs, but in emulation or rivalry with the opposing party; party spirit, party enmity, obstinate partizanship. -nĕnd f. the fourth or last weeding of a rice-field (L. 463).

m. a lake (Śiv. 1805, 1810); N. of a large lake near Śrīnagar (see El. s.v. and RT. Tr. II, 416; Śiv. 1823, 1841). -ḍuḍa m. 'a Ḍal-sponger', a man who is in the habit of following picnic parties on the Ḍal lake, and joins them as an uninvited guest; cf. ḍuḍa. --darwāza -- m. the Ḍal gate, the flood-gate of the Ḍal lake. When the Jihlam (or Vĕth) is low, the gates remain open; but when the river rises to a certain height, they automatically close, thus preventing inundation of the land round the lake (K.Pr. 245). -khögⁱ m. a special kind of boatman on the Ḍal lake, who attends to the cultivation of the famous floating islands thereon. -khöhⁱ m. 'a Ḍal-picnicker', one who wastes his money by continually spending his time in boats on the Ḍal lake. -masāla m. a certain sweetmeat made of beans flavoured with the shoots and pollen of the pë̆ʦᵘ̈ (see the next). -nābad m. lake-candy, a kind of sweetmeat made of the pollen of the pë̆ʦᵘ̈ (q.v.) or reed-mace (Typha sp.) which grows in lakes (L. 72, dal nabád).

m. (sg. abl. dala 2), pounding (e.g. grain in a mortar), husking (Gr.Gr. 124). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to pound paddy, etc., to husk grain; met. to discuss (a subject) thoroughly, to criticize minutely. dala-draka nērun m.inf. to pass through difficulties or trials, etc., and to come out strong at the end, to pass through cleansing fires. dala koḍᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (for 2 see dala 3) (f. dala küḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), husked (of grain). dala kaḍun 1 m.inf. (for 2 see dala 3), to pull off (husk) by pounding, to husk grain in a mortar. ¶ dalas hyonᵘ m.inf. to take for a pounding; hence, met. to bring a person up before one in order to reproach or revile him, to call up for a scolding.
m. a young leaf, a leaflet, i.q. dal 1, q.v. (Śiv. 1741).
f. looseness, laxity; (of the mind, etc.) unsteadiness, depression (K. 1167). Cf. ḍalun 1.

m. a sheepskin, goatskin, or skin of a similar animal, esp. an entire skin. --bạrᵃg -- m. a patch of leather (such as would be used for patching a shoe or the like). --koḍᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --küdᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), having the skin torn off; met. (of a road, village, place, etc.) thoroughly and energetically searched through and through for something concealed. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to tear off the skin; met. (to tear the skin of a road, etc.) to search anxiously everywhere for something. -khünḍᵘ̈ f. a piece of sheep- or goatskin, esp. a thick piece. -ʦakul m. a large round piece of sheep- or goat-leather.

f. (pl. nom. ḍāla, or, Śiv. 660, 1324 m.c., ḍālay), a heedless, lilting gait, the unsteady, heedless, or coquettish gait of a maid in love (Śiv. 660, 1680); (of someone sent or deputed) going along heedlessly, negligently, or in contempt of orders; disdain, indifference, contempt, disregard. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of someone dispatched on some errand or business) to start in a negligent way, to set out displaying contempt or disregard for the orders; to show contempt for, disregard (Śiv. 274, 1324, 1693).

m. (for 1 and 2 see dal 1 and 2), a pimp, a pander; cf. buḍa. The f. is dülᵘ̈, q.v. --bāpār -- m. the conduct of a pimp or pander; conduct like that of a pimp. --drāmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --drāmüʦᵘ̈ --), issued from a pimp; met. (of a boy or girl) one who by the practice of impertinence has become rude and headstrong, cheeky. --koḍᵘ-motᵘ 2 -- perf. part. (for 1 see dal 2; f. --küḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), extracted from a pimp; met. (of a boy or girl) brought up to be impudent and headstrong. --kaḍun 2 -- m.inf. (for 1 see dal 2), to draw out from a pimp; met. to teach to be impudent and headstrong. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), the son of a pimp. --nērun -- m.inf. to issue from a pimp; met. (of a boy or girl) by practising impertinent conduct, to acquire an insolent and arrogant behaviour.
f. the profession of a pimp or bawd; mode of life like that of a pimp or bawd.
m. a winnowing sieve or basket; the act of winnowing with such a sieve.
(cf. دالان) m. a hall (Gr.M., Śiv. 968); a covered balcony; a covered bridge or way connecting the upper stories of two houses.
m. the act of joining together the ceiling of flat boards over a room. --tārun -- m.inf. to fix the ceiling-boards, etc. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf., id.
adj. (f. ḍalawüñᵘ̈), that which moves or can be moved from one place to another, insecure, loosened from its position.
adj. (f. ḍalawüñᵘ̈), that which is being spoilt or marred, under- going a process of deterioration.
m. a frozen road, esp. a muddy road frozen rough and hard.
m. form, appearance, carriage of a person, esp. such a manner of holding oneself as to indicate the possession of high qualities.
m. (sg. dat. dalēṭas), the messenger of a court, a sheriff's officer, policeman sent to arrest.
f. indication, evidence, argument, proof, demonstration (Gr.M.); a story, narrative (Śiv. 869, 872, with suff. of indef. art. dalīlā, H. viii, 6, or dalīlāh).
f. husking (of grain, etc.), decortication. Cf. dalyunᵘ.
f. a passing over (Gr.Gr. 120); a slope, a sloping road, i.e. one which does not rise abruptly.
adj. c.g. inattentive, one who, though he hears, sees, and understands, acts as if he does not hear, see, or understand, a fool (Śiv. 1813).
m. the noise made by a number of children quarrelling among themselves.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dolᵘ 3, f. düjᵘ̈ 5; for dolᵘ 1 and 2 see s.v., for düjᵘ̈ 1 see dọ̆jᵘ, for 2 see s.v., 3 see dagun 2, for 4 see dolᵘ 1), to skin, decorticate (a tree, post, or the like); to husk (grain), shred (e.g. ginger in a mortar); to plane or smoothe (e.g. a carpenter planing a board). Cf. adolᵘ. ¶ dalana āmotᵘ perf. part. pass. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), that which has become decorticated; become husked. --yunᵘ -- m. inf. pass. to become decorticated; to become husked. ¶ dolᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. düjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), decorticated; husked.

conj. 2 (pres. part. ḍalān, Śiv. 765, or ḍalan, Śiv. 910, 986, m.c.; 1 p.p. ḍolᵘ, 2 p.p. ḍajyōv), to be displaced, moved from one place to another (Śiv. 1569, 1800); to be spread abroad, diffused (of scent, K. 924; of sweat bursting forth, see guma); to pass off, pass over, pass beyond, pass by or away (Gr.Gr. xxxii; governs abl. of thing passed over, Śiv. 1539, K. 1095); to walk about (El.); to slip, stumble (Gr.Gr. 5, Siv. 1743); to be moved, agitated, distraught (Śiv. 741, 765, 910, 986; Rām. 682, 1052, 1057, 1198; K. 1156, 1157). ¶ ḍolᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. ḍüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), removed from one place to another; passed over, changed; in a changed condition (Śiv. 1282).

conj. 1 (1 p.p.ḍôlᵘ, 2. p.p. ḍājyōv), to move (a thing) from one place to another, remove (a thing) (Śiv. 1055, 1249); to cause to pass over, to cause to pass by or away (Gr.Gr. 175); (with atha, q.v. for special significations) to pass the hand over anything, to smoothe (K.Pr. 93, ḍolamut for ḍôlᵘ-motᵘ), to pat, touch affectionately (Śiv. 423, K. 682, 1148). ¶ ḍölith thawun 1 m.inf. (for 2 see ḍālun 3), to remove a thing and put it somewhere else, esp. with intent to deceive.
conj. 2 (1 p.p.ḍolᵘ, 2 p.p. ḍajyōv), to go wrong, be spoiled (lit. and met.). ¶ ḍolᵘ-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (fem. ḍüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), spoiled, etc. (YZ. 204).
conj. 1 (1p.p. ḍôlᵘ, 2 p.p. ḍājyōv), to mar, spoil.

conj. 1 (1 p.p.ḍôlᵘ, 2 p.p. ḍājyōv), to sift, winnow. Cf. adôlᵘ. ḍölⁱ ḍölⁱ thawun m.inf. to winnow gradually and put by (of a large quantity of grain), to winnow bit by bit. ¶ ḍölith thawun 2 m.inf. (for 1 see ḍālun 1), to winnow.
conj. 1 (1 p.p.ḍôlᵘ, 2 p.p. ḍājyōv), to throw, fling, cast, hurl (Śiv. 1644); to apply, put into use, wield (e.g. a pen, Śiv. 1912).
f. a sieve; a winnowing basket, a winnowing scoop.
m. one who acts like a pimp (dala); an evil, mean fellow, one whose character is marked by covetousness, bad conduct, bad temper, and treachery.
conj. 3, to pull a person's character to pieces behind his back, to talk scandal about, to backbite. Cf. dal 2.
m. backbiting, talking scandal; biyⁱ-sondⁱ dalwā̃zuvᵘ karun, to talk scandal about another (K.Pr. 165).
adj. (f. ḍalwüñᵘ̈), that which is easily movable from one place to another, unstable, unsteady.
(? spelling), adj. c.g. unfortunate (El.). Cf. drölid.
m. (sg. dat. dalinis), husking (of grain, etc.), shredding; splitting, cleaving (timber, etc.); decortication. Cf. daliñ.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. dạlᵃrôwᵃ), to mislead, delude (El.).

m. (sg. abl. dama 1; pl. dat. daman 1, spelt damn in K.Pr. 46; for daman 2 see s.v.; for 3, 4 see damun 1, 2; with suff. of indef. art. damāh q.v., s.v.), breath, vital air, life, the breath of life (K.Pr. 67, Rām. 15, 17); breath or blast (of a furnace or oven); stewing or simmering over a slow fire, braising; a moment, an instant (YZ. 1, 216, Śiv. 1330, Rām. 898, 1103); suppression of the breath (as a Hindū religious exercise) (Śiv. 1017, with pun on dam 3); a sensation of oppressive heat in a hot closed room, or in the hot season from want of air or ventilation; a full supply of the necessaries of life, the life of a well-to-do person (K.Pr. 47); plunging, diving down to the bottom of the water when bathing (Śiv. 1811, 1841, 1871). Cf. damī. --anun -- m.inf. distress caused by an obstruction of the breath to arise; (in cooking) to simmer or be stewed in a tightly covered vessel (so that the dam or steam cannot escape) over a slow fire, to be braised. -dilāsa دم دلاسا m. consolation (Rām. 1726). --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to give suppressions of breath, to practise the suppression of the breath (as a religious exercise). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give breath; to give time; to console (K. 65, 859); to rest, take a temporary relaxation (of a person engaged in any heavy work overtaxing his strength); to dive (Śiv. 1811, 1841, 1871); to boast (K.Pr. 153, W. 122). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. the breath to go; breathless from wrath to occur, to lose one's breath from rage, to be struck dumb with anger; breathlessness to occur from oppressive heat and want of ventilation. --hĕth bihun -- m.inf. to take breath and sit; when a number of persons are at work on a thing, one of them to sit doing nothing, to take a rest, sit out. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take breath; (in company) to sit apart and silently, to be morose in company. -jādā adj. c.g. breathless (El.). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to draw breath, to take a temporary relaxation in the course of a heavy work. --khārun -- m.inf. to cause breath to rise, to breathe out, exhale (Śiv. 1017); to expel breath preparatory to uttering a sound (Śiv. 1845). Cf. dam wālun bel. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat one's breath; (in wordy warfare) to remain silent, to be beaten in abuse and left without reply; (in cooking) to be dressed over a slow fire (as a stew, etc.), to be braised. --karun -- m.inf. to make a breath, to await, wait a short time, pause in any work. -phacĕr m. bursting of the breath; to suffer from some private sorrow or vexation which cannot be divulged. --phȧṭⁱ gaʦhun -- m.inf. the breath to burst; to suffer from some private vexation which one is unable to divulge (as if he were not able to breathe it out or to cry out). --phȧṭⁱ karun -- m.inf. to cause a person to suffer from such a private vexation. --pakun -- m.inf. the life to go along; there to be a full supply of all the comforts and necessaries of life. -pŏkta (= دم پخت) m. a stew or soup cooked in a pot the mouth of which is hermetically closed with paste, etc. --rōzun -- m.inf. life to be carried on somehow, when there is not a full supply of necessaries. --sambālun -- m.inf. to arrange one's breath, to become steadied in mind, be calmed (Śiv. 1256, Rām. 1353, 1358). --wālun -- m.inf. to cause breath to descend, to breathe in, inhale (Śiv. 1017). Cf. dam khārun ab. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. simmering to come; to become fully braised or simmered. ¶ dama anun m.inf. to simmer or braise food in a covered vessel over a slow fire. --dama -- adv. at every breath, at every moment, continually (Śiv. 156, 315, 1017, 1404). -kuṭhᵘ m. a room which is hot for want of ventilation. -kūṭhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a small room or closet which is always hot or warm owing to want of ventilation. -katürᵘ̈ f. a diving game; potsherds or bits of metal are thrown into water, for which the competitors (usually children) dive. ¶ daman-manz adv. in moments; at every moment, in an instant (Śiv. 829). ¶ damiy adv. in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye (Śiv. 325, 326). Cf. damī.
m. any quadruped that is not rapacious, hence cattle. ¶ dömⁱ raz f. a rope for tying a cow, etc., a cattle-halter.
m. (sg. abl. dama 2), deceit, fraud, trickery; coaxing, wheedling. - bôbᵘ m. a cheat who teaches others to cheat.

m. (with suff. of indef. art. dāmāh, Śiv. 1006, or dāmā, Śiv. 1434), drinking by suction (e.g. from the breast) (K. 109, 110); supping (as contrasted with putting liquid into the mouth with a spoon, or drinking from a cup) (Śiv. 1109, Rām. 1035, 1522); (with cyonᵘ, to drink) (to drink) a sup, (to take) a sip (Śiv. 1006, 1434, 1786); damā or dāmāh, see ab., a single sip. Cf. añĕma and dŏd. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to drink gradually by suction, to suck, sup (as when one is not very thirsty) (K.Pr. 12); to suck (the breast) (Śiv. 1387, 1464). --ganḍun -- m.inf. to suck or sup down in large quantities at each gulp (as in extreme thirst). --lagun -- m.inf. to be used up (like water drunk by a thirsty person), to be all expended (as grain or money previously amassed). ¶ dāma cyonᵘ m.inf. to drink by suction, to suck up, sup. --dāma -- adv. (drinking) by sips (Śiv. 1380).

m. (sg. abl. dama 3), restraint (as in Śiv. 1017, sŏra-dama, by restraining sound, i.e. by remaining silent, with pun on dam 1); self-restraint, in this sense often compounded with shĕm, tranquillity, shĕm-dam, tranquillity and self-restraint (Śiv. 269, 931, 1033, 1404, 1754, 1811).
m. a snare, trap, gin (YZ. 17, where it is possibly confounded with the Hindī dām, a fetter).
m. a dwelling-place, house, abode, in param-dām, the supreme abode, heaven (Śiv. 1659).
m. (for 1, 2, and 3 see dam 1, 2, and 3), the edge, thick flap, or border of the padded cap worn in cold weather.
m. a pair of bellows, cf. daman; asthma (W. 3).
m. a son-in-law, a daughter's husband or betrothed (among Musalmāns) (L. 267).
adj. c.g. possessing a padded edge or flap (of a cap or the like, for use in cold weather). Cf. dama 4.
f. the cross-bar across a window or doorway, on which one can lean the arms when sitting close to it, a window-sill.
= dam 1 with the suff. of the indef. art. a moment; as adv. (wait, etc.) for a moment (YZ. 1, Śiv. 450). Cf. damī, which is the Persian form of the word.
m. a large kind of drum with parchment at each end (not like a kettle-drum) (K. 1009).

m. a skirt, tail, hem, border (Rām. 1305), i.q. dāmāna. --raṭun -- m.inf. to seize a person's skirt; met. to implore (Śiv. 179). Cf. dāmāna raṭun. --waṭun -- m.inf. to twist up the skirt, to fold up or lift up one's skirt (so as to save it from mud or from being torn by brambles, etc.) (Śiv. 1568).
f. (for 1 see dam 1; for 3, 4, see damun 1, 2; sg. dat. damüñᵘ̈), a bad smell, esp. the bad smell of stale curd or other food turned sour and gone bad.

m. a skirt, a hem, i.q. dāman, q.v. --chalun -- m.inf. to make a false accusation. -palav m. the torn edge or skirt of a garment. --raṭun -- m.inf. to seize by the skirt; met. to implore, beseech (Śiv. 1732). Cf. dāman raṭun. ¶ dāmānas mīṭhⁱ dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to give kisses to the skirt, to kiss the hem of (a person's) garment, to show great humility (Śiv. 1150).
adj. c.g. skirted, having an embroidered skirt or border (of a garment).
f. the act of seizing the skirt, making an entreaty; esp. asking in marriage, proposals for marriage made by the relations of the bridegroom to those of the bride or vice versa.
adj. c.g. foul-smelling, corrupt-smelling (of sour milk or the like gone bad).
f. a woman's veil or mantle; a certain ornament worn on the forehead.
m. the name given in schools to the syllable ddhaṁ, the final syllable of ēkaṁ siddhaṁ, the first words put down before writing the alphabet.

m. the womb, uterus (of women or lower animals); the inner part or inside (of a dish or vessel); the core or centre of a post, pillar, or the like; core, centre generally; a certain aquatic vegetable (K.Pr. 149, also ḍumb). --lagun -- m. to conceive, become with child, become pregnant.
adj. (f. ḍambiñᵘ̈), i.q. ḍambyukᵘ, q.v. under ḍọ̆mbᵘ.
m. the cold experienced at the time of snowfall, great cold. -khāna m. a very cold place, e.g. a very high mountain site.

m. a long kind of drum beaten at both ends (W. 3). Cf. ḍum-ḍum. ḍam-ḍam wāyun m.inf. to beat such a drum; hence, to proclaim by beat of drum. ḍam-ḍam wāyĕnwôlᵘ n.ag. (f. ḍam-ḍam wāyĕnwājeñ), a drummer.
or damāh دما adv. (at) a moment (lit. one moment), cf. damiy, s.v. dam 1. damī... damī دمی... دمی adv. at one moment... at another moment, at one time... at another time (K.Pr. 47).

f. a piece of the stomach of a sheep or the like, as sold by butchers, sheep's paunch (K.Pr. 55); the stomach (El.). ḍamiñĕ-kalapushᵘ m. the entire stomach of a sheep, etc., a whole sheep's paunch, as sold by butchers. Cf. ḍȧmbⁱ-kalapushⁱ under ḍọ̆mbᵘ. ḍamiñĕ-māwas  m. a certain festival held on the day of the new moon of the month of Phāgun (February-March), on the night of which pieces of sheep's paunch are offered by Hindūs to Bhairavas or Böravs.
m. having a rope round the waist, N. of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) (Śiv. 1334).

f. stamping the feet on the ground, a stamp (K.Pr. 202); a religious exercise, ecstatic and frenzied dancing at the shrine of a saint (L. 289, 459). ¶ damāli-phakīr m. a bullying mendicant faqīr, one who, when his wishes are not granted, stamps violently on the ground (K.Pr. 10).
m. a drummer, one whose business it is to make proclamation by beat of drum.

conj. 1 (pres. part. damān, or, Śiv. 1854, daman 3; 1 p.p. domᵘ), to blow up a fire (with bellows or the mouth); as vb. impers. in past tenses (past domun), to roar (of wind or a blast of air on fire) (Gr.Gr. xxxviii); to roar (as a wild beast) (Śiv. 1854). domᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. dümᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), blown up (with bellows or by the mouth, of fire).

m. (sg. dat. damanas), a pair of bellows (K.Pr. 46). For daman 1 see dam 1, for 2 see s.v., for 3 see damun 1, for 4 see bel. ¶ daman-basta f. the leather bag, alternately inflated with and emptied of air, used as the body of a bellows (K.Pr. 46). -nôrᵘ m. the metal nozzle or pipe of a pair of bellows.
f. the water-vessel for the hubble-bubble or huqqa.
f. insistence, vehement desire, exhibited by stamping the feet on the ground. Cf. damölⁱ. damᵃla-hamal karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to show or practise vehement insistence. damᵃla-hamal lāgüñᵘ̈ f.inf., id.
(? = دمیدہ) m. a kind of sweetmeat, ginger-candy. -khünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -khanjĕ), a lump of ginger-candy.
m. the hilt or handle of a sword; a handle (El.) (of a hammer, see dŏkurᵘ); the handle of a drawer (Gr.M.).

m. an earthen fire-place, esp. one with orifices for cooking, a cooking-stove, oven (Gr.Gr. 10, El., K.Pr. 25, 85, 101, 134, 164, 171, 255, W. 144, K. 161). --karun -- m.inf. to make a cooking-stove, to build a temporary mud fire-place; hence, to stop on the road (on a journey) for cooking food (K.Pr. 87). ¶ dāna-büṭhᵘ̈ f. the fire-place of a cooking-stove; i.e. the middle portion of the flat top of a cooking-stove, on which vessels are placed on removal from the open fire. -ḍākh m. (sg. dat. -ḍākas), the plastered earth on the top of a stove, burnt red by the heat. -dĕv m. a cooking-stove demon; a kind of demon, ever gorging himself with food, and having the form of a cooking-stove. -gȧjⁱ or -güjᵘ̈ f. the stokehole near the bottom of a cooking-stove, through which it is fed with fuel. -golᵘ 1 m. (for dānagolᵘ 2 see s.v.), the opening of such a stokehole. -gorᵘ m. (f. -gürᵘ̈), a man who is skilled in making cooking-stoves, one whose profession is to build such. -mīr m. a fire-place prince, a big fire-place, a large cooking-stove (K.Pr. 48). -ʦôrᵘ m. the openings on the top of a stove on which vessels are put for the purpose of cooking. -zang f. offerings made for good luck when a cooking-stove is lit for the first time.

m. (properly) a bow (the weapon), but for this the usual word is danŏrdanḍ, q.v.; this word usually indicates Sagittarius, the sign of the zodiac (Rām. 1259, 1261, 1275, K. 132). -lạgᵃn m. a certain astronomical period, the first six ghaṛis or periods of twenty minutes commencing with the rising of Sagittarius. -rāsh f. the sign Sagittarius.

m. a gift, a present; esp. a gift in charity or for pious purposes (Śiv. 1148, Rām. 73, 390, etc.). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give charity (K.Pr. 47, Śiv. 428). --karun -- m.inf. to give charity (Gr.M.). ¶ dāna-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), wanting in charitable gifts, one who does not give in charity (Śiv. 1738).
m. prosperity, good luck, used in the following: dan-bāgĕ m. praising for benefits received, thanks; good luck, good fortune (Śiv. 494, 821).

(? spelling), the Indian chestnut, Ӕsculus indica (L. 70). It is lopped to provide cattle fodder for the winter. On p. 75 L. calls this hunak dun, and states that as a medicine it has cathartic properties. Cf. ḍūnᵘ and hānakh-ḍūnᵘ.

m. a tooth, used for dand, q.v., in the following: -dag f. toothache. -dawāh m. medicine for a tooth, a cure for toothache. -ṭakar m.pl. chattering of the teeth (from ague, cold, or the like). Cf. dand-ṭakar and ḍanṭakar. -ṭakar aʦȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. an attack of chattering of the teeth to come on. --ṭuwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to close the teeth; met. to speak slowly and deliberately in order to avoid dealing with the relevant matter of a conversation. Cf. dand ṭuwȧnⁱ. ¶ dȧnⁱ-tⁱj or dȧnⁱ-tujⁱ a toothpick. Cf. dȧndⁱ-tⁱj under dand.
(? dönᵘ̈) in dān chö̃ch, f. the blackberry, Rubus fruticosus (L. 73, dhán chánch). Cf. chö̃ch and dönᵘ̈.
m. the stalk of an apple or pear (El.). Cf. dan 1. -kāḍ m. a mixture of refuse husks, stalks, etc., of vegetables, etc.
f. (sg. dat. döñᵘ̈), a stream (of water or the like, as poured from, or into, a vessel) (noted only in L.V. 39, 40).

m. grain, corn (K. 1088); a grain, seed (Śiv. 468, of a pomegranate; Rām. 1029, 1126); chick-pea, 'gram' (used for feeding horses) (K.Pr. 71); food generally (K.Pr. 100); a speck, a tiny quantity of anything (Rām. 700); a bead; a drop; a pimple, pustule; --˚ seed of such and such a plant. According to El. s.v. the word also means 'steel'. --dāna -- adv. grain by grain, drop by drop (Rām. 168, 286, 698, 1419). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give 'gram' to a horse, to feed a horse. --dyutᵘ-motᵘ -- m. fed, given 'gram' (of a horse); met. reaping the fruits of former actions done in this or a previous birth, these actions being represented as seeds from which spring the results. -lë̆dᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the root of a certain medicinal plant, Berberis sp., which root is good for horses (L. 76, spelt dand-lidar).
adj. c.g. and subst. m. wise, learned, clever (W. 22); a wise man, a sage (K.Pr. 47). In Matt. xi, 25, the pl. dat. is written dānahan دانہن.

m. wealth, riches, property (Śiv. 365, 861, 893, 952, 1067, etc.; Rām. 1123); money, treasure, cash; fortune (El. danna; K.Pr. 48; K.Pr. 260 and W. 149 have dan, so also Śiv. 1059). -boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), great in wealth, very wealthy, a leader of society, a millionaire. -bôgᵘ m. a share of wealth, esp. a share of movable property under division. -bögᵃran f. (sg. dat. -bögᵃrüñᵃ), division of joint wealth amongst a number of claimants, esp.when the amount of shares is mutually agreed upon, sharing out. --bögᵃrun -- m.inf. to share out joint property, to divide property into shares mutually agreed upon. -bāgay f. division of property, esp. of joint family property. -bajĕr m. greatness of wealth, wealthiness. -böjⁱbaṭh f. (sg. dat. -böjⁱbaṭi), partnership in business. -böjᵃran f. (sg. dat. -böjᵃrüñᵃ), division of joint property, dividing into shares. --böjᵃrun -- m.inf. to divide joint property into shares. -dōlath (dana m., dōlath f.), wealth and riches (Śiv. 579). -ḍanḍ m. a punishment in money, pecuniary punishment, a fine. -dyār m.pl. wealth and possessions, property. -kāḍay f. wasteful expenditure, extravagance, throwing one's wealth to the dogs. -mad m. arrogance of wealth, purse-pride. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. a lump of wealth, a collected store of money, esp. a hidden store. -mȧstī f. purse-pride, arrogance from the possession of great wealth. -masth adj. c.g. (as subst., m. sg. dat. -mastas), arrogant from the possession of great wealth, purse-proud. -pana m. one's whole property, including money, goods, and clothes, means of life (Śiv. 1039). -pana lagun m.inf. to become dependent on another for one's means of life. -röchⁱ 1 m. a treasure-guard, one who is appointed to take care of treasure. -röchⁱ 2 f. the guardianship of treasure. -rôchᵘ m. (f. -röchᵘ̈), a treasure-guard. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without wealth, penniless, poor. -raʦhar m. the condition of being penniless, destitution. -shĕr m. such intense desire for money that the wisher becomes thin and meagre, money-greed, avarice. -sörᵘ̈ f. gradually removing money from a store, bit by bit, either by the owner or (generally) in peculation. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦᵘ̈), possessing wealth, wealthy, rich (Rām. 1259). -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), rich in wealth, one who has earned and saved much money, wealthy. -sāvĕr m. wealthiness. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is wealthy, rich (El.). -wöshrawan m. N. of Kubēra, the god of wealth and Guardian of the North. He was son of Viśravas and step-brother of Rāvaṇa (Rām. 637). -vĕʦar m. the condition of being completely supplied with wealth, wealthiness. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), one who is completely supplied with wealth. -zōr m. power of wealth, strength consisting in wealth; strength of body due to the possession of plenty of the necessaries of life. ¶ dȧnⁱ-pȧnⁱ adv. including all one's possessions, u.w. vbs. signifying loss (of property), becoming subject to another, and so on.

m. a kind of club used in a certain game, in which one club is thrown on the ground and struck with another so as to propel it beyond a boundary-line. -kinⁱ phirun m.inf. to retort, advance arguments on the other side. ¶ danan gindun m.inf. to play the ab. game.
adj. c.g. granulated; of a granulated appearance; containing grain; bearing fruit in the form of seeds enclosed in a capsule or husk (e.g. a pomegranate).
m. (for 1 see dān 1), N. of a place about 60 miles north of Śrīnagar, the entrance to the Śāradā-kṣētra, or tract made holy by the shrine of the goddess Śāradā. (Cf. RT.Tr. II, 279 ff.)
f. any long and difficult business, esp. when it is of no value or useless.
m. a certain kind of demon, the Dānava of Sanskrit literature (Śiv. 704).
f. a tax paid by possessors of sheep, a sheep-tax (L. 464).

or ḍanḍ m. (sg. abl. danḍa 1 or ḍanḍa 1), punishment, chastisement, imprisonment, fine (K.Pr. 106, ḍanḍ), corporal punishment, etc.; divine punishment for sin (Śiv. 1912). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to punish, to fine (Gr.M.); to pay a fine (Gr.M.). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take a fine, to fine a person. --karun -- m.inf. to punish (Śiv. 1481, to mutilate). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. a fine to fall, a fine or punishment to be incurred; ʦĕ pĕyiy danḍ, you will be punished (Gr.M.). ¶ danḍa 1 (ḍanḍa) barun  m.inf. to give compensation for harm, damage, loss, or the like occurring to anything borrowed or taken in deposit. --baray -- f. the payment of such compensation. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give compensation for loss of or damage as ab. (H. v, 11). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take in compensation as ab. (H. v, 11). --khārun -- m.inf. to make a claim for compensation as ab. --khasun -- m.inf. to have a claim for such compensation made against one.

m. a tooth (of man or beast) (K.Pr. 48, 255; YZ. 75, 213; Śiv. 52, 126; Rām. 631, 929); the tusk of an elephant (Śiv. 13). --bĕhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the teeth to sit (against each other), i.e. to be silent; hence, (of one hitherto impudent and free of speech, but now silent) to be conquered or tyrannized over and to remain subdued and silent, passively to suffer tyranny. --bĕhanāwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to reduce to dumbness, to conquer, to subdue (one who has heretofore been impudent and free of speech). --hāwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to show the teeth; to show one's old age; met. (of clothes, vessels, etc.) to show signs of being worn out. --lōsȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. or danda-māla lōsañĕ f. pl. inf. the teeth to become weary, to thank a person with excessive pæans of gratitude. -ṭakar, dan-ṭakar (see dan 4), or ḍanṭakar m.pl. chattering of the teeth (from cold, ague, or the like). --ṭuwȧnⁱ -- or dan ṭuwȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to close the teeth; met. to speak slowly and deliberately, in order to avoid dealing with the relevant matter of a conversation. Cf. dan ṭuwȧnⁱ under dan 4. --wahārȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to spread out the teeth, to laugh even when some improper action is pointed out. ¶ danda-bürᵘ̈ f. a gap between two teeth. -baran f. (sg. dat. -barüñᵘ̈), a gap between two teeth, esp. when wide. -dag or dandag f. pain in the tooth, toothache. -gūjⁱ, -gūjᵘ̈, dȧndⁱ-gūjⁱ, or dȧndⁱ-gūjⁱ f. a certain powdered dainty distributed to the relations on the third and fourth days after the birth of a child, composed of sesame, etc., fried in ghī, and flavoured with various medicaments. -gūrᵘ̈ f. a gum, the flesh of the gums. -holᵘ adj.(f. -hüjᵘ̈), crooked-toothed. -khŏkhurᵘ adj. (f. -khŏkürᵘ̈), gap-toothed, one who has lost teeth, and shows it. -khilāl m. an ornamented toothpick of gold, silver, or the like. -khambyulᵘ m. a space, interval, or gap between the teeth, from the loss of a tooth or other cause. -khamijᵘ̈ f., id. -khamyulᵘ m., id. -khārĕ f.pl. the sockets of the teeth, the gums. -khraph f. (sg. dat. -khrapi), a wide gap between teeth. -khrapal adj. c.g. one who has wide gaps between his teeth, owing to loss of teeth, or naturally. -khörish f. a disease of the teeth, accompanied by irritation of the gums. -khŏsorᵘ m. a broken-off piece of the tartar of the teeth. -khāv m. a disease of the teeth, in which the teeth fall out; a worm supposed to injure the teeth. -khāv pyonᵘ m.inf. an attack of such worms to occur, caries of the teeth to come on. -khay f. tartar of the teeth; a disease of the teeth due to not keeping them clean; foul teeth. -khöyin m. a disease of the teeth, toothache arising from accumulation of tartar. -khözᵘ̈ f., id. -mal m. dirt of the teeth, esp. accumulated tartar. -mal-wāy m. tooth-tartar rheumatism, a disease of the teeth said to affect the phlegmatic humour. -māl f. a row of teeth, all the teeth of the upper or of the lower jaw. -māla lōsañe f. pl. inf., i.q. dand- lōsȧnⁱ ab. -phȧlⁱ m.pl. tooth-pearls, teeth (i.e. a set of teeth) small and elegant in shape. -pīrᵘ̈ f. a big tooth, one of the grinders. -tujⁱ f. a toothpick (K.Pr. 132), see dȧndⁱ-tⁱj bel. -wŏgunᵘ adj. (f. -wŏgüñᵘ̈), shallow-toothed, one who possesses short thick-set teeth. -wôlᵘ m. a spike with a bent point, used as an instrument for extracting teeth; met. a tool for extracting anything by its roots from its position inside anything else. -woṭᵘ m. a tooth-bunch, a row of teeth from back to front. -wāv m. an instrument for sharpening the teeth of a saw or the like. wôvᵘ̈ f. general pain of all the teeth, dental neuralgia. -zôlᵘ m. a tooth-joint, the interstice between two teeth near the gum. --zĕv gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the tongue to go from the tooth, to become suddenly silent, to be silenced, to be left without an answer. ¶ dȧndⁱ āmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), come between the teeth; thoroughly or easily chewed; met. (of one previously esteemed unconquerable) utterly subdued, entirely come under another's power. -gūjⁱ or -gūjᵘ̈ f., i.q. danda-gūjⁱ ab. --koḍᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --küḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), pulled out by the teeth; met. accomplished with great difficulty and exertion. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to pull out by the teeth; met. to accomplish satisfactorily, but with great exertions, some action or business. --lagun -- or dandan lagun m.inf. to be applied to the teeth, to knock against the teeth; (of some task) to grate in the teeth, to be unpleasant, to be disliked, to run counter to one's wishes. -tᵃj or -tujⁱ; or dȧnⁱ-tⁱj, dȧnⁱ-tujⁱ, q.v., s.v. dan 4 f. a toothpick, see danda-tujⁱ ab. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come between the teeth, to be well chewed; (of some hard and tough morsel) to become easily chewed by infirm teeth; met. (of one previously esteemed unconquerable or to be a tough customer) to become utterly subdued, to come entirely under another's power. ¶ dandan khasun m.f. to mount on to (people's) teeth; on the completion of any public action (good or bad) to become the subject of public censure, to be gossiped about unfavourably. --lagun -- m.inf., i.q. dȧndⁱ lagun ab. ¶ dandas dôdᵘ m. toothache (Gr.M.).
in dand-lidar, see dāna lë̆dᵘ̈rᵘ̈, s.v. dāna.
or ḍanḍa 2 m. a pole, a post, staff, rod; the pole supporting the hinged mat roof of a boat; a pestle (El.).

or ḍanḍa 3 f.pl. a certain gymnastic exercise (the hands and feet are placed on the ground, and the body swung backwards and forwards from the wrists and ankles). --karañĕ -- f.inf. to perform this exercise.
m. being dashed to pieces, of someone or something falling from a height or the like (used esp. in abuse); met. sudden death, however caused.
f. a toothache, i.q. danda-dag under dand.
or -dakh m. (sg. dat. -dakas), i.q. dañ-dab, q.v.
m. the name of a celebrated forest in the Deccan, the Daṇḍaka-vana of Sanskrit literature (Śiv. 556; Rām. 208, 272, 284, 321, 369, 1144, 1777).
adj. (as subst., f. dandöñᵘ̈), toothed, fanged, tusked; one who is disfigured by ugly projecting front teeth or incisors (Gr.Gr. 137, K.Pr. 49).
m. inḍañ-ḍañ karun m.inf. to make the sound of ḍañ-ḍañ', to show the hollowness of anything (lit. or met.) by ringing it.
m. the bark of the walnut-tree (El.; L. 352 has dandarsa).
m. (sg. dat. danḍawatas), prostration of the body, obeisance (K. 133).
or ḍŏnḍūra f. a kind of drum used in proclaiming orders; proclamation by beat of drum (Rām. 716; K. 404, ḍanḍūr; El. ḍanḍora). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give notice, or proclaim, by beat of drum.

f. the outer edge of a dish or the like (K.Pr. 227, the edge of a mat). According to El. not used for the edge of cutting instruments, but in Śiv. 1631, the edge of a sword. --kadüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to draw out an edge; (in carpentry) to plane down the edge of a plank; (in hammering out a metal dish or the like) to form the bent or turned-down edge or lip. ¶ dạndᵃri-phuṭᵃ adj. (f. -phuṭᵘ̈), broken-edged, of a dish or the like.

m. (in the Roman character this word appears under various forms, such as dānih, dāni, dānye, dānyi, L. 330 has even dhān. For dāñĕ 2 see döñᵘ̈. When the first member of a tatpuruṣa, or appositional, comp., this word takes the form dã̄, see Gr.Gr. 74. In the word ḍã̄gorᵘ, a paddy-seller, the initial d has become cerebralized. Cf. Gr.Gr. 149, where the dental d is an error), the rice-plant, paddy; rice in the husk, paddy (K.Pr. 10, 15, 69, 75, 165; W. 141; Śiv. 841, 1315). For full particulars regarding this crop in Kashmīr, see L. 330 ff. and El. s.v. dányí. ¶ dã̄-ambar m. a pile of threshed rice in the husk. -bēr or -bēra f. one of a series of low banks dividing up a rice-field so as to facilitate irrigation. See -ḍūrᵘ bel. -bīra f. a paddy-crowd; in time of scarcity a crowd collected to receive rice at any place where it is obtainable. -bôrᵘ m. a load of unhusked rice, a bag full of winnowed paddy. -bŏstūrᵘ m. a leathern bag full of paddy, or the paddy therein contained. -chakh f. (sg. dat. -chaki), scattering of paddy, esp. the line of fallen paddy on the track along which paddy is being transported. -dal m. the first husking of paddy (paddy is husked by pounding in a mortar: this is done two or three times, and between each husking it is winnowed). -dalyunᵘ m. the first husking of paddy as ab.; the paddy after being thus husked for the first time. -ḍūrᵘ m. a section of a paddy-field as divided by low banks for purposes of irrigation. See -bēr ab. -gë̆ḍᵘ̈ f. a sheaf of reaped paddy, usually consisting of six times as much of the straw as can be grasped in the hand at one time. Cf. -khorᵘ and -lôwᵘ bel. -gọ̆nᵘ m. a pile or heap of sheaves of paddy, esp. a small one. Cf. -gŏñⁱ bel. -guna f. a grain-sack or bag, for use with pack-animals. -gŏñⁱ f. a high pile or stack of sheaves of paddy, put together to allow them to become thoroughly dry. Cf. -gọ̆nᵘ ab. -gurᵘ m. a paddy-horse, a pack-horse loaded with paddy. -gāsa m. paddy-straw. -hönzᵘ̈ m. (f. -hānzañ), a boatman (or boatwoman) whose profession it is to collect paddy from the villages on the river-banks for sale in the city. -hāyukh m. (sg. dat. -hāyĕkas), the grain-pan of the large scales in which paddy is weighed. -hyolᵘ  m. an ear of the paddy-plant (Gr.M.). -kā̃durᵘ m. a large receptacle made of matting for storing threshed unhusked paddy. -khāh m. paddy land, a group of paddy-fields. -khal m. a paddy-threshingfloor, a place where paddy is collected prior to threshing. -khar m. an ass's load of grain. -khār f. (sg. dat. -khörᵘ̈), a certain weight of threshed paddy, a khār or kharwār (about 152 lb.) of paddy (Gr.Gr. 74): the area over which one khār of paddy seed-grain is sown is exactly equivalent to four British acres (L. 243; cf. -path bel.). -khorᵘ m. a certain load or measure of paddy in the ear with the straw, consisting of twelve handfuls or as much as can be grasped twelve times with the hand, two sheaves. Cf. -gë̆ḍᵘ̈ ab. -khītⁱ f. a paddy-field. -khĕwar m. the collection of a store of paddy little by little: e.g. when the paddy has been threshed by the cultivator, and has been collected previous to the Government assessment for purposes of taxation, it is supposed not to be touched till Government permission is given; in such a case the cultivator, for his immediate needs, privately carries off from the pile, little by little, a store for his personal consumption before receiving this permission. -kala m. paddy-head, i.e. the bearded tip of an ear of paddy, containing very small grains. -kanz m. a mortar in which paddy is husked; a mortar full of paddy; as much paddy as will fill a mortar. -kĕsᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the beard of the paddy-ear. -kuṭhᵘ̈ f. a paddy-granary (usually built with wooden boards). -kạtᵃra m. a small amount of threshed paddy, usually as much as can be held in the palm of the hand. -lāv f. paddy-reaping, the paddy harvest. -lôwᵘ m. (in reaping paddy) the amount of straw held in the hand and reaped with one cut of the sickle. Cf. -gë̆ḍᵘ̈ ab. -lāy f. parched paddy, paddy roasted so that each grain bursts. -müṭᵘ̈ f. a large, high, earthen jar used for holding paddy, esp. when filled with it. -maṭh m. (sg. dat. -maṭas), a kind of large earthen jar for holding paddy. -mö̆ṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -mŏchĕ), a handful of paddy (K. 178). -nörᵘ̈ f. a long, narrow strip of a field grown with paddy. -phĕkh f. (sg. dat. -phĕkas), 'a dust of paddy,' a very small quantity of paddy, e.g. the amount collected or distributed at one time by or to one person. -pholᵘ m. a small quantity of threshed paddy (Gr.Gr. 164); a single grain of paddy (K. 178, in this sense usually only plural, Gr.Gr. 164). -phulay f. blossoming of paddy, the flowering of the rice plant (taking place in July, August, or early September). -phulạyi-kani adv. at about the time of rice-blossoming (indefinitely). -phulạyi-kyutᵘ adv. at the time of rice-blossoming (definitely). -phọ̆tᵘ m. a moderately large kind of basket used for holding paddy; such a basket full of paddy; so much paddy as will fill such a basket (Gr.Gr. 74). Cf. -phŏtᵘ̈rᵘ̈ bel. -phuṭᵃ̇jᵃ̇ or -phuṭᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a pile of threshed paddy. -phŏtᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a small kind of basket for carrying paddy; such a basket filled with paddy; so much paddy as will fill such a basket. (These baskets are plastered over with mud.) Cf. -phọ̆tᵘ ab. -pȧjⁱ or -püjᵘ̈ a large kind of basket for holding paddy; such a basket full of paddy; so much paddy as will fill such a basket. -polᵘ m. a large kind of wide open basket, woven of withies and boughs, for holding paddy; such a basket full of paddy; so much paddy as will fill such a basket. -püṭᵘ̈ f. empty paddy husks still on the plant, i.e. husks in which the grain has not formed for want of moisture and which are gaping at the top, as if longing for a drink. -path m. a certain measure of land, a field of such an area that it will require one trakh (about 9 1/2 lb.) of paddy seed for sowing. It is equal in area to one British rood (L. 243). Cf. -khār ab. -pạthᵃr m. ground on which paddy thrown, usually accidentally or carelessly, has taken root and grown up. -pathurᵘ m. a paddy-floor, a level open space on which paddy is spread out to dry. -pyuṭhᵘ m. a sack of leather or gunny full of paddy, adapted for carrying on a man's back and shoulders. It holds about a khār or 152lb. -roṭᵘ m. (in bartering vegetables, etc., for paddy or the like) the weight of anything in paddy. -raṭh f. (sg. dat. -raṭi), id. -shupᵘ m. a winnowing basket for paddy; so much paddy as can be held at one time by such a basket. -sörᵘ̈ f. piling of unthreshed grain (always with reference to paddy conveyed from one place to another, e.g. from a field to be stacked up elsewhere). -thal f. paddy seedlings ready for transplanting. -thāl barun m.inf. to fill the paddy dish, to take the paddy omen. (On the eve of the New Year and similar festivals a metal tray is loaded with paddy, accompanied by flowers, cooked rice, silver, walnuts, cakes, etc., and omens taken from it.) -ʦaph f. a paddy plant, a rice plant as it springs from a single seed. -waguvᵘ m. a paddy-mat, a mat on which threshed paddy is spread out for drying. -wāph m. (sg. dat. -wāpas), paddy-sowing, the time at which paddy is sown (late April to early June). -wörᵘ̈ f. a paddy-barge, a small kind of open barge used for conveying paddy by river to the city. -vĕv f. paddy-sowing, the act of sowing paddy. -zamīn  f. (sg. dat. -zamīni), paddy-land, land in which paddy is sown or to which it is transplanted, land suited for growing paddy, rice land. -zyurᵘ m. paddy-pollen, the young paddy in blossom.

f. (sg. dat. danĕshṭhi ), the name of the twenty-third of the twenty-seven lunar mansions or asterisms; in Sanskrit Dhaniṣṭhā. danĕshṭh-kumār m. N. of a demigod. In Rām. 572 he is associated with Viśvakarmā, the architect of the gods, and in 593 identified with him.

f. coriander seed (El.), Coriandrum sativum. ¶ dāñĕwali bạrᵃg m. greens or spinach (sāg) of the leaves of the coriander plant. -gūjᵘ̈ f. powdered and sifted coriander seed. -kulᵘ m. the coriander shrub. -path m. a certain medical application, a plaster or lotion of powdered coriander seed mixed with water and applied to the affected portion of the body by means of a rag.

m. (sg. abl. ḍanga 1), the shackle or rope by which the forefeet of horses or cattle are tied together to prevent them straying, a hobble-rope. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to tie the forefeet of an animal together as ab. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf., id., also used for tying the feet of a man together, to prevent him running away. ¶ ḍȧngⁱ-ḍulijĕ f.pl. the use or consumption of another's property at one's own will and without constraint or prohibition. -sᵃh m. a hobbled tiger; met. a coward, one who is timid and easily frightened. K.Pr. 49 translates this 'a tiger in the stable', i.e. a tyrant in his house.

m. the act of tying the feet of a horse or other animal to prevent it straying. --karun -- m.inf. to tie a person's feet, to impede him in any business, lit. or met. -raz f. a rope for tying the feet of cattle; occasionally, a rope by which a man's feet are bound to prevent his running away.
in ḍanga-ḍanga m. an occupation or business (like a drum, hollow within but outwardly noisy) of no consequence, but about which a great fuss is made.
m. a tumultuous assembly, a crowd, a company or body of men, esp. a company of police, soldiers, or the like, acting as one body.

dung-dawāl, or dun-dawāl (= دنگ ودوال) m. magnificence, grandeur, pomp; (in Kāshmīrī) a great collection of persons or things, e.g. of people at a festival, of ornaments and other presents for a bride and bridegroom, of troops come together for a battle, etc. Cf. dangala.

f. the upper loft of a cow-house, inhabited by people in winter for the sake of warmth. The children esp. sit in it, and in it the guest is made to sleep, for it is the warmest room in the house (L. 249).
m. (sg. dat. ḍangaras), a bullock; a quadruped (El.); met. a stupid man; a term of abuse (El.).
adj. c.g. wealthy, rich (Śiv. 703, with emph. y, daniy).

adj. c.g. sound, well, healthy (esp. when disease is prevalent); in good condition (of things). Cf. dünḍᵘ̈ 1. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain or continue in a good, firm condition. --thawun -- m.inf. to put in good health, or in a firm, good condition.
m. Portulacea aleracea? (El., who spells the word dhannī).
or (Gr.M.) danu-danḍ m. a bow (the weapon). K. (371, 429, 430, 561, 562) always spells danudanḍ.
m. chattering of the teeth (from cold, ague, or the like). Cf. ḍand- ṭakar, s.v. dand, and dan-ṭakar, s.v. dan 4. --aʦȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. an attack of such chattering to come on.
m. a tooth, used for dand, q.v., in the following: danta-kath f. gossip, verbal report, common talk, legend, as distinguished from anything based on written authority.
m. a certain metal weight used in weighing. The weight which it indicates is one döñᵘ̈, q.v.
m. N. of the physician of the gods, the Dhanvantari of Sanskrit literature (Śiv. 855).
dapā-daph, or daphā-daph f. (sg. dat. -dapi), a quarrel commencing with mutual abuse and winding up with a hand-to-hand fight.

m. (on the occasion of a marriage, when an ambassador arrives at the house of a relation of the bride or bridegroom formally to invite him to the festival) the formal dinner given to such an ambassador. Cf. dapun 1 and 2 and dapawañ.

f. (on the occasion of a marriage or other festival, when the ambassadors arrive at a house formally to invite the members of the family to the festival) the money-present given by the invited to the inviters. Cf. dapun 1 and 2 and dapan-bata.
n.ag. (f. dapawüñᵘ̈), one who speaks; one who commands; one who instructs by message; one who personally invites to a wedding or the like (see dapun 1 and 2).

m. (sg. dat. ḍāpas), lying down, resting (El. has dāf m. rest, and ḍāp f. sleep). --ḍulagun -- m.inf. to be sleepless, to toss and tumble in one's bed. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to rest, give rest (to) (El. dāf). --trāwun -- m.inf. to take to one's bed (from disease, sorrow, weakness, or the like); to sleep (El. ḍāp trāwüñᵘ̈ f.).

m. pushing, thrusting, repulse, repelling (El.); used in special senses in the following: --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become destroyed at a distance, to be thrust away to a distance and there to perish. --karun -- m.inf. to thrust away or carry away to a distance and there to destroy, to make away with. --sapadun -- or --sapazun -- m.inf., i.q. --gaʦhun ab.
f. one time, one turn or bout.
m. burial, interment; (in Kāshmīrī) a shroud.

m. a stink; (in Kāshmīrī) a certain dish made by cooking together the flesh on a sheep's or goat's head together with the animal's paunch. -kȧlⁱyĕ (= دفر قلیہ) m. an abominable stinking mess, tasteless victuals, a dish in which much broth, vegetables, etc., are mixed to make it go further, wishwash; (in Kāshmīrī) a mess made up of the paunch and head-flesh of a sheep or goat, as ab. -lë̆jᵘ̈ f. a cooking-pot filled with the above mess, or of a kind suitable for its preparation.
