m. putting off, postponement. daphul-wakth kaḍun m.inf. to draw out postponement; somehow or other to complete an urgent work in the proper time in spite of the absence of the necessary means. --nērun -- m.inf. postponement to issue; a work to be completed as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dopᵘ; the impve. sg. 2 is daph, e.g. Śiv. 633), to say, to speak (K.Pr. 30; YZ. 20, 28, 91, 161, 250, 463; Śiv. 40, 74, 78, 80, 82, 88, etc.), to order, command; to send a message, to instruct by message; to say to oneself, consider, think (Śiv. 530, 785); to explain (El.); (on the occasion of a son's marriage or similar festival) to invite friends and relations formally by word of mouth (Śiv. 74, 79, 81, 82) (cf. dapun 2, dapan-bata, and dapawañ). ¶ dapani nērun m.inf. to go forth in order to invite; on the occasion of giving a marriage feast or the like, to go out to pay visits of invitation to one's relations, to set out to invite personally. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to arrive at a house in order to invite its inhabitants to a marriage or the like (Siv. 79, 81). ¶ dȧpⁱ dȧpⁱ sōdāh f. (of two parties) agreement after mutual consultation as to a course of conduct; esp. a mutual agreement to fight or the like. ¶ dopᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. düpᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), said; ordered, commanded; invited, etc.

m. (sg. dat. dapanas, pl. nom. dapȧnⁱ, L. 268), an invitation to a wedding issued to the relations and friends of the bride and bridegroom (Śiv. 82; L. 268 dapani). This word is really the same as dapun 1, the inf. used as a verbal noun. Cf. dapun 1, dapan-bata, and dapawañ.
m. fear, apprehension, alarm, dread, awe (K. 375, 464, 468, 577).

prep. in, into, with (Ram. 72, 900; W. 99; YZ. 10, 27); on, upon, above (phōj dar phōj, troop upon troop, Rām. 570); of, concerning, about; by, for, because of; near, hard by, at; to, as far as, according to; before, in presence of; against. For compounds commencing with this word, see s.vv.

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. dārĕñ دارنِ), having, possessing, holding, keeping; used --˚, as in alāka-dār, the owner of an estate; āsana-dār, possessing a seat, hence worthy of housing or receiving a deity (Śiv. 57); āyĕ-dār, possessing accessibility, easy to grasp; baca-dār, possessing a child, pregnant; bāḍav-dār, possessing largeness, too large; bāganayĕ-dār, divisible; bagāra-dār, greasy, rich. In Śiv. 1789 there is a pun with dār, impve. 2 sg. of dārun.
m. a level field suitable for growing corn crops, a cornfield. El. writes this dãr (i.e. dörᵘ with dental d).

m. (sg. dat. daras 1, abl. dara 1), a door, doorway, entrance to a house, room, etc. (Rām. 574); a door (of escape) (K.Pr. 227); a square in a draught or chess board (Siv. 1544, khāla-dar, the square of skin, the position inside the skin, hence the womb, being born, human life). -ḍokhᵘ m. 'door and prop'; refuge and care, support, assistance, subsistence, received from a master, friend, or the like.

m. (sg. abl. dāra 1), a beam or log of wood, a piece of timber (K.Pr. 248, Śiv. 337, 1776); a lump of wood, a worthless piece of wood (K.Pr. 50). El. writes this dãr, i.e. dörᵘ̈. ¶ dāra-banna f. a large pile or stack of logs or beams. -khŏn f. a small pile of a few beams and planks collected together for building a house or the like. -kŏl f. a small canal or water channel for conveying logs from the forest. -köñᵘ̈ f. a collection of logs, etc., esp. when brought together for building a house. -lürᵘ̈ f. a house built of timber, a log house. -ponᵘ m. a wooden wedge for splitting logs. -wan m. a dense forest of timber-trees; met. a huge collection of logs.
m. a surname, commonly used by Musalmān cultivators, as in Gaphār Ḍār غفار ڈار, Lȧsⁱ Ḍār, both proper names.

m. (sg. dat. daras 2, abl. dara 2), value, estimation, esteem; price, rate, tariff, market or current rate; the calculation of the weight of a load, etc.; a large, fixed pair of scales. for weighing heavy loads. -danḍa m. the beam of such a pair of scales; a general term for such a beam together with all its appurtenances. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to weigh. --karun -- m.inf. to calculate the weight of anything by weighing an aliquot part thereof by measure and multiplying by the number of parts. --lagun -- m.inf. the weighing to commence (e.g. of a crop of paddy or of a stack of firewood). --lāgun -- m.inf. to commence the weighing as ab. ¶ dara-dar 2, see s.v.; for 1 see dara 4. -tulukᵘ adj. (f. -talücᵘ̈), 'of under the scales'; (of anything being weighed) coming first into existence at the time of weighment. ¶ darukᵘ adj. (f. darücᵘ̈), of or belonging to weight, of or belonging to the weight or weights used to balance an article being weighed. ¶ daras khotᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. --khüʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), mounted on the scales, in the condition of being weighed; met. subject to general discussion and criticism. --pĕṭh khārun -- m.inf. to cause to mount upon the scales, to subject to weighment; met. to subject another to discussion and criticism. -pĕṭh khasun m.inf. to mount on the scales, to be in the condition of being weighed; met. to become the subject of general discussion and criticism.
m. (sg. abl. dāra 2), strength, stoutness, durability, esp. of clothes, vessels, or similar articles liable to wear out. ¶ dāra-dorᵘ adj. (f.-dürᵘ̈), very strong, very durable (as ab.).

m. N. of a certain sept of Brāhmaṇs in Kashmīr (Gr.Gr. 34). ¶ dara-bāy f. the wife of such a Brāhmaṇ (Gr.Gr. 34). -koṭᵘ m. the son of such a Brāhmaṇ, in a laudatory sense, a real son of a Dar, a good Dar (Gr.Gr. 132); -pūtᵘ m. the son of such a Brāhmaṇ (Gr.Gr. 131).

or (K. 325, 507) dārā f. a line of descending fluid, a thin stream (Śiv. 501, 1028, 1173, 1361, 1366, 1577); ȧshⁱ pȧkⁱ dārē, tears flowed in a stream (YZ. 132, m.c. for dāri); so, oshᵘ dāri pokᵘ (YZ. 417). ¶ dāri-dāri (often -dārĕ m.c.) (Śiv. 964, 1233, 1910) or dörⁱ-dörⁱ (Śiv. 1894) adv. in streams. dāri dāri wasun m.inf. 'to descend in streams', a house to be flooded in a rain-storm owing to leaks in the roof.
. In L.V. 74 this word is not confined to a thin stream of descending fluid, but is used for the flood of the ocean.
in dara-dar, see dara 4 and dara-dar 2 and 3.

or dāra 3 f. the sharp edge or point of any tool, weapon, or cutting instrument (El. dára). ¶ dāra phērañĕ f. pl. inf. the edges or point of a tool or weapon to be turned. --pĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. 'edges to fall', the edges or point of any tool or weapon to be depressed, to be blunted or turned.

f. a door (Rām. 22). nav-dār, the nine doors or apertures of the body, viz. the mouth, the two ears, the two eyes, the two nostrils, and the organs of excretion and generation (Rām. 23). ¶ dāra-pūz f. worship of the door-god; a part of the Hindū wedding ceremony, in which the bridegroom, before entering the bride's house for the purpose of marriage, worships the god who guards the door. Cf. dörᵘ̈ 3.

m. one who carries or bears up, used --˚, as in mālā-dar, one who bears a garland (Śiv. 1171, 1174); musala-dar, one who carries a pestle (as a club) (Śiv. 1160); gangā-dar, he who carries the Ganges (on his head), Śiva (Śiv. 37).
m. a cavern, cave (Rām. 1584, but here the word may also be dara 3, q.v.).

m. (sg. dat. daras 3), a support, prop, that which holds anything immovable, cf. ȧchⁱ-dara, s.v. ȧchⁱ. --logᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --lüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --) (of some living being) become motionless (Rām. 1584, see bel.). --lagun -- m.inf. to become motionless, be stopped, suddenly delayed or impeded (of some person or thing usually or preferably in motion) (Śiv. 332, 1641; of the coming of daylight being delayed, Rām. 1584, cf. dar 8); to become fixed, permanent (Rām. 1391, of the darkness of an eclipse); met. to become released from transmigration, become absorbed in the Supreme Deity (Śiv. 166, and also of the moonlight being stopped by the brighter light of the sun). Cf. dari lagun, s.v. dorᵘ 1.

f. pulling out, straining (leather, cloth, rope, or the like previously contracted, in order to lengthen it); pulling or wringing out clothes in the process of washing (Śiv. 1022). -dar 1 f. pulling, hauling (at anything) (K.Pr. 11). Cf. also dara-dar 2 and 3, s.vv. -drasa m. to pull from both ends a rope, etc., as ab., till there is danger of its breaking. Cf. drasa. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to pull out as ab.

m. a body of thieves collected together for purposes of robbery, a troop of banditti, 'dacoits,' gang-robbers. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. (of thieves) to rob in a body, to commit 'dacoity', to commit gang-robbery. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. an attack by banditti or 'dacoits' to occur.

m. (sg. dat. daras 4), a valley between two hills, down which a stream runs; (in Kashmīr) a small water-channel conducted round a rice field or the like for purposes of irrigation, the flow of which usually falls from high ground; the current or flow of water in a river (Śiv. 1638, wŏgani dara, with a shallow current). -ganḍ m. a block in such a channel so as to divert the flow of water. --ganḍun -- m.inf. to block such a channel so as to divert the flow of water. -talukᵘ adj. (f. -talücᵘ̈), of or belonging to below the source of the ab. water-channel, i.e. (water) drawn directly from where the water is falling into the channel from high ground. --sẹ̆zᵃrun -- m.inf. at the proper time to cause water to flow along one of these channels.
in dāra-pār m. rule over far and near, rule over a wide extent of country. Cf. dōr 1.
in dara-dar, see dara 4 and dara-dar 2 and 3.
m. translated 'beard' in YZ. 145. Cf. dörᵘ̈ 2. Possibly incorr. for ḍĕka, forehead.
fut. sg. 1 of darun 1 and 2, qq.v.

f. (for 1 see dara 4), obstinacy in bargaining, driving a hard bargain, eager discussion as to market price, long and obstinate chaffering (K. 952). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to indulge in lengthy bargaining, to do lengthy chaffering.

f. (of one dangerously sick) slight improvement, a slight turn for the better, turning the corner. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of one dangerously sick) slight signs of improvement to occur, a turn for the better to take place, the crisis to pass over; met. (of some business on the brink of ruin) slight signs of improvement to occur. --sö̃panüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf., id.

adj. c.g. born or produced in the Darad country. This is properly the territory round the upper Kishĕngangā, but the name is extended to include the country reaching from Citrāl to Yasīn, across the Indus regions of Gilgit, Cilās, and Bunjī, to the Kishĕngangā Valley in the immediate north of Kashmīr. Cf. RT.Tr. I, 47n, and II, 435.
in the following: daram-bôyᵘ m. a forester, one who inhabits the wild hill-country of Kashmīr, and occupies himself with cattle-tending or similar occupations.
m. adjustment of a dispute; (in Kāshmīrī) causing a person to like something which he has hitherto disliked, reconciling, winning over, propitiating, satisfying.
adj. c.g. bearing, upholding, possessing, retaining, used --˚ as in mōha-dāran (m.c. mōha-dāranō), he who possesses or is continually subject to illusion (Śiv. 1425).

f. concentration of the mind on any subject; intense abstract meditation (esp. when practised with suppression of breath) (Śiv. 62, 132, etc.); firmness, steadfastness. dāranāyĕ-dār m. one who possesses steadfastness; N. of the Supreme Being, He Who is firm and sure (Śiv. 1789, with pun on dāranāyĕ dār, hold thou fast with abstract meditation).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. daranôwᵘ), caus. of darun 1, to cause a person to keep a fast, to teach to keep a fast according to proper rules (Śiv. 1749).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. dāranôwᵘ), caus. of dārun, to cause to bear, carry, etc. dyān dāranāwun m.inf. to cause (a person) to meditate (Śiv. 451), see dyān dārun under dārun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ḍaranôwᵘ), to frighten (El.). Caus. of ḍarun, q.v.

m. hesitation, tardiness; delay caused by obstinacy or excessive eagerness; cf. darkh. --lagun -- m.inf. such delay to occur (e.g. by eagerness and overcrowding of the recipients in the distribution of charity). --lāgun -- m.inf. to cause such delay.

f. lateness, tardiness; delay caused by excessive eagerness, esp. when the necessaries for the work delayed run short. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. delay to occur in some work commenced, but for which materials are found to be insufficient, whether such delay is accompanied by excessive zeal or by neglect.

m. (for 1-4 see dar, dara), looking at, esp. looking respectfully at anything, respectful visiting. -diwayĕ gaʦhun m.inf. to go on a pilgrimage to a holy place with a troop of pilgrims, to join a pilgrimage, to visit a place of pilgrimage on one of the great days when there is a concourse of people there, to go to a mēlā. Cf. diway. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to show respect to anyone.
m. a heavy and long-continued fall of rain.
f. (sg. dat. -sĕpi), a kind of chalk, found mostly in the hills of Kashmīr.
adj. (f. dāraticᵘ̈), i.q. dāratukᵘ, see dāruth.
m. a beam, rafter, esp. the main beam of a roof or ceiling on which the rafters rest.
(El.) (prob. incorrect for dyārawôlᵘ, see dyār), adj. rich.
n.ag. (f. ḍarawüñᵘ̈), fearful, timid by nature, a coward.

n.ag. (f. dārawüñᵘ̈), one who bears or carries (Śiv. 1258); one who puts or places (Śiv. 1082); (with awatār) one who takes an incarnation (Śiv. 851, 862); (with dyān) one who meditates (Śiv. 1534); one who bears or is distinguished by (any particular quality, ornament, beauty, or the like) (Śiv. 514, 1260, 1537); one who owes money to any particular person, so-and-so's debtor. Cf. dārun.
adj. c.g. long, tall, extended, stretched out.
m. drawers (of a chest, etc.), a chest of drawers (the English word).

f. a certain kind of grass, Poa cynosuroides, used by Hindūs in religious ceremonies, the kuśa or darbha of Sanskrit (Rām. 320, 398, 552, 1291, 1298). ¶ darbi-ḍē̃ṭônᵘ or -ḍē̃ṭun m. a girdle made of this grass, and worn by certain Hindū ascetics (Brahmacöris). -gë̆ḍᵘ̈ f. a wisp of this grass; cf. -gyoḍᵘ bel. -gāsa m., i.q. darb. -gyoḍᵘ m. a load or bundle of wisps of this grass; cf. -gë̆ḍᵘ̈ ab. -hurᵘ̈ or -hürᵘ̈ f. a wisp or small bundle (as much as can be held in the hand) of this grass in a dried and woody condition as imported from outside Kashmīr. -kã̄ḍ m. a stem of ripened darb grass in seed, dried and hard. -köñᵘ̈ f. a pile or heap of this grass, esp. of small quantities (Rām. 1289). -lŏʦhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a tied-up bundle of this grass, of such a size that it can be grasped by the two hands. -lôvᵘ m. a tied-up bundle or wisp of this grass, of such a size that it can be grasped by one hand. -māwas f. the festival of the new moon of the month of Bādᵃrapĕth (August-September) on which Hindūs collect this grass. -raz f. a girdle of this grass, put on a bride at the marriage ceremony (Sanskrit pariṇayadāna), and on a Hindū boy at the ceremony of his initiation (Sanskrit upanayana). -tᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a small dried stick of imported darb-grass; cf. -hurᵘ̈ ab. -tulᵘ m. a small bundle of this grass. -zạnḍ f., id.

adv. from door to door; subst. m. a beggar, a vagrant. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become a vagrant, to become debased; to become harassed in searching for something hidden or the like. --karun -- m.inf. to debase, make wicked (e.g. a master or a father debauching a pupil or son); to hide anything so as to harass a person by making it necessary for him to search for it.
f. beggary, vagrancy; (in Kāshmīrī) worthlessness of character.

m. a house, a dwelling; a hall of audience, court (Śiv. 952, 1036); holding of a court, a levee, durbar (K.Pr. 29, 51); a royal audience (Śiv. 10, 1508, 1579); the executive Government; a post of honour, a high position (Śiv. 10). -gara m. a master's house, the house of a servant's master (K.Pr. 50). --karun -- m.inf. to make a house, to reside, hence met. to apply oneself steadily to any work (Śiv. 1798); to hold a court or levee (Śiv. 1798, with pun on the double meaning). --murkhas karun (= دربار مُرَخّص کرن), to dismiss a court, to dismiss the courtiers from a levee (H. viii, 11).
m. one who attends a court, a courtier; one entitled to a seat at a levee or durbar; vill., a better-class villager who does not work himself and wears white clothes (L. 253).

f. pain, ache, trouble, grief, affliction; pity, sympathy, compassion; love, affection (K.Pr. 50; Śiv. 974; H. ix, 8). --āsüñᵘ̈ f.inf. love or affection to come into being or to arise. ¶ darda sān adv. very affectionately, very lovingly (u.w. vbs. of giving or the like).
m. quick progression, running fast so that one's feet make a noise on the ground. --karān -- adv. fast and with noise, u.w. vbs. meaning 'to go' or the like.
(El.) f. the astringent leaves of Rhus cotinus or allied species, used in dyeing.
f. a portal, door; a royal court, palace (ba-dargāh-i padar, in the palace of the father, Rām. 1511); a mosque; a shrine or tomb (of some reputed saint) which is the object of worship or pilgrimage.

adj. c.g. intricate, confused, entangled, distorted, embroiled; afflicted. --barham درہم برہم adj. c.g., id. (Gr.M.; Rām. 229, afflicted, upset). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become confused or paralysed with astonishment at some unexpected obstacle. --karun -- m.inf. to confuse, paralyse with astonishment, as ab.
or daridrī adj. c.g. poor, needy, poverty-stricken.
adv. with great excitement, eagerly, fervently, ardently, angrily, indignantly (Rām. 329, 818).
adj. c.g. necessary, required, wanted (Śiv. 1079, 1792); required to be done, necessary to be done, proper (course of conduct) (Śiv. 1792).

or darakh m. (sg. dat. darkas or darakas), disputing (El.). ¶ daraka-darakh f. delay caused by disputing or emulous zeal, people getting in each other's way, hurly-burly. Cf. daranga. For gender see Gr.Gr. 75. ¶ darka karun m.inf. to cause delay in this way by disputing or mutual emulous zeal. --raṭun -- m.inf. (in a quarrel or dispute) to delay it by excess of obstinacy.

or darᵃm virtue, morality, customary observance of prescribed conduct, duty, good works, piety, religion (K.Pr. 105, 187; Śiv. 51, 170, 516, 1028, etc.); personified in darmay, O Piety! (Śiv. 51); charity, almsgiving (El., K.Pr. 48); virtue, nature, character, essential quality, peculiarity (Śiv. 1673, 1898). --arth kām mōksh -- m.pl. religious merit, wealth, pleasure, and final emancipation (the four objects of existence) (Śiv. 1798). -bĕñĕ or darma-bĕñĕ f. a sister in respect of religion; (when referring to a grown-up unmarried woman) a woman who, owing to mutual religious sympathy or after taking religion as a witness to the assertion, is looked upon as a sister, and treated accordingly. --Dās -- N. of a celebrated Kāshmīrī ascetic. He built several small houses, the biggest of which was sufficient for only two persons. Hence the phrase Dharᵃm Dāsüñᵘ̈ kuṭhürᵘ̈, a Dharᵃm Dās's chamber, hence any small room. He died in 1877. (See K.Pr. 50.) --gārun -- m.inf. to remember morality affectionately, zealously to follow moral duties. -karm m. (sg. dat. darmas-karmas), morality and the performance of religious actions, the sum-total of all one's moral duties and observances (Śiv. 681); cf. darma-karm bel. -möjᵘ̈ f. a mother in respect of religion; a woman who, owing to community of religious belief or after calling religion as a witness to the assertion, is looked upon as a mother, and treated as such. ¶ darma-aina or -öna m. 'a piety-mirror'; a kind of small mirror intended to be used for giving in charity. -boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), great in piety, respected owing to good moral character; very virtuous. -bāg m. a piety-garden; a public garden founded as an act of virtue by a private person. -bajĕr m. greatness in piety, respect paid to a man owing to his good moral character; greatness of virtue, virtuousness. -bĕñĕ f. a sister in religion, i.q. darm- bĕñĕ ab. -bôyᵘ m. a brother in religion, a male friend who, owing to mutual religious sympathy or after taking religion as a witness to the assertion, is looked upon as a brother, and treated as such. -dã̄d m. a piety-bull, a Brahminy Bull, a bull set at liberty by Hindūs as an act of piety, and allowed to roam at will; met. a stout lumpish fool of a fellow who follows his own courses. --ḍolᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --ḍüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), one who has abandoned customary rules and piety, a reprobate. --ḍalun -- m.inf. to abandon customary rules and piety, to become a reprobate. -dān m. pious gifts, charity (Śiv. 1148, 1738). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go from piety, to abandon pious practices, to become a reprobate. -hān f. loss of piety; a reputation for conduct wanting in piety. -hān khasüñᵘ̈ f.inf. an accusation of a repute of want of piety to be incurred. -hān yiñᵘ̈ f.inf. a repute for want of piety to be incurred. -hīñĕr m. want of piety. -hyūnᵘ adj. (f. -hīñᵘ̈), wanting in piety. -kinⁱ adv. according to the rules for pious observance, devoutly. -kangañ f. 'a piety-comb', a kind of small-sized woman's comb intended to be used for giving in charity (it has teeth on both sides). -kanguvᵘ m. 'a piety-comb', a man's comb intended for a similar purpose (it has teeth on only one side). -karm m. (sg. dat. darma-karmas), a work of piety, a religious action; cf. darm-karm ab. -phal m. the fruit of piety, the divine reward for good works in this or the other world. -phȧlⁱ baṭañ f. a piety-fruit Brāhmaṇ woman, a Brāhmaṇ beggar- woman who in asking for alms reminds each person applied to of the reward earned by pious actions such as giving in charity. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall from piety, to give up pious practices. -röchⁱ f. protection of piety, the upholding of pious practices; protection from harm owing to one's personal piety. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without piety, a reprobate. -raʦhar m. absence of piety. -rāza  m. a king of justice; hence, a just judge, one who decides justly (Śiv. 1754); N. of Yama, the Lord of the Lower World, who judges the soul after death (Śiv. 810, 1148, 1911; K. 493, 538, 848). -sabā f. an assembly for pious purposes, a holy assembly (Śiv. 65, 969, 1070). -shösᵃtᵃr m. a code of moral laws. -shösᵃtᵃrᵃ m. one who teaches a code of moral laws. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), possessing piety, pious. -saʦhar m. piety, a pious disposition, pious conduct. -wākh m. a word of piety, true words, a truthful statement (K. 722). -zān f. (sg. dat. -zöñᵘ̈), knowledge of moral law or duty. ¶ darmücᵘ̈, see darmukᵘ bel. --kath -- f. a word of piety; a truthful statement; good advice or a just decision given by an arbitrator or the like. ¶ darmukᵘ adj. (f. darmücᵘ̈), of or belonging to piety (Śiv. 448, 520, 598, etc.); sprung from good works or piety (e.g. good luck, the reward of virtue); that which is given as a gift for pious purposes. ¶ darmas sg. dat. for virtue, for piety (Śiv. 750, in sense of acc.); used almost as a precative interjection equivalent to the English 'for goodness sake', 'for heaven's sake' (Śiv. 1554, 1630, 1673, 1737). --āmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), 'come for piety,' hence received as a present, esp. a present given as a pious action. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give for piety, to give or endow for pious purposes. --dyutᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --diʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), given for pious purposes, given as an endowment. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be given as a present, esp. for pious purposes.

adv. in the belly, but used met. in the following: --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be delayed (in the accomplishment ofany work). --karun -- m.inf. to delay as ab. --lagun -- m.inf. to be in doubt, incertitude (Rām. 1670).
adj. c.g. any article, land, or the like, given for or devoted to pious or charitable purposes; a pension (El.).
adj. c.g. faithful to duty, virtuous, pious, just.
a superintendent, inspector, manager, intendant, overseer (El.).
adj. (f. ḍaröcᵘ̈), fearful, apprehensive, timid; a coward, dastard.

adv. in front (of), before (Rām. 235); under consideration, under trial. --karun -- m.inf. to place or lay before, to introduce, bring forward, adduce; --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come in front, be before; to be in hand, be pending; to happen, occur (Rām. 235).
adj. c.g. worthy of being looked at, beautiful.

m. (sg. dat. darshĕnas), a look, seeing (Śiv. 806, 903, 907); a meeting, an interview (El., Śiv. 167, 190, 238); a visit of respect, or of adoration (to a king or god), homage (Śiv. 101, 433, 1038); a visit paid to the shrine of a deity, a visit of worship to a temple. ba-darshĕn adv. in sight, visible (Rām. 1664). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to grant an interview, to show oneself, to appear (to someone) (YZ. 44, Śiv. 283, 346, 485, 487, 690, 898, etc.). --hāwun -- m.inf. to show oneself (Śiv. 511, 715, 740, 1243, 1527). --karun -- m.inf. to pay a visit of adoration or respect (Śiv. 508, 927). ¶ darshĕn-gāh m. a place where one interviews a superior, a palace (El., YZ. 172).
m. medicine, drug, remedy, cure. With suff. of indef. art. nōshĕ-dārōh = نوش دارو, an antidote (Rām. 901).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. ḍaryōv), to fear, to be or become afraid (Śiv. 1067, K. 180). ḍaryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ḍaryē-müʦᵘ̈), one who has become afraid, fearful, a coward; timid, apprehensive.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dôrᵘ), to bear, to carry, uphold (Śiv. 1392); to put, to place (Śiv. 433, 1361); to owe (money), to have on loan; to reach out (a wallet, the hand, or the like); to receive something (El., K.Pr. 15); to extend or stretch out (a limb) for any purpose (K.Pr. 261); to offer (e.g. one's neck to the sword, YZ. 51, or the head to be bound, Śiv. 1395); to accept, agree to, assent to, acquiesce in; to perform, to carry out, a fast or other religious obligation (cf. darun 1). ös dārun, m.inf. to open the mouth to receive anything (K.Pr. 145, 171); to swallow up (K.Pr. 76). dyān dārun, m.inf. to perform religious meditation, to meditate (Śiv. 1, 62, 132, 156, 198 dörith-kĕth = dörith, 228, etc.); often with dāranāyĕ (see dāranā), to meditate with abstract meditation, to meditate profoundly, e.g. in Śiv. 1789, with pun on dāranāyĕ-dār, He who is steadfast, God. dyāna dārun, m.inf. to hold (someone) in meditation, to meditate (upon someone) (Śiv. 252, 1195). halam dārun, m.inf. to hold out the skirt to receive something (K.Pr. 50, 153). kan dārun, m.inf. to apply the ear, listen, pay heed (Śiv. 163, 584, 596, 812, 966, 1439, 1517, 1580, 1614). rṻph dārun, m.inf. to assume a certain form, take the form (of) (Śiv. 94, 100, 739, 861, 975, 977, 1134); so avatār dārun, to assume an incarnation, become incarnate (Śiv. 581, 1238, 1739); libāsāh dārun, assume an outward appearance (of) (Śiv. 833); kāyā dārüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to take a body, assume bodily form (Śiv. 1458); warn dārun, to take (a certain) colour, assume (a certain appearance) (Śiv. 840). samsār dārun, m.inf. to adopt the world, to give up asceticism and assume the life of a householder (Śiv. 1224). vairāgyĕ dārun, m.inf. to adopt asceticism, become an ascetic (Siv. 1753). vrath dārun, m.inf. to keep a fast, to fast (Siv. 526, K. 1168). zīṭhⁱ atha dārȧnⁱ, m. pl. inf. to stretch out the arms (in greediness or yearning) (H. vii, 25). --pārun -- m.inf. to perform or accomplish a fast. ¶ dörⁱ dörⁱ dyunᵘ m.inf. to perform or complete anything in great haste and confusion, not arranging things in proper order, to do anything hastily and untidily. ¶ dôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. dörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), borne, carried, upheld; placed, put; (money) borrowed or owed; (of a vessel or hand) reached out to receive something; accepted, agreed to; (of a fast or the like) accepted, undertaken. ¶ dāran dinⁱ m. pl. inf. (among Hindūs) to perform the morning and evening oblations. ¶ dörith dyunᵘ m.inf. to dash down, knock down (Śiv. 324, K. 83, 351, 736), esp. with the intention of breaking. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. voluntarily to abase oneself. --rōzun -- m.inf. to lie before a smiter or executioner so as to allow him to strike the more easily, to be a craven, 'to kiss the rod,' 'turn the other cheek.'

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dorᵘ 4; for 1, 2, 3 see s.vv.; for an example of dorᵘ 4 see Śiv. 1905), to maintain or keep a fast, to fast (Śiv. 740, 1749); usually with a cognate accusative such as vrath (Śiv. 758, 1168, 1351, 1408, 1583, 1905); dyān darun, to meditate, concentrate one's mind upon God (Śiv. 161, 520), but more usually dyān dārun, see dārun, but cf. dyān darun under darun 2. In Śiv. 1749 daronu-y is fut. pass. part.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. daryōv), to become steady (of something in motion), to become firm, to stand steady (K.Pr. 80, Śiv. 171, 244, 346, 907, 936, 1066, 1251, 1351, 1584); to become firm, strong; to become well and strong after an illness; (of a child) to be impudent, audacious, naughty; (of rain) to cease falling (K.Pr. 116, Śiv. 1236, 1286); to be known off by heart or by rote; dyān darun, abstract meditation to be maintained without distraction (Śiv. 1752, pres. part. daran), but cf. dyān darun under darun 1. ¶ darana-kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas; f. -küṭᵘ̈ 1, sg. dat. -kacĕ), a neglected child, not looked after because the parents have too many children or are too poor. -küṭᵘ̈ 2 f. (sg. dat. -kacĕ), a certain medicinal plant with small but long leaves, usually found in the neighbourhood of lakes or ponds. ¶ darith dyunᵘ m.inf. to throw away some despised article. ¶ daryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. daryē-müʦᵘ̈), become steady, firm, strong; entirely recovered from illness and again become hale and hearty; (of a child) become impudent, audacious, naughty, etc., as under darun.
m. the handle of the upper millstone of a hand grinding-mill.

m. (sg. dat. dāratas, pl. nom. dārath), a debt, money, etc., taken on loan. dārath-waturᵘ m. a bond acknowledging a debt, an IOU. dāratukᵘ or dāratyukᵘ adj. (f. dāratücᵘ̈ or dāraticᵘ̈), of or belonging to a debt, that which is taken on loan; that which has to be paid to clear off a debt.

m. a door, a doorway (Śiv. 247), esp. the main door for entrance or exit into a house or room; a gate, lock of a canal, or the like, as in ḍal-darwāza, the flood-gates of the Ḍal Lake (K.Pr. 245). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to shut a door. -hākh f. (sg. dat. -hāki), the side posts of a door. -hang m. the cross beam at the top of a doorway, the lintel. -poṭᵘ m. the leaf of a door, a door (as distinct from a doorway). --thāwun -- m.inf. to open a door, unlock a door (H. viii, 11). -ṭang m. the hole into which the wooden spike corresponding to the bolt of a door shoots. Cf. ṭang. --trapun -- m.inf. to close a door, lock it against someone (H. viii, 11).
m. a dervish, a religious mendicant, esp. a recluse who gives himself up to religious meditation (L. 234).
(Rām. 1078), دریا, dȧrⁱyā, or dȧrⁱyāv (Rām. 739 et passim) (sg. dat. daryāwas or dȧrⁱyāwas), a river (El.; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 50, 63, 76, 95, 121, 250; Śiv. 253, 737).
pl. ag. and abl. of dörᵘ̈ 3, q.v. (Śiv. 340, 958).
adj. (f. darishᵘ̈), meanly obstinate, one who drives a hard bargain, close-fisted.
m. a fissure, cleft, crack, flaw; a seam, suture (of a garment, etc.); a joint in plastering, the line or crack along the edge of plaster laid on a wall or the like.
m. male actor or dancer who dresses in woman's clothes, and sings and acts in that character. dạrza-pöthᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the conduct or business of such an actor.
f. N. of a darkish grub which injures the roots of maize and cotton and is one of the worst vegetable pests of Kashmīr (L. 157).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. dạrᵒrᵒ), to make steady; to make firm; to make steady by practice, train by practice. Causal of darun 2, q.v. in all its senses.

m. destruction, desolation (e.g. from an earthquake or flood) (Gr.Gr. 148; Śiv. 737, 852; Rām. 41, 176, 228, etc.; K. 225, 789, 799, 884). --karun -- m.inf. to destroy or reduce to desolation (K. 325), esp. of the sudden dissipation of a collection of articles stored up. ¶ ḍāsa-nāv f. utter desolation, utter destruction, esp. of stored articles (compared to a ship going down with all its cargo). -pathᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. destruction or devastation caused by scattering (e.g. when a heap of grain is scattered abroad and lost).

m. (in commencing some urgent work) delay, hindrance, obstruction, checking; voluntary self-hindrance, laziness (K.Pr. 177). Cf. dọ̆shᵘ 1. --bihun --, doshᵘ bihun m.inf. delay (through want of preparation, neglect, indolence, or the like), checking, hindrance to occur in the commencement of anything which one wishes to accomplish. --lagun --, doshᵘ lagun m.inf., id. --tulun -- m.inf. to avoid or get over such delay, to remove the cause of it, etc. --wŏthun --, doshᵘ wŏthun m.inf. to set about commencing a work which has been delayed.

m. (f. dösī, q.v.), a servant, slave (K. 728); (in religion) a servant (of God), a humble worshipper, a devotee (Śiv. 232, 599, etc.); often a part of a proper name as in Bawönī Dās, 'a servant of the goddess Bhavānī,' N. of a man; similarly, Daram Dās (K.Pr. 50). ¶ dāsa-bāv m. the condition of a servant, servitude, service (K. 1067); the attitude of a devout man to God (Śiv. 620, 1076, 1100). -pônᵘ m. employment as a servant; esp. taking to servitude or acting like a servant (by a one not previously a servant).

(contr. of دست), a hand, used in the following compounds and phrases: das-basta (= دست بستہ), adj. c.g. having the hands bound; hence, with hands folded in supplication (Śiv. 188, 354). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to put the hand to anything, to attempt to do something the commencement of which is impossible. Cf. das 1. -gāh (= دست گاہ), m. power, strength, ability; independence (Rām. 1146). --karun -- m.inf. to put the hand to, or interfere with, anything with which one has no concern, to stick the finger into another's pie or to put the hand into another's pocket; to wish to do this.

m. the lower timber of a doorway (Śiv. 1076, 1100; in the latter, with pun on dās 1); the sill of a window (H. v, 4). ¶ dāsa-ḍūrᵘ̈ f. the long groove cut on one side of this timber. -kijⁱ or -kijᵘ̈ f. the peg or wedge for fixing this timber in its place. -kala m. the front of this timber. -kūṭᵘ m. a piece of wood suitable to be used as the lower timber of a doorway. -ṭukra m. a broken piece of such a timber.
or dasarāray f. a great collection of ornaments (such as those given to a bride, or worn by a daughter-in-law).
f. of ḍāsᵃr, q.v., a careless housekeeper who habitually destroys household articles by using them improperly.
f. the mutual giving and accepting of gifts.

f. a rag, tatter; a fringe; a votive rag hung up on the wall of a shrine (L. 270, dush). In Gr.M. 1588 the word is wrongly used to mean 'seam'. ¶ dashĕ f.pl. the fringes of a cloth or garment, made by leaving the ends unwoven, or by undoing the weaving of the unhemmed ends (K.Pr. 156). -dupᵃṭa m. a sheet worn over the shoulders, fringed at both ends. -ḍē̃ṭun or -ḍē̃ṭônᵘ m. a fringed waistband, chiefly used by women, but also by men. --thawañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to place fringes; to tie votive rags, fringes of silken thread, etc., at a sacred place in token of a petition made for the accomplishment of some boon. These are untied when the boon is granted.

m. strength, lastingness, durability, the property of not being easily worn out (of clothes, etc.). dāsh na dāsh m. a person's entire property (used with reference to loss, robbery, or conversely, collecting, amassing).
f. (in astrology) the influence of a predominant planet, the position of the planets as to affect a person's good or evil fortune (Śiv. 1477, Rām. 420). Cf. düshᵘ̈ 3.
adj. c.g. strong, durable (of clothes, etc.).
card. ten (L.V. 69). This is a word borrowed from Skt. The true Ksh. word is dah, q.v.

m. 'the destroyer of the ten (kinds of sin)', N. of a certain rare astronomical conjunction occurring on the (1) tenth lunar day of the (2) light half of the month of (3) Zēṭh (Sanskrit Jyaiṣṭha) when, on that day, (4) the moon is in the asterism Hasta, (5) the weekday is Wednesday, (6) the karaṇa, or second half of the lunar day, is Gara, (7) there is vyatīpāta (i.e. when the sum of the longitudes of the sun and the moon amounts to not less than 213˚ 20' and not more than 226˚ 40'), (8) there is the Ānanda yōga (this seems to be a name for the first ghatikā, or twenty-four minutes, also for the twenty-ninth and fifty-seventh ghaṭikās on a Wednesday), (9) the moon is in Kanyā (Virgo), (10) and the sun in Vṛṣabha (Taurus). Bathing at the confluence of the Ganges and the Jumna, and similar sacred spots, with appropriate offerings, is believed by Hindūs to be very efficacious on this occasion (K.Pr. 44, where it is confounded with dashĕhār 2; Śiv. 1793, with pun on dashĕhār 3). This conjunction last occurred in Samvat 1944, equivalent to June 1, 1887.

m. 'the destroyer of the ten (kinds of sin)', N. of a festival held in honour of Rāma's conquest of Rāvaṇa on the tenth lunar day of the light half of the month of Öshid (Sanskrit Āśvina = September-October), the Indian Dasahrā (K.Pr. 44, where it is confounded with dashĕhār 1).
m. in Śiv. 1793, a fanciful compound (equivalent to the Sanskrit daśēndriyaviṣayāhṛti) and meaning the employment of the ten (senses). It is made up to pun with dashĕhār 1, q.v.
adj. c.g. possessing a fringe or fringes, fringed (of a garment or the like).

m. redemption by the tenth (Sanskrit daśamōddhāra), N. of a certain mystic exercise practised by Yōgīs (Śiv. 1655). There are, according to their teaching, ten essential elements (Sanskrit, dhātu) of the body, viz. in order of production, skin (tvak), blood (asṛk), flesh (māṁsa), fat (mēdaḥ), bone (asthi), marrow (majjā), semen (śukra), vital breath (prāṇa), soul (jīva), and energy (śakti). In this system there are also ten (not the usual nine; cf. dwār) doors or openings of the human body, viz. two nostrils, two eye-orifices, two ear-orifices, two mouth-orifices (the windpipe and gullet), and two orifices of excretion. The tenth and most excellent of the bodily elements, i.e. energy, operates through the orifice of rapture, i.e. the urethra (ānandadvāra or śukradvāra), here compared to immortality-giving ambrosia (amṛtātmaśukradvāra). Uddhāra means 'redemption', and the whole compound therefore means redemption brought about by operating the supreme and most excellent of the bodily powers.
m. slowness, slackness in work, laziness.
m. (sg. dat. dashĕrathas), Daśaratha, N. of a famous king, the father of Rāmacandra (Rām. 40, 67, 70, 102, etc.).

m. (sg. dat. -rāwanas), Rāvaṇa, N. of a celebrated demon with ten heads, conquered by Rāmacandra (Rām. 583, 841, 1033, 1149), esp. the image of Rāvaṇa borne at the festival of the Rāma-līlā or daśaharā. Cf. dashĕhār 2.

m. (sg. dat. daskhatas), a signature (Gr.M.). Cf. das 2. --karun -- m.inf. to sign, subscribe (Gr.M.); myönis mölⁱ-sandi daskhata khath, a letter signed by my father (H. xii, 21); ath korun mölⁱ-sondⁱ das- khath, on it she wrote the father's signature (H. xii, 22).
m. (for 2, 3, see dasth 1, 2), a handful; a hank or skein of silk, etc.; a quire of 24 sheets of paper (L. 380); a handful, or posy, of flowers (YZ. 69, Śiv. 76, 187, 192, Rām. 573, K. 1, etc.).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. dastaladiñ), worn out or become thin owing to diarrhœa.

m. the sash or fine muslin cloth wrapped round to form a turban; a turban, a puggaree (El. only a man's) (K.Pr. 51, 56, 86, 126; Rām. 1431, 1458). syodᵘ dastār, a straight turban, is an expression indicating prosperity (K.Pr. 137). --badalun -- m.inf. to exchange turbans (a solemn covenant of friendship). -lāṭh m. (sg. dat. -lāṭas), the length of cloth in a single twist of a turban. -phī˜ṭun m. a kind of small longish turban. -pọ̆ʦhᵘ m. the fringe or embroidery at each end of a turban-cloth. -shikhurᵘ m. a turban made up of old, torn cloth, a ragged old puggaree. -zang f. a present made for the sake of good luck to the teacher of a bridegroom or similar person on the occasion of the ceremonial wrapping the turban round the latter's head; a similar present made on other similar occasions. -züṭᵘ̈ f. a turban-rag, an old worn-out turban.

m. (sg. dat. dastas, abl. dasta 2; for 1 see s.v.), the hand (YZ. 76, Rām. 63). zabar-dasth زبردست adj. c.g. having the upper hand, vigorous, powerful, strong (Rām. 925); high-handed, overbearing, tyrannical.

m. (sg. dat. dastas), purging or loose stool, diarrhœa. Also occurring in the form dasta 3 and then always m.pl. ¶ dasta-ḍōr m.pl. violent purging, repeated diarrhœa. -dĕv m. (f. -dĕviñ), a diarrhœa demon; hence, one (esp. a child) who has been attacked by diarrhœa. --gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. an attack of diarrhœa to come on. -kay (= قی دست) m.pl. severe bilious purging and vomiting; cholera. -kay gaʦhȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. an attack of cholera, etc., to occur. -nôrᵘ m. disease of the rectum caused by excessive diarrhœa. -nāwa gaʦhañĕ f. pl. inf. an attack of excessive watery diarrhœa to occur. -pakȧnⁱ m.pl., id. -rōz f. a diseased state of the body due to frequent diarrhœa. --ʦalȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. sudden violent diarrhœa to occur. --ʦaṭȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the pain or gripes due to excessive diarrhœa to occur. --vĕsarȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to void a loose stool owing to fear.
m. a model, exemplar, rule, canon, formula (Rām. 682); a rule, custom, practice (Gr.M.); a custom, habit (Gr.M.).
f. 'dustoorie', an allowance of money in a price, a commission.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dosᵘ; 2 p.p. dasōv or dasyōv, Gr.Gr. 208, 225), to slap with the open hand, thump with the fist, etc. ¶ dȧsⁱ dȧsⁱ freq. part., beating frequently; hence dȧsⁱ dȧsⁱ sŏn adj. c.g. having beaten gold frequently; met. made firm and strong by beating (as gold is heated and beaten to purify it); fine gold, valuable as pure gold (K.Pr. 259). ¶ dosᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (fem. düsᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), slapped, thumped. ¶ dasith thawun m.inf. to slap, thump, esp. one who is weaker than oneself, to bully. --trāwun -- m.inf. to slap or thump severely.
m. (sg. dat. dāsatas; pl. nom. dāsath), servitude, slavery, the condition of a servant.

adj. c.g. (as subst. f. dasᵃladiñ), one (or that) concerning whom (or which) preparations have been delayed, e.g. a bridegroom at a wedding, or a Hindū boy at the initiation ceremony, in which delay has occurred owing to faulty preparation or indolence.
or ḍāsurᵘ m. (f. ḍāsarĕñ), one who is destructive, who makes a habit of destroying things or of seattering things collected, a destroyer (Gr.Gr. 148).
(but with change of meaning) f. a kind of wide, shallow basket, used for holding fruit, flowers, or the like.
adv. quickly, without delay, at once (Śiv. 1874).

m. [sg. voc. dātā (Rām. 946)], a giver (Śiv. 1730); esp. one who is a generous giver, one who gives liberally in charity (Śiv. 859, K. 842); one who is liberal, generous (Śiv. 1776); the client of a sacrificing priest, the person for whom he sacrifices and who gives the sacrifice. In the voc. it is equivalent to our polite 'sir' (Rām. 946). -bāy f. the wife of the client of a sacrificing priest. -dihī f. extreme liberality, lavish generosity, esp. in giving charitable gifts on the occasion of a festival, at sacred spots, or the like. -gara m. the house of a sacrificing priest's client. The compound is chiefly used in counting; e.g. such and such a priest has so many houses, i.e. so many clients.
i.q. dāta 1, q.v. (Śiv. 667); also voc. of dāta 1 (Rām. 946) and 2 (Rām. 732).
f. [voc. sg. dātā (Rām. 732)], 'a female supporter,' a nurse, a mother.

f. (sg. dat. dati, Gr.Gr. 70), a lump of earth or mud, a clod (K.Pr. 187, Śiv. 1531); dirty earth, mud, etc. (Śiv. 535). mĕʦi-datī voc. f., O thou who art like a clod of earth (Rām. 1603). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a lump of clay to happen (upon the heart), a weight of care, anxiety, or longing (e.g. for the return of some loved one far from home) to lie upon the heart. ¶ data kaḍañĕ f. pl. inf. to extract (i.e. pick up) clods (as missiles); met. to vituperate, to scold or abuse with virulence. -waturᵘ m. clod-flinging; met. virulent abuse, vituperation. -waturᵘ gaʦhun m.inf. to be violently overwhelmed or dissipated (as if under a rain of clods). -waturᵘ karun m.inf. to violently overwhelm or dissipate as ab. -waturᵘ sapazun m.inf., i.q. data-waturᵘ gaʦhun, ab.

m. (sg. dat. dātas), a primary element of the earth; a metal (Śiv. 1556), mineral, ore; an element of words, a grammatical or verbal root or stem; one of the seven humours of the body, semen. --pakun -- m.inf. spermatorrhoea to occur. --ʦalun -- m.inf. an involuntary emission of semen to occur.
m. a large mass of bhūrja-bark paper (whether written on or not) with the sheets stuck together in a mass.

m. (sg. dat. dātharas), a general name for all the tools and appliances needed or used by a workman or artisan. Cf. dŏbⁱ-dāthur under dọ̆bᵘ 1. --wahārun -- m.inf. to spread out one's tools preparatory to commencing a work.

f. a woman who is in the habit of splitting or marring (either inanimate objects or friendships, etc.), a mischief-maker (lit. and fig.). dạthᵃri-nāsh m. a man who habitually spoils other people's businesses, or corrupts other people's habits or natures.
f. (sg. dat. -shĕkᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), power or ability to grant all that a petitioner asks for.
m. (sg. dat. -dŏgalis, ag. and pl. nom. -dŏgᵃ̇lᵃ̇), a sudden fall into deep sleep owing to exhaustion, weariness, or the like.

m. (sg. dat. dataris, ag. and pl. nom. datᵃ̇rᵃ̇), the white thorn-apple, Datura alba (El. Datura stramonium and D. fastuosa; L. 76) (used as a poison); a single leaf, flower, or fruit of this shrub. --lagun -- m.inf. datura to take effect, intoxication to be induced by eating datura; met. to be felt like datura, (of food proffered) to be regarded with extreme disgust or aversion (as if thought to be poison). ¶ datᵃ̇rᵃ̇-bạrᵃ̇g m. datura-leaf. -byôlᵘ  m. datura-seed. -kã̄ḍ m. the stem or trunk of the datura-shrub. -kulᵘ m. the datura-shrub. -konḍᵘ m. the thorns surrounding the seed capsule of the datura. -kāṭh m. (sg. dat. -kāṭhas), a piece of dry datura-wood. -pan m. a collection of datura leaves. -pōsh m. the datura-flower. -wạthᵃr m. a datura-leaf.
m. (sg. dat. dātatas), a habit of or natural disposition for giving gifts, generosity, a charitable disposition.
f. a kind of small virulent ant. ¶ dạtᵃrĕ pĕñĕ f. pl. inf. ants to fall, the irritation caused by these ants to be experienced.
m. the hope or expectation of help from any person in endeavouring to obtain anything.
m. a piece of thread, so much as is put on a needle at one time. Cf. dôwᵘ.

f. running (Gr.Gr. 128); the swift current of a stream (Śiv. 506); āb-dav, a water current, a water drain (H. iv, 4). --tulüñᵘ̈ -- to raise running, to set off or set out at a run, to run off, hasten away (Śiv. 699). ¶ dava-dav (= دوا دو) f. running to and fro or in every direction, bustling about; being active or energetic in any business. -dav gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. such running to and fro to occur. ¶ davi-davi adv. running to and fro; hence, quickly, eagerly, not only u.w. vbs. of motion, but also met., as in the case of eating.

m. a time, turn; opportunity, chance (K.Pr. 41); a stroke or cast in a game; a charge or counter-charge in a dispute, a retort; an attack or counter-attack in gaming or in a dispute (Rām. 1349). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. an opportunity to come (K.Pr. 41); (in gaming or a quarrel, of one previously conquered) fortune to turn, an opportunity for a counter-move or counter-charge to occur. ¶ dāwa-har f. mutual retort, a quarrel consisting in accusations and counter-accusations, or in attacks and counter-attacks. ¶ dāwas bihun m.inf. to sit under an attack, esp. in gaming or in a quarrel to be subject to a violent attack resulting in loss. --logᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. pass. (f. --lüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), one who is subject to an attack, esp. a person who, owing to his being alone and friendless, is being forcibly dragged into some losing business. --lagun -- m.inf. to be attacked as ab.

a stake, a wager. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. a wager to be laid, a bet to be made. --khārun -- m.inf. to raise a stake; hence, to wager, make a bet, lay a stake. --khasun -- m.inf. a stake to ascend, a wager to be laid, a bet to be made. --karun -- m.inf. to challenge one to a wager, to offer a bet. --ladun -- m.inf. to lay a bet, (in a dispute) to offer a bet.
adv. running, very quickly, at once, u.w. vbs. of motion.

f.pl. a general name for the finer 'strings' (i.e. muscles, veins, arteries, etc.) of the body. Cf. dāv 1. --galañĕ -- f. pl. inf. the 'strings' to melt away, to become weak and lean from disease, sorrow, or the like.
m. (f. dāwādārĕñ), a claimant; the plaintiff in a lawsuit (K.Pr. 54).
c.g. one who holds a claim, a persistent claimant, one who will carry his claim even into a future life.

or dawā دوا m. medicine, physic (K.Pr. 116, Rām. 897, 1320). For gender see W. 18. khŏrākh dawāhukᵘ, a dose of medicine (Gr.M.). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take medicine. --karun -- m.inf. to do medicine, to attend (a patient) (Gr.M.).

or dāwā دعویٰ m. a pretension, claim, demand; a complaint founded on a claim (W. 142, K.Pr. 170); a plaint in an action at law; charge, accusation; an objection, contention, assertion (Rām. 987; El. dáwá). --āsun -- m.inf. a claim for property to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to make a claim; to raise an objection (Gr.M.). --thawun -- m.inf. to make a claim, put in a claim (Gr.M.).
f. an unchaste woman (Gr.Gr. 107), a woman unchaste in practice and by inclination; when --˚ this word is masc. (Gr.Gr. 107), cf. bĕñĕ-dāwal, mājĕ-dāwal.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. dawanôwᵘ), to cause to run, make to run (El.).

or (Gr.Gr. 172) diwanāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. dāwanôwᵘ), i.q. dāwun, q.v. gōsa diwanāwun, to provoke anger (Gr.M.); dēv ʦhĕpa diwanöwin, he caused the gods to (run away and) hide themselves (Śiv. 123), cf. pānas ʦhĕpa dāwañĕ under dāwun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. f. dāwanöwᵘ̈), to cause (a woman) to be unchaste with some third person, to prostitute a woman. Caus. of dāwüñᵘ̈, q.v.
f. (sg. dat. dawöʦᵘ̈), an inkholder, an inkstand, an inkhorn, a portable case with receptacles for ink, writing-reeds, etc.
n.ag. (f. dāwawüñᵘ̈), one who causes to give; one who causes to be given, one who gives by the hand of another (Śiv. 855, 867).
m. a drought, a total failure of rain when it is required. Cf. drāg.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dowᵘ. This verb is impersonal in the tenses formed from the past participles. Thus dowun, it was run by him, he ran), to run, go quickly, hasten (Śiv. 880, 1494). ¶ dawān pres. part. c.g. running, hence, as adv. very quickly, u.w. vbs. of going, eating, reading, etc. ¶ dawönⁱ adverbial part. while running; hence, adv. very quickly, u.w. any verb. ¶ davyō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. davyē-müʦᵘ̈), running, going at a great speed.

conj. 1 [poet. pres. part. dāwan (Śiv. 1094, 1756), 1 p.p. dôwᵘ ], to cause to give (Śiv. 130, 605, 646, 691, 1817); to cause to be given, to give through another person (Śiv. 26, 519, 736, 1182, 1787, 1879). Causal of dyunᵘ (q.v.) in all its meanings (Gr.Gr. 172). El. spells this word dyāwun. Cf. dāwanāwun. gŏta dāwun, to cause (so and so) to dive (Śiv. 1397); ṭakh dāwun, to cause lopping to be done, to be lopped (W. 149, K.Pr. 260); pānas ʦhĕpa dāwañĕ, to cause oneself to become invisible (Śiv. 1756); wŏṭh dāwüñᵘ̈, to cause (so and so) to leap (Śiv. 1815). ¶ dôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. döwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to be given, given through another person.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. f. döwᵘ̈), to be unchaste (of a woman).

m. [sg. abl. dayĕ, often written dayi; voc. dayĕ (Śiv. 513, 1288, etc.)]. The Supreme Deity conceived as a person, the personal Deity, God, Providence, Fate, the Arbiter of destiny (often written dai or daī in the Roman character) (K.Pr. 54, 201; Śiv. 159, 282, 915; Ram. 1709, 1729; K. 35, 112, 528). boḍᵘ day, the great god, a N. given to Viṣṇu in Śiv. 1383, 1487 (voc. baḍi dayĕ). ¶ dayĕ-bata m. the first ceremonial eating together of a bride and bridegroom (Śiv. 1202, 1223). -dana m. wealth devoted to God, church property, money devoted, or intended to be devoted, to God (Śiv. 952); God's wealth, heavenly riches, i.e. true wealth, complete union with the Deity, extreme and real holiness (Śiv. 1067, 1216, 1240, 1347, 1554, 1754). -dayĕ karun m.inf. to say "O God, O God", to console oneself when at the end of one's resources by repeatedly calling God to mind. -gara m. God's house, paradise, heaven (Rām. 583); a mountain or forest hermitage. -gath f. (sg. dat. -güʦᵘ̈), God's going, the way of God, God's actions (Śiv. 1652, 1787; Rām. 30, 122, 1296; K. 45, 78, 210, 313, 608, 1105); a piece of good luck (Śiv. 693). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. 'to become of Providence', to be providence to anyone, to show a person extreme favour, granting more even than he hoped for. -gazab m. 'the wrath of Providence', harsh fate, being reduced to utter poverty by some sudden calamity. -kahᵃr m. 'fury of Providence', being overwhelmed by some sudden calamity. -krapā f. the favour of Providence; complete success even when one has not had the necessary means for securing it. -lônᵘ m. fate, Providence (Śiv. 1546, 1628, Rām. 1604, K. 34). -muʦᵘ m. profit from Providence, the cup of prosperity being filled to overflowing. -röchⁱ f. protection by Providence, the being in God's keeping. -wö̃ʦh m. (sg. dat. -wö̃ʦas), 'deceiving by Providence,' sudden and unexpected failure when apparently on the brink of success. --wö̃ʦun -- m.inf. cheating by Providence to occur, unsuccess as ab. to take place. ¶ dȧyⁱ gaʦhun m.inf., i.q. dayĕ gaʦhun ab. --wū̃ʦᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (--vǖ̃ʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈--), become cheated by Providence, finding oneself unexpectedly unsuccessful when on the brink of success.

card. (f. ḍāy or ḍāyĕ), two and a half (often written ḍai or ḍāī in the roman character) (K.Pr. 80, W. 105, 106). -gaz pl.m. two yards and a half (Śiv. 1235, 1284). ¶ ḍāyĕ gürᵘ̈ f. two and a half gürᵘ̈s (or space of twenty-four minutes each and thus roughly equivalent to one English hour) (K.Pr. 102); so ḍāyĕnᵘ̈y garĕn, for only two and a half gürᵘ̈s, for but an hour (K.Pr. 105). See gürᵘ̈ 1. --khôrᵘ -- adj. (f. --khörᵘ̈ --), weighing two and a half kharwārs of about 152 lb. each; also, in fem. subst. f., a weight for weighing that amount. --monᵘ --  adj. (f. --müñᵘ̈ --), weighing two a half manwaṭās or mans (cf. man 2) of 3 lb. each, i.e. weighing 3 3/4 sērs or 7 1/2 lb. --pôwᵘ 1 -- adj. (f. --pövᵘ̈ --), measuring two and a half spans (of twelve finger-breadths each); a span is about 96 barley-corns, cf. ongul. --pôwᵘ 2 -- adj. (f. --pövᵘ̈ --), weighing two and a half pāvs (of 20 tōlās each, a pāv being a quarter of a sēr); as subst. m. or f., a weight used for weighing that amount. --syūrᵘ -- adj. (f. --sīrᵘ̈ --), weighing two and a half sērs of about two pounds each; as subst. in f., a weight for weighing that amount. ¶ ḍöyⁱ bāgay f. division into two and a half portions, i.e. three shares, two of two-fifths each, and the remaining share of one-fifth. ¶ ḍāyĕ-y pōsh tula adj. c.g. weighing but two and a half flowers; hence, met. very delicate-limbed, tender in limb.
m. advice, counsel. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give advice, to advise. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take advice, receive counsel. --wanun -- m.inf. to address advice (to a person), to advise.

f. (often spelt dāī in the Roman character), a maidservant; esp. a maidservant in attendance on a woman, a lady's maid; a nurse (Gr.M., YZ. 20, Śiv. 437, 1237, Rām. 1038). zanāna-dāy, f. a maidservant (Gr.M.). ¶ dāyĕ-bāpār m. conduct like that of a maidservant, fondness for serving (esp. on the part of a woman who is not a servant). -küṭᵘ̈ f. a female servant's daughter. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), her son. -kȧthᵃr m. a female servant's son (an affectionate term used in the presence of her mistress). -wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), possessing maidservants, a rich man (or woman) whose household is well supplied with them.

f. sympathy, mercy, compassion, pity, (to, for = pĕṭh) (Śiv. 17, 105, 189, 452, etc.; K. 137, 764, 983, 1103); humanity (Gr.M.); favour, kindness (El. daiyá); mercy personified, the goddess of mercy (Śiv. 1495); hence often used as a name of the goddess Durgā or Pārvatī, the wife of Śiva (Śiv. 36, 103, 1129, 1139, 1155, 1223). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show mercy, to show kindness (on = pĕṭh) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 36, 466, 628, 645, 760, 987, 1129, 1296, 1534, 1851). --karith -- conj. part. having shown mercy, used as an interj. = 'please' (Gr.M.). ¶ dayāyĕ or dayāyi sg. dat. ag. and abl. used as interj., in (your) mercy, please, have the kindness to. --kinⁱ -- or --sṻty -- (Śiv. 192, 1319, 1483), id. -pĕṭh āmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), one (e.g. a god, a master, or a spiritual preceptor) who has become kindly disposed (to any person). -pĕṭh yunᵘ m.inf. 'to come upon kindness', to become kindly disposed (towards any person) (Śiv. 1236).
adj. c.g. one who shows mercy, compassionate (Śiv. 234, voc. dayākarō).
(Śiv. 1217) or dayālu (Śiv. 159), adj. c.g. merciful, compassionate. (Voc. dayālā, Śiv. 1697; dayālō, Śiv. 466, 915.)
adj. c.g. pitiful, merciful by nature, tender-hearted, mild, gentle, kind, humane (Śiv. 158, 238, 427, etc.; Rām. 1388); N. of God, the All-Merciful (Śiv. 364, 466, etc.).
m. (sg. dat. dāyĕkas), a wise counsellor, adviser, prompter (Śiv. 667); the person who teaches the necessary procedure in any festival, marriage, etc.
m. (sg. dat. as in 1). --˚, one who is accustomed to give, a provider, as in mokshĕ- dāyĕkh, he who gives salvation; phala-dāyĕkh, he who gives the fruit (of virtuous actions, etc.).
m. conduct like that of a maidservant (of a woman who is not a servant, but acting as one); nursehood (Gr.Gr. 144).
m. the condition or nature of a servant-maid, readiness to work, or the habit of working, as a servant-maid.
f. (sg. dat. -güʦᵘ̈), i.q. dayĕ-gath, q.v. under day.

(sg. dat. day ĕtas pl. nom. dayĕth), a house-god, one of the tutelary deities of a house. ¶ dayĕth-gāḍa f.pl. an offering of cooked rice and fish made in the dark half of the month of Pŏh (Sanskrit Pauṣa = December-January), on a Tuesday or Saturday, to the tutelary gods of a house. Cf. gāḍa-bata, s.v. gāḍ. --rāza -- m. the chief of the tutelary gods of a house, the archetype or ideal pattern of a house personified as a deity.
f.pl. of dodᵘ, see dodᵘ and dazun.

m. burning; ostentatious pride or self-conceit, such as is calculated to arouse jealousy; rage, indignation against some person or thing. ¶ daza-buza m. 'burning-parching', pride of wealth or beauty, extreme self-conceit, extreme vanity. -buza āsun such pride or self-conceit to exist continually (in a person). -buza gaʦhun m.inf. jealous hatred to arise owing to another flaunting his or her wealth, beauty, high rank, or the like. -buza hyonᵘ m.inf. jealous hatred to spring up at the sight of another's qualities, wealth, honours, beauty, or the like. ¶ daza-daza m. burning, a feeling of burning; burning pain (K.Pr. 16); hatred caused by the prosperity of another, envious hatred. -daza āsun m.inf. envy or jealousy to exist continually (in a person's heart). -daza gaʦhun m.inf. jealous hatred owing to another's prosperity to arise (in a person's heart). -daza hyonᵘ m.inf. rage owing to opposition to arise. -daza karun m.inf. jealous anger to arise at the spectacle of another's prosperity. -nār pyonᵘ m.inf. 'burning-fire to fall'; the rage or indignation caused by an enemies' success, or by opposition to oneself, to occur. --ta buza hyonᵘ -- m.inf. burning and parching to take (a person), intoxication of pride of place or of pride of wealth, etc., to become manifest; violent fever to occur.

adj. c.g. of a burning nature; esp. used with reference to a certain kind of rice-soil, chiefly found in low-lying ground near swamps, but also sometimes in the uplands. It is hot and feverish, and special precautions must be taken to run off irrigation water when the rice plant shows signs of a too rapid growth (L. 320).
n.ag. (f. dazawüñᵘ̈), on fire, burning (K.Pr. 54); alight (of a candle, lamp, etc.) (Rām. 721).

conj. 2 [1 p.p. dodᵘ (often written dọ̆dᵘ), f. düzᵘ̈ (K.Pr. 80, 178); 2 p.p. dazōv, pl. dazöy, f. dazöyĕ (Gr.Gr. 227)], to burn, to be burnt (K.Pr. 8, 9, 61, 150, 210; YZ. 10, 397; Śiv. 1650, 1818); (of a woman) to be burnt as a satī (Śiv. 117); (of a flower, a garden, etc.) to be burnt, parched, by drought (Śiv. 948); met. to be touched, moved, or inflamed (with pity, etc.) (YZ. 557); to feel pain, sorrow, anguish (K.Pr. 2); to be enraged; to be jealous, be consumed with envy or jealousy (K.Pr. 161). The caus. of this verb is zālun (Gr.Gr. 176). ¶ dodᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. düzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), burnt (Rām. 759); (of a flower, a garden, etc.) burnt, parched, withered by heat (Śiv. 345, 1611, 1686); filled with anger and hatred; burnt, filled with agony (YZ. 298, 514, Rām. 1393). ¶ dazan-ākh m. (sg. dat. -ākhas), a mark or scar left on the skin after a burn has healed, a brand. -dāg m. a mark of burning (on cloth, wood, etc.). -dawāh m. (sg. dat. -dawāhas), a healing ointment for application to a burn. -mŏshᵉ̆kh m. (sg. dat. -mŏshkas), the smell of burning. ¶ dazana yunᵘ m.inf. pass., i.q. dazun (Gr.Gr. 169). ¶ dazanas dôdᵘ m. (there is) pain from a burn (K.Pr. 54, W. 124). ¶ dazith pyōmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --pyēmüʦᵘ̈--), risen to extreme prosperity, esp. when the rise is undeserved. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to become extremely prosperous, esp. when this is undeserved.
m. looseness, slackness, flaccidity, esp. of a box or the like made of wooden boards which is loose or slack in the interior. Cf. ḍyobᵘ.

f. an elderly lady, such as a mother, grandmother, the chief wife in a household. The term is used by the sons or grandsons, etc. The voc. is dĕdi (K.Pr. 54, 80). Met. a term of respect added to a female name, as in Lāl Dĕd, the famous Kāshmīrī poetess, whose songs are household words (cf. K.Pr. 20, 47, etc.). The corresponding word for 'father' is bāba (K.Pr. 22). -möjᵘ̈ f. an ancient dame, such as an old grandmother, a term of respect used by her descendants.
(? spelling), a kind of fern, which is dried and eaten in winter (L. 73).

f. a large metal pot (for culinary or other purposes), a cauldron, kettle (K.Pr. 54, 193, W. 119, Śiv. 1533). ¶ dēga-bata m. a large pile of rice cooked in a cauldron, for a wedding feast or the like.

or dĕgulᵘ (sg. dat. dĕgalas), m. a globular wide-mouthed earthen pot for cooking meat (K.Pr. 107, 229). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go to pot, to become like the contents of a pot; met. (of human beings, esp. when struck by some epidemic) to lie crowded together; (of earthen vessels) lying close together so as to be liable to knock against each other.
(Śiv. 1856) or dēha-abimān  (Śiv. 1758), m. pride in one's own body, self-conceit; spiritual delusion.
(Śiv. 1208, 1425) or dēha-andakār  (Śiv. 1685, 1807), darkness of the body, darkness caused by the existence of the body, spiritual delusion, spiritual ignorance.
m. looseness, slackness; looseness of a knot or the like; slackness in work.
ḍĕji 1, ḍë˘jᵘ̈, see ḍyolᵘ and ḍyojᵘ.

m. (sg. ag. ḍĕkan or ḍĕkⁱ), the forehead, brow (YZ. 447; Śiv. 467, 1147, 1155, 1189; Rām. 969, 1353, 1430); fate, destiny, fortune (conceived by Hindūs to be written on the forehead) (K.Pr. 183, Rām. 721); a woman's fate, her husband; good luck, success (El.). -boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), one endowed with great luck, one who is well born and prosperous (El.); in fem., esp. of a woman blessed with such a husband (Rām. 734). -bajĕr m. good luck, prosperity. -dĕd f. a woman who is lucky in having a good husband. -dag f. the death of a woman's husband. -drölid adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -drölⁱdĕñ), poor in fate, one whose fate is adverse, even though he deserves prosperity. --gᵃhun -- m.inf. to grind the forehead (in the dust), to implore very humbly. -lônᵘ m. fate, lot in life (YZ. 326); a woman's fate, her husband (Śiv. 438). -lônᵘ wuchun m.inf. to see one's fate, to test one's fate, to inquire as to the result of any undertaking, to have one's fortune told. -munörᵘ̈ f. waning of good luck, loss (even when undeserved) of good fortune. --nērun -- m.inf. fortune to issue, the fated result of any condition to issue or become manifest. -pĕṭhukᵘ adj. (f. -pĕṭhücᵘ̈), of or belonging to on the forehead (as of the down on the forehead, or of an ornament, or of the intellect). -pĕṭhukᵘṭika adj. c.g. an ornament of on the forehead; met. one who is highly respected, venerated (Śiv. 407), see -ṭika and ḍĕkukᵘ ṭika bel. -röñᵘ̈ f. a fate-queen, a woman lucky in having an excellent husband. -sĕdath f. (sg. dat. -sĕdüʦᵘ̈), good fortune, success (Rām. 1598). -ṭhĕl f. height, broadness, expansiveness, of the forehead. -ṭika m. an ornament worn on the forehead, an ornamental patch of gold, silver, tinsel, or the like, or a jewel worn on the forehead. -ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ f. a black mark (made with charcoal or the like) on the forehead; a woman who goes proudly, as if boasting of her good fortune, whether she really has good fortune or not. -ʦṻṭhᵘ̈ f. a woman who goes about boasting of the excellence of her husband, esp. such a woman who does so without valid reason. Cf. ʦũ̄̈ṭhᵘ̈ and ḍĕkⁱ sᵃs trāwȧnⁱ below. ¶ ḍĕkⁱ ḍĕkⁱ karun m.inf. good luck to come upon good luck, a steady increase in good fortune to occur. ḍĕkⁱ ḍĕkⁱ karān yunᵘ m.inf. to come along on one's forehead, to show the greatest humility, to beg and implore with utter self-abasement. ḍĕkⁱ sᵃs trāwȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to strut about proclaiming one's good fortune, to boast of one's prosperity. Cf. sᵃs, and also ḍĕka ʦũ̄̈ṭhᵘ̈ ab. ¶ ḍĕkukᵘ adj. (f. ḍĕkücᵘ̈), of or belonging to the forehead, either of things external, such as an ornament, or of things internal, such as the forehead-bone or the intellect. --bata -- m. rice of luck; a man's support in life which he gets by mere luck, and which he does not deserve as a reward for his industry or virtue. --ṭika -- m. one who shines like a forehead ornament, a person of great honour, one much respected. Cf. ḍĕka pĕṭhukᵘ ṭika ab. ¶ ḍĕkunᵘ adj. (f. ḍĕküñᵘ̈), of or belonging to fate; of or belonging to a woman's husband. --bata khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat the rice of one's fate; hence, when a man is deprived of office for some fault or other reason, to sit idle, living on what one has of one's own without pay. ¶ ḍĕkas ḍūnⁱ phuṭarāwȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to break walnuts on the forehead (as if to show how sound it is); to boast openly of one's good fortune, to act boastfully. ḍĕkas ḍĕkas dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to reproach one's fate, curse one's luck, as when one suddenly comes upon an unexpected obstacle, or when something begun well turns out badly.
f. a machine for drawing water (being a lever supported on a long post, having a bucket suspended to one end and a weight of earth or stone at the other), a dip-well (L. 324, 459, dhenkli).
f. (sg. dat. dĕküʦᵘ̈), trouble, perplexity, difficulty, distress.
f. (sg. dat. ḍĕküʦᵘ̈), a fault, imperfection (of any thing, business, or the like).

or dĕkh دق m. (sg. dat. dēkhas), difficulty, trouble, worry; esp. the feeling of annoyance caused by another's abuse, etc. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be harassed by abuse. --karun -- m.inf. to trouble, worry (Gr.M.); to harass by abuse. -lay f. reproach for abuse, reproach tendered to one who is harassing another by abuse. -lāyĕ diñĕ f. pl. inf. to tender such reproaches.

or dēkh (q.v.) دق m. (sg. dat. dĕkas or dĕkhas), difficulty, trouble, worry, distress, harassment; consumption, pulmonary disease. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be irritated, annoyed, worried, harassed by abuse, etc. --karun -- m.inf. to tease, irritate, annoy, trouble, harass, worry, plague. ¶ dĕkⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to be worried, troubled, consumed by grief, as if one were suffering from consumption, esp. by the conduct of a loved son, wife, or the like.
or dĕkh-kār m. reproach, contemptuous address, scoffing.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. dēkhaladiñ), one who is sorrowful, grieved, unhappy (Gr.M.); annoyed, worried; esp. one who is annoyed by another's abuse.

m. husk, rind, peel, bark (K.Pr. 8, 80); skin of the body (K.Pr. 169). (In K.Pr. 8, 169, this word is written dyal.) --tulȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to raise skins; met. to beat a man with a cane so as to raise blisters or weals. --wālȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to strip skins; to skin a man, or to bark a tree; met. to beat a person with a stick so as to give him the pain of being skinned alive.
f. a thong made of straw (El.).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ḍĕlyōv), to be or become slack, loose (e.g. a knot or the like); to be slack, ill, weary; to lose one's powers from old age, etc.; (of rice) to be spoilt by excessive boiling, to be boiled to a mash. ¶ ḍĕlyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ḍĕlyē-müʦᵘ̈), loosened, etc., as ab.
m. (sg. dat. dĕlaras), i.q. dĕlᵃr, but larger.
m. N. of a village to the west of Śrīnagar, near Vārāhamūla (Baramula).
f. a piece of thick bark of a tree, rind, cork.

m. the brain; the air passages within the head; airs, conceit, pride, haughtiness, arrogance. --hāwun -- m.inf. to show great conceit, to put on airs (esp. in order to avoid doing something one is asked to do) (Rām. 1605). --khārun -- m.inf. to cause conceit to rise, to cause another to show conceit, to turn another's head. --khasun -- m.inf. pride to rise, airs to be put on, the head to be turned (esp. when one is asked to do something). --raṭun -- m.inf. to hold conceit; to abstain from asking for help for fear of being insulted by a refusal. --wālun -- m.inf. to cause conceit to descend, to bring another's pride low, to humble one to the dust. --wasun -- m.inf. pride to be brought low, to be humbled to the dust.
adj. (f. -dārĕñ), vain, conceited; proud, haughty, arrogant.
m. the middle part of the inside (of a boat), the hold. ḍĕmb-ḍĕmb m. looseness of the contents of a hold recognized by their shaking together and sinking. Cf. ḍĕm-ḍĕm.

m. an island; esp. an artificial lake-island built up when the water is low so as to stand above flood-level [these are cultivated and are very fertile (L. 345); sheep also graze on them (L. 363)]; a ferry, a ford (El.). Cf. ḍēm. ¶ ḍēmba-gŏgᵃ̇jᵃ̇ or -gŏgᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a kind of turnip grown on these islands, described as heavy, not well flavoured, and when eaten tending to produce phlegm or mucus. -hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), the green leaves of the above turnip used as a kind of spinach, said to be pungent and not otherwise well flavoured. The seeds of the plant are like mustard-seeds, and yield oil (K.Pr. 153). -hönzᵘ̈ m. (f. -hānzĕñ, but his wife is -hönzᵘ̈-bāy), a cultivator of such an island. His wife usually assists him, and takes the products to market in a little skiff (W. 115, L. 381); the -hānzĕñ works on her own account. -nāv f. the tiny dug-out or skiff in which vegetables from such islands are brought to market (L. 381). -rād m. a floating-island, such as exist on the Ḍal lake and elsewhere in Kashmir. Root crops and the like are grown upon them. -ʦakh m. peat (L. 62).

m. the sound made by a cracked or loose-jointed metal vessel, wooden board, or the like, when tapped by the finger. Cf. ḍĕmb-ḍĕmb, under ḍĕmb. ḍĕm-ḍĕm karun m.inf. to test for a crack in the ab. manner. ḍĕm-ḍĕm gaʦhun m.inf. the sound of a crack or the like to issue when such a test is made.

adj. c.g. of or belonging to the brain; vain, conceited; proud, haughty, arrogant. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. lit. to become brainy, hence to become mad, delirious; to become unconscious, to collapse (e.g. when at the point of death).

or din 1 m. a day, the period between sunrise and sunset, daytime (K.Pr. 48, din; 187, dĕn; Śiv. 1002, 1032; Rām. 225, 419); a day of twenty-four hours, a day and night; a day, the day of such and such an event, a date; (in pl.) days, the time of such and such a state of affairs (Śiv. 110); adv. by day, in the daytime (Śiv. 1555). --barun -- m.inf. to get through the day,:esp. under circumstances of difficulty, such as want of food, sickness, or the like, to tide over the day somehow or other (Śiv. 1065). -dĕn kaḍun m.inf. to pass several days in ineffectually endeavouring to carry through some business; to waste one's time over an impossible task. --guzarāwun -- m.inf. to pass the day, spend the day (Śiv. 1624). -rāth (Śiv. 107, 1554; Rām. 1673) or rāth-dĕn (Śiv. 160, 215, 524, 541, 735, 986), adv. day and night, night and day, continually. ¶ dĕna or dina adv. on (such and such) a day (Śiv. 1042, 1413; with ō added m.c.dĕnō (Śiv. 1420). dĕna dĕna or dina dina adv. daily, every day (Śiv. 1412). dĕna-parimān m. the extent of a day, the varying length of a day between sunrise and sunset.
m. a debtor; esp. with ref. to a creditor, the man who owes him money, so-and-so's debtor.
m. the condition of not being securely based, instability (esp. of some heavy globular object).
f. a cow, used in the compound kāma-dēnu , in Sanskrit 'kāmadhēnu', the mythical cow from which all desires are milked, the cow of plenty (Śiv. 1439).
m. (sg. dat. dēnukas), N. of a demon slain by Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) (K. 225).

:m. (sg. abl. ḍēra 1), a collection, accumulation; a heap, mound, pile, stack (K.Pr. 118, Śiv. 1185); a store, granary, magazine (El., Siv. 1862); --˚ plenty of, as in dyāra-ḍēr, plenty of money (K.Pr. 137). --gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. heaps to occur; (of things left unswept away owing to laziness) to lie scattered about in heaps. --khārȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to raise heaps, to leave things in untidy heaps. --khasȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. heaps to be raised; to become piled in heaps (of dust, etc.) (Śiv. 1238). --sārun -- m.inf. to collect a heap, to pile up a heap (K.Pr. 48).

m. a tent, temporary dwelling, abiding place, temporary lodging in another's house when away from home. --ḍēra phērun -- m.inf. to wander from lodging to lodging, esp. when one has no house of one's own; to spend time fruitlessly. --dith bĕhun -- m.inf. to take a temporary lodging and remain there uninterruptedly during one's stay (e.g. when a spy or detective wishes to observe another's actions). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to pitch one's tent, determine upon the place of one's temporary lodging; to settle down temporarily in a place for the purpose of protecting or spying on someone. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to wander about living temporarily in various places, esp. in forests. --trāwun -- m.inf. to settle down near someone else for some purpose.
or dish f. a point of the compass, quarter, cardinal point, of which usually ten are counted, the four main points, the four intermediate points, the zenith, and the nadir (Śiv. 521, Rām. 1770).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ḍēshĕnôwᵘ), to cause, to see, show. Cf. ḍēshun.
n.ag. (f. dēshĕwüñᵘ̈), one who sees, perceives, observes, etc. (YZ. 68).
adv. visibly, before one's very eyes; immediately on seeing (YZ. 32, 178, 260, 412; Śiv. 654; Rām. 655).

or conj. 1 [1 p.p. ḍyūṭhᵘ (K.Pr. 47), pl. ḍīṭhⁱ; f. ḍīṭhᵘ̈ (K.Pr. 47), pl. ḍēchĕ; 2 p.p. ḍēchyōv (cf. Śiv. 1108); conj. part. ḍīshith (K.Pr. 34, 146, 154; YZ. 15, 167, 203, 247, 465; Śiv. 498, 600, etc.)], to see, look, look at, behold, view, observe, perceive (YZ. 21); cyāni ḍēshĕna, by thy seeing, i.e. by seeing thee (Śiv. 1044), (K.Pr. 188 has dúnṭhum for ḍyūṭhum). The pass. of this verb is drē̃ṭh yunᵘ, to be seen (Gr.Gr. 169), see drē̃ṭh. For its causal, hāwun, to show, is used (Gr.Gr. 176); cf., however, ḍēshĕnāwun. ¶ ḍyūṭhᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (pl. ḍīṭhⁱ-mȧtⁱ; f. ḍīṭhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, pl. ḍēchĕ-maʦa), seen, perceived, observed, etc.
sg. ag. and pl. nom. of dyosᵘ, q.v.

a prefix converting an interrogative word into an intensive affirmative (Gr.Gr. 256), as in the following: --kana -- adv. a long time ago (Gr.Gr. 257). --kȧnⁱ -- adv. for a long time (Gr.Gr. 257). --kani -- adv. a long time ago. --kar -- adv., id. (Gr.Gr. 257). --kōr -- adv., very much, exceedingly, esp. u.w. vbs. signifying good bodily health, freedom from sickness, etc. --kati -- adv., i.q. --kar ab. --kotᵘ -- adv. very much, exceedingly, in great quantity. --kūtᵘ -- adj. (pl. --kǖtⁱ --; f. --kǖʦᵘ̈ --, pl. --kṻʦa --), very much (in quantity), (pl.) in great numbers (Gr.Gr. 257). Equivalent to Hindī bahut kuch. --kyāh --  inan. c.g. everything (= Hindī sab kuch); a great deal (Gr.Gr. 257).
or ḍē̃ṭun m. (sg. dat. ḍē̃ṭanas), a girdle, waist-band, cummerbund (El. ḍenṭon). Cf. darb and dash. ḍē̃ṭan-lāṭh m. a light, small, waist-band (chiefly worn by women).

m. (sg. abl. dĕwa 1; f. dĕviñ), a devil, demon, spirit, ghost, hobgoblin (K.Pr. 55, Rām. 445, 641, etc.); like our 'devil' the word is often used humorously, or even half-affectionately, esp. with reference to children, as in bōma-dĕv, a passion-devil, a naughty child who is a spoil-sport; dasta-dĕv, a poor devil of a child that is a victim of diarrhœa; banga-dĕv, a bang-sot; bᵃsari-dĕv, a scald-devil, a pot too hot to hold. -draṭhāyĕkh m. a general word for demons of all kinds (K.Pr. 55). Cf. draṭhāyĕkh. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. the devil to fall, a sudden calamity to happen. ¶ dĕwa gindun m. the sport of a devil, i.e. a sudden death or similar unexpected calamity. -ʦũ̄̈ṭh f. a fat, ugly, foolish woman, who practises devilry, i.e. worries and interferes with other people. See ʦũ̄̈ṭh.
f. N. of the mother of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) (Śiv. 706, 1384; K. 22, 23, 26, 42, 43, 377, 404, etc.). -nandan m. Dēvakī's son, N. of Kṛṣṇa (Śiv. 1435, 1436).
f. a she-devil, a she-demon; met. a woman who is a she-devil, ugly, gross in form and feature, without discrimination, and habitually injuring others. The word is f. of dĕv in all its meanings.

adv. a particle of interrogation, inquiry, or doubt, often translatable by 'do you think?' 'perhaps', 'pray', 'indeed?' (W. 25; Śiv. 75, 287, 974, 1699; Rām. 50, 79, 368, 1169; K. 157, 163, 357, 503, 623, 841).

f. (in calculating dates for Hindū religious ceremonies) when a lunar day ends during a solar day, to continue the ceremonies of that lunar day during the rest of that solar day into the next lunar day.
m. (sg. dat. dēwakas), Dēvaka, N. of the father of Dēvakī, the mother of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) (K. 445, 464).

m. a royal court; a tribunal (of justice or revenue); a council of state, senate, divan; a court or hall of audience; a finance minister, head of revenue or financial department (cf. L. 401); a secretary; a steward; the collected writings of an author. dīwān-khāna دیوان خانہ m. a tribunal, office; a hall of audience, hall, court (Śiv. 968); a palace (El., K.Pr. 161).
adj. c.g. mad, insane, lunatic (YZ. 164, 193, 564; K.Pr. 66; Rām. 638, 907, 1050, 1467, 1529); in an ecstasy, frenzied; inspired; mad (of a dog) (K.Pr. 146).
m. a wall (YZ. 394, 409; K.Pr. 227; Rām. 22, 574, 799) (El. makes the word f. as in Hindōstānī, but cf. W. 18).
or dīwatā m. (pl. ag. dēwatav, K. 606), i.q. diwatā, q.v. (Śiv. 64, 76, 127, 130, 188, 201, 211, etc.; K. 14, 17, 18, 53, 56, 85, etc.), the image of a deity, an idol.
m. bankruptcy, insolvency. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to become bankrupt (Gr.M.).
m. a bankrupt, an insolvent (Gr.M.); a spendthrift, one who recklessly spends all his money. -dās m. 'Mr. Bankrupt', one who is beggared by reckless extravagance.
m. (El.), i.q. diva-dār, q.v., s.v. div.
f. a kind of small cooking-pot with a narrow mouth, used for cooking small quantities of rice.
m. the eye, sight. -dorᵘ adj. (f. -dürᵘ̈), eye-hard, hence disrespectful, bold, impudent.

m. sight, seeing, vision; look, appearance (khŏsh-dīdār, of beautiful appearance, YZ. 47); interview. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give an interview, to show oneself (YZ. 140, Śiv. 416). --karun -- m.inf. to look at, see (with gen. of obj. YZ. 530).
f. N. of a certain bird, described as resembling a sparrow, with a sweet voice, and kept as a song-bird, the Indian skylark (L. 146, dedar) (Śiv. 181); ? a pheasant (El.).

f. (sg. dat. ḍēdĕ), the main entrance of a large house or palace, the hall door, front portico (K.Pr. 54, Rām. 564). -wān or -wôñᵘ m. (his wife is -wān-bāy or -wöñⁱ-bāy, but a woman who performs the duties of a doorkeeper is -wāñĕñ), a doorkeeper, porter, gatekeeper, watchman (El. díḍwoin).
f. audacity, boldness, daring (in a bad sense, e.g. of a robber or the like). Cf. ḍyuḍᵘ.

f. a blow given by the beak of a bird, a peck, beak-bite (K.Pr. 38, 56). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to peck, bite with the beak; met. privately to interfere with and impede another who is comfortably placed, to give 'pin-pricks'. ¶ diga-dig f. mutual pecking, as in a cock-fight.
adj. c.g. (of a bird) ready to strike with the beak, inclined to peck.
m. one who is sky-clothed, naked, a naked ascetic; N. of Śiva (Śiv. 153, 632, 926, 1021, 1169, 1584).

m. (his wife is ḍī˜gamīr-bāy, while a woman who performs his duties is ḍī˜gamīrĕñ), the headman of a village, who is responsible for its good order and for its government revenue; a braggart village tyrant, one who bullies his neighbours. --lāgun -- m.inf. to act (without authority) as a village headman, to bully or oppress those weaker than oneself, to act as a braggart.
f. a female head of a village, a village headwoman. See ḍī˜gamīr.
