f. the habit of village tyranny, a practice of bullying one's neighbours. --hāwüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to display village tyranny, to pretend to be a village headman, and to act as if one had such authority.

m. eveningtide, the late afternoon, twilight, a part of the fourth division of the day, lasting for an hour before sunset, about 4 p.m. (El. dígar); boḍᵘ digar, a little before 4 p.m. (K.Pr. 177); lŏkuṭᵘ digar, a little after 4 p.m. (ib.); aḍ digar, see aḍ. ¶ digaran m. 5 o'clock (El.). ¶ digaras adv. at evening twilight (El.). --bögⁱ -- or --bögin -- adv. about eveningtide, in the late afternoon or thereabouts.
adj. and adv. other, another, next, following (YZ. 200); over again, again; moreover, further, besides.
m. a cooking vessel, large, round, brazen, with narrow mouth (El.).

f. a continual flow or stream, esp. of tears (cf. ȧshⁱ-digiñ under oshᵘ), blood, or other humour from a wound or the like. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a stream to flow, esp. of the thin stream of oil or the like issuing from a crack in the vessel containing it.
m. the body; esp. the human body (K.Pr. 243, Śiv. 753, 1777, 1887); the personal form taken by an impersonal deity (Śiv. 712). ¶ diha-dorᵘ adj. (f. -dürᵘ̈), strong-bodied, able-bodied.
m. sportively tossing an infant in the air.
. K. 109 has ḍiji-ḍiji instead of ḍija-ḍija.

f. (sg. dat. ḍē̃jĕ), a ball, a small globular mass; esp. of wool, cotton, thread, string, or the like. Cf. āma-˚ under ām 1. Cf. ḍyū̃gᵘ, of which it is f. in sense of dim. (Gr.Gr. 36). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to form balls, to become globular (of something which ought to flow in a steady stream). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a globular abscess or glandular swelling in the abdomen to occur. ¶ ḍē̃jĕ tȧlⁱ anun m.inf. to bring (the thread) under the ball; met. to prevaricate or pervert the words of an opponent in a disputation, to twist unfairly an opponent's language. ḍē̃jĕ tȧlⁱ pan, pana tȧlⁱ ḍī˜jᵘ̈ anüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to bring the thread under the ball, and the ball under the thread; met. by the use of such perversion to render an opponent without reply, to see that oneself is in the wrong but not to confess it, to maintain one's cause by arguments known to oneself to be wrong (K.Pr. 162).
m. a regent or guardian of a quarter of the sky (Rām. 1770).

f. a mode of reverently prostrating oneself before a god or highly reverenced human being. The body is thrown straight on the ground, which is touched with the forehead. --diñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to make such prostrations.
m. a metal cooking-pot, a small cauldron, a saucepan.
m. slackness, dilatoriness. --karun -- m.inf. to delay in some work which requires haste.

m. the heart, mind, soul (K.Pr. 56, 133, 194; YZ. 17, 52, 149, 180, 208, 212; Śiv. 55, 487, 492, 706; Rām. 26, 261, 298, etc.); spirit, valour. dil-o-jāna sṻty, with heart and soul, heartily, cordially (El.), cheerfully. --ba dil دل بدل m. interchange of hearts, mutual love, heart to heart (K.Pr. 56). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give the mind (to), to apply oneself diligently (to) (K.Pr. 46). --lagun -- m.inf. the heart to be set (upon = pĕṭh) (K.Pr. 43, YZ. 263), the heart to be given or applied (to). ¶ dilas prayĕwunᵘ n.ag. (f. --prayĕwüñᵘ̈ --), pleasing to the heart, cheering (El.). --tasallī diñᵘ̈ -- دلس تسلی دنِ f.inf. to comfort (El.).
m. suffix giving an obscene sense, as in mājĕ-dil, one who has incestuous intercourse with his own mother, a term of abuse (Gr.Gr. 107). Cf. dinal and dāwal.
m. 'mind-soothing'; soothing, comfort, consolation, encouragement (Gr.M., K. 1004). --dyunᵘ -- (Rām. 491) or --karun -- (Rām. 781), m.inf. to soothe, comfort, console.
adj. c.g. bold, brave, intrepid (Rām. 501, 908, 1351, 1457, in all dilāwār).
adj. c.g. attractive, charming, lovely; beloved (El.).
adj. and subst. m. heart-ravishing, captivating, beloved; heart-ravisher, a lovely person, a beloved one (YZ. 18, dilbaran, ag. sg.).
adj. c.g. beloved, pleasant, delightful, agreeable, (of a book) interesting (W. 158, Gr.M.).
adj. and subst. c.g. possessing or winning the heart, delighting the heart, charming; having heart, encouraged; a lover, mistress, sweetheart (El.).
adj. c.g. intrepid, bold, daring, venturesome, brave, courageous, valiant (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. heart-stricken, oppressed in mind, afflicted, grieved, low-spirited, melancholy, sad (K.Pr. 106, Rām. 349).
adj. c.g. grieved in heart, sorrowful, sad of heart (El.).
f. intrepidity, boldness, daring, courage, bravery (El. dilerí) (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. heart-attracting, alluring, attractive, winning (Rām. 318).
adj. c.g. beloved, a beloved object (Rām. 153, 804).
adj. c.g. contented, glad, pleased, comfortable (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to rejoice (tr.), to gladden (El.). --sapadun -- m.inf. to rejoice (intr.) (El.).
adj. c.g. heart-burning, heart-inflaming, touching, pathetic (Rām. 1083).
give thou to me; dima, I shall give; see dyunᵘ. YZ. 437 has dīma, m.c.
I will give thee (YZ. 25). See dyunᵘ.
I shall give to thee (dima + y), see dyunᵘ.
m. a kind of vegetable found only in the Ḍal and in the Ancār lake. This vegetable is said to be found only in Kashmir (El.).
(? spelling) m. a hyena. It is said to be very rare in the valley (El.).
m. the belly, the cavity of the abdomen. --naṭun -- m.inf. the belly to tremble; to tremble at heart from fear or panic in face of some calamity.

adj. c.g. miserable, wretched (Rām. 1249), i.q. dyūnᵘ, q.v.; subst. m. distress, misery, wretchedness (Śiv. 1635). ¶ dīna-dayāl m. he who shows pity to the wretched, a friend of the poor; a title of the Deity (Śiv. 1436, 1697).

m. faith, religion (K.Pr. 27); esp. the religion of Islām. --tulun -- m.inf. to raise (the cry of) 'religion', to start a religious riot or battle; to create or excite an uproar by an unpopular act, word, gesture, or the like. ¶ dīna-bôjᵘ m. (f. -bājĕñ), a sharer in religion, a co-religionist. --tulun -- m.inf. to change one's religion, become a convert to a religion different from that in which one was born.
(Śiv. 107), sg. abl. of dyunᵘ, q.v. Cf. also dĕn.
n.ag. (sg. dat. dinagrākas; f. dinagrākañ), a giver (Gr.Gr. 106, 107).
adj. c.g. fit to be given, worthy to be given (Gr.Gr. 130).
(Śiv. 1219), m. plur. dat. of dinukᵘ, the genitive of dyunᵘ, q.v.
f. an unchaste woman, a prostitute (Gr.Gr. 107, K.Pr. 57).
m. (sg. dat. dīnānāthas), Lord of the wretched, Him to whom the wretched fly for help, a N. of Śiva (Śiv. 1555). Cf. dīn 1.
sg. dat. of din 1 and also (Gr.Gr. 112, Śiv. 1262, 1387) of dyunᵘ (inf.), the act of giving, to give, qq.v.
n.ag. a giver, one who is generous (El., Gr.Gr. 107, K.Pr. 57). See dyunᵘ.
neg. conj. part. not having given (Gr.Gr. 111); also din with suff. of acc.-dat. sg. of 2nd person, they will make thee, or for thee (Gr.Gr. 184). See dyunᵘ.

adj. (f. dīndārĕñ), religious, devout, pious (Gr.M.); (in Kāshmīrī) a fanatic, hence ready to take up arms even without cause, bellicose, pugnacious. The fem. is a woman of this description; for such a man's wife, see the next. -bāy f. the wife of such a man.
f. constancy in religion; (in Kāshmīrī) readiness to take up arms, pugnacity, see ḍīndār.
f. a short sleep, a doze.
conj. 3 to be wrapped in sleep, to be sound asleep (L.V. 78).
(Śiv. 1911), sg. abl. of dyunᵘ, q.v., in order to give, inf. of purpose.
impers. fut. part. it is to be given, one should give (Gr.Gr. 111). See dyunᵘ.
(Śiv. 1430), m.c. for dina, sg. abl. of dyunᵘ, q.v.
(Śiv. 1651, 1714), sg. gen. of dyunᵘ, q.v., of giving. Also sg. gen. of din 1, see dĕn.

m. (sg. dat. dīpas), a light, a lamp (Śiv. 314), esp. the small lamp consisting of a cotton wick burning in a saucer of oil, or the jewelled lamp used in worship (Śiv. 513, 738, 835, 1093, 1175, 1205, 1346, 1523, 1692, 1706); used met. in idioms such as kŏla-dīph m. the lamp, or glory, of a family (Śiv. 1536). ¶ dīpa-dān m. an illumination, esp. the illumination of the Diwālī festival (see -mālā bel.) or the illumination on the eighth lunar day of the bright half of the month of Phāgun (Phālguna) on the occasion of making offerings to deceased ancestors. -mālā f. a celebrated festival, the Diwālī of India, held on the new moon of the month of Kārtikh (Kārttika) in honour of Kārttikēya, the Indian war-god. In the daytime Hindūs bathe and put on their best attire. At night they worship Lakṣmī, and their houses and the streets are illuminated (Śiv. 1093, 1150). -shrād m. a ceremony (at which lamps are lighted) performed in the months of Māg or Phāgun of the year after a death, in honour of the deceased; genl. a festival observed by all Hindūs on the eighth day of the bright half of Phāgun, = -dān ab.
m. (sg. dat. dīpas), an island; used --˚ as in Sangal-dīph, the island of Sangal, Ceylon (K.Pr. 186).

or ḍī˜phᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a private assembly of a few (four or five) men met together for consultation, a private committee, privy council. ¶ ḍī˜phᵃrĕ karañĕ f. pl. inf. to form such small privy councils, to form small private committees out of a number of people assembled together.
adj. c.g. bright, splendid, brilliant (Śiv. 1122, dīptimāna, m.c.).
f. (sg. dat. dīpᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), brightness, light, splendour (Śiv. 1657).
m. steady, constant, firm, resolute, brave, courageous, self-possessed. ¶ dīra-vīr m. a hero.
dīshē̃kā, or dīshē̃khā f. evacuation of the fæces, easing oneself.
m. one who is habitually slow, dilatory; lazy at work.
(? درتنہ) m. a set of garments of very fine muslin; a single garment of very fine muslin.

or m. (sg. dat. dīshĕs, but pl. dat. dēshĕn, ag. dēshau), a province, country, kingdom (Śiv. 244, 661, 673, 1881; K. 639, 648, 692); a city (Gr.M.; cf. shĕhar); a native country (El., who makes the word f.); the people of a country, the general population, everyone (K.Pr. 57). ¶ dīshĕ drāmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --drāmüʦᵘ̈ --), one who has left the country (for his country's good), one who is everywhere of bad repute on account of well-known evil conduct. --koḍᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. küḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), expelled from the country; hence, one who is of thoroughly bad repute wherever he goes. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to expel from the country, banish (as a punishment) (Gr.M.); to give a person a bad character that pursues him everywhere. --nērun -- m.inf. to leave the country, to abandon one's country under pressure of calamity, famine, or the like; to acquire an evil reputation all over the country on account of bad conduct. -shūbay f. a good reputation known over the whole country. -sāway f. universal prosperity of a country. -vĕhᵃwath f. (sg. dat. -vĕhᵃwüʦᵃ), respect for the country, regard for popular opinion as an incentive to good conduct.
or dīshē̃khā or dīrgashĕnkā m. going out to stool, going to the closet; voiding excrement, stooling.

f. drowsiness, sleepiness, nodding of the head in sleepiness. -ḍiska f. mutual nodding of the head in sleepiness (of two persons sitting near each other, whose heads knock against each other in drowsiness). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. drowsiness or weary sleepiness to come on, esp. (to a person travelling and weary with a long journey or going by night) stumbling along half asleep to take place.
f. a small girdle or cummerbund. Cf. ḍē̃ṭônᵘ.

m. a god, a deity, esp. a mātṛkā, or divine mother, cf. diwath 2. The word is used in the following compounds:-- ¶ diva bögⁱ adj. c.g. or adv. for the sake of a god, (devoted) for a god, (sacred) to a god, and so forth. -dŏh m. a god's day, a day sacred to a god or to gods (as distinct from a day sacred to ancestors, or devoted to memorial ceremonies or the like). -dār or dēwa-dār m. the Himalayan cedar, the deodar (Cedrus deodara, El.); the wood of this tree. See El. s.vv. deodár, díár, and divadár. Divadār is the word in use in Śrīnagar. The wood is used as a substitute for sandal-wood in Hindū religious ceremonies (Śiv. 1080, 1613). -dôrᵘ adj. (f. -dörᵘ̈), made of deodar wood. -dörⁱ adj. c.g., id. -dār-mỗkun m. a small ball of deodar wood, used for rubbing on a rough stone, the resulting powder being employed instead of sandal-wood as a material for the forehead marks worn by Hindus. Cf. mỗkun. -gŏn or -gōn m. the Hindū worship of the divine mothers (the sixty-four Yōginīs), usually on the day before any important ceremony, such as the initiation of a boy (upanayana) or a wedding. Cf. L. (deogun) 260, 261, and El. s.v. -gōn dyunᵘ m.inf. to perform this worship. -gŏn (or -gōn) mahārāza  m. the hero of this worship, i.e. the boy whose initiation or marriage is to follow. -gŏn (or -gōn) mahārĕñ  the heroine of such a worship, i.e. the girl who is to be married a few days afterwards. Her formal initiation into Brahmanism dates from this diva-gŏn (L. 261). -gŏn ras m. the soup or gravy of the sheep's flesh offered to the divine mothers at the diva-gŏn ceremony. -gōn thöjⁱ f. the vessel in which the meat offered at the diva-gŏn ceremony is cooked. -gōn-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), the person at whose expense the diva-gŏn ceremony is performed. -gōn zang f. the ceremony of securing good omens at the commencement of the diva-gŏn ceremony. -gōnas bihun m.inf. to set to work at, i.e. to begin, the performance of the diva-gŏn ceremony. -kāv m. a certain bird, described as a large crow, dark-coloured all over, even on the neck; perhaps Cuculus melanoleucus. -pẹ̆tᵃr m. a libation to the gods (pitṛs) and deceased ancestors made by Hindūs at the morning bath.

or دیو m. (dīv, Śiv. 69, 71, 1718, 1724, etc., K. 255, 604; dēv, Śiv. 120, 123, 124, 128, 131, etc., Rām. 445, 892, 1714, K. 416, 451, etc.), a god of the Hindū pantheon; met. a person of upright and noble character; a title added to the name of a god or a great man or hero, as in arzuna-dēv, the revered hero Arjuna (Śiv. 1178, 1734); ātma-dēv, the self-god, the deity who is the great Self of all things, Śiva (Śiv. 1761, 1772); ādi-dēv, the primeval god, Śiva (Śiv. 1160, 1788). ¶ dēva-dēv m. a god of gods, a chief god, such as Brahmā (Śiv. 627). -lūkh m. the world of the gods, heaven (Śiv. 36, 1913, K. 591, 1049). -sar, see divᵃsar. -sthalī f. a god's place, a place frequented by gods, a place hallowed by the presence of many gods (Śiv. 1170).

or dēv ī f. a goddess of the Hindū pantheon (Rām. 1444, K. 84); esp. Dēvī, the śakti or wife of Śiva (Śiv. 63, 81, 82, etc.; Rām. 50, 55, etc.; K. 268, 269, 654, 655). -bal m. a place sacred to Dēvī and hallowed by her special presence, such as Jwālāmukhī, etc. -diwatā m. a general term for all the gods and goddesses of the Hindū pantheon.
m. a place sacred to Dēvī or other great Hindū goddess, and hallowed by her special presence. Cf. dīvī.
or dēvasar (Śiv. 1170), m. N. of a pargana in the Marāz division of Kashmīr, the ancient Dēvasarasa (RT.Tr. II, 470).
m. a god, a deity (there are three times ten millions of them, Śiv. 635); met. a god-man, a man of godlike nature, one of handsome appearance and virtuous character.

f. (sg. dat. diwüʦᵘ̈), sagacity, comprehension, quickness of apprehension, power of inference, acumen; ability to understand the condition even of something invisible. --āsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such power of inference to exist. --niñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of one formerly possessed of great acumen) such power of inference to be lost (by a change of circumstances, etc.). --tulüñᵘ̈ -- , f.inf. 'to lift sagacity', to abuse or revile one who is honoured on account of his sagacity. --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. sagacity to rise (and go away); (of one previously endowed with great sagacity) power of inference to depart (owing to some change of circumstances). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. sagacity to come; (of one who has previously not grasped a thing even when before his very eyes) understanding suddenly to come. ¶ diwüʦᵘ̈-band adj. c.g. one who is habitually able to infer conditions of actions, etc., even when they are not seen by him; sagacious. -wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), id.

f. (sg. dat. diwạti or diwüʦᵘ̈), one of the mātṛkās or divine mothers or personified energies of the principal Hindū deities, usually reckoned as seven in number, viz. Brāhmī (or Brahmāṇī), Mahēśvarī, Kaumārī, Vaiṣṇavī, Vārāhī, Indrāṇī (or Aindrī or Māhēndrī), and Cāmuṇḍā, but sometimes as eight, nine, or sixteen (cf. div) (Śiv. 1453). The word is also applied to one of the seven married women who personate the mātṛkās on the occasion of their worship, and are adored in their behalf. -thöjᵘ̈ f. the dish containing food, etc., offered to the mātṛkās on the occasion of their worship. ¶ diwạta gūlᵘ m. a ball of rice, etc., used in the worship of the mātṛkās on the evening of the fifteenth day of the waxing moon and on similar occasions. Hindū women take these with songs to the river bank, where they worship them, and then allow them to float away. -khir m. an offering of rice-milk, etc., made to the mātṛkās. -mūnᵘ m. the plastered wall of the mātṛkās, a plastered representation of the kalpavṛkṣa, or celestial wishing-tree, on the north-east wall of the place on the river bank used for the worship of the mātṛkās. -wörᵘ̈ or diwaʦa-wörᵘ̈ f. an earthenware pitcher filled with fruit, water, and simples, placed in the north-east corner of the place on the river bank used for the worship of the mātṛkās; the ceremonial placing of this pitcher in this position by women with songs on the evening fixed for the worship. ¶ diwᵃʦa-tabücᵃ f. the dish of offerings of food made to the married women who personate the mātṛkās as ab. and who eat the offerings. ¶ diwaʦa-wörᵘ̈ f., see ab.
n.ag. (f.diwawüñᵘ̈), one who gives, a giver, etc., n.ag. of dyunᵘ, q.v., in all its meanings (Gr.Gr. 105; Śiv. 209, 851, 858, 861, etc.; f. 1511).

f. (sg. dat. diwạyĕ), the special conjuncture of the planets on which it is right to visit a holy place (cf. daras 5); hence, the mēlā or fair brought about by the concourse of people on these occasions (K.Pr. 55, 159; Rām. 1420, 1452); the fun of the fair, a tamāsha (K.Pr. 126). In K.Pr. the word is spelt diwai. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make a pilgrimage to a religious mēlā, as ab. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a religious mēlā as above to begin, the pilgrims to commence to assemble. ¶ diwạyĕ-rang m. that which resembles a religious mēlā, a temporary, non-religious assembly or fair.

m. (sg. dat. diwaris), a lofty stone-built shrine or temple for receiving the image of a god, a linga, or the like. ¶ diwȧrⁱ-küñⁱ f. a squared, polished, block of stone, such as would be used in building such a shrine.
interj. an exclamation used to drive away a dog (El.).

m. a hole or pit in the ground (H. xii, 6). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to dig such a hole, e.g. in order to collect water, to let water issue (H. viii, 7), or as a receptacle for rubbish. ¶ dŏbukᵘ adj. (f. dŏbücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a pit; produced from or found in a pit (such as mud, fish, or the like). ¶ dŏbas gaʦhun m.inf. to go into a pit, to fall into mud; met. to sink into a foul or mean employment. --wasun -- m.inf. to descend into a pit; met. to take to a mean or blameworthy mode of livelihood.

m. the confluence of two rivers. Cf. ḍab 1. ¶ dŏba-gāv m. N. of a village at the confluence of the River Pahōr or Pohur with the Jehlam or Vĕth. The confluence is about four miles below Sōpūr. See RT.Tr. ii, 425.

the English word 'double', in Hindī dabal or ḍabal, but in Kāshmīrī referred by folk-etymology to dŏb 1, a pit, because the coins referred to below are 'pitted' or 'hollowed' by being stamped. Used in the following: dŏbal paisā or pö̃sa m. the double pice, or the coin representing a quarter of an anna made current by the English. --rupay -- f. the standard current English rupee.
a kind of blanket consisting of two breadths sewn together (the two pieces being 1 1/2 yards broad, with a length of 10 yards) (L. 371); ? spelling. Cf. ekbari.
f. the profession, condition, or livelihood of a washerman (Gr.Gr. 144).
f. the condition of one who is accustomed to shamming illness or weakness in order to escape some danger or punishment.

f. a washerman's club, used for beating the clothes he is washing (Gr.Gr. 38). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to use this club for washing clothes. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the washerman's club to be experienced; met. to become deeply grieved by the frequently repeated recollection of one's own or others' troubles. Cf. dŏbusᵘ. ¶ dŏbiñĕ-loṭhᵘ m. a kind of washerman's club, in the shape of a short cudgel. -ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. the blow given by a washerman's club; beating clothes with such a club.
perf. part. a variant of dọ̆bᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, see dọ̆bᵃrun.
or dŏbus m. the wooden mallet or club used by washermen for beating clothes in the wash (Gr.Gr. 144). Cf. dŏbiñ.
f. (sg. dat. dọ̆bᵃrüñᵃ), secret burying, hiding in the ground.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. dọ̆bᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. dọ̆bᵃrun, q.v. dọ̆bᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. dŏbᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. dọ̆bᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, see dọ̆bᵃrun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dọ̆bᵒrᵒ), to bury, to hide in the ground; to bury a corpse (Gr.M.). ¶ dọ̆bᵒrᵒ-motᵒ (also spelt doburᵘ-motᵘ) perf. part. (f. dọ̆bᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), buried, hidden in the ground. ¶ dọ̆bᵃrith thawun m.inf., i.q. dọ̆bᵃrun. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. hurriedly to bury or hide in the ground, esp. of stolen goods or the like.
adj. (f. ḍübᵘ̈), variegated, brindled, dappled, spotted, having dark spots or marks on a light ground. Cf. ḍaba-hôrᵘ.

m. (f. dö̆bᵘ̈ 1, a washerwoman; dŏbⁱ-bāy, a washerman's wife, Gr.Gr. 34), a washerman, a man who lives by washing other people's clothes (W. 121; K.Pr. 58, 154, 231; Rām. 784 ff., 1154; L. 464). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give a washerman, to send clothes to be washed by a washerman (as distinct from washing one's own clothes). ¶ dŏbⁱ-bāy f. a washerman's wife. -bāyĕ dọ̆bᵘ m. N. of a game played by girls. They stand in a circle, holding each other's hands, while each in turn runs under the other's arms, a kind of 'kiss in the ring'. --chalun -- m.inf. to get clothes washed by a washerman (as distinct from doing one's washing oneself). -dāthᵃr m. a place where washermen spread out clothes to dry. -dāthur m. the collection of a washerman's implements, lye, etc., used in washing. -gāṭh m. (sg. dat. -gāṭhas), a washerman's ghāṭ, the place on the bank of a river, etc., where washermen wash clothes. -küñᵘ̈ f. a washerman's stone, the stone on which a washerman beats the clothes he is washing. -tān m. the sheet in which a washerman ties up for transport his bundle of clothes for the wash. -wān m. lit. a washerman's shop; hence, either the place where he plies his trade or the place where he lives (K.Pr. 159). -wạsᵃla m.pl. the bundle of clothes for the wash, i.e. clothes collected for or given out for washing; the bundle of clean clothes returned from the wash. -wasth m. (sg. dat. -wastas), id. ¶ dŏbi drāv adj. c.g. come from the wash, cleaned and returned by the washerman. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to have had clothes washed by a washerman (lit. to drag clothes from him). --nērun -- m.inf. to come forth from the washerman, (of clothes) to have been washed by him.
adj. (f. dö̆bᵘ̈ 2) or dobᵘ (f. dübᵘ̈), (of a vessel or dish) nearly full, not quite full.
f. the condition or livelihood of a washerman.
or dọ̆chᵘ adj. (f. düchᵘ̈), dark-coloured, black, esp. u.w. reference to bears and other wild animals; met. dark-natured (of a man), black-hearted (cf. dachĕr).
m. a forest village, a village situated in the wild country at the foot of the hills, esp. N. of a certain village lying seven kōs north-east of Śrīnagar.

m. (sg. dat. ḍŏcaris, ag. ḍŏcᵃrᵃ), the state or condition of being bowed owing to the body not being straight, crawling on the ground. Cf. ḍocᵘ. --dọ̆curᵘdyunᵘ -- m.inf. doing anything or acting in a humble way (as if crawling on the ground). --trāwun -- m.inf. to keep humbly following another in the hope of getting something done according to one's wishes. --tröwith bĕhun -- m.inf. to give up some work or to refuse to commence a work (from unwillingness or laziness) by affecting inability to continue.

adj. hunchbacked, used in the following: --trāwun -- m.inf. to show oneself hunchbacked; hence, met. to regard with indifference any work, even if its carrying out is necessary. Cf. dŏcurᵘ. ¶ ḍocᵘ-ḍocᵘ, in ḍocᵘ-ḍocᵘ karun m.inf. to progress like a hunch- back, to limp along, when one is unable to walk (owing to weakness, illness, old age, lameness, or the like), to get along somehow or other. docᵘ-docᵘ dyunᵘ m.inf. to give limping; hence, in any work or business, to carry it along somehow or other, even when one is unable to do it properly.

m. milk (YZ. 90; W. 129; K.Pr. 11, 64, 137, 241; Śiv. 435, 1380, etc.; Rām. 427, 557, etc.); curdled or clotted milk (the dahī of India) (Śiv. 45, 1006); the milky juice of Euphorbia or other similar plant. K.Pr. spells this word dud. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give milk, to act as a wet nurse, to follow the profession of a wet nurse; to give milk (K.Pr. 31, can a bull give milk?). --raṭun -- m.inf. to stop the milk, (of a cow) to refuse to allow milk to flow. --rōzun -- m.inf. milk to stop; (of a cow) the flow of milk to be suddenly stopped. --ti kôluy gaʦhun -- m.inf. even milk to become black, i.e. anything which is usually easily got to become unobtainable, or any work which is usually easily done to become very difficult. --ʦalun -- m.inf. milk to flee; (of a cow or the like) the flow of milk to stop owing to advanced pregnancy; (of a suckling child) to cease from the breast, to be weaned. --wālun -- m.inf. to cause milk to descend, i.e. to cause milk to flow, to cause a woman or animal to give milk (K.Pr. 99). --wasun -- m.inf. milk to descend; milk to commence to flow (of a pregnant woman or cow when approaching the time of delivery); milk to flow involuntarily when a mother sees a loved child. ¶ dŏda-ahākh f. (sg. dat. -ahākas), a certain very white whitewash, made up of lime mixed with milk and other materials. -ala f.pl. milk-pumpkins, a certain dish of pumpkins cooked with curdled milk. -ambȧrⁱ m. a certain kind of apple with a milky taste, and considered the best kind of all. It is also called the Samarkhand apple. It ripens early and will not stand exportation (L. 350, dud amri). ¶ dŏda-bab 1 m. a foster-mother's husband, a foster-father. -bab 2 f. a bosom or udder full of milk. -baba barana yiñĕ f. pl. inf. the breasts to fill with milk; met. to feel extreme affection for a person on seeing him (e.g. even when a naughty child is brought up for punishment) or on calling him to mind. -bahā m. steaming over boiling milk (an operation performed for cleaning delicate articles, such as herons' plumes or the like). -bāna m. a milk-bowl or milk-jug, i.e. either a vessel suited for this purpose, or a vessel full of milk, fresh or clotted. -bĕñĕ f. a milk-sister, the daughter of a foster-mother, a foster-sister. -brag m. (f. -bragiñ), a certain kind of heron. -brakh m. (sg. dat. -brakas), the wasting and illness caused to a suckling child who is suddenly taken away from the breast. -brakh lagun m.inf. the ab. wasting to occur. -brakh pyonᵘ m.inf. id. -brôrᵘ m. a milk-cat; one, esp. a child, who is always longing for sweet or curdled milk in preference to other food. -bŏy f. the smell of milk; a smell like that of milk, a milky smell. -bôyᵘ m. a milk-brother, the son of a foster-mother, a foster-brother. ¶ dŏda-chỗpᵘ m. a kind of small churning-stick. It has a paddle-wheel at one end, and the stick is revolved between the palms of the hands, the milk being contained in a gourd or similar vessel. -chir f. the small thin stream of milk as it issues from the pap; met. any small quantity of milk; the milky juice making the substance of grain in the first stage of its formation. This juice is supposed to be conveyed from the moon. Cf. chir 4. -chira m. a milk-lamb, the young of any animal (esp. of a sheep or goat) while still suckling. -cāhy f. tea with milk, tea boiled with milk. -cöṭⁱ f. a kind of earthen jar for holding milk, large in capacity but with a small mouth, used by the forest buffalo herdsmen. ¶ dŏda-dôdᵘ m. inflammation of the breasts due to the sudden cessation of the demand for milk owing to the death of the child. -dām m. milk-supping; drinking milk by mouthfuls, i.e. putting the lips to the breast or to a vessel and filling one's mouth, then swallowing, and then repeating the process. Cf. dām. -dand m.pl. milk-teeth, the first teeth of a suckling child. -dāra f. the stream of milk when poured out; a very small amount of milk. ¶ dŏda-gab m. a milk-sprout, i.e. the first tender sprout from a seed, or the like. -gagur m. (sg. dat. -gagaras), a milk-rat, an affectionate term for a very young suckling infant, male or female. -golᵘ m. a mouthful of milk. -gūrᵘ m. (f. -gūrᵘ̈), a milk cowherd, a cowherd or other person who sells milk, a milkman. The fem. signifies a woman who follows this profession. ¶ dŏda-hĕḍur m. (sg. dat. -hĕḍaras), a milk-mushroom, a small delicate species of mushroom. -hāl f. (sg. dat. -hāli), a ball of milk, the name of a kind of rice, described as long in shape, soft, very well flavoured, fragrant, and white. -hāma f. a bunch of a certain tender grass, tasting like milk, that grows in rice-fields. -hĕm f. milk-bean; a kind of bean. -har 1 m. a milk-quarrel, strife between two suckling children for one woman's breast (when a woman is suckling two children). Cf. dŏda- rᵃsh bel. -har 2 m. milk-cream, cream of milk. -hörᵘ̈ f. a cow that is a good milker, although slender in appearance. -hyolᵘ m. a milk-ear, an ear of corn which is not yet ripe. ¶ dŏda-kāl m. the amount of milk taken from a cow or buffalo at one milking. -kōl (cf. کول) m. a milk-cup, a milk- jar (YZ. 130). -kürᵘ̈ f. a kind of sauce made of curdled milk beaten into a liquid and cooked with clarified butter, oil, and condiments. -krṻḍ 1 m. N. of a certain creeper, described as having a small root, but spreading very widely, with a milky juice, and delicate milk-white flowers. -krṻḍ 2 f. N. of a certain kind of rice-plant, the grains of which are soft, with a pleasing scent, and tasting of milk. -krörᵘ̈ f. a kind of cake made of inspissated milk, eaten when cold and congealed. -krǖrᵘ̈ f. N. of a certain kind of rice-plant, the grain of which is described as having a dark husk, as tasting like milk, soft, fragrant, and white (L. 463, dud krïr). -krāy f. a milk-cauldron used for boiling milk; such a vessel when full of milk. -kᵃy f. an earthenware vessel for holding milk till it becomes sour, and in which it is then churned, a churn. ¶ dŏda-lōṭa m. a milk-darling; a good-looking well-mannered child. -lyūṭᵘ m. a milk-chick; met. a suckling child; any child up to eight or nine years of age. ¶ dŏda-möjᵘ̈ f. a milk-mother, a foster-mother (W. 17), wet nurse; a woman (usually a relative) appointed to act as mother to, i.e. as an attendant on, a young unmarried virgin child-wife in her father-in-law's house (YZ. 384, L. 269, Śiv. 1095 (möjiy m.c. for möjᵘ̈), 1151). -môlᵘ m. a milk-father, the husband of a foster-mother, a foster-father (W. 17). -mālay f. milk-love, love or desire for milk, curds, or the like. -mölyunᵘ m. the home of a foster-father, esp. of a girl's foster-father. -mösm m. a milk-child, a child in the suckling stage. Cf. mösm. -maṭh-hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -maṭh-hishᵘ̈), like a milk-jar; met. very clear, spotless, white. ¶ dŏda-nörᵘ̈ f. a wide-mouthed vessel for holding milk; such a vessel full of milk. ¶ dŏda-phrasth m. (sg. dat. -phrastas), the white poplar, Populus alba. There is a fine grove of these trees in the Gurais valley. The poplar is said by Kāshmīrīs to be the minister of the kingly plane-tree (L. 79, 81, dudh prast). -phuṭa f. a milk-knot, a tumour or morbid swelling in the breast occurring during lactation, through superfluity of milk owing to the removal of the child. -phyorᵘ or -phyūrᵘ m. a milk-drop; met. a very small amount of milk. -prāh  m. milk-possession, a kind of demoniacal possession or hysterical affection (accompanied by delirium and palsy) which sometimes attacks a pregnant woman, or a lying-in woman, or a newly born child, when milk or curds is brought near her or it from a distance on a dark night in winter or similar time. -prāʦa f.pl. milk-mouth-corners, the corners of the mouth of a suckling child; met. very delicate mouth-corners. ¶ dŏda-rᵃsh f. milk-enmity, i.q. dŏda-har 1 ab. Cf. dŏdⁱ rᵃsh bel. ¶ dŏda-shurᵘ m. a milk-child, a suckling child (W. 114, Rām. 807, 1249, 1653); met. any young child. -shurⁱ-bāpār m. conduct of or like that of a young child; esp. obstinate, ignorant, unreflecting conduct on the part of a grown-up person. -shurⁱgī f., id. -shuril f., id. -shurⁱ-pöthⁱr m., id. -sọ̆ñᵘ m. (f. -sŏñĕñ), a milk-co-father-in-law; when a foster-father or foster-mother accompanies a foster-daughter on her marriage to her husband's house as her attendant and quasi-father or quasi-mother, he is called a milk-co-father-in-law of the bride's father-in-law. The actual fathers of the bridegroom and bride are each sọ̆ñᵘ, or co-father-in-law to the other. -sāth m. (sg. dat. -sātas), the milk-moment; the auspicious moment for the ceremonial offering, by her own blood relations, of a present of curdled milk to a pregnant woman approaching the time of her delivery. Cf. dŏda-zang bel. -syunᵘ m. a kind of broth made of mutton cooked in clotted milk. -syothᵘ m. ground parched grain (sattū) cooked with inspissated milk. ¶ dŏda-thañi-ʦūr m. thief of milk and butter, N. of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna), i.q. dŏda-ʦūr bel., q.v. -ṭŏ̈ṭhᵘ̈ f. a stream of milk, esp. the thin stream of milk that flows from anything (such as the finger) dipped into milk, and then raised up; hence, a very small quantity of milk. ¶ dŏda-ʦḍᵘ  m. a large earthenware vessel for milk, fresh or clotted; such a vessel full of milk. -ʦaḍawôrᵘ m. an earthenware vessel into which a cow is milked, the Kashmīr equivalent of a milk-pail (Śiv. 1502). -ʦopᵘ m. as much clotted milk as can be taken in the hollow of the hand for drinking, a 'sup' of milk. -ʦūr m. the thief who stole milk, N. of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) in allusion to his baby exploits in Gōkula. ¶ dŏda-wŏgra m. a thick kind of rice-milk. -wörᵘ̈  f. a kind of small globular earthen vessel for holding milk or curds. -wüṭᵘ̈ f. a cob of unripe Indian corn (makāī) in its milky stage. -woʦhᵘ m. a milk-calf, a suckling male calf; met. an ignorant, stupid, child. -waʦhürᵘ̈ f. a suckling female calf; met. a stupid, ignorant girl. ¶ dŏda-zĕl or -zĕliñ f. the cream of clotted milk. -zāng f. milk-gift; the auspicious gift of a full jar of clotted milk sent by her own relations to a pregnant woman approaching the time of her delivery. Cf. dŏda-sāth ab. -zĕv f. a milk-tongue, the tongue of a suckling child, which has not tasted any flavour except that of milk; met. a delicate or soft tongue. ¶ dŏdⁱ-rⁱsh f., i.q. dŏda-rᵃsh and dŏda-har 1 ab. -ʦolᵘ m. (f. -ʦüjᵘ̈), a child who has given up milk, a weaned child. ¶ dŏdukᵘ  adj. (f. dŏdücᵘ̈), of or belonging to milk, fresh or clotted (dahī); derived from or made from milk (e.g. cream, etc.); produced from milk (e.g. a person's virtues or vices derived from his mother's milk). ¶ dŏdasdrṻrᵘ̈pë˘ñᵘ̈ f.inf. a torch to fall on milk; any business or thing to be utterly destroyed in its very inception; like an infant whose life depends on its mother's milk, and who loses its mother immediately after birth. --driyĕ pĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. curses to fall on milk; an impediment to occur in the very commencement of any auspicious action, like a curse falling on the drinking of milk by a newly born child. --kȧnḍⁱ ʦārȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to collect thorns in milk, to search for faults in some action or business which is blameless, to pick holes without cause, to be over-scrupulous (K.Pr. 61). --lagun -- m.inf. (of a pregnant cow nearing the time of calving) the first signs of a flow of milk to become evident.
num. adj. c.g. one and a half (K.Pr. 58). W. 105 makes this word ḍoḍᵘ, with f. düḍᵘ̈.
f. a kind of bracelet (El.) (? spelling of this word; El. has dōdabungir, and makes it m.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dŏdarôwᵘ), to cause to rot (Gr.Gr.); to allow to spoil or get rotten by want of care; (of human beings) to make weak by harassment; (of sorrow) to render a person weak. dŏdarôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. dŏdaröwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), allowed to get rotten by want of care; weakened by sorrow, harassment, or the like.
in dŏdarȧyⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to disappear, esp. of the pustules of smallpox.

m. N. of a village about ten miles to the north of Śrīnagar. It is the ancient Dugdhâśrama, and here the valley of the Sindhu (Sind) River debouches into the great Kashmīr plain (RT.Tr. II, 419, 489).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. dŏdaryōv), to rot, decay; to be worn out (of clothes); to be withered, weak, decrepit (of human beings) (K.Pr. 50, Rām. 1634). dŏdaryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. dŏdaryē-müʦᵘ̈), rotted, decayed; worn out, weakened, decrepit.
f. a cow which is in milk; N. of a certain medicinal plant, the leaves of which exude a milky juice when cut; ? the dandelion, cf. dūdal.

adj. (f. dŏdürᵘ̈), decayed, rotten, worm-eaten, worn out (of trees, wood, clothes, utensils, or the like); weak, decrepit (of human beings); (as subst.) rotting, rottenness (El., Gr.Gr. 121, K.Pr. 12). --aʦun -- m.inf. to enter decayedness, worn-outness, etc.; an attack of weakness or decrepitude to occur. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause decrepitude to enter; by constant worrying to make a person prematurely old.
m. extreme thirst. --hyonᵘ --, --pyonᵘ --, or --wŏthun -- m.inf. great thirst to occur.

dọ̆dᵘ adj. (f. düzᵘ̈), burnt; full of rage. Properly 1 p.p. of dazun, q.v. -wan, also spelt dọ̆dᵘwan or düdᵘ̈wan, see bel. subst.m. and adj. c.g. a burnt-down forest; met. (as adj.) like a burnt forest (of a bare, leafless, tree, plant, etc.); met. of a country, of a custom, etc. ¶ dȧdⁱ-kã̄gⁱrⁱ f. the fire- brazier of a burnt man; met. when one is well off and comfortable to calumniate or reproach another with whom one has no concern. -wạtᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. false calumny without necessity or cause. ¶ düdᵘ̈wan m. a burnt forest, a forest which has been burnt down by a conflagration. düdᵘ̈wanas nyūrᵘ yunᵘ m.inf. new growth to come to a burnt forest; met. (of a family, a business, etc.) to take new life (after apparent destruction).

m. pain, agony, anguish, mental (YZ. 574, K.Pr. 167, Rām. 291, 1422) or physical (K.Pr. 23, 53, 65, 76); the pain of sickness, sickness (Śiv. 1855, dödis dag, the pain of sickness); sickness, ailment, disease (El.). The part of the body in which pain is felt is put in the dat. Thus, dandas dôdᵘ, a pain in the tooth, toothache; kalas d., a headache; kalējas d., liver complaint; kanas d., earache; zuwas d., pain in the body (Gr.M.). On the other hand, dazanas d., there is pain from a burn (K.Pr. 54); nafsa d., difficulty of breath, breathlessness (YZ. 398); pŏtra d., grief for a (dead) son (YZ. 417), grief of a barren woman longing for a son (K.Pr. 174); andarimⁱ dödⁱ, internal pains, heart-grief (K.Pr. 13). Cf. dag 1. --āsun -- m.inf. to suffer pain, be pained (El.). --hyuhᵘ -- m. something like pain, a feeling of pain. --karun -- m.inf. to ache, be painful (Gr.M.). --lagun -- or --sapadun -- m.inf. to suffer pain, be pained (El.). ¶ dādi-sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), pained, suffering pain (Rām. 242). ¶ dödⁱ-kôṭⁱ adj. (f. -köṭᵘ̈), grieved, afflicted (El.). (The spelling of this word is doubtful; El. spells dãdkóṭ.) The word is probably incorrect for -kôṭhᵘ, see under dôdᵘ 3.

m. love, affection (shown to a beloved child, pupil, friend, or the like). Cf. dag 2. --barun -- m.inf. to seek affectionately for a loved friend, relation, or disciple, on the successful completion of some work, or on a similar occasion.

m. envy, hatred, jealousy. --tulun -- m.inf. to raise envy or jealousy, to arouse envy or jealousy in others by flaunting one's success, wealth, or the like. --wŏthun -- m.inf. envy or jealousy to be aroused. ¶ dödⁱ-kôṭhⁱ adj. (f. --köṭhᵘ̈ --), angrily disposed towards another. Cf. dödⁱ-kôṭⁱ under dôdᵘ 1. -wōv f. envy, jealousy, hate. -wōv tulüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to arouse envy, jealousy, etc. -wōv wŏthüñᵘ̈ f.inf. envy, jealousy to arise at another's success.
adv. continually, always; thoroughly, well done (K.Pr. 25, ḍāḍi). Cf. ḍāḍa.
in dödⁱ ogun m. a forest conflagration (K. 256).
. In the old Ksh. of L.V. 79, ḍöḍⁱ is spelt döḍⁱ.

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. dödⁱladiñ), one who suffers pain, esp. mental pain (YZ. 203) caused by another's action; miserable, grieved, afflicted (El., Gr.M., YZ. 562, 564, 573, Rām. 292); one who is suffering from sickness, sick; painful (of a wound) (YZ. 74). Cf. dôdᵘ 1.

m. pounding, beating, esp. the pounding of grain to remove the husk, husking (Gr.Gr. 123). The pounding is usually done in a mortar with a heavy pestle worked like a pedal by the foot (K.Pr. 224). Cf. dŏga-athawār, bel. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give pounding, to pound; esp. to give a thorough final pounding to grain that has already been husked in a mortar. ¶ dŏga-athawār f. a light pounding given to grain, in which a light hand-pestle, not the pedal-pestle, is employed. -bọ̆chᵘ adj. (f. -bö̆chᵘ̈), hungry for pounding; (of grain, etc.) incompletely husked, husked only once and requiring further pounding. -chih f. (sg. dat. -chishᵘ̈), an incomplete husking, as ab.; cf. chih 2. -diwath f. (sg. dat. -diwati), a pestle-goddess (cf. diwath 2), a woman, a portrait, or statue, ugly and irregularly featured or formed. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to draw from pounding, to complete the pounding of grain when it is entirely husked. -mŏzūr m. (f. -mŏzᵃrĕñ), one who lives by hiring himself or herself as a grain-husker. -mŏzūrⁱ f. wages paid to a professional grain-husker.
or dŏgȧlⁱ bata m. cooked rice with clotted lumps of rice in it. Cf. dŏgulᵘ.

or dŏgunᵘ adj. (f. dö̆gᵘ̈ñᵘ̈), twofold, double, twice as much or as many (Rām. 600, 630, 1032); doubled, folded over (e.g. paper or string, Gr.M.). ¶ dŏgȧnⁱ m.pl. the word used for the numeral 'two' in multiplication, as in trih dŏgȧnⁱ shĕh, three doubles (are) six, i.e. twice three are six (Gr.Gr. 86).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dŏganôwᵘ), to husk grain by pounding in a mortar, i.q. dŏgawun, q.v., also with caus. sense to get grain husked by another, to cause to be husked. dŏganôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. dŏganövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of grain) husked; caused to be husked by another.
f. a woman who is in the habit of pounding grain. Cf. dŏgᵃr.
f. N. of a kind of small bird with a long beak.
m. globularity, roundness (e.g. of a gourd, radish, or a forehead).
f. wages paid for husking grain.
conj. 1 (1 p.p.dŏgowᵘ), to pound grain in a mortar with a pedal-pestle so as to remove the husk, to husk grain (Gr.Gr. 123). Cf. dŏganāwun. dŏgowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. dŏgüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), husked as ab.
adj. c.g. thoroughly pounded, thoroughly husked and cleaned (of grain, etc.).
f. (sg. dat. ḍögiñᵘ̈ 1), a witch, a vampire, a woman believed to have the power of killing a person by drawing out his heart. Cf. ḍögiñᵘ̈ 2 and ḍögyunᵘ.
f. a female witch or demon (Ram. 1163). i.q. ḍögin, q.v.
? (L. 354), a large kind of water-chestnut, with a thick shell.

adj. (f. dŏgᵘ̈jᵘ̈), shaped like the fist, lumpish, lumpy (Gr.Gr. 145); subst.m. a lump of any soft or moist substance, such as mud, or a ball of rice ready to put into the mouth. Cf. dŏgᵘ̈jᵘ̈ and dŏgal-bata.
m. (sg. dat. ḍŏgaris; ag. and pl. nom. ḍŏgᵃrᵃ), (in spinning) the spool or winder for receiving the spun thread; a four-legged machine for winding off silk from a cocoon.

adj. (m. sg. dat. ḍŏgaris, sg. ag. and plur. nom. ḍŏgᵃ̇rᵃ̇; f. sg. nom. ḍŏgᵘ̈rᵘ̈), stout, plump, globular-waisted (like a spool of spun thread, e.g. a gourd or a forehead). See ḍŏgurᵘ 1. ¶ ḍŏgᵃrĕ mŏnjĕ f.pl. a bunch of thick vegetable stalks.
m. a wizard, a weaver of spells sufficient to cause another's death or to relieve a person possessed by a witch. The fem. of this word is ḍögin or ḍögiñᵘ̈, qq.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dọ̆gᵃnôwᵃ), to double, make twice as much or as many (Śiv. 1756); to fold double; to twist double or in two strands (of string, etc.) (Śiv. 1217, 1643); to do twice over, repeat (Gr.M.). dọ̆gᵃnôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. dọ̆gᵃnövᵃ-müʦᵃ), doubled.
f. a woman who lives by pounding grain for hire. Cf. dŏgarĕñ 1.
f. a woman who is an industrious and expert husker of rice. Cf. dŏgᵃr.

m. a blow with the closed fist, a thump (K.Pr. 56, dug); the fist (Gr.Gr. 145, El. daug). -dọ̆gᵘ m. a kind of shampooing, in which the back and loins are thumped with the fist, believed to relieve weariness and to aid digestion. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to strike, thump (K.Pr. 59). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to receive a thump, to be beaten (K.Pr. 59). --lāyun -- m.inf. to strike with the closed fist, to thump. ¶ dŏgi ti bārav dŏgⁱ hata ti bārav m.pl. grumbling at one stroke, and also grumbling at a hundred strokes; met. grumbling at whatever is given, whether little or much, persistent ingratitude; also (cf. K.Pr. 58) a complaint to the magistrate for one blow, and also a complaint for a hundred blows (i.e. the punishment is the same in each case, equivalent to "one may as well be hanged for a sheep as for a farthing").
or ḍogᵘ m. a gathering on the back of the finger-tip, a whitlow.
f. a small lump of any moist substance, such as soft earth, or a small ball of boiled rice ready to be put into the mouth (dim. of dŏgulᵘ, q.v.).

m. (this word often becomes duh in compounds or derivatives; YZ. always spells the word dōh), daytime, as opposed to night (Śiv. 332); a day, amongst Hindūs from sunrise to sunrise, and amongst Musalmāns from sunset to sunset (YZ. 112, Śiv. 168, 458, 594, 1443, K.Pr. 59). trĕyimi dŏha, on the third day, YZ. 104; ʦŏn dŏhan, for four days, YZ. 158; tami dŏhay, on that very day, YZ. 174, but see dŏhay, s.v. boḍᵘ dŏh, a big day, a great day, a holiday, but not necessarily a day of rejoicing; cf. K.Pr. 28. Besides indicating the period of twenty-four hours, this word is also used to signify the day from sunrise to sunset, and in this sense the comp. dŏh-rāth is used to indicate the day of twenty-four hours. Cf. K.Pr. 176, Śiv. 1584. So rāth-dŏh (Śiv. 341), adv. night and day. --āsun -- m.inf. a day to be; esp. a lucky day to come, to be a day of good luck, to be a day on which something referred to turns out satisfactorily. --barun -- m.inf. to fill the day, to spend the day, to pass a day satisfactorily in earning one's livelihood. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give (a whole) day, voluntarily to occupy oneself the whole day over anything. --dari lagun -- m.inf. the day to become stopped, the day to approach evening, to be about an hour before sunset. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. a day to go, a day to pass, a day to elapse (K.Pr. 161). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to drag out the day, to occupy oneself throughout the day (e.g. a poor man earning his livelihood, or a sick man getting better). --khārun -- m.inf. to cause the day to mount, i.e. to spend the day in paid labour. --khasun -- m.inf. the day to mount; the day to be spent in paid labour. --lōsun -- m.inf. the day to grow weary, eventide to fall (K.Pr. 18, lūsum dŏh, the day wearied for me, i.e. I found it was evening). Cf. dŏhⁱlūsyunⁱ, etc., bel. --nibāwun -- m.inf. to pass the day, spend the time. --prāwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to obtain days, (of a sick person or the like) to pass through the critical period of an illness, so as to gain hope of recovery. --rāwun -- m.inf. a day to be lost or wasted, a day to be spent fruitlessly, one's time to be wasted. --rāwarun -- m.inf. to lose a day, to waste a day, to spend a day fruitlessly, to waste one's time (K.Pr. 188, W. 139). --ṭhukun -- m.inf. to bury the day; met. to complete one's day's work (K.Pr. 131). --wŏlangun -- m.inf. to get through the day; esp. to spend the day fasting from poverty or the like. --wasun -- m.inf. the day to descend; to be near eventide. --yinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. days to come; esp. good times to come. ¶ dŏha sg. abl., as adv., on (such and such) a day (YZ. 104, Śiv. 740, 1549); day by day (Gr.Gr. 158); so prath dŏha, day by day (Gr.Gr. 157, W. 95). --aki -- adv. on a certain day, one day, once upon a time (Śiv. 164, Rām. 230, 1286). --dŏha -- adv. day by day, every day. -dȧshⁱ adv. on an ordinary day (as distinct from a holiday), u. w. vbs. of doing, eating, or the like. -dȧshⁱ-hondⁱ adj. (f. -dȧshⁱ-hünzⁱ), of or belonging to ordinary working days (e.g. vessels, clothes, conduct, etc.). -kāḍay f. spending a whole day over anything, esp. with the desire of causing delay, lingering over anything. -nöshⁱ f. spending a day fruitlessly, wasting time in idleness. --path dŏha -- adv. day after day, day by day, every day, daily (Gr.Gr. 158). -törᵘ̈ f. day-delay, delay of only a single day for the accomplishment of anything; procrastination owing to unwillingness to carry out any work. ¶ dŏhā dŏhā adv. daily, every day (H. viii, 3). ¶ dŏhⁱ adv. after the day is over; hence, late, too late. dahi dŏhⁱ adv. after ten days (Gr.M.). Cf. dohᵘ. --lūsyunᵘ -- m. evening, the time of sunset; cf. dŏh lōsun ab. -lūsiñ, or -lōsañĕn, or -lūsiñ-bögⁱ, or -lōsañĕn-bögⁱ, or -lūsiñĕn-bögⁱ, or -lōsañĕn-bögin, or -lūsⁱñĕn-bögin adv. at eventide. Cf. dŏh lōsun ab. ¶ dŏhāh m. a day (indefinite) (Śiv. 1444). dŏhāh khanḍā m. about a day, but something less (Gr.Gr. 93). ¶ dŏhukᵘ or duhukᵘ adj. (f. dŏhücᵘ̈ or duhücᵘ̈), of or belonging to a day, esp. to a certain day; born or produced in a single day. ¶ dŏhas (sg. dat.), adv. by day, in the daytime (YZ. 90, 118, Śiv. 325). drustis dŏhas adv. all day long (Gr.M.). -kyutᵘ adj. (f. -kiʦᵘ̈), for a day; sufficient for one whole day.

card. c.g. (pl. dat. dŏhaiṭhan or dŏhöṭhan), sixty-two. ¶ dŏhaiṭhukᵘ or dŏhöṭhukᵘ adj. (f. dŏhaiṭhücᵘ̈), of sixty-two, commenced or done in the sixty-second year. ¶ dŏhaiṭhas- (or dŏhöṭhas-)kyutᵘ̈ adv. in the (or a person's) sixty-second year.
ord. (f. dŏhaiṭhimᵘ̈), sixty-second. Also spelt duhaiṭhyumᵘ or duhöṭhyumᵘ.
adj. (f. dŏhaiṭhiñᵘ̈), of the value of, or costing, sixty-two (rupees or the like). Also spelt du˚.

adv. even day by day; daily, every day (Gr.Gr. 158, Śiv. 327, 648, 1906); always, continually, perpetually (Śiv. 645, 1905), over and over again; generally, as a rule (W. 95, Gr.M.); on (that) very day (YZ. 174).

or duhulᵘ m. (sg. dat. duhalis, ag. duhᵃ̇lᵃ̇), daytime, the time from sunrise to sunset (Gr.Gr. 146, 156). ¶ dŏhᵃ̇lᵃ̇ or (K. 972) dŏhali adv. by day, in the daytime (Gr.Gr. 156, K.Pr. 49, 59). duhᵃ̇lᵃ̇-gāsh m. daylight, the light of day, esp. the remains of daylight at eventide, twilight. -gaṭa f. darkness by daytime (from clouds, a dust-storm, or the like). -khāv m. (f. -khöviñ), one who eats by day on a day in which he should fast; esp. a Musalmān who does not keep the fast of Ramaẓān, during which eating between sunrise and sunset is forbidden (K.Pr. 14). -lạgᵃn m. a day marriage, a wedding of which the auspicious moment for the ceremony occurs in the daytime. -sāth m. (sg. dat. -sātas), an auspicious moment (e.g. for setting out on a journey, or for entering a house for the first time) which occurs in the daytime, and not in the night-time. -ʦūr m. a thief by daylight, one who steals only in the daytime (most thieves steal by night; see the following). -ʦūrᵘ̈ f. thieving which is done by day only, not the usual thieving which is done by night. -vil f. a time or hour in the daytime. ¶ dŏhaliy adv. only in the daytime; esp. u. w. vbs. of stealing or the like, see duhᵃ̇lᵃ̇ ʦūr ab. ¶ dŏhalyukᵘ adj. (f. dŏhalicᵘ̈), of or belonging to the daytime; born or produced in the daytime. ¶ dᵃ̇hᵃ̇lad adj. c.g. smoky; harassed or confused by smoke. --gagur hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. --hishᵘ̈ --), like a rat confused by smoke, put to great shame by calumny or abuse.
adj. (f. döhijᵘ̈), burning the vitals, touching the vulnerable part, touching the quick, heart-burning lit. and met.

m. a group of ten, a ten (Gr.Gr. 84); with suff. of indef. art., dohwāh khanḍā, a group of about ten, but a little less than ten (Gr.Gr. 84). ¶ dȧhⁱ m.pl. groups of ten, the form used for dah, ten, in multiplication, as in zᵃh dȧhⁱ wuh, two tens twenty, twice ten is twenty (Gr.Gr. 86, W. 104). ¶ dahi dŏhⁱ, after ten days; so --warihĕ zyāda --, more than ten years; --warihĕ pĕṭha --, from a ten year, for the last ten years; --bajĕ --, at the stroke of ten, at ten o'clock (Gr.M.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dö̃jᵒrᵒ), to put down or set down in the right way, to deposit in a safe manner or place; (of food, etc.) to prepare properly, to cook in a proper manner. dö̃jᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. dö̃jᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), put by properly, put down or set down in a safe place; (of food, etc.), properly prepared.

or dojᵘ adj. (f. dö̆jᵘ̈ or düjᵘ̈ 1), unintelligent, stupid; one who pretends stupidity in order to avoid obeying another's instructions, e.g. pretending that one does not hear or see, when one really does hear or see. --bāzanda -- adj. c.g. playing stupid, intentionally pretending to be stupid in another's presence. ¶ dȧjⁱ-bāpār m. pretended stupidity of conduct, conduct of one who pretends to be stupid. -pöthᵃr m., id.

f. a band of twisted twigs or withes. ¶ dājĕ-korᵘ m. an ornamental band or hoop of twisted twigs fastened round baskets, etc. -kranḍa m. a wicker trunk or covered box so ornamented. -kronḍᵘ m. a smaller and finer-worked kind of the ab. wicker box. -krünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kranjĕ), a basket similarly ornamented. -lŏngunᵘ m. a small kind of tray so ornamented. -lŏngüñᵘ̈ f. a vessel or tray for holding flowers or the like, smaller than the preceding, similarly ornamented. -phọ̆tᵘ m. a large kind of basket bound round with these wicker rings. -photᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a similar but smaller basket.

f. a water-channel, a ditch, esp. in rice-fields or the like. ¶ ḍã̄jĕ karun m.inf. to supply with a water-channel; met. make any person satisfied with food and drink. --karañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to make water-channels; to throw any liquid on to level ground so that it flows away thence in streams in different directions.

m. (sg. dat. dŏkhas), pain, sorrow, trouble (K.Pr. 62 dokh, 164 dukh; Śiv. 13, 94, 199, etc., nom. pl. Śiv. 41, 105); esp. sorrow caused by the death of a beloved one (YZ. 570, 574); bodily pain (El.); mental grief; difficulty, vexation, annoyance (El.); fatigue, labour, toil; a misfortune, unhappy event (Gr.M.). This word is often opposed to sŏkh, happiness, as in Śiv. 41, 444, 483, 922, 1819. --barun -- m.inf. to suffer distress or trouble (Rām. 302); to put oneself to inconvenience; to labour, toil. -dôdᵘ m. pain, trouble, sorrow generally (Rām. 291). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give pain (to); to occasion trouble, to bother; to give bodily hurt (to), to hurt; to give mental distress (to), to distress, torment (El.); to give offence, cause vexation (Gr.M.); to be dangerous, offensive (of an animal) (Gr.M.). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to suffer pain or trouble, to be afflicted. --kāsun -- m.inf. to put a stop to grief, to relieve grief, console (me = mĕ, Śiv. 1434) (Śiv. 978, 1438). --ʦhunun-- m.inf. to cause sorrow to another (e.g. by killing a beloved one, by causing pecuniary loss, or by giving bad news). ¶ dŏkha borᵘ-motᵘ (Śiv. 171), adj. (f. --bürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --) or dŏkha barith, adj. c.g. full of grief; mournful, affecting (of a circumstance or story) (Gr.M.). -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), afflicted, grieved (e.g. by the death of a loved one); mournful, sorrowful, grief-causing, compassion-rousing (e.g. an action, a statement, or an occupation). -māri adv. pitifully, compassionately, struck by sorrow. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), afflicted, sorry; sorry (for an offence) (Gr.M.). --tulun -- m.inf. to raise from grief; esp. when a woman is suffering from grief owing to the death of some dearly loved one, to take her away from the mournful scene, or to divert her mind from the mournful thoughts, to console. --tulawañ -- f. payment (or wages) for raising from grief, i.e. the gifts of money and jewellery, etc., given to a woman some time after the death of a husband or other loved person, in order to console her. --wọ̆thᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --wö̆ʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), gone out of mourning as in next. --wŏthun -- m.inf. to rise from grief; to put off signs of grief for the death of a loved one after the customary period of mourning, to go out of mourning. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), pierced by sorrow, pained, afflicted (Gr.M.); distressed, esp. by the death of one beloved. ¶ dŏkhⁱ adv. with difficulty, not easily (Gr.M.). ¶ dŏkhas bihun m.inf. to sit for grief; to sit in mourning during the period of impurity after the death of a near relation.

f. (sg. dat. dō̃ki), a peck of a beak. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (to thrust in one's beak; met. to put an impediment in the way of something approaching a successful conclusion). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make a peck; met. to prevent the success of any action by false accusations or the like (e.g. by maligning a servant to his master, or a suppliant to the supplicated). ¶ dō̃ka-dō̃kh f. (sg. dat. -dō̃ki), beak to beak, the mutual pecking of birds fighting; met. the wordy warfare of children or women.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. dŏkhaladiñ), one who is suffering from sorrow, trouble, etc., uneasy (El., Gr.Gr. 135); esp. one who is suffering from grief owing to the death of a beloved one.
adj. c.g. uneasy, pained, afflicted (Śiv. 1438); vexed, troubled (El., Gr.M.).

m. a support, prop, esp. a support for the back when seated, a cushion, pillow, bolster (Rām. 432); help, assistance. Cf. aḍ and al 1. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give support; esp. to rest the back against a support, e.g. a wall, or to place a bolster or the like behind one's back.
. Add at end of article '--ʦānun -- m.inf. to hold up from below, support, prop up (K. 326, 331)'.
m. a reed mat used as the covering or roof of a boat, etc. (El. ḍúk). Cf. ḍȧkhⁱdār.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ḍŏkyōv), to be bent, humpbacked (from disease, old age, etc.); to come out too little, to come out too short (e.g. of cloth coming out shorter than the measured amount of thread originally given out before weaving, or of a copper vessel weighing less than the amount of copper given out for its manufacture). ḍŏkyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ḍakyē-müʦᵘ̈), become bent, humpbacked; come out too little, too short, as ab.

a kind of hammer for use in metal-work, with a drum-shaped head. (El. dauker; L. 460, dokar; Śiv. 1563.) ¶ dŏkȧrⁱ-dab m. hitting with a hammer, esp. the welding together of heated metal. --dan m. the wooden handle of such a hammer.

m. (sg. dat. ḍŏkaris-ḍŏkaris), the condition of a bent or humpbacked person (from old age, injury to the spine, or the like). Cf. ḍŏkhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ and dọ̆kᵘ. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to do a little work as best one can when one is bent by old age.
adj. (f. ḍŏ̈cᵘ̈), humpbacked, crooked-bodied; bent from old age. Cf. ḍạkhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ and ḍŏkurᵘ-ḍŏkurᵘ.

f. an impediment, intervention, obstacle, esp. the prevention of the success of any action or business nearing its accomplishment by tale-telling, treacherous betrayal of a secret, or the like. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such treacherous impeding to occur. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause such impeding by betraying a secret or the like. ¶ dŏkri-bāz adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -bāzañ), a tale-bearing impeder, one who is addicted to impeding in this way.

m. a hindrance, impediment. Cf. ḍūlⁱ 2. -dōl lagun m.inf. continual impediments to keep occurring, either in the accomplishment of some necessary work or preventing its commencement. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give impediment; when one person is employed on another's work and wishes to complete it, a third person to impede him by arguing or by carrying tales. --lagun -- m.inf. an impediment to occur, esp. in the commencement of a necessary work. --yunᵘ -- m.inf., id. ¶ dōla rōzun m.inf. to impede, hinder. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. an impediment to occur just at the conclusion of a work. -yārĕ f.pl. pine-trees as an impediment; (on a mountain road) a block caused by a thicket or group of trees.
m. shape, form, fashion, appearance; pattern, model, specimen; the form of some representation of another object, likeness; met. form, in the sense of formed character, proper bringing up. Cf. bĕḍōl.
m. a large drum, a kind of kettle-drum (Śiv. 1029, K. 1009).
m. a bucket (of leather or metal) for drawing water, a well-bucket.

adj. c.g. crooked; squint-eyed, crooked-eyed; adv. crookedly, not straight, not squarely, transversely, u.w. vbs. of placing, position, or the like. -dukônᵘ adj. (f. -duköñᵘ̈), doubly squint-eyed, squint-eyed with both eyes, so that one sees double when looking with both eyes. -dōla adv. (of more than one thing) not evenly together, not straight together, awry, zigzag, u.w. vbs. of placing, position, etc. -dōla wuchun m.inf. to see crookedly; to look upon with enmity, to regard jealously; to look deceitfully, guilefully (YZ. 266); to look flirtingly or archly. -kônᵘ adj. (f. -köñᵘ̈), squint-eyed. -kāñĕr m. squint-eyedness, squinting. -vüñᵘ̈ f. a zigzag path so as to reduce the slope on a mountain-side. -wạy m. id.

f. (sg. dat. dōlüʦᵘ̈), good fortune, prosperity, riches, wealth (K.Pr. 52, 157, 246, 254; Śiv. 430, 579; Rām. 142, 330). ¶ dōlüʦᵘ̈-band (= دولت مند) adj. c.g. very wealthy. -wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), id.
n.ag. (f. ḍōlawüñᵘ̈), that which is plentiful and easily obtained (esp. of food). The idea of being so common as not to be appreciated is usually present in this word. Cf. ḍōlun.
adj. c.g. possessing form, esp. having a pretty form, pretty, elegant (of vessels, ornaments, clothes, or the like).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. ḍọ̆lᵘ), to be unused owing to its having no owner, to lie unused, to be left unenjoyed; to be unappreciated owing to its commonness or the ease with which it can be obtained; i.q. ḍōlun. ¶ ḍŏlyō-mutᵘ perf. part. (f. ḍŏlyē-müʦᵘ̈), left unused, unenjoyed, unappreciated.

conj. 2 (pres. part. ḍōlān or m.c.ḍōlan, Śiv. as bel.; 1 p.p. ḍūlᵘ,pl.ḍūlⁱ; f. ḍūjᵘ̈, pl. ḍōjĕ; 2 p.p. ḍōjyōv), to be very easily obtained and hence unappreciated and unused, to be of no value, to be a drug in the market (YZ. 548, Śiv. 1287, 1289); to be unused owing to having no owner. i.q. ḍŏlun. ¶ ḍūlᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ḍūjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), unused, unappreciated, as ab.
m. winnowings, siftings, the refuse which is separated from grain by winnowing.
m. a small metal amulet or ornament in the shape of a drum, worn on the neck; the small metal case in which charms are worn by Musalmāns (El.). -raz f. a necklace made of a number of such amulets.
adj. (f. düjᵘ̈ 4; for düjᵘ̈ 1 see dọ̆jᵘ, 2 see s.v., 3 see dagun 2, 5 and for dolᵘ 3 see dalun); crushed, pounded (of grain); used --˚ after numerals, as in du-dolᵘ, pounded or husked twice over.

m. the skirt, usually the front skirt, of a garment (El. daul, dul = dāman) (K.Pr. 61, 112, 125, 248, 254; W. 135). --düjᵘ̈ -- f. the various pieces which go to make up the front edge of a bodice. --dᵃnun -- m.inf. to shake out the skirt, to shake dust or dirt out of the skirt (K.Pr. 112, where dul den is for dolᵘ dᵃn, imperat. sg. 2). --dᵃnith trāwun -- m.inf. to shake out one's skirt and abandon; to abandon any task and give up all connexion with it, to wash one's hands of anything. ¶ dȧlⁱ cīrȧnⁱ m.pl. inf. to wring out one's skirts; to repudiate or free oneself from the damage resulting from an accusation. -sörᵘ̈ f. collecting and carrying away in the front skirt of one's garment. --trôwᵘ -- adj.f. (f. --tröwᵘ̈ --), one who carelessly scatters abroad money, household goods, etc., wasteful, extravagant, an uneconomical housekeeper. -trāvĕr m. wastefulness, bad housekeeping. --ʦoṭᵘ -- m. one the skirt of whose coat is torn or cut; a skirt, the lower part of which is torn. --ʦaṭȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to cut or tear the skirts; met. to eagerly press a guest to take food (even when he does not want it), to force hospitality upon a person. ¶ dali dᵃnith trāwun m.inf. to shake off from the skirt; met. to put any unpleasant memory out of the mind. --dᵃnith ʦhunun -- m.inf., id.
adj. c.g. made of skin, esp. of tanned leather.
f. a 'dalee', a present of fruit, flowers, sweetmeats, etc. (brought on a tray).
f. a piece of cloth let into a garment to prevent its being too tight, a gore, a gusset.

or ḍombᵘ  m. the stomach; the contents of the stomach; met. the womb (K.Pr. 47); offspring, a person's son or daughter. --chalun --  m.inf. to wash out the stomach; met. to find out another's intentions without his knowledge under pretext of merely conversing with him, to worm out another's intentions. -ʦaph m. (sg. dat. -ʦapas), stomach and bowels, the abdomen; met. one's own begotten child (K.Pr. 61) (ʦaph, q.v., is fem., and possibly this word should also be f. In that case the sg. dat. would be ʦapi). ¶ ḍȧmbⁱ-dôdⁱ m. offspring-pain, the sorrow of a childless married couple. -dag f. an offspring-blow, the sorrow or pain felt by a parent when a child is suffering, or when a child is misconducted; the pain felt by a childless married couple. -kalapushᵘ m. the entire stomach of a sheep, etc., as sold by butchers, a sheep's paunch. Cf. ḍamiñĕ- kalapushᵘ under ḍamiñᵘ̈. -kānul or ḍȧmⁱ-kānul m. (sg. dat. -kānalas), a beam, a rafter, supporting the boards of a roof. -lọ̆ʦhᵘ m. a lump of entrails with their contents. -phĕl m. a cancer in the stomach; met. a bad son, a son who grieves his parents by his evil ways. ¶ ḍambi phŏlun m.inf. to blossom from the belly; met. to have a son or daughter possessing all kinds of good qualities, hence --phọ̆lᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --phö̆jᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), blessed with such a son or daughter. --phaṭun -- m.inf. to burst from the belly; met. to bear offspring from one's own womb, to bear a child, hence --phoṭᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --phüṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), a child who is born from one's own womb. ¶ ḍambyukᵘ adj. (f. ḍambicᵘ̈), of or belonging to one's own belly, a son or daughter born from one's own womb, i.e. not an adopted son or born of a co-wife. Cf. ḍambyunᵘ.
m. a brick of tea as imported from Central Asia.
m. a projecting rocky mountain crag.
m. the stick by which the string of a cotton-carding bow is struck by the carder. Cf. dūnᵘ 2 and dūñᵘ̈ 2.
f. wages paid for carding wool, cotton, etc.

card. c.g. (pl. dat. dŏnawȧnⁱ or dŏnawanī; ag. and abl. dŏnawȧyⁱ, see Gr.Gr. 85), an emphatic form of zᵃh, two, meaning 'even the two', 'even both', 'both' (Rām. 239, 269, 724, 1115, 1503, etc.). Cf. dŏshĕway. dŏnawȧnⁱ-hondⁱ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to both and only to them.
m. the name of a Rākṣasa or demon, in Sanskrit Dundubhi (Rām. 472, 477).
f. proclamation by beat of drum, i.q. ḍạnḍūra.
m. the front of the face, the profile.
m. the railing of a balcony.
adj. (f. dünzᵘ̈ 2, for 1 see s.v.), having ugly projecting teeth; tusked (Gr.Gr. 137); met. toothed, notched.
m. the skirt of a hill, the slope at the middle of a hill.
m. a joining groove or mortice in carpentry. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to cut such a groove or mortice.
m. an elevated stage erected in a field on which the crop-watcher sits.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. dūnᵘ, f.pl. dōñĕ), to card or clean cotton, wool, etc. dūnᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. dūñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), carded.
adj. (f. ḍōnivᵘ̈), made of walnut wood (e.g. a box or the like).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. döñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), to consider about, reflect on, think over (Śiv. 1667); i.q. döñᵉ̆run, q.v. döñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. döñᵉ̆röwᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), reflected upon, considered.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. döñᵒrᵒ), to consider about, reflect on, think over (Śiv. 1050). Also döñᵉ̆rāwun (e.g. Śiv. 1667). döñᵒrᵒ-motᵒ  perf. part. (f. döñᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), reflected upon, considered.
m. (sg. dat. dönis, abl. dāni), a churning-stick, a dasher (Gr.Gr. 12; Śiv. 1435, 1838).

m. a pomegranate (the fruit), Punica granatum (L. 73, 348, 350, dán; K.Pr. 146, dain; Śiv. 468). According to El. s.v. there are three varieties of this fruit grown in Kashmīr: ʦọ̆kᵘ dönᵘ, mŏdur d., and jigari d. The pomegranate ripens in September, and is of inferior quality. The word is declined in Gr.Gr. 54. -bạrᵃg m. the leaf of a pomegranate-tree. -dĕl m. the soft outer skin of a pomegranate. -hüṭᵘ̈ f. the wood of the pomegranate-tree, esp. the split wood. -kujⁱ or -kujᵘ̈ f. a small pomegranate-tree. -kulᵘ m. a pomegranate-tree (El.), esp. when large and full-grown. -künḍᵘ̈ f. the hard outer shell of a pomegranate. -mūrᵘ̈ f. the young non-fruit-bearing shoot or branch of a pomegranate-tree. -mŏrba m. pomegranate conserve. -pholᵘ m. a single pomegranate seed. -pōsh m. a pomegranate flower (YZ. 527, Rām. 644). -ras m. pomegranate juice. -shīra m. a drink made of pomegranate juice and used as a cooling medicine. -thürᵘ̈ f. a pomegranate bush, a bushy young pomegranate-tree.

f. (sg. dat. dāñĕ 2), the name of the amount of a certain weight, equivalent to the weight of six seeds of the Abrus precatorius, each weighing about eight barley-corns. Cf. dāñukᵘ; met. a very small amount, hence döñᵘ̈döñᵘ̈ every particle, every single piece (Śiv. 1524, m.c. döñᵘ̈ döñī), and dāñĕ dāñĕ adv. in every particle, to the last grain, entirely (Śiv. 1301, 1308, 1313).
adj. (f. düñᵘ̈), fortunate, happy, rich, opulent (L.V. 27).
. The word döñᵘ̈ (Skt. dhanikā) is used like our 'carat' to indicate the fineness of gold. See sata-döñᵘ̈, p. 944a, l. 38, for particulars.
f. (sg. dat. dō̃pi), a sword-stick, a walking-stick with a sword hidden inside it.
m. (sg. dat. dŏpas), a shrub, a small bush (Gr.M.).
m. (sg. dat. dŏpas), the sound caused by falling from a height (e.g. on to a roof), crash, flop, bang. --karith -- adv. with such a sound, crash, u.w. vbs. of falling, etc.
two-dotted; (in Sanskrit grammar) the sign or visarjanīya.

m. (really 1 p.p. of dāpun, q.v.), a thing said (K.Pr. 139); an order, command. ¶ dapi-kömᵘ̈ f. a work done by command, and not voluntarily. --karun -- m.inf. to carry out a work under another's orders, and not of one's own motion.
m. land covered with very shallow water, a watery country, a slightly flooded country (from rain or overflow). Cf. dōr 5, dūr 5, and ḍūrᵘ.

m. circuit, revolution; circuit of rule, jurisdiction, power, authority, dominion, sway (Rām. 997); a high or responsible office, such as that of treasurer or head of a city. --karȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to occupy such high positions in due course, or otherwise. ¶ dōra-dōr 1 f. might, power, sway (Śiv. 738). dōra-dōr karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to gradually reach a high position or station. ¶ dōrĕ-phyurᵘ m. reversal of one's circuit, going back on one's course, losing one's way (Śiv. 1834). dōr-ĕ zamāna دور زمانہ m. the revolution of ages (Śiv. 726).
or dair 1 m. firmness, constancy, calmness, gravity, fortitude (Śiv. 338, 1022, K. 414). Also written dörᵘ̈ 1 (e.g. Śiv. 52, 128, 728) and döry or dairy (e.g. Śiv. 1109, 1271, 1373, 1563).

f. running, a run; (of a horse or the like) galloping, a gallop (Gr.Gr. 127). --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring the act of running; hence, to come running, to come quickly. --niñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to run fast, gallop. --trāwüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf., id. --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to get over at a run; (of a road) to pass over very quickly; (of a book, etc.) to get through very quickly, to read quickly, to gallop through. ¶ dōra-dōr 2 f. running hither and thither, haste, hurry, bustle; much or frequent running or galloping; contest in running, a race. ¶ dōri yunᵘ m.inf. to come running, to run up (to a person) (K. 223).
m. a convent, a monastery; (in Kāshmīrī) the world (for Persian dair-ĕ tang) (YZ. 238).

f. a weaver's loom. ¶ dōri khôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. --khörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), that which has been put on a loom (of the warp for weaving). --khārun -- m.inf. to set the warp on a loom. --khasun -- m.inf. to mount the loom, i.e. (of the warp) to be set on the loom. --khotᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --khüʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), mounted on the loom, i.e. (of the warp) ready on the loom for weaving. --phyurᵘ -- m. the act of working the loom up and down and (the shuttle) backwards and forwards, weaving. --wothᵘ -- 1 p.p. (f. --wüʦhᵘ̈ --), descended from the loom, i.e. (of cloth) quite new and fresh from the loom.
m. a field, a little garden (El.). Cf. ḍōr, dūr 5, and ḍūrᵘ.

m. (sg. dat. ḍōras, abl. ḍōra, but ag. ḍūrⁱ), a thick string, a cord, a rope, halter (not so thick as a cable). Cf. ḍūrᵘ̈. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give rope, to give breathing time, to allow a person a short space in which to recover himself (in a fight or the like). -pan m. a short piece of rope or of the strand of a rope.

m. a round, revolution, circuit; a round, tour, course, circuit; the circulation of disease, periodic attacks of ague or the like. -bôjᵘ m. a circuit-sharer, i.e. a friend whose tastes, habits, and occupations are the same as one's own. -bata m. the preparation of many various kinds of food for a large number of guests invited on festival occasions and the like.
m. a long piece of cloth as it issues from the loom. See dōr 3.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. dōranôwᵘ), to cause to run. Caus. of dōrun (Gr.Gr. 174, Śiv. 1479).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. dōrovᵘ), to cause to run (K. 597).
m. one who conducts himself badly, evil-conducted, wicked.
m. (as subst., f. dŏrāʦārĕñ), i.q. dŏrāʦār, q.v.
durgam adj. c.g. impassable, difficult of access or approach, inaccessible (or nearly so), impenetrable, impervious (Gr.M.); difficult of attainment.
c.g. a bad smell, stink, esp. of rotten fruit or food.
f. (sg. dat. dŏrgüʦᵘ̈), poorness, poverty (lit. and fig.); destitution (Śiv. 1246, 1895); defeat (El.).
or dairī f. patience (in misfortune). --thawüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to exercise patience (Gr.M.).

c.g. an adjectival suffix meaning 'bearing', 'upholding', etc., as in diha-dörī, carrying a body, in bodily form (Śiv. 1887); Gōvardana-dörī, he who upheld Mount Gōvardhana, i.e. Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) (Śiv. 733); jaṭa-dörī, he who wears his hair in matted locks, i.e. Śiva (Śiv. 1895); mukuṭa-dörī, she who wears a diadem, i.e. Pārvatī (Śiv. 1501).
adj. c.g. difficult to get (K. 61); rare, scarce (Gr.M.); difficult to get to, hence difficult to do, almost impossible (of a task) (Śiv. 743, 1003, 1758, K. 202).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. dōryōv), to run (El., Gr.M., K. 434, 1162). dūrⁱ dūrⁱ  freq. part. (for dūri dūri, see dūrᵘ), running running, hence as adv. very quickly, u.w. vbs. of going, etc.
f. the conduct of a dŏrzun (q.v.), wickedness, malice, mischief-making.
f. the nature of a dŏrzun (q.v.), wickedness, maliciousness, a mischief-making nature.
m. (sg. dat. dŏrzanas), a man who is wicked, vile, malicious, a mischief-maker.
f. a kind of candied sugar, usually --˚.

adj. (f. dürᵘ̈ 1, for 2 see s.v.), firm, hard, strong, compact, durable, solid (K.Pr. 88, Śiv. 337, 1777); robust (K.Pr. 243, duruye for doru-y); earnest (El.); manly (El.); strong (of arguments) (Gr.M.); strong, firm, steady, obstinate (in purpose or resolution) (Gr.M.); strong, permanent, immortal (Gr.M., K.Pr. 243); fine (of weather, L. 460). El., L., and K.Pr. spell this dur and durr; K.Pr. 167 spells dürᵘ̈ dar, cf. bukurᵘ. --droṭᵘ -- adj. (f. dürᵘ̈-drüṭᵘ̈), hard and stout, stiff and strong, hard and thick. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become tight or jammed (of a knot or the like); to become stiff, solid, tough (of food which even cooking does not make tender). --karun -- m.inf. to make firm; hence, to exercise patience or perseverance, to take courage, to be firm; to be composed, calm. ¶ dari lagun m.inf. to be suddenly stopped, suddenly caused to halt (of something in motion). Cf. dara lagun, s.v. dara 3. ¶ dȧrⁱ-wôlⁱ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is hard, hard-fisted, one who meanly insists on getting all he can.
m. a single row of a number of people arranged in rows; any particular tribe or caste to which a person belongs, cf. bāca-bạth.

f. (for 1 see dör), the beard (of men) (K.Pr. 9, 156, 168, written dár; Rām. 582, K. 662, 664). --dazüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the beard to burn; met. to experience great annoyance from something happening in one's presence. ¶ dāri-buḍᵘ adj. (only m.), old bearded, a grey-beard, of ripe age (used specially in blessings or the like, e.g. a mother saying 'May I see you a grey-beard'). -chaj m. a fine flowing beard ('shaped like a winnowing sieve'). -chyotᵘ m. a grey-beard, a venerable old man, a respected elder (Rām. 1600). -khᵃʦ m. a long beard. -kôsᵘ adj. (only m.), one whose beard has been shaved off. -lab f. one side of a beard, e.g. the right side, or the upper half. -lôwᵘ m. a long thick beard. -phë̆ʦᵘ̈ f. a small piece of a beard. -wāl m. the hair of the beard. -wôlᵘ m. bearded, possessing a beard. -zyūṭhᵘ adj. (only m.), long-bearded (Gr.Gr. 75).
m. cessation of rain, stoppage of a shower; a temporary cessation in the middle of a shower. --karun -- m.inf. such a temporary cessation of rain to occur.

f. (for 1 see dör), a private or back doorway (Śiv. 340, 949, 958, 1360, 1367); a postern-gate, wicket, sally-port; a window, a casement (H. v. 4, K. 921; El. dãr); a window-shutter (K.Pr. 135, Śiv. 965, 1450). According to El. glass or mica is used in small windows in the houses of the rich. --bar sŏrun -- m.inf. to see to casement and door, to lock up the house for the night. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to shut or lock a casement. Cf. dār 6. ¶ dārĕ bar trọ̆pᵃrȧnᵃ m. pl. inf. to cover casements and doors, to shut tightly all the doors and windows of a house, so as to stop even the circulation of air, for purposes of secrecy. dārĕ trọ̆pᵃrañĕ f. pl. inf. to cover the casements, to close them so tightly as to stop even the circulation of air (Śiv. 1703). ¶ dāri dara dyunᵘ m.inf. to give pulling at the side-door, to cause a person to pull frequently at the side-door; hence, in negotiations for a marriage or the like, the petitioned party to harass the petitioner by delaying to give a definite reply one way or the other. dāri dara lagun m.inf. pulling at the side-door to be experienced; hence, lack of dignity to be experienced by persistent petitions for something even after refusal. dāri drasa lagun m.inf. dragging at the side-door to be experienced, to be put to shame by accusations against or gossip about the members of one's family. Cf. drasa. dāri-kinⁱ adv. (to go out, look, etc.) by or through the window (Gr.M., K.Pr. 254, Rām. 331). dāri-poṭᵘ m. the door of a side-doorway; the window-flap of a casement, the board which closes a window; a window which is closed by a board (El.).

f. a child's doll. Cf. achĕ- dörᵘ̈ under ȧchⁱ. ¶ dāri-dajĕ f.pl. doll-rags; hence, dolls. -dajĕ pöthᵃr m. doll-like conduct, used with reference to the relations of a bride and bridegroom who act foolishly as if (like dolls) they were motionless, and without sense of dignity or shame.
adj. (only m.) bearded, one on whom a beard has grown or is growing, one who has passed boyhood (Gr.Gr. 134). Cf. dārĕl.

f. a wall of stone, earth, or brick (K.Pr. 7, 87, dus; Śiv. 1562). For the method of building an earthen dŏs, see L. 249. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to set up a wall round an open space, garden, or the like. ¶ dŏsa-hoṭᵘ m. a length of mud wall made at one time in a mould. Cf. -yĕndᵃr bel. -ʦôkᵘ m. an encircling wall, a wall surrounding a garden or the like on all four sides; usually not of great height; the support of a wall, a buttress. -ʦọ̆pᵘ m. a small, slight wall round a garden or the like. -yĕndᵃr m. a kind of mould used for making a mud wall. It is composed of two long planks facing each other at a distance fixed by a cross-piece at each end, thus forming a long trough. Into this the mud is forcibly pressed and pounded. Cf. L. 249. -yĕndra-püṭᵘ̈ f. one of the planks forming this trough-mould.
ḍusa adj. c.g. one whose body is bent or awry from disease or the like; met. a lazy fellow who goes about with his shoulders up to his ears, a loafer, a lounger.

or (K. 702, 857) dŏshĕwᵘ̈y card. c.g. (pl. dat. dŏshĕwȧnⁱ, dŏshĕwȧniy or dŏshĕwanī, ag. and abl. dŏshĕwȧyⁱ, see Gr.Gr. 85), an emphatic form of zᵃh, two, meaning 'even the two', 'even both' (Rām. 1409, K. 36, 103, 6317). Cf. dŏnaway (L. dushwai, 458).
n.ag. (f. dŏshĕwüñᵘ̈), that which oozes or trickles; that from which anything oozes or trickles, leaking.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. dọ̆shᵘ 2, for 1 see s.v.), to trickle, drop, leak, ooze; to trickle (of a slight shower of rain) (K.Pr. 220). dọ̆shᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. dö̆shᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (that which has) trickled, oozed, etc.

(for 2 see dŏshun) or doshᵘ 1 m. delay, hindrance, in the commencing of some urgent work; indolence, laziness. Cf. das 1. --bihun -- m.inf., i.q. das bihun. --lagun -- m.inf., i.q. das lagun. --wŏthun -- m.inf., i.q. das wŏthun, for all of which see das 1.
adj. (f. düshᵘ̈ 1), one who works lazily, a 'slacker'.
card. c.g., i.q. dŏshĕway, q.v. and declined similarly, see Gr.Gr. 85.
f. a female servant, a maidservant; a female devotee (Śiv. 1459). Cf. dās.
