m. a wall-builder, a mason, builder, plasterer (Gr.Gr. 142). -bāy f. his wife. -koṭᵘ m. his son. -zang f. a present of money, rice, salt, etc., given (as a good omen) to a mason on the occasion of laying the foundation or of other important stages in the building of a house.
f. a mason's wages, the wages of a plasterer (Gr.Gr. 143).
m. a male friend, a friend (K.Pr. 60; Rām. 843, 1650). --sapadun -- m.inf. to befriend (El.). --thawun -- m.inf. to count as a friend, to favour.

(sg. dat. ḍŏsaris, ag. ḍŏsᵃ̇rᵃ̇), a bowed or bent condition of the body owing to old age, disease, or the like. --aʦun -- m.inf. such a condition to enter; the body to begin to be bowed as one of the first symptoms of old age or disease.
f. the condition, profession, or trade of a mason (Gr.Gr. 142, 143).
in the following: dŏtadŏta gaʦhun m.inf. to be torn or cut into threads (of papers, cloth, etc., eaten by worms, etc.). dŏta dŏta karun m.inf. to reduce to threads, as ab.
adj. c.g. rude, harsh-natured, a misanthrope.

m. (sg. dat. ḍōṭhas, abl. ḍōṭha, but ag. ḍūṭhⁱ), hail (L. 460, dont). ¶ ḍōṭha-cholᵘ m. a violent hail-storm, covering a small tract and lasting only a short time, but very destructive to crops, etc. -cholᵘ hyuhᵘ adj. (f. --hishᵘ̈ --), very hot-tempered, one who flies into a violent storm of abuse (like a sudden hail-storm). -nāv f. a 'hail-boat'; hail lying on the ground after a hail-storm. -pholᵘ m. a single hailstone. -pathᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a great mass or pile of fallen hail, hail that has collected in heaps. -rāṭh f. (sg. dat. -rāṭhi), a 'hail-swarm', a violent hail-storm. ¶ ḍūṭhⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. (fruit or crops) to be destroyed by hail; met. the fruit of any action or labour to be lost on the eve of accomplishment. --karun -- m.inf. to destroy the fruit of any action or labour on the eve of its being accomplished (as ripe crops are destroyed by hail).
m. (sg. dat. dō̃tas), in dō̃ta-dō̃th f. tooth to tooth; wordy warfare (wherein the combatants grind their teeth at each other). Cf. dö̃th.
m. (sg. dat. dö̃tas), ivory (El. dánt). Cf. dō̃th. ¶ dö̃ta-khünḍᵘ̈ f. a piece of ivory.
m. (sg. dat. dötas or daitas), a fabled kind of demon, the daitya of Sanskrit; met. a cruel, hard-hearted man, who is rough and forbidding in appearance and nature. Cf. daity.
m. (sg. dat. dö̃tanas), a piece of wood used as a toothbrush, a teeth-cleaner. dö̃tan-mūrᵘ̈ f. a twig suitable to be used as a tooth-cleaner.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ḍū̃ṭᵘ, 2 p.p. ḍö̃cyōv), to hate, show hatred to (esp. of some powerful monarch hating some subject); to envy (El. ḍánṭún). ḍū̃ṭᵘ-motᵘ (f. ḍũ̄̈ṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), one who has been made the object of hatred.

m. (of an accountant or the like) one who cannot count correctly, one who makes mistakes in the simplest rules of arithmetic, a bad arithmetician. ¶ dȧtⁱ-likha m. incorrect calculation, wrong arithmetic.

m. divine power, destiny, fate, fortune (Śiv. 1475). --phērun -- m.inf. fate to turn, a sudden change from prosperity to the reverse to take place. --wunun -- m.inf. fate to be bad, hard luck to occur, as when one is on the eve of success to be met by failure. ¶ döwa or daiwa wunun m.inf. to have bad luck by fate, i.q. döv wunun, ab.
f. (sg. dat. döwāgüʦᵘ̈), the course of destiny, the will of God, destiny.
or duwanzāh card. c.g. fifty-two (Gr.Gr. 84). ¶ duwanzāhan-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to fifty-two; bought for, costing, or priced at fifty-two (rupees, etc.).

m. a kind of fine cord or twisted thread used for fastening along the ends of a garment (partly for the sake of ornament and partly for strength), binding-cord. Cf. dāv 1. ¶ dövⁱ-dār adj. c.g. (a garment) embroidered with binding-cord. -höshī f. a braid embroidered with binding-cord for use as ab. -kömᵘ̈ f. embroidery with this binding-cord. -kurta m. sufficient of this binding-cord for one garment. -kūṭᵘ̈ f. one branch or sprig of this embroidery. -nāl m. embroidery on the collar of a garment.

f. the second lunar day of a lunar fortnight (Rām. 1767). ¶ dŏyĕ-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to this second day, e.g. the moon of this day (Śiv. 513); (of a work, business, etc.) commenced or occurring on this day.
interj. in bŏ-döy, I, good Sir! (L.V. 67).
card. c.g. eighty-two. ¶ dŏyĕshītan-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), costing eighty-two (rupees, etc.); belonging to eighty-two (persons, etc.).
adj. (f. dŏyĕshītücᵘ̈), born, produced, begun, etc., in the eighty-second year.
m. (sg. dat. dŏyĕtas), duality, twoness; (in religion or philosophy) dualism as opposed to monism, (according to a monist) considering that which is really one to be two.
or dŏyĕtöjih card. e.g. forty-two (El. dótajih, i.e. dôtöjih). ¶ dŏyĕtöjihan-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), costing forty-two (rupees, etc.); belonging to forty-two (persons, etc.).
adj. (f. dŏyĕtöjihicᵘ̈), born, produced, begun, etc., in the forty-second year.
or dŏyĕtöjⁱhyumⁱ ord. (f. dŏyĕtöjihimᵘ̈), forty-second (El. dótãjihyum, i.e. dôtöjihyumᵘ) (Gr.Gr. 78).
card. c.g. thirty-two (El. dótrȧh, i.e. dôtrᵃh) (Rām. 1525). ¶ dŏyĕtrᵃhan-hondᵃ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), costing thirty-two (rupees, etc.); belonging to thirty-two (persons, etc.).
adj. (f. dŏyĕtrᵃhücᵃ), born, produced, begun, etc., in the thirty-second year.
ord. (f. dŏyĕtrᵃ himᵘ̈), thirty-second (El. dótrȧhyum, i.e. dôtrᵃhyumᵃ).
m. circuit, compass; a ring, a circle; a kind of light stoneless finger-ring, worn chiefly by women (El.).

ord. (f. dŏyimᵘ̈), second (K.Pr. f. sg. nom. duyim, 70; YZ. 13; Śiv. 703, 886, 997, 1189; Rām. 180, 324; K. 669, 684); other, another (Rām. 384, 683); (with nouns of time) next, as in döyimi rĕta pata, after next month (Gr.M.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dọ̆yᵘ), to milk (a cow, etc.); to express liquid by a process similar to milking. ¶ dọ̆yᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. dö̆yᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), milked (of milk, or of the udder, or, in the f., of a cow, etc.); milked or squeezed out (of any other liquid expressed by a process similar to milking). ¶ dŏyĕn-nörᵘ̈ f. a kind of earthen pitcher used as a milk-pail. -ʦoḍᵘ m., id., but globular in shape, with a wide mouth. -wörᵘ̈ f. a small kind of pitcher used as a milk-pail.
or ord. (f. ḍöyimᵘ̈), the ord. of ḍāy, q.v., two-and-a-halfth. ḍöyyumᵘ-kan m. the upper part of the cartilage of the ear, which is bored by Brāhman women to receive the thread of an ear-pendant.
m. (sg. dat. dōzakhas دوزخس or dōzakas), Hell (Gr.M., H. 19, 20).

f. (sg. dat. dŏʦhi), a certain position of the hands, with the fingers extended, and the open palms placed side by side and slightly hollowed (as if by a beggar to receive food, and hence used as an indication of supplication); the hand similarly hollowed for drinking (YZ. 163). --ganḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to put the hands in this position; hence, to make a humble supplication. ¶ dŏʦhi dŏʦhi öhī karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. (of a suppliant) to bless a donor in token of gratitude, with the hands placed in this position.
m. the Toon tree, Cedrela toona (El.).
or drē̃chĕr m. hardness, harshness, dryness, esp. of something once soft, such as a fruit, a gourd, a vegetable, or the like. Cf. drỗṭhᵘ (Gr.Gr. 30, 140).
?, drüḍᵘ̈ ?, f.?, hardness, strength; cf. droṭᵘ. drüḍᵘ̈-rostᵘ̈ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), wanting in strength, weak, tender, delicate (K. 1107).
f. the ridge, side, or swell of a mountain, where people rest on their way up. --dŏyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to milk the breast of a mountain; met. to fight a wordy battle, to engage in a war of words.

m. a famine, dearth, high price or scarcity of provisions (K.Pr. 9, 60, 128, 147, 204; YZ. 396). --tulun -- m.inf. to raise a famine, to cause a famine, or to cause provisions to become dear by misgovernment or the like. --wŏthun -- m.inf. a famine, or high price of provisions to arise. ¶ drāga-dāñĕ m. famine-rice, rice high-priced on account of scarcity; met. anything universally necessary which, owing to its scarcity, has become high-priced. -drikh f. (sg. dat. -driki), a famine-leech; a woman wasted away by hunger owing to dearness of provisions. -dĕv m. (f. -dĕviñ), a famine-demon, one who by misgovernment or other means causes provisions to be high-priced. -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), famine-stricken (of a human being or of a country or city). -kuʦurᵘ adj. (f. -kuʦürᵘ̈), a famine-puppy (i.e. one born in a famine season); one who likes or desires a famine or high prices; one who, even in times of plenty, is mean and niggardly in his food expenditure, owing to his having once suffered from famine. -kuʦarĕñ f. a woman who, having once experienced famine, or who, owing to her association with one who has, is niggardly in the distribution of food even in times of plenty. -warihy m. a famine-year, esp. a year which is remembered as one in which a famine has occurred (YZ. 406). - waharukᵘ adj. (f. -waharücᵘ̈), of or belonging to a famine-year; born, produced, or commenced in a famine-year. -wȧrⁱhyukⁱ adj. (f. -wȧrⁱhicⁱ), born, produced, or commenced in a famine-year, esp. in some particularly remembered famine-year. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), suffering from famine or high prices, (a place) where prices rule high. -zad adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -zadiñ), famine-stricken. ¶ drāgukᵘ adj. (f. drāgücᵘ̈), born, produced, or commenced in a time of famine. ¶ drāgas-kyutᵘ adv. in or during a time of famine, u.w. vbs. of becoming, being born, commencing, etc.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. drāgaladiñ), famine-stricken (Gr.Gr. 135).
m. (sg. dat. dragaras), a plot (in or near a rice-field) which, owing to its having long lain fallow, is unfit for sowing or the like.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. drakyōv), to run, esp. to run in order to get over a long distance quickly, to go along at a steady trot.

m. a broker, an agent (K.Pr. 60); a marriage-broker, a go-between who arranges marriages (L. 268); a go-between, pander. (The fem. drölᵘ̈, q.v., means 'a bawd', while drāla-bāy means 'a broker's wife'.) ¶ drāla-bāy f. a broker's wife. -har  f. brokers' quarrelling; sham quarrelling, like that which brokers practise with the sellers in order to deceive their buyer-clients, or vice versa.
f. the conduct of a go-between or broker; conduct like that of a broker.
f. the profession of go-between or a broker, broker.

f. a circular cake of moist cow-dung spread out in the sun to dry for fuel, a cake of cow-dung fuel. ¶ dramba-chal m. a piece of a cake of cow-dung fuel. -nār m. a fire of cow-dung fuel, esp. such a fire as used by goldsmiths for melting the precious metals. --thipañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to pat cow-dung fuel, to prepare the moist cakes of cow-dung fuel for drying; met. (of a person once prosperous, but reduced to poverty) to take to a lowly occupation for a livelihood. --wahārañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to spread out moist cakes of cow-dung to dry; met. to throw filth about in improper places.

m. (sg. dat. dramanas; pl. nom. draman), a kind of grass, bent grass, Panicum dactylon or Cynodon dactylon, the dūb-grass of India, used as a fodder; (El.) the short grass of the field, green grass. --zyonᵘ -- m. dūb-grass to spring up (on a person's grave or at the place where his body was cremated); hence, a long time to have passed since a person's death. ¶ draman bọ̆dᵘ m. a handful of dūb-grass, as much as can be grasped in the hand and plucked from the ground. -bēra f. a boundary-mound between fields or surrounding a field, on which dūb-grass grows plentifully. -boṭhᵘ m. the bank of a river, lake, road, or the like on which dūb-grass grows freely. -kānüjᵘ̈ f. the stalk of dūb-grass, a decoction of which is used as a medicine in fevers, etc. -köñᵘ̈ f. a small quantity of dūb-grass. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -mŏnjĕ), the tangled clump of roots of the dūb- grass. -tulᵘ m. a small quantity of dūb-grass, whether torn up from the ground or not. -ʦakul m. (sg. dat. -ʦakalas), a piece of open ground on which dūb-grass grows freely. -zanḍ m. a pile of rooted-up dūb-grass.
m. (sg. dat. drāmanas), chewing the cud (of ruminants). --karun -- m.inf. to chew the cud; met. to misappropriate property entrusted to one.
f. (sg. dat. drüñᵘ̈), low marshy ground near lakes, covered with thickly grown grass and water-weeds, and engulfing like a quicksand any one who steps upon it.

f. a place where there is a toll-office, the locality of a custom-house, a frontier station. Cf. RT.Tr. II, 399. ¶ dranga-bal m. a frontier toll- house, custom-house, passport office. --pĕñĕ -- f.pl.inf. perturbation or distress of mind to occur when caused by hearing or seeing something causing fear, to be terrified. -rôchᵘ m. a custom-house officer, an examiner of passports.
m. a gang or body of people collected for a sudden robbery or the like.
? gend., N. of a certain fish taken in August and September. It is doubtful if it is a separate species, being more probably a name given to any fry that comes to the net (L. 158).
f. Drās, N. of a town and district in Bāltistān, west of Śrīnagar. See D. 222 ff.
m. pulling at a rope, a cloth, or a like, to detach it from something to which the other end is fixed. Cf. dara 4. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to pull, as ab.

(K. 932; El. m.), drĕshṭī f. (Śiv. 1019), or drĕshṭi f. (Śiv. 1431, K. 230), seeing, viewing, beholding (also with the mental eye) (Śiv. 1061, 1076, 1277, 1492, 1889, K. 932); the sight, the faculty of seeing (Śiv. 1019, 1023); the mind's eye, wisdom, intelligence. ¶ dēha-drashṭ (Śiv. 1545) or -drĕshṭi (Śiv. 1016, 1431, 1796), looking upon the body as one's Self, confounding the Self with the body, religious ignorance. sama-drĕshṭi, f. regarding all things impartially (Śiv. 1853). drĕshṭi-tala adv. visibly, before one's eyes (Śiv. 1621, 1623).
in drāsi drāsidinⁱ m. pl. inf. to pour forth a torrent of reproaches or abuse.
adj. c.g. manifest, visible, evident (El.), i.q. drĕshṭānth, q.v.

f. (sg. dat. drüʦᵘ̈), urging or obstinacy shown by another to one who is performing any action he does not like; (pl.) the diseases and other accidents of childhood (Rām. 1586). --nakha wālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to pay such urging, i.e. when doing anything against one's will, to carry it through somehow or other at as little expenditure of trouble, etc., as possible.

or drĕṭha-pö̃ʦukh m. (sg. dat. -pö̃ʦakas) (in Hindū ritual), the period of five lunar asterisms, commencing with the second half of Dhaniṣṭhā, and the whole of Śatabhiṣaj, Pūrvabhādrapāda, Uttarabhādrapāda, and Rēvatī, during which it is forbidden to collect earth, wood, or grass.

or drĕṭhāyĕkh m. (sg. dat. draṭhāyĕkas), a certain kind of demon said to have his dwelling in cemeteries, to have the power of moving about invisibly, but able to show himself in some terrible human form, and on dark nights to haunt cross-roads and wild places (K.Pr. 55).
f. N. of the wife of the five Pāṇḍavas, the heroes of the Sanskrit epic the Mahābhārata. Sg. dat. draupadiyĕ (Śiv. 996, 1329; K. 1017, 1067).
m. a thing, substance, object; in pl. goods and chattels, property, wealth, goods, money (K. 644).
f. a certain medicinal plant growing on the shores of lakes, whose juice is used for eye-diseases. Cf. drēkh.
(El. drekh), m. (sg. dat. drēkas), Pistachia integerrima (El.). ? i.q. drē̃ka-türᵘ̈, q.v.
m.(sg. dat. drĕshtāntas), an example, allegory, instance, exemplification. --hāwun -- m.inf. to show clearly, make evident (Rām. 133, 1707).
m. N. of a celebrated king, father of Duryōdhana (see Duryōdan). He was blind (K. 539, 543, 1035).

m. (sg. dat. drē̃ṭhas), the faculty of eyesight (El.). --āmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), become visible (of something very minute, which one is by some means enabled to see, or of something visible to most people, but which owing to weak sight is generally invisible to some person, and which he is now able to see). --wasun -- m.inf. (of something visible), to become suddenly invisible (owing to failure of sight, illusion, or the like). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to become visible, as in --āmotᵘ ab.; to be seen (Śiv. 104, 180, K. 159, 193, 411, 434, 436-9). This is used as the pass. of ḍēshun, to see, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 169). --yiwawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --yiwawüñᵘ̈ --), that which becomes visible; visible, that which can be seen by everyone.
adj. c.g. visible, that which can be seen by anyone.
m. (f. drē̃ṭhawüñᵘ̈), that which can be seen by anyone, openly visible, in sight.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. drã̄ṭhyōv or drē̃ṭhyōv), to become hard. drā̃ṭhyō-motᵘ or drē̃ṭhyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. drā̃ṭhyē-müʦᵘ̈ or drē̃˚), become hard (of something formerly soft, e.g. a fruit, or a young sapling).
f. (sg. dat. drihi), contraction of the brows, a frown. --ladüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to frown.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. drihaladiñ), a frowner, one who frowns, frowning.

f. a husband's younger brother's wife; a term of address used between wives of two or more brothers. ¶ drikākañĕ-bọ̆dᵘ m. behaviour like that of the wives of two brothers to each other, mutual quarrelling or dislike between two women. -tônᵘ m. the mutual relationship between a younger brother's wife and an elder brother's wife.
m. a marmot, Arctomys hemachalanus (El. and L. 117).

f. a kind of grass or creeper, described as long, thin, and soft, but nevertheless tough. -hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -hishᵘ̈), like drina, hence of some edible vegetable tough even after being cooked, too tough to chew.

f. a vow, oath (Śiv. 119, 647, 974); especially a mutual oath, a solemn obligation, or a solemn asseveration made by one person to another (K.Pr. 70). --āsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an oath to be, an oath to exist, an oath to bind a person, to swear (El.). --hāwüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make a solemn asseveration in order to convince another, to call God, one's guru, or the like to witness (K. 812); El. also gives --karüñᵘ̈ -- and --khë̆ñᵘ̈ -- with the same meaning. ¶ driyĕ-dĕgul m. (sg. dat. dĕgalas), a vow-basin, i.e. that by which an oath is taken, e.g. when a father swears by his son's head. Cf. K.Pr. 70.

f. (so reported, but m. in the following phrase), a certain plant growing amidst dūb- grass (Panicum dactylon) and described as having thin circular leaves, prob. i.q. drab of L. 72, Polygonum sp., which is eaten boiled with milk. ¶ drŏbas wasun m.inf. to eat unwholesome diet when an invalid; to eat forbidden food (of one who is performing a fast); to lead a dissolute life.
or drö̃jⁱ drö̃jⁱ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to continually and angrily scold a child, a servant, a wife, or other member of a family.
(also spelt drugun) conj. 3 (2 p.p. drŏgyōv), to become dear, to be raised greatly in price, esp. of something usually cheap. drŏgyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. drŏgyē-müʦᵘ̈), become dear, as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. drọ̆gᵃrôwᵃ), to raise the price of anything, to cause something usually cheap to become high-priced (e.g. by misgovernment, or by cornering the market). drọ̆gᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. drọ̆gᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ or drọ̆jᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), raised in price, as ab.

adj. (f. drö̆jᵘ̈), dear, high-priced (K.Pr. 204); expensive, precious, valuable (Śiv. 1284); (of a quality, action, or conduct) rare. ¶ drŏgi bāzạra adv. from a dear market, at a high price, for a great price. --bāzạrukᵘ -- adj. (f. --bāzạrücᵘ̈ --), bought for a great price. --mŏla -- adv. at a high price, for a great price. --mŏlukᵘ -- adj. (f. --mŏlücᵘ̈ --), high-priced, costing much, very dear.

m. a certain kind of grass (Sorghum halepense). It is regarded as poisonous till it comes into flower, but its poisonous properties then depart and it is one of the best cattle fodders (L. 71, durháma), i.q. drŏhāma.
m. dearness, scarcity, famine (of something usually cheap and easy to get) (Gr.Gr. 140).
m. a Ḍōm, a man of unclean, vile caste, esp. one employed as a spy or messenger. ¶ drö̃jⁱ-bāpār m. conduct like that of a vile Ḍōm. -bāy f. a Ḍōm's wife.
indrö̃jⁱ drö̃jⁱ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf., i.q. drö̃ch drö̃ch karüñᵘ̈, q.v.
f. the profession or conduct of a vile Ḍōm or spy; vile conduct generally.
m. (sg. dat. drŏkas), in the following: drŏka-drŏkh f. mutual romping, skipping and dancing, gambols (for gender see Gr.Gr. 75).

f. (sg. dat. drŏki), vomiting, sickness, squeamishness (El.). --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring on or cause vomiting. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an attack of vomiting to come on. ¶ drŏka diñĕ f. pl. inf. to give vomits; met. to utter foul abuse (of one who feels himself superior in rank to the abused). --mārañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to bring vomits into action; met. to boast of oneself, in order by so doing to put another to shame.
or drukun conj. 1 (1 p.p. drọ̆kᵘ or drukᵘ; 2 p.p. drŏcyōv or drucyōv), to play, sport, gambol. drŏkⁱ drŏkⁱ yunᵘ m.inf. to come playing playing; hence, (of children) to play till one is weary.

adj. c.g. poor, needy, poverty-stricken, unfortunate (K. 1090, 1154). -küṭᵘ̈ f. the daughter of a poor man; a poverty-stricken girl or (sometimes) woman. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a poor man's son; a poverty-stricken boy; a son of misfortune, one miserably poor (K.Pr. 189).
f. conduct like that of one who is poverty-stricken, whether really so or not.
f. a bawd, a female pimp.
f. commission paid to a broker, brokerage. --khë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to earn or receive brokerage.

or droshᵘ adj. (f. drö̆shᵘ̈ or drüshᵘ̈), the reverse of an epicure, one who will eat cooked vegetables not cleared of their stalks, etc., or who pays no heed to flavour and will eat unpalatable food, a fellow who will eat anything or do anything without reflecting. Cf. drọ̆sᵘ.

or drosᵘ adj. (f. drö̆sᵘ̈ or drüsᵘ̈) (of cooked vegetables or the like), dirty, turbid, mixed up with stalks, leaves, etc., and hence unpalatable, not cleared; as subst. m., cooked vegetables of this description. Cf. drọ̆shᵘ.
or drū̃ṭhᵘ adj. (f. sg. nom. drö̃ṭhᵘ̈, dat. drã̄chĕ), become hard, hardened (of something, such as a fruit, a sprouting branch, or the like, formerly soft); (of personality) hard, rough, audacious.
adj. (f. nom. drüṭᵘ̈, dat. dracĕ), strong, tough, not easily broken. Cf. dorᵘ 1 and draḍ.

m. a kind of sickle (K.Pr. 61, 146; Śiv. 1532). Cf. dröʦᵘ̈. --aʦun -- m.inf. the sickle to enter, reaping to commence. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to apply the sickle; met. to cut off any family or business, to destroy, wipe off the face of the earth. --lagun -- m.inf. to be utterly cut off as ab. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause the sickle to enter, to commence reaping. ¶ drötⁱ-dan m. the handle of a sickle. --lāgȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to apply sickles, to brand a person with a red-hot sickle (formerly a common punishment); met. to make a person squirm under abuse. -nāṭa f. (carving) flesh with a sickle; met. (in carving meat) to hack and hew, neglecting the joints; similarly, to cut fruit, etc., wrongly, or to cut cloth, etc., wrongly.
m. smeared over with, fouled all over with, used --˚, after some word signifying dirt, mud, or the like.
f. a kind of small sickle for cutting grass or the like. Cf. drôtᵘ. ¶ drāʦi-dan m. the handle of such a sickle. -ṭŏkh dyunᵘ m.inf. to interrupt another speaker by the sudden use of abusive language.
f. a large elevated light, a torch, beacon.

m. the sound caused by anything falling from a height into water, splash, plop. ¶ druba-gāḍa f.pl. 'splash-fish', a certain kind of fish-soup, the broth made by boiling gobbets of the flesh of fish in a great deal of water. The lumps of fish thrown for boiling into this water make a splash. --wāyun -- m.inf. to propel a boat in a certain fashion, rowing in a wind, the oars being thrown up in the air and coming splash into the water.
or drǖ̃khᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a withered old woman, a hobbling old hag.
m. the skin of men or animals (El. drúl). See drūrᵘ.

or dryūrᵘ 1 m. (sg. dat. drīris, abl. drēri), the skin of men or animals, hide. (El. has drúl, for drūlᵘ.) --wālun -- m.inf. to skin, to flay; met. to skin a person alive with abuse, to put to shame by foul abuse. --wasun -- m.inf. to be skinned, to be flayed; met. to be skinned alive by abuse, to be put to shame by foul abuse.

or dryūrᵘ (cf. dyūrᵘ) m. (sg. dat. drīris, abl. drēri), glue (made by boiling down skin, etc.); the gum, resin, or resinous pitch that exudes from the bark of certain trees after incision. ¶ drīrⁱ püṭᵘ̈ f. a pitch plaster, a glue plaster, used for uniting broken limbs, healing open sores, splicing wood, etc.

(? = درست) adj. (f. drustᵘ̈), entire, full, complete in all its parts (Śiv. 1428); certain, correct (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to make correct, rectify (Gr.M.). ¶ drustĕ wati adv. all the way, during the whole journey (Gr.M.). --röʦᵘ̈ -- adv. all night (Gr.M.). ¶ drustis dŏhas adv. all day (Gr.M.). --rātas -- adv. all night (Gr.M.).
adj. (f. drusᵘ̈), entire, full, complete in all its parts. Cf. drustᵘ.
adj. (f. sg. nom. drǖ̃ṭhᵘ̈, dat. drũ̄̈chĕ), i.q. drỗṭhᵘ, q.v.
m. N. of a famous Hindū saint who became the polar star, and who is hence often referred to as a symbol for unmovability. druva-rāz m., id. (Śiv. 858).
m. a woman's husband's younger brother, a brother-in-law younger than one's husband (Gr.Gr. 133).

or drikh f. (sg. dat. drᵃki or driki), a leech (El. darak and drik; K.Pr. 15, with suff. of indef. art. drakah, for drᵃkhāh; L. 157, 461). ¶ drᵃka-(or drika-)gorᵘ (or) m. a leech-seller (El.). -gürᵘ̈ f. a female leech-seller. -gȧrⁱ-bāy f. a male leech-seller's wife. --lāgañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to apply leeches. --pĕñĕ-- f. pl. inf. leeches to fall or be applied; met. to be distraught from grief (as if leeches were sucking away one's life- blood). -ʦopᵘ m. the mark of a leech-bite. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a leech-applier (El.).
card. two, used for zᵃh (q.v.) in various phrases, such as dū-pahar, midday (K.Pr. 176); dū-zang, two-legged (ib. 61); har-dū, both (ib. 235).
m. N. of a village about 14 miles south of Śrīnagar, once an important town, but now reduced. ¶ dǖrukᵘ adj. (f. dǖrücᵘ̈), of or belonging to the village of Dṻr.
m. (cf. W. 18), a prayer, a supplication (to God); an invocation of good, a blessing; an imprecation, curse, malediction = bad-duā, see bad.

or dubᵘ (Gr.Gr. 17) m. onomat. the noise of falling, crash, bang, esp. the noise of anything falling from a height on to a roof or the like. -dub m. a knock, e.g. a knock or tap on a door or on the trap-door of a cellar to indicate a person's presence. ¶ duba-dujⁱ 1 or -dujᵘ̈ 1 f. a knock or tap as ab.

adj. c.g. fallen upside down (of a jar or other vessel). -dujⁱ 2 or -dujᵘ̈ 2 adv. upside down. --phērun -- m.inf. to be turned upside down (e.g. a vessel or the like). --phirun -- m.inf. to turn a vessel upside down so as to empty it completely. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall upside down (esp. of a vessel full of something).

m. utter destruction (of a house, field, or the like, destroyed by an earthquake, inundation, war, or the like). Cf. ḍubᵘ. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such utter destruction to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to cause such utter destruction, esp. of the destruction caused by an invading or conquering army.

adv. for the second time, twice, again (Śiv. 1644, 1897, Rām. 204, 426). In Śiv. 1326 this word is altered to dubāla(y), for the sake of rhyme. --wuchun -- m.inf. to see again, look at again, revise (a written composition) (Gr.M.).
f. the noise of the beating of the heart, etc., under the influence of fear or the like. Cf. dubᵃrahāray.

adj. (f. dubürᵘ̈), two-doored; hence, (of a road or the like) admitting only two passengers at a time; (of a house) possessing two doors. ¶ dubari-shāh m. resting on two sides; inability to make up one's mind, 'sitting on a fence.' -shāh rōzun m.inf. one person to build his hope on two alternatives; to depend upon two alternatives, e.g. a house with two doors. -shāh thawun m.inf. to give two persons (unknown to each other) hope for something suitable for only one person.
adj. (f. duböʦᵘ̈), having two relations; hence, anything produced or utilized by two people, or suited for two people, e.g. a house, an occupation, a bed for a married couple, or the like.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ḍubyōv), to dive; to sink, drown, be drowned; to drown oneself; to be immersed, be submerged, inundated; to be destroyed, ruined; to be immersed in sin, to be a great sinner. ḍubyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ḍubyē-müʦᵘ̈), sunk, submerged, immersed, under water; drowned in sin, a great sinner.
f. a repeated knocking at a door, cf. dub-dub under dub; thumping or loud beating of the heart from fear or the like. Cf. dubarāray.
m. a sound (Gr.Gr. 17), probably i.q. and merely another spelling of dub.
m. wasting away, destruction (like something plunged in water and dissolved). Cf. ḍuba-ḍās.
m. a meeting of two persons, esp. when unexpected.
m. a two, anything consisting of two, a pair, a double. -nyāy m. an unfair division, giving an unfair share of a thing (e.g. food or cloth) which should be divided equally, i.q. duk-nyāy, see dukh 2.
f. a two (in a pack of playing-cards).
(? spelling) in dūd-phras, m. the Himalayan poplar, Populus ciliata (El.). The word is probably the same as dŏda-phrasth under dŏd, q.v.
m. one who is in the habit of coming as an uninvited guest to a feast, etc. (? the same as the duda of El., which he translates 'invitation').
f. the habit or practice of attending feasts or dinner-parties uninvited.
m. dandelion, Taraxacum officinale (El.). ? i.q. dŏdijᵘ̈.
adv. twice a day (of eating, drinking, or the like).
adj. c.g. stout and strong (of anything animate or inanimate).
adj. c.g. two-handed, having two hands (Ram. 1351).
m. the name of the letter ḍa, used in schools. Cf. ḍakaḍö.

adj. (f. dudȧjⁱ or dudüjᵘ̈), only twice pounded, of paddy, etc., which has been pounded once to remove the husk, and only once again pounded to make it perfectly clean. Most grain is pounded three times; met. hail (from its resemblance to coarsely pounded grain) (Śiv. 1243).
adj. (f. dudünjᵘ̈ or duḍȧnjⁱ), occurring twice a day (of eating, drinking, or the like).
f. the habit or custom of attending a feast though not invited. Cf. ḍuḍa.

f. a dive (into deep water), esp. of a skilled diver. Cf. ḍung. ḍū̃gadiñĕ f. pl. inf. to give dives, to dive and as soon as one returns to the surface to dive and dive again. ¶ ḍū̃gi phirun m.inf. to dip anything deep into any liquid, as if one were causing it to dive; met. to cause one to dive deep into liquor, to cause him to drink deeply. --phērun -- m.inf. to drink deeply, as ab.

or ḍũ̄̈ga m. a kind of covered boat for passengers with their baggage and servants, and in which the passengers also live (Śiv. 1488, 1683); a ferry-boat (Gr.M.); ḍũ̄̈ga is the boatmen's pronunciation. For an account of this boat see L. 381 (dúnga); ḍū̃gas kĕth, in a boat (Śiv. 1780). -rᵃkh f. (sg. dat. -rᵃkhi), the mark on the boat. A man is supposed to drop a cooking-vessel overboard, and to make a mark on the side of the boat where it fell over. Then, when the boat arrives at its destination and the pot is sought for, he points out the mark and says, "here is where it fell overboard, let us dive here for it." Hence, any useless mark made by a fool. -hönzᵘ̈ m. (his wife is -hānzañ), a boatman of a ḍū̃ga.
or dugāla m. a kind of double-bladed mattock, one blade above and the other below, on the principle of the spikes of a pickaxe.
f. worry or harassment by having to do two things (esp. two incompatible things) at the same time. ¶ dugā̃gȧlⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. such worry to occur.
adj. c.g. one skilled in diving, one accustomed to dive, a diver.
adj. (f. dugö̆bᵘ), of double weight, very heavy, stouter than necessary (usually of ornaments, such as bracelets or the like).
adj. (f. dugübᵘ̈), with two sprouts (of a sprouting seed).
m. multiple sight, a disease of the eyes which apparently multiplies the object observed two or more times (Śiv. 1756.) --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such a disease to occur.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. dugöshⁱladiñ), suffering from multiple vision.
m. a kind of bag with two compartments.
m. (sg. dat. ḍugaras), a Ḍōgrā, a man of the Ḍōgrā tribe, which occupies a high position in the Jammū territory (K.Pr. 255).
ord. (f. duhatimᵘ̈), two-hundredth. Two hundred is zᵃh hath (Gr.Gr. 80).
adj. (f. duhatiñᵘ̈), of the value of, or costing, two hundred (rupees or the like).
adj. (f. duhöriñᵘ̈), worth two cowries; hence, of very little value, worthless.
adj., only f., pregnant; as subst. a pregnant female (human or other).

f. (sg. dat. dōja for dōjĕ, see j), the blackboard used as a slate for teaching writing in schools. The ink used is a kind of whiting. ¶ dōja-mṻnthᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the religious ceremony performed when, at an auspicious moment, a child is given its first lesson in writing on one of these boards. -püṭᵘ̈ f., i.q. dūjᵘ̈.

or dȧjⁱ f. (for 1 see dọ̆jᵘ), a small square plot of ground, such as a seed-bed; the plastered square piece of floor (Hindī caukā) arranged for eating or religious worship; the preparation of such a plastered square; a small square piece of cloth, a handkerchief, a towel; a patch of cloth; a rag, a piece of rag; a bandage (El., who spells the word daij, daj, dȧj, and daṅj). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to prepare the plastered square as ab. --lāgüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to apply a patch, to patch a torn garment, etc.; to patch a person's words, to explain or give sense to something unintelligible said by another person, by supplying missing words or the like. --ʦānüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause a patch to enter, to patch a torn garment, etc. ¶ dajĕ-bāgay f. to divide a field into long, narrow seed-beds or the like. -hurᵘ m. a bundle of rags, used for plastering the ground as ab. -hurᵘ̈ f. a bundle of rags, esp. when they are fastened together. -kĕth düjᵘ̈ f. a handkerchief tied up so as to contain money or the like, a bundle made by tying up something in a handkerchief. -lọ̆ʦhᵘ m. a bundle of rags tied together, as in a swab or mop-head. -lŏʦhᵘ̈rᵘ̈  f. id. -phī˜ṭun m. (sg. dat. -phī˜ṭanas), a small towel for drying the hands; any small piece of rag. -phī̃tunᵘ m. a small piece of cloth, a very small handkerchief. -rĕl f. a long strip of rag, a bandage (El. dajiryel, m.). -rē̃ṭun m. a piece of old torn rag for wiping the hands, etc. -shikhürᵘ̈ f. id. -sörᵘ̈ f. rag-collecting; stealing grain from a heap and carrying it away in filled handkerchiefs. -tᵃr f. a strip of rag, a bandage (El. dajitur, m.). -züṭᵘ̈ f. a worn-out piece of rag for wiping the hands, etc.
(cf. دوک) f. one of the row of sticks planted in the ground on which the warp is set previous to putting it in the loom. The sar of India.
adj. c.g. (of cloth) become loosely woven, esp. of a spot of looseness of fabric in a cloth which is elsewhere tightly woven, threadbare. Cf. dukh 1.

f. (sg. dat. duküjᵘ̈ or dukȧjⁱ), doubt, hesitation. ¶ dukȧjⁱ gōmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), fallen into hesitation, become doubtful. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go into doubt, to fall into doubt, to begin to hesitate.
adj. c.g. having the threads thinned or loosened (of good cloth battered and spoiled by the washerman), washed threadbare. See dukh 1.
adj. c.g. stout-limbed, strong and powerful.
m. a poker or stick for stirring a fire.

f. (sg. dat. duki, pl. nom. duka), local thinness or looseness in the fabric of a piece of cloth otherwise strong and unworn, threadbareness. ¶ duka f.pl. patches of thinness, general looseness or threadbareness in the fabric of a piece of cloth, even when new. --gaʦhañĕ -- f. pl. inf. such looseness to occur, esp. the threadbareness or disorganization of a woollen cloth caused by careless washing.

f. (sg. dat. duki), a pair, used --˚ to signify a few of anything (e.g. rice), a little. ¶ duk-nyāy m. division into two unequal parts, unfair halving; i.q. ducĕ-nyāy, see ducĕ. ¶ duka nyāy m. favouritism, e.g. in a company of which the members are all of equal honour, to show favouritism by being more polite, etc., to one's own friends, and less to the friends of others. -vēri adv. two at a time, in twins; u.w. vbs. of bringing forth, etc. -vīrᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -vēri), a twin birth, a birth at which two children are born together. ¶ duki duki adv. by twos and twos; hence, little by little, u.w. vbs. signifying to eat, give, or the like.
m. a certain throw of the dice in the game of caupar or nard, in which two dice each show the number 1, a double one, 'aces' (Śiv. 280).
or dukhamyulᵘ adj. (f. dukhambilᵘ̈ or dukhamilᵘ̈), two-pronged, forked.
adj. c.g. broken or cut in two (e.g. a fruit, or a grain of rice when being pounded).
adj. (f. dukhörᵘ̈), measuring or containing 2 khārs or kharwārs. A khār or kharwār is a dry measure containing 16 trakhs of about 4 3/4 sērs (El.). Cf. dukhāryunᵘ.
adj.(f. dukhrüpᵘ̈), bored with holes in two places, or in the same place above and below.
adj. (f. dukhrövᵘ̈), lit. two-pattened; hence, in weaving cloth or the like, having the woof stretched by holding it under wooden pattens worn on the two feet.
adj. (f. dukhūrᵘ̈), two shoes, each belonging to a different pair (u.w. reference to words for shoes, etc., which are masculine).
f., i.q. dukhūrᵘ, q.v., but u.w. reference to words for shoes, etc., which are feminine.
f. a second breakfast, luncheon; the hour at which such a second meal is eaten. Cf. dukôlᵘ, aḍ-kôjᵘ s.v. aḍ, and kôlᵘ.
m. the act of eating twice in one day (lit. having two breakfasts). Cf. duköjᵘ̈ and kôlᵘ.
adj. (f. duköñᵘ̈), one-eyed with two (eyes), i.e. squinting so badly that one can only see with one eye at a time.
f. scissors (El. dúkãr; L. 463 dakúr). --wāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cut cloth, etc., with scissors.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. duköshⁱladiñ), one who fasts for two complete days.
m. a certain musical instrument, described as consisting of linked rings fixed to a staff. Cf. dahara.
m. a pair, a couple, esp. of two similar things (Rām. 966).

m. rolling (Śiv. 1015); a rolling stone, a large globular rock or stone, such as rolls down in avalanches, etc. --gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), gone a-rolling; met. (of a man, a fruit, or the like) rolled down or fallen from a height; (of a business, etc.) uprooted and cast down. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go a-rolling, to roll (El.); met. (of a man, a fruit, or the like) to roll down or fall from a height; (of a business, etc.) to be thrown down, destroyed. --karun -- m.inf. to set a-rolling, to roll or cast down from a height; (of a business, etc.) to destroy. --trāwun -- m.inf. to be in a position to be easily knocked or rolled down; met. (of a thing or business) to be sure ultimately to be cast down and destroyed, to be in a hazardous position; after a long delay to be on the point of happening, to be hovering on the brink. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to roll or knock down from a height; met. (of a business nearing completion) to knock down by opposition. ¶ ḍulan dyunᵘ m.inf. to give rollings, to cause to roll, to roll (tr.) (El.).

m. rolling the body on the ground; lying at ease upon the ground, lolling. Cf. ḍulungᵘ. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. or ḍulagᵃ̇nᵃ̇ dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to roll on the ground (Śiv. 535); to lie face downwards on the ground, to rest, to loll (K.Pr. 54); (of a business, esp. when some opposing influence has disappeared) to revive. --trāwun -- m.inf. to throw oneself down upon the ground (e.g. in sorrow) (Rām. 1537); to delay work already commenced (from laziness or unwillingness, etc.).
or ḍulāmĕr m. globularity, rotundity, sphericity.

or (Śiv. 324) ḍulawun conj. 1 (1 p.p. ḍulanôwᵘ or ḍulowᵘ), to roll a thing from one place to another, esp. something too heavy to lift; to roll (a heavy stone or the like) away from a place (e.g. the stone rolled away from the Holy Sepulchre); to roll something down from a height, to hurl down (Śiv. 324). ¶ ḍulanôwᵘ-motᵘ or ḍulowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ḍulanöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ or ḍulüwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), rolled along or away.
adj. c.g. having two branches, forked (e.g. a tree, a creeper, an ornament, a string, etc.).
m. the condition of having two crooked shanks, bandiness, bowleggedness.

m. a kick with the two hind legs of a horse; met. an interruption, impediment, suddenly occurring to anyone engaged in some occupation. --bihun -- m.inf. such a kick to be settled on one; hence, to be suddenly much obstructed, suffer great and sudden obstruction. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to suddenly obstruct as ab. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. an obstruction as ab. to occur.
n.ag. (f. ḍulawüñᵘ̈), that which is easily rolled, rollable.
f. the act of rolling. Cf. ganḍa-ḍulay under ganḍ.
or ḍulijᵘ̈ f. a kind of bowl, usually of earthenware, used for eating, wide at the top and narrower at the bottom. This word is f. of ḍulᵘ 1, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 36).
f. a kind of litter for one person, borne by two men, used principally by women. Cf. ḍūlᵘ 1.
m. on the point of rolling; met. (of an action or business) in a critical position, that of which the success is in doubt.
adj. (f. dulünḍᵘ̈), having both the shanks crooked, bandy-legged, bow-legged.
adj. (f. dulünjᵘ̈), (of a human being) having the shanks of double length, long-shanked; having both shanks crooked, bandy-legged, bow-legged; (of a tree) having two trunks, having a forked trunk.
m. a kind of bird like a crane, with long legs.
adj. (f. dulürᵘ̈), possessing two strands (of a necklace, rope, thread, or the like).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. ḍulyōv; El. gives a perf. part. ḍulᵘ-motᵘ, for which I can find no other authority), to roll (e.g. of a large globular rock, a tree-trunk, or the like) (El.).
m. rolling oneself on the ground, lying at ease upon the ground, lolling. Cf. ḍulagunᵘ.
m. (sg. dat. ḍulanis), the act of rolling. dulȧnⁱ dinⁱ, m. pl. inf. to give rollings, to roll oneself about (H. xii, 23).
f. a procuress, a bawd; f. of dala 3, q.v.

m. a kind of large earthen or metal vessel in which one can bathe (El.), or in which a large quantity of rice or the like can be washed before cooking (K.Pr. 147, 237). The f. of this word, in a dim. sense, is ḍulijⁱ, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 36). --parmūzun -- m.inf. to wipe out the pot; esp. on the festival of the Śivarātri (commencing on the 11th of the dark half of the month of Phāgun = Feb.-March) ceremonially to empty into a lake or river the contents of a large cooking pot as an offering to the village tutelary deity (kṣētrapāla). ¶ ḍulⁱ barȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to fill the pots, to perform the Hindū rite of ceremonially touching a vessel containing fragrant objects, preparatory to offering them to the village tutelary deities Vaṭukanātha and other Bhairavas (see börav). The rite is performed by both right- and left-handed Śāktas on the five days and nights commencing with the 11th of the dark half of the month of Phāgun. -pröpyunᵘ m. the offerings to the deity of boiled rice, cakes, etc., made on the above ceremony of the Śivarātri, portions of which are given to the spiritual preceptor and to the officiating priest. --pūzun -- m.inf. to perform the above worship on the five days and nights commencing with the 11th day of the dark half of Phāgun. Cf. hērath.
m. a kind of litter or sedan chair (El., who writes the word dúl). Cf. ḍūlⁱ.

m. rolling, in the following (cf. ḍulun): ḍulⁱ- brörᵘ̈ f. sending on a fool's errand, as when a meeting is mutually arranged and wrong directions are given by one of the parties to the other. -brörᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to be deceived by an imaginary disappearance, as when the master of a house sees thieves coming into it and, because they have hidden in some place near him, imagines that they have gone away. -brörᵘ̈ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to send on a fool's errand, e.g. when two persons are dispatched on some work and one misleads the other by sending him off to imaginary secret meetings.
(1 p.p. of ḍōlun, q.v.), adj. (f. ḍūjᵘ̈, f.pl. ḍōjĕ), that which is left unused; hence, deserted, abandoned (as an orphan or the like) (Gr. Gr. 18).
f. (sg. dat. ḍōlĕ), a litter, a kind of sedan (esp. for respectable women), a 'dooley' (K. 1007). Cf. ḍūlikⁱ and ḍūlᵘ 1.

f. in the following (cf. dōl): ḍūlⁱ diñᵘ̈ f.inf. to impede one work for the benefit of another work by giving false information or spreading false reports or the like. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show hostility to any work by delaying its successful completion. --wanüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give false intelligence in order to impede the accomplishment of another's work.
? spelling, m. a cowherd, shepherd, cotton-carder (El.). ? cf. ḍūmb.

m. (sg. dat. dumaṭhas), a large kind of memorial building with an echo inside, a dome, a vault (El. ḍumuṭ); a boundary pillar (usually of brick, whitewashed). "These dumaṭhs are very big conical stones, and, according to the Paṇḍits, as old as the Pāṇḍavas. They are supposed to be the petrified bodies of wicked men, whom some good people in olden times cursed because they were troubled by them, and so they became stones" (K.Pr. 61).

or (K.Pr. 116) ḍūm m. (a ḍūmb woman and a ḍūmb's wife are both called ḍūmbiñ), a man of a certain low caste, in India called a Ḍōm; an informer, policeman, night watchman of a village (El.). Ḍūmbs are plucky fellows, and carry letters at night through the jungle and over desolate hill and plain (K.Pr. 61). -ḍagur m. Ḍōm and menial, Ḍōms and their kin, a jingle from ḍūmb; a collection of low-caste people, thieves, etc. Cf. ḍagur. ¶ ḍūmba dĕgulᵘ m. a large kind of earthenware pot, in which a great number of articles are tightly squeezed together for cooking. Cf. ḍūmba-lĕjⁱ and -lyolᵘ bel. -kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a large, heavy kind of brazier or 'kāngrī'. -küṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kacĕ), a Ḍōm's daughter. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a Ḍōm's son. -lĕjⁱ or-lë̆jᵘ̈ f. i.q. ḍumba dĕgulᵘ, as ab. but of medium size. -lyolᵘ m. (sg. dat. lĕlis), i.q. ḍūmba dĕgulᵘ ab.
or (El.) duma m. the tail of an animal.
f. conduct of a Ḍōm; conduct like that of a Ḍōm, mean and disreputable conduct.
f. conduct of a Ḍōm; conduct like that of a Ḍōm, mean and disreputable conduct.
f. the profession or duties of a Ḍōm, such being a village watchman, a policeman, an informer, letter-carrier, etc.
m. noise, bustle, tumult, uproar; celebrity, display, parade, pomp, ado.
m. goods, etc., collected to do honour to an expected guest, ornaments collected to present to the bride, bridegroom, or their friends in preparation for a wedding, or similar collections.
m. a kettledrum or similar instrument (K.Pr. 61, 70); the noise made by such. Cf. ḍam-ḍam. ḍum-ḍum wāyĕnwôlᵘ n.ag. a drummer, a town-crier (El.).
or dumbijᵘ̈ (H. xi, 9) (= دمچی) f. the tail of an animal; a crupper (El. dúmij).
adj. c.g. (of any work or business) trembling in the balance of success or failure.
adj. (f. dumösiñᵘ̈), two months old (u.w. ref. to things with or without life).
adj. (f. dumösᵘ̈), lasting for two months, two months old (u.w. reference to things without life).
m. smoke-coloured, N. of the elephant-god Gaṇēśa (Gȧnⁱsh or Ganēsh) (Śiv. 14).
f. a certain nominal coin, the sixteenth part of an ānā, the damṛī of India.
m. a leaf platter for serving food or the like.
m. a thick coarse kind of rope made up of twisted withes or of twisted strands of thread.
adj. (f. dunamatiñᵘ̈), of the value of ninety-two (rupees, etc.), worth ninety-two, costing ninety-two.
m. the name of the Śāradā and Nāgarī letter, used in schools.

f. (sg. dat. danjĕ; the abl. is properly danji, but usually written danjĕ), condition, state (K.Pr. 62); nature, temperament, constitution, habit of body; temper, humour, disposition (mizāj); natural behaviour, habit, conduct according to one's own nature, inborn habits, disposition. Cf. ḍanja and ḍünḍᵘ̈ 1. --āsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. one's nature to exist, acting according to one's nature to occur, nature to assert herself. ¶ danjĕ-kun wuchun m.inf. to look towards the condition, to calculate resources, to see if one has sufficient means for any proposed course of action. --rūdᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --rūzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), restored to good health or good condition (after sickness or the like). --rōzun -- m.inf. to be restored to good health or sound condition (after sickness or the like); to continue in good health (YZ. 72).
f. (sg. dat. ḍanjĕ), a habit, practice, disposition (esp. a bad habit). Cf. dünḍᵘ̈ 1. --āsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a (bad) habit to exist; met. bad luck to occur resulting in misery and want.
. A variant form of ḍünḍᵘ̈ 1 appears in wŏphar-ḍünjᵘ̈, p. 1131a, l. 42. The word ḍünjᵘ̈ is evidently a back-formation from ḍanjĕ, the sg. dat. of ḍünḍᵘ̈.
f. the beam of a pair of scales, esp. of a small light pair. Cf. ḍünḍᵘ̈ 2.
f. (sg. dat. ḍanjĕ), the beam of a pair of scales. Cf. dünḍᵘ̈ 2.
f. diving, plunging below the surface into deep water. Cf. ḍū̃g. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to dive, plunge into water.
adj. c.g. a diver; one who dives much, a good diver.
f. the profession of a cotton- or wool-carder.
m. the name of the figure 2, used in schools.
adj. (f. dunövᵘ̈), two-named, known by two different names, possessing an alias.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. dūnᵘ), to sweep (El.). dūnawôlᵘ n.ag. (f. dūnawājĕñ), a sweeper (El.).

f. (for 2 see dondᵘ), the minute grains or rice-dust distributed through husked rice; the fine wires hanging down from an ear-ornament or the like, on which minute beads are threaded. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to clean (by winnowing) such minute grains from husked rice. -kala m. the small minute ends or tips of the rice-grains, broken off in the process of husking. -mŏkta m. minute seed-pearls threaded on the ab. wires.
dūnʦhᵘ, dūnʦhᵃr, etc., see dū̃ʦh, dū̃ʦhᵘ, dū̃ʦhᵃr, etc.

m. (sg. abl. ḍōni), a walnut (the fruit), Juglans regia (El., L. 73, 79, 80, 348, 352, K.Pr. 229, qq.v. for full details regarding the tree and fruit; K.Pr. 236; Śiv. 1023, 1571; with suff. of indef. art. ḍōnāh, Śiv. 1015, 1774). phŏka-dūnᵘ m. a puff-walnut, hence a bubble (Śiv. 1774, 1775). -dach f. walnut grape, a particular kind of grape (W. 114; El. dun-dach). ¶ dūnⁱ-dĕl m. the thin skin of the kernel of a walnut. -gūjⁱ or -gūjᵘ̈ f. one of the four quarters of a walnut kernel (cf. -gūlᵘ bel.). -gŏl or -gŏlur f. the outer rind of a walnut, outside the shell. -gūlᵘ m. an entire walnut kernel (consisting of all the four parts, cf. -gūjⁱ ab.). -gŏlur m. see -gŏl ab. -hüṭᵘ̈ f. the wood of the walnut-tree, walnut wood, valued for making furniture, etc. -kulᵘ m. a walnut-tree (K.Pr. 60, written ḍōni˚). -künḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kanjĕ), a half walnut shell; a whole walnut shell. -lünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -lanjĕ), a small branch of a walnut-tree, usually full of fruit, and hence used metaphorically as an expression for extreme fruitfulness. -lang m. the trunk or main branch of a walnut-tree. -murra f. the walnut catkin, used as a vegetable for cooking (L. 347). -pīr  f. a walnut shell. -tīl m walnut oil (L. 353). -zyunᵘ m. walnut wood used for burning, firewood of walnut.
f. a piece of goat's flesh, esp. a long strip cut off from the upper part of the leg.

m. a quarter less than one, three-quarters (W. 105); a quarter less than any specified number (W. 105), as in dūnᵘ hath, a quarter less than a hundred, seventy-five; dūnᵘ trĕh, a quarter less than three, two and three-quarters (El.); dūnᵘ zᵃh, one and three-quarters. dūnᵘ-sôdᵘ m. three-quarters and one and a quarter; met. considering the total cost of any proposed work, calculating the pros and cons of any proposed course of action, as if one were to say "is it a quarter less than one (twenty-five per cent loss) or a quarter more than one (twenty-five per cent profit)?" dūnᵘ-sôdᵘ bōzun m.inf. to calculate the pros and cons of any proposed course of action.

f. the smoke-fire over which a Hindū ascetic sits for lengthened periods inhaling the smoke by way of a religious exercise (Śiv. 305). --dazüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a smoke-fire to burn; met. continual worry or sorrow to be experienced, owing to the continual presence or neighbourhood of some irritating cause.
m. (sg. dat. dūnis, abl. dōni), a cotton-carder, a man whose profession it is to card cotton, wool, or the like. Cf. dōna 2. ¶ dūnⁱ-wān m. a cotton-carder's place of business.

f. (sg. dat. dōñĕ), a bow (El. dúnuí); esp. the bow used by a cotton-carder. He twangs its string against the uncleaned cotton or wool, thus cleaning it (Gr.Gr. 121); met. in Rām-bạdᵃrüñᵃ dūñᵘ̈ f. the bow of Rām Bạdᵃr (= Rāmacandra), a rainbow (cf. L. 463). Cf. dūnᵘ 2. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to card (cotton, etc.); met. to toss aside in all directions a mass of articles, esp. in the hope of finding and getting hold of some particular thing hidden amongst them. ¶ dōñĕ-phamb m. cotton which has been carded.

f. noise, outcry heard in the distance. --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to raise an angry noise or angry tumult heard in the distance, as when made by children out of sight of their parents, or raised by the masters and mistresses of a house against the conduct of a servant not present. --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a noise or outcry to occur.

duniyāh (Rām. 1074, 1103), dunyā دنیا m. (sg. dat. dunⁱyāhas or dunyāhas دنیاہس), the world (El.); the present world, the present life or state of existence (K.Pr. 62); the world, as opposed to a religious life (K.Pr. 27); the people of the world, people; worldly enjoyments or blessings, worldly goods, the good things of this life, wealth, riches (K.Pr. 62). dunyāhas yunᵘ m.inf. to come into the world, be born (K.Pr. 242).

or (Śiv. 1799) duniyāh-dār adj. c.g. (as subst., f. dunⁱyādārĕñ), worldly, a person of the world; one possessed of the good things of this world, a rich man, a mammonist; (in Kāshmīrī) one who supports his relations by showing hospitality or giving material help on the occasion of festivals or the like (Śiv. 1799). -bāy f. the wife of such a rich man.

f. worldliness, attention to the concerns of the world; worldly affairs, economy; mammon, worldly goods or possessions, riches; wife and children, family; a show of politeness; (in Kāshmīrī) the virtue of helping one's poor relations by showing hospitality or giving material help on the occasion of festivals, etc. (Śiv. 1509).

m. incense, frankincense, a fragrant-burning gum (Siv. 1856); a certain wild plant, i.q. dᵃpa, q.v. -dag or -dŏg m. the pounding of the dupa- or dᵃpa-plant; met. the thorough pounding of any substance (ef. Śiv. 1856). -ganḍᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the root of the dupa- or dᵃpa-plant. -löṭᵘ̈ f. a long stick of incense for burning, a candle of incense-gum. -zuvᵘ̈rᵘ̈ -ज़ुव॒॑रू॒ । धूपाधारिका f. a censer.
m. a kind of cloth or mantle in which there are two breadths. Cf. dupᵃṭa.

m. lit. two watches (a day being divided into four watches of about three hours each); hence, midday (Gr.Gr. 157; Gr.M.). ¶ dupaharan adv. at midday (Gr.Gr. 157). -bögⁱ or -bögin adv. at about midday, at midday or thereabouts. --tāmath -- adv. till midday (Gr.M.). ¶ dupaharas adv. at midday (Gr.M.). -bögⁱ or -bögin adv. at about midday, at midday or thereabouts.
or adj. (f. dupaliñᵘ̈), i.q. dupolᵘ, q.v.
m. a heavy iron-headed hammer; an iron mallet, a sledgehammer.
m. (sg. dat. dūpas), incense. Cf. dᵃpa, dupa, and dᵃph. dūpa- dīph m. incense and lamps (used in worship) (Śiv. 1175, 1523, 1692, K. 1046).
adj. c.g. two-bladed, two-edged (e.g. a mattock or a knife).
adj. c.g. split lengthways into two pieces (of a log, a post, firewood, or the like).
adj. (f. duphüjᵘ̈), (of a field) bearing two crops (spring and autumn); (of a tree, etc.) bearing two different kinds of fruit on different branches.
adj. (f. dupüchᵘ̈ 1; for 2 see dupokhᵘ), of or belonging to two lunar fortnights; born, produced, or made two lunar fortnights ago.
adj. (f. dupŏhᵃr), two-cornered, two-pointed, two-peaked, forked.

adj. (f. dupüchᵘ̈ 2; for 1 see dupochᵘ), having two sides or wings; (of a bird) two-winged; (of a wheeled vehicle) two-wheeled; of or belonging to both parties (e.g. a feast to which a man invites both his own and his wife's relations).

adj. (f. dupüjᵘ̈), weighing 2 pals of about one-tenth of a pound each, weighing (approximately) 3 ounces; composed of materials weighing 3 ounces (e.g. a turban, in the making of which 3 ounces of thread were used up); hence, of such an article, very fine, very delicate and light.
adj.(f. dupatürᵘ̈), possessing two leaves, two-leaved (e.g. a seed-sprout just showing two leaves).
adj. (f. dupūrᵘ̈), having two layers or strata; having two sections, one above the other (e.g. an ear-pendant); two-storied (of a house).

or dupaṭa m. 'having two breadths', a kind of light muslin wrapper or cotton shawl (El.), usually with embroidered edges, worn by men, loosely thrown over the shoulders (Śiv. 1725, K. 976, both with suff. of indef. art. dupaṭāh), and used by women as a head-covering and veil. Cf. dupacĕl.
m. a pearl. dur-fishān درّفشاں adj. c.g. pearl-scattering (YZ. 6, of the mouth scattering words like pearls). Cf. dūr 2.

adj. c.g. distant, remote, far, i.q. dūrᵘ, q.v. -pahān adj. c.g. somewhat distant, moderately distant (Gr.Gr. 94). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go far away, to go to a distance (Śiv. 279); to become at a distance, to find oneself far away (Śiv. 328). --pĕṭh -- adv. after a long time.

m. a pearl (El.); an earring or ear pendant, esp. one with a single pearl set in it and worn on the lobe of the ear (H. vii, 11). So kana-dūr, ear-pearl (YZ. 448). Cf. dur. ¶ dūra-horᵘ m. a pair of such pendants, one for each ear (Gr.Gr. 81). -hȧrⁱ kan m. a single one of such a pair of ear pendants. -hȧrⁱ rĕkh f. (sg. dat. -hȧrⁱ rĕkhi), a small broken or chipped ear pendant. -kan m. a single ear pendant. -kanüjᵘ̈ f. the bent or hooked wire which passes through the lobe of the ear and supports such a pendant. -pholᵘ m. a handsome ear pendant, set with precious stones and crystal, and suspended by a golden wire (Rām. 1040). -ʦākh m. (sg. dat. -ʦāki), a double set of ear pendants, two for each ear.
(? ḍūr), the border round the bottom of a phēran, or long dress like a nightgown worn by Kāshmīrīs (El.). Cf. ḍūrᵘ̈.
an irrigated field, vegetable land (L. 460). Cf. dōr 5, ḍōr, and ḍūrᵘ.

m. a scourge made of twisted thongs, with which offenders are punished. --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to scourge as above. -raz f. a kind of whip, consisting of a rope made up of twigs and twisted bark, used by gardeners to keep birds off fruit-trees, etc. Its crack is very loud, i.q. kura, q.v. --ta kura wazȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. play the tunes of the whip and of the scourge to crack of the whip all round, as in clearing a space at a palace gate or the like. -ṭās m. the crack of the dura-raz or kura, see ab. --wazȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to make the whip sound, to give a criminal a flogging. --wazanāwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to ply the whip all round one, esp. of one acting with cruelty.
adj. c.g. far-sighted, far-seeing, keen, discerning; provident, foreseeing, sagacious (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. of two colours; of two kinds, of two forms.
adj. c.g. possessing two flavours (e.g. sweet and sour at the same time).
m. farness, distance (of space, time, relationship, etc.); separation (from a beloved) (Śiv. 157, K. 407, 479); cyônᵘ dūrĕr, separation from thee (YZ. 47, 142, Śiv. 271).
m. a kind of thick woollen blanket, used as a bed-covering in cold weather.
adj. (f. durȧnjⁱ or durünjᵘ̈), of two colours, two-coloured.
adj. (f. durüsᵘ̈), possessing two flavours (e.g. sweet and sour at the same time).
adj. (f. durüṭᵘ̈), twice as heavy, weighing twice as much (as something else).
adj. in durukha-māth دورخہ مات (in chess) checkmate by both rooks (Rām. 1316).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. dūryōv), to be distant, to become distant (of place or time). duryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. duryē-müʦᵘ̈), become distant, having reached a distant land; (that which has) happened a long time ago.
N. of one of the principal combatants in the war of the Mahābhārata, often used as a symbol of a cruel wicked man (Śiv. 996, 1329, 1372; K. 534, 539, 540, 693, 1068).
f. the actions or conduct of a male actor who dresses as a female. See dạrz 1. Used in the following: --khārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to paint one's face and otherwise get oneself up like such an actor.

or dūr دور adj. (f. dūrᵘ̈ 1; for 2 see s.v.), distant, remote, far, at a distance, a long way off (of place or time, cf. dūr 1) (K.Pr. 25, 81, 203, 207, 239; YZ. 36; Śiv. has dūrᵘ, 1063, 1834, and dūr, 106, 443, 636, etc.); (of a road) long; bö̆zᵘ̈-nishĕ dūrᵘ, beyond the intellect, incomprehensible (Gr.M.); so hōshĕ dūr (YZ. 219). --dūrᵘ hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to break off mutual visiting, to break off intimacy. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to put at a distance, cease to have connexion or intercourse (with) (of a business or a person). --karun -- m.inf. to put far away, keep at a distance; to put away or aside (K.Pr. 56); to expel (El.). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain apart (from any person, business, or the like) (Śiv. 106, 878). ¶ dūrⁱ-gāth m. (sg. dat. -gātas), the fault of being distant (e.g. of a village which has the disadvantage of being too far away). ¶ dūri adv. at a distance (El. dūrē, K.Pr. 62, 156, H. vii, 18). dūri dūri adv. (for dūrⁱ dūrⁱ see dōrun), at a great distance. -pĕṭh adv. at a distance (El.). ¶ durĕn gaʦᵃn or --güʦᵘ̈n -- adv. by distant goings, (a work, etc., accomplished) by means of long journeys. ¶ dūryukᵘ adj. (f. dūricᵘ̈), begotten or made at a distance, born or existing a long way off or a long time ago; --safar دور یک سفر m. a journey of distance, a long journey (Gr.M.).
m. (pl. dat. ḍūrĕn, Gr.Gr. 56), a garden-bed, a flower-bed, a parterre (Śiv. 1028; K.Pr. 47, dat. ḍaurih, translated 'field'). Cf. dōr 5, ḍōr, and dūr 5.

f. (sg.dat. ḍūrĕ Gr.M.), a string, twine; braid, esp. silken braid, a ribbon; the string of a pair of drawers, a breeches' string (Gr.Gr. 20); a bale of cotton (Gr.M.). Cf. ḍōra. ¶ ḍūrⁱ-dolⁱ m. a coat of which the edge of the skirt is ornamented with braid or cord. -dār adj. c.g. braided (of a garment having its edges ornamented with silk braid). -kār m. silk embroidery on alwand or plain pashmīna cloth (L. 377). See alwand.

f. (for 1 see dūrᵘ; sg. dat. dūrĕ, not dōre), a narrow lane between houses, an alley (Gr.Gr. 20, 62, K.Pr. 114, Rām. 1720); a street without shops (El.). ¶ dōri-golᵘ m. the narrow, contracted throat or entrance of such a lane; met. a very narrow lane itself. -phēra m. wandering about through lanes, losing one's way in a city's lanes.
f. (for 1 see dorᵘ 1), pulling, dragging, usually --˚, as in kana-dürᵘ̈, pulling by the ear. Cf. dara 4.

m. a present of clothes, jewels, etc., given by her father's people to the mother of a son or daughter on the occasion of the worship of the Mother goddess which takes place on the day before the child's wedding, initiation, or similar solemn occasion. -dāy f. the servant woman who brings and offers this present. --khārun -- m.inf. to offer this present. -mahönyuvᵘ m. the male servant who carries this present from the house of the mother's father. -prās m. the fourth part of the above present, which, according to custom, is returned to the giver. -wājĕñe f.pl. the women relations who escort this gift from the house of the mother's father.

m.(pl. dat. ḍṻsan, Gr.Gr. 51), a stout club, a cudgel, such as that carried by door-keepers. This is the word used in Śrīnagar (El., K.Pr. 206, ḍēs, 253, ḍus). Cf. ḍã̄g. Met. a clumsy fool, one who does nothing but sit and eat. --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to give clubs; hence, (of a body of soldiers or the like) to attack and cudgel a crowd. ¶ ḍṻsa-dab m. a blow from a club.
adj. (f. dusatatiñᵘ̈), worth, or costing, seventy-two (rupees or the like).

m. (sg. dat. dūshĕs, but pl. dat. dōshĕn), a fault, vice, crime (Śiv. 1724, 1814); deficiency, imperfection; an error, mistake (Gr.M.). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to find fault with, make objections (against = pĕṭh (Gr.M.). --khārun -- m.inf. to find fault with, to bring a charge, make an accusation against a person. --ladun -- m.inf. to make an accusation against a person, to find fault with anything. ¶ dūshĕ-hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), faulty. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), faultless. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), faulty, either by nature or by becoming imperfect. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), full of faults.
m. a kind of shawl, in which there are two breadths, and worn loosely over the shoulders, a wrapper. In Kashmīr they are usually made of the fine wool of the Central Asian goat (Śiv. 793, 1326).
adj. c.g. full of faults, faulty, sinful (Śiv. 1738).
adj. c.g. having two conditions, doubtful, trembling in the balance (of success or the reverse). ¶ dushĕrtas-pĕṭh adv. in doubt, hesitatingly.
or dŏyĕshīth card. (pl. dat. dushītan), eighty-two.
adj. (f. dushītiñᵘ̈), worth, or costing, eighty-two (rupees, etc.).
m. an enemy, rival (K.Pr. 47, 60, 142; YZ. 24; Rām. 37, 385, etc.); the enemy (in a campaign) (Gr.M.).
f. enmity, hostility, resistance, discord (El.); enmity, spite (Gr.M.). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to oppose, hate, resist (El.).
m. (sg. dat. dushmanatas), i.q. dushmanī, q.v. (Rām. 1437).
adj. c.g. corrupted, depraved; corrupt, vicious, bad, evil; a miscreant, vile wretch (Rām. 808, voc. dushṭa).
f. (for 1 see doshᵘ 2), a small scrap of vegetable or the like.
f., i.q. dashā, q.v. sankaṭā- düshᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -dashĕ), N. of a certain ill-omened conjunction (Yōginī) of the stars, in Sanskrit Saṁkaṭā-daśā (Śiv. 482).
f. a weight (of iron, etc.) of two seers, for weighing that amount in a pair of scales.
f. a kind of pickaxe, a mattock with two blades, each pointed at the end.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. dusyōv. This verb is also spelt ḍŏsun, e.g. in Gr.Gr. xxxii), to be bent (of the body), to be hunch- backed; to be unable to rise from one's seat (e.g. from chill, or owing to having eaten too much). ḍusyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ḍusyēmüʦᵘ̈), bent, bowed, become unable to rise from one's seat.
adj. [sg. dat. dusīris, abl. dusēri; f. sg. nom. dusīrᵘ̈ 2 (for 1 see s.v.) ], weighing two seers, of the weight of two seers, each equal to about two English pounds.
adj. c.g. cut in two parts, (of a log or the like) split in two. Cf. duṭakh.

or ḍuṭakh m.pl. (pl. dat. du(ḍu)ṭakan ), cutting (something tall) half-way up, so as to divide it into two parts. duṭakh karȧnⁱ or ḍuṭakh karȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to make two parts; esp. (of something lofty) to break in two so as to knock down the upper part (e.g. a broken column). Cf. duṭaka.
adj. c.g. (of cloth, etc.) woven with doubled thread.
adj. c.g. giving a bang (ṭās) or explosive sound twice from a single cause (e.g. both barrels of a gun going off together from pulling the trigger only once).
f. a garment made of two breadths of cloth. Cf. chiṭh.
m. (sg. dat. dṻtas; pl. dat. dṻtan), a messenger; a messenger of God, or of a god, an angel (Gr.M.).
f. persistent petitioning, begging till the request is granted. --trāwüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to beg persistently as ab. --trövith bĕhun -- m.inf. to besiege a person with such persistent petitioning.
f. the profession or business of a messenger.
adj. (f. dutöcᵘ̈), possessing two door frames (cf. tākh); (a house, etc.) provided with two doors for each story.
adj. (f. duṭüpᵘ̈;), of or belonging to both sides or parties, e.g. duṭopᵘ sāl, an invitation (to a wedding) from both sides (i.e. both from the bridegroom's people and from the bride's people).
adj. (f. dutöpᵘ̈), twice put in the sun, twice spread out in the sun to dry (of damp grain or the like).
adj. (f. dutöshᵘ̈), in two layers, folded in two.
f. (sg. dat. dutriki), N. of the sign used for the letter ra when subscript to and following another consonant in the Śāradā character.
(for 2 see dutrôkᵘ), a stone or other article weighing two trakh (of 9 1/2 lb. each), used as a weight in a pair of scales.
adj. (f. dutrücᵘ̈), weighing, or of the weight of, two trakh (of 9 1/2 lb. each).
adj. (f. dutröcᵘ̈ 2, for 1 see s.v.), i.q. dutrokᵘ, q.v.
f. a loin-cloth, a dhōtī, with suff. of indef. art. dōtyāh (K. 973).

or ḍuvᵘ m. sweeping away; hence, utter destruction, total disappearance (Gr.Gr. 124). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to carry entirely away another's property, to loot out and out. --karun -- m.inf. utterly to destroy (e.g. the supplies, etc., of an enemy's army which has been defeated); to carry entirely away as booty, to loot out and out. --lagun -- m.inf. sweeping away to occur; (of any collected property) to be destroyed utterly. ¶ ḍuwan-phash m. sweeping, clearing away dust, etc.
f. distinguishing between two; hence, distinguishing in the honour to be shown respectively to a number of honourable persons, deciding as to the relative precedence of such persons.
f. a sweeping brush, a broom (Gr.Gr. 120).
adj. c.g. of two, composed, etc., of two; marked with the number 2; subst. m. the two or deuce (at cards, dice, etc.).
adv. at two times, twice (a day, etc.).
adj. (f. duwarishᵘ̈), of or belonging to two years; two years old; lasting for two years; occurring every two years (Gr.Gr. 75).
adj. (f. duwȧchⁱ or duwüchᵘ̈), of or belonging to two times, occurring twice (a day, etc.).
adj. (f. duwöpᵘ̈), (of a field, etc.) twice sown, i.e. either with two different crops in the same year, or sown a second time with the same seed owing to the first sowing having failed.
adj. (f. duwörishiñᵘ̈), of the age of two years, two years old.
adj. (f. duwörᵘ̈), wrapped or lapped round with two strings or with a string consisting of two strands (of an ornament, a girded rope, or the like).
m. a place where two roads join a main road, a place where a road forks.
adj. (f. duwöṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. duwācĕ), having two joints, joined in two places.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ḍuwᵘ), to sweep (dust) away, to sweep (a floor) clean (Rām. 582); met. to sweep clean, carry off the total of someone else's possession, to rob and clean out. ¶ ḍuwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ḍuwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), swept clean (of a floor); swept clean, utterly robbed of everything; carried off, plundered (of property). ¶ ḍuwith ʦhunun m.inf. to sweep something away (Gr.M.). ¶ ḍuwan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. ḍuwan-wājĕñ), one who sweeps, a sweeper; esp. a man of the Wātul caste, who earns his living as a Mihtar or sweeper (K.Pr. 231).

f. duality; the considering anything which is essentially one to be two; dualism, the assertion of two principles, or the existence of the human soul as separate from the Supreme Being, opp. to monism (Śiv. 336, 513, 554, etc.; Rām. 10, 178, 179, 1499); hostility, mutual opposition. --bōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to consider as distinct two persons who should be looked upon as equal, to treat two such persons with different degrees of favour, to show partiality to one of two persons with equal claims. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make a distinction between two things which are exactly the same (e.g. the two eyes in the same head), or between two similar things, beings, actions, etc. --karith diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to breed disunion between two people who mutually love each other.
m. one who sews, used --˚, as in jālakh- dūz, q.v.
m. the place where two branches of a tree (Rām. 603), or the roots of two fingers, meet and from which they start.
adj.(f. duzünjᵘ̈), two-legged (esp. of human beings, but also of birds, etc.), biped.
m. having two sources of strength, having twofold resources.
adj.(duzuvᵘ̈), having two lives or two bodies; met. very able-bodied, very powerful or strong (of a man, a horse, etc.).
adj. (f. duzë̆vᵘ̈), two-tongued, double-tongued; false, insincere of speech; self-contradictory, one who intentionally makes contradictory statements.

or dū̃ʦhᵘ̈ f. (pl. nom. dō̃ʦha), separating out, pulling out (e.g. wool, etc.), sorting out. Cf. atha-dū̃ʦh, and Gr.Gr. 127. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to search for anything hidden in a mass of other articles, to hunt for anything lost amongst rubbish, to "look for a needle in a bundle of straw". ¶ dō̃ʦha kaḍañĕ f. pl. inf. to separate anything out into its component parts, to open out; to explain a book section by section.
f. the act of separating out, sorting out, opening out wool, etc. Cf. dū̃ʦh and aḍ- dū̃ʦhari, s.v. aḍ.
f. (sg. dat. dū̃ʦhᵃrüñᵃ), separating out, sorting out, sifting out; opening out matted cotton-wool or the like.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. dū̃ʦhᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. dū̃ʦhᵃrun, q.v. dū̃ʦhᵃ- rôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. dū̃ʦhᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. dū̃ʦhᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, see dū̃ʦhᵃrun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dū̃ʦhᵒrᵒ), to separate out, sort out a collected mass, so as to collect what is rubbish and throw it away; to open out matted cotton-wool or the like. The verbal noun is dū̃ʦh (Gr.Gr. 127). dū̃ʦhᵒrᵒ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. dū̃ʦhᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), sorted out, as ab.; opened out, as ab.
m. a kind of wild honey-bee. dö̃ʦhⁱ-sondⁱ or dǖ̃ʦhⁱ-sondⁱ adj. (f. -sünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to such a bee (e.g. its honey, or its hive).
m. N. of a pargana about 10 miles to the west of Śrīnagar (RT.Tr. ii, 476) dö̃ʦhyukᵘ or dǖ̃ʦhyukᵘ adj. (f. dö̃ʦhicᵘ̈ or dǖ̃ʦhicᵘ̈), of, belonging to, produced in, or existing in this pargana.
m. a fire-place or kitchen range with two openings in the top to receive the cooking vessels.

m. (sg. dat. duʦĕtis), having a twofold impression in the mind, mistaking one thing for another (e.g. a rope for a snake, and so on); (in religion) the error of seeing two when there is only one, dualism, as opposed to monism (Śiv. 1756, also with the meaning of losing one's way). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to mistake one thing, action, or course of conduct for another, to be deceived. --karun -- m.inf. to cause another to make such a mistake, to deceive, cheat. --mēlun -- m.inf. such a mistake or such a confusion of ideas to occur (e.g. a rope for a snake, a mirage for water, a false track for a path, an enemy for a friend, and so on).

m. onomat. the cry of a cow, 'moo!'; the imitation of this cry by a human being. --karun -- m.inf. to utter 'moo!', to moo (as when one utters it when defeated in a gambling match or quarrel, or when one denies the possession of property entrusted to one), to utter a grunt of dissatisfaction or denial.
m. (sg. dat. dwādashāntas), 'the twelfth end.' dwādashānta-manḍal m. in Yōga philosophy, the circuit called the dwādashānth, a name given to the brahmarandr, q.v. s.v. brahm (Śiv. 1656).
f. the twelfth lunar day of either fortnight of the Hindū luni-solar month (cf. L. 265, shrāwun dvādashī).
m. the third of the four yŏg (Skt. yuga) or ages of the world. -yŏg (K. 12) or dwāpara-yŏg (K. 606) m., id.

m. a door, gate, passage, entrance (Śiv. 688, 829, 955, 972, 1033, 1099, 1473, 1911, esp. 1074-82; K. 71, 73, 79, 1123, 1161, etc.); an opening or aperture in the human body (of which there are nine, viz. the mouth, the two ears, the two eyes, the two nostrils, and the organs of excretion and generation; but according to others there are ten, made up by counting the windpipe and gullet separately; cf. dashĕmōddār) (Śiv. 340, 520, 1078, 1469). ¶ dwāra-köñᵘ̈ f. the wood collected for building the framework of a house; the entire wooden framework of a house below the attics, including door-posts, etc. See köñᵘ̈ 4. -pūz or -pūzā f. the worship of the inferior deities at the entrance to a temple; met. the propitiation of the underlings hanging round the entrance to a royal court or the like by one who desires to obtain an audience; (on the occasion of marriages, etc.) the ceremony of worshipping the god of the threshold (Śiv. 1073, 1074, 1097).

f. N. of the capital of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) (on the western point of the modern Gujarāt, and supposed to have become submerged by the sea) (Śiv. 865, 949, 1330, 1469; K. 589, 592, 593, 632, etc.). -nāth m. Lord of Dwārakā, N. of Kṛṣṇa (Śiv. 1409).
m. hatred, dislike, repugnance, enmity (Śiv. 1048, 1312, 1558, 1755). ¶ dwēshĕ-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), free from hatred, incapable of hate, amicable, loving (Śiv. 587).
f. a small side door, a shutter. Cf. dörᵘ̈ 3.

m. [with a suff. of indef. art. dyānāh (Śiv. 1165, 1726)], meditation, contemplation (esp. profound religious contemplation) (Śiv. 24, 107, 165, etc.; K. 11, 202, 379, etc.); attention, regard, advertency; consideration, reflection (Gr.M.); mental representation of the personal attributes of the divinity to whom worship may happen to be addressed (Rām. 1769, 1775); the object of meditation (Śiv. 1418); (in Kashmīr) a pictured representation of a god or venerated human being (such as a spiritual preceptor, parent, etc.), used as an object of contemplation. dyānaki dyānō, O thou that art the object meditated upon in religious meditation (Śiv. 1418). -dāranā f. meditation and concentration of the mind (joined with suppression of breath) (very common in Śiv., e.g. 279, 1484). --darun 1 -- m.inf. to meditate, concentrate the mind upon God (Śiv. 161, 520). --darun 2 -- m.inf. meditation to be maintained without distraction (Śiv. 1752). --dārun -- m.inf. to apply the mind to contemplation; to concentrate the mind on the attributes of a deity the object of worship, to perform religious meditation (Śiv. 1, 62, 132, 156, 198, 228, etc.); to pay attention or regard (to), to observe, notice. dyāna-dāranāyĕ dyān dārān, contemplating (the deity) with meditation and concentration (Śiv. 307). --dāranāwun -- m.inf. to cause a person to meditate (Śiv. 451). --karun -- m.inf. to contemplate, meditate (on), give thought or attention (to), to think over; esp. to meditate profoundly on past experiences. --rōzun -- m.inf. meditation to remain; the mind to be concentrated on some object, in spite of distractions, and even when busied on other work. --thawun -- m.inf. to keep meditation, to concentrate the attention on some object in spite of distractions and even when busied on other work. ¶ dyāna-pūzā f. worship carried out by means of contemplation (Śiv. 1178). -sŏran m. calling to mind in meditation (Śiv. 155, 983, K. 112). -warukh m. (sg. dat. -warakas), a paper on which is painted a pictorial representation of a god or venerated person, and which is used as an object of contemplation. -yōg m. profound meditation (Śiv. 1028).
f. conscience, honesty, probity, piety, virtue (Rām. 1240).

m. (when used alone this word is generally plural) money, coined money, cash (K.Pr. 8, 33, 153, 188; YZ. 120, 245; K. 478); monetary wealth (Śiv. 59, 365, 952, 1079, 1092, 1819; Rām. 1240; K. 123, 945, etc.). [This word is a corruption of the Sanskrit dīnnāra, which itself is the same as the Latin denarius. The word therefore in the plural means literally denarii; hence, coined money. Cf. RT.Tr. II, 308 ff.] -dana m. wealth consisting in money, wealth, possessions. -vyār m.pl. (a rhyming jingle of dyār) money and the like, money, etc., the various things which together constitute wealth (Gr.Gr. 95). ¶ dyāra-bôgᵘ m. a share of wealth after it has been divided out. -bāgay f. division of wealth, sharing out a common fund or store. -böjⁱbaṭh f. (sg. dat. -böjⁱbaṭi), joint wealth, a common fund or store of money. -böjᵃran f. (sg. dat. -böjᵃrüñᵃ), division into shares of a common fund. -bọ̆kᵘ m. a handful of money, as much as can be received in the hollowed palm with the fingers extended. -chalin-wôñᵘ m. water in which copper money has been washed, used as an emetic in cases of poisoning or the like. -dādi adv. with the pain caused by the love of money, see the following. -dôdᵘ m. 'the pain of wealth', the pain inevitably associated with the love of money, the pain endured in the process of gaining or losing money or in working hard to gain it, auri sacra fames. -daham f. 'the money tenth'; N. of the tenth lunar day of the dark half of the month of Phāgun (in Sanskrit Phālguna = February-March) on which a father-in-law expends money lavishly in the purchase of presents to be sent to the bride, his daughter-in-law, in honour of the Śivarātri festival commencing on the following day. -danḍ m. compensation paid in money for any loss or damage caused by the payer; a money fine. -dunḍ m. free expenditure of money for any purpose. --ḍēr -- m. a heap of money, plenty of money (K.Pr. 137). -har  f. a quarrel about money, a struggle for the possession of any specific sum of money; reckless expenditure of money for any specific object (as if bullets of silver and gold were being fired in a battle). -kāḍay f. extravagant wasteful expenditure, expending much money to gain a little. -kŏla m. a flow of money (either as income or expenditure), money flowing like that in the stream of a canal. -karawôñᵘ m. money-juice; karawôñᵘ is water boiled with or without herbs and given as a drink to allay the thirst of fever; here money is represented as being drunk in this way to allay thirst; hence, spending money on necessaries of life when they are very dear, like our 'eating solid gold'. -kạtᵃra m. a small stock of stored money, esp. when secret, a 'nest-egg'. -kö̆ʦhᵘ̈ f. a kind of money-purse carried under the armpit; met. so much money as would go into such a purse, a purseful. -mad m. arrogance due to the possession of riches. -mŏṭh f. (sg. dat. -mŏṭhi), a fistful of money. -shĕr  m. intense unsatisfied longing for money. -sōr m. (f. -sūriñ), one who is secretly rich, but putting on the outward seeming of poverty, a miser. -sösyunᵘ m. 'a cash thousander'; a sösyunᵘ is a monetary term meaning the value of a thousand cowries, a hundred of which are considered to be equivalent to the pice (paisā) of British India.
