A 'cash thousander' is therefore ten pice in coined money, not in cowries. Cf. RT.Tr. ii, 312. -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), abounding in money, full of money, rich (of a person, a house, a treasury, a business, etc.). -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a rich man, a millionaire, Dives (Gr.Gr. 136, K.Pr. 62, W. 118). -wan m. a great quantity of money. Cf. ban and wan. -wôñᵘ  m. money- water = dyāra-karawôñᵘ, ab. ¶ dyarav-bāgī adv. in exchange for money.

in the following: dyārath-nŏsh f. the daughter-in-law of a husband's younger brother, i.e. the wife of a husband's nephew. Cf. dyārathᵃr. dyārath-zāmaturᵘ m. the son-in-law of a husband's younger brother, i.e. the husband of a husband's niece.
m. the son of a husband's brother (Gr.Gr. 133). -nŏsh f. i.q. dyārath-nŏsh, q.v., s.v. dyārath.

m. a quasi-infinitive formed from dyār, and used in the following phrase: dyāranas dah sās m. ten thousand for talking of money, (but the ten thousand are only cowries, and are equal merely to a hundred pice or one rupee and nine anas. Hence the phrase is something like our "great cry and little wool"). Cf. dyāra- sösyunᵘ, s.v. dyār.
or dyāraza f. the daughter of a husband's brother (Gr.Gr. 133).
m. the object of dyān, q.v., the object of religious meditation, that which is meditated upon (L.V. 59).
adj. (f. ḍë˘bᵘ̈), loose, slack, not compact, soft through and through, pliant (esp. of anything made of wood or metal).

or ḍyojyᵘ m. (sg. dat. ḍĕjis), a pair of ear pendants worn suspended from the lobe of each ear; esp. the kind worn by a married Brāhmaṇ woman so long as her husband is alive (L. 262). ¶ ḍĕji-horᵘ m., id. (El. dejihor and dijahur) (Gr.Gr. 81, L. 262). -hȧrⁱ-kan m. a single one of such a pair. -hȧrⁱ-shitiñ f. a small ear-pendant of little value.

m. (sg. dat. dĕlis), a soft kind of grass growing in marshy land. There are said to be two varieties, one of which is twisted into string for use as thongs for wooden sandals (khrāv), while the other is used for making twine for tying up parcels in shops. --˚, the word is used to indicate rough rope made of other materials, as in bangi-d., rough rope of hemp bark; brana-d., ditto of elm- bark. Cf. banga and bran (Gr.Gr. 25). ¶ dĕlⁱ gë̆ḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -gĕjĕ), a bundle of this grass, as much as can be held in one hand. --gĕḍürᵘ -- f., id. --gyoḍᵘ -- m. a larger bundle of this grass. -pulahorᵘ m. a pair of sandals made of this grass, worn by Kāshmīrīs in the mountains. -pushĕṭh (sg. dat. -pushᵉ̆ṭi), a thong made of this grass, for tying on a wooden sandal (khrāv); cf. pushĕṭh. -ʦürᵘ̈ f. a small handful of this grass. -wājĕñ f. a woman who gathers and sells this grass.

adj. (f. ḍë˘jᵘ̈ or ḍĕjⁱ), loose, slack, flabby; loose, unsteady (of something requiring support, cf. aḍa-ḍ, s.v. aḍ); (of a knot) loose, easily untied; (of a tied-up parcel or the like) loose, untied. ḍyolᵘ-motᵘ adj. (f. ḍë˘jᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), become loose, slack, flabby, etc., as ab. Cf. ḍĕlun.
m. a kind of large mattock, esp. used in the cultivation of rough, stony, mountain land.
adj. (f. ḍë˘njᵘ̈ or ḍĕnjⁱ), having an insecure base, tottering, unsteady (of something resting on uneven ground, etc.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. dyöñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), to cause to recollect, to bring to mind. dyöñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. dyöñᵉ̆röwᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), caused to be recollected, brought to a person's memory by someone else; (of a person) caused to remember.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. dyöñᵒrᵒ), to remember, recollect accurately. dyöñᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. dyöñᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), remembered, recollected, called to mind.
m. the solid foundation of a wall or the like (El., Gr.Gr. 12).

m. N. of a sacred place in the Khuyᵉ̆hōm (the ancient Khōyāśrama) Pargana of Kashmīr, some 30 miles north-west of Śrīnagar in the hills bordering on the Wôlur lake. Cf. RT.Tr. II, 488. Here is a cave sacred to Pārvatī containing a Śiva-liṅga and a stone image of a cow with streaming udders.
m. (f. dyörᵘ̈), a rich man (or woman) (Gr.Gr. 12).
m. the sound caused by snapping the middle finger and thumb in time to music and as a kind of accompaniment.
for dyutᵘ, in the compound hyotᵘ-dyotᵘ, taking and giving, see hyonᵘ.

adj. (f. ḍiḍᵘ̈, dat. ḍijĕ), impudent, audacious, insolent, rude; one who disregards authority, one who sticks at nothing in robbing or the like, one who threatens with the object of robbery, one who bluffs for that purpose. --lāgun -- m.inf. to threaten or bluff with the intention of robbing some person. --matun -- m.inf. general plundering by violence to occur (when authority is lax and despised). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. plundering to fall, to be plundered of one's property, to be robbed (of a person).

(Gr.Gr. 237, 238) m.sg. diʦāv; diʦām, by me (K. 520); diʦānas, by him to him (Rām. 1444); pl. diʦöyēy; f. sg. and pl. diʦöyĕ. ¶ 1 perf. part. dyutᵘ-motᵘ (Śiv. 1206). ¶ The causal is dāwun or diwanāwun (Gr.Gr. 172), or dāwanāwun, qq.v. ¶ To give, grant (passim); to impart, yield, produce, emit; to give (a blow, etc.) (Śiv. 873); to lay (eggs); to create (Śiv. 1306); to cause, occasion (as pain, etc.) (Gr.M. 1680); to allow, let, permit (after the abl. of an inf., e.g. pakana dyunᵘ, to allow to go); to appoint (to an office, etc.) (Rām. 869); to inflict (a punishment) (Gr.M. 673); to put, place (Gr.M. 215; Śiv. 492, 792, 968); to put on, wear (a crown, a helmet, etc.) (Rām. 979, 1001); to apply, put (to) (K.Pr. 12, Śiv. 1111); to give forth, raise (a cry, etc.) (Gr.M. 231, Śiv. 828); to do, make, perform (an action) (Śiv. 660, 709, 1161); to close (a door) (K.Pr. 26, Rām. 16, 22, 31); to aim (a gun, etc.); to fire (a bullet, arrow, etc.) (Rām. 109, 320, 499, 1406, 1408, 1410, 1455); to have sexual intercourse with a woman (K.Pr. 246). ¶ This verb is very commonly used with a substantive to form a nominal compound verb. Such so-called compounds are often hardly compounds at all, each member retaining its own meaning, as in bāg dyunᵘ, to give a share, to divide; bal dyunᵘ, to give an offering, make a sacrificial offering. At other times the compound acquires a special meaning, as in ȧchⁱ diñᵘ̈, to apply the eye, hence, to cast the evil eye; ongul dyunᵘ, to apply the finger, hence, to tickle the throat so as to promote vomiting. Such compounds will be found under the various substantives which form the first member. ¶ The verb dyunᵘ is often added to the conjunctive participle of another verb, without materially altering the latter's sense, as in barun or barith dyunᵘ, to fill. ¶ dinī impers. fut. part. c.g. that which is to be given, the amount due to another. ¶ dina-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a giver, one who gives; hence, a charitable, or generous person; m. an unchaste man, an habitual adulterer or fornicator. Cf. dinal and Gr.Gr. 107. ¶ dyutᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. diʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), given, etc., as ab. (YZ. 211).

(sg. dat. --lambakas --), a billow of smoke, a large puff of smoke. --tulun -- m.inf. to raise smoke; met. to use threats and abuse in order forcibly to compel a person to do something, to abuse and illtreat with violence. --ʦhĕway --f. abatement of smoke; hence, putting out a fire just lit, as when there is no food to cook or on the occurrence of some sudden sorrow, such as the death of a relation or friend; met. the occurrence of some calamity. --wŏthun -- m.inf. smoke to rise; met. to be abused and illtreated violently as under --tulun ab. ¶ dᵃha golᵘ m. a pipe for carrying away smoke, a chimney-pipe. -họ̆bᵘ m. the smoke-mouthful; hence, the small hole in the top of a fireplace made as a passage for the smoke. -kaṭh or -kruṭh f. (sg. dat. -kaṭi), the acrid taste of smoke, a smoky taste. -lambukh m. (sg. dat. -lambakas), i.q. dᵃh-lambukh ab. -mŏshᵉ̆kh f. (sg. dat. -mŏshki), the smell of smoke, esp. of unseen smoke, whether pleasant or unpleasant. -mŏyĕ f. slight smoke, a light cloud of smoke (Gr.Gr. 164). -phakh m. (sg. dat. -phakas), an unpleasant smell of smoke. -ring f. a trace of smoke, a thin line of smoke rising from a small fire, a slight cloud of smoke (Gr.Gr. 162). -wọ̆bᵘ m. a smoke-hole, a small hole in a wall over a fireplace for the issue of smoke. -wŏmād f. (sg. dat. -wŏmözᵘ̈), an unpleasant smell of smoke (e.g. of a room full of smoke or of clothes which have been exposed to smoke). ¶ dᵃ̇hᵃ̇-gagur m. (sg. dat. -gagaras), a smoke-rat, hence a heavy hanging cloud of smoke, collected owing to there being no exit. -golᵘ m., i.q. dᵃha-˚ ab. --gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), smoked, that which has been exposed to smoke, smoky, smoke-begrimed. -gard f. smoke-dust, soot. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become smoked or smoky, to become smoke-begrimed. -konḍᵘ m. smarting of the eyes, etc., from smoke. -konḍᵘ karun m.inf. to scour the bottom of a cooking-pot to remove the smoke-stains. --korᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --kürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), smoked, dirtied by smoke, sooty. --karun -- m.inf. to dirty with smoke, to make or allow to become sooty (e.g. by putting anything in a smoky place). -kaṭh f., i.q. dᵃha-˚ ab. -kuṭhᵘ m. a smoke-room, (in the case of a large cooking-room) an upper chamber of boards for collecting all the smoke, which is then permitted to issue through one orifice. -katurᵘ m. a smoke-jar, an earthen vessel placed reversed over a lamp so as to catch and collect lamp- black. -lambukh m., i.q. dᵃh-˚, q.v. -mã̄d f. the evil smell of the smoke of burning a dead body or the like. -mŏshᵉ̆kh f., i.q. dᵃha-˚ ab.-nôrᵘ m. a smoke-pipe for conveying heated air from a stove so as to distribute heat. -phakh m., i.q. dᵃha-˚ ab. -ring f., i.q. dᵃha- ˚ab. -ʦhĕway f., i.q. dᵃh-˚ ab. -wọ̆bᵘ m., i.q. dᵃha-˚ ab. -wŏmād f., i.q. dᵃha-˚ ab. ¶ dᵃhi-khotᵃ m. a chamber over a fireplace for collecting the smoke and directing it out by one exit. -kūṭhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a room full of smoke, a smoky room. -ʦọ̆lᵘ m. a smoke-hearth, (in a fireplace with three openings one behind the other) a brick chimney issuing from behind the hindmost opening.

When ya follows a consonant, or when a follows ñ or sh, it becomes ĕ, which is represented by or in Nāgarī and by zēr in the Persian character. Thus, وِتھ vĕth, the River Jehlam; میانِہ, myāñĕ, my (fem. plur.); بِنِہ, bĕñĕ, a sister. This letter is commonly pronounced like the e in 'met', but some Kāshmīrīs, especially Hindūs, put a slight y-sound in front of it, as if we said 'mʸet'. Before ⁱ, ĕ is unchanged in pronunciation, but is written in the Nāgarī character as modified. Thus, tĕṭhⁱ, bitter (pl. masc.). Before ᵘ it becomes yo, as in ṭyoṭhᵘ, bitter (sing. masc.). Before ᵘ̈ it becomes modified to ë˘ (see below), as in ṭë˘ṭhᵘ̇, bitter (sing. fem.), pronounced almost ṭʸüṭh. Before ᵃ it becomes ẹ̆ (see below). ¶ When ĕ (i.e. ya) follows ʦ, ʦh, or z, the y is generally dropped, and ĕ becomes a. Thus diʦ + ya is not diʦĕ, but diʦa. The same also often occurs after s. The rules for this will be found in the grammars, under the head of the conjugation of verbs. ¶ In the foregoing cases we actually find a used where we should expect ĕ after ʦ, ʦh, or z. We have seen that after ñ an a is pronounced as ĕ. This is because the sound of y is inherent in ñ, which is pronounced as ny. The letter ña is therefore naturally pronounced as nyĕ. This change is universal. Kāshmīrīs also maintain that the sound of y is inherent in the four letters c, ch, j, and sh. In other words, they say that c is the same as cy, ch as chy, j as jy, and sh as shy, and they write them indifferently; and respectively. It thus follows that when ĕ follows any one of these three letters the y of the ya is usually, but not necessarily, omitted, so that cĕ is written cya or ca; chĕ is written chya or cha; jĕ, jya or ja; and shĕ, shĕ or sha. In other words, both and are pronounced as cĕ, and so on for the others. In the case of, as in the case of, the pronunciation of a as ĕ is universal, and hence, in this dictionary, is always transliterated shĕ, not sha. Here, in contrast to the foregoing, we have a change of spelling, but no change of sound. ¶ Moreover, owing to the constant confusion between i and ĕ, ci is often written (i.e. ca for cĕ) or cĕ, and, conversely, we even find ci written instead of ca or cĕ. Similarly, the postposition nisha (or, better, nishĕ), from, is often written in the Roman character nishi, and its real sound is nearer nishĕ than anything else. So on, for the others. ¶ We have seen that ya only becomes ĕ when it follows a consonant in the same word. When ya is initial or follows a vowel it is pronounced yĕ, and will be so transliterated. Thus, یِمِس, yĕmis (not yamis), to whom; بِیِہ, biyĕ, also. ¶ The letter ĕ is quite often interchanged with i, both in speaking and in writing. Most Kāshmīrīs seem to be unable to distinguish between the two sounds.

This vowel bears the same relation to ĕ that ạ bears to a. That is to say, ĕ becomes ẹ̆ in cases in which a would become ạ. Its pronunciation is hardly affected. It is represented in Nāgarī by putting the mark over the corresponding sign for ĕ, and in the Persian character by zēr. Thus, from the, وِتھھُن, vĕṭhun, to be fat, we get, وِتھھَرُن, vẹ̆ṭhᵃrun, to make fat, in which the ĕ has been modified to ẹ̆ owing to the influence of the following a-mātrā.
This is the modified form of ĕ before ᵘ̈. It has a sound lying between i and ü, with a slight y-sound preceding, as in ṭë˘ṭhᵘ̈, above, under ĕ.

This is the long ē of Hindī, pronounced like the a in 'mate'. It is represented by in Nāgarī, and by yē in the Persian character. Thus, میل, mēl, unite. This sound cannot commence a word. In such a position ē always becomes yē. Thus, ēr, wool, becomes yēr. In the Nāgarī character an initial ē is optionally written, thus or, but the word is always pronounced yēr, and will be so written in this dictionary. The Persian character has always ییر. ¶ When ē is followed by ᵃ, ⁱ, or ᵘ̈ it becomes ī. Thus, from tēzun, to be sharp, we have tīzᵃrāwun, to make sharp; from the base khēt- we have khītⁱ, a field (pl. nom. khētĕ); and from the base sēr- we have sīrᵘ̈, a brick (pl. nom. sērĕ). When ē is followed by ᵘ it becomes yū. Thus, from phērun, to revolve, we have for the past participle, masc. sing. phyūrᵘ, plur. phīrⁱ; fem. sing. phīrᵘ̈, plur. phērĕ. ¶ The letter ē is quite often interchanged with ī, both in speaking and in writing. Most Kāshmīrīs seem to be unable to distinguish between the two sounds.
m. and N. of the elephant-god Gaṇēśa, lit. one-tusked; voc. -danta (Śiv. 7).
a wide kind of blanket made at Shupiyon in one breadth; compare the dōbari blanket made in two breadths sewn together (L. 370). This word should probably be spelt akhbari.

. The sixth (or, if we count the aspirate ch as a separate letter, the seventh) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet, the third consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the twenty-ninth consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It has the sound of the letter g in the English 'game'. ¶ The Sanskrit aspirate sonant gha does not exist as a pronounced sound in Kāshmīrī. When a Hindī or Sanskrit word containing this letter also occurs in Kāshmīrī, the gh is representedby g. Thus, the Hindī ghōṛā, a horse, is represented in Kāshmīrī by gurᵘ. Some writers retain this gh in writing. Thus, they write for gara, a house, on the analogy of the Hindī; but this custom is both useless and misleading. In the present work such words will always be spelt with g, and hence words found in any native book spelt with should be looked up in the English order under g. ¶ The character is named gagar-gö, and gösⁱ-ga. ¶ The letter غ sometimes occurring in words borrowed from Arabic or Persian is also represented in Kāshmīrī by g, like which it is pronounced. Thus غالب is pronounced gölib.
m. the sprout of a plant (vegetable, tree, etc.); the womb, see bel. ¶ gaba phaṭun m.inf. to burst forth from the womb, to be born (W. 141, K.Pr. 255).
in gaba-kônᵘ m. the first and the last of the row of sticks set up in the ground on which the warp is arranged, prior to putting it in a loom for weaving.

m. a kind of wadded woollen quilt. -chiṭᵘ̈ or -chiṭh f.
