m. a dewlap; the wattle (of a cock); a double chin (El.).
f. a woman suffering from prolapsus uteri; esp. one in this condition owing to habitual profligacy.
m. linen cloth, cloth made of hempen-flax.
m. darkness (Gr.Gr. 140); hence, met. foulness, dirtiness caused by contact with something else; e.g. muddiness (of water), dimness (of a mirror), opacity (of the atmosphere), and so on. Cf. goṭᵘ.
m. (sg. dat. gachas), plaster, lime plaster, whitewash (Gr.M.); gypsum (L. 63). ¶ gachi-kuṭhᵘ m. a room of which the walls are plastered (Rām. 1627, 1783).
m. (sg. dat. ?), marrow. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to extract marrow; met. to thrash a person unmercifully, so that he has not even strength to arise.

f. a fish (K.Pr. 14, 38, 63, 140, 150, 168, 258; H. i, 8, 9). Regarding the fish of Kashmīr, see El. s.v. gáḍ. --āpᵃrüñᵃ --, f.inf. to feed fish into a person's mouth; met. to confound a person in argument; to defeat a person in a scolding match, to render him speechless by giving him abuse so foul that he is at a loss to invent anything fouler in reply. --raṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to fish (El.). --raṭanwôlᵘ -- n.ag. m. (f. raṭanwājĕñ), a fisherman (El.). ¶ gāḍa-bāha m. fish-steam, a diet of fish combined with the application of the steam and juice of cooked fish, employed as a remedy in cases of impotence and the like. -bata m. N. of an offering of cooked fish and rice, usually made in the month of Pŏh (Skt. Pauṣa = December-January) to the Vāstupuruṣa, or personified archetype of a house worshipped as a deity; cf. dāyĕth-gāḍa, s.v. dāyuth. -dĕgulᵘ m. an earthenware vessel used for cooking a spiced stew of fish previously fried in oil. Cf. -tövᵘ̈, bel. -güñᵘ̈ f. a piece or slice of fish, cooked or uncooked, sliced fish as a dish (K.Pr. 205, -gani). -gañĕ khārañĕ f. pl. inf. to raise bits of fish; met. to cudgel or whip the naked body so as to raise weals (considered to resemble fishes in shape). -hönzᵘ̈ m. (f. -hānzañ), a fish boatman, a man who lives by netting fish, a fisherman. The f. is a woman who lives by selling fish so caught (Gr.M.). -kāh f. (sg. dat. -köshᵘ̈), the eleventh lunar day of the dark half of the month of Phāgun (Skt. Phālguna = February-March), on which offerings of fish are made to the böravs (bhairavas) in preparation for the Śivarātri festival culminating on the ensuing thirteenth lunar day of the dark half of the same month (cf. börav). -khŏḍ m. a hollow flooded in the rainy season and filled with fish. When the water dries off the fish remain behind and are caught. -khôrᵘ m. the outer basket-work of a kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈, or portable brazier, of which the inner earthenware receptacle for burning fuel has been broken, and which is commonly used as a fish-basket; see khôrᵘ 1. -khāv m. fish-eater, a kind of fish-eating bird, described as small, of a dark colour, and possessing a long beak. -kala m. the head of a fish; a person with a head shaped like that of a fish. -kan m. the ear-bone of a fish, i.e. the flat bones at the side of the head of a large fish, supposed to cover the ears. These are used in the manufacture of little boxes or the like. -konḍᵘ m. a fish-bone. -kȧndⁱ-dôvⁱ m. a kind of embroidery resembling the backbone of a fish, herring-boning. -kᵃnañĕ f. pl. inf. to sell fish; met. to go about from house to house uttering scandalous tales against a person; to engage in a verbal quarrel, to use Billingsgate. -krāy f. large iron pan for frying fish. -lĕjⁱ or -lë̆jᵘ̈ f. an earthen pot for cooking fish; such a pot full of cooked fish. -lüṭᵘ̈ f. the tail end of a fish. -pakhᵃsh m. the fin of a fish. -parmāna m. a stone or iron weight for weighing fish (usually heavier than similar weights used for other purposes). -shĕhalun m. the smell of unwashed fish; genl. a fishy smell. -shikār m. fishing (W. 114). -ṭhyupᵘ m. a kind of deep basket made of withies, built like a cage, in which fish are kept. -ṭĕpun m. (sg. dat. -ṭĕpanas), fish-guts. -tövᵘ̈ f. a pan in which pieces of fish are fried before making them into a stew. Cf. -dĕgulᵘ ab. -wörᵘ̈ f. a fishing-boat; genl. a small boat used as tender to a larger one.
m. a fort, citadel, castle (K.Pr. 17); esp. a small masonry fortress built in the hills by some local rājā.
adj. c.g. whole, entire; esp. of something bought or sold as one whole.
m. a suppliant (El. gada) (YZ. 322, sg. dat. gadāyĕs); a mendicant, a beggar (Śiv. 1238).
m. an earthen waterpot, pitcher, jar, pot (Gr.M.).
m. N. of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna), the club-bearer, Gadādhara (Śiv. 938).
m. (of cattle, houses, children, wealth), abundance, a great quantity (whether existing or coming in).
m. private agreement, esp. (but not necessarily) with evil intent against some one, secret conspiracy. Cf. garb.
(? spelling), a certain measure for rice-straw (L. 243). 50 gaddis = one trakh of about 11 lb. ? the same as gë̆ḍᵘ̈.
f. begging, mendicity (Śiv. 1475, gadāyĕ, sg. dat.; but H. x, 2 gadöyiyĕ-hondᵘ, sg. gen.). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to beg, beg for.

adj. (f.gadüjᵘ̈ or gadȧjⁱ), abundant, multitudinous (of prosperity, off- spring, cattle, wealth, etc.) (Gr.Gr. 145). --prasun -- m.inf. to produce offspring in large quantities, to be excessively fertile (of women, or female cattle).

m. goitre, bronchocele. For an account of goitre in the Valley see El. s.v. gaḍur (L. 460, gadaru). gadᵃ̇rᵃ̇-lav m. a kind of hay-rick. Grass growing in swamps, etc., is collected and dried. It is then twisted into rough ropes, and stored in large masses in the forks of trees for use in the winter.
m. (f.gāḍᵘ̈rᵘ̈), (in old times) a man or woman of the Vaidya caste, whose profession was that of a physician; N. of a village on the bank of the Sind (Sindhu) River, formerly inhabited by them.
adj. c.g. inarticulate, speaking thickly or convulsively, faltering. gadᵃgada wön ī f. a sobbing statement, a sorrowful statement full of sobs.
m. a beloved (esp. an only) son. -han m.dim. a little beloved son, as a term of affection, a darling little boy.
adj. (f. gạḍᵘ̈rᵘ̈), one who suffers from goitre.
f. a royal palace, esp. that portion of it in which the king transacts business, the royal court.
adj. c.g. (of a garment, cloth, or the like), having a hole, holed. Cf. godᵘ.
m. the flowers of the Delphinium saniculæfolium (El. ghāfiz).
m. the opening in the top platform of a native cooking range, over which vessels are set for cooking (K.Pr. 125). Cf. güjᵘ̈.

or grã̄gal (Rām. 184) f. insolent pride, arrogance, self-conceit; diversion or distraction of the attention from some work in which one is engaged, owing to something interfering with it, interruption (Gr.Gr. 128, K.Pr. 187, Śiv. 80, 244); the state of being not right (El.). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to interrupt (Gr.M.); to disturb, distract, make distraught (Rām. 184). ¶ g(gr)ã̄gali gaʦhun  m.inf. in the course of one piece of work, to forget about it and to become busily engaged in another work, to have one's attention diverted from anything. --karun -- m.inf. to distract a person's attention by directing it to something else (e.g. to turn the attention of a crying child).
or grã̄galāwun conj. 1 (p.p. gā̃galôwᵘ), to distract or divert a person's attention, to interrupt him when busily engaged in some work.
or grã̄galilad adj. c.g. insolently proud, arrogant; interrupted, distracted (of one busily engaged); suffering from indigestion.

or grã̄galun conj. 3 (p.p. gã̄galyōv or grã̄galyōv), to have one's attention diverted from any work, to be interrupted; to take up some pleasant business in the midst of some other work which one forgets.
f. loud thundering, esp. when unseasonable; met. the human 'thundering' of abuse.
f. thunder, the rumbling noise of thunder (L. 456, K.Pr. 245, 253, Śiv. 1868); any loud sound like thunder, a thunderous roar (Śiv. 1232).
m. the name for the letter ga, used in schools.

or gagorᵘ m. [sg. dat. gagaras (Gr.Gr. 58); f. gagᵘ̈rᵘ̈ (Gr.Gr. 35), see bel.], a male rat (Gr.Gr. 35, K.Pr. 46, 63, 64, 196, 199); a certain rat-shaped bird, the White Nun or Smew, Mergellus albellus (L. 131). For rats in Kashmīr see L. 112. ¶ gagar-dand m. a rat's tooth; met. a human tooth which is very thin and sharp. --konḍᵘ m. a certain mountain plant with yellow flowers and thorny leaves, believed to keep away rats, Astragalus sp. (L. 76). Its root is used as a remedy for toothache, and also for making toothbrushes. -kuṭhᵘ m. a rat's room, a small dark room infested by rats in which in former days children used to be shut up as a punishment. -mĕngañ f. rat's dung. -sörᵘ̈ f. rat collection, i.e. making up a store by stealing little by little at a time. -ṭukh m. (sg. dat. -ṭukas), a hole gnawed by a rat in a cloth or the like. -ṭinḍa m. a rat-trap. -tāph m. (sg. dat. -tāpas), partial sunshine here and there, shining on the ground through orifices in the clouds. -ʦhal m. a kind of rat-trap. -ʦhāy f. 'rat's shade', i.e. the sunshine without warmth of a winter morning or evening. -ʦhyotᵘ adj. (f. -ʦhë˘ṭᵘ̈), rat's leavings, the remains of food or of a fruit which has been partially eaten by rats. The word is an adjective agreeing in gender with the food referred to. -wāl f. (sg. dat. -wöjᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 69), a rat's nest, a rat hole (K.Pr. 3, wájí for wöjᵘ̈). -yurmī f. Rhododendron campanulatum (El.). ¶ gagᵘ̈rᵘ̈, f. a female rat; a mouse (K.Pr. 64). --phaṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'a mouse to split', met. disunion to arise between associates or partners in any work.
m. N. of a sacred place on the east of the town of Śrīnagar, and in the middle of a lake lying at the north foot of the Gōpādri or Taḵẖt-ĕ Sulaimān.
m. brightness, brilliancy, lustre, light (Śiv. 1068, H. xii, 2), cf. gāsh.
m. a place (used --˚); time, turn, as in shōra-gāh, a time or opportunity for outcry, a proclamation (H. vi, 13). gāh bĕgāh گاہ بیگاہ, adv. in season and out of season (H. vi, 13).
m. shade, dim illumination (of ground or other place overshadowed by trees, creepers, or the like).
m. excessive eating, gorging oneself with food (so that one can neither move nor speak).
m. one who sticks or follows close behind another in order to accomplish some object.
f. sticking or following close behind another in order to obtain some object.

or guhulᵘ 1 m. a natural forest-bower, a dark place in a forest shadowed over and hidden by trees, creepers, etc. (Śiv. 1752). ¶ guhali-gupan, m.pl. cattle of the forest, cattle led out into the forest to graze, as opposed to stalled cattle (K.Pr. 71).

or gahana m. an ornament, trinket, jewels, women's ornaments (Śiv. 1227, 1228, 1232, 1233, 1235); El. spells this word gehna. -pāth f. (sg. dat. -pöʦᵘ̈), a general term for the paraphernalia (including jewellery and dishes) given to a bride as part of her dowry.

m. (f. gahᵃrüʦᵃ), a child (e.g. an orphan) dependent on some one who is not a parent; in f. also , one of a number of daughters of a needy family, who is hence unwelcome and treated with unkindness, and has to depend for her food on others' charity.

or gaibī, göbī غیبی (YZ. 38), adj. c.g. invisible, unseen; concealed (K.Pr. 28); the Invisible, Fate. gaibücᵘ̈ balāy, heaven's misfortune, evil fate (K.Pr. 4). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to disappear (H. iii, 6). --sö̃panun -- m.inf., id. (Rām. 1193, 1589).

adj. c.g. other, different, strange, foreign; ˚-- other than, contrary to (W. 110). -hözir غیر حآضر adj. c.g. not present, absent (W. 110). -jins غیر جنس adj. c.g. of or belonging to a different race, kind, or species. In Rām. 1096 spelt gairĕ- jins. -mumkin غیر ممکن adj. c.g. impossible, impracticable, not feasible (W. 110). -wöjib غیر وآجب adj. c.g. contrary to reason or law, improper, unreasonable, unjust, wrong (W. 110). -zān adj. c.g. ignorant (H. vii, 27; xi, 5).

görath غیرت m. (sg. dat. gairatas), jealousy; source or cause of jealousy; care of what is sacred and inviolable; a nice sense of honour; honour; courage, spirit, strength of mind, coolness in difficulties (Rām. 685, 865, 966, 1081); modesty, bashfulness; envy, emulation; disdain, indignation; enmity.
(Rām. 1096), i.q. gair-jins, see gair, p. 296b, l. 21.

or güjᵘ̈gāh m. the bushy tail of the yak (Bos grunniens) employed as a 'chowry' or long brush for whisking off insects, flies, etc., one of the emblems of royalty, and, as such, used in worshipping the image of a god; a string composed of several tassels (made of the hair of this tail) suspended as an ornament from an elephant's neck, or fastened to a horse's ears and extending on both sides to the saddle. --karun -- m.inf. to wave such a fly-whisk over a king, the image of a god, etc. (Śiv. 213, 1147, 1895).
m. inarticulate noise or shouting (as that of a number of children assembled together).
m. meanness in giving; persistent graspingness in receiving.
adj. (f. gakhürᵘ̈), one who is mean or dishonest in giving, or persistently grasping in receiving.
f. the act of grinding, triturating (grain, etc.).

f. (sg. dat. gāli, Gr.Gr. 69), an abusive or contumelious expression, abuse, foul or insulting language (Rām. 339); a feeling of shame caused by another's actions, mortification, humiliation (Gr.Gr. 10, H. ix, 4). Cf. gözᵘ̈. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a feeling of humiliation or mortification to occur (as when a gift offered, or an order given, by a person of some consequence is refused or disregarded).

m. a shout, scream, shriek. gal-wān 1 adj. c.g. (as subst., f. gal-wöñᵘ̈; for galwān 2, galwöñᵘ̈ 2, see s.v.), one who habitually bullies and shouts at others; one who, on receiving merely a slight touch or push from another, screams out as if he were badly hurt, so as to charge him with hurting him severely. -wānᵃgī f. the habit of habitually bullying and shouting abuse at others (esp. with the intention of black- mailing, exciting undeserved compassion, or the like). -wönil f., id. ¶ gala-boḍᵘ adj. (f.-büḍᵘ̈), one who has naturally a loud voice.

m. the lower part of the cheek, the jowl. Cf. golᵘ 2 and Gr.Gr. 51. --hĕñ f. jowl-pinching (e.g. the playful pinching of a child or woman's cheek). ¶ gala-dodᵘ 1 adj (f. -düzᵘ̈), one the corners of whose lips are burnt (by hot food, pungent spices, etc.). -dodᵘ 2 m. a kind of thick cake or loaf whose ends or edges are burnt in the oven. -gĕv m. ghī on the cheek (or corners of the lips) (but not in the mouth); hence, assumed prosperity, something fine outside, but worthless or empty within. -horᵘ m. the pair of cheeks on one person's face. -mọ̆nḍᵘ m. a lump of a jowl, a gross fat jowl. -tachañĕ f.pl. scratchings of the cheek; hence, weeping and crying out in jealousy of another's success, etc. -vyoṭhᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ṭhᵘ̈), fat-jowled. -wŏzulᵘ adj. (f. -wŏzüjᵘ̈ or -wŏzȧjⁱ), (of a person) red-jowled, red-cheeked; (of an inanimate object) fair without and ugly or worthless within.

f. the throat, windpipe, neck. -gati adv. round the neck or throat (e.g. of wrapping a blanket or the like). -khaph f. (sg. dat. -khapi), throttling, choking. -tan f. the chin-strap for holding on a cap; the part of a horse's headstall near the bridle. -wüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -wacĕ), the neck of a coat or other garment.
m. (f. galadārĕñ), a grain-merchant. The f. is either his wife or a female grain-merchant.
f. the profession of a grain-merchant, grain-selling.

f. N. of a method of prayer to Śiva, called in Sanskrit galamudrā. It is uttered from the throat, like the bleating of a goat, and is said to have been originally used for the prayer uttered by Dakṣa in goat's language, when his head had been burnt and a goat's head was given to him instead (Śiv. 357).
f. a mistake, a blunder (Gr.M.); inaccuracy. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to draw out inaccuracy, to look out for blunders, to criticize (a book or the like) (Gr.M.).

m. the hold or place in a boat in which luggage is stowed; according to El. (s.v. gálo) it is the space in the centre of the boat occupied by the passengers. -püṭᵘ̈ f. the hatch or board which covers the top of this 'hold'.
n.ag. (f.galawüñᵘ̈), that which melts or decreases (K.Pr. 254, of snow).
n.ag. (f. gālawüñᵘ̈), one who causes to melt, etc.; a destroyer (Śiv. 158, 813, 853, 860, 862, 1321, 1381, 1417).
a wrapper, a thing that is rolled round (another thing); (in Kashmīr) the receptacle in which the day's receipts of a shopkeeper are deposited, the till.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. golᵘ, f. güjᵘ̈; 2 p.p. gajyōv), to melt, dissolve (intr.) (Gr.Gr. viii, K.Pr. 95, W. 136, Śiv. 583, 1538, 1540); to be destroyed (YZ. 280; Śiv. 165, 767, 930, 1127; Rām. 2, 377; H. xii, 10, 24, 25); to be entirely expended, melted away; to waste away, disappear (El., K.Pr. 75); to waste away (from disease, sorrow, unrequited love, or the like) (YZ. 33, 266; Rām. 779, 1662); to pass away, expire (of time) (Śiv. 1521); to waste away, become distraught, collapse (from sorrow or the like) (Rām. 1190). ¶ gȧlⁱ gȧlⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to go melting melting; to be much ashamed (because one cannot suitably return a favour, or because one is treated rudely in the presence of one's superiors); to be in a state of terror owing to apprehended calamity. ¶ golᵘ-motᵘ perf. part (f. güjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), melted or dissolved; destroyed; entirely expended. ¶ galith gaʦhun m.inf. to be melted (of metals, snow, etc.); to be destroyed; to be humble or humiliated by abuse or fear.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. gôlᵘ, f. göjᵘ̈; 2 p.p.gājyōv), to cause to melt (as metals by fire; in H. vii, 19, of wood melting before a saw); to destroy (Śiv. 13, 125, 170, 269; Rām. 77, 617; H. ii, 11); to cause to melt away, entirely to expend anything; to cause to waste away (e.g. a disease or hard study making a person thin, or a lover's absence causing one to pine) (YZ. 34, 264, 307, 312, 332; Rām. 1497, 1594); to cause to disappear (Śiv. 105, 452). jigar gālun (Rām. 192) or pān g. (Rām. 1281, 1458, 1545), to cause one's own liver or heart to melt, to serve a person with heart and soul, to devote oneself to a person, to strive earnestly for any particular object. ¶ gôlᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. göjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), melted; destroyed (Śiv. 888); entirely expended.
m. a certain disease, a swelling of the jowl or lower part of the cheek.
or galuth m. (sg. dat. galatas), destruction, esp. of something inanimate; the state of being or becoming expended, consumed, exhausted.

m. (f. galwöñᵘ̈ 2; for galwān 1,galwöñᵘ̈ 1, see under gal 1), a professional tender of strings of ponies on the mountain pastures (he has made such a name for himself that the words thief and galwān are synonymous, L. 365); a horse thief, esp. a mountaineer who steals horses from distant villages. The f. is a galwān's wife. Cf. gulubān.
m. overcoming, victory, conquest. --karun -- m.inf. to conquer (El.). --karanwôlᵘ -- n.ag.m. (f. -wājĕñ), a conqueror (El.).

m. grief, mourning, woe (Rām. 1101, 1655), sorrow, sadness (K.Pr. 217; YZ. 181, 249; Śiv. 475, 842, 926; Rām. 453); solicitude, care, concern, anxiety (Śiv. 1017, 1754, 1770, Rām. 323); fear (Śiv. 424, 1848; Rām. 553, 898, 979); kē̃h gam chuna, there is no sorrow; hence, it is of no consequence, no matter. --barun -- m.inf. to grieve, to suffer sorrow (El.). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf., id. (El.; K.Pr. 93; YZ. 104, where kainh is evidently incorr. for khĕh; Rām. 875, 1138). --kāsun -- m.inf. to remove grief (El., Śiv. 1455). ¶ gama-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), free from grief; fearless (Śiv. 586).

m. a village, a hamlet [Gr.Gr. 160; K.Pr. 6, 9, 64, 109, 136, 231, 251, 253; Śiv. 1107, 1682 (in both cases opp. to shĕhar, a city); Rām. 1037, 1717]. -guṭh m. (sg. dat. -guṭhas), a village and the like, villages, etc. (as when a person says, "I am going to the villages, etc.," i.e. to the countryside). Cf. guṭh. -kun adv. towards, in the direction of, a village, u.w. vbs. of going, etc. (Gr.Gr. 160). ¶ gāma-baṭa m. a village paṇḍit, a brāhmaṇ inhabitant of a village (whether learned or unlearned). -baṭañ f. the wife of a village brāhmaṇ. -chān m. a village carpenter (usually not an expert workman). -drọ̆shᵘ m. one accustomed to eat coarse, insipid, dirty food (like a poor villager). -dēwölⁱ m. a village bankrupt, a village spendthrift (who wastes his food, etc., because they are cheaply got); anyone who is extravagant in this way. --gāma-- adv. in every village, in each village (Rām. 214, 1766). -ganḍ m. a village knot, the banding together of villagers to enforce or carry out some object; hence, any such agreement made by a number of persons gathered together (e.g. a strike). -grūstᵘ m. (sg. dat. -grīstis), a village cultivator; esp. cont., some silly fat fellow who has been driven to take to village cultivation by his fellow-citizens who will have none of him. -labār m. a village rascal, a sturdy fool of a villager unacquainted with city ways, a Tony Lumpkin. -lawand m., id. -layĕ adv. occurring in villages, peculiarly in villages, especially in villages. -pacĕ adv. village-like, as in villages. ¶ gömⁱ-gām m. a whole village (including houses, fields, crops, inhabitants, cattle, etc.) (K.Pr. 12).
m. the act of going. See wūrdhwa- gaman.
m. diversion, pastime, amusement, esp. when accompanied by singing, acting, or the like.
adj. c.g. deep; deep in sound, deep-sounding; profound, sagacious, grave, serious; solemn, secret, mysterious (Śiv. 1753); dense, impenetrable (Śiv. 1062, of a forest).
m. a secret (El.), prob. incorr. for gambīr.
adj. c.g. sorrowful, grieved, sad, dejected (Gr.M., W. 145, Rām. 24).
adj. c.g. afflicted, sorrowing, sad (Rām. 361); commiserating, pitying, condoling, a comforter (Rām. 773).
m. an insolent fellow, esp. one who is an ignorant fool.
m. a fruitful field, esp. the rich land near a village site (L. 461 gámdu).

m. a log (of wood); a beehive (El.). mã̄cha-gan, m. a bee's nest, a group of honeycombs, a hive (cf. Gr.M.). ¶ gana-khürᵘ̈ f. shame caused by the non-success of any act or conduct, humiliation. -köʦᵘ̈ f. N. of a kind of small bird, described as crow-coloured and having a long tail. It is said to be perpetually fighting with other birds. -manḍav m. a kind of house built only of large logs, and found only in wild forest localities; a cooking-place cut off from one side of a room by a small wall or the like, nowadays found only in distant forest villages, but formerly in use throughout Kashmīr.

m. the keeper of a brothel (Gr.Gr. 37, K.Pr. 4); a prostitute's bully, one who lives with a harlot as her husband; frequently used as a mere term of abuse (H. v, 10; ix, 2; K.Pr. 54, 107). The f. is göñᵘ̈ 1 (Gr.Gr. 37), q.v. For particulars regarding these men and their occupation see El. s.v. ¶ gāna-buḍᵘ̈ f. the old woman of a gān, an old woman who acts as a procuress, a bawd. -bukᵒrᵒ m. a gān's face, shamelessness like that of a gān, shameless double-facedness. -buthᵘ m. a gān's face, shamelessness in asking, whether entitled to ask or not, and persisting in spite of insulting refusal. -buthörᵘ̈ f. a gān's ugly-facedness; shameless adherence to a course of conduct in spite of prohibition, of disgrace, or of punishment, etc. -har f. a gān's quarrel, a fight among prostitutes; a quarrel between any kind of low people; the friendship and hatred of prostitutes (quarrelling amongst themselves when a customer turns up, and good friends when there is none); similar friendship and hatred between other people. -küṭᵘ̈ f. a harlot's daughter; a woman who conducts herself as such. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a harlot's son; a shameless fellow who conducts himself as such (Gr.Gr. 132). -ʦamadüjᵘ̈ f. a gān's pretence at modesty; when occasion arises the passing of oneself off as a modest person, although one is really shameless. -wān m. the harlots' market, a place where they ply their trade. -way f. a harlot's fee, the price of a harlot. -yārᵘ̈zᵘ̈ f. harlot's love; false love kept up only so long as it is profitable.

adj. compact, solid; used --˚ in the sense of full of, densely filled with, as in ānanda-gan (Śiv. 102, 363, 867, 982, 1000, 1045, 1058, 1220, 1293, 1338, 1368, 1603, 1617), of bliss compact, full of bliss, an epithet of the Deity, or of a holy man (Śiv. 1759); ʦĕth-gan, full of intelligence, pure thought (also an epithet of the Deity) (Śiv. 1426).

m. the underground floor of the house (El., L. 461) usually inhabited by cattle, a cow-house, a cattle-stable. Cf. guhⁱ-gān s.v. guhᵘ. ¶ gāna-pōr m. the ground- floor of a three- or four-storied house (which floor is used as a cattle-stable).
m. a flock, troop; esp. (pl.) certain troops of demigods considered as Śiva's attendants and under the special superintendence of the god Gaṇēśa (Śiv. 2). See ganēsh.
f. conduct of or like that of souteneur (see gān 1); vile and shameless conduct.
m. (sg. dat. ganapatas), N. of the Hindū god Gaṇēśa; see ganēsh. -yāra m. N. of a holy bathing-place sacred to Gaṇēśa (Śiv. 11).
m. a meat-seller, a butcher (El. ganai).

f. (sg. dat. gönzᵘ̈), a bad smell, a stink (from decaying food, etc.). Cf. ganda. --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause anything to give forth a bad smell; met. to cause a thing to stink, to give it a bad name by not using it or using it improperly. --tulüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to raise a stink; met. to bring a person into disrepute by publishing his vicious conduct. --wŏthüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. a stink to rise; (of something previously good) to become stinking; met. (of a person of good repute) to become unworthy by doing something reprehensible. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a stink to come; (of food) to become corrupt; (of person of good repute) to acquire an evil reputation. ¶ gānda-ṭhūl m. an egg that is set, one in which the chicken is formed and about to be hatched out.

m. tieing; a knot, knot on a cord (Gr.Gr. 123, 145); any similar knot (e.g. in wood); the principal bead on a rosary (Śiv. 1314); the joint of a finger or toe; a knot tied closely and therefore difficult to be undone; difficulty, complication in any business; a bandage (El.). ganḍacĕ jāyĕ, at the place of a stop, at a stop (in reading a book according to punctuation) (Gr.M.). --dith thawun -- m.inf. to lock up safely, put by in a secure place. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to make a knot, to tie, to tie (up), tie (on). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. a knot to happen; to be brought to one's bearings (e.g. a child who has been free to be put under the discipline of a school); to be finally fixed for certain (e.g. a wedding which has been several times postponed); to be choked in swallowing, a piece of food to stick in the throat. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to tie, knot, tie up; to tie up a broken or dislocated bone, to put in splints. ¶ ganḍa adv. in a knot; hence, all together, all at once, in totality; (put up, fastened up, etc.) with a knot, securely (Śiv. 1311). -ḍulay f. rolling in a knot; hence, suddenly to fall down and die (esp. when walking). -dyolᵘ m. knotting-grass, a soft kind of grass which shopkeepers use for tying up parcels. It is also used for tying up a cut finger or the like. Cf. dyolᵘ. --ganḍ -- f. mutual connexion, mutual union; the ties of this world, worldly ties (Śiv. 1217). --gurᵘ -- m. a horse kept in a stable and not left to roam at grass. -nôrᵘ m. a wooden pipe or conduit for conveying water, as on a bridge, over a valley or depression from one hill to another, an aqueduct. -nēthᵃr m. a knotted marriage, marriage which is tied up, i.e. which has been formally agreed to by both parties but not yet consummated. -pan m. 'a knot-thread', a silken string lapped with silver wire, used by a woman for tying the hair that falls in plaits down her back. It ekes out the hair and extends down to the loins. -prān m. a knot-onion, the globular root of the onion plant, an onion. -wörᵘ̈ f. 'a knotted garden', i.e. a private, walled-in garden, to which the public is denied access. -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), a knotted union, the joining of two things firmly together (by sealing-wax, glue, sewing, or the like).
m. sugar-candy (El. possibly a misprint for kand, i.e. qand قند).

adj. c.g. stinking, fetid; filthy, dirty (e.g. a road, Gr.M.); rotten, putrid; foul, obscene, indecent (of speech); harsh, sour, vile (of temper). Cf. gānd. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become stinking; to be beaten and rendered ashamed and without answer in a mutual war of abusive words. --khash-khāsh -- گندہ خش خاش m. a stinking poppy-seed, a stinking thing of no account; hence met., a low mean fellow, an utter fool, one respected by no one, one of the lowest and vilest caste. --karun -- m.inf. to make stinking; met. to conquer a person in a mutual war of abusive words, rendering him humiliated and with no answer. -kusᵘ̈ f. 'a stinking unchaste woman', a low prostitute, a vile woman who admits the vilest to her embraces. -lyunᵘ m. N. of a certain wild creeping plant, which burns even without drying; it is used as a medicine for colic in horses and tumours; Daphne oleoides (L. 76, 459). -sŏy m. a kind of nettle, used as a remedy for indigestion and for worms in children. Cf. sŏy.
(? cf. گندم گون) m. gipsywort, Lycopus Europæus (El.).
adj. c.g. worthy of being tied (Gr.Gr. 129), hence (of clothes, ornaments, or the like) fit to be worn.

m. a certain kind of Hindū demi- god, a Gandharva, a celestial chorister (Śiv. 733, 1523); cf. gandur. gandarva-kanyā  f. (sg. dat. -kanyāyĕ), a daughter of the Gandharvas, a Gandharva virgin (Śiv. 1453). -lūkh m.pl. the Gandharva people, Gandharvas (Śiv. 800, 1116); the worlds of the Gandharvas, the heaven inhabited by them.
m. (sg. dat. gandakas), sulphur; ? light yellow (L. 459, gandak). ¶ gandakh-kān f. a sulphur-mine. -wôñᵘ m. sulphur-water, water smelling of sulphur, such as that which issues from a sulphur-mine.
adj. (f. ganḍᵘ̈jᵘ̈, or ganḍᵃ̇jᵃ̇), knotted, not untied; hence, whole, complete, not divided; wholesale (a term used in selling things) (Gr.Gr. 145).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gônḍᵘ; 2 p.p. gānjyōv), a verb found only in El., i.q. ganḍun 2, q.v.

m. knotting, binding, the act of binding; betrothal, the ceremony of betrothal (El.); things tied on the body, clothing, dress (K.Pr. 161, 260, W. 149); esp. fine clothes, handsome apparel (Śiv. 60). Properly the inf. of ganḍun 2 in special senses. ¶ ganḍan-böth m. (sg. dat. -bötas), asking an unanswerable question, setting an impossible task. -gorᵘ m. a bookbinder (Gr.Gr. 149). His wife is ganḍan- gȧrⁱ-bāy.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. gonḍᵘ, f.pl. ganjĕ; 2 p.p. ganjyōv Gr.Gr. 209, 225) to knot, tie, to tie up; to bind (a prisoner), to fetter (YZ. 134, 481; Śiv. 1395, 1705; Rām. 705, 818); to fix, fasten (Śiv. 1109, with a nail); to fasten together (YZ. 420); to bind (a book); to build, construct (Rām. 311, 794, 795, 797, a causeway; 48, a path; 799, a wall); to fasten (a necklace, or the like) (H. v. 12, Śiv. 812, 1204); to fasten (on to the body), to put on or wear (clothes) (K.Pr. 51, 126; Śiv, 535; Rām. 1591), (a crown) (Rām. 1738), (or a weapon) (Rām. 38); to make fast (a boat to anything) (Gr.M.); to yoke (El., Śiv. 1859); to entangle (El.); to stop (a chariot or the like) (Śiv. 1154). dāwāh ganḍun, m.inf. to put forward a claim, to present a plaint in a court of justice or before a king (H. v, 11); gulⁱ ganḍȧnⁱ, m. pl. inf., see gulᵘ; holᵘ ganḍun (K.Pr. 83, Rām. 1462), kamar (Rām. 127) or kambar (Rām. 882) ganḍun, m.inf. to tighten the waistband, to gird up the loins; küñᵘ̈ ganḍith koli ʦhunun, m.inf. to tie a stone to something and fling it into a river, esp. of abandoning children in this way (Rām. 352, 1037, 1587); lār ganḍüñᵘ̈, f.inf. to put to flight and pursue, to chase (K.Pr. 3); man ganḍun, m.inf. to fix the mind (on something) (Rām. 90, 1134, 1684); nār ganḍun, m.inf. (Rām. 378, 507, 715, 725, 739, 1484, 1610), or rĕh ganḍüñᵘ̈, f.inf. (Rām. 391, 725, 1784), to set fire to, to set on fire; zātukh ganḍun, m.inf. to draw up a horoscope (Rām. 86, 1275). ¶ ganḍan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f.-wājĕñ) one who ties, binds, etc.; esp. the man who frames the tölīm, or paper of instructions according to which shawl-weavers work out a given pattern (El.). Cf. gul-ĕ tölim, s.v. gul 1, and tölīm.
m. (sg. dat. gandaras) a kind of demigod, a Gandharva, a celestial minstrel (Śiv. 434), cf. gandarv; met. a youth, a fine young stripling, esp. one who is good-looking, brave, and strong. Cf. gandᵃr.
m. the larynx, Adam's apple. ganḍȧrⁱ-wadal f. 'distress in the larynx', serious injury from a fall (so that the middle of the body is, as it were, all dislocated).
f. a fine-looking damsel, a good- looking fine healthy young girl. Cf. gandur.
f. a lump (root) of green ginger or similar plant.
m. thickness (Śiv. 1068); thickness, crowdedness (e.g. of a grove of trees or threads woven into cloth); thickness (of curdled milk, etc.). Abs. noun of gonᵘ 2 in all its meanings.

(Śiv. 1278) or gȧnⁱsh (Śiv. 1160), m. N. of a certain Hindū god, Gaṇēśa. He was the son of Śiva and Pārvatī and was the god of wisdom and of obstacles. In the latter capacity he is invoked, at the commencement of all undertakings and at the opening of all literary compositions, for the removal of obstacles to a successful conclusion. He is the leader of the gaṇas or demigods who attend on Śiva (see gan 3). ¶ gȧnⁱshĕ-bal m. N. of a bathing-place sacred to Gaṇēśa (Śiv. 1160). -ṭujⁱ f. a small stone worshipped as a representation of the Hindū god Gaṇēśa, usually of a red colour.
or ganith m. (sg. dat. ganĕtas), mathematics, astronomy (a Hindū word), astrology. -waturᵘ m. an almanac, esp. one adapted for astronomical or astrological use.

f. the Ganges (Rām. 605), including any holy stream locally considered as equivalent to the Ganges. Thus the River Sind (Sindhu) of Kashmīr is so identified (RT.Tr. 335); met. an excavation, a hole, a pit (see bel.); a rat-hole (K.Pr. 63). --khanüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to dig the Ganges'; to pick holes in a person, to calumniate him to his superiors; to commence preparations for compassing a person's ruin, to dig a met. pitfall (Rām. 343, in which Rāvaṇa is described as digging a pitfall and falling into it himself). --nērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'the Ganges to come forth'; to be in lucrative employment, from which one is likely repeatedly to obtain money. ¶ ganga-āra m. the Ganges hill stream, the head-waters of the Ganges (Śiv. 1075, 1884) or of the River Sind, which flow from the Uttaramānasa Lake. See ganga-bal, bel. -aiṭham or -öṭham f. the eighth day of the light half of the month of Bādᵃrapĕth (Skt. Bhādra- pada = August-September), on which Kāshmīrī Hindūs visit Uttaramānasa on pilgrimage. See the next (L. 263, 266). -bal m. any place of pilgrimage on the Ganges, esp. the famous lake on Mount Haramŏkh (Skt. Haramukuṭa) known as Uttaramānasa, Uttaragaṅgā, or (in Kāshmīrī) Ganga-bal. This is looked upon as the source of the Kashmīr Ganges or Sind River, and on the Ganga- aiṭham (see ab.) it is visited by thousands of Hindū pilgrims who deposit in the sacred waters the bones of those who died during the year (see El. s.v.; RT.Tr. II, 407; K.Pr. 178, 202; Śiv. 1634; Rām. 250). -jaṭa m. matted locks (full) of the Ganges, i.e. the matted locks of the god Śiva (Śiv. 1258, 1893). According to legend the Ganges in its descent from heaven first alighted on Śiva's head, and continued for a long period entangled in his hair. Cf. jaṭa- gangā (Śiv. 188), the Ganges of (Śiva's) matted locks. -jaṭan m., i.q. -jaṭa (Śiv. 359); N. of a sacred place in the west of Bīru Pargana in Kashmīr, visited by pilgrims on the Ganga-aiṭham (see ab.) (Śiv. 1173, or m.c. jaṭönē, 359, 366). El. s.v. puts it in the Dūnʦ Pargana. -më̆ʦᵘ̈ f. sacred earth from the banks of the Gang (or Sind) River, kept in Hindū houses for ceremonial purposes. -wôñᵘ m. the water of the Ganges, Ganges water (Gr.Gr. 73, Śiv. 1309). -vĕs f. the Gangā-friend, an unmarried girl relation who is placed near a bride in the marriage ceremony to ward off ill-luck. -zal m., i.q. ganga-wôñᵘ ab. (Śiv. 1096).

f. the River Ganges (Gr.Gr. 176, 199; Gr.M.; Śiv. 213, etc.; Rām. 111, 112, 1754); (K.Pr. 65, gara-manz gangā, Ganges in the house, i.e. good fortune comes to him who stays at home); i.q. ganga-bal (K.Pr. 202), q.v. under gang. -dar  or -dār  m. he who bears the Ganges on his head, N. of Śiva. Cf. ganga-jaṭa, s.v. gang (-dar, Śiv. 37, 155, 233, 859, 988, 1096, 1177, 1780; -dār, Śiv. 71, 209, 413, 1075, 1577, 1840, 1893). -sāgar 1 m. N. of the confluence of the Ganges with the sea, the mouth of the Ganges, a famous place of pilgrimage; -sāgar 2 f. a kind of pot carried by ascetics (Śiv. 1096, 1150). -mātā f. Mother Ganges, N. of the Ganges (Śiv. 205).
f. an oath, in token of the truth of a statement, taken by touching Ganges water. -ṭyokᵘ m. a mark placed on the forehead of one who takes such an oath.
m. the large brush with which the warp is arranged (El. gangain).
f. a kind of metal water-pot, with a lid and spout, after the fashion of a teapot.
f. (sg. dat. ganiki), a kind of wild fruit, small, red, and in shape globular, growing on a thorny shrub.

adj. c.g. and subst.m. (Rām. 1177), considered as plunder, spoil, booty (K.Pr. 67); a boon, blessing, a godsend; looked upon as a piece of good luck (Rām. 663); something looked upon as valuable which one would not easily get in circumstances other than the present (Śiv. 1444, 1714; Rām. 13, 14); hence, easy to be got (at the present time) (Rām. 331, 691, 836, 1460, 1531); a good opportunity (for doing something) (Rām. 1177).
m. a store, hoard, treasure (K.Pr. 257, Siv. 430); a magazine, granary, storehouse; an emporium, market, place of merchandise.
m. a bell, a gong (Śiv. 1729, 1847); an hour (marked by striking a gong) (Gr.M.). --bajawunuy -- adv. as the clock strikes (Gr.M.).
f. the form which the letter ka takes in the Śāradā character when it is the first member of a compound consonant, as in kta.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ganyōv), to become thick (of liquids) (Śiv. 1006, 1202); to be strong (El., ? YZ. 91); to be steadfast, confirmed (e.g. of love, a desire, or a habit) (Śiv. 662, 795, 1757); to be firmly fixed, steadfast (e.g. God in the worshipper's heart) (Śiv. 1437, 1649).
f. a large piece of the felled trunk of a tree which has been split off for cutting into firewood, etc. Cf. gan 1 and güñᵘ̈ 1.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. gạnzᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. gạnzᵃrun, q.v., to count (Gr.Gr. xviii, Śiv. 74, 353, 532, etc., Rām. 355); to cause to count (El.); to consider as, look upon as (such and such) (Rām. 173, 383, 1638).

conj.1 (1 p.p.gạnzᵒrᵒ), to calculate, number, count (El.; Gr.Gr. xviii; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 50, 155; YZ. 310; Śiv. 479, 886, 1653; Rām. 551, 738); to count as, consider as, look upon as (such and such) (Rām. 499, 1438, 1447); to consider (a subject), to think about (Śiv. 1310; Rām. 137, 1241, 1351, 1434, 1674); to consider, reflect (Rām. 768, 957, 1116, 1249, 1285, 1663).
f. (sg. dat. -ʦŏdöshᵘ̈), the fourteenth day of the light half of the month of Wāhĕkh (Skt. Vaiśākha = April-May), on which Hindūs celebrate the festival of the god Gaṇēśa.

m. a kind of rice, used both for eating and also by Brāhmaṇas for making parched grain for use in religious ceremonies. The burnt stalks of this rice make pearl ashes, used by washermen for cleaning clothes, hence the word is used to mean also 'pearl ashes' (El.); Amaranthus anardana and gangeticus (El.). See L. 78, 330, 338. -kã̄ḍ m. its stalk, the ashes of which are used as ab.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gạñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), to make thick, to make solid; to make firm, to make steadfast, to confirm (Śiv. 740, 1389).
or gaflath غفلت f. (sg. dat. gaphlüʦᵘ̈), neglect, indifference (Gr.M.). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to treat with indifference, be neglectful (Gr.M., Rām. 1639).
m. a maker, workman, used as a suff., e.g. zar-gar, a worker in gold, a goldsmith; i.q. gorᵘ 3, q.v.
a form often assumed by gara, q.v., in comps.

m. N. of a certain poisonous plant. --ʦāpun -- m.inf. to gnaw gār; met. to be reduced to the extremest straits for food, to have scarcely anything to eat; to fast (as a religious act), to starve oneself (Rām. 1573). --raṭun -- m.inf., id. (Rām. 1577).
f. a cave, cavern, pit, hollow, den, grotto (Śiv. 410, Rām. 461-3, 467).

m. (this word often assumes the form gar in comps., see bel.), a house, a dwelling (K.Pr. 26, 65-8, 119, 153, 255; YZ. 249, 467; W. 11; Śiv. 34, 82, 83, etc.; Rām. 115, 136, etc.); a home (Rām. 1370); a room (in a house); a den, nest, hole, burrow (of any animal); a case, holder, receptacle (Gr.M.); the frame of a picture (Gr.M.); a socket, a groove; a compartment, cell, square (of a chessboard, etc.); column (in a register, etc.). --aʦun -- m.inf. to enter a (new) house (done at an auspicious moment, with religious ceremonies). --aʦan bôgᵘ-- m. a present given to the bridegroom's parents, etc., by the parents of the bride when the latter first enter the former's house, or by the former when they first enter the latter's house, i.q. gar-aʦawañ, bel. -bār m. house and door, house and home; family, household (Rām. 813, 829). -bār karun m.inf. to keep house and home, to support a family, be a householder. -drāv adj. (f. -drāyĕ), gone forth from the house, esp. of one who is absent from home against his will. --karun -- m.inf. to build a house; met. to make a family, to act as a wife to a husband or as a husband to a wife. -pata adv. in every house, in each house (K.Pr. 29). -pĕṭh, i.q. gar-pĕṭh, bel. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause to enter a house, to invite one's relations or connexions by marriage to a festival in one's house. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a housekeeper, householder, master (or mistress) of a house; one who owns a house or houses. Cf. gar-wôlᵘ bel., which means the master of a house (Gr.Gr. 136). -wara m. a house and its appurtenances, a house (El.). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to go home, to return home (K.Pr. 153; H. v, passim). ¶ gar-aʦawañ f., i.q. gara-aʦan bôgᵘ, ab. -bugiñ f. the mistress of a house, the real owner-mistress of a house, as opposed to anyone else living in the house who is apparently the owner. -bugiy m. the master of a house, the real owner of a house, as opposed to anyone living in it who is apparently, but not really, the owner. -bāra m., i.q. gara-bār (ab.) (Rām. 469). -divatā or -dayotᵘ m. the tutelary deity of a house, to whom Hindūs make sacrificial offerings in the month of Pŏh (Skt. Pauṣa = December-January). -godᵘ m. a house-hole; met. the hole through which one's money goes, the expenses of carrying on a house. -gunḍa m. a great man in a house, a house bully, one who hectors and bullies in his own house, but is meek and a coward out of doors; a lazy master of a house (K.Pr. 65). Cf. gọ̆nḍᵘ 2. -göñᵘ̈ f. a house-prostitute, a private prostitute who plies her trade in her own house and does not publicly solicit. -grākh n.ag. (f. -grākañ), the head of a house, the person who is responsible for the carrying on of a household. -gar karun 1 m.inf. (for 2 see s.v. gar-gara), to do house-house, to go from house to house (for begging, to pass the time, etc.). -gar kuʦurᵘ m. (f. --kuʦürᵘ̈ -- see the next), a house-to-house puppy, a fellow who habitually goes from house to house, esp. a greedy fellow, who does this in the hope of filling his belly. -gar kuʦürᵘ̈ f. a house-to-house bitch, a woman who habitually goes begging from house to house; an unchaste woman who goes from house to house. -kulⁱ adj. c.g. home- made, suitable only to be sold or bought at home, as contrasted with things sold and bought in the market. -nāway f. the cleaning of the house; (in a Hindū family) the cleaning and whitewashing of the reception-rooms of a house some eight or ten days before a festival such as a marriage or investiture with the sacred thread. An auspicious moment is selected for its commencement. (Cf. El. s.v. garanáwai.) -pĕṭh or gara-pĕṭh adv. on the house, in the house, (with verbs of motion) to the house; as subst.m. the 'to-the-house', bringing a daughter's husband to live in her parents' home, instead of his taking her to his own parents' home, cf. and-pĕṭh s.v. and, of which this is the converse. -shānth f. (s.g. dat. -shönʦᵘ̈), 'peace in the house,' a Hindū ceremony of making offerings to the tutelary deity of the house, for securing peace and prosperity therein. -sipāh or -sipôyᵘ m. a house-soldier, one who is a great hero and bully in his own house but meek and cowardly outside. -ʦhöḍᵘ̈, -ʦhö̃ḍᵘ̈, or-ʦhönḍᵘ̈ f. house-search, searching a house, esp. another's house, for lost and stolen property. -ʦhāḍay f. searching for lost property, etc., only in the house (and not outside).-ʦūr m. a house thief, a thief (e.g. a servant or a member of the family) who steals in the house in which he is employed or lives. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ Gr.Gr. 38,39), a house- holder, the head or master (mistress) of a house (Gr.Gr. 135, K.Pr. 204); the title by which such a person's wife refers to her husband, or (in f.) the title by which such a person refers to his wife. Cf. gara-wôlᵘ ab., which means the possessor of a house. -wār m. liking for or suitability for household work, a taste for housekeeping. -vīrᵘ̈ f. a house-lizard. To hear its voice is a good omen. -vēṭh f. household utensils, in the shape of pots, pans, pestles, mortars, and the like. -warzukh m. (sg. dat. -warzakas; f. -warzücᵘ̈), one who keeps a house in good order, clean, tidy, and with economy; a good house-master or housewife. ¶ gȧrⁱ bë̆ñᵘ̈ f. a woman who is apart in (her own) house, i.e. who stays at home and has not to go out to earn her living; a lady-like woman, a thorough lady; a woman who stays at home because she is too poor to go out and buy things. -börⁱ adv. with all one's family and household goods, u.w. vbs. of going, etc. ¶ gari 1 adv. (for 2 see gürᵘ̈ 1) in the house, at home (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 66, 67, 71, 120, 123, 163; W. 144; Śiv. 35, 56, 411, etc.); from the house (K.Pr. 68, in 57 spelt gare; Śiv. 576, 1622, 1836; garē, m.c. 1723). ¶ garukᵘ adj. (f. garücᵘ̈), of or belonging to a house, domestic (Gr.Gr. 151); produced in a house, esp. when the speaker is referring to his own house, or to the house of a person whom he is addressing or who is within sight; garukᵘ ṭhikāna, m. a person's address (Gr.M.); m.pl. garȧkⁱ, the people of a house, the family (Gr.M.).
m. translated 'passer' or 'sparrow' in YZ. 409. ? Cf. görᵘ̈ 1. The word, however, is probably garāh; see gürᵘ̈ 1.
f. continued longing, unsatisfied even by obtaining the desired object, but still wishing for more and more. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such unsatisfied longing to occur.
adj. c.g. honoured, respected (on account of one's virtues, wealth, lineage, etc.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. garanôwᵘ), to cause to be made, to get made, to make (with help) (H. xi, 17).
n.ag. (f. gārawüñᵘ̈), one who searches eagerly for anything (Śiv. 206).

m. the womb; the being with child; the inside, interior (of a box or the like). ¶ garba-gã̄ḍay m. making a relationship by marriage (while the children are) in the womb. This occurs when two women friends find themselves in the family way at the same time, and agree that if one child turns out to be a boy and the other a girl the two shall marry. -jōsh m. distress of the womb (felt by a woman from the seventh month of her pregnancy up to her confinement). -kuṭhᵘ m. the central room of a house, the drawing-room. -ṭhēla m. the womb (El.). -zāl m. the net of the womb, the integument covering the womb. -zyuṭhᵘ adj. (f.-ziṭhᵘ̈), the eldest from the womb, a woman's first child.

f. (sg. dat.gardüñᵘ̈, Rām. 16, 825, 850, 853), the neck (K.Pr. 73, YZ. 146, Rām. 37, 299, 370, etc.); met. decapitation, beheading (K.Pr. 27). --diñᵘ̈ --  f.inf. to decapitate, behead (Rām. 816; H. ii, 8, tas, him). ¶ gardañĕ ganḍ m. the articulation of the neck, a name given to the nape of the neck, the cervical ligament.
f. wandering, change; revolution; --˚ downfall, misfortune, affliction; (in Kāshmīrī) a circle (El.).
or gardīsh (? f.), turning round, circulation, revolution. gardīshhāyĕayām = گردشہائی ایام the revolutions of days, cycles of time (Rām. 132).
m.onomat. gargling. gar-gar karun 2 m.inf. (for 1 see s.v. gara, p. 295b, l. 38), to gargle.
adj. c.g. poor, destitute (K.Pr. 66, 75; W. 118; YZ. 241; Rām. 72, 141, 1135, 1734, 1739); meek, mild; humble, lowly.
f. poverty, indigence; meekness, mildness, lowliness, humility.
adj. c.g. one who is affected by continual longing, unsatisfied even by the attainment of the desired object, but who is still wishing for more and more.
f. a good housewife, a woman who manages her house well (Gr.Gr. 38).
f. an unconscientious woman (?), only noted in K.Pr. 132 (garin), where it is so translated.

adj. c.g. hot, warm (W. 112, Rām. 1198); in a state of heat; fervid, ardent, zealous; fiery, choleric; warm, rich (e.g. a man or a place of pilgrimage) (K.Pr. 236); active, lively, brisk (as a market) (Rām. 139); (of news) exciting, arousing, causing energy (Rām. 777, 798); as subst. the hot season.
f. heat, warmth (W. 112, Siv. 27); hot weather, the hot season; activity, briskness, fierceness, vehemence; sexual passion, lust, heat; fever, the venereal disease.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. garmyōv), to be hot (Gr.Gr. xviii).
f. weight, burden; heaviness, gravity; heaviness of spirit, depression, grief, vexation (Rām. 1461); scarceness, scarcity, dearth, dearness.

m. Garuḍa, N. of a bird celebrated in Hindū myth as chief of the feathered race and enemy of the serpent race. He was the vehicle of the god Viṣṇu (Vishnu) (Śiv. 720, 732, 793, 1324; Rām. 398, 598, 600).
m. he who sits upon Garuḍa, i.e. whose vehicle is Garuḍa (see garuḍ), N. of the Hindū god Viṣṇu (Vishnu) (Śiv. 160, 1407).

or gaḍun conj. 1 (1 p.p. gorᵘ 4 or goḍᵘ, for 1, 2, 3 see s.vv.), to make, form, fashion, put together (as a carpenter); to forge, to work metals (H. v, 5); to malleate, to mould. kalam garun, to mend a pen (Gr.M.). -ʦarun m.inf. a jingling repetition of garun, to make and prepare, to do all the work necessary in the preparation of anything (e.g. a brazen vessel or an ornament). ¶ gorᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. gürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made, prepared, fashioned, forged, etc. (K.Pr. 73, 173, Śiv. 280). ¶ garanay neg. conj. part. not having made (Gr.Gr. 111); as adj. c.g. not made, not yet made, not yet hammered out into shape. ¶ garana yunᵘ m. inf. pass., lit. to be made, to be hammered into shape; met. (of living beings) to be hardened, to become obstinate in refusing to do anything, to jib; (of things or actions) to be hard, difficult (Gr.Gr. 169).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. gôrᵘ 2, for 1 see s.v.), to search eagerly for (Rām. 439, 1487); to remember affectionately, to miss (a friend), every now and then to think of a person and long for his presence and assistance; to inquire (El.); to search (L. 463). ¶ gôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. görᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), missed, longed for, as ab.
m. a wooden stand for supporting a water-jar (Hindī ghaṛō̃cā).

f. (sg.dat. gardi), dust (Gr.M., K.Pr. 50). -banga f. a drug extracted from the female hemp plant, a kind of charas (L. 67). ¶ gardi gaʦhun m.inf. to become dusty. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), dusty, full of dust.

or garath m. (sg. dat. gartas or garatas), the forming, fashioning, forging, hammering out of anything; hence (of any manufactured metal article), the ultimate manufactured shape, the form, shape, fashion; the model or fashion according to which a thing is to be made. Cf. garun and Gr.Gr. 128. The word is reported to be m., though most words ending in ath are f. Cf., however, waṭath.

or garaz غرض m. (sg. abl. garza H. vii, 26, garaza Rām. 651), an aim, end, object (Gr.M.); design, view, purpose, intention (H. vii, 26, Śiv. 572, Rām. 107); interest, concern, connexion (with anything) (Gr.M.). Regarding the gender of this word (which in Hindōstānī is f.), see W. 18. As adv., also (Rām. 651) garaza, in short, in a word, in fine (Rām. 432, 664, 373). -mand غرضمند adj. c.g. concerned, interested; selfish, designing (K.Pr. 66, Rām. 1150). Cf. bē-garaz and K.Pr. 235.
adj. c.g. drowned, immersed; met. overwhelmed (with), buried (in), smothered (in) (something material) (Rām. 141, buried under heaps of gold).
m. a bell-ringer, a man whose business it is to strike a gong at certain hours of the day (K.Pr. 67, W. 154); a small bell (El.).

m. rubbing down, grinding between two stones (e.g. of sandal-wood) (Gr.Gr. 124). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to grind down, rub down, abrade, rub smooth; to criticize a person over and over again. ¶ gasa āmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), worn down, worn away by constant use. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be worn away by constant use.
for gāsa, in the following: gās-phūs m. old dry grass or straw; weeds; met. (of clothes or used papers) worthless, only fit to be thrown away.

m. grass (K.Pr. 252; Śiv. 197, 1049; Rām. 96, 449, 1631; H. x, 5; xi, 6, 7); hay; straw; fodder; weeds; a plant of the grass kind, a grass (Rām. 883). nākāra gāsa, weeds (Gr.M.). -örᵘ̈ f. a ring made of a wisp of grass fastened up with string, used for supporting globular vessels. -bonᵘ m. a pile of grass, a hay-rick. -banna f. a pile or rick of straw or grass gradually formed by additions from time to time. -bôrᵘ m. a load of grass, carried on the head, or deposited for sale on the ground. -bạrᵃg m. a leaf of grass; a small amount of grass, etc., just a little hay or straw (Rām. 1519). -ḍongᵘ m. a grass-platform built in trees on which articles are kept for safety. -dyār m.pl. money for cutting grass (K.Pr. 33). -gë̆ḍᵘ̈ f. a bundle similar to the next, but smaller, composed of six handfuls (K.Pr. 80). Cf. -khorᵘ, bel. -gyoḍᵘ m. a bundle of grass or the like made up for fodder or for sale. -khorᵘ m. a bundle of twelve tied-up handfuls of rice-straw, with the grain (K.Pr. 32). Cf. -gë̆ḍᵘ̈, ab. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat grass, to graze (El., K.Pr. 105, W. 87, Śiv. 1464). -khë̆shᵘ̈ f. a small bundle of rice-straw, etc., esp. as much as is grasped in the hand at one time. -köñᵘ̈ f. a small pile of rice-straw or the like. -koṭᵘ m. the sprout or young stalk of a rice plant, etc., a blade of grass (Śiv. 1049). -küṭᵘ̈ f. a single long straw of paddy, etc. -lŏʦhürᵘ̈ f. a bundle of straw, etc., tied in the middle, a sheaf. -lôvᵘ m. a handful of straw grasped near the root (H. xi, 12). -nambal f. a swampy piece of land growing grass suitable for fodder. -nār m. a straw or grass fire; the straw that remains unburnt in such a fire. -pahörᵘ̈ f. a grass hut, a hut built of, or thatched with, grass, straw, etc. -pulahorᵘ m. grass-sandals, sandals made of grass. They are worn on the mountains. -raz m. a straw rope (H. xi, 9). -thôpᵘ m. a bundle of grass, straw, etc. -tᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. the inner shaft of a paddy-straw, the stem after removing the outer cortex. -tulᵘ m. a single straw, a stem of grass, etc.; met. a small amount of straw, etc. -zanḍ m. a quantity of straw, without reference to the amount. ¶ gösⁱ gaʦhun m. (of a field) to become covered with weeds; met. to become very lazy (K.Pr. 105, ghás, wrongly translated 'lustful').
f. mutual rubbing or grinding together (e.g. of two millstones); met. mutual conversation.

m. fainting, becoming insensible, swoon (e.g. from hunger, grief, etc.) (Śiv. 499, 1454, Rām. 396). --gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. faintings or insensibility to occur, esp. of coma when a person is at the point of death, or of fainting from extreme hunger.

or gwāsh (H. viii, 9) m. brightness, brilliancy (Śiv. 908); lustre, light (K.Pr. 254, Śiv. 15, 251, 314, etc., Rām. 417); daybreak (K.Pr. 176, Rām. 679, 798); daylight (L. 459, Śiv. 1192); enlightening, light that dispels darkness (e.g. of the rising sun or a lamp) (YZ. 175); clearness, brightness (of the eye) (Śiv. 331, 1125; Rām. 200, 671, 1174, 1192); eyesight, power of sight (YZ. 417, 457; Rām. 229, 772, 1103, 1114); the light (of a house), a beloved son (Rām. 236); light, joy after grief, consolation (Rām. 903, 1102); achĕn-hondᵘ gāsh, light of the eyes, brightness of the eyes, eyesight; met. a darling, a beloved person, e.g. a son, a brother, or the like (Rām. 194, 238, 247, 257, 529, 1228); a very great treasure, a treasured possession (Rām. 1523); cĕshman- hondᵘ gāsh, id. (Rām. 495). Cf. gāh 1. El. spells this word both gásh and gãsh (i.e. gösh). --anun -- m.inf. to bring light, to illuminate (Śiv. 1558); to brighten, bring light to (Śiv. 1595, 1736); met. to explain. --phŏlun -- or --phŏllun -- m.inf. light to blossom, dawn to come (Rām. 295, 1636; H. iii, 3; v, 5, 7; viii, 9; xii, 2). --phŏlawunᵘ -- or --phollawunᵘ -- adv. immediately on the flowering of light, i.e. at early dawn (Gr.M., Rām. 1105, 1109). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. light to come, illumination to occur (in the midst of or after darkness) (Śiv. 1358, 1710, Rām. 4); dawn to come (Rām. 1257, 1264, 1533); darkness to be cleared away by a lamp, etc.; met. knowledge to be gained, the darkness of ignorance to be swept away, mental illumination to come (Rām. 59). --yiwawunᵘ -- adv. immediately on the coming of light, at dawn. ¶ gāshĕ-brôrᵘ m. 'the god of light', the light of dawn. -brörᵘ̈ f. the goddess of light, N. of a conspicuous peak in Lahar Pargana (see RT.Tr. II, 410). It is sacred to Mahādēva, and is said to be brilliant with crystal rocks. -lᵃth f. (sg. dat. -lᵃti, Gr.Gr. 162), a very little light (e.g. of an oil wick or of a star) (Gr.Gr. 162); a dim light of the eyes, dimness of vision. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), deprived of light, dark; without lustre, without brightness, dim (Śiv. 157, 1192); (of the eyes) dim, blind (K.Pr. 1, YZ. 156, 431). -tārukh m. (sg. dat. -tārakas), the morning star. -wọ̆bᵘ m. a small window to give light and air to a dark room.
adj. c.g. rubbed away, worn away, worn thin (e.g. a coin).
m. silence (Gr.Gr. 138), esp. acting with heedlessness of consequences, even though warned beforehand. Cf. goshᵘ 1 and 2.
m. brightness, brilliancy, voc. gāshĕra, O thou who art brightness personified! (Rām. 217).
f. a woman who behaves as if she were a prostitute, one disposed to unchastity.
adj. c.g. rubbed down, worn down, with the impression worn off (of a coin or the like).
m. the time of brightness, i.e. either the light of early dawn or just before nightfall, twilight.
f. (sg. dat. (?) güshᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), an unchaste woman, esp. one who is such with some discretion, a woman disposed to unchastity.
f. (sg. dat. gasīṭi), the condition of being crowded or tightly packed (of a room, a receptacle, etc.).
adj. (f. gāsüvᵘ̈), made of straw or grass; met. of no value, worthless (K.Pr. 18).

m. profound insensibility, a dead faint, being like one dead. --mārȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. 'to strike faintings', nearly to die over and over again; met. (with reference to an insect fluttering round a candle at the risk of its life) to walk round and round a thing to inspect it, to be fascinated or infatuated by anything so that one cannot leave it, but must admire it on all sides and long for it (Śiv. 1609; K.Pr. 42, of a man flaunting his clothes, mārān gatai for gata-y). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. fainting to occur (generally). ¶ gatan aʦun m.inf. to enter dead faints, to become comatose when at the point of death.

f. darkness, obscurity (K.Pr. 67, 193; Siv. 104, 1040, 1066; Rām. 295, 417, 1596, 1610); the shade or darkness thrown by dense black clouds. Cf. Gr.Gr. 72. Cf. añi-gaṭa, p. 31a, l. 16, and Rām. 92, 1257. -kār m. darkness, gloom (K.Pr. 253, L. 456, Rām. 1035); met. violence, tyranny, oppression. -kārunᵘ pahar m. the watch of oppression; met. a short time (lit. a watch of three hours) of terrible calamity (such as that occupied by a fierce and bloody battle, an earthquake, or the like). -kārunᵘ tāph m. (sg. dat. -karanas tāpas), violent and distressing heat of the sun. -pach m. (sg. dat. -pachas), the dark fortnight of a lunar month, the fortnight of the waning moon (L. 354, Śiv. 166). -zolᵘ m. a dull light, very little light, a glimmer of light just showing on a dark night or through black clouds.

m. skill, cleverness, intelligence; wisdom, discrimination, judgment (K.Pr. 87, 218; Śiv. 1212, with pun on gāṭa 2; H. i, 6). -ȧthⁱ adv. with the hand of skill, cleverly, intelligently, skilfully. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give wisdom, to teach (El.). --ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ -- f. conceit for one's own cleverness (whether entitled to entertain such conceit or not); having a high opinion of one's own wisdom or cleverness.
m. falling short, insufficiency, failure, want (Śiv. 1212, with pun on gāṭa 1). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. falling short to occur; expectations to fall short, loss to occur in place of profit.
m. wisdom, cleverness, skilfulness; vigilance, prudence (El.). gāṭajyārukᵘ jawāb, an answer of intelligence, a pertinent answer (Gr.M.).
f. (sg. dat. gaṭaki), darkness; esp. spiritual darkness (L.V. 104).
adj. c.g. blackened, darkened, disgraced (of personal character, family, etc.).
m. being hacked or cut to pieces (esp. w. reference to the limbs of a human being). Cf. güñᵘ̈ 1.

m. (sg. dat. gaṭāṭōpas), a covering for a palanquin, carriage, or any article of furniture, etc. (so as to shade or darken it); met. a tumult, a terribly involved battle (in which darkness, preventing recognition of friend or foe, is caused by the confused multitude of combatants).

m. (sg. dat. gātas), a blot, stain (in character) (Śiv. 1554, Rām. 1667); disgrace (in a family). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give a stain; to bring a disgraceful charge (justified or unjustified) against a person.

m. (sg. dat. gāṭhas), a landing-place, ghaut, quay, wharf, a place on the bank of a river where boats stop to discharge or take in goods or passengers (K.Pr. 58, W. 153, Śiv. 1806); a ferry, ford; a bathing-place, or a place for washing clothes (on the bank of a river). -dār m. the man in charge of a landing-place, who collects the harbour dues, a harbour-master. -dörī f. the fee or tax paid at a landing-place, harbour dues. -dār-bāy f. the wife of a harbour-master. -dārĕñ f. a woman who acts as harbour-master, a harbour-mistress. ¶ gāṭha-hūnᵘ m. (f. -hūñᵘ̈), the dog at a landing-place (that prowls around eating what it can pick up) (K.Pr. 68); met. a person, clever enough but without application, who wanders about from place to place and does not succeed in making any profit. -wôlᵘ m. a boatman who sticks to the river bank (and does not go off to work in his boat).
m. a knot (K.Pr. 76), see bar 1, p. 116b, l. 40.

m. (sg. dat. gatas), going, the act of going (i.q. gath 3), esp. --˚ in ata-gath 1 and 2 (q.v.), coming and going (Śiv. 1364, 1808); a turning round, a revolution (El., K.Pr. 128). --karun -- m.inf. to revolve (El.).
m. (sg. dat. gatas), a goer, used --˚ as in wata-gath, a road-goer, a traveller (Gr.M., Śiv. 1829).
m. (sg. dat. gaṭas), the stem of a huqqa, connecting the fire-bowl with the water-receptacle.

f. (sg. dat. güʦᵘ̈, Śiv. 1364, Rām. 1426), going, moving, gait, deportment, motion in general; march, going, progress, movement; a means of success, way; state, condition (vaikunṭha- gath, the condition of heaven, i.e. a condition the same as that of heaven, Śiv. 997); the way, conduct, mighty works (of God) (K.Pr. 102, Rām. 567); refuge, resource; the course of the soul through existence [parama-gath, the supreme course, final beatitude, salvation (Śiv. 19, 102, 1539, 1781, etc.); so gath alone, the way of salvation, beatitude (Śiv. 161, 674, 884, 1759)]; a happy condition, bliss generally (Śiv. 1098, 1246, 1710); dayĕ-gath, the way of God, God's majesty (Śiv. 1652, 1787, Rām. 122), a piece of good luck, bliss granted by God (Śiv. 693, Rām. 1296), the way approved by God, a holy life (Rām. 30). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to die after another (e.g. a widow becoming satī after her husband's death, H. iii, 4); to devote oneself to death for the sake of something (e.g. a moth for a lamp) (YZ. 430); to follow a person to the death, to be true till death.
f. a tied-up bundle, esp. of clothes or the like.
adj. (m. sg. dat. gātakas; f. gātücᵘ̈), a killer, a murderer, a destroyer. Commonly --˚.

adj. (f.gāṭᵘ̈jᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 35), wise, clever, shrewd, prudent (K.Pr. 58, 107, 210; Rām. 128, 129); skilful, expert; learned, intelligent; eloquent (El., Rām. 1279. Cf. katha-gāṭulᵘ s.v. kath). Cf. Gr.Gr. 145.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. gaṭyōv), to become less, lessen, diminish, decrease (Śiv. 1565); to become shrunken (of something green and fresh), to be shrivelled up; to become lessened (by loss of a part).
conj. 1, an old form of garun, q.v. (L.V. 80).
m. a kind of gold or silver embroidery, worn by rich women on the borders of their garments, or used as a braid on military uniforms.
conj. 1(1 p.p. gạṭᵃrôwᵃ), to make dark, to turn (light) into darkness, to turn (day) into night (Śiv. 350).
f. sorrow, grief, the pain of sorrow.
f. N. of the god Śiva's wife, Pārvatī (Śiv. 643, 655, etc.). -shĕnkar m. Gaurī and Śaṅkara, i.e. Pārvatī and Śiva, looked upon conjointly as one deity (Śiv. 197, 644).
in phĕkⁱ-gav m. a hole, a puncture, a hole (in a garment); the orifice in a ripened boil, etc., through which the purulent matter exudes.
m. currency, the being in season for sale, the frequent occurrence of buying and selling of any article (e.g. owing to its being in season, or in a country where it is an important commodity).

f. (sg. dat. gōvᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 70 K.Pr. 69, 241), a cow, a milch-cow (El. gáo) (L.V. 95; K.Pr. 68, 72, 91, 105 (voc.), 126, 242, 253; Rām. 96; H. vi, 15; xi, 12); a word, speech (Śiv. 522). --prasüñᵘ̈ -- f. inf. a cow to be born; met. a necessary occasion for the willing expenditure of money or the like to occur. ¶ gōvᵘ̈-gān m. a cow-house, cow-stable. -hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to a cow. -khyolᵘ m. a herd of cows (Gr.Gr. 152). -loṭᵘ m. a young cow (giving little milk). -zabān f. N. of a certain plant, Macrotomia Benthami, used as a medicine for the heart (L. 74, 389, gáo zabán).
in gav-rochᵘ, a cowherd (El. gau-roch). Cf. gāv 2.
sing thou, a Hindī form, used m.c. instead of gĕv in Śiv. 1721, 1812.
m. Onosma macrocephala (El. gáoza). Cf. bān 1 (p. 109b, l. 4).
f. surrounding and attacking a person (e.g. a thief, the enemy in a war, etc.), capturing by surprise. Cf. gōvᵃrun.
or gawöyⁱ 1 m. a witness, one who gives testimony of something which happened in his presence (K.Pr. 78).
adj. c.g. digesting; swallowing, putting up with; digestible; palatable, agreeable, pleasant. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be pleasant, to give rise to a pleasant sensation, to be agreeable.
m. (sg. dat. ?), the entering a person (e.g. an evil spirit entering a person, or, met., an idea, etc., to take possession of him).
m. a kind of wild deer, said to resemble a cow in form.
or gawöhī گوآہی f. evidence, testimony (H. x, 12).
f. N. of a celebrated town and place of pilgrimage in the Bihār province of India, visited by Hindūs for the purpose of making oblations to the manes of their deceased ancestors (Śiv. 627, 1495).

f. N. of a sacred verse in the Ṛgvēda (iii, 62, 10) repeated by every Brāhmaṇ at his morning and evening devotions. It is personified as the wife of Brahmā and the mother of the four Vēdas (Śiv. 1512, 1526).

m. an instrument for measuring, a yard measure (K.Pr. 221); a yard (of measure), in Kashmīr equal to about 48 finger-widths, and about half an inch longer than the British yard (L. 243; K.Pr. 43, 87, 173, 179, 249; Śiv. 1235, 1284); the khām gaz is about 15/16 of the full gaz (see khām 1); anything measurable (e.g. land, cloth, etc.) a yard in length. akh gaz zyūṭhᵘ, a yard in length (Gr.M.). ¶ gaz-pipal (? spelling), N. of a certain drug made from cones of the Himalayan spruce (L. 80). ¶ gaza-bodᵘ m. innumerable yards in length, yards and yards (e.g. of a long strip of cloth, or a road). Cf. bọ̆dᵘ 2 or bodᵘ 1 (p. 84a, l. 3). -phyurᵘ m. the turning of a yard measure, measuring over again as a check on the first measurement.
or (El.) gaza m. an elephant. ¶ gaza-mŏkh m. he who has an elephant's face, N. of the Hindū god Gaṇēśa (see Ganēsh, p. 293a, l. 26) (Śiv. 5). -ʦam m. elephant's hide (Śiv. 166, 816).
m. anger, passion, rage, fury (Rām. 1318); wrong, injustice, oppression; a curse, calamity, affliction, awful event.

(cf. Hindī gajar), m. the chimes rung at the expiration of a pahar or watch of the day or night; esp. amongst Kāshmīrī Musalmāns, those rung at the end of the fourth or last watch of the night; hence, the time just before daybreak (K.Pr. 176).
adj. c.g. capable of being measured with a measuring rod (of things for sale, e.g. cloth).

m. (sg. dat. gazēndras), a king of elephants, a noble elephant; esp. a certain famous elephant rescued (when being overpowered by a crocodile) by the Hindū god Viṣṇu under the form of Hari or Harihara, in answer to his prayer of faith. The story is often quoted as an instance of the divine graciousness of Viṣṇu (Śiv. 856, 1471).
adj. c.g. of or belonging to the town of Ghaznī (H. i, 1).
m. enraged, fearful, tremendous, dreadful; (in Kāshmīrī) excessively heavy, tremendous (of a fall of snow, or the like).

f. a carrot, Daucus carota (L. 346). It is eaten by Kāshmīrī Musalmāns, but not by Hindūs (El.). gāzᵃri-ã̄cār m. carrot pickle, pickled carrot. -pŏlāv m. a certain dish, skinned carrots cooked with seasoning of clarified butter and sugar.
m. leanness, thinness (natural or owing to disease, etc.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. -nôwᵘ), to cause (a person) to go, to despatch, send off on a message. This verb does not mean to cause to go, in the sense of driving, for which pakanāwun is used (Gr.Gr. 176).

conj. 2 (1 p.p.goʦhᵘ Gr.Gr. 113, 235), to be prope/r, right, advisable (K.Pr. 100 guts for goʦhᵘ, YZ. 191, Śiv. 1596, Rām. 19, 154, 1137); to be necessary (L.V. 19, 29, 45, K.Pr. 69, YZ. 185, Śiv. 1705); to be wanted, desired (Śiv. 1240, 1448; Rām. 591, 658, 840; goʦhum, I want, YZ. 463, Śiv. 1899; gaʦhiy, thou desirest, Śiv. 633). This verb is employed either actively or passively with the fut. p.p. of another verb to indicate propriety, necessity, or desire. It is only employed in the present, in the fut. (genl. with pres. signification), or in the past tense. For the present, see Gr.Gr. 183. See also Gr.Gr. 113. Thus:-- ¶ A. Actively (Gr.M., Gr.Gr. 113):--ȧsⁱ gaʦhav rōzȧnⁱ, we are proper to be remained, i.e. we must remain; ȧsⁱ gaʦhav dinⁱ, we must give; marun goʦhus-na, I do not wish to die (Śiv. 700); bharuth gaʦhi rāza āsunᵘ, Bharata should become king (Rām. 155); kã̄h gaʦhĕm-na ḍēshunᵘ, no one may see me (H. xii, 2). ¶ B. Passively:--Here the personal subject (when expressed) is put either in the dative or the genitive. ¶ (a) Person not expressed: --gaʦhi muāph karunᵘ, pardon to be made is proper, please pardon (Gr.M.); jān gaʦhi, good will be proper that, i.e. you had better (do so and so) (Gr.M.); gaʦhi yiʦh āsüñᵘ̈, a desire is proper to be, one should wish (yiʦh is f.) (Gr.M.); so Śiv. 75, 1448, 1713, 1752, 1753; Rām. 19, 154; H. v, 4; xii, 19, 20. In Rām. 1644 we find (1) the impersonal gaʦhi mīṭhⁱ dinⁱ, it is proper that kisses should be given, and (2) personal gaʦhan cĕnⁱ, drinkings are proper, one should sip. ¶ (b) Person in the dat. (Gr.M., Gr.Gr. 113):-- mĕ gaʦhi, there is necessary to me, I want (Gr.M.); asĕ gaʦhi rōzunᵘ, to us to remain is necessary, we must stay (Gr.M.); asĕ gaʦhi phikirᵘ̈ thawüñᵘ̈, we must take thought (Gr.M.); asĕ gaʦhan nākāragiyĕ trāwañĕ, we must abandon evil actions (Gr.M.). So Śiv. 1448; Rām. 79, 150, etc.; H. xii, 4, 5, 10, 13, etc. For examples of the use of this verb with pronominal suffixes, see Gr.Gr. 183. In the present tense the person must be indicated by a suffix if it is in the 1st pers. sg. or 2nd pers. sg. or pl. In the 3rd pers. the use of a suffix is optional. Thus tamis gaʦhān chuh (or chus) zi parahö, to him it is desirable that I should read, he thinks it proper that I should read. ¶ In other tenses when the person is the 2nd, the suffix of the dative of the pronoun must always be added to the verb, whether the full pronoun is expressed or not. Thus, yus ʦĕ gaʦhiy, (the kind) which you want (Gr.M.); so Śiv. 707, 1224, 1705; H. xii, 7, 13. ¶ (c) Person in the gen. (Gr.M., Gr.Gr. 114):-- myônᵘ gaʦhi gaʦhunᵘ, my going is proper, I must go (Gr.M.); gaʦhi cyônᵘ kōshish karüñᵘ̈, you should try (Gr.M.); cyōnⁱ gaʦhan trih jild thawȧnⁱ, you must reserve three books (Gr.M.); anugrah cyônᵘ gaʦhi āsunᵘ, thou shouldst show favour (Śiv. 1596); cyônᵘ gaʦhi zyunᵘ sŏmbᵃrunᵃ, thou must collect firewood (H. xii, 20); tuhondᵘ gaʦhi yunᵘ, you must come (H. xii, 15).

This tense has also a shortened form in the sg. 3, and pl. 1, 3, as follows:--sg. 3, gav (H. v, 8; vi, 6, 16; viii, 2; YZ. 22; K.Pr. 148; Śiv. 1239; Rām. 32, 62, 106, 209, 1152, et passim); poet. gawa گوہ (YZ. 31); pl. 1, gay (Gr.Gr. 235); 3, gay (Gr.Gr. 235; H. vi, 9; YZ. 204; Śiv. 59, 129, 686; Rām. 40, 205, 208; for me, gayĕm, Rām. 1614; for thee, etc., gạy, Gr.Gr. 236, Rām. 121, 221). f.sg. 1, gayĕs (Śiv. 484, 937; Rām. 1219, 1236); 2, gayĕkh (Śiv. 571, 832, 834, Rām. 1570); 3, gayĕ (YZ. 177, 194, 237; Śiv. 83, 86, 92; for me, etc., gayĕm, Rām. 164, 469, 687, 848; to me verily, gayᵉ̆may, H. vii, 12; for thee, gayiy, Gr.Gr. 236, gayĕy, Rām. 1446; for him, etc., gayĕs (Śiv. 431, 833, 843; Rām. 90, 183, 255; for them, etc., gayĕkh, Rām. 166, 262); pl. 1, gayĕ (Śiv. 1661); 2, gayĕwa; 3, gayĕ (Śiv. 830, 1000, 1076; Rām. 64, 167, 183; for thee, gayiy for gayĕy, Gr.Gr. 236). In Rām. 508, 513, 1757, gay is m.c. for gayĕ. ¶ 3 past (Gr.Gr. 231), m.sg. 1, gayōs (Śiv. 322); 2, gayōkh; 3, gayōv (for thee, gayōy, Rām. 346); pl. 1 gayēy (for him, gayēs, Rām. 460); 2, gayēwa; 3, gayēy (Rām. 1760; YZ. 84, gayyih; for me, etc., gayēm, Śiv. 328; for him, etc., gayēs, Śiv. 996); f.sg. 1, gayēyĕs; 2, gayēyĕkh; 3, gayēyĕ (YZ. 235, gayē; for thee, gayēyiy, for gayēyĕy, Gr.Gr. 236); pl. 1, gayēyĕ; 2, gayēyĕwa; 3, gayēyĕ (for thee, gayēyiy, for gayēyĕy, Gr.Gr. 236). ¶ 4 past (Gr.Gr. 231), m.sg. 1, gayās; 2, gayākh; 3, gayāv; pl. 1, gayāy; 2, gayāwa; 3, gayāy (for thee, gayöy, Gr.Gr. 241). The f. is the same as in the 3 past. ¶ There are two forms of the perf. part.: (1) m.sg. gōmotᵘ (YZ. 133, 188; Śiv. 16, 66; Rām. 365); pl. gömȧtⁱ (YZ. 25, 36; Śiv. 706, 1642; Rām. 52, 166); f.sg. gömüʦᵘ̈ (YZ. 39, 40, 253; Śiv. 744, Rām. 440); pl. gömaʦa (Śiv. 1666); or (2) m.sg. gamotᵘ (Rām. 230, 565, 756, 1416, 1541) or gŏmotᵘ (H. v, 2; ix, 1); pl. gamȧtⁱ (H. xii, 20, Rām. 1426, 1692); f.sg. gamüʦᵘ̈ (H. xii, 10, Rām. 297, 753, 770, 772); pl. gamaʦa.] ¶ This verb means, primarily, 'to go,' but is often used secondarily in the sense of 'being' or 'becoming'. It is hence one of the most frequently used verbs in the language. ¶ To go, proceed (L.V. 19, 41; Śiv. 16, 53-5; Rām. 21, 109, 391, et passim); to go, go away, depart (L.V. 95, Rām. 52, 104, 211, 215, et passim); to go, to disappear (L.V. 9, Śiv. 1276, Rām. 219); to go, become absent, to die (Rām. 275, 367, 876); to go (to any place) (L.V. 36, Rām. 64, 166, 418); to go (into), to be put or to fall (into anything) (Śiv. 1210, Rām. 343); to go (of a letter in the post) (Gr.M.); to go (to a person or place), to reach (of news, etc.) (Śiv. 1225, Rām. 281, 508, 737, 1757); to march, start on the march (of an army) (Gr.M.); to go (to a certain condition, e.g. to joy, to become joyful (Śiv. 924; similarly, Śiv. 1642, 1739, 1760, Rām. 32); to go, lead (of a road) (Gr.M.); to go, elapse, pass (of time, etc.) (H. viii, 10; Śiv. 22, 706, 1704, 1717; Rām. 535, 787, 947, 1297); to go, be in motion (of the wind) (El.); to go, as we say of a worn-out garment, 'to go' (at the knees, etc.), cf. khŏn, khūrᵘ̈ 1. ¶ āshʦaras gaʦhun, to go to astonishment, to be surprised, filled with wonder (Rām. 567, 934); manas gōs, it went into his mind, he determined, made up his mind (to do so and so) (Rām. 557, 619, 623, 1012); reflected, considered (Rām. 1346, 1348); māra gaʦhun, to go to death, to meet a violent death (H. viii, 11; x, 7; Rām. 701, 868, 972); phikiri gaʦhun, to go into meditation, to meditate (Rām. 1368); pānas gaʦhun, to go for oneself, to go one's way without let or hindrance (H. iii, 8, etc.; Rām. 1375). ¶ To be, become (L.V. 16, 59, etc.; K.Pr. 9, 103, 148; YZ. 47, 149, 463; Śiv. 3, 40, 68, 129, 1659, 1694; Rām. 10, 20, 298, 463, et passim); to happen, turn out, occur (W. 101; L.V. 81, 84, 85, 102; YZ. 22; H. ix, 1; Śiv. 912, 1454, 1843; Rām. 118, 277, 687); to come into existence (L.V. 100, Śiv. 983, Rām. 90). ¶ sôruy samsār gav kuñĕ trāyĕ, the whole world became in one condition, i.e. everyone found himself in the same state of prosperity, there was neither rich nor poor (Śiv. 1239); chis kay gaʦhān, vomitings are happening to him, he is vomiting (Gr.M.); sītāyĕ gav gash, to Sītā fainting happened, she fainted (Rām. 396); kyāh gav, what happened? what is the matter? (YZ. 176, 269); kyāh gọ̆yᵘ, what happened to you? what is the matter with you? (Rām. 346, 347); sŏnas sartal gaʦhĕs, for gold base metal will become, gold will be turned into base metal (Rām. 682); shĕstᵃras ṣŏn gaʦhiy hösil, thine iron will be turned into gold (L.V. 100). ¶ This verb is commonly used to form nominal compounds, as in önta gaʦhun, to go beyond the end, to be at the last extremity; atha g. to get out of hand, be insubordinate; bạḍᵃran gaʦhüñᵘ̈, increase to take place; bakawās gaʦhun, mutual abuse to occur; bul gaʦhüñᵘ̈, a mistake to occur. For these and many others see under the respective nouns. As further examples may be quoted gumān gaʦhun, supposition to occur (to a person), to suppose, conclude (Rām. 463, 1324); khöli gaʦhun, to become void, to miss the mark (of a bullet) (Gr.M.); pöda gaʦhun, to appear, become manifest (Rām. 319, 466, 1063, 1293); to be created, born, produced (Rām. 597); tabāh gaʦhun, to be wrecked (of a ship) (Gr.M.); mĕ chuna shĕkh gaʦhān, I have no suspicion (Gr.M.); gayĕ bŏn ta hyorᵘ, she was tossed up and down (Gr.M.). ¶ In the second past, gauv or gav is often used as an equivalent of the present tense of the verb substantive, as in khŏsh gōs, I became pleased, i.e. I am pleased (Gr.M.); ʦēr gauv, it is late (Gr.M.), cf. gaʦhĕm ʦēr, I shall be late (Rām. 946); similarly Śiv. 59, 571, 604, 813, 821, 1545, 1660; Rām. 764, etc. In this sense it is frequently employed in definitions (cf. W. 140), as in karzdār gauv suy yus rupayĕ dārān āsi, a debtor is he who owes money (Gr.M.), similarly Śiv. 1226, 1227, 1553, 1556, 1758. In other connexions it means 'is by nature' (Śiv. 1287), or 'is the same as' (Śiv. 1448, 1449, 1753). ¶ With the conj. part. of another verb, gaʦhun forms a so-called intens. comp., as in mīlith gaʦhun, to be exactly alike (Gr.M.), to become united (L.V. 11, etc.); mashith gaʦhun, to forget (L.V. 59), with dat. of subject, as in yina mashith gaʦhiy, (take care) that you do not forget (Gr.M.), and gen. of thing forgotten (Rām. 871); wuphith g., to fly away (Gr.M.). Similarly, chapith g., to hide oneself (Rām. 398); dazith g., to be burnt up (Rām. 1080, 1082); hĕth g. (Hindī lē jānā), to take away (Śiv. 705, Rām. 236, 402, 469, 601); to go with (a person), to take (a person) along with one (Rām. 297, 793); khasith g., to ascend, rise, arise (L.V. 27, Rām. 867, 886, 900, 1761); khĕth g. (H. khā jānā), to eat up; karith g., to make and finish (Śiv. 210); marith g., (Hindī mar jānā), to die (Śiv. 706, Rām. 264, 753, 1425, 1577); rūzith g., to be stopped, impeded (Rām. 1092); ʦalith g. (H. calā jānā), to go away (Rām. 336, 1089, 1112, 1379); wuḍith g. (H. uṛ jānā), to fly away (Rām. 260); wasith g., to descend (Rām. 604, 1713, 1718, 1719); wŏthith g., to ascend, rise, arise (Rām. 1099, 1741).
m. a moderately sized bunch of greens, potherbs, etc. Cf. gë̆ḍᵘ̈.
f. a small bunch of greens, potherbs, etc., usually --˚. Cf. gĕḍurᵘ.

(sg. dat. gĕli), hitting anything by throwing a stick at it (as when knocking down a fruit from a tree, or the like). ¶ gĕla-küṭᵘ̈ f. a kind of very venomous snake of a grey colour and about a span and a half long. f. (sg. dat. gēli, Gr.Gr. 69), a thick solid beam of even size, suitable for cutting into building-planks.

m. circumference, circuit, compass (Śiv. 1185); boundary, environs; a sphere, a circle (El.). --trāwun -- m.inf. to encompass, surround, walk round.
m. a collar, the opening or neck of a garment (Rām. 1305).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gyūrᵘ; f. gīrᵘ̈, pl. gērĕ; 2 p.p. gēryōv), to surround, encompass; to encircle; to beset, hem in; to invest, blockade. ¶ gyūrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. gīrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), surrounded, etc.
m. slight darkness of complexion (Gr.Gr. 139, where it is spelt gĕshyāmĕr).
or gĕshumᵘ adj. (f. gĕshömᵘ̈ or gĕshimᵘ̈), slightly dark-complexioned (of a man or woman) (Gr.Gr. 139, where it is spelt gĕshyômᵘ).
a ringlet, curl, sidelock (YZ. 69); the hair of a woman's head, the whole hair when gathered up, twisted, and fastened on the back or top of the head (YZ. 153).

m. clarified butter, ghī (i.e. butter which has been boiled gently, strained and allowed to cool; El. spells this gyáu, and K.Pr. gyav (K.Pr. 10, 15, 34, 69, 73, 191, Śiv. 1660, Rām. 1612.
