In K. 743, the sg. obl. is irregularly gĕyĕ, instead of gĕwa). Cf. khām 1. -bata m. rice cooked in clarified butter. -khọbᵘ m. a khọ̆bᵘ or quilted cap worn on a greasy head. -kalapushᵘ m. a kind of night-cap worn on a greasy head. --mathun gaʦhun -- m.inf. to churn ghī (and) go, to be very shameless and heedless in the face of deserved rebuke. -pöjᵘ̈ f. a certain measure of ghī, viz. six sērs or twelve pounds. -sīrᵘ̈ f. a wad of cotton smeared with ghī and applied to the throat as a remedy for difficult breathing. -thīrᵘ̈ f. N. of a certain plant, Adiantum Capillus Veneris, used in medicine as an expectorant (L. 75); it grows on the banks of ponds. -ṭĕkh f. (sg. dat. -ṭĕki), a single drop of ghī. -ʦoḍᵘ m. a kind of earthen vessel for holding ghī. -zīrᵘ̈ f. a certain kind of rice-plant, with a small red husk, and a soft, white, sweet grain tasting like ghī. ¶ gĕwa (gyĕwa)-bagāra m. a dish composed of clarified butter and vegetables (El. gyauabagaira). -mūl m. a certain medicinal root, growing in watercourses, employed as a remedy for indigestion, fever, etc.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gĕwanôwᵘ), to cause to sing (Śiv. 1394, 1785). to cause others to sing, i.e. to vie in singing (K. 989).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. gyovᵘ, f. gë̆vᵘ̈), to sing (K.Pr. 69, 208; Śiv. 241, 276, 503, 735, 953, 1459, 1497, 1731). gŏn (or yĕsh) gĕwun, to sing the praises (of so and so), to commend (Gr.M.). El. spells this both gyewun and gyauwun. gĕwun 2, a song (H. iv). gĕwan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a singer; one who is in the habit of singing; a professional singer. gyovᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. gë̆vᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), sung; one in whose honour praises are sung (voc. gĕvimati, Śiv. 1417).
f. (sg. dat. gē̃ʦi), moving or shaking of anything slightly (with the hand, a lever, etc.).
a sec. suff. forming abs. nouns, as in dātagī, generosity, from dāta, generous; zindagī, life, from zinda, living. It is derived from an older -ak-ī.

or gīdᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. gīdĕ, Gr.Gr. 62), the excrement of a newly born child or other newly born animal (usually loose). --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to beat a person severely (quasi to such a degree that he involuntarily befouls himself).
m. (sg. dat.-dākas), Segeretia oppositifolia (El.). Cf. kanakh.
adj.(f.gidᵘ̈rᵘ̈), one the lower parts of whose cheeks are large and (naturally) swollen-looking. Cf. gạḍᵒrᵒ.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. gijyōv), to be strong, violent, tyrannical. gijyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. gijyē-müʦᵘ̈), one who has become habitually violent or tyrannical by frequently acting so.

m. earth, mud, clay. -kār گل کار m. working at earth, building (K.Pr. 137); a mason (Rām. 574). ¶ gili-ṭūrᵘ m. lit. 'a bud from the earth'; hence, a flower or plant which has budded and bloomed perfectly under most unfavourable conditions; N. of a certain flower (Rām. 1091).

f. a kind of bird, described as small and singing very sweetly after flying high up in the air; ? a lark (the jall of L. 146) (Gr.Gr. 13, Śiv. 1810, Rām. 422). In K.Pr. 121 the voc. is giliyĕ, and is translated 'O waterfowl'.
in gil-māl m. surrounding (an enemy, thief, or the like) and binding him. Cf. gērun.

f. (sg. dat. gilüñᵘ̈), the act of whirling about or turning about (the arms or other limbs, or something held in the hand, such as a sling) (Rām. 480); cf. gilanāwun 1 and gilawun 1; a movement of the limbs, an active movement (Skt. cēṣṭā, wrongly translated 'an attempt' in Gr.Gr. 121). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. whirling to occur; met. inward anger (whether with cause or causeless) to arise, esp. when engaged in some work. ¶ gilañĕ mārañĕ f.pl. inf. to turn or shake one's head or limbs about before people in the desire to show off one's jewellery (e.g. shaking the head to make the ear-pendants swing and so become conspicuous), to flaunt or flourish one's ornaments.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gilanôwᵘ), to whirl something in the air, to fling something into the air so as to cause it to revolve. Cf. gilawun 1.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gilanôwᵘ), to steal, carry away someone's property secretly or deceitfully. Cf. gilawun 2.
m. (sg. dat. gilāphas), a covering, cover, envelope, wrapper (El., K.Pr. 132).
m. (cor. from the English), a glass, a tumbler (in Kashmīr usually made of metal). Cf. El. s.v. glás.
m. a cherry, Cerasus vulgaris (El.); the sweet cherry, Prunus cerasus (L. 348). According to L. the word gilās is a corruption of 'cerasus'. --kulᵘ -- m. a cherry-tree (El.).
m. (sg. dat. gilaṭas), plating, gilding, silvering.
conj. (1 p.p. gilovᵘ), to whirl something (e.g. a sling) in the air; to flourish, shake out, flaunt (K.Pr. 154); to flourish, brandish (K.Pr. 34). Cf. gilanāwun 1.
conj. 2 (1 p.p. gilovᵘ), to steal by some act of deceit, to swindle. Cf. gilanāwun 2.
n.ag. (f.gindawüñᵘ̈), one who sports, sportive, fond of play (Śiv. 1383).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. gyundᵘ, f. ginzᵘ̈; 2 p.p. ginzōv), to play, sport (Śiv. 956, 1435, 1461; Rām. 94, 357); to play (ball or the like); to gambol (as children) (K.Pr. 156, Rām. 357); to play, game, gamble; to play (a game, etc.), amuse oneself with anything. nardas gindun, to play chess, draughts, backgammon, etc., to gamble (Gr.M.); rās gindun, to play the rās-dance, to join in the rās-dance (Śiv. 974, 1442); zāras gindun, to gamble (K.Pr. 137). ¶ gindan-bôjᵘ m. (f. -bājĕñ), a game-companion, a partner in a game, (in children's games) one who is on the same side in a game. -chīz m. a thing for playing with, a toy (Gr.M.). -gorᵘ m. (f. -gürᵘ̈), an amusement-maker, a professional singer. The f. is a female singer. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is skilled in playing games, in singing, in dancing, or the like.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gyundᵘ, and so on, as in gindun 1), to carry off, esp. to carry off someone's property by swindling him; to eat up a large quantity of food.
adj. c.g. destitute of fire or energy, impotent, spiritless.

or gēr (Rām. 919), m. circumference, circuit, ring. Cf. gēra. --anun -- m.inf. to surround, hem in, encompass, blockade (e.g. a thief whom a number of people are pursuing, or a besieged city); met. to distress, vex, worry, harass. -bacĕ m. causing (a person) to go round in a circle. -karun m.inf. to vex, harass, or worry a person by surrounding him (Śiv. 1675). --raṭȧnⁱ -- or gēr raṭȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. (of two persons grasping each other in fighting) to go round and round each other in circles, to struggle violently, wrestle round and round (Rām. 919). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to become bewildered or confused by sickness, fear, worry, or the like; to be seized, arrested.
m. a certain measure of length, the length of the forefinger (El.), 2 1/4 inches, or one-sixteenth of a gaz or yard (L. 243).
f. the sixteenth part of a yard, four finger-breadths; a piece of cloth of such a length.
m. anything round; esp. a kind of round flat cake. -kŏnḍal f. (sg. dat. -kŏnḍali or -kŏnḍüjᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 69), a circular mark, the boundary of any circular area.
f. an amount collected from a village on account of arrears, in addition to the revenue (L. 409, 435, 450).
adj. c.g. taken, seized, arrested, captured (Rām. 53, 384, 879); involved (in), entangled (Rām. 297); entangled (in calamity), at one's wit's ends (Rām. 1217).
m. a Christian place of worship, a church (Gr.M.).

f. a kind of snake. It is said to be able to put its tail into its mouth and then to roll along like a hoop, and to adopt this original method for attacking a human being; N. of a kind of two-headed ornament of gold or silver hung on to the neck of a suckling child.
m. mobbing and beating (e.g. a thief attempting to abscond). Cf. gīr.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. gīryōv), to be giddy, to totter, reel.
m. crying, weeping, lamentation (YZ. 497). --karun -- m.inf. to lament, etc. (YZ. 126, 194, 456).

f.(sg. dat. gīrĕ, Gr.Gr. 62), red chalk, red ochre (Śiv. 1019). Cf. gyūrᵘ. ¶ gīri-rang m. the colour of red ochre. -ranga or -rȧngⁱ adj. c.g. of the colour of red ochre; coloured or painted with red ochre (Śiv. 1047).
f., --˚, a song, as in bombura-gītā, the song of the bee (see bombur). Cf. gīth.
m. (sg. dat. gitas), a span about 9 inches in length (El. git).
f. a song, esp. a hymn in honour of a god (Śiv. 241, 735, 1394, 1497, 1721, 1785).
f. (sg. dat. glöñᵘ̈), disgust (caused by seeing or experiencing something foul, stinking, or the like).
m. heaviness, weightiness (Rām. 603, 1153); deafness. El. spells this word gŏbar, gŏber, and gŏbir. Cf. Gr.Gr. 138.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. gŏbyōv), to be heavy, to be too heavy (K.Pr. 49, Rām. 415); to become heavy, to begin to be felt heavy (of load on a journey) (K.Pr. 76); the body to become heavy, to be unable to support oneself (through illness, etc.); to become tired; to become lazy at any work. gŏbyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. gŏbyē-müʦᵘ̈), become heavy (of a load, or a work); wearied, become lazy, etc.

or (H. viii, 1, 3)gobur m. (sg. dat. gọ̆bᵃras or gabaras), a youth, a boy, esp. one who is healthy and sturdy; a young son (esp. used in this sense as a term of endearment) (Rām. 1283); a son generally, a male child (El.; K.Pr. 12 voc., 22, 63, 76, 142, 174 abl., 163, 253; W. 135; YZ. 414, 429; H. viii, 1, 3; Rām. 28, 74, etc.). ōra-gŏbur, a stepson (K.Pr. 236, spelt wurah-gabar). ¶ gọ̆bᵃra-gūlᵃ m. 'a son-kernel', a son who is especially loved, e.g. on account of his handsomeness or his good behaviour (esp. when an only son). -tandal f. (sg. dat. -tandali), a row of sons, the existence of a large family of sons.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. gọ̆bᵃrôwᵃ), to make heavy, cause to be heavy; to load another heavily, to impose a heavy load on another; to distress a person by bringing serious charges against him, putting him in debt, or the like. Caus. of gŏbun (Gr.Gr. 173).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gọ̆bᵒrᵒ), i.q. gọ̆bᵃrāwun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 175).

adj. (f. gö̆bᵘ̈), heavy, weighty (Gr.Gr. 138, Śiv. 1027, 1868); (of motion) ponderous, slow; gọ̆bᵘ (or gọ̆bᵘ gọ̆bᵘ) chuh pakān, he is progressing slowly (Gr.Gr. 76). ¶ gabi-bāri adv. heavily with child (of women or female animals), used with verbs of rising, standing, or the like. Possibly really connected with gab 1 and not with gọ̆bᵘ. -khŏra or -khōra f. 'heavy-footed' (cf. khŏr 1 and khōr 2), hence, a woman heavy with child, one who is at least five months gone in pregnancy.
m. a man who is trained, educated, well-behaved, polite.
m. 'King Gōcam'; putting some mark on a person as a joke, e.g. putting a piece of cloth sticking on the top of his turban and so on, in order to make him an object of ridicule.
in -büdᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. an insulting gesture made by shaking in a person's face the closed fist with the top of the thumb projecting between the second and third fingers. Cf. gūṭh.
in -köṭhᵘ̈  f. the cob of Indian corn after the seeds have been extracted, the core of the Indian corn cob. It is dried and used as fuel (L. 337).

m. the beginning, commencement, of anything (K.Pr. 15, Śiv. 46, 774); the part of the stem or trunk of a tree immediately above the root (K.Pr. 118, Rām. 606); the ankle (as the beginning of the shin-bone), the malleolus, external malleolus (El.); the leg (the part being put for the whole (El.)). El. makes this word f. --barun -- or gŏḍa barun m.inf. to fill up the root or from the root, i.e. to fill in earth, etc., round the roots of an old and decaying tree in order to revive it; met. to strengthen the foundation or base of any work or action, esp. of one which is in a bad way. ¶ gŏḍa adv. at first, firstly (K.Pr. 70, guḍah; Śiv. 8, 33, 1160, 1367, 1792; Rām. 474, 1174; H. iv, 2; v, 9; viii, 3; xi, 5; xii, 5). -ôchᵘ m. the ankle-string used for fastening the grass-sandals commonly used in Kashmīr. Cf. ôchᵘ. --örᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be fettered on the ankles; met. to be prevented from seizing the opportunity of undertaking some wished for and profitable work, owing to being previously inextricably involved in something unwished for and unprofitable, to suffer estoppel. -barun m.inf., i.q. gŏḍ barun ab. -holᵘ adj. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), crooked-ankled. -korᵘ m. an ankle-bracelet, an anklet. --rab karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to put mud on the ankle; to break faith by refusing to perform a promise made (to someone on condition of his performing some difficult work). -shutᵘ or -shutun adv. from the first, from the beginning. -sǖtⁱ or -sṻty adv., id. ¶ gŏḍukᵘ adj. (f. gŏḍücᵘ̈), of or belonging to the beginning, etc., first (El.); (of a branch or the like) springing from the root (of a tree, etc.).

m. a rhinoceros. ¶ gö̃ḍa-nyoṭhᵘ m. a thumb-ring made of rhinoceros-horn and worn by women. -pötᵃr m. a cup made of rhinoceros-horn, often used in making offerings at a Hindū śrāddha. -wöjᵘ̈ f. a finger-ring made of rhinoceros-horn and worn by both men and women.
m. an anus foul owing to bad conduct or disease, a term of abuse. Cf. gūdᵘ.

adv. at first, first, in (or at) the beginning; for the first time (Śiv. 124, 131, 722; Rām. 384, 670; H. iii, 1; x, 12; xi, 2, 3, 10); especially (El. gŏḍain); according to El. this word is also a subst. f. meaning beginning, commencement. ¶ gŏḍañiy adv. at the very first, first of all (H. viii, 10; x, 3, 10; xii, 4, 6).

adj. (f. gŏḍañicᵘ̈ H. xii, 10), first (in time or in order) (K.Pr. 70), used as ord. of akh (Gr.Gr. 76, Śiv. 61, H. viii, 5, 13); elder, El. gŏḍañukᵘ bôyᵘ, an elder brother; gŏḍañiki törīkha, on the first (of the month) (Gr.M.).
m. a hole (in cloth, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 9). zamīnas godᵘ, a hole in the ground (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to pierce (El. gaud).

m. (f. göḍᵘ̈), a male fish, esp. one of a small kind (Śiv. 1815); --˚ used as a kind of surname appended to the name of a fish-seller. The f. means a female fish of any size (Rām. 723). Cf. āra-göḍᵘ̈, s.v. āra, and gāḍ.

m. aspersion, ceremonial sprinkling with water or other liquid (as in the consecration of a king, asperging on an idol or liṅga, etc.); a swarm (Gr.M.); machi-goḍᵘ, a swarm of flies (Gr.M.). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to asperge (Śiv. 1160, 1741).
(?spelling) in goḍᵘ-prān m. a leek (El. gauḍa-prán). It is not eaten by Hindūs of the Valley.
f. a cart, wagon, carriage, coach. --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to mount a carriage, to get into a carriage. --khasith gaʦhun --, to go in a carriage, to travel in a carriage, to drive (Gr.M.).

or gŏgulᵘ m. (sg. dat. gŏgalas), a large turnip (cf. gŏgᵘ̈jᵘ̈ and Gr.Gr. 35), Brassica rapa (K.Pr. 11, 171); met. a globe or ball of wood, a globe, a sphere (El.). Cf. gunglū. ¶ gŏgal-dᵃph m. (sg. dat. -dᵃpas), 'turnip-incense,' the roots of Jurinea macrocephala, used as incense (L. 77). --karȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to make globes; hence (of a heavy load) to squeeze, by overburdening the shoulders, esp. when the load is unfairly excessive. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -mŏnjĕ), the part of a turnip-root above ground, when it is large and globular.

or gŏgᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. the turnip plant; a moderately sized turnip, Brassica rapa (L. 346). This word means an ordinary turnip, while the masc. gŏgulᵘ means a large turnip (Gr.Gr. 35). According to El. (s.v. gogij), in winter time both Hindūs and Musalmāns consume large numbers of turnips. The turnips of Haripūr are said to be the best in the valley. Cf. gŏgul. El. has also gugchí. ¶ gŏgᵃji-ã̄cār m. turnip pickle. -āra m. a 'turnip necklace', slices of skinned and dried turnips strung on a string, and stored for winter use. -bodᵘ m. a bunch of turnip-tops (Gr.Gr. 145). -ḍār m. a turnip field. -hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), turnip-tops (W. 114). -hüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -hacĕ), a dried slice of turnip, stored for use in winter. -khünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -khanjĕ), a slice of turnip. -khav f. a pit in which turnip-tops are stored so as to keep them moist for winter use. -mulⁱvĕñ f. dried full-grown turnip-tops, stored in autumn for winter use. -musᵘ m. a kind of very small turnip-root. -pathᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. N. of a tableland in the Nāgām (Skt. Nāgrāma) Pargana, in which turnips are almost everywhere grown. -pạtᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a turnip-leaf (Gr.Gr. 74); a bundle of turnip-leaves. -sinwāh m. the small amount of turnips and turnip-tops used in making a sauce for a single meal. Cf. syunᵘ. -ʦakul m. (sg. dat. -ʦakalas), a globular-shaped lump of turnip, cut into shape by a knife. -ʦöryunᵘ m. the refuse leaves, stalks, etc., thrown away when preparing turnips for cooking or for storing dry. -wö̃kh f. (sg. dat. -wö̃ki), a string of dried turnip-tops, with portions of the roots attached, stored up for winter use. Cf. wö̃kh. -wörᵘ̈ f. a small plot of ground close to a house in which turnips are cultivated, a turnip-garden (common in villages).
m. dung, ordure, fæces (K.Pr. 59, 71). Cf. guhᵘ. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat ordure; met. to utter filthy lying words.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gŏhanôwᵘ), to make to be bright; to make a fire burn up; to make a jewel brilliant. Caus. of gŏhun (Gr.Gr. 174).
m. nature, essence, substance; origin, root, stock; any hidden virtue; intellect; wisdom; a pearl, a jewel, a gem, precious stone (Śiv. 428, 430).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. gŏhyōv), to shine, be bright (of a fire, a jewel, etc.). Its caus. is gŏhanāwun (Gr.Gr. 174).
m. drawing in of the arms, legs, etc., under the influence of cold, fear, etc., crouching, cringing, shrinking.
m. N. of a certain country in India, on the bank of the Yamunā (Jamnā), near Vṛindāvana (Brindāban), and the scene of the youthful exploits of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) (Śiv. 1385, 1391).
m. 'the joy of Gōkul' (q.v.), N. of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) (Śiv. 1320).
m. noise, din, clamour, confusion of voices, outcry, tumult. ¶ gŏla-gôshᵘ m. the noise of a number of people speaking together.
f. (sg. dat. gŏli Gr.Gr. 69), the skin or rind of a walnut-shell or other nut (Śiv. 1023, 1571). Cf. gŏlur, and ḍūnᵘ-gŏl or -gŏlur, s.v. ḍūnᵘ.
m. a widow's bastard, the son of a widow woman who takes service as a concubine. Cf. gūlⁱ 2. -bacĕ m. a widow's bastard; met. an ill-conducted youth who behaves as such a bastard.

m. rose-water (El., W. 134); a rose (K.Pr. 40; YZ. 257; Śiv. 55, 187, 188, 190-2, 555; Rām. 197, 397, 644, 650). There are two great varieties of the rose in Kashmīr--lāl gŏlāb, or red rose, and āra-wal (see āra 2), the yellow rose. -tǖrᵘ̈ f. 'rose-cold', the season when roses bloom in the winter, during which a moderately cool wind blows. -zyurᵘ m. a collection of rose petals (used as a medicine).
f. a collyrium-club, i.e. a club instead of a stick of collyrium, a blow in the eye; met. foul abuse. Cf. gŏlᵃkh.

cf. گلالہ m. the red poppy, Papaver rhœas. The plant is used medicinally as a cardiac tonic, and its young leaves are much esteemed as a vegetable (L. 72, 76, 462; K.Pr. 102; Rām. 203, 279, etc.). It is said to be specially common in barley-fields. El. also gives gul-lāla, and moreover gives gulālā as meaning tulip.
m. a slave, bondsman; a servant (El.; YZ. 157; H. vi, 14; viii, passim).
(? spelling), m. a curlew, Numenius arquata (L. 124).
m. a pellet-bow; (in Kashmīr) the earthen pellet fired from such a bow; a bolus, a soft kind of pill made up with medicaments and molasses. Cf. gōna.
adj. c.g. victorious; dushmanas-pĕṭh gölib sapanun, to overcome the enemy (Gr.M.).
(K.Pr. 158), said to be incorrect for gari, in the house. According to others it should be göli or gāli, and is a meaningless word.
in the following.-wā̃ḍulᵘ m. a vessel into which water for washing grain is received after use. -wôñᵘ m. the dirty water in which grain has been washed.
m. confusion, jumble, mess; an indefinite or indeterminate action or course of conduct.
adj. c.g. of the colour of a rose, rose-coloured, rosy, pink. --ṭang -- m. N. of a kind of pear, see ṭang.
m. (sg. dat. gŏlaras), the shell or skin of a walnut or the like; a nut (El.). Cf. gŏl 2, and ḍūnᵘ-gŏl or -gŏlur, s.v. ḍūnᵘ.
or gŏlᵘ̈khᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. gŏlᵃki), a small stick-shaped piece of collyrium for application to the eyes as a medicine.
m. (inmuha-gọ̆lᵘ, Siv. 1056), muddiness (of water) (the soul is compared to water which has been muddied by muh or illusion). Cf. guhulᵘ 2.

m. a cave; esp., in Kashmīr, a solitary piece of level ground surrounded by desert mountains, such as robbers could hide in, a robber's lair. gölⁱ-höjⁱ f. a jail, prison (in which robbers find an unwished for 'lair').

m. the mouth of a jar, opening of a bag, entrance to a cave (Rām. 462, 464), or the like. Cf. dān 1 and güjᵘ̈; also basma-golᵘ s.v. basm (Śiv. 1572), and dōri-golᵘ, s.v. dūrᵘ̈ 2. ¶ gȧlⁱ-örⁱ or gȧlⁱ-yörⁱ f. the rope or string tied round the neck of a jar, and by which it is suspended and carried. ¶ gali phirun m.inf. to empty a jar by inverting it and pouring out the contents. --phirith hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to empty out the contents of a jar as ab., and take the whole contents (leaving nothing for anyone else).

m. the inside part of the corners of the mouth; the lower part of the cheek, the jowl (K.Pr. 74, 156). In dŏda-golᵘ (s.v. dŏd) this word means 'mouthful'. so rata-gᵒ, p. 846a, l.Cf. gal 2. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to deny something previously said by the speaker, to dissimulate. ¶ gȧlⁱ khasȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. the corners of the mouth to rise, hence (of the cheeks) to be puffed out (by wind) (K.Pr. 207), or to be swollen (by disease). ¶ gali gali adv. in mouthfuls (of giving to drink or the like) (Śiv. 1575). --myūṭhᵘ -- m. a kiss on the inner part of the cheek (obsc.). --ʦopᵘ -- m. a bite on the inner part of the cheek. --zĕv -- f. the tongue in the cheek; met. the condition of being unable to reply when a lie is discovered, being rendered mute, dumbfounded, speechless.
adj. c.g. of, belonging to, or produced in, a village.

m. a quality (K.Pr. 36, guan; Śiv. 1060), esp. a good quality (Rām. 39, 1067); the virtue, or property of a medicine, or the like (Gr.M.), or of a special astrological conjuncture (Rām. 1260, 1281); a virtue, such as learning, deftness, mercy, nobility of temperament (Śiv. 886, 966, 1195, Rām. 604); (according to Hindū philosophy) one of the three guṇas or constituents of existing things, viz. goodness, passion, and darkness (Śiv. 193, 447, 797, 977, etc.). Cf. gōn. --gĕwun --, m.inf. to sing the virtues (of so and so), to praise widely, to speak well (of) (Gr.M.). ¶ gŏna-mã̄th m. sg. dat. -mã̄tas), 'one endowed with good qualities'; hence, a skilled professional singer. -wān adj. c.g. possessing good qualities, excellent (Śiv. 1077, 1081); virtuous, worthy; accomplished, skilful (Śiv. 1142); effective, possessing virtue (of a medicine, or the like). ¶ gŏnau-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), devoid of good qualities (Śiv. 751).
m. a bowstring (El.). This is really another form of gŏn. Cf. gōn-bal.
m. a pellet bow (El.). Cf. gŏlēla.

m. a fault, offence, a sinful act (Gr.M., K.Pr. 12); crime, iniquity, sin (Rām. 495); vice (El.). -gār گناہ گار or gunahgār گنہ گار m. a sinner (K.Pr. 136). --karun -- m.inf. to sin (K.Pr. 171, H. viii, 11).
m. strength in any particular good quality, such as learning, dexterity, or the like. Cf. gŏn and gōn.

m. a bud (K.Pr. 256), a rosebud. -dahān غنچہ دہان one who has a mouth like a rose- bud (YZ. 16, 145). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be collected together (like a rosebud), to be closely packed; (in Kāshmīrī) to become bewildered, perplexed, confused, nonplussed (in a dispute or the like).

f. a small village or hamlet, esp. one newly settled; the land enclosed in the old Mug̱ẖul embankments (L. 211, gund). --kaḍüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to beg successfully several times in a place in which one has once before begged successfully. --nērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. when one has the expectation of getting a thing only once from any place, to find oneself able to get it several times from that place.
m. the earthenware vessel of a kāngrī or portable brazier (El.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gọ̆ndᵘ; 2 p.p. gŏnzōv), to display or express one's thoughts or feelings. This verb is impers. in tenses derived from the p.p. Cf. grāv.

or gundun conj. 1 (1 p.p. gọ̆ndᵘ or gundᵘ; 2 p.p. gŏ(u)nzōv ), to complain of, to make a complaint about (anything, acc.) (Śiv. 1435); to ridicule. This verb is impers. in the tenses formed from the p.p. Cf. grāv.
m. a posy, bouquet; a handful of anything except grain and grass (El.).
f. 'a female posy', a very beautiful woman (YZ. 548). Cf. gŏndurᵘ.

m. a posy, a nosegay (YZ. 89) (usually --˚ after the name of the flower, e.g. pōshĕ-gọ̆ndᵘ, a nosegay of flowers, H. v. 4); a plume of heron's feathers bound up with pearls, precious stones, and gold and silver wire. It is worn on a turban on state occasions (YZ. 89, 390, L. 118). ¶ gŏndⁱ-tīrⁱ f. (sg. dat. -tīrĕ), heron's plumes, used as ab. Cf. braga- tīrᵘ̈ under brag.
m. the jaw. ¶ gȧnḍⁱ pĕnⁱ m. pl. inf. the jaws to fall; loosening of the jaw-bones of children due to dysentery.
m. a great log of wood, esp. one not trimmed; met. a great man, a man of high rank and power, i.q. grọ̆nḍᵘ. Cf. gar- gunḍa s.v. gara.
m. the Turkestan pack-saddle, which consists of two straw-filled pommels joined in front (H. xi, 9).
f.pl. a humble request (for help in any work or the like).

m. a kind of handsel or present given to cowherds and similar servants on monthly wages when they are first engaged. --karun -- m.inf. to make a commencement of cultivation; this is a formal ceremony performed by husbandmen on an auspicious day and at an auspicious hour (K.Pr. 247).
m. endowed with good qualities, possessing virtue (Śiv. 1060); (of an inanimate thing, such as a medicine) possessing virtue, effective.
m. (sg. dat. gönikas), an accompanist, a musician who plays for dancing women, prostitutes, etc.
f. the profession or conduct of a souteneur. See gān 1.
or gunja m. a large tame cat, well-grown and fat.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. gūnᵘ, f. gūñᵘ̈; 2 p.p.gōñōv) (in arithmetic) to multiply; (in rope-making, etc.) to twist several strands together; to study over and over again, practise, repeat several times something one is learning.
adj. c.g. evil-smelling, stinking (by nature or occupation).
m. a stack, rick (L. 463, Śiv. 1212, Rām. 12); a pile (Gr.Gr. 26).

f. a stack, a high pile of straw or the like; a granary (El.). ¶ gŏñĕ-bāha m. heating, sweating, fermenting (of such a stack). gŏñĕ karañĕ f. pl. inf. to make stacks; to acquire a great deal of anything (e.g. knowledge, virtue, money, or goods).
(f. güñᵘ̈ 2, for 1 see s.v.), adjectival suff. added to numerals, and signifying 'fold', as in hata-gonᵘ, a hundredfold. Cf. gunᵘ.
f. a harlot, a prostitute (K.Pr. 65, gáni) (f. of gān 1, q.v., Gr.Gr. 37). See El. s.v. gányi for particulars of women of this kind in Kashmīr. göñĕ-war m.pl. a harlot's coquetry.
adj. (f.güñᵘ̈ 3), compact, solid, dense (Śiv. 194); coarse, gross; stout, strong.
f. a small wild fruit, of a dark-red colour and sour taste, growing on a thorny shrub; probably the gaun, Elæagnus parvifolia of L. 74. Cf. gīwāñ.
m. a cowherd; esp. the famous cowherd, i.e. Kṛṣṇa (Krushn) (Śiv. 705, 733, 1320, 1380, 1436).
f. (sg. dat. gŏphi), a cave, a cavern (K.Pr. 249, Śiv. 933, 1817, 1894, Rām. 517), a pit, a hole (El., who makes it m.; Gr.M., also m.). gŏphi-golᵘ m. the opening, or mouth, of a cave.
m. (sg. dat. gōpas), a cowherd; esp. one of the cowherds of Vṛndāvana, amongst whom Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) spent his youth. Their chief was named Nanda (Śiv. 1461), who was Kṛṣṇa's foster-father.
or göfil غآفل adj. c.g. unmindful, neglectful, negligent, heedless (K.Pr. 46, göphilō, voc.).

or gūpī f. a cowherdess, a herdmaiden; esp. the herdmaidens who attended on the youthful Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) in Vṛndāvana (Śiv. 705, 992, etc.). -nāth m. (sg. dat. -nāthas), the lord of herdmaidens, N. of Kṛṣṇa (Śiv. 858, 1382, 1423, 1443).
adj. c.g. concealed. Usually --˚, as in ākāra-gŏpᵃth, q.v. s.v. ākār.

or gōr 1 m. a teacher, schoolmaster; a religious preceptor, a spiritual guide, a guru [Śiv. 15, 82, 707, etc. (always gŏr); Rām. (gŏr) 9, 43, 44, 48, 86, 180, etc., (gōr) 954, 1255]; a family priest, a Brāhmaṇ (El., Gr.Gr. 51). (The word gōr is generally used only in the second and third of the ab. senses, while gŏr is used in all three senses.) The abl. of comparison of this word must be made by adding the postposition to the abl. of the gen. Thus, gŏra-sandi khŏta, not gŏra khŏta (Gr.Gr. 49). -bĕñĕ f. the daughter of one's teacher or spiritual guide (always treated as one's own sister); a spiritual sister, a woman who is a fellow-disciple or who is a follower of the same spiritual guide; a female fellow-student. -bāv m. respect, reverence, paid or due to a teacher or to a spiritual guide; similar respect paid or due to any venerable person. -bôyᵘ m. the son of one's teacher or spiritual guide; a spiritual brother, one who is a fellow-disciple, or who is a follower of the same spiritual guide; a fellow-student. -dār m. the house of a person's teacher or of his spiritual guide; a monastery in which such a spiritual guide resides. -möjᵘ̈ f. the wife of a teacher; the wife of a spiritual guide; a spiritual mother (looked upon as equal to one's own mother). -mŏkh m. (sg. dat. -mŏkhas), the mouth of the spiritual teacher; hence, what proceeds from his mouth, the instruction, esp. the acceptance of initiatory mantra or prayer taught by him. -mŏkhⁱ m. the Gurmukhī alphabet, used in the Panjāb, and said to have been invented by the Sikkh Guru Aṅgad. -mǖ̃thᵃr m. the mantra or initiatory prayer taught to a disciple by his spiritual guide. ¶ gŏra-shĕbd m., i.q. gŏr-mũ̄̈thᵃr, ab. (Rām. 43). ¶ gōra-bāy f. the wife of a family priest. -bôyᵘ m. a polite term for one's family priest. -koṭᵘ m. the son of a person's family priest. -wār f. the day named after the guru of the gods, Thursday (El.), i.q. braswār (Rām. 1259).

m. deep thought, reflection, meditation (Gr.M.); (in Kāshmīrī) a private grudge, hidden malice. --karun -- m.inf. to consider carefully, pay attention (to = pĕṭh) (Gr.M.). --rōzun -- m.inf. a private grudge to be left (as the consequence of the object of the dislike having interfered with a person's work, etc.). --thawun -- m.inf. to cause a private grudge to be left, as ab.
or gōrᵘ̈ گور f. a grave, a tomb.
f. the profession, condition, professional knowledge, or professional acts of a family priest.
or gōramala m. a gravedigger (El.). Cf. gōr 4.

f. the third lunar day of the light half of the month of Māg (Skt. Māgha = January-February), sacred amongst Hindūs to the goddess Gaurī or Vāgīśvarī, on which a festival is held by teachers and their pupils; a set of verses, written on coloured paper, together with a picture of Sarasvatī, the goddess of learning, surrounded by an ornamental border, prepared on the occasion of this festival.
or gōrawār, see gŏr, p. 297b, l. 6.

m. a cat. -ȧchⁱ f. a cat's eye; a human eye resembling in colour that of a cat, a brown eye. -gonjᵘ m. 'a puss of a cat', a fine fat tawny cat. Cf. gonjᵘ. -kāʦurᵘ adj. (f. -kāʦürᵘ̈), very brown (of a person's complexion or skin).

m. N. of a certain fruit, a small apricot, Prunus Armeniaca (El. gordol and gurdálú). ¶ gŏrdölⁱ-ö̃ṭⁱ f. an apricot stone. -kujⁱ or -kujᵘ̈ f. an apricot-tree. -lünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -lanjĕ), a branch of an apricot-tree, esp. when separated from the tree, with or without fruit hanging from it. -phulay f. the flowering of an apricot-tree.
m.onomat. the bubbling or gurgling sound of air passing through water, as in the case of a hubble-bubble or native tobacco-pipe.
or gūril f. (sg. dat. gŏrili or gūrili), the profession, conduct, or condition of a family priest, or of a teacher, or of a spiritual preceptor (cf. Gr.Gr. 142, gŏr or gōr 1, gūrⁱlözⁱ, and gōrözᵘ̈).
f. the condition or profession of a gŏryunᵘ, q.v., i.e. of a Hindū family priest, who conducts worship according to the rules of the Tantras and not according to those of the Vēdas. Cf. gōrözᵘ̈.
m. the planet Jupiter, i.q. brahaspath.
m. a preparation of tobacco and molasses (guṛ) for smoking in a ḥuqqa.
f. the profession or occupation of a teacher, of a spiritual guide, or of a family priest. Cf. gŏrinözᵘ̈, gŏril, gūrⁱlözⁱ, and Gr.Gr. 143.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gūrᵘ; f.pl. gōrĕ; 2 p.p. gōryōv), to babble in delirium or the like; to talk in one's sleep; to lament (Gr.Gr. xx).
m. a Hindū family priest, who conducts worship according to the rules of the Tantras and not according to those of the Vēdas.
m. a large rock; esp. a rock placed on the edge of the precipice side of a mountain path to guard wayfarers from falling over.

m. (for 2 see gārun; the f. görᵘ̈ 2, q.v., is used for the kernel), the singhārā, or water-chestnut, the fruit of the esculent water-lily, Trapa bispinosa. The kernel is eaten and the shells are used for fuel. It grows wild in the lakes of Kashmīr and is an important food crop (L. 354; El. gāṛī; qq.v. for full particulars, also K.Pr. 92, 120, Śiv. 1807). Cf. gūlᵘ. ¶ gāri-gotᵘ adj. (f. -güʦᵘ̈), 'singhārā-lean,' a person who is lean by nature and whom no diet will fatten. -phalhār m. a gruel or porridge made of cooked flour of the water-chestnut, eaten by Kāshmīrī Hindūs on fast-days. This is the name given to it by Hindūs; other people call it gāri-wugra, q.v. bel. (El. s.v. gāṛī). -pūrᵘ m. a water-chestnut cake, made of water-chestnut flour cooked in clarified butter, and eaten by Hindūs on fast-days. -raz f. water-chestnut rope, the water-chestnut worked up with butter, etc., into a rope-like form for making into cakes; the kernels are boiled whole in water and then pounded into a paste. Cf. öṭⁱ-raz, under ôṭᵘ. -wugra m., see -phalhār ab. ¶ görⁱ m.pl. water-chestnuts (of a crop of them or the like). -gūjⁱ or -gūjᵘ̈ f. the kernel of the water-chestnut, extracted by roasting the nut and then breaking it. -gōjĕ gaʦhañĕ f. pl. inf. to become water-chestnut kernels; met. the eyes to become swollen and almost blind through weeping, disease, or the like. görⁱ-gōjĕ is used as a curse, "may your eyes become thus" (K.Pr. 66). -gām m. a village inhabited by people who gather water-chestnuts (see the next) (K.Pr. 120). -hönzᵘ̈ m. (f. -hānzañ), a boatman who collects water-chestnuts for sale (K.Pr. 121). The f. is his wife. -konḍᵘ m. the complete spine or horn on a water-chestnut. -künḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kanjĕ), the incomplete, broken horn on an empty or 'blind' water-chestnut. -kôvᵘ m. a water-chestnut crow, a kind of bird something like a young crow, with a long beak, which dives for water-chestnuts and eats them; a long pole, with a crescent-shaped hoe at one end, used for scraping up the water-chestnuts from the mud at the bottom of a lake (cf. L. 355, cokdan and kama-khuru, s.v. kam 4). -nambal f. (sg. dat. -nambali), a water-chestnut field, the shallow part of a lake in which water-chestnuts grow. -pọ̆ʦhᵘ m. a water-chestnut guest, a guest invited to a dinner when water-chestnuts are in their prime, i.e. at the beginning of autumn. -ʦôkᵘ m. a tool for splitting open water-chestnuts.
m. a species of starling (El.). ? = görⁱ- kôvᵘ, s.v. gôrᵘ.

m.(f. gürᵘ̈ 2, for 1 see s.v.), a doer, maker; hence, esp. an artisan, a maker of things for sale, used as a sec. suff.; e.g. aina-gorᵘ, a maker of mirrors; lāyĕ-gorᵘ, a seller of parched grain; ganḍan-gorᵘ, a bookbinder; kangañĕ-gorᵘ, a comb-maker, a comb-seller; manḍan-gorᵘ, a man who kneads cloth in water to soften it (Gr.Gr. 149). The f. gürᵘ̈ indicates a female maker of the thing referred to, while a maker's wife is -gȧrⁱ-bāy.

f. the dried kernel of the water-chestnut (El.). See görⁱ-gūjⁱ under gôrᵘ. El. also gives gólí for this word, and gólí-kutsur, as meaning a seller of the kernels. Cf. gūlᵘ. -gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to become such a kernel (which is extracted by roasting and splitting); met. to be publicly disgraced or discomfited (e.g. by having one's failings proclaimed or being defeated in an abuse-combat). -karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. publicly to discomfit as above.
adj. (f.gürᵘ̈ 3), hard, solid, tough (e.g. wood that cannot be cut); dense, solid, of thick solid material (e.g. a metal vessel that will not ring when struck).
(YZ. 90), ? meaning. Apparently translated as a sg. dat. of gāv, q.v., which is impossible, the word being fem.

m. wrath, rage, anger, passion; displeasure, a hurt feeling (Śiv. 85, Rām. 758); anxiety, trouble, sorrow (Rām. 72, 453, 675, 758, 1088, 1120, 1572, 1675, 1693, 1739). --diwanāwun -- m.inf. to provoke to anger (Gr.M.). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. anger or rage (against someone, in dat.) to occur (K.Pr. 100, Rām. 1556, 1574, 1605). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to drag out anger, to assuage anger, to appease. --karun -- m.inf. to make anger, to enrage, anger.
m. bathing, ablution, a bath (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to bathe (El.).
adj. c.g. full of wrath, angry, wroth.

m. brilliancy, brightness, clear visibility (e.g. of a distant peak) (Śiv. 1811); brightness, clearness (of the sky); brightness (e.g. of a garden beautiful with flowers or of a clean well-kept house) (Śiv. 963, 1028); the bright parts of a garden, the flower clusters (Śiv. 1690). Cf. gāsh.
(El.), gosh búg (L. 351), and goshibeigi (El.) (? spelling of all three), a kind of early pear. See ṭang.
m. a corner, nook, closet; a lobe (of the liver). Cf. jigar.
adj. c.g. (of a human being) starving with hunger, so famished as to be ready to snatch away forcibly another's food, ravenous.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. göshᵒrᵒ), to make (day) bright, to brighten, i.e. the clouds to blow off and leave the sky clear.
m. (sg. dat. gōshtas), meat, flesh. --āba گوشتابہ or gusht-āba گشتابہ m. a rich soup of pounded or minced meat (K.Pr. 208).

m. silence, not speaking; esp. the silence of one who, though he sees and hears what is going on, says nothing, and acts as if he knew nothing about it; heedlessness, carelessness of consequences after full warning (Gr.Gr. 139).

adj. (f. güshᵘ̈), silent (Gr.Gr. 138, 139); esp. one who, although he sees and hears or has been instructed, acts as if he were entirely ignorant, heedless (of instructions), one who after full warning acts without consideration of consequences.
f. a woman who is dirty in person, clothes, work, and predisposition.
f. the condition of being littered with a quantity of dirty straw, grass, etc. (of a place or house) (K.Pr. 56, of a garden).

m. an ascetic, a religious mendicant, a saint, a holy man who has abandoned the world and house and home and become a wandering devotee (K.Pr. 79, 161; Śiv. 45, 189, 305, 349, 1264, etc.; Rām. 73, 394); with suff. of indef. art. gŏsôñwāh (Śiv. 814, 825, 826). ¶ gŏsöñⁱ-bāy f. the abandoned wife of a man who has become a mendicant devotee; a woman who has herself become a mendicant devotee. -ḍīphᵃrĕ f.pl. 'mendicant committees', the whole body of mendicants at a religious assembly, such as a bathing-place festival. These people assemble in large numbers on such occasions, and form themselves into small groups or schools according to the sect or particular body of ascetics to which each belongs. Cf. ḍīphᵘ̈rᵘ̈. -güḍᵘ̈wa m. an ascetic's water-pot; met. one who is left alone without a single relation in the world. -koṭᵘ m. an ascetic's son; an ascetic boy, a boy who has taken to the life of a mendicant devotee; a boy who takes to begging. -küṭᵘ̈ f. an ascetic's daughter; a girl who has taken to a mendicant devotee's life; a girl who has been compelled by poverty to take to begging. -ruth m. (sg. dat. -ratas), an ascetic's vow of fasting; taking to an ascetic life, taking the vow of asceticism. -tŏmul m. (sg. dat. -tŏmalas), ascetic's rice, the rice (or food) given to a mendicant; met. a mixture of a number of things of different kinds.
adj. (f. güsᵘ̈), rubbed down, ground down, polished. Used --˚. Cf. aḍa-gosᵘ, p. 11a, l. 22.
m. (sg.dat. gösᵘ̈s or gāsas, Gr.Gr. 54), a grass-seller, a man who lives by selling grass, hay, straw, etc. -bāy f. his wife.
m. the name given in schools to the letter gha of the Śāradā alphabet.

m. a dip, a dive; diving, plunging; esp. becoming wet through by falling into water or mud. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to plunge (oneself or another) into water, to dip, to duck; (according to Baptists) to baptize. --dāwun -- m.inf. to cause another to plunge himself (Śiv. 1397), or a third person, into water. -gŏth f. (sg. dat. -güʦᵘ̈), diving over and over again (in a water frolic or the like). --khĕnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. 'to eat dives', to be dipped, to suffer immersion, to dive; met. to be plunged in sorrow. -khŏr (= غوطہ خور) m. a diver; anything that dips or is dipped; a sort of firework (so called because, being lighted, it is thrown into water, when it dives, and every now and then shows above the water). --lagȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. dives to be experienced; met. sorrow, caused by painful reminiscences or memories of wrongs suffered, to be experienced, to have painful memories. ¶ gŏtan gaʦhun m.inf. to go into plunges, to be distraught by a multitude of duties all occurring together at the same time.
m. narrow gold or silver lace used as an edging for cloth, a narrow fillet of brocade.

f. (sg. dat.gōṭi), a kind of chequered cloth of thirty-six squares for playing chess, causar, or similar game, a dice-board; an aim, desired object. --marüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to obtain a desired object, achieve one's object.

f. (sg. dat. gö̃ṭhi), a bolt, door-chain; a method of tying up a parcel with a special knot marked or sealed so that it cannot be opened by an unauthorized person. Cf. gã̄ṭh and gö̃ṭhᵘ̈. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to knot, fasten; to bolt, fasten (a door) (K.Pr. 76).

f. (sg. dat.gö̃ṭi), a kite, a falcon, a vulture (El. gánṭ, gáṅth, and ghánṭ; W. 114, gant; K.Pr. 65, 147, gáṅth; Rām. 973, 1629). ¶ gö̃ṭa-ôlᵘ m. a kite's nest (K.Pr. 65). -bacĕ m. the young one of a kite. -brörᵘ̈ 1 f. a paper kite (W. 114 gantbror). -pakh f. (s.g. dat. -pakhi), a kite's wing; met. a flaunting dress, the dress of a flaunter. -ṭhūl m. a kite's egg.
f. (sg. dat. gö̃ṭi), a bell, a plate of brass or mixed metal for striking the hours, a gong. ¶ gö̃ṭa-brörᵘ̈ f. a bell (not a gong, as it is hollow and has a tongue).
m. a small or moderately sized book bound in the English fashion.
f. a knot, a hard lump. Only noted in the compound shishĕr-gö̃ṭhᵘ̈, a frost-knot, i.e. an icicle (Śiv. 335). Cf. shishur and gö̃ṭh 1.
or guṭil f. a kind of axe, adze, or hatchet, with a wide cutting-edge, used for splitting logs into planks (H. vii, 12, guṭⁱlā, is guṭyulᵘ, q.v., with suff. of indef. art.).

or guṭyulᵘ m. a man who uses the gŏṭil, or adze with which planks are split from logs and then trimmed (El. gotilyí, translated 'sawyer'). In H. vii, 12 this word, with the suff. of the indef. art., becomes guṭⁱlā.
m. a kind of pocket of which the two edges can be fastened up. Cf. gŏʦürᵘ̈.
adj. (f. güʦᵘ̈), lean, thin (by nature or owing to illness, etc.) (Gr.Gr. 8, 9).
adj. (f. güṭᵘ̈ 1, dat. gacĕ), falling short, insufficient, too little, too small.

adj. (f. güṭᵘ̈ 2, dat. gacĕ), dark, not bright, not cleaned (e.g. a mirror); turbid; as subst. darkness, i.q. gaṭa (YZ. 175; Siv. 15, 251, etc.; Rām. 285, 1607). Cf. añi-goṭᵘ under onᵘ 1 and Rām. 743, 744, 974.

m. N. of a celebrated hill near Mathurā, which was lifted up and supported by Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) upon one finger for seven days to shelter the cowherds from a storm of rain sent by Indra to test Kṛṣṇa's divinity (Śiv. 701, 994, 1392). -nāth m. (sg. dat. -nāthas) the Lord of Gōvardan, N. of Kṛṣṇa.
m. a N. of the Hindū god Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) (Śiv. 180, 1320, 1383, 1417, Rām. 3).

or gōvarun conj. 3 (2 p.p. gōvᵃryōv or gōvaryōv), to be in the condition of not being thoroughly awake when one is suddenly awakened, to be still heavy with sleep (under such circumstances); to be sleepy, drowsy, genl. gōvᵃrana āmotᵘ perf. part. pass. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), become heavy with sleep as ab.

f. the place on the top of the wall on the left-hand side of the entrance to a house, where offerings to the spirits of the dead are deposited. These offerings (amongst Hindūs) continue daily for a year after death, and consist of cooked rice, sesame, clarified butter, etc.
f. N. of a wild shrub with short branches used for basket-work.
f. the heel of a shoe, that part of the sole which is under the heel and which is usually made of wood.
adv. as one would say, as it were, as if, as though, so to speak (W. 100). -ki گویا کہ adv. as if that, as it were, as if, like (K.Pr. 138).
(for 1 see p. 314a, l. 37), in the following, gȧyⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to become useless, to become unprofitable (e.g. of unavailing skill, dissipated earnings, or of food that does not nourish).
m. (for 1 see p. 314a, l. 36), N. of a small bird that haunts the reedy shores of lakes.
m. threatening, menace, reproof, addressed to a child pupil, a servant or the like. Cf. gāl (p. 282b, l. 18). gözⁱ-wôdur m. (sg. dat. - wādaras), a menace-marauder, one who robs another with menaces.
m. range, field of action, district; the range or field of influence of a heavenly body, as ascertained for the purpose of preparing horoscopes or the like (Rām. 418).

f. (sg. dat. gō̃ʦhi), a moustache (Gr.Gr. 133, K.Pr. 219, 239). ¶ gō̃ʦha wuṭhañĕ f. pl. inf. to twist the moustaches, to show that one considers oneself as good as another (in power, etc.), to stand up to a person, swagger. ¶ gō̃ʦhi mathun m.inf. to hope for help (by act or material). --wuchun -- m.inf. to look at the moustache; hence, to treat with respect. --wôlᵘ -- m. one who has plenty of helpers and backers (and whom others are consequently afraid to attack).
m. moustached, one who wears a moustache (Gr.Gr. 133). N.B. the form gō̃ʦhalad is not used (Gr.Gr. 135).
f. a pod, a seed-vessel; a musk-pod; a cocoon.
or gŏʦürᵘ̈ f. a small square bag or pocket open on one side of the square; a small purse, a bag (El.); used met. cf. khĕn 2 and khrŏv; cf. gọ̆tᵘ, p. 310b, l. 40, and canda-g., p. 172b, l. 44.
or grŏcawaṭh m. (sg. dat. gracawaṭas), any thing or person large, heavy, and globular in shape.
m. a vulture; an eagle, said to be numerous towards the south-east end of the Valley (El.). ¶ grada-hyurᵘ or gradi-hyurᵘ m. a vulture's throat; hence, great greediness, perpetual avidity.
m. a man who habitually meets a request with shouts of abuse.

m. a planet, esp. as influencing destiny (Śiv. 1477). ¶ graha-gath f. (sg. dat. -güʦᵘ̈), (in astrology) the going or motion of the planets, an unfavourable conjuncture of the planets, i.e. the favourable planets to be in unlucky conditions and the unfavourable planets in prime. -ʦār m., id.
adj. c.g. subject to an eclipse, i.e. (of food, amongst Hindūs) rendered impure by the occurrence of an eclipse, and hence not fit to be eaten afterwards.
m. (sg. dat. grahasthas), a householder (Śiv. 579, 840); the life or condition of a householder, as opposed to that of a wandering mendicant or of a hermit (Śiv. 1713).
m. a planet, i.q. grah 2, q.v. (Śiv. 489, 924, 730, 1149). ¶ grahȧdⁱ-bal m. (in astrology) an unfavourable position of the planets (Śiv. 489).
f. a female disease, hæmorrhage from the womb, chronic flooding.

f. demoniacal possession, a system of divination practised in the hill country of Kashmīr and by the Shin tribes to the north. The person believed to be possessed is also believed to be at the time endowed with the gift of prophecy. For a full description of the ceremony see Biddulph, Tribes of the Hindoo Koosh, pp. 96 ff.
f. the mistress of a house, the wife of a householder, the mother of a family (obs.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. grakanôwᵘ), to heat a liquid till it boils, to cause to boil; to cook (El. grĕk-) (Gr.Gr. 174).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. grakowᵘ), to cook in water, to stew, boil.
n.ag. (f. grakawüñᵘ̈), (of water, etc.) boiling up, boiling hot.
f. (in a shopkeeper) pride or conceit caused by the fact that a large number of customers are demanding some particular article in his stock.

f. (sg. dat. graki), boiling up, bubbling up of anything being cooked (Śiv. 1828). --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring to the boil, to heat to bubbling (of liquids being cooked). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring to the boil, as ab. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to boil up; hence, to become ripe (of corn, etc.); to ripen (of pustules in smallpox or the like); to be luxuriant (of a ripening crop). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. boiling up to commence (of liquids being cooked). ¶ graka-wôñᵘ m. boiling water; it is drunk as a remedy for fever and indigestion. -wörᵘ̈ f. a vessel in which gold ornaments are boiled in acidified water in order to clean them.

m. (sg. dat. grākas), a customer, buyer (in a shop) (K.Pr. 219, 229, YZ. 119), or a customer, client (of some professional person), in each case whether occasional or regular. -bāy f. the wife of the regular client or customer of some professional person (e.g. a barber or a flower-seller); a woman who is such a regular client. ¶ grāka-bôyᵘ m. the buyer-brother, a regular customer or purchaser of things at a shop; a regular client or customer of any professional person. -gara m. the house of such a regular client (visited regularly by the barber, flower-seller, etc., in the course of his business).

m. (sg. dat. grākas; f. grākañ, Gr.Gr. 38, 106, 136), a sec. suff. forming nouns of agency. Thus, karan-grākh, a doer; khĕna-grākh, an eater; zöñᵘ̈-grākh, a knower. See Gr.Gr. 106 for the rules for the use of this suffix. With nouns it indicates possession, when the thing possessed accompanies, but does not form part of, the possessor. Thus, lari-grākh, the owner of a house (Gr.Gr. 136). It thus often indicates a profession or trade, as in hāka-grākh, a vegetable seller (Gr.Gr. 38); gāsa-grākh, a grass-cutter (K.Pr. 178).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. grakyōv), (of heated liquids) to boil up, bubble up, boil over; to be in violent motion (of liquids) (Gr.Gr. xx). The causal of this verb is grakanāwun (Gr.Gr. 174).

m. lit. a village sacrifice, a sacrifice in which everyone in the village will take a share, and from which the sacrificing priest will gain a very large amount of fees; hence, met. an opportunity for gaining a large sum of money or making a very big profit.
m. the Indian marten, Mustela flavigula (L. 110), said to be sprung from the union of a black serpent and an iguana.
m. agitation, anxiety, misgiving (e.g. when one desires to do something at a small expenditure and finds that it is costing much more than was anticipated).
f. a feeling of disgust (for any person or thing), i.q. grāna.
f. disgust rising from surfeit, having eaten so much of anything that one loathes it. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such loathing to occur. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to condemn, blame (Gr.M.).
f. (sg. dat. grünzᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 29, 69), counting, enumeration, reckoning, computation. --karüñᵘ̈ -- m.inf. to number, reckon, count, compute (El.). ¶ grünzᵘ̈-phyurᵘ̈ counting backwards.
or grŏph m. in the following: --karun -- m.inf. to swallow, eat up (food); met. to wear anything away, make worn out; entirely to misappropriate anything entrusted to one.

m. a mouthful of food, as much as can be put into the mouth at one time [Śiv. 594, 1461 (of milk)]. Often --˚. --karun -- m.inf. to swallow; met. to misappropriate goods entrusted to one; to swallow up, to destroy (Śiv. 1352, 1480). --sö̃panun -- m.inf. swallowing or destruction to occur (Śiv. 1465).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. grôsᵘ), to swallow down, to devour in one mouthful (L.V. 22).

m. a corn-mill, a grinding mill (K.Pr. 6, 27; L. 456; Śiv. 1503, 1795, 1828; W. 2 has ghraṭᵘ, i.e. groṭᵘ). -anwār f. the revolution of a mill; met. perpetual or continual revolution (of the soul through transmigration) (Śiv. 1795, 1914). -bal m. the ground outside a village, on the bank of a river, where the village corn-mill, driven by the stream, is situated (K.Pr. 71). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give grinding; to put to the mill, to 'grind' a pupil, make him study hard; to wear down a person by refusing him any liberty. -khôrᵘ m. or -khörᵘ̈ f. in the large water-mill, the large wickerwork receptacle, which is filled with wheat and which delivers it gradually to the millstones. --lagun -- m.inf. to be put into the mill; to be worn down by being refused liberty (e.g. in a prison). -laʦhulᵘ m. a brush for sweeping up the flour or the refuse coming from a mill. -pahörᵘ̈ f. the hut on the bank of a river in which the water-mill for grinding corn is kept. -ʦakᵃj or -ʦakᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. one of the stones (upper or nether) of a mill, a millstone. It is believed that a Yĕch, or fairy, no matter how strong, cannot lift a millstone, and hence anything placed under it is safe from him (K.Pr. 141). -wôlᵘ m. a miller (K.Pr. 6).

m. the gulping sound made when swallowing food or water. Cf. griṭh and grŏṭh 1. --graṭh -- m. the series of gulping sounds made when drinking water; the similar sound made by rice when being boiled. --karun -- m.inf. to make a gulping sound when swallowing quickly.
f. a small light handmill. Cf. graṭa.

f. reproaches made to a person (esp. to a friend) for improper conducṭ, remonstrance, expostulation, admonition (Śiv. 1832, Rām. 307, 1624); complaint, accusation, blame (El. gráo). -gŏndun m. remonstrance (and) criticism, a kindly affectionate remonstrance. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to remonstrate, as ab.; to accuse, complain, blame (El.) (dat. of obj. Gr.M.). ¶ grāwa-grāv f. mutual reproaches, mutual recriminations (esp. between the relations of a bride and bridegroom, respectively, as to the alleged small amount of the dowry, etc.); frequent reproaches (not mutual).
f. striking by the wings (as a large bird attacks smaller ones); met. attack or violent oppression of a weak person by a powerful one.

f. shaking, trembling, quivering (H. vii, 11, of ears of grain); tottering, trembling (cf. āyĕ-grāyĕ, s.v. āy 2) (Rām. 1118); a jerk, sudden push causing movement (e.g. to a vessel, so as to cause the contained liquid to shake up or to be splashed out); agitation of the mind (Rām. 1742), indignation. El. spells this word gráe. Cf. brō̃ṭh-grāy and brū̃ṭhⁱ-grāy, s.v. brō̃ṭh (p. 128, col. a, l. 10, and col. b, l. 6). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to knock or push a vessel containing liquid, so as to cause the contents to be spilt. --kadüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to rinse (a cloth or an empty vessel). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be shaken or upset (of a vessel, so that the contents are spilt); to be unsteady, impermanent, not "founded on a rock" (H. ix, 12); (of the mind, etc.) to be agitated, to become filled with indignation (in this sense grāy is usually --˚ following a word signifying 'mind' or the like). --mārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause to shake (of ear-rings, K.Pr. 153). ¶ grāyĕ diñĕ, f. pl. inf. to give wavings, to cause to wave (H. vii, 11). --mārañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to flutter, tremble (of locks of hair, YZ. 64).

f. roaring, speaking with a thundering voice (Gr.Gr. 126, Śiv. 1117); loud singing, a thundering chorus (Śiv. 1614). --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to raise a roar (of a crowd of people shouting the same thing).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. grozᵘ; 2 p.p. grazōv. This verb is impersonal in the tenses formed from the past participles), to roar (e.g. of a tiger, a torrent, or thunder) (K.Pr. 9, 233; Rām. 170, 674, 971, 1331, 1501, 1567). For the n.ag. of this verb see Gr.Gr. 106.
m. Tibet barley, Hordeum hexastichon, var., an important food staple among the mountain people. The grain has not the chaff scales adhering to it, but is naked like wheat (L. 330, 341, grim).

m. (sg. dat. grimⁱtas), cattle urine, cow's urine. Hindū brides have their hair washed with a mixture of this and milk two days before the marriage (K.Pr. 112, 114, grumit). ¶ grimⁱta-gūrⁱ f. the cistern (made of a covered jar buried in the floor of a cowhouse) for collecting the cattle urine. -wôñᵘ m. a mixture of cattle urine and water (generally in the proportions of half and half).
m. compressing, squeezing, throttling. Used in the phrase hȧṭⁱ grindam dyunᵘ, see hoṭᵘ 1.
m. one of the six Kashmīr seasons (L. 326), the hot season, consisting of the months of Zēṭh (Skt. Jyaiṣṭha = May-June) and Hār (Skt. Āṣāḍha = June-July).
f. (sg. dat. grīstili), the profession of a cultivator, farming, cultivation of the soil; skill in cultivating, knowledge of farming.
m. the gulping sound made in swallowing, esp. in swallowing soft food. Cf. graṭh and grŏṭh 1.
m. a kind of thick gruel, made by boiling a little rice in much water, and then mashing it.
m. abuse, railing at a person.
m. the mutual pushing and shoving of a crowd in a confined space.

m. (sg. dat. grahanas), an eclipse of the sun or moon (Śiv. 424, Rām. 285, 438). The word is spelt grônᵘ in YZ. 268, Rām. 1391, 1629, 1771. ¶ grahana-kã̄dur m. a Hindū who does not observe fasts (even neglecting to fast on the occasion of an eclipse), and who on such occasions eats forbidden foods. -mad m. the occurrence of an eclipse.
adj. (f. grühᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ 1), fierce or cruel not only by disposition and conduct but in appearance.

m. (sg. dat. grŏkas), slight or partial cooking in water. --nĕngalun -- m.inf. to swallow one's own saliva; met. to bear or endure an insult or a wrong, to stomach an insult. --trāwun -- m.inf. (in cooking vegetables) to pour off the water in which they are being cooked (after they have been heated for but a short time and in order to put other water over them instead), to change the water in cooking; the first water is poured off to remove the dirt, so as to leave the vegetables clean. ¶ grŏka-wônᵘ m. the froth which rises at the commencement of boiling rice; this is given hot as a remedy for fever accompanied by indigestion or flatulence.
m. (sg. dat. grŏkas), swallowing (El.). ? incorr. for grŏṭh 1.
m. a great log of wood, esp. one not trimmed; met. a great man, a man of high rank and power, i.q. gonḍᵘ 2. Cf. gar-gunḍa, s.v. gara, p. 295b, l. 28.
f. a deep well in the bed of a river hidden under the water, usually in mountain streams. Cf. grühᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ 2.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gröshᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), to cause to be taken, to cause a gift to be taken by another.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gröshᵒrᵒ), to take, receive (into the hand, etc., of something given by another).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gröshᵒrᵒ. This verb is impersonal in the tenses formed from the past participles), (of a shower of rain, esp. a violent one) to stop suddenly.
m. eating up all the food before one, clearing out the dishes.
m. the spending by one member of a company of the whole of its joint earnings.
m. the gulping sound made when swallowing a liquid. Cf. graṭh and griṭh, also amañĕ-ta-grŏṭh, p. 28b, l. 21. --nĕngalun -- m.inf. to gulp down together food and liquid.
m. (sg. dat.grŏṭas), a bubo or boil occurring on the inner part of the thigh or armpit, said to be caused by excessive walking. Cf. grüṭᵘ̈.
f. the heel, esp. the tendo Achillis; according to El., also the calf of the leg, or the leg genl. (El. also graz).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. grŏʦowᵘ), to splash about, shake up (a liquid in a vessel).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. grŏʦyōv, Gr.Gr. 226), to be splashed about (as a liquid in a vessel), shaken up, agitated. Cf. grakun.
f. a deep place in a river, esp. in the curve of a large river. Cf. gröñᵘ̈.
(? spelling), N. of a certain soil, containing a large proportion of clay (L. 319). The word appears to be properly guroṭᵘ, q.v., or its f. gurüṭᵘ̈.
f. the hard core of a boil not yet ripe, i.e. before matter has fully formed in it. Cf. grŏṭh 2 and gũ̄̈ṭh.

or grūstᵘ m. (sg. dat. grīstis), a farmer, husbandman, cultivator of the soil; a tenant farmer (El.; K.Pr. 69, 129, 224; L. 456; H. ix, 4, 7). According to El. the word is pronounced grūst in Śrīnagar and grōst elsewhere. ¶ grīstⁱ-bāy f. a farmer's wife (H. ix, 1). -gara m. a village husbandman's house, in which he lives; the condition of such a householder. -kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈, f. a rudely made peasant's kangrī or portable fireplace (K.Pr. 129). -pacĕ adj. c.g. equal in rank to a husbandman, a fellow-husbandman. The expression is used in arranging marriages, etc.

m. dust, clouds of dust; vexation, soreness, ill-feeling, affliction, grief; hence (in Kāshmīrī) the suffering from a violent internal pain (such as headache, etc.); unwillingness to do some work ordered by another.

f. a female sheep, a ewe (El. gaub and gob, K.Pr. gub, gabi, or gabih), (K.Pr. 5, 36, 119, 192, 218; W. 18; L. 463, gab; Rām. 94). ¶ gabi-buthᵘ m. 'ewe-faced', one whose face shows that he is easily frightened, timid-faced. gabi-buthi rāmahūnᵘ, a wolf with a sheep's face (K.Pr. 63, W. 21). -dŏd m. ewe's milk (YZ. 90). -gūdᵘ m. one who is vile and impotent, a mean worthless fellow. Cf. gūdᵘ. -māz m. ewe's flesh, ewe-mutton (considered to be flavourless). -rôchᵘ m. a ewe-guardian, a shepherd. -röchⁱ-bāy f. a shepherd's wife.
(? spelling), m. Viburnum cotinifolium, V. fœtens (El. gúch).

or gūḍᵘ (Gr.Gr. 20) adj. (f. gṻḍ or gǖḍᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 20), hidden, invisible; (of a story, poem, etc.) difficult to understand, difficult, mysterious; (of a road or the like) difficult to be traversed or travelled over, almost impassable, difficult of access or issue; (of a person) a dolt, an idiot, one who no matter how one teaches him cannot learn what is taught.
(cf. گذر) or (Rām. 1496) guzarun conj. 3 (2 p.p. gudaryōv), to happen, befall (esp. of some trouble, grief, or calamity), (H. v, 9, where gudariv is poet. for gudaryōv, viii, 5).
f. an unchaste woman (one who by her unchastity has diseased private parts). Cf. gōda and gūdᵘ.
m. a cow's tethering rope (one end fastened round the neck and the other to a peg in the ground) (K.Pr. 219).
f. in guḍārĕ gĕwañĕ f. pl. inf. to refuse to carry out an order by making pretended excuses.
m. obsc. the anus, cf. gōda; vulva (El.). Cf. Gr.Gr. 19.
f., i.q. gurᵘ̈ 1. This is the form in use towards Islāmābād (El.).
m. a small round metal pot, shaped like a bowl (El.), a lōṭā. -golᵘ m. the top or mouth of a lōṭā,the part above the neck. -ʦokᵘ m. the bowl of a lōṭā.
m. a child's swinging cot, a swing.
f. the 'thundering' of the human voice in abuse, loud roaring in abuse.
or (Gr.M.) gugūstulᵘ m. a swing (in which people swing themselves for enjoyment); a swing perch (in a parrot's cage) (Gr.M.). --trāwun --, m.inf. to swing oneself in a swing (Gr.M.).

f. a kind of blanket worn on journeys in wet weather. One edge is gathered up and fastened in a bunch. This is put over the head, and the remainder falls over the rest of the body, thus protecting the clothes beneath from the rain.
m. dirty, muddy, etc. (of water or the like) (Gr.M.). Cf. gọ̆lᵘ.

m. cow-dung; buffalo-dung (K.Pr. 251); manure (El. guh, q.v. for description of the various methods of applying manure) (L. 459, gu). Cf. gŏh. ¶ guhⁱ-ambār m. a pile of cow-dung, a dunghill. -bonᵘ m. a medium-sized dung-heap (Śiv. 126). -gān m. a room in which cow-dung is stored (esp. by cowkeepers who own many cattle). -khürᵘ̈ f. a woman engaged in collecting or clearing away cow-dung; hence, met. any woman dirty in person and clothing. -kyomᵘ m. a certain worm bred in cow-dung. -lôdᵘ m. a large pile or stack of cow-dung, collected in winter with the object of drying it in the summer. -lōla m. a fool (in conversation, etc.). --liwun -- m. inf. to plaster with cow-dung. -lyobᵘ m. the amount of cow-dung evacuated by the animal at one time. -nôrᵘ m. the rectum. -ryūnzᵘ m. (sg. dat. -rīnzis), the scarabæus beetle. It makes balls of cow-dung and mud and rolls them along. According to popular tradition it has quarrelled with the sea and makes these balls in order to fill it up (Śiv. 1647, 1648, Rām. 436).
f. a Gujorᵘ woman (Gr.Gr. 39). See gujorᵘ.

gujur, or gujurᵘ m. (f. gujaröñᵘ̈, q.v.s.v., and gujȧrⁱ-bāy, see bel.), a man of a certain pastoral tribe which roams over the hills of Kashmīr and the neighbouring countries, the Gujurs of Swāt, and the Gūjars of Western India (Gr.Gr. 39). ¶ gujȧrⁱ-bāy f. the wife of a Gujorᵘ. -künḍᵘ̈ f. a Gujorᵘ camp. -koṭᵘ m. a Gujorᵘ lad. -küṭᵘ̈ f. a Gujorᵘ lass.

orgȧjⁱ f. the opening of a native cooking-range through which fuel is fed (K.Pr. 26, 48, 54, 64, 119, 256). Cf. dān 1, gag, and golᵘ 1. ¶ gajĕ-ṭhorᵘ m. the cover or door (usually of earthenware) of this opening.

or gūjᵘ̈ f. the kernel of a fruit (e.g. of a walnut, a cocoa-nut, or water-chestnut) (Gr.M., K.Pr. 66, 100, Śiv. 1807); the kernel or inner meaning of anything, intelligible only to the initiated. Cf. gūlᵘ 2 and Gr.Gr. 36. ¶ gōjĕ-pĕndulᵘ or -panzulᵘ m. a complete, unbroken kernel of a walnut (i.e. all the four sections unseparated from each other). -tīl m. oil derived from kernels (e.g. walnut-oil). -ʦhar f. a large kind of basket in which walnut kernels and the like are carried about for sale.
m. a deadly epidemic affecting first the lower animals and subsequently human beings, plague.
m. wheat bran, the husk of ground wheat when sifted apart (K.Pr. 130, translated 'straw').

m. a rose (YZ. 212); a flower (K.Pr. 47, 56, 164; Rām. 22, 204, 438, etc.). gul-andām گل اندام adj. c.g. having a body like a rose or a flower, delicate, slender, graceful (Rām. 185, 394, 1223). gul-ĕ-anār گل انار (Rām. 646, 1018), i.q. gulnār, q.v. s.v. gul-dasta گل دستہ m. a handful of roses, a posy, a bouquet, a bunch of flowers. -hȧtⁱ f. N. of a kind of rice (requiring to be cooked in sixteen parts of water to one of rice, and especially suitable as an easily digested food for invalids). -kand گل قند m. conserve of roses, candied roses. -ĕ-kōsam m. safflower (Rām. 1006). -marg m. N. of a well-known flowery valley about 3,000 feet above the valley of Kashmīr, much frequented by Europeans in the heat of summer. Cf. El. s.v. -shan گلشن m. a rose (or flower) garden (YZ. 232, Rām. 319, 369). -ĕ-sōsan گل سوسن m. the white iris, commonly planted on graves (L. 248). -ĕ-tölīm گل تعلیم m. the pattern of a Kashmīr shawl intended for the manufacturer, that he may see the design of the shawl. Cf. ganḍan-wôlᵘ, s.v. ganḍun 2, and tölīm. -zār گلزار m. a rose (or flower) garden (YZ. 46, Rām. 22, 188); a bed of roses (Rām. 1664).
m. a species of bracelet, massive and open (El.).
m. the act of churning or beating up by hand of two liquids together (e.g. curdled milk and water).

f. N. of a certain plant, the leaves of which grow along the ground, and the juice of which is used as a cooling drink in fevers, consumption, etc.; according to L. 76, it is an internal styptic. El. has gul, Cichorium intybus, and gúl, Plantago major. Cf. baḍa-gula, s.v. baḍa. -byôlᵘ m. the seed of this plant, used as a medicine for dysentery. -hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), the leaf of this plant, which is boiled like a vegetable to extract the juice used as ab. -ras m. the juice, as ab. -wạthᵃr m., i.q. -hākh ab.

m. a kind of sweet cake (wheat-flower, sugar, curdled milk, with anise and cardamom seeds, made into balls or dumplings and fried in clarified butter). -gorᵘ m. a man who makes and sells these cakes. -kroʦhᵘ m. the ladle he uses.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gulovᵘ), to roll something in the mouth, to mumble it without swallowing it.
or gul-ĕ anār گل انار m. the flower of the pomegranate (Rām. 646, 1018); hence, as adj. c.g. very red, crimson (Śiv. 13).
m. one who takes care of a herd of horses during the pasturage season (El.). Cf. galwān 2.

m. the forearm, the arm between the elbow and the wrist (K.Pr. 10, Rām. 1305, 1418, 1538); the wrist (El.). --˚ it often means one of a pair (of armlets or the like). Cf. bȧhⁱ 1 and bāwoṭᵘ. ¶ gulⁱ ālawȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to wave the forearms; esp. to pass the hands over the head and face in order to pacify, or to show affection (K.Pr. 13). --ganḍȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to bind the forearms, to stand in a reverent attitude with the arms folded in front (H. v, 9); to stand with the hands folded together in reverence (Śiv. 718, 721, 791, 1155, 1296, 1394, 1457, 1504; Rām. 494, 505, 852). -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), one whose forearm is cut, i.e. who has had his hand cut off at the wrist, either as a punishment for theft or as the result of disease (cf. Rām. 1305). ¶ guli-myūṭhᵘ m. a kiss on the forearm; hence, a bracelet or other ornament fastened on the forearm of a child on the occasion of some festival, or on that of a bride at a wedding, by the relations or connexions by marriage. Cf. L. 258, 271, and Rām. 1093. -ʦopᵘ m. a bite on the forearm (cf. Rām. 1538). -walun-hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -walüñᵘ̈-hishᵘ̈), one, e.g. an official, who has fallen under the influence of a plausible servant or friend. -walun-lāyĕkh adj. (f. -walüñᵘ̈-lāyĕkh), id.

m. (pl. dat. gōlĕn Gr.Gr. 56), the kernel of a fruit; esp. the kernel of the water-chestnut (Trapa bispinosa) (Gr.Gr. 36, 56). El. golí and gúlyí, both fem. Cf. gôrᵘ and görᵘ̈, also gūjⁱ. El. has also gúl, Plantago major. Cf. gula 2. ¶ gūlⁱ-kuʦorⁱ m. (f. kuʦarĕñ), a water-chestnut sheller, a man who makes a living by shelling water-chestnuts and selling the kernels. The f. is either his wife or a woman who earns her living in this way.
f. a small ball, a bullet (K.Pr. 86); a pill. Cf. gōla 1. --layüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to hit with a bullet (obj. in dat., Gr.M.). --trāwüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to fire, or discharge, a bullet (Gr.M.).
f. a widow woman who takes service as a concubine. Cf. gōla 2. ¶ gōli-kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a son begotten on a widowed maidservant.

m. sweat, perspiration (Gr.Gr. 136, Rām. 1041, 1042). --ḍalun -- m.inf. sweat to burst out owing to modesty or awe. -hotᵘ adj. (f.-hüʦᵘ̈), covered with sweat, sweaty, all in a muck of sweat (Gr.Gr. 136). -shrān m. a sweat-bath, the bursting forth of sweat, so that one is as it were bathed in it. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. sweat to come, guma ām, I am sweating (K.Pr. 12).
m. doubt, surmise, conjecture, opinion (Gr.M., Rām. 231, 463). --karun -- m.inf. to believe, fancy, conjecture (Gr.M., YZ. 199).
m. slight dirtiness, smuttiness (of something darkened in colour by dirt) (Gr.Gr. 140).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. gumanyōv), to be discoloured, dirtied, (of something white) to become or be grey (Gr.Gr. xix).
m. an agent, superintendent, manager of a business (El., Gr.M.).
f. a kind of cloth, dimity.
m. a kind of firework, a bomb fired into the air, and there exploded.
m. an arch, vault; a dome, cupola. -shĕbd m. the sound of a dome; hence, an echo.
or gumunᵘ adj. (f. gumüñᵘ̈), slightly dirtied, discoloured, blackened, smutted (Gr.Gr. 130).
f. a missing or losing of one's way; erring, going astray (H. vii, 12).

f. a pack-saddle, a pair of large saddle-bags used for conveying grain, etc., on an animal's back. They are generally made of goat's hair (El.) (YZ. 421, 427, abl. gon̄ih). guni-tolᵘ m. one side or sack of such a pack-saddle.
m. a colouring material made up of red chalk and other materials, used to polish gold ornaments, a kind of jeweller's rouge.

f. (sg. dat. gunᵃsi), a poisonous, round-headed, short, thick serpent found in the mountains of Kashmīr. It is said to be black on the back and yellowish on the belly. It is a foot and a half long, and, according to some natives, ash-coloured. Its bite is often fatal (El., q.v. s.vv. ganas and gunas for further particulars; see also L. 155, K.Pr. 79, 212, W. 122, Rām. 1469). ¶ gunᵃsa-bacĕ m. a young gunasa; met. a man who habitually gives sorrow to others. -pūtᵘ m., id.
(? spelling), m. a crown, a diadem (El.). Probably incorr. for gọ̆ndᵘ, q.v.
m., i.q. gonḍᵘ 2, q.v. Cf. gar-gunḍa s.v. gara, and K.Pr. 65.
adj. c.g. drowsy, sleepy; (of a sick man) comatose.

or gunusᵘ m. a kind of metal bracelet or armlet. According to El., s.v. gunus, it is a small band adorned with beads, etc., and is worn by Musalmān women. ¶ gunȧsⁱ-dāv f. such an armlet worn thin by use. -horᵘ m. a pair of armlets. -jūrⁱ f., id.

m. (sg. dat. günzᵘ̈s or ganzas Gr.Gr. 54), a tanner, a currier (K.Pr. 65 gaṅz). -phakh m. (sg. dat. -phakas), 'a currier-stink,' a currier who is poor, wretched, and evil-smelling owing to his occupation; met. any vile person.
(f. guñᵘ̈), suff. added to a numeral meaning 'fold', 'times', as in dŏgunᵘ, twofold, double; aiṭha-gunᵘ, eightfold. Cf. gonᵘ 1.

f. (for 2 see gonᵘ), a piece or fragment, esp. of flesh or fish (H. viii, 13; x, 7; in each case pieces of a python); often --˚, as in gāḍa-güñᵘ̈, lumps of fish (see gāḍ and K.Pr. 205, -gani), manz-güñᵘ̈, the middle slice of a fish (K.Pr. 136, -gani). ¶ gañi-bāgay f. dividing out by bits (e.g. a tree cut up and divided amongst people).
m. N. of a village at the east foot of the Taḵẖt-ĕ Sulaimān or Gōpādri Hill near Śrīnagar (RT.Tr. II, 290, 454, Śiv. 953).
m. giving charity or conferring benefits privately, "letting not the left hand know what the right hand doeth."

m. (sg. dat. gupanas), an animal of the cattle class (bulls, cows, calves, generally) (K.Pr. 219, Śiv. 1464); a quadruped (El.); met. a man who leads the life of and has the morals of cattle; pl. cattle (Gr.Gr. 152, K.Pr. 71, 227). ¶ gupan-ḍangij f. a platform built on one side of a cowhouse, on which, for the sake of its warmth, people live in the winter. Cf. ḍangij for particulars. -gān m. a cowhouse. -gūrᵘ m. a cowherd, a milkman, a dairyman. These men in the spring-time collect large herds of cattle, belonging to others, and drive them away to the mountains to graze. They take their wives and families with them (El. gŏpan-gúr; K.Pr. 172). -khĕjⁱ or -khë̆jᵘ̈ f. a moderately sized herd of cattle. -khyolᵘ m. a large herd of cattle, such as is driven out to the mountains for grazing (Gr.Gr. 152). -nĕnd f. a method of weeding wet rice-fields by causing cattle to splash up and down the wet fields of mud (L. 327, 463). -rôchᵘ or (El.)-rachan-wôlᵘ m. a cattle herd, a man who drives out cattle for grazing and watches them. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who possesses herds; one rich in cattle (Gr.Gr. 136).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. gupᵘ; impve. sg. 2, guph), to hide, conceal; conj. part. gupith used as adv. secretly (Rām. 21, 519).
f. a woman as stupid as cattle, a stupid woman (f. of gupun, cattle).
m. in gūrukᵘmundī m. Sphæranthus mollis (El.). Cf. mundī.

for guroṭᵘ, q.v., in the following:--gura-dāñĕ m. a kind of paddy with the husk of a light-tawny colour, and large white rice-grains. -kanōra m. another kind of paddy, 'the light-tawny slave.' It has the tip of the husk light-tawny coloured and its grain white. -küʦhᵘ̈ f. a kind of shrub growing in the wilds. It is used for making the kāngrī or Kāshmīrī portable brazier. Cf. köñᵘ̈ 2. -kāʦurᵘ adj. (f. -kāʦürᵘ̈), (of a man or a beast) of a light-tawny complexion or colour. -mushikh or -mushᵉ̆kh f. (sg. dat. -mushki), 'light-tawny musk,' a kind of paddy with light-tawny husk and sweet-scented pale-yellow grain. -ṭö̃jᵘ̈ f.'the light-tawny pear', another similar paddy, but with a large white grain.
m. the condition of being of a light-tawny colour, light tawniness. Cf. guroṭᵘ.
or gūra-gūra m. swinging, dandling, rocking (a child) (Śiv. 329, 1321, 1381; Rām. 210, 211, 1040); met. a gentle rocking of a house by an earthquake or the like.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. guraṭyōv), to be light tawny coloured, to be fair coloured (Gr.Gr. xix).
adj. c.g. pompous, haughty; a bully, tyrannous.
(? gura-gāsa, cf. gura), m. a kind of medicinal herb. The pounded leaves are applied externally for snake-bites and panther wounds (L. 76).
m.onomat. a rumble, thunder. --karun -- m.inf. to rumble, to thunder (K.Pr. 116, gar gar).
f.onomat. a native tobacco-pipe, a kind of huqqa, a hubble-bubble, so called from the bubbling sound it makes (El. guriguri).
m.pl. a herd, troop, or collection of horses, when limited to a certain number (Gr.Gr. 93).
(? spelling), m. the Himalayan snow-cock, Tetraogallus himalayensis, the Rām cikōr of sportsmen (L. 118).

adj. (f. sg. nom. gurüṭᵘ̈, dat. guracĕ), of a light-tawny colour, light brown. This word often takes the form gura (q.v.) when ˚--. ¶ gurüṭᵘ̈ më̆ʦᵘ̈ f. a kind of slimy yellow earth used for plastering. It is found in the hills and principally employed for decorating town houses. (Cf. grutu.) --rab -- f. mud made by mixing this earth with water.
m. (sg. dat. guranas), a certain small fish inhabiting the streams and morasses (L. 158, gúran; W. 123). It is said to have a delicate taste.
m. (sg. dat. guranas), a bunch (of grapes or the like) (El., K.Pr. 255). Cf. dach.

m. (sg. dat. gurasas), skim milk (L. 462); buttermilk, milk and water which has been churned and from which the butter has been taken. The Kāshmīrīs are very fond of this (El., K.Pr. 73, 78, 87, 241; Śiv. 1461). gurus-wurus id. (El.). ¶ guras-gūrᵘ m. (f. -gūrᵘ̈), a buttermilk seller, a cowherd who lives by selling buttermilk. The f. is a female seller. -krörᵘ̈ m. a kind of curd cake made by boiling buffalo buttermilk. -kᵃy f. a buttermilk vessel; a vessel in which milk is churned to buttermilk. -kyomᵘ m. the worm which breeds in sour buttermilk; met. a baby which is very tiny. -nörᵘ̈ f. a kind of small earthen vessel, narrow at the top, used for holding buttermilk or the like. -ʦoḍᵘ m. a kind of earthen tub or vessel in which buttermilk is kept; such a vessel full of butter-milk. -wörᵘ̈ f. a very small vessel used for ladling buttermilk, or similar uses.

m. (f. gurᵘ̈ 1, q.v.), a horse (K.Pr. 71-4; W. 9, 154; L. 461; Rām. 921, 1322 ff.; H. iii, 8; x, 3, 5); the knight (in chess). ¶ gurⁱ-bachēra m. a colt, a young horse not yet fit for riding. -jūrⁱ f. a pair of horses, esp. two horses well matched in strength (Gr.Gr. 82). -khĕjⁱ f. a small troop of horses. Cf. -khyolᵘ bel. -khạpᵘ̈ṭᵘ̈ f. a small lean horse or mare, a half-starved pony. -khorᵘ m. a kind of grass with circular leaves, growing in lakes or marshes. -khyolᵘ m. a troop of horses, esp. a herd or troop let loose in the forest to feed (Gr.Gr. 152). -lĕd f. (sg. dat. -lë̆zᵘ̈), horse-dung (cf. K.Pr. 73). -loṭᵘ m. a small weak lean horse, a half-starved pony. -laṭᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. 'a stick of a horse', a small weak lean horse or mare, a half-starved pony horse or mare. -māz m. horseflesh; met. human flesh in an unhealthy condition, the merest scratch on which leads to purulent sores. -paḍur m. a horse's hoof. -pūtᵘ m. a colt (K.Pr. 104). -rēmph f. dim. (sg. dat. -rēmpi Gr.Gr. 66), a poor little horse (spoken in pity) (Gr.Gr. 163). -rᵃsh f. horses' mutual hatred (arising immediately on seeing each other); met. such hatred when it occurs between human beings. -sondᵘ adj. (f. -sünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to a horse. -sŏʦal f. a certain plant, a kind of mallow (sŏʦal) with large round leaves. When these are broken a milky juice exudes which blisters the skin. -ṭiñ f. a strong taste or desire for equitation. -ṭaph m. (sg. dat. -ṭapas), a blow from a horse, either from its head or from its leg. -ṭüṭᵘ̈ f. a small horse, a pony. -ʦūr m. a horse-thief, one who steals horses and carries them off to a distance for sale. -wāl m. horsehair, esp. the hair of a horse's tail. -wôlᵘ m. a horse-owner; one in charge of horses, a groom. ¶ guri khasun m.inf. to mount a horse, to ride (K.Pr. 72). --karañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to mount the high horse; met. to get on another's shoulder, to declare one's intention to disobey one's superiors as a commencement to making them subservient to oneself. --wasun -- or guri-pĕṭhawasun m.inf. to dismount, get off a horse (K.Pr. 72, H. xii, 2). ¶ guris-kĕth or -pĕṭh adv. on horseback (Gr.Gr. 44). --khasun -- m.inf. to mount a horse (Śiv. 788; H. ii, 11; iii, 8). --wŏthun -- m.inf., id. (H. ii, 6).

m. (sg. dat. gūris, but acc. pl. gōrĕn, Gr.Gr. 56, K.Pr. 114, Śiv. 1423), a cowkeeper, cowherd, milkman, a man of the cowherd caste (K.Pr. 63, 71, 72; W. 141; Śiv. 990, 1000, 1055, 1322, 1388, 1390, 1837; H. xi, 12, 13); a milk-seller (El.). One of the four classes into which the Mihtar or Wātul caste is divided is the cowherd class (El.). ¶ gūrⁱ-bāy f. a cowherd's wife (Gr.Gr. 35, Śiv. 1493, H. xi, 12) (a cowherdess is gūrᵘ̈, q.v.). -dȧjⁱ or -düjᵘ̈ f. a cowherd's plot, the plot of land where a cowherd collects his cattle, dries his cowdung, and the like. -gāv f. a cowherd's cow, a fine fat healthy well-cared-for cow that gives plenty of milk. -hakhur m. (sg. dat. -hakharas), a cowherd's bull, a fine fat bull kept by cowherds for breeding purposes; met. a fool. -khọ̆bᵘ m. a kind of padded cap worn by cowherds. -pȧjⁱ or -püjᵘ̈ f. a large kind of wide-mouthed basket woven from twigs, used by cowherds for carrying cowdung, grass, etc. -polᵘ m. a basket similar to the foregoing but larger. -pyār m. cowherd's love; friendship of a fool (who only does harm when his help is invoked).
f. a cowherdess, a milkmaid (K.Pr. 215) (a cowherd's wife is gūrⁱ-bāy). See gūrᵘ.

f. (for 2 see gorᵘ 2; sg. abl. gari 2, for 1 see gara, p. 296a, l. 49), a space of twenty-four minutes, a ghaṛī of India (K.Pr. 120, Rām. 947) [two and a half of these are considered to be equal to an English hour (K.Pr. 102).
