Cf. ḍāy; it contains 60 ʦyuhᵘ of 24 seconds each (K.Pr. 176)]; any indefinite short space of time; any particular moment of time (Śiv. 839); a watch, a clock; a gong; a native instrument for measuring time on the principle of a clepsydra (El. gȧir). garĕ-manz, at the hour (K.Pr. 67, W. 154). suli-gari (H. v, 7, sōli-gārē, m.c.), at dawntime, at dawn. mandiñi gari, at midday (K.Pr. 228). patimi gari, during the last hour (of anything, such as the travail of childbirth, life, the day, etc.) (K.Pr. 167). ¶ gari gari adv. at every ghaṛī, frequently, again and again [K.Pr. 70; Śiv. 75, 246 (garē, m.c.), 416, 1069, 1412]. ¶ garāh f. a single gharī, just twenty-four minutes; adv.  sometimes, occasionally, now and then. garāh... garāh, at one time... at another time (K.Pr. 9; Śiv. 537, 769-78; Rām. 920-3, 1536-8).

f. one of the strings supporting the scale-pans of a balance. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the scale-string to go, i.e. one of the strings to slip over the end of one arm of the balance so as to weigh incorrectly.
f. ? a receptacle. Cf. danda-gūrᵘ̈, s.v. dand 1 and grimⁱta gūrᵘ̈, s.v. grimith.
f., i.q. gŏril, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 143). Cf. gōrözᵘ̈.
adj. c.g. violent, furious, angry, wrathful, passionate (Gr.M.).

m. (sg. dat. guṭhas), the place in a village where cattle congregate, or which is suitable for such a purpose; a country village. ¶ guṭha-hūnᵘ m. (f. -hūñᵘ̈), a dog of the cattle-pens; met. a wandering shameless fellow, who goes about from village to village begging at every house.
f. (sg. dat.gūṭi), a certain insulting gesture made by showing the closed fist, with the top of the thumb projecting outside between the second and third fingers. Cf. gōcĕ-büdᵘ̈rᵘ̈r, p. 275b, l. 20.
f. (sg.dat. gũ̄̈ṭhi), the hard core of an incipient boil or bubo. (?) a tumour behind the ear (El. gãnt). Cf. grüṭᵘ̈.
f. a fat stupid woman (f. of gūṭhᵘ, Gr.Gr. 38).
m. (f. gūṭhiñ q.v.), a fat stupid lout (Gr.Gr. 38).
f. a bunch, clump, cluster; a tassel, a skein, etc. (of embroidery, thread, etc.). Common --˚.
f. a tied-up bundle or package, a parcel.
m. a village inhabited only by cowherds, a station of herdsmen.
adj. (f. guyᵘ̈jᵘ̈ or guyijⁱ), made, or consisting, of wheat. guyulᵘ ôṭᵘ m. wheat flour.

m. (sg. dat. guyanas), straw left uneaten by cattle, i.e. the portion of their fodder which they leave uneaten, refuse fodder (K.Pr. 252). ¶ guyĕn-bodᵘ m. a small bundle of refuse straw-fodder. -gāsa m., i.q. guyun. -köñᵘ̈ a small heap of refuse straw-fodder. -lŏʦhürᵘ̈ f. a bundle of refuse straw-fodder. -thôpᵘ m. a handful or so of the same. -tulᵘ m. a small amount of the same. -zanḍ m., id.

m. a watch-house (El.); a custom-house, octroi-post. -bān گذر بان m., i.q. -wān, bel. -hūnᵘ m. an octroi-post hound, a tyrannical, evil collector of octroi. -wān m. a watchman (El.); a collector of octroi or customs. -wān-bāy f. his wife. -wöñᵘ̈ f. a female octroi-collector; hence, met. a pugnacious, abusive woman.
m. passing time, passing life, living; life; a sufficiency to support life (K.Pr. 201, guzrán), course of life; subsistence, livelihood, employment (Gr.M., H. xi, 19).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. -rôwᵘ), to pass time, etc. (Śiv. 1624); hence, to submit to the changes of fortune with indifference, to endure such and forget them; to make to pass on, to forward (El.). Cf. gudarun (p. 278b, l. 13). This verb is impersonal in the tenses derived from the p.p. (Gr.Gr. 19).
(? f.), payment, tribute; an alienation of a portion of the revenue of a village in favour of someone (L. 449).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. guzaryōv), to pass, go, elapse; to happen, occur, befall (Rām. 1496). Cf. gudarun (p. 278b, l. 13).
f. a quarrelsome, abusive, shameless woman. Cf. hazurᵘ.
f. a woman who has burnt herself on her husband's funeral pyre, a 'suttee'. Cf. gath karüñᵘ̈, p. 311a, l. 36.
(L.V. 22), i.q. gāh 1 (p. 280b, l. 4), q.v. Cf. gāsh or gwāsh (p. 308a, l. 48).

f. N. of a certain wild thorny shrub with white flowers. According to El. (s.v. gíwáin) it is a species of Elæagnus; (L. 74), Elæagnus parvifolia (gaun). gwāñĕ f.pl. the fruit of the ab. They are said to be like small plums.
or or giyān گیان m. knowledge; esp. knowledge of divine things, divine wisdom (L.V. 60; K.Pr. 190; Śiv. 26, 154, 247, 854, 950, 992, etc.; Rām. 39, 1683, 1731-2).
m. a bundle (of grass, sticks, etc.). Cf. gë̆ḍᵘ̈ (p. 276b, l. 43).
or adj. c.g. one who possesses knowledge, esp. knowledge of divine things (Śiv. 1514, 1591), as in ātma-gyönī, one who possesses knowledge of the soul as one with the Supreme Spirit (Rām. 1683).
m. a heap of straw, chaff, etc. -dāñĕ m. threshed paddy mixed with blind husks, chaff, and other impurities.
adj. (f. gë̆ʦᵘ̈), lean, skinny (by nature), esp. of children.
m. in gyundᵘgyundᵘ karun m.inf. to give unwholesome food to an invalid.

m. (sg. dat. gīris, abl. gēri), spinning of the head, giddiness, dizziness, vertigo (from disease or from turning round and round) (El. also ghyūrᵘ) (Rām. 922). --anun -- m.inf. to bring spinning of the head; met. to worry or torment a person by setting him a very difficult or hopeless task. --lārun -- m.inf. to be worried by taking great but useless trouble over something that is hopelessly ruined. --lārawun -- m.inf., i.q. --anun, ab. --syūrᵘ -- m. (sg. dat. gīris-sīris, and so on), whirling of the head and the other accompanying symptoms (turning round and round, distress, languor, sensation of darkness, exhaustion, and so on).
m. (sg.dat. gīris, abl. gēri), land in a lake made up of the matted roots of thatching and similar grass, used --˚ as in pĕʦi-gyūrᵘ, a clump of mat-grass.
m. (sg. dat. gīris, abl. gēri), red chalk, red ochre. Cf. gīrᵘ̈ (p. 297a, l. 9). ¶ gēri-rȧngⁱ adj. c.g. coloured with red ochre; having a colour similar to that of red ochre.

m. sobbing; the upward explosion of breath caused by violent weeping, etc. ¶ gitⁱ gaʦhȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. sobbing to occur, words to be broken (by grief, etc.). ¶ gitĕn aʦun m.inf. to enter (the stage) of sobbings, to speak with voice broken by sobbing; to give forth the death-rattle, to be at the point of death.
m. (sg. dat. gᵃchas), a kind of edible mushroom, morel (L. 462 guchī). Cf. kana-gᵃch.
or gah m. the act of grinding, rubbing down to powder, trituration (Gr.Gr. 124). Cf. gᵃhun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. gᵒhᵒ, f. gᵘ̈hᵘ̈ orgᵘ̈shᵘ̈; 2 p.p. gᵃhyōv, gᵃshyōv or gᵃshōv. According to Gr.Gr. 210 and 225, only gᵘ̈shᵘ̈ and gashyōv are the correct forms, but the others also occur), to grind, pulverize, triturate; to polish, wear smooth by trituration. gᵒhᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. gᵘ̈hᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ or gᵘ̈shᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), ground, triturated; polished, worn smooth.
m. a sudden display of energy (in one not previously energetic) (K.Pr. 68, gĕr). --nīrith yunᵘ -- m.inf. suddenly to display energy in the middle of some work.
m. breaking to pieces, a smash. badanas gōs gᵃrbāl, (he fell down, and) his body was smashed to pieces (Rām. 1411).
m.onomat. the hum of a spinning-wheel or similar rapidly revolving instrument.

m. ordure, of a human being or of a dog (K.Pr. 85, gasuí for gᵃsᵃy; spelt gĕs in K.Pr. 114, and gus, ib. 77). --mathun -- m.inf. to beat (defile with) ordure; met. publicly to disgrace, publicly put to shame by abuse, etc. (esp. some respectable person). ¶ gᵃsa-cār m. pain caused by constipation. -ḍȧkhⁱjĕ or ḍȧngⁱjĕ f.pl. the receptacle for ordure, the rectum. -dūrᵘ̈ f. a lane in a village or town in which ordure, etc., is allowed to lie about, a stinking lane. -gọ̆bur m. (sg. dat. -gŏbaras), a son of ordure, a naughty, troublesome boy. Cf. -kūrᵘ̈, bel. -gurᵘ m. (f. -gurᵘ̈), an ordure-horse, one who is like a horse in regard to easing himself; a man who habitually goes to stool several times a day. -gᵃs f. diarrhœa. -khorᵘ adj. (f. -khürᵘ̈), 'an eater of filth,' hence one who is personally filthy, dressed in filthy clothes, and habitually has a filthy smell. -kūrᵘ̈ f. a daughter of ordure, a naughty, troublesome girl. Cf. -gọ̆bur, ab. -kyomᵘ m. a worm in ordure (whether at the time of emission or in corrupted ordure). -lyobᵘ m. a large lump of ordure. -malawāy m. causeless anger frequently indulged in by one to whom such anger is natural. -motᵘ adj. (f. -müʦᵘ̈), a madman who rolls in filth and covers himself with it. -nolᵘ m. a rough and dirty cowry. -nolᵘ baith dyunᵘ m.inf. easy success to come unexpectedly. -nĕngürᵘ̈ f. an unhealthy fragment of ordure (not emitted in properly formed fæces). -phakh m. (sg. dat. -phaki), the stink of ordure. -pōn m. an anus defiled with ordure. -shōda m. a man who by nature is often in a furious rage, using at the time filthy abuse. -trang or -trĕng f. sudden and unexpected evacuation by an infant in arms, or child taken into one's arms. -ṭaṭhüjᵘ̈ f. a wooden vessel for carrying away or for retaining ordure. -ʦūr m. an ordure-thief, one who evacuates in a prohibited place (e.g. a garden). -yĕch m. (sg. dat. -yĕchas), a demon who haunts places where ordure is deposited; met. an ugly man of terrifying appearance. -zĕv f. an ordure-tongue, a tongue which utters calumnies or rude or indecent remarks. ¶ gᵃsᵃy m. only ordure, nothing but ordure (K.Pr. 85).
adj. c.g. ordurous, horribly ugly and filthy (usually of something inanimate).
m. swiftness of the current of a river; met. a rapid torrent (of words), a quick inrush (of wealth), and so on.

m. (sg. dat. gᵃṭapas), sudden and unexpected death or destruction without any apparent cause (such as sickness, a blow, or the like). ¶ gᵃṭapa adv. suddenly, unexpectedly (u.w. vbs. of hindering or the like).
f. (sg. dat. gᵃti, Gr.Gr. 70), great swiftness or rapidity of the current of a river or the like, a swift flood (Śiv. 1830); a rise in a river (Gr.Gr. 70).
f. (sg. dat. ?), choking caused by too greedily drinking. -gōjĕ f.pl. uncertainty as to the complete success of any enterprise.
adj. (f.gᵃtᵃjᵃ), having a very swift current, in spate (of a river); hence, rapid (of a torrent of words), quickly incoming (of wealth), and so on; excessive, very much. Cf. gᵃth and Gr.Gr. 145.

. The seventh (or, if we count the aspirate ch as a separate letter, the eighth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is the thirty-third (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the thirty-sixth) and last consonant in the Śāradā or Nāgarī alphabet, and the thirty-fourth and penultimate consonant in the Perso-Arabic alphabet as adapted to Kāshmīrī. It also represents the Arabic letter ح (the tenth letter in the Perso-Arabic alphabet) when occurring in Arabic words borrowed by Kāshmīrī. It is pronounced as an aspirate, as in India Proper. In schools it is named hāla hö. ¶ In Kāshmīrī words this character represents an original h, as in hotᵘ (Skt. hataḥ), smitten; dāh (Skt. dāhaḥ), burning. It also frequently represents an original sibilant. Thus, it represents ś in words such as öhī, a blessing (Skt. āśīḥ); bĕhi, he will sit down (Skt. upaviśati); dah, ten (Skt. daśa-); hihur, a father-in-law (Skt. śvaśura-), but hash, a mother-in-law (Skt. śvaśrū-); hūnᵘ, a dog (Skt. śun-); hīr, a head (Skt. śiraḥ); hat-, a hundred (Skt. śata-); wuh, twenty (Skt. viṁśati-). It represents ṣ in words such as bāha, steam (Skt. vāṣpa-); hār, N. of a month (Skt. āṣāḍha-); shĕh, six (Skt. ṣaṣ-); mahanyuvᵘ, for *manahivᵘ, a man (Skt. manuṣaḥ); vĕh, poison (Skt. viṣam). It represents s in words such as dŏh, a day (Skt. divasaḥ). It represents both original s and original ś in hyuhᵘ (i.e. hihᵘ), like (Skt. sadṛśaḥ, Pr. sarisō with the elision of medial r not uncommon in Dardic languages). If, in the process of declension or conjugation such an h is followed by ü-mātrā or by ĕ (ya), the sibilant returns under the form of sh. Thus bāh, the twelfth lunar day (Skt. dvādaśī), sg. dat. böshᵘ̈; pyuhᵘ (pihᵘ), ground to powder (Skt. √ piṣ), f.sg. pishᵘ̈, pl. pishĕ; hyuhᵘ, like (see ab.), f.sg. hishᵘ̈, pl. hishĕ; ʦôhᵘ, astringent (? Skt. kaṣāyaḥ), f. ʦöshᵘ̈. ¶ The pronominal suffix kh, representing both the nom. of the pronoun of the 2nd pers. sg. and also any case of the pronoun of the 3rd pers. pl., becomes h when followed by another pronominal suffix. Thus, karān chu-kh, thou makest, karān chu-h- as, thou makest for him; koru-kh, they made him, korᵘ-h-am, they made him for me (Gr.Gr. 181). ¶ An initial h is sometimes dropped, as in atha, a hand (Skt. hasta-, Pr. hattha-); asun, to laugh (Skt. √ has-).

interj., i.q. hata 2, q.v., as in ha-biñ = hata-biñ (W. 100); ha-dĕd, for hata dĕdi (id.); used as an interjection between men, with a or i suffixed to the vocative, as in ha wazīra, O Vizier (H. xii, 19); ha māli, O father (L.V. 107).

interj. O, ho (L.V. 107; K.Pr. 43, 242, 250, W. 100; Śiv. 189, 1580, 1590, 1739; H. ii, 2, 4; Rām. 1040-1, 1795). ¶ This interj. is generally used in calling a male person at a distance, or in sorrow (K.Pr. 261); with it ō is suffixed to the voc. case, as in hā nārānō, ho Nārāyaṇa; hā kākō, O father (nom. kākh)! (Gr.Gr. 97). In Śiv. 1308 ff. hā gŏsāñĕ, O Lord of Yōgīs! the ō is not suffixed; so H. ii, 3, etc. In Rām. 1040-1 an inan. m. object is addressed. Cf. hasa and hata 2.
interj. ho, O, used in addressing a brother or male friend older than, or equal in age to, the speaker, and not at a distance.
in --kadᵃl -- N. of the second of seven bridges across the River Vĕth (Jehlam) in Śrīnagar, the so-called Habba Kadal (RT.Tr. II, 449).
m. one grain, one berry, one seed; (in medicine) a pill; a particle, a small piece or portion (of), a jot or tittle.
f. dūb-grass, panic grass, Panicum dactylon or Cynedon dactylon (commonly used as fodder for horses).
adj. composed of seven metals (iron, antimony, lead, gold, tin, copper, and silver) supposed to be a most valuable amalgam (H. xii, 22).
habshī حبشی m. an Abyssinian, a negro (El.). habshī-dīshī adj. c.g. of or belonging to the country of Abyssinia, Abyssinian (Gr.M.).
adj. (f. hacivᵘ̈), made of wood, wooden (K.Pr. 74, W. 15, hachuv).

hadd حد m. boundary, term, limit; bounds, extreme, extremity, extent; bar, obstruction, impediment, separation; a definition; the point, verge (of an event), utmost point or degree. az had از حد, adj. and adv. boundless, unlimited (Śiv. 633); very, exceedingly. --pānas karun -- m.inf. to make a limit for oneself, to make oneself perfect (H. vii, 15). ¶ hada nērun m.inf. to go beyond the bounds, to break bounds, wilfully to make a breach in decorum, to break family rules or customs. -nishĕ nĕbar, adv. beyond limit, enormously (El.). --nyūrᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --nīrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), one who has gone beyond the bounds of decorum, one who has broken the rules and customs of his family. --rachun -- m.inf. to put a limit upon (anything, dat.), to have moderation (K.Pr. 178). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), boundless, without bounds; one who has gone beyond the bounds of decorum, etc.; adv. without limit (Rām. 1104). --roṭᵘ-moṭᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --rüṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), one who is grasped by bounds, one who is restrained within the bounds of decorum. --raṭun -- m.inf. (of a child, a woman, a servant, or the like) to restrain within the bounds of decorum. -raʦhar m. boundlessness; the condition of being outside the bounds of decorum. --rōzun -- m.inf. to keep within the bounds of decorum, to act decorously.

f. weeping and crying aloud, loud lamentation. (Cf. hŏḍ.) --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the loud crying of an old man or of a child to occur when he is given unwelcome food, etc., or when a person he is fond of goes away. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause a child, etc., to wail by crossing it in its wishes.
m. obstinacy, pertinacity. Cf. hŏḍ. Walī Haḍ, N. of a certain Kāshmīrī renowned for this quality (K.Pr. 189). --lāgun -- m.inf. to begin to show obstinacy or pertinacity.

m.pl. the larger bones of a man or beast. --kaḍȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to pull out the bones; met. to afflict greatly, torture, harass (a man or animal, by imposing difficult tasks, causing to make painful efforts, or the like). --nērȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the bones to be extracted, to be greatly afflicted, tortured (by being engaged in a difficult task, by painful efforts, by banishment from home, or the like).

m. a scoundrelly knave, quarrelsome, abusive, and void of modesty, virtue, or respect. Cf. hā̃ḍurᵘ. --hönzᵘ̈ -- m. (f. --hānzañ --), id. (lit. a boatman of this description; Kāshmīrī boatmen and boatwomen are famous for their powers of abuse).
c.g. one who is obstinate or pertinacious.

f.pl. the joints of the larger bones of men or animals. --kaḍañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to pull out the joints, to afflict a man or animal (as if the joints of his bones had become loose) by beating, imposing excessive labour, or the like. --nērañĕ -- f. pl. inf. the joints to be extracted; met. to be much afflicted (by excessive labour or effort, by a difficult task, by absence from home, etc.).
adj. c.g. pertinacious, obstinate (esp. in a bad sense).
f. pain derived from piercingly cold wind; the pain of frostbite. Cf. hūhū. hạdᵘ̈rᵘ̈ hạdᵘ̈rᵘ̈ diñᵘ̈ f.inf. such cold to be experienced in spite of warming appliances being at hand.
f. a thin piece of lotus-stalk. hạdᵃrĕ-bọ̆dᵃ m. a bundle of such stalks, a handful of them held or tied together.
f. a pregnant woman or female animal. ¶ hạdᵃrĕ-dŏd m. the milk secreted by a pregnant woman or cow (usually after the sixth month).
or hã̄ga m. a kind of fine sieve for sifting flour. ¶ hā̃ga-chöñᵘ̈ f. the act of sifting with such a sieve.
or hā̃güjᵘ̈ f. of hã̄gul, q.v.
m. a cart, a wheeled vehicle of the cart class (K. 118, 119, 180); a trolly (L. 464).

or hā̃gulᵘ m. (sg. dat. hã̄galas or hã̄galis. The female is hā̃gȧjⁱ or hā̃güjᵘ̈, q.v.), the stag or bārah-sī˜g (commonly called bara singha and often with twelve-pointed antlers; El. hánglu or hangul; L. 458). ¶ hã̄gal-hĕng or hā̃gȧlⁱ-hĕng the horn of this stag. It is used for sword-hilts and the like, and when powdered is used medicinally.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hogᵘ; 2 p.p. hajyōv), to go to stool, evacuate; to dung, mute.
or hā̃gurᵘ m. a certain aquatic bird (El. hágar), described as like a crow in shape, with a long bill of a dark-blue colour, and haunting lakes that are surrounded by tall reeds.

(cf. ہہ) m. warm breath (as it issues from the mouth) (Śiv. 1063). It is distinct from hᵃh, cold breath (L.V. 56, 57). See hᵃh. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to breathe upon any person or anything so as to warm it, etc. ¶ --dān -- or hahā-dān m. a kind of fire brazier, wide and globular, with two main openings, and round its waist a network of small holes (W. 124). --kôlᵘ -- or hahā-kôlᵘ m., id.

m. the making of the sound hāhā, loud lamentations uttered by a number of people, public lamentation (K. 451, 762), or (Rām. 1287) by a single person. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such public lamentation to occur; a great general grief to occur.
m. a wife's brother, a brother-in-law (K.Pr. 29, 30, 108, 171).
(? spelling), f. breathlessness (El. haṅharáí). Cf. hāh.

or hȧrⁱshun or hürᵘ̈shun conj. 1 [1 p.p. hahorᵘ or huhurᵘ (dat. haharis), f. hahürᵘ̈, harüshᵘ̈ or harishᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 212. Cf. an-huhurᵘ], to arrange for the marriage of a boy or girl, to marry off so and so (Gr.Gr. 212, 219, 231; K.Pr. 71, a girl). --baharun -- or hȧrⁱshun bȧrⁱshun m.inf. to arrange, undertake, carry out any person's marriage. ¶ hahorᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hahürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, harüshᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ or harishᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), one for whose marriage arrangements have been carried out, one who has been duly married (K.Pr. 13, W. 110).

interj. O, addressed to a woman (K.Pr. 158; Śiv. 850, 941; Rām. 1103, 1106, 1454); a mere exclamation used by women in poetry (Śiv. 1104, 1131, 1358). -hai, exclamation, alas! (Śiv. 87, 323). Cf. hāy 1. -hāy, id. (Śiv. 536).
f. (sg. dat. höbati, Rām. 1589), fear, fright (Rām. 1589); dignity, majesty; (in Kāshmīrī) an example (El.).
or höbungᵘ m. one who is stupefied, struck dumb, struck motionless by regret, sorrow, or the like.

or höl (? cf. حیل), f. (sg. dat. haili), custom, habit, intercourse (El.); skill acquired by repeated practice of some business or act (for the accomplishment of which skill acquired by practice is necessary) (Śiv. 1691). See höl.
adj. c.g. perplexed, bewildered, distracted, confounded (Śiv. 371, 831, 1261, 1288; Rām. 877, 1127); harassed, plagued, worried (El.), K.Pr. 217, 247). --karun -- m.inf. to perplex, puzzle (El.).

m. (sg. dat. höratas حیرتس), perturbation and stupor (of mind), astonishment, amazement, consternation. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to become astonished, amazed. --trāwun -- m.inf. to surprise (El.). ¶ höratas gaʦhun m.inf. to become amazed, e.g. at unexpectedly seeing something hitherto considered impossible or non-existent.
interj. hallo! u.w. sg. masc. or pl. masc. (El.).
m. the pilgrimage to Mecca. ¶ hajas gaʦhun m.inf. to go on this pilgrimage (Gr.M.).

m. (sg. dat. hājatas), want, need, necessity (Gr.M., Śiv. 1072); a thing wanted or needed, a needful or necessary thing. na hājath, there is no need (of such and such a thing, gen.), it is unnecessary to do such and such a thing (K.Pr. 40, W. 124). na hājath myônᵘ, I am not wanted (K.Pr. 249).
m. crookedness (in shape) of any thing; crookedness of a condition or of an action.
(? spelling), f. weeding and working a rice field by cattle (L. 463), i.q. gupan-nĕnd, p. 294a, 1. 40.

(? spelling) in haka-khal m., said to mean 'the threshing-floor (khal) of sheep'; N. of a tract of country in Kashmīr where sheep are collected in large numbers in summer (L. 361). ? a misprint for kaṭa.
in --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be distracted by opposing or dissimilar cares (e.g. by the sudden coming of some cause for fear, and simultaneously, by being buried in a multiplicity of duties). Cf. hākulᵘ.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hakarôwᵘ), to cause to become hard and dry, esp. of soft food allowed to become dry and stale. ¶ hakarôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hakaröwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), allowed to become dry and stale as ab.
conj. 3 (1 p.p. hakaryōv), to be or become hard and dry, esp. of soft food drying up and becoming stale. Cf. hakürᵘ̈. hakaryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hakaryē-müʦᵘ̈), become hard and dry as ab.

m. (sg. dat. hakhas), justness, propriety, rightness, correctness, truth; justice; right, title, privilege, claim, due, lot, portion, share, proprietorship; duty, obligation; that to which one has a right; that for which one has a just claim, one's rights (K.Pr. 75); as adj. c.g., true (El.). hakh-ĕ khodā حق خدا m. the duty of God, (a husband) sacred (to a wife) as God (H. xii, 15).

m. (sg. dat. hākas), herb, potherb, cabbage, spinach, greens, edible vegetables (with or without stalks) (K.Pr. 4, 40, 67, 134, 219; Y.Z. 404; L. 464; Śiv. 1328; Rām. 606, 1283). -wākh m. (sg. dat. hākas-wākas), vegetables. ¶ hāka-bodᵘ m. a bundle of spinach (Gr.Gr. 145). -bạrᵃg m. a cabbage leaf; met. a small collection of such leaves. -byôlᵘ m. potherb seeds, cabbage seeds, or the like. -ḍūrᵘ m. a small plot of ground in which potherbs are grown, a cabbage plot. -grākh m. (sg. dat. -grākas; f. -grākañ), a vegetable seller, a greengrocer (Gr.Gr. 38). -köñᵘ̈ f. a little spinach, a small quantity of vegetables (Gr.Gr. 163). -loṭᵘ m. the thin stalk of a cabbage leaf. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. a cabbage-stalk. -mŏyā f. a little spinach (only used of cooked spinach) (Gr.Gr. 165. Cf. -tulᵘ bel.). -nĕhȧlⁱ f. a collection of young cabbages fit for transplanting. -nal m. the stalk of a cabbage leaf. -rang m. cabbage-colour; met. the change of colour in the face to a colour resembling that of a cabbage (owing to disease, sorrow, etc.), pallor. -thal m. a long strip of ground in a vegetable field, divided transversely into small beds for convenience of irrigation. -thôpᵘ m. a little spinach, a small amount of spinach (Gr.Gr. 164). -tulᵘ m. a single cabbage leaf; a small bunch of such leaves. The suff. of the indef. art. is often added, so that we get -tulwā or -tulā. This word may be used either for cooked or for uncooked spinach (Gr.Gr. 164, 165). Cf. -mŏyā ab. -ʦar m. a mass of half-dried cabbages twisted up into a kind of rope and stored for winter use, a string of vegetables (K.Pr. 192). -wörᵘ̈, f. a vegetable garden (L.V. 63). -wạthᵃr m. a cabbage leaf, a spinach leaf (Gr.Gr. 74). -zanḍ m. a bundle of cabbage leaves, a small amount collected ready for cooking (Gr.Gr. 163).

m. (sg. dat. hakas), a collection of splinters, twigs, and small pieces of driftwood carried by the current down a forest stream, or a stream that has issued from a forest. It forms the best fuel for the native portable brazier (L. 250). ¶ haka-hönzᵘ̈ m. (f. -hānzañ), a boatman whose employment it is to collect this floating wood for sale. -pholᵘ m. a collection of splinters, etc., left after cutting logs with an axe, and suitable for use as firewood.

f. (sg. dat. hāki), a doorpost, a jamb. ¶ hāki-chal f. a doorpost. -türᵘ̈ f. the tenon or the like at each end of one of the four members of a door-frame, fitting into a mortise or the like in the adjoining member. -tān m. a beam of a door-frame, a doorpost.

f. (sg. dat. haki), a market cry, a cry or loud proclamation made in a market by a seller of something which he has not with him, but which is deposited elsewhere. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to utter such a cry; met. to make a loud public proclamation of some fact, esp. of some fact hitherto kept secret. --dith nērun -- m.inf. having made such proclamation to go forth; met. owing to some trouble or sorrow, to tell one's friends and relations, and then to abandon one's former mode of life, one's hitherto virtuous conduct, or the like. ¶ haki khasun m.inf. to utter the market cry, e.g. to go into the market and proclaim that there is a boatfull of fruit, etc., for sale lying by a neigh ouring river bank.

or hakhur m. (f. hakhürᵘ̈, q.v.), a bull, bullock, ox (K.Pr. 69, 162). This is the word most used outside Śrīnagar, esp. towards Islāmābād. In Śrīnagar dã̄d or dānd, see dã̄d, is more used. El. also gives hakhuḍ, i.e. hakhoḍᵘ.
or họ̆khᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a cow which has never calved, a heifer (usually not more than four years old); met. a full-grown unmarried girl, who conducts herself foolishly. The word is fem. of hakhorᵘ, q.v.
m. the cry uttered in driving away cows. --hȧkhⁱ karun -- m.inf. to urge on (a child or a servant engaged in any work), so as to get him to work quicker and finish it soon.

or (Śiv. 686) hakaikath حقیقت m. (sg. dat. hakīkatas), essence (of a thing), essential property or quality; truth, reality, fact, true or real nature or state or circumstance or facts (Śiv. 686); gist, pith; rightness, sincerity; account, narration, relation, story, explanation; (in Kāshmīrī) beauty of dress and action, when united with a noble temperament.

m. a wise man, a sage (H. vi, 14); a physician or doctor (whether merely a person skilled in curing the sick or a doctor by profession) (K.Pr. 74, 80, 251, 257; W. 143; L. 335; Rām. 130). For a full account of these men, see L. 232 ff. -bāy f. his wife. -wān m. 'a doctor's shop'; a place appointed for the assembling of sick persons and of doctors to cure them, a hospital, a dispensary.
f. the practice of medicine, the profession of a doctor.
m. in --lāgun -- m.inf. without cause angrily to engage in a quarrel.
m. one who is ever ready to fight or quarrel, with or without cause; one who is of a quarrelsome disposition.
m. honest, genuine conduct (in buying, selling, giving, receiving, making a profit or loss, etc.).
c.g. someone, someone or other, something, something or other; appearing now and then, produced sometimes, occasional, incidental.
m. one who habitually exercises consideration, one who is anxious, full of care. Cf. hākal.

f. a plank or board of moderate size (say 6 cubits or 9 feet long) used for making doorways and the like, split out from the trunks of forest trees, and collected for transport and sale. Cf. hakarun. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to become such board; met. (of the body) to waste away from disease or the like. ¶ hakarĕ-bar m. a house door made up of such planks. -chal f. a piece of such a board. -khünḍᵘ̈ f., id. suitable for roofing houses or the like. -khünḍᵘ̈gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to become a piece of board; met. of something soft, e.g. a cake or a piece of bark, to become hard and dry.
m.inf. to be struck dumb, dumbfounded, struck, confounded, confused, amazed, aghast (= Hindostanī hakkā-bakkā hōnā).

m. (sg. abl. hala 1), a plough. A plough and a pestle are the weapons of Balarāma, the brother of Kṛṣṇa (K. 909), and also (Śiv. 13, 1160) of the elephant-god Gȧnⁱsh or Gaṇēśa. ¶ hala kaḍun m.inf. to draw out from the plough, i.e. to carry on all the agricultural operations necessary for a field from the commencement of ploughing up to the time of sowing.

m. state, condition, circumstances, case, situation (YZ. 10, 247; Śiv. 700, 812, 1316, etc.; H. vii, 9; ix, 4; Rām. 51, 211, 292, etc.); existing or present state (Śiv. 279, 372); as adv. at present, now (Śiv. 1748). kami hāla, in what condition ? as adv. wonderfully, in wondrous way (Śiv. 814, 943, 972). hāl hölī حال حآلی, the whole state of affairs, an account or story in detail (Rām. 465). --karun -- m.inf. to arrange a state of affairs, to arrange (H. x, 17). -mast m. a man of position (K.Pr. 133). ¶ hāli-hairān حال حیران adj. c.g. in a state of confusion, perplexed, distracted, harassed (Rām. 320, 850, 1218, 1662); engaged on some profitless labour, wasting one's time (K.Pr. 142). -hairönī حال حیرانی f. a state of confusion, perplexity, distraction, harassment; profitless labour, waste of time. ¶ hālas adv. for the present. ¶ hālay (abl. hāla, with emphatic y), in (such and such) a condition, etc. (Śiv. 661, 831, 1330). ¶ hālạy adv. just now, even now.
m. (sg. abl. hala 2), the afterbirth, secundines (K.Pr. 34). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat the afterbirth; hence, to die in giving birth to a child (K.Pr. 158).

f. (sg. dat. höjᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 169), a house, a hall. Generally used --˚, and then sometimes masc. (dat. -hālas, Gr.Gr. 69), thus hȧstⁱ-hāl, f. an elephant-stable; bö̃dⁱ-hāl, f. a prison (YZ. 384, 385; H. ix, 4), but ʦāṭa-hāl, m. a school- house (Kaśmīraśabdāmṛta, II, i, 287).
m. untying, loosing; grinding, trituration; (in Kāshmīrī) striving, straining, efforts. --karun -- m.inf. to strain, exert oneself with great efforts (L.V. 48). Cf. hala 3.

f. a ball, a sphere (El.); a certain game; a kind of hockey in which a ball is propelled by sticks. ¶ hāla-gŏgᵃ̇jᵃ̇ f. a similar game, hockey on horseback (El.), polo. ¶ hāli-gŏgᵃ̇jᵃ̇ f. a hockey ball, as used in the ab. game.
f. N. of a large and prosperous village inhabited almost exclusively by Brāhmaṇs, about thirty miles south of Śrīnagar in Pargana Shukru (RT.Tr. II, 275).
f. in daman-hāl (sg. dat. -hāli), the main pipe of a blacksmith's bellows (L.V. 4). Cf. khāra-hāl, s.v. khār 1.
f. in hālgaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. a habit to be formed, or acquired (K.Pr. 75). Cf. kŏ-hölᵘ̈.

interj. expressing urgency (H. xii, 17), as in hala dis, give it to him at once; hala wanus, tell him at once. --hala -- interj. and adv. at once, as in hala hala raṭun, stop him at once (of someone running away). Cf. hĕla 1 and hal 3. --karun -- m.inf. to complete some necessary work with energy (of a number of people collected together and urging each other on).
(? cf. حلب) m. a kind of thick glass used for making mirrors (Rām. 31, 397, 1011).
adj. c.g. made of thick glass, see halab.
m. N. of Balarāma, the brother of Kṛṣṇa; the Haladhara of Sanskrit literature (K. 42, 46, et passim), so called from his carrying a plough as a weapon (see hal).
m. the name used in schools for the letter ha.
adj. c.g. legal, lawful, allowable (K.Pr. 36, 37, 75, 150, 252; W. 154). --nimakh -- adj. c.g. faithful, loyal (of a servant) (Gr.M.).

m. the front skirt of the phĕran or long gown worn by Kāshmīrīs (K.Pr. 50, 153). Used met. for begging (cf. --dārun) (K.Pr. 152; H. v, 4, 5). --dārun -- m.inf. to offer the skirt (as a beggar to receive alms) (K.Pr. 155; H. ix, 11); met. with great humility to make a request for something to be done. --dörith yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come and make such a request, to approach with a humble petition.
m. (sg. dat. hālatas), state, condition; nature, constitution (Gr.M.).

m. a locust (El. hálau and hálú). Small numbers visit Kashmīr nearly every year. Musalmāns eat them. They dry them in the sun, grind them to powder, and make cakes of them (El.; L. 156, 461, hálu; Śiv. 1064; K.Pr. 75).
m. engagement in practice of or study for the acquirement of any work or knowledge. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. instruction resulting in the attainment of expertness in carrying out any work to be obtained.
in halka gāsa m. N. of a certain medicinal plant, Polyganum sp., said to be good for saddle sores (L. 76).
f. plating, gilding (e.g. of a book, an image, a paper, or the like). Cf. bēl-hᵒ, p. 104b, l. 43.

adj. c.g. violent by nature, one ready to rage with anger without just cause, violently quarrelsome; mad (of a dog) (Gr.M.). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become such. --hūnᵘ -- m. (f. --hūñᵘ̈ --), a mad dog, a dog suffering from hydrophobia.
m. in --karun -- m.inf. to attack and beat and bruise.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. halyōv), to be or become crooked, bent, askew, awry; to become out of the perpendicular, to become oblique (K.Pr. 214); to be or become warped (of a board) (Gr.M.); to shake, to tremble (Rām. 605) Cf. alun. --ḍalun -- m.inf. to become crooked and go wrong; (of something well poised and steady) to topple, to become unsteady; (of an an. being) to be thrown off one's balance by grief, sorrow, anxiety, or the like. --ḍangun -- m.inf. (of a healthy man) to be suddenly afflicted by disease. ¶ halyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. halyē-müʦᵘ̈) (of something naturally straight) become crooked or awry; thrown out of the perpendicular, become oblique; met. thrown out of one's balance, angry, angered, agitated.
m. a maker of halᵃwa (q.v.), a confectioner (El. halawóí and halwáí). ¶ halwöyⁱ-wān m. a confectioner's shop.

(Rām. 451, 511, 872, etc.), halamotᵘ (Rām. 563, 688, 855), halamath (Rām. 526, 565, etc.), or halamothᵘ (Rām. 36) m. (sg. dat. halamatas), Hanumān, N. of a monkey chief celebrated in Hindū mythology. He was son of the Wind and of immense strength. He was one of the chief allies of Rāma-candra in his war with Rāvaṇa, i.q. hanumān.
f. (sg. dat. hạlᵃrüñᵃ), the act of making crooked, awry, oblique.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hạlᵃrôwᵃ), to make crooked, make awry, make oblique. hạlᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. hạlᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), made crooked, made awry, made oblique.
m. a kind of pudding (made of flour, ghī, syrup, dried cocoanut, spices, etc.), 'hulwa.'

m. the pole by which a boat is propelled in a river (esp. upstream), a punting-pole (Śiv. 1780, 1841). A boat is usually equipped with two, a longer, called hama-tulᵘ, and a shorter, called hama-tᵘ̈jᵘ̈. They are made of young deodārs (L. 79). ¶ hama-tᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f., see ab. In Gr.M. spelt hama-tujᵘ̈. -tulᵘ m., see ab. -tulⁱ zīrᵘ̈ f. pushing with such a pole, punting. --wāyun -- m.inf. to propel (a boat) with a punting pole, to punt (Śiv. 1488, 1805).

f. darkenedness, dirtiedness, of some white or coloured article spoiled and darkened by dirt. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'darkenedness to fall', to ripen, become dark and healthy (of small-pox pustules, or the like).

f. a kind of grass growing self-sown in rice-fields, the stalks of which resemble paddy stalks, Panicum colonum. It is an excellent food for horses (L. 71, Śiv. 1111; cf. dŏda-hāma, p. 189a, l. 35). -dāñĕ m. the grain of this grass. It is like panic seed, is eaten by Hindūs, and is presented as an offering in Hindū temples (L. 334). -lörᵘ̈ f. a kind of small cucumber, described as elongated in shape, hollow, and with a good flavour.
or (H. vii, 4) hamud (= حمد), m. praise (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to praise (El.); esp. to praise or bless (God). --parun m.inf. to recite praises (H. vii, 4).

m. a carrier of burdens, a porter (L.V. 107, voc. hamāli); (in Kāshmīrī) a grain-carrier (he carries it in leather bags each holding a kharwār or about 152 lb.); a man who lives by tending cows and selling their milk, a cowherd, a milkman. --wadun -- m.inf. to perform an ancient method of lamentation on the decease of the head of a household. In this the surviving relatives every morning for ten days after the death used to collect a crowd of grain-porters and cowherds and sing to them the deeds of the deceased to the accompaniment of loud wailing.
m. gestation, pregnancy; the fruit of the womb, the young that is borne in the womb, fœtus. --raṭun -- m.inf. to conceive, become pregnant.
f. N. of a pargana of Kashmīr, lying to the west of the Wŏlur Lake, the ancient Śamālā and the Hummel of the maps. RT.Tr. II, 484.

m. a hot bath, a Turkish bath, ḥammām, a bagnio, either at home or outside (K.Pr. 75, 160, 242). See L. 281 for particulars. -gȧjⁱ f. the furnace of a Turkish bath (K.Pr. 48). --karun m.inf. to take a course of Turkish baths as a cure for rheumatism. It lasts one or two days.
f. darkening or blackening (of the face from disease, sorrow, or the like); met. 'blackening of the face' owing to its owner being subjected to a disgraceful accusation.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. hāmanyōv), to become dark-coloured from disease or the like; to become ripe (of smallpox pustules).
m. the coin or piece of gold or other metal placed by Hindūs in the mouth of the corpse as a viaticum.
m. encouragement or incitement to engage in any act (such as that given by a grown-up person to a child).
adv. just as, even as, like (YZ. 198).
adv. always, ever, continually (El., W. 95). --bahar (? spelling), a medicinal plant used internally as an antiphlogistic (L. 75).
m. the noise of rapid footfalls in running backwards and forwards, the sound of running.
f. display of pride or self-conceit by an unworthy person (in order to cause annoyance to another), groundless and malicious arrogance.
pron. even this, this very, this same (K.Pr. 22).
adj. c.g. residing together, living in the same house, of the same house (El.).
m. a companion, a familiar friend (H. vii, 21, 24).
m. the owner or keeper of a ḥammām or Turkish bath; the attendant at such a bath; met. one accustomed to follow implicitly, and without question, advice given by others.

m. (sg. gen. hamsunᵘ in Śiv. 897, 1516), a swan (L.V. 86; Śiv. 351, 1105); the soul (cf. haṁs 2). In Hindū mythology the swan is the vehicle of the god Brahmā (Śiv. 160, 801). See haṁs 2. hamsa-dôrᵘ or (Śiv. 1177) hamsa-dwār m. 'the soul-door', N. of a holy mountain spur, passed by Hindū pilgrims on the route up the sacred mountain of Haramŏkh in Kashmīr (Śiv. 1052, 1177, 1516, 1607, 1891; Rām. 249). Cf. JRAS., 1910, p. 1337.

m. N. of a certain mantra, or mystic formula used by Śaiva Hindūs. It is said to be a representation of the Sanskrit words sō 'ham, written in reversed order as 'haṁ saḥ, meaning 'I am that', i.e. 'I am one with God', or 'God and I are one'. It is thus used as a name for the sacred syllable ōṁ, in its character of the anāhata śabda (in Kāshmīrī, anāhath, or anāhata, shĕbd) or unobstructed sound, also called the azapā (see anāhata-shĕbd and azapā) or unuttered word. It is described as being almost inarticulate, and as being really uttered only by the deity, indwelling in the breast of the worshipper, and therefore to have no human utterer or obstructer of its sound. It is often represented as being equivalent to the Supreme Himself (Śiv. 1011, 1027, 1064, 1687, 1693, 1783). When this mantra is mentioned, by a play of meanings, it is often capable of being translated by 'swan' (hams 1). Cf. hamsa-nād, bel. ¶ hamsa-gad m. i.q. -nād, bel. (Śiv. 1607). -gath f. (sg. dat. -güʦᵘ̈), the unobstructed path of this mantra, as explained ab. (L.V. 65). -nād m. i.q. haṁs, ab. Owing to the play on the meaning of haṁs 1 mentioned ab., this formula is represented as having wings to bear the soul to the Supreme (Śiv. 897, 1516, 1827, 1891). Cf. JRAS., 1910, p. 1337.
m. he whose seat is a swan, N. of the Hindū god Brahmā, whose vehicle was that bird (Śiv. 160, cf. 801). See hams 1.
f. a neighbourhood (Gr.M.). Cf. the next.
m. living under the same shade; hence, a neighbour (K.Pr. 75; Śiv. 41, 897; H. x, 5, 12).
m. a neighbour, a near-dweller. ¶ hamsöyⁱ-bāy f. a neighbour's wife; a female neighbour.
m. a section of a log of wood cut out of a tree trunk which has been split up lengthways into four sections, so that each has three corners.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. hamyōv), to be extinguished (of fire); met. to be extinguished, cooled (of anger, fever, etc.). hamyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hamyē-müʦᵘ̈), extinguished, cooled (of fire, anger, fever, etc.); pacified, cooled (of an angry person, or one suffering from fever).
m. a charge, attack, assault, onset (Gr.M.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. hạmᵒrᵒ), to extinguish (a fire or the like); met. to cool, assuage (pride, fever, anger, grief, etc.), caus. of hamun, q.v. hạmᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. hạmᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), put out, extinguished (by someone) (of fire); met. cooled, assuaged (by someone) (of pride, fever, anger, etc., as ab.); cooled, assuaged (of a person affected by the ab.).
f. a long purse or scrip (esp. one hung at the side); a purse (Śiv. 1311).

or hanā or hanāh f. (sg. dat. hani, Gr.Gr. 70), a part, a fragment (Śiv. 1869); a little of anything as in dih hanā, give a little (Gr.M.); hanā trukhᵘ, moderately intelligent (K.Pr. 76); often --˚ (Gr.Gr. 165) as in āba-hanā or pã̄-hanā, a little water (Gr.M.); kapara-hanā, a small amount of cloth, some cloth (Gr.M.); --˚ also used as a dim. suff. as in ạbᵃra-han, a very thin or slight cloud; añĕcĕ-han (cf. añoṭᵘ), a small dish-cover; asana-hanā, a small laugh, a smile; bāna-han, a small vessel, a cup (YZ. 421); gāḍi-han, a small fish (K.Pr. 14); gāma-han, a small village (K.Pr. 109); kañi-hanā, a pebble (YZ. 235); kōri-han, a little daughter, a pet daughter (K.Pr. 70); lōri-han, a little stick, a walking stick (K.Pr. 70); raʦhi-han, a very little of something (H. v, 6). han-han f. every part, every fragment, every constituent, every bit, the entirety (of anything or action) (Śiv. 554, 773, 975, 1002, 1431, etc.; Rām. 345, 517, 579, etc.); as adv. bit by bit (of an army or the like), man by man, company by company, gradually (Rām. 1325). ¶ hana-wana adv. bits from everywhere, in great numbers, suddenly (of profit, increase, or the like) (Śiv. 1347, 1411). ¶ hanā or hanāh f. a little, a small quantity, as in añĕma-hanā, a little rice-gruel; bata-hanā, a little cooked rice (H. x, 3); dŏba-hanā, a small pit (H. viii, 7); kashĕna-hanā, a small amount of scratching (H. xii, 16); pã̄-hanā, a little water; also used to indicate something or other indefinite (only with reference to fem. things or actions). ¶ hani hani adv. bit by bit, little by little (Śiv. 160); in every bit, in every fragment, throughout the totality (Śiv. 180, 235, 368, 868, 1107, 1146, 1281, etc.; Rām. 1484, 1617); in small pieces; in many fragments (L.V. 103; H. viii, 6). hani-pĕṭh han f. bit upon bit; hence (of things collected or earned), gradual gain, little by little from here and there.

f. (sg. dat. höñᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 69), loss, harm, damage (Śiv. 238, 425, 1756; Rām. 1076, 1238, 1609, 1703, 1728, 1771; K. 797); diminution; disgrace (Śiv. 1677); injury, interruption to work (Gr.M.). --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring loss; hence, to spread abroad scandal about or charges against a person (whether deserved or not). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- loss to occur; blame to occur; hence, blame to fall on someone or something immediately responsible for breakage, or the like, where such breakage was impending and required only the merest touch to cause it to take place (Rām. 255); to become despondent (Rām. 664). --khārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause loss to mount; hence, when anything has been damaged or destroyed by one person, to charge another person with being the cause thereof. --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. loss to mount; hence, when one person has caused loss or damage, another to be held responsible for it or charged with it. --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to suffer loss (Rām. 761). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. disgrace to come; a bad repute for immorality, etc., to be gained.
onomat. m. the noise made by a vessel of brass, or similar vessel, being struck by some hard object, clang, clash, crash. Cf. ṭhiñ.

m. N. of a kind of wild walnut tree and of its fruit. This is probably the dán hunak dun of L. 70, 75, which he identifies as the Aesculus indica or Indian chestnut, and says is used in medicine as a cathartic, while its lopped leaves are used as cattle fodder. El. translates it as horse-chestnut. Cf. hānē and hanū-ḍūnᵘ.

f. (sg. dat. handi), chicory, Cichorium Intybus, endive (K.Pr. 251). It is valued as a vegetable (L. 72). It has three varieties ārᵃm-hand, kahū-hand, and wan-hand. El. probably by a misprint also spells this word haud. ¶ handi-byôlᵘ m. chicory seed, used as a remedy for diarrhœa. -lū̃ṭᵘ̈ or -lū̃ṭh f. (sg. dat. lū̃ṭĕ), a bunch of partly dried chicory-leaves kept for use when required. -mūl m. chicory root, used as a medicine for several diseases. -pōsh m. chicory flower. It is bright blue, and is often cultivated in gardens (L. 72, Rām. 1094). -ras m. the juice of the chicory-root, used as a medicine for continued fever. -thôpᵘ m. a bunch or handful of chicory plants. -ʦyūṭᵘ m. (sg. dat. -ʦīṭis, abl. -ʦēṭi), a decoction of pounded chicory root, used as a medicine or regimen for invalids.
f. (sg. dat. hanḍöjᵘ̈), a badly conducted woman, an unchaste woman. Cf. hath-hanḍöjᵘ̈, s.v. hath.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. hanḍôwᵘ), to use (a garment, an ornament, or the like) till it begins to show signs of wear. hanḍôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hanḍöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), worn till signs of becoming worn out by constant use appear.
or hȧnḍish f. a fine kind of pincers used by goldsmiths. Cf. atha-hᵒ, p. 58b, l. 1.
f. a general term for all the ornaments (esp. the smaller ones) worn by women.

conj. 3 (1 p.p. hanḍyōv) (of a garment, ornament, etc.), to have been used, to show signs of slight wear. ¶ hanḍanhār adj. c.g. used only a short time; hence (as compared with other things of the same kind), good for much further use or wear; strong, lasting, durable.

adj. (f. hạnḍᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or hạndürᵘ̈), frozen hard (of a lake, etc.); (e.g. of water, milk, food, clothing, a country, a season) extremely cold, freezingly cold (W. 112). In L. 335 the word (spelt handru) is used for a cold wind that blows from the mountain peaks, and chills and shrivels up the rice crop. --lagun -- m.inf. freezing to come on; (of a man's body) to become stiff with cold (e.g. when at the point of death, or the like). ¶ hạndᵃ̇rᵃ̇-khünḍᵃ̇ f. the part of the water of a lake or pond which has been frozen over.
m. dried and withered rice-straw standing barren in the field.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. hạndᵃrôwᵃ), to cause (something previously warm) to become extremely cold, to freeze (something), to ice. hạndᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. hạndᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), made extremely cold (by some cause), frozen (by someone).
m. extreme coldness, a frozen condition (e.g. of a thing, a country, or a season) (W. 112). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to feel icy cold (K.Pr. 63).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. hạndᵃryōv), (of a liquid) to become frozen, to turn to ice); (of anything else) to become freezingly cold, to be frozen; met. (of love) to be frozen, indignation to be felt against one whom one has hitherto loved (Rām. 1011, 1048). hạndᵃryō-motᵃ perf. part. (f. hạndᵃryē-müʦᵃ), frozen; become very cold; filled with indignation against a friend.
or hanū-ḍūnᵘ m. the Indian horse-chestnut, Pavia Indica (El.). Cf. hānakh-ḍūnᵘ.

m. the top part of a head-covering or turban (K.Pr. 76); the upper part of a door-frame, a lintel (Śiv. 1075). -kuṭhᵘ m. the lintel-room, i.e. a small upper, room over a large doorway, a room over a portico; according to El., the small centre chamber on the second floor, which is often used as a dormitory (El.). ¶ hanga-dü jᵘ̈ f. a kind of square kerchief used as a head-covering by Musalmān women. -nyās m. the cross-bar of the upper part of a door-frame, a lintel. -ʦhôgᵘ m. a kind of curl or ringlet hanging in front of the ear, worn by people living in the country to the north of the Kashmīr Valley. -ʦracĕ f.pl. a method of braiding the hair in plaits, principally used by girls; cf. ʦrüṭᵘ̈. -wār m. a horqizontal beam along the wall of a house for supporting an upper story; cf. wār 2. -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), lintel-joining; hence (in building) fastening one beam above another; (in making clothes) fastening one part above another. ¶ hangi or hangas lāgun 1  m.inf. to place (a flower or an ornament) on the head. ¶ hangas-manz adv. in the centre of the turban; hence met. by conflation with hang 2, in a place of security and honour (K.Pr. 259).

m. understanding, intellect, wisdom; majesty, authority; dignity, gravity; strength, power, ability. ¶ hangi lôgᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. --löjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), accepted with great honour, received with great respect (of a person or thing). --lāgun 2 -- or hangas lāgun m.inf. to receive or accept with great respect. ¶ hangas-manz, see under hang 1.
m. a side in relationship (as we say 'on the mother's side', 'on the father's side').

adv. on account of, for (this, that, or other) cause (principally u.w. pronouns). --manga -- adv. if ever, if at any time, if at all; (according to El.) adj. c.g. sudden; cf. the next. --ta manga -- adv. suddenly, unexpectedly (K.Pr. 221; H. iii, 6; K. 1087); by chance, accidentally; without hesitation, promptly.
adj. c.g. stained, an object of disrepute (owing to bad conduct or the like); esp. one who, on account of such a stain, is barred by his caste-fellows from intermarriage.

m. one who is possessed of dignity, authority, etc. (see hang 2); hence, the chief man in a village, the man in a village who by reason of his wealth wisdom and age is the admitted leader of the others. His wife is called hangdārĕñ.
m. (f. hangdārĕñ), 'one who owns relationship,' a relation either on the father's or on the mother's side. See hang 3.
f. the condition or office of being the chief man in a village. See hangdār 1.
f. relationship; the condition of having a wide circle of relations. Cf. hangdār 2.
(? spelling) f. a bar (El.), ? incorr. for hö̃kal, a door-chain.
m. the part of the head between the ear and the outer corner of the eye (K.Pr. 81, where it is translated 'chin', as if for hŏngunᵘ); the curl of hair lying on this part of the head.
or hānē m. the Indian horse chestnut, Pavia Indica (El.). Cf. hānakh-ḍūnᵘ.

(Rām. 680, 748, etc.), hanūmān (Śiv. 1422; Rām. 653, 709, etc.), or hanumath (Rām. 702, 716), m. N. of the monkey chief and demigod, who befriended Rāma-candra in his exile, i.q. halᵃmotᵃ, q.v. for further particulars.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. honᵘ), to hinder, cause obstruction to; to reduce to inferiority or poverty; publicly to show disrespect, to put a person of consequence to public disgrace, to offer a public insult to (anyone). honᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f.hüñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of a work) impeded, hindered; (of a person) by deceit, or violence reduced to inferiority or poverty; publicly insulted or put to shame.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. hānyōv), to become very cold, to be thoroughly chilled. hānyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hānyē-müʦᵘ̈), chilled, made very cold (of something previously warm).
m. N. of a sacred spot passed on the pilgrim route to Amarêśvara.
in hanzĕpanzĕ rōzun m.inf. to keep oneself in good health after illness by paying attention to diet, etc.
họ̆nzᵃra or họ̆nzūra m. a kind of necklace, made of a precious metal, and with small ornamental bells hanging down in front; a collar (El.). ? Cf. Ar. حنجور, the gullet.

or thüñᵘ̈ f. butter (cf. dã̄da- thᵒ, p. 187b, l. 24) (El. thain, thaing, thainyi, thanyi, thauí; L. 458, than; W. 129, thaṇⁱ; Śiv. 702, 1381, 1387, 1461; K. 99, 148-50, 156, 470; H. ix, 4; K.Pr. (thani), 34, 74). --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring butter, to churn milk till the butter forms. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to give butter', to wheedle, coax, cajole (another to a course of conduct) (K. 515). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to become butter', (of the heart, feelings, etc.) to become soft, tender, gentle (Śiv. 602, 1463). --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to collect the butter after churning. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to make butter', to make (someone's heart or feelings) soft and tender. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. butter to come, butter to appear in the process of churning. ¶ thañi-atha adj. c.g. butter-handed, one who has soft hands; (as subst. m.) so much butter as can be lifted on the palm of the hand. -bāna m. a butter-dish, a dish for holding butter, a dish, or vessel, filled with butter. -bata m. boiled rice cooked with butter. -buthᵘ m. 'a butter-face', a good-looking fellow with his face soft like butter. -dŏgᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a globular pat of butter. -dŏgulᵘ m. a large globular lump of butter (as much as can be held on the palm of the hand). -ḍūnᵘ m. a pat of butter, the size of, and shaped like, a walnut; a walnut, the kernel of which is as soft as butter. -han f. (sg. dat. -hani), a small amount of butter, a little butter. -mandᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ or -mandüñᵘ̈ f. a ball of butter as formed in churning. -maṭh m. (sg. dat. -maṭas), 'a butter-jar'; met. one whose body is plump and at the same time soft. -nomᵘ m. as much butter as can be raised on the finger-nail, a very small amount of butter. -raʦh f. (sg. dat. -raʦi), a small amount of butter. -sulla adj. c.g. unable to walk, etc., owing to habitual weakness, a victim of chronic debility. -sīrᵘ̈ f. 'a butter-wad', rubbing butter on the throat as a remedy in smallpox and other diseases. -thaph f. (sg. dat. -thapi), as much butter as can be held in the hollow of the hand. -ṭọ̆ṭᵘ m. a cotton seed of butter, a very small amount of butter. -ṭyonḍᵘ m. a very small amount of butter (see ṭyonḍᵘ).
in hapa-dĕgulᵘ, see hŏpa-dĕgulᵘ, s.v. hŏpa, and họ̆pᵘ.
f. the conduct of a bear (fierce, pugnacious, and savage); (with reference to a human being) conduct like that of a bear.
m. the ugliness of a swollen jowl. Cf. hapa 1 and hŏpa.

m. (sg. dat. hapas, abl. hapa 2), a human corpse, a dead body. -rang m. the colour of a corpse, the appearance of a corpse (e.g. the appearance of a person in a faint, or suffering from severe fatigue or disease).

in hapi-hāyun m. a famine, a scarcity (K.Pr. 76). The phrase is said to be connected with haph (q.v.), a corpse, and a conflation of hāwun, to show, and hyonᵘ, to take, and to express 'insufficient to give a corpse', i.e. less than nothing; but this explanation is very doubtful.
m. a child's ball (of wood coloured externally with polished lac).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. hapyōv), (from haph, a corpse), to become exhausted or worn out by delay (e.g. when anxiously expecting the completion of some work being performed by another, which is greatly delayed, or by hunger when there is great delay in the service of food). ¶ hapyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hapyē-müʦᵘ̈), exhausted, worn out, as ab.

m. (sg. dat. hāpatas. The f. is hāpüʦᵘ̈, a she-bear), a bear (L. 111, Ursus torquatus). According to El. there are in Kashmīr a black and a brown bear, the former large, and the latter more fierce (L. 111, 458; K.Pr. 57, 76, 92, 248; H. ii, 10 ff.; Rām. 862). -nāg m. the bear spring, N. of a spring in the Lĕdorᵘ Valley. Near to it is a copper mine which was worked in former days (El.). Cf. RT.Tr. iv, 617. We should expect this word to be spelt hāpath-nāg, but El. has hāput-, i.e. hāputh. ¶ hāpath-baca m. a bear-cub. -carb m. bear's grease, the fat round the entrails of a bear, used as a medicine for rheumatism, etc. -māy f. a bear's watching, a bear's keeping ambush for an opportunity of springing on a hunter; met. waiting for an opportunity to fall upon and crush another person. -ṭang m. N. of a kind of pear (El.). -ʦam f. bearskin. -yārᵃz f. a bear friendship (see bel.); hence, stupid friendship, friendship that does harm. The original meaning is a reference to a well-known story, told as follows in K.Pr. 77:-- 'a bear formed friendship with a man who was passing through his jungle. For some time he brought his friend large quantities of honey. One day the man fell asleep after eating the honey. While asleep a bee attracted by the sweetness alighted upon his mouth. The friendly bear seeing this thought that he would save the man from the pain of a sting, and so he went and fetched a large piece of rock and aimed it with all his might at the place where the bee was. The stone frightened away the bee, but killed the man' (W. 21, L. 111).
f. of hāputh, q.v. a she-bear.

m. [in Śiv. 1132, 1617, 1776 (hara-y), the nom. sing. is hara m.c.; the voc. hara is very common, e.g. Śiv. 127, 161, 287, 313, etc.], N. of the Hindū god Śiva, so called (Śiv. 233) because he is said to be the destroyer (Sanskrit hara) of sin, sorrow, misfortune, and stumbling-blocks (L.V. 78-9, 98; Śiv. 254, 1039, 1061, 1076, 1173, 1181, 1197, 1402). In Śiv. 950, 1011, 1611, 1687, and 1889, the word has a double meaning, being also equivalent to har 6. ¶ hara-dwār m. N. of a holy place where the Ganges issues from the Himālaya mountains, sacred to Śiva (Śiv. 950, 1076, 1099). In Śiv. 950 hara- dwāray, may also be translated 'at every door'; cf. har 6. -mŏkh or har-mŏkh m. (sg. dat. hara-mŏkhas), N. of a celebrated mountain in Kashmīr, the Sanskrit Hara- mukuṭa or Śiva's diadem. Into the Ganga-bal lake (p. 291b, l. 33), which lies at the foot of the north-eastern glacier of this mountain, Hindūs cast the bones of those that have died. [See RT.Tr. II, 407, K.Pr. 79 (legend), (haramŏkh) L.V. 50; Śiv. 251, 950, 955, 1176, 1528; (harmŏkh) 1011, 1030, 1222, 1561, 1595, 1617, 1680-1, 1687, 1889; Rām. 249]. In Śiv. 950, 1011, 1687, the word also means 'in every mouth', and in 1889, 'the whole totality of creation considered as one with Śiva,' see har. 6. -mŏkha-gang f. i.q. ganga-bal, p. 291b, l. 33).

m. the name of the fourth month of the Kāshmīrī Hindū year (which commences with Ṯs̱ithᵃr or Caitra), called in Sanskrit Āṣāḍha, and equivalent to June-July (Gr.Gr. 51; W. 106; K.Pr. 79, 138; Śiv. 1636). ¶ hāra-kani adv. about Āṣāḍha, in the month of Hār or thereabouts (Gr.Gr. 159). -mujᵘ̈ f. a kind of radish, of very pungent flavour, that grows in the month of Hār. -nākh m. (sg. dat. -nākas), N. of a certain early, luscious kind of pear that ripens in the month of Hār (L. 330, harnak). -nawam f. (sg. dat. nawümᵘ̈), N. of a Hindū festival held on the ninth lunar day of the bright half of the month of Hār in honour of the goddess Śārikā, at her temple on the Hāra-parbuth or Pradyumna-pīṭha hill near Śrīnagar. The N. Hāra- parbuth is derived from the Skr. Śārikā-parvata, and has nothing to do with the name of the month (see hār 2); cf. RT.Tr. notes on I, 101 and 113. -pav m. a scarcity of water in the lakes in the month of Hār. - satam f. (sg. dat. -satümᵘ̈), N. of a Hindū house-festival in honour of the sun, held on the seventh lunar day of the light half of the month of Hār. In each room in each house a circle is drawn to represent the sun and is worshipped. -satümᵘ̈-bôgᵘ m. N. of a customary present sent to the house of a girl's father-in-law by her relations on the ab. festival. -traṭh m. (sg.dat. -traṭas), N. of a tract and village 10 miles north-west of Śrīnagar (cf. RT.Tr. I, 102 n.); f. (sg. dat. -trạti), lightning or a thunderbolt in the month of Hār; N. of a certain medicinal plant growing on the mountain plateaux, said to shine in the dark. -ʦŏdāh f. (sg. dat. -ʦŏdöshᵘ̈), N. of a Hindū festival held on the 14th lunar day of the bright half of the month of Hār, on which offerings are made to the Śaktis, or energic powers of the deities personified as their wives (L. 265). -wôñᵘ m. water of Hār, i.e. the water in the lakes in that month. It is looked upon as warm. -zã̄ḍ f. sultry weather in the month of Hār, the mountains being hidden under heavy dark clouds which also cover the sky, and there being no wind. -zāl f. (sg. dat. -zöjᵘ̈), a heat fog, or heavy clouds accompanied by extreme heat in the month of Hār. ¶ hörⁱ-wa-harȧdⁱ adv. in summer and in autumn; hence, in every year, always. Cf. harud. ¶ hārukᵘ adj. (f. hārücᵘ̈), of or belonging to the month of Hār.
m. cream of milk (cf. dŏda-har 2, p. 189a, l. 42; H. ii, 3); a scum that rises like cream to the surface of dahī (curdled milk), oil, or the like (K.Pr. 255). --lagun -- m.inf. cream to rise on milk.

m. in hāra-parbuth m. (sg. dat. -parbatas), N. of a celebrated hill, also known in Sanskrit as Pradyumna-pīṭha, lying to the north of the city of Śrīnagar. It takes its name from the goddess Hörī (see Hörī 2) or Śārikā, whose temple is on the N.W. side of the hill. On its southern extremity is a rock believed to be an embodiment of the god Gȧnⁱsh or Haridrā-Gaṇēśa, see hörī 1. See RT.Tr. I, 101 n.; 113 n., and II, 446; Śiv. 952, 1500, etc. El. spells the word harí parbat.

m.pl. a group or bunch of young shoots just bursting out on the trees in spring. Only used in pl. except in the phrase har yunᵘ, bel. El. translates 'branch'. -hã̄gul m. 'a sprouts-stag' (see hã̄gul); hence, a bunch or group of thorns on the branches of a long creeper. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. sprouting to come, the first bursting of trees into bud in the spring.

f. (in some compounds the obl. form sg. of this word is hürᵘ̈ 2. For 1, see s.v.), a quarrel, quarrelling, fighting, wrangling, coming to blows (K.Pr. 11, 59, 134, 203, 215; YZ. 405); tumult, war, a battle (K. 649). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such fighting to arise (YZ. 398). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make war (El.), fight, quarrel (K.Pr. 77, 83). --ʦuvüñᵘ̈ --, f.inf. a quarrel to arise (K.Pr. 37, 126). ¶ hara-har f. mutual quarrelling or fighting, esp. among neighbours, or the like. -har karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to dispute, to fight (El.). -hari-bāz adj. c.g. quarrelsome, contentious, pugnacious, cantankerous. ¶ hürᵘ̈-bāz adj. c.g. quarrelsome, of a quarrelsome disposition. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is engaged in a quarrel; one who sets others quarrelling.

f. copper-red and dark markings on a white or other ground, dapple, brindle, piebald, mottle (K.Pr. 78); cf. hôrᵘ. --hūnᵘ -- m. a piebald dog, considered to be specially unfaithful; hence, met. for anything considered untrustworthy, esp. the world, health, or wealth (K.Pr. 52). ¶ hāra-kö̃ṭh adj. c.g. mottled, dappled, brindled, esp. of a black beard mixed with white hairs, or a heap of grains of rice, or the like, some white and some red. -wātᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. N. of a bird, described as medium in size with yellowish wings and a dark beak. Probably the hárwat of L. 130, the white-eyed duck, Aythya nyroca. ¶ hāri-dār m. (a pile of rice, or the like) of mixed colours (some grains white, others red, and so on). -pholᵘ m. a dapple, a spot of red; esp. a small amount of red grains seen in a pile of rice.
in har-tar adj. c.g. (of food) very delicious.

f. a cowry (L.V. 98; K.Pr. 4, 18, 37, 56, 77, 90, 106, 138, 234; YZ. 124, 395; W. 144, 154; Śiv. 1079); met. anything of small value (Śiv. 591); as adv. in the least, to the least degree (Rām. 1295). ¶ hāra f.pl. cowries; met. a collection of coined money, wealth, cash (Śiv. 1788). -bọ̆chᵘ m. cowry-hungry, greedy for money; esp. (owing to poverty) desire for money in order to accomplish some work; (of a servant or official) greedy for tips or bribes. -bāgay f. division by cowries; esp. (amongst Musalmāns) division of inherited property to the heirs according to the legal shares calculated in the proportion of so many cowries each. -bar, a mere cowry (Śiv. 1795). -kāman f. (sg. dat. -kāmüñᵘ̈), cowry-carcity, want of money, no money to buy things. -māl f. a necklace of cowries, put for the sake of ornament or sport round the necks of cows, goats, monkeys, or the like. -mŏṭh f. (sg. dat. -mŏṭhi), a fistful of cowries, esp. a handful of cowries taken up to throw down in gambling. -nolᵘ m. a complete, unbroken cowry. -ʦūr m. a cowry thief, met. a miser, a skinflint. -wôlᵘ m. (-wājĕñ), a monied man, a wealthy person. -zār m. cowry-gambling (in the game a handful of cowries is thrown down, and the winning or losing depends on the number that fall with their backs up); a kind of heads or tails. -zōr m. power due to wealth. -zörⁱ m. a cowry-gambler, see ab.

adj. c.g. every, each; all (K.Pr. 29, H. ii, 2); har-cand ہر چند conj. although (W. 100); har-dū ہردو, num. both (K.Pr. 30, 235); har-dam ہردم adv. at every moment, at all times, always (El.). har-kuni adv. everywhere (W. 95). har-ranga ہرِرنگہ adv. of every kind (K.Pr. 77, 78; W. 137). In Siv. 950 hara-dwāray may mean either 'at Haradwār' or 'at every door'. Similarly hara- mŏkh, qq.v. under har 1.
f. defeat (El.). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to defeat (El.). --sapadüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be checkmated (El.).

c.g. sec. suff. added to an old obl. form of the infinitive, forming nouns of agency, as in bakhᵃcan-hār, one who gives, from bakhᵃcun, q.v. It also indicates fitness, as in karan-hār, fit to be done; khĕna-hār, fit to be eaten (Gr.Gr. 129).

f. (sg. dat. haraküʦᵘ̈), motion, action, movement (Rām. 118, 710, 712, 952); gesture, gesticulation; act, deed; opposition, prevention, hindrance. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be interrupted, disturbed, hindered; immovability or rigidity of the limbs to occur (from rheumatism, paralysis, or the like). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to shake (tr.) (El.); to move, stir oneself, be up and doing (Gr.M., K.Pr. 79).

adj. c.g. forbidden, prohibited, unlawful, wrong (K.Pr. 37, 150; W. 154); excluded; sacred, inviolable; illegitimate, spurious; as subst. m., an unlawful act, wrong-doing, iniquity (K.Pr. 75); fornication, adultery (El.). -khāv m. an eater of unlawful things; hence, one who subsists on wealth earned by unlawful means (e.g. robbery, theft, swindling, or the like). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to live on unlawfully gotten wealth. -körī حرامکآری f. adultery, fornication (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to do unlawful things; esp. (of a woman of good family) to go wrong with men, to start leading a loose life. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a bastard; esp. a widow's bastard; met. a rascal (Gr.M.). -kȧṭil f. the conduct of a bastard; evil conduct, loose conduct (indicating that the doer can only be a widow's bastard, not of respectable family). -zôdᵘ m. a vile person (El.), a fornicator. -zözᵘ̈ f. a habitually unchaste woman. ¶ harāmukᵘ adj. (f. harāmücᵘ̈), of or belonging to the forbidden thing; hence, bastard-born, illegitimate; (of property) unlawfully earned (e.g. stolen property) (K.Pr. 77).
adj. (f. -hörᵘ̈), dappled, mottled, speckled; with dirty marks.
a deer, i.q. haryunᵘ 1, q.v. (Śiv. 267, 529). In Śiv. 660, 1680, the sg. gen. is haranunᵘ.

the form which haran or haryunᵘ 1 takes in the following:--harạna-ȧchⁱ f. an eye like that of a deer; a woman with eyes like those of a deer, a deer-eyed woman. -koṭᵘ m. (f. -küṭᵘ̈), a young deer, a fawn.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hāranôwᵘ), to defeat, conquer, overcome (in play or in battle); (in a mercantile transaction) to overcome another so that he loses his capital expenditure.
(? gender), heat, warmth; feverishness; (in Kāshmīrī) herpes, scabies (El.).
n.ag. (f. harawüñᵘ̈), (of a leaf, petal, etc.) dropping to the ground, withered and being shed; (of a person) one who is becoming withered, wasting away (from disease, cares, etc.).
n.ag. (f. hārawüñᵘ̈), one who is being conquered in a game or battle; one who in a mercantile speculation lets his invested capital be lost.
f. (sg. dat. hārawacĕ), a species of waterfowl in Kashmīr (El., Śiv. 1816).

conj. if (forming conditional sentences); also in other senses, as in wuchta hargāh mēliy, see if you can find it (Gr.M.; W. 99; H. xii, 3). --ay -- (H. viii, 10). --kiy -- (H. viii, 7, 13), id. hargah- na ہرگہ نہ conj. if not, otherwise, unless (El., Gr.M.).
(? spelling and gender), the black currant, Ribes nigrum (L. 73). Perhaps connected with hār 1. Cf. hāra-nākh, s.v. hār 1.

m. N. of the Hindū god Viṣṇu, one of the members of the triad of great gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva. Under the name of Hari, Viṣṇu is looked upon as the special protector of his devotees when in trouble. Hence, he is often called upon in the Sanskrit vocative case harē (e.g. Śiv. 733, 1841, etc.), and his name is sometimes even quoted, esp. m.c., in the Sanskrit nom. sg., i.e. hariḥ (e.g. Śiv. 1402). Other Sanskrit forms are also met in Śiv., e.g. harēḥ, the gen. sing. in the sense of the dat. sg. hari-har (Śiv. 856), hariḥ-har (Śiv. 1100, 1104) or harī-har (Śiv. 1164) m. [voc. harē-hara (Śiv. 1296), harē-haray (Śiv. 934), hari-hara (Śiv. 1587), or hariḥ-haray (Śiv. 1636)], Hari and Hara, i.e. Viṣṇu and Śiva (see har 1); esp. Viṣṇu (the Preserver) considered as one with Śiva (the destroyer). This is considered to be a profound religious mystery. hari-nārāyan m. i.q. hari 1 ab. (Śiv. 700, Rām. 119). hari-shĕmbhu m., i.q. hari-har ab., Sanskrit sg. voc. harē- shĕmbhō (Śiv. 1722-3).
in hari-hỗputᵘ or -hỗpuṭᵘ m. (of moveable or immoveable property, food, or the like, when stolen or improperly consumed) the whole, the entire, every bit.
m. N. of an ancient king famed for generosity, piety, and self-abnegation, in Sanskrit Hariścandra.

(? spelling and gender), N. of a certain fish found in Kashmīr. It weighs about a pound, has one dorsal and five ventral fins, small mouth, dark back, silver belly, and firm scales, and is in season from October till May (L. 158).
m. an outdoor servant employed to go on errands, carry letters, etc.; a running footman, courier, messenger, peon; a spy, detective, mouchard.
f. the profession of a spy or detective.

adj. c.g. unlawful, illegal; illegitimate, spurious; wicked, atrocious; as subst. m. a doer of what is forbidden or unlawful, a wicked person; a rascal, a cheat; a bastard. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become unlawful or forbidden (e.g. food which has become impure by having been partly consumed by someone else). --karun -- m.inf. to cause (food, etc.) to become impure by partly consuming it, or allowing another partly to consume it.

m. (sg. dat. harphas), a letter of the alphabet; blame, censure, reproach, stigma, animadversion (K.Pr. 78). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. censure to arise, esp. on account of a breach of hospitality. harpha pata harpha adv. literally (El. harfa pat harfa).
m. the head or supreme controller in any business. ¶ harta-karta karun m.inf. to conduct or manage a business with full authority.
f. (sg. dat. hartāli), orpiment, sulphuret of arsenic, yellow arsenic, ratsbane.

m. (sg. dat. harᵃdas, abl. harᵃda, and so on), the autumn or harvest season consisting of the two months Öshid and Kārtikh (in Skr., Aśvina and Kārttika = September-October and October-November) (K.Pr. 78, 203; L. 326; Śiv. 1039, 1573; H. ix, 8; Rām. 1006, 1661); cf. hörⁱ wa harȧdⁱ, s.v. hār 1. --lagun -- m.inf. autumn to commence; the fruits of autumn to come in, the ripening-time or harvest to commence. --waṭun -- m.inf. autumn to close; hence, the entire harvest to be brought home and stored. ¶ harᵃda-byôlᵃ m. autumn seed, seed sown in autumn for the spring crop (wheat, barley, pease, mustard, etc.). -kölⁱ adv. in the season of autumn, in the autumn. -kani adv. in about autumn, in the autumn or thereabouts. -wôñᵘ m. autumn water, the clear and pure water obtained in autumn. -wāph m. (sg. dat. -wāpas), autumn-sowing. ¶ harᵃdukᵃ adj. (f. harᵃdücᵃ), of or belonging to autumn. harᵃdas-kyutᵘ adv. in the autumn.
adj. in --nūn -- m. crushed salt as sold in the market (? in small pieces the size of cowries, hār).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. hôrᵘ), to take away, put away, remove (Śiv. 1500, 1577, 1889; Rām. 968, 1153); to abandon, banish, give up (e.g. sinful thoughts) (Śiv. 1753, 1816, 1819, 1892); to lose (in a mercantile transaction); to lose (in play, battle, etc.) (Rām. 1489, K. 252); to be defeated, be overcome, be unsuccessful; to throw down (Gr.Gr. lxxxiii); to pour forth, cause to flow, shed (blood, tears, or any other liquid) (YZ. 16, 39, 71, 275; Śiv. 1158, 1361; Rām. 284, 566, 640; K. 889). ¶ hôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), defeated in play or in a battle; (of money invested in a mercantile transaction) lost.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. horᵘ), to abandon, put away, get rid of (Śiv. 928, 1587); to lose, abandon (life) (Rām. 624, 1182); to take away, remove, destroy (Śiv. 1726); to allow to fall or drop, to shed (e.g. tears) (YZ. 262; Rām. 168, 273, 286, 376, 774, 842, 966, 975, 1201, 1309, 1403, 1482, 1717, 1736) (or blood) (Rām. 1020, 1201, 1480, 1482, 1725).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. haryōv), to fall; esp. as leaves from a tree (L.V. 72), as tears or as petals from a flower (Śiv. 1061, 1062; H. xii, 9; as rain, Rām. 1546); met. (of energy, strength, etc.), to waste away (K.Pr. 47, Siv. 165, Rām. 248, 1577); (of liquid or powder) to dribble or drip from a vessel; to waste away, disappear, be destroyed (L.V. 72; Śiv. 1164, 1752; H. vii, 24); to become lifeless (Rām. 905). ¶ haryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. haryē-müʦᵘ̈), fallen (of withered leaves, etc.) (Śiv. 1651); wasted away (of a stout person, or the like). ¶ harith pyonᵘ m.inf. to become withered (of a plant or tree); to waste away (from sickness, anxiety, old age, etc.).
adj. (f. hārüñᵘ̈), of or belonging to the month of Hār; see hār 1. --tāph -- m. (sg. dat. -tāpas), the heat of the sun in the month of Hār; met. any violently hot sunshine.
f. a female deer, a doe. The word is the f. of haryunᵘ 1, q.v.
m. N. of a bird, described as of the crane kind, and mottled white in colour.
m. (in some compounds this word takes the form harạna, q.v. The f. is harüñᵘ̈, q.v.) a deer (YZ. 12, 68, harnah).
m. N. of a village about 14 miles S.W. of Śrīnagar, said to be the ancient Hiraṇyōtsa. See, however, RT.Tr. i, 288, where it is stated that the position of Hiraṇyōtsa is unknown.
adj. (f. hariñᵘ̈), (of a tree or the like) having shoots or buds just bursting forth. Cf. har 3.
adj. c.g. vain, futile, idle, frivolous, absurd; subst. m. nonsense, twaddle. -gorᵘ m. (f. -gürᵘ̈), an idle talker, a prater; a gad- about, a gossip.
adj. c.g. one who is quarrelsome, pugnacious, contentious (Gr.Gr. 134, W. 111).
m. (sg. dat. harshĕs), joy, gladness (Śiv. 483, 717, 925, 932, etc.). ¶ harshĕs gaʦhun m.inf. to rejoice, become full of joy (Śiv. 929, 1128).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. harᵃshyōv), to rejoice (Rām. 1700, pres. part. harᵃshĕn, m.c.; K. 475).
interj. in hȧrⁱ hȧrⁱ, the cry used in driving a cow (H. xi, 8). Cf. huri.

m. a stew of meat cooked with pounded wheat and rice. -gorᵘ m. a man, usually a Musalmān, who lives by preparing this stew. --karun -- m.inf. to make such a stew; met. to beat a man or beast with stick or fist till his flesh and skin are cut, to drub, beat to a jelly, roast the ribs of (so-and-so). -wān m. a shop or place where this stew is sold.

harshēshŏr m. N. of a sacred place (in Sanskrit Harṣēśvara) about ten miles east of Śrīnagar. Here there is a Liṅga or representation of Śiva in a small cave on the summit of a high ridge to the north of the village of Khunᵃmŏh (RT.Tr. 459) (Śiv. 925, 927, 932, 1180, harshēshŏr).

or hürᵘ̈shun conj. 1 (1 p.p. haryushᵘ), i.q. haharun, q.v., to arrange for the marriage of a boy or girl, to marry off so-and-so. hȧrⁱshun bȧrⁱshun conj. 1, i.q. haharun baharun, see haharun; to arrange, carry out, undertake, any person's marriage. ¶ haryushᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. harishᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), one who has been duly married.
m. (sg. dat. hȧrⁱshĕtas), great joyfulness, a feeling of intense happiness.

m. laughter, esp. laughing at a person, ridicule. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. ridicule to occur (to so-and-so), to become a subject of public ridicule or scoffing, to be subject to a general verdict of 'serve you right'. ¶ hāsa-ḍās m. ridicule incurred owing to the destruction of one's property or work.

interj. of respect, used (1) as a suffix of respect added to nouns, as in falönⁱ söhiba-hasa, Mr. So-and-so (Gr.M.); or as a pure interjection following the noun to which it refers, but usually separated from it by the subject of the sentence, as in hē söhib, bŏh, hasa, chus zānān, Sir! I suppose (Gr.M.; H. ii, 11; v, 7; x, 4, 8, etc.). ¶ hasö interj. of respect, generally used with a verb to emphasize an affirmative statement, as in āhan-sö karān hasö chuh, Yes, Sir, he is doing (Gr.Gr. 101). -hē interj. of respect used by men to men, usually with juv or sö added, as in hasö-hē nārān juv (or sö), ho Nārāyaṇ (Gr.Gr. 97).
m. malice, envy (YZ. 405, Rām. 785). tas chuh myônᵘ hasad, I envy him (W. 125).
(? spelling), f. a variety of grape grown in Kashmīr. See El. s.v. dach.
m. (as subst., f. hasakhürᵘ̈), rude, insolent.

m. surrounding, encompassing; restriction, limit; siege, blockade; dependence, reliance; chuh ath pĕṭh kyāh hasar, what reliance is on this? what good comes of this? what is the good of doing this? (Rām. 1649).

f. a mother-in-law, the mother of a man's wife or of a woman's husband (K.Pr. 76, 80, 158, 231; W. 142; Śiv. 56, 881; Rām. 762, 1696). ōra-hash, a husband's stepmother (Rām. 759). ¶ hashĕ-bāpār m. the conduct or actions of a mother-in-law to her son- or daughter-in-law; met. conduct like that of a mother-in-law. -nŏshĕ f.pl. mother-in-law and daughter-in-law (e.g. when engaged together in some work) (Gr.Gr. 72).
interj. an expletive used in address (Śiv. 249, where the speaker addresses himself).

in the following: -dāñĕ m. paddy which, owing to unfavourable winds or to drought, has withered and barren ears. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become withered and without fruit or seed (of edible fruits or seed- crops) (Śiv. 255). --karun -- m.inf. to wither up and render barren (edible fruits, seed-crops, etc.).
adj. c.g. withered and dried up (of edible fruits or seed-crops, etc.). See hāshĕ.
m. rape by violence, esp. rape of somebody else's girl-wife (Gr.Gr. 139).
m. the usual conduct of a mother-in-law to her son- or daughter-in-law, a mother-in-law's affectionate ways; similar conduct shown to a person who is not so related (Gr.Gr. 139, 147).
m. (sg. dat. hashmatas), equipage, retinue, train; state, dignity, pomp, parade; (in Kāshmīrī) degree, rank (El.).
(Gr.Gr. 37) or hȧsⁱtiñ f. a she-elephant. See hostᵘ.
f. (sg. dat. haski), rivalry, emulation; contention. ¶ haska-hasᵃkh f. mutual emulation or rivalry; emulation exhibited by mutual abuse, mutual recrimination.

interj. used by a Hindū woman when addressing her husband, when she is alone with him, and she is near by. She does not mention his name, but merely uses the interjection (Gr.Gr. 100); cf. hatōv, bel. ¶ hatā interj. hallo!, used in addressing male juniors or inferiors, usually with ā added to the obl. form of the noun, as in hatā gulyā, ho Gulᵘ (Gr.Gr. 97, W. 100); hatā juwā, hie, Sir (K.Pr. 80). ¶ hatau interj. used, like hatabā bel. by women, with various suffixes added to the noun. Thus, hatau -- au or hatau -- a, used when addressing familiars or juniors (male or female), as hatau kākau, O father (kākh); hatau himath kaulau, O Himat Kaul; hatau gana, O Gana. hatau-- a bāyau, used when addressing men or women by their proper names only, as hatau mahādēva bāyau, O Mahādēv (Gr.Gr. 99). ¶ hatō interj. used by a man in sorrow or in addressing a person at a distance, ō or au being suffixed to the obl. case of the noun, as in hatō paryō, hallo Porᵘ (Gr.Gr. 98; W. 100; Śiv. 553, 588; H. x, 5; Rām. 1375). ¶ hata-bā interj. used (like hatau, ab.) by a woman in addressing a man or woman (W. 100) with various suffixes attached to the noun, as follows: hatabā--bā, used when addressing a man or woman respectfully; especially when addressing a priest, as in hatabā himath-bā, O Himat. hatabā--au, when addressing familiars or juniors (male or female), as hatabā kākau, O father (kākh), hatabā--a, id. as hatabā kāka. hatabā--a bāyĕ or hatabā --a bayau, used in addressing a man by proper name only, as hatabā mahādēva bāyĕ or hatabā mahādēva bāyau, O Mahādēva (Gr.Gr. 99). hata-bāhē interj. used by a man in addressing an elderly priest, a person of the middle class, or servant, bā being suffixed to the noun, as in hatabāhē zana- bā, O Zana (Gr.Gr. 97). ¶ hata-biñ interj. used when a man addresses a woman (W. 100); möjᵘ̈ is suffixed if she is older than the speaker, as in hatabiñ pārvath möjᵘ̈, O mother Pārvat; biñ is suffixed if she is of moderate age, or of an age equal to that of the speaker, as in hatabiñ Saraswath biñ, O sister Saraswat.
