It is not used in other cases (Gr.Gr. 98). ¶ hata-dĕdi (K.Pr. 80) or -möjᵘ̈ interj. used by a man when addressing an elder woman, möjᵘ̈ being suffixed to the noun, as in hatamöjᵘ̈ pārvath möjᵘ̈, O mother Pārvat (Gr.Gr. 98). -sa (H. x, 5) or -sö interj. used in addressing equals, male or female (W. 100). -söhē interj. used by a man addressing a man respectfully. If the caste of the person addressed is not mentioned, then juv or sö or both must be suffixed to it. Thus, hatasöhē rāma kaul, O Rām Kaul ('Kaul' being the name of a caste); hatasöhē nārān-juv (or nārān-juv-sö), O Nārāyan; hata- söhē gana-sö, O Gana. Sö may also be added to a caste-name, as in hatasöhē rāma kaul-sö. If bā is suffixed, it indicates that the person addressed is older, and is a priest, a person of the middle class or a servant, as in hatasöhē sahaz-bā, O Sahaz; cf. hatabāhē, ab. (Gr.Gr. 96, 97). ¶ hatōv interj. used by women in addressing a man or woman at a distance, au being suffixed to the obl. case of the noun, as in hatōv manasā rāmau, hallo Manasā Rām. It is also used by Musalmān women in addressing their husbands. Thus hatōv ködirau, O Kādir. Hindū women use hata, ab., and do not mention the husband's name (Gr.Gr. 100). ¶ hatay (El. hatai) or hatöy interj. used by men in addressing female juniors or inferiors, y being suffixed to the obl. case of the noun, as in hatay (or hatöy) waʦhariy, O female child (waʦhürᵘ̈) (Gr.Gr. 99) (W. 100, hatāi, hatöi). In H. xii, 16, it is used by a mother addressing her daughter.

f. firewood, esp. sticks collected in the forest to be used as such. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give firewood; met. (of a fraudulent shopkeeper) to sell damaged goods as in first-class condition, or goods under weight as up to weight. --khë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to eat firewood; hence, met. to be cheated, as ab. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. firewood to be applied, to be cheated, as ab. ¶ hatạba-hönzᵘ̈ m. (his wife is -hānzañ), a man who collects sticks for firewood in the forest and brings it in boats for sale.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. haṭôwᵘ), i.q. hạṭᵃrun 2, q.v. haṭôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. haṭöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), rolled to a different place; removed, put to one side, put aside.

card. (pl. dat. hatan), a hundred. For one hundred, the word is sing. as in Śiv. 166, 711; H. i, 9; v, 10, 12; while for two hundred or more it is plur. as in H. v, 1. For the higher hundreds, hath is used up to eight hundred; but for nine hundred and above shĕth (q.v.) is used. Thus zᵃh hath, two hundred; trihath, three hundred; nav shĕth, nine hundred; bāh shĕth, twelve hundred (Gr.Gr. 84), but hath sās, a hundred thousand (Śiv. 1875) (K.Pr. 7, 58, 216; H. i, 8, 9; ii, 12; Rām. 536, 796); a copper coin, at present corresponding in value to the British pice, so called because in ancient times it corresponded to 100 dīnnāras (RT.Tr. II, 310 ff., esp. 312, 315). In this sense it is only used when more than two pice are referred to in counting, as in trihath, three pice; pönʦhath, five pice (Gr.Gr. 85, K.Pr. 216). -gobᵘ m. (of a tree, etc.) possessing a hundred shoots. -güñᵘ̈ f. the base of the rectum. -gorᵘ m. (f. -gürᵘ̈), one who (visits) a hundred houses; hence, met. a gossip, a gadabout; a wandering beggar; a fickle restless fellow (Rām. 1652). -hanḍöjᵘ̈ or -hanḍāl f. she who has a hundred lovers, an unchaste woman; cf. hanḍāl. -haṭurᵘ m. (f. -haṭürᵘ̈), a persistent and impudent cheat. -khanḍ m. about a hundred. -shĕth m. a little more or less than a hundred, a hundred or thereabouts. ¶ hata-bodᵘ or -bọ̆dᵘ adj. (f. -büzᵘ̈), consisting of hundreds; counted in hundreds; in pl., hundreds (of such and such a thing), in the sense of a very great number. See bọ̆dᵘ 2 (Gr.Gr. 144; Śiv. 1626; H. ix, 9; K. 478, 928). -gonᵘ adj. (f. -güñᵘ̈), a hundred- fold. -môrᵘ adj. (f. -mörᵘ̈), a killer of hundreds; met. of a malicious character, maleficent, envenomed. -wahorᵘ, or -wahurᵘ, or (Gr M.) -wuhurᵘ adj. (f. -warishᵘ̈), a hundred years old; that which has lasted a hundred years. ¶ hȧtⁱ hūnⁱ khyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. --khyē-müʦᵘ̈ --), distracted by the necessity of carrying out a number of different urgent and difficult works at the same time. hȧtⁱ hūnⁱkhyonⁱ m.inf. to be distracted, as ab. hȧtⁱ wạhȧrⁱ adv. after a hundred years. ¶ hathāh khanḍā m. a group of about a hundred, but a little less (Gr.Gr. 84).

m. (sg. dat. haṭhas), obstinacy, stubbornness, malevolent pertinacity; a kind of forced yōga or abstract meditation amongst Hindūs, in which the mind is obstinately withdrawn from external objects (Śiv. 1833, K. 877). --karun -- m.inf. to show obstinacy, to act obstinately.

m. (sg. dat. hāṭhas), obstinacy, malevolent pertinacity. --phuṭarun -- m.inf. to break a person's obstinacy (by opposing it); to keep in subjection (a servant, or the like) by dealing crossly with him from the very first. --phuṭarāwun -- m.inf., id.

m.pl. a callosity, a corn (K.Pr. 15); a scar, cicatrix. --gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m.pl.inf. corns or callosities to come on the feet or hands. --karȧnⁱ -- m.pl.inf. a crop of callosities to come on the hands from hard manual work.
m. (sg. dat. hāṭas), a market, a bāzār; traffic, buying or selling in a market.
m. a (smith's) large hammer, a sledge-hammer.
or hȧthⁱyār m. a tool, implement; a weapon; (pl.) arms [Śiv. 12 (hȧthⁱhār), K. 595, 948 (hȧthⁱyār)].
adv. to the best of one's power, so far as lies in (one's) power, to one's utmost (Rām. 1531).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. haṭyōv), to be or become lean or thin, to waste away (from sickness, sorrow, anxiety, or the like); to move away, fall back, retire, be driven back, repulsed (Śiv. 1163, 1557). haṭyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. haṭyē-müʦᵘ̈), become lean, etc., as ab.
or hȧtⁱyā f. destruction of life, murder; esp. murder of a Brāhmaṇ, a cow, or respectable person (this, of course, from the Hindū point of view),--a Hindū word.
adj. (f. hatiñᵘ̈), costing or worth a hundred (rupees, or the like).
f. (sg. dat. hạṭᵃrüñᵃ), the act of making thin, causing to waste away (a man or beast by putting to severe exertion or by ill-treatment).
f. (sg. dat. hạṭᵃrüñᵃ), the act of rolling or moving something from one place to another.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hạṭᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. hạṭᵃrun 1, q.v. hạṭᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ 1 perf. part. (f. hạṭᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. hạṭᵒrᵒ-motᵒ 1, see hạṭᵃrun 1.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hạṭᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. hạtᵃrun 2, q.v. hạṭᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. hạṭᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. hạṭᵒrᵒ-motᵒ 2, see hạṭᵃrun 2.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hạṭᵒrᵒ), to cause to become thin, to cause to waste away (by overwork, ill-treatment, or the like). hạṭᵒrᵒ-motᵒ 1 perf. part. (f. hạṭᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to become thin, as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. hạṭᵒrᵒ), to roll anything from one place to another; to move to one side, put aside (= Hindī haṭāna); met. to put aside or successfully resist (a claim) (Gr.M.). hạṭᵒrᵒ-motᵒ 2 perf. part. (f. hạṭᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), moved aside, etc., as ab. ¶ hạṭᵃri hạṭᵃri phērun m.inf. to wander hither and thither to great distances, with much toil, and to no profit. hạṭᵃri hạṭᵃri phirun m.inf. to roll something about from place to place; to cause some poor fellow to wander, as ab. hạṭᵃri hạṭᵃri phiranāwun m.inf. to cause some poor fellow to wander about from street to street, to no profit, and with great toil.

card. the form which hath, a hundred (q.v.) takes in multiplication as in kāh hȧtⁱ, eleven times a hundred. It can only be used with numerals above ten. We cannot say ʦōr hȧtⁱ, four times a hundred, but must say hath ʦākh, a hundred times four (Gr.Gr. 86).
m. (f. hȧtⁱyārĕñ), a murderer; esp. of cows, or of men (a Hindū word).
f. a habit of murdering; met. wicked conduct as bad as that of a murderer.
hav interj. an exclamatory pleon. suff. used in poetry, e.g. in H. ii, 10; an interj. used by a woman in addressing her husband (H. v, 4; xi, 11). Cf. hay 2.
(? spelling) f. the female monāl pheasant, Lophophorus refulgens (L. 119).
in hāwa-dōr f. tantalizing (as when one promises some gift or to perform some work, and then merely shows it, and does not carry out the promise). Cf. hāwun.
in hāwa-bāv m. coquettish gestures tending to excite amorous sensations, coquetry, blandishments.
m. (amongst Hindūs) an oblation to the gods; havĕ-kavy, m.pl. oblations to the gods and to deceased ancestors (K. 974).

(Rām. 130) or hawā ہوا (Rām. 867, 1651) m. air, atmosphere (Rām. 130, 867); air, wind (Śiv. 340, 501, 505; H. ii, 6), esp. a gale (Rām. 1651); air, climate (Gr.M.); a gas; rumour, report; credit, good name; affection, favour, love, desire, passionate fondness; lust, carnal desire, concupiscence; an empty or worthless thing; puffed-up-ness, impertinence, sauciness (e.g. on the part of a child, a wife, or a servant).
f. Eve, the mother of mankind (Gr.M.; H. vii, 7).
or hĕwal f. (sg. dat. hawali), backbiting, speaking ill of a person in his absence. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to go about backbiting a person out of envy.

or hawālath حوالت m. transfer, consignment, commitment; charge, trust, care, custody (K.Pr. 13; YZ. 102; Śiv. 662; H. x, 7; Rām. 218, 374, etc.); consignment (of any property, duty, or liability) in trust (H. v, 10). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be committed to (someone's) charge, to be delivered in trust, etc. --karun -- m.inf. to give in charge or possession (of), to deliver in trust, to entrust, deposit, to commit to the care (of), to commit to the custody (of) (H. v, 7, 12; viii, 4; x, 12; xii, 22). ¶ hawölⁱ hĕth or hawölĕth f. (sg. dat. --hë̆ʦᵘ̈ --), (in expressing gratitude for favours received) the act of making over to another the fruits of one's former virtuous conduct. -mawölⁱ m.pl. a number of persons visiting another and wasting his time. ¶ hawālath Khŏdā حوالت خدا interj. adieu! (L. 458).
m. (f. hawāladariñ), one to whom anything is entrusted, a trustee; m. a military officer (of inferior rank), a havildar.
f. the business or act of taking things in trust, trusteeship.
m. (amongst Hindūs) an oblation, burnt offering, sacrifice.
(El.), haiwān, höwān حیوان m. a quadruped, an animal as distinct from man, a beast, a brute (Gr.M.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hāwanôwᵘ), to cause to show or display, to cause to explain; to cause a Hindū religious offering to be performed; to cause (a solemn oath) to be taken (Rām. 1575).
or (Śiv. 190, 739) hāwas m. eager desire (Śiv. 190, 340, 739); lust, concupiscence, inordinate appetite; ambition; curiosity. Cf. hawus.
(Śiv. 190, 739) i.q. hawas, q.v. ¶ hāwạsa adv. with extreme desire, very eagerly.

f. a whiff, a puff (El.); very little of anything [often --˚, as in āba hawāwā, a very little water. In this sense only used for liquids, air, and things that cannot be said to have pieces (W. 21, 130)]; a moment of time, a twinkling of an eye (Rām. 549, 987). ¶ hawāwi-hanā f., id.
n.ag. (f. hāwawüñᵘ̈), one who shows, etc., see hāwun (Śiv. 623, 854).
f. (sg. dat. hawölë˘ʦᵘ̈), i.q. hawölⁱ hĕth, q.v. s.v. hawāla.

adj. c.g. of or pertaining to the air; airy, windy; idle, vain, capricious, flighty; licentious; badly-conducted, disobedient; a votary of pleasure (used in Kāshmīrī, esp. with reference to children, women, servants, horses, or the like). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. (of a child, woman, servant, horse, etc.) to become disobedient and badly conducted, licentious, etc. --karun -- m.inf. to lead into or encourage in licentious conduct, etc.
m. one who shows, as in wata-hāwukᵘ, one who shows a road, a guide (Gr.M., YZ. 432).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. hôwᵘ), to show, display, point out (K.Pr. 14, 81, 61, 87, 165, 242, 247; YZ. 18, 117, 126, 231, 411, 454, 461; Śiv. 15, 28, 33, 99, etc.; H. iii, 8; iv, 7, etc.; Rām. 6, 44, 61, etc.); to make manifest, to explain; to perform a Hindū religious offering; to take (a solemn oath) (H. v, 9; Rām. 1056; K. 812). This word is considered to be the causal of ḍēshun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 176). hôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. höwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), shown, displayed; manifested, explained.
f. a pair, two of anything; esp. a pair of plough-bullocks. dā̃da-hawürᵘ̈, a yoke of oxen (K.Pr. 10) (vill., cf. horᵘ 1).
or hāwusᵘ m. eager desire; lust, concupiscence, inordinate appetite; ambition; curiosity, i.q. hawas. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such desire, etc., to arise. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to fulfil a desire.
m., i.q. hawus, q.v. --gaʦhun -- m.inf., i.q. hawus gaʦhun, q.v. s.v. hawus. --kaḍun -- m.inf. i.q. hawus kaḍun, see hawus. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. extreme desire to arise.
f. a litter, a palanquin, a carriage (Śiv. 1699).
m. a cry of trouble or sorrow, an 'alas'; interj. alas! (El. háe, W. 101, hāi; L.V. 67; Śiv. 536; Rām. 4; H. v, 7). --karun -- m.inf. to groan (El.). ¶ hāyi interj. alas! (YZ. 342, 543, 544).
conj. an optional form of ay, if, u.w. the past cond. as in karihē hay, if he had made (Gr.Gr. 257).
interj. used in addressing female juniors or inferiors, y being also suffixed to the abl. case of the noun, as in hāy waʦharity, O female child (waʦhürᵘ̈) (Gr.Gr. 99).

f. soot (Rām. 651, 1199, 1212). ¶ hāyĕ gaʦhun m.inf. to go to soot; hence (of some valuable or pretty person or thing) to be spoiled, to lose its value or beauty. -raza f.pl. ropes of soot, a quantity of soot gradually collected. -lọ̆ʦhᵘ m. a lump or clotted mass of soot.
interj. used by a man in addressing his wife (H. xi, 14, 10, 19), or by a woman addressing a woman (H. v, 2; ix, 7). Cf. hau, hav.

or hayā حیا m. shame, sense of shame, modesty; shyness, bashfulness (K.Pr. 29); modest respect shown to an elder, etc., respectful obedience. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. modest respect to occur, respect to be shown to the wishes of an elder or the like (whether voluntary or involuntary); discouragement to be felt (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to make respectful obedience, punctiliously and modestly to carry out the wishes of an elder, etc. -vĕʦar m. habitual respect shown to the wishes of an elder, etc. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. vë̆ʦᵘ̈), one who modestly conforms to the wishes of his elders and betters.
m. a large pair of scales used for heavy weights of grain, etc. (K.Pr. 136; Śiv. 589). ¶ hāyĕkh-ḍünḍᵘ̈ f. the beam of such scales. -pôturᵘ m. the pan of such scales.
or hȧzⁱ interj. used by Musalmāns in addressing a superior (literally, Saint!) (L. 279; W. 100, 101; H. v, 9).
m. (sg. dat. hazīmatas), rout, defeat. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to be routed, to be defeated (Rām. 916, 1400).

f. (sg. dat. hazrüʦᵘ̈), presence; dignity; a title applied to any great man, the object of resort, Your Majesty (El.; H. iv, 2, etc.; vi, 8, 10, etc.). -bal ll m. the most popular of all the Musalmān shrines in the Kashmīr Valley; said to be built over the remains of the miracle-working Pīr Dastagīr Sāḥib, and to contain a hair of Muhammad's beard. In Phākh Pargana (El. and RT.Tr. II, 457).
adj. (f. hazᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or hazürᵘ̈), impudent, insolent (esp. of a child or youth). hazürᵘ̈ guzürᵘ̈ta bāzürᵘ̈ f. a young woman who is impertinent, immodest, and who goes her own gait.
m. jesting; a jest, joke; buffoonery; nonsensical talk; obscene language; in Kāshmīrī, angry blame or censure.
adj. c.g. an accuser, calumniator; (of an action, thing, or state) that which renders one liable to blame even by a slight connexion.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. hāʦaladiñ), a calumniator; that which injures a person's reputation by merely a slight connexion.
m. the condition of being smitten; misery, affliction, wretchedness; humility (El.).
pron. adv. that many, so many (W. 94, haʦ).

f. (sg. dat. hāʦi), an accusation of a crime, or the like (K.Pr. 137; YZ. 312; H. vi, 9; K. 150, 675, 676); calumny, defamation. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an accusation to occur; met. (of something destroyed after slight use or experience, or of the user or experiencer of something so destroyed) nothing but the blame to remain. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to accuse (El.). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an accusation or blame to be incurred (whether rightly or wrongly). --lāgüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring an accusation (true or false). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an accusation to come; to find oneself wrongly charged with something committed by another. ¶ hāʦi-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to an accusation; hence, the condition of being breakable by a mere touch, extreme brittleness, the condition of something which 'came in two in my hand'. --lagun -- m.inf. to become an innocent subject of an accusation (esp. of theft, or the like).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. hāʦiladiñ), one who is defamed by calumny, or whose reputation is injured by an accusation (true or false).
adj. (f. hāʦüjᵘ̈), (of a person) slanderous, calumnious; one who habitually accuses, a habitual calumniator.
m. reproach, scolding uttered to or by a child.
f. (sg. dat. hạʦᵃrüñᵃ), the act of striking a blow; hence, reducing to misery.

interj. of respect, used by a man to a man, as in hē huzūr, sir; hē nārān, O Nārāyaṇa (L.V. 109; Śiv. 14, 155, et passim; Rām. 50, 51, etc.); the word juv or sö (or sa, Gr.M.) or both are often suffixed to the noun, but juv cannot be used with a word indicating caste. Thus hē nārān juv, hē nārān sö, hē nārān juv sö; hē gana kaul, O Gaṇa Kaul; hē rāma kaul sö, O Rāma Kaul. We cannot say hē gana kaul juv, because kaul is a caste-name. Cf. Gr.Gr. 96 and Gr.M. s.v. Gr.M. gives also forms such as hē söhib-a, hē söhib-a-sa, hē söhib... hasa, all meaning 'sir'. In Śiv. 507 (hē bawānī) the interj. is used in addressing a goddess.
or hĕch f. nothing (K.Pr. 164). ¶ hĕca kaḍañĕ f. pl. inf. to extract nothings; hence, owing to want of help or appliances, to be stopped over and over again when commencing some necessary task.
f. wages paid for teaching, a tutor's salary, school fees.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. hĕchanôwᵘ), to teach, instruct, inculcate; to advise, prompt; to admonish, reprove (K.Pr. 16, Śiv. 1000, K. 949). ¶ hĕchanāwan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a teacher, instructor, tutor, admonisher, etc.
c.g. one who learns and does nothing else, one who for any purpose applies himself zealously to the study of any particular subject, a scholar (El.).
f. money paid for learning, a scholarship.
n.ag. (f. hĕchawüñᵘ̈), one under instruction, a learner, a pupil.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. hyochᵘ, f. hë̆chᵘ̈), to learn, master; to acquire knowledge (cf. Gr.M.) (K.Pr. 101, 118; YZ. 238; Rām. 12, 1437; K. 486). hĕch lāyȧnⁱ rīnzⁱ, learn to throw balls (H. v, 3). ¶ hĕchan-vizᵘ̈ the time of learning, the period of life during which education continues, school and college days; the time on any particular day during which instruction is received, school-hours; a time suitable for receiving instruction. ¶ hyochᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hë̆chᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), one who has learned, educated, taught by others or self-taught.
n.ag. (f. hĕḍawüñᵘ̈), a ridiculer, one who makes another subject to ridicule or contempt.
f. ridicule, bringing another into contempt.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. hyoḍᵘ; 2 p.p. hĕjyōv), to ridicule, blame, abuse; make a subject of contempt, mock at. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. ridicule to occur, public ridicule to be incurred by some great effort or important transaction coming to naught directly it is attempted or commenced.

m. (sg. dat. hĕḍaras), a mushroom (K.Pr. 189), Agaricus sp. (L. 73). Cf. hĕnḍa. It is said to be produced by thunder. It is eaten both by Hindūs and Musalmāns, cooked with ghī and condiments. The country people preserve them by drying (El.). ¶ hĕḍar-rāṭh or -rã̄ṭh f. (sg. dat. rāṭhi), a natural mushroom bed (usually found on the lower mountain slopes).
f. (sg. dat. hẹ̆ḍᵃrüñᵃ), maliciously causing a person to be ridiculed or to become a subject of contempt.

m. stupefaction, consternation (so that even one's breath is stopped) caused by unexpected calamity (such as the news of the death of a beloved person, total destruction of property, terror at the approach of an enemy, or the like). --anun -- m.inf. to be seized by such consternation. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such consternation to occur.
n.ag. (f. hĕkawüñᵘ̈), one who is especially energetic, one who is specially notable beyond others for his energy.
in hĕka-hĕkh f. (sg. dat. -hĕki), striving over and over again to the best of one's ability to accomplish some difficult or impossible task. Cf. hĕkun pyonᵘ, s.v. hĕkun, hĕkath pë̆ñᵘ̈, s.v. hĕkath.
f. (sg. dat. hĕkmüʦᵘ̈), wisdom, knowledge (Gr.M.); cleverness, contrivance, ingenuity (H. i, 11, 12; Rām. 871); device.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. hyokᵘ; f. hë̆cᵘ̈; 2 p.p. hĕcyōv), to act or strive successfully in some difficult task (L.V. 108); to be able, to can. ¶ This verb is commonly used to form a potential compound with the conj. part. of another verb. In such cases it generally indicates physical ability as opposed to tagun (q.v.), which implies mental ability (i.e. to be able to do a thing, in the sense of knowing how to do it). Thus, --anith, to be able to bring; --būzith, to be able to hear; --dith, to be able to give, and so on. In this meaning the future tense of hĕkun is usually employed in the sense of the present, as in hĕka arzith, I can earn. Cf. Gr.M. s.v. (L.V. 107; YZ. 48, 142, 222; Śiv. 711, 895, 908, 1099, 1624, 1631, 1633; Rām. 196, 211, 293, 581, 631, 645, etc.). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. 'striving one's best to fall (to one's lot)', to be compelled to use all one's power's, esp. when the task is beyond one's strength. Cf. hĕka-hĕkh, s.v. hĕkh 2, and hĕkath pë̆ñᵘ̈, s.v. hĕkath. ¶ hĕkan-höjᵘ̈ f. (applied to a person) vigorous ability, esp. in setting people by the ears, in doing profitless or improper actions, or the like. -hyurᵘ m. id. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājyĕñ), possessed of ability, powerful; esp. one who is mighty both in quarrelling and as a carrier of heavy loads. Commonly used with reference to an able-bodied virago.

or hĕkath f. (sg. dat. hĕkᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈ or hĕküʦᵘ̈), ability, power; esp. exercise of power or ability to perform some difficult task, such as carrying a heavy load, travelling over a difficult road, undertaking a difficult occupation, or the like (Gr.Gr. 128). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. exercise of ability to fall (to one's lot); hence, to put one's self to the exercise of one's best ability for the complete accomplishment of some difficult task. Cf. hĕka-hĕkh, s.v. hĕkh 2, and hĕkun pyonᵘ, s.v. hĕkun. --rōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. ability to remain (of an old man or one starved, etc.), to act with all the ability and strength of a young person, one's physical powers to be retained in spite of old age or disease. ¶ hĕkᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈-wôlᵘ̈), wisdom, knowledge (Gr.M.); cleverness, contrivance, ingenuity (H. i, 11, 12; Rām. 871); device.
f. dirty ground, covered with litter, mud, dirt, etc.; dirt used as manure (Gr.Gr. 25; L. 461). ¶ hĕla khasañĕ f. pl. inf. dirty places to arise (of the body, garments, etc.), to become dirty.
written hĕlah kar, and translated 'endeavour' in K.Pr. 187, and hĕllah kar, translated 'be encouraged' in K.Pr. 81. The word is probably the same as hala 3, under which cf. hala karun.

f. a pod, a legume, the pod of a pea, bean, or similar vegetable (K.Pr. 81; cf. dŏda- hĕm, p. 189a, l. 38, and kara-hĕm, s.v. kara 2). ¶ hĕma-phal m. a quantity of beans, peas, or the like which have been shelled.
f. a crease in cloth, leather, or the like. --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a crease to rise, a crease to come into existence.
adj. c.g. marked with a long crease, whether by nature or accidentally. Cf. hĕm 2.
f. (sg. dat. hĕmüʦᵘ̈), magnanimity (Śiv. 728); spirit, courage, bravery; power, strength, ability (Rām. 36).
f. (sg. dat. hĕmmüʦᵘ̈), spirit, courage, bravery (K.Pr. 91, 232); good ambition (W. 33).

f. slaughter, esp. slaughter of living creatures for food lawful to Kāshmīrī Hindūs; sin (generally) (Śiv. 897). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. extreme rapacity to occur, of such a kind that it does not stop at robbing the powerless of their property or even the hungry of their food (Rām. 607).

m. (sg. abl. hĕna 1), a state of fear of punishment for some fault, owing to previous experience of such punishment, 'a burnt child dreading the fire.' --rōzun -- m.inf. to be afraid of the consequences of any action owing to previous experience of the unpleasant results of a previous similar action.
m. the act of taking (Gr.Gr. 120, where 'placing' is a misprint).
m. the Lawsonia inermis or Indian myrtle, henna (used for staining the nails of the hand and feet) (El.).
m. India. hĕnda-lürᵘ̈ अत्युन्नतसदनविशेषः f. a mansion, a palace.
f. a mushroom, esp. an edible one; cf. hĕḍur. Mushrooms are used in stews, broths, or the like.

or hendavĕnd (= ہندوانہ)  m. a water melon (L. 348, 462; K.Pr. 174, 184, 218). -kāl m. the water melon season (about the months of August and September). -pŏkhur m. (sg. dat. -pŏkharas), a water basin for irrigating water melons; a young water melon with the sprouts just opening. -pālēza m. a kind of trellis on which water melons are grown. ¶ hĕndavĕnda-kulᵘ m. the water melon plant (El.).

m. the horn of an animal (K.Pr. 49, 81; Rām. 634, 924; K. 351). --phuṭarȧnⁱ -- m.pl. inf. to break (so-and-so's) horns; met. to humble, abase, humiliate, esp. when some mighty person is abased by some feeble person over whom he has tyrannized. --ṭᵃsanȧnᵃ -- m.pl. inf. the thrust in the horns; met. causelessly to tyrannize over and oppress feeble persons. ¶ hĕnga-mŏ̈nḍᵘ̈ f. the base or root of a horn; met. hidden pride, concealed self-satisfaction (owing to some private cause, such as the secret accumulation of wealth, or the like). -phuṭᵘ adj. (f. -phuṭᵘ̈), broken-horned, having a horn or horns broken; met. humiliated (by the loss of fortune, friend, or the like). -traṭh f. (sg. dat. traṭi), extreme pride or conceit (owing to wealth, family, or the like) combined with miserly conduct. -zyūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈), long-horned; met. arrogant, puffed up with conceit (owing to having numerous adherents, relations, friends, or the like). ¶ hĕngan më̆ʦᵘ̈ ladüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to put earth on the horns; met. causelessly, and out of arrogance, to engage in quarrelling, abuse, or the like).

adj. c.g. horned, possessing horns; endowed with especially large horns (Gr.Gr. 134); met. haughty or full of pride owing to the possession of wealth, fine qualities, and many adherents. -mŏnjȧl m. of great reputation owing to endowment with wealth, high virtues, and many adherents, a grandee, magnate.
f. a kind of rosary made of seeds brought from Southern India; a single seed of such a rosary; N. of a Śakti or goddess.

m. (sg. dat. hĕnaras), a stream fouled with filth, ordure, etc., a sewer, drain (K.Pr. 250). ¶ hĕnar-graz f. the roar of a sewer, pouring forth of ordure and urine with a sound like that of a great river; met. insolence and tyranny shown by a vile person suddenly raised to power (K.Pr. 9). -kyomᵘ m. a worm or maggot bred in a sewer, met. a dirty child lean of body and dark in complexion. -wôñᵘ m. sewer water, the liquid conveyed in a sewer.

f. (sg. dat. hēri 1, for 2, see hīrᵘ̈, for 3, see hyūrᵘ), a staircase, a flight of stairs, a ladder used as such (Śiv. 61, 598, 847, 1036, 1081; Rām. 44, 571-2). It may be either outside (K.Pr. 246) a house or inside, in either case leading to the upper storey (cf. hyūrᵘ); a damaging crease or mark in woollen cloth caused by shrinking in the wash. --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. lit. to bring such a crease (of washed woollen cloth which has been spoilt by shrinking), to be creased thereby, to be creased and damaged in the wash. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to lead into dissolute ways, to debauch. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. crooked creases and lines to appear in woollen cloth which has shrunk in the wash. ¶ hēra-pôwᵘ m. a single step in a brick or wooden staircase, a stair. ¶ hēri-bar m. a staircase door, a door, or plank used as a door, at the foot or at the head of a staircase. -khotᵘ m. a closet under a staircase. -lāday f. a complimentary present divided among the workmen employed on building a house when the staircase is set up. -tronᵘ m. the triangular space under a staircase, used in Kashmīr as a dark cupboard for storing firewood, rice, etc. There are usually two in a house, one on each floor. -wọ̆bᵘ m. a kind of barred window over an inner staircase in order to give light. --wasun -- m.inf. to come downstairs (K.Pr. 246, K. 656).

f. (sg. dat. hērüʦᵘ̈), N. of a celebrated Hindū festival, the Sanskrit Śivarātri, in honour of the god Shiv (Śiva), lasting for five days from the 11th lunar day of the dark half of Phāgun (in Skr. Phālguna = February-March) until the day of the new moon (L. 266, K.Pr. 81, Śiv. 524). It is preceded by a festival of cleansing the house, commencing on the 1st lunar day of the dark fortnight and ending on the 8th. Cf. ḍulᵘ 1 and hurᵘ 2. ¶ hērüʦᵘ̈-bôgᵘ̈ m. N. of a present given by the relations of a Hindū girl to the relations of her husband on this festival. -truwāh f. (sg. dat. -truwöshᵘ̈), the thirteenth lunar day of the dark half of Phāgun, being the middle day of the Hērath festival. According to tradition King Dāmodara II of Kashmīr was changed into a serpent, and was told that he would never leave his snake-form till the whole of the Sanskrit Rāmāyaṇa was read through to him on the night of this date. No one has ever succeeded in accomplishing this feat, and he still lies under the curse (RT.Tr. note to i, 166).

hēryumᵘ, or hīryumᵘ adj. (f. hĕrimᵘ̈, etc.), of above, belonging to a higher region; of a place higher than that of the speaker (Gr.Gr. 152); upstairs, of or belonging to the upper rooms of a house. --pôrᵘ -- m. the upper quarters, the upper room of a house (Gr.M.).
adv. above; upstream (of a river) (K. 75); -pĕṭhᵃ adv. from above, downwards (K. 450). Cf. hyorᵘ.

m. feeling, sense; a sense, a faculty of sense (Śiv. 1514); imagination; (in Kāshmīrī) memory or expert knowledge due to previous thorough acquaintance with any thing or subject, or to previous thorough experience (Śiv. 80, 189); meditation (on something), concentration of mind (Śiv. 1530, 1532, 1687, 1845, 1853, 1857); care, attention, carefulness (Śiv. 1017). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to call to a person's memory how to deal with some forgotten subject, to remind about. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such expert knowledge to be acquired. -hōsh m. memory and sense, mental faculties generally. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to capture the intellect, compel attention (Śiv. 257); to capture the senses (Śiv. 1453). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. thorough knowledge of any science or art to come by study and practice; the senses to return in the case of fainting, senselessness, etc. ¶ hĕsa phērun m.inf. to be brought to one's senses (e.g. of a madman, or one suffering under delusions); to have some forgotten business forcibly called to one's memory; to be cognisant of (Śiv. 1428). --phirun -- or --phirawun -- m.inf. to bring a person to his senses, as ab.; forcibly to stir up a person's memory about something forgotten. --phirawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --phirawüñᵘ̈ --), one who brings another to his senses, or stirs up his memory, as ab. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), experienced, thoroughly cognisant by practice. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come to one's senses (from madness, delusion, or the like). ¶ hĕsas āsun m.inf. to remember (Śiv. 1719).
m. the act of helping or forwarding (someone's work or desires), grant of help (Śiv. 122, 584, 1510).
adj. c.g. (of a horse) habitually curvetting, frisky-natured, high-spirited; (of a man) one who habitually gocs capering along, one who habitually skips along, one who bounds along. Cf. hĕṭh.

(hyotᵘ, taken, and dyutᵘ, given), in --lagun -- m.inf. the alarm and agitation caused by the knowledge that one is at the point of death to be experienced; similar alarm and agitation to be experienced under other circumstances.
m. (sg. dat. hĕṭas), capering, frisking; self-conceit (as indicated by such a gait). Cf. hĕṭal.
m. hindrance, obstruction, delay. --lagun -- m.inf. such delay to occur (when a work should be done quickly).

adj. (as subst., sg. dat. hĕtas), friendly, kindly, well disposed; pleasant, agreeable (L.V. 28). hĕth samāgam (Śiv. 1848), a friendly meeting, and also (with double meaning) having taken (hĕth 1) a meeting, having met. Cf. hyotᵘ 1.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. hẹ̆tᵃriladiñ), one who suffers from white leprosy, a leper (El. hittarilad; W. 111 hėtarilad).
f. white leprosy (El. hittar; W. 111 hėtar); cf. atha-hĕturᵘ, p. 58b, l. 12. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. white leprosy to fall (i.e. to become afflicted with it).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hĕwanôwᵘ), to cause to take, etc. (Gr.Gr. 172). Caus. of hyonᵘ, q.v., i.q. hyāwun.

n.ag. (f. hĕwawüñᵘ̈), one who takes, a taker; a buyer, purchaser, a customer; one who takes (abuse or ill-treatment), one who is poor-spirited, who is long-suffering, who 'takes it lying down'; one who exhibits equanimity and takes all things equally, as they come. Cf. hyonᵘ. ¶ hĕwawañĕ khörᵘ̈ adv. even at the very commencement.
interj. addressed to a male inferior (W. 100). hēyöī interj. addressed to a female inferior (W. 100).

m. (of men, etc.) a kindly disposition, kindliness, benignity, kind-heartedness; (of ornaments, etc.) becomingness, enhancement (of beauty); (of a medicine) benignness, balsamicness, the possession of remedial properties; and so on for other things.
f. the cry used in inciting or encouraging workmen engaged in any employment--principally used by inhabitants of the forests, etc.
or hihurᵘ m. (sg. dat. hi(ĕ)haras ), a father-in-law (either of a husband or of a wife) (K.Pr. 135, Śiv. 56, H. x, 12).

f.pl. a certain game, generally played by two young women. According to the description they hold each other's hands, with their feet together, and so rise face to face. Then bending their bodies backwards they dance, uttering a cooing cry at the same time.
m. in hikörⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to go mad, to lose all sense of decency, good conduct, discrimination, and religion.
(? spelling), m. a cluster of grapes (El.).

f. (sg. dat. hili), N. of an aquatic weed (W. 8, Śiv. 1804). It grows abundantly in the city lake, and is placed over the region of the bladder by native physicians when there is strangury (El.). Used met. to represent a thing of no value (K.Pr. 43). --barüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cover (sown seeds, young plants, etc.), with this weed to protect them from the sun. --ta hēch --, weeds and nothing, a thing of no value (K.Pr. 164). ¶ hili-göḍᵘ̈ f. a certain delicate flavoured fish that haunts lakes in which this weed grows. -robᵘ m. a small trench or basin dug round the root of a melon or pumpkin plant and filled up with this grass, which is kept wet, so as to supply the plant with the necessary moisture. -ʦakh m. (sg. dat. -ʦaki), a block or clump of this weed occurring when the water is low in autumn, so as to impede the progress of boats.

m. evasion, shift, wile, artifice, trick, plot, stratagem (YZ. 420); pretence, colour; evasion, method of evading (Rām. 276); deceit, deception, fraud (El. gives híla and hailah). --karanwôlᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --karanwājĕñ --), an impostor (El.).
(? spelling), the hillu of L. 463, where it is described as the equivalent of gupan-nĕnd and of haji, q.q.v., and as meaning weeding and working a rice-field by cattle.
n.ag. (f. hilawüñᵘ̈), a man, a dog, or other animal who having once robbed or taken anything with impunity, repeats the wrong action over and over again and becomes a confirmed robber, etc.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. hilyōv) (of one who has once committed oppression, robbery, or the like with impunity), to become a habitual and confident robber, tyrant, etc.; cf. atha-hilȧnⁱ, p. 58a, l. 46. hilyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hilyē-müʦᵘ̈), one who by the continued practice of robbery, tyranny, or the like, is expert in doing it, one who has become a professional robber or confirmed tyrant.
f. (sg. dat. hilᵃrüñᵃ), the act of inducing or tempting another to act as a confirmed robber, oppressor, etc. See hilun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hilᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. hilᵃrun, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hilᵒrᵒ), to induce or tempt another to become an habitual robber, oppressor, etc. Cf. hilun.
m. the Himālaya Mountain. Personified as father of Pārvatī, wife of the god Śiva, in Śiv. 426, 635, 683, 686, 692, 714, 728, 837, 1219, 1221, 1259, 1318, 1440, 1456. Cf. himālay.
f. protection (K.Pr. 104); guardianship, patronage, support (K.Pr. 81). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to protect, guard, patronize. ? Cf. El. himayit karinyi, to entrust.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. himyōv), to become snow, to be turned into snow (L. 16).
adj. c.g. deprived or bereft of, free from, devoid of; deficient, defective, faulty; (of a person) mean, vile, despicable (owing to lowness of caste). Cf. hyūnᵘ.
or (Gr.Gr. 14) hiñⁱ f. neighing of a horse, whinnying (El. hin). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to neigh (El.). ¶ hiñĕ-gurᵘ m. a neighing horse, a horse given to neighing.
adj. c.g. of or belonging to India (Gr.Gr. 150); the Hindōstānī language (Gr.M.). --zĕv f. the Hindōstānī language (Gr.M.).
m. defectiveness, deprivation, the state of being without, want or absence (of) (e.g. of a person, loss of caste or of a limb; of a thing or quality, deprivation of some part).
m. (sg. dat. thinganas; f. thingüñᵘ̈), a delightful child, a plaything of a child, a child who charms by his or her intelligence, handsomeness, and the possession of good qualities. Cf. ṭhingun.
m. (sg. dat. ṭhinganas), a saucy boy, pretty, but too free with his tongue. Cf. thingun.
adj. (f. hīnünjᵘ̈), deprived of a limb, maimed, mutilated; (of a thing, action, or business) rendered useless by loss of a necessary part.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hīñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), to cause to be diminished.
m.inf. (1 p.p. hīñᵒrᵒ), to cause to be diminished, to cause to diminish, (e.g. money diminished by giving it away or by regular taking from a store).
m. a diamond, adamant (K. 590, 914, 921, 923); met. a very sharp intelligent boy (spoken of as such in the circle of his own relations or caste-fellows).
m. (in Hindū mythology) N. of a noted Daitya or Demon. He was twin brother of Hiranyĕkashĕph (q.v.) and was killed by Viṣṇu in his third, or boar-, incarnation (Śiv. 856, 1254).

m. (sg. dat. hiranyĕkashĕpas (in Hindū mythology) N. of a Daitya or Demon king (in Sanskrit Hiraṇyakaśipu) noted for his impiety. He had obtained a boon from Brahmā that he should not be slain by god, man, or animal. When he was illtreating his pious son Prahlāda, who was a devotee of Viṣṇu, that god appeared out of a pillar in the form of the 'Narasiṁha' (half-man, half-lion) incarnation and tore Hiraṇyakaśipu to pieces (Śiv. 857).
m. butter purified by several washings.
(? spelling and gender), N. of a certain medicinal herb, the roots of which have purgative properties, Euphorbia Thomsoniana (L. 75). A hairwash is also made from this plant (L. 74).

in hīri gaʦhun m.inf. to be reduced to poverty, esp. by the want of the means necessary for any necessary work. Prov. akhāh gōmotᵘ hīri, vīri mangān ṭang, one who has nothing seeks for pears on a willow tree (i.e. seeks for sustenance even in unlikely places). Cf. K.Pr. 7 for a variant. The opposite of this word is kīri, q.v.
(? spelling and gender), N. of a certain colour, a chocolate brown, chocolate (L. 459).
hirs حرص m. desiring eagerly, greediness, avidity, avarice, covetousness; esp. greediness for more of something previously obtained and enjoyed. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. covetousness or envy to arise.

f. (sg. abl. hēri 2, for 1, see hēr, for 3, see hyūrᵘ), a head (esp. when separated from the body) of a man, a sheep, or the like. El. (apparently incorrectly) says this word is never applied to the human head (K.Pr. 27, 197). Cf. kala-hīrᵘ̈, s.v. kala. ¶ hēri-phŏphüjᵘ̈ f. a small head, a little head, esp. the little head of a sheep or a goat separated from the body. -pröpyunᵘ m. a religious offering of a sheep's or goat's head made together with clarified butter, to the Hindū god Gạnⁱsh (Gaṇēśa) or to Brahmī and the other Mātṛkā goddesses.

m. an account, reckoning (El.; K.Pr. 82, 139, 246); computation, arithmetic; an account, bill of charges, bill (Gr.M.); the account for a good action, the reward for such (K.Pr. 75). --bōzun -- m.inf. to understand the value of anything (K.Pr. 234). -kitāb حساب کتاب m. an account with a merchant (Gr.M.). hisābukᵘ farᵃd حسابک فرد m. a bill (Gr.M.).

m. the cry made in scaring away birds (e.g. domestic fowls or sparrows). hish hish karun m.inf. to say 'hish hish' to a child, or the like, to encourage (e.g. in learning to walk, or in learning its lessons).
a jingling repetition of hishō, in hishĕm hishō (m.c. for hishĕ), all equally alike, all equally big (K.Pr. 212).

or m. similarity, likeness, resemblance (cf. hyuhᵘ) (YZ. 23). El. makes this word (spelt hishir) an adj. meaning 'convenient', but cf. the next. --karun -- m.inf. to compare (El.). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. similarity to come; a close friendship to arise amongst a number of people owing to frequent association, community of occupation, and commensality, or the like.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hishᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), to cause to resemble, to make similar to something else.

or hisa m. part, portion, lot, share, division (Ram. 815). --āmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), received as a share; met. received as one's lot in life (i.e. a husband by a wife, or a wife by a husband). --bāgay -- f. division into shares, calculation of the amount of each share. --khasun -- m.inf. the share to mount; hence, to be received as one's share. --karȧnⁱ -- m.pl.inf. to divide a number of articles into shares, to divide out a number of articles; to cut up a single thing into shares. zᵃh hissa karȧnⁱ, to divide or cut in two (Gr.M.). -nomᵘ m. a very small portion of anything (quasi, as much as can be lifted on a finger-nail). -pāsa (= حصہ پاس) m. a share of property due from another in whose possession the whole is. -rasa (= حصہ رسا، حصہ رسد) m. a share in joint family property, the amount due to each coparcener. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a shareholder, coparcener.
m. (f. hissadariñ), a shareholder; a partner in a business.

m. (sg. gen. hītas), a cause, a reason (K. 114); a groundless reason, an excuse, apology (K.Pr. 36); a pretence, evasion, feint, blind, subterfuge (K.Pr. 149, Śiv. 1458); a groundless charge, a false accusation; a method, means, as in hīth guzarānukᵘ, a means of support (Gr.M.), hīth gālanas, a means or cause of so-and-so's destruction (K. 31, 72). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. a mere and unnecessary excuse to be made (e.g. for something which was bound to occur) (Rām. 406). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to evade, sham, shuffle, make excuses (for refraining from or for doing any action). --khasun -- m.inf. a false accusation to be brought, a groundless charge to be laid (Rām. 1667). --karun -- m.inf. to make an excuse; (of something petty) to be a cause of something serious (e.g. indiscretion in diet to be the cause of sickness becoming more violent or returning). --lāgun -- m.inf. to make pretended excuses, esp. to pretend sickness, to malinger, in order to get off doing something. --ʦhādȧnⁱ -- m.pl.inf. to seek for excuses; to seek for grounds of accusation against anyone. --wuchun -- m.inf. to see excuses, to advance pretexts in order to hinder some work. ¶ hīta, adv. on account (of), for the sake (of); tamiy hīta, on that account, for that reason (Rām. 1754). sītāyĕ-handi hīta, on account of Sītā (Rām. 228). -wörᵘ̈ f. a small or slight pretext. -wörᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. a slight pretext or reason to occur (e.g. a very slight and unexpected thing to cause death, or the like). -wörᵘ̈karüñᵘ̈ f.inf., id.

f. the jasmine and its flower (El. hí; K.Pr. 248 hí, 70, 182, 190, 204, 262 híi; YZ. 258; Śiv. 168, 225, 1686; Rām. 212, 649, 651, etc.). -āsmān m. (El.) or -āsmönī f. (Rām. 1095), lilac, jasmine (El.). -āsmīn (? spelling) m. Syringa Persica (El.). ¶ hiyĕ-māl f. a jasmine garland, a garland of jasmine flowers (often used as an offering to a Hindū god) (Rām. 1025, 1090, 1571, 1581). -pōsh m. the jasmine-flower. -rang gaʦhun m.inf. the face to become yellow (like a jasmine) owing to sorrow, anxiety, sickness, or the like. -thürᵘ̈ f. the jasmine creeper (YZ. 543, Śiv. 345). -tan f. jasmine bodied, applied to a slender and graceful sweet-scented woman (Rām. 247, 378).

f. the use of words alone, verbal prohibition, prohibition by word only, forbidding. This word appears to be wrongly spelt. We should expect either hīʦᵘ̈ or hīʦh. Moreover, although reported as fem., it is masc. in the following. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. only to mention; in order to remind a person of some thing or action, to utter its name and nothing more.
m. one who is full of excuses, a pretender; evader, malingerer; one who tries to lay the blame on others.
m. happiness, rejoicing, a feeling of happiness (L.V. 73).
interj. an exclamatory pleon. suff. used in conversation, as in kyāh-hŏ, what? (H. v, 4).

interj. ho, used to male inferiors (W. 100); used to a king (Rām. 1446); lo! an expletive in poetry (Śiv. 1590, 1702, 1710, Rām. 679). -hō interj. the crooning sound made to soothe a baby; -hō karun, to croon (to a baby) (Śiv. 1379).
or hub حب m. love, affection, friendship; inclination, wish, desire. In the following idiom the word is f. --thawüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bestow affection upon a person.
f. (sg. dat. họ̆bᵃrüñᵃ), the act of conquering, defeating, overcoming, esp. in anything involving a contest, such as gambling, quarrelling, or fighting. Cf. họ̆pᵃran.
conj. 1(1 p.p. họ̆bᵃrôwᵃ), to conquer; i.q. họ̆bᵃrun. Cf. họ̆pᵃrāwun. ¶ họ̆bᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. họ̆bᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. họ̆bᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, see họ̆bᵃrun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. họ̆bᵒrᵒ), to repress, restrain, subdue, defeat, crush (by assault, abuse, or the like) some person who is vigorously contesting (e.g. in gambling, in quarrelling, or fighting). ¶ họ̆barana yunᵘ m. inf. pass. to be defeated, overcome by assault, etc., when busily engaged in any work (esp. when engaged in gambling, quarrelling, fighting, or the like). ¶ họ̆bᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. họ̆bᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), conquered, defeated, overcome as ab.
m. a mouthful of crushed up grass or other similar food taken by a herbivorous animal; a similar mouthful of spiced thick pulpy food pressed together.
m. dryness (natural or induced); hot dry weather; drought (El.).

f. disobedience, obstinacy (esp. of a child, a horse, or the like), in spite of urging. Cf. haḍ 1. In K.Pr. 28 and W. 123, the word is translated 'weeping' (huḍ). The word may be a misprint for hã̄ḍ, q.v. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show obstinacy (esp. of a child who refuses to study, or a horse that jibs, in spite of beating). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. obstinacy (generally, not specially of a boy or a horse) to be shown.

f. engagement in a difficult but objectless or useless work. Cf. họ̆dᵘ. ¶ hŏdahᵃri-bāz m. a man accustomed to engage himself in work which while troublesome and difficult is at the same time useless or purposeless.

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. hŏdahᵃriladiñ), (of a person) one who is engaged in work which is troublesome and difficult, and at the same time useless or purposeless; (of a work) troublesome, etc., as ab.
adj. c.g. a person of an angry and obstinate temperament.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. hŏḍiladiñ), one who is attacked with a fit of anger, and refuses obstinately to be placated.
conj. 2 (1 p.p. họ̆dᵘ, f. hö̆zᵘ̈), to become dry, to be wanting in relish (see họ̆dᵘ); to become dried up, withered (L.V. 25).

adj. (f. hö̆zᵘ̈), (of food) dry, wanting in gravy, oil, ghī, or the like, insipid; plain boiled rice (Gr.Gr. 27); met. (of conversation, or the like) dry, insipid, wanting in affection; (of a task or journey) useless, objectless. Kāshmīrīs eat a mouthful of rice and a mouthful of vegetables alternately. If the vegetables are exhausted first, any rice left is called họ̆dᵘ, and is not eaten (K.Pr. 82). -họ̆khᵘ adj. (f. hŏ̈zᵘ̈-hŏ̈chᵘ̈), dry and insipid, as ab. (lit. and met.). Cf. họ̆khᵘ-họ̆dᵘ (p. 327b, l. 8). ¶ hö̆zᵘ̈ har f. a causeless, objectless, quarrel.

f. a high repute (esp. of a living person). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such high repute to be spread abroad (esp. of some person not entitled to it). ¶ hōgi-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), enjoying high repute (of a person).

f. a pearl-oyster shell (Śiv. 1551, 1755; Rām. 1142); the shell of any aquatic mollusc (cf. kŏla-hö̃giñ, s.v. kŏl 2); ? a snail (L. 157, 464, hāngi). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to become an oyster-shell; met. to become excessively thin, to be wasted to a skeleton from disease, grief, etc. ¶ hö̃giñĕ-mŏkta m. a pearl from a pearl oyster (not one from an elephant's frontal bone, or any other similar object popularly counted as a pearl).

f. fish split open, cleaned, and dried in the sun; dried fish (K.Pr. 2, 244). ¶ hŏgāḍa-gorᵘ m. a fish-drier, a seller of dried fish. -ʦhᵃr m. a dish of dried fish, roasted and served with spiced sauce.

m. a father-in-law's house, i.e. the house from which a man has taken his wife (a wife's father-in-law's house, being usually her husband's house) (L. 270, huhur) (Śiv. 56, hŏhawurᵘ gara). ¶ hŏhawȧrⁱ-böʦⁱ m. the family of a man's father-in-law's house, the relatives of a man's wife. --bāy -- f. the lady of a man's father-in-law's house, i.e. the wife of a man's wife's brother, the wife of a man's brother-in-law. Cf. hahar. hŏhawaryukᵘ adj. (f. hŏhawaricᵘ̈), of or belonging to a man's father-in-law's house.
adv. (occurring) suddenly over and over again, u.w. vbs. signifying00 possession by a demon, an attack of fainting, raving, or the like.
f. (sg. dat. hŏjüʦᵘ̈), argument, plea, allegation; proof, reason; objection, pretext, excuse; a voucher; a document acknowledging debt, an I.O.U.; a bond (Gr.M.).
m. a pilgrim (to Mecca); one who has performed the Mecca pilgrimage (El.); often used as a title, e.g. K.Pr. 74, 108.
see hāl 2, gölⁱ-höjⁱ, s.v. gölᵘ̈, hĕkan- höjᵘ̈, s.v. hĕkun, etc.

m. the flickering light or flashes of summer lightning (without thunder). -bāwun gaʦhun m.inf. to become summer lightning; met. to appear and immediately disappear, to come into existence and immediately be destroyed (of a thing, an action, an occupation, or any condition of the mind, such as joy, sorrow, etc.).
m. the hookah or pipe and its apparatus, by which tobacco is smoked through water.

f. (sg.dat. hö̃kali), a chain (YZ. 280); esp. a door-chain, or similar chain for fastening up a chest or the like; a chain for measuring land (mēnan-hö̃kal, El.). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to apply the chain, to fasten up a door or a chest with a chain. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the door-chain to be applied; met. one's whole family and relations to be destroyed (as if the house were perpetually shut up). ¶ hö̃kali-hār m. 'the cowry in the chain'; N. of an ancient game, in which cowries are thrown in a chain round a board with 64 squares. -pôwᵘ m. the staple on the opposite leaf of a door to which a chain is fastened when the door is chained up.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hö̃kalôwᵘ), to cause to shrink up through cold, esp. of food cooled to a jelly or the like. hö̃kalôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hö̃kalöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), to cause to be shrunken by cold.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. hö̃kalyōv), to shrink on account of cold (of the body, or of soft warm food, etc., that cools to a jelly). ¶ hö̃kalyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hö̃kalyē-müʦᵘ̈), shrunken or shrivelled up by cold.

m. failure to accomplish something which seemed to be on the point of completion, and which thereby puts to shame the person failing. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. shame at complete and sudden unsuccess to be felt by one apparently on the point of success. --karun -- m.inf. to put a person to shame by failing, when the time comes, to give promised assistance which is necessary for success. -thörᵘ̈ f. unsuccess-hurry, i.e. needless haste or flurry in doing anything.

for họ̆khᵘ in the following:-- -dorᵘ m. the season of dry roads, dry weather, the dry season. -hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), a bundle of dried cabbage leaves for cooking. Cf. hāka-ʦar, s.v. hākh 1. -syunᵘ m. dried vegetables, cabbages, potatoes, egg-plants, gourds, etc., and their leaves, cut up into pieces and dried in the autumn sun, for use as a relish or for making stews, etc., in winter. -tǖrᵘ̈ f. dry cold, i.e. severe cold in winter, which precedes rain, and which is relieved by rain falling. -tāv m. burning up of crops owing to want of rain; fever owing to supposed drying up of the bodily juices; roasting or frying meat or other food without grease. -tövᵘ̈ f., id. -zᵃl adj. (f. -zᵘ̈jᵘ̈), a scratcher of dry things; a niggardly miser, who although wealthy will not spend money even on necessaries.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. hŏkhanôwᵘ), to cause to be dry or dry up, to parch; to cause to wither, to cause to shrivel up. Cf. họ̆khᵃrāwun and Gr.Gr. 174. ¶ hŏkhanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hŏkhanöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), dried up (by some one), caused (by some one) to become dry.

m. the condition of being dried up and withered (of crops, owing to drought). --aʦun -- m.inf. such withering to begin; met. (of the body of a living being) gradually to become withered and lean. --karun -- m.inf. (of paddy crops or the like) to become dried up and withered owing to drought.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hŏkhowᵘ), to make dry, to dry (of damp grain, clothes, etc., spread out in the sun or elsewhere to dry). hŏkhowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (hŏkhüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), dried as ab.

f. the dry season, the time of the year preceding the winter (which is snowy and wet), approximately the autumn (Gr.Gr. 128). ¶ hŏkhayĕ-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, belonging to, produced, or gathered together in this dry season.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. họ̆khᵘ; 2 p.p. hŏchyōv), to dry, dry up, become dry (K.Pr. 9, YZ. 396); to be dry, parched; to wither, pine away, shrivel up (YZ. 180). ¶ The causal of this verb is hŏkhanāwun or họ̆khᵃrāwun (Gr.Gr. 174). ¶ họ̆khᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hö̆chᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), dried up, etc. (K.Pr. 103). ¶ hŏkhith gaʦhun m.inf. to dry up, become dry (K.Pr. 251).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. họ̆khᵃrôwᵃ), to make dry, to dry up; to cause to wither (Śiv. 128); esp. met. to torment a person by stopping him (e.g. by preventing a hungry person from eating, or obstructing one commencing or engaged in important work). ¶ họ̆khᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. họ̆chᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), obstructed, impeded (by some one), as ab.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. họ̆khᵒrᵒ), i.q. họ̆khᵃrāwun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. lxxxiv).

adj. (f. hö̆chᵘ̈), dry (K.Pr. 114); dried; dried up (H. vi, 15; K. 588); parched; sapless, juiceless; without advantage or profit; dry, wanting in affection (of profane learning) (Śiv. 992, 1650). --gāsa-- m. straw (El. hauk-gás). -họ̆dᵘ adj. (f. hŏ̈chᵘ̈-hŏ̈zᵘ̈), dry, plain (as bread, food); simple, unseasoned, unsavoury, insipid. Cf. họ̆dᵘ-họ̆khᵘ (p. 323a, l. 8). -họ̆khᵘ m. dry, without its gravy (of food); dried, of clotted or clammy articles stuck together, which have been dried so as to permit of their easy separation.

m. a ruler, a governor, an official, officer; a judge (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 74, 137; W. 143; L. 335). -i alā حآکم علا m. the chief ruler, the governor of a city (Gr.M.); esp. a certain official, the Governor of Kashmīr (L. 401).

f., i.q. hail, q.v. skill acquired by practice. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such skill to come, to become expert. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make a person skilful by continual practice; to give a person a habit.
m. a farm labourer, an agricultural servant, i.q. hölⁱ, q.v.

m. want of success in gaining what one has long desired (Śiv. 804); trouble (El. hól, i.e. hôlᵘ); despair, hopelessness (Rām. 1024, 1041, 1499, 1576, 1638). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. the extreme despair caused by such want of success to occur, to be reduced to the point of death by such despair (YZ. 531).

adj. (f. hüjᵘ̈), crooked, bent, distorted, awry, oblique, askew (L.V. 108; K.Pr. 34, 75, 155; Śiv. 1018; Rām. 634, 1068, 1207, 1293, 1457); curved (YZ. 476); deformed, humpbacked, bow-legged, etc. (W. 123); offended, displeased, of a cranky nature; out of the perpendicular, oblique; flexible (El. hul); crooked (morally) (K.Pr. 83). -holᵘ adv. crookedly, awry, esp. u.w. vbs. of coming, going, looking, etc. (K.Pr. 188, W. 139); as adj., intricate (El.). -kolᵘ adj. (f. hüjᵘ̈-küjᵘ̈), spoiled by crookedness, or by becoming bent, etc., usually of inan. objects (Gr.Gr. 95). ¶ hȧlⁱ-pöṭhⁱ adv. crookedly (Gr.Gr. 153).

m. either side of the waist, the floating ribs in that locality, the flank (El. hul). --ganḍun -- m.inf. to gird up the loins (Rām. 1462). -wolᵘ m. a jingling compound signifying 'girdles and the like' (Gr.Gr. 95). ¶ hȧlⁱ-dôdⁱ m. pain (such as rheumatism) in the locality of floating ribs, pleurodynia. -ganḍun or hali-ganḍun m. (sg. dat. -ganḍanas), a waistband, cummerbund (El.). -köñᵘ̈ f. the floating ribs at the waist. -lāṭh m. (sg. dat. -lāṭas), a kind of fringed waistband of silk or other coloured material, a girdle worn by women (El. hiláṭ).
m. a ploughman, an agricultural labourer, a farm-servant. -bāy f. his wife. -koṭᵘ m. (f. -küṭᵘ̈), his son or daughter (e.g. so and so's ploughman's son).
f. the work of a ploughman or farm labourer, usually paid by giving him a fourth share of the produce. See hölⁱ.
f. the share of a crop paid to a farm labourer as his wages.
f. (sg. dat. họ̆mᵃrüñᵃ), cooling, esp. cooling of pride, anger, etc., by disgrace, forcible action, or the like.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. họ̆mᵃrôwᵃ), to appease, cool, assuage (one's own or another's anger, pride, fever, etc.), esp. when done by force or by putting to disgrace. Cf. hamun, hạmᵃrun, and họ̆mᵃran. họ̆mᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. họ̆mᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), appeased, cooled, assuaged (of anger, etc., as ab.); appeased, etc. (of a person under the influence of anger, etc.).

hunar ھنر f. excellence in any art; art, skill (K.Pr. 60, 150); attainment, accomplishment (Rām. 128); ingenuity, cleverness; knowledge, science; virtue, merit. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. skill or accomplishment to be acquired. ¶ hŏnari bĕhun m.inf. to practice skilfully an art or profession, to exhibit skill in one's work.
adj. c.g. skilful, clever, ingenious (Gr.M., Rām. 128).

adj. (f.hünzᵘ̈), the postposition of the genitive case, governing the dative; used with all feminine and all plural nouns, and also with animate nouns in the m.sg. In the last case, the final s of the preceding dat. sg. causes the initial h of the hondᵘ to be elided, so that the postposition apparently becomes sondᵘ, as in ʦūra-sondᵘ, of a thief, for ʦūras-hondᵘ, mölⁱ-sondⁱ, of a father, for mölis-hondᵘ. This postposition is occasionally used with adverbs, as in yuri-hondᵘ wŏla, come (to the direction) of here, come hither (H. v. 5).
m. a ram, esp. a large fat one (LV. 77; K.Pr. 82, 158).

f. (sg. dat. hŏnjĕ), a bill of exchange, money-order, draft, cheque. ¶ hŏnjĕ-gāsa khyonᵘ m.inf. to eat the grass of a money-order; hence, to live or support oneself on one's own earnings. -way f. the commission on bill of exchange, money-order, or the like.
m. extreme coldness of a liquid (such as water, milk, etc.), the state of being frozen hard (cf. hạndurᵘ).
m. in hȧnḍⁱ-pākh m. (sg. dat. -pākas), cooking tough food or the like for a long time, so as to make it tender and digestible.
f. (sg. dat. hŏnjĕ), the name given to the character, or non-initial ē. Cf. hŏnjōr.

f. N. of the root of a certain wild creeper, said to be very poisonous, but used medicinally for the relief of fistula, ulcers, and similar diseases; met. looking upon all food and occupation as deadly poison, disease accompanied by inertia and total loss of appetite. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such inertia and loss of appetite suddenly to occur. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such loss of appetite, etc., to come on owing to agitation of mind, indigestion, or other disease.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. hŏngaladiñ), a person suddenly afflicted with intense inertia and loss of appetite. See hŏnga.
f. the chin; esp. the prominence below the semi-circular crease below the under lips (K. 428).
m. the chin, i.q. hŏngañ, q.v.
m. a mountain peak (cf. tọ̆ngᵘ) (El. thung); a tower, minaret (El. thong); a leading man, honoured and respected, among his fellows (cf. thonᵘ 2).
f. or hŏnja-horᵘ m. the N. of the character of the diphthong ai, when non-initial. Cf. hö̆nḍᵘ̈ 2.
f. (sg. dat. hŏnjĕ), the chin, poet. for hŏngañ (q.v.) (YZ. 72, 447).
(? spelling) m. a certain bird, the Spatula clypeata, or Shoveller. It is a kind of duck, with a large spoon-shaped bill. The male has very handsome plumage (L. 128).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. hōnyōv), to be arrogant, intoxicated, maddened (by drugs, access of wealth, anger, delusion, possession by an evil spirit, etc.). ¶ hōnyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hōnyē-müʦᵘ̈), intoxicated, etc., as ab.

m. a gusset on each side of a garment under the sleeves (Śiv. 1597). ¶ hōnza-püṭᵘ̈ f. a gusset- cloth, the piece of cloth cut ready for sewing in as such a gusset. -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -waṭas), joining up a number of pieces of cloth to form a gusset-cloth.
f. the occupation or livelihood of a boatman; met. vile conduct distinguished by shamelessness, disrespect, lawlessness, and foul language.

m. (sg. dat. hönzᵘ̈s or hānzas (Gr.Gr. 55). The f. of this word is hānzañ or hānzĕñ, which signifies a boatman's wife), a boatman (see El., s.v. hánz) (K.Pr. 63, 76; H. i, 4). -bāpār m. conduct of a boatman. The boatmen of Kashmīr have a very bad reputation for morality; hence, conduct like that of a boatman, conduct distinguished by shamelessness, disrespect, lawlessness, and foul and abusive language. -gönzᵘ̈ m. a jingling compound signifying 'boatmen, etc.' (Gr.Gr. 95). -har f. boatmen's quarrelling, quarrelling like that between boatmen, distinguished by disrespect, shamelessness, and foul-mouthed abuse.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. höñᵉ̆ladiñ), marred by the loss of something (e.g. a person by loss of reputation or of a limb, a work or thing by breakage or loss of some essential element).
f. (sg. dat. höñᵉ̆rüñᵉ̆), the act of causing loss; causing diminution of anything (by taking away a portion); causing disgrace to (a respected person), showing disrespect to, putting to public shame.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. höñᵉrôwᵉ), to cause loss, to mar by causing loss; (of a person) to disgrace. höñᵉrôwᵉ-motᵉ perf. part. (f. höñᵉröwᵉ-müʦᵉ), marred by diminution; disgraced (by abuse, etc.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. höñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), (of hot food) to make cold, to allow to get too cold. höñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. höñᵉ̆röwᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), (of food) allowed to get too cold, etc.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. höñᵒrᵒ), (of hot eatables) to make cold, to allow to get cold; (of a person) to displease, disappoint. höñᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. höñᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of hot food) cooled, made cold, allowed to get too cold; (of a person) displeased, disappointed.
m. a man of harsh or churlish disposition, ever envious of others' success, a churl. Cf. hᵒnᵒ.
m. the presiding deity of a sacred spot (see thāna); N. of a village and sacred spot on the pilgrim route to Amarêśvara in Kashmīr.

adj. c.g. possessing puffed out cheeks. -dĕgulᵘ or hapa-dĕgulᵘ adj. (f. -dĕgüjᵘ̈), having cheeks puffed out and globular like a cooking pot (see dĕgulᵘ); ugly and swollen-jowled. -lyolᵘ adj. (f. -lë̆jᵘ̈), id.
(? spelling), a certain wild food-plant, Dipsacus inermis (L. 72).
m. (sg. dat. höphas), an exclamation of regret; as interj. Ah! alas! what a pity! it is of no value! (K.Pr. 118).

m. a keeper, guardian, protector; the Preserver of all things (a name of the Deity); one who has the whole Qŏr'ān by heart; a blind man (so-called because such commonly know the Qŏr'ān by heart). (Cf. ölⁱ-höphiz).
f. a courtesan, prostitute, dancing girl, nautch-girl. ¶ höphiza-nagma m. a nautch, a dance by a nautch-girl accompanied by a chorus of singers and instrumental music.
f. (sg. dat. họ̆pᵃrüñᵃ), defeat, being overcome (by violence, abuse, or the like) (of a person vigorously engaged in any work). Cf. họ̆bᵃran.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. họ̆pᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. họ̆pᵃrun. Cf. họ̆bᵃrāwun. họ̆pᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. họ̆pᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. họ̆pᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, see họ̆pᵃrun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. họ̆pᵒrᵒ), to defeat, overcome (by violence, abuse, or the like) any person vigorously engaged in any work. Cf. họ̆bᵃrun. ¶ họ̆pᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. họ̆pᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), defeated, overcome, as ab.
m. swelling of the cheeks, a puffing out of the cheeks (from anger, etc.).

adv. there (within sight) (Gr.Gr. 155); thither (El., W. 94). -kun adv. in that direction (Gr.Gr. 160). ¶ hōra adv. thence, from that place (within sight) (Gr.Gr. 156, W. 94). -kani adv., id. (Gr.Gr. 159).

f. an agreement, contract, bargain; used in the following:-- hōra-bürᵘ̈ f. lit. (?) a fissure in a bargain (cf. bürᵘ̈); undoing a bargain, etc., by repaying a debt immediately after it has been incurred, undoing a work immediately after it has been accomplished, or the like.
f. presents made by a host to a visitor on his departure, for him and for his relations and friends--the bidāygī of India.
m. beating, fighting, in hŏrdus ta bŏrdus, a hullabaloo (K.Pr. 85), lit. beating and smiting.
m. an amount to be repaid, the principal of a debt (K.Pr. 238).

m. N. of a district near the city of Śrīnagar, at the southern extremity of the Hāra-parbuth (see hār 2) where there is a rock worshipped from ancient times as an embodiment of the Hindū god Gȧnⁱsh or Haridrā-Gaṇēśa (see RT.Tr. II, 446).

f. N. of a goddess, in Sanskrit Śārikā, a form of Durgā. Her shrine is on the N.W. side of the Hāra-parbuth hill (see hār 2). Durgā is said to have taken the form of a Śārikā bird (see hörᵘ̈ 1 and Śiv. 1046, 1782) and to have carried the hill to its present position in order to close the gates of hell. See RT.Tr. I, 101 n. and II, 446 (Śiv. 1500).
f. a general name for the crops that ripen in the month of Hār (see hār 1), mostly pulses.

höricᵘ̈ (Rām. 109) or hörinjᵘ̈ (Rām. 344) f. a bow (El. hārij and hārinj); tīr-i höricᵘ̈ tīr-i hörinjᵘ̈ (Rām. 109), (Rām. 344), an arrow with a crescent-shaped head. ¶ hörinjĕ-gāsa m. N. of a kind of grass (Rām. 1298).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. hūrᵘ), to repay a loan, repay a debt (K.Pr. 187), return a thing lent, pay or return for something (K.Pr. 106); met. to return evil for good; drüʦᵘ̈ hōrañĕ f.pl. inf. to repay childish diseases, to get over such diseases (Rām. 1587). Cf. hōrun nakha wālun (L. 459), p. 1115a, l. 10 ¶ hōran-pāṭhi m. a loan which is continually borne in mind as necessary to be repaid; a benefit which the recipient feels must be repaid by a benefit. ¶ hūrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hūrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of a debt or other obligation) repaid; (of some pain or transaction which has to be undergone) undergone and done with.
adj. (f. hörᵘ̈ 2), speckled, dappled, brindled, mottled, piebald (i.e. with light markings on a dark ground or vice versa) (K.Pr. 82). Cf. hār 4 and ḍaba-hôrᵘ.
m. a pair, two of anything (usually of inanimate things, Gr.Gr. 81); often --˚, as in ạlᵃka-horᵃ, a pair of earrings (see ạlᵃka); pula- horᵘ, a pair of sandals; wölⁱ-horⁱ, a pair of rings (see wôlᵘ).

f. (for 2, see hôrᵘ. The word may also be 1 p.p. f. of hārun), N. of a kind of mainā or starling (Sanskrit śārikā, see hörī 2), gracula. Cf. hörī 2 (K.Pr. 77, 78; Mainā-Coracias Indica, W. 13; Śiv. 962, 1046, 1362, 1365, 1782; Rām. 4, 95, 1102). ¶ hāri-baca m. a starling-fledgling; a small starling.

m. N. of a village about 2 1/2 miles N.W. of the gardens of Shālimār, near Śrīnagar, probably the site of the ancient Saḍarhatvana (RT.Tr. I, 173; II, 455). The intake of the Śrīnagar waterworks is now at this village.
m. incomplete, and hence unsuccessful, result of some laborious or lengthy work.

m. understanding, judgment, intellect (Śiv. 237, 491, 1028, 1032, 1061, 1809, 1848); sense, discretion (YZ. 204, 219; Śiv. 1270, 1365, 1590, 1690, 1800; H. i, 5; Rām. 1043); mind, soul; remembrance or coming into mind of something previously experienced or known (Śiv. 343, 844, 1055); knowledge of a science or art gained by practice; movement of the limbs as a sign of a person coming to after a faint, or the like (Rām. 873). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. intelligence or comprehension to come (to a child, or the like, as the result of education). --karun -- m.inf. to consider, think (Rām. 354); to be sensible, have sense, not to be a fool (Rām. 329); to take heed (Rām. 818, 1506). --nyunᵘ -- m.inf. to take the senses, destroy a person's presence of mind, render distraught (Rām. 1626). --rōzun -- m.inf. memory to remain; hence, to bear in mind, keep in memory something which one has not practised for a long time (Śiv. 935, rūdum-na hōsh, I did not bear in mind); to remain sensible, keep one's senses (Rām. 533, rūdus na hōsh, he became insensible); one's presence of mind to remain (Rām. 1392, 1459, rōzān na kē̃h hōsh, he entirely loses his presence of mind; so Rām. 1520). --thawun -- m.inf. to bear in mind; to guard carefully and attentively something committed to one's charge. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. memory or intelligence to come (to someone who is mistaken or a fool); (of a person in a faint, or the like) to show signs of life by movements of the limbs. ¶ hōshĕ-kinⁱ adv. attentively, with care and attention, with one's senses alert (Rām. 1286). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without understanding; unwary, foolish; deprived of sense or consciousness, unconscious, in a faint; intoxicated, stupified; (= bē-hōsh, q.v.). hōshĕ-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), experienced, learned (e.g. in book learning, or in experience, or in some science or art) (Śiv. 1029). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come into remembering; to gain knowledge or call to mind (by study, practice, thinking over, or the like) some mode of action, science or art, esp. when previously known and forgotten (Śiv. 189). ¶ hōshĕs pyonᵘ m.inf. to fall into memory, to call some forgotten thing to mind after long thought (K. 224). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come to one's senses (after a faint, agitation, or the like) (Rām. 1733).
(cf. حاشیہ) m. a braid or flowered embroidery used for putting along the edges of a cloth, etc.
adj. c.g. embroidered (of the edges of a cloth).

hushⁱyār (Śiv. 1485, 1866), hushyār or husyār (Śiv. 1710) adj. c.g. intelligent, prudent; acquainted; well-informed; sensible, knowing; mindful, cautious, alert, watchful, vigilant, on one's guard; awake, conscious, in one's senses (Śiv. 1866). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become intelligent, to become sensible; to arrive at the age of puberty; to become conscious, to come to one's senses; to awake from sleep (W. 87, Śiv. 1710, H. v, 5); of something previously unknown, knowledge to be gained, memory of some forgotten thing to come. --karun -- m.inf. to apprize, make acquainted; to render a person cautious or vigilant, to put him on his guard (against), to warn; to rouse, awake a person from sleep; to remind. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain (or be) careful (in respect of), to be on (one's) guard (against), to be vigilant (Śiv. 1485); to keep watch, to look out; be on the alert (K.Pr. 46).

f. (K.Pr. 56), product, produce, outcome (K.Pr. 56, YZ. 157, Rām. 20); profit, gain, good (El., Rām. 26, 802). bē-hösil, adj. c.g. fruitless, profitless (Rām. 15). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a product to result, as in shẹ̆sᵃtaras sŏn gaʦhiy hösil, for iron gold will result to thee as a product, i.e. your iron will be turned into gold (L.V. 100, K.Pr. 46). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to obtain, reap a result (K.Pr. 30).
m. the thirteenth of the twenty-seven lunar mansions or lunar asterisms, in Sanskrit hasta, said to be shaped like a hand, and to be part of the constellation Corvus.

m. (in composition this word sometimes takes the form hȧsⁱ. The f. is hastiñ or hȧsⁱtiñ, q.v.), an elephant (L.V. 24, 47; K.Pr. 3, 69, 80, 150, 190, 218; YZ. 124, 481; Śiv. 353, 751, 894, 967, 1562; H. vi, 16, 17; Rām. 1269; K. 29, etc.). ¶ hȧsⁱ-gan m. an elephant's ear; N. of a sacred spot called in Sanskrit Hastikarṇa, about 36 miles S.E. of Śrīnagar; Cf. RT.Tr. v, 23, and II, 461. -hö̃kal f. a chain used as an elephant's shackle. -hö̃kal gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. an elephant's shackle to occur; met. a powerful person to find himself stopped by some impediment. -khēl f. a troop of elephants (e.g. wild in the forest). -kara m. an elephant's trunk. -yüḍᵘ̈ gāsa-gë˘ḍᵘ̈ f. for an elephant's belly, a wisp of grass; hence, when very much is required of anything for any purpose, very little to be received, a drop in the ocean. ¶ hȧstⁱ-ambörⁱ f. an elephant-litter, see ambörⁱ; N. of a children's game, in which one child poses as an elephant, and the other mounts him (K. 221). -baca m. a baby elephant, i.e. one about a year old. -bürᵘ̈ f. an elephant-trap, a concealed pit for catching wild elephants. -dö̃th m. (sg. dat. dö̃tas), an elephant's tusk, ivory. -höjⁱ or -höjᵘ̈ f. an elephant stable. -hāl f. (sg. dat. -höjᵘ̈), id. -wôlᵘ m. an elephant keeper, an elephant groom, an elephant driver, a Mahāwat (K. 431).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. hö̃ṭhyōv), to be fruitless, barren, lit. and met. hö̃ṭhyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hö̃ṭhyē-müʦᵘ̈), become fruitless.
f. (sg. dat. hö̃ṭhᵃrüñᵘ̈), causing to be fruitless, rendering fruitless, lit. and fig.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. hö̃ṭhᵃrôwᵃ), to make fruitless, render fruitless (esp. something of which the fruit is expected to come quickly), lit. and fig. hö̃ṭhᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. hö̃ṭhᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), rendered fruitless, as ab.
f. barren (of a woman, cow, or other female animal) (El. hönṭ) (K.Pr. 65, 76, 99). Cf. kāwa-hö̃ṭhᵘ̈, s.v. kāv 1.

1 p.p. of hŏʦun (f. hö̆ʦᵘ̈), gone bad, decayed, tainted (Gr.Gr. 212; K.Pr. 12, 177, 247). Cf. aḍa-họ̆tᵘ, p. 11a, l. 30. ¶ hŏʦa-bata m. boiled rice steeped in water for several days, then strained and fried in oil. It is eaten with spices such as pepper and cloves.

adj. (f. hüʦᵘ̈), struck; used --˚ as a sec. suff. meaning 'affected by' (Gr.Gr. 136). Thus, āra-hotᵘ, afflicted by pity, pitiful; bŏchi-hotᵘ, smitten by hunger, starving (YZ. 410); nẹ̆ndᵃri- hotᵘ, sunk in sleep (L.V. 32; YZ. 47; Śiv. 998, 1661, 1865); guma-hotᵘ, sweaty; lawa-hotᵘ, dewy; prayĕma-hotᵘ, overcome by affection (Śiv. 1666); tāpa-hotᵘ (Śiv. 1813) or tāwa-hotᵘ, warm, hot; trēshi-hotᵘ, thirsty (YZ. 406, 411; Śiv. 1585); ʦakhi-hotᵘ, full of rage (H. vii, 14).

m. the throat (K.Pr. 81, 155, 194, 250; YZ. 54, 374; Śiv. 169, 360, 504, 792, 812, 1040, 1436, 1877; H. viii, 1; Rām. 974, 1041-2, 1122, 1489; K. 309). --ʦaṭun -- m.inf. to cut a person's throat (H. v, 7). ¶ hȧṭⁱ-ganḍ m. a knot in the throat; hence, inability to eat proffered food (owing to fear, sorrow, delusion, or the like); tying up the neck or mouth of bag or sack filled with articles; tying up the mouth of a filled jar. -grindam m. a disease of the throat in which the air passages are obstructed by phlegm, (?) bronchitis. -grindam dyunᵘ m.inf. to throttle, to compress the throat by a noose or by the hands. -shrūʦᵘ̈ f. 'throat clean', a bride with ornaments on her neck. -vĕsorᵘ m. throat deranged, a disease of the throat accompanied by internal swellings. -vesorᵘ pyonᵘ m.inf. such a disease of the throat to occur. -wothᵘ adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), throat-descended; hence, nearly full to the throat (of a jar, etc.); meeting with approbation (of something selected and approved out of a number of things). Cf. haṭi wasun, bel. ¶ haṭi gaʦhun m.inf. to happen or come into existence in the throat; hence, a promise to be made (K.Pr. 81). -pholᵘ m. the bead necklace ordinarily worn by Kāshmīrī women, composed of strung pearls, gold, coral, or the like, or (when these are not available) of a single bead on a string. -pholᵘ ganḍun m.inf. to tie on the necklace; (among women) met. to put on a necklace as a sign that mourning for a dead person is over, to go out of mourning. -pholᵘ ʦaṭun m.inf. to cut the necklace; (of women) met. to put off one's ornaments as a token of grief; (of men or women) to go into mourning. -pholᵘ ʦaṭith bĕhun m.inf. to be in mourning, as ab.; met. to give up one's occupation (as if one were suffering great grief and could not do one's work). --wālun -- m.inf. to cause to descend from the throat, to swallow something difficult to swallow (e.g. owing to its size or shape, or owing to disease of the throat); met. to cause to go down the throat, to induce a person to swallow a thing, to make him like and accept something, even if he disliked before. --wasun -- m.inf. to go down from the throat, to be swallowed down (of something for any reason difficult to swallow); met. to meet with approval (of something selected and approved out of a number of things); cf. hȧṭⁱ wothᵘ, ab. -wasth m. (sg. dat. -wastas), any neck ornament of the necklace kind. --wothᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --wüʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), (of something for any cause difficult to swallow) swallowed down; approved of and selected (out of a number of things). Cf. hȧṭⁱ-wothⁱ, ab.
hoṭhᵘ m. (?) a shore (El. hauṭ, hauṭh, where it is probably a misprint for bauṭh, i.e. boṭhᵘ 1).

m. the house of a man's father-in-law, i.e. of his wife's father (K.Pr. 29). ¶ hōwᵃ̇rᵃ̇-böʦᵃ̇ m. the inhabitants of a man's father-in-law's house, a man's wife's father's relations. -bāy f. the lady of a father-in-law's house, the wife of a man's brother-in-law.
adj. (f. höwᵘ̈), evident, clear. The only authority for this word is El., who spells it hó,ú. It seems to be the 1 p.p. of hāwun, q.v., used as an adj.
m. a reservoir, cistern, pond, pool, tank, vat, trough, basin of a fountain.
m. a large vessel or cistern for collecting water (usually of metal).

m. (of food) dryness, want of gravy, oil, ghī, or the like, insipidity; (of conversation, etc.) dryness, insipidity, want of affection; (of a task, journey, or the like) uselessness, want of object. Cf. họ̆dᵘ.
adj. c.g. present in attendance, at hand (K.Pr. 81, Śiv. 696); in attendance (in a court, or the like) (Gr.M., Śiv. 676).
f. attendance (in a court of justice, etc.) (Gr.M., Śiv. 698).
hŏʦⁱ, hö̆ʦᵘ̈, see họ̆tᵘ and hŏtun.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. hō̃ʦaladiñ), one who is subject to ceremonial impurity; that, contact with which renders one ceremonially impure, or (met.) injures one's reputation. See hō̃ʦh.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hŏʦanôwᵘ), i.q. họ̆ʦᵃrun and họ̆ʦᵃrāwun, qq.v. (Gr.Gr. 174).

m. (sg. dat. hō̃ʦas), (among Hindūs) ceremonial impurity (owing to a birth, death, or the like); pollution arising from contact with some impure object; (met.) ill-repute arising from contact with something. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat impurity; to become or be ceremonially impure, as ab. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. such ceremonial impurity to befall. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. ceremonial impurity to come; met. (among thieves, etc.) to become an object of suspicion to one's comrades. ¶ hō̃ʦa-bāpār m. the business of providing and cooking food for one who is ceremonially impure (as they have to eat apart). -shọ̆dᵘ adj. (f. -shö̆zᵘ̈), pure from impurity, one who has passed through a period of ceremonial impurity and is now pure; (of food) not ceremonially impure, not to be eaten by one who is ceremonially impure.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. họ̆tᵘ; 2 p.p. hŏʦōv), to go bad, rot, decay (esp. of food, or the like). The causal of this verb is hŏʦanāwun or họ̆ʦᵃrāwun (Gr.Gr. 174). --aʦun -- m.inf. (of food, fruit, etc.) to begin to decay, to show signs of turning bad; met. (of friendship or similar relation) to begin to turn into enmity. --yunᵘ -- m.inf., id. ¶ hŏʦⁱ hŏʦⁱmarun m.inf. decaying and decaying to die; to die a lingering and painful death (esp. used in invoking an evil fate on an enemy). ¶ họ̆tᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. hö̆ʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), decayed, gone bad.
f. (sg. dat. họ̆ʦᵃrüñᵃ), (of food, fruit, etc.) the act of causing to decay or to go bad.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. họ̆ʦᵃrôwᵃ), to cause to decay, i.q. họ̆ʦᵃrun. Cf. Gr.Gr. 174.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. họ̆ʦᵒrᵒ), (of food, fruit, etc.) to cause to decay or go bad, i.q. họ̆ʦᵃrāwun.
m. the wrist, the forearm (H. xii, 12, 15).
m. a kind of small mould used by goldsmiths, into which gold is hammered so as to shape it into a boss or other ornament.
m. he who dwells in the heart, God, the conscience as a form of God (Śiv. 270).

m. bubbles, ebullition, of boiling water, food, etc.; met. a condition of bubbling over with self-conceit; bubbling over with talk, unrestrained flow of language (esp. of some sage or the like pouring forth words of wisdom).
f. (sg. dat. huzᵘ̈), a long mine or hollow passage dug in the ground, a wall, or the like. ¶ huda-gulᵘ (? spelling), m. a tunnel (L. 464).
in huda-hudañĕy, apparently the f. sg. dat. or pl. nom. of the sg. gen. of huda-huda, a word of unknown meaning in L.V. 84.
f. an open seat placed on an elephant's back, a howdah.

dem. that (within sight), this (at some distance, but within sight); both subst. and adj. It may be either an. or inan., and the an. forms are sometimes m., sometimes f., and sometimes c.g.
