Sing. nom. an. m. huh; f. hŏh; inan. huh; dat. an. c.g. humis; inan. huth; gen. an. c.g. humⁱ-sondⁱ, or husondᵘ; inan. humyukᵘ; ag. an. m. humⁱ; f. humi; inan. humⁱ; abl. an. c.g. and inan. humi, or huwa; pl. nom. an. and inan. m. hum; f. huma; dat. an. and inan. human; gen. an. and inan. human-hondᵘ, or huhondᵘ; ag. an. and inan. humau. ¶ It will be observed that in the pl. there is no distinction between an. and inan., and that gender is only distinguished in the nom. ¶ When used as an adjective, the only inan. form used is the dat. sg. huth, as in huth gāmas, to that village (Gr.M.). In other cases the animate forms only are used, agreeing in gender with the qualified noun, but in this case the f. sg. dat. is humi, not humis. Thus humis hūnis, to that dog (m.), but humi hōñĕ, to that bitch. ¶ When the adj. pronoun is in agreement with a noun in the gen. case the usual rule for adjectives is followed. When the word qualified is the genitive of a m. sg. an. noun, the pronoun is put in the dat. as in humis hūnⁱ-sondⁱ of that dog. If the noun is m. inan. sg., the pron. is put in the abl., as in humi gāmukᵘ, of that village. If the noun is f., either an. or inan., the pron. is put in the f.dat. (see ab.), as in humi hōñĕ-hondᵘ, of that bitch; humi jāyĕ-hondᵘ, of that place. If the noun is plur., m. or f., an. or inan., the pron. is put in the dat. pl., as in human hōnĕn-hondᵘ, of those dogs; human hōñĕn-hondᵘ, of those bitches; human gāman- hondᵘ, of those villages. ¶ For the dat. sg. and subsequent cases, the various forms of the pron. ath are commonly used for huth, etc. See ath 1. ¶ It will be noted that this pronoun can only be used for things within sight of the speaker, or for things referred to as close by. For things not in sight or not close by, tih must be used. ¶ huti 2 c.g. (for 1, see hutⁱ) emph., that very person or thing within sight; that person or thing within sight also. ¶ huth-kun adv. in that direction, thither (Gr.Gr. 160). ¶ huthy-kun adv. emph. even in that direction, in that very direction.
m. pain derived from piercingly cold wind, chill. Cf. hạdᵘ̈rᵘ̈. Used in the following: --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such pain to occur. --mēlun -- m.inf. to be chilled to the bone.
m. a chamber, room, closet, cell; a hut (Rām. 1549).
see holᵘ 1. This word is spelt haj in K.Pr. 34 and YZ. 476.
? gend. only noted in mai trāv hukai (K.Pr. 207), translated 'do not step so haughtily'.

hukum m. judgment, judicial decree, sentence, verdict; an order, command (Rām. 794, 1185, 1688, 1702, 1742, 1752). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to command, give an order (El.; W. 187; H. ii, 7; viii, 4; x, 5). --karun -- m.inf. to convict, sentence, condemn (El.); to decide (El.); to command (El., Rām. 1186). --mānun -- m.inf. to obey an order (Gr.M.). --phuṭᵃrun -- m.inf. to break an order (Rām. 1753). --tulanwôlᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --tulanwājeñ --), one who obeys, obedient.
f. rule, sway, sovereignty. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to rule (Rām. 1137, 1737).
m. the sound made in driving away kites or other birds of prey (K.Pr. 147).
(? spelling), m. a girdle (El.). Cf. holᵘ 2.
in hul haji (? spelling), a certain cattle disease, pox. The native remedy for this is slitting the ears (L. 459) (? holᵘ-hüjᵘ).

f. the festival known in India as the hōlī, the great spring festival of the Hindūs, held on the 8th of the light fortnight of the month of Phāgun (Sanskrit Phālguna = February-March) in celebration of the vernal equinox.

or (Śiv. 86) hōm or (K. 96, 943) hūm m. (amongst Hindūs), an oblation with fire, a burnt-offering (of ghī, fruit, or the like). ¶ humukᵘ adj. (f. humücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to a burnt-offering (such as the thing offered, the altar or implements employed, the ceremony observed, the country in which it is performed, or the like). ¶ humas bĕhun m.inf. to sit (i.e. station oneself) for a burnt-offering, to commence a burnt-offering.
adj. c.g. one who is in the habit of making burnt-offerings. Used --˚, as in ạndᵃra-humal, p. 32b, l. 30.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. humᵘ), (amongst Hindus) to make a burnt-offering (see hum) (Śiv. 379; Rām. 226, 636, 956, 998). humᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. humᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), offered in a burnt-offering; met. (of any food) eaten and digested.
adj. (f. humüvᵘ̈), made of ash-wood. Cf. humᵘ.

m. a kind of tree growing on the lower mountain slopes; the ash, Fraxinus floribunda or Moorcroftiana (L. 79, hom; El. hamú, húm); its wood, described as soft and smooth. The latter is much prized by agriculturists for implements, esp. plough handles, and boatmen esteem it for paddles.
f. conduct of a dog; conduct like that of a dog, i.e. vile conduct practised again and again in spite of abuse or punishment earned previously for the same action.

f. (sg. dat. hōñĕ), a female dog, a bitch, see hūnᵘ 1 (K.Pr. 7, 82, 102). ¶ hōñĕ-bŏkotᵘ m. (f. -bŏkᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), a bitch's whelp, i.e. a puppy more than a month old. -kuʦurᵘ m. (f. -kuʦürᵘ̈), a bitch's whelp, i.e. a puppy just after it is born, less than a month old.

m. (sg. dat. hūnis, abl. hōni. The f. is hūñᵘ̈, q.v.), a dog (K.Pr. 35, 52, 58, 82, 84, 114, 224; H. viii, 4, 9, 10, 12; Rām. 807, 849). ¶ hūnⁱ-aḍijⁱ f. a dog's bone; met. hardness gained by a man of bad conduct owing to his being universally ill-treated and being knocked about by everyone. -bukurᵘ m. 'dog-faced'; met. a stubborn fellow who will not give up his habits, no matter how much he is beaten or abused. -buthᵘ m. id. (Gr.Gr. 75); 'a dog's face,' stubbornness (cf. K.Pr. 82, honih buth, a bitch's face). -buthörᵘ̈ f. 'dog-facedness'; stubbornness, persistence in misconduct in spite of abuse or disgrace. -hāl m. 'a dog's condition'; hence, frequent ill-treatment and abuse of a man, as if he were a dog. -har f. 'dog's quarrelling'; the fighting of a number of people for a trivial cause, the fighters, as it were, tearing each other limb, and in a moment becoming good friends again. -loṭᵘ m. 'a dog's tail' (which retains its curl no matter how much you bandage it); an ill-born low fellow, who does not change his nature, even when instructed and trained. -māray f. 'dog-killing'; killing men, as if they were dogs, without discrimination, in a time of anarchy. -më̆ṭᵘ̈ f. 'the dog's bit'; (amongst Hindūs) when dinner is served, one of the three bits of food taken from the dish and thrown outside as an offering to a god, for dogs to eat (K.Pr. 133). -māz m. dog's flesh, vile food (K.Pr. 36). -māzas wātal-wāza m. a low-caste cook for dog's flesh; hence, setting a mean fellow to mean or doubtful work (K.Pr. 84). -rôchᵘ  m. a dog-guard; hence (1) a dog-keeper, a person employed to feed and tend dogs; (2) a person employed to guard (e.g. a cooking-place, or an eating-place) from dogs. -röchⁱ f. dog-guarding; hence (1) feeding and tending dogs; (2) guarding food, etc., from dogs; (3) the guarding (of a house, etc.), by a dog; (4) a club used to protect oneself from dogs. -ṭãw m. a single bark or howl of a dog; a similar lamentable cry or howl uttered by a human being. -ʦopᵘ m. the bite of a dog, the wound caused by such a bite; the disease caused by such; met. a malicious, malevolent man. -wôlᵘ m. a man employed to look after dogs; one fond of keeping dogs. -wŏph m. (sg. dat. -wŏphas), a dog's flying (at a person), the attack made by a dog. -wōray f. the barking or howl of a dog; met. a lamentable cry or howl by a human being. -wushka 1 m. one who habitually acts contrary to orders. -wushka 2 f. dog-barley, darnel, tares (as in Matt. xiii, 25) (K.Pr. 84, 251; W. 139). -wath brörⁱ-wath f. (sg. dat. -wati), dog's path (and) cat's path; (of two persons who are thrown together in business) acting at variance, discord, cat-and-dog relations.
f. the small green nucleus-shoot of the kernel of a lotus seed. ¶ hūnⁱ-hüṭⁱ f. the nucleus-wood, the centre of the trunk of a tree left standing as a support for the pile of logs cut away from it.
adj. (f. hupörimᵘ̈), of or belonging to over there (within sight) (Gr.Gr. 151).
adv. in or from that direction (in sight), i.q. humi-pörⁱ, see huh (Gr.Gr. 160).
f. a virgin of paradise, a black-eyed nymph (K.Pr. 50; Rām. 395, 1072, 1167, 1175, 1234).
(? spelling), interj. the sound used for driving away cows (K.Pr. 239). Cf. hȧrⁱ.
adv. suddenly, rashly, careless of cause, unexpectedly.
in darbi-hurᵘ̈, i.q. hürᵘ̈ 1 in darbi-hürᵘ̈ (see darb) pȧñⁱ-hurⁱ, p. 746a, l. 41, and raza-hᵒ, p. 856a, l. 4.

m. a birth-bed, a lying-in bed, the bed of grass or straw in a lying-in room, used by a woman during the days of her impurity (eleven for a Hindū) after giving birth to a child. Among Hindūs, the grass is first changed, and the mother and child are bathed on the ninth day. Amongst Musalmāns, the grass is changed daily and the bathing is on the seventh day. In each case the child is given its name on the day of bathing (L. 258, 259, 270). --trāwun -- m.inf. amongst Hindūs, on the above ninth day of bathing, seven vessels are filled with food and are regarded as representing seven tutelary deities. The food is formally consecrated and is then distributed amongst neighbours and relations. When the period of impurity is over the empty jars, the straw bedding, and other things of the lying-in room, are scattered on a river bank as offerings to the tutelary deities. Cf. L. 259 for further details. hurᵘ trāwun is to do this scattering. ¶ hurⁱ-kaṭh m. the ram of the lying-in bed; N. of a sacrifice offered to a tutelary deity of a Hindū family either to secure the birth of a son, or to ward off evil from a woman just delivered of a son. The animal sacrificed is a ram, which is stroked three times by the mother before the sacrifice (L. 258). -lë̆jᵘ̈ f. (amongst Hindūs) the jar of the lying-in bed; the jar in which all food for the lying-in woman is placed, after being cooked on a fire worshipped by an attendant girl (see L. 258); one of the seven vessels filled with food on the ninth day, and considered to represent tutelary gods; see hurᵘ trāwun ab., and L. 259. -mã̄ḍay f. the setting about, or engagement in, the customary festival on the occasion of the birth of a son or daughter. -phọ̆tᵘ m. the lying-in-bed basket, N. of a basket containing ginger, salt, rice, sweetmeats, turmeric, etc., sent as a present by the mother's parents to their daughter, on the day of the birth of her child (L. 259). -pröpyunᵘ m. the offerings of rice, flesh, fish, etc., put into the seven vessels round a lying-in woman's bed (see hurᵘ trāwun, ab.). -pöthᵃr m. the arranging of all the necessaries (the grass bedding, jars for offerings, cooking utensils, etc.) in a lying-in room; a genl. name for all the appurtenances of a lying-in room. -rôchᵘ m. (among Hindūs) the guardian of the lying-in bed; N. of the tutelary deity, a personification of the sixth day after the birth of a child (when the chief danger for mother and child is over), in whose charge they both remain during the eleven days of lying-in (see ab.). -sāway f. the prosperity of the lying-in bed; the rejoicings and congratulations received on the birth of a child. -ʦhāwüjᵘ̈ f. the she-goat of the lying-in bed, i.e. (amongst Hindūs) an offering of a she-goat and other articles to the tutelary god on the eleventh or twelfth day after the birth of a child, in order to ward off evil from it. ¶ huri bĕhun m.inf. to be seated on the lying-in straw; (of a lying-in woman) to be in the straw, to be on the lying-in bed, to be confined (during the eleven days after birth); (of the same) to perform the necessary ceremonies to secure the birth of a son; the announcement to friends, etc., of the birth of a son. --bīṭhᵘ̈ -- f. seated on the lying-in bed, a woman who is brought to bed with a child (during the days of her confinement in the lying-in room); a woman who is engaged in the ceremonies prescribed for securing the birth of a son. --drāyĕ -- p.p. f. a woman who has just emerged from the lying-in bed, i.e. a woman who has happily passed through the time of her lying-in without any untoward occurrence; a woman who has passed through her time of lying-in, but is still delicate and still unable to engage in household duties. --wö̆ʦhᵘ̈ -- 1 p. p. f. a woman who has risen from the lying-in bed, i.e. a woman who has recovered from her confinement, and is able to engage in household duties; a woman who is past the age for child-bearing. ¶ huris bĕhun m.inf. to be seated for the lying-in straw; hence, to assemble on the occasion of a festival in honour of the birth of a son.

f. (for 2, see har 4), dry wood (Rām. 585), esp. a small piece or stick (K.Pr. 25, har); the small fuel used in a cooking stove; chippings (hari hari, by chippings and chippings, i.e. little by little, K.Pr. 787); harĕ hĕñĕ wuri-dānas, to take small chips (as fuel) for a long fire-trench cooking stove (requiring long bits of wood for fuel; cf. wura, K. Pr. 85); cf. kȧnḍⁱ-hürⁱ, s.v. konḍᵘ 2. --baḍāwüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to extinguish the fuel, to put out the fire of a cooking stove. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to withdraw the fuel, i.e. to draw the fuel and extinguish the fire in a cooking stove.

m. a piece of rag used for plastering a floor, cooking place, or the like with the usual mixture of mud and cow-dung; cf. cōka 1. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to apply such a rag, to plaster, as ab. ¶ hurⁱ-aiṭham or -öṭham f. (sg. dat. -aiṭhümᵘ̈), N. of a certain date, the eighth lunar day of the dark half of the month of Phāgun (Sanskrit Phālguna = February-March) on which the houses of Hindūs are freshly plastered and otherwise purified in preparation for the festival of the hērath or Śiva-rātrī, see -satam, bel. and hērath. -më̆ʦᵘ̈ f. a kind of white earth used for plastering, and giving the appearance of whitewash. -satam f. (sg. dat. -satümᵘ̈), the seventh lunar day of the dark half of the month of Phāgun, on which houses are plastered and otherwise purified in preparation for the Śiva-rātrī, see -aiṭham, ab., and hērath.

m. the shouts or outcry raised in a town when it is suddenly raided or attacked by robbers, an uproar (Gr.Gr. 51, K.Pr. 127). --tulun -- m.inf. to raise such an outcry; met. (of a number of children or women suddenly attacked) to scream out for help. --wŏthun -- m.inf. an outcry to be raised owing to the plundering, etc., of a town; met. loud outcries of lamentation to be raised by the mourners in the mourning room of a house in which a death has occurred.
or husyörī (Rām. 1635), sense; prudence, discretion; carefulness, vigilance, watchfulness. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be careful, vigilant; to keep awake (Rām. 1635).
f. N.P., short and familiar for Ḥusainī, a woman's name (K.Pr. 85).
m. that which remains over and above after a sacrifice, the remnant of an oblation (Śiv. 1658, 1881).
m. that which conveys oblations (to heaven); hence, blazing fire, a raging fire (L.V. 38).

adv. there, u.w. ref. to something within sight, or not distant. Cf. Gr.Gr. 155, and hutith. ¶ hutinukᵘ or hutyunukᵘ adj. (f. hutinücᵘ̈), of or belonging to there, as ab. ¶ hutinas adv. i.q. hutĕn. Cf. Gr.Gr. 155.
adv. in that manner, so (Gr.Gr. 153). -pöṭhⁱ adv., id. (Gr.Gr. 153).
adj. (f. huʦhᵘ̈), of that kind, like that (within sight or not distant) (Gr.Gr. 153).
or (Gr.Gr. 156) hututh adv. there, in that place near or within sight. Cf. hutĕn.
adv. there, in that place (within sight) (Gr.Gr. 156). -kun adv. in that direction, thither (Gr.Gr. 160).

f. (sg. dat. hacĕ), that which has become thin or wasted (cf. haṭun); hence, a stick, a piece of wood (K.Pr. 119); wood (Śiv. 1902-4); paddy standing in the fields, which for any reason has become dried up and withered (K.Pr. 47, 162), or a chip of dried fruit (cf. bam-ʦū̃ṭhᵘ). --˚ dried up (of potatoes, radishes, cucumbers, or the like, sliced, dried, and stored for winter use), cf. ala-hüṭᵘ̈, p. 22a, l. 50, and kīshĕ-hüṭᵘ, a certain fillet of hair, s.v. kīsh. ¶ hacĕ f.pl. bits of wood, a heap of split wood; met. help, assistance, esp. when rendered voluntarily and without being sought for. --gaʦhañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to become sticks; hence, to become withered or wasted (of a hungry person who does not get food); to waste away in prison, or the like. --kaḍañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to reduce to sticks; met. to cause a man or beast to waste away by overwork, or the like; to wear out any article by constant use. --karañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to make sticks; met. to torment a hungry person (esp. one under one's protection) by keeping food away from him; to prepare dried slices of roots, etc., see ab. --nērañĕ -- f. pl. inf. the sticks to issue forth; to waste away, become feeble (of a woman, owing to excessive child-bearing; of a man in his old age, by being worn out by long service). -pholᵘ m. a small heap of wooden chips or split wood.

adv. there, in that place (within sight or not distant) (Gr.Gr. 154). Often confused with huti 1. huti 1 adv. there, in that place (within sight or not distant) (W. 94); thence (El., Gr.Gr. 155). Often confused with hutⁱ. -kinⁱ adv. thence, from that place (within sight, etc.) (Gr.Gr. 158). -pĕṭha adv., id. (Gr.Gr. 155). ¶ hutyukᵘ adj. (f. huticᵘ̈), of or belonging to there (as ab.).

f. a general outcry and lamentation (e.g. on the occasion of a death, conflagration, inundation, or the like) (Rām. 835, 1161). --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to raise such an outcry. --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such an outcry to arise.
m. presence, the royal presence; the person of a monarch or any high functionary; as interj. Your Highness, (politely) Sir! (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. of or belonging to the presence. --nōkar -- m. a personal servant (H. viii, 5).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. hyôwᵘ), to cause to take, etc. (Gr.Gr. 172). Caus. of hyonᵘ, q.v.; i.q. hĕwanāwun, q.v.

m. an ear, spike, or tassel (of corn, paddy, or the like, El. hilyi) (K.Pr. 168, translated 'sheaf'; YZ. 392, 397; L. 464; Śiv. 1212; H. vi, 15; Rām. 12). ¶ hĕla-hĕl f. (of corn, etc.) the commencement of the formation of the ear or tassel. ¶ hĕlⁱ-basta f. the leaf-casing or sheath of an immature ear or tassel of corn. -phal m. the fruit of an ear, corn (e.g. barley, paddy, wheat, panic, etc.) generally. -mūr, -mūran, or -mūray f. husking the ear, a method of removing grain from the ear by rubbing. -ray m. a kind of blight in which the stalk and ears of the rice plant wither (L. 334 hil rai). ¶ hĕli-drāv adj. c.g. (of corn) in the ear; of (a field, or the like) possessing corn in the ear. This word is reported to be c.g. We should expect a f. -drāyĕ. --nērun -- m.inf. to become in the ear, as ab. -pĕṭhukᵘ adj. (f. pĕṭhücᵘ̈), 'of on the ear,' collected straight from the ear, i.e. quite clean and fresh. -wothᵘ adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), descended from the ear, i.e. i.q. hĕli- pĕṭhukᵘ, ab.
m. (f. hĕndⁱyöñⁱ, in the meaning of a female Hindū), a Hindū; in Kashmīr, a Hindū of the upper castes.

conj. 1 irreg. [inf. hyonᵘ, dat. hĕnis, abl. hĕni or hĕna 2 (for 1, see hĕn); pres. part. hĕwān; fut. pass. part. hyonᵘ, f. hë̆ñᵘ̈; impers. fut. part. hĕnī; conj. part. hĕth; neg. conj. part. hĕnay; freq. part. hĕ hĕ or hĕth hĕth; adverbial part. hĕwönⁱ; 1 p.p. hyotᵘ 3 (for 1 and 2, see s.v.), pl. hĕtⁱ;f. hë̆ʦᵘ̈ 3 (for 1 and 2, see hyotᵘ 1 and 2), pl. hĕʦa; 2 p.p. hĕʦōv, pl. hĕʦöy; f.sg. and pl. hĕʦöyĕ; 3 p.p. hĕʦāv, pl. hĕʦöyēy; f. same as f. of 2 p.p.; fut. sg. 1 hĕma, 2 hĕkh, 3 hĕyi; pl. 1 hĕmaw, 2 hĕyiw, 3 hĕyin; past. cond. sg. 1 hĕmahö, 2 hĕhökh, 3 hĕyihē; pl. 1 hĕmahöw, 2 hĕyⁱhīw, 3 hĕhön; impve. pres. 2 sg. hĕh, pl. hĕyiw, 3 sg. and pl. hĕyin; pol. 2 sg. hĕta, pl. hĕyⁱtaw, 3 sg. and pl. hĕyⁱtan; fut. hĕzi; past. hĕzihē ], to take, receive (L.V. 14, 45; Śiv. 1084, 1096; H. ii, 1; iii, 1, 2, etc.); to receive (as an answer to prayer) (Rām. 1260); to take, get possession of (Śiv. 1006); to take hold of, seize, grasp (Śiv. 1532, 1734, 1780, 1873; Rām. 38, 698, 800); to take forcibly, to plunder; to take, imprison, capture (a person) (Śiv. 1004, 1341; Rām. 361); to buy (L.V. 89, K. 178), also mŏlⁱ hyonᵘ (e.g. K.Pr. 234); to accept (Śiv. 687); to take (good and bad treatment with equal indifference), to bear all things with equanimity; to take (a blow or an insult) lying down, to be poor spirited; to take, receive (a beating, or the like) (K.Pr. 59); to assume, wear (clothes, or the like) (Rām. 345, 1457); to take or assume (a character) (e.g. in a play) (Śiv. 1705); to take (a disease), be attacked (by sickness); to hold, retain, keep (Rām. 56); to adopt (a course of conduct, or of thought) (Śiv. 1754, 1858); to take (as a helper), to take refuge with (Śiv. 1164, 1178); to carry (Śiv. 1149, 1150, 1159, 1211, 1494, 1504, 1665, 1729; Rām. 81, 236, 305, 584, 603, 644, 676, 890, 900, 1394); to carry (news, a message, or the like) (Rām. 560, 800, 832, 928, 1780); to bring, fetch (L. 460, YZ. 242); to carry (a child, etc., in one's arms, etc.) (Śiv. 1357-8, 1381, 1385, 1401, 1542; Rām. 1286; kŏchhĕ, in the bosom, (Śiv. 377, Rām. 1522); to hold, carry (in the hand) (Śiv. 214, 392, 801, 855, 860, 1093, 1400; Rām. 121, 389, 821, 1308); to carry, draw (a sword) (Rām. 648, 903); to carry (a weapon with the object of attack) (Rām. 431, 1096, 1312); to seize (of fire or flames seizing something) (Śiv. 68, 92, 118; Rām. 103, 849, 1014, 1169, 1561, 1578, 1613); to begin (see bel.). hyonᵘ-dyunᵘ m.inf. to take and give, reciprocal giving and taking (Śiv. 1832; Rām. 1440, 1744). ¶ In the sense of beginning hyonᵘ is used with the inf. or fut. pass. part. of another verb, which agrees in gender with the object (if any). Thus, suh karun hĕwān chuh, he takes the act of doing, i.e. he begins to do; suh chuh khath lēkhunᵘ hĕwān, he takes the letter to be written, i.e. he begins to write it; suh chuh zanāna mārüñᵘ̈ hĕwān, he takes the woman to be beaten, he begins to beat her. In this sense, hyonᵘ is most often used in the past tenses, and being a transitive verb, then itself agrees with the object (if any) in gender and number, the subject being put in the case of the agent. Thus, parun hyotun, he began to read; tȧmⁱ chuh khath lēkhunᵘ hyotᵘmotᵘ, he has begun to write the letter, lit. by him the letter to be written has been taken; tȧmⁱ chĕh zanāna mārüñᵘ̈ hë̆ʦᵘ̈- müʦᵘ̈, he has begun to beat the woman, lit. by him the woman to be beaten has been taken (Gr.Gr. 116). But other tenses also of hyonᵘ are used in this sense, although not so frequently. Thus:-- ¶ Impve. Śiv. 540, 941, 1301, 1770 (all masc.). Fut. (masc.) Śiv. 1190, 1193, 1195, 1202, 1720; Rām. 23, 718, 719, 1773; fem. karüñᵘ̈ hĕn būlⁱ, they will begin to chirp (Śiv. 1721). ¶ The past tenses naturally appear in various forms. Thus:-- hyotᵘ, subject not expressed, Śiv. 1197, 1327; subject in agent case, Śiv. 1118, 1200, 1223, 1300; Rām. 170, 239 (timau wanunᵘ hyotᵘ), 709 (Lakshmanan grazunᵘ hyotᵘ), 1333, 1636. ¶ With suffixes of agent case, hyotum lāyun nādāh, I began to utter a call (Rām. 1720); hyotum naʦun, I began to dance (L.V. 94); wuchun hyotᵘmas, I began to look at it (L.V. 48); hyotun, he or she began, YZ. 249; Śiv. 1233, 1707; Rām. 336 (she began), 654 (pariyĕ hyotun samāna trāwun, the fairy began to cast off her ornaments), 1178, 1755; wanunᵘ hyotᵘnas, he or she began to say to him or her (YZ. 249, 389); wanunᵘ hyotᵘnakh, he or she began to say to them (YZ. 215, Rām. 270); hyotᵘnakh prān nērun, their life began to depart (Rām. 1333); hyotukh banāwun, they began to make (Śiv. 960); hyotukh pakun, they began to march (H. x, 1); hyotᵘhas wanāwun, they began to sing his praises (Śiv. 960); hĕtin vih-hihⁱ hāwȧnⁱ, she began to show airs and graces (Rām. 332); hĕtikh tāj sārȧnⁱ, they began to collect the crowns (Rām. 1462). ¶ The suff. is even used when the main verb is intransitive, and when, therefore, it cannot refer to the subject. Its presence here is, in fact, logically indefensible, and is due to false analogy with the construction with transitive verbs. Thus, chĕtȧnⁱ hĕtin kēsh, hairs began to grow white (Śiv. 1704); hë̆ʦᵘ̈nas yiñᵘ̈ nẹ̆ndᵃr, sleep began to come to him (H. v, 6). ¶ This verb is often used in nominal compounds such as:-- and hyonᵘ, to take the end, go through a thing from beginning to end (Śiv. 120) (conj. part. and hĕth, throughout, Śiv. 1206); apozᵘ hyonᵘ növⁱ, to take untruth on the voice, to speak untruly (Rām. 1056); awatār h., to take an incarnation, become incarnate (Śiv. 1384); bôrᵘ h., to take the burden, accept responsibility (Rām. 134); dāg h., to become branded (Rām. 203, 387, 643, 1713, 1718); dŏg h., to take a beating, to be drubbed (K.Pr. 59); danḍa h., to take in compensation (H. v, 11); gam h., to suffer woe, be full of sorrow (Rām. 1655); gāsa h., to carry grass in token of submission, as if to say 'I am thy cow', Rām. 96; hĕs h., to seize the mind, compel attention (Śiv. 25); to captivate the senses (Śiv. 1453); lādan hë̆ñᵘ̈, to accept a favour (Rām. 1439); jān hyonᵘ, to take life, to kill (Śiv. 130, 680; Rām. 67, 310, 492, 913); khūn h., to kill, to murder (Rām. 814, 837, 1075); khabar hë̆ñᵘ̈, to carry news (Rām. 560); kala hyonᵘ, to hold the head, to fondle (Rām. 269, 1129); to cut off the head, behead (Śiv. 739); kirāyĕ h., to take on lease (Gr.M.); mŏlⁱ hyonᵘ, to buy (H. x, 14; K.Pr. 234; YZ. 120, 157, 161, 169, 191, 242, 268); mŏshᵉ̆kh h., to smell (Gr.M., Rām. 617); nāv h., to take a person's name, to utter it with reverence (Rām. 271); pānas h., to take upon oneself, take responsibility for (Rām. 134, 502); prān h., to take life, to kill (Śiv. 1387, Rām. 1238); path h., to take a back seat, be defeated, be overcome (Śiv. 1237, 1246); to refrain from (Śiv. 1843); rukhsath h., to take permission to depart, to take leave (Śiv. 694, 1167; H. xii, 10, 13; Rām. 1180, 1183, 1678); rath h., to take blood, to kill, murder (Rām. 1240); samāgam h., to take a meeting, to meet; hĕth samāgam, having met, and also (with double meaning, see hĕth 2 and hyotᵘ 1) a friendly meeting (Śiv. 1848); ʦhāl hë̆ñᵘ̈, to take a leap (Rām. 561, 886); ʦȧpⁱ hĕnⁱ, to take bites, to bite (H. x, 7, of a snake); wath hë̆ñᵘ̈, to take the road, to go forth (Rām. 680, 1598); yād h., to keep in memory, remember (H. xii, 17); zāg hë̆ñᵘ̈, to wait for, expect (Śiv. 272, 1382); zima hyonᵘ, to accept responsibility, admit (H. xii, 15); zanm h., to take birth, be born (Śiv. 34); zĕvi h., to take upon the tongue, to mention, to name, to mention so-and-so's name (K. 675, 1055); zuv h., to take life, to kill (L.V. 54; Rām. 810, 858). ¶ hĕna-bāna m. a vessel of patience, one who bears (praise and blame, good fortune and bad fortune, good treatment and bad treatment, etc.) with equanimity, one who takes all things easily, as they come. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. giving or taking, barter, traffic; esp. borrowing and lending. -hār n.ag. c.g. fit to be taken; a thing which should certainly be bought (on account of its excellence, beauty, etc.); (of a man) one who takes others' abuse or ill-treatment with equanimity, one who is poor-spirited. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a taker; one who accepts abuse or ill-treatment with equanimity; one who will accept a thing under pressure; a buyer, a purchaser. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. pass. to be taken; to be taken prisoner, arrested (K.Pr. 81); to be involved in difficulties (K.Pr. 81), become entangled in some difficult or complicated business; to be engaged in some business (Gr.Gr. 169). ¶ hĕnī impers. fut. pass. part. c.g. what should certainly be taken, what one should certainly endeavour to get by prayers and entreaties. ¶ hĕth conj. part. having taken. Very often used with various adverbial meanings. Thus:-- ¶ (a) taking (so-and-so or such-and-such), having (so-and-so) as a companion, accompanied by (Śiv. 731, 800, 1100, 1101, 1108, 1311, et passim; Rām. 136, 205, 1110; H. viii, 9). ¶ (b) together with, in company with (Śiv. 698, 1175, 1353, 1440, 1456, 1484, 1529, 1886; Rām. 49, 308, 693, 695, 793, 859; H. xii, 23, 25). ¶ (c) together with, in addition to, and also (Śiv. 64, 201, 213, 368, 686). ¶ (d) together with, including, plus (Śiv. 32, 369). ¶ (e) other phrases are gam hĕth, having taken sorrow, i.e. sorrowfully (Rām. 1101); sŏkh hĕth, happily (Śiv. 1459); ʦūrⁱ hĕth, secretly (Rām. 659). ¶ hĕth gaʦhun m.inf. having taken to go, to take away, carry off (= Hindī lē jānā) (K.Pr. 36 hit; Śiv. 53, 63, 705, 722, 1600, 1617-8, 1887; Rām. 398, 402, 406, 415, 469, 601, 746, 926, 1044, 1354; H. v, 1; vii, 3, etc.). --jān -- (Śiv. 316) or --zuv ta jān -- (Śiv. 191), adv. taking (life and) soul, with all one's heart and soul. --sāthay sāth adv. having (a person) always with one, being always accompanied by (so-and-so) (Śiv. 1552). --pānas sṻty -- (Śiv. 1672), --sṻty --, or (e.g. Rām. 1322) --sṻtin --, adv. having taken with (one), having with one, (going) along, and having (so-and-so) with one, accompanied by (YZ. 88; Śiv. 169, 805, 955, 1116, 1172, 1419-20, 1456; Rām. 1039, 1100, 1322-3, 1554-5, 1698, 1758). --sṻty sṻty -- adv. taking (so-and-so) along with one (Śiv. 1154, 1445, 1581). --ʦalun -- m.inf. having taken to abscond, to plunder and carry off (L.V. 86). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. having taken to come, to bring (= Hindī lē ānā) (Śiv. 76, 668, 718, 720, 723, 730, 1667, 1831, 1836, 1856; Rām. 382, 694, 834, 943, 1120, 1144, 1464, 1631; H. i, 8; iii, 1; viii, 6, etc.). ¶ hyotᵘ-dyotᵘ m. taken and given (dyotᵘ for dyutᵘ), presents given to a bride and her relations on various Hindū festivals following a marriage. -dyutᵘ m. taken and given; taking and giving, trade, traffic, barter with any person (= Hindī lēn-dēn). -motᵘ (f. hë̆ʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), taken, accepted; taken by disease, gradually wasting away from sickness; taken by force; bought, purchased.

or hyurᵘ 1 adv. up, above, on the top (K.Pr. 43); upwards (Śiv. 61, 847); cf. hyūrᵘ and hēr. -bŏn or bŏn ta hyorᵘ adv. up and down, above and below; from top to bottom; cf. bŏna-hyorᵘ, p. 110b, l. 15, and hēri bŏn and hyūrᵘ -bŏn, s.v. hyūrᵘ.-bŏn gaʦhun m.inf. to become up and down; to suffer vicissitudes. --khasun -- m.inf. to mount, go up (Rām. 280; K. 74, 233), e.g. upstairs (H. iii, 2, 9) or up stream (H. xii, 6); hyorᵘ hyorᵘ khasun, to rise gradually upwards (K. 70). -kun adv. upwards, towards above (Gr.Gr. 161, Rām. 1416), at the top, near the top; above, in the sky. Cf. hyūrᵘ-kun. ¶ hĕri-hyorᵘ adv. above the top, extremely high, highest of all. -kani or -kanĕn adv. at the top, on the height. -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of or belonging to (something) on the top.

adj. (f. hë̆ʦᵘ̈ 1), friendly, affectionate, kind; beneficial, advantageous, salutary, convenient (L.V. 61); cf. hĕth 2. --nērun -- m.inf. to turn out friendly; to become salutary, profitable, to have beneficial results (whether expected or not). --wanun -- m.inf. friendly and good advice. ¶ hë̆ʦᵘ̈ kathkarüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to make a kind word, to put in a good word (esp. for some absent person).
adj. (f. hë̆ʦᵘ̈ 2), (properly 1 p.p. of hyonᵘ, q.v.) (in business, or the like) the amount to be collected, the amount (originally taken, and now) due.

adj. (f. hishᵘ̈), like, closely resembling, exactly like (L.V. 10, 77, 109; K.Pr. 212); (of things compared) all alike, resembling each other (Śiv. 901). The object with which comparison is made is put in the nom. or in the dat. or, occasionally, in the gen. A good example of the use of the genitive is the phrase cyônᵘ hyuhᵘ. Here if we look upon cyônᵘ as the nom. of the possessive pron. 'thy', the words mean 'like thine' (so Śiv. 1696); but if we look upon it as the gen. of ʦᵃh, thou, they mean 'like thee' (so Rām. 810). ¶ Hyuhᵘ is very commonly used with pron. adjs. of manner, thus,-- yuthᵘ hyuhᵘ, this kind of (Śiv. 1207); f. yiʦhᵘ̈ hishᵘ̈ (Śiv. 1728, Rām. 359); tyuthᵘ hyuhᵘ, of that kind (Rām. 1000); kyuthᵘ h., of what kind? (Śiv. 780, Rām. 1074); similarly kus h., what sort of? (Gr.M.). ¶ As examples of the word governing the nom., we have, e.g. an hyuhᵘ, like food (Śiv. 1229); ara h., like a saw (Śiv. 1776); gŏsôñᵘ h., like a mendicant devotee (Śiv. 825); lūkan-hondᵘ (nom. of gen.) h., like (the conduct) of people (Śiv. 1799); pampōsh h., like a lotus (Śiv. 813, 1536); prān h. (value) like (your) life (Śiv. 1547); sūrĕ h., like the sun (Śiv. 98, 346, 740, 1586); yinsān h., like a man (H. x, 7); yār h. (treat) like a friend (Śiv. 1687). ¶ There is a slight difference in meaning when governing the dat. Thus,-- môlᵘ (nom.) hyuhᵘ, (he is) like a father (to him); but mölis (dat.) hyuhᵘ, (the son is) like the father (Gr.Gr. 94). Other examples of the use with the dat. are:-- (a) with pronouns, ʦĕ hyuhᵘ, like thee (Śiv. 472, 1344, 1540; Rām. 933); tas h., like him (Śiv. 35, 997, 1366; Rām. 1116); tath h., like that (thing) (H. xii, 4); kath h., like what? (Śiv. 901). ¶ (b) With nouns subst. cyönis garas hyuhᵘ, like thy house (Gr.M.); hūñĕ h., like a bitch (K.Pr. 7); larĕ h., like a house (or houses) (Śiv. 1330); lālas h., like a ruby (H. xii, 4); rāzabāyĕ h., like a queen (or queens) (Śiv. 1237); sīmābas h., like quicksilver (Śiv. 1464); ṭhūlas h., like an egg, oval (Gr.M.). ¶ With words indicating comparative age, hyuhᵘ indicates the comparison. Thus,-- buḍᵘ hyuhᵘ ȧnⁱzĕn, you must bring whoever among them is old, not 'bring him like an old man' (Gr.Gr. 94); kö̃sa hyuhᵘ, the youngest (among a number) (YZ. 418); lŏkuṭᵘ h., id. (H. xii, 1); zyuṭhᵘ h., the elder (of two princes) (H. viii, 5; similarly, Rām. 699, 859). ¶ Hyuhᵘ, like the Hindī sā, often has simply an intensive force, and in this use sometimes gives an idiomatic meaning to the compound, as in alsēṭh- hyuhᵘ, very fat; hence, a fat fool. ¶ Other examples (by no means pretending to be complete) of various idiomatic uses of this word are,-- dôdᵘ hyuhᵘ, something like a pain, a sort of pain (Gr.M.); kunu-y hyuhᵘ, exactly alike; shālĕn byôlᵘ chuh hyuhuy, (one) shôlᵘ seed is exactly like (another), lit. 'for shôlus the seed is exactly similar' (K.Pr. 193, spelt hihúí). hyuhᵘ samakhun m.inf. like (what one wanted) to become visible, just what one desired to be obtained. ¶ Cf. hyuvᵘ, which is used with the same meaning, and in exactly the same way as hyuhᵘ.

m. a hiccough; convulsive sobbing or breathing. --lagun -- m.inf. an hiccough to come on. hikⁱ-kyulⁱ m. 'a hiccough-nail', a very painful disease caused by obstruction of the breath during a hiccough.

adj. (m. sg. dat. hīnis, abl. hīni; f. hīñᵘ̈), incomplete, deprived of, bereft of; in this sense common --˚, cf. anga-hyūnᵘ, maimed, p. 33a, l. 43 (Śiv. 749, 1309, 1738); low, vile, base, mean (by caste, quality, occupation, conduct, or the like); ugly (Śiv. 1640).

adv. (abl. hēri 3, for 1, see hēr, for 2, see hīrᵘ̈), up, above; upwards (Rām. 922); cf. hyorᵘ and hēr. -bŏn m. upness and downness, vicissitudes; as adv. up and down, above and below; from top to bottom; cf. hyorᵘ-bŏn, s.v. hyorᵘ, and hēri-bŏn, bel. -kun adv. upwards, towards above (Gr.Gr. 161); at the top, on the top; above, in the sky. Cf. hyorᵘ-kun. ¶ hēri-bŏn adv. up and down, above and below (Śiv. 1412), from top to bottom; cf. hyŏrᵘ-bŏn, s.v. hyorᵘ, and hyūrᵘ-bŏn, ab. -kani adv. above; upstairs. -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of or belonging to above or upstairs; hence, of or belonging to any place higher than some other place with which comparison is made.

m. the gullet, the throat. L.V. 57 spells this word hyuḍᵘ. ¶ hirⁱ-gŏgul m. adj. (f. hivᵘ̈), like, i.q. hyuhᵘ, q.v. m. cold breath as it issues from the mouth. Cf. L.V. 56, 57, where it is contrasted with hāh, q.v. According to L.V. hᵃh takes its rise in the brahma- randhra or cervical suture, while hāh takes its rise from the navel. See brahma-randr, p. 121a, l. 8.
adv. very quickly, speedily, u.w. vbs. of falling, throwing, speaking, walking, etc. (L.V. 99; K.Pr. 46, hĕk).
the womb (El. hal,m.). hᵃl diñᵘ̈ (f.inf.) or hᵃl dyunᵘ (m.inf.), (of a woman in childbed) to fill the rectum with wind from the intestines in order to facilitate delivery. Cf. hᵃlun.

conj. 3 [2 p.p. hᵃjyōv (Gr.Gr. lxxxv)], labour (with a child) to begin, the labour pains or straining to commence. Cf. hᵃl. ¶ hᵃlan aʦun m.inf. to enter labour pains, to begin to be in labour. --lagun -- m.inf., id. --lüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ -- perf. part. f. a woman who has begun to be in labour.

adj. (f. hᵘ̈ñᵘ̈) (properly 1 p.p. of hᵃnun, q.v.), swollen, dropsical; swollen and hollow, become worthless (like a blown out bladder) (Rām. 853, 973); huge, stout (Rām. 1337); churlish, morose, glum, grumpy, surly, sullen, unsympathetic. Cf. honᵘ.

adj. (f. hᵘ̈rᵘ̈), superfluous, remaining over and above; abundant (El. hur, hurr; cf. hurᵘ 3 and hᵃrun). -hāyẹ̆ka tōlun m.inf. to weigh one's surplus profits on (huge) paddy-scales (see hāyukh), to make a profit in business for exceeding one's expectations. ¶ hᵃri tōlun m.inf. to weigh with abundance, to give generous overweight (Śiv. 1476).

This is the ordinary i of Hindī, pronounced like the i in 'pin'. It is represented in the Nāgarī character by and in the Persian by zēr. Thus, نِشِہ, nishĕ, near. When followed by ᵃ, ⁱ, or ᵘ̈ it is not perceptibly changed, but before ᵘ it becomes yu. Thus kitᵘ becomes kyutᵘ. In the Nāgarī character we meet both and, but the pronunciation is always that of the latter, and that spelling will be followed in theis dictionary. ¶ The sound of i cannot commence a word. In such a position i always becomes yi. Thus, ih, this, becomes yih. In the Nāgarī character it is optionally written or, but the word is always pronounced yih, and will be so written in this dictionary. The Persian character always has یِہ. ¶ The letter i is quite often interchanged with ĕ, both in speaking and in writing. Most Kāshmīrīs seem to be unable to distinguish between the two sounds.

This is the ordinary long ī of Hindī, pronounced like the i in 'pique'. It is represented in the Nāgarī character by and in the Persian by yē preceded by zēr. Thus, شِین, shīn, snow. When followed by ᵃ, ⁱ, or ᵘ̈ it is not changed, but before ᵘ it becomes yū. Thus, from the base nīl- we have nyūlᵘ, blue. This sometimes occurs before an ordinary u; thus, the genitive of bīma, a policy of insurance, is byūmukᵘ. ¶ The sound of ī cannot commence a word. In such a position ī always become yī. Thus, īran, an anvil, becomes yīran. In the Nāgarī character it is optionally written or, but the word is always pronounced yīran, and will be so written in this dictionary. The Persian character always has یِیرَن. ¶ The letter ī is quite often interchanged with ē, both in speaking and in writing. Most Kāshmīrīs seem to be unable to distinguish between the two sounds.

m. (sg. dat. sikas, abl. sika 2, for 1, see s.v.; f. sikiyöñᵘ̈, or sīkiñ) a Sikkh, a follower of the Sikkh religion founded in the Panjāb by Guru Nānak (K.Pr. 200). ¶ sika-brôhmun m. (sg. dat. -bröhmanas), a man who acts as priest to a foreigner resident in Kashmīr (Sikkhs from the Panjāb, being typical foreigners). sika-koṭᵘ m. a Sikkh boy, the son of a Sikkh.

m. a skewer, a spit (K.Pr. 189, 200); any long thin piece of metal. --lāgȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to apply skewers, to burn a person with red-hot metal skewers or the like (as a punishment); met. to cauterize a person with harsh language or abuse.
f. secondary suffix used to form nouns of condition from substantives. Thus, chān, a carpenter, chönil, the condition of a carpenter (Gr.Gr. 142).
a kind of good white rice with a dark leaf (L. 248, 463). Perhaps connected with amṛĕth, q.v.
ᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ f. two primary suffixes forming abstract nouns. See Gr.Gr. 118 ff.
or ith-kĕth, a suffix which added to the root of a verb forms the conj. part. (Gr.Gr. 103, 197). In the Persian character it is spelt it اِت.
c.g. (as subst., m. sg. dat. i ṭas), a secondary suffix, forming adjectives of quality, as in rūp-iṭh, very beautiful, achīṭh (from ȧchⁱ, the eye), possessing the evil-eye (Gr.Gr. 138).

. The eighth consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is also the eighth consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and is the seventh consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It is pronounced, as in India proper, something like an English j, but is rather more dental, i.e. the place of contact between the tongue and the palate is slightly nearer the teeth than is the case in English. In schools, its name is zȧyⁱ zö. ¶ The Sanskrit aspirate jha does not exist as a pronounced sound in Kāshmīrī. When a Hindī or Sanskrit word containing this letter also occurs in Kāshmīrī, the jh is, subject to the remarks below, represented by j. Thus, the Hindī jhamak, brilliancy, is represented in Kāshmīrī by jamak(h). Sometimes the jh is retained in writing. Thus, in El., the word jan, a clang, is written jhan, as in Hindī, but this in no way affects the pronunciation. In the present work j will always be written, and jh never, in transliterating Kāshmīrī words, even when an affected purism induces a scribe to write in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character. It must, however, be remarked that, so far as the present writer's experience is concerned, he has never come across any instance of the use of this letter, even in the case of borrowed words. ¶ As already remarked, the Kāshmīrī j is rather more dental than the corresponding English letter. This makes it easy to change it into the dental sonant sibilant z, and the change is very common, although, so far as the present writer has been able to ascertain, subject to no definite rule. Sometimes the two letters are optionally interchangeable, as in the case of the Persian word juzw جزو, a quire, which, when borrowed by Kāshmīrī, takes the form juzᵃwa or jujᵃwa. At other times the use of j or z indicates variant meanings of the same word, as in the case of juv, a suffix of respect, and zuv, life, both of which native authorities connect with the Sanskrit word jīva-. As a rule, however, in words borrowed from other languages, such as Persian, which possess both j and z, the custom of the original language is followed, as in Persian jārī جاری, running, Kāshmīrī jörī; Persian zabān زبان, language, Kāshmīrī zabān. There are, nevertheless, exceptions even to this, as in the case of juzᵃwa or jujᵃwa above mentioned, or in the case of the Persian ziyāda زیادہ more, which becomes jyāda in Kāshmīrī. In pure Kāshmīrī words the nearest approach to a rule is that when an original j is followed by y it is not changed to z. To Kāshmīrī ears every j has a y-sound inherent in it, and it follows that many Kāshmīrīs, when writing their own language in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, put no dot under when it represents z, but, on the contrary, represent the j-sound by jy. Others, again, make no distinction in writing between the two sounds, representing both by. There are thus three systems of writing this pair of sounds, viz.:-- ¶ 1. 2. 3. ¶ j ¶ z ¶ The third system is that followed in this dictionary; but, as the second system is also in very general use, all important words will also be given with the spelling of that system, with cross-references to the spelling according to the third system. Thus, the word jörī جآری, running, will be found in its proper place in alphabetical order; but, as the word is often written and pronounced jyörī, that word is also given in its proper place, with a cross-reference to jörī. ¶ So strongly is the y-sound heard by Kāshmīrīs in the letter j, that ja is usually pronounced jĕ, ya following a consonant being always sounded as ĕ or yĕ (see article ĕ). Thus, the word jangul, a forest, is commonly written and pronounced jĕngul, and the borrowed Arabic word jald جلد is pronounced by some jalᵃd and by others jĕlᵃd. Conversely, an original jy may be represented by j or even z. Thus, the Sanskrit jyōtiṣa-, an astronomer, is represented in Kāshmīrī by jūtish or even zūtish, as well as by jyūtish, the former being the usual spelling, although the latter, from a Paṇḍit's point of view, is etymologically more correct. ¶ As has already been said, the Sanskrit or Hindī jh is represented in Kāshmīrī by j. This j, like an original j, is also liable to be changed to z. Thus, the Sanskrit budhyatē, Prakrit bujjhaï, is represented in Kāshmīrī by bōzi, he will hear. ¶ It thus follows that, if a word beginning with jĕ or jy is not found in this dictionary, it should be looked up under ja or j respectively, and vice versa. Moreover, as j and z are sometimes interchangeable, if a word is not found under j it should be looked up under z, and vice versa.

or jyā جا or (H. ii, 4; x, 12) jāh or (Śiv. 203, Rām. 573) jyāh f. i.q. jāy, q.v., a place. yĕkh jyā یک جا adv. in one place, together (Śiv. 905, H. as ab.); so, ba yĕkh jā بیک جا, id. (Rām. 573, 1685); jyā-ba-jyā جا بجا adv. here and there, everywhere (Śiv. 725). Cf. bē-jā.
m. a herd of cattle. ¶ jaba-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a herd-owner, esp. an owner of great herds.
m. a kind of grass, good for cattle-fodder (L. 70, 359).

m. an outer robe or long cloth coat or gown (of any colour), the sleeves of which reach not quite to the wrist; a coat of mail, any coat of defence. jaba-jāma or jĕba-jyāma جبہ جامہ m. a coat of mail (in Kashmīr composed of rings locally made) (El. also jabajáwa) (Rām. 919, 979; K. 556, 557).
m. (sg. dat. jabᵃrūtas), omnipotence; might, power, prowess (Rām. 742, 923, 1340).
m. (sg. dat. jã̄cas), knowledge of some art or science.
m. an ancestor; (in Kāshmīrī) a great-grandfather, the grandfather of one's father or of one's mother. ¶ jada-buḍⁱ-bab m. a great-great-grandfather on the side of either parent.
(cf. جد and اجداد) m. a distant ancestor, further back even than a great-great-grandfather. Cf. jad.
(cf. jadwal), a ruled line (round a page), a marginal line. -püṭᵘ̈ f. a rule, consisting of a wooden or pasteboard board provided with threads on which the paper is pressed, and thus becomes ruled.

m. (the f. is jadöjⁱ, q.v.), a mean and importunate beggar, a shameless beggar that is never satisfied (Śiv. 1246); a man whose conduct is that of such a beggar. -küṭᵘ̈ f. the girl-daughter of such a beggar. -kaṭh m. a boy-son of such a beggar, a beggar's brat; a boy who himself habitually acts as such a beggar.
f. the conduct of a mean, greedy, and importunate beggar; conduct such as that.
f. a mean and importunate beggar woman, a shameless beggar that is never satisfied; a woman whose conduct is that of such a beggar; see jadāl.
f. covetousness accompanied by meanness and importunity.
(Rām. 814) jādŏh, (Rām. 873) jyādō or (Rām. 901) jyādōh m. magic, enchantment, charm, conjuring. Cf. jôd.
(YZ. 44), jôdugār, or jyôdugār (Rām. 866), i.q. jôd-gar, s.v. jôd.
m. the refuse part of vegetables, cabbage-stalks, or the like.

m. the making of a ruled line or ruled border (round a page), ruling a marginal line (cf. jadal). -kalam m. a pen for ruling or making marginal lines, an etching pen, the English crow quill, or the like.

or jĕg m. a sacrifice, a sacrificial ceremony (Śiv. 74, 311, 392, 861; Rām. 79, 80, 1140, 1320, 1675, 1699, 1700; K. 305, 371, 402, etc.); esp. a joint general sacrifice to ward off or counteract some public calamity; a harvest home (El.). ¶ jaga-yüzᵘ̈man m. (his wife is jaga-yüzᵘ̈man-bāy), the head person in whose name such a sacrifice is conducted on behalf of the others, usually one of the largest contributors to the cost.
m. (sg. abl. jaga 1), N. of a certain bird, a kind of swan of a pale yellow colour.
in jaga-phamb m. old cotton wadding which has been used for padded clothing, for padded caps, or the like.
f. (sg. dat. jagargōṭi), N. of a kind of bhang; see banga.
m. one who, out of pure perversity, attacks others and stops their work.

m. pretended obstinacy or determination (e.g. such as is displayed by natives of Kashmīr when bargaining, their arms flung violently about and saying that they will never, never, consent to pay or receive such a price,--all this being merely part of the ordinary procedure preliminary to an agreement).
m. one who exhibits such sham obstinacy as that described under jāgurᵘ 1.
m. dignity, rank, high position, esp. in the Persian phrase māl o jāh, wealth and dignity (YZ. 233, 401).
m. angry obstinacy or persistence (esp. in quarrels).
m. N. of a village in Kashmīr famous for the tobacco grown there (K.Pr. 86).
m. a ship; the tree of a camel's saddle, or the saddle and its appurtenances. -wôñᵘ m. a sailor (esp. in a sea-going ship).
m. ignorance, foolishness; foolish or senseless disputation, a war of words (K.Pr. 183). Cf. jahal.

m. victory; hence, a cry of victory, the cry 'may there be victory to so-and-so' (Śiv. 92, 915), as interj. victory! (Śiv. 1896). jai-jai interj. victory (to so-and-so)! (Śiv. 159, 188, 685, etc.). jai-jai-kār m. making the cry of victory, the cry of 'victory to so-and-so' (Śiv. 5, 65, 1160, etc.). Cf. jay.
m. Croton tiglium, i.q. jamāl-gōṭh, q.v. (El.).

(? = جزا فزا 'reward-increase') m. lamentable entreaty, pitifully begging for something. The affiliation of this word is doubtful. If the Persian equivalent suggested above is correct, they would be the cry of a beggar, that the granting of his request would bring abundance of reward.

f. a kind of hookah, or native pipe for smoking tobacco through water, a hubble-bubble (El. jajir) (K.Pr. 61). --tulanwôlᵘ -- m. a pipe-bearer (El.). ¶ jajīri-gaṭh m. (sg. dat. -gaṭas), the upright stem of a hookah, issuing out of the water-receptacle; cf. gaṭh 2. -ṭang m. N. of a kind of pear (L. 350n). -wôñᵘ m. the water of a hookah, through which the tobacco-smoke passes. It is used medicinally as a lotion for burns.
m. an uproar, esp. that caused by a number of children, accompanied by the sound of blows or slaps on the various limbs.
m. prating, jawing, with the object of urging another.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. jokhᵘ, 2 p.p. jachyōv. This verb is used impersonally in tenses formed from the past participles) to work zealously. Cf. jūrun.
m. a written counterfeit, a forgery.
m. N. of a certain small bird with a sweet voice, ? a lark. It is kept as a pet (Śiv. 181).
or jĕl (= جلد) adv. quickly, speedily (Śiv. 478, 1286; H. vi, 16). -jal adv. very quickly, very speedily (Śiv. 971).
m. an embroiderer; a maker of saddle-cloths and rugs (El.).
m. a kind of fringe on a woollen garment or shawl, woven or netted in a fancy pattern.

or jĕlāv m. blazing (cf. ālav); brilliancy, effulgence; flame, blaze, burning of fire (Rām. 1578, 1582, 1613; K. 884); met. brilliancy of character, gloriousness, glory; dignity, dignified appearance (K.Pr. 261). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give effulgence or glory (e.g. to a jewel by polishing, to a person by conferring honour, to a business by making it prosper).
or jĕlᵃd جلد adv. quickly (El., K.Pr. 3, 157; Śiv. 356, 661; Rām. 718, 770, 1078, 1382; H. xii, 15, 23, 24). jald-jald pahān or jald pahān adv. quickly (El.). Cf. jal 2.
f. quickness, speed; haste, hurry. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make speed, to hurry (Śiv. 799).
m. a kind of nut resembling a pistachio. It is much esteemed as a dainty.
(? spelling and gend.) a tax levied on a village on account of expenses of English visitors (L. 415).
m. manifestation; splendour, lustre, effulgence, glory. With emph. y jalŏy (H. vi, 17). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give forth glory, to manifest oneself in glory (H. vi, 7).
m. N. of a certain dangerous internal disease, said to be due to blood-disorder. It is either pneumonia or congestion of the lungs, both of which are called by the same name.
m. a goblet, bowl, cup (El.). ¶ jāma-khôsᵘ m. a large bowl (El.).
or jĕma, i.q. jamā, q.v. --thawun -- m.inf. to make a collection, to pile up, to heap up (Śiv. 1302). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come together, to assemble (Rām. 797).

jĕmā or (Rām. 142) jamāh or (Rām. 690, 820, 1130) jĕmāh m. a collection, congregation; amount, sum total, whole, total (of a whole) (Gr.M.); capital, principal; collection, savings (Gr.M.); the land-tax, the Government demand, land revenue, takrörī jamā (تکرآری جمع), an item of revenue charged against a village, but disputed by the villagers (L. 406, 449). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go together, to gather, to assemble, collect (Rām. 1130). --karun -- m.inf. to collect, accumulate, amass (K.Pr. 246); to add up, add together; to save, store up, lay by (K.Pr. 255, W. 22); to add to a sum already there, to deposit (money in a bank, or the like) (Gr.M.); to credit, to carry to credit in an account. --sapanun -- m.inf. to become assembled, to assemble (Rām. 142, 820). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come together, to assemble (Rām. 363, 690, 1130).

or jyāma m. a garment, robe, gown, vest (YZ. 19, 233, 458, 536; Śiv. 58, 98, 179, 281, 344, 789, etc.; Rām. 39, 119, 156, etc.; K. 421; H. x, 9); a long gown (having from eleven to thirty breadths of cloth in the skirt, which at the upper part is folded into innumerable plaits. The body-part, being double-breasted, is tied in two places at each side). -kan جامکن m. N. of a room adorned with pictures, and the like, found in the houses of the rich. It is properly a room adjoining a bath in which people change their clothes. -takta جامہ تختہ m. a kind of embroidered or flowered woollen shawl or cloth; i.q. jã̄wār, q.v. Cf. jāmawār.
m. a congregational mosque; the main Musalmān Masjid in Śrīnagar (El.).
f. (sg. dat. jamaki), radiance, lustre, sparkle, glitter, refulgence.
f. (sg. dat. -gōṭi), a certain purgative nut (resembling the pistachio nut), croton tiglium. Cf. jaipāl phal.
f. a horoscope, an astrological record of nativity.

f. (sg. dat. jamöʦᵘ̈), a company, body, society, band, party, troop, group, congregated or collective body, assembly, congregation (K.Pr. 86, 207); a meeting, gathering; class, order, rank; in Kāshmīrī, esp. a collection of men in rows, a regiment.
m. a kind of Kashmīr shawl in which the jēgā-design (see jēgā) is interlaced with strips of various colours covered with small flowers (L. 376, 377). Cf. jã̄wār, and jāma-takta, s.v. jāma.
m. (in exchanging, bartering, conversation, etc.) adequacy, suitableness, fitness, being entitled to.

or jamēl f. a leather-bag or wallet; a beggar's wallet (of cloth or any other material). --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to don the beggar's wallet, i.e. to go out begging, to go forth on a begging expedition. Cf. jūlⁱ ʦhunüñᵘ̈, s.v. jūlⁱ.
m. the flare or blazing up of burning straw, or the like. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. a sudden flare or blazing conflagration to take place. -mālā f. a flaring line of fire. Cf. jĕnjĕm.
in jamōth karun m.inf. (amongst Musalmāns) to utter the call or cry summoning the faithful to a solemn religious meeting.
m. lacquer or burnishing material used by jewellers.
f. N. of a river, the river Yamunā (Jumna) in Hindōstān (Śiv. 213, 1057, 1151, 1386, 1489; K. 70 ff., 218, 229, 267, 305, 702, 864).
(? spelling) m. a bull buffalo (L. 360). Cf. mǖ̃shⁱ.
m. the sound of metallic vessels, etc., striking against each other, clang (El. jhan).

(often written jyān) m. (this word is f. in Hindī, see W. 18), the breath of life, vitality; life, spirit, soul, mind (K.Pr. 50; YZ. 8, 22, 62, 140, 152, 212; Śiv. 130, 191, 226, 680; Rām. 67, 156, 310, etc.); animation, vigour, energy, force, stamina; the best part, the essence (of a thing); that which imparts life or beauty, etc. (to a thing); ornament, grace, beauty; a sweetheart, darling (voc. jāna, K.Pr. 86). ¶ jāna-mīr m. prince of (my) life-breath, a darling and worthy son; esp. of some great person (K.Pr. 48); a living being (Rām. 1126). -marg m. one who dies in childhood or before he has reached man's estate. ¶ jāni yār جان یار (for یار جان) m. a soul-friend, a thorough friend (K.Pr. 5).

(often written jyān) adj. c.g. good, excellent, first-rate (K.Pr. 71, 86, 255; Śiv. 54, 239, 431, 707, 1102, 1656, 1712; Rām. 796, 1069, 1262, 1278; K. 984; H. vii, 27); beautiful (YZ. 18, 207; Śiv. 469, 882; Rām. 589, 596, 624, 1330; K. 219); good, right, advisable, proper (K.Pr. 24, 51, 95; Rām. 503); much (in a good sense) (Śiv. 426); as adv., well (Rām. 191, 1227, 1622; H. xi, 17); as interj. jān kyāh, how well! how excellently! (L.V. 89); cf. jwān. -buthᵘ adj. (f. -buʦhᵘ̈), good-looking (El.). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be advisable, proper (to do anything) (Rām. 191, 401); to be right, proper (H. xi, 18); to turn out well (for a person), to result happily (L.V. 85). --pahān -- adj. c.g. moderately good, not altogether good. --pöṭhⁱ -- adv. well, excellently. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. (of rain) to fall fast (Gr.M.).
(? spelling and gender), the population of a village including agriculturists and menials (L. 462).
my life (borrowed from Persian) (K.Pr. 153), see jān 1.
(cf. جانان) adj. c.g. very charming, very excellent, of extreme merit.
m. (sg. dat. janatas), paradise, heaven, the abode of the blessed dead (H. iii, 7; xii, 13, 20-4).

or jānāwār m. (often spelt jyānᵒ), a bird. (jānawār, YZ. 143; Śiv. 158, 502, 1607, 1752; Rām. 314-16, 412, 1198; jānāwār, Śiv. 1721; Rām. 527; H. viii, 1; ix, 1, 3, 5); an animal (jānawār, Rām. 370, 373, 404, 1288). The above is the Hindū spelling, Musalmāns say jānwar, jānawar, or jānawara, q.v. Cf. Gr.M.

m. a garment made of rags sewn together, a patchwork coat, a patched coat, a poor man's ragged garment (K.Pr. 24, 86, 228; Rām. 345). -sᵃʦ m. a tailor who makes coats by sewing rags together; one who makes coats of good material in a similar fashion, a patchworker. -sᵃʦan f. (sg. dat. sᵃʦüñᵃ), the needle used in making patchwork.

or jĕnḍa m. a flag, banner, standard, ensign. -bardār m. a banner-bearer, standard-bearer. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to plant the flag; met. after careful preparation to make oneself firm in any place, course of action, or the like. --dith bĕhun -- m.inf., id. -khān m. 'captain flag', a soldier whose contribution towards a fight is to wave the flag; hence, a cowardly warrior, a poltroon, a shirker. --lāgun -- m.inf. to set up a flag; met. to insist on a claim (H. v, 11).
adj. c.g. having life, living, alive; having power or strength, active; lively, spirited (e.g. of a horse).
m. a kind of iron-bound club used as a weapon by hill Gujurs and herdsmen.
m. the sacred thread worn by Hindūs (L. 261).

(often spelt jĕng) m. fighting; fight, battle, war, combat (K.Pr. 31, 86, 210; Śiv. 571; Rām. 481, 924, 1324, 1420, 1452). --dinⁱ -- m.pl.inf. to give combats, i.e. violently to oppose another with abuse as well as action. --karun -- m.inf. to fight (W. 147). ¶ janga-jang f. mutual combat, wordy warfare. Regarding gend. see Gr.Gr. 75.
adj. c.g. of or pertaining to a forest or wood; born or produced in a forest or wood; uncultivated; wild, savage, uncivilized, barbarian, clownish, boorish. --kiʦᵘ̈ -- f. Edwardsia mollis (El.).
(often written jĕngul) m. (sg. dat. jangalas; pl. nom. jangal), a jungle; forest; in Kāshmīr esp. a mountain forest (YZ. 284; Śiv. 206, 267, 273, 495, etc.; Rām. 201, 388).

in jāni-ādan m. N. of a certain plant growing in the hills and described as possessing leaves that are red and blue on the face and green on the reverse, the ṇīl-kanṭhī of India, Salvia sp. used medicinally as a diuretic (L. 75).

or jĕnjāl m. entanglements, embarrassments, troubles, cares or anxieties (of worldly concerns or engagements) (Śiv. 1695); a teasing, tiring, or troublesome person or business; a plague, pest, bore; in Kāshmīrī, esp. noisy behaviour, speaking loud, shouting out (Śiv. 278); bombast.

adj. c.g. occasioning trouble, embarrassing, troublesome; a troublesome person, one who molests; in Kāshmīrī, esp. one who behaves noisily, one who is in the habit of speaking loudly or wrangling; bombastic.
or janjurᵘ m. a face twisted downwards by the habitual practice of anger, etc., a lowering countenance.
or jĕnjūrⁱ f. (sg. dat. janjūrĕ, etc.), a chain (Śiv. 1017).
f. the eighth lunar day of the dark half of the month of Bādᵃrapĕth (August-September), on which Hindūs celebrate the festival of Kṛṣṇa's (Krishna's) birth (L. 266).
m. demoniacal possession, loss of reason, insanity, madness (El.).
or (Rām. 1496) jānawar, or jānawara m. i.q. jānawār, a bird, q.v. (El., YZ. 398, Rām. 1496).
f. (sg. dat. japi), a sudden leap on to the back of a horse or similar riding animal. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to do this, to leap on to a height.
in --tulun -- m.inf. when someone is detailed to do some work, to worry him by excessive urging to perform it quickly.
(? = جعفری) m. N. of a certain flower, ? the marigold, for which El. gives japhiri m. According to El. there are two varieties, shĕsh-barg j. (six-leaved m.) and makhmal j. (velvet m.) (Rām. 644).
in -- ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to wave or brandish the arm as a threat or challenge to another.
or jĕra adv. in showers, in floods (of tears, etc.) (Śiv. 1588); hence, very much exceedingly (Śiv. 334). Cf. jȧrⁱ 1.
in jāra dyunᵘ m.inf. to drive away or divorce a wife for bad conduct.
adj. c.g. (of a trinket, etc.) bestudded, inlaid, enchased, mounted.
m. the sound of a heavy fall of rain.
m. a lattice, window, casement; an open summer-house or pavilion on the roof of a mansion (K. 716).

or jĕrun conj. 1 (1 p.p. jorᵘ), to inlay or set (with jewels), fix or set (jewels), bestud, enchase, mount (with silver or gold) (Śiv. 169, 1726; Rām. 568). ¶ jorᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. jürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), jewelled, studded with jewels (Śiv. 1640; K. 555, 921, 984).
f. the root of any medicinal herb, a root used as a medicine, a medicinal root.

or jĕshᵉ̆na (cf. جشن) m. a banquet, feast, feasting (K.Pr. 66); a kind of nautch, a kind of dance by professional dancers accompanied by songs and instrumental music (according to El., the dancers are males) (K.Pr. 136, Śiv. 1705).
f. N. of the foster-mother of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna), in Sanskrit Yaśōdā. -nand, m. the darling of Yaśodā, N. of Kṛṣṇa (Śiv. 1423).
. The word 'jasōdā' is borrowed from India. The true Ksh. form of the word is yĕshōdā, q.v.
m. (sg. dat. jastas), zinc, spelter; pewter.
adj. (f. jastüvᵘ̈), made of zinc or pewter.
adj. c.g. made of zinc or pewter.
m. a crowd of multitudes coming and going.

f., i.q. jaṭa 1 (Śiv. 778, 892). -dar m. he who wears matted locks, N. of Śiva (Śiv. 235, 629, 934, 1173). -dār m., id. (Śiv. 153, 379, 770, 918, 1078, 1615). -dörī m., id. (Śiv. 197). -mŏkuṭh m. (sg. dat. -mŏkuṭas or -mŏkaṭas), the crown of the head covered with matted hair. jaṭa-mŏkaṭa-gangā, the Ganges (which issues) from the matted hair on the crown of Śiva's head (Śiv. 892). Cf. ganga-jaṭa, p. 291b, l. 43.

m.pl. the twisted and matted hair of a Hindū ascetic (Śiv. 1120, 1258, 1893; Rām. 112). In Śiv. 1560 the word is sg. and the abl. is jaṭi; cf. jaṭā. -dörī m. he who wears matted locks, N. of Śiva (Śiv. 1046, 1895). -dārawunᵘ n.ag. m., id. (Śiv. 1040). -gaṅgā f. the Ganges, as it issues from the matted locks of Śiva (Śiv. 188); see gang-jaṭa, p. 291b, l. 43. -gŏsôñᵘ m. an ascetic who wears such matted hair. -mŏkuṭh or -mukuṭh m. (dat. sg. -mŏkuṭas or -mŏkaṭas), a diadem composed of matted hair, a crown of the head covered with matted hair (Śiv. 188).
f.pl. plundering, pillaging, or similar action done by a fortuitous crowd of people. -jōsh m. the uproar raised by such a crowd.
m. Nardostachys jatamansi, spikenard (El., on whose authority the gender is put as m.).
m. N. of a vulture who befriended the Hindū hero Rāma. He was mortally wounded in attempting to rescue Sītā when she was carried off by Rāvaṇa (Rām. 317, 405, 441, 526, 534).

f. (sg. dat. jüʦᵘ̈), the hair or down of the body; similar down on anything else; fur (K.Pr. 82, 162); the hairs of fur (cf. brörⁱ-jath, p. 125b, l. 30). --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. having set a person a task, pitilessly to urge him to complete it. --galüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be put to needless and great exertion. --gālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to put another to needless and great exertion.
adv. quickly, speedily, instantly, at once (K.Pr. 87, jaṭ-paṭ).
m. worn out and abandoned (used esp. of books and the like).
f. a little straw sandal or shoe, esp. one that is worn out. Cf. khrāv.

m. a game played by children in the early part of the night of the eighth lunar day of the light half of the Hindū month of Phāgun (February-March) after the ceremony of floating lights on a river. The children go in a crowd begging from house to house and from market to market.
m. (sg. dat. jaṭilis; f. jaṭijᵘ̈), one who wears matted hair, see jaṭa 1.
m. the thickness of a barley corn (a measure of length); met. a very small amount of anything, a jot, a tittle (Śiv. 557).
m. going, in āv ta jāv, coming and going (K.Pr. 18). Cf. āv 1.
m. N. of a certain medicinal plant, stated to be sweet smelling and employed as a stomachic (? = Hindī ajwān, Ligusticum ajowan or Ptychotis ajowan).
in jāvi laʦhᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a bundle of twigs used as a sweeping-brush, a broom.

or jĕwāb جواب m. answer, reply, response (to a letter, writing, saying, or question) (Śiv. 555; Rām. 804; H. iii, 4; xii, 17); a retort, rejoinder; anything answering to another, counterpart, double, pair; return, reward, compensation; discharge, dismissal, congé; refusal (of an offer of marriage, etc.).

or (Śiv. 22) jŏwān or (Śiv. 326) jĕwān جوان adj. c.g. young, youthful, in the prime of manhood or womanhood; vigorous; as subst. c.g. a young man or woman (K.Pr. 87; YZ. 211; W. 48; Śiv. 22, 326); a youth (YZ. 9, 207).
m. a kind of embroidered or flowered woollen shawl or cloth, i.q. jāma-takta, p. 373b, l. 32; cf. jāmawār. -nȧrⁱwār m. a kind of sleeve made of this cloth and worn by well-to-do women.
often spelt jĕwönī f. youth, adolescence, puberty (Rām. 14, 99, 359, 1137, 1625); the season of youth.
m. victory (Śiv. 111, 658), i.q. jai. ¶ jayĕ interj. mayst thou have victory! (Śiv. 1256). This word is really a Sanskrit imperative. -jayĕ-kār, i.q. jai-jai-kār, q.v., s.v. jai.

f. (El. jáí) a place (K.Pr. 87, 165; YZ. 14, 383; Śiv. 180, 519, 1087, 1232, 1330, 1488, 1743; Rām. 202, 8, etc.; K. 956; H. i, 3, 4, etc.); place, room, ground (Śiv. 90, 1716); room, space (K.Pr. 78); position (L.V. 50); the place or proper place for anything (K.Pr. 50, 217; Śiv. 767); a proper place, an opportune moment for doing anything (Rām. 844); a place in which one dwells, a dwelling place (Śiv. 1236; Rām. 57, 72). -shāy (= جائی شی) f. a house with its appurtenances, such as garden, grounds, etc. ¶ jāyĕ sg. dat. commonly used for jāyĕ-manz, in a place (Śiv. 106, 169, 473, 969, 1071, 1136, 1190, 1468, 1618; Rām. 880, 1652, etc.), as in akis jāyĕ, in a certain place; prath jāyĕ, in every place (Śiv. 1534; Rām. 34, 105, 108, 472, 1715, 1716; K. 862); yith jāyĕ, in this place, here; similarly in the plur. dat. sārĕnᵘ̈y jāyĕn, in all places, everywhere (Gr.M.). --jayĕ -- adv. in each place, in every place, here and there (Śiv. 719, 885, 1242, 1480). -phyurᵘ m. to change one's place; esp. (of a sick person) to go away for change of air. -pĕṭh anun m.inf. to bring to the place (of execution), to execute (El. jáí pĕṭh anun). -yimdād جائیء امداد f. a place of help, a circumstance in which help is required, need of assistance (Rām. 381).
m. a large three- or four-storied house, a mansion.
adj. c.g. (of the body) covered with much down or short hair (Gr.Gr. 135); (of anything inanimate) covered with down like the down of the body. Cf. jath.

m. an ornament worn on the turban, consisting of a band of velvet about six inches long and two broad, embroidered, ornamented with precious stones, and bearing an almond-shaped gold plate; cf. bom bur-par, p. 108a, l. 31. See L. 375 for particulars as to the spread of imitations of the shape of the jēgā in the pattern of shawls and carpets (Rām. 1457).
m. a prison, a jail (the English word) (K.Pr. 245).
? m. a row, string, line; a chain (Rām. 16).
m. great brilliancy, blazing brightness (Śiv. 1843). Cf. jamjam.

m. wringing the hands in extreme agitation, perturbation, the being beside oneself with fear, sorrow, or the like. --anun -- m.inf. to bring (i.e. commence) wringing the hands in extreme agitation, to be at one's wits' ends for fear, sorrow, or the like. ¶ jīris-pĕṭh pyonᵘ m.inf. to fall on such agitation, to be filled with agitation and to have to act at once, to be agitated and to have no time to make up one's mind. Cf. jöris-pĕṭh pyonᵘ, s.v. jôrᵘ.
f. a heap of straw and other rubbish, a rubbish heap; spilling over of excess from a piled heap. Cf. jöṭhil.

m. (sg. dat. jiyĕs), a suff. of respect, i.q. juv and jiy, q.v. This is the Hindī form of the word, and is probably borrowed from India proper. Cf. brahmā-jī, p. 121a, l. 38. It is sometimes added directly to the noun, as in bābā-jī (Śiv. 555), nārad-jī (Śiv. 639), shivanāth-jī (Śiv. 131), vishn-jī (Śiv. 1357), and sometimes to an obl. form, as in krushna-jī (Śiv. 110), narasimha-jī (Śiv. 857); shiva-jī (Śiv. 516).

m. the liver; looked upon as the seat of the affections, equivalent to the English heart (YZ. 140; Śiv. 329, 1005). --dazun -- m.inf. the liver to burn or to be inflamed, to be heart-broken (YZ. 298, 514). --gālun -- m.inf. to cause one's liver to melt, to show affectionate service (to = path) (Rām. 192). -gōshĕ جگر گوشہ m. a lobe of the liver; met. one dear or beloved, a darling (YZ. 152). -trāsh جگر تراش ? m. cutting of the liver, the liver being cut to pieces, rending of the heart (Rām. 1539).
(? جلو or جلب), f. in --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. tightly to squeeze a horse's flanks between the heels when riding him (k.381). Cf. jilb.

or jilⁱb (? جلب) f. a horse's bridle, rein [drāv jilbi, he went out to (stand in attendance by) the horse's flank (cf. K.Pr 261)]. jilⁱbi pakun m.inf. to go by the flank, to curvet (of a horse) (K. 1008). Cf. jilav.

m. (sg. dat. jildas), the skin; hide, leather; binding of a book; a book; a volume of a book (Gr.M.); (regarding the gend. of this word, which is f. in Hindī, see W. 18). -gorᵘ m. a bookbinder (W. 111).
f. the large carpet-like body-cloth of a horse, elephant, or the like, a horse-cloth, housings. Cf. julⁱ.
f. a small piece of anything; a small part of any action; a short space or moment of time. Cf. jumbish.

m. one of the Genii, a male fairy; an elf, spirit; a demon, an ogre (K.Pr. 84; Rām. 863, 892). --aʦun -- m.inf. a demon to enter (a person), to be possessed by a demon. --ʦānȧnⁱ -- m.pl.inf. demons to be caused to enter; esp. of some very prosperous person, to become possessed by devils. ¶ jina-gāra f. 'demon longing', i.e. greediness or voracity like that of a demon. -phrôtᵘ m. a demon-boor, i.e. a fellow who conducts himself like a demon, a blackguard, a barbarian.
m. a bier with a corpse upon it; a bier; a corpse; (in Kāshmīrī) a long-limbed ablebodied fool.
m. genus, kind, sort; goods, articles (as a group; hence, in sg.) (Gr.M.); cf. gair-jins, p. 296b, l. 21. ba-jinsan adv. in kind, in detail, to all appearance (Rām. 346).
m. an uproar, loud shouts made by a crowd against some unpopular measure.
m. the body (with limbs and members) (Gr.M.).
m. strength of body. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is able-bodied, strong.
f. a small section, fragment, piece, particle, bit; (of time) an instant.
f. (sg. dat. jīʦᵘ̈), victory (Gr.M., El. makes the word m.). --prāwüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to gain a victory, to conquer (him = tas pĕṭh) (Gr.M.).

m. a form of address, used --˚, i.q. jī and juv, qq.v.; as in brahmā-jiy (Śiv. 485; sg. ag. 679; dat. 717, 718). nārad-jiy (Śiv. 807; sg. ag. 796, 802, 879, 911). shiwa-jiy (Śiv. 679, 683, 811, 845, 1184; sg. dat. 992).
jñönī, learned spelling of gyān, gyönī, respectively, qq.v.
or jochᵘ adj. (f. jö̆chᵘ̈ or jüchᵘ̈), a shabbily dressed person, a male sloven; one whose actions are slovenly or ungraceful, a clumsy fellow, a lout.
m. a malevolent charm, an evil spell (Rām. 869, jyôdāh, with suff. of indef. art.). -gar or (Rām. 866) jyôdugār m. one who knows how to cast such spells, a wizard.
m. land granted rent-free or revenue-free in perpetuity (L. 305). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to extract a jögīr, i.e. to make a grant of land rent- or revenue-free (K.Pr. 33).

m. impeding or stopping another's work by conspiring or uniting with others for this purpose. --milawun -- m.inf. (of a number of people collected together) deliberately to stop some work, so as to prevent its accomplishment --ʦhunun -- m.inf. violently, or by robbery, or the like, to stop another's work. ¶ jaga-bogᵘ m. deliberately to stop another person when speaking, or the like, to interrupt and stop a conversation.
adj. c.g. ignorant, illiterate (Gr.M.); an ignorant fool (K.Pr. 46).
m. a fever resulting from chill, characterized by inward burning and outward chill (horses are specially liable to it). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. an attack of such fever to come on.
f. network; lace, bobbinet; a lattice, grating, trellis-work.
m. N. of the country of Jamū (Jummoo), lying to the south-east of the Kashmīrvalley. ¶ jȧmⁱ-wāla adj. c.g. born or produced in Jamū.
(often written jyönī) f. goodness, excellence; welfare (Gr.M.).
in jönⁱ-jān جآنِ جان m. the whole self, body, breath, and soul considered as an entirety.
in jōr dyunᵘ m.inf. to count, add up. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take the total, to test the number of any collection of articles, to check the total.

m. a pair, couple (K. 538); one of a pair, a fellow, mate, match, counterpart. This word and jūrⁱ are generally, but not always, used with reference to animate objects, while horᵘ, q.v. is generally used for a pair of inanimate objects. Jōra and jūrⁱ cannot be used interchangeably. Jōra is most used with numerals, as in akh jōra (but also akh jūrⁱ), one pair; zᵃh jōra, two pairs, and so on; but kōtar-jūrⁱ, a pair of pigeons; gurⁱ-jūrⁱ, a pair of horses, and so on; both atha-jōra and atha-jūrⁱ, the two hands, with slightly different meanings; see p. 58b, l. 27. It is also looked upon as the singular of the plural zᵃh, two. See Gr.Gr. 81, 82. Cf. jūrⁱ. With the suff. of the indef. art. we have jōrāh, see bel. -bôjᵘ m. (of a man or child) a mate, a fellow; one who is alike another in all particulars and actions. -judöyⁱ f. separation or disassociation of a pair, esp. the dissolution of the union between husband and wife, the sorrow caused to one by the death of the other (K.Pr. 231). -püṭᵘ̈ f. a double shawl; a shawl made up of two thicknesses or two widths joined together. ¶ jōrāh c.g., pl. any pair, some pair (Rām. 447); about two. This word is declined in the plur., c.g. pl. ag. jōrāhau (Gr.Gr. 81, 93). -khanḍā c.g. about two, but a little less (Gr.Gr. 81, 93).
m. (really the same as jōra 1 in a special sense), a suit (of clothes) (Gr.M.).

m. a kind of stocking or sock reaching only to the ankles (El.). -gorᵘ m. a stocking-maker; a stocking-seller. -salay f. a needle for making stockings, a knitting-needle. -sāz m. a stocking weaver (El.).

or jyörī adj. c.g. running, flowing (Śiv. 205, 532, 1892, 1893; Rām. 722); proceeding, progressing; current, usual; continuing, continuous, permanent; issued and in force (of an order) (Gr.M.); opened and still open (of a school, or the like) (Gr.M.); as adv. in streams, continually, without cessation (Rām. 1735).
adj. (f. jürᵘ̈), mounted (as jewels) (El.). Cf. jarun.
m. in:--jöris pĕṭh pyonᵘ m.inf. to fall into agitation on the non-success of some work, when no other means of carrying it out appears to be available. Cf. jīrispĕṭh pyonᵘ, s.v. jēra.

m. boiling; effervescence; heat (Śiv. 1031; Rām. 533, 1733); excitement (K.Pr. 103, YZ. 204); passion, emotion (Śiv. 844); lust; fervour, ardour, zeal, vehemence (Rām. 713, 1387, 1392, 1459); enthusiasm; frenzy; anger, rage (Rām. 329, 689, 818, 1266). --anun -- m.inf. excitement, emotion, etc., to come or take place. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. (in cooking) to boil, to bring to a boil.
f. (sg. dat. jūʦᵘ̈), light (Śiv. 1881), esp. the smokeless light given forth by phosphorescent wood, or the like, phosphorescence. Cf. jūtⁱ and jūth.
m. a great talker of nonsense, a babbler.
f. a pile of refuse, a rubbish heap (of waste straw, wood, etc.). Cf. jēṭil.
m. an ascetic wearing matted locks (see jaṭa); hence, a person under no vow of asceticism who parades himself like a mad ascetic with matted locks.
or jōy جوئی f. a rivulet, stream (El. jwí; Śiv. 506, Rām. 1501); a water-channel (Gr.M.). ¶ jōyĕ-jōyĕ adv. in floods (Rām. 1483).

or (H. vii, 16) judāh adj. c.g. separated, apart (YZ. 191, Rām. 1304); separate, distinct; apart (from), free (from), void (of) (Rām. 1055); apart, broken in two, split apart, split open (Rām. 1709). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go apart, become separated (H. vii, 16). --karun -- m.inf. to separate (El.).
f. separation, parting (K.Pr. 231; YZ. 142, 557; Rām. 1026; H. vii, 16); absence; estrangement, discord (Rām. 1616).
(? spelling) in juga juga, dancing (a bird or similar object) up and down (e.g. on the hand) (K.Pr. 37).
m. (sg. dat. jugatas), gain, esp. sudden and unexpected gain of wealth without exertion, a valuable windfall.
f. a triangular gold ornament studded with jewels worn by women on each side of the forehead.

m. (sg. voc. jōgi, Rām. 1778; pl. dat. jōgĕn, Rām. 73, 784, 1735), a kind of Hindū ascetic, a Yōgī, esp. a member of the kan- phaṭā or 'split-eared' Yōgīs (Śiv. 206, 528, 529, 588, etc.; Rām. 96, 1134). -pāthchāh (= یوگ پادشاہ) m. 'the King of Yōgīs,' N. of a certain thorny creeper growing on the lower slopes of the hills. In medicine it is used as an antiphlogistic (L. 76). -pöthᵃr m. the Yōgī character--one of the stock characters in a theatrical performance. -pāwurᵘ m. a Yōgī's slipper, a magic slipper, by wearing which a Yōgī is supposed to go from place to place through the air.
or juzᵃwa (= جرو) m. a part or section of a book consisting of a fixed number (e.g. eight) of leaves; a quire (of paper); a printer's sheet.

f. (sg. dat. jōlĕ), a bag, sack, pouch, wallet; esp. a beggar's wallet. --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to don the beggar's wallet, i.e. to go out begging, to go forth on a begging expedition. Cf. jambēl ʦhunüñᵘ̈, s.v. jambēl.
m. 'the day of the congregation', Friday (on which day Musalmāns assemble to pray at the great mosque). Cf. jumā.
m. the whole, aggregate, total. --ālam جملہ عالم m. the whole world; He who is the (source of the) entire universe, God (H. i, 13).
f. motion, movement; in Kāshmīrī, a small piece, a bit, of any inanimate object. Cf. jimish.

m. the bell-shaped pendant of an earring; an earring with one or more of these pendants (K.Pr. 153). -bölī m. an earring adorned with pendants. -horᵘ m. a pair of earrings with pendants. -kan m. a single one of such earrings.

m. one who has a big belly, a corpulent person with a big appetite. -müʦᵘ̈ f. a corpulent and gluttonous woman, who greedily fills her belly at the expense of the other members of the household, a greedy slut.
adj. c.g. big-bellied and greedy, voracious, gluttonous.
m. the belly, esp. a big belly.
adj. c.g. impulsive, emotional, insisting on having one's own way, one who will have his own way.
f. insistence on having one's own way, intolerance of others' wishes.
m. N. of a gambling game, in which one player holds a number of cowries or similar objects in his hand and the other bets whether the number is even (Pers. جفت) or odd (Pers. طاق).
f. a small hut or hovel.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. juryōv), to come to hand, to be got, be had, be obtained, procured, earned.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. jūrᵘ, 2 p.p. jūryōv. This verb is used impersonally in tenses formed from the past participles) to work zealously and expertly. Cf. jakhun.

f. (sg. dat. jōrĕ), two things, a pair of any two similar things. This word is the same in meaning as jōra 1, but the two words are not interchangeable, one being preferred in some cases, and the other in others; see jōra 1. Thus we have dā̃da-jūrⁱ, a pair of bullocks (K.Pr. 187); atha-jūrⁱ, the two hands; kōtar-jūrⁱ, a pair of pigeons; kȧrⁱ-jūrⁱ, a pair of bracelets. We have both akh jōra and akh jūrⁱ meaning a pair; see p. 20a, l. 8. jōrĕ jōrĕ adv. in pairs (K. 1007). --mārañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to become unbridled, uncurbed, unrestrained. ¶ jōri-judöyⁱ f. separation of a pair, esp. the separation of husband and wife, the sorrow caused to one by the death of the other (cf. jōra-judöyⁱ, K.Pr. 231), (YZ. 557); discord between a married couple (Rām. 1616). -shāla m. a double shawl (a grand and expensive garment) (Śiv. 281, 1687).
f. a suit of clothes, i.q. jōra 2 (Gr.M.).
f. (sg. dat. jūʦᵘ̈), the light given forth by a lamp, fire, or the like, glare, flare. Cf. jūtⁱ and jōth.
m. (in a running race) touching the winning post, the winning of a race.
or jyūtish m. a Hindū astrologer (L. 302, Śiv. 479).
f. light, esp. the illumination given forth by scented lamps in a Hindū temple, or the like, at the time of worship. Cf. jōth and jūth.

or jyuv m. a form of address, a term of respect, Sir, Master, used --˚ after a proper name, as hē nārān-juv ho, Sir, Nārān (Gr.Gr. 96); voc. hata juwa, hie, Sir (K.Pr. 80).
