Similarly, in Śiv. we have brahmā-juv (697, 848, sg. dat; 802, 1116, 1142); krushna-juv (853); nārad-juv (1336, sg. ag.); rāma-juv (1040, 1781); vidura-juv (1328, sg. gen.); vishnu-juv (581), all these being proper names. In Rām. we have brahmā-j(y)uv (597, sg. dat.; 704, 1745, ag.; 1086, 1177, gen.); lȧkhⁱman-jyuv (380, 1172, sg. ag.); cf. jiy. This word should be distinguished from zuv, which means 'life'.
m. (sg. dat. juwaras), the edible seeds of a kind of water-lily, the Euryale ferox (El. jewar, so L. 72, 345; Śiv. 1808). ¶ juwar-gōjĕ f.pl. the kernels of this seed.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. jüʦᵘ̈ladiñ), i.q. jaʦᵃl. Cf. atha-jᵒ, p. 58b, l. 33.
adj. c.g. very good, excellent. Cf. jān 2.
adj. more, additional (Gr.M.); superfluous, redundant; too much, excessive; with emph. y, kam yā jyāday, less or more (H. ii, 12). Cf. kam 1.
or jyōtī f. light; esp. bright light, brilliance, glory (L.V. 76). -rṻph m. he whose form is all glorious light, an epithet of Śiva (Śiv. 104, 305, 512, 981, etc.). -sŏrṻph m., id. (Śiv. 346).

. The ninth consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Rōman character, the first when written in the Śāradā or the Nāgarī character, and the twenty-eighth when written in the Perso-Arabic character. Its Kāshmīrī name is kōvka. It is sounded like an English k, but without any trace of the aspiration which is often heard in English when that letter is uttered. It is also used to represent the sound of the Arabic q ق (qāf), which, in Kāshmīrī, occurs only in words borrowed directly or indirectly from that language. In such cases the q ق is usually pronounced as k in speaking Kāshmīrī. Some writers, however, represent it by kh. ¶ The aspirate of k is kh کہ, which is the second consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet when written in the Śāradā or the Nāgarī character. Its Kāshmīrī name is khŏnⁱ kha. This aspirate kh is also used to represent the Arabic and Persian ḵẖ خ, which occurs only in words borrowed from those languages. In such cases, the ḵẖ خ is pronounced as the ordinary aspirated kh in speaking Kāshmīrī. Except in a few isolated words, such as ʦọ̆kᵘ, sour, when k is followed by ü-mātrā, by y, or by ĕ, it is changed to c. Thus, batukᵘ, a duck, fem. batᵘ̈cᵘ̈; √thak-, be weary, 2 p.p. thacyōv; nyukᵘ, thin, nicĕr, thinness (Gr.Gr. 30; Gr.M., p. 23). Similarly, except in the case of a few isolated words, such as khū̃khᵘ, speaking nasally, kh, when followed by any of these letters, becomes ch. Thus, họ̆khᵘ, dry, fem. hö̆chᵘ̈; √likh-, write, 2 p.p. lichyōv; tryukhᵘ, clever, trichĕr, cleverness (ib.).
f.pl. the two forearms, from the elbows to the fingers. --mēnañĕ -- f. pl. inf. 'to measure the forearms'; hence, to struggle with the forearms against the forearms, to wrestle at arm's length.

? f. N. of a garment worn by men, a long gown with flaps in the skirt. The skirt and breast are open, and sometimes has slits in the armpits. It resembles the alkhölikh, q.v., but is fastened with strings instead of buttons (Rām. 976).
in kabā-kūṭᵘ  m. an impalement post, the post on which a criminal condemned to death is impaled.
m. roasted meat, collops, or slices, or small pieces of meat roasted on a skewer or spit, and then treated with grease (K.Pr. 200). Cf. lĕjĕ-kabāba, s.v. lë̆jᵘ̈.

f. (sg. dat. kabaṭi), a boy's game, the kabaḍḍī of India proper. It is a kind of prisoner's base. A boy enters the territory of the rival party and runs through it. He must cry 'kabaṭh' the whole time, and as long as he does so without taking breath he cannot be made a prisoner.
f. jaundice, i.q. kāmal 1 and kã̄bal.

f. N. of a certain medicinal plant, Solanum nigrum, used as an antiperiodic (L. 71, kámbe; 76, kambai; El. kámbeí); i.q. kāmal 2. ¶ kā̃bayĕ-byôlᵘ m. its seed, used as medicine. -pan m. its leaf. -ras m. its juice. -wạthᵃr m. its leaf.
(? spelling and gend.), a kind of grass, the dub grass of India (L. 71).
m. a family (El.); a man's wife; a woman's husband (Rām. 265); the members of a family (Rām. 276, 1425). -krônᵘ, family and relations (Rām. 1780).
adj. c.g. one who makes or sells roast meat; met. an evilly conducted person, who is of an angry and miserly disposition, and who is at the same time addicted to other vices.

m. acceptance; consent, assent; recognition, sanction; admission, acknowledgment; choice (El.); that to which God has consented, one's fate (K.Pr. 25). --karun -- m.inf. to accept (El.); to choose (El.).
in kabz-bandī قبضبندی f. constipation, costiveness (El.).
m. a grasp, clutch (of the hand); possession, occupancy; the handle or hilt (of a sword); a hinge; a sheath (El.).
m. rawness, greenness; (of food) rawness, uncookedness; immaturity; incompleteness.

spelt kachy in Śiv. 500 m. (sg. dat. kachas), the short grass of the field, green grass (esp. the kind that grows in damp soil) (K.Pr. 43, L. 463, W. 144, Śiv. 500), met. a trifle (K.Pr. 181). -nĕnd f. the first of the four khushābas or weedings by hand of a rice field, i.q. arīʦar (L. 463; cf. 327). ¶ kacha-döñᵘ̈ f. (for kacha-dāñĕ, 'kacha-paddy'), a kind of grass that grows plentifully in the Valley of Kashmīr. Its pods are eaten by children and by persons reduced to poverty. See RT.Tr. i, 211 ff. (I, 36 ff.) for an instance of its use. Cf. K.Pr. 43.
m. (sg. dat. kācas), a carrot, Daucus carota (El.).
or (K. 605) kã̄kshā f. wish, desire, longing (K. 605, 623, 798, 1114, 1127, 1134).
or kachīrī f. a court of justice. These are the words as spelt by El. In India the word is kacahrī.
m. hardness, toughness (of the woody condition reached by vegetables, radishes, or the like, allowed to grow old before they are plucked).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kỗchᵘ), to wish, want, desire, long for (K.Pr. 69; Śiv. 319, 1107; Rām. 1213). kỗchᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. kö̃chᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), wished for, desired.
in lȧchⁱ āradith kȧchⁱ ʦaṭun, a jingle of lȧchⁱ, and meaning 'by a thing of small moment' as opposed to lȧchⁱ, 'by a hundred thousand (efforts).' Perhaps based on kach.
in kaci-pūtᵘ m. a young he-goat, a male kid. Cf. kacyulᵘ 2.
f. want of experience (in anything), ignorance due to want of practice (K.Pr. 76, kachal).
(? spelling and gender), the Himalayan spruce, Picea morinda, i.q. röyil, q.v. (L. 79, 80, kachil).
m. a goat; met. a foolish fellow with a long scanty beard. Cf. kaci-pūtᵘ, s.v. kaci.
or kadd قد m. size, stature, height (El., Gr.M., YZ. 12, 229).
m. a representative (Gr.Gr. 10), a paid representative engaged on behalf of someone to supervise a particular work, e.g. sowing or reaping a certain area, a work-overseer. Cf. kādᵃr.
m. the bed of a river, a river channel, the section of a river bed from bank to bank, the width of a river (Gr.Gr. 10).
m. the stalk or stem of a reed, grass, or the like, straw. In the compound with dan 5 (p. 221a, l. 13) the word is spelt kāḍ. ¶ kā̃ḍa-bôrᵘ m. a load or bundle of straw, reed-stems, etc.
m. a man's length, the stature of a man (as a measure of length) (Rām. 632, zangan kaḍun kāḍ, to stretch oneself the whole length of one's body. So K. 119).
m. a section, part in general; a cluster, bundle, multitude (Śiv. 32).

m. the foot; a footstep, step, pace (El.); (of a horse) his paces, mode of going (K.Pr. 71); a footprint, the mark of a foot (Śiv. 1666). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to set forth (H. x, 11, 12). --tulun -- m.inf. to raise the footstep; walk vigorously, step out (K.Pr. 46; Rām. 1648; L.V. 99). --trāwun -- m.inf. to put down the foot, to walk, to step forward (Śiv. 496, 1088; cf. 1849; H. iv, 5).

f.pl. (Gr.Gr. 118), scolding, blaming, finding fault with (a servant, a child, or the like). The f.pl. of kaḍun also takes the form of this word. kaḍañĕ-pösᵃrañĕ f. pl. inf. to scold, to blame, as ab.
f. pulling out; hence, using up, expending, used --˚ as in dŏha-ᵒ (see dŏh), dana-ᵒ (see dana 1), dyāra-ᵒ (see dyār), qq.v.
adj. c.g. lazy, one who dawdles at work.

also (vill.) karun conj. 1 (1 p.p. koḍᵘ, pl.f. kajĕ; 2 p.p. kajyōv), to pull out, drag out, pluck out, root up (K.Pr. 33, 175; YZ. 569; Śiv. 124, 1111, 1462; Rām. 849; H. x, 13; K. 432); to take out, extract, bring out (K.Pr. 64, 94; YZ. 104, 454; Śiv. 1693; Rām. 1523; H. viii, 4, 11, 12); to take out (from a receptacle) (H. viii, 7, 10; xii, 17); to take out, withdraw (e.g. money from a bank) (K.Pr. 26); to bring forth, bring out, lead forth (H. iii, 4, 8; xii, 1); to draw out, entice out (of a place) (Rām. 375); to tear out, or off, dislocate (H. viii, 7); to tear off, pull off, strip (cf. dāla) (Śiv. 1329, Rām. 1233); to take off, detach (something fastened to another) (H. viii, 10); to take off (clothes) (H. v, 9; xii, 6, 7); to draw (a sword) (Rām. 411; H. viii, 13; x, 7; K. 33); to pull, drag (Śiv. 830; cf. broḍᵘ); to drive out, turn out, cast out, expel, banish; (Śiv. 706; Rām. 1167; H. iv, 2; viii, 11); to release, let go (Śiv. 1285); to deduct (cf. p. 155a, l. 29); to extract (e.g. venom from a wound) (Gr.M.); to drive away (weariness, etc.) (Śiv. 1752, 1867); to dig out; to accomplish, complete, effect; to pluck (fruit, vegetables, etc.) (K.Pr. 10, 80; Rām. 1283); to find out, bring to light, invent, discover; to strike (a balance); to bring out (a person's qualities), to train, bring up (a person, horse, etc.) (cf. p. 122b, l. 3); to bring out, produce, display (Śiv. 1299; H. x, 2, 12; xii, 15); to let out, give utterance to, utter (Śiv. 1907); to extract (a passage), to quote (Gr.M.); to experience (trouble, adversity, etc.) (Rām. 419); (of a period of time) to pass (it) somehow or other, to manage to spend (it), to while (it) away (K.Pr. 117, Rām. 1740); (generally) to pass (time) (H. viii, 3, 11; x, 11; xii, 4, 5, 11). This verb occurs very frequently in idiomatic expressions, of which the following are only a few examples. Many others will be found elsewhere in this Dictionary:-- ¶ āh kaḍun, to sigh (YZ. 494); armān-- --, to drive out longing, to achieve one's long-desired object (Śiv. 706, 1655, 1830); atha-- --, to pull the hand (Śiv. 1462, YZ. 439); dŏh-- --, to pass the day somehow or other, to while it away (K.Pr. 117); dēwôlᵘ-- --, to become bankrupt (Gr.M.); kāḍ-- --, to stretch one's whole length, to extend the limbs (Rām. 632, K. 119); kruh kaḍȧnⁱ, to be at the point of death; kash-- --, to pull a bow, draw a bow, prepare to discharge an arrow (Rām. 117, 123, 1271); to serve (a person) to his complete satisfaction; mūla-- --, to pull up by the roots (Gr.M.; Rām. 929, 1375, 1626); tāna tāna-- --, to pull off limb after limb, to tear limb from limb (Rām. 698, 1405); ṭās-- --, to make the sound of a slap; to smack the lips (?) (K.Pr. 138); to spend to the last farthing; ʦopᵘ----, to take a bite out of something (K.Pr. 238); ʦörith-- --, to quote (from a book) (Gr.M.); wani-- --, to recognize (a person or thing) as (so-and-so or such-and-such) (Śiv. 950). ¶ galatī kaḍüñᵘ̈, to pick out mistakes, criticize (Gr.M.); wŏṭh-- --, to leap (Śiv. 998); zĕv-- --, to thrust out the tongue, to put it into position for immediate speech (K. 508). ¶ koḍᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. küḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), pulled out; expelled, banished, and so on with all the meanings of kaḍun. küḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ kath, an extract (from a letter) (Gr.M.). ¶ kaḍith hāwun m.inf. to produce and show (Rām. 670, 1466). --nyunᵘ -- m.inf. to take out and carry away, to carry out, to carry away (K. 57, 69, 191, 254). --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to cast out altogether, to expel, drive out (W. 85; Rām. 148, 257, 1391, 1608, 1695); to take off, doff (clothes) (H. x, 9).

kā̃durᵘ 2, or kā̃dᵘ̈rᵘ̈ m. a large kind of jar, wrapped round with grass or twigs, and often plastered with mud, used for storing grain or as a receptacle for articles in frequent use. Cf. pp. 109b, l. 30 and 230a, l. 2.

also written kadal m. a bridge (Śiv. 1830). See El. s.v. for a full account of the mode in which bridges are made in Kashmīr. The principle is that of a cantilever. -onᵘ m. a blind man who sits on a bridge to beg from passers by (who for his selfish ends blocks the traffic, and who gets out of the way only when he hears approaching footsteps); met. any selfish person who in every way pursues his own object without consideration for others. --ʦaṭun -- m.inf. to cut a bridge; met. (of a mischievous and extravagant wife) altogether to hinder her husband from crossing over to the other side (where prosperity and peace are to be had) (K.Pr. 70). ¶ kạdᵃla-bal m. the bathing place on the bank of a river and close by a bridge. -kānul m. the main beams that support the floor of the wooden cantilever bridges used in Kashmīr; cf. kānul. -kūṭᵘ m. the beams (in general) of a bridge. -ṭhoṭhᵘ m. the central pier supporting a long Kashmīr bridge. It is usually built of stone or brick.
or (Rām. 18)kadürᵘ̈ m. greatness, dignity, honour (Śiv. 497); rank (El.); doing honour, honouring (Rām. 18); (in estimating) the value or worth (e.g. of a precious stone) (K.Pr. 123).
m. one who wants work- people for any special work, an employer of workmen or workwomen, such as a large farmer who wants people for reaping, or the like. Cf. kād.
also spelt kā̃durᵘ 1 m. (f. kā̃dᵃrĕñ, q.v.), a baker (of bread or of other articles; cf. p. 140b, l. 28) (Gr.Gr. 148; K.Pr. 20, sg. dat. kā̃dᵃris; W. 18, 114).
also spelt kã̄durĕñ f. a baker's wife; a female baker. Cf. kā̃dᵃr (Gr.Gr. 39).
m. resinousness, the condition of possessing resinous sap (cf. kā̃golᵘ 1); cf. L. 80 kanglan, the white resin of the blue pine, used as an application for wounds.
adj. (f. kā̃güjᵘ̈), full of tarry sap (e.g. soft fir-wood), and hence easily inflammable.

or kā̃gürᵘ̈ or kā̃gᵃr f. (sg. dat. kã̄grĕ or kã̄garĕ, abl. kã̄gri), the portable brazier, or kāngrī, much used in Kashmīr (K.Pr. kángár, 129, 131, 178; káṅgrí, 50, 128, 129). For particulars see El. s.v. kángri; L. 70, 250, kangar; and K.Pr. 129. The word is a fem. dim. of kang, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 37). ¶ kā̃gri-khŏphᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a worn-out brazier. -khôrᵘ m. the outer half (made of woven twigs) of a brazier, remaining after the inner earthenware bowl has been broken or removed; see khôrᵘ. -kŏnḍolᵘ m. the circular earthenware bowl of a brazier, which contains the burning fuel. -köñᵘ̈ f. the covering of woven twigs outside the earthenware bowl of a brazier; see köñᵘ̈ 2.
f. (sg. dat. küshᵘ̈), the testing of gold by its colour (ascertained by rubbing on a touchstone). Cf. kah-wüṭᵘ̈.

or kah card. c.g. (pl. dat. kāhan, Śiv. 522, L.V. 95), eleven (Gr.Gr. 76); kāh, Rām. 1740; kah, K.Pr. 91, 95, 153; YZ. 82; kahai, only eleven (K.Pr. 97, W. 124). As a rule kah is used in the Musalmān dialect and kāh in the Hindū dialect. --shĕth -- card. c.g. eleven hundred. With kāh, hath becomes shĕth (Gr.Gr. 84, Rām. 740-1). ¶ kāha-nēthᵃr m. N. of a certain Hindū birth-ceremony. On the eleventh day after birth (if all goes well) the mother ceases to be impure. The kāh-nēthᵃr ceremony is then performed. A Brāhmaṇ priest is summoned, and the mother drinks the five products of a cow. The seven birth-room vessels (see hurⁱ-lë˘jⁱ, p. 346b, l. 41) are filled with food of which relatives and friends partake. A tree is traced in chalk upon the wall, and the family astrologers cast the child's horoscope (see L. 259, kah netar). -nôwᵘ m. he who possesses eleven names; esp. the Hindū God Rudra (a form of Śiva) who appears under eleven forms, each of which again is a Rudra. The usual list of the names of these eleven Rudras is, in Sanskrit, Ajaikapad, Ahir- budhnya, Hara, Nirṛta, Īśvara, Bhuvana, Aṅgāraka, Ardha-kētu, Mṛtyu, Sarpa, and Kapālin. -röthᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. N. of a present sent by a Hindū to his daughter's father-in-law and other relations on the eleventh day after the death of his father or other senior relation. It is on this day that the śrāddha ceremony for the deceased is performed.
m. watering of fields, whether sown or not, by sprinkling (either from rain, or from reservoirs). Cf. kö̃bari-kāh, p. 382b, l. 13.
f. (sg. dat. köshᵘ̈), the eleventh day of a lunar fortnight (according to the Hindū almanac) (Gr.Gr. 69; cf. gāḍ, p. 276a, l. 37).

f. a lace made of leather, a strip of leather used as a thread for sewing together the component parts of leather articles (such as shoes, bellows, or the like) (H. xi, 14). ¶ kāha tārañĕ f. pl. inf. 'to pass the laces over', i.e. to sew leather goods with this leather lace.
(for قہر) force, power, vehemence, severity; rage, fury, wrath; in Kāshmīrī, esp. anger against a servant for some fault or impropriety. Cf. kahᵃr.
adj. c.g. very wrathful, furious with rage (Rām. 309). Cf. kahᵃr.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. kaharyōv), to become rough, coarse, hard; (of a person's nature) to become hard, harsh; (of food by bad frying) to become hard, to be fried to a chip. kaharyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. kaharyē-müʦᵘ̈), become harsh, hard, etc., as ab.
m. (sg. dat. kahatas), drought, scarcity, dearth; failure of crops; famine.
m. Lactuca sativa (El.); cf. hand. -khorᵘ m. N. of a certain edible fungus, Hydnum coralloides. It grows in rotten wood, and in the burnt-out hollows of Picea Morinda (L. 73 káho khur).
m. coffee (roasted, or roasted and ground, or the decoction); in Kāshmīrī, sweetened tea (the liquid) (L. 254, 464).
f. (sg. dat. kahwacĕ), a touchstone (for testing gold) (K.Pr. 206; Rām. 1609, dat.). Cf. kah 1.
adv. inter. by what means? how? (L.V. 108). Cf. kĕhō 2.
m. (amongst Musalmāns) the offering made on the eleventh solar day of a lunar month. This word is also a form of köhyumᵘ, q.v. used by Musalmāns. Cf. kāh 1.
m. force, violence, vehemence, severity; rage, fury, wrath, vengeance. Cf. dayĕ-kahᵃr, p. 266a, l. 16, and kahār.
m. (sg. dat. kāhᵃrubāhas), 'straw-attracting,' yellow amber; (in Kāshmīrī) a loadstone, a magnet (Gr.M.).
adv. how?, in what manner? (poet.) (Śiv. 1624). -tām adv. somehow or other (poet.) (K. 1119). -tāmath adv., id. -tāñ adv., id. (K. 366, 740). -tāñĕth adv., id.
adv. at what price? As in kȧhⁱ chĕh dã̄-khār, at what price is a khār of paddy? like our 'how much is wheat a bushel?' (K.Pr. 109).
in kai zag (L. 463), see kĕvⁱ-zag, s.v. kyovᵘ.
or kaikēyī or kökayī, i.q. kaikī, q.v.

m. (Hindū mythology) N. of a mountain (in Sanskrit kailāsa), the fabulous residence of Kubēra, the god of wealth, and the paradise of Śiva. It is said to be situated among the loftiest peaks of the Himālaya, near lake Mānasa (Śiv. 63, 79, 114, 116, 270, 390, 393, 648, 737, 1076, 1100, 1349, 1440, 1456; Rām. 937). ¶ kailāsa-kŏh (Śiv. 252) or kŏhi-kailās (Śiv. 823) m. the mountain of Kailāsa, i.q. kailās. -wās (Śiv. 1257) or -wösī (Śiv. 195, 779) m. he who dwells in Kailāsa, a N. of Śiva.
or kö̃sar m. the condition of being the youngest in a family, see kū̃sᵘ. Another form of this word is kaĩʦhar or kö̃ʦhar (Gr.Gr. 141).

m. in Hindū mythology N. of a demon (Skt. kaiṭaha). He and another demon named Madhu are said to have sprung from the ears of Viṣṇu, when he was asleep. They were about to devour Brahmā when Viṣṇu slew them (Śiv. 1321).
m. howmuchness, howmaniness, the quantity of anything.
or kö̃ʦhar m. the condition or position of the youngest son of a family. Cf. kū̃sᵘ.
(cf. کج) m. crookedness; esp. the condition of something originally straight, but which has become crooked. Cf. holᵘ-kolᵘ, p. 331a, l. 50, kaj-raftār, and kolᵘ 2.
کجابہ m. a camel-litter. Cf. sērĕ-kajāba, a pile of bricks so shaped, p. 930a, l. 27.
(YZ. 569, kajin), (eyes, fem.) were torn out by her, see kaḍun.
in kāji-tamonᵘ adj. (f. -tamüñᵘ̈), dark-skinned, dark-complexioned (over the whole body).
adj. c.g. and subst. m. one who wears his turban awry, a fop, a beau; (cf a king) one who wears a curved crown (YZ. 2), see kaj 1.
kaj-raphtār adj. c.g. walking crookedly or obliquely; perverse (Gr.M.); unprincipled, irregular. Cf. kaj 1.
m. a crow, in kākā-jī, the revered crow, i.e. the crow known in Sanskrit as Bhusuṇḍa, who was famous for his piety (see busunḍ) (Śiv. 1772, where the word may also mean a revered elder. Cf. kākh).

f. the wife of an elder male relative; esp. an eldest brother's wife (cf. böyⁱ-kⁱ, p. 149b, l. 6) (K.Pr. 156; Rām. 510; H. v, 10; K. 1017); a paternal uncle's wife, or (in the lifetime of one's grandmothers or similar female relatives of at least that degree) one's own mother. Cf. kākh, māmaturᵘ, and māsaturᵘ.
m. any substance meant to be smoked, such as tobacco, bhang, or the like (vulg.).

or kakuv m. (sg. dat. kakawas), the Bartavelle or Greek partridge (Perdix rufa) (fabled to subsist on moonbeams, and to eat fire at the full moon). It is believed to be tortured by a perpetual thirst, even though it drink water continually, drop by drop (El. and K.Pr. 101, kakkū; K.Pr. 145, kakkav; L. 119, kak, Caccabis chukar; Rām. 97). --karun -- m.inf. to play the partridge, i.e. to abscond, to run away, esp. to do so without being seen (cf. K.Pr. 145). --pạṭhᵃrāwun -- m.inf. to dress the hair over the forehead in a certain way used esp. by prostitutes; cf. kōkala. -rangishⁱ f. (of a human being) quickness in walking, the habit of or facility in walking quickly (cf. K.Pr. 101, the crow learnt to walk like a partridge). -ṭhūl m. a partridge's egg. -trēsh f. a partridge's thirst; met. a thirst which is not quenched by frequently repeated small draughts of water.

or kākad m. paper. According to El. the manufacture of paper in Kashmīr is said to have begun in the time of the Emperor Akbar. Before that time birch-bark was used (see burza). The great paper works of Kashmīr are situated at Naushāhar, near to Śrīnagar. (H. kākad, xii, 6, 7, 11-2, 15-8, 22; kākaz, viii, 10). -bạrᵃg کاغذ برگ m. a leaf, or sheet of paper (Gr.M.). -chal f. a bit or scrap of paper (Gr.M.). -dasta کاغذ دستہ m. a quire of paper, 24 sheets. -gar m. a paper-maker; a paper-seller, a stationer. -gara m. a house made of paper equivalent to our 'house of cards', a house that can be at once destroyed (Śiv. 1778). -han f. a piece of paper (Rām. 1163). -kūṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kōcĕ), a strip of paper; esp. a long strip of paper rolled up, formerly used in Kashmīr for business accounts or the like. -kyomᵘ m. a paper-worm, an insect which eats and destroys paper that is not cared for, a fish-insect, book-worm, or the like.
adj. c.g. of paper, made of paper; paper-like, thin, delicate. --ḍūnᵘ -- m. a superior kind of walnut, with a shell like paper and a large excellent kernel (L. 352).

m. (sg. dat. kākas), a father (only used with reference to one's own father); an elder male relative (esp. when --˚ added to a person's name or referring to him); an eldest son of a family is so addressed or referred to by his brothers and sisters (K.Pr. 156, 217, 251); a much-respected person outside the family may also be so addressed (K.Pr. 217). Cf. kākañ. ¶ kāka-hö̃kal f. distant relationship (i.e. a relationship which is admitted, or which is traditional, but the exact degree of which cannot be stated). -lāla m. a beloved elder, such as a beloved father of a house or person in similar position of authority in a house, is thus addressed by the other members. ¶ kākunᵘ adj. (f. kāküñᵘ̈, of or belonging to one who is elder (e.g. an elder brother) (cf. bāyyunᵘ, p. 149b, l. 17) (K.Pr. 251). kākunᵘ hāputh m. 'Daddy's bear', the bogey with which children are threatened to make them good, as in 'be quiet, there's a bear coming'; hence, nothing to be really afraid of (K.Pr. 92).
m. unwillingness (due to laziness, apprehension of trouble, or the like) to undertake any work when urged to do so.
(?) m. Serratula anthelmintica, a kind of sawwort (El., who also gives as synonyms bukokī, kāla zīra, kālī zīrī, and malwa bakchī. Cf., however, kāla-zyurᵘ, s.v. kāla 3).
m. a mark; esp. a stain, an ugly mark (Rām. 1011).
m.(f. kākᵘ̈rᵘ̈, K.Pr. 132, kākir), a dishonest man, a swindler (rare), f. a similar woman (in K.Pr. 132 translated 'sharp').
or kọ̆kᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the hard outer rind of a water-melon or similar fruit; the hard crust of snow which has melted on the surface of a road and then frozen again. Cf. ala-kᵒ, p. 22b, l. 9.
(? spelling) f. N. of a certain potherb, used as an acid vegetable, probably Rumex acetosa (L. 72). Cf. obulᵘ and aibij.

f. (sg. dat. küjᵘ̈ 1, Gr.Gr. 69; K.Pr. 92 has kajī, but Śiv. 1757 has kali, and L.V. 64 has pl. dat. kalan; for küjᵘ̈ 2, see kolᵘ 1), longing, regret, yearning (L.V. 64; YZ. 271; Śiv. 1757; Rām. 650; K. 499, 1102, 1142); worry, worrying, anxiety (K.Pr. 92); thought, consideration, calculation (i.q. kalanā, q.v., Śiv. 583, 769); loving thought, affectionate meditation (Śiv. 524, 1575; K. 279). --ganüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. longing (for any object) to increase (L.V. 48). --kaḍüñᵘ̈ --, f.inf. to pull out longing, to suggest or prompt a wish, to cause a person to long (for anything) (Śiv. 576).

m. a time, a season (cf. āpayĕ-kāl, barsāth-kᵒ, p. 127a, l. 31, hĕndawan-kᵒ, p. 338b, l. 21) (YZ. 454; Śiv. 659, 1325, 1723, 1758); time, a period of time (YZ. 237; Rām. 548); esp. one of the four ages or satya, trēta, dwāpara, and kali yugas (L.V. 91); a meal-time; a meal (YZ. 435); the appointed time, Fate, Destiny (Rām. 276, 282); the time of death, death (Śiv. 158, 165, 708, 1563; Rām. 192, 412, 769; K. 68, etc.); Death (personified) (Śiv. 281, 864, 1209, 1465, 1480, 1723, 1908, 1915; Rām. 414, 956; K. 38, 363, etc.); N. of Śiva in his terrific form (Śiv. 1333); --˚ the amount of anything taken at one time, as in bata-kāl, p. 137a, l. 8, the amount of rice sufficient for a single meal, dŏda-kāl, p. 189a, l. 47, the amount of milk taken from a cow at one milking; anta-kāl, the end-time, the time of death (K. 8, 238); yüʦᵘ̈ kāl, a long time (Rām. 1297; K. 489, 685, 704, 794, 1111), for, or from, a long time (Śiv. 1209; Rām. 306, 895, 1137). With suff. of indef. art. (kālāh, kālā) this word is used adverbially when --˚, as in az-kālāh, only once to-day, p. 74a, l. 16; kē̃h-kālā, for a short time, for a while (Gr.M., K. 603); similarly wārayāh kāl, for a very long time (H. viii, 2). There are three times,-- present, past, and future--or, as an alternative explanation, the three conditions of waking, dreaming, and sound sleep (Śiv. 1428, 1694). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. time to pass (Śiv. 81, 706); kĕ˜h kālāh gav, a short time passed (H. v, 10; viii, 2); wārayāh kālāh gav, a long time passed (H. viii, 2). --kshēph karun -- m.inf. to pass time, to spend time (Gr.M.). --wātun -- m.inf. time to elapse; kōtāh kāl wôtuy, how much time elapsed for thee? how much time did you spend (in such and such a place, etc.) (Gr.M.). ¶ kāla adv. at (such and such) a time; (opp. to pagāh, to-morrow) at (the evening) time, in the evening, this evening (K.Pr. 194, 227). Cf. kālacan. -kāji adv. both at breakfast and supper, i.q. kāji-kāla, p. 430a, l. 1. -pĕṭha adv. from some time, i.e. for some time since (Gr.M.); kē̃h kāla-pĕṭha, from some time, some time ago; yüʦᵘ̈ kāla-pĕṭha, from a long time, and so on for other similar expressions (Gr.M.). -shēkhar m. (in Hindū mythology) the crest of Time or of Death, a N. of the god Śiva (Śiv. 1174). -samhār m. N. of the god Śiva in his terrible form of Rudra, who will destroy the universe on the last day, literally, the destroyer of Time or of Death (Śiv. 68, 122, 864. In 118, 152, 1577, the name specifically refers to the destruction of death). -samhörī m., id. (Śiv. 203, 621, 1888). -zāl m. the net of time, passage or efflux of time; -zölⁱ adv. by efflux of time (L.V. 64). ¶ kālan adv. --˚ at such and such a time (cf. arinĕn-kālan, p. 44a, l. 26). ¶ kālas adv. at (such and such) a time (Śiv. 862, 1887). Cf. kölⁱ-kālas, p. 438b, l. 9. wārayāhas kālas, for (during) a long time (H. iii, 1).
f. (sg. dat. kali), a machine, an engine (Śiv. 1575, 1870).

m. the day after to-morrow, in az-kāl. See az 1 (p. 74a, l. 13) where it is incorrectly translated 'to-morrow', This word, therefore, differs in meaning from the Hindī kal. The Kāshmīrī for 'to-morrow' is pagāh. (El. kãl, i.e. köl); yesterday (Śiv. 1333). ¶ kāli 1 adv. (for 2, see s.v., for 3, see kôlᵘ 1) on the day after to-morrow, used --˚, as in az-kāli, to-day and the day after to-morrow, nowadays (p. 74a, l. 15). ¶ kölⁱ 1 adv. (for 2, see under kôlᵘ 1) on the day after to-morrow, used --˚, as in az-kölⁱ (p. 74a, l. 16), to-day and the day after to-morrow, nowadays. -kĕth adv. on the day after tomorrow (Gr.Gr. 157; W. kolkiet, 95). -kĕth-kani adv. about the day after to-morrow, on the day after to-morrow or thereabouts.
f. (sg. dat. kali), i.q. kalā, q.v. (Śiv. 1657, 1842). shĕshi-kal, a digit of the moon (L.V. 25, 69).
f. (sg. dat. kali), any practical art; accomplishment, skill, dexterity; yōga-kal, skill in yōga, the practice of yōga, or mental absorption, L.V. 14.
in kala-kal m. a noise, uproar; the act of raising an uproar. Cf. kŏlakŏl.

(L. 460, kal) m. the head of a human being or other animal (cf. gāḍa-kᵒ, p. 276b, l. 4) (K.Pr. 51, 92-3, 136, 169; YZ. 565; Śiv. 124-5, 128, 205, 313, 319-21, etc.; Rām. 269, 410, 630, 634, 1457, 1738; H. iii, 1, 5, 9; K. 236, 390, etc.); the top, end, or tip (of anything) (cf. dünzᵘ̈-kᵘ̈, p. 229a, l. 42; dā̃-kᵒ, p. 230a, l. 29; and muji-kᵒ, s.v. mujᵘ̈); the head or beginning (of anything) (K.Pr. 118, kulah); the front (of anything) (cf. dāsa-kᵒ, p. 252a, l. 10); the commencement (of a story, or the like). --chāwun -- m.inf. to fling the head (at so-and-so), to thrust (at) with the head, to butt (akh akis-kun, mutually Rām. 923, but kalas kañĕ chāwun, to fling stones at a person's head, Rām. 1433). -dāla m. head-leather, thick skin on a man's head which by itself gives him the appearance of stoutness. --ḍōlun -- m.inf. 'the head to be of no value', i.e. to become very humble, to stoop to humility (in supplicating another to grant a request). --dārun -- m.inf. to offer the head (to the executioner); hence, to become entirely subject or obedient to another. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give the head (including the mind, voice, etc.); hence, to become entirely engrossed in the accomplishment of some object, to devote oneself with ardour to some work. -ganḍ hyonᵘ m.inf. to tie up the head; esp. to tie up the top of a bundle of articles. --ganḍun 1 -- m. a turban. --ganḍun 2 -- m.inf. to add a preface or introduction to a book. -hīrᵘ̈ f. a decapitated head (e.g. of a goat) (K.Pr. 197); met. (as a term of reproach) a head as useless as if it were decapitated, an empty noddle. -hērĕ-pröpyunᵘ m. an offering of the head of a sheep or other animal made by a Hindū to a god. --hĕth lalanāwun -- m.inf. to take hold of a person's head and fondle it (Rām. 269, 1129). -hāʦh f. (sg. dat. -hāʦi), a charge resulting in decapitation, a charge of a capital crime. -khaphürᵘ̈ f. half of the cranium of the head, i.e. the forehead and adjacent part of the skull, the front of the cranium, see khaphürᵘ̈. -kȧnⁱ adv. in the direction of the head, at the head end (of an animal) (H. xi, 9). -kinⁱ dyunᵘ m.inf. to throw (a person) head-foremost, to cast head-first (K.Pr. 171, W. 144). -kôpᵘ m. head and cranium, i.e. an entire head including the hair; cf. kôpᵘ 3. -kāpi-sān adv. with head and hair i.e. entirely (e.g. of a person diving and plunging so that his entire body is under water, or of a person greedily eating up an entire dish, as if, like an ogre, he were eating an entire animal, head, hair, and all). -māl f. a chaplet of heads, or skulls, said by Hindūs to be worn by the god Śiva (Śiv. 88, 814, 891). -mālā-dar (Śiv. 1174) or -māla-dārawunᵘ (Śiv. 1260, 1537) m. he who wears a chaplet of skulls, N. of Śiva. -māz m. the flesh of the head, the flesh of the head of a sheep, goat, or similar animal, cut off from the bone and sold by butchers. -phŏphüjᵘ̈ f. a small head, a little head, a head which is small as compared with the other members of the body; cf. hēri-phŏᵒ, p. 345b, l. 46. -pushᵘ m. a head covering, a kind of skull-cap (worn chiefly by women) (El.; K.Pr. 146, kalaposh; L. 459, kal pōsh; W. 140) (cf. gĕv-kᵒ, p. 316b, l. 4); (from its shape) a sheep's paunch, see ḍȧmbⁱ-kⁱ, p. 218a, l. 10, and ḍamiñĕ-kᵒ, p. 220a, l. 39. -pushⁱ-korⁱ m. the lower part or edge of this skull-cap. -pushᵘ madun m. (sg. dat. --madanas--), a skull-cap cupid, a man who either owing to want of a proper turban or through shamelessness habitually wears such a woman's skull-cap, and who is vain of his personal appearance when doing so. -pĕṭhⁱ wŏṭh f. a leap over (so-and-so's head) (H. ii, 9). Similarly -pĕṭhⁱ, (whirling a thing) over one's head (K. 187); -pĕṭhⁱ-kinⁱ (flung it) over his head (K. 351). -shēkh m. (sg. dat. -shēkhas), one who (on account of great wealth or good qualities, high family, or the like) is proud, haughty, insolent; one who (for similar reason) is entitled to great respect. -ṭāph f. (sg. dat. -ṭāpi), a slap (with the open hand) on the head. -ʦhaṭh f. (sg. dat. -ʦhaṭi), a cold blast on the head; met. terror caused by some great calamity (e.g. by undergoing punishment or by the pain due to some severe disease). -ʦhŏṭh m. (sg. dat. -ʦhŏṭi), scurf of the head. -ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ʦanjĕ), a blow on the head (from a fist, kick, or the like); met. the occurrence of anxiety due to fear of death, or the like. -ʦanjĕ-kūrᵘ̈ f. 'the daughter of a blow on the head', i.e. an orphan girl dependent upon others who treat her unkindly. -ʦanjĕ-nĕcyuvᵘ m. 'the son of a blow on the head', i.e. an orphan boy situated as ab. -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), having the head cut off, beheaded; met. one who is audacious in order to help another, a knight errant, quixotic, chivalrous; warm-hearted, generous, of a noble disposition; one who fearlessly and audaciously engages in vile and contemptible employment. --ʦaṭun -- m.inf. to behead (K.Pr. 214; Rām. 997; H. iii, 2; viii, 6; cf. Rām. 471). -walyunᵘ m. anything wrapped like a turban round the head; esp. when worn by a woman. -vyoṭhᵘ 1 m. N. of a certain medicinal plant, used as a remedy for colds or the like. ? the kalawint, mentioned in L. 75 as a plant used as an antineuralgic medicine. -vyoṭhᵘ 2 adj. (f. -vë̆ṭhᵘ̈), large-headed. ¶ kalas dôdᵘ m. a headache (El., Gr.M.). --dyunᵘ akhāh -- m.inf. to strike a person a single blow on the head (Rām. 483, 819). --harakath karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to shake the head (Rām. 712).

or kal 3 f. (sg. dat. kalāyĕ or kali), a digit, or one-sixteenth part of the moon's diameter. Hence, the expression 'sixteen kalā's' indicates complete brightness of the moon, or, met. of anything else (Śiv. 1438, 1658).

(for 1, see kāl 1) adj. black (YZ. 66, 228); cf. kôlᵘ 3. --dāna -- m. Ipomœa cœrulea or Pharbites nil (El.). --gaṭa -- f. the black darkness of a cloudy moonless night (Rām. 402); met. a time of lawlessness, injustice, and calamity. -sarᵃph m. (sg. dat. -sarpas), the black and most poisonous variety of the Cobra, Coluber naga (Śiv. 1055, Rām. 1469). --zīra, see kakshĕma, and cf. the next. L. 346 says it is Carum, sp., and that it is a garden spring crop cultivated as a condiment for improving the condition of horses and other cattle. --zyurᵘ -- m. the seed of the Nigella indica, a kind of cummin. Cf. kālī and kakshĕma.

or kālacĕn adv. in the evening (K.Pr. 105; H. v, 5; viii, 3); cf. kāla, p. 434a, l. 21. --bögⁱ -- or --bögin -- adv. at about evening, at eveningtide. ¶ kālacanan adv., i.q. kālacan. --bögⁱ -- or--bögin -- adv., i.q. kālacan bögⁱ. ¶ kālacanas bögⁱ or --bögin -- adv., i.q. kālacan bögⁱ.

m. (according to Hindūs) the fire that will destroy the world, conflagration at the end of time. -rudᵃr m. (sg. dat. -rudras), the god Śiva regarded as the fire that is to destroy the world (Śiv. 153, 1120, 1147). Cf. kāl 1.

m. (N.B.--This word is f. in Hindī), a reed; a reed-pen; a pen (cf. jadwal-kᵒ, p. 371a, l. 14) (K.Pr. 152; Śiv. 1912; H. ix, 12); a painter's brush; a mode of writing, character, handwriting; a cutting of a tree for planting, a set, a slip (cf. dachĕ-kᵒ, p. 185b, l. 38); a short length of thin wood (e.g. a bamboo) (cf. baĩs-kᵒ, p. 131b, l. 12). -chapōṭa m. a splinter of a reed pen, a reed pen originally long, but which by use and constant cutting, has become worn down to a mere splinter or stump. -dāna (= قلم دان) m. a pen-case, pen and ink case, a standish; esp. one of the highly-ornamented papier mâché pen-cases, for which Kashmīr is famous (W. 111; L. 378, kalamdán). -dönī adj. c.g. of or belonging to a (papier mâché) pen-case; one of the three qualities of paper made in Kashmīr, the kind now chiefly manufactured, containing no hemp fibre (L. 380); kār-i-kalamdönī, papier mâché work (L. 378). -dāna-khỗṭᵘ m. the upper half, forming the cover, of such a Kāshmīrī pen-case. --garun -- m.inf. to mend a pen (Gr.M.); to make a pen (El.). kalam-nôrᵘ m. a tubular box for holding pens. -trāsh (= قلم تراش) f. a penknife (Rām. 1268). -zan قلم زن m. a pen-smiter, a penman, a quill-driver (K.Pr. 92); a painter, draughtsman (Rām. 130). ¶ kalama-phuṭᵘ̈ f. an old worn-out and broken reed-pen; a reed-pen worn down to a mere stump.
f. calculation. kalanāyĕ-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), not calculating, not doing anything in the hope of reward (Śiv. 1537).
m. a kind of wandering Musalmān monk, a Calender (K.Pr. 29, sg. voc. Kalandarai).
m. (sg. dat. kalankas), stain, mark, soil; esp. a moral stain, or a stain in reputation; a blemish, defect (Gr.M.).
m. transportation (the punishment) (borrowed from Hindī). kālā-pönī sōzana yunᵘ, to be sentenced to transportation (Gr.M.).

m. reed-cotton, rush-cotton, the cotton-like flower of a certain reed (? Phragmites communis), which grows in marshes and on the borders of lakes in Kashmīr. ¶ kalaran-bôrᵘ m. reed-cotton plaster; a grey-coloured plaster (cf. bôrᵘ 2) made up of mud mixed with this reed-cotton, which is applied to the inner walls of houses, like whitewash.

m. a seller of spirituous liquor, a wine merchant; met. a drinker of spirituous liquor; hence, applied to Śiva as he who drinks the nectar of absolute bliss (Skt. svânandâmṛtapāyin) (Śiv. 1260, 1537).
m. (sg. abl. kalāyĕ 1), a fort (esp. on a mountain or on an eminence), a fortress, castle, citadel, fortification. I.q. kila, q.v.

f. (sg. dat. kalāyĕ 2), tin (K.Pr. 93, 103); a coating of tin given to culinary vessels, etc.; the application of such coating (El., K.Pr., kaláí). kalāyĕ-gar قلعی گر m. a tinner of pots and pans; a tinman.
f. a bramble (El. who makes the word m., but dach is f.).
m. the liver. ¶ kalējas dôdᵘ m. pain in the liver, liver complaint (Gr.M.).
in kālī-zīrī f. Serratula anthelmintica (El.), see kakshĕma and kāla 2. -zēwar m. Bupleurum marginatum (El.).
see kal 1 and 2, and also kalā.

m. (for 1, see kāl 2, for 3, see kôlᵘ 1) in kāli-nāg m. the name of a Nāga or snake who inhabited the river Yamunā (Jamnā), and was slain by Kṛṣṇa. The Skt. form of the name is Kāliya or Kālīya (K. 230 ff.).

in kali-kāl m. (gen. -kālukᵘ, Śiv.338; -kālunᵘ, Śiv. 1758) (amongst Hindūs) the time of the Kali- yŏg (see the next) full of evil and sin (Śiv. 338, 1325, 1723, 1758). -yŏg m. (among Hindūs) the fourth and worst of the four ages of the world, in Sanskrit Kali-yuga. It is the age of vice, and is at present current (Śiv. 1521; Rām. 51; K. 6, 7, 12). Cf. kāl 1.

kalama, or kalma m. a word, speech, expression, phrase (Gr.M.); the Muslim creed or profession of unity, viz. lā ilāha illa'l-lāh, wa Muḥammad rasūlu'l-lāh, there is no god but The God, and Muḥammad is the apostle of The God (K.Pr. 227).
f. N. of one of the wives of Kṛṣṇa. She was a daughter of the Sun (K. 703).
f. of like character (to such and such), usually --˚, the former member indicating someone blameworthy.
f. a copper coin of small value, such as a pice.
m. (in Hindū legend) N. of a tyrannical demon, who was burnt to death by the saint Mucukunda through a stratagem of Kṛṣṇa (Krishṇa). In Skt. the name is Kālayavana (Śiv. 1479; K. 578 ff., 614, 624).
(L.V.) or kalpanā (Śiv.) f. creating in the mind, imagining; (hence, in Śaiva theology) earthly desire (which is all vanity) (L.V. 30, 33; Śiv. 1658).

m. (sg. dat. kalpāntas), (amongst Hindūs) the end of a yuga or age, esp. of the present, or Kali, age (see kali 3), the dissolution of all things, the last day (Śiv. 119); met. a great calamity or agony (comparable to what will happen at the last day); a kalpa or fabulous period of time consisting of 4,320,000,000 years (Śiv. 854, 1209). Cf. mahākalph. ¶ kalpāntas tāñ adv. up to the end of the age, to the end of all time, i.e. practically equivalent to our 'to all eternity'.
m. (in Hindū mythology) one of the five trees of Svarga or Indra's paradise, fabled to fulfil all desire, the wishing tree, the tree of plenty. In Sanskrit kalpavṛkṣa (Śiv. 1013, 1213, 1553).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. kalyōv), to become dumb, become speechless (Śiv. 434, 741, 748, 986); to be stricken dumb, to be left without an answer. kalyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. kalē-müʦᵘ̈), become speechless (of one who formerly could speak); (in a dispute) become speechless, left without an answer.

m. (sg. dat. kalashĕs), a jar; esp. (among Hindūs) a sacred jar or cup which is set up before beginning the ritual of worship, and into which water and fruits are cast. It is supposed to represent all the gods. --wahārun -- m. the ceremonial setting up of this jar before commencing the principal ritual; met. the first thing done in any work. ¶ kalashĕ-ḍūnᵘ m. a walnut which forms part of the fruit cast into this jar. At the conclusion of the main worship, and after the jar has been removed, these walnuts are distributed to the members of the congregation to be eaten by them. -lawa f. the ceremonial sprinkling of the worshippers with water from this jar, after the conclusion of the main ritual. -nörᵘ̈ f. the above jar. -wörᵘ̈ f., id.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kạlᵃrôwᵃ), to make dumb, cause to be dumb, to make speechless; to strike dumb, to leave without an answer; caus. of kalun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 173), also kạlᵃrun.
m. broiled flesh-meat dressed with anything. See s.v. ḍaphar, p. 233a, l. 33.

adj. c.g. deficient, less, short (K.Pr. 39; H. iii, 46), little, small, inconsiderable, few (K.Pr. 93, 94; Śiv. 1230, 1248; Rām. 520, 657; K. 660); young (of age) (YZ. 7); scanty; less (opp. to more) (Śiv. 444, 1596); abated; short (of life, stature) (Gr.M.). ˚-- it gives the idea of defectiveness, inferiority, or negation. -bakht کم بخت or -bakt (Śiv. 1041) adj. c.g. unfortunate, unlucky (W. 110). -bāna m. one possessed of no luck, luckless. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become less, to diminish, decrease (Rām. 845, 1022, 1174, 1192, 1562). -jyāda (= کم زیاد) adv. more or less (u.w. vbs. of giving, or the like) (H. ii, 12). --kam 1 -- کم کم adv. (for 2, see kyāh), only a little, little by little (u.w. vbs. of giving, or the like). --karun -- m.inf. to diminish, to lessen (tr.), to make less (El., Śiv. 1256). -nasīb کمنصیب adj. c.g. unlucky, unfortunate (El.). -phahm کم فہم adj. c.g. of feeble understanding, stupid, ignorant (W. 110). -pahān adj. c.g. somewhat less (than a fixed quantity, or the like). --sapadun -- or --sapanun -- or --sapazun --, m.inf. to diminish, to become less, to grow less, to lessen (intr.) (El., Gr.M., Rām. 229). -yāb کمیاب adj. c.g. scarce, rare, uncommon, hard to get (Gr.M.). -zōr کم زور adj. c.g. weak, feeble, infirm, powerless; ineffectual (Śiv. 1734). -zāth کم ذات adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. -zātas), of low origin or caste, low- bred (Rām. 816). -zuv adj. c.g. having little life, weak, impotent (naturally or owing to disease). ¶ kamạy-hanā or kamᵘ̈y-hanā f. a little (of anything), a small amount. -mŏyā f., id.

m. (amongst Hindūs) love, sexual love (L.V. 71, Śiv. 1749); Love, Desire personified; non-sexual love (Śiv. 179); pleasure, enjoyment (cf. darm, p. 244a, l. 10); (in Hindū theology) desire (as an impediment to free communion with God) (Śiv. 767, 888, 1568, 1798; Rām. 42, 977); kām krūd lūb muh, desire, wrath, greed, and illusion, four vices often grouped together in Hindū theology (Śiv. 18, 269, 932, 1647). ¶ kāma-dīn or kāma-dēnu  (El. also kāmadayan) f. (sg. dat. kāma-dīni, Śiv. 1006, 1368; K. 845 ff; pl. nom. kāma-dīna, Śiv. 1388, 1439; K. 97, 218, 229, 261, 944, 974); (in Hindū mythology) the desire-cow, the cow of plenty, N. of a fabulous cow belonging to the god Indra, said to have been produced at the churning of the ocean, and to yield whatever may be requested of her (K. 13-4, 844); met. a cow that gives much milk, a milch-cow (K. 97, 218, 229, etc.); a cow (generally) (El.).

m. work; sg. abl. kama 1, used in the following:--kama drāv adj. (f. -drāyĕ), issued from work, i.e. thoroughly experienced, well trained by practice (e.g. a well-trained horse); (of an iron weapon, or the like) thoroughly forged (by repeated hammering, etc.). --nērun -- m.inf. to issue from work, i.e. to become thoroughly trained by practice, to become thoroughly experienced; (of an iron weapon, or the like) to become thoroughly forged (by repeated hammering, etc.). -züṭᵘ̈ f. a work-rag, i.e. a working garment, an old worn-out garment used for working in, esp. the worn-out, torn garment worn by collectors of water-chestnuts.
said by El. to mean 'some'. Probably a mis-spelling of kã̄h, see kē̃h.
kama 2, see kyāh. Note that this word is often used to mean 'extraordinary things', 'what (wonderful) things!'

sg. abl. kama 3, in the following:-- kama-görⁱ or -görᵘ̈ f. N. of a particular kind of water-chestnut and of its kernel, see gôrᵘ and görᵘ̈ 2. -khuru (? spelling and gender), a kind of hoe on a long pole for scraping up and gathering water-chestnuts (L. 461, kamkhuru, cf. 355; see görⁱ-kôwⁱ, p. 298a, l. 33, and cokdan).
f. sons, grandsons, and the like, when referred to as a whole.
m. a lotus, a lotus flower, to which a beautiful eye (Śiv. 1741) or a beautiful foot (Śiv. 1266; Rām. 938; K. 184, 392) is often compared; a N. of Śiva (Śiv. 1538).
kã̄bal, or kã̄bay 1 f. jaundice, excessive secretion or obstruction of bile.
or kã̄bay 2 f. N. of a certain medicinal plant, Solanum nigrum, used as an anti-periodic (L. 76, kambai; El. kámbeí).
m. he who was born in a lotus, N. of the Hindū god Brahmā. kamalaza-nāth m. the lord who was born in a lotus, N. of Brahmā (L.V. 8).
f. a kind of black woollen blanket, said to come from the West.

f. [(sg. dat. kamöñᵘ̈ (Gr.M.) or kamāni (Gr.M.))], a bow (the weapon) (Gr.M.; YZ. 6, 50-1, 208; Rām. 117, 121, 140, 446, 480, 919, 977, 982, 999, 1269, 1421); an arch (Gr.M., Śiv. 1715); the sign Sagittarius; (in Kāshmīrī, by confusion with kamand, q.v.), a bowstring; the bowstring-like top of a sidedoor or casement, the chord of an arch. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to draw a bow (El. who makes kamān m.). --shērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to prepare a bow, to string a bow (Rām. 1420, 1452).

f. (sg. dat. kāmüñᵘ̈), scarcity, rarity. ¶ kāmüñᵘ̈ adv. (K.Pr. kámani or kāmuni), under conditions of scarcity, (obtainable) with great difficulty (owing to rarity) (K.Pr. 29); at a famine price (K.Pr. 38, 250). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become at a famine price, to be wanting when necessary (K.Pr. 95, 114, 242).

(or kamawun or kamāwun, qq.v.) conj. 1 (1 p.p. kamanôwᵘ), to earn, acquire, gain; to accumulate, save; to acquire (a quality, condition, etc.) by practice or experience; (of iron, hard leather, or the like) to work at, to bring into proper condition, or to perfect by first softening it and then working upon it; to smelt (metal). kamanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. kamanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), earned, acquired; (of a quality, condition, etc.) acquired by practice, thoroughly learnt; (of iron, leather, etc.) brought into proper condition by being softened and then worked upon; (of metal) smelted.
m. a halter; a noose; a snare (El.); a bowstring (Rām. 977). Cf. kamān.
m. a gourd or vessel made of wood or earth, used as a water-jar by religious ascetics (Śiv. 543).
m. N. of a place to the north of the Naupūrᵘ quarter of Śrīnagar, formerly inhabited by makers of bows (Persian kamān-gar).

m. the flank, loins, waist (El.); cf. kambar. -band کمر بند m. a waistband, girdle (El.); i.q. kambar-band, p. 444b, l. 15. -basta کمر بستہ adj. c.g. having the loins girt, in a state of readiness, on the alert, ready for action (Rām. 573). --ganḍun -- m.inf. to gird up the loins, get ready, arm (for) (Rām. 127), i.q. kambar ganḍun, p. 444b, l. 17.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kamawanôwᵘ), to cause to earn; caus. of kamawun (Gr.Gr. 171).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kamowᵘ), to earn, etc., i.q. kamanāwun, q.v. The caus. of this vb. is kamawanāwun (Gr.Gr. 171). ¶ kamowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. kamüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. kamanôwᵘ motᵘ, q.v. s.v. kamanāwun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. kamôwᵘ), i.q. kamawun and kamanāwun, qq.v., but principally used in the sense of acquiring, earning, or the like. ¶ kamāwan-kulᵘ m. the earning tree, i.e. the bread-winner of a family (i.q. kamāyi-kulᵘ, s.v. kamöyⁱ).
adj. c.g. that which has received thorough working, thoroughly worked, perfected, made or become complete; useful, producing excellent results (Rām. 9, m.c. -dörī).

or kamar کمر (q.v.) m. the loins, the waist; a girdle, zone, belt; the middle (of a mountain, etc.); the flank (of an army). -band (= کمر بند) m. a girdle, zone, sash, belt, waistband; a long piece of cloth folded round the loins. --ganḍun -- m.inf. to gird up the loins (Rām. 882), i.q. kamar-ganḍun, s.v. kamar. -kash (cf. کمر کش) m. N. of a certain medicinal root given to women after childbirth.
m. (sg. dat. kambᵃrakas), a certain kind of cotton cloth made with very fine threads, a kind of cambric.
or kümbᵘ̈ f. (for kȧmbⁱ 2, see kombᵘ), the sheath of a sword, a scabbard. Cf. kō̃b (El. kómb and kumb). ¶ kambi anun m.inf. gradually to bring under subjection, to tame (a man, beast, bird, etc.).

or (El.) kamcī قمچی m. a whip, a scourge. -dan m. a whip-handle. --lāyun -- m.inf. to flog, to whip (El.). -shĕlakh (= قمچی شلق) m. (sg. dat. -shĕlakhas), a beating with a whip, a whipping, a scourging.
or kāmadēv m. N. of the Hindū Cupid, the god of love. His wife was Rati, the Hindū Venus (K.Pr. 93; K. 735, 739); met. a person beautiful as the god of love, a Cupid (K. 263-8, 978).

f. (i.q. kamĕr), littleness, scantiness; paucity, scarcity, lack; deficiency (Gr.M., W. 112, Rām. 710); decrease, diminution, abatement (Śiv. 843); fall (of price). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make deficiency, to do deficiency; to show want of zeal, not to exercise one's full powers (Rām. 409, 1515).
m. Mallotus Philippinensis, used as a dye, and also, in medicine, as a vermifuge (El. Rottleria tinctoria, a name now not used; L. 68, kamila).
adj. c.g. (of something animate) low, mean (by qualities as well as birth and family) (K.Pr. 94).
f. (sg. dat. kāminiyĕ, K. 264), a loving or affectionate woman.
f. earning, acquiring; earnings, gains, profits; work, performance. kamāyi-kulᵘ m. the bread-winner of a family, i.q. kamāwan-kulᵘ, q.v. s.v. kamāwun.
m. (sg. dat. kampas), shaking, trembling (K. 415, 554). būmi-kamph, an earthquake (Rām. 281); cf. bum 3 and kö̃ph. kampas gaʦhun m.inf. to go to trembling, to be seized with trembling (K. 367).

m. N. of one of the two great divisions of the Valley of Kashmīr. It comprises the districts on both sides of the river Vĕth (or Jehlam) below Śrīnagar, while the other, Marāz (q.v.), comprises those above. Śrīnagar itself is called Yamrāz. The corresponding Skt. names are respectively Kramarājya and Maḍavarājya (RT.Tr. ii, 15, and II, 436). According to popular tradition, however, the valley was once divided between two brothers named, respectively, Kāmanadēva and Malhanadēva, after whom the tracts were named respectively Kāmarājya and Malhanarājya. For another popular etymology, see El. s.v. Kashmír, and K.Pr. 138.
adj. c.g. of or belonging to Kamrāz (see the preceding); N. of a certain violent wind, i.q. baḍa shāl, p. 82b, l. 28 (L. 465).
m. Kaṁsa, N. of an Asura or demon (he was king of Mathurā, and the cousin and implacable foe of Kṛṣṇa, by whom he was slain (Śiv. 117, 653, 738, 748, 1425; K. 30, 37, 64, 72, et passim).
m. (sg. dat. kamsāntakas), he who was the (causer of the) death of, Kamsa, a title of Kṛṣṇa (Śiv. 1398). See kams.
conj. 3, to tremble, to shiver (only El., probably corruption of kö̃pun, q.v., and should be spelt kömun).
f., see krüsᵘ̈-kamürᵘ̈ and kraʦi-kamürᵘ̈, s.v. kraʦh 2.
adj. c.g. obtaining one's object, successful (Gr.M.).
f. success, prosperity in an undertaking (YZ. 250).
m. a farm labourer who lives in the farmer's house.

m. (sg. abl. kana 1), the ear (El.; K.Pr. 154, 206, 246; W. 18; YZ. 187; Śiv. 98, 197, 408, etc.; Rām. 11, 28, 58, 171, 245, 353, etc.; K. 507; H. iii, 5, 9; vii, 11); the edge (of a leaf, or the like). Paṇḍits often spell this word kaṇ. --dārun -- m.inf. to place the ear, to lend the ear, attend to, listen to (Gr.M.; Śiv. 163, 395, 584, 596, 802, 966, 1439, 1517, 1580, 1614; Rām. 6, 48, 1491, 1496; K. 15, 261, 638, 991). --khĕnⁱ -- कर्णचोदनम् m. pl. inf. to eat the ears; hence, to besiege a person's ears, to worry by continued talking (e.g. in requesting, giving advice or giving information). --khȧrⁱ gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the ears to become erect (e.g. on hearing good news, or on learning some secret). --mā̃jȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to clean the ears; esp. of a woman preparing her ears to receive ornaments; met. to polish up the edges of anything. --phyushᵘ -- or kȧnⁱ phish m. (of something said) the act getting into the ear and sticking there; esp. of children who perversely listen to people talking and do not forget what they hear, whether they are meant to hear it or not; cf. our saying about little pitchers having long ears. -pakhᵃsh adj. c.g. of the size of a piece of an ear; hence, very small, tiny (as a measure of size). -path m. a kind of ear ornament, shaped like the leaf of a tāl-palm, and studded with precious stones or pearls. --thawun -- m.inf. to offer the ear, lend the ear, listen (to), attend (to) (Śiv. 40, 182, 697, 765, 807, 821, 988, etc.; Rām. 29, 55, 60, 209, 334, 455, 500, 528, etc.; H. ii, 7). --thāwun -- m.inf., id. (L.V. 91; YZ. 556; Śiv. 533, 544, 880, 1594, 1668, 1803; Rām. 83, 1758; H. viii, 6, 8, 11; ix, 1, 4). --ʦŏmbun -- m.inf. to bore the ear (to receive earrings, etc.) (Śiv. 1290). --zorᵘ -- m. a deaf ear, the ear of one who is deaf; esp. in a phrase to avert ill-luck from self-praise, shaitāna-sȧndⁱ kan zȧrⁱ, (may) Satan have deaf ears (K.Pr. 191). ¶ kana-bal m. power of hearing, esp. the acute hearing of blind men and the like, who, though unable to read, are able to remember the contents of a book by merely hearing it read; cf. kana-pav, bel. -ḍōl m. disregard, indifference; although hearing, acting as if one did not hear; turning away the ear (from), refusing to listen (to) (K.Pr. 94). -ḍölī diñᵘ̈ f.inf. to refuse to listen (to a person) (H. v, 2). -dūr m. a kind of earring or pendant, usually set with a single pearl and worn on the lobe of the ear (El.; YZ. 36, 448; Śiv. 1689; Rām. 1040); i.q. kana-dürᵘ̈ 2,bel.-dürᵘ̈ 1 f. pulling the ear, esp. the disciplinary pulling of a pupil's ears by his teacher. -dürᵘ̈ 2 f. a kind of wooden tassel set on each corner of the roof of a house, that swings to and fro like an ear pendant (cf. kana-dūr, ab.) (K.Pr. 123, L. 464). -gŏgulᵘ m. the ear-turnip, i.e. the meatus auditorius externus, the mastoid process of the ear (El.); a general name for the whole ear with its root; cf. -yöjᵘ̈, bel. -hȧpiñ f. a centipede, Scolopendra (Hindī kan-khajūrā; El. kanahaiping). -kapas f. 'cotton in the ear', strict injunction (given to a messenger, so that he shall not forget his message). -kuʦorᵘ m. 'an ear-puppy', one who immediately conveys to another news that he has just heard from someone else, a tattling newsmonger, a tattler. -lĕḍ adj. c.g. weak-eared, one who believes everything he hears, and who acts upon it as if it were true. -mal m. dirt of the ear, ear-wax, etc. -mọ̆nḍᵘ 1 m. the root of the ear. -mọ̆nḍᵘ 2 (f. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ 1, sg. dat. -mŏnjĕ 1), dull of hearing, hard of hearing. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ 2 f. (sg. dat. -mŏnjĕ 2), i.q. -mọ̆nḍᵘ 1. -mana-tū m. (when a grown-up person is sporting with a child) pretending to shout loudly into the ear. The speaker makes motions as if he were going to shout, and then merely murmurs these words 'kana mana tū' into the child's ear. -pholᵘ 1 adj. (for 2, see kana 2), worn or torn at the edges (esp. of garments and the like). -phoṭᵘ adj. (f. -phüṭᵘ̈), having the ear torn or broken (from a blow, or the like); (of something inanimate) having the edge torn or broken. -pyushᵘ m. a flea in the ear (and hence invisible); hence, some very small thing which cannot be seen, but whose existence is perceived by some other sense. -pav m. skill in remembering narratives or literary passages after a single hearing; cf. kana- bal, ab. -ronᵘ adj. (f. -rüñᵘ̈), ear-maimed, one having ears that are not adorned with the usual earrings, etc.; ugly-eared. -tihijᵘ̈ f. the 'ear-sprout', i.e. the lobe of the ear. -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), having the ear or ears cut (Gr.Gr. 75); (of something inanimate, e.g. a sheet of paper) having the edge or edges cut. -wöjᵘ̈ f. an earring (El.; K.Pr. 36, 236; W. 114; K. 926, 1047). -wôlᵘ m. a large earring, worn both by men and by women (El.; Śiv. 98; K. 60, 755, 770, 926, 1047). -wān m. the passing of news from ear to ear, the spreading of a general report in this way. -woṭᵘ m. a kind of cap reaching down to the ears, worn by Panjābīs; a pad made of rags or straw put on the shoulders under a load that is being carried. -wȧṭⁱ-byôlⁱ m. N. of a certain kind of paddy. -yöjᵘ̈ f. the ear-biscuit, i.e. the entire ear with its root; cf. -gŏgulᵘ, ab. -yār m. an ear-friend, a confidential friend, a close and dear friend to whom one can confide secrets. -zūjᵘ̈ f. the zūjᵘ̈ is a kind of long cloth hanging down the back from the crown of the head to the small of the back; when it hangs only as far as the ears it is called kana- zūjᵘ̈. In former times in schools, when one pupil defeated another in a learned discussion, the defeated pupil was made to put on and wear a kana-zūjᵘ̈, and hence the word still means also defeat in a contest of learning. ¶ kȧnⁱ-achar m.pl. letters the sound of which are known by ear and not by sight (e.g. in the case of a blind man, or of one too stupid to read). -katha f.pl. words spoken into a person's ear, private communications conveyed by a whisper, etc. -phish m., i.q. kan phyushᵘ, ab. -phisarāray f. long whispered communication, continued whispering in the ear. -pȧtⁱ adv. behind the ear, i.e. (when one hears) as if one did not hear; inattentively (K.Pr. 229). -shĕchⁱ f. news or a message conveyed privately, a secretly conveyed message, whispered news. -sīrᵘ̈ f. slitting the ear of a cow, as a remedy for cattle-pox (L. 459). -tᵃ̇jᵃ̇ or -tᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. an ear-pick, a small metal or wooden spike for clearing out the ears. -tȧlⁱ anun m.inf. to bring under the ear, to make a practice of eavesdropping. -tȧlⁱ nyunᵘ m.inf. to take (a person) under the ear, to let him have one's ear, to patronize (K.Pr. 102). -tȧlⁱ wanun m.inf. to say under the ear, to say privately (Gr.M.). -tȧlⁱ yunᵘ m.inf. to come under (so-and-so's) ear, to tell (false) tales to a person, to calumniate secretly to so-and-so. ¶ kanas bata ladun m.inf. to put food into one's ear (instead of into one's mouth) (originally of a drunkard), to be an utter fool (K.Pr. 94, 206). --dôdᵘ -- m. ear-ache (W. 114).

m. an arrow (El.; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 68; Śiv. 353; Rām. 320, 367, 499, 503, 552, 685, 727, 932, 1298, 1453, 1455; K. 824). --barun -- m.inf. to aim an arrow (L.V. 71). ¶ kāna-dag f. the range of an arrow, a bowshot. -nôrᵘ m. a quiver. -phal m. the metal tip or point of an arrow.

f. sec. suff. indicating a small quantity, u.w. words signifying vegetables or wood, as in hāka-kāñ, a little spinach; pōshĕ-kāñ, a few flowers; zinⁱ-kāñ, a little firewood (Gr.Gr. 163), with suff. of indef. art. darbi-kāñāh, a small heap of darbha-grass (Rām. 1285). Cf. köñᵘ̈ 5.
m. --˚ a ball of cooked food; cf. ana-kan, p. 29b, l. 37, and bata-kan, p. 137a, l. 11. ¶ kani-hanā f. a little ball of cooked food, a small quantity of food (K.Pr. 150, kanih- hanā).
f. (sg.dat. köñᵘ̈), a mine, a quarry (El., m.), a source (El., f.). Cf. gandakh- kᵒ, p. 290a, l. 35.
postpos. i.q. kinⁱ, q.v. āb-dawa-kāñ, (enter) through the water-drain (H. v, 4).

m. --˚ a single one, esp. one of a pair, as in bīrbali-kan, one of a pair of earrings (p. 119a, l. 2). So, dachĕ-kan, a single grape (p. 185b, l. 40); dūra-kan or dūra-hȧrⁱ-kan (p. 238b, ll. 43, 47); ḍĕjⁱ-hȧrⁱ-kan (p. 267b, l. 19); jumka-kan (p. 374a, l. 18); lōlakh-kan, s.v. lōlakh. With the exception of dachĕ-kᵒ, each of these examples refers to some kind of earring. Cf. kunᵘ.
m. a digger, an engraver, used --˚, as in mŏhar-kan, a seal-engraver, see mŏhar.

m. (for 1, see kan 1), a particle, atom, granule; esp. (in the pl.) the broken fragments of grain remain when rice is being husked, broken rice. -khĕʦürᵘ̈ f. a mixed pottage in which this broken grain is used instead of legumes, see khĕʦürᵘ̈ 2. kana-pholᵘ 2 m. (for 1, see kan 1), a single fragment of this broken rice.

adv. inter. (for 1, see kan 1), from when? since when? (usually referring to a time long past). ḍĕṭha-kana, a long time ago, from a long time ago, see ḍĕṭha and Gr.Gr. 256). kana-pĕṭha adv., id. kana-shutun adv., id.
pleon. suff. added to inter. adverbs, as in kĕtha-kana, how? (K. 272).
. This word is also used with adverbs that are not interrogative, as in yithay-kana, in this very manner.

m. (sg. dat. -gᵃchas), a kind of edible mushroom, morel, Morchella sp. (L. 73; El. kanagich, kanaguch, kána kach, kangach, Morchella semilibera). kana-gᵃch-rāṭh f. a bed of these mushrooms. These abound on the mountains (L. 73) and are believed to be caused to issue from the earth by the noise of thunder. Cf. gᵃch.
m. (sg. dat. kanakas), Segeretia oppositifolia (El.). Cf. gīdar-dākh (p. 278b, l. 11).
adj. c.g. (of a person's natural form) thin, lean, meagre.
or kanāath قناعت m. (sg. dat. kanātas), content, contentment (Gr.M.); resignation; tranquillity; ability to do without.
m. a certain kind of silken garment (cf. آویزہ).
f. (sg. dat. kanāyüʦᵘ̈), the wall of a tent; a kind of canvas screen forming an enclosure round a tent, or with which a sort of courtyard is formed in camp.

m. crystallized sugar, sugar- candy (El.; K.Pr. 62, 94; Śiv. 45, 435, 1169, 1202, 1524; Rām. 42, 998, 1335, 1557). El. also has gand, which may be a misprint for qand (قند). kanda-ʦọ̆kᵘ m. the bottom part of a piece of crystallized sugar; (sugar is crystallized in a kind of jar, and the bottom of the resulting lump is naturally the thickest part; cf. Pers. kūza). Cf. mŏdurᵘ.

m. an edible root, a bulb; (in Śaiva philosophy) the 'bulb' which is supposed to be the root of the nāḍis or tubes through which the prâṇa or life wind circulates. It is also called maṇipūraka, and is said to be situated in the region of the navel or solar plexus; (cf. Śivasūtravimarṣiṇī, i, 12, and Yōgacūḍāmaṇi-upaniṣad, 12). In L.V. 56, it is called kandāpurā. kanda-mūl m.pl. edible roots, radish, etc.; esp. the roots eaten by Hindū forest ascetics.
in khŏsh-kandām, adj. c.g. possessing a beautiful form (Rām. 1040). The word is apparently a corruption of andām اندام, see p. 418a, l. 35.
(? spelling) N. of a hilly tract in Kashmīr (L. 359, 436).
f. a certain wild plant used as a potherb, Morina longifolia (L. 77, khandij or kandcher). According to L. the dried plants and roots are esteemed by Ladakhīs as incense.
m. a candelabrum; (in Kāshmīrī) the shade of a lamp (El.).
f. the selvedge, or non-ravelling edge of a textile fabric.
K.Pr. 84) m. a kind of long tubular box in which heron plumes (cf. brag) and similar valuable articles are kept for safety (K.Pr. 83, kandíl).

f. an unmarried girl, a virgin (El. kanya); esp. a bride, up to and including the marriage ceremony (cf. kañĕkh); Virgo, the sign of the zodiac (El. kin, Śiv. 478, K. 131). -dān m. (amongst Hindūs) the giving of a girl in marriage (Śiv. 685, 687). -koṭᵘ m. 'a virgin-boy', a boy still unmarried. -shrān m. the ceremonial bathing of a girl at her marriage or on a similar religious occasion (Hindū).
f. (sg. dat. kañĕki), an unmarried girl, a virgin, i.q. kañĕ 1 (Rām. 624-5; K. 703, 765-81); u.w. ref. to a married woman suspected of unchastity, but proved to be chaste (Rām. 1058).

adj. c.g. possessing stones, stony, rocky, full of stones, stony country (El. kanyal). --van -- m. a forest which is full of stones and nothing else; N. of a well-known village in the Dachinpôrᵘ Pargana of Kashmīr.

adj. c.g. possessing a flank (cf. köñᵘ̈ 1) used --˚ as in aḍa-kāñĕl (p. 11a, l. 38), half lying on one side; hence almost confined to bed; okᵘ- kāñĕl (p. 19a, l. 18), possessing only one flank or rib; hence having no strength.
adv. and postpos., i.q. kani 2, q.v. Cf. ạndᵃra-kanĕn (p. 32b, l. 5), ōra-kᵒ (p. 41b, l. 23), az-kᵒ (p. 74a, l. 20), and hĕri-kᵒ (p. 367a, l. 39).

f. the topmost story, or attic, of a house of several stories, in which the tenants live during the summer season (K.Pr. 101, 219 kánin; cf. brörⁱ-kāñĕñ, p. 125b, l. 37, and köñī and köñᵘ̈ 4). kāñĕñi-pŏhur m. id., i.q. köñᵘ̈-pŏhur, see köñᵘ̈ 4, p. 461a, l. 1.

m. the condition of being one-eyed, monocularness (cf. dōla-kᵒ, p. 211b, l. 17); one-sidedness, unevenness (cf. aṭa-kᵒ, p. 56a, l. 24); clumsiness (cf. atha-kᵒ, p. 59a, l. 37). --˚ imperfection, disease (cf. baba-kᵒ, p. 77a, l. 35).
f. a heap of stones that are of moderate size (Gr.Gr. 93).

m. the fire-receptacle or fire-place, kept burning in former times in the court- yard of a Kāshmīrī house for the benefit of guests, etc., and distinct from the three religious domestic fires of a Hindū; (at the present day) a fire-place or brazier lit in the open air on mountain sides, etc., for the sake of warmth or for keeping off wild beasts. nāra-kang, a fire-receptacle; hence, met. a shower of sparks (falling on a person) (Rām. 1082). Cf. kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈, which is the fem. of this word in a dim. sense (Gr.Gr. 33, 37).
adj. c.g. poor, indigent (El.). Cf. kankāl.

f. a hair-comb, esp. the comb used by women (cf. kanguwᵘ 2) (El. kangain). --wālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to comb one's hair (H. v, 4). ¶ kangañi-gorᵘ m. a comb-maker or comb-seller (El. kanganyigur, a brush- maker (sic); Gr.Gr. 149); a man whose profession it is to card the wool from which pashmīna cloth is made. -phuṭᵘ̈ f. an old broken comb.
f. N. of a large village in the Lār district of Kashmīr, on the right bank of the river Sind, and the ancient Kaṅkaṇapura (RT.Tr. II, 490).
m. a large portable brazier (El.). See kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈.
a kind of water-chestnut, with a very thick shell and long projecting horns (L. 354).
(? spelling), a kind of millet, Setaria italica (L. 337, 366).
or kanguwᵘ 1 m. the shoulder-blade, scapula (said to resemble a comb in shape) (El. kangū, Gr.M.). kangȧvⁱ- türᵘ̈ f. the end or point of the collar-bone.
m. (pl. nom. kangan 3), a kind of bracelet. kangan tulȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. 'to lift up one's bracelets', to bully, tyrannize over.
m. the kind of hair-comb used by men (cf. kangañ) (El. kangū). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to comb (El.). ¶ kangȧvⁱ-gorⁱ m. a comb-maker or comb-seller. -phuṭᵘ̈ f. an old broken comb.

or kanĕn (cf. kinⁱ and kun) postpos. governing abl. or, in the case of animate rational beings, the dat. Considered by native grammarians to be a sec. suff. It is used in various ways, viz.:-- ¶ (1) Governing the abl. of adverbs of place and other words, it indicates 'on to', and is u.w. vbs. of putting, and the like, as in anda-kani, (put) on the outer side (p. 31b, l. 43); apāri-kani, (put) on the other side (p. 39a, l. 30); ōra-kani, (put) on there, on the far side, or (H. v, 2) in that direction (p. 41b, l. 21); bŏna-kani, (put) down (p. 110b, l. 18); brō̃ṭha-kani, (put) in front, (lay) before, (sit down) before (Rām. 268) (p. 128a, l. 39); hĕri-kani, (put) at the top (p. 367a, l. 39); khōwari-kani, (put) on the left side (Śiv. 1090) (p. 425b, l. 15); pĕṭha- kani, (put) above (everyone else), in the place of honour (Śiv. 1716), and so on. ¶ Often the idea of 'putting', etc. is dropped, and the compound is used simply as an adv. or post.pos. (governing dat.), as in anda-kani, outside (Śiv. 422); bŏna-kani, below (H. iii, 2); brō̃ṭha (or bōnṭha) -kani, in front; garas brō̃ṭha-kani, opposite the house (Gr.M.; so H. ii, 3; iii, 1; viii, 11, etc.); labi-kani, at the edge (Śiv. 842, 1445, 1570); pĕṭha-kani, above, on the top of (H. viii, 1); wŏzali-kani (a bite) on the red side (of an apple) (K.Pr. 238). ¶ In all the above cases it may be put into the genitive, and then forms and adjective indicating 'of or belonging to such-and-such a position', as in anda-kanyukᵘ (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of or belonging to what is outside, of or belonging to the outside; apāri-kanyukᵘ, of or belonging to the opposite side; ōra-kanyukᵘ, of or belonging to the far side; bŏna-kanyukᵘ, of or belonging to below, nether; brō̃ṭha-kanyukᵘ, of or belonging to what is in front; hĕri-kanyukᵘ, of or belonging to something on the top, and so on. ¶ (2) So far we have dealt with kani as a postposition governing the ablative. The word with which it is compounded, anda, apāri, ōra, and so forth is put in the ablative because it is governed by kani. But adverbs of place can be placed independently in the ablative, and then indicate motion from. Thus: ōr, there; ōra, from there: yōr, here; yōra, from here, and so on. kani may also be compounded with these ablatives without changing their meaning. Here it is not a question of kani as a postposition governing the ablative, but one of kani as an adverb being suffixed, without changing the meaning, to another adverb indicating motion from. Thus, ōra-kani, means not only 'on there' (under 1), but also 'from there' (Śiv. 1674, Rām. 946) under this rule. Similarly we have hōra-kani, from there, thence; kōra-kani, whence? (Rām. 949); pata-kani, from behind (Śiv. 1734); tōra-kani, thence; yōra-kani, hence, or (relative) whence (Gr.Gr. 159); brō̃ṭha-kani, from opposite, as well as 'in front'. Similarly, with nouns, we have ösa-kani (issuing) from the mouth (H. viii, 7); tālawa-kani (down) from the ceiling (H. viii, 6). ¶ Similarly, as an adverb, kani is sometimes added pleonastically to an adverb of place, without causing a change of meaning. A good example is pĕṭh-kani (s.v. pĕṭh), above, in the upper portion; hence, in the place of honour (K.Pr. 103) (cf. pĕṭha-kani, ab.); tami pĕṭhⁱ-kani, on the top of that, in addition to that (H. iii, 8). ¶ (3) As a postpos. kani may also indicate the reason for anything, as in ạdᵃri-kani (p. 15a, l. 45), (money) for the sweetmeats; ami-kani or awa-kani (p. 54b, l. 37; p. 55b, l. 36) for that reason, therefore; humi-kani or huwa-kani, therefore; kami-kani or kawa-kani, wherefore? tami-kani or tawa-kani, therefore; yĕmi-kani or yĕwa-kani, wherefore; yimi-kani or yiwa-kani, for this reason (Gr.Gr. 159). ¶ (4) As a further development of this sense it may often be translated by 'for', in the sense of 'as a substitute for', 'instead of', 'in the place of', 'to serve as'. The following examples are mainly taken from Śiv., but the use runs through all literature; ashĕ-kani, (blood) instead of tears (Rām. 1483); bāri-kani, (silver used) as plaster (Rām. 568); dāji-kani, in place of a dowry (Śiv. 1677); dūpa-dīpa-kᵒ, instead of incense and lamps (Śiv. 1692); dāra-kᵒ, in place of wood (Śiv. 337); dāryau-kᵒ, to serve as casements (Śiv. 340); kaharau-kᵒ, serving as palankeen-bearers (Śiv. 84); laṭi-kᵒ laʦhulᵘ, a besom used as a tail (K.Pr. 124); mŏkta-kᵒ, instead of a pearl (Śiv. 1145); mŏkaṭa-kᵒ, in place of a diadem (Śiv. 892); pakhᵃcau-kᵃ, in place of the side-arms of a spinning-wheel (Śiv. 1014); pōshĕ-kᵒ, instead of a flower (Śiv. 863; cf. 1692); rūda-kᵒ, instead of rain (Śiv. 713); rathabāna-kᵒ, serving as a charioteer (Śiv. 1146); sumi-kᵒ, to serve as a bridge (Śiv. 1793); sŏna-kᵒ, instead of gold (Śiv. 169); traṭi-kᵒ, serving as a necklace (Śiv. 1557); wardanau-kᵒ, (bark) for a bridal garment (Rām. 763); yikili-kᵒ, to serve for a beam (K.Pr. 41); yōñĕ-kᵒ, instead of a sacrificial thread (Śiv. 1014). ¶ (5) As a postpos. governing a word signifying time or season, it indicates uncertainty (Gr.Gr. 159), as in ṻtra-kani, about the day before yesterday (p. 68b, l. 21); az-kani, about to-day, perhaps to-day (p. 74a, l. 19); brō̃ṭhus-kani, about, or perhaps, next year (p. 129a, l. 32); dạhum-kani, on about the tenth lunar day (p. 201a, l. 43); dã̄-phulạyi-kani, at about the season of paddy flowering (dã̄-phulay, p. 230b, l. 12); hāra-kani, about the month of Hār (p. 343b, l. 44); harᵃda-kani, at about autumn (p. 348a, l. 12); kölⁱ-kĕth-kani, on about the day after to-morrow (kölⁱ-kĕth, p. 434b, l. 9); pagāh-kani, perhaps to-morrow (pagāh). ¶ (6) Examples of other relations indicated by this postposition are:--āmpa-kani, by means of beak-to-beak feeding (H. viii, 1; perhaps incorr. for kȧnⁱ 3); kuni-kani, in any way (H. xii, 13); pata-kani, afterwards (H. x, 1); thürᵘ̈-kani, (turning) backwards (H. v, 4). ¶ In all the above (whether under head 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6) kani can be put into the genitive as under head 1, to indicate of or belonging to the motion from, reason, or indefinite time indicated.
(YZ. 263), for kãh, and kenih (YZ. 200) for kĕ˜h, for both of which, see kē̃h.
m. a slave (El. who says it is m., but in other languages the word means 'a slave-girl', and so also YZ. 21).

or kanjĕr 1 m. (f. kanjĕrĕñ, q.v.), a prostitute's husband, a souteneur, a brothel-keeper. This is a Hindī word, and is i.q. the Kāshmīrī gān (K.Pr. 96). -pônᵘ m. conduct like that of a souteneur, scandalous infamous and shameless conduct. -tônᵘ m., id. -wān m. a place where these men congregate.
f. a souteneur's wife, i.e. a prostitute (see kanjar).
f. conduct like that of a prostitute's husband or souteneur; scandalous, infamous, and shameless conduct.
m. (f. kaṅköjᵘ̈), one who is wretchedly poor (Śiv. 1216, 1723); one who is a persistent beggar; one who is miserly, avaricious. Cf. kangāl.
m. a species of Elæagnus (El.). -marʦ m. Elæagnus orientalis (El. kankol mirich).
? m. the apparatus for securing blankets, etc., consisting of two ropes attached to the back of a Kāshmīrī saddle (H. xi, 9).

m. (f. kānᵃ̇jᵃ̇, etc., q.v.), a stalk or soft branch (e.g. of a gourd-vine) (cf. al, p. 22b, l. 20); the second crop of young sprouts coming out in spring from the roots of vegetables that have been cut in the preceding year. These are also used for food. kānȧlⁱ-hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), the second crop, etc., as ab.
m. a basket-weaver (El. kányúl), esp. one who weaves the external basket-work of the kāngrī or portable brazier of Kashmīr, see köñᵘ̈ 2 (L. 458 kainyal).
m. a servant who works for his food and gets no other wages (rare). Cf. gura- kanōra, p. 298b, l. 16.
m. (sg. dat. kanṭhas), the throat (El., also kö̃ṭh, q.v.; K. 60, 583, 927). --thawun -- m.inf. to remember (El. kanṭ thawun), know by rote.
m. (in building) a beam (cf. ḍȧmbⁱ-kⁱ, p. 218a, l. 13); esp. one of the main beams of a Kāshmīrī cantilever bridge, the roadway of which it supports. Cf. kạdᵃla-kᵃ (p. 385a, l. 37).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. kānyōv), to be, or become, one-eyed; met. to become lopsided, incomplete on one side; to become maimed, to lose a limb (esp. one of a pair of limbs); to be defeated, conquered (Gr.Gr. xiv).
m. a law, regulation (Gr.M.); bē-kānūn, illegal, unlawful (Gr.M.).
m. the maple, Acer (El., L. 79, 81, kanar).
adj. (f. kañivᵘ̈), made of stone (Rām. 635; H. v, 4); met. stony, without feeling (YZ. 483).
adj. (f. kāñivᵘ̈), made of the withies called köñᵘ̈, see köñᵘ̈ 2.
f. a girl, virgin, daughter (Śiv. 33, 35, 45, 1453, 1491; K. 901). Cf. kañĕ 1.
one of the best kinds of white rice (L. 332, 463), ? i.q. koñᵘ 1.

m. a kind of mortar cut out of a large block of wood, in which grain is husked by being pounded, a husking mortar (K.Pr. 116; W. 2, kans; L. 80, 462; Śiv. 1533). Cf. dã̄-kanz, p. 230a, l. 31, and kã̄s. --aʦun -- m.inf. to enter a mortar, to put one's head into a mortar, to put oneself into such a position as to be subjected to great calamity; (as a punishment) to be compelled to go about wearing a heavy mortar as if it were a hat, and thus to be made an object of general derision (K.Pr. 136). -muhulᵘ m. mortar and pestle, the pestle and mortar, as ab. (L. 463, kanz ta mohl). ¶ kanza-kŏkürᵘ̈ f. a hen that haunts the neighbourhood of a husking-mortar for the sake of the scattered grains; met. a girl-child that acts similarly with the same object. -kö̆mᵘ̈ f. the fine bran found in a mortar after husking grain; see kö̆mᵘ̈. -kuʦürᵘ̈ f. 'a mortar whelp (f.)', hence a poverty-stricken woman or girl, who haunts husking mortars on the chance of picking up a few grains for food. Cf. -kŏkürᵘ̈, ab.
m. a large ball or globe of stone or lac; met. a round fat globular-shaped man.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. konzᵘ) to singe a plucked fowl, or the like before cooking; met. (in gambling or the like) to render a person penniless, 'to pluck a pigeon.' ¶ konzᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. künzᵘ̈- müʦᵘ̈), singed, as ab.; rendered penniless, as ab. ¶ kanzan-phakh m. (sg. dat. -phakas), the smell of singeing, as ab., or the like.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kạnzᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. kạnzᵃrun, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kạnzᵒrᵒ), to render a person penniless (in gambling, or the like). Cf. kanzun.
kānʦhāh; for kãʦhāh, kã̄ʦhāh; see kē̃h.

kānᵘ̈jᵘ̈, or kānüjᵘ̈ (f. of kānolᵘ, q.v.), a filament or tendril of a plant (cf. dachĕ-kᵒ, p. 185b, l. 47, and drāman-kᵒ, p. 245b, l. 31); the fine wire used to unite the segments of a necklace, to hang an earring from the ear, or the like (cf. dūra-kᵒ, p. 238b, l. 49); the handle of a kāgᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or portable brazier (K.Pr. 129, kánjih). kānᵃjĕtulañĕ f. pl. inf. to root up the (root-) filaments; met. ferociously to destroy root and branch, to exhibit oppressive violence.

m. (sg. dat. kạnᵃkas), wheat (El. kạnak; Gr.M.; L. 330, kanak). ¶ kạnᵃka-ʦŏ̈ṭᵃ f. a cake of wheaten meal (Gr.Gr. 74). -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), coarsely-ground wheat (W. 115, kanakwāt; wāṭh here means 'any coarsely-ground grain' and not, as W. says, 'a seam').
or kāñᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a dim. of kônᵘ 1. See pana-kᵒ, p. 734b, l. 33, sᵃtra-kᵃ, p. 947b, l. 24, and yōñĕ-kᵒ, p. 1201a, l. 8.

or kanürᵘ̈ f. the part of a spinning wheel on which the little wheel rests (El. kanar m.) (it is wound round with grass string); a separate grass string or rope fastened along the edge of the top and sole of the grass sandals used in Kashmīr, in order to fasten the whole together.

postpos. governing abl. (cf. kinⁱ, of which it is a variant). It also governs the dative if the governed noun or pronoun is or refers to a human being. It indicates locality, as in kala-kȧnⁱ, at the head end (of an animal), and laṭi-kȧnⁱ, at the tail end (H. xi, 9); route or method, as in dāri-kȧnⁱ (flung out) through the window (H. v, 4); and, esp., motion from, as in yĕs-kȧnⁱ, from whom (it will escape) (H. ii, 8).

m. a skull, cranium, skull-bone (Śiv. 661). The Hindū god Śiva is believed to wear a necklace of skulls. ¶ kapāla-māl f. a necklace of skulls (Śiv. 266). -mālā-dar m. he who wears a necklace of skulls, N. of Śiva (Śiv. 1171). -mōʦan m. N. of a sacred spring in Kashmīr, near Shupiyan. It is the Skt. Kapālamōcana, and is said to mark the spot where Śiva cleared himself from the sin attaching to him after cutting off Brahmā's head (RT.Tr. II, 472; Śiv. 1171).
(Śiv. 11) Sanskrit, m. sg. voc., O thou with braided hair (applied to the god Gaṇēśa).

f. cotton (seeds and all) (El., K.Pr. 181, L. 330 kapás); the cotton plant (El. m., Gr.M.). --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to pluck cotton from the plant, to gather cotton (K.Pr. 80). kana kapas kaḍüñᵘ̈, to pluck cotton from the ear, to attempt an impossibility (K.Pr. 94). --wanüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to speak falsely (in malice or to deceive). ¶ kapasi-düjᵘ̈ f. a plot of ground planted with cotton shrubs. -ḍār m. a field in which cotton shrubs are grown, or which is suitable for growing them. -kôḍᵘ m. (his wife is kapasi-köḍⁱ-bāy), a man whose profession it is to extract the seeds from raw cotton in a machine for that purpose, a cotton cleaner. -kulᵘ m. the cotton shrub. -kọ̆thᵘ m. a sack stuffed full of cotton, a bale of cotton; met. a very stout man. -pōsh m. the light yellow flower of the cotton-shrub (L.V. 102); met. anything of a light yellow colour. -ṭọ̆ṭᵘ m. the cotton-pod. -ṭŏṭh m. (sg. dat. -ṭŏṭas), a small unripe or imperfect cotton-pod.
f. (sg. dat. kapatüñᵘ̈), the cutting out of the cloth into properly shaped pieces when making a garment, 'cutting out' (Gr.Gr. 121); met. dividing out into portions genl.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kapaṭanôwᵘ), to cause (so-and-so) to cut clothes; to cause clothes to be cut (caus. of kapaṭun, q.v., Gr.Gr. 171).
