conj. 1 (1 p.p. kapaṭôwᵘ), i.q. kapaṭun. kapaṭôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (1 p.p. kapaṭövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. kapoṭᵘ-motᵘ. See kapaṭun.

m. (sg. dat. kapaṭas), deceit, hypocrisy (Śiv. 557, 572, 588); esp. wearing a cloth on the head, or to have the head covered in order to deceive others, so as to manifest one's assumed high character or high position; kapaṭa-ʦarĕth m. conduct of deceit, jugglery, deception (L.V. 38).
adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. kapaṭas), deceitful, dishonest, fraudulent, insincere, false, hypocritical.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. kapoṭᵘ; 2 p.p. kapacyōv), to cut out cloth for making a garment, to cut out clothes (Gr.Gr. 120, YZ. 505, Śiv. 1597). ¶ kapoṭᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. kapüṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, sg. dat. kapacĕ-maʦĕ), cut out (of cloth, as ab.).

m. (sg. dat. kaphas), phlegm (one of the three humours of the body) (El. kaf). -ganḍ m. a kind of tumour in the throat; swelling in the throat of cattle (L. 459, kafgan). --karun -- (with confusion with خفہ کرن) m.inf. to display anger (quasi, so that one splutters forth phlegm and spittle). ¶ kapha-loʦhᵘ m. a globular lump of thickened phlegm.

m. (sg. dat. kāphas), (in Muslim legend) a fabulous mountain, supposed to surround the world and to bound the extreme horizon. kŏh-ĕ-qāf (Persian), id. Hence, in Kashmīr, in Śiv. 206 kŏh-kāph (pl. dat. kŏhan- kāphan), (in) mountains and Qāfs; hence in mountains and mountain forests.

m. grave clothes, a winding-sheet, shroud (used both by Hindūs and Muslims. In the case of Hindūs, it is burnt with the corpse) (El., L. 263, kafan). nölⁱ kafan prāwun, to put on a shroud, to don a robe of mourning (worn by a person as if ready for death and burial) (YZ. 22); to engage in a perilous enterprise, to risk life, to court death.
m. a bird's cage, a coop (Rām. 405).
f. a dress resembling a shroud worn by a faqīr or Musalmān mendicant. It reaches to the feet, and opens in front.
adj. (f. kapörimᵘ̈), of or belonging to what direction, of what place? (Gr.Gr. 151).
adv. where? in what place? kapôrᵘ-kun adv. whither? to or on to what place? ¶ kapörⁱ adv. whence? from what direction? u.w. vbs. of motion (Gr.Gr. 159); in what direction? (Gr.Gr. 159).

m. cotton cloth, calico (Gr.Gr. 162-3, Gr.M., K.Pr. 221); (sg. or pl.) clothes made of calico, apparel, garments genl. (Gr.M.); zᵃh jōra kaparȧkⁱ, two suits of clothes (Gr.M.). ¶ kapar-chal f. a piece of calico, esp. when long and stretched out (Gr.Gr. 162). -dōra m. a doubled piece of calico, used as a quilt or for a similar purpose. -mĕkarāz f. a pair of scissors for cutting calico; met. a termagant, a scold (male or female). -rĕl f. a very long and very narrow strip of calico. -rē̃ʦh f. a small piece of cotton cloth, a little rag (Gr.Gr. 163). -thān m. a roll of uncut calico, calico in the piece, a thān of calico (Rām. 911). -tilim f. a long narrow piece of a calico, a strip of calico (Gr.Gr. 163). -tᵃr f. a long strip of calico, only an inch or two wide (Gr.Gr. 162). -ʦādar f. a sheet of calico worn over the upper part of the body, a chuddar, a cotton shawl (El.). --ʦhunȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to put on clothes; to wear clothes (Gr.M.). -ʦumüṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ʦumachĕ), playful pinches given to a child or other person when wearing new clothes for the first time, 'nips for new.' -wôñᵘ m. a calico seller, a draper. -zŏv f. a kind of louse that fastens itself into clothes; met. one who clings closely to another in the hope of his supplying some need, a parasite. ¶ kapara-hanā f. a piece of cotton cloth (Gr.M.).
m. i.q. kapur. This form is used in villages and by children.

adv. when? at what time? (Gr.Gr. 156; Gr.M.; L.V. 87; YZ. 253; W. 94; Rām. 69, 1209, 1211-2; K. 394, 849, 937; H. ii, 4); when? (expecting a negative answer); hence, practically equivalent to 'never' (Śiv. 1790-1, in each case with a pun on kar, impve. sg. 2 of karun, to do); Rām. 327, 363, 380-1, et passim; ḍĕṭha kar, a long time ago (Gr.Gr. 257). -bögⁱ or -bögin adv. about when? at what time? -hyuhᵘ adv. about when? u.w. vbs. of coming, going, or the like. -kani adv. at what time? -sanā adv. when? (with a shade of doubt or anxiety in the question) (Gr.Gr. 180-1). -sanā-bögⁱ or -sanā- bögin adv. about when? (with a shade of doubt or anxiety) (Gr.Gr. 181). -tām adv. at sometime or other (in the immediate past); till when? (W. 94); also (doubtfully) when? as in kartām (or tāñ, etc.) āv, did he come at any time? if so, when? (Gr.Gr. 256; Rām. 1012, kar-tāñ). -tāmath adv., id. -tāñ adv., id. (Rām. 1012). -tāñĕth adv., id. ¶ karukᵘ adj. (f. karücᵘ̈), of or belonging to what time? of when? (Gr.Gr. 151).

m. a letter, a syllable, as in ōm-kār, q.v. p. 27b, l. 49 (L.V. 34; Śiv. 50, 914, 1760, 1789). a-kār, the letter a, the first letter of the alphabet, and hence used, like our 'alpha' in 'alpha and omega', as an epithet of the Deity (Śiv. 1771).
m. a beam or rafter in kara-ganḍ m. a beam under the roof of a house connecting the front and back walls so as to strengthen them. Cf. kürᵘ̈ 4.

m. an act, a deed (Śiv. 323, 913, 1018, 1721, 1796); work, operation, labour, action (K.Pr. 96, 210, 227; YZ. 26; Śiv. 8, 1778; Rām. 28, 62, 64, 86, etc.; H. v, 12; xi, 2, 10); occupation, service, profession (Gr.M.; L.V. 108) (dĕn-kār, the day's work); work, the result of work (e.g. embroidery-work, mosaic-work, etc.) (Śiv. 337, 1796); cf. cikan-kār, p. 170a, l. 48, ḍūrⁱ-kār, p. 239b, l. 37; mĕtra-kār, s.v. mẹ̆thᵃr. kār-ĕ-kalamdönī کار کلمدآنی m. papier-maché work, so called because the best specimens of the old work were pen-boxes (kalam-dönī, q.v., p. 439b, l. 37) (L. 378). ¶ This word is common --˚, in the sense of 'work', 'doing', as in jai-jai-kār, 'doing victory! victory!', i.e. making an ovation (K. 10, 11, 54, etc.); viwāha-kār, marriage ceremonies (Śiv. 411); pŏrushĕ-kār, the deeds of a man, manliness (Śiv. 1791), and so on. ¶ kār-kömᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. kāras-kāmĕ), work and business, all the work of a person or connected with some affair. ¶ kāra-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is always engaged in work, a busy person, one who has no leisure.
in kar-kar karun m.inf. (onomat.) to make a rustling or crackling sound (as made by new calico, new paper, etc.). Cf. kᵃr.
in kar-nāv 1 f. (for 2, see s.v. karnāv 2) a large ferry boat, established and supported by some public-spirited person for carrying people free across a river (El. karanáv, a ferryman).
impve. sg. 2 of karun 1 and 2, qq.v.
in kāra wôñᵘ m., i.q. the preceding.

m. a hand (obs.); an elephant's trunk (see p. 354b, l. 30) (El. karra). -pönʦokᵘ m. (in Hindū chronology) the period of five lunar asterisms named in Sanskrit Hasta, Citrā, Svāti, Viśākhā, and Anurādhā. They are looked upon as an auspicious period for putting on new clothes. ¶ kari-phērañĕ m. the act of clenching the fist; extreme hunger.

m. the pea, Pisum sativum (L. 330 karré; Gr.Gr. 164; H. xii, 16-7). -düjᵘ̈ f. a piece of cloth containing peas, a kerchief full of pease (cooked or uncooked. Children carry peas in this way for eating); a plot of ground in which peas are cultivated. -dāl f. pease-pottage, dāl made with pease; split pease. -hĕm f. (sg. dat. karas-hĕmi), pease and beans. -muṭhᵘ m. (sg. dat. karas-muṭhis), pease and pulse (Phaseolus aconitifolius) (these are often cooked together). -mǖ̃thᵃr f. (sg. dat. kara-mǖ̃thᵃri), a pease-invitation. When a Hindū child in school is being taught the alphabet, on his beginning to learn to read and write consonants joined to vowels, and conjunct consonants, parched pease and pulse (Phaseolus aconitifolius) are distributed by his family to his fellow-pupils. The invitation to this distribution is called by the above name. -muṭhⁱ-mũ̄̈thⁱr m. (sg. dat. -muṭhⁱ-mũ̄̈th90 ᵃras), the distribution of parched pease and pulse, as ab. -pholᵘ m. a single pea; a small number of peas, a few peas (Gr.Gr. 164); (in plur.) pease, many peas.
in kara-phar m. power, greatness, great influence (from riches, high office, or the like).
in kara-môrᵘ m. failing of the limbs, feebleness, weakness, exhaustion, being done up (resulting from a long journey, extreme exertion, or the like).
in kara-wôñᵘ m. boiled water (given to invalids to whom fresh water is forbidden). Cf. nūna-kara-wôñᵘ, s.v. nūn.
f. (sg. dat. karā- hüʦᵘ̈), aversion, dislike, disgust, loathing, horror, abhorrence, detestation; in Kāshmīrī, usually with ref. to food.
m. generosity, nobleness, excellence; grace, favour, courtesy; success (El.).
f. (sg. dat. karāmüʦᵘ̈), a miracle (K.Pr. 86). The gender and, consequently, the declension of this word are uncertain.

m. a cause (see bel.) (L.V. 75, Rām. 1421, K. 174); a reason (Gr.M.; Rām. 61, 1300; K. 4); a motive, purpose; a means (L.V. 76 kārȧnⁱ pranavȧkⁱ, by means of the praṇava, see bel.); (according to Śaiva theology) a causal deity or creator of the universe. There are three of these, viz. Brahmā (the Creator), Viṣṇu (the Preserver), and Mahēśvara or Rudra (the Destroyer), the last-named being one of the forms of Śiva (Śiv. 64, 678, 1158, 1466, 1728). There are also five causes of the universe, viz. the above three, Sadāśiva (Śiva as the lord of the manifested universe), and Īśvara, or Śiva himself. These five are represented by the praṇava, or mystic syllable ōṁ, which is said to be formed from the union of the pentad a, u, m, bindu, and nāda (see bĕnd), or, again, by the five mystic syllables Śi, vā, ya, na, and maḥ, which together are considered to express the same meaning as ōṁ (Śiv. 914, 1520). ādi-kāran, a first cause; ami kārana, for this reason (Gr.M.); wŏtpatti-kāran, a cause of origin, a Creator (Gr.M.).
pl. dat. of kār 1 and 2, qq.v.
n.ag. (f. karanāwavüñᵘ̈), one who causes to do or to be done (Śiv. 247), etc., see karanāwun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. karanôwᵘ), caus. of karun, q.v. in all its senses (Gr.Gr. 170); to cause to make or do (Gr.M.; Śiv. 735, 740, 1859, 1876); to cause to be made or done (Śiv. 1309, 1315, 1467, 1648, 1693, 1749, 1816, 1877; Rām. 589; K. 454, 951, 957, 990; H. x, 13; xii, 24); to cause to ejaculate (Śiv. 127, 1915).
f. the goddess over each sense or organ of the body; in the plural, the total of these goddesses, the sum of the senses, the vital principles (Śiv. 1493).

m. fixedness, fixity, permanence; consistency, stability, firmness, constancy; quietude, quiet, peace; patient waiting, patience; settlement, determination, confirmation; agreement, engagement (Gr.M.): reality, certainty, truth. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to wait patiently.
adj. c.g. fixed, firm, settled, established; (of health) sound, strong, hearty (Gr.M.).
in karārakarāra adv. very slowly, gradually and slowly.
f. wages for doing or making (Gr.Gr. 129).
m.pl. N. of a sept of Kāshmīrī Brāhmaṇas living in Śrīnagar.

n.ag. (f. karavüñᵘ̈), one who does or makes, a doer, a maker, etc., in all the meanings of karun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 105, 192; Śiv. 63, 196, 215, 282, 598, 645, 737, 852, 858-9, 1018, 1421, 1507, 1520, 1523, 1888; K. 200, 218, 386, 400, 402, et passim).
m. the Hindū overseer of a village, a government official whose duty it is to collect the Mahārāja's share of the grain (El.; K.Pr. 139; L. 402, 421; H. ix, 1).
f. N. of one of the cucurbitaceæ, Momordica charantia (El. karela). karēla-bọ̆ngᵃr f. a kind of bracelet (El.).
m. the condition of never having born children, the condition of any female up to the time she bears her first child. See kürᵘ̈ 2.

(? spelling) m. a plateau or raised plain; esp. one of the six large cultivated plateaux in the Kashmīr Valley (El. karewah, q.v. for particulars). The word is said to be of Persian origin (cf. RT.Tr. II, 425), but this is very doubtful. It does not occur in Persian dictionaries. The true Kāshmīrī word for these plateaux is wuḍar, q.v. (L. 320).
m. N. of a town and tract of country in Baltistān forty miles east of Dras.
m. N. of a village about ten miles south of Śrīnagar.
m. N. of a certain weight, the fourth part of a pal which = about 1/10 of a lb.
f. a mason's or plasterer's trowel (El. karin m.; Gr.Gr. 120, f.).

f. (among Hindūs) a line of flour or meal drawn by the performer of the Anvaṣṭakā śrāddha ceremony a year after the death of his father or other relative. The Anvaṣṭakā is the ninth day of one of the four months Āgrahāyaṇa, Pauṣa, Māgha, and Phālguna (or, according to others, of one of the first three of these).
f. (sg. dat. karkaṭi), the sign Cancer (El. kurukauṭ, Śiv. 479, K. 131).
m. the proprietor of a factory; esp. the proprietor of a shawl factory, a shawl manufacturer (El.).

or kalki m. (in Hindū mythology) N. of the tenth incarnation of the god Viṣṇu; it is yet to come. He is to appear mounted on a white horse and wielding a drawn sword as a destroyer of the wicked (Śiv. 862, karki). The Sanskrit form is kalki.
in kārkōṭa-nāg m. N. of Nāga or sacred spring in the Pīr Pantsāl Range near the Tōshĕmaidān Pass. It takes its name from the Nāga, or snake-god, Kārkōṭa, see RT.Tr. iii, 490; II, 399 (Śiv. 1164).

m. an action, a deed (L.V. 58, 61, 75; W. 110; Śiv. 105, 285, 1013, 1213, 1511, 1539, 1737, 1849; Rām. 1202; K. 968, 1092, 1096); often used in special senses, e.g. a deed done in a previous life, and affecting one's present life by its fruits of happiness or sorrow (Śiv. 171, 425, 1801); hence, what is fated, a man's present fate (K.Pr. 187; Śiv. 533, 1511, 1665; Rām. 208, 255, 1076, 1202, 1556); Fate, personified as a god (Rām. 581); a religious rite, the performance of religious obligations (cf. p. 244a, l. 26, and 244b, l. 27); esp. funeralrites, obsequies (Rām. 311); a pious or good action or work (Śiv. 51, 448, 598, 657, et passim; Rām. 67, 999; K. 7, 717, 1070). nitĕ karm, a continual act, an act done at regular intervals; esp. the daily obligatory rites in a Hindū household (K. 968); nitĕ karma, by continual action, continually, perpetually (Śiv. 1541). (In Hindūism) actions are of three kinds, good actions, sins, and actions that are partly good and partly bad (miśra) (Śiv. 1844). ¶ karma-boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), one who has a great fate, one who is very prosperous. -bajĕr m. great prosperity. -hīn (Śiv. 1473, 1554) or -hyūnᵘ (Śiv. 1216, 1738), adj. (f. -hīñᵘ̈), deprived of (the fruits of) former virtuous acts, luckless, one who has no good acts to his credit. -khanḍĕth f. (sg. dat. -khanḍë˘ʦᵘ̈), the shattering of the results of good actions done in a former life, i.e. great bad fortune. -lēkhā or -līkhā, f., i.q. -rᵃkh, bel., the lines of fate on the forehead (Śiv. 1477, 1492, 1511); personified as a goddess (Śiv. 1143, 1152); a person's fate, destiny (Rām. 40, 120). -lônᵘ m. fate (K.Pr. 219; Śiv. 449, 643; Rām. 120, 302, 1015, 1034, 1036, 1187, 1768); a woman's destined fate (considered as a reward of former good actions), a husband (Śiv. 690, 822, 940, 945). -phal m. the fruit of good actions, the resultant fate springing from former actions (Śiv. 1241, 1828). -rᵃkh or (L.V. 107) karmüñᵘ̈ rᵃkh f. (sg. dat. -rᵃkhi), the lines of fate, supposed to be inscribed by Brahmā on the forehead of the skull on the sixth night after birth and indicating the future good or evil fortune of the bearer. -rēkhā or -rīkhā f., id. -sĕd f. (sg. dat. -së̆zᵘ̈), success in action; hence, the successful carrying out, or due performance of pious actions (Śiv. 1830). -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a master of (good) fate, one who is extremely prosperous.
adj. c.g. one who is very prosperous, one who has great good fortune (Śiv. 495); one who is wont to perform pious actions, of a pious nature (Śiv. 427, 671, 687, 1070-3).
f. (sg. dat. karmāyë˘ʦᵘ̈), the good or evil fate which is the result of deeds done in a former life. Cf. karm.
adj. c.g. skilled, clever, diligent, hard-working; performing (good) works, very virtuous (Rām. 634).
m. ivy, Hedera helix (El., L. 461 kirmil).

m. (for 1, see p. 465a, l. 47), N. of a tract of country in the Uttar Pargana of Kashmīr, lying between the River Kishĕngangā and the Kājnāg Range, the ancient Karṇāha or Karṇāḍha. In it is the ancient Tīrtha or bathing place of Shĕrdi, sacred to the goddess Śāradā. See RT.Tr. viii, 2485, and II, 405.
f. a musical horn; the largest brass trumpet that sounds the bass; a trumpet, bugle, clarion, etc. (K. 1009).
f. (sg. dat. karniki), the root of the nose (below the centre of the forehead).
m. the boatman of a free ferry boat, see kar-nāv 1, p. 465a, l. 47 (El. karanāv).

or kŏrōr card. ten millions, a crore (El. karór; Gr.Gr. 80; Śiv. 619, 731, 908); karōr sūrĕ (pl.) (Śiv. 904-5) or karōra-sūrĕ (sg.) (Śiv. 936, 1155; K. 449, 881) ten million suns. ka(kŏ)rōra-bodᵘ adj. in tens of millions, in crores, unnumbered (W. 164, Rām. 1415, kaᵒ).
m. camphor (Śiv. 47). karpūra-gauram, the initial words of a Sanskrit mantra or mystic formula sacred to Śiva (Śiv. 211).

m. (sg. dat. kartāhas, Śiv. 317), a doer (Gr.M.); a maker, a creator (Śiv. 317, 911); a proprietor, master, head of a house or association. Cf. hartā-kartā, p. 351a, l. 15; nyāyĕ-kartā, a doer of justice (Gr.M.).
f. (sg. dat. kartali or kartüjᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 69), a kind of sword, small in size (El. m.; L.V. 62, 88; YZ. 278).
or körtikh m. (sg. dat. kārtikas), N. of a month, the Skt. kārttika, October-November (K.Pr. 128; W. 107, kārttik; Śiv. 470; Rām. 205).
m. N.P., in Skt. Kārttikēya or Skanda, the Mars or god of war in Hindū mythology. He was the son of Śiva, but without the direct intervention of any woman (K. 820).
m. business, profession (El. perhaps a misprint for kartūt, i.e. kartūth, q.v.).

m. (sg. dat. kartūtas), business, duty, obligation (Rām. 812); profession; conduct, behaviour (Gr.M., Rām. 1519); a course of conduct, a series of actions (K. 840); esp. (in Hindū marriage ceremonies) the obligatory gifts sent to the bride's relations, or the business of giving the dowry, or the like. Cf. kartūl.
m. a manager, chief administrator; esp. [in a Hindū religious act, such as a sacrificial oblation, funeral offering (śrāddha) or the like], the superintending official.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. kôrᵘ), to boil (something, e.g. milk, clarified butter, or other liquid) (Gr.Gr. 104, 197; L. 458); to melt (lead or the like) (Gr.M.). kôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. körᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), boiled, etc., as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. korᵘ; f. kürᵘ̈ 1). In the modern language this verb is quite regular. Its regular conjugation is given in full in Gr.Gr. But in the old Kāshmīrī of L.V. there is a form kiyĕm, I made f. things (L.V. 81), which is parallel to the Hindī kiyā. ¶ to do, perform, practise, transact (business) (passim, e.g. L.V. 34, 37; K.Pr. 78; YZ. 40, 41, 85, 100, 212, 233, 245, 264; W. 135; Śiv. 119, 121, 158, 324, etc.; Rām. 62, 105, 145, 234, 506, 590, 653, 954, 1030, 1342, 1671, 1781, etc.; K. passim; H. ii, 4, 11; iii, 8, etc.); to act (passim, e.g. Śiv. 522, 1708, etc.; Rām. 619, 846-7, 930, 1508, etc.; K. passim); to keep, open (a shop), to run (a house) (K.Pr. 66); to achieve, effect, accomplish (passim, e.g. Rām. 608, 1702, etc.); to commit (a crime) (e.g. Rām. 27, 241, 473, 504, 968, 1215); to make, form, frame (passim, e.g. L.V. 17, 65, 81, 82; K.Pr. 14, 182; YZ. 41, 49, 57, 78, 93, 142, 155, 179, 193, etc.; Śiv. 32, 373, 965, 1188, 1615, 1687, 1690, etc.; Rām. 131, 323, 418, 1152, 1298, 1301, 1320, 1372, 1545, 1571, 1783, etc.; K. passim; H. i, 1, 3, 7, etc.); to make, create (K. 210, 577); to make, draw (a line) (Gr.M.); to avail; to render, to cause to become, to turn or change (something into) (passim, e.g. Śiv. 114, 339, 712, 751, 846, 859, 1013, 1016, 1018, 1030-1, 1046, 1308, 1349, 1491, 1527, etc.; Rām. 185, 279, 306, 457, 554, 744, 839, 844, 1018, 1145, 1203, 1263, etc.; K. passim; H. x, 7; xii, 15); to make or give (a name) (Rām. 85, 534, 1282, 1296); to make a marriage, to marry a wife (Rām. 126, 136, 324, 328, 330; H. viii, 1, 2); to make (a sound), utter (speech, etc.) (Rām. 103, 389, 789, 1611); to make an utterance, to repeat words, as in shiwa shiwa karān, uttering the cry of 'Śiva, Śiva' (L.V. 65); Lȧlⁱ Lȧlⁱ karān, crying out 'Lȧlⁱ, Lȧlⁱ' or 'it is Lal, it is I Lal' (L.V. 105. Similarly Śiv. 29, 75, 127, 154, 378, 434, 539, etc.; Rām. 240, 1021, 1403). ¶ This verb is very commonly used with a substantive or adjective to form a nominal compound verb. Such so-called compounds are often hardly compounds at all, each member retaining its own meaning, as in amal karun, to do action (p. 28a, l. 9), to act, or with pĕṭh, to act upon (a request), to comply (Gr.M.); āradan karüñᵘ̈, to do worship, to worship (p. 42b, l. 45) (id.); prạkh˚ṭᵘ karun, to make manifest. At other times the compound acquires a special meaning, as in an karun, to eat food (p. 29b, l. 21); khabar karüñᵘ̈, to inform (p. 391a, l. 26); khās karith, especially, mainly (p. 417a, l. 18); mihrbönī karith, please! Such compounds will be found under the respective substantives or adjectives which form the first member. ¶ With an adjective signifying nationality, this verb signifies 'to speak the language of the country referred to', as in angrīzī karun, to do the Englishman, to speak English; köshurᵘ karun, to play the Kāshmīrī man, to speak Kāshmīrī (El.). ¶ karun hyotᵘ-motᵘ adj. (f. karüñᵘ̈hë˘ʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), be un to be done, commenced. --kyutᵘ -- adj. (f. karüñᵘ̈kiʦᵘ̈), for being done, intended to be done, suitable to be done (cf. Gr.Gr. 115). ¶ kȧrⁱ kȧrⁱ freq. part. doing (anything) over and over again (Śiv. 349). ¶ korᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. kürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), done, made, etc., as ab. ¶ karonᵘ or karunᵘ, fut. pass. part. to be done, necessary to be done (Śiv. 1230, 1305, 1749; Rām. 1781); that which must be done, a thing determined or predestined (Śiv. 67, 317; Rām. 1671). ¶ karan-grākh n.ag. (f. -grākañ), a doer, etc., one who does, etc., habitually, as ab. (Gr.Gr. 106, 193). karan-hār adj. c.g. worthy of being done, fit to be done, necessary to be done (cf. Gr.Gr. 129). -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a doer, a maker, etc., as ab. (Gr.Gr. 106, 193; Śiv. 1287). ¶ karana karān, this form implies a condition of difficulty, as in such chuh karana karān magar wȧdⁱ wȧdⁱ, he works indeed, but he does it weeping (W. 87). ¶ karanī impers. fut. part., c.g. necessary to be made, to be made (K. 72); necessary to be done (Gr.Gr. 111). ¶ karönⁱ adverbial part. on doing, etc., at the time of doing, etc. (Gr.Gr. 197). ¶ karith, having done. In the old Kāshmīrī of L.V. used instead of the modern kĕth as a suffix of the conjunctive participle, as in hĕth karith, having taken (L.V. 12), dith karith, having given (id.). In nominal compounds, karith often gives an adverbial force, as in sakhtī karith, with great difficulty, by using extreme measures (Rām. 433, 909). --dyunᵘ --, m.inf. to make out and out, to accomplish, complete (Rām. 1203, 1589; H. x, 12); cf. Hindī, kar dēnā. --gaʦhun --, m.inf. to do, or make, completely, to finish off (L.V. 96, Śiv. 210); cf. Hindī, kar jānā. --krövith -- conj. part. having done completely. --thawun --, m.inf. to place, arrange (Śiv. 1084, 1302; Rām. 1253).
m. one who out of tender pity has become incarnate, a title of the Deity (Śiv. 152, 316, 415, 1569, 1576, 1840).
see karun hyotᵘ- motᵘ, p. 473a, l. 38.
f. (in a wall or fence) the portion made of hard mud or bricks.
m. a performer of the krayĕ ceremony, see krayĕ.

m. a debt, money borrowed (Gr.M., K.Pr. 157). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to lend money, to give credit, become a creditor (Rām. 1312). --tulun -- m.inf. to borrow money gradually, or byinstalments. --ʦaṭun -- m.inf. to borrow money, to incur debt.
c.g. one who lends another money, a creditor; one who takes a loan, a debtor (Gr.M.).
m. a sheet for lying on.
m. the larger wooden mortar in which grain is bruised (El.). Cf. kanz.

m. someone, anybody; a person, an individual; cf. bē-kas, without anyone, friendless, forlorn (Śiv. 190). This word is often used with Persian numerals, as in yak kas, one person, dū kas, two persons (K.Pr. 118, 240; W. 156).
m. a small red cap worn by Musalmān women (El.).
n.ag. (f. kāsavüñᵘ̈), one who removes, makes away with, etc. See kāsun 1 (Śiv. 105, 813, 1190; H. i, 11).
m. drawing, pulling, in kash kaḍun m.inf. to draw, to drag, to draw (a bow) (see kaḍun) (Rām. 117, 123, 248, 1269, 1271); to practise any work to one's complete satisfaction.
? f. a tea-spoon (El. who states that the word is m.).
m. labour, trouble, pain (incurred in some impossible or unwelcome forced task).
(? = Turkī قاشق) m. a table- or dessert-spoon (El.).

m. (sg. dat. kashĕpas), N. of celebrated Rishi, the son of Brahmā, in Skt. Kaśyapa. It was he who turned the valley of Kashmīr from a lake to dry land. He was the father of all living beings. One of his sons was Garuḍa, the vehicle of Viṣṇu (Rām. 225, 598; K. 26, 1038).

f. (sg. dat. kashiphi), an opening, a declaration, solution, explanation; a manifestation, disclosure, apocalypse, revelation; inspiration; in Kāshmīrī, knowing another's secret thoughts; unintentionally revealing one's own secret thoughts.
f. the country of Kashmīr (K.Pr. 97, K. 959). Cf. kashmīr.
conj. would to heaven, would that (W. 145, YZ. 479, Rām. 811).
m. a (beggar's) cup or bowl, usually a coco-nut shell, or the lower half of a broken pitcher, especially used by religious mendicants and the like (K.Pr. 24).

m. the country of Kashmīr (this word is borrowed from India or Persia. The indigenous word is kashīrᵘ̈, f., q.v.) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 865, 1257; K. 958). -mar m. the hermitage of Kashmīr, i.e. the holy land of Kashmīr (Śiv. 1159).
m. trouble, worry, inconvenience; sorrow, woe (Gr.M.; Rām. 1570, 1769).
m. N. of a territory to the south-east of the Kashmīr Valley on the upper Cināb river, the ancient Kāṣṭavāṭa, and the Kishtwar of modern maps (RT.Tr. II, 431; Śiv. 1504).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. koshᵘ. This verb is used impersonally in the tenses derived from the past participles), to itch (Rām. 825); to scratch oneself or another in an itchy place, to scratch (El.; K.Pr. 163, 218; L. 463; H. xii, 16, 17). ¶ kȧshⁱ kȧshⁱ kaḍun m.inf. itching and itching to extract; hence, to draw out (money from a purse) with itching fingers, (of a miser) to give or spend, unwilling and meanly, a very small amount out of great wealth. ¶ kashĕn-phash m. a single scratch on an itching place.

f. that which remains after the essential part has been removed (e.g. an emptied honeycomb) (cf. El. kūsh, beeswax; L. 459, kashri, the (refuse) core of maize) (cf. mö̃ch-kᵒ, s.v. mã̄ch; makāyi-kᵒ, s.v. maköyᵘ̈). kashᵃri-nār m. a fire of such refuse.
adj. c.g. obstinate, pig-headed, in any business, esp. when this obstinacy is due to a mean or petty character.
f. obstinacy or pig- headedness, as ab.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kosᵘ; 2 p.p. kasōv), to fry (Gr.Gr. 208, 225). kosᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. küsᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), fried.

conj. 1 (1 p.p.kôsᵘ), to take away, remove, rid of (El.; K.Pr. 57; YZ. 209, 257, 479; Śiv. 212, 282, 1351, etc.; Rām. 110, 1062, 1076, 1230, 1510, 1657, 1686, 1771, 1779; K. 385, 473, 547, 1064, etc.; L.V. 8, 73; H. i, 12; vi, 6); esp. in a religious or psychical sense to put away (sin), to remove (guilt), to expel (a demon in possession; cf. dakhᵃl kāsun, p. 207a, l. 45); to expel (pain) (YZ. 485; Śiv. 104, 168, 171, 926, etc.; Rām. 20, 293); to remove (sorrow, anxiety) (Rām. 72, 714, 770, 1479, 1570, 1769; K. 724); to annul (a curse) (Rām. 215, K. 1091-2); to expel or cure (a disease) (cf. myondᵘ 1). kôsᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. kösᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), taken away, removed, as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. kôsᵘ), to shave (as a barber) (El.; K. 483, 662, 664). mas (or mast) kāsun, to shave the hair (of the head) (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 138; H. xii, 4, 5, etc.). nam kāsȧnⁱ, to pare the nails; see nam1. kôsᵘ- motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. kösᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), shaved, shaved off (of hair).
m. intention, design, resolve, resolution (Gr.M., W. 6).

or kasam قسم m. an oath, asseveration, adjuration (El.; K.Pr. 14; Rām. 771, 1059-60, 1062, 1532); an uttered charm, a mystic word, a word of power, incantation (H. xii, 22). --hāwun -- m.inf. to show an oath, to asseverate, to offer to make oath in order to convince a person (Rām. 1056, 1058; H. v, 9); to swear (El.). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to swear (El., Gr.M., Rām. 154). --karun -- m.inf. to make oath by calling a god or the like to witness; to swear (El.; H. v, 9).
in kata-ganḍ m. great opposition, stopping another (e.g. in his business or the like).

com. gen. one who cuts off or destroys, a destroyer, used in compounds such as kaṭa-sankaṭa (Śiv. 161) or sankaṭa-kaṭa (Śiv. 892, 934, 1078, 1501), a destroyer of perils, an attributive name of Śiva or (Śiv. 1501) Pārvatī.
m. a side-glance, a passing glance (Śiv. 1731); a leer.
m. (f. katöjⁱ or katöjᵘ̈), mean-natured, possessing all the vices of a mean nature, such as always asking for things, perpetually quarrelling, etc., vile.
in katān kēūm (? spelling), linseed oil (El.).
m. a kind of shawl-work, in which the shawl is embroidered with silk and gold thread (L. 377). Cf. katun 1.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kataranôwᵘ), caus. of katarun, q.v., to cause to slice; to cause to be sliced, to get sliced (Gr.Gr. 171).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. katorᵘ), to cut in slices, slice, cut up (El. katurun; H. x, 7). katorᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. katürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈) cut up, cut into pieces.
f. wages for spinning, wages paid to a person who spins thread, the charge for spinning (K.Pr. 214). --karüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to earn money by spinning, to take to spinning for a livelihood (H. xi, 19).
katĕnan, katinan, katĕnas, or katinas adv. in what place, where (Gr.Gr. 155). Cf. kati.
katinan, katĕnas, or katinas, i.q. katĕn, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 155).
adv., i.q. katĕn, q.v., but used only in addressing a female (Gr.Gr. 155).

f. (sg. dat. kathi, Gr.Gr. 70), a story, narrative, account, fable, statement (L.V. 45, 62; K.Pr. 190; L. 458; Śiv. 91, 426, 553, 1098, 1362, etc.; Rām. 30, 43, 48, 396, 828, 1173, 1242, 1525; K. 938; H. iv, 5; vii, 1; viii, 1; x, 1, 2, 4); a word, speech, language (L.V. 91; K.Pr. 17, 33, 41, 245; YZ. 53, 155, 182; Rām. 334, 967, 1108, 1251, 1568; K. 400, 1151; H. ix, 7; xii, 9); a proverb, saying (Rām. 13, 27, 1643, 1646); talk, conversation (K. 47, 524, 617); a thing, affair, matter, case, circumstance, occurrence (K.Pr. 87; Śiv. 73, 718, 786, 838, 1085, 1194, 1902; Rām. 120, 167, 181, 956, 1296, etc.; K. 182; H. iii, 5; xii, 1); talk (as opposed to action) (Rām. 1388); talk, discussion (cf. nētra-kᵒ, s.v. nēthᵃr 1). -bāth f. (pl. nom. katha-bāta), conversation, talking together (H. xii, 25). -bāth karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to converse (El.). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to speak, or utter, words (Rām. 899, 1611); to converse (Śiv. 66; Rām. 142, 379, 1079; K. 938); to tell a story (Śiv. 741); to hold speech (with a woman), i.e. to make improper advances to her (H. xii, 1). --rachüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to keep a word, to keep a secret confided to one. --rāwüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. speech to be lost, of two or more persons not speaking to each other (on account of a quarrel or the like); to lose a word, a word to be rendered useless (K.Pr. 242). --rāwarüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to lose speech, to render speech useless, to act contrary to advice. ¶ katha-bĕmörⁱ f. disease of speech, inability to speak properly, or to hear properly what another says. -cāv m. speech-longing, eager desire to speak; eager desire to hear something spoken (e.g. a story, etc.). -gorᵘ m. loquacious, garrulous, one who speaks whether addressed or not. -gāṭulᵘ m. skilled in speech, eloquent (Gr.M.). -kukāl m. a prater, a garrulous talker, one who speaks in season and out of season. -kath f. frequent repetition of the same words; rumour, report; a conversation (Gr.M.). -kutāl m. talkative, garrulous; esp. one who is always going about telling invented stories. -közⁱ m. ready tongued, skilled in speech, eloquent. -rotᵘ m. much conversation, a long talk. -törᵘ̈ f. delay caused by talking. -ʦŏsorᵘ m. frequent mutual conversations (esp. among women). ¶ kathi gaʦhun m.inf. to go on a word, to act according to something said (e.g. instructions). -hanā f. a single little word, etc., dim. of kath in all its meanings (Rām. 1616). --lagun -- m.inf. to attend to the word, to follow out instructions. -kọ̆ʦhᵘ m. a word-bribe, a bribe given to someone to speak a good word to a person in authority, or the like; a bribe offered to a child to make it do something. ¶ kathāh f. (kath with the suff. of the indef. art. added), a single word, only a word (Gr.Gr. 93; K.Pr. 5 (katā), 216; YZ. 264; Rām. 824); a reading or recitation of one of the Hindū scriptures. Often used in various idiomatic senses, such as 'merely a story', 'a mere piece of talk', 'a mere yarn', 'a thing no longer existing', 'a tale that is told', and so on (Rām. 545, 777, 1053). kathāh chĕna, it is not even a word, it is nothing (Rām. 741); there is no telling, it is impossible to tell (Rām. 701). So, interrogatively, kathāh chyā, is it possible (i.e. it is impossible) to tell (Rām. 1377).

m. (sg. dat. kaṭas), a male sheep, a ram (Gr.Gr. 52, Gr.M., K.Pr. 32, L. 463, W. 18, Rām. 923); a sheep (generally) [K.Pr. 189, 213, 245; W. 114; YZ. 397 (pl. nom. kaṭh, wrongly written kạty).] In K.Pr. 82, a small sheep, as contrasted with honḍᵘ 1, q.v. ¶ kaṭa-mȧlⁱñār m. brownish (the colour), half-whiteness, half-cleanness (Gr.Gr. 141). -malyunᵘ adj. (f. -maliñᵘ̈), 'ram-dirty,' of the mottled or brownish colour of a ram, half-white, half-clean (Gr.Gr. 141). -maṭa adj. c.g. plump, equally fully-formed all over (without hollows or lumps). -māz m. mutton (El., W. 114). -ñūrⁱ f. the hoof of a ram. -pröʦᵘ̈ f. the corner of a ram's mouth; met. something long and creased in two (esp. u.w. reference to the page of a manuscript, which is always two folios made of one sheet folded lengthwise). -prāʦh-hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -prāʦh-hishᵘ̈), like the corners of a ram's mouth, long and creased in two, as in the preceding. -pūtᵘ m. a ram's son, a young sheep, a young ram (Gr.Gr. 131); N. of a child's game, in which a child is carried across the shoulders, as a lamb is carried.

m. (sg. abl. kāṭha 1), wood, dried wood, a stick, a dried hard stalk (L.V. 38; Rām. 1080, 1200; K. 976). The dim. is köṭhᵘ̈ 1, q.v. -bāṭh m. a jingle of kāṭh, wood and the like, wood etc. The word is reported to be m., but according to I.K. iii, 14, such jingles are f. ¶ kāṭha-brörᵘ̈ f. a wooden cat, an imitation cat made of wood, set to frighten away mice, etc.; a house or roof made with very lofty wooden supports or beams. -chān m. a good kind of rice, with a white grain (El., L. 463). -chiṭh f. (sg. dat. -chiṭi), a kind of cheap chintz. -khŏn f. (sg. dat. -khŏni), as much wood as can be held under one arm, an armful of wood (for fuel or the like). -köñᵘ̈ f. a small amount of wood, a little wood (Gr.Gr. 163). -kar m. a wooden railing or fence (round a garden or the like, or in front of a balcony); the wooden frame of a mirror or the like. -lọ̆ʦhᵘ m. a heap of sticks. -lŏʦhürᵘ̈ f. a small heap of sticks. -tulᵘ m. a small collection of dried twigs (Gr.Gr. 164). -ʦᵃñĕ f.pl. charcoal made from dry sticks. -zanḍ m. a little dried wood, a small collection of dried twigs (cf. Gr.Gr. 163).

m. a son, almost always --˚ in a contemptuous sense, or in abuse or anger, as in gāna-kaṭh, son of a pimp. Exceptions are sŏ-kaṭh, a good son, and sŏkha-kaṭh, a son of happiness (Gr.Gr. 132, Gr.M.); küṭᵘ̈ (q.v.) is used for the f. of this word as well as of koṭᵘ.

m. (sg. abl. kāṭha 2), laziness, in the following: --kāṭh-kasūr m. the fault of laziness, laziness, used in phrases such as kāṭh-kasūr kösith karav, we shall work having expelled our laziness, i.e. we shall do our best. Cf. köṭhⁱ 2 and köṭhᵘ̈ 4.

f. acridity, pungency (esp. of smell); cf. kruṭh. --kaḍüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to expel acridity, to take away the acrid smell or flavour of sour ghī or the like by cooking; to enjoy or eat anything till one is completely satisfied; cf. the next. --kaḍith -- adv. having expelled acridity (as ab.); completely, to one's fill (of eating, sleeping, etc.).

or kāṭha 3 adj. c.g. (for f., see köṭhᵘ̈ 3), hard, dry, sapless. Cf. an-kāṭh, p. 29b, l. 23. ¶ kāṭha-dach f. a wild grape with no, or hardly any, juice. -dönᵘ̈ m. a pomegranate which has no, or hardly any, juice.

in kaṭh-kār m. icy cold weather, the freezing cold of a blizzard, or the like (Śiv. 332). -koshᵘ or kaṭhyushᵘ m. freezingly cold weather accompanied by wind and icy mist (L. 353, kut kushu; Śiv. 336, 347-8; Rām. 674). -kȧshⁱ-dĕv m. lit. a frost-demon; hence, freezing weather, stinging, and, so to speak, biting with hailstones; met. a chilly person, who is always cowering over a fire.
or kathulᵘ m. one who is talkative, garrulous; one who is skilled in narrating stories, or the like, a good story-teller.
adj. c.g. divided into two halves, halved (of a fruit, a walnut, or the like). See khã̄ṭh.
m. hardness, etc., abs. noun der. fr. kaṭhyunᵘ, q.v.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. kāṭhyōv), to be hard (Gr.Gr. xiv).
adj. c.g. hard, solid, stiff; hard-hearted, ruthless (K. 860).
adj. (f. kāṭhüvᵘ̈), made of wood, wooden (Gr.Gr. 161).
adj. (f. kaṭhiñᵘ̈), hard, stiff; cruel, ruthless, ferocious (Gr.M.); inflexible, inexorable; sharp, violent (of pain, etc.); hard, difficult (Gr.M.; Śiv. 744, 848, 1854, 1877).
m. frosty weather, the freezing cold of a blizzard, or the like, i.q. kaṭh-koshᵘ, p. 487a, l. 37.
m. one who is treated (affectionately) as a son (generally applied to a son-in-law, not to an adopted son, or the like); --˚ a son (as an affectionate term). Cf. dāyĕ-kạthᵃr, p. 266b, l. 1.
(? spelling) in K.Pr. 22, said to mean 'a (stupid) child or disciple'. Probably kaṭhᵘ̈y is meant, i.e. kaṭh 2 (q.v.) with emph. y.

adv. in what place? where? (Gr.Gr. 150; Gr.M.; L.V. 106; K.Pr. 178; W. 94; YZ 33, katē; 56, 59, 163, katih; Śiv. 282, 346, 370, etc.; Rām. 202, 221, 253, etc.; H. vii, 20, etc.); from what place? whence? (Gr.Gr. 155; K.Pr. 99; Śiv. 522, 1357; K. 141; H. x, 4; xi, 7, etc.). Often used in the sense of 'where?' with the expectation of a negative answer, and thus equivalent to 'nowhere', 'not at all' (Śiv. 351-2, 1079, 1284, 1787, 1888); cf. katĕn. -kinⁱ adv. from what direction? whence? (Gr.Gr. 158); whence? by what means? how? (Rām. 544, 1293, 1307). --kotᵘ -- adv. whence where? used to indicate a great indefinite distance, as in kati-kotᵘ chuh Kashīri-pĕṭha Lāhōr, Lahore is a very long way from Kashmīr. --kūtᵘ -- adj. (f. --kǖʦᵘ̈ --), from where how much? used to indicate indefinite length (in space or time); cf. the preceding. --kōr -- adv. from where where? i.q. --kotᵘ, ab. -pĕṭha adv. from what place? whence? (Gr.Gr. 155; H. ii, 2). -sanā adv. where? i.q. kati, but indicates a shade of doubtfulness, quasi 'I wonder where?'; cf. Gr.Gr. 180-1. -tām, -tāmath, -tāñ, or -tāñĕth adv. somewhere, anywhere. The underlying idea in the mind of the speaker is a question with doubt, as in, e.g. 'is so-and-so anywhere? if so, where?' (Gr.Gr. 256). ¶ katiy adv. (kati with emph. y) wherever, in whatever place (Gr.M., YZ. 15). ¶ katyō, i.q. kati, with interjection ō (YZ. 43). ¶ katyukᵘ adj. (f. katicᵘ̈), of or belonging to what place? of where? (Gr.Gr. 150, YZ. 45). Cf. katīkō.
(? spelling) f. a young heifer (L. 360). Perhaps i.q. küṭᵘ̈.
f. a swallow, Hirundo rustica (El. kaṭij, kōtiz; L. 117, 155, katij).
pron. adj. of, or belonging to, where? (poet., i.q. katyukᵘ, p. 484a, l. 1. q.v.) (H. ii, 2).
f. the condition or conduct of a despised child (cf. kaṭh 2), used --˚ as in harām-kȧtil, p. 348b, l. 40, q.v.
m. a certain gum resembling gum-tragacanth.

or katurᵘ m. a large potsherd or piece of a bowl; esp. one used for holding a fire of burning charcoal (cf. nāra-kᵒ, s.v. nār, and nȧṭⁱ-kⁱ, s.v. noṭᵘ), or for receiving ordure (cf. mal- kᵒ, s.v. mal 1); a similar sherd of ice or the like, a piece of sheet-ice (Śiv. 337) (cf. tula-katorᵘ). The f. of this word is katᵘ̈rᵘ̈, q.v., which is used as a diminutive (Gr.Gr. 33, 35).
see kotᵘ 2, l. 3 of next column.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. koṭᵘ; 2 p.p. kacyōv), to cut (El.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. kotᵘ), f. küʦᵘ̈; 2 p.p. kaʦōv, pl. kaʦöy, Gr.Gr. 225, 227), to spin (thread in a spinning-wheel) (El.; K.Pr. 65, 126, 253; Śiv. 1014, 1872). kotᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. küʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), spun (of thread, etc.).
or (El.) kāṭur (= Turkī قاطر) m. (f. kātᵘ̈rᵘ̈), a mule (El. kāṭur; Gr.M. kātur).
also spelt kaṭᵃr f. a scrap or piece of leather; a small leathern pouch or bag.
adv. in what place? where? (Gr.Gr. 156); to what place? whither? Cf. kotᵘ 2.
f. a flock of rams, a number of rams (Gr.Gr. 93).
f. a name of the goddess Pārvatī, the consort of Śiva (K. 267).

m. a small amount of grain (say, as much as can be held in the palm of the hand); a drop (El. katra); a small amount, a small store of anything (cf. māyā-kᵒ). According to another authority, the word means 'grains' only, without reference to the amount. Cf. dā̃-kᵒ, p. 230a, l. 37, and dyāra-kᵒ, p. 270b, l. 38.

katürᵘ̈ or kütrᵘ̈ f. a potsherd (esp. a small potsherd) (dim. of katorᵘ, q.v., Gr.Gr. 33, 35) (El. katir, baked clay) (cf. mal- kᵒ, a filth-pan, s.v. mal 1, and nȧṭⁱ-kⁱ, s.v. noṭᵘ). ¶ katri-khünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -khanjĕ), a bit of potsherd. -khash m. a cut (on the throat or elsewhere) caused by a potsherd. ¶ katari-ashkhāsh m. destruction (i.e. execution, or killing) by cutting with potsherds (instead of with a sword); hence, using a potsherd instead of a sword for any purpose for which the latter is employed. -bata m. 'boiled rice from a potsherd', i.e. a method of killing a person, in which first his limbs are broken to pieces, and then these fragments are again broken into pieces like fragments of potsherds. -zôrᵘ m. (f. -zörᵘ̈), an inveterate gambler, one who has gambled away all his (or her) property, and is reduced to gambling with potsherds; met. one who is ruining himself (or herself) by extravagance, or who has done so.

m. N. of a certain sept of Brāhmaṇs, the members of which follow the Tāntrik or Kulâcāra ritual; a member of this sept. ¶ kaula-bāy f. the wife of a member of the Kaul sept (Gr.Gr. 34). -koṭᵘ m. the son of such a Brāhmaṇ; esp. a worthy son, spoken of with respect (Gr.Gr. 131). -pūtᵘ m. id., but not necessarily in a laudatory sense (Gr.Gr. 131).
m. a Government Council (the English word) (Gr.M.).

or kōrav m. a man of the Kuru tribe (see kuru 1); in pl. N. of one of the opposing parties in the great war of the Mahābhārata, the other party being the Pānḍavs (Śiv. 1328; K. 533, 546-7, 699, 895, 899, 904, 1035).

m. (sg. abl. kāwa 1; f. köviñ, Gr.Gr. 37), a crow (El. káo; Gr.Gr. 37, 51; Gr.M.; L.V. 28; K.Pr. 28, 36, 82, 101, 195; Śiv. 735, 1756; Rām. 319, 642, 685, 893, 973, 1191, 1629). ¶ According to El., there are in Kashmīr two kinds of crows, one wholly black, and the other with a dirty white neck. Cf. hôrᵘ kāv (K.Pr. 82), a black and white crow; hence, a marked man. ¶ Crows, being great travellers, are believed to carry news from far distances, and are often apostrophized in poetry and asked for news of an absent beloved. Cf. Rām. 893. ¶ kāwa-ỗṭᵘ m. the mark ∧ used in manuscripts to indicate 'caret', i.e. that a letter or letters have been omitted. -bôrᵘ m. a high piled up burden (just as a crow by collecting straws and sticks one by one makes a very high pile). -dach f. a kind of semi-wild vine producing small black grapes (El., W. 115); the Barberry, Berberis Lycium (L. 74, 75, 76, káodách); cf. kāvürᵘ̈ dach, p. 496a, l. 33. -dinⁱ m.pl. of the next, suspicious glances (as a crow looks at a person suspiciously from a distance). -dyunᵘ 1 m., i.q. the preceding; cf. kāwa dyunᵘ, s.v. kāwa 2. -hö̃ṭhᵘ̈ f. a woman that bears only one child. -kŏḍurᵘ m. 'crow's pip', N. of a kind of paddy with a full-shaped red grain. -khūrᵘ m. N. of a certain medicinal plant, said to resemble a crow's leg in shape. -kumorᵘ m. N. of a certain bird; cf. kumorᵘ. -kan m. pl. 'crow's ears', very acute ears, which (like a crow) can distinguish even a single very faint and obscure sound. -kāwa adv. 'crow by crow'; met. of a great crowd gradually collecting, just as crows gather one by one into a great flock; cf. K.Pr. 100. -lorᵘ m. name of a kind of paddy with full-shaped grains partly red and partly white. -pakh f. (sg. dat. -pakhi), a crow's wing (used as a simile for anything intensely black); N. of a kind of gambling game, played with cowries placed in the four corners of a ruled board. -punimᵘ̈ f. the full moon of the month of Māg (January-February), on which it is customary to feed crows. -pūrᵘ m. a crow's footprint (as left in snow or the like); hence, after a heavy fall of snow, the tracks indicating a concealed path made by the first venturesome person to go forth. -pūtᵘ m. a crow's fledgling, a young crow (Gr.Gr. 131, K.Pr. 195); met. a miserably thin child or the like. -patolᵘ m. a kind of grass doll made for feeding crows on the full moon of Māg (see kāwa- punimᵘ̈, ab.). -shupᵘ m. 'a crow's winnowing-sieve', a shell of a pearl-oyster. -ʦhyoṭᵘ m. 'crow's leavings', fruit, etc., which has been partly eaten by a crow. It is not considered to be thereby rendered impure. -ʦopᵘ m. a crow's bite; the mark of a crow's beak on some fruit which it has partly eaten; see the preceding. -yĕñĕwôlᵘ m. a crow's wedding procession, i.e. the evening procession of thousands of noisy crows returning to roost; hence, a badly arranged wedding arrangement, everything upside down (K.Pr. 100). ¶ kövⁱ trôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. --trövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), abandoned by a crow, of some fruit or the like scattered or thrown away by a crow, and hence belonging to nobody; met. 'nobody's child', a person who has no family, etc., to belong to. ¶ kāwan-gōjĕ f. pl. crows' kernels, i.e. nuts or the like scattered hither and thither, or gobbled up, by crows; hence, met. of property scattered and squandered, as in dyār gayĕs kāwan gōjĕ, his money became crows' kernels (K.Pr. 101).
m. a caw, the sound made by a crow. --karun -- m.inf. to caw (K.Pr. 101).
m. a poet (a Hindū word) (Gr.M.), i.q. kȧviy, q.v.
m. a poet; esp. a panegyrist. Cf. kavi.
m. (in Hindū religion) oblations to deceased ancestors (K. 974), opp. to havy, q.v.
m. (for 1, see kāv 1), the ear (El.). --dyunᵘ 2 -- m.inf. to listen (El., W. 87). Perhaps this is a ghost-word. Cf. kāwa dyunᵘ 1, s.v. kāv 1. According to El., it is in use towards Bāramula.
f. a small brass cup or bowl (Panjābī kaulī). In Kashmīr it is an imported article. Cf. kawolᵘ.
m. darkening, becoming black; abs. noun of kāworᵘ, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 139).
f. a collection of crows (such as occurs in the evening), a crow-parliament. See kāv 1.

or kāwujᵘ m. (his wife is kāwȧjⁱ-bāy or kāwajĕñ), the attendant at a Hindū burning ghāt, whose perquisite is the clothing of the corpses. In Kashmīr he is always a Musalmān (El.; K.Pr. 101, 122; L. 263).
m. a large cup (El. kauwul). Cf. kawȧlⁱ.
or kāwurᵘ adj. (f. kāvürᵘ̈), dark-coloured, black (Gr.Gr. 139); cf. kôwᵘ 3. kāvürᵘ̈dach f. a kind of black-coloured grape (El. káwir dach). Cf. kāwa-dach, p. 494b, l. 48.

or k āwarun conj. 3 (2 p.p. kāwᵃryōv), to turn black, to become black, usually in the sense of being spoiled; e.g. of a red fruit turning black, or the hands losing their natural colour and darkening through illness or emaciation (Śiv. 1259, kāwarun; cf. atha kāwᵃranᵃ, p. 59b, l. 5).
m. vomiting; vomit. Genl. used in plur., as in chis kay gaʦhān, he is vomiting (Gr.M.). -dasta m.pl. severe bilious vomiting and purging; cholera. Cf. dasta-kay, p. 256a, l. 37.
f. the body (obs. exc. in poetry) (Śiv. 158, 1458, 1479, 1572, 1630, 1742). -kashṭh  m. (sg. dat. -kashṭas), distress of the body (from hunger, thirst, heat, disease, or the like).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. kāyaryōv), to be or become soft, weak; (of a human being or animal) to be or become soft, weak, powerless, inert, lazy.
m. N. of a village about four miles south of the town of Avantipura, on the bank of the river Vĕth (Jehlam), the ancient Katikā, and the Kai of RT.Tr. II, 460.
m. the nature of pine-wood (Gr.Gr. 139); hence (cf. kāyorᵘ 1 and 2), weakness, softness; (of human beings, animals, etc.) softness, inertness, laziness.
a certain bird (? a kind of partridge), described as haunting mountain forests, as having a variegated white and yellow plumage and a sweet voice.
m. N. of a considerable village of Kashmīr (the ancient Katimuṣa) on the left bank of the river Vĕshau (ancient Viśōka) (RT.Tr. ii, 55).

kāyurᵘ, sometimes written kāyirᵘ 1 m. the wood of the yörᵘ̈, or Himalayan blue pine (El. kāyūr or kāiar, Pinus excelsa; Gr.Gr. 139; K.Pr. 101; L. 79, 80, kairu; 456, kayur). This wood is very soft and easy to pierce; the word is hence used met. to indicate a person who is 'soft', i.e. weak, powerless, unresisting; cf. kāyorᵘ 2 and also aḍa-kāyurᵘ, p. 11a, l. 50. The shavings of this wood are used for torches (L. 80), and its fire is not lasting (K.Pr. 101). kāyiri-ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ f. charcoal made from the wood of the pine-tree. It is used for making gun- powder (El.), and is much esteemed by blacksmiths (L. 80).
or kāyurᵘ 2, sometimes written kāyirᵘ 2 adj. (f. kāyürᵘ̈, also written kāyirᵘ̈), weak, feeble; (of a human being) weak, feeble, inert, lazy. Cf. kāyorᵘ 1 and also the Skt. kātaraḥ.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kôyᵘ), to make lazy, to make a person work as if he were lazy; to make (oneself) lazy, to 'ca' canny' (Gr.Gr. xiv); to cause procrastination.
m. predestined fate; hence, the (predestined) time of death (Rām. 871).
f. blackness; blackness of mood, harshness, a dark temper (Rām. 1570).
m. a tumult, broil, wrangling (El. kaziyih).
m. (sg. dat. kazalas), lamp-black, soot; as adj. sooty, black (YZ. 147).
f. pl. how many?; see kūtᵃ, p. 484b, l. 49 (W. 94, kaʦ); also 1 p.p., f. pl. of katun, q.v.
f. (for 3, 4, see kāʦh 1, 2), (in building) a truss, two obliquely set posts, meeting at an angle to support a cross beam. --˚ the joint of the knee or similar hinge joint of two long bones.
see kūtᵘ, p. 484b, l. 47 (for 3, 4, see kāʦh, 1, 2).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. kāʦaladiñ), one who suffers from consumption, a consumptive.
m. a kind of woollen turban, worn only by Musalmān teachers.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kāʦarôwᵘ), to make brown, to dye brown (e.g. with madder) (Gr.Gr. 170).
m. brownness (Gr.Gr. 139); esp. brownness of the hair or eyes, a swarthy complexion.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. kāʦaryōv), to become tawny or brown, to be browned (Gr.Gr. 170).

m. (sg. abl. kāʦa 3, for 1, 2, see s.vv.), pulmonary disease, phthisis, consumption (Gr.Gr. 52, K.Pr. 207). ¶ kāʦa-kŏtholᵘ adj. (f. -kŏthȧjⁱ or -kŏthüjᵘ̈), one who suffers from phthisis, consumptive. -wāv m. an epidemic of consumption; met. a time of general calamities (such as plague, earthquakes, or the like).

m. (sg. dat. kaʦhas), the armpit; the corresponding pit at the root of the legs, the groin. ¶ kaʦha-brôrᵘ m. a bubo, or glandular swelling, in the armpit, the bag̱ẖal- bilāī of India (believed to be dispersed by getting a cat to lick it). -wāl m. the hair of armpits. -wüṭᵘ̈ f. (in a Kāshmīrī coat) the gusset under the armpits. ¶ kȧʦhⁱ-tȧlⁱmēlun m.inf. to get quite close under a person's armpits, i.e. approaching a person secretly in order to give a bribe; hence, to give a bribe. -wödᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a bubo (El. kaʦawádir m.). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to get up to a person by his armpit (i.e. unexpectedly, without his seeing, and not straightforwardly from the front), to make a flank attack.

m. (sg. abl. kāʦa 4, for 1, 2, see s.vv.), glass (Gr.Gr. 10, 31, 52); crystal; (in Kāshmīrī) a species of pottery made of a fine kind of clay, from which bracelets and certain vessels are made (Gr.Gr. 10). Cf. nyūlᵘ kāʦh hyuhᵘ, s.v. nyūlᵘ. ¶ kāʦa-bọ̆ngᵃr or -bŏngᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a common kind of bracelet worn on the forearm, made of this pottery (El.). -bōṭa m. a kind of small winged insect, ? the winged white-ant (Śiv. 1647). -gorᵘ m. (f. -gȧrⁱ-bāy), a man who makes bracelets, etc., of this pottery (the fem. is either his wife, or a woman who does this work) (El.); a bottle-maker (El.). -korᵘ m. a kind of bracelet made of this pottery (El.); cf. kaʦha-kar, s.v. kaʦha. -më̆ʦᵘ̈ f. the fine earth from which this pottery is made. -tĕmbar m.pl. cataract (the disease of the eyes). -tĕmbarlad adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -tĕmbarladiñ), one who suffers from cataract. -zūnᵘ̈ f. the crystal-clear moonlight of the month of Kārtikh (October-November) (Rām. 1620).
in kaʦha-kar m.pl. a set of bangles or bracelets (usually silver or gold) worn by women on their arms. Cf. kāʦa-korᵘ, s.v. kāʦh 2.
kã̄ʦhāh, kĕ˜ʦhāh, kē̃ʦhāh, kũʦhāh, kū̃ʦhāh, see kē̃h.
in kȧʦi bĕhun m.inf. to sit silent (used of a questioner who has no counter-reply to the answer he has received, either because the answer puts him out of countenance, or because it is satisfactory).

or kaʦulᵘ m. (sg. dat. kaʦalas), a kind of little box or vessel in which small articles are kept (e.g. small toilet articles, such as spangles, or esp. the number of small necessaries, scents, incense, etc., used by a sacrificing priest in religious ceremonies), a pyx; cf. nörⁱ-kⁱ, s.v. nôrᵘ. ¶ kaʦal-düjᵘ̈ f. a cloth in which these small boxes containing articles used in religious ceremonies are wrapped and kept, a pyx-cloth. -ḍūnᵘ m. a pair of cups, the open faces of which fit together like the two halves of a walnut-shell (cf. ḍūnᵘ), and which are used for carrying scents, etc., for religious ceremonies.

adj. (f. kāʦᵘ̈rᵘ̈), brown, tawny (W. 20); esp. (of a person) with brown hair and eyes (Gr.Gr. 139, K.Pr. 100) (a brown-haired man is considered to be invariably stingy and selfish, K.Pr. l.c.). kāʦȧrⁱ-bōṭa m. brown-haired (genl. u.w. reference to children).
pron. adj. (f. kaʦimᵘ̈), who, or which, of many ? which out of many (Gr.Gr. 149). Cf. kǖtyumᵘ.

pron. indef. used either as a subst. or as an adj. ¶ [It has in the singular two sets of forms, one animate, the other inanimate. In the nominative singular animate it has a set of forms which are confined to the masculine, and of which the distinguishing vowel is u, and another set of forms which are of common gender, and of which the distinguishing vowel is a. In the other cases of the singular it is of common gender. ¶ The inanimate forms of the singular are all of common gender. ¶ In the plural there is no distinction between animate and inanimate, and all forms are of common gender. ¶ The simplest forms of the sg. nom. are kū̃h (an. m.), kã̄h (an. c.g.), and kē̃h (inan. c.g.). To these ʦ is added as an indefinite suffix, so that we get some such form as kū̃hʦ, kã̄hʦ, or kē̃hʦ respectively, but such forms are now obsolete, although grammarians give a form kē̃ʦ or kēnʦ, which is now not used except in the nom. plur. (cf. Gr.Gr. 67, 91). In Rām. 150 there is, however, the form kē̃hʦh-āh, and this is the only instance yet noted of the preservation of the h before the ʦ. ¶ This form kē̃hʦhāh leads us to the second set of nominative forms used at the present day. Under the rule of Kāshmīrī phonetics that a final surd must be aspirated, kū̃hʦ, kã̄hʦ, and kē̃hʦ regularly become kū̃hʦh, kã̄hʦh, and kē̃hʦh respectively. These have been contracted to kū̃ʦh (L.V. 60), kã̄ʦh, and kē̃ʦh, to which the suffix āh of the indefinite article is added, so that we finally arrive at the forms kū̃ʦhāh, kã̄ʦhāh, and kē̃ʦhāh, which are now in everyday use, as optional forms of kū̃h, kã̄h, and kē̃h respectively. ¶ The suffix ʦ is not used in the oblique cases of the singular, which have special forms, but reappears in the plural, where it is used throughout. ¶ For the singular oblique cases, the animate form is kaĩsi and the inanimate form is kuni. ¶ For the plural, the nominative is kē̃h, kē̃ʦ or kēnʦ, or kē̃ʦhāh, and the base of the oblique cases is kē̃ʦ. ¶ The above remarks primarily refer to the use of this pronoun as a subst. Its use as an adjective is very similar, but is more lax and will be dealt with later on. ¶ The following are therefore the forms occurring in declension:-- ¶ Singular, nominative; animate; masculine, kū̃h (K. 578, 795), kū̃ʦhāh (Gr.M.); common gender, kã̄h (El. kahn) (L.V. 107; Śiv. 79, 81, 85, 214, 423, 985, 997, 1189; Rām. 139, 164, 504, 720, 729, 770, etc.; H. i, 2; vi, 10; xii, 2), kã̄ʦhāh (Śiv. 356-7, Rām. 884). ¶ Inanimate, common gender, kē̃h (El. kihn) (Śiv. 309, 329, 589, 594, 636, 647, 984, etc.; Rām. 149, 360, 520, 559, etc.; L.V. 9, 11, 19, etc.); kē̃ʦhāh (Śiv. 117, 974, 1529; Rām. 162, 587, 653, 1081) (kē̃hʦhāh, Rām. 150). In old Kāshmīrī we have also kũh (L.V. 2), and kū̃ʦh (L.V. 60). ¶ All oblique cases except gen., an. kaĩsi (Śiv. 1216, 1228, 1460; Rām. 133, 139, 215-6, 543, 1093, 1220, 1230, 1597, 1621, 1780; H. ii, 8; iii, 3; L.V. 35) or kö̃si (K.Pr. 171, 208; H. v, 9); inan. kuni (Śiv. 306, 1281, 1757; Rām. 780). ¶ Gen. an. kaĩsi-hondᵘ (Rām. 381, 754, 881, 1228); inan. kunyukᵘ (see bel.). ¶ Plural, an. and inan., c.g. nom. kē̃h (Śiv. 123; Rām. 778, 861-3, 1071-6, 1379; L.V. 32); kē̃ʦ or kēnʦ (Gr.Gr. 67, 91) or kē̃ʦhāh (Gr.M.); dat. kē̃ʦan (Gr.M., K.Pr. 102); gen. kē̃ʦan-hondᵘ (Gr.M.); ag., abl. kē̃ʦau (Gr.M., K.Pr. 102). ¶ It will have been observed that in all the above forms, except kaĩsi, the stem vowel is long and is nasalized, thus, ū̃, ã̄, ē̃. In writing in the Nāgarī or Śāradā character the nasalization is often represented by an n before ʦ, thus, kūnʦhāh, kānʦhāh, kēnʦhāh, kēnʦ, kĕnʦan, kēnʦau. This perhaps indicates a real variation of pronunciation, but, so far as the present writer's experience goes, there is no true n-sound, but only a nasalization of the vowel except in the nom. pl. kēnʦ, in which the n is generally distinctly audible. The vowel is also very commonly written and pronounced short throughout, thus, ũ, ã, ĕ˜. This is particularly common in the Musalmān dialect (e.g. in H.), but also occurs in Hindū poetry, so that we get kũh کُنہ (El. kuhn) (Śiv. 311; Rām. 715, 1076, 1762; L.V. 2, 35, 60); kũʦhāh کُنچھہاہ; kãh کنہ (El. kahn); kãʦhāh کَنچھہاہ; kĕ˜h کِنہ (El. kihn) (H. i, 6; ii, 5; iv, 4, 6; v, 8; viii, 2; ix, 6; xi, 15; xii, 6, 7, 15); kĕ˜ʦhāh کِنچھہاہ (H. vii, 26; x, 3; xii, 4, 5, etc.) or even kĕnʦāh کِنچھاہ (H. vii, 20); kĕnʦ, کِنچھ; kĕ˜ʦan کِنچھن; kĕ˜ʦau کِنچھَو. ¶ The final h of kū̃ʦhāh, kã̄ʦhã̄h, kē̃ʦhāh is also sometimes omitted, so that we get kū̃ʦhā, kã̄ʦhā, kē̃ʦhā. In the Persian character, moreover, the final āh of these three words is often written ah, so that we get kū̃ʦhah کونچھہَہ, kã̄ʦhah کا نچھہَہ, kē̃ʦhah کینچھہَہ, etc. There are other minor variations of spelling, which it is unnecessary to note here. ¶ When used as an adjective, all the forms given above for the use of this pronoun as a substantive may be employed, number for number, case for case, an. masc. for an. masc., an. c.g. for an. c.g., and inan. for inan. Moreover kū̃h (kũh), kã̄h (kãh), kē̃h (kĕ˜h), or kē̃ʦhāh (kĕ˜ʦhāh), etc., may be used without change to agree with any inan. noun in any case of either number. The following examples of adjectival use occur in the literature at present available:--An. m. sg. nom. kũh (Rām. 373); kū̃h (K. 419); kã̄h (Śiv. 35; Rām. 1425, 1498; H. v, 8). ¶ Inan. sg. nom. kĕ˜h (H. v, 10; vi, 16; viii, 1, 2; x, 1, 7; xii, 5); kē̃h (Śiv. 23, 375, 429, 518, 644, 750, etc.; Rām. 188, 219, 298, 302, 409, 533, etc.); kã̄h (Śiv. 255, 477, 771, 1757; Rām. 417, 617, 836, 967, 1649); kãh (K.Pr. 201); kã̄ʦh (L.V. 41); kē̃ʦh (L.V. 59); kē̃ʦhāh (Rām.300, 699); kĕnʦhāh (H. xii, 4, 19); kũh (Rām. 231, 836); and the irregular kũ̄̈h (Rām. 689, see bel.). L.V. 77 has an inanimate fem. kö̃h (in kö̃h-ti). ¶ Obl. kuni (K. 949; Rām. 762, 1023, 1037). ¶ Pl. nom. kē̃h (Rām. 775, 786, 852, 1343). In H. xi, 7, kĕ˜h is used as an. fem. pl. nom. The only available example of this form as m. is the irregular kễhⁱ of H. vi, 11.] ¶ As subst. an. anyone (Śiv. 77, 81, 85, 214, 423, 985, 997, 1189, 1228; Rām. 133, 139, 215, 381, 504, 720, 770, 884, 915, 1379, etc.; H. i, 2; ii, 8; iii, 3; vi, 10; xii, 22; L.V. 35, 60); someone (Rām. 944, 1179). ¶ As subst. inan. anything (Śiv. 329, 589, 594, 636, 647, 728, 984, 1434, 1451, 1749, 1858; Rām. 149, 360, 520, 559, 758, 1158, 1287, 1342, 1399, 1658, 1661, 1670; H. i, 6; ii, 5; iv, 4, 6; v, 8; viii, 2; ix, 6; xi, 15; xii, 6, 7, 15; K.Pr. 201); something (Śiv. 309, 974; Rām. 786; H. vii, 20, 26; x, 3; xii, 18). ¶ As adj. an. any (Śiv. 35; Rām. 1425, 1498; H. v, 8); some, a certain (H. vi, 11; xi, 7). ¶ As adj. inan. any (Śiv. 23, 255, 375, 429, 477, 644, 750, 763, 771, 777, 843, 844, 873, 1072, 1757; Rām. 188, 219, 298, 302, 409, 471, 617, 654, 817, 836, 1343; H. vi, 16; viii, 1; x, 1, 7; xii, 5, 19); some, a certain (Rām. 300, 599, 786, 1150, 1388, 1743; H. v, 10; viii, 2; xii, 4, 19). ¶ As adv. at all, in any respect (with neg. not at all, in no respect) (Rām. 283, 331, 347, 754). ¶ kũh compounded with an interrogative pronoun becomes still more indefinite, as in kũh kus, anyone whatever (Rām. 715); kũh kyāh, some... or other, of some kind or other (adj. inan.) (Rām. 231, 373), so kũh kami sāta, at some time or other (Rām. 836); kē̃h na-ta kyāh, nothing at all (L.V. 19). In kũ̄̈h kath jāyĕ, in any place whatever, the vowel of kũh has been changed (Rām. 689). Cf. ō̃h-kṻtⁱ (p. 390b, l. 30). ¶ biyĕ kū̃h (m.) biyĕ kã̄h (c.g.) (Rām. 729, 1246), etc., anyone else; someone else; someone more; as adj. an., any other. biyĕ kã̄h-ti anyone else at all (Rām. 164). biyĕ kē̃h, etc., anything else (H. xii, 8); something else, something more (H. iii, 8). ¶ na kū̃h (m.) (K. 582), na kã̄h (c.g.) (Rām. 139, 1076), etc. (or the na may follow), no one. As adj. an., not any, no. na kē̃h, etc., not anything, nothing (L.V. 9, 11, 90). As adj. inan., not any, no (Śiv. 518; Rām. 26, 104, 208, 275-6, 912, 1002, 1270, 1710, 1730; L.V. 41, 77). As adv., not at all (H. ii, 5; v, 5; xii, 2). El. kihnnah. It often takes the form kĕh-na, with short vowel and no nasal. ¶ prath kū̃h (m.), etc., each one, every one (Śiv. 357, 1216, 1460). prath kē̃h, etc., each thing, everything (Śiv. 306, 1281, 1757). ¶ sôruy kã̄h, etc., everyone. sôruy kē̃h, etc., everything (Siv. 1758). ¶ yus kã̄h, etc., whoever (Śiv. 356, yus kã̄ʦhāh); yih kē̃h, etc., whatever (Rām. 45, 256, 470, 790, 1745; yih kē̃ʦhāh, Śiv. 117, 695, 1184, 1529; Rām. 162, 587, 653; H. iii, 1, 8; v, 8); yih kē̃h... ti kē̃h, whatever... that (correl.) (Rām. 1660). ¶ kã̄h akhāh, etc. c.g. a certain man (or woman), a certain person, equivalent to the Latin quidam. ¶ kã̄h-ti, etc., anyone even, anyone at all (Rām. 1497; H. vii, 23; kũh-ti, Śiv. 311, Rām. 1762). As adj. any even, any at all (H. i, 5). kē̃h-ti, etc., anything even, anything at all (Śiv. 1476; Rām. 710, 1295, 1492); as adj. any at all (H. viii, 9). ¶ kĕh-na, see na kē̃h under na kū̃h, ab. ¶ kē̃h kē̃h pl. several of various kinds (Rām. 775). kē̃h kē̃h (pl.)... kē̃h kē̃h (pl.) some... others (Śiv. 125). kē̃h (pl.)... kē̃h (pl.) some... others (Rām. 778, 861-3, 1071-6; K.Pr. 102; L.V. 32). Similarly (sg. inan.) kē̃h... kē̃ʦhāh... kē̃h some... some... some, part... part... part (Rām. 1081). ¶ kễh-kyuthᵘ or kē̃h-kyuthᵘ adj. (f. -kiʦhᵘ̈), 'like something or other,' hence, used as a euphemism for something terrible or harmful, which it is ill-omened or inadvisable to mention. ¶ kũh akhāh m. a certain man, i.q. kã̄h akhāh, ab., but only masc. ¶ kuni-kinⁱ (Rām. 780) or kuni pöṭhⁱ, adv. in some way, in some way or other (K. 375, 448); in any way (K. 616). ¶ kunyukᵘ adj. (gen. of kē̃h) (f. kunicᵘ̈), of anything (Śiv. 475, 491, 728, 819, 1546; Rām. 1742). ¶ kaĩsi phiri, adv. sometimes, now and then; several times, frequently (El. kensih phiri, kentsi phiri). ¶ kē̃ʦhāh karun m.inf. to do something; esp. (in a bad sense) to do something malicious (to a person) (H. xii, 5, 10, 13, 19). -mē̃ʦhāh m. something or other.
conj. or; yutᵘ kĕhō totᵘ, here or there, at some place or other (K.Pr. 102).
f. (sg. dat. kē̃kalacĕ), a lizard, chameleon (K.Pr. 102; K. 836-7; L. 156, kauklat).

m. the ibex or Ladākī goat (Capra sibirica, L. 114 kel and kail, El. kail). It is found in the mountains of Ladak, Baltistān, and Wardwān. kĕlⁱ-phamb, kilⁱ-phamb, or kīlⁱ-phamb m. the under hair of the ibex. It is imported from Ladak and is a valuable shawl-wool. It is superior to all other wools, and finds its way with great difficulty to the Indian markets. For further particulars see El. s.v. kíl-phamb. Cf. bŏṭa- phamb, p. 138b, l. 24 (L. 114, kel famb; K.Pr. 94, kil-phamb).
f. the fruit of the plantain tree (Musa sapientium), a banana. It does not grow in the valley. -thürᵘ̈ f. a plantain tree (see ab.).

m. the resin of a deodar or other fir-tree, fir-tar; according to L. 80 (kilam) it is a kind of black pitch distilled from the roots of the Himalayan blue pine (Pinus excelsa, see kāyorᵘ and yörᵘ̈) and is used by men who work in the rice-fields, who anoint their legs and arms with it to protect themselves against water insects. Sheep are also marked with it.
or kĕli adv. of time (inter.) at what time? when? (Gr.Gr. 156).
m. pounded or minced meat, sold in this condition in the butchers' shops.
adj. c.g. one who is clever at supporting a large family on a small income, a clever, economical, and industrious housemaster or housewife.
f. successfully carrying housekeeping with a small income, clever economy.
in kĕmȧtⁱ kū̃shⁱ f. a kind of high-heeled shoe (see kū̃shⁱ) made of a special kind of variegated and embossed leather.
or کمخواب m. silk or satin worked with gold or silver flowers, 'cincob,' brocade (Śiv. 535, 789, 901).
m. a little worm. This term is principally used when scaring a little child from any small wormlike object of which it may catch sight.
adj. c.g. full of worms, defiled by worms, maggoty, worm-eaten. --karun -- m.inf. to make a person maggoty, i.e. to pester him with repeated unreasonable requests.
an adverbial suff. added pleonastically in wuñ-kĕn, now, at present (Gr.M.; Śiv. 634, 841, 1713, 1718-9; Rām. 852); a by-form of kani.
m. the fruit of the blue lotus or water lily (Nymphæa) (Śiv. 1809). Cf. kĕna-rab, s.v. kyonᵘ.
m. moistness, clamminess (cf. atha-kᵒ, p. 59a, l. 40).
m. a method of rice cultivation, in which the soil is ploughed wet (L. 332, 463 kenalu).
or kĕnnun conj. 3 (2 p.p. kĕnyōv or kĕnnyōv), to become moist; esp. to become too moist, too wet, too liquid (e.g. of food being cooked, or of earth being made into mud for plaster). Cf. kyonᵘ.
f. a kind of cup with a foot to it. Musalmān women eat their rice out of it. It is either of clay or copper (El.; H. x, 3). kĕnzi-khôsᵘ m., id.
kēnʦan; for kĕ˜ʦan, kē̃ʦan; see kē̃h.
kēnʦau; for kĕ˜ʦau, kē̃ʦau; see kē̃h.
kēnʦh; for kĕ˜ʦh, kē̃ʦh; see kē̃h.
kēnʦhāh; for kĕ˜ʦhāh, kē̃ʦhāh; see kē̃h.
m.pl. rays, beams (of the sun, etc.). Only used in pl.
m.pl. the various natures of men or women (kindly, crooked, good, evil, tender, cruel, and so on) (L.V. 92).

m.pl. in kiyāmatȧkⁱ kēran, translated in K.Pr. 214 by 'the day of resurrection'. If the word is not the same as kēran 1, it may possibly be a corruption of the Arabic قرن, a conjunction of the planets.
m. sect, religion, faith. köfir -kēsh, of an infidel sect, prone to infidelity (YZ. 11).
m. N. of a demon slain by Kṛṣṇa, in Skt. Kēśâsura (K. 368, 380).
m. a name of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) (Śiv. 737, 933, 1127, etc.; L.V. 8, 14).

f. the beard of corn (El. kisar; K.Pr. 112, translated 'barley'); the glumes of rice (L. 460, kesar); rice-chaff (El. kisr, Gr.Gr. 293, K.Pr. 234 = YZ. 124). kĕsari-bôrᵘ m. a kind of wall-plaster made of mud, etc., mixed with corn-beards.
or kīth m. (sg. dat. kētas or kītas), a comet (Śiv. 483, sg. voc. kēta); (in Hindū astronomy) the descending node, considered as the ninth planet (Rām. 399, 400, 406, 1277; K. 132).

postpos. governing dat. in, as in athas kĕth, in the hand (K.Pr. 29, YZ. 242, Śiv. 620), thālas kĕth, in a dish; nāvi kĕth, in a boat (Śiv. 1589). Generally speaking it can only be used with words signifying a receptacle or a conveyance. Thus, we cannot say garas kĕth, in a house, or mūlas kĕth, in a root, because a house or a root is not used as a receptacle for putting things into. For this purpose a horse or the like, is looked upon as a conveyance, and we can say guris kĕth, which must be translated 'on horseback'; similarly, nakhas- kĕth, on the shoulder (Rām. 890); khŏni-kĕth (carrying a child) on the haunch (H. xi, 13) (Gr.Gr. 43; Gr.M.; W. 97, kĕt; Śiv. 12, 245, 286, 543, 967, etc.; Rām. 151, 305, 625, 665, etc.; K. 378, 429, 433; H. ii, 7; iii, 2). For a special use, see kölⁱ-kĕth on the day after to-morrow (p. 434b, l. 8).

a suff. added pleonastically to the conj. part. of a verb, as in karith or karith kĕth, having done (Gr.Gr. 104, 197; L.V. 9; Śiv. 198; K. 50, 60, 110, etc.). L.V. 12 has also an older form karith used in the same way.

adv. in what manner? how? (Gr.Gr. 153; Gr.M.; L.V. 10; YZ. 24; Śiv. 157, 271, 594; Rām. 113, 157, 237, etc.; K. 4, 47, 52, etc.); with emph. y, kĕthay (Rām. 1017-9). -kana, or -kanan, or -kanas adv., i.q. kĕtha (Gr.M.; K. 272, -kana). -kinⁱ, how? by what means? by what manner of means? (K. 614). -pöṭhⁱ or -pöṭhin adv. in what manner? how? (El. kitha pãṭ and kiṭha póṭh; Gr.Gr. 153; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 15, kitah páṭhi; W. 96, kĕta pöṭh; Śiv. 171, 743, 755, 763, 820, 1251, etc. -pöṭhⁱ, with emph. y, kĕthay-pöṭhⁱ, 576; Rām. 53-4, 111, 412, etc., -pöṭhⁱ; 951, 1362, -pöṭhin; K. 9, 669, 799, -pöṭhⁱ; H. iii, 9; v, 8, etc., -pöṭhⁱ). Occasionally used indefinitely like kĕtha-tām-pöṭhⁱ, bel., in some way or other (Rām. 1111). -sana, -sanā-pöṭhⁱ, or -sanā-pöṭhin adv., i.q. the preceding, but the question is asked with a shade of doubt, quasi 'I wonder how', 'I should like to know how' (K. 165, 213, 328, 1134, -sana). -tām-pöṭhⁱ, or -tāmath-pöṭhⁱ, or -tāñ- pöṭhⁱ, or -tāñĕth-pöṭhⁱ (or -pöṭhin may be substituted throughout for -pöṭhⁱ) indef. adv. in some way, in any way, somehow, anyhow (Gr.Gr. 154). The underlying idea in the mind of the speaker is a question with doubt, as in, e.g. 'did he do it in any way? if so, how?' ¶ kĕthau or kĕthō adv. how? used in addressing a person at some distance or out of sight (L.V. 91, Śiv. 440, Rām. 812).

or kīwal m. alone, solitary; esp. one who has no family, relations, or connexions by marriage; lone, lonely, lone and lorn (Rām. 1219, 1591, 1623). As adv. only, merely, nothing but (Gr.M., L.V. 72, Śiv. 1472).

m. He Who is alone, Who is isolated (from all phenomenal existence), and is pure spirit, a title of the Supreme Śiva (Śiv. 161, 180, 361, 1540, 1605; these are all vocatives, for sg. nom. see Śiv. 512, 1333).

pron. suff. of the sing. nom. of the second person as in poku-kh, thou wentest; korᵘm-akh, thou wast made by me (Gr.Gr. 184). If this suff. is followed by another pron. suff. it becomes h. Thus karān chu-kh, thou makest, karān chu-h-a-s, thou makest for him (Gr.Gr. 181). With this word may be compared the Armenian kho, thy, in which Indo-European t- has become kh-.

pron. suff. of any case of the plur. of the third person, as in karān chu-kh, he makes them or he makes for them; koru-kh, he was made by them (Gr.Gr. 186). If this suff. is followed by another pron. suff. it becomes h, as in korᵘ-h-a-s, I was made by them (Gr.Gr. 181).

m. the sky, the firmament; (in Saiva philosophy) i.q. ākāsh, the principle of absolute vacuity, the wide and limitless expanse of empty space; -sŏrṻph m. he whose nature consists in the principle of absolute void, the Supreme Deity of the Śaivas (L.V. 15).

m. a dream (H. vi, 12, 14). --ḍēshun -- (H. vi, 11, 12, 14, 15) or --wuchun -- m.inf. to see a dream, to have a dream vision. ¶ khöbi, adv. in a dream (YZ. 9, 14, 250, 531). ¶ khābukᵘ töbīr m. the interpretation of a dream (H. vi, 14). ¶ khābas andar, adv. i.q. khöbi (YZ. 80). Cf. khwāb.

f. (El. wrongly makes the word m.) knowledge, acquaintance, information (regarding anything) (Rām. 132, 298, 733, 1248, 1349, 1652; H. iii, 3); information, belief, impression, surmise (that so-and-so is the case) (H. xii, 2); memory, remembrance (Rām. 1209-15); notice, care, heed, precaution (K.Pr. 105); information, a piece of information (Śiv. 844, 1280-1; Rām. 435, 560, 907, 1543); news, tidings, a piece of news (YZ. 38, 229; Śiv. 725, 729; Rām. 90, 209, 405, 508, 695, 750, 777, 798-9, etc.; H. ii, 1, 6; iii, 1; x, 7, 8, 14; xi, 20; xii, 23, 24; K. 36); report, rumour (Rām. 1308, 1757). ʦĕ chĕyĕ khabar, is there information to thee? do you know? (Gr.M.; similarly, Śiv. 761, 763, 769, 1292; Rām. 145, 272, 351, 493, 664, 761, 970, 1318-9, 1353, 1524; H. v, 7; xii, 20); panani pānücᵘ̈ khabar, consciousness of one's own existence (Śiv. 492). --kar --, when was the news? who knows when (such-and-such occurred) (H. ii, 4); when did one ever hear that? i.e. never at any time (Rām. 848, 1372). --karanwôlᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --karanwājĕñ --), an informer (El.). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to inform, tell (Gr.M.; W. 143; Śiv. 719; Rām. 91, 121, 840). --thawüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take care, be careful (Gr.M.). ¶ khabari-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), thoughtless (El.). ¶ khabarāh f. a piece of news (H. ii, 6).

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. khabardārĕñ), informed, certified (Śiv. 918, Rām. 405); aware; conscious (El.); careful, cautious (Rām. 870); attentive, heedful (Rām. 1743); ware of, careful against (K.Pr. 137, Rām. 799). As subst., a newsman, informer (H. ii, 1, 6; x, 7, 8; xii, 23); as interj. take care! beware! (Gr.M., W. 101).
f. informing, getting information; taking care, carefulness (Rām. 868); care, charge, custody, guardianship.
in khaca-gurᵘ m. a horse whose mane and tail-hair have been cut short.
in khacĕ-ryū̃ṭᵘ m. a low mean fellow, human only in form, but an animal in character, a low brute of a fellow. Cf. rē̃ṭun.
in khacĕ-zag a kind of paddy, producing a red coloured rice.

f. (sg. dat. khüzᵘ̈), the complete and sudden carrying off or disappearance of something collected or piled up (such as a heap of food, grain, or the like). --tulüñᵘ̈ --f.inf. to carry off or to destroy at once and completing something gradually collected; to consume entirely (a pile of food, or the like). --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. total disappearance or consumption to occur (e.g. of a pile of cooked or uncooked food by eating; or of something gradually collected to be suddenly destroyed by the act of God).
m. an ass, i.q. khar 1. This is the form that the word takes towards Islāmābād (El.).
(cf. khaḍa, khoḍᵘ, and khüḍᵘ̈), in khaḍ-cōd f. a woman, previously chaste and modest, who has taken to harlotry. Principally used in obsc. abuse. -kusᵘ̈ f., id.
m. a beam of wood (L. 458); a kind of forest wood useful for making beams. -kūṭᵘ m., id.
m. the vulva, the female organ of generation. Cf. khaḍ and khōḍᵘ.

m. N. of a site about four miles from Varāhamūla on the right bank of the Vitastā (Vĕth or Jehlam). Its Sanskrit name was Khādanāhāra. See RT.Tr. iii, 14 n. It is the lower limit of navigation on the Vĕth or Jehlam, the upper limit being Khanabal (see khan) (K.Pr. 103).

or khāndar m. a marriage, the marriage ceremony (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 126; L. 461; Śiv. 53, 412, 631, 638, 741, 838; Rām. 364; K. 665, 950). -bôgᵘ m. the marriage-share, i.e. the present which has to be sent to the house of the husband of any previously married sister of the bride or bridegroom. --karun -- m.inf. to carry out a marriage of a son or daughter (Rām. 136). -wôlᵘ m. the person who carries out a marriage, i.e. the father or guardian of a bride or bridegroom. -wŏʦhav m. a marriage festival; met. any household festival on the scale of or resembling a marriage festival. ¶ khã̄dara-bāpath adv. for the purpose of a marriage, on account of a marriage (e.g. a wedding present). -brō̃ṭh adv. before (in point of time) the marriage ceremony. -khã̄dar m. marriage upon marriage, many marriages; (a time in which) there are marriages upon marriages; the marriage season, the season which Hindūs consider to be propitious for marriages, and in which many marriages occur. -pata adv. after (in point of time) the marriage. ¶ khā̃daras-kyutᵘ adv., i.q. khã̄dara bāpath, ab.; at the time of the marriage.
f. an unchaste woman, i.q. khüḍᵘ̈, and principally used in low, obscene, abuse.

khidmath خدمت, khüdᵘ̈math or (qq.v.) khazmath or f. (sg. dat. khạdᵃmüʦᵃ, etc.), service, attendance, ministry (El. khidmat, m.) (khạdᵃmath, Rām. 791, 1531, 1638; khidmath, K.Pr. 22, 36, 94, 107; khizmath, K.Pr. 107; H. ii, 3); gurĕn-hünzᵘ̈ khazmath, service of horses, groom's work (H. xii, 3).
(Śiv. 435), khidmathgār خدمت گار (Śiv. 341) or khüdᵘ̈mathgār (Śiv. 970, 1793) m. a serving man, a servant (Śiv., as ab.); a table-servant, a butler (K.Pr. 25, khidᵒ).
f. the first milk given forth by a woman when a child is born; similarly (of a cow) beestings milk.
f. cheating, swindling (by lying tales, or the like). ¶ khāgari-pŏlāv m. a swindling ragout, swindling by fair promises (as if one promised a delicious ragout).

m. a cultivated field, esp. a seed bed for paddy, or the like (K.Pr. 121 khuāh, as if for khwāh). ¶ khāha milawan m. intermingling of cultivated fields, i.e. when the lands of two adjacent villages are close together on the common border, and are to a certain extent locally intermingled. -püṭᵘ̈ f. a cultivated field which has been measured, and of which the area is known. -wôñᵘ m. the water brought by irrigation into rice-land. ¶ khāhas-manz adv. in, or into, a field (commonly used with regard to agricultural operations, or the like). -pĕṭh adv. to the field (the postposition pĕṭh being here, as in the case of certain other words, used after verbs of motion).
m. a man of the Khas (Sanskrit Khaśa) tribe, i.q. khokhᵘ 2, q.v.
adj. c.g. wishing, desiring. Cf. dilkhāh.
m. a place where wine is made and deposited (El.).

f. (sg. dat. khaharüñᵘ̈ 1), a whetstone, a grindstone. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to apply the whetstone, to whet; met. to confirm, promote, add fuel to a person's anger. --lagüñᵘ̈ 1 -- f.inf. the whetstone to be applied, whetting to be going on (with regard to any cutting weapon or tool). ¶ khaharüñᵘ̈-gorᵘ̈ m. a man whose profession it is to apply the whetstone, a knife-grinder, a sword-grinder, etc. --khasun 1 -- m.inf. to mount on to a whetstone or grindstone, to be put to the grindstone (of a cutting weapon or tool). --khotᵘ-motᵘ 1 -- perf. part. (f. --khüʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), mounted on to the whetstone or grindstone.

f. (sg. dat. khaharüñᵘ̈ 2), extreme obstinacy in one's opinion or purpose (of a stupid, foolish, person, who has no real reason for his obstinacy), pig-headedness. --lagüñᵘ̈ 2 -- f.inf. such obstinacy to be practised (by such a person). ¶ khaharüñᵘ̈ khasun 2 m.inf. to mount on to obstinacy, to be obstinate, as ab. --khotᵘ-motᵘ 2 -- perf. part. (f. --khüʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), obstinate, as ab., pig-headed.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. khohᵘ, 2 p.p.khahyōv), to ornament with a pattern; habitually to gaze at a person with intent to do him an injury, to watch him with evil intent. ¶ khahan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who makes patterns; one who habitually gazes, as ab.; met. one who is outwardly friendly to another, but is really watching for an opportunity to injure him.
m. a tent, pavilion (El. khema). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to pitch a tent, to encamp (El.).

or khör خآر m. good fortune, prosperity, welfare, well-being, weal (K.Pr. 25, 103, 150). dwā-yi-khör, a prayer for (so-and-so's) welfare (H. i, 3); cf. khörᵘ̈ 3. -khāh خیر خواہ m. a well-wisher; a government spy (L. 421). -khöhī خیر خوآہی f. the profession of a government spy (L. 421).
(? spelling) in khair-pōsh (?) m. Villarsia nymphoides (El.). Probably khürᵘ̈-pōsh. Cf. khorᵘ 1 and kūrū.
f. (sg. dat. khajālüʦᵘ̈), bashfulness, shame, sense of shame (K.Pr. 4); a sense of humiliation, lowliness.

m. openness, (of a receptacle) ability to receive more than its actual contents; width, extension, wideness (El., Rām. 796); a finger's breadth (El. cf. tọ̆sᵘ, p. 1037a, l. 49). Cf. kholᵘ and Gr.Gr. 141.
adj. c.g. ashamed, abashed; bashful, modest (El. khajal). --karun -- m.inf. to humiliate, abash; esp. to humiliate a person by directing abusive language at him.
or khüjᵘ̈ f. oilcake, the cake left after oil has been pressed out from walnuts, oilseeds, or the like. Cf. khal 3 (L. 462, kaj). khȧjⁱ-lŏkhurⁱ m. a lump or ball of oilcake.

m. a plan, sketch, outline, tracing, delineation; (in Kāshmīrī) the marks or remains on paper after writing or drawing has been rubbed or wiped out. --trāwun -- m.inf. to make the first drawing or outline (as a guide to the painter) of a picture or design that is to be coloured; to mark the lines of a drawing or pattern on a substance to be engraved (as a guide for the engraver).
m. (sg. dat. khākas), dust, earth, ashes (YZ. 19; Śiv. 828; Rām. 156, 444, 874, 1537). With iẓāfat, khāk-i-gam, the ashes of grief (Rām. 441).
