f. onomat. the rustling or crackling sound made by dried skins, sheets of bark, or the like, when they are moved (K.Pr. 26 khakarāy).

or khỗkhur or m. (sg. dat. khã̄kharas), the interstices or hollow under or between a number of great rocks piled together; --˚ a bone of the body devoid of flesh, etc. Cf. ȧchⁱ-khỗkhur (p. 8a, l. 28), aḍiji-˚ (p. 14a, l. 38), and khã̄kur.

or khakhürᵘ̈ f. a kind of torture inflicted as a punishment on a criminal (by throwing him on the ground and dragging him a long way by his legs) (K. 450); dragging in this way done by children in play. --˚ used met. (cf. buthⁱ-˚, p. 142a, l. 48). ¶ khakhari-thāl m. a kind of large caldron (so heavy that it cannot be lifted, and is dragged about only with difficulty). khakhari-zāl m. a drag net, a kind of fishing net dragged along the bed of a river (not thrown in and lifted out).
m. a certain small seed used as an eyesalve; Sisymbrium irio (El.), London-rocket.
(? spelling) m. the osseous rim of the orbital cavity (El.). Cf. khã̄khur.
adj. (f. khā̃kijᵘ̈), somewhat beloved (u.w. reference to a child whom one loves, but whom one is scolding).

m. (sg. abl. khala 1), a threshing-floor (K.Pr. 29; Śiv. 1212, 1476, 1748; H. ix, 9); met. a harvest, crop (El.); a granary (El.). -andar adv. in or on the threshing-floor. --ganḍun -- m.inf. the fastening of a threshing-floor, i.e. the hedge or wall surrounding it. -pahörᵘ̈ f. the hut on a threshing-floor in which the guardian stays. -pȧlⁱyār f. the hedge round a threshing-floor. -rôchᵘ m. the guardian of a threshing-floor. -sörᵘ̈ f. the collection or piling up of crops on a threshing-floor; the carrying away of crops or grain from a threshing-floor and accumulating it elsewhere. -zāg f. the night-watching of a threshing-floor. ¶ khala-bāgay f. the division on the threshing-floor, esp. the separation of the Government share and that of the village servants before the grain is taken away. -bonᵘ m. the pile of crops or of grain on a threshing-floor. -borᵘ m. the little gate giving admission to a threshing-floor. -baran m. the large gate of a threshing-floor, for the entrance and exit of cultivators, etc. -ḍuvyunᵘ m. the sweepings of a threshing-floor, the refuse left there after the grain is removed. -nĕbar adv. outside the threshing-floor. -zāgay f. the night-watching of threshing-floor. ¶ khalas-manz adv. in the threshing-floor. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause to enter into the threshing-floor, to commence carrying crops into it.
m. a mole; an artificial spot painted on the face to increase beauty, a beauty-spot (El., who gives both khal and khál; YZ. 10, 11, 67, 68).

f. dried skin, leather; the skin of a living being (K.Pr. 156, māz vĕʦĕs na khali, his flesh will not fit into his skin, i.e. he will not be able to contain himself for joy); cf. udᵘ̈rᵘ̈-khal, p. 15a, l. 40. -khish f. 'slaughtering of hides'; hence, the skin of a sheep, together with all the edible parts, when it is slaughtered, as opp. to the offal (K.Pr. 237, where the compound is freely translated 'slaughter of beasts'). -würᵘ̈ f. skin-cake, a kind of stew made of chopped sheep- or goat-skin boiled till it is tender and served with spices. This word is generally used in the plural (-warĕ).
m. a maternal uncle, a mother's brother. Sg. voc. khāla (K.Pr. 260, W. 156).
f. oil-cake, i.q. khȧjⁱ. Cf. ȧlⁱshi-khal, p. 25b, l. 5.
f. skin. khāla-dar m. the chess- board square of skin; hence, the position inside the skin, the womb, being born, human life (Śiv. 1644).
adv. at some time or other, sometimes. -kã̄ʦhāh c.g. an. someone or other.
(for خآلی) adv. only, merely. Cf. khölⁱ.

adv. (for 1, see khal 1), together, as a whole, wholesale (of a number of articles sold together at an inclusive price); cf. khili. -khanjĕ adv. all together, good and bad together, all sorts together without distinction. ¶ khali 1 (for 2, see kholᵘ) in khali karun m.inf. to mix up bad and good together (of grain, or the like, of which the good grains have been originally separated from the bad).
m. being marred by fault or negligence, disturbance; slight injury, trouble, inconvenience (Rām. 735). In Kāshmīrī with suff. of indef. art. khalalā خللا m. interference (El.). Cf. khilāl 2.
f. the act of stirring (with a ladle, etc., in cooking) (K.Pr. 208, sg. abl. khalani). Cf. khŏluwᵘ.
(? spelling and gender) N. of a certain medicinal herb, Senecio Jacquemontiana (L. 75).

m. liberation, release, deliverance; in Kāshmīrī, adj. c.g. free (El.). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become free, be set at liberty (YZ. 462); (of a woman in labour) to be delivered (of the child); met. to become free of worldly troubles, to die (H. iii, 4). --karun -- m.inf. to set at liberty, release (El.). --sapanun -- m.inf. to become free, be set at liberty (YZ. 136). -wôrᵘ m. a deed of sale (of a horse, cow, or the like), a deed of release.

m. (sg. dat. khalᵃtas), a robe; a robe of honour with which princes or those in authority confer dignity on subjects (K.Pr. 245); the complete set of dresses worn by a bridegroom, a bridegroom's outfit of clothes. ¶ khalᵃta-bāha m. (at a marriage) the present of gold, etc., ornaments given by the father of the bride to the bridegroom, as a contribution towards the cost of his wedding outfit. ¶ khalᵃt-ĕ-shöhī خلعت شاہی m. a royal robe, a magnificent robe of honour (H. x, 4).
f. scattering (articles) hither and thither; confusion, commotion, hurry (El.), bustle, hubbub, rushing about and making a stir (K.Pr. 78). Cf. khalbürᵘ̈.
f. (in some work being done by someone else) thrusting in the hands and throwing it into confusion. Cf. khalbȧlⁱ.

f. pricking, pain; care, solicitude, anxiety (Rām. 714); apprehension, misgiving; a cause of anxiety, cause of trouble, impediment (Rām. 110); (in Kāshmīrī) the hidden relics of a disease that remain after an apparent cure.
m. (sg. dat. khalkatas), a created being, a creature (El.); creation, the world, universe (Gr.M.).
f. freedom (El. khalásí). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to release.
m. lands under management of government, crown or government land (L. 426).

or (El.) khulun conj. 3 (2 p.p. khalyōv), to be or become spread out or spread about, to be or become wide. The caus. (or tr.) form of this verb is khạlᵃrāwun or khạjᵃrāwun (Gr.Gr. 174). khalyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. khalē-müʦᵘ̈), opened, spread out, spread about.

conj. 1, another form of khārun, q.v. (1 p.p. khôlᵘ, f. khöjᵘ̈, H. vii, 19; 2 p.p. khājyōv), to cause to mount, to cause to ascend; to take upstairs (H. x, 7); to fix (upon a machine) (H. vii, 19); zima khālun, to cause responsibility to mount (upon so-and-so), to prove (so-and-so) responsible (H. x, 12); and so on in all the meanings of khārun.
m. (sg. dat. khalaras), a kind of small stone mortar, used for pounding medicines, etc.
subst. m. a dried skin; the skin of animals (El.); as adj. (f. khalᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 1) met. withered and shrunk, very old and withered.
m. (sg. dat. khalwatas), retirement, solitude, privacy (El.); a private place, a secret place, a closet, a place of retirement (Rām. 1744).
or khalᵘ̈kh خلق m. (sg. dat. khalkhas), creation; mankind; people; the people or population of a country (Rām. 207, 1130).
f. (sg. dat. khạlᵃrüñᵃ), the act of widening out, opening out (e.g. a narrow hole); spreading out (a garment, or the like). Cf. kholᵘ and khalun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. khạlᵃrôwᵃ), to widen (e.g. a narrow hole); to spread out, loosen (e.g. a garment). This verb is the caus. of khalun, another form being khạjᵃrāwun (Gr.Gr. 174).
f. a small piece of dried crumpled up skin (cf. basta-khᵒ, p. 135a, l. 45) (K.Pr. 84, khalari).

m. a bend, curl, crook; crookedness, curvature (YZ. 51, 53); bending, flexure; being bent into a fork. --aʦun -- m.inf. bending to enter, fiexure or curvature to occur, esp. when the subsequent straightening would be difficult. --karun -- m.inf. to bend, crooken; to bend, to twirl (a rosary in prayer) (K.Pr. 212).

m. unripe, green, crude, immature (K.Pr. 119; Śiv. 1112; Rām. 1030; H. vi, 15); imperfect, bad, inferior, worthless, of small value (K.Pr. 64; Rām. 298, 383); inexpert, inexperienced; untaught and stupid (K.Pr. 11); not solid or substantial, not made of masonry; rough, approximate (as an estimate); lower, smaller (weight or measure, opp. to pŏkhta, the larger of two standard weights, etc.). -gĕv m. uncooked ghī (clarified butter). --gaz -- m. the smaller yard measure in Kashmīr, being 15/16ths of the pŏkhta yard. It is used for measuring cloth, etc. --paĩsa -- or --pö̃sa -- m. the copper pice formerly current in Kashmīr, now being superseded by the British pice worth about a farthing (cf. hath). Its value varied from time to time (H. vii, 25-6). --rŏpay -- m. the old local Kāshmīrī rupee, now being superseded by the British rupee, and about half its value (L. 242). --sīrᵘ̈ -- f. an unbaked brick, a mud brick. --tab -- m. a kind of fever, low fever; the start of fever when the temperature is low and the pulse is going up, fever with a temperature over 102˚ is called pokᵘ tab. -tamā خام طعام adj. c.g. entertaining vain desires; hence, (in Kāshmīrī) very covetous, avaricious (K.Pr. 103). --tīl -- m. raw oil, unboiled oil. ¶ khāmi-khām خامِ خام adj. c.g. absolutely raw, not in the least cooked (and so on, in all the uses of khām).

m. uncured skin, undried and fresh from the animal. --marun -- m.inf. to apply or fix damp skin, as in making the top of a drum; to fix damp skin on the face as a disguise or kind of mask, as was the custom in Kashmīr in former times.
f. cough and stridor due to obstruction of the larynx, common in Kashmīr owing to specific disease and leprosy. It is rare in England. Cf. khamun.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. khamadārĕñ), become crooked, crookened (of a stick, or the like).
adv. willingly or unwillingly, nolens volens, perforce; certainly, positively, inevitably, at all events.
adj. c.g. suffering from cough, etc.; see khama.

f. a sharp-pointed stone or potsherd (Rām. 1250); a large piece of ice from the heavens. These pieces of ice are said to be so large as to kill people (El. khambirri; cf. kham 2). ¶ khambarĕ pĕñĕ f. pl. inf. a very violent storm of rain or ice, as ab. (compared to a shower of pointed flints), to fall.
khamijᵘ̈ or khamyulᵘ, in danda-khambyulᵘ, etc., p. 224b, ll. 19 ff.
f. the hollow left in a heap of grain, when a portion of grain is removed from it.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. khomᵘ. This verb is impersonal in tenses formed from the past participles. Thus khomun, it was coughed by him, he coughed), to be subject to attacks of coughing accompanied by stridor due to obstruction of the larynx; to be breathless (El., Rām. 483). Cf. khama.

m. a hole, a pit; esp. a hollow in a pile of grain, caused by taking some of the grain out of it (cf. khambᵘ̈rᵘ̈ and atha-khan, p. 58b, l. 43); the hollow or depression between two mountain peaks; a breach or channel cut in the bank of a flooded river for drawing off superfluous water; a breach cut by the water in the bank of a flooded river (cf. Gr.Gr. 123). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to make such an artificial cut in the bank of a flooded river. --ganḍun -- m.inf. to block up such a cut or breach in the bank of a river so as to stop the flow of water through it. --gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. such breaches in the bank of a river to occur; met. pits to occur (in the belly), extreme hunger to occur (cf. bata-khan, p. 136b, l. 44). ¶ khana-bal m.inf. the place where such a cut or breach occurs in the bank of the main river; N. of a place at the head waters of the river Vĕth (Jehlam) in Anatnāg Pargana, where three rivers meet and together form the Vĕth. See RT.Tr. II, 412, 414 n. It is the upper limit of navigation in Kashmīr, as khādan-yār (q.v.) is the lower limit (K.Pr. 103). -rôchᵘ m. the watchman of such a cut or breach. He guards the embankment and directs the course of boats, etc.
m. lord, prince; a title of Musalmān nobles; common adjunct to Paṭhān names (H. ii, 1, 12). ¶ khāna-bāy f. the wife of a Khān.
m. a table (not used by Hindūs) (El., K.Pr. 103, YZ. 29).
f. (sg. dat. khöñᵘ̈), a mine, a place whence minerals are dug (Gr.M.).

m. a house, dwelling (K.Pr. 4, 37; Rām. 131, 305; H. vi, 4); a receptacle, drawer, compartment; a pigeon-hole (in a desk); a socket; a square (of a chessboard) (Gr.M.); a window-pane (Gr.M.) Often --˚ as in dīwān-khāna, a hall of audience (Śiv. 968), köd-khāna, a prison (Rām. 587, 684; H. v, 7, 8; vi, 10), kutub-kh., a library, mahala-kh., a palace, etc., qq.v. -dāmād خانہ داماد m. a son-in-law in the house; a son-in-law who lives in his father-in-law's house (as Jacob did in Laban's), and who has to work as a drudge until the marriage, i.e. usually for a period of seven years (L. 267). --dāmödī -- خانہ دامآدی f. the system under which such a son-in-law is taken into a house (L. 267). -möjᵘ̈ f. a house-mother; hence, a darling and much loved girl member of a family (W. 17). -mājĕr m. the condition of such a loved girl. -môlᵘ m. a house-father; hence, a darling and much loved boy member of a family (K.Pr. 104, W. 17); a young gentleman (El.).
m. (f. khānadārĕñ), a family man, a householder (Śiv. 339, 1065, 1313); (from the point of view of the wife) a husband; (fem.) (from the point of view of the husband) a wife.
adj. c.g. possessing compartments or partitions, pigeonholed (e.g. a window or a desk).
f. the state of a master of a family; housekeeping (Śiv. 578, 587, 1049); living in the world, the life of a householder (as opp. to an ascetic life) (Rām. 1621).
m. a Musalmān convent, monastery, a religious establishment for holy men.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. khananôwᵘ), to cause to dig; to cause to be dug, to get (a pit) dug, to have dug (H. x, 13).

m. (sg. abl. khanḍa 1), coarse sugar (Śiv. 207, 283, 374, 1169, 1202, 1524). ¶ khanḍa-gurᵘ m. a sugar horse, sugar moulded into the form of a horse (given to children. So also sugar in other forms, such as that of a man, a parrot, an elephant, etc.); cf. -mahan- yuwᵘ, bel. -grohuñᵘ m. 'sugar-fierce', i.e. one who deals honestly in all his affairs. -hākᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. sugar-priced, sold at the price of sugar; hence (of something very valuable) sold at a very small price (only of fem. articles). -mahanyuwᵘ m. a sugar man, sugar moulded into the form of a man, cf. -gurᵘ, ab.; met. a man of a thoroughly pleasing appearance and sweet disposition. -maṭh m. (sg. dat. -maṭas), a jar full of sugar; met. a charming, sweet-dispositioned man, sincere, virtuous, and well-to-do. -mŏṭh f. (sg. dat. -mŏṭhi), a handful of sugar; as much sugar as can be contained in the hand. -pholᵘ m. a small, indefinite amount of sugar. -phuṭᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a tied-up packet of sugar. -ʦṻn m. sugar-powder, castor sugar; met. any powder resembling such sugar.

m. a part, a portion, piece (K. 430); a division of the earth, a region, country (Śiv. 1257), used --˚ to indicate indefiniteness, with slight diminution, as in kruh, a kōs; kruh khanḍ, about a kōs, but a little less. In such compounds the noun generally takes the suff. of the indef. art., and khanḍ then becomes khanḍā, as in kruhāh khanḍā; similarly dŏhāh khanḍā, about a day, but something less; rŏpayāh khanḍā, about a rupee, but something less; akhāh khanḍā, nearly one (Gr.Gr. 93, W. 13, khand). --karun -- m.inf. to break into fragments, to break in pieces (K. 429).
m. laughing, smiling; a laugh, a smile. --karun -- m. to smile (YZ. 234).
in khanḍa-hŏgöḍᵘ̈ f. a kind of dried fish (cf. hŏgöḍᵘ̈).

in khanḍa-wāv m. a shawl-weaver, a weaver of the cloth called pashmīna, both made of the fine wool of Central Asian goats (cf. L. 316, 317). Regarding the Kāshmīrī shawl-weavers, see L. as ab., and El. s.v. khándawáo (K.Pr. 104, 201). -wāv-bāy f. his wife. -wāv-kôjᵘ m. a shawl-weaver's breakfast. These people sit at their looms from early morning to night with only a short respite for food (L. 316). They breakfast at about 11 a.m. (later than other people), and this expression is used to indicate that time of day (K.Pr. 176). -wāvil f. the profession of a shawl-weaver. -wāv-tᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a shawl-weaver's needle (used in picking up and joining the threads). -wāv ʦọ̆lᵘ m. a wretched, lowly, shawl-weaver.

m. N. of a quarter of the city of Śrīnagar, the ancient Skandabhavana, named after Skandagupta, who founded a vihāra, or monastery, here. It is situated on the right bank of the river between the sixth bridge (Nowᵘ Kạdᵃl) and the 'Īdgāh on the western out- skirts of the city. See RT.Tr. II, 339.
f. (sg. dat. khanḍë˘ʦᵘ̈), the condition of being broken; the condition of being maimed, etc.; loss (of the fruits of former good actions), ill-luck.
m. (sg. dat. khandakhas or khandakas), a ditch, moat, fosse, trench.
f. (sg. dat. khạndᵃrüñᵃ), the act of breaking into fragments; division into shares (Gr.Gr. 121); dividing a work among a number of people.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. khạnḍᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. khạnḍᵃrun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. khạnḍᵒrᵒ), to break to pieces; to break off or take off some part or limb; to divide into shares. khạnḍᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. khạnḍᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), broken into fragments; having some part or limb broken off or taken away; divided into shares.
m. the wearing many clothes, the being well-clothed, see khonᵘ.
m. or khanjarī f. a poniard, a dagger (El.; YZ. 6, 449; Rām. 38, 371, 903, 434).
m. the condition of being broken, etc., as in khonḍᵘ, q.v.

f. a mode of printing or staining silk, striped silk. khanjᵃ̇rⁱ-pushĕṭh f. (sg. dat. pushṭi), a thong made of this stuff, for tying on a wooden sandal (cf. dĕlⁱ-puᵒ, p. 267b, l. 50). ¶ khanjȧrⁱ-wö̃ka f.pl. a method of tying the hair in long plaits down the back. This method is principally used by prostitutes, and sometimes by little girls.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. khonᵘ 2, for 1, see s.v.; f. khüñᵘ̈), to dig (K.Pr. 155, 247; L. 459; Śiv. 590, 746, 994, 1043, 1197, 1214, 1373, 1754; Rām. 343, 958, 1147, 1724; H. xii, 6); to engrave (Śiv. 414, 671, 1760; Rām. 1583). ¶ khonᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. khüñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), dug (e.g. a field, or a well); engraved. ¶ khanan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a digger. ¶ khanith kaḍun m.inf. having dug to drag out; met. to elicit (a person's secret thoughts or intentions).
Old Persian Xapā), adj. c.g. displeased, vexed, angry. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become angry.

m. one who is a fornicator or adulterer, a lecher. Genl. used --˚, the first word being such a word as 'sister', 'daughter', or the like, to indicate, in foul abuse, that the person referred to has misconducted himself with such a female relation.
m. a severe cudgelling (as a punishment).
f. (sg. dat. khapi), a rope halter put on a horse for feeding.
f. in khapa-khaph f. a method of copulation, called in Sanskrit kīla.
f. (sg. dat. khapi), a confused sound, a disturbance (esp. caused by out- siders or naughty children to a peaceful company).

f. one-half of the cranium or brain-pan, generally used --˚, as in kala-khᵒ, 'the front half of the cranium of the head,' i.e. the forehead and neighbouring parts of the skull. See kala. ¶ khaphari phamb ʦānun to put cotton-wool into the cranium; met. (just as thrusting a very small piece of cotton-wool into a wounded cranium causes intense pain; and as the cotton-wool appears from the pain to be much larger than it really is) greatly to increase another's slight pain (physical or mental) by some petty action.

(cf. خفّت) m. (sg. dat. khaphtas), sudden pride or self-conceit (exhibited, without reason, by a fool). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to expel self-conceit, to take down a person's pride; esp. (of a merchant) to make public his bankruptcy, to disclose the fact that he is at the end of his resources.

adj. (f. khapüṭᵘ̈, dat. khapacĕ), smashed, broken to pieces (e.g. an earthen jar or a skull so broken). A variant form of the f., khạpᵘ̈ṭᵘ̈, is used --˚, to form diminutives in a contemptuous sense, as in aina-khạpᵘ̈ṭᵘ̈, a small mirror of no value; gurⁱ-khⁱ, a wretched starved little horse; kȧrⁱ khᵒ, a mean little worn-out bracelet.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. khopᵘ. This verb is impersonal in tenses formed from the past participles) to be one who habitually has unlawful intercourse with women (esp. one who does this forcibly), to be a raper, to be a fornicator, to be an adulterer; to commit adultery (El.).
f.inf. conj. 1 (1 p.p. f. khüpᵘ̈), to have unlawful connexion with a woman (esp. when with one who is unwilling), to rape (so-and-so).
m. a kind of fine cloth, muslin.

m. (f. khürᵘ̈ or khariñ), a donkey, an ass (L.V. 88; K.Pr. 26, 73, 104-5, 166, 174, 190, 215, 235, 262; H. iii, 8, 9; v, 7; K. 224); often used ˚--, to indicate the commonest, largest, or coarsest of the kind, like 'horse' in our 'horse-radish', 'a horse-laugh', etc.; cf. khar-bādām, bel., and kharkhasun, s.v. Towards Islāmābād the word is pronounced khaḍ (El.). -āhang f. an ass's bray (K.Pr. 235). -baca m. a baby ass, a very young ass's foal. -bādām m. a kind of bitter almond, see El. s.v. bádám. -bôrᵘ m. an ass's load; met. a heavy load, too heavy to be comfortably carried by a man. -khāv adj. c.g. an ass-eater; met. one who is universally condemned and vilified (K.Pr. 104). -khāv gaʦhun m.inf. become a subject of ill-repute, to get a bad name, acquire (justly or unjustly) an evil repute. -khāv karun m.inf. to give a person a bad name, to bring him into disrepute (whether deserved or not). -kan m. 'ass-eared', a hare, i.q. khargōsh, q.v. s.v. -kura m. an ass's colt; met. a capricious troublesome child. -lĕd f. (sg. dat. -lë̆zᵘ̈), ass's dung. -mĕng m. a kind of grass, said to make man garrulous and mad, when eaten unawares. -paḍur m. N. of a certain fruit, a kind of pear. -palana m. an ass's pack-saddle. -pūtᵘ m. an ass's colt (K.Pr. 104). -sᵃh m. a certain animal, described as a small-sized leopard that kills only small animals, not larger than an ass. -ṭö̃cᵘ̈ f. N. of a certain fruit, a kind of wild pear (El. khar-ṭánj). -ṭö̃g f. the bray of an ass. -trēl f. N. of a kind of small wild apple. -ʦam f. ass's skin; met. any hard and tough skin, like that of an ass. -ʦŏth f. (sg. dat. ʦŏ̈ʦᵘ̈), an ass's anus; the generative organs of an ass (male or female). -ʦũ̄̈ṭh f. (sg. dat. ʦũ̄̈ṭi), an ass's fart. -wôlᵘ m. a man who, as a means of livelihood, owns asses for carrying burdens, an ass driver who owns his asses (L. 459). ¶ kharas khārun m.inf. to mount (a person) on an ass; met. to put (a person) to public shame, to disgrace. --khasun -- m.inf. to become mounted on an ass; met. to be put to public shame, to become disgraced (K.Pr. 16, 105; cf. 174).

m. (sg. abl. khāra 1; the pl. dat. of this word is khāran 1, which is to be distinguished from khāran 2, q.v., s.v.), a blacksmith, an iron worker (cf. bandūka-khār, p. 111b, l. 46; K.Pr. 46; H. xi, 17); a farrier (El.). This word is often a part of a name, and in such case comes at the end (W. 118) as in Wahab khār, Wahab the smith (H. ii, 12; vi, 17). ¶ khāra-basta f. the skin bellows of a blacksmith. -büṭhᵘ̈ f. the wall of a blacksmith's furnace or hearth. -bāy f. a blacksmith's wife (Gr.Gr. 34). -dŏkurᵘ m. a blacksmith's hammer, a sledge-hammer. -gȧjⁱ or -güjᵘ̈ f. a blacksmith's furnace or hearth. -hāl f. (sg. dat. -höjᵘ̈), a blacksmith's smelting furnace; cf. hāl 5. -kūrᵘ̈ f. a blacksmith's daughter. -koṭᵘ m. the son of a blacksmith, esp. a skilful son, who can work at the same profession. -küṭᵘ̈ f. a blacksmith's daughter, esp. one who has the virtues and qualities properly belonging to her father's profession or caste. -më̆ʦᵘ̈ 1 f. (for 2, see khāra 3), 'blacksmith's earth,' i.e. iron-ore. -nĕcyuwᵘ m. a blacksmith's son. -nay f. (for khāranay 2, see khārun), the trough into which the blacksmith allows melted iron to flow after smelting. -ʦᵃñĕ f.pl. charcoal used by blacksmiths in their furnaces. -wān m. a blacksmith's shop, a forge, smithy (K.Pr. 30). -waṭh m. (sg. dat. -waṭas), the large stone used by a blacksmith as an anvil.
m. N. of a demon, who was slain by Rāmacandra. He was a younger brother of Rāvaṇa (Rām. 337, 340, 350, 633).

or khwār خوار adj. c.g. poor, distressed, become poor, reduced to poverty; deserted, abandoned, friendless, wretched (Śiv. 421, Rām. 1697); abject, vile, base, contemptible (cf. khārakhas) (K.Pr. 247); ruined, desolate (El.); ruined, destroyed, spoiled (K.Pr. 248, Rām. 1380-1); distraught, full of anxiety or sorrow (Rām. 1623). --gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. -gömüʦᵘ̈), become poor; become contemptible, despised, despicable (YZ. 486); become distressed, become full of anxiety or sorrow, distraught (Rām. 1463, 1665); etc., as ab. --karun -- m.inf. to reduce a person to distress or poverty (e.g. by unkindness, by robbing him, or by seducing him to profligacy) (Rām. 1386, 1481); to make despised, bring to contempt (YZ. 37, 568); to ruin, destroy (Rām. 1380). --ta kharāba -- adj. c.g. reduced to the greatest straits, greatly distressed (by loss of livelihood); reduced to distress (by disease), etc.

m. a certain kind of worm or caterpillar possessing fourteen legs. ¶ khara-pāv karān adv. in great haste, in great hurry, without time for sitting down (u.w. vbs. of giving, taking, etc.). -zang-hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -zang-hishᵘ̈), like the leg of this worm; hence, very small, minute, microscopic.

f. (sg. dat. khörᵘ̈ 1, Gr.Gr. 71), an ass's load (the ḵẖarwār of Persia and India); a dry measure containing sixteen trakh of 11 19/175 lb. each, and hence equal to 177 129/175 lb. avoirdupois (L. 243). According to El., however, a trakh is about 9 1/2 lb., and a khār is hence 152 lb. (K.Pr. 5, 28, 90, 106, 118, 138, 168; W. 103; Śiv. 591, 1795). By local custom, a khār of rice, maize, and barley consists of only 15 trakhs, or 166 22/35 lb. (L. l.c.). As a measure of land, a khār represents the area which is supposed to require a khār weight of rice-seed, or exactly 4 British acres (L. l.c.). -bôrᵘ m. a load (of grain, or the like) weighing one khār. khār ḍŏḍ khār f. about one or one and a half khār (in weight). --maṭi khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a khār weight to mount on the shoulder; met. a heavy responsibility to be imposed upon one (e.g. to find oneself responsible for the support of a large family when one is without the necessary means). --zᵃkhörᵘ̈ -- f. about one or two khār (in weight). ¶ khörᵘ̈-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of a khār; hence (of a basket, or the like) large enough to contain a khār (of grain, etc.). ¶ khörᵘ̈v-pöṭhᵘ̈ or -pöṭhin adv. in khārs, i.e. in a large number of khārs, in an indefinite number of khārs.
in khar-khar m. onomat. the rattling or rustling sound made by skins of dry leather, or similar dry sheets. Cf. khᵃr-khᵃr, s.v. khᵃr 2.
m. a thorn (L.V. 96, K.Pr. 47, Śiv. 827), i.q. khāra 2, q.v.

adj. c.g. good, excellent; genuine, real, true; just, fair, right; upright, sincere (Gr.M.); clear, manifest, permanently bright (Śiv. 1642, 1774); cf. khorᵘ 6. --karun -- m.inf. to make clearly intelligible, to make clearly understood. -sara karun m.inf. to make a clear enquiry; hence, after due investigation to decide correctly.

adj. c.g. standing up, erect, upright; standing, stationary; (of something which may be liquid, etc.) solid, undissolved (Śiv. 336); solid, substantial, firm (Śiv. 330, 340, 625); ready, prepared (Śiv. 1586). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to stand up, become erect; (of one asleep) to rise from sleep, to be aroused, to be awakened, to awake (K. 232). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain standing, to stand, stay, wait; esp. to stand in attendance, or in order to help.

or khār 4 (L.V. 96, K.Pr. 47, Śiv. 827) m. (for 1, see khār 1), a thorn, prickle, spine (K.Pr. 47; Śiv. 827, 1530); (in Kāshmīrī) envy, jealousy, secret hate; desire (El., YZ. 52); great sorrow (Rām. 1484, cf. khār 2). -khāra (= خار خار) m. disquietude; longing for something unobtained or unobtainable; the growth of secret hatred. Cf. khura-khura, s.v. khura 1.
adj. c.g. salt, saline, brackish. --më̆ʦᵘ̈ 2 -- f. (for 1, see khār 1), saline soil, soil impregnated with alkali, sour soil (the kharzamin of L. 321). --wôñᵘ -- m. salt water, brackish water.
sg. abl. of khar 1 and 2, qq.v.

in khāra-wāl f. raising and lowering; bringing up and down (e.g. a great load or equipment up and down in mountainous country); (in Śaiva philosophy) the raising of the soul to the Brahma-randr (Brahma-randhra, p. 121a, l. 8) and the bringing it down again.

or (cf. khār 2) kharāba adj. c.g. ruined, spoiled, desolate, depopulated, wasted; abandoned, lost, miserable, wretched; bad, worthless, vitiated, corrupt, noxious, vicious. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become bad, ruined, spoiled, etc., as ab. (materially or morally). --karun -- m.inf. to make bad, ruin, spoil, corrupt, as ab. (materially or morally) (YZ. 49, 179, 209).
(for خار و خس, cf. khār 2) m. sweepings, rubbish; anything vile; (on land which should be cultivated) overgrowth of brambles, thorns, weeds, or the like (Śiv. 1530).
f. (for 1, see khār 1; sg. dat. khārüñᵘ̈), the act of raising, etc.; cf. khārun. This word is used only with reference to feminine things.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. khāranôwᵘ), i.q. khārun, q.v. (Śiv. 1671).
f. wages paid for lifting or for carrying up (e.g. for landing goods on the bank of a river out of a boat, or for carrying loads up a mountain).
n.ag. (f. kharawüñᵘ̈), one who, or that which, is disliked, unpleasing, unpleasant.
n.ag. (f. khārawüñᵘ̈), one who raises or lifts (Śiv. 856), etc., in all the meanings of khārun, q.v.
f. the act of lifting up, raising up, carrying up, etc. Cf. khārun (Gr.Gr. 128).
m. a musk melon (mature in August) (El. kharbúz); a melon, Cucumis Melo (L. 348, 462). -kulᵘ m. a musk melon plant (El.).

m. (sg. dat. karcas), outgoings, disbursements, outlay, expenditure; expenses (Rām. 91); cf. kharj. --bĕhun -- m.inf. expenditure to be dispensed, i.e. to be proportionately spread over different objects. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to dispense expenditure, as ab. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. as in --gōm --, expenditure occurred by me, i.e. I spent (H. viii, 10). --karun -- m.inf. to make expenditure, to spend, disburse (sampadā kharᵃc kürᵘ̈n, he expended property, Gr.M. i, p. 67). --lagun -- m.inf. expenditure to be incurred. ¶ kharca-bardār (= خرچبردار) m. 'the bearer of expenses', a servant whose office is to supply the requirements of a household, a steward (Śiv. 1154). -sān adv. with expenditure, in a manner involving expenditure. -waröy adv. without expenditure, in such a manner as to avoid expenditure.
f. expenditure, esp. continued expenditure (e.g. on housekeeping, etc.), as distinguished from an isolated act of expenditure; jyāda kharciyi-kinⁱ wartāwun, to live extravagantly (Gr.M.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. khorcᵘ), to spend, expend.

adj. c.g. one suffering from scald-head, one with the head covered with sores due to this disease; met. (of a fruit, etc.) having the skin pitted with spots resembling the sores of scald-head. Cf. khorᵘ 2 and khürᵘ̈ 4.
m. a purchaser, a buyer (Śiv. 1665; Rām. 1259, 1529).
f. the condition of being universally disliked, the condition of one whose mere presence in a house is looked upon as a disgrace. Cf. khürᵘ̈ 3.
or khürᵘ̈ 5 f. a she-ass, a jenny-ass, see khar 1 (W. 17 khạrin).
m. (sg. dat. kharjas), expenditure, outgoing (YZ. 404); expense, cost, money spent (or to be expended) for any purpose (H. xii, 4, 5, 11, 20). Cf. kharc.
f. travelling expenses; (in Kāshmīrī) expense (El. who makes the word m.).
m. a curry-comb (K.Pr. 105). --karun -- m.inf. to use a curry-comb, to curry (a horse), to groom (a horse).
(cf. خرخشہ) m. a crowd, tumult, riot; (in Kāshmīrī, by conflation with khārakhas) a pile of rubbish.
m. a loud sardonic laugh, a fierce threatening laugh.
conj. 2 (1 p.p. khorᵘ), to be disliked, to be objectionable (Śiv. 164, 840); to be rough to the touch.

conj. 1 (caus. of khasun, Gr.Gr. 175; 1 p.p. khôrᵘ), to cause to rise, to raise, to elevate, lift up, carry up (K.Pr. 72, 87, 114; W. 149; Śiv. 61, 1023, 1254, 1392, 1840; Rām. 177, 625; K. 836-7); to lead up, to cause to ascend (YZ. 172; Śiv. 1036, 1222, 1687); to lift up on to (e.g. a horse, a seat, a cart, or a person's shoulders) (Rām. 1354; K. 254, 288, 298, 658, 931); to raise, pile up (cf. ḍēr); to put forward (a claim, or the like) (cf. danḍ); to draw water (from a well, or the like) (YZ. 112-3; Śiv. 1559, 1629); to bring up (an accusation), to charge with (cf. dūsh) (K. 31); to rear, set up (Śiv. 713, 1075-6; Rām. 1147); to enter (in a register or account book) (cf. bardāsht khārun); to enter credit, to give credit, to give goods on credit (Rām. 1312); to mount or place (upon the tongue), to utter reverently (the name of a god, etc.) (Śiv. 1908); to offer a (present), make an offering (cf. durⁱbata) (Śiv. 108); to raise (the breath), exhale, expire (opp. to wālun, to inhale) (Śiv. 1017, 1753, 1845, 1909; Rām. 17); to assume (a character, professor, or the like) (cf. dürzᵘ̈); to put up (a stake), lay (a wager) (cf. dav 3); to raise (a stake), conquer or win (a game) (cf. bözⁱ 1) (Rām. 1316); to set anything upon a machine preparatory to working upon it (e.g. thread on a loom, or wood on a lathe) (cf. dōr 3, so carkas khārun, to set on a lathe); similarly, razi khārun, to mount (a person or thing) upon a rope, to hang (Rām. 165, 1019, 1487, 1526, 1706). Cf. L.V. 102 tᵃyĕ khārĕnam zöyijĕ tᵃyĕ, the spinner raised fine threads (made) of me (from the spinning wheel). ¶ This verb is very commonly used with a substantive to form a nominal compound verb. Such so-called compounds are generally simple in meaning, each member retaining its own signification, as in ḍēr khārȧnⁱ, to raise heaps, i.e. to make untidy heaps. In others the compound acquires a special meaning, as in dŏh khārun, to spend the day in paid labour; kō̃da khārüñᵘ̈, to raise a kiln; met. to raise or make a really good kiln in which only perfect bricks are baked (Śiv. 1033; cf. kō̃da khasüñᵘ̈, p. 384b, l. 28). Such compounds will be found under the various substantives which form the first member. In vill. use this verb often takes the form khālun (e.g. H. vii, 19). El. gives a variant khāsun. ¶ khôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. khörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), lifted, raised, etc., as ab. ¶ khāranay 2 neg. conj. part. (for kāra-nay 1, see khār 1), without having lifted (as in kŏhas bôrᵘ khāranay thokᵘ, even without carrying the load up the mountain he is tired, i.e. he is weary even before he has tackled the heavy part of his work). ¶ khārañĕ-wālañĕ adv. (in gamblers' phraseology) by laying down stakes, and taking them up when won, i.e. (gambling) for stakes actually laid down (as in ready money gambling), and not for the value of stakes named (e.g. in written bets).
f. of khāryukᵘ (sg. dat. khāracĕ), a newly-born or very young filly (K.Pr. 73).
the Persian form of khār 3, q.v. (K.Pr. 82).
m. (f. khārüṭᵘ̈, q.v.), a newly-born or very young male foal.
? m. Cotoneaster obtusa and rotundifolia (El. kháriz, i.e. khārᵘ̈zᵘ̈. Judging from the form of the word it should be f., but El. shows it as m.).
in khȧrⁱ-khara adj. c.g. (K. 446), translated by the Sanskrit commentator bhītyā udyōgī, or 'strenuous by fear', rendered courageous by terror, having the courage of despair. Cf. khūrᵘ 5 and khara 2.

adj. c.g. particular, peculiar, special, distinct (Gr.M.); private, kept for private use, personal; choice, select, choicest, best, excellent, noble; cf. khāsa 2. --karith -- adv. specially, especially; mainly, principally (Gr.M.).
in khas-ʦēr f. a kind of apricot (El.). Cf. ʦēr (El. has -ʦēra).
in khasa-was f. (sg. dat. khasa-wasi, Śiv. 1027, or khasi-wasi, Śiv. 1682), rising and falling, ascending and descending (Śiv. 1027, 1682). Cf. khasun wasun (p. 420b, l. 22) and wasa-khas.
(cf. خص) in khas kŏkur m. a capon (L. 459, kas kokar).
m. a kind of fine cloth; muslin.

adj. c.g. special, private, personal; choice, select, choicest, best (YZ. 2, 274; Śiv. 620, 629, 818, 1797; Rām. 1726); excellent, noble. āma-khāsa, people in general and people in particular, low and high, high and low, rich and poor (Rām. 582, 1599). dukhtar-i- khāsa, one's own daughter (H. v, 11). --pöṭhⁱ -- or -pöṭhin adv. excellently, well. --mahanyuwᵘ -- m. a good man, i.e. one who is not only good looking, but who is also skilful in his business, and full of other virtues. --zanāna -- f. a good woman, i.e. one fair to look upon and endowed with many virtues.

n.ag. (f. khasawüñᵘ̈), one who rises, etc. (see khasun), an ascender (e.g. the moon, YZ. 145); one who is accustomed to ride, a rider (Śiv. 1188, 1324); esp. of a youth or maiden growing up to manhood or womanhood; an ascent, rising ground opp. to wasawunᵘ, a declivity (K.Pr. 72).

m. cutting, esp. beheading (of a man, a beast, a bird, or the like), the slaughter of an animal or bird in this way for food; cf. khish; met. misery, wretchedness (K.Pr. 2). haṭis khash, cutting the throat (K.Pr. 81). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give a cut (to), to cut (obj. in dat.) (not necessarily to behead) (H. v, 4, 6). --karun -- m.inf. to behead, to slay with the sword (Rām. 396, 1344).
adj. c.g. beheaded (of some bird or animal slaughtered by a butcher), see khash.
m. anger, wrath. --karun -- m.inf. to make wrath (to), to make (a person, dat.) angry (H. ii, 3).
m. a butcher (who kills animals or birds by beheading them).
adj. c.g. one who suffers from scab, scabby.
m. a poppy; poppy-seed; in Kāshmīrī, a poppy-head; poppy-oil (El.). -gŏlur m. a poppy-pod, a poppy-head. -gö̆ʦᵘ̈ f., id.

m. a kind of cutaneous disease, scab (principally affecting the arms and legs); cf. khŏsorᵘ. --nērun -- m.inf. scab to appear, an attack of scab to come on. ¶ khashĕrⁱ-kã̄gⁱrⁱ f. a kind of portable brazier or kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈ (q.v.) of which the basket work portion is made of coarse twigs marked as if pitted by scabs; met. a term of abuse used in curses or evil wishes made to another, (may you be) in the midst of scab! -phĕphur m. (sg. dat. phĕpharas), a scab-pustule. -paijāma m. the drawers or paijāmas of a person suffering from scab (filthy and defiled by scab); met. (in abusing and cursing) a condition as horrible as such a pair of drawers.
m. a kind of net used for skimming dirt, conferva, etc., from the surface of the water.

inkhȧshⁱ na makǖrⁱ adj. c.g. neither slaughtered (and hence eatable) nor dead of itself (and hence uneatable) (of an animal or bird which is excluded from discrimination as to whether it is eatable or uneatable). Cf. khash.
adj. c.g. wounded (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to wound (El.).

conj. 2 [1 p.p. khotᵘ 1, or according to some khothᵘ, f. khüʦᵘ̈ (khüʦhᵘ̈) (Gr.Gr. 210); 2 p.p. khaʦōv, or according to some khaʦhōv (Gr.Gr. 210). L.V. 27 has an irr. conj. part. khȧsⁱtⁱ for khasith. Opposite to wasun q.v. (Śiv. 1664, 1874; Rām. 280, 1106; K. 851). The caus. is khārun q.v., Gr.Gr. 175, also (El.) khāsun], to ascend, to go up (L.V. 75; K.Pr. 250; Śiv, 86, 1654, 1664, 1871; Rām. 80, 280, 916, 1106, 1747, 1759; K. 1059); to climb (e.g. a mountain, tree, staircase, or the like, dat. with pĕṭh) (K.Pr. 7; Śiv. 95, 785, 847, 931, 1081, 1167, 1176, 1244, 1246, 1854, 1890; Rām. 44, 471, 653 a tree; H. iii, 2, 9; x, 8; xii, 7; K. 182, 232, 629); to rise, come up (e.g. out of water) (H. i, 6, 8; xii, 11-2; K. 233); to go up stream (of river travelling) (H. xii, 6); to mount (a horse or a person's shoulders) (cf. aṭa-bāri khᵒ, p. 52b, l. 5, guri khᵒ, p. 229a, l. 22, and khôsᵘ khᵒ, p. 417b, l. 35 (K.Pr. 7, 168, 174; Śiv. 720, 732, 788, 793, 801, 894, 1089; H. ii, 6, 11; iii, 8; K. 253, 389-90); to ride (a horse or other riding animal) (H. x, 3; K. 757); to mount or ride (a carriage) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 84, 580, 668, 1913; Rām. 281, 1437, 1453, 1712; K. 378, 406, 490, 870, 985); to ascend (on to a throne, a bed, a funeral pyre, or the like) (Rām. 1713; H. iii, 7; v, 5, 6, 9; x, 7; xii, 21, 24); to climb up on to (the bank of a river), to ascend (from bathing) (boṭhᵘ khasun) (K. 271, 276, 413); to mount (on to), be put (upon), be imposed (upon) (e.g. a burden or responsibility) (cf. börⁱ khasȧnⁱ, p. 118a, l. 41) (Śiv. 1637; Rām. 559, 1237; H. iii, 3); to rise, grow up into a heap (cf. ḍēr khasȧnⁱ, p. 236b, l. 10) (Śiv. 1199, 1235, 1238); to rise (into the air), to soar, fly (cf. arshĕs khᵒ, p. 44b, l. 28) (Rām. 867, 922; K. 851); to rise (of the sun, etc.) (K.Pr. 120; Śiv. 692; Rām. 259, 431, 1121; K. 57); to rise (of clouds in the sky, darkness, etc.) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1290); to rise (of water in a river) (K. 70, 74); to be lifted raised (cf. boṭhᵘ khᵒ, p. 140a, l. 34); to rise, be swollen (of a blister, boil, etc.) (cf. basta khasüñᵘ̈, p. 135a, l. 46 and hᵃth) (K.Pr. 207, the cheeks); to rise (in price or value); to rise (of the spirits), to become joyful (Rām. 1094); to rise in the mind (of an idea, emotion, etc., esp. anger) (cf. bōsh, cölⁱ, dĕmāg) (Śiv. 106, 375, 759; Rām. 309, 473, 785, 865, 917, 1377; H. viii, 7; K. 137, 443, 445, 561, 618, 796, 908); to rise, to begin to be uttered (of an outcry, or the like; gaʦhi bishta khasun, the cry of 'shoo' should be uttered, K.Pr. 35) (Rām. 1761); to rise, to be made (of an accusation, calumny, etc. (cf. darma-hān khasüñᵘ̈, p. 244b, l. 14) (Rām. 1667); to rise, to come upon one's head, to be incurred (of guilt, sin, etc.) (Śiv. 593; Rām. 1181, 1219, 1238, 1592, 1596, 1619; H. ix, 5); to rise, come on the tapis, begin to be employed, etc. (K.Pr. 146); to rise, come into visibility (e.g. dirty spots on a clean garment) (cf. hĕla khasañĕ, p. 330b, l. 35); to be put on to a machine (cf. carkas khᵒ, p. 175b, l. 43, dōri khᵒ, p. 237a, l. 26, khaharüñᵘ̈ khᵒ, p. 394b, l. 25) (H. vii, 20); to stand upright, to stand up (Rām. 800, K. 25); to be raised, exalted, promoted; to turn out well (K.Pr. 12, 177); to be turned out (in the process of manufacture) (Śiv. 1872); to be presented, offered, sacrificed (K. 1141); to embark, go on board (a ship) (Gr.M.); to mount (in sexual intercourse); to be put on the scale (for weighment) (cf. daras-pĕṭh khᵒ, p. 234b, l. 40); to get to the head, take effect (of intoxicating drugs) (Śiv. 3; H. viii, 7, poison, met. for rage); to be spread out, put on, coated; to turn out to be so much (of a share) (cf. hissa); to pass, elapse, expire (of time, esp. when this occurs profitably) (cf. dŏh khᵒ, p. 199b, l. 34); to march against, assault; to be put on the fire; to be put down, inserted, registered; to be contained in, to fit; to grow, grow up (El., K.Pr. 165, Śiv. 1132, Rām. 1504); (of a ship) to mount (a rock, sandbank, etc.), to run (aground) (Gr.M.); (of a criminal) to mount (the empalement stake), to be empaled (Śiv. 1630). ¶ This verb is very frequently employed with a noun to form an idiom, in which the idea of rising is almost lost (cf. e.g. ã̄ṭh, bôgᵘ, bāth 2, baṭhi khᵒ (p. 140b, l. 2), byôlᵘ, danḍ, hakh 3, and many others). The idioms are given under their respective nouns. ¶ khasun wasun m. rising and falling, rise and fall, (of tide) ebb and flow (Gr.M.). Cf. khasa-was, s.v. khas 2. ¶ khasan-bāna m. 'a vessel of rising'; hence, met. the attainment of a high position by an ambitious person. ¶ khasith gaʦhun m.inf. to go up, ascend, to go above (L.V. 27). ¶ khotᵘ 1 p.p. (for 2, see s.v.; f. khüʦᵘ̈), risen (on to, dat.), as in kŏhas khotᵘ, ascended on to the mountain. Only used thus, predicatively and governing the noun of the thing ascended. -motᵘ perf. part. (f. khüʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), risen, etc., in all the meanings of khasun, frequently in the meaning of 'standing up, erect' (of a tree, or the like).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. khōsᵘ), i.q. khārun, q.v. (El.).
f. a kind of wooden scoop for baling out water from a boat, a baler.
f. the globular part of the skull, the top and back of the skull, the crown of the head (El. khásir).
m. a castrated animal. --karun -- m.inf. to castrate (a horse, ram, etc.); met. to weaken (a person), to deprive of vigour.
in khȧsⁱ pôwᵘ wȧsⁱ pôwᵘ  m. 'up a quarter and down a quarter', (in sharing out) a little more or less, an approximate share. Cf. khas 2, khasun, and wasun.

in khaṭa-bürᵘ̈  f. 'a hole of concealment', hence (1, intransitively) hiding, staying in a hidden place, and (2, transitively) hiding, putting in a hidden place. -maṭa adv. (a jingle-formation) in hiding, esp. in reference to the children's game of 'hide and seek'; cf. khaṭith-maṭith, p. 423a, l. 5. -sörᵘ̈ f. a secret collection, i.e. a store of grain secretly collected by degrees from other people's heaps.
(? spelling = خاتم بند) m. a beautiful kind of inlaid ceiling, a speciality of Kashmīr (L. 372, 379).

m. circumcising, circumcision (esp. amongst Musalmāns) (L. 271). -hāl f. the ceremony of circumcision. -höjᵘ̈-mahārāza m. the 'bridegroom' of the circumcision ceremony, the hero of the ceremony, the boy on whom circumcision is performed.
n.ag. (f. khaṭawüñᵘ̈), one who conceals, a concealer (Śiv. 981).
in khatēra karun m.inf. to punish for some fault (a child or servant) by beating accompanied by scolding, 'to give what for.'

m. (sg. dat. khatas), writing, handwriting, penmanship; a letter, note, epistle (Rām. 854; H. xii. 21, mölⁱ-sandi daskhata khath, a letter signed by the father; xii, 22-3); a document, deed (of sale, etc.) (YZ. 454); khat-i āzödī, a document of freedom, a deed of manumission (Rām. 676). --dyunᵘ-- m.inf. to give a letter; to give a letter of dismissal (to a wife), to divorce a wife, to give a writing of divorcement (K.Pr. 105, khatt). --ninawôlᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --ninawājĕn --), a letter-carrier, a courier (El.). -pạthᵃr m. correspondence, interchange of letters (Gr.M.).
m. (sg. dat. khã̄ṭas), the half of a fruit, a walnut, or the like. Cf. khỗṭᵘ.

adj. c.g. concealed, obscured (El.; Rām. 197, 558, 1158, 1355); private, secret (Gr.M.); as adv. secretly (see khaṭun) (Śiv. 773, 1393; Rām. 416, 502; H. xii, 6); similarly khȧṭⁱthạy pöṭhⁱ (Śiv. 25; khaṭith pöṭhin (Rām. 905), secretly. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain hidden; to remain apart and out of sight (Rām. 496, 728, 838, 955, 1007, 1009, 1329). --sapadun -- m.inf. to disappear (El.). --thāwun -- m.inf. to hide away, to conceal (El.; YZ. 158, 159).
m. N. of a certain flower blossoming in August-September.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. khoṭᵘ, 2 p.p. khacyōv), to conceal, hide (K.Pr. 247; YZ. 289; Śiv. 331, 333 pass., 336, 410, 1561; Rām. 19, 207, 258; K. 208, 283, 598); to banish, make away with, cause to disappear (Śiv. 19 pass.; Rām. 258, 1017); to cause to disappear, overwhelm, get the mastery over (e.g. cold getting the mastery over water, and turning it to ice) (L.V. 16). ¶ khȧṭⁱ khȧṭⁱ freq. part. used as adv., secretly, privately (Śiv. 1374; K. 82, 1143). ¶ khoṭᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. khüṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), hidden, concealed (Śiv. 991). ¶ khaṭith conj. part. used as adv., secretly, in a hidden manner (H. xii, 6); also as adj., concealed, obscured (El.); see also s.v. khaṭith. -maṭith adv. (a jingle formation), id. (cf. khaṭa-maṭa, p. 421a, l. 35). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain hidden, to be concealed; see s.v. khaṭith. --thawun -- or --thāwun -- m.inf. to put in a secret place, to hide away (Gr.M.; YZ. 158, 159); see s.v. khaṭith.
m. end, conclusion; (amongst Musalmāns) a recitation or perusal of the Qur'ān or the recitation of a Saint's texts (L. 78).
m. danger, peril (Gr.M.); fear, apprehension (El.). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to suffer from fear, to become terrified.
f. profits made by buying cheap and selling dear, esp. when this is done dishonestly, or by means of bribery.

f. (sg. dat. khüvᵘ̈), a small pit dug in the floor of a house, in which turnips and the like are stored in the winter, to prevent their drying up; cf. mŏnjĕ-khav, s.v. mö̆nḍᵘ̈ 1. --khanüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to dig such a pit. ¶ khüvᵘ̈-gŏgᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a turnip stored, as ab.

m. an eater (K.Pr. 14, 104, 153); voracious, a glutton; one who habitually eats (frequently --˚; cf. añĕma, atha, dŏhulᵘ, dand 1, gāḍ, harām, khar 1, māl 1, ṭyonḍᵘ, etc.; so ādȧmⁱ-khāv, a man-eating animal) (Rām. 1631) (El. kháo).
f. for khrāv, q.v. in khāwa-horᵘ m. a pair of wooden pattens.
f. one who is an eater, used --˚ as a feminine noun signifying 'an eater' in the sense of 'a destroyer' (of son, husband, or the like).
or khöwind خآوند m. a lord, a master (H. viii, 10, of a dog); a husband (K.Pr. 82; H. iii, 1-4; v, 1, 8, 10-2; x, 5, 12; xi, 11; xii, 18).
m. a plank on which masons or plasterers stand when at work; a scaffold (in house building).
m.pl. events infringing the usual course of nature, unusual things, miracles.
f. rust (of metal) (YZ. 525; Śiv. 282; Rām. 31, 655); met. tartar of the teeth (cf. danda-khᵒ, p. 224b, l. 36) (El. khai and kháí). --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to polish (metal) (El.).
f. low ground in the neighbourhood of a stream liable to be flooded by inundation.

m. imagination, fancy (El., Śiv. 1706); sentiment, idea, thought, surmise, conception (Gr.M.); thought, notice (of), taking notice (of) (Śiv. 819, 832, 920); an idea, an imagination (Gr.M.); a sentiment, opinion (mazahabī khayāl, a religious opinion, Gr.M.); khayāl-i khām, an inferior (i.e. evil) intention, treachery (Rām. 383). --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause thought to enter (a subject), to devote attention (to a subject) (Gr.M.).
m. a repository, magazine, store house, granary; a treasury; treasure (Śiv. 428, 1754; Rām. 1135, 1734); revenue, finances.

m. the ripening of the leaves (i.e. these turning yellow or red in autumn). Possibly a met. extension of khazāna 1, with allusion to the golden colour of the leaves. --lagun -- m.inf. the turn of the leaf to begin, the leaves to begin to change colour, Autumn to commence.
(H. xii, 3) or khizmath (K.Pr. 107; H. ii, 3), i.q. khạdᵃmath, q.v.
or khüzᵘ̈r m. a date (the fruit) (Rām. 807). -kulᵘ m. the date palm.

m. (sg. abl. khĕna 1), food (Gr.Gr. 120; L.V. 71; K.Pr. 106; L. 460; Śiv. 759, 1042; H. xii, 16-7); eating (W. 111); cf. khyonᵘ. -cĕn m. food and drink (K. 203, 209); eating and drinking at the same time; cf. khĕna-cĕn, bel. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give food, to give to eat, to feed. --raṭun -- m.inf. to stop food (e.g. a doctor stopping a patient's food, or disease taking away appetite). Cf. khyonᵘ raṭun, s.v. khyonᵘ. ¶ khĕna-bọ̆chᵘ adj. (f. -bö̆chᵘ̈), hungry for food; one who is always hungering, e.g. one who at meal-time is always ready to eat up everything before him, or who wants to eat every time he sees food. -bŏhadur m. a hero at eating, one who is able to eat large quantities, and who is ready to do so even at the cost of indigestion. -bulbul m. a nightingale at eating, one who habitually has a small appetite. -bāna m. a food-dish, a dinner-plate (W. 111); ability to eat much, or to digest much food. -bônᵘ m. a food-dish, a dinner-plate (usually cont.). -bāpath adv. for food, for eating (not for any other purpose). -bāpathạy or -bāpathᵘ̈y adv. intended only for eating (though capable of being used for something else). -brörᵘ̈ f. a cat at eating, a woman who like a cat wants to get hold of everything edible she sees, one who is always hankering after dainties. -biʦᵘ̈ f. a weakling at eating, a woman who eats slowly and in moderation. -bāv m. a thing which is useful only for food, and not for any other purpose. -cĕn m., i.q. khĕn-cĕn, ab. -cỗṭᵘ m. lit. 'a mouth for eating'; met. worthiness to receive food, deservingness to be given food (on account of modesty, or the like, when food is offered). -ḍulᵘ m. an earthenware eating vessel, an earthenware dinner-plate (such are chiefly used by Musalmāns). -dorᵘ adj. (f. -dürᵘ̈), hard in eating, tough, stringy. -gāra f. continual longing for food, insatiability. -gorᵘ m. an eater, one who is always eating and on the look out for food. -gŏʦurᵘ m. 'an eating-bag', id.; cf. gŏʦᵘ̈rᵘ̈. -khötᵃra adv., i.q. khĕna-bāpath, ab. -mŏdurᵘ m. sweet in eating, sweet in taste. -myūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -mīṭhᵘ̈), id. -thörᵘ̈ f. haste in eating, hurrying over one's food (in order to complete some work). -törᵘ̈ f. delay in eating, taking a long time over one's food. -ṭyoṭhᵘ adj. (f. ṭë˘ṭhᵘ̈), bitter in eating, bitter in taste. ¶ khĕnāh-cĕnāh m. 'a food, a drink', a good, tasty, meal. ¶ khĕnas khĕn-brēsh m. 'eating-excitement at eating', jealousy at another's good dinner, although one is eating equally good food oneself; met. jealousy felt by a prosperous man at another's prosperity. -kyutᵘ adj. (f. -kiʦᵘ̈), intended for food; fit for food, good to eat. -lāyĕkh adj. c.g. fit for food, good to eat. ¶ khĕnạy or khĕnᵘ̈y m. only food; only eating. Cf. khyonuy, s.v. khyonᵘ.
m. an impediment, stumbling block, hindrance put by another to any work.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. khyū̃cᵘ, pl. khī̃cⁱ; f. khī̃cᵘ̈, pl. khē̃cĕ), to pull, draw (Gr.M., K. 87, 542); to draw (a line) (Gr.M.).

or khë̆jᵘ̈ f. of khyolᵘ, q.v., a small flock, herd, or troop of animals. Cf. gupan- khĕjⁱ (p. 294b, l. 36) and gurⁱ-khⁱ (p. 298b, l. 36) (Gr.Gr. 152). ¶ khĕji-wadal f. pain, worry, etc., given to a herd or flock (by some outside influence); met. worry, oppression exercised against a crowd of people by one daring person, a brave attack by one upon a multitude. ¶ khĕjau-khĕjau adv. in flocks, in herds, in troops (as in 'going about in troops').
f. a troop, body, company, i.q. khyolᵘ. Cf. hȧsⁱ-khēl, p. 354b, l. 29, and khĕl 2. With suff. of indef. art. khēlāh (K. 224).

m. a kind of lotus-leaf, lotus-grass. ¶ khĕla-bạrᵃg m. i.q. khĕl. -wạthᵃr m., id. (Gr.Gr. 74, Śiv. 1842). ¶ khĕlas-andar adv. in a lotus-leaf (e.g. used as a wrapper). -kĕth adv., id. -manz adv., id. -manz-bāg adv., id.
f. in khĕl-khāna (= خیل خانہ) m. a family, an entire household, an assembled group of all one's household and relations (e.g. on a pilgrimage to some holy place). Cf. khēl.

f. (sg. dat. khĕli, K. 277), sport, play, fun, frolic, esp. the frolics of children with their elders (Śiv. 1383; K. 364, 511, 858, 863, 941, 960). -bôjᵘ (K. 197), khēli-bôjᵘ (K. 304), or khēlan-bôjᵘ (K. 504), m. a play-fellow. --karañe -- f. pl. inf. to frolic, as ab. (K. 145, 200, 218, 250, 293, 297, 388, 742, 863-4).
adj. c.g. (of a lake, or the like) possessing many khĕl lotus-leaves. See khĕl 1.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. khēlanôwᵘ), to cause to play, to cause to sport (Śiv. 1876; K. 324, 946).
n.ag. (f. khēlawüñᵘ̈), one who plays (trans.), one who habitually plays (cf. khēlun) (Śiv. 949, 1325, 1432 ff.); one who plays, one who sports (intrans.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. khyūlᵘ), to play (trans.) as in rās khēlun, to play the rās-sport (Śiv. 737, 1054, 1353, 1376, 1390, 1429, 1493; K. 293); to dandle, fondle, play with (a child) (K. 184); conj. 3 (2 p.p. khēlyōv), to play, sport (intrans.) (Rām. 1554; K. 157, 183, 211, 226, etc.); to play (with), to contest (with) (Rām. 1435); to sport (sexually) (K. 810).
in khĕma-khĕm m. (of two persons) mutual repeated fixed staring at each other.
adj. c.g. fit to be eaten, edible, meant to be eaten (Gr.Gr. 129).

m. (sg. dat. khĕnāshĕnas), refusal to eat food, abstaining from food (by a person who is seeking death); abstaining from food owing to anger, or the like. --karun -- m.inf. to abstain from food, as ab.
adj. c.g. to be eaten, intended to be eat, intended to be used for food (and not for other purposes).
f. (sg. dat. khĕpüʦᵘ̈ 2), a sense of shame, a feeling of disgrace.

f. (sg. dat. khĕpi), a pile (esp. of straw, etc., or of sheets of paper); a portion of money or other property (suddenly acquired by plundering, cheating, or the like), a share of property dishonestly acquired. --athi yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a share to be acquired, as ab.

adj. (f. khĕpüʦᵘ̈ 1, for 2, see khĕpath), one who is of dwarfish and ill-proportion form, and who also wears mean clothes, an unsightly scarecrow of a fellow. -hyuhᵘ adj. (f. khĕpüʦᵘ̈-hishᵘ̈), one who is like such a scarecrow, 'a bit of a scarecrow himself.' ¶ khĕpȧtⁱ khyōmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --khyēmüʦᵘ̈ --), i.q. khĕpotᵘ.
m. the rope bridge used over rivers in Kashmīr.
adj. (as subst., f. khĕrkhishᵉ̆ladiñ), one who suffers death or total destruction as described under khĕrkhyushᵘ, q.v.

or khirkhyushᵘ m. killing a person by cutting off his limbs by slow degrees, with blunt weapons, or the like; killing a person after killing the members of his family one by one before his eyes, painful destruction root and branch. The expression is chiefly used in cursing and abuse.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. khēryōv), to bloom, blossom (El.).
m. a kind of silk cloth, usually worn by woman as a girdle or sash. ¶ khēshĕ-mŏy f. a long narrow strip of this material worn as ab. -püṭᵘ̈ f., id.

or khë̆shᵘ̈ f. as much straight grass, straw, standing corn, or the like as can be grasped by the hand (but not in the form of a crushed-up lump). With the suff. of indef. art. khë˘shāh f. a single handful, as ab. Cf. gāsa-khᵒ, p. 307b, l. 30.
m. storing up food little by little (i.e. not buying a great store at once owing to poverty, thoughtlessness, or the like).
f. (sg. dat. khë̆ʦᵘ̈), loss, harm, injury (L.V. 10, 77).
(also written kshĕtriy by Paṇḍits), m. a member of the kṣatriya or regal and military caste of Hindūs (Rām. 1261, K. 982).
m. eating, used --˚; cf. aḍ-khᵒ, p. 10a, l. 29, and bata-khᵒ, p. 136b, l. 47.
f. a mooring cable, a hawser (usually made of withies); a tow-rope (Gr.M. where it is shown as m.). --ganḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to moor with such a cable.

m. an advance of grain; when grain has been threshed, and has been collected previous to the Government assessment for purposes of taxation, it is supposed not to be touched till Government permission is given. This word signifies a portion of grain taken out of the heap by permission of the official in charge, for the cultivator's immediate needs. It also means portions similarly taken by the cultivator without such permission; cf. dā̃-khᵒ, p. 230a, l. 19. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. (of the official) to give such an advance.
f. (sg. dat. khēwaṭi), an assigned share of revenue, an assessment of revenue by apportionment as in asömīwār khēwaṭh, an assessment on holdings (L. 403).

f. the wages of eating (Gr.Gr. 129); a present given on the occasion of certain food being eaten, as in bata-khĕᵒ (p. 136b, l. 48), the present given by a bride's relations to her husband's people on the occasion of her first meal in her husband's house.
n.ag. (f. khĕwawüñᵘ̈), one who eats, an eater.
n.ag. contr. of khĕwawunᵘ, q.v. (El. khyewun).
or khiʦurᵘ m. (f. khĕʦürᵘ̈ 1 or khiʦᵘ̈rᵘ̈), low, vulgar, unrefined (by nature, or in dress and general appearance).

f. a dish composed of rice, pease, and various millets, etc., the khicṛī of India (K.Pr. 64, 245). It is offered in the worship of the Hindū god Kuvēra (see bel.). The word is used met. for mixtures generally. When ˚-- this word often takes the form khĕʦi, see bel. --khë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to eat this dish; to eat mixed food. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to prepare this mixed food; met. to make a mixture, to concoct (lit. and fig.). ¶ khĕʦi-māwas f. the khicṛī new moon, the day of new moon of the month of Pŏh (Skr. pauṣa = December-January) on which day Hindūs offer this mixed food to Kuvēra and his fairy (yakṣa) followers (L. 266, khich máwas). -māwasi-dŏh adv. on the day of the khicṛī new moon, as ab. -māwasi-kyutᵘ 1 adj. and adv. (f. -māwasi-kiʦᵘ̈), for the day of this new moon (of something prepared, done, given, or the like). -māwasi-kyutᵘ 2 adv. on the day of this new moon (esp. used in fixing a date for coming or going). ¶ khĕʦari-bāpath adv. (of rice, pease, etc.), for (making) this mixed dish. -barith adj. c.g. filled with this mixed food. -kyutᵘ adj. and adv. (f. -kiʦᵘ̈), i.q. -bāpath, ab. -māwas f., i.q. khĕʦi-māwas, ab.

m. affliction, trouble, pain, distress (e.g. from disease, poverty, homesickness, or the like) (L.V. 18; Rām. 101; K. 87, 541-2, 754). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give pain, to afflict, to cause distress (to). ¶ khīdas gōmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), gone to affliction, afflicted, troubled, harassed, distressed.
m. (sg. dat. khikharas), a kind of wicker or straw basket, in which small charcoal is brought into the towns for sale.
m. a pair (horᵘ) of leather sandals, the upper portion consisting of leather straps, and the sole of solid leather, the caplī or cappal of India.
m. a pin; a skewer; a tooth-pick (cf. danda-khᵒ, p. 224b, l. 17).
m. disorder, ruin, damage (Gr.M.); disorder, interruption, i.q. khalal.

f. (sg. dat. khilāphüʦᵘ̈), the office or dignity of a Caliph; imperial dignity, monarchy; (in Kāshmīrī) the condition of being one who is the monarch of a lover's heart, the condition of being an object of adoration (K.Pr. 132).
in khili-mili adv. intimately mixed up (of a number of different things). Cf. khali, s.v. khala 2.
m. becoming lean or thin, leanness, thinness (from disease, sorrow, etc.); (of the moon) waning; (of the water of a river) drying up, diminishing.
f.pl. sportive leaping about (like a sportive child, a calf, etc.). --karañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to leap about, as ab. -waʦhorᵘ m. (f. -waʦhürᵘ̈), a sportive calf, as ab.

f. the insolent pride of an unworthy man who has been exalted, the pride of a beggar on horseback, arrogance. ¶ khingari khasun m.inf. to mount on such arrogance, i.e. to become full of such arrogance. --khotᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --khüʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), filled with such arrogance.

or (Śiv. 374) khyīr or khīr m. (sg. abl. khira 1), rice-milk, a dish made of rice and milk (rice, parboiled in water, is again boiled in milk, with the addition of sugar, and sometimes spices, etc.); cf. kshīr, of which this is another form. --bögᵃrun -- m.inf. to divide out rice-milk; (among Hindūs) after an offering of rice-milk to a god, to divide the remainder amongst relations, servants, etc.; esp. such a division of an offering of rice-milk made to the goddess Śītalā, after a child has recovered from smallpox. --bāwun -- m.inf. (among Hindūs) to offer rice-milk in worshipping a god. --karun -- m.inf. to prepare rice-milk; esp. (among Hindūs) to prepare rice-milk for an offering to Śītalā, as ab. ¶ khira-bahugun m. a small brazen vessel (v. bahugun) full of rice-milk; the amount of rice-milk contained in such a vessel. -dīkⁱca m. a saucepan in which rice-milk is prepared, or which is filled with it. -khôsᵘ m. a metal cup full of rice-milk. -pröpyunᵘ m. (among Hindūs) after rice-milk has been offered to a god, the amount that remains over and above, and that is consumed by the worshipper, his friends, servants, etc. -sāl m. (among Hindūs) an invitation to a meal of rice-milk. -thāl m. a metal dish containing rice-milk. -ṭôkᵘ m. an earthenware platter of rice-milk. -ṭūrᵘ m. a metal cup or bowl of rice-milk. -ṭö̃ṭhᵘ̈ f. a trickle of rice-milk; hence, a mere drop or two of it, a very little rice-milk.

adj. c.g. froward, insolent, uncontrolled, uncontrollable, ungovernable, arrogant (of one who has grown up without proper control, and with evil associates); astonished (El. khírah). --gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈--), become insolent, etc., as ab. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become insolent, etc., as ab.
f. (sg. dat. khirüñᵘ̈), a particular tone or time in music, (?) the moderate time (as opposed to fast or slow). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to sing in this tone.
f. a small door; a window, casement. ¶ khiriki-dastār m. a kind of turban wound round the head so as to show an opening in front, the khiṛkīdar pagaṛī of India.

m. picking out, i.e. pilfering, dishonestly misappropriating a portion of money which has been entrusted to one for safe custody or for some special purpose. --karun -- m.inf. to pilfer or misappropriate, as ab.

f. beheading an animal or bird, butchering in this way (K.Pr. 237); cf. khash and khal-khish, p. 397a, l. 33. -khish m. (by butchers, or the like) frequent or continued beheading, as ab. -khish karun m.inf. to do this repeated butchering.
f. relationship, consanguinity, affinity; in Kāshmīrī, relationship by marriage.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. khyuskᵘ; 2 p.p. khiscyōv. This verb is impersonal in tenses derived from past participles) to walk arrogantly, to strut.
m. (sg. dat. khislatas), temper, humour, disposition, habit (El.).

in khith-khith adv. (of a happy infant) laughing, crowing. khith-khith gö̆ʦᵘ̈ f. habitually laughing or crowing (of a happy-tempered girl-child); met. (of a girl or woman) of a happy, laughing, disposition.
m. a lord of fields, a landowner; hence, met. a family priest, spiritual preceptor, or the like, who has many clients or pupils. See khītⁱ-brītⁱ, p. 421a, l. 49.
m. a certain kind of tutelary deity who is guardian of cultivated fields, a kind of börav, q.v.

f. (sg. dat. khētĕ, Gr.Gr. 61), a field, esp. a cultivated field, land under cultivation (as a means of livelihood) (K.Pr. 107); cultivation, farming (as a profession); frequently --˚, as in dã̄- khītⁱ, a paddy-field (p. 230a, l. 19). -brītⁱ f. the position of a client or pupil, etc., in respect to a family priest or spiritual preceptor or the like (the client, etc., being the 'field' which the other cultivates as a means of livelihood); cf. khītīshŏr. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to do cultivation, to cultivate land as a livelihood. --lāgüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to carry on cultivation, to live by cultivating. ¶ khēti barith adj. c.g. (of a man) 'full of cultivation', hence, one who cultivates many fields and varied crops. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a cultivator, a farmer.
? m. treachery, treason; breach of trust, misappropriation, embezzlement (K.Pr. 11).
m. (El.), temper, disposition (cf. khōy f.) (El. khó, i.e. khôwᵘ; YZ. 5).
(? spelling) m. Oreoseris lanuginosa (El. khó, i.e. khôwᵘ).
or khūbsūrath خوب صورت adj. c.g. beautiful, handsome (Gr.M.; H. xii, 4, 5, 10, 15, 19).
m. a kind of padded or quilted cap worn in the cold weather. Cf. pp. 138b, l. 14; 299b, l. 8; 316b, l. 2.
m. (of a precious metal, or the like), the condition of being unrefined, foulness (Śiv. 766); (of a coin, etc.), baseness, adulteration, alloy (K.Pr. khuchar, 153). Cf. khọ̆ṭᵘ.
f. a kind of bag or purse used for carrying money or valuables on a journey, usually made of woollen material.
m. a kind of heavy, clumsy, boat, without any roof, used for the transport of stone, bricks, and rough goods that are not injured by rain (L. 381, kuchu, El. khúch).

m. (sg. abl. khŏḍa 1), a pit, a hole dug in the ground (H. x, 13); a ditch (Gr.M.); esp. a hole dug in the ground in which money or other treasure is buried for safety, a pit-hoard; a cavity (El.), a rent (El.). --khanun -- m. to dig a pit (Śiv. 590, 746, 1215); met. to dig a pit (for a person), to lay a trap for his destruction (e.g. by calumniating him to his superiors). Cf. khŏna-waṭh, s.v. khŏn. ¶ khŏḍa-onᵘ adj. (f. -üñᵘ̈), a blind man whose eyeballs are sunken in as if at the bottom of a pit (an appearance presented by persons blind from smallpox, or sometimes by persons born blind). -bal m. N. of a site in Śrīnagar, where, according to legend, King Pravar- sēna II first reached firm land in seeking for a place on which to build the city of Pravarapura, the modern Śrīnagar. The ancient name of the site was Kṣurikābala. See RT.Tr. iii, 347 and note on 339-49. -buzy m. dependent on a pit; hence, wasted away to nothing like a thing long buried in a pit. The expression is used in curses or in angry abuse, as in 'may you become wasted away, as ab.' (Gr.Gr. 161). -gupun adj. (m. sg. dat. -gupanas; f. sg. nom. -gupüñᵘ̈), a man who conceals his own opinions, one who keeps his opinions to himself (like a foolish animal in a pit). -han or -hanā m. (we should expect the word to be f.), a small pit. -kharᵃc m. expenditure on a multitude of works (necessitating frequent withdrawals from a pit-hoard); met. any continual secret expenditure. -kônᵘ adj. (f. -köñᵘ̈), a one-eyed man, whose blind eye is sunken; cf. -onᵘ, ab. -kyomᵘ m. a kind of worm or maggot that always lives in a hole in the ground. -mọ̆nḍᵘ m. the root left in the ground when a tree is cut down. -pachin m. any bird that, out of fear of danger, lives in a pit, one that is full of cunning devices for concealment; met. a rich man who is a miser (i.e. who unnecessarily puts on an appearance of poverty, like a bird who can fly away perfectly well, and yet prefers to hide in holes). -phë̆ṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -phĕcĕ), 'false scandal from a pit,' i.e. cheating by privately retailing false scandal. -ʦūr m. a pit-thief, one who steals money, etc., deposited or hidden in a hole in the ground. -ʦūrᵘ̈ f. theft such as the ab. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), (of ground, etc.), covered with holes, full of holes. -wôñᵘ 1 m. water that has collected in a pit, etc. -wôñᵘ 2 m. a low shopkeeper who does not sell in the market, but who sells in a hidden place (as though in a pit), a hole and corner merchant. -wörᵘ̈ f. a little very-low-lying garden in the midst of other vegetable gardens (principally seen in the villages).
pron. self. -pasandī خود پسندی f. self-complacency, self-conceit (Rām. 817). See bē-khŏd (e.g. YZ. 32, Rām. 483).

or khŏdāy خدائی m. (sg. dat. khŏdāyĕs, K.Pr. 89; H. vii, 4; x, 5; so, H. xii, 7, gen.; xii, 15, ag.), God (Musalmān and Christian) (K.Pr. 121, 168; YZ. 101; H. vi, 5, 6, 7, 10; x, 7, 8), voc. khŏdāyā (YZ. 15; khŏdāyĕ, W. 101; H. iv, 1; v, 7); khŏdāyō (K.Pr. 74, W. 101, YZ. 98), O God! bar khŏdāyō, O great God (H. v, 7). bā khŏdā, one who believes in God, a true believer (H. xii, 20). hak-i-khŏdāy, a husband (sacred to the wife as God) (H. xii, 15). hawālath khŏdā, adieu (L. 458). wāda-y-khŏdā, an oath by God (H. xii, 7, 15). -söb m. God the Master, the Lord God (H. iii, 8; x, 5). khŏdāyĕ-sondᵘ chuy kasam, interj. I adjure thee by God (H. xii, 7).
m. an abusive name for Shī'a Musalmāns.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. khŏḍadārĕñ), pitted, holed, possessing a hole (e.g. a stone, with a small pit in it, or a rock with a cave).
adj. c.g. full of pits or hollows (of anything inanimate).
conj. but, but on the other hand.
f. ownership, lordship, sovereignty; divinity, providence; the property or quality of a beneficent lord or master, favour; (in Kāshmīrī), adj. c.g. extremely rare, difficult to obtain.
(El. p. 155) or khoḍaʦur (El. p. 5) ? spelling, m. the back of the head (El.).
m. a servant; esp. a servant in charge of a mosque or shrine (L. 289).
adj. c.g. self-coloured; as subst. m. N. of a kind of blanket having the natural colour of the wool (L. 370).
m. the vulva, the female organ of generation (Gr.Gr. 9). Cf. khaḍ and khaḍa. ¶ khȧḍⁱ-dinal f. an unchaste woman. -dāwal f., id. -düzᵘ̈ f., id.

f. (sg. dat. khŏjĕ 2; for 1, see s.v.), a small pit, a small hollow place or hole; esp. one of a series of holes in the ground used in a boys' game. The boys are blindfolded and try to drop little balls into the holes. ¶ khŏjĕ or khŏjĕ-andar adv. in the hole, the expression used in the ab. game when a pellet falls into a hole. -han 2 or -hanā 2 f. (for 1, see s.v. khŏjĕ 1), a single one of these holes in the ab. game. -manz adv., i.q. khŏjĕ, ab.

m. accustomed, habituated, inured; (in Kāshmīrī) one who is familiar, saucy, pert, 'cheeky'; one who, without respect to his elders and betters, shows off his cleverness before them. --gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. -gömüʦᵘ̈), become pert, etc. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become pert, etc.
m. a man who collects water-chestnuts (see gôrᵘ) in the Kāshmīr lakes. Cf. ḍal 1, p. 209b, l. 47, where the meaning is extended to indicate the gardeners of the floating islands on the Dal lake.
in khŏh-pāy m. a difficult path on a mountain or in a forest obstructed by thorns, venomous insects, etc. Cf. kŏh, kōh.

in khȧh ⁱ-wath f. (sg. dat. -wati), a new path across the paddy fields made by the coming and going of cultivators, after the flood-water has dried off in the autumn (the former tracks having, of course, been obliterated by the rainy season floods and irrigation). Cf. khāh 1.

m. a man of distinction; a title of honour (El., K.Pr. 5). The word is a variant of khŏjĕ 1. --kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈ --, f. the finely worked, highly coloured, portable brazier used by the wealthier classes, as distinct from the grīstⁱ kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈, or ordinary peasant's brazier (K.Pr. 129).

m. (for 2, see khö̆ḍᵘ̈), a Khoja, a Musalmān merchant (K.Pr. 107); cf. khōja. -bāy f. his wife. -han 1 or -hanā 1 m. (for 2, see khö̆ḍᵘ̈), a single Khoja. -ṭhūl m. a low, disreputable looking Musalmān merchant.
m. muddiness (of water, or the like). Cf. khūlᵘ.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. khŏkhalôwᵘ), to cleanse (a dirty garment) by dipping it into water, and shaking it about therein.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. khŏkhalyōv) (of clothes, or the like) to be rinsed in water (by being dipped in water and shaken about therein, so as to cleanse them).
m. hollowness, emptiness (of a nut, or the like, apparently good, but possessing no kernel). ¶ khŏkharĕra-sān adv. accompanied by such hollowness; hence, empty, hollow, as ab.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. khŏkharyōv), to become hollow (of something originally solid, such as a tree).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. khōkhȧsⁱdārĕñ) (of a child) one who is always mischievously restless. See khōkhosᵘ.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. khōkhȧsⁱladiñ), i.q. khōkhȧsⁱdār, q.v.

or khŏkhurᵘ adj. (f. khŏkhürᵘ̈), hollow, apparently solid, but hollow within [e.g. a bamboo, or (K.Pr. 229), a blind walnut]; met. (of speech, or the like) fine words signifying nothing; (of anything) solid-looking, but worthless; danda khŏkhorᵘ, a toothless man (K.Pr. 48). Cf. khūkhorᵘ.

m. the perpetual mischievous restlessness of a naughty child. --āsun -- m.inf. such restlessness to exist. --dᵃnun -- m.inf. shaking of the ground or of things to occur through this restlessness, as we say 'the whole house is being shaken down' by a naughty child's goings on. --karun -- m.inf. to create such restlessness in a naughty child. ¶ khōkhȧsⁱ-dĕv a restlessness-devil; a little devil of a child, who is not only restless himself, but makes other children restless too.

(K. 146) or khŏkhᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. the crawling of children. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of a child) to crawl. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. crawling to come, (of a child) beginning to crawl to happen, crawling to be commenced. ¶ khŏkhja-khŏkhja adv. at a crawl, orawlingly, as ab.
m. the snout of a lower animal (including the end of the nose and the mouth).
m. (sg. dat. khŏkhatas), a small dark closet in the interior of a house.
m. a bugaboo, bogeyman, bugbear, hobgoblin, ogre (a term used in frightening children). ¶ khakha-bôṭᵘ or khŏkha-bôṭᵘ m., id. (K.Pr. 61 has khukarbāṭi). -motᵘ m., id.
m. a man of the Khas (Skr. Khaśa) tribe. This word is generally used in the plural, a man of the tribe, in the singular, is khāh 2, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 8).
adj. c.g. of the dust, dusty; composed of, or coloured like, ashes or dust (K.Pr. 18).
f. pl. intestinal worms, ascarides (El. khólah, m.sg.).
f. pl. burning of pepper, etc., or other pungent article. --pĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. burning to fall, the mouth to be burnt by a pungent taste. --wasañĕ -- f. pl. inf., id.
m. purslane-seed, used as a medicine.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. khūlᵘ 2, for 1, see s.v.; 2 p.p. khōjyōv), to open (e.g. a box); to open, untie (a knot, etc); to open (a tied-up parcel, etc.); to open, loosen (clothes) (Śiv. 1219); to release, set free (a prisoner in bonds). khūlᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. khūjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), opened, etc., as ab.
m. the stirring up of clear water, so as to make it muddy (K. 233). Cf. khalan.

adj. (f. khüjᵘ̈ 2, for 1, see khȧjⁱ), open, spread out, spread wide; broad, wide (Gr.M.); clear (El.); (of a hollow, or receptacle) able to receive something in addition to its actual contents; (of a garment) loose, flowing; cf. khula, khalun, and khạlᵃran. ¶ khali 2 adv. (for 1, see khala 2) with something spread out (e.g. wearing flowing garments).

m. (pl. nom. khölⁱ 2, for 1, see s.v.), the kernel of a fruit stone or of a nut, etc. (El. khol, a seed). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to extract a kernel. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat a kernel. ¶ khölⁱ-māl f. a necklace made up of golden beads shaped like kernels.

or khölī خآلی adj. c.g. (for 2, see khôlᵘ), empty, vacant, void (K.Pr. 55); hollow, having nothing in it (El. khálí; Rām. 1456); as adv. only, merely (Gr.M., Rām. 766); as postpos. governing the abl., deprived of, free from, devoid of, as in gaṭa-pacha-nishĕ khöliy, (the moon) deprived of its dark fortnight (Śiv. 166). jāy khölī karüñᵘ̈, to make a place empty; to devastate a place (cf. Rām. 915); met. to leave a place empty, to disappear, to die (Rām. 809). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go void; (of a bullet, or the like) to miss the mark (Gr.M.); (of the brain) to become empty, to lose one's senses, become idiotic (K.Pr. 166). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come empty; to return unsuccessful (from an expedition, or the like) (Rām. 489).
f. ignorance, want of experience in any work.

f. (sg. dat. khŏni, Gr.Gr. 70), the part of the arm near the elbow, and towards the wrist, the upper part of the fore-arm; the middle part of the sleeve of a garment, the part of the sleeve near the elbow; the hollow immediately over the hip, on which women carry small children (H. xi, 13); a pile, a heap (cf. dār-khᵒ, p. 235a, l. 28). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'the elbow to go', a hole to come in the elbow part of a sleeve. ¶ khŏna karañĕ f. pl. inf. to make piles, steadily to continue earning and making one's pile. -wath m. (sg. dat. -waṭas), the elbow-joint, the elbow. -waṭa khŏḍ khanun m.inf. to dig a pit with the elbow; met. to commence a difficult and almost impossible task (Śiv. 590, 746, 1214). ¶ khŏnⁱ-kha the name of the letter kha where written in the Śāradā character (used in schools). -kil f. a nudge with the elbow; esp. in order to draw attention. ¶ khŏni gōmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), (of a garment) gone in the elbow, having the elbow of the sleeve torn, cut, or worn into a hole. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to hold on the hip or haunch (a child or bundle, for carrying it). -kĕth adv. on the haunch (as ab.) (H. xi, 13). --thaph karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to seize by the elbow; met. to follow another's instructions, to do exactly as he tells one.
f. a vain woman, one who knows or thinks herself to be beautiful and fortunate in having a rich and loving husband.

N. of a Kashmīr village, the ancient Khōnamuṣa, about ten miles south-east of Śrīnagar. It is famous as the birthplace of the poet Bilhaṇa, and contains a sacred spring called Dāmōdar Nāg (RT.Tr. II, 458; Śiv. 930).
m. a small ditch or moat.
adj. (f. khünḍᵘ̈ 1, sg. dat. khanjĕ 1), broken, divided into parts; hence, deprived of a part or limb or member, maimed, mutilated; unevenly formed, irregularly angled.
f.pl. collecting anything which can be gathered in armfuls (such as crops, or the like) (cf. khŏn). --karañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to collect in this way.
khôṭᵘ, khönṭᵘ̈, etc., see khō̃ṭa, khỗṭᵘ, khö̃ṭᵘ̈, etc.
f. a kind of light plough, pulled by a man, used in a twice-ploughed field (Śiv. 1530).
(for 2, see khanun) adj. (f. khüñᵘ̈ 2, for 1 see s.v.), well-clothed, wearing many clothes, well-dressed (K.Pr. 154).
m. (sg. dat. khōphas), terror, dread, fear (El., who spells the word khóf) (K.Pr. 105, ḵẖauf; Śiv. 1833).
or khŏpᵘ̈rᵘ̈  f. an old ruined thatched mud hut; an old worn-out kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or portable brazier (cf. khôrᵘ 1). Cf. kā̃gri-khᵒ, p. 387a, l. 8, and lari-khᵒ, s.v. lürᵘ̈.

m. a foot; esp. the human foot (YZ. 79; Śiv. 1640; K. 88, 427, 605). Cf. khōr 2. ¶ khŏra-bāna m. a shoe, boot, etc.; cf. khōra-bāna, s.v. khōr 2 (W. 111, khwarạ-bāna). -ganḍ m. tying the feet; met. making a child stay in one place (in order to keep it in good behaviour); cf. khōra-ganḍ, s.v. khōr 2. -kônᵘ (f. -köñᵘ̈), 'foot one-eyed,' i.e. one who does not know his own shoes and who habitually, when leaving a house, takes someone else's shoes. In this connexion the Kāshmīrī shoe may be compared with our umbrella. The shoes are, of course, left outside the door on entering a house; cf. khōra-kônᵘ, s.v. khōr 2. -nyŏṭh m. (sg. dat. -nyŏṭhas), the thumb of the foot, the great toe; cf. khōra-nyŏṭh, s.v. khōr 2. -phȧlⁱ m.pl. foot-pearls, the pretty tender feet of a baby, or the like; cf. khōra-pholᵘ, s.v. khōr 2. -roṭᵘ m. seizing the feet; met. impeding (a person); cf. khōra-roṭᵘ, s.v. khōr 2 (cf. K. 83). -shã̄d or -shānd m. (turning a person round in bed) so that his feet are where his head was and vice versa (done as an alleviation in sickness); as adv.  from foot to shoulder; cf. khōra-shã̄d, s.v. khōr 2. khŏra karun shānd, to walk from the foot of the bed to the pillow (H. v, 5). -trūnᵘ m. a stocking. -ṭyonḍᵘ m. the tip of the foot, the tip of the toes. Cf. khōra-ṭyonḍᵘ, s.v. khōr 2. ¶ khŏras-pĕṭh khŏrʦhunun m.inf. to put a foot on the foot; met. out of hatred to bring a false charge (against a person).

or khōr 1 or khorᵘ 4 (q.v.) خور adj. and subst. m. eating; an eater; used --˚ as in gŏta-khŏr, one who eats dives, a diver; caki-khōr, an eater of desire, i.e. an old servant ready to attend to one's every want (p. 168b, l. 48).
