m. the foot of any living being, i.q. khŏr 1, q.v. According to El. this word properly means 'instep', but is generally used for 'foot'. In Gr.M. it is once extended to mean 'leg' (K.Pr. 110, 154, 248, 260; YZ. 535; Śiv. 200, 1829; Rām. 355, 477, 634, 710, 1092, 1201, 1250, 1254, 1432, 1633; H. v, 9; K. 32, 119, 187, etc.). --darun -- m.inf. the foot to be firm; the foot to be steady (in slippery places, or the like). --dārun -- m.inf. to plant the foot firmly; to stand perfectly steady. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to put the foot; esp. to put down the foot to save oneself, when one stumbles or slips. --phuṭun -- m.inf. breaking or dislocation of the foot to occur (K.Pr. 222). --phuṭᵃrun -- m.inf. to cause breaking or dislocation of the foot (Rām. 552). -pĕṭh mārun m.inf. (for khōras-pᵒ mᵒ) to slay (an animal) over the feet, i.e. near the closed feet of the person for whose benefit it is sacrificed (K.Pr. 158). --sārun -- m.inf. to feel for with the feet (e.g. searching about with one's feet for one's clothes in the dark, or a blind man feeling his steps). --thawun -- m.inf. to put down the feet (on the ground); esp. the setting down of the feet as part of a Hindū wedding ceremony. --ʦhĕnun -- m.inf. the foot to become cut or wounded (e.g. from violent contact with a stone). --ʦaṭun -- m.inf. to cut off or amputate the foot (e.g. as a punishment, in a surgical operation, or as the result of an accident). --wahārun -- m.inf. to spread out the feet, to lie at full length (K.Pr. 236; cf. K. 605, khŏr waᵒ); met. to take rest after hard work. -zᵃh m.pl. the two feet, the feet (of a person). ¶ khōra-bāna m. a shoe, a boot; cf. khŏra-bāna, s.v. khŏr 1. -ganḍ m. tying the feet (e.g. as a punishment); met. being unable to get about owing to pressing engagements (e.g. a marriage) at home; cf. khŏra-ganḍ, s.v. khŏr 1. -holᵘ adj. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), crooked-legged, bandy-legged, knock-kneed (either from birth or through disease, etc.). -han f. a small foot (e.g. a child's foot or a man's foot small in proportion to his other limbs). -horᵘ m. a pair of feet, the feet (of a two-footed being). -kônᵘ m. i.q. khŏra-kônᵘ, q.v. s.v. khŏr 1; (also) one who cannot get about owing to not being able to find his shoes. -mŏy or -mŏyā f. a delicate little foot (e.g. that of a child or of a beautiful girl). -nam m. a toe-nail. -nyukᵘ adj. (f. -nicᵘ̈), small footed, having the foot small as compared with other limbs. -nyŏṭh m. (sg. dat. -nyŏṭhas), the great toe, i.q. khŏra-nyŏṭh, s.v. khŏr 1 (K. 631). -pholᵘ m. a foot-pearl, the delicate foot of a beautiful girl; cf. khŏra-phȧlⁱ, s.v. khŏr 1. -roṭᵘ m., i.q. khŏra-roṭᵘ, s.v. khŏr 1 (K.Pr. 236). -shã̄d or -shānd, i.q. khŏra-shã̄d, s.v. khŏr 1. -shēr adv. from foot to head, from head to foot. -ṭyonḍᵘ m., i.q. khŏra-ṭyonḍᵘ, s.v. khŏr 1. -ʦhoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦhüṭᵘ̈), small-footed, having the feet small in comparison with the other limbs. -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), having the feet cut off, as in khōr ʦaṭun, ab.; having no feet from birth. -zyūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈), long-footed, having the feet long, as compared with the other limbs. ¶ khūrⁱ-hujara m. a foot-house, i.e. a lean-to house built against the wall of a larger one. Such houses quickly become distorted and crooked; hence, met. anyone of a crooked, deceitful nature. -tȧlⁱ adv. to or from under the feet (e.g. put under the feet, or take up from under the feet) (cf. K.Pr. 24, khor tal).
in khōr gaʦhun m.inf. (of a living being) to become thin, to become wasted; (of clothes, or the like) to become worn out. Cf. khār 2.
m. (W. 18) food, victuals, provisions; daily food, rations, diet, regulated allowance of food; a dose (of medicine) (cf. dawāh, p. 262b, l. 34) (Gr.M.).
m. charity, alms (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 62; H. v, 9).
adj. c.g. 'eaten and carried away'; hence, spent, embezzled, made a way with (K.Pr. 147).
adj. c.g. (of a shoe, or the like) supplied with or possessing a heel, made with a heel (i.q. khōri-wôlᵘ 1, s.v. khūrᵘ̈ 1 and khōridār 1.
in ba-khörī (= بخوآری), contemptibly, meanly, basely (Rām. 1186).
adj. c.g. (of a shoe, or the like) possessing a heel (i.q. khōri- wôlᵘ 1, s.v. khūrᵘ̈ 1, and khōrĕl).

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. khōridārĕñ), one who suffers from distress of mind or who is afflicted (e.g. owing to his having committed some serious fault), i.q. khōri- wôlᵘ 2, s.v. khūrᵘ̈ 2 and khōrilad.

adj. c.g. separated, excluded (Gr.M.). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become excluded; (of a case in a court of law) to be dismissed, struck off (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to exclude; (of a case, as ab.) to dismiss.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. khōriladiñ), one who suffers from distress of mind, or who is afflicted (e.g. owing to having committed some serious fault), i.q. khōridār 2. Cf. khūrᵘ̈ 2, qq.v.
f. the itch; scab; mange; itchiness, irritation (cf. danda-khᵒ, p. 224b, l. 28).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. khōryōv. Note, however, that there is also a 1 perf. part. khūrᵘ-motᵘ, see bel., as if the verb belonged to the 2nd conj.), to fear, be afraid (K. 88); esp. (of children, or the like) to be afraid (e.g. in the dark of the 'bogey-man'), to be frightened, terrified into fits; to suffer from a terrifying dream or nightmare. ¶ khūrᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. khūrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), frightened, terrified, as ab. ¶ khōryō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. khōryē-müʦᵘ̈), id.
adj. (f. khöriñᵘ̈), weighing one khār, see khār 3 (Gr.Gr. 147).

m. N. of a round-leafed swamp-plant (considered by natives to be a kind of lotus, cf. bŏd-khorᵘ, p. 83b, l. 9 and waṭa-khᵒ, p. 1157a, l. 4). Limnanthemum nymphoides (L. 71 khur, Śiv. 1837). It is much valued as a food for cattle which increases the yield of milk. Cf. buḍa-khorᵘ, bŏṭa-khorᵘ, gurⁱ-khorⁱ, s.vv. buḍa, bŏṭa, and gurᵘ. Probably the kúrú of El. which he translates Villarsia nymphoides. Cf. also khair 2. ¶ khȧrⁱ-nal m. the stem of this plant, which is cooked as a vegetable. -püjᵘ̈ f. a kind of large basket full of the leaves of this plant. -wạthᵃr m. a leaf of this plant.

m. the old worn basket-work round the outside of a disused kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or portable brazier, when the inner earthen- ware vessel for retaining the burning coals has been broken and thrown away. It is often used for carrying fish, see gāḍa-khôrᵘ, p. 276a, l. 46. Cf. khŏphᵘ̈rᵘ̈.

adj. (f. khürᵘ̈ 1), one who is afflicted with scald-head (Tinea capitis), one bald-headed from this cause, a scald-head, a bald-head, cf. kharēla and khürᵘ̈ 4 (W. 144, khor); met. a mean, dirty, person; cf. guhⁱ-khürⁱ, p. 280b, l. 21, a wicked man; kharis-rāj, a wicked man's reign (K.Pr. 105). ¶ khȧrⁱ-khapa m. 'anger of a scald-head'; met. groundless arrogance. khȧrⁱ- parmāna m. a scald-headed weigh-man, a bald-headed fellow employed by a merchant to put the weights into the pan of the scales; a scald-head who is a mean fellow even among other scald-heads. ¶ khari-kala m. a scald-headed fellow; a term of abuse used in scolding children. -kashun yunᵘ m.inf. the itch of a scald-head to come on.

adj. (f. khörᵘ̈), equal to a khār, weighing or measuring a khār (see khār 3); often --˚, as in aḍ-khôrᵘ, weighing half a khār; hatabŏdⁱ-khôrⁱ, weighing hundreds of khārs (H. ix, 9); cf. aiṭh, dah, ḍāy.-bôrᵘ m. a load weighing a khār.

f. (for 1, see khār 3), a large basket receptacle made of withies used in mills. It receives the wheat, etc., to be ground, and delivers it to the mill-stones. In the compound graṭa-khôrᵘ, see graṭa, the word is masc. (Śiv. 1914; in Śiv. 1795, khār).

m. a certain measure of grain, a load of twelve local seers, eight of these being equal to a khār of ninety-six local seers, see aiṭha khorᵘ path, p. 66b, l. 18, and khār 3; (in cutting crops or grass) a certain measure consisting of twelve handfuls, or as much as can be grasped twelve times in the hand, two sheaves, see dā̃-khorᵘ, p. 230a, l. 14, and gāsa-khorᵘ, p. 307b, l. 26 (K.Pr. 132, khur).
in graṭa-khôrᵘ and (p. 1206b, l. 4) yĕci-khôrᵘ, i.q. khörᵘ̈ 2, q.v.

good; goodness; good fortune, prosperity, welfare, well-being, weal; health, happiness; cf. khair 1. -shēr m. happiness or sorrow, prosperity or misfortune (used in expressions of doubt and the like).
m., i.q. khŏr 2, an eater, used --˚, as in añĕma-khorᵘ, an eater of rice-gruel, gᵃsa-khorᵃ, an eater of filth (see añĕma and gᵃs). Cf. khŏr 2.
f. of khôrᵘ 2; see also khārun.
m. disapproval, blame, censure (K.Pr. 218, 221, khur). Cf. kharun.
f. the pl. nom. of this word is khārĕ which occurs in danda-khārĕ, the sockets of the teeth, the gums. See dand 1, p. 224b, l. 23.
adj. c.g. (f. khürᵘ̈ 2), i.q. khara 1, pure, genuine; pure, unalloyed (K.Pr. 206, khur, opp. to khọ̆ṭᵘ); i.q. khara 2, erect, standing up (cf. kan 1).
in bāna-khörᵘ̈ f., the weight of carrying on a household, p. 109b, l. 35; cf. khörⁱ, possibly a met. use of khūrᵘ̈ 2.
in hĕwawañĕ khörᵘ̈, even at the very beginning. ? sg. dat. of khār 3.

m. one who can only grow a small thin chinbeard and cannot grow whiskers, etc. (K.Pr. 110). Such men have the reputation of affability (K.Pr. 100). -dörᵘ̈ f. the thin little beard of such a man. -khĕn or -khyonᵘ m. a Khōsa's dinner; a dinner party at which there are many trays of food served, all of which the guests succeed in eating, so that nothing is left. The manner of accomplishing this feat is said to have been devised by a smart Khōsa; see K.Pr. 110 for the stories connected with it. -mahanyuwᵘ m. a man with such a beard.
adj. c.g. having the bark diseased as described s.v. khŏsorᵘ, q.v.

or khush خوش adj. c.g. pleasant, charming, agreeable (Śiv. 470, 475, 499; Rām. 1279); pleased (with, dat.) (K.Pr. 157; Śiv. 171, 356, 373, 714); healthy, happy, well-pleased, glad, cheerful, satisfied, contented (El. khúsh) (Śiv. 476, 482, 656; Rām. 146, 198, 261, 660-1, 858, 1066, 1279, 1397); willing (dinas khŏsh, willing to give, Gr.M.); fond of (khĕnas khŏsh, fond of eating, Gr.M.). --ākha --, see s.v. khŏshākh. --andām -- خوش اندام adj. c.g. fair-formed, possessing a beautiful body (Rām. 1039). --dīdār خوش دیدار adj. c.g. pleasant to look upon (YZ. 47). -dil خوش دل adj. c.g. happy-hearted, delighted; of happy mind, lively in disposition (Gr.M.; Rām. 98, 831, 1134). -dil karun خوش دل کرن m.inf. to delight (El.). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become pleased, be pleased (Gr.M.; Śiv. 356, 386, 431, 696, 710, 783-4, 795, 807, 899, 1334, 1348, 1712; Rām. 116, 136-7, 392, 451, 589, 872, 1282, 1284, 1327, 1344; H. viii, 1, 9, 14; xii, 9, 12); to become pleasing, to become agreeable (to, dat.) (Śiv. 894, 1071, 1238; Rām. 213, 592, 1371, 1512; H. viii, 11). --hāl خوش حال, see s.v. --khath -- خوش خط m. neat handwriting, good handwriting. --kandām -- (for --andām, ab.) adj. c.g. possessing a beautiful form (Rām. 1040). --karun -- m.inf. to make happy, to please (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 191; Rām. 304; H. xii, 3); to make pleased (with, dat.) (Śiv. 714). --pöṭhⁱ -- adv. in a happy manner; (of a journey) safely and comfortably (Gr.M.). --sapadun -- m.inf. to become happy, to become pleased (Śiv. 1103, 1286; Rām. 304, 481, 702, 900, 1296, 1330, 1461); to exult (El.); to become pleased, satisfied (with, dat. or abl.) [Śiv. 1044 (abl.), 1295 (dat.), 1471 (dat.)]. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be pleasant (to a person), to seem nice (Hindōstānī pasand ānā) (Gr.M.; YZ. 25; Śiv. 485, 806, 1718; Rām. 317, 611, 1033, 1279). --yiwunᵘ -- (Rām. 128, 353) or --yiwawunᵘ -- (YZ. 9; Śiv. 1462; Rām. 247, 1039) n.ag. (f. -wüñᵘ̈), one that pleases, pleasant.

or m. a welcome, a compliment (El.). The word is like our 'welcome' derived from the following: khŏsh-ākha interj. 'welcome', properly a phrase like the English word, art thou come (ākha) well (khosh) ? Cf. khŏshāmad.
(for 1, see khŏsh-hāl) adj. c.g. left-handed; (by extension of meaning) one who habitually uses by preference all his left-hand members (not only the hand).
m. flattery, adulation (Gr.M.); cf. khŏshākh. --karun -- m.inf. to pay compliments (to), fawn (upon), flatter (El., Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. fragrant, odoriferous, aromatic (El., YZ. 234); as subst., f. fragrance, odour (Gr.M.).

or khŏshāl 1 adj. c.g. happy, glad (K.Pr. 106, 181; Śiv. 1318); fortunate. khŏshāl khānas zuv aʦun m.inf. to disturb others in sorrow by a merry noise (e.g. ignorant children shouting in merriment in a house of mourning or where there is illness. In this it is said that khānas is a corruption of kanas, and this phrase is said to mean lit. 'as when a louse goes into a happy ear').

f. joy, pleasure, enjoyment (Gr.M.); joy, happiness (opp. mātam) (Śiv. 327); will, voluntariness (panañi khŏshiyi-kinⁱ, at one's own choice, Gr.M.); will, what is willed or determined (e.g. the will of God) (Rām. 851, 969). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make merry, rejoice, exult (El., K.Pr. 107, Rām. 796). -sān or (Rām. 752, 1370) khŏshiyĕ-sān adv. joyfully, gladly (Rām. 750, 752, 1218, 1330, 1370).
adj. c.g. dry; parched; withered. As subst. m., sg. dat. khŏshkas gaʦhun m.inf. to go by land, as opp. to ābas gaʦhun, to go by water (K.Pr. 49, W. 124). Cf. the next.
f. dryness; dry land. khŏshkī wati-kinⁱ, (to go) by land as opp. to öbī-wati- kinⁱ, by water (Gr.M.). Cf. the preceding.
in khŏshra-bāshirᵘ̈ m. a whispered conversation, talking in whispers. Cf. khūsri.

adj. (f. khö̆shᵘ̈), left-handed; able to use the left hand as well as the right, ambidextrous. Cf. khôwurᵘ. ¶ khŏshⁱ-atha m. the left hand; as adv. with the left hand. -khŏr f. acting in the left-handed or opposite way, acting contrary to custom, emancipated conduct (L.V. 10, 77). khōwurᵘ adj. (f. khōvᵘ̈rᵘ̈), right and left reversed (e.g. when one puts the right shoe on the left foot and vice versa, or when one performs right hand actions on the left and vice versa) (K.Pr. 250). -pav m. one who habitually does everything left-handedly (not only with his hand, but with all his members), one who is sinistral. -war m. winding to the left, winding counter-clockwise (e.g. a string); cf. the English 'left-handed' screw. -wȧrⁱ adv. counter-clockwise.
m. (sg. dat. khösiyĕtas), property, peculiar nature, attribute, natural disposition (Gr.M.).

or khŏsurᵘ m. a condition of the bark of a tree or of a walnut, or the like, in which it is worm-eaten and the under part reduced to powder; with dand 1 (p. 224b, l. 30) it signifies the tartar of the teeth as it breaks off. Cf. khashurᵘ.

m. a bowl-shaped metal cup, used by Hindūs for drinking, and by Musalmāns also for eating rice. That used by Musalmāns is larger than that used by Hindūs (El. khŏs and khós; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 248; YZ. 275; Śiv. 195, 1759; H. ii, 3). ¶ khösⁱ-dạndⁱrⁱ f. the edge, or lip, of such a cup. -ʦokᵘ m. the bowl part of such a cup.

m. riding on the shoulder, esp. a forfeit in children's games, according to which the winner rides on the shoulders of the loser (K. 252 ff.) with suff. of indef. art. khôsāh, a single ride on another's shoulders; cf. aṭa-bôrᵘ, p. 52a, l. 44. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give another a ride on one's shoulder, as ab.; to be ridden, as ab. (K. 221, 252). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take a ride on another's shoulders, as ab. (K. 252). --khārun -- m.inf. to give another a ride upon one's shoulders (K. 254). --khasun -- m.inf. to mount upon another's shoulders, as ab. (K. 253).

khōta, or (Gr.Gr. 49) khŏtan postpos. indicating comparison, than. It governs either the abl. or the abl. of the gen. Thus kañi (or kañĕ-handi) khŏta trakurᵘ, harder than a stone. For further particulars, see Gr.Gr. 49, Gr.M., and W. 98; YZ. 27, 186, 200; Śiv. khŏta 166, 434, 497, 784, 1062, 1087, 1290, 1657; khōta 1867-8; Rām. khŏta, 265, 730, 976, 1239, 1272, 1404, 1493; H. khŏta, iii, 8; xii, 10, 19; K. khŏta, 906, 1102). The word is sometimes used to indicate merely the ablative case, as in dŏha-khŏta dŏha, from day to day (Śiv. 410).
adj. c.g. irregular in shape, unsymmetrical (esp. of a child's face, or the like).

adj. c.g. of or belonging to the district of Khōtan in Central Asia. --trēl -- f. a kind of apple of moderate size, red in colour, and of superior quality (El. khotunyi trēla, L. 349 khatoni trel). The trēl is a small species of apple of good flavour. This is larger, but with equal flavour.

adj. c.g. (as subst. m., sg. dat. khŏṭas), (of a living being) wanting a limb, maimed. --gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈--), become maimed. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become maimed (of anything animate or inanimate); (of a work) to turn out wrongly.
in khŏṭh-khŏṭöyⁱ f. the condition of being full of fraud, a swindling disposition, guileful nature, perfidiousness.

in the following: --gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), gone to shame, put to shame, disgraced, infamous, of bad repute (due to the divulging of some disgraceful action). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to have a feeling of shame, to become disgraced, to get an ill repute (owing to some disgraceful action). --karun -- m.inf. to disgrace (a person), put to shame, give an evil repute (by disclosing some disgraceful act).
m. a thought, suggestion, idea (K.Pr. 182); inclination, propensity; affection, regard, favour; pleasure, satisfaction; carnal desire (H. viii, 3).
f. (sg. dat. khôtūni, H. x, 7; xii, 15), a noble woman, a lady (H. v, 11; x, 7, 12; xii, 15, 18-20, 22, 25).
adj. (f. khö̃ṭᵘ̈rᵘ̈), of uneven shape, irregularly shaped (of a stone, or the like). Cf. khỗṭᵘ and ỗṭurᵘ-khỗṭurᵘ.

postpos. for the sake of, on account of, out of consideration or regard for, on behalf of. It governs either the abl. or the abl. of the gen. Thus kāmi (or kāmĕ-handi) khᵒ, for the sake of the business. The use of the genitive is, however, principally confined to animate nouns (Gr.M.; W. 98, 99).

adj. (f. khö̆ṭᵘ̈, dat. khŏcĕ), base (of an apparent precious metal), impure, alloyed (K.Pr. 206, opp. to khorᵘ 6; Rām. 1607); flawed (of a precious stone) (H. xii, 3); counterfeit, spurious (El.); (of an action) base, wicked, blameworthy (Śiv. 105, 171); one who habitually cheats, swindling, knavish. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become base; to become wounded in battle (Rām. 1355).

m. (pl. nom. khö̃ṭⁱ), the half of anything (e.g. a box in two halves); esp. the half of anything globular or nearly globular in shape (e.g. of an apple, a pear, a walnut, or a kidney; cf. bŏka-wacĕ-khᵒ, p. 99b, l. 49 and wölinjĕ-khᵒ, p. 1115b, l. 34), a hemisphere; in the comp. aina-khỗṭᵘ (p. 30b, l. 8) it means a receptacle. Cf. khã̄ṭh.
f. (sg. dat. khã̄cĕ), N. of a certain kind of small fish.

m. a wall-cupboard, a store cupboard for holding pots and pans, etc., a small closet (cf. bāna-khᵒ, p. 109b, l. 42; brā̃da-khᵒ, p. 119b, l. 14; brörⁱ-khⁱ, p. 125b, l. 32; dᵃhi-khᵃ, p. 198b, l. 31; and hēri-khᵒ, p. 345b, l. 12); the part of a ḍū̃ga or country boat, either immediately behind or immediately before the centre part occupied by passengers. Cf. gālav (El. khaut, khut). ¶ khȧtⁱ-bāgay f. distributing from various store-rooms; esp. (at a crowded wedding or similar feast, when there is not room to distribute food to all the guests in one place) distributing the food from various places or rooms. -bata m., id.
in khati kaḍun m.inf. to train (e.g. a horse in his paces, or a man in conduct). Possibly a metaphorical use of khotᵘ 2. --nērun -- m.inf. to be trained, as ab.
m. the condition of being on the left (Gr.Gr. 139).

orkhōwurᵘ (Gr.Gr. 23) adj. (f. khōvürᵘ̈), left (not right) (K.Pr. 43; YZ. 535; L. 461); north (Gr.Gr. 151, Rām. 516; El. gives 'south', see wŏturᵘ); cf. khọ̆shᵘ, p. 418b, l. 27. --atha -- m. the left hand (H. viii, 7). --dachyunᵘ -- adj. on the right and on the left, on each side. --gām --, a village considered to be on the left-hand side of the sun's course, as opposed to a dachyunᵘ gām on the right side of the same. The former are less fertile (L. 435). --khōr -- m. the left foot (YZ. 535, Rām. 552). --pôrᵘ -- m. the left side; N. of a pargana or fiscal division of Kashmīr on the eastern or left side of the Lẹ̆dᵘ̈rᵘ̈ Valley (RT.Tr. 465). ¶ khōwᵃ̇rᵃ̇ or khōwȧrⁱ adv. from the left (u.w. vbs. of going, etc.); on the left (Gr.Gr. 155, Śiv. 246). -kinⁱ adv. from the left, commencing from the left (Gr.Gr. 159, Rām. 856); on the left (Rām. 421). -pörⁱ adv. from the left (Gr.Gr. 160); on the left (Gr.Gr. 160). -pav m. one who is practised in using his left hand, left- handed or ambidextrous. ¶ khōwari in khōwari-kani adv. on the left, towards the left, leftwards (u.w. vbs. of placing, etc.) (Śiv. 1090). -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of belonging to, or produced on the left. -pāryukᵘ adj. (f. -pāricᵘ̈), on the left, of or belonging to the left. ¶ khōvürᵘ̈ bab f. the left hand bosom of a woman. --nürᵘ̈ -- f. the left arm. --zang -- f. the left leg. ¶ khōwaryukᵘ adj. (f. khōwaricᵘ̈), of the left, that on the left; esp. (the fruit) on the left side (of a tree, which, owing to the course of the sun are not so sweet as those on the right); of or belonging to the north (Gr.Gr. 151).
f. habit, disposition, temper, (Rām. 1501) in Kāshmīrī, politeness (K.Pr. 89 ḵẖoe). Cf. khō 1.
m., see danda-khöyin, p. 224b, l. 39. Cf. khay 1.
f. the corruption of stagnant water (accompanied by putrefaction and a foul smell), slime (Śiv. 1804); the disease of itch; a disease of the teeth (see danda-khᵒ, p. 224b, l. 41).
or -buḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈ or -buḍᵘ̈), very fearful, timid, easily terrified. Cf. boḍᵘ (p. 84b, l. 12) (Gr.M.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. khōʦanôwᵘ), to cause to fear, to make afraid, to terrify, to frighten (El., Gr.M., Rām. 25, K. 222).
n.ag. (f. khōʦawüñᵘ̈), frightened, terrified, afraid; timid (El.); terrible (El.).

conj. 2 (1p.p. khūʦᵘ, 2 p.p. khōʦōv), to be afraid, to fear (K.Pr. 59; Rām. 492, 553, 633, 636, 704, 758, 932, 1226, 1749; K. 139, 158, 245, 247). The object may be in the dat. (K.Pr. 221; Rām. 30, 33), or in the abl. (Śiv. 1804), or governed by a postposition, such as nishĕ. Thus, wananas khōʦun, to be afraid to speak; gaʦhana khᵒ, to be afraid to go; Khŏdāyĕs-nishĕ khᵒ, to fear God (Gr.M.). ¶ khūʦⁱ khūʦⁱ freq. part. used as adv., in continual fear. ¶ khūʦᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. khūʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), frightened, afraid. ¶ khōʦan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who fears, a coward; esp. a coward in wordy warfare.
adj. c.g. easily terrified, see khrakh, and cf. khrakilad.

f. (sg. dat. khraki), terror, alarm, fright (e.g. that of an unbroken horse when first ridden, or of a child). --khë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f. inf. to suffer from terror. ¶ khraki-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who suffers from terror, one who by nature is easily terrified, i.q. khrakilad.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. khrakiladiñ), one who suffers from terror, one who by nature is easily terrified, i.q. khraki-wôlᵘ, s.v. khrakh.
m. the snorting noise made in clearing the nose of liquid mucus, or in clearing the chest when suffering from cold; cf. khrŏñ. -khrañ m. the frequent repetition of this sound.
m. abuse, scolding, a threat (such as is addressed to a child, a servant, or person of low caste). --karun -- m.inf. to threaten (El.). --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to scold, as ab.
adj. c.g. cracked, fissured, i.q. khrapidār.

f. (sg. dat. khrapi), a crack, a fissure, esp. in a stone, or the like; a gap (between the teeth; cf. danda-khᵒ, p. 224b, l. 24). --karith -- adv. very quickly, very speedily, u.w. vbs. of doing, speaking, etc.
adj. c.g. possessing cracks or fissures, i.q. khrapal.

or khrēs f. a feeling of shame, a sense of shame (due to consciousness of disgrace on account of some wrong action). --wālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause a sense of shame to descend, i.e. to put a person to public disgrace, to humiliate. --wasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a sense of shame to descend; to be put to great shame, to be put to public disgrace.
? m. onomat. (sg. dat. khraṭas), the noise made in swallowing, the sound of a gulp. --karith -- adv. having made such a sound, with a gulping sound.

(also sometimes khāv) f. a clog, patten, or wooden sole, worn by Kāshmīrīs in winter (El. khráo m.) (K.Pr. 110; Śiv. 1711, 1829; Rām. 305-6, 729; H. v, 9); a weaver's shuttle (in shape like our netting needle, used by shawl-weavers or pashmīnā-weavers). ¶ khrāwa-chān m. a patten-carpenter, a patten-maker. -horᵘ or khāwa-horᵘ m. a pair of pattens (Gr.Gr. 82). -hȧrⁱ-khŏr m. one of a pair of pattens. khrāwa-phyurᵘ m. the act of turning round of a weaver's khrāv, disarrangement of the order of the shuttles containing the various coloured threads. ¶ khrāvi-dab m. a blow from a patten (a patten being taken off the foot and used as a weapon). -han f. a small patten, a child's patten. -jaṭiñ or -jaṭiñāh f. an old, worn out, wooden patten (cf. jaṭin). -jaṭiñāh is mostly used in questions, as in khrāvi- jaṭiñāh chĕy-nā, have you not got an old patten? -khŏr m. a single one of a pair of pattens. -mŏy or -mŏyāh f. a small patten, a child's patten. Like -jaṭiñāh, ab., -mŏyāh is used mostly in questions. -nŏkᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the hole near the toe of a patten for receiving the strings with which it is fastened to the foot. -paḍur m. (sg. dat. paḍaras), 'a patten-hoof,' the under part of a patten. -sadāh m. the sound made by a patten in walking, 'the clang of the wooden shoon.'
m. the Laughing Gull, Larus ridibundus (L. 123, krind), found on the Kashmīr lakes in the winter.

khruwᵘ, or khryuwᵘ (sg. dat. khrivis), N. of a village about twenty miles S.E. of Śrīnagar, the ancient Khaḍūvī. It is a spot sacred to the goddess Jwālāmukhī Durgā, and is largely visited by Hindū pilgrims (RT.Tr. II, 459; Śiv. 93, 95, 1137).
f. (sg. dat. khrī˜ʦi), a mouse (El. khrínts). -hishᵘ̈ f. like a mouse; met. any fem. thing that is tiny in form. -zan f., id.
m. a dent (e.g. caused by a blow given to a metal vessel). --aʦun -- m.inf. a dent to be made, as ab. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to straighten out a dent. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause or make a dent.
adj. c.g. dented (of a metal vessel by a blow, or the like).
adj. c.g. one who habitually snores in his sleep, a great snorer.
m. (sg. dat. khrŏkas), snoring, a snore (cf. خرخر).

m. the snorting noise made in clearing the nose of liquid mucus; cf. khrañ and khrõ̆v. -khrŏñ m. the frequent repetition of this sound; the rattling sound caused by phlegm in the throat, due to a cold.
adj. c.g. one who is liable to suffer from a cold, with consequent phlegm in the throat.
m. onomat. wheezing of the chest (due to a cold, or the like); cf. khrŏñ. -khrõ̆v m. repeated wheezing, continued wheezing. -khrỗv-gŏʦorᵘ m. one who habitually wheezes. Cf. goʦᵘ̈rᵘ̈.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. khrõ̆vkhrõ̆vladiñ), one who wheezes, one who suffers from wheezing, i.q. khrõ̆v-khrõ̆v-gŏʦorᵘ, s.v. khrõ̆v.
m. the pedal of a loom. Cf. khrāv (W. 15 krāvⁱ pl. nom. for khrövⁱ).
f. (sg. dat. khracĕ), any very small copper coin of little value; any fem. thing which has become much worn by old age and long use.
f. an unchaste woman (cf. khaḍ, khaḍa, and khoḍᵘ).
f. a kind of coarse woollen blanket.
in khǖ̃kha-paṭôrᵘ or -pŏṭôrᵘ adj. (f. -paṭörᵘ̈), a flat-nosed person, who habitually speaks through his nose.

m. the condition of possessing a flat nose; flat-nosedness; the nasality of speech consequent upon this condition (Gr.Gr. 140). ¶ khũ̄̈khĕra-sān adv. in a nasal tone, u.w. vbs. of speaking, or the like.
adj. c.g. (as subst. khũ̄̈khĕradārĕñ), flat-nosed; hence, one who speaks through the nose, one whose voice is nasal.
m. hollow, empty, lacking a kernel (of a fruit of the nut kind, such as an almond or a walnut). Cf. khŏkhorᵘ.

adj. (f. khū̃khᵘ̈ 1 Gr.Gr.36 or khǖ̃khᵘ̈ 1), having a deformed or flat nose, and hence habitually speaking through the nose (W. 11 khoṇkh). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become subject to such a condition (from disease or naturally), to become flat-nosed, etc.
or khǖ̃khᵘ̈ 2 f. self- conceit arising from undeserved praise, or the like. --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such self-conceit to mount (i.e. to be felt).

adj. c.g. wide, widely extended, i.q. kholᵘ, q.v.; released, independent, free (Śiv. 1835); open, clear, cloudless (of the sky) (Rām. 678, khulō, m.c.). -khula adj. c.g. wide, expanded, having plenty of room (e.g. a place already containing people, but with room for more); (of handwriting) open, wide, wide apart.
adj. c.g. forming the purest and best part or substance of anything; (in Kāshmīrī) beautiful and excellent in its own kind; as subst. m. the substance, gist, pith of anything (Gr.M.).
adj. (f. khūjⁱ or khūjᵘ̈), muddy (of water, or the like).

m. intoxication; languishing appearance of the eyes (the effect of drinking, or of drowsiness, or of love, etc.), a languishing look, languishment. pur-khumār (YZ. 269) or pūrᵘ-khumār (H. v, 2), (of a loved one) full of languishment.
m. a large vessel or jar; a dyer's vat (K.Pr. 177).
or (Rām. 915) khū̃ m. blood (YZ. 16; Rām. 814, 837, 842, 1075, 1162, 1201); killing, slaughter, murder (Gr.M.). khū̃-rīzī خون ریزی f. bloodshed, slaughter, carnage (Rām. 915).

f. (sg. dat. khanjĕ 2), a piece, bit, fragment; met. as in bukᵃ̇rᵃ̇-khᵃ̇ (p. 102b, l. 2) a piece of face, insolence; buthⁱ-khⁱ (p. 142b, l. 7) a piece of face, imperturbability. khündᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. (Rām. 969) or khanjĕ gaʦhañĕ f. pl. inf. (Rām. 1488), breaking or fragments to happen (to, dat.); hence (subj. in dat.) to be broken to fragments, to be shattered to pieces.
adj. c.g. bloody, covered with blood (Rām. 921); bloody, sanguinary; subst. m. a murderer, assassin.
adj. c.g. bloodthirsty, sanguinary, fierce, cruel (Gr.M.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. khunzᵘ), i.q. khṻnzun, q.v.khunzᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. khunzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. khǖnzᵘ-motᵘ, q.v. s.v. khṻnzun.

(also khunzun) conj. 1 (1 p.p. khǖnzᵘ), to pluck (the feathers of a bird); to pluck out the hairs (of a man, etc.). ¶ khǖnzᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. khǖnzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), plucked (of a bird or man, etc.), as ab. ¶ khǖnzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈kŏkürᵘ̈ f. a plucked fowl, a fowl (dead or alive) from which the feathers have been plucked.
f. a kind of warm woollen blanket (K.Pr. 205, khani). In K.Pr. 201 the sg. dat., written khanih is translated 'a mendicant's cloak'. ¶ khañi-waguvᵘ m. a kind of reed mat.
adv. (formed from خفت) at bedtime, at the time for going to sleep, about 9.30 p.m. (K.Pr. 177).
m. the hard shell of a coco-nut (used for the water bowl of the native pipe or hubble-bubble); a chestnut (El. khuprah, p. 156 or khúprah, p. 11).
in khura-khura m. longing for something unobtained or unobtainable (K.Pr. 57, khur-khurah, translated 'proudness'). Cf. khāra-khāra, p. 408b, l. 31.

adj. c.g. roughened (of a stone, or the like originally smooth, but become rough by lapse of time). --dūjᵘ̈ -- f. a writing board which has become rough through constant use or through dirt; see dūjᵘ̈. --gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. gömüʦᵘ̈), become roughened, as ab. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become roughened, as ab.
f. food, victuals, fare; in Kāshmīrī, dry grām or similar grain used as food.

m. the condition of being spoiled by many knots and tangles (of thread taken from the spinning wheel or in hanks); met. (of a business) the condition of being tangled or complicated, utter confusion; torment, vexation (Rām. 1510). --aʦun -- m.inf. knottiness to enter, to become spoiled by being tangled and knotted, as ab.); met. (of a business) to become tangled and complicated, as ab. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to make tangled, as ab.; (of a business) to throw into utter confusion, as ab. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. tangledness to come, to become tangled, as ab.; (of a business) to become utterly confused, as ab. ¶ khurⁱ-kã̄gⁱrⁱ f. 'a brazier (full) of tangles', i.e. a collection of many faults (as when a number of new faults appear in something originally faulty). -khōkhosᵘ m. a public office, or place of public business which, in order to harass the people, is filled with false accusations. For the Sanskrit word khurkhuṭādhikaraṇam, see RT.Tr. vii, 298 n.; cf. khōkhosᵘ. -māv yiñᵘ̈ f.inf. to be at one's wit's end, owing to failure to accomplish some difficult task. -zāl m. 'a tangle-net', a kind of fishing-net (Rām. 1781). ¶ khuris-manz yunᵘ m.inf. to find oneself suddenly entangled in some very objectionable business.
f. a 'tangle-net', a kind of net used by boat-men; cf. khurⁱ-zāl, s.v. khurᵘ (K.Pr. 112, khuri). -wālawöshᵘ̈ f. a springe attached to a net, used by hunters for catching deer and birds.
m. the leg of a bed, stool, or the like. Cf. khōr 2.

f. (sg. dat. khōrĕ), the heel (El. khúr, m., Gr.M.); met. a great hindrance (K.Pr. 119). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to use the heel; hence, (in riding) to spur a horse, etc., with the heel. ¶ khōrĕ tachañĕ f.pl.inf. the heels to pare (the earth); met. to be agitated or distraught with pain or sorrow (as if one who was unable to use his limbs was being dragged along with his heels scraping the ground). ¶ khōri gōmotᵘ perf. part. (f. gömüʦᵘ̈), (of a shoe, etc.) gone at the heel, having the heel worn away. -holᵘ adj. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), crooked-heeled. -raz f. a strap at the heel of a shoe, used to fasten it more firmly when the wearer is going a long distance. -wôlᵘ 1 adj. (f. -wājĕñ 1), (of a shoe, or the like) possessing a heel, made with a heel (i.q. khōridār 1 and khōrĕl).
m. the name for the sign for non-initial u in the Śāradā character, corresponding to, and closely resembling in form, the Nāgarī. The sign for the corresponding long vowel is ar-khǖrᵘ̈, q.v.

f. (sg. dat. khōrĕ), affliction, distress of mind (Śiv. 196, 1895, khörⁱ) (e.g. that occurring to a servant in a great house owing to the commission of some fault); cf. khōridār 2 and khōrilad. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such distress of mind to come to one. ¶ khōri-wôlᵘ 2 adj. (f. -wājĕñ), one who suffers from such distress of mind (i.q. khōridār 2).

f. (for 1 and 2, see khorᵘ 2 and 6), want of affection, dislike (for a person); cf. kharun. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. want of affection to occur, love for a person to cease, love to be changed to hate; (for an inan. obj.) liking to cease, a sudden aversion to be felt.
m. an oar, a paddle (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1780, 1804).
f. scald-head, Tinea capitis; --˚ met. a condition of humiliation or mortification; cf. gana-khürᵘ̈, p. 287b, l. 27; cf. khorᵘ 2 and kharil 2 (El. khar, m.; Gr.Gr. 33, 35 f.; K.Pr. 111, khur).
adj. (f. khūrᵘ̈ or khǖrᵘ̈), afraid, fearful, used --˚, as in aḍ-khūrᵘ, p. 10a, l. 25, half-afraid, timid. Cf. khōrun.
or khariñ f. a jenny-ass, a she-ass, see khar 1 (El. khȧir, W. 17).
see khōr 2 as well as khūrᵘ (1-5).
adj. c.g. full of tangles or knots (see khurᵘ); hence, full of difficulties and impediments, (of a business, or the like) full of anxious moments, a never-ending source of anxiety, i.q. khurⁱlad.
adj. c.g. possessing legs (of a stool, bed, table, or the like). Cf. khūrᵘ 1.
adj. c.g. (of a syllable or letter) possessing a non-initial u, see khūrᵘ 2.
m. N. of a district in Kashmīr near the Pīr Panṯs̱āl Pass, see RT.Tr. II, 470. The N. is a double one.
m. the process of weeding rice growing in water (L. 325, 327, 463).
(? spelling and gender), the net in which water chestnuts (see gôrᵘ) are collected (L. 355).
in khūsri tabūsri f.pl. (probably better spelt khūsrĕ ta būsrĕ), whispered conspiracy, mutual whispered consultation, esp. with evil intent against another. Cf. khŏshra.
adv. may be, perhaps, I'll see if I'll do it (used by an insolent or spoiled servant, or the like, when told to do something); an interj. never mind, it's no matter (K.Pr. 3, khūstū).

f. abstraction from the bottom of a heap (e.g. a mouse carrying off from a pile); met. the aimless pulling done by a little child at something that attracts it; cf. khutun. --khutiñ karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. continually to abstract from below, as ab.; met. to harass.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. khutᵘ, 2 p.p. khuʦōv), to dig from below, to dig out from below (e.g. digging out, and stealing, from the bottom of a grain-heap); met. to dig into (a person), to squeeze, harass.

m. a stumble, slip, trip (in walking); met. a misfortune, calamity (K.Pr. 111, khunt). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to stumble, slip, trip; met. (in a transaction) to be tripped up, to be cheated. --lagun -- m.inf., id. (El., Gr.M., K.Pr. 144).
m. N. of a district in Kashmīr, stretching in a semi-circle round the north shore of the Wŏlur lake; the Khūyāśrama or Khōyāśrama of Sanskrit. See RT.Tr. viii, 2695-98, and II, 488. (El. khwíháma).
adj. (f.khūʦᵘ̈), fearful, troubled, distressed (properly, 1 p.p. of khōʦun) (El.).
or khāb خواب m. a dream (El.); cf. khāb. --wuchun -- m.inf. to see a dream, to dream (El.). ¶ khwöbi adv. in a dream. ¶ khwābas-manz adv. in a dream.
or khwāyish, khwöyish f. a desire, wish (El. khwáish).
khyōv, khĕyāv, khĕyiv, khĕyōv, see khyonᵘ.
in khyāv khyāv  the act of giving food continually; causing continual or gradual misappropriation by another of property entrusted to him.
f., i.q. khĕwawañ, q.v., see bata- khᵒ, p. 137a, l. 7.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. khyāwanôwᵘ), caus. of khyonᵘ, i.q. khyāwun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 172).

(also khyāwanāwun) conj. 1 (1 p.p. khyôwᵘ), to give to eat, to cause to be eaten; to cause to eat, to feed, etc. (K.Pr. 4, Śiv. 970, 1784, K. 373) (causal of khyonᵘ in all its meanings, Gr.Gr. 172); esp. to cause another to misappropriate or embezzle property entrusted to him. shōr khyāwun, to cause another to eat a noise, to roar at a person (Rām. 828; cf. 1780). ¶ khyôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. khyövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to be eaten; (of property entrusted) caused to be misappropriated or embezzled by the trustee.

m. a flock, a herd, a troop (of animals) (Gr.M.; L.V. 108; K.Pr. 236, 249; Rām. 910, 1301; K. 182, 207-8, 214, 327); often --˚, as in gōvᵘ̈-khyolᵘ̈, a herd of cows (Gr.Gr. 152; so, K. 210, 212-3, 382); sometimes also used for a company of human beings; cf. mahanivⁱ-khⁱ, s.v. mahanyuwᵘ. --anun -- m.inf. to bring a flock along, to lead or drive a herd home, to bring it from another village to one's own village. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to lead forth a flock, drive out a herd from the village to an outside spot such as a grazing ground. --nyunᵘ -- m.inf. to bring a flock, etc., or herd along from one spot or village to another. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to bring in a flock, etc., from outside. --wālun -- m.inf. to bring down a flock, etc. (from the mountains or forests to the village). ¶ khĕlⁱ-kaṭh (sg. dat. -kaṭas), the ram of a flock of sheep, the tup; met. a stout lusty fool of a fellow. -röchⁱ 1 f. the guardianship of a flock, shepherding, herding. -rôchᵘ (pl. nom. -röchⁱ 2), the guardian of a flock, a shepherd, herdsman. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who owns a flock; a flock-owner, one who owns many flocks. ¶ khĕli-bāpath adv. for the sake of the flock, for the herd, etc. --khĕli -- adv. in troops (K. 859). -khötᵃra adv. i.q. -bāpath, ab. ¶ khĕlis-andar adv. in the flock, within the herd. -kyutᵘ adj. (f. -kiʦᵘ̈), i.q. khĕli-bāpath, ab. -manz adv., i.q. andar, ab. -manz-bāg adv., id.

conj. 1 irreg. [the inf. of this verb is often spelt kheun in the roman character. Its caus. is khyāwun or khyāwanāwun (Gr.Gr. 172). ¶ Inf. and fut. pass. part. khyonᵘ (Gr.Gr. 112, 191; Śiv. 1202, 1223; Rām. 599, 813, 849 fut. pass. part., 1027; H. xii, 16 fut. pass. part.); acc. khĕnas (YZ. 169, Śiv. 1387, K. 138); abl. khĕna (L.V. 27, 63; K.Pr. 106; Śiv. 1042, 1430; Rām. 1577; K. 148); or khĕni (Śiv. 1084, m.c. khĕnē; H. x, 5; K. 204, 1144 m.c. khĕnē); gen. khĕnukᵘ (Śiv. 759, fem.); pl. nom. khĕnⁱ; f. sg. nom. khë̆ñᵘ̈ (Rām. 1629, K. 160); pl. nom. khĕñĕ. Pres. part. khĕwān (Gr.Gr. 103; Rām. 458, 698, 876, 936, 979, 1022, 1159; H. vi, 16; xii, 4, 6, 17). Impers. fut. part. khĕnī (Gr.Gr. 111). Conj. part. khĕth (Gr.Gr. 104, 197; L.V. 27, 77; YZ. 393, khet; Śiv. 328, 1073; Rām. 1631, 1653; K. 138). Neg. conj. part. khĕnay (Gr.Gr. 111, K.Pr. 104). Freq. part. khĕ khĕ (Gr.Gr. 105, 198) or khĕth khĕth (Gr.Gr. 105, 198). Adverbial part. khĕwönⁱ (Gr.Gr. 196). N.ag. 1 khĕwawunᵘ (Gr.Gr. 105); 2 khĕnawôlᵘ (Gr.Gr. 106). ¶ Fut. (Gr.Gr. 202) sg. 1 khĕma (Śiv. 1533; Rām. 972; H. viii, 11); khĕmay, for thee (Rām. 268, 387; H. iii, 1); 2 khĕkh (Śiv. 1434; Rām. 668; H. ii, 3; vi, 2); 3 khĕyi (Rām. 1780; H. xii, 15); khĕyiy, for thee (L.V. 88); khĕyiwa, you (Rām. 1742, K.Pr. 102); inter. khĕyā (K.Pr. 153). Pl. 1 khĕmav; 2 khĕyiv; 3 khĕn; khĕnam, me (Rām. 1191). ¶ Cond. past. (Gr.Gr. 253) sg. 1 khĕmahö; khĕmahas, for him (K.Pr. 144); 2 khĕhökh; 3 khĕyihē; khĕyihēs, it (K. 240). Pl. 1 khĕmahöv; 2 khĕyⁱhīv; 3 khĕhön. ¶ Impve. pres. (Gr.Gr. 247) sg. 2 khĕh (Śiv. 1824; H. iii, 1); khyuh (vill.) (H. x, 5); khyō (vill.) (H. x, 12); khĕm, for me (Gr.Gr. 248); khĕn, him (Rām. 599); 3 khĕyin (Rām. 1597); pl. 2 khĕyiv (YZ. 404); 3 khĕyin. Pol. (Gr.Gr. 249) sg. 2 khĕta (Śiv. 379, 578); khĕtam, for me (Śiv. 283, 374; H. iii, 1); 3 khĕyⁱtan; pl. 2 khĕyⁱtav; 3 khĕyⁱtan. Fut. khĕzi (Gr.Gr. 250; L.V. 90, khĕzē, m.c.; H. xii, 16). Past. khĕzihē (Gr.Gr. 251). ¶ 1 p.p. (Gr.Gr. 211) m.sg. khyōv (or khyauv) (H. x, 12) or khĕv (Rām. 81, 766, 1138, 1400; H. ii, 2); khyōm, by me (Gr.Gr. 217); khyōth, by thee (Śiv. 1328, K. 1090); khyōn, by him (H. vi, 16); khyōwa, by you; khyōkh, by them (Rām. 916); pl. khyēy or khēy (H. x, 2); khyēm, by me (L.V. 81); khyēth, by thee; khyēn, by him; khyēwa, by you; khyēkh, by them; f.sg. and pl. khĕyĕ (Rām. 1306); khĕyĕm, by me; khĕyĕth, by thee (Śiv. 702); khĕyĕn, by him; khĕyĕwa, by you (H. x, 12, vill. khĕyĕv); khĕyĕkh, by them. ¶ 2 p.p. (Gr.Gr. 233) m.sg. khĕyōv; pl. khĕyēy; khĕyēn, by him (Rām. 459); f.sg. and pl. khĕyēyĕ. ¶ 3 p.p. (Gr.Gr. 238) m.sg. khĕyāv; pl. khĕyēyēy; f.sg. and pl. khĕyēyĕ. ¶ Perf. part. khĕmotᵘ (Rām. 154, 344) or khyōmotᵘ (K. 1147), see bel.]. ¶ To eat (cf. bata, gŏh, gāsa; L.V. 27, 63, 77, 81, 88; YZ. 404; Śiv. 283, 1073, 1464; Rām. 81, 268, 387, 458-9, 599, 698, 766, 849, 972, 1159, 1173, 1191, 1306, 1577, 1629, 1653; H. iii, 1, etc.; K. 138, 141-2, 148, 160, 204, etc.); to take (medicine) (cf. dawāh-khᵒ, p. 262b, l. 35; Gr.M.), to eat, to live on, have as a means of subsistence (cf. drölⁱ khë̆ñᵘ̈, p. 243b, l. 25; hŏnjĕ-gāsa khᵒ, p. 337b, l. 43; harām khᵒ, p. 348b, l. 33); met. to eat the good things of this life, to enjoy oneself (L.V. 27, 90); to receive, meet with, experience (cf. cō̃kh khë̆ñᵘ̈, p. 170a, l. 12; cōṭh khᵒ, p. 178a, l. 1; dab khᵒ, p. 181a, l. 28; dŏkh khᵒ, p. 206a, l. 38; hō̃ʦh khᵒ, p. 360b, l. 11; Śiv. 1836; Rām. 916, 1400, 1743); to suffer, endure, experience (e.g. a beating, sticks, slander, swindling) (cf. bözⁱ khë̆ñᵘ̈, p. 152b, l. 28; cōb khĕnⁱ, p. 156b, l. 30; daka- ḍula khĕnⁱ, p. 203b, l. 48; gŏta khĕnⁱ, p. 310b, l. 25; mār 1; Rām. 344, an arrow); to undergo (a process), to be subjected to (some operative medium) (cf. bahā khᵒ, p. 94a, l. 17; barsāth khᵒ, p. 127a, l. 28; bazyunᵘ khᵒ, p. 155b, l. 11; dam khᵒ, p. 216a, l. 48); to feel (an emotion, such as fear, sorrow, etc.) (cf. bīm khᵒ, p. 107a, l. 26; bayĕ khᵒ, p. 148b, l. 21; gam khᵒ, p. 286b, l. 18) (Rām. 876, 979, 1022, 1027, 1138); to corrode, erode, wear away (tr.); to consume, spend; (with kasam, etc.) to take (an oath), to swear (Gr.M., Rām. 154); to embezzle, misappropriate (property entrusted to one) (cf. mush) (H. x, 2); to eat, to enjoy, experience the rapture of (any pleasant thing or experience) (YZ. 169). ¶ This verb often makes a nominal compound with a noun in some very metaphorical sense, as in aphsūs khyonᵘ, to eat alas, to regret (Rām. 668, 936); dam khyonᵘ, to eat one's breath; hence, to be silenced in wordy warfare; driy khë̆ñᵘ̈, to eat (i.e. take) an oath; hal khyonᵘ, to eat the after- birth, i.e. to die in childbirth; hatab khë̆ñᵘ̈, to eat firewood, i.e. to be cheated; shōr khyonᵘ, to experience a noise, to be roared at (Rām. 1780; cf. 828). Such idioms will usually be found under the various substantives which form the first member of the compound. ¶ This verb is also sometimes used with the conjunctive participle of another verb to form similar metaphorical compounds, as in būzith khyonᵘ, to eat after understanding; hence, to vie with, emulate. Such idioms are given under the verbs forming the first members of such compounds. ¶ khĕ khĕ freq. part. eating frequently, eating excessively, continually eating, eating without cessation. --ta khĕ -- freq. part., id. ¶ khĕh, impve. sg. 2, in the phrase khĕh khōʦh ma 'eat, fear not', used in permitting a person to eat while at work; esp. in sportive abuse (obsc.). ¶ khēmatis drāmun karun m.inf. 'to chew the cud of something embezzled', to embezzle, misappropriate something entrusted to one. Cf. drāmun, see khyōmotᵘ, bel. ¶ khĕna-grākh n.ag. (sg. dat. -grākas; f. -grākañ), an eater; esp. one who is fond of eating good food, an epicure, a bon-vivant, gourmet (Gr.Gr. 106). -wôlᵘ  n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), an eater (Gr.Gr. 106, 193); esp. a glutton; one who is skilled as regards the fitness or otherwise of any article for food; one who misappropriates what is entrusted to him, an embezzler. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. pass. to be eaten, to be edible (Gr.Gr. 170). ¶ khĕni cĕni adv. (inf. of purpose) to eat and drink, for the purpose of having a meal. Cf. khyonᵘ cyonᵘ, bel. ¶ khĕnay neg. conj. part. not having eaten; as adv., without having eaten, u.w. vbs. of going, or the like (K.Pr. 104). ¶ khĕñi, fut. pass. part. f. abl. -vizi adv. at the time of eating, at dinner time. ¶ khĕth conj. part. having eaten, etc. (Śiv. 328, 1073, 1087). --cĕth -- conj. part. having eaten and drunk, used as adv., after a meal, after dinner (Śiv. 328, 753, 1584, 1712, 1832); cf. khyonᵘ cyonᵘ, bel. --dith -- conj. part. having eaten and given; esp. u.w. vbs. of coming or of going, as in 'he went away after eating and giving'. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to eat up (K.Pr. 161, YZ. 393). --karith -- conj. part. esp. used as adv., after eating and doing (such and such a business). --ʦhunun -- m.inf., i.q. khĕth gaʦhun, ab. (Rām. 1631). ¶ khyōmotᵘ perf. part. (m. sg. dat. khyēmatis or khēmatis; f. sg. nom. khyēmüʦᵘ̈ or khēmüʦᵘ̈), eaten, etc. in all the various senses of khyonᵘ; esp. embezzled. --cyōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. khyēmüʦᵘ̈ cyēmüʦᵘ̈), eaten and drunk (of a meal). Cf. khyonᵘ cyonᵘ, bel. ¶ khyonᵘ m.inf. the act of eating; frequently used as a subst., eating, food, dinner (L. 73, kheun; Rām. 599; K. 241, 306, 309). khyonᵘ-cyonᵘ m. to eat and drink (of a meal at which both are done at the same time); as subst. meat and drink, food, board (Śiv. 1449; K. 401, 524, 932, 1131); cf. khĕn cĕn, p. 401b, l. 9. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give food, to give to eat; to support (another) with food; gar-bār paradĕn dyututh khyonᵘ, his house and home thou hast given to others to enjoy (Rām. 813). --raṭun -- m.inf. to stop eating, refrain from food (e.g. under a doctor's orders or from want of appetite owing to sickness); cf. khĕn raṭun, p. 401b, l. 13. --kyutᵘ -- adj. (f. khë̆ñᵘ̈-kiʦᵘ̈), fit to be eaten, intended for food. ¶ khyonuy m. only food, good for nothing but food; cf. khĕnạy, p. 402a, l. 24.
m. (sg. dat. khicis), obstruction, hindrance (by thrusting with the hand, etc.), standing in a person's way, pushing back a person who is going along. Cf. lȧṭⁱ-khyucⁱ, s.v. loṭᵘ 1.
or adj. (m. sg. dat. khīnis; abl. khīni; f. sg. nom. khīñᵘ̈), wasted, emaciated, feeble. ¶ khīna-pach m. (sg. dat. -pachas), the waning half of a lunar month, the fifteen days of a waning moon.
m. (sg. dat. khiris), a kind of straw mat or cushion, on which Hindū students and ascetics sit. They mostly come to the Valley of Kashmīr from Kashṭawāṛ (Kishtwar of the maps).

m. (sg. dat. khisis), the leather case in which barbers or surgeons keep their instruments. ¶ khisⁱ-phyurⁱ m. reversal of expectations, turning out contrary to expectations (e.g. when a merchant expects from some transaction only a small profit and yet makes great gain, or vice versa).
m. (sg. dat. khisis), a kind of bird, a teal (?). Cf. kyusᵘ. ¶ khisⁱ-pūtⁱ m. a young teal.
m. a scratch or superficial tear of the skin. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to cause a scratch, to scratch a person's skin so as to leave a mark. --lagun -- m.inf. a scratch on the skin to occur.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. khᵃhaladiñ), having the skin scratched, suffering from a scratch or scratches. Cf. khᵃh.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. khᵃñĕdārĕñ), filled with or covered with nose-mucus.
or khiñĕl adj. c.g. one who is always defiled with nose-mucus, one who suffers from running at the nose. -khāryukᵘ m. a young colt just born, whose nose is always running.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. khᵃñĕladiñ), i.q. khᵃñĕdār, q.v.
m. something that has not happened, a cock-and-bull story, a traveller's tale, fiction. --trāwun -- m.inf. to tell a cock-and-bull story, in the presence of someone who knows the truth.
m. onomat. the rustling sound made by paper, or the like. -khᵃr m. onomat. the noise made in tearing paper, or the like. Cf. khar-khar, s.v. khar 4.

f. tobogganing down a mountain side (sitting on a sled, or smooth flat stone used as a sled, with the legs straight out in front, and so sliding down). --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to toboggan, as ab. --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf., id. ¶ khᵃra-patᵃjᵃ f. 'a toboggan-mat', the smooth flat stone used as a toboggan in Kashmīr.
in khᵃra-ponzᵃ unmeaning scrawls in imitation of writing, made by untaught children, or the like.
adj. c.g. very much, exceeding, beyond count or measure.

or (f.) khᵃsüñᵃ conj. 1 (1 p.p. khᵒsᵒ), to pluck the hair of the privities, to tear them out with the nails (in obsc. abuse). This verb is also conjugated in the feminine, and is then used in abuse by females one to another (Gr.Gr. 120, 192).
m. the fluff or loose threads from the threads in a loom. Cf. dāri-khᵒ, p. 238a, l. 24, and khᵃʦh.
adj. c.g. (of cloth in the loom) fluffy, see khᵃʦ.
m. (sg. dat. khᵃʦas), a brush used by weavers for clearing off the fluff from the threads on the loom. Cf. khᵃʦ of which this word is probably only a variant spelling.
in khᵒtᵒ-khᵒtᵒ m. onomat. the noise made by a mouse when gnawing.

(also written khiñᵘ̈)  f. the mucus of the nose, the water that runs from the nose (El. khain. The form khiñᵘ̈ is said to be vill.). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. shame or disgrace to be felt, mortification to be experienced, owing to failure to accomplish some impossible task becoming public property; cf. būta- khᵒ, p. 141b, 1. 2. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to expel or pull out the mucus of the nose, to pick one's nose. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause mortification as in --gaʦhüñᵘ̈, ab. -zan adv. like nose-mucus (with reference to any slimy filth, which should be thrown away, or propelled, to a distance). ¶ khᵃñĕ-brôṭᵃ m. a drop of nose-mucus as it issues from the nose. -barith adj. c.g. having a running nose, defiled with nose-mucus, snotty (e.g. a child). -düjᵘ̈ f. nose-mucus-cloth, a handkerchief for wiping the nose. -khāv adj. c.g. a child that eats its own nose-mucus. -lŏponᵘ adj. (f. -lŏpüñᵘ̈), one who is habitually filthy with nose-mucus. -lọ̆ʦhᵘ m. a clot of nose-mucus. -motᵘ adj. (f. -müʦᵘ̈), one whose nose habitually secretes copious mucus. -nŏkorᵘ adj. (f. -nŏkürᵘ̈), a person, esp. a child (boy or girl), with a nostril blocked with mucus. -nakawôrᵘ m. a nostril blocked with mucus; one who has one nostril so blocked. -nostᵘ m. (f. -nüstᵘ̈), a person, esp. a child (boy or girl), whose nose (i.e. both of whose nostrils) is always blocked with mucus, and who consequently speaks in a nasal manner. -nasth f. (sg. dat. -nasti), a nose full of mucus; a woman having such a nose. -nastūrᵘ adj. (f. -nastūrᵘ̈), i.q. -nostᵘ, ab. -shĕrbath f. (sg. dat. -shĕrbüʦᵘ̈), any drink defiled by nose-mucus or similar filth.
f. a fall due to slipping on a smooth or greasy surface, a slip.
(? spelling) m. the cord bending (? binding) the spokes of the large wheel together in the spinning wheel (El.).
m. greatness, grandeur; nobility, eminence; pride, haughtiness (El., K.Pr. 112, Śiv. 324).
m. twisting, see laci-kīcam, s.v. lüṭᵘ̈.
m. the aromatic rhizome or root-stock of the Acorus calamus, or sweet-flag. It is used in medicine as an anti- phlegmatic.

or kīh f. a lump of matted hair pulled out in combing, hair pulled out in combing, the loose hair found in the hand or comb when dressing the hair (El., H. v, 4). The ordinary hair of the head is kīsh, m., q.v. ¶ kīhi-hᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a quantity or mass of hair pulled out at one time by a comb, a lump of combings. -raz f. a rope made of hair combings, a 'switch'. -wāl m. a single hair pulled out in combing.
or kinj f. the cat in the game of tipcat, see loṭhᵘ. The word is a by-form of kijⁱ, q.v.

kijᵘ̈, kījⁱ, or kījᵘ̈ f. a wooden peg or spike (Rām. 435); a peg for tethering cattle; a tent-peg; a small nail, tack, spike, or wedge for fastening anything (cf. ala- kᵒ, p. 23a, l. 34; chāna-kᵒ, p. 162a, l. 13; dāsa-k, p. 252a, l. 9) (K.Pr. 41 kīj, 112 kij; El. kíj). Cf. kyulᵘ. ¶ kiji-khrāv f. a wooden patten with a peg at the fore-end, which is grasped between the toes, and by which the patten is held to the foot. -kū̃shⁱ f. a kind of high-heeled shoe worn in winter, see kū̃shⁱ.

or kaikī or kökī (by Paṇḍits often written kaikayī or kaikēyī, in Sanskrit fashion), f. in Hindū legend, N. of one of the wives of King Daśaratha, Rāmacandra's stepmother, and mother of Bharata. In Sanskrit her N. was 'Kaikēyī'. By her intrigues she procured Rāmacandra's banishment, in order to secure the throne for her own son. She is hence considered a type of all slanderous intriguers. (Rām. 5, 40, 153, 206, 256, 277, 297, etc., always spelt kīkī; obl. form kīkīyĕ, Rām. 82, 148-9, 155, 182, 261, 266, 282, and (m.c.) kīkiyī, Rām. 83).

f. (sg. dat. kili), a nudge, a thrust with the elbow, knee, or the like, to call attention (cf. khŏni-kᵒ, p. 402b, l. 1) (Gr.Gr. 13); a slap with the edge of the open hand (El.); esp. a slap given in the act of sexual intercourse. ¶ kila diñĕ f. pl. inf. to give nudges, to thrust and push (e.g. in making way through a crowd) (K.Pr. 56). ¶ kili-hondᵘ m. born of a blow given in sexual intercourse; hence, as a term of abuse, born of casual or secret intercourse, unlawfully begotten. --kili khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to hurt a person with repeated slaps or cudgellings; to poke over and over again (e.g. to poke a corpse on the funeral pyre to make it burn quickly) (K.Pr. 101).
m. a fort (esp. one on a mountain or eminence), a fortress, castle, citadel, fortification (Gr.M.). I.q. kalāy 1, q.v. There is another kila, pl. of kil, q.v.
(El.), kulmanch (L. 74), kulmānch (L. 79) (? spelling and gender), the Guelder, Viburnum fœtens, a honey flower (L. 74). The word is apparently connected with mã̄ch, honey. Cf. kulāra and kwīllim.
or (Rām. 17) kaimath m. (sg. dat. kīmatas), price, value, worth (K.Pr. 88, Rām. 17). The form kaimath (or kömath) is probably due to confusion with the next.
postpos. indicating motion from; from the direction of, from near (H. v, 7). Cf. kinⁱ.
conj. or, as in suh kina bŏh, he or I (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 82, 121, kih nah; W. 153; YZ. 110, 206; Śiv. 923, 1664; Rām. 280, 289, 445, 450, etc.; H. v, 7; viii, 3, 11; xii, 18, 19, 23).
m. hatred, rancour, malevolence, malice, spite, grudge, resentment, animosity (El. kín and kínah, Rām. 802).

m. (in astrology), the centre of a circle; the first, fourth, seventh, and tenth places in a horoscope (Rām. 144, 1262). kindᵃ̇rᵃ̇ bĕhun m.inf. (of a planet) to be in the centre of its orbit, (?) to be in prime (Śiv. 730, 924).
or kī̃jᵘ̈ f. the cat in the game of tipcat (lȧṭhⁱ kinja loṭhᵘ, L. 464, lat kinch lut, see loṭhᵘ). The word is a by-form of kijⁱ, q.v. kinja is a variant spelling of kinjĕ or kinji.

or occasionally (e.g. Śiv. 1894-5) kin or kȧnⁱ (q.v.) postpos. (cf. kȧnⁱ 3, kani 2, kun, kāñ 2, and kiñ), governing ag. or abl. or occasionally the ag. of the gen. (as in himāla- sȧndⁱ-kinⁱ, Śiv. 728). There does not appear to be any distinction of meaning dependent on the case governed. The word primarily means 'from', as in achiv-kinⁱ, (tears falling) from the eyes (Rām. 284, 482, 1201, 1482); ạndᵃ̇rᵃ̇-kinᵃ̇, from within (p. 32b, l. 17); apörⁱ-kinⁱ, from the far side (p. 39a, l. 42); brü̃ṭhⁱ-kinⁱ, from in front, from before (p. 128b, l. 14) (Gr.Gr. 158); dachinⁱ-kinⁱ, from the right (p. 186a, l. 36) (Gr.Gr. 159), cf. bel.; khōwᵃ̇rᵃ̇-kinᵃ̇, from the left (p. 425b, l. 8) (Gr.Gr. 159); pȧtⁱ-kinⁱ, from behind (path) (Gr.Gr. 159); pĕṭhⁱ-kinⁱ, from above (pĕṭh) (Gr.Gr. 159), but 'upon' in Śiv. 166; thȧjⁱwörī-kin, from Thȧjⁱwôrⁱ (Śiv. 1895); tȧlⁱ-kinⁱ, from below (tal) (Gr.Gr. 159; Rām. 1410, contrasted with hyorᵘ-kun, upwards); wana-kinⁱ, from the forest (Śiv. 1440). ¶ In this sense it is added pleonastically to adverbs already signifying motion from (Gr.Gr. 158) as in ati-kinⁱ, from there, thence; huti-kinⁱ, thence; kati-kinⁱ, whence? tati-kinⁱ, thence; yĕti-kinⁱ, whence (relative); yiti-kinⁱ, hence. ¶ Sometimes it indicates progressive motion, the idea of 'from' being more or less dormant (cf. W. 97, kin, by the side of), as in bŏnⁱ-kinⁱ, below, in the sense of going along the foot of anything (e.g. an embankment) (p. 110b, l. 24); brū̃ṭhⁱ-kinⁱ, not only 'from before', as ab., but also 'ahead', in the sense of going along in front of another person; öbī wati-kinⁱ, (to go) by the water route (Gr.M.); himāla- sȧndⁱ-kinⁱ, via the Himâlaya (Śiv. 728); kōcĕ-kinⁱ, (wandering) through lanes (Rām. 44); khala-kinⁱ, by way of the threshing floor (Śiv. 1476); khŏshkī wati-kinⁱ, (to go) by the land route (p. 419a, l. 20); kŏlav-kinⁱ, (swimming) along the streams (Rām. 620); löriy-kinⁱ, via Lār (Śiv. 1894, so K.Pr. 124, lāri-kinⁱ). ¶ With adverbs of place, it is even used pleonastically, and may altogether lose the root-idea of motion from. Thus, dachinⁱ-kinⁱ, on the right hand (Rām. 856), on the south (cf. ab.) (Rām. 1682); khōwᵃ̇rᵃ̇-kinᵃ̇, on the left (Rām. 421, 856); nĕbȧrⁱ-kinⁱ, on the outside (Rām. 1558); outwardly (Śiv. 764); pachimⁱ-kinⁱ, on the west (Rām. 1681); pūrⁱ-kinⁱ, on the east (Rām. 1681); wŏtȧrⁱ-kinⁱ, on the north (Rām. 1682). Cf. buthⁱ-kinⁱ, face to face, bel. ¶ It sometimes indicates reason or cause, as in ami-kinⁱ or awa-kinⁱ (p. 54b, l. 39; p. 55b, l. 39), for that reason, therefore; zānana-kinⁱ, through knowing (Gr.M.); āsana-kinⁱ, owing to being (so-and-so) (Gr.M.); bē-khabariyi-kinⁱ, owing to neglect (Gr.M.); anubawa-bāwa-kinⁱ, owing to the condition of perception (Śiv. 75, 982); murkha- bö̆zᵘ̈-kinᵘ̈, owing to foolish thought (Śiv. 881); nirmala rǖpa-kinⁱ, owing to (thy) pure form (Śiv. 886). ¶ It often signifies a means or method, as in achiv-kinⁱ, by means of the eyes; hence (to come) as fast as one can see, (to come) at once (Śiv. 717); barau-kinⁱ, (looking) through the doors (Śiv. 958); dāri-kinⁱ, (to go out, or look) through a window (dörᵘ̈ 3) (Gr.M., K.Pr. 254, Rām. 331); akᵃli-kinᵃ, by means of intelligence, to the best of one's intelligence (Rām. 546); kana-kinⁱ, by means of the ears, by hearing (Śiv. 1815); mana-tana-kinⁱ, (knowing) with mind and body (Śiv. 241); myönⁱ-kinⁱ, through, by means of me (Gr.M.); yōga-kinⁱ, by means of ascetic practices (Śiv. 984); zĕvi-kinⁱ, (singing) with the tongue (Śiv. 241). ¶ Like the Hindī sē, it is very often used to form adverbs of manner, as in āgyāyĕ-kinⁱ, according to a command (Śiv. 1051); ạndᵃ̇rᵃ̇-kinᵃ̇, inwardly (as well as 'from the inside') (Śiv. 764); avë̆zᵘ̈-kinᵘ̈, wrongly (p. 71a, l. 7); bakta-bāganāyĕ-kinⁱ, by good fortune (Śiv. 411); buthⁱ-kinⁱ, impudently, audaciously (p. 142b, ll. 10 ff.); face to face (Rām. 152, 920); (falling) on the face (Rām. 5, 8, 926, 1176, 1180, 1201, 1242, 1354); dana-kinⁱ, (to return) like a hockey-ball (p. 222a, l. 38); hence, to retort; darma-kinⁱ, devoutly (p. 244b, l. 20) (Śiv. 428); dayāyĕ-kinⁱ, in a kindly way; as interj. please! have the kindness to (p. 267a, l. 3); hōshĕ-kinⁱ with due care and attention (p. 353a, l. 27), carefully, heedfully (Rām. 1286); lōla-kinⁱ, affectionately (Śiv. 702); kuni-kinⁱ, in some way or other (p. 390a, l. 34) (Rām. 780); mana-kinⁱ, with the mind, with heart and soul (Śiv. 62, 272, 335, 1534); nāwa-kinⁱ, (known) by name (Śiv. 1289); parhēza-kinⁱ, cautiously (parhēz, caution) (Gr.M.); pȧzⁱ-kinⁱ, in truth (Rām. 1149); rāma-rṻpa-kinⁱ, in the person (or in the character) of Rāma (Śiv. 701; so 737, 778); ranga-kinⁱ, in appearance (Śiv. 1366); tawāzau-kinⁱ, politely (tawāza, politeness) (Gr.M.); zarra-kinⁱ, ever so little, hardly at all (zarra, an atom) (YZ. 231).
m. horripilation, the standing on end of the hair and down of the body (from excitement, surprise, terror, etc.), thrilling, a thrill.

f. hire, rent (of a house, a boat, or the like) (El. kiráí; Gr.M.; khar kirāy, hire due for the services of an ass, K.Pr. 104); fare, hire, freight (ḍākücᵘ̈ kirāy, the postage of a letter, Gr.M.). --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to borrow (sic. El.). ¶ kirāyĕ-cīrⁱ f. the document fixing the rent of a house, a lease (Gr.M.). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take on lease or on hire (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to take on hire, in phrases such as nāv chĕh kirāyĕ karüñᵘ̈, a boat must be taken on hire (Gr.M.).
m. (f. kirāyidārĕñ), a lease-holder, the tenant (of a house, etc.) (Gr.M.).
in kīri gaʦhun m.inf. to be full, to be fully supplied, to have everything required; opp. to hīri gaʦhun (p. 345b, l. 33), q.v.
m. a worm. -kash کرم کش m. 'a worm-puller', a rearer of silk worms (L. 367, where it is translated 'worm-killer', as if for kirm- kush or -khash (p. 417b, l. 37).
adj. c.g. crimson-coloured, crimson, scarlet (L. 459, krimsi. In 251, L. calls the colour dark maroon).
(? spelling) f. (?) Ficus carica (El. Ficus caricordes).

adj. c.g. of or belonging to Kirpārām, the boat-loving Sikh Governor of Kashmīr (1825-31). --capa -- m. fancy strokes in rowing, so named by boatmen in honour of Kirpārām (L. 382, kirparámi chappr), and said to have been invented by him. The following are some of these fancy strokes, the rowers all keeping time together:-- the handles of the paddles (capa) are caused to strike the gunwale at every third stroke; the paddles are thrown out as far as possible and noisily smacked flat on the water at the third stroke; or at each third stroke the blade is struck by the hand, or a salaam is made; or the third stroke is made soft and swishing, distinct from the two vigorous strokes that preceded it (see Pioneer Mail for September 30, 1910).
f. mention, report, description (Śiv. 47); celebrating, praising (Śiv. 107).
(? spelling, gender, and number), water insects found in flooded fields (L. 80). The word looks like a plural of some word like kirzᵘ̈. Cf. krṻl 1.
m. 'the pestle that says "kirⁱ-kija", as it goes up and down'; hence, a kind of swing or merry-go-round, in which the seat goes round and round and up and down.
or kisᵘ̈ f. the little, or fifth, finger of the hand (cf. atha-kisᵘ̈, p. 59b, l. 3) (Gr.Gr. 13; K.Pr. 17; Siv. 701, 994, 1392; K. 326-7); the little toe (El.).
m. the filament of a lotus or other plant. Cf. nāga-kᵒ, s.v. nāg 2.

m. (pl. ag. kēshau, Rām. 402; kīshĕv, K. 33), hair (on the head or on the body); esp. a long tress of hair, hair in long tresses (Śiv. 1704, 1725; Rām. 183, 402; K. 33); a ringlet (El.); cf. kih. kīshĕ-hüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -hacĕ), a long fillet or braid of hair; esp. the double long braid worn by women commencing at the forehead, going over the head to the back of the neck, and then hanging down. Cf. hüṭᵘ̈.
or kishĕmish f. a small dried grape without stones, a sultana raisin, currant (Gr.M.).
in kishmishī dach, a kind of grape growing in Kashmīr (El., s.v. dach). Cf. the preceding.
f. a beggar's wallet or cup (El.; K.Pr. 15; L. 457, 458).
or kᵃsm m. kind, sort, species (El.); used in the genitive, as in gurun chuh aki kisamücᵘ̈ göḍᵘ̈, the gurun is a kind of fish (W. 123).
or kᵃsa m. a tale, story, narration (El.).
f. a book (El.; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 166; W. 13; H. x, 11). -lēkhanwôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -lēkanwājĕñ), a clerk, a writer (El.).
m. thin, lean, spare (by nature, not by disease) (esp. of children).
m. (sg. dat. kīṭas), a worm, an insect.
m. a kind of bird, resembling the domestic fowl in appearance and voice; a kind of rat (cf. an-kitȧrⁱ, p. 29b, l. 30).
f. a small potsherd. Cf. katᵘ̈rᵘ̈.
m. a thorn or foreign particle in the eye; a stye or ulcer in the eye (believed to be caused by such).
m. loneliness, orphanhood; the condition of having no relations or connexions by marriage.
conj. corruption of the Pers. ki کہ, that. Often added pleon. to hargāh, if (H. viii, 7, 13). Cf. hargāh.
m. (sg. dat. kiyāmatas قیامتس), the resurrection, the last day (K.Pr. 214); confusion, tumult, uproar, an extra- ordinary to-do (K.Pr. 206).
m. pain, torment, affliction (L.V. 80). --karun -- m.inf. to cause affliction (to, dat.) (L.V. 51).

or ku, a prefix implying deterioration, depreciation, deficiency, want, littleness, hindrance, reproach, contempt, guilt, or the like. It is a Sanskrit prefix, but in Kāshmīrī it appears not only prefixed to borrowed Sanskrit words, but also to pure Kāshmīrī ones. Words to which this prefix is added will be found below in their proper alphabetical order.

f. a bad bone; met. the bone of some wretched fellow fit only to be beaten, or of some low fellow fit only to carry burdens, or the like, as in amis chuh kŏ-aḍijᵘ̈, he has a bad bone, i.e. he is not worth anything but a beating or to put to bearing burdens.
m. a long-prepared opportunity for bringing another under subjection, the successful climax of such a preparation.
(? spelling) f. a sheath, scabbard (El. kómb), i.q. kȧmbⁱ, q.v.
m. (sg. dat. -bāzanas), a worthless vessel or utensil; met. a totally unworthy person.
m. hunchbackedness, the condition of being humpbacked.
adv. in an evil work, in bad conduct, u.w. vbs. signifying expenditure, or the like.
adj. capable, able, clever, skilful, competent; a fit or competent person, an able man, etc. (Rām. 1302).
m. N. of ạ certain medicinal plant, used as a cure for herpes.
adj. c.g. of or belonging to Kābul, the capital of Afghānistān. --phrasth -- m. a kind of poplar (L. 81).

m. (sg. dat. kôbulas), the city of Kābul, the capital of Afghānistān; the country of Afghānistān, which in K. is treated as equivalent to the Kāmbōja of Sanskrit literature (K. 578, 582, 586, 619 ff.).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. kŏbyōv), to become hunchbacked (from disease, accident, old age, or the like).
adj. (f. kŏbᵘ̈rᵘ̈), one who has become hunchbacked (by disease, or the like, and who was not born so). Cf. kọ̆bᵘ 2.

N. of a certain astronomical period in the month of Öshid (Skr. Āśvina = Septr.-Oct.) during which the sun is in Virgo (it corresponds to the Sanskrit Kāmāri-pakṣa, for which, see bel.); hence, the spring crops (wheat, barley, etc.) usually sown in this period. ¶ kö̃bari-kāh m. the timely rain (kāh 2) that falls during this period, and after which the spring crops are sown (L. 328, kámbar ká). -pach m. N. of this period, in Sanskrit Kāmāri-pakṣa. It is the dark half of the luni-solar month of Öshid (see ab.). During it, not only are the spring crops sown, but also offerings are made by Hindūs to their deceased ancestors (L. 266, Kambar pach). -shrād m. the oblation (Sanskrit śrāddha) offered by Hindūs to deceased ancestors during this period.
m. bad seed, that which (in the case of a plant) produces inferior seedlings, or which (in the case of a man) produces evil offspring. ¶ kŏbyālyukᵘ adj. (f. kŏbyālicᵘ̈), born of a bad seed.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kọ̆bᵃrôwᵃ), to make hunchbacked (by a blow, or the like); to make an inanimate object humped (e.g. to make the trunk of a tree crooked).
m. a hump on the back, hump-backedness (K. 428).

adj. (f. kö̆bᵘ̈), hump-backed (K. 427); a hunchback, esp. one born so (K.Pr. 116); crooked (El. kŏb); cf. kŏburᵘ. --kulᵘ -- m. a hunchback tree, a tree with a crooked trunk. Such tree is easily climbed and is the rendezvous for this purpose of all the children of the neighbourhood; hence, met. an under-servant, who is the fag and drudge of all the upper servants, and who never has a moment's peace (see K.Pr. 116 for the origin of the metaphor).

or (H. iv, 7) kabar f. a grave, a tomb, esp. a Musalmān's tomb (as in K.Pr. 22) (K.Pr. 138 kabrí). -wö̆bᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f., id. (El. kabar-wabar). ¶ kö̆bᵃrĕ wālun m.inf. to cause to descend into a tomb, to inter (H. iv, 7, kabari).
. Add 'In wū̃ṭa-kᵒ, kö̆bᵘ̈rᵘ̈ is used met. for "a camel's hump" (p. 1159b, l. 47)'.

(often spelt kōcĕ 1, see art. C) m. a lane, an alley, a narrow road between houses (YZ. 40, 253; Śiv. 1466, 1625, 1849; Rām. 44), a shopless street (El. kóchih); an alley leading to a house (L. 462). -phyurᵘ m. alley-wandering; hence, losing one's way in the lanes of a town; met. losing one's way in some complicated business, losing the thread of an argument, or the like.
m. an evilly behaved person, one of bad conduct, one of evil or corrupt life, one who is immoral.

f. (sg. dat. kŏchi, often written kŏchĕ), the lap, the lower part of the bosom (where babies are carried or dandled) (K.Pr. 174, 227; YZ. 141; Śiv. 1549; K. 94, 158, 341, 469; L.V. 70). ¶ kŏchi (or kŏchĕ) hyonᵘ (or) m.inf. to take or carry in the bosom or lap (Śiv. 377, 1381, 1401). -kĕth adv. in the bosom (e.g. with verbs of carrying or embracing) (Śiv. 1357, 1542; Rām. 665, 928, 1522; K. 161). -pĕṭhukᵘ adj. (f. -pĕṭhücᵘ̈), of on the lap, (of a child much fondled) a mother's darling.
adj. c.g. big-bellied, corpulent, large-bodied, full-bodied (only with reference to animate beings). Cf. kōch (Gr.Gr. 133).
m. a tortoise. (The Sanskrit translation, however, means 'crocodile'. This word is perhaps the same as the kuchu of L. 381, see kuchu).
or kŏ-cỗṭhᵘ adj. (f. -cö̃ṭᵘ̈ or -cö̃ṭhᵘ̈), foul-lipped, foul-mouthed; one who habitually uses foul abuse; as subst. a foul, dirty lip. Cf. cỗṭᵘ.
adj. (f. kücᵘ̈), unripe, raw, green; (of food) raw, uncooked, insufficiently cooked; immature, crude; unfinished, imperfect, incomplete; rude, rough, sketchy; built of unbaked bricks, built of mud.
m. the collar of the long cotton coat (phēran) worn by Kāshmīrīs. It is a separate piece of stuff cut to shape the neck and sewn on to the body of the garment.

or kaid قید m. imprisonment; a prison; hence, as adj. imprisoned (Gr.M.). -khān (H.) or -khāna قید خانہ m. a prison (Gr.M.; Rām. 587, 684; H. v, 7, 8). --karun -- m.inf. to imprison (H. v, 7, 9; x, 5, 12). --lagun -- m.inf. to become imprisoned (H. v, 8; vi, 11).

f. a kiln; a potter's kiln (Rām. 1446; H. xi, 11); a brick-kiln (Śiv. 1033); a lime-kiln. -bal m. the place where a kiln is erected, a brick or potter's kiln (Gr.Gr. 165). --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a kiln to arise; met. to become like such a kiln (which contains no imperfectly baked articles, but only well-made perfectly baked ones), hence, a collection of good ('pucka') articles or qualities to exist. Cf. Śiv. 1033, where the causal form of the verb is used.
m. (sg. dat. ködakas), a wrapper of paper, or the like, for containing loose leaves, such as those of a weakly-bound book, or the like.
(? spelling) m. the tail feathers of the nīlyujᵘ (q.v.) bird. They are worn by Persian and Hindōstānī women (El. konḍal; cf. also El. s.v. nílúj).
m. an evil body, a vile body, (this) vile body (in self-depreciation) (L.V. 7).
adj. potent, powerful, mighty; a common Musalmān N.P. ködir-i-mutlakh قآدر مطلق m. the Omnipotent, the Almighty, N. of God (Musalmān) (Gr.M.).
m. an evil day, an unlucky day, an inauspicious day (W. 110).
adj. c.g. ill-formed, misshapen, ungainly, ugly.
f. (sg. dat. kŏdrüʦᵘ̈), power, ability, authority; esp. God's power, omnipotence (El., Gr.M., Śiv. 602).

also spelt kuḍur, kŏḍurᵘ, or kuḍurᵘ 1 m. (sg. dat. kŏḍaras), the small hard seed of a grape or similar fruit. ¶ kŏḍar m.pl. of the ab., met. audacity, hard-heartedness, and other blameworthy qualities of soul (as distinct from external defects).
m. the brain. Cf. köḍⁱ. ¶ köḍⁱ-al f. N. of a kind of pumpkin.

m. one who cleans seeds from raw cotton, a cotton-cleaner; a cotton carder (El. káḍhí) (L.V. 102). ¶ köḍⁱ-bāy f. a cotton-cleaner's wife; a woman who lives by cleaning cotton. -yĕndᵃr m. the machine used for extracting seeds from raw cotton.
f. (for 2, 3, see kôḍᵘ 1, 2), the brain; cf. kôḍᵘ 1. --tārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to extract the brain, to knock out a person's brains (in a fight, or as a capital punishment, etc.).

m. a mountain (Śiv. 63, 202, 206, 252, 422, 1392; Rām. 96, 205, 400, 443-4, etc.); a range of mountains (El. koh, i.e. kōh). ¶ kŏha-dāmān (= دامان کوہ) m. the foot or declivity of a mountain. -kŏhai, adv. on every mountain, from mountain to mountain (H. ix, 2). -lüṭᵘ̈ f. 'the tail of a mountain', a hill at the foot of a mountain range; any small hill.
m. a mountain, i.q. kŏh, q.v. (Gr.M., K.Pr. 78, 114, 161, 262; W. 156; YZ. 89; Rām. 375, 439, 746, 1337), with Persian iẓāfat, kōh-i (Śiv. 648, 823; Rām. 937). kōh-i-tōra, Mount Sinai (H. iv, 5).
a form of kū̃h, see kē̃h, used in the comp. kō̃h-kṻtⁱ, how many? or how many! (Rām. 690). Cf. kũh kus, etc., s.v. kē̃h.
f. a gift, or present (offered or received, when a person visits or pays his respects to a prince or other person of high rank), a naẕrāna.
m. a mountainous region, a highland, forest (El., Rām. 523).
f. habitual practice of any vile or repulsive occupation. Cf. hāl 6.
ord. (f. köhimᵘ̈), eleventh (Gr.Gr. 76, Rām. 1158, f.). Musalmāns commonly employ the form kahyumᵘ. Cf. kāh 1.
adj. c.g. crooked, distorted, awry; (of a person's nature) crooked.

card. the form which kāh 1, eleven, takes in the arithmetical process of multiplication, as in bāh köhⁱ akh hath ta dŏyĕtrᵃh, twelve elevens (are) a hundred and thirty-two. This word can only be used with numerals above ten (Gr.Gr. 86).
in koi kok (? spelling and gender), a turnip-rooted Umbellifer (L. 71, eaten in times of famine). ? Cf. kyovᵘ.

m. (sg. ag. köjⁱ 1, abl. kāji 1), the morning meal, breakfast (Gr.Gr. 157, K.Pr. 104); the hour of the morning meal, about 4 1/2 hours after sunrise (K.Pr. 176), the fore- noon. Cf. aḍ-kôjᵘ, p. 10a, l. 32; khanḍawāv- kôjᵘ, p. 403a, l. 27; i.q. cāsht, q.v. (El. also kanj). --khyāwun -- m.inf. to cause to eat the morning meal, to give breakfast (to), esp. (when owing to a death in a family, the members fast by eating only once a day, in the evening) to cause the members of a family to break such a fast by inducing them to take the morning meal. kāji-kāla adv. both at the morning meal and at the evening meal, both at breakfast and at supper (there being only two meals a day); cf. kāla-kāji, s.v. kāl 1. -pȧtⁱ adv. after the time of the morning meal, after the early forenoon. ¶ köjⁱ-bata m. the food eaten at the morning meal; the morning meal itself, breakfast. -gāsa m. the early morning meal of grass, or the like, given to cattle. -samay m., i.q. -wakth, bel. (K. 204). -wakth m. (sg. dat. -waktas), the time of the morning-meal, breakfast-time. -waktan adv. at the time of the morning meal, at breakfast time. -waktas adv., id. ¶ köjis adv. at the hour of the morning meal, at breakfast time (u.w. vbs. of coming, going, or the like) (El. also kanjis). -bögⁱ or -bögin adv., id., but more indefinite, at about breakfast time. ¶ kājyukᵘ adj. (f. kājicᵘ̈), of or belonging to, or produced at the time of the morning meal (i.e. in the forenoon).

or köjᵘ̈ 1 f. (sg. abl. kāji 2, for 3, see s.v.), a slab, a flat stone; esp. a flat stone on which sandal-wood, condiments, or the like, are ground with a muller (K. 151). kāji-tīl m. a kind of medicinal oil, ground out of medicaments on such a slab. It is used as a remedy for skin diseases. -waṭh m. (sg. dat. -waṭas), the stone muller used with the above grinding slab (El. kájiwat or kájwaṭ) (K.Pr. 60, 112, 114, 148).
f. (sg. dat. kŏ-küjᵘ̈), evil longing, vicious desire. kŏ-küjᵘ̈ adv. with an evil longing, with desires fixed on or exercised in evil objects or occupations.

m. a method of wearing the hair, esp. adopted by prostitutes and the like. It is described as tying the hair across the upper part of the forehead, and letting it hang down each cheek in a ringlet (El. translates 'a ringlet, a lock of hair'). Cf. kōkh and kakav.

f. a gold or silver bracelet or armlet. Cf. kö̃kun. ¶ kö̃kañĕ-mast m. a woman's hair when naturally curling. -worᵘ m. a kind of small cake, made out of the little amount of flour left over when baking a number of cakes or loaves, and indicating that the tale of loaves is complete.
also kō̃kawun conj. 1 (1 p.p. kō̃kanôwᵘ), to praise (one person to another), to recommend (a person).
m. an evil action, a wicked deed (W. 110, Śiv. 19, K. 12); an unlucky action; (amongst Hindūs) an evil action done in a former birth, resulting in unhappiness or misfortune in the present life.
adj. c.g. one who suffers from an unhappy fate owing to actions done in a former birth (Śiv. 423). See 1.
adj. c.g. an evil doer, a sinner (Rām. 52).
m. the sound of a cock-crowing or any similar inarticulate meaningless sound (Śiv. 1814).
f. (sg. dat. -kathi), an ill word, a word that should not be spoken, an abusive or indecent expression.
m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a bad son, one, who by bad conduct, is a disgrace to his parents and family (Gr.Gr. 132).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kō̃kowᵘ), i.q. kō̃kanāwun, q.v.
m. (of a human being) an evil nature, a bad disposition.

m. (sg. dat. kōkas), fine outward appearance (due to dress, ornaments, etc.). --cārun -- m.inf. to 'tie up' one's dress, to arrange one's dress, etc., to dress oneself up; esp. to arrange or tie up the hair, etc. Cf. kōkala.
m. an impure vulva, one belonging to a habitually unchaste and depraved woman. ¶ kŏ-khaḍyukᵘ adj. (f. -khaḍicᵘ̈), one born from such, one utterly vile and baseborn.
f. used in the gen. kŏ-kili-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), born of unlawful (incestuous) sexual intercourse; used in abuse. Cf. kil.
(? spelling), the Kashmīr Pucras Pheasant, Pucrasia biddulphi (L. 120).

adj. (f. -köjᵘ̈), of or belonging to an evil time, born or produced at an evil or ill-omened time. ¶ kŏkölⁱ adv. at an evil or ill-omened time. --warshun -- m. (sg. dat. --warshĕnas --), rain at an evil time, untimely rain; met. the production or appearance of anything at an ill or awkward time (whether the thing is desired or not).
adj. (f. kŏ-kömᵘ̈), one who does evil deeds, wicked, sinful (Rām. 1776).

kŏkur, or (Gr.Gr. 58) kŏkurᵘ m. (pl. nom. kŏkar; f. sg. nom. kŏkürᵘ̈), a cock (the barn- door fowl) (K.Pr. 221); a fowl (K.Pr. 117, 236); a kind of round white pebbles used by little girls as a toy (in this sense employed in the plur.); fem. a hen (El. kŏhir; K.Pr. 117, 163, kukĕr; Śiv. 1814). ¶ kŏkar-bã̄g f. the crowing of a cock; cock-crow, early morning (El., K.Pr. 176). -bã̄gi adv. at cockcrow, at dawn (El.). -bövᵘ̈ f. a fowl's thigh; hence, the thick flesh off the side of a fowl. -dō̃ka-dō̃kh or -dō̃kha-dō̃kh f. (sg. dat. -dō̃ka-dō̃ki), the mutual pecking of cocks, cock-fighting. -gām m. a fowl-village, a village in which fowls are reared, or in which the inhabitants make a speciality of rearing fowls (H. xi, 8). -kun (? spelling and gender), fowl cholera (L. 366). -morᵘ m. a fowl-house (cf. K.Pr. 240). -māz m. fowl's flesh (a word principally used by Musalmāns). -nāg m. N. of a fountain in Pargana Bring (the Sanskrit Kukkuṭēśvara (El. Kukir Nāg, RT.Tr. II, 469 Kukᵃr Nāg). -pūtᵘ m. (f. -pūʦᵘ̈), a chicken (Gr.Gr. 131). -tīrᵘ̈ f. a fowl's feather. -tīrĕ lāgañĕ f. pl. inf. to apply fowl's feathers; met. to put a person to shame, to make him an object of blame by bringing a charge of some fault (esp. when undeserved). -tīrĕ yiñĕ f. pl. inf. fowl's feathers to come; met. to be reduced to poverty. -zang f. a fowl's leg; standing on one leg (like a fowl). ¶ kŏkürᵘ̈ f. a hen. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to calumniate, to make a person an object of blame (esp. when undeserved).
adj. (f. -körᵘ̈), (of an animate object) ill-shaped, ugly.

m. a bracelet inkö̃kan-band m. the tying on of the bracelet; esp. at a Hindū sacrifice the ceremonial tying on, by the sacrificing priest, of a red thread round the right fore-arm of the sacrificer, and of another round the left fore-arm of the sacrificer's wife. Cf. kö̃kañ.
in kọ̆kᵘ-mọ̆kᵘ m. contraction or drawing together all one's limbs, and drawing one's garments tight round one (e.g. under the influence of cold or of great fear).
adj. c.g. an ill-natured tattler, one who habitually goes about saying unpleasant things. Cf. kīkī.

m. a race, a family, stock (Śiv. 1322; K. 379, 467, 604). In Śiv. 1536 manz kŏla is translated by the Sanskrit saṁsāra-madhyāt, (I shall escape) from existence in the world (?) as if kŏl were used met. for the whole family of mankind. -aḍijᵘ̈ f. bone of a (good) family; hence, good stock, as in kŏl-aḍijĕ- hünzᵘ̈ kūrᵘ̈, a girl of a good stock. -akŏl m. family and no family, the entire universe comprised in two categories, (1) those things which can be conceived as existing in groups or families, and (2) those things which cannot be so conceived (L.V. 2). -cĕmākh کل چماق m.
