(sg. dat. -cĕmākhas), a habitual or professional sharper, swindler, cheat. -kūrᵘ̈ f. a girl of family; hence, a virtuous maiden of good stock. -kōrĕ-yĕhānath کل کورہ اہانت f. the disdain shown by a girl of high family; met. the insulted feeling experienced by a child under instruction, even when he is being instructed by his elders and betters, the sulkiness of an unwilling pupil. -mŏl m. (sg. abl. kŏla-mŏla, cf. kŏla-mŏla- rostᵘ, bel.), family and money-value, family and property (the two things considered in arranging a marriage). -nāshukh m. (sg. dat. -nāshĕkas), a destroyer of a family, a bad son who brings disgrace on his family. -pŏtᵃr or -pŏthᵃr m. (sg. dat. -pŏtras), one who is born of excellent stock of high rank and repute. -rīth f. (sg. dat. -rīʦᵘ̈), the traditional customs of a family. -tārukh m. (sg. dat. -tārakas), the saviour or restorer of a family, a good son of high repute and of good stock, who by his virtuous acts, or by clearing off his ancestral debts, is an honour to his family. ¶ kŏla-dīph m. the lamp, or glory, of a family (Śiv. 1536). -gātukh m. (sg. dat. -gātakas), the murderer of a family; a man of good stock, who ruins or disgraces his family. -kalankh c.g. (sg. dat. -kalankas), a stain on a family; one of respectable stock who disgraces his family by sinful practices, or the like. -kshĕy m. the total destruction of a family, the wiping out of a family. -mŏla-rostᵘ adj. (f. -mŏla-rüʦhᵘ̈), without family and money-value, of low stock and poor (u.w. reference to a person whom one is considering as a possible bride or bridegroom; see kŏl-mŏl, ab.). -mār m. a kind of serpent, whose bite is said to be so deadly that not only does the person bitten die, but also his whole family. -nāsh m. destruction of a family; also i.q. kŏla-mār.

f. (sg. dat. kŏli 1), a river, a stream, a brook (cf. chaʦa-kŏl) (K.Pr. 103, 114; W. 149; L. 457 kulih, dat.; YZ. 407; Śiv. 1023, 1569; Rām. 42, 620; H. xii, 2, 4; K. 563); an artificial stream, canal, irrigation channel (cf. dāra- kᵒ, p. 235a, l. 30) (L. 464); met. a stream or flow of something other than water (cf. dyāra-kŏla, m., p. 270b, l. 28). El. kŏl, kúl, and kwŏl. ¶ kŏla-obujⁱ f. a variety of the plant obujⁱ (q.v.) which grows in streams. -budij f. a kind of rice with a fragrant white soft grain; cf. mŏshka- budij, s.v. mŏshᵉ̆kh. -bal m. ground near a river or stream (cf. bal 3). -boṭhᵘ m. the bank of a river (Rām. 1007). -buzⁱ adj. c.g. dependent on a river, become part of a river, merged in a river (e.g. something fallen into it, or someone who has plunged into it) (cf. buzⁱ). -ganḍ m. 'tying up a channel', stopping the flow of water through an irrigation channel in order to divert the stream in some desired direction. -grazun m. the roar or noise made by the current of a river or stream (e.g. when it strikes some impediment to its flow). -gŏta m. bathing in a stream or canal; falling accidentally into such; met. falling accidentally into any water. -gŏta lagȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. tumblings into water to occur; met. to be distraught, full of perturbation, agitated (from sorrow, anxiety, abuse given by another, or similar cause). -hö̃giñ f. a fresh-water shell, the shell of a fresh-water bivalve. -hūñᵘ̈ f. a kind of water-animal said to resemble a leech (the Sanskrit durnāmā apparently means 'cockle'). -kŏlur m. the Blue-winged Teal or Garganey, Querquedula circia (L. 130, kulkilar). -kôwᵘ m. a kind of bird resembling a crow which haunts small streams and water-channels. -nöyid m. a kind of fresh-water crab. -phȧṭⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to die by drowning (mostly used in curses). -ṭū̃cᵘ m. a kind of long-billed fish-eating bird, which haunts river banks. -tār m. the act of jumping or stepping across a small brook or water-channel. -ṭyū̃ṭᵘ m. a certain bird, ? a lapwing. -wŏdᵒrᵒ m. a river-otter. -wān m. the spring-clearing of a river or canal by removing the mud, etc., that has accumulated in the winter (L. 461 in atilkulwān, 464; Śiv. 239). ¶ kŏli dörith dyunᵘ m.inf. to fling into the river; met. to cast away, get rid of (K.Pr. 76). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go into the river; to fall into a river (K.Pr. 8, 192, 224, 263); met. to become useless, ineffectual. --kŏli khasun -- m.inf. to go upstream along the bank of a river, to walk upstream (H. xii, 4). -kun adv. to or towards the river, in the direction of a river, etc. (u.w. vbs. of motion) (Gr.Gr. 161). -ʦhunun m.inf. to throw into a river (K.Pr. 114, 146; Rām. 352, 1037, 1587-8); met. to make fruitless, to make ineffectual (an action or thing). -wŏṭh f. (sg. dat. -wŏṭi), a jump into a river; esp. a jump into a river in order to commit suicide, throwing oneself into a river.
m. a cup (YZ. 130). Cf. dŏda-kōl, p. 189a, l. 49.
m. N. of a well-known village in the Divᵃsar (Skr. Dēvasaraḥ) Pargana of Kashmīr. The workmen there are said to be the cleverest in the Valley (K.Pr. 94).
adj. c.g. of or belonging to, or produced in the village of Kŏlagômᵘ. --ḍaba m. name of a special kind of casket made in Kŏlagômᵘ.
onomat. ? gend. the sound of calling or summoning (Rām. 677). Cf. kal 5.
m. a man who habitually has sexual intercourse with his own daughter.

m. N. of a lake in Kashmīr visited by Hindū pilgrims on their way to Harmŏkh (p. 343a, l. 31), q.v. In Sanskrit it is called Kaulasaras. The pilgrims throw money into it as they pass by (Śiv. 1177, 1892).
adj. c.g. shrewd, cunning, crafty; malicious; (in Kāshmīrī) one who habitually gains or attains his or her object solely by his own cleverness, a Machiavel.

f. a wife (K.Pr. 13, 59, 70, 132, 147; W. 16; H. iii, 4; v, 3, 5, 9; viii, 3, 11; K. 685, 699). ¶ kŏlayĕ-buzy or kŏlayi-buzy adj. c.g. one who is dependent on a wife, i.e. who has only one relation, viz. a wife (see buzⁱ, p. 153a, l. 30) (Gr.Gr. 161); as adv. (u.w. vbs. of going, etc.) entirely under one's wife's orders (whether owing to her personality, or to her holding the purse-strings). -grünzᵘ̈aʦun m.inf. to become extremely subservient to someone, in order to get a desired object. -mahanyuvᵘ m. a wife's man, one who is always by his wife's side; one who customarily follows his wife's advice in business matters, etc.; one who is a henpecked husband. -motᵘ m. 'a wife-madman', i.e. one who through love for his wife neglects his business, etc., one who is uxorious. -pônᵘ m. acting like a wife, being very subservient, humble obedience. -tônᵘ m., id. -yozᵘ m. one who is uxoriously subservient to his wife. A yozᵘ is a fool who wears his outer garments as inner garments, and vice versa.

in the following: kŏlaʦh wöjᵘ̈ वा॑जू॒। दायविशेषः f. a ring given by a bride's parents to their son-in-law when she first goes to her husband's house. It is used there as a kind of guide or omen for the auspicious helping of food; cf. kŏluʦhᵘ. -wörᵘ̈ f. an earthen dish in which the hands are washed after helping food (which is done with the unaided hand), a finger-bowl.
(for 1, see kŏl 2) in kŏli-vĕṭhⁱ kshĕ m. the name given in schools to the Śāradā or Nāgarī compound letter kṣa.
f. a mouthful of water used for rinsing the mouth (Śiv. 836).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. kōlyōv), (of food) to become browned by roasting, frying, or the like. Cf. kūlᵘ.
m. a kind of Shrike, ? Lanius erythronotus, the Rufous-backed Shrike (cf. L. 149).
m. a kind of bird, the bald coot, Fulica atra (L. 122, kolar).
m. N. of a kind of river fish. The word is said to be very rare.
the dividing out of cooked rice, condiments, etc.; helping or distributing food; met. taking out or putting back, etc., any collection of articles. Cf. kŏlaʦh.
or kŏlyūnᵘ adj. (f. kŏliñᵘ̈ or kŏlīñᵘ̈), of good family, of high birth; (of an animal) of good breed.

adj. (f.kȧjⁱ or küjᵘ̈ 2; spelt kaj in K.Pr. 92, 239; for küjᵘ̈ 1, see kal 1), dumb, mute (cf. aḍa-kolᵘ, p. 11a, l. 36) (Gr.Gr. 9; Gr.M. 93; L.V. 20, 86; YZ. 436; Rām. 1207). ¶ küjᵘ̈ adj. f. dumb, a dumb woman (K.Pr. 239). Used as the proper name of a certain dumb woman (K.Pr. 92, kaj, mis-translated 'deaf'). --bahāth -- (cf. بہات) f. (sg. dat. bahöʦᵘ̈), a false calumny, a false accusation against a person's character. The connexion of this compound with kolᵘ is doubtful. Cf. kaj 1 and kal 1. ¶ kȧlⁱ-mọ̆nḍⁱ adj. (f. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈), one who is habitually silent, one who never has a word to say, one who sits silent (either from want of education or from natural disposition) amid general conversation, one who is taciturn. ¶ kalis ḍolᵘ m. one who, though he hears, pretends not to hear. Cf. ḍalun 1.

adj. (f. köjᵘ̈), the form which kāl 1 takes when used adjectivally and --˚. It follows kāl 1 in all its meanings. Examples are okᵘ-kôlᵘ, one who eats only once a day (p. 19a, l. 15); yüʦᵘ̈- kôlᵘ, of or belonging to a long time ago (H. ii, 4); rĕta-kôlᵘ m. the hot-season, summer (Śiv. 327). harda-kôlᵘ, of or belonging to winter (see kölⁱ, bel.). ¶ kāli 3 adv. (for 1, see kāl 2, for 2, see s.v.), at such and such a time, used --˚, as in brō̃ṭh-kāli, in former times (p. 128a, l. 15); path-kāli, in former times (L.V. 91; K. 240); path-kāli pĕṭha, from olden times (till now) (Śiv. 1653). -hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of at such and such a time, used --˚, as in brō̃ṭh-kāli-hondᵘ, of or belonging to former times; of or belonging to the beginning, initial (p. 128a, l. 16). ¶ kölⁱ 2 adv. (for 1, see kāl 2), in the course of time, at some time (either past or future), at some time or other (K.Pr. 207; Śiv. 527, 1020; Rām. 247, 1602); at (the right) time (Gr.Gr. 157, Rām. 1676); at the appointed time, at the destined moment (L.V. 74); --˚ at such and such a time, as in brō̃ṭh-kölⁱ (with vb. in a past tense) in former times, at the beginning; (with a vb. in a future tense) in future times, in the future (L.V. 92) (cf. brō̃ṭh-kᵒ, p. 128a, l. 19; harᵃda-kᵃ, in the autumn, p. 348a, l. 11) (K.Pr. 30, YZ. 534); yüʦᵘ̈-kᵘ̈, for a long time (Śiv. 343); kē̃h-kᵒ, after some time (K. 624, 734). -kālas adv. sometimes, now and then (Śiv. 165). ¶ kālyukᵘ adj. (f.kālicᵘ̈), of at such and such a time, used --˚, as in brō̃ṭh-kālyukᵘ, existing or born in former times, old fashioned (p. 128a, l. 20).
bent, crooked, etc., in holᵘ-kolᵘ, see holᵘ. Cf. kaj 1.
in hāha-kôlᵘ or hahā-kôlᵘ, see p. 324a, l. 43.
adj. (f. köjᵘ̈ 3), black. Cf. kāla 2. With emph. y, kôluy, see dŏd, p. 188a, l. 40.

f. an armful, as much space as there is inside the bent arms joined together at the fingers (Śiv. 1849, K. 720). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to lift up (some weighty object) by embracing it with the arms (Rām. 926). ¶ kŏma karañĕ f. pl. inf. to make armfuls, i.e. to earn a great quantity of anything.
m. a tribe, race, family, sect, caste (K.Pr. 260, W. 141, kaum); kōm-ĕ-Marwān, the tribe of Marwān (a dirtily clothed wandering lot) (K.Pr. 142).
m. one who is mean, despicable, unworthy of respect.
the Hindū pronunciation of kömᵘ̈, q.v.
adv. with an evil mind, with evil intention; with an angry mind.
c.g. a youth (m. or f.) used --˚ in rāza-kumār, a prince (Śiv. 1290) or a princess (Śiv. 971, 1285); as a portion of N.P. danishṭh-kŏmār (Rām. 572, 593).

m. N.P. of the Hindū god of war, called in Skt. Kumāra, Kārttikēya, Skanda, or Subrahmaṇyā. He is said to have been the son of Śiva and Pārvatī, and to be the leader of the gaṇas or hosts of Śiva (Śiv. 1278, 1581). ¶ kŏmāra-brôrᵘ m., i.q. kŏmār 2. -jī m., id. (Śiv. 517). -shēṭh f. (sg. dat. shīṭhᵘ̈), the sixth lunar day of the bright half of any month, esp. that of Hār (= June-July, Skt. Āṣāḍha), on which women who desire sons fast in honour of Kumāra (the Skt. Kumāraṣaṣṭhī).
m. (sg. dat. kāmatas), height, stature (El. kāmat) (Rām. 520). Cf. the preceding.

or kŏmakh کمک m. (sg. dat. kŏmbakas), help, aid, assistance (El. kumbak; Rām. 734; H. xi, 7); reinforcement (of an army, etc.); association of villagers for any particular joint object, assembly en masse of the inhabitants of the village for such (L. 458, kumak).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kọ̆mbᵘ), (amongst Hindūs) to suppress, or do away with (some impediment to religious welfare) by means of the kumbhaka meditation (L.V. 75). See kumbᵘ 1.
m. the fore-end of the sleeve of a garment, the cuff. (It is made of a separate piece of material.) ¶ kȧmbⁱ-chal f. the piece of cloth of which the cuff is made. -wār m., id.
adv. with an evil face; with a face distorted (by anger, or the like).

often written kumörī f. a maiden, a virgin, older than seven, and younger than twelve years; a girl, a daughter (El. komārī) (Śiv. 37, 939, 945; Rām. 127, 137, 1220); a princess (Rām. 734, 1637, 1692). rāza-kŏmörī, a king's daughter, a princess (Śiv. 577, 630, 961, 1218, 1224, 1362, 1517).

m. orkö̆mᵘ̈ f. m. the fine bran produced from the husks of the grain when paddy is pounded for the purpose of decortication (Śiv. 702, kö̆mᵘ̈, so K. 1118, 1143 ff.); chaff (El., K.Pr., kum) (K.Pr. 204). ¶ kö̆mᵘ̈-ṭaṭhȧjᵘ̈ or -ṭaṭhüjᵘ̈ f. the wooden trough from which cows are fed with this bran. -ʦŏcĕ f.pl. cakes made of this bran (K.Pr. 103). -worᵘ m. a kind of thick round cake made of this bran. -yöjᵘ̈ f. another kind of cake made of the same (K.Pr. 3, 190).

f. (Hindūs generally write this word, and pronounce it kōm, cf. gōvᵘ̈, p. 316a, l. 31. Examples are Śiv. 1237; Rām. 469, 687; K. 89, 265), a work, action, deed (K.Pr. 64, K. 360); work, labour (K.Pr. 106, 114); a task, job, undertaking (cf. dapi-kᵒ, p. 232a, l. 23) (Gr.M.; Rām. 310; K. 469, 794, 1034, 1036, 1064 ff.); a matter, affair (Gr.M.; Rām. 360, 1185; H. xi, 11; K. 89, 519, 565, 581, 749); business, transaction of business (K.Pr. 149; Rām. 469, 687, 848, 1163, 1280, 1446, 1611; K. 169, 480); workmanship, manufacture; work (as in needle-work, embroidery-work, etc.) (cf. dövⁱ-kⁱ, p. 262a, l. 17); work, means of livelihood, profession (kyāh kömᵘ̈ chukh karān, what work do you do? El.) (Gr.M.); a post, employment (Gr.M.); a necessity, obligation (Rām. 1148); a purpose, object (Gr.M.), chhuh kāmĕn lagān, it serves (various) purposes (Gr.M.); nērihē jān kömᵘ̈, good work would have issued, it would have been of use (Gr.M.); wāzan chĕh rāzan-sṻty kŏsa kömᵘ̈, what have cooks to do with kings (that they should be treated on equal terms) (Śiv. 1237). So kyāh kömᵘ̈ (K. 1122). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give employment (to), to employ (dat. of person) (Gr.M.). -kār m. (sg. dat. kāmĕ-kāras), work and the like; work, business, duties, occupation, business; transactions, dealings (Gr.M.). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to do an action (Gr.M.; Rām. 71, 1171, 1474); to do work (Gr.M.); in folk-tales the expression kömᵘ̈ kürᵘ̈n, he did a deed, or similar phrase, is common, and is equivalent to our 'and what do you think he did' in a fairy-tale (e.g. H. ii, 5, 7; viii, 4; x, 2, 3, 7, 12, 14; xii, 22). -kö̆ṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. kāmĕ-kŏcĕ), i.q. kömᵘ̈-kār (K. 265, 281, 417). ¶ kāmĕ-hondᵘ adj. (fem. -hünzᵘ̈) (sing. gen.), of use, useful (Gr.M.). -manz anun m.inf. to bring into use, to use (El.). ¶ kāmi-kār m. a doer of work; esp. a good worker, a hard worker, an industrious worker. -rostᵘ adj. (f.-rüʦhᵘ̈), without work, idle, out of work (El.). -rostᵘ karun m.inf. to dismiss, discharge (El., W. 87). -ṭôṭhᵘ m. one who is loved on account of work done by him; one who habitually shows affection to another merely on seeing his actions. -ʦūr m. a work thief, a lazy fellow who hides himself when he finds that there is work to do.
(? spelling) m. the branch of a tree (El. who gives kón on p. 8, and koṅ on p. 159). Perhaps the same as kônᵘ 2.

f.pl. the caulking of a boat. (This is done by packing in a kind of grass rope between the planking; cf. kônᵘ 5 and kọ̆thᵘ). --kaḍañĕ -- f.pl.inf. to pull or pick out the caulking between the planks of a boat; met. to pick holes in a person's character, to criticize unfavourably.

or kŏnḍa m. a kind of large bowl or basin made of metal or earthenware (Gr.Gr. 145); a deep still spring (El., Gr.Gr. 145); (amongst Hindūs) a hole dug in the ground for receiving consecrated fire; cf. ạgᵃna-kŏnḍ (p. 16b, l. 34) (Rām. 631). Cf. kọ̆nḍᵘ.

or (Gr.Gr. 69) kunḍal f. (sg. dat. kŏnḍali or kŏnḍüjᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 69), the earthenware bowl of a kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈, kāngrī or portable brazier, which holds the burning coals (K.Pr. 25, 129, 210); the outcry of a number of people running after a person and shouting abuse at him. Cf. kŏnḍul. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to shout abuse, as ab.
in girda-kŏndal, p. 300b, l. 10, i.q. kŏnḍul, q.v.
f. N. of a diagram in a horoscope in which are marked the positions of the various planets, etc., at the time of one's birth (cf. mūl 2).

or kŏnḍolᵘ adj. (f. kŏnḍᵘ̈jᵘ̈, Gr. Gr. 145), ring-shaped, annular; bowl-shaped; as subst. m., i.q. kŏnḍal 1 and 2, qq.v.; cf. ālakŏnḍul. kŏnḍali-wahay f. N. of the ring-like form assumed by the letter ā when non-initial in the Śāradā character, when following the letter ṅ, j, or ṭ, as in jā.
pron. indef. only noted in L.V. 55, where it occurs in the pl. ag. kandĕv... kandĕv, by some... by others, by several people... by several other people.

or konḍᵘ 1 m. a large bowl or basin, a cauldron for cooking or other use (cf. liwan-kọ̆nḍᵘ, s.v. liwun; maĩzi-kᵒ, s.v. maĩz); (amongst Hindūs) a hole dug in the ground for receiving consecrated fire; i.q. kŏnḍ, q.v. -kās m. 'removal of the (dirty) pots and pans after a feast'; hence, leisure after the completion of a work; cf. the next. -kāṭh m. the litter of dirty cauldrons and bits of firewood left after a great feast, used in phrases like konḍᵘ-kāṭh kösith, having cleared up the litter (he did so-and-so); used met. when a person gives up laziness, and takes to serious work (quasi, he clears up the litter after his feast, and sets to work). Cf. the preceding. --manḍulᵘ -- m. scouring round a cooking pot after use with scouring earth, water, etc., in order to clean the inside from the remains of food or the outside from smoke, etc.; met. disgracing a person by covering his face with mud (Śiv. 128). Cf. dᵃh, p. 198b, l. 7. ¶ kȧnḍⁱ-lë˘jⁱ f. the small vessel in which are kept the scouring-earth, water, etc., used for scouring cooking pots, etc., as ab. -wā̃-ḍulᵘ m. the large bowl or tub in which water is kept for scouring purposes, as ab. -wā̃-manḍulᵘ m., i.q. konḍᵘ-manḍulᵘ, ab. -wôñᵘ m. the dirty water with which vessels have been scoured, as ab.

f. used in pl. kŏnjĕ f.pl. delay deliberately made in making a gift or granting a request, or in order to show indifference or contempt. ¶ kŏnjĕ-āʦha f., id. The word āʦha is said to be meaningless here, but cf. ôʦhᵘ, endeavour; āʦha may be pl. of a fem. öʦhᵘ̈. --karañĕ lagañĕ -- f. pl. inf. openly to make such delay. --lagañĕ -- f. pl. inf. such delay to occur, hence (on the part of the person who is expecting) anxiety to be felt (K.Pr. 128, konjih).

m. a thorn, prickle, spine (cf. miʦar-kᵒ) (El. kŏnḍ, kúnḍ; K.Pr. 61; L. 75, 76, kund; 464, kundu; YZ. 99; Śiv. 1734, 1807; Rām. 354, 1200, 1210, 1218, 1224, 1226, 1329, 1355, 1424, 1432, 1529, 1633; H. viii, 1); the sharp bone of a fish (cf. gāḍa-kᵒ, p. 276b, l. 10) (K.Pr. 168); a small nail, a sprig, a tack. ¶ kȧnḍⁱ-babⁱrⁱ f. a kind of basil. -bombur m. a kind of bee whose body is said to be covered with spines. -dŏph m. (sg. dat. -dŏpas), a thorn-bush, a thorny bush. -hürᵘ̈ f. a collection of (dry) thorn branches, a heap of thorns (Rām. 585); cf. hürᵘ̈ (p. 347b, l. 35). -nār m. a fire of thorns (very fierce in its burning); a valley road between two mountains choked with thorns, and almost impassable. -pȧlⁱyār f. a thorn fence (round a garden, or the like). -pōsh m. the flower of any thorny shrub; N. of a certain flower. -pay m. a thorn fence. -thürᵘ̈ f. any thorny shrub, a thorn-bush (K.Pr. 218, L. 282); N. of a special thorny shrub used for making fences. -ʦhar f. a thorn-creel, a large kind of basket full of, or for holding, thorns; N. of a certain piece of wood in the topmost roof of a house. -ʦhürᵘ̈ f. a basket made of thorns; a basket full of thorns. -zāl m. a piece of ground covered with or surrounded by thorns, as by a net (YZ. 257; Śiv. 1568, 1686, 1854). Cf. W. 112, kạndizār.
m. (f. künḍᵘ̈ 2, q.v.), a stingy person, a miser.
also written kọ̆nḍᵘ m. a stain (cf. lashi-kọ̆nḍᵘ, s.v. lȧshⁱ), the act of causing a stain, staining.

m. a washerman's dressing iron (El. kunḍh); a scraper or grater for grating radishes, or the like; usually ˚--, the second member being the article to be grated, as in the following:--kȧnḍⁱ-mujⁱ f. grated radish, but mujĕ-konḍᵘ, a radish-grater (cf. mujᵘ̈).

m. saffron, Crocus sativus (the plant and the dried flowers (El.; L. 330, 342; K.Pr. 55; Rām. 1092, 1626). It is in great request as a condiment and as a pigment for the tilaka or forehead-marks of the Hindūs. See El. and L. for particulars regarding the cultivation (El. also kangan, kongs, and kwong). -bakusᵘ or -bŏkusᵘ m. the outer dark-coloured calix-leaves of a saffron flower. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. mŏnjĕ), the bulb or root of a saffron plant. -pōsh m. the saffron flower (El., Śiv. 1180, Rām. 1043). -püṭᵘ̈ f. the yellow-coloured portion of the stigma of the saffron-flower. -tihijᵘ̈ f. the orange-red tip of the stigma of the saffron flower. It is from this that the first quality saffron is made (L. 344). -ṭūrᵘ̈ ʦhunüñᵘ̈ f.inf. 'to pour forth the saffron-bowl' (an allusion to the old custom of Hindū times, according to which a girl chose her husband at a svayaṁvara, or assembly of candidates for her hand. She signified her choice by emptying upon the happy suitor a small bowl containing saffron and water); hence, met. to express approval (of), to select on account of charm or worthiness. -wörᵘ̈ f. a saffron garden, a plot in which the saffron-crocus is grown (L.V. 88; H. v, 7).

adj. c.g. in Rām. 1141, lāl-i könī, translated in the Skt. commentary by 'ratnaṁ bahumūlyam', a jewel of great price. The phrase probably represents the Pers. لعلِ کانی, a ruby of a mine, i.e. a genuine, not artificial, ruby.
f. the attic or topmost floor in a house, in which the tenants live during summer time (El. kányi). Cf. brörⁱ-köñī, p. 125b, l. 34, and köñᵘ̈ 4; i.q. kāñĕñ.
f. abstract noun of kônᵘ 3, q.v. Cf. lari-könil, s.v. lürᵘ̈.
m. (sg. dat. könṭaras), a cock-sparrow (K.Pr. 245 voc., W. 18).
m. a pad of grass rope or rags which carriers place on their shoulders to take the pressure of the load.

m. rice-water, gruel, or the like, liquid residue when grain is boiled, congee (El.), sour gruel, or vinegar made from rice-water, etc. (K.Pr. 26, 147, 248); cf. chāri-kᵒ, p. 165a, l. 38. ¶ kānz-pôwᵘ m. the jar in which gruel is kept in order to turn sour. -myulᵘ m. 'gruel terms', close intimacy and friendship between near neighbours, so that they will receive each other's gruel. ¶ kānzi gaʦhun, also written kānji gaʦhun m.inf. to go sour (of milk).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. köñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), to make one -eyed, to knock out or destroy a person's eye (Gr.Gr. 173); met. by some cutting remark to render a person answerless in a dispute.

m. a summoner, the man sent by her people to invite a young bride on a visit from her husband's house. (The invitation is a matter of some ceremony, and must be accompanied by a present to the husband, L. 262). kȧnⁱ-wôlⁱ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), id.

m. a ball of thread as it is made on the spinning wheel (K.Pr. 259). ¶ könⁱ barana yinⁱ m. pl. inf. pass. the balls of thread to become filled up; hence, met. (when a person has been reduced to a skeleton by famine or disease, and receives relief or is convalescent) the filling out of his internal organs and veins due to returned appetite and good food.
m. N. of a kind of paddy, with a soft and fragrant grain. Cf. kañi-hāl, p. 461a, l. 37, and El. kúnyí dányí; ? L. 332, 463, kanyun.

f. the region of the ribs, side, flank; sometimes extended to mean 'rib'. Cf. hȧlⁱ-kⁱ, p. 331b, l. 14, and lara-kᵒ, s.v. lar 2 (K.Pr. 182, kānih). ¶ kāñi-kumolᵘ adj. (f. -kumȧjⁱ or kumüjᵘ̈), having tender or delicate flanks; met. gentle natured; active and zealous in obedience. -lar f. the end of a rib; the side of the human body where the ribs are, the loin (El. kányilaṛ). Cf. lara-köñᵘ̈, as ab. -phĕl m. a carbuncle on the side; met. any near relation who gives great pain or worry. kāñi-panzur m. the skeleton of the ribs; met. a man who is so thin that he is mere skin and bone.

m. a thin stick, a slight rod (cf. lashi-kônᵘ, s.v. lȧshⁱ); esp. one of the row of sticks set up in the ground by a weaver, on which he arranges the warp prior to putting it in a loom for weaving. Cf. gaba-kônᵘ, p. 274b, l. 1.

adj. (f. küñᵘ̈), tawny coloured, reddish brown. --dã̄d -- m. a tawny bull (L.V. 66, sg. dat. kȧñⁱ dã̄das). --hāputh -- m. the red bear, Ursus arctus or Isabellinus (L. koin hápat, 111, 458). ¶ küñᵘ̈ gāv f. a tawny cow.
f. the small withy from which is woven the wicker basket-work forming the outside of the kāngrī or portable brazier used in Kashmīr. Cf. kônᵘ 2, kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈ and gura-küʦhᵘ̈, p. 298b, l. 19.
in burza-kônᵘ, a man whose profession it is to remove bark from birch-trees. See burza, p. 130b, l. 32. Cf. also lari-kônᵘ, a house-broker, s.v. lürᵘ̈.
in kȧñⁱ-gāsa m. N. of a kind of long white grass used for making sandals, well-ropes, etc. (L. 68 koin, Carex rubigena).

adj. (f. köñᵘ̈), one-eyed, monocular, blind of one eye (K.Pr. 1, 14, 66, 95, 100, 249); cf. cipa-kônᵘ and dōla-kônᵘ (p. 211b, l. 16). --˚ often used to indicate clumsiness, or the like, as in atha-kônᵘ, p. 59a, l. 33. --kalam -- m. a one-eyed pen, i.e. a pen of which one side of the nib is damaged. ¶ könⁱ-bāgay f. a one-eyed division, an unfair division (looking more in one direction than another; hence, giving more to one person than another). ¶ kāñi-ȧchⁱ-gāsh m. the gleam of a one-eyed eye, i.e. of the eye of a one-eyed man (a very rare thing, and difficult to bring about); hence, met. used with reference to some object which is rare or difficult of accomplishment.

(cf. köñī and kāñĕñ) in köñᵘ̈-pŏhur m. the top floor or attic of a house of several stories, in which the tenants live during the summer season (L. 461 kuinphor). -pĕṭh adv. on the top floor, in the attic, as ab. ¶ köñⁱ-pōr m. i.q. köñᵘ̈- pŏhur, ab. ¶ köñiyĕ-pōr m. i.q. köñⁱ- pōr, but with more emphasis on the fact that it is the topmost floor that is referred to, the very topmost floor, the very attic.
adj.(f. köñᵘ̈), having holes or orifices filled or choked up (e.g. a sieve choked up with dirt). Cf. kŏna.

f. sec. suff. u.w. nouns signifying things such as vegetables or wood, to indicate a small amount or a small bundle of the article referred to, as in gāsa-köñᵘ̈, a small bundle of grass (p. 307b, l. 32); hāka-köñᵘ̈, a little spinach (p. 326b, l. 21); kāṭha-kᵒ, a small bundle of wood (kāṭh); mujĕ- kᵒ, a few radishes (mujⁱ); niran-kᵒ, a small bundle of thatching-reeds (nirun); pōshĕ-kᵒ, a few flowers (pōsh); zinⁱ-kⁱ, a little firewood (zyunᵘ) (Gr.Gr. 163). Cf. kāñ 1.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kö̃panôwᵘ) (of an animate being) to cause to tremble (by frightening, or the like); (of something inanimate) to cause to tremble, to shake (something). (El. kampanáwun, Gr.Gr. 171).

(1 p.p. kö̃powᵘ), i.q. kö̃panāwun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 171). kö̃pawana yunᵘ m.inf. pass. to be caused to tremble (e.g. by a nightmare, or by agitation); to be distraught and totter almost to the point of fainting.
n.ag. (f. kö̃pavüñᵘ̈), (of an animate being) shaking, trembling (from fear, disease, or the like); (of an inanimate object) shaking, trembling (e.g. from the wind).

or kömph m. (sg. dat. kö̃pas), trembling, shaking (from fear, or the like, not the shivering from cold, etc.) (Gr.Gr. 123, K. 91, 579). logᵘ kö̃pas (for kö̃panas, cf. kö̃pun), he began to tremble (K. 107).
m.pl. vile qualities (of a person) characterized by immoral actions (cf. فعل).
m. a body of travellers or traders, etc., a caravan (Śiv. 1029).
m. an infidel, a non-Muslim, idolater, pagan, impious wretch (El., K.Pr. 183). -kēsh کآفر کیش adj. c.g. prone to infidelity; met. a mistress, a sweetheart (YZ. 11, a mixture of both meanings).
m. an evil or foul vulva. kŏpōnukᵘ adj. (f. kŏpōnicᵘ̈), born from a foul vulva, one who is utterly vile in character.
or -pöṭhin adv. in an evil manner, evilly, wickedly.

or kömpun conj. 3 (2 p.p. kö̃pyōv), (of an animate being) to tremble (from fear, or the like) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 343, 1286, 1297, 1754; Rām. 935, 937; K. 234-5, 436, 886); (of something inanimate) to quiver, to shake (Rām. 74, the reflexion of the sun in water; 170, the atmosphere at a loud cry; 1042, the earth; K. 91, a tree-branch) (El. kampun). The caus. of this vb. is kö̃panāwun or kö̃pawun (Gr.Gr. 171).

kôpūr (= کاپور), kôphurᵘ or kôphūr (= کافور) m. camphor; considered as very cooling to a fevered body (Śiv. 537), and to be an example of perfectly pure whiteness (kôpur, Śiv. 537; kôphurᵘ, Śiv. 771; kôphūr, Śiv. 619, 815, 1149). kôphura-rang adj. c.g. of the colour of camphor, pure white, snow-white (Śiv. 359).
m. a bad or wicked son, the third of the three kinds of sons,--a sonequal to the father, one better than the father, and one not so good as the father (K.Pr. 174).
m. evil progeny, evil offspring, evil issue (of men, beasts, or plants).
f. a leather bag for holding ghī, oil, or the like, the kuppā of India.
m. a collection, bunch, total; genl. --˚, as in zara, the unshaven hair of a young child, zara-kôpᵘ, the total head of hair of this kind. Cf. kala-kᵒ, p. 435a, l. 10, and kôpᵘ 3.

m. (of any thing) a position or condition which is natural and expected, in its right place. kāpi yunᵘ m.inf. (of any thing) to take a natural and desired position, to be in the right place and stay there.
m. the top of the skull, the brain pan. Cf. kôpᵘ 1, and kala-kᵒ, p. 435a, l. 10.

adv. in what place? where? (Gr.Gr. 155; W. 94; Śiv. 279; H. ii, 2); whither (El.); ada kōr or ada kōr-kun, then where? i.e. (if not there) then where is it? (see p. 12b, l. 29); ḍĕṭha kōr, everywhere, very much, exceedingly (see p. 257b, l. 32). -kun adv. in what direction? where? (Gr.Gr. 160); whither? (Rām. 513, K. 801). ¶ kōra adv. from where? whence? (Gr.Gr. 156, W. 94); (?) recently (El.). -kani adv. from where? whence? (Gr.Gr. 159, Rām. 949). This expression is chiefly used in addressing a new arrival or in similar circumstances. -kanĕn adv. in what direction? where? -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of or belonging to what direction? of where? ¶ kūrⁱ or kūry adv. where even? verily in what place? where ever? (Gr.Gr. 156).

(? کرہ, a globe, quasi the globe of the eye) m. in kŏra pyonᵘ m.inf. a glance to fall (upon something); looking (at something) to occur; esp. a longing glance to fall, etc. --trāwun -- m.inf. to look longingly (at), to gaze covetously.
in kōrā-kūrī f. a condition of tyranny or anarchy.

m. (for 1, see kōr) voluntary abstention from food, loathing against even the mention of food or drink in sickness or the like, eating absolutely nothing in such a case, i.q. kūrⁱ- kōra, s.v. kūrⁱ 2. -kāh m. the Hindū fast of the eleventh day of a lunar fortnight, when it is kept solely by total abstinence from food and drink.

adj. c.g. 'virgin'; hence, unwashed, uncleaned (of an article, e.g. cloth, as it comes from the shop, and which has not been washed since it was brought home), new, fresh from the shop, bran new (K.Pr. 181). -bāna m. an unused earthen vessel, as it is received from the potter. -kapur m. calico fresh from the shop, unbleached calico. -pūʦᵘ̈ f. a woman's veil fresh from the shop. See pūʦᵘ̈.
in kōra-hüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -hacĕ), the block of wood that supports the iron spike of a native ploughshare; a certain forest insect that burrows under the skin and causes great pain, ? a kind of tick.
m. a kind of loose piece of embroidered cloth hanging from the front part of the sleeve of a dress. It has no use, and is worn principally by prostitutes. -norᵘ m. a sleeve furnished with this cloth.
m. the Qur'ān, the Muslim sacred book.

m. a sacrifice, victim, offering, oblation. Yīd kŏrbān, one of the four chief Musalmān holidays of Kashmīr (L. 268), the 'īdu'l-qurbān or 'īdu'ẓ-ẓŏḥā, held on the tenth day of the month Ẕu'l-ḥijja, in commemoration of Abraham's offering up of his son Isaac, or (according to Musalmān tradition) Ishmael. --lagun -- m.inf. to become a sacrifice, to offer oneself as a sacrifice, to throw oneself before a person as if one were a sacrificial offering (YZ. 569).
m. one who has many daughters; (in obscene abuse) one whose daughter is unchaste, or one who has incestuous connexion with his own daughter (Gr.Gr. 134; cf. kōlal).
in kōri-kach m. (sg. dat. kachas), the grass called kach (q.v.), when in the springtime it is so small that it cannot even be cut or plucked up.
m. the Numidian crane, Anthropoides virgo.

m. a director, manager; an officer whose business it is to keep records; in Kashmīr, a Persian-knowing Brāhmaṇ employed by Government. The title dates from the time of Sult̤ān Zainu 'l-'ābidīn in the 15th century. These men are by profession writers, merchants, and farmers, never soldiers (El. kárkun, s.v. baṭa; L. 302).

m. a bracelet, wristlet, bangle (massive and open, El. kaur and kúr; Gr.Gr. 45, 46, 55; K. 60; H. xii, 10-15, 18, 25); an anklet (cf. gŏḍa-korᵘ, p. 277a, l. 35) (K. 184); a link or ring in a chain (Gr.M.); a hoop, a band (cf. dājĕ-korᵘ, p. 202b, l. 25); the ring of cream, etc., on the edge of a dish of milk, or the like. ¶ kȧrⁱ-chal f. a piece of a broken bracelet, etc. -gulᵘ m. a single bracelet (on one forearm). -jūrⁱ f. a pair of bracelets, one for each arm. -khünḍᵘ̈ f. a piece of a bracelet; a little old worn-out bracelet. -khapᵘ̈ṭᵘ̈ f. a mean little worn-out bracelet (cf. khapoṭᵘ, p. 406b, l. 7). -phuṭᵘ̈ f. a small bracelet, esp. one that is broken. -pī˜th f. (sg. dat. -pī̃ʦᵘ̈), a tiny bracelet for a child.

f. (for 2, see kôrᵘ 2; cf. also kārun), the neck (El. kár and kãr; Gr.Gr. 13; K.Pr. 156, kār; YZ. 64; W. 12; Śiv. 52, 971, 1363). -mārüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to bend the neck; to bow the head or nod in acquiescence; to nod the head in a pleased sort of way (K.Pr. 77). Cf. nigayĕ-kᵒ, s.v. nigay. ¶ kāri-holᵘ adj. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), crooked necked, wry-necked (by nature or from rheumatism, etc.). -pȧtⁱ 1 m. N. of a certain wild flower, described as dark in colour, with small tooth-shaped shoots at the back (pȧtⁱ) (Rām. 649, 655). -pȧtⁱ 2 adv. on the back or nape of the neck (Rām. 1615). -thodᵘ adj. (f. -thüzᵘ̈), 'high in the neck,' one who carries his head high in public, one who occupies an honourable position and knows it (cf. Śiv. 971, 1363).
m. the slipperiness on the bank of a river in frosty weather.
adj. (f. körᵘ̈ 2; for 1, see s.v.), one-eyed (= kônᵘ 4, q.v.) (L.V. 20); crooked limbed, deformed (of a person). ¶ körⁱ-shiñⁱ f. the misfortunes, inconveniences, etc., arising from poverty.

m. the deficiency or distorted shape in a superficies with corners (e.g. a piece of cloth or an area of land) owing to the angles being too large or too small, want of symmetry or deficiency due to want of symmetry of this kind.
or, or kusalyā f. Kausalyā, N. of a wife of king Daśaratha. She was mother of Rāma-candra (Śiv. 1140, 1483; Rām. 83, 191, 1227, kausalyā; 40, 82, 209-10, 225, etc., kusalyā).
m. a violet (El.); safflower (Skt. kusumbha) (YZ. 254, 257; Rām. 645, 1008, 1094). A woman's hands or feet are compared to it for delicacy and beauty (Rām. 189, 355, 1082, 1251).
m. bad company, evil companionship, consorting with evil-doers (Śiv. 1808).

or kaũsar m. N. of a mountain lake in the Pīr Pantsāl Range, in Skt. Kramasaras and the Kōnsᵃr of RT.Tr. It is supposed to mark a footstep (krama) of Viṣṇu, and is an object of the Naubandhana pilgrimage (RT.Tr. II, 393; Śiv. 1170; L.V. 50).
m. a treasury; a treasury of words, a dictionary (a Hindū word) (Gr.M.).
m. (f. kŏ-shānücᵘ̈), one who is of mean family, descended from a family which is unworthy (either in regard to virtue or to fortune).
f. a bad rumour, a report or rumour (true or untrue) about some calamity or other similar unwished for occurrence.
m. (sg. dat. -shĕkunas), an ill-omen; mostly used with reference to the commencement of a journey or of a festival.

or kushĕl m. health, well-being, welfare; esp. health recovered after illness (a Hindū word). -hum m. (among Hindūs) a special small oblation offered for the benefit of his family by each participant, after the conclusion of an important general sacrificial ceremony. ¶ kŏshĕla-pạthᵃr m. a letter giving news of welfare; hence, politely, a letter (Gr.M.).
f. (sg. dat. köshiyĕ), the city of Kāśī or Benares. Its tutelary deity is Śiva (Śiv. 672-3, 694, 865, 1257; K. 691, 873, 884, etc.). -nāth, m. the Lord of Kāśī, a title of Śiva (Śiv. 1409).

or kôshyurᵘ adj. (f. köshirᵘ̈), of or belonging to Kashmīr, Kāshmīrī; a man of Kashmīr (El.; H. xi, 6); the Kāshmīrī language (El., YZ. 239); (f.) a woman of Kashmīr (El.); the Kāshmīrī language (Gr.M.). -pahān adj. (f. köshirᵘ̈- pahān), somewhat Kāshmīrī, more or less Kāshmīrī, closely resembling something produced in Kashmīr. ¶ köshirᵘ̈ al f. a kind of pumpkin, long in shape and green in colour (cf. El., s.v. al). --mujᵘ̈ -- f. a species of radish (El. köshírí múj). --nāsth -- f. a kind of yellow snuff made of Kāshmīrī tobacco. --zĕv -- f. the Kāshmīrī language (El.).

adj. (f. köshᵘ̈ 1), of or belonging to the eleventh lunar day (on which Hindūs fast) (cf. kāh 3); hence, subst. m. a severe fast, such as that which is held on that day. --karun -- m.inf. to fast (Rām. 188).

m. pounded chaff of wheat, barley, maize, or the like, which remains after husking the grain in a mortar (El. kosh and kúsh; cf. kisr, s.v. kĕsürᵘ̈); a honeycomb (H. ix, 5). In composition this word has a wider signification. Thus ara-koshᵘ (p. 41a, l. 17) is 'sawdust', and cāhi- koshᵘ (p. 158a, l. 11) is 'used tea leaves'. El., s.v. kúsh, also gives the meaning 'beeswax'; cf. kashürᵘ̈. ¶ kȧshⁱ-dāl f. millets, etc., or dāl, in the husk, cooked as a porridge, porridge of unhusked millet. -pholᵘ m. a single flake, or a very small amount, of chaff, as ab. -ʦŏ̈ṭᵘ̈ f. a cake made only of chaff, as ab. It is used as a medicine.
in kaṭh-koshᵘ, etc., s.v. kaṭh 4, q.v.

in okᵘ-köshᵘlad (p. 19a, l. 20), a word derived from kāh 3 (sg. dat. köshᵘ̈), the eleventh day of a lunar fortnight, on which Hindūs fast. Hence, okᵘ-köshᵘlad means one who suffers, or who would suffer, from a single one of these fasts, lit. suffering from a single eleventh lunar day.
or kösith m. a messenger, a courier (K.Pr. 128); a postman who carries mail-bags from one stage to another, a letter-carrier (El.); an envoy, an ambassador (Rām. 708, 726).
see kösid, of which it is a corruption (El.). The word may also be the conj. part. of kāsun 1 and 2.
or m. N. of a celebrated gem, in Skt. Kaustubha, obtained, according to Hindū legend, at the churning of the ocean and worn by Viṣṇu on his breast (Śiv. 792, 1436; K. 60).
(? spelling) m. the musk-deer (L. 462, kastura). The word should perhaps be kŏstūrᵘ, q.v.

kŏstūr, or kastūrᵘ m. (pl. dat. kastūrĕn, Gr.Gr. 56), a certain bird, the Grey-winged Blackbird, Merula boulboul (L. 152, kastura). According to El. it corresponds to the shah bulbul and to the hazār dastān or nightingale. It has a melodious voice, and is valued as a cage-bird (El. kastūr and kostūr; K.Pr. 147, kastur; L. gives kastura both for this bird and for the musk-deer. See kŏstūra; Śiv. 327).
f. musk; the sweet-scented lousewort, Pedicularis brevifolia (it has a delicious odour, but not of musk) (L. 77). kŏstūrĕ-gagᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a musk-rat. -nāph, f. a musk-pod; musk (Śiv. 501).
(? spelling) f. labour (El.; possibly by this is meant köṭhᵘ̈ 4, or some connected word not elsewhere recorded).
a small pair of scales, such as those used by jewellers for weighing gold, etc.
m. a pin (used for fixing garments, etc., or as a brooch-pin, necklace-clasp, etc.).
f. the leading of a horse in a procession. Such horses, decorated with ornamented trappings, are led at the head of a royal procession, or before a bridegroom, etc.
or kōtāmath, adv. up to where? till when? (W. 93).

adv. lit. 'with a weak kick'; hence, met. with a feeble or silly excuse (e.g. for not completing some simple or easy work). --lagun -- m.inf. (of some work) to become suddenly, or for no reason, stopped.
or kūṭapāl m. the chief official of a town or fortress, the chief of the police, the captain of a fort (K. 404, 792-3, 819). Cf. kuṭawāl.
m. a bad bastard; hence, a naughty, bold, bad little boy.

f. (sg. dat.kö̆ṭhᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 71), N. of a certain medicinal plant Aucklandia Costus. The root, which is fragrant, is a government monopoly. For full accounts of this plant, see El. s.v. kŏṭ and L. 77. L. gives the botanical name as Saussurea Lappa. Cf. cōb-ĕ-kŏṭh, p. 156b, l. 34; L. 83, 389, 418.
m. (sg. dat. kōṭas), a coat or cloak (of the English fashion; the English word borrowed) (Gr.M.).
in kō̃th-möjᵘ̈ f. the eldest woman of a family in a household, the head lady of a family.
m. (sg. dat.kö̃ṭhas), the throat, the front of the neck (El. kãṅṭ, kauṭ, and kanṭh). -māl f. an ornament worn by women on the front of the neck (El. kauṭmal, kauṭmál, and kãnṭhmál).
f. (sg. dat. kö̆ʦhᵘ̈), a hank of thread (esp. of the loose single strands of thread, preparatory to twisting into thread in strands); a ball of sewing-thread (Gr.Gr. 69).
or kŏʦh f. (sg. dat. kö̆ʦhᵘ̈), a kind of large leathern bag for transporting grain. Cf. kọ̆thᵘ, kö̆ʦhᵘ̈ 1, and kŏʦhul (Gr.Gr. 146).

m. a granary, a store-room; the wall, circumvallation, or enceinte round a town or fortress (K. 757-8); cf. kūṭh 1 and kuṭhᵘ̈. -dār m. (f. -dārĕñ), a man in charge of a store-room, a store-keeper, a house-steward (YZ. 420).

m. a gold necklet; a necklace or rosary (of beads of gold, or silver, or pearls, or jewels, or crystal, or of the earth of Karbalā). -gan a particular fragrant gum-resin (the exudation of the tree Amyris agallochum), bdellium (Śiv. 377).
or kŏthulᵘ  m. (sg. dat. kŏthalas), a large bundle or parcel (esp. one of awkward shape, and hence requiring much tying up). Cf. kọ̆thᵘ and kŏʦhul.
m. a man who caulks (a boat or ship) (cf. nāwa-kᵒ, s.v. nāv 2).

m. a load, a burden, bundle (especially one awkwardly shaped, and hence requiring to be tied up and difficult to carry) (Gr.Gr. 33, 37; K.Pr. 3); the caulking of a boat or ship (cf. nāwa-kᵒ, s.v. nāv 2); cf. kŏth 2 and kö̆ʦhᵘ̈ 1. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to caulk the seams or holes in a boat or ship. Cf. kŏna. ¶ kŏthⁱ-kuchay m. a servant of a judge or other person in authority who acts as a go-between in taking bribes from litigants on behalf of his master. Cf. kuchay and kọ̆ʦhᵘ.

m. the knee (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 200-1, 237; Rām. 285, 1129, 1146; K. 1125). --mūrun -- m.inf. when one is seated on the ground, to move the knees so as to make room politely for another. --nạmᵃrāwun -- m.inf. to bend the knee, to fall on one's knee (Gr.M.). --trāwun -- m.inf. to kneel (El.). --yunᵘ -- m. the knee to come, i.e. the ability to crawl on the knees to come (of a child beginning to learn to crawl on its hands and knees) (K.Pr. 260). ¶ kŏṭhⁱ-ã̄cĕ f.pl., see the next. -ö̃ṭᵘ̈ f. the knee-cap (pl. -ã̄cĕ). -ganḍ m. tying the knees (of a person, to prevent his going). -köʦᵘ̈ f. the poples, ham (El. kúṭkáts); cf. köʦᵘ̈ 3. -në̆ṭhᵘ̈ f. the patella, knee-cap, knee-pan (El. kútanyíṭ). -ʦŏcĕ f.pl. cakes made and distributed in honour of the occasion of a child first beginning to crawl on its hands and knees. -wace f.pl. the knee-joint.

m. a kind of stocks in which prisoners are confined by the legs; an impalement stake, the stake on which a criminal is impaled, a gallows (El.; K.Pr. 5, 215; Śiv. 1630). ¶ köṭhis ladun m.inf. to hang (a criminal) (El.). -pĕṭh āsun m.inf. to be hanged (El.).
m. a high-heeled shoe worn by the Paṇḍits of Kashmīr (El. kóṅth, i.e. kỗthᵘ).
f. (sg. dat. kāchĕ, Gr.Gr. 63), a small stick, a stalk (Gr.Gr. 29); dim. of kāṭh 1, q.v.
f. (sg. dat. kāchĕ), the fifth, or little, finger or toe.

adj. f. (sg. dat. kāchĕ), hard, dry, sapless (used as the f. of kāṭh 3, q.v.); most commonly used with ref. to radishes and similar roots; hence, as subst. f. the hard rind of a vegetable root (cf. mŏnjĕ-kᵒ, s.v. mö̆nḍᵘ̈ 1).
adj. f. (sg. dat. kāchĕ), habitually lazy, indolent in doing any work. A feminine form, used as a fem. of köṭhⁱ 2, q.v. Cf. kóṭ.
f. a small bag, tied up as a parcel, and carried, like a parcel, on the head or under the arm; dim. of kŏthul, q.v.
f. the old Kāshmīrī wooden riding-saddle (El. kãṭh m. and kãṭhí f.; L. 463).
adj. c.g. lazy, indolent; weary from over-work (K.Pr. 182, kāṭ); cf. kāṭh 2 and köṭhᵘ̈ 4. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become lazy or wearied, as ab.
adj. c.g. causing death, deadly. zahᵃr-i-kötil, deadly poison (Rām. 827).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kỗṭᵘ; 2 p.p. kö̃cyōv), to pilfer secretly (esp. from goods entrusted to the thief). kỗṭᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. kö̃ṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), pilfered, as ab.

or (Gr.Gr. 58) kōturᵘ m. (sg. dat. kōtaras; f. nom. kōtᵘ̈rᵘ̈), a pigeon or dove (wild or tame) (El.; L. 462, kotar; Rām. 93; K. 922, 947); N. of a sept of Kāshmīrī Brāhmaṇas. A cock pigeon is also nar-kōtur, and a hen is māda-kōtur (W. 17). ¶ kōtar-bāz m. one who trains pigeons, a pigeon-fancier (W. 111). -jūrⁱ f. a pair of doves (Gr.Gr. 82); esp. a pair of doves (male and female) swung, or let loose, in a wedding ceremony, over the bride and bridegroom. -morᵘ m. a dovecot (K.Pr. 57). -nal m. 'a dove's leg', a species of pear (L. 350, kotenal). -pūtᵘ m. a young pigeon (Gr.Gr. 131); a boy of the Kōturᵘ sept of Brāhmaṇas. -rath m. (sg. dat. -ratas), pigeon's blood. It is of a very red colour, and the compound is often used in similes to express extreme redness.
f. (sg. dat. kŏcĕ), in kömᵘ̈-kŏ̈ṭᵘ̈, q.v., p. 444a, l. 8.

(f. küṭᵘ̈, q.v.), a seedling-sprout, the first sprout of a young plant (cf. gāsa- koṭᵘ, p. 307b, l. 34; muji-kᵒ, s.v. mujᵘ̈); a bush, a thicket of bushes (K. 111, 219, 350); a male child (generally used with reference to caste or profession), usually, but not always, with the idea of praise. It is also occasionally used to indicate the young of animals. Thus, baṭa-koṭᵘ, a (real) son of a Brāhmaṇ, a good Brāhmaṇ; chāna-koṭᵘ, a carpenter's son, a real son of a carpenter, a good carpenter; harạna-koṭᵘ, a fawn (p. 349a, l. 24); mö̃shĕ-koṭᵘ, a buffalo-calf; cf. Gr.Gr. 132 (K.Pr. 174; H. xii, 25). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become insufficient, to be found to be too short, not long enough (K. 166). ¶ kȧṭⁱ gūlⁱ m.pl. the kernels of water-chestnuts which have just sprouted in the spring-time, see the next; cf. gūlᵘ 2. --görⁱ -- m.pl. young water-chestnuts which have just sprouted in the spring-time; cf. gôrᵘ 1. --gāsa -- m.pl. a kind of grass growing in marshy ground, used as a remedy for eye-disease. kȧṭⁱ-har f. a fight amongst naughty boys; a fight between two young buffalos.

in kötⁱ-nọ̆mⁱ m. the being confined in all directions, being stopped from going in any direction, imprisonment; met. taking measures to prevent another exercising his free will as regards income and expenditure, etc., tying up another's power of expenditure.

adv. in what place, where? (Gr.Gr. 156; W. 94; Rām. 209, 211, 219, etc.; K. 363, 1161; H. xi, 5); towards where? whither? (El. kŏt; Gr.M.; L.V. 9; K.Pr. 99, kut; Śiv. 410, 416, 1733, 1862); for what reason? why? (Rām. 238, 450). As an interrogative expecting the answer 'no', this word may be used with a sense equivalent to 'nowhere', 'not at all' (Śiv. 1035); cf. kotᵘnanas, kotᵘnas, and katuth. --bā -- adv. where, sir? (used in addressing a male equal). --biñ -- adv. where, madam? (used in addressing respectfully an equal or elder woman). -kun adv. in what direction? whither? --sa -- adv. where, sir? (used in addressing a male superior). -sanā adv. where? i.q. kotᵘ, but indicates a shade of doubtfulness, quasi 'I wonder where' (cf. Gr.Gr. 180-1). --ta kōr -- adv. where and where? i.e. nowhere (Śiv. 279). -tām, -tāmath, -tāñ, or -tāñĕth adv. up to how far? how far? (Gr.M.); somewhere, anywhere. The underlying idea in the mind of the speaker is a doubtful question, as in, e.g. 'is so-and-so anywhere? if so, where?' (Gr.Gr. 256). ¶ katū adv. where (used in addressing an inferior)?
or kotᵘnas adv. in what place? where?; towards what place? whither? Cf. kotᵘ 2.
f. a small kind of louse, described as red in colour and a great biter.
in kōv ka, the Kāshmīrī name of the letter ka, when written in the Śāradā character (used in schools).
m. a bad time, a time of disaster (famine, epidemic, plague, or the like).
f. a hen crow (El. kāvin, Gr.Gr. 37). See kāv 1.
adv. at a bad time; in a time of calamities, etc.; at an inauspicious time; at a wrong time, untimely, unseasonably. A contracted form of this word is kŏzi.
m. paralysis of half the body, hemiplegia.
m. a hooked stick or crook, such as would be used for pulling down fruit from a tree, or for fastening a rope to (e.g. in the case of a tent- peg). Cf. görⁱ-kôvⁱ, p. 298a, l. 33.
m. dark-coloured, black; cf. kāworᵘ. --kaṭh -- m. a black ram (used in sacrificial offerings to demons).
adv. by a bad method, in a bad way.

m. (sg. dat. kŏwatas), strength, power, virtue, force, vigour, energy, authority (El.). Regarding the gender of this word, see W. 18. kŏwata-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), powerless, without strength, unable (El. kuwatrust).

f. (sg. dat. kŏwati), a bad path, a dirty foul pathway, or difficult road (e.g. on a mountain or through a forest, etc.). kŏwati lagun m.inf. to go on a bad path, to take to evil courses; to turn out badly (of an action).
adj. c.g. strengthening, invigorating, tonic, nourishing (of food, medicine, etc.).
adj. (f. kŏ-wöcᵘ̈), one who utters ill words, abusive, foul-mouthed.
often written köida m. a rule, regulation, law, institution (Gr.M.); usual course of procedure, custom, usage, habit, manner, mode, way (Gr.M.). Cf. bē-köida.
often written köim قآئم adj. c.g. fixed, established (Gr.M.). -mukām قآئم مقام m. one who acts in the place of another, a locum- tenens (Gr.M.).
often written köimī (for قآئم) adj. c.g., i.q. the preceding (K.Pr. 216). Properly (قآئمی) subst. f. fixity, permanence, but used ab. as adj.
or m. a certain bird, described as red in colour, about the size of a sparrow, and as uttering a deep cry when flying up into the air.
m. paralysis of half the body, hemiplegia.
m. a bad man, a wicked person, a sinner (K.Pr. 202).

adv. who knows? God knows! used in sentences such as kōzana kyāh bani tas, God alone knows what will become of him; hence, who knows how? God knows how! who knows by what means (L.V. 73, 74). kōzanañi f. sg. abl. of sg. gen. how? by what means? (L.V. 72).

adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. -zātas), of bad, or low, caste, low- born; used also, as a term of reproach, with reference to a well-born person who acts vilely, of a bad disposition, bad-natured (W. 110).
adv. at a bad time, in a time of calamities, etc., at an inauspicious time; at a wrong time, unseasonably. A contracted form of kŏ-vizi, q.v.

m. a judge; (a Muslim) judge or magistrate (who passes sentence in all cases of law, religious, moral, or criminal), a Qāẓī; in Kashmīr, esp. a Muslim doctor of laws, who decides questions of religion and morality (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 101, 145). -bāy f. his wife.
f. the office or duties of a judge (see közⁱ); a habit of acting as such a person.
or kŏ-ʦöl m. one who habitually wears dirty clothes; hence, a man of vile conduct (Śiv. 750).
f. (sg. dat. -ʦē̃ki), a vile vulva; a woman with such (obsc. abuse); cf. kŏ-ʦŏth. kŏʦē̃ki-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), born of a vile vulva; hence, one who is vile in character.
m. an unexpected trick (esp. when it stops or confines the deceived person).
or kŏʦhulᵘ m. (sg. dat. kŏʦhalas, Gr.Gr.58; f. kŏʦhᵘ̈jᵘ̈), a porter, esp. one who carries grain (in a kŏth, or leathern sack) (El. kŏtsúl). Cf. kŏth 2.

or koʦhᵘ m. a bribe (El. kauʦ; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 99, khuʦh); cf. kŏthⁱ-kuchay, p. 489a, l. 4. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give a bribe, to bribe (Gr.M.). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take bribes (El.). ¶ kŏʦhⁱ-khŏr or kŏʦhⁱ-khāv m. a bribe-eater, a bribe-taker.
or küʦhᵘ̈ f. a bag, sack, pouch, or wallet, made of cloth (Gr.Gr. 63). Cf. kọ̆thᵘ, of which this word is a fem. dim. (Gr.Gr. 33, 37); cf. also kŏth 2.
f. (sg. dat. -ʦŏti), a vile vulva; a woman with such (obsc. abuse); cf. kŏ-ʦē̃kh. kŏʦŏti-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), born of a vile vulva; hence, one who is vile in character.
adj. (f. köʦᵘ̈ 1, for 2, 3, see s.vv.), a miser, one who will not spend money, even though rich. Cf. katun 2.
f. (for 1, see kôʦᵘ), a kind of scissors or pincers for cutting betel-nut, the sarōtā of India; a pair of scissors (for cutting cloth, etc.) (L.V. 103).
f. (for 1, see kôʦᵘ), the under part of the leg between the thigh and the knee, the ham.
or kāʦan 2 f. in yẹ̆ndra-kᵒ, p. 1199a, l. 24, q.v.
sg. dat. of krüṭᵘ̈, q.v. s.v., and under kroṭᵘ.
m. one who is accustomed to make an uproar, a loud-voiced person.

or krēkh f. (sg. dat. kraki), a loud noise, outcry (in fighting, from terror, or in lamentation) (cf. nāra-kᵒ, s.v. nār 1) (Gr.Gr. 6, 65, 66; H. iii, 3); an exclamation, a cry (by one person or many) (Rām. 377); met. a loud noise (e.g. the roaring of the sea) (Gr.M.); a complaint (El.). krakh is the form used in Śrīnagar, while krēkh is used elsewhere (El., H.). -cikh or -cīkh f. (sg. dat. kraki-ciki or -cīki), outcry and shriek, a loud outcry. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to raise an outcry, to shriek out (on receiving a blow or in pain, etc.), cry aloud (Rām. 407, 949; K. 445, 600; H. v, 7; xii, 7). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to shout, to roar (El., K. 232); to complain (El.). --lāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cry out, cry aloud (Rām. 390, 1360; K. 443). --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make a noise (El.); to cry out (Gr.M.). ¶ kraka-nād m. an outcry raised by a number of people; the screaming of children (Gr.M.).

m. (the f. is kröjᵘ̈, q.v., and signifies either his wife, or a female potter), a potter (always a Musalmān) (El.; K.Pr. 114; L. 462; W. 17; H. xi, 10, 11). krāla-anzan m. a kind of rice; cf. anzan. -ḍabur m. the roof of a potter's house (flat and not ridged). -kō̃da f. a potter's kiln. -khŏḍ m. N. of a quarter in Śrīnagar, near the Haba Kadal bridge, and inhabited by potters. -mọ̆nḍᵘ m. a kind of vegetable, growing wild in spring in grassy places, Capsella Bursa-pastoris (L. 71). -pan m. the potter's string with which he cuts the soft vessels from the lump of earth on the wheel. -sangürᵘ̈ f. N. of a hill on the south-east of the Ḍal lake near Śrīnagar. -ʦaküjᵘ̈ f. a potter's wheel. -wān m. a potter's shop (usually his house, where he stores and sells his pots).

m. a footstep; progression (Śiv. 1754, 1851); progressive order, uninterrupted progress, series, succession; lata-kram, a step with the foot; hence, a kick (see lath). ¶ krama krama gālun m.inf. to destroy progressively; hence, to keep maltreating or worrying (a servant or the like), to do so over and over again. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without order, without system (Gr.M.). -sar m. old N. of a lake and village in the Divᵃsar Pargana. It is supposed to mark a footstep (kram) of the god Viṣṇu. See RT.Tr. II, 393.

f. a group of people known by the same title, or carrying on the same profession; nearly equivalent to, but not the same as 'caste' or 'sub-caste', a tribal section (K.Pr. 260, W. 141, L. 304), cf. RT.Tr. II, 430; a surname, a nickname, added to a man's original name by reason of his special calling, or because of some special circumstance that has occurred to him (El.; see K.Pr. 115 for examples).

m. a kind of large covered trunk or basket made of withies, a kind of 'khilta'. Those used by natives of Kashmīr are a little larger than those used by English travellers, and are not covered with leather (El., K.Pr. 1, kranḍ). -wôrᵘ m. a smaller kind of the same.
or krangūs m. a kind of cowry, long in shape and with no back.

m. a kind of basket made of withies not closely woven together, so that it has numerous interstices. It is used for carrying vegetables, roots, or the like (El., K.Pr. 115). Cf. kranzulᵘ. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become such a basket; met. to be reduced to a skeleton through sickness. ¶ kranjali pôñᵘ sārun m.inf. to carry water in such a basket; hence, to be employed on fruitless labour.
m. a reed basket (Śiv. 1592). Cf. kranjolᵘ.

or krĕpā f. compassion, favour (shown to a person), tenderness, mercy, loving-kindness (Śiv. 626, 629, 1487, 1636); krĕpāyi-kinⁱ, through kindness; hence, kindly (do so-and-so), please! (Gr.M.). Cf. dayĕ-krapā, p. 266a, l. 18.
m. a miser, one who is mean and niggardly. Cf. krupunᵘ.

m. (sg. dat. krapas), chopping, cutting, cutting off, esp. used for cutting wood, or for cutting food with the teeth in the act of eating; cf. krĕph. kraph-kraph m. onomat. the noise made by the jaws in eating, champing, as in kraph kraph karith khyonᵘ, to make a noise with the jaws in eating.
m. onomat. (sg. dat. krāpas), the noise of the breaking of wood or similar substance, 'crack.'
m. breaking with the sound of a snap (e.g. of a bone or a piece of wood) (cf. krāph); the act of reducing to small fragments or to powder.
m. the earthy smell of newly-baked earthenware pots, such as is observed in a potter's house. krāran-phakh m. (sg. dat. -phakas), the stink of boiling oil or the like.
m. N. of a tract on the western outskirts of the city of Śrīnagar.
m. a miller (only El.), i.q. graṭa- wôlᵘ, p. 305a, l. 5.
f. (sg. dat. krüʦᵘ̈), a writing, a composition (Gr.M.).

onomat. m. the sound made in swallowing food, the noise of a gulp; cf. krith and kruth 1 and 2. --kaḍun m.inf. to withdraw the sound of gulping, to have eaten to repletion, to be satiated; met. to have all that one desires of property, wealth, or the like. --karith -- adv. having made a gulping sound, (to eat, etc.) with a gulping sound.
or krĕṭun (Gr.Gr. xv) conj. 3 (2 p.p. kraṭyōv), to become thin (of someone or something formerly stout or thick). kraṭyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. kraṭyē-müʦᵘ̈), become thin, as ab.

f. the harvesting, usufruct, or collection of crops, fruit, flowers, etc. (YZ. 31, 254; Śiv. 269, 526, 1720, 1801); the final reaping of a harvest (K.Pr. 247); the village festival on the first day of spring, on which farmers commence to plough their fields for the new crop (Paṇḍit's explanation of kṛṣyârambhaḥ).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. krôwᵘ), to do, to make (Gr.Gr. xvi). Cf. karith krövith, p. 473b, l. 29.
f. an iron boiling-pan, a cauldron (El. kváí).
f. a deed, an action; esp. a religious performance, a religious rite, such as a śrāddh, etc.; (according to El.) alms, esp. in connexion with the dead (El. krai, K.Pr. 115).
f. grain which has fallen to the ground at the time of reaping, and which springs up spontaneously in the following year; esp. self-sown rice (L. 334, kre).
f. the daily religious rites performed in a family for ten days after a death. The word is sing., and the plur., which is the same in form, is used in the same sense. Cf. kray 1 (L. 263, kari).

(sg. dat. kraʦi), N. of a certain lunar mansion, in Skt. Kṛttikā, the Pleiades. It contains six stars. ¶ kraʦi-kūrᵘ̈ f. (pl. nom. -kōrĕ), a daughter of Kṛttikā, N. of any one of the six stars of Kṛttikā. The pl. is used to signify the entire constellation.

kriʦh, or krĕʦh f. N. of a certain plant, a green spiny potherb which grows spontaneously on grassy ground, prob. Cousinia Thomsonii, Clarke. This is a thistle-like plant, the leaves of which together with the spines are eaten by villagers as spinach in spring, when they are young and tender. Later on the shoots become woody and the spines very formidable (El. krits). ¶ kraʦi-kamürᵘ̈ f. one of the spines among the flowers of this herb; met. anything extremely thin or slender. -konḍᵘ m., id. -koṭᵘ m. (f. -küṭᵘ̈), a boy (or girl) who is lean and thin for want of proper nourishment. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a child who is lean and wasted for want of proper nourishment; hence, met. an orphan. -pōsh m. the flower of this plant. The flowers appear among the above spines.

kriʦh, or krĕʦh f. N. of a certain plant of the yam species, Dioscorea deltoides. It is used in medicine as a diuretic, and its tubers are used to provide a soap for cleaning wool (L. 75, 78, krits; El. knís or krís); the word is also used for the cleansing material itself. -mūl m. the tuber of this plant, used as ab.
m. trouble, pain, sorrow, affliction (mental or bodily) (Gr.M.; Rām. 208, 421, 989). Cf. krēṭh.
or krĕhañār m. blackness (literal or moral) (Gr.Gr. 139, -ñĕr).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. krĕhanyōv), to become black, to be made black (Gr.Gr. 21).

for krĕhonᵘ, in the following:--krĕhna-braz f. a kind of rice with dark-coloured straw and husk and a large white and red grain. -krṻḍ f. a kind of rice with dark-coloured straw and husk and a small white grain. -lyūṭᵘ m. N. of a kind of rice growing in marshy ground, with a small white grain. -māz  m. 'black flesh', the liver (El., Gr.M.). -māz-chal f. a piece of liver (Gr.Gr. 162). -sŏn m. 'black gold', a dark-soiled piece of ground, valuable for orchards or fruit gardens, which is very fertile and produces plenty of valuable fruit.

adj. (f. krĕhüñᵘ̈), black, dark-coloured (Gr.Gr. 139; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 116, kruhun; L. 159, kruhun; Śiv. 1543, 1704); morally black, black natured. --kṭa- (or -kta-) kāl-hyuhᵘ --(or --) adj. (f. krĕhüñᵘ̈ -- -hishᵘ̈ --), black like the black kāla-kūṭa poison swallowed by the Hindū god Śiva; hence, intensely black, jet black.

m. (sg. dat. krē̃kas), a stone set in a ring, the jewel of a ring (Rām. 609, 1249). Cf. nūna-kᵒ, s.v. nūn. ¶ krē̃ka-nadī f. N. of a river in the Lār Pargana of Kashmīr. It is passed by Hindū pilgrims on the way to Harmŏkh, and Śrāddha offerings to the deceased are made on its banks (Rām. 245). -nūn m. a pure kind of crystallized salt. -wöjᵘ̈ f. a ring in which a stone is set.

m. (sg. dat. krĕpas), cutting (with scissors, e.g. cloth or the hair (Gr.Gr. 123); (onomat.) the noise of such cutting, 'clip,' 'snip'; cf. kraph. krĕph-krĕph m. onomat. the noise made by such cutting, 'clip, clip,' 'snip, snip.'
(? spelling) N. of a certain plant eaten in time of famine (L. 71).
n.ag. (f. krēshĕvüñᵘ̈), one who eagerly longs for anything, one who ardently desires (YZ. 8).

f. N. of a certain fibre plant, Iris ensata (L. 68, krishm; El. kríshún, Iris pseudacorus). It grows wild on river banks, and besides being used for making ropes, is eaten by sheep. It has bright blue flowers. krĕshimi-raz f. a rope made of this fibre. These ropes serve many purposes in agriculture, but the fibre is not very durable (L. 69).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kryūshᵘ), to long for, covet, be eager to possess (YZ. 21).
m. (sg. dat. krēṭhas), trouble, pain, worry (mental or bodily).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. krēṭhyōv), to be hard, unyielding (of some material object); to be hard, inflexible in character (of a person).
(? spelling and gender), the European Common Tern, Sterna hirundo (L. 123, kreu, by which krēv is probably meant).
or krich m. onomat. a creaking or grating sound, such as that made by the teeth against a fruitstone, or by a Persian wheel at a well, or by a spinning-wheel. kric-kric or krich-krich m., id.
f. play, sport. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to play, to sport (K. 279).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. krīḍyōv), to play; esp. to play music.
(? spelling) m. a kind of vegetable (El.; cf. krami-hākh, s.v. kromᵘ).
onomat. m. in krith kaḍun m.inf. to make a slight sound in the throat (e.g. the sound of swallowing). Cf. kraṭh and kruth 1 and 2.
f. an act, action, i.q. kriyā (L.V. 63); esp. a good work, a holy action, a ceremonial act of religion, or the like (L.V. 63, K. 454).
adj. c.g. used --˚, a doer, a maker, as in sarwa-kriy, the maker of all things, the Creator (L.V. 59).
f. an act, action (Gr.M., Śiv. 1754). Cf. kriy 1.
f. of krāl, q.v., a potter's wife, a female potter (K.Pr. 144; W. 17; H. xi, 11); kröjⁱ-mās, the aunt of a potter's wife (L.V. 47, K.Pr. 47).
m. the scab of an ulcer, i.q. krôrᵘ, q.v. (only El.).

in the following:--krȧmⁱshĕr m. N. of a sacred place and village in Yĕch Pargana. ¶ krami-hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), a certain vegetable, the knol-kohl, Brassica oleracea, var. caulo-rapa (L. 72, 346, karm ság, karm hak, or kremi hák).

m. a kind of basket for holding grain made of earth or of withies; a kind of iron vessel for ladling out oil; a kind of lamp-post or iron torch holder, on the top of a pole or tripod. Cf. lashi-kronḍᵘ, s.v. lȧshⁱ.
m. abusive reproach, blame giving, scolding (Rām. 754, 1785); the mutual abuse of a number of people. This word is most often used with reference to the wordy warfare of women.

m. a woman's relations through her father or through her brothers-in-law (El. a tribe, a word used by Hindū women; Gr.Gr. 12, 23; K.Pr. 236; YZ. 23; Rām. 1780). Cf. krônᵘ 1. ¶ krāni nērun m.inf. to go outside the (custom) of the family; esp. to give more to a bride than the amount customary in the family; (of a bride) to go forth from her parent's house to live with her husband (Rām. 1036, 1586). ¶ krönⁱ-kôsⁱ adj. (f. -kösᵘ̈), removed far from the family; hence, born in a family which has no near relatives; one who has broken all connexion with his relatives. -küṭᵘ̈ f. a girl who is born in a family which has many respectable relations.

m. the scab or crust on a sore or wound (El. also król, i.e. krôlᵘ Gr.Gr. 12); the scum or skin that rises on the top of a vessel containing food. --bĕhun -- m.inf. scab to form on a sore. --tulun -- m.inf. to raise the scab from a sore; met. to raise the covering from over something hidden, to divulge a secret, to reveal a hidden matter.
f. a kind of cake made of inspissated milk and buttermilk mixed. It is eaten cooked in oil. Cf. maĩshĕ-kᵒ, s.v. mǖshⁱ.
m. ache or pain in the limbs (e.g. from rheumatism or from excessive weariness on a journey).
m. a kind of vetch, Dolichos uniflorus or biflorus, the kulthī or kurthī of India; (?) the krotha of L. 75, a medicinal plant used in renal calculus.
in krotᵘ-krotᵘ m. an indefinite or inarticulate sound issuing from the mouth, esp. the twittering of birds, or the munching sound of eating.
adj. (f. krüṭᵘ̈ 1) (of a rational being) thin (naturally), wasted away (by disease).
(in āra-krỗtᵘ, p. 40b, l. 50), adj. (f. krö̃ʦᵘ̈), overcome (by pity or other feeling).
(? spelling) N. of a certain fish found in Kashmīr (L. 158), ? khö̃ṭᵘ̈.

m. a kind of iron shovel with a long handle, used for drawing out coals from a fireplace. It is also used as a griddle; cf. gula- gula-k., p. 284b, l. 32 and nāra-k., s.v. nār 1 sarpa-kᵒ, p. 937b, l. 33; tāvi kraʦhi ladun, p. 1047b, l. 6 (L. 464, krúts). --lāgun -- m.inf. to retort fault-finding by fault-finding, to repay an accusation by a counter-accusation. ¶ krȧʦhⁱ-ashud m. a certain medicine used for the eyes when inflamed in the hot season. -worᵘ m. shovel-cake, a kind of cake made of rice-flour cooked on a shovel, a griddle-cake.

m. anger, wrath (Gr.Gr. 136; Gr.M.; L.V. 71; Śiv. 13, 18, 68, 92, 106, 118, 122, 170, etc.; Rām. 977, 982, 1514; K. 137, 561, 618, 796, 826, 903, 908, 1055); revenge (only El.). krūda-hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), angry, wrathful, full of wrath (Gr.Gr. 136).

m. N. of a kind of creeping plant, described as thorny and possessing a sweet-scented white flower. Cf. dŏda-krṻḍ (p. 189b, l. 3) and krĕhna-krṻḍ (p. 469a, l. 49). ¶ krṻḍa-pōsh m. the flower of this plant. -thürᵘ̈ f. the shrub or creeper plant itself. -zāl m. a thicket or mass of this creeper (Rām. 1252).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. krūdaladiñ), angry, passionate, wrathful (W. 21, krödalad).
f. (sg. dat. krūdāvēṭhi), an attack of wrath, a fit of rage. Cf. āvēṭh, p. 72a, l. 31.
adj. c.g. angry, passionate, violent in temper (Gr.M.; Śiv. 537; Rām. 709, 1416, 1428, 1724, 1753).

m. a certain measure of distance, the kōs of India, about two miles (Gr.Gr. 93; Rām. 536, 545-8, 600, 630, 741, 796, 885, 1070, 1301, 1601; K. 111); with suff. of indef. art. kruhāh (Rām. 1719). --kaḍȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to be at the point of death. -khanḍ m. about a kōs, but a little less (Gr.Gr. 93). ¶ kruha-bọ̆dᵘ m. several kōs, an indefinite large number of kōs (Rām. 1601, K. 193). ¶ kruhā-khanḍā or kruhāh-khanḍāh m. about a kōs, but a little less, i.q. kruh-khanḍ, ab. (Gr.Gr. 93). ¶ kruhāh m. about a kōs (Gr.Gr. 93). kruhāh sāsāh, a thousand kōs, an indefinite long distance (K.Pr. 45).
or kruhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. kruhĕ), acridity, roughness of taste; also met. cf. man-kruh, s.v. man 1, and kruṭh.
m. the weevil that breeds in husked rice (K.Pr. 183, krul); an insect (El. krēl; W. 115, kröl). Met. cf. mö̃ʦa-k., s.v. mö̃ʦh.
m. the withy or twig with which firewood is tied up into a bundle. krṻla-ganḍ m. the tying up of a bundle of firewood in this way.

for krūlᵘ, q.v., in krṻl khārun m.inf. to set up or paint the krūlᵘ pattern. ¶ krṻla-pach m. a kind of almanac of the first fifteen days of the new year, drawn up on a sheet of paper for the amusement of children. -ʦŏ̈ṭᵘ̈ f. a cake offered to the household god on the occasion of the painting of the krūlᵘ pattern.
m. a kind of auspicious vine- pattern painted in whitewash on the doors and walls of a house by the women of a family on the occasion of a marriage or similar festival (Śiv. 1075-6).

(Gr.Gr. 21) krümᵘ̈, or (Śiv. 855), kṻrm m. (f. krumiñᵘ̈, q.v.), a tortoise (Śiv. 1755, 1817; Rām. 599); a crocodile (only El. krím). According to Hindū mythology Viṣṇu's second incarnation was that of a tortoise, which supported Mount Mandara at the churning of the ocean (cf. Śiv. 855).
f. of krum, q.v. a female tortoise.

f. (sg. dat. kranjĕ), a kind of large basket made of withies; esp. used at weddings and similar festivities for holding the cooked food in quantities (L. 24; H. v, 7). --zālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to light fires of wood in earthen pots elevated on tripods at festivals or in times of rejoicing (such as welcoming the arrival of some great person). Cf. kronḍᵘ.
conj. (1 p.p. krupᵘ), to cut (with scissors, e.g. cloth or the hair) (Gr.Gr. 21); to scrape (only El.).
or krupyunᵘ adj. (f. krupiñᵘ̈), niggardly, miserly, one who grudges even necessary expenditure, mean (Gr.Gr. 139). Cf. krapan.

or kyūrᵘ (for *kryūrᵘ) m. [sg. dat. krṻris, krīris (K. 836, 838), or kīris; ag. krǖrⁱ, krīrⁱ or kīrⁱ; abl. krēri (K. 836, 839) or kēri ], a well (Gr.Gr. 18, 19; K.Pr. 256; L. 464 and W. 12, krur; Śiv. 1026, 1629). The form krūrᵘ is mostly used by Hindūs, and kyūrᵘ by Musalmāns. ¶ krǖrⁱ-bal or krīrⁱ-bal m. the ground round a well (Gr.Gr. 165). ¶ krīrⁱ-bal m., see krǖrⁱ- bal, ab. -carkh (sg. dat. -carkas), the windlass or pulley over a well over which the well-rope passes. -dayuth m. (sg. dat. -dayĕtas), the tutelary deity of a well, supposed to remain hidden therein and to guard the water. -pahī f. the framework over a well to which the rope is attached. -ʦôkᵘ m. the (wooden) cover of a well. -sag m. irrigation (usually of a vegetable garden) from a well. -wôñᵘ m. well-water (El.; Gr.Gr. 73; W. 115, krariwonⁱ).
adj. (f. krǖrᵘ̈), cruel, fierce, ferocious, harsh, pitiless, ruthless (L.V. 27), i.q. kūrᵘ 1.

adj. black, dark. As subst. m. Krishna (Skt. krṣṇa), N. of the eighth incarnation of the Hindū god Viṣṇu (Śiv. passim, K. passim); also a common Hindū proper name, e.g. that of the author of Śiv. (Śiv. 28, etc.).
f. vituperation, repeatedly cursing some one else (on the occasion of loss of money or similar calamity).
m. (a Skt. compound) an action done, esp. (among Hindūs) a deed done in a former life, affecting one's good or evil fate in the present life (Śiv. 1511).
adj. having attained one's desire, having accomplished one's object, satisfied, contented (K. 933).
f. acridity, an acrid taste. Cf. dᵃha-kruṭh, p. 198a, l. 28, kaṭh 3 and kruh 2.
onomat. m. the cheeping of a young bird; cf. kraṭh, krith, and kruth 2. -kruth m., id.
onomat. m. a very slight sound uttered by any animate being. Cf. kraṭh, krith, and kruth 1.
m. the breaking to pieces of the limbs (e.g. from a fall from a height, or from a merciless beating).

adj. [m. sg. dat. krīṭhis, abl. krēṭhi (Śiv. 333); f. sg. nom. krǖṭhᵘ̈ or krīṭhᵘ̈, dat. krēchĕ ], hard, severe (e.g. a sickness); hard, rough-mannered, bearish (K.Pr. 148; Śiv. 333, 769) (cf. mana-kᵒ, s.v. man 1); obtainable with great difficulty, to be found only after much labour (L.V. 51-4, 80; YZ. 386); painful, giving pain, difficult, hard (e.g. a road, or a grief) (Śiv. 842, 1630; Rām. 419, 517, 1010, 1430, 1489, 1751); often contrasted with myūṭhᵘ, sweet, e.g. Rām. 1430, 1489, 1751.
adj. (f. kruʦᵘ̈), unpleasant, not liked (of a quality, thing, or action).
f. (for 1, see kroṭᵘ sg. dat. kracĕ), chaff, chopped straw, chopped stalks of plants such as linseed (cf. ȧlⁱshi-kⁱ, p. 25a, l. 6), used for mixing with mud for plaster.

f. a ladle, a large spoon, a brazen or iron cooking ladle (El. krats). --khë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to eat the ladle'. When a Kāshmīrī Hindū is at the point of death a ladle is put into his hand, and from it food and other gifts are given to some outcaste Brāhmaṇa. The acceptance of this food is called 'eating the ladle'.
m. the wild white rose, Rosa Brunonis (El., kru̇r; L. 459, krir, a dog-rose).

(often, esp. in the Persian character, written khĕmā کہما, and so pronounced. So also in Rām. and K.) f. patience, forbearance, forgiveness (Rām. 38). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show forbearance (to), to forgive (Śiv. 53, 121, 705, 760, 768, 1115, 1165, 1186, 1283; Rām. 730, 1181, 1514, 1521, 1637; K. 89, 329); to show mercy, be merciful (Rām. 161, 1231, 1240; K. 911, 937).

(sometimes, esp. in the Persian character, written کہن, and so pronounced) m. a moment of time, an instant (Śiv. 605, 1042, 1341, 1405, 1439; K. 562, 778). ¶ kshĕna-kshĕna adv. at every moment, continually (Siv. 1412, 1427, 1437; K. 62). -mātᵃr m. (sg. dat. -mātras or -mātạras), a mere moment of time, an instant (Śiv. 854, 913, 930, 979, 1066, 1163, 1182, 1303).
m. (sg. dat. kshēpas), throwing, casting; passing (of time). Cf. kāla kshēph karun, p. 434a, l. 15 (a borrowed Skt. word used only by Hindūs).

m. loss or (Rām. and K.) khĕy کہی, waste, wearing away; removal, destruction (Śiv. 101, 1171, 1452, 1541, 1596; Rām. 227; K. 660) (a Hindū word generally employed with a religious application, such as destruction of sin, or the like, or of demons).

or khīr m. milk (Śiv. 207, 283, 1169, 1202, 1524; Rām. 80-1); (a Hindū word, mostly used with a reference to religious rites). kshīra-(khīra-)sāgar  m. the ocean of milk, one of the fabulous oceans by which, according to Hindū legend, the earth is surrounded (K. 14).
m. agitation, disturbance, distraction (Śiv. 22, 754, 843, 896, 930). (The word is borrowed by Hindūs from the Sanskrit kṣōbhaḥ.)

(or kta-)kāl (or) m. a corruption of the Sanskrit word kāla-kūṭa, the name of deadly black-coloured poison said to have been drunk by the Hindū god Śiva at the famous churning of the ocean. Cf. krĕhonᵘ, p. 469b, l. 12.

N. of a poor humpbacked girl (in Sanskrit Kubjā), who showed devotion to Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) on his way to fight the demon Kaṁsa. In recognition of her devotion Kṛṣṇa embraced her, and stayed a short time in her house (Śiv. 702, 1470; K. 425 ff., 520 ff.).
(K.Pr. 116), kucih (kuchih) (K.Pr. 5), incorr. for kuchĕ, kuchi, see kuṭhᵘ̈. kūcih (kūchih) (K.Pr. 239), incorr. for kōcĕ, see kūṭᵘ̈.
f. (sg. dat. kuci), the female breast, bosom (El.).
(? spelling) f. (sg. dat. kū̃ci), a corner (El. kúnch).
m. (sg. dat. kūcas), marching, march; journey; departure (El.).
m. onomat. the creak (of a door, a machine, or the like).
m. a grain-merchant, one who buys unhushed grain from cultivators, stores it, husks it, and then sells it. Cf. kọ̆thᵘ.
adj. c.g. pure, holy, blessed; an epithet of the Deity (Gr.M.).
m. N. of a certain inferior grain eaten by the poorer villagers, the kōdō of India, Paspalum scrobiculatum.
adj. (f.kuḍᵘ̈rᵘ̈), hard, difficult (of a road, mountain pass, or the like); coarse (El.); passionate, wrathful, hard to get on with, unbearable (K.Pr. 117).

(? spelling and gender), N. of a kind of small good apple (see El., s.v. ʦúnṭ). L. 349 spells the word kuddu sari, and says it is in shape long, and is juicy and rather acid, ripening early and not keeping.
i.q.kūrᵘ̈, q.v. This is the form used towards Bāramulā (El.).
m. an earthen pot or pan, a cauldron, a vat (cf. rangȧrⁱ-kⁱ, p. 838a, l. 42).
or (vill.) ködⁱ m. a captive, a prisoner (Gr.M.; H. v, 7, 8, 9; vi, 11; x, 5, 12; K. 998, n.pl. kǖdⁱ).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kuhᵘ, 2 p.p. kuhyōv), to pull up (shrubs, plants, etc.), to clear the ground preparatory to digging.
(cf. کنج) m. a corner (El.); an intermediate point of the compass, such as north-east, south-east, and so on. El. makes this word f.
or kū̃jĕl adj. c.g. possessing corners, angled (e.g. of something quadrangular or pentangular), i.q. kūnal.
or kujᵘ̈ f. a small or young tree; a bush, shrub (K.Pr. 36); a plant (as distinct from a tree) (K.Pr. 27, 80; W. 128). Cf. olici- kujⁱ, p. 23b, l. 45, and kulᵘ.
m. (sg. dat. kūkas), a loud shouting, shriek, or outcry made by a single person.
f. the hen of the black or Indian cuckoo, Cuculus indicus, the kōil of India. Cf. kukyulᵘ, of which it is f. (K.Pr. 9). In Śiv. 503 the pl. nom. is kukila.

m. (f.kukilᵘ̈), the black, or Indian, cuckoo, Cuculus indicus, the kōil of India (Śiv. 1814). ¶ kukila-phōj m. a flock of cuckoos (Śiv. 1860). ¶ kukili-hoṭᵘ m. a cuckoo's throat; met. a human voice sweet as that of the Indian cuckoo. -pǖrⁱ f. the putting down of the foot of a cuckoo, a cuckoo's gait; met. (of a beautiful woman) a gait charming as that of a cuckoo. -pôṭᵘ m. a kind of medicinal grass growing in wet ground. It is used as a laxative (L. 75, kakilipot; Śiv. 1808).
in byôlᵘ-kukᵘ, a cuckoo, see byôlᵘ-kukᵘ, p. 150a, l. 24 and zabi-kukᵘ, p. 1215b, l. 21; cf. kukilᵘ̈ and kukyulᵘ. (L. 138, shakuk or kuku, Cuculus canorus).
f. a kind of tall hat, worn especially by mendicant devotees and the like.
m. the totality, the whole; the whole (of), total, sum; all, universal; esp. the total (in counting, adding, etc.).
(? spelling), m. Viburnum fœtens (El.). Cf. kīl-mīch and kwīllim.
f. a kind of small disc-shaped cake made of flour, milk, sugar, clarified butter, etc. kulicĕ-worᵘ m., id.
sg. gen. f. of kulᵘ, q.v.

m. (sg. dat. kuluphas), a lock (of a door, chest, or the like), a padlock (K.Pr. 164, 220). --karun -- m.inf. to lock (El.). --muʦarāwun --, m.inf. to unlock (Gr.M.). --thāwun -- m.inf. to unlock (a door, etc.) (H. iii, 8).

m. (sg. dat. kulimis), N. of a kind of jasmine, Jasminum multiflorum, or J. hirsutum, or J. pubescens. ¶ kulimⁱ m.pl. the ornamental ivory knobs at the bottom of a lute, to which the strings are fastened. -pōsh m. the jasmine-flower.

m. (f. kujⁱ or kujᵘ̈, q.v.), a tree (K.Pr. 9, 60, 116, 168; YZ. 397; Śiv. 167, 182, 197, 267, 367-8, 497-8, 505, 713, 1025, 1208, 1396, 1651, 1678, 1813; Rām. 479, 602-3, 653, 692, 1097, 1178, 1407-8; K. 12, 111, 170 ff., 219, 232, 270 ff., 350, 775, 890, 970). When --˚, this word has a wider extension, and includes the idea of a creeper or a shrub, as in ala-kulᵘ (see al), a pumpkin-vine; dañĕwali-kᵒ (dañĕwal), a coriander shrub; datᵃ̇rᵃ̇-kᵃ̇ (daturᵘ), a datura shrub; cf. kujⁱ. It is also used in metaphorical senses, as in bata-kᵒ (p. 137a, l. 9), the food-tree, i.e. the bread-winner of a family. -koṭᵘ m. trees and the like, trees shrubs bushes etc. --pĕṭh pôñᵘ khārun -- m.inf. as it were to water a small seed of enmity, anger, crime, to fan a spark of anger, sin, etc., to foment such. ¶ kulⁱ-dadürⁱ f. a hollow in a tree, such as that in which a bird or other living creature takes up its abode (H. ii, 10); a kind of bird that lives in hollow trees. It digs out hollows in trees itself. ? a woodpecker. -gŏḍ m. the part of the trunk of a tree immediately above the root; the root itself. -goḍa-gardan f. a neck resembling the root of a tree, i.e. a thick neck, a neck grown thick by self-indulgence in eating and drinking. -gañĕr m. thickness of trees, the closeness together of trees in a wood, or the like. -kôṭᵘ m. a kind of bird that drills holes in a tree with its beak, ? a kind of woodpecker. -kôwᵘ m. a tree-crow, a kind of bird so heavy in body that small shrubs bend under its weight. -tihᵒrᵒ or tyuhorᵘ m. the top of a tree, a treetop (Śiv. 747). -wüñᵘ̈ f. a clump of trees, a grove of trees (natural or artificial) (W. 112, kuliwanⁱ). ¶ kuli-pĕṭhukᵘ bôjᵘ m. one who owns a share in the fruit of a tree; met. a shareholder in joint family property. -pĕṭhukᵘ ʦū̃ṭhᵘ m. an apple on a tree (which is visible to all, and which anyone can pluck); met. (in business) money, etc., which everyone can see and which anyone can take, as in asondᵘ dana chuh kuli pĕṭhukᵘ ʦū̃ṭhᵘ, his money is like an apple on a tree.
