adj. (m. pl. dat. kōlĕn; f. sg. nom. kūjᵘ̈, f. dat. kōjĕ), reddish-brown, tawny, ruddy (cf. kōlun).
m. N. of a village about twelve miles south of Śrīnagar.
m. softness, delicacy (e.g. of a flower, or of a hand) (Gr.Gr. 141); gentleness, tenderness; tenderness, softness (of food); softness (e.g. that of butter caused by warmth).
(Rām. 1173) or kūmal (Śiv. 1538) adj. c.g., i.q. kumolᵘ, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. kumalôwᵘ), to make soft or tender (e.g. food by cooking); to make a person's heart tender, to make him compliant by supplication, or the like; to soften, to melt (something congealed); caus. of kumalun (Gr.Gr. 170).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. kumalyōv), to become soft or tender (e.g. food by cooking); to become tender (of the heart), to be full of pity and grace (Śiv. 308, K. 82); to become soft, to melt (of ice, snow, butter, or the like) (El.).
or m. (in Hindū legend) N. of a demon, the brother of Rāvaṇa (in Skt. Kumbhakarṇa). He used to sleep for six months at a time and then wake to gorge himself (Rām. 636, 926).
m. (amongst Hindūs) a particular religious exercise, profound meditation brought on by closing the mouth and nostrils and thereby suspending the breath (Skt. kumbhaka) (L.V. 34, K.Pr. 187).
or m. N. of a certain astrological mansion, one of the signs of the zodiac, Aquarius, in Skt. kumbha (Rām. 1277, dat. kumbi).
adj. (f. kumüjᵘ̈), soft, delicate; gentle, tender; tender, soft (of food) (El. kumul); soft (e.g. butter when subject to warmth).
m. N. of a certain small bird, with a high melodious voice. Cf. kāwa- kumorᵘ (Rām. 675).
or f. N. of a certain bird, said to resemble the Indian cuckoo (kukilᵘ̈) (Śiv. 504). Probably fem. of kumorᵘ, q.v.
m. a corner (El., Gr. Gr. 18). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. a corner to come; in a machine, a driving band to become displaced.
(? spelling) in kŏkar-kun (L. 366), fowl-cholera, see p. 432a, l. 37.

postpos. (cf. kani 2 and kinⁱ) governing the dat. (Gr.M.), also used as a sec. suff. not governing any case (Gr.Gr. 160, Gr.M.); towards, in the direction of, to (W. 97). The following examples are taken principally from Śiv. and Rām. u.w. vbs. of motion (Śiv. 341, 532, 538, 654, 1010, 1193, 1196, 1209, 1275, 1437, 1555, 1560, 1709, 1722-3, 1745, 1860; Rām. 114, 205, 249, 388, 443, 495, 521, 750, 1193, 1207; H. viii, 6, 11). ¶ (a) As postpos.:--ath-kun, towards that, in that direction (p. 55b, l. 20) (Gr.Gr. 160); biyĕ-kun, (going) anywhere else (H. xii, 4); dakhĕnas-kun, (reached to the south) (Rām 632); danjĕ-kun wuchun, to look towards the condition (p. 226a, l. 8), to calculate resources; kŏli-kun, towards the river (p. 437b, l. 42) (Gr.Gr. 161); mājĕ-kun, towards the mother (möjᵘ̈) (Gr.Gr. 161); mölis-kun, towards the father (Gr.Gr. 161); tas-kun, (love) towards him (YZ. 77); tath-kun, towards that, in that direction (Gr.Gr. 160); ʦĕ-kun phīrᵘ̈, she turned towards thee (Rām. 1275); wārĕ-kun, towards the garden (Gr.Gr. 161). ¶ (b) As suffix:--ākāsh-kun, towards, or up to, the sky (Rām. 924, 1055); andar-kun, to within (p. 32a, l. 42); apôrᵘ-kun, to beyond (apôrᵘ); ōr-kun, in that direction (Gr.Gr. 160); otᵘ-kun, in that direction (p. 53a, l. 13); bŏn-kun, downwards (p. 110b, l. 8) (Gr.Gr. 161); brō̃ṭh-kun, towards the front (p. 128a, l. 23) forwards; in future (Śiv. 1756); gām-kun, towards the village (p. 286b, l. 30) (Gr.Gr. 160); gara-kun, towards the house (Gr.Gr. 160, Rām. 1370); but garas-kun (Rām. 1090, 1693); hyorᵘ-kun, upwards (p. 367a, l. 34) (Rām. 1410, contrasted with tȧlⁱ-kinⁱ, from below); kōr- kun, whither? (Rām. 513); nagar-kun, (went) to the city (Rām. 1554); tūrⁱ-kun, thither verily (Rām. 1254); wŏturᵘ-kun, towards the north (Rām. 632; cf. 783); yipôrᵘ-kun, in this direction (W. 95); yāra-sondᵘ-kun, in the direction of the friend's (house) (H. x, 11). ¶ From the idea of motion towards, there is developed the meaning of 'to' after verbs of saying, addressing, etc. (Śiv. 79, 86, 394, 429, 555, 708, 941, 1007, 1252, 1318; Rām. 55, 198, 209, 220, 252, 307, 371, 373, 379, 442, etc.; H. v, 2; vii, 4, 20, etc.), and various other dative senses, such as (making a bow) to (Śiv. 156); (looking towards or at) (Śiv. 584, 758, 760, 768, 1008, 1593, 1737; Rām. 245, 535-6, 670, 825, 980, 1048, 1084-5, etc.); (showing) to (H. vi, 5); (becoming manifest) to (L.V. 22, Śiv. 171); (turning the ear) to (Śiv. 544); (turning the mind) to, (having and inclination) to, (or taste) for, etc. (Śiv. 596, 750, 754, 1181, 1293, 1751); (devoting the mind) to (Rām. 565, 1134, 1673); (affection) to, (longing) for (YZ. 77; H. iii, 7; vii, 3); (good intentions) to (Rām. 521); (do service) to (Rām. 627); (give welcome) to (Rām. 751); (promise) to (Rām. 627); (arrive) at (Rām. 1167, 1428; H. x, 5); (happen) to (Rām. 536, 1116); (attach) to (Rām. 993, 1178); (wield a weapon) against (Rām. 40, 999); (go for refuge) to, (take refuge) with (Rām. 1291, 1478, 1584); (a test) in reference to, (a test) of (Rām. 459); (limbs pressed) to (limb) (Rām. 1117); akh akis-kun, one to, or against, the other (Rām. 518, 923). ¶ A further development is the meaning 'in', 'at', as in:--akith-kun, on one side (H. xii, 14); ōr-kun, on the far side, over there, as well as 'in that direction'; andas-kun, at the end (H. xii, 6); ath-kun, there, as well as 'in that direction' (p. 55b, l. 20); brō̃ṭh- (or bōnṭh-) kun, in front (H. i, 8; K. 555), as well as 'in a forward direction' (p. 128a, l. 23); dachan-kun, on the right-hand side (dachyunᵘ) (W.); hyorᵘ-kun or hyūrᵘ-kun, at the top, as well as 'upwards' (p. 367a, l. 34); khôwur-kun, on the left (W. 129); kōr-kun or kotᵘ-kun, where? as well as 'whither?' path-kun, at the back, behind (Śiv. 1194; H. v, 8); afterwards (H. iii, 5; v, 5); finally, ultimately (Śiv. 1344, 1901); (with verb in future) behind (the present time); afterwards, in the future (Śiv. 70, 311); (with verb in past) behind (the present time), formerly, in the past (Śiv. 72, 425, 1908; K. 347); pĕṭh-kun, above, in the place of honour (K. 476, 516).
adv. anywhere, at any place (Śiv. 1428), i.q. kuni 1, q.v.

f. a certain potherb, growing wild amidst other potherbs; it is also used medicinally in colds and inflammatory diseases, being considered cool and dry; it is said to be the same as the kulfa of India, Portulaca oleracea or purslane. It is believed to grow with particular freedom in famine years, when it is used for food (L. 71).

in kuna-pöthᵃr m. a present given to artizans employed in making the necessary materials on the occasion of a son's marriage; the present is given for good luck, and especially by a man who has only one son.
m. cornered, possessing corners, i.q. kū̃jal.
m. a kind of vessel, usually of earthenware, narrow at the bottom and wide at the top.
also spelt kunatöjī and kunātöjī card. c.g. thirty-nine (Gr.Gr. 77).

card., the word used for the numeral 19 in multiplication. It can only be used with numbers greater than ten, as in wuh kunawuhⁱ trih hath ta shīth, twenty nineteens (are) three hundred and eighty (Gr.Gr. 86).
m. a billet, a log; a trunk or stump of a tree; a kind of clog or wooden fetter (for prisoners).
m. pure gold, the finest gold (Śiv. 531, 1293). --char hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. --hishᵘ̈ --), like a drop of pure gold; hence, very flawless and brilliant.

f. (sg. dat. kanjĕ), the hard woody shell of a fruit, such as a walnut, pomegranate, or the like (K.Pr. 120; L. 353, kandi); used for the hard rind of a special kind of gourd, see ala-kᵒ, p. 22b, l. 16; an encampment, see gujȧrⁱ-kⁱ, p. 281b, l. 41. ¶ kanjĕ-nār m. a fire of such shells; esp. a fire of the shells of the water-chestnut. Cf. görⁱ-künḍⁱ, p. 298a, l. 31. L. 460 has incorr. kanga, for kanjĕ. -trọ̆pᵘ m. a certain method of sewing together pieces of cloth, 'top- sewing.'
f. of konḍᵘ 3, q.v. (sg. dat. kanjĕ), a miserly woman, a skinflint who stints even her necessary expenditure.

m. loneliness, solitariness; esp. the condition of one who has lost all his relations and is alone in the world; (in Śaiva philosophy) detachment from all conceptions, and consciousness only of the identity of the soul with the Supreme (Śiv. 1212).
(? spelling) Stipa sibirica, a kind of grass poisonous to cattle (L. 70).

adv. ever, at any time (Gr.M., K. 504); at some time, sometimes; anywhere, in any place (Gr.M.; W. 95; Śiv. 1428, kun; 23, 97, 846, 1540, 1666, 1757, kuni; Rām. 1158; H. viii, 7; K. 82, 152, etc.); somewhere (H. viii, 7); at all, in any respect (H. v, 6; viii, 1, 2, 9; xii, 1, 22; K. 641); prath kuni, everywhere (Gr.M.); har kuni, everywhere (W. 95); kuni-kani, in any way (H. xii, 13); with emph. y, kuniy, at any time (Rām. 1654); anywhere (Rām. 91) (El. kunyi). -kuni adv. sometimes, now and then (Gr.M.; K. 476, 480, 963, 992), wherever, in every place that (Rām. 739). -na adv. at no time; nowhere (El.; W. 95; L.V. 9, 11, nā kunē, m.c.; K.Pr. 201, nah kune).
f. in Hindū mythology, N. of the mother of the Pāṇḍavas, the heroes of the Sanskrit Mahābhārata (K. 535-46, 1015).

m. a 'blind' bunch of grapes, i.e. a bunch of grapes which began to form, but from which all the grapes have fallen or been removed while yet in an early stage, and before they have approached maturity.

kunzᵘ̈ or kūnzᵘ̈ f. a key (of a lock) (El. and Gr.M. kunz; K.Pr. 24 kunj; H. iii, 8, kunz; K. 465 kunzᵘ̈); cf. Hindī kunjī. kunzᵘ̈(kūnzᵘ̈)-kuluph  (cf. Arabic-Hindī قفل کنجی) m. key and lock; N. of a mode of dressing the hair in which the various locks are plaited (or interlocked) together in a special way; a method of tying a garment.
m. N. of a certain large aquatic bird.
kūnʦhāh; for kũʦhāh, kū̃ʦhāh; see kē̃h.

sometimes (e.g. Śiv. 329) written kun card. (f. kuñᵘ̈), one, only one, a single (Gr.Gr. 81; K.Pr. 119, 220; Śiv. 1239, 1544, 1561, 1622; Rām. 410); only, the only [as in kunᵘ nĕchyuwᵘ, an only son; so kunᵘ boktᵘ, the only devotee (K. 828)]; exactly one (Gr.M.); one and the same (Rām. 301); alone, by oneself (YZ. 436, Rām. 1623, K. 895); only, bare (El.). (K.Pr. spells kuñᵘ̈, kuni; and the dat. kuñĕ, kunih.) kunᵘ zonᵘ adj. (f.kuñᵘ̈ züñᵘ̈), a person alone, one all alone, by oneself, genl. used with a verb, as in 'sitting alone', and so forth (Śiv. 1199, K. 563). ¶ kunuy adj. (f. kuñᵘ̈y), only one (L.V. 84, 94; H. vi, 7; vii, 2; x, 8); a single (K.Pr. 9, 91, 117, 119, kunuī; Śiv. 25, 328, 512, 712, 715, 883, 898, 907, 912, 1274, 1281, 1443, 1548, 1643, 1646, 1756, 1763, 1764, 1768; Rām. 1229; K. 288, 761); one, become one, united (K.Pr. 83, of quarrelsome dogs becoming one for common object, kunī for pl. nom. kuniy); (of several things compared) one and the same, all one (L.V. 90; K.Pr. 125, kunī; K. 821); alone, by oneself (L. 458, kuni; Śiv. 779, 1189, 1713; Rām. 1361, 1744); left all alone, with no friends or relations, or (e.g. on a journey when one is separated from his fellow-travellers) companions, or the sole survivor (e.g. in a battle) (Rām. 981). --hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. kuñᵘ̈y hishᵘ̈), exactly similar (Hindī ēk sā) (Gr.M.). --zonᵘ -- adj. (f. kuñᵘ̈y züñᵘ̈), one who is alone (Śiv. 534; Rām. 1051, 1219, 1225; H. viii, 7; xii, 15); left all alone (e.g. of one on a journey separated from his comrades, or a single survivor in a battle) (Rām. 973, 1200). ¶ kuñᵘ̈y f. of kunuy, ab.; also, in the game of heads and tails played by children with cowries (in which a number of cowries are thrown up into the air, and those that fall open side downwards and upwards respectively are counted), when only one cowry falls with the open side downwards, and all the others fall with it upwards, the throw is called a kuñᵘ̈y, and the owner of the single cowry wins the game. kuñᵘ̈y (or kuñiy) züñᵘ̈ (or) f. of kunuy zonᵘ, ab.
adj. (m. pl. dat. kōnĕn; f. sg. nom. kūñᵘ̈, sg. dat. kōnĕ), cornered; used --˚ as in öṭha-kūnᵘ, eight-cornered, octagonal (p. 66b, l. 23).
m. the foundation (of a house, or the like) (El. kān and kan; Gr.M.; Śiv. 448; Rām. 607).

f. (sg. dat. kañĕ 2, for 1, see s.v.), a stone, a rock (L.V. 103; K.Pr. 34, 88, 95-6, 122, 183, 226; YZ. 108, 130, 234-6, 394, 496; L. 464 kánah; Śiv. 589, 602, 1463, 1902-4; Rām. 352, 397, 568, 787, 789, 918, 1037, 1174, 1197, 1251, 1433, 1587, 1694; H. vi, 7; K. 111, 890). (El. kain, kainyi, K.Pr. kane, kani, and kanih in various cases.) ¶ kañi-āra m. a rocky spring; a mountain stream. -chal f. a fragment of stone, a piece of stone broken off from a larger stone. -ḍēr m. a pile or heap of stones (K.Pr. 48). -hāl f. a kind of paddy; cf. koñᵘ 1. -hönzᵘ̈ m. a stone boatman, a boatman who makes his living by conveying stone in a boat. -har f. a stone quarrel, a fight or battle in which the combatants assail each other with stones flung from slings (common in Kashmīr in ancient times). -hürᵘ̈bāz m. a man who engaged in such a fight. -khō̃khur m. an irregular cavern created by a number of rocks naturally piled together, such as is found in wild mountainous country; cf. khã̄khur.-khraph f. (sg. dat. khrapi), a long fissure-like space between two rocks. -köjⁱ f. a flat stone on which condiments, etc., are ground with a muller (K. 151); cf. köjⁱ 2. -küñᵘ̈  f. stone on stone, i.e. mutual lapidation, a fight in which the combatants fling stones at each other; the punishment of death by stoning, lapidation (H. x, 13, kañĕ-küñᵘ̈). -küñᵘ̈ karun m.inf. (note that the verb is masc.) to kill a person by stoning, to execute a criminal by lapidation; met. to kill a person by any means. -küñᵘ̈trāwun m.inf. (note the inf. masc.) to leave (a person) to be killed by stoning, to deposit or set a person in a position for execution by lapidation. -lürᵘ̈ f. a stone house, a house built of stone; a house used for storing stone. -mŏnḍa m. a man employed to quarry stone in the hills, and to sell it when quarried, a quarryman. -nōl m. the broad strap at the end of the rope with which a ḍū̃ga, or boat, is towed (El. spells this word kanyinol, and it is given on his authority). -nôṭᵘ or -nỗṭᵘ m. a round smooth stone (such as is found in a mountain stream). -pholᵘ m. a small round stone or pebble (such as would not weigh more than an ounce or so), a particle of gravel (H. xii, 15); the pl. (kañi-phȧlⁱ) is used to mean gravel of the bladder (El.). -phürᵘ̈ f. a heap of stones measuring a yard (gaz) every way. -pōr m. the lower story of a house (built of stone, the upper stories usually being built of brick). -pyotᵘ m. the tip or point of a long rock or stone. -ʦôkᵘ m. a stone wall built round a square enclosure, preparatory to building operations or the like therein. -ʦŏl f. a fireplace for cooking, put together of loose stones for immediate requirements. -ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. a blow from a stone (K.Pr. 62, translated 'a slap of the hand'). -ʦyūnᵘ m. a stone pillar (e.g. in the doorway of a house, or at the corners to support the upper stories). -wotᵘ m. a shower of stones (e.g. when flung from an army of slingers). -waṭh m. (sg. dat. waṭas), a round stone, such as is found in the bed of a river, esp. one of moderate size that can be lifted by a man. ¶ kañāh (with suff. of indef. art.) a single stone (YZ. 107).

m. (sg. dat. kūpas, pl. dat. kōpan, Gr.Gr. 51), anger (L.V. 23; K. 328, 814); esp. anger of fate, misfortune, ill-luck (Rām. 1779). kūpas gaʦhun m.inf. to become angry (K. 325, 809, 813, 875, 895, 910).
m.pl. infidels, non-Muslims, idolaters, pagans (H. iv, 3) (for kuffār, the Arabic pl. of köphir, q.v.).
in kupȧtⁱgaʦhun m.inf. to become angry (esp. with some servant, or the like). Cf. kupᵘ and kupun.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. kupyōv), to be or become angry or wrathful (esp. of some great person or god wrathful at some act of disrespect). Cf. kupᵘ and kupotᵘ.
in kupⁱgaʦhun m.inf. to become angry (with some one); cf. kupun and kupotᵘ. kupi adv. angrily.
a paddle (L. 462) incorr. for khūrᵘ 4, q.v.
f. a groove or long mark cut in a main beam of a roof to receive the edges or ends of the boardings; a dirty crease in clean cloth. -wüṭᵘ̈ f. i.q. kura 1 in the sense of a groove.
f. N. of a certain small fish, found only in reedy water.
for kurᵃra, q.v. kura-ṭās m. the crack of a whip. Cf. also dura ta kura, p. 239a, l. 24.
card. a score, twenty (W. 104); probably a borrowing from Hindī. Only mentioned by W. (104).
m. N. of a certain village about two miles from the spot where, according to Hindū legend, Sītā descended into the earth (Rām. 1719).
(cf. کرسی) f. a chair; a foundation. The only authority for this word is El. Probably instead of 'foundation' we should read 'plinth'.
(? spelling) m. serpent stick, Staphylea emodi (El.). Cf. citra 2.
or kurakoṭᵘ m. iron slag, the remains after melting iron (Śiv. 1563, kurkoṭᵘ).
m. a kind of tunic (K.Pr. 124). Cf. kurtⁱ.
m. a measure of length, six gaz, each of which is about 1/2 an inch longer than an English yard (El.).
f. a kind of inner garment, said to be common in the Panjāb (El. kurtin). kurtañĕ-nürᵘ̈, the sleeve of such a coat (K. 419).
f. a kind of long quilted overcoat reaching to the knees. Cf. kurta.
(? spelling) m. Villarsia nymphoides (El. kúrú, 'it is very abundant in the lakes, and is used for fodder.' Cf. khair and khorᵘ 1).

m. N. of a people of Northern India, celebrated in Hindū legend as taking a part in the great war of the Mahābhārata. In this their leader was Duryōdhana (see bel.). -rāza m. the king of the Kurus, Duryōdhana (K. 893). Duryōdhana was never really their king. He was a son of the king, and leader of the Kuru army in the Great War. -yŏdd  m. war with the Kurus, fighting against the Kurus (K. 897).
(? spelling) m. a measure of rice straw, consisting of 96 bọ̆dᵘ or handfuls (see p. 84a, l. 6) (L. 328). Perhaps by this spelling korᵘ is meant.

m. (sg. dat. kurukshētras), (in Hindū mythology) the traditional scene of the great battle of the Mahābhārata between the Kurus and the Pāṇḍavas. It is the plain stretching south of Ṭhānēśvar towards Pānīpat in the Eastern Panjāb. Pilgrimages were made thither from Kashmīr; cf. RT.Tr. viii, 540, 2220 (Śiv. 927).
conj. 3(2 p.p. kṻryōv) (of someone or something previously gentle or soft) to become ruthless, cruel, fierce; to become hard. kǖryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. kǖryē-müʦᵘ̈), become fierce or hard, as ab.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kūrᵘ), to rub water into the hair to soften it before shaving the head.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. kūrᵘ 2), to gouge out, extract (e.g. the kernel of a walnut with a knife, or the eye; cf. p. 8a, l. 35); to loosen from the foundation, to make the foundation loose (Gr.Gr. xv). Cf. nasakh.
m. rubbish, sweepings, chips, litter (Gr.M.). Probably the same word as the preceding.

m. (in comps. this word sometimes takes the form kura 3, q.v.), a whip, a horse-whip, an ox-whip (K.Pr. 187); esp. a long whip made of pliant branches of the vine, with which gardeners frighten away birds during the vintage. Its crack is very loud (El.).

f. (sg. dat. kōrĕ), a young girl, married or unmarried (El.; Gr.Gr. 20, 36, 61 declined, 62; K.Pr. 16, 83, 119; YZ. 201; Śiv. 895); a virgin (YZ. 229); a daughter (Gr.Gr. 72, 134, 136; L.V. 92; K.Pr. 25, 31, 47, 54, 62, 71, 92, 137, 164, 241; YZ. 2; W. 9, 12, 18; L. 459; Śiv. 34, 38, 432, 533, 822, 871, 1313; Rām. 115, 1086, 1177, 1597-8; K. 66, 71-2, etc.; H. v, passim; xii, passim). With suff. of indef. art. kōrāh (Śiv. 34, 432; Rām. 115). ¶ This word is also spelt kūḍᵘ̈, and this pronunciation is common in the village dialect (H. v, 5, 12). ¶ kōri-bojᵘ m. the parent, guardian, or other person, who at a marriage formally and with due ceremony gives the bride to the bridegroom. -byôlᵘ m. (the growth of) a girl's seed, i.e. the gradual growth in character and disposition from babyhood to maturity (compared to tender shoots, flowers, and fruit coming in order from a single seed). kōri-dŏd m. the milk of a woman who has borne only a daughter to whom she is giving suck. It is used as an ingredient in medicines for curing deafness. -dadᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a girl who from the day of her birth is little and plump. -dil, -dilal, or -dinal m. one who habitually has incestuous intercourse with his own daughter (Gr.Gr. 107, -dinal; K.Pr. 4, horiadilh); a term of abuse. -dāwal m., id. (Gr.Gr. 107); also one whose daughter is unchaste. -gūdᵘ m. one who hankers after his daughter's privities, one who lusts after his own daughter (a term of abuse). -han f. a little girl (El., W. 113); a pet daughter (K.Pr. 70). -hār f. the daughter's cowry, i.e. amongst Musalmāns a few copper coins given to each daughter to represent her share in the distribution of the family inheritance. -khoḍᵘ m., i.q. -gūdᵘ, ab. -khã̄dar m. a daughter's a marriage ceremony (which is much more expensive than that of a son) (Rām. 864). -lagᵃn m. the auspicious astrological moment for the marriage of a daughter. -lĕkh f. (sg. dat. lĕki), indecent abuse alluding to a daughter or other girl, as in kōri-dil, etc., ab. -mahanyuwᵘ m. the appropriate conduct of a girl, extreme modesty, modest purity. -möjᵘ̈ m. the mother of a girl; esp. the mother of a bride; a mother of many daughters, or one who has only daughters and no sons. -môlᵘ m. the father of a girl; esp. the father of a bride; one who is the father of many daughters, or one who has only daughters and no sons. -nala m. one who acts as pimp for his own daughter. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ, Gr.Gr. 136), one who is a father or (f.) mother of many daughters (Gr.Gr. 134, 136); at a wedding, the father or (f.) mother of the bride.
f. an unripe grape, a sour grape. Vinegar is made from them (El. kur).
or (Śiv. 537) kūr adj. (for 2, see kūrun; f. kǖrᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 20), cruel, fierce, ferocious, harsh, pitiless, ruthless (W. 20, Śiv. 537, Rām. 457). Cf. krūrᵘ 2.
f. husked barley, whole barley groats.
f. (for 1, see karun 1), a woman who has never been pregnant, a virgin; a barren woman (El. kȧir). Cf. kūrᵘ̈.
f. curdled milk cooked and spiced, used as a relish with other food.
in kūrⁱkūrⁱ aʦun m.inf. to go so close up to another that the two seem, as it were, one person swallowed up in another.
in kūrⁱ-kōra m. i.q. kōra 2, q.v.

m. kuśa-grass, Poa cynosuroides, a sacred grass employed at various Hindū religious ceremonies (L.V. 45); N. of one of the sons of Rāmacandra, in Skt. Kuśa. His brother's name was Lava (see Lav). He was created by the saint Vālmīki out of a doll made of Kuśa-grass, as a substitute for Lava, whom he believed to be dead (Rām. 1296, 1327, etc.). For an account of his birth, see Rām. 1283 ff.

or kū̃shⁱ f. (sg. dat. kō̃shĕ), a kind of shoe with high iron heels, and the uppers lessening towards the heels. It was formerly used in Kashmīr for winter travelling. At the present day it is mostly used by women (Hindū or Musalmān of a very respectable class) (El. kúṅsh; K.Pr. 110, 111, 153, 219). Cf. kĕmȧtⁱ. ¶ kō̃shi-khalᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. an old worn-out shoe of this kind; see khalᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 2. -khŏr m. a single one of a pair of these shoes. -phrath m. (sg. dat. -phratas), an extremely worn-out shoe, more worn out than -khalᵘ̈rᵘ̈, ab.
adj. c.g. opened, uncovered; loose, wide (El.).
(sg. dat. kushĕwüʦᵘ̈), N. of the capital city of Kuśa, the son of Rāmacandra, in Skt. Kuśāvatī (Rām. 1738).
or kasūr m. a fault, a defect (El. kasūr; Gr.M.; H. vii, 13).
m. (f. kusᵘ̈, q.v.), an unchaste man, a libertine, a debauchee, a fornicator, a lecher.
f. of kusᵘ, q.v. a publicly and obscenely unchaste woman, a drab, a strumpet (obsc.).

adj. (f. kū̃sᵘ̈. When not followed by a mātrā-vowel or by -is of the m.sg. acc.- dat., the base of this word is kö̃s-, kaĩs-, kö̃ʦh-, or kaĩʦh-) youngest brother (or sister) (of a group of brothers and sisters or the like), the youngest child of a family (Gr.Gr. 141, K.Pr. 83, YZ. 436), (a youngest son is the father's butt, the mother's scorn, and the brothers' fag, K.Pr. 83). --hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. kū̃sᵘ̈ hishᵘ̈), i.q. kū̃sᵘ (YZ. 418). --ʦāṭh -- m. (sg. dat. kū̃sis ʦāṭas), the youngest (i.e. the last entered) boy in a school or the like. ¶ kö̃sa- (or kaĩsa-, or kö̃ʦha-, or kaĩʦha-) koṭᵘ, (or, or, or) m. (f. -küṭᵘ̈), the youngest son (or f. daughter) of a family.
m. (sg. dat. kutakas), beating, whipping, flogging (esp. of school correction).
m. the captain of a fortress; hence, the chief officer of police of a city or town, the chief constable, the city magistrate (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 114; H. v, 7, 8, etc.). Cf. kōṭapāl.
f. the office or post of chief constable, etc. (Rām. 512).

m. a fortress (cf. kōṭha). kūṭa-rāj m. the rule of a fort, i.e. the rule of a freebooter who has established himself as a petty king in some fort, and levies tribute from the surrounding country (a common occurrence in old times). Cf. andar-kūṭh, p. 32a, l. 44.
m. (sg. dat. kūṭas), a heap, a pile. Cf. an-kūṭh, p. 29b, l. 25.
m. a wooden granary (L. 460). Cf. kōṭha and kuṭhᵘ̈.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. kuṭhyōv), to become poverty stricken, to be hard up (owing to want of employment, diminution of business, or the like), to become distressed, to be in distress; (of times) to become hard (L.V. 91).
adj. (f. kuṭhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 1), difficult of accomplishment, requiring labour for carrying out.

m. a room in a house, a chamber, a closet (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 95, 121, 124, 220; YZ. 343; Rām. 1627; H. iii, 8; vi, 3; ix, 4, etc.); esp. the floor or floors between the ground floor and the top- most floor of a house (El. kuṭ, K.Pr. 237); (in astrology) a room or mansion in which some constellation is at some particular moment. Cf. ạgᵃnᵃ-kuṭhᵃ, p. 16b, l. 36. ¶ kuṭhⁱ-nakawôrⁱ m. 'a room-nostril', a very small room, a tiny closet. -pōr m. the particular floor or story of a house (usually the first floor or middle story), which is divided into rooms (L. 461, kutphor; Śiv. 1246). ¶ kuṭhi adv. in a room, in the room (used in this form in the sense of the locative).

f. (sg. dat. kuchĕ), a granary (K.Pr. 5, Śiv. 1248); (a tradesman's) shop or storehouse (K.Pr. 26, kūṭ). Cf. kōṭha. ¶ kuchĕ-hönzᵘ̈ m. a boatman who pounds rice at so much a kharwār for the great folk in the city of Śrīnagar. These men keep boats to carry the rice about in (K.Pr. 116, kuchĕh-hánz).
or kūṭhürᵘ̈ f. a small room, a closet (L.V. 101, kūṭhᵘ̈rᵘ̈; K.Pr. 50, written kotrī for kūṭhᵃri, sg. abl.).
m. a title of Śiva, as the presiding deity of kūṭⁱhēr and kūṭi-tīrᵃth, qq.v., in Skt. kōṭīśwara (Śiv. 1166).

or kūṭī-tīrᵃth m. (sg. dat. -tīrthas), N. of a Kashmīr site sacred among Hindūs on the bank of the river Vĕth (Jehlam) near the western extremity of the town of Bārāmūla (RT.Tr. II, 483; Śiv. 1080, 1166, 1172).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kuṭᵘ; 2 p.p. kucyōv), to pound, crush, reduce to powder (L.V. 80).

or kūṭunᵘ m. (sg. dat. kūṭanas), a piece of a staff or stick (not a piece of any wood, but of a straight piece prepared for some purpose) (Gr.Gr. 148, K.Pr. 126). Cf. kūṭᵘ and lōri-kūṭun, s.v. lūrᵘ̈, --˚ a piece in a wider sense, as in ạndᵃram-kᵃ (p. 32b, l. 38), and nāni-kᵒ, s.v. nān. In cum-kᵒ (p. 171b, l. 26) it is used metaphorically.
pron. adj. (f. kǖtimᵘ̈), consisting of how many? of how many? Cf. kaʦyumᵘ.
pron. adj. (f. kǖtiñᵘ̈), of how much price? of what price? how highly priced? worth how much? (Gr.Gr. 148).

pron. adj. [m. sg. dat. kṻtis; ag. kǖtⁱ; pl. nom. kǖtⁱ (written kṻty, Śiv. 164, 435; Rām. 176, 701, 1342; K. 981, or kītⁱ کیتِ, YZ. 24) (Śiv. 712-3, 742, 1067, etc.; Rām. 35, 690, etc.; K. 478; H. vii, 25) or (old) kaitⁱ (written kötⁱ YZ. 25) (L.V. 81); in Śiv. 1872, with emph. y; exceptionally küʦᵘ̈y, for the sake of rhyme; dat. kaitĕn or kötĕn; ag. kaityau or kötyau. ¶ Fem. sg. nom. kǖʦᵘ̈ (YZ. 231), köʦᵘ̈ (H. vii, 15), or küʦᵘ̈ (I.K. iv, 114); ag. kāʦa (H. i, 12); pl. nom. kaiʦa (L.V. 81), or kṻʦa (K. 936), or köʦa, or kaʦa (I.K. iv, 114; Śiv. 1663; H. x, 6). ¶ The base of this word is kat- or, more usually, kait- or köt-. The vowel ai or ö of the latter is changed either to ū or to ṻ before a mātrā-vowel, and in the m.sg. acc. ¶ When the suff. of the indef. art. is added to kūtᵘ, the latter becomes kōtāh, or sometimes kaitwāh or kōtwāh, for which see bel.] ¶ how much (Gr.Gr. 59, 91; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 17; Śiv. 415, 496, 1181, 1253; Rām. 1613; K. 1103-4); (in pl.) how many? (see bel.). This word is very frequently used in the sense of our 'how much!' to signify a great quantity, an immeasurable quantity, or (in the plural) 'innumerable'; e.g. K. 28, 142, 478, etc., and so elsewhere, passim. --kôlᵘ -- adj. (f. kǖʦᵘ̈köjᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, what time? of what date? -sanā, i.q. kūtᵘ, but with a shade of doubt, quasi 'I wonder how much'. -tām, -tāmath, -tāñ, or -tāñĕth pron. adj. indef. (f. kǖʦᵘ̈-tām, etc.), of some indefinite quantity, (pl.) of some indefinite number. The underlying idea in the mind of the speaker is a question with doubt, as in, e.g. 'did he give anything? if so, how much?' (Gr.Gr. 256). ¶ kǖtⁱ, or (Śiv. 164, 435) kṻty, or (L.V. 81) kaitⁱ m.pl. of kūtᵘ (for f., see ab.) how many? (Gr.M.; YZ. 24, کیتِ; Śiv. 435; Rām. 35, 738, 1377, etc.); often used to mean 'very many', 'innumerable', as in (Śiv. 164, 712-3, 742, etc.; Rām. 1082, 1323, etc.); similarly kē̃h kǖtⁱ, very many (Rām. 690). With emph. y, this word becomes kaitiy (K.Pr. 243, spelt kahtī). ¶ kōtāh, kaitwāh (K. 568, 637, 783), or kōtwāh (K. 821, 1014, 1131) pron. adj. [pl. nom. kaityāh or kötyāh (see bel.); f.sg. and (Rām. 1627) pl. kaiʦāh (Rām. 98, 372; K. 427, 526, 532, 610) or köʦāh (Śiv. 47, 1235, 1255)], how much? how great? (Gr.M.; YZ. 60; Śiv. 435, 538, 703, 748, 870, 917, 971, 1255, etc.; Rām. 645, 1208, 1571, 1610; H. vii, 24). Like kūtᵘ this word is often used to mean 'very much', 'very many', e.g. Śiv. 47, 495, 653; Rām. 792, 1053; K. 275, 428, 445, 523, etc. This word is the form taken by kūtᵘ when the suff. of the indef. art. is added. In K. 821 kōtwāh is treated as indeclinable, agreeing with a noun in the sg. abl. --kāl -- m. how much time? how long a period? as adv. for how long? ¶ kṻtis adv. (m. sg. dat. of kūtᵘ), for how much? hence, for what price? at what price? ¶ kaityāh (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1486; K. 786, 1070; H. ix, 5, 11) or kötyāh (YZ. 29, 41-2, 184; H. vii, 31; x, 7, 8; xii, 20) (pl. of kōtāh, ab.) how many? i.q. kǖtⁱ (cf. Śiv. 164, 1486, and H. xii, 20, where both forms are used side by side) (K.Pr. 11, spelt kātiyāh, 248, spelt kahtyāh).

m. (pl. dat. kūṭĕn not kōṭĕn, Gr.Gr. 56), a large beam or log of wood, suitable for building or the like, a beam (Gr.M., L.V. 23, Śiv. 1080) (cf. nȧrⁱ-kⁱ, s.v. norᵘ); a long slender stem of a tree (El. kūṭ); met. a pillar or anything extended in length (cf. nāra-kᵒ, s.v. nār, and nörⁱ-kⁱ, the stem of a blowpipe, s.v. nôrᵘ). [L.V. has sg. abl. kōṭi for mod. kūṭi.] ¶ kūṭⁱ-laṭⁱrⁱ or -laṭᵃr f. the end of a beam which is cut off as not required, when the beam is being fitted into its place (Gr.Gr. 37). -türᵘ̈ f. the tenon at the end of a beam, fitting into a mortice in the beam to which it is fitted and joined.

f. (sg. dat. kōcĕ), a piece, a fragment (K.Pr. 239); esp. a long thin piece (as a short length of thread, a strip of paper, a piece of lotus-filament (nadȧrⁱ-kⁱ), or a strip of meat (māz-kᵒ); with suff. of indef. art. kūṭᵘ̈āh, a single piece (K.Pr. 15, kuṭāh, translated 'food'). Cf. dövⁱ-kⁱ, p. 262a, l. 21; kākaz-kᵒ (p. 433a, l. 47); s.v. nadorᵘ, nadȧrⁱ-kⁱ; and s.v. nĕchapatᵃr, nĕchapatri-kᵒ).

f. (sg. dat. kacĕ, Rām. 1319), a sprout, a seedling sprout, a blade of grass or the like (Śiv. 1049); a female child, a daughter. As in the case of koṭᵘ, q.v., of which it is the f., this word is generally used with reference to a caste or profession, but this f. form is principally used only with reference to some mean or despised profession (cf. kaṭh 2) as in bā̃ḍa-kütᵘ̈, a buffoon's daughter; wāza-küṭᵘ̈, a cook's daughter. Hence used in metaphorical expressions, such as (Rām. 1319) shikas-küṭᵘ̈, a daughter of defeat or misery, i.e. an unfortunate woman. kacĕ-bacĕ m.pl. (a comp. of which the first member is f.pl. and the second m.pl.), all the children (esp. little children), girls and boys, of a family, i.e. daughters, sons, grandchildren, etc.

m. N. of a sacred place in the valley of the ārᵃpath, to the east of Islāmābād in Kashmīr, the Kōṭhēr of RT.Tr. II, 467. According to Stein, the name represents the Skt. Kapaṭêśvara, but Śiv. plainly refers it to the Skt. Kōṭîśvara (Śiv. 1166). Cf. kūṭīśŏr and kūṭi-tīrᵃth.
m. N. of an elephant belonging to Kaṁsa, which was killed by Kṛṣṇa (K. 373; cf. 431 ff.).
or kuvīr m. (in Hindū legend) the god of riches and treasure, and regent (lōkapāla) of the northern quarter (Śiv. 1154, 1819; K. 591).
adv. by what means? how? (H. v, 9). Poet. for kawa, see kyāh.
(? cf. Pers. کوزہ) m. a kind of sweetmeat (Gr.Gr. 15). Cf. nābad-kuza.

m. wild indigo, a small shrub, generally found in villages near mountains; Indigofera heterantha (El. kuts; K.Pr. 184, kuʦ L. 68, 70, 461). The twigs are used in basket-making; cf. gura- küʦhᵘ̈, p. 298b, l. 19, and köñᵘ̈ 2. -ʦᵃñĕ f.pl. charcoal made from this plant.
m. (f. kuʦarĕñ), see gūlⁱ- kuʦorᵘ, p. 284a, l. 46.

or kuʦurᵘ m. (f. kutsürᵘ̈ 1 or kuʦᵘ̈rᵘ̈), a young dog, a puppy (K.Pr. 83, 121) (cf. nĕñĕ-kᵒ, s.v. nĕñĕ 2). (When a human being is spoken of metaphorically as a puppy, the fem. is kuʦarĕñ; cf. drāga-kᵒ, p. 241b, l. 22, and kuʦorᵘ 1.) kuʦari-karañĕ f.pl. puppy actions, puppy coaxings, the coaxing and fondling shown to each other by children.
f. a small penis, esp. that of a baby. Cf. mŏma-kuʦurᵘ, the nipple of the breast (s.v. mŏm).
see kotᵘ-motᵘ, s.v. katun 1, p. 490b, l. 44.
(? spelling) m. the Guelder, Viburnum fœtens (El.), a honey-flower; i.q. kīl-mīch, q.v.
f. a stone mortar (for pounding salt, spices, or the like). ¶ kwöji-tīl m. oil crushed out in such a mortar. -waṭh m. (sg. dat. waṭas), the stone pestle of such a mortar.

pron. inter. [In the sing. this pron. is an. or inan., and the an. forms in some cases distinguish between the masc. and fem. genders. The inan. forms when used as substantival pronouns make no distinction of gender; but, when used as an adjectival pronoun, in the nom. either the inan. or the an. form may be used in agreement with an inan. noun. If the an. form is used it agrees with the noun in gender. In the plur. there is no distinction between an. and inan., and gender is distinguished only in the nominative. ¶ The gen. sg. and pl. is used only as a substantival pronoun. When used as an adjectival pronoun in agreement with a noun in the gen. sg., the pronoun is put into the an. dat. if the noun is an. masc. (as in kamis nĕcivⁱ-sondⁱ, of what boy?). It is put into the inan. abl. if the noun is inan. masc. (as in kami kᵃsmukᵃ, of what kind?), and is put into the an. fem. dat. if the noun is fem., whether an. or inan. (as in kami kōrĕ-hondᵘ, of what girl? kami kāmĕ-hondᵘ, of what work?). In the plural there is no difficulty. If the pronoun is adjectival and in agreement with any noun in the gen. plur., it is, as usual, put into the dative plural, as in kaman nĕcivĕn-hondᵘ, of what boys? kaman kōrĕn-hondᵘ, of what girls? kaman kāmĕn-hondᵘ, of what works? ¶ In the an. dat. sg., kamis is used for both masc. and fem. if the pronoun is used substantivally; but if it is used adjectivally, in agreement with an an. fem. noun, the fem. form is kami, not kamis. The inan. dat. sing. is used both substantivally and adjectivally. ¶ Sg. nom. an. m. kus, kusᵘ (poet.); f. kŏssa; inan. kyāh: dat. an. (m. and f.) kamis, kas; f. (only as adj.) kami; inan. kath: gen. an. (m. and f.) kȧmⁱ- sondᵘ, kasondᵘ, kas; inan. kamyukᵘ, kawukᵘ: ag. an. and inan. m. kȧmⁱ; f. kami: abl. an. and inan. (m. and f.) kami, kawa. Pl. nom. m. kam; f. kama: dat. (m. and f.) kaman: gen. (m. and f.) kaman-hondᵘ, kahondᵘ, ag. and abl. (m. and f.) kamau, kamav. For most of the above forms see Gr.Gr. 89 and Gr.M. See also the references bel. ¶ In the word kyāh, the final h is often dropped, so that we also find kyā. In the Persian character the word is generally written kyah or kĕh کیہ (Gr.M., K.Pr. 15).] ¶ Who? which? what? ḍĕṭha kyāh, a great deal; see ḍĕṭha. As an adjective kyāh in all its adjectival forms is sometimes used in an exclamatory sense, i.e. what! in the sense of our 'what a!', 'how wonderful!', 'how beautiful!', 'how extraordinary!', and so on, as in kami lōla, with what (passionate) love (Śiv. 957; so L.V. 78; Śiv. 426, 661, 812, 814, 943, etc.; Rām. 4, 22, 155, 175, 556, 769; K. 223). Cf. the use of the word kyāh as an interjectional adv., bel., p. 500a, l. 12. ¶ Or, again, this pron. may be used contemptuously to mean 'what?', in the sense of 'nothing at all' or 'very petty', as in ʦŏmbi kus kan, who (i.e. no one) will pierce the ears (Śiv. 1290); wuñ kyāh pĕv, now what has fallen? i.e. what has fallen now is a mere nothing (Śiv. 1294; so Śiv. 1811); wāti kas and, for whom (i.e. for no one) will she reach completion? (Rām. 128). ¶ This pronoun, compounded with the indefinite pronoun kũh, itself takes an indefinite meaning, as in kũh kus, anyone whatever (Rām. 715); kũh kyāh, some kind or other of (Rām. 231, 373); kũh kath jāyĕ, in any place, anywhere (Rām. 689); kũh kami sāta, at any time (Rām. 836). ¶ kĕh for kyah (i.e. kyāh, see ab.) in the following:--kĕhŏ or kĕhō adv. an inter. particle, i.q. kyā and kyāh, bel., used familiarly in addressing a younger or inferior male; cf. the next and kyā-bā, bel. (kĕhŏ, H. v, 4, 5; kĕhō, K.Pr. 87). kĕhay adv. the same as the preceding, but used when addressing a younger or inferior female. Cf. kyā-biñ, bel. ¶ kahondᵘ adj. (f. kahünzᵘ̈), pl. gen. of whom (pl.)?, u.w. ref. to persons or things, masculine or feminine (Rām. 766); m. sg. abl. kahandi-sṻty, through whose instrumentality? through whom? (Rām. 176), i.q. kaman-hondᵘ, bel. ¶ kam 3 (for 1, 2, see s.vv.) (f. kama), m. pl. nom. who? which? u.w. ref. to persons or things; as subst. (Śiv. 742, 1811; Rām. 1213; H. xii, 1); as adj. (L.V. 39, 109; Śiv. 1037; Rām. 122, 1619; K. 223, (fem.) 275). --kam 2 --pl. m. (for 1, see kam 1) (f. kama kama), which (pl.) out of several; how many kinds of, usually in a commendatory sense, how many great (kings, gods, or the like), and so on (Śiv. 129, 413, 586, 970, 1719, 1847; K. 638). ¶ kamau pl. ag. and abl. (m. and f.) by or from whom? also written kamav (Rām. 9). ¶ kȧmⁱ m. sg.ag. (f. kami), by whom (an. or inan.)? as subst. (YZ. 147; Śiv. 576, 738, 826, etc.; Rām. 78, 159, 160, etc.; K. 903; H. iii, 3; x, 12); as adj. (Rām. 184, 1191). -sondᵘ adj. (f. -sünzᵘ̈), sg. gen. (an., m. or f.) of whom? whose? (Rām. 1241). Another form of this sg. gen. is kasondᵘ, q.v., bel. ¶ kami 1 f. of kȧmⁱ, ab., q.v. (Rām. 346, adj. inan.; K. 1115, id.). ¶ kami 2 f. sg. dat. when used as adj. See ab. ¶ kami 3 sg. abl. (an. or inan., m. or f.), from whom? from what?; as adj. (L.V. 41, 84, 85; Śiv. 528, 661, 812, 1041, etc.; Rām. 340 inan. m., 1084 id., 1210 id., 1579 an. f., etc.; K. 514, 653, 1121). (K. 607, 1117). --khötᵃra -- adv. wherefore? why? (El.). -kani adv. for what? wherefore? why? for what reason? (Gr.Gr. 159). --mŏkha -- adv. on what account? for what reason? wherefore? (H. x, 4). --pörⁱ -- adv. from what direction? whence? (Gr.Gr. 159, K. 799); in what direction? (Gr.Gr. 151, 159). --pāryukᵘ -- adj. (f. --pāricᵘ̈ --), of, or belonging to, what direction? of where?; born, or produced, where? -pata adv. after whom? after what? behind whom or what? --pöṭhⁱ -- adv. in what manner? how? (K. 602, 607, 799). -patukᵘ adj. (f. -patücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, behind whom or what?; born, or produced, since what? -puʦhy adv. for what? why? (Gr.M.; Rām. 1361, 1649). --ranga -- adv. in what manner? how? (Gr.Gr. 154, Gr.M.). --sana --, see kus sana, bel. (Śiv. 1600). --tām -- (Śiv. 1725, 1861) or --tāñ --, see kus tām, kyāh tām, bel. --vizi -- at what time? when? (Gr.Gr. 157). ¶ kamū, i.q. kam 3, ab., with an interjectional ū attached, O who? (m. pl. nom.) (Rām. 215, used by a woman in impassioned verse). Cf. kasū, bel. ¶ kaman pl. dat. (m. and f.) to whom? (Rām. 1441 an. m.); as adj. (Rām. 687 an. f.). -hondᵘ (f. -hünzᵘ̈), pl. gen. (an. and inan., m. or f.), i.q. kahondᵘ, q.v., ab. ¶ kamis an. sg. dat. to whom? (m. subst. and adj.; f. only subst.); as subst. (Śiv. 244, 532, 845, 1796; Rām. 997, 1230, 1347). ¶ kamav, see kamau, ab. ¶ kȧmiy, i.q. kȧmⁱ, ab., with emph. y (Śiv. 574; Rām. 1023-5). ¶ kamyukᵘ inan. sg. gen. (f. kamicᵘ̈), of what? (H. vi, 13, 14). ¶ kas an. sg. dat. to whom? as subst. (L.V. 17, 21, 33; Śiv. 278, 286, 583, 738, etc.; Rām. 218, 340, 447; 1620 f.; K. 290, 304, 545, 581, 846). In Rām. 1347 kas and kamis are used side by side with identical meanings. As adj. (Rām. 351 m., 1319 f.). Often used as an an. sg. gen. (or dat. of possession) (Śiv. 91, 189, 243, 324, 585, etc.; Rām. 1576; K. 175, 1057, 1111, etc.). Used with force of acc. whom? (Śiv. 249, 534, 1298, etc.; Rām. 1307). The use of this form as an adj. is rare. The only instance noted is kas dēvas, to what god? (Śiv. 243). ¶ kasū, i.q. kas, with interjectional suffix ū, to whom? (Rām. 211, 1532). Cf. kamū, ab. ¶ kŏsa poet. for kŏssa. See kus, bel. (Rām. 1609). ¶ kus or (e.g. L.V. 39) kusᵘ (f. kŏssa, or (poet.) kŏsa, or (vill.) kusa. See kŏssa, bel.), sg. nom. m. an. (and, as adj., also inan.) who? as subst. (L.V. 7, 78, 88; Śiv. 47, 243-9, 432, 472, etc.; Rām. 176, 238, 293, 738, etc.; K. 31, 98, 327, etc.; H. xi, 2; xii, 1); as adj. an. (L.V. 14, 39; Śiv. 1887; Rām. 882, 1324); as adj. inan. (L.V. 78; Śiv. 1062, 1226, 1770, 1831, 1912; Rām. 1605; K. 1161). With emph. y, kusuy, who really? (H. xi, 19). --hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. kŏssa hishᵘ̈), like what? what kind of? (Gr.M.). --kus -- who or which of several (f. sg. nom. kŏssa kŏssa, etc.; H. x, 6, kusa kusa). --sana -- or --sanā -- pron. inter. (f. kŏssa sana or --sanā --; inan. kyāhsana or --sanā --, q.v., bel.), i.q. kus, but implying a shade of doubt (Gr.Gr. 180 ff.), quasi 'I wonder what', 'what kind of' (L.V. 39, kawa sana, adj. inan. sg. abl.; Śiv. 1600, kami sana; Rām. 1408, kus sanā wã̄dur, I wonder what monkey (this is); so K. 287, kŏsa sana). Hence, often used indefinitely, 'I wonder who,' i.e. 'someone or other' (Rām. 834, m. sg. ag. kȧmⁱ sanā). --tām -- m. (f. kŏssa tām, etc.), i.q. kus, but implying a doubt if there is anything to ask, as in kus tām āv (did anyone come? If so) who came? (Gr.Gr. 256); someone or other, someone indefinite (W. 137; L.V. 86; K.Pr. 164; Śiv. 1725, 1861); used sometimes as an indefinite pronoun, or as an indefinite article, a, a certain (Gr.M.). --tāmath --, --tāñ--, or --tāñĕth (f. kŏssa tāmath, etc.), id. (Śiv. 85 --tāñ; Rām. 1397, kam tāñ, I wonder who = some unknown people; H. v, 4, --tāñ; viii, 10, --tāñ). ¶ kusa, vill. for kŏssa, q.v. and see kus, ab. ¶ kasondᵘ adj. (f. kasünzᵘ̈), sg. gen. (an., m. or f.) of whom? whose? (Śiv. 534, 805, 1794; Rām. 965). Another form of this gen. sg. is kȧmⁱ-sondⁱ, ab. ¶ kŏssa, or (poet.) kŏsa, or (vill.) kusa, f. of kus, ab., q.v. As subst., who? (L.V. 7; Śiv. 1091; K. 919, kŏsa); as adj. an. f. what? (L.V. 39); as adj. inan. f. what? (Śiv. 1041, 1237, 1682, 1710; Rām. 1609, kŏsa; K. 1003, kŏsa, 1092, id.). ¶ kusuy, see kus, ab. ¶ kath, sg. dat. inan. to what? for what? or (used as acc.) what? as subst. (Śiv. 763, 901, 1031, 1228); as adv. for what? i.e. how? (Rām. 1580); as adj. (Śiv. 16, 832, 889, 1471; Rām. 250, 418, 880, 1652). -kun towards what? whither? in what direction? (Gr.Gr. 160); where? --tām -- adv. up to what? to what limit? how far? Also i.q. kath, but implies that the speaker is in doubt if there is anything to ask, as in kus tām, ab. --tāmath --, --tāñ --, or --tāñĕth --, id. ¶ kathō, i.q. kath, used familiarly in addressing a male. With pleon. kyutᵘ added, kathō-kyutᵘ, for what? (H. xi, 11). ¶ kawa sg. abl. inan. from what? i.q. kami 3, ab.; as adj. inan. (L.V. 39); as adv. by what? how? (W. 129; L.V. 41; Rām. 468, 1033; K. 64, 359); why? (L.V. 56; YZ. 49, 53, 151, 209, 264; Rām. 502, 1361; K. 319, 608). -bāpath adv. for what? why? -khötᵃra adv., id. -kani adv., id. -kinⁱ adv. for what cause? wherefore? why? -kanĕn adv., id. -pata adv. after what? since what? since when? -puʦhy adv. for what reason? why? (Rām. 765; K. 9, 87, 996). --ranga -- adv. in what manner? how? --sana --, see kus sana, ab. (L.V. 39). ¶ kawā by what? how? i.q. kawa, but used when addressing a male equal or inferior. Cf. kaway, bel. ¶ kawau, or kawō (= kawa, with interj. au, ō), O why? (YZ. 270, kawō, addressed by a woman to her beloved). kawau-bāpath adv. O why? (Rām. 407, addressed by a man to a man). ¶ kuwa adv. by what means? how? poet. for kawa (H. v, 9). ¶ kaway adv. by what? how? i.q. kawa, but used in addressing a female equal or inferior; cf. kawā, ab. (Śiv. 578). -bāpath adv. for what? why? used as ab. (Rām. 1017-22). ¶ kawukᵘ  adj. (f. kawücᵘ̈), sg. gen. inan. of what? genl. used as adv. how? (incredulously); hence, equivalent to a negative. ¶ kyā, i.q. kyāh (H. vi, 5), but, when so spelt, generally used as a mere inter. particle, indicating a question. Occasionally in this way it has the force of a particle of emphasis, as in yihuy kyā gav Sadāśiv, this person is no other than Sadāśiva, or who else is it but Sadāśiva (Śiv. 821). -bā adv., i.q. kyā, but employed only when addressing a brother or other male person of equal rank; cf. kĕhō, ab., and the two next. -biñ adv., i.q. kyā, but used only in addressing an elder sister or other female of superior rank; cf. the preceding and kĕhay, ab. -sa or -sö adv., i.q. kyā, but used only in addressing an elder male, or one of superior rank. Also, i.q. kyā sana, bel. (Gr.Gr. 181). --sana -- or --sanā -- adv. an inter. particle, i.q. kyā, but indicating doubt, as in kyā sana khĕwān chwā or kyā sanā khĕwān chuh, what, is he really eating? kyā sanā tȧtⁱ āsyā, I wonder will he be there (Gr.Gr. 180). --zan -- adv. what like? what sort of? ¶ kyāh or (see ab., p. 497b, l. 4) kyah or kĕh کیہ inan. sg. nom. what? As subst. (L.V. 21, 34, 42, etc.; K.Pr. 15; YZ. 146, kyah; 233, kyāh; Śiv. 58, 158, 160, 164, 203, 225, 323, etc.; Rām. 122, 157, 234-5, 238, etc.; K. 34, 39, 49, 141, etc.; H. ii, 2, 4, 11; iii, 4, 8, 9, etc.). kē̃h na ta kyāh, (there is) nothing, so what (is there), i.e. all is vanity (L.V. 19). As adj. (Śiv. 83, 160, 426, 643, 721 (fem. inan.), 908, 910, 923, etc.; Rām. 10, 51, 152, 158, 160, 164, etc.; K. 317, 361, 524, 528, etc.). ¶ The word kyāh or kyā or kyah is often used as a mere inter. particle, indicating that a question is asked. Thus, kyāh chuh murʦ karān, does he make images? (Gr.Gr. 199; so, Gr.M., kyā or kyāh; L.V. 18, 66; Śiv. 710, 874, 913, 1562; Rām. 11, 48, 756, 1367, 1629; K. 572, 1101, 1152; H. vii, 27, 28). ¶ Again, it is sometimes used as an interjectional adv., as in jān kyāh, how good! (L.V. 89); kyāh zabar, how excellent! (W. 101; so, Śiv. 436, 499, 573, 870; Rām. 796, 892, 1197, 1200; H. vii, 27, 28); cf. kyāh kǖtⁱ, how many! (Śiv. 742) and p. 485a, l. 29. Or it may be used adverbially in the sense of 'how', introducing a subordinate clause, as in wuch rath kyāh chuh pashpān, see the blood, how it is flowing, i.e. see how it bleeds (Gr.M.; so, Rām. 25, 686, 1147, 1221, 1224, 1338, 1353, 1372, 1380, 1522, 1751; K. 1136). Or it may be used as the equivalent of kyāzi (q.v.), why? (L.V. 67, 74; Rām. 222, 257, 347, 407, 1628, 1702, 1706; H. x, 14). Occasionally, like kyā, ab., it is little more than a particle of emphasis, as in tami kyāh korᵘ, what did she do? i.e. it is no other than she who did it (Rām. 1145; so, H. v, 8, 9; viii, 1; ix, 10, etc.). yitⁱ kyāh, here, in fact; here, you see (H. x, 12); yitⁱ kyāh... ȧtⁱ kyāh, here, you see on the one hand... there, on the other hand, you see (H. viii, 13); ada kyāh, then of course, of course, certainly (H. viii, 11; xii, 4). ¶ Occasionally kyāh is used with a disjunctive force, as in kyāh Kīkī kyāh Kusalyā, whether Kaikēyī or Kauśalyā (Rām. 301); möjᵘ̈ kyā mās, mother or aunt (Rām. 734; similarly, Rām. 1038; H. iv, 7), and in kyāh... ada yā, whether... or (Rām. 845). ¶ kyāh kĕtham adv. what's its name, what d'ye call it, u.w. ref. to something hitherto unknown, and which cannot be described by any name. --sana -- (Rām. 78) or --sanā --, see kus sana, ab., I wonder what (Rām. 78, 1391, 1493); as adj. (Rām. 202; K. 608, 919); as adv. I wonder how, or why (Rām. 1348, 1493). To this another inter. is sometimes added, as in kyāh sanā kyāh, I wonder what on earth (Rām. 1306, 1421); kyā sanā kus, I wonder who on earth (Rām. 1366); kyā sanā kȧmⁱ, I wonder by whom on earth (Rām. 596); kyāh sanā kati, I wonder where on earth (Rām. 221, 253); kyā sanā kyuthᵘ hyuhᵘ, I wonder what kind of (Rām. 1074). --tām -- or --tāmath -- pron. what? used when the speaker is in doubt as to whether there is anything to ask, as in kyāh tām wonun, what did he say? i.e. did he say anything? Here the speaker did not notice at the time what the man said, and afterwards recalls the fact of his perhaps having spoken, and, being in doubt, asks the question (Gr.Gr. 256); something or other, something indefinite (L.V. 86); wuchiv tȧmⁱ kyāh tām korus ʦhal, behold what deceit he did to him! behold how he deceived him! (Rām. 1417). --tāñ -- or --tāñĕth --, id. (Gr.Gr. 256; Śiv. 85; Rām. 146; K. 88, 181; all --tāñ); something or other (Rām. 432); wuchun gāṭulᵘ chuh kyāh tāñ, see (i.e. test) how clever he is (Rām. 129). ¶ kyōh, a contracted form of kyāwu, bel., q.v. ¶ kyuhᵘ tām, --tāmath --, --tāñ --, or --tāñĕth -- adj. that which cannot be described by any definitions, indefinable (cf. kyuthᵘ tām, p. 502b, l. 4). ¶ kyāwu (L.V. 19) or kyōh (L.V. 3, 5, 65), an old form of kyāh, used as a kind of disjunctive conjunction in the sense of 'whether... or', or 'as well as', in the phrase dĕn kyāwu (or kyōh) rāth, whether by day or by night, by day as well as by night, day and night, continually.

adj. (f. kë̆ñᵘ̈), wet, moist, damp; cf. kĕnun. ¶ kĕna-bobᵘ m. N. of a certain aquatic fruit, found growing in lakes, described as red, but white inside, and containing many small seeds. -rab f. the soft, but not liquid, mud first formed on a road by a slight shower; (in building) mud used as mortar.

m. (sg. dat. kĕvis), a kind of plant growing in marshes. According to L. 72 (kĕv) it is Chaerophyllum sp., and is looked upon as an excellent substitute for carrots, both by the herdsmen and by the red bears. It has been identified at Kew as really Sagittaria sagittifolia, or Common Arrowhead, but possibly the name may be used for two different plants. For the manner in which its roots are joined together by a fibrous network, see kĕvⁱ-rāṭh, bel., and cf. Śiv. 1807. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to root up one of these plants in the marshes. This is a long, slow business; hence, met. to spend a long time over completing any work. ¶ kĕvⁱ-gŏgⁱjⁱ f. a kind of turnip; a small potato. -gāsa m. the edible leaves of the kyowᵘ-plant. -mujᵘ̈ f. a young tuber of this plant, used as a vegetable. It is globular in shape; cf. mujĕ-kyowᵘ, s.v. mujᵘ̈. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. a full-grown large tuber of this plant. It is also globular in shape. -nambal f. a piece of marshy ground, in which this plant grows plentifully. -rāṭh f. (sg. dat. -rāṭhi), lit. the tangled roots of this plant, i.e. an underground fibrous network spread over a wide area, made up of the roots of this plant all tangled together. -zag m. N. of a kind of paddy yielding a red grain when husked (L. 463, kai zag).

or pron. adj. (f. kiʦhᵘ̈), of what sort? of what kind? (Gr.Gr. 153; Gr.M.; L.V. 84, 85); as adv. how? (Gr.M.; L.V. 71; H. ii, 5). --hyuhᵘ -- (f. kiʦhᵘ̈ hishᵘ̈), i.q. kyuthᵘ, what kind of? kyāh sanā kyuthᵘ hyuhᵘ, I wonder what kind of (Rām. 1074; cf. kyāh sanā, p. 500a, l. 43). --sanā -- adj. i.q. kyuthᵘ, but with a shade of doubt in the question, quasi 'really of what sort?' (cf. Gr.Gr. 180-1). --tām --, --tāmath --, --tāñ, or --tāñĕth -- adj., i.q. kyuthᵘ, but with a shade of doubt, quasi 'I wonder of what sort'; that which cannot be described by any name, indefinable (cf. kyuhᵘ tām, p. 500b, l. 22); (contemptuously) what sort of? i.e. very unpleasing, bad, worth nothing, of no use.

or postpos. m. (pl. nom. kitⁱ; f. sg. kiʦᵘ̈), for, for the sake of (Gr.Gr. 14; Gr.M.; W. 97, kiut); also forming advs. of time, see bel. ¶ When used with the meaning of 'for', etc., kyutᵘ governs the dat., as in mölis-kyutᵘ, for the father; mālĕn-kyutᵘ, for the fathers. Like the postpositions of the gen., it is an adj., agreeing with the governing noun in gender, number, and case, as in mölis-kyutᵘ pôñᵘ, water for the father; mölis- kiʦᵘ̈ gāv, a cow for the father; guris-kitⁱ rawa, blankets (nom. pl. m.) for the horse; mölis-kiʦa pōthĕ, books (nom. pl. f.) for the father (Gr.Gr. 44). ¶ Similarly, if the governing noun should be in the dat., we should have mölis-kitis pöñis, to the water for the father; mölis-kiʦan gōvᵘ̈n, to the cows for the father (Gr.Gr. 44), and so on for other cases. For instances of this use of kyutᵘ, see bel. ¶ Special attention should be paid to the use of kyutᵘ with the infinitive and with the future passive participle of a verb. Used with the infinitive, it governs the dative in the ordinary way, as in yith pōthĕ paranas-kyutᵘ prang, a couch for reading this book (Gr.Gr. 114) (cf. esp. ninas-kyutᵘ, s.v. nyunᵘ). The fut. pass. part. has the same form as the infinitive, but is an adjective, its m. sg. nom. having the form karun, karonᵘ, or karunᵘ. This adjective, combined in apposition with kyutᵘ, and agreeing with it in gender, number, and case, forms a passive verbal adjective of necessity, fitness, or purpose, like the Latin gerundive; thus cyonᵘ- kyutᵘ, intended to be drunk, potable (p. 179a, l. 43). So paronᵘ-kyutᵘ pŏstukh, a book (m. sg.) to be read, a book for reading (but we cannot say paronᵘ- kyutᵘ prang, as that would mean 'a couch to be read', not 'a couch for reading'); parüñᵘ̈-kiʦᵘ̈ pūthⁱ, a book (f. sg.) to be read; ranȧnⁱ-kitⁱ hākh, vegetables (m. pl.) to be cooked, i.e. for being cooked; karañĕ-kiʦa kāmĕ, works (f. pl.) to be done (Gr.Gr. 115, Gr.M.); khyonᵘ-kyutᵘ, (food) to be eaten, something to eat (K.Pr. 248); bĕhunᵘ-kyutᵘ makān, a house to be dwelt in, in which to dwell (Rām. 591). ¶ When used to form an adv. of time, kyutᵘ also governs the dat., but, being used adverbially, it often does not change its own form. As an adv. of time, it is more definite than kani. Thus, dã̄-phulạyi- kyutᵘ (p. 230b, l. 14) means, definitely, 'at the time of rice-blossoming', while dã̄-phulạyi-kani (p. 230b, l. 12) means 'in, or about, the time of rice-blossoming'. Kyutᵘ cannot be used in this sense with all words. Its chief use is to indicate a season, as ab. Other examples are bahāras-kyutᵘ, in the spring-time (p. 96b, l. 9); barsātas-kyutᵘ, in the rainy season (p. 127a, l. 40); bēli-wāpas-kyutᵘ, in the sowing season (p. 150b, l. 15); dŏhaiṭhas-kyutᵘ, in (so-and-so's) sixty-second year (p. 201b, l. 38); drāgas-kyutᵘ, in a time of famine (p. 241b, l. 42), and so on. In this sense it is sometimes added either pleonastically or with the sense of 'for' to advs. of time. Thus, rāth, to-night; az rāth-kyutᵘ sāl, an invitation for to-night; rāth-kyutᵘ, to-night or by night (Gr.M.; H. iii, 1); pagāh- kyutᵘ, for to-morrow (Gr.M.). ¶ kitⁱ m. pl. nom. chŏkas-kitⁱ dawāh, medicines for the wound (Rām. 1308; similarly, Rām. 1505; H. v, 1; xi, 11). ¶ kiʦᵘ̈ f. sg. nom. wöjᵘ̈ kōrĕ-kiʦᵘ̈, a ring for the daughter (H. v, 1; so, x, 11; xi, 12). ¶ kyutᵘ m. sg. nom. dŏhas-kyutᵘ, for a day, sufficient for a whole day (p. 200a, l. 47); biyis- kyutᵘ, for someone else (L.V. 61; so, Rām. 744; H. ii, 1; x, 5; xii, 4, 5, 11, 16, 24).
. On p. 502, l. 14, note the idiom rᵒtᵒ kyutᵘ (p. 845a, l. 24), which is an adjective, meaning 'sometimes good and sometimes bad'.
or kạhüñᵘ̈ f. repeated asking, persistent begging; repeating a statement over and over again. kạhüñᵘ̈-kạhüñᵘ̈ f. repeated reproach or abuse.
f. onomat. the crashing noise of breaking or falling timber, or the like.
f. (sg. dat. kᵃlaphᵃʦᵃ), trouble, vexation, distress, inconvenience; (in Kāshmīrī) the preparations or arrangements necessary for any Hindū religious sacrifice, or the like.

f. (sg. dat. kᵃlüʦᵃ), littleness, smallness; fewness, paucity, deficiency, insufficiency, scarcity; want, indigence; difficulty; (in Kāshmīrī) (of a thing) rareness (on account of insufficient production, or the like).
impers. fut. part. c.g. to be sold, for sale, exposed for sale (in a shop) (K.Pr. 108, kanani).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. kᵒnᵒ; 2 p.p. kᵃñōv), to sell, dispose of (El. kȧnun and kunun; K.Pr. 78, 150; W. 144, kunun; YZ. 119, 122; Śiv. 53, 590; H. vii, 17, 26; viii, 9; xii, 3; K. 178). --dᵃnun -- m. to sell etcetera, to sell and do the other things necessary to complete a sale, to sell and take the price of the article sold. -kyutᵘ adj. (f. kᵃnüñᵃ- kiʦᵘ̈), on sale, for sale, to be sold. ¶ kᵒnᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. kᵘ̈ñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), sold, disposed of.

m. onomat. a single creak, grating, or rustle (of a door, of a machine, or the like); cf. kar 3. -kᵃr m. onomat. a continued creaking or rustling, as ab.; the clucking of a hen (K.Pr. 120, kur kur). -ʦᵃr m. onomat. the worrying noise of doors opening and shutting caused by people coming and going; the worrying rustling of uneasy children, or the like, going about.
m. (another form of kissa, q.v.) a story, tale, narration (Gr.M.; Śiv. 117, 653).
m. the Kāshmīrī form of kism, q.v. (Gr.M.).
in kᵃta-kᵃta m. tickling (the act). --karun -- m.inf. to tickle (El. kuta-kuta karun).
adj. c.g. artificial, imitation, fictitious, bogus (L. 458, kut; K.Pr. 103, kĕṭah; 246, kuṭah). -kŏl f. a winter stream, dry in hot weather (W. 115).

m. a stain, mark, dark spot; stain, stigma, obloquy; a fault charged (truly or falsely). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to bring a charge (true or false) of some fault. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to attribute a fault (true or false).
conj. 2 (1 p.p. kᵒtᵒ, 2 p.p. kᵃʦyōv), i.q. kᵃʦun, q.v.

f. a kind of large earthenware vessel, in which milk is kept to ripen, and is then churned; a churn (Śiv. 1435, 1462, 1838); cf. dŏda-kᵃy, p. 189b, l. 16, and guras-kᵃy, p. 304a, l. 48. kᵃyĕ-wörᵃ f. a small wide-mouthed vessel used as a churn.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kᵃʦanôwᵃ), to make damp, to cause to be damp (see Gr.Gr. 174). Cf. kᵃʦawun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. kᵃʦowᵃ), to make moist, to moisten. Cf. kᵃʦanāwun.

or kᵃtun conj. 2 (1 p.p. kᵒtᵒ, f.pl. kᵃʦa; 2 p.p. kᵃʦyōv, m.pl. kᵃʦöy or kᵃʦēy, Gr.Gr. 224-5, 227), to become moist, damp (by contact with a liquid). The caus. of this verb is kᵃʦanāwun or kᵃʦawun, not kᵃʦᵃrāwun (Gr.Gr. 174). kᵒtᵒ-motᵒ perf.part. (f. kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈-mᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), made damp, made wet, wetted (K.Pr. 121, sg.m. kuʦamut, sic).

adj. (f. kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), wet, moist, damp; full of juice, juicy; sappy (L.V. 51). Often used met., as in āra-kᵒtᵒ (p. 41a, l. 5) damp with compassion, compassionate, or (YZ. 39; Śiv. 113, 948, 1473, 1527; Rām. 1595) deserving of compassion (p.p. of kᵃʦun, q.v.).
see kᵒtᵒ, kᵃtun, and kᵃʦun (in YZ. 39, written köʦ, see kᵒtᵒ).

. The tenth (or, if we count the aspirates ch and kh as separate letters, the twelfth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is the twenty-eighth (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the thirty-first) consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the thirtieth consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It is pronounced, as in India proper, with the tip of the tongue touching the front teeth, and not the gums, the resulting sound being softer and more dental than in English. ¶ When this letter is immediately followed by ᵘ̈ or by y (including ĕ, see art. ĕ), it is changed to j. Thus, wôlᵘ, a large ring,but fem. wöjᵘ̈, a small ring; wūlᵘ, fickle; wōjĕr, fickleness.
privative particle, as in lā-makān لا مکان adj. with no abode, without a dwelling-place, inexistent (as an epithet of the Deity) (H. vii, 29).

f. a lip (YZ. 213); an edge, margin, verge, brim, brink (cf. dāri-lab, p. 238a, l. 26); a bank, shore, coast; a brow (of a hill); (in Kāshmīrī) side, direction, point of the compass, quarter (Rām. 568); a boundary-wall, party-wall, the wall of a house or room (El.; L. 464; K.Pr. 149; Rām. 577; Śiv. 211, 1076; K. 155); cf. lobᵘ 1 and lar 2. --lagüñᵘ̈ --, f.inf. a wall to be applied; a quarrel or hostility to arise between friends; (of any article in a dish, etc.) to go bad, turn sour. -rĕz لبریز adj. c.g. brimful, overflowing, running over (El.). ¶ laba-côkᵘ m. (sg. dat. -cökis), the slit, with corded edges, about half a span long, at each side of the lower end of the Kāshmīrī nightgown-like dress; cf. cākh 1. -düjᵘ̈ f. the sewing together, by the edges, of two pieces of cloth; repeating a person's words when reproaching him, quoting in reproof. -düjᵘ̈ lāgüñᵘ̈ f.inf. sympathetically to repeat another's words, and to do the same when he changes his mind, and says the opposite. -dörᵘ̈ f. a side door, esp. a small one. -ganḍ m. tying up the side, i.e. the formation of a screen, e.g. by a wall or a curtain. -holᵘ adj. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), crooked-edged. -shē̃kā or -shē̃kh f. urinating, passing water; cf. dīrgashĕnkā (p. 242a, l. 40) and lagushē̃kā, s.v. -tāph m. (sg. dat. -tāpas), side-heat, i.e. the heat cast by the sun when low in the sky and near setting; the heat of the sun in this manner falling on the side, not on the front of a house; met. standing aside from any work, and merely looking on or superintending. -tāpas bĕhun m.inf. to sit in the side-heat, as ab.; (of a superintendent) on account of some impediment to dissociate himself from his duty, or abandon his work. -tāpas thawun m.inf. to expel a person from some office or duty. --ta mūnⁱ hĕnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to take the sides and inner walls, to cling to the walls; hence, (of a child or the like) to walk about secretly or modestly. -ʦôkᵘ m. (sg. dat. -ʦökis), the lower course, near the foundations, of the four walls of a house. It is usually built of stone, or the like, even when the rest of the house is of wood. -ʦolᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüjᵘ̈), broken, or spoiled, at the edge (e.g. a room, a vessel, or a garment). -ʦyopᵘ adj. (f. -ʦë˘pᵘ̈), broken, or dinted, at the edges. Cf. ʦĕph.

m. profit, gain (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1776, 1806, 1809); the end, aim, object, of any work; interest on money (El., Gr.Gr. 148). ¶ lāba-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), profitless, fruitless, affording no profit; having no object, objectless. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), profitable, giving profit. -saʦhar m. the condition of being profitable, profitableness, fruitfulness, productiveness. -sôvᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), fully profitable, richly productive. -sāvĕr m. the condition of being richly profitable, rich productiveness. --vĕnā -- or --vinā -- adj. and adv. without profit, useless (El. lábavenna).

adj. c.g. edged, having an edge (cf. okᵘ-labal, p. 19a, l. 25, and aiṭha-labal, having eight edges, and hence, octagonal, p. 66b, l. 28); esp. edged, in the sense of having a bad edge, crooked-edged, having uneven edges, lopsided.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. labanôwᵘ), caus. of labun in all its senses; e.g. to cause to obtain (Rām. 408).
m. a country bumpkin, a boor, an ignorant and clumsy fellow. Cf. lĕbāra and gāma-labār (p. 287a, l. 3).
f. a reward for finding (something lost, etc.).
n.ag. (f.labawüñᵘ̈), a finder, getter (of something lost, forgotten, hidden, etc.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. lobᵘ2, for 1, see s.v.), to get, take, receive, obtain (El.; Gr.M.; L.V. 31, 35, 75, 90; K.Pr. 36, 46, 157; YZ. 56, 230, 237, 380; Rām. 116, 426, 541, 544, 565, 1037, 1133, 1146, 1307, 1310, 1373, 1504, 1509, 1530, 1713; Śiv. 10, 381, 497, 680, 890, 934, 1565; K. 61, 285, 612, 621, 659, 739, 765; H. ii, 9, 10); ārām l., to receive rest, to find surcease (Rām. 259); nishcay l., to obtain certainty (Śiv. 159); sazā l., to receive punishment, be punished (Gr.M.). ¶ to gain, get, find (something lost, forgotten, hidden, etc.) (Gr.M.; Rām. 45, 108, 566, 640, 1116; Śiv. 97, 1450); to reach (a place) (Rām. 318; Śiv. 1699-1701); to take (as such and such), consider, look upon as (Rām. 577, 1254, 1500); to catch sight of, see (suddenly) (Rām. 1499). lobᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. lübᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), got, etc., as ab.

or lāburᵘ m. (sg. dat. labaras), a piece of ground higher than a surrounding or adjoining tract, an eminence, high ground. According to El., labur is the word used in Śrīnagar, and lāburᵘ in vill. Cf. aḍ-lāburᵘ, p. 10a, l. 34, and aḍa-lāburᵘ, p. 11b, l. 3.
m. (f. lābᵃrĕñ), a professional money-lender, a usurer (Gr.Gr. 148).

adj. c.g. without remedy, helpless, powerless, without resource (Gr.M.; L.V. 89; Rām. 29, 64, 106, 788, 949; Śiv. 421, 678, 1581); disabled, disarmed (Rām. 411); destitute, forlorn, poor (Gr.M.); humble, humiliated, forlorn (Rām. 116); cāra-lācār, utterly helpless (Rām. 1666).
m. one who is low, mean, vile, a shameless beggar.
f. the conduct of a vile person; conduct like that of a vile person, shameless begging, or the like.
f. the conduct or condition of one who is mean, vile, a shameless beggar, or the like.

card. (sg. abl. lacha, K.Pr. 150; pl. dat. lachan), a hundred thousand (El.; Gr.Gr. 80; K.Pr. 18, 23, 150, 181; YZ. 159; Rām. 1651; K. 786, 846); akh lach rŏpayĕ, a hundred thousand rupees (Gr.M.); yōzana-lach, a hundred thousand leagues (L.V. 26). ¶ lacha-bodᵘ or -bọ̆dᵘ adj. (f. -büzᵘ̈), in hundreds of thousands, by hundreds of thousands (cf. bọ̆dᵘ 2) (Gr.Gr. 144; W. 164; Śiv. 32, 51, 715, 731, etc.; K. 660, 727, 1008, 1014). -nôwᵘ  m. having a hundred thousand (i.e. innumerable) names (Rām. 1783; Śiv. 53, 181, 834; H. ii, 2); the philosopher's stone (which by its touch converts base metals into gold). -phyurᵘ m. returns in hundreds of thousands, i.e. an income from business which amounts to this. -trigunᵘ āy m. a life lasting three times a hundred thousand years (an expression used in praising or complimenting a person). -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a man who possesses hundreds of thousands (of money), a millionaire. ¶ lȧchⁱ āradun m.inf. to honour by a hundred thousand; to accomplish, or conciliate, by innumerable means, to spare no pains to please a person. --āradith kȧchⁱ ʦaṭun -- m.inf. 'having honoured by a hundred thousand, to cut by a trifle', i.e. after having spared no pains in order to gain a person's friendship, to destroy that friendship by a single piece of tactlessness; cf. kȧchⁱ. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to buy by a hundred thousand rupees' worth at a time, to make enormous purchases; to make enormous profits by business, to become a millionaire. ¶ lachan-hȧndⁱ lach hundreds of thousands of hundred thousands, innumerable, countless (Rām. 1323, Śiv. 731).

f. (sg. dat. lāchi 1; for 2, see lôchᵘ), the red animal dye called 'lac', produced by the Coccus Lacca; shellac, the wax formed by this insect; sealing-wax (made from shellac) (Gr.M.). ¶ lācha (or lāchi)-hondᵘ  adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), made of shellac. -mŏhar f. a seal for use with sealing-wax. -ʦrüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ʦracĕ), a 'lac-wheel', a circular cake of lac. ¶ lāchi-hāl f. (sg. dat. -höjᵘ̈), a house built of lac, with its true nature disguised by external painting, etc. Such a house is described in the Mahābhārata. If it is wished to destroy a person, he is enticed into it, and the whole set on fire. The Sanskrit name for such a house is jatu-grha, the modern form of which--jauhar--is used in Rajputana for the burning to death of all the women of a city to save them from a conquering enemy.
m. nasty bitterness combined with viscosity (e.g. of some fruit gone bad and slimy).
adj. (f. lȧchiñᵘ̈), costing a hundred thousand (rupees, etc.); (of a thing, action, business) accomplished by innumerable means or exertions.
adj. (f. lāchivᵘ̈), made of woollen cloth or paṭṭū (see lôchᵘ).

(cf. لچک) m. a kind of head-dress worn by Musalmān women, consisting of a skull-cap, with a long appendage hanging down behind so as to conceal the hair at the back (El. lachakah, lachiká) (K.Pr. 132). --dyunᵘ -- m. inf. to give such a head-dress; met. to make a person ashamed by conquering him publicly in a dispute or discussion, and so rendering him silent. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to be put to shame, as ab.
f. helplessness; inability, incapacity; forlornness, destitution, want of means, poverty (El.; Śiv. 212, 583).
f. (generally used in pl.). laḍa f. pl. fighting in sport (as in wrestling, cudgel-play, etc.). laḍa karañĕ to fight, as ab. (K. 504, 941).

f. (sg. dat. lözᵘ̈; but YZ. 307, pl. dat. lādan), the plaited fold or hem round the bottom of the nightgown-like garment worn in Kashmīr. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take up this hem, i.e. to shorten the garment by making this hem; hence, in filling a receptacle, to raise its edges, so as to make it hold more (e.g. by surrounding the top edge with paper, or cloth, or withies); to seize the edge of a person's garment in humble entreaty (YZ. 307). --khārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to raise the hem, i.e. to raise the edges of a dish, as ab. ¶ lözᵘ̈-pan m. the skirt-hem, as ab., but narrow (the ordinary hem being three or four inches wide).

c.g. a secondary suffix forming adjectives of quality, and indicating that the quality not only accompanies the object, but is actually a necessary part of it. Thus from phakh (base phak-), a stink; phakalad, stinking (Gr.Gr. 135; cf. 133). When used as an adjective it is of common gender, but, when used substantively, its fem. is ladiñ, as in bakalad, a chatterer (masc.); bakaladiñ, a chattering woman.

f. (sg. dat. lüzᵘ̈), a heaped up load, a high load made by piling things one on the top of the other. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to climb up to (by making a pile and getting on to its top, so as to reach to something above) (K. 148). ¶ lada-bata m. a pot full of heaped-up cooked rice, filled straight from the cooking pot, intended to be sent to someone; hence, a present of cooked rice so sent. lada-sörᵘ̈ f. sending presents or contributions to a dowry from time to time (e.g. to a person in authority, a friend, or a son-in-law), with the intention that the recipient should allow them to accumulate. Cf. lodᵘ.
(sg. dat. ladākas), the country of Ladakh or Western Tibet, to the north and north-east of Kashmīr. ladākukᵘ adj. (f. ladākücᵘ̈), produced in, or coming from, Ladakh.

f. (sg. dat. lādüñᵘ̈), kindly help, a kind action (to one who needs it) (Rām. 1439; Śiv. 178, 1594). --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a kind action to mount upon a person, i.e. to be indebted for kindness, to owe a debt of gratitude, to be under an obligation. --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to establish a kind action, to draw a person's attention to a kind action done to him, to put a person under an obligation (Rām. 1143); to do a kind action (Rām. 639, 1741).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ladanôwᵘ), to cause to be built, to get built (Gr.M., K. 1149), etc. Caus. of ladun in all its meanings.
f. support, maintenance, protecting (of one who is helpless, poverty-stricken, wretched, or the like), kindly help; a grateful return for such help, requital for a kindness. Cf. lādan.
m. the building of a house from the foundation upwards, house-erection; the wages for building (Gr.Gr. 122).
m. (a paper showing that there is) no claim, a receipt for money paid (YZ. 122, 454).
f. wages for carrying a thing sent, for building, or for filling a receptacle. Cf. ladun.
f. wages paid for the work of filling a scale-pan (see lāduwᵘ).
f. the profession or employment of filling scale-pans (see lāduwᵘ).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. laḍôwᵘ), to cause to fight, to set fighting, to incite to blows; to use (a weapon) in fight.
n.ag. (f. ladavüñᵘ̈), one who sends or dispatches something; one who builds. Cf. ladun (of which it is the n.ag. in all its meanings).
n.ag. (f. laḍavüñᵘ̈), one who fights, a fighter; one who is ready to fight, pugnacious.
f. a complimentary present (cf. lodᵘ and ladun), used --˚ as in hēri-lāday (see p. 345b, l. 13), a complimentary present given to masons when the stairs of a house are completed.
m. a kind of mendicant. These men go about with a stick in each hand. They strike these sticks against each other as they call out demanding alms. They are sturdy violent beggars.
adj. (f. laḍöcᵘ̈), warlike, pugnacious, turbulent, a brawler; one who goes about armed, and ready at once to use his weapons, a bravo.
adj. c.g. born, or produced, in the country of Ladakh (see ladākh).
(often written laḍöi and laröyⁱ) f. a battle, warfare (with arms or wordy) (H. x, i); --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to fight.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. lodᵘ, f. lüzᵘ̈; 2 p.p. lazōv), to send, dispatch (someone or something) (Gr.Gr. 122; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 259; YZ. 202, 209, 395, 459; Rām. 136, 833, 858, 1103, 1451, 1596; Śiv. 639, 1736; K. 40, 642, 686, 695, etc.; H. iv, 2; vii, 7; x, 3; xii, 15); to send as a present, supply, grant, give (from a distance) (Śiv. 1086, 1216, 1347, 1554; K. 620); ¶ to push, elevate, raise (Gr.Gr. 122, Śiv. 640); to raise (e.g. water in the hands) (YZ. 163); to set up (a shop or the like) (Śiv. 1211); to build, construct (Gr.Gr. 122, 209, 225; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 57; YZ. 409; Rām. 593, 607-8, 978; Śiv. 337, 1696, 1776) (cf. mal lᵒ, s.v. mal 1; nāṭa ladañĕ, s.v. nāṭh); ¶ to put into, fill (a receptacle) (K.Pr. 64, 94, 128; H. v, 7; viii, 4, 7, 12); to put into (e.g. a foot into a stirrup) (YZ. 535); to load (e.g. a ship) (El., Gr.Gr. 122, Gr.M.); to lay a burden (on someone) (Rām. 485, 846, 1008, 1230, 1743; H. ii, 5; v, 9); ¶ to apply (e.g. mud to the body) (Rām. 277, 1371); to wind up (string) (Gr.Gr. lxv); to string (a bow) (El.). ¶ Often used to make nominal compounds, such as buthᵘ ladun, to build a mouth, i.e. to make a mouth, to show displeasure by twisting the features (p. 141b, l. 46); dūsh l., to bring an accusation (p. 253a, l. 45); dav l., to lay a bet (p. 260b, l. 21); drih ladüñᵘ̈, to build a frown, to frown (p. 242a, l. 49); mȧsⁱtī ladüñᵘ̈, to give oneself airs; māz ladun, to build flesh, become stout; rāh ladun, to send along a road, to send away or carry off (from a person); hence, to destroy (K.Pr. 121); and so many others, which will be found under their respective nouns. --padun -- m.inf. to practise sending presents, etc. Cf. lodᵘ podᵘ (p. 508b, l. 48). ¶ ladan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who sends presents, etc.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. loḍᵘ 2, for 1, see s.v.; 2 p.p. lajyōv), to fight (literally, or in wordy warfare) (Rām. 1437; K. 60, 242, 247, 446-7, 553, 561, 563, 571, 760-1, 774, 817, 821, 826, 1024). ¶ lȧḍⁱ lȧḍⁱ hyonᵘ m.inf. to get after continued fighting, i.e. to insist on getting something, to persist in trying to get something till one is successful. ¶ laḍith conj. part., as adv., obstinately, persistently (Śiv. 1672). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to engage in fighting, to fight, quarrel.
m. (sg. dat. laḍaras), a kind of water-rush or reed, the stem of which is sheathed; cf. lāyĕ-laḍur, s.v. lāy 1, and pĕʦi-l., s.v. pë̆ʦᵘ̈. laḍar-pōsh m. its dark-red flower (Rām. 647, 1093).
m. a man whose duty it is to fill the empty pan of a scale when weighing grain or the like.
m. gradually rising woodland ground at the foot of a hill; N. of a Kashmīr village about ten miles to the west of Śrīnagar.
m. a gradually rising road (e.g. at the foot of a steep ascent).
adj. c.g. verbal; (of a translation) word for word, literal (Gr.M.).

f. customary rule, established practice, custom, fashion, habit; prevalence of anything (e.g. an epidemic and so on) (Gr.Gr. 125) (cf. nāma-lᵒ, s.v. nām). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a custom, practice, fashion, or prevalence to become established.

m. a long or tall trunk or branch of a tree. lā̃ga-zyūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈), (of a person) having too long limbs, long-shanked, etc.; (of grasses, vegetables, etc.) too long-stalked, having too long leaves, etc.
f. contact, touching (K. 852); imitating, imitation (Gr.Gr. 126). Cf. lāgun.

f. (in giving, receiving, paying, earning, or the like) the customary or fixed amount; payment at the customary rate for work done; a customary present or offering made to a superior, a naẕr (K. 102, 374, 406). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a customary rate or amount (as ab.) to become fixed; a conventional method of doing anything to be fixed; to be attacked by an infectious disease. --tarüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to become infected from contact or the like (e.g. with infectious disease, or with disrepute owing to evil associations). ¶ lāgi-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), (work done) without payment, (work) not done for reward, disinterested (work) (L.V. 61, 65).
adj. c.g. harmonizing with, matching, forming one of a pair or set; as subst. m. employment of or application of something for a special purpose (cf. atha-laga, p. 59b, l. 16).
adj. c.g. worthy, fitting, suitable, matching, a match (Gr.Gr. 130).
m. delay (K.Pr. 119, in the phrase chuna kē̃h ti lagān, there is no delay. Possibly the word is pres. part. of lagun).
conj. 1 (caus. of lagun, with special meanings (Gr.Gr. 175); 1 p.p. laganôwᵘ), to cause to suffer pain, to cause to feel sore; to cause to be fit, to make suitable; to cause to take effect (Gr.M.).
f. a crop (El.); cultivation, cultivated ground (El. lāganai and loganai; Gr.Gr. 129, K.Pr. 247). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f. inf. to cultivate (El.).
adj. c.g. lean, thin, gaunt, meagre (H. vi, 15). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become thin, to waste away.
f. (sg. dat. lāgüʦᵘ̈), expense, expenditure, outlay; cost, price, cost-price, prime-cost, capital expenditure (Śiv. 1710).
f. the cost of uniting or joining; the cost of making a thing, prime-cost.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lagôwᵘ), to apply; to apply anything to oneself, to wear or put on (clothes or the like) (Gr.M.).
n.ag. (f. lagawüñᵘ̈), that which is being joined or united, fit to be joined, fitting, etc., in all the meanings of lagun, q.v.

f. the act of causing to be attached, fixing, applying; met. inflicting (a wound, as in chŏka-lāgay, p. 159b, l. 20, inflicting a wound on oneself); a joining in combat, a quarrel (cf. ȧchⁱ-l., p. 8a, l. 41; buthⁱ-l., p. 142b, l. 22).

m. (f. lāgdārĕñ, a person who receivs a payment of customary or fixed dues (e.g. a custom-house official); a person, animal, or the like, who by custom earns his or its living by performing some customary duty.
f. a livelihood dependent on customary gifts or offerings.
m. (f. lāgidariñ), a person who is entitled to receive customary dues or gifts; a person or animal in whom a disease is due to appear (owing to the time for its development having run out).

conj. 2 [1 p.p. logᵘ, f.lüjᵘ̈ 2; for lüjᵘ̈ 1, see logᵘ; for lüjᵘ̈ 3, see lojᵘ; 2 p.p. lajyōv. The causal of this verb is lāgun, q.v. The regular form laganāwun, q.v., has special meanings (Gr.Gr. 175)] to be attached (to), joined (to), be connected (with), fastened (to) (Rām. 577, Śiv. 1862); to be bound (to); to be moored, come to anchor; (of a ship) to run aground (L. 84-5; YZ. 34; Rām. 1334); to stick, adhere (to); to become joined together, closed (e.g. a door or the eyelids, cf. ȧchⁱ lagüñᵘ̈, p. 8a, l. 39; nöjⁱ lagañĕ, s.v. nāḍⁱ; K.Pr. 102); to be added (to), appended; to apply oneself (to) (Rām. 2; Śiv. 69, 1612; K. 4, 21, 90, 92, 144, 508-9, 514, 525, 612, 959); ¶ to find oneself in a certain position, to become liable to some operation, to be put to use (for some purpose), as in barkari l., to find oneself in front, to be set in the forefront of battle (p. 123a, l. 3); baṭhi l., to find oneself on the bank (out of a cargo-boat), to become usable (p. 140b, l. 4); buthi l., to take one's stand in front (p. 143a, l. 39); caṭi l., to become liable to a fine (p. 177a, l. 19); dara or dari l., to become subject to stoppage, to be suddenly halted (pp. 235b, l. 43; 237b, l. 48); dāwas l., to become subject to an attack (p. 260b, l. 44); graṭa l., to be put into the mill, to be worn down (p. 304b, l. 43); and so in many other expressions which will be found under the respective nouns (so, YZ. 569, Rām. 1670); esp. to become an offering (to or for), to offer oneself as a sacrifice (for), to be devoted (to) (YZ. 20; Rām. 212, 511, 938, 1120, 1131, 1494, 1635; Śiv. 190, 215, 359, et passim); balāyĕ l., to become (an offering) to (avert) a calamity, to be devoted on behalf of another (p. 106b, l. 32); chapi l., to put oneself forward as an offering, to offer oneself as a sacrifice for another (p. 163b, l. 32); pörⁱ l., id., s.v. pôrᵘ (K. 45, 54, 101, 158, et passim); ¶ to become involved (in), to experience (e.g. happiness) (L.V. 70; Rām. 339, 533; Śiv. 156, 332, 828, 1309, 1641; K. 808; cf. bēgāri l., to be involved in forced labour, to be pressed for service, p. 92a, l. 29); to be applied (to) (Rām. 474); to be close to, to adjoin, touch (Śiv. 1903); to take to (a road), to follow (a path) (Śiv. 583, 1247, 1895); to be put (into, e.g. bö̃dⁱ-wān l., to be put into jail, p. 83b, l. 39) (Rām. 1584;
