Śiv. 1214; H. v, 8; vi, 11); to come into close contact or connexion (with, dat.), to be absorbed (in), to be incorporated (in), to become one (with) (L.V. 58; Rām. 993; Śiv. 1039); dil l., the heart to be devoted (to), set (upon, pĕṭh) (K.Pr. 43; YZ. 263); ¶ to become subject (to, as in bārawan l., to become the object of reproaches) (K. 906, similarly, H. viii, 5); to become caught (in a trap, etc.) (YZ. 68, 342, 475; Rām. 340, 1103, 1614; H. v, 2); to be employed (in), occupied (in), engaged (in) (Śiv. 67, 844; K. 1030); ¶ to take effect (of a medicine; cf. ashud l., p. 48a, l. 46); to attain (to), reach, arrive (at) (H. viii, 5; xi, 5; cf. bāl-bachĕ l., to reach the mountain-foot, p. 103b, l. 38); (of a place) to be reached, to be arrived at (H. xi, 5); to have the intended, or natural, effect, to answer, come off, be achieved (Rām. 1492, 1573); ¶ to come into contact, to start, be set going, to arise, happen, take place (very frequently used in this and cognate senses to form nominal compound verbs, as in bŏcha lagüñᵘ̈, hunger to be felt; bȧsⁱtⁱ lagüñᵘ̈, a fixed residence to be adopted; bāṭh-baṭil lagüñᵘ̈, lamentations to be started; biyĕr lagun, delay to occur; bözⁱ lagüñᵘ̈, swindling to occur, to be cheated; and so on for many others, which will be found under the respective nouns) (cf. L.V. 41; K.Pr. 43, dab l.; Rām. 206, 598, 1667; K. 95, 183); to be experienced, felt (as in brakh l., a crushing blow to be experienced; dôdᵘ l., pain to be felt; gŏta lagȧnⁱ, plunges to be experienced; hence, to have painful memories; and many others, which will be found under the respective nouns) (cf. āy lagun, (long) life to be experienced, Rām. 390, 1206, 1465; similarly, K.Pr. 128; Rām. 172, 636; Śiv. 1858; K. 837, 1125, 1147; H. v, 2; vi, 16; viii, 7; ix, 12); to be incurred, subjected to (as in bahā lagun, steam to be incurred, to become mouldy; bāj l., a tax to become payable; bram l., delusion to be incurred, Rām. 339); (of a fit of disease, demoniacal possession, or the like) to attack (a person) (as in brikh lagüñᵘ̈, pain in the eye to come on; chōr lagun, sudden diarrhœa to come; būth l., a demon to take possession of a person; and so on) (cf. K.Pr. 13, of a nettle-sting; Rām. 984, 1350); to reach, be felt (by, dat.) (Rām. 1084, 1201, light fell on the eyes); (of fire) to be kindled (cf. nār lᵒ, s.v. nār), to catch; ¶ to be habitually employed, esp. of language, etc. (e.g. lajyōy, it was habitually said by you, K.Pr. 158; yĕs logᵘ, to whomever there is a habit of saying (so-and-so), i.e. whoever habitually says (so-and-so), K.Pr. 241); ¶ to be joined (to), obtain, find, get (Śiv. 1755); (of a name) to be called, to be given to a person (Rām. 607); to become close to a person, pata l., to follow close behind (K. 417); ¶ to fall to a person's lot, to have to be done (as in bakhēra l., a piece of troublesome work to have to be done (so, H. viii, 5); to be incumbent (on), to be necessary to be done (by), to be proper to be done (Rām. 77). [In this sense it is generally used in the future indicative or past conditional, with the future passive participle of another verb. There are three ways of using it in this sense, viz.:-- ¶ (1) the governed verb is put in the fut. pass. part. and agrees with the personal subject, as in lagaw- na ȧsⁱ mĕtran trāwȧnⁱ, we should not abandon friends, or ¶ (2) the governed verb is construed passively, as in ʦĕ lagi (or lagihē) mārüñᵘ̈ sa zanāna, that woman is proper to be beaten by thee, i.e. thou shouldst beat that woman, or ¶ (3) the governed verb is put into the infinitive, which is treated as a verbal noun, as in asĕ totᵘ lagihĕ gaʦhun, for us, the going there would be proper, i.e. we should go there (K. 34). Cf. Gr.Gr. 113 and Gr.M.]; ¶ to have suitableness or a harmonious relation, to fit, suit, become (Gr.Gr. 175, 204; K. 1067); to get into vogue or fashion; to be perceived (as such-and-such), to taste (nice, nasty, etc.) (Rām. 1751); (of a crime or the like) to be imputed (to), to be charged (against) (Rām. 1060); to feel sore (of some part of the body)  (Gr.Gr. 175, 204); ¶ to be undertaken, to begin (as in bārav lagun, search to be undertaken; similarly, Śiv. 1550, 1720, 1727). [In this sense it is used with the oblique infinitive of another verb to form an inceptive compound, as in suh karani logᵘ, he began to do; suh logᵘ khath lēkhani, he began to write a letter; suh logᵘ zanāna mārani, he began to beat the woman] (Gr.Gr. 207; Gr.M.; YZ. 536; Rām. 10, 97, 202, 221, et passim; Śiv. 69, 86, 119, et passim; K. 14, 25, 51, 57, 151, et passim; H. v, 5, 7; viii, 6; x, 1, 7, 8; xii, 1); to apply oneself (to), to set to work (at, dat.), to begin (to, dat.) (used with any noun or infinitive, in much the same sense as above) (K. 40, 56, 136, 156, 229, 235, 241, 261-2-3, 294, 297, 315, 317, 339, 345, et passim); to begin to exist, to begin (e.g. nightfall, H. viii, 9). ¶ logᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. lüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), joined (to), bound, etc., in all the above senses (YZ. 20, 68, 342, 475; Rām. 577, 1584; Śiv. 583, 1309, 1727). ¶ lagan-hār adj. c.g. fit to be joined, etc. (Gr.Gr. 129). ¶ lagan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), in all the above senses; esp. one who is arrested on some charge; one who has been beaten in gambling. ¶ lagith gaʦhun m.inf. to become tightly or closely attached, as ab.

conj. 1 (caus. of lagun, q.v. There is also a regular caus. form, laganāwun, q.v., which is used in special meanings (Gr.Gr. 175); 1 p.p. lôgᵘ, 2 p.p. lājyōv), to attach, unite, join, connect, (Gr.M., Rām. 570); to fasten, attach (cf. kŏkar-tīrĕ lāgañĕ, p. 432a, l. 45) (Rām. 671, K. 419); to fix, affix, apply (cf. düjᵘ̈ lāgüñᵘ̈, p. 203a, l. 19; cūnⁱ lāgüñᵘ̈, p. 172b, l. 19; drᵃka lāgañĕ, p. 242b, l. 49) (Rām. 477, 1127, 1132, 1763); to put, place (cf. bö̃dⁱwān lāgun, p. 83b, l. 39 (YZ. 315); jĕnḍa lāgun, to set up a flag, H. v, 11); ¶ to fix, put on (a crown, turban, shoe, etc.) (Śiv. 321, 361, 1615, 1829); to put (clothes) on, to dress (a person) (K. 973); ¶ to put to (a boat), to moor (cf. baṭhi l., p. 140b, l. 9); to cause (a boat) to run aground (Rām. 1202); to put to, to shut, close (a door, etc.); ¶ to apply, touch with (cf. atha l., p. 59b, l. 18; K.Pr. 73) (L.V. 44, pānas lögith mĕʦĕ, having applied (rubbed on) earth to his body; K. 70, 75, 1000); to bring into close contact, or connexion (with, dat.), to incorporate (in), make one (with) (Śiv. 1008, 1671); to cause to approach, to take (a person) (to a certain place or person) (cf. bāl- bachĕ l., p. 103b, l. 42) (Rām. 375); to entangle (in a net, trap, etc.) YZ. 210; Rām. 218, 614, 1595, 1606); ¶ to employ (an article for a certain use), to apply (something to a certain purpose) (K. 11; Śiv. 531, 1710); esp. to employ (a thing in worship), to make an offering (of something) (L.V. 39, 40, 42, 78, 79; Rām. 1119; Śiv. 52, 112, 187, 662, etc.; K. 1, et passim); to put, or set (to work), to employ, engage (cf. bã̄ḍ l., p. 82a, l. 18) (YZ. 146, K. 1066); to apply, to use (cf. ashud l., p. 48a, l. 49; dar l., p. 234b, l. 23; drötⁱ lāgȧnⁱ, p. 249a, l. 47; kroʦhᵘ lāgun, p. 478a, l. 28) (K.Pr. 243, Rām. 977); ¶ to fix an imputation (upon), to impute (to), to charge (with) (cf. hāʦh lāgüñᵘ̈, p. 360a, l. 40) (YZ. 19; K. 150, 675); ¶ to cause (an act) to begin, to set (an act) going (cf. bakh l., p. 99a, l. 13; bīr lāgüñᵘ̈, p. 117b, l. 36; bāṭh lāgun, p. 139b, l. 1; ḍã̄b l., p. 182a, l. 15; daranga l., p. 247b, l. 13) (Rām. 80, 525; K. 322; H. iii, 7); ¶ to imitate, to act in the character of, to pretend to be (such-and-such, or so-and-so), to act as, to dress oneself up as (cf. ḍī˜gamīr l., p. 196b, l. 21; ḍyuḍᵘ l., p. 267a, l. 44) (Gr.Gr. 125; Rām. 52, 66, 586, 922, 1017, 1019; Śiv. 487, 528-9, 1813; K. 13, 186, 221-2, 251, 298, 380, 388, 1020; H. i, 2; v, 9, 10, 11; x, 7, 12, 14); to act the part (of so-and-so), to perform the office (of so-and-so), to act (in such-and-such a capacity) (L.V. 43; Rām. 12, 134, 190, 388, 1038, 1529; Śiv. 494; K. 195); pānas lögith (L.V. 44), having assumed thine own character, (of the Supreme Śiva) having become indiscrete; ¶ to put together, construct, build (Śiv. 337); ¶ to arrange, to carry on (a process) (cf. khītⁱ lāgüñᵘ̈, p. 421b, l. 6); to plough, cultivate (El., Gr.Gr. 129). ¶ lôgᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. löjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), united, joined, etc., as ab. ¶ lögith ʦŏpᵃrith conj. part. used as adv., substituting on account of resemblance, using an inferior substitute as a makeshift.
or lagushĕnkā f. urine, piss; emission of urine, urinating. Cf. dīrgashĕnkā.

m. (a Hindū word) the moment of the sun's entrance into a zodiacal sign (Rām. 1259, 1261; K. 57, 130); an auspicious or lucky moment; esp. (amongst Hindūs) the moment of a wedding; hence, the festival of the wedding of one person to another, a man's or woman's wedding festival (u.w. ref. to one party of a marriage, as we talk of so-and-so's wedding, and not with reference to both parties considered together) (El. lagan, a wedding; L. 261; Śiv. 730, 1081, 1102, 1118, 1125; K. 25, 779) (cf. nĕcivⁱ-lⁱ, s.v. nĕcyuwᵘ). ¶ lạgᵃna-cīrᵃ or --ʦᵘ̈rᵘ̈ -- f. the paper formally sent by the bride's people to the bridegroom's people, inviting the latter to the wedding festival (L. 258, 268). -dachinⁱ f. (among Hindūs) the presents given at a wedding by the parents, etc., of the bride or bridegroom, each to their own family priests, etc. -dūsh m. (amongst Hindūs) a marriage-blemish; esp. (in the case of a Brāhmaṇa bride) a marriage postponed till after she has attained the age of twelve years (before which time a girl of this caste should be married). -dūsh kāsun m.inf. to take away such a blemish; i.e. to marry a girl after she has attained the age of twelve years. Such a marriage is performed very simply and without the usual distribution of gifts, etc. -lạgᵃn f. the occurrence of a number of marriages at the same time and in the same locality. --ʦᵘ̈rᵘ̈ -- f., i.q. lạgᵃna cīrⁱ, ab. -vizi charun m.inf. to have diarrhœa at the time of one's wedding; hence, met. to do something that seriously interferes with other work on which one is busily engaged. ¶ lạgᵃ̇nᵃ̇ āmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈--), got or obtained by marriage (of a wife with reference to her husband or vice versa; but generally used when there is some inequality in the marriage, as if one side or the other had got a bad bargain). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come (i.e. be obtained) by marriage (of a husband or wife). ¶ lạgᵃnan aʦun m.inf. to enter (the proper condition) for marriages; i.e. the slender and graceful appearance of a boy or girl approaching marriageable age to become manifest.

or lāha in laha-prāh or lāha-prāh m. an attack of hysterical fever or a cataleptic condition brought about by some sudden terror (looked upon as a kind of demoniacal possession which attacks babies or pregnant women). Cf. prāh.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lahanôwᵘ), causal of lahanun (q.v.) in all its senses. lahanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. lahanöwᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to become soft, rough, etc.; causal of lahanyō-motᵘ, q.v., ab.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. lahanyōv), (of an intelligent man or animal) to become slack (by non-exertion, want of application, worry, or the like); (of the skin or muscles) to become relaxed (by shampooing, etc.); (of something naturally soft) to become hard or rough (by exposure to the sun or to fire); (of a mild-tempered person) to become rough or harsh (through irritation or want of exertion). lahanyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. lahanyē-müʦᵘ̈), softened, roughened, etc., as ab.
f. self-will, indocility. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such to arise, self- will to be exhibited. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show indocility, to act in a self-willed manner.

f. an increase of wealth (from one's ordinary business); esp. when such increase is marked or more than ordinary, a windfall of profit. -bahar f. prosperity, increase of wealth and fortune; prime and vigour, fulness and flush, glow and glory.
f. a sweet, gentle sound, a low sweet tone; a pleasing song of praise, a pæan (Śiv. 1295). --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to emit such a sound, to sing soft and low.

adj. (f. lahavüñᵘ̈), stiffened, dried, somewhat hardened or indurated (e.g. of grain, or the like, which was soft or damp, and to which heat or the like has been applied); (in reference to motion, speech, etc.) moderately quick, fairly rapid. lahawan-phash m. drying, airing, slight kiln-drying (of something damp or soft).
in lahi-lahi, a fight with blows (L. 460).
adj. c.g. in need of some necessity, without means for accomplishing some necessary work. Cf. lojᵘ.

m. a disaster, calamity, piece of evil fortune (e.g. being charged with some crime, or finding oneself unexpectedly faced with an almost impossible task, or called upon to pay up security incurred in guaranteeing someone else's debt). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to accept such a calamity (e.g. to admit the truth of a false charge, to pay up a security, or to guarantee to perform some almost impossible task with which one is faced). --khārun -- m.inf. to bring such a calamity on a person (charging with a crime, making him liable to pay a security, or to carry out some almost impossible task). --khasun -- m.inf. such a calamity as above to come upon a person (e.g. a charge of crime to be brought, or a difficult task to be imposed). -loṭᵘ the tail of a calamity, the results of a calamity (such as the helplessness of a family when the head has died); the fruits of adverse fortune (e.g. of following bad advice, of becoming liable for a security, of being the subject of obloquy, etc.). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be involved in calamity (e.g. having to pay up a guarantee, or to become subject to a false charge, etc.). ¶ lā̃ja-bôrᵘ m. distress or anxiety over the thought of some almost impossible task with which one is faced. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), free from calamity (as above) (referring either to a person or to a task which he has to accomplish).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. lã̄jaladiñ), subject to calamity (of a person, a business, a property, etc.). For the meaning of 'calamity', see lã̄j.
m. poverty owing to the want of the means or appliances for necessaries, destitution. Cf. laj and lojᵘ.
m. good joining (e.g. of the parts of a broken article fitted together), a neat joint. Cf. lagun.
m. lapis lazuli (El.); a beautiful purple (El.).
adj. c.g. made of lapis lazuli; of the colour of lapis lazuli.

f. a horse's bridle, a rein (El.; Gr.M.; Rām. 1335; H. xi, 9). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to put on a bridle (on to a horse); met. to reduce a person to silence (by oppression), not to let a person even speak. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a bridle to be applied; (of a horse) to be brought under control of a bridle; met. to be reduced (by some oppressor) to silence, not to be given an opportunity even of speaking.
f. in chŏka-lākañ, p. 159b, l. 25, q.v.

f. (sg. dat. lāki), a great collection or pile of property (of things carried in loads and ultimately collected together). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a collection to come (to a person), great quantities (e.g. of gifts, donations, or the like) to be received. ¶ lāka-sörᵘ̈ f. the collection load by load and, similarly, sending away, of great quantities of property. -sāray f. the collection (e.g. in the way of many different gifts and donations) of many loads of property. ¶ lāki lāki adv. by gradual collection in heaps and piles.
or lö̃kh f. (sg. dat. lã̄ki or lö̃ki), an island (E. lönk) (Śiv. 1820 (lö̃kh)); a residence or garden on an island (El.); a stride (El., Gr.Gr. 11).
in lakh-lānath (?) لق لعنت f. (sg. dat. -lānüʦᵘ̈), reproach, calling shame to a person, abusing for improper conduct. Cf. lĕkh.
for lach in lakh-trakh, a hundred-thousand trakh or measures of about 9 1/2 lb. (Śiv. 1828). See trakh.
a piece, part, portion, some, a little; yakh-lakh = یکلخت adv. all at one piece, all at once, altogether, completely, entirely (K. 561).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. lakhanôwᵘ), to cause to enter forcibly; esp. obsc.; (with a fem. subject) to cause to be forcibly entered; hence, to act as a bawd or procuress for another woman. Caus. of lakhun, q.v.

(often spelt by purists lakshĕn or) m. a mark, token, sign, characteristic, distinguishing mark (Rām. 125, 135, 667, 1261; Śiv. 224, 242, 513, 979, 1045; K. 129, 134); a mark, a sign, an omen (K. 235).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. lokhᵘ; 2 p.p. lachyōv), to put into (something hidden and narrow), to force into; esp. obsc. (cf. mŏnḍa l., s.v. mŏnḍ 2). ¶ lokhᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. lüchᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), forced into, as ab. ¶ lakhan -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who forces into; esp. a habitual rake.

(often spelt by purists lakshman or), m. name of a brother of Rāmacandra (in Sanskrit, Lakṣmaṇa). He was a son of Daśaratha by his wife Sumitrā (Rām. 1, 36, 86, 223, 322, 326, etc.; Śiv. 852, 1419, 1482 K. 730).

(often spelt by purists lakshmī) f. N. of the goddess of fortune, prosperity, and beauty (in Sanskrit, Lakṣmī), regarded as the wife of Vishnu (Skt. Viṣṇu) (Rām. 115, 580, 1086, 1120, 1276; Śiv. 432, 484, 714, 796, 1092, 1150, 1288; K. 59, 642, 665-6, 735, 929); good fortune, prosperity, wealth (Rām. 128, Śiv. 59).

(often spelt by purists lakshmīwān), adj. c.g. one who possesses (or is the spouse of) the goddess Lȧkhⁱmī (q.v.), i.e. the god Vishnu (Śiv. 581, see bel.); one who is possessed of good fortune, fortunate (Śiv. 581, with double meaning).
m. a long strip of paper or the like rolled tightly up, a roll of paper.
see lȧkhⁱmī; lakshman or, see lȧkhⁱman; lakshmīwān, see lȧkhⁱmīwān; lakshĕn or, see lakhĕn.

m. (of butcher's meat) the flesh of the shoulder, a shoulder of mutton. --karun -- m.inf. to make (one's limbs into) butcher's meat; hence, met. to set a person to such hard work that he is thoroughly worn out or till every bone seems out of joint. --lakta gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become bits of butcher's meat; hence, met. to be cruelly overworked, as ab.
m. paralysis of half the body, hemiplegia.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. lạkᵃwaladiñ), suffering from hemiplegia.
a primary suffix used to form nouns of agency from the roots di- and dāv-, always in an obscene sense. Cf. al 3, p. 23a, l. 12 (Gr.Gr. 107).

m. a ruby (K.Pr. 123; YZ. 75, 213; Rām. 217, 569, 643, 744, 1116, etc.; Śiv. 2, 163, 194, 428, 713, 793, 818, etc.; H. i, 9; viii, 3, 11; x, 2, 5, 12; xii, 2, 3, 4, etc.); the pupil of the eye (Rām. 1139, 1194, 1293, 1614; Śiv. 707, 1210, 1250, 1259); cf. ȧchⁱ-lāl, p. 8a, l. 43. lāl-ĕ-könī لعلِ کآنی m. a ruby of the mine, a ruby of great price (Rām. 1141); met. a precious and beautiful virgin (Rām. 1055). lāl- pharōsh = لعل فِروش m. a ruby-seller, a jeweller (H. xii, 3). -shĕnākh = لعل شناخت, properly f., 'understanding of rubies,' but in H. xii, 4, 5, etc., used as a noun masculine with the meaning of lāl-shinās, bel. (sg. dat. -shĕnākas, H. xii, 4, 5, 6, etc.). -shinās لعل شناس m. one who understands rubies, an expert in jewels, a lapidary; a ruby-seller (K.Pr. 123). ¶ lāla-pholᵘ m. a single ruby; the pupil of the eye (Rām. 1105); met. a darling son, a perfect darling of a son. Cf. lāl 2.

f. a blister, a swelling of the skin; the pus or matter in a boil, carbuncle, or the like (cf. bīka-lala, p. 99b, l. 31; māz-lal, s.v. māz). --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a blister to rise, a swelling to form in the skin. --wasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a swelling to subside or descend; hence, (of a fat round belly) to become thin or hollow.

or (L.V. 105, K.Pr. 64) lāla m. a darling, a beloved (usually referring to a child or the like, but in L.V. 105, referring to the Deity) (Rām. 1770, Śiv. 1380); a beloved person generally (Śiv. 1691); 'the baby,' a name by which a woman refers to her child (K.Pr. 64). Cf. lāl 1, with which it is often confused.

f. (sg. dat. lali), N. of a celebrated mystic poetess of Kashmīr, who lived probably in the fourteenth century. She was a Śaiva by religion, and her verses are still frequently quoted. She is popularly known as Lal Dĕd or 'Granny Lal', and, in Sanskrit, her name was Lallā. Many collections of her verses have been made under the Sanskrit name of the Lallā Vākyāni, or 'Sayings of Lallā'. The most complete edition is that published by the Royal Asiatic Society in 1920 (L.V. 3, 48, 49, etc.; K.Pr. 47, 82). In token of respect Hindūs refer to her as Lalīshŏrī (Śiv. 1656, 1773).
f. a woman, a wanton woman, a temptress (Śiv. 759, where the word is used met. for worldly temptations from the path of holiness).

adj. c.g. red. lāl gulāb لال گلاب m. the red rose, one of the two varieties of Kashmīr roses. The other is yellow, and is called arawal, see El., s.v. guláb. lāl hāputh m. the brown or red bear (Ursus Arctus or Isabellinus) (L. 111).

f. slackness or flabbiness of the flesh of the belly, etc., marked by heavy breathing and intumescence; cf. lalal. --pọ̆tᵘ -- m. the son of a barren woman, i.e. something impossible, a thing which cannot occur, an unbelievable occurrence.
f. a female (human or of the brute creation) suffering from a swollen and flabby belly (e.g. from being pregnant, or from disease). Cf. lala 1.
f. a handkerchief, a square piece of cotton for wiping the perspiration from one's face or for blowing the nose.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lalanôwᵘ), i.q. lalawun 1, q.v. (L.V. 105; YZ. 559; Rām. 216, 269, 1129, 1522; Śiv. 329).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. as in the preceding), i.q. lalawun 2, q.v.
f. longing, ardent desire; covetousness, cupidity, greed.
f. ardent affection, love (for a husband, wife, child, etc.); longing, ardent desire.
adj. c.g. full of longing, ardently desirous; covetous, cupidinous, greedy.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. lalowᵘ), to take to one's breast (cf. lŏl); hence, to fondle, dandle, protect (YZ. 559; Śiv. 1190, 1371, 1574); to soothe (a pain) (L.V. 105; Rām. 1105; H. v, 6); (of a fire) to keep (the coals) together, to keep it alive. Another form of this verb is lalanāwun 1 (L.V. 105), q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lalowᵘ), to talk foolishly, to babble (YZ. 480); to describe something (e.g. sorrow or the like) in broken or babbling language (YZ. 570). Cf. lalanāwun 2.
(? spelling) N. of a kind of apple grown in Kashmīr. It is of pale yellow colour, and sweet (L. 349).
in lāli-māli adv. very peacefully and affectionately, comfortably; cf. lōl. -māli bĕhun m.inf. to settle down comfortably (in some occupation or the like).
f. a display of affection (given when it is not felt, e.g. shown in the presence of the parents to their naughty child).

m. a cave or hole dug in the ground or in a bank, a dug-out; a heap of stones or earth (El., K.Pr. 13); cf. lamb, and mĕʦi-lam, s.v. më̆ʦᵘ̈. --wasithyunᵘ -- m.inf. a dug-out to come falling; met. to be suddenly overwhelmed with much work or many duties; a sudden and unexpected windfall of great wealth to occur.
m. a Lama, a Buddhist priest of Tibet.
m. for lama 1 in atha-lam, q.v. (p. 59b, l. 21).
f. a determined attack, a fearless onslaught on the foe.

f. for lama 2 in the following:-- ¶ -lisar m. delaying, procrastination, deliberate neglect. -lisar trāwun m.inf. deliberately to procrastinate, to ca' canny. -yĕsal m. the occurrence of delay or procrastination (in some work requiring speedy accomplishment).
for lamba in lam-chĕr m. a long male stick (chēr as m. of chīrᵘ̈ 2, q.v.), i.e. a tall man, a long fellow.

f. one of the divine mothers, or personified energies of the principal Hindū deities. In Sanskrit they are called mātṛkā, and are variously reckoned as 7, 8, 9, or 16 in number. They are closely connected with the worship of Śiva. -ʦakᵃr m. the circle or assembly of these mothers (Skt. mātṛkā- maṇḍala). -ʦakra-poshᵘ m. a beast devoted for sacrifice in the joint worship of all these mothers; met. anything devoted, or destined, to destruction (L.V. 63).

(cf. lam 2) m. the act of pulling, dragging, dragging away (cf. atha-lama 1, p. 59b, l. 23) (Gr.Gr. 27). -lam f. pully-haully, pulling one against another (as in a tug of war); met. persistently importuning of an unwilling person to join in some common action.
(cf. lam 3) f. delay, slowness in doing any work, dilatoriness, laggardness (Gr.Gr. 148); cf. lang 2. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to become dilatory, to ca' canny. -törᵘ̈ f. delay, dilatoriness.

(cf. Pers. دامن) f. (sg. dat. lāmüñᵘ̈), the low, wild, sparsely inhabited ground at the foot of a mountain; a village in such a country. lāmüñᵘ̈-hondᵘ̈ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, such a country or village.
f. (sg. dat. lamüñᵘ̈), pulling, pulling out, forcibly extracting (cf. lama 1); pulling, tugging, towing. -raz f. the tow-rope of a boat.
(cf. lama 2), f. in --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show dilatoriness, to be dilatory, to be laggard, to make delay.
n.ag. (f. -vüñᵘ̈), a dragger; hence, that which hangs suspended (cf. atha-lamawunᵘ, p. 59b, l. 27).
or lam 1 (q.v.) m. a cave or hole dug in the ground or in a bank, a dug-out; a heap of earth or the like (cf. mĕʦi-lamb, s.v. më̆ʦᵘ̈).
adj. c.g. long, lengthy; (of a human being) tall. Cf. lam 4.
m. 'he who has a pendulous belly', N. of the god Gaṇēśa (Śiv. 4). See ganēsh.
m. (sg. dat. lambakas), the form or the taking of solid, or apparently solid, form of something ordinarily impalpable (e.g. smoke becoming soot, flame, a cloud; cf. dᵃh- lambukh, p. 198a, l. 11).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. lomᵘ), to drag, pull, tug at (El.; L. 459; L.V. 95; K.Pr. 126; Rām. 118, 122, 979; Śiv. 179; H. viii, 9); to pull, to pluck (vegetables or the like) (K.Pr. 184); to tow a boat (El., Gr.M., L.V. 106); to pull at, to devote oneself to, be a slave to (Śiv. 754); to depart, go away, set forth (Śiv. 1751). lȧmⁱ lȧmⁱ freq. part. dragging (and) dragging; hence (as adv.), with much urging. laman-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a tower, the man or woman who pulls a boat by a tow-rope; met. one who is ready to depart (quasi, who is towing his boat away from his home).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. lamūṭiladiñ), a habitual delayer, one who by nature impedes any work on which he is engaged.
f. delay (caused by sloth, laziness, or the like). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause delay in this way.
m. (f. lamᵘ̈rᵘ̈), one who causes delay (in a joint work or the like), a slacker, one who ca's canny (Gr.Gr. 148).
m. scolding, abuse, rebuke (Gr.M.); insult (El., who makes the word f.). --karun -- (El. --karüñᵘ̈ --), to scold, etc. (El.); to insult (El.).

f. (sg. dat. lānüʦᵘ̈), a curse, imprecation, anathema (Rām. 656); a reproach; a curse, i.e. a cursed thing, an intolerable nuisance (K.Pr. 30, 235); cf. dāgi-lānath, p. 196a, l. 9. --pashpüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. imprecation to ooze out, general public blame to be incurred. --wasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. imprecation to descend, to be humiliated owing to reproaches.
(Śiv. 973), i.q. nandan, q.v., also = the English 'London' (H. xi, 3).

adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. lanḍaras), having no wife, children, etc., having no family. --mŏnḍur -- m., id., but more general, having no relations of any kind; alone in the world. ¶ lanḍar-bāpār m. the condition or behaviour of being alone in the world, a solitary life; the evil conduct resulting from such a condition (intriguing with other people's wives, and so on).

m. the trunk or main branch of a tree (cf. ṭȧpⁱ-lⁱ, p. 1013b, l. 29) (El., Rām. 603-7, Śiv. 368); met. the thick part of the leg, the thigh (El.); cf. lünḍᵘ̈ 2. --lünḍᵘ̈ -- f. the trunk and branches of a tree (as a whole conception); all a person's relations and connexions, his family in the widest sense. ¶ langas dôdᵘ m. pain of the thigh (El.).

m. delay, retardation; cf. lama 2. --kāsun -- m.inf. to take away delay, to remove its cause, to complete anything up to time in spite of delay. --rōzun -- m.inf. to be deferred to the last moment (of a gift, repayment of money due, or the like). --thawun -- m.inf. to delay to the last moment, as ab.
m. in mas-lang, a woman's head of hair. See mas 2.
f. a small branch (El.). Cf. lünḍᵘ̈ 2.
m. hunger. --karun -- m.inf. to abstain from food, to fast.

m. a public kitchen (e.g. kept by a great man for his followers and dependants); an almshouse, an establishment at some holy place, where food is distributed free to all comers (such as pilgrims, etc.). --pakun -- m.inf. to cook food in such a public kitchen; hence, to be occupied only in providing food for oneself and others. --thawun -- m.inf. to start such a public cook- house (as a charity), to endow a poorhouse.
m. an anchor (cf. lŏh-lᵒ, p. 515b, l. 18).
m. (of a wall or the like) slope, want of perpendicularity, cant, obliquity, list, slant. --karun -- m.inf. to become out of the perpendicular, as ab. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. such obliquity to occur.
m. the superintendent, or person in charge, of a public kitchen. See laṅgar 1.
f. cooked provisions given to the poor at a public kitchen; (in Kashmīr) a great pile of cooked rice. See langar 1, and bata-langȧrⁱ, p. 137a, l. 20.
n.ag. (f. langavüñᵘ̈), one who walks with a halting gait or lamely; hence, one who traverses a difficult mountain path.
f. lameness, limping, a halting gait (Gr.Gr. 128). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a halting gait to become manifest.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. longᵘ; 2 p.p. lanjyōv. This verb is conjugated impersonally in the tenses derived from the past participles), to be lame (Gr.Gr. 128); to walk lamely, to limp, to be crippled.
m. a kind of monkey, the Himalayan langūr (Semnopithecus Schistaceus) (L. 108).
m. a greedy fellow who haunts places where food is distributed free, a 'free-luncher'. Cf. langar 1.
f. (sg. dat. langōcĕ), a loincloth. --karith --, wearing a loincloth (H. xii, 23).
adj. c.g. (of a tree or the like) endowed with branches, branched; (of a man) possessing many relatives of all branches. Cf. lünḍᵘ̈ 2.

m. lameness (due to being crippled); (of a pillar or the like) the condition of being awry; (of a portable brazier or the like) the being damaged through having the handle broken or the like. Cf. lünḍᵘ̈ 2, longᵘ, and langar 3.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lanjyorᵘ), to form into branches, to open out (e.g. a bundle of straw or sticks); to open out, disentangle (cotton or the like). Cf. lünḍᵘ̈ 2.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lanjyorᵘ), to cripple, to lame a person; (of anything with more than one leg) to make unsteady (by breaking or otherwise damaging one of the legs). Cf. longᵘ.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lạnjᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. lanjĕrun 1, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lạnjᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. lanjĕrun 2, q.v.
f. N. of the capital of Rāvaṇa (Rām. 174, 228, 391, 393, et passim; Śiv. 704, 737-8, 852, 1422, 1482). See lö̃kh.
m. a long branch or rod cut from a tree (used for knocking down leaves or fruit from trees, or similar reaching at high objects) (El.) (Gr.Gr. 10, a stake).
m. Gymnosporia spinosa (El.). (The word should probably be spelt lāph.)
m. a loquacious fellow full of nonsensical and foolish talk, a chatterer, a jabberer. --shĕpar m. a foolish, untrue reply to some question.

m. (sg. dat. lāphas), self-praise; boasting, bragging, bluster (El. lāf; K.Pr. 124); (in Kāshmīrī) an angry asseveration, an angry bluff; (?) Gymnosporia spinosa (see lāp). --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to wager publicly that such-and-such an unlikely thing is the case, to bluff publicly and aloud. --dyunᵘ -- m. sg. inf. to boast, assert boastfully or scornfully (Rām. 1065, 1215, 1444-5).

f. (sg. dat. lari 1; for 2, 3, 4, see lar 2, lorᵘ 1, lürᵘ̈), a thread (Śiv. 163, 247, 338); a strand (of a rope or cord) or string of a necklace of many strings (cf. mŏkhta-lᵒ). ¶ lara-milawan f. (sg. dat. -milavüñᵘ̈), the joining up or being joined up of a rope, string, or garland, by the mutual uniting of each separate strand, the splicing of a rope, etc. -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), the splicing together of a broken or partially broken rope, string, garland, etc.

m. Lār, the ancient Lahara, the N. of an important Pargana in Kashmīr. It comprises the whole of the valleys drained by the river Sind and its tributaries as well as the alluvial tract on the right bank of that river after its entry into the great Kashmīr plain (RT.Tr. II, 488) (El.; K.Pr. 2, 124; Śiv. 1684, 1894). lārukᵘ adj. (f. lārücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, Lār (K.Pr. 79).

f. (sg. dat. lari 2; for 1, 3, 4, see lar 1, lorᵘ 1, lürᵘ̈), the side or flank of a man (K.Pr. 57; Śiv. 1825; H. vii, 7); cf. lab and s.v. pāha 2, pāha-lara. -lab f. close- besideness, i.e. intimate and immediate connexion between cause and effect, giving and receiving, reception and dismissal, etc. -lab hë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. to exhibit attachment or devotion, e.g. of a guest, a child, or a wife to the head of a house, or of an animal to its master. -lab raṭüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to become devoted or attached to (a person, country, etc.). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. onesidedness to happen, e.g. (in the case of friendship) anger to occur on one side, (or of a vessel or garment) to be damaged on one side. --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to lie down (for sleep, rest, etc.); to show laziness or indifference in any work. ¶ lara-köñᵘ̈ f. a bone of the side, a rib (El. larakaiṅ or laṛakányi). Cf. kāñi-lᵒ, p. 460b, l. 39. ¶ lari hyonᵘ m.inf. to take to one's side; hence, to collect people to help one, to take a person as a helper, to collect comrades for a fight, or the like; to lie down on a bed, to curl oneself up in bed. --phērun -- m.inf. to turn by the side; hence, to turn over from one side to the other, when lying on a bed; (of a fallen person) to roll over (Śiv. 1236, 1286); (of one who has been knocked down) to get up again (and be ready for action). --phirun -- m.inf. to turn a thing or recumbent person over on its or his side; to awake or arouse a sleeping or senseless person by shaking him, turning him over, etc.; (of a recumbent person) to turn over on the other side, or from side to side. --phirun dyunᵘ -- m.inf. (of a person lying on a bed) to turn over from one side to the other; (of a person asleep, or fallen down senseless) to be roused and get up in one's full senses. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain by one's side; (in a combat) to be at hand as a helper. -tāph m. (sg. dat. -tāpas), heat of the sun falling on, or applied to, one side only of the body.

f. running; running away, fleeing, absconding (Gr.Gr. 127, W. 114); pursuit; hence, harassment, persecution (K.Pr. 157, 187; Śiv. 1795). --aʦüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. running away to enter, i.e. running away or fleeing to occur, abandoning house and home to come into existence, to have to abscond (K.Pr. 37). --ganḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause a person to flee, etc. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause (so-and-so, dat.) to flee, to pursue (Gr.M.; Rām. 1301; H. ii, 9). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. running away, abandoning house and home to occur, to be compelled to run away, to be pursued (K.Pr. 128). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to find oneself compelled to run away; to be compelled to finish some work in a hurry (owing to some impediment or the like having delayed it). --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. vviolently to urge running, i.e. to compel a person to run away, or hurriedly to finish some business. --ʦānüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to set a person running, to set in a run a person already walking, to put to flight (Rām. 470; H. ix, 2). ¶ lāra-lār f. (of a crowd) running away in all directions, scattering in flight. ¶ lāri āmotᵘ perf. part. (f. -āmüʦᵘ̈), one who pursues with the object of putting to flight. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to run (at, dat.), to rush at, attack (Rām. 648). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to run after, with the object of putting to flight (K. 156, 614).
in lar-watharū m. a small rice-field (L. 463, where it is spelt lar wattru). Cf. baḍ- watharū, p. 81b, l. 48. Probably incorrect for līr, q.v.

(for 2, see lārun 1) f. (sg. dat. lārüñᵘ̈), quivering, shivering, trembling (from palsy or other disease, from epilepsy, terror, etc.) (Gr.Gr. 121); shaking, shivering (El.). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. shivering to come on, esp. the quivering on the approach of death. ¶ lārüñᵘ̈-hotᵘ̈ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), one who is attacked by shivering, as ab.
or lārawun conj. 1 (1 p.p. lāranôwᵘ orlārowᵘ), to cause to run, to put to flight (Gr.Gr. 171).
n.ag. (f. lāravüñᵘ̈), one who burnishes, a burnisher.
n.ag. (f. as in 1), one who runs; one who pursues or chases, a pursuer (K.Pr. 217); one who runs away, a fugitive.
n.ag. (f. as in 1), that which smears and adheres (as grease on the inside of a pot); that which defiles by contact; that which is being acquired or which is about to be acquired.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. lāriladiñ), one who runs away in terror, a fugitive.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. lôrᵘ), to burnish, polish, rub with a whetstone. ¶ lôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. lörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), burnished, polished with a whetstone. ¶ lāran-mŏhara m. a burnishing stone. -ṭulᵘ m. the same.

or (vill.) lāḍun conj. 3 (2 p.p. lāryōv), to stick to (W. 132); to be smeared (upon anything), to stain, dirty, defile, pollute (El.; K.Pr. 112, 125; Rām. 1171); to be connected, blended, absorbed in, mixed with; to touch, be in contact with (Rām. 656); to stick to (anything), adhere to (K.Pr. 23, 153, 252; Śiv. 1802; H. viii, 6); to remain close to (any person or thing) (Śiv. 211); to benefit or be useful to (Śiv. 1795); to become a person's property, to become acquired (K.Pr. 48, Rām. 1158). lāryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. lāryē-müʦᵘ̈), smeared upon; blended; touched; acquired.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. lārüñᵘ̈ladiñ), one who is afflicted with quivers or shivers after insensibility due to emaciation, one who is palsied.
shaking, quaking, trembling (cf. zuwa- lᵒ, p. 1236b, l. 47).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. larzōv), to quake, tremble, fear (cf. لرزہ) (Rām. 1622).

m. a pile, heap, or collection of wealth, accumulated wealth. --athi lagun -- m.inf. a heap of wealth to come into the hand; to become, all at once, possessed of great wealth accumulated by another. --athi yunᵘ -- m.inf. great wealth to come into the possession of a person other than he who accumulated it. --banun -- m.inf. great wealth suddenly, and without exertion, to be acquired. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. the same. --zēnun -- m.inf. to gain possession of great wealth accumulated by another.
m. the city of Lhāsa; hence, the country of which it is the capital, Central Tibet (K.Pr. 255).

in lasa-ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ f. an affectionate term of address (implying a certain amount of reproach) employed by elders to a woman (esp. to a little girl). [The verb lasun means 'to live long', and ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ is cold charcoal. Hence, the compound implies 'though I wish you to live long, still you are only a lump of charcoal'.]
m. a certain precious stone, a cat's eye (El. lasan).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lāsowᵘ), to cause a person to live long and prosperously; e.g. carefully to nurture a child.
n.ag. (f. lasavüñᵘ̈), (esp. of a child or the like) one who lives happily (as compared with his contemporaries and companions) (Śiv. 204, 1324).
f. a dead body, a corpse.
f. a small fragment, in lāshĕ kaḍañĕ f. pl. inf. to cut or divide into many small parts.

f. an army (Gr.M. where it is wrongly shown as masc.; Rām. 514, 695, 701, 1322 ff., 1381, 1442, etc.; H. ii, 6-8, 11; x, 9, 11, 13). [The word is usually feminine in Kāshmīrī, not masc. as elsewhere; cf. W. 18.] lashkari-hünzᵘ̈ jāy karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to encamp.

f. a torch (L. 80, 464; Rām. 248, 971, 1484, 1610, 1696; Śiv. 1688). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to apply a torch; hence, to start a general conflagration, to set on fire (lit. or met.). --ganḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a general conflagration to be started; (met.) the heat of fever or rage to arise. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take a torch; to feel the great heat of fever, rage, sorrow, on the ground of disaster or the like. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the burning of rage, sorrow, etc., to be felt. ¶ lashi-buḍurᵘ m. a spark of burning resin from a burning torch. -bạrᵃg m. a small fragment of a torch. -drǖrᵘ̈ f. a long thick piece of the wood of a torch. -hüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -hacĕ), a piece of wood for making a torch. -kulᵘ m. the wood of which torches are made (usually the yörᵘ̈-tree) (L. 80, 464). -kĕlam m. the resin or pitch which exudes from the wood of a burning torch. -kônᵘ m. (sg. dat. -könis), a piece of the wood of a torch. -kŏtod;nḍᵘ or konḍᵘ m. the black stain left on the body or clothes by the soot of a burning torch; cf. konḍᵘ 4. -kronḍᵘ m. the torch-holder at the top of a high tripod, used as a beacon. -kazul m. (sg. dat. kazalas), the soot of a torch. -ṭyūrᵘ m. a piece of the wood of a torch. -tyū̃thᵘ m. the long thin end of a piece of wood used as part of a torch.
adj. (f. lāsücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, Central Tibet. See lās 2.

conj. 2 [1 p.p. lūstᵘ or (vulg.) losᵘ; f. lǖʦhᵘ̈ (Gr.Gr. 211) or lǖsᵘ̈;2p.p. löʦhōv or lasōv (Gr.Gr. 228, 229); ben. sg. 3, lashĕn (Gr.Gr. 251)], to live (El.; L. 458; Rām. 425, 657, 696, 912, 1268, 1340, 1486); to live well, to live comfortably, to live long, live in good health (Gr.Gr. 205; L.V. 27, 35; Rām. 270, 385, 1627, 1737; K. 103, 503, 1110); to live long (as compared with others), to survive (K.Pr. 3, 150); to come to life, revive (Rām. 897); to survive from some trouble, to escape from trouble (K.Pr. 246; H. x, 7); ben. sg. 3, lashĕn is commonly used in blessings and wishes for long life (K.Pr. 7, spelt lasin). --basun -- m.inf. to lead a long, happy, and prosperous life as a householder. Cf. losᵘ-bosᵘ, s.v. losᵘ and basun lasun (p. 133b, l. 34). ¶ lasan in lasan-byôlᵘ m. a. magical powder for giving a happy and prosperous life with many children. ¶ lūstᵘ-motᵘ 1 (for 2, see lōsun) perf. part. (f. lǖʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ or lǖsᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), one who has lived or is living a happy and prosperous life (e.g. a child, whose condition is compared with that of his contemporaries or companions).
m. a plug, something for stopping a hole; cf. lŏta. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to plug a hole.
adj. c.g. one who kicks, a kicker (W. 111).
m. annoyance caused by the noisy trampling of feet; hence, the experience of vile abuse.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. latôrᵘ), to trample upon; hence, to abuse, revile, censure. ¶ latörith thawun m.inf. to subdue with abuse (as though trampling under foot); to bring under one's own power by crying out assurances of protection. ¶ latôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. latörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), subdued by abuse.
m. absconding, running away (esp. secretly to a foreign country).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. laṭôwᵘ), to depart secretly, abscond.

f. (sg. dat. lati, Gr.Gr. 70) a kick (El. laṭ and laṭh, m.; Gr.Gr. 126; W. 111; L.V. 102; K.Pr. 116, 118, 124; Śiv. 797, 1064, 1606; K. 346, 450) (cf. nam lath nāvi lath, s.v. nam 1); (in rice cultivation) weeding and working the soil with the feet (L. 463-4); the sole of the foot (K.Pr. 232; Rām. 1171; Śiv. 1098; H. viii, 7); cf. lö̆ʦᵘ̈ lath, p. 535b, l. 5. -- dith gaʦhun -- m.inf. to give a kick and go; hence, to abandon (a person, thing, work, business, etc.) and hasten away. --dith trāwun -- m.inf. to kick and abandon; hence, to abandon (a thing, work, or business) and get rid of it or expel it with scorn. -khŏr or -khōr m. the step of a staircase or rung of a ladder (on which the foot is placed). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a kick to be suffered; hence, the experience of undeserved abuse. --lāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to kick (a person) (Rām. 920, K. 600); to spurn, to shun at a distance. ¶ lata-gas m. a rubbing down by kicks, i.e. a bit of ground worn dusty by continual walking over it. -körⁱ  f. kicking, hitting with a kick someone who has been knocked down. -kram m., id. -liwan f. (sg. dat. -liwüñᵘ̈), 'kick-plastering,' i.e. trampling on a thing continually, e.g. woollen cloth in a stone trough to clean it, or mud to make it uniform in consistency for plastering or the like. -liwan karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to do 'kick-plastering', as ab.; hurriedly to fit things together anyhow, without regard to the work being properly done. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. massage with the feet; a kicking (K. 237). -môrᵘ adj. (f. -mörᵘ̈ 1), one who having been knocked down suffers a kicking from another. -mörᵘ̈ 2 f. kicking a person who has been knocked down. -mūrᵘ̈ f. trampling and stamping (on any person or thing). -mūran f. (sg. dat. mūrüñᵘ̈), stamping with the heel on anything (esp. something small). -sör ᵘ̈ f. searching for anything by feeling with the feet (e.g. in the dark, or for something fallen into deep water). -wüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -wacĕ), a gang-board of a boat, a gang-plank.

f. (sg. dat. laṭi), going to a person's residence, visiting. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (with some object in view) to visit a person. ¶ laṭa-laṭh f. (sg. dat. -laṭi), to visit frequently a person or place, in order to accomplish some business. laṭa-ponzᵘ m. expending or wasting time in going to and from some place on some business. -sörᵘ̈ f. carrying away by repeated journeys collected articles and accumulating them elsewhere.

m. (sg. dat. lāṭas), a twist, esp. a single twist of a turban (wrapped in several twists round the head) (K.Pr. 119) (cf. lō̃gi-lāṭh, p. 512a, l. 3, and laṭh 4; pura-lᵒ, s.v. pura 1); the twist of a girdle or the like (cf. ḍē̃ṭan-lāṭh, p. 258b, l. 30); the twisting, griping pain of indigestion or the like (cf. lōṭh). --lagȧnⁱ 1 -- m. pl. inf. twistings to come on, to suffer griping pains.

f. (sg. dat. laṭi), epilepsy, falling sickness (El., Śiv. 1564). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an attack of epilepsy to come on. ¶ laṭa-krüṭᵘ̈ f. faintness or insensibility resulting from fever; cf. kroṭᵘ. -krüṭᵘ̈ pyonᵘ m.inf. to lie prostrate, owing to such faintness.

m. (sg. dat. lāṭas), annoyance or worry caused by some contretemps (possibly the same word as lāṭh 1; cf. lōṭh), in the following:-- --lagȧnⁱ 2 -- m. pl. inf. in doing anything for another, delays to be caused by unwillingness. Cf. lôṭᵘ. ¶ lāṭa āmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), annoyed by a contretemps (cf. --yunᵘ, bel.). --anun -- m.inf. to distress a person by impeding him. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to become agitated owing to the distress occasioned by some contretemps which upsets arrangements or makes some contemplated action impossible.

f. (sg. dat. laṭi), a time, turn, occasion (El. laṭ, m., or laṭi, f.) (Śiv. 1564; K. 159, 201, 576; H. viii, 7); one time only (aki laṭi, once; trĕn laṭan, thrice; cf. aki-laṭi-aki, etc., p. 20a, l. 39); aki laṭi... biyi laṭi, at one time... at another time (K.Pr. 8). ¶ laṭi laṭi adv. time and again, time and time, over and over again. laṭi laṭh f. necessarily visiting a person on one occasion only. Cf. laṭh 1.
m. (sg. dat. lāṭas), a lot (at an auction) (the English word) (Gr.M.).
in laṭh-paṭh m. (sg. dat. laṭas-paṭas), an outer cap worn over a head-dress in cold weather.
f. (sg. dat. (?) lāṭi), the flame of fire, a blaze (Rām. 1080).
m. a kind of fine smooth cotton cloth. -düjᵘ̈ f. a piece of such cloth, a kerchief.
m. the plaited hair of a woman (in three united plaits hanging down the back).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. laṭiladiñ), subject to epilepsy, epileptic. Cf. laṭh 2.
f. a graceful girl (voc. latiyĕ, K.Pr. 124, 243, 1606). Cf. lᵃth 1 and latūr.
m. form of laṭᵃr, in phāha-laṭur, q.v., s.v. phāh.
f. a slender girl (? El. latúrih, the young of any animal). Cf. lᵃth 1 and latiy.

laṭᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or laṭürᵘ̈ f. a small tail (dim. of loṭᵘ) (Gr.Gr. 37); hence, a piece of wood split longways (cf. laṭawaṭ, gurⁱ-lⁱ, p. 298b, l. 45, and phāha-lᵒ, s.v. phāh); a plait of hair, a pigtail (Śiv. 124); kūṭⁱ-laṭⁱr, a piece of wood cut off the end of a beam (p. 485b, l. 19) (Gr.Gr. 37). laṭᵃri-tālav m. a roof constructed of long beams joined together.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. lȧṭⁱladiñ), marred by faults, faulty, censurable; producing faults, damaging (by association or contact). Cf. loṭᵘ 2.

m. Lava, N. of a son of Rāmacandra, born to Sītā in Vālmīki's hermitage (Rām. 1282, 1290, 1328, 1357, 1360, 1368, 1370, 1376, 1389, 1396, 1408, 1416, 1438, 1503, 1512, 1534-5, 1764). He ruled over the town of Lahore, which was named after him (Rām. 1738). Cf. lôhūr.

m. (sg. abl. lāwa 1), desire, longing for anything. --dāv kaḍun --m.inf. to achieve one's longing. --dāv nērun -- m.inf. a longing to be achieved. ¶ lāwa barun m.inf. to feel a longing. -büṭhᵘ̈ f. a hearth for longing, a place where longings are satisfied (e.g. a father-in-law's house). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to fulfil one's longing. -pyāv m. the birth of the first child of a young bride (in her husband's father's house, naturally the subject of longing). -pyāwal f. a bride who has just brought forth her first child. -pyāway f. the festival of rejoicing on the first child of a bride.

m. grass dried and twisted into rough cables, and so preserved as fodder for winter consumption; cf. gaḍᵃ̇rᵃ̇-lav, p. 278a, l. 41. -brôrᵘ m. a mass of these grass-cables, stored by hanging round a tree-trunk, the equivalent for our hayrick. -gāsa m. the grass collected in the forest for making these cables, hay.
f. reaping. Cf. dāñĕ-lāv, p. 230a, l. 39; hay (L. 70, 460 (lao and láa)).

or lawa 1 f. sprinkling, scattering liquid in a few sparse drops (cf. ö̃ta- lawa, p. 53a, l. 43, and kalashĕ-lawa, p. 441a, l. 46); esp. the sprinkling from light rain or dew (El. lawa and lauwa); dew (Gr.Gr. 137, L. 459). ¶ lawa diñᵘ̈ f.inf. to sprinkle with water; (as a religious ceremony) to asperge. -hotᵘ adj.(f. -hüʦᵘ̈), covered with light drops (of rain or dew), dewy (Gr.Gr. 137, Śiv. 112); hence (of vegetables, etc.), very fresh, with the dew on it. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to consecrate, devote an offering, etc., by aspersion.
in lawa-düjᵘ̈ f. a piece of tough meat.
m. the condition of being quite new and fresh, absolute freshness; freshness, bloom, youthfulness. Cf. lôwᵘ 2.
or lavʦörⁱ adj. c.g. exactly fitting, exactly harmonizing (of a wall, pillar, or the like, in reference to the main building). Cf. lowᵘ.

f. possession by a spirit, devil, or the like. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. insensibility, unconsciousness, delirium, or the like to occur from possession by a spirit. --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to lift possession off, i.e. to restore a person possessed by a devil to his senses, to exorcise. --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. possession to rise off, i.e. to be exorcised.

(for 1, see lāv 1) m. rust, verdigris, canker (K.Pr. 153). -borutᵘ adj. (f. -barᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), gone bad throughout, spoiled inside and out, turned green by exposure (of clothing, food, etc.). -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), rusty, attacked by verdigris, cankered; (of food, etc.) gone bad. --khasun -- m.inf. rust or verdigris to rise, i.e. show itself; (of food, etc.) corruption to occur.
in lāwa-lö m. the name used in schools for the Śāradā equivalent of the letter la .
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. lāwaladiñ), rusty, coated with rust, verdigris, or the like.
adj. c.g. free, independent; ignorant, foolish; slothful, sluggish; poor, scarce of provisions; a libertine (m. or f.), rake, frequenter of taverns and stews, a gallant.
? gend., a rope (only noted in L.V. 107).
m. a kind of cake, made of wheat-flour, in shape something like a pancake.
f. (sg. dat. lawaṭi), the fork-tailed shrike.
m. the leader of a group of low-caste or mean people.
m. a plump young male child.

m. (sg. dat. lāwasas), a kind of offering of food made to the Mātṛkās and other deities on the fourteenth night of the bright half of the month of Māg (Skt. Māgha) (January-February); the festival on which these offerings are made. ¶ lāwạsa-brôrᵘ m. the name of an image of one of the forms of Śiva, set up for worship at this festival. lāwasa-ʦŏdāh or lāwạsi-ʦŏdāh f. (sg. dat. -ʦŏdöshᵘ̈), the fourteenth of the light half of Māg, on which this festival is held.
f. (sg. dat. lawacĕ), a plump fat young female child.

m. fusing, melting; complete mental absorption (in the Deity), consciousness of pure existence and nothing else (Śiv. 1601, 1728, 1863); disappearance, dissolution, absorption, extinction, destruction; cf. lay 2. -- gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become completely absorbed in or swallowed up in, to be intimately united with. --karun -- m.inf. to make absorption (in anything), to become absorbed (in, dat.) (L.V. 76, Rām. 31). ¶ layĕ anun m.inf. to bring (anything) to absorption, to bring (anything) under one's own power by concentration of mind (L.V. 82). --wŏthun -- m.inf. to rise to destruction, to become dissolved into nothingness (L.V. 1).

(sometimes written lāī) f. grain parched, so as to become inflated or puffed out, pop- corn (cf. dã̄-lāy, p. 230a, l. 43) (K.Pr. 40, Rām. 1615). --nērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (grain while being parched) to arrive at the condition of popcorn. --phaṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. lāy to burst, (of grain) to become inflated or burst as popcorn. ¶ lāyĕ-bôyᵘ m. the lāy- brother, (at a marriage ceremony) the brother or other male relation of the bride, whose office it is to make a burnt offering (hōma) of lāy. -gorᵘ m. (his wife is -gȧrⁱ-bāy, and a female seller is -gürᵘ̈), a popcorn-seller, one who lives by making and selling popcorn (Gr.Gr. 149). -jān m. (his wife is -jöñᵘ̈), a popcorn-seller (he carries it on his head in a basket, and cries it in the markets). -jönil f. the profession of a popcorn-seller, as ab. -khir m. popcorn cooked with milk. -loḍᵘ m. a kind of sweetmeat made up of popcorn, sugar, etc. -laḍur m. stout and active, vigorous, sturdy, robust (usually of a child); cf. laḍur. -mọ̆nḍᵘ m. a ball-shaped cake made up of powdered popcorn and other ingredients. -mŏṭh f. (sg. dat. -mŏṭhi), as much popcorn as can be held in one hand, a handful of popcorn. -pholᵘ m. a single grain of popcorn; a small quantity of popcorn. -sotᵘ m. ground popcorn. -sütᵘ̈ m. a mass of ground popcorn.

f. extreme affection, exclusive devotion (to any one) (K.Pr. 201; Rām. 1712, 1757; Śiv. 382, 658, 1565); cf. lay 1, in the sense of which it is sometimes used. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. ardent affection to arise (Rām. 423). hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to become ardently affectionate, esp. (of one absent from home or friends) to feel ardent love for those who are absent, to become homesick. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be devoted to (a person, an art, study, etc.) (L.V. 60, 68; Rām. 1762). --rōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. love to continue or grow continually (even though the lover be separated from the object). ¶ layĕ rōzun m.inf. to continue full of loving affection.
f. reproach, reproof; cf. dēkh-lāy, p. 206a, l. 15. lāyĕ-lāy f. a mutual fight between two parties.

(also written löikh) and löyikh adj. c.g. fit, proper, meet (Rām. 430); adapted, suitable; worthy, deserving, due (K.Pr. 40, khĕnas lāyĕkh, worth eating; Śiv. 667, 669; H. x, 4; xii, 10, 19); able, capable, competent. Construed with the dat., or (in the case of a verb) optionally with the fut. p.p. Thus, lānatānas lāyĕkh, deserving of reproof; shēranas lᵒ, in need of repairs; kᵃnunᵃ lᵒ, fit to be sold, saleable (Gr.M.; so H. xii, 10, 19); lēkhüñᵘ̈ lāyĕkh, some feminine thing worthy of being written.
n.ag. (f. layĕvüñᵘ̈), worth a good price. Cf. layun 2.
n.ag. (f. lāyĕvüñᵘ̈), one who beats; (of a sunbeam or the like) dazzling; (of a child or the like) worrying, troublesome.
the Musalmān creed, a corruption of the Arabic lā ilāha illa-'llāhu, there is no god but the God (H. vi, 17).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. lôyᵘ), to strike, beat, hit (a person or animal) (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 127, 187; YZ. 96, 97, 362, 436; Rām. 758; Śiv. 1364, 1606); to strike (sc. a horse), to drive (Gr.M.); to make or do with vehemence, eagerness, or smartness (Rām. 212, 250; H. iii, 1, 2, 9; ix, 8; x, 1) [cf. thaph lāyüñᵘ̈, to strike seizing, to seize hold (of) (Rām. 919; H. v, 9); wŏṭh lāyüñᵘ̈, to strike jumping, to jump, to leap (K. 233, 237, 446, 632)]; to raise or set up (a cry, rumour, or the like) (cf. bākh lāyüñᵘ̈, p. 99a, l. 44; bōlas lāyĕna yunᵘ, p. 105a, l. 33; caṭh lāyun, p. 177b, l. 17, nād lᵒ, nĕdān lᵒ) (Rām. 248, 390, 491, 650, 1360, 1720; Śiv. 781, 1323, 1336, 1370, 1440, 1746; K. 291, 443); to apply, fix, insert, drive in (YZ. 103, 113; Śiv. 1530; cf. būkh lᵒ, to lower a bucket into a well, p. 100a, l. 2); (of the rays of the sun, etc.) to dazzle (the eyes); to throw to a distance (K.Pr. 263; K. 890; H. i, 6, 7, 8; v, 3, 4, 5); to discharge (a gun, or the like) (H. ii, 11; viii, 10) [gūlⁱ lāyüñᵘ̈, to fire a bullet, to hit with a bullet, to shoot (something or someone) (W. 145)]. ¶ (With cognate acc.) lūrᵘ̈ lāyüñᵘ̈, to strike a cudgel, to cudgel (with dat. of person) (Gr.M.); makh lāyun, to strike, or slay, with an axe (dat. of person) (K.Pr. 144); nēza lᵒ, to strike (with) a spear; capāth lāyüñᵘ̈, to give a slap (K.Pr. 156; cf. p. 174a, l. 23) (YZ. 362; Rām. 248, 376, 411, 502, 529, 872, 920, 982, 1353, 1368, 1399, 1418, 1453; Śiv. 1364, 1606; K. 600, 1145; H. iii, 5, 6); mushᵉ̆th lāyüñᵘ̈, to strike a blow with the fist; nĕkⁱ lāyȧnⁱ, s.v. nyokᵘ. ¶ to offer (a complaint or the like) (Rām. 183, 242, 465, 1536). ¶ lāyun khyonᵘ m.inf. to eat a beating, to suffer a beating, to be beaten. ¶ lāyun pyonᵘ m.inf. a beating to fall, a drubbing to be experienced (dat. of patient).
conj. 2 (1 p.p. loyᵘ), to become absorbed; esp. (amongst Hindūs) to become absorbed (in the Supreme), to reach final beatitude (L.V. 59); to become dissolved into nothingness (L.V. 59).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. loyᵘ), to be worth (so much in the market) (Gr.Gr. 204; L. 459; K.Pr. 18, 158, 240; YZ. 54); to be worth buying, to be valuable (Śiv. 1450, 1566). layanhār adj. c.g. that which is worth (so much); hence, worth a good deal; that which fetches a good price.

f. shame (K.Pr. 196; K. 552-3, 575, 813, 1062); bashfulness, modesty. -lānath f. (sg. dat. -lānüʦᵘ̈), 'shame and curse,' a daughter (as the cause, from her birth, of shame and expense, as compared with a son). ¶ lazi-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), shameless (El. gives lazarust as meaning 'tasteless'. This is probably a misprint for lazata- rostᵘ; see lazath).

m. (sg. dat. lazatas), pleasure, delight, enjoyment; sweetness, deliciousness; taste, flavour, relish, savour. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to enjoy a flavour or delight (of food, study, converse, etc.). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. a flavour, etc., to be enjoyed.
adj. c.g. (as. subst., f. lazathdārĕñ), sweet, delicious, luscious; pleasant, delightful; savoury, tasty.

conj. 2 (2 p.p. lazyōv or lazōv (Gr.Gr. 216)), to be fit, suitable (K.Pr. 125); to fit to or into. --pazun -- m.inf. (of the brothers, etc., of the bride) to give her the customary presents. Cf. bazun-lazun, p. 153b, l. 27. ¶ lazyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. lazyē-müʦᵘ̈), suitable, fitted.
f., i.q. laz, q.v. modesty, bashfulness (Śiv. 883, 885, 898, 1057).
m. the condition or conduct of a eunuch. Cf. lã̄ʦh.
f. (sg. dat. laʦi), rubbish, dust (El., Gr.M.). --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to raise dust (El.). --wālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring down dust, i.e. to sweep out the walls of a room, etc.

or lö̃ʦh m. (sg. dat. lã̄ʦhas), a eunuch, an impotent man, a hermaphrodite. According to El. s.v. lānts, the eunuchs live chiefly in Tāshĕwān, in Śrīnagar. They dance and sing at marriages, and are hired to make loud lamentations at burials of the rich (Gr.Gr. 11, 142; K.Pr. 101, 123, 135); (as adj.) unmanly, cowardly (El.). ¶ lö̃ʦha-hamal m. pregnancy (of a woman) caused by intercourse with a eunuch; hence, an impossibility (cf. K.Pr. 123). -hamala m. a eunuch's attack, i.e. an attack made by a weak person upon a powerful one. -koṭᵘ m. a child-eunuch, a eunuch in childhood. -kuṭun or -kūṭun m. one who acts like a eunuch, one who acts in a cowardly or feeble manner. -trö̃ʦh or lö̃ʦhi-trö̃ʦhi adj. c.g. unevenly joined, having parts joined that do not fit together; (of a garment or the like when worn) badly fitting.

f. a sweeping brush; cf. laʦhulᵘ. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to use a sweeping brush, to sweep away; to destroy utterly. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be swept away; entire loss or destruction (of people or property) to occur. ¶ laʦhajĕ-gāsa m. a kind of grass used for making sweeping-brushes. -tᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a piece of this kind of grass, a 'hair' of a sweeping-brush.
m. a broom (for sweeping), a besom (K.Pr. 124, Śiv. 1503). Cf. laʦhüjᵘ̈.
adj. c.g. ignorant, fat and boorish. Cf. labār.
m. easiness (in all senses, e.g. of a road, of a mountain pass, a task, a problem, and so on). Cf. lyoṭhᵘ.

f. (sg. dat. and pl. nom. lë̆zᵘ̈), dung of horses, mules, asses, or elephants (Gr.Gr. 25; K.Pr. 73 (pl.); L. 459 (lid)). ¶ lë̆zᵘ̈-nār m. a fire with such dung for fuel. -pholᵘ m. the amount of such dung voided at one excretion.
m. destitute of strength, defeated (in combat, etc.), admitting defeat by retreating (El. lyad); cowardly (El.). Cf. lĕḍun.

or lẹ̆durᵘ adj. (f. lë̆dᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 1 or lẹ̆dürᵘ̈), yellow (El.); wan, pale (El., Gr.M.). --bam-ʦū̃ṭhᵘhyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. lë̆dᵘ̈rᵘ̈ bam-ʦū̃ṭhᵘ hishᵘ̈), yellow like a quince, quince-yellow, slightly greenish-yellow. --gagôrᵘ hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. lë̆dᵘ̈rᵘ̈ gagôrᵘ hishᵘ̈), jasmine-yellow, pale-yellow. --kŏng hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. lë̆dᵘ̈rᵘ̈ kŏng hishᵘ̈), saffron-yellow, slightly reddish-yellow, orange-yellow.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. lĕḍyōv), to be overpowered, to be conquered, defeated; cf. lĕḍ. lĕḍyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. lĕḍyē-müʦᵘ̈), defeated, having given up a struggle or fight owing to defeat.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. lẹ̆dᵃrôwᵃ), to make yellow, to cause to become yellow, to dye or paint (anything) yellow. lẹ̆dᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. lẹ̆dᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), made yellow, coloured yellow (by some external means), caused to become yellow.
or lẹ̆dᵃrēr m. yellowness (natural or adventitious).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. lẹ̆dᵃryōv), to become yellow, to turn yellow (Gr.Gr. 7). lẹ̆dᵃryō-motᵃ 2 perf. part. (f. lẹ̆dᵃryē-müʦᵃ), become yellow, yellowed.

or lidᵘ̈rᵘ̈1 f. turmeric (El. lidir, lidar). ¶ lẹ̆dᵃrĕ-ganḍᵃrᵃ f. a turmeric-root, turmeric before it is ground to powder. -wal-pōsh m. the N. of a pretty yellow flower blossoming in the very early spring even when the snow is still on the ground; perhaps a variety of Aconitum Napellus.

or lidᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 2 f. N. of a river of Kashmīr, the 'Liddur' of tourists. It rises in the north-east of the Valley among the mountains and glaciers of that region; and after a south-westerly course, joins the Vĕth or Jehlam between Islāmābād and Vijᵃbrôrᵃ (El. Lidur).
f. discharge which collects in the corners of the eyes, rheum of the eyes. ¶ lĕgi-ȧchⁱ f. an eye filled with rheum. -lọ̆ʦhᵘ m. a clot of eye-rheum or eye-mucus.
(? spelling) m. Cotoneaster obtusa and rotundifolia (El.). The twigs are used in basket-making, and for twig bridges. Probably a mis-spelling of liñᵘ̈ 1, q.v.

f. a small earthen cooking-pot, a saucepan (El. also lejí and lij; L.V. 95; K.Pr. 4, 64, 80, 87, 119, 125, 132, 136, 246; H. xi, 10); cf. lyolᵘ; nāra-lᵒ, s.v. nār; nāṭa-lᵒ, s.v. nāṭh. --ṭĕkᵘ̈rᵘ̈ -- f. pot and pottle, big pot and small pot, pots and pans, all the cooking-pots, etc., in a kitchen, batterie de cuisine. ¶ lĕjĕ-chalin-wôñᵘ m. pot-washings water, the slops poured out of a cooking-pot after washing its interior. --chalañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to wash pots, to serve as a cook, or as a scullion. -chalyunᵘ (sg. dat. -chalinis), pot-washings, pot-slops. -kabāba m. mutton cooked in a pot with grease. --mŏlawañĕ -- f. pl. to settle the price of pots; met. to linger or show a little delay in any work which one is really anxious to accomplish (e.g. when, being urged to hasten, one does not wish to exhibit anxiety to finish), to haggle over one's work. -phuṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -phucĕ), an old or worn-out cooking-pot, esp. a small one. -ṭuṭakh m. (sg. dat. -ṭuṭakas), one who is always looking towards the cooking-pot, a greedy fellow.
or (Gr.Gr. 138) lĕkalūṭh adj. c.g. one who habitually interlards his conversation with indecent language, foul-mouthed, ribald; (of a story, conversation, etc.) indecent, pornographic, ribald, bawdy.

f. (sg. dat. lĕki), indecent abuse, indecent suggestive and insulting talk (El. also lyĕk) (Gr.Gr. 138; K.Pr. 114, 119, 125, 132) (cf. mājĕ-lᵒ, s.v. möjᵘ̈); indecent or immoral proposals made to a woman (H. viii, 3, 11). --diñᵘ̈ --, --kāḍüñᵘ̈ --, or --ʦārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to abuse (El.). -thŏkh f. (sg. dat. lĕki-thŏki), indecent abuse and spitting (e.g. directed at some infamous person). ¶ lĕka-har f. (sg. dat. -hürᵘ̈), an abuse-quarrel, a quarrel consisting in the exchange of indecent abuse by persons at a distance from each other, a Billingsgate altercation; a quarrel caused by indecent abuse. --kaḍañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to produce indecent abuse, to abuse a person with foul language. -lĕkh f. mutual foul abuse (L.V. 23). -lūṭh adj. c.g. one who uses foul abuse on the slightest provocation, a foul-mouthed blackguard. -mŏl m. payment in foul abuse, the repayment of a kindly action or hospitality, etc., by such abuse. --pĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. foul abuses to fall, i.e. to be experienced. -purᵘ adj. (f. -purᵘ̈), full of indecency (e.g. an abusive reply, or a scabrous story, or a business which earns abuse). -pūrᵘ adj. (f.-pūrᵘ̈), id. -shĕlakh m. (sg. dat. -shĕlakas), a scourge of foul abuse, foul abuse uttered to one who is unable to reply (e.g. a servant or dependent). --ʦārañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to collect foul abuses; i.e. to speak in terms of indecent abuse of someone (not necessarily present). -wātul adj. (f. -wātᵘ̈jᵘ̈), a foul-mouthed cad; one who, without respect of persons, habitually utters indecent abuse. -zĕwal adj. c.g. foul-tongued, foul-mouthed. ¶ lĕki ṭūsᵘ m. a blow for abuse, hitting in the face one who abuses you.
or līkhā f. a writing, that which is written. Cf. karma-lēkhā, p. 471b, l. 27 (Rām. 40, 120; Śiv. 1143, 1152, 1477, 1492, 1511).
conj. 1 (lēkhanôwᵘ), to get written, cause to be written (Gr.M., K. 955).
impers. fut. part., c.g. that which is to be written, worthy of being recorded.
n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a writer, one who writes; esp. a professional writer, a scrivener. Cf. lēkhun.

or likhun (q.v.) conj. 1 (1 p.p. lyūkhᵘ, f.līchᵘ̈; 2 p.p. lēchyōv), to write (El.; L.V. 107; Rām. 130, 132, 255, 302, 721, 841, 843, 1036, 1159, 1729, 1765; Śiv. 661, 1422, 1511; K. 129, 135, 643, 848, 955; H. viii, 10; ix, 12; x, 13; xii, 11, 15, etc.); to draw (a picture) (Rām. 1149; Śiv. 1152, 1492); inf. as verbal n. lēkhun, writing, handwriting, the art of writing (Gr.M.). ¶ lēkhan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who writes, a writer, copiest, scribe (El.); an author, the writer of a book; a newswriter. Cf. lĕkhan-wôlᵘ. ¶ lēkhana yunᵘ  m.inf. pass. to be written, inscribed, noted down (Gr.M.); to be able to be written, to be writable (Gr.M.); met. to be inscribed in the heart, to be burnt into the memory. ¶ lēkhunᵘ lāyĕkh adj. (f. lēkhüñᵘ̈ lāyĕkh), worthy of being written, worthy of being recorded in writing. ¶ līkhith dyunᵘ m.inf. to write down (a document, etc.) (YZ. 122). ¶ lyūkhᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. līchᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), written, put into writing (Rām. 302, 843, 1263; Śiv. 661); (as subst.) a thing written, handwriting (Gr.M.).
f. weeping aloud, lamentation (YZ. 570, lĕl; Rām. 429); cf. lila. -wöñᵘ̈ f. a word of lamentation, lamentations uttered on some woeful occasion, or afterwards on calling it to mind.

f. the mud at the bottom of standing or running water, sediment, dregs (El. lamb and lum) (Śiv. 1132, 1536, 1571, 1839); land in which springs occur (L. 321, limb); cf. lyombᵘ. --khë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to eat mud; met. to beg and implore an unwilling person. ¶ lĕmbi pampōsh phaṭun m.inf. a lotus to sprout from mud; met. an excellent son to be born of an unworthy father, good to spring from evil, or the like.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. lĕmbanladiñ), muddied, covered or defiled with mud (cf. lĕmb and lyombᵘ).
in lēn-dēn m. taking and giving; buying and selling; borrowing and lending; traffic, trade, business-dealing.
or ling m. the male organ of generation; (in grammar) gender; the genital organ of Śiva worshipped in the form of a phallus. A Hindū word.

f. (sg. dat. lēphi), a large wadded quilt used to cover several members of a family at night in the winter. ¶ lēphi-tolᵘ m. the outer covering of such a quilt. -wūrᵘ̈ f. an extra outer covering, or wrapper, of such a quilt, used to keep it clean.
m. a poultice, a plaster (El. lefa).
or lē̃phun m. (sg. dat. lē(lē̃)phanas ), grease, greasiness (adhering after contact with a greasy substance).
adv. share by share, portion by portion; justly, properly, fairly (e.g. in distributing).

in lĕṭha-lôrᵘ m. the beating or drubbing a man in every limb. -lôrᵘ gaʦhun m.inf. such a drubbing to occur; the pains and aches, as if every limb were broken, caused by extreme fatigue to be felt (cf. loṭhᵘ gaʦhun, s.v. loṭhᵘ). lĕṭha-pan m. a carpenter's rule.

f. licking, in the following:--lĕv-brôrᵘ m. (f. -brörᵘ̈), a 'lick-cat', one whose mouth is always watering for something, a perpetual hankerer. --karüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to lick, to lick up (K.Pr. 10 (written lyav)).

f. the act of licking, tasting with the tongue (Gr.Gr. 120); to be licked up, the small remainder of food, which must be licked up to finish it; cf. lĕvyunᵘ. --diñᵘ̈ f.inf. to lick (a dish, etc.) clean; to be always faithful and obedient (of a wife, son, servant, or the like).
m. (sg. dat. lĕvinis), a thing to be licked up, the small remainder of food, which must be licked up to finish it. Cf. lĕviñ.
in lēwā-dēvī f. a state of taking and giving, of paying and repaying, business relationship.
(? spelling) the gargoyle of a shrine (L. 460). ? Cf. lawüṭᵘ̈.
f. (sg. dat. lĕwüñᵘ̈), licking, a lick (Gr.Gr. 121). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to lick, to lick up, finish food by licking up the remains; to taste, to test by tasting.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lĕwanôwᵘ), to cause to lick, to cause to taste; to give one a smack or a taste of anything.
f. the act of washing (K.Pr. 55, where it is spelt lĕwai).
n.ag. (f. lĕʦavüñᵘ̈), that which is becoming weak, flaccid, feeble, etc.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. lĕʦyōv, Gr.Gr. 226), to be, or become, weak, flaccid. lĕʦyō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. lĕʦyē-müʦᵘ̈), weakened, become flaccid.
f. (sg. dat. lë̆ʦᵃrüñᵃ), causing to be weak or flaccid.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lë̆ʦᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. lë̆ʦᵃrun, q.v. lë̆ʦᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. lë̆ʦᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. lë̆ʦᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, see lë̆ʦᵃrun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lë̆ʦᵒrᵒ), to cause to be weak, flaccid, feeble, or the like. lë̆ʦᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. lë̆ʦᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), rendered weak, etc., as ab.
m. raiment, garb, vesture, robe, apparel; outward appearance, dress (Śiv. 833).
f. (sg. dat. lichi), i.q. lᵃch, q.v.
m. regard, consideration, respect, respectful attention (Gr.M.).

m. accounts, calculation of income and expenditure or of debt and credit, etc.; cf. dȧtⁱ-likha, p. 257a, l. 38. --bōzun -- m.inf. to understand the calculation, i.e. to clear up accounts, to strike a balance and discharge the obligation (K. 945, 952). --karun -- m.inf. to clear up accounts, to determine the balance. -pürᵘ̈ f. skill in accountancy. -tryukhᵘ m. skill in dealing with accounts.
f. the profession of a writer or of a copiest of manuscripts.
m. a professional writer, a scribe, a clerk, a copiest (of manuscripts) (Gr.M.).
f. the profession of a scribe, quill-driving.
f. the occupation or profession of a writer.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. lyukhᵘ3; for 1 and 2, see s.vv.; 2 p.p. lichyōv), i.q. lēkhun, q.v. The word is always thus spelt in the village dialect of H. ¶ likhana yunᵘ m.inf. pass. (of some liquid substance) to be absorbed in (something else, e.g. into a sponge). ¶ likhith gaʦhun m.inf. to become written, to be reduced to writing; yih gav likhith, that which has been written, i.e. one's fate (K.Pr. 251).

f.pl. lamentations, loud mourning, sorrowful ejaculations; cf. lĕla and līlā. -wöñᵘ̈ f. lamentation, mourning (esp. on the loss or departure of someone beloved). -zār m. a prayer or request accompanied by lamentation (to soften the heart of the hearer). -zörⁱ f. addressing or praying to or appeasing God, a master, or someone in authority, with words mixed with lamentations.

f. play, sport, pastime; beauty, charm, grace; the uncontrolled, wilful, or unexpected action of a god, of a great person, or of any ordinary man; (in Kāshmīrī) a story, a tale, novel, fairy-tale, fable; a woeful petition, a heart- rending appeal (Rām. 304, 1216, 1478, 1584); prayer or praise offered by one in distress (Rām. 75, 852, 1046, 1291; Śiv. 40, 93, 129, 131, 163, 229, 308, etc.); a respectful petition, a representation made to a superior (Rām. 708, K. 387). Cf. lĕla, lila, and līlȧmⁱ.
or nilām m. (Hindī nīlām, Portuguese leilám), an auction, public sale (Gr.M.).
f. pl. actings, taking parts in a theatrical performance. (The word occurs only in L.V. 81, and is doubtful. Probably it really represents two words, līla (pl. nom. of līl, for līlā, q.v.) and mĕ.)
in lili karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. lovingly to encourage or incite a child in its play.

adj. c.g. completely absorbed in, swallowed up in, intimately connected with. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become intimately united with, absorbed in, swallowed up. --rōzun -- m.inf. to be engrossed in, absorbed in.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. liñĕladiñ), slippery, slimy.
m. absorption (of one thing into another), intimate union; softness, gentleness, mildness.

f. an arch over a doorway (mĕḥrāb). -dār 1 (for 2, see s.v.) m. a piece of wood suitable to form such an arch. -dörᵘ̈ f. a side door or window with such an arch. -püṭᵘ̈ f. the panel (usually of fretwork or lattice-work) within such an arch. -thürᵘ̈ f. the vine-creeper of such an arch, i.e. the fretwork or lattice-work below it. -tākh (cf. tāq طاق) a side door or window with such an arch. -ʦôkᵘ m. the framework supporting such an arch.
(for 1, see s.v. linga), adj. c.g. (of doorway) possessing an arch, arched (see linga).
adj. c.g. having the form of a phallus, a title of Śiva (see lĕng) (Śiv. 1577).
n.ag. (f. lingavüñᵘ̈), (of a pillar, post, or the like) awry and loose in its foundation.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. lingyōv), (of a post, pillar, beam, or the like) to become loose and out of place, to become awry or distorted and loose. lingyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. lingyē-müʦᵘ̈), distorted, as ab.
adj. (f. liñivᵘ̈), made of liñᵘ̈-wood. See liñᵘ̈ 1.

(f.) orlyuñᵘ (m.) a certain tree growing in the hill forests, Cotoneaster bacillaris, used for making walking-sticks and alpen-stocks (L. 79, 82, lun); a fibre plant, also used for fodder, Cotoneaster sp. (L. 68, 70); Cotoneaster obtusa and rotundifolia (El. lín; L. 70, luni), the twigs of which are used for basket-making, and for twig bridges. Cf. lehan. This word also appears under the masculine form lyuñᵘ.
f. slipperiness (of a road). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. slipperiness of a road to occur; hence, a fall to occur owing to such slipperiness.

m. (sg. dat. līpas), smearing, wipings, what is left sticking to a pot after emptying it; smearing, defilement (Śiv. 23, 518). -pāph m. (sg. dat. -pāpas), the sin that is a necessary accompaniment of any unworthy conduct, etc.
or liviñᵘ̈ f. a mere smear, ever so little (in describing the quantity of some greasy or sticky substance). Cf. liwun (Gr.Gr. 120).
f. defeat; a punishment inflicted by a powerful person upon a weaker. --khë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be defeated; to be punished, as ab.
f. a long narrow rag or strip of cloth (cf. pura-lᵒ, s.v. pura 1). līra-bāgay f. dividing out shares into long strips, esp. in dividing land amongst claimants in this manner. Cf. lar 3.

or līsa m. a kind of creeper, of which the small leaves are cooked as a vegetable (Amaranthus polygonoides). According to L. 75 it is used medicinally as an expectorant. -khürᵘ̈ f. a cooked dish of this vegetable.
adj. c.g. weak, feeble (from illness or the like). -lav adj. c.g. habitually slack or feeble in the performance of work.
m. feebleness, spiritlessness, due to laziness, weakness, sluggishness, or the like; cf. lam-lisar, p. 524a, l. 23. --trāwun -- m.inf. to show neglect by laziness or wilful delay.
m. the remainder, the small amount remaining in a receptacle after the bulk of its contents have been removed (cf. lᵃsh).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. lisyōv), to be pleased (Gr.Gr. lxvi).

dragging, in litha-khŏkhᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. 'drag-crawling', dragging oneself along the ground on one's back with the knees drawn up; cf. khŏkhücᵘ̈ and lithanāwun. -khŏkhurᵘ adj. (f. -khŏkhürᵘ̈ 1), one who, through infirmity of the legs, crawls in this way. -khŏkhürᵘ̈ 2 f. = -khŏkhᵘ̈jᵘ̈, ab.; cf. khạkhᵃr. -khūrᵘ̈ f. dragging one's feet along the ground, walking without lifting the feet from the ground.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. lithanôwᵘ), to drag a person along the ground; to render dirty and dusty; cf. litha and lithawun. lithanôwᵘ-motᵘ (f. lithanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), dragged along the ground; spoiled and dirtied with dust, etc.
f. (sg. dat. lithavüñᵘ̈), the dragging a person along the ground.
adv. with dragging along the ground.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lithowᵘ), to drag along the ground, i.q. lithanāwun, q.v. lithowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (lithüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), dragged along the ground.

f. (sg. dat. litrĕ or litᵃrĕ), a saw (for cutting) (Gr.M.; H. vii, 19). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to saw; to split, cut to pieces; met. cursing, imprecations against something alive (as if cutting it to pieces). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be sawn, cut to pieces; to suffer sawing; hence, to suffer, or to be destroyed, by contumelious reviling. --wālüñᵘ̈ -- m.inf. to bring down a saw (on anything); to set to work at sawing, to begin sawing. --wāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to apply a saw, wield a saw, to saw. ¶ litri-dan m. the handle of a saw. -dand m. the tooth of a saw; (meton.) a saw.
f. the amount of grain put at one time into a mortar for husking.
or lipiñᵘ̈, a smear (Gr.Gr. 120), see lipiñᵘ̈.
f. a kind of sweetmeat, a small cake of sugar covered with seeds, the Indian rēwaṛī. livᵃrĕ-gorᵃ m. a maker, or seller, of these sweetmeats.

for liwan 1 (see liwun) in the following:-- -ḍuv f. the thorough sweeping and fresh-plastering of a house on the occasion of some festival or religious occasion. -ḍuway f. the performance of this sweeping and fresh-plastering. -zang f. the plastering-omen, i.e. an offering of rice, etc., to a near female relation before beginning this sweeping and fresh-plastering on the occasion of a marriage or the like. This is done to secure good luck. Cf. liwan-zang, s.v. liwun.
f. (sg. dat. livüñᵘ̈), smearing, plastering, see liwun.

f. (sg. dat. livüñᵘ̈), a spade (El.; K.Pr. 124; L. 464, lewan; K. 1037). ¶ liwañĕ-dan  f. the handle or stem of a spade. -phāl m. the iron blade of a spade. -pôturᵘ m. the wooden shoulder of a Kāshmīrī spade, into which the iron blade is fitted, and on which the foot is pressed in order to push the blade into the ground.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. lyuwᵘ), to plaster, to smear, daub (Gr.Gr. 14, 120, 206; K.Pr. 251 (lĕwanas), 147 (liwun)); to plaster with clay and cow-dung (or with mortar) (Rām. 595). ¶ liwan 1 (for 2, see s.v.), in liwan-hurᵘ m. the piece of cloth used like a painter's swob for plastering a mixture of clay and cow-dung. -kọ̆nḍᵘ m. the vessel used as a vat for mixing clay, cow-dung, and water for plastering. -phash m. the plaster-stroke, the act of applying plaster on a smooth surface, such as the ground or a wall, plastering. -zang f. the same as liwa- zang, q.v., s.v. liwa.
f. (sg. dat. liyāküʦᵘ̈), propriety, fitness, suitableness; skill, ability, capability. -nāma لیاقت نامہ m. a letter of recommendation, a certificate (Gr.M.).

f. shame, remorse. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show repentance or remorse for some fault before one's superiors; publicly to ask pardon from one who has been wronged. --hë̆ñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to feel remorse, to show remorse in the hope that one will obtain forgiveness. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to act under a feeling of remorse.
interj. ho!, O! (with voc.) (K.Pr. 250, Rām. 1778). lō-lō, id. (Śiv. 330, 346, 408, 1037, 1053, 1365, 1468, 1669, in each case used as a meaningless refrain in a song).

m. (sg. dat. lŏbaras), dried cowdung, cowdung-cake for fuel (cf. boṭhᵘ 2) (K.Pr. 48, 63, 241, lubar; L. 460 lubr). ¶ lŏbar-lōh m. 'a cowdung-porcupine', a man who has a reputation for learning, but who, on being tested, turns out to be an ignorant fool. -lōlō m. insincere affection, apparent love which is outwardly displayed, but which does not really exist. -nār m. a fire of cowdung fuel; met. (of a sudden display of anger or the like) that which at first is very hot, but which is quickly consumed and cools down. -ṭās m. the flop of the fall of a piece of dried cowdung; met. u.w. ref. to some person or thing which is so utterly lost or destroyed that it has passed entirely out of memory.

(for 2, see labun) m. the edge, margin, border, of anything; the bank of a river (El. lúb); cf. lab. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take the edge; hence, to go outside anything (e.g. a business, employment, friendship, house and home), to betake oneself to a solitary life, to become a hermit. -kun adv. at the edge, on the margin, marginally; wati lobᵘ-kun, by the wayside (Gr.M.). --lobᵘ -- adv.
