(with verbs indicating position) along the edge, along the margin; cf. lȧbⁱ lȧbⁱ, bel. --lobᵘ hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take side after side; hence, gradually to abandon any duty or business and to betake oneself to solitude. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain at the edge, to remain outside any duty or business, to remain in solitude; (on a journey or the like) to keep off the highway (so as to avoid tolls, etc.); cf. labi rōzun, bel. --thawun -- m.inf. to put to the edge; to expel, throw out, turn out of office. Cf. labi thawun, bel. ¶ lȧbⁱ lȧbⁱ adv. (with verbs of motion) along the edge, sidling up near (a person), cautiously (approaching) (Rām. 319). Cf. lobᵘ lobᵘ, ab., and labi labi, bel. ¶ labi bĕhun m.inf. to sit to one side, to sit aside, to keep clear of anything (K.Pr. 150). -kani adv. (with verbs indicating position) towards the edge, by the edge, near the edge, to one side (Śiv. 842, 1445, 1568). -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, near the edge or near the side. --labi -- adv. (with verbs of motion) along the edge, along the outside, by the side; (with verbs of taking out, etc.) by, or over, the edge (of a vessel, etc.); cf. lȧbⁱ lȧbⁱ, ab. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain outside, to stay apart, stand aside; to stand apart from any business, even though connected with it, to abstain from doing one's share of work; cf. lobᵘ rōzun, ab. --thawun -- m.inf. to put to one side, to put aside; to put (a person) to one side, to act independently of the instructions (of a superior, a teacher, or the like). Cf. lobᵘ thawun, ab.
adj. c.g. having a wrong corner on one edge, uneven-edged. Cf. lū̃ṭᵘ̈.

m. smallness (as compared with bigness); smallness, a state of contraction, a condition smaller than before; youthfulness (as compared with the age of elders, elder brothers, or the like) (Rām. 325). Cf. lūkᵘ.

m. (sg.dat. löchis; abl. lāchi 2; for 1, see lāch), a kind of coarse woollen cloth or paṭṭū (El.); a kind of garment. The long nightgown-like garment worn by Kāshmīrīs has the general name of phĕran (q.v.). This, if made of wool, is called lôchᵘ, and if made of cotton is called pôʦhᵘ (q.v.) (K.Pr. 180). ¶ löchⁱ-āmun m. the acrid smell of burning woollen cloth, or of burning wool. -düjᵘ̈ f. a piece of this woollen cloth. -janda m. an old worn-out and much patched woollen garment. -palav m. a woollen garment too small or too thin for the wearer; a piece of woollen cloth. -züṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -zacĕ), a woollen rag, an old rag of a coat, a thoroughly worn-out woollen garment.

or (q.v.)löṭᵘ̈ f. a long-shaped ball or bead of gold or other precious metal. Cf. löṭᵘ̈. ¶ lācĕ-dupa m. a stick, or long-shaped pastille of incense (as burnt in Hindū worship); cf. dupa-löṭᵘ̈, p. 232a, l. 33. --khasañĕ -- f. pl. inf. long balls, i.e. clots, to rise; clots of grease or the like to rise from triturating some moist article.
m. a fool, dolt, one without understanding. -shōda m. one who continually acts foolishly (like a dranḳen man), a habitual dolt.

m. coral (supposed to grow on a marine tree) (El. ludir). lọ̆dᵃra-hoṭᵃ m. a neck adorned with a coral necklace; a coral necklace (usually of three or four strands, and much worn by cowherdesses and the like people). -hüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -hacĕ), the wood of the marine tree on which coral is supposed to grow; the red wood of the lōdh tree (see lôdᵘ 1). (In India, lōdhrā is the bark of this tree.) -māl f. a string or necklace of coral.

m. the usage of sending complimentary presents or instalments of dowry (e.g. to a friend, a great man, or to the home of a girl's husband); cf. lada-sörᵘ̈, s.v. lad 2. --podᵘ -- (sg. dat. ladis padis), the carrying out of this usage.

(for 2, see laḍun) m. a kind of sweetmeat made of sweetened meal formed into a ball. Cf. lāyĕ-loḍᵘ, s.v. lāy 1. ¶ lȧḍⁱ-hum m. (amongst Hindūs) a kind of oblation with fire offered to the god Gaṇeśa and his subordinates. It consists mainly of these sweetmeats. -sahākār m., id.

m.(sg. dat. lödis), N. of a certain tree, from the wood of which a dye is extracted. The lōdhra or lōdh of India (Symplocos Racemosa). Its red-coloured wood is called lọ̆dᵃra- hüṭᵘ̈, q.v., s.v. lọ̆dᵃr. lödⁱ-hüṭⁱ f. (sg. dat. -hacĕ), the wood of this tree.

m. (sg. dat. as in 1), a large heaped up pile, esp. of cowdung or the like, a dung- hill; a heap, a pile, a large quantity of anything (Rām. 677). lödⁱ-lŏbur m. (sg. dat. lŏbaras), lumps of cowdung, taken, after an interval for fermentation, from such a heap and dried. When this is burnt the oil which condenses from the vapour is used as a medicament. Cf. bȧṭhⁱ-tīl, p. 149b, l. 37.

f. in lŏgi-hondᵘ tŏgawôrᵘ m. imitation of a superior thing by the use of an inferior article (e.g. wearing coloured glass in place of a precious stone); imitating the actions of a superior or richer person, aping one's betters.
adj. c.g. a greedy person who is continually eating quantities of dainties, a person with a sweet tooth; a person who is a habitual calumniator, a backbiting gossiper.
f. private cooking of dainties for oneself.
f. (sg. dat. lŏgüʦᵘ̈), a dictionary, vocabulary, glossary (Gr.M.).

adj. (f. lüjᵘ̈ 1; for 2, see lagun, and for 3, see lojᵘ), 1 p.p. of lagun, q.v.; as adj. matching, forming one of a pair, a good fit; engrossed or absorbed (in any work), cf. mana-logᵘ, s.v. man 1. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. (of a remedy) to become suitable, to fit (the disease or the patient), to be a specific (for a disease). --gaʦhawunᵘ-- n.ag. (f. lüjᵘ̈ gaʦhawüñᵘ̈), that which (when applied) suits or fits exactly, found to suit, found to be a good fit. --lônᵘ -- m. the happening of fate, the occurrence of what is fated (whether wished for or not wished for). --yē dörⁱyĕ -- m. mutual reproaches (esp. amongst a number of women assembled together). ¶ lagi logᵘ adj. (f. --lüjᵘ̈ --), close up to, side by side of.

lohᵘ or lôhᵘ m. a porcupine (believed to follow a lion, and to indicate its passage by a low growl; cf. phĕ˜w); a fox (El. loh, luhf, luhv, or loshᵘ; L. 110, loh). lȧhⁱ-loṭⁱ or löhⁱ-loṭⁱ m. a porcupine's tail; a fox's tail; met. one who is unsteady, restless, uncertain in his goings or gait.
in lŏh-langar m. an iron anchor, an anchor (Gr.M.); met. the burden of one's daily and constant duties (which prevent freedom), daily drudgery (from which one cannot escape) (L.V. 67).
in lŏh-lŏh m. coaxing (a babe to laugh, a child to do its lessons, or the like).
or lōlürᵘ̈ f. ardent love, longing, eager desire. lŏhlari (H. vi, 3) or lōlari (K. 392, 1013), adv. with ardent love, with great affection, with eager longing.
m. the town of Lahore, in the Panjāb, said to have been founded by Lava, the son of Rāmacandra (Rām. 1263, 1738).

adj. (f. lüjᵘ̈ 3, for 1, see logᵘ, and for 2, see lagun), one who is reduced to poverty owing to not having the necessary money or means for undertaking any work; one who is indigent, destitute. Cf. laj.
m. a child, a boy (El. lok); a certain medicine made by cooking the juice of plants; cf. luk. -hanā f. a bit of a boy; met. a smart, bold boy.
m. a certain person, so-and-so (used where some well-known person is referred to, but not named).
in lŏka-torᵘ m. a pair of lattice-shutters in a door. -tȧrⁱ-poṭⁱ m. one-half of such a pair of lattices.
m. a certain kind of cotton cloth, usually dyed yellow, and suitable for use as a garment.

m. smallness (El. also lŏkaʦār and lŏkochār; W. 112, lo˙kutchār); childhood, boyhood, youth (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 125, 126, 245; YZ. 516; Rām. 1784, 1785; Śiv. 22, 44, 279, 956, 1582, 1615; K. 863, 1135). ¶ lŏkacyārukᵘ daga-daga m. the over-confidence, audacity, head- strongness of childhood. Cf. dag 1. ¶ lŏkacyāras ʦhŏhdinⁱ m. pl. inf. to give free rein to childhood, to enjoy the happy wanton days of childhood.

f. (sg. dat. lö̃karüñᵘ̈), decoration, ornament; esp. the dowry of ornaments, etc., given to a bride by the bridegroom's people (K.Pr. 131; Śiv. 1224, 1226-7, 1235; K. 912); wedding presents generally, given to a bride by either party.

in lŏkh lŏkh m. muttering continuously, continuous whispering, continuous low talking. --lŏkh karun -- m.inf. to do muttering, to keep talking, never to stop talking (K.Pr. 262); esp. (of one who is asleep) to appear to be awake (by conversing, opening the eyes and the like); (of one who is dead) to appear to be alive. --lŏkh karawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --karawüñᵘ̈ --), a mutterer, a prater; one who makes a habit of whispering scandal.
see lukh 2. This spelling is throughout employed in the village dialect of H.

f. (sg. dat. lö̃ki), the Kāshmīrī form of the Sanskrit Laṅkā (see lankā), the N. of the capital and residence of Rāvaṇa, identified by some with Ceylon or the chief town in it. For an account of its origin, see Rām. 590 ff. (Rām. 41, 62, 77, 608, 719, 755, 795, et passim).
f. (sg. dat. lŏki), the head (of a human being).
adj. (f. lŏkhürᵘ̈), congealed, solidified, concreted, thickened, coagulated (e.g. boiled rice, clarified butter, honey, liquid mud, etc.).
f. a solidified mass, a lump, a shaped mass (cf. bata-lŏkhᵃr, p. 137a, l. 18); a morsel, a mouthful, a portion of food (El. lŏkhar; K.Pr. 27).

adj. (f. sg. nom. lŏküṭᵘ̈, dat. lŏkacĕ), small (Gr.M., W. 112, Śiv. 326); smaller, shorter, younger (as compared with another person or thing) (K.Pr. 17, L. 461); junior (in a family) (Gr.M.; Rām. 529, 1145). ¶ As subst., m.  a son (f. a daughter); a young child, a baby (K.Pr. 87; Rām. 1471, 1522); a boy till his beard appears, a young person, a juvenile (El.; K.Pr. 36; Śiv. 334, 658); (f.) a little girl (Rām. 1025, 1614). --hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. lŏküṭᵘ̈hishᵘ̈), smallest, shortest, youngest, etc., of all (as compared with a number of other persons or things) (H. xii, 1). --mŏkoṭᵘ -- adj. (f. lŏküṭᵘ̈ mŏküṭᵘ̈), very small, etc. (as compared with others). --thāwun -- m.inf. to despise (El.).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. lōkyōv), to shrink in size, to become smaller (K.Pr. 173); to be small, to be little (El. lŏkun). lōkyō- -motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. lōkyē-müʦᵘ̈), shrunken, become smaller in size.

f. the inner part of a dress where it covers the bosom, the bosom of a dress (K.Pr. 76, sg. dat. lulih; Rām. 216, 1286; Śiv. 329, 1190, 1547). ¶ lŏla-mata lāy f. fondling and caressing, showing great affection by public fondling and petting, affectionately stroking all over (with reference either to a beloved child, or some beautiful and admired objec).

m. (sg. abl. lōla 1; gen. lōlukᵘ, and (Śiv. 276) irreg. lōlunᵘ), passionate love, devotion, affection (directed to a person, a thing, or an action) (L.V. 3, 25; K.Pr. 187; YZ. 49, 266, 451, 459, 514; Rām. 11, 33, 513, 539, 566, etc.; Śiv. 83, 166, 168, 189, 190, 193, 207, etc.; K. 107, 301, 523, 681, 857, 1114); compassion (El. lŏl). --barun -- m.inf. to show love, to display, or feel, affection (Rām. 617, 751, 815, 1639, 1645, 1663; K. 428, 1129). --barawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. -baravüñᵘ̈), one who shows love, a lover. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. affection to come; i.e. passionate love and longing to come over a person at the remembrance of some loved person now long parted from the rememberer (Rām. 1765). ¶ lōla, adv. very lovingly, affectionately (Rām. 1760; Śiv. 39, 51; K. 344, 514, 1148). -borutᵘ adj. (f. -barᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), full of love or affection; desirous (El. lolabrut); full of the power of causing love, adorable, lovable, captivating. -kār m. a love business, i.e. the carrying out of some festivity (e.g. the marriage of a much loved and only son) with great affection. -motᵘ adj. (f. -müʦᵘ̈), 'love-mad'; i.e. acting with intense affection; full of love in all one's acts. -pọ̆tᵘ m. a much beloved son, a son loved above all others (such as an only son, or the son of one's old age). -pūtᵘ m., id. --thāwun -- m.inf. to hold a person in love, to show constant love, to be constant in love (Rām. 1656).
f. the tongue (in the compound guhⁱ-lōla, m. dung-tongued, a fool in talk, p. 280b, l. 28).
m. (sg. dat. lōlakas), a kind of ear-pendant or ear-drop, small at the top, but wide and thick or globular below. -horᵘ m. a pair of these. -kan m. a single one of these. See kan 3.
m. N. of a Pargana and Valley to the north-west of the Wular Lake in Kashmīr; the ancient Laulāha (RT.Tr. II, 487). It is now commonly called by Europeans the Lolab Valley.
n.ag (f. lŏlavüñᵘ̈), one who pretends distaste or unwillingness for anything which he wishes. Cf. lŏlun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. lọ̆lᵘ; 2 p.p. lŏjyōv), to play with (e.g. a customer) (i.e. to refuse to sell a thing at first, in order to get a better price), to pretend unwillingness when really desiring something.
f., i.q. lŏhlürᵘ̈, q.v. lōlari adv. with ardent love, with great affection (K. 392, 1013).

m. want of success, failure. ¶ lȧlⁱ-wŏhav m. a certain gesture used in cursing or abusing a person (the two fore-arms being joined together and shaken, with the fingers spread out). -woturᵘ m., id.; cf. wotᵘ 1. -wütᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f., id.
f. reaping used --˚ as in atha-lōn, p. 59b, l. 29.

f. the taking from the seller, without payment, of a trifle extra (e.g. when the full amount has been weighed, taking a few handfuls more; cf. atha-lōnawañ, p. 59b, l. 31. Something like the 'dastūrī' of India) (K.Pr. 104).
for lō̃cĕ, see lū̃ṭᵘ̈. K.Pr. 126, spells this lonchih.

m. the eave-border of the edge of a thatch or roof, its purpose being to hold the hatch covering in its place. It is usually made of birch-bark and mud. --waṭun -- m.inf. to fold the roof-edge, i.e. to make such an eave-border. ¶ lȧnḍⁱ-ʦhürⁱ f. the basket of the eave-border, i.e. its support. ¶ lanḍi-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ), (of a house) wanting such an eave-border. ¶ lanḍis nār ganḍun m.inf. to set fire to the eaves of a roof (which results in putting the whole into conflagration); met. to cause a person to burst into furious rage; to burst into furious rage.
m. a kind of wooden cup with a handle, used in the kitchen for measuring rice, etc., a pipkin; cf. dājĕ-lŏngunᵘ, p. 202b, l. 32, and mimizⁱ-lⁱ, s.v. mimyuzᵘ.
f. a small lŏngun (q.v.), used, e.g., as a flower-vase; cf. dājĕ- lŏngüñᵘ̈, p. 202b, l. 34, and mimizⁱ-lⁱ, s.v. mimyuzᵘ.

adj. (f. lünjᵘ̈ or lünḍᵘ̈, q.v.), lame, halt, crippled (El., Gr.M., W. 20, K.Pr. 95 (f.)); cf. lünḍᵘ̈ 1. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become lame; (of a thing of a work) to be deprived of utility owing to suffering loss of a part. --karun -- m.inf. to walk lamely, to halt in one's gait. --lyoʦᵘ -- adj. (f. lünjᵘ̈ë˘ʦᵘ̈), lame and weak; (of a place, a crowd, a tract of country) full of lame and weak people, full of helpless people. ¶ lȧngⁱ-côṭⁱ adj. (f. -cöṭᵘ̈), lame-hurt, suffering from lameness, lame. Cf. cōṭh 1.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. lūnᵘ; 2 p.p. lōñōv), to reap (corn, etc.) (L. 459; W. 141; K.Pr. 232, 256; Rām. 14, 1364, 1512; Śiv. 1532; H. xii, 23). According to some, this verb is written lŏnun (Gr.Gr. lxvii). lūnᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. lūñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), reaped.

m. (sg. dat. lönis), fate, destiny, luck, fortune (according to Hindūs, the result of conduct in former lives) (K.Pr. 219; YZ. 271, 315; Rām. 421, 1036, 1038, 1230, 1492, 1586, 1710); esp. the fate that causes a marriage (Rām. 134); a woman's husband, her 'fate', her fated mate (Rām. 420, 1589); ḍĕka-lônᵘ, the fate (inscribed) on the forehead, a woman's husband (Śiv. 438); dayĕ-lônᵘ, God as fate, a husband (Rām. 1604; Śiv. 1546, 1628; K. 34); karma- lônᵘ, fate (Rām. 302, 1015, 1034, 1036, 1187, 1768), a woman's husband (Śiv. 449, 643, 690, 822, 940, 945). --mēlun -- m.inf. to be united to a suitable husband, to find a fitting mate. --wasun -- m.inf. 'fate to descend'; (hence, of an unmarried girl) the time of her marriage to be near. ¶ lānĕ-ʦūrū m. Xanthium strumarium (El.). ¶ lönⁱ-böcⁱ-baṭh or -böjⁱ-baṭh f. (sg. dat. ᵒ-baṭi), the union of a husband and a wife according to destiny. -bāganay f. (of a husband and wife) having the fated share of worldly prosperity or the reverse. -bāgay f. sharing according to fate; (of a man and woman) their union as husband and wife according to fate. -baṭh m. (sg. dat. -baṭas), the fated share; hence, a woman's husband. -büṭhᵘ̈ f. the hearth (awarded) by fate, the home of a woman's husband. -bözⁱ f. the trickery of fate, an adverse fate; esp. the early widowhood of a woman lately married. -milawan f. (sg. dat. milavüñᵘ̈), the uniting (of a husband and wife) by fate. -myulᵘ m. the union (as fated) of a husband and wife. -ʦūr m. a fate-thief, a destroyer of good luck (H. vii, 12).

f. (sg.dat. lö̃pi), a long step, a long stride (as over a ditch or the like), a leap from one foot. --tārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cross over by taking a long stride or leap from one foot. ¶ lö̃pa trāwañĕ f. pl. inf. to go along by making such leaps or long strides. -lö̃ph f. competing with another in such strides. --mēnañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to take long strides as if one were measuring land.
m. a receptacle for storing grain, a kind of huge jar (made of withies etc. plastered over with mud) in which grain is stored, a clay granary (L. 460).
m. 'a damaged lump'; hence, a person who stays immovably in one place (as if some limb were broken and he could not stir), a lazy loafer, an indolent lump of a fellow.
adj. (f. lŏpüñᵘ̈), a great fat heavy lazy fellow (so called from his resemblance to a grain-receptacle, cf. the preceding). Cf. māz-lᵒ.
m. one of a shallow, hasty, disposition, who readily betrays his private thoughts, easily frightened or angered, and not readily distinguishing between honour and dishonour.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lōranôwᵘ), to cause to become weak, to cause to waste away (Gr.Gr. 175).
f. a wife (El. lārī). Cf. lāra.
or lōrimᵘ̈ f. a small smooth round stone, a pebble in a brook.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. lōryōv), to become weak, deficient, thin, emaciated, lean, wasted away (Rām. 200, 907). ¶ lōrān yunᵘ m.inf. gradually to waste away or become emaciated (of condition, wealth, strength, etc.). ¶ lōryō-motᵘ or lūryō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. lōryē-müʦᵘ̈ or lūryē-müʦᵘ̈), wasted away, gaunt, attenuated, as ab.

m. (sg. abl. lari 3; for 1, 2, 4, see lar 1, 2, and lürᵘ̈), the roof of a house. The fem. of this word, lürᵘ̈, means 'a house'. ¶ lari-burza m. birch-bark used, or suitable for, roofing. -nāv f. a state barge with the boatmen seated both before and behind the portion occupied by the passenger; used only on long journeys (El. larináo, which he marks as m.; L. 382).
m. (sg. dat. löris), a heap, a piled-up mass. löris bĕhun m.inf. to sit on the pile, to become head of a house or of a community, etc. (esp. after deposing another).
adj. (f. lürᵘ̈), possessing strands (of a rope or the like) used --˚, as in okᵘ-lorᵘ (p. 19a, l. 27), aiṭha-lorᵘ (p. 66b, l. 29).

adj. (f. lörᵘ̈), smeared on to something, sticking close to something (e.g. of syrup or the like smeared on the inside of a vessel); one who tenaciously prefers (e.g. some special food or occupation) to the exclusion of all others (Śiv. 1643). Cf. lārun 3.

(for 1, see lôrᵘ 2) m. a cucumber (Cucumis sativus, L. 346, lár; El. lãr; Gr.Gr. 13; K.Pr. 124, 137, 214); cf. daba-lörᵘ̈, p. 181b, l. 10. -byôlᵘ m. cucumber seed; the name of a certain kind of rice plant, bearing a small fragrant seed (El. lãrbyol). -kulᵘ m. the cucumber plant (El.).

m. fatigue, weariness, languor (Gr.Gr. 122, Gr.M.). --aʦun -- m.inf. weariness or fatigue to attack (a person), i.e. to begin to be felt. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause (a person) to feel weariness or fatigue.

f. a woman who has lately had a child, a woman during the first twelve days after delivery (L. 258). -azār the pains of childbirth. -hurᵘ m. a childbirth bed, the straw bed on which a woman is laid for delivery; meton. a lying-in-room. -lë̆jᵘ̈ f. the process of cooking food for a lying-in woman. -tab m. fever following on childbirth, puerperal fever. -zar m. the pains of childbirth, the illness consequent on childbirth. -zörⁱ marun m.inf. to die in childbed.
pl. of lūsᵘ̈, see lūsᵘ and lōsun.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. lōsaladiñ), fatigued, wearied.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lōsanôwᵘ), to cause to be weary; to pitch away and smash (a cup, dish, or other vessel).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lōsowᵘ), to smash (a cup, dish, or other vessel, by throwing it down or striking it, etc.).
n.ag. (f. lōsavüñᵘ̈), one who is weary, one who suffers from fatigue; (of a vessel of any kind) in the state of being smashed (by a blow or otherwise).

conj. 2 [1 p.p. lūsᵘ or (L.V. 3, 44, 98) lūstᵘ, f.lūsᵘ̈ (K.Pr. 57) or lūʦhᵘ̈ (L.V. 48, 60); 2 p.p. lōsōv or lōʦhōv (Gr.Gr. 211, 228)], to become weary, fatigued (L.V. 48, 60; K.Pr. 57, 120; YZ. 253, 261; Rām. 189, 535, 645, 648, 734, 1574, 1766; Śiv. 1065, 1636, 1676) (cf. dand lāsȧnⁱ, p. 224a, l. 39); (of the sun, moon, or other heavenly body) to set (Rām. 974); (of the day or night) to come to an end (L.V. 3, 44, 98; K.Pr. 18) (cf. dōh l., p. 199b, l. 36); (of a cup, dish, or other vessel) to become broken. lūsᵘ-motᵘ or (old) lūstᵘ-motᵘ 2 (for 1, see lasun) perf. part. (f. lūsᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ or lūʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), wearied, tired (W. 125; K.Pr. 127); set (of a heavenly body); come to an end; broken (etc., as ab.).
in losᵘ-bosᵘ adj. (f. lüsᵘ̈-büsᵘ̈), one who lives a long, happy, and prosperous life as a house holder. Cf. lasun-basun, s.v. lasun and basun lasun, p. 133b, l. 34.
adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, Central Tibet. See lās 2.
m. a plug inserted violently or tightly into a hole or pipe; esp. obsc. Cf. lata 1.

m. a small, round, metal pot (for general use, generally made of brass or copper) (Rām. 1178); a darling, a favourite child (cf. dŏda-lōṭa, p. 189b, l. 20). -mana m. any person, animal, thing, or work, which is especially loved.
adj. c.g. that which does not appear to be heavy; light, not heavy; easy.

m. (sg. dat. lōṭas) in the following:-- lōṭh phērun m.inf. the pangs of regret (or someone or something lost) to be felt, sad memories to be aroused (cf. phērun); griping pains in the stomach to be felt (cf. lāṭh 1); the desire to hinder another's work to be felt (cf. lāṭh 2). --phirun -- m.inf. when a man is engaged in a work, the sudden desire to hinder its execution to arise; indigestion, causing griping pains, to occur.

m. a club, a mace, a thick wooden stick not of great length (cf. dŏbiñĕ-lᵒ, p. 184a, l. 19). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. 'a club to occur', i.e. to be racked with fatigue (cf. lĕṭha-lôrᵘ gaʦhun, s.v. lĕṭha). ¶ lȧṭhⁱ dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to give clubs, to beat, to drub (with a stick, or even with the fist, etc.). lȧṭhⁱ-har f. a fight with clubs between a number of people. -kinjᵘ̈ or -kī̃jᵘ̈ f. 'club and wedge', the 'cat' used in the game of tip-cat. -kinjĕ-loṭhᵘ m. the club used in the game of tip-cat; the game of tip-cat (L. 464, lat kinch lut).
m. the hump of a bull or similar animal (El.).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. lŏtyōv), to become, or be, light (not heavy), to become lighter; (of a disease) to become light, the patient to become convalescent; (of a human being) to become free from labour, to cease work. lŏtyō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. lŏtyē-müʦᵘ̈), become light, lightened; convalescent.

adj. (f. lö̆ʦᵘ̈), light (in weight) (Gr.Gr. 27; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1027, 1048, 1665); mild, gentle, soft (of voice, wind, heat, cold, rain, or the like) (K.Pr. 168; Śiv. 1868); gentle (of gait), soft, slow (Gr.Gr. 76; Gr.M.); easy, manageable, easy to endure; trivial, of no importance, frivolous, puerile; of a person or thing (Śiv. 1551); (as adv.) quietly, gently, secretly (K. 811). --gọ̆bᵘ -- m. light (and) heavy; hence, possessing two opposite qualities (e.g. at once honoured and despised, liked and disliked, too little and excessive, causing gain and loss, etc.). --hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. lö̆ʦᵘ̈ hishᵘ̈), very light, etc., as ab. --lọ̆tᵘ -- adj. and adv. (as adj. f. lŏ̈ʦᵘ̈lŏ̈ʦᵘ̈), very light, lightest of all (among a number of things); light throughout; continuously gentle or slow (of speech, motion, or the like); (pl.) several, each of which is light, etc.; as adv. gently, gently, i.e. continuously gently (Rām. 1352, 1416). --wanun --, to whisper (El. lút wanun); --zānun -- m.inf. to consider trivial, to treat with contempt (Gr.M.). ¶ lŏti adv. gently, mildly (H. xii, 5); slowly. --lŏti -- adv. continuously gently; continuously slowly, slowly throughout (K. 169, 986). ¶ lö̆ʦᵘ̈ lath f. (sg. dat. lŏʦĕ lati), a light kick, a feeble kick; hence, gradual convalescence from a sickness, or alleviation of an epidemic. --lath gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. convalescence, or disappearance of an epidemic, to occur (whether gradual or complete). --lath karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. completely and quickly to cure a violent disease.
m. (sg.dat. lötis), a certain resinous root found in mountain forests, used in the preparation of incense.
in lôṭᵘ-pôṭᵘ m. unwillingness to engage in any work when it is time to begin it (characterized by delay, inability, or refusal), jibbing at one's duty. Cf. lāṭh 2.
m. (f.lö̃ʦᵘ̈), one whose work, business, or occupation is well-established.

or (q.v.) löcⁱ f. (sg. dat. lācĕ), a long-shaped ball or pill of gold or other precious metal; a long-shaped ball or stick of incense-paste or similar matter formed by rolling between the palms of the hands. Cf. dupa-l., p. 232a, l. 33, and löcⁱ.

m. (sg. dat. laṭis), a tail; esp. a long tail (e.g. of a cow or buffalo) (a short tail is the fem. lüṭᵘ̈, q.v.) (Gr.Gr. 37; K.Pr. 34 (of a cat), 68 (of a cow), 83 (of a dog), 124; Rām. 715, 739, 1406; Śiv. 1564, 1877; H. v, 7; xi, 9); the stalk or pedicle of a plant (e.g. cf. dachĕ-loṭᵘ, p. 185b, l. 45; hāka-l., vegetable stalks, K.Pr. 184; mujĕ-lᵒ, s.v. mujᵘ̈); the tail or latter end of anything (shāma-loṭᵘ, the end of evening, late in the evening, Rām. 217); met. gōvᵘ̈-loṭᵘ̈, an insignificant cow, a young cow giving little milk (p. 316a, l. 41). ¶ lȧṭⁱ-khyucⁱ adj. (f. -khicᵘ̈), (of a garment) having the ends in tails, having the ends badly-fitting, crooked, or uneven. -mūran f. (sg. dat. mūrüñᵘ̈), tail-twisting (e.g. in driving a cow or bullock); (met.) destruction or destroying by a sudden attack. -marʦ m. tail pepper; cubeb (Piper Cubeba) (the fruit of which is described as tasting like pepper, and having a tail). It consists of a longish bunch of pepper-corns grouped round a fairly thick stalk. This is connected with the stem of the plant by a somewhat thinner stalk, which, when plucked with the bunch, resembles a tail. -mūray f. i.q. lȧṭⁱ-mūran, ab. -rôdᵘ m. 'long-tail', a certain insect or worm, described as being produced in foul mud or cowdung, thread-like in form, and possessing a tail. -tārukh m. (sg. dat. -tārakas), 'a tail-star,' a comet (W. 115) with the tail pointing downwards (which is a bad omen). When the tail points upwards a comet is tāj-tārukh, or 'tiara-star', and is a good omen (El.). -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), having the tail-cut, bob-tailed; (of something inanimate) having one corner cut off; (of a work) having a portion cut off. -zyūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈), long-tailed.

m. (sg. dat. laṭis), an accusation, charge (of some crime). --khārun -- m.inf. to bring an accusation, to lay a charge. --khasun -- m.inf. a charge to be brought, an accusation to be laid or incurred. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. a charge or accusation to arise.
adj. (f. lüvᵘ̈ 1; for 2, see s.v.), bowing down, inclined, crooked (e.g. a wall, pillar, or the like).

m. (sg. dat. lövis), (of grass, etc.) as much as can be held in the hand, a wisp of grass, etc. (six of these make one gë̆ḍᵘ̈, cf. p. 229b, l. 32) (El.; K.Pr. 49 (lov), 247 (obl. lawah); Śiv. 1212; H. xi, 12); met. in such idioms as dāri-lôwᵘ, a long thick beard (p. 238a, l. 28).

adj. (f.lövᵘ̈), quite new and fresh (of vegetables or the like); fresh, blooming, youthful (e.g. the body, age, etc.) (K.Pr. 125, lāv for lāvi). --bọ̆dᵘ -- adj. (f. lövᵘ̈-bŏ̈zᵘ̈, cf. bel.), of fresh intellect, i.e. (esp. of a child) sharp, quick-witted. ¶ lövᵘ̈ bŏd f. (sg. dat. lāvĕ bö̆zᵘ̈), a fresh intellect, (esp. of a child) quick wit, sharpness. lövᵘ̈-bọ̆dᵘ̈ adj. (f. lövᵘ̈-bŏ̈zᵘ̈), sharp-witted.
m. in lŏy-gŏy m. practice, the being engaged in practice.
f. bell-metal, white copper. -bāna m. a dish or other vessel made of bell-metal.
m. (sg. dat. lŏyĕnas), the rust or verdigris formed on a bell-metal vessel. Cf. lŏy 2.
adj.(lŏyivᵘ̈), made of bell-metal. See lŏy 2.

f. a kind of sweetmeat, made of wheat-flour, cooked with spices, sugar, etc. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make such a sweetmeat (YZ. 96); met. to make a large collection of property (got as a bargain or the like). --karȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to collect a quantity of goods (got as a bargain or on other opportunity).
adj. c.g. necessary, requisite, indispensable (Gr.M.); obligatory, incumbent (Gr.M., Śiv. 41); suitable, proper, meet (El., Śiv. 1184).

m. lightness, non-heaviness; lightness or getting milder (of a disease); ease, facility (El. latsar and lautsar); despicableness, insignificance; cf. lọ̆tᵘ. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give lightness, i.e. to make a person mean, to abuse or censure publicly (e.g. a father scolding a son). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to experience abuse, as ab. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf., id. --lagun -- m.inf. disgrace, dishonour, degradation to be incurred.
m. swelling, puffing out of the face (from disease, extreme rage, etc.) (El. lantsar); inordinate pride. --khasun -- m.inf. swelling as ab. to rise; pride to be displayed.

f. the profession or occupation of a eunuch (even when carried on by one who is not a eunuch. These persons wear women's clothing, dance and sing at marriages, and are hired to make loud lamentations at the burials of the rich (El.)).
or lṻʦhil f. the condition or conduct of a eunuch (Gr.Gr. 142); conduct like that of a eunuch.
m. a tied-up bundle or clump of grass or the like.
or lö̆ʦhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a small tied-up bundle or clump of grass or the like.

or loʦhᵘ m. a lump, clump of anything; a clot (e.g. of phlegm, nose-mucus, or the like). ¶ laʦhi gaʦhun m.inf. to be treated as such a clot, to suffer the mortification of being rejected, abused, neglected, or the like. --karun -- m.inf. to cause such mortification.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lọ̆ʦᵃrôwᵃ), to make light, to make lighter, to ease (a burden) (Śiv. 1810).

m. (pl. dat. lōban, Gr.Gr. 51), desire, greed, avarice, covetousness (El.; Gr.Gr. 138, 149; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 220; Rām. 348, 1633; Śiv. 1283); (among Hindūs) avarice personified,--one of the six enemies of man, which impede union with the Supreme Deity, the other five being kām (Skt. kāma), sexual desire; krūd (Skt. krōdha), wrath; mad (Skt. mada), arrogance; mōh (Skt. mōha), delusion; and matsar (Skt. matsara), jealousy (L.V. 12, 30, 43, 71; Rām. 979, 1762; Śiv. 18, 22, 59, 104, 1672, etc.). --karun -- m.inf. to covet (El., W. 150).
m. in lūb-ĕ-lubāb (= لبِ لباب), the pith, or quintessence, of anything (Rām. 1773).
n.ag. (f. lūbawüñᵘ̈), one who is very covetous or greedy for anything; applied also to any member of a person's body which exhibits ardent desire, lust, or the like.
adj. (as subst., sg. dat. lūbiṭas), avaricious, covetous, greedy, esp. when importunate (Gr.Gr. 138, Gr.M.); a miser (El. lôbishṭ).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. lūbyōv), desire or greed to be experienced; to feel desire, be desirous (K.Pr. 17, Śiv. 1663).
conj. 1 (1p.p. lūbᵃrôwᵃ), to cause to be desirous or covetous, to tempt, provoke desire (Rām. 1784).
adj. c.g. greedy, covetous; a miser (El. lobi). --ḍombᵘ -- m. 'greedy-guts', one who is continually eating everything he sees, without regard to its wholesomeness or unwholesomeness.
adj. c.g. wicked, corrupt, vicious, depraved, profligate, dissolute.
f. pl. a kind of large loaf or cake made of wheaten flour lightly cooked in ghī.
f. (sg. dat. lūcᵃrüñᵃ), the act of making small, shortening, reducing in size, narrowing, contracting.

(Rām. 716), or ludar m. a corruption of the Sanskrit Rudra, a N. of the god Śiva; N. of a group of gods, eleven in number, supposed to be inferior manifestations of Śiva (Rām. 1770); owing to the fact that Rudra was more especially the god of tempests, and that the monkey-god Hanumān (see halᵃmotᵃ) was the son of the Wind, the word is used as a title of Hanumān (Rām. 716, 902, 1604). -wāv m. the Rudra-wind, another title or epithet of Hanumān (see ab.) (Rām. 855, 906).
f. greed, greediness, rapacity, voraciousness, the being never satisfied but always asking for more.

f. (sg. dat. lō̃gĕ), a kind of waist-cloth (fringed and embroidered with silk, silver thread, or the like) worn principally by women. A Hindū woman never goes abroad without wearing one (El. lūngī); a kind of coloured and embroidered turban worn by men. ¶ lō̃gi-lāṭh m. (sg. dat. -lāṭas), such a waist-cloth, which is wrapped only once (not twice or more) round the waist; cf. lāṭh 1. -poʦhᵘ m. the fringed edge of such a waist-cloth. -shikhurᵘ m. an old ragged waist-cloth. -shikhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f., id. -züṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -zacĕ), id.
(? lukᵘ or lukh), m. Trypha Angustifolia (El.). ? = lŏka 1.

m., in Hindū cosmogony, a mythical mountain that encircles the earth (in Sanskrit lōkâlōka). Beyond it there is complete darkness, while on this side there is light. It thus divides the visible world from the regions of darkness (Śiv. 605, 1452).
f. a crowd or collection of many people (Gr.Gr. 152); cf. lūka-lᵒ, p. 519a, l. 25. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring a large crowd together.

(vill.) or lūkh 1 (often written lōkh) m. [sg. dat. lukas or lūkas, but, being plural in signification, this word is generally found in the plural (e.g. K.Pr. 168), with a pl. dat. lukan or lūkan, not lōkan (Gr.Gr. 51); but it is sometimes found, as a noun of multitude, in the singular (e.g. lūka- sondᵘ, K.Pr. 116; lūkas, K.Pr. 158)] the human race, mankind, people in general, an assemblage, group, or class of people (El. lūk; Gr.M.; L.V. 53; K.Pr. 262 (luk); 121, 158 (lūk); 168 (lok); YZ. 455; Rām. 202, 206, 766, 878, 1131, 1133, 1154, etc.; Śiv. 478, 489, 758, 800, 828, 839, 1245, 1316-7, 1391, 1519, 1627, 1635, 1799; K. 318, 416-7, 565, 652, 675, 995; H. ii, 11; xi, 13); a nation, a defined group, or class of people (Śiv. 800, 1116; K. 377, 879, 1013, 1176); a man's 'people', his servants, followers, soldiers (K. 660, 745, 759, 761); often used as a plural suffix for words signifying human beings, as in rāza-lūkh, king-people, i.e. kings (K. 657). ¶ lūka-chŏkh m. (sg. dat. -chŏkas), a procession of a few people. -hĕḍun m. (sg. dat. hĕḍanas), public ridicule. -kath f. (sg. dat. -kathi), what is said among people generally, that which is common report, that which is generally whispered about from ear to ear. -lūkh f. (sg. dat. -lūki), a great crowd of people (e.g. of people who have crowded to some place of refuge at a time of disaster). For the gender, see Gr.Gr. 75. -lūkay f. a great crowd of people called together and assembled. -laz or -lazzā f. shame at what is said by the outside world, humiliation caused by, or sense of shame felt before, public opinion (Śiv. (-lazzā) 883, 893, 1057); met. a houseful of unmarried daughters. -motᵘ m. common opinion, public report, public repute, what is commonly said (about a person or thing). -sāway f. general prosperity of a whole population. -vĕhawath f. (sg. dat. vĕhawüʦᵘ̈), respect for public opinion, that fear of general disapproval which prevents a person from always following his personal inclinations.

m. (declined like lūkh 1, being the same word, but with a specialized meaning. For the irreg. pl. gen. lūka-hondᵘ, see bel.) someone other than one's relations, a person not related to the person referred to, an outsider (W. 132, 144; L.V. 88; K.Pr. 193; YZ. 196; Śiv. 1065). -ṭākh (sg. dat. -ṭākas), (in an assembly or the like) all the people who are not related to oneself or to some person referred to. ¶ lūka-bāy f. a woman who is not related to oneself or to the person referred to. -buzⁱ, -buzy adj. c.g. dependent on people, belonging to other people (Gr.Gr. 161); cf. buzⁱ, p. 153a, l. 26. -hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of or belonging to so-and-so who is not related to oneself, of or belonging to someone who is not one of one's own people (L.V. 88; K.Pr. 57, 116, 120, 126, 163, 193, 242, 247); this word has the form of a genitive feminine. The regular genitive (also in use in other meanings) would be sg. lūka-sondᵘ (K.Pr. 116), pl. lūkan-hondᵘ. -kathan gaʦhun m.inf. to go (i.e. act) upon the words of others; hence, to become angry with, or show hostility to, a person (esp. to one's own people) at the verbal instigation of outsiders; to act against one's own interests owing to outside instigation. ¶ lūkas saṭh m. (sg. dat. -saṭi), acting or living like other people, obeying Mrs. Grundy.

m. (declined as in lūkh 1, q.v.), a world, a region, a division of the universe, of which (according to Hindū mythology) there are fourteen (seven higher and seven lower), the highest of all being called in Sanskrit Satya-lōka, while the lowest of all is the hell Patāla (cf. dīv-lūkh, p. 261b, l. 45) (Rām. 342, 515, 609, 846, 1759; Śiv. 36, 674, 699, 1197, 1887; K. 330, 591, 603, 723, 770, 773, 776, 1049); yiha-lūkh, the world here; para-lūkh, the other world; yiha-lūkh para-lūkh, this world and the next (K. 424, 1106). ¶ lūka-pāl m. (amongst Hindūs) a god who is a regent or guardian of one of the four quarters (or points of the compass) or of one of the four intermediate points (eight in all). (These are (in Sanskrit) Indra (regent of the East), Agni (of the South-East), Yama (of the South), Nairṛta (of the South-West), Varuṇa (of the West), Vāyu (of the North-West), Kubēra (of the North), and Īśāna (of the North-East) (Śiv. 1147, 1457; K. 335, 538, 1049).)
f. (sg. dat. lūkᵃrüñᵃ), a making smaller, reducing (something), cutting down, causing to shrink.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lūkᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. lūkᵃrun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 173, Gr.M.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lūkᵒrᵒ), to make smaller, pare down, cause to shrink in size, to shorten (Gr.Gr. 173, 174).

adj. (f. sg. nom. lūcᵘ̈; dat. lōcĕ (K.Pr. 125, YZ. 427)), small (as compared with another) (K.Pr. 125; YZ. 421, 427); small, little, insignificant (K.Pr. 24); (of age) young (esp. as compared with another) (El.; K.Pr. 127; Rām. 447, 549). --boḍᵘ bōzun -- m.inf. to understand small and great; hence, to comport oneself with propriety to old and young; (in distributing or weighing out a number of things of varying size) to distribute evenly. --dŏh -- m. an ordinary day, a day on which there is no special festival, not a high day or holiday; a small day, i.e. the little portion of a day of twenty-four hours that remains unexpired when it is late at night.
f. secret wealth hidden in a pile of bags, a secret pile of money-bags.

adv. affectionately (Gr.Gr. 18; cf. lōl); to one's great surprise, strange to say, surprizingly, as in lūlⁱ wuchum, to my great surprize I saw him. -anzan f. (sg. dat. -anzüñᵘ̈), a kind of rice plant, with a white scented grain; the grain of this plant. -anzun m. (sg. dat. -anzanas), another kind of rice-plant with a yellowish-white, small, scented grain; the grain of this plant.
m. the down on the body (of man or animals); a single hair of this down (used as a simile for smallness or fineness).
m. a rake, a fornicator, a profligate.
f. (sg. dat. lanjĕ 1), a woman who is lame, halt, crippled; cf. longᵘ (f. nom. lünjᵘ̈, dat. lanjĕ. This word is apparently a back-formation from lanjĕ).

f. (sg. dat. lanjĕ 2), the branch of a tree (El.; Gr.Gr. 62; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 7; Rām. 606, 1488; Śiv. 368, 1048, 1694); a branch of the body, an arm or leg (Rām. 694); a branch of a river; a branch of a business, a department; a branch of a man's family (e.g. the father's side, or the mother's side, and so on to more distant branches); a creeper, a climbing plant (Gr.M.); the handle of a portable brazier or the like. ¶ lanjĕ f.pl. branches (in all the above meanings); a collection of branches, branches and twigs; the branches of a family, a man's relations and connexions. --kaḍañe -- f. pl. inf. to pull branches (from a tree); met. to worry a person by sending him hither and thither simultaneously on many duties. --nērañĕ -- f. pl. inf. branches to issue; hence, to be worried by various duties, as ab. -phuṭᵘ adj. (f. -phuṭᵘ̈), having its branches broken; having one's legs broken; met. one whose means of support, such as relations or connexions, have failed; (of a portable brazier or the like) having its handle broken.
m. (sg. dat. lūpas), in the following:--lūph dyunᵘ m.inf. to erase, wipe out (writing, a pattern, etc.); to put an end to, destroy (a business, construction, etc.). Cf. lūpith.
in lūpithʦhunun m.inf. utterly to erase, wipe out, destroy, i.q. lūph dyunᵘ, s.v. lūph.
or lūrᵘ 1 (for 2, see lūrun) m. the act of pulling down, demolishing (cf. lūrun and (p. 181b, l. 17) daba-lūr). lūrⁱ lāyun m.inf. to scold, abuse in a shouting voice.
f. (sg. dat. lūrüñᵘ̈), the act of pulling to pieces, knocking down bit by bit, demolishing (of a house, wall, or the like) (Gr.M.).
f. wages for pulling down a house, the wages of a housebreaker.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lūranôwᵘ), to get pulled down, to cause to be broken down bit by bit, to get demolished (of a house, wall, or the like).

m. the utter breaking up and scattering of the fragments (of a house, wall, or the like); the utter destruction or nullifying of some work or condition even after it is completed or attained (Śiv. 3).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. lūrᵘ 2, for 1, see lūr; 2 p.p. lūryōv, to pull down, knock down bit by bit, demolish (a house, wall, or the like) (L.V. 74, Rām. 737, Śiv. 278). lūrᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. lūrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), pulled down bit by bit, broken up, demolished, as ab.

f. (sg. dat. lōrĕ), a club, a pole, a stick (El. lor and lúr; Gr.Gr. 24; Gr.M.; W. 12, 141; K.Pr. 62, 120, 210; L. 464; Rām. 1312; K. 154, 331, 326); a stick, in the sense of a handle of a wheel (K.Pr. 131); a stick, in the sense of a blow with a stick (K.Pr. 146, 216). --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to carry off a person's property by repeated acts of extortion. --lāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cudgel (with dat. of person) (Gr.M.). ¶ lōri-dab m. a blow from a stick. -gurᵘ̈ f. a false charge or accusation. -gurᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. a false accusation to be made, to be subjected to a false accusation. -gurᵘ̈ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to bring a false accusation (against a person). -han f. a little pole, small stick, small staff, a walking-stick (El., W. 113, K.Pr. 70). -har f. (sg. dat. -hari or -hürᵘ̈), a fight with clubs (esp. between two parties of people). -hürᵘ̈bāz m. one who is skilled in fighting with the club, a club-man. -hạrᵃl m. one who is addicted to fighting with, or attacking with clubs, a club-man. -kūṭun m. (sg. dat. -kūṭanas), a small light club, a stick (unbarked) (K.Pr. 126). -prath m. (sg. dat. -pratas), beating or flogging, a thwacking. -shĕlakh m. (sg. dat. -shĕlakas), beating with a stick (esp. in punishing a naughty child). -ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ʦanjĕ), a blow from a cudgel; a sudden and unexpected sorrow or calamity. -wôlᵘ m. a club-bearer, a mace-bearer.

f. (sg. dat. lari 4; for 1, 2, 3, see lar 1, 2, and lorᵘ 1), a house (El. lȧr, lur m.; cf. lorᵘ). For an account of the Kāshmīr house, see El. s.v. lur (Gr.Gr. 136; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 57, 124, 166, 219, 242; YZ. 409; Rām. 1014; Śiv. 61, 448, 598, 784, etc.; H. vi, 3); cf. burza-l. (p. 130b, l. 37), dāra-l. (p. 235a, l. 34), kañi-l. (p. 461b, l. 15). lürᵘ̈-mürᵘ̈ f. house and hut, house, etc.; hence, landed property, house and grounds, house and the surrounding lands, immovable property. -würᵘ̈ f., id. (El. lȧr-wȧr). ¶ lari-cōkh m. (sg. dat. -cōkas), a group of four houses, i.e. a dwelling composed of four houses forming a hollow square, and facing each other internally, all usually occupied by a single householder. -cōkᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or -cō̃khᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a group of such four-fold houses. -grākh n.ag. (sg. dat. -grākas; f. -grākañ), an owner of houses (Gr.Gr. 136); a house-seeker, one who is anxious to buy houses. -grākay f. a collection of would-be purchasers at a sale of a house or houses. -khŏpᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or -khŏphᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. an old broken-down house, a house in the last stage of decay; cf. khŏphᵘ̈rᵘ̈. -kônᵘ m. (sg. dat. -könis), a house-broker, a man who lives by buying houses, breaking them up, and selling the materials; cf. kônᵘ 3. -könil f. the profession of such a house-broker. -lobᵘ adj. (f. -lübᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or situated close to, a house. -mari-bôgᵘ m. (sg. dat. -bögis), the partition of immovable property amongst heirs when there is no one entitled to inherit it as a whole; cf. lürᵘ̈-mürᵘ̈, ab. -pōr m. a floor or story in a house of several stories. -pāwurᵘ m. (sg. dat. -pāwaras), a small house, a cottage; cf. pāwurᵘ. -trangürᵘ̈ f. a house-heap, a row of houses touching each other, a street of houses. -trŏ̈p ᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a block or group of houses crowded together. -ʦôkᵘ m. (sg. dat. -ʦökis), the square-shaped foundation walls of a house. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), the master or owner of a house (Gr.Gr. 136); the owner of many houses.
lōsañĕn, or lūsⁱñĕn, see dŏhⁱ-lūsiñ, p. 200a, l. 34.
see dŏhⁱ-l. (p. 200a, l. 32), and cf. lōsun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. lūṭanôwᵘ), to cause to plunder, to cause to be plundered, to give up to plunder.

m. the Kāshmīrī form of Rōhitâśva, N. of the son of the pious king Hariścandra. When the latter was reduced to dire poverty, he sold himself as a slave to provide the cost of burning the corpse of Lutāsh. For further particulars of the Kashmīr version of the story, see K.Pr. 122.
f. (sg. dat. lǖʦᵘ̈), a certain contagious skin disease, accompanied by swelling and pustules (? cf. Hindī lūtā, a 'spider-lick').

m. (sg. dat. lūṭas), robbery, pillage, plundering (El.; Gr.Gr. 18, 149; K.Pr. 127, 157, 217; K. 569) (cf. ȧnⁱ-lūṭh, p. 30b, l. 29); plunder, pillage, spoil, booty, loot. --karun -- m.inf. to rob, plunder (El., Rām. 1010); (with dat.) pādshāh-garas lūṭh karun, to rob the king's house (K.Pr. 209). -mār m. plundering and pillage, havoc, sack. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to plunder and scatter, to commit havoc (Rām. 747). ¶ lūṭa-dyār m. pl. plundered goods, goods collected by a course of plunder, plunder, loot, stolen goods. --nyunᵘ -- m.inf. to plunder and carry off (goods) (Śiv. 1312). ¶ lūṭas hūsas böcⁱ-baṭh f. (sg. dat. --böcⁱ-baṭi --), collecting together or uniting for a plundering expedition. Cf. bôcᵘ and baṭh 1.
f. a kind of small lōṭā, or brass pot.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. lūṭᵘ; 2 p.p. lūcyōv), to plunder, pillage, spoil, ravage, rob (Śiv. 341, 1754; K. 418). lūṭᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. lūṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈; sg. dat. lūcĕ-maʦĕ), (of property) plundered, ravaged, robbed.
m. (f. lūṭᵃrĕñ), a plunderer, ravager, robber (Gr.Gr. 149, Śiv. 1754).
f. the business or occupation of a plunderer.
f. the business or occupation of a plunderer.

or lū̃ṭh f. (sg. dat. lō̃cĕ), the edge or border of a garment, the skirt of a coat, etc.; --˚ a bunch (of vegetables or the like; cf. bumbi-l., p. 107b, l. 41, and handi-l., p. 337a, l. 48; mulⁱvĕñĕ-lⁱ, s.v. mulⁱvĕñ). lō̃cĕ lamun m.inf. to pull or drag the edges of a person's garment; (when some offence has been committed) to hint, or threaten that a person will be accused of it; to ask a debtor to pay up, to dun (K.Pr. 126).

f. (sg. dat. lacĕ), a tail; esp. the short tail of a sheep, goat, or the like (El. laṭ) (a long tail is the masc., loṭᵘ 1, q.v.) (K.Pr. 63 (of a sheep); Rām. 717); the tail-end of anything, e.g. the tail-end of a fish (gāḍa-l., p. 276b, l. 20) or a low hill at the end of a mountain range (kŏha-l., p. 390b, l. 21) (K.Pr. 136). --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to raise (a person's) tail, i.e. to incite, spur, stimulate (esp. one who is lazy, diffident, or unwilling). --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the tail to rise, to become incited, etc., as ab. ¶ laci kīcam m. twisting of an animal's tail (to make it go on).
in lūtⁱ-pūtⁱ m.pl. one's children as a whole, all one's sons, daughters, grandchildren, etc.
f. (for 1, see lowᵘ), a ewe (El. lau).
f. the wife of a eunuch, a woman married to a eunuch (without knowledge of the fact that he is such).
f. membrum virile (used in obscene abuse).

m. (sg. dat. lĕbis), a lump of cowdung, as evacuated; a fixed down or stuck down cover (such as a lump of mud) over the mouth of a jar or the like. --karun -- m.inf. to fasten down or cover the closed mouth of a jar or the like with a lump of mud. --thobᵘ -- m. concealing, hiding, keeping quiet (e.g. a fault, a loss, or the like). --thawun -- m.inf. to close up a covered (or locked) receptacle with mud (which is then impressed with a seal).
adj. (f. lë̆cᵘ̈), a secondary suffix used in the word aḍalyokᵘ, incomplete (p. 11b, l. 9).

m. (sg. dat. lĕlis), a large kind of jar (earthenware or metal) or pot (holding as much as nine or ten seers or more) used for cooking and other purposes (El. lul and lyul) (Gr.Gr. 25; K.Pr. 27, 125; cf. nāra-lᵒ, s.v. nār); (met.) a bulky, fat fellow (cf. hŏpa-lyolᵘ, p. 342a, l. 17); cf. lë̆jᵘ̈. --phuṭun -- m.inf. a jar to be smashed; met. ruin to occur, a business, friendship, means of support, or the like to be ruined. ¶ lĕlⁱ-bŏy f. the smell of an earthen jar. -katᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a large sherd or piece of an earthen pot (used as a griddle or the like). ¶ lĕli họ̆khᵘ bata m. in the cold parts of Kashmīr, or in the winter, when the warmth of the sun is not sufficient to dry freshly gathered paddy, it is put into a jar and dried over a fire. When rice husked from this paddy is cooked and made into boiled rice, it is called by this name.
m. (sg. dat. lĕmbis), mud collected or accumulated at the bottom of a receptacle containing liquid, sediment, dregs (El. lumb). Cf. lĕmb.
adj. (m. sg. dat. lĕṭhis; f. sg. nom. lë̆ṭhᵘ̈; dat. lĕchĕ), easy, not difficult (e.g. an instruction, a journey, a course of study, a task, an occupation, and so forth). Cf. lĕchĕr.

adj. (m. sg. dat. lĕʦis; f. lë̆ʦᵘ̈), weak, feeble, powerless (K.Pr. 36 (pl. dat. lĕʦĕn, written liʦan); YZ. 393). --longᵘ -- adj. (f. lë̆ʦᵘ̈ lünjᵘ̈ or lë̆ʦᵘ̈ lünḍᵘ̈), weak and lame, feeble and crippled or awry. Cf. longᵘ lyoʦᵘ, p. 526b, l. 41.
adj. (f. lichᵘ̈), rough, hard; astringent; (of food) tough, hard to chew; cruel, unkind, harsh.
m. (sg. dat. likhis), a fixed gaze, a stare, a longing look; a mark aimed at, butt, target (Rām. 1785). --karun -- m.inf. to stare (at), to look longingly (at).

m. (sg. dat. likhis), a thing written; an account, a reckoning; regard, estimation (Rām. 301); state, condition, style, fashion. -tryukhᵘ m. accounting, keeping accounts of receipt and expenditure. Cf. likhun.
m., in ganda-lyunᵘ, p. 289b, l. 42. Probably a by-form of lyuñᵘ, q.v.

m. (sg. dat. lithis), hard labour, travail, heavy toil, exhaustion (such as that caused by travelling in stormy weather). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. the experience of heavy toil, exhaustion, and humiliation to be suffered; to be crushed under a load of exhaustion and humiliation (Rām. 158). --karun -- m.inf. to cause such travail, exhaustion, and humiliation; to crush a person under a load of exhaustion and humiliation (Rām. 158).

m. (sg. dat. līṭis; abl. lēṭi), a kind of grass (used as a medicine) (Rām. 646); often --˚, cf. batakh-lᵒ, p. 144a, l. 46, dā̃da-lᵒ, p. 187b, l. 9); the young of a bird, a chick, a chicken (cf. dŏda-lᵒ, p. 189b, l. 21).
adj. c.g. one who is importunately greedy (esp. for food), i.e. who is greedy, and who in season and out of season is always begging for something to eat.
or lich f. (sg. dat. lᵃchi), the egg of the body-louse, a nit (cf. Hindī līkh) (El. lichh). lᵃcha phŏharĕ f. pl. a clump of nits (cf. phŏhürᵘ̈).
or lichal adj. c.g. infested with nits, lousy.
or lichĕr m. pungency, fieriness, harshness, roughness (in taste or handling); (of a human being) hardness, harshness, irascibility.
f. desire, greed, avidity; esp. jealous greed, covetousness. --ganḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such greed to arise, craving to take place.
conj 3 (2 p.p. lᵃhanyōv), (of a crop) to delay ripening (Gr.Gr. lxviii). Cf. lᵃhunᵃ.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. lᵃhyōv), to be sufficient (Gr.Gr. lxvii).

adj. (f.lᵃhüñᵃ), having the ripening delayed; (of grain, edible fruit, or the like) not gone soft and formed into a mass with others, but fully ripe and soft, non-agglomerated; (of a female animal such as a cow or mare who is being examined as to whether she is pregnant or not) not pregnant. Cf. lᵃhanun.

or lish f. a small bit or portion, a particle, an atom, a very small quantity, a mote (cf. līsh); a tiny spike or short thin fragment of anything (e.g. of wood, or of meat), a little sharp point, a spiculum. lᵃsh-trᵃsh or lish-trish f. spike and splinter; hence, a woman's store of ornaments few and meagre in quantity, a poor collection of jewellery. ¶ lᵃshĕ(lishĕ) kaḍañĕ  f. pl. inf. to extract motes; hence, (in discussing a proposed marriage or the like) minutely to criticize or examine a person's wealth, relations, occupations, circumstances, or the like; (in an argument) to oppose meticulous objections. lᵃshĕ(lishĕ)-pāshĕ  f.pl. a tiny collection of tiny things; minute criticism, as ab. lᵃshĕ(lishĕ)-pāshĕ kaḍañĕ  f. pl. inf. i.q. lᵃshĕ kaḍañĕ, ab. ¶ lishā f. a single tiny fragment or piece.
or lishĕl adj. c.g. pervaded with, or full of, small particles or little thorns, or spines (e.g. food, or a tree).
m. dislocation of a limb or joint; tearing or cutting away of a member of a garment, undoing the seam uniting one part of a garment to another. --lagun -- m.inf. dislocation of a limb to occur.
f. (sg. dat. lᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), a slender woman (naturally, not by illness or the like); cf. latūr and latiy. lᵃʦa f.pl. a mass of small fish (e.g. in a basket, arranged for sale).

f. (sg. dat. lᵃti 2, for 1, see s.v.), a secondary suffix used to form diminutives of words signifying breath or light, as in prānalᵃth, a spark of life; shāhalᵃth, a trace of breath; gāshĕlᵃth, a very little light; ʦö̃gⁱlⁱth, a little lamp (Gr.Gr. 162).

(for 2, see lᵃth 2) or liti in the following:--lᵃti (liti) chiti gaʦhun  m.inf. (of a collection of separate things) (e.g. a heap of grain) to become needlessly scattered about, and so rendered useless. lᵃti (liti) chiti karun  m.inf. to render useless, as ab.
adj. used apparently only in the feminine. Thus:--lᵃtᵃjᵃputᵃjᵃ f. misshapen, lopsided, and ugly from this cause.
f. satisfaction, contentment (e.g. on the removal of hunger, cold, an impediment, or the like).

f.pl. a collection of small holes (e.g. a lattice or gauze in a wall, a door, etc.). --trọ̆pᵃrañĕ -- f.pl.inf. to close these holes with a curtain, mat, or the like, to stop a draught of cold air passing through them.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. lᵃyyōv), to be sufficient, to be fit, to be competent.
adj. (f. lᵘ̈chᵘ̈), hard, tough, rough (in taste or handling); (of a human being) hard-natured, rough-natured, irascible, i.q. lyochᵘ, q.v.

. The eleventh consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet, the twenty-fifth (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the twenty-eighth) consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and thirty-first consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. It has the sound of the letter m in English. In schools its name is mōv mö.

or mā (see bel.) adv. prohibitive particle, used (Gr.Gr. 255) only with the pres. impve., as in ma kar, make thou not, mā karin, let him not make, the ben., as in ma bŏyyĕn, may it not be! God forbid! (Gr.Gr. 252), or, occasionally with the fut. ind. indicating a wish, as in mā lagaham (= lagakh + m), mayst thou not find thyself (H. v, 2). As in the last example, ma or mā is sometimes repeated, under the form of m, as a suffix added to the verb; cf. under mā, bel. It is not used with the pol. impve., with which ma-ta or ma-tā is employed; nor is it used with the fut. impve. or past impve., with which na is employed, as in kȧrⁱzi na, you must not make, kȧrⁱzihē na, you should not have made (Gr.Gr. 255; Gr.M.; W. 96, 151; YZ. 38; Śiv. 52, 425, 539, etc.; Rām. 24, 27, 29, 33, 46, etc.; K. 65; H. xii, 7). ¶ ma-bā, please do not (Gr.Gr. 256); similarly ma-sö and other polite forms of prohibition (Gr.Gr. 256), both used in the same way as ma (L.V. 88; Rām. 1342, ma-sa). ¶ ma-ta or ma-tā adv. prohibitive particle, the same as ma, but generally used only with the pol. impve., as in mata (or matā) karta, please do not make (Gr.Gr. 255, 256; L.V. 53, where it has the force of a negative question; YZ. 142, 266; Śiv. 22, 28, 578, 1247, 1737, 1879 ff.; Rām. 1019; K. 34, 364, 378, 580, 906, 1107). Occasionally ma-ta is used with the pres. impve., as in Śiv. 525. As in the case of ma, ma-ta also may have the polite suffixes bā, sö, etc., added without affecting the sense, beyond adding a further tinge of politeness. Thus mata-bā, mata-sö, and so on (Gr.Gr. 256); matō (Śiv. 553). ¶ mā or (poet., H. v, 9) māh adv. the same as ma, ab., q.v. It is also used before or after a verb to indicate a question asked in hesitation (Gr.Gr. 256), as in karān mā chuh or mā chuh karān or mā karān chuh, I wonder if he is making, is he really making? According to El., in this sense it is never the first word in a sentence, but the above is the account given by I.K. VIII, i, 29 (Gr.M.; L.V. 89; Śiv. 23, 335, 575, 593, 795, 807, 1255, 1802, 1897; Rām. 754 ff., etc.; K. 38, 64, 505, 587, 1134, 1157, etc.; H. i, 2; v, 8, 9; vii, 20; viii, 9, 13; x, 5, 12; xii, 23). This word is also used as a negative in the apodosis of a conditional sentence, as in hargāh-ay wuchihē... mā mārihē, if he had seen... he would not have killed (H. viii, 10); hargāh-kiy sara karihē... mā diyihē hukum, if he had investigated... he would not have given the order (H. viii, 13). ¶ As in the case of the purely prohibitive ma or mā, this dubitative mā may also be repeated, under the form of a verbal suffix, as in mā lōsĕm (= lōsi + m), I wonder if he is weary (Rām. 234).
prep. with, along with, together with (used, esp. by Musalmāns, with borrowed Arabic or Persian words) (W. 90).

m. a certain dish made of boiled rice, colouring matter, clarified butter, sugar, saffron, raisins, and spices (El.; H. ii, 3). According to K.Pr. 74 it is a 'company dish'. -pholᵘ m. a pile of such rice; a single grain of such.

or mö̃ch  m. (sg. dat. mã̄chas or mö̃chas), honey (El.; Gr.Gr. 10; Gr.M.; L. 461; K.Pr. 150, 155). ¶ mā̃ch-goḍᵘ m. a bee's nest (in a tree-hollow, etc.), a beehive; a honeycomb. -gan  m. a beehive (L. 460); a honeycomb (Gr.M.). -phar m. honey in the comb (El.). -tabukh or mö̃ch-tabakh m. (sg. dat. -tabakhas), a kind of large covered jar for holding honey (used esp. in sending presents of honey). -tᵃlᵃrᵃ or mö̃ch-tᵃlᵃrᵃ f. a honey- bee (El. -tular, m., -tilar and -tulir, f.; L. 458, 461, mánch tilr; H. ix, 1, 3-6). ¶ mö̃ch-kashᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the sediment left after straining honey, the refuse beeswax.
mã̄chorᵘ, or m ã̄chur ᵘ m. slipperiness, greasiness (e.g. that caused by contact with greasy or sticky fingers). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. greasiness to arise (of some liquid putrifying and becoming slimy).
see mȧchⁱ, mashun, and moṭhᵘ 2 and 3.
adj. c.g. full of flies. Cf. machyulᵘ.
m. cheapness, small value (of anything), worthlessness. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become of small value, to become worthless.
adj. (f. machilᵘ̈), covered with dirty spots (of some bright polished surface). Cf. machĕl.

f. a fly (K.Pr. 128, machh; 23, 163), a bee (El. mach m. and machh f.; Gr.M.); a spot, or other damage (e.g. a particle removed from the reflecting surface) on a mirror or similar polished surface; a dark spot on a fair surface, such as a ṭīkā, a beauty-spot, a black pimple, or the like. --aʦüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. a fly to enter; a spot (as above) to occur on a mirror, etc.; 'a fly to occur in the ointment,' suspicion or estrangement to occur in the mind of one of two friends (or master and servant, or similar close relations). --bĕhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a fly to sit down; a spot of dirt to occur (e.g. on a lamp, a mirror, a metal ornament or vessel, etc.). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a fly to infect, i.e. food or the like to become corrupt and develop maggots. --ʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to suck a bee (as if a person, in the presence of much honey, instead of taking any or even touching it, took to sucking a bee); hence, of a wealthy person, to live in a penurious or mean way. --ʦᵃhawunᵃ -- n.ag. (f. --ʦᵃhavüñᵃ --), one who sucks a bee, as ab. --ʦaṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cut a fly; met. conceitedly to attempt as possible an impossible task. --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a fly to arise, i.q. mȧchⁱ lagüñᵘ̈, ab. ¶ machĕ-gũ̄̈ m. a fly's buzz; a hum, any such soft sound. -goḍᵘ m. a swarm of flies (Gr.M.). -khāv m. a fly-eater, N. of a certain winged insect that eats flies. -ṭĕcĕ f.pl. a group of pimples, acne, blackheads, or the like (Gr.Gr. 134). -ṭĕcĕl adj. c.g. pimply, marked with blackheads or acne (Gr.Gr. 134). -wugra m. unwholesome cooked rice (mixed with dirt, etc., as if mixed with flies). -wahārun m. any instrument for driving away flies (such as a fan, flapper, etc.). --wahārañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to drive away flies (e.g. by a fan, flapper, or the like). --wāmañĕ -- f. pl. inf., id.

m. the part of the back between a man's shoulders; cf. moṭᵘ. --dagun -- m.inf. to pound a person (with fist or club) on the naked back between the shoulders. ¶ macilⁱ-ʦünḍⁱ f. a slap on the naked back between the shoulders (usually of a child).
m. poverty, beggary, destitution. --lāgun -- m.inf. to pretend poverty, (of a well-to-do person) to assume the garb, attitude, and general appearance of poverty.

m. intoxication, drunkenness, inebriety; madness, insanity; ardent passion, lasciviousness; rut-ichor, the juice that exudes from the temples of an elephant in rut; arrogance, conceit (L.V. 43; K.Pr. 228; Śiv. 755, 1417, 1479, 1562, 1758; K. 534, 600, 829, 1052; H. vii, 15); fury (K. 350); met. intoxicating liquor, wine (L.V. 81). -hostᵘ m. an elephant in rut (Śiv. 353, 1562; Rām. 599; K. 431, 913, 948). --khasun -- m.inf. pride, conceit to arise. --phū̃kun -- m.inf. to display pride or arrogance. -zal m. the ichor which exudes from the temples of an elephant in rut. ¶ mada-pān m. wine, made out of pears, apples, mulberries, or grapes (El.). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), free from pride or arrogance; free, or freed, from intoxication, sober, sobered. --wālun -- m.inf. to bring down from pride, to bring down a person's pride (Śiv. 857). --wasun -- m.inf. to descend from pride, a person's pride to be brought down. -vĕsar f. weakness from intoxication, the wrecking of the constitution and clouding of the intellect due to the habitual consumption of intoxicating drugs; the relaxation or looseness of the limbs due to drunkenness or the like. -vĕsorᵘ adj. (f. -vĕsürᵘ̈), one whose intellect is clouded by the habitual use of intoxicating drugs. -wothᵘ adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), one whose pride has descended, one who is no longer proud.

f. mixing (Gr.Gr. 126), esp. mixing up or kneading (by rubbing with the palms of the hands) of flour or other food with water, buttermilk, etc. (Gr.Gr. 10); cf. mã̄ḍay and namda-mö̃ḍ. --diñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to mix food, as ab. ¶ mã̄ḍi onᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. --üñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), mixed, kneaded, as ab.; made obedient, brought under influence; (of a difficulty) conquered by constant practice. --anun -- m.inf. to bring into mixing, to mix or knead flour, etc., as ab.; to make (a person) obedient to oneself, to bring under one's influence, make docile; to conquer a difficulty by constant practice. --aʦun -- m.inf. to enter kneading (of flour, etc.) to become mixed, kneaded, etc.; to join and be associated in the practices of any community, to adopt a course of behaviour, to become a communicant. --ʦāmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. ʦāmüʦᵘ̈), kneaded, mixed, as ab.; entered into intimate communion, one who has adopted the practices of another. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to become kneaded, as ab.; to come under anyone's influence, become obedient; (of a difficulty) to be conquered by practice.
adj. and subst. f. female (W. 17) (cf. nar māda, s.v. nar 2); a female (Gr.M.).
m. the belly, the stomach. dar- māda lagun m.inf. to find oneself in the stomach, to be in doubt, to be in incertitude (Rām. 1670).
adj. c.g. bad, not good; bad, corrupted.
m. (for gender, see W. 18), assistance, help (Gr.M.).
f. a certain medicinal plant, wild basil (Śiv. 187-8, 1401). mādȧli-pōsh m. its leaf and its flower; a bundle of its leaves.

m. a certain musical instrument (said to give forth the fifth note on the scale, called madhyama in Sanskrit, and to sound like the cry of a heron. It is described as a large jar with long strings across it).
m. a player on the madam, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. mā̃ḍanôwᵘ), to cause to knead, esp. with the feet. This word is applied to the kneading of large quantities of dough, and to the washing of thick coarse woollen cloth (El. manḍanáwun; K.Pr. 85, mándanáwun).
adj. c.g. blinded by intoxication, dead drunk, drunk with passion; blinded by passion or pride, arrogant.
f. (of a woman) charming, lovely, heart-stealing; (m.) a lover (El.).
f. a mother. mādar-zāda (= مادر زاد) m. born of the same mother, a uterine brother (Rām. 1427).

or مدارا) m. gentleness; soothing (Rām. 1731); civility, politeness, coaxing (Rām. 1676); humility; (as adj. c.g.) encouraged, comforted (El. madárá). --karun -- m.inf. to console, soothe; to ask politely, make a polite request (to) (Rām. 780).
m. N. of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna), Mādhava (Śiv. 1322, 1334, 1417; Rām. 3).
(K.Pr. 49), i.q. mad, q.v. Cf. ḍarhā (q.v.) for ḍar.
m. a follower of the celebrated Muslim saint Shāh Madār, whose tomb is at Cawnpore in India; a swaggering bully who terrorizes his neighbours.
in the following:--mādri-zāl f. (sg. dat. -zöjᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 69), a kind of net-like cloth woven from fine cotton thread.

m. in Hindū legend, N. of a demon. He and Kaiṭabha were believed to have sprung from the ears of Vishnu (Viṣṇu) while he was asleep; and when they were about to devour Brahmā, Vishnu slew them (Śiv. 1321). -sūdan m. the slayer of Madhu, a N. of Vishnu (Śiv. 1417).

m. (the f. is madüñᵘ̈, q.v.) (sg. dat. madanas, voc. madanō), N. of the Hindū god of love, Cupid; hence, a handsome person, a lover, a gallant, an adored one (K.Pr. 12, 237; Rām. 1143, 1490); semen virile (K.Pr. 186); --˚ an actor or other person taking the part of handsome gallant character. Cf. kala-pushᵘ-madun (p. 435a, l. 36) and mahārāza-madun (p. 556b, l. 39).
conj. 1 (1p.p. mỗḍᵘ; f. mö̃ḍᵘ̈, dat. mã̄jĕ), to knead flour, etc., and water, etc., to mix; cf. manḍun. mỗḍᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mö̃ḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, dat. mã̄jĕ-maʦĕ), kneaded.
f. (the word is the f. of madun, q.v.), a she-Cupid, a charming, lovely woman.
m. the middle in ādy mady and, beginning, middle, and end (quoted from Sanskrit) (Śiv. 1767).

m. N. of the tenth month of the Hindū luni-solar year (in Sanskrit, Māgha) (January-February) (Gr.Gr. 51; W. 107, māgh; K.Pr. 60, 128, 147, 171; Śiv. 590, 1162, 1351). --darun -- m.inf. to keep a fast throughout the month of Māg (eating only at night),--a Hindū religious ceremony. -mās m. the month of Māg (the term used in phrases referring to religious rites). ¶ māga-bata m. cooked rice in Māg, the N. of an offering (bali) of cooked rice scattered on house-roofs and elsewhere for the crows. -noṭᵘ darun m.inf. to keep the fast of the Māg water-jar,--a particular vow or fast kept in ancient times by Hindūs. The procedure was as follows:--For the first three days of the month of Māg the celebrant eats only in the evening; he then fasts for a whole day; then for three days eats only in the morning; then fasts for two days; then for three days he eats only at night; then fasts for two days; then again three days night-eating; and so on to the end of the month. Every day, for two praharas (i.e. six hours), he stands in a frozen stream in water reaching up to his navel, and lets ice-cold water trickle on to his head from a jar in the bottom of which a hole has been pierced. -tǖrᵘ̈ f. the cold of the month of Māg, winter cold. ¶ māgukᵘ adj. (f. māgücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the month of Māg.

f. N. of the tenth lunar asterism, or lunar mansion, called Maghā in Sanskrit. It contains five stars,--a Regulus, g, z, h, and n Leonis (Śiv. 1861). ¶ maga-māwas f. (sg. dat. -māwạsi), the lunar day which falls on the new moon of the Hindū month of Bādᵃrapĕth (in Sanskrit, Bhādrapada) (August-September). It is believed that according as rain falls or does not fall on this day, so the prospects of the crops are good or bad (cf. our St. Swithin's day on July 15).
(or) m. N. of a certain country, i.q. magad, q.v. maga-dīsh, the land of Magad (K. 1004).
f. a row of short curls at the back of the head extending from ear to ear. --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to wear such curls.
m. N. of a certain kingdom, equivalent to the country round the modern districts of Paṭnā and Gayā. In Sanskrit, Magadha (K. 550). Cf. mag 2.
or magāl a jingling repetition of agal, q.v. in agal-magal (p. 16b, l. 10) or agāl-magāl (id., l. 16).
m. a man who wears his hair in short curls at the back of the head. Cf. mag 3.

in magar lagun m.inf. continually to follow a person, to dog his footsteps, to follow on the skirts (of), beset (e.g. in the hope of obtaining something, or of a thief, or some disease or calamity). --rōzun -- m. inf., id. --thawun -- m.inf. to set a person to follow, as ab.
in magar-maʦh m. a crocodile (Gr.M.). Cf. makar 1.
conjunct, but, except, unless (El., Gr.M., W. 100, K.Pr. 164).

f. asking, begging (from someone), a request, petition (Gr.Gr. 129) (K.Pr. 145, 174; K. 488). mã̄gạyĕ nērun m.inf. to go out for begging (esp. of a respectable person who has fallen on evil times), to take to begging, to have recourse to asking for alms. --phȧlⁱ -- m.pl. grains of begging, the store of rice, etc., collected in small amounts by a beggar. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come by begging, to be gained by begging.
m. power, ability, capacity (see hatul magdūr) (Rām. 1531).
m. the west, the western quarter (El., YZ. 2).
or mã̄gun 1 m. the leader of a company of actors, a stage-manager.
adj. (f. mā̃güñᵘ̈), one who keeps his intentions or purpose hidden, reticent, reserved, uncommunicative, secretive.
adj.(māgüñᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the month of Māg, q.v.

or magan adj. c.g. intent (on), devoted or addicted (to); cf. nẹ̆ndᵃri-mᵃ, s.v. nẹ̆ndᵃr. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become intent (on), addicted or devoted (to) (e.g. to a business, to grief, illusion, wrath, joy, and so on); to become inattentive, heedless, forgetful (quasi, having the mind intent on something else) (Rām. 9).

or māh 1 ماہ m. the moon (YZ. mah, 9, 12, etc.; māh, 62, 63, etc.); a month (El. mah, misprinted as meaning 'mouth') (K.Pr. 204 (māh)). This Persian word occurs in literature chiefly in borrowed Persian expressions, such as māh-ĕ-dilsōz, a heart-inflaming moon (Rām. 1483), māh-ĕ-tābān, a radiant moon (Rām. 193).

(for 1, see mah 1) f. (sg. dat. möshᵘ̈), i.q. mahā, q.v.; cf. ḍaba-māh (p. 183b, l. 34). --karith -- conj. part. used as adv., having swallowed without noticing the taste, taking with a gulp; met. having swallowed (i.e. misappropriated) something entrusted to one. ¶ māha f.pl. a quantity or collection of beans. -sas m., i.q. mahā- sas, see mahā.

or māh 2 f. a bean (Phaseolus radiatus, L. 78, 330, 336). ¶ mahā-dāl f. split beans; bean porridge. -ḍār m. a bean- field (either prepared for bean-sowing, or in which beans are growing). -hĕm f. a mess of bean and other legumes. -pholᵘ m. a single bean; a small collection of beans (esp. when few in number). --pĕñĕ -- f.pl.inf. beans to fall, i.e. to be thrown at anyone; met. hatred to arise between friends. -sas m. a porridge of whole-beans cooked in clarified butter. -worᵘ m. a bean-cake or bean-loaf made of bean-flour, offered to the matṛkā-goddesses on the occasion of marriages and other festivals. -vürᵘ̈ f. a porridge or thick sauce of bean-flour and spices.
adj. c.g. exceedingly strong, very powerful or mighty; a very mighty or powerful person (Rām. 552).
or mahōbath (Śiv. 844, Rām. 81, 1053) m. (for gend., see W. 18) (sg. dat. mahabbatas محبتس), love, affection (Gr.M.; YZ. 256; Śiv. 844; Rām. 81, 1053; H. x, 4).
m. a great gift, largess, bounty (K. 843).
(or) or mahādanu-danḍ  m. a great, or mighty, bow (the weapon) (K. 370-1, 402, 429).
m. the great (god) Ganēsh, i.q. ganapath, q.v. (Śiv. 1, 1142).
. In Śiv. 1142, the word refers to Shiv (Śiva), and not to Ganēsh.

m. Time (personified) (Rām. 1510); N. of a form of Shiv (Śiva) in his character as destroyer of the world (Rām. 735, 1058, 1518; Śiv. 165, 372, 594); a N. of Yama, the god of death, Death personified (Śiv. 1888).
m. (sg. dat. mahākalpāntas), (in Hindū theology) the end of a mahākalph (q.v.), when there is total dissolution of the whole universe including even the gods themselves (Śiv. 979).

m. (sg. dat. mahākalpas), (in Hindū theology) a vast cycle of time (in Sanskrit, mahākalpa), corresponding to the life of Brahmā, which consists of a hundred years of which each day and night is usually said to consist of a kalpa or 4,320,000,000 mortal years; cf. kalpānth. At the end of each kalpa, there is a dissolution of all things, but Brahmā survives. At the end of a mahākalpa (mahākalpânta, or in Kāshmīrī mahākalpānth) Brahmā himself dies, and there is total dissolution.

f. (for gend., see W. 18), a place, position, situation; a district, quarter; a mansion, a palace (W. 18). -bāgay f. division of a tract of country by metes and bounds, division of a town into various specified quarters or districts, each part having a separate designation. ¶ mahala-khān (or -khāna) (or) (= محل خانہ) m. the inner part of a palace, a harem, seraglio (K. 977; H. viii, 3, 11 (both -khān)). dökhil-i-mahalakhāna, (of a woman) brought into, or made a member of, the harem (H. xii, 19).

m. a district, division, quarter (of a city or town), ward, parish (K.Pr. 236); in composition this word generally takes the form mahla, as in:--mahla-bôjᵘ a ward-partner, i.e. a friend of the same quarter of a town (u.w. ref. to the meeting of two such persons in some place far from home). -ganḍ m. unity of opinion, confederation, coalition amongst all the inhabitants of a ward. -wölⁱ m.pl. the inhabitants of a ward (spoken of as a whole group).

f. (sg. dat. mahālakshmiyĕ), i.q. lȧkhⁱmī (q.v.) or lakṣmī, N. of the goddess of fortune, the wife of Vishnu; identified by worshippers of Śiva with Dēvī (see dīvī), the wife of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 96).
f. rubbing in ointment, rubbing the affected part after applying ointment.
m. (sg. dat. mahāmantras), a great or efficacious charm, a powerful spell (cf. manthᵃr) (Śiv. 1449).
f. worldly illusion, which makes the material world appear really existent; the same personified as Śiva's energic power (Śiv. 60, 196, 530, 651, etc.).
f. (sg. dat. mahānavümᵘ̈), 'the great ninth,' the ninth lunar day of the light half of the month Öshid (in Sanskrit Āśvina = September-October), sacred to the goddess Durgā (L. 266, Maha Nowmi).

m. a man (El. mohanyú or mŏhnyu) (Gr.Gr. 58; Gr.M.; W. 18 mahaniu, 111 mahiniu; K.Pr. 30, 146, 156; H. x, 1, 4); a serving-man, a slave (K. 1163); man, mankind, the human species (Gr.M.); a person (man or woman; cf. nŏshĕ-mᵒ, a daughter-in-law person, s.v. nŏsh). ¶ mahanivⁱ-bal m. power owing to possessing a multitude of servants or slaves. -khyolᵘ m. a crowd of men (Gr.Gr. 152). -koṭᵘ m. the son of a slave. -rēmph f. a poor man, a poor miserable fellow (Gr.Gr. 163). -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who possesses many slaves or servants.
. In the sense of 'serving-man', mahanyuwᵘ often takes the form mahönyuwᵘ. Cf. sŏñⁱ-mⁱ, p. 924b, l. 36.
m. a great man, an eminent or distinguished person, (in a religious sense) a very holy person (Śiv. 743, 1773).

or mahārāza (q.v.) m. a great king, an independent king, a king (Gr.M.; L. 258; Śiv. 700, 1227, 1353, 1521; Rām. 145, 986; K. 438, 1121); a paramount king; used as a polite vocative interjection, Sir! (Gr.M.).
in maharājī wath f. a highway (El., who makes it m.). Cf. mahārāj.

m., i.q. mahārāj, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 39); (usually, in Kashmīr) a bridegroom (cf. mahārĕñ) (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 201; Śiv. 629, 726, 786, 840, 882, etc.); cf. nēthᵃr 1. -madun m. (in a theatrical performance) the actor who takes the part of a king or of a bridegroom. -motᵘ adj. (f. -müʦᵘ̈), a king-lunatic, one who (mad or sane) dresses himself in grand apparel, but wears the wrong ornaments on the wrong parts of his body.

f. a great queen, i.q. mahāröñᵘ̈, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 39); a bride, i.e. a girl during the days of the ceremonies preliminary to marriage, or shortly after marriage (cf. mahārāza) (Gr.Gr. 39; Gr.M.; L. 258, mahārāni; K.Pr. 130; Śiv. 1090-1, 1227; K. 28, 654, 684); cf. nēthᵃr 1. mahārĕñĕ möjᵘ̈ f. a bride-mother, i.e. a bride (as ab.) who is no longer a child (quasi, who is as old as her mother, or old enough to be the bridegroom's mother).
f. a great queen, the principal wife of a king; a queen in her own right; a bride = mahārĕñ (L. 258, mahārāni).
m. N. of a form of the god Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 152, 234, 1143).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. mahôrᵘ), to separate by rubbing with the hand lumps of particles (such as lumps of rice grains clotted together), to crumble (anything). mahôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mahörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), crumbled (by some one).
adj. c.g. very beautiful, very handsome (Rām. 1258).
m. (sg. dat. mahārishis), a great sage or saint (in Sanskrit maharṣiḥ) (Rām. 78, 1681).
f. the great Śakti, i.e. the energic power of Śiva (cf. shĕkhᵃth) (Śiv. 7, 1520).

m. (sg. dat. mahātmas; sg. nom. with indef. art. mahātmā, Śiv. 848, 870, 875), majesty, dignity; a treatise giving an account of the merits of a divinity or shrine (Śiv. 743, 848, 870, 875, 1282, 1754).
adj. c.g. one who possesses great discrimination.
f. great knowledge, the great knowledge, the knowledge of divine things (Śiv. 96, 1094, 1151).
m. a great hero, a mighty warrior (Rām. 1268); a title of Halᵃmotᵃ (Hanumān).
m. an idiom, phraseology, method of terminology, expression (Gr.M.).
m. a buffalo, another spelling of mū̃shᵘ, q.v.

m. greatness, glory, majesty (esp. one of the attributes of Śiva, as the container of all the fourteen worlds); the tale of a person's greatness, a full account of his glory (Śiv. 1166, 1503, 1628). mahimna-pār m. N. of a hymn in honour of Śiva, called in Sanskrit the mahimnaḥ stava (Śiv. 867).
adj. c.g. made firm, firm, stable, strong (H. xi, 9); strong, established, which cannot be abrogated (H. iv, 6).

m. soft plaster, dressing for wounds, ointment, salve. -gorᵘ m. an apothecary who makes his living by preparing ointments. -püṭᵘ̈ f. lint or cloth on which ointment is smeared for application to a wound, etc.
f. N. of a certain tīrtha or sacred bathing place in Kashmīr (Śiv. 1030, Rām. 249).
m. (amongst Muslims) a marriage portion settled upon the wife before marriage, dowry, jointure (L. 269, mehr).
f. a portion of a boat, situated behind the prow or in front of the stern (El.).
m. a kind of thin small worm or caterpillar, yellow and black in colour, which feeds on leaves. mạhȧrⁱ-dôwⁱ m. a kind of fine binding cord of twisted silver wire and silk (see dôwᵘ, p. 262a, l. 10).
adj. c.g. pure, simple, unnalloyed. -nĕnd f. the second weeding of a rice crop (L. 463, mahznind).
a document or petition attested by a number of witnesses laid before a judge (with the view of promoting a suit); a public attestation by a number of people.

m. (f. mahᵃladārĕñ), the head man of a district or parish, an officer in charge of a ward, an alderman; (in Kashmīr) the officer in charge of a division of a city, the ward-watchman, who guards the village by night, and sees that Government orders are carried out (K.Pr. 105). According to El. (s.v. mahallodár), his chief duty seems to be to act as a spy over the people. Sometimes women fill this post. Mahᵃladārs are generally heartily hated by the people, which is not to be wondered at. When a woman fills the post she is called by the f. term mahᵃladārĕñ, which, according to El., also means the wife of a mahᵃladār, but cf. mahᵃladār-bāy, bel. -bukurᵘ m. the gruffness of the ward-watchman; hence, arrogance, insolence, rudeness; cf. bukurᵘ, p. 102a, l. 43. -bāy f. the wife of a ward-watchman. -wān m. the office, or residence, of the ward-watchman.
f. the office or duties of a ward-watchman; conduct like that of a ward-watchman, rudeness, insolence, arrogance.
adj. c.g. one who is a confidant, one who is intimately acquainted (with a secret, dat.) (H. ii, 4).
m. slowness, inactivity, dullness, laziness (Gr.Gr. 140). Cf. mö̃ṭh.
see möl. mail-ṭang m. a kind of pear, Pyrus kumaonensis (El.), the beam-tree (Pyrus lanata, L. 74).

or mön m. a frog (the word is used outside Śrīnagar, El. mainah, i.e. maināh, with indef. art.; Gr.Gr. 22); cf. miñ 2. -phal m. Randia dumetorum (El.; L. 75, mani-phal, used medicinally as an emetic).
