or maināwatī f. N.P., N. of Mēnakā or Mēnā, wife of the Himâlaya and mother of Pārvatī. (mainā) (Śiv. 895, 1219, 1221, 1490); (maināwatī) (Śiv. 656, 691, 784, 881, 918, 1103, 1359).

adj. c.g. a little, a few (of any mass or group of persons or things) (El. manai, máne; W. 130, mönai). --kāla (or wakta) pĕṭha --  adv. from a short time, a short time ago, lately (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to diminish, lessen (El. máne k.). --sapadun -- m.inf. to diminish, grow less (El. máne s˚).

m. universal or general lamentations (on the occasion of some great public calamity). --tulun -- m.inf. (of a population, or crowd of people) to raise such lamentations. --wŏthun -- m.inf. such lamentations to rise.

m. Mahēśvara, one of the names of the god Śiva. Used in the following:--maĩshĕr-wörᵘ̈  f. Mahēśvara's garden, a garden or similar place where women assemble and dance with songs on the occasion of the Śiva-rātri and other festivals.

or möth (= میت) m. (sg. dat. maitas or mötas), a dead body, a corpse (El. mãt, dead; K.Pr. 139, sg. dat. mātas). möta-palav m. a dead man's clothes, the clothes formerly, in his lifetime, worn by one who is now dead.

m. (sg. dat. maitanas), the condition of dying, dying. --phērun -- m.inf. to become as if at the point of death (from fear, sorrow, or the like). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. the condition of becoming, as it were, at the point of death (from fear, sorrow, etc.) to occur.
according to L. 463, N. of a kind of rice, a good cropper with a red grain.

or mö̃z f. the Indian henna, Lawsonia inermis (El. mánz; K.Pr. 137, mã̄z). (From the powdered leaves of this plant is made a paste used by women to dye their hands and feet a reddish orange.) Cf. mazēṭh. ¶ maĩzi-atha m. a hand dyed with henna. -khŏr m.pl. feet dyed with henna. -kọ̆nḍᵘ m. a bowl for holding henna-dye. -nam m.pl. the nails (of the hands or feet) dyed with henna. -pōsh m. the flower of the henna-plant; N. of a certain plant, the flower of which is of a reddish orange colour. -rāth f. (sg. dat. röʦᵘ̈), a night on which henna is applied, i.e. a festive occasion [e.g. a marriage, on which occasion a bride's hands and feet are stained with henna, or an investment of a boy with the Brahminical thread (El. mánzirāt; L. 258 ff., mehnzrāt)].
(? spelling and gend.) a log harrow (L. 461).
m. an event, incident, circumstance, occurrence.
m. a council, assembly, congregation (El., Gr.M.).
m. the fruit or nuts of the Cupressus sempervirens or allied species (El.).
or (Gr.Gr. 147)mājyulᵘ adj. (f. mājijᵘ̈), apathetic through modesty, diffident, bashful, unpretending, shy (Gr.Gr. 147); (of a child) tied to his mother's apron-strings (Gr.Gr. 147).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. mỗjᵘ), to polish, scour, or rub clean a metal article (with polishing powder or the like) or (by extension) some non-metallic article (cf. kan mā̃jȧnⁱ, p. 447b, l. 2). mỗjᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mö̃jᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), polished, scoured, as ab.
the part of the body low down behind the pudenda, the anus, (often extended to mean the rectum) (El. mekad).
f. the bone behind the anus,? the coccyx.
m. a place (Śiv. 477, 1867; Rām. 523); a house, a dwelling-place, home (Śiv. 16, 1121; Rām. 272, 591, 1242, 1253, 1712, 1747).
m. an alligator, a crocodile. Cf. magar 2.
f. the sign Capricornus of the zodiac (Śiv. 477, Rām. 1276).
m. a box or case (esp. one of a circular oblong shape in which rolls of paper are carried); (in Kashmīr) a volume (El.).
m. N. of a celebrated linga or phallus sacred to Shiva (Śiva) (in Skt. makêśvara) (Rām. 941, 943, 951, 953).

m. (sg. dat. makas), an axe (Gr.Gr. 39; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 144; Śiv. 13, 1573, 1856); met. in comp. indicating violence, as in daga-makh, lit. an axe with a blow; hence, ultimate recourse to force (p. 193b, l. 12). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to apply an axe, to chop, chop at (a tree, etc.) (Rām. 1580; H. vii, 4, dat. of obj.); met. to cut down all round, destroy (e.g. a business, a man's character, etc.). --lagun -- m.inf. an axe to be applied, a tree to be cut down or round, or pruned with an axe; met. (of a work, condition, or business) to be cut down. ¶ maka-dan m. the handle or shaft, of an axe. -dār f. the edge of an axe. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), an axe-man, a man wielding an axe, or armed and threatening with an axe.

m. velvet (Śiv. 500, 576; Rām. 201); N. of a certain plant, described as having bunches of leaves, red on the upper surface and yellow at the back, probably a small fragrant kind of marigold. Cf. jāphurᵘ.
f. a kind of cake made of wheat-flour, butter, etc.
adj. c.g. of velvet, made of velvet; velvety, like velvet.

(also mạkᵃra) m. (sg. dat. mạkᵃras, similarly, with iẓāfat, mạkᵃr-i-zan, the wiles of women (H. x, 13)); plot, machination; duplicity, wile, artifice, imposture, pretence; cf. mạkᵃral. -wörᵘ̈ f. a coquette, a woman who out of coquetry pretends anger, etc. mạkᵃra wahārun m.inf. to exercise coquetry (as ab.), to coquet.
m. forgery (El., prob. another spelling of mạkhᵃr, q.v.).
or makur m. (sg. dat. makaris) (L.V. 18) or makaras (L.V. 31), a mirror.

f. (sg. dat. makāyĕ), Indian corn, maize, Zea mays (El. makãi; L. 330, makái). ¶ makāyi-ôṭᵘ m. maize flour. -düjᵘ̈ f. a plot on which maize is grown. -ḍongᵘ m. a stage erected on tall poles in a field of maize, on which the watcher sits. -ḍār m. a field in which maize is growing, or which has been prepared for maize sowing. -jāma m. the leafy covering of a maize-cob. -kã̄ḍ m. the stalk of a maize plant or (meton.) the whole plant. -kashᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the part of a maize-cob that carries the seeds, the non-edible part of a maize-cob. -pholᵘ m. a quantity or collection of maize seeds; a single maize seed. -tyū̃tᵘ m. (sg. dat. -tī˜tis), porridge of pounded maize. -ʦŏ̈ṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. ʦŏcĕ), a maize loaf, maize bread. -worᵘ m. a maize cake, or wide thick loaf of maize. -wüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -wacĕ), a maize-cob. -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. wāṭas), maize porridge, boiled coarsely-ground maize (W. 115, makaiwāt).
adj. c.g. coquet, one who simulates anger or the like. Cf. mạkhᵃr.

f. a small axe, a hatchet (El. makaz) (Gr.Gr. 39, 66; K.Pr. 70, 195 (makaz)); cf. makh. --wāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to ply a hatchet. ¶ makᵃʦi-dan m. the handle of an axe. -dạndᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the edge or point of a hatchet.

m. (sg. abl. mala 1), dirt, filth (Gr.Gr. 147; W. 110, 153; L.V. 31, 49; K.Pr. 10, 40, 237; Śiv. 1022, 1575; Rām. 1692); muck, mud, sediment (cf. nȧṭⁱ-mⁱ, s.v. noṭᵘ); ordure. -borutᵘ adj. (f. -barᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), full of dirt, dirty, filthy (Rām. 1517); cf. mala-borutᵘ, bel. -grāy f. wiping or brushing or rubbing off dirt. -hĕm f. a long smudge of dirt. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to wash off dirt; to evacuate, ease oneself, stool. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to put off dirt; met. to go out of mourning, to put off mourning garments. --khārun -- m.inf. to raise dirt, to raise an island or other piece of land by digging earth and piling it up. -kal m. an accumulation of dirt, dirt and the like (a jingle of mal). -kala m. a head full of dirt, hair (esp. a woman's) filled with accumulated dirt on an uncared-for head. --karun -- m. to ease oneself (in a regular manner), to go to one's daily stool. -kᵒtᵒ adj. (f. -kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), damp with dirt, i.e. dirtied, marked with dirt. -katorᵘ m. a filth sherd, a receptacle for ordure, a filth-pan. -katürᵘ̈ pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. the filth-pan to fall; met. to be discarded after being put to some humiliating or disgusting use. -katürᵘ̈ ʦhunüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to cast away the filth-pan; met. to abandon, discard, or expel some member of one's family on account of hatred. --ladun -- m.inf. to build dirt, to pile up an embankment, or the like. -liwan  f. (sg. dat. -livüñᵘ̈), a muck-spade, a kind of spade used for digging out mud from under water and piling it up on an embankment, island, or the like. -mās m. an intercalary month. -mösⁱ adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, an intercalary month. -môsᵘ adj. (f. -mösᵘ̈), one who performs the religious duties connected with an intercalary month. -phĕran m. a muck-coat, a kind of smock worn over one's clothes when employed on dirty work. -palav m. a bundle of dirty clothes (ready for the wash). -pāwun m.inf. to cause mud to fall, to dirty (e.g. new or clean clothes). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. dirt to fall, to become dirty (from use, etc.) (L.V. 18). -shrōʦh f. (sg. dat. shrōʦi), cleaning off filth, the act of washing the privities after evacuation. -sĕs f. a kind of skin disease described as a wide white mark or freckle. -sĕs pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. such a mark as ab. to appear. -sĕsal adj. c.g. freckled, marked with white spots, as ab. -tān m. the under supports of a house amid the dirt. --trāwun -- m.inf. to wash off dirt; to put off mourning garments, etc.; to go out of mourning (cf. phir mal, L. 263). -tᵃʦh f. (sg. dat. -tᵃʦhi), a dirt- rag, a clout for wiping off dirt. -tᵃʦh karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to wipe up after cleaning off dirt. -ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ f. dirt and charcoal; met. abuse. -ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. humiliation to be experienced from abuse. -ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to cause humiliation by abuse. -wôñᵘ m. dirty water, water which has been used for washing off dirt, washings; muddy water of a stream in flood. -wās m. a smock put on over the clothes to protect them from dirt. -waturᵘ m. a dirt-leaf, the covering leaves at the beginning and end of a book, a book-cover. -wāy m. a whiff of dirt; hence, an attack of disease, the first symptoms of disease; the last symptoms of disease before complete recovery. -wāy gaʦhun m.inf. the first symptoms of disease to occur; met. to be sulky, or inwardly angry, with one's people for a very slight cause. -züṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -zacĕ), an old valueless upper garment, worn over costly clothes to keep off the dirt. ¶ mala-borutᵘ adj. (f. -barᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), full of dirt, filthy; cf. mal-borutᵘ, ab. --byūṭhᵘ -- adj. (f. -bīṭhᵘ̈), settled from dirt, clear (e.g. water once turbid, from which the mud has settled at the bottom of the vessel). -dar m. a kind of white blister. -gōjĕ f.pl. kernels of filth; met. profitlessness, futility, fruitlessness, wasted labour, loss of the results of labour. -gōjĕ karañĕ f. pl. inf. to cause the loss of the results of labour, to render futile. -mᵃtrözᵃ f. a condition of ordure and urine; a heap or pile of ordure, etc.; cf. mᵃthᵃr; cf. -öz (i.e. -özᵘ̈) in Gr.Gr. 143. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), free from dirt, pure, clean, limpid. --wŏthun -- m.inf. to rise from dirt; met. to go out of mourning, to put off mourning garments. ¶ malas bĕhun m.inf. (of a bride) to sit indoors with her hair down for a week before the marriage (L. 268).

m. riches, money, property, wealth, possessions, merchandise, stock, goods, effects, estate (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 14, 48, 77, 123, 133, 216; YZ. 233, 236, 401; Śiv. 430, 703; Rām. 610; H. i, 9; iii, 1; viii, 9); cargo (of a ship) (Gr.M.). ¶ māl-ĕ-muft مال مفت m. property by gift (K.Pr. 133). ¶ māla-khāv m. one who commits breach of trust, a fraudulent trustee. -motᵘ or (K.Pr. 133) -mast adj. (f. -müʦᵘ̈), 'property-mad,' one who is drunk with wealth, a Crœsus, very wealthy; (as subst., m.) extreme passion for property. -poʦᵘ m. goods-trust, trusting a person with the collection or accumulation of property (e.g. through previous experience of his honesty). -paʦh f. (sg. dat. -paʦi), credit given to a person, or general trust in a person, on account of his known wealth; confidence in the safety of property entrusted to any person. -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), rich in property, full of property; producing much property, very profitable. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a rich person, rich.

(sg. abl. mala 2), m. the cheek and temple, the hemi-cranium, used in the following:-- mala-goḍᵘ m. the bone of the top of the skull, from the forehead to the nape of the neck. Cf. gŏḍ, p. 277a, l. 9.

f. a garland, wreath, chaplet, a necklace (Gr.Gr. 46, 65; K.Pr. 70; Śiv. 2, 88, 163, 194, 266, etc.; Rām. 489, 1025, 1090, etc.; K. 60, 97, 183, 423, 583, 1077); a rosary, chain; a row, a line (cf. danda-māla, p. 224b, l. 45); a row of mountain tops, a sierra (Śiv. 1684, 1707); met. a beautiful woman (Śiv. 436, 573; Rām. 1194). ¶ māla-dŏgunᵘ m. a necklace or garland of two ropes, a double-rowed necklace. -ganḍ m. (in a rosary) the knot between each bead (cf. māli-ganḍ, bel.); the act of stringing a necklace or garland. -trọ̆ṭᵘ m. a garland-necklace, the whole group of such (of many strands) worn at one time (K. 85). ¶ māli-ganḍ m. (in a rosary) the knot between each bead (cf. māla-ganḍ, ab.). -pholᵘ m. a single bead of a rosary. -pan m. the thread of a rosary.
for mala 4 in mal-guzār m. a graveyard (El.).
or mālal m. one who commits incest with his own mother or stepmother.

f., i.q. māl 2, being the borrowed Sanskrit form of the word. Cf. dīpa-mālā, a row of lights; hence, the Dīwālī festival (p. 232b, l. 31), and jamjam-mālā (p. 347a, l. 12) (Śiv. 1171, 1174, 1314, 1436, 1489).

m. a seaman, sailor, mariner; esp. a boatman, waterman (a polite term instead of hönzᵘ̈, q.v.). -bāy f. a boatman's wife. -koṭᵘ 1 m. a boatman's son (used as a term of commendation), a real or good son of a boatman (cf. Gr.Gr. 132).

m. the leader of prayer in a Musalmān mosque, a mullā (W. 135, mallạ; K.Pr. (mallah) 106, 134, 252; H. vi, 13); a Musalmān who superintends the religious rites on the occasion of births, marriages or deaths, generally a teacher or schoolmaster; a gravedigger (El.). -bã̄g ملا بانگ f. the call to Musalmān matins (El. m.). -bã̄gi adv. at day dawn (El.). -ciñ f. the Mullā's saucer, a present of food given to a Mullā by his client. -khōsh m. a gravedigger (El.). -koṭᵘ 2 m. a Mullā's son (used as a term of commendation), a real or good son of a Mullā (cf. Gr.Gr. 132). -tabᵃc f., i.q. -ciñ, ab. -wālawöshⁱ f. a Mullā's net, i.e. fear of the Mullā's disapproval, fear of what he will say.
m. a base man (K.Pr. 9, where it is opposed to alagaḍi, a great man).
m. (sg. dat. malakas), an angel (H. iv, 2).

m. weariness, fatigue, languor, onnui; dejection, sadness, melancholy (YZ. 20, Śiv. 425); affliction, grief, anguish; vexation, displeasure, estrangement (Śiv. 661; Rām. 762, 1574). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. estrangement, etc., to occur.
adj. c.g. heaped, brimful (Śiv. 1213); full, replete, abundant.
f. (sg. dat. malāmüʦᵘ̈), reproof, rebuke, censure, reproach, accusation, reviling. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to rebuke.
m. in the following:--mālamuhⁱ- ʦū̃ṭᵘ  m. a kind of wild apple, pink in colour, with a sub-acid sweet flavour, good for cooking (L. 350, malmu, where it is described as green).
m. a kind of Musalmān darwēsh, who lets the hair of his head grow to its full length, and leaves it uncombed and dishevelled; met. any ugly terrifying fellow, tall, long-armed and long-legged.
f. the conduct or condition of a terrifying-looking fellow.
m. in gᵃsa-malawāy (p. 306a, l. 14), i.q. mal-wāy, q.v., p. 564a, l. 46.
n.ag. (f. malavüñᵘ̈), one who rubs (anything on to anything) (Śiv. 1189).
f. longing (for), hankering, yearning. --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to dispel a longing, to quench a yearning. --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a yearning to depart, a longing to be dispelled.
adj. c.g. producing longing, alluring, fascinating, attractive, seducing.
also spelt malīʦ (El.) m. (sg. dat. malēchas), (amongst Hindūs) an outcast, a man of irreligious or impure conduct.
f. the condition or conduct of an outcast.

interj. (prop. voc. of môlᵘ, q.v.), O Father!; hence (as a polite form of address) Sir! Good Sir! (L.V. 91). With the interjection ha prefixed we get ha māli, Good Sir, which L.V. 107, by a pun, equates with hamāli, O burden-bearer (cf. hamāl); so hā māli (K.Pr. 9, 74, 242).
m. a kind of fine woollen cloth (made of lamb's-wool). -gar مالیدہ گر m. a washer of woollen cloth (El.).

m. (sg. dat. malikas), a king; a title of honour or respect (cf. bŏṭa-mᵒ, p. 138b, l. 20) (used sarcastically in the Voc. K.Pr. 191); (in Kashmīr) a way-warden, a man whose duty it is to keep mountain passes and forest roads clear, and to watch and help travellers on them.
m. a strong man, a hero, athlete, wrestler, boxer (L.V. 24, K. 434).
f. (sg. dat. malölë˘ʦᵘ̈), i.q. malāla, q.v.
adj. (f. malüʦᵘ̈), dirty, filthy, grimy; (as subst., m.) dung, filth (El., who also spells the word múlat).
m. (properly angels, the plural of the Arabic ملک, but in Kāshmīrī) an angel, a guardian angel.
f. in the following:--malāyĕ karañĕ f.pl.inf. to express sorrow with lamentations and beatings of the breast and other parts of the body.
adj. c.g. having the light-grey colour of natural pashmīna woollen cloth; as subst., pashmīna or other similar cloth of this colour.
m. (sg. dat. malakas), a wave (of water) (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 50, malḵẖ) (cf. pā̃-mᵒ, s.v. pôñᵘ).
adj. c.g. fatigued, tired, weary; sick, indisposed; grieved, sad, dejected. --karun -- m.inf. to offend (El.).

(El., K.Pr.), mālūm معلوم, môlum (El., Gr.M., Śiv. 1283) or môlūm adj. c.g. known (Śiv. 1283; Rām. 356, 380, 447, 732, 1533); clear, evident, certain, obvious, apparent. --karun -- m.inf. to know, understand (Rām. 806, 1347); to discover, find out, ascertain (El., Rām. 1384); to perceive, behold, recognize; to deem, suppose. --sapanun -- m.inf. to become known (to), to be discovered (K.Pr. 206); to appear, seem, be deemed, supposed; to learn (El.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. molᵘ; 2 p.p. majyōv or malyōv), to rub, anoint, shampoo (K. 942, 956); to rub (something on to a person) (YZ. 19, 234; Śiv. 503, 529, 593, 815-16, etc.; Rām. 389, 1537; K. 425, 973, 976). molᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. müjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ or mülᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), rubbed, anointed; smudged (with dust, dirt, etc.).
f. a large pot of earthenware (El. malir and mallar).
adj. (f. maliñᵘ̈), dirty, filthy, grimy (Gr.Gr. 147, Śiv. 752).

or mölyunᵘ m. the original home of a married woman, the house of a man's father-in-law (L. 270, 458; K.Pr. 158; Śiv. 82, 83; Rām. 195, 263, 764, 1035, 1620; K. 856). ¶ mālinⁱ-büḍⁱ f. a woman whose blood-relations are in a higher rank of life, or more wealthy, than those of her husband. -bajĕr  m. the fact or state of the higher rank or greater wealth of a married woman's relations, as compared with those of her husband. -böʦᵘ̈  m. a member of a married woman's family, one of her blood-relations. -dorᵘ  m. the family of a married woman, i.e. the total of her blood-relations. -gara m. a married woman's home, i.e. her father's house, where she was born. -vĕʦhay f. (of a married woman) non-existence of blood-relations. ¶ mālinyukᵘ adj. (f. mālinicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the family of a married woman's blood-relations (Rām. 768); the home of this family.
f. (sg. dat. mạlᵃrüñᵃ), rubbing down, rubbing together (e.g. medicaments in making an ointment or the like).

m. furbishing, giving an outward appearance of cleanness to a garment, ornament, etc., by the application of varnish, lacquer, or the like. --karun -- m.inf. to do furbishing; met. to show hospitality or politeness (esp. to a person unworthy of it).
m. dirtiness, uncleanness, filthiness, griminess; met. cf. man-mᵒ, p. 572a, l. 7.
adj. (f. -khöñᵘ̈), a much-petted child, a much-loved child, a best-loved child, a spoilt child (Rām. 286, 1034, 1125).
m. the two breasts of a woman, or a pair of udders or dugs of a female beast. Cf. mama and mŏm.

m. a maternal uncle (his wife is māmañ, q.v.) (K.Pr. 135, 251; K. 454). ¶ māma-bĕnathᵃr m.pl. a maternal uncle and his sister's son, i.e. a man and his maternal uncle, when spoken of together. -hihur m. an uncle-in-law, the brother of the mother of a husband or wife, i.e., as regards the husband, his wife's maternal uncle; as regards the wife, her husband's maternal uncle (K.Pr. 135). -shĕkur m. one who acts, walks, or speaks like a eunuch.
m. (a polite name for) the breast of a woman or udder or dug of a female beast (esp. a single breast or dug); cf. mam and mŏm. -ṭang m. a kind of pear (L. 350).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. mamalyōv), to become motionless, without movement (from fear, agitation, or the like); (of a limb) to go to sleep, to become as it were paralysed, to become benumbed; cf. mamanun. mamalyō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (mamalyē-müʦᵘ̈), become motionless, benumbed, paralysed, as ab.
f. the wife of a maternal uncle (cf. mām) (K. 454).
m. motionlessness, paralysis (from fear, agitation, disease, or the like) (cf. nĕta-mᵒ, s.v. nĕth 2).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. mamanyōv), to become motionless, paralysed, stupefied, benumbed (from fear, agitation, or the like); cf. mamalun. --aʦun -- m.inf. such motionlessness, as ab., to overtake a person. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. such motionlessness, as ab., to occur (to a person). ¶ mamanyō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. mamanyē-müʦᵘ̈), become motionless, as ab., stupefied, stunned; paralysed (of a limb).
or māms m. flesh (L.V. 81); mutton (El.). Cf. mās 2 and māz.
f. regarding as 'mine', a confident sense of ownership; pride, arrogance, self-sufficiency (Śiv. 18, 110, 339, 1313, 1572).

adj. (f. māmatᵃr or māmatᵘ̈rᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a maternal uncle (mām), used in the following, and other similar, compounds expressing relationship: --bēma -- m. a sister's husband on the side of the maternal uncle, i.e. the husband of the daughter of a maternal uncle, the husband of a cousin on the mother's side. --bôyᵘ -- m. a brother on the side of a maternal uncle, i.e. a first cousin (male) on the mother's side (Gr.Gr. 132). ¶ māmatᵘ̈rᵘ̈ (or māmatᵃr) bȧyⁱ-(or böyⁱ-)kākañ   f. the wife of a first cousin on the mother's side (Gr.Gr. 133). --bĕñĕ -- f. a first cousin (female) on the mother's side (Gr.Gr. 133). --rag -- f. relationship on the side of the maternal uncle. Cf. piturᵘ.
adj. (f. mamüñᵘ̈), motionless, paralysed, stupefied, benumbed (cf. nĕta-mᵒ, s.v. nĕth 2).

m. (sg. abl. mana 1), the mind (considered as the seat of perception and passions) (Gr.M.; L.V. 5, 12, 17, 18, 23, 27, etc.; K.Pr. 57; Śiv. 26, 49, 57, 163, etc.; Rām. 6, 17, 47, 50, etc.; K. 470, 472; H. vi, 6, where the word is fem.); intellect, intelligence, understanding (Rām. 74, 557, 847, etc.; K. 585); the heart, soul, spirit (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 57; Rām. 32, 54, 58, 348, 397, 565, etc.; K. 94, 262, 287, 800, 804, etc.); character, disposition, mood, temper (Gr.M.; K. 82, 860, etc.). -khạndurᵘ (sg. dat. -khạndᵃras), agitation of mind, emotion; (as adj.) agitated in mind, overcome by emotion. -khạndᵃrĕr m. agitation of mind, emotion. -kruh m. acridity of mind, i.e. disgust, aversion, of the mind. --lagun -- m.inf. the mind to be fixed (on, dat.); to have the heart or affections set (upon, dat.), to fall in love (with, dat.) (K. 266, 716, 800); to take delight (in, dat.). --lāgun -- m.inf. to apply the mind (Gr.M.). -mēchĕr m. sweetness of mind, i.e. affection felt towards a person, a feeling of affection; participation of two persons in a common work, induced by mutual affection. -mēl union of hearts; mutually affectionate participation of two persons in some work. -malⁱñār m. blackness of heart, i.e. estrangement, alienation, quarrelling between friends. -myulᵘ m. sympathy, mutual affection, being of one mind. --phērun -- m.inf. the mind to become reversed (quasi, to vomit), the mind to be changed and to revert to its previous opinion, recantation or revokement to occur. --phirun -- m.inf. to change one's own or another person's mind (Rām. 148). -phyurᵘ m. change of mind. -prasand (for من پسند, with conflation with the Skt. prasanna, Kāshmīrī prasan), adj. c.g. comfortable (El.); with karun m.inf. to gladden; with sapadun m.inf. to rejoice. --raṭun -- m.inf. to seize the mind, to bring it under subjection (L.V. 55, K. 500). -srọ̆dᵘ or -srŏzar m. mind in common, unanimity, common consent, union of hearts, sympathetic association or participation. ¶ mana-ganḍ m. a knot on the mind, concealment of thoughts. -ganḍal adj. c.g. one who conceals his thoughts. -grāy f. agitation of the mind. -kūmal adj. c.g. kind, gentle-hearted (El.). -krūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -krūṭhᵘ̈), hard-hearted, stony-hearted. -logᵘ m. devotion of the mind or heart (to); as adj., appealing to the mind, heart-entrancing, fascinating. -poʦᵘ m. trust of the mind, confidence (in), faith (in), belief (in). -paʦh f. implicit trust (in); firm faith (in a religious sense). -shọ̆dᵘ adj. (f. -shö̆zᵘ̈), clean-hearted, pure-hearted, of an honest and equable temper. -sath f. (sg. dat. -süʦᵘ̈), freedom from anxiety. -sṻty adv. cordially (El.). -sôwᵘ  adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), firm-minded, dispassionate, stoical; persevering, tenacious of purpose, unfaltering, persisting. -sôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. -sövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), thrown away or abandoned in consequence of a vow (e.g. a Brahminy bull let loose or an oblation scattered by Hindūs upon water). -wāz adj. c.g. courageous; intrepid, undismayed by evil fortune, imperturbable. ¶ mani bĕhun m.inf. to agree or become of one mind (as to aim, wish, etc.). --bĕhanāwun -- m.inf. to bring a person to agreement. --byūṭhᵘ -- 1 p.p. (f. -bīṭhᵘ̈), come to agreement, come to an understanding, assenting, acquiescent. -kāman or -kāmanā f. the desire of one's heart, a heartfelt longing (K. 339, 596). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain in the mind, to be kept in remembrance, to be ever carried in the memory; to be kept secret in the mind. ¶ manukᵘ dŏkh m. remorse (El.). ¶ manas bĕhun m.inf. to agree (to), assent. --karun -- m.inf. to remember, call to mind. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain in the mind, be kept secret. --thawun -- m.inf. to put by into the mind, to keep in one's memory, to bear perpetually in mind, never to forget.

m. honour, respect, reverence, paying honour (to) (Gr.Gr. 137; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1071; K. 90, 1130); dignity, rank, high reputation, respectability (L.V. 24; K. 455, 670, 1071); size, extent, magnitude (as a special attribute) (K. 837). --karun -- m.inf. to pay honour (to), show great respect (to), treat with honour (K. 133, 401, 534, 715, 848, 900, 1021); to have self-respect (K.Pr. 117); to rival (another person) (Śiv. 432; Rām. 530; K. 852, 1171). --raṭun -- m.inf. to keep up one's dignity, to hold one's head high, to show no sign of humiliation (even when asking for necessary help). ¶ māna-hān f. (sg. dat. -höñᵘ̈), loss of honour, dishonour, disgrace, humiliation; cf. mānas-hān (K. 797). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without honour, unrespected; (of an occupation) producing dishonour, degrading, derogatory. -sān adv. with great deference, with great respect. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), respected, highly esteemed, venerated; (of an occupation) producing respect, dignified, honourable. -wālay f. contumely, indignity, insult, dishonour. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), full of honour, full of self-respect (Gr.Gr. 137); (of an occupation or office) earning respect, dignified, honourable. ¶ mānukᵘ adj. (f. mānücᵘ̈), (properly gen. sing.) respected, highly esteemed, greatly respected; (of an occupation or office) producing honour, dignified, honourable.
m. (sg. abl. mana 2), a certain weight, equivalent to forty seers, a maund (K.Pr. 12, 76, 80, 101, 196; Śiv. 1285).

m. a suffix used with any numeral except one, two, four, or multiples of four, indicating one and a half seers (or three pounds). Thus tra-man, three times one and a half seers or four and a half seers; pānʦh-man, five times one and a half seers or seven and a half seers; shĕ-man, six times one and a half seers or nine seers; sath-man, seven times one and a half seers or ten and a half seers; nav-man, nine times one and a half seers or thirteen and a half seers, and so on. But a single one and a half seer is manoṭᵘ, q.v.; twice one and a half seers, or three seers, is pānzuwᵘ; four times one and a half seers, or six seers, is trakh, q.v.; eight times one and a half seers, or twelve seers, is zᵃ-trakh, or two trakh; twelve times one and a half seers, or eighteen seers, is tra-trakh, or three trakh, and so on for further multiples of four.
or (Śiv. 1794) manāh m. forbidding, inhibiting; prohibition, prevention (Gr.M., Śiv. 1794); --karun -- m.inf. to forbid.
adj. c.g. much, in great degree, abundant.
in mana-wôñᵘ m. whey, the liquid of curds.

m. the act of thinking or consideration, meditating or reflecting (upon); thought, reflection, study (Śiv. 1001, 1792). -māl f. a kind of jewelled garland bound on the head of a bride in a wedding ceremony (Śiv. 1204).

f. (sg. dat. manüñᵘ̈), a kind of kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈, or portable brazier, used mainly by boatmen. It is made entirely of pottery within and without, and is not covered with wicker-work. It is carried about under the clothes for warmth (W. 124, K.Pr. 129) (cf. nāra-mᵒ, s.v. nār). ¶ manạñĕ-tīl dazun m.inf. the oil of a brazier to burn or blaze up (and burn the body); met. to become utterly involved in calamity. -tīl zālun m.inf. to set on fire the oil in a brazier (as ab.); to involve a person in utter calamity.
f. honouring, respecting. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show respect (to), pay reverence (to) (K. 722).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. mananôwᵘ), to cause to agree to; to persuade, appease, console, soothe (Śiv. 24, 1634, 1786; Rām. 1525, 1636, 1676, 1691, 1731). mananôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mananövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), appeased, soothed.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mānanôwᵘ), to cause to be honoured (Śiv. 1211).
or mönind prep. like, resembling, after the likeness of; bē-mānand, incomparable (Śiv. 775); mönind-ĕ-bahar = مآنندِ بحر, like the sea, like a river (K.Pr. 64).
f. an honoured woman, i.e. a true, faithful, and loving wife (Śiv. 668).
m., i.q. man 1, mind, the seat or faculty of reason and feeling, the thinking faculty, the heart, soul (L.V. 2); the faculty of imagination (L.V. 27).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. manasôwᵘ), to dedicate anything (with appropriate religious ceremonies, and the recital of proper texts); to make a solemn (promise, vow, etc.) (Rām. 627).

m. perfect perception, full consciousness (of pleasure, pain, etc.), used in the following:--manaskār rōzun m.inf. to devote one's attention exclusively to some object or work; the attention to be devoted exclusively, as ab.
f. extreme respect, great reverence shown to a superior or great honour shown by a superior to an inferior (K. 906).
f. (manüʦᵘ̈), acknowledgment, assent; faith, trust (Rām. 46); promise, vow; desire, intention. Cf. mānath.
f. (sg. dat. mānüʦᵘ̈), belief, religious belief. Cf. manath.
f. (sg. dat. manāvüʦᵘ̈), persuading a giver through a third person (to give or do something). Cf. manāwun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. manowᵘ), to calm, appease (Śiv. 160). manowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. manüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), appeased.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. manôwᵘ), to cause (through a third person) another person to agree (to a course of conduct, esp. to give something), to persuade a person (through another) to give something. manôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. manövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to agree (by a third person), as ab.
n.ag. (f. mānavüñᵘ̈), one who honours or respects (Śiv. 1194); one who has full faith (in a god, a spiritual teacher, a religion, or the like); one who is persuaded (to agree).
adj. c.g. slow, tardy, inactive, lazy (Gr.M.). Cf. mondᵘ.

f. (sg. dat. mandachi), modesty, bashfulness, shame (Gr.Gr. 125, 137; Gr.M.; W. 114; K.Pr. 4; Śiv. 871, 884; K. 662, 1141). --kāsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to remove modesty, to cure (a person's) modesty. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. bashfulness to attack (a person). --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. bashfulness to rise (i.e. to depart). ¶ mandacha-buthᵘ m. bashfulness-faced, shamefaced. -vĕʦar m. natural shamefacedness, born modesty. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), full of native modesty, bashful, of modest disposition (Gr.Gr. 137, Gr.M.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. mandachôwᵘ), to make (a person) ashamed, to put to shame, to confuse (Gr.Gr. 171; K.Pr. 16, 119, 259; YZ. 23, 466; Śiv. 22, 73, 89, 124, 225, 525, etc.; Rām. 292, 347, 364, 386, 764, etc.). ¶ mandachāwan-küṭᵘ̈  f. a daughter, etc., who puts (respectable) parents, etc., to shame. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas; f. -küṭᵘ̈, ab.), a son (or other youth) who puts his (respectable) parents (or other respectable people) to shame. ¶ mandachôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (manachövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), put to shame (e.g. of a respectable person put to shame by public abuse, or by a disreputable child), disgraced.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. mandachyōv, also written mandachōv), to become bashful, to become shamefaced, to become ashamed, feel shame, be abashed (Gr.Gr. 125, 171; K.Pr. 4, 26, 59, 135; Śiv. 354, 489, 839, 884, 886, 1288; Rām. 1241, 1773; K. 566, 661, 664, 675, 686, 721, 775, 801, 1134, 1143). mandachō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. mandachē-müʦᵘ̈), ashamed, feeling shamefaced.
m. the Sanskrit form of manḍul, q.v., used in religious terms such as dwādashānta- manḍal, p. 262b, l. 15 (L.V. 33, Śiv. 1656).

m. (properly the same as manḍal 1), a circular disk (i.q. manḍul) (L.V. 75); a circular tract of ground; hence, a territory or province (approximately circular in form) ruled by a single king (Śiv. 1539, 1823).
m. shaving off of the beard and moustache (as is done by Hindūs at sacred bathing places, on the death of a parent, or in certain ceremonies of initiation).
m. a room, a chamber. This is the word in use towards Bārāmūla (El.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mandanôwᵘ), to cause to churn; to cause to be churned, to churn (Śiv. 855, n.ag.); to spill (tr., El.). Cf. mandun.
m. (sg. dat. manḍapas), a hall for ceremonial occasions (such as sacrifices, public meetings, and the like) (K. 1015).

or mandĕr or mandir m. a temple, a pagoda (Śiv. 21, 868, 1178, 1181, 1731, 1747); a palace (K. 810-11, 1045, 1115, mandar). mandĕr-brôhmun m. (sg. dat. -bröhmanas), a temple-Brāhmaṇa (who officiates at sacrifices and other rites). -bröhmüñᵘ̈ f. a temple-Brāhmaṇa woman (who performs ceremonies, etc.); the wife of a temple-Brāhmaṇa.
m. a kind of house found in forest villages. Cf. gana-manḍav, p. 287b, l. 32.
f. wages for cleaning cloth by kneading it (cf. manḍun).
mandiñ, mandiñukᵘ, mandiñĕn, mandiñĕs, see mandyuñᵘ.
f. an exchange, a place where merchants meet to transact business (Gr.M.).
m. a kind of long fine woollen turban or turban cloth, woven with silk and gold thread.
m. the person in charge of a temple, and responsible for its management.

adj. (f. mandüchᵘ̈), ashamed, become bashful (K. 328). -motᵘ adj. (f. mandüchᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to feel bashfulness, put out of countenance, abashed (Rām. 886, 1468); one who is stopped (from making a request or the like) by bashfulness, abashed.

f. N. of the wife of the demon Rāvaṇa. According to the Skt. Adbhuta Rāmāyaṇa, she was also the mother of Sītā, having become accidentally pregnant of her, in Rāvaṇa's absence, by drinking milk mixed with the blood of certain Ṛṣis. See JRAS. for 1921, p. 422. There is nothing like this in the Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa (Rām. 46, 422, 430, 665, 964, etc.).
f. a large masonry building, a palace (Rām. 1784).
f. the inner fleshy part of the thigh (El.); the rump, buttocks (K.Pr. 49); cf. mandul, of which this is the fem. mandajĕ-horᵘ m. the two thighs, the thighs (looked upon as a pair).
f. a number of people sitting in a circle; bĕhun manḍüjᵘ̈ karith, to sit in a circle (Gr.M.); f. of manḍul, q.v.
m. (sg. dat. mānḍakas), N. of a particular musical air (in Skt. maṇḍaka) (Śiv. 1827, where the comm. translates the word by 'breath').

m. (sg. dat. mandalas), the hip, thigh; the rump, buttocks (K.Pr. 166, 208). Cf. mandüjᵘ̈ and maĩshĕ-mᵒ, s.v. mǖ̃shⁱ. ¶ mandal-bachĕ f.pl. the edges of the thighs. -gạkhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. rubbing the ground with the buttocks. -horᵘ m. the buttocks (spoken of as a pair). -vyoṭhᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ṭhᵘ̈), fat-buttocked.

or manḍulᵘ m. (sg. dat. manḍalas), a circle (Śiv. 128, a circle of dancers) (Śiv. 1325, 1390; K. 294); a circular piece of ground on which people meet; the orbit of a heavenly body (Śiv. 198, 1663); a circle of pictures of the gods in the hall of sacrifices (Śiv. 960); a picture of the orb of the sun painted in the houses of Brāhmaṇas of Kashmīr on the seventh lunar day of the bright half of the month of Hār (Skt. Āṣāḍha) (June-July). bū-manḍul, the circuit of the earth, the whole earth, the terrestrial globe (K. 13, 17); ranga-manḍul, an arena (K. 433); rāsa-manḍul, the circular dance of Krishna (Kṛṣṇa) and the herdmaidens of Gōkula (K. 293); yĕgña-manḍul, a sacrificial arena, the hallowed ground on which a sacrifice is being held (K. 305). --shĕhalun -- m.inf. cooling rain after a long season of heat to occur. ¶ manḍȧlⁱ-brôhmun m.inf. the Brāhmaṇa who paints the above pictures in the hall of sacrifice. -masāl m. the powdered paints used in making the above pictures. Cf. masāla.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. mondᵘ; 2 p.p. manzōv), to churn, beat up (a liquid) (K.Pr. 224; Śiv. 1461, 1838, 1869; K. 161); to spill (intr., El.); met. to explain thoroughly a long and intricate book or other subject (quasi, to extract its butter, or essence, by churning) (Śiv. 49). mondᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. münzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), churned; thoroughly explained, as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. monḍᵘ; 2 p.p. manjyōv), to adorn (a woman or child with fine clothes, ornaments, etc.), to bedizen, deck, bedeck; to anoint, rub (El.); to tread, trample down (El.); esp. to wash woollen cloth (by kneading it with the feet in a trough, with soap, etc., and water) (K.Pr. 174). Cf. mã̄ḍun. ¶ manḍan 3 in manḍan-gar or manḍan-gorᵘ m. (f. -gürᵘ̈), a professional cleaner of woollen cloth or of woollen garments, as ab. (his wages are manḍawañ, q.v.) (Gr.Gr. 149). manḍan-gar-bāy or manḍan-gȧrⁱ-bāy f. the wife of such a cleaner. manḍan-garī f. the profession of washing woollen goods, as ab. -wŏkhul m. (sg. dat. wŏkhalas), the trough in which such woollen goods are trodden. ¶ monḍᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (münḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, sg. dat. manjĕ-maʦĕ), adorned, bedecked; (of woollen objects) cleaned, as ab.
f. a ball of butter (used either --˚, compounded with a word meaning 'butter', or alone).

m. (sg. dat. mandiñĕs), midday (El. mandain). ¶ mandĕñ or mandiñ adv. at midday (K.Pr. 176, mandĕni; 193, 228, mandini). -gürᵘ̈ f. the midday hour. -gaṭa f. darkness at midday; met. misgovernment, misrule, maladministration (with its accompanying calamities); unduly ignoring, turning the cold shoulder (to a person). -ṭhag m. a midday robber, an open swindler, swindling a person before his very eyes. -ʦūr f. a midday thief, a thief who steals by day, a thief who steals in the presence of his victim. ¶ mandĕñukᵘ or mandiñukᵘ adj. (f. mandiñücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, midday. ¶ mandĕñĕn or mandiñĕn adv. at midday (Gr.Gr. 157; K.Pr. 66; YZ. 127, 350; Śiv. 332, 351, 1756; Rām. 1023, 1145). -bögⁱ or -bögin adv. at about midday. ¶ mandĕñĕs or mandiñĕs adv. at midday. -bögⁱ or -bögin adv. at about midday.
m. an obstacle, hindrance (Gr.M. mönī); --karun -- (El. mána karun) m.inf. to forbid. Cf. manā 1.
m. meaning, intended sense, intent, signification (K.Pr. 30; H. iii, 4, 5; vi, 14; vii, 27, 28); the meaning of an action, object, purpose, intention (Rām. 1187).

f. a demand, begging, request for something (Gr.Gr. 125; Rām. 610; K. 489; H. xi, 16). --āsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. begging to come into existence, general asking for something to occur, universal demand for something on account of its scarcity or rarity. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of something hitherto disregarded or made little account of) a sudden and general demand or inquiry for anything to occur. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a demand (for anything) to come from various distant places. ¶ manga-mang f. continually or frequently asking for something. -mang karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to ask frequently for something (esp. for food) (W. 144, K.Pr. 135).
in hanga-manga, hanga ta manga, see hanga, p. 339a, l. 26.

m. happiness, good luck, felicity; a blessing, benediction, expression of good wishes, auspiciousness (Śiv. 1186, 1745); an auspicious ceremony (e.g. the festival on recovery from sickness); the planet Mars (El.). -wār m. Tuesday.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. manganôwᵘ), to cause to be asked for, to get someone to ask for; to send for, cause to be brought to one (YZ. 497; Śiv. 675; Rām. 263, 274, 593; K. 1034; H. vi, 16; xi, 8); to claim (El.).
m. an adopted son. --anun -- m.inf. to adopt (so-and-so) as a son. ¶ mangatukᵘ adj. (f. mangatücᵘ̈), one who has been adopted, an adopted son or daughter.
f. the profession of begging, mendicancy.
m. (his wife is mangathyārĕñ, but a female beggar is maṅgathyörᵘ̈), a professional beggar, one who lives by mendicancy.
n.ag. (f. maṅgavüñᵘ̈), one who begs or asks for something; a beggar, mendicant (K.Pr. 135, K. 992).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. mongᵘ, f. münjᵘ̈ (K. 488, 588, 718); 2 p.p. manjyōv), to ask for, request, demand, beg, solicit, entreat, crave (Gr.Gr. 125, 129; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 25, 31, 56, 105, 136, 150; YZ. 541; Śiv. 308-10, 707, 753, 1173, etc.; Rām. 63, 149-52, 612, etc.; K. 67, 142, 268, 278, 306, 423, etc.; H. xi, 14; xii, 4, 5, 7, 10, 11, 14, 15, 18, 19); to ask (a person to approach), to call up (a person to oneself) (K. 374, 996). hisāb mangun, to call for (a person's) account, to call a reckoning (K.Pr. 246). --lāyĕkh -- adj. c.g. fit to be asked for (e.g. owing to the known liberality of the giver, its abundance, or desirability). --tagun -- m.inf. to know how to ask for, to be skilled in begging for something desired; to intend to get something asked for. ¶ mongᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. münjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), asked for, demanded (Rām. 592); asked, entreated (for something) (K. 26). ¶ mangan-bāna m. a vessel of asking, i.e. a person suitable for being asked, or suitable for asking. -buthᵘ m. a face for asking, audacity in asking, barefaced begging, the conduct of a sturdy beggar. -hār adj. c.g. worthy of being asked for. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), an asker, a beggar. ¶ maṅganī impers. fut. part., c.g. (of a thing) about or fit to be asked for; (of a person) about or fit to be asked from. ¶ mangith nyunᵘ, m.inf. to ask for and get, to receive on demand. kūrᵘ̈ mangith niñᵘ̈, to take and marry a girl (K.Pr. 83).
in manira-dāg m. Aconitum sp. (L. 74, used to make a hair-wash).
m. a snake-stone, a certain stone which is believed to have the power of extracting the poison from a snake's bite.
f. a charcoal brazier, a chafing-dish.

f. (sg. dat. mānmöñᵘ̈), mutual emulation, mutual competition, mutual out-vying (among several persons engaged on similar occupations, and each trying to win a wager or price) (K.Pr. 66; Śiv. 1313, 1519, 1533). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to regard each other in emulation. ¶ mānmöñⁱ adv. in emulation.
m. love, amorous passion, lust, carnal desire (L.V. 43); Kāma, the Indian Cupid.
f. ornaments for women, consisting of bracelets, rings for the nose, ears, and neck, made of earthenware, tin, iron, brass, and copper (El. manárí).

m. a weight of one and a half seers (i.e. three pounds) (K.Pr. 13, 44, 136). Cf. man 3. ¶ manȧṭⁱ mēnȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to weigh amounts of one and a half seers; met. associates to quarrel mutually. --mīnith khë̆nⁱ -- m. pl. inf., id. ¶ manȧṭⁱ (or manᵃ̇ṭᵃ̇) dab khyonᵘ  m.inf. (of an arrogant or insolent person) to become quieted, be brought to one's senses, be taught one's place (by punishment, suffering, or the like) (K.Pr. 56). manȧṭⁱ (or manᵃ̇ṭᵃ̇) dab pyonᵘ  m.inf. becoming quieted, etc., as ab., to occur to a person.
m. (with indef. art. manshāh, Gr.M.), origin, beginning; motive, object, intention, design (Gr.M.); purport, tenor, drift.

or mantᵃr m. (sg. dat. mantras), a passage of the Vēdas, a holy text; a formula sacred to any particular deity, a mystical verse, magic formulary, spell, charm, incantation (L.V. 11, 34, 39, 40, 58; Śiv. 11, 126, 154, 632; Rām. 956; K. 877-8). Cf. mö̃thᵃr 1.
m. three pounds of anything (El. manṭun). Cf. manoṭᵘ.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. mônᵘ, f. möñᵘ̈; 2 p.p. māñōv), to respect, revere, esteem highly (Śiv. 414, 449, 472, 984, 1049, 1204, 1298, etc.; Rām. 71; K. 898, 905, 1043, 1053); to admit, allow, acknowledge, confess, own (Gr.Gr. 174; Gr.M.; Śiv. 693, 944); to agree to, assent to, comply with (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 261; YZ. 515; Śiv. 695; K. 323, 403, 405, 574, 718, 846); to take, assume, suppose; to heed, follow (advice) (Gr.M., K.Pr. 135, K. 616); to take for granted, grant; to think of, call to mind, remember (K. 1155); to hold, view, consider, regard as, deem, look upon as (L.V. 23, 73; Śiv. 48, 280, 877, 1062, 1449, 1503, etc.; Rām. 180, 1513, 1645; K. 113, 341, 533); to hold to be true or right, to approve of (K.Pr. 2; Śiv. 1133, 1311, 1555, 1773; K. 582); to obey (Gr.Gr. 5; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 256; Rām. 748, 840; K. 240, 466, 630); to give in to, submit to (K.Pr. 182, K. 623). ¶ mānunᵘ m. obedience; na-mānunᵘ, disobedience (Gr.M.). ¶ mônᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. möñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), agreed to, approved of, etc., as ab.; generally approved of (by everyone), highly esteemed or respected (K.Pr. 163).

manŏsh, manōsh, or manŏshy m. (sg. dat. manᵃshĕs), a man, a human being (i.e. homo, as distinct from supernatural beings and brutes) (L.V. 81, 107; Rām. 27, 63, 65, 139, 339, 576, 578, 863, 1498; K. 56, 490, 680, 754); (pl.) people in general (Gr.M.). ¶ manᵃshĕ (or manŏshĕ)-bŏy  m. (the gender is reported as masculine, but the word bŏy is feminine; cf. mö̃ʦa-bŏy, s.v. mö̃ʦh, which is fem.), the smell of a man; the (unexpected) smell of human habitations (in a forest or desert place). -lūkh m. the world of men (Rām. 515, 609, 1262). -zāth m. mankind, the human species (Rām. 1167).

m. the middle, midst, mean (Gr.M., K.Pr. 136, Śiv. 1662, Rām. 1123); aṭa-manz, the middle of a market, a place where four ways meet (p. 56a, l. 32). Cf. anz-manz (p. 36b, l. 35). ¶ adv., in the middle, mid (Śiv. 1206, 1463, 1478, 1671; H. xii, 11). ¶ postpos. (governing dat.), in, within (Gr.Gr. 152; Gr.M.; W. 97; L.V. 44, 98; Śiv. 16, 21, 64-6, 72, 82, 87, 89, 92, etc.; Rām. 74, 164, 208, 216, 272, etc.; K. 222, 256, etc.; H. ii, 1, 7, etc.); in (of time, as in brinzis-manz, in the twinkling of an eye) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 605, 829, 913, 1066, 1209); into (Gr.M.; Śiv. 118, 126, 158, 322, 343, 409, 437, etc.; K. 233, 621, etc.); between (Rām. 1269); among, amidst (Śiv. 69, 446, 580, 791, 1199; Rām. 87, 112). ¶ As a postpos. this word naturally follows the word it governs, but occasionally (e.g. K.Pr. 57; Śiv. 64, 66, 82, 87, 89, 92, etc.; K. 118, 193, 231) it precedes it. Occasionally also this postposition governs the abl. instead of the dat., as in vĕvahāra-manz (Śiv. 587); manz mana (Śiv. 1406); manz tapōwana (Śiv. 1409); prayāga-manz (Śiv. 1172). ¶ manz-anz adj. c.g. being or dwelling inside, including or comprised in; cf. anz-manz. -atha m. the middle of the hand, the palm of the hand; cf. athas-manz, p. 66b, l. 1. --aʦun -- m.inf. to come in, intervene, come between; to become a surety (between two people) (K.Pr. 136). -bāg m. the middle, the interior (Śiv. 329); adv. in the middle, within, in the interior, in the centre (Gr.M.; L. 458; K.Pr. 103; Śiv. 914, 1459, 1668, 1695; K. 251, 294, 631, 719); postpos. (governing dat.) in the middle (of) (W. 97; YZ. 107; Śiv. 20, 329, 1107, 1547, 1588, 1756; Rām. 426, 543, 723, etc.); into the middle (Rām. 910, 1713). -bāga adv. and postpos. (governing abl.) from in the middle, from, out of (W. 98; K. 283 (adv.), 894 (adv.)); also manz-bāg in this sense, as in Rām. 632. -bāgukᵘ adj. (f. -bāgücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the interior. -bāgan adv. in the middle, within, in the interior (Śiv. 329). -güñᵘ̈ f. the middle slice of a fish (see p. 294a, l. 12); (in a human being, etc.) the middle lump of flesh, the flesh above the anus. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take into (one's company), to accept (so-and-so) as a member of a company or association (K.Pr. 80). -manḍali naʦun m.inf. to dance in the middle circle, to interfere improperly or malevolently in other people's business. --raṭun -- m.inf. to grasp the middle; to throw one's arms round a person's waist (K. 399). ¶ manza adv. and prep. (governing abl.) from within, from in, from among (W. 98; K.Pr. 150; Śiv. 15, 18, 31, 122, 239, 666, etc.; Rām. 80, 1567, etc.; K. 32, 728; H. viii, 7, 11; x, 12, etc.); dŏyau manza, from among two, (which) of two; occasionally governing dat. as in timanạy-manza (Śiv. 34); manza zalas, from out of the water (K. 245, 758), but zala-manza (K. 272); asĕ manza, from among us (K. 287). ¶ Occasionally also this word is used instead of manz, as in aki dama-manza, in a single instant (Śiv. 1130), dyāna-manza, in meditation (Śiv. 1789); nagara-manza, in the city (Śiv. 1822); ʦaḍi-manza, in the milk-pail (Śiv. 1837). ¶ Used as an adv. at an interval of so much (Rām. 1719); on such-and-such an account, accordingly, therefore (K. 316); on the contrary, but (K. 1095). ¶ manza-mara (also written) adv. about the middle, i.e. at some indefinite time, during about some short time or other (esp. on the same day as that in which the speaker uses the expression) (cf. Gr.Gr. 84 and mara 3). -marukᵘ (also written) adj. (f. -marücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, some indefinite short time (esp. of to-day, as ab.). --wọ̆thᵘ -- adj. (f. -wö̆ʦhᵘ̈), risen from the middle, suddenly risen (in wealth, power, etc.) (and not by inheritance or from his youth); suddenly intervening or interfering in the middle of another's business or conversation. --wŏthun -- m.inf. suddenly to rise in wealth or power (and not by inheritance or from boyhood); to rise and depart from an assembly; to interfere mischievously in someone else's business or conversation. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to interrupt, or intervene in, a conversation. ¶ mȧnzⁱ, postpos. governing abl., even within, just between; exactly between (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1397, 1462, 1504, 1733; K. 171); (governing dat.) (Rām. 931); from within (Śiv. 1386). --aʦun -- m.inf. to interfere (selfishly, kindly, or maliciously) in another's business, to dip one's finger into another's pie. --bögⁱ -- or --bögin -- adv. from within. --tarun -- m.inf. to cross over (water, by going) into it, to wade across (Rām. 778).
m. weakness (of persons or things), dilapidation, worn-outness; (of a person) sickness, illness (Gr.Gr. 140); slowness, clumsiness, feebleness.

m. a stage in a journey (Rām. 946); the distance of a complete journey (possibly of many stages) (Rām. 885, 1430); manzil ba manzil (منزل بمنزل), adv. stage by stage (Rām. 831); manzil-mubārakh, welcome to a person arriving from a journey (Rām. 751).

(i.q. manzil, q.v.) m. (sg. dat mȧnzⁱlas), a place for alighting, an hotel, caravanserai; a house, lodging; a mansion of the moon; a story or floor (of a house); a day's journey, a stage (in travelling) (Śiv. 1309, 1627). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to complete a long and wearying stage. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. a long wearying stage to fall to the lot of a traveller; met. some difficult and toilsome necessity to fall to the lot of a helpless person. --ʦaṭun -- m.inf. to travel (El., Rām. 207). ¶ mȧnzⁱlas wātun m.inf. to arrive at (the end of) the stage; met. finally to reach the last stage of a difficult and toilsome business, to have the end of such in sight.
in the following:--manzīla yunᵘ m.inf. (of a person) sudden ruin to occur.
m. a child's swinging-cot, a swing-cradle (Śiv. 352, 1321, 1379 ff.; Rām. 632; K. 118-19). Cf. guga-manzulᵘ, p. 279b, l. 34.
or (H. i, 12) mônzūr منظور adj. c.g. approved of, admitted, accepted, sanctioned (Śiv. 636, 692, 900; H. i, 12).

adj. (f.manzimᵘ̈), middle, intermediate, internal (Gr.Gr. 152, Śiv. 1467); middling, mediocre, moderately good, middle-class (Gr.M., K.Pr. 136); cf. anzyumᵘ-manzyumᵘ, p. 37a, l. 18. --yôrᵘ -- m. (f. manzimᵘ̈ yārĕñ, Gr.Gr. 135, a female go-between) an intermediary, a go-between (Gr.Gr. 135, 142; W. 149; K.Pr. 260; Śiv. 1670); a broker (Gr.M.); a matchmaker, a go-between who arranges a marriage, a go-between in love matters (L. 261, 268; Śiv. 713; Rām. 134). ¶ manzimᵘ̈ yörī f. the action or profession of a matchmaker or broker. --yārᵃz -- f. the action or profession of a matchmaker, the office of a go-between (Gr.Gr. 142); the profession of a broker (Gr.M.); the wages or fee paid to a matchmaker.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mạnzᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. mạnzᵃrun, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mạnzᵒrᵒ), to make imperfect, to diminish (Gr.Gr. lvii).
(? spelling and gend.), N. of a certain medicinal plant, used as an antidysenteric and in menorrhagia (L. 75).

or manᵘ̈rᵘ̈ m. (his wife is manᵃr-bāy) (see below), but a female lapidary is manᵃrĕñ, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 39), a lapidary, a man who works on precious stones or on shells, a shell-worker (Gr.Gr. 148). -bāy f. a lapidary's wife. -koṭᵘ m. the son of a lapidary (used with the idea of praise), a true son of a lapidary (Gr.Gr. 132); hence, a good, or skilled, lapidary (Gr.Gr. 132). -thöjᵘ̈,also written manạr-thöjᵘ̈ m. a lapidary's polishing wheel or lathe (worked with a bow). -wān m. a lapidary's shop or workshop.
f. a female lapidary, etc.; see manᵃr.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. manᵒsᵒ), to give something in fulfilment of a vow, to devote something to pious uses, make a pious endowment. manᵒsᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. manᵘ̈sᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), given, etc., as ab.
or muāf معاف adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. māphas), pardoned, forgiven; subst., m. forgiveness (K.Pr. 124). --karun -- m.inf. to pardon (Gr.M.; Śiv. 423, 593).

m. a hut, a small house (K.Pr. 7, 138); an ascetic's leaf-hut in the forest; a shelter or small hut (erected in desolate or forest localities as a refuge for travellers) (RT.Tr. II, 387); a cell, a small room (cf. bata-mar, a store-room for food (p. 137a, l. 27). This word is not uncommonly --˚ in place names; cf. āhᵃl-mar (p. 17b, l. 38; ālȧʦhⁱ-mar, p. 26a, l. 8). El. also has mar, f., a fort, a castle. --hĕnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to take huts, i.e. from grief, distress, distaste for the world, or the like, to take to a solitary hermit's life in some cave, in the forest, or the like.

m. killing, taking life, slaughter, murder (Gr.Gr. 124; W. 114; Rām. 217, 1032); hitting, beating, striking (cf. ã̄cĕ-mār, p. 53b, l. 11; cō̃ca-mār, p. 157a, l. 31; gir-mār, p. 303a, l. 6). --˚ sometimes indicates a person who kills, strikes, or hits, as in chūrī-mār, a dagger-striker, one who strikes (himself) with a dagger (p. 165a, l. 42). This word also takes the form māra, q.v., s.v., from which in the oblique cases it is indistinguishable. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give killing, to kill (Rām. 103); to give a beating, to drub (Rām. 618, 961, 1276). -ganḍ m. tying up and beating, a kind of punishment, in which the victim's arms and legs are tied up, and then he is thumped with fists. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. murder to occur. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to receive a beating. --khasun -- m.inf. a charge of murder to be brought. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat a beating, to suffer a beating, to be beaten. --karun -- m.inf. to commit murder. --maṭi khasun -- m.inf. murder to mount on the shoulder, a charge of murder to be brought (against a person). ¶ māra-būth m. (sg. dat. -būtas), a demon of murder, a murderous demon (L.V. 71), -dĕv m. a death-demon, torment caused by an evil death, or due to some evil death. -wārĕñ f. a midwife who attends the birth of a dead child.
m. (a corruption of manḍal 2, in the sense of 'territory'), a province, tract, as in Kashmīra- mar, the land of Kashmīr (Śiv. 1159).

m. a serpent, a snake (cf. kŏla-mār, p. 437a, l. 28) (YZ. 35, 64, 141). mār-i-pēʦān, a serpent of convolutions, a kind of serpent that makes itself into a ring round its victim, and thus kills it at its leisure (Rām. 913).
m. the Hindū god of love, Cupid; love, passion. māra-motᵘ m. extreme love, affection, fondness (YZ. 37); an ardent lover (Rām. 1585).

f. (sg. dat. mörᵘ̈ 1, Gr.Gr. 75; for 2, see môrᵘ 2; for 3, see s.v.), N. of a canal issuing from the Ḍal lake, and passing behind that part of the city of Śrīnagar which lies on the right bank of the river Vĕth (Jĕhlam). It empties itself into the ā̃cār marshes north-west of the city (cf. RT.Tr. II, 416) (K.Pr. 137), a lake genl. (El.). ¶ mörᵘ̈-bal m. N. of a landing place with masonry steps on the bank of the Mār (Gr.Gr. 165). -hönzᵘ̈ m. a boatman living or plying on the river Mār (they have a bad name); met. an impudent, dishonest, evil-conducted fellow. -hānzañ f. the wife of such a boatman; met. an impudent, unchaste, dishonest woman. -wôñᵘ m. the water of the Mār (noted for its purity) (Gr.Gr. 73); lake-water genl. (El. mãrwóin).

m. killing someone or some animal, murder; as adj. c.g. beaten, killed (El. márah, K.Pr. 138); cf. mār 1. -cīrⁱ f. a letter announcing a death. -gã̄ḍay f. the action of binding and beating a person (cf. mār-ganḍ, p. 586b, l. 38). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go to death or to beating, to be killed (YZ. 477; Rām. 701, 868, 972, 1424; H. x, 7, 8, 13); met. to be obstructed, impeded. -hāʦh f. (sg. dat. -hāʦi), a charge or accusation of murder. -hāʦh yiñᵘ̈ f.inf. an accusation of murder to be made (against a person). --karun -- m. to knock down finally, to give a knock-out blow, to kill (e.g. by a sudden blow) (Rām. 1585, 1726 (met.)); (of a business) to knock down a work or an occupation, to obstruct it so that it cannot be resumed. -mār f. (for gend., see Gr.Gr. 75), a fight between a number of armed men; utter killing, death in every part of the body (Rām. 1484); (on the occasion of an epidemic) a multitude of deaths. -māray f. mutual beating or striking, a broil, affray. --sö̃panun -- m.inf. (so-and-so's) death to have occurred; hence, to have become dead, to be dead and gone (Rām. 1381); cf. māray sö̃püñᵘ̈, s.v. māray. -wātul m. a public executioner (Gr.M.; H. viii, 4, 11-13; x, 12). -wātᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a female executioner (for executing women); the wife of an executioner.

in mara-phēra m. turning of wish; hence, (after agreeing to do something, or being ordered to do it) to do it unwillingly, e.g. in distributing something, to worry the recipients by grudging or delay, even while consenting to carry out the distribution. Cf. marwāna.

in the following:--mara-mar f. general mortality, a great number of deaths occurring in any locality (owing to epidemic, massacre, etc.); the near approach of death, the last flicker of life (when all hope of recovery is abandoned). -mara m. the abandonment of all hope of life, being at the point of death.

a suffix added to cardinal numerals to indicate 'about'. Thus, from aiṭh, eight; aiṭha- mara, about eight; daha-mara, about ten (p. 199a, l. 15) (W. 103). Also added to manz, in; see p. 584a, l. 22. Cf. Gr.Gr. 84, where the suffix is given as amara, the initial a being the termination of the oblique case of the numeral.
m. a field of battle, tumult (El.); quarrelling, strife (K.Pr. 137); an assembly, meeting, congregation (Śiv. 89; H. vii, 23).
m. (sg. dat. maramatas), repairing, repair (El., Gr.M.); --karun -- m.inf. to repair (El.).
m. the end of death, death (K. 540).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. maranôwᵘ), to cause to be pasted or joined together (causal of marun 1, q.v.) (Gr.Gr. 175).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. māranôwᵘ), to cause to kill, to incite to kill, to have (so-and-so, or such-and-such an animal) killed, to cause to be slain (Rām. 1473, 1476); to cause to be slain, and hence, to capture a piece (in chess) (Rām. 1314); to ruin, mar, spoil (Rām. 1160).
f. wages paid for beating (a person, cattle or other animals); N. of a certain game, in which small balls are aimed at a mark.
n.ag. (f. maravüñᵘ̈), one who is dying, a person at the point of death.
n.ag. (f. māravüñᵘ̈), one who kills, a slayer (Śiv. 856, 1321); a murderer, a homicide (K. 64); a beater, one who beats, a flogger. ʦhāla mārawunᵘ, one who leaps (cf. p. 593a, l. 6) (Śiv. 1322).

f. killing, beating, i.q. māra, used --˚ as in hūnⁱ-māray, p. 336b, l. 48; māra-māray, p. 587b, l. 7. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to slay, kill, murder (Śiv. 578). --sö̃panüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to become killed, to be killed.

m. one of the two great divisions of the Kashmīr valley, embracing the whole south-east end. The ancient name was Maḍavarājya. The other division is called Kamrāz (Kramarājya), q.v. for further particulars; cf. RT.Tr. II, 436 (K.Pr. 138; H. xi, 5). marāzukᵘ adj. (f. marāzücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, Marāz.

m. a man, vir, male human being (W. 149; K.Pr. 103, 250, 260; Śiv. 974). ¶ marda-mahanyuwᵘ m. a male man, i.e. a thoroughly masculine man, an able-bodied man endowed with all his wits, a real man. -nāl m. the neck- piece of a man's garment. -norᵘ m. the sleeve of a man's garment. -phĕran m. a man's phĕran, i.e. the garment worn by Kāshmīrīs of both sexes, somewhat like a night-gown with wide sleeves. -pöthᵃr m. the work of a man, or work suitable for, or intended for, a man, man's work (as distinct from woman's work). -pôʦhᵘ m. a man's undergarment (made of cotton, and worn next the skin). -zan, man or woman (H. vii, 23).
adj. c.g. manlike, virile; manly, brave; of, or pertaining to, or suitable for, a man.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. mardôwᵘ), to rub away, to wear out (a garment, dish, or the like) by use; to rub down with ointment a boil or the like. ¶ mardāwana āmotᵘ perf. part. pass. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), rubbed away, worn away by use (e.g. a garment, dish, or the like); (of a boil or the like) reduced by rubbing down, as ab. mardāwana yunᵘ m.inf. pass. to become worn away by use, as ab.; (of a boil, etc.) to be reduced, as ab. ¶ mardôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mardövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), rubbed, as ab. (in both senses).
f. oppression, tyranny; (in Kāshmīrī) met. the conduct of a lovely woman, amorous sport (H. x, 12).

f. (sg. dat. marēdi or mardi), a certain pinkish-white powder formed from a certain stone. It is used for marking swastikas, circles, or other mystic religious signs. --wahārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to spread out this powder, i.e. by means of a charm or similar mark, to prevent the access of outsiders to any act or person. ¶ mardi-pholᵘ or marēdi-pholᵘ m. a quantity of this powder. -phĕkh or marēdi-phĕkh f. (sg. dat. -phĕki), id. -rᵃkh or marēdi-rᵃkh f. (sg. dat. -rᵃkhi), a line marked with this powder (e.g. at a sacrificial rite, the mark of a swastika or mystic circle, or a boundary line circumscribing the operations). -rᵃkh trāvüñᵘ̈ f.inf. (at a sacrifice, etc.) with this powder to mark the boundary line enclosing the holy ground within which the operations take place, and within which access is prohibited to unauthorized persons or things.
m. a road, a way, a path (lit. and fig.) (Gr.M.; L.V. 63, 82; Śiv. 1655, 1801); (in pl.) ways (i.e. customary actions) (Gr.M.)

m. death (YZ. 559, 562); (in Kāshmīrī) grief caused by a death (esp. of one on whom many depend) (cf. jāna-marg, p. 374b, l. 28). --pharun -- m.inf. ruin caused by the death of someone on whom the ruined person was dependent to occur. ¶ marga-būñᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -bōñĕ), a woman who has grown old and seen many of her descendants and relations die before her. -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), afflicted and sorrowing owing to the death of someone very dear. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), full of sorrow for the same reason.
f. a valley or plateau high up among the mountains (full of wild flowers, with level ground and a cool pleasant climate). Frequent --˚, as in gul-marg, p. 283b, l. 23.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. margaladiñ), one who is sorrowing for the death of a dear one (esp. of one on whom the person sorrowing was dependent).
f. twists and turns; crisp, curly, or waving hair; quavering, trilling, or shaking of the voice; a crenated arch; a tassel for tying up and closing the end of a pillow.
interj. welcome! hail! God bless you! bravo! (Śiv. 657; H. ii, 10).

adv., used --˚, an old obl. case of mār 1, q.v. 'by striking by'; hence, through, by reason of, on account of, in consequence of, as in dŏkha-māri, by reason of sorrow, i.e. compassionately, pitifully (p. 206b, l. 2).

f. a violent epidemic, cholera, etc. (cf. mörī). ¶ mȧrⁱca-buḍⁱ f. a particularly deadly epidemic killing quickly, cholera. mȧrⁱca-dĕv m. the demon of an epidemic such as cholera. mȧrⁱca-dĕviñ f. the female demon of the same. mȧrⁱca-kônⁱ m. a death from cholera or similar violent epidemic. ? Cf. kān 1.
m. a kind of woollen cloth woven in varied colours (? = merino). ¶ marīnukᵘ adj. (f. marīnücᵘ̈), made of this cloth. ¶ marīna-sondᵘ adj. (f. -sünzᵘ̈), id.
m. a carrier who conveys goods on mules or ponies, a muleteer (L. 364, 383, 459).
m. the wild goat of Ladak, the Markhor (Gr.M.).
f. a certain tube believed to exist in the heart, the vitals, a vital part of the body.
f. the hidden or secret meaning of anything, the pith, or essential, meaning; the secret or hidden intention of a person.
f. pl. the joints of any limb.
m. a rustling sound, rustling, murmuring, murmur; crackling, crackle; sound of crunching, etc.
m. marble, usually in the phrase sang-ĕ-marmar, employed with the same meaning.
m. a road covered with hard frozen snow (and, hence, made passable owing to freedom from mud and inequalities).
adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, or produced in, Marāz, q.v.
f. a lamentation for the dead, a dirge (esp. the one sung during the Moḥarram in commemoration of Ḥasan and Ḥusain).
m. station, post of honour, rank, dignity (L.V. 87, K.Pr. 145); time, turn. Cf. marith martaba, p. 592b, l. 18.
m. a glazed earthenware jar (used for keeping preserves and pickles, etc., in); a vessel of the finest porcelain which poison cannot penetrate.
m. (sg. dat. martĕlūkas), the world of mortals, the world (Rām. 551).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. môrᵘ. Causal of marun 2, q.v.), to kill, slay (Gr.Gr. 175, 206, 207; Gr.M.; L.V. 30, 43, 71, 77; K.Pr. 80, 262; YZ. 48, 101, 147; Śiv. 112, 120, 709-10, 1252, 1369, etc.; Rām. 38, 65, 105, 108, 227, 334, 350, 365-7, etc.; K. 33-5, 39-41, 52, 64, 81, 86, etc.; H. ii, 7, 11; v, 7; vi, 11; viii, 4, 12, 13; x, 5, 12, 15, etc.); [pān mārun, to kill oneself, commit suicide (Śiv. 1439; Rām. 165, 387, 646, 877, 1370, 1605), cf. bel.]; to destroy, ruin (Śiv. 13, 1753); to strike, beat, thump, smite (Gr.Gr. 104, 124, 197; L.V. 83; K.Pr. 138; YZ. 16, 50, 93; Rām. 371, 440, 584; K. 433; H. v, 6); [pān mārun, to beat oneself (Rām. 404, 1162, 1536), cf. ab.]; to attack (K. 663); to overcome, conquer, vanquish, defeat (cf. gōṭh mārüñᵘ̈, to win at chess, p. 311b, l. 30) (Śiv. 106, 214, 280, 1797; K. 570, 627); to seize, take, capture, catch; to master, subdue, tame, mortify (affections, appetites, lusts, etc.), reduce to quietude or subjection (L.V. 49); to quench, allay, suppress, smother (Śiv. 1078); to apply, fix, fasten; to strike, hit (the mark) (Rām. 1042) (cf. nishāna, mᵒ); to shoot, discharge, fire (a gun, etc.), hurl (a missile), lay on (a sword, etc.); ¶ to strike up (a run, dance, etc.), raise or set up (a cry), make or do (esp. with vehemence, eagerness, or smartness) (e.g. grāyĕ mārañĕ, to strike flutterings, to flutter, p. 306a, l. 27; YZ. 64; Rām. 1118; gata mārȧnⁱ, to faint often, p. 310a, l. 15; körᵘ̈, to bend the neck, to shake the head, p. 467a, l. 19, K.Pr. 77; thāh mārüñᵘ̈, to dive, Rām. 546; tāla mārañĕ, to clap the hands, Śiv. 276, 374, 1453; ʦhāla mārañĕ, to strike leaps, to bound along, Śiv. 528, 764, 820, 972, 1380, 1615; Rām. 820, 1097, 1328); ¶ to melt, make liquid (metals, etc.); to reduce to ashes. ¶ mörⁱ mörⁱ freq. part. beating repeatedly, giving a severe flogging (to so-and-so). ¶ môrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), killed; struck; melted, etc., as ab. ¶ māran-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a killer, a striker, a beater, etc., as ab.; as adj. deadly (El.). ¶ mörīth trāwun m.inf. to kill, slay (H. x, 8). --ʦhunun -- m.inf. (an intensive compound = Hindī mār ḍālnā), to kill outright, to slay (W. 85; Rām. 232, 1163, 1376, 1414).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. morᵘ, Gr.Gr. 223; also optionally conjugated like marun 2, Gr.Gr. 204. The causal of this verb is maranāwun, Gr.Gr. 175) to paste on (e.g. paper on a wall), fasten on, fasten together (cf. khām marun, p. 400a, l. 34). morᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), pasted on.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. mūdᵘ, K. 625, 689; f. mŏyĕ, YZ. 76; 2 p.p. mŏyōv, Gr.Gr. 211, 223, 228. The causal of this verb is mārun, q.v., Gr.Gr. 175), to die, to expire (Gr.Gr. 5, 204; Gr.M.; L.V. 12, 35, 68, etc.; K.Pr. 28 (mod for mūdᵘ), 63; YZ. 42, 110, 401, 408; Śiv. 156, 243, 622, 1279, 1585, 1760, 1900; Rām. 161, 176, 463, 518, etc.; K. 105, 369, 562, 625, 660, 689, 804; H. ii, 3, 6; v, 9; viii, 1, 2, 7, 11; x, 7; xii, 19); to fade, wither; to be lost (as a stake or bad debt); to be dead (as in a game); (of an object aimed at or a target) to be hit (Śiv. 1752) (cf. nishāna mᵒ). ¶ mūdᵘ-motᵘ or mūmotᵘ perf. part. (f. mūmüʦᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 111, K. 560), dead (Śiv. 707; Rām. 960; K. 678; H. ii, 3, 4, 10; viii, 1; x, 8; xii, 20); a long time dead (as a corpse); a dying person (as good as dead) (K.Pr. 146). ¶ mȧrⁱ mȧrⁱ yunᵘ m.inf. dying over and over again to come (back), to survive some deadly task, to come safely through a forlorn hope. ¶ marun 3 or marunᵘ m. death, the act of dying (K.Pr. 136, 138, 203; YZ. 183, 556; Śiv. 342, 622, 706, 1197, 1340, 1424; Rām. 99, 177, 874, 1486, 1762; K. 187, 355, 439, 847); esp. Death personified (sg. gen. maranunᵘ, L.V. 73-76); yitha maranas, as if for death, as if dead (K. 55, 65); when --˚, this word may mean 'wretched', 'despicable' (= Skt., hatakaḥ), as in pŏtra-marun, (his) despicable son (K. 22). --mạshᵉ̆run -- or --mạshᵉ̆rāwun -- m.inf. to forget death, to be heedless as to death, to act as if one would never die (Rām. 177). --māshĕvith -- adv. having forgotten death, i.e. (doing something) after banishing all fear of death, acting as if one would never die. According to I.K. IX, i, 10 (= Gr.Gr. 104, 198), this phrase is used in a causal sense,--'having caused (so-and-so) to forget death', but the above is the meaning given by other authorities. --zānun -- m.inf. to know death, to heed death, to conduct oneself with the knowledge that death is inevitable, opp. to --mạshᵉ̆run, ab. (Rām. 177). ¶ maran-dāra f. fear of death; cf. the maranüñᵘ̈ shö̃kh of L.V. 73-6. -gürᵘ̈ f. the moment of death, a person's destined hour of death. -kāl m., id. -nĕng m. the time of dying, (in speaking of someone dead or dying) the time of the condition of a dying man, the period or time during which a person is dying. -vizᵘ̈ or marana-vizᵘ̈ f. the hour of death, the time of death (e.g. spoken of when warning a person as to his behaviour) (Śiv. 287, 1331, 1901; Rām. 376). ¶ marana-sar adj. c.g. one who is at the point of death. ¶ mȧrin- (or mȧrinⁱ-)bāgĕ (or bögⁱ)   m.pl. the visibility of death, the signs of approaching death becoming visible (e.g. by failing health). -bögⁱ yinⁱ m. pl. inf. the signs of approaching death to become visible (e.g. by a dream, omen, or failing health). -nĕng f. (of a dying person) the time of the condition of dying, the moment of death. -nĕngan adv. at the time of death, on a person's death-bed (e.g. of a person's last words, a death-bed gift, or the like). -vidān m. the last rites performed to a dead person. -vidönⁱ m. the money expended on the last rites of a dead person. -wān f. (sg. dat. -wöñᵘ̈), a rumour (true or false) of a person's death (with pë̆ñᵘ̈, such a rumour to become current). -wôñᵘ m. death- water, a drink which makes a person afraid of death; a poisoned drink. ¶ maranan aʦun m.inf. to be at the point of death or to be inflicted by some incurable and fatal disease; to feel oneself as good as dead, to give up the hope of life (from some terrifying predicament or the like). ¶ maranȧnⁱ-dyönⁱ m.pl. anxiety as to the coming of death, a continual apprehension of death. -ʦhraṭh m.pl. (pl. dat. -ʦhraṭan), terror (due to the knowledge of the immediate certainty) of death. ¶ marith conj. part. having died (Rām. 303, 812, 877); marith ösⁱ, they were having died, they had died (Śiv. 706); often used as an adv., meaning 'after death', as in K.Pr. 13, 145, 262; Rām. 1530; H. iv, 7. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to die (= Hindī mar jānā) (Rām. 264, 753, 1381, 1425, 1577; H. vi, 16). --martaba -- m. praise of a person after he is dead (though he may not have been praised when he was alive) (cf. de mortuis nil nisi bonum); similar praise of something lost or destroyed.
m. private intention (to do something contrary to instructions), doing something (with a private contrary intention); cf. mara 1. --phērun -- m.inf. a secret intention (as ab.) to be changed.
m. (El. márúk and maryukᵘ), a noose, a lasso (El.); a hangman's noose; a scaling ladder used by thieves (El.); a horse's halter (El.). Cf. mölⁱ-māⁱ, p. 566b, l. 22.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. marzaladiñ), suffering from an incurable disease.

m. pepper, black pepper (El. also marits; K.Pr. 62 (misprinted marats), 138, 233; K. 373). --mathun -- m.inf. to pound pepper; met. goading oneself, i.e. (in fury, despair, etc.) beating oneself, tearing one's own face with one's nails or the like. --ʦāpun -- m.inf. to chew pepper; met. shouting out to people generally when in a rage. ¶ marʦa-gŏsôñᵘ m. (sarcastically) a peppery saint, u.w. ref. to a child (esp. a boy) who is of a passionate disposition. In Sanskrit literature there are various legends of peppery saints, whose curses caused great mischief. -pŏnd f. (sg. dat. pŏndi), pepper-sneezing; met. pride, haughtiness, vainglory, arrogance. -pŏnda trāwañĕ f. pl. inf. to emit pepper-sneezes; met. arrogantly to display rage (esp. to one's inferiors). -pī˜piñ f. a teetotum (a kind of top); a kind of musical instrument (played by blowing into it) (cf. pī˜piñ). -ṭĕchĕr m. pepper-heat; irritability (of character). -wã̄gun m. long pepper, red pepper, a pod of red pepper, a red chilli, Capsicum sp. (L. 346; H. v, 6). -wã̄gan-āra m. a chain or string of red chillis, dried and kept for winter use. (They are strung on a thread, like a necklace.)
f. conj. 1 (1 p.p., f. marʦövᵘ̈. This verb is construed impersonally in the feminine (cf. marʦüñᵘ̈)), inward wrath to be caused to a person, indignation to be caused to a person.

conj. 1 (1 p.p., f. mürʦᵘ̈. This verb is always construed impersonally in the feminine, with the logical subject in the dative, as in marʦān chĕ-s, there is inward wrath to him, i.e. he is inwardly wrathful; cf. Gr.Gr. 182, 188, 215); inward wrath to attack, indignation to be felt, impatience to be felt (Gr.Gr. 117, 119, 192, 248).
m. disease, sickness, illness, malady, distemper (K.Pr. 138). marza-dĕv m. a severe sickness, a deadly or incurable disease (ascribed to possession by a demon).

m. wine. It is made out of the juice of the grape, which grows luxuriantly in Kashmīr (El.; L.V. 104; K.Pr. 5, 102, 138, 139; YZ. 193, 209, 343, 366; Śiv. 1203, 1220, 1260, 1326, 1823, 1844, 1874; H. vii, 31). -khôsᵘ m. a wine-glass, a wine-cup (YZ. 275). --mŏnjĕ bĕhun -- m.inf. the wine to lose its office (cf. mŏnjĕ bĕhun, p. 575a, l. 15); hence, to use (secretly, and without opposition) property or wealth accumulated by another. -wū̃ṭᵘ̈ f. a jar of wine. -wū̃cĕ-pĕṭh nẹ̆ndᵃr f. sleep on a wine-jar, i.e. to sit apart and without care.

m. a month (El. máṅs) (Śiv. 1351, 1443; Rām. 1258); cf. mal-mās, p. 564a, l. 7. ¶ māsa-nēthᵃr m. the festival on the last day of the first month of the life of a newly-born child (L. 260). -wār f. (amongst Hindūs) the monthly śrāddha, or commemorative offerings of piṇḍas, or rice-balls, on the day of the month on which a person died. This goes on each month for a year after his death, on the same date of each month. ¶ māsan-andar adj. c.g. 'among the months', i.e. a child or animal whose age can only be counted by months and not by years. -hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of (so many) months.

m. the hair of the head (Rām. 283); cf. masth 1. -kala 1 m. (for 2, see s.v.), a head covered with hair. --kāsun -- m.inf. to cut the hair, to do haircutting, to shave (Gr.M., Śiv. 1351). -lang m. a woman's head of hair (esp. unbound). --pārun -- m.inf. to plait or bind (a woman's) hair, to comb the hair (Gr.M.). -pāray f. the act of plaiting or binding (a woman's) hair. -wö̃kh f. (sg. dat. wö̃ki), a woman's long plaited hair hanging down behind. -wāl m. a single hair of the head.
m. flesh (Śiv. 762, 763). Cf. māmas and māz.
ink, in the following:--mas-phyorᵘ or -phyūrᵘ m. a spot of ink; the dot which indicates the sign anusvāra in the Śāradā or Nāgarī alphabet. -phīrⁱ am m. the syllable am, written.

f. a mother's sister, a maternal aunt (L. 458, L.V. 97, K.Pr. 47, Śiv. 1445, Rām. 734); cf. māsaturᵘ. -pörⁱ f. an adoptive maternal aunt, a woman who adopts or treats a child as if it were her real nephew or niece on her sister's side. ¶ māsa-hihurᵘ m. the husband of the maternal aunt of a husband or wife, a husband's or wife's maternal aunt's husband; cf. muṭhⁱ-mās, s.v. muṭhᵘ. -hash f. the mother's sister of a husband or wife, a husband's or wife's maternal aunt. -nāñ f. the mother's sister of a mother, a mother's maternal aunt, a maternal grand-aunt. ¶ māsi-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a maternal aunt; (as subst., m.) the home of a maternal aunt.
(? spelling) f. a boot, stockings reaching to the calves of the legs (El. spells this word mas and mass).

i.q. masth 2, q.v. intoxicated, drunk (Śiv. 90, 189); lustful, lascivious, wanton; rampant, furious, mad; intoxicated with pride, arrogant (Śiv. 81, Rām. 614); (as subst.) intoxication, etc. (Rām. 636).
f. a fable, parable, apologue; a proverb, adage, proverbial saying (Gr.M.); a comparison, simile, allegory, metaphor; with indef. art. masallā, by confusion with musallā مصلی, q.v. (K.Pr. 170).

m. spicery, spices, condiments, seasoning (Gr.M.); cf. manḍȧlⁱ-masāl, p. 576b, l. 19. --khārun -- m.inf. to raise spices; met. to praise merit in one who has none. -gorᵘ m. a maker of a kind of bean porridge (eaten by Musalmāns). -würᵘ̈ f. a kind of spiced cake.
adj. c.g. seasoned with spices. --würᵘ̈ -- f. a spiced cake; esp. a cake made of turmeric, salt, carraway-seed, assafœtida, and pulse, eaten at certain household festivals (L. 260, masáladár wári).
m. (sg. dat. māsāntas), (amongst Hindūs) the last day of a solar month.

adj. (f. māsatᵃr or māsatᵘ̈rᵘ̈), of or relating to a maternal aunt; cf. mās 3. --bēma -- m. the husband of the daughter of a maternal aunt, the husband of a maternal cousin. --bôyᵘ -- m. a mother's sister's son, a maternal cousin (Gr.Gr. 132). --dryuyᵘ -- m. the mother's sister's son of a woman's husband, the son of a husband's maternal aunt, a husband's maternal cousin. --hahar -- m. the mother's sister's son of a wife, a wife's maternal cousin. ¶ māsatᵘ̈rᵘ̈ (or māsatᵃr) bĕñĕ  f. the daughter of a maternal aunt, a female maternal cousin (Gr.Gr. 133). --bȧyⁱ- kākañ -- f. the wife of a mother's sister's son, the wife of a maternal cousin (Gr.Gr. 133). --sāl -- f. the daughter of the maternal aunt of a wife, a wife's maternal female cousin. --zām -- f. the daughter of the maternal aunt of a husband.
m. (of a trustee or the like) committing breach of trust (with regard to what has been entrusted to him) and saying nothing about it, secret breach of trust or peculation. Cf. māshĕl.
in the following:--mashĕ karun m.inf. (a child) to embrace or caress affectionately (its parents).
m. a jeweller's or goldsmith's weight, equal to eight ratti or seeds of the Abrus precatorius.
f. a large kind of gourd with red flesh. It is not eaten by Brāhmaṇs.
adj. c.g. one who interferes secretly in another's work; (f.) a libidinous woman. Cf. māsh.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mashĕnôwᵘ), to cause to be forgotten, to forget, i.q. mạshᵉ̆run and mạshᵉ̆rāwun (Gr.Gr. 174).
for mạshᵉ̆rövith in marun māshĕvith, see marun 2 (p. 592a, l. 5) and mạshᵉ̆rāwun (Gr.Gr. 104, 198; K.Pr. 106).
adj. c.g. busied, occupied, busy, engaged (in) (El. mushghúl, Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. well-known, famous (K.Pr. 235; YZ. 160; Śiv. 673; Rām. 92, 1133; H. xi, 3).
f. the scum or dirt of melted fat or butter.
f. will, pleasure, wish, desire (H. vii, 7).
m. a beloved man; (in Kāshmīrī) a lover (K.Pr. 4).
or mashāl مشعل f. a torch, flambeau, cresset, a lantern (El. mashil; K.Pr. 88, mashal).

conj. 2 [1 p.p. moṭhᵘ (Gr.Gr. 209, 212); f. müṭhᵘ̈, pl. nom. machĕ (K. 480); 2 p.p. machyōv (Gr.Gr. 231). The causal of this verb is mashĕnāwun or mạshᵉ̆rāwun (Gr.Gr. 174)], to be forgotten (by, dat.) (Śiv. 1220; Rām. 1535, 1630); (with subject in the dative) to forget (Gr.Gr. 205; Gr.M.; L.V. 67; K.Pr. 13, 36, 101; YZ. 430; Śiv. 330, 753, 1688; Rām. 63, 289, 524, 719, 806, 1232, 1234, 1395; K. 91, 159, 409, 470, 480, 1101, 1139; H. v, 7; ix, 8; x, 6). ¶ mȧshⁱ mȧshⁱ freq. part. being forgotten over and over again; as adv. sometimes, now and then. ¶ mashith gaʦhun m.inf. to forget (with subject in dat.) (Rām. 871); to become forgetful, to become subject to delusion (L.V. 59, Śiv. 1464). ¶ moṭhᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nom. müṭhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, dat.machĕ-maʦĕ), forgotten.
or mashwara (= مشورہ) m. counsel, advice, opinion (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to consult, to reconcile (El.).
m. a leather bag for carrying water, a mussuck. mashka-wôñᵘ m. water conveyed in, or which has been conveyed in, a mussuck.
