f. writing, drawing (the letters); practice, usage, use (K.Pr. 139); practice for acquirement (by some unskilled learner), bungling practice of a beginner, as in the following:-- --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ --  f.inf. bungling practice to occur, i.e. a remedy to be applied irregularly, intermittently, or ignorantly, so that only harm results. --karüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to apply a remedy irregularly, experimentally, or ignorantly, to act as a quack, to experiment (upon); to practise (a game or the like) (Rām. 1594).
m. a mussuck-carrier, a water-bearer, a 'bhīstī'. Cf. mashᵉ̆kh 1.

adj. c.g. acquired by practice; relating to a copy or exercise; practised on; cf. mashᵉ̆kh 2. --püṭᵘ̈ -- مشقی پتھ f. a small blackboard used as a slate on which writing is practised, a writing tablet.

m. forgetting, forgetfulness (Gr.Gr. 121); a mistake (El., Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to cause or induce forgetfulness (Rām. 1277); to do forgetting, to forget (Rām. 46). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to put out of one's memory, to think no more of, discharge from the memory, consign to oblivion.
f. (sg. dat. mashᵉ̆rüñᵉ̆), forgetfulness, the act of forgetting.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. mạshᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), to forget, i.q. mạshᵉ̆run, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 104, 174; L. 460; YZ. 499, 554; Śiv. 87, 342, 438, 1718; Rām. 177, 1231-2, 1674; K. 470, 861); to cause to be forgotten (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 87; Śiv. 1633, 1648, 1880; K. 247). ¶ mạshᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. mạshᵉ̆rövᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), forgotten, not remembered. ¶ mạshᵉ̆rövith conj. part. having forgotten. Sometimes this word takes the form māshĕvith (Gr.Gr. 104, 198); see marun 2 (p. 592a, l. 5) (K.Pr. 106); ʦhunun mạshᵉ̆rövith, to overlook (an offence) (Gr.M.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mạshᵒrᵒ), to cause to be forgotten, to forget (Gr.Gr. 174, Śiv. 1030). mạshᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. mạshᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), forgotten (by someone), passed into oblivion.
adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, a mosque. mȧshⁱdi mala (= مسجدی ملا) m. the Musalmān teacher in charge of a mosque.
(for 1, see mas 2) m. a jeweller's polishing instrument (usually a special kind of stone fixed in a wooden handle).
m. a buffoon, fool, jester, droll, wag, facetious fellow (K. 989). -pöthᵃr m. (of one who is not a professional actor) action like that of a buffoon, comical procedure.
f. (of a professional actor, or one who is not) the action, conduct, or profession of a buffoon.
f. a woman (not a professional actress) who acts comically.
f. advice, counsel. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to hold a consultation, to counsel, advise (K.Pr. 87; H. viii, 3; xi, 19), to reconcile (El.).
or masananda a couch, a throne (Rām. 1218); a large cushion, covered with embroidered rugs and the like. --pairȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to spread the rugs, etc., over such a cushioned throne, etc.
m. (as subst., f. mastöñᵘ̈), drunken, drunk, etc. = mast (YZ. 209); as subst., an ascetic who acts like a mad man (or mad woman) (Śiv. 819, 891, 1450) (cf. nanga-mᵒ).

mast, or (q.v.) mas 2 m. (sg. dat. mastas), the hair of the head, the wig (Gr.Gr. 32, 52; L. 460; L.V. 24; Śiv. 197); a curl of hair, ringlet (El.). --kāsun -- m.inf. to cut the hair, to do hair-cutting, to shave (a person, dat.) (K.Pr. 138; H. xii, 4, 5, 10, 13, 19), i.q. mas kāsun. ¶ masta-phash m. hair- dressing, arrangement of the hair. -wāl, a single hair of the head (L.V. 24).

masᵃth, mast مست, or (q.v.) mas 5 adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. mastas, f. pl. masta, K. 276), intoxicated, drunk (Śiv. 383, 1220); lustful, lascivious, wanton; rampant, furious, mad, insane; proud, arrogant (cf. dana-masth, purse-proud, p. 221b, l. 46); plump, well-favoured, vigorous (H. vi, 15); elated, transported, overjoyed, delighted (Śiv. 491); --˚ drunk with; hence, replete with; cf. māl-mast, very wealthy (p. 565a, l. 17; K.Pr. 133). So nanga- masta, entirely naked, mother-naked (K. 276).

or mȧsⁱtī مستی f. intoxication, drunkenness (Śiv. 1260); wantonness, lust; pride, haughtiness. --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. haughtiness, puffed-upness, arrogance, (of one once poor, weak, etc., suddenly become rich, powerful, etc.) to come into existence. --ladüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to become haughty, to presume, swagger, give oneself airs. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. insolence to arise.
f. the action or conduct of a mad ascetic.
m. the husband of a maternal aunt, a maternal uncle by marriage. Cf. mās 3.
f. N. of a certain flower (El. m.; Rām. 650, 1031, 1094, 1273).
adj. c.g. essential, that which is the essence of anything.

f. a mother (Śiv. 494, 624, 869; Rām. 301, 732, 1015, 1187, 1721; K. 535, 1128); used --˚, as in gangā-mātā, Mother Ganges, p. 292a, l. 25 (Śiv. 205, 426, 431, 1137, 1461); Yĕshōdā mātā, Mother Yaśōdā (K. 115), and so on.
adv. in the house of a mother's father (u.w. vbs. of going, being, etc.). Cf. mātāmāl.

m. grief, mourning (YZ. 515, Śiv. 327). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. mourning to fall, sudden grief or mourning to occur (Śiv. 824). -saray or -sarāy (= ماتم سرا) f. a house of mourning, a collection of persons assembled for lamentations (Śiv. 829). ¶ mātama-vyotᵘ (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), full of grief, distraught. ¶ mātamas bĕhun m.inf. to sit for mourning, (of a number of persons) to collect together to lament (for the consolation of those bereaved by death).

m. the home of a mother's father, a maternal grandfather's house (Rām. 166, 262); cf. mātāli. -dorᵘ m. the people of a mother's father's house, a mother's relations. -pokhᵘ m. a relation on the side of a mother's people, a relation through the maternal grandfather. -rag f. relationship through the maternal grandfather. -rē̃ʦh f. some slight relationship with (so-and-so's) maternal grandfather (Gr.Gr. 163). ¶ mātāmālukᵘ adj. (f. mātāmālücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a maternal grandfather's house.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. mātamladiñ), distraught with grief.

or mārtanḍ N. of a famous sacred spring near Islāmābād in Kashmīr. Here there are famous ruins of a temple of the sun (Sanskrit Mārtāṇḍa, from which the name is derived). It is also called Bawan (see bawan 2). Cf. El., s.vv. mártand and maṭan, and RT.Tr. II, 465 (K.Pr. 139, Śiv. 1163).
m. N. of a certain sage (in Skt., Mataṅga) (Rām. 473).

m. (sg. dat. matas), thought, idea; the teaching of a religion or sect, doctrine, belief, creed, religious opinion (Gr.M.); sect, persuasion, party (in religion or philosophy); agreement with, or adherence to, any doctrine or belief; disposition of mind, design, wish, aim, intention, purpose, eagerness to set to work; advice, counsel; intelligence, understanding, power of comprehension. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. eagerness to set to work to become manifest. ¶ mata-wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), a follower of (such-and-such) a creed, etc. ¶ matukᵘ  adj. (f. matücᵘ̈), gen. sg. of math, esp. a follower of (such-and-such) a creed, etc.

or mã̄th f. (sg. dat. māti), conquest, defeat, checkmate (in a contest, or in games such as chess) (Rām. 1316). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to checkmate, to beat, defeat, nonplus. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be conquered, defeated, to lose (a game). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to checkmate, beat, defeat (El., K.Pr. 64). --sapadüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. defeat to occur, to be checkmated, beaten, defeated.

m. (sg. dat. mã̄ṭas), a target, or similar place to aim at in various games of chance (El. mánṭ). ¶ mã̄ṭa-jāy m. a place where there is such a target, a place for gambling, a gambling-hell. -shāy f., id.

m. (sg. dat. maṭas), a large earthen vessel or jar (used for storing rice, liquids, etc.) (K.Pr. 139, 145). ¶ maṭa-hönzᵘ̈ m. (sg. dat. -hönzᵘ̈s or -hānzas (Gr.Gr. 54); the f. -hanzĕñ indicates a woman of the caste or profession), a boatman who works a very large boat for carrying logs and other heavy timber from the forests. -hönzᵘ̈-bāy f. the wife of the preceding.

m. (sg. dat. maṭhas), a small cell or room; a kind of temple dedicated to some particular god (generally built of stone or brick and circular in form), a cella; a travellers' rest-house, as provided in wild parts of the country, where no other accommodation is available; a seminary, college, place of learning.
m. calming, consoling, reassuring (e.g. a frightened or hurt child) (K. 234, 451). --madāra -- m., id.
m. butter-milk, tyre churned without water; the act of churning, churning. --karun -- m.inf. to churn.

m.inf. (1 p.p. maṭhôrᵘ), by gentle hammering to straighten out a bent or dinted piece of metal; met. to calm or console (one who is subjected to annoyance); cf. mạṭhᵃrun. maṭhôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. maṭhörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), hammered straight or flat, as ab.; calmed, consoled, as ab.
adv. sometimes, now and then (u.w. vbs. of coming, going, or the like).
m. (f. mathᵘ̈rᵘ̈), extraordinarily fat, one who is fatter or stouter than his (or her) fellows.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. mothᵘ; 2 p.p. maʦhōv), to rub, anoint, polish by rubbing, rub (something) into (Gr.M.; L.V. 103; K.Pr. 137, 253; YZ. 155, 461; Rām. 159, 413, 874, 1612; H. v, 9; ix, 4); to drag along in the dust; to pound, beat, churn (cf. marʦ mᵒ, p. 594b, l. 7) (Gr.M.). mothᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. müʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), polished, anoited; dragged along in the dust; pounded, churned.

f. N. of a celebrated town in India, the birthplace of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna), and the scene of many of his exploits. Now commonly spelt 'Muttra' (Śiv. 865, 1330, 1468; K. 22, 376, 416, 468, 554, 567, 592-4).
adj. c.g. and adv. (as subst., sg. dat. mātras or mātᵃras), measuring as much as, reaching as far as, as in kshĕna-māthᵃr, the period of an instant (Śiv. 854, 913, 930, 979, 1066, 1163, 1182, 1303).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. mạṭhᵒrᵒ), by gentle repeated hammering to straighten out a bent or dinted piece of metal; met. to mollify, console, persuade, talk over, gain over (an angry or distressed person); cf. maṭhārun. mạṭhᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. mạṭhᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), rendered straight or undinted, as ab.; talked over, gained over, as ab.
f. madness, lunacy, the conduct of a madman (Gr.Gr. 143); conduct like that of a madman.
m. object, intention, aim, purpose (El. mutlab) (Gr.M., K.Pr. 139); the meaning or purport (of anything) (Gr.M.). Cf. matbal.
f. a mother, used ˚--, as in -rǖpⁱ adj. c.g. having the form or character of a mother; performing the duty of a mother (L.V. 54).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. matyōv), madness to arise, to become mad, to become foolish (K.Pr. 139, 215; YZ. 15; K. 263, 284); to rave abusively, violently to give vent to abuse. ¶ mȧtⁱ mȧtⁱ drāmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --drāmüʦᵘ̈ --), (esp. of a child) well known as passionate and unruly (cf. the next). mȧtⁱ mȧtⁱ nērun m.inf. maddened and maddened to go forth; hence, (esp. of a child) to be widely known as passionate and unruly. ¶ matyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. matyē-müʦᵘ̈), gone mad, attacked with lunacy; engaged in raving abuse (against another).
f. madness, lunacy, the conduct of a madman (Gr.Gr. 143); conduct like that of a madman. mȧtⁱlāza karañĕ f. pl. inf. to do mad actions, to act like a madman.

or mō, adv. (prohibition particle, i.q. ma, q.v., but more respectful) (L.V. 30, 36, 72; Śiv. 274, 1003, 1324, 1635, 1671, 1702, 1815; Rām. 727, 816, 1041, etc.). na mō, i.q. mō (Rām. 1231). Cf. mav, mōv.
or (= موقع) m. a fit or proper time, occasion, opportunity (Gr.M.).
m. a time, a season (of the year) (Gr.M.).
adv., i.q. mau, i.e. a prohibitive particle, the same as ma, q.v., but more respectful (Śiv. 1008; Rām. 9, 97, 1030). Cf. mōv.

f. the back of the hand from the wrist to the root of the fingers, the metacarpus (El. máo); a cutting, a branch cut off from a parent tree to be planted separately (El. máo) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1819). --diñᵘ̈ --  f.inf. to apply the palm (to the mouth to conceal it); (in weighing goods) to touch (the scales) with the palm of the hand (so as to make the article weighed appear more than it really is), to give false weight. ¶ māvi māvi adv. in handfuls, fistfuls (Śiv. 1212). --roṭᵘ tōl -- m. weighing fairly (in which the beam of the scales hang from a string fastened to the middle of the beam and held in the palm of the hand); giving false weight by privily pressing the beam of the scales with the palm of the hand.
(for 2, see māwurᵘ) f. N. of a certain river (the Māhurī of Sanskrit) in Mȧchⁱpūr Pargana (RT.Tr. II, 425).
f. the dewlap of an ox.

or mŏwal 1 f. N. of a certain plant, the cockscomb (Amaranthus cruentus). Bread-cakes made from the seed are a common food with the peasants (El. mawur). According to L. 75 (mowal) its seeds are used in medicine as a demulcent.
adj. c.g. (of a cloth) possessing an edge or fringe.
according to L. 463, N. of a kind of rice, a good cropper with a red grain.

f. (sg. dat. often written māwȧsi), the day of the new moon, when the sun and moon dwell together or are in conjunction; the 15th day of the dark half of every lunar month (cf. khĕʦi-māwas, p. 424a, l. 46) (L.V. 22; Śiv. 209, 526, 740). --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to observe the rites of the night of the new moon. --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to keep or observe ritely the night of the new moon. ¶ māwȧsi-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the night of the new moon (Śiv. 1042).
m. something in exchange, compensation, return, retaliation; a fitting reply, a retort (Rām. 841).

m. the edge or fringe of a cloth. ¶ māwȧlⁱ-trọ̆pⁱ m. a kind of hem joining the edges of two cloths. -ʦhyonᵘ adj. (f. -ʦhë˘ñᵘ̈), having the edge or fringe torn. -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), having its edge or fringe cut off.
adj. (f. māvᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 2), (of a person) reserved, uncommunicative, secretive.

f. magic, illusion; love (for earthly things) (L.V. 67); illusion (in the sense of māyā, q.v.) (K. 18, 247, 295, 409); love, affection (K.Pr. 201, may; YZ. 474; Śiv. 39, 103, 536, 1136, 1140, 1472, 1619, 1743; Rām. 158, 270, 303, 987, 1363, 1516, etc.; K. 470, 1101-2); sitting apart secretly, on secret watch (cf. brörⁱ-māy, p. 125b, l. 40; hāpath-māy, p. 342b, l. 42; mūdⁱ-māy, p. 549b, l. 9) (YZ. 383, 490); cf. māyā. --bögᵃrüñᵃ -- or --böjᵃrüñᵃ -- f.inf. to divide out love, to behave lovingly to every one, to show a very kindly general disposition. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. affection to come into existence, love (for so-and-so) to be felt (for the first time). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to remain hidden and watchful, to act secretly (Rām. 1465). --lāgüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to put on secrecy, i.e. to pretend to be asleep, or motionless and inattentive, in order to discover some hidden matter, to play the spy in this way. ¶ māyĕ-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, affection; hence, one who exhibits a general affectionate disposition. -rǖpⁱ adj. c.g. acting in the character of a deceiver, (f.) a Delilah (L.V. 54). -rosᵘ or -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), void of affection, heartless, unfeeling, unkind.

or mai می f. wine, spirituous liquor (K.Pr. 131; Śiv. 1863; Rām. 513, 1489); nectar, a drink which restores a dead man to life (Rām. 1500). mai-khāna می خانہ m. a wine house, wine shop (El. mekhāna, K.Pr. 131).
adj. c.g. used --˚, consisting of, composed of, as in shiwa-may (L.V. 16) consisting only of Śiva; shŏda-ʦĕtta-būda-may, consisting of pure discrimination (Śiv. 1850).
i.q. ma or mā, prohibitive particle (H. v, 2, poet.).

f. illusion, trick, artifice, deception; an illusory image, a phantasm; (or māy, q.v.; K. 18, 247, 295, 409) an illusory phantom (often personified) sent forth by the Deity to confound sinners (K. 17, 42, 48, 72, 78-9, 214, 293, 301, 409, 592-3, 757, 774, 960); spiritual illusion, an illusive power depending on the Deity, whereby mankind believe in the existence of external objects which are in fact purely ideal, the illusory power which prevents man from recognizing his identity with the Supreme (Śiv. 17, 30-1, 34, 46, 96, 158, etc.; Rām. 179); the external world, Nature personified; worldly (as distinct from spiritual) prosperity, opulence, riches (Śiv. 84, K. 1157); compassion, pity, sympathy; love, affection (cf. māy). This word and māy and māyĕ are commonly used interchangeably. -gan adj. c.g. well supplied with accumulated wealth, rich, wealthy; cf. māyĕ. -kạtsupera;ra m. a little store of wealth (cf. kạtᵃra), esp. the secret savings of a miser. -pholᵘ m. a hidden hoard of wealth. -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), possessing much wealth, wealthy, rich; cf. māyĕ-sāvĕr, s.v. māyĕ. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), possessing wealth, wealthy, rich. -zāl m. the noose of affection, the bonds of love; the noose of illusion (Śiv. 67, 424); a figure drawn on the ground by the Brāhmaṇs at the burning of a Hindū corpse (El.).
adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. māyātītas), one who has passed beyond illusion (see māyā), one who is not subject to illusion (Śiv. 1458).

m. source, root, origin, essence, substance; wealth, money, cash, means (El. máyih) (cf. māyā); capital, stock, principal; ferment, leaven; a kind of gruel given to an invalid or to one who is convalescent (cf. ana- māyĕ, p. 29b, l. 49); paste (for fixing paper, etc.), glue (El. máyí, Gr.M.); glue, size (Gr.M.); grain (swelling, but not ripe) (L. 460, máyah). -sāvĕr m. (of a person) plenteousness of wealth; (of a thing or work) richness in essential attributes, greatness of intrinsic value; (of paper, etc.) the condition of being thoroughly covered with paste or size. Cf. māyā- sôwᵘ, s.v. māyā.
adj. c.g. thick, solid, strong, substantial; rich, wealthy; fermented; (of paper) well covered with paste, sized, smooth (Gr.M.). Cf. māyĕ.
f. a certain dish composed of rice, ghī, and spices cooked in buttermilk, and used in oblations.
adj. c.g. deceitful, fraudulent; N. of a demon (Rām. 457).

m. flesh, the flesh of the body (cf. athukᵘ māz, p. 66a, l. 33; maʦhi-mᵒ, p. 609a, l. 48; and nam ta mᵒ, s.v. nam 1) (K.Pr. 121, 152, 156, 232; Rām. 984, 1445, 1577, 1657; H. vii, 14, 24); flesh, meat, butcher's meat (cf. gabi-māz, p. 275a, l. 14; gurⁱ-mⁱ, p. 298b, l. 48; hūnⁱ-mⁱ, p. 337a, l. 4; kŏkar-mᵒ, p. 432a, l. 39; kala-mᵒ, p. 435a, l. 22; môwᵘ-mᵘ, p. 611b, l. 14) (W. 114; L. 461; K.Pr. 36, 84, 199, 237); the fleshy part of fruit (El.); cf. māmas and mās 2. -bēr  f. 'a hedge of flesh', swelling of the gums. -khĕl m. a mushroom (Agaricus campestris) (El. mánskhel; L. 73, mazkhel). It is found on the walnut, pine, and mulberry. -khāv m. a flesh-eater, one who is fond of eating flesh, one who is carnivorous; a kind of water insect that bites the body; a certain disease in which the fleshy parts of the body waste away in sores. -kūṭᵘ̈ f. a long strip of meat. --ladun -- m.inf. to build flesh, to become stout (from eating good food, leading a jolly life, and so on). -lal f. a flesh-blister, a throbbing in the soft flesh. -lŏponᵘ adj. (f. -lŏpüñᵘ̈), 'a flesh jar,' a short very fleshy man, a fat little fool. -mēchĕr m. 'sweetness of flesh', mutual affection. -myulᵘ  m. union of flesh, near relationship (marked by mutual affection). -nāṭh f. flesh for food, esp. mutton (El. mads-nāṭa, m.); cf. nāṭh. -pholᵘ m. a lump or piece of meat. -palav m. a flat piece of meat cut off with the skin attached. -rān f. (sg. dat. -röñᵘ̈), the meat of the thigh (as in a leg of mutton). -tikh m. (sg. dat. tikas), a small piece of meat. --tulun -- m.inf. to raise the flesh, to raise weals by flogging; cf. mūrĕn mᵒ tᵒ, p. 589a, l. 31. -vĕtharan f. a stout, fleshy, woman (esp. an old one). ¶ māza-bŏy f. 'the smell of flesh', the natural affection which springs up between near relations. mada-māza wālun m.inf. to cause to descend from pride and from flesh; hence, to destroy a person's pride and bravery, utterly to humiliate and destroy (Śiv. 857).

m. taste, savour, relish, smack (K.Pr. 16, 255) (cf. nūna-mᵒ, s.v. nūn); a titbit; delight, pleasure, enjoyment (Gr.M.; K. 25, 223, 648, 650, 716); jest, joke, fun, sport, amusement. --gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. flavours to go, i.e. to exhibit apparent disgust (for something really longed for). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take flavour, to taste, to enjoy (lit. and fig.); to take pleasure, to enjoy oneself, to revel. --karȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to enjoy oneself; to enjoy or amuse oneself (at the expense of), to make sport or fun (of), to laugh (at). --lagun -- m.inf. pleasure, enjoyment, to be experienced (K. 148, 220, 277). -motᵘ adj. (f. -müʦᵘ̈), enjoyment-mad, full of enjoyment (K. 255); giving enjoyment, ravishing, rapturous. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), tasteless (El.). --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause taste to enter, to give (one) a taste (of); to show (one) some sport or fun, to afford (one) enjoyment. --wuchun -- m.inf. to test the taste (of), to see how (a thing) tastes; to show indifference (to something unpleasant). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. enjoyment, flavour, or pleasure to be felt.
مزہ دار adj. c.g. tasty, savoury, tasteful, palatable, delicious (lit. and fig.).
adj. c.g. of, or relating to, a religion, or sect, etc. (Gr.M.).

m. (sg. dat. mazākas), taste, relish; wit, humour; (in Kāshmīrī) false comforting, consoling a person with promises which are not fulfilled; a practical joke (K.Pr. 125). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. disappointment to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to console or conciliate with false promises. ¶ mazāka-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is accustomed to console or conciliate with false promises.
f. (sg. dat. māzüñᵘ̈), a kind of twig broom (Gr.Gr. 121).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. māzanôwᵘ), to cause (a person) to like (something previously disliked), to cause (a person) to acquire a taste (for).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. māzonᵘ), (of something previously not wished for, or disliked) to make (it) an object of desire, to acquire a taste for. māzonᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. māzüñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), become an object of desire. Cf. māzun.

m. a place of visitation; a Musalmān shrine; (amongst Musalmāns) a sepulchre, tomb, grave, a graveyard (L. 271). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go to the tomb; hence, to become dead (used in imprecations, etc.). -bal m. a Musalmān graveyard.
f. (sg. dat. māzarüʦᵘ̈), an apology; (in Kāshmīrī) words of welcome (to a guest on arrival), hospitality (K.Pr. 203); hospitable pressing to eat (at a feast, etc.) (Śiv. 1072).
n.ag. (f. māzavüñᵘ̈), one who has acquired a taste (for something not previously liked); one who cleans out dregs from the inside of a vessel.
adj. c.g. firm, fixed, fast, tight (Gr.M.); strong, stout.
f. (sg. dat.mazēṭhi), madder, the plant and its dye (L. 344, majjit; 68, mazait = Rubia cordifolia or its substitute Geranium nepalense). Cf. maĩz; El. majíth or manjít, both m.

m. a place of manifestation, scene of a deed, a theatre, stage (El., K.Pr. 86); the object or manifestation (of divine vengeance, etc.); the breaking out of a deadly epidemic. --wŏthun -- m.inf. an epidemic to break out. --yunᵘ -- m.inf., id.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. mazharladiñ), one who is afflicted by an epidemic disease.
m. the contents of a writing or letter, import, sense, tenour, purport (Rām. 842).
adj. c.g. one who consoles with promises which he does not fulfil, conciliating with false promises.
m. the man in charge of a Musalmān graveyard.

f. harm, injury, hurt, detriment. --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of a person) to become utterly exhausted or fatigued and incapable of doing more. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. great exhaustion or fatigue to be experienced.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. môzᵘ; 2 p.p. māzōv), to acquire a taste (for), to become addicted (to) (esp. with reference to something not previously desired) (Gr.Gr. 121); to clean out the inside of a vessel, to wipe out dregs. Cf. māzanun. ¶ môzᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mözᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), desired, wanted; (of a vessel) having the dregs inside wiped or cleaned out. ¶ māzan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who acquires a taste (for anything), one who desires something not previously wished for.
m. madness, lunacy (Gr.Gr. 140, Rām. 709, K. 290). --anun -- m.inf. to bring madness, to cause madness; madness to arise. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. madness to arise.
m. (sg. dat. maʦas), a fish (esp. a large one) (Śiv. 1755, 1817); the fish incarnation of Viṣṇu (Vishnu) (Śiv. 854).

f. (sg. dat. maʦhi), the upper- arm (between the shoulder and the elbow) (properly the region of the biceps and triceps, El.) (YZ. 106, 458, 497; Śiv. 201; Rām. 443; H. x, 5). ¶ maʦha-band m. a kind of ornament or charm tied on the arm below the shoulder. -gagur m. (sg. dat. -gagaras), a certain animal inhabiting the mountain forests, described as a large kind of winged rat, ? a flying fox. --ʦāpañĕ -- f.inf. to bite one's arms; hence, to feel and exhibit great regret (e.g. by silent weeping or the like). -zōr m. muscular strength of the arms. ¶ maʦhi-ganḍas thawun m.inf. to keep (for someone) with great care (as if keeping it tied under the arm). -khash m. a wound on the arm; met. worry owing to having to incur great expense, or to losing a large sum of money. -māz khyonᵘ m.inf. to eat the flesh of one's arm; to show anxious desire.

f. (sg. dat. maʦhi), pounded meat (it is pounded to a paste in a mortar). ¶ maʦhi-dāl f. a dish of this pounded meat, with crushed pulse. -ganḍ m. a piece of pounded meat roasted or fried. -worᵘ m. a soup containing balls (or cakes) of this pounded meat fried in oil.
f. (sg. dat. maʦhi), conciliatory treatment, persuasiveness, persuading by gentle means, consolation (Gr.Gr. 147). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to treat in a conciliatory manner or persuasively.
adj. (f. maʦhilᵘ̈ [sic]), hard, tough (e.g. grain hard to pound).
adj. (f. maʦhijᵘ̈), kindly, affectionate, tender, consolatory (Gr.Gr. 147); arousing affection, interesting, enchanting (i.q. a work, a book, etc.).
f. (sg. dat. mạʦᵃrüñᵃ), the act of driving mad; tantalizing, tantalization.
conj. 1 (mạʦᵃrôwᵃ), to drive mad, madden (Gr.Gr. 7, Rām. 1313); to tantalize; to delude, mislead, deceive (Śiv. 1399). Cf. mạʦᵃrun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mạʦᵒrᵒ), to drive mad (Rām. 1313); to tantalize; to deceive, delude (Rām. 323). Cf. mạʦᵃrāwun.
m. sweetness (of food, speech, voice, lit. or fig.; cf. atha-ᵒ, p. 59b, l. 40); taste (El.). Cf. myūṭhᵘ 2.
m. (f. mēgiñᵘ̈, q.v.), N. of a certain untouchable caste, the Mēgh or Mēg of the Panjāb hill-country. mēga-bāy f. the wife of a Mēg.
f. a woman of the Mēg caste (see mēg) (but the wife of a Mēg is mēga-bāy).
or mihnath محنت m. (also occasionally, as in Gr.M., f.) (sg. dat. mĕhanatas or, if f., mĕhanüʦᵘ̈ (Gr.M. 1836)), toil, exertion, labour (El., Gr.M., K.Pr. 142 (mĕhnatas, sg. dat.)).
m. a guest; a poor orphan (who is always somebody's guest) (K.Pr. 261).
or (El.) mahmāndörī مہماندآری f. hospitality. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show hospitality, to entertain (El.).
adj. c.g. laborious, diligent, industrious, painstaking (Gr.M.).
m. a Major (the English word); (in Kāshmīrī) a superior officer, e.g. a head groom or master of the horse (H. x, 5, 12, 13).

f. (sg. dat. mēkhi), a nail, a pin of wood or iron; a peg, tent-peg; a stake, pile, post; a wedge, spike. --bagārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. after abusing and threatening (a person, esp. a woman) to award punishment, to add injury to insult. --diñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to fasten, or hammer in, a nail, etc.

f. the ceremony of investing a youth with the brahmanical thread (El. mēkhla). --tārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to carry out this investiture. ¶ mēkhali mahārāza m. the hero of this investiture, the youth who is invested. -wôlᵘ m. the particular youth (among his brothers in a family) who is to be so invested; the father or other guardian of the youth; a priest or other person worthy of performing the ceremony.
or mĕkarāz f. a pair of scissors (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 165, 192); shears (Gr.M.); pincers (Gr.M.).

m. meeting, coming together, assemblage (Gr.Gr. 124); union, intercourse; mixture, mixing together (Śiv. 1020); agreement, reconciliation; concord, intimacy, friendship, acquaintance (Gr.M.);.M.).; an interview; metting (Gr.M.). -gēl m. close intimacy, close alliance; familiarity. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. friendship, intimacy to occur; a meeting (of two persons) to occur; mixing together, trituration together to occur; and so on through the various meanings of mēl. --thawun -- m.inf. to have or keep up an intimate friendship, to associate (with) (Gr.M.).

m. meeting, assembly, company (cf. mȧtⁱ-mⁱ, s.v. motᵘ 1); a large concourse of people (for religious or commercial purposes), a fair (esp. at some sacred place). -mahārāza m. the manager or getter- up of a spectacle at a fair. -motᵘ m. the festival or holiday of a fair at some holy place.
f. a present given, at the first meeting after a marriage, by the near relatives of the bride to the bride's father-in-law and mother-in-law.

n.ag. (f. mēlavüñᵘ̈), that which is becoming joined or united (to something else); that which can be easily found or met with (even though usually rare or scarce); one who is accustomed to show a friendly disposition to others, one who is urbane, conciliatory.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. myūlᵘ (Gr.Gr. 19, K. 1129), f. mījᵘ̈ (K.Pr. 3, 425); 2 p.p. mĕjyōv); to be joined, be united (Gr.Gr. 124, 205; Śiv. 473, 511, 1313, 1390, 1616; Rām. 1088, 1435, 1501, 1548; K. 701, 846) (cf. nēthᵃr mᵒ); to be met with, be found (Gr.Gr. 205; Gr.M.; YZ. 17, 27); to be joined (to a person), to be got (by, dat.), to be attained to (by, dat.) (cf. hūhū mēlun, to be chilled, p. 325a, l. 8) (Gr.M.; L.V. 78, 79; K.Pr. 3; Śiv. 1012, 1844, 1897; K. 845); to be met, encountered (Śiv. 1067, 1313, 1809; Rām. 140, 264, 534, 917, 1528; K. 102, 425, 689, 699, 700, 706, 1016, 1129); to come to hand, come into possession, be found (after search) (K.Pr. 258); to be united (with), become one (with), be absorbed (in, dat.) (L.V. 1, 68, 105; YZ. 24; Śiv. 164, 527, 1429, 1538, 1775); to agree (with), be reconciled (to) (Gr.M.); to have sexual union (with a woman); to agree (with), resemble exactly, be exactly alike (Gr.M.); to be mixed (with) (Rām. 100, 1502); to be joined in combat (Rām. 864); to mix (?) (El.). ¶ mīlith gīlith bĕhun m.inf. to live in cordial intercourse, to live in harmony. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. having become united to go, to go away together, or in a body (L.V. 9, K. 107); to become united (to), mingled (with, dat.), absorbed (in, dat.) (L.V. 11, 29, 30, 69; Śiv. 55, 1775; Rām. 521, payas-kun, absorbed in the clue). --rōzun -- m.inf. to unite and live with, to live in harmony (with). ¶ myūlᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mījᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), joined, united; met with, obtained, found after search; mingled, mixed up.

f. (sg. dat. mīñᵘ̈), measurement, measuring. Cf. atha-mēn, p. 60a, l. 17. ¶ mēna-mēn f. measuring over and over again, keeping on measuring (e.g. along piece of land requiring measurement in several places). -tōl measuring and weighing.
f. wages paid for weighing or measuring, a weighman's fee, etc.
n.ag. (f. mēnavüñᵘ̈), one who weighs or measures, a weighman, a measurer.
conj. 3 to suffer from leprosy (cf. myondᵘ 1), used in the following:--mĕndith marun m.inf. to die of leprosy (or some other terrible disease) (an expression used principally in malediction).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. mĕndⁱladiñ), afflicted with leprosy (W. 111).

f. the temple of the head (El. menga, myeng). --hāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show the temple, a scornful contradiction or counter-statement to be made in emulation by a powerless person. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make scornful contradiction or counter-statement, as ab. ¶ mĕnga-dag f. a blow on the temple, i.e. continual unseemly prating or chattering; a headache (caused thereby) (K.Pr. 158). -dagal adj. c.g. a continual chatterer. -ʦörⁱ m.pl. the middle part of the temple. --wŏthañĕ -- f. pl. inf. the temples to rise, to frown in anger. ¶ mĕngan-nār 1 (for 2, see mĕngun), fire in the temples, anger accompanied by flushing of the temples.
adj. c.g. possessing a temple (of the head); met. haughty, arrogant, domineering, hectoring, blustering.
or mĕngüñᵘ̈ f. rat's dung (f. dim. of mĕngun, q.v.). ¶ mĕngañĕ-gôrᵘ a kind of water-chestnut (the unbroken nut). - görᵘ̈ f. the dried kernel of the preceding.

m. (sg. dat. mĕngāṭas), an indication or mark of pride or arrogance (e.g. such as the mode of wearing a turban, etc.) (cf. mĕng). --hāwun -- m.inf. to display such an indication; hence, to assume a threatening or bullying attitude.

m. (sg. dat. mĕnganas), sheep (or goats') dung (El. mengin; L. 459, mengan); (met.) a little boy (because small and of no account) (K.Pr. 249). mĕngan-nār 2 (for 1, see mĕng) m. a fire of dried sheep (or goats') dung.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. myūnᵘ (Gr.Gr. 26), f. mīñᵘ̈; 2 p.p. mēñōv), to measure (length, superficies, or quantity) (Gr.Gr. 5, 21, 104; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 127, 155; YZ. 421; Śiv. 1592); to estimate, guess (El.). ¶ mēnan-bāna m. a measuring vessel, a measure (holding so much). -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a measurer, surveyor. ¶ myūnᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mīñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), measured, that which has been measured.
f. a woman who sells firewood; the wife of a male seller of firewood. See mĕnzur.
or mĕnzȧrⁱgī f. the profession of selling firewood.
or mĕnzᵃr m. (sg. dat. mĕnzaras; f. mĕnzarĕñ), a seller of firewood, a wood-seller; cf. narakukᵘ-mᵘ, s.v. narukh. mĕnzar-wān or mĕnzȧrⁱ-wān a public fire-wood market.
f. the soft unripe fruit of the singhārā, or water-chestnut (cf. gôrᵘ 1). It is easily split with a knife or by the nails, and is considered a great delicacy (Gr.Gr. 25, myas).
mĕthun, or mithun f. (sg. dat. mĕthani or mĕ(mi)thuni ), the third sign of the Zodiac, Gemini (Śiv. 482, K. 130).
f. the gift given to the bridegroom by the members of the bride's family on her going to her husband's house after the marriage. Cf. mȧtⁱ-mūr (p. 602b, l. 23).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. mēṭhyōv), to become sweet (in taste) (Gr.Gr. 21, K.Pr. 62); (of a sour person) to become sweet-tempered; to attain to a pleasant condition; to become intently interested in any matter. mēṭhyō-motᵘ perf. part. (mēṭhyē-müʦᵘ̈), sweetened, etc., as ab.

m.(sg. dat. mĕtras), a friend (Gr.Gr. 144; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 9, 22, 47, 78, 126, 141, 142; Rām. 154, 179, 450, 837, 1162, 1318, 1756, 1781; K. 44, 102, 365, 477, 871, 888). --sapadun -- m.inf. to become a friend, to befriend; to connive at, to share, to be a party to (El.). ¶ mĕtra-bāy f. a female friend; the wife of a friend. -gara m. the home or house of a friend. -hāl f. (sg. dat. -höjᵘ̈), the abode of a friend, the place or country where a friend lives. -kār m. the deeds which should be done by a friend, a friend's duties.
f. a female friend (El. mitharain). Cf. mẹ̆thᵃr.
or mĕtᵃruth m. (sg. dat. mĕtratas), friendship (Gr.Gr. 144, K.Pr. 17). Cf. mẹ̆thᵃr.

f. (sg. dat. mĕcĕ), the ball of any kind of food rolled in the hand before putting it into the mouth, a gobbit of food (cf. ana-mᵒ, p. 29b, l. 42; bata-mᵒ, p. 137a, l. 28; hūnⁱ-mⁱ, p. 336b, l. 50; mimizⁱ-mⁱ, p. 571b, l. 21; K.Pr. 247, pl. dat. michan, 133 (nom. sg. miṭ), 245 (with indef. art. mĕṭah); a small lump or ball of the size of such a gobbit (cf. burza-mᵒ, p. 130b, l. 38, and bata-mᵒ, as ab.). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to become a gobbit, i.e. met. of something soft, to be crushed up into a lump and spoiled. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make a gobbit, i.e. met. to crush something up in the hand and so spoil it. ¶ mĕcĕ-khāv m. (f. -khöviñ), a fellow who eats gobbits, i.e. who goes to people on whom he has no claim and eats gobbits of their food (as a beggar might do). -tār m. accomplishing by gobbits, i.e. met. (in some great work which requires great expense and exertions to carry out) to work at it with very small means.
m. the cry of a cat, mewing, mew; cf. myauv. -brôrᵘ m. (f. -brörᵘ̈), a mew-cat, a cat accustomed to mewing; a crying child (that mews like a cat).

or mēwa میوہ m. a fruit (Śiv. 367, mēᵒ; H. xii, 21, 22). -gorᵘ m. a fruiterer (K.Pr. 142). -hēr f. a ladder (for plucking fruit from a high tree). -kulᵘ m. a fruit-tree. -kani m. (a present) of fruit (given on the occasion of a visit to a bride or bridegroom by the relations of the other). -pholᵘ m. a heap or collection of a few fruit. -ʦhürᵘ̈ f. a fruit-basket, a basket for holding fruit. -wüñᵘ̈ f. a piece of ground containing fruit-trees. -zār m. a collection of many kinds of fruit.
adj. c.g. possessing fruit, fruitful, fertile (El.).
m. an entertainer, a host; (in Kāshmīrī) a guest (K.Pr. 135; H. vii, 4).
adj. c.g. mixed with earth, connected with, or attached to, earth.
adj. (f.mĕʦivᵘ̈), made of earth, earthen (Gr.Gr. 161, K.Pr. 50, Rām. 1378).

f. earth, soil, land, clay, loam, dust (Gr.Gr. 161, 164; Gr.M.; W. 8, mėts; L.V. 44; K.Pr. 50, 71, 143, 144, 152, 191, 250; YZ. 394; Śiv. 353, 1290, 1527; Rām. 116, 918, 1199, 1371, 1603, 1672, 1724; K. 160, 396, 432); (cf. nāwa-mᵒ, s.v. nāv 2). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to become (or turn to) clay; met. to suffer grievous disappointment; to feel oneself utterly disgraced, to feel plunged in humiliation. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to pull out the clay, i.e. to pull up by the root; met. to uproot, utterly to destroy; to be employed on useless labour (used as an expression of censure, etc.). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make into earth; met. to make worthless (esp. to spoil or defile food so as to make it uneatable); by public abuse or the like to humiliate a respectable person. ¶ mĕʦi- (or mĕʦĕ-) bāna  m. an earthenware vessel (in pl. earthenware) (Gr.M.). -bôrᵘ m. a load of earth or mud carried on the shoulders (cf. bôrᵘ 1); mud-plaster (cf. bôrᵘ 2). -dọ̆gᵘ m. a fist of earth; hence, the lump of mud fixed on a potter's wheel (to be shaped into a vessel, etc.). -hönzᵘ̈ m. a mud-boatman, a boatman who brings down earth from the foothills for sale in the city (W. 115). -hönzᵘ̈-bāy f. his wife. -hānzañ f. a boatwoman who sells earth, as ab. -khāv m. one who habitually eats clay (a form of disease); a kind of worm or maggot (described as resembling a thick thumb). -lam or -lamb m. a place outside a village or town where earth is dug out and collected to serve for making plaster, etc. -lŏponᵘ m. a receptacle shaped like a huge jar, and made of unbaked clay, for holding grain, etc.; a hollow in the ground in which clay is stored. -liwun m. mud-plaster. --murⁱ trāwȧnⁱ -- m.pl.inf. to relieve the skirts of earth; a method of ordeal to discover something believed to be stolen. The owner of the property compels the persons suspected to take earth from a heap and to carry it in the skirts of their garments (cf. murᵘ) to some other place and there to fling it down so as to form a new heap. The idea is that the one of the suspected persons who is the actual thief will take the opportunity of flinging down the stolen article hidden in one of his loads of earth, so as to restore the article without his guilt being discovered. When the new pile is completed, the owner privately searches in it, and finds his property. He thus gets it back, and the thief avoids detection. -mŏyā f. a little earth (Gr.Gr. 165). --nūn dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to put salt into the ground, to sow with salt, to render the ground barren; met. to ruin a person (esp. in revenge). -pholᵘ m. a little earth (Gr.Gr. 164). -phọ̆tᵘ m. a basket of (i.e. containing) earth (Gr.Gr. 73). -thabun m. a large lump of moistened earth (made into a lump for some purpose). -tār m. an earthen lamp-shelf. -wôñᵘ m. muddy water.

f. (sg. dat. (?) mīzᵘ̈), a certain medicinal root; pounded and mixed with butter it is used as an ointment for surface swellings. If this is the same as the Sanskrit mēdā, the form of the dat. is doubtful. mida-sat (El.) Cuscuta reflexa.
or (sometimes written mēg 2) m. cloud (Śiv. 268, 575, 1557; K. 56). ¶ mīga-zã̄ḍ f. a heavy mass of dark clouds (such as causes darkness). -zāl m. a long line of clouds.
adj. c.g. covered with jeweller's rouge (of an ornament); (of a silver or gold ornament) coloured, painted with a paste.
m. the pulpit in a Musalmān mosque (El.).
adj. c.g. friendly, kind, loving, affectionate, benevolent (El., Gr.M.); as subst. m. a friend.

f. favour, kindness, friendliness, goodness (El., Gr.M.); a favour, a kindness (Gr.M.). --karith -- conj. part. having done a kindness; hence, as interj. please! (Gr.M.). ¶ mihrböniyĕ-kinⁱ adv. by means of kindness; hence, please! pray! be good enough to (do so-and-so) (Gr.M.). -sṻty adv., i.q. -kinⁱ (Gr.M.); with kindness, in a kindly manner (Gr.M.); through (so-and-so's) kindness (Gr.M.).

m. jeweller's rouge, a plate-powder, a powder for polishing jewelry; any fine powder. -gorᵘ m. maker of, or worker with, jeweller's rouge. --khārun -- m.inf. to apply jeweller's rouge to an ornament or the like.

f. (sg. dat. mīli), ink (Gr.M., W. 8, L. 461). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to mark a heap (of grain or the like to prevent theft). ¶ mīli-ondurᵘ m. an ink-pot, an ink-bottle; cf. andar. -bônᵘ m. an ink-vessel, an ink-bottle; cf. bāna 1. -ḍṻs m. an ink-stick, a stick used for mixing ink. -dawāth f. an inkstand, a pen- case and ink-bottle combined (W. 33). -gorᵘ m. an ink-maker, an ink-seller. -kalam m. an ink-pen, a pen suitable for writing with ink; a pen full of ink. -ʦrüṭᵘ̈ f. a pill of dry ink, from which ink is made by mixture with water. -wôñᵘ m. ink-water, the water with which an ink-bottle is washed, inky water. -wörᵘ̈ f. an ink-vessel, a jar in which ink is stored (not an ink-bottle for writing).
f. intimate association with some impurity, e.g. of oil with a portion of sediment or milk with a portion of water (Gr.Gr. 128).
in milan-sār adj. c.g. of an amicable disposition, warm-hearted; cf. milasār. -sôrᵘ adj. (f. -sörᵘ̈), id.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. milanôwᵘ), to unite, join, add, connect, attach (Gr.M.; Śiv. 905, 1010, 1556, 1621, 1688, 1827); to cause to meet, bring together, introduce (one person to another) (Gr.M.); to put side by side, to compare (one thing with another) (Gr.M.); to mix (El., Gr.M.). milanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. milanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), joined, connected; brought together, introduced (to each other).
m. a confederate (El.); cf. milan-sār, s.v. milan. --sapadun -- m.inf. to connive (at), to share, to be a party (to) (El.).
m. (sg. dat. milatas), religion, faith, creed; a religious community, church.
f. (sg. dat. milavüñᵘ̈), mutual joining, union, commingling; being close together, close proximity, close association (K.Pr. 125).

conj. 1 (i.q. milanāwun, q.v.; 1 p.p. milowᵘ), to unite, join (cf. jogᵘ milawun, p. 371a, l. 50) (Gr.Gr. 121, 128; Gr.M.; L.V. 69; Śiv. 307, 662, 1654, 1831); to add together (Gr.M.); to commingle, intermingle, mix (Śiv. 353); laḍöyⁱ milavüñᵘ̈, to join battle (H. x, 1). milowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. milüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), united, joined; mixed, mingled.
or (El.) miliʦār m. mixing, mingling; coalescence (of several things); agreement, harmony, concord, mutual good understanding; society (El.); an accident (El.).
f. an earthen vessel for containing the chalk ink used by boys at school, a kind of ink-bottle; cf. mīl. milᵃri-wörᵃ or mila-wörᵘ̈ f., id.
f. a bundle or skein of string (cf. pana-mᵒ, s.v. pan 3).
f. (sg. dat. milᵃrüñᵃ), uniting, joining together, mixing together (e.g. mixing boiled rice with curds).
m. property, landed property, an estate (Gr.M.).

m. the afternoon; the afternoon meal, luncheon; the midday meal of children (El.; Gr.Gr. 157; L. 461, mimuz; K.Pr. 104, 176, id.). This is the word used by Hindūs, Musalmāns employ nimyuzᵘ. ¶ mimizⁱ lŏngüñᵘ̈ f. 'the afternoon pipkin', the afternoon lunch composed of roasted grain, etc. -më̆ṭᵘ̈ f. 'the afternoon lump (or ball)', a little food or slight snack eaten in the afternoon. -wakhᵃth (sg. dat. -waktas), the afternoon meal (of man or beast). -vēla m. the afternoon time, the afternoon (as a space of time). ¶ mimizis adv. at the time of the afternoon meal, in the afternoon (Gr.Gr. 157). -bögi or -bögin adv. in or about the afternoon.
m. Pisces (the sign of the zodiac) (El.; Śiv. 480; Rām. 419, 1278).

m. a kiss (on the mouth, cheek, forehead, or the like), kissing (Gr.Gr. 132); cf. mŏñ and muñ. miñĕ-pūtᵘ m. a loving kiss on the mouth (face to face) (esp. as given to a child) (Gr.Gr. 132). Cf. mŏñe-pūtᵘ, col. b, l. 5, and muñĕ-pūtᵘ, col. b, l. 39.
f. a frog (cf. main). miñĕ-mŏnḍukh m. (sg. dat. -mŏnḍakas), a frog (Śiv. 1827). Cf. nĕñĕ-mŏnḍukh, s.v. nĕñĕ 3.

f. (sg. dat. minüʦᵘ̈), kindness, favour, obligation; grace, courtesy; entreaty, humble and earnest supplication, an entreaty which humiliates the entreater, asking a favour (Gr.M.); grateful thanks, praise. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to acknowledge the granting of a favour, to admit an obligation. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. voluntarily to undergo the humiliation of asking a favour. --mānath -- f. the formal begging (for the bride), the formal proposal of marriage made by the bridegroom's people to the bride's people. --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to humiliate a person (i.e. by the granter calling the grantee's attention to his generosity) in granting a favour, to put (a person under) an obligation. ¶ minüʦᵘ̈-rostᵘ̈ adj. (f. - rüʦhᵘ̈), (obtained) without the necessity of asking a favour. ¶ minüʦᵘ̈n-tal karun m.inf. to humiliate a person by often putting him under favours (and talking about it).

m. a chief, leader, master, head, prince; a title by which the Saiyids (or descendants of the family of Muḥammad) are called; the winner in a game; esp. in the game of mīri mīri phaʦh played by children (see mīr 2). Used --˚ to indicate something specially large or excellent, as in dāna-mīr, a big cooking-stove (p. 221a, l. 39); jāna-mīr, a darling son (p. 374b, l. 25); gagar-mīr, Sir Rat (K.Pr. 63); jāna-mīr in Rām. 1126 is translated 'a living being' (quasi, a lord of life, one who possesses life). mīr-akhur = میرآخور m. a master of the horse, a head groom (K.Pr. 95).

or mīrᵘ̈ f. the larger hole in the ground which serves as a mark in the game of pitching walnuts, called mīri mīri phaʦh, for an account of which see K.Pr. 142. The smaller hole is called phaʦh. mīri gaʦhun m. to reach the mark (in tipcat) (Śiv. 1015) or in the above game; met. to win (in gaming, disputing), to succeed in an almost hopeless task.
m. the officer in charge of irrigation, in special charge of each main channel, whose duty used to be to see to repairs and to call out labour (L. 323).
m. a master of the horse; a groom (El.). I.q. mīr-akhur, p. 587b, l. 32.
m. inheritance, heritage, hereditary estate, patrimony (cf. mölⁱ-mirās, p. 566b, l. 19) (Gr.M., L. 428).
a decurion) m. in the following:-- mirdā lagun m.inf. to interfere, unsolicited, in another's work by assuming the leadership and setting to work at it.

m. a singer (of a caste which follows that profession from generation to generation). -bāy f. his wife; a female of the above caste, who sings with her husband. -koṭᵘ m. (f. -küṭᵘ̈), the son (f. daughter) of such a singer; a boy who follows the occupation of such a singer.
or mēsh f. the Ram, the zodiacal sign Aries (Śiv. 476, Rām. 1279).
f. the outer corner of the eye, the edge of the eyelid (El.).
f. the point of a fine thorn; a splinter of wood (El., Gr.Gr. 13); a small loose piece of skin, a rag-nail (El., Gr.Gr. 147); cf. mishyulᵘ. mishĕ-ḍogᵘ m. a kind of sharp-pointed whitlow.
interj. a drawl used for urging cattle along, etc.; hence, a word indicating repulsion (K.Pr. 237).
adj. c.g. (of cloth, leather, a bush, a flower, etc.) covered with small thorns or spines.
adj. c.g. of musk, musky (YZ. 5); black, jetty, raven (of locks) (El., YZ. 17).
m. a tiny spicule of loose skin at the root of, or by the side of, a finger-nail, a 'dolly-idler', ragnail (Gr.Gr. 147); a splinter or thorn under the nail (Gr.Gr. 147). Cf. mish 2.
adj. c.g. poor, needy, indigent (El.; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 27, 143); (as subst.) a beggar, one who is poverty-stricken (H. ix, 11).
adj. c.g. like, similar, in the phrase bē-mislu-mānand بے مثل و مانند, without likeness and comparison, incomparable (Śiv. 775).

m. a ruler (for ruling lines) (Gr.M.). (It is a series of strings, strained and glued to a paper or pasteboard. The paper to be ruled is pressed upon it, and by slight pressure the ruled lines appear as ridges.)

conj. 1 (1 p.p. miṭôwᵘ), to wipe out, abolish, cancel (e.g. a debt); to settle a quarrel satisfactorily to both parties; satisfactorily to clear off or complete (some difficult work). miṭôwᵘ-motᵘ, perf. part. (f. miṭövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), wiped out, abolished, cleared off (as ab.); (of a quarrel) settled satisfactorily to both parties; (of some difficult work) cleared off, satisfactorily accomplished.
f. a certain potherb, Trigonellum fœnum-græcum, the mēthī of India proper (L. 70, 359, methi).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. miṭyōv), to be wiped out, abolished, cancelled; (of a quarrel, etc.) to be settled satisfactorily to both parties (Gr.Gr. 23); (of some difficult task, long standing debt, or the like) to be satisfactorily completed, cleared off, etc. miṭyō -motᵘ perf. part. (f. miṭyē -müʦᵘ̈), wiped out, abolished, cancelled; (of a quarrel) settled, as ab.; (of a difficult work, long standing debt, etc.) satisfactorily completed and done with, paid off, etc.
f. (sg. dat. miṭᵃrüñᵃ), wiping out, cancelling (e.g. a debt); (of a quarrel) settling satisfactory to both parties; completion, clearing off, satisfactory accomplishment (of some difficult task).
m. the middle, centre; the waist, loins (YZ. 73); a scabbard, sheath.
or mizāz m. temper, disposition (El.; Gr.M. mizāz; Rām. 1249, mizāz); constitution, health, condition of body (Gr.M.).
f. the conduct of an out- caste or non-Hindū. See mī˜ʦh 2.

in miʦar-konḍᵘ m. a kind of thistle (it is crushed with water, and the resultant juice is used as a medicine for fever and as a diuretic). It is also burnt as a charm against demons (L. 75, mitsari kund). miʦrⁱ-konḍⁱ m., id.
or mīʦ 1 [sic] m. (sg. dat. mī˜ʦas), a measure, a thing for measuring (El. míṅts). mī˜ʦa-bāna m. a measuring vessel.

or mīʦ 2 [sic] m. (sg. dat. mī˜ʦas), a non-Hindū, an outcaste, one who does not discriminate according to Hindū rules as to purity and impurity or edible and non-edible food; a class, nation, or tribe of such persons. mī̃ʦa-byôlᵘ m. the seed of non-Hindūs; met. the members of the Musalmān faith (in which women can have several husbands, one after the other, and, consequently, have many children).
m. (sg. dat. mīʦatas), the habits or life of an outcaste. See mī˜ʦh 2.
m. hair; a single hair (Rām. 873); cf. mōy. mō-kalam مو قلم m. a paint brush (Gr.M.). mō-yĕ-wāl m. hair, a head of hair (Rām. 1350, 1415); a single hair (Rām. 735).
m. thickness, stoutness, plumpness (Gr.Gr. 29, 30, 140; Śiv. 766; Rām. 630). Cf. mọ̆ṭᵘ.

adj. c.g. fisted, having a fist; (of a weapon) continually, or firmly, held in the hand; close-fisted (of a rich man), niggardly. --kākaz -- m. a kind of stiff smooth paper (it is ten times the width of a fist long and nine times the width of a fist wide).
or mochᵘ or muchᵘ1 m. a goldsmith's forming mould, on which he hammers sheet gold or other metal in order to give it any required pattern or form.

m. delight, pleasure, joy, gladness; (in Kāshmīrī) respect, reverence, honour, dignity, character (Gr.Gr. 137, K.Pr. 262). ¶ mōda-baröyⁱ f. the showing of reverence. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), wanting in respect, discourteous; (of an action) rude, causing disrespect, indicating disrespect. --wālun -- m.inf. to bring down from respect, to lower a person in public estimation, to disgrace him, to humiliate (Śiv. 69). -wālay f. the action of subjecting another to disrespect, humiliation. --wasun -- m.inf. to descend from respect, to lose one's reputation, be dishonoured. -wothᵘ adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), dishonoured, disgraced. -vĕʦar m. worthiness of honour, high respectability. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), full of honour, much respected (Gr.Gr. 137); (an action) indicating great respect.
f. meaning, object (H. vi, 7). Cf. mudā 2.

or maidān میدان m. a plain, field, lawn (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 54, 57, 205; YZ. 95, 178; Śiv. 1064, 1155, 1634, 1733; H. iii, 1; viii, 9; x, 1, 5; xi, 3; xii, 20); a field of battle (Rām. 915, 1378); open ground, country (as opposed to town) (YZ. 40). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give room (to), give a wide berth (to); to make room (for); to give an opportunity for, or lay oneself open to, an attack. --hāwun -- m.inf. to show an open space, i.e. to attack and utterly conquer.
adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, an open plain; (of a plant) growing in a plain; (of a horse or the like) grazing on a plain; (of a road) approachable by, or running over, a plain.
f. N. of the second wife of Pāṇḍu, and mother of Nakula and Sahadēva, in Sanskrit Mādrī (K. 538).

adj. (f. mŏdᵘ̈rᵘ̈), sweet, honied (in taste) (W. 112, 131; K.Pr. 18, 30, 146; K. 979; H. vii, 31); pleasing, charming, agreeable (K. 62, 400; H. ix, 7); melodious (K. 970). (El. spells this word mádúr, mŏdur, mŏḍur, and mudur.) ¶ El. gives several varieties of fruit used with this word. In his spellings they are modari-tséra, a kind of apricot; mŏdir ṭánj, a kind of pear (so W. 116); mŏḍur bádám, a kind of almond; moḍur bamtsúnṭ, a sweet quince; mŏdur dáṅ (= dönᵘ̈), a kind of pomegranate; moḍur tsúnṭ, a small sweet kind of apple; cf. W. 116. --kand-hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. mŏdᵘ̈r ᵘ̈kand-hishᵘ̈), sweet as sugar (lit. and met.). --mö̃ch-hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. mŏdᵘ̈rᵘ̈ mö̃ch-hishᵘ̈), sweet as honey. ¶ mŏdᵘ̈rᵘ̈ bēr f. a sweet hedge, a sweet receptacle, (a person, work, or place) in whom or which sweetness (lit. or met.) is experienced. --zĕv -- f. a sweet tongue, an eloquent tongue; as adj., c.g. eloquent (El. moḍir zeo).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mọ̆dᵃrôwᵃ), to make sweet, to sweeten.
or mọ̆dᵃrēr m. sweetness (W. 112, L. 464, Śiv. 499); something sweet (e.g. sugar).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. mọ̆dᵃryōv), to be, or become, sweet (of food, nature, voice, etc.) (Gr.Gr. 7). mọ̆dᵃryō-motᵃ perf. part. (f. mọ̆dᵃryē-müʦᵃ), become sweet, sweetened (in all senses).
f. a place of assembly; an assembly, a company of people, congregation (Gr.M.).
m. in mŏgadyunᵘ m.inf. to give a child the breast, to suckle (K. 159).

adj. c.g. of or relating to a Mogul. --cāhy -- or --cāhⁱ -- or --cāy -- f. a kind of tea (the drink). According to El. (s.v. chái) it is prepared as follows:--For every tōlā (half-ounce) of tea five cups of water are poured upon it in the bahugun or teapot. It is then boiled for half an hour, when more cold water is added, along with condiments and sugar, after which it is boiled for half an hour more; milk is then added. It is now ready for drinking. The colour is reddish.

or mŏgulᵘ m. (sg. dat. mŏgalas), a Mogul; (in Kāshmīrī) one who is cruel, terrible (K.Pr. 146) (cf. phanāyi-mᵒ, s.v. phanöyⁱ).mŏgal-byôlⁱ m. N. of a kind of paddy with a hard fat grain. -cāhⁱ f. a certain way of making tea (see cāhⁱ) (K.Pr. 39), i.q. mŏgȧlⁱ cāhy, q.v.
adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, the month of Māg, q.v., as adv., in the month of Māg (i.e. in the cold season) (Rām. 172). --dāñĕ -- m. paddy collected in the month of Māg for a year's use.

or mūh m., i.q. muh, q.v. (very common in Hindū poetry in the sense of religious illusion) (Śiv. 66-7, 87, 170, 350, etc.; Rām. 218; K. 212); stupor, swoon (Rām. 1042). Being personified as 'Illusion', it often has the genitive in -unᵘ, as in Śiv. 737, 1674, 1805; Rām. 1042. (For compounds of this word, see muh.)
m. a place of destruction or danger, a precipice, or the like (Rām. 950).

f. a seal, a seal-ring (El. muhr, Gr.M., K.Pr. 17); the impression of a seal, a stamp (Śiv. 414; H. x, 3, 10); a certain gold coin (current in India for about £1 16s., in Kashmīr valued at 12 chilkī rupees), a gold mohur (El. mŏhur; Gr.M.; W. 21; K.Pr. 36, 78, 181, 243; Śiv. 1079, 1092, 1285; K. 953; H. i, 9; v. 10, 12). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to put a seal (on), to seal, to stamp (H. x, 3, 10). --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to seal a document (with one's own seal to authenticate the signature). -zihar f. a collective term for gold and silver ornaments. ¶ mŏhara-khonᵘ or (Gr.M.) mŏhar-kan مہر کن m. a seal-engraver, a lapidary (El. mohar-kand). -wöjᵘ̈ f. a signet-ring.

m. a shell, a cowrie; a bead (of glass or coral); the bezoar stone; a rubber, shell, pebble, or the like used for giving smoothness and glossiness to paper, cloth, etc., a polishing instrument. Cf. lāran-mŏhara, p. 531b, l. 42.
f. a fascinating woman; N. of the female form assumed by Viṣṇu, when he cheated the demons of nectar at the churning of the ocean (K. 929).
adj. c.g. necessitous, needy, poor, in want (K.Pr. 134, Śiv. 1239, Rām. 91); in need (of, dat.) (Rām. 139); as subst. a poor man, a pauper.

or mohᵘ m. a mosquito, gnat (El. moh, múh; Śiv. 751.) ¶ mȧhⁱ-ȧḍijⁱ f. a mosquito's bone; met. something impossible or incredible. -ambȧrⁱ m. a small juicy tart kind of apple (L. 349; mohi amri); cf. ambȧrⁱ, p. 27b, l. 4. -anzan f. a kind of paddy, described as having a small, sweet-scented, soft grain; the grain (rice) of this paddy; cf. anzan, p. 36b, l. 42. -byôlᵘ m. 'mosquito-seed', N. of another kind of paddy, described as having a full, white grain. -wan m. another kind of paddy, described as having a very full red-coloured grain.

m. a wave, surge, billow; whim, caprice, emotion, ecstasy; (in Kāshmīrī) exquisite beauty, ravishing loveliness (Śiv. 1327). --wuchun -- m.inf. to look on (indifferently) at caprices; hence, to neglect to correct naughty children, to look on at anything without worrying, to look at undismayed (Rām. 1396).
or (W. 99) mūjib موجب postpos. governing abl. (H. viii, 16), by reason of, on account of, in accordance with, in conformity to (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 157; H. viii, 16). Cf. ami mūᵒ, p. 54b, l. 42, and mūzūba.

(also written möjⁱ, or by paṇḍits môjᵘ̈) f. a mother (El. máj, mój; Gr.Gr. 36, 63, 72, 143, 147, 161; Gr.M.; W. 17, 115; L. 462, mojh; L.V. 97; K.Pr. 47, 51, 62, 64, 74, 87, 126, 130-1, 144, 156, 191, 261; YZ. 36, 76, 531; Śiv. 34-5, 80, 99, 435, 438, 599, 649, etc.; Rām. 180, 234, 275, etc.; K. 65, 82, 118, 140, 159, 164, 245, 758, etc.; H. v, 6; viii, 1; ix, 9, etc.). --bawöñᵘ̈ -- f. 'mother Bhavānī', used in Kashmīr for the śakti or energic power of one of the chief Hindū deities, conceived as a personality to be worshipped (e.g. Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, or Durgā) (Śiv. 79, 80, 109, 496, 1315). --dīvī -- f. 'mother goddess', id. (Rām. 1584). Cf. möjⁱ-b(h)agavatī with the same meaning in Śiv. 101. ¶ mājĕ-bata m. 'food from mother'; met. some easy employment which suits one's inclinations, a soft job. -dil, -dilal, or -dinal m. three terms of filthy abuse, each meaning 'one who has incestuous connexion with his own mother' (see Gr.Gr. 107). -gŏbur m. (sg. dat. gŏbaras), a mother's boy, a boy who clings to his mother's skirt. -kōrĕ f.pl. mother and daughter, i.e. a daughter accompanying her mother (Gr.Gr. 72, L.V. 92, Śiv. 1313); cf. kōri-möjᵘ̈ (p. 468a, 1. 30). -lĕkh f. (sg. dat. -lĕki), abuse of a person's mother (a form of abuse). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), motherless, a child whose mother is dead or who is absent. -raʦhar m. the condition of being motherless. -tônᵘ m. (sg. dat. -tönis), motherliness, action like that of a mother by a woman to one who is not her child; motherhood (Gr.Gr. 143). -ṭôṭhᵘ m. (f. -ṭöṭhᵘ̈), a mother's darling, a mother's pet. --wadun -- m. (sg. dat. -wadanas), a mother's lamentation, i.e. lamentation like that of a mother for a son who has died; hence, violent lamentation on the occurrence of a calamity. --wadun wŏthun -- m.inf. general loud lamentation by the general public on the occurrence of any great public calamity. -yĕtīm c.g. a motherless child (an expression of the language of compassion). ¶ māji-khŏta kūrᵘ̈büḍᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. the daughter to become greater than the mother, u.w. ref. to some small action or business which unexpectedly becomes of great importance.
or mukadam m. the head revenue officer of a village, a village headman (El.; K.Pr. 215, 231; H. ix, 1, 10); the headman of an office (El.); a policeman (El.).

m. the condition of obtaining release (from any condition), freedom (Gr.Gr. 138, K.Pr. 126); freedom from business, cessation from work, disengagedness, vacation; leisure or opportunity (for doing something) (K.Pr. 245). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give freedom; to discharge (El.); esp. (amongst Musalmāns) to give (a wife) her freedom, to divorce (her). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to accept freedom, (of a woman) to be divorced (as ab.).

f. release, liberation (Gr.Gr. 128); cessation from work, disengagedness, vacation, leisure, leisure or opportunity to begin some new work (K.Pr. 138). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. leisure to be obtained (for doing something), an opportunity to be found.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. mŏkalôwᵘ), to untie, unloose, liberate, release, set free, save (Gr.M.; YZ. 382; Śiv. 3, 4, 18, 53, 61, 151-2, etc.; Rām. 312, 401, 684; K. 495, 765, 898; H. v, 8); to complete (a work), finish (Śiv. 53; K. 469; H. vi, 16; ix, 6; x, 1; xii, 5); to leave, abandon (Gr.M.). mŏkalôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mŏkalövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), unbound, released, freed; completed (of some work being done).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. mŏkalyōv), to be released, let go, liberated, untied (of a person or thing), to escape, be freed (Gr.Gr. 128; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 65; Śiv. 7, 110, 250, 392, 1834; K. 346; H. v, 8; vi, 10, 11; ix, 11); (of a work) to be finished, completed (Śiv. 392; H. viii, 6, 8); to be done (with a thing), to have nothing more to do (with it) (Gr.M., Rām. 614); to get leisure (for doing something), to find an opportunity (for); (in a religious sense) to be freed from the bonds of existence, to become absorbed in the Deity, to secure salvation (Rām. 54-5; K. 239, 352, 495). mŏkalyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mŏkalyē-müʦᵘ̈), released, let go, untied (K. 571); finished, completed; having obtained an opportunity (for).
mŏkuṭa, or mŏkuṭh m. (sg. dat. mŏkạṭas), a tiara, diadem, crown (Śiv. 188, 778, 792, 892, 1501; Rām. 1738; K. 59 (mŏkạṭa), 925, 954 (mŏkuṭa)).

m. (sg. dat. mŏkhas), the face (Śiv. 5, 68, 122, 203, 238, 333, 800, etc.; Rām. 561, 631, 756, 1265-6, etc.; K. 927, 1116); a mouth (cf. gŏra-mŏkh, p. 297a, l. 41) (K. 1060, 1145-6); the cheek (El., also mŏk); the opening, or mouth, of a boil, etc.; face (in the sense of audacity) (K. 1121). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to show the face; hence, (of the dawn or the like) to show the first signs, to begin (Rām. 1265). --karun -- m.inf. to form a mouth, (of a boil, etc.) to ripen and form an opening for the pus. --phirun -- m.inf. to turn away the face, to become opposed to (a person), to take up a position of opposition. --raṭun -- to seize the face, to gaze on the face (H. v, 9). ¶ mŏkha sg. abl. used as adv. face to face (YZ. 180, Rām. 1350); used in idiomatic phrases, as in kami mŏkha, with what face (shall I do so-and-so), how shall I dare (to do so-and-so) (K. 1121); sŏkha-mŏkha, unexpectedly, suddenly (Śiv. 238, 978, 1679, 1892). ¶ as postpos. on account of, because of (cf. ami mŏkha, p. 54b, l. 45) (Śiv. 1649; H. viii, 9; x, 4); by, by means of (cf. shẹ̆tra-sandi mŏkha, (he will be killed) by his enemy (Rām. 957)). ¶ mŏkha-dorᵘ adj. (f. -dürᵘ̈), hard-faced, i.e. insolent, disrespectful. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to put in front (of some one), to set before, present; to bring face to face (of combatants, mutual abusers, and so on). --dyutᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. diʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), put face to face (of combatants, etc.). --lagun -- m.inf. face to face censure or abuse to be publicly directed against a person for some fault which he has hitherto been successful in hiding; (of a calamity) to be suddenly brought face to face (with a person), a sudden calamity to befall. -muday f. a face to face accusation. -mŏkh f. meeting face to face. -mandach f. shame at being face to face, shyness, timidity, shamefacedness. --nērun -- m.inf. to go forth to meet (an enemy) (K. 587). -prath m. (sg. dat. pratas), a blow with the mouth, an insolent speech. -pashĕwañ f. the present given to a woman on first seeing her newly-born child. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come face to face with a person; to face, confront (an adversary) (K. 628, 819-20, 871); to face (a piece of work, etc.).
f. (sg. dat. mŏkhi), a cutting (of trees, etc., for planting) (Gr.Gr. 16). mŏkha diñĕ f.pl.inf. to set, or plant, cuttings.
adv. by rote, by heart, without book, memoriter.
or mukhurᵘ adj. (f. mọ̆khürᵘ̈ or mukhürᵘ̈), talkative, garrulous, loquacious, fluent, voluble (esp. of a child); impertinent, saucy, perverse, audacious (in language, esp. of a child) (Gr.M.).

or mŏkta m. a pearl (not necessarily the pearl found in the pearl-oyster) (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 117, 118, 159; YZ. 24, 27, 39, 71, 163; Śiv. 247, 787, 900, 1012, 1145, 1210, 1678, etc.; Rām. 168, 566, 569, 577, 640, etc.; K. 28, 97, 183, 590, 831, 843; H. i, 9); a pearl-like object said to be found in the frontal bone of certain elephants. Musalmān women are often called by this name, which they often pronounce 'Mŏkhit' (El.). -grū̃phᵘ m. a pearl-bud, a cluster of pearls; hence, a pearl necklace (K. 923). --hö̃giñ -- f. a pearl-oyster (cf. hö̃giñĕ-mŏkta, p. 324a, l. 20). -hāl f. (sg. dat. -höjᵘ̈), N. of a certain kind of paddy producing a thin, long, white sweet-smelling grain (Śiv. 1112, 1212, 1748); the rice produced by this paddy. -hār m. a pearl necklace (K.Pr. 85, 221; YZ. 54; Śiv. 1153, 1794; Rām. 370, 1041; K. 927, 954); cf. mŏktukᵘ hār (Rām. 1122). -hoṭᵘ m. a neck adorned with a pearl necklace; a kind of pearl necklace of several strands. -jūrⁱ f. a pair of pearls (forming a pair, e.g. in a pair of earrings or the like) (Gr.Gr. 82). -lar f. a string of pearls (Śiv. 163, 338, 1136). -lürᵘ̈ 1 f. (for 2, see mŏkᵃth 2), a house made of, or adorned with, pearls (Śiv. 247, 1036). -māl f. (sg. dat. -māli), a long chain-necklace of pearls (hanging down like a garland) (Śiv. 713, K. 60); a N. of Rādhā, the beloved of Krishna (Śiv. 713). -nam m. 'a finger-nail of pearl'; hence (as a description of something which it is found possible to obtain) rare and intrinsically of great value. -pholᵘ  m. a single pearl (Rām. 1542); a collection of pearls, a few pearls (Gr.M.). -ṭang m. a kind of ear-ornament (shaped like a pear-fruit and with pearl drops). -wôñᵘ m. a pearl-seller.

or (Śiv. 1794) mŏktār 1 adj. c.g. and subst. m. chosen, selected; invested with authority, an agent, delegate, representative; invested with full power, absolute, independent, at full liberty (to act as one chooses) (Śiv. 914, 1714, 1794).
or mukharĕr m. impertinence, sauciness (of language), daring (Gr.M., mukharir).

or mŏkᵃth, mŏkth adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. mŏktas), released, liberated; esp. finally emancipated from the bonds of worldly existence, one who has renounced all worldly attachments and who has secured final beatitude, (in a religious sense) saved, free from reincarnation (Śiv. 320, 1042, 1114, 1144, 1522, 1533; K. 48, 72, 301, 352, 607). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become 'saved', as ab. (K. 187).
adj. (f. mọ̆khᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), finally emancipated, released from transmigration, united with the Supreme, i.q. mŏkhᵃth, q.v.
m. one who delegates power (to another), the client of a lawyer (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. garrulous, talkative (K.Pr. 132, mákir); the word is perhaps another spelling of mŏkhorᵘ, q.v. It has only been noted in the above passage.
m. a nonce-word in Śiv. 1794, to pun with mŏktār 1. It is offered as a contraction of the Sanskrit mukhya-tārakaḥ or 'Supreme Saviour'.
adj. c.g. abbreviated, abridged, a summary (Śiv. 747); as adv. in short, to sum up, finally, to make a long story short (Śiv. 117, Rām. 1743).

(Śiv. 1112) or mŏktī f. (sg. dat. mŏktiyĕ or (Śiv. 1526) mŏktīyĕ), i.q. mŏkᵃ̇tᵃ̇, q.v. (Śiv. 209, 992, 1007, 1112, 1359; K. 626). -dvār m. the gate of spiritual emancipation, death and final release (K. 299, 455, 606).

or mŏkolᵘ adj. (f. mŏkᵘ̈jᵘ̈), released, set free, free, let go, emancipated (Gr.Gr. 138); free from other work, at leisure, or having the opportunity for doing something; abandoned, untenanted (of a house) (Gr.M.).

m. (sg. dat. mỗkanas), a small ball or roll of scented wood or lotus-filaments, used for rubbing on a rough stone, the resultant powder being employed for various toilet uses (e.g. making a tilaka or sectarian mark on the forehead).
or mö̃kun m. a bug. mö̃kan-ṭŏph f. (sg. dat. -ṭŏpi), a bug-bite, or wound like a bug-bite; met. a hindrance caused by some mean person; a stinging remark.

f. (sg. dat. mö̆kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈, K. 114), another spelling of mŏkᵃ̇tᵃ̇ (q.v.) (Śiv. 858, 1163, 1688; Rām. 541; K. 301, 424, 611, 1077); mŏkta-lürᵘ̈ 2 f. (for 1, see mŏkhta), an abode of final liberation (Śiv. 247, 1036).
i.q. mŏkta, so spelt in Śiv. 1688 to serve as pun on mŏkᵃth 2.
or mŏktī (q.v.) f. (sg. dat. mŏktĕ), release from transmigration, final emancipation, union with the Supreme (cf. mọ̆khᵒtᵒ and mŏkhᵃth) (L.V. 29, Rām. 6).
another spelling of mọ̆khᵒtᵒ, mŏkhᵃth, qq.v.
m. the shuttle of a weaver's loom. mȧkⁱ tārȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to pass shuttles backwards and forwards; met. to be busy on some continuous monotonous work.

m. price, worth, cost, value (cf. kŏl- mŏl, p. 436b, l. 47) (Gr.Gr. 16, 146; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 9, 71, 74, 100, 123, 206, 242; Rām. 1229; K. 178); intrinsic value, worth (Rām. 188). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take a price, to charge a price (Gr.M.). --khārun -- m.inf. to raise the price of anything; met. to extol, cry up, puff, eulogize. --khasun -- m.inf. price to rise, to achieve good repute, to rise in general favour. --karun -- m.inf. fix a price (Gr.M.; K. 954; H. viii, 9). -tŏl m. price (indefinitely), price and cost, value, appraisement. -tŏl wuchun m.inf. to settle the price, or value (of), to value, appraise, estimate. ¶ mŏla-baröyⁱ filling up the value, payment of agreed compensation for anything destroyed, lost, etc. -mŏl f. increase in value owing to general demand. -mŏla pyonᵘ m.inf. to be successfully accomplished after much exertion. --pokᵘ -- adj. (f. -pücᵘ̈), sold for more than its intrinsic value (owing to scarcity, rarity, difficulty of obtainment, etc.). --pakun -- m.inf. to be purchasable only at a high price (owing to scarcity, difficulty of obtainment, or the like), the price (of anything) to go up. --pakanāwun -- m.inf. to sell (an article) at an excessive price (as ab.); to raise the price. --pakawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --pakavüñᵘ̈ --), dear, high-priced, that of which the price has risen (e.g. on account of scarcity, stocks being low, etc.). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without price, priceless; priceless, valueless (in Śiv. 1566, the word may be interpreted in either of these senses). -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), of great price, of high value, of great intrinsic value. ¶ mŏlⁱ sg. instr. at a price (K. 157); hence, purchasable, that which can be obtained only by purchase (K.Pr. 203). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take at a price, to buy (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 146, 234; YZ. 121, 124, 157, 161, 169, 191, 242, 268; Rām. 1317).

(also written mail) m. inclination (to) (Śiv. 750); penchant, bent, bias (K.Pr. 100, mol; Śiv. 1691); wish, desire (Gr.Gr. 22; K.Pr. 11, 73; YZ. 230, 412; Śiv. 970); attachment, partiality, fondness, affection, love; desire for food (El.; cf. bē-möl). --barun -- m.inf. to show an inclination (to), to have a penchant (for), to have a taste (for). --mashun -- m.inf. to forget one's desire (e.g. when 'the grapes are sour').
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mŏlanôwᵘ), to settle the price of anything. Cf. mŏlawun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mŏlowᵘ), to fix the price of (anything) (Rām. 1105). Cf. mŏlanāwun.

m. a possessor, proprietor, a lord (El., YZ. 157, Rām. 70); a master (Gr.M.); the owner, proprietor, or landlord (of a house, etc.) (Gr.M., K.Pr. 107). asᵃl mölikh, the real owner, the principal in a firm or business (Gr.M.).
adj. (f. mŏlᵘ̈jᵘ̈), high-priced, costly, expensive (Gr.Gr. 146, Gr.M., Śiv. 1230); valuable (Gr.M.).

m. (sg. dat. mölis, abl. māli), a father (Gr.Gr. 36, 41, 56, 72, 143, 161; Gr.M.; W. 6, 9, 17 mol; L. 460 mol; L.V. 91, 107 (see māli); K.Pr. 51, 134, 144; YZ. 22, 155, 418; Śiv. 35, 438, 517, 599, 640, 649, 1278, 1906; Rām. 264, 275, 534, 599, 760, 812, 1426, etc.; K. 459-60, 473, 503, 614, 641, 689, 765, 875, 1027; H. v, 6; viii, 1, 13; xii, 4, 5, 10, 13, etc.); voc. māli, see s.v. -möjᵘ̈ father and mother, parents (El., who makes the word m. It is really two words of different genders; Gr.M.; W. 115, mol-möj; YZ. 531, (möjᵘ̈-môlᵘ̈) 36). ¶ māli-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), fatherless (K. 47). ¶ mölⁱ-mirās m. that which is inherited from a father, paternal inheritance, patrimony; qualities, etc., inherited from a father, inherited paternal tendencies. -māryukᵘ m. a father's halter; hence, hatred for a father's murderer, a death feud (on account of a father's murder). -mẹ̆thᵃr m. a father's friend. -pŏthᵃr m.pl. father and son (Gr.Gr. 72). -sondᵘ adj. (f. -sünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a father. -sath f. (sg. dat. -süʦᵘ̈), confidence in help or protection from the existence of a father; met. entire freedom from anxiety. -yĕtīm c.g. (a child) whose father is dead, a fatherless (child). -zāyunᵘ m. hereditary disposition, hereditary virtue, vice, health, disease, etc. ¶ mölis bŏwanis m. a certain form of blessing, wishing a person long life as a father.
m. acting like a father, tender-hearted and kindly conduct like that of a father, fatherliness (Gr.Gr. 143).

m. the breasts of a woman or udders and dugs of a female beast (El. spells this word mŏn); mother's milk, milk. Cf. mam and mama. ¶ mŏma cĕwawunᵘ n.ag. (f. -cĕwavüñᵘ̈), one who drinks from the breast, a suckling child. --cyonᵘ -- m.inf. to drink from the breast; to be a suckling child. -dām m. sucking the breast. -golᵘ m. a mouthful of mother's milk; hence, sucking the breast. -kuʦurᵘ m. the nipple of the breast.
m. the breast (mamma) (El., where the word is probably a misprint for mŏm, q.v.).

m. silence, taciturnity (El. moṅ, adj. silent). --dārun -- m.inf. to keep a vow of silence. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to have recourse to silence, to sit silent and motionless even when one ought to be helping another, to be surly and disobliging. --karun -- or mōnam karun m.inf. to remain silent, to keep silence.

m. kissing on the cheek (among women); cf. miñ 1 and muñ. --karun -- m.inf. to kiss (El. monyi karun). ¶ mŏñĕ-pūtᵘ m. a loving kiss on the cheek of a child (Gr.Gr. 132, Gr.M. muñĕᵒ). Cf. miñĕ-pūtᵘ, col. a, l. 43, and muñĕ-pūtᵘ, l. 39 bel.
m. the Impeyan pheasant, which is said to be found in Kashmīr (El.).

m. (in Hindū mythology) the N. of a demon (in Skt., Muṇḍa) who with Caṇḍa was killed by Dēvī, the consort, or Śakti, of Śiva. mŏnḍa-daham the 'Muṇḍa-tenth', the tenth lunar day of the dark half of the month of Wāhĕkh (Skt., Vaiśākha) (April-May), on which the slaughter of Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa is celebrated.

f. a widow (a widower is mŏnḍurᵘ, q.v.) (Gr.Gr. 144; Gr.M.; L. 465, mund; K.Pr. 145; K. 551). ¶ mŏnḍa-kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a widow's son (who needs a father's care and is laxly brought up). --lakhun -- m.inf. to disgrace a respectable person by abuse. --pöthᵃr -- m. a group of widows, esp. all the widows in a joint family household. -shāhzāda m. 'a widow's prince', the spoilt darling child of a widow.

(for 1 and 2, see under mŏnḍ 1 and 2) m. a turn to play (as in 'it's so-and-so's turn to play'); used esp. with ref. to outdoor games, e.g. in the indigenous tip-cat, for the turn of the player who strikes the 'cat' out of the hole into which it is thrown by the mŏnḍa-dar, or bowler. Similarly in cricket and the like. The word is also used met. as in 'my turn will come to pay you off for this'. -dar m. the opponent to the party who is 'in'; e.g. the bowler in the game of tip-cat. --darun -- m.inf. to act as a monḍa-dar, as ab. --raṭun -- m.inf. to have the turn to be in, as ab. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. such a turn to come to a person.
mŏnḍukh, see nyoñᵘ and nĕñĕ-mŏnḍukh (s.v. nĕñĕ 3).
m. (sg. dat. mŏnḍakas), a frog, usually in the compound miñĕ-mŏnḍukh (see miñ 2) and nĕñĕ-mᵒ (see nĕñĕ 3).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. mŏnḍyōv), (of an edged tool, weapon, etc.) to become blunt, become dull-edged; (of an intelligent man) to become dull, stupid; to become weak. mŏnḍyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mŏnḍyē-müʦᵘ̈), blunted; (of someone formerly intelligent) become stupid, blunted in wit.
m. (sg. dat. mŏnḍaras), a widower (a widow is mŏnḍ 2, q.v.).
m. (sg. dat. mŏnḍaras), the trunk, or stump, of a tree, a log (Gr.Gr. 37, K.Pr. 231).
or mŏnḍusᵘ m. (sg. dat. mŏnḍasas), widowhood (Gr.Gr. 144). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to live a widow, to endure widowhood.
f. (sg. dat. mọ̆nḍᵃrüñᵃ), the act of making blunt (a sharp weapon, tool, etc.); causing a clever man to be stupid.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mọ̆nḍᵃrôwᵃ), to make blunt (a weapon or a tool); to cause (a clever person) to become stupid.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mọ̆nḍᵒrᵒ), to make blunt (a weapon, tool, etc.) (Gr.Gr. 7); to cause (a clever person) to become stupid.

adj. (f. münzᵘ̈), slow, dull, stupid (naturally or from disease or other cause); thin, emaciated, delicate, sick (Gr.Gr. 140); (of something wooden or metallic, or clothes or the like), worn out, worn away. Cf. mand and mọ̆nḍᵘ 4.

m. the trunk or stump of a tree, including the solid part of the root (cf. mö̆nḍᵘ̈ 1) (El. múnd) (cf. khŏḍa-mᵒ, p. 392a, l. 50, and nasta-mᵒ, s.v. nast); a log, a heavy block of wood (Gr.Gr. 37, Śiv. 1856); a pillar; --˚ any clumsy lump (Rām. 631), cf. gala-mọ̆nḍᵘ, p. 282a, l. 50, or used in the names of various cakes (cf. alapōshĕ-mọ̆nḍᵘ, p. 22b, l. 27; lāyĕ-mọ̆nḍᵘ, p. 543a, l. 48), or in such compounds as kana-mọ̆nḍᵘ, p. 448a, l. 11, the root of the ear; murkha-mŏnḍᵘ, a fool-block, an utter fool. ¶ mŏnḍⁱ-ala m. tottering of the trunk, rooting up; hence, utter destruction; cf. ala 4. -pākh m. (sg. dat. -pākas), log-cooking, i.e. cooking on a fire on which a whole chopped log is consumed; met. cooking for a very long time. -zyunᵘ m. log firewood, a log chopped up for firewood.

f. (sg. dat. mŏnjĕ 1, for 2 see mọ̆nḍᵘ 4), the thick stalk of a vegetable (f. of mọ̆nḍᵘ 1); that part of the stalk of a vegetable or other growth which is below ground, including the upper part of the root (cf. hĕnga-mö̆ndᵘ̈, the root of a horn, p. 339a, l. 42); used --˚ to indicate something lumpy and hidden (as in dana-mᵒ, p. 221b, l. 42; hirⁱ-mⁱ, p. 367a, l. 47; nāga-mᵒ, s.v. nāg 1), a hidden lump or store of wealth, or to indicate some kind of cake (cf. adrakh- mᵒ, p. 15b, l. 6; alapōshĕ-mᵒ, p. 22b, l. 30; and nadȧrⁱ-mⁱ, s.v. nadorᵘ); cf. also mūla-mŏnjĕ, p. 567a, l. 36. ¶ mŏnjĕ bĕhun m.inf. to become workless, (of an official or the like) to lose one's post, become out of work (cf. mas mŏnjĕ bĕhun, s.v. mas 1); (of a business or the like) to become slack, to go downhill. --bĕhanāwun -- m.inf. to put out of work, dismiss from a post; to cause (a business) to become slack. -dĕl m. the bark of the stem of a vegetable. -gāḍa f.pl. a kind of fish pasty. -gūlᵘ (sg. dat. -gōli), a kind of pasty of water-chestnuts. -gorᵘ m. (his wife is -gȧrⁱ-bāy, but a woman who follows the same profession is -gürᵘ̈), a maker, or seller, of pasties, a confectioner (K.Pr. 142). - hākh (sg. dat. -hākas), a vegetable with a thick stalk. -khav f. a hole in the ground in which vegetable stalks are kept (as in a silo) for use in winter. -köṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kāchĕ), the hard wood-like stalk of a vegetable or its bark. -nadorᵘ m. a pasty of lotus-stalks. -ray m. a certain disease of the rice-crop, in which the roots are attacked, and the plant withers from the root upwards (L. 334, munj rai).
m. gruel-water, the water in which rice or the like has been boiled. Cf. aḍa-mọ̆nḍᵘ 1, p. 11b, l. 14.

f. (sg. dat. mŏnjĕ), trampling, rubbing with the feet (cf. manḍun, used --˚ as in lata-mö̆nḍᵘ̈, trampling with the feet, trampling down, crushing under the feet (K. 237); so (of the hands) ʦari-münḍᵘ̈, clapping the hands in derision (K. 222, 232).
or monḍᵘ m. rubbing clothes in the wash (cf. amonḍᵘ, p. 8a, l. 43); used in the following: --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to rub clothes in the wash (cf. aḍa-mọ̆nḍᵘ 2, p. 11b, l. 19).

adj. (f. mö̆nḍᵘ̈ 3, sg. dat. mŏnjĕ 2; for mö̆nḍᵘ̈ 1 and 2, see s.vv.; for mŏnjĕ 1 and 2, see mö̆nḍᵘ̈ 1 and 2), (of a tool, weapon, or the like) blunt-edged, blunt (cf. kana-mᵒ, p. 448a, l. 12, dull of hearing) (Gr.Gr. 30, 74, 140; Gr.M.; W. 21); (of a person) dull, stupid (El. maunḍ); simple-minded (K.Pr. 93).
f. a small short stump or trunk of a tree, a small log.

m. a species of pulse, Phaseolus Mungo (El. Phaseolus Max or Radiatus) (Gr.Gr. 51, 164; W. 134, 155; L. 330, 338, 440; K.Pr. 42, 180). It is said to have cooling properties, and is much used as a diet for invalids. ¶ mŏnga-düjᵘ̈ f. a mŏng-field, a field prepared for sowing this pulse, or in which it is a crop. -hāl f. (sg. dat. -höjᵘ̈), a kind of rice bearing a fat round-shaped grain. -muzawar m. mŏng-soup, a kind of drink (cf. our barley-water) made of water in which the pulse is boiled. It is given to invalids; cf. muza-war, s.v. muza. -pholᵘ m. a little, or small quantity of mŏng (Gr.Gr. 164). -shāl m. a kind of rice with a fat round-shaped grain (cf. -hāl, ab.); 'a mŏng-jackal,' a very timid person, a great coward (one who hides himself, like a jackal, even in a field of short-stalked mŏng, when he sees a little dog in the distance). -ʦŏgan m.
