'fours of mŏng', i.e. what seems a very little to turn out, on calculation to be immeasurably great, a trifle becoming immense. The allusion is to a popular story, in which a king agreed to pay a physician a fee for curing his piles as follows: on the first square of a chessboard were to be placed four grains of mŏng; on the second square four times that number, or 16; on the third square four times the number on the second square, or 64; on the fourth square four times the number on the third square, or 256; and so on through the 64 squares, the number on each square being four times that on the preceding square. The fee was to be the total amount of grains so placed. ¶ The king looked upon this as a very trifling matter and gave the necessary orders; but when the total came to be calculated out it came to millions of maunds. Indeed, so great was the amount, that the king could not pay it, and had to make over his whole kingdom and private property in order to discharge the debt. -worᵘ m. a cake of mŏng-flour mixed with sauce and fried.
f. a certain bird, the Lesser Cormorant, Graculus sinensis (L. 132, mung).
f. a pill of charas (the resinous inflorescence of the hemp-plant) prepared for smoking.
f. a kind of wooden maul for applying plaster; a club, a mace (K. 390).
(? spelling and gender), saffron in a dry condition, made from the white base of the flower-stigma. It is not the best quality (L. 344).
m. a wild creeper chiefly found in forests, used internally as a remedy for skin diseases (L. 76, mangal).
m. a kind of water-weed, with numerous small leaves floating in masses over the water. mŏngölⁱ-byôlⁱ m. the seed of this plant; met. a collection of innumerable articles.
m. (sg. dat. mŏngaras, Gr.Gr. 58; f. mŏngᵘ̈rᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 33), the young of a goat, a kid (Gr.Gr. 35).
adj. c.g. proud, haughty, arrogant, disdainful; --˚ honouring, obeying (cf. ān-mönī, p. 30a, l. 32).
f. pride, self-respect, the condition of one who keeps up his sense of dignity (even when reduced to poverty) and who refuses to ask for help.

m. a king among sages, a great sage of ancient days (Śiv. 277, 631, 676, 696, etc.; Rām. 951, 1682, 1752; K. 47, 355, 384, 386, 577, 582, 1038, 1054); met. a sedate gentle-natured man who, at the present day, leads an ascetic life, a man of saintly disposition.
or mŏnjĕl adj. c.g. possessing a hidden root (cf. mö̆nḍᵘ̈ 1); hence, met. respected, honoured, highly thought of, worshipful, distinguished (cf. hĕngal-mŏnjal, p. 339b, l. 45).
or mŏnjaṭh m. (sg. dat. mŏnjaṭas), a kind of cowry-shell with three corners.
adv., as in aḍ-mŏnjĕ (p. 10a, l. 41), at a reduced price. ? Cf. mö̆nḍᵘ̈ 1.
m. clumsiness, unskilfulness, want, or loss, of dexterity (Gr.Gr. 30, 140).

(also written munjhōr) or (El.) magar m. the name of the ninth month of the Hindū year (in Sanskrit Mārgaśīrṣa and Hindī Agahan, and corresponding to November-December) (El. monjhór; W. 107, mo˙njhor; K.Pr. 128; Rām. 1634; K. 267). mŏnjhūri adv. in the month of Mọ̆njᵘhōr (Rām. 206).
i.q.mō̃ṭhurᵘ. mōnṭhᵘ̈rᵘ̈, i.q. mō̃ṭhᵘ̈rᵘ̈.mönṭhurᵘ̈, i.q. mö̃ṭhurᵘ, qq.v.

f. henna, the powdered leaves of the henna plant, or Broad Egyptian Privet (Lawsonia alba, etc.), beaten up with catechu and made into paste, much used by women on festive occasions for dyeing the hands and the soles of the feet a reddish orange, and sometimes by men for dyeing their beards (YZ. 79, 329, 446, 546; Śiv. 910).
f. (sg. dat. möñᵉ̆rüñᵉ̆), gaining or inducing a person's consent, agreement, or compliance; gaining or inducing confession, admission.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. möñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), i.q. möñᵉ̆run, q.v. (K. 616).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. möñᵒrᵒ), to cause or induce a person to consent, agree, or comply (K. 616); to cause or induce a person to confess; causal of mānun, q.v. in all its senses.

m. fear, alarm. --bĕhun -- m.inf. fear to sit down, terror to take possession of a person (and remain), constant fear (of something) to be experienced. --bĕhanāwun -- m.inf. to put and keep a person in constant fear. -dāñĕ m. a kind of paddy, the grain of which is dark on one side and pale red on the other.

f. a great collection of snow, a snowdrift, the piled-up snow on a mountain side, such as may fall in an avalanche, an avalanche (L. 458, mān; Śiv. 1301, 1308; Rām. 1579). māñĕ-bayĕ f. fear of (being overwhelmed by) an avalanche.
adj. (f.müñᵘ̈), weighing so many man (of one and a half seers, or three pounds each). Used --˚ as in daha-moñᵘ, weighing ten man (p. 199a, l. 13). See man 3.
f. a kind of dye-stuff (for dyeing woollen or cotton cloth black).
f. a certain weight equivalent to four maunds or 160 seers of two pounds each. See man 2.
or muöfī معآفی f. forgiveness, pardon (Gr.M.).

m. a peacock (Gr.Gr. 22; K.Pr. 203; Śiv. 1640; K. 922, 951). -mujᵘ̈ f. a carrot (Daucus carota) (El. mormúj; L. 67, 82, mor mujh). -pakhᵃch m. (sg. dat. -pakhcas), a peacock's feather. -tīrᵘ̈ f. the feather of a peacock's tail. -ʦạndᵃrakh m. (sg. dat. -ʦandrakas), the expanded tail of a peacock. ¶ mōra-chal, see mŏrchala. -kach m. (sg. dat. -kachas), a kind of creeping grass possessing narcotic properties (L. 76). Cf. kach.
m. the general appearance, look, or guise (of a man, etc., which distinguishes him or it from others).

adv. in front of, face to face (Rām. 704, 1407; K. 579, 660, 759). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to put in front (of an opponent), to set obstacles, etc., in his way. --roṭᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --rüṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), seized or taken before a person's (esp. the owner's) face. --raṭun -- m.inf. to take, or seize (something) in front of a person or before his face.

or muralī f. a flute, fife, pipe (Gr.M.; Śiv. 989, 998, 1323, 1439, 1453; K. 260-2, 270, 275, 280, 282, 412). -dar m. he who carries a flute, N. of Kṛṣṇa (Krishna) (K. 260). -manōhar m. he who charms with a flute, another N. of Kṛṣṇa (Śiv. 853).

conj. 1 (1 p.p., f. mōranövᵘ̈. This verb is used impersonally in the feminine gender in tenses formed from the past participle; cf. mōravünᵘ̈), to appease, cool (one's own, or another's, anger, pain, abuse, sorrow, etc.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p., f. mōrüvᵘ̈. This verb is used impersonally, and in the feminine gender in tenses formed from the past participle (Gr.Gr. 117, 119, 192, 214, 220). (anger, sorrow, pain, etc.) to be assuaged, calmed (cf. mōrüñᵘ̈); to assuage, calm, appease, cool (as ab.) (cf. mōranāvüñᵘ̈).
conj. 1, noted only in the phrase nakh mōrawȧnⁱ, s.v. nakh 2, q.v.; cf. mūrun. To be distinguished from mōravüñᵘ̈, q.v.
or mŏrabbā (= مربی) m. preserved fruit, preserve, jam, conserve, confection (cf. dönᵘ̈-mᵘ̈, p. 223b, l. 10) (Gr.M. mŏrabba).

mŏrachala, or mōrachal m. a whisk, or fan, of peacock's feathers (for driving away flies, etc.). It is used in state ceremonies (e.g. carried and used over a king, an idol, or the like). -bardār m. the carrier, or wielder, of such a whisk (Śiv. 1148). --karun -- m.inf. to use such a whisk (YZ. 171; Rām. 1079, 1132); met. to show great honour, or hospitality, to a guest.
adj. c.g. dead, defunct (K.Pr. 9, 145, 165); as subst., m. a dead body, a corpse (Gr.M. murda) (Rām. 130, 1500).
m. a dead body, a corpse; carrion; as adj. c.g. dead; impure, polluted, obscene; dirty (El.); (in Kāshmīrī, as subst., f.) an unchaste woman, a strumpet, trull.
f. a violent epidemic, cholera, etc. (cf. mȧricᵘ̈).

m. N. of a certain demon (in Skt., Mārīca), son of Sunda and Tāḍaka. He was severely wounded by Rāma in the latter's boyhood (Rām. 109). During the period of Rāma's banishment Rāvaṇa persuaded Mārīca much against his will to take the form of a golden deer, and so to entice Rāma from his hermitage. Sītā was thus left an easy prey to Rāvaṇa. On this occasion he was killed by Rāma (Rām. 344, 366, 375, 433).
m. a kind of shawl-work embroidered with silk and gold thread (L. 377).
a certain caterpillar which causes considerable loss to trees, especially to the Wych Hazel (L. 157, 459).
conj. 1, noted only in the phrase nakh mōrun, s.v. nakh 2, q.v. Cf. mūrun, of which it is apparently a by-form. To be distinguished from mōrüñᵘ̈, q.v.

conj. 3 (2 p.p., f. mōryēyĕ. This verb is conjugated in the feminine), calm (of anger, pain, abuse, sorrow, etc.) to be produced (to a person), to be calmed, to become quieted (Rām. 490); (of a flower or the like) to droop, become flaccid. mōryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mōryē-müʦᵘ̈), calmed, as ab.; (of a flower) drooping, become flaccid.
adj. c.g. an embroiderer, a man (or woman) who embroiders or does similar work.

or (vill.) moḍᵘ m. the body (of a man) (El. maur) (H. ii, 5-7, 9-11); (with suff. of indef. art.) morᵘāh, Rām. 671). ¶ mȧrⁱ-dyādumⁱ adj. (f. -dyādümᵘ̈), one who has reached old age, old, aged, an ancient; one who is virtuous, worthy (i.e. distinguished by quietness of character, self-restraint, truth, religious feeling, etc.). -dyādȧmⁱ mahanyuwᵘ m. an old man who is the oldest in a company, the senior present. mȧrⁱ-sāday f. caring for the body, attending to and curing an invalid; the custom of performing the funeral rites over an imitation of the body of a Brāhmaṇ who has died, and whose body for any reason cannot be found. The imitation body is made of leaves, etc. ¶ maris bĕhun m.inf. to be in comfortable circumstances (i.e. without care or sorrow, and well supplied with creature comforts).
m. a killer, one who kills; used --˚ as in hata-môrᵘ, p. 357b, l. 28.
m. a dovecot (cf. kōtar-morᵘ, p. 491b, l. 49) (K.Pr. 57); a fowl-house (cf. kŏkar-morᵘ, p. 432a, l. 38) (El. mur) (Gr.Gr. 9); a hut (Gr.Gr. 9). Cf. mar 1.

adj. (f. mörᵘ̈ 2), killed; as one dead, swooned, or the like; struck, hit (cf. nījĕ-mᵒ, s.v. nījᵘ̈ 1); (of grain, etc.) infertile, infecund, barren, husk without grain; (of a plant) dead, withered. Cf. mārun.
in mörⁱ-mondⁱ adj. (f. -münzᵘ̈), beautiful, pretty, lovely, well-formed (El. mãrmund) (YZ. 316).
(for 1, see mār 4; for 2, see môrᵘ 2) f. a female sheep, a ewe (one which has not yet had young).
or mŏsarmān m. (f. mŏsalmānañ (Gr.Gr. 38) or mŏsarmānañ), a believer in the religion of Islām, a Musalmān, a Mohammedan, a Moslem (W. 17, musalmān, f. musalmönⁱ; K.Pr. 116, 147).
f. the Mohammedan religion, Islām, Mohammedanism.

or mushᵉ̆kh, also written mushikh (= مشک) m. (but f. in the compound dᵃha-mŏshᵃkh, p. 198a, l. 32) (sg. dat. mŏshkas, etc.), musk (YZ. 9); a scent, a sweet smell, odour (Gr.M.; Śiv. 47, 1660; Rām. 1096, 1626, 1772) (cf. nāsti-mᵒ, s.v. nāst); a stink, a foul smell; the act of smelling, sniffing at something that has an odour; a pinch of snuff (K.Pr. 36, mushak). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take a smell, to smell (something) (Gr.M., W. 88, Rām. 617). --raṭun -- m.inf. a smell to take hold, the smell of something to cling to something else. --wŏthun -- m.inf. a smell to arise, to become corrupt and stinking. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. a smell to come, the smell of something at a distance to be experienced. ¶ mushka-budij f. a kind of paddy with a small, white, highly scented grain (L. 463); the rice grain of this paddy; cf. kŏla- budij, p. 437a, l. 43. -barith adj. c.g. filled with scent, fragrant (El. mushkaberrit). -vīrᵘ̈ or -vīr f. the musk willow (cf. bŏṭa-vīr, p. 138b, l. 43). ¶ mushkȧnⁱ-dār m.pl. great fragrance, a very sweet odour (Gr.M.; K. 777, 924).

or mösᵃm (= معصوم) adj. c.g. (as subst., f. mösümᵘ̈), an infant or child (esp. one ten years old or younger) (YZ. 26, ma'sūm; Śiv. 471 (f.)); cf. môsum. -bata m. offerings of food given to children (given by his sons, etc., on the death of an old man).
f. the actions of a child, childishness.
or musurᵘ adj. (f. mŏsürᵘ̈ or musᵘ̈rᵘ̈), marked with the scars of smallpox, pock-marked.

f. a species of sweet-smelling grass, Cyperus pertenuis (the nāgar mōthā of India proper) (L. 76, most, used as a stomachic medicine). Cf. bēra-mōsta, p. 117b, l. 30. ¶ mōsti-mūl m. its root (which is long and thin). -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. the root and lower part of the stalk of this plant.
adj. c.g. acquired, collected; tax, duty, toll, excise, custom, postage (Gr.M.); the result of labour, the crop (of a field, etc.) (Rām. 97).

c.g., i.q. mösm, q.v. (sg. ag. mōsaman, Rām. 602, 1417; pl. dat. mōsaman, Rām. 267, 283), a boy child, a boy (Rām. 267, 280, 356, 380, 447, 806, 1347, 1384, 1533); a girl child, a little girl (Rām, 1621).

or musur m. (sg. dat. mọ̆sᵃras), a certain pulse or lentil, Ervum lens (El. masur). --karun -- m.inf. to make mŏsur; met. to pound or crush (some hard substance) to powder. ¶ mọ̆sᵃra-dāl f. split mŏsur, split pease; porridge made of this lentil. -hĕm or musạra-hĕm f. the pod of mŏsur; met. a secure subsistence for a family during future generations (such as a grant of land rent-free or the like).
adj. (f. mösiñᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a month, (lasting) for a month, (existing) for a month, a month old. Cf. mās 1 and nawa-mᵒ, s.v. nav 1.
or musᵘ 1 m. a kind of small globular turnip (Gr.Gr. 17). mŏsⁱ-gŏgⁱjⁱ f., id. Cf. gŏgᵃji-musᵃ, p. 279a, l. 19.
adj. (f. mö̃sᵘ̈), of (so many) months old (El. móṅs); (YZ. 367, Rām. 628, K. 43) (cf. nawa-mᵒ, s.v. nav 1).
(? mö̆ṭᵘ̈) in (?) mot-nĕnd f. the third weeding of a rice-crop (L. 463, motnind).
(for متصدی), m. an accountant, a clerk (H. ix, 7).

or (q.v.) mö̆ṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. mŏṭhi), a fist, the closed hand; a fistful, as much as can be held in the closed hand (cf. ana-mᵒ, p. 29b, l. 46; öṭⁱ-mⁱ, p. 53a, l. 31; dyāra-mᵒ, p. 270b, l. 44; hāra-mᵒ, p. 344b, l. 43, etc.); shampooing with the closed fist (done to the feet, etc.). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to shampoo, as ab. --ganḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to clench the fist (at a person); met. to bring a charge (against someone), to charge a person (with some fault). --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to let loose the fist; to gamble (holding a fistful of cowries in the hand, the number of which is guessed by the opponent). ¶ mŏṭha-gŏgᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. 'fist-turnip', i.e. hurting a person when shampooing him with the fist. ¶ mŏṭhi-phash m. fist-stroking, i.e. shampooing, as ab.

or maut موت m. death (El. mĕṭ, mót, móth; K.Pr. 10, 56, 105, maut; H. ix, 4) (cf. nẹ̆ndᵃri-mᵃ, s.v. nẹ̆ndᵃr). ¶ mōta-waröyi adv. without death, immortal (El. motaveráí). ¶ mōtȧnⁱ ʦhraṭh m.pl. (dat. --ʦhraṭan --), the throes of death, the pangs of a dying man; similar pangs experienced at some calamity.
m. (sg. dat. mö̃tas), a suckling child.
f. (sg. dat. mö̃ṭhi), silence, refusal to speak, inertness, great laziness (even in the most necessary actions). Cf. mū̃ṭhᵘ.

or mỗṭhunᵘ adj. (f. mö̃ṭhüñᵘ̈), (of a tree) having its branches lopped off, a bare stump; (of a person) one who has his arms or legs broken or amputated; one who has lost all his relations, one whose family is extinct (i.e. who has lost all his descendants).
or mũ̄̈thridār adj. c.g. giving an excellent out- turn (e.g. a crop, oilseeds, etc.).
see nadȧrⁱ-mỗⁱ, a short, drum-shaped piece of lotus-stalk, s.v. nadorᵘ.
m. the bare trunk of a tree; a log of wood.
adj. (f. mö̃ṭhᵘ̈rᵘ̈), an inert, lazy, person. Cf. mö̃ṭh.

or mǖ̃thᵃr 1 m. (sg. dat. mö̃tras), an initiatory secret formula (confided to a disciple by his spiritual teacher); any sacred mystical formula; a magical formula, charm, spell (El. mãnthᵃr). Cf. manthᵃr.

or mǖ̃thᵃr 2 f. (sg. dat. mö̃thri or mũ̄̈thri), outturn (of a crop; e.g. the outturn of rice from a quantity of paddy, or of oil from a quantity of oilseeds) (cf. kara-mᵒ, p. 466a, l. 2; muṭhⁱ-mⁱ, p. 605a, l. 9); the result of husking (L. 461, mántr). --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to calculate or estimate the outturn (of a crop, or of the oil produce of oilseeds, by testing a sample of known amount). --nērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a certain amount of outturn for a whole crop to be established by such estimation. --wuchüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to inspect the outturn, i.q. --kaḍüñᵘ̈, ab. ¶ mǖ̃thri-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), (of a crop) giving no, or very little, outturn (as ab.); as adv. (with verbs of giving, etc.), (of gifts of paddy or the like) without previous estimation of the outturn (of grain, etc.). -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), (of paddy, oilseeds, or the like) giving a rich outturn (as ab.). -sāvĕr m. (with reference to a cultivated field, or to a crop of paddy, oilseeds, or the like) richness of outturn (as ab.).
or moṭhᵘ 1 m. a change of fortune or luck (from good to bad or the reverse, but esp. the former).

f. (sg. dat. mŏchĕ, often written mŏcha), i.q. mŏṭh, q.v. the fist, the closed hand (L.V. 24; K.Pr. 227; Śiv. 377, 703); a fistful, a handful (K. 178, 1118, 1144-6) (cf. chañĕ mŏchĕ, empty-fistedly, i.e. in a condition of poverty, p. 162a, l. 49); stroking with the hand, patting (K. 1148). ¶ mŏchĕ-(mŏcha-)mã̄gay  f. fistful-begging, i.e. begging from house to house, and getting a handful of grain here and a handful there. -mūran f. (sg. dat. mūrüñᵘ̈), the act of husking grain between the hands. -pholᵘ m. (a beggar's store of) grain which has been collected by handfuls, as ab.

adj. (f.nom. müṭhᵘ̈, dat. machĕ), (of a thing) worthless, of no value; (of a person originally sharp) become dull, stupid. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become worthless, not to have the expected, or hoped for, result. --karun -- m.inf. to make (out to be) worthless, to show scorn for the results of another's great endeavours.
adj. (f.nom. müṭhᵘ̈, dat. machĕ), forgetful; also 1 p.p. of mashun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 209, 212).
f. a bit of a trunk (see the preceding), a hard block of wood (esp. a hard piece full of knots).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. mŏṭyōv), to become fat, stout, thick (Gr.M.); (of liquids) to become thick (by boiling down, etc.); to become extensive (of a work or business); to become vain, puffed up; to agree to a course of action; to become trained, to become docile (Śiv. 1562); to agree (to do any work). mŏṭyō-motᵘ perf. part. (mŏṭyē-müʦᵘ̈), become fat, fattened; become gross, unwieldy (Śiv. 762); become thickened (by boiling down); become extensive, enlarged (of a business); become vain, puffed up; one who has agreed to undertake a work and does so.
f. (sg. dat. mọ̆ṭᵃrüñᵃ), making fat or stout; making (some liquid) thick by boiling down (Gr.Gr. 121); telling a story or writing a book, etc., at great length.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. mọ̆tᵃ̇rôwᵃ̇), to make fat, fatten; to boil down and make thick (a liquid); to extend or make long a story or written composition; to induce a person to agree to and undertake a course of action.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mọ̆tᵒrᵒ), i.q. mọ̆ṭᵃrāwun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 7).

adj. (f. mö̆ṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. mŏcĕ), fat, plump, stout, corpulent (Gr.Gr. 29, 34, 140; Gr.M.; Śiv. 336) (cf. nala-mᵒ, s.v. nal); great, large; gross; dense, thick (Gr.M., W. 20); coarse. --drọ̆ṭᵘ -- adj. (f. mö̆ṭᵘ̈ drö̆ṭᵘ̈), very stout and strong, thick and hard. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become stout; met. (after long expectation) to give up hope, become hopeless. --kôḍᵘ -- m. the cerebrum (El.); cf. kôḍᵘ 1. --karun -- m.inf. to render a person hopeless (after long expectation).

m. the part of the back between a man's shoulders (on which burdens are carried) (for short, translated 'shoulders' in the ff.) (YZ. 551; H. xi, 10); cf. macyulᵘ. --darun -- m.inf. lit. the shoulders to become firm (for bearing a burden); met. to make up one's mind or resolve after consideration, to undertake (some difficult task). --dārun -- m.inf. lit. to offer one's shoulders (i.e. to help a man to carry a heavy burden) (K. 253); met. to offer help (with money, etc.) to anyone endeavouring to carry out a task beyond his strength. --dāran-wôlᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --dāran-wājĕñ --), one who is by nature ready to give help, as ab. --dārawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --dārawüñᵘ̈ --), one who is ready and willing to help, as ab., one who bears another's burdens. ¶ mȧṭⁱ-bôrⁱ m. the burden on (or intended to be placed on) a man's shoulders, a person's load. -düjᵘ̈ f. the cloth placed between a woman's shoulders (to prevent the dirt, etc., of her hair spoiling her clothes). -dāñĕ f. 'shoulders-paddy'. In former times land-tax was paid in kind, the Rājā of Kashmīr taking half the crop, which he sold in the city of Śrīnagar. The royal share was brought to the city in one of three ways--by boat, on horses, or on the shoulders of the cultivators. That brought in the last-named way was called 'shoulders-paddy'. -palav m. the shoulders-cloth, a cloth put on the back between the shoulders beneath a load. -sörᵘ̈ f. shoulders-collection, moving a pile of articles from one place to another in coolie-loads. -wôrᵘ m. a water-jar made for carrying on the shoulders. -wōrath f. (sg. dat. wōrüʦᵘ̈), shoulders-cover, a garment just large enough to cover the back down from the shoulders (typical of great poverty). ¶ maṭi adv. on (a person's) shoulders; hence, made over to so-and-so's responsibility (Śiv. 360, 1560; Rām. 211, 217, 362, 512, 850, 1122; K. 426, 489, 519, 565, 749, 1036, 1064, 1068). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go on to the shoulder, responsibility to be thrust upon one (K.Pr. 81). --khārun -- m.inf. to lift on to the shoulder; met. to throw the blame of something on to someone else. --khasun -- m.inf. blame to be thrown on someone by someone else, as ab.; cf. khār maṭi khasüñᵘ̈, p. 408a, l. 41, and mār mᵒ khᵒ, p. 586b, l. 48. --karun -- m.inf. to make on the shoulder, to make over, or entrust, some thing or work to another (K. 1034). --mara gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become permanently made over or entrusted; cf. the next. --marana āmotᵘ -- perf. part. pass. (f. --marana āmüʦᵘ̈--), saddled (for support, safe keeping, etc.) on another; cf. the next. --marana yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come permanently on the shoulder, (of some person or thing) to be permanently saddled upon another (so that he is responsible for his support or for its safe keeping). --maṭi -- 'on the shoulder, on the shoulder!'--an expression implying praise and encouragement (Śiv. 1560). --maṭi dinⁱ -- m.pl.inf. to utter cries of praise and encouragement, as ab. cf. marun 1

adj. (f. müʦᵘ̈ 1, Gr.Gr. 63, K.Pr. 70; for 2, see s.v.), mad, maddened, furious, a madman (Gr.Gr. 9, 37, 140, 143; Gr.M.; L.V. 105; K.Pr. 70, 80, 139, 147, 169; YZ. 259, 310, 474; Śiv. 1661, 1666; K. 195; H. v, 9); silly (W. 20); intoxicated (by liquor, pride, love, passion, etc.), a drunkard (Gr.M.; K. 281, 283-4); overpowered (by sleep, or the like); enraptured, charmed, intoxicated, delighted (K. 108, 936); intoxicated (by), devoted (to), a slave (to), rapturously busy (in something, dat.) (K. 386-7); deep, profound (of sleep) (Śiv. 1311). Often used --˚ in various figurative senses, as in kŏlayĕ-motᵘ, 'wife-mad,' uxorious (p. 442a, l. 19); khᵃñĕ-motᵃ, habitually and profusely snivelling (p. 405a, l. 40); mahārāza-motᵘ, a lunatic who thinks himself a king; māla-motᵘ, a Crœsus; mēla-motᵘ, the festival at a fair; māra-motᵘ, an ardent lover; maza-motᵘ, ravishing. pōshĕ-motᵘ, 'flower-mad,' a flower-fancier (K.Pr. 173). --bata -- m. comfort owing to great cheapness of food, clothing, etc. ¶ mȧtⁱ-ala m. a madman's trembling (cf. ala 4), a sudden attack of madness or fury. -hasun m. a madman's laughter; hence, a person (esp. a child) who habitually romps and plays like a lunatic. -mēla m. a collection of madmen, an assembly of persons maddened by drink, Indian hemp, or the like. -phash m. an occasional attack of madness (not occurring at regular intervals, but intermittently). -pöthᵃr m. the conduct of a madman, conduct like that of a madman. -wôñᵘ m. maddening water (e.g. of some river, the water of which, when drunk, drives one mad); met. a condition of anarchy or tyranny and wickedness in which the Government officials and the inhabitants of a country all act like madmen. -wôñᵘ wasun -- m.inf. such a condition of anarchy and wickedness to descend, i.e. to become prevalent. ¶ müʦᵘ̈ nẹ̆ndᵃr f. deep, heavy sleep, coma. ¶ maʦa-kŏnḍul m. one who acts like a lunatic, though sane. -phyār m. the raving of a mad woman, the nonsense spoken and done by her; the wildly conducted son of a mad woman. -pöthᵃr f. the conduct of a mad woman; conduct like that of a mad woman; a group or assembly of mad women. -wardan m. clothes that do not fit (i.e. too long, too short, too loose, or too tight for the wearer), badly cut clothes.

m. embracing, hugging (cf. nāla-motᵘ, s.v. nāl 1) (K. 292, 399). mȧtⁱ-mūr f. a fistful of silver coins given by her mother and other female relations to a bride on her starting after marriage for her husband's house. These are intended to be given by her as presents to her father-in-law's people. Cf. mēṭhöyⁱ.
adj. c.g. silly (El. mutwāl); intoxicated, drunken (Śiv. 1260). Cf. motᵘ 1.
i.q. ma or mā, prohibitive particle (H. v, 11, poet.); cf. mav. -mö 1  a particle denoting uncertainty or hesitation.
in mōv-mö2 m. the name of the letter ma , used in schools.
f. the comb of a cock (cf. mawal 2); the root of a fish's ear (? the gill).

m. the string held in the palm of the hand from which the beam of a pair of scales is suspended; cf. māv. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to pull the above string of a balance (so as to show a false weight); to give another person an opportunity (for doing something). --lagun -- m.inf. an opportunity to occur or become available. --ʦhāḍun --m.inf. to wait for, or seek for, an opportunity. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. an opportunity to come (after long waiting for it).
adj. (f. mövᵘ̈), fleshy, brawny. --māz -- m. the entire flesh or carcass of a butchered sheep, goat, etc.

(cf. موی) f. a little, a little bit, a scrap (K. 1119); often used as a suffix forming diminutives for all words except those indicating kinds of wood and grain (Gr.Gr. 164) (cf. bāga-mŏy, p. 90a, l. 2; khōra-mŏy, p. 410a, l. 49; khrāvi-mŏy, p. 416b, l. 3; khēshĕ-mŏy, p. 418a, l. 6); nĕcivⁱ-mŏy (masc.), a baby boy, s.v. nĕcyuwᵘ; and nāra-mŏy, s.v. nār. ¶ mŏyā or mŏyāh f. the same as mŏy, with the indef. art. added, a little (cf. añĕma-mŏyā, p. 37b, l. 2; bata-mŏyā, p. 137a, l. 30; hāka-mŏyā, p. 326b, l. 25; khōra-mŏyā, p. 410a, l. 49; khrāvi-mŏyāh, p. 416b, l. 3) (Gr.Gr. 164, W. 21). ¶ mŏyĕ mŏyĕ adv. little by little. -wāl m. 'a hair of a little', a very little.
m. hair (YZ. 5, 17, 73, 289). Cf. mō and mŏy.
m. stockings reaching above the knees (El.).
or mazūr (= مزدور) m. (f. mŏzᵃrĕñ), a hired labourer, a paid workman (cf. dŏga-mŏzūr, p. 194b, l. 26; Gr.M. mazūr; W. 17, 18, mazur; f. muzrėñ).

(? = معذور) adj. (f. môzūrᵘ̈), excused; helpless, powerless; unserviceable; (in Kāshmīrī) crook-backed, one bent double by disease and only able to walk on one's hands and knees, a cripple (Gr.Gr. 23). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become crook-backed, as ab. --karun -- m.inf. to make (a person) crook-backed, to injure his waist, thighs, or the like, as ab. --kŏthulᵘ -- adj. (f. kŏthᵘ̈jᵘ̈), a crook-back bundle, i.e. a man who (through laziness or weakness) goes about like a crook-back on his hands and knees.
(? = معذوری) f. the condition of being crook-backed, the being compelled to walk on one's hands and knees.
f. bodily labour, work; wages paid to a hired labourer, price of labour, hire (cf. dŏga-mŏzūrⁱ, p. 194b, l. 28, and nāwa-mᵒ, s.v. nāv 2) (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 142, mazūri).

m. a man, a human being (usually in a more or less contemptuous sense; for instance, in folk-tales it is used by demons speaking of human beings). Used esp. in the following:--mö̃ʦa-bŏy f. the smell of a man, the scent given forth by a solitary human being in some place where there are no others (as when, in English folk-tales, a giant says 'I smell the smell of a man') (H. xii, 15); cf. manᵃshĕ-bŏy, p. 581b, l. 40. -krṻl m. 'a human weevil', (esp. with ref. to a child) a miserable specimen of humanity, a starveling child.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. mọ̆tᵘ or mọ̆ʦᵘ; 2 p.p. mŏʦōv or mŏʦyōv), to remain over and above, to be left remaining (Gr.Gr. 226; L.V. 1, 2, 9, 11, 21; Śiv. 1019, 1658, 1757, 1901). mọ̆ʦᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mö̆ʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), remaining over and above, that which has remained over.
f. (sg. dat. mọ̆ʦᵃrüñᵃ), the action of leaving over and above, leaving a residue.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mọ̆ʦᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. mọ̆ʦᵃrun, q.v., to leave over and above, to leave a residue (Śiv. 1344, 1866, 1881).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mọ̆ʦᵒrᵒ), to leave over and above, to leave a residue (i.e. after dealing with a number of things to leave a part undealt with). Cf. mọ̆ʦᵃrāwun.
adj. c.g. soft, tender; esp. (of a human being) mild, gentle, affable, kind.
m. (f. mragiñ, q.v.), a deer, an antelope (L.V. 47); (m.) a buck, stag; (f.) a doe. mraga-shĕr or -shēr or -shōr f. N. of the fifth lunar asterism (in Skt., Mṛga-śiraḥ).
f. (sg. dat. mragāzë˘ñᵘ̈), the skin of a deer (esp. of the black antelope) (used by Hindū ascetics as a seat, garment, etc.).
f. epilepsy, falling-fits (attributed to possession by an evil spirit).
f. (f. of mrag, q.v.), a female deer, a doe.
m. (sg. dat. mratas), death, decease (Rām. 63, 108, 406, 1299, 1397). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. death to come.
m. a name of Śiva, as he who conquers death, in Skt. Mrtyuṁjaya (Śiv. 376, 916, 1086, 1256, 1698).
or mŏbārakh مبارک interj. welcome! (El., YZ. 463, Śiv. 1720). --karun -- m.inf. or (Rām. 751) manzil-mubārakh karun m.inf. to congratulate, to welcome (El.; H. x, 8).
or muchᵘ 2 (for 1, see mọ̆chᵘ) adj. c.g. or m. (f. muchᵘ̈), come loose, come apart, separated (e.g. a door come apart from its post, and so on of two or more things usually forming one whole).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. muchᵘ 3), to complete a vow, to conclude a fast, to eat after a fast.
m. foolish, silly, dull, stupid, ignorant (L.V. 66, K.Pr. 146). Cf. muḍa.

adj. c.g. a fool, a blockhead, dunce, an ignorant, illiterate fellow; slow of understanding (El. muḍah) (Gr.M; K.Pr. 190, 216); cf. mūḍ. -cŏbur m. a stout, healthy, or fat blockhead (esp. in a family, the members of which are expected to be educated).
m. joy, gladness, happiness (YZ. 101, 191, 246, 259). (This word is masculine in all the above passages. In Sanskrit it is fem.)
m. a desire, wish (Rām. 1153, 1565). Cf. mŏdā.
adv. at last, finally (Rām. 788, 833, 843, 970); in short, to sum up, to make a long story short (Rām. 70, 1044, 1159).
f. the condition of an illiterate blockhead, stupidity, ignorance (Gr.M.).
m. the defendant (in a lawsuit) (Gr.M.). Cf. muddaādār and mudoyᵘ.
adj. c.g. perpetual, lasting, eternal; (of a lover) constant (YZ. 228).
or mudawār m. the middle of the upper part of the roof of a house, a roof-ridge; meton. a ridge-pole.
m. length of time, space of time, interval of time; a long time or season; antiquity. mudatukᵘ adj. (f. mudatücᵘ̈), of long standing, old, ancient.

m. a gall, or sore (on the shoulder or back of a horse). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. a gall to arise. ¶ mudawas mȧchⁱ f. a fly on a horse's sore (which comes back again and again); met. following a person continually, clinging to, dogging.
f. a fixed look, a stare. --ganḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to fix a stare, to stare. ¶ mudȧyⁱ mudȧyⁱ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to answer an accusation or a calumny face to face.
m. the defendant in a lawsuit (K.Pr. 54). Cf. mudāla and mudoyᵘ.
m. a claimant, suitor; the plaintiff (in a lawsuit) (Gr.M.). Cf. muddaādār and mudāla.

f. (sg. dat. mudri), any particular position or intertwinings of the fingers (in Sanskrit, mudrā), commonly practised in Hindū religious worship. Such have an occult meaning, and are believed to have magical efficacy (L.V. 2).
m. (sg. dat. mūḍatas), ignorance, stupidity, folly.
adj. (f. mūḍyē-müʦᵘ̈), become confounded, confused, become dull, stupid. This word has the form of a perfect participle, but no other form of such a verb as mūḍun has been noted.
p.p. of marun, q.v. used as adj. (f. mŏyĕ), dead (Gr.Gr. 19, K.Pr. 146).
m.sg. or pl. dead, deceased (before the present time). -māy f. silence (of a person) like that of a corpse, deadly taciturn.
adv. gratis, gratuitously (El., K.Pr. 203); cf. mupht. māl-ĕ-muft, property by gift (K.Pr. 133).
adj. c.g. having high or prominent or fat cheeks.

m. loss of consciousness, perplexity, delusion, embarrassment; folly, ignorance, infatuation; illusion of mind, delusion (K. 209); (in a Hindū religious sense) the illusion that transient things are eternal, or that the phenomenal world has real existence (very common in Hindū poetry in this sense) (L.V. 67, 74; Śiv. 18, 268-9, 347, 888, etc.; Rām. 1762). This word is a corruption of mōh or mūh (q.v.) which is borrowed directly from Sanskrit. When this word is used to indicate 'Illusion' personified, it has the genitive in -unᵘ, as in Śiv. 711, 1332, 1693, 1778. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. astonishment, delusion, embarrassment, insensibility, fainting, etc., to occur; delusion to depart, true knowledge to be acquired (Śiv. 1276). --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to stupefy, perplex, infatuate. --wŏthun -- m.inf. infatuation to arise; arrogance, insolence, to come into existence. ¶ muha-māyā or (Rām. 1077) f. delusion caused by unreality of the universe being considered as real (Śiv. 893); an illusion, an illusive appearance (Rām. 1077). ¶ muhas gaʦhun m.inf. to go to delusion, to become deluded (K. 657, 783, 930).

m. an urgent, or momentous business, important affair; exigency, an affair of consequence; (in Kāshmīrī) misfortune, poverty (El. muhyum; K.Pr. 165; H. i, 4, 5, 11, 12; viii, 9; x, 3). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. poverty to fall (of a rich man being reduced to beggary). --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to cast poverty, to reduce another to beggary. -zad adj. c.g. poverty-stricken (H. x, 4). ¶ muhima, by poverty; hence, as postpos. governing abl., in the case of poverty, i.e. in the case of (such-and-such a thing) not being forthcoming, if there is not (such-and-such a thing), as in sini muhima sŏʦal, if there is not a plate of meat and rice, there is (at least) a mallow. ¶ muhⁱmunⁱ, sg. gen., in muhⁱmȧnⁱ phŏtⁱ m.pl. utter poverty.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. muhimladiñ), suffering from utter poverty, poverty-stricken.
m. a great collection of jewelry and ornaments.
f. a small pestle, a rod (f. dim. of muhulᵘ, q.v.) (cf. nāra-mᵒ, s.v. nār).

m. a pestle (W. 3, mahol, 114, möhal); esp. a long heavy wooden pestle for husking rice, etc., in a mortar (El. muhil) (L. 462); cf. kanz-mᵒ (p. 459b, l. 29), nāra-mᵒ, s.v. nār, and yẹ̆ndra-mᵒ, s.v. yẹ̆ndᵃr. muhᵃ̇lᵃ̇-khün ḍᵘ̈ f. a pestle worn light and thin by use.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. muhᵘ, f. mushᵘ̈ (Gr.Gr. 210); 2 p.p. mushyōv or muhyōv (Gr.Gr. 225); cf. Gr.Gr. 225), to swindle, defraud, delude, cause illusion to (Śiv. 1728); to fascinate (Gr.M.); (conj. 2) to suffer illusion, to be deceived (L.V. 13). ¶ muhᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mushᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), swindled, defrauded. ¶ muhith gaʦhun m.inf. to run off with property after swindling. --nyunᵘ -- m.inf. to steal property by swindling. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. openly to carry off property gained by swindling.
or muhūrta m. a moment, a short period of time (K.Pr. 176; K. 970, 1037); a period, time (auspicious or otherwise). Cf. brahma-muᵒ, p. 120b, l. 45; K. 970 has bröhmī-muᵒ, with the same meaning.
m. contending, disputing; contention, disputation, altercation; disputation, argument carried on in an assembly.

m. that which is carried to the account or credit (of), credit; allowance, deduction. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give credit (for a sum), to allow an abatement or deduction, to give the net amount due (Śiv. 1860).
adj. c.g. approved, permitted, tolerated; (in the Kashmīr revenue system) a system of annually settling the revenue demand of a village partly in kind and partly in cash (L. 407, 411, 450).
adj. c.g. existing, extant, present (Śiv. 1521); at hand, available (Gr.M.).
adj. (f. mujᵘ̈), laziness, inaction, abstention, through laziness, from even the most necessary actions such as eating and drinking.

(sometimes written muj, mujⁱ, or mūjⁱ) f. a radish (K.Pr. 15, 94, 107, 146, 167). The two varieties of radish in Kashmīr are the köshirᵘ̈ mujᵘ̈ and the wāṭa mujᵘ̈. Cf. El., s.v. múj (Gr.Gr. 16, 145, 163, 164; L. 457, 463 (mujh)). ¶ mujĕ kaḍañĕ f. pl. inf. to pluck radishes; met. heedlessly to waste time over any work. ¶ muji (or mujĕ)-bọ̆dᵘ  m. a bundle of radishes (Gr.Gr. 145). -caṭiñ f. a conserve of radishes, radish chutney. -dã̄d m. a radish-ox; met. a fool, a noodle. -dā̃durᵘ m. a radish-gardener, a man who cultivates or sells radishes. -ḍākur m. the juice expressed from pounded radishes; the flesh of a radish; cf. ḍākur 2. -ḍēmb m. a radish island, a lake-island in which radishes are profusely cultivated. -dar m. radish-rate, a scale-pan containing radishes for weighment. (Radishes can be weighed only roughly, and, as the purchaser will not take less than the stipulated weight, he usually gets something over); hence, met. overweight in weighing. -ḍār m. a field of radishes. -dĕv m. a radish-devil, i.e. a man round as a radish, a great round fat fellow (esp. when a fool and ugly looking). -gab m. the sprout of a radish (found in the centre of the leaf-cluster). -gë̆ḍᵘ̈ f. a row of bundles of radishes. -hüṭᵘ̈ f. a chip of dried radish. (Radishes are sliced and then dried, and so preserved for use.) -khünḍᵘ̈ f. a slice or bit of radish. -kala m. the top of a radish (where the sprouts appear). -konḍᵘ m. a radish-grater, an appliance for grating radishes; roughness caused by cold, or chapping, of the back of the hand. -köñᵘ̈ f. a few radishes (Gr.Gr. 163), i.q. -tulᵘ, bel. -koṭᵘ m. a radish seedling (for transplantation). -kyowᵘ m. a small kind of radish; cf. kĕvⁱ-mujⁱ, p. 502b, l. 30. -loṭᵘ m. the long thin tail at the bottom of a radish. -mŏla adj. c.g. the price of a radish; met. a very small price (given for something valuable). -mulⁱvĕñ f. a collection of radish leaves dried for winter consumption. -pạtᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a bunch of radish leaves (Gr.Gr. 74). -thôpᵘ m. a few radishes (Gr.Gr. 164), i.q. -tulᵘ, bel. -tulᵘ m. a few radishes (Gr.Gr. 164); a bunch of young tender radish leaves; a young radish together with its tender leaves. -türᵘ̈ f. the flower (or seed-) stem of a radish. -ʦakul m. a circular slice of a large radish. -ʦöryunᵘ m. the refuse leaves of a radish (after selecting the ones good to eat). -ʦyūṭᵘ m. a sauce of grated or of pounded radishes. -wū̃ṭh m. a radish-camel, i.e. a camel which is continually helping itself from a pile of radishes; met. a fat greedy fool. -wạthᵃr m. a radish leaf. -zanḍ m. a few radishes (Gr.Gr. 163), i.q. -tulᵘ, ab.
m. an affair, matter (Gr.M.); a law-case, a criminal or civil trial (Gr.M.).

adj. c.g. having one's face blackened, publicly disgraced. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. (of some respectable person) to experience disgrace (by being subjected to public abuse or the like). --karun -- m.inf. to put to disgrace, as ab.
adj. c.g. settled, fixed, established (Gr.M.; Rām. 143, 1680). --karun -- m.inf. to establish, fix, ratify (El., Gr.M., Śiv. 638).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mukôwᵘ), to finish, complete; cf. mukun 3. mukāwan-kōmᵘ̈ or --kömᵘ̈ -- f. hurried completion.
m. brokerage, commission on a sale or purchase. I.q. mukīmāna, q.v.
f. (sg. dat. mukharüñᵘ̈), loquacity, etc. (see mọ̆khorᵘ); sauciness, impertinence (in language) (see ditto).
m. (sg. dat. mukharanas), display of impertinence or sauciness (in language).
m. an informer, a spy (in Kashmīr the profession is not looked upon as dishonourable, L. 421).
m. an appraiser, a broker; esp. a pashmīna-broker (El., who spells the word also makáim).
m. a broker's fee, commission (K.Pr. 109). Cf. mukaymāna.
f. a blow or thump with the fist.
m. bran; a preparation of gold and silver leaves, etc., which is plastered over a Musalmān Kāshmīrī bride's face ten days after the wedding, when she returns to her husband's house (K.Pr. 131).
m. the lord of final emancipation (see mŏkᵃ̇tᵃ̇) (Śiv. 858, 938, 984, 1159).
m. scurf (in the head and elsewhere).

m. wailing, used in the following:-- ¶ mukan-hāl f. (sg. dat. -höjᵘ̈ or -höjⁱ), a wailing room, the room or place in which the customary wailing for a dead person is performed by the women of the house and of the neighbourhood. -höjᵘ̈ bĕhun m.inf. to sit in the place of lamentation; to begin the lamentations at a death (when a number of people assemble for loud lamentation).
m. to eat sattū (i.e. ground parched grain) or other food in the same manner. (Sattū is eaten by picking up the food with the tops of the fingers, and pitching it from a distance into the mouth.)
conj. 3, only noted in the following:-- mukyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mukyē-müʦᵘ̈), completed, finished. Cf. mŏkalun and mukāwun.
m. a N. of Vishnu or Krishna, said to mean 'the giver of final liberation (Skt. muku)' (Śiv. 1417).

or mūkūf (= مَوقُوف) adj. c.g. stopped, suspended, discontinued (Gr.M., Rām. 1744); postponed, destined not to occur (Rām. 63, 99); dependent (upon, dat.) (Gr.M.); remitted, forgiven (of a tax or the like) (Rām. 1132).
adj. (f. mucᵘ̈) flat-nosed, snub-nosed. ¶ muka-nostᵘ m. a man who has a flat-nose, flat-nosed. -nasth f. a flat-nosed woman; met. a woman of a quarrelsome disposition.

(also spelt mōl) m. (pl. dat. mūlan, not mōlan, Gr.Gr. 51. With emphatic y the ablative of this word is mulay, q.v.), a root (of a plant or tree) (Gr.Gr. 43, 51; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 146, 184; Śiv. 747, 1430, 1530; K. 979); the root or fang of a tooth (cf. armi-mūl, p. 43b, l. 19); the root, basis, groundwork, beginning, principle, origin, cause, source (Gr.M.); the intention, root-idea (of a work, thought, etc.); the basis, foundation (YZ. 332; Śiv. 165; Rām. 710, 952, 961, 1375; K. 171). --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to fix roots, (of a tree lately planted) to become firm by spreading out its roots; to found a family (e.g. when a childless person adopts a son); to set up a person in business (by providing capital, etc.). --kaḍun -- or mūla kaḍun m.inf. to pull up the root, i.e. to pull up a tree by the roots (Gr.M. mūla kaḍun; K.Pr. 100, id.; Rām. 929, 1626, id.); to destroy utterly (a family); (of an object of study) to probe to the bottom, analyse. --nērun -- m.inf. the root to go forth, to be pulled up by the root; (of a family) the only offspring to be cut off; (of a subject of study) to be probed to the bottom. --ʦhĕnȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to cut the roots, to cut off, destroy (Rām. 768). --yinⁱ -- m.pl.inf. (of a newly planted tree) roots to spring forth, to take root; (met.) to take root, to be rooted to one's seat, to refuse to get up and work. ¶ mūla-dana m. capital, principal, stock-in-trade. -dyār m.pl. accumulated capital. -gab m. a sprout from the root. --gālun -- m.inf. to destroy from the root, utterly to destroy (Rām. 154, 159). -mŏnjĕ adv. root and trunk, root and branch (u.w. vbs. indicating pulling up, destruction, etc.). -phyurᵘ m. inversion, transmutation, from the very beginning. -pŏrush m. the founder of a family, the earliest ancestor; the leader of a row of persons; the name of a special piṇḍa or lump of rice offered to Manes at obsequial ceremonies or śrāddhas. -rã̄ḍa m. a hereditary rascal, a rascal belonging to a rascal family; a rascal from his birth. -tala adv. thoroughly, from the very bottom, after thorough discussion (Śiv. 27, 1343). ¶ mūlan drôtᵘ pạtran sag m. a sickle to the root and water to the leaves; hence, acting outwardly as a friend, but secretly as an enemy.

f. the N. of the 17th (or, according to some, the 19th) lunar asterism (Skt. mūlā). mūla-kŏnḍüjᵘ̈ f. a horoscope or diagram in which are marked the positions of the various planets, etc., at the time of a person's birth.
m. the place of origin; wealth, assets, resources; (in Śaiva mysticism) the mystical circle above the organ of generation.

m. (sg. dat. mulākātas), meeting, a visit (El., Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to meet a person, to make a visit (Gr.M.) --karanāwun -- m.inf. to cause a person to be met, to introduce one person to another (Gr.M.).
m. original capital (invested in business), principal.
f. earnest money, part of the price paid in advance on the conclusion of a bargain.

or mūlay adv. even from the foundation or basis (cf. mūl 1) (Rām. 710, 952, 961); root and branch, absolutely (Gr.Gr. 22); ever, at all (El. mulai). -na, adv. never, not at all, not in the least (Rām. 1618, 1654).
adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, a country (Gr.M.).
m. kings; used in Rām. 70 as equivalent to mulᵃkh, q.v.

m. (sg. dat. mulkas), a kingdom, rule, state, country, territory, region, land (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 216; YZ. 236; Rām. 512, 822; H. i, 1). --tulun -- m.inf. to raise the country, to raise a great outcry against some unpopular action or conduct. ¶ mulk-ĕ-bēgāna ملکِ بیگانہ m. a foreign land (K.Pr. 146).

f. a collection of turnip-tops or similar green-stuff dried and stored for winter use, radish leaves (K.Pr. 146); cf. gŏgᵃji-mulᵃvĕñ, p. 279a, l. 17, and muji-mulⁱvĕñ, p. 558b, l. 3. ¶ mulⁱvĕñĕ-lū̃ṭh f. a scrap of rope of these dried leaves. (These dried leaves are twisted up into ropes for preservation.) -wö̃kh f. a rope made up of these dried leaves.

m. an affectionate kiss on the forehead or cheek (usually of a child); cf. miñ 1, mŏñ. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take a kiss, to kiss. --karun -- m.inf. to take a kiss on the mouth by force, to kiss, esp. an unwilling child or woman. ¶ muñĕ-pūtᵘ m. a kiss (given to a darling child). Cf. miñĕ-pūtᵘ, col. a, l. 43, and mŏñĕ-pūtᵘ, l. 5 ab.

or (Gr.Gr. 20) mūnᵘ̈ f. sheep's wool, wool (Gr.Gr. 146) (K.Pr. 159, 245). --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring wool; hence, met. to annoy another by refusing consent to something, in spite of his urging; cf. the next. --ösas anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause wool to grow in a person's mouth; hence, met. to annoy him by refusing consent to something which he is vehemently urging by word of mouth. --ösas yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. wool to come in the mouth, to be annoyed, as ab. --khārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to raise wool, i.q. --ösas anüñᵘ̈, ab. --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. wool to rise, to be annoyed, as ab. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. wool to come, i.e. to be annoyed, as ab. ¶ mūni wọ̆thᵘ adj. (f. --wö̆ʦhᵘ̈ --), (of a sheep) very woolly; that from which the wool has been removed, shorn.

f. (sg. dat. munki), a species of dried grapes or raisins, bloom-raisins. ¶ munka-caṭiñ f. a 'chutnee' or jam made from these raisins (used as a medicine). -shīra m. the expressed juice of these raisins soaked in water.
f. (sg. dat. munüñᵘ̈), the act of pounding (grain in a mortar), husking (grain in a mortar).
f. wages for pounding grain in a mortar, wages for husking.

adj. c.g. illuminated, enlightened; elucidated, explained, illustrated; clear, bright, brilliant. --karun -- m.inf. to make a person brilliant; i.e. to endow him completely with wealth, health, prosperity, and virtue. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. suddenly to become endowed, as ab.
m. Sphœranthus mollis (El.) (cf. gūrukᵘ mundī, p. 298b, l. 11).
m. one who has taken a vow of silence.
adj. c.g. a cloth of mixed cotton and wool; a kind of cotton cloth made to resemble woollen stuff with fine spots; (as adj.) woolly, covered with wool (of a sheep, etc.).
in munj rai (L. 334), see mŏnjĕ-ray, p. 575a, l. 38.

f. proclamation by beat of drum. --nērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. proclamation to issue, proclamation to be made (Rām. 92, 1001, 1069, 1679). --phirüñᵘ̈ -- or --phiravüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make proclamation, proclaim (Rām. 89, 679).
f. diminishing, waning, in ḍĕka- manörᵘ̈, p. 204b, l. 12, q.v.
m. a writer, scribe, secretary, amanuensis (Gr.M.).
adj. (f. munᵘ̈jᵘ̈), made of wool, woollen (El. monul) (Gr.Gr. 146); paṭṭū, or coarse woollen cloth (El.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. munᵘ, f. muñᵘ̈), to pound (grain in a mortar), to husk (in a mortar) (L. 461; K.Pr. 15, 147; Śiv. 1533). munᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. muñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of grain) husked (in a mortar).
mūnʦhᵃran, mūnʦhᵃrun, see mū̃ʦhurᵘ, mū̃ʦhᵃran, and mū̃ʦhᵃrun.
or muñĕrun, noted only in the phrases ṭaka muñᵉ̆rith and ṭaka muñĕrith, see p. 992a, ll. 11 ff. The verb apparently means 'to half-close the eyes', cf. muñᵘ̈.

m. (sg. abl. mōni), the inner plastered side of a room, etc., a plastered wall (Gr.Gr. 20) (K.Pr. 71, 82, 147). --hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. -hishᵘ̈), (motionless) like a wall, (of a person) motionless, taciturn. mōni ʦitra-kār m. the work of a picture on the wall; met. something done by no one knows who (e.g. something carefully deposited, and then being destroyed without anyone, so far as it is known, approaching it; in such a case it is said that one of the pictures on the wall must have got up and done it), mysterious damage.
m. the pupil of the eye, i.q. müñᵘ̈ 1.
f. the pupil of the eye (K. 394, 927, 1123).

f. the pupil of the eye (Rām. 90, 191, 243, 1174, 1367; K. 184). -pholᵘ m. the pupil of the eye (Rām. 1423); the image of in the pupil of the eye (El. manyaphul, manyiphul). ¶ mañĕ  f.pl. the two eyeballs. -pholᵘ m. the pupil of the eye. --phērañĕ -- f. pl. inf. the eyeballs to turn; met. affection or friendship to depart. -phyurᵘ m. turning of the eyeballs; met. departure of love or respect (for a person).
in the following:--müñᵘ̈-gôḍᵘ̈ m. (sg. dat. -göḍis), the flesh of the nape of the neck. -göḍᵘ̈ or -görᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -gājĕ), the nape of the neck.
in üḍᵘ̈-müñᵘ̈ (p. 13b, l. 26). The word is fem. of moñᵘ 2, q.v.
gratuitous, gratis; (in Kāshmīrī) easy, (a task) which costs nothing (Rām. 726). Cf. muft.
f. squeezing, shampooing, twisting, husking (grain), etc., used --˚ as in atha-mūr, p. 60a, l. 29; hĕlⁱ-mūr, p. 364b, l. 8 (Gr.Gr. 127, K. 890); ? sharpness, expertness (in K.Pr. 222).
f. a small branch, a spray, a twig; cf. mūrᵘ̈ 2. mura mura f. a condition of being crowded together.
m. a patron, protector, the guardian of an infant (Gr.M.).
m. will, intention, purpose (Gr.M. K.Pr. 100). Cf. nā-mᵒ.
f. (sg. dat. murüñᵘ̈), the act of husking (grain, etc.) by rubbing between the hands or under the heel. Cf. mūran.

f. (sg. dat. mūrüñᵘ̈), the act of shelling (paddy, peas, etc.) between the hands, etc. (cf. hĕlⁱ-mūran) (p. 364b, l. 8) (Gr.Gr. 121); friction of, or rubbing, the skin gently with the tips of the fingers (e.g. to allay itchiness); twisting between the fingers, squeezing, etc. (cf. atha-mūran, p. 66a, l. 38, and mŏchĕ-mūran, s.v. mö̆ṭhᵘ̈) (K.Pr. 146). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to tickle with the tips of the fingers; to twist thread between the tips of the fingers (so as to stiffen it).
m. N. of a demon slain by Kṛṣṇa (Krishna). His proper name was Mura, and he was an Asura by tribe. Hence, his name in Sanskrit was Murâsura (K. 758 ff.).

m. (sg. dat. muratas), a moment, an instant, any short period of time; a moment (auspicious or otherwise) for any solemn or important occasion. --raṭun -- m. to seize the moment, to begin a work at the fixed auspicious moment, or at the time fixed by holy books.

f. (sg. dat. murüʦᵘ̈ or murʦᵘ̈), an image, an idol (El. murits); a statue, a picture, a portrait, an image (Gr.M.; K. 803, 878); figure, form. murʦᵘ̈-gar m. a picture-maker, a portrait-painter, an artist (of pictures), a sculptor (El. muritsgar). -garī f. the profession of a portrait-painter, picture-making.

f. manhood, virility, fortitude (cf. bē-murawath, K.Pr. 30); humanity, generosity, benevolence, kindness; urbanity, affability, politeness. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to practise kindness or civility (towards), show kindness (to), deal kindly (with).
f., i.q. mūr, q.v. Cf. hĕlⁱ-mūray, p. 364b, l. 8.
f. pl. (also murmurⁱ, f. sg.), a certain dish made of rice first slightly boiled and then parched.

m. a candidate for admission into a Musalmān religious order, during his state of probation; a disciple, a proselyte, a scholar, a follower, a pupil (L. 288, 460; K.Pr. 212, 222); a devotee, a hermit.

m. (sg. dat. murkhas), a fool, an ignorant fool, a blockhead (Śiv. 1215). ¶ murkha-bŏd f. (sg. dat. -bö̆zᵘ̈), fool's-wit, stupidity, silliness, simplicity (Śiv. 352, 881, 1791). -bö̆zᵘ̈gaʦhun m.inf. to follow a fool's advice. -cŏbur m. a young fool (esp. one born of intelligent parents). -mọ̆nḍᵘ m. 'a block of a fool', a blockhead, an utter fool.
f. the conduct or actions of a fool; conduct like that of a fool, incompetence, ineptitude.
adj. c.g. permitted (to leave), allowed (to depart). --karun -- m.inf. to dismiss (an assembly) (H. viii, 11).
f. a low vile woman (in conduct, appearance, or occupation); the wife of such a man.
m. the enemy of the demon Mura, who was slain by Kṛṣṇa (Krishna); a N. of Krishna (Śiv. 720, Rām. 3).
f. in ḍūnⁱ-murra, p. 224a, l. 18, q.v.
m. (sg. dat. murtas), a man, a person, homo (used in counting, as in zᵃh murth, two men; ʦōr murth, four men; and so on).
adj. (f. murtimö̃ʦᵘ̈), having a material or bodily form, endowed with a corporeal frame; corporeal, incarnate; porsonified.
(?) m. a rice crop followed by pulses or buck- wheat (L. 336); cf. beth-muru, p. 139b, l. 42.

or mūḍun conj. 1 (1 p.p. mūrᵘ), to shell or husk (grain, pulse, etc.) by rubbing between the hands, etc. (Gr.Gr. 19, 121, 127); to rub the skin (e.g. of the palm of the hand) gently with the tips of the fingers (to allay itchiness, etc.); to crush with the teeth, or eat, parched pease, etc.; to twist thread between the tips of the fingers (so as to stiffen it); to twist the hand, as in atha mūrith nyunᵘ, to twist the hand and take, to wrench out of the hand (Gr.M.); atha mūrun, to wring the hands (in sorrow, etc.) (Rām. 724); kŏchĕ mūrun, (of a suckling child) to rub the bosom, to snuggle in the bosom, to be at rest in the bosom (L.V. 70). mūrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mūrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), husked, rubbed, eaten, etc., as ab.
adj. (f. mūrᵘ̈ 1), husked (of grain), used --˚, as in aḍ-mūrᵘ, p. 11b, l. 22.

f., i.q. murᵘ 1, q.v., used in the following:-- murᵘ̈ barüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to put alms into the front skirt of a garment (cf. murᵘ wahārun, s.v. murᵘ 1). When any respected old man died in poverty it was formerly the custom for one of his children (esp. his youngest daughter-in-law) to hold out her skirt in this way, into which the relations of the deceased put contributions towards the funeral expenses, etc. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the front of a garment to go, i.e. to be worn out or torn. --yiñᵘ̈-- f.inf. loss to occur (as the result of some work involving great labour, and from which profit was expected, but which has received an unexpected check). ¶ muri bĕhun m.inf. to sit on (another's) front skirt, to sit close to a person (to see that he does his work properly). --bihith dörᵘ̈ khǖnzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to sit close to a person and pluck his beard, i.e. under pretence of displaying affection to abuse a person by using gentle language.
f. the fine core, nucleus, or pith of a fruit, grain, or wood.

m. the front part of a man's or woman's long coat (the lower part of which hangs down, and can be lifted up like an apron to receive anything); a sleeve (El. múr), the width of sleeve or trousers at wrist or ankle (Gr.Gr. 19); see murᵘ̈. --dārun -- m.inf. to hold up the front skirt of a coat (to receive, e.g. grain); met. to beg for alms, to ask for something (Rām. 1486). --wahārun -- m.inf. to spread out the skirt; esp. to hold out the skirts (as ab.) for alms, but without asking for anything. This, in former times, was a custom in Kashmīr when some respected old man died in poverty. His children used then to collect contributions in this way to provide funds for the necessary funeral rites, etc. Cf. murᵘ̈ barüñᵘ̈, s.v. murᵘ̈, bel. ¶ murⁱ-düjⁱ f. a patch sewn on to the front of such a coat. -mã̄gay f. very humble petitioning (indicated by holding the front skirt as ab.) (K.Pr. 174). -palav m. the front of a coat, as ab. -ʦoṭᵘ  adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ), (a coat) of which the front has been torn.
m. a jingling repetition of shurᵘ, a child, as in shurⁱ-murⁱ, children, etc., i.e. a man's family, his household (Gr.M., K. 786).

f. (pl. nom. mūrĕ, not mōrĕ, Gr.Gr. 62), a small branch, a spray, a withe, a twig (i.q. mur, q.v.) (cf. atha-mūrᵘ̈, p. 60a, l. 31; dönᵘ̈-mūrᵘ̈, p. 223b, l. 9; dö̃tan-mūrᵘ̈, p. 258b, l. 35) (Gr.Gr. 20, 62; Rām. 1121. 1190, 1250; K. 91). mūrĕn māz tulun m.inf. to raise the flesh with twigs, to flog a man with twigs on the bare flesh.
f. a charge of an offence brought by the guilty person against an innocent person. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring such a charge.
f. (sg. dat. mōrĕ), a drain, gutter, sewer.
or mūsā موسیٰ m. Moses (K.Pr. 85 (sg. dat. musi); H. iv, 5); sang-ĕ-mūsā, N. of a close- grained black stone used for ornaments (L. 65).
m. aid, assistance (L. 409, 432, 450). tukhm musāda, an advance of seed-grain made by Government to cultivators (L. 407, 409, 432, 450).
m. a pestle; a club, mace (Śiv. 13, 1160). musala-dar m. one who carries a pestle (as a club) (Śiv. 1160).
m. a place of prayer, an oratory, a mosque; (amongst Musalmāns) a carpet or mat on which to say prayers. Cf. masal and musla.
f. (sg. dat. musarüñᵘ̈), (of a knot) the act of undoing (i.e. either becoming untied of itself, or being deliberately untied by someone). Cf. muʦaran.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. musarôwᵘ), i.q. musarun, q.v. musarôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. musarövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. musorᵘ-motᵘ, q.v., s.v. musarun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. musorᵘ), to loosen, untie, undo (a knot, bonds, a bolt, or the like); to open (a shut box). Cf. muʦarun. ¶ musarana yunᵘ m.inf. pass. to become unloosed (of a knot, bonds, a bolt, or the like); to become opened (of a closed box); to become revealed (of secret thoughts); to become published (of something of which the publication was prevented or prohibited). ¶ musorᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. musürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), unloosened, opened, etc., as ab.

? f. stealing, robbery, theft, only noted in the following:--mush dith khyonᵘ m.inf. swindling, cheating in every way (in business). --dith mŏkulᵘ -- adj. (f. --dith mŏküjᵘ̈ --), utterly solitary, entirely alone, with no second, unique.

adj. c.g. ascertained, defined, certain, fixed (El. mushakhas). --karun -- m.inf. to come to a decision after much discussion, to confirm, establish, ratify, determine; to select and appoint a person out of many candidates. --pöṭhⁱ -- or --pöṭhin -- adv. certainly, necessarily.
adj. c.g. difficult, hard (Gr.M.; W. 149; K.Pr. 114; Śiv. 1191; Rām. 324, 383, 827, 885), i.q. mushkyulᵘ, q.v.
adj. (f. mushkijᵘ̈), difficult, hard (Gr.M.; Rām. 98, 464, 824); painful; dubious, doubtful, obscure; (as subst.) mushkilĕn- manz, in difficulties (Gr.M.). Cf. mushkil.
adj. c.g. longing, yearning, enamoured (of), entranced (with, dat.) (H. iii, 1, 7-9).
m. (sg. dat. mushṭikas), N. of a demon in the employ of Kamsa, the enemy of Kṛṣṇa (in Skt., Muṣṭika) (K. 368, 440).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mushᵘ; 2 p.p. mushyōv or mushōv, Gr.Gr. lx), to steal.

m. (f. mushᵉ̆röñᵉ̆), a demon, a devil; met. an ugly, terrible-looking, wicked man. -dĕv m. (f. -dĕviñ), a fierce-looking devil, i.q. mushᵉ̆rān. -koṭᵘ m. (f. -küṭᵘ̈, dat. -kacĕ), a son (or daughter) of a devil, a fierce, wicked boy (or girl). -mọ̆nḍᵘ m. a huge evil spirit, or devil, who immovably, like a tree-trunk or pillar, infests some particular place. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. a demon to fall (upon a person), to become possessed by a devil (involving madness, epilepsy, etc.).

f. (sg. dat. mushti), a fist (Gr.M.); a blow with the clenched fist (K. 254, 432, 440, 441); a handful, a fistful. --hāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show the fist (with the thumb extended) (an action signifying desire for sexual intercourse, and hence used vulgarly to indicate defiance, derision, or 'don't you wish you may get it?') (K.Pr. 14). --lāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to smite (with) the clenched fist (Gr.M., Rām. 920). --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf., id.; met. to swindle in buying or selling, etc. ¶ mushta-har f. a fight, or riot, in which the weapons are clenched fists. -mushᵉ̆th f. a mutual fight with clenched fists, a boxing match.
m. (f.mǖ̃shⁱ or mū̃sh, etc., q.v.), a bull buffalo (Rām. 472).

or mū̃sh or mũ̄̈sh or maīsh f. (f. of mū̃shᵘ, q.v.; sg. dat. maĩshi or mö̃shi, Gr.Gr. 67), a buffalo-cow, a milch buffalo (El. mãnsh; Gr.Gr. 132; L. 360, mesh). ¶ maīshĕ- (or mö̃shĕ-) dŏd  m. buffalo-milk. -dāla m. buffalo-hide. -guhᵘ m. buffalo-dung (K.Pr. 251). -gurᵘ m. 'a buffalo-horse', a fierce-looking, brawny, long-limbed fellow (esp. a fool). -krörᵘ̈ f. a kind of cake made of dried buffalo-milk. -koṭᵘ m. a young buffalo (usually fierce) (El. mánsha-kauṭ) (Gr.Gr. 132). -mandul m. a 'buffalo-rump'; met. a brawny, lazy fellow. -rôchᵘ m. a buffalo-herdsman.
m. (sg. dat. musībatas), adversity, misfortune, disaster (W. 137; K.Pr. 77, 87).

m. (amongst Musalmāns) a mat or carpet on which to say prayers, a small skin used for this purpose (El.); a skin (of any animal), a skin mat, a hide (K.Pr. 213; Śiv. 529, 816, 894; H. xii, 18, 21, 22).
m. a tenant, a farmer or farm-holder, a contractor (L. 405, 408, 450).
m. (sg. dat. mustakas), a species of Chenopodium. (In Hindī this word signifies Cyperus rotundus, a species of fragrant grass; cf. mōsta.)

conj. 1 (1 p.p. musᵘ 3; for 1, see mọ̆sᵘ; for 2, see s.v.); 2 p.p. musyōv or musōv; cf. Gr.Gr. 208, 225), to eat clumsily (instead of putting gobbets neatly into the mouth with the hand, 'chucking' it carelessly into the mouth from a distance), to eat greedily and indecently.
adj. (f.musᵘ̈ṭᵘ̈), loose, not tied up (of straw, firewood, etc., usually tied up in bundles).
musawwada مسودہ, a rough draft, a first sketch (with blottings and corrections), the original draft (of a letter or the like) (Gr.M.).

(for 1, see mọ̆sᵘ; for 3, see musun) m. weariness, fatigue, exhaustion (from overwork, etc., or sorrow, etc.) (Gr.Gr. 17). --aʦun -- m.inf. such fatigue or exhaustion to enter (i.e. to be felt or experienced). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to put away the feeling of such fatigue or exhaustion (e.g. by resting, or by the receipt of happy news, etc.). --nērun -- m.inf. such fatigue or exhaustion to depart (as ab.).
m. a respectable person, a trustworthy person; (in Kashmīr) one of the hangers-on at a Government office, to whom the head delegates his duties (L. 420).
f. inertness, laziness; a long wrinkle or crease in cloth, paper, etc.
(for 1 and 2, see mö̃thᵃr 1 and 2) or mǖnthᵃr f. the name for the non-initial letter i. Cf. ār-mṻnthᵃr (p. 43b, l. 45).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -dārĕñ), (of cloth, paper, etc.) creased, wrinkled.

m. a kind of vetch or pulse, Phaseolus aconitifolius, the mōṭh of India proper (Gr.Gr. mōṭh, 23; L. 330, 363, mothi; K.Pr. 119, 189; Rām. 1504). ¶ muṭhⁱ-buzay f. a conflagration reducing to ashes in a moment; cf. buzun. -dāl m. a pottage of this pulse. -koshᵘ m. the shell of this pulse. -mās f. a woman who shows pretended affection (quasi, saying, 'I am your aunt'; cf. mās 3. Such is here looked upon as worth merely a single grain of this pulse). -mǖ̃thᵃr f. an old custom in Kashmīr schools, in which, when a boy begins to learn to write, this and other pulses, parched, are distributed amongst all the pupils of the school; cf. kara-mǖ̃thᵃr (p. 466a, l. 2). -pholᵘ m. a single grain of this pulse (looked upon as representing no value). -phȧlⁱ-yārⁱz f. friendship (worth only) a single grain of this pulse; temporary and hypocritical friendship.
adj. (f. mū̃ṭhᵘ̈), dull, stupid, muddle-headed, lazy (Gr.Gr. 140); cf. mö̃ṭh. mū̃ṭhⁱ-trọ̆pⁱ m. a kind of sewing, in which two edges of cloth are joined together.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. mū̃trôwᵘ), to subject to a charm, to conjure, exorcise (Gr.Gr. lxi); to consecrate, dedicate, devote. mū̃trôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. mū̃trövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), charmed, exorcised, conjured, subjected to a charm; consecrated, dedicated, devoted.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. mū̃tryōv), to be subjected to a charm or spell (Gr.Gr. 61); according to some authorities, conj. 1 (1 p.p. mū̃trᵘ), to subject to a spell (Gr.Gr. 61).
m. an invitation to a Brāhmaṇ to a religious ceremony or the like.

f. (sg. dat. macĕ), a large earthenware vessel, about three feet in height, for containing such articles as grain, charcoal, or beverages (El. maṭi) (El.; K.Pr. 42, 219, 220; Śiv. 1874). ¶ macĕ-katurᵘ m. a broken piece, or sherd, of such a granary. -wörᵘ̈ f. a small jar, two or three inches high, shaped like this granary.
or muwöfik موآفق adj. c.g. conformable, concordant (Gr.M.); favourable, propitious (Gr.M., of wind; Śiv. 726).

in muza-wara m. a dish of the water in which rice and mŏng (q.v.) have boiled, mixed with condiments. It is given to invalids (El. says that it is made of rice and poppy water). Cf. mŏnga-muza- war, p. 378b, l. 8.
m. moment, importance, consequence (Gr.M.). kē̃h muzāyĕka chuna, it is of no consequence (Gr.M.).
postpos. governing abl., on account of, according to; wanana mūzūba, according to instructions (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. existing, extant, ready, at hand, available; present, manifest, undeniable (Rām. 129).
f. the cloth put over the face of the corpse of a Brāhmaṇ.
(written مزلامہ in the Persian character) in Rām. 649, where the comm. translates it 'sins' (pāpāni).
f. alienation, estrangement, hostility between friends.

f. (sg. dat. muʦarüñᵘ̈), loosening, untying, opening (a knot, bonds, a box, door, etc.) (Gr.Gr. 121); explanation of a difficult statement, unravelling a complicated state of affairs; becoming loosened, etc., as ab. Cf. musaran.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. muʦarôwᵘ), i.q. muʦarun, q.v., Gr.M. [L. 462; YZ. 106 (untied), 165 (swept the hair off her face); Śiv. 26, 66, 207, 247, 990, 1399, 1646, 1702, 1725, 1747; Rām. 274 (tore off their garments), 523 (opened their eyes), 1135, 1466, 1618 (open a door), 1772 (opening the heart)]. muʦarôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. muʦaövᵘ̈ -müʦᵘ̈), i.q. muʦorᵘ-motᵘ, q.v., s.v. muʦarun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. muʦorᵘ), to loosen, untie, undo (a knot, bolt, bonds, and so on), to cause to open or be opened (Gr.Gr. 121; Gr.M.; YZ. 458; Śiv. 396, 520, 949, 1078, 1469, 1763, 1890; Rām. 141, 624, 842, 1344; K. 90, 160) (rag muʦarüñᵘ̈, to open a vein, bleed (a person)); to unravel or explain a difficult or complicated statement or state of affairs, to disclose. ¶ ȧchⁱ (or achĕ) muʦarañĕ, to open the eyes (Śiv. 168; Rām. 125; H. xii, 22); bar muʦarun, to open a door (Rām. 1569, 1637, 1639; K. 69, 73; H. viii, 3, 10; xii, 23); jigar muᵒ, to open the liver, to open out one's heart and display bitter sorrow, divulge a secret, or the like (Rām. 263, 269; cf. sīna muᵒ, Rām. 1235; H. vii, 21); lōl muʦarana yunᵘ, love to be released, love to burst forth (K. 681, 857). Cf. musarun and muʦarāwun. ¶ muʦorᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. muʦürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), opened, etc., as ab. ¶ muʦaran-war m. ravelling a string, untwisting a twisted string; met. causeless anger. ¶ muʦarana yunᵘ m.inf. pass. to become untied, opened, etc.; to disclose some long-kept secret about oneself.
f. profit (in selling, etc.), utility, gain (mutsáí, El.). Cf. muʦᵘ.
adj. (f. mū̃ʦhᵘ̈rᵘ̈), dilatory, lazy, slow in action.
f. (sg. dat. mū̃ʦhᵃrüñᵃ), dilatoriness, laggardness, dawdling.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mū̃ʦhᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. mū̃ʦhᵃrun, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. mū̃ʦhᵒrᵒ), to wait, be dilatory, be laggard, to drawl.

m. N. of an ancient king (in Skt. Mucukunda). He assisted the gods in their wars with the demons. As a reward, he was given the boon of long and unbroken sleep. The gods also decreed that whosoever dared to interrupt his sleep should be burnt to ashes (Śiv. 1478; K. 598, 601 ff.).
m. profit (on a contract); as adj. (f. muʦᵘ̈), useful (El.). Cf. muʦay.
f. a piece of wood for joining together a number of boards or posts, by being nailed to each. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to nail a joining piece, as ab. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf., id.
in myā̃-pūtᵘ m. the young of a sheep or goat, a lamb, a kid, a young ram (Gr.Gr. 131).
m. the time, or place, of a promise; a fixed time, period (in interest, money-lending, etc.), the course (of a bill of exchange) (Gr.M.).

(cf. معدہ) m. the stomach, belly. --ḍalun -- m.inf. the stomach to be distraught, indigestion to occur, a pain to be felt in the stomach. --dorᵘ -- adj. (f. -dürᵘ̈), strong-bellied, one who has a good digestion; stout-hearted, courageous. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to put another's aim or desires to the test; cf. --wuchun, bel. -pachĕr m. stoutness of belly, a very strong power of digestion, a good digestion. --paṭhun -- m.inf. strength of digestion to be achieved. --wuchun -- m.inf. 'to watch the belly', to test another's intentions; cf. --hyonᵘ, ab.
m. the showing of affection under all circumstances (e.g. to a child, whether it is well behaved or naughty, in order to encourage it in the way it should go).
m. the condition of being mine; hence, the condition of one who says 'thou art mine', an expression exhibiting extreme affection.
m. the mew of a cat (Gr.Gr. 25; K.Pr. 168, myou). Cf. mĕ˜v.

m. (sg. dat. mĕnḍis, K.Pr. 78), the amount of food taken into the mouth at one time, a gobbet (taken up between the fingers and thrust into the mouth with the thumb) (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 33, 73, 78, 82; K. 205-7, 213, 1101). -ṭyonḍᵘ m. a collection of moderate sized gobbets (a jingling compound) (Gr.Gr. 95).

m. (sg. dat. mĕndis), leprosy (W. 111, mio˙nd). --kāsun -- m.inf. to remove, cleanse, or cure leprosy; met. to remove some long-standing impediment, defect, or the like. --thawun -- m.inf. to impose leprosy; hence, met. to do some irretrievable (or removable only with great difficulty) harm to a person (e.g. to impute a fault, to blast his character, put some terrible impediment in his way, etc.). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. leprosy to fall, i.e. to attack a person. --wasun -- m.inf., id. ¶ mĕndⁱ-thras f. 'a mat of leprosy', the disease of leprosy covering the whole body (an expression used in imprecations, wishing evil to another, or the like).
adj. (f. më̆nzᵘ̈), leprous, afflicted with leprosy; met. wasted away by prolonged ill-health or disease, infirm, withered.

possessive pron. (f. myöñᵘ̈), my, mine. The word is used as the gen. sg. of the personal pron. bŏh, I, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 12, 56, 63, 87; K.Pr. 57; Śiv. 18, 42, 45, 1204, 1437, 1649, etc.; Rām. 217, 247, 301, 334, 338, 656, 684, 721, 1040, 1229, 1586, 1590, etc.; K. 17, 105, 122, 137, 321, 369, etc.; H. i, 10; vii, 27, 28, etc.); used idiomatically to mean 'my house', 'my home'. myāni bāni m. of, or belonging to, my share (lit. 'in my dish').

m. union, uniting, intimate relationship, identity with (K.Pr. 101; Śiv. 652, 1009, 1429); reconciliation (El., Gr.Gr. 14); acceptance of the fact of intimate union (L.V. 7); cf. ȧchⁱ- myulᵘ, p. 8a, l. 44; atha-mᵒ, p. 60a, l. 49; man- mᵒ, p. 572a, l. 10; māz-mᵒ, p. 614b, l. 44, and myūlᵘ 2. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. thorough union, or fitting together, to occur (Śiv. 55, K. 437). --karith dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to bring together, join together, cause to meet, unite (Rām. 1589).
m., i.q. myulᵘ, q.v., meeting, union (YZ. 346); union, identity (L.V. 36).

m. a kiss, kissing (cf. guli- myūṭhᵘ, p. 284a, l. 27) (K.Pr. 81, YZ. 108). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give a kiss, to kiss (esp. on the forehead) (Rām. 287, 1430). --karun -- m.inf. to kiss (El., Rām. 1093). ¶ mīṭhⁱ dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to give kisses, to kiss (Śiv. 730, 976, 1150, 1398, 1528, 1911; Rām. 588, 1553, 1644). --karȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf., id. (K. 174, 285, 398, 461, 475, 857).

adj. (sg. dat. mīṭhis, abl. mēṭhi; f. mīṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat. mēchĕ), sweet (lit. and fig.) (Gr.Gr. 19; Gr.M.; W. 20, miot; K.Pr. 5, 106, 143, 148, 159, 208; Rām. 1489); pleasant, agreeable, delicious (Gr.M.; Rām. 1751; K. 309, 401, 932, 1131; H. vi, 11); elegant, charming. mīṭhᵘ̈bēra f. a sweet hedge, a sweet tract; hence, met. an object of great affection.
or miñĕ-mürᵘ̈ f. a female deer, a doe, a hind (H. ii, 8, 9).

m. (sg. dat. mᵃtras), urine, piss (El. muthar) (K.Pr. 128, 144, 186, 235; K. 586). --karun -- m.inf. to make water (El.). ¶ mᵃtra-bĕmörᵃ f. a disease marked by copious discharge of urine, diabetes or the like. -gö̆ʦᵘ̈ f. the bladder (El. mútaragúʦ). -mȧchⁱ f. a urine-fly, a kind of fly that haunts places where urine collects (when it settles on the human body it is very difficult to drive away); hence, -mȧchⁱ-hyuhⁱ adj. (f. -mȧchⁱ-hishⁱ), one who is like a urine-fly, one who persistently attaches him- or herself to another and cannot be got rid of, an 'Old Man of the Sea'. -motᵘ adj. (f. -müʦᵘ̈), a urine-maniac, one who (either by nature or owing to diseases) passes great quantities of urine. -nôrᵘ m. the urethra; meton. the penis or vulva. -phyorᵘ or -phyūrᵘ m. a drop of urine; a very small quantity of urine passed at one urination. -ʦᵃran f. (sg. dat. -ʦᵃrüñᵃ), the urethra; meton. the penis or vulva. -ʦŏ̈ṭᵘ̈ diñᵘ̈ f.inf. to give a urine-cake (such a cake, when prepared according to certain magical rites, is said to make the person who eats it subservient to the person of whose urine the cake is made); met. to make a person completely subservient to oneself. -ʦŏ̈ṭᵘ̈ lagüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to become completely subservient, as ab.
f. the condition of being fouled with urine. Cf. mala-mᵒ, p. 564b, l. 17.

The twelfth (or, if we count the aspirates ch and kh as separate letters, the fourteenth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is the twentieth (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the twenty-third) consonant in the Śāradā or in the Nāgarī alphabet, and the thirty-second consonant in the Perso-Arabic alphabet as adapted to Kāshmīrī. In schools it is called nastuv-nö. It also, in the case of words directly borrowed from Sanskrit, represents the Sanskrit cerebral nasal ṇ, the sound of which does not occur in Kāshmīrī, although Paṇḍits often write the character when it occurs in the original. Thus, the Sanskrit word guṇa becomes gŏn in Kāshmīrī, but Paṇḍits commonly write it or. It is pronounced nearly as in English, the sound varying slightly according to the letter which follows it. When, however, it precedes certain palatal letters, it tends to become palatalized. Before ü-mātrā and ĕ (i.e. ya) it becomes ñ, as in yīran, an anvil, pl.nom. yīrüñᵘ̈; from tonᵘ, thin, we have tañĕr, thinness; and from the verb ranun (first conjugation), to cook, we have a first past participle ronᵘ, with a feminine rüñᵘ̈. When followed by y with any other vowel except a (in which case ya becomes ĕ), it also becomes ñ, but the y disappears. Thus, the second past participle of ranun is ran + yōv +, and becomes rañōv. But these changes do not occur in the conjugation of verbs of the third conjugation. Thus, the second past participle of the verb banun (third conjugation), to become, is banyōv, not bañōv. See Gr.Gr. 28, 29, 226; Gr.M., p. 22.

. The thirteenth (or, if we count the aspirates ch and kh as separate letters, the fifteenth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is the tenth consonant in the Śāradā or in the Nāgarī alphabet, and has no special place in the Perso-Arabic alphabet, in which it is usually represented by نِ, as in وُنِ for wuñ; سپنِ for sapüñᵘ̈; and انِک for üñᵘ̈kh. ¶ This letter is of frequent occurrence in Kāshmīrī, and its sound, differing from that of an English or Sanskrit ny, is that of the ñ in the Spanish word campaña, or of that of the gn in the French campagne, being represented in the International alphabet by ɲ. ¶ In schools this letter is named khŏna phuṭⁱ ñĕ. Kāshmīrī Paṇḍits distinguish it from the Sanskrit ñ, and mark it with a subscribed dot  to show that it is what they call aprasiddha, i.e. not used in Sanskrit. As, however, the Sanskrit letter never occurs except in conjunction with other palatal consonants, and as, in Kāshmīrī, is principally used by itself, and not in conjunction with other consonants, there is no danger of the two being confused, and in this Dictionary the dot is omitted, as in wuñ, written, not. Although thus considered aprasiddha ñ is not (except in words borrowed directly from Sanskrit) the nasal corresponding to the other aprasiddha consonants ʦ, ʦh, and z. With these, n, not ñ, is used, as in nʦa, nʦha, and nza. So, in Śiv. 1489, we have the Kāshmīrī word pönʦh, five, and also the borrowed Sanskrit word pañʦa. ¶ This letter seldom begins a word in Kāshmīrī, and in the few cases in which it occurs as an initial, it shows a tendency to assume the sound of ny, so that in nearly every case a word so beginning may be written with either ñ or ny, although the two characters have quite different pronunciations. Thus, the word ñoñᵘ is sometimes written and sometimes. ¶ This letter is, in the first place, the regular Tadbhava representative of a Sanskrit ny. Thus, Skt. dhānyam becomes the Kāshmīrī dāñĕ; Skt. puṇyam, Ksh. pŏñĕ; Skt. kanyakā, Ksh. kañĕkh; and Skt. pānīyam (through *pāniyam, *pānyam), Ksh. pôñᵘ. The letter is also found as the representative of a dental n followed by ü-mātrā, ĕ, or y, for examples of which see art. n. ¶ As in the case of y and sh, the inherent vowel of ñ is ĕ, not a, so that must be transliterated ñĕ, not ña. When followed by ü-mātrā, as in ñᵘ̈, Paṇḍits commonly omit the ü-mātrā, which they look upon as inherent in the closed consonant, and write merely. This, however, leads to confusion, as there would then be no distinction between, e.g. karawañ, the wages for doing, and karavüñᵘ̈, she who does, if both are written, as is frequently done. It is therefore better to write each word fully, as in and, and this course is followed in the present Dictionary.

adv. particle of negation, equivalent to 'not', 'no', 'neither', 'nor'. In a direct sentence it is usually suffixed to the verb, as in gaʦhi-na, he will not go; pokᵘ-na, he did not proceed; gayōv, he went, gayō-na, he did not go; chuh, he is, chuna, he is not (p. 159a, l. 14) (Gr.Gr. 177, 255; W. 96, 151; L.V. 35, 98, 104, etc.; Śiv. 5, 35, 45, etc.; Rām. 74, 77, 104, etc.; H. i, 6; ii, 1, 4, 8, 9, 11, etc.; and so elsewhere passim). When two verbs are both negatived, the na is prefixed, not suffixed, to each, as in na gaʦhi na diyi, he will neither go nor give. ¶ This word is not used with the simple or the polite imperative (see ma), but is used as a prohibitive with the future imperative, as in dȧpⁱzĕm-na, you must not speak to me (H. v, 8); kȧrⁱzi-na, you must not make (H. viii, 1; xii, 6); wȧsⁱzi-na, you must not descend (H. xii, 11); mȧngⁱzĕs-na, you must not demand from her (H. xii, 18). ¶ In a subordinate sentence, na precedes the verb, as in tȧmⁱ ʦȧṭⁱ par, yuthᵘ na wuḍith gaʦhi, he cut the feathers, so that it should fly away (Gr.M.). ¶ When employed to negative a verbal adjective or noun, na precedes the word it negatives, as in na-bananī, impossible; but, if the sentence, not the word is negatived, na, as usual, is suffixed to the verb, as in chu-na bananī, it is not possible. ¶ With an indefinite pronoun, it usually precedes the pronoun, as in na kū̃h, no one (p. 389b, l. 38); na kĕ˜h, nothing (id., l. 40). Cf., however, kĕh-na, nothing (p. 389b, l. 45; p. 390a, l. 18); kuni-na, nowhere (p. 453b, l. 26). ¶ Similarly, it often precedes an interjection, as in na-bā, no, Sir! (is) not, Sir! (Gr.Gr. 102); na-dĕd, no, Madam! (used in addressing a mother or elderly female) (W. 96); na-sa, no, Sir! (Śiv. 1247). ¶ Used alone as interj. indicating negation, no! (K.Pr. 18). ¶ Between two words a single na is often equivalent to 'neither... nor', as in ōr na yōr, neither there nor here (p. 41b, l. 16), and in such cases sometimes has a special idiomatic force, as in dāsh na dāsh, a person's entire property (apparently, what is lasting and what is not lasting) (p. 252b, l. 39); höhⁱ na pröhⁱ, (occurring) suddenly over and over again (p. 325a, l. 18); pĕv na pĕv, while in the act of falling (K.Pr. 175); cf. zĕn nā zĕn, bel. Or na may be repeated, as in na... na (or ta na), neither... nor (K.Pr. 46). So, na... ta..., neither... nor. na... na... ta, nor... nor... nor (L.V. 15). na danan ta mĕtran adv. neither for one's own profit nor for another's (e.g. expenditure, loss, etc.). na dazüñᵘ̈ ta wuʦüñᵘ̈ f. neither being burnt nor being consumed by fire, the being unaffected by. one's own, or another's, prosperity or adversity, stoicism. ¶ na-ta 1 adv. and not, nor (L.V. 37, 96, 97; Śiv. 1540; YZ. 7; K.Pr. 135). na-ta 2 adv. not then, i.e. (if) not then, or else, otherwise, or (El.; W. 99; L.V. 19, 71; K.Pr. 150; Śiv. 171, 311, 593, etc.; Rām. 268, 1342, 1588; K. 559, 571, 1146, etc.; YZ. 83, 105, 119, 180); aki na-ta aki laṭi, at one time or another (Śiv. 1564). na-ta 3 adv. not verily, forsooth not (Rām. 63). na-tay, i.q. na-ta 2, ab. or else, otherwise (tay = ta + ay 2) (Śiv. 682; Rām. 103, 325, 401, etc.). na-zi, an emph. equivalent for na, as in na-zi pazi, it is not at all proper (K. 34; so K. 82, 453). ¶ nā 1, i.q. na, ab. (L.V. 2, 9, etc.). nā... nā, neither... nor (L.V. 7). zĕn nā zĕn, they are being born, (and) they are not being born, immediately on being born, while they are yet being born (L.V. 47); cf. pĕv na pĕv, ab. nā 2 (= na + a 3 or ā 1) adv. a negative interrogative suffix added to verbs, as in karān chunā (chuh + na + ā 1), does he not make? karyōn-nā, did he not make? karān chĕkh-nā (na + a 3), does not thou (fem.) make? cf. a 3 (Gr.Gr. 180; L.V. 83; Śiv. 871, 882, 1096, etc.; Rām. 145, 152, 154, 329, 540, 1051, etc.; H. vi, 1; viii, 7; ix, 7, etc.; K. 369).
