As a negative interrogative, this word often has the force of an emphatic affirmative, like the English 'is it not good?' meaning 'it is very good' (Śiv. 573 ff., 651, 793, 838, 1134, etc.; Rām. 188, 193, 668, 757, 759; K. 101, 126, 1171). ¶ nau or nō adv. no certainly (in addressing a man. In addressing a woman, nāy, bel., is used) (W. 96; Rām. 216, 218, 293-4, etc.; H. vii, 23; xi, 15; K.Pr. 135). ¶ nu... nu..., neither... nor (H. xii, 4). ¶ nay 1 (= na + ay 1) adv. a negative interrogative suffix, i.q. nā 2, but used when addressing a woman, as in karān chĕkh-nay, dost thou (fem.) not make? cf. a 3, esp. p. 2a, l. 40 (Gr.Gr. 180). nay 2 (= na + ay 2) conj., a suffix indicating a negative supposition. If not, unless. It may be appended to a verb, as in karihē-nay, if he had not made, but is more usually attached to the subject of the sentence, as in rūd-nay pĕyihē, if rain had not fallen; sunay (= suh + nay) karihē, if he had not made; cf. ay 2 (El. nai; Gr.Gr. 257; Śiv. 168, 634, 1236, etc.; Rām. 165, 338, 496, etc.; K. 1107, 1123; K.Pr. 46, 100). nay 3 (for 4, 5, see s.vv.) (= na + emph. y) not verily, not at all (Śiv. 46, 327, 348, 579, etc.; H. v, 5; ix, 6, 8, 10, 12, etc.; YZ. 23). ¶ nāy adv. negative particle, used like na when addressing a woman with respect, but emphatically. Not, certainly, certainly not (W. 96, nāi). Fem. of nau, ab.

m. the sky, the atmosphere, heaven; firmament (L. 464; Śiv. 1076, 1879; Rām. 458, 504, 678, 888, 1032, 1333, 1550). nab (or nȧbⁱ) logᵘ-motᵘ  perf. part. (f. --lüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), attached to the sky, one who is up in the sky; hence, met. become full of haughtiness. --lagun -- m.inf. to reach to the sky; met. to be filled with pride, to become haughty, to have a feeling of contempt for others, to despise people. ¶ naba-ö̃dⁱ f. a storm in the sky, heavy with dark clouds and furious dust. -dub m. a crash from the sky, a fall from a great height; an earthquake or similar calamity in which mountains, buildings, and the like are upset. -grañ m. anxiety from the sky; hence, a clap or peal of thunder. -grāy f. a shaking of the sky accompanied by thunder, believed to be produced by an earthquake. -gāsh or -gôshᵘ m. brightness of the sky, the illumination of a starlit night (when there is no moon). -gaṭa f. a darkness of the sky (from clouds, etc.). -nañĕr m. clearness of the sky (when there is not a trace of clouds). -nār m. fire from the sky, an earthquake or similar calamitous portent accompanied by a fiery sky; haughtiness, excessive pride, despising people. -nār anun m.inf. haughtiness, etc., to arise. -nār hyonᵘ m.inf. to be filled with jealousy. -nār khasun m.inf. excessive haughtiness to be displayed. -nār wŏthun m.inf. great jealousy to arise. -phal m. fruit in the sky, i.e. something non-existent, impossible, or lost for ever (e.g. dead or destroyed). -pōsh m. flowers (growing) in the sky, something impossible, non-existent, or utterly destroyed; something weak or unsubstantial, and on this account disappearing before one's very eyes. -ṭub m. utter destruction from the sky, i.e. (esp. of a country) utter destruction from an earthquake or similar calamity, or from bad government. -traṭh f. (sg. dat. -traṭi), lightning from the sky, the lightning of a thunder- storm, a thunderbolt. -zã̄ḍ f. hoar-frost in the sky, blackness in the sky due to frosty weather. -zāl m. a cloud covering of the sky, a clouded sky. ¶ nȧbⁱ ö̃dⁱ f., i.q. naba-ö̃dⁱ, ab. -grañ m., i.q. naba-grᵒ, ab. -gaṭa f., i.q. naba-gaᵒ, ab. --logᵘ-motᵘ --, see nab logᵘ motᵘ. --lagun --, see nab lagun, ab. -pōsh m., i.q. naba-pōsh, ab. -traṭh f. (sg. dat. -traṭi), i.q. naba-traṭh, ab. -traṭh hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -traṭh hishᵘ̈), like a thunderbolt; hence, one who is always causing great and sudden destruction, a break-all. ¶ nabukᵘ adj. (f. nabücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the sky; produced in the sky. --nār -- m. twilight (El. nabukār, a misprint). ¶ nabacĕ tāra wālañĕ f. pl. inf. to bring down the stars from the sky; met. to exhibit great energy or industry in one's study or in other work. ¶ nabunᵘ 1 (for 2, see s.v.) adj. (f. nabüñᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the Sky (personified). nabañĕ tāra f.pl. the stars of the sky, the stars of heaven. ¶ nabas khasun m.inf. to mount to the sky; to be filled with (esp. groundless) pride or haughtiness.

f. the navel; a focus or central point (L.V. 34, 57); cf. nāph. --ḍalüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the navel to be displaced, rupture (the disease) to occur. ¶ nāba-ṭang m. a pear on the navel; hence, the use of pretended smooth words (in order to gain some object), wheedling, soft solder. -ṭang wālȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to bring down a pear on the naval; hence, to wheedle a person into doing something. ¶ nābi-sthān m. the locality, or neighbourhood, of the navel, the navel (El. nabistán).

m. refined white sugar, sugar candy (cf. ḍal-nāᵒ, p. 210a, l. 5, and nūn nābad gaʦhun, s.v. nūn) (L. 254 (the Persian form nabāt); L.V. 108; Śiv. 435, 478, 499, 591, etc.; Rām. 1653; K.Pr. 78, 146, 155, 159, 233). -dọ̆rᵃg f. a three-cornered lump of candy. -kuza m. sugar crystallized in an earthen pot or pan.
in the following:--nābȧdⁱ rang m. a kind of colour, pale orange. -trēl f. a kind of small, sweet, juicy, yellow apple (L. 349, nabádi trel).
adj. c.g. non-existent, annihilated, ruined, destroyed, disappeared, vanished. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become annihilated, non-existent, etc.
f. non-existence, annihilation, ruin. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. annihilation, non-existence, disappearance to occur (to any person or thing).
(a misprint in El. for nabukᵘ nār, p. 619a, l. 42).
(for 1, see p. 619a, l. 47) m. the non-production of anything (e.g. failure or barrenness of a crop, or non-result of any action). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such non-production, etc., to occur.
f. (sg. dat. nabūvüʦᵘ̈), rareness, costliness, preciousness.
nācāra adj. c.g. helpless, destitute, forlorn, distressed, miserable (YZ. 45, 100, 253).
m. (sg. dat. nācas), dancing; an entertainment at which dancing girls perform, a nautch. Cf. naʦun.
f. a brook, a small river (cf. nadī) (L.V. 57, 96; K.Pr. 17, 47, 149).

m. sounding, a sound, cry, noise (Gr.Gr. 10, Gr.M.); a voice, a cry, exclamation (L.V. 72); (in Kāshmīrī) a call, summons (Śiv. 256, 471, 510, etc.); kraka-nād, screaming (Gr.M.). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to cry aloud, call out, shout (Gr.M.; YZ. 109, 154); to call, summon (someone within easy reach of the voice) (L. 459; W. 88; Śiv. 440, 450, 1337; Rām. 377, 474, 476, 1139, 1766; H. i, 10; x, 12; xii, 17; YZ. 437); in pl. --dinⁱ -- to utter repeated calls (Rām. 1356, 1630); to utter repeated cries, to utter lamentations, appeals for mercy, help, or the like (Rām. 1356, 1535, 1630); anun nād dith, to summon, send for (Gr.M.). --lāyun -- m.inf. to strike a call, to call (very loudly) to a person from a distance, to shout to (Śiv. 1323, 1370, 1441, 1746; Rām. 491, 650, 1720; K. 291). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. a sudden call to come; the summons (to the other world) to be received, to die. ¶ nāda-bĕnd, i.q. bindu-nād, p. 111b, l. 22 (Śiv. 669, 1320, 1336, 1594, 1602, 1757, 1891). -nād m. calling or summoning over and over again, repeated calling (at one time, not at intervals); although masc., this compound is treated as a fem. in the following. -nād karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to call repeatedly in this way. ¶ nādas gaʦhun m.inf. to go on a summons, to go to call or summon a person. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come on a call, to come in answer to a summons (conveyed by a messenger or the like).
f. (sg. dat. nadāmüʦᵘ̈), repentance, penitence, contrition, regret, shame.

adj. c.g. ignorant, unlearned, simple (Gr.M.); unwise, foolish (of an action) (Gr.M., K.Pr. 47); an ignorant fellow, a fool, a blockhead (El.; W. 144; Śiv. 241, 762, 1900; Rām. 805; H. ii, 5; xi, 11; K.Pr. 54, 149).
adj. c.g. impecunious, poor, indigent (El. nadeor) (Rām. 1351). Cf. nĕdörⁱ.
f. a river (whether great or small) (cf. nad) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 24, 239, 532, 1910; Rām. 245, 622, 805, 1439, 1501; K. (pl. nom. nadiyĕ) 586), -boṭhᵘ m. the bank of a river (Gr.M.).

or nöḍī f. [sg. dat. nāḍi; the nom. pl. is optionally the irregular nöjⁱ or nöjᵘ̈ (cf. ōh-nöjᵘ̈, p. 18a, l. 12)], one of the larger blood-vessels; by the ignorant used to denote any blood-vessel, tendon, or other similar prominent object felt under the skin; (in Yōga philosophy) the tubes in the body through which the life-winds circulate. There are fourteen (of which ten are principal) of these, rising from the kanda, or region between the pudendum and the navel (L.V. 69; Śiv. 1082, 1891; see L.V., s.v. nāḍi). -dal m. the whole group of these tubes (L.V. 80). ¶ nöjⁱ or nöjᵘ̈ f. pl. irr. the veins, tendons, etc., as ab., considered as a whole. --khasañĕ -- f. pl. inf. the veins or tendons, etc., to swell (c.g. from holding the breath). --lagañĕ -- f. pl. inf. the windpipe to be choked, i.e. to get a sore throat from shouting excessively. --lāgañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to cause a person to get a sore throat, as ab. (by not obeying his call, and, hence, making him shout excessively).

or nadurᵘ m. the stalk of a lotus, the leaf-stem of the Nelumbium speciosum (L. 72, 461; Śiv. 1850; K.Pr. 149, 155). According to El. (s.v. nadir) Hindūs cut this up into small pieces, cook it with oil and condiments, and eat it along with flesh or dāl (cf. mŏnjĕ-nᵒ, p. 575a, l. 37) (L.V. 89; cf. nadorᵘ 2). ¶ nadȧrⁱ-ã̄cār m. a pickle made of lotus-stalks, cooked in the sun with mustard, salt, oil, and tamarind-juice. -curma m. a dish of broken lotus-stalks fried in oil or ghī. -caṭiñ f. a chutnee, or pickle, of pounded lotus-stalks. -ganḍ m. the lump or knot at the root of a lotus from which the stalk issues. -khünḍᵘ̈ f. a broken piece of lotus-stalk (as prepared for cooking). -kūṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kōcĕ), a long piece of lotus-stalk. -mỗkun m. a piece of lotus-stalk, about two or three inches long, for grinding to powder for toilet purposes; see mỗkun 1. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. a pasty of lotus-stalks (Gr.Gr. 75). -mỗthunᵘ m. a short piece of lotus-stalk (about two or three inches long) shaped like a drum bulging in the middle. -nambal f. a lotus-bed, a plot in a lake where lotuses grow profusely. -nāṭa f.pl. lotus-stalks cooked with flesh-meat; cf. nāṭh. -pālakh f. (sg. dat. -pālaki), lotus-stalks stewed with spinach. -ras m. a sauce of lotus-stalk juice mixed with condiments. -syunᵘ m. a stew of meat and lotus-stalks. -talörᵘ̈ f. a certain dish of fried lotus-stalks. -talöyⁱ a pancake (lit. a blanket) of lotus-stalks. -ʦakul m. a round bit of a lotus-stalk, a small disc of lotus-stalk chopped across. -ʦyūṭᵘ m. a soup of parched lotus-stalks, pounded with salt. It is quickly made and used when other soup is not available. -wāl m. the filament of a lotus-stalk. ¶ nadarinⁱ zȧdⁱ m.pl. N. of a certain disease, in which the body is covered with holes like the hollows of lotus-stalks. The disease is generally mentioned in abusive cursing-- 'may your body become like this'.
adj. (f. nadürᵘ̈), not strong, weak, infirm (L.V. 89, where there is a play on the meaning of nadorᵘ 1).

m. (f. nadᵃhürᵃ, q.v.), a certain bird, the osprey (K.Pr. 149 translates it doubtfully as 'cormorant', but the Sanskrit kurara means 'osprey'). ¶ nadᵃharüñᵃ naṭh f. a nadᵃhar's trembling; hence, any special fear (K.Pr. 149).
for words beginning thus see under naph-.

m. lead (the metal) (Gr.M.). ¶ nāga-gōla m. a ball (esp. a large ball) of lead. -gūlⁱ f. a leaden bullet. -köryun m. the melting of lead (see kārun). -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. a piece or lump of lead melted and cast into any desired shape. -pal m. large boulder or rock of lead ore. -ʦrüṭᵘ̈ f. a round disc of lead (e.g. made by hammering flat a ball of lead). ¶ nāgukᵘ 1 adj. (f. nāgücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, lead; made of lead.

m. (f. nögiñ, q.v., Gr.Gr. 37), a snake, esp. a fabulous serpent-demon or semi-divine being, having the face of a man and the tail of a serpent, and said to inhabit Pātāla. In Kashmīr, they are the deities of springs (Gr.Gr. 37, L. 342, Śiv. 1455, K. 230 ff.); a fountain, a spring of water (Gr.Gr. 51; Gr.M.; L. 464; Śiv. 1109, 1181, 1883; H. iii, 4, 59; v, 9; vi, 15; xii, 6, 7, 11, 12, 14; YZ. 396, 406; K.Pr. 150). Cf. hāputh-nāg, p. 342b, l. 33, and nīla-nāg, s.v. nīl, and many other place-names (e.g. in Śiv. 1164-78; K.Pr. 134, 233). ¶ nāga-babᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a certain plant, water-cress (Nasturtium officinale) (L. 72). -bal m. a spring sacred to some nāga demi-god and hence a place of worship or pilgrimage. -gāḍa f.pl. the fish in a sacred spring. (The visiting of these is considered to be propitious, and to eat them is looked upon as a sin.) -kīsar m. N. of a small tree with fragrant blossoms, Mesua Roxburghii. -lay f. a tract of country in which there are many springs. -nikh or nāg-anikh f. (sg. dat. -niki) 'many springs', a place where there are many springs. -nẹ̆ndᵃr f. deep and sweet sleep (like that by a cool spring) (Śiv. 1691). -nāth m. (sg. dat. -nāthas), the lord, or king, of serpents, ruling over all water-springs (Śiv. 1181, 1585). -phǖ̃sⁱ  f. a serpent's noose, the fettering by a serpent which winds itself two or three times round a human body; a kind of noose used as a weapon, esp. a sort of magical noose of this kind. -rād m. a kind of sacred spring or lake (Śiv. 191, 509, 1591; Rām. 1495, 1720, 1722); a fountain (Śiv. 964). -rāza m. a royal serpent, a serpent demi-god of high rank (of whom there are several in Hindū mythology, such as, e.g. Vāsuki, Takṣaka, Karkōṭa, and so on). -wôñᵘ m. the water of a spring, spring water (El. nágawóiṅ, Gr.Gr. 73, Śiv. 1522). -wuziñ f. the steady perpetual flow of water from a spring; met. a steady perpetual flow of wealth, coming easily from some invisible source. -zal m. the water of a spring (Śiv. 929). ¶ nögⁱ-rāy m., i.q. nāga-rāza, ab. (Rām. 1026, 1571). ¶ nāgukᵘ 2 adj. (f. nāgücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a spring.

or nāgah ناگہ adv. suddenly, unexpectedly, all at once, unawares, abruptly. nāgahücᵘ̈ balāy f. a sudden, unexpected, calamity (such as divine anger, anger of a king, an earthquake, a lightning stroke, conflagration, plunder, false accusation, or the like).
adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, a city or town. -pan m. N. of the best kind of betel leaf.

m. a large drum, a double drum (El. also nagár, Gr.M., L. 459). --kọ̆nḍᵘ -- m. the body or bowl of a double drum. --wāyĕnwōlᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --wāyĕnwājĕñ --), a drummer (El. nagár wáyanwol). ¶ nagār-khāna نقار خانہ m. the place at the porch of a palace where the drums are beaten at stated intervals (Śiv. 725).
subst., f. and adj. c.g. the Nāgarī character; anything written or composed in that character; (a pen, etc.) suited for writing the character.
m. (sg. dat. nagbatas), pride, haughtiness, consequential airs. --khasun -- m.inf. pride, haughtiness, etc., to arise. --lagun -- m.inf. pride or haughtiness suddenly to attack a person.

m. a song (El. naghma); (in Kāshmīrī) a dance of women or boys (El. nagamah) (Śiv. 1731); cf. baca-naᵒ (p. 79a, l. 20) and höphiza-naᵒ (p. 342a, l. 38). --lāgun -- m.inf. to set a dance going (H. iii, 7); to start dancing or capering in joy (Rām. 525).
f. an unchaste woman (esp. one who is so privately).
f. repeated asking, asking for something again and again (even when some has been already given once or twice). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to ask in this way, to irritate by asking again and again.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. nã̄griladiñ), one who asks over and over again (even after already having obtained several times).
adj. (f. nāgüvᵘ̈), made of lead, leaden.

f. (for gend., see Gr.Gr. 37), a small town, a village, a hamlet. --navüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a village to become excessive; met. a single man to have a great number of descendants (sons, daughters, grandchildren, great-grandchildren, etc.).
adv. causelessly, uselessly, unnecessarily. --pahāka -- adv. without a cause, for no reason (u.w. vbs. of abusing, confining, and the like). ¶ nahākas-pĕṭh adv. absolutely uselessly, to no purpose.

adj. c.g. unjust, wrong, iniquitous (El. nahakk, K.Pr. nāhakk); as adv. without ground, without cause, without rhyme or reason (Śiv. 571, 575, 589; K.Pr. 158); nāhaka adv., id. (Śiv. 1796; Rām. 1670; K.Pr. 67, 180).
adj. c.g. careless, free from care, without fear, brave.
adj. c.g. unlucky, ill-fated, inauspicious; (in Kāshmīrī) bad, wicked; bad, not good (e.g. a thing, a road, or the like).
f. (sg. dat. nahāvüñᵘ̈ 1; for 2, see nahāwunᵘ, s.v. nahāwun), an article for obliterating writing, etc., an eraser (Gr.Gr. 121).
f. wages for destroying, for pulling down (a house, etc.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nahôwᵘ), to erase (writing, etc.) (cf. buthᵘ naᵒ, p. 142a, l. 3) (Gr.Gr. 121); to pull down and scatter (a house, wall, or the like), to put an end to. ¶ nahôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nahövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), erased, wiped out, destroyed, etc., as ab. ¶ nahāwan-kal f. prohibiting. -kal diñᵘ̈ f.inf. to cause a person to change his mind. ¶ nahāwunᵘ fut. pass. part. (f. nahāvüñᵘ̈ 2; for 1, see nahāwan), fit to be erased, worthy of, or destined to, destruction.
in nahīthʦhunun m.inf. to cancel, make void (H. xii, 4).

f. (the pl. nom. of this word is, exceptionally, the same as the sg.) the veins, etc. (e.g. of the arm or neck), which are visible from outside; cf. nāḍi. --khasañĕ -- f. inf. pl. these veins to rise, i.e. become prominent (e.g. the veins of the neck or cheek to swell from the exertion of coughing, shouting, or the like, or from rage). --wŏthañĕ -- f. inf. pl., id.; met. to become enraged.
breakfast; a snack, a small amount of food taken in default of a regular meal. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take or eat breakfast; to eat a snack in default of a regular meal.
or nahar f. a river, stream, canal (Śiv. 499). nahri-tār m. an aqueduct (L. 458).
adj. c.g. marked with the figure or number nine; the nine at cards. Cf. nawa 3.
m. a deputy, used in such compounds as nāib taḥṣīldār نائب تحصیلدار, a certain subordinate revenue official (L. 401, 422).
m. N. of a certain month, April-May, in the phrase ạbᵃ̇r-i-naisān ابرِ نیسان vernal showers (Rām. 1141).
m. a womanlike man, a weak feminine fellow, a man who lives among women.
m. (sg. dat. najāsatas), dirtiness, nastiness, filth, impurity, ordure.
m. (for gender, see W. 18) salvation (a Musalmān word).
adj. c.g. befouled with ordure, filthy, nasty.
adj. c.g. ugly-nosed, big-nosed, crooked-nosed. -wôrᵘ m. a nostril (El. nakawár). -woṭᵘ adj. (f. -wüṭᵘ̈), flat-nosed.
m. denial, refusal (K.Pr. 14); prohibition. --karun -- m.inf. to refuse, decline (Gr.M.); to prohibit (dat. of obj. prohibited) (H. iv, 6); to deny (having done so-and-so) (Gr.M.).

adj. c.g. unserviceable, unprofitable (Gr.M.); useless, worthless, despicable, bad (common in this sense, equivalent to the Hindī burā) (Gr.M., W. 21, K.Pr. 204); bad, prejudicial (governs dat.) (Gr.M.); bad, wicked, naughty (Gr.M.).
f. unserviceableness; worthlessness, uselessness, badness; evil actions, wickedness (Gr.M.).
m. a nostril, see p. 627a, l. 38.

m. a nail of the finger or toe; a kind of perfume (a dried substance of a brown colour, and of the shape of a finger nail, generally added to incense) (cf. Hindī nakh). nakha-tᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a spike in the nail; hence, trouble, worry, distress (compared to the distress caused by digging in the ground with the nails in search of something lost). Cf. nakha-tᵃjĕ, s.v. nakh 2.
m. (sg. dat. nākas), heaven; (considered as produced in heaven) a variety of pear (see bel., and cf. hāra-nāᵒ, p. 343b, l. 47) (L. 350). -ṭang m. a kind of pear (see ab.).

m. (sg. dat. nakhas), the shoulder (esp. as a bearer of burdens) (Śiv. 1504, 1665) (cf. nal-nakh, p. 631b, l. 42, and nala-nakha, p. 632a, l. 24). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. (at a funeral) to lift the bier on to the shoulders. --mōrun -- m.inf. to suffer a slight blow; be lightly pressed down; cf. mōrun. The phrase apparently means literally 'to twist the shoulder' (?), or possibly it should be referred to nakh 1. --mōrawȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to give (rice) a slight repounding (in a mortar). Perhaps this should come under nakh 1. --phuṭȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the shoulders to be dislocated, i.e. to become fatigued. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause the shoulder to enter, to bow the shoulders in order to receive a burden. --wālȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to bring down the shoulders, to make them weary (of some boy or the like carried a long way on the shoulders). --wasȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the shoulders to descend, i.e. to be wearied by carrying a heavy burden. ¶ nakha adv. near, close by (El.; W. 152; Śiv. 274, 1631; H. ii, 9; K. 294; K.Pr. 62, 96, 133); near (as a helper) (Śiv. 443, K.Pr. 96); (postpos. governing dat.), near (to) (K.Pr. 210). -chala wālañĕ f. pl. inf. to cause the pieces of the shoulder to descend, (in cutting out a garment) to cut out the shoulders. -chath f. loss on the shoulder, the completion of some work unwillingly or carelessly; cf. chath nakha wālüñᵘ̈, p. 166b, l. 27. --ḍakha -- adj. c.g. close up to, near, come up close, come up close to help, a close companion, an ally (K. 43). --ḍokhᵘ -- adj. (f. --ḍüchᵘ̈ --), one who is close (to help), a support, a helper; cf. nokhᵘ- ḍokhᵘ, s.v. nokhᵘ. -nakha adv. shoulder to shoulder, one by one each mutually near. -nokhᵘ adj. (f. -nüchᵘ̈) and adv. one who is very near; adv.  very near. -nonᵘ adj. (f. -nüñᵘ̈), bare-shouldered. -palav m. a shoulder cloth, the folded cloth on the shoulder used as a pad when carrying a jar of water or the like. -pūrᵘ m. walking slowly, slow progress (Śiv. 1832). -tᵃjĕ f.pl. 'pins on the shoulder'. In former days Kāshmīrīs wore a kind of blanket, the head passing through a hole in the centre, and the two halves hanging down before and behind. The edges at each side were then fastened together by wooden thorns or pins. Such a garment is still worn by chief mourners at a Hindū funeral till the days of impurity are passed. This method of fastening the clothes is called by the above name; cf. nakha-tᵘ̈jᵘ̈, s.v. nakh 1. -tᵃjĕ lagañĕ f. pl. inf. long tears or cuts to occur in a garment, requiring to be fastened together by pins, as in the preceding. -tal adv. under the shoulder; hence, near, close by (L. 152). -tȧlⁱ adv. from near, from the vicinity (u.w. vbs. of motion). -talukᵘ adj. (f. -talücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, near by, produced, occurring, or existing close by. -ʦürᵘ̈ f. a straw or rope ring for supporting a water-jar or the like. --wālun -- m.inf. to bring down from one's own shoulder, to discharge a responsibility; (when there is joint responsibility for a work, for one person) to rid himself of the responsibility (by merely telling the other how to do it), perfunctorily to supervise; to repay (a loan, or the like) (El. also naka wálun, L. 350; cf. horun nak walun (sic), to discharge a debt, L. 459); to get through (a day), pass (a difficult day) completely (Rām. 291); cf. bēgörⁱ nakha wālüñᵘ̈ (p. 92a, l. 26), chath nakha wālüñᵘ̈ (p. 166b, l. 27), and drath nakha wālüñᵘ̈ (p. 249b, l. 10), all meaning 'to do scamped work'. -wālay f. merely telling a person to do a thing, and not seeing that he does it, perfunctory supervision. -wālay karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. perfunctorily to supervise. --wasun -- m.inf. to descend from the shoulder, to be completed, got rid of (e.g. of a debt being paid off, or of the life of a person at the point of death) (Śiv. 1562,). -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), to join up the shoulders of a garment (in tailoring). -wothᵘ m. repayment of a debt, etc. -wothᵘ gaʦhun m.inf. a debt to be repaid. -wothᵘ karun m.inf. to repay a debt. --wothᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --wüʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), completed, got rid of; repaid (of a debt). ¶ nȧkhⁱ adv. (carried) on the shoulders. ¶ nakhi, i.q. nȧkhⁱ (K. 469). --khārun -- m.inf. to lift up on to the shoulder (e.g. a child, a burden, etc.); to undertake a responsibility. --khasun -- m.inf. to mount on to the shoulder (K. 390); to become insolent; to be lifted on to the shoulder; a responsibility to be incurred. ¶ nakhan bata harun m.inf. 'rice to fall on the shoulders'; hence, to be put in the way of earning a living (e.g. of a young man who is now fully trained for some employment). ¶ nakhas khôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. --khörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), mounted on the shoulder, carried on the shoulder (e.g. a child); become insolent. --khārun -- m.inf. to lift (e.g. a child) on to the shoulder (K. 288); to make insolent; to undertake responsibility. --khasun -- m.inf. to ascend on to the shoulders, (of a child) to climb on to the shoulders; to become insolent; the responsibility for the completion of anything to be incurred. --khotᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --khüʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), ascended on to the shoulder; become insolent; that for the execution of which responsibility has been incurred. -kĕth adv. on the shoulder (Rām. 746, 890); -pĕṭh adv., id. (Rām. 446, 584, 644, 888).

m. the nose, in the following idioms:--nākh dōla rōzun m.inf. the nose to remain askew, to have the nose put out of joint (e.g. when A refuses help to B in any work, for B to carry it out alone with great success, and A is thus put to shame). --dōla thawun -- m.inf. to put a person's nose out of joint, as ab.
m. a slave-, horse-, or cattle-market; a tax levied on the sale of horses or cattle; the person who levies this tax (i.q. nakhösⁱ) (K.Pr. 71).

or nakhᵃch (= نقش، نقشہ) m. (sg. nakhcas), a delineation, a portrait; a painting, a picture; a map, a plan. Cf. naksh, nakshĕ. nakhᵃch-gorᵃ m. a painter, delineator, designer, one who paints or draws patterns; a map-maker.

adj. c.g. maimed, wanting a limb; (of an inanimate object) having some essential part missing (and thus useless). --karun -- m.inf. to maim; to make useless by depriving of some essential part. -zad adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -zadiñ), maimed, etc., i.q. nākhēz.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. nākhēzladiñ), maimed, wanting a limb; rendered useless (by the loss of some essential part).
c.g. an atheist, an impious wretch (YZ. 98).
adj. c.g. indisposed; unhappy, displeased (Gr.M., Śiv. 881, Rām. 104); disgusted.
m. the official whose duty it is to collect the tax on the sale of horses (see the preceding).
adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. nakhwaṭas), having a nose like a globular stone, ugly-nosed (described as having a nose which is long, broad-tipped, and with wide nostrils).

m. (El. makes the word f.), trick, artifice; joke, waggery; feminine airs or blandishments; coquetry, flirting, etc. --karȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to coquet; to show pretended dislike. --gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. coquetry to be displayed; pretended dislike to be shown. --rōṭun -- m.inf. 'to stop by coquetry', insincerely to refuse (e.g. of a newly married bride, although desiring union, through modesty repelling her husband).
adj. c.g. flirtatious, one (male or female) who habitually coquets; elegant (so El.).
m. a limner, draughtsman, painter (e.g. of houses, of papier mâché articles, lacquer-work, or of shawl-patterns) (El., L. 377-8, 458 nakásh).
f. drawing, designing, painting (esp. on papier mâché, or in making shawl-patterns) (El.).
m. painting, in naksh karun m.inf. to paint (El.). Cf. nakhca.
m. a delineation, portrait, picture (Gr.M.); a design, plan; a map, chart (El.); cf. nakhca. --tulun -- m.inf. to draw a picture (Gr.M.).
m. the Sanskritized spelling of nĕchatur, q.v., sometimes used by Paṇḍits (Śiv. 38).
m. N.P. of the fourth Pāṇḍava prince, in Skt. Nakula (K. 1012, 1066, 1068).
m. ready money, cash (El. nakad, Gr.M.); coin of a just standard.

m. transportation, removal; transcribing, copying; imitating, mimicking; a copy, transcript (Gr.M.); a translation (El.); a history, narrative, tale, story. --karun -- m.inf. to imitate, mimic; to act, represent a personal character; to make a copy of, to copy; to translate (El.); to caricature, parody, burlesque, travesty.

m. the hollow stalk of any vegetable (cf. hāka-nal, p. 326b, l. 28; khȧrⁱ-nal, p. 410b, l. 46; kōtar-nal, p. 491b, l. 49) (K.Pr. 41); a thread; the leg-bone, the leg (anatomically) (El.). -cōd adj. c.g. dissolute, profligate, immoral. --gindun -- m.inf. to impede, hinder. -nakh m.pl. leg and shoulder; hence, the limbs of the body as a whole. -pūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -pūṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat. pōchĕ), coarse-threaded, i.e. (of cloth, etc.) woven with coarse thread, coarse (of cloth). -sān m. habitually acting as a go-between in relation to dissolute conduct, the trade of a pimp. -woṭᵘ m. the little roof put along the top of a mud wall to protect it from the weather (it is made of wood, straw, etc.). -vüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -wacĕ), a kind of soft stone (used for making drinking cups and stools; when powdered it is used as a remedy for bruises or wounds); i.q. -woṭᵘ, ab. (Śiv. 1562). -waṭh m. (sg. dat. -waṭas), a large lump of stone similar to the preceding (K.Pr. 82, nalawaṭ); a kind of small stone mortar used for pounding pepper or the like. ¶ nala-dab m. a blow on the leg-bone. -dorᵘ adj. (f. -dürᵘ̈), possessing a strong stalk; possessing or consisting of strong thread. -gōmotᵘ perf. part. (f. -gömüʦᵘ̈), having reached a condition of uselessness, become worthless. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to reach a condition of uselessness, to become worthless. -hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), a kind of vegetable with a hollow stalk. --karun -- m.inf. to render useless. -mọ̆ṭᵘ adj. (f. -mö̆ṭᵘ̈), having a stout stalk (of a plant). -nakha adj. c.g. having strong legs and shoulders, strong-limbed. -nakha gaʦhun m.inf. strong-limbedness to go, i.e. to become weak or wasted. -nakha wasun m.inf. strong-limbedness to descend, i.q. the preceding. -phuṭᵘ adj. (f. -phuṭᵘ̈), (of a plant) having the stalk broken; having the leg broken. -ʦhọ̆ṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦhŏ̈ṭᵘ̈), having a short stalk. -ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. a blow with the leg, a kick. -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), having the stalk broken; having the leg broken. -vyoṭhᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ṭhᵘ̈), stout-legged. -zyūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈), having a long stalk, long-stalked.

m. the collar of a coat, i.e. the border of the garment called the kurta, round the neck and down the breast (cf. dövⁱ-nⁱ, p. 262a, l. 22; marda-nᵒ, p. 589b, l. 25) (El.; K.Pr. 51, 123); tabakh-nᵒ, p. 962b, l. 25; the neck (of the body) (H. v. 9; vi, 9; viii, 10); the bosom (including the neck) (El., Śiv. 814, K.Pr. 102). --dāmāna (or dāmȧnⁱ) karun --  m.inf. to make the collar into a skirt, to turn (a coat) upside down (a device for giving an old garment a new lease of life). --phirun -- m.inf. to turn a (worn) garment back to front (to give it a new lease of life). --walun -- m.inf. 'to cover the neck'; hence, angrily to scold or attack (Rām. 553); to be surrounded by the coils of a serpent (of a man, beast, tree, etc.) (lit. or met.) (Śiv. 874; Rām. 346, 1073, 1191, 1614). ¶ nāla-düjᵘ̈ f. a kerchief or piece of cloth fastened to the neck of a garment (before or behind) to strengthen it, or to protect it from dirt. -dolᵘ m. 'the skirt on the neck', urgent coming and going (in order to accomplish some purpose), going urgently backwards and forwards. -dolᵘ kaḍun m.inf. to experience the worry of coming and going long journeys for some purpose (esp. fruitlessly). -hoṭᵘ m. the neck and the parts near it (of a man or beast, or of a garment) (YZ. 374). --kaḍun --  m.inf. to draw off from the neck, to put (or take) off a garment (Śiv. 1329). -kholᵘ adj. (f. -khüjᵘ̈), (of a garment) wide-necked, too loose in the neck. ¶ nāla-motᵘ m. an embrace, embracing (K. 399). -motᵘ karun m.inf. to embrace [Śiv. 505, 890, 1615; Rām. 1115, 1481 (pl.), 1733 (pl.); K. 246 (pl.), 461 (pl.), 475 (pl.), 857 (pl.); YZ. 354 (pl.)]. nālamati raṭun m.inf. to hold in an embrace, to give a long and affectionate embrace (Śiv. 1258, 1324, 1381, 1468, 1556; K. 265, 292, 750, 1012, 1015, 1025, 1129). ¶ nāla-pakhᵃsh m. (in making a garment) the piece cut out of the cloth to make the orifice for the neck. --roṭᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --rüṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), seized by the neck, seized so that one cannot proceed, arrested. --raṭun -- m.inf. to seize by the neck, arrest, to seize forcibly and retain (K.Pr. 102, Rām. 762); to embrace (Śiv. 275, YZ. 371). -trᵃth or -trith m. (sg. dat. -trᵃtas or -tritas), the slit in a garment for the neck. ¶ nölⁱ adv. on the neck (e.g. with reference to a necklace, garland, or the like) (Śiv. 2, 88, 169, 266, 978, 1106, 1153, 1326; K. 60, 85, 927; YZ. 22); (with reference to garments) (worn) on the person (Śiv. 98, 166, 889, 1037, 1607; Rām. 763, 1448; K.Pr. 152). --gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), worn on the neck (YZ. 36); one who angrily scolds or threatens. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. angrily to scold, threaten (K.Pr. 152). --ʦhunᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. ʦhu ñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), put on the neck (e.g. a necklace) (Śiv. 891); put on the neck, (of a garment) worn, donned. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to put (a necklace, etc.) on the neck (K.Pr. 102; Śiv. 163, 194, 1794; Rām. 489, 512, 715); to put on the neck, to put on, don (a garment) (Śiv. 1709; H. viii, 10; x, 4; xii, 7; YZ. 374; K.Pr. 26, nál ʦhᵒ); to throw a rope round the neck, to halter (K.Pr. 102).

m. a horseshoe (El.; H. xi, 17; K.Pr. 73, misprinted náe); the horseshoe-like iron 'tips' fastened to the heel or sole of a human being's shoe. -band نعل بند m. a shoeing smith (El.); a maker of iron tips for shoes. -bȧndⁱ (= نعل بندی) f. shoeing (a horse or other beast), giving (a horse) new shoes; a light tribute, horseshoe money (exacted under Musalmān rule, on the plea of keeping up the cavalry of the state, or in consideration of the horsemen not devastating the country). -bȧndⁱ lagüñᵘ̈ f.inf. such a tax to be imposed. -bȧndⁱ lāgüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to impose such a tax. --lāgȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to apply shoes, to shoe (a horse); to scold (a woman to teach her manners), to chide, admonish. ¶ nāla-khünḍᵘ̈ f. a piece of a horseshoe. -khŏr or -khōr m. a hoof of a horseshoe, i.e. the shoe of a single hoof, a single horseshoe.
m. an artificial watercourse, a channel, a canal (esp. when forming a boundary between two pieces of land) (Śiv. 1680, Rām. 244).

f. complaints, lamentations, moans, groans (Śiv. 165, 1249, 1258); a hubbub, outcry (K. 153); grief (El., who makes the word m.); as adv. with loud lamentations (Rām. 445, 875). --diñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to lament, complain (esp. with reproaches) (Rām. 278, 1540; H. vii, 22-3; YZ. 41, 102, 475). --trāwañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to pour forth lamentations (Rām. 242, 292, 376, 893, 1551). ¶ nālan lagun m.inf. to lament (to a person), to appeal to a person with loud lamentations. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come to lamentations, to begin lamentations (Rām. 279).

m. false denial (e.g. of the receipt of money entrusted, or that one has done or said something), false disowning, disclaiming, or repudiation (K.Pr. 152). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to deny falsely as ab., to embezzle.
n.ag. (f. nālavüñᵘ̈), one who makes lamentations mixed with reproaches.
postpos. or prep. with, together with (a corruption of Hindī) (H. xi, 4).
m. a water-pipe, a pipe for conveying water. -wôñᵘ m. water conveyed through a pipe.
f. a kind of leather shoe.
adj. (f. nālöñᵘ̈ 1; for 2, see s.v.), one who mingles lamentations with reproaches; one who petitions with lamentations.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. nālyōv), to lament (Śiv. 181; Rām. 207, 675, 1491); to lament reproachfully.
f. apipe, a tube. -cīrᵘ̈ f. a machine for boring or cutting pipes (Śiv. 1018). nali-wôñᵘ m. pipe- water, water conveyed through a pipe.

m. a (person's) name (W. 110; L.V. 8; Śiv. 677, 1014, 1113, etc.; Rām. 394, 1655; K. 127, 215; YZ. 256; K.Pr. 260); cf. nāv 1. --ganḍȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to bind names; hence (of a bard) to recite a poetical narrative (of events, or of heroes), to recite a literary work. --rōzȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. (merely) the names to remain, (of some person or occurrence) all to be forgotten except the name. --thawȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to leave nothing but the name to remain (as ab.). -warī نام وری f. reputation, fame, celebrity, renown. Cf. nāma-warī, bel. ¶ nāma-lag adj. c.g. become famous, well-known. -logᵘ adj. (f. -lüjᵘ̈), famous, well-known (by tradition), conventionally accepted by name as illustrating certain qualities. --lagun -- m.inf. to be fixed on the name, to be debited or credited against (so-and-so's) name, to be imputed to, to be ascribed to. -pay m. information (regarding some hidden person or thing); a person's address (where he is to be found). -pay hyonᵘ m.inf. to search for, to set inquiries in motion for. -war (= نام آور) adj. c.g. famous, renowned, celebrated. -warī (= نام آوری) f. reputation, fame, celebrity, renown. Cf. nām- warī, ab.

m. the nail of finger or toe (cf. ongᵘji-nam, p. 33b, l. 27; atha-nᵒ, p. 60b, l. 5; khōra-nᵒ, p. 410b, l. 1; mŏkhta-nᵒ, p. 561a, l. 12; maĩzi-nᵒ, p. 615a, l. 23) (Gr.Gr. 93; L. 462; Rām. 1022; H. v, 6; YZ. 329, 546; K.Pr. 163, 243); the prow of a boat or ship (according to El., also the stern) (Śiv. 1841, K.Pr. 76) (cf. nāvi-nam, s.v. nāv 2). --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to coax or wheedle a person to reveal a secret. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to apply the nail; hence, to open out with the nails compact or tangled wool, cotton, or the like; to scratch with the nails (oneself or another). --kāsȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to cut or pare the nails. --lath nāvi lath -- f. 'a kick on the prow and a kick on the boat itself', bewilderment caused by having to be in two places at once or having to do two things at once. --phirun -- m.inf. to turn the prow, (when a boat is tied by one end to the bank for loading purposes) to turn the boat round with the other end to the shore (for loading at that end also); cf. nama-phyurᵘ, bel. --raṭun -- m.inf. to fasten the prow of a ship (to the shore), to moor a ship in this way; to back one party in wordy warfare. --thawȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to keep the nails uncut. --tal onᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --tal üñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), brought under one's nail, (a person or thing) completely brought (after difficulty) into one's power or under one's influence. --tal anun -- m.inf. to bring under one's power or influence. --tal thowᵘ-motᵘ -- or --tal thôwᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --tal thü(thö)vᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), brought under a person's power or influence. --tal thawun -- or --tal thāwun -- m.inf. to bring (a person or thing, without delay) under one's own power or influence. --tulȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to lift the nails, to torment another (e.g. by making him do extra hard, difficult, or unpleasant work). --tal rūdᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --tal rūzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), staying, or fixed, under another's power or influence. --tal roṭᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --tal rüṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), kept wholly or partly under one's own power or influence. --tal raṭun -- m.inf. to seize and put, or keep, a person or thing under one's influence (esp. secretly). --tal rōzun -- m.inf. (of a person or thing) to remain or stay under a person's power or influence. --ta māz -- m. 'nail and flesh', very near relationship, close kinship. --trakarun -- m.inf. the bow of a ship to be too high (e.g. from overloading the stern, or from running aground). --ʦalȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. 'the nails to run away', to be put to excessive expenditure of labour (e.g. in searching for something destroyed or hidden, or in polishing and scouring cooking utensils). --ʦarȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the nails to become long (e.g. in keeping a vow). --ʦaṭȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to cut off the nails; to torture a person (e.g. to acquire information). --wŏthȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the nails to rise (K.Pr. 152); to be tormented (e.g. to perform some difficult task in very cold weather) (K.Pr. 217). ¶ nama-khünḍᵘ̈ f. a piece of a nail, a chip of a nail. --phyurᵘ -- m. the turning of the prow, i.e. the changing the end of the boat fastened to the shore (as in nam phirun, ab.). -sār f. the post at the prow of a boat uniting the two sides. -sörᵘ̈ f. touching a person with the nails (e.g. to draw his attention). --wāyun -- m.inf. to propel a boat (by standing at the prow and wielding an oar, punting-pole, or the like). ¶ nȧmⁱ koḍᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. --küḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), accomplished gradually and successfully (as in the next). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to extract by the nail (as a kernel is extracted by scraping of the rind with the nails); hence (esp. of some work which is not directly under one's own authority) without trouble gradually to accomplish it in accordance with one's own needs. --kāḍay -- f. gradual accomplishment of a work properly and without trouble (cf. the preceding). -tᵃj f. a nail-pick, a little spike for cleaning the finger-nails from dirt accumulated under them. --ʦolᵘ -- adj. (f. -ʦüjᵘ̈), (of a child or the like) disgusting or repellent in appearance (owing to thinness, dirtiness, bad condition, or the like) (cf. the next); cf. nomᵘ 1 for this sense. --ʦolᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --ʦüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), accomplished without trouble (cf. the next); thin, wasted away (e.g. as a starveling child) (cf. nomᵘ 1); (of a child or the like) disgusting, repellent (owing to thinness, etc.). --ʦalun -- m.inf. to be accomplished without difficulty (cf. --kaḍun, ab.). -ʦūr m. a thief with the nail; (esp. in gambling 'odd or even' with cowries) one who cheats by concealing with the finger-nail one cowry of those thrown down, so as to make the number counted favourable to the cheater. -ʦūrī f. cheating, as ab. -ʦūrᵘ̈ f. (usually of a child) persistently scratching a sore or wound on one's own body to allay the irritation, even when forbidden. ¶ namukᵘ adj. (f. namücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a finger- or toe-nail; of, or belonging to, the prow of a boat. ¶ naman kijĕ diñĕ f. pl. inf. to thrust spikes under the nails; met. to torment, torture. --më̆ʦᵘ̈aʦüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. dirt to get under the nails; met. to be greatly worried (cf. K.Pr. 152).
or nau card. the word used for 'nine', see nav 1, when spoken of as a separate number, as in akh nau or akh nam, one nine (W. 104).

m. a letter, an epistle (Rām. 832); a document; a book, a history, story (Rām. 1765). -pögām نامہ پیغام m. a message (of news), news sent. -pögām anun  m.inf. to bring news (of so-and-so). -pögām phērun m.inf. news to be circulated, to get news (of so-and-so), to hear about (e.g. about some distant friend's condition). -pögām phirun m.inf. to circulate news (as ab.). -pögām yunᵘ m.inf. news (as ab.) to be received.
m. (sg. dat. namakas), salt. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat (so-and-so's) salt, to get employment or food, etc., from someone.

f. (sg. dat. nāmüñᵘ̈), (among Hindūs) N. of the vessel of wood or copper containing offerings and libations made in place of the śrāddha, or full memorial rite, in the name of a deceased child who has died before investment with the sacred thread. The ceremony is performed on the twelfth lunar day of the light half of the month of Shrāwun (Skt. Śrāvaṇa = July-August) at the bathing place of Kapāla-mōcana. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make this offering.
or namānamath card. (pl. dat. nama(mā)namatan ), ninety-nine (Gr.Gr. 80).
or namānamatyunᵘ adj. (f. nama(mā)namatiñᵘ̈ ), costing, or worth, ninety-nine (rupees, etc.).
adj. c.g. unmanly, cowardly, a coward (Rām. 487, 501); impotent.

m. respectful or reverential address, adoration, obeisance (K.Pr. 102; Śiv. 5, 39, 66, 319, etc.; Rām. 125, 327, 833, etc.; K. 62, 115, 143, 197, etc.; K.Pr. 47, 102); (according to El.) a compliment.
f. (sg. dat. nāmüʦᵘ̈), calling out by name (as in calling out an attendance list); calling by name, taking the name of. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to point out the name (of a person, place, or thing).
adj. (f. namatiñᵘ̈), costing, or worth, ninety (rupees, etc.).
card. the multiplicative form of namath, ninety, as in kāh namȧtⁱ nav hath ta namath, eleven nineties are nine hundred and ninety (Gr.Gr. 86).

n.ag. (f. namavüñᵘ̈), one who bows or bends; bending down (e.g. the branch of a tree laden with fruit); humble, meek; (of a scalepan) going down (owing to its containing the heavier weight); as adv.  (with verbs of weighing, etc.) in excess, too heavy, on the heavier end of the balance, weighing too much.

f. a grass-grown lake, a lake choked by vegetation, a shallow lake, a marsh, swamp (it has rich peaty soil, L. 320) (cf. görⁱ-nⁱ, p. 298a, l. 41; gāsa-nᵒ, p. 307b, l. 40 (L. 320, 464); nadȧrⁱ-nⁱ, p. 623a, l. 36); a ferry, a ford (El.). ¶ nambala-syomᵘ m. the silt of a marsh (washed out in the rainy season, and, when deposited on paddy fields, increasing the fertility). ¶ nambali-boṭhᵘ m. the edge, bank, or margin of a marsh. -dȧjⁱ or -düjᵘ̈ f. a field (usually a rice-field) in a marsh. -dāñĕ m. (a kind of) paddy grown in a marsh. -gām m. a village, the cultivated land of which consists of marsh. -gāsa m. marsh-grass. -wôñᵘ m. marsh-water.
m. N. of a quarter of the city of Śrīnagar, the ancient Namuci-bila, where there is the cave of the demon Namuci, which formed an entrance to Pātāla, or the infernal regions. Cf. RT.Tr. iii, 468.

or namạda m. felt or close woollen cloth (formed without weaving) used in coverings for horses or in garments to keep off rain (L. 377). -gorᵘ m. a maker of this felt, a maker of felt rugs (El.). -gȧrⁱ-bāy f. his wife. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become felt; hence, to become stiff and hard (e.g. woollen cloth from much washing); to become hard and tough (e.g. a stale cake). -khünḍᵘ̈ f. a piece of this felt. -mö̃ḍ f. joining up pieces of felt (done by kneading them together; cf. mã̄ḍ). -palav m. a little ragged bit of a felt quilt.
the Persian for 'I do not know', used to signify 'ignorance' (K.Pr. 153).
m. leanness, thinness, of a wasted appearance; unpleasing appearance, disgustingness (owing to leanness, dirtiness, etc.). Cf. nam 1 and nomᵘ 1.
f. modest demeanour, modesty, humility (Gr.Gr. 120). namiñĕ kramiñĕ adv. without haughtiness, modestly.
conj. part. of namun, q.v., used as adj. to mean 'prone' (El., written namut on p. 185 by a misprint).
adj. c.g. moist, damp, dank; dewy; flaccid or slack owing to dampness.
f. moistness, humidity; flaccidity or slackness due to damp.
m. Nimrod (K.Pr. 153). namrūdȧnⁱ dam dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to give forth the breaths of Nimrod, to boast of one's own great and good qualities, to brag.
adj. c.g. apparent, visible (El.); shown, exhibited; conspicuous.
adj. c.g. apparent, visible, manifest (Śiv. 1119; Rām. 62, 463, 1085); conspicuous.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. namyōv), to bend, to bow (H. vi, 16; K. 70, 74, 494, 583, 719, 937, 988, 1164); to lean, stoop, be crooked (Gr.M.); to bow oneself, in reverence (Śiv. 94, 156, 315); to bow (YZ. 78, 86); to bend down (K.Pr. 168); to be humble (Śiv. 103, Rām. 11); to nod (El.). ¶ namith rōzun m.inf. to remain in a bowed condition, to show continual reverence, to be of humble mien. ¶ namyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. namyē-müʦᵘ̈), bowed, bent; bowed in reverence; bowed, reduced in pride, etc.

m. a sample, specimen, muster (Gr.M.); pattern, model (Gr.M.); type, form; example to be followed (Gr.M., Rām. 777). -wörᵘ̈ f. a test sample, a sample of a large consignment of grain or the like sent to the consignee by another route (for comparison with the main consignment when the latter arrives).
adj. c.g. unsuccessful; (in Kāshmīrī) without hope, without expectation (H. i, 10).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nạmᵒrᵒ), to cause to bend, to cause to bow (Gr.M.); to cause another to show reverence by bowing; to bow (the head, etc.) in reverence. nạmᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. nạmᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to bow or bend; caused to show reverence by bowing (e.g. one person caused by another, or one's own head caused to bow by one's self).
card. the multiplicative form of nav 1, nine, as in zᵃh nȧmⁱ aradāh, two nines are eighteen.

f. (sg. dat. nāni, Gr.Gr. 70), the navel. ¶ nāna ʦaṭüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to sever the navel cord (Rām. 636). -dorᵘ adj. (f. -dürᵘ̈), possessing a stout navel; hence, courageous, stout-hearted. ¶ nāni-kūṭun m. the navel cord.

f. a paternal grandmother, the mother (or stepmother) of a father (K.Pr. 24, 159, 165); a maternal grandmother, a mother's mother. Cf. baḍa-nᵒ (p. 82b, l. 23) and māsa-nᵒ, p. 596a, l. 27, and ōra-nöñᵘ̈ (p. 42a, l. 2). ¶ nāñĕ-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without a grandmother, one who has no grandmother (W. 141, nāni-rust). -shrād m. the shrād (Skt. śrāddha) or memorial rite in honour of the departed spirit of a paternal or maternal grandmother. -tônᵘ  m. the condition or state of being a paternal or maternal grandmother; affection, etc., such as that shown by a grandparent.

adj. different, of various kinds (K. 226); used ˚--, as in nānā-prakörⁱ adv. of various kinds, of different kinds, in various ways (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1492; K. 200, 682); -ranga, id. (K. 979); -rȧngⁱ, id. (K. 297, 331, 701, 962).

adj. (f. nanawörᵘ̈), bare-footed (Śiv. 173; Rām. 1424, 1434, 1436; K. 1011, 1128; YZ. 99; K.Pr. 96, 153, 248). ¶ nanawāri-nāv nērun m.inf. the name of 'Bare-foot' to issue; hence, a bad reputation to come from a single fault.

m. happiness, pleasure, joy; a son (cf. jasōdā-nand, p. 377b, l. 49); N. of a cowherd who was the foster father of Krushna (Kṛṣṇa) (Śiv. 990, 1461; K. 108, 127, 403, 471, etc.); (abl. of gen.) nandani, in Nanda's house (K. 44). ¶ nanda-gōph (sg. dat. -gōpas), or nanda-gūrᵘ (sg. gen. -gōryunᵘ), Nand, the cowherd (common as a N.P.) (-gōph, K. 99, 115, 317, 345, 357; -gūrᵘ, K. 48, 66, 72, et passim, gen. 48, 71, 76, 143, 235, etc.). -lāl m. Nanda's darling, a N. of Krushna (Śiv. 947, 1320, 1380, 1434, 1436, 1447). -pūrᵘ m. N. of a large village on the Ḍal lake near Śrīnagar.

f. a certain term in gambling. (One player holds in his fist an unknown number of cowries, and his opponent guesses how many will remain over (three, two, one, or none) after dividing the whole number by four. The game thus is on the lines of our 'odd and even'. If the whole number is exactly divisible by four, so that there is no remainder, the result is called nand.) nanda-pur f. the name of this gambling game.
m. N. of Śiva's door-keeper and chief attendant (cf. nandikēshŏr). nandi-rāza m., id. (Śiv. 214).
m. N. of one of Śiva's chief attendants (in Skt. Nandikêśvara) (Śiv. 84, 116, 388, 1167); a N. of Śiva himself (Śiv. 867).
m. (sg. dat. nandanas), a rejoicer; a son ('the rejoicer of his father'), esp. a darling son or the son of a wealthy person (Śiv. 1435-6, 1461).

m. nakedness, bareness (cf. nĕtha-nañĕr, s.v. nĕtha); the having had the covering removed, clearly visible (e.g. the sun or stars by the dissipation of clouds) (cf. naba-nᵒ, p. 619a, l. 1); manifestness (Śiv. 1068, Rām. 167); the condition of being revealed (of a secret or the like) (cf. aḍ-nᵒ, p. 10a, l. 42). --wanun -- m.inf. to speak nakedness, to say unspeakable things, to reproach harshly, to abuse (Rām. 265, pĕṭh, against).
f. honour, esteem, reputation; shame, disgrace, infamy, ignominy; impropriety (El.). --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to do blaming, cause remorse. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. shame to come, remorse to be felt.

adj. c.g. naked, nude, bare (Gr.M.; L.V. 94; Śiv. 1258, 1309; K. 273, 276, 277; K.Pr. 154); (of a criminal or the like) detected (K.Pr. 221); (of a woman showing humility) uncovered, unveiled (K. 453). --karun -- m.inf. to make naked, make bare, strip (Gr.M.); to make manifest, display without concealment. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become nude; to become manifest, to be displayed without concealment. --mast -- or -masth m. naked and mad, a naked madman; stark naked (K. 276, K.Pr. 133). -mastān or -mastāna m. naked and mad, a naked Hindū ascetic. -nonᵘ adj. (f. -nüñᵘ̈), naked, bare, nude; bared of all necessities, absolutely desolate.

f. nakedness, nudeness, bareness; bareness, absence of covering, complete revelation, unveiling (a secret). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of something secret or hidden), complete revelation to occur, to be disclosed. --karüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. (of something secret or hidden), entirely to reveal, to disclose.
adj. (f. nangürᵘ̈), absolutely destitute, possessing nothing at all (as if he were naked; cf. nanga) (Śiv. 1651).
m. (sg. dat. nānakas), the inscription or device on a coin. The nānak-shāhī rupee is worth 12 to 16 British annas (L. 242).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. nanyōv), to be (or become) naked; to be manifest, well known (Rām. 736, 1066, 1779); (of a secret or of a hidden thing or act) to be unveiled, to become disclosed, to become revealed, made manifest (cf. bēd nanüñᵘ̈, p. 83a, l. 31) (L.V. 4; Śiv. 559, 817, 990, 993, 997, etc.; H. vii, 1). nanyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nanyē-müʦᵘ̈), made naked; unveiled, disclosed, revealed, made manifest.
f. (sg. dat. nạñᵉ̆rüñᵉ̆), the act of making naked; revealing, unveiling (something secret or hidden), revelation.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nạñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), to make naked, unveil (Gr.Gr. 7); to reveal, unveil, make manifest (anything secret or hidden). nạñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. nạñᵉ̆rövᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), made naked, unveiled; (of a secret, etc.) revealed, unveiled, made manifest.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nạñᵒrᵒ), to make naked, unveil; to reveal, unveil, make manifest (some secret or hidden thing) (cf. bēd nᵒ, p. 83a, l. 34). nạñᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. nạñᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made naked; (of a secret, etc.) revealed, unveiled, made manifest.
adj. c.g. impure, unclean, dirty, filthy, polluted, defiled; lewd, licentious.
in napa-napa m. splendour, sheen, glitter, refulgence; cf. nö̃pun. napa-napa karawunᵘ n.ag. (f. --karavüñᵘ̈ --), brilliant, sparkling, glittering, refulgent.

f. (sg. dat. nāphi), the navel (El. náfah) (Śiv. 201, 501); cf. nāb. --ḍalüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the navel to be ruptured. --ganḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to tie up the navel, to cure rupture of the navel. ¶ nāphi-gorᵘ m. (f. -gürᵘ̈, a female of this profession) a person whose profession it is to cure rupture of the navel.
i.q. naphā, q.v.; (in Kāshmīrī) plenty, enough; napha chuh, it is enough (El.). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), useless (El.).

or naphāh (= نفع) m. gain, profit, emolument, proceeds, interest (Gr.M. nafā, Rām. 164). --āsun -- m.inf. profit to become, i.e. to accrue (esp. from trade). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. profit or interest to accrue (esp. from invested capital).
m. the bag or bladder of musk, a musk-pod (as found in the musk-deer) (L. 116, 462).
adj. c.g. not understanding, unintelligent, stupid (Śiv. 164, K.Pr. 149).

m. (sg. dat. naphkas), blowing, puffing; inflation; flatulence (El.). --karun -- m.inf. an attack of flatulence to come on. --yunᵘ -- m.inf., id. ¶ naphka-ḍī˜jⁱ or -ḍī˜jᵘ̈ f. 'a flatulence lump', flatulence accompanied by gout or rheumatism. -ṭujⁱ or -ṭujᵘ̈ f., id.

or nafar نفر m. an individual; a servant; (in Kāshmīrī revenue terminology) nafrē نفری a unit of persons for cultivation, consisting of a man, his wife, and one adult son, entitled to four acres of irrigated land. The nīm nafrē, or half unit, consisting of a man and his wife, entitled to two acres; and the pāv nafrē, or quarter unit, consisting of a bachelor, entitled to one and a half acres (L. 402).
adj. disobedient, refractory; subst., m. N. of a purple-coloured flower, a species of poppy.
adj. c.g. of the colour of the nā-farmān poppy, purple.
m. (sg. dat. naphratas), abomination, horror, disgust (El.).

m. a voluntary act of religion which is not prescribed; certain prayers, the reading of which is not compulsory; special prayers made in times of calamity or the like, rogations (L. 288); a work of supererogation.

or naphᵃʦ m. breath of life; soul, spirit, self (K.Pr. 150); concupiscence, lust, inordinate desire (K.Pr. 150); (in Kāshmīrī) the belly (as the claimant for food), the craving for food (Śiv. 1633, K.Pr. 149); the belly (as the receptacle of food) (Śiv. 1795; H. x, 3). --brū̃ṭhⁱ yunᵘ -- m.inf. the belly to come in front, to fill the belly greedily and without shame. --kala kaḍun -- m.inf. the belly to thrust up its head, i.e. to do anything (e.g. importunate begging, praising the unworthy, serving wicked people, taking to evil ways) under pressure of hunger or poverty. --manz thawun -- m.inf. to put the belly between, i.e. (when acting as a go-between in business matters) to seek or hope to make a profit unknown to either party. --phaṭun -- m.inf. the belly to split, (when suffering from extreme hunger) to become ready to eat anything (no matter how unwholesome or unlawful). --phuṭun -- m.inf. the belly to be brought low, (of a formerly hearty eater) to eat very little (owing to distaste, sickness coming on, or the like), to lose one's appetite. ¶ naphʦa-dôdᵘ  m. difficulty of breathing (YZ. 398); belly-pain, i.e. belly anxiety, anxiety for food (which compels a man to take to uncongenial work). naphʦüñᵘ̈ hã̄ḍ f. lamentation of the belly, labour to fill the belly.
f. impurity, uncleanness, foulness, defilement, pollution, dirt; lewdness, licentiousness.
adj. (f. nāpöcᵘ̈), badly cooked, imperfectly cooked and consequently indigestible.
m. (sg. dat. napumsakas), a eunuch, one who is impotent (K. 617).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nopᵘ), to swindle or beggar (a person) (esp. by gambling), to rook (a person); to take dishonest bribes (for services the taker has no intention of rendering). Cf. nĕpun. ¶ nopᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nüpᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), swindled, rooked, as ab.; swindled into giving a bribe, as ab. ¶ napith thawun m.inf. to beggar another by swindling. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to beggar a person by swindling (esp. in gambling) or by taking bribes for some service that will never be performed.

m. a (hollow) reed (Śiv. 1806, K.Pr. 155); a reed generally, a reed-like plant (e.g. sugar-cane) (K.Pr. 155). -boṭhᵘ m. a bank covered by reeds. -gāsa m. a reedy kind of grass, a reed with leaves. -kaculᵘ or -kacur m. Zinziber zerumbet. -kônᵘ m. a stick of reed (such as that used for making a pen), a pen. -könⁱ dĕl m. the outer bark of the preceding. -könⁱ-kākaz m. the inner paper-like bark (lining the hollow pipe) of this stick-reed. -köñᵘ̈ f. a reed found chiefly in the Anchar lake, of which the weaver's brush is made (El.) (cf. gangañ). -nambal f. a reedy marsh, a marsh in which reeds grow. -pahörᵘ̈ f. a reed hut, a hut built of reeds. -pash m. a reed thatch. -poshᵘ adj. (f. -püshᵘ̈), (a house, etc.) possessing a thatched roof. -patulᵘ m. a reed raft. -wôñᵘ m. the water of a reedy marsh. ¶ nara-ganḍ m. a knot in a hollow reed; the length of reed between two knots. ¶ nȧrⁱ-khȧrⁱ 1 (for 2, see norᵘ) adj. c.g. (of land) covered with reeds and swamp plants. --khȧrⁱ gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become covered with reeds and swamp plants (esp. of land sown with rice, but which produces only reeds).

m. fire, light, flame (cf. bĕbi-nᵒ, p. 77b, l. 26; basa-nᵒ, p. 131a, l. 45; bȧṭhⁱ-nⁱ, p. 140b, l. 33; dramba-nᵒ, p. 245a, l. 43; gāsa-nᵒ, p. 307b, l. 42; kȧnḍⁱ-nⁱ, p. 455a, l. 25; kashᵃri-nᵃ, p. 481b, l. 36; mĕngan-nᵒ 1 and 2, p. 578a, l. 46, and p. 579b, l. 4; nabukᵘ nār, p. 619a, l. 42; nūna- nār, p. 640b, l. 48) (Gr.M.; W. 11; L. 460; L.V. 23, 25, 97; Śiv. 68, 118, 122, 417, 827, 948, 1685-6 Rām. 58, 93, 157, 186, 212, 257, 279, 1065 ff., etc.; H. iii, 4; YZ. 10, 60, 202, 307, 497, 514, 524; K.Pr. 3, 30, 60, 65, 101, 112, 125, 128, 137, 155, 204); met. rage, fury (cf. dana-nᵒ, p. 272, l. 11). --baḍāwun -- m.inf. to draw out the fuel from a cooking range (after cooking), to extinguish a fire. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to set fire (to a house), to commit arson (Rām. 179, 393, 407, 718); to light (firewood, etc.) (H. xii, 21-2, 24; K. 631). --gŏhun -- m.inf. a fire to be or become bright, (of a conflagration) to blaze up, increase in fierceness; met. (of prosperity) to show manifest increase. --ganḍun -- m.inf. fire to catch, fire to be kindled (Rām. 378, 507, 725); to set fire (to) (cf. lanḍis nār gᵒ, p. 526a, l. 1) (Rām. 715, 739); met. (as a disease) internal burning to attack (a person). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. a conflagration to occur to, fire to seize (such-and-such) (Rām. 103, 1014, 1169, 1560). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to draw a fire, to extinguish a fire (by withdrawing the fuel from a cooking hearth). --lagun -- m.inf. fire to catch, to be set on fire, to catch fire (K.Pr. 95). --shĕmun -- m.inf. a fire to be extinguished; met. passion, rage, a violent quarrel, or the like, to be assuaged. --shomᵘrun -- or shomᵘrāwun m.inf. to extinguish fire; to allay, or assuage, rage, passion, a violent quarrel, or the like. -shāntun m.inf. fire to go out, to be extinguished. --shö̃ʦᵃrun -- or shö̃ʦᵃrāwun m.inf. to extinguish a fire or a conflagration; met. to calm passion, rage, or the like. --trāwawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --trāwavüñᵘ̈ --), an incendiary (El.) (cf. --trāwun, Rām. 1386). --ʦhĕta gaʦhun -- m.inf. fire to become extinguished (Rām. 58, 1028; H. xii, 23). --ʦhĕwun -- m.inf. fire to be extinguished; passion, rage, etc., to be allayed. --ʦhẹ̆wᵃrāwun -- m.inf. to extinguish fire; to allay or assuage passion, rage, or a violent quarrel. --ʦāpun -- m.inf. 'to gnaw fire'; hence, to show unconquerable and violent energy in any work. --wahārun -- m.inf. a conflagration to spread. --wŏthun -- m.inf. fire to rise; a burning feverish sensation to be experienced; rage, passion, etc., to arise. --zālun -- m.inf. to make a fire, light a fire (Rām. 1069; H. iii, 1). ¶ nāra-bād m. N. of a certain unbearable disease, of which the symptoms include fiery rheumatism. -bāgay f. the fire-box of a stove, a fire-place. -brah or -brāh f. (sg. dat. -brüshᵘ̈ or -bröshᵘ̈), a high flame of fire, a pillar of flame. -brȧhⁱ f. a high flame of fire, a pillar of fire. -busar f. a torrent of blazing sparks (such as that from a rocket). -basta f. a blister caused by burning. -büṭhᵘ̈ f. the edge of the upper part of a stove (on which the burnt-out ashes are thrown). -dodᵘ adj. (f. -düzᵘ̈), burnt by fire (Rām. 1209). -damölⁱ f. the trampling of feet at a fire, the excitement (marked by people rushing about) at a conflagration. -drāv adj. c.g. issued from fire, purified by cleansing fires (K.Pr. 155). -dĕv 1 m. a fire-demon, a conflagration. -dĕv 2 m. (f. -dĕviñ), one who cowers over fire, a slave to the fire-place, a fire-worshipper. -gāh m. the glare of fire (esp. when this is visible but the fire is not itself seen); cf. -gāsh, bel. -gȧjⁱ or -güjᵘ̈ f. a stove full of fire, a cooking stove (in which food is actually being cooked), a furnace (K.Pr. 54). -gāsh m., i.q. -gāh, ab., q.v. -han f. a little fire, a small piece of fire handed to another, or a small fire collected together. -har f. a riot at the scene of a conflagration. -jōsh m. the heat of fire; met. (from the heat it gives forth) a filled portable brazier or kāngrī (kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈). -jōsh tapun m.inf. to warm oneself with a kāngrī. (This is done by keeping it close to the bare abdomen under the long nightgown-like garment worn by Kāshmīrīs); cf. -totᵘ, bel. --koḍᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --küḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), pulled out from the fire, purified by cleansing fires; (of a person) taught good manners, etc., by a course of abuse, beating, etc. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to pull out of the fire, to purify (e.g. gold or silver) by cleansing fire; to teach a person decent behaviour by abuse, etc. -kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a kāngrī (see kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈) or portable brazier filled with burning coals. -khŏḍ m. a fire-pit. -khal m. 'a fire threshing-floor', anything of metal or the like which is white or red hot. -kan m. a spark of fire. -kang m. a great blazing heap of fire (Rām. 1082 vr.l.). -krakh f. (sg. dat. -kraki), the outcry at a conflagration, the confused clamour on such an occasion. -kroʦhᵘ m. a fire-shovel. -kūṭᵘ m. a pillar of fire. -katurᵘ m. an earthenware basin or bowl (such as the bottom of a broken water-crock) filled with burning charcoal. -kyomᵘ m. a certain winged insect. (It suddenly issues from the forests, and is believed to be produced by forest-fires.) -lĕjⁱ or -lë̆jᵘ̈ f. an earthenware vessel with a cover, into which the burning charcoal is cast when withdrawn from a stove (at the end of cooking); cf. -lyolᵘ, bel. -lĕlⁱ-bata m. boiled rice, the grain of which has been dried by putting it outside such a jar as the -lĕjⁱ or -lyolᵘ (instead of drying it in the sun); cf. nārȧlⁱ họ̆khᵘ, s.v. nārȧlⁱ. -lyolᵘ m., i.q. -lĕjⁱ ab., but larger. -muhüjᵘ̈ f. an iron rod heated red hot (e.g. for boring a hole in wood). -muhulᵘ m. a terrible flash of lightning or a thunderbolt (looked upon as resembling a pestle). -mahanyuwᵘ m. a kind of man-shaped demon or spirit believed to give warning of a forest conflagration. (In former times he was believed to give warning beforehand.) -manan f. (sg. dat. manüñᵘ̈), a portable brazier (kāngrī). -mŏy f. a small fire. -nār m. fire on fire, a great conflagration, spreading on from place to place. -pahörᵘ̈ f. a temporary hut used by people whose home has been destroyed by fire. -pahur m. the building or rebuilding after a house has been burnt down (esp. when, as often happens, only the upper stories of a house, containing the living rooms, are burnt down). -pōr m. the new upper stories of a house, as rebuilt after a fire (the stone lower story remaining unharmed). -puran f. (sg. dat. purüñᵘ̈), the site of a burnt-down house (on which nothing has been rebuilt). -rĕh or f. a flame; the glare of fire. -thapul adj. (f. -thapüjᵘ̈), 'a fire-snatcher,' a man who plunders during a conflagration. -ṭhipᵘ̈rᵘ̈ m. a portable brazier (kāngrī) filled with a quantity of burning charcoal. -tĕmbᵃr f. a spark of fire (Rām. 1613). -traṭh f. (sg. dat. -traṭi), a lightning flash of fire, a very bright torchlike flash of lightning, a thunderbolt (El. nártraṭ). -totᵘ m. a scar caused by the use of the kāngrī or portable brazier. (It is carried for warmth under the clothes against the belly or thighs); cf. -jōsh tapun, ab. -tȧtⁱgaʦhȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. such scars to be formed. -tyū̃gul m. a spark, esp. a large one (El. -tĕngul, fire). -tyolᵘ m. a painful kind of blister or swelling. -ʦhaṭh f. (sg. dat. -ʦhaṭi), a burning wind-storm (said to be caused by contact with lightning); a flare projected from a fiery source (igniting objects at a distance). -ʦhẹ̆wᵃran f. (sg. dat. -ʦhẹ̆wᵃrüñᵃ), extinguishing (or trying to extinguish) a conflagration. -ʦhĕway f. the being extinguished of fire. -ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. great fierceness of fire. -ʦūr m. a fire-thief, one who privily sets fire to other people's houses, an incendiary. -wŏkhul adj. (f. -wŏkhüjᵘ̈), 'a fire trough,' one who, and without fear of being burnt, is always ready to heap up or collect fire. -wŏkhur m. raising up and down, i.e. stirring the burning mass of charcoal in a portable brazier (kāngrī). -wura f. a large stove, with many openings, such as is used for cooking meals for many guests on festive occasions. -wuzamal f. fire-lightning, blazing lightning (Rām. 482, 862, 1017). -wuziñ f. 'a fire-fount', the beginning of fire starting from some hidden place, the beginning of a burning sensation in the body. -zōwᵃran f. (sg. dat. -zōwᵃrüñᵃ), lighting a fire, nursing a newly lit fire. ¶ nāras narĕ diñĕ f. pl. inf. to refuse entirely.

adj. c.g. a man, a male (of any animal) (Gr.M., W. 17, Śiv. 1771); a male human being (K.Pr. 262); as adj. c.g. male, masculine (H. viii, 1). -kala adj. c.g. male-headed, bold, and intelligent (esp. of a child). --māda -- نر مادہ m. male and female; a hinge; a male and female screw; a certain medicinal plant (the tubers of which are said to grow in closely connected pairs, and are used as a tonic) (Aconitum heterophyllum, L. 74). -māda-kyulᵘ m. the pin of a hinge. -māda-tākh m. the square projecting part of a hinge. ¶ nara-nārāyĕn  m. Nara and Nārāyaṇa, originally regarded as identical (used hence as a N. of Krushna (Kṛṣṇa)), but also considered as distinct beings, Arjuna being identified with Nara and Kṛṣṇa with Nārāyaṇa (Śiv. 1618). -sing m. Narasiṁha, N. of the fourth incarnation of Vishnu (Śiv. 857).

m. a long chasm or narrow valley at the foot of a mountain (often overgrown with brushwood), a glen, a defile, the 'nullah' of Anglo-Indian parlance. The word is a frequent termination of local names (cf. RT.Tr., notes to viii, 595 and 959, and nörⁱ-wath, s.v. nôrᵘ); a precipice (El.). -bal m. such a 'nullah', esp. when possessing a stream or waterfall; N. of a place about 14 miles to the south-west of Śrīnagar, where there is a confluence of two mountain streams forming the Chaʦa-kŏl (q.v., s.v.) River. It is a sacred bathing-place of some repute (RT.Tr. II, 418).

or nārada, i.q. nārodᵘ, q.v. (K. 39, 172, 359, 573-4, 581, 628, 630, 749, 806, 918, 934, 964, 1000); esp. in the compounds nārad-munīshŏr, Nārada, the chief of sages (Rām. 1682, K. 47); nārada-munīshŏr (K. 355, 384, 386, 577, 582, 961); nārad-ryoshᵘ, Nārada the sage (Rām. 49, 144, 639; K. 817).
adj. c.g. (of wood or other fuel) causing (when burnt) an exceptionally fierce flame.
adj. c.g. manly, of a manly character.
adj. c.g. relating to hell, hellish, infernal.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. nāraladiñ), one who suffers from a conflagration, one who suffers heavy loss from his house having been burnt down, one who is burnt out of house and home.
in nārȧlⁱ họ̆khᵘ m. paddy (unhusked rice) dried by the application of artificial heat (as is done in winter when the sun has no heat). Cf. nāra-lĕlⁱ-bata, p. 648a, l. 4.
in nāram-nôrᵘ m. name of a certain medicinal creeping plant. When pounded it is applied to boils, etc.

m. a Kāshmīrī corruption of Nārāyĕn, q.v., generally used as a N. of the Supreme Deity (El. Narain) (L.V. 107, 109; Śiv. 1331; Rām. 79, 178, 226, 975, etc.; K. 14, 16, 58, 98, 113, 153, 173, etc.). The word is also a common proper name, as in Gr.Gr. 96, 97. -chiṭh f. (sg. dat. -chiṭi), a kind of cloth coloured with patterns of yellow and red, and specially used in religious worship.
m. or (Gr.M.) nārangī f. an orange.

or (m.c.) narāyĕn m. a N. of the god Vishnu (in Skt. Viṣṇu) (considered as the being who existed before all worlds, and who moved on the waters of creation (Skt. Nārāyaṇa). This word should properly be spelt nārāyĕn, with the first syllable long, but in poetry the first syllable is often shortened m.c., so that we find narāyĕn, e.g. in Śiv. 162, 796, 1101; Rām. 75, 145, 223, 970, 986, 988-9, 1478-9, 1751). The word is commonly used in Kāshmīrī as a name of the Supreme Deity, whether identified with Vishnu or not (Śiv. 700, 781, 1053, etc.; Rām. 846, 851, 984, 1157, 1704). Cf. nārān.
adj. c.g. dissatisfied, discontented (Gr.M.); unwilling; displeased, offended, affronted (Gr.M.).

m. a man or piece (in any game such as chess, etc.) (Gr.M., Śiv. 280); any game played with counters or pieces, such as backgammon, chess, draughts or causar (Gr.M.). ¶ narda-bāz m. a single game of chess, etc., as ab. -khorᵘ m. 'a gambler scald-head', a man who is a habitual or professional dicer (and hence with an evil reputation). -püṭᵘ̈ f. a chess-board or the like. -zörⁱ  m. a habitual or professional dicer, a gamester (and, as such, a rogue).
adj. c.g. possessing an arm, used --˚ as in okᵘ-narĕl, one-armed (p. 19a, l. 29).
m. a vessel made of an empty coco-nut.

adj. c.g. soft (to the touch), delicate, tender (Gr.M.); smooth, sleek (H. vii, 24); ductile, plastic; mild, tender (in disposition), peaceable (Gr.M., Śiv. 873); soft, low, subdued (of a sound); slack, depressed, dull (of a market, trade, or the like). -dil نرم دل adj. c.g. gentle, kind, soft-hearted (Gr.M.). -garm نرم گرم adj. c.g. neither very hot nor very cold, of moderate heat; mild and sharp, mild and rigorous, now forbearing and now severe; the good and the bad, the vicissitudes of fortune; (of the market of anything) sometimes rising and sometimes falling, sometimes in demand and sometimes not. -hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -hishᵘ̈), very soft (etc., in all the meanings of narm). -pahān adj. c.g. somewhat soft, moderately soft, a little soft (etc., in all the above meanings). --zamīn -- adj. c.g. soft soil; met. meek, tolerant, patient, submissive, long-suffering.
f. N. of a river in Central India, the Nerbudda of the maps.
m. 'the Lord of the Narmadā', a N. of Śiva (Śiv. 857).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. narmôwᵘ), to soften; to make mild, appease, assuage (a person's wrath). narmôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. narmövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made soft, appeased, etc., as ab.
f. softness, smoothness, sleekness (K.Pr. 167); pliancy; tenderness, delicacy, gentleness, mildness, civility (Gr.M.); want of firmness, tameness.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. narmyōv), to become soft; to become mild, gentle, appeased. narmyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. narmyē-müʦᵘ̈), softened; become mild, become gentle.

or nārud or nārad m. (in Hindū mythology) the N. of a divine Rishi (in Skt., ṛṣi) or Saint, regarded as one of the four sons of Brahmā, and one of the ten principal munis or rishis. He acted as a messenger between gods and men, was a friend of Krishna (Kṛṣṇa), a leader of the heavenly musicians, and the inventor of the vīṇā, or lute. In the story of Krishna he often appears as a kind of Tempter, leading on Kaṁsa and other evil people to further wickedness, so as to insure their destruction. He had a reputation for promoting quarrels by tale-bearing (false or true) (Śiv. 392, 631, 639, etc.; Rām. 590, 847, 943; K. 38, 296, 340, 358, 383, 387, 573, 584, 741, 896, 930-9, 1000); hence, anyone who makes quarrels, one who sets people at variance (esp. by tale-bearing, etc.).
adj. c.g., i.q. nā-rāz, q.v.; as subst., f. dissatisfaction, discontent; unwillingness; displeasure.
m. N. of a quarter in the city of Śrīnagar on the east bank of the river Vĕth (Jehlam). It was anciently known as Narēśvarīmaṭha.

m. (sg. dat. narakas), a hell, a place of torment (Gr.M.; Śiv. 122, 161, 417, 1539; Rām. 58, 366, 651, 1028, 1234; K. 495); the place to which souls go after death for judgment. --anun -- m.inf. to curse a dead enemy or villain (the curse being one which consigns him to hell). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come to hell, to fall into hell (after death). ¶ naraka-wösⁱ adj. (as subst., f. -wāsĕñ), one who dwells in hell, or fit to dwell in hell (Rām. 667, 1159). -wāsĕñ, see the preceding. ¶ narakukᵘ mĕnzur m. (f. narakücᵘ̈ mĕnzarĕñ), a wood- cutter of hell, a man who sells firewood in hell; hence, met. a vile, dirty, ugly, wretched fellow. ¶ narakunᵘ ʦȧkⁱwār m. one who has a hell-bowl; hence (used in curses) as miserable as one who lives in the lowest pit of hell.

m. a forked fishing-spear (the 'fork' consisting of several spikes) (L.V. 23, nāruʦᵘ); a hook (El. náruts). ¶ nārȧʦhⁱ-dan m. the shaft of a fishing-spear. -göḍᵘ̈ f. a fish caught on a fishing-spear. -kān m. the iron-forked point of a fishing-spear. -kȧnḍⁱ m.pl. the thorns, i.e. the forked points, of a fishing-spear.
f. a kind of reed used as a swamp fodder (L. 71, 359). Cf. also nar 1 and norᵘ.
adj. c.g. (of a garment) sleeved, in chiṭh-nᵒ, p. 166b, l. 45, and jā̃wār-nᵒ, p. 379b, l. 31.

f. the nose, i.q. nast, q.v. -dọ̆gᵘ m. snub-nosedness. -sēr f. bleeding at the nose. --ʦŏmbüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bore the nose. -ʦĕmburᵘ or -ʦĕmurᵘ adj. (f. -ʦĕmbürᵘ̈ or -ʦĕmürᵘ̈), snub-nosed. -ʦĕpoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦĕpüṭᵘ̈), flat-nosed. -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), having the nose cut off or slit. --ʦüṭᵘ̈ phērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the initial stages of a fight or quarrel to take place.

m. (sg. dat. nasakhas), punishment by mutilation (such as cutting of the nose, ear, finger, etc.); (in Kashmīr, also) punishment generally. --karun -- m.inf. to punish (esp. by mutilation). --kūrun -- m.inf. to spy upon a person (esp. an innocent person) as if he were guilty of some offence.

f. in the following: --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take unwholesome food (esp. when this is done by an invalid); cf. sạkrī. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. unwholesome feeding to occur (e.g. when an invalid is given wrong medicine or wrong food, with the result that he becomes worse).

adj. c.g. unworthy, improper, impertinent, rude; as subst. (with suff. of indef. art.), nā-sazāh m. an improper thing. nā-sazāh parun m.inf. to recite an improper thing, to use rude or impertinent language (Rām. 964).

m. destruction, ruin, perdition, annihilation (cf. ölⁱ-nⁱ, p. 23b, l. 25; dạthᵃri-nᵃ, p. 258a, l. 47; kŏla-nᵒ, p. 437a, l. 31; nẹ̆ndᵃri-nᵃ, p. 642b, l. 13) (Śiv. 91, 170, 311, 1818; Rām. 8, 1104; H. ix, 3; K. 796; K.Pr. 112); death; cf. nöshⁱ. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be destroyed, annihilated (Śiv. 268); so nāshĕs gaʦhun (K. 547). --karun -- m.inf. to annihilate (Śiv. 257, 347, 603; Rām. 170; K. 377, 872). ¶ nāshĕ-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), indestructible (Śiv. 736, 1387, 1736).

m. intoxication (lit. and fig.), drunkenness (W. 24); an intoxicating liquor or drug, an intoxicant; pride, arrogance. --āsun -- m.inf. to become, or be, intoxicated; to be intoxicated with pride. --khasun --  m.inf. intoxicating drink, etc., to get to the head, to be or become intoxicated (Śiv. 1874); the intoxication of pride to arise. -wothᵘ adj. (f. -vüʦhᵘ̈), one whose intoxication has descended (i.e. departed), sobered.
adj. c.g. (of a drug) intoxicating, producing intoxication, intoxicant.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. nashĕladiñ), one who is perpetually fuddled owing to the habitual consumption of intoxicants, a drunken sot.
adj. c.g. addicted to intoxicating drugs, a drunkard, a sot, an opium-eater, hashish-eater, or the like.
[] adj. c.g. destroyed, (of a ship) wrecked (Gr.M.).
m. (sg. dat. nāshĕkas), a destroyer (cf. kŏl-nᵒ, p. 437a, l. 1).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. nū̃ṭhᵘ or nūṭhᵘ or noshᵘ; 2 p.p. nashyōv. Cf. nỗṭhᵘ and nö̃ṭhun), to become destroyed, to disappear (Gr.Gr. 206, Śiv. 1255, K.Pr. 36); to go wrong, be spoilt, spoil; to be worn away, worn out (W. 156, K.Pr. 262). ¶ noshᵘ-motᵘ, nūṭhᵘ-motᵘ or nū̃ṭhᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nüshᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ or nǖ(nũ̄̈)ṭhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ ), destroyed; gone wrong, spoilt. ¶ nashĕnī impers. fut. part. c.g. it is to be destroyed, destruction is about to occur; (personally) destined to destruction, sure of eventual destruction. ¶ nashun m. destruction, in the following:-- nashĕn-bāna m. a vessel of destruction, i.e. fitness for destruction, showing every sign of imminent destruction.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nôshᵘ), to destroy, spoil, ruin (Rām. 1472, nöshⁱ for nöshᵘ̈).
f. (sg. dat. nạshᵉ̆rüñᵉ̆), destruction, causing to be lost or perished (Śiv. 338); spoiling. Cf. nöshᵉ̆ran.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nạshᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), i.q. nạshᵉ̆run, q.v. (Śiv. 1003). nạshᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. nạshᵉ̆rövᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), i.q. nạshᵒrᵒ- motᵘ, s.v. nạshᵉ̆run, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nạshᵒrᵒ), to destroy, to cause to be lost or perished; to spoil, mar; cf. nöshᵉ̆run, nạshᵉ̆rāwun, nöshᵉ̆rāwun. nạshᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. nạshᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), destroyed (by some one); spoiled.
m. luck, destiny (cf. kam-nᵒ, p. 442b, l. 16).
f. (sg. dat. nasīhüʦᵘ̈), advice, counsel, admonition, exhortation, precept (El., Gr.M., Rām. 827). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to advise, admonish (El., K.Pr. 149).
adj. c.g. a satyr; (in Kāshmīrī) monstrous, horrible, very bad.

or nasth f. (sg. dat. nasti. This word, especially in composition, often takes the form nas, q.v.), the nose (cf. khᵃñĕ-nᵃ, p. 405b, l. 1; muka-nᵒ, p. 559a, l. 32 (Gr.Gr. 66, 137; L. 462; Rām. 335, 929, 1268; YZ. 6, 449; K.Pr. 147, 155); the nose, or point, of a shoe or other pointed object. ¶ nasta-holᵘ adj. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), crooked-nosed, wry-nosed; cf. nasti-holᵘ, bel. -khanzar m. a 'nose-dagger', a well-formed nose (dagger-shaped, i.e. curved and thin). -mọ̆nḍᵘ m. a 'nose-stump', a thick coarse nose. -nasth  f. (sg. dat. -nasti), (of a pair of shoes) nose to nose, which is a bad omen foreboding a quarrel. -ʦhyonᵘ adj. (f. -ʦhë˘ñᵘ̈), having had the nose wholly or partly cut off; having a nose of such a shape that has apparently been cut off. -wöjᵘ̈ f. a nose-ring (worn by female Brāhmaṇas) (El.). -wājĕ-raz m. a gold chain connecting the ear with a nose-ring and partly supporting its weight. ¶ nasti-dọ̆gᵘ m. a (sudden) blow on the nose; met. causelessly raising another's rage. -ḍŏgurᵘ adj. (f. -ḍŏgürᵘ̈), a short globular nose. -dŏgis-pĕṭh rŏzun m. 'to remain (waiting) for a nose-blow', to seek for an occasion for enraging a person. -holᵘ adj. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), crooked-nosed, wry-nosed; cf. nasta-hol ᵘ, ab. -rᵃkh or -rikh f. (sg. dat. -rᵃkhi or -rikhi), a line on the nose, esp. when a person convicted of some fault makes a black line on his nose with his first finger, indicating, as it were, that if he ever commits the like fault again his nose may be cut off.

or nāsth f. (sg. dat. nāsti), snuff (according to El. most of the snuff used in the Valley is imported from Peshāwar. The home manufactured article is cheaper but much inferior; cf. kôshirᵘ̈ nᵒ, p. 481b, l. 50) (L. 464). Cf. nās. ¶ nāsti-chŏd f. (sg. dat. -chö̆zᵘ̈), craving for snuff (e.g. when a habitual snuff-taker is deprived of it). -ḍaba m. a snuff-box. -düjᵘ̈ f. a pocket handkerchief used by snuff-takers for wiping the nose. -gorᵘ m. a snuff-maker or -seller. -gȧrⁱ-wān m. a snuff shop. -gọ̆ʦᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a small bag for holding snuff, a snuff-bag. -khᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ f. the mucus expelled by snuff. -mushikh m.
