(sg. dat. mushikas), a pinch of snuff (L. 464, nást mushk). -phĕkh f. (sg. dat. -phĕki), 'snuff-powder,' as much snuff as can be lifted up in the hollow of the bent fingers. -phuṭᵃ̇jᵃ̇ f. a parcel of snuff (e.g. for use when travelling). -phuṭulᵘ m. a larger parcel of snuff than the foregoing. -phyokᵘ m., i.q. -phĕkh, ab. -phyoṭᵘ m. as much snuff as can be lifted on the ends of two or three fingers. -pūrⁱ f. a packet of snuff. -shōda m. a person addicted to snuff-taking, a slave to the habit. -shīshĕ m. a glass jar for holding snuff.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. nastöñᵘ̈), ugly nosed (whether long, thick, flat, cut off, or whatever its defect may be) (Gr.Gr. 137).
m. (sg. dat. nāstĕkas), an atheist, an unbeliever, a denier of the existence of supernatural beings.

adj. (pl. dat. nạstūrĕn, Gr.Gr. 56; f. sg. nom. nạstūrᵘ̈), flat-nosed, having a nose like a hoof, having a deformed nose (Gr.Gr. 56, 137). khᵃñĕ-nᵃ means having a nose plugged with mucus, see p. 405b, l. 4.
m. the N. used in schools for the letter na, when written in the Śāradā character. -nö karun m.inf. to say 'na, na', i.e. 'no, no' (coquettishly, or through modesty).
m. a running sore, an ulcer (W. 141, nāṣūr, 154, nāsur; K.Pr. 37).
or nasīyĕth (= نصیحت) f. (sg. dat. nȧsⁱyüʦⁱ or nāsīyüʦᵘ̈), advice, counsel, admonition (H. xii, 17). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give instruction (H. xii, l. 16).
in nata-nata adv. regularly, in regular system, by regular method (cf. aki nata aki laṭi, p. 20a, l. 42).
in nāṭā-ṭūṭī adj. c.g. imperfectly educated or trained (in any subject), an amateur. Cf. nāṭh.
adj. c.g. trembling, quivering (from fear, agitation, or the like); palsied.
or nôtuwān adj. c.g. weak, feeble (Gr.M.; H. i, 2).
m. a kind of small-sized earthen water-jar, globular in shape, with a narrow neck shaped like the ghaṛā of India, but smaller. Cf. noṭᵘ.
a nose, used in the compound nath-wöjᵘ̈ f. a nose-ring (W. 115).

m. (sg. dat. nāthas), a master, lord (L.V. 7); a common termination of proper names (esp. of gods or saints) as in amarnāth, see s.v., bōlānāth, see s.v., böravnāth, p. 130a, l. 7, dīnānāth, see s.v., all names of Śiva; dwārakā- nāth, p. 264b, l. 11, gōpī-nāth, p. 294a, l. 41, names of Kṛṣṇa; kamalaza-nāth, the lord who was born in a lotus, i.e. Brahmā (L.V. 8); sura- guru-nāth, the lord of the chief of the gods, i.e. the Supreme Śiva (L.V. 5, 65). So Śiv. 43, 66, 82, 168, 210, 438, 514, 536, 783, 1038, etc.

f. (sg. dat. nāṭi), flesh, the whole flesh of an animal (considered as food) (cf. drötⁱ-nⁱ, p. 249a, l. 50; nadȧrⁱ-nāṭa, s.v. nadorᵘ) (El. náṭá; K.Pr. 11, naṭān, misprint for nāṭan, 61 pl. nom., 155 id.); cf. nôṭᵘ 1 and nāṭā. -aḍijᵘ̈ f. flesh and bone, flesh with the bone. ¶ nāṭa-dĕgulᵘ m. a kind of earthenware cauldron for stewing meat. -dĕv m. (f. -dĕviñ), a 'flesh-devil', a gluttonous meat-eater. -jŏrāba m. a kind of stocking made of fine woollen yarn, covering the foot and ankle. --khasañĕ -- f. pl. inf. the fleshes to rise, to become fat (owing to prosperity, etc.). -khāv 1 adj. (as subst., f. -khöviñ), a habitual meat-eater (esp. one who eats it to excess). -khāv 2 m. N. of a certain disease in which the flesh (usually of the thighs and the neighbourhood) is corroded by dangerous sores. --ladañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to 'build fleshes', to swell with joy. -lë̆jᵘ̈ f. an earthen saucepan for cooking meat. -pash m. a thatch of meat, a dish filled up to the top with a covering of stewed meat. --vĕndañĕ -- f. pl. inf. great satisfaction to be experienced. --vẹ̆zᵃrañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to set a person to work over and over again without consideration of the labour involved. ¶ nāṭi-han f. a small piece of meat (K.Pr. 101); a helping of meat. -pholᵘ m. a bit of meat.
m. (sg. dat. naṭas), a dancer, a tumbler, a mime, actor, buffoon.

f. (sg. dat. naṭi), trembling, shaking, quivering (Gr.Gr. 66, Śiv. 1752, K.Pr. 149) (cf. nadᵃharüñᵃ nᵒ, p. 622b, l. 26); shaking palsy, paralysis agitans (cf. atha-nᵒ, p. 60b, l. 12). --aʦüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. shivering, trembling, etc., to attack a person (K.Pr. 246). --lāgüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to pretend shivering or trembling (e.g. to excite pity for apparent poverty). --naṭh -- f. severe continued trembling, shivering, etc. --ʦānüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause an attack of trembling, etc., to occur (e.g. by terrifying or the like); to cause oneself artificially to tremble, etc. (so as to excite pity in others).
f. a thread by which papers are tied together; hence, a file of papers (Gr.M.).
m. fruit, consequence, result, effect, inference (Gr.M.); moral (of a story).
f. the profession of an actor, buffoon, dancer, or the like. See naṭh 1.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. naṭiladiñ), afflicted with trembling (through fear, agitation, or the like); afflicted with palsy or paralysis agitans, palsied. Cf. naṭh 2.
f. the act of trembling, shaking, quivering (Gr.Gr. 120).
m. (sg. dat. nāṭakas), a drama, a theatrical play; a garden dinner party, a dinner of choice food given to friends in a flower-garden or similar pleasant place, a picnic.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. naṭyōv; according to El. there is also a 1 p.p. noṭᵘ), to tremble, quiver, shake, to be afraid (El.; Gr.Gr. 120; K. 80; K.Pr. 175, inf.pl.); to be agitated, to palpitate (cf. bindurᵘ nᵒ, p. 112a, l. 35; ḍimburᵘ nᵒ, p. 218b, l. 20) (Śiv. 1559). naṭān naṭān adv. shaking and trembling; esp. (with vbs. of speaking, asking, or the like) trembling with fear, apprehensively, timorously.
f. (sg. dat. nạṭᵃrüñᵃ), the act of causing to tremble (e.g. by frightening, threatening, or the like).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nạṭᵃrôwᵃ), to cause to tremble (e.g. by frightening, threatening, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 7); to wave (Gr.Gr. xli). nạṭᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. nạṭᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), caused to tremble, as ab.
adj. c.g. afflicted with trembling (through fear, agitation, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 120); afflicted with palsy or paralysis agitans, palsied.
? f. a period, time, turn; musical instruments, or drums, sounding at the gate of a great man at certain intervals (K.Pr. 67).
nā-umēdī نا أمیدی; see nā-wumēd, nā-wumīdī.
m. New Year's day according to the Persian calendar, counted by Musalmāns in Kashmīr as the beginning of spring (L. 325, 362).
f. 'new-belly', a buffalo with her first calf, exempt, under that name, from tax (L. 360).

card. (sg. abl., in comp., nawa 1; pl. dat. nawan), nine (El. nau, nauṅ, i.e. naũ; Gr.Gr. 76, 84; Śiv. 520, 893, 1469; Rām. 1258, 1281; H. iii, 8); cf. nam 2. -shĕth, card. (pl. dat. -shĕtan), nine hundred (Gr.Gr. 80, 84); nine pice (cf. p. 357b, l. 3). ¶ nawa-dār m.pl. the nine doors or apertures of the body, viz. the mouth, the two ears, the two eyes, the two nostrils, and the organs of excretion and generation (Śiv. 396, Rām. 23); a part of the procedure of the funeral decoration of a Hindū corpse, in which pearls are placed on each of the above nine orifices. -dwār m.pl. the nine orifices as in the preceding (Śiv. 340, 949, 1078, 1082; cf. Śiv. 520, 1469; Rām. 1769, 1783). -mara card. about nine (Gr.Gr. 84). -môsᵘ adj. (f. -mösᵘ̈), nine months old (Rām. 628); of, or belonging to, nine months. -mösyunᵘ adj. (f. -mösiñᵘ̈), nine months old, i.e. having completed nine months and in the tenth. -nö m. the name of the numeral figure 9 in the Śāradā character. -ryotᵘ adj. (m. sg. dat. -rĕtis; f. sg. nom. -rë̆ʦᵘ̈), nine months old, that which has completed nine months. -shrād m. the memorial ceremonies during nine days after a Brāhmaṇa's death, in which jars of water (increasing in number each day by one) are offered, and special offerings of food are made, on the fourth, fifth, ninth and tenth nights. -shotᵘ adj. (f. -shë̆ʦᵘ̈), (of cloth) woven with nine hundred threads forming side by side the width of the cloth. -shĕtukᵘ adj. (f. -shĕtücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the nine hundredth year, nine hundred years old. -shĕtyumᵘ ord. (f. -shĕtimᵘ̈), nine hundredth (Gr.Gr. 80). -shĕtyunᵘ adj. (f. -shĕtiñᵘ̈), costing nine hundred (rupees, etc.); fixed at nine pice (e.g. the amount of a regular payment or the like). -wuhurᵘ adj. (f. -warishᵘ̈), nine years old; lasting nine years. ¶ nȧvⁱ in nȧvⁱ nawaway, i.q. nawaway, bel., q.v. (Gr.Gr. 85). ¶ nawukᵘ adj. (f. navücᵘ̈), nine completed years old. ¶ nawan andar adj. c.g. 'among the nines', i.e. in the ninth year (of age, etc.). -hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, nine; costing nine (rupees, etc.). ¶ nawaway card. (acc. nawawanī; ag. nawawȧnⁱ), even the nine; cf. nȧvⁱ nawaway, ab. (Gr.Gr. 85). ¶ naway card. exactly nine, only nine, nine and no more or less (Gr.Gr. 84).

m. name, appellation (El., náo; Gr.M.; L. 462, nao; L.V. 15, 98; Śiv. 28, 30, 34, 214, 227, 243, 414, etc.; Rām. 317, 364, 368, 386, 539, 607, 622, etc.; H. ii, 1; xii, 4, 8, 18; K. 2, 3, 21, 92, 101, 116-17, 120-1, 124, etc.; K.Pr. 151, 261); good name, repute, reputation, fame, honour, renown; cf. nēkh-nāv (p. 629b, l. 13) and nām. --badal gaʦhun -- m.inf. change of name to occur, a person to be called by his wrong name. --bọ̆ḍᵃrāwun -- m.inf. to cause the name to sink, to disgrace one's name and that of one's family by evil conduct. --bāshun -- m.inf. to utter a name (e.g., in the Śrāddha ceremony, to utter the names of one's ancestors). --dār -- adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -dārĕñ), bearing a name, marked with a name (e.g. a medal); possessing a good name, of good repute; famous, famed. -dörī f. good repute, reputation, fame. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take a name, call out a name (as in taking a roll call) (K.Pr. 243); to take, keep, retain (the memory of) a name (Rām. 56, 271). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to pull out a name, to get a good reputation, suddenly to become famous; to defame (El.). --khārun -- m.inf. to raise a name, to elevate the name of one's family, to make a family famous by success, bravery, high office, or the like; to raise (upon the tongue), to take (on the tongue) (Śiv. 1908). --karun -- m.inf. to name (El., Rām. 85, 534, 1282, 1296). --nērun -- m.inf. a name to go forth, fame (or infamy) to be acquired (L.V.49; Śiv. 1133, 1353-4; K.Pr. 180, 248). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. a name to fall, a name to be given or gained (Śiv. 845, 892, 934, 996, 1007, 1384; Rām. 8, 120, 1456; K.Pr. 85). --thawun -- m.inf. to leave a reputation (good or bad) behind one (Śiv. 70, 357, 430, 709, 864; Rām. 7). --wālun -- m.inf. to bring down a name, to disgrace a name. --wasun -- m.inf. a name to descend, i.e. to be disgraced; a name to come down (in the world) (e.g. by poverty, disaster, or the like). --zēnun -- m.inf. to conquer a name, to win undeserved good repute (e.g. a low person marrying into a good family, or a person re- building a ruined temple that has been originally built by someone else, or completing a work of which another has done nearly all but which he did not finish). ¶ nāwa postpos. (governing the masculine ablative of the genitive), for the name of, for the sake of (W. 98, 152); by name (as in 'by name he is so-and-so') (Rām. 341). -boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), having a great name, famous, of high repute. -bajĕr m. greatness of name, high repute, fame. -kāḍay f. calling a person by various new names (e.g. in reproach or scolding, or in joke). -nāwa adv. name by name. -phēra m. change of name (e.g. by mistake to ask for a thing by a wrong name). -phiran f. (sg. dat. phirüñᵘ̈), giving a thing a new name. -phyurᵘ m. by mistake to give a thing the wrong name. -path nāwa adv. name after name (e.g. in calling out a list of names). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), nameless; as adv. , without naming, without mentioning. ¶ növⁱ adv. and postpos. in the name of; hence, for, as in myāni növⁱ (given) for me; cyāni nᵒ, for thee; tasandi nᵒ, for him; rāmani nᵒ, for Rāma. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to call by name, to mention (Rām. 1056); to extol. --hyonᵘ lāyĕkh -- adj. (f. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ lāyĕkh --), worthy of praise, praiseworthy.

(obl. nawa 2), i.q. nowᵘ, in the following:-- -böñᵘ̈ f. a collection of cooking vessels reserved for special occasions (such as religious festivals) and not for ordinary use. -gara adj. c.g. newly made, bran-new. -gorᵘ adj. (f. -gürᵘ̈), id. -jawān نوجوان c.g. a person in the bloom of youth, in the prime of life (Gr.M.). -phal m. the new crop (of grain, fruit, etc.), the grain or fruit just at the time of reaping or gathering. -sādan f. (sg. dat. -sādüñᵘ̈), a flux-powder (used by goldsmiths, coppersmiths, or the like). -shīn m. the new snow (falling at the beginning of winter). -shīn khārun m.inf. to bet on giving the first news of the new snow (this is a kind of betting competition); cf. the next. -shīn khasun m.inf. such a competition to take place. (The person who first sees the new snow puts it in a covered dish and offers it as a present to the other competitors. They have to give him a dinner or other agreed stake.) -sāl m., i.q. nawa-rĕh-sāl, bel. (Śiv. 1748). ¶ nawa-rĕh m. New Year's Day, the first day of the light half of the month of Tsithᵃr (Skt. Caitra = March-April) (L. 265). -rĕh bāgi adv. for the new year. -rĕh bôgᵘ m. a new year's gift (esp. that given to a female relative). -rĕh dŏy f. the second lunar day of the new year (on which, among Hindūs, no auspicious acts are performed). -rĕh sāl m. an invitation to a new year's feast (cf. nav-sāl, ab.). -rĕh tray f. the third lunar day of the new year (on which a married woman with her husband and children are feasted in their parents' houses) (L. 265, treh). -rĕh zang f. the good omen of the new year. (On New Year's Day a newly married couple are feasted at the bride's father's house, and omens taken for the new year.) -rĕha-kani adv. on or about New Year's Day. ¶ nawa-rĕhukᵘ adj. (f. -rĕhücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the new year. ¶ nawa-rĕhas-kyutᵘ adv. on the New Year's Day. ¶ nawan-bāna m. renewal.

f. a boat, a ship (cf. ḍēmba-nᵒ, p. 217b, l. 32; ḍāsa-nᵒ, p. 252a, l. 23; dasta-nāwa gaʦhañĕ, p. 256a, l. 43; ḍōṭha-nāv, p. 258a, l. 2; lari-nᵒ, p. 530b, l. 5) (El. náo; Gr.Gr. 48, 143; wāwa-nᵒ, p. 1172b, l. 33, zödⁱ-nāwa, p. 1217a, l. 21 L. 458, náo; L.V. 106-7; Śiv. 253, 516, 1683, 1719, 1801, 1805, 1830; Rām. 311, 789, 973, 1334; YZ. 107; K.Pr. 66, 208, 232, 254). --badal gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of a dead person) to come to life again (before the funeral ceremony) (cf. nāwa-badal, etc., bel.). --bọ̆ḍᵃrāvüñᵃ -- f.inf. to cause a boat or ship to sink. --baḍāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause a boat to set out, to weigh anchor. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a ship to be stopped, to run aground. --raṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to stop a ship, to bring it to anchor, to tie up along the bank (of the river). ¶ nāwa-badal or -bad ȧlⁱ f. coming to life again (before the funeral rites) (it being supposed that the messengers of Death have carried him off at the wrong time, and have had to rectify the mistake). -badȧlⁱ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to come to life, as ab. (cf. nāv badal gaʦhüñᵘ̈, ab.). -chān m. (f. -chöñᵘ̈ = his wife), a ship-carpenter, a ship- or boat-builder. -chönil f. the profession or occupation of ship- or boat-builder. -ḍokhᵘ or nāvi-ḍokhᵘ m. the reed mat, supported on movable sticks, used as an awning or flap-roof of a boat. -ḍakhijᵘ̈ f. the movable pole used for supporting the sloping mat flap-roof of a boat, when it is desired to raise or lower the outer edge; cf. nāvi-dȧchⁱ, bel. -ḍamb m. the womb of a boat, i.e. the middle part of a boat in which the cargo is carried. -dāñĕ m. boat-paddy, i.e. unhusked rice brought to market from the villages in boats. -ḍuvyunᵘ m. the sweepings of a boat, i.e. the dirty grain remaining in the bottom of the hold after removal of a grain-cargo; cf. ḍuviñᵘ̈. -gañĕr m. a crowd of boats massed together. -gāsa m. fresh grass (usually aquatic grass) brought in boats for sale as fodder. -gāṭh m. (sg. dat. -gāṭhas), a boat-wharf, a place where boats load or discharge their goods, or take on or leave passengers. -hönzᵘ̈ m. (f. -hanzañ = his wife, and also a woman following the same occupation), a professional boatman or sailor. -hönzil f. the occupation or profession of a boatman. -kāḍ m. the length of a boat. -kȧdᵃl or -kadal m. a boat-bridge, a bridge of boats. -kọ̆thᵘ or nāvi-kọ̆thᵘ m. the process of caulking a boat or ship. -kŏthurᵘ m. a boat- or ship-caulker. -më̆ʦᵘ̈ f. a soft white clay brought from the hills to the city in boats. -mŏzūrⁱ f. the money paid for the hire of a boat, or for freightage, or as wages to the boatmen, or for passenger fare, or the like. --nīrith gaʦhañĕ -- the boats to go forth; the necessity for doing something immediately to occur (quasi, to avoid missing the boats). -pash m. the planks that form the sides of a boat or ship, the strakes of a boat or ship. -püṭᵘ̈ f. a plank used for or usable for building a boat or ship. -rād m. the length of a boat or ship. -söl m. an excursion or pleasure trip in a boat. -söl khyonᵘ m.inf. to take a pleasure trip in a boat. -sār f. the cross-beam of a boat, from side to side. -sörᵘ̈ f. collecting (e.g. paddy, firewood, etc.) by boat, i.e. making a store of boatload after boatload. -tār m. crossing (a river, etc.) by boat, being ferried across, crossing (another) over in a boat (L.V. 98); ferry-hire (Śiv. 1201; K.Pr. 18). -törᵘ̈ f. delay of a boat, delay in the progress of a boat, or in its starting. -ʦraṭh m. (sg. dat. ʦraṭas), sea- sickness, vomiting or unhappiness (bodily or mental) caused by the violent motion of a boat in a storm. -wôlᵘ or nāvi-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a ship-owner. ¶ nāvi-ḍȧchⁱ f., i.q. nāwa-ḍakhijᵘ̈, ab. --daka dith gaʦhun -- m.inf. to give a push to the boat and go; met. to abandon one's house and home, to abscond, decamp. -ḍokhᵘ m. see nāwa-ḍokhᵘ, ab. --khasun -- m.inf. to go on board (a ship or boat). -kĕth loc. in a boat (Gr.Gr. 43, Śiv. 1589). kọ̆thᵘ m. see nāwa-kọ̆thᵘ, ab. -nam m. the prow of a boat or ship (according to El., s.v. nam, also the stern) (Śiv. 1840). -rᵃkh  f. (sg. dat. -rᵃkhi), the mark on the ship; hence, stupidity, silliness (in allusion to a fool who let a dish fall overboard from a travelling ship, and made a mark on the side of the ship at the place where it had fallen over. At the end of the journey, being asked where the dish was, he pointed to the mark on the boat, and said 'it fell over there'). -ʦopᵘ m. a little worn-out uncomfortable boat. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), i.q. nāwa- wôlᵘ, ab. --wôlᵘ-motᵘ-- perf. part. (f. --wöjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), brought down into the boat; made a proselyte, induced to join another person's religion or customs. --wālun -- m.inf. to cause a person to descend into the boat; to make a person a proselyte, to induce a person to adopt one's own religion or customs. --wasun -- m.inf. to descend into a boat or ship, to go aboard; to become a proselyte, etc., as ab. -wath f. (sg. dat. -wati), the ship road, the route by which a boat goes. --wothᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --wüʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), descended into a ship or boat, gone aboard; become a proselyte, one who has joined a new religion or set of customs.

m. newness, novelty, freshness (El. navir, Gr.Gr. 138); a novelty, new thing, discovery (Gr.M.). --chāwun -- m.inf. to enjoy newness, avail oneself of newness (e.g. to wear new clothes, live in a new house, etc.). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give newness, make as good as new (e.g. by polishing and putting in order something dirty or worn out). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take newness, to avail oneself of newness (e.g. as in --chāwun, ab., but with an added sense of appreciation). --raṭun -- m.inf. to take newness, to become as new (e.g. of something dirty or worn being polished or put in order).
m. good news, glad tidings (cf. navĕ-hondᵘ nᵒ, l. 9 ab.); invitation (to kinsfolk and brethren) to a wedding; (in Kāshmīrī) a humble offering (K. 1046).
adj. c.g. new, novel, fresh, recent.
m. (sg. dat. navĕtas), newness. Cf. nawuth.
adj. c.g. marked with the figure 9. Cf. nahᵃla.
m. a nawwāb, 'nabob,' the governor of a town or district, a viceroy.
m. environs, borders, suburbs; coasts, parts adjacent; (in Kāshmīrī) state, condition, circumstance, situation.
m. (sg. dat. nāwakas), an arrow (El. m.; in Hindōstānī the word is f.).
or nōwakh f. (sg. dat. nā(nō)waki ), a deep hole in a rapid mountain torrent, where there are eddies or where the water runs gently against the main current of the stream.

f. (sg. dat. navümᵘ̈), the ninth lunar day of a lunar fortnight (cf. hāra- nawam, p. 343b, l. 50). ¶ navümᵘ̈ dŏh adv. on the ninth lunar day. -hondu adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the ninth lunar day.
in nawam-nowuy adj. ever new and new (L.V. 93). Cf. nowᵘ 2.
adj. c.g. wanting in proper qualities.
m. coarse, broad tape (used to lace beds and to border tents, etc., with) (Śiv. 1859).
m. the office or post of the Government superintendent of forest timber. Cf. nawörⁱ.
f. (sg. dat. nawati), a roadless, pathless place.
f. (sg. dat. navᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), becoming new, becoming as good as new, gradually becoming renewed.
n.ag. (f. nawavüñᵘ̈), one who is becoming new; one who is being subject to renewal.
f. polishing, cleansing, scouring (cf. gar-nᵒ, p. 296a, l. 1).
f. the hire of a boat or ship, ferry-hire (Gr.Gr. 143).
in pāwah nāwai (K.Pr. 87). Read pāwanāway, see pāwanāwun.
f. (sg. dat. -wŏmīzᵘ̈), hopelessness, despair (for nā-wŏmīdī, q.v.) (Śiv. 420).
adj. c.g. hopeless, despairing (Gr.M. nā-ummēd); despairing (of, nishĕ with abl.) (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to disappoint, cause to despair.
m. the Government officer in charge of forest timber. Cf. nawāra 2.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. navyōv), to be or become new, to become new and new (Gr.Gr. 121, 240; Gr.M.; Rām. 994, 1769); to be fresh, gradually to become covered with fresh leaves; to be or become excessive, be prevalent (Gr.Gr. xli; Gr.M.; cf. nạgᵃr navüñᵘ̈, p. 624b, l. 37); to increase in vigour, etc., to flourish (Śiv. 1291); to be born (El. nauwun); (of a great event) to spring from a trivial cause. navyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. navyē-müʦᵘ̈), become new and new, ever becoming improved.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nôwᵘ), to cause to bathe, to bathe (something) (Śiv. 24, 1057, 1351, 1397, 1489; Rām. 676, 947, 991, 1031, 1235, 1292, 1726, 1772); to purify (Rām. 1625, with fire); to polish, cleanse (metal), to rub, scour (lit. and met.) (L.V. 93; Śiv. 534, 1711, 1786, 1826; K. 973). nôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. növᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), bathed; cleansed, polished, scoured.
m. (sg. dat. nawatas), newness; the becoming new or as good as new, renewal. Cf. navyuth.

(for 1, 2, and 3, see p. 618a, ll. 38, 42, 50)  f. (pl.dat. nayĕn 1, for 3 see s.v.), a reed, cane; a tube, a pipe (cf. khāra-nᵒ, p. 407b, l. 46); a flute, a fife (H. vii, passim). -shĕkar نی شکر m. sugar cane (El., Gr.M. naishĕkar). --wāyüñᵘ̈ -- to play the flute; to follow eagerly.

f. (pl. dat. nayĕn 2), a hill forest (Śiv. 962, 1024, 1571, 1600, 1681, 1883); (according to El.) a flat, wide, cultivated headland in the mounds (? mountains) (El. naih) (K.Pr. 156). nayĕn phērun m.inf. to wander about in a hill forest.
adj. c.g. not to be found or got, unprocurable, unattainable (K.Pr. 76).
m. (sg. dat. nāyĕkas), a leader, the headman (of a village or the like), a foreman, overseer (Śiv. 201, 1536).
(for 1, 2, see nay 4, 5) m. the eye (used esp. with reference to a beautiful eye, etc.).
f. a barber's wife (H. xi, 19). Cf. nöyid.
m. a cane-brake, a reed-bed (H. vii, 26-9).
m. (sg. dat. nāyĕkis), a boatman, a sailor.

m. blandishment, coquetry, amorous playfulness, feigned disdain; fondling, coaxing, dalliance, toying; pride, whims, airs and graces; coaxing, kind words (H. ii, 7). --bōzȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to listen to blandishments, to accomplish or carry out (another's) desires. --hĕnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to accept blandishments, to indulge whims, humour. --karȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to show pretended distaste, to coquet; to coax (in order to get something) (K.Pr. 156). -parward (= ناز پروردہ) c.g. delicately brought up, one who has been delicately brought up, a spoilt child (Rām. 487). ¶ nāza-thürᵘ̈ f. a flirt, coquette. ¶ nāzücᵘ̈ thürᵘ̈ f. a flirt, coquette. ¶ nāzan kharīdār āsun m.inf. 'to become a purchaser of blandishments', i.e. sought for assistance to be found (in the carrying out of some desired object), one's desires to be fulfilled (by some one). Cf. Śiv. 1665.

f. sight, vision, view (Gr.M.; W. 13; Rām. 536, 1193; K.Pr. 38); look, regard, glance (Rām. 457, 848, 1168; H. vii, 13; viii, 6, 11; xii, 23; YZ. 185, 450; K.Pr. 23); favourable regard, countenance; view, opinion, estimation (Gr.M.); regard, relation, reference; influence of an evil eye (cf. bad nazar, p. 81b, l. 21) (K.Pr. 55). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to apply the vision, to inspect, regard, look, look about (Śiv. 767; Rām. 1365, 1396). -guzar نظر گذر f. the passing of the eye over something, taking a look at, examining; the influence of a malignant eye. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to observe, inspect, watch (H. ii, 1; x, 7, 8; xii, 23). --pilüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the vision to reach, to be able to see (so far as such-and-such) (Śiv. 785). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to fall under notice, to come under notice; to chance to see. --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to look (upon), regard, set eyes (upon); to keep the eye (upon), to watch, guard (K.Pr. 247); to look (after), attend (to); to be intent (upon); to cast a wistful eye (upon); look sweet (upon). --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to throw a glance, cast a glance (upon), to look up (Śiv. 17, 509, 514, 902, 918, 958, 1034, 1099, 1820, 1878; Rām. 370, 1287, 1294; YZ. 224). ¶ nazari onᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. --üñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), brought under view. --anun -- m.inf. to bring under view, take a look at; --bĕhun -- m.inf. to sit for looking, to sit in watch (H. x, 7). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to come into view (esp. unexpectedly). --koḍᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --küḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), criticized, commented on, passed under review. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to criticize, comment on, pass under review. --khasun -- m.inf. to be approved of, to be highly appreciated. --khotᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --khüʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), approved (of), liked, highly appreciated. -tal onᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. -tal üñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), brought under view. -tal anun m.inf. to bring under view. -tal āsun m.inf. to be borne in memory. -tal thowᵘ-motᵘ or -tal thôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. -tal thü(thö)vᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ ), put into mind, put into memory, kept in mind. -tal thawun or -tal thāwun m.inf. to put into memory, to keep in memory.
m. a watcher, a watchman, a detective (H. ii, 1; x, 7, 8; xii, 23).
n.ag. (f. nazavüñᵘ̈), spoilt by having parts broken, shaky, unstable (from this cause).
or nȧzⁱdīkh (Śiv. 22), postpos. (governing dat.) near (to) (W. 97; H. viii, 10); adj. or adv. near (Śiv. 22, 110, 328, 370, 443; Rām. 798, 1664; K.Pr. 203). Cf. nīzīkh.
an example, instance, specimen, in bē-nazīr, incomparable (p. 115a, l. 14; Gr.M.).
m. (of food, etc.) liable to cause rheum or cold.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. nazyōv), to become shaky, unsteady, loose, or out of shape owing to breakage. nazyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nazyē-müʦᵘ̈), become shaky, etc., owing to breakage.
m. (sg. dat. nāzanas), the hoping (owing to heedlessness or laziness) that some work will be undertaken by some one else, to thrust a burden on to some one else's shoulders. Cf. nāzanun.
m. rheum, cold, catarrh (Gr.M. nazal; L. 459, a cough). nạzla-shōr m. a bad state of health resulting from rheum, severe illness caused by such.
f. a thin delicate woman (El. also náznún); a belle, a beautiful woman (Rām, 519, YZ. 30); a mistress, sweetheart, beloved woman; m. a beautiful youth (YZ. 9, 248).
m. (a female dancer is naʦiñ, q.v.) a professional male dancer.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. naʦanôwᵘ), to cause to dance, to set dancing (K. 951, 957; K.Pr. 14). naʦanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. naʦanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), one who has been set dancing.
f. dancing, the act of dancing (Gr.Gr. 128).
n.ag. (f. naʦavüñᵘ̈), one who dances, a dancer (K. 922).
dancing (K.Pr. 159); whirling or throwing the body or the limbs of the body (as in joy, despair, rage, agitation, or similar circumstances).
f. (a male dancing as a male is naʦal, q.v.), a female professional dancer, a nautch-girl (K. 957); a male dancer in woman's dress and acting a woman's part; dancing, the act of dancing (Gr.Gr. 120).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. noʦᵘ, f. nüʦᵘ̈ 2, for 1, see s.v.; 2 p.p. naʦōv. This verb is impersonal in the past tenses), to dance (cf. bangi- manz nᵒ, p. 113a, l. 5) (Gr.Gr. 120; Gr.M.; L. 459; L.V. 94; Śiv. 1104, 1443, 1454, 1463, 1662, 1668, 1724-5, 1874-5; K. 98, 442; K.Pr. 26, 83, 156, 235, 238); to caper, frisk about; to bound, jump up and down. --phĕʦun -- m. only a small amount (of things required in large quantities for the execution of any work) to remain available, to be nearly all used up. ¶ nȧʦⁱ nȧʦⁱkhyonⁱ m.inf. heedlessly to squander inherited or acquired property (K.Pr. 135). ¶ naʦan-thurungᵘ m. a single turn in dancing; (of an animal, a ball, a river-course, etc.) a bound round or a sudden twist round. -thurungᵘ dyunᵘ m.inf. to cause to turn round suddenly, as ab. -vil f. the time of dancing, an occasion for or opportunity for dancing; a single turn or revolution of the body.

a prefix used in the formation of compound words, indicating 'not', 'without', as in nĕ-gorᵘ, not manufactured, naturally formed; nĕ-pŏturᵘ, having no son; nĕ-kama, useless. It is the equivalent of the Sanskrit niḥ. Words with this prefix will be found in their proper alphabetical order.

m. a trace, mark, token, clue (K. 268, 284-5, 1162); a person's address. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give a clue, to give the address (of). --nishāna -- m. a mark or token (which affords a clue). --rōzun -- m.inf. a trace or clue to remain (behind), a trace to be left. --thawun -- or --thāwun -- m.inf. to give or point out a clue (Śiv. 1878); to promise (to visit a person) (Gr.M.). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. a trace to come, a clue to be obtained. ¶ nēba-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who has given a clue. ¶ nēbas gaʦhun m.inf. to follow up a clue. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to come upon a clue, hit upon a clue. --wôtᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --wöʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈--), one who has found a clue. --wātun -- m.inf. to arrive at a clue, to find a clue.
adj. (f. nĕbagörᵘ̈), cooked without oil or ghī (cf. bagāra) (W. 110).
m. the act of defæcation (a back formation from nĕbar nērun, see nĕbar 2); human ordure.

adv. outside, without (Gr.Gr. 152, nẹ̆bᵃr, q.v.) (Gr.M.; W. 95; Śiv. 766, 866, 991, etc.; H. iii, 8; viii, 7; x, 7; K. 664); out of doors (Gr.M.); abroad, not at home (L.V. 4); cf. andar-nᵒ (p. 32a, l. 49). As postpos. governing either the abl. or else the abl. with nishĕ (Gr.M.; W. 97 says it governs dat.), outside, beyond (cf. khala-nĕᵒ, outside the universe, p. 397a, l. 21; hada-nishĕ nĕᵒ, beyond limit, p. 322a, l. 29); (governing dat.) to outside (H. x, 5). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go outside; to become well known (Rām. 167). -kun adv. to the outside, outwards (El., Rām. 481). --karun -- m.inf. to put outside, to draw out (El.); cf. andᵃryumᵃ nĕbar karun, to turn inside out (p. 33a, l. 3). --nērun -- m.inf. to go forth outside, to go outside (K.Pr. 30, 102; Rām. 167, 174, 299, 390, 467-8, 669, etc.); to go outside (school, etc.), i.e. having finished one's education to take public or other service; to go outside the house (to ease oneself), to defæcate. -pahān adv. a little outside, somewhat outside, just outside. ¶ nĕbȧrⁱ adv. outside, externally, etc., i.q. nĕbar, but more emphatic (Śiv. 764, 1807). -kinⁱ adv. outside (Rām. 1558).

a form of nĕbar 2, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 152), used in the following:--nẹ̆bᵃr-drövī f. a habit or custom of going about the town and meeting friends, etc.; the habit of acting as a secret light woman, who visits her lover privately. ¶ nẹ̆bᵃra adv. or postpos. governing abl., from outside, outwards (cf. ạndᵃra nĕᵒ, p. 32b, l. 8) (W. 95, nebara; 98, nebarạ; L.V. 94; K. 493, 899, 1129, 1141); outside, outwardly (K.Pr. 156). --drāv --  adj. c.g. (W. 21), one who makes a habit of going outside the house and meeting, or gossiping, with friends; f.  an unchaste woman who is in the habit of going privately out to her lover or lovers. ¶ nẹ̆bᵃ̇rᵃ̇ adv. and postpos. governing abl., outside; at the outside edge (of), on the frontier (of some country) (K. 619). --ʦȧmⁱ -- adv. 'on the outer skin' (without considering what is inside); hence, unsuitably, with unpleasant results (esp. u.w. vbs. implying 'eating', 'enjoying', or the like; c.g. with reference to eating tempting but unwholesome food). -ʦȧmⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to become unsuitable, to have unpleasant results, as ab. -ʦȧmⁱ karun m.inf. to lead a person to action which has unpleasant results, as ab.

adj. (f. nẹ̆bᵃrimᵃ), outer, external (El. nebrum; Gr.Gr. 152; Śiv. 1355, 1821; Rām. 1658; K. 983; K.Pr. 13); one who has gone outside (from school, etc.), i.e. one who, having finished his education, has taken public or other service (K.Pr. 156). The converse is ạndᵃryumᵃ, q.v. --mahanyuwᵘ -- m. an external man; a man who has left his home (for public service, business, or the like); hence, a good business man, a man of the world.
adj. good (L.V. 35); as adv. well, successfully, fortunately (L.V. 37). Cf. nēkh.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nēchanôwᵘ), to give (a person or thing) a high reputation, to extol; cf. nēchawun and nēchō-motᵘ. nēchanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nēchanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), extolled.

or nĕchapạtᵘ̈rᵘ̈  f. an almanac (cf. bösⁱ-nĕⁱ, p. 131b, l. 34) (Gr.M.). ¶ nĕchapatri-kūṭᵘ̈ f. a kind of almanac (not like a book with pages, but written on one side of a long strip of paper which is kept in a roll). -pūthⁱ f. an almanac (in book form). -warukh m. (sg. dat. -warakas), a single leaf of an almanac.
m. a lunar asterism or mansion, i.q. nĕchotᵘ; the season during which the sun, or the moon, is passing through a lunar mansion; hence, a time or moment fixed by astrology (L.V. 3). Cf. nĕshⁱtur.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nēchowᵘ), to give (a person or thing) a high reputation, to extol, proclaim, i.q. nēchanāwun. Cf. nēchōmotᵘ. ¶ nēchowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nēchüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), extolled. ¶ nēchawana āmotᵘ perf. part. pass. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), one who has become extolled, one who has gained universally a high reputation. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. pass. to become extolled, to gain universally a high reputation.
adj. (f. nēchēmüʦᵘ̈), one who has achieved a high reputation; one who is endowed with a virtuous disposition. Cf. nēchawun and nēchanāwun.
m. an asterism in the moon's path, a lunar mansion. There are twenty-seven of these. Cf. nĕchatur and nĕshⁱtur.

m. a boy, a man-child, a lad (El. nechú) (cf. bōlāki-nĕᵒ, p. 105b, l. 39) (Gr.M.; W. 18, 110, and L. 464, nechu; Śiv. 326; Rām. 128; K. 559, 941; K.Pr. 156, 215); a son (cf. baṭa-nĕᵒ, p. 138, l. 40; khāra-nĕᵒ, p. 407b, l. 45) (Gr.Gr. 14, 136; W. and L., as ab.; Śiv. 1331; Rām. 695-9, 859, 965, 1375; H. iii, 9; v, 2; viii, 3, 11, 13; xii, 1; K. 137, 458, 734, 741-2; K.Pr. 107, 137, 145). ¶ nĕcivⁱ-dôdⁱ m. son-pain, i.e. the pain of childlessness, longing for a son. -han f. a little son, an only son; esp. a darling only son (W. 112, nechiuhun). -khã̄dar m. the marriage festival of a person's son. -lạgᵃn m. the wedding of a person's son (esp. u.w. ref. to an invitation to such). -mahanyuwᵘ m. a male child, a son. -mŏy m. a single little son, a baby boy child. -sondᵘ sg. gen. (f. -sünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a son. -sọ̆ñᵘ m. the father of the bridegroom (from the point of view of the bride's father) or the father of the bride (from the point of view of the bridegroom's father) (the two fathers-in-law are called 'sọ̆ñᵘ' to each other). -sŏñĕñ f. the mother of the bridegroom (from the point of view of the mother of the bride) or the mother of the bride (from the point of view of the mother of the bridegroom), the two mothers-in-law being sŏñĕñ to each other. -wājĕñ f. the mother of a good son (Gr.Gr. 136); (at a wedding) the mother of the bridegroom (as distinct from the mother of the bride). -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ, see ab.) one who has a son (i.e. a real son), the father of a good son (Gr.Gr. 136); (at a wedding) the father of the bridegroom (as distinct from the father of the bride).
m. a person's previous experiences (past and done with). --phirȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to detail one's previous experiences (in order to excite pity).
adj. (f. nĕdöjᵘ̈), unmarked, without mark or blemish, faultless, unobjectionable. Cf. dāg.
or nidān 1  m. stored treasure, a treasure (Śiv. 58, 520, 893).
or nidān 2 m. a false tale, an imaginary story, a work of fiction, a fairy tale, a fable. --lāyun -- m.inf. to spread abroad a false tale.
or nidān 3 m. a primary cause, the first or essential cause (Śiv. 808).

m. a horrible vision conjured up by insanity or the like and indicating the approach of death. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to be in a state of utter misery which can only end in death. --hāwun -- m.inf. to show a person such misery, or to serve as an example of such, as a warning of the consequences of evil conduct. --wuchun -- m.inf. to recognize such misery (in oneself or another, as the result of evil conduct).

or nĕdôrᵘ (= نادار) adj. (f. nĕdörᵘ̈), wanting strength, wanting durability (cf. dār 3); wanting in endurance, wanting in patience (cf. dörī 1); wanting the necessities of life, poverty-stricken. Cf. nādār.
adj. (f. nĕdyörᵘ̈), without wealth, without money, poverty-stricken. Cf. dyār.
adj. (f. nĕgürᵘ̈), not made, not fashioned (e.g. a stone mortar in its natural condition and not worked into shape).

f. sleep (of mankind or beast) (K. 91); the closing or sleeping of a flower. ¶ nĕha drāv adj. c.g. one (man or beast) whose sleep has vanished, or (of a flower) which has begun to open. -gaṭa f. darkness during sleep-time, darkness in night-time. -phŏli adv. at the flowering from sleep, at the flowering of dawn, at dawn (Gr.Gr. 156, where a word nĕha-phọ̆lᵘ, break of day, is also given).

f. absconding, running away to a distance, in the following:-- nĕh anüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to chase to a distance [K.Pr. 25, wrongly translated to bring people (to prayer)]. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to flee to a distance.

m. short warmth (as when the sun breaks for a short time through the clouds); a short display of brilliant power, a miraculous action (Rām. 1099); a temporary display of any virtue or the like (Rām. 1619).
adj. c.g. prosperous, flourishing (L.V. 24, Rām. 1653); rich, wealthy (K. 1104); pleased, happy.
for nĕhölⁱ, q.v., in hāka-nĕᵒ, p. 326b, l. 26.

f. a seedling (for transplanting), young plant, shoot, sucker; a rice-nursery (in which seedlings are grown) (L. 331, 463, niháli). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to plant cuttings, saplings, or the like; to transplant seedlings. --thôpᵘ -- m. a bundle (as much as can be grasped in the hand) of seedlings, etc., for planting out. ¶ nĕhāli-dāñĕ m. rice which is transplanted (not sown broadcast). -ḍūrᵘ m. a seed-bed in which plants are sown for transplantation.

m. a veil, hood, covering (for the face); (in Kāshmīrī esp.) the long veil (like a burqa') worn by respectable women. -düjᵘ̈ f. the part of this veil which covers the face (with a network in front of the eyes). (It is separable from the rest of the veil.)
adj. c.g. without work, unemployed, idle; unserviceable; useless, worthless, good-for-nothing; not fond of work.

adj. and adv. good, virtuous, excellent (K.Pr. 157); kind, gentle (K.Pr. 35); as adv. well; very, exceedingly; cf. nēch. -bakhtī 1 نیک بختی adj. c.g. of good or happy lot, fortunate, happy. -bakhtī 2 نیک بختی f. good fortune, happiness. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become good, to turn out good. -nāv (= نیکنام) famous, illustrious (El.). -pūrᵘ m. wish, desire (Rām. 1034). -pūrᵘ aʦun m.inf. desire to enter, desire to be experienced (esp. desire acquired for something not previously wished for). -pūrᵘʦānun m.inf. to cause desire to enter, to experience desire (for something previously not wished for). --sapazun -- m.inf. to become good, to turn good. ¶ nēka-pākh adj. c.g. (of a story, occurrence, etc.) containing happiness and sorrow, vice and virtue, and so on.
adj. (f. nĕkhüpᵘ̈), uneducated, unskilled, clumsy, awkward (in any work).
adj. (f. nĕkörᵘ̈), ugly, unsightly. --bĕkôrᵘ -- adj. (f. nĕkörᵘ̈ bĕkörᵘ̈), id.
nikᵒṭᵒ, or nikuṭᵘ adj. (f. nĕküṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. nĕkacĕ, and so on), very small, tiny (of a thing or living being, e.g. a child) (K. 106).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. nēkyōv), to become good, to take to good behaviour (of one previously ill-behaved), to become reformed. nēkyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nēkyē-müʦᵘ̈), one who has become well-behaved; a reformed character.

m. rule, principle, regular practice (of anything), custom, rule (Gr.M.); religious observance (cf. nĕti-nēma- kinⁱ, s.v. nĕth 2) (Śiv. 1111, 1213, 1532); a vow, the keeping of a vow; cf. nĕyĕm. -darm m. (among Hindūs) virtuous conduct consisting in (or associated with) all the various religious ceremonies and obligations. --karun -- m.inf. to perform the rule, (among Hindūs) to live according to Hindū religious rule; to make a rule, to make over something for a certain purpose, to devote (Gr.M.). --rachun -- m.inf. to adhere to custom. --thawun -- m.inf. to carry out a vow, to perform a promised vow; to carry out a vow (in the sense of carrying out a fast, a religious duty, or the like). ¶ nēma-boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), one who has become eminent by the long and strict performance of austerities, fasts, or the like. --pyōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --pyēmüʦᵘ̈ --), fallen from the rule, i.e. one who has given up attending to some rule, performing a fast, regularly performing Hindū religious duties, or the like. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to give up performing duties (as ab.). -rostᵘ adj. and adv. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), one who does not follow the usual and obligatory religious observances; without order, without discipline (Gr.M.); as adv. without rule, irregularly. -sostᵘ f. (-süʦhᵘ̈), one who habitually performs proper religious observances. -wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is particular in carrying out religious observances. ¶ nēmukᵘ sg. gen. (f. nēmücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, religious observances, etc.
m. an invitation (to a feast, etc.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nĕmontrᵘ), to invite, issue an invitation (to a feast or the like).
f. (sg. dat. nĕmüʦᵘ̈), an intimation, indication, direction, trace, clue, hint. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give an indication, to hint, direct. --wanüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to explain a reason (for). Cf. nĕmȧtⁱ.
f. (sg. dat. nēmüʦᵘ̈), comfort, convenience, ease; a benefit, favour, boon, blessing (K.Pr. 206, níámat); a delicacy, dainty.

adv. and postpos. because (of), by reason (of); for the benefit (of); for the purpose (of); for the sake (of), for (Rām. 1057, Nārān nĕᵒ, for the sake of Nārāyaṇa, for God's sake!); on account (of), with a view (to). Cf. nĕmath.
Pahlavī nemāj) f. prayer, adoration, worship, divine service (El. namāz; K.Pr. 89, 157); esp. the prayers prescribed by Musalmān law, which are said five times a day.
or ñĕmazŏla c.g. or nĕmazọ̆lᵘ (f. nĕmazŏ̈jᵘ̈) adj. very indolent, lazy, torpid, sluggish, laggard.
m. the noise made in chewing food.
m. a person who prays, one who habitually follows the rules for Musalmān prayer (K.Pr. 204).
f. a kind of stone mortar (in which Indian hemp or the like is pounded).
or nĕnum a jingle of anam or anum, q.v., in the compound anam-nĕnam or anum-nĕnum.
f. a piled-up large heap of stale boiled rice (solidified owing to its staleness) (cf. bata-nᵒ, p. 137a, l. 34, and nĕng 1).

f. (sg. dat. nĕndi), the weeding of a rice-field (L. 327-8, 464, nind, ninda, 456; Śiv. 1111, 1532; K.Pr. 10); (cf. atha-nĕnda, p. 60b, l. 6; dal-nĕnd, p. 209b, l. 16; gupan-nᵒ, p. 294b, l. 40; kach-nᵒ, p. 383a, l. 44). ¶ nĕnda-cŏbur m. (sg. dat. -cŏbaras), a man who is energetic at weeding. -drāv  adj. c.g. that which has issued from weeding, (a field) that has been weeded. -kāb m. food brought in a cauldron to the field for the people engaged in weeding (cf. قاب). -kād or -kādᵃr m. a man engaged to work at weeding. ¶ nĕndi drāmotᵘ  perf. part. (f. drāmüʦᵘ̈), (a field) of which all the weeding has been completed. --koḍᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --küḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), id. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to draw out from weeding, the weeding of a field to be completed. --wasun -- m.inf. to begin the weeding (of a field).
m. (as subst., sg. dat. nĕndakas), blaming, reproachful; censorious, abusive, scurrilous.

m. (sg. dat. nĕndanas), a certain vegetable (described as having round leaves and a long sweet stalk). --wŏsta-hākh -- m. (sg. dat. --wŏsta-hākas --), a certain stew made up of the two vegetables nĕndun and wŏsta-hākh. ¶ nĕndan-bạrᵃg  m. the leaf of the nĕndun plant. -wŏsta-hākh m. (sg. dat. -wŏsta-hākas), i.q. nĕndun wŏsta-hākh, ab.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nyondᵘ), to blame, reproach (K. 1053).

f. sleep (müʦᵘ̈ nẹ̆ndᵃr, deep sleep, see motᵘ 1) (Gr.Gr. 136; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1311, 1512, 1631; Rām. 674, 908, 1059, 1104; H. v, 6; K. 94, 119, 601; YZ. 34; K.Pr. 35, 95, 139, 154, 189, 253); cf. nāga-nᵒ, p. 624a, l. 29. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to sleep (El.; H. v, 6; K. 605-6; K.Pr. 257). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. sleep to fall, to become overwhelmed with sleep, to fall asleep (Rām. 872, 1175; H. v, 5, 7; YZ. 92, 153). --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- m.inf. to betake oneself to sleep, to be asleep (Śiv. 861, 1702). ¶ nẹ̆ndᵃri-ȧchᵃ f. a sleepy eye, an eye that cannot keep open owing to sleepiness. -ḍing or -ḍingir f. a short sleep, a doze (cf. ḍingir). -dĕv  m. a sleep-demon; hence, sleeping sickness, a disease marked by excessive sleep night and day; a person who is habitually a great sleeper. -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), attacked by sleep, sleepy (Gr.Gr. 136); sound asleep (L.V. 32; Śiv. 998, 1661, 1866; YZ. 47); (of a flower) closed, asleep. -haʦar m. sleepiness; the condition of sound sleep; the closed condition (of a flower). -magᵃn adj. c.g. plunged in deep sleep. -mōth m. (sg. dat. -mōtas), sleep-death, a very sound sleep (such that no sound can break it), a dead sleep. -nāsh m. breaking of sleep, (as a disease) broken sleep. -nỗṭhᵘ adj. (f. -nö̃ṭhᵘ̈), one whose sleep has been broken (e.g. by a noise). -tāch f. a kind of powder (made from a certain black seed) which is used as an eye-medicine. -ṭhŏla f.pl. 'horn-thrusts of sleep', great sleepiness, the being unable to keep awake. -wudᵘ adj. (f. -wuzᵘ̈), just awakened from sleep. --wudᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --wuzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), awakened from sleep, awake. --wŏthun -- m.inf. to rise from sleep, to become awake (El.). -zŏla f. a pleasant little sleep, a doze, forty winks.

(for 1, see nyoñᵘ) or ñĕñĕ f.pl. flesh (of man or beast), mutton (El. ninyi). -bŏkhᵃca adj. c.g. 'a bundle of flesh'; hence, a stout, fleshy man or woman. -bŏkutᵘ adj. (f. -bŏkᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), 'a flesh-whelp'; hence, a stout, fleshy person (esp. a child); a fine solid lump of meat (esp. cooked meat). -bŏkᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈ f. a fleshy woman (esp. a girl), as ab.; a solid lump of spiced and cooked meat. -kuʦorᵘ m. 'a flesh-whelp'; hence, a lump of spiced meat. -pholᵘ m. a piece of flesh ready cooked.
in nĕñĕ-mŏnḍücᵘ̈ or -mŏnḍüjᵘ̈ (Gr.M.) f. a female frog; -mŏnḍukh m. (sg. dat. -mŏnḍakas), a male frog (Gr.M.; L. 156, 460, ningi mundak). Cf. miñĕ- mŏnḍukh, p. 485a, l. 48.
f. a great pile of cooked rice. Cf. nĕnd 1.

m. a time, an occasion, the time at which anything occurs (cf. bata-nĕng, bel.) (L.V. 50); --˚ as adv. (in this connexion often nĕng or nĕngan), at the time of, in the season of, in the period of. Cf. buḍᵃñ-nĕng, in the period of old age, p. 87, l. 23; bata-nĕng, dinner time, p. 137a, l. 36; bata-nĕngan, at dinner time, id., l. 38.
or ningalan m. the act of swallowing, gulping down (cf. El. nyingal, swallowing).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nĕngalôwᵘ), to cause to swallow, to put something into a person's (or animal's) mouth with a view to his swallowing it, to induce a person to take (food, medicine, or the like); to swallow (Rām. 915, 985). nĕngalôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nĕngalövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to be swallowed.

or ningalun conj. 1 (1 p.p. nĕngolᵘ; f. nĕngüjᵘ̈), to swallow, gulp down (cf. grŏkh nᵒ, p. 302a, l. 26; grŏṭh nᵒ, p. 305a, l. 17.) (El. ningalun; Śiv. 980, 1451; Rām. 415; H. vi, 15; K. 191, 345, 737; K.Pr. 216). ¶ nĕngolᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nĕngüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), swallowed, gulped down. ¶ nĕngalith ʦhunun m.inf. to swallow down, to swallow completely (Rām. 413); to swallow and digest; met. to make away (another's property) and convert to one's own use.
or ñĕngur m. (f. nĕngᵘ̈rᵘ̈1 or ñĕngᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 1), one who speaks as if continually gulping (cf. nĕngalun); one who gabbles, who does not speak clearly, who swallows his words.
or ñĕngᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 2 or nĕngürᵘ̈ f. a small hard lump of human ordure as excreted (esp. a child's) (cf. gᵃsa-nᵃ, p. 307a, l. 21).
m. ruin by a fall from a height (lit. or met.).
or ñĕph f. (sg. dat. nĕpas or ñĕpas), to eat with a champing sound, to crunch. Cf. nyŏph.
or nĕpŏturᵘ adj. (as subst., sg. dat. nĕpŏtras; f. nĕpŏtᵘ̈rᵘ̈), sonless (either through not having begotten a son, or whose son is dead) (W. 132, K. 606, K.Pr. 126).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nyopᵘ), to swindle another (esp. by taking bribes for services which the taker has no intention of rendering); cf. napun. nyopᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. në̆pᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), swindled, as ab.

for nyūrᵘ 2, in the following (cf. aʦa-nēr, p. 70a, l. 30). ¶ nēra-nēr  f. a coming out at once, speedy production, speedy completion. ¶ nēran-bāna m. 'a vessel of goings forth', i.e. a man whose wealth is habitually being dissipated. -kāl m. the time for goings forth, i.e. the period, from first to last, during which a number of successive obligations must be performed.
or niᵒ adj. c.g. without splendour, without lustre (Śiv. 1458).
or niᵒ adj. c.g. free from self-conceit, devoid of pride or egoism (Śiv. 1602).
or niᵒ m. disrespect, contempt, scorn.
or niᵒ adj. c.g. formless, without form; a N. of the Supreme (Śiv. 178, 204, 284, 393, etc.; Rām. 846).
(Śiv. 1754) or nĕrālamb (Śiv. 1846) or niᵒ adj. c.g. having no prop or support (lit. or fig.).
or niᵒ adj. c.g. free from disease, free from defects or blemishes, infallible (Śiv. 1759, 1863).
or niᵒ adj. c.g. incessant, continual (Gr.M., Śiv. 1426).
or niᵒ adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. nĕrantas), without end, without limit, limitless (K. 385).
adv. without consideration, precipitately. Cf. parī 1.
or niᵒ adj. c.g. unbarred, unimpeded, free, irresistible (Śiv. 1426, nirᵒ).
or niᵒ adj. c.g. useless, vain, fruitless.

or niᵒ adj. c.g. hopeless, despairing (of, nishĕ, Rām. 236) (El., Gr.M., nirāsh; Śiv. 1710; Rām. 236, 1256). According to W. 110, nyerāsh is a subst. m. meaning 'disappointment, despair'. --karun -- m.inf. to make hopeless, disappoint (El.).
f. a habit of making gifts or oblations, generosity. --zānüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to know generosity, having recognized a person's generosity to implore him over and over again for something more.
n.ag. (f. nēravüñᵘ̈), one who goes out, etc., in all the meanings of nērun, q.v. (H. v, 8); one who is in the habit of going out.
or niᵒ adj. c.g. without strength, powerless, impotent, weak, feeble (esp. from sickness) (El. nyerbal, Gr.M. nirbal, K. 1026); weary, fatigued (Gr.M.).
or niᵒ f. want of strength, weakness, feebleness.
or niᵒ adj. c.g. impertinent, unmannerly, wanting in due respect.
or niᵒ adj. c.g. without wealth, poverty-stricken, poor (W. 110, nerdān, probably a misprint) (Śiv. 1041, 1211).
or niᵒ f. a woman who is disheartened, heavy-hearted, downhearted, downcast.
or niᵒ adj. c.g. without fault, without defect, faultless (W. 110, nirdush).
or niᵒ adj. c.g. devoid of all properties or qualities, without attributes (Śiv. 193, 275, 689, 770, 977, 991, etc.).
or niᵒ adj. c.g. profitless, useless (El. nyerláb).
or nirlēph adj. c.g. unsmeared, stainless (Śiv. 1021, 1757).
or niᵒ adj. c.g. free from desire (Śiv. 772, 888).
or niᵒ m. clearness, brightness, (of the sky) freedom from clouds.

or niᵒ adj. c.g. free from foulness, clean, clear, bright, shining, translucent (Gr.M.; W. 110; Śiv. 24, 27, 162, 330, 348, etc.; Rām. 87, 1056, 1063, 1692, 1703, 1707, 1728); (of the sky) clear, serene (Gr.M.).
or niᵒ m. the remains of an offering made to a deity; esp. water which has been used in a libation.
or niᵒ adj. c.g. cleanly conducted, one who is particular as to cleanliness, including his dress, appearance, food, and drink.

or niᵒ adj. c.g. free from illusion, free from unreality, free from the delusion by which one considers the unreal universe as really existent and as distinct from the Supreme Spirit (Śiv. 1430, 1803); (as subst.) freedom from such illusion (Śiv. 1742, 1824).

or niᵒ adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, a nĕrmāl or libation water. --karun -- m.inf. to make like water which has been used in a libation, to make any food or drink taboo or unusable, to make food unconsumable.
or niᵒ adj. c.g. without root; hence, baseless, unreasonable (Gr.M.).

or niᵒ  m. decision, conclusion (after discussion, e.g. the decision of a law-court) (Gr.M.); decision (as to an atonement); discussion, investigation, consideration (Śiv. 27, 376, 1024, etc.); explanation (of a difficult problem or passage in a book).

conj. 2, irreg. (1 p.p. drāv, Gr.Gr. 229, 236; 2 p.p. drāyōv, Gr.Gr. 229, 241. The regular past participle nyūrᵘ occasionally occurs in compounds, see nyūrᵘ-motᵘ, bel. In Śiv. 56, the 1 p.p. is drôwᵘ for the sake of rhyme), to go out, come out, issue forth, emerge (cf. bara nᵒ, p. 116b, l. 38; brō̃ṭh nᵒ, to go out ahead (of so-and-so), p. 128a, l. 31; brō̃ṭha nᵒ, to go out to meet (a guest), id., l. 43; canga-tala nᵒ, p. 173a, l. 16; gang nērüñᵘ̈, p. 291b, l. 21; nĕbar nᵒ, p. 620b, l. 22) (Gr.Gr. 21, 246, 249-50; Gr.M.; Śiv. 56, 85, 97, 121, 349, etc.; Rām. 121, 239, 299, 371, 390, 462, 467-8, etc.; K. 178, 245, 408, 416, 491, 738, etc.; YZ. 113, 178, 208; K.Pr. 57, 62, 102); ¶ to appear, become manifest (cf. brukᵘ nᵒ, p. 122a, l. 28; gᵃr nīrith yunᵘ, p. 295a, l. 9; khashurᵘ nᵒ, p. 419b, l. 3) (Śiv. 347, 523, 666, 668, 1503, 1548); to rise (as a heavenly body), come out (Gr.M.; Rām. 1013, 1257); to go forth (from privacy), to become celebrated, to become well known (of reputation, a person, etc.) (cf. mȧtⁱ mȧtⁱ nᵒ, p. 607b, l. 4; nāv nᵒ, s.v. nāv 1) (L.V. 49; Śiv. 1133, 1353-4; Rām. 92; K. 842); to go beyond bounds, to overflow (Gr.M.); ¶ to be produced, take rise (from), issue (from) (Śiv. 25, 30-1, 60, 99, 181, etc.; Rām. 97, 1517; K. 114; YZ. 394); to issue, be born, be produced (Rām. 88, 621, 1456); to issue (from), be the son (of) (cf. dala nᵒ, p. 210b, l. 7) (Rām. 634, 1458, 1493); to germinate, shoot (cf. hĕli nᵒ, p. 364b, l. 16) (Śiv. 1291, 1297, 1848); ¶ to depart, disappear (of pain, etc.) (cf. musᵘ nᵒ, p. 596b, l. 5) (Śiv. 923; Rām. 50, 348 (life), 647 (winter), 1106 (a stain), 1127; K.Pr. 154); to depart (from a custom) (cf. krāni nᵒ, p. 472a, l. 46); to go forth (from), be excluded (from), have no part or share (in) (cf. bāgi nᵒ, p. 90b, l. 49); to go forth (in the sense of being pulled out, or of being put an end to) (cf. bēkh, or bum, nērüñᵘ̈, pp. 99b, l. 16; 107b, l. 16; baṭha nᵒ, p. 139b, l. 26; cilikh nērüñᵘ̈, p. 171a, l. 48; haḍ nērȧnⁱ, p. 322b, l. 8, or haḍa nērañĕ, id., l. 26; mūl nᵒ, p. 567a, l. 22) (Rām. 550, 1333, 1339, 1427, 1633); ¶ to come out of a certain condition, to have done with a condition (cf. bĕmāri drāv, p. 108a, l. 46; kama nᵒ, p. 442b, l. 42; nīji drāmotᵘ, p. 627a, l. 1); to come out or appear (as a balance or share) (cf. bāganay or bāgay nērünᵘ̈, pp. 91b, l. 44; 93b, l. 15; mö̃thᵃr nērüñᵘ̈, p. 606a, l. 27); to result, prove, turn out (cf. chiwalayĕ nērañĕ, p. 168a, l. 12; ḍĕka nᵒ, p. 204b, l. 14; hyotᵘ nᵒ, p. 367b, l. 37) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 585, 995, 1820, 1830, 1899; Rām. 487; H. vi, 11; ix, 9; K. 860; YZ. 23); to be deduced (Rām. 1261); ¶ to sally forth, go out (from a house, etc.), go away, set out, depart (cf. āli nᵒ, p. 23b, l. 21; ȧṭⁱ ȧṭⁱ nᵒ, p. 69a, l. 10) (Gr.M.; L.V. 3, 92, 102; Śiv. 927, 998-9, 1493; Rām. 119, 165, 174, 192, 515, 560, etc.; K. 28-9, 76, 83, etc.; YZ. 30, 40, 138, 159, 474; K.Pr. 10, 67); to sally forth (for combat) (cf. mŏkha nᵒ, p. 560a, l. 15) (Rām. 917, 975, 1300; K. 452, 553, 745, 760, 775, etc.); to go forth (with an intention), to take to something out of doors as a profession (cf. bēchani nᵒ, p. 80a, l. 48; mã̄gạyĕ nᵒ, p. 552b, l. 36); (of an order, etc.) to be issued (Rām. 794, 1069; H. xi, 4); ¶ to issue (from some process or preliminary treatment), to be completed (so far as that treatment is concerned), to be performed, accomplished, effected (cf. atha nᵒ, p. 60b, l. 10; bĕha drāv, issued from sitting, i.e. cleared of sediment, p. 94b, l. 7; braka nᵒ, p. 122b, l. 5; byāli nᵒ, p. 150b, l. 38; dŏbi nᵒ, p. 183a, l. 2; dala-draka nᵒ, p. 209b, l. 22; khati nᵒ, p. 422a, l. 8; lāy nērüñᵘ̈, p. 543a, l. 27) (L.V. 23; Śiv. 49; Rām. 736, 1066, 1607; K. 573); to turn out successfully, to be successfully performed (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1104-5, 1140, 1233, 1283; Rām. 1573, 1576, 1763; K.Pr. 59); to rise (of cream on milk) (Gr.M.). ¶ drāmotᵘ perf. part. (f. drāmüʦᵘ̈), gone forth, issued, as ab. (Gr.Gr. 110; Śiv. 678, 1475; Rām. 1672); celebrated. ¶ nīrⁱ nīrⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to arrange hurriedly (esp. a marriage or the like without regard to the advice of seniors). ¶ nīrith gōmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), gone forth, esp. gone beyond bounds (e.g. off the side of a road, out of a country, or beyond the rules of good conduct). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go forth (beyond some limit) (Śiv. 409; Rām. 1541; H. ii, 3; xii, 15; K. 153, 908); to go over a boundary, to go beyond recognized or existing limits, to pass over a frontier, leave a country (Rām. 1528); to run away, bolt (K. 658); to abandon good conduct, take to evil practices; to depart (K. 450); (of a woman) to take to loose conduct; (of food) to be over-cooked. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come forth (from inside), to emerge (H. xii, 12; K. 624, 839). ¶ nyūrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nīrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈). (This is the regular form which, however, appears to be used only in a few compounds, such as hada nyūrᵘ-motᵘ, issued beyond bounds, p. 322a, l. 30.)
or niᵒ m. carrying on, conduct, management, accomplishing.
or niᵒ adj. c.g. devoid of hatred, incapable of feeling hatred, absolutely passionless (Śiv. 1271).

or niᵒ m. extinguishing, extinction; emancipation or salvation (after death) (Śiv. 1014, 1660); a ceremony for the peace of the soul of a dead Hindū; happiness in life as an ordinary householder, a peaceful life.
or niᵒ adj. c.g. without fancy or imagination; free from desire (Śiv. 1013, 1694, 1849); free from anxiety, happy and careless (as, e.g., a child).
f. (sg. dat. -köshᵘ̈), N. of the eleventh lunar day of the bright half of the month of Zēṭh (in Skt., Jyaiṣṭha = May-June) on which Hindūs fast.
or niᵒ m. unpeopled, uninhabited, desert, lonely, desolate; depopulated, deserted.
m. inequality (by birth or quality), difference.
adj. c.g. not attached to, indifferent, not caring for association (with any work or person).
adj. c.g. naked, nude, stark naked (esp. when connected with impropriety). --pöṭhⁱ -- adv. nudely, barefacedly and shamelessly.
f. deep unconscious sleep (L.V. 32). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. deep sleep (esp. as the result of excessive labour) to fall.
adj. c.g. sapless, pithless, fruitless, worthless, vain, unsubstantial.
adv. at an unlucky time. Cf. sāth.
m. hindering, stopping, obstructing; preventing, prohibition.
see nĕshyū̃kᵘ. nĕshū̃kᵘ, i.q. nĕshyū̃kᵘ, q.v.
or niᵒ adj. c.g. free from care or anxiety, without solicitude, contented, tranquil (Śiv. 232, 275, 682, etc.; K. 509); unconcerned, thoughtless, unreflecting.
or niᵒ adj. c.g. free from wish or desire, free from all worldly desire (Śiv. 275, 344, 682, etc.); as subst., m. freedom from such desire (Śiv. 58, 1113).
adj. c.g. distrusted, one who is not trusted, suspected (Rām. 1211).
adj. c.g. destitute of fire or energy, impotent, spiritless, dull.
adj. (f. nĕshī˜cᵘ̈), free, or freed, from fear or anxiety, careless, secure (K. 152, 383, 427, 815). nĕshī˜kⁱ pöṭhⁱ adv. fearlessly; in a way so as to relieve fear, encouragingly, cheeringly.
or nishbọ̆dᵘ adj. (f. nẹ̆shᵉ̆bŏ̈zᵉ̆), wanting in intellect, without understanding, uneducated, silly, a fool (Gr.M., L.V. 83, Śiv. 1310).

or nĕshⁱphȧlⁱ or nishphal adj. c.g. without fruit, bearing no fruit, fruitless; useless, unprofitable, inefficacious (Gr.M. nishphal); as adv., in vain, fruitlessly. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become fruitless; (of a missile) to miss the mark (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to make fruitless; to waste (time) (Gr.M.). ¶ nĕshⁱphȧlⁱ karun m.inf. to render useless or valueless (Rām. 8); to cause to be not used (by displaying defects or the like).
m. want of understanding, want of intellect, want of sense, silliness, foolishness (Gr.M. nĕshbŏzar).

or nishkāl adj. c.g. that which has no destruction, immortal, everlasting (Śiv. 1256, 1331); as subst., m. an evil time; hence, the result of an evil omen, in the following:-- --ḍēshun -- m.inf. an ill omen to come true. --hāwun -- m.inf. an ill omen to occur. --wuchun -- m.inf., id.
or nishkapaṭh adj. c.g. free from deceit or fraud, guileless, veracious.
or (Gr.M.) nishkāran adv. without cause, without reason, causelessly, needlessly (Gr.M.).
or nishkriy adj. c.g. inactive, not performing actions, actionless (Śiv. 772).
or nishpath adj. c.g. without trust, unbelieving (L.V. 36).
adj. (f. nĕshⁱpŏtⁱrⁱ), (of a living person) having no son; (of a dead person) leaving no male issue.

m. (sg. dat. nĕshⁱtaras), a lunar asterism, a lunar mansion; the period or time when the sun or some star is in, or enters into, this asterism (important for astrological calculations) (Rām. 124, 508); cf. nĕchotᵘ, nĕchatur. nĕshⁱtargạnzⁱrȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to count the asterisms, to exhibit anxiety as to what is to be done for the accomplishment of some desire, or for warding off some ill.
adj. c.g. free from thought, or anxiety, or care; heedless, unconcerned, careless.
adj. (f. nĕsümᵘ̈), unequal (by birth or in quality), different.

nĕsạph or nisph نصف s.m. the half (of anything); adj. half, semi-. --sheb -- نصف شب m. midnight (K.Pr. 176). --shĕban -- adv. at midnight (Śiv. 1661). ¶ nĕsph-ā-nĕsph نصفا نصف adv. half-and-half, by halves (Rām. 82).
m. an offering or oblation (of raw rice, fruit, clarified butter, etc.) made at a Śrāddha ceremony in honour of deceased relatives, and given to the Brāhmaṇa celebrant.
adj. c.g. (of a vessel) full. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be filled to the brim, to be chock full.
or nĕṭakay adv. in every way, entirely, absolutely, (with a negative) at all.
m. (sg. dat. nĕṭas), cheating or swindling by the help of laughter or ridicule. Cf. në̆ṭᵘ̈.

f. (sg. dat. në̆ʦᵘ̈ 1, for 2, see nĕtun), removing (by cutting or plucking) the wool of a sheep or similar animal, shearing (cf. atha-nᵒ, p. 60b, l. 15, and pŏha-nᵒ, s.v. pŏh) (Gr.Gr. 126); the wool so plucked or shorn (cf. atha-nᵒ, as ab.); met. doing work without payment, slave labour, forced gratuitous labour. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to afflict a person by compelling him to work for nothing.

adv. continually, constantly, regularly, perpetually (L.V. 46, 65; Śiv. 57, 114, 204, etc.; Rām. 8, 73, 573, 893, 1124, 1127, 1629, 1635; K. 125, 229, 265, 525, etc.; obligatorily. Cf. nityĕ. ¶ nĕta-mamunᵘ adj. (f. -mamüñᵘ̈), paralyzed, permanently deprived of motion or the power of motion. -mamañĕr or -mamañār m. paralysis, motionlessness. -nēm m. obligatory religious rites performed at regular intervals; cf. nityĕ-karm, p. 663a, l. 45. -nīmī adv. continually, daily, everyday. -sŏtī f. the insensibility of profound sleep or the like. -sŏth adj. c.g. dead asleep, comatose, so sound asleep that one is insensible. ¶ nĕtⁱ adv. continually, regularly, perpetually. ¶ nĕti-nĕma-kinⁱ adv. every day, day by day, and according to rule. -nēma-wôlᵘ adj. (f. -nēma-wājĕñ), one who works diligently and with daily regularity. ¶ nitō-nĕth adv. continually, without cessation (Śiv. 642).
in the following:-- nĕtha-nonᵘ adj. (f. -nüñᵘ̈), naked, bare, nude (Gr.M.; W. 132; L. 462, netnun; Śiv. 88, 890, 998-9, 1057, etc.; Rām. 1517; K. 271-2; K.Pr. 126). -nañĕr m. nudity, nakedness.
in the following:-- nĕthur-pathur m. compelling an incapable person to do some work.

m. a marriage ceremony, a wedding (cf. ganḍa-nᵒ, p. 289b, l. 11) (W. 136; K. 23, 24, 615-17, 638, 650 ff., 711, 1081, 1139; K.Pr. 22, 241). In kāha-nᵒ (p. 387b, l. 11 and p. 835b, l. 2) and māsa-nᵒ (p. 596a, l. 1) the word is used for certain birth-ceremonies (El. nethar or nyethar). --ganḍun -- m.inf. to make the formal agreement for a marriage (accompanied by the giving and receipt of presents), to hold the formal betrothal ceremony. --karun -- m.inf. to marry (El.; Rām. 324; H. viii, 2; xii, 15; K.Pr. 2); to give (a person) in marriage (Rām. 1247). -pöthᵃr m. the associations or accompaniments of a marriage (such as the results of marriage, earning money, the life of a householder, the begetting or bearing of children and bringing them up). ¶ nētra-bôgᵘ m. a present given by the relations at a wedding, a wedding present. --drāv -- adj. c.g. 'issued from marriage', i.e. a newly married person. -gã̄ḍay f. the formal negotiations between the parties to a marriage, the settlement of the marriage terms. -ganḍa-ganḍ f. the formal arrangements for a marriage, the formal betrothal before a marriage. -grākh m. (sg. dat. -grākas; f. -grākañ), one whose marriage has been completed. --koḍᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --küḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), 'pulled out from a wedding,' one who has been successfully married (by the aid of the relations on both sides), married off. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to pull out of a marriage, (of the relations of a bride or bridegroom) to marry off (a person). --kāḍay -- f. the carrying out a marriage, the marrying off of a person. -kath f. (sg. dat. -kathi), wedding-talk, the preliminary negotiations with a view to marriage (K.Pr. 256). -katha ʦhunañĕ f. pl. inf. to send out the formal proposals for a marriage (usually sent by the bride's people). -katha yiñĕ f. pl. inf. the formal proposals for a marriage to arrive. -mahārĕñ f. the bride at a marriage ceremony (and during a few days before and after the ceremony). -mahārāza m. the bridegroom at a marriage ceremony. --mēlun -- m.inf. to meet in marriage, to be united in marriage (esp. of a high person with a lowly one). -wahara-wôdᵘ m. the festival on the first anniversary of a wedding. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is either immediately about to be married or who has been married a few days ago. ¶ nĕtrukᵘ sg. gen. (f. nētrücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a wedding. ¶ nētras kyutᵘ adv. at the time of a wedding.
f. a tailor's thimble (shaped like a ring) (cf. kŏṭhⁱ-nⁱ, p. 489a, l. 25); a thumb-ring (H. vi, 16). Cf. nyoṭhᵘ.
f. the top part of a churn, through which the churning-stick passes. It is held in its place by the great toe (nyoṭhᵘ) of the operator, which is inserted into a hole in it.
or ni-trihonᵘ, adj. (f. nĕ(ni)-trihüñᵘ̈ ), void of love or affection (e.g. of one to whom much affection has been shown by his relations, but who does not return their love).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nyotᵘ; f. në̆ʦᵘ̈ 2, for 1, see nĕth 1), to cut or pluck off the hair or wool of an animal, to shear, to fleece (El. nyetun; Gr.Gr. 126; K.Pr. 82, 83). nyotᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. në̆ʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), shorn, fleeced.

f. (sg. dat. nĕcĕ), swindling (in the distribution or giving of any article, by interfering with its proper distribution); cf. nĕṭh. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to swindle one of the sharers in some gift by giving him far less than his due share. ¶ nĕcĕ-tār m. to carry through (some work involving large expenditure, such as a marriage festival) meanly and at very small expense although one has plenty of means to do it lavishly.

f. when the stigmas of the saffron flower have been collected, the remaining sun-dried flowers are beaten with sticks and winnowed. The whole mass is then thrown into water, when the petals swim and the essential parts of the flower sink. The parts which sink are called nĕwal. These are collected and sold (L. 344, niwal).
m. putting off, getting rid of (e.g. a petitioner or beggar by making some little concession or by some excuse).
m. warding off, in nĕwār dyunᵘ m.inf. to finish off somehow or other (e.g. an impossible or unpleasant task when proper means are not available, or when a person intervenes and composes a quarrel).
m. (sg. dat. nĕwārakas), one who keeps off, wards off; esp. one who habitually wards off evil or calamities from others.
f. (sg. dat. nĕwārüñᵘ̈), the act of warding off, keeping off, preventing; warding off in the sense of getting rid of, i.e. finishing very quickly some work which has been begun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nĕwôrᵘ), to ward off, keep off, prevent (Śiv. 13, 1889); to get rid of (some work, esp. a distasteful one), to hurry through and get it done. nĕwôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nĕwörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), warded off, prevented; hurriedly completed, as ab.
m. dwelling, residence; dwelling-place, abode, house. --karun -- m.inf. to dwell, reside, inhabit; to take a lodging or a temporary residence (by a traveller or by one absent from home).
m. caress, blandishment; kindness, politeness, favour, courtesy; presentation (to a superior), an offering, a tribute of respect; a respectful representation, address, petition.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nĕwôzᵘ), to caress, soothe, cherish; to favour, patronize; to make a humble offering (to a superior), to tender a tribute of respect; to make a respectful address (to), to petition, to represent (Gr.M., K. 1014). nĕwôzᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (1 p.p. nĕwözᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), tendered as a respectful offering; stated respectfully, stated in a petition.
m. one who wards off; esp. one who habitually wards off (evil, etc., from others) (Śiv. 627, 1505). In Śiv. 1889, nĕwörī is m.c. for nĕwörⁱ, see nĕwārun.
adj. c.g. a resident (of), an inhabitant (of), a native (of).
m. one who shows clemency or courtesy; one who makes an offering; one who makes a present to a superior; one who makes a respectful address, a petitioner.

or niyĕm m. a rule, regulation, precept (Gr.M., niyĕm; Śiv. 267, 269); custom, usage, practice; agreement, assent, promise, vow; cf. nēm. --karun -- m.inf. to make an arrangement, compact, promise, vow (L.V. 87). --thawun -- m.inf. to make a promise, to come to an agreement.
adj. c.g. ascertained, determined, settled, concluded.

or nyēza m. a short spear, a lance, javelin (Rām. 963); iron railings, or the like, forming a fence (H. v, 4). -bardār نیزہ بردار m. a spear-bearer, a spearman, a lancer. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to wound with a javelin, to spear. -kil f. a stroke with a spear, a blow causing a spear-wound. --lagun -- m.inf. a javelin to be attached, to be wounded by a spear, to be speared. --lāyun -- m.inf. to smite with a javelin, to spear.
adj. (f. nĕzuvᵘ̈), lifeless; hence, weak, helpless, unable to work.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nibôwᵘ), to carry on or through, to conduct, manage, accomplish (Gr.M.); to pass (time, the day, etc.) (cf. dŏh niᵒ, p. 199b, l. 39) (Gr.M.); to spend time (in expectation). nibôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nibövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), accomplished, etc.; passed (of time, etc.), etc.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. nibyōv), to be accomplished or performed; to succeed, be successfully carried out. nibyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nibyē-müʦᵘ̈), accomplished, successfully carried out.
m. smallness, littleness, minuteness (cf. ös-niᵒ, p. 46b, l. 6) (Gr.Gr. 30, 139); leanness, thinness (El.).
m. profound and repeated meditation, constant musing (Śiv. 1001, 1205, 1792).

f. a feeding trough for cattle. ¶ nigayĕ-körᵘ̈ f. 'feeding-trough-necked', the condition of having the head bent low, a habit of humility. -pütᵘ̈ f. the board in front of a feeding trough to which the heads of the feeding cattle are tied.
m. a precious stone, a jewel (H. viii, 3, 11).
adv. extremely, very, used by Musalmāns to form the superlative degree of adjectives (W. 22).

m. blueness, dark greenness, greenness; a collection of fresh spring grass. --aʦun -- m.inf. fresh greenness to appear, fresh shoots to come. --phērun -- m.inf. blueness to spread over any person or thing (from illness, fear, a blow, etc.). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be covered with fresh springing grass.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nījᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. nījᵃrun. nījᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ  perf. part. (nījᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), caused to become blue or green, etc.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nījᵒrᵒ), to make blue (or green), to cause a thing to change to that colour; to cause to be blue (by illness or a blow, etc.).

(for 2, see nyūlᵘ) f. (properly f. of nyūlᵘ, the fresh feminine thing) a collection of fresh young spring grass. (Sheep, goats, and cattle are fed on dried grass during the winter. When, in the spring, they are first given this fresh grass, it acts as a spring medicine, causing diarrhœa and consequent leanness till they grow accustomed to it.) ¶ nījĕ-bombur m. (sg. dat. -bomburas), a kind of large stinging fly which is found at the season of this fresh grass. -boṭhᵘ m. a bank covered with this grass. -büṭhᵘ̈ f. a small bank (such as a field boundary) bearing this grass. -dŏd m. the milk of a cow fed on this grass, and consequently thin, and wanting in the fatty constituents. -dand m. the teeth of an animal fed on this grass (one of the consequences being that they are weak, as compared with their condition when eating the dried winter grass). -khāv adj. c.g. an eater of this grass, a herbivorous animal which eats this grass too greedily (with consequential diarrhœa and other ill effects; cf. -môrᵘ, bel.). -kyomᵘ m. a certain winged insect found in this grass. -môrᵘ adj. (f. -mörᵘ̈), 'struck by this grass,' a full-bodied man who has become thin and wasted (like a sheep or goat which eats this grass too eagerly; see -khāv, ab.). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to happen (i.e. to begin) upon this grass, (of cattle, etc.) to begin to graze on the new spring grass. -syunᵘ m. the flesh of sheep or goats fed on this grass (and consequently lean, skinny, and without fat). -tyūrᵘ m. (sg. dat. -tīris), a flock of sheep or goats fed on this grass (hence, lean from the consequent diarrhœa). -wôñᵘ m. water flowing from a place where this grass grows. ¶ niji drāmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --drāmüʦᵘ̈ --), issued from this grass, a herbivorous animal which is become accustomed to eating this grass, and is consequently immune from its ill effects. --drāv -- adj. c.g., id.

m. (properly a contracted form of nyukᵘ, small, q.v. In some of the following compounds the word is an adjective equivalent to nyukᵘ), a small ball, a marble, or the like; a small solid cowry; (met.) (as a term of affection to a darling son), a son, a boy (K.Pr. 237). -cirn m. 'a little lump of suet', a small lump, a small mass. -cirna-wād m. that which is to be completed little by little. -donzᵘ m. 'a little splinter of rice'; hence, a lean very intelligent boy; cf. dünzᵘ̈ 1. -dünzᵘ̈ f. a bunch of tiny bead-pearls (usually artificial, but sometimes real); a lean very intelligent girl; cf. dünzᵘ̈ 1. -gāḍa f.pl. a shoal of little fishes, or such a crowd collected in a net; cf. nicĕ gāḍa, s.v. nyukᵘ. -gula f. N. of a certain medicinal leaf, used as a blood purifier. -görⁱ m.pl. a collection of a certain kind of small water chestnuts. -khorᵘ m. 'a marble scaldhead'; hence, a naughty boy who wastes his time playing marbles (when he ought to be at school). -nika m. a collection of small pieces (e.g. bits of meat or splinters of wood). -nika karun m.inf. to mince (meat, etc.); met. to give (a person) a good whipping or cudgelling. -nôrᵘ m. 'a (mere) collection of bits of intestines'; hence, a thorough beating or whipping (given to a person on every part of his body); cf. nôrᵘ 2. -nôṭᵘ m. 'a mere mass of bits of flesh'; hence, a thorough beating, as ab.; cutting up flesh, wood, vegetables, or the like, into small bits. -phal m. a collection of small seeds (such as linseed, mustard, etc.). -pholᵘ m. a very small ball (e.g. seed pearls, shot, or the like). -suka m. small things (as compared with larger things; e.g. chips off a block, small change taken out of a store of money, and the like). -zag f. a kind of paddy, the grain of which is small, long, and of a red colour, and which grows in marshy land. -zạgᵃr f. another rice, with a fine red grain, and growing in marshy land. -zār  m. a certain gambling game played with small cowries or small earthen balls. -zörⁱ  m. one addicted to this game.

m. matrimony, marriage, nuptials (among Musalmāns, and so in the following) (El. niká). --karun -- m.inf. to settle a marriage, to fix a betrothal. -parun m.inf. to recite the marriage, i.e. to sign the marriage contract.
f. (sg. dat. nikarüñᵘ̈), the act of chopping up (e.g. wood), reducing to mincemeat, mincing (e.g. meat).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nikarôwᵘ), to make thin (e.g. a log of wood with a saw); to chop into small pieces. nikarôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nikarövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), thinned, pared down, as ab.; chopped up, as ab.
nīkh, see nyunᵘ. Cf. also nāga- nikh, s.v. nāg 2.
f. goodness; good; piety, virtue, a good deed (K.Pr. 226). nīkī karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to do good (to), show kindness (to) (Rām. 256).
f. silence from a sense of shame, shamefacedness.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. nikyōv), to become thin, gradually to diminish, little by little to decrease or become lean, to waste away (El.; W. 113, nyikun). nikyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nikyē-müʦᵘ̈), become lean, thinned.
f. (sg. dat. nikᵃrüñᵃ), the condition of having been reduced to small pieces, dismemberment, the condition of having been chopped up (e.g. of a log of wood or the like).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nikᵃrôwᵃ), to attenuate, pare down, cut down, make thin (e.g. a thick stick with a knife or saw) (El.); to chop to pieces (e.g. a log, with a hatchet). nikᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. nikᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), attenuated, pared down, cut down, as ab.; chopped up, as ab.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nikᵒrᵒ), to chop up, mince, reduce to small pieces (e.g. a log of wood, meat, etc.). nikᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. nikᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), chopped up, minced.

or nīla-nāg m. N. of a Nāga king or snake-deity (see nāg 2) (Śiv. 1169). It was by following his advice that Kashmīr is said to have been freed from Piśācas, and rendered habitable by men all the year round. Before that the country had been occupied by Piśācas for six months in each year. His habitation was close to the famous spring now called Nīla-nāg, near the village of Vērnāg, and is the traditional source of the river Vĕth or Jehlam (RT.Tr. II, 411). There is another small lake called by his name situated in a valley between two spurs descending from the Pīr Panʦāl range (ib. 474).

f. the colour blue, dark blue; lividity; (in Kāshmīrī) convulsions (the disease of children); cf. nyūlᵘ. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an attack of convulsions to come on. ¶ nīla-gurᵘ m. a horse white [sic] all over, a grey horse. -har m. the turning dark (i.e. going bad) of the cream of milk, top-scum of jam, or the like; cf. har 2. -khᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a certain bird, described as small and dark-coloured, with a long tail and a prolonged sweet-sounding call. -khürᵘ̈ f. name of a certain creeping plant, described as not tall, with long slender leaves and small spiny fruit. -kanṭh m. (sg. dat. -kanṭhas), he who possesses a blue neck, a N. of Śiva, whose neck was dyed blue by his swallowing the deadly kālakūṭa poison at the churning of the ocean (Śiv. 169, 192, 235, etc.). -küñᵘ̈ a kind of hard dark-coloured stone (used for making mortars and the like) (Rām. 517). -krôshᵘ m. (f. -kröshᵘ̈), a certain bird, the European Roller (Coracias garrula) (L. 136, nilakraish; Śiv. 1693, 1816); cf. nila-krôshᵘ, s.v. nila 2. -kray f. Crozophora tinctoria, Trichodesma indica (El., where the word is spelt -krai). -kūṭhⁱ f. an indigo factory (Gr.M.) (borrowed from Hindī nīl-kōṭhī). -pal m. 'blue rock', a certain kind of stone found in large blocks of a dark colour. -ras m. 'blue juice', liquid (such as the water of a lake, or the juice of curds, etc., or of cooked food) which has become corrupt. -sar m., id. -sȧrⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. (of juice, as ab.) to become black and corrupt; (of the whole body when bruised) to become black and blue. -sȧrⁱ karun m.inf. to make juice (as ab.) become corrupt; to make a person's whole body black and blue (by a beating or the like). -tō̃g m. a bruise (turned black and blue). -tō̃g khārȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to cause a black or blue bruise (by a blow or the like). -tō̃g khasȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. such bruises to rise (i.e. to occur). -thŏth m. (sg. dat. thŏthas), blue vitriol, sulphate of copper. -warih m. a year in which the crops do not ripen, a famine year. -waṭh m. (sg. dat. -waṭas), a kind of large dark stone (generally globular) (according to El., s.v. nīlawaṭ, this is marble, said to be found in a quarry behind the famous Shālimār Gardens) (Rām. 1582).
