m. for nīla 2 in the following:-- --phirȧnⁱ -- or --phirawȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to whirl an athletic's club.

for nīl 2, in the following:-- -khrüñᵘ̈ f. a certain plant, described as a creeper with a long dark-coloured leaf. -krôshᵘ m. (f. -kröshᵘ̈), a certain bird, the European Roller (Coracias garrula) (L. 136, nilakraish); cf. nīla-krôshᵘ, s.v. nīl 2. -pūtᵘ m. a kind of pigeon found in the highest mountains (where no other birds and no trees are observed).
(for 1, cf. nīl 1 and 2) m. a kind of athlete's club; cf. nila 1. -bözⁱ f. the athlete's exercise of whirling one of these clubs.
m. a sapphire (K. 922). nīlama-kān f. a sapphire-mine.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nīlanôwᵘ), to make blue or green (Gr.Gr. 174; cf. nīlun).

or nīlyujᵘ m. a certain bird, the mallard (Anas boscas) (of whose skin pōstīns are made for the wealthy. The four curled central feathers of the tail are worn by the Panjābī and Hindōstānī women, and are called kōnḍal) (El. nílúj; L. 129, nilij). nīlijⁱ-tāj m. the crest of this bird.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. nīlyōv), to become blue, dark blue, livid (Rām. 1022, 1210; YZ. 96); to become green (e.g. of the leaf of a plant); (the causal of this verb is nīlanāwun, not nīlᵃrāwun (Gr.Gr. 174)). nīlyō-motᵘ  perf. part. (f. nīlyē-müʦᵘ̈), become blue; become green.

or nīlyuwᵘ m. (sg. dat. nilivis or nīlivis), the act of causing a person to give or award (money, punishment, etc.), or of causing him to do anything, compulsion (K.Pr. 200, nílu). --āsun -- m.inf. compulsion to exist. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. compulsion to be experienced. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to use compulsion, as ab.
adj. half, in such Persian phrases as nīm garm نیم گرم adj. lukewarm (El.). nīm khanda نیم خندہ m. a half-laugh, a smile (El.).
m. the time occupied in closing the eye, the twinkling of the eye, a moment, an infinitesimal period of time (L.V. 26); opp. to wunmēsh (the time occupied in opening the eye) (Śiv. 1069, 1427).
the Musalmān form of mimyuzᵘ, q.v.
nīn, nina, ninⁱ, ni ni, ninī, see nyunᵘ.
adj. c.g. foodless, fasting, abstaining from food (Śiv. 200, 689, 1272).
(Śiv.) or niranzan (Rām.) m. one who is unstained, a N. of the Supreme Being (Śiv. 363, 689, 994, 1339, etc.; Rām. 846, 1704, 1746).
f. (sg. dat. nīrāzüñᵘ̈), lustration with lamps of a bride and bridegroom, of a newly arrived king, or other highly honoured person.

m. (sg. dat. niranas), thatching-grass, thatching-reeds. ¶ niran-bodᵘ m. a handful or similar bundle of thatching-reeds. -gorᵘ m. a thatching-reed worker, a thatcher. -köñᵘ̈ f. a small bundle of thatching-reeds. -zanḍ m. a small bundle of thatching-grass (esp. when not enough for what is required).

or nishĕ adv. and postpos. [governing dat. and abl. In the first case it indicates primarily rest in a place or motion to a place, and in the second case (with an important exception noted below) motion from a place. In the first case it is the equivalent of the Hindī pās, in the second of pās sē. According to some authorities nish is used only in the sense of rest in a place or motion to, and nishĕ only in the sense of motion from, but this distinction is not commonly observed in manuscripts]. ¶ A. As adv., near, close by (nishĕ, L.V. 30, 46; Śiv. 251; Rām. 1552). ¶ B. Governing the dat., at the side of, beside, alongside, near, at hand, close by (nish, W. 97; Śiv. 683, 702, 1066; Rām. 313, 757, 1246, 1466; H. x, 5, 12; K. 170; nishĕ, Gr.Gr. 13; Gr.M.; L.V. 31; Śiv. 572, 727; Rām. 992, 1283; H. ii, 9; vii, 20; x, 4); asĕ nish, near us, i.e. in our family or caste (such-and-such a thing is allowed or prohibited) (Rām. 324); amis nishĕ, with him, i.e. his custom or nature (is such-and-such) (Rām. 1661); pānas nishĕ, near oneself, in one's own heart (Rām. 18, 45, 129, 236); nyūn pānas nish, he took (it) with him (K. 204); ¶ in the possession of (mĕ nishĕ chuh sĕṭhāh, I have plenty, Gr.M.) (nish, Śiv. 432, 900-1; Rām. 1524; nishĕ, Śiv. 58-60); ¶ (after verbs of motion, bringing, sending, showing, etc.) to, up to (tim ʦȧlⁱ rāzas nishĕ, they fled to the king) (nish, Śiv. 698, 880, etc.; Rām. 81, 133, 223, 255, etc.; H. ii, 11; iii, 2; v, 8, 10; viii, 5, 13; x, 1-5, 11, etc.; K. 485; nishĕ, Śiv. 208, 388, 720, 847, etc.; Rām. 1710; H. ii, 7; x, 7; xii, 19, 22; K. 37, 81-2, 123, etc.); nishĕ pānas (to summon) to oneself (K. 374); tas nishĕ prakhoṭᵘ, known to him (K. 128); ¶ in the opinion of (so-and-so) (chuh mĕ nishĕ jān, in my opinion it is good, Gr.M.) (nish, Rām. 1460; nishĕ, Rām. 1650, 1656); ¶ owing to, because of [in this sense more often governing the abl. (nishĕ, Rām. 29)]. ¶ C. Governing the abl., with the important exception that, in the case of singular masculine animate nouns, it optionally governs the dative, from near, from (Gr.Gr. 48, 49; W. 98, nishi) (nish, with abl., Śiv. 22, 125, 681, etc.; Rām. 83, 1304, 1386; with dat., Śiv. 431, etc.; Rām. 895, 1060, 1177, 1190; nishĕ, with abl., Śiv. 61, 99, 106, etc.; Rām. 2, 20, 27, 111-12, 174, etc.; H. vi, 12; vii, 2; K. 114, 212; with dat., Śiv. 30, etc.; Rām. 83, 424, 683, 895, 1347, etc.; K. 392, 576, 630); occasionally, in poetry, it takes the dative case even of an inanimate noun, as in wanas nishĕ, from the forest (Rām. 1198), phalis nᵒ, (issued) from the seed (Rām. 1456); ¶ from, owing to, because of (nishĕ, L.V. 27, Rām. 802); ¶ with, by means of (rājĕ nish sēr, sated with royalty, Rām. 365; nāra nish, by means of fire, Rām. 1203; with dat., K. 573); ¶ from, beyond, more than (nishĕ, L.V. 48); ¶ used after verbs of fearing or the like, as in chuh dāndas nishĕ khōʦān, he is afraid of the bull (an. sg. m.) (Gr.M.); mŏkalana nishĕ nā-wumēd, despairing of accomplishment (Gr.M.); (nish, with dat., Rām. 932). ¶ Governing the abl. (or an. sg. dat.), or the abl. (or an. sg. dat.) of the genitive, it indicates comparison, as in rŏpa nishĕ chuh sŏn jān, gold is better than silver (Gr.Gr. 49); kañĕ-handi (or kañi) nishĕ chuh trakurᵘ, he is harder than a stone (id.) [nish, with abl., Rām. 270, 600 (tawa nish dŏgan zīṭhⁱ, twice as long as that), 771; cf. Rām. 352 (tawa nishĕ kō-na, why not than that, i.e. why not rather); with dat. Rām. 559].

نشان m. (El. also nishān), sign, signal, mark (Gr.M.; Rām. 462, 775, 904, 1505) (cf. nēb-nᵒ, p. 619b, l. 23); impression (Rām. 1125); a mark, a trace, a small fragment (Śiv. 651, 921, 1121); a token (as a sign of recognition) (H. x, 8, 14; xii, 21); esp. a mark indicating quality or the like, or a mark (e.g. a signature) indicating approval (Śiv. 1599); a target, butt, bull's-eye (Śiv. 1715, Rām. 999); proof (El.); address (of a person), intimation of a person's residence (Rām. 501). --karun -- m.inf. to aim, to take aim (El.). --marun -- m.inf. a mark to be hit (Śiv. 175); entire concurrence with another's opinion to occur. --mārun -- m.inf. to hit the mark; to lead another person to complete concurrence with one's own opinion. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. the mark to present itself; also i.q. --marun, ab. --rōzun -- m.inf. the mark to remain or abide (e.g. the mark of a blow, or a paint-mark); met. (of a dead person) his memorials still to remain.

m. (sg. dat. nishātas), liveliness, sprightliness, cheerfulness, glee; N. of certain beautiful gardens, situated on the north shore of the Ḍal lake near Śrīnagar. They are said to have been laid out by one of the servants of 'Alī Mardān Khān, a former ruler of Kashmīr (El., Śiv. 1823).
m. certainty (Śiv. 159, 1759); --thawun -- m.inf. to be assured (Gr.M.).
m. a kind of juice or resin issuing from certain trees.
adj. c.g. seated, sitting; settled (as dust).

adv. and postpos., i.q. nish, q.v.; near (H. ii, 8); near (governing dat. after vb. of motion) (Śiv. 431, 790; Rām. 64, 147, 598, 616, 821, 841, 1256, 1352, 1369; H. viii, 4, 10); ¶ (governing abl., or, with sg. an. m. noun, dat.); (with abl.) from (Rām. 32 (far) from, 1398 (free) from, 1426 (far) from); (with dat.) (Rām. 1442, tas nᵒ (designing) against her, Rām. 1150). ¶ In poetry the word (like nishĕ) sometimes governs the dat. of an inan. noun, with this sense, as in pöñis nᵒ, (born) from water, Rām. 1517.
f. a mark, sign, token; a distinctive mark; a token of remembrance, keepsake, souvenir; (among Musalmāns) a marriage agreement, a betrothal (L. 268, nishān).
[] adj. c.g. intent on, devoted to, used --˚ as in brahma-nishṭh, p. 120b, l. 48 (Śiv. 1859).
f. position, condition, state (Śiv. 1492); belief, firm adherence, devotion, close attachment (Śiv. 1621, 1770).
m. a lancet, a fleam (Rām. 1117). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to lance, to apply the lancet (to); to bleed, phlebotomize.

f. (sg. dat. nīʦᵘ̈ 1, K. 1018; for 2, see nyūtᵘ, for 3, see nyūʦᵘ), conduct, (esp.) right or wise conduct or behaviour, prudence, policy, political wisdom or science, moral philosophy or precept (K. 1018); good advice, guidance (K. 1004, 1033). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to consult together, to discuss the advisability (of anything) (K. 181, 367). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give moral advice; to advise generally (K. 1003). ¶ nīʦᵘ̈-wôlᵘ̈ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one skilled in moral conduct, (esp.) one who is accustomed to give good advice.

or nēthᵃr 2 (q.v.) m. the eye (Śiv. 26, 794, 863, 907, 959, 1259, 1538, 1706, 1741, 1743; K. 601, 926). ¶ nitra-gāsh m. the brilliancy of the eye, the brightness of the eye; met. a darling only son. -kamal an eye-lotus, an eye like a lotus bloom. -prakāsh m. the brightness of the eye; met. a darling only son.

adv., i.q. nĕth 2, q.v. It occurs ˚-- in compounds borrowed from Sanskrit, such as nityĕkarm m. a daily necessary rite, a constant act or duty, i.q. nĕta-nēm (p. 660b, l. 46) (K. 968); hence, -karma adv. by constant practice (Śiv. 1541); nityĕ-muktī f. everlasting salvation (Śiv. 663); nityĕ-sīwakh m. one who is a slave for ever (K. 384); nityĕ-vrĕth f. a woman who is constant in her conduct (Śiv. 1369).

f. (sg. dat. nivrĕʦᵘ̈), return, coming back; (as a religious technical term) abstaining from work, inactivity, the not depending for salvation on 'works' (opp. to pravruth, q.v.) (Śiv. 1427, 1481, 1759, 1859).
n.ag. (f. niwanāwavüñᵘ̈), one who causes to take; one who causes to be taken away (Śiv. 852).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. niwanôwᵘ) (causal of nyunᵘ), to cause to take; to cause to be taken away (Gr.Gr. 172, Śiv. 1393).
a kind of rice, hardy growing at a high elevation, with a red, soft, well-flavoured grain (L. 333 niwár, 463 niwar).
f. the wages for carrying or conveying (Gr.Gr. 129).
n.ag. (f. niwavüñᵘ̈), one who takes away, etc. (as in nyunᵘ, q.v.) (Gr.Gr. 192, Śiv. 1200); esp. one who captures, captivates (Śiv. 946, 1446).

m. petition, supplication, prayer; inclination, wish, eager desire, longing; a gift, a present; an offering, a thing dedicated. --karun -- m.inf. to pray, supplicate; to dedicate, devote, consecrate. --thawun -- m.inf. to vow, to dedicate.
m. (sg. dat. niyĕmatas), a boon, benefit, favour (El. niamat); i.q. nyāmath.

f. (sg. dat. niyüʦᵘ̈; K.Pr. 157 m., with sg. dat. niyĕtas), intention, intent, purpose, aim, object (El. níyat) (K.Pr. 157); desire, wish; a person's natural inclinations, esp. virtuous inclinations. --ganḍüñᵘ̈ -- f. inf. to adhere firmly to a design or purpose, to be fixed in one's intention, to be determined on a course of action. --karüñᵘ̈ --  f.inf. to form the design, etc. (of); to intend, design, purpose; to will, to resolve, to make a vow. --rōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. one's good inclinations to remain unchanged (e.g. when a generous person is raised to high office and he still remains generous). --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to retain one's good inclinations as ab., not to be spoilt by a change of circumstances.
adj. c.g. own, special, proper, peculiar, one's own (L.V. 67).
adj. and adv. near, close, contiguous (H. viii, 6, 10; x, 4); as adv. nearly, about; postpos. governing dat., near (maranas nᵒ, at the point of death, Gr.M.) (H. viii, 6; x, 3). Cf. nazdīkh.
f. extreme humility (by natural habit, or shown when asking pardon, making a request, or the like). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. humbly to ask forgiveness, to conciliate with humility.
m. lowness, humbleness; vileness, baseness, meanness, abjectness; meanness of mind, miserliness.
m. (sg. dat. nīʦatas), miserliness, meanness, illiberality (Gr.M.).
nīʦᵘ̈ 1 and 2, see nīth, nyūtᵘ, nyūʦᵘ.
f. lowness, humbleness; vileness, baseness, meanness, abjectness.
see nawa-nö, s.v. nav 1, and nastuv-nö.
m. fruitlessness, barrenness; fruitlessness, futility. Cf. nö̃ṭhun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nö̃chᵒrᵒ), to ruin, spoil, vitiate. Cf. nö̃ṭhun, of which it is the causal.
f. an elevated earthen or wooden trough for conveying water for the irrigation of uneven ground.
adj. c.g. singular, rare, uncommon, wonderful (El.).
m. a kind of pointed shoe.
f. a female serpent (see nāg 2) (Gr.Gr. 37); a small water-spring (see nāg 2). nögiñĕ-bal m. a small sacred spring (esp. when a place of pilgrimage). Cf. nāga-bal (col. a, l. 18).
m. (sg. dat. nögindras), i.q. nāga-rāza, col. a, l. 40, q.v. (Śiv. 2, 521, 978).
m. N.P., the patriarch Noah (H. iv, 3).

or nohᵘ m. the bowels of man or beast. ¶ nöhⁱ- (or nȧhⁱ-) gŏʦürᵘ̈ (or) f. the bag of the bowels, the bag-shaped portion of the bowels in which the refuse of digestion is collected, ? the large intestine. -kala m. the head of the bowels, the upper part of the bowels, the stomach and neighbouring part of the intestines. -patᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. the 'mat of the bowels', the lower part of the bowels. -ras m. juice of the bowels, i.e. soup (for an invalid) made from the intestines of sheep or goats. -raz f. the rope of the bowels, the bowels of a slaughtered sheep or goats (like a long rope when unfolded). -ʦrüṭᵘ̈ f. the 'potter's wheel of the intestines', i.e. the convoluted part of the bowels near the navel, ? the small intestine.

m. a servant, a domestic, an attendant, a retainer (El., Gr.M., K.Pr. naukar) (K.Pr. 2, 25, 42). -bāba m. a servant father; one who is a servant by profession. --bĕhun -- m.inf. to sit down as a servant, to take service, become employed (in service) (H. iii, 3; viii, 5). -bāy f. a servant's wife. --cākar -- نوکر چاکر m.pl. servants, domestics, a group of, or the class of, servants.
f. the profession or occupation of a servant, service.

or nōkarī نوکری f. service, attendance (El. naukarī), employment, a post, a situation (H. viii, 5; xii, 3). --cākȧrⁱ -- نوکری چاکری f. the condition of one who lives by service, service as a profession.

m. (sg. dat. nōkas), a point, tip, end; the nib (of a pen); the beak or bill (of a bird); the canthus or corner of the eye (El., cf. nōkhun); (in Kāshmīrī) handsome dress, fine clothing. nōkh-cōkh نوک چوک m. talking by innuendoes, stinging allusions, sarcastic observations; (in Kāshmīrī) splendour of personal appearance. --cārun -- m.inf. to arrange one's appearance, to put on one's best clothes. --thawun -- m.inf. to tidy or arrange one's dress, head-dress, etc.
or nōkal adj. c.g. pointed, having a sharp point.
or nōkdār نوکدار adj. c.g. (as subst., f. nōk(h)dārĕñ ), pointed, having a sharp point; wearing gorgeous apparel, one who is of exalted rank.

or nŏkta نقطہ m. a point; hence, a particular on which one can condemn a person. --karun -- (H. xii, 4) or --raṭun -- (H. xii, 19) m.inf. to make (or catch) some point (against a person, dat.), to get up something (against), catch (a person) tripping.
m. (sg. dat. nōkhanas), a disease of the eyelids, pterygium (El.). Cf. nōkh.
in nokhᵘ-ḍokhᵘ m. an asylum for help, one who, or that which, is come close to help. Cf. nakha-ḍokhᵘ, p. 628b, l. 3.
pointed, having a point. Cf. khᵃñĕ-nŏᵃ, p. 405a, l. 43; khrāvi-nŏkᵘ̈rᵘ̈, p. 416b, l. 6.
f. a complaint or accusation (in a court of law) (El., Gr.M.).

m. a complete, unbroken, cowry (cf. gᵃsa-nolᵃ, p. 307a, l. 18; hāra-nolᵘ, p. 344b, l. 46) (Gr.Gr. 9); hence, a small lump (of anything) (L.V. 81). ¶ nȧlⁱ-baith m. (sg. dat. -baitas), (in gambling) the falling upside down of a cowry (cf. gᵃsa-nolᵃ baith dyunᵘ, p. 307a, l. 20).
adj. c.g. named; hence, well-named, famous, celebrated, notorious.
f. (sg. dat. nōmᵃrüñᵃ), abstracting, abridgment, giving the meaning of a long statement in a few words, making a précis.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nọ̆mᵃrôwᵃ), to depress, prostrate, lay low, cause to bow, to bend (El.); to humiliate, abase, abash; to cause to nod (El.); i.q. nọ̆mᵃrun. nọ̆mᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. nọ̆mᵃrövᵃ -müʦᵘ̈), depressed, prostrated, laid low; humiliated, abased, abashed.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nōmᵃrôwᵃ), to abridge, abstract, make a précis of; i.q. nōmᵃrun. nōmᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. nōmᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), abridged, etc.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nọ̆mᵒrᵒ), to depress, prostrate, lay low, cause to bow (Gr.Gr. 7); to humiliate, abase, abash; cf. nọ̆mᵃrāwun. nọ̆mᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (nọ̆mᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), depressed, prostrated, laid low; humiliated, abased, abashed.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nōmᵒrᵒ), to give the meaning of a long statement in a few words, to abridge, abstract, make a précis of; cf. nōmᵃrāwun. nōmᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. nōmᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), abridged, as ab.
adj. (f. nömᵘ̈), having a name; having such-and-such a name, named (so-and-so) (often --˚) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 782, 796, 959; Rām. 457; K. 373, 485, 635, 670, 687, 714, 867, 887). Cf. nôvᵘ.

m. as much as can be raised on the finger-nail, a very little (of anything) (cf. hissa-nᵒ, p. 354a, l. 49); ʦēra-nᵒ, p. 1079a, l. 48; as adj. (f. nümᵘ̈), thin, wasted away (e.g. a starveling child); cf. nam 1. --aʦun -- m. wasting away (as ab.) to enter (i.e. to become manifest).
m. a group of nine (Gr.Gr. 84); with the suffix of the indefinite article, nomwāh khanḍā, a group of about nine but a little less (Gr.Gr. 84).
i.q. nömī, in the following:--nömⁱ ʦūr m. a notorious thief; hence, (met.) a famous, or well-known, person (whether a thief or not).
in nömⁱ nāma adv. name by name.
f. (sg. dat. nöniki), a cut or wound in a vein or artery.

adj. (f. nüñᵘ̈), naked, bare (cf. nĕtha-nonᵘ, s.v. nĕtha; nakha-nᵒ, p. 628b, l. 10; nanga-nᵒ, s.v. nanga) (L.V. 88; Śiv. 1196, 1651; Rām. 918; K. 825; K.Pr. 86, 154, 159); bare (of a sword) (H. viii, 6); manifest, apparent, open, public (El. nŏn; Śiv. 330, 347, 523, 666, 941, etc.; Rām. 787, 1766); famous, renowned (El. nun; Śiv. 1902; H. vi, 7); clear, bright, cloudless (of the sky) (Śiv. 268, 331); clear, distinct (of a statement) (K. 141); bright, shining (e.g. gold, an ornament); as adv. clearly, manifestly, visibly. ¶ nȧnⁱ pöṭhⁱ or nȧnⁱ pöṭhin adv. clearly, manifestly, publicly, visibly. ¶ nonuy adj. (nonᵘ + emphatic y), absolutely naked, stark naked (L.V. 46); as adv. shamelessly (u.w. vbs. of abusing and the like). note that in K. 141, nonuy wanun means "to speak plainly". ¶ nañi rāgi adv. on the bare back (e.g. of a horse, or of a man being whipped, etc.).
for nāñ, q.v. in ōra-nöñᵘ̈, p. 42a, l. 2.

adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, nān نان, bread; hence, nönⁱ-yār m. a bread-friend, a sham friend, a false friend, one outwardly friendly (but not heart to heart), a superficial friend (K.Pr. 5). nönⁱ-yārⁱz f. superficial friendship.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nö̃panôwᵘ), to cause to shine (Gr.Gr. 174). See nö̃pun.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. nö̃pyōv), to shine, gleam, beam, glow, sparkle, glisten, glitter, glare (Śiv. 1707, Rām. 1755); cf. naph. The causal of this verb is nö̃panāwun, not nö̃pᵃrāwun (Gr.Gr. 174). nö̃pyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nö̃pyē-müʦᵘ̈), polished so as to shine, (of something formerly not bright, but now rendered) brilliant, glittering, etc.

or nörijᵘ̈ f. a gutter, drain, conduit, waterpipe (Gr.Gr. 65, Śiv. 1213). ¶ nörija-dag f. the fall of a stream of water shooting out of an elevated drain or gutter and falling from a height to the ground. -wôñᵘ m. water flowing through a conduit.
m. a coco-nut (Gr.M.); a ḥuqqa, or tobacco-pipe, made of a coco-nut; cf. nörⁱjīl. -dŏd the milk of the coco-nut. -gūjᵘ̈ f. the kernel of a coco-nut.
adj. c.g. stringy (of some vegetable which, even when cooked, is full of tough stringy fibres). Cf. nörᵘ̈ 1.

m. the arm or sleeve of a coat (cf. okᵘ-nᵘ, p. 19a, l. 28; cūri-nᵒ, p. 175a, l. 17; kŏrāba-nᵒ, p. 468b, l. 2; marda-nᵒ, p. 589b, l. 26) (Gr.Gr. 9, 33; W. 135; K.Pr. 154, nuruí; 248, 262). --phirith -- adv., lit. having turned back the sleeves, i.e. with the cuffs turned up (L. 459). ¶ nȧrⁱ-kōca m. a piece of cloth cut for making a sleeve. --khȧrⁱ 2 -- (for 1, see nar 1) adj. c.g. unevenly made or divided (of a garment, or piece of land). --khȧrⁱ karun -- m.inf. (of a garment or piece of land) to make uneven, to divide unequally or unevenly. -kūṭᵘ m. a ceiling rafter. -ʦhọ̆ṭᵘ m. (of a coat) short-sleeved. -ʦhyonᵘ (f. -ʦhë˘ñᵘ̈), (of a garment) having the sleeves cut or torn off. -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), (of a garment) having the sleeves cut off. -wār m. a kind of embroidered cuff (made of brocaded silk, etc.) worn at the ends of the sleeves, donned by rich women or brides. -wār khỗṭᵘ m. the half of a pair of such cuffs, a single cuff of a pair. -zyūṭhᵘ  adj. (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈), (of a garment) long-sleeved (cf. zēṭhĕn narĕn, a sign of respectability, K.Pr. 262). ¶ nari-nērē adv. very near, close by (Rām. 248); cf. nyūrᵘ 3. -norᵘ adv. from sleeve to sleeve; hence, secretly, privately (esp. between two persons). -norᵘ bōzun m.inf. (between two persons) to act in mutual privacy.

m. a pipe, tube, drain-pipe, water-pipe, tubular conduit (cf. añĕma-nᵒ, p. 37b, l. 4; dᵃ̇hᵃ̇-nᵃ̇, p. 108b, l. 24; daman-nᵒ, p. 220a, l. 25; ganḍa-nᵒ, p. 289b, l. 8; kalam-nᵒ, p. 439b, l.46); any long hollow receptacle (cf. kāna-nᵒ, p. 449a, l. 17); a tubular intestine (esp. one of larger size) (cf. ạndᵃram-nᵃ, p. 32b, l. 44; bīka-nᵒ, p. 99b, l. 33; dasta-nᵒ, p. 256a, l. 41; guhⁱ-nⁱ, p. 280b, l. 32; mᵃtra-nᵃ, p. 605b, l. 20; nika-nᵒ, p. 627b, l. 21); a tube of the body through which the vital airs pass (i.q. nāḍi, q.v.) (Śiv. 1889). ¶ nörⁱ-dag f. the fall of a spout of water issuing from a pipe high up. -kūṭᵘ m. a blow-pipe (the implement). -kaʦul m. a vessel with a spout, used in offering liquid libations; cf. kaʦul. -wan m. a red yellow and white thread used for tying round the fore-arm on festive occasions. -wan-band m. such a thread only one span long. -wan-dastār m. a turban ornamented with this thread, worn (esp. by boys) on festive or ritual occasions. -wan khārȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. (at the ceremony of a Brāhmaṇa boy's initiation with the sacred cord) the particular ceremony of tying his hair with this thread. -wath f. the narrow path along the bottom of a 'nullah' (cf. nār 2).

m. (pl. nom. nörᵘ̈), a muscle, a tendon; a tube of the body through which the vital airs pass (i.q. nāḍi, q.v.) (Śiv. 969); a vein (El. nãr, naur); the tough fibres or strings in a vegetable (cf. nörᵃl). --kaḍȧnⁱ -- m.pl. 'to pull out the muscles'; hence, to pound rice till it is reduced to powder. --khasȧnⁱ -- m.pl. the tendons to rise, i.e. the muscles to swell up (from anger, e.g. the swelling of the muscles of the cheek).

f. (pl. nom. nārĕ), a water- jar, shaped like a gourd, with a neck (cf. cāhⁱ (or cāyĕ)-nᵒ, pp. 158a, l. 12; 179a, l. 22; kalashĕ-nᵒ, p. 441a, l. 49); a cup, a dish, a trough (cf. añĕma-nᵒ, p. 37b, l. 6; dŏda-nᵒ, p. 189b, l. 40; dŏyĕn-nᵒ, p. 269b, l. 46; guras-nᵒ, p. 304b, l. 2). nārĕ-golᵘ m. the neck of such a jar.
f. (pl. nom. nārĕ), a small stream, a conduit (such as that used in irrigating a rice-field).

(or, by paṇḍits,) f. a son's wife, a daughter-in-law (cf. bĕnath-nᵒ, p. 114b, l. 12; bāpath-nᵒ, p. 116a, l. 44; bāwᵃza-nᵃ, p. 148a, l. 43; dyārath-nᵒ, p. 271a, l. 43; dyārathᵃr-nᵃ, p. 271b, l. 1; hashĕ-nŏshĕ, p. 352b, l. 26) (Gr.Gr. 16, 72; W. 142; Rām. 136, 848; K. 750, 752, 831, 914; K.Pr. 80, 141, 157-8, 164, 214, 246). ¶ nŏshĕ-bāv m. the relationship or condition of daughter-in-law. -mahanyuwᵘ m. a daughter-in-law person, i.e. a woman who bears the relationship of daughter-in-law to some one. -tônᵘ m. the conditions implied by the relationship of daughter-in-law.
m. a drink, a draught, an antidote (cf. nōshĕ-dārōh, p. 236a, l. 49) (Rām. 901).
adj. c.g. destructive, destroying; perishing, perishable, destructible, mortal (Gr.M.).
m., i.q. nạshᵉ̆ran, q.v. The word is reported to be m., but nạshᵉ̆ran is f.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nöshᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), i.q. nöshᵉ̆run, see nạshᵉ̆run (Rām. 959). nöshᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. nöshᵉ̆rövᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), i.q. nöshᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, s.v. nöshᵉ̆run.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nöshᵒrᵒ), i.q. nạshᵉ̆run, q.v.; cf. nöshᵉ̆rāwun. nöshᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. nöshᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. nạshᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, s.v. nạshᵉ̆run, q.v.
m. a destroyer, as in wata-nôshᵘ, a way-destroyer; hence, a highway robber (L.V. 43).
f. destruction, waste (cf. dŏha-nöshⁱ, p. 200a, l. 21), i.q. nāsh, q.v.
or nŏksa m. a copy; a writing-book, copy-book; a recipe, prescription (of medicine, or ingredients for any composition) (Gr.M.).
adj. (f. nüstᵘ̈), one whose nose has been cut off, noseless; one with a very small nose (cf. khᵃñĕ-nᵃ, p. 405a, l. 47; muka-nᵒ, p. 559a, l. 31) (Gr.Gr. 137).
f. a stove, a fire-place with a chimney, i.q. bukhörⁱ, q.v. (Rām. 1069).
m. (sg. dat. nōṭas), a bank-note (the English word).
in nöth-hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -hishᵘ̈), satiated (with food), gorged, replete, surfeited.
f. (sg. dat. nö̃ṭhi), the winking or twinkling of the eye (cf. ȧchⁱ-nö̃ṭh, p. 8a, l. 47) (Śiv. 1209, K. 206).

m. a eunuch, one who conducts himself like a eunuch, an effeminate man; impotent, incapable of begetting children; (in character) ignorant, uneducated, fruitless. -dã̄d m. a castrated ox, a bullock. -monᵘ adj. (f. -müñᵘ̈), one employed in a fruitless task; one who works at a task in such a manner that his task is fruitless. -pyāv m. a fœtus being born before its proper time, a miscarriage, abortion.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. nö̃ṭhyōv. Also treated as a verb of the 2nd conj., with 1 p.p. nū̃ṭhᵘ, which is also attributed to nashun, q.v., cf. nôṭhᵘ), to be ruined, spoiled (Gr.M.); to turn out badly, to be in a bad condition (Gr.M.); to be or become fruitless, to have no fruit, to be barren or impotent. Cf. nö̃chᵃrun and nö̃ṭhᵃrun, which are causals of this verb. ¶ nū̃ṭhᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nǖ̃ṭhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), ruined, spoiled, etc. (by some cause). ¶ nö̃ṭhyō-motᵘ  perf. part. (f. nö̃ṭhyē-müʦᵘ̈), gone bad, gone to ruin, etc.
or nǖ̃ṭhᵃran f. (sg. dat. nö̃ṭhᵃrüñᵃ or nǖ̃ṭhᵃrüñᵃ), ruining, spoiling, breaking; (of a person) leading wrong, debauching.

or nǖ̃ṭhᵃrun conj. 1 (1 p.p. nö̃ṭhᵒrᵒ or nǖ̃ṭhᵒrᵒ), to ruin, spoil; to break; to lead (a person) wrong, to debauch. nö̃ṭhᵒrᵒ-motᵒ or nǖ̃ṭhᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. nö̃ṭhᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ or nǖ̃ṭhᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), ruined, spoiled; broken; led into evil courses. This verb is a causal of nö̃ṭhun, q.v.
m. a small penis (a term used in ridicule or abuse).
adj. (f. nö̃ṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat. nã̄chĕ), destroyed, ruined, spoiled, put out of order (cf. nẹ̆ndᵃri-nᵃ, p. 642b, l. 14); as good as ruined, going to ruin. Cf. nū̃ṭhᵘ, s.v. naṣḥun, and nö̃ṭhun.

m. a jar, a pitcher, a jug with a long neck (cf. ā̃cār-nᵒ, p. 9b, l. 47; māga-noṭᵘ darun, p. 551b, l. 33) (Śiv. 1503, 1559, 1818; H. iii, 5, 9; xi, 13; K.Pr. 11, 12, 82, 155, 159, 160); an earthen- ware well-bucket (cf. nȧṭⁱ-bāv, p. 146b, l. 27). ¶ nȧṭⁱ-örⁱ f. a circular ring of grass-rope used for supporting a full jar on the head or on the ground, etc. -bĕha m. a wooden or rope ring for supporting a full jar. -golᵘ m. the neck of a water-jar. -kāh f. (sg. dat. -köshᵘ̈), the eleventh lunar day of the light half of the month of Zēṭh (Skt. Jyaiṣṭha = May-June) on which high caste Hindūs fast and worship with fruit, flowers, and jars filled with water and with milk. -katurᵘ m. a broken part (of the lower globular portion) of a jar. -katürᵘ̈ f. a potsherd. -mal m. the sediment which collects and fouls the bottom of the inside of a jar. -sag m. watering a garden or the like with water from a jar (and not directly from irrigation channels). -sörᵘ̈ f. collecting water or the like by carrying it in jars.
m. a piece of flesh (cf. nika-nᵒ, p. 627b, l. 24, and nyukᵘ nᵒ); cf. nāṭh. nöṭⁱ-wāza m. an imperfectly trained cook, a bad cook.
or nỗṭᵘ (cf. p. 461b, l. 23) m. a round piece of rough stone, a pebble (cf. kañi-nᵒ, p. 461b, l. 23).
f. raking up an old story against a person (Gr.Gr. 121).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nọ̆wᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. nọ̆vᵃrun, q.v. (El. nauráwun). nọ̆wᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. nọ̆wᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. nọ̆wᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, q.v., s.v. nọ̆vᵃrun.

or nọ̆wᵃrāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. nọ̆wᵒrᵒ), to cause to have ample results (e.g. to cause a seed to give great produce; or a great event to be made to spring from a trivial cause) (Gr.Gr. 7); to increase (tr.) (El. nauráwun). nọ̆wᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. nọ̆vᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), that which has been caused to have ample results, a great result caused to spring from a trivial cause.
adj. (f. növᵘ̈), for nāv 1, at the end of an adjectival compound, possessing a name (as in lacha-nᵒ, p. 506b, l. 43, possessing a hundred thousand names, Śiv. 53, 834); named (so and so). Cf. nômᵘ.

m. the ceremony observed on first cooking, at an auspicious moment, the new rice of the year's crop; cf. ala-nowᵘ, p. 22b, l. 21, the festival of the new pumpkin crop. --dyunᵘ -- m. to observe the ceremony of eating the new rice (Rām. 1661). ¶ nȧvⁱ-bôgⁱ m. a present of the new rice sent with money, etc., to a newly married bride by her relations. -sāl m. an invitation to the festival of cooking the new rice (esp. one sent to a son-in-law and his friends by the wife's relations).

adj. (f. nüvᵘ̈), new, fresh, recent, novel (El. nú, nau; Gr.Gr. 138; Gr.M.; L.V. 93; Śiv. 425, 943, 1597; Rām. 10, 1321, 1341, 1369, 1464; H. i, 11; K. 210-11; K.Pr. 87 (fresh milk), 159); recent, modern (Śiv. 1506, 1545); new, fresh (of age) (YZ. 553, K.Pr. 252); strange; (as adv.) recently (El., K.Pr. 158). In some compounds this word takes the form nav- or nawa-, see nav 2. nowuy nowᵘ, altogether new (Śiv. 1705, 1756; K. 324). The fem. of this word nüvᵘ̈, a new woman, is used as a substantive to mean 'a new wife' (married after two or three former wives have died); cf. navĕ-hondᵘ, bel. (K.Pr. 156). --bahār -- (= نوبہار) m. early spring (Śiv. 54). --kadal -- m. the 'New Bridge', the N. of the sixth bridge across the river Vĕṭh, or Jehlam, in the city of Śrīnagar (El. nú kadal). ¶ navĕ-hondᵘ adj. (f. gen.) (f. -hünzᵘ̈), (gen. of nüvᵘ̈, see ab.) of, or belonging to, any female being or thing; of, or belonging to, a new (additional) bride (married after the death of former wives) (K.Pr. 156). -hondᵘ navīd m. the glad tidings of the new bride, i.e. the birth of a child to a new bride (i.e. a bride who has been married as the successor to two or three previous wives). ¶ nȧvⁱ-sondⁱ adj. (f. -sünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, any new male animate being. ¶ navi sara adv. again. ¶ nüvᵘ̈ puy f. new offspring; new creation, new nature, the new times (as contrasted favourably with former times). ¶ navyukᵘ adj. (f. navicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, any new inanimate thing or action.
f. (sg. dat. nowᵘrüñᵘ), making new, renovation.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nowᵘrôwᵘ), i.q. nowᵘrun, q.v. (Śiv. 1506, 1756). nowᵘrôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nowᵘrövᵘ-müʦᵘ), i.q. nowᵘrᵘ-motᵘ, s.v. nowᵘrun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. nowᵘrᵘ), to renew (Śiv. 1506, 1756, nowᵘrāwun), to make as good as new; to cause to increase, to make abundant. nowᵘrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nowᵘrᵘ-müʦᵘ), renewed, made new, made abundant, made to increase.
m. a barber (El. nái). Cf. nöyid.

m. (f. nāyë˘zᵘ̈), a barber (El. naid; L. 457, 458; H. v, 6; xi, 18; xii, 4, 5, 10, 13, etc.; K. 972; K.Pr. 111, written náwid). -bāpār m. the profession of a barber, a barber's work (even when done by one who is not a barber by profession). -bāy f. a barber's wife. -khyusᵘ m. a barber's wallet (in which he carries his tools). -wān m. a barber's shop. -zang f. a present for luck given to a barber for shaving a bridegroom and his friends.
f. the profession of a barber.
a beholder, inspector, observer; an inspector, superintendent, supervisor; the sheriff of a court, the executive officer of a court (Rām. 581); (in Kāshmīrī) a head cook (K.Pr. 81).
f. blandishment; (in Kāshmīrī) a source of hoped for help.
or (El.) nāzuk نازک adj. c.g. thin, slender, slim (El.); delicate, tender (Gr.M.; Rām. 185, 1205, 1223, 1226); neat, elegant, gracious (El.).
or nruga-rāza m. N.P. name of a son of Manu Vaivasvata, who was reborn as a lizard (K. 840).
the spelling for nowᵘ 2, used by El.
in nūjĕ karñĕ (for --karañĕ --) f.pl. suddenly and unexpectedly to burst out in abuse; to imitate weeping, talking, etc.
m. loss, waste; loss, damage (Gr.M., W. 136); injury, harm (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to injure (El.).

m. a mongoose, an ichneumon (L. 109, Rām. 97); (according to El.) a rat, a weasel. ¶ nūla-cika f.pl. the cry of the mongoose; a similar cry uttered by a human being or beast. -har f. a fight between mongooses, or a fight between a mongoose and a snake; met. a fight between men or animals in which each is regardless of wounds. -kala m. one who has a mongoose's head, i.e. a person possessing a head with a long fine snout. -wöjᵘ̈ f. the hole of a mongoose (i.e. its den).

or sometimes spelt nun (which is also written for nunᵘ) m. salt (cf. basi-nᵒ, p. 131a, l. 48; ḍāka-nᵒ, p. 205b, l. 31; krē̃ka-nᵒ, p. 470a, l. 18) (Gr.Gr. 18; Gr.M.; L. 463; W. 136; Rām. 187, 842; H. v, 6, nun; K.Pr. 36, 66, 71, 109, 153, 159, 218, 245). According to El. (s.v. nun) two varieties of salt are found in the bāzārs of Kashmīr, viz. rock salt, from the Panjāb, and powder salt, called Bŏṭa nūn, from Ladak. The former is about twice as dear as the latter. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to feed (cattle, horses, etc.) with salt (K.Pr. 149); to put salt (into something, e.g. to sow salt in earth; cf. mĕʦi nūndᵒ, p. 609a, l. 6).--nābadgaʦhun -- m.inf. salt to become (as scarce as) sugar-candy; something usually easily obtainable to become unobtainable (e.g. owing to poverty or the like even some cheap necessary to be unobtainable). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. salt to fall (instead of rain), i.e. something to be greatly missed (e.g. the regret felt for some person or thing lost, until it is restored). --ʦēṭani bĕhun -- m.inf. to sit at salt pounding (i.e. to be reduced to this employment); hence, owing to becoming blind or maimed, to be unable to work. ¶ nūna-atha m. a hand of salt; the becoming fruitless (of some work begun under favourable auspices). -bāṭh m. (sg. dat. bāṭhas; his wife is -bāṭhĕñ or -böṭhiñ), a salt carrier, a man who conveys salt (on camels, bullocks, etc.) from the mine, etc., to the market. -böṭhᵘ̈ f. a load of salt (carried on a camel or the like. It weighs 160 seers); cf. -guna, bel. -böṭhil f. the trade of salt-carrying. -dᵃhᵃrᵃ f. three seers weight of salt (cf. dᵃhᵃrᵃ 2). -ḍünḍᵘ̈ f. the beam of the scales used for weighing salt. -drāg m. a salt famine, scarcity of salt, extreme high price of salt. -guna f. a pack-saddle load of salt, 160 seers of salt; cf. -böṭhᵘ̈, ab. -gurⁱ m.pl. horses of salt (which quickly melt away); hence, false conciliation, swindling negotiation, inducing by false promises. -gurⁱ hāwȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to display salt horses, to induce by false promises, as ab. -khan f. (sg. dat. -khüñᵘ̈), a salt mine; cf. khān 3. -khĕʦürᵘ̈ f. too salt pottage (see khĕʦürᵘ̈ 2). -kamöyⁱ f. labour at salt, labour in the salt mines. -kamyulᵘ m. a worker in salt mines (whose hair, features, and body generally are white with salt powder). -kān f. (sg. dat. -köñᵘ̈), a salt mine; cf. kān 2. -küñᵘ̈ f. a lump of rock salt. -krē̃kh m. (sg. dat. -krē̃kas), a crystal of salt (clear and transparent. It is used as a stone in signet rings, see krē̃kh). -kara-wôñᵘ m. salt water boiled down, brine. -maza m. a salt taste, saltishness, the taste of salt (even though no salt be present). -nār hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -nār hishᵘ̈), like a fire of salt; hence, furiously angry (esp. of a master or senior angry with a servant or junior). -pholᵘ m. a lump of salt (not more than about two pounds in weight) (K.Pr. 95). -phȧlⁱ gaʦhȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to become lumps of salt; (of the hands or fingers) to be shrivelled and shrunk with cold. -pal m. a piece of salt weighing about four tōlās. -pēn f. (sg. dat. -pīñᵘ̈), forcibly putting lumps of salt into the mouth of a cow or similar animal. -pyushᵘ m. a flea of salt, a very small speck of salt. -shrād m. an offering of salt to the manes of the deceased made on the fourth day after death by his heirs. -ṭujⁱ or -ṭujᵘ̈ f. a lump of salt; f. of -ṭulᵘ, bel. in a dim. sense. -ṭukh m. (sg. dat. ṭukas), a very small piece of salt. -ṭulᵘ m. a lump of salt (larger than -tujᵘ̈, q.v.) (K.Pr. 147). -tral f. a large heavy lump of salt. -trēsh gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. salt-thirst to occur; hence, distress to be experienced by the non-obtainment or withholding of necessary supplies preventing the performance of some urgent and necessary work. -trēsh karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to cause distress, as ab. -ʦāl f. a handful of powdered salt scattered through the fingers. -ʦamal adj. c.g. salt-skinned, having the skin fouled by sweat, etc. -ʦopᵘ m. a small amount of salt (esp. powdered). -wān m. a place where salt is to be got (e.g. a pit where it is dug, or a site where it is piled, or where it is sold). -wôñᵘ 1 m. salt water, water in which salt is dissolved, or which tastes salt. -wôñᵘ 2 m. a salt merchant. -wöñil f. the business of a salt merchant. -zahār adj. c.g. (of food) spoiled, uneatable, on account of being too salt.
m. N. of a village about fourteen or fifteen miles north of Śrīnagar in Lār Pargana, and (according to El.) said to be fruitful, populous, and salubrious (Śiv. 1681, 1889; Rām. 244 (nūnar)).
f. N. of a certain vegetable, described as cooling, bland, and purificatory of the blood. According to L. 75 it is used in medicine as an internal styptic. nunari-byôlᵘ m. its seed.

m. (f. -böñᵘ̈), a darling child (esp. a child born in old age, or born in a wealthy family); a darling generally (Śiv. 940, 1543; Rām. 247; YZ. 148, 173, 378); (of a child) pretty (El. nundbón) (K.Pr. 156).
m. N. of a sacred lake on Mount Haramŏkh (see p. 343a, l. 31) below lake Gangabal (see p. 291b, l. 33). Its Sanskrit name was Kālôdaka or Nandisaras (see RT.Tr. II, 407).

m. saltness, a salty flavour, piquancy; the possession of excellent qualities, a deservedly high reputation. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. saltness to become; hence (of one who has long been childless, or whose position in life has been humble, etc.), a sudden rise in prosperity, repute, or happiness (by the birth of a son, increase in possessions, elevation in rank, etc.).
nūnṭhᵘ-motᵘ, see nū̃ṭhᵘ, nū̃ṭhᵘ-motᵘ, s.vv. nashun and nö̃ṭhun.

conj. 3 (1 p.p. nunyōv), to be (or become) salted (esp. too salt); (of something not salted, but for some other reason) salty, tasting saltish. nunyō-motᵘ  perf. part. (f. nunyē-müʦᵘ̈), salted, esp. too salt; become salty in taste (without salt, as ab.).
f. a house, esp. a large dwelling in a village or in a forest. According to El. the word is in use towards Warahmul (Bāramūla).

adj. (f. nuñᵘ̈), salty, too salt (of food or the like) (Gr.Gr. 15, nun; W. 6, nun; K.Pr. 93, nun). ¶ nunⁱ-pōsh m. a certain wild flowering plant, the violet (so called because villagers exchange violets for salt; L. 464, nuna posh). ¶ nuñᵘ̈ ʦam f. the skin of a person foul with sweat.

m. light, brilliance, splendour (cf. bē-nūr, p. 114a, l. 40) (Śiv. 325, 619, 833, 1292, 1775; H. vii, 6; YZ. 61, 114, 174; K.Pr. 159, 243); brightness, cheerfulness (K.Pr. 84, 160). nār path gav az-nūr, the fire retreated from brightness, i.e. ceased blazing (Rām. 1081).

f. the arm (from the shoulder to the hand) (cf. khōvürᵘ̈ nᵒ, p. 425b, l. 23; nāras narĕ diñe, p. 648b, l. 30) (Gr.Gr. 10, 33; K.Pr. 57; Śiv. 1065, 1441, 1725; Rām. 410, 630, 1578; H. xii, 15; K. 161, 563, 791, 827; K.Pr. 25, 57, 248, 261); the arm (of a garment) (K. 419). ¶ narĕ-holᵘ adj. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), crooked-armed, bent-armed. -horᵘ m. the pair of arms (of a man). --tarañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to wave or flourish the arms, as if in a fight. -ʦhọ̆ṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦhŏ̈ṭᵘ̈), short-armed. -ʦhyonᵘ adj. (f. -ʦhë˘ñᵘ̈), one whose arm has been cut off, armless. -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), id. (cf. K. 791, 827). --wāyĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to throw the arms up and down (as in pain or trouble). -zyūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈), long-armed. ¶ nari nyūrᵘ adj. (f.--nīrᵘ̈ --), close to the arm, very near (Rām. 248).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. nǖ̃ṭhᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. nö̃ṭhᵃrun, q.v. nǖ̃ṭhᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. nǖ̃ṭhᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. nö̃ṭhᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, q.v., s.v. nö̃ṭhᵃrun.
nū̃ṭhᵘ, nū(nū̃)ṭhᵘ-motᵘ , nǖ(nũ̄̈)ṭhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ , see nashun and nö̃ṭhun.

(for 1, see naʦun) f. a plug in a pipe or the like to stop the flow of liquid (Śiv. 1874). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a hole to be plugged, as ab.; met. (of a woman) suppression of the menses to occur. --ʦalüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the plug to come away, the obstruction to a flow of liquid to be removed; esp. an attack of profuse urination or diarrhœa to come on.

m. the last trace or remains of something destroyed (K.Pr. 172). --hāwun -- m.inf. to display the traces left by something after its destruction (e.g. the skin of a dead animal, or the rags of a destroyed garment). --thawun -- m.inf. to keep the remains of something destroyed (e.g. as evidence, or for sentimental reasons).
m. comfort, convenience, ease; a benefit, a favour, boon, blessing; a delicacy, a dainty; cf. niyĕmath. -hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -hishᵘ̈), very sweet, a great delicacy.

adj. c.g. separate, distinct, different. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain apart; to keep away from any work or business. --thawun -- m.inf. to put apart, to put to one side; to separate (a person) from some work.
m. a knife for cutting the nails of the fingers and toes, a nail-cutter (Śiv. 414).

m. a deposit, a pledge; (among Hindūs) assignment of the various parts of the body to different deities, which is usually accompanied by prayers and corresponding gesticulations. --thawun -- m.inf. to give a pledge, to make a deposit.
m. the top part of a doorway, a lintel (cf. bar-nᵒ, p. 116b, l. 23; hanga-nᵒ, p. 338b, l. 42) (W. 129, K.Pr. 45). nyāsa-hang  m. the face of a lintel (cf. hanga-nyās, ab.).
m. (sg. dat. nyāsatas), the business or practice of giving pledges.

conj. 1 (1 pp. nyôwᵘ 2) (causal of nyunᵘ), to cause to take, to cause to take away (Gr.Gr. 172, Śiv. 1863); to cause to be taken away, have sent forth, have despatched (H. xi, 6); cf. niwanāwun. nyôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nyövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to be taken away.

m. discussion, quarrel, dispute (cf. ashᵉ̆ka-nᵉ̆, p. 48b, l. 37; ducĕ-nᵒ, p. 185b, l. 15; duk-nᵒ and duka-nᵒ, p. 207a, ll. 16, 19) (Śiv. 1816, Rām. 1142, YZ. 310, K.Pr. 103); tumult, quarrel, fight (El. nyáí); justice (Gr.M.); a decision (e.g. the resultant fate shown by an astrological calculation, Rām. 420; or the decision of fate, Rām. 1710). --andun -- m.inf. a dispute to be settled, a lawsuit to be decided (K. 847). --ạnzᵃrun -- or --ạnzᵃrāwun -- m.inf. to settle a quarrel, decide a lawsuit. --karun -- m.inf. to fight (El.); to argue, dispute (Rām. 104, 484, 1212, 1263). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. a quarrel to occur. --tulun -- m.inf. to raise a quarrel. --wŏthun -- m.inf. a quarrel to arise. ¶ nyāyĕ-kartā m. a doer of justice, just (Gr.M.). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without dispute, indisputable. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), full of dispute, disputable (of some subject of a quarrel).
m. a clenched fist, the fist (El.). nĕkⁱ lāyȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to strike blows with the clenched fist.

m. (sg. ag. nĕmbⁱ, or, in composition, sometimes nĕmⁱ), the fruit or berry of the nimba tree (Melia azadirachta) (a bitter berry, used in medicine as a febrifuge); a lemon (Gr.M.). ¶ nĕmⁱ-bạrⁱg m. its leaf or leaves (also used as a medicine, in poultices for wounds, and chewed at funeral ceremonies). ¶ nĕmbⁱ-ras m. its juice, used as a febrifuge medicine.
or nyömᵘ̈ f. a kind of stone mortar (in which articles are pounded) (W. 6, ṇiām).

or nĕñĕ 1 (for 2, see s.v.) or ñoñᵘ adj. (f. në̆ñᵘ̈ or ñë˘ñᵘ̈), destitute of energy, dull, slack, torpid, sluggish; without bravery, poor-spirited. ¶ nĕñĕ-mŏnḍȧjⁱ or -mŏnḍüjᵘ̈ f. a female frog. -mŏnḍaji-hāyukh m. (sg. dat. -mŏnḍaji-hāyĕkas), a scalepan of frogs (which it is impossible to weigh owing to their jumping about); an uncontrolled or ungovernable body of men. -monḍukh m. (sg. dat. -mŏnḍakas), a male frog.

m. (sg. dat. nyŏpas), the act of eating, devouring, swallowing; cf. nĕph or ñĕph. --karun -- m.inf. to swallow, devour; (met.) to devour (i.e. misappropriate) (another's wealth). ¶ nyŏpas ladun m.inf. to bring to swallowing, i.e. to swallow down something large at one gulp; met. to devour (i.e. misappropriate) (another's property).

m. (sg. dat. nyŏṭhas), the thumb (cf. atha-nᵒ, p. 60b, l. 18; khŏra- (khōra-)nᵒ, the great toe, p. 409b, l. 22; p. 410b, l. 4) (K. 631; El. noṭh, nyaṭ, nyauṭ, nyeṭ, nyuṭ). ¶ nyŏṭha-jŏrāba m. a thumb-stocking, a knitted stocking (with a separate stall for the great toe). -ʦhyonᵘ m. (f. -ʦhë˘ñᵘ̈), one whose thumb or great toe has been cut off; a glove or stocking from which the stall for the thumb or great toe has been cut off. -ʦoṭᵘ m. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), id. ¶ nyŏṭhas ʦỗgᵘdazun m inf. the lamp to burn the thumb; met. to be a habitual robber, thief, or misappropriator.
m. a skilled accountant, a rapid (arithmetical) calculator.

or nyoṭhᵘ m. a thumb-ring (cf. gö̃ḍa-nᵒ, p. 277a, l. 48). Cf. në̆ṭhᵘ̈ 1. ¶ nyŏṭhⁱ ongᵘjᵘ f. a false conditional promise (when the promiser falsely promises to do something, if the other person will do something specified first).

m. a certain plant described as a 'land-growing lotus', and said to have a flower externally red and white within, ? Hibiscus mutabilis (? El. nyío, a flower of Kashmīr; probably the neaó posh of L. 459, where it is translated 'carnation'; Śiv. 54; Rām. 1090); cf. baḍa-nᵒ, p. 82b, l. 25. nyövⁱ-wuḍar m. a tract of high dry land covered with these plants.

adj. (f. nicᵘ̈), slender, lean, fine, thin (Gr.Gr. 30, 139; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 160); mean, ignoble, worthless (Gr.M.); small, not worthy of consideration, contemptible (K. 364); small, tiny (in this case often at the end of a compound as in khōra-nᵒ, small footed, p. 410b, l. 2; so ȧchⁱ-nⁱ, p. 8a, l. 50; ösᵘ̈-nᵘ̈, p. 46b, l. 9; atha-nᵒ, p. 60b, l. 18) (Rām. 1611); cf. nika. --nôṭᵘ -- m. a collection of small pieces. --nyukᵘ -- adj. (f. nicᵘ̈nicᵘ̈), small (and) small, i.e. (of a numbering of things) each small; slender all over (K. 74); nyukᵘ nyukᵘ gāsh, very slight beams of light, daybreak (K.Pr. 176). --sukᵘ adj. (f. nicᵘ̈ sᵘcᵘ), (a jingle formation) a little, a few small (pieces, out of a mass of all sizes large and small) (Gr.Gr. 95). ¶ nicĕ gāḍa f.pl. a shoal of small fishes; a crowd of small fishes collected in a net. Cf. nika gāḍa (p. 627b, l. 8). ¶ nicᵘ̈ picᵘ̈ f. (of a woman) slender or delicate in every limb. --yĕḍ -- f. (sg. dat. nicĕ yüḍᵘ̈,), the lower belly, the part below the navel.

adj. (m. sg. dat. nīlis, abl. nīli, Gr.Gr. 59; f. nījᵘ̈ 2, for 1, see s.v.) dark blue, blue (cf. aḍa-nᵒ, p. 11b, l. 24) (Gr.M., Rām. 1502); green (cf. aḍa-nᵒ, as ab.) (Gr.Gr. 19, Gr.M.); dark-coloured, livid; green, luxuriant (L.V. 36); fresh, moist, not dried (cf. aḍa-nᵒ, as ab.); unripe (Gr.Gr. 19); not cooked, raw, fresh; cf. nīl 2. --kāʦhhyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. nījᵘ̈ kāʦh hishᵘ̈), very green-coloured (e.g. of a person suffering from sorrow or disease, corresponding to our livid); very green (applied to an inanimate object, e.g. a stone or a plant); very fresh and moist, not dried. ¶ nījᵘ̈y, see nyūluy, bel. ¶ nīlⁱ-pholⁱ m. a kind of small green glass, or crystal, beads worn by women, hanging down from the hair behind. -phȧlⁱ-dār adj. c.g. wearing a string of green glass, or crystal, beads, as ab. ¶ nīli-gŏta m. a dive into blue (of a garment, cloth, etc.), the being dipped into, or soaked in, a blue dye. -khum or -khumb m. a dyer's vat full of blue dye. -phĕkh m. (sg. dat. -phĕki), blue dye powder. -ranga adj. c.g. green coloured. ¶ nīlis drôtᵘ dyunᵘ m.inf. to put the sickle to the green (crop); met. to destroy something before it is ripe or completed, to destroy at the very inception. --drôtᵘ lagun -- m.inf. to be destroyed at the birth or on inception. ¶ nyūluy  adj. (f. nījᵘ̈y), unripe, not dried up, green and juicy; not cooked, raw.

conj. 1 irreg. [inf. and fut. pass. part. nyunᵘ or (Gr.Gr. 112, 192; Rām. 150, 718, 1105, 1642); acc. ninas (Gr.Gr. 112, 192; Śiv. 1385) or ninis (Gr.Gr. 192); ag. ninan (Śiv. 1004); abl. nina or nini (K. 747); gen. nyunukᵘ (Rām. 953); pl. nom. ninⁱ (Gr.Gr. 14); f. sg. nom. niñᵘ̈ (Rām. 613); pres. part. niwān (Gr.Gr. 103, 168, 194; Rām. 26, 928, 1179, 1525; K. 205; YZ. 413); impers. fut. part. ninī (Gr.Gr. 111); conj. part. nith (Gr.Gr. 104, 198; Śiv. 995; Rām. 374, 942, 1160, 1167, 1622; K. 2, 21, 92, 125); neg. conj. part. ninay (Gr.Gr. 111); freq. part. ni ni (Gr.Gr. 105) or nith nith (id.); adverbial participle niwönⁱ (Gr.Gr. 196); n.ag. 1 niwawunᵘ (Gr.Gr. 105, 192); 2 ninawôlᵘ (Gr.Gr, 106, 193); 3 ninagrākh (Gr.Gr. 106, 193). ¶ fut. (Gr.Gr. 202) sg. 1 nima (Śiv. 1579); nimath, thee (Śiv. 631, Rām. 1027); nimas, his, her (Rām. 323, 548); 2 nikh (Śiv. 635); nihan, her (Śiv. 413); 3 niyi (K.Pr. 83, nĕyi), with hon. suff. niyō (Śiv. 227); niyĕm, me (Śiv. 882; Rām. 661, 1667; K. 938); pl. 1 nimav (H. xii, 19); nimōn, him (YZ. 119); 2 niyiv; 3 nin (Gr.Gr. 13; Śiv. 80; Rām. 363); ninay, thee (K.Pr. 57, ninanai). ¶ cond. past (Gr.Gr. 253) sg. 1 nimahö; 2 nihökh; 3 niyihē; pl. 1 nimahöv; 2 niyⁱhīv; 3 nihön. ¶ impve. pres. nyūhas, by them of him (H. viii, 9); pl. nīy (Gr.Gr. 211, 218; H. v, 9); nīm, by me (Gr.Gr. 218); nīth, by thee (Gr.Gr. 218; H. x, 1); nīn, by him (Gr.Gr. 218; H. v, 7; K. 196, 592); nīnas, by her from her (Śiv. 1312, K. 755); nīy, by us (Gr.Gr. 218); niy, by us (Rām. 531); nīwa, by you (Gr.Gr. 218); nīkh, by them (Gr.Gr. 218; K. 203, 557); nīhawa, you by them (K.Pr. 109, niyihawah); f. sg. and pl. niyĕ (Gr.Gr. 211, 218; H. ii, 1, 6; niyēyĕth, by thee; niyēyĕn, by him; niyēyĕ, by us; niyēyĕwa, by you; niyēyĕkh, by them. ¶ 3 p.p. m. sg. niyāv, the fem. sg. and pl. being as in 2 p.p. (Gr.Gr. 238); niyām, by me (Gr.Gr. 238); niyāth, by thee; niyān, by him; niyāv, by us; niyāwa, by you; niyākh, by them; pl. niyēyēy; niyēyēm, by me; niyēyēth, by thee; niyēyēn, by him; niyēyēy, by us; niyēyēwa, by you; niyēyēkh, by them. ¶ The passive of this verb is nina yunᵘ (Gr.Gr. 169, 170), and this may have a special meaning, for which see bel. (Gr.Gr. 169). The causal of this verb is nyāwun or niwanāwun, qq.v. (Gr.Gr. 172). The causal of the passive is nina anun, see bel.]. ¶ To carry away, take away (cf. athi nᵒ, p. 66a, l. 2; kaḍith nᵒ, p. 386a, l. 30) (L.V. 57; Śiv. 1385; Rām. 683, 819, 1622; H. x, 5; K. 69, 83; K.Pr. 109); to carry (from one place to another), convey (to), take (to) (Śiv. 1504, 1579; Rām. 255, 416, 602, 626, 661, 718, 721, 841, 927-8, etc.; H. viii, 11; K. 429, 894; YZ. 119); to take (out of a receptacle) (YZ. 114); to bring (news, etc.) (H. ii, 1, 6; x, 7, 8; xii, 23; YZ. 413); ¶ to take away, to make away with, to cause to be lost (cf. diwath niñᵘ̈, p. 264b, l. 47; hōsh nᵒ, p. 353a, l. 10) (Rām. 26, YZ. 418); to take away (dishonestly), steal (cf. lūṭa nᵒ, p. 538a, l. 30; muhith nᵒ, p. 555b, l. 5) (Rām. 1026; H. viii, 9; K. 751; K.Pr. 147); to take to oneself and depart, to appropriate to oneself, run away with, carry off (Śiv. 995, 1312-13; Rām. 323, 503, 1160, 1162-3, 1373; H. viii, 9; xii, 19; K. 205, 287, 673-4); to take, seize, capture (Gr.M.; Śiv. 677; Rām. 363, 374, 470, 1288; H. vi, 9; x, 5; xi, 18; K. 191, 335, 755, 1144, 1146; YZ. 129); ¶ to take, accept (cf. brȧmⁱ nᵒ, to take by delusion, to be swindled, p. 123a, l. 43; būzith nᵒ, p. 154a, l. 23; kȧnⁱ tȧlⁱ nᵒ, p. 448b, l. 34; mangith nᵒ, p. 579a, l. 48) (Śiv. 952; Rām. 82, 150, 613; H. v, 12; x, 1; xii, 25; K. 109, 204, 496); to take to (a course of conduct) (cf. dōr nᵒ, p. 237a, l. 9); ¶ to take (a person or animal), to conduct (cf. khyolᵘ nᵒ, p. 426a, l. 45) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 80, 227, 280, 631, 1004, 1380, 1555, 1560, 1630, etc.; Rām. 514, 1167, 1480, 1551; K. 389, 400, 557, 564; YZ. 162, 232); to lead away (Rām. 375; H. iii, 7; K. 196, 203, 283, 592; YZ. 95); ¶ to win, gain (Śiv. 826; K. 2, 938); to captivate (the heart, etc.) (Śiv. 1439; K. 802, 804). ¶ Often used in compound phrases, as in:-- bözⁱ niñᵘ̈, to win a game (K. 938); carkh niñᵘ̈, to take a circuit, to go round in a circle (Rām. 551); kaḍith nyunᵘ, to carry off, go off with (K. 254, K.Pr. 57); mangith niñᵘ̈, to take (a girl) in marriage (K.Pr. 83); nĕngalith nyunᵘ, to swallow down (K. 345); raṭith nᵒ, to arrest, capture (H. v, 7, 9; x, 5); tulith nᵒ, to raise up, lift up (Rām. 531; H. iii, 7; K. 73, 124, 838); ʦhāl niñᵘ̈, to take a leap, to jump (Rām. 548); warith niñᵘ̈, to take (a woman) in marriage (Śiv. 413, 635, 882); and so many others, which will be found under the other members of the respective compounds. ¶ nina āmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), carried off; distraught, at one's wits' ends. --onᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --üñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), driven to one's wits' ends, made distracted. --anun -- m.inf. (causal of nina yunᵘ, bel.), to make a person distraught, to drive him to his wits' ends, to distract a person. --bāgi -- adv. (giving, etc.) for conveyance elsewhere, (given) to be taken away somewhere. -hār n.ag. c.g. fit to be taken away somewhere. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a carrier, a conveyor (cf. khath nᵒ, p. 422a, l. 45); a carrier off (as in theft or the like), a thief. -wath f. (sg. dat. -wati), the road or way by which things are conveyed; a means or action which will induce a person to convey. -vizᵘ̈ f. the time (appointed) for conveying, the time at which conveying occurs, the time during which conveying takes place; the time of a theft. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. (forming passive) to be carried off; to be distraught, at one's wits' ends (Gr.Gr. 169); the causal form of this passive is nina anun, ab. ¶ ninas kyutᵘ adj. (f. --kiʦᵘ̈ --), (ready) to take away, (arranged as a means) for taking away; one who habitually takes (and never gives), a man of a grasping character. ¶ ninay neg. conj. part. not having brought or conveyed (Gr.Gr. 111). ¶ nyū-motᵘ perf. part. (f. nī-müʦᵘ̈), conveyed (from one place to another); taken with oneself (K. 772); seized, captured (Śiv. 677).

m. (sg. dat. nīris, abl. nēri, K.Pr. 5), a mountain meadow (at the foot of or amidst mountains) (cf. aṭa-nᵒ, p. 68a, l. 42; düdᵘ̈wanas nyūrᵘ yunᵘ, p. 191a, l. 17 (Gr.Gr. 19; L. núr; Śiv. 1011, 1222; K.Pr. 5)). --khasun -- m.inf. to ascend a mountain meadow, to stroll amidst mountain meadows to visit the hills (e.g. on a holiday) (K.Pr. 218). ¶ nēri drāv 1 (for 2, see nyūrᵘ 3) adj. c.g. issued from the mountain meadows; met. (like cattle which have returned after feeding on the mountain meadows) plump, prosperous, and in good fettle. --wothᵘ -- adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), descended from the hill meadows; met. (like cattle returned from feeding in the hills) plump, prosperous, and in good fettle.

m. N. of a certain cattle disease, affecting the mouth (cf. añĕma-nᵒ, a stye in the eye, p. 37b, l. 7; ös-nᵒ, p. 46b, l. 12, which L. 459, spelling the word asnur, describes as swelling of the mouth and feet, as if connecting the word with nyūrⁱ, q.v.). --yunᵘ 1 -- m.inf. this cattle disease to occur.

adj. (f. nīrᵘ̈ or nyūrᵘ̈) near (to), close (to), hard by, adjoining (all of place) (cf. nari-nērē, p. 649a, l. 39) (Gr.Gr. 19, K. 1126), near (of time). --pahān -- adj. (f. nīrᵘ̈ pahān), somewhat near (Gr.Gr. 94). --yunᵘ 2 -- m.inf. to come near, to approach. ¶ nēri āsun m.inf. to be near, close by; to be near (in time). --āsawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --āsavüñᵘ̈ --), that which is near, close by; that which is near (in point of time). --drāv 2 -- (for 1, see nyūrᵘ 1) adj. c.g. issued from near by, i.e. got without labour, found without any trouble. --neri -- adv. near and near, each near the other. -nyūrᵘ, adv. and postpos. governing dat. near, close (to) (K. 396, 1115). --pakun -- m.inf. to come or go from near, to come or go from the neighbourhood (of anything) (lit. or met.). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain near, to be in attendance on a person (= Urdu ḥāẓir rahnā). ¶ nēryukᵘ sg. gen. (f. nēricᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the vicinity.

or ñūrⁱ f. (sg. dat. nyōrĕ, Gr.Gr. 60), a cleft hoof (cf. kaṭa-ñᵒ, p. 487a, l. 8) (El., Gr.Gr. 60). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a certain disease of the hoofs to occur. ¶ ñōrĕ f.pl. the lower (cleft) part of a cleft hoof. ¶ nyōri-chŏkh m. (sg. dat. -chŏkas), a blow from a cow's (or similar animal's) hoof.
adj. (f. nīʦᵘ̈ 2; for 1, see nīth; for 3, see nyūʦᵘ), accepted, taken (e.g. a bribe, or a share of something due).

adj. (f. nīʦᵘ̈ 3; for 1, see nīth 2; for 2, see nyūtᵘ), low; low, vile, base, mean; petty, insignificant, inferior; miserly, stingy (Gr.M.); of low caste, of vile birth. ¶ nīʦa-bāv  m. a lowly state, a humble condition, poverty (K. 1103). -pān m. a lowly self, a humble personality (K. 1134). ¶ nīʦⁱ-bāpār m. the conduct of a person of low caste, vile by profession, or the like; conduct like that of a person of low caste, or otherwise despicable.

When wa follows a consonant it becomes ŏ, which is represented by in Nāgarī and by pēsh in Persian. Thus, دُد, dŏd, milk. This letter has the sound of o in 'hot'. Some pronounce this with a very faint w-sound preceding the ŏ; thus, dʷŏd. When followed by ᵃ or ⁱ the pronunciation of ŏ remains unaffected. When followed by ᵘ or ᵘ̈ it becomes modified to ọ̆ or ŏ̈ respectively. ¶ The letter ŏ is quite often interchanged with u, both in speaking and in writing. Most Kāshmīrīs seem to be unable to distinguish between the two sounds.

This is the modified form which ŏ takes when followed by ᵘ. It is pronounced nearly the same as o. Thus, گُن, gọ̆nᵘ, a stack, is pronounced gon. This word cannot be transliterated gonᵘ, as it is spelt with in the Nāgarī character.

This is the modified form which ŏ takes when followed by ᵘ̈. It is pronounced nearly the same as ü, but tending towards a short ö. Thus, چھھپ, ʦhŏ̈pᵘ̈, silent (fem.), has a sound which lies between ʦhüp and ʦhöp.

This is the sound which a takes when followed by ᵘ. It is nearly the same as that of the first o in 'promote'. It is represented in Nāgarī by and in the Persian character by pēsh. Thus, بُڈ, boḍᵘ, great. We sometimes meet this letter when a is followed by an ordinary u, as in ogunᵘ for agunᵘ (also used) fire. When, in the process of declension or conjugation or for any other reason, the ᵘ or u disappears, the raison d'être for the o disappears also, and it reverts to the original a, which is then, as before, subject to further changes. Thus, the dative singular of boḍᵘ is baḍis, the agent singular is bȧḍⁱ, and the direct feminine singular is büḍᵘ̈. Similarly, the dative singular of ogun is ạgᵃnas.

This letter bears the same relation to ā that o does to a. It is the form that ā takes when followed by ᵘ (or in some cases by u, see ā). It has the sound of a prolonged broad ō, nearly the equivalent to that of the o in 'glory'. Like ō it is represented in Nāgarī by, and in Persian by wāw. Thus, from the base māl- with ᵘ added, we have, مول, môlᵘ, a father.

This letter bears nearly the same relation to ā that ü does to a. It is the form that ā takes when followed by ⁱ or ᵘ̈. As explained under ā, it also often takes this form when followed by an ordinary i, or even when in a monosyllable and not followed by any mātrā-vowel. It is sounded something like a much prolonged German ö. It is represented in Nāgarī by and in the Persian character by آ. Thus, مآلِ, mölⁱ,fathers; آس, ös, face.

This is the long ō of Hindī, pronounced like the second o in 'promote'. It is represented in Nāgarī by and in the Persian character by wāw. Thus, پوش, pōsh, a flower. When ō is followed by any mātrā-vowel it becomes ū. Thus, from pōṭhun, to be fat, we have pūṭhᵃrāwun, to make fat; from the base bōl- we have būlⁱ, speech, but dat. sing. bōlĕ; from bōzun, to hear, we have the past participle būzᵘ (masc.) and būzᵘ̈ (fem.). ¶ Unlike u and ū, the letter ō can commence a word, e.g. ōra-kani, thence. ¶ The letter ō is quite often interchanged with ū, both in speaking and in writing. Most Kāshmīrīs seem to be unable to distinguish between the two sounds.
adv. yes. ō-tu, adv. yes but, yes with a reservation.
f. (cf. obulᵘ), a certain wild plant growing in dry ground in the beginning of spring, the leaves of which have a sour taste. Used as an astringent medicine (abuj, L. p. 75).
m. (cf. obujⁱ), a certain plant growing in damp soil, with a long-shaped leaf sour to the taste; Rumex acutus (El.). Cf. aibij.

m. mica, talc. ¶ obura-chhal f. a piece of mica. -dörᵘ̈ f. a side-door ornamented with mica, usually the door of a winter bathroom -han 1, hanā 1 f. a small piece of mica or a pinch of powdered mica. -kā̃gürᵘ̈ f. a portable brazier ('kāngrī') ornamented with mica. -mŏcĕr m. thinness like that of a leaf of mica. -mọ̆nḍᵘ 1 m. a thick lump of mica not easily split into leaves. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ - f. a thick slab of mica as it issues from the mine. -māyĕ m. a starch mixed with mica applied by washermen to clothes in order to give them a 'finish'. -mŏy 1, -mŏyā 1 f. a little mica. -tilim f. a small strip of mica. -warukh m. a leaf of mica. -watun m. a long strip of mica. -zôlᵘ m. a pattern formed in strips, or particles, of mica.

m. a cloud. ¶ obura-oburᵘ̈ f. clouds overcasting the sky. -gacĕr m. darkness caused by clouds. -gāsh m. illumination given by white clouds (e.g. a road lightened at night by them). -gaṭa f. darkness (at night) caused by clouds. -goṭᵘ m. darkness (in the daytime) caused by clouds. -han 2 or hanā 2 f. very thin or slight cloud. -lambukh m. a long, heavy, terrifying cloud. -māl f. clouds scattered in lines, like a garland. -mọ̆nḍᵘ 2, m. a large heavy rain-cloud. -mŏy 2 or -mŏyā 2 f. a slight cloud, a few clouds. -ring f. a very light or slight cloud. -ʦroṭᵘ, m. an isolated circular patch of thick cloud in a clear sky. -ʦhāy f. the shade cast by a cloud. -zāl m. a network of light clouds (prognosticating neither absence of heat nor of rain). ¶ ạbᵃras tal under a cloud (YZ. 165, 288).
f. watering of the mouth, flow of water in the mouth, salivation.
m. a kind of perforated frying-pan for parching singārā nuts. ¶ ȧchⁱ-gôrⁱ m. parched singārā nuts.
m. the string of the grass sandals commonly worn in Kashmir. āchi gaʦhun m.inf. to be reduced to poverty; āchi gômotᵘ perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), reduced to poverty.

adj. (m. sg. dat. adaris ag. ạdᵃ̇rᵃ̇, abl. abari, pl. nom. ạdᵃ̇rᵃ̇, dat. adarĕn; f. üdᵘ̈rᵘ̈, dat. ạdᵃrĕ, and so on), moist, wet, damp (either naturally or by the application of water). Cf. K.Pr. 18. -zĕn-hyuhᵘ adj. (f. üdᵘ̈rᵘ̈-zĕn-hishᵘ̈), very wet (of mud and the like). üdᵘ̈rᵘ̈-khal f. extreme insult, giving extreme dishonour, or (with reference to an inanimate object) consigning to destruction. üdᵘ̈rᵘ̈-züṭᵘ̈ f. a wet rag; an old rag used for wiping off sweat, for mopping up liquids, or the like. ạdᵃri-kani (sg. dat. of üdᵘ̈rᵘ̈), "for the moist articles," an expression used with reference to the price of sweetmeats sent by Kāshmīrī Brāhmaṇs as presents for their married daughters on various festivals.
f. the name of one of the lunar mansions or asterisms.

subst. m. and adj. (f. öḍicᵘ̈), subst. an agreement to maintain another's horse or cow for half the profits of its labour and for half its offspring; adj. of an animal so kept. öḍiki-dar m. one who gives a horse or cow on such terms to another for maintenance.
f. a mixing, mingling; a commencement (of a work or of making something).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. öḍᵃrôwᵃ), to mix (as flour with water); to set a person to work; to commence. öḍᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (ödᵃröwᵃ-müʦᵃ), mixed (of flour, etc., with liquids); set to work; commenced.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. öḍᵒrᵒ), to mix up together, to heap up; to commence, begin the making of anything. öḍᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. öḍᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), mixed, mingled; commenced.

adj. (sg. dat. aḍis; f. nom. üḍᵘ̈, sg. dat. ajĕ), half, halved; a part. oḍu-y, only half, hence incomplete, as in pūthⁱ chĕh üḍᵘ̈-y, the book is quite incomplete. aḍi-pöri adv. (u. w. a vb. signifying arrival, etc.), lit. at half a side or direction; hence, very near. üḍᵘ̈-hār f. half a cowry; a thing of the size or value of half a cowry. -müñᵘ̈ f. a certain measure of weight, half a müñᵘ̈; a thing weighing half a müñᵘ̈. A müñᵘ̈ of 30 pals is equivalent to a seer and a half. An üḍᵘ̈-müñᵘ̈ is therefore three-quarters of a seer or 15 pals, equivalent to 60 tōlās. It approximates 1 1/2 English pounds. ¶ ajĕ hāri-hondᵘ (gen. of üḍᵘ̈-hār, above), of half a cowry, worth only half a cowry, worth nothing, contemptible. --röʦᵘ̈ -- adv. (sg. dat. of üḍᵘ̈ rāth, cf. aḍ-rāth under aḍ), at midnight. --röʦᵘ̈-bögᵘ̈ --, or --röʦᵘ̈-bögin -- adv. at about midnight. --wati -- adv. (sg. dat. of üḍᵘ̈ wath, half a road), at half-way (to or from a place) (after a verb of resting, etc.). --wati-pĕṭh -- at half-way, having reached half-way (he did so and so), e.g. ajĕ wati-pĕṭh trôwun bôrᵘ, half-way (on the journey) he threw away his load. ajiy wati adv. (for ajĕ + y wati +), even at half-way, exactly half-way.
f. a wrong mixing, a wrong uniting.
f. quarrelling, including hitting each other and mutual abuse.

or ödidⁱ, ödith adv. to-day in past time, in the part of to-day that has already expired. -nan, -nas adv. the same as ödⁱ. -pĕṭha adv. (continued, etc.) from the expired part of to-day. -shutun adv. the same as ödⁱ-pĕṭha. ödi-y adv. in the part that has expired of this very day. ödyukᵘ adj. (f. ödicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the expired part of to-day.
f. a dust-storm; blindness caused by a dust-storm, darkness; the metaphorical blindness caused by terror, error, or the like.
m. defectiveness, absence of good qualities.

m. (sg. dat. ạgᵃnas or ạgnas (Śiv. 124), abl. ạgᵃna or ạgna, pl. nom. ạgᵃn, and so on), fire, generally applied to flaming fire (as e.g. in K.Pr. 40). ¶ agᵃna-kŏnḍ m. a hole or enclosed space for the consecrated fire at a sacrifice. -kuṭhᵘ m. the name of a particular muhūrta, or moment, fixed for sacrificial purposes. -mŏkh m. having Agni (the god of fire) in the mouth; a title of the god Śiva; voc. hē agᵃna-mŏkha, Śiv. 378. -manan f. a movable receptacle for consecrated fire, for use in a domestic fire-sacrifice. -pĕnḍav or -pë̆nḍᵘ̈ f. a sacrificial altar, or piece of ground used as such. -pröpyunᵘ m. the share of sacrificial food taken by the officiating priest. -ṭyokᵘ m. (sg. dat. -ṭĕkis), a mark made on the forehead with ashes of a fire-sacrifice. -wạtᵃr f. a general name for all the articles offered in oblation at a fire-sacrifice.
adj. (f. ügüñᵘ̈), onefold; composed of a single strand, not twisted with other strands (of a rope, string, etc.).
(f. ogurᵘ̈-thogurᵘ̈), having uneven members, ill-proportioned (of anything whether animate or inanimate).

in agi lagun m.inf. to go forward with the object of self-destruction to meet a calamity (as if walking into fire), such as an approaching enemy, or to deliberately expose oneself to infection in an epidemic.
in ogᵘ-dŏh m. the first day of a lunar fortnight.
m. the same as āg-bāg; see under āg above.
m. an interjection, or cry, of sorrow or pain.

f. a blessing.-pāṭh m. the recital of a blessing; an expression of politeness in greeting or leaving a friend (cf. K.Pr. 182). -wād, m. a blessing, with indef. suff. āh, öhī-wādāh (spelt āhīᵒ) (K.Pr. 15).

cf. wōnöjⁱ f.pl. the two pipes in the throat, the windpipe and the gullet, both of which are considered by uneducated natives as conveying food to the stomach, as well as for breathing. Cf. öhⁱ-rünḍⁱ. ōh-nöjᵘ̈n gaʦhun m. to go the wrong way (of food, when swallowing).
m. an appointment, post, office, rank (in the army), and so forth (Gr.M.).
yohuryundᵘ, q.v. adv. a short way off (u.w. vbs. of putting and the like). -pahān adv. id.
f. the clavicle or collar-bone. Cf. ōh-nöjᵘ̈.
m.pl. the lower orders, common people. -mö̃jörⁱ m.pl. the lower orders, common people; poor people; people of lower caste.
m. a kind of heron peculiar to Kashmīr (El.).
adj. c.g. of universally accepted purity (of a current coin or the like).
f. an estimate, appraisement, valuation; an inference as to results.
m. (sg. dat. ö̃kas and so on), a numeral mark, 1, 2, 3, etc., especially made for purposes of identification.

or sukh m. (sg. dat. sŏkhas), happiness, welfare, well-being, comfort, ease (Gr.M.; Śiv. 41, 281, 444, 482, 752-3, 922, 1459, 1635, 1819, 1835; Rām. 175, 662; K. 6, 32, 632, 808, 1099, 1100, 1168; K.Pr. 62, 164, 201, 206, 253); rest, leisure, peace (El. sŏk, sŏkh). --barun -- m.inf. to enjoy or experience happiness (Śiv. 1113; K. 958, 1078, 1093); to prosper (K. 318, 473). -dās f. N. of a kind of rice-plant, with a soft white grain (El.); the grain of this rice. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give happiness, make happy (Śiv. 946, 1438, 1639; Rām. 880). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. happiness to happen, to find happiness, to become happy, secure, or the like (esp. when unexpected). -rāth f. (sg. dat. -röʦᵘ̈), a night of happiness, a pleasant night (e.g. occupied with good or pleasant company, or a night of some great festival). -sar m. N. of a beautiful bird frequenting Kashmīr (El.). -sᵃʦan f. (sg. dat. -sᵃʦüñᵃ), a festival in honour of some happy event (e.g. on the birth of a son); cf. sᵃʦan 1, which is m. -sāway m. abundance of happiness. ¶ sŏkha-bolᵘ adj. lukewarm (El. sŏkabul, sŏkhabŏl, sokhabaul); cf. sŏkha-wushonᵘ, bel. -hã̄ḍ f. labour, exertion, expenditure (of money or of thought), in order to attain happiness. -kār m. a festival of (or on account of) happiness. -küṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kacĕ), 'a daughter of happiness', a daughter born in happy circumstances and brought up happily. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a son born in happy circumstances and brought up happily; a son of happiness, i.e. a good son who gives happiness to his parents (Gr.Gr. 132). --mŏkha -- adv. suddenly, unawares, unexpectedly by chance (Śiv. 238, 978, 1679, 1892). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain, or live, happily or in comfort (K. 363, 376). -sān  adv. with happiness, happily, comfortably (Gr.M.; Śiv. 85, 342, 393, 482, 630; Rām. 55); quietly (El.); (as adj.) pleased, happy, delighted. --thawun -- m.inf. to put in an entirely happy or comfortable condition (even in case of opposition). --wushonᵘ -- adj. (f. --wushiñᵘ̈ --), pleasantly hot, slightly warm, lukewarm; cf. sŏkha-bolᵘ, ab. -wushⁱnēr m. lukewarmness. -wushötⁱ adj. c.g. causing happiness, giving happiness. ¶ sŏkhas, sg. dat., as adv. in happiness, happily, in comfort (Rām. 484, 542). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go to happiness, to become happy (Rām. 1152). -pĕṭh adv., i.q. sŏkhas, ab. (Rām. 754, 825). -tal adv., id. (Rām. 1088). --wātun -- m.inf. to reach happiness, to become happy (Rām. 1666, 1750).
f. the office or occupation of a teacher, see ôkhun.

m. (with reference to giving an account of any circumstance), the opposite state of the case, giving an untrue account, untruth; generally used as an adverb. -mökhith adv. untruly, not exactly truthfully (with verbs of narration, etc.).
m. (sg. dat. ākhunas, pl. dat. ākhunan, YZ. 387), an ākhūn, or Persian teacher; a teacher of Persian, a Mussulman religious teacher. -bāy f. the wife of such a teacher.
conj. 1 to make a mark; to impress a mark upon anything, to brand (L.V. 76).
m. a disease (? an ache) affecting half of the head; described as not occurring on either side of the head.
m. the name of two villages, one in the Anatnāg (Anantanāga) and the other in the Lār (Lahara) Pargana of the Valley of Kashmīr.
m. only one (used in the sense of 'there is only one', 'only one can do it', and so on).

m. card. (dat. akis; gen. ȧkⁱ-sondⁱ or akyukᵘ; ag. ȧkⁱ; abl. aki; but these forms are usually referred, not to okᵘ but to akh, q.v.), one, one only, a single one. This word appears mostly in compounds. The usual word for 'one' is akh, which has borrowed all its cases except the nominative. Hence, for compounds beginning with ȧkⁱ or aki see under akh. The present article deals only with those compounds which commence with okᵘ. -okᵘ-wāri adv. singly, one by one. -borᵘ 1 adj. (f. -bürᵘ̈), where there is room for only one foot (of a road or the like). -borᵘ 2 (f. -bürᵘ̈), possessing only one door (of a house, etc.). -dolᵘ m. grain or the like which has been pounded only once in a husking mortar, or which is imperfectly husked. -dandorᵘ adj. (f. -dandürᵘ̈), having only one edge, as a cooking-pot, or a sword. -dandȧrĕl c.g. a thing, like a cooking-pot, or a sword, which has only one edge. -dôrᵘ adj. (f. -dörᵘ̈), possessing only one side- or back-door (of houses, etc.). The feminine is diminutive (of huts, etc.). -kôlᵘ m. one who eats food only once a day, whether on certain holy days, or on account of a vow, or on account of sickness. -kāñĕl adj. c.g. very weak, having no strength, as possessing only one rib. -köshⁱlad adj. c.g. one who would suffer from one day's fasting, either owing to want of food, or on account of sickness. -lobᵘ adj. (f. -lübᵘ̈), having only one side or edge (not applied to living creatures). -labal c.g. a thing which has only one side or edge (not applied to living creatures). -lorᵘ adj. (f. -lürᵘ̈), a rope or string of one strand. -norᵘ (f. -nürᵘ̈) or -narĕl c.g. having only one arm. -pôrᵘ adj. (f. -pörᵘ̈), on one side, one-sided (e.g. of a person suffering from hemiplegia, of sitting on one side of a seat, of the motion of a carriage, or of a house supported on one side). -pūrᵘ adj. (f. -pūrᵘ̈), where there is room for only one foot (of a road, path, or bridge). -poshᵘ adj. (f. -püshᵘ̈), having only one roof, pent-roofed (of a house). The fem. is diminutive (of a hut). -rosᵘ m. anything one-flavoured, as for instance food merely soaked for boiling, or fruits or medicinal herbs from which only one flavour can be extracted. -tôhᵘ (f. -töshᵘ̈), single-fold, not of double thickness (of a bed-covering, wrapper, etc.), i.q. okᵘ-tôshᵘ below. -tôpᵘ adj. (f. -töpᵘ̈), placed once in the sun or before a fire to dry. -tôshᵘ adj. (f. -töshᵘ̈), single, not folded, of a cloth, etc. Cf. okᵘ-tôhᵘ above. -ṭāsal adj. c.g. making the sound 'ṭās' only once, i.e. going off with a bang, like a gun, etc. -tôwᵘ adj. (f. -tövᵘ̈), heated once in a fire. -ʦôrᵘ m. a small fixed or movable fire-place, large enough for one cooking vessel at a time (El. auktsór, uktsŏr. -wôrᵘ adj. (f. -wörᵘ̈), having a single twist (of a rope or string). -wāri okᵘ-wāri adv. one by one. -warishᵘ̈ f. a female child or animal one year old. -wörshiñ f. a female or a crop, born or produced in the same year with something else referred to by the speaker; of the same year. -zongᵘ (f. -zünjᵘ̈) or -zangal, c.g., possessing only one leg, of a living being, or of a thing (bed, stool, etc.). ¶ okuy, ükᵘ̈y, see under akh.

in the following: -shūrⁱ f., or -shūrᵘ m. the name of the sign employed in the Śāradā character for non-initial ō. -shĕwahay f. the name of the sign employed in the Śāradā character for non-initial au. -sangōr m. the name of the sign, put, in schools, at the commencement of the alphabet after the Sanskrit words ōṁ svasti, and before the syllables. It itself is read as ekaṁ, and the whole auspicious formula is therefore ōṁ svasti ēkaṁ siddhaṁ.
f. collapse owing to the fall or withdrawal of a support, as in the case of the sudden withdrawal of an old man's stick, or the support on which a porter wearied of his burden is leaning.
m. an insecurely fastened burden, a load slipping off the shoulder.

f. a certain fruit, a small sour plum, Prunus domestica (El.). This may be the same as the aluchá (آلوچہ) of L. 73, 348, which he translates by "bitter cherry, Prunus cerasus, var. b". ¶ ölici-kujⁱ (or -kujᵘ̈) (or) f. the bush on which it grows. -rang m. the colour of a plum, plum-colour, purple-red.
m. a potato, Solanum tuberosum; cf. L. 346, where it is spelt ālū.

m. a nest (cf. K.Pr. 65, 100, 144, where the word is spelt aul); a recess in the wall used as a shelf. -yērun m.inf. to put together or build a nest; hence, to make anything or do anything gradually, bit by bit, and secretly. ¶ āli drāv m. just issued from the nest; hence, a young person when he has first left house and home and set up for himself, an inexperienced person; just born (see below). --nērun -- m.inf. to issue from the nest; to set out from home to make one's way in the world; to be born (the womb being compared to a nest), 1 past m. sg. 1, āli drās (K.Pr. 10). ¶ ölⁱ-nāsh m. destruction of a nest; hence, the sudden destruction of a human house and home.
m. delay in answering or refusal to answer, usually employed when the refusal is deliberate, owing to unwillingness or intent to deceive, and not to ignorance.
m. humbugging, cheating, a term used in children's games; cf. byucᵘ.

m. the name of the fifth of the seven bridges which cross the Vĕth (Jehlam) in Śrīnagar.
f. the name of the chief mosque in Śrīnagar.
m. (sg. dat. -wākas and so on), a polite greeting, a "how do you do?" Cf. āla-guʦar.
m. disrespect, contempt shown by one to another.
m. a vice or forceps used by carpenters or blacksmiths for extracting nails, etc.
m. (sg. dat. -būtas and so on), i.q. amar-būth, q.v.
m. the name of a village about 4 miles north of Śrīnagar on the road towards the Sind Valley. The ancient Amarēśvara. Cf. RT.Tr. vii, 183 n.
m. the mystic syllable ōṁ, used at the beginning and end of a reading of the Vēdas, previously to any prayer, and also as an auspicious salutation.
m. the plant Emblica myrobalan, Emblica officinalis, Gærtn.

adj. (m. sg. dat. ömis, abl. āmi; f. sg. nom. ömᵘ̈, pl. nom. āmĕ), raw, uncooked (Śiv. 1216); half-cooked; unripe. --dŏd -- m. unboiled milk; fresh milk, sweet milk. --pan -- m. loose-spun thread. --ṭôkᵘ -- m. a platter or similar earthen vessel of unbaked clay. --zômᵘ -- adj. (f. ömᵘ̈-zömᵘ̈), mixed up, confused, not clear, of a command or prohibition. --zāmotᵘ dŏd -- m. a mixture of sweet and curdled milk.
f. the feeling of disgust, accompanied by vomiting and diarrhœa, experienced by a woman in the earlier months of her pregnancy.

m., i.q. ongᵘjᵘ, q.v. -˚ (added to any word expressing a thing capable of measurement in length), a finger's breadth, a measure of length equal to about eight barleycorns (cf. K.Pr. 226). --dyunᵘ -- m. to tickle the throat with the fingers in order to induce vomiting. ¶ ongula m. -˚ measuring one finger-breadth (see above).
m. the small cutters used by a jeweller or goldsmith.

often written ongᵘjᵘ f. a finger (cf. K.Pr. 59, 157, 191, 218); a toe. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be cheated, to be swindled out of anything. ¶ ongᵘji-ganḍ m. a finger-joint, a toe-joint. -nam m. a finger-nail, a toe-nail. -pö̃ʦam f. a method of swindling, as when a thief who is caught stealing conceals somewhere the stolen property and displays his five fingers, i.e. his open hand, to show that there is nothing in them. -ṭyonḍᵘ m. (sg. dat. -ṭĕnḍis), the top joint of a finger or toe, a finger-tip, a toe-tip.
see ö̃ta under ỗtᵘ and önth.

m. (sg. dat. öntas, and so on), the end of anything, cf. and and anth. ¶ önta-gômotᵘ adj. (f. -gömüʦᵘ̈), gone beyond the end, being at the last extremity, absolutely poverty-stricken. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go (beyond) the end, to be at the last extremity, to be absolutely destitute; to become subject to another, dependent, submissive, humble. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), endless, limitless; very long, of which the end is not apparent, tedious (e.g. of a road, or a story); cf. anta-rostᵘ, under anth. -raʦhar m. endlessness, limitlessness; tediousness. ¶ öntha-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), i.q. önta-rostᵘ ab. -raʦhar m., i.q. önta-raʦhar ab.
they brought (with masc. sing. obj.), see anun.

adj. (m. sg. dat. anis, Śiv. 746; f. üñᵘ̈ sg. ag. añi, K.Pr. 66), blind (Śiv. 16). --sapanun --, to become blind. ¶ ȧnⁱ-arāth m. (sg. dat. -arātas), evening, twilight; cf. arāth. -bishta m. one who acts like a blind man, one who acts without foresight. -gāsh m. all the light that is visible by a blind man; hence, met., dimness, very little light. -lūṭh m. looting by a blind man, circumstances under which even a blind man can plunder; hence, met., misgovernment, tyranny. -mushta f.pl. hitting by a blind man; hence, met., ill-treating without excuse, ill-treating or striking the wrong person. -raz f. a string of blind men. A number of blind men form a line and go along the pilgrim-roads begging.
