The front man sings a song, to which the others reply in chorus. -sörᵘ̈ f. search by a blind man; hence, met., searching for anything in the dark; or searching futilely and without system for anything lost or destroyed. -thapa f.pl. grasping by a blind man; hence, met., when the proper resource is wanting, using the first thing that comes to hand as a substitute, or taking hold of anything without first seeing what it is. ¶ anis mushᵃth hāwüñᵘ̈ na sawāb na gŏnāh to shake one's fist at a blind man is neither a good action nor a sin (he does not see it, and it neither pleases him nor angers him); used of making an exertion the result of which is absolutely indifferent. ¶ añĕ-ȧchⁱ-gāsh m. the light of a blind eye; the little, but much treasured, light of a blind eye; hence, met., an only son, a darling son, a favourite son. -chapürᵘ̈ f. a children's game. One boy is blindfold and another boy hides, the former, after being unblindfolded, having to find out where the latter is. -gāth m. (sg. dat. -gātas and so on), a disgrace, a mark of shame or dishonour brought on as the result of some sinful act, or (in the case of a family) by sinful practices. -khörötⁱ adj. c.g. extremely unpleasant, deserving to be hidden away. ¶ añi-gaṭa f. or -goṭᵘ m. darkness, whether by day or by night (Śiv. 157); met., the sensation of darkness caused by fainting or the like; f.abl. añigaṭi, in the dark (K.Pr. 13, 82, cf. 226). -gaṭilad adj. c.g. dark (of a night, or the like) (Gr.M.).

un 1, unᵘ 1, a m. prim. suff. forming (1) the verbal noun or infinitive, and (2) the future passive participle, as in karonᵘ, karun, or karunᵘ, the act of doing, to do, or about to be done, necessary to be done. See Gr.Gr. 112 ff.
he was brought by them, see anun (cf. YZ. 129).
he was brought by him for me (YZ. 350), see anun 2.
a prim. suff. forming a kind of adverbial pres. part. Thus, kar-önⁱ, while doing. It is only used by rustics (Gr.Gr. 196).
f. hope (rare). --thawüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to hope (for); as in öph thüwᵘ̈nas he hoped for it.
adj. (m. sg. dat. oprubŏdis; f. sg. nom. oprubö̆zᵘ̈, dat. oprubŏzĕ), unenlightened, uneducated, without understanding.
adj. (m. sg. dat. apis; f. nom. üpᵘ̈, dat. apĕ), ignoble, mean, of low degree, of small consideration (K.Pr. 33); ignorantly satisfied with a small return for one's labour.

m. (sg. dat. öpis-ʦöpis, abl. āpi-ʦāpi), putting rice-milk for the first time into a child's mouth, the annaprāśana ceremony, performed six months after birth in the case of a boy and seven months after birth in the case of a girl.

adv. on the far side of anything, over there, beyond. Cf. āra-pôrᵘ, öryumᵘ-pöryumᵘ, örⁱkaṭin-törⁱkȧṭⁱ, ar-war, ara-war, and wūry. -kun adv. on the far side, opposite, in that (opp. to this) direction (Gr.Gr. 160). --na yōr -- adv. neither there nor here, undecidedly, hesitatingly. -yōr adv. there and here, inconsistently, (of a place) uncertainly, indefinitely; in any direction, i.e. on all sides (K. 656). -yōr pakun m.inf. to wander (El.). ¶ ōra adv. from the far side, from over there cf. wōḍa. -kani adv., (with vbs. of placing) on the far side, (with vbs. of coming) from the far side, thence (Gr.Gr. 159, Śiv. 1674). -kanĕn adv. id. -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or produced in the far side, or in some place other than here. -yōra adv. from that side and this, thoroughly; (knowing) from both sides, or the whole, of a subject; mutually. ¶ ōrukᵘ adj. (f. ōrücᵘ̈), of or produced on the far side, hence foreign, not belonging to this country. -yōr adv. of there, here; in reversed order, the preceding being put after the succeeding. -yōrukᵘ adj. (f. ōrücᵘ̈-yōrücᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or produced in, there and here, of uncertain origin.

(cf. wōra) in ōra-bĕñĕ f. the daughter of one's stepmother, a stepsister. -bāpār m. the conduct of a stepmother to her stepchildren. -bôyᵘ m. a stepbrother, by the same father but a different mother. -dryuyᵘ m. a husband's younger brother by a different mother, a stepbrother-in-law. -hash f. a stepmother-in-law, the stepmother of a wife's husband or of a husband's wife. -möjᵘ̈ f. a stepmother, the co-wife of one's own mother. -môlᵘ m. a stepfather, the second husband of one's mother, one's own father being dead. This can, of course, only occur amongst Musalmāns, not amongst Kāshmīrī Hindūs. -nöñᵘ̈ f. a stepgrandmother, the stepmother of one's father or of one's mother. -pokhᵘ, -paksh m. step-relatives, a general term for the near relations of one's stepmother. -rᵃsh f. the mutual jealousy between co-wives and between their respective children. -zām f. (sg. dat. ag. and abl., and pl. nom. -zōm, pl. dat. -zōmᵃn, ag. and abl. -zōmᵃw), a husband's stepsister, a stepsister-in-law.

a secondary suffix forming adverbs of place, as in tōr, there. Its abl., ōra, forms adverbs of motion from, as tōra, from there. With emphatic y, ōr becomes ūry, as in tūry, even there (Gr.Gr. 155, 156).

f. (sg. dat. öriʦi, and so on), the daily or continual arcā, or worship and feeding a brāhmaṇ which goes on for a year after a death in a family. öriʦi-brôhmun m. the brāhmaṇ who receives the offerings of food on these occasions. öriʦi-ṭūrᵘ̈ f. a copper vessel, in which the food offered on these occasions is cooked.

adv. scattered here and there in a group without order; esp. (in a children's game) of a handful of cowries scattered on the ground, and hence, generally, of any number of things accidentally fallen on the ground.
m. the space between the top of a wall and the roof, used as a kind of shelf.
m. longing, craving; persistent begging, importunate supplication.
adj. (f. örᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), afflicted, distressed, whether by sickness or by cruelty.

adj. (m. sg. dat. aris, K.Pr. 15; f. sg. nom. ürᵘ̈), (of an an. obj.) sound, well, healthy; (of an inan. obj.) firm, hard, not easily broken (El. ur, and so K.Pr. 263; cf. K.Pr. 15, where ȧrⁱ, the m. pl. nom., is written ari). -wurᵘ adj. (f. ürᵘ̈-wurᵘ̈), extremely or entirely sound, etc.; extremely or entirely firm, etc. -zuv m. good health, freedom from sickness. -zuv ta dorᵘ-kọ̆ṭhᵘ adv. (used in blessings or good wishes), with healthy body and firm knees (for walking). ¶ ari-wuri adv. (u.w.vbs. of giving, etc.), completely, entirely, in perfect condition (of the gift), or cheerfully, whole-heartedly (of the giver).

m. a kind of plum, ālū-ĕ-Bukhāra (Prunus domestica) (El. er), = K.Pr. 137, ár, and L. 73, 348, Prunus communis. -kujⁱ f. a plum-vine, a creeping tree on which a species of plum grows. -kulᵘ m. a plum-tree.

f. encircling; a circle, band, fillet; a ring (as of rope, or as formed by a snake lying curled up); a wisp of straw or grass, bound in a ring, for supporting round-bottomed vessels so as to prevent their overturning. Cf. āra 1 and āru. -pörᵘ̈ f. surrounding a person to prevent his departure, forming a circle of people round him, crowding round a person.
adv. talking hither and thither, speaking in such a way as to confuse a person, with the object of deceiving or swindling him. Cf. ōr 1.

(for 1 see āsun) m. (sg. dat. ösas (K.Pr. 15, 90, 157), abl. ösa 1, and so on), the mouth, the face (Śiv. 199, 1795); cf. ās 1. -bab f. (putting) the nipple into the mouth to quiet a suckling babe (to put, thawüñᵘ̈); hence, met. giving great pleasure to a person, giving him something that he longs for. -bĕha m. temporary silence, as in the phrase ös-bĕha chuy nā? can't you hold your tongue for a little? -nicĕr m. the condition of having a small mouth; a reticent habit, taciturnity, a habit of speaking little. -nyukᵘ adj. (f. -nicᵘ̈), having a small mouth, small-mouthed; one who speaks little, taciturn, not loquacious, reserved, reticent by nature. -nyūrᵘ m. a certain cattle disease, swelling of the mouth and feet (cf. L. 459, asnur). -phakh m. (sg. dat. -phakas), the stink of an evil-smelling mouth, foul breath. -pav m. greediness, gluttony, edacity. --surawun -- m.inf. to clean the mouth; hence, to mind one's words, speak carefully or respectfully, to use proper language, not to use foul talk, e.g. ös suraw, 'clean your mouth,' said to some one who is using indecent abuse. -thopᵘ m. restraint of the mouth; esp. shutting by one woman the mouth of another who is lamenting, thus inducing her to restrain her voice; met. a gift or other inducement given to a gabbler or censorious person to make him hold his tongue. --ʦhẹ̆ṭᵃrun -- m.inf. to render the mouth impure; hence, putting food into one's mouth, eating; esp. taking food twice daily after the conclusion of the funeral fast held by a brotherhood after the death of one of its members. -ʦhyonᵘ adj. (f. -ʦhë˘ñᵘ̈), having the mouth split or cleft, either from birth, from disease, or injury. --ʦaṭun -- m.inf. to cut the mouth; hence, to stop a person speaking as soon as he commences; to stop a person eating something he has just put into his mouth. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to make a face indicating disgust at nasty food or at having the same food over and over again. ¶ ösa bab nērüñᵘ̈ f.inf. the nipple to slip from the mouth (of a suckling child); met. a slip to occur betwixt cup and lip, a sudden disappointment to happen on the brink of success. -boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), big-mouthed; hence, loud-voiced; hectoring, laying down the law; impudent; loquacious, given to much talking. -hath m. a hundred mouths (K.Pr. 25). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to drag out from the mouth; hence, to utter forcibly, esp. a command or abuse. -kath f. (sg. dat. -kathi), a word in the mouth; hence, any word or statement which is remembered and held ready for utterance on the tongue, even though previously heard only once; gossip, hearsay. -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), having the lips, the tongue, or other parts of the mouth cut off; met. ugly-mouthed, having an ugly mouth; or, speaking badly or indistinctly. -zĕv f. a tongue in the mouth, i.e. which fills the mouth and leaves room for nothing else, the tongue of a babbling, loquacious person.
m. pleasure, luxury, enjoyment of wealth, etc., spelt ash in K.Pr. 2 and aish in K.Pr. 173. öshĕ-motᵘ adj. (f. -müʦᵘ̈), luxury-mad, addicted to luxury or enjoyment.
m. a herb, esp. one used for medicine, a simple, medicine (Śiv. 49, 517, 632, 1838). Cf. ashud.
m. the name of a month, equivalent to September-October. Cf. K.Pr. 128, where it is spelt āshid.
adj. (f. öshë˘rᵘ̈-pitarĕñ), one who, like a near relation who is not bound by the ordinary rules of ceremonial politeness, finds fault with or impedes another, an interfering busybody.
f. (sg. dat. öshᵉ̆rüñᵉ̆), dependence on a person for livelihood, taking refuge with a person.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. öshᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), i.q. öshᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. öshᵉ̆röwᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), i.q. öshirᵘ-motᵘ, q.v.

conj. 1 (poet. pres. part. öshᵉ̆ran (Śiv. 1050); 1 p.p. öshᵒrᵒ or öshirᵘ), to go to for refuge or protection, to take refuge in (a place) or with (a person) (Śiv. 1050, 1867); to settle in (a country) for one's livelihood; to live under (a person's) patronage. ¶ öshirᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. öshirü-müʦᵘ̈), one with whom refuge is taken; a country in which one settles; a patron.

m. a tear (weeping) (Śiv. 1588, 1619, 1892). --sĕṭhāh pakān -- many tears flow (El.; cf. YZ. 132, pl.; 417, sg.). ȧshⁱpĕy, tears fell (YZ. 262). --trāwun -- m.inf. to weep (Śiv. 1250, 1741, 1910). --yunᵘ -- tears to come, to weep; hence, to weep tears of envy, to be envious or jealous. kawa yiyĕm oshu-y? why should a tear come to me? why should I cry? (K.Pr. 58, where the word is spelt ushye, and 76, where it is aushye). ¶ ȧshⁱ or ashi. All the following compounds here commencing with ȧshⁱ may optionally commence with ashi. ȧshⁱ-buka m.pl. the welling-up of tears in the eyes; tears filling the eyes but not streaming forth. -dag f. the pain in the eyes caused by tears, tear-swollen eyes. -digiñ f. a sudden and copious torrent of tears, as it were a flow of water from a broken jar. -dāra f. a stream of tears. So ashicᵘ̈ dār (Śiv. 1366). -ganḍ m.pl. a knot of tears; an accumulation of tears in the eyes, not flowing forth, but forming 'knots' or 'beads' in the eyelashes. -gaṭa f. the flow of tears produced by smoke, etc; the temporary darkness or blindness caused by such. -gaṭakār running or watering of the eyes, from disease, from smoke, or from the application of drugs. -phyorᵘ m. (sg. dat. -phĕris), a tear-drop (Śiv. 1210). -phyūrᵘ m. (sg. dat. -phīris), a tear-drop, usually applied to a very small or minute drop. -ṭörⁱ m.pl. eyelids filled with tears. -ʦāla f.pl. a handful of tears, tears sufficient to fill the hollow of the hand, a great flood of tears. -ʦörⁱ m.pl. (of the eyes), fullness with tears, tearfulness. ¶ ashi-phĕrⁱ m.pl. the name of a sacred place (tīrtha) in Kashmīr, where there are two springs, one hot and the other cold, which are said to be the goddess Pārvatī's tears of sorrow and joy respectively. It is situated in the hill-country of Lahara (Lār) Pargana, beyond the Hamsadvāra Mountain, about half-way along the Haramukuṭagaṅgā pilgrim route. ¶ ashicĕ-dāra f.pl. streams of tears (poet.). Cf. ȧshⁱ-dāra ab. ¶ ashiñĕ-dāra f.pl., id. (poet.). So -ʦāla f.pl.,id. (poet.) (Śiv. 1255, 1688).

m. (sg. dat.öshis, abl. āshi), a woman's husband (used by the wife), only used in old language and poetry. The fem. is āshëñ, a wife, which is still in use. ¶ öshⁱ-nāv m. a relation by marriage, a connexion. -nāv-bāy f. the wife of a relation by marriage. -növī f. relationship by marriage.
or m. the name of a part of the northern quarter of the city of Śrīnagar, the ancient Avantibhavana.
f. name of a place on the eastern side of Śrīnagar and to the south of the temple of Gōpāditya. It is sacred to the sun, its ancient name being āditya-guhā. Cf. RT.Tr. II, 453 ff.
f. a pestle for husking rice.
f. paste, made of flour, used for joining paper, book-binding, etc.; leaven (El.).

adv. the day before yesterday, used principally in villages and by old-fashioned Musalmans. W. 95 spells the word otar or utar. ōtrukᵘ adj. (f. ōtrücᵘ̈), produced on, of, or belonging to, the day before yesterday. -kani or ṻtra-kani adv. about, probably, the day before yesterday (Gr.Gr. 159). -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of or belonging to about the day before yesterday.
adj. (f. ỗṭᵘrᵘ-khỗṭᵘrᵘ), not joined together, not pieced together; imperfectly formed, incomplete in shape.
f. meditating in wrath against a person, regarding him wrathfully; maliciously searching out a person's weak points.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ö̃ṭᵒrᵒ; 2 p.p. ö̃ṭᵃryōv), to meditate in wrath against a person, to regard him wrathfully; maliciously to look out for a person's weak points.

adv. thither, to that place (within sight or pointed to). Cf. Gr.Gr. 156. -kun adv. towards that direction (within sight or pointed out). Cf. Gr.Gr. 160. -kunᵘ̈y adv. towards that very direction (within sight or pointed out). ¶ otuth adv., i.q. otᵘ. Cf. Gr.Gr. 156. otᵘthᵘy adv. to that very place (Gr.Gr. 156). otuy adv. id. Cf. id.
adj. (f. öʦᵘ̈), alone, only (Śiv. 1658), often used adverbially at end of a compound to signify merely so and so; tall, prominent in shape. Cf. El. ot, only, and yôtᵘ.

m. (sg.dat. ötis, abl. āṭi), flour, of wheat or other grain (Śiv. 1828, cf. K.Pr. 77, 85, where it is spelt auṭ cf. āṭhih in K.Pr. 158, which is a misprint for āṭih, i.e. āṭi, voc. sg.). ¶ öṭⁱ-basta f. a leather bag for holding flour. -mŏṭh f. (sg. dat. -mŏṭhi), as much flour as can be grasped in the hand, a fistful of flour; hence any small quantity of flour. -pholᵘ m. a small quantity of flour, a little flour. -raz f. flour worked up with butter, etc., into a rope-like form for making into cakes. -thaph m. (sg. dat. -thapi), lit. a handful of flour; hence, a lump of dought.

f. (sg. dat. ācĕ), the stone of a fruit. --kumalüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to become soft-stoned; met. of a limb, to become pliant or supple by practice, used in reproaches or abuse, or in ö̃ṭᵘ kumalyēyĕs nā? hasn't his kernel softened yet? --marüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. 'to be dead-stoned', to be thoroughly satisfied, with no possibility of the desire being felt again. ¶ ã̄cĕ f.pl. fruit-stones, a group of stones inside a fruit. -mār m. killing fruit-stones; met. killing something so insignificant as not to be worth killing, even though it deserves it=using a steam-roller to crack a nut, wasting powder and shot, or breaking a butterfly on the wheel. -tīl m. oil expressed from fruit-stones.
. An additional meaning is the 'Adam's apple' in the throat, and hence, genl., the throat, throttle (K. 449).

m. nectar; met. anything liquid delicious like nectar, a pleasant drink. ¶ ö̃ta-dāra f. a stream of nectar, a flow of pleasant drink. -lawa f. a few drops of nectar, etc.; a sprinkling with drops of nectar, etc.
m. the limit of bottomlessness, the depth or deepness of anything; the shallowness of anything. -wỗtᵘ m. the depth or shallowness of anything (water, etc.), more indefinite than ỗtᵘ. Cf. Gr.Gr. 95.

m. (a corruption of the Sanskrit meaning, confounded by folk-etymology with ôṭᵘ), a ceremony in which a person for whose benefit a sacrifice is being performed, and the members of his family, inspect the reflections of their faces in the clarified butter before it is offered as an oblation.
m. the waist-string worn by brāhmaṇs to support the cloth worn over the privities. Cf. aṭh 2 and üṭᵘ̈.
m. the name given to the cooked water chestnut by the people living on the shores of the Wulur Lake (El.). See also ôṭᵘ.

or auv (m.pl. ēy; f.sg. and pl. ēyĕ), the suffix of the 2 p.p. of all verbs, see Gr.Gr. 108 and 223 ff. The final v is dropped before personal terminations, and, in forming the perf. part., before -motᵘ.
m. extreme softness (of things). Cf. öyⁱjyār.
f. entrance (of a supernatural being into the body), possession, demoniacal possession, inspiration (Śiv. 1649); i.q. āwaṭh.
adj. c.g. possessed by a supernatural being or demon, inspired.
adj. (f. övijᵘ̈), very soft (of things), delicate, thin. pōshi khŏta övyulᵘ, more delicate than a flower (K.Pr. 88, where the word is spelt áwel). Cf. öyⁱlⁱ.
he came for thee (āv + ay), see yunᵘ (Gr.Gr. 241).
they came for thee (āy + ay), see yunᵘ (Gr.Gr. 241).
m. a law, statute, edict, decree. öyīn ba öyīn adv. decree by decree, (of a series of events) each in its destined, or due, order (Rām. 24).
m. (Śiv. 500), i.q. aina with suff. āh of indef. art.
m. (sg. dat. öyitas), the sun (esp. in old language), used nowadays as a proper N. (El. āyūt).
m. softness, delicacy (of anything animate or inanimate); cf. övijyār.
adj. (f. öyⁱjⁱ), very soft, very delicate, easily broken, slender, very weak (of persons or things); cf. övyulᵘ.
f. a sec. suff. used to form abstract nouns from substantives; e.g. chānöz the condition of a carpenter (chān) (see Gr.Gr. 143).
(? = عاجز) adj. c.g. poor, destitute (H. ix, 11).
m. an apology, excuse; a defence in a law case (Gr.M.). Another form of wŏzr, q.v.
f. bearing in mind, attentive consideration; esp. jealous thoughts, envy. -gözᵃran f. jealously counting and recounting another's possessions or family of children, envy.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. özᵒrᵒ), to bear in mind, attentively consider; to be jealous of, to envy; to interfere in a discussion or dispute. -gözᵃrun m. inf. to jealously count and recount another's good fortune; to intervene in a discussion and give, as it were, a judicial opinion regarding it.
m. N. of a certain bird of Kashmīr (El., who spells it auz).
f. (sg. dat. ōʦhaṭi), fainting, insensibility, a swoon.
adj. (f. üʦhᵘ̈), feeble, weak, emaciated (cf. Gr.Gr. 141).
m. quick effort, exertion, endeavour; the word always conveys the idea of speed with the endeavour.

. The fourteenth (or, if we count the aspirates ch and kh as separate letters, the sixteenth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character, the twenty-first (or, if we include ʦ, ʦh, and z, the twenty-fourth) consonant when written in the Śāradā or the Nāgarī character, and the third when written in the Perso-Arabic character. Its Kāshmīrī name is paḍurⁱ pö. It is sounded like an English p, but without any trace of the aspiration which is often heard in English when that letter is pronounced. ¶ The aspirate of p is ph پہ, which is the twenty-second (or, if we include ʦ, ʦh, and z, the twenty-fifth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet whe written in the Śāradā or the Nāgarī character. Its Kāshmīrī name is phariñᵘ̈ phö. ¶ This aspirate letter ph is also used to represent the Persian and Arabic letter f ف, which occurs only in words borrowed from those languages. In such cases the ف is usually pronounced in Kāshmīrī like an ordinary ph. Thus faqīr فقیر is usually pronounced phakīr. The aspiration is, however, not so strong as in India proper, so that some persons pronounce the word, and even write it, pakīr. In the middle or at the end of a word some people are inclined to retain the f-sound, or something like it, so that we often hear mupht مفت pronounced muft, and māph (for معاف) pronounced māf or, as in Persian, mu'āf. ¶ The letters p and ph are two of the few Kāshmīrī consonants which are never epenthetically affected by a succeeding vowel.

m. the foot, in Persian phrases, such as az-pā, (fallen) at the feet (Rām. 454); sar-ba-pā, from head to foot (YZ. 69); bar-pā بر پا or (Rām. 573) bar-pāh, adj. c.g. fixed, established. Cf. pusht-ĕ-pā, s.v. pusht.
for words beginning thus, see under pônᵘ.
f. a sheep's or goat's leg, a trotter. -holᵘ adj. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), (of a sheep or goat) crooked-legged; (of a man, met. in abuse) crooked-legged. -ras m. a soup made of trotters.
adj. used --˚, as in gāma-pᵒ, village-like, as in villages (p. 287a, l. 8); grīstⁱ-pⁱ, equal in rank to a husbandman, a fellow husbandman (p. 306b, l. 1).
f. pl. of pokᵘ, q.v. See also pakun.
adj. c.g. over stout, over thick, too fat.
m. (of grain, fruit, etc.), ripeness; strength, fatness, plumpness, power, might, valour.

m. in pacĕr-bandī f. fencing made of boards; a method of building the walls of a house with planks fitted into grooves in the sides of perpendicular posts, see L. 371 (pachar bandi) for particulars. Cf. pütᵘ̈.

m. (sg. dat. pachas), the half (waxing or waning) of a lunar month, a (lunar) fortnight, consisting of fifteen lunar days (cf. kö̃bari-pᵒ, p. 382b, l. 16; khīna-pᵒ, p. 428b, l. 37; pĕtᵃra-pᵃ, s.v. pĕtur) (K.Pr. 154, 161, 176). The fortnight of the waxing moon is called zūna- pach, q.v., s.v. zūn, and the fortnight of the waning moon is called gaṭa-pach (p. 310a, l. 41), q.v. (Śiv. 166, K. 57). ¶ pacha-bodᵘ adj. (f. -büzᵘ̈), consisting of, lasting for, or occurring before or after, many lunar fortnights. -wār f. (among upper-caste Hindūs) the commemorative rite (śrāddha) performed by the relations of the deceased once a fortnight for three months after the first month after a death. It is performed on the same lunar day of each fortnight as that on which the death occurred. ¶ pachukᵘ gen. sg. (f. pachücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a lunar fortnight.

m. (sg. dat. pachas), a party, the people of one party, as opposed to those of another (Gr.M.). ¶ pacha-pāth m. (sg. dat. -pātas), partiality, unfairness (Gr.M.). -pāta-rostᵘ adj. (f. -pāta-rüʦhᵘ̈), impartial (Gr.M.).

f. (sg. dat. pachöñᵘ̈), knowledge, acquaintance, ascertainment, recognition, experience, discrimination, discernment; recognition or acquaintance (with a person) (K.Pr. 260); distinguishing mark, characteristic; indication, token, sign. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to recognize; to discriminate, discern. --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to introduce (one person to another), to acquaint, cause to recognize.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pachônᵘ; 2 p.p. pachāñōv), to perceive, know, comprehend, understand; to recognize, identify; to distinguish, discern, discriminate. pachônᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pachöñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), perceived, comprehended, understood; recognized, identified; discerned, discriminated.
or pachitāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. pacha(i)tôwᵘ ), to regret (Gr.Gr. xliii).
or pōchĕr m. stoutness, thickness, strength (cf. myāda-pᵒ, s.v. myāda); prosperity, thriving, success (cf. atha-pᵒ, p. 60b, l. 22).

m. (f. pachiñ), a bird (esp. a large one, not a sparrow or the like) (cf. khŏḍa-pᵒ, p. 392b, l. 1) (L. 129; Rām. 694); El. s.v. pachhin describes it as a 'water-fowl of Kashmir'; cf. L. 129, sok pachin, the Pintail duck, and K.Pr. 35, which certainly refers to an aquatic bird generally. -bövᵘ̈ f. the thigh of such a bird (e.g. the leg of a cooked fowl). -pūtᵘ m. the young of such a bird (Gr.Gr. 131). -ṭhūl m. the egg of such a bird. -tīr f. the feather of such a bird; a quill (such as is used for writing).
f. (pl. pachēra), the ropes or chains by which an animal's hind legs are tied, heel-ropes (cf. potᵘ-pᵘ, s.v. potᵘ); the peg or post to which such heel-ropes are fastened.

f. a heel-rope, a heel-chain, i.q. pachīr, q.v. (cf. potᵘ-pᵘ, s.v. potᵘ). ¶ pachārĕ diñĕ f. pl. inf. to fix heel-ropes or the like on an animal. --lagañĕ -- f. pl. inf. heel- ropes to be applied; met. to become distraught by being compelled to work without intermission, not to have a moment's freedom from duty, to find oneself unable to leave one's work for a moment through fear of its going wrong.

m. the west (Śiv. 246; Rām. 516, 1681); a foreign country in the west. --kun -- adv. in, or into, the west; (with a verb of motion) to, or towards, the west. ¶ pachimⁱ kinⁱ adv. from the west. ¶ pachimi kani adv. in the west; from the west. --kanyukᵘ -- adj. (f. --kanicᵘ̈ --), produced in the west, of western origin. ¶ pachimyukᵘ adj. (f. pachimicᵘ̈), western, produced or born in the west, in a westerly direction (Gr.M.).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. pocᵘ, fem. pücᵘ̈; 2 p.p. pacyōv; pücᵘ̈ and pacyōv also occur in the conjugation of pakun, q.v.), to become digested (esp. of indigestible food); (of property entrusted to another) to become successfully misappropriated. pocᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. pücᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, which is also the perf. part. f. of pakun, q.v.), become digested, as ab.; become misappropriated, as ab. pacyō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. pacyē-müʦᵘ̈), id.

m. the foot; cf. padma-pᵒ, s.v. padᵃm (Śiv. 169, 178, 191, 205, 433, 445, 500, etc.; Rām. 69, 193, 243, 287, 316; K. 62, 70, 75, 212, 310, etc.); a step (El.); the mark of a foot, a footprint (K. 396); a section (of a book), a chapter, part, canto. --malȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to shampoo the feet, stroke the feet (as a service, or in token of reverence). --namȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the feet to bow; hence (impersonally) to bow or bend the feet, to show reverence (K. 494); cf. pādi namun, bel. --phalȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the feet to swell; met. to be utterly wearied by continual coming and going; cf. pȧdⁱ phᵒ, s.v. podᵘ. --raṭȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to grasp the feet of another (in reverence, supplication, or the like). --siwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to show respect by touching the feet. ¶ pāda-kamal m. a foot-lotus, a lotus-foot, a foot beautiful as a lotus, (as a reverential term) a foot (K. 147, 184, 392, 460, 462, 962, 1128). ¶ pādi namun m.inf. (used as an impersonal verb, as in pādi nomᵘnas, it was bowed by him at his feet), to bow before a person's feet, to greet respectfully, prostrate oneself before another (K. 74, 583, 719, 937, 1164). -pranām m. prostration at another's feet (in reverence, etc.). --rᵃkh -- or pādĕ-rīkhā f. (sg. dat. --rᵃkhi --), a certain mark on the sole of the foot (considered, in chiromancy, as indicating future kingship). It is a straight unbroken line from the great toe to the heel (Rām. 1263). ¶ pādan lagun m.inf. to be attached to a person's feet, to prostrate oneself at another's feet (in reverence or the like). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall at (a person's) feet (in reverence or the like) (K. 310, 336, 413, 839, 851, 856, 961, 1016-17; YZ. 262). ¶ pādas lagun m.inf. to be attached to (a person's foot), to prostrate oneself at a person's foot, to be entirely devoted to him (K. 1141). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall at a person's foot (i.q. pādan pyonᵘ, ab.) (K. 490, 513, 681, 910, 1012, 1028).

m. a foot (Rām. 9); a place, position, station (cf. aṭala-pᵒ, p. 67b, l. 36; para-pᵒ, s.v. par 4; parama-pᵒ, s.v. param) (L.V. 10, 77-9; Śiv. 858, 1050, 1555); a quarter or line of a stanza, a verse (cf. dada-pᵒ, p. 187b, l. 39) (L.V. 78, 84); a complete or inflected word (Śiv. 92, 1019).

f. (this word is reported to be masculine, but, from the next, it appears to be feminine), (of a fine powder) the condition of being scattered about over a considerable area. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. scattering to occur; esp. powder, etc., to be scattered in a line on a road or the like.
f. (sg. dat. püzᵘ̈), breaking wind, a fart (Gr.Gr. 126).
f. the sole of the foot; esp. the mark of the sole on the ground, a footprint.
m. a father. ba-dargāh-ĕ-padar بدرگاہ پدر in the palace of the father (Rām. 1511).
or pādᵃ̇rᵃ̇-sᵃ̇h m. a lion (El. pádir suh; Gr.M., by error, padarᵒ; Rām. 910, 1332).

m. reward, recompense; requital, retaliation, revenge; (in Kāshmīrī) trouble, distress (from any cause, such as disease, poverty, loss, grief). --anun -- m.inf. to bring distress, to cause sudden distress (as ab.). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. distress (as ab.) to occur.
f. a way, road, path (cf. param pᵒ, s.v. param); position, station, rank, dignity (Śiv. 320, 1088, 1518).
f. a woman of perfect beauty. In Hindū legend there are four classes of woman, of which this is the most perfect. The Skt. form of the word is Padminī (K.Pr. 186).
m. a lotus-seat, a kind of throne (Śiv. 1102, 1805). Cf. padᵃm.
m. one who is incessantly going, a vagrant. padōri phalañĕ f. pl. inf. to be wearied by continually going (as in searching for something lost).
f. a habit of much walking about; esp. a habit of gadding about to find out hidden things, the habit of a Paul Pry.

or pādshĕh پادشہ, pāthchāh (q.v.), or pātashāh (q.v.) m. a king, monarch, sovereign (Gr.M.; W. 140 ˚shāh; Śiv. 432, pādashāh; Rām. 748, 927, ˚shāh; 452, ˚shĕh; YZ. 2, 103, ˚shāh; 161, ˚shĕh; K.Pr. 31, 161, 174, 209, 227, 246, ˚shāh).
f. royalty, sovereignty, sway, rule (cf. pāthshöhī and pātashöhī).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. podᵘ; 2 p.p. pazōv), to break wind, to fart (Gr.Gr. 126).

m. (sg. dat. paḍaras), the hoof of a horse, cow, or other four-footed hoofed animal (cf. gurⁱ-pⁱ, p. 299a, l. 1; khar-pᵒ, a kind of pear, p. 407a, l. 28; khrāvi-pᵒ, the under part of a patten, p. 416b, l. 9) (K. 73, of an ass); met. the foot of a human being (K.Pr. 156). ¶ paḍar-chotᵘ adj. (f. -chüʦᵘ̈), white-hoofed (a horse with one white hoof being considered unlucky); met. one who brings about or causes an unlucky omen. -holᵘ adj. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), uneven hoofed, having a damaged hoof. ¶ paḍurⁱ pö m. the name used in schools for the letter pa when written in the Śāradā character.

m. water for washing the feet. --arigⁱ -- m. pl. worship (of a god or human being) by laving the feet and making other similar offerings. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to offer such worship. ¶ pādĕ-pranām m. reverent worship as above (Śiv. 986, 1141, 1168, 1170). -pūz f. the ceremony of offering this worship. -rīkhā, see pādi-rᵃkh, p. 681a, l. 17. -zal m. water which has been used for washing feet (esp. in worship or adoration) (K. 931, 1045).

m. (sg. dat. padmas), a lotus, used in the following compounds borrowed from Skt.:-- ¶ padma-nāb  m. a name of Vishṇu (Śiv. 344). -pād m. a foot like a lotus, a lotus-foot (Śiv. 976, 1088); he who has feet like lotuses, a title of Śiva (Śiv. 238, 1263, 1334). -pạthᵃr m. (sg. dat. -pạtras), a lotus-leaf (Śiv. 1432).

f. a long cloth worn round the head, a turban or pagṛī (K. 419). --badalüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to exchange turbans (in token of close friendship); generally, to form a firm friendship; to change one's own turban (for a clean one). --badalāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause (another) to exchange turbans, as ab., to form a close friendship with another; to cause a turban to be changed for a clean one.

adv. on the following day, to-morrow (Gr.M.; W. 95, paga; Rām. 143, 165, 431; H. iii, 4; vi, 16; xii, 10; YZ. 88; K.Pr. 21, 178, 194, (pagah) 227); met. to-morrow, very soon (Rām. 176, 689, 1460, 1512, 1528). -kani adv. about to-morrow, perhaps to-morrow (Gr.Gr. 159). -kyutᵘ adj. (f. -kiʦᵘ̈), for to-morrow (Gr.M.). -tām or -tāmath or -tāñ or -tāñĕth, until to-morrow, up to to-morrow. ¶ pagahukᵘ adj. (f. pagahücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, to-morrow.

adj. c.g. mad, insane. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become mad; met. (of a person or thing) to become discarded, pushed away, sent packing, rejected (on account of some fault or flaw). --karun -- m.inf. to make mad; met. to discard, reject, as ab.
f. a small turban, a little pagṛī (such as would be worn by a boy); a man's turban (El. pagir).

f. (sg. dat. pöshᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 31), a collection of dung or human ordure (used as a manure for vegetables, while animal dung is used for grain crops) (El. pah, Gr.M.). --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to throw such manure (on a field) (Gr.M.). --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to spread heaps of manure (over a field). --wahārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to spread manure (on a field).
in bar-pāh (Rām. 573) for bar-pā برپا see pā, p. 678a, l. 37.

or pāha 1 adj. c.g. a thing temporarily borrowed for use (and to be returned identically; i.e. not a loan of which merely the equivalent is to be returned). The same as the Persian 'āriyat; cf. atha-pᵒ, p. 60b, l. 25. --onᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --üñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), taken on loan, as ab. --anun -- m.inf. to take on loan (for use). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give on loan (for use, as ab.). --nyunᵘ -- m.inf. to take away on loan (as ab.). -pöṭhⁱ or -pöṭhin adv. on loan (for use).
in pāha-lara f. pl. the ribs (spoken of as a whole). Cf. lar 2.
in nahāka-pahāka, a jingle of nahāka, q.v. Cf., however, pahākh.
f. (sg. dat. pahāki), a grazing ground high in the mountains, to which cattle are sent in the hot season.
or pahālwān m. (f. pahālwöñᵘ̈, q.v.), a hero, champion (Rām. 492, 530, 1402, pahalᵒ); an athlete, wrestler; a stout sturdy fellow (YZ. 93, pahlawān); brave. Cf. phailwān.
f. the profession of a wrestler.
f. the profession of a wrestler.
f. the wife of a professional wrestler, the wife of an athlete, etc. Cf. pahālwān.

adv. somewhat, a little, used with adjectives and adverbs, as in boḍᵘ-pᵘ, somewhat big, p. 85a, l. 3; so brō̃ṭh-pᵒ, p. 128a, l. 34; dūr-pᵒ, p. 238b, l. 32; kam-pᵒ, p. 442b, l. 19; kôshurᵘ-pᵘ, p. 481b, l. 43; nĕbar-pᵒ, p. 620b, l. 28; narm-pᵒ, p. 651b, l. 22; nyūrᵘ-pᵘ, p. 673b, l. 32; path pᵒ, s.v. path 3 (El. pahan; H. x, 7; xii. 6).
(? spelling and gender), a certain medicinal plant, used as a diuretic (L. 75).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pahonᵘ), to wear handsome clothes, be decked out, adorned. pahonᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pahüñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈. This word is mostly used in the f., as applied to a woman), dressed in fine clothes, decked out.

m. a division of time consisting of three hours, an eighth part of a whole day and night, a watch (cf. prath pahara, s.v. prath 2; patyumᵘ pahar, patim paharan, etc., s.v. patyumᵘ) (Gr.Gr. 158; W. 106; Śiv. 628, 1443, 1712; K. 969; H. iii, 1; v, 8); a turn of watch, a period during which a watchman is on guard (H. viii, 5, 6, 8, 10, 11, 13). pahara-wôlᵘ m. a watchman, sentinel (H. viii, 8).
m. a hill, mountain; a mountainous tract, 'the hills.' pahārukᵘ gen. (f. pahārücᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or born in the hill-country.
m. a watch, watchman, sentinel; a guard, a corporal and his men (K 968). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to be diligent in attending guard.
f. a watchman's work, sentinel's duty, guard.
f. (sg. dat. paharöʦᵘ̈), a kind of large high-edged metal cauldron or pot. (Śiv. 1554, with pun on pŏha-rāth, a night in the month of Pŏh.)

f. (sg. dat. pahiyĕ, Gr.M.), the circumference, felly, or outer rim of a wheel (cf. ratha-pᵒ, s.v. ratha); hence, a wheel (Gr.M.), the wheel to which a well-rope is attached (cf. krīrⁱ-pⁱ, p. 475b, l. 34).
(? pahᵃl-mŏ̈nḍᵃ), ? f. Pyrethrum sp., a certain medicinal plant. The root (mö̆nḍᵘ̈) is said to be good for toothache (L. 76).
f. a shepherd's wife (El. pahaj), see pahôlᵘ.

m. (f. pahöjᵘ̈, El. pahaj), a goatherd, a shepherd (as found in the hill country. He spends the summer there, with his family and dogs, until driven down to the valleys by the snows of winter) (El. pohol, pŏhul, puhul, and púhul; L. 464, pohl) (L.V. 108; K.Pr. 172, 249, poholᵘ). pahölⁱ-bāy  f.his wife.
m. a mountain stream (deep and rapid); N. of the river of the Lolāb Valley (El. puhór).

f. a hut, a cottage, a hovel, a small grass or reed dwelling (cf. ḍāka-pᵒ, p. 205b, l. 17; graṭa-pᵒ, p. 304b, l. 48; gāsa-pᵒ, p. 307b, l. 43; khal-pᵒ, p. 396b, l. 50; nar-pᵒ, p. 646a, l. 45; nāra-pᵒ, p. 648a, l. 22; pĕʦi-pᵒ, s.v. pë̆ʦᵘ̈; rĕshⁱ-pⁱ, s.v. ryoshᵘ) (El. páhar; Gr.M.; K. 1160, 1162); cf. pāhürᵘ̈ and pörᵘ̈ 2. pahārĕ-hondᵘ gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a hut.
adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, the hills, produced in the hills.
adj. (f. pahᵘ̈jᵘ̈), possessing corners, cornered; globular, but possessing corners.
or pŏharĕñ f. of pohurᵘ, p. 703b, l. 12.
or pahur m. (sg. dat. paharas), a roof, a thatch (cf. nāra-pᵒ, p. 648a, l. 24). --tārun -- m.inf. to put on a roof, to roof (a house, etc.).
f. a hut, cottage, i.q. pahörᵘ̈, q.v. (YZ. 477).

in pȧhⁱ-pan m. pl. a corruption of pŏhⁱ-pan, q.v., l. 49, bel. In the month of Pŏh, leaves fallen in great numbers from the trees collect on the ground. Hence, this compound is used to signify a great crowd of people collected together in order to buy some scarce but necessary commodity.

or pödā adj. c.g. born, created, generated, produced (Gr.M., W. 129, Śiv. 1329-30); manifested, exhibited; invented, discovered; procured, acquired, earned, gained. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become produced, become born, come into existence (Rām. 1293; K.Pr. 127, 163); to become manifest, to become visible, appear, come into sight (Rām. 319, 466, 1063, 1627; H. ii, 1; iii, 8; x, 4, 5, 7; xii, 10; YZ. 177). --karun -- m.inf. to bring into being, create, make, produce (Gr.M., gŏḍañi pᵒ kᵒ, to make for the first time, invent; L.V. 99; Śiv. 32; Rām. 696, 1515; H. iii, 8; vii, 4, 6, 8; xii, 7; K.Pr. 46); to manifest, make manifest. --karan-wôlᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --karan-wājĕñ --), a creator (Gr.M.). --sapanun -- m.inf. to come into being, be created (Gr.M.); to become manifest, to become visible, to appear (Rām. 388, 1357).
or pödal adj. c.g. walking, on foot (Gr.M.). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go on foot, to walk (Gr.M.).
or pödāwār پیداوار m. produce, that which is produced (Gr.M.).
or pögām m. a message (Rām. 800, 1604); news, intelligence (cf. nāma-pᵒ anun, p. 636b, l. 31) (Rām. 451, 513).

or pöjāma (= پاجامہ) m. trousers, long drawers (cf. khashĕrⁱ-pⁱ, p. 419b, l. 12; pȧṭⁱ-pⁱ, s.v. poṭᵘ 2) (Śiv. 789, paijyāma; K.Pr. 95, 219); cf. pājiwôrᵘ. -band m. the string by which drawers are fastened round the waist, a trousers-string. -ḍūrᵘ̈ f., id. -gĕgürᵘ̈ f. the upper part of a pair of drawers round the waist and thighs.
(cf. پیک) adv. running at full speed (K. 825).

f.pl. or paikȧrⁱ, pökȧrⁱ , m.pl. پی کڙی chains (for the legs of convicts), shackles, gyves, fetters (K. 36, 90, 366, 461). pökᵃrĕ gaʦhañĕ f. pl. inf. fetters to be imposed; met. (owing to want of assistance) household cares to confine one to the house (so that one can never get out), to be a slave to household cares.
or pöl m. white pus (of a boil or the like), purulent matter. ¶ paila-dag f. the pain caused by accumulated pus in a yet unopened sore. -digiñ f. a flow, a stream, of pus.
a foot, in pairi path pairi adv. step by step (El.).

or pöra or (Rām. 1146) pör m. fear, terror, agitation. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. such fear or terror to fall (upon a person); kŏṭhĕn pör pyonᵘ, agitation to fall to the knees, the knees to shake (from fear, rage, etc.), to be unable to stand steady (from this cause) (Rām. 1146).
or pöravī پیروی f. following, pursuit. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to follow after (in order to take care of), to protect (H. i, 1).

or pörāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. pai(ö)rôwᵘ , to put (clothes, etc., dir. obj.) on another person (dat.) (cf. phĕran pᵒ, p. 705b, l. 27) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1725, 1821); to adorn (oneself or another) (Śiv. 1632, Rām. 662 pairawun). Cf. pairun.
(also written pörawunᵘ) n.ag. (f. pairavüñᵘ̈), one who puts on clothes; one who adorns (Śiv. 516).

or pörun conj. 1 (1 p.p. pūrᵘ, f. pǖrᵘ̈; 2 p.p. pairyōv; conj. part. pṻrith), to wear (clothes), to put on (clothes, ornaments, etc.) on oneself or on another (Gr.M.; L.V. 76; Śiv. 1388, 1438, 1440, 1447, 1597; Rām. 182, 214, 654; K. 29, 85, 97, 183, 422-3, 650; H. v, 10; x, 2, 9; YZ. 373, 541); to adorn, ornament (El. perun) (cf. masnad pairȧnⁱ, p. 600a, l. 27) (K. 420, 637, 843, 913, 928, 984); to put (a saddle on a horse), to saddle (H. xi, 9).

or pö̃sa m. a certain copper coin, a pice (cf. dŏbal pᵒ, p. 183b, l. 18; khām pᵒ, p. 400a, l. 14; pŏkhta pᵒ, p. 727b, l. 8) (El. pãṅsah) (Gr.M.; W. 146 pāṇsa; H. vii, 25-6; YZ. 402; K.Pr. 106, 145); cash, money (cf. pāñirⁱ-pⁱ, p. 748b, l. 11) (El.; K.Pr. 73, 164). -phyurᵘ m. pice-exchange, (in buying and selling) profits in pice (not in large sums). -wād m. counting by pice (and not by large sums; used with reference to the passing of money, or in giving, receiving, or counting profits). -waĩsa m.pl. pice and the like, pice etc. ¶ paĩsā-khanḍā or pö̃sā-khanḍā m. about one pice (in this, the final ā in each case represents the suffix of the indefinite article; see āh 1).
or pbö̃shĕ card. about five (Gr.Gr. 83, Rām. 663, K. 938).

or pötav (= پاتابہ) f. 'puttees', a bandage for the legs on a journey, worn by both Hindūs and Musalmāns (cf. pula-pᵒ, p. 730b, l. 21) (El. paitawa, L. 458, patawa). paitavi- (or pötav-)horᵘ  m. a pair of 'puttees' (one for each leg). -khŏr or -khōr m. a single puttee (for one leg).
m. (a corruption of paiwand, q.v.), junction, connexion, intimate union, absolute oneness in bodily personality (Śiv. 643).
m. junction, connexion (El.; Gr.M.); a joint, piece, patch; graft, grafting, budding (cf. arra-pᵒ, p. 44b, l. 17; barga-pᵒ, p. 120a, l. 44; pirth-pᵒ, p. 770a, l. 1) (Śiv. 1573). Cf. paivĕn.
adj. c.g. (a stock to which a graft has been applied) grafted, budded.
adj. c.g. patched, pieced; grafted, engrafted (on to a stock); produced from, or borne by, a grafted tree.

or pözār m. a slipper, a shoe (made of leather) (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 56, 165, 248). -dĕl m. a mean little worn-out useless shoe. -dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to give shoes, to drub with the shoe; met. to beat with abuse and disgrace (El. paizār dyunᵘ) (Rām. 1090). -jūrⁱ f. a pair of slippers, etc. (Gr.M.). -körⁱ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to drub and abuse. -podᵘ m. the sole of a shoe. -phrath or -phrith m. (sg. dat. -phratas or -phritas), an old worn-out ill-fitting shoe.--pȧṭⁱ karȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to do shoe-soles, i.e. to drub with shoes; hence, met. to abuse, threaten and abuse. -shikhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a worn-out shoe. -züṭᵘ̈ f. a rag of a shoe, a worn-out shoe.
m. trousers, long drawers (i.q. paijāma, q.v.).
f. (sg. dat. pạjᵃrüñᵃ), felling a hem (in sewing).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pạjᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. pạjᵃrun, q.v. pạjᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (1 p.p. pạjarövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. pạjᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, see pạjᵃrun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pạjᵒrᵒ), to fell a hem (in sewing) (Gr.Gr. 7). pạjᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. pạjᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of cloth, etc.) felled and hemmed.
adj. c.g. determined, obstinate, stubborn, obdurate. -mọ̆nḍᵘ 1 (for 2, see pakh 1) m. 'an obstinate block', hard-hearted, grumpy, cruel, pitiless.

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. pākaladiñ), one who is afflicted with a purulent gathering, one who suffers as if he had such a gathering; met. one who becomes easily enraged (e.g. by a mere word); (of a rag, lint, or the like) fouled with pus.
m. the condition of being thoroughly cooked, maturity, ripeness; the trade, business, or occupation of cooking.

m.inf. (1 p.p. pakanôwᵘ), to cause to move or go (YZ. 100); to put in motion, set a-going (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1885; H. xi, 14); to drive (an animal) (H. xi, 8); to stir, agitate (with a spoon or the like); to propel (a boat) (Śiv. 1804-5, 1830); to hasten, urge, impel, propel, drive (Gr.Gr. 176; K. 298, 986, 1125); to cause to flow or run (e.g. a stream of liquid); ¶ to promulgate, to put in force, put in operation; to make current, give currency to, put in circulation, issue (as coin, etc.); (in a market) to cause the sale of goods to flourish, to cause certain goods to be in great demand (cf. mŏla pᵒ, p. 566a, l. 86); to discharge, fire (an arrow, bullet, etc.), to shoot, to throw (a dart, stone, etc.); ¶ to originate, introduce, bring into use; ¶ to cause to go on well, to cause to flourish, keep in good working condition (cf. bözⁱ pakanāvüñᵘ̈, p. 152b, l. 14); to support (another), carry on (another's) household affairs, keep him comfortably off.
m.inf. to cook, to dress victuals (esp. by boiling in water); to cause to cook (El.). pākanôwᵘ-motᵘ b perf. part. (pākanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈) cooked, dressed, boiled (by some one).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. pākanyōv), (of a boil or the like) to become ripe; (of grain being roasted for popcorn) to become completely cooked. pākanyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pākanyē-müʦᵘ̈), (of a boil or the like) ripened; (of popcorn) completely roasted.
f. wages for going, wages of a messenger.
m. (sg. dat. pakawanas), docility, readiness to accomplish orders.
conj. 1 (p.p. pākowᵘ), to cook, dress victuals (esp. by boiling) (cf. payith pākavith, s.v. payun) (Gr.Gr. 122, Śiv. 1717). pākowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pāküvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), cooked (by boiling).

n.ag. (f. pakavüñᵘ̈), one who goes, one who proceeds (K.Pr. 47, of a river flowing on; Śiv. 239 (id.), 538; H. x, 11; K.Pr. 99); one who is going, one who is at the point of death, moribund; that (esp. something inferior) which is being successfully sold, that for which there is a great demand in the market (cf. mŏla pᵒ, p. 566a, l. 39); one who successfully supports himself, one who carries on his livelihood. ¶ pakawunuy adv. immediately on starting; hence, quickly, speedily.

m. the act of walking, used in special senses in the following:-- paka-mọ̆nḍᵘ 2 (for 1, see paka 2) m. (the lower part of the leg, including the hoof, (of a sheep or goat) a trotter; cf. pāca. paka-mŏnḍⁱ-būrⁱ f. the hoof end of a trotter (used for making broth). paka-mŏnḍⁱ-ras m. trotter-broth. paka-pakh f. (sg. dat. -paki), continual coming and going, going backwards and forwards (till one is weary). For the gender of this word, see Gr.Gr. 75.

m. (sg. dat. pākas), matter, pus. ¶ pāka-cār m. the wringing of pus, the pain or torture from a gathering full of pus before it bursts, the pain of an unopened ripened boil, etc. -dag f., id. -ḍọ̆gᵘ m. a whitlow full of pus. -digan or -digiñ f. a flow of pus, the stream of ripe pus issuing from an opened boil, wound, or the like. -ḍusurᵘ m. a boil or carbuncle full of pus. -lala f. a lump of thickened pus. -phĕphur m. a boil full of pus. -phyorᵘ or -phyūrᵘ m. a drop, or bead, of pus. -raz f. a flow of pus. -shĕl m. a string of clotted pus. -ṭhisorᵘ or -ṭhusurᵘ m. a scabby sore or pimple full of pus. ¶ pākukᵘ 1 gen. (f. pākücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or connected with pus.
m. (sg. dat. pakhas), the act of taking a side, partisanship, party spirit (cf. pönʦa-pokhᵘ, s.v. pānʦ). pakha-ʦhyonᵘ 1 adj. (f. -ʦhë˘ñᵘ̈), (of a person) deserted by one's party, left helpless.

m. (sg. dat. pākas), cooking or dressing food (esp. by boiling) (cf. hȧnḍⁱ-pⁱ, p. 337b, l. 37; mŏnḍⁱ, p. 574b, l. 31; phŏṭⁱ-pⁱ, p. 715b, l. 4) (Gr.Gr. 122; Śiv. 1020; K.Pr. 4, 219). pākh dyunᵘ m.inf. to cook something by boiling (K.Pr. 40); to cook (some work), i.e. a worker to annoy a person by delaying the completion of his task, to ca' canny. pākh lagun m.inf. to be in a condition of cooking, to be being cooked; to be completely cooked; to be annoyed by delay in the execution of some work. ¶ pāka anun f.inf. to cook thoroughly (esp. by boiling). -dār adj. c.g. well-cooked. -dorᵘ adj. hard to cook, tough in spite of cooking. --drāmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --drāmüʦᵘ̈ --), issued from cooking, that of which the cooking is finished, ready cooked. -drāv adj. c.g., id. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to draw out from cooking, to dish up cooked food. --nērun -- m.inf. to issue from cooking, to have its cooking completed, to be ready cooked. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), uncooked, raw, not fully cooked, badly cooked. -raʦhar m. uncookedness, rawness. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to become fully cooked; (of a boil or the like) to be fully ripe (cf. pākh 1). ¶ pākukᵘ 2 gen. (f. pākücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or connected with cooking.

f. (sg. dat. pakhi), the wing (of a bird) (cf. gö̃ṭha-pᵒ, p. 311b, l. 45; kāwa-pᵒ, p. 495a, l. 17; pönʦa-pokhᵘ, s.v. pānʦ) (El. m.; Śiv. 351, 1011, 1064, 1640, 1687, 1752, 1783; Rām. 531; H. viii, 7; YZ. 38, pāk, see pākh 4; K.Pr. 35); a feather (El. f.). ¶ pakha-dünzᵘ̈ f. the flesh at the root of a fowl's wing. -mūl m., id. -pūstīn f. a kind of warm overcoat. -ʦhyonᵘ 2 adj. (f. -ʦhë˘ñᵘ̈), (of a bird) having the wings cut off; (of a cloak or the like) having one side cut off. -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), (of a bird, or something having wings) having the wings cut off; a piece cut off a wing. -wörᵘ̈ f. the flesh at the root of the thick, plump wing of a fowl. -wāv 1 m. the air or wind created by the movement of a bird's wings. --yiñĕ -- f. pl. inf. wings to come, encouragement to be felt, courage to be mustered, (after impediment or the like) to feel ready to undertake work (owing to the cessation of impediment).

adj. c.g. pure, clear, clean, holy, spotless, hallowed, blameless, innocent (cf. nēka-pᵒ, p. 629b, l. 23) (Gr.M.; Rām. 771; YZ. 221; K.Pr. 162, 199); undefiled, unpolluted, immaculate, free (from) (H. v, 10). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain pure, to keep oneself undefiled.
i.q. pakh 3, a wing (noted only in YZ. 38, where possibly it is a misreading).
m. a large fan, a punkah (Gr.M.). -wāv 2 m. the wind caused by the motion of a punkah. --wāyun -- m.inf. to put a fan in motion, to fan (K. 928, 980, 1132).
f. N. of a country to the north-west of Kashmīr. It was known to Musalmān historians by the name of Pakhlī, and was defined as the hill country between Kashmīr and the Indus (RT.Tr. II, 434).
adj. c.g. feathered, possessing feathers (of something not naturally feathered, e.g. a dress embroidered with feathers); (of a fish or the like) possessing fins of a special kind.

or pakhānḍ m. a religious hypocrite, one who puts on the airs of a pious person, one who hypocritically wears the dress or sectarian marks of a religious mendicant. The same as pākhanḍ, pakhȧnḍⁱ, etc., qq.v. --wahārun -- m.inf. to play the hypocrite, to counterfeit one's appearance (e.g. pretending to be ill when one is in good health or putting on assumed piety).
m. a hypocrite, a sham religious mendicant or the like. The same as pakhanḍ, pakhānḍ, pakhȧnḍⁱ, etc., qq.v.
pākhȧnḍⁱ, or pakhönḍⁱ m. a hypocrite, one who deceitfully pretends to be a religious mendicant, or other religious person. Cf. pakhanḍ, pakhānḍ, pākhanḍ.
see pakhyukᵘ, col. a, l. 23 ab.
m. the Himalayan honeysuckle (Lonicera quinquelocularis, El.) (L. 461, pakhr phul).
m. a small piece of cloth or the like (for patching), a patch; cf. pakhᵃsh 2. pakhᵃca-wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), the joining of a patch, patching.

m. the sacrifice (yāg) of the lunar fortnight (pakh, for paksh, see pakhᵃch), (amougst Hindūs) a sacrifice performed on the day of the new and full moons. --thawun -- m.inf. to carry out this sacrifice throughout one's life, to make a practice of performing it. -worᵘ m. an oblation-cake offered at this sacrifice.

paksh, or pakhᵃsh 1 (for 2, see s.v.) m. (sg. dat. pakchas), a wing; a feather (cf. mōr-pᵒ, s.v. mōr); a flank, a side; the fin (of a fish) (cf. gāḍa-pakhᵃsh, p. 276b, l. 21); a party, class, faction; kinship, relationship, a person's relatives (on one side or the other, as we say 'the father's side', 'the mother's side') (cf. ōra-paksh, p. 42a, l. 4); the half of a lunar month, a fortnight (consisting of fifteen lunar days); the side of an argument, position, opinion, thesis; partiality, assistance, protection, defence; the wheel of a vehicle (cf. pakhᵘ̈cᵘ̈) (L.V. 26).
m., i.q. pakhucᵘ, a small piece of cloth, a patch (cf. kan-pᵒ, p. 447b, l. 11; nāla-pᵒ, p. 632b, l. 32).

m. the radial-like spokes of the large wheel of a spinning wheel (yẹ̆ndᵃr, q.v.). This wheel consists of a large number of spokes issuing close together as radials from the hub. Two of these wheels are side by side on the same axle, and are further connected together by a string running alternately round the end of one spoke to the end of the corresponding spoke on the opposite wheel, and so back again, till all the spokes are connected each with its opposite number. The whole thus forms one broad wheel of which the circumference is formed by the numerous strings crossing from spoke to spoke. Round this circumference is passed the driving band, which, when the large wheel is revolved, turns the small wheel on which the thread is spun (cf. kônᵘ 1) (Śiv. 1014).
adv. in ȧndⁱ-pȧkhⁱ, outside and near by, here there and everywhere (p. 31b, l. 31). Cf. pakh 2, pokhᵘ, and pakhᵃch.

or pakhidār adj. c.g. (as subst., f. pȧkhⁱdārĕñ), one who is a member of one side or other (paternal or maternal) of a family; (at a festival or the like) a guest who has arrived as a member of or connexion (as family priest or the like) with one or other side of the family. --mū̃trunᵘ -- m. an invitation to a person on the ground of his connexion (as priest or the like) with one side of a family.
f. the mutual connexion between the members of the two sides of a family.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. pokᵘ, f. pücᵘ̈; 2 p.p. pacyōv), to go, tread, proceed, progress, advance (cf. brũh brũh pᵒ, p. 120b, l. 21; nēri pᵒ, p. 673b, l. 45; phū̃ki pᵒ, p. 689b, l. 34; pawa pᵒ, s.v. pav) (Gr.Gr. 5, 111, 178, 183-4, 204; Gr.M.; L.V. 19; Śiv. 654, 724, 732, 805, 879, 917, 1626, 1654, 1829, 1834, 1861, 1867; Rām. 42, 231, 319, 440, 778, 861, 870, etc.; K. 147, 417, 1008; H. v, 7; viii, 7; YZ. 407; K.Pr. 84); to walk, travel (cf. brörⁱ pᵒ, p. 125b, l. 43) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1309; Rām. 946, 1047, 1195, 1225, 1250, etc.; K. 533, 1125, 1158, 1160; H. iii, 1, 2; x, 1, 4; xii, 2, 7) (pathar pakun, to go on foot, L. 460); to come along (Śiv. 1442, 1481, 1666; Rām. 365); to go (to, dat.), to reach, achieve, gain (Śiv. 717, 1027, 1474); ¶ to flow, run (as a stream, a pen) (cf. dāl paküñᵘ̈, p. 210a, l. 20; dāth pakun, p. 257a, l. 19) (Rām. 357, 948, 1543; K. 586; YZ. 132, 417; K.Pr. 17); to be let loose (as the bowels) (cf. bād pᵒ, p. 82a, l. 4; dasth pakȧnⁱ, p. 256a, l. 45); to blow (as wind); to sail (as a ship) (Gr.M.; L.V. 107; Śiv. 1801, 1806); to fly along (as a bird) (Śiv. 1810); to go, be in motion (of a watch or the like) (Gr.M.); to set out, start (Śiv. 634, 728; Rām. 1099); ¶ to be current, be in vogue, to pass (as a coin) (Gr.M.); to be in operation, be in force; to conduct or comport oneself, to behave (nasīhüʦᵘ̈- mūjub pakun, to follow advice; cf. parda pᵒ, s.v. parda) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1067); ¶ to go on well, to flourish, thrive (as a business) (cf. bözⁱ paküñᵘ̈, p. 152b, l. 44; langar pakun, p. 527a, l. 28) (Gr.M.); to carry on, to support oneself, to live comfortably (cf. dam pᵒ, p. 216b, l. 14); (in the market) the sale of goods to flourish, the market to be hot, (of something inferior) to be successfully sold (cf. mŏla pᵒ, p. 566a, l. 33); (of goods in the market) to be on sale (K.Pr. 173, pachai, i.e. pacĕy); ¶ to walk about, walk around (Śiv. 1400-1, 1494, 1497); to go on, continue (from some past time), to be transmitted or handed down; ¶ to pass, work, serve, answer, be of avail; to try tricks or pranks, to practise trickery or deceit. ¶ pokᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pücᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), gone, started, etc.; (of a road) gone over, travelled over; sold well in the market, got rid of by sale, sold (in spite of faults). ¶ pakan-pūrᵘ m. the beginning of walking, first steps (e.g. of a baby, or a convalescent sick person, or a person recovering from a broken leg). -pāy m. privilege, right, authority, discretion, will, pleasure. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who goes, one who proceeds; esp. one who goes fast, one who habitually walks hurriedly; one who is at the point of death, moribund. ¶ pakān (or poet. pakan) gaʦhun  m.inf. to go on foot (Gr.M., Śiv. 845); to hasten (to, pĕṭh), to set forth, go along (Śiv. 321, 686, 699, 1097, 1627; Rām. 121, 141, 201, 205, etc.; K. 414, 433); to flow (of a liquid) (Rām. 109). ¶ pakanī impers. fut. part. it is to be gone, one must go (Gr.Gr. 111). ¶ paköniy adv. immediately on going; hence, immediately, on the spot. ¶ pakith gaʦhun m.inf. to be at once accomplished, (of some difficult task) to be easily and successfully accomplished.
m. Euonymus fimbriata and Hamiltonii (El. pakúá).

m. (sg. abl. pala 1), a great stone, a boulder, a globular rock (cf. āra-pᵒ, p. 41a, l. 45; nāga-pᵒ, p. 623b, l. 47; nīla-pᵒ, p. 634a, l. 9; nūna-pᵒ, p. 641a, l. 6) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1463; Rām. 413, 795; H. xii, 14, 15; K.Pr. 134). --chāwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to fling boulders; met. to have a violent quarrel (esp. when accompanied by mutual abuse). ¶ pala-har f. a boulder-quarrel, i.e. a quarrel in which the two parties fling boulders at each other (K.Pr. 134); met. a violent quarrel including gross mutual abuse (esp. between former friends). -mönzᵘ̈  f. a certain medicinal plant growing in rocky ground. It is internally used in herpes (L. 75). --pôñᵘ ḍalun -- m.inf. to disapprove of (mentally object to) another's request or order. -tala ponzᵘ hyuhᵘ m. 'like a monkey from under a rock', i.e. one who suddenly and unexpectedly or hurriedly rises up, or wakes up (e.g. one busily occupied or immersed in thought who is suddenly faced with something to be done at once). ¶ palan pôñᵘ dyunᵘ m.inf. 'to water rocks', i.e. to make useless efforts.

m. a protector, in khitra-pāl, etc., qq.v. (Śiv. 179, 391, 1147, 1221; lūka-pāl, p. 519b, l. 27); a shepherd (El.). -gām m. the shepherd's village. N. of a village romantically situated at the head of the Lë̆dᵘ̈rᵘ̈ ('Liddur') Valley.

m. (sg. abl. pala 2), a certain weight, the twentieth part of a seer, i.e. four tōlās (say two ounces) (Gr.Gr. 147, YZ. 404, K.Pr. 224); anything weighing this amount. ¶ pala pala adv. pal by pal, bit by bit (u.w. vbs. of seeing, examining, etc.). --pala kᵃnun -- m.inf. to sell pal by pal; met. to lose no opportunity of giving a bad name (to a person of good reputation).
f., in pālgaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. pain to be experienced (K.Pr. 75).

m. flesh (used in offering to a god), --˚ in al-pal, wine and flesh, i.e. two of the five things offered in the Kaula, or left-handed, worship of Śiva, the expression being employed to indicate all the five, which are wine, flesh, fish, special attitudes, and sexual intercourse. In Skt. these are called the five 'm's', as the name of each (madya, māṁsa, matsya, mudrā, maithuna) begins with that letter (cf. al-pal, p. 25a, l. 11) (L.V. 10).

m. a goal, butt, destination (esp. in alluding to a place, or the like) (cf. baḍi-pᵒ, p. 85b, l. 34) (K.Pr. pallah). -boḍᵘ 1 m. a village or country which is very distant. --karun -- m.inf. to make a goal, to be determined in one's goal (esp. when the goal is a place, even when it is distant or difficult).
m. the ornamental edge of the cloth of a turban. -boḍᵘ 2 adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), possessing a wide fringe of this kind.
m. (sg. dat. palakas), the eyelid, eyelash; a moment, instant, the twinkling of an eye. palakas-manz adv. in the twinkling of an eye, in an instant, in a moment.
m. (sg. dat. pālakas), a guardian, a protector (K. 54, 185).
f. (sg. dat. pālaki), spinach (El., who makes the word m.) (cf. nadȧrⁱ-pⁱ, p. 623a, l. 40).
(Śiv. 488) or pālanā f. protecting, guarding, nourishing, cherishing, fostering (Śiv. 100, 287, 488, 662, 1137, 1193, 1254, 1470, 1534, 1560, 1587, 1697, 1888).
or (L.V. 14) palān (= پالان) m. a saddle (of a horse), a riding-pad (on an elephant), a pack-saddle, or the like (cf. khar-pᵒ, p. 407a, l. 29).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pālanôwᵘ), to cause to be protected or cherished; to cause to be guarded, maintained (a thing, promise, etc., as in pālun), to obey carefully (an order) (K. 724). Causal of pālun, q.v., in all its meanings.

m. a bedstead, a bed (in the English sense, with legs) (Rām. 519, 705; H. iii, 7; v, 5, 6, 9; viii, 13; x, 5, 7, 8, 12). -khūrᵘ m. the leg of a bedstead. -wār m. bedclothes (fitting the bed as regards size).

m. a method of tying up a person as a punishment, in which his neck is bowed down between his legs, and his ankles and also his wrists tied together. --phirun -- m.inf. to tie up in this manner. --phirawun -- m.inf., id.
impers. fut. part. worthy to be protected, cherished, etc., as in the preceding.
m. N. of a tree, Butea frondosa.

or pạlᵃṭun conj. 3 (2 p.p. palaṭyōv. According to some, this verb is of the 2nd conj., with a 1 p.p. paloṭᵘ. See Gr.Gr. 206. Cf. paluṭᵘ, which is only another form of paloṭᵘ), to melt, deliquesce, become moist, damp (cf. atha pạlᵃṭȧnᵃ, p. 61a, l. 43). palaṭyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. palaṭyē-müʦᵘ̈), become moist, become damp, deliquesced.

m. covering of the body, clothes, a garment, coat (cf. dāmāna-pᵒ, p. 219b, l. 50; löchⁱ-pⁱ p. 507b, l. 13; mal-pᵒ, p. 564a, l. 14; murⁱ-pⁱ, p. 588b, l. 42; mȧtⁱ-pⁱ, p. 603a, l. 9; möta-pᵒ, p. 604a, l. 26; māz-pᵒ, p. 614b, l. 49; nakha-pᵒ, p. 628b, l. 11; namda-pᵒ, p. 638a, l. 1; pō̃bᵃri-pᵃ, p. 678b, l. 24; phĕran-pᵒ, p. 705b, l. 25; phiska-pᵒ, p. 713b, l. 28; phŏtⁱ-pⁱ, p. 715b, l. 20; potᵘ pᵒ, s.v. potᵘ; rūda-pᵒ, s.v. rūd; rĕka-pᵒ, s.v. rĕkh; rōt-pᵒ, s.v. rāth 1; rawa-pᵒ, s.v. rawa) (K.Pr. 151); met. the skin (as covering the body) (cf. phĕkⁱ-pⁱ, p. 720b, l. 44); a piece of cloth, a rag (cf. rata-pᵒ, s.v. rath). --dalav -- m. clothes and the like (i.e. clothes, quilts, and other baggage). --tulȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to gird up the clothes (K.Pr. 224); to tear off the skin, to flay (wholly or partially).

m. discouragement, a feeling of defeat (i.q. pŏlun, q.v.), in the following:-- palav dyunᵘ m.inf. to discourage, dishearten, defeat. --dith gaʦhun -- m.inf. (of a number of people assembled in the hope of something being accomplished) to go away unsuccessful or disheartened (owing to the expectation not being fulfilled).
a jingle of ālavith, see p. 26a, l. 42.
f. the hire or cost paid for taking care (of any person or thing), or for maintaining religious practices, a vow, or the like.
n.ag. (f. pālavüñᵘ̈), one who protects, takes care of (Śiv. 857, 1171, 1253, 1255, 1411, 1552); one who protects, cherishes; one who adheres to religion, a vow, or the like.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. palozᵘ. According to some this verb is of the 3rd conj., with a 2 p.p. palazōv, see Gr.Gr. 206), to be, or become, useful, serviceable, helpful (Gr.Gr. 206, 226). palozᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. palüzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), become useful, become serviceable, become helpful.
or pālēza 1 m. a field of melons or cucumbers (cf. hĕndawan-pᵒ, p. 338b, l. 27).
m. hemiplegia; constipation. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. an attack of hemiplegia to come on.
f. a battalion, a regiment (El., Gr.M., L. 402); an army (Rām. 857).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. polᵘ, f. püjᵘ̈; 2 p.p. pajyōv), to give privately.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pôlᵘ, f. pöjᵘ̈ 1 (L.V. 62), for 2, see s.v.; 2 p.p. pājyōv), to protect, guard, nourish, cherish, foster (Gr.Gr. 31; Śiv. 418, 977, 1391, 1723, 1758; Rām. 300, 1122, 1431, 1509; K. 320, 584, 743); to take care of, guard, maintain (a thing, a quality, a promise, a command, a course of conduct, etc.), carefully to follow (instructions, etc.) (L.V. 62; Śiv. 285; Rām. 154, 291, 1601, 1687, 1711; K. 67, 280, 519, 522, 719, 782, 828); pūzā pālüñᵘ̈, to carry out worship completely, to worship (K. 337, 1042); pazun pālun, see pazun 1; salām pālüñᵘ̈, to make a bow, salute reverently (H. xii, 16); pôlᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pöjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), protected, cherished, taken care of, as ab.
adj. melted, deliquesced, in paluṭᵘ gaʦhun m.inf. to become deliquesced; hence, to be unaccomplished, to be a failure. Cf. palaṭun.
m. a weight (used in scales) for weighing a pal of four tōlās or two ounces (cf. pal 2) (Gr.Gr. 147).
adj. (f. paliñᵘ̈), weighing a pal (as in the preceding); (of cloth or the like) so much as can be woven from a pal weight of thread.
n.ag. (f. pạlᵃzavüñᵃ), he who, or that which, is useful, serviceable, helpful.
conj. 2 or 3 (1 p.p. pạlᵒzᵒ, 2 p.p. pạlᵃzōv), i.q. palazun, q.v. (cf. atha pạlᵃzȧnᵃ, p. 61a, l. 50). pạlᵃzan-wôlᵃ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), useful, serviceable.
f. a fence, a wall, a hedge, railings (cf. khal-pᵒ, p. 397a, l. 2; kȧnḍⁱ-pⁱ, p. 455a, l. 28) (Gr.M.).

f. censure, denunciation, reproach, a rebuke; taunting; putting to shame (esp. on some public occasion), dishonouring (an honoured person, by reproaching him for former misdeeds) (Śiv. 1112; Rām. 683, 1038, 1062, 1154, 1778; YZ. 19, 371; K.Pr. 115, 119 (read pāma nai), 163, 250). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. censure to be attached (to, dat.), to be blamed, to be publicly censured (Rām. 339, 1060). ¶ pāma daga f.pl. disclosing former misdeeds (up to now hidden) by public reproaches, public taunting. --diñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to use public reproaches to another (in the course of abuse), to taunt publicly (W. 139, K.Pr. 107). --hĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to be a victim of public reproaches or censure, to be publicly taunted. --pām -- f. mutual reproaches, mutual taunting. --rōzañĕ-- f. pl. inf. censures to remain to a person, a person (dat.) to get a bad name or an evil reputation (H. x, 3). -waturᵘ m. a flood of abusive taunts (K.Pr. 259, pāmatur). ¶ pāman lagun m.inf. to become subject to public taunts.

for pam (see pampōsh) in the following:--pamba-hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), the stalk of wild rhubarb (which grows on the mountains surrounding Kashmīr) (El., L. 72). -lŏkhᵃr f. the nut-case of the lotus (El.); a kind of violent poisonous tumour or boil (in the middle of the back below the shoulders). -lŏkhᵃr pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. such a tumour or boil to attack a person. -sar m. a lake full of lotuses (and hence bearing a fine crop of lotus seeds); a certain marsh or lagoon lying to the south of the Wŏlur lake (the ancient Pampāsaras) (RT.Tr. vii, 940; II, 481-2). -ʦālan f. (sg. dat. -ʦālüñᵘ̈), wild rhubarb (which grows abundantly on the mountains of Kashmīr). The dried root is sold in the bāzārs, and when triturated and mixed with oil, is used as an application to wounds and ulcers. The stalk, which is eaten by Hindūs and Musalmāns, is pamba-hākh ab. (El.). It is used by dyers in the preparation of orange and gold dyes (L. 68, pamb tsallan).

m. (sg. dat. pambachas), the nut of the lotus. It is eaten as a delicacy by both Hindūs and Musalmāns (El., L. 72, Śiv. 1801). According to L. 76, it is the lotus plant itself (Nelumbium speciosum) which is used medicinally as a nervine tonic. ¶ pambach-dĕl m. the outer bark of the lotus nut. -gūjⁱ f. the kernel of the lotus nut. -hūnᵘ m. the nucleus-shoot of the kernel of the lotus nut (cf. hūnᵘ 2). -künḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kanjĕ), the hard shell of the lotus nut. -māl f. a garland made of lotus nuts.

m. the lotus (Nelumbium speciosum) (cf. lĕmbi-pᵒ, p. 524b, l. 21) (L. 72; W. 3; Śiv. 26, 44, 54, 57, 167, 180, 187, 189, etc.; Rām. 93, 186, 533, 548, 1095, 1494, 1632; K. 1, 59, 926-7, 1176; YZ. 96, 152; K.Pr. 138); a lotus-flower (Gr.M.). The lotus grows abundantly in the Kashmīr Valley. The seeds, stalks, and roots are eaten. It blooms in August and September. The nuts (pambuch) are regarded as a great delicacy. The stalks (nadorᵘ) ripen in October. The broad leaves are used as plates (El.). The word is really a compound of pam and pōsh. Pam also takes the form pamb, q.v. ¶ pampōshĕ-bạrᵃg m. the lotus leaf. -düjᵘ̈ f. a lake or lagoon full of lotuses in full bloom, -dal m. the lotus leaf. -ḍal m. a lake full of lotuses. -wöjᵘ̈ f. a ring made of the hollowed pericarp of a lotus; a gold ring of similar shape. -wạthᵃr m. (sg. dat. wạtᵃras), a lotus leaf.
(? spelling and gender), a certain wild plant which is used for food (L. 72). ? the same as pamba-ʦālan, p. 733b, l. 27.
m. one who habitually talks nonsense (disconnected or useless speech, or without any connected thread of thought), a babbler, a silly chatterbox.

m. (sg. abl. pana 1), N. of a certain offering, consisting of flowers, scents, fruit, roots, etc., followed by cakes smeared with clarified butter, made by Hindū married women to Ganēsh (Gaṇēśa) and other gods at the passing of the sign Leo, in the fourth and following lunar days of the bright half of the month of Bādᵃrapĕth (Bhādrapada) or August-September. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to make this offering. ¶ pana-sāth m. (sg. dat. -sātas), the auspicious moment for making this offering. -ʦŏ̈ṭᵘ̈ f. the buttered cake offered on this occasion.

m. (gen. pānukᵘ), the human body (Gr.Gr. 91; Gr.M.; W. 31; L.V. 44; K.Pr. 57; Śiv. 240, 285, 362, 1057, 1287; Rām. 240, 358, 636, 672, 946, etc.; K. 111, 167, 214, 272, 291, 298, 448, 506, etc.; H. iii, 4; vii, 24-5 (met.); YZ. 42, 170, 200, 234, 267; K.Pr. 15, 252); the body of an animal (K. 380); esp. one's own body, self (cf. pāna) (Śiv. 156, 205, 227, 330, 351, etc.; Rām. 181, 207, 664, 998, 1281, etc.; K. 60, 150, 246, 250, 278, 283, 292, 511, etc.; YZ. 18) (panunᵘ pān, see panunᵘ); met. a man's own personality (cf. panani pānücᵘ̈ khabar, consciousness of one's own existence, p. 391a, l. 20; nīʦa-pān, p. 674b, l. 22) (Gr.M.; L.V. 5, 7, 62, 71, 82, 85); bodily existence (cf. bāla-pᵒ, youth, the youthful state, youthfulness, p. 104b, l. 6, and Śiv. 660, 1106, 1444, 1834, 1843; Rām. 1469; K. 264; H. vii, 11, 15). --gālun -- m.inf. to cause one's body to melt, to serve a person (dat.) with heart and soul, to devote oneself to a person (Rām. 1281, 1458); to strive earnestly for any particular object (Rām. 1545). --mārun -- m.inf. to kill one's own body, to commit suicide (Rām. 165, 387, 404, 440, 646, etc.; YZ. 16, 48); cf. pāna-môrᵘ, p. 736a, l. 3. -parudᵘ m. one who has changed his mode of living, or gone for change of air (used of sheep and cattle) (L. 459, pánporad). --razi khārun -- m.inf. to mount oneself on a rope, to hang oneself, to commit suicide by hanging (Rām. 1019, 1487, 1536, 1706). ¶ pānukᵘ sg. gen. (pānücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, one's own body. ¶ pānas 1, sg. dat., used as adv. in such phrases as nanga pānas, with a naked body (K. 273).

m. (sg. abl. pana 2), a very small portion of anything, a particle, scrap, shred. ¶ pana pana gaʦhun m.inf. to become cut up into scraps (e.g. of a cloth cut up into shreds). --pana karun -- m.inf. to cut up into tiny pieces, to shred (cloth, paper, etc.). ¶ panan gaʦhun m.inf. to go into scraps, i.e. (of some circumstance, news, story) to master every individual item. --wātun -- m.inf. to ascertain every item or particular (e.g. of some task about to be undertaken).

m. the betel leaf, Piper betel (K. 977). pāna-bīr m. a preparation of areca nut and spices rolled up in a betel leaf for chewing, a betel roll or quid. It is commonly presented by one person to another as a token of civility. It is also given in confirmation of a pledge or the like or as a challenge taken up by him who accepts it (K. 977, 982).

m. (sg. abl. pana 3), a thread, thread, sewing thread (cf. ômᵘ pᵒ, p. 27a, l. 28; öṭⁱ-pⁱ, p. 68a, l. 48; ḍē̃jĕ tȧlⁱ pᵒ, p. 202b, l. 2; ganḍa-pᵒ, p. 289b, l. 9; krāla-pᵒ, p. 470b, l. 21; lözᵘ̈-pᵘ̈, p. 508b, l. 26; lĕṭha-pᵒ, p. 537b, l. 27; māli-pᵒ, p. 565a, l. 50; pham-pᵒ, p. 698a, l. 24; pöṭⁱ-pana-dāv, s.v. pôṭᵘ) (L.V. 106; Śiv. 474, 1014, 1217; K.Pr. 11, 87, 162). ¶ pana-ḍī˜jᵘ̈ f. a small-sized ball of thread (cf. -ḍyū̃gᵘ, bel.). -dāv f. so much thread as is put into a needle at one time, a needleful of thread (cf. pöṭⁱ-pana-dāv s.v. pôṭᵘ) (K.Pr. 208). -ḍyū̃gᵘ m. a large-sized ball of thread; cf. -ḍī˜jᵘ̈, ab. -ganḍ m. a skein or hank of thread. -kônᵘ m. the ball of thread as it is wound on the spinning-wheel. -kāñᵉ̆r f. id., but of small size. -kŏth f. (sg. dat. -kö̆ʦhᵘ̈), a skein or hank of thread. -lar f. a thread to be twisted with another thread in order to strengthen the latter, a strand (of a cord). -milᵃr or -milürᵘ̈ f. a bundle or skein of thread. -pĕcukh m. (sg. dat. pĕcakas), a reel of thread.
m. drinking, drink (cf. mada-pān, p. 548b, l. 1). -dach f. a kind of grape. According to El., s.v. dach, it is the same as ḍūnᵘ-dach, see p. 223b, l. 47.

m. (sg. abl. pana 4), a leaf (esp. of a tree) (cf. datᵃ̇rᵃ̇-pᵃ̇, p. 259a, l. 21; kā̃bayĕ-pᵒ, p. 382b, l. 47; nāgar-pᵒ, p. 625a, l. 12; pȧhⁱ-pⁱ, p. 684a, l. 11; pŏhⁱ (or pōhⁱ)-pⁱ, p. 684a, l. 49; phrasta-pᵒ, p. 709a, l. 15) (Gr.M.; L.V. 83; Śiv. 505, 1039, 1208, 1651; Rām. 189, 206, 1634; K.Pr. 82, 162, 175); green vegetables (used as food) (cf. an-pan, p. 29b, l. 32) (K.Pr. 205, pani, as if from ponᵘ). ¶ pana-barg m. a single tree-leaf (Śiv. 994). -bata m. rice boiled till it is soft and easily digestible. -chöñᵘ̈ f. 'leaf-sifting', leanness (from disease, sorrow, etc.), gauntness (quasi, the condition of withered leaves blown from trees). pana-chạthᵃr m. (sg. dat. -chạtᵃras), a leaf parasol, an umbrella made of leaves. -ḍēr m. a pile of withered leaves. -köñᵘ̈ f. a small bundle of leaves. -lünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -lanjĕ), a leafy bough. -lang m. a leafy trunk or main bough of a tree. -morᵘ m. a leaf cottage. -mȧrⁱ hĕnⁱ m. pl. inf. to take leaf huts; hence (owing to sorrow, worry, or religious reasons) to take to a secret, solitary abode. -pö̃pur m. (sg. dat. pö̃paras), a species of moth, whose favourite resting-place is the leaf of some tree, where it gives forth a prolonged and very shrill noise (El., Śiv. 1685). -tulᵘ m. a collection of leaves. -ʦᵃñĕ f.pl. leaf-charcoal, the charcoal of burnt leaves. -wạthᵃr m. (sg. dat. wạtᵃras), the leaf of a tree; a leaf (L. 461, panwatr). -zanḍ m. a few leaves, a small bundle of leaves.

refl. pron. (for the gen. of this word, panunᵘ, q.v. s.v. is used. The ag. or instr. sg. is pāna, Gr.Gr. 91), self, oneself (cf. pānas ʦhĕpa dāwañĕ, p. 263a, l. 47; had pānas karun, p. 322a, l. 23) (Gr.Gr. 91, 152; Gr.M.; Śiv. 26, 69, 278, 1151, 1189, etc.; Rām. 75, 81, 83, 223-8, etc.; K. 89, 124, 203-5, etc.; H. vii, 15; x, 1, 6; YZ. 196, 220; K.Pr. 164). ¶ Like the corresponding Hindōstānī pronoun, āp, this word can refer to any person in either number (Gr.Gr. 91). Thus: I myself (L.V. 31, 44, 60, 61; Rām, 877, 1033, 1307, etc.; K. 849; H. vii, 15; K.Pr. 4); we ourselves (K. 861); thou thyself (L.V. 44, 66; Rām. 22, 235, 647, 1124, etc.; K. 69, 385, 560, 1063; H. xii, 11, 25); you yourselves; he himself (L.V. 33, 59; Rām. 304, 316, etc.; K. 39, 46, 49, 50, 196, 283, etc.; H. i, 1; ii, 5; vi, 4, etc.); she herself (Rām. 1015, 1030, 1034, 1077, etc.; K. 66, 928-9; H. v, 9-11; vii, 1; xii, 7); they themselves (K. 292; H. iii, 8; viii, 3, 8; x, 12). ¶ pāna-gȧrⁱ f. a woman who is her own mistress, i.e. who herself is mistress of the house. -khŏdⁱ 1 adj. c.g. self-dependent, independent, acting on one's own authority. -khŏdⁱ 2 adv. independently, on one's own authority. -môrᵘ m. killing oneself, suicide; cf. pān mārun, p. 735a, l. 50. -môrᵘ ʦhunun m.inf. to engage oneself in committing suicide, to make arrangements for suicide. -röchⁱ 1 f. self-protection. -röchⁱ 2 adj. c.g. one who protects himself (or herself, or his or her property). -warzukh adj. (f. -warzücᵘ̈), selfish, self-interested, self-seeking. -yĕʦhukh adj. (f. -yĕʦhücᵘ̈), self-interested, self-seeking, self-centred, egotistical, selfish. ¶ pönⁱ-pān (K. 164) or pönⁱ-pāna refl. pron. one's own self, one's very self (as in mahnivⁱ pönⁱ-pānas gūlⁱ löyᵘ̈, the man shot himself, Gr.M.) (L.V. 60; Śiv. 983, 1843; Rām. 714, 1429, 1668; K. 955; YZ. 162, 219-20). --pānas -- dat. used as adv. amongst (them-, etc.) selves, each other, mutually (K. 204, 286, 312; YZ. 121). -pānay adv. of himself (herself, itself), voluntarily, spontaneously, of one's own accord (K. 742); refl. pron. myself, thyself, himself, etc. (Rām. 583, 1194). ¶ pānas 2 adv. for oneself, to oneself (K. 155, 372, 374, 400, 406, 544, 580, etc.); hence, without opposition, unconstrainedly, of one's own free will, spontaneously (K. 75, 77, 1155; H. vi, 4; vii, 2); in adverbial phrases, such as zinda-pānas (I shall leave thee alone) alive (K. 560). --aʦun -- m.inf. to go into one's own house, to enter one's home (K. 748). --bĕhun -- m.inf. to sit in one's own house, to stay at home (K. 632); to sit down free from duty, to rest after finishing one's work (H. viii, 8). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go without opposition, to go (home) safely, or without apprehension (K. 20, 118, 142, 311, 612, 632, 665, etc.; H. iii, 8; v, 9; viii, 3; K.Pr. 161, 163). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take with oneself, to take home, to carry off to one's own home (Rām. 1143i). --nērun -- m.inf. to go forth on one's own business, to go away (without impediment), to set out on one's way home (K. 729, 934, 939; H. xii, 6). --nyunᵘ -- m.inf. to bring home, take home (K. 894). --phērun -- m.inf. to return home (K. 837). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain safely at home (K. 363, 376). --ʦalun -- m.inf. to run away home (K. 559). --wātun -- m.inf. to arrive home safely (K. 256). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come without opposition, to go, or come (home) safely, or without apprehension (K. 76, 391, 495, 667, 706, 1113, 1155); to set out home (H. xii, 12). --yĕʦhawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --yĕʦhavüñᵘ̈ --), one who wishes for himself, selfish. ¶ pānasᵘ̈y adv. i.q. pānas, but emphatic (K. 883; H. vii, 3); of oneself, spontaneously (K. 78). ¶ pānay (refl. pron.) he himself (etc. in all three persons and both numbers) (Gr.Gr. 169; L.V. 33, 59; Rām. 34, 151, 168, 462, 561, etc.; K. 16, 37, 264, 338, 362, 730, etc.; H. vii, 1; x, 12; YZ. 167, 220; K.Pr. 157, 182); (adv.) of himself, of herself, of itself, etc., spontaneously (El. pánai; Śiv. 67, 159, 162, 284, 495, 554, 631, 651, etc.; Rām. 146, 299, 541, etc.; K. 69, 70, 269, 328, 577, 580, etc.). --pāna -- adv. of one's own accord, spontaneously (K. 742). ¶ pānyō pānyō m. (of a number of persons engaged in common business) the working of each person selfishly for his own interests. --pānyō lagun -- m.inf. (of a number of persons) each to pursue his own interests.
a jingle of dana in dana-pana, p. 221b, l. 49; cf. also dȧnⁱ-pȧnⁱ, p. 222a, l. 32. The word is probably connected with pan 2, q.v.
m. width, breadth (of cloth, etc.) (El. panah, Gr.M.). -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), (of cloth or the like) specially broad, fine and broad.

m. protection, defence, shelter, shade, asylum, refuge. --mangun -- m.inf. to seek protection (from), to beg for an asylum; to pray for deliverance (from); to avoid, eschew; to implore mercy; to surrender at discretion.
adj. c.g. (of a cloth, surface of land, or the like) specially wide, fine and wide, very wide (Rām. 741, K.Pr. 204).
m. (sg. dat. pānakas), a kind of drink (made up of honey, sugar, cloves, nutmeg, pepper, cardamom, musk, saffron, sandal, etc.) used in religious worship (Śiv. 231).
m. the feeling of self, i.e. the looking upon another as equivalent to oneself (as in friendship or the like), loving sympathy (Gr.Gr. 141, K. 1080).

f. the deceiving a milch-cow (by letting its calf suck her for an instant so as to start the milk flowing, and then removing the calf unknown to her and going on milking her by hand); met. cheating a human being by means of this character.

(K. 252), pānawöñᵘ̈, or (Rām. 429, m.c.) pānawöñī adv. mutually, reciprocally (El. pánawuiṅ; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1244; Rām. 81, 94, 429, 453, 1092, 1635; K. 103, 297, 477, 567, 808, 810, 1019, 1078, 1081; H. viii, 1, 2; xi, 19; xii, 25 (pānawöñ); x, 1 (pānavüñ); YZ. 254).
card., i.q. pānʦ, q.v., of which it is the Skt. form, used only in a few borrowed Skt. expressions, such as panca-yindⁱ, the five indriyas, or organs of sense (L.V. 79). Cf. panʦa.
m. (sg.dat. pancāyĕtas), a body of arbitrators, council, or jury, consisting of five or more members, i.q. panch, q.v. (Gr.M.).
m. (sg. dat. pancas), a body of arbitrators, council, or jury, consisting of five or more members, i.q. pancāyĕth, q.v.; cf. pö̃ch. --karun -- m.inf. to assemble the members of such a body.
(? spelling) f. the N. of a certain medicinal plant, Geranium sp., said to be good for wounds caused by a burn (L. 76, panchpatri. We should expect the word to be spelt pönʦa-patᵃr or -patᵘ̈rᵘ̈).
m. a minister or priest who officiates at a Hindū sacred place, and lives upon the offerings of pilgrims.

m. a pillar or columnar support. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to elevate (some sunk-down house or the like) on struts or supports; met. to support or console some afflicted or depressed person. --karun -- m.inf. to lift up a heavy load on to the back.
