(f. --paharücᵘ̈ --), of, or belonging to, the last watch of the night. --paharan -- adv. at the time of the last watch of the night, at, in, or during the last watch of the night (Gr.Gr. 157). --paharan bögⁱ (or bögin) --  adv. at about the last watch of the night. --paharas -- adv. at, in, or during the last watch of the night (K. 969). --paharas bögⁱ (or bögin) --  adv. at or in about the last watch of the night. ¶ patimⁱ dŏh yinⁱ m. pl. inf. the last days to come, the time of a person's death to approach (Śiv. 594, Rām. 1326). --pörⁱ -- adv. in behind, from behind (Gr.Gr. 160). -sondᵘ  adj. (f. -sünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, what is behind (whether animate or inanimate); of, or belonging to, what is subsequent (as ab.). ¶ pȧtⁱmĕn-hondⁱ  adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, those things that are behind (whether animate or inanimate); of, or belonging to, what is subsequent (as ab.). ¶ pȧtⁱmyukⁱ adj. (f. pȧtⁱmicⁱ), of, or belonging to, what is behind (esp. when inanimate); of, or belonging to, what is subsequent (as ab.).
adj. (pāṭivᵘ̈), made of silk, silken. Cf. pôṭᵘ.
m. a leaf, i.q. pạthᵃr 1, q.v. (Śiv. 1430, 1541).

also written pạtᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. pạtri), a leaf (of a plant) (not a large one) (cf. gŏgᵃji-pᵃ, p. 279a, l. 23; muji-pᵒ, p. 558b, l. 5) (Gr.Gr. 74); a leaf of a book; a leaf of paper (cf. jaman-pᵒ, p. 374a, l. 36); esp. the leaf of the cinnamon shrub (El. patra m., but properly f.pl.) (Cinnamomum albiflorum). This is said to be eaten by musk-deer, and to be the cause of the production of musk. It is used in Hindū religious worship. Cf. pạthᵃr 1, of which it is the fem. in a diminutive sense. Note that, while pạthᵃr becomes wạthᵃr, when the second member of a compound word, pạtᵃr, in such a position, remains unchanged. ¶ pạtri-kāṭh m. the wood of the cinnamon tree. -zanḍ m. the cinnamon shrub.
f. a leaf or straw mat (cf. khᵃra-pᵃ, p. 406b, l. 45; rĕka-pᵒ, s.v. rĕkh) (Gr.Gr. 35, 146; K.Pr. 49, 215); any flat support (cf. nöhⁱ-pⁱ, p. 625b, l. 16). This word is f. of patulᵘ, q.v.
f. a plank over a water- channel (used like a bridge); a hanging shelf.

m. a kind of copper or bell- metal pot or pan with a wide mouth (the patīla of India), used for cooking. According to El. (s.vv. paitila and patila) it is a Musalmān vessel corresponding to the Hindū bahugun, q.v. It is used as a teapot.
adj. c.g. one who habitually wears hair braided in a bow-shape on each side of the forehead (see paṭiñ). This method of wearing the hair is principally adopted by dancers and prostitutes.
m. (sg. dat. paurānikas), a person well versed in ancient histories, a reciter of such, a bard-historian.
adj. c.g. relating to a man, human; manly, virile. paurushĕ-sūkᵃth m. N. of a celebrated hymn in the Ṛg Vēda (X, 90), called in Skt. puruṣa-sûkta (K. 15).

m. the navigable channel (marked or buoyed in a shallow lake or wide river) [cf. hāra-pav, a buoyed channel (required) in (the rainy month of) Hār (when ordinarily the lakes are full to overflowing and hence no marked channel is needed; hence, scarcity of water in that month, p. 344a, l. 8); potᵘ-pav, p. 787b, l. 7; sọ̆dra-pᵒ, s.v. sọ̆dᵃr]; met. the practised or customary way of doing anything; practice, exercise, study, the making frequent use of anything, the acquirement of dexterity in using anything (cf. ös-pav, p. 46b, l. 16; atha-pᵒ, p. 61b, l. 40; khŏshⁱ-pⁱ, p. 418b, l. 38; khōwᵃ̇rᵃ̇-pᵃ̇, p. 425b, l. 12; rōt-pᵒ, s.v. rāth 1; röʦᵘ̈-pᵘ̈, s.v. rāth 2 the frequent repetition of a thing, in order to fix it on the memory (cf. kana-pav, p. 448a, l. 29). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. the navigable channel to fall before one, i.e. to be found out and available; met. in some complicated or difficult operation, to succeed in one's intention. ¶ pawa ḍalun m.inf. to be displaced from the navigable channel, to be compelled to leave the recognized channel (on account of some obstruction or the like, and to go by some other route); (in any action or occupation) to depart from one's familiar practice. -nēr f. (of a boat) going along the (recognized) navigable channel. -nörᵘ̈ f. a small narrow marked or buoyed navigable channel (as ab.). --nērun -- m.inf. to follow through and come out of such a recognized navigable channel; (in any action or occupation) to achieve the result by following familiar practice. --pakun -- m.inf. to go along the established navigable channel; (in any action or occupation) to follow familiar and easy practice. -pǖ̃ʦᵃhpyonᵃ m.inf. the expected and intended (esp. when published beforehand) result to be achieved in any work. ¶ pawukᵘ gen. adj. (f. pavücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a navigable channel, as ab.; (of any action or occupation) well practised, well learned; successfully carried out according to one's intention.
m. a foot, a leg, in khara-pāv karān, doing the legs of a centipede, i.e. in great haste (p. 407b, l. 8, q.v.).
m. a causing to fall, a felling, in āv-pāv, sudden death (p. 70b, l. 28).

f. a quarter, the fourth part of anything (El. páo; W. 105, pau); a certain weight, a quarter of a sēr, i.e. about twenty tōlās or half a pound (a sēr being about two pounds) (Śiv. 1828; K.Pr. 28, 201, 224); a span, twelve finger-breadths, the length between the point of the extended thumb and the point of the extended little finger (cf. atha-pāv, p. 61b, l. 4); something (e.g. a piece of cloth or a piece of land) measuring a span; a kind of wooden peg used for fastening the wooden beams distributed through a brick wall in order to strengthen it. pāv-nafrē پاو نفری, a quarter unit of cultivators in Kāshmīrī revenue terminology, i.e. a bachelor entitled to one and a half acres of irrigated land (L. 402, pao nafre). See naphar. ¶ pāwa-ganḍ m. to fasten the pegs in the wooden beams, as ab. --pāv karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to fix peg upon peg, to fix a number of pegs, as ab.
or pavithurᵘ m. a ring of the sacred grass called darbha (Poa cynosuroides) worn on the third, or ring-, finger by Hindūs at certain religious ceremonies.
adj. c.g. pure, hallowed, holy (Gr.M. paritr).
or pāvürᵘ̈ f. surrounding on all sides, crowding (a person) in all directions (e.g. by a number of persons or, met., by calamities, etc.) (cf. āwürᵘ̈-pᵘ̈, p. 71b, l. 19); the being surrounded, as ab.

m. wind, moving air (Śiv. 983, 1825, 1869); the vital air, breath (L.V. 17, 25, 33, 37, 42; Śiv. 983, 1469, 1827, 1870; Rām. 9, 1659). --sandyā -- f. N. of a sacred bathing place in Kashmīr, sacred to the goddess Samdhyā (Śiv. 1496).
m. purifying, purificatory, purifying from sin.

conj. 1 to cause to be felled (by a third party), to cause to be dropped (e.g. into a river or the like); to cause a loss (by a third party) in a business or the like (K.Pr. 87); to cause another to fall into prison or the like. yād pᵒ, to cause memory to fall, to cause a person to remember, to call to another's memory (Śiv. 73, 1884).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pôwᵘ), to cause to fall, to fell, to lay low, knock down (Gr.Gr. 23, 172; Śiv. 353, 1715; Rām. 340, 376, 707, 709, 1552; K. 693, 830; H. iii, 9; K.Pr. 201, 263); to cause to lie down, to cause to repose; to put down (on to or into anything) (cf. atha pᵒ, p. 61b, l. 43) (Śiv. 1711, 1875); to cause to fall, to bring into existence, to cause to come into existence (cf. bājᵃr pāvᵘ̈ñᵘ̈, p. 98a, l. 24; mal pāwun, p. 564a, l. 16 (Śiv. 28, 1758; K. 552-3); pushĕ pᵒ, p. 780a, l. 28; shĕkh pᵒ, s.v. shĕkh 2); to let drop, let fall; yād pāwun, to cause memory to fall, to call to (a person's) memory (Śiv. 1002, 1822, 1909; Rām. 1630; H. vi, 11); pathar pᵒ, to knock down to the ground, to fell (cf. p. 798b, l. 27) (Śiv. 1626) This verb is the causal form of pyonᵘ, q.v. ¶ pôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), felled, knocked down. ¶ pövith thawun m.inf. to knock down and leave there, to bring low; to drop and abandon.
m. a small house, a (poor man's) cottage (cf. lari-pᵒ, p. 531b, l. 11); an abode (K.Pr. 54, 111). pāwᵃ̇rᵃ̇-han f. a small cottage, a tiny cot.
m. a sandal, a slipper (cf. jūgⁱ-pⁱ, p. 371b, l. 22).

m. water or any drinkable liquid, esp. milk (L.V. 54); (in Kāshmīrī) reviving (a dried up plant) by watering it (Śiv. 1863). --aʦun -- m.inf. (of a withered plant) revival by watering to enter, to be revived by watering; (of a person weakened by illness) to convalesce (owing to the application of appropriate remedies). --phērun 1 -- m.inf. convalescence or revival to return, strength to come back (of a withered plant, a person weakened by illness, or the like). --phirawun 1 -- m.inf. to revive (a withered plant by means of watering, a person weakened by illness by means of proper medical treatment, and so on). --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause revival to enter, to revive (a withered plant) by watering it; to give strength (to a person weakened by illness) by means of appropriate treatment.

m. a means, expedient, device, resource, plan, contrivance (for doing something successfully) (cf. bacan-pᵒ, p. 80b, l. 44; pakan pᵒ, p. 728b, l. 4; pōshĕn-pᵒ, p. 781b, l. 34) (Rām. 934, 1045, 1232, 1477, 1580, 1674; K. 87, 361, 570, 651, 756, 775, 802, 882, 895, 980; H. ix, 11). --karun -- m.inf. to make a device (for something), to contrive an expedient, to take measures (Śiv. 519, 1137). ¶ pāyĕ-boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), possessing great resources, of great dignity, high and mighty (YZ. 25, 240, 543); cf. baḍi pāyĕ, p. 84b, l. 39. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without expedient, without resource; (of some action or occupation) that for which the necessary means are wanting; (of a disease or the like) that for which no remedy is available. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), possessing many expedients, having many resources, helpers, or the like; (of a disease or the like) that for which many remedies are available.

m. a foot, a foot-print (YZ. 40, 232, 407); a trace, mark, vestige, clue (cf. raga-pay, s.v. rag; rata-pᵒ, s.v. rath) (Śiv. 1601, 1700-1, 1729, 1863, 1885; Rām. 521; H. iii, 3); a sign, gesture, hint, intimation (as to the whereabouts of something) (cf. nāma-pᵒ, p. 636b, l. 19; a person's address, the place where he lives (Gr.M., Rām. 1487)). Cf. pata 1. --anun -- m.inf. to bring a clue, search out a clue (to), get to the bottom (of a mystery or secret). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to follow up a clue, to search out the entire truth (about something) (Śiv. 439). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to pull out a clue, to find out all the facts after much trouble (cf. raga-pay kaḍun, s.v. rag). --phērun 2 -- m.inf. a clue to be discovered, information to come (about something hidden). --phirawun 2 -- m.inf. to give a person a clue, to give information about (some mystery or something hidden). --thawun -- m.inf. to watch, or attentively consider, a clue. ¶ payā-pay adv. successively, one close upon another, close together (i.q. payham, q.v., s.v.). ¶ payĕs wātun m.inf. to arrive at the clue, to gain thorough knowledge (of something secret) (Śiv. 821, 937; Rām. 1478, causal). --wötith -- conj. part. used as adj. c.g. one who has become thoroughly acquainted with (another's secret). --wātawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --wātavüñᵘ̈ --), id.

m. strength, durability, (of a human being) healthy longevity (Śiv. 196). pāyĕs pyonᵘ m.inf. to come to one's senses (i.e. to abandon unprofitable or unworthy conduct and take to respectable life) (Śiv. 94, 315, 1298, 1722, 1751; K. 32, 328, 365, 559).

f. a fence, hedge, hedgerow (cf. kȧnḍⁱ-pⁱ, p. 455a, l. 32, which, however, is reported as masc.) (K.Pr. 156). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to put a fence (round a garden or field), to fence in. ¶ payĕ-kāṭh m. the wood, small branches, or twigs, etc., used to form a fence. -mūrᵘ̈ f. one of the twigs filling up the spaces between the main posts of a fence. -zanḍ m. all the wood, twigs, etc., requisite for making a fence as collected together ready for use.
m. a foot (K. 988). -āb پای آب m. foot-water, i.e. (in rice cultivation) the lower villages, as compared with sir-āb or the upper villages (L. 435, paiáb).
m. strong, durable, healthy and long-lived. See pāy 2.
f. a woman of the class of outcaste Brāhmaṇs called Pāyuch (q.v.); a woman who supports herself by acting as one.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. payĕnôwᵘ), to bake (bricks or the like); to heat (a metal in a forge or the like). payĕnôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. payĕnövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), baked, as ab.; (of a metal) heated, as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. payonᵘ), to scorch, torrify (cf. buthᵘ pᵒ, p. 142a, l. 11); to refine (a metal) by smelting; (met.) (of some respected person) to become overwhelmed with shame (at some impudent request or the like); cf. payun. payonᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. payë̆ñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of a precious metal) refined, smelted.
m. a message; news, intelligence (Rām. 832, 859); a mission, embassy.
adv. successively, one close upon another, close together. Cf. payā-pay, p. 812a, l. 26.
or pāyirᵘ̈ 1 f. a stirrup (L.V. 14, payirᵘ̈). ¶ pāyiri-horᵘ m. a pair of stirrups. -khôr m. a single stirrup.
or pāyirᵘ̈ 2 f. a troop, body, or band of pilgrims, foot-travellers, or the like. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a body to assemble.

or pāyyuchᵘ m. (f. pāyĕch-bāy is his wife, see bel., while pāyĕchĕñ, q.v., is either a woman belonging to this class of outcaste Brāhmaṇs, or else a woman who supports herself by acting as one), a man (esp. a Brāhmaṇ) who supports himself by accepting funeral offerings and similar gifts, and who is in consequence outcasted. In India he is called a Mahābrāhmaṇa (a sarcastic title). --dyunᵘ -- m. to make gifts to one of these men on the occasion of an obsequial ceremony (such as that held on the eleventh day after death). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. (such a man) to eat the obsequial food on such an occasion. ¶ pāyĕch-bāy f. the wife of such an outcaste Brāhmaṇ. -koṭᵘ m. the son of such a Brāhmaṇ. -küṭᵘ̈ f. his daughter. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), the son of such a Brāhmaṇ (when contempt is indicated). ¶ pāyĕchⁱ-pônⁱ m. the conduct or occupation of such an outcaste Brāhmaṇ; similar vile conduct performed by any other person. -tônᵘ m. the occupation or livelihood of such a Brāhmaṇ; the conduct of such.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. poyᵘ), to heat (a metal) red hot, to purify, refine, melt, or smelt (a precious metal) by heat, to scorch, torrify (cf. atha pᵒ, p. 62a, l. 1; buthᵘ pᵒ, p. 142a, l. 8); to bake (earth), to make bricks, pottery, or the like. Cf. payĕnun. ¶ poyᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. püyᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), roasted, smelted, baked, etc., as ab. ¶ payĕn-kō̃da f. a kiln (a potter's, a lime-kiln, and brick-kiln, or the like); a furnace (for smelting). -thöjⁱ or -thöjᵘ̈  f. a crucible, a melting-pot. -ʦᵃñĕ f.pl. a special kind of charcoal (made from deodar and similar wood) used in smelting furnaces. -wôlᵘ m. a metal-smelter; a brick-baker. -wān m. a smelting furnace. ¶ payith pākavith conj. part. having got someone completely to accomplish (something), having got a thing accomplished. --sŏn -- m. gold which has been refined in a furnace; met. a person who has been cleansed ceremonially, undefiled.
m. truthfulness, honesty, probity, truth (El. also pazir) (Gr.Gr. 141, Gr.M., Śiv. 1754); sĕzara-pazara-kinⁱ, with straightness and truth, honestly (cf. sĕzar-pazar, s.v. sĕzar) (Gr.M.).
f. (sg. dat. pāzüʦᵘ̈), extracting, draining out, drawing out (e.g. water from a well), emptying; met. gradual total expenditure of amassed wealth. Cf. pāzun.
f. an ornament worn on the feet or ankles (consisting of a chain with small bells attached).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pôzᵘ), to extract, bring out (from), draw out (e.g. the contents of a vessel or water from a well), empty out (K.Pr. 35). pôzᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pözᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), that from which the contents have been entirely drawn out or extracted, emptied out.
m. (sg. dat. pazanas), the carrying out of hereditary family religious customs, family worship. --pālun -- m.inf. to maintain and carry out such customs.

conj. 2 (reported as conj. 2, but Iśvara-kaula treats the verb as conj. 3), (1 p.p. pozᵘ; 2 p.p. pazyōv, Gr.Gr. 226) to turn out to be true (e.g. an unfounded fear to turn out to be justified) (Gr.M.); pazunukᵘ wākh, the word of truthfulness, a word of honour (Rām. 291); to be proper, be fit, be suitable (cf. lazun pazun, p. 545b, l. 28) (Śiv. 593, 971, 1752; Rām. 1182, 1639; K. 476, 484, 524, 536, 590, 651, 726, 924, 971, 1043, 1046, 1071, 1150, 1162; H. vi, 8; YZ. 304, K.Pr. 125). In the latter sense used in the future or conditional past with the fut. pass. part. of another verb to indicate propriety. In this case, when in the fut. it has the force of the pres., as in pazĕ-m karun, it is proper to be done for me, i.e. it should be done for me. So, in the cond. past, ʦĕ pazihē suh mārunᵘ, he would have been proper to be beaten by thee, i.e. thou shouldst have beaten him (Gr.Gr. 113-4; Gr.M.; Śiv. 535, 744, 840, 870, 1252; Rām. 12, 808, 813, 843, 1238, 1435, 1439, 1575; K. 360, 365); or it may be used with the dative of the infinitive, as in nāsh pazi-y bananas, destruction is proper to become to thee (Śiv. 91; K. (pazi) 34, 37, 67, 81, 89, 133, etc.; YZ. 554). pozᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. püzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), that which has turned out to be true; fitted, become suitable. ¶ pazunᵘ m. that which is proper, (a person's or thing's) proper duty or natural action; panunᵘ pazunᵘ pôlun, (the fire) did what was to be expected of it, it did its proper duty (Rām. 1601).
m. (sg. dat. pazatas), truthfulness, honesty, rectitude of conduct. Cf. pozᵘ 1.
f. (sg. dat. pạzᵃrüñᵃ), the showing or proving to be true, showing the true facts.
conj. 1 (pạzᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. pạzᵃrun, q.v. pạzᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (pạzᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. pạzᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, s.v. pạzᵃrun.

conj. 1 (pạzᵒrᵒ), to show or prove to be true, to show the entire truth of a matter, to prove by showing the truth, to decide the truth (Gr.Gr. 7). pạzᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (pạzᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), proved by truthful means.
f. truthfulness, sincerity (Gr.Gr. 142); true, sincere, and trusting mutual friendship.
adj. (f. pȧzⁱyörⁱ, or, as subst., pȧzⁱyārĕñ), (of a person) truthful, honest, veracious, sincere, true (Gr.Gr. 135, 142, Gr.M.); upright (of a judge, etc.) (Gr.M.).
m. (sg. dat. pāʦakas), (of food) easily digested, digestible; (of medicine) a digestive.
f. (sg. dat. paʦüʦᵘ̈), trust, confidence, belief (in a person, etc.).
f. incompleteness, insufficiency, falling short of the desired result, or of the necessary quantity (for securing any result). Cf. pāʦun.

f. (sg. dat. paʦhi (see also pọ̆ʦhᵘ 1 and 2) although the corresponding verb is paʦun, q.v.; cf. poʦᵘ), trust, confidence, faith, reliance, assurance, belief (cf. atha-pᵒ, p. 61b, l. 38; bōla-pᵒ, p. 105a, l. 21; banda-pᵒ, p. 111a, l. 38; māla-pᵒ, p. 565a, l. 23; mana-pᵒ, p. 572a, l. 37) (Gr.Gr. 126; Gr.M.; Śiv. 309, 841, 1312; K. 10); commercial credit (L. 459); respect, credit (K.Pr. 13). --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause belief, convince (Śiv. 795, 1226, 1307; Rām. 1599). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to rely (on), trust (in), confide (in), believe, depend (on). --niñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to trust (El.). --thavüñᵘ̈ -- or --thāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (rightly or wrongly) to believe in, have faith in the existence of (something not evident), to be assured, certain (Gr.M.); to rely (upon), have trust (in) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1873). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. trust to come (to a person, dat.), as in kas yiyihē paʦh, who would believe? (K. 175, K.Pr. 85). -yĕʦh f. trust and affection, i.e. complete trust (in), excessive trust in (cf. Śiv. 1071, yiʦhi paʦhi sān; so K. 10, yĕʦhi-paʦhi- sostᵘ, full of affection and trust; K. 1002, 1036, 1044). -yĕʦh anüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to cause complete trust (in). --yiwawunᵘ -- adv. in such a manner as to cause trust, persuasively. ¶ paʦha-dar m. (f. -dariñ), one who is the object of trust, trustworthy, to be depended upon, honourable, honest. ¶ paʦhi-dar m. (f. -dariñ), one who is the object of trust, trustworthy, to be depended upon, honourable, honest; trustful, confiding, suspicionless. paʦhi-wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), trustful, confiding.

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. paʦhidārĕñ), that in which one may have confidence, i.e. that which ultimately fulfils expectations (e.g. a cow bought when it is not in milk, but which in due course gives plentiful milk, or a piece of land in which seed is sown, and which ultimately bears a fine crop).
f. hospitable reception (of a guest), hospitality.
f. hospitable reception (of a guest), hospitality, entertainment (Gr.M.). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to entertain, to show hospitality (Gr.M.). pȧʦhⁱlāzi adv. hospitably.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. poʦᵘ; 2 p.p. paʦōv; in K. 34 pol. impve. written paʦh-ta), to trust, believe in, give credit to (e.g. trusting with a loan of money, or trusting a person by giving him authority, or by confiding to him a secret formula, or the like (Gr.Gr. 204; L.V. 27, 104); to believe in the existence of (anything, dat.), to believe that (anything, dat.) will come into existence, or happen (K. 34); to trust (a person), i.e. to trust that he will do no harm if allowed to live, to let a person live without danger to oneself (K. 559). --prārun -- m.inf. to await the payment of a loan, to show patience or forbearance in such waiting; to wait patiently for the completion of some work; (in asking for a loan) to wait confidently for its being granted. ¶ poʦᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. püʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), one who is trusted, as ab. ¶ paʦan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who trusts, as ab.; (when work to be done by another is delayed) one who is patient or forbearing in awaiting its accomplishment.
in pāʦun pyonᵘ m.inf. loss to be caused by insufficiency of materials (for any work). Cf. pāʦay.
in pĕ-koṭᵘ m. a kind of tiny silvery fish; a tiny little boy-child. -küṭᵘ̈ f. a kind of tiny silvery fish; a tiny little girl-child.
adj. c.g. turning, twisting, winding; twisted, coiled. Cf. ạshᵉ̆ka-pᵉ̆, p. 48b, l. 40.
f. the wife of a paternal uncle, (pẹ̆thᵃr or pẹ̆tᵃr, q.v.) an aunt by marriage (El. pihchain).

m. (sg. dat. pēcas), turn, winding; a twist, coil, plait, fold (YZ. 10); entanglement, complication, maze, perplexity; a screw (Gr.M.); a machine; (met.) bellyache, colic, gripes. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to wind round, to twist; to screw; to circumvent, to deceive, hinder. --yunᵘ m.inf. circumventing to occur, to be hindered; an attack of colic to come on.
adj. c.g. twisted, convoluted, coiled, spiral; winding, sinuous; intricate, complicated, involved; crooked, tortuous; artful, tricky, wily, crafty, deceitful.
m. (sg. dat. pĕcakas), a reel of thread (cf. pana-pᵒ, s.v. pan 3); the bottom on which thread is wound.

f. (sg. dat. pë̆zᵘ̈ 1; for 2, see pyodᵘ), acquaintance with another's private affairs; esp. becoming cognisant of the internal arrangements of another's house (with a view to theft, house- breaking, etc.) (cf. phēran-pᵒ, s.v. phērun, and pyodᵘ). --aʦüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. after preliminary successful experience from which nothing untoward has occurred, to be encouraged to take to criminal or debauched practices. --ʦānüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to encourage another after he has had a preliminary successful experience to adopt a criminal or abandoned life.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pēḍanôwᵘ), to cause to ooze, to cause to exude (Gr.Gr. 174).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. pĕdyōv), to become cognisant of anything, to gain experience of anything; esp. to become encouraged to engage in a criminal course of action by the experience of having done it once or twice before with impunity. pĕdyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pĕdyē-müʦᵘ̈), one who is encouraged to adopt a criminal course of conduct as ab.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. pēḍyōv), to exude, ooze, drop out (El. also paiḍun) (Gr.Gr. xlviii, 246). The causal of this verb is pēḍanāwun, not pīḍᵃrāwun (Gr.Gr. 174).
another spelling of pyēmotᵘ, for which, see pyonᵘ.

f. (sg. dat. pīñᵘ̈ 1; for 2, see s.v.), starch or size (put on threads before weaving or on cloth after weaving. It is applied with a brush in order to strengthen the warp (K.Pr. 171)); a similar liquid applied to iron implements (such as knives, swords, etc., to strengthen them); a horrible mixture of salt, pepper, soot, etc., forced as a punishment into a person's mouth; a dose of salt put into an animal's mouth as a medicine (cf. nūna-pēn, p. 641a, l. 8). --diñᵘ̈ --  f.inf. to size thread or cloth; to apply liquid to an iron instrument, as ab.; to force salt, pepper, soot, etc., into a person's mouth as a punishment. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to clean off, or wash off, the size from cloth. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to pull out the size, i.e. to wash cloth so as to remove the size put on the warp before weaving. --khārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to apply the strengthening liquid to a newly-made iron implement. ¶ pĕna-kam m. size applied to cloth, as ab. -kam karun 1 (for 2, see pyonᵘ), to apply size, as ab. -kônᵘ m. one of the row of sticks set up in the ground by a weaver, on which he arranges the warp prior to putting it on to a loom for weaving (cf. kônᵘ 2). -küṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kacĕ) a certain long-leaved water-grass, the juice of which is used as an eye-medicine. ¶ pīñᵘ̈ dyunᵘ m.inf. to insert a remedy (such as ointment, etc.) into the orifice of a wound (as if salt was being put into a cow's mouth). --lāgun -- m.inf. to apply to an unhealthy wound a bandage smeared with ointment, etc.

conj. 1 (pēnowᵘ), to size or starch (thread, cloth, etc.); to rub liniment (on to a painful part of the body, etc.); cf. pēn. pēnowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pēnüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of cloth, etc.) sized, starched; rubbed with liniment.

f. (sg. dat. pĕndi), a ball (for playing with) (L. 458, pind). pĕndi gindun m.inf. to play at ball; met. to be tossed about like a ball, to be subject to the vicissitudes of fortune, to have ups and downs.

m. a round mass, a lump (cf. lŏpta-pᵒ, p. 529a, l. 37); esp. the piṇḍa, or ball or lump of rice, etc., offered to the manes at Hindū obsequial ceremonies or Śrāddhas (cf. pŏtra-pᵒ, s.v. pọ̆thᵃr). --chapȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to make an offering of these lumps by casting them into a river, lake, or the like. ¶ pĕnḍa-dān m. the ceremony of making these offerings. -milawan f. the joining of these cakes, the ceremony of joining together the three portions of cakes, representing respectively the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather of the sacrificer. -myulᵘ m. 'union of these pĕṇḍas', close blood-relationship. pĕnḍa-ʦȧrⁱ-wörⁱ f. a cooking-pot for the preparation of these pĕṇḍas.
m. a sacrificial altar or piece of high ground used as such (cf. ạgᵃna-pᵃ, p. 16b, l. 42) (K. 372, 1037). Cf. pë̆nḍᵘ̈.
m. shrinking together of the parts or limbs (of anything), shrinking into a ball (cf. gōjĕ-pᵒ, p. 281b, l. 3).

f. (sg. dat. pĕnjĕ), a house-altar (cf. ạgᵃna-pᵃ, p. 16b, l. 43) (K.Pr. 55); a person's home, one's own home; in composition this word often indicates intimacy (temporary or otherwise). ¶ pĕnji-bôjᵘ m. (f. -bājĕñ), 'a sharer in the same altar'; hence, a boon companion (in dissipation), a fellow debauchee. -chamb m. (like the sudden fall of a victim on an altar) a crashing fall, sudden and unexpected destruction. -chamb gaʦhun m.inf. sudden and unexpected fall (i.e. destruction) to occur (e.g. with reference to the fall of a person from a high office) (K.Pr. 227). -chamb karun m.inf. suddenly and unexpectedly to throw down a person (e.g. cast him down from some high office). -ʦāṭh m. (sg. dat. -ʦāṭas), 'a pupil at the altar,' a fellow-plotter, a conspirator. -yār m. a boon companion (in dissipation), a fellow debauchee. -yārᵃz f. boon companionship, as ab. (esp. when the companionship is casually contracted and is only temporary, as when, e.g. a couple of people join forces in a gaming house).
m. a complete kernel of a walnut or similar nut (in which the kernel is in sections joined together).
f. the cleaning or sizing brush applied by weavers to the warp before weaving or to the finished cloth. See pēn (W. 145, penⁱtᵒd).
m. in the following:-- pĕpanz ta paran karȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. humbly to fall at a person's feet and to crave something or coax him to do something. pĕpanza paran m.pl. craving and coaxing, as ab.
m. thirst.--hyonᵘ -- m.inf. thirst to seize a person, to be parched with thirst. --lagun -- m.inf. thirst to arise or be felt.
m. a calamity (esp. a hostile attack or incursion). pēra yunᵘ m.inf. to become subject to scandal or evil report (whether true or false). Cf. pīr 3.
f. a ball or lump of leavened dough; a kind of sweetmeat made of curds.
or pīrĕr 1 m. greasiness, sliminess, slipperiness; smoothness.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. pēriladiñ), of ill repute, with tarnished reputation, debased, defiled; debasing, defiling.

m. front, fore part; adv. in front (of), before (Gr.M.; H. vi, 9, gay pēsh-ĕ-pātashāh, they went before the king, i.e. were taken into his presence). -andāz پیش انداز m. the outer, or front, supporting beam of an outer balcony or the like; cf. pushwān. --anun -- m.inf. to bring before (a person, dat.), to present to a person, to cause (him) to experience (such-and-such) (H. xii, 25). --sapadun -- m.inf. to become in front, (of a case in court) to come on, be put up (Gr.M.). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come before (a person, dat.), to come to meet (a person), step forward (Gr.M.); to present (itself), to arise, occur, happen (Rām. 1395). ¶ pēshĕs bĕhun m.inf. to sit in front (of the house), to expose oneself to public view; (met.) to take to a harlot's life. --nērun -- m.inf. to go forth in front, to lead an attack, uprising, or the like. --thawun -- m.inf. to set in front, to appoint (a person) to lead an attack, to appoint a leader or (in an emergency) a dictator, to set forward a person to lead a complaint, and so on.
m. urine, piss (El.). pēshābukᵘ ṭhēla m. the bladder (El.).

m. vocation, profession, craft, trade, business; custom, habit, practice; art, skill; (in Kāshmīrī) one of the side-pieces of a garment attached to the part hanging down in front. --kamanāwun -- or --kamawun -- m.inf. 'to work the profession', to lead the life of a harlot, to practise prostitution. --kamöyⁱ -- f. a prostitute's earnings. --karun -- m.inf. to practise prostitution.
adj. c.g. sportive, coquettish, modest and charming.
m. a deputy, a high official, a magistrate (El.); a certain high official, a prime minister (H. vi, 11).
f. the office of a pēshkār, q.v.; a chief secretaryship, the office of prime minister (Rām. 511).

m. early mid afternoon (i.e. about 1.30 or 2 p.m.) (K.Pr. 176, pĕshin). pĕshnukᵘ sg. gen. (f. pĕshnücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, this time. pĕshnan bögⁱ (or bögin)  adv. in about the early mid afternoon. pĕshnas bögⁱ (or bögin)  adv., id. pĕshnas-kani adv., id.

f. (sg. dat. pĕtarüñᵘ̈), protecting, guarding, nourishing, cherishing, fostering (children, a family, a flock, something entrusted, and so on); maintaining, carrying on, keeping up (a business or occupation made over to one by someone else).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pĕtarôwᵘ), i.q. pĕtarun, q.v. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf., i.q. pĕtarun pyonᵘ, s.v. pĕtarun, q.v. ¶ pĕtarôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pĕtarövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. pĕtorᵘ-motᵘ, s.v. pĕtarun, q.v. ¶ pĕtarāwan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), i.q. pĕtaran-wôlᵘ, s.v. pĕtarun, q.v.
n.ag. (f. pĕtaravüñᵘ̈), one who protects, guards, cherishes; one on whom the responsibility for performing some difficult work lies.

or pĕtarāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. pĕtorᵘ), to protect, guard, nourish, cherish, foster (children, a family, a herd of cattle, something entrusted, or the like) (Rām. 1589); to maintain, carry on, keep up (some business or occupation made over to one's charge), to undertake a responsibility (esp. of some difficult or impossible duty) (L.V. 61). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. a responsibility (for guarding (Rām. 981) or fostering, or for carrying on any duty) to fall upon, or be thrust upon, a person (H. ii, 5). ¶ pĕtorᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pĕtürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), guarded, fostered, taken care of; (some difficult or impossible duty) for which (a person) is responsible, carried on. ¶ pĕtaran-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who protects, one who guards; one who carries on, or is responsible for, some duty.

adv. and postpos. (as adv.) on the back (cf. atha pᵒ thawun, p. 61b, l. 16; K.Pr. 227; bāl pᵒ hāwun, p. 103b, l. 47) (L.V. 14, 15); above, up above (Gr.Gr. 152, 155, 159; Śiv. 965, 1352); in addition, also (K.Pr. 17). ¶ (As postpos. governing dat. and occasionally the acc.) on, upon (cf. athas-pᵒ, p. 66b, l. 3; chambas-pᵒ, p. 161b, l. 30; kŏñᵘ̈-pᵘ̈, p. 461a, l. 5; mas- wū̃cĕ-pᵒ, p. 595b, l. 22; nakhas-pᵒ, p. 629a, l. 42) (Gr.Gr. 43; Gr.M.; W. 97; L.V. 103; Śiv. 79, 116, 125, 192, 199, 210, 324, 496, 571, 1162 (governing abl.), etc.; Rām. 89, 96, 281, 354, 444, 597, 631, etc.; K. 58, 124, 161, 267, 270, 272, 331, 339, etc.; H. iii, 1; iv, 4; viii, 13; xi, 12, 16; athⁱ-pⁱ, thereupon, xii, 7); above, over (Śiv. 1603, etc.; K. 5, 905; YZ. 99, 279); on, in addition to (cf. hani-pᵒ han, p. 336a, l. 14) (Śiv. 640, 877); at, throughout (of time) (cf. rātas-pᵒ, s.v. rāth 1) (Śiv. 1477, Rām. 1275); (directed) at (e.g. an arrow at a mark) (Rām. 999); in a certain condition (e.g. of happiness, misery, or the like) (Rām. 754, sŏkhas-pᵒ, in a state of comfort, comfortable, so 825); (engaged) on, (busy) on (Rām. 960; K. 541, 617); on the point of, at the very time of (cf. bögis-pᵒ wātun, p. 91a, l. 23); up to, till (cf. nasti dŏgis-pĕṭh rōzun, to wait for a blow on the nose, p. 658b, l. 23); up at, close up to, in the presence of (cf. buthis-pᵒ, p. 143b, l. 26; khōr-pĕṭh mārun, p. 410a, l. 15) (Śiv. 1048, 1081, 1176-7, etc.; Rām. 462, 672; K. 88, 329, 398, 465, etc.; H. iii, 4); (with a verb of motion) to, towards, up to (cf. dayāyĕ-pᵒ yunᵘ, p. 267a, l. 7; gara-pᵒ, p. 296a, l. 7; jāyĕ-pᵒ anun, p. 380a, l. 19; khāhas-pᵒ, p. 394a, l. 29; pĕtis-pĕṭh wātun, s.v. pyotᵘ) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 63, 86, 313, 321, 374, 393 (with acc.), etc.; Rām. 622, 719, 793, 821, 887, etc.; K. 410, 490, 679, 702, 836, 838; H. iii, 4, 59; v, 9; xii, 2, 6, 11, 12, 14); on, in, at (cf. ajĕ wati pᵒ, p. 13b, l. 41; and-pᵒ, p. 31b, l. 10; bar-pᵒ hūñᵘ̈, p. 116b, l. 12; dūri-pᵒ, at a distance, p. 239b, l. 7; gara-pᵒ, p. 296a, l. 7; purüñᵘ̈-pᵘ̈ hāwun, p. 763b, l. 4) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 90, 154, 356, 1036, etc.; Rām. 564, 707, 1004, 1558; K. 810-1, 995, 1115, 1162; H. v, 11, ḍēras-pᵒ, (put) into a tent); (in astrology, a star) in (a certain sign) (Rām. 1280); through, by means of (dayāyĕ-pᵒ, in mercy) (Śiv. 1236); on account of, for the sake of, because of, through (cf. nahākas-pᵒ, p. 625b, l. 44) (Śiv. 111, 1015, 1137, 1184; Rām. 292, 395, 537, 752, etc.); on, founded on, based on (cf. bāzĕ-pᵒ thawun or rōzun, p. 113a, ll. 6, 10; dushĕrtas-pᵒ, on doubt, hesitatingly, p. 254b, l. 40) (Śiv. 1596); (of anger, etc.), on, directed against (Rām. 266, 282, 1215); regarding, with reference to (cf. parilūkas-pᵒ, p. 759b, l. 9) (K. 598, 800, 1055, 1105; H. viii, 6, 8, 11, 13); on, after (cf. dabas-pᵒ dusᵘ, p. 181b, ll. 38, 44; dūr-pᵒ, after a long time, p. 238b, l. 36); on to, up (or down) on to (cf. athas-pᵒ atha dyunᵘ, p. 66b, l. 5; daras-pᵒkhasun, p. 234b, l. 40; khŏras-pᵒ khŏr ʦhunun, p. 409b, l. 39) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 23, 701, 704, 785, 994, 1090, 1098, 1222, 1630, etc.; Rām. 113, 190, 203, 271, 358, 387, 397, etc.; K. 83, 118, 327; H. ii, 11; iii, 5, 7; v, 5, 6, 9; viii, 1; x, 5, 7; xii, 5, 7, 21, 24). ¶ As stated above, this postposition ordinarily governs the dative case. Occasionally, however, it governs the accusative in the same form as the nominative. Examples (all also given above) are and-pᵒ, p. 31b, l. 10; bar-pᵒ, p. 116b, l. 12 (K. 995); dūr-pᵒ, after a long time, p. 238b, l. 36, but dūri-pᵒ, at a distance, p. 239b, l. 7; gara-pᵒ, p. 296a, l. 7; khōr-pᵒ, p. 410b, l. 15 (K. 702). ¶ Occasionally pĕṭh is used as equivalent to pĕṭha, in the meaning of 'from on', and governing the abl. (Śiv. 1247, Rām. 274). ¶ pĕṭh khārun m.inf. to elevate (e.g. a humble person to an honourable post, or to lift something to a higher place) (cf. kulᵘ pĕṭh pôñᵘ khārun, p. 438b, l. 36) (Śiv. 1392, K. 931). -kun adv. up, upwards, on high; above, elevated (K. 476, 516). --pĕṭh -- adv. higher and higher. ¶ pĕṭha adv. and postpos. (as adv.) from on, from off, from above (K. 890). ¶ (As postpos. governing abl. or abl. of gen.; or (in the case of a singular masculine living being) optionally the dative) from on, from off (Gr.Gr. 48; Gr.M.; W. 98; Śiv. 1108, 1878; Rām. 562, 712; K. 84, 232, 443, 716, 985, 1008); down from (L.V. 57; Śiv. 421, 501, 508, 966, 1300, 1879; Rām. 765, 974, 1352; K. 277-8, 450; H. ii, 6; iv, 5; xii, 2); from near (Gr.Gr. 48); from the midst of (Rām. 959); from (generally) (cf. bŏna-pᵒ, from below, p. 110b, l. 20; buthi-pᵒ tulun, p. 143a, l. 48; buthi-pᵒ wŏthun, p. 143b, l. 3) (Gr.M.; W. 98; L.V. 93; Śiv. 672, 897, 1097, 1176; K. 593, 1047; H. ii, 2; v, 7; xi, 3); beginning from, continuing from, ever since (cf. ödⁱ-pⁱ, p. 14a, l. 1; anda-pᵒ, p. 32a, ll. 3, 4; ȧzⁱki-pⁱ, p. 74a, l. 45; brō̃ṭha-pᵒ, p. 128a, l. 44; dahi warihĕ pᵒ, p. 200b, l. 11; kāla-pᵒ, p. 434a, l. 25; mainay-kāla-pᵒ, p. 583a, l. 42) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 527, 1340, 1553; Rām. 348, 1715; K. 244, 782, 1148); out of; on, upon (= pĕṭh) (cf. rāth pĕṭha pë̆ñᵘ̈, s.v. rāth 2) (K. 234; H. v, 9; x, 3, 10). ¶ Also used with adverbs, as in az-pĕṭha, p. 74a, l. 21 (K. 63); ȧzⁱ-pⁱ, p. 74a, l. 39; huti-pᵒ, p. 356a, l. 34; kana-pᵒ, p. 449a, l. 36; kati-pᵒ, p. 483b, l. 37, whence?; so tati-pᵒ, thence; yĕti-pᵒ, whence; yiti-pᵒ, hence (Gr.Gr. 155, K. 244). ¶ pĕṭha bŏna adv. from above and from below, from top to bottom (L.V. 17). -kani  adv. above; on the top of (H. viii, 1); in front; (down) from the top (K.Pr. 27); pre-eminently; from the first, from the beginning (Śiv. 1716). -kanĕn adv., id. -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, above; upper, higher; pre-eminent, chief. --pĕṭha -- adv. superficially, cursorily, skimming the surface; attending to the chief points (in an argument, or the like), carrying out the chief things (without reference to detail), and so on. -roṭᵘ m. the act of stopping from above, impeding from aloft (e.g. something which prevents a rope which is being thrown or pulled up reaching the required height), something in the way above; (in weighing) that which is more than sufficient to balance, that which is over and above the correct weight or measure. -raṭh or pĕṭhⁱ-raṭh f. (sg. dat. -raṭi), (in raising a pillar, pulling up a rope, or the like) that which prevents it reaching the top, that which is in the way above; (in supplying thread to be woven into cloth) an additional quantity (beyond the required weight) given in order to secure extra strong material. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain above, stand over (K. 74). ¶ pĕṭhⁱ adv. and postpos. (governing abl.) from on, from above (cf. atha-pᵒ, p. 61b, l. 19; pashĕ- pĕṭhⁱ shīn trāwun, p. 777b, l. 9) (Śiv. 1079, 1092, 1165, 1401, 1725); on, upon, over, above (Gr.Gr. 155; Gr.M.; Śiv. 205; Rām. 1078, 1172, 1613; K. 194; H. iii, 8; K.Pr. 127, written píṭhi); (with verbs of motion, etc.) over (e.g. jumping over something) (cf. kala-pᵒ wŏṭh, p. 435a, l. 42 (Śiv. 1810; K. 187, 237; H. ii, 9). -ḍakha m. a support from above (e.g. of something hanging). -kani, postpos. (governing abl.) over and above, in addition to (H. iii, 8). -kinⁱ adv. and postpos. (governing abl.) from above, from on (Gr.Gr. 159); above, superior to (K. 904); above, on the top of (Śiv. 166; Rām. 576, 578, 1118); above, over (K. 351, 842). -kinⁱ dyunᵘ m.inf. to give from above, to give over and above; esp. to make an offering of some animal (such as a sheep or a goat) in order to ward off some calamity or some untoward event. -kinⁱ lagun m.inf. to become an offering as ab.; (of some living being) to sacrifice oneself, or even offer one's life, for the salvation of others (from some calamity). -man m. a certain kind of offering (in which, at midday on a Tuesday or Saturday, a mixture of seven kinds of cooked grain is left at a cross- roads). -mana lagun m.inf. to be cast away as an offering at a cross-roads, as ab.; met. (of some living beast) to be abandoned as an offering to ward off some calamity, to be sent forth like a scape-goat. --pĕṭhⁱ -- adv. along the top, skimming the top; superficially. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall (upon) from above; to fall upon, make a violent attack (upon a person). -raṭh f. (sg. dat. -raṭi), i.q. pĕṭha-raṭh, ab. -wöñᵘ̈ earning over and above (e.g. additional wages, extra price, pay for extra work, etc.); additional work (added to other work). -wāñukᵘ sg. gen. (f. -wāñücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, excess earnings or additional work, as ab. ¶ pĕṭhukᵘ sg. gen. (f. pĕṭhücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, above, upper (cf. bāla-pᵒ, p. 104a, l. 14); of, or belonging to, that which is upon (anything) (cf. buthi-pᵒ, p. 143b, l. 5; ḍĕka-pᵒ, p. 204b, ll. 16, 19; hĕli-pᵒ, p. 364b, l. 18; kŏchi-pᵒ, p. 383b, l. 21; kuli-pᵒ, p. 439a, ll. 10, 13) (Śiv. 467); of, or belonging to, the beginning (of anything); beginning from; elevated, chief. ¶ pĕṭham pĕṭh adv. on the top and again on the top, filling up and filling up, one on the top of the other, piling and piling up (u.w. vbs. of feeding, filling, inserting, or the like). ¶ pĕṭhan adv. and postpos. from, starting from, beginning with (cf. az-pᵒ, p. 74a, l. 32). ¶ pĕṭhay adv. and postpos. (governing abl.) from the very beginning, from the very start, beginning from, continuing from, ever since (Śiv. 658); down on (as in sitting down on) (K.Pr. 31). -bāna adj. c.g. the first, occurring at the very beginning, primitive; (as adv.) at the very beginning (of an action or condition). -bānukᵘ sg. gen. (f. -bānücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the very beginning, occurring at the very beginning. ¶ pyoṭhus pĕṭh adv. upon and upon, one over the other, one on the top of the other.

m. (sg. dat. pĕtas), the bilious humour, bile, gall (El. pyut) (cf. rata-pᵒ, s.v. rath). --nērun -- m.inf. the bile to exude, a crop of small red boils (believed to be due to this cause) to appear. ¶ pĕta-kiṭurᵘ m. a gathering in the inner eyelid caused by the bilious humour,? a stye. -phĕphur m. (sg. dat. -phĕpharas), a stye on the outer eyelid.

m. (sg. dat. pĕtas), vain talk, empty chatter, i.q. pith, q.v., used in the following:--pĕth pĕth m. delirium, garrulous madness. --pĕth lagun -- m.inf. garrulous madness to attack (a person) (consisting in repeating the same thing over and over again in and out of season).
m. one who interferes by giving advice or instructions to those not under his orders, one who takes upon himself authority to which he is not entitled.
f. taking upon oneself authority to which one is not entitled.
m. a walk, a journey (El.) (? pö̃than 3, q.v.).
adj. (f. pĕṭhimᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, above, topmost, upper, first (Gr.Gr. 152, K.Pr. 18).
or pẹ̆tᵃr m. a paternal uncle, a father's brother (El. pitar) (Rām. 1555). His wife is pĕcĕñ, q.v. pẹ̆tᵃra-bāpathᵃruth m. (sg. dat. -bāpathᵃratas), the relationship of paternal uncle and nephew.

or pitur 1 m. (pl. nom. pĕtᵃr or (K. 1043) pitar), a deceased ancestor (to whom libations are made in obsequial rites), manes (cf. diva-pᵒ, p. 261b, l. 30) (Śiv. 1163, 1430; Rām. 311; K. 1043). ¶ pĕtᵃra-bögᵃ adv. for the sake of an ancestor (e.g. a libation), of, or connected with, an ancestor. -bȧktⁱ m. one who is devoted to (offering libations to) the manes. -dŏh m. the day on which libations are offered to the manes. -pach m. (sg. dat. pachas), the (dark) fortnight (of the month of Öshid, i.e. Skt. Āśvina = September-October) during which libations are offered to the manes. -phāka m. a fast in honour of, or on behalf of, the manes (such as that held on the anniversary of the death of an ancestor). -shāph m. (sg. dat. -shāpas), the curse of the manes, i.e. the curse (and its consequences) incurred by a son who has neglected to offer the customary libations to the manes. ¶ pĕtᵃri-kã̄gᵃrᵃ f. the ancestor-brazier, a name given to the paper on which a family priest who conducts the libation-ceremonies keeps a record of the family ancestors. -nĕmȧtⁱ adv. for the sake of the manes (e.g. a libation).
f. a falling, (as it were an avalanche) a great quantity, used --˚ as in rana-pĕv, an immense amount of cooking, s.v. ran.
f. (sg. dat. pĕvüñᵘ̈), the act of falling, used --˚, as in rūda-pᵒ, s.v. rūd; shīna-pᵒ, s.v. shīn.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pĕwanôwᵘ), to cause preparations for food to be begun, to get the kitchen fire lighted.

n.ag. (f. pĕwawüñᵘ̈. This word is n.ag. of pyonᵘ, q.v. (see Gr.Gr. 105), in all its senses, and esp. in the following:--) fallen down (from a high position to a lower one); that which falls (e.g. rain) (Śiv. 1309, K.Pr. 254); one who falls, i.e. who can be defeated in a combat; (a business or the like) which is calculated to have a satisfactory result; that which is coming into existence, that which is happening, occurring, being born. pĕwawanis adv. at the time (of rain) falling, during a fall of rain.
n.ag. (f. pĕwawüñᵘ̈. This word is the n.ag. of pĕwun), one who sets about lighting a kitchen fire, a cook.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pyowᵘ), to start preparations for cooking (lighting the stove and the like), to set the kitchen fire alight (K.Pr. 164). ¶ pĕwan-vēla m. the time for beginning preparations for cooking, i.e. for lighting the cooking fire, etc., i.e. about an hour before sunset. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), (m.) the man who lights the cooking fire, i.e. a cook; (f.) the eldest daughter-in-law or other female relative, who (for the sake of good luck) lights the cooking fire on festal occasions. -vizᵘ̈ f., i.q. -vēla, ab. -zang f. (at a wedding or similar festive occasions) the gift (of rice, money, etc.) made, for good luck, to the female member of the family who lights the cooking fire (e.g. given to the bride's father's sister or the like by the relations of the bridegroom).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pẹ̆zᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. pẹ̆zᵃrun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pẹ̆zᵒrᵒ), to instigate (a person) to the commission of some evil deed by divulging secret particulars (as to the means of its accomplishment, etc.) (e.g. instigating theft by divulging the locality of the property to be stolen, or how it is hidden). Cf. pĕdun and pyodᵘ.
adj. c.g. twisting, winding, coiling. mār-i-pēʦān, a serpent of convolutions, a kind of serpent that makes itself into a ring round its victim, and thus kills it at its leisure (Rām. 913).
m. the horny part of the hoof of a cow or the like; hence, the kick (of a cow) (K.Pr. 241).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. pĕʦyōv), (of fruit, vegetables, etc.), to become dried up, to become dry and sapless, to become desiccated (and unfit for eating, cooking, etc.). pĕʦyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pĕʦyē-müʦᵘ̈), become dried up, as ab.

f. a certain tall strong reed, or rush, growing in the Kashmīr lakes, of which matting is made (El.), the reed-mace (Typha sp.). A sweetmeat is made of its pollen (see ḍal-nābad, p. 210a, l. 5). According to El. it is Typha angustifolia and T. latifolia (W. 139; L. 68, 72, 345; Śiv. 1806; K.Pr. 5, 7, 71). ¶ pĕʦi-bọ̆dᵘ m. a bundle of these reeds (as much as can be grasped at one time in the hand). -bani hyonᵘ m.inf. (fire) to seize on a stack of reeds, a stack of reeds to take fire; met. to be parched with thirst. -ḍal m. a reed lake, a lake in which this reed grows. -kalam m. a stem of this reed. -kān m. an arrow-like stem of this reed (Śiv. 353). -kônᵘ 1 m. a single plant or stem of this reed (kônᵘ 2). -kônᵘ 2 m. a reed mat maker (kônᵘ 3). -köñᵘ̈ f. a small bundle of these reeds (cf. Gr.Gr. 163). -kĕsurᵘ m. the stamens (and, hence, the pollen) of the flower of this reed. -laḍur m. (sg. dat. -laḍaras), the edible soft inside portion of the root of this reed. -lürᵘ̈ f. a hut made of reed mats plastered with mud; a hut with a mat roof. -lôwᵘ m. a wisp of these reeds (ready for weaving). -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. the root of this reed; a pillow or cushion woven of this reed. -nambal f. a marsh in which this reed grows. -nār m. a fire of these reeds. -nörᵘ̈ f. a long narrow canal-like lake, in which these reeds grow. -pahörᵘ̈ f. a mud hut with a reed-mat roof. -pash m. a mat roof. -poshᵘ adj. (f. -püshᵘ̈), furnished with a reed-mat roof. -raz f. a rope made of these reeds (useful as a well-rope). -tulᵘ m. a single stalk or piece of this reed (K.Pr. 125); a small amount of these reeds (cf. Gr.Gr. 164).
for such words as phã-wāl, phã-wôñᵘ, phã-wār, phã-vüṭᵘ̈, phã-watun, see under phamb.
n.ag. (f. phabavüñᵘ̈), one who (or that which) causes or produces a successful result.
m. the turning out successfully of any act or business; (of a human being) the becoming successful, becoming wealthy.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. phabyōv), to turn out well, to turn out successfully; (of a human being) to become successful, become wealthy. phabyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phabyē-müʦᵘ̈), turned out successfully; (of a human being) become successful, become wealthy.
in the following:--phacakh-pholᵘ m. a packet of powder given as a joke to another, under the pretence that it is a different powder which he asks for, a kind of 'sell'.
m. the condition of cracking, bursting, splitting, the condition of being cracked. (Cf. dam-phᵒ, p. 216b, l. 5.)

m. (sg. dat. phadᵃranas), a certain vegetable with a long stem, said to be very hard to chew. -hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -hishᵘ̈), like this plant; hence, generally, tough, hard to chew even after cooking, and then fit to be eaten only after being cut up into small pieces.
m. a certain medicinal shrub. Its leaves are given to cows in order to induce a plentiful flow of well-flavoured milk.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phā̃gowᵘ), to cause (a baby) to wail, to make it wail; (of a baby) to wail, pule.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phỗgᵘ; 2 p.p. phã̄jyōv, this verb is impersonal in the tenses derived from the past participle), (of a baby) to wail, whimper, pule; (of a cat) to mew.

m. (sg. dat. phāganas), N. of the twelfth month of the Hindū year (= February-March), in Skt. Phālguna (W. 107; K.Pr. 128, 167, 171). phāganunᵘ rĕth m. (sg. dat. phāgananis rĕtas), the month of Phāgun.
(sg. dat. phāganas), emptiness. --zyonᵘ -- m.inf. emptiness to be born (of a house or the like becoming empty or deserted of its inmates, owing to death or misfortune).
adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, the month of Phāgun. --gŏgᵃ̇jᵃ̇ -- f. turnips of Phāgun, i.e. turnips dug up in the autumn, and stored in a pit till that month.

m. warmth (esp. that caused by putting one limb against another) (K.Pr. 60, 171, 204, 228); supporting, cherishing (of a child, etc., who has lost his natural supporters). --barun -- m.inf. (of a child or other who has lost his natural supporters) to gain support. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. (of a bird) to keep (eggs) warm, to sit on eggs (to hatch them) (K.Pr. 117, 121); to support, cherish (one who has lost his natural supporters). ¶ phāha-büṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -bachĕ), 'a warmth-hearth'; hence, a warm embrace; (allusively) the private parts of a woman. -dār adj. c.g. producing warmth, warm (of a garment or the like). -kŏkürᵘ̈ f. 'a warming (i.e. sitting) hen', warming oneself, keeping oneself warm in plenty of wraps. -kūṭhürᵘ̈ f. 'a warmth-closet', a heated room, a room kept warm. -laṭur m. 'a warmth-stick' (quasi, a stick burning and giving warmth); hence, a warm or loving embrace. -laṭürᵘ̈ f., id. (allusively) the male organ of generation.
f. (sg. dat. phaharüñᵘ̈), harshness, roughness, hardness; harshness, cruelty, sternness.
phihrawáo, see phahᵃra-wāv, col. a, l. 30.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phaharôwᵘ), to make (something smooth or soft) hard, rough, rugged; to render (a person's disposition) hard, stern, cruel. pharôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phaharövᵘ̈-mᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), made hard, etc., as ab.
m. hardness, harshness, roughness (cf. atha-phᵒ, p. 60b, l. 28) (Gr.Gr. 138); (of disposition) harshness, cruelness, sternness.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. phaharyōv), (of something smooth or soft) to become hard, rough, rugged; (of a person's nature) to become harsh, cruel, stern.
m. understanding, conception, perception, apprehension, intellect, intelligence, sense. Cf. kam-phᵒ, p. 442b, l. 18 (W. 110, fahm).

or phohurᵘ adj. (f. phạhᵘ̈rᵘ̈), hard, rough, rugged (cf. atha-phᵒ, p. 60b, l. 25) (Gr.Gr. 138); harsh, abusive, severe, cruel, stern. ¶ phahar-gāsa m. madder (Rubia cordifolia) (El. phaharghás). ¶ phahᵃra-kã̄ḍ adj. c.g. (of straw, vegetable stalk, etc.) rough or coarse-stemmed; (of hair) coarse, rough. -wāv m. a file, a rasp (El. phihrawáo) (H. v, 10).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phôhᵘ, f. phöshᵘ̈, K. 738), i.q. phᵃhun 1, q.v., noted only in the phöshᵘ̈ of K. 738.

or phöd m. a small bead or stud of gold or silver fastened on to an ornament. ¶ phöda-lāgay f. beading, the condition of being studded with such beads (on an ornament), a bead-pattern; the work of applying beads. -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), the soldering or otherwise fastening of such beads in a pattern or an ornament.
adj., c.g. strong, brave, valiant, valorous (El., Gr.M.); i.q. pahalwān, q.v.

m. poverty, want, destitution; starvation, abstention from food, fasting (religious or due to sickness); fasting, a fast (cf. pĕtᵃra-phᵃ, s.v. pĕtur) (K.Pr. 9, 28, 199). --bāna -- m.pl. vessels in which the necessary food on a fast day is cooked. -bata m. the (dainty) food eaten after the conclusion of a fast. -dorᵘ adj. (f. -dürᵘ̈), one who is firm in a fast, one who goes through a fast unflinchingly; one who has undertaken a fast. --darun -- m.inf. to undertake a fast, to fast (in a religious sense). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to fast, to abstain from food (as a religious exercise or on account of illness). -hotᵘ adj. (f.-hüʦᵘ̈), fasting, starving. -khĕn m. the eating of (dainty) food after the conclusion of a fast. --karun -- m.inf. to go without food, to fast (from want or ill-health). --lagun -- m.inf. fasting (owing to want of food) to be experienced, starvation to be felt. -phākh f. (sg. dat. -phāki), fast on fast, the occurrence of one religious fast immediately following another. --thawun -- m.inf. to undertake a (religious) fast. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who fasts (as a religious exercise). ¶ phākay adv. without food, without making arrangements for food (e.g. when going on a journey).
adj. c.g. one who gives forth an evil stench, stinking (of a human being, or of his clothes, etc.); esp. one who habitually breaks wind.

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. phakaladiñ), (of a human being) one who gives forth an evil smell (esp. one whose breath smells, or whose clothes give forth a bad smell) (Gr.Gr. 135); stinking (of over-ripe fruit, or over-kept food), rotten.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. phākaladiñ), one who is fasting (for want of food or as a religious exercise) K.Pr. 154).
adv. only, solely, merely, simply, and no more (Śiv. 71, 543, 745, 752).

m. (sg. dat. phakas), an evil smell, a stench, a stink (cf. ös-phᵒ, p. 46b, l. 14; dᵃha-phᵃ or dᵃ̇hi-phᵃ̇, p. 198a, l. 36; b, l. 26; günzᵘ̈-phᵘ̈, p. 293b, l. 17; gᵃsa-phᵃ, p. 307a, l. 23; kanzan-phᵒ, p. 460a, l. 30; krāran-phᵒ, p. 476a, l. 24; phȧrⁱ-phⁱ, s.v. phorᵘ 1; prāna-phᵒ, s.v. prān 2; rahna-phᵒ, s.v. rahun) (Gr.Gr. 135; K.Pr. 65, 125, 221, 240). --tulun -- m.inf. to raise a stink, to give out a stink (owing to rottenness); met. to publish a scandal (against some one); (when some member of one's own family is detained in some distant place) to utter consoling words without going to look for him, to talk without taking action. --trāwun -- m.inf. to emit a stink, to fart. --wŏthun -- m.inf. a stink to rise (e.g. from rotten flesh, a corrupt wound, or burning matter). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. a stink to come or arise, as ab. (H. ii, 4); (in making gifts or distributing alms) a bad name to arise owing to the exhibition of niggardliness. ¶ phaka-gānd f. (sg. dat. -gönzᵘ̈), a bad stink, a horrible stench. -nôrᵘ m. the rectum. -phorᵘ m. a stench-belly, i.e. a belly full of filth (owing to indigestion or the like); as adj. (f. -phürᵘ̈), one who has such a belly; (in f.) a woman who is addicted to unnatural vice. -ṭö̃cᵘ̈ f. a kind of wild pear, acrid in taste, evil smelling, small, and juiceless, which is looked upon as food for monkeys; met. a woman with such qualities. -ṭö̃jᵘ̈ f., id. -tsdigraph;ēr f. a kind of wild apricot, small, acrid, and evil smelling. -zodᵘ m. the anus (used in abuse). -zyurᵘ m. a kind of small aniseed with an evil smell, used medicinally for boils, etc. ¶ phakas wurun tulun m.inf. to raise the cover from over a stink; hence, to reveal one's own or another's secret bad conduct. --wurun ʦhunun -- m.inf. to put a cover on a stink, to put a stop to scandal about one's own or another's bad conduct.
m. (sg. dat. phākas), N. of a pargana, or fiscal division, in Kashmīr on the north side of the Vĕth (Jehlam) River, close to Śrīnagar (RT.Tr. II, 452).
f. a dove; adj. c.g. dove-colour, fawn-colour.

(often pronounced pakīr) m. (f. phȧkⁱröñⁱ, q.v.), a man who is indigent, a beggar, a poor man (L. 234); a religious mendicant, ascetic, devotee, fakeer (cf. chŏka-phᵒ, p. 150b, l. 28; damāli-phᵒ, p. 219b, l. 21; phȧlⁱ-phⁱ, p. 694b, l. 12) (H. i, 2; ii, 1-3, 9; iii, 1; x, 7-9, 12, 14; K.Pr. 15, 30, 167). -bāpār m. business like that of a beggar; esp. (at a wedding of rich people), giving a mean dowry, etc. -küṭᵘ̈ f. a beggar's daughter; a woman who lives in a state of poverty. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a beggar's son, a man living in a state of poverty. -pholᵘ m. a bead on fakeer's rosary. -pöthᵃr m. conduct of a beggar; conduct like that of a beggar, (of one who is not poor) niggardly conduct at a festival or the like. -tulukᵘ m. a beggar's begging dish; as adj. (f. -tulücᵘ̈), one who, though rich, is ever proclaiming his or her poverty.
f. poverty, beggary; the life of a religious mendicant, fakeerhood (H. x, 9, 14). --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to adopt the life of a religious mendicant.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phokᵘ; 2 p.p. phacyōv), to state one's poverty or inability (e.g. in giving charity, to have to stop while the giving is in progress owing to insufficient means or supplies); to spit out after chewing (Gr.Gr. xlix).

adj. c.g. emitting a stench, stinking. phȧkⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to become stinking; met. (of some person or thing hitherto looked upon with affection) to become detested, to become abandoned with disgust. --karun -- m.inf. to abandon with disgust (some person or thing hitherto looked upon with affection), to acquire detestation for.
f. (f. of phakīr, q.v.), a female beggar; a female ascetic, a female fakeer.
f. beggary, the condition of a beggar, mendicancy.
m. (sg. dat. phȧkⁱratas), the condition of a beggar, mendicancy; asceticism (voluntarily undertaken by one who has hitherto led the life of a householder).

m. fruit (including grain) (cf. naba-phᵒ, p. 619a, l. 13; nika-phᵒ, p. 627b, l. 27) (Gr.Gr. 72; Gr.M.; L.V. 86; Śiv. 182, 591, 1212, 1291, 1297, 1550, 1573, 1784, 1813, 1914; Rām. 1364, 1512; K. 178, 219, 226, 979; H. ix, 9; YZ. 394; K.Pr. 10, 187, 190); produce, crop, yield (cf. nav-phᵒ, p. 664b, l. 30; phȧlⁱ-phⁱ, p. 694b, l. 15; potᵘ-phᵘ, s.v. potᵘ) (Rām. 27); a result, fruit, consequence (Śiv. 1511, 1585, 1748, 1795, 1828; Rām. 437, 505-6; K. 717, 775, 849, 1061-3); hence, reward, recompense, meed, retribution (cf. darma-phᵒ, p. 244b, l. 30; karma-phᵒ, p. 471b, l. 35; pŏñĕ-phᵒ, s.v. pŏñ; pāpa-phᵒ, s.v. pāph) (Śiv. 228, 627, 667, 1241, 1536; Rām. 1642; K. 528, 841, 1096); aim, object, purpose; an inference (from something said) (Gr.M.); use, good, profit, benefit, advantage (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1159, 1182; K. 317, 671); interest on capital; the kernel of a fruit, grain after being husked (cf. ȧlⁱshi-phⁱ, p. 25b, l. 11; hĕma-phᵒ, p. 33a, l. 49; hĕlⁱ-phⁱ, p. 364b, l. 6); the outcome or answer of a sum, of an astrological calculation, riddle, etc. (Śiv. 524); the outcome, or fulfilment, of an omen, dream, portent, or the like (K. 676); mixed oilcake, grain, and chaff, used as cattle-fodder (cf. -dal, -pholᵘ, and -ṭhaṭhüjᵘ̈, bel.); boiled rice, together with the water in which it has been boiled; the materials of which colours are formed (El.) (cf. -gorᵘ, bel.). -dal m. mixed oilcake, grain, chaff, etc., given to cattle as fodder. -dānd m. a bull kept for breeding purposes, a stud bull. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to feed cows on the mixed fodder described ab. -gunᵘ m. an almanac showing the lucky and unlucky days, etc., of the year. -gorᵘ m. a seller of cooked food consisting of wild vetch and other grains seasoned with salt and fried in oil; a dye-seller, a man who sells dyes for cloth. -gȧrⁱ-wān m. a dye-seller's shop. -honḍᵘ m. a fruit-ram, a large ram fattened on fruit (L.V. 77). -hār m. a diet consisting wholly of fruit (to the exclusion of grain) adopted on fast-days (cf. ala-phal-hār, p. 22b, l. 24); according to El., the Hindū name for the cooked water-chestnut (cf. gāri-phᵒ, p. 298a, l. 1). -hörⁱ m. one whose diet consists of fruit alone. -hār-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who (owing to a fast, vow, or the like) eats fruit only (esp. with ref. to such a person when eating in company with others who have no restrictions as to food). -kulᵘ m. a fruit-tree (K.Pr. 168). -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a fruit-ram, a ram fed on grain, a fatted ram. -lunḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -lanjĕ), a fruit-laden bough. -pholᵘ m. a small amount of any grain (L.V. 86); a pile of mixed grain, chaff, etc., for cattle fodder. -phrēʦar m. the coming of a fortunate and happy result (from some auspicious cause). -phryūstᵘ or -phryūʦᵘ m. (f. -phrīʦᵘ̈ or -phrǖʦᵘ̈), (of some auspicious cause) producing a happy and fortunate result. -sēr 1 m. anything weighing a full seer (two pounds). -sēr 2 adj. c.g. one who has wealth and grain to his full satisfaction (cf. phala-sēr, bel.). -sörᵘ̈ f. collection of grain; esp. bringing it home from the threshing floor. -ṭhaṭhüjᵘ̈ f. a trough or similar vessel at which cattle are fed, a cattle-manger. The food consists mainly of grain and chaff mixed with water. -ʦạndᵃr m. a bright moon. -zyunᵘ m. firewood cut from a fruit-tree. It is used for cooking. ¶ phala-barith adj. c.g. full of fruit, bearing much fruit (K. 223); fertile (El.). -dāta m. one who tests another's work and praises it, thereby encouraging him to further exertions. -gọ̆bᵘ adj. (f. -gö̆bᵘ̈), having great results (e.g. a business, action, portent, or the like). -gŏbĕr m. the condition of having great results (as ab.). -gonᵘ adj. (f. -güñᵘ̈ 1, for 2, see phal 2), giving heavy produce (e.g. a field), bearing a heavy crop. -gañĕr m. the condition of bearing a heavy crop (as ab.). -mūl m. fruit and roots (as offered together in religious ceremonies). -purᵘ adj. (f. -purᵘ̈), full of produce, full cropped (e.g. a field, a tree, or the like); (of some business or work) having rich results. -purn adj. c.g., id. -prāpath f. (sg. dat. -prāpüʦᵘ̈), the ripening or coming into existence of a result. -pūrĕr m. the final settlement of a quarrel, discussion, or the like; the final resulting of any action. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), fruitless, barren (of a field, tree, action, etc.) (Śiv. 167, 1539); as adv. fruitlessly, without result. -raʦhar m. barrenness, etc., as ab. -sēr m. (of a field, tree, etc.), satiated with fruit or produce, bearing plenteous fruit; satisfied with (i.e. having a full amount of) wealth, property, offspring, etc., or with the duties connected with them (cf. phal-sēr 2, ab.). -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), having plenteous fruit; esp. when the fruit is manifest. -sasʦar or -saʦhar m. plenteous of manifest fruit, as ab. -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), rich in fruit, bearing plenteous fruit, fruitful, fertile (Gr.M.). -sāvĕr m. richness of fruit. -sāway f., id. -ʦhorᵘ adj. (f. -ʦhürᵘ̈), bearing no fruit (of a field, tree, action, business, etc.); (of fruit-bunch, legume, or the like) having no fruit (fair outside, but empty of fruit). -ʦharĕr m. the condition of bearing no fruit, as ab. -ʦorᵘ adj. (f. -ʦürᵘ̈), bearing much fruit. -ʦarĕr m. the condition of bearing much fruit. -wāl f. the chaff and other refuse thrown away in winnowing rice. -wāl hë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. to winnow rice, etc., to clean rice by winnowing. -wôlu 1 (for 2, see phal 2) m. (f. -wājĕñ, K. 178), a fruit-seller (K. 178); a grain-seller; one who experiences the result of former actions, or that which causes such results. -vĕʦar m. (of some action, conduct, etc.) the condition of bearing fruit (as in the next). -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), (of some act, conduct, etc.) bearing fruit, having inevitable results, big with results. -zēchĕr  m. the condition of having far-reaching results. -zyūthᵘ 1 (for 2, see phal 2) (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈), bearing a great quantity of fruit; having far-reaching results; having long-lasting results.

m. a ploughshare (cf. ala-phᵒ, p. 23a, l. 36) (Śiv. 1531); the metal blade of a mattock or the like (cf. liwañĕ-phᵒ, p. 542a, l. 9, and phal 3); a red-hot lump of iron. -hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -hishᵘ̈), hot, burning hot (like a red-hot lump of iron). ¶ phāla-waṭh m. (sg. dat. -waṭas), a large block of stone used as an anvil.

f. a strip, a flake (L. 462, fal, a piece; W. 121); a long piece of timber (split off a log or standing tree from end to end); a strip, or piece, of fish similarly flaked off. -wölⁱ-zad or phala-wölⁱ-zad adj. c.g. living and acting like one stupefied or witless (in apparel, speech, conduct, etc.), as though smitten by extreme poverty. ¶ phala-güñᵘ̈ 2 f. a long piece of wood which has been split off from a post, or long piece of flesh which has been cut off from a fish. --karañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to make a long strip or piece of wood cut from a post, or of fish split into two or three lengths; met. to flog or drub anyone, esp. an unruly child or dog. --tulañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to raise splinters (in cutting or shaping wood) (H. vii, 14); to raise long pieces, to raise weals, to flog a naughty child with a birch rod or the like. -wôlᵘ 2 m. (f. -wājĕñ), (a tree, post, etc.) of which a part has been split off. --wālañĕ -- 1f. pl. inf. to split off long pieces from a standing tree or the like; to beat or drub a standing person. -wölⁱ-zad, see phal-wölⁱ-zad, ab. -zyunᵘ m. firewood consisting of long split logs. -zyūṭhᵘ 2 adj. (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈), split into long planks or beams; firewood consisting of long split logs.
m. an omen, augury, presage; enchantment, spell; a good omen (El. fál) (Śiv. 1748); a portent (Rām. 744). --wuchun -- m.inf. to seek the explanation of an omen (from an astrologer or the like).
m. the metal tip of an arrow (cf. kāna-phᵒ, p. 449a, l. 18); the blade of a mattock or the like. Cf. the next.
adj. c.g. fruitful, possessing fruit (lit. and met.); (of firewood) producing many split sticks (cf. phal 2).
m. (sg. dat. phalakas), a kind of sling fastened as a punishment to a naughty child's feet, by which he is hung head downwards. --ʦaṭȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to abuse in a rage (a person or a business).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phālanôwᵘ), causal of phalun 2, to split (a tree, log, or the like) from top to bottom, to tear; to divide into calculated shares, to distribute a number of articles in proper proportions; to wear out (a garment, etc.) by long use. phālanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (phālanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), split; properly shared out; caused to be worn out, as ab.

m. the shutters of a shop as a whole, a complete set of shop-shutters. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to close the shutters of a shop, to shut up shop, to stop the traffic of one's shop (K.Pr. 102, Śiv. 1248). --lagun -- m.inf. the doors of a shop to be shut; met. a house to become empty and deserted by its inhabitants. -püṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -pachĕ), a single shutter, one of the boards which form a set of shop-shutters.

f. (sg. dat. phalāwaṭi), the successful gaining of the intended result of any action or course of conduct. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such an intended successful result to occur without any difficulty or inconvenience to the performer.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phalowᵘ), to split a post or log; cf. phalun 2. phalowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phalüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), split (by some one).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phālowᵘ), to tear, rend, split, cleave (wood) (cf. atha phᵒ, p. 60b, l. 33); to wear out (clothes by wearing them). Cf. phalun 2, of which this is the causal. ¶ phālowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phālüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), split, cloven (by some one); worn out (by some one). ¶ phālavith dyunᵘ m.inf. to divide out, share out; to give after wearing out, i.e. to borrow clothes, wear them out, and then return them.
n.ag. (f. phalavüñᵘ̈), that which bears good fruit (lit. and met.).

n.ag. (f. phalavüñᵘ̈), that which is easily split, that which is ready or fit for being split; that which becomes worn out; that which stands wearing out, that which lasts long. Cf. phalan-hār, s.v. phalun 2.
also written phalai f. (of fruits) the season of fruiting, (of grains) harvest time.
m. (f. phalöñᵘ̈), such a, such-and-such, a certain (man); such a man, such a one, so-and-so, such a thing (El. falán, falãnyi).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. pholᵘ 3 (for 1 and 2, see s.vv.), f. phüjᵘ̈; 2 p.p. phajyōv), to bear fruit (Gr.Gr. 205, L.V. 66); to bear good or plentiful fruit, have a good yield; to have a good result, turn out successfully (e.g. arrangements for defence against injury); to have a good outcome or fulfilment (of an omen, dream, portent, or the like). ¶ pholᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. phüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ 1), that which has borne fruit (esp. good fruit), as ab. ¶ phalith gaʦhun m.inf. to bear fruit or results at once or after a very short time.

conj. 2 (p.p. as in phalun 1. The causal of this verb is phālanāwun, q.v.), to be split from top to bottom, to be split (of a tree-trunk, log, or the like); to be divided into calculated shares, distributed, shared among several people (Gr.Gr. 205); to be split (by use), to become worn out (of e.g. a garment, a metal dish, or an ornament) (cf. atha phalȧnⁱ, p. 60b, l. 30; pād phalȧnⁱ, p. 681a, l. 1; ʦam phalüñᵘ̈, p. 1072a, l. 24.; phĕkⁱ phalȧnⁱ, s.v. phyokᵘ) (Gr.Gr. 174, 205); to become worn away (e.g. the edge of a tool) (K.Pr. 195). ¶ phȧlⁱ phȧlⁱ mahārāza m. wearing out and wearing out (and still) royal; hence (of some garment, ornament, or the like) in good condition though much used. ¶ pholᵘ-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. phüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ 2), split; divided, shared, a shared portion (of something divided); worn out, as ab. ¶ phalan-hār n.ag., c.g. easily split; that which stands wearing out, (of a garment, carpet, vessel, ornament, or the like) that which lasts a long time, lasting, strong, durable.
adj. c.g. one who is distraught, crazy, driven mad (e.g. by grief, loss, poverty). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become crazy, as ab.
f. a small split off piece of timber (dim. of phal 2, q.v.).

(cf. پنبہ) m. (as the first member of a compound this word may become phã or pham), cotton wool (cf. dōñĕ-phᵒ, p. 231b, l. 10; ḍī˜gi-phᵒ, p. 267b, l. 8; jaga-phᵒ, p. 371a, l. 34; khaphari phamb ʦānun, p. 406a, l. 14; phȧtⁱla-phⁱ, s.v. phȧtⁱla) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1610; H. viii, 6, 13; K.Pr. 167); the wool of the Ladākī goat (cf. bŏṭa-phᵒ, p. 138b, l. 24; kĕli-phᵒ, p. 436a, l. 38; phēri-phᵒ, s.v. phyūrᵘ 2) (L. 465, pamb; Rām. 717, 1014, 1613); cotton-like down of plants, catkins (cf. phrasta-phᵒ, s.v. phrast); birds' down or the like (cf. braga-phᵒ, p. 120a, l. 27). ¶ phã-wāl or pham-wāl m. the coarse hair found in cotton wool and discarded before spinning; the coarse hair found mixed in the soft wool of the Ladākī goat, and similarly discarded before spinning. -wôñᵘ m. a seller of the wool of the Ladākī goat. -vüṭᵘ̈ f. a light bale of Ladākī wool (weighing eight to twelve pounds). -watun m. (sg. dat. -watanas), a square sheet of cotton wool (about a span across. It is so prepared after having been opened out and picked clean by the fingers). ¶ pham-phĕran m. a Kāshmīrī coat (see phĕran) wadded with cotton wool (and worn in winter, a quilted coat). -pan m. shawl-thread (El.). ¶ phamba-üṭᵘ̈ f. a long piece of cleaned cotton wool ready for spinning (cf. -māl, bel.). -dạgᵃla m. a wadded quilt or coat (stuffed with cotton wool). -ḍī˜jⁱ or -ḍī˜jᵘ̈ f. a ball of cleaned cotton wool. -dār adj. c.g. stuffed with cotton wool, wadded, quilted. -dastār m. a kind of cap made of pashmīna, i.e. the cloth made from Ladākī wool. -dĕv m. a doll made of cotton wool. -ḍyū̃gᵘ m. a large ball of cleaned cotton wool (Śiv. 589, K.Pr. 136). -māl f. a necklace of cotton wool, i.e. the long piece of cleaned cotton wool ready for spinning (cf. -üṭᵘ̈, ab.). -sīrᵘ̈ f. (at the time of spinning) the piece of cleaned cotton wool (about ten or twelve inches long) held in the hand (cf. -tọ̆mbᵘ); a certain bird (Śiv. 1011, 1694). -thŏs f. as much cleaned cotton wool as can be taken up by the fingers. -thọ̆sᵘ m. as much cotton wool as would form the wick of a lamp or the like. -tọ̆mbᵘ m. the piece of cotton wool held in the fingers of the left hand at the time of spinning (cf. -sīrᵘ̈, ab.). -ṭūpⁱ f. a cap wadded or quilted with cotton wool. -tāsa m. the covered earthen pot in which cleaned cotton wool is kept. -ʦöryunᵘ m. the refuse left in cleaning cotton wool.
m. a noose, snare, trap, gin (for small birds). Cf. phand.

m. mortality, frailty, destruction, death; as adj. passed away, departed, deceased, defunct; non-existent, extinct; cf. phanöyⁱ. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be destroyed, to perish, pass away, vanish; to cease to be, to die. --karun -- m.inf. to destroy, cause to perish, cause to vanish.

m. artifice, deceit, fraud (Rām. 435, 702, 1150); deceiving by magic; falsehood (cf. canj-phanj, p. 173a, l. 31) (Śiv. 277); a foolish or unprofitable speech, vain words; working a puppet- show or the like. phanda-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a swindler, deceiver.

m. a striking, thwacking, beating, bastinado (with fist, sand bag, or stick) (cf. atha-phᵒ, p. 60b, l. 36). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to drub, thrash, beat, bastinado (with fist, club, or sand bag). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to suffer such a drubbing. --karun -- m.inf. to drub, bastinado, as ab. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. such a drubbing or bastinado to befall (a person).
adj. c.g. false, deceitful, fraudulent; one who exhibits magical tricks, or who works a puppet-show.
m. (sg. dat. phandanas), the act of defrauding, cheating, etc.
m. (sg. dat. phanḍanas), the act of beating, thwacking, bastinadoing; beating a carpet or the like to expel the dust.
or phünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. phanjĕ), a calamity, disaster, misfortune (e.g. resulting from royal displeasure, pillage, imprisonment, or the like). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a disaster suddenly to occur.
f. total destruction, i.q. phanā, q.v. phanāyi-mŏgulᵘ m. 'a Mogul of destruction', total destruction (esp. of property which has been collected together), total loss of one's life's savings.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phônᵘ; 2 p.p. phāñōv), to empty entirely (a dish or the like), to carry away everything; to deprive a person of all his property; cf. phöñᵉ̆ran. phônᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phöñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), emptied entirely, deprived of all property, as ab.
m. inarticulateness, stammering, impediment in speech (Gr.Gr. 138).
f. (sg. dat. phạphᵃrüñᵃ), stammering (esp. when put on by one who does not naturally stammer), imitation of stammering.

m. a gambling house, a gambling den. ¶ pharas bĕhun m.inf. to haunt a gambling house, to be addicted to visiting gambling parties, to associate with gamblers. --bĕhawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. bĕhavüñᵘ̈), a spendthrift who wastes his property in gambling houses. --byūṭhᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --bīṭhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), one who is engaged in playing dice in a gambling house; hence, a reckless spendthrift.
f. (sg. dat. pharāgüʦᵘ̈), freedom (from business, care, anxiety, etc.), leisure, ease, convenience, comfort, tranquillity (Śiv. 1304); easy circumstances, competency, affluence. Cf. phārēkh.
adj. c.g. one who habitually indulges in telling false stories. Cf. phᵃr 1.
(? فراسیون) m. Salvia moorcroftiana (El. farásíum and farásium, by which is probably meant the Ar.-Prs. farāsiyūn, translated in the dictionaries by 'wild leek').
n.ag. (f. pharavüñᵘ̈), one who steals, a pilferer; one who secures the results of another's work; one who causes loss or ruin; one who spoils another's project.
adv. to-morrow; next day, on the morrow (H. vi, 11).
m. deception, deceit, fraud, trick, imposture (El. faréb).
adj. c.g. free from care, free from labour or business, at leisure, unoccupied, unemployed, disengaged (Rām. 1736). Cf. pharāgath.
f. an old bawd. (So in Kāshmīrī. In Persian it is the name of a man, whose mistress was Shirīn, and who to please her dug through an immense mountain.)
m. a Frank; a European, a Portuguese, an Englishman (K.Pr. 169 pharhung).
(f. pharhünjᵘ̈), European, of, or belonging to, Europe, etc. Cf. the preceding.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pharkôwᵘ), to expose for testing, to expose for publication; to enquire into the meaning (of anything). pharkôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pharkövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), exposed or published for examination, advertised.

f. (sg. dat. pharki), separation, intervening space, interval; distinction, difference, discrepancy (Śiv. 647, f.; El. makes this word m.). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. deficiency to occur. --nērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a deficiency to issue, a discrepancy to be found. --rōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a difference or discrepancy to remain as a result. --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause a discrepancy, to prove a discrepancy; to differ (El.).
adj. c.g. approximate, more or less. Cf. pharkh.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phorkᵘ, f. phürkᵘ̈, not phürcᵘ̈), to test, put to the test, to examine, to compare, contrast. ¶ phorkᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phürkᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), tested, examined; compared. ¶ pharkan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who puts forward something for comparison, one who proclaims something as excellent, one who advertises; that of which the virtues become widely known; worthy of being widely known.

(in Persian), adj. c.g., excellent, strong; (in Kāshmīrī) a kind of fine paper highly glazed. It is the best quality made in the Valley. The second quality is called Dahmashtī, and the third quality Kalamdönī (p. 439b, l. 38) (L. 380).
m. a seller. Used --˚ (as in lāl-phᵒ, p. 522a, l. 21) (H. xii, 3).
? m. haste, hurry, quickness, expedition. --karān -- adv. hurriedly, hastily.
adj. c.g. a gabbler, one who speaks rapidly and without restraint, a jabberer.
adj. (f. pharphüshᵘ̈ or pharphȧshⁱ), heedless, careless, unobservant, off-hand, scatter-brained.
m. a carpet, mat, floor-cloth (Śiv. 965, 1084; Rām. 571); a mattress, bedding (Śiv. 575, 1825); pharsh-ĕ- ārām, a mattress of peace, a couch of happiness (Rām. 1060).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. phorᵘ), secret theft to occur (to some one), to have one's property pilfered (Gr.Gr. 174, 204; K.Pr. 125); secretly to help oneself to the results of another's success; to be a cause of loss or ruin (cf. atha pharȧnⁱ, p. 60b, l. 37, and marg pharun, p. 590b, l. 14) (Gr.Gr. 174, 204; Śiv. 170; Rām. 280, 1154, 1587-8; K. 551, 883; H. iv, 2); to commit a fault, be a sinner (Rām. 1702); to be a cause of want of success, to have a project spoiled. ¶ phorᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), one who has secretly carried out a theft, caused loss, etc. ¶ paran-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who habitually commits theft, causes ruin or loss, etc., as ab.

or phȧrⁱyād m. a complaint (El. faryád, f.; Rām. 338, 939); pitiful lamentation (to another) (Rām. 1491, 1496). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to weep aloud, to complain (El. f., Rām. 417); to bring a complaint in a court of justice (H. x, 2); to call for help, cry for redress (Rām. 381; H. vii, 22); to utter a challenge (Rām. 491). --karun -- m.inf. to complain (El. f.); to lament (Rām. 1356, 1540). --lāyun -- m.inf. to lament (Rām. 183, 465, 1536). --tulun -- m.inf. to raise an outcry, to cry out in terror, fear, grief, or the like (Rām. 445). --trāwun -- m.inf. to utter laments (Rām. 875).
or phȧrⁱyödī m. a complainant, a plaintiff (El. faryódí, a defendant, a probable slip of the pen); a petitioner, a complainer (Rām. 675).

m. (f. phariñᵘ̈), one who commits secret thefts, a pilferer (Gr.Gr. 120, K.Pr. 132); one who causes loss or ruin; one who spoils work undertaken or a project. ¶ phariñᵘ̈ phö m. the name used in schools for the Śāradā form of the Nāgarī letter pha.

or phȧryushᵘ adj. (f. phȧrⁱshⁱ or phȧrishᵘ̈), rough, rugged, hard (lit. and met.) (cf. atha-phᵒ, p. 64a, l. 13); harsh, cruel, unkind, (of language) cutting; hard, difficult to understand, intricate; difficult (to do) (K.Pr. 136, parisuī for pharyushuy). phȧrⁱshĕ- kã̄ḍ hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -kã̄ḍ hishᵘ̈), (of a vegetable) tough and rough (even after cooking). -kāl m. hard times, dearth, scarcity.
m. a single (person or thing); a single sheet or piece of paper, a leaf.
or pharᵘ̈dᵘ̈ (cf. فردی) f. a roll, catalogue; (in Kāshmīrī) a wrapper of pashmīna cloth.
