m. roughness, ruggedness, hardness (cf. atha-phᵒ, p. 60b, l. 49) (Gr.Gr. 138); harshness, cruelty, unkindness; hardness, difficulty in being understood, intricacy; famine, want due to scarcity, hard times, dearth. --tulun -- m.inf. to raise a famine (by not taking precautions against want of rain or other agricultural calamities, allowing too free export of grain, or other causes of the high price of food). --wŏthun -- m.inf. a famine suddenly to come on (due to failure of crops).

m. a splitting open, tearing open; mutual hostility (esp. when secret), discord (Gr.Gr. 148). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to split open (e.g. a fish for cleaning). --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to cause mutual hostility (by slandering, etc.), to set at odds, embroil.

m. corruptness, unsoundness, wrongness, wickedness, viciousness, depravity, iniquity (Rām. 1497); disorder, disturbance, mischief, violence, waste, ruin, sedition, rebellion, war; disagreement, discord, dissension, strife, quarrelling, quarrel, brawl. --karun -- m.inf. to start a quarrel over some special cause (between oneself and someone). --tulun -- m.inf. to begin a quarrel (with someone). --wŏthun -- m.inf. a quarrel or dispute to arise over some special cause. ¶ phasāda-gorᵘ m. (f. -gariñ), a quarrel-manufacturer, one who sets people quarrelling (by insinuations, slander, or the like).
m. a tale, fiction, romance; (false) vaunting, gasconade, rodomontade (Rām. 1405).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phasanôwᵘ), i.q. phạsᵃrāwun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 174).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phāsowᵘ), to split open, tear open; to net (an opponent), to bring a member of an opponent's party over to one's own side (in order to learn the other party's secrets), to suborn a traitor, to win over; cf. phösᵃrāwun. phāsowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phāsüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), split open, etc., as ab.; won over, as ab.

adj. c.g. spread abroad, divulged, apparent, manifest, palpable, gross; (in Kāshmīrī) subst. m. abuse (esp. abuse charging a respectable woman with unchastity). --karun -- m.inf. to divulge (dat.) (Rām. 194; H. xii, 7). --parȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to abuse (esp. to abuse a man by making charges against his female relatives) (Rām. 965).

m. fashionable appearance, the being well-dressed, elegance of apparel (cf. masta-phᵒ, p. 601a, l. 1); cleanness, brightness (Gr.Gr. 134); cf. phīs. -gash m. devotion to elegant apparel, etc., foppishness.
m. a violent wind-storm, a cyclone; madness, lunacy, eccentricity, craziness (cf. mȧtⁱ-phⁱ, p. 602a, l. 46; pitᵃ̇rᵃ̇-phᵃ̇, s.v. pitur 2) (Gr.Gr. 135).

m. sweeping, sweeping away (dust, etc.) (cf. ḍuwan-phᵒ, p. 262a, l. 43) (K.Pr. 119); wiping out (writing, a painting, etc.), erasure (cf. atha-phᵒ, p. 61a, l. 22, and phēsh); wiping out, dispersing (a crowd), dissipating (anything collected); 'leeping,' plastering (the ground with mud or cowdung) (cf. brā̃d-phᵒ, p. 119b, l. 11; liwan-phᵒ, p. 542a, l. 24); stroking, rubbing the limbs, rubbing (to allay itching, etc.) (cf. kashĕn-phᵒ, p. 481a, l. 47; mŏṭhi-phᵒ, p. 604b, l. 1) (K.Pr. 111); slightly applying anything, slightly performing any operation (cf. lahawan-phᵒ, p. 516a, l. 47; tawan-phᵒ, p. 1046b, l. 47). --anun -- m.inf. to wipe out; destroy; to stop some work. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to sweep (away dirt, etc.), to wipe out, erase; to wipe out, destroy, dissipate, as ab.; to plaster (the ground); to stroke; to brush (the hair) (cf. phash 1 and masta-phᵒ, p. 601a, l. 1). --karun -- m.inf. to rub (dat.) (Rām. 1293, 1367). --phash dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give rubbings (to), to keep rubbing (dat.) (Rām. 910). ¶ phashĕ-kônᵘ m. utter destruction, wiping out of existence (cf. kônᵘ 1). -nāv f. 'a boat of destruction', wiping away, dissipating or destroying a collection of articles.
adj. c.g. one accustomed to wearing fashionable clothes, a dandy, a fop, well-dressed (Gr.Gr. 134).

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. phashĕladiñ), one who is mad, lunatic, eccentric, silly, crazy, one who acts contrary to custom in a crazy way (Gr.Gr. 135); one who is taken in, made a fool of (at a dinner party by making away with his food, drink, or the like); cf. phash 2. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be taken in, as ab. --karun -- m.inf. to take in a guest, as ab.
m. acting like a lunatic, acting (even when warned) against custom, craziness, eccentricity.

adj. c.g. wicked, vicious, mischievous; factious, seditious, rebellious, turbulent, quarrelsome; a vicious or mischievous person, one who sets others quarrelling (by slander or the like); a turbulent fellow, a quarrelsome person, a brawler (Rām. 678).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. phosᵘ; 2 p.p. phasōv), to be (or become) noosed, ensnared, entrapped, caught (Gr.Gr. 205); to be entangled, to stick (as in mud, or a narrow passage). The causal of this verb is phasanāwun or phạsᵃrāwun (Gr.Gr. 174). phosᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. phüsᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), noosed, ensnared, caught; entangled, stuck, as ab.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. phosᵘ; 2 p.p. phasōv), to become opened, split open, dismembered, made tender (e.g. by pounding or by cooking), to be boiled to rags. phosᵘ-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. phüsᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), broken up, made tender, as ab.
m. (f. phösᵃrĕñ), one who causes hostility between mutual friends (by slander or the like), one who sets people at odds, an embroiler (Gr.Gr. 148). Cf. phās.
f. (sg. dat. phạsᵃrüñᵃ), noosing, entangling, catching, trapping; entangling (a person in some unpleasant work or business), inveigling, involving, implicating.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phạsᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. phạsᵃrun 1, q.v. (cf. atha phᵒ, p. 61a, l. 29) (Gr.Gr. 174).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phạsᵒrᵒ), to noose, entangle, catch, trap (Gr.Gr. 7); to entangle (a person in some unpleasant work or business), to inveigle, involve, implicate; cf. phösᵃrun, phösᵃrāwun. phạsᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. phạsᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), entangled, etc. (by some one); inveigled, involved, etc. (by some one).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phạsᵒrᵒ), to make tender by cooking, to boil to rags. phạsᵒrᵒ-motᵒ 2 perf. part. (f. phạsᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), boiled to rags, etc., as ab.

m. in the following:-- phaṭa-phaṭa āsun m.inf. great pride to occur (on account of some small amount of wealth, knowledge, talent, or the like), to have an overweening opinion of oneself, to give oneself airs for a petty reason, to show foolish pretensions, be puffed up. -phaṭa karun m.inf. to show such unfounded pride. -phaṭa karawunᵘ n.ag. (f. -phaṭa karavüñᵘ̈), one who shows such pride (esp. said of a young fellow full of self-conceit); (of a clever fellow), one who prides himself on some newly-acquired knowlege. -phaṭa lagun m.inf. such pride to be felt (by a person unworthy of showing it).

in phāta-kŏnḍal f. a draggle-tail woman, a sloven, a slut, a dowdy (a dirty woman who habitually acts like a beggar woman, going about in dirty worn-out clothes, even if she need not). phāta-müʦᵘ̈ f., id. -phȧkⁱröñⁱ f., id.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phāṭanôwᵘ), to cleave, to split (El., Gr.Gr. 171); to plunge into, to immerse, drown (something) (Śiv. 1755). Cf. phāṭawun and phaṭun.
m. sapless, pithless, outwardly fine or prosperous but worthless within.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phāṭowᵘ), to cause to burst, to burst (something), to split (cf. bôsᵘ phᵒ, p. 132a, l. 8) (Gr.Gr. 171, K.Pr. 164); (of clouds of smoke, extreme heat) to distress (a person by compelling him to hold his breath); to plunge (something into water). Cf. phāṭanāwun. ¶ phāṭawan-wād m. causing annoyance by remaining silent, holding one's tongue in spite of entreaties. ¶ phāṭowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phāṭüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), split (by some one); distressed (by having to hold one's breath); plunged (by some one into water).

n.ag. (f. phaṭavüñᵘ̈), that which is being split; that which is ready to be split, or which is fit to be split; that which is sprouting, shooting, germinating (of a seed or the like); that which is plunged or being plunged into water; he who is plunged into disgrace (by bad conduct or the like); sinkable, of high specific gravity, that which will not float, heavy.
m. an apricot (El., borrowed from Ladakhī pha-tiṅ).
in phaṭh-kār m. reproach, censure, vocal blame. --kārun -- m.inf. to reproach, censure. --kôrᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --körᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), reproached, censured.
m. (sg. dat. phāṭas), in phāṭh karun m.inf. to split (something), to tear asunder down the middle (something long, such as a wooden post or the like).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. phoṭᵘ, f. phacĕ, Gr.Gr. 209; 2 p.p. phacyōv, Gr.Gr. 225), to be torn, to be split, to crack, burst, break, be torn, be rent (cf. ȧchⁱ phaṭañĕ, p. 8b, l. 8; atha phaṭȧnⁱ, p. 61a, l. 32; bôgᵘ phaṭun, p. 132a, l. 5; gagᵘ̈rᵘ̈ phaṭüñᵘ̈, p. 280a, l. 25; lāy phaṭüñᵘ̈, p. 543a, l. 29; naphᵃʦ phᵒ, p. 645b, l. 15; phĕl phᵒ, p. 693a, l. 35; pōna phaṭüñᵘ̈, s.v. pōna) (Gr.Gr. 30, 171, 204, 209, 225; Gr.M.; W. 142; K. 381, 1114; H. x, 12; YZ. 150; K.Pr. 80, 170); to show the mark of a crack (between two pieces joined together); ¶ to burst forth in large numbers (e.g. a crop of boils) (cf. phĕl phaṭȧnⁱ, p. 693a, l. 33); to sprout, shoot, germinate (cf. ḍambi phᵒ, p. 218a, l. 25; lĕmbi pampōsh phᵒ, p. 524b, l. 21) (Gr.Gr. 204, W. 146, Śiv. 1023); to burst open (as corn in roasting); to burṡt forth, spout out (as through an opened aperture) (K. 195, 237; K.Pr. 165, 255); to burst (with joy, pride, or the like) (cf. pī˜ʦhi phᵒ, s.v. pī˜ʦh); ¶ to be immersed, to sink, drown, be plunged (into) (Gr.Gr. 5, 9, 10, 204; Gr.M.; Śiv. 707, 1569, 1833; K. 488); to be plunged (into debauchery, bad conduct, or the like); to be stuck (in mud) (Gr.M.). ¶ phaṭun lāyĕkh adj. (f. phaṭüñᵘ̈ lāyĕkh), (used in reproach or cursing) worthy of being split or drowned, fit to be destroyed. ¶ phȧṭⁱ phȧṭⁱ nērun m.inf. to become bold, impudent, rude, insolent; to become profligate, abandoned. ¶ phoṭᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phüṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), split, cracked; sprouted; plunged (into deep water), drowned (K. 488); met. plunged (into debauchery, bad conduct). ¶ phaṭān phrāṭān  adv. splitting (the difference); hence, finally, ultimately, at the end of it all (u.w. vbs. indicating the conclusion or arbitrament of a quarrel, dispute, or the like). Cf. phrāṭh. ¶ phaṭith bĕhun m.inf. to burst and collapse (e.g. an over-full sack) (K.Pr. 158). --drāmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --drāmüʦᵘ̈ --), sprouted, germinated; sprouted, issued forth, become manifest, become famous; issued forth (from rule), gone beyond bounds, run riot, run wild. --nērun -- m.inf. to sprout, germinate; to sprout, issue forth, become manifest, become famous (Śiv. 25); to burst forth, issue forth violently (Rām. 728, 1406, 1613); to issue forth (from rule), to go beyond bounds, run riot, run wild. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to burst open (e.g. a full bag or case from a sudden blow); to burst, pop (as grain in roasting); to burst forth, become dissipated, fling oneself into debauchery; to burst forth, be thrust out (āyĕs phaṭith zĕv, his tongue burst forth (from his mouth, when knocked down senseless), Rām. 483); to put out (the tongue in thirst, fatigue, shame, etc.) (Rām. 1091).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phỗṭᵘ, f. phö̃ṭᵘ̈, dat. phã̄cĕ; 2 p.p. phã̄cyōv), to clean the interior by the application of fire (e.g. of a vessel which has formerly contained clarified butter, oil, or other greasy substance). phỗṭᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phö̃ṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), cleaned out by fire, as ab.

or phatah or phatih m. victory, conquest, triumph (El. fatah); used as a proper name; esp. derisively as a pompous title (K.Pr. 169). So phatih pharȧngⁱ, 'Mr. Englishman,' a caricatured Englishman (K.Pr. id.). -kạdᵃl m. N. of a bridge over the Jehlam in Śrīnagar (El.); -mand فتحمند adj. c.g. victorious, triumphant (El. fatahmand).

f. (sg. dat. phatᵃrüʦᵃ), languor, debility; (in Kāshmīrī) weariness, distress, trouble, worry (preceding, or during the carrying out of any work or business, and so rendering its completion difficult). --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. deliberately to cause such trouble or weariness. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such trouble or weariness to be incurred (e.g. in searching for something lost, whether it be found or not). ¶ phatᵃrüʦᵃ-dār adj. c.g. (of a work or business) full of worry, difficult to accomplish without much labour.

m. a thick kind of lamp-wick (made of cotton rolled between the palms of the hands). -khọ̆bᵘ m. a kind of quilted cap worn in the cold weather, in which the quilting is stuffed with wick-like rolls of cotton; cf. -ṭūpⁱ, bel. -koshᵘ m. one whose profession it is to make the cotton-rolls for these hats. -phamb m. cotton suitable for making lamp-wicks; cotton which is obtained by teasing out a lamp-wick. -ṭūpⁱ f., i.q. -khọ̆bᵘ, ab.

or phōj m. or f. an army (El. m.; Śiv. 482, f.; Rām. 693, 793, 854, 859, 1100, 1396, 1440, 1444, m.); a flock, herd, troop (Śiv. 1860). phōj-dar-phōj فوج در فوج adv. in troops, in multitudes (Rām. 570). phōja-lashkar, for فوج و لشکر f. army and host, a mighty host (Rām. 695).

m. a syringe or pipe for distributing a high shower of water from a ground-level reservoir in a garden, etc. --wŏthȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. a shower of water from such a machine to spout out; (blood) to spout out (from a wound, etc.).
f. disgrace, shame, ignominy, infamy. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to disgrace, put to shame, rebuke (El.). Cf. phṻzĕth.

m. excess, exuberance; increase, gain; superiority, excellence; a free gift, grace, bounty, favour. --banun -- m.inf. mercy to come into existence (i.e. in the immediate presence of calamity), salvation to come, to be saved by the skin of the teeth. --karun -- m.inf. to be gracious (to), to show mercy or favour (to), to deal bountifully (with); to save (a person) faced by immediate calamity, to save by the skin of the teeth.
m. one whose face has no hair on it except for a thin, scraggy, tail-like beard.

f. (sg. dat. phaʦi), weak, thin, fine, easily torn cloth, fine muslin (with holes in it like net); a thin, scraggy, tail-like beard (unaccompanied by moustache or whiskers) (cf. phë̆ʦᵘ̈ and phĕʦh); the smaller of the two holes into which walnuts are thrown in the children's game called mīri mīri phaʦh. The larger hole is called mīr (cf. mīr 2 and (for an account of the game) K.Pr. 142, Śiv. 1015).
m. a very small lump of flesh; met. a small thin penis.
m. a small piece of hard tripe, tough even after cooking.
f. a small thin strip of meat or vegetables, tough even after cooking.
m. anxious thirst or longing for something lost, disappeared, or unobtainable, just when it is required. --barun -- m.inf. to suffer such longing. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to display such longing.

f. (sg. dat. phĕki), powder, dust (cf. mardi- or marēdi-phᵒ, p. 589b, l. 50; nāsti-phᵒ, p. 659a, l. 2; nīli-phᵒ, p. 670b, l. 36); hence, a very small amount of anything (cf. dā̃-phᵒ, p. 230b, l. 2). ¶ phĕka-dawāh m. powder-medicine, medicine in the form of powder or dust. -nūn m. powdered salt, salt powder. -wād m. one employed in a business dealing with very small quantities, a petty dealer.

m. a certain poisonous kind of boil, a carbuncle, a bubo or cancer (cf. dada-phᵒ, p. 187b, l. 42; ḍȧmbⁱ-phⁱ, p. 218a, l. 17; kāñi-phᵒ, p. 460b, l. 40). --phaṭȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. a crop of carbuncles to appear on a person. --phaṭun -- m.inf. a carbuncle to burst. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. a carbuncle to appear (on a person). ¶ phĕla-cār m. 'the wringing of a carbuncle', the agony caused by it before it bursts or is opened. -dag f. the pain of a carbuncle. -gŏgᵃ̇jᵃ̇ or -gŏgᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. the core of a carbuncle, the hard knotty lump felt inside one. -gar m. a bubo-like swelling in the armpit, hollow of the knee, or similar place, that accompanies a carbuncle; cf. ganḍ. -grüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -gracĕ), the hard core of a boil, etc. -gāsa m. a certain medicinal plant; the long leaves are applied to bubos, etc., to hasten the ripening. -hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), a kind of vegetable described as having a long thick stalk and thorny leaves. -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), suffering from a carbuncle. -wödᵘ̈ m. a carbuncle doctor, a man whose profession it is to cure boils and the like. ¶ phĕlas dĕl khĕwawunᵘ n.ag. (f. --khĕwavüñᵘ̈ --), 'one who would eat the skin of a carbuncle,' one who leads a miserly life and is filled with foul desires, a mean swindler (cf. K.Pr. 169, where it is wrongly translated).

m. an act, action, deed; esp. a shameful deed, a crime (Gr.Gr. 21); a trick (Gr.Gr. 21). --bāz فعل باز adj. c.g. one (esp. a boy) who habitually and openly does evil actions, mischievous, naughty; a cheat. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. an evil action or crime suddenly to happen. --karun -- m.inf. to commit a crime.

f. the distress displayed by a nursling child when crying (e.g. for its nurse, etc.); distress felt by oneself when calling out, lamenting, or speaking, and failing to get an answer, or one's demand satisfied. --barüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to experience such distress (e.g. when experienced by a child crying for its nurse, or by a starving or lamenting person whose requests are disregarded). --khārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to distress a person, as ab. --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such distress to arise.
in phĕnḍa-shöjᵘ̈ f. a female jackal cub. Cf. phĕnḍᵘ̈rᵘ̈.
f. a fair maiden, a pretty unmarried girl. Cf. phĕnḍ.

m. great lamentation (for something lost, damaged, or the like, in the hope that someone will be moved to restore it or make the loss good); cf. zār 1. --barȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to utter loud lamentations, as ab. --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to give forth such lamentations, to continue making them without cessation.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. phĕpharladiñ), afflicted by a boil or boils.
m. a naughty, impudent, disobedient boy.

m. (sg. dat. phĕpharas), a boil (on the body), an abscess, a pimple (cf. khashĕrⁱ-phⁱ, p. 419b, l. 10; pāka-phᵒ, s.v. pākh 1; pĕta-phᵒ, s.v. pĕth 2) (El.; W. 144, phephara, pl. nom.; L. 458, fafar; K.Pr. 111). ¶ phĕphar-dag f. the pain of a boil or abscess; similar pain caused by a cut, distress of mind, or the like. -vĕphar m. (? pl.) an abscess, a pimple (El. phephar-wephar).

m. (sg. abl. phōri 2; for 1, see phīrᵘ̈), moving about, roaming, wandering, strolling (cf. dōri-phᵒ, p. 239b, l. 26); turning round, circular motion, rotation; turning round, change (cf. nāwa-phᵒ, s.v. nāv 1) (Śiv. 61); an error, mistake, blunder. -dār adj. c.g. doubtful, suspicious, hesitating; containing errors (in a calculation or the like). --gēra -- m. walking round and round (some place or thing), surrounding on all sides. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. a mistake to occur. -kôlᵘ mēlun m.inf. a mistake to happen (at the start of any action), to make a wrong start; cf. phira-kôlᵘ mēlun, s.v. phir. -kôlᵘ gaʦhun m.inf. a mistake to arise. --karun -- m.inf. to do coming and going, to walk backwards and forwards; to cause mistakes, lead wrong (in calculation), cheat a person in accounting. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. a cause of dispute, due to a mistake, to arise between two people. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), unobstructed (by error, inconsistency, ignorance, or the like). --thawun -- m.inf. to settle a discrepancy (in a calculation). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. an obstruction to occur (in some business). ¶ phēri drāv adj. c.g. (of a boy) come home from wandering about; passed through (the circle of business); hence, one who has become skilled in commercial pursuits. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go on the round, to go round and round a field or garden of ripe produce in order to watch it.

m. a kind of dress, the usual garment worn by Kāshmīrīs, in shape like a night-gown with wide sleeves, and worn both by men and women (the only difference being that that worn by women has wider sleeves). When made of wool it is called lôchᵘ, and when made of cotton it is called pôʦhᵘ, qq.v. (see El. s.v.) (cf. mal-phᵒ, p. 564a, l. 12; marda-phᵒ, p. 589b, l. 27; pham-phᵒ, p. 698a, l. 22; phirith pheran ʦhunun, p. 707b, l. 26; pōshĕ-phᵒ, s.v. pōsh 1; pata phᵒ, s.v. path 3) (Gr.M.; L. 464; W. 3; K. 270, 272-3; YZ. 8, 126, 194, 440, 462; K.Pr. 126, 129, 169, 180, 204). -janda m. an old patched phĕran. -jōr m. a double phĕran, i.e. two, one inside the other, sewn together. The outer is usually of woollen cloth and the inner of cotton. -palav m. a worn out, too small, phĕran. --pairāwun -- m.inf. to put clothes on (a person, dat.), to clothe (Gr.M.). -shikhurᵘ m. a rag of a phĕran, a dirty tattered phĕran. -züṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. zacĕ), a tattered phĕran.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phēranôwᵘ), to turn (some one or something), to turn round, to circulate; to cause to wander, to set wandering (Rām. 1321, K. 132).

n.ag. (f. phēravüñᵘ̈), one who wanders about (Śiv. 160, 1755; Rām. 96, 1255); one who habitually reverses his conduct, etc., or turns back; one who avoids doing work to which he has agreed; one who goes on vacation.
in aki pheri (W. 95) for aki phiri, see phyurᵘ 1.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. phyūrᵘ 1, f. phīrᵘ̈; 2 p.p. phēryōv, for phyūrᵘ 2, see s.v. The transitive form of this verb is phirun, q.v.), to return, come back (to a place) (cf. pānas phᵒ, s.v. pāna); path phᵒ, s.v. path 1 (L.V. 51, 89; Śiv, 1709, 1790, 1836; Rām. 207, 946, 1577; K. 208, 359, 515, 633, 646, 882-3, 1018); to come back (to one's senses) (L.V. 89; K. 413, 659, 663); (with path-kun) to go back, retreat (Rām. 1345); to revolve, go round (cf. carkh phᵒ, p. 174b, l. 29; lari phᵒ, p. 529b, l. 20) (Gr.Gr. 21, 174, 204, 207; Śiv. 1828; K. 563); ¶ to wander about, ramble, travel about (cf. bölⁱ phᵒ, p. 104a, l. 20; ḍēra phᵒ, p. 236b, l. 16; nayĕn phᵒ, p. 670a, l. 2; phū̃ki-phᵒ, p. 689b, l. 30) (Gr.Gr. 15; Gr.M.; Śiv. 586, 598, 889, 948, 999, 1024, 1082, 1181, 1388, 1428, 1440, 1450, 1571, 1682, 1862; Rām. 44, 456, 550, 641, 1424, 1427, 1559, 1693; K. 106, 122-3, 146, 149, 151, 186, 195, 208, 217, 282, etc.; H. i, 2; ii, 5; YZ. 40, 89, 541-2); to be tossed up and down, put down and taken up (cf. ḍū̃gi phᵒ, p. 195a, l. 9); ¶ to walk round (anything) (cf. ȧndⁱ phᵒ, p. 31b, l. 23; charka phᵒ, p. 174b, l. 33) (Śiv. 322, 1166, 1567, 1609; Rām. 88, 1077, 1333, 1339); ¶ to be reversed, turned back to front, inverted (cf. atha phērȧnⁱ, p. 60b, l. 41; duba phērun, p. 183a, l. 23; döv phᵒ, p. 362a, l. 25; man phᵒ, p. 572a, l. 11) (Gr.Gr. 204; Rām. 278, 315); to be done backwards; to turn oneself (towards, kun), to become at length favourable (to, kun) (Rām. 1275); lari (or larĕ) phᵒ, to roll over (see p. 529b, l. 20) (Śiv. 1236, 1286); to have one's back turned to something, to be turned away (from, dat.) (potᵘ phᵒ, to desist (from), see potᵘ) (Rām. 843; H. v, 4); to be reversed (of a wish), a wish to work contrariwise (Rām. 847); to turn from a promise, break a promise (K.Pr. 256); to be turned back (e.g. the edge of a cutting tool) (cf. dāra phērañĕ, p. 235b, l. 8); ¶ to be circulated, to spread abroad, spread over (something) (cf. nījĕr phᵒ, p. 627a, l. 16; nāma- pögām phᵒ, p. 636b, l. 33) (Rām. 632, K. 924); to come into action as a change, begin to take effect (cf. maitun phᵒ, p. 607b, l. 13; nas-ʦüṭᵘ̈ phērüñᵘ̈, p. 654b, l. 14; prañĕr phᵒ, s.v. prañĕr; pay phᵒ, s.vv. pay 1 and 2) (Rām. 1363, 1763; K. 474, murʦhā phērüñᵘ̈, swooning to come on); ¶ (of a tool, weapon, etc.) to be plied (Rām. 919); to be upset (of liquid) over anything (K.Pr. 11); ¶ to cease from work, take a holiday (L.V. 12); ¶ (of food) to go bad, become corrupt, to rot (Gr.Gr. 204); to become changed (cf. ȧchⁱ phērañĕ, p. 8b, l. 2; mañĕ phērañĕ, p. 586a, l. 1; marwāna phᵒ, p. 595a, l. 4); regret to arise (cf. lōṭh pᵒ, p. 537b, l. 42) (Gr.Gr. 204; Śiv. 574-5, 838, 841; H. viii, 1, 7, 10). ¶ phērun thōrun m.inf. to saunter about (instead of doing one's duty), to play truant (Śiv. 326). Cf. phyurᵘ thurᵘ, s.v. phyurᵘ 2. ¶ phēran-dŏh m. a day on which no work is done, an office holiday. -kal f. (esp. of a child) wasting one's time running about (instead of going to school, etc.), playing truant, idling (when one should be at one's lessons). --pĕd -- f. (sg. dat. --pë̆zᵘ̈ --), a liking or propensity for playing truant, as ab. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who wanders about; one who turns back (from something begun); one who breaks his promise, one who (when the time comes) does not adhere to an agreement, one who changes his mind. ¶ phīrⁱ phīrⁱ freq. part., used as adv. again and again (Śiv. 1222, Rām. 1168, K. 1129). ¶ phīrith conj. part. having turned, etc., often used as adv. in the sense of 'back again', 'over again', as in āv phīrith tayār karana, (the house) was rebuilt (Gr.M.; L.V. 51, 89; Śiv. 1035); back again, in return (K. 822); often used in reporting a conversation, to mean 'in reply'; see phīrith dapun, bel. (K. 1105) and potᵘ phīrith, s.v. potᵘ. --anun -- m.inf. to bring back (Gr.M.). --dapun -- m.inf. to speak back, to speak in reply, to answer (Śiv. 80; Rām. 356, 360, 681, 811; K. 581; H. iii, 1, 8; v, 4, 5, 6, 8, 11, etc.). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give back, return, refund (Gr.M., K. 770). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to turn back, go away from (a place), return home (Rām. 484, 953, 1004, 1179, 1566; K. 685, 864); to retreat; to turn away from; to become hostile (cf. atha phīrith gaʦhȧnⁱ, p. 61a, l. 1) (H. iv, 3). --ladun -- m.inf. to send back (e.g. a message in reply) (H. x, 3). --nērun -- m.inf. to go forth back again (H. x, 14; xii, 19). --sōzun -- m.inf. to send back, to send home (Rām. 304). --wanun -- m.inf., i.q. --dapun, ab. (Śiv. 394, Rām. 1385; H. v, 2, 4; x, 7). --wasun -- m.inf. to come down again (e.g. after going upstairs) (H. iii, 9). --wŏthun -- m.inf. to rise back again, equivalent to our 'to up and answer' (H. viii, 6; x, 2, 6; xii, 11). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come back, return, come home (Gr.M.; Śiv. 97; Rām. 1541; K. 226, 308, 391, 706, 1060; H. ii, 3; v, 1, 4, 10; viii, 10; YZ. 138, 178, 416); to pay a circuit of visits, to go from house to house (prath garas) (K. 147). ¶ phyūrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phīrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), turned back, inverted, crooked; returned, come back, come home; one who has changed his mind; turned (to), inclined (to, kun); gone bad (of food, etc.); come back (to life). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take back (El.). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come back, return (El.).

m. licking; wiping out, erasing (writing, a painting, etc.) (cf. atha-phᵒ, p. 61a, l. 24, and phash 3); putting a stop to any work which is on the point of success. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to wipe out, as ab.; to put a stop to any work on the point of success; to lick (cf. phēshun) (Rām. 398, 1174, 1393). --lagun -- m.inf. wiping out, as ab., to occur (to anything); (of some work on the point of being successfully completed) to be completely stopped.

or phĕshil adj. c.g. unlucky, bringing or indicating bad luck, ill-omened, sinister, detrimental (cf. pōna-phᵒ, s.v. pōn) (K.Pr. 96). --buthᵘ -- m. an unlucky face, i.e. the sight of something unlucky (seen the first thing in the day); a man with an unlucky face (the sight of which brings bad luck); cf. buthⁱ-phⁱ, p. 142b, l. 34. --kā̃dᵃr -- m. 'a baker who bakes ill-luck', one who at inopportune times (e.g. on a festive occasion) talks about unlucky subjects. --kā̃daryunᵘ wān -- m. an assembly or party of people engaged in ill-omened talk; a country full of such people, or a place where such people assemble. --küṭᵘ̈ -- f. (sg. dat. --kacĕ --), an ill-omened daughter, a daughter who brings bad luck. --kaṭh -- m. (sg. dat. --kaṭas --), a son who brings bad luck. --zang -- f. an ill omen, an omen prognosticating bad luck.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phēshĕnôwᵘ), to distress a person, to make a person distraught, esp. to tantalize; cf. phĕshun. phēshĕnôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (phēshĕnövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), tantalized, etc., as ab.
n.ag. (f. phēshĕvüñᵘ̈), one who exhibits distress or tantalization by licking his lips (cf. phĕshun).

or phēshun conj. 1 (1 p.p. phyoshᵘ or phyūshᵘ; 2 p.p. phĕshyōv or phēshyōv), to lick the lips (in thirst, fear, anxiety, etc.); to do this as a habit (cf. atha phēshȧnⁱ, to bite or wring the hands in token of regret, p. 61a, l. 27) (Rām. 1708); to be much distraught (indicating the fact, as ab.), to be tantalized.

or phī˜ṭun m. sg. dat. phē̃(phī˜)ṭanas ), a kind of small turban (esp. one meagre and worn out) (cf. dastār-phᵒ, p. 256b, l. 26) (K.Pr. 119); a small cloth (cf. dajĕ-phᵒ, p. 203a, l. 37). Cf. phī˜tun.

f. (sg. dat. phĕci), so much fine powder as can be taken up by the finger-tips, e.g. a pinch of snuff (K.Pr. 218); cf. phyoṭᵘ and phyokᵘ 2. phĕciʦᵘtⁱldᵉdᵒtdᵒtʦᵘtⁱldᵉdᵒtdᵒt m. great wealth which should be employed liberally, but which is employed in beggarly pinches.

f. (sg. dat. phĕci), bad news, false scandal, scandalous gossip, calumny, evil report provoking mutual quarrelling, mutual fear, pain, distress, grief, or interfering with success (cf. khŏḍa-phᵒ, p. 392b, l. 8). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such false information to be heard. --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to spread or whisper such false information, to utter scandalous gossip. --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause fear, pain, distress, grief, quarrelling, injury to another's work, etc., by such false scandal.

m. making a sound indicating ridicule (with the intention of making some one angry); a certain hunting animal which is said to follow a lion and to indicate its passage by a low growl, ? a porcupine (cf. lōh and pŏʦha- lôwᵘ; but El. phú, a dog, and loh, a fox).
adj. c.g. fringed (of a turban, shawl, or the like), having long fringes; wearing long-fringed apparel.
adj. c.g. (of a cloak, turban, or the like) fringed, possessing a long fringe; (of a human being) wearing long-fringed clothes.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phĕʦowᵘ), to take secretly, carry off secretly (Gr.Gr. li).
f. (sg. dat. phĕʦi), a thin, tail-like, scraggy beard (unaccompanied by moustache or whiskers). Cf. phë̆ʦᵘ̈ and phaʦh.
noted only in the compound naʦun phĕʦun, p. 663b, l. 27, q.v.
f. a small, thin, tail-like beard (shaped like a fringe, cf. phë̆ʦᵘ̈); a lock of hair left on the top of the head (the rest being shaved), a topknot.
f. a fringe (esp. when long) of a turban, shawl, or the like; (when whiskers and moustache are lacking) a thin, scraggy, tail-like beard (cf. dāri-phᵒ, p. 238a, l. 29). Cf. phaʦh and phĕʦh.

m. a ransom, redemption, sacrifice; consecration, devotion; devoting oneself (to save another); adj. c.g. devoted (to), sacrificed or dying (for). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become a ransom (for), be sacrificed (for), be devoted (for or to).

m. (in buying and selling, bartering, or the like) a difference or misunderstanding (between the parties as to amount, number, or the like, of the subject of the transaction). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to settle such a difference or misunderstanding. --karun -- m.inf. to cause such a difference or misunderstanding; esp. (for the purpose of cheating) to cause such a misunderstanding to occur (e.g. between the amount apparently and actually sold). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. such a difference or misunderstanding to arise. --rōzun -- m.inf. such a difference (in counting, measuring, etc.) to remain unadjusted (owing to mistake, carelessness, or the like). --thawun -- m.inf. deliberately to allow such a difference to remain unadjusted.
(? spelling and gend.), a certain fibre plant, Carex sp. (L. 68, fikal).

or phikirᵘ̈ f. thought, consideration, reflection (El. fikr); opinion, notion, idea, imagination; counsel, advice; care, concern, solicitude, anxiety, grief, sorrow (cf. potᵘ phᵒ, s.v. potᵘ) (Śiv. 112; Rām. 126, 1368; H. xii. 5, 20). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to think (upon), to consider, reflect (upon), ponder (H. xii, 19, 24); to turn the attention (to), take thought (of); to make provision (for); to think how (to do anything), to plan, scheme, contrive; to be thoughtful or anxious (about), be concerned, anxious. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. anxiety to be felt. --rōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. anxiety to stay (in a person), anxiety to fill a person. --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to feel anxiety as to the support of one's family. ¶ phikira karañĕ f. pl. inf. to make considerations, to think over things. ¶ phikiri aʦun m.inf. to enter into thought, to be meditated upon, to be familiar to one's thoughts, to become well known. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go into anxiety, to become anxious (H. viii, 10; xii, 4). --khasun -- m.inf. to ascend into the thought, to become pleasing to the mind, to be charming. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall into the thought, to come under consideration. --tarun -- m.inf. to pass over into the thought, the advice of another to be received in the mind. --tārun -- m.inf. to pass over some fact or instruction into another's thought. ¶ phikiran gaʦhun m.inf. to go into anxieties, to meditate anxiously. --lagun -- m.inf. to fall into anxieties.
adj. c.g. thoughtful, intelligent, discriminating (e.g. a child who is acute in distinguishing between what is proper and what is improper).

f. froth, foam, scum; foam or froth from the mouth. --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring froth to a person's mouth; hence, to distress a person by putting him to some difficult and exhausting work. -lọ̆ʦhᵘ m. a clot or lump of foam or froth (on water or issuing from the mouth). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. foam to come; distress to come, as ab.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. phīnaladiñ), covered with foam; having froth issuing from the mouth; distraught with extreme and exhausting labour; (of a work or business) causing such distress.
m. (sg. dat. phi(fi)ndakas), the nut of the Corylus avellana (El.).
m. anxiety and fear as to illness or grief overwhelming some beloved son, friend, etc. phipharȧnⁱ lagȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. such anxiety to occur.

m. (sg. abl. phira 1), inversion, used in the following:-- phir-phyār m. constant or repeated change; change, reversal; inconsistency, alternations, vicissitudes (e.g. in the attitude of a king to his subordinates or in the conduct of an office). -phyār gaʦhun m.inf. such reversal of conduct, etc., to occur. -phyār karun m.inf. to reverse a policy, to undo the work or policy of a public officer. ¶ phira-kôlᵘ m. (owing to forgetfulness or inattention) the wrong reversal of any action, upsetting an arrangement. -kôlᵘ mēlun m.inf. such reversal of action to come into existence, to make a wrong beginning; cf. phēra-kôlᵘ mēlun, s.v. phēra. -kath f. (sg. dat. -kathi), talking (in the presence of outsiders) a secret language; esp. the peculiar argot used for stage directions by bã̄ḍs (see p. 82a, l. 16) or strolling singers and actors (L. 313, phirkat). -mahārĕñ f. a bride when she has first come to her husband's house. -mahārāza m. a bridegroom when he has first come to the bride's house to take her away to his own house. (This takes place some time after the marriage ceremony.) -mal m. the uncleanness of garments, head, etc., adopted by a woman after a death in the family, mourning (L. 263 phir mal). -mal kaḍun m.inf. to put off such uncleanness (by washing, bathing, etc.), to go out of mourning. -mal thawun m.inf. to put on or wear such uncleanness, to go into mourning. -mala-wājĕñ f. a woman who is in such mourning. -motᵘ adj. (f. -müʦᵘ̈), one who acts contrary to all established custom, one who acts like a lunatic. -sāl m. the first invitation after a marriage given to the bridegroom by the bride's relations (L. 258, phirsal). -sāl mahārāza m. the bridegroom invited to such a feast. -thurⁱ adj. c.g. one who does things the reverse way, one who acts contrary to custom. -thurⁱ pöṭhⁱ or -thurⁱ pöṭhin adv. in a reversed manner, upside down, back to front. -thurᵘ 1 m. reversal, inversion, in wrong order. -thurᵘ 2 adj. (f. -thurᵘ̈), one who does something in the reverse direction, one who is accustomed to act contrary to custom. -thurᵘ karun  m.inf. to do reversing (Śiv. 1477); esp. (of a bride) to take the first journey to her husband's house and to return thence to her parents' house. -thurĕr m. reversal of any action or thing; reversal of the seasons, unseasonableness of the seasons of the year. -wörᵘ̈ f. transfer of the contents of one vessel to another; transfer of the contents (e.g. grain) of a large cargo-boat into small boats, unloading into barges. -wārĕ-dāñĕ m. grain transferred from a cargo-boat to small boats; met. grain which has been dirtied and become dusty or become damp, and which has been turned upside down out of a heap. -wārĕ-hönzᵘ̈ m. a boatman who buys rice from a large cargo-boat, and sells it in small boats. -wārĕ-hānzañ f. his wife. -zang f. an ill omen. -zang lagüñᵘ̈ f.inf. an ill omen to come.
m. anything or action which is reversed; one who acts contrary to established custom.

m. separation, disunion, abandonment, departing, departure; distance, distinction; anxiety, grief, regret (on account of absence). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to recall before others former sorrows. --lagun -- m.inf. to bear sorrow in the heart (owing to another's hostile actions).

f. (sg. dat. phirüñᵘ̈), inversion or turning upside down (of things piled up in a heap); a certain dish of spices, almonds, flour, etc., cooked in milk; altering, changing by substitution (cf. nāwa phiran, p. 665b, l. 35). Generally, as a verbal noun, in all the senses of phirun, q.v. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to turn upside down or turn inside out (e.g. paddy turned out for drying, or a garment exposed for airing).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phiranôwᵘ), to cause to turn round (Gr.M.); to circulate (a notice or the like) (Gr.M., K. 404); to cause to wander about (cf. hạṭᵃri hạṭᵃri phᵒ, p. 359b, l. 5) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1026, 1625, 1861); to cause (a horse) to go in a circle, to exercise (a horse) by lunging, or to exercise a horse generally (K. 948); to surround (El.). phiranôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phiranövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to turn round, etc., as ab.

m. flight, running away, absconding; (in Kāshmīrī) reduced to poverty by the loss of all one's possessions and family. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become reduced to poverty, as ab. --karun -- m.inf. to reduce to poverty, as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phirowᵘ), to cause to go round, to circulate (cf. atha phᵒ, p. 61a, l. 10) (Śiv. 983); to whirl (something) (Rām. 739); to cause to wander far; to cause to be reversed or turned upside down (potᵘ phᵒ, to turn some one back); to cause to be surrounded (cf. pālang phᵒ, s.v. pālang); to circulate (a proclamation or the like) (Rām. 89, 1554); to bring into action (as a change); to cause to come into existence (as a change) (cf. pay phᵒ 1 and 2) (s.vv. pay 1 and 2); to disobey, refuse to carry out an order. phirowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phirüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to revolve, caused to wander far, caused to turn upside down, etc.

n.ag. (f. phiravüñᵘ̈), one who causes to revolve (cf. nila- phirawȧnⁱ, p. 633b, l. 8); one who causes to wander far; one who causes to reverse, who turns (something) upside down; potᵘ phᵒ, one who causes (another) to turn back; one who is disobedient.
adj. c.g. absconded, fugitive, runaway, escaped, a runaway; (in Kāshmīrī) i.q. farār, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phyurᵘ; for 2, see s.v. El. shows this verb as intransitive; but it is really the transitive form of phērun, q.v.), to turn round, cause to go round, whirl (cf. lari phᵒ, p. 529b, ll. 26 and 31; nila phirȧnⁱ, p. 633b, l. 8) (Śiv. 52, 1750; H. vii, 18); to cause to wander about, to cause to flow over (Śiv. 1213, 1644); to circulate (news, etc.) (cf. nāma-pögān phᵒ, p. 636b, l. 36) (Rām. 679); to toss up and down (cf. ḍū̃gi phᵒ, p. 195a, l. 6); to promote, advance, produce, devise (Śiv. 1855); to repeat, perform repeatedly, practise diligently (cf. pŏrān phirȧnⁱ, s.v. pŏrān) (Śiv. 798, 1612); ¶ to turn over (pages) (Gr.Gr. 14, Gr.M.); to turn over (beads in a rosary) (Śiv. 102, 1314); to turn over (e.g. clothes in the wash) (L.V. 103); to cause to walk round, to cause to circumambulate; to pour from one vessel to another (cf. gali phᵒ, p. 283a, l. 31) (Gr.M., Śiv. 969, Rām. 513); ¶ to reverse, turn back to front, invert, turn upside down, move (something) backwards and forwards (cf. atha phᵒ, p. 60b, l. 45; buthᵘ phᵒ, p. 142a, l. 6; duba phᵒ, p. 183a, l. 25; mŏkh phᵒ, p. 559b, l. 34; man phᵒ, p. 572a, l. 15; nam phᵒ, p. 635a, l. 39) (Rām. 148, 330, 847; K. 146; H. iii, 5; YZ. 259); (with potᵘ) to turn some one back; to reverse, cancel, make void (L.V. 107; Śiv. 600, 708, 1013; Rām. 790); to repeal, revoke, reverse (a law, custom, or the like); to turn aside (zĕv phirüñᵘ̈, to turn aside the tongue, to change the line of conversation, change the subject of a talk, K. 1108); to change some thing or quality into another (cf. prañĕr phᵒ, s.v. prañĕr); to turn (a garment, etc.) inside out (cf. nāl phᵒ, p. 632a, l. 49; norᵘ phirith, p. 649a, l. 16) (K.Pr. 169); to do a thing backwards (cf. bọ̆dᵘ phᵒ, p. 84a, l. 24; dana- kinⁱ phᵒ, p. 22a, l. 38); ¶ to ply (a tool such as scissors, etc.) upon an article (L.V. 103, Śiv. 1870); to weave (grass shoes) (K.Pr. 123); to cause to surround (cf. ganḍ phirun, to cause knots to surround (a person, dat.), to bind, fetter, shackle, K. 816; pālang phᵒ, s.v. pālang); ¶ to complain, to deplore, bewail, fret over memories of past times, to call to memory (in sorrow), to tell a tale of past woes (cf. lōṭh phᵒ, p. 537b, l. 47; nĕdāg phirȧnⁱ, p. 622b, l. 27). ¶ phirun pyonᵘ m.inf. to fall upside down; fretting to occur, painful memories of past woes to recur. --rōzun -- m.inf. deep regret at want of success to be felt and to continue, to feel disappointed at the non-satisfaction of a longing. ¶ phirⁱ phirⁱ freq. part. turning (some one) back again and again (K. 140); turning (some one or something) backwards and forwards, or round and round (K. 150). phirⁱ phirⁱ ʦhunun m.inf. to be a receptacle of good fortune, to be full of prosperity. ¶ phiran-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ, one who inverts; one who points out clues; one who laments to another, one who complains or tells a tale of woe; one who speaks reproachfully. ¶ phirith dyunᵘ m.inf. to repay (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to reverse, to turn back to front or upside down; to bring a counter accusation; to return (a favour, an injury, etc.). --nyunᵘ -- m.inf. to turn upside down and take away (the contents), to take away the entire contents of anything, to empty. --phĕran ʦhunun -- m.inf. 'to put on the coat back to front'; hence, to bring a counter accusation. --thawun -- m.inf. to put down upside down or back to front, to reverse. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to put on (a garment) inside out, back to front, or otherwise reversed; to insist on plenteously making over (something to somebody) (cf. phŏti phŏti phirith ʦhunun, s.v. phọ̆tᵘ). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to return, come back (W. 86, probably incorr. for phīrith yunᵘ, p. 706b, l. 32). ¶ phyurᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phirᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), turned back or stopped from some journey, work, etc.; reversed, turned upside down; turned (of a garment, with the clean side out); emptied out (of some vessel); turned over (of the pages of a book); turned inside out (of a garment, etc.); repealed, reversed (of a law, rule, custom, or the like); (in fem.) translated 'slut' in K.Pr. 169.

f. a time, turn, used in the ablative phiri, (so many) times [as in aki phiri (p. 20a, l. 43) one time, once (K. 680, 918); once upon a time; phiri aki, once again, once more (K. 572); dŏyi phiri, twice (K. 27); dŏyimi phiri, at the second time (YZ. 13); pönʦi phiri, five times (see pānʦ); trayi phᵒ, thrice (K. 63); sadāhi phᵒ, seventeen times (K. 570, 999); biyĕ phᵒ, at another time, once again (K. 565); yimi phᵒ, this time (K. 577); kaĩsi phᵒ, now and then (p. 390a, l. 4); kṻʦi phᵒ, how many times? i.e. very many times (Gr.M.); (see kǖtⁱ, p. 485a, l. 26) (Gr.M.).]
f. (sg. abl. phēri 1 for 2, see phēra), a coarse kind of shawl thread (El.), knots or the like of this thread embroidered into cloth.
f. of phyurᵘ, 1 p.p. of phirun, q.v.

m. fashionable appearance; the being well-dressed, elegance of apparel; cf. phash 1. --karun -- m.inf. to dress elegantly (esp. when one is poverty-stricken, but does not want the fact to be publicly known), to dress oneself up. --wālun -- m.inf. to strip off fine clothes; met. publicly to dishonour (a person), to abuse publicly.
m. doubt, hesitation (esp. when endeavouring to act according to another's private advice).

m. in phis-phis m. muttered rapid angry speech, angry mumbling (esp. in answer to one who is remonstrating); whispering (Gr.Gr. 13). -phis-gŏʦurᵘ adj. (f. -phis gŏʦᵘ̈rᵘ̈), one who habitually mutters when angry, as ab.; cf. gŏʦᵘ̈rᵘ̈. -phis lagun m.inf. muttering in anger, as ab., to be started.
f. whispering, in kȧnⁱ- phisarāray, p. 448b, l. 21.
in kȧnⁱ-phish, p. 147b, l. 5; i.q. phyushᵘ 2, q.v.

m. vicious or immoral conduct, sin, iniquity, impiety; immorality, adultery, obscenity, impudence. phiska-palav m. 'a garment of indecency', a garment too small (not sufficient to keep the body warm, or doing so only with difficulty).
m. (f. phīsürᵘ̈), one who is in the habit of wearing fine clothes, a fop, dandy, exquisite.

in the following:-- phiṭa phiṭa lagun  m.inf. intoxication or excitement caused by the obtainment of some specially fine garment, ornaments, good quality, or the like, or by the obtainment of some extraordinary thing. Cf. phta and phiṭun.
n.ag. (f. phiṭavüñᵘ̈), one who swaggers about in public (proud of one's fine clothes, high position, or the like), a fop, coxcomb.
in the following:-- phith phith lagun m.inf. yearning or attempting to do some impossible action to be experienced (esp. of a child trying to walk before it can do so).

f. (sg. dat. phī˜ṭi), a severe blow or stroke (from a stone or stick suddenly hurled); esp. a blow on the eye or other part of the body from such a thing as the edge of a shawl suddenly thrown up, or a finger or stick suddenly thrust out. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give such a blow. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a blow to be received.
m. discord, conflict, civil war, revolt, revolution, mutiny. --trāwun -- m.inf. to revolt (El.).
m. Prangos pabularia (El. fitrásályún). It is looked upon as a cure for rot in sheep (El.).
m. (sg. dat. phiṭanas), the feeling of intoxication or pride felt by the wearing of fine dress, ornaments, etc., in public, coxcombery, foppery. Cf. phiṭa.

m. a small piece of cloth, leather, paper, etc., cut or torn off from the main piece (cf. dajĕ-phᵒ, p. 203a, l. 40). Cf. phē̃ṭun. ¶ phī̃tȧnⁱ gaʦhȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to become torn into small pieces. --karȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to cut or tear into small pieces, as ab., to cut or tear up into fragments.
n.ag. (f. phiʦavüñᵘ̈), one who is forgetful, absent-minded.

cong. 1 (1 p.p. f. phiʦᵘ̈; this verb is conjugated impersonally in the feminine, and the person who forgets is put in the dat., as in phiʦān chĕs, there is forgetting to him, i.e. he forgets; so phiʦᵘ̈s, he forgot), forgetting to occur; hence, with subject in dat., to forget (Gr.Gr. 182, 188, 192, 203, 215). According to Gr.Gr. 120, 192, the infinitive of this verb may also be masculine. Thus, phiʦun phiʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ perf. part. f. forgetting having occurred, forgotten (of something fem.).
f. forgetfulness (of past times or occurrences).
m. the spring festival among village people, in which, in order to celebrate the beginning of agricultural operations, bonfires of straw and the like are lighted in the fields.

adj. c.g. absolutely without means, penniless (of one who has to incur some great expense, e.g. on a marriage, and has no means with which to carry it out). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become penniless as ab. --karun -- m.inf. to render penniless (e.g. by gambling, warfare, swindling, or the like).
f. impecuniosity, straits (for money, etc.), as in phö̃gra, q.v.

phuhᵃr 1, or phuhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 1 f. the burnt scum or sediment adhering to the sides and bottom of a cooking-pot; burnt bread (El. phuhur, Gr.Gr. 17, phᵘhurᵘ, m., K.Pr. 35); the scab (of a wound); a crust of dirt or the like (cf. lᵃcha-phŏharĕ, p. 506b, l. 31). --bĕhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such burnt scum or sediment to form; a scab to form. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such scum or sediment to form on the edge or sides of a cooking-pot. ¶ phŏhari-chal f. a strip of such burnt scum or sediment. -khünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -khanjĕ), a bit of this scum or sediment. -khāv c.g. one who is in the habit of eating this scum (used met. to express one who eats worthless or mean food). -kōka m. a foster-brother (Turkī کوکہ) of this scum; hence, esp. an orphan child given bad food by his protectors, and otherwise treated with contumely. -ʦokᵘ m. a mark or skin of this scum on the inside of the bottom of a pot; the part of a pot covered with this scum. -waguwᵘ m. a mat of this scum, a large surface-skin of this scum; met. a kind of mat made of fine grass.

or phôhᵘ, an impalement-post used in the following. The word has not been noted as used in the nominative singular:-- phahi (or phāhi) dyunᵘ  m.inf. to impale (H. v, 10). --dyutᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --diʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), one who has been impaled, one who has been executed by impalement. -kūṭᵘ m. an impalement-post. --lagun -- m.inf. to suffer impalement (as a judicial punishment or otherwise).
m. blossoming, blooming, expansion (of a flower, etc.); (of good qualities, beauty, etc.) blooming, coming to perfection, progress towards completion.

adj. c.g. hollow, apparently full but empty (Śiv. 1310). --basta -- f. a hollow skin, the skin bag used by iron-workers as a bellows; a flatulent woman, a woman whose skin is apparently blown out with wind, and, hence, unable for exertion. --bạstūrᵘ -- or --bŏstūrᵘ -- m. or adj. m. a. skin (bag) filled with air; a man whose skin is apparently blown out with wind, and, hence, unable for exertion. --dam -- m. to cook or steam in a tightly closed vessel, digest, seethe. --damölⁱ -- f. puffing and blowing (e.g. to revive a dying fire). --ḍūnᵘ -- m. a hollow walnut; hence, a bubble (in the water); a bubble, foam (Śiv. 1774-5). --drāv -- adj. c.g. cleansed or purified by fire (of gold or the like). --më̆ʦᵘ̈ -- f. a kind of whitewash or distemper which, after drying, comes off at a touch; cf. -sĕph, bel. --nĕcyuwᵘ -- m. a useless, worthless, feckless son, one who is ready to follow any advice that comes. --nôrᵘ -- m. the pipe of a blacksmith's bellows. --nērun -- m.inf. to issue from the fire, (of gold or the like) to issue from cleansing fires, to be purified by fire. --pholᵘ -- m. an empty grain or fruit, a berry apparently good and solid, but hollow, an artificial grain or berry (made of glass or the like). --sĕph -- f. (sg. dat. -sĕpi), 'hollow chalk,' the chalk used for mixing with water to form the ink used by children in schools for writing on their blackboards employed as slates. After writing, when dry, the writing is obliterated by merely blowing on it. Cf. -më̆ʦᵘ̈, ab.
m. (a jingle of mŏkaddam), a subordinate officer of a mŏkaddam, q.v. (K.Pr. 231).
adj. c.g. one who incites, instigates, or stimulates (esp. another to a quarrel).

m. (sg. dat. phŏkas), a puff or blow of breath from the mouth (cf. pīra-phᵒ, s.v. pīr 1) (Gr.Gr. 123, Gr.M., Śiv. 1847); breath (El.; K.Pr. 11, phukh); a blowing out, a swelling out with air (cf. āma-phᵒ, p. 26b, l. 50); a breath, emptiness, nothingness (cf. phuñᵘ phᵒ, s.v. phuñᵘ) (L.V. 41); incentive, stimulus (cf. ȧchⁱ-phⁱ, p. 8b, l. 1); cf. phukār. --āsun -- m.inf. to incite, stimulate enmity, instigate a quarrel. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to blow up a fire with the mouth; to puff, to blow (off dust) (Gr.M.); to incite or stimulate to a quarrel; to swell up (of the skin of the body); to blow out (a light). --khasun -- m.inf. cold to be suffered (owing to insufficient covering or the like). --ladun -- m.inf. to incite, stimulate. --lagun -- m.inf. incitement or stimulus to be felt; (of a light) to be blown out.
conj. 2 (1 p.p. phọ̆kᵘ), to blow (of the wind) (El.).
adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, or produced in Phākh Pargana.

or phŏllanāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. phŏlanôwᵘ), (of a flower, plant, etc.) to cause to blossom (by proper cultivation, etc.) (Śiv. 26 (phŏllanāwun), 1809); to cause (a man) to be popular, prosperous, and happy; to make (a person, animal, or thing) fine and handsome (by dress, adornment, embellishment, etc.); to cause a work to prosper; to spread out (things collected in a mass). phŏlanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phŏlanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), brought to full blossom (by cultivation, etc.); made popular, as ab.; made fine and handsome, as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phŏlowᵘ), (of a flower, plant, etc.) to cause to blossom (by proper cultivation, etc.) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1020); to cause (a man) to be popular, prosperous, and happy; to expand, distend (something) (Gr.M.); to make (a person, animal, or thing) fine and handsome (by dress, adornment, embellishment, etc.); to cause a work to prosper; to spread out (things collected in a mass); causal of phŏlun, q.v. phŏlowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phŏlüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to blossom; made popular, fine, handsome, etc. (as ab.); spread abroad (of things collected in a mass).

or phŏllawunᵘ n.ag. (f. phŏlavüñᵘ̈), (a flower, etc.) which blooms, one which is in full bloom (L.V. 96, K.Pr. 47, Śiv. 225 (phŏllawunᵘ);one who blooms out, one who becomes fine and handsome, one who is prosperous and with a large family; (of a work) one which turns out successfully; (of luck, fate, or the like) blooming, fortunate, happy (K. 311). The phrase gāsh phŏlawunᵘ or phŏlawani gāshĕ, is used adverbially to mean 'immediately on the blossoming of light', i.e. at early dawn (Gr.M.; Rām. 1105, 1109).
m. a kind of flummery (given as a food to invalids).

or phŏllun conj. 2 [1 p.p. phọ̆lᵘ or (Śiv. 54) phọ̆llᵘ, f. phö̆jᵘ̈ (Śiv. 1684, 1686) or phö̆jjᵘ̈; 2 p.p. phŏjyōv. The causal of this verb is phŏl(l)anāwun, phọ̆lᵃrun, phọ̆lᵃrāwun, or phŏl(l)awun, qq.v. (Gr.Gr. 174)], to expand (of a flower), to blossom, to burst forth in bloom, to flower (cf. pōsh phŏlȧnⁱ, s.v. pōsh 1; pushĕ phᵒ, s.v. pushĕ) (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 46; Śiv. 54 (phŏllᵒ), 132, 167, 267, 491, 555, 1025, 1157 (ll), 1180, 1270, 1536 (ll), 1571, 1573, 1686, 1744, 1760 (ll); Rām. 93, 647, 678, 1025, 1777; K. 250; YZ. 46; K.Pr. 138, 256); to bloom, flourish (El. phulun; Gr.Gr. (phŏllᵒ), 174, 205; Rā. 204; YZ. 170); to bloom, to become filled with joy (Rām. 1431; K. 94, 100, 1016, 1141); (of light, dawn, etc.) to bloom forth, i.e. to begin to shine (cf. gāsh phŏlun, p. 308b, l. 18) (Śiv. 1684; Rām. 92, 295, 679, 1257, 1636; K. 79; H. iii, 3; v, 5, 7; viii, 9; xii, 2); (of a work begun) to turn out successfully; to bloom out, to become fine and handsome; (of a man or the like) to be prosperous and popular (with much wealth and many children) (cf. ḍambi-phᵒ, to blossom from the belly; hence, to have good children, p. 218a, l. 20) (K.Pr. 157). phọ̆lᵘ-motᵘ or (Śiv. 498) phọ̆llᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phö̆jᵘ̈ -müʦᵘ̈, Śiv. 1727) (of a flower) expanded, (of a plant) in full bloom (Śiv. 44, 498, 1727); successfully accomplished, as ab.; become prosperous, as ab.
i.q. pholᵘ 1 with suff. of indef. art. Cf. bata-phᵒ, p. 137a, l. 41.
f. (sg. dat. phọ̆lᵃrüñᵃ), expansion (of a flower), causing to blossom; making (a person, animal, or thing) fine and handsome (by adorning it, etc.); spreading out (things collected in a mass).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phọ̆lᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. phọ̆lᵃrun, q.v. phọ̆lᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ 1 p.p. (f. phọ̆lᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. phọ̆lᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, q.v., s.v. phọ̆lᵃrun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phọ̆lᵒrᵒ), (of a flower, plant, etc.) to cause to blossom (by proper cultivation, etc.); to cause a man to be popular, prosperous, and happy; to make (a person, animal, or thing) fine and handsome (by dress, ornament, embellishment, etc.); to cause a work to prosper; to spread out (things collected in a mass). phọ̆lᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. phọ̆lᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), brought to full blossom (by cultivation, etc.); made popular, handsome, etc., as ab.; caused to prosper, as ab.; spread out, as ab.

adj. (f. phö̆jᵘ̈) (this word is properly the 1 p.p. of q.v., used --˚ as an adj.), as in aḍa-phọ̆lᵘ, half-blown, p. 11b, l. 29, and Rām. 1266; so nĕha-phŏlᵘ, and adv. nĕha-phŏli, at the blossoming from sleep; at dawn (p. 625a, l. 47).

grain (the generic term) (El. phaul, phol, phul; L. 460, phul) (L.V. 86); a small bone of the wrist or ankle (cf. phĕkⁱ-phⁱ, s.v. phyokᵘ 1); a kind of silk braid used to ornament the edge of a cap or similar piece of apparel (cf. aṭa-phᵒ, p. 56a, l. 25, and phȧlⁱ-wār, bel.); a secret connexion between two people (e.g. by religion, qualities, or actions), close intimacy (W. 142); ¶ a single grain (cf. bata-phᵒ, p. 137a, l. 40; cana-phᵒ, p. 172, l. 27; dönᵘ̈-phᵘ̈, p. 223b, l. 11; muṭhⁱ-phⁱ, p. 605a, l. 13; raʦa-phᵒ, s.v. raʦh) (L.V. 47; Śiv. 255, 367-8; Rām. 12, 1456; K. 178, 1144; K.Pr. 4, 168, 217); a single fruit (of a bunch) (K.Pr. 255); any single small round object, e.g. a pearl (cf. caphkȧlⁱ-phⁱ, p. 173b, l. 35; dūra-phᵒ, p. 239a, l. 1; ḍōṭha-phᵒ, p. 258a, l. 4; haṭi-phᵒ, p. 356a, l. 42; kana-phᵒ, p. 449a, l. 29; kañi-phᵒ, p. 461b, l. 24; H. xii, 15, a pebble; lë̆zᵘ̈-phᵘ̈, p. 508b, l. 34; lāla-phᵒ, p. 522a, l. 29; māli-phᵒ, p. 565a, l. 49; nika-phᵒ, p. 627b, l. 29; nīlⁱ-phⁱ, p. 670b, l. 27; phŏka-phᵒ, p. 688b, l. 20; phakīr-phᵒ, p. 690a, l. 50; phōta-phᵒ, s.v. phōta; pīra-phᵒ, s.v. pīr 1; pita-phᵒ, s.v. pita 2; ranga-phᵒ, s.v. ranga 2 rīnzⁱ-phⁱ, p. 855a, l. 46) (Śiv. 474, 1094, 1314; Rām. 1653; K. 1143; YZ. 75, 213; K.Pr. 78, 95, 233); a pearl, in the sense of something delicate and beautiful (cf. danda-phᵒ, p. 224b, l. 48; khŏra-phᵒ, p. 409b, l. 24; khōra-phᵒ, p. 410b, l. 6); a small coin, a bit (K.Pr. 238); the pupil of the eye (cf. lāla-phᵒ, p. 522a, l. 30; mañĕ-phᵒ, p. 585b, l. 50) (Rām. 1105, 1423); a small lump of flesh or the like (cf. māz-phᵒ, p. 614b, l. 48; nūna-phᵒ, p. 641a, l. 1; ñĕñĕ-phᵒ, p. 644a, l. 43; nāṭi-phᵒ, p. 660b, l. 24) (K.Pr. 73, a lump of manure); a small collection of grains or the like, a small quantity of anything; esp. of things which, like grain, consist of great numbers of small articles (cf. arga-phᵒ, p. 43a, l. 16; öṭⁱ-phⁱ, p. 53a, l. 34; athi-phᵒ, p. 66a, l. 5; bēcha-phᵒ, p. 79b, l. 35; basi-phᵒ, p. 131b, l. 1; bȧṭhⁱ-phⁱ, p. 141b, l. 35; byölⁱ-phⁱ, p. 151a, l. 1; haka-phᵒ, p. 326a, l. 37; hāra-phᵒ, p. 344b, l. 20; khanḍa-phᵒ, p. 402b, l. 49; mā̃gạyĕ-phᵒ, p. 552b, l. 40; mŏnga-phᵒ, p. 578b, l. 12; mardi-phᵒ, or marēdi-phᵒ, p. 589b, l. 48; mŏchĕ-phᵒ, p. 604b, l. 38; mĕʦi-phᵒ, p. 609a, l. 9; mĕwa-phᵒ, p. 611a, l. 35; māyā-phᵒ, p. 612b, l. 30; phacakh-phᵒ, p. 685a, l. 4; pröpinⁱ-phⁱ, s.v. pröpyunᵘ; pŏyĕ-phᵒ, s.v. pŏyĕ; rūzⁱna-phⁱ, p. 859b, l. 30 tŏmᵃla-phᵃ, s.v. tŏmul; ʦᵃñĕ-phᵃ, s.v. ʦᵃñ (Gr.Gr. 164, Gr.M.). ¶ It will be observed that this word may mean either 'a single grain or other article' or 'a small quantity of such'. It often happens that, compounded with the same word it may take either sense, so that the meaning of the whole is in doubt. Thus, dachĕ-phᵒ, a single grape, and a small collection of grapes, p. 185b, l. 46; dā̃-phᵒ, p. 230b, l. 5; kara-phᵒ, p. 466a, l. 12; kȧshⁱ-phⁱ, p. 480a, l. 36; lāyĕ-phᵒ, p. 543b, l. 3; macāma-phᵒ, p. 548a, l. 22; mahā-phᵒ, p. 548a, l. 22; mŏkhta-phᵒ, p. 561a, l. 15; makāyi-phᵒ, p. 563b, l. 6. The plural phȧlⁱ is not used to indicate a small amount, but indicates indefinitely 'grains', 'small round articles', etc. (Gr.Gr. 164, Gr.M.). ¶ pholᵘ barun m.inf. to tell tales (against some one), peach (against). --ḍalun -- m.inf. to dislocate the wrist or ankle. --phyotᵘ -- m. 'braid and embroidery'; met. a secret collection or store of precious metals or valuables (Gr.Gr. 95). --wāṭun -- m.inf. to mount a pearl or other round jewel in its setting; to set a dislocated wrist or ankle; to form an intimacy with some powerful person for one's own protection. ¶ phȧlⁱ-bọ̆ngⁱr f. a kind of glass bangle (see bọ̆ngᵃr) studded with coloured beads. -chula m. the act of rubbing by hand from the cob the seeds of Indian corn or the like. -chŏmba m. the act of beating Indian corn, legumes, etc., with a stick or flail to release the grains from the cobs or pods; cf. chŏmb. -kŏkürᵘ̈ f. a miserly or niggardly woman (quasi, a woman who, although rich, feeds herself as a hen picks up grains). -maköyⁱ f. Indian corn freed from the cob. -phakīr m. (f. -phȧkⁱröñⁱ), a poor miserable beggar, who supports himself by the few grains of food received in begging. -phal adj. c.g. (of something formerly incomplete) quite complete. -phala adv. completely, entirely. -sörᵘ̈ f. taking away and collecting grain by grain or little by little (esp. when this is done secretly). -söriñ f. getting into close intimacy with some one in order to worm out his secret intentions. -sᵃʦan f. (sg. dat. -sᵃʦüñᵃ), a kind of pin with a large shining head. Musalmān women adorn their head-dress (kasāba, q.v.) with it (El. phalsatsan). -wād m. (rice, etc.) dealt with or distributed grain by grain or in very small quantities. -wār m. a coloured silk braid used as a border of a cap or similar article of apparel. ¶ phali phali bāwoṭᵘ m. 'an armlet on every ankle and wrist'; hence, a naughty disobedient child. phali wasith bata m. soft boiled rice (in which the grains are not separate).
adj. (f. phüjᵘ̈) (this word is properly the 1 p.p. of phalun 1 and 2, q.v., used --˚ as an adj.), (of a garment) worn out, ragged. Cf. aḍa-phᵒ, p. 11b, l. 26; kana-phᵒ, p. 448a, l. 21).

m. oil impregnated with essence of flowers by steeping them in it, scented oil (K.Pr. 159). -kangañ f. a comb impregnated with scented oil; a woman who is in the habit of combing her hair with scented oil. -wŏḍ f. a head, the hair of which is impregnated with scented oil; a woman whose hair is so impregnated.
f. a woman with uncombed or untidy hair (esp. one habitually so).

adj. (f. phö̆njᵘ̈), wanting in substance, pithless, hollow (of something apparently externally strong, but unsubstantial within, or, met., of someone outwardly virtuous, wealthy, or powerful, but really worthless). Cf. phōnsa.

adj. c.g. wanting in substance, pithless, hollow (of something apparently externally strong, but unsubstantial within, or, met., of someone outwardly virtuous, wealthy or powerful, but inwardly worthless). Cf. phọ̆ngᵘ.
m. a glass shade (of a candlestick, etc., hanging lamp, etc.) (Rām. 1659).
f. (sg. dat. phöñᵉ̆rüñᵉ̆), the act of emptying entirely (e.g. a vessel); entirely emptying a person (of wealth, property, etc.), depriving (him) of all property. Cf. phānun.
m. in phönⁱ-kôlⁱ m. (of an abandoned house or the like), emptiness, desolateness; (of a person) ruined, poverty-stricken. Cf. phuñᵘ.
(sg. dat. phŏphi), f. a father's sister, a paternal aunt (Rām. 734).
conj. 3 (1 p.p. phö̃phalyōv), to be fit for any work, to be fit for use (Gr.Gr. li).

adj. (f. phŏphatᵃr or phŏphatᵘ̈rᵘ̈), bearing the relationship of a paternal aunt (phŏph) (Gr.Gr. 132). --bôyᵘ -- m. a paternal cousin, the son of a paternal aunt (Gr.Gr. 132). ¶ phŏphatᵃr bĕñĕ f. a female paternal cousin, the daughter of a paternal aunt (Gr.Gr. 132).

adj. (f. phüphᵘ̈), speaking indistinctly, lisping, spluttering, of stumbling or stammering speech (Gr.Gr. 138). ¶ phapha-kār adj. c.g., i.q. phophᵘ. -karawunᵘ adj. (f. -karavüñᵘ̈), spluttering with heat, bubbling up (in boiling), pouring out steam, boiling hot.
m. an order, command, decree (cf. nā-phŏrmān).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phŏrmôwᵘ), to order, command, decree (Śiv. 637, 684, 838).
f. the Persian language (El. phārsí; K.Pr. 146, phársí); as adj. c.g. Persian (El. fársí).

conj. 2 (2 p.p. phūrᵘ. The causal of this verb is phōra- nāwun, not phūrᵃrāwun, Gr.Gr. 174), to throb, quiver, palpitate, twitch (cf. ȧchⁱ phōrañĕ, p. 8b, l. 4; bulⁱ bulⁱ phōrüñᵘ̈, p. 106a, l. 30) (Gr.Gr. 174, 206); a sound, or speech, to be uttered (K. 510); to gabble, jabber, speak rapidly, declaim profusely; to utter some sound inadvertently or unintentionally (Śiv. 287, 1331); to utter unintelligible or indistinct sounds (e.g. as when a dumb man tries to speak) (cf. dᵃda phᵒ, p. 187b, l. 35).

m. (sg. dat. phörisis), Persian teaching (commencing with the learning of the Persian alphabet and going on to the study of Persian language and literature). phöris-wôlᵘ m. one who is acquainted with Persian or Persian literature.

m. the belly, the intestines generally (cf. phaka-phᵒ, p. 689a, l. 16); met. the whole body (cf. phürᵘ̈ 2). --sādun -- m.inf. to accomplish a body, i.e. to perform the funeral obsequies over an artificial body made of flour, etc., when a Hindū has died, but his body cannot be found. ¶ phȧrⁱ-buzⁱ adj. (f. -buzᵘ̈), one whose belly is burnt, esp. one whose belly is accidentally burnt by contact with a burning kāngrī or portable brazier. -buzay f. the burning of the belly, as ab. -dôdᵘ m. belly-grief, i.e. longing for offspring. -dag f. pain in the belly (esp. that owing to starvation). -dag tulüñᵘ̈. f.inf. to cause a man (e.g. a client, a servant) or an animal to suffer the pangs of hunger. -kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. a burning brazier to enter the belly, i.e. the pain to be felt by a married woman's parents when, owing to the death of her husband or the like, and consequent destitution, she has to return to their house; (when a person brings a charge of theft) the tables to be turned (by the accused falsely accusing the charger with the crime). -phakh (sg. dat. -phakas), a belly-stink, an evil smell in, or arising from, the belly; (as the child of such-and-such a mother), a wicked, ill conducted, child. -wōv f. pain in the belly caused by insufficient food being given to a very hungry person; the pain felt by a very hungry person at the sight of food which is denied to him. -wōv tulüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to cause such pain to be felt, to starve or insufficiently feed a person, to let a man starve in the midst of plenty. -wōv wŏthüñᵘ̈ f.inf. such hunger pain to arise or be felt.
m. ? ridicule, scoffing, joking (YZ. 121 (pl.), here translated by the Latin merces, but the correct meaning appears to be as ab.). Cf. phᵃr 1.
m. the name used in schools for the Śāradā letter corresponding to the Nāgarī cerebral ṣa.

or (Gr.Gr. 174) phushüñᵘ̈ conj. 1. (This verb is impersonal, and the person by whom anger is felt is put in the dative; moreover, when the verbal form is capable of expressing gender, it is put into the feminine. Thus phŏshān chĕs, there is inward anger to him, i.e. he is inwardly angry; phŏshĕs, there will be inward anger to him, he will be inwardly angry; phö̆shᵘ̈s, he was inwardly angry (Gr.Gr. 182, 188, 203, 215). The infinitive, however, may take also the m. form phŏshun, the fem. form referring to the wrath of females (Gr.Gr. 120, 192). The 1 p.p. f. is phö̆shᵘ̈) inward anger to be felt (but not exhibited), secret resentment to be felt, secret umbrage to be taken; cf. phᵃsun. phö̆shᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ perf. part. f. secret wrath felt (by some one, dat.).

cong. 1 (this verb is a feminine impersonal, and is treated like phŏshüñᵘ̈, q.v. The 1 p.p. f. is phọ̆shᵉ̆rövᵉ̆), inward anger to be caused to be felt by (dat.) a person, as in phọ̆shᵉ̆rāwān chĕs, inward anger is caused to be felt by him, i.e. so-and-so causes him to be inwardly angry. phọ̆shᵉ̆rövᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆ perf. part. f. that by which inward anger has been caused to enter, that which has produced inward anger (used impersonally in the f.).

adj. (f. phüshᵘ̈), mad, eccentric, blundering, one who does things the wrong way, even when previously warned, one who acts contrary to custom; crazed; cf. phash 2. phȧshⁱ-pöthᵃr m. acting like a mad man, eccentricity; crazy conduct.
f. (sg. dat. phösᵃrüñᵃ), mutual hostility (roused between friends by slander or the like). Cf. phās.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phösᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. phạsᵃrun 1, q.v.; esp. to net (an opponent), to bring a member of an opposite party over to one's own side (in order to learn the opponents' secrets), to suborn a traitor, to win over; cf. phösᵃrun, phạsᵃrāwun, phāsawun. phösᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ  perf. part. (f. phösᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. phösᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, s.v. phösᵃrun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phösᵒrᵒ), i.q. phạsᵃrun 1, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 1); esp. to net (an opponent), to bring a member of an opponent's party over to one's own side (in order to ascertain the other party's secrets), to suborn a traitor, to win over. phösᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. phösᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. phạsᵒrᵒ-motᵒ 1, q.v.; won over to the other side, as ab.

f. a noose (Śiv. 504, pl. nom. phösⁱ for phāsĕ, m.c.); esp. a hangman's noose (K.Pr. 29). Cf. phū̃sⁱ. ¶ phāsi dyunᵘ m.inf. to execute by hanging, to hang (a criminal) (Gr.M.). --lagun -- m.inf. to suffer death by hanging (in process of law, or by suicide, or accidentally, or by murder).

(? cf. فوطہ) m. an artificial pearl (made of powdered glass melted down) (according to El. a kind of composition of which necklaces are made) (Śiv. 1310; YZ. 24, 27). -dörᵘ̈ f. a child's doll decked with imitation pearls; cf. dörᵘ̈ 4. -gorᵘ m. (his wife -gȧrⁱ-bāy; a woman who follows the profession is -gürᵘ̈), a maker of imitation pearls. -lar f. a string of artificial pearls. -pholᵘ m. a single artificial pearl. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), an itinerant seller of artificial pearls.

m. (sg. dat. phŏṭas), a lump occurring in a dish of boiled rice or the like (due to bad cooking, as each grain should be separate). ¶ phŏṭa-ras m. bad cooking (in which lumps as ab. are produced). -sas m. dāl- or pease-pottage badly cooked (with lumps in it). -wã̄gun m. (sg. dat. -wã̄ganas), a naughty bold boy.
m. (sg. dat. phōtas), death. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. destruction or bringing to naught to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to destroy, bring to naught (a thing, quality, business, etc.).
f. (sg. dat. phōṭaki), the having succeeded in accumulating everything that one wants, complete well-being, full prosperity, affluence.
m. a poverty-stricken man (in spite of his being industrious and apparently well-to-do).
m. a notification of the law in or respecting a particular case; a decree, judgment, award, decision; an order, command (H. ii, 7, photuwāh, with suff. of indef. art.).
or phŏtᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a kind of small wicker basket (cf. dājĕ-phᵒ, p. 202b, l. 39; dā̃-phᵒ, p. 230b, l. 21) (Gr.Gr. 6, 37; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1247).

m. a large basket (El. phaut, a basket lined with bójpatr, i.e. burza, birch-bark) (cf. dājĕ-phᵒ, p. 202b, l. 37; dā̃-phᵒ, p. 230b, l. 16; hurⁱ-phⁱ, p. 347a, l. 1; mĕʦi-phᵒ, p. 609a, l. 10) (El. phatú; Gr.Gr. 27, 37; W. 128, 142; Śiv. 1615; Rām. 621; YZ. 258, photī; K.Pr. 36, 119). ¶ phŏtⁱ-bāgay f. division by basketfuls. -dạndᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the edge of a basket. -kā̃gᵃr f. a large kind of kāngrī, or portable brazier, surrounded by basketwork. -köñᵘ̈ f. the withy from which baskets are made, the basket-withy; cf. köñᵘ̈ 2. -mēn f. (sg. dat. -mīñᵘ̈), measuring (grain, etc.) by basketfuls. -palav m. old clothes, which are exchanged with basketwork-sellers in exchange for their goods. -sörᵘ̈ f. conveying grain in baskets from the field to the house or the like. ¶ phŏti phŏti muhim m. the sudden fall of poverty (esp. on a rich person). --phŏti phirith ʦhunun -- m. the sudden accession of wealth to a poor man (lit. (fate) to give in basketfuls).

or phoṭᵘ 1 m. extreme cooking, cooking with the application of much or prolonged heat, intense boiling, boiling down to a small compass; esp. the extreme boiling down of food prepared as a regimen for a lying-in woman, for the first ten days after the child's birth. --karun -- m.inf. to do boiling down, as ab. ¶ phŏṭⁱ-(or phȧṭⁱ-)bata  m. rice boiled down to a third or fourth of the original quantity (used as a regimen for lying-in women and invalids). -pākh m. (sg. dat. -pākas), boiling food down as a regimen, as ab. -trēsh f. drinking water boiled down till it is reduced in quantity as ab. (given to the same people). -wôñᵘ m., id.
m. consolation, condolence, sympathetic language, comfort, encouragement. phȧṭⁱ dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to console; to encourage.

adj. (f. phüṭᵘ̈ 1; for 2, see s.v.) (properly the p.p. of phaṭun, q.v., but used as an adj. --˚), split, cracked, broken (cf. aḍa-phᵒ, p. 11b, l. 32; kana-phᵒ, p. 448a, l. 23) (Gr.Gr. 9, 10, 209); sunken in water, drowned (cf. kŏla phȧṭⁱ gaʦhun, p. 437b, l. 23). ¶ phȧṭⁱ used as adv. in the following:-- dam phȧṭⁱ gaʦhun, p. 216b, l. 7; dam phȧṭⁱ karun, id., l. 11; kŏla phȧṭⁱ gaʦhun, as ab.

orphaida or phöda m. profit, advantage, benefit, good, avail, utility (K.Pr. 219, pháidah); gain, yield, interest (on money); El. faida. -mand فآئدہ مند adj. c.g. profitable, beneficial, advantageous, useful, efficacious (El.). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), useless, profitless, unavailing, of no use (El.).

or faiz فیض m. overflowing, abundance, plenty; beneficence, munificence, liberality, bounty, grace, charity; good, benefit, profit. --nērun -- m.inf. profit (from anything begun) to result, the fruits of one's work to issue. ¶ phöza-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), producing good results, fruitful, profitable (of a work or business, or of a person).
m. the condition of having a long rent, crackedness, fissuredness, the condition of being split. Cf. phrāṭh.
or phᵃrakal adj. c.g. one who is liable to become breathless with only slight exertion; one who is habitually liable to be terrified.
or phᵃrakalad adj. c.g. (as subst., f. phr(phᵃr)akaladiñ ), one who permanently or continually suffers from breathlessness, an asthmatic.

or phᵃrakanāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. phra(phᵃra)kanôwᵃ ), to put out of breath, cause to pant; to distress, afflict (by chasing, terrifying, or the like). phrakanôwᵘ-motᵘ or phᵃrakanôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. phra(phᵃra)kanövᵃ-müʦᵃ ), put out of breath, afflicted, distressed (as ab.).
or phᵃrakawunᵃ n.ag. (f. phra(phᵃra)kavüñᵃ ), one who pants or is out of breath; one who pants (owing to exertion, terror, or the like), one who is much agitated.

or phᵃrakh m. (sg. dat. phrakas), breathlessness (El. phrĕk), asthma (El. also has phrak, breath); breathlessness from fear or the like (Śiv. 1810). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to take away breathlessness, assuage an attack of asthma; met. to soothe the breathlessness due to terror or intense exertion, to relieve or release a person from such terror or exertion. --khasun -- m.inf. breathlessness to come on (e.g. from hill-climbing or the like); an attack of asthma, etc., to come on. --trāwun -- m.inf. to be relieved from breathlessness; hence, to be relieved from terror, intense labour, etc. ¶ phraka-dār adj. c.g. breathless; filled with terror or anxiety (whether anticipatory or due to some occurred cause). --drāv -- m. issued from (i.e. successfully passed through) anxiety, i.e. one who, having passed through the initiatory and anxious preliminaries, is now well skilled in any occupation. -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), struck by terror (at something that has occurred). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to pull out from breathless exertion, i.e. by instruction or giving experience, to make (e.g. a stupid or helpless child) skilled and experienced. --nērun -- m.inf. to become skilled and experienced (see --drāv, ab.). -phrakh f. (for gend., see Gr.Gr. 75), severe and rapid breathlessness; terror caused by some sudden or unexpected cause (e.g. an attack by a wild beast). -phrakh lagüñᵘ̈ f.inf. such terror to be felt. -zad adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -zadiñ), one who is terror stricken (at some task, e.g. owing to his having failed in a similar task before, or to his belief in his inability to accomplish it).
or phᵃrakun conj. 1 (1 p.p. phr(phᵃr)okᵃ ; 2 p.p. phra(phᵃra)cyōv . This verb is impersonal), to breathe hard, to breathe violently, to be breathless (e.g. from extreme exertion or from terror).

or phrasth m. (sg. dat. phrastas. In some compounds this word takes the forms phrȧsⁱ and phrȧsⁱtⁱ) the Italian poplar (Populus nigra, El.; L. 79, 81; Śiv. 1553). Its loppings are used to provide winter fodder for cattle (L. 70). Cf. dŏda-phᵒ, p. 189b, l. 42, and kābulī phᵒ, p. 382a, l. 30. ¶ phrȧsⁱ-zyunⁱ m. (sg. dat. -zinis), firewood made from the poplar. ¶ phrasta-mŏnḍᵘ m. the trunk of the poplar tree. -mura f.pl. the catkins of the poplar. -phamb m. the cotton-like ripened catkins of the poplar. -pan m. the leaf of the poplar. ¶ phrȧsⁱtⁱ-mūr m. a branch of a poplar tree. ¶ phrastukᵘ sg. gen. (f. phrastücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the poplar.
or phrȧsⁱtyuwⁱ adj. (f. phrastüvᵘ̈ or phrȧsⁱtivⁱ), made of poplar wood. Cf. phrösⁱlyuwⁱ.
adj. c.g. possessing a crack, cracked by nature, found to be cracked (and hence rejected). Cf. phrāṭh.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. phrāṭaladiñ), cracked or scratched, covered with scratches, having many scratches (cf. the next).
or phrith 1 m. (sg. dat. phratas), an old worn-out shoe (cf. kō̃shi-phᵒ, p. 480b, l. 16; pulahȧrⁱ-phⁱ, s.v. pul; paizār-phᵒ, s.v. paizār).

m. (sg. dat. phraṭas), a sudden death (not in the ordinary course of nature) (e.g. from a deadly weapon, or a terrifying sight or news). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to slay (a man or beast) unawares. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. sudden death to occur; to be struck senseless (as if suddenly killed). --karun -- m.inf. to cause sudden death; to cause (a person) suddenly to fall senseless (as if struck by sudden death); violently, or severely, to reproach (K. 1105). ¶ phraṭa-mār m. sudden death, slaying (another) suddenly and unawares. --marun -- m.inf. to die a sudden death. It is believed that when a person dies a sudden death in battle, his corpse sometimes still retains some spark of life and acts, for a certain time, as if alive. -māz m. the flesh of an animal killed unawares (and not in the way of ordinary slaughter). -tam m. instantaneous death (e.g. from a lightning-stroke). -tam gaʦhun m.inf. sudden death (as if from a lightning-stroke) to occur.

f. (sg. dat. phrāṭi), a long rent, a crack, fissure, split (cf. dā̃da-phᵒ, p. 187b, l. 18, where the word is m.). Cf. phaṭān phrāṭān, s.v. phaṭun. ¶ phrāṭa gaʦhañĕ f. pl. inf. scratches to occur (on the body, foot, etc., on a metal or wooden surface, or the like). -zad adj. c.g. (as subst., f. phrāṭazadiñ), scratched, marked with scratches.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. phrāṭiladiñ), scratched or cracked, marked with one single scratch (cf. the preceding).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phrôṭᵘ), to split, divide, cause a fissure (in something) (cf. phaṭān phrāṭān, s.v. phaṭun). See phrāṭh and phrôṭᵘ.
or (Hindū) phrȧṭyômᵘ̈ m. outspoken reproach, verbal censure. Cf. phraṭh.
m. acting like a lunatic (i.e. doing everything wrongly and contrary to custom), boorishness. Cf. phrôtᵘ.

or phrēʦhar m. the condition of bearing good fruit or results, excellence of quality (in that the results are excellent), excellent fruitfulness (cf. atha-phᵒ, p. 61a, l. 6; phal-phᵒ, p. 692a, l. 5); good fortune (El. frētsar); cf. phrūsᵘ and phryūstᵘ. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to produce good fruit, to cause excellent fruitfulness to occur; to be produced as excellent fruit, excellent fruit to result. --lagun -- m.inf. good results to come.
sg. dat. and pl. nom. of phrǖʦhᵘ̈, see phryūstᵘ.

m. fickle, vain, worthless in character. --shōda -- m. one who is capriciously or fitfully dissolute; one who is indifferent to wrath; one whose wrath is quickly appeased. -shūdil f. fitful dissoluteness; quick appeasement of wrath.
m. the pipe or tube of the entire bark of a long tree-branch. -paiwand m. a parasitic creeping plant on the bark of a tree.

(for 1, see phrath) m. (sg. dat. phritas), a fœtus, a child in the act of coming into birth, just-born offspring. --trāwun -- m.inf. to release the fœtus, (of a woman) to be in childbed (and in the act of bringing forth), to be giving birth to.
phrǖʦᵘ̈, see phrūsᵘ or phrūstᵘ, and phryūstᵘ.
adj. (f. phrösⁱlivⁱ), made of poplar wood. Cf. phrastuwᵘ.

adj. (f. phröʦᵘ̈), one who (like a lunatic) does nothing in the usual way, an ignorant boorish fellow (rude in speech, gait, clothing, eating, action, and so on), a stupid boor, a Tony Lumpkin (cf. bula-phᵒ, p. 105a, l. 47; jina-phᵒ, p. 375a, l. 16; phuṭᵘ-phᵘ, s.v. phuṭᵘ). Cf. phyôtᵘ.
m. a single ploughing or digging of a field (before sowing). phröṭⁱ dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to prepare (a field) for sowing, by more than one ploughing or digging.
adj. (f. phröṭᵘ), rent, torn, fissured, cracked, broken (cf. phuṭᵘ phᵒ, s.v. phuṭᵘ). See phrāṭh and phrāṭun.

f. continually following another till the completion of some work (e.g. an employer following his servants to keep them up to work). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (in cultivation or the like) to follow the plough, etc.; to go behind workers (to see that they work properly). --mārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to follow workmen, as ab. (esp. when done secretly).

in the following:-- phrôwᵘ zālun m.inf. according to tradition, in old times the inhabitants of Kashmīr had every winter to leave the country for six months in the possession of demons. Before departing they set their houses on fire and left them in ashes. This is commemorated at the present day in the Anantanāg Pargana by lighting bonfires at the end of the month of Öshid (in Skt. Āśvina = September-October). This phrase is used to imply the lighting of these bonfires. Cf. RT.Tr. iv, 710.
