or phrūstᵘ (Gr.Gr. 19) or (q.v.) phryūstᵘ adj. (f. phrǖʦᵘ̈ or phrǖʦhᵘ̈), praiseworthy, commendable; bearing good fruit, auspicious, having excellent results, profitable, lucrative, productive of success, (of a son or the like) a credit to the family, successful (El. phrúts).

adj. (f. phrǖʦᵘ̈,phrīʦᵘ̈, or phrǖʦhᵘ̈; sg. dat. phrēʦĕ or phrēʦhĕ; m. sg. obl. phrēsa, phrēsta, phrēʦa, or phrēʦha), praise- worthy, commendable (cf. atha-phrᵒ, p. 61a, l. 17); bearing good fruit, having excellent results, profitable, lucrative, productive of success, (of a son or the like) a credit to the family, successful (cf. phal-phᵒ, p. 692a, l. 7); cf. phrūsᵘ or phrūstᵘ and phryūʦᵘ. phrēsa-(phrēsta- or phrēʦa-)kulᵘ ( or) m. (f. -kujⁱ or -kujᵘ̈), a producer of good fruit, (a son, daughter, servant, etc.) a credit to his family, one who employs successfully property inherited or in his charge.
f. a broken skin or blister caused by burning, scalding, or the like. phsara wasañĕ f. pl. inf. blisters or breakings of the skin to be caused by burning, scalding, or the like.

in phta-phta m. scraps, small bits (of something worn out or gone bad); cf. phuta. phta-phta gaʦhun m.inf. (worn-out garments or food gone bad) to become small scraps, break up into little pieces. --karun -- m.inf. to tear, or break up (clothes, food, etc.) into small scraps; met. to put on a false appearance of enjoyment (by painting oneself, anointing, decorating oneself, wearing ornaments, etc.). Cf. phiṭa.
m. a dog (El.). Cf. phĕ˜w. Sg. dat. phuwas (YZ. 90).
m. the condition of being burst, broken.
(El.) m. the tail of a bird. Cf. the next.
f. a turban (as worn on the head). --wālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring down (another's) turban, i.e. to dishonour or disgrace him publicly. --wasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be publicly dishonoured or disgraced.
f. ridicule, derision; the head-feathers or crest of a bird (Śiv. 1812).
m. cheese made from ewe's milk.
f. in phuh karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to save up, gradually to accumulate, little by little to save up the surplus after one's daily expenditure.
or phuhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 2 or phuhürᵘ̈ f. inherited wealth (cf. pröñᵘ phᵒ, s.v. prônᵘ). --āsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. inherited wealth to exist; met. (in a battle or the like) firm allies and other help to exist.

m. a puff or blow of breath from the mouth; a hiss, a bubbling up of steam (Gr.Gr. 123); a swelling up with wind (cf. āma-phᵒ, p. 26b, l. 50); met. angry speech (Gr.Gr. 123); display of pride; cf. phŏkh. --anun -- m.inf. to bring hissing, to cook gently, to simmer (something, dat). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to swell up (of the skin of the body); to show pride, be consequential; to simmer (something, dat.) gently. --trāwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to let out hisses, to show overweening pride. --trāwun -- m.inf. after simmering something, to pour off the water together with the scum and other impurities.
n.ag. (f. phukāravüñᵘ̈), one who puffs out his breath, one who speaks in anger or in overweening pride.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phukôrᵘ), to puff out the breath, to speak in anger or overweening pride (Gr.Gr. 123); to bubble up (of steam) (Gr.Gr. 123); to simmer (food). phukôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phukörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), uttered in anger or overweening pride; (of food) gently simmered.
n.ag. (f. phukavüñᵘ̈), one who blows on a weak fire with the mouth so as to make it burn up; a fire, brazier, or the like, which is being blown up in this manner.
m. (sg. dat. phukas), a blow-pipe; the blowing of a fire (Gr.Gr. 123); blowing a fine stream of drops of water out of the mouth (done to cloth to take out a crease) (cf. phukᵘ).

f. (sg. dat. phū̃ki), smelling, taking a smell (of something) (Gr.Gr. 125). --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take a sniff (at something), to take a quick smell (at something). ¶ phū̃ki phērun m.inf. to go about with a sniff; hence, to come from near (any person or thing, as if merely to take a sniff at a thing and come away) (used in forbidding). --pakun -- m.inf. quietly to go near (any person or place, as if to smell it) (esp. used in forbidding).
f., in wātal-phukh, p. 1164b, l. 3, q.v.
f. (sg. dat. phū̃khë˘ʦᵘ̈), power (due to possession of money, property, allies, or the like).
m. a bubble; a boil or other swelling. --khasun -- m.inf. a boil or other swelling to rise.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phukᵘ, 2 p.p. phucyōv), to blow upon from the mouth (cf. phū̃kun); esp. to blow up a fire in this way (Gr.Gr. 122, K.Pr. 131); to clean rice, etc., from chaff by blowing on it. phukᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (1 p.p. phucᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of a fire) blown up from the mouth; (of rice, etc.) cleaned from chaff, as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phū̃kᵘ, f. phǖ̃cᵘ̈; 2 p.p. phū̃cyōv), to smell (something), inhale (a scent) (Gr.Gr. 125); used met. in mad phū̃kun, to breathe forth pride, to display arrogance (cf. phukun) (K. 1052); to bellow (as a bull) (K.Pr. 49). phū̃kᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phǖ̃cᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), smelt (e.g. a flower).
m. the blowing a fine stream of liquid from the mouth, i.q. phukh (q.v.) (K. 152-3). phukⁱ trāwȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to spread abroad untrue and invented stories.

f. a kind of salt used for seasoning tea. It comes from the Nubra valley in Ladāk, and contains carbonate and sulphate of soda, with a little chloride of sodium (K.Pr. 39). --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'the salt to rise', (of a living being) quickly to become stout and fat. --ladüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to gain stoutness or fatness (owing to the accession of wealth or the like).

m. a measure of rice straw. The handful of stalks cut at one time by the sickle is bọ̆dᵘ, q.v. 2 bọ̆dᵘ = 1 ʦaph (q.v.), and 4 ʦaph = 1 phula. Near the river, where straw is sold for consumption, the handful is ʦaph, and 2 ʦaph = 1 phula. In each case 12 phulas = 1 kuru (q.v.). See L. 328.
m. (sg. dat. phulaṭi), a kind of club with a thick head bound with leather, an Indian club. phulaṭa-bözⁱ f. wielding, or practising with, Indian clubs (K. 947).

also written phulai f. blossoming, blooming (cf. bādam-phᵒ, p. 86b, l. 15; dā̃-phᵒ, p. 230b, l. 9; gŏrdölⁱ-phⁱ, p. 300b, l. 25; pōshĕ-phᵒ, s.v. pōsh 1) (Gr.Gr. 22, K.Pr. 56); spring time (El. phulai; Śiv. 181, 1720, 1727); the ripening of a small-pox pustule, or the like. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. blossoming to come on, the blossom-season (i.e. spring) to begin; small-pox pustules to begin to ripen. ¶ phulȧyĕ-gonᵘ adj. (f. -güñᵘ̈), thick blossoming; met. one who has many children, grandchildren, etc. --gañĕr -- m. abundance of descendants, the having many sons, daughters, and grandchildren; cf. phuli-gañĕr, p. 695a, l. 13. -dār m. (of a cloth) marked or embroidered with representations of flowers, flowered. -motᵘ adj. (f. -müʦᵘ̈), one who is devoted to blossoming, one who makes a practice of wasting his time in enjoying the season of flowers; one whose mind blossoms, one who has a rapturously joyful heart. -rang m. the nature of blossoming; hence, transientness, evanescence, impermanence. -sāl m. a picnic in the flower-season.

m. cataract (of the eyes). ¶ phulⁱ pĕni m. pl. inf. cataract to occur (in a person's eyes). ¶ phuli-chŏkh m. (sg. dat. -chŏkas), a slight boiling of vegetables. -gañĕr m. abundance of descendants (sons, daughters, grandchildren, etc.). Cf. phulayĕ-gañĕr, s.v. phulay.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. phulⁱladiñ), one who is afflicted with cataract of the eyes.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. phungᵘ; 2 p.p. phunjyōv), to become uncompleted, to be left unfinished; (in gambling) to be beaten by the other side; to miss the mark (in shooting). phungᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phunjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), uncompleted, left unfinished; unsuccessful (in gambling, shooting, etc.).
m. (sg. dat. phungaras), a short violent gust of wind or the like.
m. a boil (on the body); a nodosity or lump on a tree.

in phuñᵘ phŏkh m. (sg. dat. --phŏkas --), uninhabited, desolate, tenantless, deserted (e.g. a house or some place, such as a holy site, frequented only at certain seasons). --phŏkh gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become desolate, deserted, utterly destroyed (of a house or the like). Cf. phônᵘ.
m. the head of man or beast.
or phuphüjᵘ̈ f. (dim. of phuphulᵘ), a small head of man or beast (cf. hēri-phᵒ, p. 345b, l. 41; kala-phᵒ, p. 435a, l. 25).
m. longing, ardent desire. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. longing to engage in any work to occur, zeal to be shown.
(sg. dat. phurüʦᵘ̈), quick intelligence, brightness, sharpness; activity, quickness, alertness, nimbleness.
f. quivering, palpitation; sexual fury, rut, wild desire for sexual intercourse (cf. phurish); angry or impertinent contradiction.

f. desire for sexual intercourse, lustfulness (esp. when constantly possessing a person), satyriasis, nymphomania; cf. phūriñ. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such lustfulness to possess a person (male or female).
f. a time, opportunity, occasion (Rām. 488, 691); freedom (from), leisure, convenience (H. xii, 17); respite, reprieve, rest, ease (Rām. 663). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an opportunity to occur.
m. dexterity, skilled alertness. Cf. phurath.
f.pl.inf. false boasting, unfounded glorification (? cf. phᵃr 1).

f. roasted fish (El. phar, a kind of fish) (El.; K.Pr. 168, 242; K.Pr. 242, describes the way in which these are prepared). ¶ pharĕ gaʦhañĕ f. pl. inf. to become starved (for want of food). --karañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to starve (a person). Cf. phȧrⁱ-dag, p. 702b, l. 20. ¶ phari-gāḍa f.pl. small fish roasted together. -gôḍᵘ m. a seller of roasted fish. -hönzᵘ̈ m. a fisherman who nets small fish for roasting (K.Pr. 168). -ʦar m. a preparation of roasted fish as carried for sale in a basket on a woman's head.
f. a man's dead body, a corpse; cf. phorᵘ 1. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to become a corpse; hence, met. (of an invalid) to become wasted away.
m. old dry grass or straw (cf. gās-phᵒ, p. 307b, l. 1); rubbish, litter.

f. (sg. dat. phōsĕ), a kind of cap, made of leather lined with wool, and peaked. According to tradition this is the kind of cap that in ancient times was worn by Yĕchs or Kobolds. It is believed that if anyone can find a Yĕch's cap and put it under a millstone, the Yĕch becomes his servant (K.Pr. 141). --band gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'the Yĕch's cap to be fastened under a millstone'; hence (owing to falling into poverty) to become utterly dependent, to lose one's independence.
f. a noose (El. pháṅsi) (cf. nāga-phᵒ, p. 624a, l. 33) (Rām. 702-4); esp. a hangman's noose. Cf. phösⁱ.

in phuta-phuta m. tiny pieces (such as the result of the crumbling of decayed leaves or paper); cf. phta. -phuta gaʦhun m.inf. to crumble, as ab. -phuta karun m.inf. to crumble (something), as ab.; met. to adorn oneself (as a lover, male or female, before an assignation).
f. a morbid swelling, in dŏda-phuṭa, p. 189b, l. 46; i.q. phuṭh 1, q.v.

adj. c.g. (of something in metal) full of cracks or deep scratches (likely to end in cracks); (of cloth, paper, etc.), covered with creases (liable to cause tears); (of a conversation or the like) filled with intricacy or covert allusions (and leaving a shade of doubt or suspicion).
adj. c.g. (of a cloth, leaf, or the like) creased, wrinkled, puckered.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phuṭanôwᵘ), i.q. phuṭᵃrun and phuṭᵃrāwun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 204).
m.pl. intense irritation, formication, fierce itching (necessitating scratching). --tulȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to cause itching, to rouse itching. --wŏthȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. such itching to arise.
n.ag. (f. phuṭavüñᵘ̈), splitting, being broken, being smashed; easily broken, fragile; being broken in, being tamed, being brought to order, learning manners.

m. (sg. dat. phūṭas), discord, dissension, split, quarrel, feud; cf phuṭh 2. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. dissension to arise or take place (between or among), to be divided (in opinion, etc.). --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to sow discord (between or among), to set by the ears.
f. (sg. dat. phuṭi), a morbid swelling, a boil (cf. phuṭa and phuṭᵘ, also rata-phᵒ, s.v. rath.

f. (sg. dat. phuṭi), breakage, a crease, crack, split, flaw (Gr.Gr. 126); discord, dissension, feud; cf. phūṭh. --aʦüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a crack to come, a crease to appear (in leather, paper, or the like); the seeds of dissension between mutual friends to come into existence. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to form a crease between the nails (in a paper, or the like, preparatory to tearing it). --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to form a crease (for folding). -kara m. the remainder, what remains over. --ʦānüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to form a crease (in cloth, paper, or the like, by drawing between the finger-nails); (by calumny or the like) to plant a seed of dissension between two mutual friends. ¶ phuṭa-wād m. very small coin or the like (esp. when employed in making large payments). -wôṭᵘ adj. (f. -wöṭᵘ̈), joined after a break, that of which the cracks have been repaired; small coins, small change; a collection of broken useless things (dishes, ornaments, etc.).
adj. c.g. (of a cloth, leaf, or the like) creased, wrinkled, puckered; (of a conversation or the like) full of mystery, containing covert or indirect meaning.

m. a large parcel, a large package (cf. nāsti-phᵒ, p. 659a, l. 6); (a small bundle is phuṭᵃ̇jᵃ̇, q.v., Gr.Gr. 35). phuṭᵃ̇lᵃ̇ khasȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. 'bundles to rise', i.e. swellings, lumps, or intumescence to rise on the body (from disease, a beating, etc., or the swelling of the eyelids from weeping).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. phuṭᵘ, f. phuṭᵘ̈, dat. phucĕ; 2 p.p. phucyōv. Its causal is phuṭanāwun or phuṭᵃrāwun, Gr.Gr. 174), to be broken, smashed, broken down (cf. bāna phuṭȧnⁱ, p. 109b, l. 49, and p. 110a, l. 21; khōr phuṭun, p. 410a, l. 11; lyolᵘ phᵒ, p. 544a, l. 18) (Gr.Gr. 126, 174, 204; Gr.M.; Rām. 919, 933, 1659; K.Pr. 239); to burst out or forth, gush out; to be dispersed, be separated, detached; (of a limb) to be dislocated (cf. khōr phᵒ, p. 410a, l. 11; nakh phuṭȧnⁱ, p. 628a, l. 31) (Rām. 545, 779); to be tamed, brought low (e.g. a haughty person by grief), to be broken in (of a formerly naughty child or animal) (cf. naphᵃʦ phᵒ, p. 645b, l. 18) (K.Pr. 174); to be reduced, allayed, assuaged (e.g. a fever); to be broken, rendered useless, destroyed (cf. parĕ phuṭañĕ, s.v. parĕ). ¶ phuṭᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phuṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), broken, smashed; burst forth; tamed, brought low, broken in; allayed, assuaged. phuṭan-hār n.ag. c.g. that which is easily broken, fragile.

m. languor, weakness, infirmity; defect, imperfection, unsoundness; coolness; discord, quarrelling, quarrel, row, riot. phutūra tulun m.inf. to raise discord, bring about quarrelling (by slander, causing opposition, or the like). --wŏthun -- m.inf. quarrelling or discord to arise.

or phuṭᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. (f. of phuṭulᵘ, q.v.), a small bundle (of clothes or the like) (Gr.Gr. 35); a packet, a parcel, a bundle (cf. buhᵃ̇rᵃ̇-phᵃ̇, p. 96b, l. 28; burza-phᵒ, p. 130b, l. 47; dā̃-phᵒ, p. 230b, l. 20; khanḍa-phᵒ, p. 403a, l. 1; nāsti-phᵒ, p. 659a, l. 5) (Gr.M.).

f. (sg. dat. phuṭᵃrüñᵃ), uttering reproof or the like (against some ill-conducted person), breaking in (a boor to good manners) (Gr.Gr. 121). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to reproach, discipline (an unruly child).

or phuṭarāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. phuṭᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. phuṭᵃrun, q.v., in all its meanings; to break, smash, shiver, shatter (cf. ḍĕkas ḍūnⁱ phuṭarāwȧnⁱ, p. 205a, l. 18, and hāṭh phuṭarāwun, p. 358a, l. 12) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 126, 1531, 1807; K. 824; YZ. 484; K.Pr. 87, 171, 187); to break (something) open, to burst (something) open (Gr.M.). phuṭᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. phuṭᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. phuṭᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, s.v. phuṭᵃrun (K.Pr. 11).

or phuṭarun conj. 1 (1 p.p. phuṭᵒrᵒ), to break, smash (something) (cf. hĕng phuṭarȧnⁱ, p. 339a, l. 34; khōr phuṭᵃrun, p. 410a, l. 13) (Gr.Gr. 121, 204; L.V. 26; Rām. 140, 552, 738; K. 350, 758, 825; K.Pr. 92, 139); to dislocate (a limb or the like) (H. ii, 11; xii, 3, 4; K.Pr. 57); to break (something) open (Rām. 405, K. 461); to disperse, separate, detach; to tame, break in (to good manners) (cf. hāṭh phᵒ, p. 358a, l. 8); to allay, assuage (e.g. a fever); to break with, give up (cf. bāna-khörᵘ̈ phuṭarüñᵘ̈, p. 109b, l. 39); to exchange a coin or other money of high value for several of low value, to get small change for a bank-note or coin of value; to break or disobey (a command) (Rām. 1209, 1753). ¶ phuṭᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. phuṭᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), broken, smashed, dislocated; dispersed, separated; tamed, broken in; (of a fever, or the like) assuaged (by something); (of money of large value) turned into small coin, turned into small change. ¶ phuṭᵃrith ʦhunun m.inf. to smash (something).
m. a morbid swelling, a boil (cf. rata-phᵒ, s.v. rath); i.q. phuṭh 1, q.v.

adj. (f. phuṭᵘ̈ 1, sg. dat. phucĕ), (properly 1 p.p. of phuṭun, q.v.), broken, used --˚ as in banda-phᵒ, p. 111a, l. 23; dạndᵃri-phᵃ, p. 226a, l. 49; hĕnga-phᵒ, p. 339a, l. 46; lanjĕ-phᵒ, p. 526a, l. 30; nala-phᵒ, p. 632a, l. 29. --phrôṭᵘ -- m. a pile of broken pieces, a rubbish-heap.

f. (sg. dat. phucĕ), a fold, plait, pucker, crease (all with idea of the beginning of a break); a wrinkle (El.); met. doubt or suspicion raised by a mystery heard in conversation. --˚ a broken piece of anything, something broken (cf. aina-phᵒ, p. 30b, l. 9; kalama-phᵒ, p. 440a, l. 1; kangañi-phᵒ, p. 457a, l. 18; kangȧvⁱ-phⁱ, p. 457a, l. 35; kȧrⁱ-phⁱ, p. 467a, l. 4; lĕjĕ-phᵒ, p. 517a, l. 5).

(for 1, see phoṭᵘ 3) f. a little cupboard under the roof of a house, an attic-closet (used as a store-room). phŏcĕ f.pl. an open space or niche over a window or side door of a house (in which firewood is kept to dry).

f. disgrace, shame, ignominy; abuse. --khë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to eat abuse, to experience abuse, to be abused. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to abuse (a person). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. abuse to fall (on a person), to be subjected to a scolding (by a superior or schoolmaster).
m. in phyāh barun m.inf. to feel anxiety or solicitude (in the desire to prevent some apprehended evil) (K. 286). --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to become filled with such solicitude.
f. loud and continued lamentations at some one's absence. Cf. phyāh.

m. strained water, the dirty water squeezed out of something that has been washed, or the water strained off after cooking (cf. atha-phᵒ, p. 61a, l. 35) (Gr.Gr. 124). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. refuse water to come into existence; met. something to turn out wrong, a wrong result (causing disappointment) unexpectedly or owing to some mistake to come from any action. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to pour or strain off the water (in which food has been cooked). --karun -- m.inf. to make refuse water; hence, to perform some improper work causing disappointment by its results. --nīrith gaʦhun -- m.inf. straining water to issue forth; met. some one's secret or opinions to be let out (with deplorable results) in the presence of his enemy (esp. when done ignorantly). --nīrith ʦalun -- m.inf. unseasonable or objectionable words suddenly and unexpectedly to be uttered or divulged. --trāwun -- m.inf. to strain off, or wring out, water (after cooking or washing).

m. (f. phyörᵘ̈), one who is deaf and dumb (cf. maʦa-phᵒ, p. 602b, l. 12). phyāra-katha f.pl. the talk of a deaf and dumb person (i.e. speaking on the fingers or by gestures); similar nonsense (even if distinct) uttered by one who is not deaf and dumb.
m. in phir-phyār (see phir), apparently a jingle-word.
f. (sg. dat. phyārüñᵘ̈), straining off, filtering.
f. pouring a liquid off from the dregs, or (vice versa) the pouring off of superfluous liquid from something being soaked, straining off, filtering.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. phyôrᵘ), to strain off, filter (Gr.Gr. 124, Gr.M., Śiv. 1032); to pour off superfluous water (from things soaked, boiled, etc.). ¶ phyôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phyörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), strained, filtered; (of the liquid) strained off, filtered off (from something). ¶ phyāran-dȧjⁱ or -düjᵘ̈ f. a piece of muslin through which a liquid is filtered, a filtering cloth. ¶ phyörinⁱ bônᵘ m. a vessel for filtering, a strainer. -wôñᵘ m. water which has been strained off, percolated water.
m. eccentric conduct (marked by incoherence of speech and action, etc.).

f. (sg. dat. phyāʦi), a rude, clumsy, ignorant woman, incoherent and crack-brained or eccentric in speech or action. Cf. phyôtᵘ. ¶ phyāʦa-kŏnḍal f., i.q. phyāʦh. -kŏnḍul m. a man who acts in this way. -katha f.pl. incoherent words, nonsensical babbling.
or phyuhᵘ m. (sg. dat. phĕhis or phihis), a kind of paddle or broad spade used for removing snow from house-roofs, or for scraping up mud in the streets.

m. (sg. dat. phĕkis), the shoulder (El. phúk, phyuk, pyuk) (Gr.M.); the shoulder of a garment. ¶ phĕkⁱ-örⁱ f. a circlet of rope or the like put on the shoulder to support a burden carried thereon. -dajal or -dajĕl adj. c.g. (of a garment) patched on the shoulder. --gŏgal gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the shoulders to become turnips, the shoulders to become blistered from carrying a heavy burden. -gav m. a garment of which the shoulder is tattered and torn (cf. gāv 1). -holᵘ m. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), (of a person, a picture, a garment) crooked shouldered. -pholᵘ 1 m. the round bone of the shoulder; a shoulder of mutton. -pholᵘ 2 adj. (f. -phüjᵘ̈), broken shouldered; shoulder-weary. --phalȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the shoulders to be split, pain in the shoulder due to frequently carrying heavy burdens to be felt. -palav m. the coat of the shoulder, i.e. the skin over the shoulder; the piece of cloth that forms the shoulder of a garment; a pad placed on the shoulder for carrying burdens. -ʦumᵃṭh f. (sg. dat. ʦumᵃṭi), a pinch or nip on the bare shoulder. -ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. a slap on the bare shoulder. This used to be a school punishment inflicted on one boy by another at the teacher's order. --wasȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the shoulders to descend, i.e. to be sore from carrying a heavy burden, the shoulders to be lowered or bowed from this cause. -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), the sewing of the shoulder-piece on to a garment, the shoulder-seam (by which a separate piece of cloth is added). ¶ phĕkĕn-hondᵘ shrapun phyārĕn m. the digestion of the strainings (cf. phyôrᵘ) (to become the property) of (one's own) shoulders; hence, any thing, action, or employment done by oneself to result only to one's own profit (even though undertaken for another). ¶ phĕkyukᵘ sg. gen. (f. phĕkicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the shoulder (of the body, or of a garment).

m. (sg. dat. phĕkis), a pinch (of any powder or the like. It is taken up between the tips of the fingers) (cf. nāsti-phᵒ, p. 659a, l. 8). Cf. phë̆ṭᵘ̈ 1, phyoṭᵘ, and pyukᵘ. phĕki phĕki dawāh m. medicine by pinches (i.e. taken over and over again); hence, some one or something which gives delight (e.g. a wife, son, servant, relation, or the like, who arrives at the right time just when he or she is wanted or expected, or any material object similarly come to hand).

m. (sg. dat. phĕris), a drop or spot (of any liquid) (cf. ȧshⁱ-phⁱ, p. 47b, l. 46; cyū̃-phᵒ, p. 179a, l. 18; mas-phᵒ, p. 585b, l. 38; pā̃-phᵒ, s.v. pôñᵘ; ras-phᵒ, s.v. ras; rata-phᵒ, s.v. rath) (Rām. 845, 1189, 1334, 1562); a very small quantity (of any liquid or semi-liquid) (cf. añĕma-phᵒ, p. 37b, l. 8; dŏda-phᵒ, p. 189b, l. 50; mᵃtra-phᵃ, p. 605b, l. 21; pāka-phᵒ, p. 725b, l. 12; pā̃-phᵒ, s.v. pôñᵘ) (Śiv. 1210); a round spot (esp. when intended as a mark of identification) (cf. ȧchⁱ-phⁱ, p. 8b, l. 14); a point (El. phur); cf. phyūrᵘ 2. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to put a spot, to mark with a spot for identification; to mark spots in a written paper in order to indicate a passage to be cancelled. ¶ phĕrⁱ-wād m. one who deals with liquid articles in drops, one who serves out by drops. ¶ phĕri phĕri adv. drop by drop.
adj. (f. phyörᵘ̈), 1 p.p. of phyārun, q.v., used --˚ as adj., strained, having the refuse water poured off (cf. aḍa-phyôrᵘ, p. 11b, l. 37; phĕkĕn-hondᵘ shrapun phyārĕn, p. 721a, l. 11).
or phyūshᵘ, see phĕshun or phēshun.

m. (sg. dat. phĕstis), one who (in conduct or any business) is wanting in profoundness, wanting in vigour, empty-headedness. phĕsta-kākañ f. a woman who by age or position is entitled to respect, but who is really silly, unpleasing in appearance, and indolent.

m. (sg. dat. phĕtis), a kind of puffed out flower in silk-embroidery (cf. pholᵘ-phᵘ, p. 694a, l. 43). ¶ phĕtⁱ-dār adj. c.g. embroidered with such flowers. -khọ̆bᵘ m. a quilted cap embroidered with such flowers. -kalapushᵘ m. a kind of cap embroidered with such flowers worn by newly born babies. -kū̃sh f. a kind of shoe (see kū̃sh) ornamented with such flowers (worn by brides, etc.). -lāgay f. the art of making such flowers, flower-embroidery. -pulahorᵘ m. grass shoes ornameṇted on the toes with these flowers. -ṭūpⁱ f. a quilted cap so ornamented. -wö̃ka f.pl. the long plaited tresses hanging down a woman's back when so ornamented.
m. as much fine powder as can be lifted between the tips of the fingers, a pinch of dust (cf. nāsti-phᵒ, p. 659a, l. 9). Cf. phë̆tᵘ̈ 1 and phyokᵘ 2.

adj. (f. phyöʦᵘ̈), an ignorant boorish fellow (rude in speech, gait, clothing, eating, action, and so on), a stupid boor, a Tony Lumpkin, one who (like a lunatic) does everything the wrong way and contrary to custom. Cf. phrôtᵘ and phyāʦh.
see phērun, as adj. --˚, cf. rasa- phyūrᵘ, that of which the juice has returned, revivified, s.v. ras.

(for 1, see phirun) m. (sg. dat. phiri s; abl. phiri, cf. phirᵘ̈ 1), reversal of motion, inversion (cf. dōrĕ-phᵒ, p. 237a, l. 1; mūla-phᵒ, p. 567a, l. 38; man-phᵒ, p. 572a, l. 17; mañĕ-phᵒ, p. 586a, l. 3; nama-phᵒ, p. 635b, l. 43; nāwa-phᵒ, p. 665b, l. 36) (Śiv. 1834); reversal (of habit, nature, hopes, etc.) (cf. achĕn- pacĕ-phyurᵘ, p. 9a, l. 17; khisⁱ-phⁱ, p. 429a, l. 4); turning (something) away or backwards (cf. buthⁱ-phⁱ, p. 142b, l. 40); confusion, doing something in wrong order (e.g. in distribution of anything, giving to the wrong person, changing one's speech by directing it to a new person, or changing the direction of one's glances) (cf. ȧchⁱ-phⁱ, p. 8b, l. 17; atha-phᵒ, a slip of the hand, p. 61a, l. 37); making a mistake in counting (and having to do it over again), or counting backwards (cf. grünzᵘ̈-phᵘ̈, p. 303b, l. 39); disarranging order (e.g. of the leaves of a book); disarrangement, wrong order (cf. khrāwa-phᵒ, p. 416a, l. 40); ¶ turning (clothes inside out) (K.Pr. 258, phur); turning (a box or vessel) upside down; turning over (the leaves of a book) (K. 951); doing something backwards and forwards (cf. dōri-phᵒ, p. 237a, l. 31); doing (something) backwards or back again (cf. gaza-phᵒ, p. 318b, l. 16); repetition, doing something over again (cf. āla-phᵒ, p. 22b, l. 2); ¶ change, exchange (of one thing for another) (cf. pacĕ-phᵒ, s.v. püṭᵘ̈); change (of place or the like) (cf. jāyĕ-phᵒ, p. 380a, l. 17); wandering about, sauntering (cf. phyūrᵘ 3 and kōca-phᵒ, p. 383a, l. 28); ¶ returns (in business) (cf. lacha-phᵒ, p. 506b, l. 47; paĩsa-phᵒ, s.v. paĩsa). ¶ phyurᵘ gaʦhun m.inf. reversal to occur; esp. (in any action, such as counting, studying, teaching, giving, going, etc.) in forgetfulness of the right order to do it in the wrong order. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to set (things out of order) in order. --karun -- m.inf. to set in disorder (e.g. by interrupting a calculation, reading, lesson, etc., or by disarranging the order of the leaves of a book). -thurᵘ m. simultaneous coming and going of people (e.g. mutual friends) between two places (e.g. their respective homes). -thurᵘ karun m.inf. to make such mutual visits (e.g. the customary interchange of visits between the two families immediately after a wedding, or between relations after the death of a relation). Cf. phērun thōrun, p. 706a, l. 38.

(for 1, see phērun) m. (sg. dat. phīris; abl. phēri), a kind of thorn (? apparently like those round a thistle flower); a drop, a spot, a small lump (cf. phyorᵘ; ȧshⁱ-phⁱ, p. 47b, l. 48; mas-phᵒ, p. 595b, l. 38; mᵃtra-phᵃ, p. 605b, l. 21; pā̃-phᵒ, s.v. pôñᵘ; ras-phᵒ, s.v. ras; rata-phᵒ, s.v. rath) (El. phūr, K.Pr. 244); a very small quantity (of any liquid or semi-liquid) (cf. añĕma-phᵒ, p. 37b, l. 11; dŏda-phᵒ, p. 189b, l. 50). ¶ phēri-dār adj. c.g. (of new woollen cloth or the like), full of knots or lumps of wool. --nērun 1 -- m.inf. such knots to disappear (from new woollen cloth); hence, to show signs of wearing out, to look worn. -phamb m. the kind of wool which produces cloth full of these knots, i.e. the wool from which pashmīna cloth is made.
m. wandering about, sauntering (cf. phyurᵘ 2, col. a, l. 20 ab.). phēri nērun 2 m.inf. to go forth a-saunter, to wander through bye-lanes selling things, to go out hawking.
m. (sg. dat. phishis), a certain medicinal root (used for making plasters for wounds, boils, or the like).
or phish m. in kan-phᵒ, p. 447b, l. 5, the getting of something into the ear. ? Cf. pyushᵘ, a flea, a small particle, or ? cf. the preceding.
m. splitting or cutting open (a fish, fruit, or the like). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to split open (a fruit, etc.), to rip up the belly (of a man or other animate being).
m. secret anger, resentment (esp. when excited by another's calumny, traducing, etc.).
n.ag. (f. phᵃhavüñᵃ), (a part of the body) which causes great pain (owing to a wound or a burn, etc.), smarting.

or phuhun conj. 1 (1 p.p. phᵒhᵒ or phuhᵘ; f. phᵘ̈hᵘ̈ or phuhᵘ̈; 2 p.p. phᵃhyōv or phuhyōv), to split open the belly (e.g. of a fish or fowl for cleaning), to cut open (a fruit or the like). Cf. phāshun and phᵃh 1. ¶ phᵒhᵒ-motᵒ or phuhᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. phᵘ̈hᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ or phuhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), having the belly split, cut open, as ab. ¶ phᵃhan-wôlᵃ 1 or phuhan-wôlᵘ 1 n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who splits open bellies, etc., as ab.

or phuhun 2 m. the experience of severe pain (in some part of the body, from a wound, burning, etc.); inward wrath, secret anger, inward hostility (against some one); see Gr.Gr. 192. In both cases the pain or wrath must be felt by a man (Gr.Gr. 120); see phᵃhᵃñᵃ. phᵃhan-wôlᵃ 2 or phuhan-wôlᵘ 2 n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who excites hostility or who fans already existing hostility (e.g. by calumniating, traducing, or the like).

or phuhᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ conj. 1 [1 p.p. f. phᵘ̈hᵘ̈ or phuhᵘ̈; 2 p.p. f. phᵃhyēyĕ or phuhyēyĕ. This verb is impersonal, the logical subject being put in the dative, thus phᵃhi-y, there will be inward anger to thee, i.e. thou wilt be inwardly angry (Gr.Gr. 203). In tenses capable of expressing gender they are always put into the feminine, thus phᵃhān chĕ-s, there is inward anger to him, he is inwardly angry (Gr.Gr. 182); phᵘ̈hᵘ̈s, he was inwardly angry (Gr.Gr. 215); the verbal noun or infinitive may be either masculine or feminine (Gr.Gr. 192). Thus phᵃhun 2 (q.v.) or phᵃhᵃñᵃ, inward anger, the former referring to the anger of a man, and the latter to that of a woman (Gr.Gr. 120). The causal of this verb is phuhanāwun, not phuhᵃrāwun (Gr.Gr. 174)]. ¶ Severe pain to be felt in some part of the body, to be painful, to ache (Gr.Gr. 188, 215, 248); inward wrath or hostility to be felt, secret anger to burn within one (against some one). --diñᵘ̈ --  f.inf. by calumny or the like to urge on one who already has an inward anger against a person to still further anger; to add fuel to the flame of hostility. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. inward wrath or hostility to be further increased (by calumny, opposition, or the like). --phᵃhᵃñᵃdiñᵃ -- f.inf. again and again to add fuel to the flame of a person's wrath or hostility.

or phar 1 m. false talk, esp. a cock-and-bull story, a tall yarn (intended to cause laughter or astonishment) (K.Pr. 219). --trāwun -- m.inf. to tell publicly a cock-and-bull story, to spin a yarn. --wanun -- m.inf. to tell such a story.
m. in phᵃr-phᵃr onomat. m. the sound caused by burning leaves or paper. phᵃra-phᵃra gaʦhun m.inf. the sound of blazing leaves to occur; a burning sensation to be felt inside the body.
f. a hurrying woman, one in agitated hurry.

m. hidden rage in one person or in a body of persons, caused by opposition; general discontent or dissatisfaction; secret disaffection. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such disaffection to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to cause, or be a cause of, such disaffection.

adj. c.g. (of some solid food) decayed (so that at a touch it will fall to pieces), rotten. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become decayed (as ab.), to go bad. --karun -- m.inf. to spoil food (by ignorantly treating it so that it decays or goes bad).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. phᵃsyōv), inward anger to be felt, secret resentment to be experienced. Cf. phŏshüñᵘ̈.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phᵃsᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. phᵃsᵃrun, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. phᵃsᵃrᵃ), to cause a person to be inwardly wrathful, to fill with inward anger (by opposing him, by non-compliance, or the like).
m. urging, incitement. --karun -- m.inf. to keep on urging, to continue incitement.
m. a load carried on the back. --anun -- m.inf. to fasten a load on the back (by a cloth brought under the arms and tied).
f. twisting, contortion, writhing; intricacy, perplexity, trouble; tenesmus, colic, gripes.
a jingle of nicᵘ̈, see p. 670a, l. 45.
f. pain, agony, suffering, distress (K. 104); a nuisance, cause of annoyance (El. pida); fever (El.).
f. (sg. dat. pīḍanas), a certain part of a spinning-wheel (? the driving-band).
f. (sg. dat. pihüñᵘ̈), the act of grinding. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to do grinding, to keep on urging an unwilling or careless worker.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pihanôwᵘ), to cause to be ground (in a mill, etc.), to get ground; causal of pihun, q.v. pihanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pihanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), got ground, that which one person has caused another to grind.
f. wages paid for grinding, a miller's fee.
n.ag. (f. pihavüñᵘ̈), one who is grinding (wheat, etc.), a grinder, a miller.
m. an ox-goad, the painā of Hindōstān (K.Pr. 219, wrongly translated 'yoke').

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pyuhᵘ, f. pishᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 210; 2 p.p. pishyōv, Gr.Gr. 225), to grind (grain, etc., in a mill) (Gr.Gr. 31, Gr.M., L. 460); met. to thrash, beat, pound, thwack, goad (cf. dā̃da-pᵒ, p. 187b, l. 13). --karun -- m.inf. to beat (in the way of school correction with a light rod), to give a flogging (to a schoolboy or the like). ¶ pihⁱ pihⁱ ʦhunun m.inf. persistently to teach (a stupid or inattentive pupil), to repeat a lesson to him over and over again so as to impress it on his memory. ¶ pihan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one whose profession is that of grinding (corn, etc.), a miller. ¶ pyuhᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pishᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), ground (in a mill).
(? spelling and gender), a kind of deer, the Goral, Cemas or Nemorhaedus goral (L. 115).
m. (f. pikᵘ̈ṭᵘ̈), a very small child (esp. a suckling); ? a certain large fish (L. 158, pikút or pekri gāḍ).
f. (sg. dat. pilüñᵘ̈), arriving at, reaching to (esp. something lofty, the end of a difficult task, or a high place) (Gr.Gr. 121, K.Pr. 257).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pilanôwᵘ), i.q. pilanun and pilawun, qq.v. (Gr.Gr. 171, W. 139); to hold out, or hand (a thing to some one) (K.Pr. 7); cf. pilun. pilanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pilanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. pilonᵘ-motᵘ (s.v. pilanun) and pilowᵘ-motᵘ (s.v. pilawun), qq.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pilonᵘ), to cause to arrive, to cause to reach, to cause to succeed in accomplishment, to cause to reach up to, to hold out, or hand (a thing to some one) (K.Pr. 228); to convey (to a person or place); cf. pilun, pilanāwun, and pilawun. pilonᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pilüñᵘ̈ -müʦᵘ̈), caused to arrive, etc., as ab.; conveyed.
m. an upstairs veranda, a covered balcony (supported below by pillars in the open air) (cf. potᵘ pᵒ, s.v. potᵘ). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to erect such a veranda.

f. (sg. dat. pilavüñᵘ̈), the causing (of a thing) to arrive elsewhere; sending (a thing) to some destination or recipient; the causing to reach, the distance to which (something) may be made to reach, the reach (of anything) (cf. atha-pᵒ, p. 61a, l. 45). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to send (a thing) on by means of several people passing it from hand to hand.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pilowᵘ), to cause (a thing or news) to reach a person (sending it by some one), i.q. pilanun and pilanāwun (Gr.Gr. 171), qq.v.; to hold out (something) to a person (W. 139, pilanāwun; K.Pr. 127). pilowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pilüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (a thing or news) sent from one person to another through a third person. Cf. pilonᵘ-motᵘ (s.v. pilanun) and pilanôwᵘ-motᵘ (s.v. pilanāwun).
n.ag. (f. pilavüñᵘ̈), that which can be reached to from below (cf. atha-pᵒ, p. 61a, l. 47).
adv. at any time, at all, ever.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. pyulᵘ, f. pijᵘ̈. According to I.K. this verb is conj. 3, with 2 p.p. pilyōv. The causal of this verb is pilawun, pilanun, or pilanāwun, Gr.Gr. 171), to arrive, reach to, reach up to, succeed in accomplishing, to be able to do (e.g. something high up or at a distance, the accomplishment of a difficult task or business, the mastery of some branch of learning, and so on) (cf. nazar pilüñᵘ̈, p. 676a, l. 22) (Gr.Gr. 13, 121; Śiv. 785; K.Pr. 170). pyulᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pijᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), one who has arrived, one who has mastered (something difficult), one who has reached (something high up), and so on, as ab.

m. childbirth, delivery, confinement, bearing a child (cf. buḍa-pᵒ, p. 85a, l. 50; potᵘ pīn, s.v. potᵘ); cf. pīñᵘ̈. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give birth. ¶ pīna-pyāwal f. a woman who has brought forth children, a matron. ¶ pīnukᵘ or pyūnukᵘ sg. gen. (f. pīnücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a birth (cf. buḍa-pᵒ, p. 85b, l. 1). This word is often used with ordinal numerals, as in dŏyⁱmi pyūnukᵘ, of the second birth (e.g. connected with a woman's second labour), and so on.
f. (sg. dat. pinaki), intoxication, stupor, drowsiness.
f. (of a woman) normally pregnant, in the family way; one who has just borne a child.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pīnowᵘ), (of a midwife) to deliver a woman in childbirth, to bring a woman's children into the world; (cf. prasun). pīnüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ perf. part. f. (of a woman) one who has given birth to a child.
f. (sg. dat. pindi), a certain waterfowl, the Indian Little Grebe, Tachybaptes albipennis (L. 123). pindi-ṭhūl m. its egg.

m. pride, haughtiness, arrogance, conceit, contempt for others. --anun -- m.inf. to show contempt. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. contempt to be displayed. --khasun -- m.inf. contempt to arise, i.e. to be felt (e.g. for another's actions), want of consideration (for another's labours) to be shown.

f. a kind of small millet, Panicum italicum (El. also pingi; L. 330, 337, ping, panicum miliaceum; K.Pr. 87). -hyolᵘ m. a head of the seeds of this millet. -tūjⁱ f. the husked seed of this millet. ¶ pingi-kāṭh m. (sg. dat. -kāṭhas), its stalk. -rôchᵘ m. a kind of scarecrow used in a field of this millet for the purpose of frightening away birds. It is a post stuck in the ground, with a number of black rags fastened at its top. -wŏgra m. a porridge or gruel of this millet from which the water in which the grains have been cooked has not been strained off. -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), a porridge of this millet from which the water in which it has been cooked has been drained off.
f. (sg. dat. pingüñᵘ̈), in sŏna- pingan, p. 917a, l. 48, q.v.
adj. c.g. secret, hidden, concealed (H. vii, 10).
m. a great-grandson, the son of a daughter's daughter (cf. par-pinzurᵘ, p. 751a, l. 50).
or pinzürᵘ̈ f. a great- granddaughter, the daughter of a daughter's daughter (cf. par-pinzürᵘ̈, p. 751b, l. 2).

(for 1, see pēn) f. (of a woman) having had a child, used --˚ with numerals, as in du-pīñᵘ̈, having had two children; trᵃ-pīñᵃ, having had three children; ʦu-pᵒ, having had four children; pānʦa-pᵒ, having had five children, and so on. Cf. pīn.
m. a cask, a barrel (the Portuguese pipa, borrowed through Hindōstānī pīpā) (Gr.M.).
in pipal-kulᵘ m. the holy fig-tree, Ficus religiosa.
f. a kind of musical instrument, blown into at one end through a narrow mouthpiece (cf. marʦa-pᵒ, s.v. marʦ); a frog-shaped earthen- ware musical instrument, used by children as a toy. Cf. shīna-pᵒ.
f. persistent pursuit, unremitting pursuit, unceasing urging or imploring. --ganḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. persistently to importune.

m. an old man (cf. rĕshⁱ-pⁱ, s.v. ryoshᵘ); a saint (Muslim), a holy man (W. 155; H. v, 8; vi, 13); a spiritual guide or father (Muslim) (cf. bē-pīr, p. 162, l. 29) (L. 270; W. 22; K.Pr. 170-1, 181, 189, 196-7, 212, 246, 252); a magician (hardly to be distinguished from the preceding); a founder or head of a religious order (Muslim); Monday (W. 107). -manī f. respect paid to a spiritual teacher (or similar revered person). -manī gōr-manī f. such respect paid to a Muslim or Hindū spiritual preceptor (or to a similar revered person). -marạd پیر مرد c.g. an old person (man or woman) (L. 458, piri mard); cf. mard. -murīdī پیر مریدی f. discipleship of a saint, the following of the profession of religion (Musalmān) (L. 308). -nĕcyuwᵘ m. the son of a magician or religious teacher (who, by his father's knowledge and practice of appropriate charms, has acquired exceptional virility); a boy descended from such a magician or religious teacher. -parast پیر پرست adj. and subst. c.g. a saint-worshipper, one who habitually spends his time worshipping saints (L. 286). ¶ pīra-üṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -acĕ), a meeting of heads of a religious order (for worship, etc.); a meeting of magicians (for incantations, etc.). -böcⁱ-baṭh f. (sg. dat. -böcⁱ-baṭi), the occupation of a number of heads of a religious order, or of magicians, for a common object (cf. bāca-baṭh, p. 79b, l. 32). -bôgᵘ m. the share (given to) a religious teacher (out of property). -böjⁱ-baṭh f. (sg. dat. -böjⁱ-baṭi), the partnership of spiritual teachers or magicians (e.g. in disciples, servants, or the like). -bāy  f. (a female pīr is pīröñᵘ̈, q.v.) the wife of a spiritual teacher or magician. -drāl m. a magician's broker, a go-between between him and his clients. -ganḍ m. the persistence of a magician (in uttering spells), the obstinate utterance of some spell till its results become apparent. -gurᵘ m. a religious teacher or magician's horse (well treated, groomed, and fed, quiet and willing); any horse with the above characteristics. -kūrᵘ̈ f. the daughter of a magician or religious teacher (who, through her father's knowledge and practice of appropriate charms, has attained to exceptional physical vigour); a girl descended from such a magician or religious teacher. -lĕkh f. (sg. dat. -lĕki), abuse directed against a person's spiritual teacher. -phŏkh m. (sg. dat. phŏkas), the breathing of a magician or religious teacher (e.g. as when called to an epileptic or person suffering from demoniacal possession, he cures him by breathing over him with appropriate spells). -pholᵘ m. the bead (of crystal, coral, precious stone, or the like) worn on the neck or elsewhere by a magician or religious teacher as a sign of his vocation. -röchⁱ f. the protection of (i.e. afforded by) a spiritual teacher or magician (in the way of a spell, charm, blessing, or the like). -stān m. the head-quarters of a magician or spiritual teacher (where he gives forth his blessings and his curses); a place rendered holy by the presence of such a person or by his being buried there. -wān m. the head-quarters of a magician or of a spiritual teacher, to which epileptics, persons possessed of demons, or the like, resort to be cured by him. -war m. the boon or blessing conferred by a spiritual teacher. -wara adj. c.g. a person who habitually blesses or curses by charms, spells, or the like (esp. when in trances). -wörᵘ̈  f. a place where a number of magicians or religious teachers have assembled.

or pīrᵘ̈ 1 f. a square four-legged stool (also used as a small table, El.) (Gr.Gr. 62, pīrᵘ̈; Gr.M. pīrᵘ̈; Śiv. 1016); the preface (of a book); a pedigree, a race or generation of progenitors or descendants. ¶ pīri-bāgay f. dividing out or forming a brȧnch of a pedigree. -dūrĕr m. distance of relationship. -gạnzᵃran f. (sg. dat. -gạnzᵃrüñᵃ), calculation of a pedigree, ascertainment of relationship (as required in marriage arrangements). -kā̃gᵃr f. a written pedigree. -woturᵘ m., id.
f. a criminal charge (esp. when made to an official). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a charge (true or false) to be made. Cf. pēra yunᵘ, p. 752a, l. 33.

f. a half walnutshell (cf. ḍūnⁱ-pīr, p. 224a, l. 20) (El. a nut, m.). pīri-cỗṭᵘ m. walnutshell-mouthed, one with a mouth shut together like the two halves of a walnutshell facing each other; met. one who keeps his conusel, sparing of words, close-mouthed, taciturn.
f. the condition, state, occupation, or profession of a Muslim spiritual teacher or of a magician (cf. pīr 1).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pironᵘ), to string (beads, pearls, etc.); cf. pirun. pironᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pirüñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), strung (as ab.).
m. old age, oldness (of the human body).
f. old age, senility, decrepitude; the status or condition of a Muslim saint or spiritual guide; honour, reverence (paid to a person as though he were a spiritual guide).
f. the exercise of the functions of a Musalmān spiritual guide, the profession or practice of a magician.
f. a female Musalman teacher; a female magician, a sorceress. Cf. pīr 1.
f. the profession, occupation, or status of a pīr, q.v.
in pirth-paiwand (? spelling), m. grafting, budding (L. 458). Cf. barga-paiwand, p. 120a, l. 44.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pyurᵘ), to string (beads, pearls, etc.); cf. piranun. pyurᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pirᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), strung, as ab.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. pīryōv), to be, or become, smooth, slippery, or (from cooking, corruption, etc.) greasy, slimy. pīryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pīryē-müʦᵘ̈), become smooth or slimy (e.g. from corruption); become greasy or soft and slimy from cooking.
f. a stool, a low table, i.q. pīr 2, q.v. in all its meanings (Gr.Gr. 62) (cf. danda-pīrᵘ̈, p. 224b, l. 50).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pisanôwᵘ), to cause to boil over (Gr.Gr. 174).
m. softness, tenderness, delicateness, daintiness (cf. atha-pᵒ, p. 61b, l. 10) (Gr.Gr. 141).

(1 p.p. pishĕlôwᵘ), to make soft, tender, delicate, to soften; to appease; to make (a person) soft, i.e. to tantalize an expectant recipient or the like, by repeated delays, by causing him to come unsuccessfully again and again, and so on. pishĕlôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pishĕlövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), softened; appeased; tantalized, as ab.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. pishĕlyōv), to become soft, tender, delicate; to become appeased; to become affectionate. pishĕlyō-motᵘ perf. part. pishĕlyē-müʦᵘ̈), become soft, appeased, etc.
or pishulᵘ adj. (m. sg. dat. pishilis; f. pishüjᵘ̈ or pishijᵘ̈), tender, delicate, smooth, soft (of woollen goods, El.) (Gr.Gr. 141, L. 464).
m. the nipple of the breast (El.).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. pisyōv. The causal of this verb is pisanāwun, not pisᵃrāwun, Gr.Gr. 174), (of boiling liquid) to boil over (Gr.Gr. 174); to be spluttered from the mouth. pisith yunᵘ m.inf. to come to the point of boiling over; to be distracted, bewildered, perplexed, moidered.
m. (of a child, or the like) little, small, puny, spare. -pholᵘ m. a small ball made of lac (used as a toy, being flipped at a mark with the fingers).
m. he who wears a yellow garment, a N. of the god Vishnu (Viṣṇu) (Śiv. 344, 793, 1168, 1440).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. piṭanôwᵘ), to cause (a person) to lament, to distress, to harrow, torment.
(1 p.p. pīṭanôwᵘ), to weary (a person) by causing him to wait, to keep a person dancing attendance. pīṭanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pīṭanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), wearied, as ab.
m. a large kind of covered basket, a portmanteau (K.Pr. 189).
f. one who harasses another by delay in the performance of some urgent work; the being harassed, as ab.
see pitur 2; pitarĕñi-tônᵘ (Rām. 1778), see pitᵃ̇rᵃ̇-tônᵃ̇ (p. 803a, l. 48).
n.ag. (f. piṭavüñᵘ̈), one who laments, one who bewails.

or (q.v.) pĕth 3 m. (sg. dat. pitas), vain talk, useless chatter, irrelevant talk, twaddle, talking over and over again on the same subject; cf. pitun. --lagun -- m.inf. to engage in such talk. --pith -- m. the habit of indulging in such talk.

m. (sg. dat. pīṭhas), a stool, seat, chair, bench; esp. a throne (cf. bạdᵃra-pᵃ, p. 88b, l. 16); the seat of a deity. Cf. pyūṭhᵘ. ¶ pīṭha-pūzā f. 'worshipping the throne', i.e. showing great reverence to a venerated person. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who occupies a throne; hence, one who is universally reverenced or looked up to.

or pīnth or f. (sg. dat. pī˜ti, Gr.Gr. 70), very little of anything, a tiny piece (the size of a bit cut off the tip of a finger-nail), anything very small, a trifle (cf. kȧrⁱ-pⁱ, p. 467a, l. 6). Cf. pī̃tᵃr, pī̃turᵘ, pī˜ʦh, and pyū̃tᵘ.
f. a woman of high character and high rank.
f. (sg. dat. pīṭhᵃrüñᵃ), criticism, admonishing, reproving, pointing out defects (including the idea of instruction) (Gr.Gr. 121).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pīṭhᵃrôwᵃ), to admonish, good naturedly to criticize, to lecture, draw attention to faults (with the object of instruction).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pyūṭhᵒrᵒ), to admonish, good naturedly to criticize defects, to lecture, draw attention to faults (with the object of instruction) (Gr.Gr. 121).
in pitō pitōkarun m.inf. to beg and implore for something urgently needed (as one parched with thirst begs for water).
m. a deceased ancestor, i.q. pĕtur, q.v. in pitrulūkh deceased ancestors (Rām. 311).

m. (sg. dat. pitratas), blood kinship (usually characterized by mutual hostility felt by the members) (Gr.Gr. pituruth, wrongly translated 'fatherhood', 144); the hostility usually felt between such kinsfolk. Cf. pitur 2.
m. (sg. dat. pitanas), the becoming weary in importunity or urging, unavailing urging on an unwilling worker or giver. Cf. pīṭun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pyuṭᵘ; 2 p.p. picyōv. This verb is impersonal, e.g. pyuṭun, it was lamented by him, i.e. he lamented), to lament, bewail. piṭani bĕhun m.inf. to sit for lamentation, to bewail.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. pīṭyōv), to be wearied by another's delay, wait wearily, to be wearied by a long enquiry into some urgent work; cf. pitun. pīṭyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pīṭyē-müʦᵘ̈), wearied by waiting.

or piturᵘ 1 m. (pl. nom. pitar (Rām. 311); pitᵃ̇rᵃ̇ (K. 541); f. pitarë̆ñᵘ̈), a near kinsman by blood, a cousin (mutual hostility is considered usual between kinsfolk) (cf. öshorᵘ-pᵘ, p. 49b, l. 1) (Gr.Gr. 144, wrongly translated 'father'; Rām. 1038, fem.; K.Pr. 119, 130, 171). --guturᵘ -- m. belonging to the same (or to a certain) lineage (by blood-kinship). ¶ pitᵃ̇rᵃ̇-bọ̆dᵃ̇ m. the mutual conduct of kinsfolk, i.e. the enmity, abuse, and quarrelling between relations over an inheritance or the like (Gr.Gr. 144, where it is wrongly translated 'fatherhood'); similar conduct between persons who are not related. -hĕḍun m. family ridicule, i.e. when the members of the same kin ridicule one another for the slightest mistake. -hasad m. quarrelling between kinsfolk, family quarrels, backbiting among relations. -küṭᵘ̈ f. a daughter of one of one's kinsfolk (when spoken of with hostility). -kaṭh (sg. dat. -kaṭas), the son of one of one's kinsfolk (when spoken of with hostility). -phash m. a storm of the kinsfolk, harassment caused (to a person) by his blood relations. -rᵃsh f. the natural mutual enmity between kinsfolk. -tônᵘ m. the mutual conduct of kinsfolk, i.e. the enmity and hostility which naturally exists between them; so pitarĕñi-tônᵘ, with same meaning (Rām. 1778).

or pīnturᵘ or m. (sg. dat. pī˜taras), a very little of anything, a tiny bit (the size of a piece snipped off a finger-nail), anything very small (generally used --˚, the first member of the compound being the article, a small piece of which is referred to). Cf. pī˜th, pī̃tᵃr, pī˜ʦh, and pyū̃tᵘ.

adj. (f. pitᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or pitᵃr), of, belonging to, or related through a paternal uncle (pẹ̆thᵃr or pẹ̆tᵃr); a paternal cousin (K. 536). Used in the following, and similar, compounds expressing relationship:-- --bēma -- m. the husband of the daughter of a paternal uncle, the husband of a cousin on the father's side. --bāpathᵃr -- m. the son of a cousin on the father's side, a first cousin once removed on that side. --bôyᵘ -- m. the brother on the side of a paternal uncle, i.e. a male first cousin on the father's side (El. pitarboí) (Gr.Gr. 133). --dryuyᵘ -- m. a (woman's) husband's first cousin on the father's side. --dyārathᵃr -- m. the son of a (woman's) husband's first cousin (male) on the father's side. --zömiyĕ -- m. the husband of a (woman's) husband's first cousin (female) on the father's side. ¶ pitᵘ̈rᵘ̈ bĕñĕ or pitᵃr bĕñĕ f. a first cousin (female) on the father's side (El. pitarbinyi) (Gr.Gr. 133). --bāwᵃza -- f. the daughter of a first cousin on the father's side. --bȧyⁱ-(or böyⁱ-)kākañ -- f. the wife of a first cousin on the father's side (Gr.Gr. 133 pitᵃr böyⁱ-). --drᵃkākañ or --drikākañ -- f. the wife of a (woman's) husband's first cousin on the father's side. --dyārᵃza -- f. the daughter of a (woman's) husband's first cousin on the father's side. --zām -- (sg. dat. --zömᵘ̈ -- or --zōmᵘ̈ --), a (woman's) husband's first cousin (female) on the father's side. --zömⁱza -- f. the daughter of a (woman's) husband's first cousin (female) on the father's side.
or pīntᵃr or f. a very little of anything, a tiny piece (the size of a piece snipped off a finger-nail), anything very small, Cf. pī˜th, pī̃turᵘ, pī˜ʦh, pyū̃tᵘ.
f. (sg. dat. piṭᵃrüñᵃ), rendering a person miserable (e.g. by causing loss, hindering, opposition, etc.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. piṭᵃrôwᵃ), to cause to lament (cf. piṭun).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. piṭᵒrᵒ), to render a person miserable (e.g. by causing loss, hindering, opposition, etc.). piṭᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. piṭᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), rendered miserable, as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pīṭᵒrᵒ), to worry (a person) by delay, to delay the performance of any urgent work. pīṭᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. pīṭᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), worried by delay (caused by someone employed in some urgent work).
f. a military girdle, a belly-band, girth, belt; a leather portmanteau.
f. a kind of yellow earth used for making colour-wash on walls, for painting, etc.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pyuwᵘ), to drink (noted only in L.V. 81).

m. the scum of boiling rice, rice-water (K.Pr. 171). --kārun -- m.inf. to cook the scum of boiled rice; hence, to live a perfectly contented life (as if he was contented even when all he had to eat was this scum).
adj. c.g. beloved, dear; esp. best beloved, beloved more than others (e.g. a darling child, or (to a woman) her husband).
adj. c.g. one who suffers from nasal catarrh, having a cold in the head. Cf. pyū̃ʦᵘ.

f. (sg. dat. piʦhi), the pain of being scalded by boiling water, scalding; cf. pyuthᵘ. --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to scald (a person); met. to distress a person by disgraceful abuse, by vile conduct, or the like. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. scalding to fall (on a person), to be scalded; met. to be distressed by another's disgraceful abuse, vile conduct, or the like.

or pīnʦh f. (sg. dat. pī˜ʦi), very little of anything (esp. food), a tiny piece, something very small. Cf. pī˜th, pyū̃tᵘ, pī̃tᵃr, pī̃turᵘ. ¶ pī̃ʦa-köñᵘ̈ f. a certain small bird, described as flying very high, and with a long acute call (K.Pr. 42, translated 'a small-eyed man'). -wād m. very little (of anything), a minute piece, mere trace. ¶ pī˜ʦi phaṭun m.inf. to burst for a trifle, to be filled with pride on receiving something very small or trifling. --pī˜ʦi -- adv. tiny bit by tiny bit, scrap by scrap.

or pō̃bürᵘ̈ f. a coverlet or shawl of pashmīna cloth (Rām. 1120; K.Pr. 156 pumbar, 165 pombar). Cf. rĕshⁱ-pⁱ, p. 855b, l. 48 ¶ pō̃bᵃri (or pō̃bari)-dọ̆bᵘ (or) m. a man who makes a living by washing such shawls, a pashmīna cleaner. -dyār m. (at a wedding) a present made by the bride's father to the relations of the bridegroom, representing the price of a pashmīna shawl for the bridegroom's maternal uncle. -jōra m. a pair of these shawls. -madun m. (sg. dat. -madanas), a young man who swaggers about wearing one of these shawls. -palav m. a little worn-out and torn shawl, as ab. -pōsh m. one who wears one of these shawls (a sign of prosperity). -wôwurᵘ m. a weaver of the cloth for these shawls.

or paĩch m. (sg. dat. pö̃cas), a meeting of five or more persons as a court of inquiry or of arbitration; a body of arbitrators, a pancāyat (El. painch); cf. panch. -ạnzᵃran f. (sg. dat. -ạnzᵃrüñᵃ), the deciding or decision of such a body. --bĕhun -- m.inf. such a body to assemble or sit for decision. --karun -- m.inf. to call together such a body of arbitrators; to lay a matter before such a body for decision.

adj. (f. püchᵘ̈), lasting for a lunar fortnight, occurring during a lunar fortnight (e.g. of a crop ripening within such a time). Cf. pach and (s.v. pānʦ) pönʦa-pᵒ. ¶ pȧchⁱ adv. after a lunar fortnight. -pach m. an entire lunar fortnight, an exact fortnight. -pȧchⁱ adv. after each lunar fortnight, once a fortnight.

m. the sole of the foot (W, 151, K.Pr. 161); the foot (Rām. 924, 990, 1180, 1183, 1260, 1436, 1552); the foot of a camel or elephant (El.); the sole of a shoe or of a boot (cf. paizār-pᵒ, s.v. paizār); a step (El.); a footmark, a footprint (K. 185-6). In the compound lodᵘ-podᵘ the word podᵘ is merely a jingle. See lodᵘ. ¶ pȧdⁱ-dyār m.pl. a present given to a bride by her father-in-law as she takes the seven steps round the sacred fire. At each step a coin or other valuable article is put under her foot. -holᵘ adj. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), crooked-footed, having the foot, or the sole of the foot, crooked.--lagȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. footprints to appear in the dust, mud, or the like; frostbite of the sole of the foot to occur. --phalȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. weariness from continued walking to be experienced; cf. pād phᵒ, col. a, l. 1. -zyūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈), long-footed, having feet long in proportion to the other limbs. ¶ padi padi adv. at every foot, in each place; at each footprint (K. 285, 1011, 1014). --path padi -- or --pĕṭha padi -- adv. step by step, by degrees (El. padi pat padi, W. 96). -rāh m. the exertion of much coming and going (esp. when fruitless). ¶ padĕn mīṭhⁱ dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to kiss the feet, to make a very humble request to another (Rām. 1553). -pĕṭh adv. on the feet; hence, standing up, erect (of a person) (Rām. 938).

m. the vulva, the female organ of generation; esp. of a shrewish woman, or woman disliked by her husband; cf. pōn. --wasun -- m.inf. the vulva to descend, (of a foul vulva) irritation or pain to occur owing to excessive copulation.
m. a kind of wood, of which the skewer-like little sticks, on which is wound the shawl- thread, are made (El.).

m. destruction. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. destruction to occur. ¶ pōga-küṭᵘ̈ f. a daughter of destruction, i.e. a daughter who is fated to be the destroyer of her father or her father's family. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a son of destruction, i.e. who is fated to be the destroyer of his father or his father's family (Gr.Gr. 132).
(? = بوق) m. a trumpet made of buffalo-horn (used by Musalmāns). --wāyun -- m.inf. to blow such a trumpet. This is done on the last night of the month of Ramaẓān.

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. pōgaladiñ), one who shows evident marks (such as mental aberration, starved appearance, ragged apparel, and so on) of having lost everything; a child, horse, or the like, fated to destroy his or its parents, master, or the like.

or pōh or (L.V.) puh m. (the sg. gen. of this word is puhukᵘ or puhunᵘ, see bel.), N. of the tenth month of the Hindū year (December-January), the Skt. pauṣa (W. 107; K.Pr. 128, 171); a present given to the husband's relations by a bride's relations on the birth of her first child. ¶ pŏha-bōgᵘ m. the property given as the ab. present. -gāḍa f. pl. an offering of fish and other food made to the tutelary deity of a Hindū house on a Tuesday or Saturday in the dark half of the month of Pŏh. -gaṭa f. the darkness of the month of Pŏh. In this month the nights and sometimes even the days are particularly dark. -nĕth f. (sg. dat. -në̆ʦᵘ̈), wool shorn in or about the month of Pŏh. It is close and rough and unsuitable for spinning. -rāth f. (sg. dat. -röʦᵘ̈), a night in the month of Pŏh. In Śiv. 1554, it is punning alluded to by the use of the word paharāth, q.v. -tǖrᵘ̈ f. the cold of the month of Pŏh. It is the coldest month of the year. ¶ pōha-kükᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the freezing cold of Pŏh. See kükᵘ̈rᵘ̈. ¶ pŏhⁱ-pan m. pl. the (fallen) leaves of Pŏh. In this month the ground is covered with great masses of withered fallen leaves; met. anything withered like these leaves; cf. pȧhⁱ- pan, col. a, l. 11, and puhunᵘ wāv (L.V. 83) (Śiv. 1208; Rām. 206, 1634). -poṭᵘ m. a large thick warm blanket. In the month of Pŏh a whole family will sleep under one. -ʦhaṭh f. (sg. dat. -ʦhaṭⁱ), the freezing cold wind-blasts of the month of Pŏh. -wunar f. the fog of the month of Pŏh. ¶ pōhⁱ-pan m., i.q. pŏhⁱ- pan, ab. ¶ pūhi adv. in the month of Pŏh. ¶ puhukᵘ sg. gen. (f. puhücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the month of Pŏh. ¶ puhunᵘ sg. gen. (f. puhüñᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the month of Pŏh (used esp. with reference to dates in the month, but also otherwise). puhunᵘ wāv, m. the wind of Pŏh (L.V. 83). ¶ pŏhas kani adv. in about the month of Pŏh. --kyutᵘ -- adv. in the month of Pŏh.
(for 2, see pŏhurᵘ) or pŏhur m. a floor in a house above the ground-floor, i.e. the first floor, second floor, and so on. (Cf. köñᵘ̈-pᵘ̈, p. 461a, l. 1; kāñĕñi-pᵒ, p. 462a, l. 27.)
or (Gr.Gr. 39) pŏhar 2 m. (f. pahurĕñ or pŏharĕñ (Gr.Gr.)), a guest invited to some family festival, such as a wedding or the like. Such guests are invited for a stay of some days (Śiv. 830, fem.).
m. the spleen (El. pauh, poh). pȧhⁱ-khünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. khanjĕ), a piece of the flesh of the spleen.

m. a kind of wood (it grows straight and stout from the ground, and is useful for making pestles and the like; a fibre is also made from it), the witch hazel (Parrotia Jacquemontiana) (El. páhú; ? also the poh, f. a bar, of El.; L. 68, 79, 81).
m. worthlessness, the condition of being withered, worn out, or wanting in substance.
adj. (f. pöjⁱ or pöjᵘ̈), mean, vile, contemptible, a low fellow, a vile wretch (Gr.Gr. 144). ¶ pöjⁱ-küṭⁱ f. the daughter of a low fellow. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), the son of a low fellow.

f. a certain measure of weight employed for measuring liquids (such as oil, etc.). It is used --˚, and indicates a weight of six seers or twelve pounds (cf. gĕv-pᵒ, p. 316b, l. 8). ¶ pājĕ-nörᵘ̈ f. a vessel used for measuring this amount of oil, etc. -wād m. measuring (oil, etc.) by pöjᵘ̈s.
f. vileness, meanness (of caste, condition, occupation, nature, or the like) of a person.
m. vile conduct (esp. when a respectable person acts like a vile person); lowness of position in a household (Gr.Gr. 144). Cf. pôjᵘ.
m. a pedlar, a hawker; (in Kāshmīrī) an itinerant hawker of bread. -bāy f. his wife.
m. (sg. dat. pö̃kas), mud, a slough (L.V. 74).
m. a bird (El. pánkhí). Cf. pankhī.

or pŏkta adj. c.g. dressed, cooked (cf. dam-pᵒ, p. 216b, l. 16); baked (as brick, etc.) (Śiv. 1033); thorough (Gr.M.); ripe, matured, mature (Śiv. 1112, 1778; H. vi, 15); complete (El. púkhta); shrewd, knowing, expert, thoroughly informed (Rām. 1518, 1583); firm, strong, solid, well-built; (of a throw of dice or the like) successful (Rām. 298). --kār -- پختہ کار adj. c.g. of firm, sound, or solid workmanship; thoroughly skilled, firmly grounded (in the theory and practice of anything); omnipotent, the Creater (Rām. 1041; YZ. 75, 213). --karun --, m.inf. to accomplish (El.). --pa︢i︣sa -- or --pö̃sa -- m. a certain copper coin, the 'pucka pice', the quarter of an anna (cf. khām pa︢i︣sa, p. 400a, l. 14). -pa︢i︣sunᵘ or -pö̃sunᵘ adj. (f. -pa︢i︣(pö̃)süñᵘ̈ ), costing, or worth, a quarter of an anna. --rŏpay -- m. a certain silver coin, the rupee current in India, worth sixteen annas, as compared with the khām rŏpay (p. 400a, l. 19). --rŏpayĕ-hondᵘ -- adj. (f. --rŏpayĕ-hünzᵘ̈ --), costing, or worth, one of these rupees.
f. ripeness; maturedness, thoroughness, strength, solidity, firmness; shrewdness, knowingness, expertness.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pŏkhtôwᵘ), to make ripe; to make solid, firm; to confirm (a person in an appointment). pŏkhtôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pŏkhtövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made firm, made solid; confirmed (in an appointment).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. pŏkhtyōv), to become ripe; to become mature, thorough, solid, firm; to become shrewd, knowing, expert. pŏkhtyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pŏkhtyē-müʦᵘ̈), become ripe; become mature, solid, firm; become expert.
or pŏkhurᵘ m. (sg. dat. pŏkharas), the inner bowl of a mortar (for pounding); an irrigation basin round a garden plant or tree (cf. hĕndawan-pᵒ, p. 338b, l. 24).

or pū̃khurᵘ m. one of the buttocks, one side of the nates. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. (of a cripple who cannot move otherwise) to drag oneself along the ground on the buttocks, to wear one's buttocks away in this manner; met. (of one who is powerless or poverty-stricken) somehow or other, or very slowly and with great difficulty, to carry out some duty or business.

m. relationship, kinship, connexion, kin (cf. baḍa-mātāmāl-pᵒ, p. 82b, l. 20; ōra-pᵒ, p. 42a, l. 4; mātāmāl-pᵒ, p. 607a, l. 36); esp. a person's relatives (on one side, the father's, or on the other side, the mother's, each set being so described as a body); cf. pach 2. pȧkhⁱ-wôlⁱ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who has numerous relations, one who belongs to a great family (and hence has many allies); one who has many friends (with a like result). ¶ pakhyukᵘ sg. gen. (f. pakhicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or connected with kinship; esp. (with regard to a person belonging to one side of a family) belonging to the other side (e.g. a person belonging to the paternal kin would so refer to a person belonging to the maternal kin).
adj. (f. püchᵘ̈), an adjective formed from pakh 2 and 3, used --˚, as in pönʦa-pᵒ, s.v. pānʦ.

f. (sg. dat. pŏkhrĕ), a large masonry well, generally with steps down to the water (the bāolī of India). pŏkhri-bal or pŏkhari-bal m. the land immediately round such a well, or round any similar large square water-hole near a village; the N. of a popular well and bathing-place on the east side of the Hāra-parbuth hill (p. 344a, l. 44) near Śrīnagar (Gr.Gr. 165).
or pū̃khürᵘ̈ f. one side of the buttocks, one of the nates, i.q. pō̃khurᵘ; the inner side of a woman's buttocks, one on each side of the vulva. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf., i.q. pō̃khurᵘ dyunᵘ, ab., q.v.
f. purity, cleanness (natural or artificial); sanctity.
f. the business or profession of an itinerant hawker of bread.
(? spelling) m. (pl. nom. pōkar), a conical shaped heap of weeds and mud used as the soil for the floating islands on the Ḍal Lake (L. 344).

1 p.p. (f. pücᵘ̈), ripened, matured; (of something originally soft) hardened, solidified, become firm, become substantial (cf. mŏla-pᵒ, p. 566a, l. 30). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become ripe, to ripen, mature; to have ripened fruit, to be fruitful, to have the consequences or necessary results, to yield its inevitable fruit (e.g. according to the doctrine of transmigration of souls, the actions in a former life bear their fruit in the present life). --tab -- m. high fever, fever when the temperature is high and the pulse rapid. Fever below about 102˚ is called khām tab, q.v. p. 400a, l. 23.
adj. (f. pöcᵘ̈) cooked, used --˚, as in aḍa-pôkᵘ, half-cooked (p. 11b, l. 43).
or phōlād فولاد m. steel (Gr.M.; Rām. 431, 635, phōlād).
adj. (f. pŏlādüvᵘ̈), made of steel (H. v, 4).

m. a dish made of rice boiled in soup with flesh, spices, etc.; a pilao (cf. gāzᵃri-pᵃ, p. 319a, l. 16; khāgari-pᵒ, p. 394a, l. 1) (El. puláo; W. 121, pulāv; Śiv. 1824; H. ii, 3; vi, 2; K.Pr. 112, 163).
n.ag. (f. pŏlavüñᵘ̈), one who has become weakened, discouraged, disheartened; that which is blunted or worn out by use.
f. (sg. dat. pöliki), a kind of litter or sedan, a palankeen (K. 221, 298).
pōlödⁱ, or phōlödⁱ (= فولادی) adj. c.g. of steel, steel (Rām. 19, 974, 1607, pōᵒ).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. pŏlyōv), to become weak, weakened, infirm, disheartened, discouraged (cf. pulan aʦun, p. 730b, l. 25); (of a tool) to become blunted by over-use. ¶ pŏlan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is discouraged or disheartened, one who feels that he is defeated. ¶ pŏlyō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. pŏlyē-müʦᵘ̈), weakened, discouraged, blunted, etc., as ab.
adj. (f. pŏlürᵘ̈), weak, infirm, etc., inside (but stout and plump externally), plump but unsubstantial.
adj. (f. pŏjⁱ or pö̆jᵘ̈), weak, infirm (cf. atha-pᵒ, p. 61a, l. 41).

m. a kind of large wide-open basket (cf. dā̃-pᵒ, p. 230b, l. 29; gūrⁱ-pⁱ, p. 299b, l. 13); used met. in chala-pᵒ, a basket of fragments; hence, mutual recriminations (p. 161a, l. 11). Cf. püjᵘ̈. ¶ pȧlⁱ-sörⁱ f. carrying away by basketfuls, transporting in baskets. ¶ pali āsun m.inf. to become gradually collected (of wealth, goods, etc.). --karun -- m.inf. gradually to collect, as ab.; esp. to collect and hoard up what remains over and above after necessary expenditure, to save up. --rōzun -- m.inf. (of what remains over after proper expenditure) to be saved up. --thawun -- m.inf. to put in a basket; hence, to conceal (either material things, or secrets, statements, facts, or the like). --ta pathari -- adv. in the basket and on the floor; hence, scattered everywhere, here and there, above and below (u.w. ref. to signs, clues, etc.).
adj. (f. püjᵘ̈ 2; for 1, see s.v.), used --˚, weighing a pal (see pal 2) or the twentieth part of a seer, or four tōlās (each weighing about half an ounce) (cf. aiṭha-pᵒ, p. 66b, l. 32).

m. the anus (cf. gᵃsa-pᵃ, p. 307a, l. 25) (Gr.Gr. 22); the female private parts generally (cf. kŏ-pōn, p. 463a, l. 45); cf. pỗdᵘ. --ʦaṭanāwun -- m.inf. to induce another (male) to have sexual intercourse with oneself, or to commit an unnatural offence with oneself. ¶ pōna-bachĕ 1 f.pl. 'the banks of the anus', the elevated parts on each side of it. -gŏʦᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. trousers, long drawers. -kônᵘ m. one who (esp. a boy) is accustomed to cause another (male) to commit an unnatural offence with him. -köñᵘ̈ f. a woman who is habitually unchaste. -phĕshil f. (of a woman) one who has an ill-omened vulva, one who is habitually unchaste; a woman who bears a vicious child. ¶ pōnukᵘ sg. gen. (f. pōnücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the anus or the vulva.

m. a virtuous or meritorious act, good or virtuous works (L.V. 62, 79; Śiv. 995, 1579, 1653; K. 848-9). Cf. puny. --lagun -- m.inf. a virtuous act to be attached to a person, the merit of a virtuous act to be achieved (by, dat.) (Rām. 172). --zēnun -- m.inf. to earn merit by performing good works. ¶ pŏñĕ-hyūnᵘ adj. (f. -hīñᵘ̈), wanting in the results of good works (in former lives), hence, leading an unfortunate life; fixed in wicked conduct, a habitual sinner. -môlᵘ m. 'a father of good works', i.e. a holy man, himself holy, and influencing others towards good works. -motᵘ adj. (f. -müʦᵘ̈), 'mad after good works,' one who is devoted to good works. -mỗtᵘ m. that which produces the unending results of good works (e.g. fasting on the proper days, visiting and bathing at holy spots, worshipping gods, etc.). -phal m. the ripened fruit of virtuous actions (in former lives or in the present life). -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), one who has many good results of virtuous actions; an action or conduct which produces the results of virtuous acts. -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), id. -wān adj. c.g. one who has earned the results of many good actions (in a former life or in the present one) (Śiv. 320).

f. a blister or fissure on the sole of the heel; a fissure or frost-crack in hand or foot (Gr.Gr. 22, pōn). -bachĕ 2 f.pl. the banks or elevated flesh on each side of such a fissure. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a fissure to occur. --phaṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a blister to burst.
adj. c.g. one who has an anus (esp. one marked by some peculiarity).
m. N. of the seventh lunar mansion or lunar asterism, known in Sanskrit as 'Punarvasu' (Śiv. 1550).
m. the auspicious compliment uttered by a guest at the pŏnasonᵘ (q.v.) ceremony. Cf. punahsund, and shōkh ta pŏᵒ, s.v. shōkh.

m. N. of a ceremony performed by women on the occasion of the dyeing of the bridegroom's or boy's feet, etc. (performed at a Hindū wedding, the ceremonial tonsure, investment with the sacred thread, or the like). ¶ pŏnasan-bata m. the boiled rice distributed to the guests before this ceremony. -pȧnḍith m. (sg. dat. -pȧnḍitas), the superintendent (i.e. the expert person who arranges the details) of this ceremony.

f. (sg. dat. pŏndⁱ), a sneeze, sneezing (cf. marʦa-pᵒ, p. 594b, l. 17) (Gr.Gr. 126, 134; K.Pr. 143). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a sneeze to take place (esp. at the beginning of any work, for which it is a very bad omen). --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to sneeze. ¶ pŏnda-nāsth f. (sg. dat. -nāsti), snuff, which is used to cause sneezing; esp. when made of the Rhododendron campanulatum, used as a snuff for headache (L. 76, punda nást). --pŏnd -- f. sneeze on sneeze, a violent fit of sneezing, or a number of people sneezing at the same time.
adj. c.g. one who suffers from an attack of sneezing (Gr.Gr. 126).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pọ̆ndᵘ; 2 p.p. pŏnzōv). This verb is impersonal in the tenses formed from the past participles, as in pọ̆ndun, it was sneezed by him, i.e. he sneezed) to sneeze (Gr.Gr. 126, Gr.M., L.V. 46).

m. (sg. dat. pŏnētᵃras), (of a man) a second, or later, marriage. ¶ pŏnētᵃ̇rᵃ̇-kŏlay f. the wife of a man's second (or later) marriage. She is generally supposed to be bold and arrogant, and this word is mostly used with an allusion to these qualities. -kār m. the arrangements for, or ceremony of, such a marriage. -mahārāza m. the bridegroom of such a marriage. ¶ pŏnētᵃrukᵃ sg. gen. (f. pŏnētᵃrücᵃ), of, or belonging to, a second (or later) marriage.
adj. m. a man who has made a second (or later) marriage.

m. (f. pünzᵘ̈) the Bengal monkey (cf. pala-tala ponzᵘ hyuhᵘ, p. 729b, l. 25) (El. pun and ponz; L. 108, Innuus rhesus or Macacus rhesus; Rām. 331, fem.; K.Pr. 166, 173, 238); in K.Pr. 149, translated 'squirrel' (?); (in Rām. and K., according to commentary) a bear (Rām. 466, 778, 794, 931, 965, 983, 990, 1003, 1070; K. 155). As the final part of a compound, this word is sometimes employed in a depreciatory sense, to indicate something useless or confused. Cf. laṭa-pᵒ, p. 537a, l. 16, and rᵃkha-pᵃ, s.v. rᵃkh. ¶ pȧnzⁱ-ongⁱjⁱ f. 'monkey-finger', N. of a certain medicinal plant, used as a cattle medicine. -pŏṭh f. (sg. dat. -pŏṭi), a certain medicinal plant growing in the hills and used as a remedy for herpes, etc. See pŏṭh. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a monkey-man, a man who lives by exhibiting trained monkeys.

m. a group of five, a five (Gr.Gr. 83, W. 104). In the plural, pȧnzⁱ, it is used as a multiplicative, as in sath pȧnzⁱ pānʦatrᵃh, seven fives (are) thirty-five (Gr.Gr. 86, W. 104). ponzwāh khanḍā m. about five, but a little less than five, nearly five (Gr.Gr. 83).

card. (pl. dat. pönʦahaiṭhan), sixty-five (Gr.Gr. 78); a group of sixty-five, a sixty-five. ¶ pönʦahaiṭhukᵘ adj. (f. pönʦahaiṭhücᵘ̈), of the sixty-fifth (year). ¶ pönʦahaiṭhan-hondᵘ  pl. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, sixty-five; costing, or worth, sixty-five; receiving wages amounting to sixty-five (rupees, etc.).
or pönʦahṻṭhyunᵘ adj. (f. pönʦahai(hṻ)ṭhiñᵘ̈ ), costing sixty-five (rupees, etc.); having a salary (etc.) of sixty-five (rupees, etc.).
ord. (f. pönʦahatimᵘ̈), five hundredth (Gr.Gr. 80). Cf. pānʦ hath, p. 742b, l. 11.
m. the Panʦāl range and pass. See panʦāl.

(also written pö̃ʦam) f. (sg. dat. pönʦᵘ̈mᵘ̈ or pö̃ʦᵘ̈mᵘ̈), the fifth lunar day of the light or dark fortnight of any luni-solar month (cf. basma-pö̃ʦam, p. 133a, l. 44) (Rām. 1768); a group of five (cf. ongᵘji-pᵘ, p. 33b, l. 28). pönʦᵘ̈mᵘ̈-hondᵘ̈ sg. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, belonging to, born on, or existing on the fifth lunar day of either the light or dark fortnight of a luni-solar month.

card. (pl. dat. pönʦanamatan), ninety-five (Gr.Gr. 80); a collection of ninety-five things, a ninety-five. pönʦanamatukᵘ adj. (f. pönʦanamatücᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or born in the ninety-fifth (year).

card. (pl. dat. pönʦasatatan), seventy-five (Gr.Gr. 79); a collection of seventy-five things, a seventy-five. pönʦasatatukᵘ adj. (f. pönʦasatatücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the seventy-fifth (year). pönʦasatatan-hondᵘ pl. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, seventy-five; worth, or costing, seventy-five (rupees, etc.); earning a salary of seventy-five (rupees, etc.).
adj. (f. pönʦasatatiñᵘ̈), worth, or costing, seventy-five (rupees, etc.).

card. (pl. dat. pönʦashītan), eighty-five (Gr.Gr. 79); a collection of eighty-five things, an eighty-five. pönʦashītukᵘ adj. (f. pönʦashītücᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or produced in the eighty-fifth year. pönʦashītan-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, eighty-five (men, etc.); costing, or worth, eighty-five (rupees, etc.); earning a salary of eighty-five (rupees, etc.).
adj. (f. pönʦashītiñᵘ̈), worth, or costing, eighty-five (rupees, etc.); earning eighty-five (rupees, etc.).
card. forty-five (Gr.Gr. 78); a collection of forty-five things, a forty-five. pönʦatöjihyukᵘ adj. (f. pönʦatöjihicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the forty-fifth year.
adv. at forty-five years of age.

card. fifty-five (El. pánts tah pántsah; Gr.Gr. 78). pönʦawanzāhukᵘ adj. (f. pönʦawanzāhücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the fifty-fifth (year). pönʦawanzāhan-hondᵘ gen. pl. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, fifty-five; worth, or costing, fifty-five (rupees, etc.); earning wages amounting to fifty-five (rupees, etc.).
card. even all five (cf. pǖnʦⁱ pᵒ, p. 743b, l. 40) (Gr.Gr. 85, Śiv. 1831).

or pönʦukh; also written pö̃ʦokᵘ, pö̃ʦukh m. (sg. dat. pönʦakas or pö̃ʦakas), a group of five (esp. used as an astrological term with reference to the heavenly bodies) (cf. draṭha-pö̃ʦukh, p. 250a, l. 7; kara-pönʦokᵘ, p. 465b, l. 33).

m. a secondary suffix forming abstract nouns denoting general relationship, state, condition (Gr.Gr. 144; cf. bĕnüñᵘ̈-pônᵘ̈, p. 114a, l. 35; bẹ̆nᵃza-pᵃ, p. 115a, l. 9; baṭᵃñĕ-pᵃ, p. 145a, l. 16; dāsa-pᵒ, p. 252a, l. 2; kŏlayĕ-pᵒ, p. 442a, l. 21; kanjar-pᵒ, p. 457b, l. 24; so (Gr.Gr. 144) dāyĕ-pᵒ, nursehood; pöjⁱ-pⁱ, lowness of position; pāñirⁱ-pⁱ, the occupation of a water-carrier (pāñurᵘ); parzan-pᵒ, the occupation of a personal servant (parzun 1); pāyĕchⁱ-pⁱ, the conduct, condition, or occupation of an outcaste Brāhmaṇa (pāyuch); vĕsa-pᵒ, comradeship, K.Pr. 102). When the relationship is intimate, tônᵘ 2 (q.v.) is used instead of pônᵘ.

m. (sg. dat. pöñis. When the word is the first member of a compound it takes the form pã̄ (Śiv. 338, 983), and when it is the second member of a compound it takes the form wôñᵘ, see Gr.Gr. 73, 74; Śiv. 1309, 1522); ¶ water (El. póin) (cf. kulᵘ-pĕṭh pôñᵘ khārun, p. 438b, l. 35; kranjali pôñᵘ sārun, p. 474a, l. 48; āra-wôñᵘ, p. 41b, l. 1; busari-wᵒ, p. 134b, l. 39; chūla-wᵒ, p. 161a, l. 36; chalin-wᵒ, p. 161b, l. 15; p. 270b, l. 2; and p. 516b, l. 42; dyāra-wᵒ, p. 271a, l. 12; gölin-wᵒ, p. 285b, l. 36; gandakh-wᵒ, p. 290a, l. 36; ganga-wᵒ, p. 292a, l. 6; graka-wᵒ, p. 301b, l. 42; grimⁱta-wⁱ, p. 303a, l. 14; hāra-wᵒ, p. 344a, l. 30; khŏḍa-wᵒ, p. 392b, l. 15; khāha-wᵒ, p. 394a, l. 25; khāra-wᵒ, p. 408b, l. 38; kȧnḍⁱ-wⁱ, p. 455a, l. 8; krīrⁱ-wⁱ, p. 475b, l. 39; mal-wᵒ, p. 564a, l. 39; mīli-wᵒ, p. 566a, l. 2; mörᵘ̈-wᵘ̈, p. 587a, l. 31; mashka-wᵒ, p. 597a, l. 39; mĕʦi-wᵒ, p. 609a, l. 14; nāga-wᵒ, p. 624a, l. 43; nījĕ-wᵒ, p. 626b, l. 49; nali-wᵒ, p. 633b, l. 5; nalka-wᵒ, p. 634b, l. 21; nambali-wᵒ, p. 637b, l. 30; nūna-wᵒ, p. 641a, l. 33; nar-wᵒ, p. 646a, l. 49; nörija-wᵒ, p. 650b, l. 48; phŏṭⁱ-wⁱ, p. 715b, l. 45; phyörinⁱ-wⁱ, p. 722b, l. 34; palan pôñᵘ dyunᵘ, p. 729b, l. 31; parawan pôñᵘ shrapun, s.v. parav; pashpan-wᵒ, s.v. pashpun; potᵘ-wᵘ, s.v. potᵘ; rūda-wᵒ, s.v. rūd; vĕtha-wᵒ, s.v. vĕth) (L.V. 24, 42, 47, 106; Śiv. 24, 27, 191, 239, 240, 331, 338, 349, 499, 506, 1309, 1522, 1711; Rām. 74, 93, 233, 562, 596, 605, 623, 779, 780, 787, 789, 790, 795, 1175, 1178, 1502, 1517, 1784; YZ. 124, 346; K.Pr. 31, 115, 134, 165, 224, 234, 250, generally spelt poni). This word is chiefly used by Hindūs (El., Gr.M.). --könzᵘ̈ -- m. water and congee, a quantity of water or the like, a quantity of liquid. --ladun -- m.inf. to wash (the hair of the head). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. water to come, i.e. a flood to rise in a river or the like; water to pour from the mouth, salivation to occur. ¶ pã̄-aṭh m. (sg. dat. -aṭas), a flood of water, a rush of water from a height. -bubur m. a bubble in water (Rām. 987). -buka m. water-foam. -bāna m. a water-vessel. -bar m. a water-door, a door for admitting water; a door opening on to a river. -borᵘ m. a water-drainhole, an aperture for drawing water from an irrigation channel. -baran f. (sg. dat. barüñᵘ̈), a small door for admitting water; a small door opening on to a river. -busar f. a stream of boiling water. -batukh m.
