(sg. dat. -batakas), a water-duck, a duck that always lives on water (never flying); met. a man who always lives on the water, a boatman, a sailor. -chūl m. a water-fall, a cascade (Śiv. 983; Rām. 674, pã̄-chulō, m.c.). -dag f. 'a water-blow', the fall of water from a height. -ḍọ̆gᵘ m. 'a water-whitlow', a boil containing water, a blister on the finger. -digiñ f. a thin stream of water. -daka m. 'a water-push' a violent and swift fall of water from a height. -dara m. an (artificial) irrigation channel. -dār f. a stream of water (e.g. from a pipe, or from a jar, etc.). -dörᵘ̈ f. a source (of a spring or the like). -dŏʦh f. (sg. dat. dŏʦhi), water held in a cup formed by the joined palms of the hands. See dŏʦh. -gaḍa m. a water-jar, a ghaṛā full of water. -güḍᵘ̈wa m. a small jar of water. -gāgᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a water-jar, pitcher, gugglet filled with water. -golᵘ m. a mouth full of water; a mouthful of water, a draught of water (Gr.M.). -gara m. a water-cistern. -grŏkh m. (sg. dat. -grŏkas), a gulp of water, the amount of water gulped down in one swallow. -graṭa m. a water- wheel (working a mill or the like); sufficient water to work such a wheel. -grāy f. water-splashing, the splashing of water (of a river or the sea) on a bank or on the shore; washing (clothes and the like) in water only. -gŏʦh f. a freshwater mussel or similar bivalve (looked upon as a variety of the pearl-oyster). -hö̃giñ f., id.; an oyster-shell full of water. -han or -hanā f. a small amount of water, a little water, a trickle of water; some water (Gr.M.). -hēr f. a staircase or ladder leading from the bank of a river into a house (or the like). -kŏla gaʦhañĕ f. pl. inf. 'to become watercourses', to become splashed all over with water, to become wringing wet. -kᵒtᵒ adj. (f. -kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), damp with water. -kᵃʦar m. dampness (from water). -kᵃy f. a kind of water-jar (properly, a water-churn). -lōṭa m. a water-pot (Rām. 1178). -lav f. sprinkling with water. -lawa f., id. -mŏkhta m. a false pearl, an imitation pearl (Śiv. 338). -malukh m. (sg. dat. malakas), a water-wave. -malürᵘ̈ f. a large kind of water-jar. -maṭh m. (sg. dat. maṭas), a large filled globular water-jar. -nörᵘ̈ f. a small kind of earthen water-jar. -noṭᵘ m. a water-jar. -phyorᵘ m. a drop of water (Rām. 845, 1189, 1374, 1562); met. a very small amount of water. -phyūrᵘ m., id.; met. a dying plant which has been revived by watering. -pôrutᵘ m. 'marking the date by water'; hence, illness caused by change of air and water; cf. pôrutᵘ. -rᵃkh f. (sg. dat. -rᵃkhi), a mere line of water, the trickle of water left in a drying up stream; a mark made by a line or streak of water. -sahlāb m. a flood or inundation; a great volume of water. -shīn m. watery snow, half-melted snow; sleet. -shŏy f. (as a medicinal act) to bathe the feet in bran and water; a similar foot-bath of cold water mixed with the juice of willow-leaves. -sörᵘ̈ f. gradually collecting water (carrying it and storing it). -söriñ f. the similar collection of a large quantity of water. -saruph m. (sg. dat. -sarpas), a water-snake. -sȧrⁱpiñ f. a she water-snake; a kind of blister or swelling containing liquid. -swād m. the flavour of (a particular kind of) water. -thombᵘ m. a handful of water. -trakh m. (sg. dat. -trakas), a certain measure of water, equivalent to six Kāshmīrī seers, or about 12 lbs. weight (cf. man 3, p. 572b, l. 39, and trakh) (Gr.Gr. 74). -traṭh f. (sg. dat. -traṭi), water-lightning, lightning accompanied by heavy rain, a water-spout. Such water is said to be hot and bad-smelling (El. pántraṭ). -ʦādar f. a sheet of water, water falling from a height in a sheet, a waterfall (El. pántsádar). -ʦhal m. a mill worked by a stream of water; a machine for propelling water; a syringe. -ʦāl f. a handful of water, water contained in the palm of the hand stretched out and hollowed. -wath f. (sg. dat. -wati), a water-path, a path through water or wet ground; a passage for admitting or letting out water. -yĕch m. (sg. dat. -yĕchas), a water demon; a Brāhmaṇ who attends funerals and memorial ceremonies (who accepts mean fees). -yĕchiñ f. a female water- demon. -zāl f. a slight disease involving a crop of small boils, something like small-pox, (?) chicken-pox. ¶ pāñĕ-wôñᵘ m. (of a tract of country) partly covered with water, and partly dry.

m. a wedge (esp. for splitting wood) (cf. dāra-pᵒ, p. 235a, l. 36) (K.Pr. 164, 204); a peg (for pegging something down) (L.V. 66); (in carpentry) a piece inserted to strengthen a joint. --pyonᵘ 1 m.inf. (in a boat or the like) the joining piece to fall (out), the planks to become apart.

m. grief, sorrow, mourning (e.g. on the death of a dear one) (cf. baba-pᵒ, p. 77a, l. 13; dahyulᵘ pᵒ, p. 202a, l. 17); cf. pȧndⁱ. --pyonᵘ 2 -- m.inf. grief, etc., to befal (cf. pŏtra-ponᵘ pyonᵘ, s.v. pọ̆thᵃr). ¶ pȧnⁱ nērun  m.inf. to issue sorrowfully, i.e. (after having achieved some pleasant object, that object) to lose all flavour (owing to an access of fear, sorrow, or other disturbing element), to turn to ashes in the mouth, to become a Dead Sea apple (cf. pȧndⁱ nērun).

m. jeweller's solder, the metal mixture used in soldering together the various parts of ornaments. ¶ pȧnⁱ-kasar f. the metal (of the ornament) which is lost in the processes of soldering (and which is part of the goldsmith's profit). -mal m. the impurity due to soldering (i.e. when a gold ornament is melted down, the base metal found in the product, due to the presence of solder). -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), the soldering parts of an ornament together; the marks of soldering at a junction of two pieces of metal.

m. N. of a town in Vihī Pargana in Kashmīr (the ancient Padmapura) (RT.Tr. II, 459; Śiv. 1180). The surrounding country is well known for producing fine crops of saffron (Rām. 1092, K.Pr. 180). -wuḍar f. the plateau near this town, famous for its saffron-crocus crops.
adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, or produced in Pö̃par. --kŏng -- m. saffron grown on the Pö̃par plateau.
(? spelling and gender), a certain bramble yielding an edible fruit, Rubus saxatilis (L. 73, popai).

f. (sg. dat. pŏphi), a father's sister, a paternal aunt (L. 458, pop; Śiv. 1445; K. 537, 1015; YZ. 76). -pörⁱ m. the sacrifice of an aunt, i.e. the great love shown by a paternal aunt to her nephew (i.e. love so great that she is ready to sacrifice herself for him). ¶ pŏpha-hash f. a husband's or wife's paternal aunt (K. 1016); cf. māsa-hash, p. 596a, l. 25. -nāñ f. a paternal grandfather's sister, a paternal great-aunt.

adj. (f. pŏphatᵃr or pŏphatᵘ̈rᵘ̈), descended from, or related through, a paternal aunt (Gr.Gr. 132). Used in the following:-- pŏphaturᵘ bôyᵘ m. the son of a father's sister, a cousin on the father's sister's side (Gr.Gr. 132). --zömiyĕ -- m. the husband of a husband's father's sister's daughter, a husband's cousin by marriage on the father's sister's side. ¶ pŏphatᵃr (or pŏphatᵘ̈rᵘ̈) bĕñĕ  f. a father's sister's daughter, a female cousin on the father's sister's side (Gr.Gr. 132). --bȧyⁱ kākañ -- f. the wife of a father's sister's son, a female cousin by marriage on the father's sister's side (Gr.Gr. 133). --zām -- (sg. dat. zömᵘ̈ or (among Paṇḍits) zōmᵘ̈), a woman's husband's father's sister's daughter, a husband's female cousin of this description.
m. the husband of a father's sister, a paternal uncle by marriage.
adj. c.g. sinful, wicked, a sinner, a criminal (Gr.M.; Rām. 260, 493, 501, 651, 849, 1363, 1505, 1513, 1516).

or pö̃pur (also written -purᵘ) m. a moth (El. pómpur, popur, pámpúr) (cf. dachĕ-pᵒ, p. 185b, l. 49; pana-pᵒ, p. 735a, l. 17) (Śiv. 1685, 1777; Rām. 1071). Its attraction to a flaming light and consequent death are proverbial. pö̃pȧrⁱ-gath f. (sg. dat. -güʦᵘ̈), the sudden death of a moth (in a flame, into which it is believed to be absorbed by excess of love) (K.Pr. 128); met. (out of excessive love for another) offering oneself as a sacrifice for him.

adj. (f. püpᵘ̈), (of fruit, grain, or the like, or met.) ripe, mature (cf. aḍa-pᵒ, p. 11b, l. 45) (Gr.Gr. 8, 138; K.Pr. 119, pup). ¶ papa-sag m. the final watering of a field of corn, etc., just before the grain is ripe (L. 463, popasag). -ʦēr f. a ripe apricot.
f. (sg. dat. popᵘrüñᵘ), the making (something) ripe, ripening (something) (e.g. treating an unripe fruit by rubbing it).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. popᵘrôwᵘ), to ripen an unripe fruit by rubbing or otherwise treating it (cf. popᵘrun); met. to 'ripen' a person's body by giving him a thorough drubbing so as to cause festering sores (which 'ripen'). popᵘrôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. popᵘrövᵘ), ripened, as ab.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. popᵘrᵘ), to cause to become ripe, i.e. to rub or otherwise treat an unripe fruit so as to ripen it (cf. popᵘrāwun). popᵘrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. popᵘrᵘ-müʦᵘ), made ripe in this way.

m. the floor or story of a house (cf. gāna-pᵒ, p. 288a, l. 37; kañi-pᵒ, p. 461b, l. 30; köñⁱ-pⁱ or köñiyĕ-pᵒ, p. 461a, ll. 7, 9; kuṭhⁱ-pⁱ, p. 489b, l. 25; lari-pᵒ, p. 531b, l. 8; nāra-pᵒ, p. 648a, l. 29) (Śiv. 738, 1246, 1567, 1645; K.Pr. 34); a house, residence, abode, palace (Rām. 740). ¶ pōra-thodᵘ adj. (f. -thüzᵘ̈), (of a house or the like) possessing lofty stories. -pōr karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. (for gend., see Gr.Gr. 75), to build story on story of a house.

in the following:-- pōr dith yunᵘ m.inf. (esp. of some one in rude health) to act as if certain of long life, to conduct oneself as if forgetting the ultimate certainty of death; such a certainty to be felt. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. a hope for a long life to arise, or to be certain.
in pōr rūzithgaʦhun m.inf. rheumatism of the sides, pleurodynia, to occur and become chronic. Cf. pôrᵘ.
m. direction, point of the compass, i.q. pôrᵘ, q.v. (Śiv. 515). Cf. potᵘ pōr, s.v. potᵘ.
or purān m. a book of ancient history, legendary and traditional, a Purāṇa (Śiv. 671, 758, 1763; K. 8, 944, 991). --phirȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to tell at length one's adventures or life history.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pōranôwᵘ), causal of pōrun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 174).
or pŏrôṭᵘ m. (sg. dat. pŏrāṭas or pŏröṭis), a cake made with butter or ghī, and of several layers, like pie-crust.
f. harassing, worrying, teasing, importuning. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. worrying, harassing, etc., to occur; to worry, harass, importune.
f. (sg. dat. pōravüñᵘ̈ 1) in pōrawan lāgüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to worry, harass, importune. --wād -- m. repeated worrying, worrying over and over again, persistent importuning.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pōrowᵘ), to make dry, to remove the moisture from something damp (cf. pōrun); to oppress, distress, trouble, annoy, molest, abuse, importune. pōrowᵘ-motᵘ  perf. part. (f. pōrüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), dried (of damp cloth, green vegetables, or the like); harassed, etc.

n.ag. (f. pōravüñᵘ̈ 2), effective, efficient, efficacious (e.g. a tool, a weapon, a medicine, etc.); a match for, one who is able to conquer an opponent, etc.; (of fresh grain, damp cloth, or the like) becoming dried (by the application of heat, etc.).

m. partial dryness, nearly complete dryness (e.g. that of drying grass, clothes drying in the sun, or the like); drying up (of a flow of blood, pus, or the like, becoming cured). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. dryness to come on, to begin to dry. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take drying up, (of a wound or sore) to begin to get well.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. pōryōv. Although of the third conjugation, this verb has pōranāwun (not *pūrᵃrāwun) for its causal, Gr.Gr. 174; cf. also pōrawun) to be, or become, sufficient, efficacious, adequate, competent (e.g. of a tool, a medicine, etc.); to be a match for, to be able to conquer (in warfare, disputation, wealth, resources, etc.); to become dry (of something moist) (Gr.Gr. xlviii) (cf. pōrawun). pōryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pōryē-müʦᵘ̈), become efficient (e.g. a blunt tool which has been sharpened, or a medicine about which there were doubts of its taking the desired effect, and so on); (a weak person who has gained strength and) become a match (for some person powerful in force, wealth, etc.).

or purush m. (sg. dat. pŏrashĕs), a man, a male human being (vir) (cf. mūla-pᵒ, p. 567a, l. 40; par pŏrush, p. 751a, l. 22) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1825); a man (homo) (Śiv. 20, 102, 1045, 1338, 1404); the Original Male, the Supreme Being, God (Śiv. 1119, 1277, 1415, 1544, 1594; Rām. 1652; K. 89, 360, 633, 751, 809, 1061). ¶ pŏrashĕ-kār m. manly work, virility, heroism, ability to do hard work or difficult work, human effort (Śiv. 1791). -mahanyuwᵘ m. a male human being; an image of a man.

m. (sg. dat. pōratas), a kind of tray covered with fine sand on which children who are learning the alphabet trace the forms of letters with the fore-finger; the marking off (with a stylus) of dates on an almanac performed by astrologers for their calculations (cf. chalan-pᵒ, p. 161a, l. 27; yōñĕ-pᵒ, p. 1201a, l. 21; pā̃-pᵒ, p. 747b, l. 50).

adj. (f. pörimᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or produced in, the country beyond (cf. öryumᵘ-pᵘ, p. 45b, l. 46); (in Kāshmīrī) of, or produced in, the country beyond the mountains, i.e. in the Panjāb (Gr.Gr. 151). --ḍaba -- m. a kind of small box or casket imported from the Panjāb. ¶ pörimᵘ̈ al f. a kind of large pumpkin. --hand -- f. (sg. dat. pörimi handi), a kind of chicory or endive imported from the Panjāb. --küñᵘ̈ -- f. a kind of coloured stone. --nāsth -- (sg. dat. --nāsti --), a kind of snuff imported from the Panjāb.
m. (sg. gen. pŏrᵃshārthas), any one of the four principal objects of human life (virtue, prosperity, love, and final beatitude); human effort or exertion, human vigour.

m. a side (of man, beast, river, etc.) (cf. okᵘ-pᵘ, p. 19a, l. 30; khôwurᵘ pᵒ, p. 425b, l. 20); direction (cf. pōr 4 and āra- pôrᵘ, p. 44a, l. 47) (Gr.M.). --raṭun -- m.inf. palsy to attack half the body, an attack of hemiplegia to come on (cf. pōr 3). ¶ pāri, adv. from (a certain) direction (cf. aki pᵒ, p. 20a, l. 46); at or by the side. āsun m.inf. to be at a person's side (of a friend, master, or the like), to be at hand to assist. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain or continue at hand as a helper. ¶ pörⁱ 1 adv. in (a certain) direction (cf. aḍi pᵒ, p. 13b, l. 32; aki pᵒ, p. 20a, l. 48; ami pᵒ, p. 54b, l. 46; amiy pᵒ, p. 55a, l. 46; brū̃ṭhⁱ pᵒ, p. 128b, l. 10; patimⁱ pᵒ, s.v. patyumᵘ) (Gr.Gr. 159; Gr.M.; Śiv. ʦŏwā-pörī, m.c., in all directions, 1052, 1504, 1891); (like pāri) from (a certain direction) (cf. dachinⁱ pᵒ, p. 186a, l. 37; khōwᵃ̇rᵃ̇ pᵒ, p. 425b, l. 10; patimⁱ pᵒ, as ab.) (Gr.Gr. 159); beyond (Gr.Gr. 151). --lagun -- m.inf. (out of love and affection) to be ready to offer one's own self (as a sacrifice) for a person, to devote oneself to a person (cf. pörⁱ 2) (Śiv. 628, 1343, 1502; YZ. 173). --pörⁱ -- adv. on every side, close up to and round about (used to signify affection, with verbs of union, looking at, devoting oneself to, and the like). --pörⁱ lagun -- m.inf. to devote oneself (as ab.) continually to a person, to offer oneself over and over again (as a sacrifice) for a person (Śiv. 190, 215, 417, 961, 1261, 1517; Rām. 511, 938, 1131, 1635; K. 3, 45, 54, 93, 101, 126, 158, etc.). ¶ pāryukᵘ sg. gen. (f. pāricᵘ̈), of, or belonging to (a certain) side or direction (cf. ami pᵒ, p. 54b, l. 50; amiy pᵒ, p. 55b, l. 1; khōwari pᵒ, p. 425b, l. 20); (with reference to a river, mountain, or the like) of, or belonging to, the far side, of beyond.
in örᵘ̈-pörᵘ̈, p. 42a, l. 42, q.v. Cf. āra-pôrᵘ, p. 44a, l. 47.
f. a hut (H. xii, 2). Cf. pahörᵘ̈.

f. a sacrifice (El. pãri); hence (cf. pörⁱ lagun, l. 3 ab.) --˚, one who is ready to offer herself as a sacrifice (for some one), i.e. who shows intense love (for a person) (cf. mās-pᵒ, p. 596a, l. 18; pŏph-pᵒ, p. 749a, l. 25); (as interjectional postposition) blessings (on, dat.) (K.Pr. 86, pārī).
f. the hole of a jackal, fox, or similar animal.

or (Śiv.) pörīzān f. (sg. dat. pörⁱzöñⁱ), thorough knowledge, complete acquaintance (El. parzán); testing, putting to the test; recognition; power of recognition, consciousness (Rām. 1173); cf. parʦun. --āsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. thorough putting to the test to occur; recognition to occur. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. accurate information to occur, to gain accurate information (Śiv. 1890). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take measures for obtaining accurate information (Śiv. 238, 1046).
f. knowledge of the truth, recognition of the truth, knowledge of God (Rām. 10, 1683); recognizing, recognition (Rām. 1566); recognition, familiarity, intimacy (Rām. 1095).

(by Paṇḍits often written) m. a flower, a blossom (cf. acha-pᵒ, p. 9b, l. 7; agastĕ-pᵒ, p. 17a, l. 31; ala-pᵒ, p. 22b, l. 26; alam-pᵒ, p. 24b, l. 20; arᵃg-pᵃ, p. 43a l. 14; ariñĕ-pᵒ, p. 44a, l. 37; bumbi-pᵒ, p. 107b, l. 42, and so many other names of particular flowers; also akāli-pᵒ, p. 21a, l. 37; naba-pᵒ, p. 619a, l. 15); (Gr.Gr. 22, 51, 163; Gr.M.; L. 460; W. 6; L.V. 42, 45, 102; Śiv. 54, 112, 113, 165, 181, 188, 373, 526, 827, 1185, 1196, 1692, etc.; Rām. 354-5, 617, 644, 647, 1043, etc.; K. 838, 1046; YZ. 31, 89, 527; K.Pr. 62, 88-9, 215); a flower in a pattern; an engraved or embossed ornament or decoration (like a flower) (cf. caphkali-pᵒ, p. 173b, l. 35); a boss, knob, stud, bunch of ribbons, rosette (cf. bīrbali-pᵒ, p. 119a, l. 4); a testicle, the scrotum (El.). --khanȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to engrave, scratch, or draw a flower-pattern. -kar, see pŏshkar. -körⁱ f. a flower-pattern, flower-embroidery, a tissued flower (on cloth, paper, etc.); an embroidered cloth. --phŏlȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. flowers to bloom, blooming to occur (Śiv. 132, 267, 498, 1180, 1744, 1760; K. 250); met. blooming (of the spirits to occur), hearty health, great prosperity, or the like, to be experienced or to come about. -ʦŏchĕ diñĕ f. pl. inf. to give flowers and cakes to perform a certain Musalmān rite. It is carried out in May-June when roses are in bloom, and consists in laying roses and special cakes (see the next) on the graves of deceased relatives. -ʦŏ̈ṭᵘ̈ f. a kind of cake consisting of cheese put sandwich-like between two slabs of wheaten dough and fried. --warshun -- m.inf. to shower flowers, rain flowers from above (in token of approbation, rejoicing, or the like) (K. 196, 255). ¶ pōshĕ-bāg m. a flower-garden (El. poshibág, Śiv. 963). -bạrᵃg m. a flower-petal. -chöñᵘ̈ f. the flower-winnowing, i.e. the falling of the petals of over-blown flowers. -chạthᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a sunshade or umbrella made of flowers (used on festive occasions, e.g. held over a bridegroom). -caman m. a flower-garden. -ḍal m. a flower-lake, a low plain with a lake, and covered with flowery shrubs. -ḍūrᵘ m. a flower-bed, a flower-plot. -dasta m. a handful, or posy, of flowers (Śiv. 76). -gọ̆ndᵘ m. a flower-posy, a nosegay, bouquet (H. v, 4); (El.) a wreath of flowers, such as is donned by an old Paṇḍit when getting married. -gŏndurᵘ m., id. -grū̃phᵘ m. a cluster of flowers. -kujⁱ or -kujᵘ̈ f. a flower-shrub, a shrub which bears flowers; a shrub covered with flowers. -kulᵘ m. a flower-tree, a tree which bears flowers; a tree covered with flowers. -konḍᵘ m. a flower-thorn, a thorn growing on a flower-shrub; a thorn attached to a flower. -köñᵘ̈ f. a group of flowers (e.g. in a flower-jar), a few flowers (Gr.Gr. 163). -körⁱ f. embroidery (of a flower-pattern). -kyomᵘ m. a flower-insect (such as a bee or the like). -lünḍᵘ̈ f. a flowery twig (Śiv. 1048). -loṭᵘ m. the stalk or pedicle of a flower. -mödān m. a flower-meadow, a field of flowers (H. xi, 3). -māl f. a garland of flowers (Śiv. 659, 1165, 1690; Rām. 489; K. 423, 583, 1077; K.Pr. 70). -motᵘ adj. (f. -müʦᵘ̈), flower-mad, infatuated with flowers, a passionate lover of flowers (K.Pr. 173); met. a person who habitually dresses from head to foot in flowers or in many-coloured or richly embroidered garments (Śiv. 189, as a term of endearment). -mŏyā f. a few flowers (Gr.Gr. 165). -nūl m. the mango-bird (El.), the 'Chakōr' or Greek partridge, the Golden Oriole (L. 117, 143, poshnal, Oriolus kundoo; Śiv. 469, 963, 1360, 1365, 1440, 1690, 1721, 1785, 1812; Rām. 675, 1102, 1626). -phulay f. the blooming of flowers (e.g. that in spring). -phĕran m. a flower-garment, a garment of flowers (such as that worn by a bride). -prang m. a flower-couch, a couch or bed covered with flowers. -pathur m. (sg. dat. -patharas), a pile or collection of fallen flowers (e.g. at the foot of a flower-tree). -pūz or -pūzā f. worship with flowers (e.g. scattered before, or on, the adored object) (Śiv. 51, 95, 1131, 1145, 1167, 1183, 1199; K. 391). -rang m. the manner of a flower, i.e. evanescence, impermanence, transientness. -thal f. a flower-bed. -thôpᵘ m. a handful of flowers, a bouquet (such as is held in the hand), a bunch of flowers (Gr.Gr. 164). -thürᵘ̈ f. a flower-shrub (Śiv. 1061, 1848; Rām. 1176, 1580; H. ii, 3; YZ. 32, 66). -thürᵘ̈ khārüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to erect a flower-shrub, i.e. to draw or paint one (on a wall or the like). -tula adj. c.g. weighing as much as a flower, extremely light, of hardly any weight. -tulᵘ m. a bunch (esp. a fairly small one) of flowers (Gr.Gr. 164). -tulᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a flower-bee, a kind of bee believed to bite flowers in its search for honey. -tônᵘ m. flowerness, acting like one who tends flowers, gentleness of disposition. -tǖrᵘ̈ f. flower-coolness, the cool weather of the flower-season (i.e. spring). -ṭūrᵘ m. an unblown flower, a bud. -ʦhürᵘ̈ f. a flower-basket, a shallow basket for holding flowers; a basket filled with flowers. -ʦöryunᵘ m. the refuse (leaves, stalks, etc.) thrown away in arranging flowers. -wörᵘ̈ f. a small flower-garden (Śiv. 269, 963, 1028). -warshun m. (sg. dat. -warshĕnas), a shower of flowers (from the sky) (Śiv. 508, 1146, 1188, 1913; Rām. 1714, 1723, 1777; K. 56, 451, 567, 771, 874). -wạthᵃr m. a flower-leaf, a petal (esp. a large one) (Gr.Gr. 74). -zôlᵘ m. a cluster of flower-buds or young flowers. -zanḍ m. a collection of flowers (esp. for offering in worship or the like) (Gr.Gr. 163). -zār پوشہ زار or -zāl a place of flowers, a place where flowers grow in profusion (W. 112, -zār); cf. kȧndⁱ-zāl(-zār), p. 455a, l. 40. ¶ pōshĕn-hondᵘ tāj m. a garland (El.).

m. in pōsh pōsh karun m.inf. to incite, prompt, encourage (esp. a child to his studies or the like) (cf. pöshⁱran); (of a coachman) to shout out warnings (to people on the road to make them get out of the way). ¶ pöshⁱ pöshⁱ m. incitement, encouragement (of a person employed in any work, in order to induce him to apply himself with diligence). pöshⁱ pöshⁱ karun m.inf. (of a coachman) to shout out, as ab.
adj. c.g. clothed in, dressed in, wearing, used --˚, as in pō̃bᵃri-pōsh, one who wears a shawl. See pō̃bᵘ̈rᵘ̈, p. 678b, l. 25.

m. (for gend., see W. 18; sg. dat. pŏshākas), clothes, raiment, attire, garments, dress (Gr.M.; W. 143; H. v, 9; viii, 9; x, 2, 4, 7, 9; xii, 6, 7; K.Pr. 173). --pairun -- m.inf. to put on one's clothes, to dress (Gr.M.). --trāwun -- m.inf. to put off a garment, to disrobe oneself (H. v, 7; x, 2).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pōshĕnôwᵘ), to cause something (e.g. food provided for a number of persons) to last out and be sufficient, to cause available materials to be sufficient for the accomplishment of the work for which they are employed or the like. pōshĕnôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pōshĕnövᵘ̈ müʦᵘ̈), (of food, materials, etc., as ab.) made to be sufficient.
adj. c.g. concealed, hidden (El.). --sapadun -- m.inf. to disappear (El.).

or pōshkar (as if from pōsh) m. N. of a place of pilgrimage in the hills about 40 miles west of Śrīnagar (RT.Tr. II, 476); N. of a celebrated place of pilgrimage near Ajmere in India (Śiv. 627); a species of medicinal plant, a species of Ligularia (El.); a certain precious stone, said to be a kind of ruby.

(also written) m. (sg. dat. pŏshpadantas), a N. of an attendant of Śiva said to be the author of the hymn called mahimna-pār (p. 554b, l. 48), and, hence, in Śiv. 867, identified with Śiva himself; N. of the elephant of the north-west quarter. One of these two is said to have offered his tusks to Śiva in place of a flower-offering (Śiv. 52).
or pōshta (properly pol. impve. of pōshun), (used as an exclamation of congratulation) bravo!; (as subst. m.) congratulation, words of congratulation or welcome.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. pūshᵘ 2; for 1, see s.v.), to be sufficient (e.g. of food or the like for a large party, or of means for accomplishing an object) (K.Pr. 44, 233); (of a journey) to be completed over the whole area intended; to be accomplished without interruption, to be carried on successfully without interruption; (of something used) to last without being worn out; to be competent, to gain a victory, to get the upper hand, to prevail (Gr.Gr. 205, 252; Gr.M.; Śiv. 278; Rām. 644, 659, 941, 956; K. 31, 242, 328, 357, 361, 363, 434, 448, 545, 575, 578, 616, 641, 826, 1019; K.Pr. 73, 173). pūshᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pūshᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), completed, etc., as ab.; become victorious (K. 679). ¶ pōshĕn-hār n.ag. c.g. (of food, etc.) sufficient to go all round (among a number of people); lasting, not being worn out; one who is prevailing. -pāy m. means of success, strength, competence, ability, force, power to succeed (Rām. 1580, K. 570). -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who prevails, one who is victorious.

m. an animal of the cattle specie (such as a cow, a horse, a buffalo, or sheep), a beast (a non-human animal) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 753, 1900); esp. a beast offered in sacrifice (L.V. 63). Cf. pashu. ¶ pȧshⁱ-zān f. (sg. dat. -zöñᵘ̈), the intellect of an animal, an intellect as meagre as that of a brute; knowledge regarding beasts, veterinary science. -zāth f. (sg. dat. -zöʦᵘ̈-), the animal race, the tribe of animals.

m. (sg. ag. pöshⁱ 1), a certain kind of wood (useful for making beds and the like); a piece of furniture made of this wood. Cf. pöshᵘ̈. ¶ pöshⁱ-hüṭⁱ f. a piece of this wood. -kulᵘ m. the tree from which this wood is taken. It grows on mountain slopes. -lünḍᵘ̈ f. a branch of this tree. -nörᵘ̈ f. a long mountain path, thickly encumbered with trees. -wan m. a grove of these trees. -zyunᵘ m. firewood of this tree.
adj. (f. püshᵘ̈), possessing a thatched roof, roofed, thatched, used --˚, as in okᵘ-pᵘ, p. 19a, l. 37; nar-pᵒ, p. 646a, l. 47; pĕʦi-pᵒ, s.v. pë̆ʦᵘ̈. See pash.
f. a kind of wood of which the skewer-like little sticks, on which is wound the shawl-thread, are made (El.). Cf. pôshᵘ 1 and prüʦᵘ̈.

(for pöshᵘ̈) in the following:-- pöshⁱ-nāv f. a boat for carrying dung and refuse (K.Pr. 16, páshnáv); cf. pāh 1. -wātul m. (f. -wātalas), a mehtar, a low-caste man who conveys away ordure from the place where it has been deposited. -wātüjᵘ̈ f. a woman who is so employed.
f. (sg. dat. pöshⁱrüñⁱ), inciting, encouragement (e.g. encouraging a child in its studies, or a person to apply himself to some work with diligence). Cf. pōsh 2.

or pōsth m. (sg. dat. pōstas), skin, hide (esp. of a man); outer coat, rind, crust, shell, bark; a seed-capsule, a poppy-head. --wālun -- m.inf. to skin, flay, remove the outer husk (Rām. 374, 382, 433, 707, 843); to abuse, scold, chide severely, reprimand. ¶ pōsta-byôlᵘ m. one of the seeds inside a capsule, esp. poppy seed. -khŏkhurᵘ m. the poppy-capsule, a poppy-head. -wālay f. skinning, flaying; scolding, violent chiding.
m. the yew-tree, Taxus baccata (El. pōstal, pōstil; L. 79, 80, posthal, posthil). Its bark was formerly used by the poor as a substitute for tea (L. 72). Cf. the next.
f. a small book, a booklet, a pamphlet. Cf. pŏstukh.
or pōstukh m. (sg. dat. pŏ(pō)stakas ), a book, volume, manuscript (cf. burza-pᵒ, pp. 130b, l. 50, and 131a, l. 2) (K. 990). pŏstakh-gāḍa f.pl. 'book-fishes', i.e. a collection of useless books.
f.(sg. dat. pösᵃrüñᵃ), abuse, censure, scolding (of a servant or naughty child) (cf. kaḍañĕ-pösᵃrañĕ, p. 386a, l. 39) (Gr.Gr. 118).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pösᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. pösᵃrun, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pösᵒrᵒ), to abuse, censure, scold (a servant, a naughty child, a wife, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 118). pösᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. pösᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), scolded, as ab.

or posᵘ m. foam, froth, scum (El. paus); used met. in such compounds as braga-pᵒ, p. 120a, l. 29, and brạyĕ-pᵒ, p. 130a, l. 36. --anun -- m.inf. to cause foam or scum to arise; met. to worry by much talking, asking many questions, much verbal urging, or the like. --trāwun -- m.inf. to foam (El.). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. foam or scum to come into existence; to be worried, as ab.
(? spelling) m. worship (El. probably incorrect for pāṭh, q.v.); manner, mode (El. probably for pöṭhⁱ, q.v.).
f. (sg. dat. pō̃ṭaki), a small piece of wool (K.Pr. 224, ponṭak).
m. one who suffers from prolapsus ani or from piles.
adj. c.g. (of a sheet of paper or the like) covered with ruled lines.

m. a man who is stupid by nature, lazy and wanting in intelligence. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become stupid, to be put to shame by exposing one's ignorance, to be defeated in a discussion. --karun -- m.inf. utterly to put to silence or defeat in an argument.
m. onomat. a flop, a slapping sound, e.g. caused by a flat object falling from a height on mud or soft ground, or by a slap on the naked shoulder. Cf. paṭās.

f. (sg. dat. pŏṭi), the rectum (cf. batakh-pᵒ, p. 144a, l. 50; pȧnzⁱ-pⁱ, p. 745b, l. 42); prolapsus ani, piles, hæmorrhoids (El.) (Gr.Gr. 16). --wālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to bring down the rectum', i.e. (in running a race or the like) to put a person to great exertions and defeat him. --wasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the rectum to descend, to be exhausted by great exertions (e.g. by carrying a heavy load or running a race). ¶ pŏṭa-gagᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. 'a rectum-rat', prolapse of the rectum.

pö̃th, or paĩth f. (sg. dat. pǖ̃ʦᵘ̈), a row, a line (of people, trees, or the like) (cf. rĕyĕ-pᵒ, s.v. rĕy); a line of letters (in a book); a row, or line of descent (of a family, etc.); a road (Gr.Gr. 22, paĩth). --ʦhĕnüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a line (of people or things) to be broken; a line of descent to be broken, i.e. to fail for lack of descendants, a family to become extinct. --ʦhŏṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a family to become extinct, as ab. --ʦaṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to break a line (of people or things), to break off a line (of writing).

f. (sg. dat. pōṭhaki), lit. plumpness, fatness (Gr.Gr. 128); hence, accumulation of wealth (causing plumpness, fatness, etc.), the condition of being well-to-do. --āsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an accumulation to be made, esp. a private hoard to be collected.

m. (possession by a demon resulting in) convulsions (of a baby) (cf. prāh-pᵒ, p. 757b, l. 1); frenzy, delirium (e.g. that occurring through coming upon a cross-roads on a pitch-dark night, which is esp. liable to cause abortion to a pregnant woman, and is believed to be due to demoniacal possession). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such delirium to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to cause demoniacal possession, as ab.
or pö̃thun m. (f. pö̃thüñᵘ̈), a traveller, one who is travelling, or one who is fond of travelling.

m. a difficult and distant journey, journeying to great distance (cf. rĕyĕ-pᵒ, s.v. rĕy); foreign residence far from home. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to traverse a long and difficult journey. --karun -- m.inf. to undertake, or go, on a long and difficult journey.
n.ag. (pōṭhavüñᵘ̈), a person or thing which is gradually becoming fat, thick, strong; (of a business) becoming prosperous.

adv. (i.q. pöthⁱ, q.v.) in the manner of, like, in (such-and-such) a mode (cf. mushikas-pᵒ, p. 597b, l. 40; rasa-pᵒ, s.v. ras; rᵃ̇tᵃ̇-pᵃ̇, s.v. rᵒtᵒ) (Gr.Gr. 153; H. iii, 1; ʦuri-pᵒ, theft-like, secretly). ¶ Often used to convert an adjective or pronoun into an adverb (cf. baḍi-pᵒ, p. 84b, l. 37; bĕdiwath-pᵒ, p. 89b, l. 6; bĕnⁱ-pⁱ, p. 151a, l. 32; khāsa-pᵒ, p. 417a, l. 29; nȧnⁱ-pⁱ, p. 640a, l. 23) (Rām. 1292). ¶ Added to the agent case (cf. pöṭhⁱ) (cf. phira- thurⁱ pöṭhin, p. 702a, l. 9; prạkhᵃ̇ṭᵃ̇-pᵃ̇, p. 758a, l. 14; prakȧṭⁱ-pⁱ, p. 759a, l. 11); added to the agent case of the genitive (cf. pöṭhⁱ) (Śiv. 277). ¶ Added pleonastically to an adverb (cf. anam- nĕnam-pᵒ, p. 34b, l. 23) (Śiv. 576, 672, 790, 1668; Rām. 951, 1016, 1311, 1315, 1362; H. viii, 5, yithay-pᵒ, in this very manner).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. pōṭhyōv), to be, or become, plump, stout and solid, fat (Gr.Gr. 111, 128, 173, 246). pōṭhyō-motᵘ perf. part. (pōṭhyē-müʦᵘ̈), become stout, etc., as ab.

or pŏtᵃr (also spelt puᵒ) m. (sg. dat. pŏtras), a son (cf. kŏl-pᵒ, p. 437a, l. 4; mölⁱ-pⁱ, p. 566b, l. 26; rāza-pᵒ, s.v. rāza). (Gr.Gr. 51, 72, 143; Gr.M. putr) (Śiv. 919; Rām. 1138; K. 488, 543, 545, 594, 620, 623, 894, 1067; YZ. 155, 464, 466; K.Pr. 91); esp. a good son, a well-behaved son. ¶ pŏtra-bọ̆chᵘ adj. (f. -bö̆chᵘ̈), one who hungers for a son, one who longs for a son (K.Pr. 174); one who is tenderly absorbed in an only much-longed-for son, whom one fears to lose (K. 137). -bŏchĕr m. longing for a son. -bata m. 'son's boiled rice', i.e. the bringing up and supporting a son. -bāv m. the becoming a son, the being born as a son (to so-and-so) (K. 26-7, 95). -dôdᵘ m. pain for a son, intense longing for a son; the sorrow caused by having an unworthy son, or by losing a beloved son (K. 501, YZ. 417); intense love for, or anxiety concerning, a son (K. 817, K.Pr. 65). -dag f. 'a son-blow', the grief, or pangs, caused by a son's death; the pains of travail (K.Pr. 126). -dag pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. the sorrow on account of a son's death to fall (on a person). -dagal adj. c.g. one who suffers from grief at the loss of a son. -dŏkh m. grief caused by a son's death. -gāsh m. 'son-brightness', the joy caused by the birth (or existence, or recovery from illness, etc.) of a son, or on hearing by parents praise of a son. -kār m. the duties of a son (towards his parents) (Rām. 1248). -karm m. the conduct or duties of a son (to his parents); filial conduct; the obsequial duties of a son at his parents' death; met. the filial conduct of a servant to his master, of a pupil to his master, or the like. -mã̄gay f. prayers for a son (to a holy man, a physician, a god, or the like); prayer for a son (i.e. asking a person for a son, with a view to adoption). -möjⁱ or -möjᵘ̈ f. a son's mother (K. 143); esp. a woman who is the mother of many well-behaved and virtuous sons. -marun m. 'a son-death', a despicable son (K. 22). -ponᵘ pyonᵘ m.inf. the agony in the heart caused by the death of a son to fall (on a person), see ponᵘ 2. -pĕnḍ m. the ball or lump of rice offered by a son to the Manes at obsequial ceremonies or śrāddhas; the ceremony of making this offering. -shūkh m. (sg. dat. -shūkas), grief for a son (e.g. one who is dead) (K. 489). -sath f. (sg. dat. -süʦᵘ̈), the hope (of bliss in this world and the next) caused by the existence or birth of a son. -sāvĕr m. richness in sons, the possession of many well-behaved and virtuous sons. -sāway m. happiness caused by the possession of a satisfactory son. -tônᵘ m. son-hood, filial behaviour, conduct of a son, or (to non-parents) like that of a son (Gr.Gr. 233). -tandal f. the possession (by one person) of numerous sons. -trēsh f. libations and other obsequial ceremonies performed by a son for his father's happiness in the next world. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who has a son, or who has just got a son, esp. a virtuous son. -zāy f. the birth of a son (K. 95, 102, 129); the festival on the birth of a son.

m. (sg. dat. pöthᵃras), (originally) a vessel, dish, or similar utensil (cf. pāthᵃr and pötᵃr); hence, the collection or arrangement of all the utensils required for any specific purpose (cf. hurⁱ-pⁱ, p. 347a, l. 9; kuna-pᵒ, p. 453b, l. 8); a collection, or group, of people genl. (cf. mŏnḍa-pᵒ, p. 574a, l. 43; maʦa-pᵒ, p. 602b, l. 16); a character in a dramatic performance, a dramatis persona (cf. jūgⁱ-pⁱ, p. 371b, l. 20); (Śiv. 1705); --˚ conduct such as that of the first member of the compound, the actions or conduct of such a person (cf. barbuzⁱ-pⁱ, p. 119a, l. 44; bözⁱgar-pⁱ, p. 152b, l. 25; canaphȧlⁱ-pⁱ, p. 172a, l. 27; dŏda-shurⁱ-pⁱ, p. 190a, l. 21; dȧjⁱ-pⁱ, p. 202b, l. 22; dāri-dajĕ-pᵒ, p. 238b, l. 23; kŏ-pöthar, p. 464b, l. 16; mȧtⁱ-pⁱ, p. 602a, l. 48; maʦa-pᵒ, p. 602b, l. 16; phakīr-pᵒ, p. 690b, l. 1; phȧshⁱ-pⁱ, p. 712b, l. 38; pasörⁱ-pⁱ, p. 783b, l. 40); --˚ the conduct or actions of a person following a certain (esp. the dramatic) profession (cf. baca-pᵒ, p. 79a, l. 21; bā̃ḍa-pᵒ, p. 82a, l. 36; dạrza-pᵒ, p. 251a, l. 46; maskhara-pᵒ, p. 599a, l. 28); the conduct or duties, generally associated with a person, or the circumstances generally associated with any action (cf. marda-pᵒ, p. 589b, l. 30; nēthᵃr-pᵃ, p. 661b, l. 50). --aʦun -- m.inf. to enter a character, to act in the character of someone else, to assume another's character. --karȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to make pretences, to pretend refusal (e.g. when pressed to eat or take some enjoyment, and desirous of complying, to affect want of desire). --karanāwun -- m.inf. to cause dramatic characters to be assumed, to arrange a dramatic representation (K. 957). --lagun -- m.inf. (when something insignificant is falsely reported to be very important or in great quantity) a great crowd (of sightseers, customers, or the like) to assemble. --ʦānun -- m.inf. 'to cause a character to enter', to exaggerate the virtues or vices (of any person or thing). --wahārun -- m.inf. (in order to cheat) to spread abroad false information regarding some inferior article, action, or the like. ¶ pöthᵃras aʦun m.inf. to enter the practice (of some business), to set to work on a certain course of conduct.
adj. (f. pọ̆thᵘ̈rᵘ̈), one of the forms which pọ̆thᵃr (q.v.) takes when used as an adj. at the end of a compound, as in pönʦa-pọ̆thᵘrᵘ, possessing five sons, see p. 743a, l. 30. Cf. pŏtur.

adj. (sg. f. nom. püṭhᵘ̈, dat. pachĕ), stout, plump and solid (cf. atha-pᵒ, p. 61b, l. 20); cf. pūṭhᵘ and pōṭhun. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become plump; (in some occupation) to gain successfully the fruits of one's labour.

adv. in the manner of, like, in (such-and-such) a mode; used --˚ (cf. buḍi-pᵒ, p. 85b, l. 22; baṭa-pᵒ, p. 138a, l. 42; bāzi-pᵒ, p. 153a, l. 13; khörᵘ̈v-pᵘ̈, p. 408b, l. 1; kŏ-pᵒ, p. 464b, l. 14; mushikas-pᵒ, p. 597b, l. 45; rasa-pᵒ, s.v. ras (El. pãṭ, pãṭh, manner; Gr.M.; W. 96; Śiv. 73, 156; K. 642; H. xii, 6, 7, 17). ¶ Often used to convert an adjective or pronoun into an adv. (cf. āsān-pᵒ, p. 50b, l. 3; awush-pᵒ, p. 71b, l. 43; azān-pᵒ, p. 75a, l. 3; baḍi-pᵒ, p. 84b, l. 37; bĕdiwath-pᵒ, p. 89b, l. 6; jān-pᵒ, p. 374b, l. 49; kuni pᵒ, p. 390, l. 34; K. 375, 448, 616; khāsa-pᵒ, p. 417a, l. 29; khŏsh-pᵒ, p. 418b, l. 4; nĕsangā-pᵒ, p. 658a, l. 24; pūra-pᵒ, p. 754b, l. 26) (Gr.Gr. 153; Gr.M.; Śiv. 25, 70, 285, 728, 1426; Rām. 55; K. 229, 645, 811; kami pᵒ, how? 602, 607). ¶ Often added to the agent case (cf. bĕnⁱ-pⁱ, separately, apart, p. 151a, l. 32; nĕshī˜kⁱ-pⁱ, fearlessly, p. 657b, l. 27; phira-thurⁱ-pⁱ, back to front, p. 702a, l. 8; prạkhᵃ̇ṭᵃ̇-pᵃ̇, manifestly, p. 758a, l. 13; prakȧtⁱ-pⁱ, id., p. 759a, l. 11; pȧzⁱ-pⁱ, truly, assuredly (Gr.M.; H. x, 6, 10; YZ. 237), s.v. pozᵘ; rᵃ̇tᵃ̇-pᵃ̇, well, rightly, properly, s.v. rᵒtᵒ) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1805, 1861, 1876; H. xii, 5). ¶ Or with the agent of the genitive (cf. kañĕ- hȧndⁱ pᵒ, like a stone) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 54, 753, 1164, 1440, 1806, 1808, etc.; Rām. 510, 1332, 1634, 1737; YZ. 34). ¶ And so, added pleonastically to an adverb (cf. anam-nĕnam-pᵒ, p. 34b, l. 23; kĕtha-pᵒ, how? p. 488a, l. 21) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 52, 171, 240, 439, 490, 571, 683-4, 713-4, etc.; Rām. kĕtha-pᵒ, 53-4, 111, 412, 621, etc.; yitha-pᵒ, 59, 1007; K. kĕtha-pᵒ, 9, 669, 799; H. kĕtha-pᵒ, iii, 9; v, 8; viii, 5; x, 8; xii, 3, 24; tithay-pᵒ, xii, 23; yĕthay-pᵒ, xii, 22). ¶ Cf. pāṭh 2 in papan-pāṭh (p. 749b, l. 18) and pöṭhin.
adj. c.g. one who is devoted to good actions, religious duties, or reading holy books.
adj. (as subst., f. pŏṭiladiñ), one who suffers from prolapsus ani or hæmorrhoids.

putulᵘ, or putolᵘ m. a statue (of stone), an idol, image, effigy (Gr.Gr. 145; H. iv, 6; YZ. 480; K.Pr. 29); met. a stupid, lumpish, fellow (cf. brēṭha-pᵒ, p. 128a, l. 3). Cf. pŏtᵘ̈jᵘ̈. ¶ putal-khāna m. a temple, or room, in which idols are worshipped (H. vi, 4).
f. a tool employed by plasterers for slapping and smoothing plaster which has been applied to a wall. Cf. paṭökⁱ, paṭākh, and paṭösⁱ.
adj. (f. pọ̆tᵘ̈rᵘ̈), one of the forms which pọ̆thᵃr (q.v.) takes when used as an adj. at the end of a compound, as in pönʦa-pŏtur, possessing five sons, see p. 743a, l. 30. Cf. pọ̆thᵒrᵒ.
f. a certain part of the anus, described as above it, and ring-formed.

f. (sg. dat. pötᵃrĕ), a kind of stone, described as occurring in large smooth slabs, used for paving temple sanctuaries and the like. ¶ pötᵃrĕ-büṭhᵃ f. a mound (in the lowland below a mountain) which has an outcrop of this stone. -kān f. (sg. dat. -köñᵘ̈), a quarry of this stone. -küñᵘ̈ f. a slab of this stone. ¶ pötᵃri-ã̄gun m. (sg. dat. -ã̄ganas), a courtyard paved with slabs of this stone.
m. the pan of a pair of scales (cf. hāyĕkh-pᵒ, p. 364a, l. 45).

(sg. dat. pötᵃris), an oar (for rowing) (it is paddle-shaped, with a round or heart-shaped blade); the wooden part of the Kāshmīrī spade (consisting of a long handle with wooden block at one end, on which the foot is pressed in the act of digging, and into the lower end of which the iron blade is fixed) (cf. liwañĕ-pᵒ, p. 542a, l. 10). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to ply an oar, to row a boat; met. to keep a business vigorously going. ¶ pötᵃri-ṭŏngurᵃ m. a kind of spade with a wide blade (used for planting vegetables).
or potus in pŏtus (or potus) path  adv. one after the other, in regular succession; again and again, repeatedly.

m. (sg. dat. pötras), a cup, platter (for eating) (of earthenware or metal) (cf. gö̃ḍa-pᵒ, p. 277a, l. 50, and pāthᵃr and pöthᵃr). ¶ pötra-mēl m. 'union in dishes', eating together from the same platter or similar platters (e.g. owing to relationship, friendship, or common office); met. living together, partnership in earnings. --mēlun -- m.inf. to unite in dishes, as ab. --milawan -- f. union in dishes, eating from the same dish or at the same feast; met. communion of business or employment. -pūz or -pūzā f. 'dish-worship'; to give a feast of many dishes filled with varied food. -ʦāl f. (after the conclusion of a feast) the carrying away of the dirty dishes and cleaning them; the remains of an offering (Rām. 612).
m. a son (esp. an only boy-child) (cf. lala-pᵒ, p. 522a, l. 6; lōla-pᵒ, p. 523a, l. 17; pönʦa-pᵒ, p. 743a, l. 28); a child (Gr.Gr. 145).

adj. c.g. and adv. behind, in the rear (Śiv. 1029); subsequent to, after, following; cf. patau and path 3. --ã̄gun -- m. (sg. dat. -ã̄ganas), the rear courtyard of a house (used by the women-folk). --ongᵘjᵘ -- f. 'the finger behind', helping and inciting (someone) to an insolent action. --atha -- m. the back of the hand. --bachĕ -- f.pl. 'the back banks', the nates. --bĕha -- m. sitting down behind, (of an employed person) easily ceasing work when not under the observation of the employer, or (in his presence) ceasing or giving up work owing to inability to continue; a support below and behind a jar (or the like, on which it rests). --bal -- m. the strength of the back, the strength which one has behind one (in some task), backing up (by supporters, friends, money, help, materials, etc.). --bar -- m. a back door. --borᵘ -- m. a hole in a rear wall (for admitting air, light, etc.). --baran -- f. (sg. dat. -barüñᵘ̈), a lightly built back door. --biṭh -- f. an assembly behind (people's back), meeting of people unknown to their superiors (parents, respectable persons, masters, or the like). --büṭhᵘ̈ -- f. the space beyond the three openings on the top of a cooking range; cf. --ʦôrᵘ, bel. ¶ potᵘ chŏkh m. (sg. dat. chŏkas), the final strokes in churning (by which the butter is collected). --chalun -- m.inf. to do the after washing, to give the final rinsing in washing; (four or five months after a death) to perform the ceremonial washing of clothes which have been kept dirty during the period of mourning. --chamb karun -- m.inf. to make a precipice behind (a person), i.e. to endeavour by secret calumny, etc., to damage the actions of a person (esp. of a person who trusts the calumniator). --chŏmba -- m. the final knocking out of grain from the ear against a post (done to the remains on the threshing floor after the whole amount on the floor has been threshed) (see chŏmba); met. slander of a person behind his back. ¶ potᵘ dab m. a knocking down from behind. --ḍab -- f. a covered balcony at the back of a house. --ḍȧchⁱ -- or --ḍüchᵘ̈ -- f. the post towards the stern of a boat for supporting the mat roof; see ḍȧchⁱ. --ḍakh -- m. (sg. dat. --ḍakhas --), a rear support, a prop for a sloping rear wall of a house; (in any work) help given from behind; shoving back, pushing a boat backwards with a punting-pole or the like. --ḍokhᵘ -- m. the stern mat roof of a boat; help or support given from behind or subsequently. --dal -- m. the last of several successive poundings (of grain) in a mortar. --ḍālāna -- m. a covered balcony in the rear of a house. --ḍamb -- m. the stern hold of a boat. --ḍang -- m. hobble ropes or the like tied to the hind legs of an unruly quadruped; hobbling an animal in this way. --dar -- m. the back pan of a pair of scales (into which the weights are put). --dara -- m. the back side of anything (e.g. the body, a house, a mountain, etc.). --dorᵘ -- m. the back row of a number of people collected at some entertainment. --dörᵘ̈ -- f. a back window (K.Pr. 147). --drāmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --drāmüʦᵘ̈ --), returned, retreated; cf. --nērun, bel. --drasa -- m. pulling back (a person) (by the arm, by a rope, by his garment, or the like). --dav khārun -- m.inf. to make a counter-bet, to make a counter-accusation, to make a counter- claim. --dav karun -- m.inf. to offer a counter-bet, etc., as ab. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to turn (a person, ship, vehicle, etc.) back; cf. pȧtⁱ dyunᵘ, bel. ¶ potᵘ gab m. a secondary shoot or sprout, i.e. a shoot sprouting from a decayed or cut- down tree. --göbath -- f. (sg. dat. --göbüʦᵘ̈ --), slander behind a person's back. --gilan gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a backward whirl to occur, i.e. a mortal relapse to occur in convalescence; a change of wish to occur (e.g. the wishing to do something which one has hitherto refused to do). --ganḍ -- m. (in the rope for hauling a number of tree-trunks or the like) the final knot fastened to make all tight. --güñᵘ̈ -- f. the flesh at the tail end of a fish; the similar portion at the end of a tree, a post, or the like. --grāy -- f. (in the act of walking) involuntarily turning the body round; the final rinsing of clothes in the wash. --gas dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give abraiding behind, repeatedly to censure or object to. ¶ potᵘ khal m. a threshing floor behind (the house, i.e. close to the house and not at a distance). --kharc -- m. an additional contribution beyond the estimated expense (of doing anything). --khirikⁱ -- f. a window at the back; met. (when busily employed in any work) the mind being secretly distracted by other thoughts. --khōrĕn -- adv. (with verbs of coming) on so-and-so's heels; hence, immediately, very speedily; cf. khūrᵘ̈ 1 and pȧtⁱ khūrⁱ, bel. --khash -- m. a sword-cut from behind, a treacherous wound; met. the occurrence of some secret and unexpected severe loss. --kal -- f. subsequent anxiety, (when engaged on some work) private anxiety (about some other); anxiety as to the success of gaining some desired object. --kamöyⁱ -- f. secret (additional) earnings, illicit earnings in addition to one's authorized salary. --kana bōzun -- m.inf. to hear behind with the ear, to listen to some secret talk, to eavesdrop. --körᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the neck to go back, i.e. to become disgraced by having to take to shameful work; cf. pȧtⁱ körᵘ̈ g., bel. --kartūth -- m. (sg. dat. --kartūtas --), the subsequent sending of gifts, (after a marriage) the customary gifts sent by the bride's people to her husband and his people. --kath -- f. (sg. dat. --kathi --), a word behind, i.e. secret calumny, calumny behind the back of the person spoken against, slander (El. pautkat). --kath karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to utter such secret calumny. --kyulᵘ -- m. the after nail-piercing, (in case of calamity) the additional anxiety as to the support of one's family. ¶ potᵘ lab f. the back wall of a house or the like (K.Pr. 139); the back side of a range of mountains or the like. --lã̄j -- m. the last calamity, (when one is about to start on a necessary business for some far country) the final anxiety caused by the necessity of providing for one's family during one's absence. --lākh -- f. (sg. dat. lāki), (in piling up, load by load) the final load to complete the pile; cf. patau-lākan, p. 785a, l. 14. --lām -- f. the final attack (esp. on unsuspecting foes); met. at the end of a long journey, the final attack on (i.e. climb up) a difficult mountain pass. --lār -- f. the final running, i.e. the final pursuit of a defeated army; the final rout of a defeated army. --lās -- m. secret gain; ultimate gain (in any transaction); (in some transaction likely to cause loss) great ultimate gain. --lāṭh -- m. (sg. dat. -lāṭas), a final twist (e.g. the last twisted part of a turban); met. (near the completion of some work on which mutually all have agreed) treachery by one of the partners. ¶ potᵘ mahārāza m. the secondary bridegroom, i.e. at a marriage, the younger brother (usually a boy) of the bridegroom, who accompanies him and is dressed in fine clothes like him, the best man (L. 261, Śiv. 967). --nakh -- m. (sg. dat. --nakhas --), the back-shoulder, i.e. carrying a load on the back of the shoulder. --nāl 1 -- m. the back part of the collar of a garment. --nāl 2 -- m. the hind shoe of a horse or the like. --nam -- m. the part of a boat behind the prow; the hinder part of a boat (K.Pr. 76, puth nam). --nĕnd -- f. (sg. dat. --nĕndi --), the third, or final, weeding of a rice-field. --nērun -- m.inf. to go back, return, retreat; cf. --drāmotᵘ, ab. --nāv -- m. a name subsequently given, a nickname, a title, a nom de guerre, a nom de plume. ¶ potᵘ pachīr f. the rear tethering rope of a horse, elephant, or the like. --pachörⁱ -- f., id. --pachārĕ diñĕ -- f.pl.inf. to apply such tethering ropes; met. to keep (a wife, a child, a servant, or the like) at home, not to allow her or him to go out of the house. --phikir -- f. subsequent distress of mind; hidden distress of mind. --phal -- m. the final crop, the last crop to ripen; the final result of any action; the consequent result of any action (good or bad). --phērun -- m.inf. to turn round backwards; to desist from any work; to go back again, to go away after having paid a visit (H. xii, 19). --phirun -- m.inf. to turn (some one) back, as ab. --phīrith -- conj. part. as adv., again (El.); back again, in reply (with vbs. of saying) (H. x, 3, 6, 7); back again (with vbs. of motion) (K.Pr. 125). --phīrith gaʦhun -- m.inf. to return, retreat (El.). --phirawun -- m.inf., i.q. --phirun, q.v. --phirawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --phiravüñᵘ̈ --), one who causes to turn back, as ab. --phyurᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --phirᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), turned back (by some one) (from going in any direction, from a work, etc.). --phyūrᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (phīrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), one who has turned back; one who has desisted from any work. --palav -- m. the back part of a garment. --pilav -- m. a balcony in the rear of a house. --pīn -- m. the last birth, the last time a woman has a child (e.g. owing to her old age, or the like); cf. --pyūnukᵘ, bel. --pōr -- m. the rear or back of anything. --puran -- f. (sg. dat. --purüñᵘ̈ --), the piece of ground behind a house. --pāsa -- m. the rear or back of anything. --pash -- m. the rear thatch of a house. --potᵘ -- adv. privately, out of sight, secretly, behind a person's back (K.Pr. 174, put put). --pav -- m. the final navigable channel, i.e. the achievement of profit after passing through a series of losses. --pyūnukᵘ -- adj. (f. --pīnücᵘ̈ --), a last born child (i.e. one whose parents cannot expect to have any more, owing to old age, etc.); cf. --pīn, ab. ¶ potᵘ röchⁱ f. arrangements for guarding (one's house, etc.) in one's absence. --rikan -- f. (sg. dat. riküñᵘ̈), a slip backwards (e.g. in walking on greasy ground); met. a secret obstruction to success. --rikiñ -- f., id. --rĕl -- f. the rear or back strip of several narrow strips (of cloth, land, etc.). --rama -- or --ramb -- m. (of a horse) kicking backwards with the hind legs; backing (in a jib). --rĕma -- f.pl. subsequent anxiety of the mind (e.g. after having left home, anxiety regarding the family left behind). --rān -- f. the thigh of the hind leg (of a horse, a sheep, or the like). --roṭᵘ -- m. stopping from behind. --raṭh 1 -- f. (sg. dat. --raṭi --), id. --raṭh 2 -- f. (sg. dat. --raṭi --), (when thread is given to a weaver for being turned into cloth) a subsequent supply of thread of equal weight (supplied to make the cloth stronger). --rāth -- f. (sg. dat. --röʦᵘ̈ --), the latter part of the night. --raṭun -- m.inf. to hold back, restrain (K. 897). --rav -- m. running backwards. --ray -- m. sterility of a crop (i.e. when a grain-crop has grown to ripeness, the ears to be empty). ¶ potᵘ sab f. the back row at a meeting, a dinner-party, or the like. --sād -- m. a subsequent taste, the final taste of something eaten; counter-tasting (i.e. after taking something nasty, eating something nice to take away the taste). --shĕholᵘ -- or --shiholᵘ -- m. the cool (i.e. shade) of the afternoon. --shāph -- m. (sg. dat. --shāpas --), a curse incurred in some former life (resulting in misfortunes in the present life). --shophᵘ -- m. heirship, inheritance. --sörᵘ̈ -- f. stealthy carrying off in instalments from a collection of articles (e.g. grain from some one else's pile, or money from some one else's store). --sath -- f. (sg. dat. --süʦᵘ̈ --), hope or faith in help in one's absence (e.g. to one's people when one is away from home); subsequent hope, hope or faith in help arising subsequently. --sāth -- m. (sg. dat. --sātas --), the last moment (e.g. in a period fixed astrologically); the final time (e.g. of the day, i.e. the afternoon). --sāyĕ -- m. the shadow (e.g. of a tree) that falls behind (in the afternoon); help given by one behind (e.g. an elder brother, friend, or the like). ¶ potᵘ ṭhil kaḍüñᵘ̈ f.inf. 'to strike (the ball) back again'; hence, in a game or fight, when nearly beaten to turn upon the opponent and beat him. --tākh -- m. (sg. dat. --tākas --), an upper-story window in the back of a house. --tam -- m. 'the final weariness', i.e. (on a journey) the last rest taken on the way before arriving at the destination for the night; taking one's rest (in old age) after working all one's life. --tan -- f. (sg. dat. --tani --), the back part of the body. --ṭās -- m. a loud bang or crash from behind or occurring behind. ¶ potᵘ ʦhaṭh f. (sg. dat. --ʦhaṭi --), the final shaking out of grain in a sieve or the like (in order to clear off the chaff, etc.); calling to a person by name behind his back after he has started on a journey. --ʦhaṭh diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to call out by name to a person who has started on a journey (in order to create a bad omen). --ʦhāy -- f. a shadow behind a person; recognizing a person going along by his appearance from behind (Śiv. 896, 1133, 1479; Rām. 212). --ʦakh -- f. (sg. dat. --ʦakhi --), secret anger, anger behind the object's back. --ʦam -- f. the skin of the back. --ʦônᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. ʦöñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made to turn back, repelled; (of some business) ceased from, abandoned; cf. pȧtⁱ ʦônᵘ-motᵘ, bel. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause to turn back, repel; (of some business) to cause (work) back, to cease from (it), to abandon (it); ʦānun, bel. --ʦôrᵘ -- m. the back one of the three openings of a cooking range; cf. --büṭhᵘ̈, ab. --ʦūr -- m. one who steals in a person's absence, one who takes advantage of a person's absence to commit theft (e.g. when done by servants). --ʦūrᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. theft of things kept in the house or in a chest (esp. when committed by a member of the household) to occur. --ʦarʦun -- m.inf. to investigate privily, to prosecute private inquiries (regarding a person), to criticize a person (behind his back). ¶ potᵘ vih m. a sudden change of condition at the last moment (e.g. of an invalid's health, of a burning candle, of some crop of fruit ripening, or of some current business). --vil -- f. the last moment (for doing anything). --wān -- m. a shop behind, or in the rear; the final work in any action, the finishing touches. --wôñᵘ -- m. the last juice (i.e. in expressing any juice, that which comes last); the latter water (i.e. in boiling food, when most of the liquid is boiled away, the water or other liquid which is added afterwards). --wörᵘ̈ -- f. a back garden, a garden in of a house. --wath -- f. (sg. dat. --wati --), a back way, a way out (of a house, etc.) behind. --waʦa phērañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to be struck senseless by terror; to be made almost senseless by shame when reproved for some fault. ¶ potᵘ yunᵘ m.inf. to come back, return (H. v, 1). --zūn -- f. the end of the moonlight, the last hours of the night (L.V. 105). --zang 1 -- f. the back part of the shank, the calf of the leg. --zang 2 -- f. (on starting on a journey) an omen to occur behind one, or immediately after one has started. --zīrᵘ̈ -- f. a shove from behind (e.g. in pushing a boat off the shore); stimulating a person to further efforts; stimulating an angry person by abuse and the like behind his back. --zĕv -- f. the back part or root of the tongue. --zĕv gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the tongue to become fixed, to become dumb (e.g. when one makes a false charge, and is asked for proof, to remain silent). ¶ pȧtⁱ adv. and postpos. (governing either the case of the agent or the ablative) behind, at the back of (cf. kȧnⁱ-pⁱ, p. 448a, l. 23; kāri-pᵒ, p. 467a, ll. 26, 29) (Gr.Gr. 154; Gr.M.; Śiv. 115, 1609, patiy); after (in time) (cf. kāji-pᵒ, p. 430a, l. 5) (K. 241, K.Pr. 210). --āmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), having turned back (from), having given up doing (some work); see --yunᵘ, bel. --aʦun -- m.inf. to turn back, to give up doing (something), to abandon (one's caste or the like). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to propel (a boat) backwards; cf. potᵘ dyunᵘ, ab. --gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), (of something begun or some business) turned back, abstained from; (of burning coal or a brazier) gone out, gone cold. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go into the rear, be abstained from; (of burning coal or a brazier) to go out, go cold (K.Pr. 11). --khūrⁱ -- adv. immediately, very speedily (K. 814); cf. potᵘ khōrĕn, ab. --kinⁱ -- adv. from behind (Gr.Gr. 158); behind, behind (a person's back) (K. 162, 208); afterwards, in the meantime (K. 604); privately, secretly (K. 1149). --körᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to feel disgraced, to lower oneself by having to take to shameful work; cf. potᵘ körᵘ̈ gᵒ, ab. --korᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --kürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), (of something begun or some business) turned back (by somebody), put in the rear, abstained from; (of burning coal or a brazier) put out, made cold. --karun -- m.inf. to turn back, put behind, put in the rear (some busy person or some work); to put out, make cold (burning coal or a brazier). --pȧtⁱ brū̃ṭhⁱbrū̃ṭhⁱ -- adv. behind and behind and before and before, at one time behind and at another time before (K. 941). --ta brū̃ṭhⁱ wuchun -- m.inf. to look behind and before, to look at with affection. --ṭhorᵘ -- m. a cover behind, a hindrance or impediment which follows a person (immediately on his beginning something). --ʦāmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --ʦāmüʦᵘ̈ --), turned back (from some business or some work on which one is engaged). --ʦônᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --ʦöñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), (of some person) caused to turn back (from some business, etc., as ab.); (of some business) caused to be put in the rear, caused to be abandoned; cf. potᵘ ʦônᵘ-motᵘ, ab. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause (a person) to turn back (from some business, etc., as ab.); to cause (some business) to be put in the rear, to cause to be abandoned, to prevent (Gr.M.); cf. potᵘ ʦānun. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to turn back (from some business), to give up (what one is doing); to go back, dry up (of a well) (YZ. 406).

m. (sg. ag. pöṭⁱ 1), silk (the filament) (for particulars of the silk produced in Kashmīr, see El. s.v. póṭ) (L. 464); silk cloth (Gr.M., Rām. 1758); used met. for any fine thread-like substance in compounds such as kukili- pôṭᵘ, 'cuckoo's silk,' a kind of grass (p. 433a, l. 27) (Śiv. 1808). ¶ pöṭⁱ-dāv f. a piece of silk thread (a yard or so long), a needle-full of silk thread. -dôwᵘ m. silk thread (for embroidery or the like). -garī f. the profession of working in silk braid (e.g. for making necklaces or the like). -gorᵘ m. a maker of silk braid or thread (for necklaces or the like). -gȧrⁱ-bāy f. his wife. -gö̆ʦᵘ̈ f. the silk-cocoon (El. pãt-guts). -kyomᵘ m. the silkworm (El. pãṭ-kyum, L. 464). -pana-dāv f., i.q. -dāv, ab. (El. pãṭ-pandáo, m. silk thread). -poʦhᵘ m. a silk fringe (on a garment or the like). -thān m. silk-cloth in the piece, silk cloth (El.). ¶ pāṭyukᵘ sg. gen. (f. pāṭicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, silk.

m. a flat board (of wood), a plank, a sheet (of glass, tin, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 34, W. 17); a leaf (of a door, window-shutter, lattice, or the like) (cf. bar-pᵒ, p. 116b, l. 28; dāri-pᵒ, p. 238b, l. 16; darwāza-pᵒ, p. 250b, l. 39; lŏka-tȧrⁱ-pⁱ, p. 517a, l. 42; panjara-pᵒ, p. 741a, l. 1); the flat portion of anything (e.g. the sole of a shoe; cf. paizār- pȧṭⁱ karȧnⁱ, s.v. paizār). pȧṭⁱ-sand f. (sg. dat. -sünzᵘ̈), studying a subject by ear (and not by reading books).

m. woollen cloth, 'puttoo' (cf. bŏṭa-pᵒ, p. 138b, l. 30; rā̃gȧrⁱ-pⁱ, s.v. rā̃gȧrⁱ). For the various kinds of this cloth, see El. s.v. paṭṭú (Gr.Gr. 42, 57, 162; L. 370, 390, pattu, 462, put; W. 155, paṭṭu; Śiv. 1566; K.Pr. 31, 127, 174, 184, puṭṭu). --manḍan-wôlᵘ -- n.ag. a cleaner of puttoo (El.). This cloth is washed by trampling it under the feet in water. Cf. manḍun. ¶ pȧṭⁱ-chal f. a piece of woollen cloth. -jŏrāba m. a stocking of this cloth. -kurta m. a piece of such cloth sufficient for making a coat. -paijāma m. drawers made of such cloth. -thān m. a length of such cloth, woollen cloth in the piece. -tᵃr f. a narrow strip of woollen cloth (Gr.Gr. 162). -ʦādar f. a wrapper-sheet ('chudder') of such cloth. -wān m. a shop where such cloth is sold; a machine for stretching such cloth. -wôñᵘ m. a seller of such cloth. -wôwurᵘ m. a weaver of such cloth. ¶ -paṭyukᵘ adj. (f. -paṭicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, woollen cloth (Gr.Gr. 57); made of such cloth.
f. (f. of pŏtulᵘ, q.v.), a puppet, a child's doll; an image, an idol.

in the following:-- pöṭⁱ marüñᵘ̈ f.inf. the object (of any action) to be obtained (esp. when dishonestly). --mārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take away (another's property) or undo the result (of another's action) and abscond privately (esp. when done dishonestly).
f. a small silver coin, worth two or four annas or thereabouts.
f.pl. the ribs (of man or beast). --kaḍañe -- f. pl. inf. 'to tear out the ribs', to trounce or club a person unmercifully (esp. in the region of the ribs).

m. a single step in a staircase, flight of steps, or the like (cf. hēra-pᵒ, p. 345b, l. 8; sām-pᵒ, s.v. sām 1) (Śiv. 61; K.Pr. 154). ¶ pāvi, sg. abl. used as adv., on or from a (high) step on a staircase; met. in a position relatively higher than someone or something else, exalted (cf. bahali-pᵒ, p. 95b, l. 32). --khasun -- m.inf. to climb on to a (high) step, to become exalted above one's fellows. --pāvi wālun -- m.inf. to bring down (the staircase) step by step; to knock down (a house or the like) gradually from the top downwards; gradually to reduce a man (or something masculine) to misery, gradually to depress. --pāvi wālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf., id., but with a fem. object. --wālun -- m.inf. to bring down a person from an exalted position. --wasun -- m.inf. to descend from (a high) step, to be brought down from an exalted position; to be reduced from prosperity or happiness to misery, to become depressed. ¶ pövⁱ-hēr f. a step-ladder.
m. the staple to which the last link of the chain of a door is applied before applying the padlock, a padlock-staple (cf. hö̃kāli-pᵒ, p. 328b, l. 4); the eye (of a needle) (K.Pr. 190).

adj. (f. pövᵘ̈), measuring a quarter (of anything); weighing a quarter of a sēr (i.e. weighing half a pound) (cf. ḍāy-pᵒ, p. 266b, l. 25; pönʦa-pᵒ, p. 743a, l. 32); measuring a span (of twelve finger breadths) (cf. ḍāy-pᵒ, p. 266b, l. 22); as subst., m. N. of a certain-sized jar (cf. kānz-pᵒ, p. 460a, l. 3; sọ̆dra-könzᵘ̈-pᵘ̈, s.v. sọ̆dᵃr) (K.Pr. 26). Cf. pāv 3.

f.pl. the powdered chaff and other refuse which remains when husking rice in a mortar. -ôṭᵘ m. a flour made of this refuse, this refuse used as flour. --hĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to clear the husked rice from this refuse. --khĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to eat such refuse; met. to become discouraged (by the prospect of some difficult work). -pholᵘ m. a quantity of this powdered refuse.
adj. c.g. mixed up with, or full of, pounded chaff, etc. (of rice, etc., pounded in a husking mortar). See pŏyĕ.
adj. c.g. full of, or mixed up with, powdered chaff, etc. (cf. pŏyĕ).
f. a bamboo ladder; the cross-beam supporting a roof.
f. an anklet of gold or silver. pöyili-horᵘ m. a pair of anklets. -khōr m. a single anklet.
or pözᵘ̈ 1 m. (sg. dat. pözᵘ̈s, Rām. 93), a falcon, a hawk (W. 114, pāz; Rām. 93; K. 947; H. vi, 16; viii, 7; K.Pr. 65, 161, 167, 199). -wôlᵘ m. a falconer.

adj. (f. püzᵘ̈), true, truthful, veracious, honest (Gr.Gr. 141; Gr.M.; Rām. 827, 1629); true, not false (Gr.M.; L. 464; Śiv. 1211, 1907; Rām. 334, 428, 1108a; H. x, 6, 8); real, true, genuine, not imitation (Gr.M., Śiv. 923); true, correct (Gr.M.; Rām. 1063, 1238, 1687); as subst. truth, the true state of affairs (Gr.Gr. 135; Gr.M.; Śiv. 419, 765; Rām. 34, 51, 134, 238, 268, 364, etc.; K. 175; YZ. 136; K.Pr. 175, 257); as adv. of a truth, verily (Rām. 1243, 1318). --apozᵘ -- adj. (f. püzᵘ̈ apüzᵘ̈), true and false, a mixture of truth and falsehood; a romance founded on fact (cf. apozᵘ-pᵘ, p. 40a, l. 43) (Śiv. 419, 765). --bāpār -- m. true conduct, honest conduct, truthfulness. --karun -- m.inf. to make true, to keep, fulfil, carry out (a promise or the like) (K. 37, 628, 722). --mānun -- m.inf. to accept as true, believe, credit (Gr.M.). --pozᵘ -- adj. (f. püzᵘ̈ püzᵘ̈), true in every particular (K. 1057). ¶ pȧzⁱ-kinⁱ adv. of a truth verily, in truth (Rām. 843, 1149). --pöṭhⁱ -- adv. truthfully, verily, in truth (El., YZ. 237); assuredly, certainly, without doubt (Gr.M.; H. x, 6, 10). ¶ pazi apazi adv. (with verbs of answering and the like), is a mixture of truth and falsehood; partly admitting and partly denying. --pazi -- adv. truthfully in every particular, exactly, really (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1818). --pozᵘ -- adj. (f. --püzᵘ̈ --), entirely true, the whole truth.
or pọ̆zᵘ conjnct. but, nevertheless (cf. amā pozᵘ, p. 27a, l. 2) (Gr.M.). --akh cīzāh -- adv. 'but one thing', but, nevertheless, still, but on the other hand.
f. taking out, extraction, in atha-pözᵘ̈, p. 62a, l. 7. Cf. pāzun.

m. a porcupine (so translated by Paṇḍits, equating it not only with Skt. śvāvit, but also with Hindī sāhī. It is believed to follow a lion, and to indicate its presence by a low growl); a fox (El. potsalo). Cf. lōh and phĕ˜w.
m. the stumpy tail of a sheep, goat, or the like. Cf. pọ̆ʦhᵘ 1 and the next.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pöʦhᵃrôwᵃ), to cause to come into existence (cf. pāthanāwun, which like pöʦhᵃrāwun is the causal of pāthun, q.v. The form pöʦhᵃrāwun is, however, unusual, Gr.Gr. 173).

or poʦhᵘ 1 or puʦhᵘ m. (sg. abl. paʦhi, see also paʦh) the tail (of a beast or bird); the fringed edge or end of a shawl, turban, or the like (cf. dastār-pọ̆ʦhᵘ, p. 256b, l. 28; lō̃gi-poʦhᵘ, p. 512a, l. 6; pöṭⁱ-pⁱ, p. 790a, l. 12; pŏʦhurᵘ and pŏʦhᵘ̈rᵘ̈); used --˚ as a kind of diminutive to indicate something short and stumpy. In this use it is sometimes spelt puchᵘ (cf. shrāka-puʦhᵘ, a penknife, compared with shrākh (q.v.), a large knife).

m. the phĕran (q.v.), or long nightgown-like garment worn by Kāshmīrīs, when made of cotton cloth is called pôʦhᵘ. When made of woollen stuff, it is called lôchᵘ, q.v. Sometimes a pôʦhᵘ is worn, like a shift, next the skin, with a lôchᵘ over it (cf. marda-pᵒ, p. 589b, l. 33) (K.Pr. 42, 180, 181). ¶ pöʦhⁱ-dĕlur m. 'a bit of bark of a shift', an old worn out pôʦhᵘ, too small for the wearer. -züṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -zacĕ), a ragged pôʦhᵘ.

or poʦhᵘ 2 m. (sg. abl. paʦhi, see also paʦh), a guest (cf. görⁱ-pọ̆ʦhⁱ, p. 298a, l. 43) (El. pauts; L. 460, puts; Śiv. 1837). --lọ̆ʦhᵘ -- m. guests and the like, i.e. guests and other persons who deserve similar honour. ¶ pȧʦhⁱ-bāy f. a female guest, a lady guest. pȧʦhⁱ-pūzā f. the honour paid to a guest, the welcome given to a guest.

adj. scared, easily frightened, used in the following:-- --bukurᵘ -- adj. a scared face, one who owing to his laziness and stupidity in work is an object of frequent scolding, etc.; one who is full of timidity (e.g. one who is scared merely when addressed in a loud voice). ¶ pöʦhⁱ-bukurⁱ m., i.q. pôʦhᵘ- bukurᵘ, ab. -buthᵘ m., id.
m. foam, froth (cf. añema-pᵒ, p. 37b, l. 12).
f. the long tail of a cow, horse, lion, or the like. Cf. pọ̆ʦhᵘ 1, and the preceding.
m. trust, confidence, i.q. paʦh, q.v., used --˚ as in māla-pᵒ, p. 565a, l. 20; mana-pᵒ, p. 572a, l. 35.

m. one who wears his clothes on the wrong parts of the body (e.g. wearing a shoulder-cloth on his head and so on), or who, wearing them in the right situations, puts them on wrongly, a sloven. Cf. probᵘ 1.

m. (sg. dat. prabātas), the early dawn (technically, a hour before sunrise), sunrise, day-break (according to El. morning from sunrise to nine o'clock) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 352, 1333, 1358, 1413, 1465, 1542, 1549, 1641, 1702; Rām. 1109; K. 79, 782; K.Pr. 176 prabhát). ¶ prabötⁱ adv. at dawn, in the early morning (K. 270, 801). ¶ prabātan or prabātas adv. during the dawntide, at dawn, early in the morning (cf. prath prabātan, prath prabātas, s.v. prath) (prabātan, Śiv. 163; Rām. 143, 575, 585, 884, 1264-5, 1640; prabātas, Śiv. 1009, 1883; Rām. 73, 622). prabātan (or prabātas) bögⁱ (or bögin)   adv. at about dawn.
f. (of dress) slovenliness, unkemptness, wearing the wrong clothes on the wrong parts of the body or the right clothes wrongly put on.

or pradĕkhĕn m. circumambulation, so that the right side is always presented towards the object circumambulated, a reverential salutation performed by such circumambulation (Śiv. 322, 1136, 1161, 1221, 1505, 1622).
adj. c.g. chief, principal, preeminent, main, best, most eminent (Śiv. 1659, 1768); (as subst.) a chief person, a person of eminence (K. 24).
m. evening, nightfall, the first part of the night (Śiv. 1724).
m. N. of a son of Kṛṣṇa, in Skt. Pradyumna (K. 734, 736, 739, 745, 746, 789, 820).
m. moonshine (El. prágásh); met. beauty like that of the moon (YZ. 376).
f. (sg. dat. prahi), love, affection, adoring love (L.V. 83, 105).

m. possession by a demon (believed to cause fainting, madness, fury, fever, etc.) (cf. dŏda-pᵒ, p. 190a, l. 2). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. fury (as if due to possession by a demon) to arise (Rām. 1383). --karun -- m.inf. to enrage, fill with fury, cause delusion (from opposition, terror, seeing a ghost) (as though possessed by a demon). --pö̃than -- m. possession by a demon (inducing fever, delusion, miscarriage) of a baby or of a pregnant woman passing haunted places by night. ¶ prāha-hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), possessed by a demon, as ab. -vyotᵘ भूतावेशव्याप्तः adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), full of demoniacal possession. -zīrᵘ̈ f. 'a demoniacal shove', conduct like that of one who is possessed by a demon, raging furious conduct (of one who is sane). -zīrᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. demoniacal possession to occur; raging fury (like the conduct of one so possessed) to arise.
adj. (as subst., f. prāhaladiñ), one who is afflicted by demoniacal possession.

m. N. of a celebrated prince, the son of the demon (daitya) Hiraṇyakaśipu. He was devoted to the god Viṣṇu, and when persecuted by his father was rescued by that deity under the form of the Man-lion incarnation (Śiv. 446, 857, 1593; K. 828-9).

m. fashion, manner, mode, kind, description (Gr.M., Śiv. 1577, K. 12); species (El.). ¶ prakāra adv. in (such-and-such) a manner (cf. ami pᵒ, p. 54b, l. 48; amiy pᵒ, p. 55a, l. 48) (Śiv. 955). ¶ prakörⁱ adv. in (such-and-such) a manner (cf. ami pᵒ, p. 54b, l. 49; amiy pᵒ, p. 55a, l. 49) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1050, K. 200); with the genitive of a personal or similar pronoun, it indicates cause, as in myönⁱ pᵒ, because of me, on account of me.
m. in Śiv. 1018 translated in the comm. by antaḥsthiti or 'inmost position', but the word may also be looked upon as the equivalent of prākāra, q.v.

m. the building of the upper stories of a house. --karun -- m.inf. the ground floor walls, etc., of a house to settle (evenly) in consequence of the weight of the upper stories. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf., id., but the settlement is uneven.
m. the four outer walls of a house from ground to roof.
m. an introduction, preface (of a book or the like).

m. light, lustre, splendour, glory, brightness, sunshine, ray (cf. nitra-pᵒ, p. 662b, l. 13) (L.V. 4, 6, 9, 35, 82; K.Pr. 201; Śiv. 108, 157, 226, 249, 347, 657, 1660, etc.; Rām. 59, 219, 295, 679, 1043, etc.; K.Pr. 201).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. prakaṭôwᵘ), to make evident, make known, to bring to light, divulge, disclose. prakaṭôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. pass. (1 p.p. prakaṭövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made known, divulged, etc., as ab.

adj. c.g. clear, visible, manifest, evident (Śiv. 991, 1275; Rām. 1642, 1688, 1705, 1710); vivid, perspicuous; i.q. prạkhᵒṭᵒ, q.v. prakȧṭⁱ-pöṭhⁱ or -pöṭhin adv. manifestly, clearly, visibly, openly, without disguise.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. prakaṭyōv. According to others this verb is of the 2nd conj., with a 1 p.p. prakoṭᵘ), to be or become manifest, appear, become visible; i.q. prạkhᵃṭun. prakoṭᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. praküṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), become manifest, that which has become exposed to view. prakaṭyō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. prakaṭyē-müʦᵘ̈), id.
adj. (f. prakhyöpᵘ̈), renowned, famous, celebrated, notorious, well-known (Gr.M.).
or prạkhᵃcār m. perceptibility, ocular proof (Rām. 61, K. 45); explicitness; standing face to face.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. prạkhᵃṭôwᵃ), to make evident, make known, to bring to light, divulge, disclose, manifest (K. 449). prạkhᵃṭôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. prạkhᵃṭövᵃ-müʦᵃ), made known, divulged, etc., as ab.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. prạkhᵃṭyōv), to be or become manifest, appear, become visible, i.q. prakaṭun, q.v. prạkhᵃṭyō-motᵃ perf. part. (f. prạkhᵃṭyē-müʦᵃ), become manifest, that which has become exposed to view.

or prakhoṭᵘ adj. (f. prakhᵘ̈ṭᵘ̈), clear, visible, manifest, evident (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1402; Rām. 308, 940; K. 122, 128, 777); vivid, perspicuous; (as adv.) manifestly, visibly (K. 1112, 1165), i.q. prakaṭh, q.v. prạkhᵃ̇ṭᵃ̇- pöṭhⁱ or -pöṭhin adv. manifestly, clearly, visibly, openly, without disguise.
m. circumambulation, so that the right side is always presented to the object circumambulated, i.q. pradakhĕn, q.v.

or prakrĕth f. (sg. dat. prakrüʦᵘ̈, often written), (of a human being or the like) temperament, nature, constitution, health (Gr.M.; L.V. 57; Śiv. 932, 1013, 1056, 1350, 1483, 1551, etc.; Rām. 366, 943); (in Śaiva philosophy) primal matter (Skt. prakṛtiḥ) as opposed to spirit, primitive non-intelligent being (L.V. 25); ignorance, want of true knowledge (Rām. 40); the personified energic power of the Supreme, His Māyā or illusive power (Śiv. 27); cf. prakrĕti. prakrüʦᵘ̈-hondᵘ̈ sg. gen. (f. prakrüʦᵘ̈-hünzᵘ̈), of (so-and-so's) nature, bearing the same nature (as so-and-so, gen.) (Śiv. 1425).
f. the Skt. form of prakrath, q.v. -par adj. c.g. devoted to (the true knowledge of) primal matter, one who is able to distinguish between primal matter and the Supreme Deity (Śiv. 20).

for prālabd in the following:-- prālab phērun m.inf. one's fate to change, i.e. to find oneself, after long residence in one country, under the necessity of migrating to another. --wŏthun -- m.inf. one's fated hour to arise (e.g. to be at the point of death, to fall from high office, to be compelled to leave one's home, or the like). ¶ prālaba-boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), one whose fate is very great, a very fortunate person (endowed with wealth and success). -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a lucky person (endowed with wealth, virtue, health, honour, happiness, success, etc.). ¶ prālabukᵘ sg. gen. (f. prālabücᵘ̈), of, belonging to, connected with, or the result of, one's fate.
or prālab (q.v.) m. a person's fate in this life (the result of actions in former lives) (El. prálabad). Cf. prārabd.
m. N. of a certain demon, in Skt. Pralamba (K. 251).

m. dissolution, destruction, annihilation (Rām. 1235); the destruction of the whole universe at the end of an age (Śiv. 203, 854); general destruction, any extensive devastation (Rām. 1601, K. 909). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. utter destruction (e.g. in one moment, of one's entire possessions and family) to occur. ¶ pralayĕ-kāl m. a time of general destruction (e.g. the time of a devastating conflagration, inundation, or the like).
m. a rule, sanction, standard, authority, judgment, opinion (either general or of a single person); proof, proof or arguments brought forward in a law case (Gr.M.).

m. (sg. abl. prāna 1), the breath of life, the breath (as inspired into and expired from the lungs) (Gr.Gr. 162; Śiv. 42, 984, 1014, 1059, 1156, 1591; K. 168, 195; K.Pr. 187); the life, the living principle (of a person) (Gr.M.; L.V. 89, 90; Śiv. 49, 164, 237, 312, 435, 452, 473, 520, 776, etc.; K. 505); (in pl.) (in Śaiva philosophy) the five vital airs of the body, which it is necessary to keep under control. These five are called in Skt. (1) prâṇa, or air exhaled from the lungs through the mouth and nose, (2) apâna, the downward flowing air expelled through the anus (cf. Śiv. 1027, 1682), (3) udāna, that which rises from the throat and enters the head, (4) samāna, that which has its seat in the cavity of the navel, and is essential to digestion, and (5) vyāna, that which is diffused through the whole body (L.V. 101; Śiv. 306, 516, 597, 1082, 1291, 1437, 1513, 1547, etc.; Rām. 3, 19, 1468). --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. 'to give breaths', to bring to life, to restore to life (met. and fig.). --diwawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --diwavüñᵘ̈ --), that which brings a dying person to life, a revivifying (medicine, act, speech, etc.); one who is giving (up) his breath, one who is at the point of death; (as adv.) (done, spoken, etc.) in a person's last moments, when at the point of death. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to yield one's death, to expire, to breathe one's last, to die. --gālun -- m.inf. to destroy (so-and-so's) life, to slay (Rām. 1486). --hĕnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to gasp (from extreme pain); to take another's breaths, i.e. to beat him till he is like one dead. --harun -- m.inf. to abandon one's life, to lose one's life, to die (Rām. 624, 1182). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take another's life, to kill, slay (Rām. 1238). --kaḍȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to tear out (a person's) breaths, to slay violently (K. 68, 110, 225, 1026). --kaḍun -- m.inf., id. (K. 254, 820). --khē̃cȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to draw breaths (with difficulty), to gasp (when suffering from severe pain, or when at the point of death), to emit the death rattle. --khasun -- m.inf. 'the vital breath to rise', to be at the point of death, to be near death. --nērun -- m.inf. the vital breath to go forth, the point of death to approach, to expire, to feel at one's last gasp (from terror or the like) (Rām. 550, 1333, 1339, 1427; K. 450). --sandārȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the breaths to be resuscitated, to be revived (esp. by some small remedy) (cf. Śiv. 1048, 1753); cf. prāna- sandār, -sandāran, bel. --ṭhīkȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the breaths to stand firmly, (of a person suffering from a dangerous disease, or suddenly brought near to death) to be suddenly revived and brought to perfect health. ¶ prāna-danḍ m. a breath rod, an impalement post, or other rod for executing an offender (as a judicial punishment). -dāran f. (sg. dat. -dārüñᵘ̈), coming to life (of a sick person recovering, or a starving person relieved by a little food). -ganḍa-ganḍ m. nothing left but breath, the condition of one who is so lean as to be hardly alive. -lᵃth f.
