(sg. dat. -lᵃti), a mere breath, a spark of life (Gr.Gr. 162). -sandār m. resuscitation of breath, the coming to life of a sick, starving, or thirst-parched person (by receiving suitable medicine, food, or drink); cf. prān sandārȧnⁱ, ab. -sandāran m., id. -wövᵘ̈ f. difficulty of breathing.

m. (sg. abl. prāna 2), an onion, Allium sp. (cf. baḍa-pᵒ, p. 82b, l. 27; ganḍa-pᵒ, p. 239b, l. 18) (L. 72, 75, 346, 462; L.V. 89, 90, 101; YZ. 121). According to El. it is not eaten by Hindūs of the Valley. ¶ prāna-bagāra m. fried onions (as a seasoning). -bazyunᵘ m. cooking some dish with fried onions. -dĕl m. onion-skin, the peel of an onion, or of its stem. -gab m. an onion-sprout. -gŏgᵃ̇jᵃ̇ or -gŏgᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. an onion bulb, an onion. -khāv m. an onion eater, one who habitually eats quantities of onions. -kujⁱ or -kujᵘ̈ f. the onion plant (K.Pr. 8, 27). -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -mŏnjĕ), an onion bulb, an onion. -mushᵉ̆kh m. (sg. dat. -mushkas), the smell of an onion. -phakh m. (sg. dat. -phakas), the stink of an onion.
m. bending, bowing; a bow, a respectful or reverential salutation, prostration, obeisance (cf. pādi-pᵒ, p. 681a, l. 15) (Śiv. 860, 986, 1141, 1168, 1170).
m. the name of the mystical or sacred syllable Ōṁ (L.V. 76; Śiv. 1556, 1594, 1751, 1760).

m. confidence, intimacy; fond regard, affection, love (Śiv. 1342); (in Kāshmīrī) refinement, gentlemanly bearing, modesty, affability, courtesy. ¶ pranayĕ-vĕʦar m. thorough refinement, etc. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), thoroughly refined, gentlemanly, modest, affable, courteous.
m. restraining or suspending the breath, or breathing in a peculiar way through the nostrils, during the mental recitation of the names and attributes of some deity.

m. whiteness; cleanness, pureness; clearness, freedom from turbidity. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. whiteness or cleanness to come into existence (e.g. a coloured article fading into white, or a dirty article being washed white). --phērun -- m.inf., id. (as a change from some other colour, or from dirt). --phirun -- m.inf. to whiten, bleach, make white or clean (from some other colour or from dirt); to become white or clean (as ab.).
m. oldness, worn-outness (Gr.Gr. 141); antiquity, the belonging to olden time.

m. a couch, a seat, throne (cf. pōshĕ-pᵒ, s.v. pōsh 1) (Gr.M.; Rām. 1147, 1713; K. 339, 924, 936, 1047, 1130; H. xii, 18); a bed (K.Pr. 154); the finial of a shrine (L. 460); cf. paryö̃kh. pranga-khūrᵘ m. the leg of a bedstead.
f. edge, margin, border, end, extremity (cf. ȧchⁱ-pⁱ, p. 8b, l. 25).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. pranyōv), to be or become white; to become white, to become clean (of something washed); to become clear, to lose turbidity; to flow (El.). pranyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pranyē-müʦᵘ̈), become white; become clean, clear.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. prānyōv), to be, or become, old, become worn out (Rām. 994). prānyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. prānyē-müʦᵘ̈), become old; worn out.
f. (sg. dat. prạñᵉ̆rüñᵉ̆), whitening, cleansing, the process of making white or clean; making clear, removing turbidity.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. prạñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), to make white, whiten; to clean (by washing, etc.); to make clear, remove turbidity; cf. prạñᵉ̆run. prạñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. prạñᵉ̆rövᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), whitened, cleaned, cleared.
n.ag. (prạñᵉ̆ravüñᵉ̆), one who whitens or cleans, a whitener, a cleaner, a fuller.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. prạñᵒrᵒ), to make white, whiten; to make clean, to cleanse (by washing, etc.); to make clear, remove turbidity; cf. prạñᵉ̆rāwun.prạñᵉ̆rᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. prạñᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), whitened, cleansed, cleared.
m. (sg. dat. prapanʦas), development, diffusion, amplification, expansion (Śiv. 1728); prolixity, diffuseness, copiousness (in style or composition).

f. (sg. dat. prāpüʦᵘ̈), obtaining, acquisition (Śiv. 1216); fate, fortune, luck (K. 1090); sudden or unexpected gain or profit (e.g. discovering a hidden treasure, more than the expected profit in a business transaction, and so on) (cf. phala-pᵒ, p. 692a, l. 40); (what one has received from fate, i.e.) a person's natural disposition. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of someone formerly badly conducted) the personal character to change, and a taste for good conduct to arise in an individual.
m. what is begun; hence, fate, destiny (Śiv. 100, 764, 1015, 1766, 1790, 1795, 1801, 1914). Cf. prālab, prālabd.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. prāranôwᵘ), to cause a person to await, set a person waiting (for someone or something) (Gr.Gr. 174; Śiv. 1634, 1671). prāranôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. prāranövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), one who is caused to await, as ab.
n.ag. (f. prāravüñᵘ̈), one who awaits, one who waits for (someone or something) (Śiv. 1173).

conj. 1 (1 p.p.prôrᵘ), to await, expect, look out for, lie in wait (for, dat.) (Gr.Gr. 13; Gr.M.; L. 464, parārun; W. 125, prārān gaʦhanas, expecting to go; L.V. 83; Śiv. 2, 178, 1081, 1176, 1439, 1610, 1914; Rām. 1394, 1483, 1768; K. 20, 241, 347, 654, 679, 721, 797; H. ii, 10; v, 6, 11; YZ. 39, 43, 137, 143, 275, 279, 344, 490). ¶ prôrᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. prörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), awaited.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. prāryōv), to wait, remain patiently (vb. intr.) (Gr.Gr. 174; Gr.M.; Śiv. 415, 971, 1395, 1466, 1684; Rām. 244, 1488, 1721). Gr.Gr. 206 wrongly marks this verb as conj. 2, confusing it with prārun 1. ¶ prāran-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. prāran-wājĕñ), one who awaits, one who is patient by nature. ¶ prāryō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. prāryē-müʦᵘ̈), one who has waited, one who has been patiently expecting.

m. the return (as is customary) of a certain portion of the gift sent by a young woman's father to her husband's people on various festive occasions (cf. durⁱbata-pⁱ, p. 240b, l. 34); the portion of the gift so returned. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to return this portion (according to custom) to the giver. --nyās -- m. the amount so returned together with the presents given to the servants, etc., who accompanied the original present. ¶ prāsa-dyār m.pl. the money actually given to the original giver of this present as representing the value of the portion of the gift that should be returned. -hāra f.pl., id.

m. favour, kindness, graciousness, condescension (Gr.M., Śiv. 1591). --karun -- m.inf. to show favour (to), show grace (to) (Śiv. 655, 1337, 1441, 1740); to show favour by presenting to someone handsome garments, ornaments, or the like (Śiv. 1089). --sapadun -- m.inf. favour or grace to be experienced; a handsome present to be made to a person.

c.g. or (L.V. 65) prasonᵘ (f. prasüñᵘ̈) adj. pleased, delighted, propitiated, soothed, satisfied, content (Gr.M.; L.V. 65; Śiv. 102, 309, 384, 691, 1184); cheerful, happy, gay, glad, merry; cf. prasand. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become pleased, satisfied (Śiv. 355-6, 358, 1127; K. 427, 965). -mana adj. c.g. of happy mind, lively in disposition (Gr.M.). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain pleased, to continue satisfied (Śiv. 480; Rām. 1572, 1742). --thawun -- m.inf. to make pleased, to oblige (a person) (Gr.M., Śiv. 584).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. prasanôwᵘ), to cause a child to be born, to cause a woman to bear a child, (by medical means) to make a woman who has no children to bear one (cf. prasawun and pīnawun, Gr.Gr. 171).

i.q. prasan, q.v., in man-pᵒ, q.v. The word is formed by conflation of prasan and the Persian pasand. --ākh -- interj. welcome (lit. thou hast come happily) (El.). --sapadun -- m.inf. to be, or become, happy (El., Śiv. 44).

m. a topic, a subject of discussion; treating, explaining, discussing (a future course of conduct). --tulun -- m.inf. to raise or start such a discussion. --wŏthun -- m.inf. such a discussion to arise, or be started.
f. happiness, joy (Gr.M.); clearness, brightness, limpidity, pellucidity, transparency.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. prasowᵘ. Causal of prasun, q.v. Cf. prasanāwun and pīnawun), i.q. prasanāwun, q.v. (cf. Gr.Gr. 171).

n.ag. (f. prasavüñᵘ̈), a man who is occupied in begetting children (either in the act, or habitually addicted to it); (f.) a woman in the act of bearing a child, or who is in the habit of bearing children.
m. (sg. dat. prashĕnas), a question, inquiry, etc., i.q. prashᵉ̆n, q.v.
m. (sg. dat. prāshĕnas), eating, feeding; esp. the first giving of food to a newly-born child (cf. ana-prᵒ, p. 30a, l. 3).

(also written prashn) m. a question, query, inquiry, interrogation (Gr.M.; Śiv. 623, 1348, 1653; K. 9); cf. prashun. --karun -- to question, inquire, interrogate. --wuchun -- m.inf. to make an inquiry into the future, to look for omens, consult a prophet, seer, diviner, or the like. ¶ prạshᵉ̆na pyonᵘ m.inf. to fall out from an inquiry into the future, the result of an invited prediction to show itself, a prognostication to come true. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), an inquirer from a seer, one who consults a diviner; one who is consulted by such an inquirer, a seer, diviner, prophet. ¶ prashᵉ̆nᵉ̆ pyonᵘ m.inf. the results of one's fate to manifest themselves.

f. the tax on saffron (El. has prastar m., the close watch of the saffron growing near Pámpúr). prastᵃrĕ-bal m. the post where the official guardians of the saffron crop reside, where the tax is collected, and where smugglers are punished.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. pyāv, f. pyāyĕ (Gr.Gr. 230, 236; K.Pr. 158). The causal of this verb is prasawun, prasanāwun, or pīnawun (Gr.Gr. 171), qq.v.) to bear, bring forth offspring, give birth (to), be delivered (of), be in travail (cf. gāv prasüñᵘ̈, p. 316a, l. 35) (El.; Gr.Gr. 110, 171, 241 (incorrectly translated 'to be born'); W. 149; Rām. 629, 633; K. 46, 785; K.Pr. 31, 158, 174, 231, 260). ¶ prasani aʦun m.inf. to enter child-bearing or begetting, to reach a child-bearing or begetting age, to reach the age of puberty; to be engaged in child-bearing. ¶ prasan-wājĕñ n.ag. f. a woman who is approaching the time of labour; a woman who is of a child-bearing age. ¶ pyā-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pyā-müʦᵘ̈), one to whom a child has been born (esp. one who has quite lately had a child) (Gr.Gr. 110).
m. (This word is borrowed direct from Sanskrit, with the spelling of that language), morning-time, dawn. Cf. prātas.

m. (sg. dat. pratakas), expulsion (of a wife, son, or other member) from the family (usually for some fault, and resulting in the expelled person losing all rights as a member of the family). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to expel (a son, wife, or the like) from the family (for bad conduct, etc.), to turn out of the house (so that the evicted person loses his inheritance or share in the estate). --lagun -- m.inf. such expulsion to happen to a person, to be so expelled. -nāma m. a formal document declaring and effecting such expulsion. -zad adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -zadiñ), one who is so expelled by the head of his family.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. pratakhladiñ), one who is expelled from the family; esp. a family or sub-clan, the ancestor of which has been expelled from the original family or clan.
m. (sg. dat. pratāpas), splendour, brilliancy (K. 657); dignity, majesty, glory (K. 7); prosperity (cf. punᵘ pᵒ, p. 738a, l. 12).
adv. at dawn, early in the morning (K. 28, 203, 229, 379, 405, 592, 1155, 1163). Cf. prātaḥ-kāl.
or pratĕksh adj. c.g. visible, present, in sight (Śiv. 346, 351, 808, 1243, 1441).
in prāth-prāth m. jabbering, gibbering, talking nonsense or inarticulately (esp. of a person in a rage speaking without thought); cf. pᵃrpᵃr. prāth-prāth lagun m.inf. such nonsense-talk to begin.

m. (sg. dat. -pratas), a hit, a blow, a knock, thwack (cf. buthⁱ-prⁱ, p. 142b, l. 46; lōri-prᵒ, p. 531a, l. 13; mŏkha-prᵒ, p. 560a, l. 17). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to hit, thwack, beat (with a stick or the like).

a distributive particle, sometimes governing the abl. and sometimes the dat. (Gr.Gr. 158; Gr.M.; Śiv. 197, 365, 1042, 1119, 1126, 1427, 1546; Rām. 348, 617, 771, 1350, 1734; K. 294, 421, 436, 459, etc.). As in some of the following, it governs either the dat. or the abl. without difference of meaning, and sometimes it is simply compounded (Gr.M.). prath akhāh  adj. (sg. dat. --akis --), each one, everyone (Śiv. 1544). --akis --  acc. or dat. of the preceding; as adv. one by one (Gr.Gr. 158, Śiv. 712). --dŏha -- adv. every day, each day, daily (Gr.Gr. 158; W. 95; K 426; H. viii, 1). When an emphatic y is added, prath is dropped. Thus dŏhay not prath dŏhay (Gr.Gr. 158). --dŏhukᵘ -- sg. gen. (f. --dŏhücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or produced on, every day. --jāyĕ -- or --jāyi -- adv. in each place, everywhere (Śiv. 1190, 1534; Rām. 34, 105, 108, 472, 1108f, 1715-6; K. 862). --kã̄h -- or --kũh -- or --kū̃h --  pron. indef. each one, everyone (cf. p. 389b, ll. 47 ff.) (Śiv. 1216, 1460; Rām. 1496; K. 271 (f.), 292 (f.), 409, 711, 785, 988, 998, 1064; K.Pr. 208). --kē̃h -- (cf. id.), each thing, everything (K. 519). --kun -- adv. in every direction. --kuni -- adv. everywhere (Gr.M.), on each (every) thing, at each (every) thing (Śiv. 306, 1281, 1757). --kunyukᵘ -- sg. gen. (f. --kunicᵘ̈ --), of, or belonging to, each (thing) (Śiv. 1546). --kaĩsi-hondᵘ -- sg. gen. (f. --kaĩsi-hünzᵘ̈ --), of, or belonging to, each man (or other human being) (K. 204). --kã̄ʦhāh -- indef. pron. each man, each one, everyone (Śiv. 357). --mahanivis -- adv. man by man (Gr.Gr. 158). --mahanyuwᵘ -- m. every man (El.). --pahara -- adv. at each watch (Gr.Gr. 158). --prabātan -- adv. each morning (Śiv. 163). --prabātas -- adv., id. (Rām. 73). --ranga -- adv. of every kind (Gr.M.; Śiv. 849, 1185). --rĕta aki phiri -- adv. once a month. --subᵃh -- or --subᵃhas -- adv. every morning (also written --suba --). --shāyĕ -- adv. in every place (Śiv. 242, 271, 1238, 1332; K. 924, 940). --sāta -- adv. at each (every) moment (Rām. 582). --sātukᵘ -- sg. gen. (f. --sātücᵘ̈ --), of, or belonging to, each (every) moment. --tarafa -- adv. in all directions (Śiv. 812). --taraha -- adv. of every kind. --tarahukᵘ -- adj. (f. --tarahücᵘ̈ --), of every kind. --vēla -- adv. at each (every) time. --vēlukᵘ -- sg. gen. (f. --vēlücᵘ̈ --), of, or belonging to, each (every) time. --warihĕ -- adv. every year, yearly (Gr.Gr. 158). --vizi -- adv. at each (every) time (Gr.Gr. 158, K. 575). --vizi-hondᵘ -- sg. gen. (f. --vizi-hünzᵘ̈ --), of, or belonging to, each (every) time. --zanāni -- adv. woman by woman (Gr.Gr. 158). ¶ prathuy adv., i.q. prath 2, but more emphatic, as in prathuy tīrthan, (going) to every single holy place (L.V. 36).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. prathyōv), to become famous, well-known. prathyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. prathyē- müʦᵘ̈), become famous, well-known.
f. a resolution, resolve (Gr.M.); a promise, oath (K. 719). --karüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to resolve (Gr.M., Rām. 627).

adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. pratihatas), spoken ill of (on account of bad conduct), branded with reproach. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become ill spoken of, to get a bad character. --karun -- m.inf. to give a person a bad character. --sapadun -- m.inf. to become an object of general censure.
a learned spelling of pratigyā, q.v.
f. an image, statue, figure, idol (Śiv. 890, 1742; K. 878, 881-3).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. prôṭᵘ; 2 p.p. prācyōv), to dig, to plough (Rām. 1428). prāṭan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who digs or ploughs, a ploughman (cf. butarāth pᵒ, p. 145b, l. 8).
f. (sg. dat. pravrüʦᵘ̈), conduct, behaviour; active life, taking an active part in worldly affairs (opp. to nivruth, q.v.) (Śiv. 1427, 1481, 1860).

f.pl. rays of light, sunshine, brilliancy (El. prau, prauwa, prauwah; Rām. 542). --lagañĕ -- f. pl. inf. rays to come into contact (with the eyes), to be dazzled. --wŏthañĕ -- f. pl. inf. rays to arise, i.e. to issue (e.g. from a source of light, from a jewel, a mirror, or (met.) from a lovely face). prawa yiñĕ f. pl. inf. rays to come, to be dazzled.
m. a proclamation, a crying out. --karun -- m.inf. to make proclamation (L.V. 89).
m. the stream, current, of a river (Gr.M.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. prāwanôwᵘ), to cause to obtain, to endow (a person with wealth, etc.); to grant (Śiv. 19, 1000, 1066, 1088, 1551, 1635, 1648, 1654, 1679, 1781, 1876).
adj. c.g. about to be obtained, fit to be obtained, worthy to be obtained (K. 321).
m. living abroad or away from home; foreign residence, travelling, journey.
adj. c.g. a sojourner abroad, one who lives away from home, a traveller; one wearied by much travelling to and fro.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. prôwᵘ), to obtain, get, acquire, receive, attain, accept, reach (cf. dŏh prāwȧnⁱ, p. 199b, l. 41; jīth prāvüñᵘ̈, p. 378b, l. 28) (Gr.Gr. 23; Gr.M.; L.V. 103; Śiv. 20, 55, 102, 452, 496, 646, 884, 997, 1058, 1098, 1197, 1246, etc.; Rām. 347; K. 1154; YZ. 515); to pick up, earn, gain, reap, receive (Gr.M.); to come across, suffer (a misfortune, etc.) (Gr.M.); to procure, secure (cf. rūzī prᵒ, s.v. rūzī) (Śiv. 1506, Rām. 1646); to clothe (oneself), don (El., YZ. 22). prôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. prövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), obtained, gained, etc.

or (Śiv. 1851) priyā 1 f. affection, tender love (Gr.Gr. 127; Śiv. 585, 662, 714, 772, 915, 1571; Rām. 731); zest, wish, desire, liking (Rām. 1485). --āsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. affection, tenderness, to exist (K. 515). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. affection, tenderness, to arise. --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to hold, or feel, affection (for).

m. a celebrated place of pilgrimage at the confluence of the Ganges and the Jamunā, near Allahabad (Śiv. 627, 1172); hence, a confluence of any two rivers; N. of an island at the confluence of the rivers Vĕth (Jehlam) and Sindhu in Kashmīr (RT.Tr. II, 329; K.Pr. 173).
m. in prayās karun m.inf. to put (a person) to great labour (for the accomplishment of some task).

in the following:-- prāyĕ bĕhun m.inf. (of a woman in labour) to crouch (for delivery) in the lying-in room; hence, met. to sit crouching like a lately delivered woman, to sit idle and workless, to be out of employment. Cf. prasun, 2 p.p. pyāv, f. pyāyĕ.
adv. generally, as a rule, for the most part, almost entirely (Gr.M.).

m. (sg. dat. prāyĕcĕtas), atonement, expiation, indemnification, a religious act to atone for sin; a thing that demands expiation, a sinful act, a sin. --khasun -- m.inf. (need for) atonement to arise, to become defiled by sin, to become a sinner. --karun -- m.inf. to do expiation, perform penance (for a sinful act); to perform a sinful act (such as demands expiation).
adj. c.g. one who expiates, one who has sinned, and who is therefore bound to expiation.

or (Śiv. 51) priyĕm m. love, affection (for human beings, animals, or things), tender regard, kindliness (Śiv. 51, 70, 103, 181, 207, 239, 267, 276, 377, 380, 395, etc.); met. a love, a loved one, a beloved (Rām. 1428). --barun -- m.inf. to experience love, to become devoted to (esp. to a thing, or to an action) (Śiv. 1174; Rām. 1524, 1701). --thawun -- m.inf. to be in love with, to be fast friends with; esp. to feel affection (for a thing or action). ¶ prayĕma-pāthᵃr c.g. a vessel of affection, an object of extreme affection, that which is dearly loved. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), loveless, devoid of love, feeling distaste (for); (of some action or employment) engaged in without love, distasteful. -raʦhar m. the condition of being devoid of love, a feeling of distaste; (of some action or employment) the condition of being engaged in with distaste. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), full of love, eagerly devoted to any work; (of some work) engaged in with much love. -sasʦar or -saʦhar m. the condition of being eagerly devoted (esp. to some work); (of some action or employment) the condition of being engaged in with much love. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), one who is of a loving or affectionate disposition. ¶ prayĕmukᵘ sg. gen. (f. prayĕmücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, love, done out of affection or as a token of affection.
m. full of love, of an affectionate disposition.
m. (sg. dat. prāyĕshcitas), atonement, expiation (Gr.M.). The Skt. form of prāyĕcĕth, q.v.
m. (sg. dat. prayĕtnas), effort, exertion, persevering effort, striving.
n.ag. (f. prayĕvüñᵘ̈), that which pleases, pleasant, agreeable, satisfactory (cf. dilas prᵒ, p. 211a, l. 12) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1265).

m. a usual form, general usage; esp. the proper practice or carrying out of the prescribed ceremonial of a religious rite. ¶ prayūga-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), the skilled priest engaged for the due carrying out of a religious ceremonial. ¶ prayūgas bĕhun m.inf. to be devoted to or continually employed in duly carrying out religious ceremonials (whether for oneself or for others).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. proyᵘ), (of a thing, work, food, etc.) to be liked, to be pleasant, to be thought nice, to be highly appreciated (gen. of person pleased) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 876, 878, 1086; Rām. 592). proyᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. prüyᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of a thing, etc., as ab.) liked, found nice.

m. use, need, necessity; (in Kāshmīrī, usually) aim, object, intention, meaning, (of some business, advice, speech, or the like) (Gr.M. prayōzan). --nērun -- m.inf. the object or intention (of any act or the like) to be achieved.
f. progeny (of so-and-so), sons, daughters, grandchildren, etc. (of so-and-so); the subjects (of a king), the population of a ruler's realm (Rām. 1108c).

f. (sg. dat. prazāhi), the people (collected together on any occasion) as a whole, the whole population of any tract; a subject or the subjects of a realm (Gr.M. where it is incorrectly written prazāh, and shown as masc.) (Śiv. 883, 885, 1240, 1491).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. prazalôwᵘ), to cause to shine, make brilliant, illuminate (Śiv. 738, 836, 1881); to cause to be fine and beautiful, to dress up in fine clothes. prazalôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. prazalövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), cause to shine, make brilliant; dressed up in fine clothes.
n.ag. (f. prazạlavüñᵘ̈), shining, brilliant (Śiv. 513, 657, 1706; Rām. 204, 1225, 1257, 1264); glorious, dressed in fine clothes; brilliant, beautiful (of a person) (Rām. 520, 1291, 1297).

or prazalun conj. 2 (1 p.p. prazolᵘ), to shine, give forth light or brilliancy, to be set alight, become lighted (L.V. 4; Śiv. 314, 500, 666, 1147, 1200, 1346, 1501, 1536, 1538, 1657; Rām. 23, 1012, 1071; YZ. 181). prazolᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. prazüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), become shining, become brilliant.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. prazanôwᵘ), to recognize, etc., i.q. prazanun, q.v. (YZ. 479). prazanāwana yunᵘ m.inf. pass., i.q. prazanana yunᵘ, q.v., s.v. prazanun. prazanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. prazanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. prazonᵘ-motᵘ, q.v., s.v. id.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. prazonᵘ, 2 p.p. prazañōv), to recognize, to ascertain after testing (El. parzanun, parzun). This verb also takes the forms parzanun, parzānun, prazanāwun, and parzanāwun, with the same meaning. ¶ prazonᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. prazüñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), recognized. ¶ prazanana yunᵘ m.inf. pass. to be recognized; esp. to be, or become, visible to one with imperfect sight, to be visible to a partly blind person, to be recognizable.
m. (sg. dat. prazāpatas), (in Hindū mythology) one of the ten demigods or lords of created beings first created by Brahmā (cf. dakshĕ pᵒ, p. 209a, l. 39) (Śiv. 33, 40, 65, 76, 86, etc.; Rām. 594).
m. (sg. dat. prāzāpatas), (a corruption of the preceding, but with special meanings), the ten lords of creation, as ab.; the god Brahmā; a king (as lord of his subjects). Cf. praz.
adj. c.g. one, the corners of whose mouth are ugly or diseased.
m. vehemence, violence, excessive heat, stiflingness (esp. of heat or of an epidemic) (Śiv. 905, 917); (as adj.) vehement, powerful (Gr.M.).

m. constant practice, application (to any work); constant use (of any thing, e.g. a dish, an ornament, or a garment). ¶ praʦarukᵘ sg. gen. (f. praʦarücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, constant use, in constant use. ¶ praʦaras lagun m.inf. to begin to be brought into constant use (esp. of something which, owing to its value or rarity, should be used only occasionally, but for which no substitute is available; e.g. employing the best dinner service, or one's best clothes, for everyday use). --rōzun -- m.inf. to be (improperly, as ab.) in everyday use. --thawun -- m.inf. to put into everyday use (something not used, or only occasionally used, before).
m. the being in currency, prevalence, general use, general acceptance (as correct). --karun -- m.inf. to spread abroad (knowledge or the like) (Gr.M.).
m. (sg. dat. praʦāranas), the making current or prevalent, bringing into general acceptance (as correct).

f. (sg. dat. praʦi), a question; a riddle, enigma, conundrum (Śiv. 1873); a vow made at the beginning of a religious ceremony. praʦa-praʦh f. question on question, the asking of many hard questions (e.g. in a legal discussion, an examination, or the like).

or pröʦᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. prāʦi), the corner of the mouth (cf. dŏda-prāʦa, p. 190a, l. 8; kaṭa-pröʦᵘ̈ and kaṭa-prāʦh-hyuhᵘ, p. 487a, ll. 9, 14; rata-prāʦa, s.v. rath); the folded edge of folded paper or the like. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cut the pages (at the folded edges) of a book; to cut the crooked edge of a piece of cloth. ¶ prāʦa-hajĕr m. crookedness or unevenness of the corners of the mouth. -holᵘ adj. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), one, the corners of whose mouth are crooked or uneven. --ʦaṭañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to cut the corners of the mouth; to pull food out of a hungry or greedy child's mouth. --wahārañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to open the corners of the mouth, to gabble words mixed with laughter. --yiñĕ -- f. pl. inf. sores to come at the corners of the mouth.
f. (sg. dat. prạʦᵃrüñᵃ), bringing into use (e.g. a vessel, dish, or garment); beginning to make use of, after a course of necessary instruction (e.g. a child or a horse).

pruthwī, prathivī, or pruthivī f. the wide world, the earth (Śiv. (pruthwī) 1304, (pruthivī) 125, 200, 324, 856, 928, 1251; Rām. (prĕthwī) 64, 69; K. (pruthivī) 5, 24, 1149); earth, land, ground, soil.
(El.), a misprint for phráṭ, i.e. phrāṭh, q.v.
f. a place in level ground (generally at the foot of a mountain) where water naturally springs up or exudes from the earth, a spring.

m. love, affection, tender regard (Gr.M.; Śiv. 45, 194, 231, 491, 527, etc.; Rām. 1232; K. 82, 510, 512, 514). --barun -- m.inf. to entertain love (for), bear love (to), cherish (K. 523, 1139). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. love to occur, love to arise. ¶ prīmukᵘ sg. gen. (f. prīmücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, affection, (of conduct) inspired by love. --bata -- m. food of affection, i.e. food (on some festive occasion) received from a friend; the loving support afforded by a parent, husband, son, etc.; a happy, prosperous, peaceful life.
m. reproaching, blaming, censure, casting blame upon.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pryunᵘ; 2 p.p. priñōv), to reproach, blame, censure, to cast blame upon (Rām. 163; K.Pr. 173, prĕnun); to become beneficial (to), to cause improvement (to) (Śiv. 1873). pryunᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. priñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), reproached, censured.
f. (sg. dat. prinzüʦᵘ̈), urging, incitement, encouragement (offered to one engaged in some work, so as to induce him to greater efforts).
n.ag. (f. prinzavüñᵘ̈), one who urges or incites to greater efforts (another who is engaged in some work).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pryunzᵘ, 2 p.p. prinzōv), to urge, incite to greater effort, encourage to action, prompt (e.g. when a teacher incites a pupil to study, or a master urges on a servant engaged in some task). Cf. prīrun and prūrun. ¶ prinzan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), an inciter, prompter, as ab. ¶ pryunzᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. prinzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), incited, encouraged (in any work on which one is engaged).
f. (sg. dat. prīrüñᵘ̈), the act of sending, dispatching (a message, etc.); dispatching (a person); setting (a servant or the like) to work.
f. (sg. dat. prīranāyi), i.q. prīran, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pryūrᵘ), to send, dispatch; to impel, instigate, incite; to order, direct. Cf. prinzun and prūrun. ¶ prīran-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a dispatcher, sender; an inciter, urger; an overseer. ¶ pryūrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. prīrᵘ̈- müʦᵘ̈), sent, dispatched; impelled, incited; ordered, directed.
n.ag. (f. pritavüñᵘ̈), one who suffers from salivation, one from whose mouth there is an excessive flow of saliva.
in prith-prith m. unlimited prating accompanied by the copious issue of saliva from the mouth, spluttering talk. Cf. pritun.

m. (sg. dat. prītas), one who has just departed, one just dead, deceased; the spirit of a deceased person, a departed spirit, a ghost, goblin, demon spirit, spook. ¶ prīta-brôhmun m. (sg. dat. -bröhmanas), an outcaste Brāhmaṇ who eats the offerings made at the obsequial rites to the manes. -bata m. the food eaten by the relations at the obsequial meals during the twelve days following a death. -būzan m. food eaten at obsequial ceremonies during the year after a person's decease; eating food unsuitably mixed (e.g. milk with fish, clarified butter with honey, and so on) (i.e. the sort of food which only ghosts would eat). -nörᵘ̈ f. a pot for holding liquids offered to the spirit of a deceased during the year following his death. -ʦoḍᵘ m. a jar for holding mixed food offered on such occasions; met. the belly of a man who inordinately eats food of mixed kinds. -ʦorᵘ m. food offered to ghosts. -ʦȧrⁱ-wörⁱ f. a pot for holding such food.
f. (sg. dat. prīti (K. 606)), friendliness, friendship, liking, fondness (for), regard, affection, love (K. 606). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. love or affection to arise.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. prityōv), to be salivated, to have an excessive flow of saliva (cf. prith).
m. (sg. dat. prītatas), the conduct of a goblin, acting like a demon (such as habitual uncleanliness, habitual bad conduct, habitual annoying, eating unlawful food, or the like).

f.pl. affection, loving devotion, tender love (e.g. shown to a father, master, or other protector). --gaʦhañĕ -- f. pl. inf. affection, love to arise (for a protector, cherisher, master). --pĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. such affection to fall, i.e. to be felt. --rōzañĕ -- f. pl. inf. such affection to continue (even after the reason for this affection had disappeared).
f. a beloved woman or goddess (Śiv. 51). This is a word borrowed direct from Sanskrit.
f. (sg. dat. priʦhi), a question, inquiry (Gr.Gr. 126); recognition of the consequences of some business which is begun.

f. inquiry, interrogation, inquisition, investigation, examination (El. pritsagár, prutsagár); welcoming (a guest, a friend). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make inquisition, to investigate (Gr.Gr. 126, K. 996).
n.ag. (f. priʦhavüñᵘ̈), one who asks (in all the senses of priʦhun, q.v.) (K. 1148); esp. an inquirer as to the future, one who consults an oracle or the like, or who consults omens.

f. just discrimination on the part of a judicial officer (founded on careful inquiry and thorough investigation of both sides of the story). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f. just discrimination to be shown by a judicial officer.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pryuʦhᵘ; 2 p.p. priʦhōv), to ask, inquire, question, interrogate (El. also pratshun and pritsun) (Gr.Gr. 126; Gr.M.; Rām. 238, 427, 439, 450, 540, 597, 753, 1056, etc.; K. 284, 289, 317, 503, 609, 956, 1040, 1133, 1135, 1142; H. xii, 1; YZ. 59, 81, 391; K.Pr. 30, 132, 173, 260); to ask advice (K. 1033); to ask about, inquire about (Śiv. 1457; Rām. 111, 313, 823, 893, 895, etc.; K. 535, 584, 839, 858, 931, 946, 1003, 1162; YZ. 14, 143; K.Pr. 71). ¶ priʦhⁱ priʦhⁱ sōdāh m. to carry on work continually taking people's advice. ¶ priʦhan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who asks, inquires; an investigator, examiner; a superintendent; one who shows proper respect (asking another's welfare, etc.); one who is in the habit of previously inquiring as to the result of any proposed action. ¶ pryuʦhᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. priʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), asked, inquired from; asked about, inquired about.

adj. (f. prübᵘ̈), one who (owing to simplicity or ignorance) dresses badly, a sloven, one who is unkempt, one who wears his clothes on the wrong parts of his person, or who wrongly puts clothes on the right parts. Cf. prabākar.
m. a lord (Śiv., voc. prabō, 880); the Supreme Deity (L.V. 64).
see höhⁱ na pröhⁱ, p. 325a, l. 18, and cf. prāh.

or pröjᵘ̈ f. chaff and chopped straw (of barley, wheat, etc.) (cf. ȧlⁱshi-pⁱ, p. 25b, l. 12) (El. práj or prej, straw). ¶ prāji-bôrᵘ m. a load of chaff and chopped straw; plaster mixed with chaff, etc. -kĕsürᵘ̈ f. chaff (of barley, wheat, or the like). -kāṭh f. straw (of barley, wheat, etc.). -lôwᵘ m. a bundle or sheaf of straw. -thôpᵘ m. a handful of straw. -ṭūpⁱ f. (sg. dat. -ṭōpĕ), a cap of straw.
m. that which breathes, a living or sentient being, a living creature, animal, man (as endowed with breath) (Śiv. 442, 1059, 1591).
f. (sg. dat. pröñᵉ̆rüñᵉ̆), making old; rendering obsolete; wearing (something) out.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pröñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), to make old, render obsolete; to wear (something) out; cf. pröñᵉ̆run. pröñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. pröñᵉ̆rövᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), made old, rendered obsolete; caused to wear out.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. pröñᵒrᵒ), to make old, render obsolete; to wear (something) out; cf. pröñᵉ̆rāwun. pröñᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. pröñᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made old, rendered obsolete; caused to wear out.

adj. (f. prüñᵘ̈), white (cf. aḍa-pᵒ, p. 11b, l. 46) (El. prun, so K.Pr. 226); (of something washed) clean, pure (cf. atha-pᵒ, p. 61b, l. 6) (K.Pr. 169, prĕni for prüñᵘ̈); (of water) clear, not turbid; as subst., m. a kind of white rice (L. 463, prun; Śiv. 1032). --bata -- m. white boiled rice. ¶ prañi kanji adv. white skinned, white shelled (esp. of unhusked rice or the like, with the inner grain of some other colour). Cf. künḍᵘ̈ 1.

adj. (f. pröñᵘ̈), old, ancient, aged, of olden time (cf. aḍa-pᵒ, p. 11b, l. 48) (Gr.Gr. 12, 13, 140; Gr.M.; L.V. 63; Śiv. 943, 1506, 1545; Rām. 1547, 1768; YZ. 476; K.Pr. 159, 252); worn out, laid aside; old, of former time, former (H. vi, 11; viii, 5; K.Pr. 156); obsolete, old fashioned (Rām. 594); former, what has occurred previously (Gr.M., Śiv. 257, K. 44); (in fem.) pröñᵘ̈, an old woman (K.Pr. 208). --hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. pröñᵘ̈hishᵘ̈), worn out, old. --sapanun -- m.inf. to be old (El.). ¶ prāna-wôrᵘ adj. (f. -wörᵘ̈), old, worn out. -mọ̆nḍᵘ m. an old broken off tree-stump (lying on the ground, foul and dirty). ¶ prāni kāla adv. in olden time, in former days. -kölⁱ adv., id. --kālukᵘ -- sg. gen. (f. --kālücᵘ̈ --), of, or belonging to, olden time. ¶ prönⁱ kölⁱ adv. in ancient times, in olden days. ¶ prāñĕ katha f.pl. tales of old, ancient histories. --wati pakun -- m.inf. to walk on the old road, to follow ancient customs. ¶ prāñi mŏnji gāsa khyonᵘ m. to eat grass of the old root, i.e. to live upon one's former savings. --pūʦi -- adv. in the ancient manner, after the olden ways. --pūʦi-hondᵘ -- sg. gen. (f. --pūʦⁱ-hünzⁱ --), of, or belonging to, olden custom, of the ancient manner. ¶ pröñᵘ̈ phuhürᵘ̈ f. old savings, money formerly saved. --puy -- f. ancient offspring, the creation of olden times; old established bodily health and strength.

m. (sg. dat. pröpinis), an offering or oblation of food to a god (Hindū) (cf. ạgᵃna-pᵃ, p. 16b, l. 44; bal-pᵒ, p. 103b, l. 3; ḍulⁱ-pⁱ, p. 222b, l. 20; hēri-pᵒ, p. 345b, l. 48; hurⁱ-pⁱ, p. 347a, l. 6; khira-pᵒ, p. 409a, l. 37; kala-hērĕ-pᵒ, p. 434b, l. 47); the sacrificial formula which accompanies such an oblation. --hāwun -- m.inf. ceremonially to perform such an oblation (K. 307). ¶ pröpinⁱ-brôhmun (sg. dat. -bröhmanas), the Brāhmaṇ who recites the appropriate sacrificial formulas at such an oblation. -pholᵘ m. the portions of fruit, flour, etc., which remain over after such an offering is finished. -wôlu m. the person who makes this oblation. ¶ pröpinyukᵘ sg. gen. (f. pröpinicᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or connected with such an oblation; (of fruit, flour, etc.) of, or belonging to, the portion of the offering remaining over after the oblation is finished.

adv. in the year before last (Gr.Gr. 158). -kani adv. about the year before last. ¶ prārȧki adv., i.q. pröryus. ¶ prörⁱsukⁱ adj. (f. prörⁱsücⁱ), of, belonging to, or happening in, the year before last.
adj. (f. prörᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the year before last (cf. pröryus and parus) (El. prór, last year's; Gr.Gr. 158).
m. a large reel for winding thread, etc. Cf. prüʦᵘ̈. ¶ prȧtⁱ-ḍünḍⁱ f. the axle of this reel. -kambᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the cross-bar of this reel.
adj. (f. pröʦᵘ̈), that which has come of itself, that which comes spontaneously (e.g. wealth which comes without exertion) (cf. wôtᵘ-pᵘ, p. 1153b, l. 21).

or prövīsh f. the ceremony of entering a newly built house (at a propitious instant, and with sacrificial ceremonies), a house-warming (Rām. 609). ¶ prövishĕ-sāth m. (sg. dat. -sātas), the propitious moment for entering a new house. -tān m. a pillar set up in the north-east part of the house, representing the gods of the cardinal points, to whom worship is offered on this occasion.

m. (on the occasion of a marriage) the time fixed for the presentation by the bride's father and his people of the customary presents to the bridegroom and his family. --ladun -- m.inf. to send these presents. ¶ prūga-lodᵘ m. the sending of these presents. ¶ prūgukᵘ sg. gen. (prūgücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the occasion of these presents.

m. (sg. dat. prūnʦhas), N. of a country to the west of Kashmīr, commonly known as Pūnch; the ancient Parṇōtsa (RT.Tr. II, 433; K.Pr. 68). -wāla adj. c.g. a man of Prūnʦh; something made in or coming from Prūnʦh. ¶ prūnʦhukᵘ sg. gen. (f. prūnʦhücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or produced in, Prūnʦh.
adj. c.g. born in, or produced in, Prūnʦh.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. prūrᵘ), to send (a message, or the like, giving a person orders, or summoning him to receive instructions, or the like); cf. prinzun and prīrun. prūrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. prǖrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), sent for, summoned, etc. (as ab.); one appointed as an overseer.
adj. (f. pruthiwöñᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the earth (L.V. 52).
m. ashamed, put to shame; a miser (K.Pr. 47, prut). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be ashamed, become put to shame.

f. the spike forming part of a spinning-wheel on which the thread is wound (El. prats and prits, Śiv. 1875). Cf. protᵘ and pöshᵘ̈. ¶ praʦi-dan m. the handle of such a reel. -ḍünḍᵘ̈ f. the axle of this reel. -kambᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a cross-bar of this reel.
interj. an onomatopœic sound of derision (Gr.Gr. 18).

m. mint, peppermint, Mentha viridis. According to El. it is much eaten as a condiment by Hindūs, and is used as a remedy in the diarrhœa of children (El. púdinah and púdína). -caṭiñ f. a pickle (chutnee) made of mint.

conj. 2 or 3 (1 p.p. pugᵘ (conj. 2), f. pujᵘ̈; 2 p.p. pugyōv (conj. 3)), to fall fast asleep (esp. suddenly). pugᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (of pugun, conj. 1) (f. pujᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ 1, for 2, see pujun), suddenly fallen fast asleep. pugyō-motᵘ perf. part. (of pugun, conj. 3) (f. pugyē-müʦᵘ̈), id.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. puhȧrⁱladiñ), one who is attacked by mad fury. Cf. puhurᵘ.

m. a scorpion (El.) (?); a kind of small and very poisonous snake inhabiting rocky ground (L. 155, pohur). --āsun -- m.inf. mad fury to have attacked a person. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. mad fury to attack a person. ¶ puhȧrⁱ-balāy f. an attack of mad fury; a person who acts as if under the influence of mad fury. -dĕv m. an attack of mad fury (believed to be caused by the possession of a demon); a demon who causes such mad fury. -dĕviñ f. a female demon who causes such fury.
f. a female butcher, a woman who lives by the sale of mutton or goat's flesh; the wife of a male butcher (El. pújain); a woman whose conduct is that of a butcher woman. Cf. pujᵘ.
f. the condition or hereditary calling of a butcher.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. pujᵘ), (of work done by some one else) to be pleasing, to suit one's wishes, to satisfy. pujᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pujᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ 2; for 1, see pugun) that which (when done by another) has become satisfactory.
m. (f. pujĕñ, q.v.), a butcher (of sheep or goats) (El. púj; W. 114, puz; K.Pr. 68, 173). ¶ pujⁱ-bāy f. his wife; cf. pujĕñ. -wān m. a butcher's shop (W. 114, puz-wān; K.Pr. 178).

or pȧjⁱ f. a large broad open basket (the largest of all the baskets made in the valley. It is used for carrying rice) (cf. buthⁱ-pⁱ, p. 142b, l. 44; dachĕ-pᵒ, p. 185b, l. 48; dā̃-pᵒ, p. 231b, l. 26; gūrⁱ-pⁱ, p. 299b, l. 10; khȧrⁱ-pⁱ, p. 410b, l. 48) (El. pȧj; L. 314, 458; K.Pr. 48, 64, 76); met. 'a basket full (of disease)', used --˚ to indicate some disease affecting the entire body, as in bāda-pȧjⁱ, p. 82a, l. 9. ¶ pajĕ-bāgay f. dividing up (e.g. a pile of grain) by large basketfuls. -sörᵘ̈ f. carrying off and collecting in large baskets (as when grain is carried away from the threshing-floor). -tala nīrith gaʦhun m.inf. to emerge from under a basket, as if a person doubled up and hidden under a basket were suddenly to stand up and show himself; hence, met. to appear like a Jack-in-the-box, suddenly to spring up and become tall. -tal rūdᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. -tal rūzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), remaining under the basket; hence (of mutual hate, wrath, etc.), deliberately remaining concealed (i.e. biding the time for vengeance). -tal rōzun m.inf. to remain under a basket, (mutual hate, wrath, etc.) to remain concealed, as ab. -tal thowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. -tal thüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of anger, means of vengeance, or the like) deliberately hidden, as ab. -tal thawun m.inf. to put under a basket; met. to conceal one's hatred or wrath, biding the time for wreaking vengeance.
f. the condition or nature of a butcher (see pujᵘ); conduct like that of a butcher.

m. straw (such as rice-straw, etc); (pl.) straw shoes (cf. the next) (K.Pr. 111). ¶ pula-horᵘ m. a 'straw-pair', i.e. a pair of straw shoes, worn by Kāshmīrīs on the mountains (El.) (cf. dĕlⁱ-pⁱ, p. 267b, l. 48; gāsa-pᵒ, p. 307b, l. 45; phĕtⁱ-pⁱ, p. 723a, l. 18) (Gr.Gr. 81; L. 251; K.Pr. 123, 154, 248, 260). -hȧrⁱ-khŏr m. a man's foot wearing a straw shoe; a single straw shoe. -hȧrⁱ-khôrⁱ m. a single straw shoe. -hȧrⁱ-madun adj. (f. -hȧrⁱ-madüñⁱ), a hero (or heroine) who habitually wears straw shoes (used, esp. in ridicule, with reference to a rich person who wears such). -hȧrⁱ-phrath m. (sg. dat. -phratas), an old, worn-out, broken straw shoe. -hȧrⁱ-züṭⁱ f. (sg. dat. -hȧrⁱ-zacĕ), an old, worn-out rag of a grass shoe. -paitav f. 'straw shoes and puttees', travelling baggage (collected by an intending traveller, such as shoes, puttees, drawers, and the like). ¶ pulan aʦun m.inf. 'to take to straw shoes', i.e. to be reduced to poverty by the loss of all one's savings; to become discouraged, disheartened (cf. pŏlun). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. 'to fall into straw shoes', i.e. (of a generous person) to become miserly. --wātun -- m.inf. 'to arrive at straw shoes', (of some wealthy or famous person) to become poverty-stricken, to lose one's reputation, and so on.

m. N. of an ancient Indian sage (in Skt., Pulastya), one of the mind-born sons of Brahmā. His son was Viśravas. Viśravas had one son, Vaiśravaṇa, by his wife Dēvavarṇinī, and by another wife, Kaikasī, three sons, Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, and Vibhīṣaṇa, and one daughter, Śūrpanakhā. Kaikasī was of demon (Rākṣasa) origin, and her children were all Rākṣasas. Of her three sons, Vibhīṣaṇa was pious. The others acted fully up to their demon origin. Their half-brother, Vaiśravaṇa, was also named Kubēra, and was the god of wealth. The above is the account given in the Sanskrit Rāmāyaṇa (VII; ii ff.), but in the Kāshmīrī Rāmāyaṇa (622 ff.) Pulastya is not the grandfather, but the father of all these, and all, including Vaiśravaṇa, are borne by Kaikasī. On the other hand, in 611 Vaiśravaṇa is referred to as Pulastya's grandson. In Rām. 622 the word is spelt Pulastē m.c.
adj. (f. pulivᵘ̈), made of straw (e.g. a rope, a bed, a mat, or the like).
m. a carpenter's chisel (El., cf. ponᵘ 1); a monkey (El., cf. ponzᵘ).
(K. 198-9) said to be a corruption of the Skt. punaḥ santu, may they be again, i.e. may you have more and more (children). Cf. pŏnasondᵘ.
in pūnāyĕ wātun m.inf. to become utterly destitute.

m. (sg. dat. punḍarīkas), N. of a demon, in Sanskrit usually called Pauṇḍraka, who claimed that he, and not Krishna (Skt., Kṛṣṇa) Vāsudēva, was the real Krishna. He was killed by the latter (K. 867 ff.).

(often written punim) or pūnim f. the day of the full moon (cf. kāwa-pᵒ, p. 495a, l. 21) (Śiv. 209, 526). -dŏh or -dŏha adv. on the full-moon day (Śiv. 740; Rām. 400, dŏh). -hondᵘ gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or produced on the day of the full moon (Śiv. 525, 1042, 1574; Rām. 1771). -ʦandᵃr or -ʦandrama f. the moon of the full-moon day (Śiv. 692; Rām. 406, -dra; 312, 543, -drama); met. a king or other great man who is a bounteous and fortunate ruler.
conj. 2 (1 p.p. punᵘ), to come true (of a blessing, curse, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 206). punᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. puñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), come true (as ab.).
or (as in Skt.) m. (Śiv. 1159), i.q. pŏñ (the Skt. form of the word).

m. 'a twenty-fiver', i.e. a certain monetary value, the fourth part of a 'hundreder' (hath) (p. 357b, l. 3) or pice, and equal in value to sixteen cowries, the pūnʦhu of RT.Tr. II, 311-12, q.v. (K.Pr. 56 (púṅʦhuv), 80 (puṅʦhú), 216 (puṅʦhí)). --bar -- adj. c.g. weighing the fourth part of a tōlā (which is equal to about half an ounce). This is principally used with reference to such things as saffron, musk, spices, or the like.
ord. (f. pǖnʦimᵘ̈), fifth (El. pántshyum, pántsum, or pántsyum; Gr.Gr. 76; Rām. 181, 1153, 1279; H. x, 1, 6).
or pǖnʦᵘ̈h, also written pǖ̃ʦᵃh card. twenty-five (Gr.Gr. 77) (El. paintsah or pántsawuh); a collection of twenty-five things, a twenty-five.
or pǖnʦᵘ̈hyumᵘ̈ ord. (f. pǖnʦᵃhimᵃ or pǖnʦᵘ̈himᵘ̈), twenty-fifth (Gr.Gr. 77) (El. paintsahyum).

m. religious merit (acquired by the performance of religious actions) (Śiv. 1737); rectitude (El. pūn); solemn meals eaten during the first ten days after the death of an old and respected member of a Hindū family; see --ranun, bel. -dān m. a religious or pious gift; making religious or pious gifts. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat the solemn meals after a death, as ab. -pratāph m. (sg. dat. -pratāpas), prosperity, power, beauty, or the like, the result of virtuous actions. --ranun -- m.inf. to cook (i.e. provide) the funeral meal. When an old and respected Hindū dies, it is customary for all neighbours who are related to him to provide food and cooking for the family of the deceased. This goes on for ten days after the death, and is called by the above words.
f. a hedge (round a garden or the like) (L.V. 63).
or pŏr m. a city, district, country. Used --˚, as in Shōnita-pŏr, the N. of a city (K. 790, 818); Sŏrgā-pŏr, the city, or land, of heaven (K. 771).

m. an arrangement in sets, series, or gradations of a number of things (e.g. plucking fruit, etc., as they ripen, set by set, what ripens first, first, and what ripens later, later); the arrangement in order (of precedence, or rank) of a number of people (e.g. the allocation of seats at a dinner). For examples, see below. pūrukᵘ gen. (f. pūrücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a series (e.g. of collecting crops as they ripen, or the order of guests at a public meeting or at a dinner). Thus, gŏḍañiki pūrücᵘ̈ kapas, the cotton of the first series, i.e. the cotton which ripened first, and was first plucked; dŏyimi pūrücᵘ̈ kapas, the cotton which is next plucked, owing to its having ripened somewhat later; gŏḍañiki pūrücᵘ̈ sālarĕñ, a lady guest among those invited to sit down to eat in the first row.

adj. c.g. full, full of, complete, abounding in, very, exceeding (cf. nanda-pᵒ, p. 641b, l. 22) (W. 153), used ˚--, as in pur-cīn adj. c.g. full of curls (YZ. 5). -khumār (YZ. 269) or pūrᵘ-khumār (H. v, 2) (for پُر خمار) adj. (of a loved one) full of languishment (YZ. 269). -masāl adj. c.g. (of some dish of food) full of spices, spicy. ¶ pura 1 in pura-gūlᵘ m. (pl. dat. gōlĕn), an entire kernel of a walnut.
i.q. pūra and pūrᵘ 5, qq.v. (cf. bar-pūr, p. 125b, l. 1), full, complete (Śiv. 326, 875, 893); full, fulfilled (Śiv. 785); full (of the moon) (Śiv. 424, 692).
f. of pūrᵘ 4 used as adj., in pūr dĕsh f. the eastern quarter.

adj. c.g. full, i.q. pūrᵘ 5, q.v. -pöṭhⁱ adv. fully, completely; in full manner, regularly (Gr.M.). --sapadun -- m.inf. to become full; to be completed (of a period of time) (Gr.M.); to be fulfilled (of a prophecy, etc.) (Gr.M.); to be confirmed (of news) (Gr.M.).

m. a piece of fine cloth or muslin (as might be used for a turban, a bandage, or for straining liquids). -düjᵘ̈ f. a piece of such cloth (esp. when square). -dāv f. narrow, string-like, strip of such cloth. -līr f. an old worn-out piece of such cloth. -lāṭh f. (sg. dat. -lāṭas), a single twist of a turban made of this fine cloth.
m. a square on a chessboard or the like.
m. (sg. dat. pūrakas), a certain practice in Yōga ascetic contemplation. It consists in closing the right nostril and inhaling through the left (Śiv. 987, 1414).

f. (sg. dat. purüñᵘ̈), a certain measure of land, nine cubits (of 36 fingers) broad, and twenty-two cubits long; a level bit of land (of no particular measurement) attached to a house, a courtyard, or the like (cf. nāra- pᵒ, p. 648a, l. 31; potᵘ pᵒ, s.v. potᵘ) (K.Pr. 251 purnih-pĕṭh for purüñᵘ̈-pĕṭh). purüñᵘ̈-pĕṭh hāwun m.inf. to leave a place in order to avoid meeting an expected person, to decamp, take to one's heels, make off.
(for 1, see pūrn) m. one who fills, one who fulfils, completes (Śiv. 987, 1414).
f. (sg. dat. pūrüñᵘ̈), filling, filling up.
f. fullness, completion, completeness (Śiv. 1474); satisfaction, satiety.
f. (sg. dat. purüʦᵘ̈), filling; fullness, completion, completeness; accomplishment; satisfaction, satiety.
f. payment or wages for filling, or for fulfilling, completing, etc.
n.ag. (f. pūravüñᵘ̈), a filler, one who fills; one who completes by supplying what is missing; something which must necessarily be filled, or be completed.
or (Śiv. 246) pūrab m. an eastern land, a country lying to the east. Cf. pūrᵘ 4.
or puribⁱ m. a Brāhmaṇ who marries another's widow (cf. ʦari-pᵒ, p. 1081b, l. 36). Such a man is put out of caste by his fellow-Brāhmaṇs. -bāy f. the wife of a man descended from such a Brāhmaṇ.
m. the possessing of a complete kernel, fullness (of a nut or the like); (of a man) the quality of sagacity combined with wealth.

m. fullness, completeness (cf. atha-pᵒ, p. 61b, l. 8) (Śiv. 157); completion (cf. phala-pᵒ, p. 692a, l. 42); satisfaction, content. --karun -- m.inf. to make fullness, to be completed; (of some mercantile transaction) to have results surpassing expectation; to fulfil a promise, etc. --nērun -- m.inf. fullness to issue, to keep a promise; (weight) to be completed, (measure) to be filled up, weight to be adjusted.
conj. part. of pairun and pūrun, qq.v.
m. a man who is full of good conduct, a well-conducted man; as adj. = pūrn (cf. phala-pᵒ, p. 692a, l. 39).
(Śiv. 1658, 1667) or pūran 1 adj. c.g. full, filled up (Śiv. 1667); full, complete (Śiv. 212, 1594, 1658, 1756; K. 458); full (of the moon) (K. 280); --˚ filled with, full of (K. 329, 1174).
m. (sg. dat. purōhitas), a family priest, a domestic chaplain, a priest who conducts all the ceremonials and sacrifices of a family (Rām. 308; K. 142, 615, 617).
f. asking, questioning, inquiry; (in Kāshmīrī) good government (of a kingdom).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pūrᵘ), to fill, fill up (Gr.M., Śiv. 1474, K. 590, K.Pr. 155); to complete, supply what is wanting (Gr.M.); to satisfy (Gr.M.; Rām. 4; K. 339, 574, 768, 1002); to fulfil, carry out, complete (a promise) (K. 278); to become full (Śiv. 533); to be enough, to suffice; to be successful, to gain the desired result of any course of conduct; to reap one's fate; (in Yōga philosophy) to fill oneself (with breath), to inhale breath in the process of ecstatic meditation (L.V. 37). ¶ pūranī impers. fut. part., c.g. that which has to be filled up (e.g. a hollow in the ground which it is wished to fill up). ¶ pūrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pūrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), filled, filled up; completed, having that which was wanting supplied; filled, replete, satisfied; and so on for the other meanings of the verb.
m. the Highest or Supreme Being, an epithet of Viṣṇu or Kṛṣṇa, in Skt. puruṣôttama (K. 1041).
adj. c.g. former, of former times (a borrowed Skt. word) (Śiv. 1801).
in pūrwādi-mŏkh adj. c.g. facing the east, turned to the east. -mŏkhī adv. facing the east, eastwardly.
adv. preceded by; hence, in accordance with, according to. A word borrowed from Skt. and used occasionally --˚, as in vĕdi-pūrwakh, according to due rite, ritely (K. 971).

m. nap (of cloth); (in Kāshmīrī) a kind of size (composed of lime, barley meal, and sulphur) used for finishing, pashmīna or woollen cloth after it has come from the loom. -gar m. (f. -gar-bāy is his wife, but -gariñ is a woman who follows the profession) a pashmīna-finisher. ¶ purza-gorᵘ m. a pashmīna- finisher (El.).
adj. c.g. (pashmīna cloth or the like) which has undergone the process of finishing.
adj. (f. purᵘ̈), (of a vessel) full, filled up (Gr.M.); full, complete (cf. phala-pᵒ, p. 692a, l. 36); (of a fruit or the like) full, plump, filled out.
f. reading, studying, in likha-pᵒ, p. 518b, l. 11, q.v.

m. (pl. nom. pǖrⁱ; ag. pairiv, L.V. 38, cf. pair), the foot (cf. okᵘ- pūrᵘ, p. 19a, l. 34; kāwa-pᵒ, p. 495a, l. 24) (Gr.M., L.V. 38); a pace, footstep (cf. nakha-pᵒ, p. 628b, l. 14; pakan-pᵒ, p. 728b, l. 1) (El., Gr.Gr. 30, Śiv. 1634). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to walk slowly on foot. --ṭhaharun -- m.inf. the foot to become firm; met. to become firmly established in any post or position of authority. --ṭhaharāwun -- m.inf. to make (a person's) foot firm, i.e. to establish or strengthen (a person) in any position of authority. --tulun -- m.inf. to raise the foot, to take a step, to step (--tulanukᵘ sadāh, a sound of a step, a footfall, Gr.M.); esp. to step out, quicken one's pace. --tārun -- m.inf. to cause to go along step by step; met. (in some action) to accomplish by degrees, to cause (something) gradually to advance towards completion. ¶ pūrⁱ trāwȧnⁱ m.pl.inf. to throw forward the feet, i.e. to advance lightly and gently, to walk coquettishly.
m. a small village, a hamlet (cf. nanda-pᵒ, p. 641b, l. 12); a quarter, or portion, of a larger town (cf. kamāngar-pᵒ, p. 445a, l. 40).
m. a kind of cake fried in clarified butter (cf. gāri-pᵒ, p. 298a, l. 6).

m. (cf. pūr 3), the east, the eastern quarter (El. púr; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1412, 1589; Rām. 518); cf. purb. -kun adv. towards the east, eastwards (u.w. vbs. of going, placing, looking, or the like). ¶ pūrⁱ kinⁱ adv. in the eastern quarter, in the east (Rām. 1681). ¶ pūri-kani adv. from the eastern quarter, from the east (Śiv. 692, Rām. 1121). -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. kanicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or produced in, the east. ¶ pūryukᵘ sg. gen. (f. pūricᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or produced in the east or in an eastern country.

adj. (f. pūrᵘ̈, often written pūr), full (cf. atha-pᵒ, p. 61b, l. 5; lĕka-pᵒ, p. 518a, l. 37) (Gr.Gr. 18, 19; Rām. 554); complete, perfect (Śiv. 673, 1211, 1685, 1834; Rām. 33); satisfied (cf. ȧchⁱ-pⁱ, p. 8b, l. 20) (K.Pr. 84); fulfilled, accomplished; entire, whole, total, undivided, undiminished, unbroken, uncut (K.Pr. 239); exact, precise, just, sufficient, enough; true, standard, up to the mark; (of a date, day, night) passed, completed, elapsed (Rām. 560); full (of the moon); cf. pur 2, pūr 2 and pūra. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to complete entirely, to finish thoroughly. -khumār, see pur- khumār, p. 754a, l. 34. --nērun -- m.inf. to turn out to be complete (e.g. when measuring or weighing); to turn out to be thorough (e.g. friendship in the hour of trial). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain complete; to keep a promise or resolve. ¶ pūri dĕna adv. on the full day, at the full time, when the full time is come (esp. with reference to a pregnant woman, or an action completed at the required time). -dĕnukᵘ sg. gen. (f. -dĕnücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the full time (e.g. an action completed up to time, or a child born after the full period of pregnancy).
the form which pōr 1 takes when used as an adjective, as in pönʦa-pūrᵘ, p. 743a, l. 19.
f. manner of walking, gait (cf. kukili-pᵒ, p. 433a, l. 24, and pūrᵘ 1).
f. fullness, completeness, completion; fulfilling, accomplishment; satisfaction, satiety. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. completion to be accomplished.
f. any small thing (esp. a powder) wrapped up in paper or leaves (cf. nāsti-pᵒ, p. 659a, l. 11).

m. (but K. 166 f.), incompleteness, deficiency, insufficiency (K. 1091, K.Pr. 200); non-completion. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. or (K. 166) --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. insufficiency, etc., to happen (to so-and-so), to be found insufficient for a certain purpose (K. 166); non-completion to occur (e.g. in speaking, to stop before one has finished) (Śiv. 1454).

or adj. c.g. that which is needed to complete something incomplete (cf. pushᵘ 3); that which requires completion, that which of a part is missing. --phŏlun -- m.inf. to blossom incompletely; hence, to be not at the height of blossoming or flourishing (but to be still advancing), to blossom or flourish more and more, not to stop blossoming or flourishing (K. 100). --pāwun -- m.inf. to cause to be incomplete or insufficient (Śiv. 28). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to turn out, to be or become, incomplete or insufficient (Śiv. 533, 1597).

f. (sg. dat. pushᵉ̆ṭi), a sandal-strap, a shoe-lace (cf. dĕlⁱ-pⁱ, p. 267b, l. 50; khanjᵃ̇rᵃ̇-pᵃ̇, p. 404a, l. 23). ¶ pushᵉ̆ṭa-dyolᵉ̆ m. the grass from which these straps are woven. ¶ pushᵉ̆ṭᵉ̆-tāla-raz f. a kind of jewelled chain or string of plaited gold or silver fastened to the head as a support for a heavy earring so as to take the weight off the ear.
f. covering, clothing, concealing, used --˚, as in parda-pūshī, p. 756a, l. 47, q.v.
m: (sg. dat. pushpakas), N. of the car of Kubēra, which was carried off from him by Rāvaṇa, and from the latter by Rāma (Rām. 937). In Skt. puṣpaka.

or pushᵉ̆th m. (sg. dat. pushtas), the back (El.); the back (of a chair, etc.) (Gr.M.); the outside; support, prop, assistant; ancestors, progenitors; (in Kāshmīrī) the lower part of the spine, the part of the back about the hips (YZ. 53). pusht-bar-pusht پشت بر پشت adv. back to back (Rām. 920). pusht-ĕ-pā پشتِ پا m. the dorsum of the foot (El.). ¶ pushtukᵘ gen. (f. pushtücᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or relating to, the back, or the parts about the hips. ¶ pushtas rōzun m.inf. to stay at (a person's) back, to stand ready to help.
m. a supporting beam of an upper-story room, projecting outside the main wall of a house, and with open air below it. Cf. pēsh-andāz, p. 777b, l. 45.

f. (sg. dat. pushᵉ̆rüñᵉ̆), making over, granting, entrusting, conveying (Rām. 143); (with regard to something incomplete) the filling up of a deficiency, the adding of something required to cause an increase, the completion of the requirements of some person in need.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pushᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), i.q. pushᵉ̆run, q.v. (Gr.M.); to make over (to a person) (cf. path pᵒ, s.v. path 3) (Rām. 256); to devote (something to a person or thing) (Rām. 181, 664). ¶ pushᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. pushᵉ̆rövᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), i.q. pushᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, see pushᵉ̆run. ¶ pushᵉ̆rövith ʦhunun m.inf., i.q. pushᵉ̆rith ʦhunun, see id.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pushᵒrᵒ), to make up a deficiency, to add something required to cause an increase, to supply the requirements of a person in need; (of means) to be sufficient to complete any work; to supply, make over (to a person) (Gr.M.; Rām. 141, 735); to entrust, consign, give in charge (Gr.M.; Śiv. 483; Rām. 135, 137-8, 509; K. 623, 683, 687, 691, 738, 773, 1006; YZ. 537); to surrender (El.); to devote (a thing to a certain person or purpose) (Gr.M.; L.V. 61, pushĕrun; Śiv. 493; Rām. 151). Cf. pushᵘ 3. ¶ pushᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. pushᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), given or made over to supply a deficiency, as ab.; (of all the requirements for some work) got completely together. ¶ pushᵉ̆ran-wād m. 'a completion-reply', i.e. giving more than is sufficient for completion. ¶ pushᵉ̆rith ʦhunun m.inf. to insist on making something over or on supplying means to an unwilling recipient.
m. (a female garland-maker is pushĕñ or (L.V. 39, 40; Śiv. 1312) pushöñᵘ̈), a man who sells flowers or garlands, a florist, a mālī (El. púsh; L.V. 39, 40; Śiv. 1312).
(for 2, see pōshun) adj. (f. pūshᵘ̈), the form which pōsh 1 takes when used as an adj. --˚, as in pönʦa-pūshᵘ, p. 743a, l. 25.
(cf. پوش) m. a covering, in kala-pᵒ, p. 435a, l. 29.

adj. (f. pushᵘ̈), (with regard to something incomplete) that which is suitable for, or sufficient for, supplying the deficiency, that which renders complete, that which makes up what is wanting. Cf. push, pushĕ, and pushᵉ̆run.

or pūstyulᵘ m. a certain tree, Himalayan spruce (Abies Smithiana, El. pústúl); cf. the preceding. pūstilyukᵘ sg. gen. (pūstilicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or made of this wood (usually of something small). pūstilyuwᵘ adj. (pūstilivᵘ̈), made of this wood (usually of some piece of furniture).
f. a fur garment, a shaggy leathern coat (cf. pakha-pᵒ, p. 725a, l. 32).
f. N. of a female demon who attempted to kill Krushna (Kṛṣṇa), but who was killed by him (Śiv. 1321, 1371, 1381, 1387; K. 105 ff.). This person is also called pūth, q.v.
m. impudent, barefaced, esp. a bare faced swindler. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to swindle in a barefaced way.
f. (sg. dat. pūṭhᵃrüñᵃ), fattening, making fat, nourishing, making prosperous.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pūṭhᵃrôwᵃ), to fatten, make fat, feed up (Gr.Gr. 173); to make (a business) prosper. pūṭhᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. pūṭhᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), fattened, well fed up, well nourished up; (of a business) made prosperous.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pūṭhᵒrᵒ), to fatten, make fat, feed up; to make (a business) prosper. pūṭhᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. pūṭhᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), fattened, well fed up, well nourished up; (of a business) made prosperous.

adj. (sg. f. nom. pūṭhᵘ̈, dat. pōchĕ), stout, plump (K. 636); stout, coarse, thick (cf. nal-pᵒ, p. 631b, l. 44); cf. poṭhᵘ and pōṭhun. -hyuhᵘ adj. (f. pūṭhᵘ̈-hishᵘ̈), very plump, the most plump (of a number of similar persons or things). Cf. vyoṭhᵘ

f. (sg. dat. pōthĕ), a manuscript, a book (cf. burza-pᵒ, p. 131a, l. 3; nĕcha- patri-pᵒ, p. 621a, l. 34; lŏküṭᵘ̈ pᵒ, a small book, a pamphlet, Gr.M.) (Gr.Gr. 24, 41, 46, 60, 115; Gr.M.; K. 955, 1082). pōthi-gara m. or -kuṭhᵘ, m. a book-room, a library (Gr.M.).
in lᵃtulᵃ putulᵘ, p. 538b, l. 9. Another form of pŏtulᵘ, q.v.
in putañĕ ȧchⁱgaʦhañĕ f. pl. inf. the eyes to become weary with looking for someone whose arrival is longed for.

m. the son of a son, (a man or woman's) grandson in the male line (Rām. 611; K. 5, 763). So par-puturᵘ, a great grandson, p. 751b, l. 5. ¶ putᵃ̇rᵃ̇-nŏsh f. such a grandson's wife (K. 832). -sọ̆ñᵘ  m. the father-in-law of a son's son or daughter, a grandson's or grand-daughter's father-in-law. -sŏñĕñ  the mother-in-law of a son's son or daughter, a grandson's or granddaughter's mother-in-law. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who has grandsons, a person who has descendants in the male line for at least two generations.
m. a son (esp. an only son referred to in terms of affection). Cf. pọ̆tᵘ and pūtᵘ.

m. (sg.f. pūʦᵘ̈ 1), the young of a bird, a fledgling, a chick (cf. khisⁱ-pⁱ, p. 429a, l. 11; kŏkar-pᵒ, p. 132a, l. 43, Gr.Gr. 131; kōtar-pᵒ, p. 192a, l. 1, and Gr. Gr. id.; kāwa-pᵒ, p. 495a, l. 28, and Gr.Gr. id.; pachin-pᵒ, p. 679b, l. 38, and Gr.Gr. id.) (Rām. 97; K.Pr. 117, 118, 195); the young of any irrational animal (cf. chira-pᵒ, p. 165a, l. 9; dā̃da-pᵒ, p. 187a, l. 21; gunᵃsa-pᵃ, p. 293a, l. 18; gurⁱ-pⁱ, p. 299a, l. 2; khar-pᵒ, p. 407a, l. 31; kaṭa-pᵒ, p. 487a, l. 17, and Gr.Gr. 131; myā̃-pᵒ, Gr.Gr. 131) (Gr.M.; H. ix, 3 (young of a bee); K.Pr. 104, 166); often used --˚ met. to indicate something small and nice, as in chā̃cĕ-pᵒ (chã̄chĕ- is a misprint), a child's rattle, p. 158a, l. 25; miñe-pᵒ, p. 585a, l. 43, a kiss; mŏñĕ-pᵒ, p. 585b, l. 5, id.; muñĕ-pᵒ, p. 585b, l. 39, id., see also Gr.Gr. 131 and Gr.M.; nila-pᵒ, a kind of pigeon, p. 633b, l. 16; (m.) a son (used --˚ after caste-names and the like) (cf. dara-pᵒ, p. 234b, l. 49, and Gr.Gr. 131; kaula-pᵒ, p. 436a, l. 33, and Gr.Gr. id.; lōla-pᵒ, p. 523a, l. 19; ṭikⁱ-pⁱ, Gr.Gr. 131; ʦūra-pᵒ, id. Cf. chüʦᵘ̈-pᵘ̈, p. 166b, l. 31, and kŏ-pᵒ, p. 464a, l. 47); a son, a true son, a son like his father (K.Pr. 174. In Kashmīr there are said to be three kinds of sons, a pūtᵘ, a son like his father; a sŏpūtᵘ, a good son; and kŏpūtᵘ, a bad son); esp. a worthy son, one who is a credit to his father. In aṭa-pᵒ (p. 53b, l. 12), the name of a child's game, it is not clear whether the word pūtᵘ means 'a chicken' or 'a son'. ¶ pūtⁱ-brörⁱ f. a kind of paddy, with fine, soft, and scented rice-grain, and a white husk with red edges. -khë̆jᵘ̈ f. a procession or line of young birds or chickens. -khash m. beheading a chicken; met. an easy assault on an unresisting person. -kŏkürᵘ̈ f. hen and chickens, a hen surrounded by her chickens; met. a certain disease, in which a large boil is surrounded by a number of others.
m. the part of the body behind the pudenda, the back part of the privities.

f. (sg. dat. pacĕ 2, Gr.Gr. 26, 29, 62; for 1, see s.v.), a small board, a small plank, a lath, a flat piece of wood (cf. bömⁱ-pⁱ, p. 107a, l. 10; dŏsa-yĕndra-pᵒ, p. 252a, l. 48; gālav-pᵒ, p. 286a, l. 36; nigayĕ-pᵒ, p. 625a, l. 35; nāwa-pᵒ, p. 666b, l. 18; ranga-pᵒ, s.v. ranga 2; ringa-pᵒ, s.v. ringa) (El. paṭ; Gr.Gr. 10, 72; Gr.M.; W. 17; Rām. 570); a panel, a door-leaf, or the like (cf. linga-pᵒ, p. 526b, l. 26; phālav-pᵒ, p. 696b, l. 39); a black-board, such as is used in schools or such as is used, like our slate, by children learning to write (cf. dōja-pᵒ, p. 203a, l. 7; mashᵉ̆kᵉ̆-pᵉ̆, p. 597a, l. 35); a board (as a chess-board or drawing-board) (cf. narda-pᵒ, p. 650a, l. 42; rᵃkhᵃ-pᵃ, s.v. rᵃkh) (Śiv. 280); a tablet (cf. rᵃkha-pᵃ, s.v. rᵃkh) (Gr.Gr. 29, 34, 62-3, 162, 213); a long strip of cloth, such as is used in making the body of a coat, a shawl, or the like (cf. jōra-pᵒ, p. 377a, l. 16; khēshĕ-pᵒ, p. 418a, l. 7; pūʦi-pᵒ, s.v. pūʦᵘ̈ 2; rāda-pᵒ, s.v. rād 2); a piece of cloth, such as is used for tying a wound, or applying a medicament, a bandage (cf. ashĕd-pᵒ, p. 49b, l. 9; dīrⁱ-pⁱ, p. 271a, l. 25; drīrⁱ-pⁱ, p. 248a, l. 27) (K.Pr. 258); a bandage over the eyes or the like (cf. achĕn-pacĕ, p. 9a, l. 13) (Rām. 1607); a square piece of cloth, such as a towel, or bathing cloth (K.Pr. 91); a field (in cultivation) (cf. khāha-pᵒ, p. 394a, l. 23); the stigma of the saffron flower (cf. kŏng-pᵒ, p. 456b, l. 20); the empty husk of a grain-plant which, owing to drought, contains no grain (cf. dā̃-pᵒ, p. 230b, l. 33). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to place a bandage over the eyes, to blindfold (Rām. 1184, 1607; cf. pacĕ diñĕ, bel. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a bandage to be applied (to the eyes), blindfolding to occur; met. dislike to be shown to one formerly an object of affection; the habit to occur of refusing help or gifts to applicants. Cf. pacĕ lagañĕ, bel. ¶ pacĕ-baran f. (sg. dat. -barüñᵘ̈), a partition made of thin planks (K.Pr. 240). -chal f. a piece of board (Gr.Gr. 162). -dalav m. the joining together of boards to form a ceiling or the cover of a pit, etc. --diñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to join together boards (to form a roof, ceiling, cover of a pit, or the like); to blindfold oneself (to another), i.e. (of a master, etc.) to experience a feeling of hostility (to a servant, etc.); cf. püṭᵘ diñᵘ̈, ab. -godᵘ m. an opening (or window) in a boarded partition. -godᵘ dyunᵘ m.inf. to build up a boarded partition. -gorᵘ m. a carpenter whose business it is to saw timber into boards. --kūcĕ -- or --kōcĕ -- f.pl. planks and pieces, a pile of planks (ready for building). Although each member of this compound is plural, owing to the whole collective idea being plural, each may be translated as singular, 'a board and a beam' (Gr.Gr. 72). -khŏn m. a bundle of laths (esp. as much as can be carried under the arm). -khünḍᵘ̈ f. a piece of a broken board. -kônᵘ m. a long thin narrow piece of board, a lath (cf. kônᵘ 2). -köñᵘ̈ f. a bundle of laths. --lagañĕ -- f. pl. inf. bandages to be applied, i.q. püṭᵘ̈ lagüñᵘ̈, ab., q.v. -phyurᵘ m. change of lengths of cloth (e.g. of the main pieces of the body of a coat), taking out the worn pieces and substituting others; putting in a new piece (cf. ȧchⁱ- pacĕ-phyurᵘ, p. 9a, l. 17). -tilim f. a small broken piece of board. -tālav m. a boarded ceiling, a ceiling made up of decorated boards or planks. -yẹ̆ndᵃr m. a spinning-wheel made up of two or three laths.
f. a son's daughter, a granddaughter in the male line (a great-grand-daughter is par-pᵒ, q.v., p. 751b, l. 6).

f. the shawl-wool imported from Ladak, pashmīna wool; (according to El.) the thread spun from this wool (púí); cf. pashmīna. -wāl m. when pashmīna wool is imported it is sorted out, and the fine soft portion is taken out for spinning, while the coarser hairs are rejected. These coarser hairs are called by this name. -wôñᵘ m. (his wife is -wāñĕñ f. and the same word is also used for a woman who follows the profession), a seller of this pashmīna wool, or (El.) of the thread made from it. According to El. these men buy from the Kāshmīrī women the thread spun by them from this wool (El. púí-wányí or -wŏin). -wöñⁱ-kār m. the profession of a seller of this wool. -wöñⁱ-wān m. the shop of a seller of shawl-wool or of the thread made of it. -wöñī f. the profession of a seller of shawl-wool thread. -wöñil f. the trade of a seller of shawl-thread. -wāñuth (sg. dat. -wāñĕtas), the profession of a seller of shawl-wool thread. ¶ puyĕ-üṭᵘ̈ f. a skein or hank of shawl-wool thread as spun on the spinning machine. -ganḍ m. a roll or bundle of so many hundred threads of shawl-wool as arranged for weaving, a recognized measure of such thread. -ʦöryunᵘ m. the refuse pashmīna wool, i.q. puy-wāl, ab.
f. offspring, sons and daughters (esp. when there are many). Cf. kŏ-puy, p. 464b, l. 47; nüvᵘ̈ pᵒ, p. 667b, l. 17; pröñᵘ̈ pᵒ, p. 762a, l. 19.

or pūzā f. worship, honour, adoration, respect, homage (cf. dāra-pūz, p. 235b, l. 17; dwāra- pūz or -pūzā, p. 264a, l. 35; dyāna-pūzā, p. 268b, l. 15; pādĕ-pūz, p. 683a, l. 9; pārthī-pūzā, p. 769b, l. 43; pōshĕ-pūz or -pūzā, p. 779a, l. 15; pāṭh- pūzā, p. 794a, l. 4; pīṭha-pūzā, p. 796b, l. 1; pötra- pūz or -pūzā, p. 804a, l. 27; pȧʦhⁱ puzā, p. 808a, l. 2; (L.V. 39, 40; Śiv. pūz, 1180, 1744; pūzā, 52, 112, 187, etc.; K. pūz, 484, 1017; pūzā, 1043-4, 1054, 1069; K.Pr. 29, pūzā). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to do worship or homage (to, dat.), to worship (El.; L.V. 17, 21; Śiv. pūz, 51, 93, 526, 1161-3-5-7, 1175-6, 1181; pūzā, 21, 113, 163, 209, etc.; Rām. pūz, 580, 1640; pūzā, 612; K. pūz, 267, 340, 344, 391, 793, 1068; pūzā, 53, 322, 370, 524, 574, 651, 715, 990 (causal), 1042, 1046). --pālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to complete worship or homage, to do complete worship to (K. pūzā, 337, 1042). ¶ pūzi bĕhanāwun m.inf. to seat (a person) at worship, to set food before a Brāhmaṇ at an obsequial meal. -bata m. the food at an obsequial feast; an obsequial meal. -khāv m. a Brāhmaṇ who habitually eats at obsequial meals. -khyonᵘ m.inf. (of a Brāhmaṇ) to eat an obsequial meal. -khyāwun m.inf. to set food before the Brāhmaṇ at such a meal. -wôlᵘ m. the Brāhmaṇ at such a meal. ¶ pūzāyĕ bĕhun m.inf. to sit down to, i.e. to begin, religious worship; (of the officiating Brāhmaṇ) to sit down to eat the obsequial meal.
m. (sg. dat. pūzakas), one who worships; one who is devoted to continual worship.
m. the performance of ceremonial worship, worship (cf. shiva-pᵒ, s.v. shiv) (L.V. 22; K. 269, 322, 494, 770, 779, 843, 974, 1053).
m. a worshipper; a paid priest who officiates at a shrine.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. pūzᵘ), to worship, offer adoration to (cf. ḍulⁱ pᵒ, p. 212b, l. 24) (Śiv. 11, 863, 1174, 1420; K. 321, 344, 370, 774, 1040-2). pūzᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. pūzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), worshipped, adored; one who is being worshipped or adored.
f. (sg. dat. pūzᵃrüñᵃ), the causing to be worshipped by another.

(cf. pũ̄̈ʦhī and puʦanun) in the following:-- puʦa-pār m. tearing or plucking to pieces (esp. with the finger-nails) (e.g. a piece of cloth or paper, or a flower nipped to pieces, as when this is done for the purpose of collecting the nipped off leaves). -puʦa m. tearing into tiny pieces, as ab.
adj. f. a woman who wears the kind of cloth called pūʦᵘ̈, q.v.
or (q.v.) puʦanan f. (sg. dat. puʦüñᵘ̈), the act of plucking or nipping a flower, or the like, to pieces (leaf by leaf, petal by petal, or the like; e.g. when collecting the leaves or petals).
f. (sg. dat. puʦanüñᵘ̈), i.q. puʦan, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. puʦanôwᵘ), i.q. puʦanun, q.v. puʦanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. puʦanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. puʦonᵘ-motᵘ, s.v. puʦanun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. puʦonᵘ), to tear up, to pluck, or nip with the finger-nails, flowers (or anything similar) to pieces (e.g. when nipping off petals or leaves in order to collect them); cf. puʦa. puʦonᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. puʦüñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), nipped to pieces, as ab.
m. (sg. dat. puʦas), a ball of thread, or the like, as wound up on a spinning-wheel.
in pǖ̃ʦhīkarȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to break or smash (some hard substance) into little pieces. Cf. puʦa. and trᵃs trᵃs trapũ̄̈ʦhī, p. 1030b, l. 9

or puʦhⁱ postpos. (governing abl., or the abl. of the gen.) for, for the sake of, on account of (according to IK. II, i, 63 it is not in frequent use) (cf. ami-pᵒ, p. 55a, l. 8; awa-pᵒ, p. 55b, l. 44; kami-pᵒ, for what? why? Gr.M.; kāmi-pᵒ, for (on) business, Gr.M.; myāni-pᵒ, for me, Gr.M.; shurĕn-murĕn-handi pᵒ, for (your) family, Gr.M.) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 122, 584, 846, 1510, 1670; Rām. 2, 116, 765, 1073, 1361, 1458, 1649; K. 9, 642, 690, 775, 996). With the infinitive it indicates purpose, as in karana-pᵒ, for the purpose of doing, in order to do; wuchana-pᵒ, (desire) to see (Gr.M.).
i.q. pǖnʦᵃh, q.v. See also ǖ̃ʦᵃh pǖ̃ʦᵃh, p. 69b, l. 38, and pawa-pü̃̄ʦᵃh pyonᵘ, s.v. pav.

f. a long piece of cotton cloth thrown over the head and allowed to fall down the back of Musalmān women, the ordinary veil worn by Kāshmīrī females (cf. kōra-pᵒ, p. 466b, l. 27) (El. púts, K.Pr. 169); met. prāñi pūʦi, adv. in the ancient manner, see p. 762a, l. 12. ¶ pūʦa-rād or pūʦi-rād m. a veil-length (the veil is made of two long strips sown together side by side). -wôwurᵘ m. a seller, or maker for sale, of these veils. ¶ pūʦi-bodᵘ m. 'a veil-bundle', a particular way of wearing this veil rolled up. -püṭᵘ̈ f. one half of such a veil, one of the two strips that form it. -rād m. see pūʦa-rād, ab.

m. in the following:-- pyā pyā karun m.inf. (of a helpless baby) to show distress by continued wailing. pyā-prahāray f. (of a sick man or a hungry child) wailing in distress (as a goat does when being led to slaughter).

m. one on foot, a footman (El. piádah; W. 141, piyāda); a foot-soldier (Rām. 1323, 1373, 1435); a peon, a messenger of government, an officer of a court, an apparitor. (These men have in Kashmīr a bad character for tyranny and extortion) (K.Pr. 26, 120). -bukurᵘ m. the gruffness, rudeness, tyranny, overbearing conduct of a peon. -buthᵘ m. 'peon-faced', one who is overbearing or tyrannical like a peon. -buthörᵘ̈ f. the overbearing conduct or tyranny of a peon; tyranny or rudeness like that exercised by a peon. -bāy f. a peon's wife (considered to be usually as over-bearing as her husband). --pata lagun -- m.inf. to follow on close behind the peon, i.e. to incite him to arrest or otherwise maltreat someone against whom a charge is made. --thawȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to set peons, to depute peons to arrest someone. -wān m. the peons' quarters, i.e. the place where they collect and wait till they are deputed on some duty; the occupation or business of a peon. -wānan lagun m. to get into the peons' quarters, to be arrested under government orders and kept in custody. ¶ pyāday adv. on foot (Gr.M.); also (= pyāda), a messenger (H. ii, 12).
f. the wages of a peon, the fee or fine paid to, or extorted by, a peon. Cf. Gr.Gr. 143, suffix way.

m. a drinking vessel, a cup, a glass, a tea-cup (usually of metal) (cf. cīnⁱ-pⁱ, p. 172b, l. 9) (Śiv. 179, 286, 1260, 1327, 1537; Rām. 676, 876, 1456; H. viii, 7; YZ. 343, 512); (esp. among Musulmāns) an earthenware deep circular eating dish. -bardār پیالہ بردار m. a cupbearer, a table-servant, a Ḵẖidmatgār. -bardörⁱ پیالہ بردآری f. the occupation of a cupbearer. --hĕth rōzun -- m.inf. to remain holding a cup, to attend a guest like a table-servant, to show great hospitality to a guest.
m. love, affection, fondness, attachment, friendship. --karun -- m.inf. to love, to fondle, caress.
adj. c.g. beloved, precious, dear, darling; pleasing, agreeable, charming, lovable, winning.
m. lovingness, affectionate conduct, conduct or action intended to produce affection in another.

m. desire to drink, thirst; envious longing. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. thirst to seize a person, to attack a person; envy, envious longing, to seize a person. --wŏthun -- m.inf. thirst to arise; longing for food generally to arise.

(for 2, see prasun) the act of bringing forth offspring, parturition, giving birth (to) (cf. lāwa-pᵒ, p. 541a, l. 23; nö̃ṭha-pᵒ, p. 661b, l. 18; sada-pᵒ, s.v. sada 2); the present sent by her blood-relations to a bride's husband's people on the occasion of her having a child. ¶ pyāwa-bôgᵘ m. the gift sent as above, on the occasion of a birth; the presents given by the husband's people to the family priest, servants, friends, relations, beggars on such an occasion. -lāday f. the sending or presentation of this present by the wife's relations. pyāwa-pyāv m. parturition upon parturition, several births (of human beings or animals) occurring nearly simultaneously in the same house; the having many children.

f. a woman who has just had a child, a lying-in woman (cf. lāwa-pᵒ, p. 541a, l. 25; pīna-pᵒ, p. 737a, l. 18) (H. xi, 7; K.Pr. 252); (among a number of women) anyone who has borne a child; met. (of the tongue) inventive, imaginative, lying (K.Pr. 175).
f. the fee paid to the doctor, midwife, nurse, etc., who attend a confinement; the festivities on the occasion of a child's birth (cf. lāwa-pᵒ, p. 541a, l. 27).
f. a woman who has borne a child, used --˚ as in sada-pyāy (s.v. sada 2; L. 258 sadh piai), a woman who has recently borne her first child. Cf. prasun and pyāv 1.
f. the profession or conduct of a peon; met. evil conduct, wickedness, oppression, lying, and cheating (K.Pr. 46).
adj. (f. pë̆zᵘ̈ 2, for 1, see pĕd), familiar with affairs (esp. with other people's affairs), knowing (cf. atha-pᵒ, p. 61b, l. 47). Cf. pĕdun.

m. (sg. dat. pĕlis), a testicle (El. pyúl) (Gr.Gr. 25, 26). ¶ pĕlⁱ-bār  m. the burden of a testicle, used in cursing (quasi, when a person who has been cheated or deceived curses the offender and wishes that he may carry as a crest-ornament a human or equine testicle on his head). -duka f.pl. a pair of testicles (cf. dukh 2). -ganḍ m. binding the testicles (as a punishment done to man or beast). -koḍᵘ m. one who has his testicles torn off, a castrated animal, a eunuch. --kaḍȧnⁱ -- m. pl.inf. to castrate, capon. -vĕchĕr m. large size of the testicles. -vyoṭhᵘ m. one whose testicles are large (naturally), or enlarged (by disease or otherwise).
