. The fifteenth (or, if we count the aspirates ch, kh, and ph as separate letters, the eighteenth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character. It is the twenty-seventh (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the thirtieth) consonant when written in the Śāradā or the Nāgarī character, and the fifteenth consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. ¶ In the language of educated persons of the City, this letter is sounded much as in India, but is more dental than in the central portion of the Ganges Valley, where the sound is classed as cerebral. In Kāshmīr, on the contrary, the sound is dental, and in village talk and in old poetry is not unfrequently interchangeable with that of a dental l. This fact is recognized by the Paṇḍits of the City, who have a stock phrase, ra-layōr aikyatā, signifying that r and l are identical in nature. In the modern speech of the educated, the two letters are nevertheless distinguished both in sound and in writing. On the other hand, in the old Kāshmīrī of L.V. 74, we find chōr, a torrent, where the modern language has chūl; and, similarly, in H. viii, 13, we find the literary word môlᵘ, a father, pronounced mōr by Hātim, the rustic narrator of the story. Cf. also such pairs as ludr and rudr, both names of the god Śiva. ¶ In the village dialect r is often sounded something like the cerebral ṛ of India. This latter sound is not formally recognized in the literary language by the use of any special character, so that, e.g. from the spelling of the word it is impossible to say whether a villager would say kūrᵘ̈ or kūṛᵘ̈. Paṇḍits do, however, implicitly admit the existence of this cerebral ṛ-sound by writing in certain words the letter ḍ, while, in attempting to illustrate the village pronunciation of the same word, they write r, the r in this case representing the cerebral sound. Thus, for their own dialect, they write kaḍun, to drag out, while, for the village dialect, they write karun, meaning thereby kaṛun. Similarly they write the literary ʦhāḍun, to seek, but for the village dialect they write ʦhārun. Again, in the literary language, they have both garun and gaḍun, to make, in which the r of garun represents the ṛ of the village gaṛun. This cerebralization of r is not uniform even in the village dialect, the sound varying from place to place, and sometimes, even in villages, we hear ḍ, not ṛ, where the literary dialect has r. Thus, the literary word kūrᵘ̈, a girl, is pronounced kūḍᵘ̈ in the country near Bārāmūla, where, according to El., s.v. kúḍ, 'there is a great tendency to change r into ḍ.' In the present work, which deals only with the literary, or standard, form of the language, the spelling of the Paṇḍits is followed, but, when their spelling of the village sounds is known, it is also given. Many instances of the interchange between ḍ and ṛ will be found in H., pp. lxxix ff. ¶ It is well known that, unlike the Indo-Aryan languages, but like the other Dardic languages, Kāshmīrī has no hesitation in preserving unchanged an original conjunct consonant of which the second member is r. Thus, we have brỗtᵘ, error, compared with the Skt. bhrānti-; grônᵘ, an eclipse, for Skt. grahaṇa-; phryūstᵘ, excellent, for Skt. praśasta-; trih, three, for Skt. tri-, and many others. Similarly, even when there was no original conjunct, we find such words as drölid, Skt. daridra-, poor; drôtᵘ, Skt. dātra-, a sickle; dryuyᵘ, Skt. dēvara-, a brother-in-law; kronḍᵘ, Skt. karaṇḍa-, a basket; krāl, Skt. kulāla-, a potter; krĕhonᵘ, Skt kr̥ṣṇa-, black; trēsh, Skt. tr̥ṣṇa-, thirst; shrān, Skt. snāna-, bathing; shrūkh, Skt. ślōka, a verse; shrōtsun, to become pure, Skt. √śudh-, trām, copper, Skt. tāmra-, and so on. There are several words in which the insertion of such a conjunct r is optional, the form with r being chiefly used by Hindūs, and that without r being chiefly used by Musalmāns. Such are brō̃ṭh or bō̃ṭh, in front; shrāṭh or shāṭh, a river shoal; and zrôḍᵘ or zôḍᵘ, a water-hole. drē̃ṭh or ḍē̃ṭh, sight; srọ̆gᵃñār or sọ̆gᵃñār, cheapness ¶ In schools, this letter, in the Śāradā character, whether standing by itself or the first member of a conjunct consonant is called raka rö. If it is the final member of a conjunct, as in the syllable kra, it is called dutarikh. ¶ The Sanskrit vowel r̥ sometimes appears in Kāshmīrī writing, in borrowed words. It is said to be pronouuced as ru, as in krupunᵘ, niggardly, written, in imitation of the Skt. kr̥paṇaḥ; but, especially at the beginning of a word, or in the case of words in common use, the character signifies the sound of rĕ, and is used optionally as a method of indicating that sound. In such cases it is written, as in rĕth, a month; krĕhonᵘ, black; rĕy, written or, an ant. This rĕ is liable to the ordinary rules of epenthesis, so that when followed by u-mātrā, it is liable to be sounded as ryo or ryu. Thus, a saint, is pronounced ryoshᵘ, ryushᵘ, or even as rĕshᵘ. The sg. dat. is, however, always rĕshis, because here there is no epenthesis. So, a tortoise, is pronounced krümᵘ̈, while the same word, with another spelling , is pronounced krum. ¶ Whether initial or non-initial, in schools, the Skt. letter is called rĕnav rĕ, and the corresponding long vowel-sign is called rᵃkhav rᵘ̈ or rūkhav rū. ¶ The Śāradā letter corresponding to the Nāgarī ru is called rukharī rō, and that corresponding to the Nāgarī rū is called rā ar kharã̄ rṻ.

adj. c.g. rejected, thrown away, worthless, trashy; in the following:-- rȧdⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to become rejected, thrown away, worthless, no longer of any use. --karun -- m.inf. to render worthless, make waste of, deprive of all usefulness.

(f. -düzᵘ̈), 'having the arteries burnt,' i.e. (owing to inflammation of the throat) hoarse. --khĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. 'to eat the veins', i.e. (in a fight) to scratch an opponent's throat with the finger-nails. --maga -- f.pl. (a jingle of raga) the fine veins (or sinews) of the throat; the blood-vessels of the throat windpipe and gullet as a whole. -pāshĕ f.pl. the mutual criticism common among blood-relations; the concord or mutual good understanding between blood-relations. -pāshĕ kaḍañĕ f. pl. inf. criticizing details or finding fault with one's blood-relations. -pāshĕ nērañĕ f. pl. inf. (in any undertaking) criticism of details or blood-relations or qualities to become manifest. -pay m. the clue of the veins; hence, the union or junction of veins, nerves, or sinews. -pay kaḍun m.inf. 'to pull out the clue of the nerves', i.e. to inquire minutely into some hidden circumstance or for some hidden thing. -pay nērun m.inf. 'the clue of the nerves to become visible', i.e. to ascertain by minute investigation the facts of any hidden circumstance or thing.

m. a descendant of Raghu (see ragu), esp. Rāma-candra (Śiv. 1421).
adj. c.g. marked with a line of alien colour (and thereby flawed) (e.g. a flaw in a precious stone, or a black line on white cloth, and so on) (see rag).

m. N. of a celebrated king of India of the solar dynasty, the son of Dilīpa, and ancestor of Rāma-candra. -nandan m. the son (i.e. descendant) of Raghu, a title of Rāma-candra (Śiv. 1421). -nāth m. the Lord (descended from) Raghu, a title of Rāma-candra (Śiv. 1421).

m. a fault, sin, crime (K.Pr. 81, 117); fruitless exertion (cf. padi-rᵒ, p. 681b, l. 45). --khārun -- m.inf. to bring a charge of a fault, to accuse. --khasun -- m.inf. a charge of a fault to be brought. --ladun -- m.inf. to bring a charge of a fault, to accuse (Rām. 1230, H. v, 9); to destroy (K.Pr. 121).
m. N. of a Daitya, or demon, who is supposed to seize the sun and moon and thus cause eclipses (L.V. 22, Śiv. 1125); (in astronomy) the ascending node (K. 130); a falling star (El.).
f. a road, way, path; a course of conduct (bad-rāh بدراہ adj. c.g. one who follows an evil course, bad, wicked); az rāh-ĕ-jangal از راہِ جنگل on the road to the forest (Rām. 201)॑.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. rāhaladiñ), the person (out of many) found guilty of a fault or crime.

m. (sg. dat. rāhatas), rest, peace, quiet (El.; L. 462; H. ix, 4; YZ. 8; K.Pr. 218); happiness, comfort (Rām. 1507, K.Pr. 86); rāhat-ĕ-jān راحتِ جان m. comfort of the soul, balm of life (K.Pr. 50, 153). --sān -- adv. quietly (El.).
f. a pass or permit for use on a journey or for transporting goods, a passport (Gr.M.); esp. permission (formerly necessary) to leave Kashmīr (L. 215, 434).
rahᵃmath m. (sg. dat. rahmatas), mercy, compassion, pity.

or (L.V.) ruhun m. (sg. dat. rahanas or rahnas), garlic, Allium sativum (according to El., s.v. ruhun, in Kashmīr eaten by Musalmāns, but not by Hindūs) (L.V. 89, 90; K.Pr. 26, 80). ¶ rahna-ongujⁱ 'a garlic- finger', encouraging in bad conduct, esp. encouraging a child in naughtiness. -dĕl m. the skin of the garlic-root; a very closely woven cloth (so close that the threads can hardly be seen). -gŏgȧjⁱ f. a clove of garlic. -kujⁱ f. the garlic plant. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. the root of the garlic plant; a cake of pounded garlic cooked in oil. -phakh m. (sg. dat. -phakas), the stink of garlic.
(cf. رہزن) m. (f. rahzüñᵘ̈), a highwayman, footpad, robber (YZ. 11 rahzan; K.Pr. 30, 212); (in Ksh.) a scoundrel, blackguard, malevolent fellow (Rām. 87 rahazun).

or rahm رحم m. mercy, pity, compassion, humanity (cf. bē-rᵒ, p. 121b, l. 5) (Gr.M., K.Pr. 133). -dil رحم دل adj. c.g. tender-hearted, humane, gentle (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to show compassion (Gr.M.). ¶ rahma-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), cruel, pitiless (El. rahmrust).
m. the sweet basil (Ocymum pilosum, El.). (Cf. ban-rᵒ, p. 114a, l. 41.)
or rön m. the name of a caste (Gr.Gr. 22).
m. (sg. dat. raiwatas), N. of the father of Rēvatī, in Skt. Raivata (K. 635); N. of a mountain near Dvārakā (K. 837).
m. (sg. dat. raiyĕtas), m. a subject (of a king) (Gr.M.); a tenant.
f. a halter (for hanging with) (El.). The same as raz, q.v.

m. a king, sovereign (Rām. 213, 874, 1125, 1534, 1588; K. 133, 569; H. x, 7, 8, 14; xi, 2); cf. rāza 1. -bāy f. a king's wife, a queen-consort (K. 1166). -koṭᵘ m. a king's son, a prince. -zāda راجہ زادہ m. a king's son, a prince (Rām. 1128, 1493; H. xi, 7).
or (q.v.) röñᵘ̈ f. a king's wife, a queen-consort (Gr.Gr. 39; Śiv. 472, 1175).
m. a black or dirty mark in cloth or the like. Cf. rag, rolᵘ.
m. (sg. dat. rājatas), the business of a king, kinghood, kingship (Rām. 174, 364, 1002).

or rāj m. royalty, sovereignty, rule, reign (cf. aṭala-rᵒ, p. 67b, l. 38) (L.V. 12, 62; Śiv. 677, 680, 704, 1012, 1483, 1715; Rām. 5, 92, 100, 174, 275, 306, 365, 1143c; K. 540, 550, 552, 623, 625; K.Pr. 9, 105, 134); a kingdom, dominions (Rām. 91, 170, 830; K. 22, 466, 590, 764, 1027, 1029, 1036). --karun -- m.inf. to do sovereignty, to rule (K. 539, 543, 633, 754, 791, 794; H. x, 14). -tāj m. royalty, sovereignty; power, great wealth, affluence, dominion. ¶ rājĕs āsun m.inf. to be for ruling, to rule, be a king (K. 622, 635).
m. the name used in schools for the Śāradā letter corresponding to the Nāgarī ra.
(cf. رکاکت, an accusation) f. calumny, detraction, backbiting, as in the preceding.
adj. c.g. one who habitually looks out for faults in others and then publishes them abroad, censorious, backbiting, a detractor.

(? cf. راخ) m. secret opposition or points of difference (among friends, partners, or the like). --bōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to ascertain the secret points of difference, as ab.; hence, to distinguish between apparent equals. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. opposition to arise between closely connected persons.
m. (i.q. rakhᵃth 1, q.v.), fine clothes and ornaments, adornment of the body with fine clothes, jewelry, etc., festival garments and array.

adj. c.g. red (i.q. rakhᵃth 2, q.v.), in the following:-- -ʦandun m. (sg. dat. -ʦandanas), red sandal. -ʦandan-hüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -hacĕ), a block or piece of red sandal wood. -ʦandan-mỗkun m. (sg. dat. -mỗkanas), a small round piece of red sandal wood kept for rubbing down into sandal powder; see mỗkun. -ʦandan-ṭyokᵘ m. a tilak, or sectarial mark, worn on the forehead and made of red sandal wood; one whose forehead is so marked.
f. grazing land reserved for the king's cattle (Śiv. 1013; H. x, 5, 12).
or rākhĕsgī f. the condition, or conduct, of a demon. See rākhyusᵘ (cf. brahma-rᵒ, p. 120b, l. 50, and p. 121a, l. 2).
rakhĕpāl, or rakshĕpāl m. protection, protecting, guarding (rakhiᵒ, Śiv. 315, 354; rakhĕᵒ, Rām. 1769; rakshĕᵒ, Śiv. 202, 391, 664).

or rākhyusᵘ m. (sg. dat. rākhĕsas or (wrongly) rākhisis; pl. nom. rākhĕs (Śiv. 214)) m. (f. rākhĕsañ. This word is the true Ksh. form of rākshĕs, q.v., the latter being the Skt. form), a demon, evil spirit, goblin (cf. brahma-rᵒ, p. 121a, l. 3) (Śiv. 214, 323; Rām. 30, 60, 62, 101, 103, 108, 376, 380, 457, 906, etc.; K. 13, 55, 68-9, 82, 194, 224, 226, 558, 760, 999, etc.). ¶ rākhĕs-bāy f. a rākṣasa lady, a female demon (Rām. 620). -prakrĕth f. a demon's nature (Rām. 366). -wāsanā f. a demon's wish, a demon's intention (Rām. 847).

(cf. رخت) m. (sg. dat. rakhtas), fine clothes and ornaments, festal array (of the person) (i.q. rakh 1). --karun -- m.inf. to make fine clothes, to dress (oneself or another) in fine apparel. -rēz m. covered with fine clothes and ornaments on every limb.
adj. c.g. red, (i.q. rakh 2) in the following:-- -bīz m. N. of a demon killed by Dēvī (in Skt. Raktabīja) (Śiv. 112). rakta-ʦandun m. (sg. dat. -ʦandanas), red sandal (i.q. rakh-ʦᵒ, s.v. rakh 2).

adj. c.g. commingled, mixed or united together. -mila adj. c.g. mixed up together (of a number of small things, such as different kinds of grain, different earths, different threads, different kinds of cotton, and so on); (of a work) done jointly, done in co-operation, done in collusion.
n.ag. (f. ralavüñᵘ̈), that which is being intimately commingled; one who is becoming on close terms of intimacy; that which is suitable for being mixed (with something).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ralyōv), to be mixed intimately (with something), to be commingled, to get mixed up (with); (of persons) to be associated (with), be on close intimate terms (with) (by friendship, love, relationship, propinquity, partnership, confederacy, collusion, or the like) (Śiv. 1570). ¶ ralan-hār c.g. suitable for being mixed up (with something) (i.e. so like the other that, when mixed, they cannot be distinguished). -sār adj. c.g. mixed up (with) or being mixed up (with), or suitable for being mixed up (with), etc., as under ralun. ralan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), that which is becoming intimately commingled, as ab.; one who is becoming on close terms of intimacy, as ab.; that which is being suitably commingled, or is suitable for being commingled.

m. N.P.; esp. the name of three celebrated heroes of Hindū story, viz. (1) Paraśu-rāma or Bhārgava-rāma, the sixth incarnation of Viṣṇu. See bārgava-rᵒ, p. 120b, l. 10. (2) Rāma-candra also (see bel.) called Rāma-bhadra. He was the seventh incarnation of Viṣṇu, was the husband of Sītā and the hero of the great Skt. epic, the Rāmâyaṇa. His story is told in the Kāshmīrī language in the Śrī-Rāmâvatāra- carita of the poet Divākara-prakāśa Bhaṭṭa, quoted in this dictionary as 'Rām.' (3) Bala-rāma, who, according to some, was an incarnation of the serpent-god Śēṣa, and according to others the eighth incarnation of Viṣṇu. He was the seventh son of Vasudēva and Dēvakī, but before birth was transferred to the womb of Rōhiṇī in order to save him from the cruelty of Kaṁsa. He was the elder brother of Kṛṣṇa, who was himself the eighth incarnation of Viṣṇu. He was also called Haladhara, or the plough-bearer, see hal 1, p. 330a, l. 8, and K. 46 ff. ¶ (1) For Paraśu-rāma, see Śiv. 860; Rām. 140. (2) For Rāma-candra, see Śiv. 540-1, 701, 860, 863, 701, 734, 737, 852, 863, etc.; Rām. 1, 66, 36, 56, 87, 92, 103, 390, 501, 874, et passim; K. 27, 81. (3) For Bala-rāma, see K. 46, 127, 225, 234, 255, 310, 399, 406, 445, 463, 477, et passim. rām-bạdᵃr m. Rāma-bhadra, another name of Rāma-candra (see ab.). -bạdᵃrüñᵃdūñᵃ f. the bow of Rāma-bhadra, i.e. Rāma-candra, i.e. a rainbow, also called rāma-rām-bạdᵃrüñᵃ dūñᵘ̈. (L. 463, Rám Rám badrin dún) in Skt. literature, it is called 'Indra-dhanu', or the bow of Indra. ¶ rāma-autār m. Rāma, the incarnation (of Viṣṇu), i.e. Rāma-candra (Rām. 48, 125, 341, 500, etc.). -goḍᵘ m. a kind of jar filled with walnuts and other fruit, offered on the festival of the Śiva-rātri. -göḍᵘ̈ f. a certain kind of fish found in springs, said to have a red snout and a long thin body. It is caught in the Jehlam. When the water becomes cold, it retires to the lakes and morasses (L. 158, ramah-gad). -gurun m. (sg. dat. -guranas), another kind of fish. -hūnᵘ  m. (f. -hūñᵘ̈), a wolf (Canis Lupus) (L. 110; W. 21; YZ. 92, 129, 416; K.Pr. 63); the wild dog (Cyon rutilans, Cyon dukhunensis) (L. 110); the snow leopard (L. 461, rámahun). -rādan m. N. of a sacred place in the Lār Pargana of Kashmīr, from which the ascent on the Haramukha pilgrimage is made. See R.T.Tr. iii, 467 (Śiv. 1176, 1409, 1595, 1618, 1890; Rām. 243). rāma-rām bạdᵃrüñᵃ dūñᵘ̈ f., see rām-bạdᵃrüñᵃ dūñᵘ̈, ab. -ʦakul m. (sg. dat. -ʦakalas), a circular piece (esp. of leather). -ʦandr m. Rāma-candra, see ab. (Śiv. 740, 1490, 1758; Rām. 111, 135, 153, 337, 1119, 1390, 1483, et passim).
n.ag. (f. ramavüñᵘ̈), one who is adorned, one who is glorious, beautiful, charming (K. 59). Cf. rambun, ramun, and rambawunᵘ.
m. N. of the ninth of the Arabian months, the Muslim Lent, during which Musalmāns fast in the day time (K.Pr. 204).
or rama m. (of a horse) a buck, a rear, a sudden jib (in order to throw its rider) (cf. potᵘ rᵒ, p. 787b, l. 22). --karun -- m.inf. to buck, jib (in order to throw the rider).

f. (of a person) fine array, handsome clothes, elegance, beauty (Gr.Gr. 127); (in a work or business) deftness, skilfulness (cf. atha-rᵒ, p. 62a, l. 13). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. elegance to come (to a person), to become elegant, to find oneself in fine array; to become deft, skilled (in any action).

m. consideration, thought, meditation (on what should be done). --karun -- m.inf. to do considering, as ab.; (when engaged on any course of conduct, good or bad, and unexpectedly finding oneself in the presence of a superior) out of respect to refrain from one's object.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. rambanôwᵘ), to cause to be beautiful, etc. Causal of rambun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 175).
f. a woman in charming array; a woman charming by her conduct, speech, or actions.

or ramawunᵘ n.ag. (f. rambavüñᵘ̈), (a person) who is charming by being at once finely dressed and virtuous, one who is dignified and perfectly conducted; (of a thing or action) that which is beauteous, or perfectly made, that which is dexterously performed (Rām. 187, 1188, 1346; K. 423).

or ramun conj. 3 (2 p.p. rambyōv), (of a person) to be adorned (both by fine garments and by fine virtues), to be dignified and perfectly conducted (Gr.Gr. 127, 175); (of a thing or action) to be perfectly made or performed; to be charmingly excellent. The causal of this verb is rambanāwun (Gr.Gr. 175).
f. a metal ladle (for serving food, or the like).
i.q. rambun, q.v.; also, to be pleased, delighted; to play, sport, amuse oneself; to remain, stay, abide (K. 509).
cookery, cooking, in rana-pĕv f. a falling (quasi, a torrent or avalanche) of cooking, a great cooking (of many articles and varieties of food by many persons).

f. (sg. dat. rāni, or, according to some, röñᵘ̈), the thigh (cf. māz-rᵒ, p. 614b, l. 50; potᵘ-rᵘ, p. 787b, l. 27; sinⁱ-rān, s.v. syunᵘ) (Gr.Gr. 10). rāni-hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the thigh (e.g. the thigh-bone, flesh of the thigh, disease of the thigh, and so on).
f. (sg. dat. ranüñᵘ̈), the act of cooking, cooking, cookery.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. rananôwᵘ), to cause to be cooked, to cause to cook. Cf. ranāwun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ranôwᵘ), to cause to cook (El. possible incorr. for rananāwun, which would be the regular form, see Gr.Gr. 170 ff.).
m. in band-rand, p. 111a, l. 32. Apparently a jingle.
f. a woman whose husband is dead, a widow (esp. one who is rendered destitute by her condition).

m. a carpenter's plane (El. randah, Gr.M.). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to plane (a board), to make smooth; to repeat something heard, or a story, over and over again (as a plane goes backwards and forwards). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to plane (a board), make smooth; to bring (a person) to order (by abuse, entreaty, punishment, etc.); to clean (cotton of its seeds), to card cotton. --koḍᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --küḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), planed smooth; brought to order; (of cotton) carded; sought for in every direction, and by going over long and difficult ways.
f. a narrow strip or slip of cloth. --wālañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to tear into long narrow strips.
f. the order of preparing the cooking of the various courses of a dinner or the like.
m. a long strip of leather, a long leather strap or rope (cf. randa 2).
adj. (f. randücᵘ̈), one who habitually wanders about causelessly or without motive (badly dressed, barefoot, etc.) (cf. randa 1).
or randr m. a hole, aperture (cf. brahm-rᵒ, p. 121a, l. 8) (Śiv. 1654).
or m. the condition of having a deformed or maimed hand (see ronᵘ 1).

m. colour, colouring matter, pigment, paint, dye (cf. ölici-rᵒ, p. 23b, l. 46; ariñĕ-rᵒ, p. 44a, l. 38; asmönⁱ-rⁱ, p. 50a, l. 36; bē-rang, p. 125a, l. 8; gīri-rᵒ, p. 297a, l. 11; hāka-rᵒ, p. 326b, l. 29; kôphura-rᵒ, p. 464a, l. 13; nābȧdⁱ-rⁱ, p. 619b, l. 50) (Gr.Gr. 123, 148; Gr.M.; W. 120; Śiv. 10, 55, 344, 359, 445, 877, 1047, 1258, 1543, 1566, 1893; Rām. 397, 403, 1043; YZ. 96); the colour (of something), a distinguishing feature, that which suggests points of resemblance or non-resemblance (cf. diwạyĕ-rᵒ, p. 265b, l. 26; hapa-rᵒ, p. 324a, l. 22); colour, tint, hue, complexion (cf. hiyĕ-rᵒ, p. 363a, l. 35; shĕb-rᵒ, s.v. shĕb; shukla-rᵒ, s.v. shukl) (Gr.M., Rām. 199; K.Pr. 12, 220); mode, manner, method (cf. phulayĕ-rᵒ, p. 697b, l. 43; pōshĕ-rᵒ, p. 779a, l. 18; pönʦi-rᵒ, p. 743b, l. 23) (Śiv. 1267, 1522); form, appearance (cf. shĕwa-rᵒ, s.v. shĕv) (Śiv. 469, 618, 834, 849, 1366, 1522; Rām. 343); fashion, style; state, condition, state of affairs (Śiv. 879, 1103, 1704; Rām. 1074, 1351); kind, sort (cf. prath ranga, p. 769a, l. 52) (L.V. 84-5); feeling, emotion (Śiv. 771); a theatre, stage; a theatrical entertainment (L.V. 81; Rām. 1412, 1420, 1452); sport, entertainment, amusement, a public assembly for such (K.Pr. 76, 259); a remarkable sight, something wonderful (Rām. 523); merriment, pleasure, enjoyment, high festival; a great crowd of people (such as assembles at a festival), the scene of a festival (Śiv. 89); a field of battle. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to dye (El.). -gāsa m. Panicum miliaceum (El. rang-ghás). --gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. colours to happen; met. to experience a wretched condition. -khrāv m. painted wooden clogs. -kalam m. a colour-pen, i.e. a paint brush; a coloured pen, a penholder ornamented with colours. -küñᵘ̈ f. a colour-stone, a stone slab on which colours are ground (cf. ranga-ṭulᵘ, bel.). --karȧnⁱ -- m. inf. pl. to do play-acting; to play a part, coquet, dissemble. --lagun -- m.inf. colour to be applied, to be painted in colour; a theatrical entertainment to be performed (on some special occasion); a great crowd to assemble; a festival or joyful occurrence to happen. --lāgun -- m.inf. to apply colour, to colour, paint; to pretend to faint, to fall down in a pretended fit. -rich (? spelling), a certain medicinal plant, the seeds of which are used as an emetic (L. 75, rangarichh). -rāwul m. the Simla horned pheasant (L. 120). ¶ ranga 1 adv. and postpos. (governing abl.), for, for the sake (of), on account (of) (as in cyāni rᵒ, for thy sake; ami rᵒ, on this account; khĕna rᵒ, on account of eating); in (such-and-such) a manner or kind (cf. aki rᵒ, p. 20a, l. 50; ami rᵒ, p. 55a, l. 9; amiy rᵒ, p. 55b, l. 5; and so on; aki-rᵒ, in one manner; dŏyi-rᵒ, in two ways; trĕyi-rᵒ, in three ways, and so on; sāsi-rᵒ, s.v. sôsᵘ; sāri-rᵒ, in every way; yĕʦi-rᵒ, in many ways; sĕṭhāhi-rᵒ, in many ways) (Gr.Gr. 154; Gr.M.; K. 372); as adv., with pleasure, joyfully, zealously. -bulbul m. a kind of small bird, described as having a black head, yellow wings, and a long tail (Śiv. 1025, 1046). -būmi  f. a stage, theatre; an arena, wrestling ground (K. 372). -dūjᵘ̈ f. a blackboard used as a slate (see dūjᵘ̈, p. 203a, l. 1) and ornamented in various colours. -ḍṻs m. a painted cudgel. -lürᵘ̈  f. a wooden house of which the walls are painted in colours; a house built of burnt bricks (cf. -sīrᵘ̈, bel.). -manḍul m. (sg. dat. -manḍalas), a stage, theatre; an arena, wrestling ground (K. 433). -më̆ʦᵘ̈ f. jeweller's rouge. -maz (? spelling and gender) a kind of coloured paper used for packing purposes (L. 380). -pholᵘ m. a round piece of mineral suitable for being ground down to powder for making paint; a smart boy (who takes delight in astonishing other people). -püṭᵘ̈ f. a painted wooden board; a dyed cloth. --ranga -- adj. c.g. (of several persons or things) each of a different colour; each of a different kind (Śiv. 1075, 1180, 1185, 1203, 1820; K. 220). --rĕwawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. -rĕwavüñᵘ̈), one who is accustomed joyfully and energetically to assist in another person's festivities. -sīrᵘ̈ (pl. nom. -sērĕ) f. a (burnt) brick, a brick which has been burnt in a kiln (cf. -lürᵘ̈, ab.).-ṭulᵘ m. a small round stone held in the hand for grinding colours on a slab, a muller (cf. rang-küñᵘ̈, ab.). -thürᵘ̈ f. a painted shrub, a coloured picture of a shrub; met. a beautiful, young, and graceful woman. -ṭĕvürᵘ̈ f. 'a colour-damsel', i.e. a conceited girl, good-looking and finely dressed. -ṭyongᵘ m. a dandy, fop, coxcomb. -ʦhōṭa m. a painted walking-stick; a short piece of stick for grinding colours. -ʦolᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüjᵘ̈), that of which the colour has fled, faded; (of a festival or the like) spoiled (e.g. by weather or other impediments). -ʦĕngañ f. anything feminine (rational or irrational being, thing, condition, or the like) which is rendered charming by pictures, colouring, graceful motion, or the like. -ʦürᵘ̈ f. a certain small sparrow-like bird (described as of several colours); a pheasant (El. rangatsur). -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is accustomed to put on pretended graceful airs in everything he does, affected, full of affectation. -wörᵘ̈ f. a saucer, or cup, for holding paint; N. of a village near the ancient shrine of Śāradā in the Kishĕngangā Valley (RT.Tr. II, 280); N. of a place near Śrīnagar, on the south side of the Hāra-parbuth (p. 344a, l. 44). It is the traditional home of the ancient king Raṇâditya, and hence, by folk tradition, its name is wrongly connected with his; cf. rǖnⁱ-wôrⁱ, p. 835b, l. 40. -yẹ̆ndᵃr m. a painted spinning-wheel. ¶ rangā-rang رنگا رنگ adj. pl. c.g. (of many persons or things), each of a different colour, each of a different kind (Śiv. 1727). -rȧngⁱ adj. c.g., id.
adj. c.g. of (such-and-such) a colour, used --˚ (cf. gīri-rᵒ, p. 297a, l. 12; nīli-rᵒ, p. 670b, l. 37; shāmi-rᵒ, s.v. shômᵘ), so har-ranga, adj. every kind of (K.Pr. 77).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ranganôwᵘ), i.q. rangun, q.v. (cf. buthᵘ rᵒ, p. 142a, l. 12).
f. a she-dyer, a woman who works as a dyer (Gr.Gr. 39); a dyer's wife. Cf. rangᵃr and rangur.
f. (sg. dat. rangüʦᵘ̈), colouring, colouredness, tint, hue; bright colouring, gaudiness; (of an occupation) the quality of producing emotion or affection, soul-stirringness.
f. N. of a certain sweet-smelling flower (described as dark yellow in colour).
f. a dyer's wages or remuneration.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. rangowᵘ), i.q. rangun, q.v. (cf. buthᵘ rᵒ, p. 142a, l. 13).
adj. c.g. coloured, bright, gay, showy.
adj. c.g. a sharp, intelligent, scape-grace boy.
m. artful, or cunning, sport, a practical joke; N. of a village to the north of Kashmīr.
adj. c.g. coloured, painted; fine, showy, gaudy.
f. the being coloured, the being of various colours, variegated; bright colouring, gaudiness; variableness, variety.
f. ? a manner of walking, gait. Only noted in kakav-rangishⁱ, p. 433a, l. 5, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. rongᵘ, f. rünjᵘ̈), to colour, stain, dye, tinge, paint (cf. atha rangȧnⁱ, p. 62a, l. 16; buthᵘ rangun, p. 142a, l. 12) (Gr.Gr. 123, YZ. 79). rongᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. rünjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), coloured, painted, dyed.

m. (f. rangᵘ̈rᵘ̈ is a woman who lives by dyeing), i.q. rangᵃr, q.v. (cf. basta-rᵒ, p. 135a, l. 50). ¶ rangȧrⁱ-bāpār m. a dyer's business. -kǖ̃ḍᵘ m. a dyer's pot (containing dye-water which is boiled with cloth, etc., to be dyed). -khum or -khumb m. a dyer's vat (for storing liquid dye, or for dyeing cloth). -wān m. a dyer's workshop, a dyery (W. 114 rangạrwāṇ).

m. (the f. is rangarĕñ), which means either a dyer's wife or a female dyer; see also -bāy, bel. Cf. rangur) a dyer (El. rangur; Gr.Gr. 39, 148; W. 18, 114, rangur). According to El. he is generally a Musalmān. -bāy f. a dyer's wife. ¶ rangᵃ̇rᵃ̇-wŏrsa m. 'a dyer's death-commemoration ('urs)', the publishing of false news about anyone.
adj. c.g. i.q. ranga 2, q.v. of (such-and-such) a colour (cf. gīri-rᵒ, p. 297a, l. 12; shāma-rᵒ, s.v. shām 3), (Śiv. 1019); of (such-and-such) a kind (cf. sāsi-rᵒ, s.v. sôsᵘ) (K. 297, 331, 701, 962).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ronᵘ2, f. rüñᵘ̈ 3; 2 p.p. rañōv), to cook, boil, prepare food by cooking (cf. punᵘ rᵒ, p. 738a, l. 14) (Gr.Gr. 5, 29, 115-6, 168, 191, 209, 225, 227, 251; Gr.M.; L. 459; Śiv. 208, 413, 591, 1042, 1072, 1215, 1533; K. 737; K.Pr. 76, 87). ronᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. rüñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), cooked, prepared for eating.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ranzanôwᵘ), to please, gratify (Gr.Gr. 171, K. 980); to comfort, console. ranzanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ranzanövᵘ̈-mütsᵘ̈), pleased, consoled (by someone).
f. (sg. dat. ranzüʦᵘ̈), gratifying, consoling, comforting, appeasing, conciliating.
f. (sg. dat. ranzavüñᵘ̈), the act of gratifying, satisfying, consoling, conciliating.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ranzowᵘ), to please, gratify, delight (Gr.Gr. 171, K. 467); to comfort, console. ranzowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ranzüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), pleased, gratified, comforted, consoled (by someone).

conj. 2 or 3 (1 p.p. ronzᵘ, 2 p.p. ranzōv or (Gr.Gr. 226) ranzyōv), to become pleased, gratified, delighted, rejoiced (Gr.Gr. 171, 226; K. 19); to be comforted, consoled. The causal of this verb is ranzanāwun or ranzawun, qq.v. (Gr.Gr. 171). ronzᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. rünzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), pleased, gratified, consoled. ranzyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ranzyē-müʦᵘ̈), satisfied, gratified.
m. a report (a corruption of the English word). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to make a report (H. v, 9).
f. (sg. dat. raphāküʦᵘ̈), society, companionship, company, the general society of a place (Gr.M.); association as a helper, an aid (Rām. 34).
m. a companion, friend, ally (El. rafík, Gr.M.).
f. going, motion, walk, gait, pace, used --˚ (cf. kaj-rᵒ, p. 430b, l. 5); going, progression, procedure (Śiv. 410).
m. Randia dumetorum (El.). Cf. main-phal, p. 573a, l. 48.

m. (sg. abl. rasa), sap, juice (of trees, fruit, or the like) (cf. bangi-rᵒ, p. 113a, l. 8; dachĕ-rᵒ, p. 186a, l. 2; dönᵘ̈-rᵘ̈, p. 223b, l. 14; gula-rᵒ, p. 283b, l. 50; handi-rᵒ, p. 337b, l. 5; kā̃bayĕ-rᵒ, p. 382b, l. 48; nadȧrⁱ-rⁱ, p. 623a, l. 42; nĕmbⁱ-rⁱ, p. 671a, l. 15) (Gr.Gr. 124, Gr.M., Śiv. 1848, K.Pr. 5); serum (El.), essence, distillate (L.V. 40; Śiv. 286, 1857); soup, gravy (cf. divagŏn-rᵒ, p. 261b, l. 16; nöhⁱ-rⁱ, p. 625b, l. 18; pāca-rᵒ, p. 678b, l. 33; phŏṭa-rᵒ, p. 716b, l. 32; paka-moṇdⁱ-rⁱ, p. 725a, l. 13; sas ras dyunᵘ and mēlun, s.v. sas) (W. 140; K.Pr. 14, 41, 155, 178, 252); liquid (cf. nīla-rᵒ, p. 634a, l. 11); wine (K.Pr. 100); juiciness (Gr.Gr. 124, 175); taste, flavour (six of these are recognized, viz. sweet, sour, salt, bitter, acrid, and astringent) (Gr.Gr. 146); flavour, relish, liking, desire, delight (in), pleasure (of) (L.V. 73; K.Pr. 175, 177); love, affection (esp. love due to propinquity); a person's essence, his power, energy (L.V. 48, Śiv. 929); charm, elegance, interest, beauty; pathos, emotion, feeling (Śiv. 1111). -ashyudᵘ m. the juice of the box-thorn, or of the Amomum anthorhizum (which is used medicinally, esp. as a collyrium); cf. ashud. -dāra f. a thin stream of juice, soup, or the like. -gan adj. c.g. full of juice, juicy; (of a man) of a loving disposition; (of a literary composition) full of charm, full of sentiment. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. juice to come (in fruit or the like); interest (in one's work) to be excited; serum, pus, or the like to appear in a festering wound. --karun -- m.inf. (of a festering wound) to produce pus. --kẹ̆sᵃri gaʦhun -- m.inf. 'the juice to turn into chaff'; hence, to become distraught by being at one's wits' ends in the face of difficulties; cf. kĕsürᵘ̈. --kẹ̆sᵃri karun -- m.inf. to cause to be distraught, as ab. -kᵒtᵒ adj. (f. -kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), wet with, smeared with, or mixed with soup or gravy (cf. rasa-kᵒtᵒ, bel.). --lagun -- m.inf. charm to be experienced, to feel the charm (of some song, poem, business, etc.) (K. 183, 251, 978, 1039). --mīnith nāṭa gạnzᵃrith -- adj. c.g. 'having measured the gravy and having counted the (bits of) flesh'; hence, dividing out into exactly the right shares (not only of food, but of any thing or occupation, etc., which has to be divided). -mas, see s.v. ras-mas. -nörᵘ̈ f. a small spouted vessel (like a teapot) for distributing soup or gravy among the people seated at a dinner. -phyorᵘ m. (sg. dat. -phĕris), a drop (or very small amount) of juice, gravy, or the like. -phyūrᵘ m. (sg. dat. -phīris), id. --sas -- m. 'soup and porridge', cooked food laid as an offering at cross-roads (in times of disaster) intended to be eaten by dogs, crows, etc. -ʦomᵘ adj. (f. -ʦümᵘ̈), that of which the juice is diminished, dried up (of a country, tree, fruit, food, sauce, or the like). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. charm to come, charm to be felt (e.g. in a sport, view, business, literary work, etc.). ¶ rasa anun m.inf. gradually to propitiate a person by exercising charm. --bĕhun -- m.inf. (of running water or other liquid) to become standing (so as to become clear by allowing the deposit of sediment); (of a person) to rest or stay motionless and silent in a fixed place (e.g. for hiding or because one is out of work). -borutᵘ adj. (f. -barᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), filled with juice, juicy; (of a song, game, etc.) full of charm; (of a food) full of, or soaked with, gravy. -byūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -bīṭhᵘ̈), (of liquid previously running) become still or standing (so as to have become clear by the deposit of sediment); seated motionless and silent in a fixed place. -kᵒtᵒ adj. (f. -kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), i.q. ras-kᵒtᵒ, ab. -kᵒtᵒ sasa-kᵒtᵒ adj. (f. -kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈ sasa-kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), wet with, or smeared with, gravy and porridge (e.g. a dirty dish, from which the remains of food have not been washed off). -masa, see s.v. ras-mas. -maṭh adj. c.g. 'a jar of juice'; hence, (of a fruit) very juicy; (of a story, song, sport, conduct, or the like) full of charm. -phyūrᵘ adj. (f. -phīrᵘ̈), that to which juice or sap has returned, (a withered man, tree, or the like) to become revived; (a sulky-natured person, who has) become loving and gracious. -pöṭhⁱ or -pöṭhin adv. secretly, privately. rasa rasa adv. slowly and gently. --wasun -- m.inf. to descend from juice, (of something moist or sappy, e.g. a man, animal or plant) to become dry and light, to become quiet or gentle (by the departure of pride, anger, excitement, sourness, or the like). --wothᵘ -- adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), become dry and light, as ab.; become quiet and gentle, as ab. --wothᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --wüʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), id. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come from sap, (of a crop of rice, tree, fruit) to become ripe; (of food for cooking) to become thoroughly cooked; (of a sulky-natured person) to become loving and gracious. ¶ rasā-masā, see s.v. ras-mas.

m. (sg. abl. rāsa 1), the circular dance practised by Krishna (Kṛṣṇa) and the herdmaidens of Gōkula; a similar dance performed nowadays in commemoration of it (Śiv. 1010, 1875). --gindun -- m.inf. to perform this dance (Śiv. 947, 1442). --gĕwun -- m.inf. to sing this dance, i.e. perform it (Śiv. 1459). --khēlun -- m.inf. to perform this dance (Śiv. 737, 949, 1002, 1054, 1353, 1376, 1429, 1432, 1493). ¶ rāsa-manḍal or -manḍul m. (sg. dat. -manḍalas), the rās-circle, i.q. rās (Śiv. 1325 (-manḍal), 1390 (-manḍul); Rām. 1567 (-manḍul); K. 293).

m. (sg. abl. rāsa 2), the mouth of the womb; cf. rāsa 3. --trāwun -- m.inf. (in the case of a widow) to bear a bastard son, (in the case of a married woman) to bear a child of adultery (i.e. one whose father is not her husband); cf. rāsa 3. --wasun -- m.inf. abortion or miscarriage of an unborn widow's bastard, or of a child the fruit of adultery, to occur. Cf. rāsa 3.
for rasad, q.v. in hissa-rasa (p. 354b, l. 3), q.v.
m. a widow's bastard, or a son of adultery (i.e. the child of a married woman by a man not her husband); cf. rās 2. --kaṭh -- m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), id. (Gr.Gr. 132).

f. (when at the end of a compound this word sometimes takes the form rasa 2; cf. hissa-rasa, p. 354b, l. 3) coming on, income, import; grain, provision, supplies; allowance of food, ration; share, quota, allowance, contribution. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to contribute towards a subscription, to subscribe (money, goods, or the like). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to collect a subscription, to collect proportionate shares, or taxes according to proportion, or persons according to proportion (as in conscription); to collect supplies according to quota (for an army, travellers, or the like) (H. xi, 5, 10).
m. alchemy, chemistry, an elixir vitæ; a magic potion (L.V. 80); (in Ksh.) a dish of food, perfectly cooked with rare spices by a cordon bleu.
adj. c.g. (of fruit, food, or the like) juicy, full of juice.

m. a merchant's money (including capital, profits, and other property), stock-in-trade (K.Pr. 153). According to I.K. II, i, 18, this word is f. with a sg. obl. röshᵘ̈ as in the case of rāsh 2. --labun -- m.inf. (in a mercantile transaction) to obtain sudden and unexpected great profit.

f. (sg. dat. röshᵘ̈ also written röshⁱ), a sign of the zodiac (cf. dan-rᵒ, p. 220b, l. 42); see rāsh 1. röshᵘ̈-myulᵘ̈ or röshⁱ-myulⁱ m. concurrence of signs (e.g. when two persons such as a husband and wife, two brothers, two friends are born under the same sign of the Zodiac); met. concurrence of two people (carrying on mutual intrigue, love, business, or the like) in perfect unanimity.

f. (sg. dat. rāshi, but usually written rāshĕ, by confusion of ĕ and i), anxiety, apprehension, inner (or hidden) fear, alarm. --aʦun -- m.inf. to enter into anxiety, to become anxious (e.g. from fear of violence from an enemy); to feel a secret longing to repeat a crime (e.g. having once committed, say, theft to want to do it again). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall into anxiety, as ab.; to fall into anxiety (such as causes a person to take precautions against the occurrence of the evil feared), anxiously to take precautions. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause to enter into anxiety, to fill with anxiety, fill with apprehension; to cause a person who has once committed a crime to have a secret longing to do it again (see ab.).
f. a woman's zone or girdle.
m. envy, emulation, jealousy, grudge, spite, malice (Śiv. 710, Rām. 1147).
adj. c.g. arriving, attaining, used --˚, as in juz-rasī (p. 380b, l. 28), q.v.
m. acknowledgment of receipt or arrival, receipt; a paper acknowledging receipt, a receipt (Gr.M.).
m. a sketch, model, plan (El.); manner, custom, practice.

m. the state of being juicy, sappy, or the like, or of being moist with essence, or with perspiration, moistness, juiciness; met. the state of being gentle and kind, a kindly disposition. -mas ʦamun m.inf. the juiciness to diminish (in cooking), to become cooked dry (by the boiling away of the gravy, etc.). ¶ rasa-masa adv. slowly and with kindness, gently. ¶ rasā masā adv. easily and gently, coaxingly, compassionately.
or rasöyⁱ f. cooking (K. 136, 138, 1068); dressed food, victuals (K. 142).
m. a line, a row; (in Ksh.) a long closely packed procession of people.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. rasyōv), to be, or become, full of juice, sap (e.g. a fruit, food for cooking, a field, etc.) (Gr.Gr. 124, 175). The causal of this verb is rasanāwun (Gr.Gr. 175).
or ruswā رسوا adj. c.g. dishonoured, disgraced, abashed (Rām. 668, 713).

adj. (f. rasijᵘ̈), juicy, sappy; full of flavour, imparting flavour (Gr.Gr. 146); affectionate, of a loving disposition; graceful, charming, sweet (Gr.Gr. 146); exciting affection, fascinating, captivating, enrapturing.

f. a kind of tall earthenware pot used for cooking rice and similar offices; extreme heat (of the sun or a burning wind); a violent thunderstorm accompanied by destructive lightning, and, so it is believed, by scalding rain (cf. bᵃsar). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be scalded to death (as though by this scalding rain). An expression used in curses (cf. bᵃsar pë̆ñᵘ̈, p. 134b, l. 25). ¶ rasᵃri-bata m. rice boiled in the above kind of cooking pot (used as a regimen for a lying-in woman); scalding hot boiled rice (fresh from the pot, and before it has cooled down). -wôñᵘ m. scalding hot water (not only that heated by boiling, but such as becomes so by exposure to the sun or the like).
in the following:-- ratanjog (? spelling) m. Anemone obtusiloba (El.), ratankāt (? spelling) m. Andromeda ovalifolia (El. ratanᵒ and rȧtanᵒ).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. raṭanôwᵘ), to cause to be seized; to cause to seize (El., Śiv. 1854); to cause to be accepted; to cause to be arrested or caught, to have (so-and-so) arrested. Causal of raṭun, q.v. in all its meanings.
n.ag. (f. raṭavüñᵘ̈), one who seizes, lays hold of, etc., as in raṭun, q.v. (Śiv. 981, K. 140).
(? spelling and gender) in sang-i-ratēl (L. 65), a certain chocolate coloured stone used for ornaments and buttons.

f. (sg. dat. raṭi or (Rām. 1753) rüṭᵘ̈), grasping, seizure (L.V. 107); hindrance, obstruction (cf. potᵘ rᵒ 1, p. 787b, l. 29) (K. 1116); the equivalent weight of anything (= roṭᵘ 1) (cf. dāñĕ-rᵒ, p. 236b, l. 50; potᵘ rᵒ 2 p. 787b, l. 31; pĕṭha rᵒ or pĕṭhⁱ rᵒ, p. 795b, l. 13 (Śiv. 1566). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. hindrance or obstruction to occur. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to hinder, obstruct. ¶ raṭa-raṭh f. intervening in a fight, separating combatants. raṭa-woṭᵘ m. of equivalent weight (e.g. of the woven cloth, as compared with the thread given to the weaver for its manufacture). ¶ raṭi-raṭh adj. c.g. weighing the exactly equivalent weight (of one thing weighed against another). Cf. rȧṭⁱ-raṭa, s.v. roṭᵘ 1. ¶ rüṭᵘ̈-rostᵘ̈ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without hindrance; one who cannot be hindered or obstructed, irresistible (Rām. 1753).

m. (sg. dat. ratas), blood, life-blood (cf. bösⁱ rᵒ, p. 131b, l. 26; kōtar-rᵒ, p. 492a, l. 3; shĕwa-rᵒ, s.v. shĕv) (Gr.Gr. 51-2; Gr.M.; L. 458 rat; Rām. 109, 273, 284, 296, 357, 413, 440, 462-3, etc.; K. 237, 309, 563; K.Pr. 146, 218, 253). --anun -- m.inf. to let blood flow, to cause blood to flow; to draw blood out of a person, i.e. to insist upon a person giving, to extort (from a person). --bã̄di gaʦhun -- m.inf. to occur by stoppage of (the flow of) blood (i.e. the black swollen bruise caused by a blow, by the breaking of a limb, or by tying up tightly). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take blood, to harass or torture a person (by giving impossible or very difficult tasks, by inflicting intolerable punishment, extortion, or the like) (Rām. 1240). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to draw blood, to bleed (a person) (El.). --khasun -- m.inf. the blood to rise, vomiting of blood (hæmatemesis) to occur; the blood to rise (e.g. to the eyes in rage) (Rām. 916, K. 445). --ṭhī˜ca wasun -- m.inf. blood to flow (e.g. from a wound) in a violent torrent. --wālun -- m.inf. to cause blood to descend, i.e. to torture or harass a person (in order to extort something from him, to make him do something, or the like). --wandun -- m.inf. to dedicate one's life-blood, to be ready to sacrifice one's life (for a person or object) (Rām. 34, 169, 952, 1079; K.Pr. 155, 178, 194). ¶ rata-borutᵘ adj. (f. barᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), filled with blood, flooded with blood, soaked in blood (YZ. 126). -chūl m. a blood-cascade, a flow of blood (e.g. from a sword-wound). -chaph f. (sg. dat. -chapi), a sacrificial offering of blood, a bloody sacrifice, the slaughter of a living being (e.g. an animal, or even oneself) in a religious sacrifice. -chapi dyunᵘ m.inf. to offer (a living creature) in such a sacrifice. -chapi lagun m.inf. to be offered in sacrifice (for another's benefit), to be the victim in a propitiatory sacrifice. -dag f. blood-pain, the pain caused by diseased blood. -digiñ f. a long thin stream of blood (from a wound or the like). -ḍōr m. a rope of blood, i.e. a trickle of congealed blood from a wound or sore. -gagar m.pl. 'blood-rats', blood flowing in clots. -golᵘ m. a blood-mouthful, an accumulation of blood in the mouth. -ganḍ m. a blood-knot, a kind of painful boil very slow in ripening; met. an obstinate wrathful man. -grakh f. (sg. dat. -graki), the boiling up of blood, vomiting blood, hæmatemesis. -graka khasañĕ f. pl. inf. hæmatemesis to occur. -hūnᵘ adj. (f. hūñᵘ̈), a blood-hound (i.e. a dog which eagerly licks up blood); hence, met. a vile fellow who spends his time harassing others. -kôḍᵘ m. one who draws blood (cf. kaḍun), a bleeder, phlebotomist. -khal f. a certain disease, the symptoms of which are blood flowing in quantities from the mouth, the nose, and the anus, caused either by a wound or by internal disease. -khȧlⁱ adj. c.g. one who suffers from the preceding disease. -khali gaʦhun m.inf. to be, or become, afflicted with this disease. -khali karun m.inf. to cause a person to suffer from this disease (e.g. by a blow, or by wounding). -khanjĕ m. (so reported, but probably f.pl.), a disease of the blood, of which the symptoms are extreme redness of the eyelids and eyeballs, and coagulation of the blood. -khorᵘ adj. (f. -khürᵘ̈), blood scald-head, an abusive, noisy, quarrelsome fellow (K.Pr. 3, 4). -kyomᵘ lagun m.inf. a certain disease, in which the blood is supposed to be filled with tiny worms, to attack (a person); madness supposed to be produced by similar symptoms to occur. -lal f. blood-blister, a line of clotted blood along the roots of the teeth, ? pyorrhœa. -maṭh hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -maṭh hishᵘ̈), 'like a temple of blood', ruddy-faced, rubicund (considered to be charming); (of any limb) flushed, inflamed; (of a fruit) red, blood-red. -phuṭᵘ m. a boil filled with blood or due to diseased blood. -phuṭh f. (sg. dat. -phuṭi), a similar boil or gathering but longer in shape (due to too tight binding, to a blow, or other external cause). -phyorᵘ m. (sg. dat. -phĕris), a blood-drop. -phyūrᵘ m. (sg. dat. -phīris), id. -palav m. a dirty rag for wiping blood. -prāʦa f.pl. the corners of the mouth covered with blood; conduct caused by grief at the death of a beloved person (at the time of the death). -pĕth f. (sg. dat. -pë̆ʦᵘ̈), a disease affecting the blood and bile (causing sudden death). -pë̆ʦᵘ̈ gaʦhun m.inf. to die a sudden death by such disease. -pay m. a junction of two veins (cf. raga-pᵒ, p. 827b, l. 46); met. close blood-relationship. -rᵃsh f. hatred between blood-relations; mutual hatred similar to such. -rāṭh f. (sg. dat. -rāṭhi), lines of blood on the eye-balls, bloodshot eyes; a line-like blood mark on a limb (due to a blow or the like). -rôṭhᵘ adj. (f. -röṭhᵘ̈), a rude quarrelsome brawling fellow. -rᵃy f. a blood-ogress, a vampire; a woman who habitually (like a blood-sucking insect) insinuates herself into another's company, and then torments him or her. -rĕy f. a certain disease in which a tickling sensation is felt in the veins (as though ants were travelling through them). -rōz f. instability of blood; hence, bleeding hæmorrhoids. -rōz pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. an attack of bleeding hæmorrhoids to occur. -ʦūr m. 'blood-thief', a certain dangerous blood-disease affecting the chest, liver, and spleen. -ʦūr pyonᵘ m.inf. to be at the point of death owing to this disease. -ʦūrlad adj. c.g. (as subst. f. -ʦūrladiñ), one at the point of death from this disease.

m. (sg. dat. rātas), night-time, night (cf. aḍ-rāth 1 m. p. 10a, l. 44, half a night; but aḍ-rāth 2 f. ib., midnight, see rāth 2); (Gr.M., W. 115). Cf. rāth 2. Adv. at night, by night (Rām. 149, 659, 896, 941; K.Pr. 48, 178). --dŏh -- adv. night and day, always, continually (Śiv. 341; Rām. 871; K. 504, 525, 1081, 1094). rāth ta dŏh, id. (Rām. 514, 791, 1774), so dŏh ta rāth (H. vii, 3). -dĕn adv. night and day (Śiv. 160, 215, 524, 541, 735, 986, 1420), so dĕn-rāth adv. day and night (cf. p. 222b, l. 37) (Śiv. 107, 366, 1554), and rāth ta dĕn night and day (Śiv. 1555). --kyutᵘ -- adv. at night, in the night-time (Gr.Gr. 156; Gr.M.; Rām. 883, 1273; K. 1024, 1089; H. iii, 1); to-night (Gr.M., Rām. 146); for to-night (Gr.M.). ¶ rāta-dŏha adv. by day and night (El. ráta-doho). -krṻl  m. a bat (the animal) (El.; W. 115, rātạkröl; Śiv. 351). Seen in the daytime it is a bird of ill-omen (Śiv. 351). -mŏgul m. (f. -mŏgüjᵘ̈ or -mŏgȧjⁱ), an owl (W. 115 rātạmog̱ẖal; Śiv. 1192, 1756). -mŏgal-nam m. an owl's claw; a gold ornament shaped as such, worn on a child's head as an amulet. -röchⁱ f. guarding by night (El.). -röchⁱ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to do such guarding, to be on night sentry duty (El.). -rôchᵘ m. a night watchman, a sentry (El.). ¶ rātō-rāth adv. in a single night (of something done in a single night, i.e. very quickly). ¶ rōt-onᵘ adj. (f. -üñᵘ̈), night-blind. -añĕr m. night-blindness. -arpha روت عرفہ m. the vigil of a festival (K.Pr. 193). -bal m. power or strength (of a person, quality, action, etc.), used, or to be used, only by night; cf. -pav, bel. -bata m. food eaten at night, a night-meal; stale food remaining over from having been cooked the preceding night. -gaṭa f. the darkness of night (esp. when intense); inability to see, the darkness of blindness. -hum m. a sacrifice performed by night. -kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a brazier or kāngrī for use at night-time; such a brazier with its complement of burning charcoal, employed for keeping a room warm at night-time. -khọ̆bᵘ m. a wadded night-cap. -kalapushᵘ m. a night-cap shaped like a skull-cap, made of woollen cloth doubled. -lạgᵃn m. the lucky moment for a wedding, if it happens to be in the night-time. -nār m. the glowing ashes in the morning of a fire which has been burning throughout the night. -nāv f. a boat which travels by night (e.g. which is not tied up to the bank at nightfall, but goes on). -palav m. a night-gown. -pav m. dexterity which is exercised or is intended to be exercised only at night; cf. -bal, ab. -ṭūpⁱ f. a night-cap. ¶ rötⁱ-rāth f. the entire night; night by night (YZ. 382). -rātas adv. throughout the entire night, all night (Rām. 1635). -ʦolᵘ adj. (f. -ʦȧjⁱ or -ʦüjᵘ̈), one who habitually absents himself at night; one who is lazy by day, but industrious by night; that which lasts only for a night (and is destroyed or disappears at dawn). ¶ rātücᵘ̈ rāth 1 (for 2, see rāth 3), f. the entire night. ¶ rātukᵘ 1 (for 2, see rāth 3) gen. adj. (f. rātücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the night (K. 802; H. v, 9). ¶ rātan adv. by night, used --˚, as in aḍ-rātan, at midnight, p. 10a, l. 47; so aḍ-rᵒ-bögᵒ (or -bögin), at about midnight, ib. l. 48. ¶ rötⁱn-mȧnzⁱ adv. only in the coming night, this very night (with the idea of happening speedily or suddenly). ¶ rātas adv. by night, at night, used --˚, as in aḍ-rātas, at midnight, p. 10a, l. 50, or aḍa-rᵒ (K. 57); so aḍ-rᵒ-bögᵒ (or -bögin), p. 10b, l. 1; az-rātas, to-night, p. 74a, l. 23; drustis rātas, all night, throughout the night, p. 249a, l. 30 (Gr.M.; Śiv. 325, 332, 1465; Rām. 679, 741, 1526, 1584; H. x, 1, 6; xii, 4); all night, throughout the night (Rām. 259, K. 280); in the night-time (K. 592, K.Pr. 178); of, or to, a night (K. 295). --dŏhas -- adv. night and day (Rām. 75, 650, 1061; K. 802; YZ. 118). -pĕṭh adj. c.g. occupied, carried on, etc., throughout the night. --rāth -- adv. on this very night (H. x, 5, 12). ¶ rātasᵘy adv. in a single night, in the very night (K. 1150).
m. (sg. dat. rāṭas), a king, used --˚, as in rāza-rāṭh, s.v. rāza, q.v.
f. (sg. dat. ratiyĕ (K. 739), obl. rati (K. 41, 43-4)) N. of the goddess of Love, the wife of Kāma, the Indian Cupid. She was reborn as Māyāvatī, who married Pradyumna (K. 739-48).

f. (sg. dat. röʦᵘ̈), night (the whole period from sunset to sunrise) (cf. aḍ-rāth 2, f. midnight, p. 10a, l. 44; but aḍ-rāth 1, m., see rāth 1, half a night; maĩzi-rᵒ, p. 615a, l. 27; pŏha-rᵒ, p. 684a, l. 41; potᵘrᵘ, p. 787b, l. 35; shiwa-rᵒ, s.v. shiv; sŏkh-rᵒ, s.v. sŏkh; sata-rᵒ, s.v. sath 1), (Gr.Gr. 13, 28, 32, 46, 68-70, 146; Gr.M.; L.V. 3, 5, 19, 55, 65, 91; Śiv. 168, 350, 468, 1002, 1032, 1062, 1413, 1443, 1465, 1549, 1584; Rām. 147, 196, 924, 1108g, 1498; K. 280, 295, 1088, 1137, 1148; H. x, 5). --barüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to pass the night, spend the night (Rām. 1609; H. i, 10). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a night to pass away, a night to elapse (H. iii, 1); rāth gaʦhüñᵘ̈ ādā, the night to go to completion, the night to come to an end (H. x, 8; xii, 9, 12). --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to pass the night (H. x, 11; xii, 5). --lagüñᵘ̈ --, f.inf. the night to come on (H. viii, 9). --pĕṭha pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a night (of watching) to fall upon (something), the watching of the family through the night by the dead body of a member to occur, and thus to prohibit the performance or completion of any other business. --rāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the night to be ruined, to labour throughout the whole night. --rāwarüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause a person to labour the whole night; to waste, spend unavailingly (Rām. 1526). --sūrith -- adv. lit. the night having been exhausted; hence, on the conclusion of the night, at night's end (Rām. 1636). ¶ rāthāh f. a single night (H. xii, 5); as adv., for, or during, a single night (K. 279). ¶ röʦᵘ̈, obl. sg. (cf. ajĕ röʦᵘ̈, p. 13b, l. 34; ajĕ-röʦᵘ̈-bögᵘ̈ (or -bögin), p. 13b, l. 36), by night (Gr.M.); tamiy röʦᵘ̈, on that very night (Rām. 147). röʦᵘ̈-onᵘ̈ adj. (f. -üñᵘ̈), night-blind (cf. rōt-onᵘ, s.v. rāth 1). -añĕr m. night-blindness; cf. rōt-añĕr, s.v. rāth 1. -hondᵘ adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the night (H. iii, 1). -kiturᵘ m. a kind of bird, which flies about only at night; a man who by day is slothful, but works throughout the night (cf. rōt-bal and rötⁱ-ʦolⁱ, s.v. rāth 1). -pav m. study, labour, strength, exercised at night; dexterity or power which flourishes in the night-time. Cf. rōt-pav, s.v. rāth 1.

or rã̄ṭh f. (sg. dat. rāṭhi), a line, a row (e.g. of birds, ants, fruit on trees, clouds, mushrooms, or the like) (cf. hĕḍar-rᵒ, p. 323b, l. 20; kanagᵃch-rᵃ, p. 456b, l. 40; rum-rᵒ, p. 833b, l. 44); a procession--in this sense used --˚ with words signifying rain, or the like, to indicate violence (cf. ḍōṭha-rᵒ, a violent hailstorm, p. 258a, l. 7; rūda-rᵒ, p. 826a, l. 48); a creeping plant, a vine (cf. dachĕ-rᵒ, p. 186a, l. 6; K.Pr. 155, where it is masc.); a line (in a picture, pattern, embroidery or the like, contributing to the pattern) (cf. rata-rᵒ, p. 846b, l. 16). -wurāṭh m. the beginning and conclusion (e.g. of a story, book, speech, action, or the like, u.w. reference to inspection, criticizing, etc.). -wurāṭh bōzun m.inf. to consider, or criticize, from beginning to end.

adv. yesterday (Gr.Gr. 151, Gr.M.); last night (W. 95). rātukᵘ 2 adj. (f. rātücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, yesterday (Gr.Gr. 151, Gr.M.); of, or belonging to, last night (K.Pr. 178). rātücᵘ̈ rāth 2 f. the night before last.

m. a chariot, carriage, wheeled vehicle (L.V. 73 rathu, an old form; Śiv. 1154; K. 29, 378, 406, 490, 637, 658, 727, etc.); esp. a war-chariot (Rām. 978-9, 1352, 1354, 1437, 1449; K. 555-7). -bān m. a charioteer (Śiv. 809, 1146, 1372, 1734). -pahī f. the felly of a chariot wheel. -suwörī f. riding in a chariot, carriage driving (Śiv. 580, 786, 805, 961). -ʦakᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a chariot wheel. -wôlᵘ m. the owner of a chariot; the superintendent of a chariot establishment; a charioteer (K. 556). ¶ rȧthⁱ adv. very speedily, very quickly. ¶ rathi khārun m.inf. to arrange (things in disorder) in complete order, to make successful (Rām. 15, 177). rathi khasun m.inf. (of things in disorder) to be arranged in complete order, to turn out quite right.

or rạtᵃn m. (sg. dat. rạtnas), a gem, jewel, precious stone (El. rattan, a ruby; Śiv. 525, 855, 1153; Rām. 15-17, 1345; K. 28, 97, 178, 183, 555, 671, 673-5, etc.; H. xii, 10, 12, 14-15, 18, 20); met. (of a person) a jewel of a person, a virtuous and popular person (cf. rāza-rᵒ, s.v. rāza) (cf. Rām. 1345); (of a thing) the most excellent and admirable of its kind. ¶ rạtna-dīph m. (sg. dat. -dīpas), a jewelled lamp used, by Hindūs, in worship (Śiv. 108, 377). -ʦö̃gijᵘ̈ f. lustration of a god, an honoured guest, or the like, by waving a lamp over his or her head (Śiv. 1093 rạtᵃn-ʦᵃ).
m. the night-time (Gr.Gr. 146, 156). rātᵃli adv. in the night-time (Gr.Gr. 156; H. viii, 9; K.Pr. 49, 59).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. roṭᵘ 2; f. rüṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. racĕ; 2 p.p. racyōv) to seize, grasp, lay hold of, clutch (cf. atha rᵒ, p. 62a, l. 22; côṭᵘ rᵒ, p. 177a, l. 34; dāman rᵒ, p. 219b, l. 43; dāmāna rᵒ, p. 220a, l. 2; gāḍ raṭüñᵘ̈, p. 276a, l. 14; mōra rᵒ, p. 588a, l. 14; murath rᵒ, p. 594a, l. 33; pād raṭȧnⁱ, p. 681a, l. 4; pishⁱ-mŏṭh raṭüñᵘ̈, p. 818a, l. 31; rĕkh raṭüñᵘ̈, p. 830b, l. 41; sāth rᵒ, s.v. sāth 2) (Gr.Gr. 5, 9, 10; Gr.M.; L.V. 3, 4, 24, 26, 69, 101, 104; Śiv. 124, 179, 275, 381, 1432, 1732; Rām. 160, 170, 175, 400, 410, 416, 604, 623, 649, 905, 911, 914, 929, etc.; K. 33, 83, 110, 187, 195, etc.; H. iii, 5; K.Pr. 102, 178) (hĕth raṭun, having taken, to grasp, i.e. to hold, L.V. 69); to fasten (oneself or something) to (something or oneself) (cf. bāl rᵒ, p. 104a, l. 5; lara-lab raṭüñᵘ̈, p. 529b, l. 5; mŏshᵉ̆kh rᵒ, p. 579b, l. 16; nam rᵒ, p. 635a, l. 44) (Śiv. 1258, 1324, 1381, 1470, 1556; K.Pr. 226); to keep close (to), hug (the shore, etc.) (cf. bölⁱ rᵒ, p. 104a, l. 22) (Śiv. 1834); ¶ to take, adopt (a residence, habit, or the like) (Śiv. 574, 773, 1508; Rām. 202, 207-8, 249, 272, 321, 591, 919, 1142-43h, 1199, 1266, 1582; YZ. 150, 571); to enter (a road, course of conduct, or the like) and follow it diligently (L.V. 82; Śiv. 1833; Rām. 1158, 1577); ¶ to hold, grasp, retain (cf. athi rᵒ, p. 66a, l. 9; dĕmāg rᵒ, p. 219a, l. 34; gīr raṭȧnⁱ, p. 296b, l. 48; mān rᵒ, p. 573a, l. 12; nālamati rᵒ, p. 632b, l. 27) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 506, 1541; Rām. 944-8, 1120; K. 265, 292, 399, 672, 720-1, 750, etc.); to accept, take (cf. bȧndⁱ rᵒ, p. 111b, l. 15; hamal rᵒ, p. 334a, l. 3) (Śiv. 410, 703, 1568, 1752; Rām. 557, 561, 1143a; H. i, 7; viii, 7; YZ. 228, 320; K.Pr. 102, 166, 247); to acquire, get, take, receive (cf. büṭhᵘ̈ raṭüñᵘ̈, p. 143b, l. 42; navĕr rᵒ, p. 668b, l. 17) (Śiv. 1565; Rām. 704, 1082, 1141, 1160, 1464; H. viii, 3, 4; x, 3, 5, 8, 12; K.Pr. 22, 220); to get hold of, find (H. xii, 19); ¶ to grasp (a person's face), i.e. to look upon intently (H. v, 9); ¶ to check, restrain, stop, bring to a halt, detain (cf. dŏd rᵒ, p. 188a, l. 36; darka rᵒ, p. 243a, l. 32; hada rᵒ, p. 222a, l. 39; khĕn rᵒ, p. 401b, l. 13; khyonᵘ rᵒ, p. 428b, l. 26; nāv raṭüñᵘ̈, p. 666a, l. 15; potᵘ rᵒ, p. 787b, l. 38; path rᵒ, p. 792a, l. 41; samakhunᵘ rᵒ, s.v. samakhun; tal rᵒ, p. 996a, l. 21) (Gr.M.; Rām. 1752; K. 141, 161-5, 1056, 1145, 1171; YZ. 117); ¶ to seize, arrest (cf. bēgāri rᵒ, p. 92a, l. 33; nāla rᵒ, p. 632b, l. 3) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 25, 1033; Rām. 350, 402, 498, 587, 618, 705, 764, 807, 927, etc.; K. 335, 443, 445, 449-50, 564, 663, etc.; H. ii, 11; v, 7, 9; x, 5, 12; YZ. 129; K.Pr. 174, 256); to block (a road, way, or the like, against a person) (K. 431); (of a disease, sorrow, or the like) to seize, attack (a person) (cf. pôrᵘ rᵒ, p. 753b, l. 29) (Rām. 323); ¶ to get hold of, obtain the mastery of, bring into subjection (cf. man rᵒ, p. 572a, l. 21; nam tal rᵒ, p. 635b, l. 20) (L.V. 55, 80; Śiv. 452, 520, 1514, 1701, 1811; Rām. 19; K. 500); to seize (a person), i.e. to throw oneself upon his mercy, to take refuge with (Rām. 1304, K.Pr. 87); to engage (a servant) (H. viii, 13). ¶ This verb is often used in senses which are the equivalents of the meaning of the causal or transitive forms of the intransitive verb rōzun, to remain. Thus, athi raṭun, to take hold of in the hand, athi rōzun, to remain in the hand, p. 66a, ll. 9, 13; dŏd raṭun, to stop the flow of milk, dŏd rōzun, the flow of milk to be stopped, p. 188a, ll. 36, 37; hada raṭun, to keep (a person) within bounds, hada rōzun, to remain within bounds, p. 322a, ll. 42, 46; nam tal raṭun, to bring under one's influence, nam tal rōzun, to remain under one's influence, p. 635b, ll. 20, 23; path raṭun, to hold back, path rōzun, p. 792a, ll. 41, 42, or pata rōzun, p. 793a, l. 43, to be kept behind. ¶ roṭᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. rüṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, sg. dat. racĕ-maʦĕ), seized, accepted, etc., as ab. (cf. mōra rᵒ, p. 588a, l. 16; nāla rᵒ, p. 632b, l. 34; nam tal rᵒ, p. 635b, l. 17; shĕkan rᵒ, s.v. shĕkh 2) (K. 236, 997; H. x, 12). ¶ raṭan-bāna m. 'a vessel of taking', one who is worthy of receiving (something). raṭan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. raṭan-wājĕñ), one who seizes, accepts, etc., as ab.; one who is able to understand on a mere hint. ¶ raṭith, having grasped, having held, etc.; hence, used as an adverb, firmly, steadfastly (Rām. 1158).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. rôṭᵘ) (causal of raṭun) to cause to be grasped, to cause to stick (H. viii, 1).
m. the sun (an old word, now obs.) (L.V. 16, 53; Rām. 1188, 1346).
m. the act of going (esp. when hurried and secret) (cf. potᵘ rav, p. 787b, l. 37). --trāwun -- m.inf. to set out, begin to go (esp. hurriedly and secretly) (K. 825).

m. a kind of coarse woollen blanket, described as of a dark-hue, with a coloured fringe (Gr.Gr. 44, K.Pr. 178); according to K.Pr. 178 it is made from the fur of some animal, generally black, and imported from the Panjāb. -palav m. a worn out short blanket of this kind (considered as indicating poverty). -züṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -zacĕ), a worn out rag of such a blanket (K. 1118, 1119).
adj. c.g. going, current; lawful, right; (in Ksh. subst. m.) a proper, or advisable, course of conduct (Rām. 1320).
f. night-watch, watching a crop, or the like, by night (against thieves, animals, etc.) (cf. röchⁱ-rⁱ, p. 824a, l. 34).
m. (sg. dat. rawakas), a long upper chamber or upper verandah, for meeting and dining in (El., Rām. 569).

adj. c.g. going; dispatched, gone; āb-i-rawāna آب روانہ, flowing water (Rām. 131). --karun -- m.inf. to dispatch, to dispatch, send forth (H. x, 3). --sapanun -- or --sö̃panun -- m.inf. to depart, set out, start (on a journey) (Rām. 107, 305).
m. a goer, traveller, passenger; (in Ksh.) a knave, cheat, swindler.
f. (sg. dat. rāwarüñᵘ̈), causing to disappear, doing away with; losing, loss; spoiling, reducing to no value.
f. causing to disappear, doing away with, embezzlement; losing, loss; spoiling, reducing to no value; spoiling, looting, ruining (a country).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. rāwarôwᵘ) i.q. rāwarun, q.v. (Gr.M.); to cause to disappear, destroy (Śiv. 1565, 1625, 1814; Rām. 364, 1343, 1656); to waste (time) (Śiv. 1756); to cause (a way) to be missed (by, dat.) (Rām. 1616, 1620). rāwarôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. rāwarövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. rāworᵘ- motᵘ, s.v. rāwarun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. rāworᵘ), to cause to disappear, do away with; to embezzle (property entrusted to one); to lose (cf. ȧchⁱ rāwarañĕ, p. 8b, l. 28; atha rāwarun, p. 62a, l. 32) (YZ. 315, 384; K.Pr. 163); to lose (time), waste (time) (Gr.M., W. 139, Rām. 1526, K.Pr. 188); to spoil, reduce to no value (cf. dŏh rᵒ, p. 199b, l. 47; kath rāwarüñᵘ̈, p. 486a, l. 48; rāth rāwarüñᵘ̈, p. 848b, l. 2) (K. 155-6), to destroy; to spoil, loot, ruin (a country); to cause (a way) to be missed (by, dat.) (Rām. 1362). rāworᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. rāvürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to disappear; lost; spoiled, etc., as ab.
f. (sg. dat. rāwaṭi), circling on guard, i.e. walking round and round an object on sentry go, watch and ward patrol.

m. (sg. dat. rāwalas), one who conducts (a person), or causes (a person) to go, along a wrong or bad road (when the right or a good road is available); met. one who leads a person from a virtuous life to evil ways. wañi-rᵒ, p. 1129a, l. 14. Cf. rang-rāwul, p. 836b, l. 36.

(also spelt) m. (sg. dat. rāwanas), the ruler of Lankā and chief of the Rākṣasas or demons whose destruction by Rāma-candra forms the subject of the Rāmâyaṇa (Śiv. 738, 1425, 1482; Rām. 36, 65, 67, 77, 175, 277, 338-9, 343, 345, 349, 360, 363, etc., passim). He is said to have had ten heads, and was hence sometimes called Dashĕ-rāwun (Rām. 583, 841, 1033, 1149).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. rôwᵘ), to be lost (by, dat.); to disappear, become non-existent, be done away with (cf. ȧchⁱ rāwañĕ, p. 8b, l. 25; atha rᵒ, p. 62a, l. 29; brö̃ʦᵘ̈-rᵘ̈, p. 127b, l. 38) (Gr.Gr. 23, 174, 205; Gr.M.; L. 461; L.V. 66, 95, 108; Śiv. 350, 522, 1878; Rām. 15, 45, 244, 522 (tas rövᵘ̈, she was lost by him), 1602; K.Pr. 91, 171); ¶ to be destroyed (Rām. 177, 386, 1475, 1772-3; YZ. 37, 251, 427; K.Pr. 6); to be lost, missed (of a road), the way to be lost (Rām. 1222); ¶ to be spoiled, reduced to no value (cf. dŏh rᵒ, p. 199b, l. 44; kath rāvüñᵘ̈, p. 486a, l. 44; rāth rāvüñᵘ̈, p. 848a, l. 50) (K.Pr. 72); to be lost by violence, be robbed (Gr.M.). ¶ The causal of this verb is rāwanāwun, rāwarāwun or rāwarun (cf. Gr.Gr. 174). ¶ rôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. rövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), lost, etc., as ab. (Rām. 446, 1116, 1500; K. 123; K.Pr. 91). ¶ rāwan-dôdᵘ m. sorrow caused by loss. rāwan-dĕv  m. a loss-devil, something which disappears or is destroyed before one's very eyes (as though carried off by a devil). -dĕv pata lagun  m.inf. disappearance or destruction to dog (a person), such to occur over and over again (to a person). rāwan-tyolᵘ m. (sg. dat. -tĕlis), destruction suddenly to occur.

m. a preliminary test or experiment (e.g. calculating the produce of a crop from a sample; how much yarn is required for a length of cloth from the amount required for, say, a yard; if a method of work will do, by a short experiment; and so on). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to make such a preliminary test. --nērun -- m.inf. the result to turn out in accordance with such a preliminary experiment. --wuchun -- m.inf. to make an estimate on such a preliminary test or experiment.
m. i.q. rāza 1, q.v., a king, used --˚, as in nögⁱ-rⁱ, p. 624b, l. 1.

m. a disease or blight affecting rice and similar crops, in which no grain, but only barren straw, is produced. It has two varieties, viz. hĕlⁱ-rⁱ (p. 364b, l. 10) in which the stalk and ears are affected, and mŏnjĕ-rᵒ (p. 575a, l. 38) in which the plant withers from the root upwards (cf. potᵘ rᵒ, p. 787b, l. 38) (L. 280, 321, 334, 436, rai). ¶ rayĕ-brakh m. (sg. dat. -brakas), a blight-blow, the condition of this blight, withering of a crop; met. withering of a man (from disease), wasting away. ¶ rȧyⁱ gōmotᵘ  perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), attacked by this blight, withered; (of a person) wasted away. rȧyⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to become withered by blight; (of a person) to waste away. rȧyⁱ karun m.inf. to cause to wither (e.g. by omitting irrigation or the like); to cause (a child, or other person) to waste away (by neglect, etc.).

f. belief, judgment, opinion, thought (cf. byonᵘ byonᵘ rāyĕ, p. 151a, l. 20) (El. ráe; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1232, 1649; Rām. 386, 1232; YZ. 489); wisdom, intelligence; counsel, advice, personal wish, desire (Śiv. 767, 1479, 1481, 1743, 1751; Rām. 1156); doubt, hesitation (Śiv. 1284); determination, what is resolved upon (Rām. 368, 1549; H. viii, 11); partizanship; in shāshĕ-rāy, s.v. shöshᵘ̈, the word apparently means 'obstruction'. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an opinion, belief, judgment to be formed; hesitation to arise (in a person's mind) regarding a course of conduct (YZ. 451). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to form an intention; to consider, think (H. xii, 15); to come to a decision (after hearing both sides); to decide fairly (e.g. in apportionment); to take sides, become a partizan. --rōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a desire to be entertained, a wish to be firmly felt. --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to entertain a strong desire. --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a mature decision to be arrived at (after due consideration). ¶ rāyĕ-dar m. (f. -dariñ), a partizan, one who takes one side and opposes the other. rāyĕ-trāye adj. c.g. obedient, faithful, compliant.
adj. c.g. (of a crop) affected with blight, blighted (see ray 2).
adj. c.g. (of a crop) withered, blighted (cf. ray 2).

f. a string, a rope, cable (cf. aṭa-rᵒ, p. 52b, l. 17; bangi-rᵒ, p. 113a, l. 10; ḍanga-rᵒ, p. 227a, l. 3; dura-rᵒ, p. 239a, l. 21; gāsa-rᵒ, p. 307b, l. 47; krĕshimi-rᵒ, p. 476a, l. 49; laman-rᵒ, p. 524b, l. 42; pĕʦi-rᵒ, p. 806b, l. 43; ruma-rᵒ, p. 834a, l. 21) (Gr.M.; L.V. 95; Śiv. 1818; Rām. 494, 1128; K. 168; H. xi, 9; K.Pr. 51, 93, 178-9). A string like object (cf. ḍōlᵃna-rᵃ, p. 214a, l. 44; darbi-rᵒ, p. 240a, l. 36; gāri-rᵒ, p. 298a, l. 9; hāyĕ-raza, p. 363a, l. 15; kīhi-rᵒ, p. 390b, l. 10; khōri-rᵒ, p. 412a, l. 48; nöhⁱ-rⁱ, p. 625b, l. 20; nasta-wājĕ-rᵒ, p. 658b, l. 17; pāka-rᵒ, p. 725b, l. 13; pushᵉ̆ṭᵉ̆-tāla- rᵒ, p. 783a, l. 25); a long connected line of people, a string of people (cf. ȧnⁱ-rⁱ, p. 31b, l. 35); (pl.) a continuous heavy fall of snow, rain, or the like (cf. shīna-raza, s.v. shīn). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make a rope, to arrest by force (one or a gang of persons engaged in a conspiracy or the like). ¶ raza-gorᵘ m. (his wife is raza-gȧrⁱ-bāy, but a female rope-maker is -gürᵘ̈) a professional rope-maker, one who lives by twisting and selling string, rope, etc. -gaz m. 'a yard of rope', arresting a gang of violent criminals or conspirators. -hŏgāḍa f.pl. a string of dried fish (such fish, split and dried, are kept strung together on a string). -hurᵘ̈ f. a wisp of string, joining two ropes together by opening and twisting the ends together (cf. darbi-hᵒ, p. 240a, l. 22; and razi hurᵘ̈ karüñᵘ̈, bel.). -yēr m. a rope of wool (wool is imported from the mountain country packed in the form of loosely twisted cables). ¶ razi dara lagun m.inf. 'to be stopped by a rope' (cf. dara lagun, p. 235b, l. 43), to be thrown into vacillation (by pain, an accusation, or the like). -ḍyū̃gᵘ m. (sg. dat. ḍī˜gis), a ball of string. -hurᵘ̈ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. 'to make a rope-wisp', to wind up unevenly. --khārun -- m.inf. to mount (someone or something) on to a rope, to suspend, hang (cf. pān razi khārun, p. 735b, l. 6) (Rām. 165, 1019, 1487, 1536, 1706). ¶ razan khasun m.inf. to mount on ropes, to rise to a height (of rage, hatred, grief, etc.), to be transported (with such).
m. i.q. rāza, used --˚, as in druva-rāz, p. 250a, l. 49; the superintendent of a burning ghaut (Gr.Gr. 165). Cf. rāza-bal, s.v. rāza.
m. a mason, bricklayer, plasterer (? L.V. 85, where the meaning is obscure).

m. (in the first meaning, f. rājarĕñ or röñᵘ̈, qq.v., but in the meaning of a respectable person, the f. is röz, q.v. With suff. of indef. art. the m. is rāzāh, K. 1052) a king, prince, sovereign (cf. darma-rᵒ, p. 244b, l. 43) (Gr.Gr. 39; Gr.M.; Śiv. 89, 170, 428, 431, 472, 586, 735, 810, 829, 854, 858-9, 1043, etc.; Rām. 4, 5, 28, 115, 124, 135, 137, 284, 428, 561, 1220, 1309, 1381, etc.; K. 7, 8, 10, 23-5, 49, 50, 73, 76, 493, etc.; YZ. 71; K.Pr. 48); met. a rich and powerful person (K.Pr. 75); anything or person, the best, or the largest of its kind (dayĕth-rᵒ, p. 271b, l. 27; nāga-rᵒ, p. 624a, l. 40; nruga-rᵒ, p. 650b, l. 33); the tutelary Börav (Skt. Bhairava), q.v., or godling of a burning ghaut; (or rāz) the superintendent of a burning ghaut (Gr.Gr. 165); a respectable or honourable Hindū, an esteemed person (his wife is rāza-bāy, see bel., while an esteemed Hindū female is röz, q.v.). Cf. rāja. -ünzᵘ̈ m. a flamingo. -bôgᵘ m. a royal repast; an offering of food made to a tutelary Börav (Skt. Bhairava) of a cemetery. -bal m. a cemetery or burning ghaut, a place where Hindū corpses are burnt (Gr.Gr. 165); a funeral pile (sic., El.); cf. L. 263 razbar, the track to a burning ground. -bāy f. the wife of a king, a king's queen, a queen consort (Śiv. 1237); the wife of an esteemed Hindū (see ab.). -bayĕ m. fear of (i.e. with regard to) a king. -dār or -dwār m. the gate of a king's palace (dwār, K. 376, 465, 715, 884, 939, 982, 1014); the palace itself (dwār, K. 451, 1160-1); the abode of a rich and generous person. -hams m. a flamingo (Śiv. 1475, 1516, 1752, 1810); a swan (which is said to have a beautiful voice) (L.V. 86, Rām. 1103); met. a man of high reputation for character, richness, and generosity (Śiv. 1105). -kŏmār 1 m. a king's son, a prince (Śiv. 1290). -kŏmār 2 f. a king's daughter, a princess (Śiv. 413, 971, 1285). -kŏmörⁱ, id. (Śiv. 577, 630, 786, 826, 961, 971, 1224, 1233, 1262, 1517). -kūrᵘ̈ f., id. (Śiv. 533, 655). -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a king's ram, a ram offered with other food to the presiding Börav of a cemetery (cf. rāza-bôgᵘ, ab.). -kaṭh-bögⁱ m.pl. the shares of food offered in this way (which is offered in eleven earthenware dishes); any similar shares. -kaṭh-ciñ f. the earthen dish in which these offerings are made. -kaṭh thawun to arrange such an offering. -māha f.pl. a kind of large white bean (L. 330, 339, 346, razma and razmāh). -môlᵘ m. 'a king father'; met. a liberal and generous man. -māz m. a king's flesh, i.e. his blood- relations; hence, the condition of mutual hostility ordinarily existing between a king and his blood- relations, or between him and the kings of the countries on the immediate frontier of his dominions. -nĕcyuwᵘ m. a king's son, a prince (Gr.Gr. 73); a young boy-child of a wealthy person. -nīth f. (sg. dat., K. 1071, -nīti, but usually nīʦᵘ̈, as in K. 1018), administration of a state, politics, statesmanship; courtly etiquette, courtly punctilio, the rules of precedence in a royal court (K. 1071). -pọ̆thᵃr m. (sg. dat. -pŏtras), a king's son, a prince (used when he is handsome and endowed with all royal qualifications) (Gr.M., Śiv. 919). -rāṭh m. (sg. dat. -rāṭas), a king of kings, an emperor; met. a wealthy valiant Hindū of high character. -rạthᵃn m. (sg. dat. -rạtnas), 'a royal jewel,' a virtuous, intelligent, and brave boy, who is a credit to his family and a good son. -ryoshᵘ or m. (sg. dat. -rĕshis), one of the three classes of anchorite saints (the rājarṣi of Skt.), a royal sage (Śiv. 967, 970, 1822); a king, who by his wise discrimination and pious life is regarded as equal to one of these saints. -warn m. one of royal caste, a Rājpūt (Rām. 1778). -wath f. (sg. dat. -wati), the road leading to a king's palace, or prepared and levelled for a king's progress; a king's highway, a highway, main road. -yōg m. an easy mode of religious meditation (fit for kings to practise) (in Skt. rāja-yōga), as distinguished from the more rigorous haṭh-yōg (Skt. haṭha-yōga) (cf. p. 357b, l. 45) (Śiv. 247, 597, 1067, 1312, 1689, 1833, 1857). ¶ rāzunᵘ adj. (f. rāzüñᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a king (referred to as a special person) (Rām. 1220, K. 44); a king's home, a king's palace (Rām. 1143 f, K. 17).
m. too great length, excessive length in comparison with width. Cf. rād 2.

f. empire, kingship, royalty ruling, governing (Gr.M.); the accompaniments of royalty (wealth, servants, generosity, power, and so on) (Śiv. 1285, 1822); kingdom (El.). --karüñᵘ̈ -- m.inf. to govern (Gr.M.).
m. a coronation festival (at which a great sacrifice is performed) carried out in token of a monarch's universal sovereignty (K. 1001, 1070).
m. a certain family name found among the Brāhmaṇs of Kashmīr (Skt. rājānaka, see RT.Tr. vi, 117). The N. of the author of Śiv. is Krushna Rāzdān (Skt. Kṛṣṇa Rājānaka) (Śiv. 242).

in razō-gŏn m. one of the three properties belonging to all created things. These are satū-gŏn (Skt. sattva-guṇa) the property of goodness, tamō-gŏn (Skt. tamō-guṇa) the property of darkness or ignorance, and razō-gŏn (Skt. rajō-guṇa) the property of activity (Śiv. 447, K. 320).
a wadded quilt, a coloured coverlet.
adv. by night (H. viii, 5). Cf. rāth 2.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. rāʦowᵘ), to lay on a thin coat (of paint, varnish, oil, or the like) by dipping into the appropriate medium, to coat by dipping (cf. thŏka rāʦavith, p. 973a, l. 25). rāʦowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. rāʦüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), thinly coated, as ab.

f. (sg. dat. raʦi), the seed of the Abrus precatorius, used as a weight (Gr.Gr. 66, Gr.M.); weighing as much as one of these seeds (equal to about 1 1/2 grains. In the market, the conventional raʦh is, in India, nearly 2 1/4 grains (El. ruts, m. a weight of about 8 barleycorns)); met. a very small amount of anything (cf. thāla-rᵒ, p. 975b, l. 28; thañi-rᵒ, p. 979b, l. 29). -mŏy f. a very little of anything. ¶ raʦa-pholᵘ m. a single grain of Abrus precatorius. ¶ raʦi-han (or -hanā)  or (H.) raʦhi-han (or -hanā)  f. a little, a very small amount (of something) (H. v, 6 raʦhi-han and -hanā); as adv. a little, somewhat, for a little while (Gr.M.). --raʦi -- adv. little by little, little bit by little bit, small portion by small portion (El. ratsah-ratsah).

m. (abstract noun formed from rostᵘ, q.v.) emptiness, a vacuum; the being without (something), the condition of not having or of not being accompanied by, devoidness, -lessness, freedom from (cf. önta-rᵒ or öntha-rᵒ, p. 35b, ll. 29, 32; āshi-rᵒ, p. 47b, l. 8; bala-rᵒ, p. 103a, l. 35; dagi-rᵒ, p. 193b, l. 27; dana-rᵒ, p. 222a, l. 9; darma-rᵒ, p. 244b, l. 42; hada-rᵒ, p. 322a, l. 44; mājĕ-rᵒ, p. 557b, l. 30; phala-rᵒ, p. 692a, l. 47; pāka-rᵒ, p. 725b, l. 45; prayĕma-rᵒ, p. 774a, l. 39; rūga-rᵒ, p. 828a, l. 49; shīla-rᵒ, s.v. shīl) (Gr.M.).
f. (sg. dat. rạʦhᵃrüñᵃ), proper and complete preparation (e.g. of food in cooking), putting in complete order.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. rạʦhᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. rạʦhᵃrun, q.v. rạʦhᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. rạʦhᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. rạʦhᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, see rạʦhᵃrun. rạʦhᵃrāwana āmotᵘ perf. part. pass. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), i.q. rạʦhᵃrana āmotᵘ, see raʦhᵃrun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. rạʦhᵒrᵒ), to hide or put by in a thorough manner, take great care of (Rām. 16, 1656; K.Pr. 163); to put or arrange in complete order, properly and completely to prepare (e.g. food in cooking) (Gr.Gr. 7). rạʦhᵒrᵒ- motᵘ perf. part. (f. rạʦhᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made, completely ready as ab. rạʦhᵃrana āmotᵘ perf. part. pass. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), become thoroughly prepared, hidden, etc. as ab.
or f. (sg. dat. rĕbüñᵘ̈), N. of a certain kind of rice, with a small grain and red husk. L. 463 describes as a good white rice.
f.pl. long narrow strips of cloth, malting, or the like; cf. ricĕ. --gaʦhañĕ -- f. pl. inf. (of a garment, cloth, or the like) to become worn to rags.
or m. the heart. rĕda-dôdᵘ m. pain of the heart, pain in the heart; the pain caused by love or affection. ¶ rĕdukᵘ m. (f. rĕdücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the heart; a legitimate son or daughter.

or (? cf. ریخ) f. (sg. dat. rĕki or), bird's ordure (El., Gr.Gr. 25, K.Pr. 125); --˚ used to indicate something small and worthless (cf. dūra-hȧrⁱ rĕkh, p. 238b, l. 45). --raṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to grasp bird's ordure; met. (in wordy warfare) to encourage (one of the combatants). --vĕṭhüñᵘ̈ --  f.inf. bird's dung to swell; met. a feeling of self-importance to be felt (when a request is made to one), to give oneself airs. ¶ rĕka-aḍijᵘ̈  f. the bone behind the anus, the os coccyx. -palav f. a strip of cloth worn over the privities; a rag for wiping the privities clean. -patᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a filth- mat, a rag for receiving the ordure dropped by a caged bird; met. a rag for wiping away nose-mucus (serving as a pocket handkerchief); the anus. ¶ rĕki thawun m.inf. to abscond, run away secretly; to propel (a boat on a river) so that it is distant from the bank. rĕki rĕki or adv. along the river bank (a term used only by boatmen, with reference to bringing a boat to the bank of a river). On these senses, cf. rᵃkh.
(? spelling and gender) a system of advanced payment (which renders the receiver practically the slave of the advancer) (L. 360).
or rīkhā f., i.q. rᵃkh, q.v. (cf. pādī-rᵒ, p. 681a, l. 27; pādĕ-rᵒ, p. 683a, l. 11).

or  f. a very long narrow strip (e.g. of cloth, or of land) (cf. dajĕ-zᵒ, p. 203a, l. 41; kapar-rᵒ, p. 463b, l. 33; potᵘ rĕl, p. 787b, l. 19); a strip of ground (K.Pr. 187). ¶ rĕla-bāgay or f. division into very long narrow strips (of cloth, land, etc.); the act of dividing or being divided as ab. -milawan f. (sg. dat. milavüñᵘ̈), putting together a number of such strips, piece by piece. -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), joining together such strips.
or f.pl. anxiety caused by fear (cf. potᵘ rᵒ, p. 787b, l. 24). --karañĕ -- f. pl. inf. such fear to arise; to cause such fear to arise.
