f. (sg. dat. -rēmpi), a little (of anything) (Gr.Gr. 66); used --˚ to form a diminutive or to indicate pity (cf. gurⁱ-rⁱ, p. 299a, l. 5; mahanivⁱ-rⁱ, p. 555b, l. 39; shurⁱ-rⁱ, s.v. shurᵘ; ʦū̃ṭhⁱ-rⁱ, s.v. ʦū̃ṭhᵘ) (Gr.Gr. 163).
m. debt, a debt owed (Śiv. 1004). --kāsun -- m.inf. to repay a debt (K. 473). --wasun -- m.inf. a debt to be repaid (K. 460).
m. the name used in schools for the Śāradā letter corresponding to the Nāgarī initial or non-initial. The long form of this letter is called rᵃkhav rᵘ̈ or rūkhav rū.
m. a certain bird of the spring time.
adj. c.g. wounded, sore (Rām. 1367, of the pupil of the eye).
m. a lord of anchorites, a supreme anchorite (see ryoshᵘ) (Śiv. 671; Rām. 1255, 1682).
or rĕshyuth m. (sg. dat. rĕshĕtas), the conduct of a sage or saint, conduct of such a person, saintly conduct, sainthood (Gr.Gr. 144).
m. pay, salary (El. reṭa or reta). Cf. rĕth 1.

m. the berry of the soap-wort (Sapindus emarginatus) (El. ritha; K.Pr. 119 rentane, obl. sg. as if from rē̃ṭun, q.v.). It is used esp. for washing shawls, and, according to El., a decoction of it is said to be a specific for making the hair grow. -pholᵘ m. the hard black seed inside this berry.

or m. (sg. dat. rĕtas), a season of the year (of two months, and hence six in number) (Rām. 573); (in Ksh., usually) a month (cf. aki rĕta aki, p. 20b, l. 1; phāganunᵘ rĕth, p. 685b, l. 18; prath rĕta aki phiri, p. 769a, l. 33) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1443; Rām. 661, 665, 908, 1143h; K. 241, 267, 808, 832, 864; H. xii, 4, 5, 11; K.Pr. 91, 157); (in some connexions, esp.) the hot season, (K. 250). When used as an adj. --˚, the fem. of this word is -rë̆ʦᵘ̈, as in shĕ-rë˘ʦᵘ̈ rāth, a night of (i.e. lasting) six months (K. 295). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. a month to pass, a month to elapse (H. xii, 6; K.Pr. 161); rĕth gaʦhun ādā, (a) month to go to completion, a month to come to an end (H. xii, 4, 11). ¶ rĕthāh khanḍā m. about a month, a month more or less (Gr.Gr. 93). ¶ rĕta-kāl m. a woman's menses; the hot season (Śiv. 1687; K.Pr. 30, 180, 242). -kāli adv. in the hot season. -kôlᵘ m. the hot season (El. rĕtakol; Śiv. 327). -kālas kyutᵘ or -kölis kyūtᵘ) adj. (f. --kiʦᵘ̈ --), and adv. (suitable, etc.) for the hot season; (used, etc.) in the hot season.
m. (sg. dat. rē̃ṭanas), a bad-natured troublesome person (esp. a boy); a rag (cf. dajĕ-rᵒ, p. 203a, l. 43). In K.Pr. 119, rē̃ṭun is apparently used in the sense of rē̃ṭa, q.v.
f. (sg. dat. rĕvüñᵘ̈), joyful festivity, merry-making.

m. rhubarb, Rheum moorcroftianum (El.); cf. ribās. -cīnī ریوند چینی m. (so El., but probably f.), id. According to El. it grows abundantly on the Kashmīr mountains. The natives eat stalk and blade with great fondness. The root is used as a purgative, and, when pounded and mixed with oil, as an application to ulcers.
f. N. of the daughter of Raivata and wife of Balabhadra (K. 635). The Sanskrit form of the name is Rēvatī.
n.ag. (f. rĕwavüñᵘ̈), one who joyfully carries out festivities (cf. ranga-rᵒ, p. 837b, l. 21).
or conj. 3 (2 p.p. rĕvyōv), to engage in joyful festivities, to rejoice in great happiness; to adorn oneself for a festival (K.Pr. 134, 255). See also riwun 1.

or f. an ant (El. re m., riai, riyai f.; K.Pr. 180); a tickling sensation (as if caused by ants), itchiness (cf. rata-rᵒ, p. 846b, l. 24). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an attack of itchiness to come on. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. itchiness to be felt; met. great worry to be felt, to become distraught, irritation to be experienced (Rām. 984, 1350). --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. tiny maggots to come in a wound, or in food. ¶ rĕyĕ-ôlᵘ or m. an ant's nest, an anthill (El. ré-ól). -më̆ʦᵘ̈ f. an anthill, the pile of earth over an ant's nest, the earth thrown up out of an ant's nest. -pö̃th f. (sg. dat. -pǖ̃ʦᵘ̈), a procession of ants, a line of ants. -pö̃than m. the path along which a procession of ants walks; a procession of ants. -ṭē̃g m. a sandy or gravelly mound bare of vegetation (like an anthill). -ṭhūl m. an ant's egg; met. anything very tiny. ¶ rĕyi pakun (or) m.inf. to advance very slowly and gradually towards completion or accomplishment.
adj. c.g. pouring, scattering, dropping; --˚ scattered over (with), covered with (cf. rakhᵃth-rᵃ, p. 831b, l. 29); as subst. f. a scattering, a scattered or dispersed multitude (Rām. 206).
m. a minute fragment, particle, scrap, atom, bit, piece. rēza rēza karun m.inf. to break in pieces, to smash, crush, shatter, shiver; to cut up into small pieces (Rām. 1239; H. ii, 7, rēza kᵒ).
m. means of sustenance or support, food, daily bread, subsistence. --wātanāwun -- m.inf. to supply food (to), provide sustenance (for, dat.) (K.Pr. 183).

f. distant relationship or connexion between persons, as in mātāmāl-rē̃ʦh chĕh, there is some slight relationship with (his) maternal grandfather (Gr.Gr. 163 and p. 607a, l. 30); also a piece divided off from something larger, as in kapar-rᵒ, a piece of cloth (Gr.Gr. 163 and p. 463b, l. 35).
f. dawn (El. rĕts); as adv. early in the morning (El. and W. 95 rets). Cf. rūʦⁱ.

or f. (sg. dat. rĕʦi or), a verse, stanza, hymn (esp. of the Vēda); (in Ksh.) a title given to a clan or family based on some peculiarity of the ancestor (e.g. the title ʦamürᵘ̈ given to the descendants of a leather-seller; the title of lȧngⁱ, given to the descendants of a lame man; chān, given to the descendants of a carpenter) (Gr.Gr. 66); an insulting nickname based on some early insult (e.g. someone on some particular occasion, or for some particular reason, is called 'Fool', and is afterwards, on that account, generally nicknamed 'Fool', and thereby feels insulted. Principally found among boys, or persons of weak intellect, as for example, the nicknames used among our schoolboys) (translated 'scandal' in K.Pr. 2).
m. Rhubarb, Rheum moorcroftianum (El.), i.q. rēwand, q.v.

f.pl. long very narrow rags of cloth or the like; long very thin shavings of wood or the like; cf. rē̃cĕ. --kaḍañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to wear out cloth or the like into thin rags; minutely and to the utmost detail to study a book on a subject.
(? spelling) Viburnum cotinifolium (El. ríchhábí kílmich). Cf. gūc.
m. wind, air, flatus; rheumatism, rheumatic gout.
f. a stand or rest on which a book is placed for reading, a reading desk (formed by two boards crossing each other like the letter X).
adj. c.g. (a person, or any particular limb) suffering from rheumatism or rheumatic gout; (food, etc.) which induces this disease.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. rihaladiñ), (a person, or any particular limb) suffering from rheumatism or rheumatic gout.
n.ag. (f. rikavüñᵘ̈), one who, or that which, slides along the ground; one who carries stolen property away slowly and secretly.
m. the expression of the face, the look on a person's face. --alun -- m.inf. the expression of the face to change.

or rĕkiñ f. slipperiness (on a road or the like, causing slips and falling) (cf. potᵘ rᵒ, p. 787b, l. 18); a slip and fall (on such a road), a slither (cf. potᵘ rᵒ, as ab.); cf. rᵃkan. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a slip (while walking) to occur; to have to give up one's work (owing to obstacles, unsuccess, or the like). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. slipperiness to come (on a road, owing to rain or the like); to spoil a person's efforts. --ʦalüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a slip to occur, to slip and fall down.
(cf. رکابی) f. a kind of small round deep bell-metal or copper dish (esp. used for feeding children) (El. rikib). Cf. rikᵃb.
(cf. رکابی) f. a certain kind of eating bowl, made of brass, circular in shape, and deep (Gr.M.).
m. a reprobate, drunkard, profligate, rake; a knave, a rogue (Rām. 1581, 1775; YZ. 270, 308). rinda-pöṭhⁱ adv. impudently, resolutely (Śiv. 156).

f. a very little of anything, a slight amount (e.g. a doze lasting only an instant) (cf. obura-rᵒ, p. 7a, l. 26, or ạbᵃra-rᵃ, Gr.Gr. 162, a slight cloud; dᵃha-rᵃ, p. 198a, l. 37, or dᵃ̇hᵃ̇-rᵃ̇, p. 198b, l. 27, a trace of smoke; wāwa-rᵒ, a little wind, Gr.Gr. 162; a gust of wind, Gr.M.).

m. the hawthorn berry (Cratœgus oxycantha) (El. ríng and ringo; L. 70, 79, 460 ring); the hawthorn tree or its wood. Monkeys and other creatures eat the berries; cf. ryū̃gᵘ. ringa-hüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -hacĕ), the wood of the hawthorn tree. ringa-püṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -pacĕ), a board made of the hard wood of this tree. ringa-rôchᵘ m. N. of a certain medicinal plant, described as found in the foot-hills, and as having small leaves spread over the ground. ringa-röchⁱ mūl m. the root of the preceding, used with milk, etc., as a medicine for lumbago, rheumatism, etc.
in rini rini رنہ رنہ adv. little by little, gradually (YZ. 261, 432, 478). Cf. ring.
or rīnzᵘ̈ f. a bow (the weapon); a pellet bow (El. rénz). rēnza-nĕcyuwᵘ m. a clever sharp-witted person (esp. a boy or youth).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. rinzanôwᵘ), i.q. rinzawun, q.v.

f. (sg. dat. rinzavüñᵘ̈), secretly, or by stratagem causing property to disappear, to carry off property in this manner; the absconding or escaping secretly or by a stratagem (from prison, a dunning creditor, or the like).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. rinzowᵘ), to cause (property) to disappear, i.e. secretly, or by a dishonest stratagem, to carry off property from another's possession; to escape or abscond secretly or by a stratagem (from prison, a threatened criminal charge, a dunning creditor, or the like). Cf. rinzanāwun.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. rinzōv), to escape or flee away secretly or by a stratagem (e.g. from prison, from a dunning creditor, or the like).
m. a Musalmān religious beggar (El.). I.q. ryoshᵘ, q.v. (K.Pr. 180).

f. (sg. dat. rīʦᵘ̈) manner, way, fashion, method, rule (Gr.M.); usage, custom, practice (cf. kŏl-rᵒ, p. 437a, l. 6) (Gr.M.; L. 258 rit; K. 316, 654); pomp, ceremony (El. rít, m.). --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to initiate a new custom. --nērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a new custom to become prevalent. ¶ rīʦᵘ̈, obl. sg., in (such-and-such) a manner (cf. ami rᵒ, p. 55a, l. 11; amiy rᵒ, p. 55b, l. 7). -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who follows hereditary or established custom.
f. fine airs and dress, beauty of personal array. Cf. riwun.
f. (sg. dat. rīwüʦᵘ̈), the twenty-seventh of the twenty-seven lunar mansions, called in Sanskrit Rēvatī.
n.ag. (f. riwavüñᵘ̈), one who habitually decks himself in fine apparel and ornaments.
n.ag. (f. riwavüñᵘ̈), one who is distraught with inward grief, one who mourns.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ryuwᵘ; 2 p.p. rivyōv), to deck oneself out in fine clothes and ornaments.
m. pouring, shedding, scattering, used --˚ as in khū̃-rīzī (Rām. 915), p. 402b, l. 18.

m. (when engaged in any work) diffidence, timidity, nervousness, due to another's presence, and resulting in clumsiness, slowness, and the like. --bĕhun -- m.inf. such clumsiness or slowness, due to such nervousness, to attack a person.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. rōbaladiñ), one who is slow or clumsy in his work, owing to diffidence or nervousness due to another's presence.
or robᵘ or rubᵘ m. a round depression or basin or pit made in a mass, for receiving liquid (cf. hili-robᵘ, p. 331a, l. 6).

m. (sg. ag. röchⁱ 1), a watch- man, guardian, protector (cf. atha-röchⁱ, p. 62a, l. 11; dana-rôchᵘ, p. 222a, l. 6; dranga-rᵒ, p. 247b, l. 5; gabi-rᵒ, p. 275a, l. 15; gupan-rᵒ, p. 294b, l. 43; hūnⁱ-rⁱ, p. 337a, l. 8; hurⁱ-rⁱ, p. 347a, l. 13; khal-rᵒ, p. 397a, l. 3; khana-rᵒ, p. 401a, l. 18; khĕlⁱ-rⁱ, p. 426b, l. 5; maĩshĕ-rᵒ, p. 597a, l. 14; pingi-rᵒ, p. 740a, l. 18; rāta-rᵒ, s.v. rāth 1). (El. róchh; K. 36, 65, 79, 382); a guard, warder off (in the sense of one who obstructs from approach) (Śiv. 1672).

m. a watchman, guardian, keeper, protector, custodian (cf. dana-rᵒ, p. 222a, l. 3; pāna-rᵒ 2, p. 736a, l. 7) (Rām. 374, K.Pr. 176). ¶ röchⁱ bĕhun m.inf. to sit as a guard, to guard carefully. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain on guard, to guard faithfully.

or röchᵘ̈ f. protection, preservation, guardianship (cf. dana-rᵒ, p. 222a, l. 5; darma-rᵒ, p. 244b, l. 38; dayĕ-rᵒ, p. 266a, l. 24; hūnⁱ-rⁱ, p. 337a, l. 12; khĕlⁱ-rⁱ, p. 427b, l. 3; pāna-rᵒ 1, p. 736a, l. 6; pīra-rᵒ, p. 752b, l. 50; potᵘ-rᵘ, p. 787b, l. 14; rāta-rᵒ, s.v. rāth 1) (Gr.M.). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. guardianship to occur, divine protection to be accorded (e.g. in some calamity). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to preserve, protect, save from harm (so-and-so, dat.) (El. rãchh karun; Gr.M.; K. 104, 106, 181, 246). röchⁱ-rāwȧchⁱ f. watch and ward, guarding, safeguarding, protection, shielding. -wôlᵘ m. a paid guard or watchman. ¶ rāchi-dar m. (f. -dariñ), one who keeps guard, a keeper, guardian, custodian. -dĕv m. (f. -dĕviñ), a guardian demon, a Jinn or the like who guards any particular spot from intruders.
m. an occurrence, incident (Rām. 289); an account of circumstances, a statement of a case (Rām. 1696).
f. rascally conduct (esp. of a boy's naughtiness).
adj. (f. rözᵘ̈), long, not short, lengthy in comparison to width (cf. lȧṭⁱ-rⁱ, p. 535b, l. 38) (K.Pr. 261). Cf. rād 2.
m. grease, varnish, polish (Gr.M.); clarified butter, ghī (W. 155 rog̱ẖan, L. 359, K.Pr. 180).
in rōgi wuchun m.inf. to look out for faults or flaws (in a person), to seek out (his) weak points, pick holes in him. Cf. rugᵘ and rōgun.
adj. c.g. full of love, full of affection, impassioned.
adj. c.g. skilled in singing sweet low music.
f. a certain musical mode (in Skt. rāgiṇī); N. of a certain kind of goddess (Rām. 586 rāgiñā, with suff. of indef. art.).
m. secret opposition (esp. to a subordinate or weak person).

or rūhin or rōhinī f. N. of a wife of Vasudēva and mother of Balarāma, the step-brother of Krishna (in Skt. Rōhiṇī) (K. 42 ff.); N. of the fourth lunar mansion or asterism (Śiv. 475; Rām. 124, 1108g; K. 57).
m. N. of a certain dance performed by women at the spring festival, the New Year, and similar occasions. They dance in two lines facing each other, advancing and retreating, and singing (Śiv. 1044).
f., i.q. röñᵘ̈ q.v. (sg. dat. röjñiyĕ (Śiv. 1175) or (m.c. in Śiv. 1135) rājñāyĕ), a queen (Śiv. 1135, 1175, 1518).

m. (sg. dat. rōkas), boldness, impudence, audacity (exhibited by one who is not accustomed to do so). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such audacity to occur; met. to become impeded (by fear, anxiety, or the like), to be brought to a halt (in this way). --karun -- m.inf. to do audacity, to abuse a person without cause; to impede another (in speaking, enjoying, going, or other occupation in which he is engaged).

m. (sg. dat. rō̃khas), the groin, the joint of the thigh, hip, haunch-bone, ileum (El.). ¶ rō̃kha-holᵘ adj. (f. -hüjᵘ̈), crooked-hipped. rō̃kha-rō̃kh f. a verbal quarrel (when two or more persons abuse each other).

adj. (f. rȧjⁱ or rüjᵘ̈ 1), mixed up, commingled; esp. (of something of metal, or cloth, or the like) of mixed colour (i.e. not pure), mixed with dirt or dross of the same nature as the principal ingredients (e.g. cloth which should be white, but which is spoilt by dark threads); (as subst. m.), dark-grey coloured wool, or woollen cloth (El. rúl).
m. a straining ladle, i.e. a ladle pierced with holes (for lifting food out of the oil or other liquid in which it has been cooked), a ladle and strainer in one.
or runa in rŏna-(or runa-)zŏna  m. doing some work for the sake of amusement, doing something merely to pass the time.

f.pl. small bells (strung on a string and worn round the ankle, or put about the necks of horses, cattle, and goats) (El. rŏnyi, K. 147, 184). rŏñĕ-(or ruñĕ-)gŏḍ  m. an ankle adorned with these bells. -horᵘ m. a string or set of these bells (as tied on the ankle). -mahārĕñ f. a child bride. (When a girl is married in childhood, she wears these bells on her ankles till puberty. As soon as she reaches that age, she puts off the bells and wears a veil over her head instead.) -manzulᵘ m. a child's cradle hung round with small bells.

or rung m. a clove (Rām. 205); a gold jewelled nose-ring, in the form of a clove; met. a clever impudent boy. ¶ ronga-(or runga)-ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈  f. 'clove-charcoal', the head of a clove. -ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to become the head of a clove; hence, to become dear and hard to procure. -ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈khasüñᵘ̈ f.inf. 'the clove's head to rise', to remain obstinate and resentful in spite of all entreaties, apologies, or attempts at reconciliation.
adj. (f. rünjᵘ̈), possessing (such-and-such, or so many) colours or kinds, used --˚ (cf. aiṭha-rᵒ, p. 66b, l. 35; pönʦa-rᵒ, p. 743a, l. 35).
f. a queen, a king's wife (cf. paṭa-rᵒ, p. 785a, l. 5) (Śiv. 1521; K. 730, 785, 919, 939, 942, 980, 1132). Voc. sg. (in polite address) rainyā, O Lady! (L.V. 10). i.q. röñᵘ̈, q.v.
(? spelling and gender), a kind of stiff clay, bad for agriculture, as it always cakes (L. 321). Perhaps for rôṭhᵘ, q.v.

or (q.v.) rājarĕñ f. a queen, a king's wife (El. rányí; W. 16 rāni; Śiv. 1312; Rām. 765, 1591); met. a rich and honoured wife (cf. ḍĕka-rᵒ, p. 204b, l. 20); a kind of rice with a long, thin, pale-coloured grain. Cf. röjñī. ¶ rāñĕ bĕhun m.inf. 'to sit a-queen'; hence, not to be volatile, to do one's work consistently and thoroughly. rāñĕ-brörᵘ̈ f. N. of a form of the goddess Durgā (in Skt. Mahārājñī) believed to manifest herself by miraculous changes in the colour of the water of a spring at the village of Tūla-mūla (Skt. Tūlamūlya), in the Lār Pargana about ten miles north of Śrīnagar (RT.Tr. II, 488). rāñĕ ṭhāñĕ rōzun m.inf. to devote oneself without caprice (i.e. resolutely) to some work, to buckle to and persevere, staunchly to stick to one's work (without opposition and with all one's requirements). Cf. ṭhöñᵘ̈ and rāñĕ bĕhun, ab.

(for 2, see ranun) (f. rüñᵘ̈ 2), one who has a deformed, maimed, crooked, or withered arm or hand (cf. atha-rᵒ, p. 62a, l. 15) (Śiv. 746, 1214, 1634, 1736, 1755); footless, handless (El. raun); --˚ deformed in some other limb (cf. kana-rᵒ, p. 448a, l. 32). --kāha-nēthᵃr -- m. the maimed performance of the kāha-nēthᵃr ceremony on behalf of a boy who has died before it could be performed on the 11th day after birth. See kāha-nēthᵃr, p. 387b, l. 11. ronᵘ kônᵘ adj. (f. rüñᵘ̈ köñᵘ̈), having a deformed hand (or arm) and one-eyed; met. one who has a thieving hand and the evil eye.

or rupay f. (although here reported as f., the word is by derivation and also in use m. Owing to its ending in the letter y, a typical f. termination, it has come to be treated as f. In the references below, when the gender is clearly shown, it will be indicated in each case), a rupee (the coin, also used as a weight, see bel.). The standard current rupee of British India is called dŏbal rᵒ, f. (p. 183b, l. 21) or pŏkhta rᵒ, m. (p. 727b, l. 14; but, ib. l. 17, the gen. sg. is rŏpayĕ-hondᵘ, as if of a fem. noun). The old local Ksh. rupee, worth about half the British rupee, is called khām rᵒ, m. (p. 400a, l. 19). (El. rŏpai; Gr.Gr. rupai, f. 22, rupayĕ, f.pl. 93; Gr.M., f.; H. viii, 9, 10, m.; x, 1, 2, 6, m.; K.Pr. 88, 153, 171.) -bar adj. c.g. weighing the same as a rupee, a rupee's weight of anything. -khanḍ f. about a rupee's weight, a little more or less (cf. rŏpayāh khanḍā, p. 401a, l. 12). ¶ rŏpayĕ f.pl. rupees (Gr.Gr. 93). -hondᵘ sg. gen. (of rŏpay, f.) (f. -hünzᵘ̈) of, or belonging to, or costing, a rupee (cf. pŏkhta rŏpayĕ- hondᵘ, p. 727b, l. 17). rŏpayë˘-zᵘ̈ f.pl. a number, or collection, of rupees (Gr.Gr. 93). ¶ rŏpayāh khanḍā about a rupee, but something less (Gr.Gr. 93).
adj. (f. rŏpayiñᵘ̈), costing, worth, or earning as wages, so many rupees. Used --˚, as in pönʦa-rᵒ, p. 743a, l. 38.

or ruph m. (sg. dat. rŏ(ru)pas ), silver (Gr. 41, 51; Gr.M.; Śiv. 430, 1285, 1755; Rām. 568, 1678, 1784; K. 914; YZ. 8 rôᵒ). ¶ rŏpa-(or rupa-)hörⁱ  adj. c.g. silver-speckled, i.e. covered over with a pattern traced in silver (or silver-like) dots or spots. -hôrᵘ adj. (f. -hörᵘ̈), id. -lö̃kh f. N. of 'the Silver Island' in the Ḍal lake (El. rŏpalãnk, m.). rŏpa-(or rupa-)sondᵘ  adj. (f. -sünzᵘ̈), made of silver, silvern (Gr.Gr. 41, K.Pr. 219). ¶ rŏpⁱ(or rupⁱ) raz  f. a string made of silver (e.g. for carrying ornaments on a girdle). rŏpⁱ(or rupⁱ) tᵃ̇jᵃ̇  f. a silver bodkin or needle (used for applying collyrium to the eyes). ¶ rŏpukᵘ or rupukᵘ adj. (f. rŏ(ru)pücᵘ̈ ), of, or belonging to, silver.

m. a deserter; a member of the Rāfiẓī sect of the Shī'a Musalmāns. The sect is so called because they originally deserted Zaid, the son of 'Alī, when he forbade them to speak against the Companions of the Prophet; the Shī'a sect as a whole (L. 284; W. 123; K.Pr. 6, 28). -bāy f. a woman of this sect. -hŏḍ f. the obstinacy characterizing a man of this sect.
or rupoṭᵘ m. a kind of fish with silver scales (El. ropiṭh gád, it is found in the upper parts of the Jehlam).
or rupowᵘ adj. (f. rŏ(ru)püvᵘ̈ ), made of silver, silver (esp. vill.).
or rupulᵘ m. something partly consisting of silver, something alloyed with silver; a single rupee.
(cf. رفا) m. mending, repair, esp. of shawls (El. róp). --karan-wôlᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --karan-wājĕñ --), a mender, repairer (El.); cf. rafāgar. --karawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --karavüñᵘ̈ --), id.

m. motion, walk, gait, carriage; practice, custom, fashion, usage (Rām. 1668); high appreciation (of something rare). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. high appreciation to come (esp. of something lost). ¶ rōshĕ adv. (of motion or gait) gently, quietly, softly, slowly (Śiv. 963, 1690; Rām. 1777).
f. anger, wrath, passion, rage (Rām. 1580). rōshĕ-rōsh f. mutual resentment, mutual umbrage (e.g. between husband and wife, brethren).
adj. c.g. bright, shining, brilliant; clear, evident. -gar روشنگر m. a polisher; a cutler (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to light (a lamp, etc.), to lighten, illumine (El.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. rōshĕnôwᵘ), to enrage (a person).
conj. 1, to cause to be highly appreciated. Cf. rōsh 1.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. rūṭhᵘ, q.v.; 2 p.p. rōchyōv), to become angry (with someone, dat.) (Gr.Gr. 205, 212, 231; Śiv. 1008, 1632, 1786; Rām. 1029, 1112; K. 694; K.Pr. 72). rūṭhᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. rūṭhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, sg. dat. rōchĕ-maʦĕ), angered, filled with rage or wrath.
also written m. a thick string, in chaphkali-rᵒ, p. 173b, l. 39; a necklace (H. v, 10, 12).

adj. (This word occasionally takes the form rosᵘ, as in māyĕ-rosᵘ, heartless, p. 612b, l. 7; shūbi-rosᵘ, s.v. shūb; and shē̃ki-rosᵘ, s.v. shē̃kh 2. The fem. is rüʦhᵘ̈ (Śiv. 1847, Rām. 1205, K. 843). The opposite of this word is sostᵘ, q.v.) destitute (of), deprived (of), bereft (of), without, --˚ equivalent to the English -less (as in anta-rᵒ or önta-rᵒ, endless, p. 35b, ll. 10 and 26; āra-rᵒ, merciless, p. 41a, l. 7; āshi-rᵒ, hopeless, p. 47b, l. 6; baba-rᵒ, fatherless, p. 77a, l. 14; bōchi-rᵒ, free from hunger, p. 80a, l. 34; bö̆zᵘ̈-rᵘ̈, witless, p. 83b, l. 24; bagāra-rᵒ, (cooked) without oil, p. 92a, l. 10; bala-rᵒ, without strength, p. 103a, l. 32, and many others, which will be found under the main words) (Gr.M.; El. and W. 98, rust; L.V. 61, 65, 108; Śiv. 59, 82, 86, 157, 230, 330, 335, etc.; Rām. 9, 161, 1057, 1061, 1062, 1102, 1104, 1205, 1239, etc.; K. 25, 47, 163, 165, 213, 472, 478, 615, 627, 700, 726, 843, 912, 1090 (governing dat.), 1101 (id.), 1107 (id.), etc.; H. vii, 23; YZ. 26 (governing dat.), 46, 156, 205, 431; K.Pr. 1, gāshĕ-raʦha, written gáshah raṯs̱hah, f. pl. nom.). With emph. y, we have shē̃ki-rostuy (see shē̃kh 2) used as an adv. and meaning 'fearlessly' or 'hopelessly'.
i.q. rostᵘ, q.v. cf. lōri-rosᵘ (K.Pr. 120); shūbi-rᵒ, s.v. shūb; shē̃ki-rᵒ, s.v. shē̃kh 2.
adj. (f. rüsᵘ̈), having (such-and-such) a flavour, used --˚, as in okᵘ rosᵘ (p. 19a, l. 39), q.v.
c.g. one who takes part in the rās-dance. See rās 1 (Śiv. 1459).
in rösⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. flowing water to disappear under ground; met. wealth, property, occupation, or the like to disappear for good and all.
as first member of a compound, see rāth 1.

m., impeding, obstruction, used in the following:-- rōṭa gaʦhun m.inf. impeding, obstruction to occur. -törᵘ̈ f. delay caused by obstruction. rōṭa-ʦyūṭᵘ m. improper or imperfect pulverization, pounding in a mortar, or the like. -ʦyūṭᵘ gaʦhun m.inf. (of grain) to be, or become, imperfectly pounded (in a mortar). -ʦyūṭᵘkarun m.inf. imperfectly to pound, as ab.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. rōṭanôwᵘ), to cause to be obstructed, to hinder, to stop (Gr.Gr 175). Causal of rōṭun, q.v.

f. a female demon (Rām. 321, 329, 331, 633; K.Pr. 182); a malignant witch; met. a termagant, a shrew, an ugly woman, a hag (W. 143, rāntas; K.Pr. 235); a certain plant growing on the lower hills, the smell of which is said to produce insensibility.

or ruth m. (sg. dat. rŏ(u)tas ), (among Hindūs) a religious vow (esp. of austerity or fasting) (cf. arañĕ-rᵒ, p. 44a, l. 32; gŏsöñⁱ-rⁱ, p. 309b, l. 48; shĕwa-rᵒ, s.v. shĕv). -nĕyĕm m. the strict carrying out of a fast (on some particular occasion or with some special object).
m. (sg. dat. rōṭas), thick bread, a large thick cake of bread (Gr.Gr. 22); a sweet cake offered to a god; sweetmeats offered to Hanumān.
in the following:-- röṭh-gāḍa f.pl. a collection of small fish, kept in a basket or in a reservoir. röṭh-wã̄gan m.pl. a collection of a kind of egg-plant (El. rãtwángin, the egg-plant).
m. (sg. dat. rö̃ṭhanas; f. rö̃ṭhüñᵘ̈), one who, on the occasion of another's festival or rejoicing, is accustomed to upset it by obstructing, quarrelling, or the like; a spoil-sport.
adj. (f. röṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat. rāchĕ), rough, rugged; a bully, terrorist, swashbuckler (cf. rata-rᵒ, p. 846b, l. 19).
in kāha-röthᵘ̈rᵘ̈, p. 387b, l. 28. Cf. rāth 2.
f. the bark of a vine (esp. of the grape-vine). ¶ röṭhᵃri-hurᵃ m. a rope of the twisted bark of the grape-vine. -hurᵘ̈ f. the bark of the grape-vine.
m. a naughty, disobedient, troublesome, deceitful person (esp. a child).

conj. 2 or 3 (1 p.p. rūṭᵘ; 2 p.p. (conj. 2) rōcyōv or (conj. 3) rōṭyōv, Gr.Gr. 205) to be stopped, brought to a stand, restrained (e.g. when going anywhere, or engaged in business, to be stopped by fear, or the like, or, of a machine in motion or the like, by some external cause) (cf. atha-rōṭȧnⁱ, p. 62a, l. 26; nakhᵃra rᵒ, p. 630a, l. 26) (Gr.Gr. 175, 204, 205). The causal of this verb is rōṭanāwun, q.v. rūṭᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. rūṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, sg. dat. rōcĕ-maʦĕ), come to a stop, as ab.; stopped, impeded, brought to a stop, as ab.
m. (sg. dat. rö̃ṭasas), a male demon; a malignant wizard; met. a wicked vile-tempered fellow.
m. in katha-rotᵘ, p. 486b, l. 17, q.v.

m. seizing, grasping (cf. atha-rᵒ, p. 62a, l. 19; khŏra-rᵒ, p. 409b, l. 2; khōra-rᵒ, p. 410b, l. 9) (Gr.M., K.Pr. 236); impediment, enforced delay (cf. potᵘ-rᵘ, p. 787b, l. 28); --˚ the equivalent weight of anything (= raṭh), or (as adj.) weighing the equivalent weight of anything (cf. dāñĕ-rᵒ, p. 230b, l. 48; māvi rᵒ tōl, p. 611a, l. 20; pönʦa-rᵒ, p. 743a, l. 40; pĕṭha-rᵒ, p. 795b, l. 6). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. an impediment to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to cause an impediment, to impede. ¶ rȧṭⁱ rȧṭⁱ adv. with delay, subject to impediments. -raṭa adj. c.g. the exact equivalent in weight (e.g. of grain corresponding to an amount previously borrowed) (cf. raṭi-raṭh, s.v. raṭh).

rowᵘ, or ruwᵘ m. a hollow pit or depression on a low mound (cf. saga-rᵒ, s.v. sag 2); a ripened pustule in smallpox (each with a small pit at the top); a drain-pipe (connecting two small irrigation channels). ¶ rȧvⁱ gaʦhȧnⁱ m.pl.inf. smallpox pits to ripen (as ab.). rȧvⁱ karȧnⁱ m. pl. inf., id.
adj. (1 p.p. of rāwun, q.v.; f. rövᵘ̈), lost, done away with, disappeared from ken, become non-existent.

ruy, or rōy روی m. the face, countenance (El. róe; YZ. 5, 16, 165, 259, 289; K.Pr. 194); (in Ksh.) the front part of a house, a house-front. rŏyĕ-(or ruyĕ-)dorᵘ  adj. (f. -dürᵘ̈), 'face-hard,' insolent, impudent, brazen-faced.
f. in röyijᵘ̈ kaḍüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to start a new custom, to introduce a new fashion.

m. the cedar, deodār, the Himalayan spruce, i.q. diva-dār (p. 261a, l. 39), q.v., which is the word used in Śrīnagar, röyil being the word used elsewhere (El. rãyil, L. 80, rayil; cf. El. riyál and ríyál, Picea webbiana, i.q. birre, q.v.; YZ. 563).
m. another form of rāy 1, i.q. rāza; used familiarly --˚, as in bata-rᵒ, p. 137a, l. 49.
or rözᵘ̈ f. a Hindū woman of respected and honourable position, (f. of rāza, q.v., in one of its meanings, while the wife of such a rāza is rāza-bāy).
m. day, a day of twenty-four hours (Rām. 797, 1083). -nāmca روز نامچہ m. an ephemeris, day-book, diary (Gr.M.).

f. instability, restlessness, disquietude, confusion (cf. dasta-rᵒ, p. 256a, l. 47; rata-rᵒ, p. 846b, l. 27). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. instability to fall (on a person), to be distracted, confused, disquieted (in any occupation).

f. fasting, a fast (among Musalmāns), the keeping of Lent (Ramaẓān). --darañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to practise this Lenten fast (El.). --hĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to observe this Lenten fast. --karañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to fast (El.). --thāwañĕ -- f. pl. inf. id. (El.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. rōzanôwᵘ), to cause to stop, to stop, cause to remain (El.).
n.ag. (f. rōzavüñᵘ̈), one who remains etc., see rōzun; one who continues (in a certain condition) (Śiv. 1198).
m. (f. -dariñ), one who fasts, or keeps, the Musalmān Lent (Ramaẓān). -dar rōzun m.inf. to remain fasting in this way, to keep this Lent.
m. service, employ, situation (K.Pr. 87). rōzgār-band m. one who excels his fellows in successfully earning a livelihood.
f. the conduct of a king, kingly conduct; conduct like that of a king (marked by protecting subordinates and securing their maintenance wealth and possessions, pride, and the like).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. rōziladiñ), of a vacillating temper, irresolute, of a hesitating disposition.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. rūdᵘ, Rām. 904; f. rūzᵘ̈, Rām. 580; 2 p.p. rōzōv), to remain (cf. bahāṭhāna rᵒ, p. 97a, l. 24; börⁱ rōzȧnⁱ, p. 118a, l. 50; basta rᵒ, p. 135a, l. 31; baṭhi rᵒ, p. 140b, l. 14; bayĕs tal rᵒ, p. 149b, l. 39; dabanga rᵒ, p. 184a, l. 8; dyān rᵒ, p. 268b, l. 7; khaṭith rᵒ, pp. 423a, l. 7; 423b, l. 22; lang rᵒ, p. 526b, l. 10; manaskār rᵒ, p. 582a, l. 11; namith rᵒ, p. 638a, l. 27; nēri rᵒ, p. 673b, l. 48; pajĕ-tal rᵒ, p. 724a, l. 24; pāri rᵒ, p. 753b, l. 36; pushtas rᵒ, p. 783a, l. 12; path or pata rᵒ, p. 792a, l. 42; p. 793a, l. 43; pĕṭha rᵒ, p. 795b, l. 20; sakharith rᵒ, s.v. sakharun; syodᵘ rᵒ) (Gr.Gr. 24, 247, 249; Gr.M.; K. 472, 610, 746, 962, 1057, 1067; YZ. 269, 284). ¶ to stop, to halt (cf. dubari-shāh rᵒ, p. 184b, l. 7; dōla rᵒ, p. 211a, l. 37; lari rᵒ, p. 529b, l. 31; nasti-dŏgis-pĕṭh rᵒ, p. 658b, l. 23) (Gr.Gr. 204, 212, 246, 249, 250; Śiv. 450, 1323, 1427, 1641, 1645; Rām. 1111; K. 32, 75, 261, 273, 291, 938, 980; H. vii, 9; YZ. 197, 216); to stop, stay in a place (Śiv. 1453, 1600, 1898; Rām. 532, 904, 1092, 1193, 1196, 1360, 1407, etc.; K. 154, 253, 276, 398, 465, 664; H. ii, 9; vii, 18; xii, 1; YZ. 383); to wait (for), await, be kept waiting (for) (cf. batas rᵒ, p. 137b, l. 30; shīrith pṻrith rᵒ, s.v. shērun) (Rām. 48; K. 149, 193, 643, 654, 1005); ¶ to dwell, live, abide (cf. bāl rᵒ, p. 104a, l. 8; nyāra rᵒ, p. 673a, l. 42; pānas rᵒ, p. 736a, l. 46; shĕran rᵒ; sŏkha rᵒ, s.v. sŏkh; samith rᵒ, s.v. samun; srŏdi rᵒ, s.v. srọ̆dᵘ) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 480, 702, 988, 1349, 1570; Rām. 250, 580, 1243, 1619, 1664, etc.; K. 363, 376, 603, 1107; H. vii, 6; xii, 18; K.Pr. 35); ¶ to live, or continue habitually (in a certain condition) (cf. bāzĕ-pĕṭh rᵒ, p. 153a, l. 10; mīlith rᵒ, p. 569a, l. 2; pākh rᵒ, p. 726a, l. 5; praʦaras rᵒ, p.771b, l. 33; pyāla hĕth rᵒ, p. 814a, l. 25; shē̃ki rᵒ, s.v. shē̃kh 2; sĕka rᵒ; sŏra rᵒ, s.v. sŏr; satas- pĕṭh rᵒ, s.v. sath 1) (Śiv. 422, 587, 630, 827, 876, 897, 986, 1015-6, 1021, 1239, 1350, 1485, 1689, 1696, 1802-3, 1806, 1812, 1822, 1839; Rām. 240, 382, 689, 870, 886, 1066, etc.; K. 793, 969; H. vii, 23); ¶ to continue (cf. āsh rōzüñᵘ̈, p. 47a, l. 49; baḍith rōzun, p. 87a, l. 13; brö̃ʦᵘ̈ rᵒ, p. 127b, l. 39; brã̄th rōzüñᵘ̈, p. 127b, l. 35; bayĕ rᵒ, p. 148b, l. 26; ḍakha rᵒ, p. 205b, l. 43; danjĕ rᵒ, p. 226a, l. 14; ḍanja rᵒ, p. 227b, l. 7; hĕkᵃth rōzüñᵘ̈, p. 329b, l. 38; hōsh rᵒ, p. 353a, l. 12; khara rᵒ, p. 408b, l. 22; līn rᵒ, p. 525a, l. 41; lay rōzüñᵘ̈, p. 543a, l. 19; layĕ rᵒ, p. 543a, l. 22; magar rᵒ, p. 552b, l. 23; mani rᵒ, p. 572b, l. 11; pāma rōzañĕ, p. 733b, l. 6; parda rᵒ, p. 756b, l. 6; prasan rᵒ, p. 767b, l. 39; röchⁱ rᵒ, p. 824a, l. 19; rözⁱ rᵒ, p. 858a, l. 19; rōzdār rᵒ, p. 858a, l. 45; shŏngith shāph rᵒ, s.v. shŏngun; sŏkhĕth rᵒ; sŏrith rᵒ, s.v. sŏrun; sōṭh rᵒ) (Gr.M.; L.V. 65; Śiv. 106, 276, 375, 584, 596, 876, 1598, 1775; Rām. 11, 171, 198, 683, 723, 1246, 1711; K. 74, 78, 336, 499, 511, 864, 1036; H. i, 5; x, 1, 3, 6, 8; YZ. 260; K.Pr. 12 rodum for rūdum); to remain unchanged, persist, endure (cf. niyĕth rōzüñᵘ̈, p. 674b, l. 9; phikir rōzüñᵘ̈, p. 690b, l. 23; phirun rᵒ, p. 707b, l. 5; pūrᵘ rᵒ, p. 755b, l. 2; priwa rozañĕ, p. 772a, l. 23; rāy rōzüñᵘ̈, p. 854b, l. 17; shŏd rōzun; shig rozüñᵘ̈; shĕkh rōzun, s.v. shĕkh 2; shē̃kh rōzüñᵘ̈, s.v. shē̃kh 2; shĕl rōzun; shĕyĕ rᵒ, s.v. shāy; sumᵃran rōzüñᵘ̈; sŏr rōzun) (Śiv. 128, 189, 284, 327, 329, 348, 491-2, 738, 844, 935, 1277, 1540, 1582, 1651; Rām. 30, 509, 533, 660-1, 761, 803, 858, etc.; K. 69, 263, 1091, 1113; YZ. 72, 204; K.Pr. 178, 243); (of the mind or feelings) to remain unmoved, not to be enraged or agitated (K. 279, 1057); (to be put into a certain condition and) to remain (in it) (cf. nākh dōla rᵒ, p. 629a, l. 50; süʦᵘ̈ rᵒ, s.v. sath 2) (Rām. 146; K. 273; H. xii, 15); ¶ to continue alive, go on living, survive (from some illness, or the like) (K. 804, YZ. 246); to be left, to remain behind, to be left over and above, survive (cf. bökⁱ rᵒ, p. 98b, l. 30; dāg rᵒ, p. 194a, l. 11; dam rᵒ, p. 216b, l. 19; gōr rᵒ, p. 297b, l. 12; nĕb rᵒ, p. 619b, l. 24; nishāna rᵒ, p. 656b, l. 32; phih rᵒ, p. 686a, l. 39; pharkh rōzüñᵘ̈, p. 704b, l. 19; pali rōzun, p. 730a, l. 39; sār rᵒ; srah rᵒ; sarmāyĕ rᵒ; sūrath rᵒ) (L.V. 2, 67; Śiv. 55, 1650, 1671, 1824; Rām. 13, 1114, 1379, 1392, 1459, 1520, 1660, etc.; K. 45; H. vii, 20; YZ. 42); to (remain behind, and) be all that is left (cf. nām rōzȧnⁱ, p. 636, l. 5) (Śiv. 1658; K. 563, 660, 761; H. xii, 23); to remain (concealed), keep oneself hidden (cf. shē̃kani rᵒ, s.v. shē̃kun) (L.V. 44; Rām. 496, 502, 728, 838, 955, 1007, etc.; K. 7, 811). ¶ This verb is often used in a sense that is practically an intransitive or passive counterpart of the verb raṭun, to take hold of, as in dŏd raṭun, to stop the flow of milk, dŏd rōzun, the flow of milk to be stopped, p. 188a, ll. 36, 37. For further examples, see under raṭun, p. 850b, l. 15 ff. ¶ rūdᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. rūzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), that which has remained, continued, etc., as ab. (cf. danjĕ rᵒ, p. 226a, l. 11; nam tal rᵒ, p. 635b, l. 14; pajĕ-tal rᵒ, p. 724a, l. 20) (Rām. 761; K. 5; H. i, 5; xii, 23). ¶ rūzith gaʦhun m.inf. to remain over and above, to be saved up (day by day out of daily expenditure); (of a disease) to become chronic, permanent (cf. pōr rᵒ gᵒ, p. 753b, l. 21); to be suddenly compelled to stop (when doing something) (cf. atha rᵒ gᵒ, p. 66a, l. 33) (Śiv. 1451).

adj. c.g. pleased (with, dat.), well-pleased, content (Gr.M. rözī; Śiv. 212, 679 rözī; K.Pr. 68 rází, 93, 145 rázi). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be pleased (with, dat.), to approve (of, dat.); to be satisfied (with), content (with); to assent (to), assent (to), acquiesce (in); to become conciliated, reconciled, pacified. --karun -- m.inf. to please, gratify; to content, satisfy; to persuade, win over (Rām. 5); to conciliate, reconcile. --rōzun -- m.inf. to continue pleased with, satisfied with (e.g. with a servant) (YZ. 269). --thawun -- m.inf. to please, satisfy (e.g. a servant satisfying his master with continued service), oblige (Gr.M.).
or rūʦh f. (sg. dat. rōʦi), preference (Gr.Gr. 126, Gr.M. rūʦh). Cf. rūʦᵘ̈.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. rūʦᵘ, 2 p.p. (Gr.Gr. 224) rōʦyōv) to be preferred, to be beautiful, agreeable, desirable (Gr.Gr. 125, 175, 204, 224; L.V. 21; Rām. 1749). The causal of this verb is rōʦanāwun (Gr.Gr. 175).
in rū-wã̄gan m.pl. tomatos (El. rú wángún, m.sg. rúíwángín, sg.f.; L. 346 ruángan). Cf. bŏṭa-wã̄gun, p. 138b, l. 41.

f. protection (Gr.Gr. 121); a written charm worn on the neck, arm, or other part of the body, as protection against demoniacal possession (Rām. 1575); a book or document, the contents of which are secret (e.g. mysteries); a written charm or amulet carried by Musalmāns inside the ḍōlᵃna (q.v., p. 214a, l. 41). According to El. (s.v. rach) it consists of the names of God, or the name of Muḥammad, or the Musalmān creed, or the names of the greatest Muslim Saints, or passages from the Qur'ān. The name may also be used for the ḍōlᵃna together with its contents. ¶ rachĕ karañĕ f. pl. inf. to do guardings, to guard with great care and precautions. --karith thawun -- m.inf. to put in some safe place and guard securely and carefully. ¶ rachi-troṭᵘ m. a kind of necklace.

m. (pl. dat. rūdan not *rōdan, Gr.Gr. 51), a river, stream; (in Kāshmīrī) rain, rainfall, a shower (Gr.Gr. 18, 51, 252, 257; Gr.M.; W. 115 rud; L. 463 rud; Śiv. 713, 1391; Rām. 472, 863, 1545; K. 318-20, 325, 1087, 1137; K.Pr. 59, 181, 245, 248). --darun -- m.inf. rain to stop. --karun -- m.inf. to pour forth rain, to give rain (K. 317). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. rain to fall, to rain (El.; Gr.M.; K. 75, 325; K.Pr. 181). ¶ rūda-obur m. (sg. dat. oburas or abras), a rain-cloud. -bubur m. (sg. dat. -bubaras; pl. nom. also -babar), a rain-bubble, a single bubble formed on the surface of water or the like by rain falling on it; (in the pl.) a mass or quantity of such bubbles formed in this way, rain-froth. -bubarāy f. a clot or network of bubbles formed as ab. -barutᵘ or -borutᵘ adj. (f. -barüʦᵘ̈), full of rain, wet through with rain, covered with drops of rain. -barith adj. c.g., id. -chŏkh m. (sg. dat. -chŏkas), a rain-blow, a short violent torrent of rain (local in character). -cholᵘ adj. (f. -chȧjⁱ or -chüjᵘ̈), washed or cleaned by rain; as subst. m. a heavy fall of rain (lasting a considerable time). -chyukᵘ m. a rain-squirt, a slight shower of rain, a light gentle fall. -ḍaliñ f. a rain-slope, a sloping gutter or similar arrangement at the back of a house-roof for carrying off rain. -dāra f. a steady stream of rain. -dorᵘ m. a break in rain, a period of fine weather between rainfalls, or after long rain. -darĕr m., id. -gaṭa f. darkness accompanying, or caused by, rain; a dark night with rain. -jȧrⁱ f. a continued downfall of rain, a long rainfall. -kᵒtᵒ adj. (f. -kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), wet with rain, soaked with rain (e.g. clothes), covered (e.g. a lotus-leaf) with rain drops. -kᵃʦar m. the condition of being soaked or covered with rain, as ab. -lawa f. a light shower of rain, consisting in the sprinkling of only a few sparse drops. -nôrᵘ m. a drain for carrying off rain from a roof or the like to an outside cistern or the like. -nörᵘ̈ f. a rain-pipe or gutter (on a house or the like). -palav m. a rain-coat, a waterproof cloak, or the like; a garment wet through with rain. --pĕñĕ -- f.pl. rain fallings, a time or occasion in which rain is falling heavily. -pashpay f. the trickling of rain-drops (e.g. from a roof, or the like, after a heavy fall). -pĕwan f. (sg. dat. pĕvüñᵘ̈), the time during which rain falls, a rainy season. -rūd f. rain upon rain, incessant rain (lasting several days). -rāṭh f. (sg. dat. -rāṭhi), a short heavy fall of rain. -rᵃy f. a certain small bird. It foretells rain by continuous wailing; met. a baby that wails continuously. -rᵃy ganḍüñᵘ̈ f.inf. 'to set up the rain-witch'. In times of excessive rain, a doll made of old rags is fastened to a stake and set up in the ground. Offerings are made at its foot, and it is then beaten on the head with shoes. This is believed to cause the rain to cease, and is indicated by this phrase. -tūdotdot;rᵘ̈ f. the coolth of rain, esp. the coolness after rain in the hot weather. -traṭh f. (sg. dat. -traṭi), a thunderbolt accompanying violent rain. (The thunderbolt or lightning is looked upon as itself fiery rain.) -ṭās m. a short violent, but local, burst of rain (esp. in the rainy season). -ʦhĕviñ f. cessation of long continued rain. -ʦhĕviñĕn or -ʦhĕwawạñĕn adv. at the time of such cessation of rain, (going, doing, etc.) when the rain has stopped. -ʦhĕwawunᵘ m. the time of the cessation of such continued rain. -ʦhĕwawạñĕn adv., see -ʦhĕviñĕn, ab. -ʦhĕway f. cessation of rain. -vēla m. the time of rain, the season when rain falls, the rainy season, the rains. -wālay f. the descent of rain, the time during which rain is actually falling. -wôñᵘ m. rain-water (Gr.Gr. 73, W. 115).

rudᵃr, or rudar m. (sg. dat. rudras), the same as ludr, q.v. a N. of the god Śiva (Śiv. 2, 39, 57, 1423, 1466; K. 579, 619, 620, 625, 790, 823); N. of a group of gods, eleven in number, supposed to be inferior to Śiva, who is said to be its head (Śiv. 522); Śiva, as present in fire (Śiv. 153, 1120, 1174). ¶ rudra-manthᵃr or -mantᵃr m. N. of a certain formula or mystical verse sacred to Śiva (Śiv. 126). -sandyā or f. N. of a certain sacred place (tīrtha) sacred to Śiva (Śiv. 1496).
or rudᵃr m., i.q. lọ̆dᵃr, q.v., coral (Śiv. 1310, 1871).

or rōg m. a disease, sickness, malady, distemper (Gr.Gr. 18; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1541, 1572, 1855). ¶ rūga-hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), stricken by disease. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), free from disease, healthy. -raʦhar m. freedom from disease, good health, healthiness (often, but not only, used in blessings or the like expressions of approval). -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), suffering from disease or from an illness; suffering from the subsequent consequences of an illness (thinness, weakness, and so forth).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. rūgaladiñ), an invalid, one who suffers from a chronic or long illness.
adj. c.g. an invalid, one who suffers from a long continued or chronic illness; miserable (El. rógí).
in rugölⁱ-ʦādar f. a kind of blanket woven of woollen threads of varied colours. Said to be not strong.
in rugᵘwuchun m.inf. to bear a grudge against (a person), to act malevolently towards. Cf. rōgi.
m. in bumi-ruh, a quick movement of the eyebrows (bumb). See p. 108a, l. 6.
m. (see W. 18) the spirit, soul, life (W. 18 ruḥ); possession by a demon (epilepsy or the like), or by a spirit (as in prophecy); a spirit of the dead, (in pl.) the dead (K.Pr. 181).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. rūhaladiñ), possessed by a demon, under the influence of demoniacal possession (i.e. epileptic or the like).
adj. c.g. easily discomposed, easily perturbed, panicky.
(? spelling and gender) a certain plant used in dyeing. Mixed with other dyes it furnishes a khākī and black colour (sic) (L. 68).
m. N. of a certain medicinal plant said to have long leaves and a root shaped like ginger, and to grow in the highlands. It is given to cattle as a tonic.
(for 1, see rolᵘ)  f. a long procession of many people. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a procession to be formed.
m. the name used in schools for the Śāradā letter corresponding to the Nāgarī ru. Cf. rā ar kharã̄ rṻ, p. 823a, ll. 21, 23.

m. (sg. dat. rukhsatas), permission (El.); leave of absence; permission to depart (Gr.M., K.Pr. 217). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give leave to depart, to allow to go, bid good-bye to (a person going) (Gr.M.; Rām. 168; H. xii, 25). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take leave, go on leave, take furlough (Gr.M.); to receive permission to depart, take leave (of a person, dat.) (Śiv. 56, 83, 694, 1167; Rām. 1180, 1183, 1678; H. xii, 10, 13). --karun -- m.inf. to send (a person or persons) away, to dismiss (a court) (Gr.M., Rām. 1757).
m. N. of the eldest son of King Bhīṣmaka, and brother of Rukmiṇī, in Skt. rukmin (K. 640-1, 652, 662-3). See rukman.

or, rukmin, or rukminī f. N. of the daughter of Bhīṣmaka king of Vidarbha, and sister of Rukmin (see rukm). She was betrothed to Śiśupāla, but she secretly loved Kṛṣṇa. Kṛṣṇa carried her off before she could be married to Śiśupāla. She became Kṛṣṇa's wife and mother of Pradyumna (Śiv. 703, 1370, 1437, 1441, 1669; K. 639, 641-2, 647-8, 655 ff., 734-5 ff., 832, 920, 928-9, 1051, 1062, 1128, 1130, 1145 ff.).
(? spelling) m. Mallotus Philippinensis (El. who calls it Rottleria tinctoria, a name not now used. Cf. kamīla).

m. the hair (or a hair) on the body of man or beast, down, wool (Rām. 635, 1722); a crack (in an earthenware or metal dish, in a wooden board, or the like); met. an instant, a moment, the twinkling of an eye (L.V. 104; Rām. 408, 887, 1193, 1196); (as adj. c.g.) lasting only for an instant, taking only an instant for performance. rum rum shĕrmanda thawȧnⁱ to make every hair ashamed, to overwhelm a person with benefits. rum-rāṭh f. (sg. dat. -rāṭhi), 'the seed bed of the hairs,' i.e. the original place from which any person, family, animal, or plant has sprung, the original birthplace, cradle of a race or family. -rāṭh gālüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to destroy a person (and his entire family, root and branch) (Rām. 727, 1387). -rāṭh zālüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to set on fire the cradle of a family, i.e. to abuse a person and his ancestors back to the foundation of his family. ¶ ruma-dāh m. (of a corpse on the funeralpyre) a very slight burning (just sufficient to burn the down on the body); met. (of anything else) a mere touch of burning. ruma-jath f. (sg. dat. -jüʦᵘ̈), (of a fleece) the short wool on the legs of the animal, useless for spinning, refuse wool. --ruma -- adv. in every hair, down to the last hair, entirely, utterly (Rām. 1775; K. 475, 509). ruma-ryoshᵘ m. in Hindū legend, N. of a celebrated saint, in Skt. Lōmaśa-ṛṣi, who accompanied the Pāṇḍava heroes of the Mahābhārata on their journey to sacred places; N. of another saint, in Skt. Lōmaśa or Lōmaharṣaṇa, who was famous for his long life (Rām. 1465). ruma-rĕshyunᵘ āy m. the long life of Lōmaharṣaṇa, an expression employed in wishing blessings to a servant or child. ruma-raz f. a wool-rope, a rope made of wool or goats' hair. ruma-ʦhorᵘ adj. (f. -ʦhürᵘ̈ 1), (of a man, or one of his limbs) wanting, or deprived of, the down or hair properly grown there. -ʦhürᵘ̈ 2 f. a kind of basket-shaped hat made of Ladakhī woollen cord, worn by the inhabitants of that country. Cf. ʦhürᵘ̈ 2. ¶ rumāh m. a single hair; as adv. for a moment, but for a moment, in (or during) an instant.
m. the down of the human body or beast, wool; cf. rum. rūma-dāh m. slight burning, i.q. ruma-dāh, l. 5, ab., q.v. -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), (of man, beast, tree, or the like) covered thickly with down.
(? spelling and gender), a certain vegetable, equal to the finest English rhubarb, but not so acid (L. 72).
f. N. of the produce of a certain food plant, described as drum-shaped, of a slight dark red colour, two or three times as large as a bean, and ripening in the autumn.
adj. (f. rumȧjⁱ), hairy downy (esp. on parts where such should not be). Cf. rūmal.
f. a handkerchief, a towel, a napkin (rumāli-kĕth, in a kerchief, H. iii, 2).
adj. c.g. heavily and thickly covered with hair or down (e.g. an animal's body, a tree, or a root). Cf. rumal.
adj. c.g. (of a metal, earthenware, or wooden vessel, or the like) showing a crack, cracked.
adj. (f. rumüvᵘ̈), (a rope, or the like) made of hair or wool.

conj. 1 to plant, to dibble a plant into the ground, to transplant (rice seedlings or the like) (L. 459, 462). This word seems to be a by-form of ruwun, q.v.; noted only in L. Possibly there is a slip of the pen for ruwun.

m. (sg. dat. rṻnis, abl. röni or raini), a husband (from the point of view of the wife), a woman's husband (Gr.Gr. 20; W. 6, 18 run; K.Pr. 70, 95, 131, 134, 145, 182 (voc. written ryno), 201). Cf. rüñᵘ̈ 1. ¶ röni-süʦhᵘ̈ f. a virtuous wife whose husband is alive. ¶ rǖnⁱ-büḍⁱ f. a very lovely, well-educated, fortunate married woman whose husband is alive. -dôdᵘ m. husband-love, the intense love shown to her husband by a wife. -gurus m. (sg. dat. -gurasas), 'husband's milk,' hence (out of a collection of a variety of food) a tit-bit reserved for, or offered to, a particular person. -grākañ f. a woman who owns a husband, i.e. a woman whose husband is alive. -müʦᵘ̈ f. 'husband-mad', a woman who is infatuated with her husband. -sövᵘ̈ f. a woman who is happily married to a rich, prosperous, and exemplary husband. -sāway f. the condition of such a woman as the preceding, the state of a happy wife. -wājĕñ f. a woman whose husband is alive. -wôrᵘ m. or -wörᵘ̈ f. N. of a tract to the north-east of Śrīnagar, said to have been a residence of King Raṇâditya (see RT. Tr., p. 86) and hence said by popular tradition to have been called in Skt. Raṇâditya-vāta or -vāṭikā, although really (RT. Tr. II, 451) the ancient name was Rājāna-vāṭikā; cf. ranga-wörᵘ̈, p. 837a, l. 49. -warg m. a husband's duties or necessary conduct (in regard to his wife). -vë̆ʦᵘ̈ f. a woman whose husband is alive, a woman who has been legally married.
f. a queen (Rām. 766); a man's wife (from the point of view of the husband) (K.Pr. 102, 201, rani; Rām. 1241; K. 453; YZ. 375 reñen; K.Pr. 12, 91, 102, 122, 182, 201, 205). Cf. rūnᵘ.

m. (sg. dat. rṻpas), form, figure, appearance (cf. brahma-rᵒ, p. 121a, l. 11; jyōti-rᵒ, p. 380b, l. 19; shiwa-rᵒ, s.v. shiv; shyāma-rᵒ, s.v. shyām 3; sǖrĕ-rᵒ, s.v. sṻrĕ; satya-rᵒ, s.v. satya; swa-rᵒ, s.v. swa), (El. rúp, rúph; L.V. 15; Śiv. 6, 29, 39, 92, 94, 97, 98, 100-4, 108, 115, 170, etc.; Rām. 6, 23, 63, 285, 1121, 1765, 1771, 1779; K. 159-60, 171, 238, 411, 439, 458, etc.); a handsome form or figure, beautiful form, beauty, elegance (Gr.Gr. 138; Śiv. 896; Rām. 6, 520; K. 51, 211-2, 741, 747); a disguise (El.; K. 192, 365). (El. also gives rúp, f. a copy.) -bal m. form and strength; (a formula used in blessings, etc.) beauty and power. ¶ rǖpa-gürᵘ̈ f. a maid-servant or female attendant in the women's apartments. -hāl 1 f. (sg. dat. -höjᵘ̈), a woman's toilet-room, her dressing-room; -hāl 2 f. a kind of rice with a fine long white grain. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), fully of beauty, exceedingly beautiful. -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), id.
adj. c.g. (as subst. m., dat. rṻpiṭas) well-formed, handsome, beautiful, very beautiful (Gr.Gr. 138; Gr.M. rūpiṭh; Śiv. 940; Rām. 342, rṻpīṭh, m.c., 1258).

adj. c.g. possessing the appearance of, acting in the character of; used --˚, as in b(h)ārĕ-rᵒ, in the character of a wife (cf. börⁱyā); mātru-rᵒ, in the character of a mother; māyĕ-rᵒ, in the character of a deceiver (all three in L.V. 54); zaḍa-rᵒ, stolid like an insentient block (L.V. 20) (K. 50, 105, 356, 369, 490).
m. (sg. dat. rūshwatas), a bribe (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to offer a bribe, to bribe, corrupt (El.).
adj. c.g. grown, sprung up (of vegetation) (YZ. 13).

m. a kind of black antelope (the skin of which is looked upon as specially pure). (El. ros, rús, the musk deer; so L. 116, rass or rous, Moschus moschiferus). ¶ rūsⁱ-koṭⁱ m. (f. -küṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. kacĕ), the young of this antelope (Śiv. 493, f.; Rām. 1272, f.). -musla m. the hide or skin of this antelope, which, being pure, is used as a sitting-mat by Hindū devotees.
adj. (1 p.p. of rōshun, q.v.; f. rūṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat. rōchĕ), irascible, bad-tempered, easily enraged, peppery, fiery-tempered (K.Pr. 182).
adj. (f. rūṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. rōcĕ, 1 p.p. of rōṭun, q.v.), one who, or that which, is obstructed; one who, or that which, obstructs.
m. transplanting (rice or the like) in atha-ruv, p. 62a, l. 28. Cf. ruwun.
m. in ruv karun m.inf. to perform a kind of dance in which women in two lines face each other (Śiv. 954). Cf. rŏy and Persian رو

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ruwonᵘ), to transplant; to plant (a post or the like) in the ground, to fix (a beam or block of stone or the like) in its place (in a wall or the like). ruwonᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ruvüñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), transplanted, planted, fixed, as ab.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ruwᵘ), to bury tightly in the ground; to transplant, plant in the ground (plants or the like) (Gr.Gr. 22, K.Pr. 10). Cf. runun.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. rivyōv), to be distraught with inward grief, to mourn (El. rewun, to mourn, ryiwun, to weep, the latter according to El. being said to be obs.) (Rām. 119, 202, 261, 288, 438, 1082, 1168, 1179, 1193, 1503, 1600; H. vii, 22; YZ. 41, 102, 205, 247, 363, 436).
f. the root of a certain wild plant, used for dyeing cloth black (? El. riaul, rāl, Mimosa rubicaulis).
? f. a disease (noted only in L.V. 8).

f. daily food, sustenance. Used in the obl. case rūzī, for rūziyi, in the following:-- rūzī dyunᵘ m.inf. to give for sustenance, provide for maintenance (YZ. 395); hence, to obtain materials or occupation which provide sustenance. --ladun -- m.inf. (by good fortune) to obtain sustenance or a living quite easily and without exertion. --prāwun -- m.inf. to obtain a means of livelihood (when in poverty). --ʦhĕnun -- m.inf. one's means of livelihood to be destroyed.

(cf. روزینہ) m. the amount of rice or other grain, taken with one during absence from home or the like, viaticum, ration. -mŏṭh f. (sg. dat. -mŏṭhi), a fistful of ration, enough food for a couple of meals or so for one person. -pholᵘ m. all the grain which a traveller takes with him as food for his journey.

f. (sg. dat. rōʦĕ), liking, taste, longing for something (e.g. food) present before one's eyes, greediness (Śiv. 752, 1649); preference; cf. rōʦh. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a taste (for something hitherto not appreciated) to be acquired.

(also written) or rish (K.Pr. 180) m. (sg. dat. rĕshis), an inspired sage (in Skt. ṛṣi), a sanctified sage, a saint, ascetic, anchorite. There are three classes of these saints called in Skt., respectively, dēvarṣi, or divine sage, brahmarṣi (cf. brahma-rᵒ, p. 121a, l. 14) or Brahma sage, and rājarṣi, or royal sage (cf. ruma-rᵒ, p. 834a, l. 13; rāza-rᵒ, s.v. rāza) (El. ríshi; Gr.Gr. 144; Śiv. 36, 670, 967, 970, 1822; Rām. 49, 78, 80-1, 85, 98, 106, 122, 144, 622, 633, 636, 639, 784, 790, 1465, 1726, etc.; K. 26, 127-9, 136, 139, 243, 305-6, 308, 347, 484, 614-8, 622, 817, 1038-9, 1042-3, 1054; K.Pr. 22). A group of seven of these ṛṣis was composed of saints named Marīci, Atri, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Vasiṣṭha, who were identified with the seven stars forming the constellation of Ursa Major (cf. sata-rĕshⁱ, s.v. sath 3) (Śiv. 77, 675, 686, 1149, 1157); the keeper of a Hindū temple (El. resh; L. 287, rishi). ¶ rĕshⁱ-bālukh  m. (sg. dat. -bālakas), an anchorite's son (Rām. 233, 1328, 1380, 1413) (so -zāda, Rām. 232); met. a well-behaved boy (usually looked upon as poor, and of excellent disposition). -bāpār m. the conduct of an anchorite; met. conduct like that of an anchorite (marked by uprightness and benignity). -bāy f. an anchorite's wife; met. a virtuous woman. -ḍulᵘ m. a large irregularly shaped earthen vessel, without ornament, such as would be used by an anchorite. -khand  m. 'an anchorite's smile', tantalizing (a person, as a practical joke); cf. khanda. -khrāv f. an anchorite's wooden shoes; met. a pair of wooden shoes or clogs roughly and unevenly made, and unornamented. -kŏl m. 'the anchorite's brook', N. of a well-known river of Kashmīr, in Bring (Skt. Bhṛṅga) and other Parganas. -kŏmörī f., i.q. rĕshⁱ-kañĕkh, and rĕshⁱ-kūrⁱ, bel. -kañĕkh f. (sg. dat. -kañĕki), i.q. the next. -kūrᵘ̈ f. an anchorite's unmarried daughter; met. a virtuous well-behaved daughter of excellent family but poor and simply attired, i.e. whose only claim to be marriageable is her good character and her good breeding. -mar m. an anchorite's hut; met. a simple forest hut such as that which would be an anchorite's dwelling. -morᵘ m. a sage's body (worn away by much fasting); met. anyone's body wasted away as if by fasting. -pō̃bürᵘ̈ f. a shawl of pashmīna woven from black and white thread, such as was worn in olden times by anchorites. -pahörᵘ̈ f. an anchorite's hut. -tônᵘ m. anchorite-hood, the mode of life of an anchorite, living as an anchorite. ¶ rĕshi-môlᵘ  m. 'an anchorite father', a certain sādhu or holy man who long ago made his abode in Anathnāg (p. 36a, l. 2) or Islāmābād, and whose fame remains to this day. -mālyunᵘ m. a sacred spot in a suburb of Anathnāg, traditionally associated with the preceding Sādhu, but now a Musalmān shrine. -pīr m. N. of a famous Brāhmaṇa of high character, who lived at Śrīnagar in the quarter known as Balanḍimar (Skt. Balâḍhyamaṭha) in the days of the Emperor Aurangzēb. -pīra-sondᵘ m. a sacred spot associated with the preceding Brāhmaṇa. Here vows are paid in token of the fulfilment of some longing.

/?/ or adj. (f. -rë̆ʦᵘ̈ or), of, or belonging to, or lasting a month (cf. rĕth) used --˚, as in aiṭha-rẹ̆tᵘ (p. 66b, l. 37, misprinted ṛĕtᵘ̈), produced in eight months; nawa-ryotᵘ (p. 664a, l. 37), nine months old; pönʦa-rᵒ, p. 743a, l. 44; sata-rᵒ, s.v. sath 3.
m. (sg. dat. richis), an insolent, abusive fellow; a coarse, rude fellow.

m. (sg. dat. rīgis), a certain plant (? a kind of Hibiscus), described as a kind of lotus that grows on dry land. According to El. (s.v. ryúg) its juice mixed with honey is said to be efficacious in amenorrh œa.

m. in the following:-- rī̃gⁱ-pōsh m. N. of a certain plant, described asspreading over the ground and producing yellow flowers in the spring before the leaves sprout. (This can hardly be the same as ringa, the hawthorn, q.v., although El. spells the latter as ríng). ? cf. ryūgᵘ.

m. (sg. dat. rīnzis), a small ball or pellet (esp. a ball, usually of lac, employed in a certain game, in which it is held between the thumb and fore-finger of the right hand, and flicked at a mark with the middle finger of the left hand) (cf. guhⁱ-rⁱ, p. 280b, l. 33) (L.V. 66; Śiv. 353; H. v, 3-5; K.Pr. 190, 263). rīnzⁱ-pholⁱ m., id.
m. one who distresses or causes worry to another, following him, persecuting him, and interfering in his work.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. rᵃḍanôwᵃ), to cause trouble, calamities, disease, or the like, to beset a person and become thoroughly established (Gr.Gr. 175).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. rᵃḍyōv), (of some incurable disease, calamity, or the like) to beset a person and become thoroughly established; to become subject to abuse, cursing, reviling. The causal of this verb is rᵃḍanāwun (Gr.Gr. 175). ¶ rᵃḍith gaʦhun m.inf. (of defilement, disgrace, calamity, disease, or the like) to beset (a person) and become thoroughly established. ¶ rᵃḍyō-motᵃ perf. part. (f. rᵃḍyē-müʦᵃ), (of a calamity, incurable disease, or the like) thoroughly established; beset by abuse, etc.

rikan or rĕkan f. (sg. dat. rᵃküñᵃ etc.), (on a slippery surface) a slip and fall, a slither (cf. potᵘ rᵒ, p. 787b, l. 16); a slip or fall from one's business (cf. potᵘ rᵒ, as ab.); loss of one's employment; slipperiness (of a road or the like); cf. rikiñ. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a slip (while walking) to occur; to fall from one's business, to be deprived of one's employment, to have to give up one's work (owing to obstacles, unsuccess or the like). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause such slipperiness, (of a road) to become slippery; to cause a person to give up his work, to spoil a person's efforts. --ʦalüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a slip to occur, to slip and fall down.
f. (sg. dat. rᵃkavüñᵃ), the dragging (a person or thing) sliding along the ground.

or rikawun conj. 1 (1 p.p. rᵃ(ri)kowᵃ ), to drag (a person or thing) sliding along the ground, to drag along the ground; to carry stolen property away slowly and secretly. rᵃkowᵃ-motᵃ or rikowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. rᵃ(ri)küvᵃ-müʦᵃ ), dragged along the ground; (of stolen property) carried away secretly and slowly.

or rikh f. (sg. dat. rᵃkhi or rikhi), a line, a stripe, a stroke (cf. ḍū̃ga-rᵒ, p. 195a, l. 17; karma-rᵒ, p. 471b, l. 37; mardi-rᵒ or marēdi-rᵒ, p. 590a, l. 2; nasti-rᵒ, p. 658b, l. 28; nāvi-rᵒ, p. 666b, l. 49; pā̃-rᵒ, p. 748a, l. 3; pādi-rᵒ, padĕ-rᵒ, p. 681a, l. 17; p. 683a, l. 11) (El. rik, Gr.M. rᵃkha, L.V. 107); an unmeaning line, a scrawl (in writing) (Gr.M.). ¶ rᵃkha- (or rikha-) kalam  m. a fine pointed pen suitable for drawing fine lines, an etching pen. -ponzᵘ m. illegible, indistinct, undecipherable, or ambiguous writing. -püṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -pacĕ), a board on which paper is placed for being ruled, a drawing-board.
adj. c.g. lined, marked with lines (naturally, not artificially).

f. a female demon or ogress (the kind that is invisible and takes possession of people, causing madness, epilepsy, and the like) (cf. rūda-rᵃy ganḍüñᵘ̈, p. 826b, l. 2; rata-rᵃy, p. 846b, l. 20) (Rām. 331, 687); a female child or woman who habitually wails; a certain small bird with a wailing cry (cf. rūda-rᵃy, p. 826a, l. 50). m. adj. (f. rᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), good, excellent (Gr.Gr. 17 rutᵘ, 140; Gr.M.; Śiv. 411, 477, 513, 1009; Rām. 23, 39, 90, 521, 744, 750, 1066-7, 1527; K. 935, 1159; K. Pr. 191); good, beautiful, (of sound) sweet (Gr.M.; L.V. 51; Śiv. 395, 555, 778, 1360; Rām. 318, 323, 591, 993, 1089, 1098, 1253; YZ. 47); propitious (Śiv. 228, 479, 524, 661; Rām. 124-5, 1248, 1296, 1709; K. 129); pious (Rām. 71, K. 843); honest. --kyutᵘ -- adj. (f. rᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈ kiʦᵘ̈), sometimes good and sometimes bad, at one time suitable, at another time unsuitable. --mahanyuwᵘ -- m. a good man, a worthy person. ¶ rᵃ̇tᵃ̇ pöṭhⁱ or --pöṭhin -- adv. well, excellently. ¶ rᵃti mŏkha adv. with a good face, i.e. prosperously, bringing good luck. ¶ rᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈ möjᵘ̈ f. a good mother; hence, an artless, charming woman.

. The Kāshmīrī dental sibilant. The sixteenth consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character, the thirty-second (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the thirty-fifth) consonant when written in the Śāradā or the Nāgarī character, and the eighteenth consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. The Kāshmīrī name for character is süssö. The letter is sounded like the s in the English word 'sin'. It is also used to represent the sound of the Arabic s̤ ث (s̤ē) and ṣ ص (ṣād), which, in Kāshmīrī, occur only in words borrowed directly or indirectly from that language. In such cases they are both pronounced in Kāshmīrī like an ordinary s. ¶ The palatal sibilant is sh ش, which is the thirtieth (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z, the thirty-third) consonant when written in the Śāradā or the Nāgarī character, and the nineteenth consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. The Kāshmīrī name for the character is shĕkar-shö. It is sounded like sh in the English word 'shell'. It is also used to represent the sound of the Sanskrit letter ṣ, which, in Kāshmīrī, is written by Paṇḍits in words borrowed directly or indirectly from that language. In such cases, in speaking Kāshmīrī, it is pronounced like sh. Thus, the word pōsh, a flower, is often written by Paṇḍits because of the existence of the letter ṣ in the Sanskrit word puṣpa- with the same meaning. The Kāshmīrīs call this letter 'phörⁱ-shö'. ¶ These sibilants, s and sh, are liable to various changes in Ksh., the principal of which will here be mentioned. When sh represents a single (i.e. non-conjunct) Sanskrit ś or ṣ, the ś or ṣ when taken into Kāshmīrī, in the first place becomes h. Thus, Skt. śāka-, a vegetable, becomes Ksh. hāk-; Skt. śiraḥ, a head, > Ksh. hir; Skt. laśuna-, garlic, > Ksh. rahun; Skt. viṁśati-, twenty, > Ksh. wuh; √upaviś-, sit, > √bĕh-; √piṣ-, grind, > √pih-; viṣa-, poison, > vĕh; pārśva-, a rib, > (through ॒pāśa-) pāh-; dvādaśī, the twelfth day of a lunar fortnight, > bāh; praśasta-, good, prahasta-, > phraasta-, > phrayasta-, > Ksh. phrēst- (see phryūstᵘ); and so on for many others. ¶ While Skt. ś and ṣ thus become Ksh. h, it appears that the dental s does not undergo this change. The word shwās or shāh, breath (Skt. svāsa-), is only an apparent exception to this statement. If we compare the word with the Aryan šušī, Avesta suši, a lung, we see that it is an example of the fact that Kāshmīrī is not, like the Indo-Aryan languages, descended from Sanskrit, but from an earlier Aryan dialect which in some respects is akin to Eranian. Instead of being descended from the Sanskrit śvāsa-, the word must come from some Aryan dialect in which the word was *švāša-, or something of the sort. ¶ When this Kāshmīrī h, derived from ś or ṣ, is followed by y, ĕ, or ü-mātrā, it reverts to its original sibilant sound, and becomes again sh. Thus, the second past participle of the √pih-, given above, is pishyōv, not pihyōv, and the feminine plural of pyuhᵘ, its first past participle, is pishĕ, not pihĕ. So, the oblique singular of bāh, the twelfth lunar day, is böshᵘ̈, not böhᵘ̈. ¶ The above cases, in which ś or ṣ has become h, are all instances in which the original sibilant has been standing alone. If, on the other hand, it forms part of an original conjunct consonant, the sibilant is preserved, and is not changed to h. Thus, the Skt. śruva-, a ladle, becomes Ksh. shrŏv; and Skt. ślōka-, a verse, becomes Ksh. shrūk-. ¶ A further stage in this development is the frequent occurrence of pairs of words, in which one word has a single sibilant, and the other has a sibilant combined with a semi-vowel such as r or w. This occurs even when the semi-vowel is not original, as in Ksh. shrōʦ- or shōʦ-, purity, compared with the Skt. śauca- Other examples are:-- shrāṭh or shāṭh, a sandbank; shrôṭhᵘ or shôṭhᵘ, a corpse; shriṭhun or shiṭhun, to be congealed; so, with s, we have:-- srọ̆gᵘ or sọ̆gᵘ, cheap; swāl or sāl, an invitation; swās or sās, ashes. ¶ In pairs of words such as the above, moreover, sh and s are frequently interchanged. Thus, shrônᵘ or srônᵘ, moist; shranḍa or sranḍa, a bull (Skt. ṣaṇḍa-, in which there is no r); shrünḍᵘ̈ or srünḍᵘ̈, a casket; shrŏng or srŏng (Skt. suruṅga-), a mine; shranz or sranz, tongs; shrav or srav, a pinhole; shrawun or srawun, to ooze; and shrukun or sukun, to force into. In Ksh. sikanj, for Persian shikanja, a clamp, we have an apparent change of sh to s; but a reference to the Avesta √skand-, from which it is derived, shows that the Kāshmīrī word is not borrowed from Persian, but is descended from an Aryan dialect which has preserved the original s, while Persian has changed the original s to sh. ¶ The Sanskrit conjunct sn optionally becomes sr (shr) in Kāshmīrī. Thus, Ksh. shrān, srān, or snān, bathing, (Skt. snāna-); srĕh or snĕh, love, (Skt. snēha-). With these compare the shrūk- given above. ¶ As explained s.v. ĕ (p. 3a, ll. 39 ff.), the inherent vowel of the letter sh is ĕ, not a, so that must be transliterated shĕ, not sha. Kāshmīrīs consider that the sound of the letter y is inherent in sh, so that they write indifferently or, each of which represents the same sound, viz. shĕ. In this way, the first past participles of shē̃kun, to doubt, and of shērun, to arrange, are, respectively, shyū̃kᵘ and shyūrᵘ, but they are quite commonly written shū̃kᵘ and shūrᵘ.

or (among Hindūs) sö interj., a contraction of söhib, Sir, used in polite address by a man to a man. It is the equivalent of the Hindī jī, and is appended as a kind of vocative suffix, with or without a preceding interjection, as in nārān sö, hē nārān sö, or he nārān juv sö, all equivalent to 'Nārān!' used respectfully, as if we should say 'Nārān, Sir!' (cf. kotᵘ-sa, p. 484a, l. 41; ada-sö or ada-kyā-sö, yes, Sir, p. 13a, ll. 45, 50; āhan-sö, id., p. 18a, l. 5) (El. sa, sah; Gr.Gr. 96; Gr.M.; L. 279, sa) so ha-sa (p. 351b, l. 42) and ha-sö (ib.), hata-sa or hata-sö (p. 355b, l. 11), and hata sö-hē (ib., l. 12) (H. ii, 4, 9; x, 1, 2, 5, etc.; xii, 1, 10). ¶ With a prohibitive particle, we have ma-sö or (Rām. 1342) ma-sa, do not, Sir (p. 547a, l. 27). ¶ Used also as a respectful interrogative suffix (Gr.Gr. 181; YZ. 494, 568). Cf. söb.
m. (sg. dat. saādatas), prosperity, good fortune, happiness, felicity; saādath chum, there is good fortune to me, i.e. I am happy and ready (to do something) (Śiv. 637).

or sabā f. an assembly, council, conclave (cf. darma-sabā, p. 244b, l. 47; potᵘ sab, p. 787b, l. 42) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1570, sab; 65, 960, 1070, 1485, sabā); a public audience, levée; an invited festal assembly, at which food, etc., are distributed (Śiv. 1072, sab; 1857, sabā; K. 710, 894, 908, 987-8, 995-7, 1053, 1055, 1060); a learned society or the like (Gr.M.). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to distribute food at such an assembly. --hōrüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to carry out and complete the feeding at such a festal assembly. --rab mēlun -- m.inf. an assembly (of high-caste people) and mud to be united, i.e. non-discrimination between high caste and low caste to occur, eating together of such high and low castes, against rules of caste, or the like, to occur. ¶ saba-bal m. a meeting place, the place where a conclave assembles; a place where a wedding dinner party is carried on (Gr.Gr. 165). ¶ sabi bĕhun m.inf. to take one's seat at a festal meal. -bata m. the food at such a festival.

m. means, cause, reason, motive (cf. be-sabab, p. 132a, l. 33) (Gr.M.; H. viii, 5). bĕ-sabab, without cause, without reason (Gr.M.). ¶ sababa, sg. obl., used as adv., for (such-and-such) a reason, as in ami sababa, for this reason (Gr.M.).
m. (sg. dat. sabakas), a lesson, a lecture, a recitation of lessons (Rām. 97; H. iv, 4; v, 5, 6; viii, 3, 4, 11).

f. (sg. dat. sābüñᵘ̈), soap. (According to El., two kinds of soap are manufactured in Kashmīr; one kind from oil, called tīla-sāban, which yields a coarse soap, and another kind from fat, called supēda sāban) (cf. sĕki sāban gaʦhüñᵘ̈, s.v. sĕkh) (El. sábun; Gr.M.; L.V. 103; K.Pr. 190, 202). ¶ sābüñᵘ̈-gorᵘ̈ m. a soap-maker (El. sábinyigur). -poʦhᵘ m. soap foam, lather, soapsuds. -wôñᵘ m. soapy water.

or sabᵃr صبر m. patience, self-restraint, endurance, patient suffering, resignation (cf. be-sabar, p. 132a, l. 35) (Gr.M.). sabᵃra-kinᵃ adv. patiently (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to exercise self-restraint, to practise patience, to be patient, to wait (Rām. 408); to endure, bear up patiently. --karanwôlᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --karanwājĕñ --), patient (El.).
m. that which is generally useful, that which is of public benefit.

sabüzᵘ̈ or sabᵃz سبز adj. c.g. green, verdant, fresh (El.; L. 459; W. 21; Śiv. 500, sabạz; 1908, sabüzᵘ̈; Rām. 569, 1097); (as subst. m.), green grass, vegetation (Rām. 1098). --cāhⁱ -- or --cāy -- f. brick tea (imported via Ladāk and the Panjāb) (K.Pr. 39).

f. a way, road, path, mode, manner of procedure; water, or other drink, given as a pious duty. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to prepare, arrange; (in Ksh.) as a compliment, or pious duty, to issue a general invitation to all and sundry to a dinner or the like.
adj. c.g. patient, enduring; (in Ksh. subst. m.) patience, endurance (K.Pr. 84, 183).
m. a place abounding in verdure, a verdant mead, meadow, lawn, greensward, green (Śiv. 1797).
f. greenness, verdure; greens, potherbs, vegetables (Rām. 1007, 1098, 1495).
card., a hundred (used in Persian phrases). sad āpharī˜ صد آفرین interj. a hundred praises! bravo! well done! (Rām. 706, 792).

or (q.v.) ḍāy adj. pl. (f. sāḍa), together with (its) half, with one half more. It is used with numerals, beginning with three, and is always prefixed. Thus:-- sāḍ trĕh āna, three and a half annas; sāḍ ʦōr warihy, four and a half years; sāḍa shĕh mŏhara (fem.), six and a half mohars (W. 105, sādạ). Cf. ḍāy. ¶ sāḍa-sȧtⁱ f. a period of seven and a half years (being that occupied by the planet Shĕnashcar, or Saturn, in his revolution); (hence) the evil influence of Saturn; grievous calamity or distress; misfortune, adversity, ill-luck.

m. taste, flavour (cf. potᵘ sād, p. 787b, l. 44) (El., Gr.Gr. 146); relish (for anything), enjoyment (in anything), taste (for anything) (L.V. 45, 90; K.Pr. 94); cf. swād 1. sādas pyonᵘ m.inf. to fall into relish, to acquire a taste (for); met. to acquire a relish (for good things), (of one careless in religion, dissipated, or the like) to take to a religious life, to become concerned for one's salvation, to experience conversion.

(or, K. 435, sādu) m. a holy man, a saint, ascetic, devotee, sage, sādhu (Śiv. 178, 205, 238, 256, 270, 553, 585, 588, 596-7, 812-3, 1305, etc.; Rām. 1492, 1684; K. 435, 1097-8, 1174). ¶ sāda-biṭh f. an assembly of such pious men; the place of their assembly. -prakrĕth f. a holy nature, a virtuous disposition (Śiv. 1350, 1570, 1836). -sang m. association with the holy, virtuous company (Śiv. 245).

adj. c.g. plain, pure; white; unadorned, unmixed; without writing or impression, blank (as paper); candid, sincere, artless, guileless, open, frank (Rām. 681, K.Pr. 208); senseless (El. sádah); simple, ignorant (Rām. 222). --khrāv -- f. a patten which is not painted (but ornamented only by carved designs).

adv. always, ever, at all times (Śiv. 422; K. 521, 527). -shiv m. N. of a form of the god Shiv (Skt. Śiva) (Śiv. 437, 490, 506, 510, 528, 600, 633, 658, 727, 880, et passim; Rām. 35, 49, 55, 567, 790, 936, 1153, et passim). --sarwadā -- adv. always, perpetually; continually, without cessation, everlastingly. ¶ sadöy or sadöyⁱ adv. even continually, perpetually, ever, at all times (El. sadáí L.V. 7, sadöyⁱ).

in the following:-- sada-mondᵘ adj. (f. -münzᵘ̈), recently or just now churned, or recently produced (as butter etc.) by churning; cf. mandun. -mār m. a very recent death; hence, lamentations or condolences proferred very soon after death. -morᵘ m. very recently dead. --marun -- m.inf. to be very recently dead; lamentations or condolences to be offered immediately after a death. -pyāv m. the festival on which presents are made to a woman on the occasion of the birth of her first child. -pyāv bôgᵘ m. the present made on such an occasion. -pyāv ladun m.inf. to make these presents. -pyāwal f. a woman who has just brought forth her first child. -pyāy f. a very recent delivery of a child, a recent confinement; a woman who has just been delivered of her first child (L. 258, sadh piai); the festival on the occasion of a woman's first child being born. -pyāy karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to distribute sweetmeats on the occasion of a woman's recent delivery (esp. of her first child). -zāv adj. c.g. very recently born (of a child).
for sād 2 in the phrase syodᵘ sadā, s.v. syodᵘ, q.v.
f. plainness, absence of ornament, absence of coloured pattern; artlessness, simplicity, openness, frankness, sincerity.

or sadā 2 صدا m. (pl. dat. (Rām. 1195) sadahan), voice, tone, cry, call (Śiv. 938); (in Ksh.) a sound, noise (esp. when not articulate) (cf. khrāvi-sᵒ, p. 416b, l. 10) (Gr.M.; Rām. 123, 1195, 1287; H. viii, 9).

card. (sg. abl. sadāhi), seventeen (cf. El. sadah, Gr.Gr. 77). ¶ sadāhi phiri, seventeen times, on seventeen occasions (K. 570, 999). sadāhan-hondᵘ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, seventeen; costing seventeen (rupees, etc.), paid at the rate of seventeen, and so on.
f. (sg. dat. saḍaki), a road, highroad, highway (Śiv. 1859). --nērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a road to emerge, an ancient road to be discovered (on a journey), to find an old obliterated road.
m. (sg. dat. sādakas), a magician, one possessed of supernatural powers; esp. of powers gained by worshipping a deity or uttering charms.

f. (sg. dat. sādani), accomplishment, completion, performance, fulfilment; means, contrivance, expedient; a kind of wooden stylus used in former days for obliterating words or making alterations in rough notes or the like; a flux (for melting refractory metals) (cf. nav-sᵒ, p. 664b, l. 32) (Śiv. 983, 1726).
f. materials or the collection of tools for accomplishing any work (Gr.Gr. 129).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sadôrᵘ), (of things disarranged) to arrange in order, put in order. Cf. sandārun.
f. accomplishing, carrying out (cf. mȧrⁱ-sāday, p. 588a, l. 27). To be distinguished from sāday (Rām. 222), the emph. form of sāda.
m. 'centfoil', N. of a certain flower (El. ? Senecio, also sadbag); the Indian marigold.
m. pure devotional love, loving trust (L.V. 45).

m. that which is to be accomplished, a task (borrowed from the Skt. sādhya). Used --˚ in sidda-sādĕ, He whose task (whatever it may be) is (always) accomplished, He who is omnipotent, a title of Śiva (Śiv. 153).
m. (in Hindū philosophy) the constituent of goodness (in Skt. sattva-guṇa), see gŏn, p. 288b, l. 5, and razō-gŏn, p. 857b, l. 24 (Śiv. 1019, 1056, 1483, 1865).
or (Śiv. 1175) sath-gŏr m. an excellent spiritual preceptor, a polite form of gŏr, q.v. (Śiv. 15 ff., 109, 236, 248, 1752, etc.).

f. a group of seventeen, a seventeen, the form taken by sadāh, seventeen, q.v., as a multiplicative, as in kāh sadöhⁱ akh hath ta satashīth, eleven seventeens (are) a hundred and eighty seven (Gr.Gr. 86).
adj. (f. sadörᵘ̈), endowed with fortitude, full of gravity, constant, firm. Cf. dör 1.
adj. (f. sādȧjⁱ or sādüjᵘ̈), sweet, pleasant to the taste, savoury, tasty (Gr.Gr. 146); pleasing, agreeable, attractive, lovely, charming.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sôdᵘ, f. sözᵘ̈; 2 p.p. sāzōv), to accomplish, carry out, make perfect (cf. phorᵘ sᵒ, p. 702b, l. 10) (Gr.Gr. 129; Śiv. 554, 556, 1062, 1578, 1591, 1656). sôdᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. süzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), accomplished, perfected, carried out; considered, reflected, pondered over (in this sense, confused with sūdᵘ-motᵘ, s.v. sōdun). södith motᵘ adj. (f. --müʦᵘ̈ --), 'accomplished mad,' a sane person who pretends to be mad.
m. discrimination as to that which is good, good discrimination (Śiv. 331, 1612).
m. vegetables (El.) i.q. hākh 1, q.v. The Hindī word borrowed (cf. karm sāg, p. 471a, l. 35 and L. 72, 346) (W. 155, K.Pr. 180).

m. imitation, acting, mimicry, disguise, impersonation (Śiv. 1455); (esp. in Ksh.) (for purposes of deception) imitating sickness, poverty, affliction, fainting, helplessness or the like. --lāgun -- m.inf. to act a part in a dramatic performance; to imitate sickness, etc., as ab. --wahārun -- m.inf. to publish (or spread about) impersonations, to scatter abroad materials for dishonest impersonations; (in order to raise a riot or the like) to display opposition, loss, affliction or the like.

m. irrigation, watering, scattering or sprinkling water (on a plant or the like) (cf. atha-sᵒ, p. 62a, l. 37; krīrⁱ-sⁱ, p. 475b, l. 37; mūlan drôtᵘ pạtran sag, p. 567a, l. 49; nȧṭⁱ-sⁱ, p. 660a, l. 1; papa-sᵒ, p. 748b, l. 23) (El. sag, water; Gr.Gr. 123; Śiv. 929, 1532, 1853; K.Pr. 146, 229). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to water (Śiv. 1430); met. to support, foster, supply with necessities. --lagun -- m.inf. watering to be experienced; met. to be well supplied with all the necessities of life, to live in comfort and without care. --thawun -- m.inf. the fix watering; met. to put (some helpless or friendless person) in the way of earning a secure livelihood. ¶ saga-borᵘ m. the irrigation door, the opening in the side of a garden watering channel, admitting the water to a particular bed. -jŏy f. (in a garden or the like) the irrigation rivulet, channel, or pipe, for conveying water to the various beds. -nôrᵘ m. (in a garden or the like) a wooden pipe for conveying water underground, or across low ground. -nörᵘ̈ f. a pipe for conveying water from a well to a field or garden; a kind of bowl for sprinkling water attached to such a pipe. -nörij f. a pipe or drain for conveying water from high to low ground. -rowᵘ m. the basin or trench dug round a tree for holding water; a basin or cistern in a garden into which water is led by the irrigation channels. -wôrᵘ m. a watering-pot.
f. a necklace composed of beads and pieces of glass or stone at intervals (El.; cf. sŏnⁱ-sāga-lar, s.v. sŏn 1).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. saganôwᵘ), to sprinkle, or water, plants; cf. sagun, sạgᵃrun, sagawun and sạjᵃrun. Sagun is to irrigate a field or the like, but saganāwun, sạgᵃrun, sagawun, and sạjᵃrun mean to water plants etc.; cf. also sạgᵃrāwun. saganôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. saganövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈) (of a plant) sprinkled, irrigated.

m. the ocean, the sea (cf. bawa-sᵒ, p. 146b, l. 12; gangā-sᵒ, p. 292a, ll. 21, 23) (Śiv. 1774; dayā-s˚, an ocean of mercy, 189, 628, 1585; gangā-s˚, 1096, 1150; vīda-s˚, the ocean of the Vēdas, 50, 109, 851, 1169; K., khīra-s˚, 14).
f. (sg. dat. sā̃garüñᵘ̈), the condition of having become congealed, congelation, coagulation, petrifaction, being frozen solid.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. sã̄garyōv), to become congealed, petrified, to be frozen solid; to become dry and hard (by neglect or the like) and so to become useless. sā̃garyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sā̃garyē-müʦᵘ̈), congealed, frozen solid; gone dry and hard as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sagowᵘ), to sprinkle water on (a plant, or the like), to water (Gr.Gr. 123); cf. sagun, sạgᵃrāwun, etc., as there quoted. sagowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sagüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), irrigated, watered, sprinkled with water (on a plant).
adj. c.g. and subst. m. that which has properties; the material (as opposed to pure spirit), the material universe (L.V. 1).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sogᵘ, f. süjᵘ̈), to water, irrigate (a field, garden, etc.) (Śiv. 1853). The causal of this word is sạgᵃrun or sạjᵃrun, qq.v.; cf. also saganāwun, sạgᵃrāwun, and sagawun. sogᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. süjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of a plant or the like) watered, irrigated.
