conj. 1 (sạgᵃrôwᵃ), met. to incite, animate, stimulate (to an action), encourage, urge on; cf. sagun, saganāwun, sạgᵃrun. sạgᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. sạgᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), incited, encouraged, etc., as ab.

m. (1 p.p. sạgᵒrᵒ), to sprinkle, irrigate (plants in a garden, or the like); met. to encourage, give help, reassure, incite, stimulate, urge on; cf. sạgᵃrāwun. sạgᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. sạgᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), sprinkled, irrigated (by some one); encouraged, reassured.
adj. c.g. a helper, that which helps (whether person, thing, thought, quality, or what not) (Śiv. 1898, Rām. 1062).
m. N. of the youngest of the five Pānḍav (q.v.) princes (K. 1012, 1027, 1041, 1066, 1068).
m. an oblation, in lȧḍⁱ-sⁱ, p. 509a, l. 7, q.v.

adj. c.g. easy, simple (El. sáhil, ease, sahal, sihal, suhul, easy; Gr.M.; Rām. 63, 824; K.Pr. 183); facile; soft (El.). --holᵘ -- adj. (f. --hüjᵘ̈ --), easily bent, pliable (El. sahul-hul). --pöṭhⁱ -- or --pöṭhin -- adv. easily, with facility (Gr.M.).
m. compassion, pity, tenderness; bearing, enduring (hard work or the like). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. compassion, tenderness, pity to be felt; to endure bravely (some hard work or the like).

m. the time a little before daybreak, early dawn; food eaten by Musalmāns a little before dawn during the fast of Ramaẓān. -khān m. the man whose duty it is to cry out and proclaim the time for eating this food. -vēla m. the time of early dawn. -vizᵘ̈ f., id. ¶ sahāran adv. at a little before daybreak, at early dawn. --bögⁱ -- or --bögin -- adv. at about early dawn.

m. association; assistance, aid, help, recourse, resort; reliance, confidence; hope, encouragement. --āsun -- m.inf. assistance, support, aid to be available (to one engaged in something difficult). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to support, aid, back, help; to encourage, promise help.
n.ag. (f. sahāravüñᵘ̈), one who bears, suffers, endures, one who is patient.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sahôrᵘ), to bear, endure, suffer, bear patiently. sahôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sahörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), borne, endured.
m. boldness, daring courage; precipitancy, temerity, rashness, foolhardiness, rash impetuosity.
card. a thousand (the Skt. word sahasra borrowed; cf. sās 2). sahasra-dal m. thousand-petalled, a kind of lotus (Śiv. 41).
adj. c.g. rash, temerarious, reckless, heedless of consequences, foolhardy.
m. oversight, inadvertency, omission; error, mistake, blunder, fault; neglect, negligence. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. a blunder to occur, a mistake to be made.
n.ag. (f.sahavüñᵘ̈), one who is patient, forgiving, forbearing. sahawunᵘ sahawunᵘ adv. patiently, gently, slowly, leisurely.
or (Śiv. 897) m. a help, succour, aid, assistance (Gr.M.); a helper, adherent, patron, succourer (Śiv. 897). --karun -- m.inf. to help, aid (Gr.M.).

adj. c.g. inborn, natural, innate (Śiv. 1753, 1772, 1858, 1873); as subst. m. natural character; true nature, reality (L.V. 18, 21, 43, 45; K. 1159); (in Śaiva philosophy) the real nature of the Self (L.V. 29, 30, 35, 62).

or söhib صآحب m. a companion, associate, comrade; possessor, owner, master (YZ. 380); a lord, a great man; a person spoken of with respect, a gentleman, a European gentleman (Gr.M.; H. xi, 20); a title of respect equivalent to the English 'Mr.' (Gr.M.; H. xi (title)); the Master, the Supreme Deity, God (Śiv. 1796; H. iv, 4, 5; ix, 3; K.Pr. 48, 183, 210). söhib-ĕ-āgāh صآحب آگاہ m. an intelligent master, a master of recondite learning, a profound magician (H. ii, 9). söhib-ĕ-hōsh صآحبِ ہوش a master of discrimination, a rational person (Śiv. 1720). söhib-kār (= صآحبِ کار) m. a master of work, (of God) He who has uncontrolled authority, the Omnipotent (Śiv. 1796); söhib-ĕ-kitāb صآحب کتاب m. a master of books, a famous author (H. x, 13). söhib-zāda صآحب زادہ m. a young gentleman; a prince, a son of a king (Rām. 447, K.Pr. 184); a spoilt child, a greenhorn (Rām. 487).

(or sahīh صحیح) adj. c.g. healthy, sound; whole, entire, perfect; real, true, genuine; right, just, proper; correct, accurate, authentic; (as subst. f.) attestation, signature (El., Gr.M.); (as interj.) all right! yes! (K.Pr. 194, sahīh). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become confirmed, substantiated, certain. --karun -- m.inf. to make well, cure, set right; to complete, finish, perfect; to render valid, substantiate, verify, establish. --pöṭhⁱ -- or --pöṭhin -- adv. exactly, precisely, certainly.
(? spelling and gend.) Aster diplostephioides, the root of which is used in washing wool (L. 78).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sohᵘ, f. sühᵘ̈ or (Gr.Gr. 210 = I.K. VIII, iii, 75) süshᵘ̈; 2 p.p. sashyōv, Gr.Gr. 225), to bear patiently, endure, suffer (Gr.Gr. 210, 225; Gr.M.; K. 860); to tolerate, put up with (Rām. 1363, K. 407). Cf. shĕshun and the preceding. ¶ sohᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sühᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ or süshᵘ̈- müʦᵘ̈), borne patiently, endured. ¶ sahan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who (by nature) endures, one who is patient (by disposition) (Gr.M.).

m. a flood, torrent, stream, deluge, inundation (cf. pā̃-sᵒ, p. 748a, l. 6; sȧrⁱ pĕṭhⁱ sᵒ, s.v. sar 2) (El. sailāb; Gr.M. id.; Śiv. 1778; Rām. 722, 1603; YZ. 34 (sailāb); K.Pr. 188 (sailáb); met. utter destruction (of one's property, family, and everything)). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. a flood or inundation to come; utter destruction to overwhelm (a person) (Rām. 906, 1198).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. sahᵃlābladiñ) (of a field, or crop) spoilt by flooding; (of a person) one whose whole property and family have been destroyed.
f. neglect, carelessness, (causing delay, etc.) in any work.

adj. c.g. of, or relating to, or depending on a torrent, stream, or flood; (land) liable to be flooded; (a crop) spoilt by inundation. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. (of a growing crop, a village, or the like) to become destroyed by flood.
m. a desert, waste, wilderness, plain; (in Ksh.) an open space of ground (not hedged or walled round).
m. polishing, polish, cleaning (arms or tools), furbishing (Śiv. 282).
or söl 1 (for sail 2, söl 2, see under söl 2) m. a flood (El.). Cf. sahᵃlāb.
m. a walk, excursion, i.q. söl 2, q.v. (Śiv. 1830-1, YZ. 88). --karun -- m.inf. to make an excursion, wander, journey (Śiv. 1682, 1836, 1859).
f. (sg. dat. sạjᵃrüñᵃ), encouragement, urging on, stimulation (by help, approval, or the like).
conj. 1 (1p.p. sạjᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. sạjᵃrun, q.v. sạjᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. sạjᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. sạjᵒrᵒ- motᵘ, see sạjᵃrun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sạjᵒrᵒ) (of a plant) to cause to be watered, to cause to be irrigated; to encourage, urge on, stimulate (by approval, help, or the like). Cf. sagun 2, saganāwun, and sạgᵃrāwun. sạjᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part (f. sạjᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to be watered, caused to be irrigated, etc., as ab.
m. a water-carrier (El. saga, by a misprint for saqa, and sakah).

m. N. of a certain disease affecting cattle, horses, etc. Its symptoms are described as extreme swelling of the belly, accompanied by painful tumours. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. this disease to attack (an animal).

m. (amongst Hindūs) the performance of the śrāddha or solemn rite performed in honour of the spirits of dead parents and ancestors; the day or time for the due performance of this rite. --hāwun -- m.inf. duly to perform this rite.
adj. c.g. with desire, subject to desire, (of an action) due to, or caused by, desire (opp. to nishkām, q.v.) (Śiv. 1849).

m. (in negotiations for a marriage) the consent given by the bride's parents, the formal acceptance of a proposed bridegroom. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give the formal consent as ab. in the presence of the gods and witnesses. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to accept this formal consent.
adj. c.g. (of something usually invisible) become visible in bodily form, i.q. sākhyāth, q.v.

(cf. سکرات) orsĕkarôtᵘ m. fatigue, pain, affliction, distress. --mēlun --  m.inf. distress to be met with, great distress, etc., to be experienced, to be overwhelmed with distress, etc. --milawun -- m.inf. to cause great distress (to some one).
orsakaröʦᵘ̈lad adj. c.g. (as subst., f. sakarötⁱladiñ, or sakaröʦᵘ̈ladiñ), one suffering from, or overwhelmed by, great distress, etc., as in the preceding.
adj. one's own (of relations), german (as in 'cousin-german', or one's own mother and not a stepmother) (El., K.Pr. 144, sak).

f. setting forth (on a journey, or the like), the first starting (Gr.Gr. 127); the immediate preparations before starting. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make the immediate preparations for a journey, to start forth (on a journey). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a starting forth to come into existence, to be starting forth or to be on the point of setting out; met. to be on the point of commencing any work.

f. (sg. dat. sakharüñᵘ̈), setting forth, starting (on a journey); the being on the point of setting out. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to become engaged in starting forth, to be on the point of setting out; met. to be on the point of setting to on any work.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sakharôwᵘ), to cause (a person) to set out (on a journey), to send (a person) on a message. sakharôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sakharövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to be set forth, sent forth (on a message).
m. the becoming on the point of setting out (on a journey), or beginning any work; the desire, or hope, of the above.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. sakharyōv), to prepare to set forth, to be on the point of setting out (Gr.Gr. 127; H. xii, 18); to make arrangements for a journey; to set oneself to any task, busy oneself with (L.V. 10). ¶ sakharith bĕhun m.inf. to become ready, or be ready, to start on a journey, to remain ready to start. --rōzun -- m.inf., id. ¶ sakharyō-motᵘ perf. part. (sakharyē-müʦᵘ̈), become ready to set forth, on the point of and prepared to start; ready to start on any work.
m. N. of one of Rāvaṇ's generals, who was killed by Hanumān (Rām. 693).
adj. c.g. liberal, bountiful, generous; (as subst.) a liberal or bountiful person (K.Pr. 184 saḵẖai).

adj. c.g. become visible in bodily form (used e.g. of something hitherto unseen and unobtainable; of deities, spiritual beings, or the like; or else in comparisons, e.g. comparing a beautiful heroine to a goddess) (Śiv. 357, 1555); as postpos. in the presence of (Rām. 731) (ʦĕ sā˚, in thy presence); as subst. m. a present witness, one who bears testimony (i.q. sökhī 2, q.v.) (Rām. 1058); cf. sākār and sākshāth. -kār m. the making oneself or the becoming visible in bodily form (e.g. something hitherto unseen and unobtainable, or a deity in answer to prayer).

adj. (f.saküjᵘ̈), one who has not eaten any food, even though the usual mealtime has passed; cf. suka 2. sakaliy adv. without eating (e.g., u.w. vbs. of going, existing, doing, or the like) (L.V. 47).
adj. (f. saküjᵘ̈), all, the whole, everything (L.V. 38). sakȧliy m.pl., with emph. y, even every one, all men (L.V. 47).
f. the provision of suitable food and medicine for an invalid or convalescent, a regimen (cf. nā-sakrī, p. 658a, l. 5; El. has sakre and sukré, both translated 'abstinence'. Cf. suka 2 and sakolᵘ 1).
adj. c.g. (of food for an invalid or convalescent) agreeable to the regimen, suitable as diet. Cf. sạkrī.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. sạkriyĕladiñ), (of an invalid or convalescent) taking food according to regimen, on invalid diet.

adv. (the Skt. sâkṣāt) in the presence of, before the very eyes, visibly, evidently. The Ksh. form of this word is sākhyāth, q.v. -kār m. perception, apprehension, knowledge (Śiv. 1001, 1066, 1205, 1792).
apoplexy. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. apoplexy to occur, to have a sudden attack of apoplexy. --karun -- m.inf. to have an attack of apoplexy.

or (Gr.M.) sakhᵃtī سختی f. hardness, rigidity; cruelty (Rām. 977); grievance, hardship, adversity, indigence, distress, evil, calamity (Śiv. 663). --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to treat with harshness, severity, to illtreat (Rām. 412, 962). --karith --, adv. with difficulty (Rām. 433, 909).

or (Gr.M.) sakhth adj. c.g. hard, stiff, rigid (Gr.M.; Śiv. 335; Rām. 1415); hard, difficult (e.g. a road, pass, or the like); hard, tight (e.g. a knot); (of a wish or the like) determined, fixed (Śiv. 430); obdurate, troublesome, difficult (El. sakht, Śiv. 1505); difficult, not easy, perplexing (Gr.M.); ferocious (El.); fierce, violent (of pain, sun's heat, intoxication, or the like) (Gr.M., W. 24, Rām. 291); very, extreme, violent (of unpleasant things) (Rām. 349; H. vii, 13, 18; K.Pr. 87, saḵẖt); (as adv.) violently (Rām. 376, 441); (as subst. m.) difficulty, strait, peril, danger (Rām. 417). -kan adj. c.g. deaf (El.).

or (q.v.) swāl m. an invitation to a dinner, picnic, or the like (cf. duṭopᵘ sᵒ, p. 258b, l. 47; khīra-sᵒ, p. 409a, l. 11; nav-sᵒ, p. 664b, l. 44; nawa-rĕh-sᵒ, p. 665a, l. 4; nȧvⁱ-sⁱ, p. 667a, l. 34; phira-sᵒ, p. 702a, ll. 2, 4); (Gr.Gr. 149; Gr.M.; Śiv. 74, 86, 266, 965, 1215, 1748; Rām. 610; K. 375, 1006-7); a dinner-party, picnic (cf. phulayĕ-sᵒ, p. 697b, l. 45) (K. 1147); a banquet, feast (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 700, 1106, 1255, 1328; H. v, 9; vi, 2; YZ. 372, 435; K.Pr. 14, 228). --dapun -- m.inf. to invite to such a feast (cf. sālas dᵒ, Śiv. 79, 965). ¶ sāla-bata m. the food given at a dinner-party, picnic, or other similar feast. -sāl m. invitation upon invitation, a large number of invitations issued by a single host for dinner-party after dinner-party. -ṭôkᵘ m. the dish or tray of various foods placed before each guest at a dinner-party. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. (of an invited guest) to arrive at a dinner-party (including the ceremonial reception by the host) (Śiv. 179, 374, 413, 820, 943, 1552, 1691). Cf. sālas yᵒ, Śiv. 832. ¶ sālas anun m.inf. 'to conduct to a dinner-party', i.e. to invite an honoured guest to such (Śiv. 89).

f. (sg. dat. söjᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 69, also written söjⁱ), a wife's sister, a husband's sister-in-law (cf. māsatᵘ̈rᵘ̈ sᵒ, p. 601a, l. 46) (Gr.Gr. 69). ¶ söjᵘ̈-gŏbur m. the son of a wife's sister. -kūrᵘ̈ f. the daughter of a wife's sister.

m. right or proper course (of conduct or procedure); advice, counsel, consultation (Gr.M.; Rām. 95; H. viii, 11); agreement, harmony, concord, reconciliation (Gr.M., K.Pr. 59); conciliation, restoring harmony. --gaʦhun --  m.inf. reconciliation to occur, to become reconciled. --karun -- m.inf. to consult, to consult together (El., Gr.M., Rām. 546); to determine (on a course of conduct) (Rām 1414). --karan-wôlᵘ -- m.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a counsellor (El.). --thāwun -- m.inf. to make agreement (with), to agree (with, sṻty, a person, dat.) to do some (secret or improper action), to come to an understanding (with) (e.g. with a woman for an intrigue) (H. viii, 3).

f. (this word is f. in Ksh., but sometimes, erroneously following the practice of Hindōstānī, it is treated as m.; cf. W. 18) safety, peace (W. 13, 18); salutation, greeting, compliments (El., m.; Gr.M., m.; W. 13f.; K.Pr. 260); parting salutation, adieu, farewell, good-bye (El. f.); a complimentary present (H. viii, 3, 11). --diñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to bid farewell, bid adieu, dismiss. --ladüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to send one's compliments to a person (with a message) (YZ. 459). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf., id.; to salute, to compliment, make a bow (Gr.M., m.; H. iii, 1; xii, 4, 5, 9, etc.). --pālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make a bow, to salute (H. xii, 16). --wanüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to send one's compliments
m. a kind of girdle made of silken cloth worn usually by girl-brides.
f. a piece of wire, a needle, a bodkin, spike (cf. ṭōpi-sᵒ, s.v. ṭūpⁱ) (H. v, 4); a knitting-needle (cf. jŏrāba-sᵒ, p. 377b, l. 14); a distaff (El. salai).
m. N. of a certain kind of sacred stone (Skt. śālagrāma) containing the impression of one or more ammonites. It is worshipped as representing Vishnu (Śiv. 1016).
or sālurᵘ m. (f. sālarĕñ, Gr.Gr. 39, YZ. 375) an invited guest at a dinner-party or the like; (at a wedding) a member of the bridegroom's party (Gr.Gr. 39, 149; Śiv. 742, 968, 972, 1070).

adj. c.g. even, level (Śiv. 1531); impartial, fair; i.q. somᵘ, q.v. sama-drĕshṭi or -drĕshṭī (written by Paṇḍits) f. the regarding all things impartially (e.g. bearing sorrow and joy with equanimity, heedlessness as to poverty and riches, and so on) (Śiv. 281, 901, 1026, 1213, 1237, 1485, 1531, 1804, 1853, 1859).
m. the staircase or ladder on the bank of a river or the like for the convenience of bathers (Śiv. 1109). -pôwᵘ m. a single step on this staircase.
m. in the following:-- sāma-vīd m. N. of one of the three principal Vēdas, the Sāma-vēda, the hymns of which are sung or chanted (Śiv. 276, 394, 446, 1115, 1323, 1580).
m. hearing; singing, song, music, ecstasy occasioned by music; (in Ksh.) the noise of the lamentations of an assembly or crowd of people (W. 135, sama; K.Pr. 253, samah); a song (El. samah).
m. the heaven, sky, firmament (H. vii, 26).
f. (sg. dat. samözᵘ̈), profound abstract meditation, intense absorption or contemplation on the Supreme (Śiv. 451-2, 509, 1768; K. 969); the tomb of a saṁnyāsī or Hindū ascetic.
f. collection of materials or implements, etc.; stock, baggage, materials, apparatus (K. 1065); furniture (El.).
f. (sg. dat. samaki), a kind of gum (which exudes from a certain tree (El. samagh)). samaki-vyūrᵘ m. the gum as it oozes from the tree.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. samakhôwᵘ), to make visible, show (Gr.Gr. 171); to meet, to join as a helper.

conj. 2. (1 p.p. samokhᵘ, f. samüchᵘ̈; 2 p.p. samachyōv), to become visible, be seen (Gr.Gr. 171, 204); to meet (a person accidentally or by an intentional visit) (Gr.Gr. 116 (in this sense obl. inf. samakhana), 204; L. 461; H. xii, 25; K.Pr. 109), to pay a visit of condolence (e.g. to the sorrowing relatives of one who has died) (obl. inf. samakhani in this sense, Gr.Gr. 116); to agree, to suit (El., K.Pr. 75); to associate (El.). ¶ samokhᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. samüchᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), visited, etc., as ab. ¶ samakhani gaʦhun m.inf. to go to pay a visit, to set out for a visit; to pay a visit of condolence, as ab. (Gr.Gr. 116). ¶ samakhunᵘ raṭun m.inf. to refrain from paying a visit of condolence to a bereaved family (of some friend or relation. This is considered a breach of good manners).
f. a summons to a court of justice (the English word) (Gr.M.).

adj. c.g. like, similar, equal; common, general, average; N. of one of the vital airs which has its seat in cavity of the navel and is essential to digestion (Śiv. 306). kaityā samān, how many (on the) average? (Gr.M.).

or sāmāna m. furniture, baggage, paraphernalia (Gr.M.; Śiv. 787, 921, 1148; Rām. 588); necessaries, requisites, materials (Gr.M.; Rām. 39, 1436, 1450-1, 1675; H. vii, 5; xi, 9); tools, apparatus (Śiv. 1705); harness (El.); a woman's ornaments, etc., a woman's graces (Rām. 654, 662, 1087, 1467, 1576, 1634; YZ. 30, 267); pomp (H. xi, 20); boundary, limit, landmark, end (El.).
or (El.) samundar m. the sea (El.; Gr.M. samandar; Śiv. 836, 1638 (id.); Rām. (samandar) 449, 595, 719, 855, 987; K.Pr. 184). Cf. samudᵃr.
m. (sg. dat. samāpas), end, conclusion, termination; completion, accomplishment, fulfilment; completion, end, hence, destruction; adj. c.g. finished, completed (cf. samāpᵃth) (Rām. 1730).
or (Gr.M.) samāpt, adj. c.g. completed, concluded, finished (Gr.M.); as subst. m., i.q. samāph, q.v. (Gr.M.).
f. sameness, identity; impartiality, fairness; equanimity (Śiv. 230, 1484, 1572); (met.) considering oneself as identical with the Supreme (Śiv. 18, 110).
adj. c.g. assembled, met together, used in the phrase sŏñⁱ-sāmaṭh, s.v. sọ̆ñᵘ, q.v.

m. time (El. samáí; Śiv. 738, 1704-5, 1819; Rām. 24, 976, 1317, 1496); a particular time, occasion (cf. aki samayĕ aki, p. 20b, l. 2) (Śiv. 97, 319, 1477, 1909; Rām. 620, 1716; K. 797, 1025, 1096); the fit time, the proper time for anything (cf. köjⁱ-sⁱ, p. 430a, l. 11; Gr.M.); a time, a particular period of time (Rām. 100); an appointed time (e.g., met. the time of death) (Rām. 1561); a season of the year (Gr.M.). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. the time to fall, i.e. bad times to occur, adversity to fall on a person. --wātun -- m.inf. the right time (for anything) to come (K. 46, 355, 607, 626, 799); one's appointed time to come, to be at the point of death (K. 847, 1169). ¶ samayāh (with suff. of indef. art.) a period of time; as adv., for a time, esp. for a brief time, for a few moments (Rām. 123). ¶ samayĕs sg. dat. as adv. once upon a time, at some indefinite past time (K. 5); at a (certain) time (K. 94, 103, 204, 299, 552, 867, 906, 970, 1000, 1052, 1127); at the present time, now (K. 360); prath samayĕs, at every moment (K. 862), at each time, from time to time (K. 36, 542). --dōr karun -- m.inf. to make a revolution for time, hence, to establish an era (Rām. 997).

m. living together in intimate fellowship, living in common, joint life (of a number of people), consociation, commensality, joint family life, chumming, being a member of a joint party. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such joint life to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to carry on such a joint life. --nērun -- m.inf. such joint life to be firmly established and to continue. --thawun -- m.inf. to keep up or maintain such a joint life.
m. a member of a joint party (as in samaʦār q.v.); one who habitually lives in joint association with others.
m. N. of a son of Krushn (Kṛṣṇa), who attempted to carry off a daughter of Duryōdhana, and subsequently married her (K. 893-917).
f. a crowbar (such as is used for breaking or moving rocks).
f. the wages of a repairer, the price of repair, the cost of repair, etc., as in sambālun, q.v.
n.ag. (f. sambālavüñᵘ̈), one who repairs or puts in order, a corrector; a trainer, one who breaks in, disciplines.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. sambalyōv), to become in good order, to be put right; (of one faithless) to be confirmed (in faith) (Śiv. 1535); to come to oneself (out of a faint, after being agitated, or the like) (YZ. 15).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sambôlᵘ, f. samböjᵘ̈; 2 p.p. sambājyōv), to repair, put in order, correct, arrange (something not in order), put right (cf. dam sᵒ, p. 216b, l. 21, Śiv. 1256; Rām. 1353, 1358) (Śiv. 977, 1218; Rām. 1129, 1289; K.Pr. 10); to train, break in, discipline, tame; to adorn (El.); to prepare (El.; Śiv. 1248, 1356; Rām. 574, 977; K. 1037); to be put in good order (= sambalun, q.v.) (Śiv. 282). ¶ sambôlᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. samböjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), put in order, as ab; disciplined, as ab. ¶ sambölith pakun m.inf. to walk with discretion; to carry on any business carefully and with discretion; to conduct oneself sympathetically with everyone (i.e. generally, whether one's own people or not). --thawun -- m.inf. to put with discretion, to deposit or take care of something (so that it is well and discreetly guarded and hidden).
or (sometimes written by Paṇḍits) m. connexion, relationship (Gr.M.).
m. levelness, smoothness; the being equal, like, similar, resembling (cf. atha-sᵒ, p. 62b, l. 7); average, medium, mean.

m. destruction, ruin, utter loss (cf. kāla-sᵒ, p. 434a, l. 31) (Śiv. 12, 68, 118, 122, 152, 284, 864, 977, 1577, 1587; Rām. 341, 1004; K. 562). --mēlun -- m.inf. utter destruction to occur (to a person or thing). --mīlanāwun -- or --milawun -- m.inf. to set to work to cause utter destruction.
adj. c.g. one who causes ruin or destruction (Śiv. 203, 621, 1888). samhāri-bairav m. 'a demon of destruction', utter ruin and destruction.
m. a twig or twigs or sacrificial sticks for feeding the sacred fire (Hindū). -mūrᵘ̈ f. a twig for the sacred fire.
adv. in front, before. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go into the presence (of anyone), to attend (a court) (Gr.M.).
f. (sg. dat. sampüzᵘ̈), wealth, riches, prosperity, affluence (K. 1151, 1154).
f. N. of the goddess of affluence (Śiv. 1095, 1142; K. 748); wealth, riches, prosperity, affluence (K. 1094, 1099, 1106, 1150). Cf. sampatā.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sampanôwᵘ), to cause to come into existence, to make, frame, cause to exist (K. 589).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. samponᵘ (q.v. s.v.), f. sampüñᵘ̈) (i.q. sapanun, q.v.), to become (Rām. 18, 24, 68, 75, 114, 139, 228-9, 237, 266, 307, 309, 372, 403, 411; K. 122, 352, 428, 558); to be made, produced, formed, completed, effected (K. 119, 589); to happen, occur, take place (K. 87, 562, 677, 715, 752, 776, 799, 909, 1040, 1071); to exist (K. 7); (with dat. of possession) there is (to so and so), (he) has; to become (complete), be finished (K. 140); In the past tense, 'I became,' etc., are used to mean 'I became and am now', hence 'I am', etc. (Rām. 535); shĕran sampanun, to take refuge (with, dat.) (K. 876). Cf. sapadun, sapanun, sö̃panun, and sapazun.
m. (sg. dat. sampātas), N. of a famous vulture (in Skt. Sampāti), the son of Garuḍa and elder brother of Jaṭāyu (Rām. 534).
1 p.p. (f.sampüñᵘ̈) (see sampanun) become, finished, completed; prosperous, thriving; endowed with, possessed of (K. 636, bāla- rṻpa sᵒ, endowed with a youthful form).
m. glory (El. samrat f.) power, ability (Śiv. 1696). This word and the next are probably the same word and should probably be spelt sāmarth and samarth, respectively.

m. worldly life, mundane existence (Gr.M.; L.V. 35, 37; Śiv. 4, 28, 171, 277, etc.; Rām. 1489, 1751); the material (as opposed to the spiritual) world (Gr.M.; Śiv. 17, 189, 280, etc.; Rām. 25, 1705, 1732, 1754; K. 475; H. iv, 1; K.Pr. 243); the world, the universe (generally) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 14, 32, 54, 70, 156, 241, 244, etc.; Rām. 261, 514, 642, 743, 1096, 1325, 1420, 1452, 1603, 1682; K. 842, 1169; H. ix, 6; YZ. 61); met. the whole world, hence, a great number of people; worldly life, the life of householder (Śiv. 1224); transmigration, succession of births, the round of existence from birth to birth (L.V. 6; Śiv. 152, 254, 337, 382, 1201, 1268, 1755, 1914). -dēg f. 'a caldron for the whole world,' a caldron sufficient for cooking food for a large number of people; met. a means of support for a large number of people.
m. the making perfect, completing thoroughly; education, cultivation, training; a purificatory rite, a sacred rite or ceremony (K. 483).
adj. c.g. mundane, living in this world (Śiv. 586, 1049, 1508).

m. (sg. dat. samsataras), utter or entire destruction (Gr.M. samᵃsatur). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such destruction to occur (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to cause utter destruction, utterly to destroy. --mēlun -- m.inf. utter destruction to happen. --milawun -- m.inf. to cause utter destruction.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. samyōv), to be gradually collected or stored up (e.g. by putting articles little by little into a box), to be saved up (K. 766 (inf. dat.), K.Pr. 78); to meet together, to assemble (El. sumun; Gr.M.; L.V. 95; Śiv. 385, 502, 504, 507, 698, 830, 942, 960, 1245, 1442, 1751; YZ. 161, 203); to join (a person), meet (a person) (Rām. 649, YZ. 438 (we should meet each other)); to live together, get on together (K. 1140); to be level (cf. buthᵘ sᵒ, p. 142a, l. 16); to be level (with something else), to fit or agree (with something else), to be suitable; to be meet, proper, becoming (K. 904); to match, be a counterpart. The causal of the verb is sọ̆mbᵃrun or sọ̆mbᵃrāwun, qq.v. ¶ samith conj. part. having assembled, having come together (Rām. 145, 276, 404, 615, 779, 860, 1009, 1108c, 1130, 1334 (of water), 1679, 1684, 1714, 1757, 1760; K. 181, 405, 701; YZ. 82, 86, 173, 410); (as adv.) together, all together (Rām. 68, 88, 1455, 1537; K. 369, 835); together with (my friends), after collecting (my friends) round (me) (K.Pr. 87, sĕmit); united, in conjunction (Rām. 837, K. 266). --rōzun -- m.inf. (of a number of people) to live together in one community and on an equality. ¶ samyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. samyē-müʦᵘ̈), collected, gradually saved up; (pl.) assembled, met together (Śiv. 64, 742; Rām. 642); fitted, become suitable, found to be a match, matched.
m. the sable (mustela zibellina). -ʦam f. sable-skin, sable-fur.
m. (sg. dat. samatas), combination of a number of people for some common object, coalition, co-operation. ¶ samatō karun m.inf. to be employed in a co-operative task.
m. a catechism, question an answer; a conversation (Śiv. 117, 245, 442, 533, 596, 601-4, 1244; K. 944); an account of occurrence, a story, tale, statement (Rām. 1497, 1684).
m. a meeting, an interview (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 149, samjhog); an occurrence, event (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to meet, to have an interview (ʦĕ sṻty, with thee) (Gr.M.).

postpos. governing the abl. or optionally (in the case of singular (and occasionally plural) animate nouns and rarely inanimate nouns) the dat.; with, together with. ¶ This word is distinguished from sṻtin or sṻty (qq.v.) by the fact that it implies that the governed word (not the thing or person accompanied) is the appendage, the other being the principal. Thus, mölis-sṻtin āv, he came with the father, implies that his father had brought him along, while mölis- sān āv, would imply that he brought his father along with him (Gr.Gr. 45; Gr.M.; W. 97, 98; Śiv. 32, 71, 313, 368-9, 377, etc.; K. 374 (with sg. an.), 687 (inan.), 879 (pl. an.), 884 (inan. but governing dat.), 1017 (pl. an.), 1093 (sg. an.)). ¶ When governing an abstract noun in the abl. this word forms an adverb, as in ānanda-sān, joyfully, p. 35a, l. 21; bāwa-sān, politely, p. 147a, l. 3; darda-sān, affectionately, p. 241a, l. 10; khũ̈khĕra- sān, nasally, p. 396a, l. 39; khŏkarĕra-sān, in a hollow fashion, p. 396b, l. 4; kharca-sān, with expenditure, p. 413a, l. 34; khŏshī-sān or khŏshiyĕ-sān, willingly, p. 418b, ll. 24, 25; kala- kāpi-sān, entirely, p. 435a, l. 12; māna-sān, with deference, p. 573a, l. 21; rāhath-sān, p. 829b, l. 50; sŏkha-sān, comfortably, p. 905b, l. 24; sīra-sān, secretly, s.v. sīr 1 (Śiv. 36, 56, 70, 85, etc.; Rām. 55, 750, 1200, 1203, 1370, 1499; K. 169, 543, 600, 610, 877, 996-7; H. i, 6; YZ. 455; K.Pr. 26, 82). ¶ In such adverbial phrases, pöṭhⁱ may be pleonastically added, as in sŏkha-sān pöṭhⁱ, happily, comfortably, securely (Gr.M.). ¶ This word is used in special meanings in nal-sān, pimping, p. 631b, l. 47; shĕrāba-sān, a cup-bearer (p. 891a, l. 4).

f. the sprinkling of water on the house-deity. Among Hindūs it is customary in the early morning when bringing water to the house from outside, on arrival, first of all to sprinkle some of it on the images of the various house-deities; the same ceremony is also performed at the śrāddha obsequial rite immediately after offering the piṇḍas (see pĕṇd). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to perform this sprinkling. ¶ sañĕ-pŏtulᵘ m. the image of the household deity over whom this rite is performed. -wörᵘ̈ f. the small pitcher in which this sprinkling water is contained (Rām. 586). Cf. sȧñⁱ-wôrⁱ, p. 918a, l. 31.

(for 2, see sana 2) f. (sg. dat. süñᵘ̈, sometimes written sȧñⁱ), theft, burglary (Śiv. 1311); the proceeds of theft, stolen property (K.Pr. 164, 222). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to commit theft, steal. --dāvüñᵘ̈ --, f.inf. to cause theft to be committed, to incite to burglary (K.Pr. 149). --lagüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. theft to occur (to), (a house, etc.) to be burgled. --nērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. theft to become manifest. ¶ süñᵘ̈-borᵘ̈ m. a burglar's hole, the mine dug by a burglar. -barg m. a trace found of stolen property. -bārav m. disclosure of theft, the discovery of theft. --khasun -- m.inf. to rise to theft, to climb up to commit theft, hence, to commit theft. -ʦūr m. (f. -ʦūrᵘ̈, bel.), a professional thief, a burglar. -ʦūra-bāy f. a thief's wife. -ʦūrᵘ̈ f. a female professional thief.

m. the combined derangement of the three humours, failure of vital force at the conclusion of some long disease when the sufferer is dying or nearing death, coma, syncope (Rām. 1487); cf. sanapāth. --dörith dyunᵘ -- m.inf. symptoms of syncope to declare themselves. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. syncope to come or declare itself. --lagun -- m.inf. syncope to attack a person.

or occasionally (e.g. K. 105, 369) san 2 or sanā (i.e. sana + a 3) adv. an interrogative particle indicating doubt, hesitation, anxiety or the like. It is usually added to another interrogative word. Sometimes sana (not sanā) is added to the verb of a sentence. Thus kyā-sanā khĕwān chuh (or chw-ā), (I wonder), is he eating; khĕwān chw-ā-sana is he really eating (Gr.Gr. 180). It will be observed that the interrogative particle ā (see ā 3) can be used with this word (cf. amā- kyā-sᵒ, p. 27a, l. 18; kar-sanā, p. 465a, l. 23; kati-sᵒ, p. 483b, l. 39; kotᵘ-sᵘ, p. 484a, l. 43; kūtᵘ-sᵘ, p. 485a, l. 16; kĕtha-sᵒ, p. 488a, l. 30) (L.V. 39, kyā-s˚; Śiv. 47 (kus-s˚), 1600 (id.); Rām. (kyāh-s˚, etc.) 78, 202, 221, 253, 596, 834, 1074, 1143k, 1306, 1348, 1366, 1391, 1408, 1421, 1492-3; K. (marinā-san, why should he not die) 105, 369; (kyāh-sana, etc.) 165, 213, 287, 328, 608, 919, 1134; YZ. 187).
or sanakādĕkh m.pl. the four sons of Brahmā (Skt. Brahmán-), viz. Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana, and Sanatkumāra (Śiv. 1457).
f. a mistress, lover, sweetheart (esp. when young--under twenty--and charming).

m. (sg. dat. sanapātas), the combined derangement of the three humours, failure of vital force, accompanied by syncope or coma in the last stage of some long and mortal disease, such as consumption or the like. Cf. sana 1.
f. a pair of pincers or nippers, forceps, small tongs (Gr.M.).
m. one of the four sons of Brahmā (see sanakādi) (Śiv. 365, 1427, 1648).

f. (sg. dat. sanawöʦᵘ̈), a new custom (altered from an old one) (e.g. a new procedure in distributing customary gifts); a new route or road. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to institute a new custom; to indicate a new route. --nērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a new custom to be instituted; a new route to be discovered.

f. (sg. dat. sünzᵘ̈), joining, union, meeting (such as the confluence of two rivers, the meeting point between two lunar days, or between two changes of the moon); repeated study of some subject (cf. pȧṭⁱ-sⁱ, p. 789b, l. 15); repeated conning over of an instruction, teaching, command, injunction, charge. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to read something over and over again in order to master it as an object of study; to teach (pupils, etc.), instruct (Gr.M.; K. 486, 500). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to impress instructions upon a person, to lay an injunction or command (upon, dat.), lay a charge (upon) (Rām. 1736). --pand lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of a boy, or the like) to be taught insolence, to learn to be saucy, presumptuous, brazen, etc.
f. the morning, noon, and evening prayers of a Brāhmaṇa (i.q. sandyā, q.v.) (K. 410, 484).
f. a chair (El.); a comfortable couch, throne.
m. arrangement, putting in order; resuscitation, coming to (from a faint or the like) (cf. prāna-sᵒ, p. 761a, l. 44).
m. arranging, putting in order; resuscitating, reviving (cf. prāna-sᵒ, p. 761a, l. 48).
n.ag. (f. sandāravüñᵘ̈), one who comes to (out of a faint), coming to, being resuscitated; one who is come into a little property out of poverty.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sandôrᵘ. In some meanings this verb is impersonal), (as an impersonal verb) to be arranged, put in order; to be resuscitated, come to (out of a faint or the like) (cf. prān sandārȧnⁱ, p. 761a, l. 27) (Śiv. 1753); to make (oneself) steady, to become cool and courageous (after mental agitation), to take courage (L.V. 70); (of one coming out of extreme poverty) to find oneself possessed of a little, to save something from a wreck of property; (as a personal verb) to make (something) steady, (of a carriage) to put on the brake, to block (the wheels) (L.V. 26); to benefit, support, sustain, nourish (Śiv. 1229); cf. sadārun and sandarāwun. sandôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sandörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), that which has been put in order (impersonal); that which has been resuscitated (impersonal, as in ȧmⁱ chuh sandôrᵘ-motᵘ, it has been resuscitated by him, i.e. he has become resuscitated).

f. the mustard plant; the mustard seed (K.Pr. 184); a kind of rape plant, Brassica campestris (L. 330, sandiji). Cf. sarshĕph. ¶ sȧndija-phulay f. the season of the flowering mustard plant (early spring). -tīl m. mustard-oil. -zölⁱ dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to close the interstices of the fingers for mustard-seed, i.e. to hold a handful of mustard-seeds with the fingers tightly closed together, so that not a single tiny seed escapes; met. to scrutinize with excessive minuteness (esp. when it is absurd to do so). Hence, sȧndija-zölⁱ dinⁱ, hĕndavĕnda nīrith ʦalȧnⁱ, to close the fingers tightly in order to save mustard-seed, and pumpkins to escape and run away, i.e. to be penny wise and pound foolish (cf. K.Pr. 184).
adj. c.g. one who benefits, supports, sustains, nourishes (Śiv. 1048).

or sandiyā (Paṇḍits write this word), f. evening (El. sandiya, m.; Rām. 575); the morning, noon, and evening prayers of a Brāhmaṇa (cf. pawana-sᵒ, p. 810b, l. 23; rudra-sᵒ, p. 827a, l. 29) (L. 261, 264, sandhia; Śiv. 756, 1496; K. 971). Cf. sand 2.

f. (sg. dat. sạndᵃrüñᵃ), lightening, kindling, igniting; inflaming, inciting, stirring up, rousing. -pholᵘ m. fire-lighting, little bits of dry wood, powdered dried cowdung, or the like, for lighting a fire.
or sandarāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. sạndᵃrôwᵃ), to kindle, set alight, ignite (Rām. 9); to inflame, incite, rouse. sạndᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. sạndᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), kindled, etc.; inflamed, roused.

or sandarun conj. 1 (1 p.p. sạndᵒrᵒ), to kindle, set alight, ignite; to set kindling wood to light a fire; to inflame, incite, stir up, rouse. sạndᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. sạndᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), kindled, set alight, inflamed, incited, roused.
or (qq.v.) shrāñĕr, srāñĕr m. dampness, moistness (cf. atha-sᵒ, p. 62b, l. 13); freshness, juiciness. Cf. shrônᵘ, srônᵘ.
m. depth, lowness (cf. atha-sᵒ, p. 62b, l. 11) (Śiv. 1068, 1878); descent, declivity (El. sanyar); a ditch (El. sanyir); (of a man) profoundness, sagacity, gravity. Cf. sonᵘ.

m. joining, uniting, meeting (Rām. 1781 dŏn-hondᵘ sᵒ, union of two, unity, oneness); union, association, company, companionship (Gr. M.; Śiv. 229, 245, 249, 1267, and numerous others in the compound satsang, q.v. s.v.; Rām. 1151); fitting together, like joining with like; the accompaniments of anything, the necessary things for anything (K. 1065). --karun -- m.inf. to associate (with), have intercourse (with); (of man or woman) to have sexual intercourse (with). ¶ sanga-dūsh m. the corruption of good manners by evil associations, the ruin of a person's character by his keeping bad company (Śiv. 1814).

m. a stone (Rām. 199, 1043, 1412; YZ. 557). ¶ L. 65 gives a list of the most common local stones used for ornaments, and other purposes. These are (in his spelling) bilor, a white crystal; sang-i-baswatri, a yellow stone used in medicine; sang-i-dálam, used by goldsmiths; sang-i-farash (p. 64), a kind of slate; sang-i-Nadid, of a dark coffee colour; sang-i-Nalchan, a kind of soap-stone, from which cups and plates are made; sang-i-Musá, of a black colour; sang-i-Ratel, of a chocolate colour; sang-i-Shalamar, of a green colour; sang-i-sumák, coloured blue or purple, with green spots; Takht-i-Sulimán, coloured black, with white streaks. ¶ sang-dil سنگ دل adj. c.g. stony hearted, hard hearted, obdurate (Śiv. 487; cf. Rām. 1043). sang-i-khāra or -khārah (= سنگِ خارا) m. a hard stone, flint (Rām. 1548, 1624). sang-i-marmar سنگ مرمر m. marble (Gr.M.). sang-i-phāras a touch-stone of gems; a philosopher's stone (converting anything it touches into gold) (Śiv. 1616, 1902; K.Pr. 184). -sār  m. stoning (to death), lapidation (H. viii, 8); (in Ksh.) public general abuse; a shark, a water-elephant, a Gangetic crocodile (the ghaṛiyāl of India). -sār gaʦhun m.inf. to be stoned, to suffer lapidation; to become the object of general public abuse. -sār karun m.inf. to stone to death; to make (a person) the object of general public abuse. ¶ sanga-lāth (? cf. سنگلاخ) m. (sg. dat. -lātas), hard gravelly, or stony, soil.

m. a meeting, a visit (Gr.M.); union (with a beloved) (Śiv. 1664); a confluence of two or more rivers. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. union, partnership, to occur; an opportunity for being engaged in any work to occur.

m. in the following:-- sangarōth mēlun m.inf. to become exhausted, done up, prostrate, spent (e.g. from climbing too difficult a mountain (cf. sangur), from performing a very difficult work, from grief, heavy loss, or the like). --milawun -- m.inf. to cause a person to be exhausted as above.
f. (sg. dat. sangüʦᵘ̈), association, living together, partnership (e.g. of beggars, rakes, members of a caravan, and so on); (of a man or woman) copulation, sexual union.

m. (sg. dat. sangāṭas), a collection (of implements, tools, materials, for any object), apparatus, furniture, a collection of the things wanted on a journey, luggage, and so on. --karun -- m.inf. to collect the ab. (L.V. 17).
m. an associate, companion, comrade; confederate, ally, accomplice; a partner in business.
adj. c.g. stony, made of stone; firm, solid, strong (Śiv. 1778; Rām. 131, sangīn-bunā, with firm foundations); severe, excessive; grave, serious (K.Pr. 138).

m. (sg. dat. sangaras), a mountain (esp. when steep and difficult) (Śiv. 1651, 1684, 1707; Rām. 562, 738, 974, 1084); a hill (El.). ¶ sangar-māla f.pl. a line of mountain peaks. -māla phŏlañĕ f. pl. inf. the mountain peaks to blossom, early dawn to appear. -māla phŏlawun adv. at early dawn. -māla phŏlawañĕn adv. at the moment of early dawn. -wath f. (sg. dat. -wati), a mountain pass.
f. of sangur, q.v., in krāla-sangürᵘ̈, p. 470b, l. 24.
m. proximity, vicinity, presence (Śiv. 40, 71, 1156); as adj. c.g. close to, near by (Śiv. 1656). Cf. sannidān.

or sankalaph m. (sg. dat. sankalpas), wish, desire, fancies, esp. evil desires (Śiv. 165, 278, 452, 583, 1311, 1352, 1451, 1530, 1753, 1759, 1791, 1801, 1896); a solemn vow, the performance of an observance. --karun -- m.inf. to make a solemn vow, to make a solemn resolution (Rām. 955); to dedicate, to make a solemn and formal grant (of anything) (Rām. 615).

m. union of unequal persons or things, mixture of good and bad things. -zāth adj. c.g. of unequal birth, begotten of the union of a high-caste woman with a low-caste man, a child of unlawful intermarriage (a word used in abuse). -zöʦᵘ̈-hondᵘ̈ adj. gen. (f. -zöʦᵘ̈-hünzᵘ̈), id.

or sö̃krānth f. (sg. dat. sankaröʦᵘ̈), the passage of the sun or other planetary body from one zodiacal sign to another (cf. shishĕr-sö̃krānth, p. 898a, l. 28); the moment of such passage. (The word is a corruption of the Skt. saṁkrāntiḥ.) --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to keep a vow which is carried out on the day of this passage of the sun. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the moment of this passage (of the sun) to occur. ¶ sankaröʦᵘ̈-phāka m. the fast carried out on the day of this passage.

(or, as written by Paṇḍits) m. the act of drawing together, contraction; a N. of Balarāma (the brother of Kṛṣṇa), who was an incarnation of Vishnu (Viṣṇu) (Śiv. 1408); employed as a title of Shiv (Śiva) (as he who removes sorrow) (Śiv. 364, 987, 1166).

m. (sankaṭas), a difficulty, strait, risk, peril (Gr.M.; Śiv. 215, 254, 645, 797, 945, 1040, 1078, 1508, 1745); defeat (El.); pain, anguish, suffering, distress (from the above, or from disease, poverty, or the like) (cf. sankaṭā-düshᵘ̈, p. 253b, l. 7, and Śiv. 482) (Śiv. 161, 892, 934, 1179, 1190, 1477, 1501). --būgun -- m.inf. to experience such distress. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. voluntarily to accept such distress (e.g. by undertaking someone else's difficult work, or the responsibility for a charge brought against another). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to endure such distress (esp. when due to poverty, to cold, to want of food and clothing, and so on) (Rām. 419). --ʦalun -- m.inf. distress to disappear. --wŏlagun -- m.inf. to undergo such distress. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. such distress to come. ¶ sankaṭa-ʦōram f. (sg. dat. -ʦōrümᵘ̈), a festival held on the fourth lunar day of the dark half of the month of Māg (in Skt. Māgha) (January-February) in honour of the Hindū god Ganēsh, the destroyer of obstacles.
m. N. of one of the six systems of Hindū philosophy (in Skt. the Sāṅkhya philosophy) (Śiv. 1848).
adj. c.g. placed near, close to, amidst (Śiv. 489). Cf. sanidān.
m. the abode of the good, the home of the virtuous; an epithet of Śiva (Śiv. 310).

m. complete renunciation of the world with its possessions and attachments and becoming a wandering ascetic (Śiv. 1264, 1451, 1821); also, i.q. sannyösⁱ, q.v. (L.V. 36; Śiv. 88, 232, 270, 529, 592, 818, 823, 950, 1350, 1354; Rām. 98, 395, 1529, 1681, 1778).
or sannyās, or (q.v.) sȧnⁱyās m. a wandering ascetic who has completely renounced the world, with its possessions and attachments (Śiv. 206, 1759).

m. (sg. dat. santāpas), distress, suffering, anguish, torment (cf. bawa-sᵒ, p. 146b, l. 13) (Śiv. 1870, Rām. 1730, K. 1159). ¶ santāpa-hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), stricken by inward anguish; (of a thing, work, or the like) causing great anguish or sorrow. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), id. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), stricken by anguish.
f. (sg. dat. santüʦᵘ̈), offspring, progeny, descendants.

m. (sg. dat. santas), a venerable and pious man, a saint peaceful and forgiving, with all his passions restrained (Śiv. 238, 270, 1326, 1507, 1523; K. 764, 1053, 1097); a wandering ascetic, a faqīr (credited with magical powers) (K.Pr. 186).

süntūsh or (Gr.M.) santukh m. satisfaction, contentment (El. santush, m. patience, sántúsh, adj. confident, and santuk m. contentment) (Gr.M.; Śiv. (santōsh) 19, 170, 269, 1048, 1313, 1753, 1815, 1817; Rām. (id.) 41, 992; K. 1108, 1110, 1122, 1156; K.Pr. 187).
or (Śiv. 327) sŏntūr m. a dulcimer, a spinet, a harpsichord (Śiv. 327, 1689, 1779).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sāntwanôwᵘ), to appease, pacify; to utter kind or conciliatory words (K. 1013).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. sanyōv), to become deep (as a hollow forming in level ground, the water in a well, and so on) (Śiv. 1757) (cf. sonᵘ wŏgonᵘ, p. 918a, l. 21); to be impressed into something, to sink into (dat.) (e.g. a hard lump in a pillow or cushion pressing into the body, a blow or thrust on the body or on the eye, a too heavy wall sinking into the ground owing to weak foundations, the feet into a gravelly road) (Rām. 1250); to be thrust or stuck deeply into (e.g. a spike, a thorn, a splinter amid food stuck between the teeth or into the palate); (of the limbs of two persons in close embrace) to penetrate into (each other, dat. with kun), to intermingle (Rām. 1117); to become impregnated in something (of a soft bed or the like), to penetrate into (the hollows of the body, dat.), to fit snugly to (the form of the body) (Rām. 1495, YZ. 188); (of some incurable disease) to become established throughout the whole body; (of some mental condition, such as anger, love, sorrow, pity, gratitude, or some lesson learnt) to become thoroughly absorbed (into the heart, brain, etc.) (Śiv. 1005). ¶ sanith gaʦhun m.inf. to become absorbed, or thoroughly thrust into, as ab. (e.g. love, hate, gratitude, something taught, in the mind, or a thorn, etc., in the skin where it has gone right in and cannot be extracted). ¶ sanyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sanyē-müʦᵘ̈), thrust into, stuck into; absorbed into, etc., as ab.

m. making ready, equipment (for engaging in any work), setting to (to anything) (K. 665). --karun -- m.inf. to make the necessary preparations for beginning some intended work (Śiv. 1016, 1168; K. 1001, 1006, 1018, 1126). ¶ sȧnzⁱ-ḍaba m. one of a number of caskets containing scents and other toilet necessaries presented to a bride, before the actual marriage ceremony, by the relations of the bridegroom. -worᵘ m. a large handsome box, in which these caskets are contained, and conveyed to the bride's residence (Śiv. 1218). ¶ sanzas lagun m.inf. to be ready and equipped for setting to to any work (K. 371, 893, 1033).
m. bringing to life, life-restoring, reanimation, resuscitation (Śiv. 1059).
f. a kind of elixir (said to restore the dead to life) (Śiv. 1855).
f. (sg. dat. sạnzᵃrüñᵃ), the collecting together of the necessary equipment, preparatory to beginning a work; the starting or beginning to do any work.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sạnzᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. sạnzᵃrun, but esp. in the sense of beginning a quarrel.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sạnzᵒrᵒ), to get together equipment, to begin (e.g. of a man setting to work to cook) (Gr.Gr. 8); (of clouds, etc.) to begin (to rain); to begin to quarrel, to come to blows.
or (Gr.M.) sanʦĕth m. (sg. dat. sanʦatas), accumulation, collection, hoarding up (of money, goods, virtues, or the like) (Gr.M.).
m. a hoard, heap, accumulation, stock, store (esp. of money gradually hoarded up).
f. (sg. dat. sạñᵉ̆rüñᵉ̆), making deeper (as a pit, a well, or the like); thrusting down into; inculcation, imbuing (something into another's heart, or the like).
(1 p.p. sạñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), i.q. sạñᵉ̆run, q.v. sạñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. sạñᵉ̆rövᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), i.q. sạñᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, s.v. sạñᵉ̆run, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sạñᵒrᵒ), to make deeper (e.g. a dish, a lake, a well, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 8); to thrust down into; to inculcate, imbue (something into another's heart). sạñᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. sạñᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made deep or hollow; thrust down into; inculcated.
i.q. sannyösⁱ, q.v. a wandering ascetic, who has completely renounced the world, with its possessions and attachments (Rām. 784, 1143i; H. (saniyās) v, 10-12); as adj. c.g. intoxicated (El. saniyás).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sapadôwᵘ), to cause to become, to make, fashion, shape, fabricate, prepare, get ready, complete, finish (Śiv. 74, 102); to cause to be available, provide (Gr.M.). sapadôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sapadövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made, completed.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. sapodᵘ, f. sapüzᵘ̈), to become (very frequent in this sense; cf. dôdᵘ sᵒ, p. 191a, l. 41; dōsth sᵒ, p. 256b, l. 8; khŏsh sᵒ, p. 418b, l. 6, and many others) (L.V. 86; Śiv. 665; Rām. 1467; H. iii, 2, 7; vi, 11, 16; xii, 1); to be made, produced, formed, completed, effected (Gr.Gr. 204, Gr.M., Śiv. 1060); to arise, come into being, to happen, occur, take place (Gr.M.; H. vii, 13); (with dat. of possession) there is (to so-and-so), (he) has (Gr.M.). In the past tense, 'I became,' etc., are used to mean 'I became and am now'; hence, 'I am,' etc. (Gr.M.; Śiv. 111, 498, 501); cf. sampanun, sapanun, sö̃panun, and sapazun. The fem. of the past participle, sapüzᵘ̈ and its connected forms, can also be referred to the verb sapazun. sapodᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sapüzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), become, come into existence, completed.

or (q.v.) sampanun  conj. 2 (1 p.p. saponᵘ, f. sapüñᵘ̈), to become (very frequent in this sense; cf. onᵘ sᵒ, p. 30b, l. 22; cō̃ca sᵒ, p. 157a, l. 33; jamā sᵒ, p. 373b, l. 17, and many others) (Śiv. 500, 676, 696, 727, 729, 829, 831, 874, 941, 1103, 1283, 1304, 1317, 1335, 1464; Rām. 29, 69, 93, 96, 98, 104, 142, etc.; K. 7, 12, 19, 607, 1010; H. x, 4; YZ. 13, 123, 177); to be made, produced, formed, completed, effected (Gr.Gr. 204, Rām. 33); to arise, come into being, to happen, occur, take place (Rām. 51, 99, 146, 268, 278, 432, 562, 716, 722, 864, 1004, 1068, etc.; K. 171, 833); (with dat. of possession) there is (to so-and-so), (he) has. In the past tense, 'I became,' etc., are used to mean 'I became and am now'; hence, 'I am' (Rām. 231); cf. sampanun, sapadun, sö̃panun, and sapazun. saponᵘ-motᵘ  perf. part. (f. sapüñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), become, come into existence, completed (Rām. 455, 1262).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sapazôwᵘ), to cause to become, to make, fashion, shape, fabricate, prepare, make ready, complete. sapazôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sapazövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made, completed.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. sapozᵘ), to become (cf. cō̃ca sᵒ, p. 157a, l. 34; dabanga sᵒ, p. 184a, l. 7; daphā sᵒ, p. 232b, l. 16; data- waturᵘ sᵒ, p. 257b, l. 12; nēkh sᵒ, p. 629b, l. 21; tēr sᵒ, s.v. tēr) (Gr.Gr. 226); to be made, produced, formed, completed, effected (Gr.Gr. 204); and so on, in all the meanings and uses of sapadun, with which it is synonymous; cf. sampanun, sapadun, sapanun, and sö̃panun. sapozᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (sapüzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), become, come into existence, completed.

adj. c.g. pure, clean, clear (cf. atha-sᵒ, p. 62b, l. 19) (El. sāf; Gr.M.; Śiv. 168, 815; K.Pr. 111, 183, 231); calm, serene; open, unclouded, bright (as the sky) (Gr.M.); open, sincere, candid, pure (of heart) (Gr.M., Śiv. 572, Rām. 60); distinct, perspicuous, (of handwriting, pronunciation, etc.) clear, plain (Gr.M.; Rām. 536, 1609); as adv. clearly (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to make clear (Gr.M.); to clear (e.g. land from jungle) (Gr.M.); to make (a board or the like) smooth, to plane smooth (Gr.M.). --pöṭhⁱ -- or --pöṭhin -- adv. clearly, distinctly. ¶ sāphas nērun m.inf. to come out into the clear, i.e. to present oneself before another (ready and willing to perform some work).
m. face, surface; the page or leaf of a book; (in Ksh.) the long (usually marshy) level strip of land along the edge of a river.
m. a cloth worn round the head, a kind of turban.

adj. c.g. bearing fruit, productive; profitable, advantageous, remunerative; efficient, successful (Rām. 1686); fulfilled (of a blessing, curse, or the like). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become fruitful (K. 274, 706); to become profitable. --karun -- m.inf. to make fruitful, to cause to produce fruit.

m. journeying, travelling; a journey, travel, voyage (El. Gr.M. safar; H. x, 1; xi, 3; xii, 25); (in Ksh.) fatigue, weariness (caused by travelling) (Rām. 196, 1386, 1711). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to complete or finish a long journey. --karun -- m.inf. to travel (El.). --yinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. great troubles or calamities to come.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. sapharladiñ), suffering from fatigue or weariness (due to travelling).

adj. c.g. white (El. safed; W. 21 sufed; Śiv. 128, 445, 619, 815); as subst. m. the colour white (Śiv. 877). -pōsh سفید پوش adj. c.g. wearing white garments; (in Ksh.) a descriptive name given to the more affluent men of a village (who wear white clothes) (L. 253).
m. Dalbergia sissoo (El. safeda); adj. white (= saphēd) (Gr.M. safēda).
m. the Himalayan poplar (El. sufédar, Populus ciliata). Cf. bagnū; dūd-phras, p. 191b, l. 15; and sulölī.
m. cleanness, clearness (cf. atha-sᵒ, p. 62b, l. 21); serenity; sincerity, candour; distinctness, clarity.

m. a lake, a large sheet of water (cf. brahma-sar, p. 121a, l. 16; divᵃsar, p. 264b, l. 22; kōla-sar, p. 441b, l. 7; krama-sar, p. 471a, l. 17; nīla-sar, p. 634a, l. 14; pamba-sar, p. 733b, l. 24) (Gr.M.; L.V. 47, 50, 78, 79; Śiv. 14, 155, 164, 245, 254, 491, 511, 927, etc.; Rām. 30, 250, 1596; K. 219; K.Pr. 35, 138, 188, 243); cf. saras. -pachin m. a certain bird, probably the Indian crane (Ardea antigone or A. sibirica).

m. essence, substance, quintessence, the best or choicest part (of anything) (Śiv. 1578, 1789) (cf. tribuwana-sār, s.v. tribuwan); essence, essential part, quintessence (Śiv. 14, 50, 91, 156, 395, 514, 521, 850, etc.; Rām. 1573; K. 437, 969); marrow, cream, pith (Gr.M.); strength, vigour; valour, heroism, prowess; value, worth, excellence (K.Pr. 52); the highest, the best (of anything) (Śiv. 63); the innermost part (of a mountain range), a defile, pass (Rām. 375). -dār-dŏh m. a day of which a long time or a great part has elapsed (e.g. in the doing of something which should normally occupy a short time). --nērun -- m.inf. quintessence to issue, to become thoroughly and entirely affectionate. --rōzun -- m.inf. the quintessence to remain (after the non-essentials have disappeared). --thawun -- m.inf. one's eager desire to be fulfilled. ¶ sāra-kath f. (sg. dat. -kathi), the essential fact, the pith of a matter (Rām. 30).

m. head, top, end, point (Śiv. 428; Rām. 444 (bar sar بر سر, on the head); K.Pr. 188); origin, beginning (cf. navi sara, again, p. 667b, l. 16, and Persian سرِ نو); (as adv.) at the beginning, first (K.Pr. 187); cf. shēr 3. -basta سر بستہ adj. c.g. closed at the top or end; hence, covered, closed, shut (e.g. an envelope) (Rām. 841). -golᵘ m. the superior of a field-watcher or Shĕkh-dar (p. 876b, l. 13) (El. sargaul). -gardān سر گردان adj. c.g. dizzy, vertiginous; stupefied, bewildered, amazed; humbled, depressed (K.Pr. 103). -garm سر گرم adj. c.g. enthusiastic, ardent, zealous, eager, earnest, intent (Gr.M.); assiduous, diligent, attentive. -hang سرہنگ m. the upper beam of a door-frame, a lintel; a chief, overseer, esp. the head man or leader of a village community, or the like. sar-ē- kŏh (= سرِ کوہ) m. the pinnacle of a mountain, a mountain peak (Rām. 400 (az sar˚, از سر کوہ, from the mountain peak)). sar-kôpᵘ (= سرکوب) m. an overlooker, superior, superintendent, esp. the head, or leading, man of a village community. -kash سرکش m. proud, arrogant, insolent; chief (El.). -māyĕ سرمایہ, see s.v. sar-ā-pā سرا پا or sar-ā-pāy adv. from head to foot, from top to bottom, throughout, totally (Rām. 571 (-pāy), 1087 (-pā)). sar-pēch سر پیچ m. (sg. dat. -pēcas), an ornament of gold, silver, or jewels, worn in front of the turban; a band of silk or embroidery, from two to two and a half cubits long, worn round the turban; a similar band of pashmīna material worn round the upper part of the head by women in the cold season. -pōsh سر پوش m. a dish-cover, basket- cover, lid (K.Pr. 188). -sān, -sönⁱ, see s.vv. --ʦaṭun -- m.inf. to cut off a head, to behead (dat. of person beheaded) (H. viii, 11). -war, سرور, see s.v. -zada سر زدہ adj. c.g. depraved, base, ill-bred (Gr.M.). ¶ sȧrⁱ-pĕṭhⁱ sahlāb m. 'a flood over the top of the head' (so explained. Cf., however, sȧrⁱ 1); hence, great excess with undesirable results (e.g. great increase of wealth causing pride, or great excess of loss of capital causing destruction). ¶ sari-shām (= سرِ شام) or sarē-shām m. evening; the early evening (Śiv. 1722 (sarē-sh˚)). -shāma or -shāmay adv. (occurring) only in the evening. -shāmukᵘ gen. (f. -shāmücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or occurring in, the evening. -shāman, or -shāman-bögⁱ, or -shāman-bögin adv. at eventide, in the evening, at about evening. -shāmas, or -shāmas-bögⁱ, or -shāmas-bögin adv., id. -shômᵘ adj. (f. -shömᵘ̈), occurring, produced, etc., in the evening; (as subst. m.) the evening, eventide.

f. (sg. dat. sörᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 71), a support, post, pedestal (cf. nama-sᵒ, p. 635b, l. 46; nāwa-sᵒ, p. 666b, l. 24; thapa-sᵒ, s.v. thaph); a supporting or strengthening cross-beam in a house, a rafter (cf. thapa-sār, a banister, s.v. thaph) (Gr.Gr. 71).

m. testing, test, trial (El.); as adj. c.g. tested, tried (H. x, 4); cf. saragī and sāran karüñᵘ̈, s.v. sāran 2. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become ascertained, understood, thoroughly tested (Śiv. 631, 1589, 1891; Rām. 1067). --khara karun -- m.inf. to make close inquiry (into), to test, try (cf. khara-sara karun, p. 408b, l. 12). --karun -- m.inf. to try, to test, grasp the nature of (Śiv. 162, 349, 1750, 1772, 1800; Rām. 1606; H. viii, 13; x, 2, 6, 14); to investigate, make inquiry (Rām. 1382). --sika gaʦhun -- m.inf. 'the testing to become stamped'; hence, to become thoroughly understood or ascertained after minute (inquiry), to be thoroughly tested. --sika karun -- m.inf. to examine minutely, investigate thoroughly, scrutinize, test.
f. testing, trying, investigation (H. viii, 7, 8, 10; x, 7); experimenting (El.); temptation (El.). Cf. sara 1.
adj. c.g. simple, easy (of a road, task, or the like); plain, intelligible (of a book, or the like).

f. (sg. dat. sārüñᵘ̈), collection, bringing by instalments from one place to another, transporting and heaping up (e.g. grain from the threshing floor to the house); the being collected, being piled up. -bāna m. a vessel for transporting (e.g. a sack or the like) and piling in another place.

f. (sg. dat. as in sāran 1), touching, feeling (e.g. something in the dark, or which one cannot see, in order to find out what it is); testing (by questioning or the like) a person's secret intentions; a certain kind of treatise for expediting astronomical calculations. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to test another's hidden intentions (as if by touching or feeling) (cf. sara).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sāranôwᵘ), to cause things to be gradually transported from one place for collection in another.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. as in sāranāwun 1), to have (a thing or person) felt, touched, tested (by feeling), by another; to have a person's secret intentions found out (by questioning or the like), by another.
f. a certain musical instrument like a fiddle.
m. a player on a sārang, a fiddler.
m. (sg. dat. sarāphas), a money-changer; a banker, a 'shroff' (Gr.M., W. 118, Rām. 1066, K.Pr. 188); met. the weight, scales, etc., of an honest shopkeeper.
m. a lake, pool, pond (cf. brahma-saras, p. 121a, l. 16). I.q. sar 1, q.v.
f. a N. of Śāradā, the goddess of learning, and patron goddess of Kashmīr (Skt. Sarasvatī) (Śiv. 1095, 1151, 1497; Rām. 147, 1617).
f. the wages paid for gradually transporting a collection of articles from one place to another. Cf. sārun 1.
n.ag. (f. sāravüñᵘ̈), one who transports (gradually) from one place to another; one who collects, accumulates. Cf. sārun 1.
n.ag. (f. as in 1), one who touches, feels, tests by feeling (something which he cannot see); one who worms out another's hidden intentions or opinions. Cf. sārun 2.
n.ag. (f. as in 1), that which is being gradually transported from one place to another, or which is being accumulated. Cf. sārun 3.

or sarāy (سرائی) f. a temporary home for travellers, a caravansary, inn (El. saráí); a small or insignificant quarter of a large town; (in certain compounds) a house or room in which a number of people are assembled (cf. mātam-sᵒ, p. 607a, l. 12) (Śiv. 829).
f., i.q. sörᵘ̈ 3, q.v. gradual transportation from place to place; collection, accumulation (cf. lāka-sᵒ, p. 517b, l. 50).
m. a class of Hindū religious mendicants, who do not accept the Hindū ideas of caste, pollution, etc. (the sarbhangīs of India; they have a reputation for vehement shamelessness).
m. a head man, head, chief, commander (Śiv. 2, 36; K.Pr. 136, 187).
m. the lintel of a door.
f. cold, coldness, chilliness, rawness (Śiv. 348; Rām. 1005, 1267).
f. headship, chiefship, lordship, supremacy, domination, sway, rule, government (Śiv. 632).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. sardyōv), to become cold, to become chilly, to feel cold (Rām. 1005).
f. completeness, entirety. This word is reported as fem., but it is probably masc.
m. a chief, master, lord (Śiv. 10, 1798); the government of a country (Gr.M., Śiv. 1798).
m. the name, used in schools, of the Śāradā letter corresponding to the Nāgarī ṭha. Cf. ar-mã̄ṭa.

m. principal sum, capital, stock-in-trade; funds, assets, means, resources. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. savings to be made (after expenditure). --karun -- m.inf. to save up. --rōzun -- m.inf. to be saved up (after expenditure), to remain over and above. --thawun -- m.inf. to keep savings, to save up.

(= sarv سرو) m. (pl. dat. sarŏn, Rām. 1197) a cypress (El. sarú; Rām. 1197; YZ. 64); (in Ksh.) a kind of jewelled gold ornament worn by young married women on the forehead. -kulᵘ m. a cypress-tree (Gr.M.). ¶ sarv-i-kad سرو قد adj. c.g. cypress-like in stature, tall and graceful (Rām. 353, 520, 1494; YZ. 12, 229).
f. the occupation or profession of a money-changer.
in the following:-- sarŏrā karun m.inf. to send a person (after making all due arrangements).

(sg. dat. sarpã̄khi), a snake's eye; N. of a certain plant with a small flower resembling a snake's eye (? L. 76, sarpang, Euphorbia sp. a medicinal herb, used internally and externally for scurvy and skin diseases).

m. swelling in the head, tumour or inflammation of the brain; met. swelling in the head, great self-presumption, arrogance, 'swelled head'. --dörith dyunᵘ -- m.inf. inflammation of the brain to attack (a person). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. arrogance or self-presumption to occur. --karun -- inflammation of the brain to attack a person.
m. (sg. dat. sarshĕpas), the mustard plant or seed, rape (L. 330 sarshaf). Cf. sȧndij.
adj. c.g. full of arrogance or self-presumption, suffering from 'swelled head'.

f. brass (El.; Gr.M.; L. 458, sártal; Siv. 544, 1060, 1307-8; Rām. 682, 1067; YZ. 24, 286; K.Pr. 206). ¶ sartali-bāna m. a vessel made of brass, a brazen vessel. -hondᵘ gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, brass; made of brass, brazen. -hār a certain eye-ointment (made of burnt and powdered cowries (hār) mixed in a brass vessel with the milk of the mother of a girl baby).
adj. c.g. possessed of great knowledge, knowing much, well-informed, thoroughly taught.
m. singing, chanting (cf. sāza-sᵒ, s.v. sāz).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sorᵘ), to remember, keep in remembrance, bear in mind (L.V. 50; H. xi, 14); to experience, meet with, encounter, undergo (Gr.Gr. 9, Rām. 1509); cf. sŏrun. sorᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), remembered.

conj. 1 (1 p.p.sôrᵘ), to transport (gradually) from one place and to collect in another (e.g. grain from the threshing floor to the house) (cf. atha sᵒ, p. 62b, l. 30; kranjali pôñᵘ̈ sᵒ, p. 474a, l. 48) (Śiv. 341; Rām. 233; H. ix, 9; xi, 6, 10); to collect, heap, pile up, accumulate (cf. ḍēr sᵒ, p. 236b, l. 12) (Gr.Gr. 23; W. 141, suri, he will receive, is perhaps incorr. for sāri; Rām. 1462; K.Pr. 36, 48, 115, 259); gradually to bring near, put near (a person or place) (K. 158). sôrᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. sörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), collected after transport; piled up, accumulated.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. as in sārun 1), to feel, touch, test by feeling (e.g. to feel something in the dark, or which one cannot see, in order to find out what it is) (cf. khōr sᵒ, p. 410a, l. 18) (Gr.Gr. 120, 121-2; Rām. 237); to touch, affect (the heart or the like) (Rām. 350, 1485); (by judicious questioning or the like) to test or find out a person's private intentions or opinion. sôrᵘ-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. as in sārun 1), felt, tested, etc., as ab.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. sāryōv), to be gradually accumulated, to be gradually piled up or collected, to be transported gradually from one place to another. sāryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sāryē-müʦᵘ̈), accumulated, as ab.
adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. sarṻpas), having form, that which has form (Śiv. 1757).

adj. c.g. (a word borrowed from Skt.) all (the Ksh. word is sôrᵘ 1, q.v.). This word is used in Skt. compounds, such as the following (and similarly in Śiv. 4, 39, 115, 156, 194, 208, 212, 739, 884, 1089, 1159, 1352, 1507, 1510, 1518, 1525, 1744-5, 1759, 1799, 1886, 1889, 1892-3, 1896; K. 2, 21, etc.). -ādikār or sarwādikār m. having power over all, a universal rule, omnipotence (Śiv. 1799). -ādikörī or sarwādikörī adj. c.g. one who has power over all, one who is the ruler or superintendent of the universe, omnipotent (an epithet of the Supreme Deity) (Śiv. 1507, 1893). sarwa-gath adj. c.g. going to all places; hence, as an epithet of the Deity, All-pervading, Omnipresent (L.V. 64). sarwa-gyĕtā f. omniscience (Gr.M.). sarwa-kriy m. he who made all things, the All-Creator (L.V. 59). sarwa-shĕktimān adj. c.g. omnipotent (Gr.M.). sarwa-sw m. everything, the whole of one's possessions (Śiv. 1850).
adv. always (a Skt. borrowed word in sadā-sarwadā, p. 863b, l. 8).
sarwadikörī, see sarwa-ādiᵒ, col. a, ll. 37, 39.
adj. c.g. complete in every limb, complete in every respect, perfectly complete.

or saruph m. (sg. dat. sarpas; pl. nom. sarᵃph or saraph, dat. sarpan. The f. of this word is sȧrⁱpiñ or sarpiñ, q.v.), a serpent, a snake (cf. kāla-sᵒ, p. 435b, l. 47; pā̃-sᵒ, p. 748a, l. 17) (Gr.Gr. 48, 73; Gr.M.; L. 155, 464, saraf; W. 17, 139, saruf; Śiv. 812, 876, 1055, 1818; K. 236-41, 345; H. (sarᵃph) x, 13; K.Pr. 23, 127, 188). ¶ sarpa-gŏsôñᵘ m. a snake- charmer, one who wanders about exhibiting snakes (Śiv. 90). -kroʦhᵘ m. a snake's slough. -lyūṭᵘ m. a two-headed snake (believed to have a head at each end). -mölyunᵘ m. 'the home of a snake's father-in-law', a place haunted by (or full of) snakes. -wöjⁱ or -wöjᵘ̈ f. a snake's hole (in which it lives). -wôlᵘ m. a snake-catcher. -zāth subst. f. and adj. c.g. (as subst. sg. dat. -zöʦᵘ̈), the tribe of serpents, the snake tribe; (as adj.) a snake-like person, one who habitually destroys or injures others.

m. change, conversion; use, employment (Gr.M.); expending; (in Grammar) inflexion, declension, conjugation. sarf o nahw صرف و نحو f. inflexion and syntax, grammar (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to spend, expend, pass (time) (Gr.M.); to use, employ.

adj. c.g. flooded, inundated; (of a lake or the like) overflowing (L.V. 50). This word is obsolete at the present day, except in the following:-- sȧrⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to become inundated, flooded with water (H. iv, 3); (of a person) to become wet all over, flooded over with water (or other liquid), soaked from head to foot, plunged in (Śiv. 349). --karun -- m.inf. to flood, cover with water; to wet (a person or thing) all over. -nāwa f.pl. inundation, flooding (of land, etc.). -pĕṭhⁱ sahlāb, see p. 928a, l. 49.
adj. c.g. corrupt, decayed, decomposed, in nīla-sȧrⁱ gaʦhun, nīla-sȧrⁱ karun, p. 634a, ll. 9, 12, qq.v. Cf. sorᵘ 2 and the Hindī saṛnā.

or (K. 238) sarpiñ f. (f. of sarᵃph 1, q.v.), a female snake (cf. pā̃-sᵒ, p. 748a, l. 17) (El. serriping; W. 17, sarafiṉ; K. 238); a form of smallpox. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an attack of this smallpox to occur.

beans, peas, gram, lentils, or other similar crop (W. 124; K.Pr. 99, 182); a kind of porridge made of one of these crushed (cf. mahā- or māha-sᵒ, p. 553a, ll. 16, 27; phŏṭa-sᵒ, p. 716b, l. 33; ras-sas, p. 841b, l. 30; rasa-kᵒtᵒ sasa-kᵒtᵒ, p. 842a, l. 4) (K.Pr. 189). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. an obstacle, impediment, to occur (esp. in some completed work, owing to some mistake in the arrangements) to be spoilt in this way; to become disgraced by abuse or the like. --karun -- m.inf. to cause an obstacle, to spoil some completed work. --ras dyunᵘ -- m.inf. 'to deposit porridge and soup', to deposit cooked food as an offering at a cross-roads or similar place (intended to be eaten by dogs, crows, etc.), in order to ward off disaster (cf. ras-sas, p. 841b, l. 30). --ras mēlun -- m.inf. (owing to want of discrimination) to mix up things of opposing qualities (truth and falsehood, pure and impure, what is to be done and what is to be avoided, eatable and uneatable, and so on). ¶ sasa-mujᵘ̈ f. a dish composed of this porridge mixed with chopped up radishes, etc.
m. breath, breathing, respiration; a cough (Gr.M. sās). --karun -- m.inf. to cough (El.).

or (L.V. 43) swās m. ashes (cf. sūr-sās, p. 932b, l. 16) (L.V. 18 sās, 43 swās; Śiv. 818, 833, 951, 1355, 1436, 1444; K.Pr. 262); a kind of black smutty fungus, attacking maize and wheat (L. 337, 342). ¶ sāsa-gāsh m. a dim light. -küṭᵘ̈ f. a mountain road making descent difficult; the name of a difficult mountain on the pilgrim route in Kashmīr.

card. m.pl. a thousand (cf. dah sās, p. 199a, l. 4, and p. 271a, l. 36) (Gr.Gr. 80, 85, 144, 149; L.V. 34; Śiv. 711, 951, 1353, 1438, 1444, 1467, 1875; Rām. 122, 363, 395, 1740, 1755; K. 97, 236, 431, 765, 960, etc.; K.Pr. 150); a sum of money consisting of ten haths; each hath (q.v.) at present corresponding to a British pice (K.Pr. 238). ¶ sāsa-bodᵘ adj. (f. -büzᵘ̈), of a thousand kinds (K. 167); (in plur.) in thousands, thousands of (Gr.Gr. 144; W. 104; Śiv. 61, 203, 952, 1436; Rām. 630, 1271; K. 29, 170, 727, 913, 1008, 1132; YZ. 16, 30, 225), sāsa-bȧdⁱ sās, thousands upon thousands (Rām. 865, 1377). -grand f. (sg. dat. -grünzᵘ̈), 'a count of thousands', the being in thousands. -phyurᵘ m. gain or profit of thousands. -sāsa adv. thousand by thousand. -ṭopᵘ adj. of a thousand directions, coming from a thousand, or countless, sides (e.g. help, fortune, profits of business, and so on). ¶ sāsā (with suff. of indef. art.) a thousand, i.e. any indefinite great number (L.V. 18; K.Pr. 45 (sásah), 57, 66). ¶ sāsan-hȧndⁱ sās c.g. pl. thousands of thousands, countless thousands.

m. union, close attachment, intimacy; league, intimate consultation, conspiracy, collusion. --karun -- m.inf. to consult together, to conspire. -wöṭᵘ̈ f. (by mutual consultation) arrangement of companionship or relationship (e.g. private consultation regarding going together on a journey, or regarding a suggested marriage). -wôṭᵘ m. private agreement, joint secrecy (e.g. for the accomplishment of some work, when it is agreed to take precautions against some secret concerning it being divulged before the work is accomplished).
or satahöṭh card. (pl. dat. satahai(hö)ṭhan ), sixty-seven (Gr.Gr. 79).
ord. (f. satahǖṭhimᵘ̈), sixty-seventh (Gr.Gr. 79, where it is written satahaiṭhyumᵘ).
adj. (f. satahǖṭhiñᵘ̈), costing sixty-seven (rupees or the like); having wages of sixty-seven (rupees or the like).

f. (sg. dat. satümᵘ̈), the seventh lunar day of a lunar fortnight (cf. hāra-sᵒ, etc., p. 344a, l. 10; hurⁱ-sⁱ, p. 347b, l. 18) (Rām. 1768). satümᵘ̈-hondᵘ̈ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or occurring on the seventh lunar day.

card. (sg. dat. satanamatan), ninety-seven (Gr.Gr. 80). satanamatan-hondᵘ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, ninety-seven; costing, or worth, ninety-seven (rupees, etc.); earning wages of ninety-seven (rupees, etc.).
(? spelling and gend.) in satar gāḍ f. N. of a certain fish found plentifully in Kashmīr (L. 158, sattar gad).
(cf. شطرنجی) f. (sg. dat. sataranjĕ), a kind of checkered carpet, a carpet made of cotton, a 'durree'. ¶ sataranjĕ-palav m. a small carpet.
(? spelling and gend.) in nākh satarwati a species of pear, with a beautiful shape and a sweet juicy flesh (L. 350, nák s˚).
adj. (f. satasatatiñᵘ̈), costing, or worth, seventy-seven (rupees or the like); earning wages of seventy-seven (rupees or the like).

card. (pl. dat. satashītan), eighty-seven (Gr.Gr. 79). satashītan-hondᵘ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, eighty-seven; costing, or worth, eighty-seven (rupees, etc.); earning eighty-seven (rupees or the like).
card. (pl. dat. satatan), seventy (Gr.Gr. 79, 148). satatan-andar adj. c.g. in seventy, i.e. seventy years old.

card. forty-seven (Gr.Gr. 78) (El. satajih). satatöjihan-hondᵘ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, forty-seven; worth, or costing, forty-seven (rupees or the like); earning wages of forty-seven (rupees or the like).

card. thirty-seven (Gr.Gr. 77). satatrᵃhan-hondᵃ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, thirty-seven; costing, or worth, thirty-seven (rupees or the like); earning wages of thirty-seven (rupees or the like).
adj. (f.satatiñᵘ̈), costing, or worth, seventy (rupees or the like) (Gr.Gr. 148); earning wages of seventy (rupees or the like).
m.pl. a group of seventy, a seventy; the form taken by satath, seventy, q.v., as a multiplicative, as in kāh satȧtⁱ sath hath ta satath, eleven seventies are seven hundred and seventy (Gr.Gr. 86).

m. worrying, teasing, harassing, interrupting or distracting (a person busily occupied in some work). --lāgun -- m.inf. to distract or tease (a person busily employed on something, by raising a noise, worrying with requests, or the like). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. such worry, teasing, harassment, or distraction to come (upon a person).
f. that which causes worry, teasing, or harassment to a person (used impersonally). Cf. satövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, p. 949b, l. 38.

card. fifty-seven (Gr.Gr. 78). satawanzāhan-hondᵘ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, fifty-seven; worth, or costing, fifty-seven (rupees or the like); earning wages of fifty-seven (rupees or the like).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. satôwᵘ. This verb is impersonal, and, in tenses which change for gender, is conjugated in the feminine) to trouble, tease, worry, molest, interrupt, persecute, harass (Gr.M.). satôwᵘ-motᵘ worried, harassed, teased. The fem. is used impersonally in satövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, as in ȧmⁱ chĕm satövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, by this, there is worry to me, i.e. this worries me.
m. N. of Krushna's (Kṛṣṇa's) charioteer (in Skt. sātyaki) (K. 820).

f. (sg. dat. saṭi), a cause of alarm, a scare; as --˚ with dat., used to indicate non-identity but similarity (cf. lūkas sᵒ, p. 519b, l. 13; tamis sᵒ, s.v. tih). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a sudden scare to come, to become terrified by an accusation of a crime or by reviling or scandal, etc.

m. (sg. dat. satas), truth (El. adj. true) (Śiv. 249, 376, 582, 642, 736, 753, etc.; Rām. 27, 31, 33, 35, 509, 956, 1782); sincerity (Śiv. 182); goodness, virtue, purity (Śiv. 1437, Rām. 1054); nature, essence, natural character; substance, body, substantiality (L.V. 41); existence. Cf. sath 4. ¶ sata-kinⁱ adv. truthfully, in good truth; thoroughly (Rām. 815). -rāth f. (sg. dat. -röʦᵘ̈), the ceremonial first visit after the marriage of a bride and bridegroom to the bride's father's house (El. satarát, m. the third day after marriage) (Śiv. 1549, 1553); the present sent to the bride at her husband's house before this visit (L. 262 satrat). -röʦᵘ̈-bôgᵘ̈ m. the present paid to the bridegroom by the bride's people on the occasion of this visit. -röʦᵘ̈-mahanyuwᵘ̈ m. the servant who carries this present. -röʦᵘ̈-mahārĕñ f. the bride on this occasion. -röʦᵘ̈-mahārāza m. the bridegroom on this occasion. -röʦᵘ̈-phọ̆tᵘ̈ m. the basket or trunk in which the above present is carried. ¶ satō-sath m. truth of truth, absolute truth, that which is absolutely true (Śiv. 693). ¶ sathạy-sath m. absolute truth, the very truth (Śiv. 741, 838). ¶ satukᵘ adj. gen. (f.satücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, truth (Śiv. 382, 623, 658, 1267-8, 1654, 1743, 1771, 1884-5; Rām. 35-6, 46, 181, 1686); born of truth resulting from truth (Śiv. 236, 553, 601-4); having the nature of truth (Śiv. 245, Rām. 11). ¶ satas-pĕṭh rōzun m.inf. to continue living a sincere life.
m. (sg. dat. sāthas), company, society, association, alliance. ¶ sāthạy-sāth adv. in close company (with anyone) (Śiv. 1552).

f. (sg. dat. süʦᵘ̈), hope, expectation, prospect (cf. mana-sᵒ, p. 572a, l. 41; potᵘ-sᵘ, p. 788a, l. 6; pŏtra-sᵒ, p. 799b, l. 28; sŏmīrüñᵘ̈-sᵘ̈, p. 914b, l. 10) (Gr.Gr. 69, L.V. 102, K. 723); trust, confidence (in a person) (cf. mölⁱ-sⁱ, p. 566b, l. 28) (Śiv. 1256, 1364, 1584, 1865; K. 525; K.Pr. 194). --barüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be full of hope, to hope. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. hope to occur, to be felt (by a person, dat.); consolation to occur (K. 725). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give hope, console (K. 369, 461, 467, 500, 645, 742, 757, 856, 862). ¶ süʦᵘ̈ karañĕ f. pl. inf. to give hopes, console (K. 407, 472, 474, 477, 566, 1123); to make hopes, to feel hope (K. 1120). --rōzun -- m. inf. to pass the time in hope. --thawun -- m. inf. to confirm (a person) in hope.

m. (sg. dat. sātas), time, a particular time (cf. potᵘ sāᵒ, p. 788a, l. 10; patyumᵘ sāᵒ, p. 806a, l. 18, and Rām. 258) (L.V. 25; Rām. 836, 1023; H. iii, 6; vii, 8; xii, 4, 15; K.Pr. 22 (sáat); an instant, a short space of time, a minute, a moment (cf. prath sāta, p. 769a, l. 37, and Rām. 582) (L.V. 104; Śiv. 1304, 1883; Rām. 203, 858); esp. the auspicious moment for performing any action (cf. dŏda-sᵒ, p. 190a, l. 29; dŏhᵃ̣lᵃ̣-sᵃ̣, p. 200b, l. 37; pana-sᵒ, p. 734b, l. 1; prövishĕ-sᵒ, p. 773b, l. 1) (Rām. 1098, 1709); (in astrology) a particular fortunate or unfortunate time (L.V. 3; Śiv. 38, 1550). --nērun -- m.inf. the auspicious moment (for beginning any work) to be ascertained (by consulting an almanac or the like). --raṭun -- m.inf. to grasp the auspicious moment; i.e. (when one's preparations are not completely ready) to seize the auspicious moment by making a formal beginning (and then waiting for things to be completely ready before going on). --wuchun -- m.inf. to ascertain, or wait for, the auspicious moment (for beginning any work). ¶ sāta karun m.inf. to act on the auspicious moment, to take advantage of a lucky moment, to begin a work at the auspicious moment; so with other verbs, such as sāta gaʦhun, to go (i.e. start) at the auspicious moment, and similarly with parun, to study; yunᵘ, to come; nyunᵘ, to take; bĕhun, to take up a residence, and so on. sāta sāta adv. moment by moment, at each and every moment (Rām. 574, 1169, 1365). ¶ sāthāh or sāthā m. a moment, a short space of time; as adv., for a short time, during a short time (Rām. 1079, 1172; H. ii, 4; vi, 3; vii, 9; YZ. 553). --gaʦhith --, adv. a short time having elapsed, after a short time (Rām. 928). ¶ sötiy adv. at a particular time, at (the) very moment (L.V. 25).

card. (pl. dat. satan), seven (Gr.Gr. 76, 83; L.V. 59, 82; Śiv. 437, 535, 836, 1149, 1654; Rām. 479, 740, 924, 956, 1248, 1387, 1467; K. 328, 720-1, 723, 725; H. iii, 8; v, 8; vi, 3, 15; x, 2, 5, 12; xii, 9; YZ. 190). ¶ According to Hindūs, there are seven worlds (Skt. lōka), viz. the earth (bhūr-lōka), sky (bhuvar-lōka), heaven (svar-lōka), middle region (mahar-lōka), place of births (janar-lōka), mansion of the blest (tapar-lōka), and abode of truth (satya-lōka). There are seven lower regions, or hells, viz. (Skt.) Atala, Vitala, Sutala, Rasātala, Talâtala, Mahātala, and Pātāla.
