In Śaiva philosophy there are seven (Skt.) jñāna-bhūmi, or planes of knowledge; viz. śubhêcchā, or the plane of auspicious desire (for knowledge); vicāraṇā, the plane of consideration; tanu-mānasa, the plane of the subtile mind; sattvâpatti, the plane of acquirement of good sense; samsakti, the plane of intimate acquaintance; padârtha-bhāvinī, the plane of possession of the (true) meanings of words; and, seventhly, turya-gā, that which conducts to the turya state, or condition leading to final emancipation (cf. L.V. p. 207). ¶ sath hath card. seven hundred (Gr.Gr. 80), the ordinal of this word is satahatyumᵘ, bel. ¶ sata-dôñᵘ adj. (f. -döñᵘ̈), containing or consisting of seven kinds of paddy (see dāñĕ 1); (of an ornament or the like) weighing seven döñᵘ̈ or seven times six seeds of the Abrus precatorius (see döñᵘ̈); used like our 'carat' to express the fineness of gold. Sixteen döñᵘ̈ equal one tōlā or half an ounce. In this use, therefore, sata-dôñᵘ means '(gold) of which seven parts (are pure and nine (i.e. 16-7) parts are alloy)'. -dôrᵘ adj. (f. -dörᵘ̈), (of a house, etc.) possessing seven windows or casements (on each story) (see dörᵘ̈ 3); made of, or associated with, seven kinds of timber (see dār 2); connected with, resting upon, etc., seven beams or pillars (see dār 2). -gorᵘ ã̄gun m. (sg. dat. -garis ã̄ganas), a courtyard (into which each opens) surrounded by seven houses (each with its own family); met. such a courtyard surrounded by many such houses. -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), costing seven hundred (rupees or the like); receiving wages of seven hundred (rupees or the like). -hatyumᵘ ord. (f. -hatimᵘ̈), seven hundredth; cf. sath hath, ab. -hatyunᵘ adj. (f. -hatiñᵘ̈), i.q. sata-hotᵘ, ab. -kŏluyᵘ m. a man who has had seven wives (one after the other). -köshⁱlad adj. c.g. (as subst. f. -köshⁱladiñ), one who has fasted for seven days (e.g. owing to illness, or from poverty). -koturᵘ m. (f. -kütürᵘ̈), one who has seven sons (esp. sons of superior merit); one who has seven children (sons or daughters or both). -monᵘ adj. (f. -müñᵘ̈), weighing seven man of three pounds each (see man 3); a stone or other article used as a weight for weighing this amount. -môsᵘ adj. (f. -mösᵘ̈), seven months old, lasting seven months, known for seven months and so on (see mās 1); (a child) who has seven maternal aunts (see mās 3). -pholᵘ adj. (a field or the like) bearing seven different kinds of crops, (a dish or the like) containing seven different kinds of grain, (a necklace or the like) consisting of seven jewels, (a work) producing seven different results, and so on. -rĕshⁱ m.pl. the seven sages (in Skt. Marīci, Angiras, Atri, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Vasiṣṭha) (Śiv. 77, 638, 675, 686, 1149, 1457; K. 1038); the constellation Ursa Major (see p. 855b, l. 14). -ryotᵘ adj. (f. -rë̆ʦᵘ̈), seven months old, seven months after birth; a seven-months' child. -sŏnal f. a woman with six other co-wives (a term often used in abuse or cursing). -sôsᵘ adj. (f. -sösᵘ̈), a porridge made of mixture of seven kinds of grain (cf. sas). -sösyunᵘ adj. (f. sösiñᵘ̈), costing seven thousand, or earning seven thousand (rupees, etc.). -ṭopᵘ adj. (f.-ṭüpᵘ̈), having seven sources of profit, honour, help, or the like. -ṭāsal m. issuing seven roars or explosions (esp. with reference to a cannon or the like). -wuhorᵘ adj. (f. -wȧrishᵘ̈), of seven years, seven years old (Śiv. 578 (f.)). -wotᵘ m. approached by seven roads; having seven roads leading to seven places; (of a work) having seven devices, or having seven results. ¶ sati in sati nĕngi adv. seven times, on seven occasions (L.V. 50). ¶ satan-hondᵘ (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of seven, having wages of seven (rupees or the like); having seven relatives; a seven-months' child. ¶ sataway card. (pl. dat. satawanī or satawȧnⁱ), even the seven, all the seven (Gr.Gr. 85; Śiv. 835, 1149; K. 725). Cf. sȧtⁱ-sataway, s.v. sotᵘ. ¶ satay card. only seven (Gr.Gr. 83).
f. (sg. dat. söʦᵘ̈), the star Arcturus, considered as forming the fifteenth lunar asterism.

adj. c.g. (as subst., sg. dat. satas), good (L.V. 82); true, truthful (Śiv. 887; Rām. 1643, 1646); pure, virtuous (Rām. 1709, 1768); as subst. m. a good man, a virtuous man (L.V. 59); cf. sath 1. -gŏr m. a virtuous spiritual preceptor, i.q. sadgŏr, q.v. -pŏrush or sat-pŏrush m. (sg. dat. -pŏrashĕs), a virtuous, righteous, honourable, or pious man (Śiv. (sat-) 1045, 1338, 1404). --parbuth -- m. (sg. dat. --parbatas --), 'the true mountain', a name of the hill near Śrīnagar called 'Hāra-parbuth' (Śiv. 1136). -pọ̆thᵃr m. (sg. dat. -pŏtras), a good or virtuous son. -sang, see -satsang. -ʦĕth or saʦʦith m. (sg. dat. -ʦĕtas), he who is pure existence and spirit; a N. of the Supreme Deity (in Skt. saccit) (Śiv. 274, 982, 1110, 1344); cf. ʦĕth 1. -ʦĕth-ākāsh or (Śiv. 1124) saʦʦid ākāsh m. he who is pure existence, spirit, and the ether, a N. of the Supreme Deity (Śiv. 28, 252, 1124) (in Skt. saccidākāśa). -ʦĕth-ānand or saʦʦidānand m. he who is pure existence, spirit, and bliss, a N. of the Supreme Deity (in Skt. saccidānanda) (Śiv. (-ʦĕthᵒ), 180, 1767, 1882; (saʦʦᵒ) 273, 1045, 1098). -ʦĕth-ānanda-gan or (Śiv. 1403) saʦʦidānanda-gan m. a corruption of the Skt. sac-cid-ānanda-ghana, he who is composed of pure existence, spirit, and bliss, a N. of the Supreme Deity (Śiv. 1293, 1338, 1403). -zan m. (Śiv. 1206), i.q. sazzan, q.v.
m. hospitality, hospitable treatment (cf. ādar-sᵒ, p. 15a, l. 30); civility, graciousness (Gr.M.).

card. twenty-seven (Gr.Gr. 77, Śiv. 38, K. 1024). satôwuhan-hondᵘ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, twenty-seven; worth, or costing twenty-seven (rupees or the like); earning wages of twenty-seven (rupees or the like).
m. the good Sadā-shiv, a N. of Śiva (see sadā-shiv, p. 863b, l. 5) (Śiv. 518).
m. association with the virtuous (cf. samāgam) (Śiv. 1769).

or sattŏ m. a corruption of the Skt. sattva, the quality of goodness or purity, regarded as the highest of the three guṇas (see gŏn), in the compound satū-gŏn m. the quality of goodness (Śiv. 447, 797, 1271, 1342, 1419; Rām. 71; K. 320 (sattŏ)).
conj. 2 (1 p.p. sotᵘ, f. süʦᵘ̈), to hope (L.V. 104). Cf. sath 2.

or satatutᵘ m. a certain small bird, described as having a long beak and tail, reddish wings, and a cry like that of the kōil or Indian cuckoo (El. satatút, lapwing; K.Pr. 38 (a lapwing), 189 (a hoopoo)).

f. (of a person) good intelligence, intelligence gained from good experience, sagacity, good judgment; (of a thing) suitable quality; N. of the daughter of Nagnajit, king of Ayōdhyā, who married Krushna (Kṛṣṇa) (K. 716). satyā-nās m. destruction, ruin, total destruction, perdition, annihilation. satyā-nās gaʦhun m.inf. total destruction to occur, to be destroyed, ruined, etc. --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.intelligence, good behaviour, thoroughness, or the like, to decay or be ruined.

a Skt. word, the equivalent of sath 1, q.v. used in the following Skt. compounds:-- satya-bām  or satĕ-bāmā  f. 'having true lustre', N. of the daughter of Satrājit, and one of the wives of Krushna (Kṛṣṇa) (Skt. Satyabhāmā) (Śiv. 1437; K. 687-8, 690, 694, 772-3, 777, 935, 938). satya-bāv  m. truthfulness, satya- bāwa, adv. in truthfulness, truthfully. satya-dēv m. the god of truth, a title of Shiva (Śiva) (Śiv. 1403, 1628). satya-nārāyĕn m. a N. of Vishnu (Viṣṇu) (Śiv. 1403). satya-rṻph m. (sg. dat. -rṻpas), one who possesses the form of truth, one whose essence is truth, a title of Śiva (Śiv. 518). satya-wödī adj. c.g. a speaker of truth, truthful, sincere (Śiv. 518). satya-yŏg m. the first of the four yugas or ages of the world, the age of truth and purity, the golden age.
or ord. (f. satimᵘ̈), seventh (Gr.Gr. 76; Rām. 1154; K. 41, 132; H. v, 7; xii, 7).

(cf. سِتر) m. a veil, a covering; shame modesty, modest conduct; (in Ksh.) a place in which ladies of high position dwell secluded, a harem, seraglio; met. living in seclusion, taking up a hermit's life in a solitary place, retiring from the rest of the world. ¶ sạtᵃra-bāpār m. shyness, modest behaviour. -wājĕñ f. a woman who has taken to a solitary life, as ab. -wōrath f. (sg. dat. wōrüʦᵘ̈), a modesty-cover, a veil or other covering worn by a woman to hide her shame (e.g. a single garment worn by a woman living in poverty to hide her person). ¶ sạtᵃras bĕhun m.inf. (owing to shyness) to adopt a solitary life, to live in seclusion.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sạtᵃrôwᵃ), to make (land or the like) level, to level; to bring down a man or his fortune from prosperity. sạtᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. sạtᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), levelled, etc., as ab.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sạtᵒrᵒ 2), to level (ground or the like). sạtᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. sạt ᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of land) made level, levelled.
(for 2, see sạtᵃrun) adj. (f. sạtᵘ̈rᵘ̈), (of land or the like) level, flat, smooth (El. satur, suttur); (of a wooden beam or the like) easily split.
m.pl. multiplicative of sath 3, seven, see sotᵘ 2.

or sōdāgār m. a trader, a merchant (El. sódágar, saudágar; Gr.M. saudāgar; Śiv. 1809, sōdāgar; H. iii, 1, 3; v, 11; viii, 9, 10, sōdāgār; iii, 3, 4, sōdāgar; YZ. 112, saudāgār); (in Ksh. esp.) a fruit-seller.
or sōdāgörī f. trade (El. sodágarí, Gr.M. saudāgarī).
m. N. of a son of the Sun, his mother's name being in Skt. Savarṇā. He was the eighth of the fourteen Manus, the successive progenitors of sovereigns of the earth (Śiv. 854).

m. richness, abundance, prosperity, great property (cf. baba-sᵒ, p. 77a, l. 17; bata-sᵒ, p. 137b, l. 4; dana-sᵒ, p. 222a, l. 19; mǖ̃thri-sᵒ, p. 606a, l. 39; māyĕ-sᵒ, p. 612b, l. 47; phala-sᵒ, p. 692b, l. 8; pŏtra-sᵒ, p. 799b, l. 30). Cf. sāway.
m. that which has wide expansion, the total expanse of creation, the visible creation (L.V. 1).
f. N. of the wife of the god Brahmā (Śiv. 485, 1142).
f. the beam supporting the eaves of a house.

adj. with a quarter, increased by one-fourth, with one-fourth added (to it), a quarter more; cf. swād 2. --sēr -- m. a seer (two pounds) and a quarter; a kind of large cake offered to Ganēsh (Skt. Gaṇêśa) on the fourth lunar day of the bright half of the month Bādᵃrapĕth (in Skt. Bhādra-pada = August-September).
m. meed, compensation, requital, reward (esp. of obedience to God) (H. ix, 12); hence, a virtuous action (K.Pr. 14).

or sāvidān adj. c.g. (in Śiv. 23, 364, obl. sg. m. sāwadāna), attentive, (sāvi˚) 480, 1491, 1654; Rām. (sāwa˚) 736, 992; K. 1096, 1157); enraptured, full of joy, delighted (Śiv. (sāvi˚) 273, 308, 939, 1554).
m. a question, query, interrogation(Gr.M.); a petition, application (H. x, 5). sawāl ta jawāb m. question and answer, conversation (Gr.M.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sawôrᵘ), to prepare, construct; to undertake (a work) (Gr.M.); to arrange, regulate, rectify, correct, put in order. sawôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sawörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), arranged, regulated, rectified, corrected, put in order.

m. happiness, prosperity (resulting from wealth, health, peace of mind, or the like), plenty of the good things of this life (cf. baba-sᵒ, p. 77a, l. 20; bata-sᵒ, p. 137b, l. 6; dīshĕ-sᵒ, p. 253a, l. 23; hurⁱ-sⁱ, p. 347a, l. 19; lūka-sᵒ, p. 519a, l. 30; phala-sᵒ, p. 692a, l. 9; pŏtra-sᵒ, p. 799b, l. 32; rǖnⁱ-sⁱ, p. 835b, l. 37; sŏkh-sᵒ, p. 905b, l. 7) (Gr.Gr. 129); cf. sāvĕr. sāwayĕ-vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), endowed with prosperity, fully prosperous and happy.
(?) srōl, or (?) sīlein (El. sawálí f., srol m., sílein m.) the alder, Alnus (cf. balūt) (L. 79, sarul or kanzal, Alnus nitida).

f. that which is extra, that which is more than has been agreed upon or is usual (e.g. in paying a dowry, work, or the like); extra collections or cesses. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (in paying a dowry, or the like) to deal with more than the proper amount.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sôwᵘ), to put to sleep, lull to sleep, induce sleep (in another) (Gr.Gr. 23, 176, causal of shŏngun, q.v.; L. 464, sawun; W. 65; K.Pr. 57; Śiv. 352, 1445, 1478, 1627, 1709, 1825, 1883; Rām. 216, 1292, 1432; K. 118; K.Pr. 57, 64); cf. shŏnganāwun. sôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), put to sleep, lulled to sleep.

m. ratification (of contract, bargain, or the like), earnest money (El. sai, f.; Gr.M.). --thawun -- m.inf. to bind or fix the earnest money, to deposit the earnest money; met. after arousing desire, to offer hope of its achievement (K.Pr. 44, sai; 92, sái).
m. a sportsman, hunter, fowler, fisher (Rām. 1496). Cf. sayyād.

m. shade, shadow (cf. potᵘ-sāyĕ, p. 788a, l. 14) (El. sáyi f.; Śiv. 897, 1475, 1722); shelter, protection. -bāna (= سایہ بان) m. a canopy, the roof, or fly, of a tent (Śiv. 1146, 1733); a sunshade, umbrella, parasol. --karun --, m.inf. to rest in the shade (Śiv. 1813); to ward off rain, sunshine, etc. (by a roof, a cloth, or the like), to use an umbrella or sunshade. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), wanting in shade, shadeless; wanting protection.
m. game, prey, chase, an object of the chase (El. sayad, prey).
m. evening, sunset (El., K. 782). -kāl m. evening time, eventide.
m. a sportsman, hunter, fowler, fisher. Cf. sayād.
f. natron, impure carbonate of soda (used instead of soap for cleaning linen, etc.) (L. 78, L.V. 103, translated 'fuller's earth').

m. arms, accoutrements; apparatus, instrument, implement; decoration, adornment, toilet (esp. of a bride or bridegroom, or of a courtesan) (Śiv. 920, Rām. 1372, K.Pr. 153); trappings of a horse, (ornamental) harness, a horse's headgear; a certain gong-like musical instrument (Śiv. 107, 327, 450, 1609); (in weaving) the cross threads, the woof (El.). -bāz m. complete collection of all the apparatus and preparation (after due consultation and consideration) for any work. --wāyun -- m.inf. to sound the ab. instrument. ¶ sāza-gorᵘ  m. (f. -gürᵘ̈), a maker, seller, or applier of women's decoration, or of horses' trappings, as ab. (f.) a lady's maid, an attendant on a lady (Śiv. 1218). -sarūd m. a musical performance, concert.
adj. c.g. making, preparing, effecting (cf. söbun-sāz, p. 862b, l. 7; shākh-sāz, p. 876a, l. 50).

adj. worthy, deserving (cf. nā-sazā, p. 659b, l. 6); (as subst. m., sg. dat. sazāhas) punishment, penalty, retribution (Gr.M.; W. 11, 18). This word as subst. is f. in Hindōstānī (W. 18). Cf. sazāwal.
m. in a game something like our hopscotch, the disc (of potsherd or the like) which is propelled by the foot. saza-longᵘ m. the game referred to ab.

in saza-byôlᵘ m. a certain flower seed, a decoction of which is used as a remedy for constipation, dysentery, and other diseases. -mūl m. the root of this plant. -pōsh m. its flower, used internally as an antiphlogistic (L. 76).
adj. c.g. one who is fond of decorating or adorning (him or herself), a fop, dandy, fine lady, a woman fond of pranking herself out.
m. a player on musical instruments, a musician (El.).

m. a collector of revenue or rent, tax-gatherer, land-steward, bailiff; a superintendent, supervisor, overseer; (in Ksh.) an officer who supervises a number of shĕkh-dars (see p. 876b, l. 13), or guardians of the crops (L. 402, sazawol, which perhaps represents sazawôlᵘ, as a local corruption of sazāwal, by confusion with sazā, q.v.
f. the profession of playing the musical instrument called sāz (q.v.); meton. the profession of music, a livelihood as a musician.
(cf. سازش) f. confederacy, collusion, cabal, conspiracy.
adj. c.g. alive, living, restored to life. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become restored to life; met. (of one overwhelmed by terror, calamity, sorrow, or the like) to be consoled, comforted, reassured.
or (Śiv. 1206) sath-zan m. a good man, a virtuous man (Śiv. 20, 102, 307, 442, 588, 981, 1003, 1206, 1338, 1753, etc.).

or sasʦar m. the being accompanied by (anything), the being possessed of, the being endowed with (the opposite of raʦhar, q.v.) (cf. darma-sᵒ, p. 245a, l. 2; phala-sᵒ, p. 672b, l. 5; prayĕma-sᵒ, p. 774a, l. 45); endowments, possessions, wealth at the owner's own disposal. Cf. sostᵘ.

f. (sg. dat. së̆zᵘ̈), accomplishment, fulfilment, completion, success (cf. karma-sᵒ, p. 471b, l. 43) (K. 321, 1040); success, prosperity, welfare (cf. būta-sᵒ, p. 141b, l. 12) (Śiv. 1714, 1830); the outcome or result (of a charm or the like) (K. 878); a superhuman power or faculty (there are eight of these) (pl. së̆zᵘ̈) (in Skt. siddhi).

(also written siddh, sĕdd, and sidd) adj. c.g. accomplished, effected, performed, achieved (Śiv. 1220, 1239, 1335, 1470, 1835, (sidd) 153; K. 269, 718, 1010); proved, established (in a court of justice) (Gr.M.); succeeded, successful (Gr.M.; Śiv. 388, siddh); perfect, entire, complete (Śiv. 370, 432, 1263); perfected, sanctified (Śiv. 182, 669, 755, 1000); (as subst. m.) a man believed to be of great purity and holiness, and to be characterized by the possession of the eight siddhis (see sĕd 1) (L.V. 91, siddh; Śiv. 428, 434, 1337, 1591; (sĕd) 205, 819; (sidd) 597, 1152; Rām. 1491, 1681, 1684; K.Pr. 140, proper N.).

adj. c.g. facing, in front of (another); an exact match (to another), a pair (to another); (as adv.) straightly; hence, with straight mind, attentively, heedfully, carefully (L.V. 91); cf. syodᵘ. --sĕda -- adv. as an exact match, exactly matching; face to face (El.). --syodᵘ -- adj. (f. --së̆zᵘ̈ --), face to face (with another).
adj. c.g. three-handed. N. of a certain game (Rām. 1351).
f. (sg. dat. sĕdüʦᵘ̈), success, complete attainment (cf. ḍĕka-sᵒ, p. 204b, l. 24) (Gr.Gr. 128; Śiv. 730, 1092, 1632, 1708, 1718-19; Rām. 1510, 1598); the eight siddhis (see sĕd 1) (Śiv. 1494).
or siddi f. success, prosperity (Gr.M.). ¶ siddi-dātā m. a giver of prosperity (Śiv. 1).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. sĕdyōv), to be or become straight, direct, even (El., W. 113, sidun); to gain one's object, succeed, become successful (Gr.Gr. 128); success to be obtained; to be freed from disease, recover (from illness); (of an angry person, one excited, or the like) to recover one's temper, become normal, satisfied; to become trained, polite, well mannered. sĕdẏō-motᵘ (f. sidyē-müʦᵘ̈), become straight; become successful, and so on, as ab.
card. three (K.Pr. 176), a borrowed Persian form.
m. a tiger (El.). Cf. the next.

adj. c.g. well-fitting (of one thing to another); fitting, suitable, suiting, congruous. --karun -- m.inf. to make certain, to prove the truth (of a statement). --rōzun -- m.inf. to be fitting, to fit something; to maintain hope in the heart, to continue hopeful. --thawun -- m.inf. to give hope, to encourage.

f. (sg. dat. sĕki), sand (Gr.Gr. 147; Gr.M.; L. 463; L.V. 107; Śiv. 1733, 1755; K.Pr. 190); a file (Gr.M.). --tavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to roast sand', to cast burning sand upon a person; hence, met. to abuse violently, to vituperate. --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f. inf. to fling away (hot) sand; hence, met. to throw away, discard (a friend, relation, or some thing, owing to its becoming spoilt or acquiring a bad reputation), 'to drop like a hot potato'. ¶ sĕki-ambār m. a heap or pile of sand (as collected for some purpose). -bôbusᵘ m. 'a sand bomb', the gizzard of a fowl or similar bird. -boṭhᵘ m. the sandy bank of a river or the like. -büṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -bachĕ), (in a garden) the little sand-bank bounding the various water basins. -chȧmbⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. 'to fall over a precipice of sand'; hence, to fall immediately on standing on a weak or insecure position; to be destroyed immediately on being erected. -ḍāphar m. a wide level sandy piece of ground (even if cultivable). -kroʦhᵘ ʦhunun m.inf. 'to wield the sand-shovel'; hence, to abuse and throw away. -shrāṭh or -shāṭh m. (sg. dat. -sh(r)āṭhas ), a sand-bank (in a river) (Gr.M. -shāṭh; Śiv. 1585). --sāban gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'soap to come from sand', i.e. after much labour and expenditure of time and money, the results to turn out to be futile. -wôñᵘ m. sandy water, water full of sand.
adj. c.g. sandy; N. of class of soil, a light loam with sandy subsoil (L. 319).
adj. (f.sĕkijᵘ̈), sandy, full of sand, covered with sand, made of sand (Gr.Gr. 147); (of a fruit or other edible) gritty.
in sēlā-kônᵘ m. N. of a certain game, on the lines of our backgammon, in which the movements of the men on the board are determined by throwing numbered dice.
f. an artificial precious stone made of glass, an imitation diamond or the like (Śiv. 1310); a necklace of such imitation stones. sēlāñĕ-pholᵘ m. a single imitation stone, as ab.

f. bottom, root, foundation (e.g. of a lake, of a family, or of a story). --galüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the foundation to be destroyed, (of a family, kingdom, or the like) to be destroyed root and branch. --gālüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to destroy the foundation, to destroy utterly (e.g. one king to destroy another in war). --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to tear up the foundation, to destroy an enemy's entire family; to abuse a person and his whole family and ancestors.
adv. and prep. in the middle. Noted only in the phrase sĕmanz sŏthi, in the middle of the bridge or embankment, i.e. half-way across (L.V. 98 (= K.Pr. 18), Śiv. 371).
or sĕmbĕr the quality of being sediment, miriness, muddiness, slushiness; (of wine or the like) the possession of slight intoxicating power. Cf. syomᵘ or syombᵘ.

f. (sg. dat. sĕndi), a river (Rām. 1307, 1590); a perpetual water-fall; N. of a river of Kashmīr (El. sind, RT. Tr. II, 418, Sindhu; Śiv. 1561, 1589, 1682, 1793, 1840, 1889). ¶ sĕnda-wôñᵘ m. the water of the Sĕnd river (El. sindawáiṅ). sĕnda-wār m. an army encampment.
conj. 1. (1. p.p. sẹ̆ndᵃrôwᵃ), to cause something to turn red; to cause to go bad, cause to decay.
m. redness; hence, rustiness; burnt red, spoilt.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. sẹ̆ndᵃryōv), to change to a red (vermilion) colour, to go rusty; (of something soft), to go bad.
f. (sg. dat. sẹ̆ndᵃrĕ), red lead, minium, vermilion, rouge (Rām. 1104); met. fine dust generally, ashes (K.Pr. 253, sindar). sẹ̆ndᵃrĕ-gorᵃ m. a maker, or seller, of vermilion.

m. want of the flavour of salt (in food), insipidity; (of an action or thing) absence of pleasingness, unpalatableness, unattractiveness, want of special points (cf. atha-sᵒ, p. 62b, l. 15); weakness, slackness (in work) (of one hitherto industrious, or, approaching success, who has given up his efforts), a feeling of discouragement; cf. syonᵘ. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. (of some action or thing hitherto attractive or admired) unattractiveness to occur, to become unattractive or unwanted. --karun -- m.inf. to cause (something attractive, etc.) to become unattractive, etc.

trading, trafficking (across the sea with foreign countries); met. the getting of something rare or unobtainable. --zēnun m.inf. to conquer such trafficking, to make great profit by such trafficking; to obtain something rare and long desired.

or sĕnnun conj. 3 (2 p.p. sĕnyōv or sĕnnyōv), (food) to become soft and tender (by cooking); to become enfeebled by excessive heat or perspiration; (of a hard-hearted man) to be rendered tender hearted (by adversity, sorrow, or the like); cf. syonᵘ. sĕnyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sĕnyē-müʦᵘ̈), become soft, as ab.; become tender hearted, as ab.
f. (sg. dat. sẹ̆ñᵉ̆rüñᵉ̆), making insipid; disencouraging, discouragement.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sẹ̆ñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), i.q. sẹ̆ñᵉ̆run, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 8).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sẹ̆ñᵒrᵒ), to melt, soften (e.g. food by cooking or by the application of water); to discourage.
m. nasty-tastingness, the having a repulsive taste, the being bad-flavoured and evil smelling, nauseousness. Cf. syopᵘ.
f. (sg. dat. sĕpi), chalk (cf. dara-sᵒ, p. 249a, l. 17; phŏka-sᵒ, p. 688b, l. 24).
(El.) m. Populus fastigiata (El. sefeda). Cf. saphēdār.
m. laziness, sloth, dilatoriness. Cf. syopᵘ.

m. a weight of about two pounds, a seer (cf. man 3 and manoṭᵘ) (Gr.Gr. 21, 147; YZ. 404); a weight of a seer for weighing; anything weighing a seer (cf. phal-sēr 1, p. 692a, l. 10) (W. 135; Śiv. 1862; K.Pr. 225, 256). sēra-wād adj. c.g. weighable by seers, suitable for being weighed seer by seer.

f. bleeding at the nose (cf. nas-sēr, p. 654b, l. 7); cf. H. naksīr, a vein in the nose, bleeding at the nose, and sirā, a vein. --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause blood to flow, to bleed, phlebotomize (not necessarily from the nose). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. bleeding from the nose to come on; bleeding to come on from any other orifice of the body.

adj. c.g. full, satiated, sated (with nishĕ) (cf. phal-sēr 2, p. 692a, l. 11 and phala- sēr, id., l. 48) (Gr.M. sīr, K.Pr. 256); satisfied, contented (H. i, 3). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. satisfaction or contentment to occur, to be or become satisfied (W. 135; Śiv. 1240; Rām. 174, 365). --karun -- m.inf. to satisfy, make content, console (Śiv. 1862). --sapadun -- m.inf. to become content (Rām. 1561 (--sö̃panun), 1705 (--sapanun)).
m. a veil; (in Ksh.) a fringe (El.).

f. a sore in leprosy; a white spot, blotch, mark of skin disease, scab, wart (cf. mal-sĕs, p. 564a, l. 22) (El. a tumour, a wart; Gr.Gr. 134, a wart); a hard round scabby knot on a tree-trunk or the like. sĕsa-bombur m. (sg. dat. bomburas), a creeping line of scabs.
or (Gr.Gr. 135) sĕsalad adj. c.g. one who suffers from scabs (cf. mal-sĕsal, p. 564a, l. 25); warted (Gr.Gr. 134-5); (of a tree) scabby. See sĕs.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. sētaladiñ), an epileptic; met. a worrying naughty child. Cf. sīʦᵘ̈lad and sēth.
m. a kind of three-stringed guitar, a lute (Śiv. 392, 408, 412, 669, 1336, 1580, 1612; K.Pr. 132, sitāra).
f. indigestion (caused by eating indigestible or too much food). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an attack of indigestion to come on. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf., id.

f. (sg. dat. sīʦᵘ̈), epilepsy, a fit of epilepsy (Gr.Gr. 21); (esp. of children), causing annoyance or trouble (like an epileptic) by doing what is wrong, prohibited, or destructive. --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause worry or annoyance by doing forbidden actions, interfering, hindering, or the like. --dᵃnüñᵃ -- f.inf. to practise forbidden or wrong methods or conduct (causing useless labour, waste of time, spoiling of efforts or things, and so on). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an attack of epilepsy to come on; great labour or exertions to be made, but all in vain. ¶ sēta-kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), an epileptic boy; a boy who (like an epileptic) habitually does what he should not. ¶ sīʦᵘ̈-rostᵘ̈ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without trouble, not difficult, easy.

or siṭhāh (sometimes written sĕṭhā) adj. c.g. (pl. dat. sĕṭhāhan, Gr.M., Śiv. 420-1), abundant, copious, much, plentiful (Gr.Gr. 187; Gr.M.; Śiv. 429-30, 706, 755, 795, 912; Rām. 69, 71, 317, 421, etc.; H. viii, 4); numerous, manifold, many (cf. oshᵘ sĕṭhāh pakān, p. 47b, l. 20) (Gr.Gr. 154; Śiv. 328, 1764; Rām. 118, 304, etc.; K. 565; YZ. 267); ¶ as adv. very, extremely, much, abundantly (Gr.M.; W. 96, setha; Śiv. 431, 436, 470, 475, 537, 633, 656, 691, 708, etc.; Rām. 52, 54, 75, 80, 104, 116, 153, etc.; H. viii, 1, 9, 11, 12, 14; xii, 4, 5, 9, 10, 12, 15; YZ. 84). --āsun -- m.inf. to abound (Śiv. 428, 433, 437). ¶ sĕṭhāhi ranga adv. in many ways (Gr.Gr. 154).
m. (sg. dat. sĕtharas), a kind of mud plaster (mixed with chaff).
m. (sg. dat. sētanas), conduct which worries and annoys others (used esp. of the conduct of a naughty child). Cf. sēth.
f. a collection, or bunch, of maggots. --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a bunch of maggots to appear (in food or the like becoming corrupt).
or sĕyĕlad adj. c.g. full of, or infested by, groups of maggots.

m. straightness, directness (cf. atha-sᵒ, p. 63a, l. 1) (K.Pr. 24); straightforwardness, uprightness, honesty, sincerity (Śiv. 1829); simplicity, humility. --bōzun -- m.inf. to inspect straightness; to test the straightness (of something); to act on trust of (another's) honesty, to act confidingly. --pazar -- m. (sg. dat. sĕzaras pazaras), thorough honesty, probity, rectitude (Gr.M., Śiv. 1754).
f. (sg. dat. sẹ̆zᵃrüñᵃ), straightening, making straight (Gr.Gr. 121); making a crooked character straight, reforming (a person); aiming straight (at a mark).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sẹ̆zᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. sẹ̆zᵃrun, q.v. sẹ̆zᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. sẹ̆zᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), straightened; reformed, brought to a straight line of conduct; aimed straight at a mark, as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sẹ̆zᵒrᵒ), to make straight, to straighten (cf. dara sᵒ, p. 236a, l. 27) (Gr.Gr. 8, 21); to lead into straight habits, to reform (a person of crooked, i.e. evil, character); to aim something straight at a mark (lit. and fig.) (cf. tīr sᵒ, s.v. tīr 2) (Rām. 999).
interj. indicating great respect, and used only to a superior, i.q. shāh 1, q.v. (Śiv. 329, 599; Rām. 1396).
interj. well done! bravo! (El.; Gr.M.; W. 101, also shāhbāsh); Śiv. 656 (shābash, m.c.), 657 (shābāsh); Rām. 1338, 1647; K.Pr. 191, 196).

m. pleased, delighted, joyful, merry (El.; Śiv. 510; Rām. 69, 706, 792, 1303; K. Pr. 196). shād-u-gamgīn شاد و غمگین joyful and (i.e. or) sorrowful (Rām. 24). shād-mȧrgⁱ gaʦhun (cf. شادی مرگ) to die of joy; (in Ksh.) to faint or become insensible through excess of joy.
see shĕphakh. shifākhāna شفاخانہ, see shĕphākhāna. shafkat شفقت, see shĕphkath.

m. a king, prince, monarch (cf. baḍshāh, p. 81b, l. 35; dubari-shāh, p. 184b, l. 5) (El. shah; Śiv. 1230; Rām. 508; H. i, 1; vi, 1; K.Pr. 68, 173, 191); the king (at chess or cards) (Rām. 1314, shāh-rukh, the king and the castle); used as an interj. indicating respect (in this meaning often spelt shā, q.v.) (W. 100-1). In Ksh. more often shĕh 1, q.v. -bāsh شاہ باش interj. i.q. shābāsh, q.v. -gura m. 'King Tawny', a kind of rice with a plump white grain in a soft skin. -zāda شاہ زادہ or shĕh-zāda شہزادہ m. a king's son, a prince (El. shahzádah; Gr.M.; Śiv. (shāh˚) 964, 1836; H. (shāh˚) viii, 5, 11, 13; YZ. 262; K.Pr. 208); met. a spoilt darling son (cf. mŏnḍa-shᵒ, p. 574a, l. 45).

m. breath, the breath of life (El. shah; Gr.Gr. 162; Gr.M.); respiration (Śiv. 1211, 1827); cf. shöshⁱ, a fem. form, and shwās. --band gaʦhun -- m.inf. the breath to become bound, breathlessness to occur (to a person, dat.) (Gr.M.). --dạrᵃrun -- m. to train the breath by practice of suppression (a Yōga exercise). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to breathe (El.). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to draw breath (El.). --khārun -- m.inf. to breathe up or out, to perform expiration, as opposed to inspiration (El. to breathe) (Śiv. 1753). The opposite is --wālun --, to breathe down, or in (Śiv. 1753). --khasun -- m.inf. the breath to rise, i.e. the breath to come to the mouth, to be at the point of death. --ṭhīkun -- m.inf. the breath to stand firmly (e.g. of a healthy baby), (of a sick person) to become convalescent. ¶ shāha-khāray f. breathing out, expiration (esp. after stoppage of breath). -lᵃth f. (sg. dat. -lᵃti), a trace of breath, a mere flicker of breath (e.g. at the point of death) (Gr.Gr. 162). -phyurᵘ m. return of breath, return to life (of one at the point of death, or of one in a faint). -phyurᵘ gaʦhun m.inf. return of breath to occur, revival to take place (e.g. of one at the point of death, or in a faint, or paralyzed by fear, grief, or the like); to revive, to be consoled, confidence to be inspired (of someone sunk in despair or the like). -phyurᵘ karun m.inf. to revive (a person); to console, revive, inspire with confidence (someone overwhelmed by despair or the like).
in chapan-shāī (p. 164a, l. 20), i.q. shāy q.v.
m. a rock, a big stone (Śiv. 749 shailāh, with suff. of indef. art.); a mountain. shailā-ʦakr m. 'the circle of rocks', a N. of Hāra-parbuth, see p. 344a, l. 44 (Śiv. 108).
adj. c.g. divided into (so many) parts, sections, compartments, or the like; used --˚ as in trᵃ-shākal, made up of three parts; ʦu-shākal, made up of four parts, and so on.

m. (sg. dat. shākhas) a bough, a branch (H. vii, 10); a shoot, sprout (Rām. 1197); a dilemma, difficulty, objection, obstacle. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to raise a difficulty, to raise an objection, to carp, cavil (at); (in Ksh.) to discuss the good and bad points (of), to criticize (a person or thing, esp. when he or it is absent, and his qualities have been forgotten; e.g. a discussion about some absent person's real caste). --nērȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. young sprouts to make their appearance; after criticism, a person's or thing's true character to be established, as ab. -shumörī شاخ شمآری f. a tax on buffaloes giving milk (L. 360 shákh shumári). -sāz شاخ ساز m. a basket maker (L. 458 sháksaz). ¶ shākha-shĕmshād ساخہ شمشاد a beautiful limb (of a mistress) (slender as) a tree branch (Rām. 1494).

f. (sg. dat. shākhi), a branch (issuing from the main stem of a tree, or the like), a bough, a shoot, sprout, twig; a branch of a family, tribe, or the like; a branch issuing from a river or the like; a section of a country, town, or the like.
f. a branch; a branch in a family tree; (according to El.) a lock of hair on the top of a Hindū's head (? a mistake for shikhā, q.v.).
(? spelling) m. the European cuckoo, Cuculus canorus (L. 138, 459). Cf. kukyulᵘ.

m. (f. shöjⁱ or shöjᵘ̈ 1, q.v. For shöjᵘ̈ 2, see shôlᵘ 2) a jackal (cf. baḍa- shᵒ, p. 82b, l. 28; mŏnga-shᵒ, p. 578b, l. 13) (El.; Gr.M.; L. 110; W. 3, 17; Śiv. 1758, 1797; Rām. 94, 1108d, 1191, 1306, 1630; K. 661; K.Pr. 83, 119, 172, 192, 248). --gübᵘ̈ hāka-ʦar sȧmⁱ -- m.pl. the jackal, the ewe, the bundle of greens (are all) equal, i.e. a realm in which all warring objects are at peace, a well-managed kingdom. --ʦalith baṭhĕn lōrĕ -- f.pl. sticks on the bank after the jackal has run away, i.e. trying to drive him out of his hole, when he is no longer there; met. (while waiting for some much desired result), to neglect the right moment for action, to let opportunity slip through the fingers, quasi, to lock the stable door after the steed is stolen. ¶ shāla-hĕng m. the horn of a jackal (according to tradition, when a jackal utters a cry a horn appears on its forehead, and, when the cry ceases, disappears. If anyone can catch hold of this horn, he will secure longed-for great wealth); met. something which is very rarely seen, and which it is almost impossible to obtain. -hār f. 'a jackal's cowry', a kind of small shell found on the hills. -hôrᵘ adj. (f. -hörᵘ̈), 'jackal-brindled', speckle-patterned. -khalish f. jackal-anxiety; met. disrespect, dishonour, despising (due to loss of honour, ruining of some work, public abuse, or the like). -kāth m. (sg. dat. -kātas) Myricaria Germanica (El. shálakát). -kyowᵘ m. a certain kind of rice-plant, with a fat, ruddy, plenteous grain (see kyowᵘ). -mār f., see s.v. shālamār. -pörᵘ̈ f. a jackal's hole, a jackal's den. -thŏkh f. (sg. dat. -thŏki), 'jackal's spittle', clots of foam carried down the rivers in flood time, and believed to come from the hills. -ṭᵃkh f. (sg. dat. -ṭᵃki), 'jackal's running', very quick running by a man; met. a short cut (in a route), an up and down and difficult road, but quicker for arriving at one's destination. -wung m. a jackal's single howl. -wungun m. (sg. dat. -wunganas), jackal's howling. -zag m. a kind of rice-plant with a plump, sweet, ruddy grain (cf. zag 1). -zạgᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or -zügᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or -zạgᵃr f. a kind of rice-plant with a small long-shaped well-flavoured grain.
m. a shawl (cf. jōri-shᵒ, p. 377b, l. 8) (Śiv. 281, 1687).
f. a kind of warm shawl woven from pashmīna wool.

f. (sg. dat. shālamörᵘ̈, Śiv. 1821) N. of a famous royal palace and garden on the shores of the lake near Śrīnagar (El. shálimár; RT.Tr. II, 456; Śiv. 972, 1363, 1797, 1821). shālamörᵘ̈-hondᵘ̈ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, this garden.
f. unhusked rice, or rice growing in the fields (the word is borrowed from Hindī) (L. 245, 272, 402).
(? spelling and gend.) a certain kind of hardy rice, growing at a high elevation (L. 463). ? cf. shālī.
(? spelling) m. a shawl-weaver (L. 463, 464). Cf. shāla and shālbāf.
adj. (f. shāliñᵘ̈), beautiful, handsome, pleasing (of a person, conduct, or act); (subst. m.) N. of a village about ten miles south of Śrīnagar.

m. N. of a disease of cattle (cows, horses, or other domestic animals) (marked by intumescence and poisonous boils on the lips, throat, flanks, and other fleshy parts of the body). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. this disease to attack an animal.

(sometimes writtenshyām) m. (for gend. see W. 18) evening (cf. sari shām, sari-shāma, s.v. sar 2) (Gr.Gr. 157; Gr.M.; W. 18; Śiv. 275, 1113, 1722; (shyām) 332; Rām. 185, 1023, 1145; YZ. 127); subaha tā shām, from morn till eve (Rām. 259). In Hindōstānī this word is f. --tāñ -- adv. till evening, up to evening. Cf. shāmas tāmath, bel. ¶ shāma-gürᵘ̈ f. evening time. -gaṭa f. evening darkness, the shades of evening. -laṭi adv. at eventide, in the evening (Rām. 217). --pȧtⁱ -- adv. after evening (El. sháma pata). --shām -- adv. even on the (coming) evening, i.e. by this very evening, not beyond this very evening; hence, very quickly, immediately, before the evening, not kept over for the next day. -ʦạturᵘ adj. (f. -ʦạtᵘ̈rᵘ̈), clever at evening; (after working slackly all day) to display smartness and cleverness when it is nearing time to stop. -ʦạtᵃrĕr m. the display of such smartness. -vil f. evening time (used in phrases indicating immediateness and the like, cf. shāma shām, ab.). ¶ shāmukᵘ adj. gen. (f. shāmücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the evening (cf. sari- shᵒ, s.v. sar 2). ¶ shāman adv. in the evening (cf. sari- shāman, s.v. sar 2) (Gr.Gr. 157, Rām. 119). -bögⁱ adv. at about evening, at eventide (H. v, 5). ¶ shāmas adv. at evening (cf. az shāmas, p. 74a, l. 25; sari shāmas, s.v. sar 2) (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. (shyāmas) 1009, 1439, 1465, 1662; Rām. 1085). --bögⁱ -- or --bögin -- adv. at about evening, at, or about, evening. --tāmath -- adv. up to evening, by evening. Cf. shām-tāñ, ab.

adj. c.g. black, dark blue, dark brown, swarthy, nut-brown (cf. shômᵘ and shyām). Used in the following:-- shāma-rȧngⁱ adj. c.g. of a dark complexion or colour, brown, nut-brown; cf. shāmi-rȧnga, s.v. shômᵘ.
m. (sg. dat. shāmatas), a spot, blemish (El.).
m. swarthiness, sunburntness, a nut-brown complexion.

m. state, condition, case; quality, property, disposition; degree, importance; rank, dignity, state, grandeur, glory, pomp (cf. kŏ-shānukᵘ, p. 481b, l. 1). -boḍᵘ adj. (f. büḍᵘ̈), handsome, liberal, noble, generous, large-hearted. --dārun -- m.inf. to give assurance, inspire confidence, to reassure, to encourage, show large-heartedness, liberality, or the like. --kaḍun -- m.inf. 'to extract grandeur', to become exalted, attain dignity, rise in prosperity. -- m. pl. inf. to rejoice at the spectacle of another's virtues, prosperity, or grandeur.

or (K.Pr. 24) shānda m. the shoulder-blade (K.Pr. 24, shānda); (in Ksh.) the part of the back between the shoulder-blades, (El.) the shoulder (Rām. 237, 485, 1122, 1237); a comb. -horᵘ m. the two shoulder-blades (shāna-horᵘ kaḍun, to broaden out the shoulder-blades, e.g. due to happiness, freedom from care; so shāna-horᵘ muʦarāwun, to split open the shoulder-blades, e.g. due to opposition, or the like). --karun -- m.inf. to comb (the hair, dat.) (YZ. 164). -muran lagüñᵘ̈ f.inf. itching or tickling of the shoulder-blades, due to a beating, to be experienced, to feel as if one had such an experience; met. to suffer from another's evil conduct.

m. a pillow, a bed- cushion for the head (cf. akiy-shᵒ, p. 20b, l. 12; khōra-shᵒ, pp. 409b, l. 29 and 410b, l. 10) (El., Gr.Gr. 10, K.Pr. 43); the head-end of a bed (H. v, 5). --dith bĕhun -- m.inf. to sit (with the back) supported by a pillow; to put something under a pillow and sit, hence met. quietly to appropriate another's property (of which one has obtained possession, e.g. as a trust, or dishonestly). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to lay one's head on a pillow; to put (something) under a pillow (H. x, 7). --lagun -- m.inf. a pillow to be applied (to the head); to become a pillow, hence met. to become dependent, subservient. ¶ shānda-gonḍᵘ m. a pillow, a cushion (El.). -kürᵘ̈ f. a present of clothes and the like sent to a bride after the marriage. -sār f. a mosquito-curtain (Gr.M.). ¶ shöndⁱ lagun m.inf. to offer oneself as a sacrifice (e.g. to stop an epidemic).

f. (sg. dat. shānti, Śiv. 1012, 1017, etc.), pacification, calmness, tranquillity, ease, rest, repose (cf. gar-shᵒ, p. 296a, l. 13) (Śiv. 979, 1012, 1017, 1481, 1751, 1797, 1821, 1848; K. 435); an expiatory rite, a propitiatory rite for averting or stopping a calamity (such as an epidemic) (K. 316-17, 319). ¶ shöntⁱ-gôwⁱ m. (f. -gövᵘ̈), of a tranquil nature, free from passion; generous by nature; (fem. shöntⁱ-gövⁱ) a quiet cow, a cow that does not give milk (K.Pr. 126).

adj. c.g. allayed, calmed, pacified, calm, quiet, undisturbed, tranquil (of a person, animal, bird, river, the sky, or the like) (Śiv 1742; Rām. 1448, 1501). ¶ shānta-shĕmunᵘ adj. (f. -shĕmüñᵘ̈), one who dishonestly pretends quietude, etc.

conj. 4 (2 p.p. shāntyōv), to become appeased, allayed (e.g. fever or the like); to be extinguished of a fire (cf. nār shᵒ, p. 647a, l. 17); to come to an end, be destroyed, (of a man) to be at the point of death, to die (El. sháṅtun, death). shāntyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shāntyē-müʦᵘ̈), become appeased, allayed, become extinguished; at the point of death.
m. a tranquil nature, calmness, gentleness.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. shāpaladiñ), suffering under a curse.

m. (sg. dat. shāpas), a curse, an imprecation, anathema (cf. ali-ti-shāph, p. 23a, l. 1; potᵘ-shᵘ, p. 787b, l. 49; pĕtᵃra-shᵃ, p. 802b, l. 50) (Śiv. 257, 415, 1162, 1171, 1889; Rām. 53, 215, 239, 275, 312, 724, 1321; K. 172, 174, 346, 1091-2, 1100, 1103); a curse (placed by oneself on oneself, dat.), a vow (to do such and such) (Rām. 160, 169). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to direct a curse (against someone), to curse (a person) (Śiv. 593; Rām. 473, 1697; K. 137, 347); to utter an evil spell (on a person), to utter a charm (Rām. 436; H. xii, 15). --lagun -- m.inf. a curse to be applied (to a person), to become the object of a curse, to be cursed. --tulun -- m.inf. to raise a spell, to take a spell off (a person), to relieve (him) from a spell (H. xii, 15). ¶ shāpa-hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), afflicted by a curse, labouring under a curse, suffering from the effects of a curse. -kömᵘ̈ f. a work which is subject to a curse, a work which is under a curse (and therefore cannot succeed); work which meets with all kinds of impediments, and which cannot be accomplished (as though it were under a curse). -kār m. any good or auspicious work (e.g. a festival) which suffers throughout from misfortunes and impediments (as though it were) under a curse. -karm m. a fate or lot in life which is under a curse, or which is unsuccessful as though under a curse. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), free from curse, i.e. not spoiled by misfortunes or impediments, going on prosperously. -shurᵘ m. a curse- child, i.e. a thin, unhealthy, badly-behaved child (as though the result of a curse put upon the father). ¶ shöpⁱ lagun m.inf. to become (subject) to a curse; i.e. (of a virtuous person) to be, or become, under the authority of an evil master (as though cursed to undergo this fate). ¶ shāpas nẹ̆ndᵃr pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. sleep to fall on a curse, in the course of a work subject to many impediments, all obstacles to clear themselves away (quasi, the curse has gone to sleep); cf. shŏngith shāph rōzun, p. 885b, l. 29. -nishĕ adv. owing to a curse (Rām. 29).
m. poetry, verse; a verse, couplet; a poem (Gr.M.); (in Ksh. esp.) a narrative poem celebrating some person, country, or the like (H. xi, title). --gandȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to compose such a poem.
m. N. of a well-known village about twenty miles to the S.E. of Śrīnagar.
m. a fall of water (as in āb-shār, a waterfall) (Śiv. 1797).

f. a N. of Sarasvatī, the goddess of speech and learning. Under this name (Skt. Śāradā) she is the patron goddess of Kashmīr. Her chief shrine, also called Shāradā, Shāradā-pīṭha, Shāradā-sthāna, and similar names, is situated in the Kishangangā Valley. The name Shāradā is also applied to the country of Kashmīr itself. On the whole subject, see RT.Tr. II, 279 ff. N. of the written character allied to Nāgarī, in general use in Kashmīr. -pīṭh m. (sg. dat. -pīṭhas), 'the throne of Shāradā', the shrine of Shāradā in the Kishangangā Valley; the country of Kashmīr. ¶ shārạda-bal m. the shrine of Shāradā.
m. highness of rank, eminence, exaltation, rank, honour, dignity (K.Pr. 143, with suff. of indef. art., sharafá).
f. i.q. hörī 2, q.v. (Śiv. 1136, 1179, 1506). The word is also used to indicate the Hāra-parbuth. See hörī 2.
f. in the following (cf. shāsᵃth):--shās gaʦhünᵘ̈ f.inf. dejection, pain, sorrow, distress to occur. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause sorrow, distress, dejection.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shôshᵘ), to breathe (Gr.Gr. lxxvi); esp. to breathe with difficulty, to pant, gasp.

or shösᵃtᵃr m. (sg. dat. shāstras), Hindū holy writ, a religious or philosophic treatise (cf. darma-shᵒ, p. 244b, l. 49; shiwa-shᵒ, p. 902a, l. 5) (Śiv. 49, 50); a sacred volume, a book dealing with such subjects (L.V. 27; Śiv. 159, 248, 758, 1117).
f. (sg. dat. shāsᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), great grief, affliction, sorrow, distress. Cf. shās.

or (Śiv. 1585) shrāṭh m. (sg. dat. sh(r)āṭhas ), a sand-bank (in a river) (cf. sĕki-shrāṭh, s.v. sĕkh) (El. sháṭ, shráṭ), falls (of a river); Gr.M. shāṭh; L.V. 84-5, id.; Śiv. 1585 (shrāṭh), 1805 (shāṭh); YZ. 34; K.Pr. 68, 190); a ford (Gr.M.); stony, sandy soil (L. 321, sháth). ¶ shāṭha lagun m.inf. (of a boat) to strike on a sand-bank, to run aground (Rām. 1202 (causal), 1334).
f. a deceitful ill-conducted woman, outwardly well-conducted.
f. a general report, rumour. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a rumour to become spread. --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to spread a general rumour, to convey a rumour.

or shĕy 1 (also written shāī) (= جای) f. (with suff. of indef. art. shāyā or shāyāh), a place, esp. a place of resort, or to which one can resort (e.g. a place of refuge, a temple, or a meeting place) (cf. chapan-shᵒ, p. 164a, l. 20; jāy-shᵒ, p. 380a, l. 5; mā̃ṭa-shᵒ, p. 604a, l. 21; prath shāyĕ, p. 769a, l. 36) (El. shâí, a place; Gr.Gr. 136; Śiv. (shāy) 242, 271, 889, 1238, 1332, 1619; (shĕy) 517, 1600, 1700; Rām. 108, 250, 1768; K. 194, 209, 219, 230, 288, 289, 372, 588, 863, 924, 940 ff.; YZ. (shĕy) 235; K.Pr. 78, sháí; 87, shāy). ¶ shĕyĕ āsun m.inf. to become in an established position, to be well-established in one's home or the like (K.Pr. 193); (of a thing) to become firmly fixed in position. --rōzun -- m.inf. to be (and continue) firmly fixed in position. --thawun -- m.inf. to make established, to put into an established position, to fix firmly in its proper place. ¶ shāyi-wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who possesses a place (Gr.Gr. 136).
or shi- in shĕ-(shi-)khorᵘ, shĕ-(shi-)trokᵘ, etc.; see shĕh.

m. night (cf. nĕsph shĕb and nĕsph shĕban, p. 658a, ll. 29, 30) (Śiv. 198, K.Pr. 176). -nam شبنم m. dew (El. shabnam; L. 459; Śiv. 167, 255, 267, 325, 334, 367, 1848; K.Pr. 180); cf. lav 3. -rang شبرنگ adj. c.g. dusky, dark-coloured; (of a horse) black; (in Ksh.) very smart, very cunning, very artful (esp. applied to a boy). -rangī شبرنگی f. smartness, cunning, artfulness (esp. of a boy). ¶ shĕban adv. at night (Śiv. 1661).

m. a sound (cf. gumbaz-shᵒ, p. 287a, l. 34) (Śiv. 736, 986, 998, 1389, 1439, 1526; K. 56, 111, 493-5, 562, 1009); a word (El. shabid; Gr.M.; Śiv. 307, 782-3, 1263, 1655-6, 1660, 1729, 1756, 1766, 1789, 1827, 1868, 1882; Rām. 1731); a word in a dictionary (Gr.M.); a short statement, phrase, formula (Śiv. 1814; Rām. 43, 180). ¶ shĕbda-brahm m. spiritual knowledge consisting in words, knowledge of the Supreme Spirit; the Supreme Spirit (Śiv. 1850).
f. a small band adorned with beads and worn by Musalmān women (El. shabí).
(? incorr. for shĕbd) m. an echo (El. shabit).

f. (with suff. of indef. art. shĕchāh, K. 855; sg. dat. shĕchĕ 1), a message, news conveyed by a message, news conveyed by word of mouth (cf. kȧnⁱ-shⁱ, p. 448b, l. 25) (El. shĕch, shich, shichh; Gr.M.; Śiv. 631, 639, 722; Rām. 136, 166, 195, 262, 442, 720, 858, 893, 1103, 1596, 1780; K. 104, 358, 379, 402-3, 535, 582, 592, 640, 642-3, 646, 692 etc.; H. x, 3; YZ. 143, 489); a notice (e.g. issued by a court of justice). --anawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --anavüñᵘ̈ --), an apostle, messenger, prophet (El. shĕch anawun). -bŏd or shĕchi-bŏd f. (sg. dat. -bö̆zᵘ̈) news or instructions conveyed by message. --bōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to listen to a message, to accept news or instructions by message (Śiv. 697, 802; Rām. 1678); to accept or grasp instructions given directly by a person present. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to send a message, to send news (Rām. 1143 h; K. 404, 580, 645, 1002). --phērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. news to return, to receive expected information (from some messenger sent out to inquire). --paküñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. news to be received gradually, or bit by bit. --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to deposit a message, to communicate a message (sent by someone absent). --wātüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a message, or instructions, to arrive (Rām. 147). ¶ shĕchi-bŏd f., see shĕchⁱ-bŏd, ab.

or card. (one of the forms taken by the Skt. word ṣaṣ) six, used in the following compounds:--, m. the power of the six, i.e. the influence of the six items (the planets, etc.) which according to astrologers influence the duration of a person's life. Hence, shĕḍbala-zātukh m. (sg. dat. -zātakas), a horoscope of the six powers (affecting a person's life), a horoscope in which is calculated the length of a person's life. -būlⁱ f. a language formed (at once) by all the six vocal organs, i.e. the language of birds (which is unintelligible to mankind); met. a secret language, an argot (e.g. thieves' Latin), jargon. -bāshĕ f.pl. infant's babbling, any similar talk. -môsᵘ m. the śrāddha or obsequial ceremony performed six months after a person's death; the date of this ceremony.
(? = شدّ) in shĕda-mada adj. c.g. very proud, very arrogant.
m. a dissolute fellow, a companion of a courtezan, a harlot's bully.

adj. c.g. having six syllables (borrowed from Skt. ṣaḍakṣara, and u.w. reference to the six-syllabled Skt. mantra, or mystic formula, Ōṁ namaḥ Śivāya, Ōṁ, reverence to Śiva) (Śiv. 154, 517, 632, 1182, 1567).
m. in shĕḍar gaḍar m.pl. (a jingle of shĕḍar, but cf. gạdᵃra), the total of child relations (on a pilgrimage, a family dinner or other festival).
adj. c.g. multiplied by six, sixfold (W. 105, shėguṇ).
adj. c.g. and subst. m. (esp. of a boy) impudent, rude, shameless, saucy.
adj. (f. shĕgöjᵘ̈), rude, shameless, one who causelessly abuses or attacks others, a ruffian, bully. Cf. shigun.
adj. (f. shĕgüñᵘ̈), sixfold (e.g. a cloth or string folded six times); sixfold, multiplied by six.

(cf. شگون) m. an omen, augury; (in Ksh.) a present of money or the like; cf. shugūn. --pālun -- m.inf. to carry out the conditions of a good omen (e.g. by giving charity or performing worship, and making a formal beginning of the intended action). Cf. shugūn pālun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shẹ̆gᵃnôwᵃ), to divide into six; to multiply by six; to cause to be despised, etc. (see shẹ̆gᵃnun).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. shẹ̆gᵃnyōv), to become sixfold, to be divided into six; to become scorned, despised, slighted, owing to extreme cheapness; to be despised generally. shẹ̆gᵃnyō-motᵃ perf. part. (f. shẹ̆gᵃnyē-müʦᵃ), divided into six; despised, scorned (on account of uselessness, bad conduct, cheapness, unsuitability).

m. a king, i.q. shāh 1 (H. i, 1, 7) and used in the following:-- -mār شہمار m. a king-serpent, snake (El. shahmár); esp. a huge, terrifying, or poisonous snake, a python (H. viii, 6, 7, 13; YZ. 48, 66, 169). -māth شہمات m. checkmate (El. shahmát). -nishīn شہنشین m. a gallery or balcony from which a king shows himself to the people; (in Ksh.) a dormitory with trelliswork for walls (El.). -par شہپر m. the largest or strongest feather in a bird's wing (YZ. 558). -pōsh m. a quilted coverlet, made of cotton-cloth, and stuffed with cotton wool. -sawār شہسوار c.g. an expert horseman, a good rider (El., YZ. 50); a horsebreaker (W. 140, K.Pr. 41). -tūl m. a kind of mulberry, the fruit of which is said to be large, acid, and deliciously flavoured (El. s.v. tūl; L. 348, shah tút, using the Indian word tūt for tūl). -tarra شہ ترہ m. N. of a certain medicinal plant, fumitory (used internally in skin diseases, and for preparing a cooling sherbet in fevers) (L. 76, shahtarr, fumaria officinalis). -zāda, i.q. shāh-zāda, p. 872b, l. 42.

or (among Paṇḍits) (sometimes written shĕ) card. (pl. dat. shĕn , ag. shĕyau , six (El. shih; Gr.Gr. 76, 82; Gr.M.; L.V. 13, (shĕ) 25; Śiv. (shĕ) 706, 1443; (shĕyau) 1443; K. 913, (shĕn) 41, 111). Cf. shĕsh. ¶ In Hindū literature there are many groups of six. Thus, there are six attributes of the Deity, viz. (in Skt.) (1) sarvajñatā, omniscience; (2) tṛpti, contentment; (3) anādibōdha, having perception from eternity; (4) svatantratā, absolute self-sufficiency; (5) nityam- aluptaśakti, having potency that is incapable of being diminished; (6) anantaśakti, omnipotence. There are six enemies, or sins which impede union with the Supreme, viz. (1) kāma, sexual desire; (2) krōdha, wrath; (3) lōbha, desire; (4) mada, arrogance; (5) mōha, delusion of mind; (6) matsara, jealousy. There are six ūrmis, or human infirmities, viz. (1) śōka, grief; (2) mōha, delusion; (3) jarā, old age; (4) maraṇa, death; (5) kṣudh, hunger; (6) pipāsā, thirst. There are six avasthās, or periods of human life, viz. (1) śiśutva, babyhood; (2) bālya, childhood; (3) kaumāra, youth; (4) yauvana, puberty; (5) tāruṇya, young manhood; (6) vārdhakya, old age. There are six vikāras, or changes of condition, in a man's life, indicated by the six verbs, (1) asti, he exists; (2) jāyatē, he is born; (3) vardhatē, he grows up; (4) vipariṇamatē, he is developed; (5) apakṣīyatē, he declines; (6); naśyati, he is destroyed (cf. L.V. 13, 82). There are six seasons of the year, viz. (in Skt.) (1) Śiśara, or the cold season, comprising the two months Māgha and Phālguna (January-March); (2) Vasanta, or the spring, comprising the two months Caitra and Vaiśākha (March-May); (3) Grīṣma, or the summer, comprising Jyēṣṭha and Āṣāḍha (May-July); (4) Varṣāḥ, or the rainy season, comprising Śrāvaṇa and Bhādra (July-September); (5) Śarad, or the autumn, comprising Āśvina and Kārttika (September-November); and (6) Hima, or the winter, comprising Agrahāyaṇa and Pauṣa (November-January); (cf. Rām. 423, 573, 661, 665, 908). In Yōga philosophy there are six cakras, or mystic circles, in the human body. These are (1) mūlâdhāra, (2) svâdhiṣṭhāna, (3) maṇipūra, (4) anāhata, (5) viśuddha, and (6) ājñā. These are fully described in L.V. pp. 12 ff., to which the student is referred. ¶ shĕ-hath, shĕ-hatyumᵘ, see s.vv. ¶ shĕ-khorᵘ or shi-khorᵘ m. an area or plot of land producing six khorᵘ (see khorᵘ 3) of grain or the like. -khôrᵘ adj. (f. shikhörᵘ̈), an area or plot of land capable of producing six khārs, or ass's loads (see khār 3), and therefore equal to about 24 British acres (p. 408a, l. 34); a receptacle capable of containing that amount of grain; a pile of grain of this amount. -mọ̆khᵘ m. he who has six faces, a name of the War-god (in Skt. Kārttikēya) (Śiv. 517). -moñᵘ adj. (f. -müñᵘ̈), (a plot of land) capable of producing six mans, of three pounds each (see man), of grain; a receptacle capable of containing this amount of grain; anything measuring or weighing six mans. -môsᵘ adj. (f. -mösᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, six months or six months ago; aged six months; continuing or lasting six months. -ryotᵘ adj. (f. -rë̆ʦᵘ̈), lasting six months, six months long (K. 295). -syūrᵘ adj. (f. -sīrᵘ̈), weighing six seers of 21b. each; a receptacle capable of containing (or cooking) that amount; a weight for weighing six seers, a six-seer weight. -trokᵘ adj. (f. -trücᵘ̈), (a plot of land) capable of producing six trakhs, of about 11 (or according to El. 9 1/2) pounds each of grain; a receptacle capable of containing that amount; (anything) weighing that amount. -wuhurᵘ adj. (f. -warishᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, six years; six years old; lasting, or continuing, for six years. -wôrᵘ adj. (f. -wörᵘ̈), sixfold, folded six times, in six layers, strands, or the like, sexto, 6to. ¶ shĕn andar adj. c.g. six years old. -hondᵘ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, six. ¶ shĕnaway card. (pl. acc. shĕnawani), even all six, all the six (Gr.Gr. 85). ¶ shĕshĕway card. (pl. acc. shĕshĕwani), even all six, all the six (Gr.Gr. 85, K. 758). ¶ shĕy pl. c.g. only six (Gr.Gr. 82).

m. coolness (e.g. of the shade under a tree) (Śiv. 1013, 1611; K.Pr. 137, shajár); reduction of temperature (e.g. of fever) (cf. atha-shᵒ, p. 62a, l. 41) (Śiv. 122, 1855); coolness (after wrath, or the like).

f. cooling, comfort (after fever, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 128); (of a wrathful person, or the like) the being appeased, soothed, calmed down. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of wrath, hate, fever, or the like) the being appeased, soothed, calmed down to occur.

f. (sg. dat. shĕhalüʦᵘ̈), rest, calmness or the like resulting from becoming cool (Gr.Gr. 128); the comfort of release from anxiety, rage, or the like. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. coolness, calmness, consolation, to be experienced. --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause coolness (by consolation or the like), to calm (disease, distress, agitation, terror, or the like).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. shĕhalôwᵘ), to cool, make cool (L. 459 shaelun); to extinguish (fire) (Rām. 1633); to cool, calm down, console one enraged, agitated, terrified). shĕhalôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shĕhalövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), cooled, made cool (by someone); (of fire) extinguished (by someone); (of one enraged, etc., as ab.) cooled, calmed down, consoled (by someone).

m. (sg. dat. shĕhalanas), an evil smell like that of rotten fish, a stink. --lārun -- m.inf. to become tainted by contact with such a stink; met. to become contaminated with vice through association with vicious persons. --yunᵘ -- m.in f. a stink to come, (of food or the like) to go bad and emit a bad smell; a charge or reputation for viciousness to be incurred; the power of attracting others to be acquired. ¶ shĕhalan-dār adj. c.g. stinking, full of the smell of rotten fish; contaminated by bad repute, abuse, or the like. -phakh (sg. dat. phakas), (affecting food or the like) an evil stink like that of rotten fish.

conj: 3 (2 p.p. shĕhalyōv), to be or become cool, to become cold (Gr.Gr. 128); (of fire) to become extinguished; (of rage, agitation, despair, or the like) to become cooled, calmed, composed, at peace. shĕhalyō-motᵘ  perf. part. (f. shĕhalyē-müʦᵘ̈), cooled, become cold; (of fire) extinguished; cooled, calmed, composed, at peace.
f.pl. a heavy continued torrent of rain.

m. a capital city (the residence of a king); a country (Rām. 46, 743); N. of a village in the Vēhī pargana, where iron and flints are found (El.). shĕhārukᵘ adj. gen. (f. shĕhārücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a capital city.
m. a witness; a martyr. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to have one's throat cut (see the next). --karun -- m.inf. to make a martyr; to kill a man as if he were a beast, to cut a man's throat.

shĕhulᵘ or shiholᵘ adj. (f. shĕ(i)hȧjⁱ , shĕ(i)hüjᵘ̈  or shĕ(i)hᵘ̈jᵘ̈ ), cool (as, e.g., the shade of a tree in sunshine); cooling, coolth-producing (cf. aḍa-shᵒ, p. 11b, l. 50; atha-shᵒ, p. 62a, l. 44) (El. shihul, shuhul; K.Pr. 102); (of rage, hate, or the like) cooled, calmed; (of sleep) cool, refreshing (H. v, 6, with double meaning, 'cold sleep', meaning 'wakefulness'); as subst. m. shade, shadow (cf. bōñĕ-shᵒ, p. 115b, l. 27) (W. 133; K.Pr. 250); a cool place, a shady place (K.Pr. 165); the cool of the day, (in the hot season) the evening (cf. aḍ-shᵒ, p. 10b, l. 3; potᵘ-shᵘ, p. 787b, l. 47) (H. i, 11). --karun -- m.inf. (of a wearied person) to take rest under the cool shade (of a tree, or the like) (K.Pr. 102); met. to take rest, compose oneself, become calm and at peace ¶ shihȧjⁱ kath f. a cool word, soothing, calming, gentle language. ¶ shihȧlⁱ-būñⁱ f. a plane-tree with (its) cooling shade; met. a kindly, generous, comforting woman. -kujⁱ or -kujᵘ̈ f. a small tree (e.g. a vine) with cooling shade; met. a kindly, generous, comforting woman. -kulᵘ  m. a tree with a cool shade; met. a kindly, generous, comforting man. -ṭē̃g m. a high place of coolth; N. of a sacred site in Śrīnagar, on the right bank of the river Jehlam, close to the second bridge. The adjoining ghāṭ is known as Sōmᵃyār, the ancient Skt. name being 'Sōmatirtha' (see RT.Tr. viii, 3360). According to Hindū tradition, in a former age, when the Valley of Kashmīr was still a lake, the god Śiva was once roaming in the Himâlaya. By accident a digit of the moon slipped from his head, and fell at this spot; met. the abode of some noble and generous person. ¶ shĕhalĕn adv. in the late cool of the day (cf. aḍ-shᵒ, p. 10b, l. 6). -bögⁱ or -bögin adv. at about this time (cf. aḍ-shᵒ, p. 10b, l. 7).
adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, a capital city.

or shĕhar m. a city, town (El. shahr; Gr.M.; Śiv. 953, 1012, 1030, 1107, 1682, 1798; Rām. 182, 554, 855, 1037, 1188, 1442, 1555, 1559; H. v, 1, 9, 11; viii, 4, 11; x, 3, 5, etc.; xii, 2, 3; K.Pr. 64, 138, 224, 253); a kingdom, country (Gr.M.; Śiv. 170; Rām. 121, 1782; H. ii, 1; YZ. 2, 18, 158). -bāsh شہر باش m. an inhabitant of a city, a townsman (as opposed to a villager or country-man) (L. 272), shĕhar-i-Lankā m. the country or city of Lankā (Rām. 416, 567). ¶ shĕharukᵘ gen. (f. shĕharücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a city; a citizen, an inhabitant of a city (Rām. 202).
f. N. of kind of large round bracelet or armlet worn by women, and usually made of gold or silver. -bọ̆ngᵃr f. a similar armlet made of gold, silver, or glass, and engraved in patterns.

or (among Paṇḍits) collective num. a group of six, a six (Gr.Gr. 82); the form which the cardinal number shĕh, six, takes in multiplication, as in sath shĕka dŏyĕtöjih, seven sixes are forty-two (Gr.Gr. 86, W. 104). Cf. shēh 2 and shĕkhāh.
f. fear, apprehension, fear of danger, i.q. shē̃kh 2 with suff. of indef. art., q.v. (Gr.M.).
m. N. of a certain plant, (?) a wild carrot or turnip (El. shakakol, ? Sium).

m. sugar (cf. nay-shᵒ, p. 669b, l. 45) (El.; K.Pr. 191); (in Ksh.) treacle, molasses. Cf. chĕrkar. -kȧndⁱ شکر قند f. the sweet potato, Convolvulus batatas or Batatas edulis. -lab شکر لب f. a sugar-lip, a lip sweet as sugar (YZ. 213); a sweet-lipped girl. -mujⁱ or -mujᵘ̈ f., i.q. -kȧndⁱ ab., q.v. -mĕkarāz (= شکر مقراض) f. 'sugar scissors', language which is sweet yet cutting to the quick, a polite sneer; a person who customarily uses this kind of language. Cf. -shrākh, bel. -pholᵘ m. a mass of sugar, a heap of sugar; a lump of crystallized sugar. -pāra شکر پارہ f. a kind of sweetmeat (made of flour, butter, and sugar). -shö m. the name used in schools for the Śāradā character corresponding to the Nāgarī character. -shrākh f. (sg. dat. -shrāki), 'sugar-knife', language which is sweet yet cuts to the quick, a polite sneer; a woman who customarily uses this kind of language; cf. -mekarāz, ab. -wôñᵘ m. sugar-water, sweetened water, sherbet. -wuṭh adj. c.g. a man or woman whose language is sweet, but who is insincere in heart (Śiv. 539).
m. (sg. dat. shēkhas), (among Moslems) a venerable man, an elder; the head of a village tribe, or religious community; N. of a class of Moslems, a common title for respectable Moslems (K.Pr. 194).

m. a large division of country Used in the following:-- -dar (= شقدار) m. (f. -dariñ, his wife) an officer appointed to collect the revenue of this tract; (in Ksh.) a field-watcher, a guardian of the crops (El. shagdar, shakhdár); a spy over the shawl-weavers (El. shakhdar, L. 402 shakdár). -dörⁱ  f. (in Ksh.) the duty or profession of a crop-guardian, etc. (El.); his wages.

m. (sg. dat. shē̃kas), the conch-shell (used in worship as a trumpet) (Śiv. 1847); cf. shĕnkh. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to sound a conch, to sound a trumpet (Rām. 609). ¶ shē̃ka-hār f. a kind of cowry-shell, shaped like a conch-shell.

m. (sg. dat. shĕkas), doubt, suspense, uncertainty, hesitation, vacillation, anxiety, suspicion (El. shakk, Gr.M., Śiv. 886); incredulity, scepticism; cf. shē̃kh. -dār adj. c.g. suspicious, of a doubting nature, distrustful; suspect, questionable, that of which the existence or non-existence is doubtful. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. doubt, hesitation, suspicion to be experienced (H. v, 8; xii, 15). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to entertain doubt, feel doubtful. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to remove doubt. --karun -- m.inf. to cause doubt in another; to make (another) suspicious (of someone). --kāsun -- m.inf. to remove, or dispel, doubt, etc. --nērun -- m.inf. doubt or suspense to disappear, doubt or hesitation to be dispelled. --pāwun -- m.inf. to cause (a person) to be filled with suspense. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. doubt to fall (to a person), to entertain a doubt, to feel doubtful. --rōzun -- m.inf. doubt to remain, doubt to linger (after it should have been dispelled). --thawun -- m.inf. to cause doubt to linger (as ab.). --ʦalun -- m.inf. doubt to flee, doubt to disappear (e.g. after inquiry). ¶ shĕka-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), free from doubt or anxiety, secure, fearless; (as adv.) fearlessly. ¶ shĕkan roṭᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. --rütᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), attacked by doubt, anxiety, fear, or the like. ¶ shĕkas gaʦhun m.inf. to go into suspense, to fall into a state of hesitation. --karun -- m.inf. to throw a person into hesitation or suspense.

or (L.V. 73-6) shö̃kh f. (sg. dat. shē̃ki), doubt, uncertainty (Gr.Gr. 125, Gr.M., K.Pr. 28); suspicion, distrust, misgiving (Gr.Gr. 21, Gr.M.); hope, expectation (Gr.M., Rām. 657); fear, apprehension (Gr.Gr. 246, L.V. 73-6); a mistaken belief, a wrong impression (Rām. 890); cf. shĕkh 2 and shē̃kā. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. doubt, hesitation, uncertainty (e.g. as to the existence of anything) to arise (Rām. 1294); a mistake, or wrong impression to occur (K. 598). --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take (i.e. feel) apprehension (even when there is no cause for it). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make a mistake, to form a wrong impression. --niñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take doubt, to feel that one has reason for being suspicious, to become suspicious (about) (El. to doubt). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. doubt or suspicion to come to a person. --rōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. expectation to continue (in spite of disappointment, or the like). --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to feel hope, to be expectant. shē̃kh-ṭö̃kh or shē̃khā-ṭö̃khā f. a confused combination of fear, hope, doubt, suspicion, effort, regrets, etc. (either all at once, or one after the other). ¶ shē̃ki-rosᵘ or -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), free from doubt, hesitation, etc.; without expectation; not an object of doubt, not (or no longer) open to suspicion. -rostuy adv. fearlessly, without hesitation; hopelessly, without expectation. --rōzun -- m.inf. to wait hopefully or expectantly.
m. a group of six, a six (Gr.Gr. 82); cf. shĕka. --khaṇḍā -- m. a group of about six, or of a little less than six (Gr.Gr. 83).
m. a crest, chaplet, tuft; a diadem, crown (cf. kāla-shᵒ, p. 434a, l. 29) (Śiv. 1174, 1586); a peak, summit.
m. (sg. dat. shĕkhᵃʦas), a person, individual (Gr.M.; H. x, 1, 2, 6; xii, 3).

shĕkhᵃth or shĕkth f. (sg. dat. shĕkᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), ability, power, strength, might, capacity (cf. dātru-shᵒ, p. 259a, l. 46) (El. shakht; Gr.M.; Śiv. shĕkth, 1224, 1292, 1505, 1535, 1553, 1555, 1823; Rām. 71 (shĕktⁱ), 1449 (shĕkth); K. (shĕkᵃth), 1146, 1173); the energy or active power of a deity, personified as his wife, (as Dēvī of Śiva or Lakṣmī of Viṣṇu) (cf. parama-shᵒ, p. 760a, l. 11; shiwa-shᵒ, s.v. shiv) (L.V. 2, 68, shĕkᵃth; Śiv. shĕktī, 1511, 1526; shĕkti, 11, 39, 84, 94, 100, 103, 115, 495, etc.; shĕkth, 53, 665, 1143, 1199, 1242, etc.; Rām. 6 (shĕkth); K. (shĕkᵃth) 344). ¶ shĕkti-nāth m. the lord of the Energic Power, i.e. Śiva (Śiv. 1204, 1262, 1556). -pāth m. a shedding of power; hence, divine graciousness, divine favour (Śiv. 1012, 1036, 1219, 1492, 1535, 1551, 1553, 1556, 1683, 1748, 1823).
m. (sg. dat. shĕkunas), an omen, augury (cf. kŏ-shᵒ, p. 480b, l. 38). Cf. shugūn.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. shyū̃kᵘ, but generally written shū̃kᵘ f. shī̃cᵘ̈; 2 p.p. shē̃cyōv), to doubt, hesitate, be of two minds (Gr.Gr. 125, L.V. 70); to be suspicious. ¶ shē̃kan-hār n.ag., c.g. doubtful, an object of doubt, questionable, uncertain. ¶ shē̃kani rōzun m.inf. to remain in suspicion, to stay watching suspiciously (K. 811). ¶ shū̃kᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shī̃cᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), doubted, distrusted, an object of doubt.

f. likeness, resemblance, semblance, image; arrangement in proper form; model, pattern, mode, manner; shape, form, figure (cf. bad-shᵒ, p. 81b, l. 22) (El. shakl; Śiv. 914, 1102 (shĕkᵃl-i, with iẓāfat); H. x, 7). --ganḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bind one's form, i.e. to be or become obstinate; to put in order that which is in disorder (lit. or met.).

adj. c.g. doubtful, perplexing; sceptical; suspicious. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become doubtful, to become suspicious, to be filled with hesitation. --karun -- m.inf. to fill with doubts, make suspicious.

m. the sharp metal point of an arrow, an arrow-head; (in a ripened boil or tumour) a string of clotted pus (looked upon as its root) (cf. pāka-shᵒ, p. 725b, l. 14); poignant hidden hatred or jealousy. --kāsun -- m.inf. to pull out the arrow- head; hence, to remove a cause of hatred or jealousy; to take away (a person's) anxiety (e.g. when after long and continued efforts without success, a friend comes and helps him to complete his work). --rōzun -- m.inf. the arrow- head to stick; hence, to be filled with lasting jealousy or hatred; to be filled with anxiety as to the success of some work.
f. a huge stone, a rock (usually one which has fallen from the hills on to the low ground) (El. m.; L.V. 52, f.).
f. a stone (of any shape or size) (El. shela m.).

m. (sg. dat. shĕlakas), a beating with a whip, scourging (cf. kamca-shᵒ, p. 444b, l. 31; lōri-shᵒ, p. 531a, l. 15) (Gr.Gr. 5); (in Ksh. also) a beating with the hand or fist, a slap, a blow of the fist (cf. atha-shᵒ, p. 62b, l. 1); abuse, invective, threatening (cf. lĕka-shᵒ, p. 518a, l. 38). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat a beating, to suffer a beating, to get a drubbing, to be beaten. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. a beating (or punishment) to fall (upon a person), to be beaten.

f. (sg. dat. shĕlapi), art, skill, accomplishment, ingenuity (Gr.M., shĕlph); (in Ksh.) trade (El. shalpa). --āsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. skill to exist, to be expert in an art. --lārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. skill to adhere (to) (cf. lārun 3), to become accomplished in some art.
adj. c.g., i.q. shĕltôkᵘ, q.v., but used more with ref. to grown-up people.
(cf. شلتاق) adj. (f. shĕltöcᵘ̈), (as subst. m.) contention; (in Ksh., adj.) (esp. of a youth, m. or f.) very sharp, shrewd, acute, cunning (esp. for one's own benefit).

m. quiet, tranquillity, quiet of mind; self-restraint, absence of passion, indifference, stoicism, quietism (L.V. 71, Śiv. 334); (of anger, grief, thirst, etc.) allayment, mitigation, appeasement (Śiv. 1844); abasement, humiliation (Rām. 980). -dam m. tranquillity (or quietude) and self-restraint (L.V. 63; Śiv. 269, 931, 1033, 1404, 1754, 1811). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. allayment, etc., to occur. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take allayment, i.e. to become appeased, to become tranquillized, assuaged. --karun -- m.inf., id.
a candle, lamp (El. shama; Rām. 883, 1068, 1071; K.Pr. 193, shĕmā); (in Ksh.) the light given out by a lamp (Śiv. 1775, 1777; YZ. 148); the flame, or flare, of a lamp (H. vi, 6; viii, 13; x, 7).
or shimāl شمال m. the North (El. shamál, shimál; Rām. 582 (shiᵒ)).
m. the embroidered end of a turban (Rām. 976) or cummerbund.
m. the act of appeasing, allaying, soothing, conquering, alleviating (Śiv. 94).
f. (sg. dat. shĕmüʦᵘ̈), calmness, tranquillity of mind, quietude.
m. N. of a demon slain by Pradyumna (in Skt. Śambara) (K. 736-7, 744-5, 751).

or shĕmbū  or (as written by Paṇḍits) m. (sg. dat. shĕmbus ), a N. of Śiva, in Skt. Śambhu (L.V. 45; Śiv. shĕmbu, 503, 782, 1722; shĕmbū, 835, 918, 1128, 1814; Voc. shĕmbō, 155, 266, 1011, 1014, etc. In all these written). shembu-nāth  m. the Lord Śambhu, i.q. shĕmbu (Śiv. 1552).
m. the box-tree, Buxus sempervirens (cf. shākha-shᵒ, p. 876b, l. 1); any tall and upright tree; met. the graceful figure or limb of a mistress (Rām. 1494).

f. a sword (El. shamsher m.; W. 129; Śiv. 1631 f.; Rām. 37, 411, 648, 825, 842, 919; H. iii, 9; YZ. 51; K.Pr. 72, 92, 258), ba-shĕmshēr, on a sword, under the stroke of a sword (Rām. 299); with, by means of, a sword (Rām. 365, 371, 1186). --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to draw a sword (H. viii, 13; x, 7). --lāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give a blow with a sword, to strike with a sword (H. viii, 6). --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to raise a sword (in order to strike) (H. ii, 7; iii, 9; x, 7). ¶ shĕmshēri-hondᵘ tēg m. the blade of a sword (H. viii, 6, 13). -hünzᵘ̈ ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. a blow of a sword, a sword-cut (H. iii, 5, 6).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. shĕmyōv), (of anger, grief, thirst, etc.) to be or become allayed, calmed, pacified (L.V. 27); (of a person) to be calmed, be at peace, become peaceful (Śiv. 156, 315, 385, 754, 976, 1017, 1170, 1268, 1398, 1751, 1811; Rām. 11, 37, 171, 992, 1756); (of blazing fire, etc.) to be abated, extinguished (cf. nār shᵒ, p. 647a, l. 12); (of water) to become at rest (and gradually soak away) (L.V. 106). shĕmyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shĕmyē-müʦᵘ̈), calmed, allayed, pacified; (of fire or the like) extinguished; and so on for the other meanings of the verb.
adj. (f. shĕmüñᵘ̈), one who practises calmness, etc. (see shĕmun), used in the phrase shānta-shᵒ, p. 886b, l. 28.
or shomᵘran f. (sg. dat. shomᵘrüñᵘ), quelling, allaying, appeasing, soothing, alleviating (anger, thirst, grief, or the like); extinguishing (a blazing fire, or the like).

or shomᵘrāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. shomᵘrôwᵘ), to quell, allay, appease, soothe, alleviate (anger, fever, thirst, grief, or the like); to make quiet, tranquillize, pacify (Śiv. shĕm˚, 521, 1793, 1882; Rām. (id.) 19); to extinguish (a blazing fire or the like) (cf. nār shᵒ, p. 647a, l. 15); cf. shẹ̆mᵃrun. shomᵘrôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shë̆mᵘ̈rövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, not shomᵘrövᵘ-, as we might expect), allayed, alleviated, appeased (or ab.); (of a conflagration) extinguished.
or shomᵘrĕr m. quelling, allayment, appeasement, soothing, alleviation (of anger, fever, grief, thirst, or the like); extinguishment (of a conflagration or the like).

or shomᵘrun conj. 1 (1 p.p. shomᵘrᵘ), to quell, allay, appease, soothe, alleviate (a person, anger, fever, thirst, grief, or the like) (Śiv. shĕm˚, 1817); to extinguish (a blazing fire or the like) (cf. nār shᵒ, p. 647a, l. 14). Cf. shẹ̆mᵃrāwun.
in shĕna shĕna adv. slowly, by slow degrees, gradually.
f. knowledge, acquaintance (cf. shinās and lāl-shĕnākh, p. 522a, l. 22).

or shĕnaishcar m. the planet Saturn. (He is said by Hindūs to be the son of the Sun, and is represented as of a black colour, or dressed in dark-coloured clothes) (El. shanachara, shanaschar) (Śiv. 481 shĕnai˚; Rām. (id.) 419, (shĕna˚) 1277). shĕnashcar-rang m. 'Saturn-colour', dark colour, blackness, dirt.
m. Saturday (cf. baṭawār, p. 145b, l. 36) (El. shanyiwáṛ).

f., i.q. shē̃kh 2, fear, apprehension (K. 80, 367, 696); a mistake, wrong impression. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. doubt, hesitation, uncertainty (e.g. as to the existence of anything) to happen; a mistake, or wrong impression, to occur (Rām. 1267). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make a mistake, form a wrong impression (Rām. 1154).

m. a N. of Śiva, in Skt. Śaṅkara (cf. parama-shᵒ, p. 760a, l. 17; shiwa-shᵒ, s.v. shiv) (L.V. 18, 25, 39, 40; Śiv. 155, 190, 197, 248, 355, 384, 379, 502, 599, 714, 931, 1157, 1161, 1235, 1634, etc.; K. 619); N. of a Yĕksha (Yakṣa) or demon killed by Krushna (Kṛṣṇa) (in Skt. Śaṅkhacūḍa) (K. 299). -pōrī f. N. of a village in Kashmīr, near which Sītā is said to have disappeared into the earth (Rām. 1718).
m. N. of a celebrated teacher of the Vēdānta philosopher (in Skt. Śaṅkarâcārya) (Śiv. 1503); N. of a mountain in Kashmīr (Śiv. 953).
n.ag. (f. shĕnkavüñᵘ̈), fearful, full of apprehension (K. 149).

m. (sg. dat. shĕnkhas), a conch-shell, a conch (used as a trumpet, i.q. shē̃kh 1, q.v.) (Śiv. 386, 709, 736; Rām. 77, 224; K. 59, 491-3, 495, 1009, 1031). --wāyun -- m.inf. to play the conch-shell, to blow a trumpet (Śiv. 732, 782, 796).
m. N. of a demon who was killed by Krushna (Kṛṣṇa) (Śiv. 709, K. 491).
f. the condition or nature of a eunuch; the conduct of a eunuch (such as dancing and singing at marriages, lamentations at funerals, cf. lāʦh); conduct, such as that of a eunuch.
(? shivrāmgāsa) (? gend.) N. of a certain medicinal plant, Mentha sp., good for sword wounds (L. 76).
in lapar shĕpar, p. 529a, l. 21, q.v.

m. (sg. dat. shĕpathas), an oath, a solemn asseveration. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat an oath, i.e. to take an oath, make a solemn asseveration, swear to adopt a certain course of conduct. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take a solemn oath as to the truth of one's statement, esp. (when charged with an offence) to take a solemn oath as to one's innocence.
f. (sg. dat. shĕphagüʦᵘ̈), affection, tenderness, mercy, compassion (Rām. 1426).
m. the redness of the sky between sunset and nightfall, evening twilight (El. shafak, Śiv. 910). -bọ̆ngᵃr f. a kind of large armlet worn by women on the forearm, made of gold, silver, or the like.
adj. c.g. illumined by the redness of the sky between sunset and nightfall.
m. (sg. dat. shĕphkatas), affection, kindness, pity, compassion, mercy, clemency. --karun -- m.inf. to forgive (El.).

or shĕpushᵘ (= شپّوش) m. night-clothes; (in Ksh. esp.) a kind of warm wadded quilt (W. 140, K.Pr. 146). shĕpōshĕ- (or shĕpushⁱ-)tolⁱ  m., id. -wūrᵘ̈ f. an outer covering for such a quilt (to keep it clean).

m. an arrow, a shaft (K. (shĕrāh) 630); met. longing; intense desire (cf. dana-shᵒ, p. 222a, l. 10; dyāra-shᵒ, p. 270b, l. 45); distress, torment, anguish (Rām. 50, 125, 1110; YZ. 23, 514). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become distressed, pained, tormented (by the non-success or non-attainment of some longed-for aim or object). --karun -- m.inf. to cause such torment. --thawun -- m.inf. to cause such torment to be felt all one's life.
m. evildoing, wrongdoing, wickedness (cf. atha-shᵒ, p. 62b, l. 3, and Rām. 230, accidentally or ignorantly performing an improper action) (K.Pr. 103); (in Ksh.) envy, malignancy, jealous hatred.
shēr 1, or shōr 2 in mraga-shĕr, etc., see p. 590b, l. 6. Cf. sar 2.

m. a head (of man or beast) (cf. khōra-shᵒ, p. 410b, l. 12) (Śiv. 192, 197, 317, 453, 985, 1031, 1615; Rām. 274-5, 322, 990, 1127, 1172, 1645; K. 59, 398, 460, 465, 523, 610, 925, 931, 962, 1045, 1109); a top, pinnacle, tip, end, point; the preface or beginning part of a book. -tāj (= سرتاج) m. a crown, tiara, diadem (K.Pr. 134); a man highly respected, and an acknowledged head of his community.
m. a tiger. --banun -- or --gaʦhun -- or --sapadun -- m.inf. 'to become a tiger', to get the better of, overcome, succeed in triumphantly repelling an attack, accusation, or the like.

m. (in a house of more than one story) the northern or southern end (as distinct from the front or back). ¶ shēra-dörᵘ̈ f. a doorway or door at one of these ends of a house, a side-door. -kūṭᵘ m. the long beams running right across these ends of a house, holding together the perpendicular supporting beams. -lab f. one of the stone or brick walls forming these ends of the house. -tākh m. (sg. dat. -tākas), a small framed door or window in one of these ends of a house. -ʦyūnᵘ m. (sg. dat. -ʦīnis), a wall at one of these ends of a house which supports the main roof-rafters.
m. (sg. dat. shĕrahas), the Muslim law (K.Pr. 193). (Note that shĕra may also be an obl. case of shĕr 1, 2, or 3, qq.v.)
m. spirituous liquor, wine (YZ. 209, K.Pr. 228). -wān m. a wine-shop, spirit-shop, drinking shop, public-house. ¶ shĕrāba-sān m. a cup-bearer (El.), but? (a person) 'with wine', see sān.
f. (sg. dat. shĕrāküʦᵘ̈), sharing, participation, partnership (K.Pr. 193).

c.g. protection, preservation, security (K. 585, 763); a protector, preserver, defender; a place of refuge, asylum, place of shelter (Śiv. 600-1); one who has taken refuge (Śiv. 1752). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go to a place or person of refuge, to take refuge (with), fly (to) for protection, to seek refuge (Śiv. 75, 316, 484, 493, 605-6, 798, 1196; Rām. 32, 521, 725, 821, 829, 991, 1584, 1763; K. 767). --rōzun -- m.inf. persistently to remain under (a person's) protection. --sö̃panun -- m.inf. to become a refugee, to take refuge (with so-and-so) (Rām. 75, 495, 591, 782, 817, 938, 940, 984, 1291, 1478, 1690; K. 876 (sampanum)). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come to seek refuge, to take refuge (with a person) (Rām. 1184; K. 238, 243, 329, 584, 826, 880, 1172). ¶ shĕrani yunᵘ m.inf. to come (to one) for protection, to seek the protection (of), to take refuge (with, or in) (Śiv. 29, 987, 1134).
