c.g. (sg. dat. shĕranāgatas), one who comes for protection or refuge, a refugee, fugitive (Śiv. 1673, 1740; K. 585).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shēranôwᵘ), to cause to be arranged, or set in order; to cause to be prepared, made ready; to cause to be repaired, mended; to repair, mend (K. 954).
f. wages paid for arranging, for repairing, etc., the cost of repairs. Cf. shērun.

f. (sg. dat. shĕrbüʦᵘ̈), a draught, drink, beverage (cf. khᵃñĕ-shᵃ, p. 405b, l. 6); sherbet, sugar and water, or the like (El.; L. 72, 271, 345; K.Pr. 146); a dose of medicine, potion. shĕrbüʦᵘ̈-koshᵘ̈ m. the lees or grounds remaining after preparing sherbet.

adj. c.g. and subst. m. (sg. dat. shĕrīkas; f. shĕrⁱkiñ q.v.), confederate, united, joined, concerned (in); common, in common; (as subst.) a sharer, participator, partaker (with) (H. i, 10; K.Pr. 78); a partner, copartner, associate, colleague, ally, accomplice, confederate. --sapadun -- m.inf. to connive (at), to share, to be a party (to). ¶ shĕrīka-bodᵘ m. 'a sharer-handful', copartnership, coparcenership, sharing.
m. the body of man, beast, or bird (Gr.M., Śiv. 878).

f. shame, bashfulness, modesty (W. 123; Śiv. 873; K.Pr. 29, 193); the modest feeling due to the receipt of favours, the being overwhelmed with gratitude, the being confounded with favours granted. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to feel ashamed, be bashful, shy; to live modestly, in modest content, to pass one's time in solitary content. ¶ shĕrmi-marm f. 'the essential of modesty', the becoming full of modesty or shame. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈) modest by nature, diffident, bashful, shy.

adj. c.g. ashamed, abashed, shamefaced, confounded, bashful, modest, blushing (cf. rum rum shĕrmanda thawȧnⁱ, p. 833b, l. 41) (El. sharminda; Śiv. 89, 323, 362, 712, 874; Rām. 745, 1337, 1610; K.Pr. 228).
m. a wine-bibber, a drunkard; a wine-seller, liquor-seller, wine-merchant.
f. the stake in a wager, etc. --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to collect, or hold, the stakes in a bet or gambling, to be a stakeholder.

m. (sg. dat. shĕrtas), a condition, stipulation, engagement, treaty (K. 720, K.Pr. 196); a wager, a bet; (in Ksh.) the hidden essential quality of any thing or action (Rām. 840 (f.)). --bĕhun -- m.inf. an agreement to be assented to, a wager, or bet, to be agreed to. --khārun -- m.inf. to make a bet, lay a wager; to put forward a pretext, to raise a pretext, to decide hurriedly on a mere pretext. --khasun -- m.inf. a pretext to be raised as ab. ¶ shĕrta-shĕrth (= شرطا شرطی) f. mutual obligations; mutual conditions, mutual betting. ¶ shĕrtas bĕhun m.inf. (in a bet) to lay a stake.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. shyūrᵘ (also written shūrᵘ); f. shīrᵘ̈), to arrange, set in order (Gr.Gr. 15, 21; Gr.M.; L. 458, W. 114); to make ready, prepare (cf. kamān shērüñᵘ̈, p. 445b, l. 10) (Rām. 572, 1420, 1452; H. x, 7; xi, 12, 17); to repair, mend (Gr.M.); to finish; to adorn (YZ. 167). ¶ shīrith pṻrith rōzun m.inf. to keep oneself or remain dressed up in all one's best (e.g. a bride or bridegroom during the marriage ceremony, or a woman awaiting her lover). --thawun -- m.inf. to put in order, to put by carefully arranged and safely. ¶ shyūrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shīrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), arranged, put in order; made ready, prepared; repaired, mended; finished; adorned.
f. of shĕrīkh, q.v., a female sharer, etc.
f. the condition of sharing, coparcenary.
card. six, in shĕsh-barg, six-leaved, see jāphurᵘ, p. 376b, l. 13. Cf. shĕh 2.

(or) or shīsh subst. and adj. c.g. (sg. abl. shēshĕ (shīshĕ 1) ), that which remains over and above, that which is the rest, the remainder, residue (cf. huta-shᵒ, p. 359b, l. 30, and Śiv. 1658, 1881; shĕwa-shᵒ, s.v. shĕv). ¶ shēshĕ-(shīshĕ-)nāg  m. N. of a celebrated serpent (in. Skt. śēṣa-nāga) represented as having a thousand heads, and to form the couch and canopy of the god Viṣṇu, and sometimes as bearing the entire world on one of his heads (Śiv. 735, 1153; Rām. 223, 918; K. 41, 43, 46, 74); an ammonite (in Skt. śālagrāma), a sacred stone considered to be typical of Viṣṇu.
adj. (f. shĕshĕwa), (of a cloth, or the like) (that of) which (the warp) consists of six hundred (threads).
n.ag. (f. shĕshĕvüñᵘ̈), one who bears patiently, tolerates, endures.
m. the moon. -kal f. a digit of the moon (L.V. 25, 69; Śiv. 1657, 1842). -ras m. moon-juice, nectar, the water of immortality (L.V. 40).
or f. a N. of the goddess Durgā (in Skt. ṣaṣṭhī). Offerings are made to her on the sixth day after a child's birth. Cf. sŏndar 1.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shoshᵘ), to bear, endure; to tolerate, stand, suffer, acquiesce in. Cf. sahun. shĕshith hĕkun m.inf. to tolerate, endure patiently and with determination.
adj. c.g. motionless, paralysed, senseless, stupefied, benumbed.
m. the male organ of generation, the penis.
or shẹ̆sᵃtruwᵃ adj. (f. shĕshⁱtrüvⁱ or shẹ̆sᵃtrüvᵃ), made of iron, iron (Gr.M. shĕstᵃruvᵃ). Cf. shĕstruwᵘ.

or shẹ̆sᵃtᵃr or shẹ̆stᵃr m. (sg. dat. shĕshⁱtras or shẹ̆stras), iron (of which there are mines in Kashmīr) (El. shistir, shistur; Gr.M. shĕstᵃr; W. 128, shistar; L.V. 100 (= K.Pr. 46), shẹ̆sᵃtᵃr; Śiv. 1563, 1616 (id., shistar); Rām. (shẹ̆sᵃtᵃr), 18, 1113; YZ. 122 (shistar); K.Pr. 46, 197, 199, 243); met. a weapon, arms; armour (El. shastar). --bĕhanāwun -- m.inf. to cause iron (or a weapon) to be imposed (on some one), to cow, keep in subjection by intimidation. ¶ shĕshⁱtra-(or shẹ̆sᵃtra-) bāna  m. anything usually made of iron (e.g. a knife, or the like).
adj. (f. shĕstrüvᵘ̈), made of iron, iron (H. v, 4; xii, 16, 17). I.q. shĕshⁱtruwⁱ, q.v.
m. N. of a man (in Skt. Śatadhanvan) killed by Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) for having slain Shĕtruzith, q.v. (K. 689, 691, 693).
m. the devil, Satan (H. iii, 87; K.Pr. shaitán, 191, 184); a wicked fellow, a rascal (K.Pr. shaitán, 91).
m. (sg. dat. shẹ̆tᵃratas), enmity, hostility, spite, discord (El. shatrut, shitrut, Gr.Gr. 144, Gr.M., Śiv. 1756, K. 542). --karun -- m.inf. to hate (El.).
ord. (f. shĕtawuhimᵘ̈), twenty-sixth, i.q. shĕwuhyumᵘ, q.v.
m. the coming (esp. to a poor man) of great power and wealth.

(pl. dat. shĕtan), card. a hundred (L.V. 6). As a simple cardinal this word is the same as hath, q.v., but only used for the hundreds after eight hundred. Thus zᵃh hath, two hundred; aiṭh hath, eight hundred; but nav shĕth, nine hundred (p. 357a, l. 49; p. 664a, l. 18); kāh shĕth, eleven hundred (p. 387b, l. 8; Rām. 740-1); nawa-shĕtukᵘ (p. 664a, l. 48) (Śiv. 738, 1887 (bāh sh˚, 1200); Rām. 535 (ʦŏdāh sh˚, 1400), 545 (shurā sh˚, 1600), 885 (id.)). -shĕtⁱ m.pl. hundreds (of any article), innumerable (L.V. 6). Cf. p. 898b, l. 44. ¶ shĕta-monᵘ adj. (f. -müñᵘ̈), hard-hearted, callous, not moved by another's sorrows or necessity, mean-hearted, niggardly. -môrᵘ adj. (f. -mörᵘ̈), one who kills by hundreds, one who massacres; met. a violent, turbulent, rough, outrageous, ferocious fellow.
f. (sg. dat. shīṭhᵘ̈), the sixth lunar day of a lunar fortnight (cf. kŏmāra-shᵒ, p. 446a, l. 41). vitāla-shᵒ, p. 1164b, l. 24.

or shaiṭh card. (pl. dat. shēṭhan), sixty (Gr.Gr. 78, 84-5, 148; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 181). ¶ shēṭha-wuhurᵘ (f. -warishᵘ̈), full sixty years old. ¶ shēṭhan-andar adj. c.g. among the sixties, (any person, thing, or action, who or which is) sixty years old. --hondᵘ -- adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, sixty; earning sixty (rupees, etc.) as wages.
in aiṭha-shēṭhakh, p. 66b, l. 41, q.v., and cf. shēṭh 1.

m. (sg. dat. shẹ̆tras, also written shẹ̆tᵃras, and shĕtras. This word is opp. to mẹ̆thᵃr, q.v.; cf. Rām. 1781) an enemy, foe, adversary (El. shathar, shithar; Gr.Gr. 144; Gr.M. shĕtᵃr; Śiv. 1541; Rām. 154, 179, 450, 733, 837, 957, 1197, 1276, 1439, 1781-2, etc.; K. 132, 364-5, 599; K.Pr. 9, 78, 142). ¶ shẹ̆tᵃra-(or shĕtra-) bögⁱ  m.pl. 'shares of enemy', the becoming an object of enmity. -bāy f. the wife of an enemy; a female enemy; cf. mĕtra-bāy, p. 606a, l. 5. -buzⁱ adj. c.g. 'liability to an enemy', under the power or control of an enemy. -gara m. the home or house of an enemy (cf. mĕtra-gara, p. 606a, l. 6). -gātukh m. (sg. dat. -gātakas), a slayer of enemies (Rām. 1280). ¶ shẹ̆tᵃrüñᵃ-wạkᵃruñᵃ f.pl. an assemblage, a combination, of enemies.

f. ? a cripple's crutch. The meaning and form of this word are doubtful. It has been noted only in the following:-- shĕchĕ-somᵘ m. 'like a cripple's crutch', very slight means of support (in the way of children, allies, or the like).

m. (sg. dat. shĕtruzitas), N. of a Yādava (in Skt. Satrājit, or according to some versions Śatrujit). He was the father of Satĕbhām (Satyabhāmā), and was given by the sun a valuable jewel. He was slain by Shĕtadanwa (q.v.) for the sake of this jewel (K. 670, 675, 689, 690).
ord. (f. shĕtimᵘ̈), hundredth, i.q. hatyumᵘ, q.v., used in the higher hundreds above eight hundred. Cf. hath, p. 357a, l. 48; nawa- shĕtyumᵘ, p. 664a, l. 50) (Gr.Gr. 81, 84).

adj. (f.shĕtiñᵘ̈), i.q. hatyunᵘ, q.v., costing, or worth, a hundred (rupees, etc.); earning (wages, etc., amounting to, a hundred (rupees, etc.) (cf. nawa-shᵒ, p. 664b, l. 2; pönʦa-shᵒ, p. 743a, l. 49; but sata-hatyunᵘ, worth seven hundred).

shĕturgun, or shĕtrugn (or) m. (sg. dat. (Rām. 1698) shĕtrugnas), N. of a brother of Rāma and twin brother of Lakṣmaṇa (in Skt. Śatrughna) (Śiv. (shẹ̆taᵃrᵃ) 1420; Rām. (shĕturgun) 84, 86, 138, 283, 385, 1131, etc.; (shĕtrugn) 166, 224, 262-3, 1143d, 1758).
f. the conduct of an enemy, opposition (El. shetaráz). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to oppose (El.).

m. (sg. abl. shĕwa 1), a human corpse, a dead body (El. shau; Gr.M.; Rām. 671, 1177). El. also gives the meaning 'God' to this word. Possibly shiv (q.v.) is meant. Cf. haph. ¶ shĕwa-dĕwa m. the arrival or coming of death (esp. when unexpected or accidental) (used esp. in curses and the like). -khȧshⁱ adj. c.g. dead from an instantaneous death. -khȧshⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to suffer a sudden death. -nĕrmāl or -nērmāl m. the water with which a corpse has been washed (and hence ceremonially impure). -rang m. corpse-colour, resemblance to a corpse (e.g. the pallor of a person due to fear, fainting, sickness, or the like). -rath m. (sg. dat. -ratas), the blood of a corpse, the blood that issues from a corpse; met. an abusive description of food angrily or disdainfully refused (quasi fit only to be thrown away as something utterly unclean). -ruth m. (sg. dat. -rutas), (on the occasion of a death) a fast for ten or twelve days maintained by the relations of the deceased, who eat only once a day. -shīsh m. the ready money of the family left over and above after the expenses of a funeral.

or shēwa m. suspicion, doubt, hesitation, jealous suspicion (e.g. when one has secretly found a source of wealth, to suspect that another person has got news about its whereabouts). --aʦun -- m.inf. suspicion to enter, suspicion to be felt; by success in previous begging to become encouraged to worry the giver by further repeated begging.
or shiwāla m. a temple dedicated to Śiva (see shiv) (El. shawálah, a temple; Śiv. 1692).
or shiᵒ ord. (f. shĕ(shi) wanzöhimᵘ̈), fifty-sixth (El., Gr.Gr. 78).
f. N. of a woman of a wild tribe (in Skt. śabarī) who was an ardent devotee of Rāma, and to whom he showed graciousness (Śiv. 1471).

or (q.v.) shĕtawuh card. (pl. dat. shĕwuhan), twenty-six (Gr.Gr. 77). Cf. shĕtawuh. shĕwuhan-hondᵘ  adj. (gen. pl., f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, twenty-six; costing twenty-six (rupees, etc.); earning twenty-six (rupees, etc.).
f. (sg. dat. shĕyümᵘ̈), the sixth lunar day of any lunar fortnight. shĕyümᵘ̈- hondᵘ gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a sixth lunar day.
card. (pl. dat. shĕyĕshītan), eighty-six (Gr.Gr. 79; El. shishít, sheyishít).
or shĕyĕtöjih card. (pl. dat. shĕyĕtöjĕn or shĕyĕtöjihan), forty-six (Gr.Gr. 78).
or shĕyĕtöjyumᵘ ord. (f. shĕyĕtöjⁱhimⁱ or shĕyĕtöjimᵘ̈), forty-sixth (Gr.Gr. 78).
or ord. (f. shĕyimᵘ̈), sixth (Gr.Gr. 76; El. shâyum; Rām. 1154, 1280; K. 132, 758). See shĕyyumᵘ.
m. a tiger; cf. shĕzᵃd. shĕza-ʦam m. a tiger's skin (used as a seat for religious or ascetic purposes).
m. (f. shĕzdiñ), a tiger (Rām. 1630). Cf. shĕz.
m. one, who being inexpert, engages in some handicraft (literally a Śūdra, who is traditionally ignorant and clumsy. See the prec.).
m. (f. shidᵃröñᵃ), a Śūdra, a man of the fourth or lowest of the four principal castes (traditionally fit only for service or selling mean articles, ignorant, and clumsy). Cf. shūdr.
f. a woman of the Śūdra caste (see shidᵃr).
f. the condition, or habits, of a Śūdra (see shidᵃr); the habit of engaging in a work when inexpert (cf. shidurᵘ).
(? spelling and gend.) the widgeon, Mareca penelope (L. 129).

f. anxiety, apprehension, alarm (e.g. due to some bad omen, such as a sneeze or the like), timidity. --bōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to feel apprehension (even when graciously treated, and amid one's intimate friends and relations), to be suspicious. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to feel anxiety (due to some bad omen or the like). --rōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. anxiety to remain (in spite, e.g., of an evil omen not having been immediately fulfilled).
f. ruffianly conduct, bullying habits, blackguardism. Cf. shigun.
f. the conduct of a bully (see shigun).
adj. (f. shigüñᵘ̈) a ruffian, bully, blackguard. Cf. shĕgôlᵘ.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. shigᵃnyōv), to be jealous (of another) (Gr.Gr. lxxvi). Probably a variant of shẹ̆gᵃnāwun, q.v.

m. (sg. dat. shikᵃmas), the belly, stomach (cf. nau-shᵒ, p. 656a, l. 23) (El.; Rām. 157; H. x, 7; K.Pr. 225); met. the womb (Rām. 1386, 1523); met. the inward parts, the heart (Rām. 1516, dar sh˚, in the inmost heart). ¶ shikᵃma-gŏ̈bᵃ f. 'belly-heavy', a pregnant female, esp. when approaching the time of delivery. -phoṭᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. -phüṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), 'burst from the belly', a begotten (as contrasted with an adopted) son, or (f.) daughter.
m. one who breaks, crushes, overthrows (cf. buth-shᵒ, p. 141a, l. 24).
m. hunting, the chase (El.; Gr.M.; W. 114; Rām. 767; K. 992; H. ii, 4, 8; viii, 7); prey, game (El.; Rām. 1270, 1301; K.Pr. 65, 237, 263). --karun -- m.inf. to hunt (El.).

m. breakage, fracture; defeat, rout; (in Ksh.) reduction to poverty, destitution, indigence. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give poverty (to), to reduce to poverty; to defeat an armed opponent and deprive him of his entire possessions, so that he has to flee the country. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. (in a quarrel, gambling, or the like) to be defeated, ruined, and brought to contempt. -küṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kacĕ), 'a daughter of destitution', a woman in great distress, a woman overwhelmed by misfortune (Rām. 1319). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. poverty to fall upon a person.

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. shikasladiñ), in a condition of extreme indigence, unlucky, unfortunate (El.); (of an animal, e.g. a horse, a thing, or a place, etc.) one which reduces to indigence, unlucky, that which impoverishes.
m. i.q. shikas, q.v. defeat; weakness, debility (H. v, 5); absolute dejection, reduction to sore straits, a condition of calamity (Rām. 346).
adj. c.g. broken; defeated, routed; reduced to straits; bankrupt; sick, weak, wounded, infirm; broken-hearted (K.Pr. 196).
f. a crest, topknot, lock of hair on the crown of the head; a top, summit, peak (cf. barg-shᵒ, p. 120a, l. 47) (Śiv. 1163); a crest, plume, diadem. Cf. shikhāh and shākhā.
f. a crest, topknot; a lock of hair on the crown of the head; a crest, plume, diadem. Cf. shikhā and shākhā.
or shikhürᵘ̈ f. an old, ragged, worn out garment or the like (cf. dajĕ- shᵒ, p. 203a, l. 44; lō̃gi-shᵒ, p. 512a, l. 9; paizār- shᵒ, p. 820b, l. 37).
m. a hunter, sportsman, fowler, angler (Gr.M., L. 256). -bāy f. his wife.

f. a kind of light swift sailing-boat (El. shikárí; L. 381 shikára; Śiv. shikārĕ-kĕth, in a boat, 245). ¶ shikārĕ-ḍokhᵘ m. the mat roof of this boat. -ḍamb m. the hold of such a boat. -hönzᵘ̈ m. (f. -hānzañ, means both 'a woman who acts as a boatman' and 'a boatman's wife'), the boatman of this boat. -pash m. the high sides including the elevated bow of this boat; the boards used for this purpose.

m. good disposition or nature, right conduct, propriety, amiability, good behaviour (L.V. 24). --rachun -- m.inf. to maintain good behaviour, to live a good life. ¶ shīla-rostᵘ  adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), devoid of good behaviour. -raʦhar m. absence, or want, of good behaviour. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), full of good conduct, well conducted.
(? spelling) m. Chrysopogon glaucoptis (El.). According to El. the sieves used in paper making are made of the stems of this plant.

or shumshān m. the place where Hindū corpses are burnt, a burning ground (Gr.Gr. 165, shimshān; Śiv. 90, id.). shumshāna-bal m. a burning ground, the locality in which a burning ground is situated (Gr.Gr. 165, shimshāna-bal). -börav m. the tutelary deity or Bhairava (cf. börav) of a burning ground.
in shin-nö m. the name used in schools for the Śāradā form of the numeral figure 6.

m. snow (cf. chotᵘ shīn hyuhᵘ, p. 166a, l. 37; nav shīn khārun, p. 664b, l. 36; nav shīn khasun, ib. l. 39; pā̃-shᵒ, p. 748a, l. 8), (Gr.Gr. 14; Gr.M.; L. 464, shin; W. 139; Śiv. 349, 590, 1234, 1256, 1259, 1261, 1301, 1463, 1538, 1540; Rām. 1089, 1459; K.Pr. 130, 196, 254); cf. shöñᵘ̈. --trāwun -- m.inf. to clear away snow (off the roofs) (cf. pashĕ-pĕṭhⁱ shᵒ trᵒ, p. 777b, l. 8) (K.Pr. 167). --wālun -- m.inf. to throw down piled up snow (from a roof or the like) (Śiv. 1245); '(rain) to bring down snow,' sleet to fall. (It will be observed that snow is not represented as 'falling', wasun, but as being brought or thrown down) (Śiv. 1233, Rām. 863). ¶ shīna-gāsh m. the sheen of snow (as seen on a dark night). -möñᵘ̈ f. a snow-drift, a pile of snow on an elevated place, such as the top of a mountain (Śiv. 1301, 1308; Rām. 1579). -pī˜pī˜ or -pīpiñ or pī˜piñ f. a kind of small bird (the cry of which is supposed to indicate the approach of winter snow); cf. pī˜piñ. -pörᵘ̈ f. a hole or hollow used as a refuge or shelter in mountainous or other wild country during a snowstorm. -pĕwan m. a time of snowfall, an occasion on which snow falls. -raza f.pl. a heavy continuous fall of snow, a snowstorm. -thŏsⁱ m.pl. a pile of lumps of snow, or of snow congealed in lumps. -ṭulᵘ m. a hard lump of compressed snow, a snowball. -ʦhaṭh f. (sg. dat. -ʦhaṭi), a cold blast coming from the snow mountains, a freezing wind, a blizzard (Rām. 206). -wālanay f. the throwing down of snow (from the roofs of a house), clearing off snow (from the roofs). -wālay f. a snowfall; an occasion on which snow falls. -wôñᵘ m. snow-water, water the result of melting snow (Gr.Gr. 73).

(sometimes written shiñᵘ̈, shᵘ̈ñᵘ̈, and shṻñ) m. emptiness, a vacuum, void, blank; air (El. shinyi, f.); an empty space (e.g. a place, a house, or the like) (Śiv. 1599, 1600, 1603, 1619, 1700, 1867); the numerical figure 0, a cipher; met. that which causes emptiness, i.e. utter destruction; poverty (cf. örⁱ-shiñⁱ, p. 44b, l. 33; körⁱ-shiñⁱ, p. 467a, l. 14); (in Śaiva philosophy) the transcendental Void, the last stage of limited consciousness before the soul becomes conscious of universal experience as one with Supreme (L.V. 1, 11, 30, 69). shiñā, shiñāh, shᵘ̈ñāh, or shṻñāh m. (i.e. shiñ with the suff. of the indef. art.) a void, blank, mere emptiness, a mere nothing (L.V. 11, 30, 69); a void waste (due to devastation and utter destruction) (El. shinya f., a desert, and adj., desolate; Rām. 783, 844). shiñā gaʦhun m.inf. total or utter destruction of one's entire property to occur.
or shĕnās شناس adj. c.g. understanding, knowing, acquainted with (cf. lāl-shᵒ, p. 522a, l. 26) (K.Pr. 123).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. shināyiladiñ), one who is utterly crushed and driven to distraction by the destruction or devastation of his entire family and property.
adj. c.g. of the colour of vermilion, crimson (L. 459).

f. utter destruction, devastation (e.g. of the entire ripe crop of a field, of the accumulated results of work, or the like); cf. shiñ. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such devastation or destruction to occur. --mŏgul -- m. 'a destruction Mogul,' i.e. sudden entire destruction of the entire laboriously-acquired earnings of one's lifetime.

adj. (f. shīnüvᵘ̈), made of snow, composed of snow. --sᵃh hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. --sᵃh hishᵘ̈ --), like a lion made of snow; met. one outwardly very haughty and ill-mannered, but really of a mild and gentle nature.

m. milk (W. 155; K.Pr. 180, 197); medicine (El.). -gujorᵘ m. a man of the Gūjur tribe, whose profession is to sell milk (L. 358). -khār شیر خوار m. a suckling, an infant, a babe (Rām. 1035, 1336). -māl شیر مال f. (sg. dat. -māli), a kind of cake made of wheaten flour, butter and spices, also called shri-māl, see p. 888b, l. 35.

m. juice (of nuts or fruit) (cf. badām-shᵒ, p. 86b, l. 22; bangi-shᵒ, p. 113a, l. 12; dönᵘ̈-shᵘ̈, p. 223b, l. 14; munka-shᵒ, p. 580a, l. 38); sap; syrup; new wine; must. --aʦun --  m.inf. 'the juice to enter', a flavour to be experienced; (after having once tasted or experienced something) to be filled with longing for the taste or experience again.
f. a sweetmeat, sweets; esp. cardamoms coated with sugar, comfits; cf. shīrīn 2. shiriñĕ-pholᵘ m. a single comfit; a collection or quantity of comfits.
adj. c.g. sweet (cf. bādām-shᵒ, p. 86b, l. 25) (L. 458). Cf. shiriñ 1.

f. a whistle (formed with the lips), whistling (Gr.M.). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to whistle. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a whistle to occur, to be warned or informed by the sound of a whistle. --wāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to whistle (Gr.M.).
(? spelling) m. the mat cover of a boat (El.). I.q. pash.
f. of shūrᵘ or shyūrᵘ, see shyūrᵘ and shērun.
adj. c.g. milky, see shīrⁱ cāhⁱ, p. 158a, l. 2. Cf. L. 254, K.Pr. 39.
adj. c.g. craving, eager, avid, agog (esp. of a child incited by its parents).
f. the mass of solid muscle connecting the ribs, and close to the backbone.

(for 3, see shūsh) m. glass (Gr.M., K. 757); glass-ware; a glass bottle or jar (cf. nāsti-shᵒ, p. 659a, l. 14) (Gr.M.; Rām. 513, 677); a looking-glass, mirror, pier-glass, etc. (El. shíshí; Rām. 199, 1611). ¶ shīshĕ-bọ̆ngᵃr f. a glass bangle or bracelet (El. shishí). -bāwȧṭⁱ m.pl. a set of glass armlets (see bāwoṭᵘ). -dörᵘ̈ f. a glazed side-door or window. -gorᵘ m. a bottle-maker (El. shishigar). -khünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -khanjĕ), a piece or fragment of glass.

or shishur m. (sg. dat. shishiras or shishĕras), the cold season (lasting two months, January 15 to March 15) (L. 326, shishr; Śiv. 338); cold weather, extreme cold (Śiv. 342). --lagun -- m.inf. cold to attack (a person), to become frozen, to become frost-bitten. --lāgun -- m.inf. to apply (the amulet of) the cold weather; to apply a certain amulet to keep a person cool, i.e. to apply an amulet to the head of a newly-born child or of a newly-married daughter-in-law to ward off attacks of demons (whose home is the snowy mountains, and who cause convulsions, hysterics, and the like); the festival on this occasion (usually held in the cold month of Pŏh (December-January)). --marun -- m.inf. to carry out this festival. ¶ shishĕr-bôgᵘ m. the present made to her by the parents and relations of the newly-married bride on the occasion of the above festival. -gôrᵘ m. the amulet fixed on the occasion of this festival. It is shaped like a water-chestnut and is filled with mustard and other ingredients (see gôrᵘ 1). -gö̃ṭhᵘ̈ f. an icicle (El. shishirgánṭ; L. 461, shishr-gánt; Śiv. 335). -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. the amulet referred to ab. -mās m. a month of the cold season. -sö̃krānth f. the festival when the sun enters the sign Makar, or Capricorn, in the cold month of Māg (January-February).
m. N. of the king of Cēdi, who was slain by Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) (Śiv. 710, 1674; K. 640, 647 ff, 1051 ff. (his death)).
or shitüjᵘ̈ f. a small pustule or pock (like that of smallpox, but smaller) which covers the body in large numbers, as in that disease, ? chicken-pox. Cf. shitạlⁱ.
adj. c.g. cold, gelid, frigid, chilly (El. shatíl, apparently a misprint); cool (lit. or fig.) (Śiv. 537, 740, 1870; Rām. 1728). Cf. shītolᵘ.

m.pl. smallpox (El. shitil, shitilyí; K.Pr. 76). -ākh m. (sg. dat. -ākhas), a smallpox scar, smallpox pit or mark, a pock. --buḍᵘ̈ -- f. 'a smallpox old woman', a violent and severe attack of smallpox. -mŏgul m. 'a smallpox Mogul', a terrible attack of smallpox, such as one that kills the sufferer or eats away the features of the face. -musurᵘ adj. (f. -musᵘ̈rᵘ̈), marked with smallpox scars, pitted with smallpox, pock-marked.
or shutarikh f. (sg. dat. shi(u)tarikhi ), the name of the letter ya when it is the latter part of a conjunct consonant in the Śārada character (cf. rᵃkh, of which this is a compound).
m. cold, the cold season in the following:-- shīta-kāl m. the cold season, the cold winter time. -kölⁱ adv. in the cold season. -kālukᵘ adj. gen. (f. -kālücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the cold season.

card. (pl. dat. shītan), eighty (Gr.Gr. 79, Rām. 1070). --waʦan -- m.pl. a collection of old rags, an old worn-out garment of which only a few rags are left. ¶ shītan-hondᵘ adj. pl. gen. (f. hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, eighty; costing eighty (rupees, etc.) or earning eighty (rupees, etc.) as wages.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. shiṭhyōv), to become congealed, to coagulate, become frozen thick or solid; (of some slight virtue or fault) to become strengthened (by being practised), (of time) to become long (by delay), and so on; cf. shriṭhun. shiṭhyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shiṭhyē-müʦᵘ̈), congealed; strengthened, as ab.
adj. (f. shīṭhiñᵘ̈), costing sixty (rupees, etc.), worth sixty (Gr.Gr. 148).

f. (sg. dat. shīṭhᵃhüñᵃ), improper conduct (on the part of one whose conduct is habitually proper), departure from proper conduct (e.g. by ceasing to support one's servants, or to make gifts to petitioners).
card. m. pl. the multiplicative form of shēṭh 2, sixty, as in kāh shīṭhⁱ shĕ hath ta shēṭh, eleven sixties (are) six hundred and sixty (Gr.Gr. 86).
adj. (f. shītüjᵘ̈), very cold, glacial, frigid, freezing. Cf. shītal.
tight tying, as in a tourniquet, or too tight tying of a load, strangling; a kind of obstinate beggar (cf. shutrā). -band m. strangling, tying a tourniquet, etc., as ab.
adj. (f.shītiñᵘ̈), costing, or worth, eighty (rupees, etc.); earning (wages or the like amounting to) eighty (rupees, etc.).
card. m.pl. a group of eighty, an eighty; the form taken by shīth 2, eighty, as a multiplicative, as in kāh shītⁱ aiṭh hath ta shīth, eleven eighties (are) eight hundred and eighty (Gr.Gr. 86).

m. N. of the third god of the Hindū triad, in Skt. Śiva (cf. parama-shᵒ, p. 760a, l. 18) (L.V. 8, 14, 51-4, 8, 68, 80; Śiv. 437, 490, 506, 510, 528, et passim; Rām. 11, 117, 591-2, 609, 611, 616, 938, 940; K. 344, 792-3, 827). ¶ shiwa-jī m. i.q. shiv (Śiv. 40, 79, 116, 119, 121, 190, et passim; Rām. 50, 51, 61, 1527; K. 792). -karmī m. one who performs the duties laid down in the Śaiva scriptures (Śiv. 242). -lūkh m. (sg. dat. -lūkas), the world of Śiva, the heaven of Śiva; hence, salvation, absorption in Śiva (Śiv. 674, 1297, 1887). -may adj. c.g. made up of Śiva, consisting of him (L.V. 16). -nām m. the name of Śiva (Śiv. 1113). -nāth m. i.q. Shiv (Śiv. 43, 131, 229, et passim). -nāv m. the name of Śiva (Śiv. 111, 190, 192, 423, 1908, 1910, 1912). -pūzan m. the worship of Śiva (L.V. 22). -rṻph m. (sg. dat.-rṻpas), the form of Śiva, acting in the character of Śiva (Śiv. 737, 778, 851, 975, etc.). -rāth f. (sg. dat. -röʦᵘ̈), N. of the fourteenth day of the dark half of the month of Māg (Skt. Māgha = January-February) on which a fast is observed in honour of Śiva. -shĕkhᵃth or -shĕktⁱ f. the energic power or śakti of Śiva (see shĕktⁱ) (Śiv. (shĕkhᵃth) 1315; shĕktⁱ, 39, 100, 115, 280, 507, 513, 665, etc.; K. 344); Śiva and his energic power (L.V. 2). -shĕnkar m. i.q. Shiv, esp. in his propitious aspect (Śiv. 248, 355, 384, 791, 1157). -shāstᵃr m. a scripture of the Śaiva religion (Śiv. 159, 248, 1117). --shiwa karun -- m.inf. to utter the cry of 'Śiva! Śiva!' to be utterly devoted to him (L.V. 65; cf. Rām. 1768).

f. an image (usually made of flour) of the goddess Śivā (see shiwā) offered in the worship of the Bhairavas (see börav) on the twelfth lunar day of the dark half of the month of Phāgun (February-March) and on the five following nights.
f. N. of Pārvatī, the wife of Śiva (in Skt. Śivā) (Śiv. 112, 1138, 1167).
m. a kind of floor of the upper story of a house (described as consisting of beams only without the addition of floor boards); a kind of rice, hardy and growing on a high elevation (L. 46).
m. N. of a Muslim sect (which affirms that 'Alī was the rightful Imām after Muḥammad); a follower of this sect (K.Pr. 197). Cf. alī tashīā.

m. auspiciousness, good fortune, happiness, prosperity (Śiv. 496); (in time of trouble) fortunate alleviation, tranquillity; mercy (El.). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. good fortune to happen; (in time of trouble) fortunate alleviation to be experienced. --karun -- m.inf. to experience recovery from severe illness, to become completely well. ¶ shŏba-sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), full of good fortune, producing fortunate results.

adj. c.g. auspicious, fortunate, giving happiness (Śiv. 224, 228, 238, 242, 782, 979, 1038, 1045, 1410, 1748; Rām. 38; K. 3, 55, 58, 932, 970, etc.). --dŏh -- m. a lucky day, a day on which undertakings will be successful; the date of some great festival or the like, the date on which it occurs (e.g. our 25th December or Christmas day). --kömᵘ̈ -- f. a propitious action, an action having fortunate results. --ʦaran -- m. a foot that brings prosperity (used in humble address to its owner) (Śiv. 156, 987).
m. a wooden spoon (El.). This is the same word as cō̃ca, q.v.

m. apprehension, anxiety, suspicion; news, tidings, intelligence (esp. when anxiously expected) (K. 533). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to warn a person by a sign, to arouse suspicion (in a person's mind). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take suspicion, to occupy oneself in finding out the truth of suspicion. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. suspicion to fall, to be felt, to attack (a person). --rōzun -- m.inf. suspicion to remain, to become an object of suspicion, to become suspicious.

adj. c.g. pure, clean (Gr.M.); (of intellect) clear, acute, keen (K. 599); uncorrupt, unpolluted, pure, stainless, spotless (Śiv. 162, 1019, 1742, 1752, 1850); faultless, blameless, innocent (Śiv. 182, 239, 755, 1421, 1811); cf. shọ̆dᵘ. --karun -- m.inf. to make pure (Śiv. 1056); to correct (mistakes in something written), to edit (a book or the like), to correct (proofs or the like) (Gr.M.).

m. a debauchee, a slave to intoxicating drugs, a drug-fiend, a sot (cf. bangi-shᵒ, p. 113a, l. 11; carsa-shᵒ, p. 176b, l. 19; gᵃsa-shᵃ, p. 307a, l. 26; lōda-shᵒ, p. 508b, l. 41; nāsti-shᵒ, p. 659a, l. 12; phrika-shᵒ, p. 704a, l. 15); met. intoxicated with delusion, mad (Śiv. 69); cf. Hindī shuhadā. -bükhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a sot's babblings. -tütᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the delusions or delirium of a sot (esp. when caused by craving for his accustomed drug of which he is deprived). -wān m. a place where sots congregate, e.g. an opium-den.
f. the conduct or condition of a drug-fiend, sottishness.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. shŏdyōv), to become, or be, clean, pure, unsullied, unpolluted (Gr.Gr. 173); to be, or become, faultless, blameless, innocent. shŏdyō-motᵘ perf. part. (shŏdyē-müʦᵘ̈), become clean, pure, unpolluted, etc., become faultless, blameless, free from passion, sin, and so on.

adj. (f. shö̆zᵘ̈), pure, clean (cf. atha-shᵒ, p. 62a, l. 38); uncorrupt, unpolluted (cf. hō̃ʦha-shᵒ, p. 360b, l. 21; sŏna-shọ̆dᵘ, s.v. sŏn 1); faultless, blameless, innocent (cf. mana-shᵒ, p. 572a, l. 39). Cf. shŏd 2.
m. news, intelligence (noted only in H. ii, 10).

f. rejoicing, festivity (ba-shödī بشادی, by means of festivity, in token of festival, with public rejoicing, Rām. 89, 1554); esp. the festivities at a wedding; joy, happiness (Rām. 24, K.Pr. 13). --barüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to enjoy rejoicings, i.e. to rejoice in sympathy with another's festivities or at the prospect of such (Rām. 673 ff., 1369). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to do festivity, to exhibit joy, to rejoice publicly (Rām. 89, 453, 1001, 1679). ¶ shādĕ karañĕ f.pl.inf. to make festival, hold high festivity. ¶ shādi-bôjᵘ m. (f. -bājĕñ), one who joins heart and soul in another's festivities, a sharer in rejoicing.
m.pl. marriage rejoicing, music and singing at marriages or on other festive occasions, a band of music on such occasions (Śiv. 725).

m. the green pigeon, Columba hurriola (it is said to resemble a green parrot) (Śiv. 1782) (El. shoga, a parrot, and shógah, a crow, the latter being the word in use towards Bārāmūla; L. 462, shogh, a parrot). -tutᵘ m. 'a green- pigeon long-face', a kind of joke played upon a person who has never seen the bird, and who wants to see it when it is not the season for its appearance. The joke consists in showing him something else (e.g. a green parrot) as the bird; hence, met. when a person is longing for something, as a joke to tell him untruthfully that it has come.
m. business, occupation, employment (Gr.M.); diversion, pastime, amusement (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to employ (El.).

adj. c.g. imperial, royal, regal, princely (cf. khalᵃt-ĕ-shöhī, p. 399b, l. 31; H. x, 4); as subst. f. sovereignty, reign, royalty (ö̃kar-shᵒ, p. 21b, l. 42; cashma-shᵒ, p. 177a, l. 10). --zāfrān (= شآہی زعفران) f. saffron of the first quality (L. 344, shahi záfran).
or shöjᵘ̈ 1 (for 2, see shôlᵘ 2) f. a she-jackal (cf. dimba-shᵒ, p. 218b, l. 23) (El. sháj, W. 17). Cf. shāl.

m. (sg. dat. shōkhas), desire, yearning, deep longing, predilection (for) (El. shauk, Śiv. 181); fancy, pleasure (in); happiness, possessing all that one desires (K.Pr. 198); ardour, zeal, eagerness, avidity; (as adj. c.g.) daring, bold, audacious (Rām. 826). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. ardent desire, etc., to occur. shōkh ta pŏnasondᵘ m. a formula of blessing, or auspicious compliment, uttered by female relations and friends to a mother shortly (usually on the 6th day) after the birth of a boy, on the occasion of her formal bathing. Cf. pŏnasondᵘ. ¶ shōkha anun m.inf. to induce (a person) to do any work with eagerness and energy. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. eagerly and energetically to engage in any work.

or shŏkhur (also spelt shuᵒ) m. (sg. dat. shŏkras or shukras), (in Hindū legend) N. of the preceptor of the Asuras or demons (Skt. śukra) (Śiv. 480; Rām. (shŏkhur), 954); the planet Venus (Rām. (shŏkhur) 421, 1278; K. (shŏkr) 131); semen virile (in this sense shọ̆khᵃr). Cf. shọ̆kᵃrwār. ¶ shukra-pölikh f. (sg. dat. -pöliki), 'Śukra's palankeen', N. of a child's game, in which one boy rides on another's shoulders (K. 221).
m. paper (El. According to El., this is a Ladakhī word. Cf. Ladakhī shokskhang, a sheet of paper).
m. Friday (El. shukharwár; W. 106, shukarwār). Cf. shọ̆khᵃr.
m. a certain dish consisting of rice, flesh, and condiments (El.).

f. flame, blaze, light, flash (Śiv. 166, 1047); fire, energy (K. 984). --diñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to shine out in all directions, to shine forth (K. 926, 1007). ¶ shölⁱ-tārukh m. (sg. dat. -tārakas), (showing) a star in bright (day) light, or in fierce sunlight; met. to cause (a person) to imagine (the existence of) something non-existent.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. shōlanôwᵘ), to cause to shine; to make famous; to publish, make public, make generally known; cf. shōlawun. shōlanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shōlanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), published, made widely known.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shōlowᵘ), to publish, make public, make generally known; cf. shōlanāwun. shōlowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shōlüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), published, etc., as ab.
n.ag. (f. shōlavüñᵘ̈), shining, beaming, glowing, glistening.
(? spelling and gend.) N. of a certain medicinal herb, used for bringing boils to a head, Salvia sp. (L. 75).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. shōlyōv), to shine, beam, glow, glisten, glare, be bright (H. vi, 6).

m. a certain grain, a certain panic or millet, panicum italicum (El. shól and shálí; Gr.Gr. 12; L. 330, 337, setaria italica; Śiv. 1020; Rām. 1504; K.Pr. 193). shölⁱ-pāy m. a road cut up by numerous artificial water-channels, and hence uneven and not easily passable. -tū̃j f. the tiny grain of this millet. -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), a porridge made of this millet.
adj. (f. shöjᵘ̈), used --˚, endowed with, possessed of, possessing (Śiv. 1844, tīza-sh˚).
adj. (f. shümᵘ̈), calm, naturally tranquil-minded (of a human being); tranquil, undisturbed, calm, quiet (of mind, conduct, or the like).
adj. (f. shömᵘ̈), dark blue, dark brown, swarthy, nut-brown; cf. shām 3. shāmi-ranga adj. c.g. of a dark complexion or colour, brown, nut-brown. Cf. shāma-rȧngⁱ, l. 20 ab.

adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, Syria, Syrian; as subst. m. a kind of kabāb made of cakes of pounded meat cooked with clarified butter and spices. --ʦakul -- m. one of the round cakes of pounded meat in this dish.
m. a canopy, an awning on poles.
m. the tinkling sound of anklets; a sound like that made by anklets. shŏñ-shĕraph f. (sg. dat. -shĕrapi), a harlot, a dancing-girl who practises prostitution.
adj. c.g. (of anklets or the like) giving forth a tinkling sound (K. 147, 184).
f. sleep. --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to go to sleep, to sleep; met. to neglect urgent work (so as to delay it).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shŏnganôwᵘ), to cause to lie down, put to sleep. According to W. 65 this is a causal of shŏngun, as well as sāwun, q.v.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. shọ̆ngᵘ, f. shö̆njᵘ̈. The causal of this verb is sāwun, q.v.; Gr.Gr. 176; also shŏnganāwun, W. 65) to lie down, recline (Gr.Gr. 125); to go to sleep (Gr.Gr. 176, 204; L. 456; Śiv. 753; H. x, 7; K. 592); met. to die (L. 456); to sleep (Gr.Gr. 125; Gr.M.; L. 464; Śiv. 1718; K. 607; YZ. 118; K.Pr. 25, 95). ¶ shọ̆ngᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shö̆njᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), lain down to sleep (Śiv. 1029); asleep. ¶ shŏngith conj. part. having lain down to sleep; hence (as adj.) asleep (Śiv. 1631; Rām. 339, 486; K. 598; H. viii, 7; YZ. 79). --shāph rōzun -- m.inf. 'a curse to remain asleep' (i.e. in any virtuous act) expected or likely impediments not to occur.

m. (sg. dat. shọ̆ngᵃrapas), cinnabar, vermilion, red sulphuret of mercury. shọ̆ngᵃrapa-tham hyuhᵘ adj. (f. --hishᵘ̈ --), like a pillar of vermilion; met. glowing-faced, with glowing or ruddy countenance.
m. the N. of the city of the demon Bān (Bāṇa) (in Skt. Śōṇitapura) (K. 790, 818).
adj. (f. shönʦᵘ̈), calmed, calm, quiet, undisturbed, tranquil; virtuous, good, honest, devout, pious (El. shŏnt, shónt, shunt).
f. (sg. dat. shönʦᵃrüñᵃ), the act of appeasing, allaying, alleviating, calming; extinguishing (a fire).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shönʦᵃrôwᵃ) i.q. shönʦᵃrun, q.v. (cf. nār shᵒ, p. 647a, l. 19). shönʦᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. shönʦᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. shönʦᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, q.v. s.v. shönʦᵃrun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. shönʦᵒrᵒ), to appease, allay, alleviate, calm (strife, rage, agitation, enmity, pain, or the like); to extinguish (fire) (cf. nār shᵒ, p. 647a, l. 19); to render lifeless or helpless (by taking away life, wealth, etc.). shönʦᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. shönʦᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), appeased, calmed (by someone); extinguished (by someone); rendered helpless or lifeless (by someone).
f. a heavy shower of rain accompanied by snow, sleet (Śiv. 1309). Cf. shīn.

m. equality of condition, succeeding another in exactly the same position, successorship, the condition of an inheritor (cf. potᵘ-shᵘ, p. 788a, l. 2). ¶ shĕphⁱ-dar m. (f. -dariñ), one who accepts another position; hence, a close friend (a sympathetic neighbour, helping in prosperity and sorrow, affectionate, and so on); a helper, an ally (with the above characteristics). ¶ shĕphi yunᵘ m.inf. to come in help, to come to a person's assistance.
adj. c.g. that which causes a curse (e.g. something contact with which, or an action which is liable to bring down a curse), banned under a curse.
m. the noise of the fall of a stream of water, a splash. shŏr shŏr m. the continuous patter or splashing of a falling stream of water.

m. cry, noise, outcry, din, clamour, uproar (cf. nạzla-shᵒ, p. 675b, l. 30) (Rām. 281, 819, 1331, 1722); general outcry, disturbance due to a public calamity, to an attack, to onslaught, or the like. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat a roar, to be roared at (Rām. 1780). --khyāwun -- m.inf. to cause (a person) to eat, i.e. experience, a roar, to roar at a person (Rām. 828). --karun -- m.inf. to make a noise, create an uproar (Śiv. 1638). --tulun -- m.inf., id. --wŏthun -- m.inf. an outcry, uproar, to arise (Rām. 404, 693, 740, 1761). ¶ shōra-gāh (= شورگاہ) m. a place of outcry; hence, an outcry (H. vi, 12, 13).
shēr 1, or shĕr 3 in mraga-shĕr, etc., see p. 590b, l. 6.

m. saltpetre (YZ. 394); gun- powder (L. 462). -gorᵘ m. (his wife is shōra-gȧrⁱ-bāy), a saltpetre-maker, a gunpowder-maker. -më̆ʦᵘ̈ f. earth abounding in salt, brackish soil. -ṭās m. the bang of an explosion of saltpetre (i.e. of gunpowder or a similar compound used as an explosive in mining or the like).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shōranôwᵘ), to make a loud confused noise, to twang loudly (Rām. 123).
adj. c.g. brackish, saline (Gr.M.); (of land) barren (esp. owing to saltpetre efflorescence) (Gr.M.). Cf. shōra.
adj. (f. shörᵘ̈ 1), squint-eyed. shörⁱ-kônⁱ adj. (f. -köñᵘ̈), so squint-eyed as to be practically monocular.
f. a woman who is clear-headed, sagacious, discerning, sapient (e.g. in speaking, in hearing, in learning, or in teaching).

or shöshᵘ̈ f. gasping, panting, breathlessness, puffing and blowing (cf. āma-shᵒ, p. 27a, l. 3) (El. sháṅsh); cf. shāh 2, of which it is a fem. form. --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. panting to mount, to lose one's breath, to gasp, pant. ¶ shāshĕ-rāy f. stoppage of breathing, want of breath, exhaustion from this cause.
m. one who is versed in holy writ or in philosophy (cf. darma-shᵒ, p. 244b, l. 50); (or adj.) dealing, or concerned with, holy writ, etc.

c.g. (sg. dat. shōṭhas), a certain person or thing not named, but indicated by a gesture; so-and-so, such-and-such, as in such shōṭh gaʦhi, that person (not named, but pointed at) will go; ʦĕ shōṭhas wonun, he spoke to you (not named, but pointed at); mĕ shōṭhas wȧnⁱzi, please speak to me (not named, but pointed at).

m. (sg. dat. shō̃ṭhas), dry ginger, ginger (K.Pr. shōṅṭ). -ganḍᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a root of ginger, a single lump of ginger. -trēsh f. ginger-water-drink, boiled water in which ginger is soaked (used as a beverage, and as a potion in colds, fevers, etc.). -wôñᵘ m. water in which powdered ginger is soaked, or boiling water to which a little ginger is added, given to a lying-woman as a drink. -worᵘ m. a ginger cake; a certain dish spiced with ginger.
adj. (f. shüʦᵘ̈), used --˚, of, or belonging to, (so many) hundred (cf. aiṭha-shᵒ, p. 66b, l. 38; nawa-shᵒ, p. 664a, l. 45; pönʦa-shᵒ, p. 743a, l. 45; shĕth-shĕtⁱ, p. 899a, l. 30.
m. an Indian club, an athlete's club (for exercising the muscles).

or shōy شوئی m. or f. a slight washing, e.g. washing a little dirt off a garment or from a vessel, or washing a part of the body (cf. pã̄-shŏy, p. 748a, l. 9). --kaḍun -- or --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- m. or f. inf. to wash, as ab. --trāwun -- or --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- m. or f. inf., id.
m. a poet (Gr.M. shöir); a minstrel (L. 462).
m. cleanness, cleanliness (cf. atha-shᵒ, p. 62b, l. 5); purity, ceremonial purity, freedom from pollution; blamelessness, faultlessness.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shọ̆zᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. shọ̆zᵃrun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 173, Gr.M., Śiv. 1477). shọ̆zᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (shọ̆zᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. shọ̆zᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, s.v. shọ̆zᵃrun, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shọ̆zᵒrᵒ), to clean, cleanse, purify; hence, to make better, improve (Gr.M. shọ̆zᵃrāwun, so Śiv. 1477). shọ̆zᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (shọ̆zᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), cleansed, purified.
m. the condition of being pure, cleanness, purity, the condition of being undefiled; the becoming pure, clean, etc.; the ceremonial cleansing of parts of the body. Cf. shrōʦar.

m. (sg. dat. shōʦas), cleaning, cleansing, purifying (parts of the body, clothes, etc.); esp. purification after micturation or voiding excrement; purity, the condition of not being defiled; hence, pure (i.e. undefiled) food (H. x, 3). Cf. shrōʦh and shrōʦun.

m. a Śrāddha or obsequial rite in honour of the departed spirits of deceased relations, and observed at certain fixed periods (cf. dīpa-shᵒ, p. 232b, l.37; kö̃bari-shᵒ, p. 382b, l. 21; nūna-shᵒ, p. 641a, l. 12; nāñĕ-shᵒ, p. 644a, l. 25; nawa-shᵒ, p. 664a, l. 40) (L. 263, 266, sharadh; Rām. 308). --hāwun -- m.inf. to carry out this rite. --karun -- m.inf., id. (El.). ¶ shrāda-brôhmun m. a Brāhmaṇ who attends at this rite, and who, before the piṇḍas are offered to the Manes (see pĕnḍ), eats the consecrated food; N. of a certain Vedic verse. -bata m. the rice cooked before this rite for making the piṇḍas, and for the obsequial feast. -më̆ṭᵘ̈ f. a mere gobbit of a śrāddha, i.e. a śrāddha hurried through without the customary obsequial feast, etc. -phāka m. the fast observed on the day of this rite. -ʦȧrⁱ-wörⁱ f. the rice cooked, in a special cauldron, for this rite. -wôlᵘ m. the person who performs this rite.
f. trust, faith, belief; belief in divine revelation, religious faith (Śiv. 1241, 1420, 1471, 1634).

f. (sg. dat. shrāki), a large knife (such as is used as a weapon, or by butchers, or as a carving knife) (cf. shĕkar-shrᵒ, p. 878b, l. 39) (Gr.Gr. 73; L. 461 sharák; Rām. 242, 1489, 1608; H. x, 13; YZ. 146; K.Pr. 1, 27, 199, 206). --wāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to ply the knife, to wield a knife and cut all round (lit. and met., attacking, through hatred, all one's relations, neighbours, and friends, or cutting all round something). ¶ shrāka-puchᵘ or shrāka-puʦhᵘ m. a small clasp-knife, a pen-knife (El. shrákapúch; Gr.M. do.; L. 461 sharák poch). See pọ̆ʦhᵘ 1. ¶ shrāki-khünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -khanjĕ), the blade of a pen-knife. -khār m. a knife maker, a cutler. -khash m. a cut with a knife (Gr.Gr. 73). -ʦhĕnᵃr f. a worn out knife without its handle, a worn out blade of a pen-knife.

m. toil, labour (Gr.M.); weariness, fatigue, exhaustion. --aʦun -- m.inf. fatigue to come (to a person), to be fatigued, wearied, exhausted. --karun -- m.inf. to labour hard (Gr.M.). --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause fatigue to enter, to fatigue, weary, exhaust.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shramôwᵘ), to make (anything) a cause of labour, to labour at (anything) (as in dŏd shrᵒ, to labour at milk, i.e. at milking, L.V. 38).

m. bathing, ablution, immersion in water (Gr.M., K. 1155); ceremonial bathing (cf. kañĕ-shᵒ, p. 460b, l. 6) (Śiv. 756, 1170, 1889); met. being bathed in something, suffused with moisture (cf. guma-shᵒ, p. 287a, l. 20); cf. snān, srān. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to wash, bathe (another); esp. to bathe a corpse (a part of the last obsequies of a Hindū). --gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. 'bathings to happen'; hence, to be covered with sweat, to sweat, or perspire, profusely. --karun -- m.inf. to bathe oneself, to bathe (Gr.M.; Śiv. 239, 927, 1162, 1172, 1177, 1496, 1826; Rām. 305); to do bathing (to someone, dat.), to give a bath to (e.g. a child) (K. 942). --karanāwun -- m.inf. to cause (a person, dat.) to bathe, to bathe (a person) (Śiv. 1309, 1315). -sŏndar f. a bathing festival; e.g. the ceremonial (first) bathing of a woman after childbirth (usually on the sixth day after the birth); a festival in honour of the goddess Ṣaṣṭhī (a form of Durgā). ¶ shrāna-dēg f. a washing basin, a bathing basin; the basin for the water with which a corpse is bathed in the course of funeral obsequies. -gorᵘ m. a bathing man; a man who washes or bathes a helpless invalid; the man who bathes the corpse of a man as ab. -gürᵘ̈ f. a bathing woman; a woman who washes or bathes a helpless invalid woman; the woman who bathes the corpse of a woman as ab. -kuṭhᵘ m. a bathing hut, a hut on the bank of a river for private bathing. -püṭᵘ̈ f. the board on which a corpse is placed for bathing as ab. -paṭh m. (sg. dat. -paṭas), a piece of cloth worn round the privities in bathing, a bathing dress. -wôñᵘ m. bathing-water; the water with which a corpse is bathed; water which has been used for washing generally, dirty bath-water.
f. the fee paid to the person who washes a corpse.

or (q.v.) sranḍa m. a bull set at liberty (as an act of piety, and allowed to wander about at will), a Brahminy bull; met. a fat, corpulent, strapping fellow. -har f. a fight between such bulls; a fight between two strapping fellows.
or (qq.v.) sāñĕr, srāñĕr m. moisture; succulency, greenness, juiciness; (of a story) softness, tenderness.
m. a horn; the top, peak, summit of a mountain; the head man or leading person in a village or the like.
m. the sentiment of love or sexual passion, the erotic sentiment; dress, toilet, ornament, decoration, embellishment.
adj. c.g. one who excites love, attractive, seductive, captivating, fascinating, bewitching.
or (q.v.) sranz m. a blacksmith's tongs (H. xi, 16).
conj. 1. (1 p.p. shrapanôwᵘ), i.q. shrạpᵃrun, q.v., see Gr.Gr. 174.
f. (sg. dat. shrapüʦᵘ̈), the power of quick digestion; the quality of being quickly digested, (of food) digestibility; fading away, wasting away, decay (Gr.Gr. 128).
n.ag. (f. shrapavüñᵘ̈), (food) easily digestible, quickly digested; that which is being approved after full consideration.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. shropᵘ), to be digested (cf. phĕkĕn-hondᵘ shrapun phyārĕñ, p. 721a, l. 11) (Gr.Gr. 174, 204-5; Śiv. 1121; K.Pr. 171, 222, (sharpi for shrapi) 225); to have an appetite (L. 458); to be evaporated, to evaporate, disappear by evaporation (Gr.Gr. 204); to be soaked up (Gr.Gr. 204); (of some thin liquid) to be boiled down to thickness; (of an opinion or the like) to be digested, to be thoroughly considered and agreed to; to fade (from the memory); to waste away, fade away; to decay (Gr.Gr. 128). [The causal of this verb is shrạpᵃrun, shrạpᵃrāwun, or shrapanāwun, qq.v., Gr.Gr. 174. Its 3 p.p. is optionally shrapyāv or shrapiyāv, Gr.Gr. 205.] ¶ shrȧpⁱ shrȧpⁱ gaʦhun gradually to be evaporated, (of falling rain or other water) to disappear as fast as it falls; met. (of a story or the like) to disappear from the memory while it is being spoken. ¶ shropᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shrüpᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), digested; evaporated; soaked up (e.g. rain falling on the ground); boiled down; approved after due consideration.
f. (sg. dat. shrạpᵃrüñᵃ), the causing to be digested; boiling down, evaporation (tr.); causing to disappear, waste away (property, esp. another's); letting (something) fade from the memory.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shrạpᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. shrạpᵃrun, q.v. shrạpᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. shrạpᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. shrạpᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, q.v. ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. shrạpᵒrᵒ), to cause to be digested (Śiv. 306); to boil down; to evaporate (tr.); to cause (one's own or another's property) to disappear, esp. gradually to waste or misappropriate (another's property); to let something fade from the memory. shrạpᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. shrạpᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to be digested, etc., as ab.
m. a small hole, a pin-hole (such as those bored for an earring or the like, or appearing in a dish, etc.). Cf. srav.
m. hearing, listening; esp. the attentive listening to the reading of ancient histories, sacred texts, or the like (Śiv. 1001, 1205, 1792).
n.ag. (f. shrawavünᵘ̈), that which oozes, drips; (of a vessel) leaking. Cf. srawawunᵘ.
m. (sg. dat. shrāwakas), a kind of small earthen dish, such as a saucer or similar vessel.

m. (sg. dat. shrāwanas), N. of the fourth Hindū luni-solar month, in Skt. Śrāvaṇa, equivalent to July-August (Śiv. 327, 1540; Rām. 172; YZ. 553; K.Pr.128). ¶ shrāwạna-punimᵘ̈ f. the day of the full moon of the month of Śrāvaṇa, on which day Hindūs worship Śiva. ¶ shrāwȧnⁱ adv. in the month of Śrāvaṇa.
m. (sg. dat. shrawanas), N. of a certain constellation of three stars, one of the lunar asterisms or mansions, in Skt. Śravaṇa.
conj. 2 (1 p.p. shrowᵘ), to drip, ooze, drop forth; cf. srawun. shrowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shrüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), dripped, oozed forth.
in shri-dŏh m. a holiday, a feast day (such as New Year's day, the Śiva-rātri, etc.); cf. shrī. shri-māl f. a kind of cake, the same as shīr-māl, q.v., p. 889b, l. 14.

f. wealth, riches, affluence; N. of Lakṣmī, the wife and energic power of Vishnu (Viṣṇu) (Skt. śrī). ¶ This word is often used as an honorific prefix to the names of deities and eminent human beings. Thus, shrī-bagawān, Śiv. 194, 237, 1332; Rām. 1143l; K. 338, 480, 880; shrī-gangādar, Śiv. 45; shrī-har, Śiv. 210, 243, and so on passim; shrī-krushn, K. 174, 239, 406, 561, etc.; shrī-rām, Rām. 1724; shrī-vyāsa, K. 1038. ¶ shrī-nagar m. Śrīnagar, the capital of Kashmīr (see RT.Tr. II, 439 ff.).
m. N. of a boy friend of Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) (Skt. Śrīdāman) (K. 223, 253).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. shriṭhyōv), to become congealed, to coagulate, become frozen thick or solid, to become numb with cold (Gr.M.); cf. shiṭhun. shriṭhyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shriṭhyē-müʦᵘ̈), congealed, etc.
m. the condition of being not divided, not cut up, unbrokenness, completeness in all parts, entireness, wholeness (e.g. of a fruit or the like). Cf. shrū̃ṭᵘ.
or shrukañĕ f.pl. pouring forth torrents of tears, weeping excessively (Gr.Gr. 118). shrŏ(shru)kañĕn aʦun  m.inf. to enter weepings, to begin silent weepings.
n.ag. (f. shrŏkavüñᵘ̈), one who weeps excessively (esp. for some small reason), a cry-baby.
n.ag. (f. as in 1) one who, or that which, becomes compressed, contracted, squeezed up, crushed up, becoming shrivelled.
or shrukun 1 conj. 1 (1 p.p. shrọ̆kᵘ; 2 p.p. shrŏcyōv. This verb is impersonal) to cry, weep, whimper (of some timid person who weeps on very small provocation) (Gr.Gr. 118).

or shrukun 2 conj. 3 (2 p.p. shrŏ(shru)kyōv ), to be pressed hard or jammed against something, and in consequence to be put out of shape, crushed together, wrinkled, contracted. shrŏ(shru)kyō-motᵘ  perf. part. (f. shrŏ(shru)kyē-müʦᵘ̈ ), jammed out of shape, crushed up, shrivelled up.

or shrukun 3 conj. 1 (1 p.p. shrọ̆kᵘ or shrukᵘ; f. shrö̆cᵘ̈ or shrucᵘ̈; 2 p.p. shrŏ(shru)cyōv ), to force something solid into a narrow space, to squeeze in, to jam against (something); to crush, put out of shape, crease, distort, cause to contract by such jamming, to squeeze small; cf. sukun. shrukᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shrucᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), forced in, jammed in, put out of shape (by someone) as ab.
f. (sg. dat. shrọ̆kᵃrüñᵃ), the act of crushing, making out of shape, by forcing together (two things that do not fit), squeezing together, causing to contract (by squeezing), crushing up.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shrọ̆kᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. shrọ̆kᵃrun, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shrọ̆kᵒrᵒ), to distort or squeeze out of shape (by jamming something into a narrow space or against something which it does not fit, or by crookedly joining); to crush (something) up.
or (q.v.) srŏng f. a subterranean passage, a mine; a very narrow passage, lane, or the like.
or (q.v.) srônᵘ adj. (f. shröñᵘ̈), wet, moist, damp; succulent, not dry, green, juicy (cf. shrūʦᵘ shrᵒ, p. 896a, l. 27); (of a story, or the like) soft, tender. Cf. srônᵘ.
f. (sg. dat. shrö̆ʦᵘ̈), a vedic or sacred text (Śiv. 1116, 1865).
m. (sg. dat. shrŏṭas), an untrue story, romance, an imaginary or false statement made publicly. --lāyun -- m.inf. to make a false narrative.

or shôṭhᵘ m. (sg. dat. shrö(shö)ṭhis ), a dead body, a corpse. shöṭhis nakh dyunᵘ m.inf. 'to give a shoulder to a corpse', i.e. to give a helping hand to one overwhelmed by difficulty, to help one to bear a too heavy load (lit. and met.).
m. a sacrificial ladle. Cf. shrŏʦh.
m. purity, the condition of being undefiled (Gr.Gr. 142, Rām. 1065); (of food, or of the act of eating food) ceremonial purity, the condition of being free from ceremonial uncleanness. Cf. shōʦar.
m. the purificatory rite after micturation or voiding excrement (by cleansing with earth or water the privities, hands, and feet, and rinsing out the mouth). Cf. shōʦāʦār.
m. (sg. dat. shrŏʦas), a kind of ladle used for sacrificial purposes and for pouring clarified butter, etc. Cf. shrŏv.

f. (sg. dat. shrōʦi), cleansing (Gr.Gr. 125); esp. purification by cleansing the privities after micturation or voiding excrement (cf. mal-shrᵒ, p. 564a, l. 20); cf. shōʦh. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cleanse the privities as ab. (with earth, water, or the like). ¶ shrōʦi-wôñᵘ m. water used for cleansing the privities.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. shrōʦyōv, Gr.Gr. 226), to be, or become, pure, to become free from defilement (Gr.Gr. 125, 226-7; L.V. 105; Śiv. 1287; Rām. 58); cf. shōʦh. shrōʦyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shrōʦyē-müʦᵘ̈), become pure, freed from defilement.
adv. in a single breath and with noise (u.w.vbs. of swallowing and the like), with a loud gulp. Cf. shrutun.

m. (sg. dat. shrūkas), a verse in a certain Skt. metre, called anuṣṭubh (El. also shalúk); a stanza or verse in general (Śiv. 393, 800, 1115-6, 1131, 1186, 1519, 1588). shrūka-ʦōram f. (sg. dat. -ʦōrümᵘ̈), a certain festival held by Hindū students on the fourth day of the bright half of the month of Māg (Skt. Māgha = January-February) on which sacred verses are recited. The custom is said to be dying out.

m. a hard knot (in a string or the like) (El. binding, tying). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to make a hard or tight knot (e.g. in the string of a purse, or the like). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to tie tightly with a hard knot the ends of a binding string. --karun -- m.inf. to tie (El.). --lagun -- m.inf. to be, or become, very tightly tied up. --ta drukᵘ mēlun -- m.inf. (owing to a cold) the nose (and, according to Kāshmīrī belief, the other orifices of the brain) to be blocked up. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. 'to throw a knot', to tie with a hard knot a string round a neck (e.g. of a man, of a jar, or of a bag). ¶ shruka-pan m. the string used for securely tying up (a parcel, a bag, or the like).
or (q.v.) srünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. shranjĕ), a tiny box or casket (cf. sŏrma-shᵒ, s.v. sŏrman).
m. (f. shrutawöñᵘ̈), one who hears well, one who is the reverse of being deaf (L.V. 20).
m. (sg. dat. shrutas), the noise made in swallowing a liquid, a gulping sound (Gr.Gr. 15, a sip).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. shrutᵘ, f. shruʦᵘ̈; 2 p.p. shruʦōv), to drink with noise, to gulp down in one long breath; cf. shrukawun. shrutᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shruʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), drunk with a noisy gulp, gulped down.
adj. (f. shrū̃ṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. shrō̃cĕ), unbroken, whole, entire, complete.
f. (sg. dat. shrūʦᵃrüñᵃ), the act of making clean, cleansing; making free from ceremonial defilement.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shrūʦᵃrôwᵃ) i.q. shrūʦᵃrun, q.v. (Śiv. 285). shrūʦᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. shrūʦᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. shrūʦᵒrᵒ- motᵘ, q.v., s.v. shrūʦᵃrun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shrūʦᵒrᵒ), to make clean, to cleanse; to free (something or someone) from ceremonial defilement (Śiv. 285). shrūʦᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. shrūʦᵘ̈rᵘ̈), cleansed, as ab.
m. (sg. abl. shrōʦi), purity, cleanness; purification, cleansing, purifying, the operation or process of making pure (Śiv. 1471). Cf. shōʦh.

adj. (m. sg. abl. shrōʦi; f. sg. nom. shrūʦᵘ̈), pure, clean (El. also srúts, W. 88 shrūts) (Śiv. 1287, Rām. 1783); undefiled, innocent (cf. hȧtⁱ-shrⁱ, p. 356a, l. 29) (Gr.Gr. 142); religiously or ceremonially pure or undefiled (Śiv. 1042, 1071). --karun -- m.inf. to clean, cleanse (El., W. 88). shrūʦᵘ shrônᵘ adj. (f. shrūʦᵘ̈ shröñᵘ̈), very pure, very clean; quite undefiled. ¶ shrōʦi-shrāni adv. in a very pure manner, undefiled. ¶ shrūʦⁱ pöṭhⁱ or --pöṭhin -- adv. in an undefiled manner.
adj. (f. shrūʦⁱyörⁱ 1), one who is pure in mind and actions (including ceremonial purity).
f. pure conduct, purity of mind and actions (Gr.Gr. 142).

or shūbā f. splendour, elegance, grace, loveliness (Śiv. (shūb) 581; (shūbā) 839, 944, 1242; K. (˚bā) 1047, (˚b) 1115); a piece of beauty, a beautiful thing (K.Pr. 17). --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring elegance (to a person, thing, or action), to render elegant, beautify, make refined. --niñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. elegance or beauty to be lost, to lose refinement. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. elegance or beauty to come, to become beautified, to become refined. ¶ shūba-wônᵘ adj. (f. shūba-wöñᵘ̈), possessing beauty, adorned (L.V. 52); cf. shūbawunᵘ. shūbi-rosᵘ or -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), wanting in beauty, inelegant, wanting in refinement; as adv. unsuitably, unfairly (u.w. vbs. of arranging, dividing, etc.). -sosᵘ or -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), full of beauty, full of elegance, refined.
(sic), conj. 1, to cause to be got ready, to cause to be prepared, to cause to be fitted (El.) ? cf. shūbᵃrāwun and shēranāwun.
n.ag. (f. shūbavüñᵘ̈), beautiful, becoming (El.; Śiv. 1198; K. 85, 984, 927; YZ. 9); worthy, suitable, fit (El.). Cf. shūba-wônᵘ (p. 869a, l. 38).
f. splendour, beauty, elegance; a good reputation (cf. dīshĕ-shᵒ, p. 253a, l. 22).
adj. c.g. splendid, beautiful; elegant, refined.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. shūbyōv), to be beautiful, elegant, refined (El.; Śiv. 436, 467, 469, 475, 985, 1016, 1048, 1255, 1626, 1663; Rām. 1685; K. 59, 219, 590, 925, 927, 929; H. ii, 4, 5; vii, 5, 10; YZ. 11); to be fit, to be proper, to suit, to be worthy (El.; W. 87, shobun; Śiv. 581, 710, 909; Rām. 354, 849, 1218; K. 640-1, 672, 907, 1040; H. xii, 4, 5; K.Pr. 246). shūbyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. shūbyē-müʦᵘ̈), become beautiful, become elegant, refined; become fit, proper, suited, become worthy.
f. (sg. dat. shūbᵃrüñᵃ), making elegant, beautifying, refining.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. shūbᵃrôwᵃ), to make elegant, to beautify, refine; to adorn; met. to adorn (a house) by a gracious visit (K. 520). shūbᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. shūbᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), (of something inelegant) made elegant, beautified, refined (by some one).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. shūbᵒrᵒ), to make elegant, beautify, make refined.
adj. c.g. become, past, gone, used in the following:-- shud gaʦhun m.inf. to be finished off, to be entirely expended, done away with.
m. a misfortune, calamity (due to one's efforts or work becoming fruitless).
adj. c.g. prudent, foreseeing, circumspect, wisely cautious.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. shūdaladiñ), overwhelmed by calamities (due to efforts or work becoming fruitless).
f. purification, purifying, cleansing, refining (of metals).
f. the conduct or condition of a drug-fiend, sottishness (cf. phrika-shᵒ, p. 704a, l. 18).
or shūdᵃr m., i.q. shidᵃr, q.v. (the Skt. form of the word) (K. 982).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. shudyōv), to be, or become, inevitable, predestined. shudyō-motᵘ perf. part. (shudyē-müʦᵘ̈), destined, predestined, that which has been inevitable.

m. an omen, augury (consulted at the beginning of any action); the beginning (of anything), commencement. Cf. shĕgūna and shĕkun. -pālun m.inf. to secure the (fulfilment of an) omen; i.e. after having consulted the omens and found them favourable, to make a formal beginning of the proposed action (e.g. to make a few steps of a proposed journey, as a beginning and to postpone the rest to a more convenient season). Cf. shĕgūna pālun.

or shuhᵘ m. ice frozen solid, solid ice; frost-bite of the feet. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. frost-bite to occur, to be frost-bitten. --karun -- m.inf. to become frozen solid (e.g. food). --lagun -- m.inf. to become frozen solid, or (of a living being) to be frozen to death. ¶ shuhⁱ-dath f. (sg. dat. -dati), a large lump or block of ice. shuhⁱ-ṭujⁱ or -ṭujᵘ̈ f. a small round ball of ice; a frost-bite.
f. fame, rumour, report (El., L. 463 shhurat).
adj. c.g. frost-bitten, suffering from frost-bite, frozen through and through.

m. N. of a certain Indian saint (Skt. Śukadēva) famous for his rigid continence. He is said to have narrated the Bhāgavata Purāṇa to King Parîkṣit. He was the son of Vyāsa, who compiled the Vēdas and who was the author of the Mahābhārata (Śiv. 1077, 1355, 1376, (shukadēwa) 1433; K. 8-11, 300, 332, 487, 1176).
m. N. of a demon (Skt. śukâsura) who was sent by Rāvan (Rāvaṇa) as a messenger to Sugrīv (Rām. 832).

m. (sg. dat. shūkas), sorrow, grief, distress, affliction (cf. pọ̆tra-shᵒ, p. 799b, l. 26) (Śiv. 1452; Rām. 1755, 1760; K. 472, 489, 535, 542, 622, 724, 855, 902, 1159). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take grief, to become overwhelmed with grief, to feel utterly miserable with grief. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. grief to fall (upon a person). ¶ shūkas gaʦhun m.inf. to go to grief, to become filled with grief (Rām. 1759).
adj. c.g. white, pure, bright; shukla-rang adj. c.g. of a white colour, pure white (Śiv. 1258).
m. thanks, gratitude (K.Pr. 199); praise (El.). -guzār شکر گذار adj. c.g. thankful (El., Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to praise (El.). --karawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --karavüñᵘ̈ --), thankful (El.).
m. a network of strings or cords to hang anything in (as food, pots, a burden at either end of a yoke or pole, etc.), a swinging shelf (K. 148, 151, 154).
m. a worn out, ragged cloth, mat or the like (cf. dastār-shᵒ, p. 256b, l. 29; lō̃gi-shᵒ, p. 512a, l. 7; phĕran-shᵒ, p. 705b, l. 28).
or shūrᵘ, in wūrᵘ-shᵘ, see p. 1138b, ll. 45, 49.
for shūm, q.v. in shum gĕv m. 'miser's ghī', i.e. old long-kept clarified butter, i.e. clarified butter buried in a jar underground and kept to ripen. It is used for the preparation of a medicine.
m. a miser, a niggard (El.). Cf. shumurᵘ.

f. counting, reckoning, numbering (bē-shᵒ, countless, H. xii, 20-1, 24); calculation, amount, number; account, note, estimation. --bōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to hear counting, to hear a roll-call, to call a roll (H. xi, 16).
f. numbering, counting, enumeration; esp. the counting (of sheep for purposes of taxation) (cf. shākh-shumörī, p. 876a, l. 48) (L. 361).
subst. m. and adj. (f. shumürᵘ̈), a miser, niggard (El. shúmir); adj. avaricious (Gr.M.). Cf. shūm.
adj. c.g. having the form of the Void, reduced to becoming nothing but the Great Void (L.V. 50). See shiñ.
m. he whose abode is the Great Void, the Supreme (L.V. 15). See shiñ.
in the phrase sọ̆gᵘ shuphᵘ ta panādār, q.v., s.v. sọ̆gᵘ. Perhaps another spelling of the preceding.

or shūpᵘ m. a winnowing-basket (woven with leather strips on a withy frame), a kind of flat basket used in winnowing grain (cf. dā̃-shᵒ, p. 231a, l. 2; kāwa-shᵒ, p. 495a, l. 33) (El. ship, shup, shyúp; Gr.Gr. 17; K.Pr. 199, 254). ¶ shupⁱ-khalⁱrⁱ f. an old worn-out winnowing-basket. -köñᵘ̈ f. the withy used for making these winnowing-baskets. -wātul m. (f. -wātᵘ̈jᵘ̈), a low-caste man who lives by making and selling winnowing-baskets (K.Pr. 231).

(by Paṇḍits also written) (for 1, see shurᵘ) card. (pl. dat. shurāhan), sixteen (Gr.Gr. 77; El. also shorah; Śiv. 711, 1353, 1438, 1467; Rām. 122, 395, 545, 885, 1087; K. 765, 778, 785, 918, 960). -yār m. N. of a tract to the east of Śrīnagar, at the foot of the Taḵẖt-i-Sulaimān, and close to the river Vĕth or Jehlam. -yāra phiravith trēshĕ-hotᵘ anun m.inf. after leading (a person) round from Shurāh-yār to bring him back thirsty; hence, for a long time to keep giving continual hopes, and finally to disappoint. ¶ shurāhan-hondᵘ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, sixteen; costing, or worth, sixteen (rupees, or the like); earning sixteen (rupees, or the like, a month, or the like). ¶ shurāhway emph. card. (pl. acc. shurāhwȧnⁱ), even the sixteen, all the sixteen (K. 960).
f. the conduct of a child, childishness (W. 112); conduct like that of a child, obstinate, ignorant, unreflecting conduct on the part of a grown-up person (cf. dŏda-shᵒ, p. 190a, l. 20).
(by Paṇḍits also written), card., m.pl. the multiplicative form of shurāh, sixteen, q.v., as in kāh shuröhⁱ akh hath ta shᵉ̆satatath, eleven sixteens (are) one hundred and seventy-six (Gr.Gr. 86).

or shūrpanakhā f. N. of a female demon, in Skt. Śūrpaṇakhā. She was sister of Rāvaṇa, and wished to marry Rāma. Rāma referred her to his brother Lakṣmaṇa, but he too refused her. She then threatened to devour Sītā, but Lakṣmaṇa cut off her ears and nose. She fled to Rāvaṇa, and, as a result of her complaint, he carried off Sītā (Śiv. 1481; Rām. 333, 338, 350, 1143g-h, 1780).
m. beginning, commencement (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to begin (Gr.M.).

m. (with suff. of indef. art. shurāh 1 (Śiv. 430, 1438); f. shurᵘ̈), an infant, baby, child (cf. dŏda-shᵒ, p. 190a, ll. 14, 16, 21) (Gr.Gr. 16, 17; Gr.M.; L. 458; W. 7, 112; L.V. 70; Śiv. 340, 430, 1388, 1393, 1438, 1445, 1464; Rām. 510, 807, 1249, 1653; K. 37, 40, 87, 105-6, 127, 153, 179, 182, 185, 194, 196, 200-1, etc.; K.Pr. 61, 131, 165, 199, 231, 260); a male child, a little boy (f. shurᵘ̈, a little girl, El. shurí) (cf. shāpa-shᵒ, p. 888a, l. 18) (Gr.Gr. 163; Rām. 1363, 1438, 1566, 1594-5; K.Pr. 261). --koṭᵘ -- m. children, the children of a family as a whole. ¶ shurⁱ-bọ̆chⁱ adj. (f. -bö̆chᵘ̈), (of a childless person) hungry for a child, longing to have offspring. -bŏd f. (sg. dat. -bö̆zᵘ̈), a child's intelligence (characterized by thoughtlessness, obstinacy, tantrums, and the like); intelligence such as that of a child. -bāshĕ f.pl. childish babbling (esp. of a suckling child) (Śiv. 157, 256; Rām. 1105, 1595, 1781; H. v, 2); childish pranks, baby sports (K. 220, 259, 275). -böʦᵘ̈ m.pl. a person's family, the children of a house and other members (El., Gr.M.). -bāv m. the condition, or nature, of a child, childish ways (p. 146b, l. 29) (Śiv. 1015, K. 1078). -bö̆zᵘ̈ gaʦhun m.inf. to go according to a child's intelligence, to follow a child's advice or opinion (naturally bad). -dôdᵘ m. grief for a child, longing for a child (by a childless person); the torment caused by the wayward conduct of a child. -gindun m. (sg. dat. -gindanas), childish sport, the sport of a child; childish sport by a grown-up person. -har f. (sg. dat. -hürᵘ̈), a childish quarrel, a child's squabble. -hürᵘ̈ thurᵘ̈ khasüñᵘ̈ f.inf. a shrub to rise from a child's squabble; hence, a great quarrel (among elders) to arise from a child's squabble. -kath f. (sg. dat. -kathi), childish talk; silly talk like that of a child. -kathan gaʦhun m.inf. to go according to a child's talk, to follow a child's remarks (which are naturally liable to lead to misunderstandings). -lã̄j f. child-calamity, (when a person is poor and has a great number of children) the children to form an impediment (e.g. to going to a far country, to earn a livelihood, or otherwise). -murⁱ m.pl. children and the like, a man's family (Gr.M., K. 786). -pöthᵃr m. the conduct of a child, or conduct such as that of a child (cf. dŏda-shᵒ-pᵒ, p. 190a, l. 21). -rēmph f. (sg. dat. -rēmpi), a poor little boy (Gr.Gr. 163). -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), one who, owing to the existence of a child, is distracted by the difficulties of supporting a family.
i.q. shyūrᵘ, q.v., see also shērun and wūrᵘ-shᵘ or wūrᵘ-shūlᵘ, p. 1138b, ll. 4, 49. For 1, see shūrⁱ.
or shūrᵘ 1 in okᵘ-shᵘ, p. 19b, l. 17, q.v.
f. conduct of, or like, that of, a child (cf. dŏda-shᵒ, p. 190a, l. 19) (W. 112); playfulness, foolishness, like that of a child (on the part of a grown-up person).
f. i.q. shuril, q.v., childishness, childish conduct; conduct like that of a child (Rām. 1727).
adj. c.g. lean, weak, feeble, emaciated; (of a thing or act) thin, spare, of little use. Cf. shust. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become lean, to become thin.

or shyūshᵘ m. (sg. abl. shīshĕ 3 or shūshĕ), the lungs (El. also shásh, apparently by confusion with shöshⁱ; K.Pr. 200). shīshĕ- (or shūshĕ-)nôrᵘ  m. the pipe of the lungs, the windpipe (confused also with the gullet) (El.). -tikh m. (sg. dat. -tikas), a small piece of lung.
m. in the following:-- shuta dyunᵘ m.inf. to strike, beat (a person). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to suffer a beating. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf a beating to fall (on a person), to get a beating.
postpos. from (cf. bŏna-shuth, p. 110b, l. 22). Cf. shutᵘ.
m. (sg. dat. shūtas), a certain crop (? a pulse), described as producing a small white seed shaped like a long mŏng-seed (Phaseolus mungo).
in shutrā-shöhⁱ m. a kind of obstinate beggar. Cf. shiturᵘ.
i.q. shutᵘ, q.v. Cf. ödⁱ-shⁱ, p. 14a, l, 3; gŏḍa-shᵒ, p. 277a, l. 40; kana-shᵒ, p. 449a, l. 36; tala-shᵒ, s.v. tal 1.

or shutun postpos. since, from the time that, forming adverbs of time, as in gŏḍa-shᵒ, from the first, p. 277a, l. 40; kana-shᵒ, from a long time ago, p. 449a, l. 36; tala-shᵒ, s.v. tal 1; tana-shᵒ, since then, s.v. tana 2; so K. 740, 822, 1051, 1076, 1093. Cf. shuth.
m. a breathing, a complete breath, inspiration and expiration (L.V. 55); an inspiration, as opposed to an expiration (see wŏshwās) (Śiv. 1437, K. 345). Cf. shāh 2.

m. a N. of Krushna (Kṛṣṇa) (Skt. śyāma), so given on account of his dark complexion (cf. shyām 3) (Śiv. 1323, 1329, 1333-4, 1549). ¶ shyāma-sŏndar m. Shyām the beautiful, i.q. shyām 2 (Śiv. 345, 581, 852, 933, 954, etc.; K. 134); (adj. c.g.) dark and comely (Rām. 1036 ff. (applied to Rāma), 1606 (applied to Sītā)).

adj. c.g. dark blue, dark-coloured (i.q. shām 3, q.v.). ¶ shyāma-gal m. dark-blue-necked, a N. of Śiva, whose neck was dyed dark blue by drinking the kālakūṭa poison at the churning of the ocean (L.V. 13); cf. kṭa-kāl, p. 490b, l. 3. -rṻph m. he of the dark form, i.e. Krushna (Kṛṣṇa) (Śiv. 734, 792, 1108, 1140, 1358, 1367, 1388, 1413, 1439, 1791; Rām. 1765). Cf. shyām 2.
or shūrᵘ adj. (f. shīrᵘ̈), prepared, repaired, used --˚, as in aḍa-shūrᵘ, p. 12a, l. 2, q.v. Cf. shērun.
perf. part. (f. shīrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈) of shērun, q.v.
or shihaiṭh card. (pl. dat. shᵉ̆(shi)haiṭhan ), sixty-six (Gr.Gr. 79; El. sheheṭ, shihéṭh).
shihaiṭhyumᵘ, or shᵉ̆(shi)hṻṭhyumᵉ̆  ord. (f. shᵉ̆(shi)hai(hṻ)ṭhimᵉ̆ ), sixty-sixth (El., Gr.Gr. 79).
or shinamath card., ninety-six (Gr.Gr. 80). ¶ shinamatan-hondᵘ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, ninety-six; receiving wages amounting to ninety-six (rupees, etc.), costing ninety-six.
or shisatath card. (pl. dat. shᵉ̆satatan), seventy-six (Gr.Gr. 79).
or shisatatyumᵘ ord. (f. shᵉ̆satatimᵉ̆ or shiᵒ), seventy-sixth (Gr.Gr. 79).
m. the six-staged road, i.e. (in Śaiva philosophy) the six vikāras, or the six cakras (see p. 873b, ll. 27, 44) (L.V. 82).
f. a woman of unpleasing or disgusting appearance or conduct (unpleasing in form, dress, manner of speech, and so on), a hag, a harridan.
onomat. m. the cry used in tending or driving cattle.
in sīhraṭö̃jᵘ̈ f. a kind of small pear (El.).

m. (sg. dat. sihalas), N. of a game formerly played by Kāshmīrī children. It is somewhat on the lines of backgammon. There are five dice, each consisting of a strip of wood, with one surface rounded and the other flat. The board consists of a circle marked on the ground with five or more radii, according to the number of players. One hundred and eighty small holes are dug in the circle, and eleven in each radius. A larger hole is in the centre where the radii meet. Each player moves his piece, starting from the centre, from hole to hole along one radius, round the circumference, and back along the same radius to the centre, its progress being regulated, as in backgammon, by throwing the dice. All five dice are thrown at once, and only those that fall round side up count. When all the players but one have got round and home, the remaining player has to pay his forfeit. This is done by each of the others putting his own five dice into the central hole and kicking them as far as he can. He then rides the loser as far as the most distant die; so also for the others. ¶ The pieces are either cowries or pice or bits of potsherd. They are liable to capture as in backgammon, and the captured piece has to start again from the central hole. If all five dice fall round side up, it allows a move of 28 holes, and the player can play again. If fewer fall round side up the scores are of course much less, e.g. if there are four, the score is ten, and so on.
f. N. of a sign of the Zodiac, Leo (El. sihim m.). Cf. sᵃh and the preceding.
m. Zizyphus flexuosa (El. sínjlí. Cf. bān 1, bārj, and sīmlī).
m. the ash (Fraxinus xanthoxyloides) (El.); cf. cūjᵘ̈. The word should perhaps be spelt sījuwᵘ

(for 2, see sikh) m. a stamp, seal, signet; an impression on money, a stamped coin, sterling or current coin (Gr.M. sikka) (cf. sara sika gaʦhun and karun, s.v. sara). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to stamp, coin; to stamp (oneself or another) as authoritative, to proclaim widely (one's own or another's) might or authority, to make famous. --lagun -- m.inf. (a person's) fame to spread widely abroad, to become famous.
m. a bookbinder's press, a clamp. ¶ sikanja karun m.inf. to press together with a clamp. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to fall into straits, to become confounded, distracted.
f. a female Sikkh, a Sikkh woman; an impudent young girl (usually below the age of puberty), a rude girl, see sikh and sikiyöñᵘ̈.
f. a female Sikkh, a Sikkh woman. Cf. sikh and sīkiñ.
f. a kind of forehead ornament worn attached to a chaplet by young girls of high rank or by a bride. siki-kala m. the jewelled chaplet worn with the above.
f. a kind of apple rather large and of a deep red colour (L. 349).
m. pulmonary consumption, decline, ulceration of the lungs (El. silah, Gr.Gr. 13). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. consumption to occur, to become consumptive.
in sīla supörī m. the acorn of the Quercus incana (El. síla supárí). Cf. balūt.
m. weapon, weapons, arms, implement of war (Rām. 971, 1454; K.Pr. 31).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. silaladiñ), suffering from consumption, in a decline, a consumptive.
f. a device or method, mode (esp. for solving some complicated or puzzling task).
m. a kind of pashmina manufactured in Ladakh (El.).
(? spelling and gend.) a certain edible fungus found on the bark of the elm, Agaricus flammans (L. 73).
f. a long narrow strip of silken cloth, wound round the head, and worn under the turban; a short strip of cloth, suitable for a boy's turban.
m. mercury, quicksilver (Śiv. 1464; Rām. 372, 776). Cf. pārodᵘ.
m. a lion. The god Gȧnⁱsh (Gaṇéśa) is said to ride upon two lions (Śiv. 14). Cf. sᵃh.
f. (m. sᵃh, q.v.) a lioness (El. sihmin, semin, símiṅ, síming, a lioness, leopardess, tigress; Gr.M., a lioness, tigress; Śiv. 1817, lioness; Rām. 96).
f.pl. Indian vermicelli (the simaī of India Proper).
m. Zizyphus flexuosa (El.). Cf. bān 1, bārj, and sī˜jlī.
m. the chest, bosom, breast (El.; Rām. 183, 266, 350, 1235, 1503, 1772; H. vii, 21; K.Pr. 200). -band سینہ بند m. a stomacher, bodice, an inner garment worn by Hindūs (El.).
m. a horn; a horn (the musical instrument).

m. dress, toilet, ornament, decoration, embellishment, arranging the hair, etc.; an appliance for the decoration of the body (sixteen of these are enumerated) (Śiv. 1438); a small red cap worn by Musalmān women (El.).
m the border (of a garment), edge, fringe.

adj. c.g. tightly fitted or fastened to something, tightly thrust into or fitted into (a box or the like); (as subst.) space, distance, range, aim; see sipun. --karun -- m.inf. to hit the mark (of a target or the like).
m. (sg. dat. sipatas), good conduct, virtuous, modest, and kindly conduct; cf. siphath and sipüʦᵘ̈. --nērun -- m.inf. a good character to be developed.
m. (sg. dat. siphatas), a description; a quality, attribute, manner (Rām. 1653); (adj. c.g.) possessing good qualities, nice (K.Pr. 204). I.q. sipath, q.v.

sipôyᵘ, or sipāh (= sipāhi سپاہی) m. a soldier (Gr.M. sipāh; Rām. (id.) 1333, 1339, 1344, 1379, 1400); a man of metal, a hero; a beadle, guard, door-keeper; a native messenger of a court or the like (L. 420 sipahi).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. syupᵘ; f. sipᵘ̈), to fix tightly to something, to thrust tightly (something) into (a box, or the like); to hurl (into a mark, target, or the like); cf. sipa. syupᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sipᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), thrust tightly into, as ab.
in sipüʦᵘ̈-band adj. c.g. endued with a good character. This word is apparently an obl. form of sipath (q.v.) treated as a feminine.

or sīr 1 m. a secret (Gr.Gr. 13; Śiv. 21, 480, 675; Rām. (sir) 194, 801; (sīr) 19, 167, 429, 1246, 1766; K.Pr. (sir) 2, 72); a mystery (H. ii, 4); the secret parts (of a woman) (H. xii, 7). --bāwun -- m.inf. to divulge a secret (Rām. 133, 340, 1214, 1468, 1772; H. vii, 21; K.Pr. 23). --phaṭun -- m.inf. a secret to be divulged. --phāṭawun -- m.inf. to break, reveal, another's secrets. --thawun -- m.inf. to keep a secret, not to divulge a secret. ¶ sira-bôjᵘ m. (f. -bājĕñ), a sharer in a secret. ādanaki- sīra-bôjᵘ, a sharer of innate secrets (Rām. 213) (cf. ādanukᵘ bôjᵘ, p. 14b, l. 44). -kath f. (sg. dat. -kathi), a secret word (or direction, to be divulged at the proper time, e.g. sealed orders). -sān adv. secretly (K.Pr. 201, sírah-s˚).

i.q. sar 2 in sir-āb (= سر آب) adj. c.g. watered from the head of a stream, (of a village) a high-land (village), as distinct from a low-land (village) (pāy-āb, p. 812b, l. 25, q.v.) (L. 435). sir-dāna (= سر دانہ) m. (of a rice crop) full grains, as distinct from weak, imperfect, or blasted grains (L. 335).
f. (sg. dat. sīrüʦᵘ̈), way of life, conduct, character, nature, disposition; virtue, morals, qualities.
adj. c.g. enough, sufficient (K.Pr. 201). Cf. sēr 3.
