or sirī or (q.v.) sṻrĕ m. the sun (El. sirí, siriyi; Gr.M. siri; Rām. (sirī) 219, 1262, 1265, 1275, 1341, 1617, 1755; K.Pr. 120, siriyih; 201, sg. dat. siryas). Cf. sṻrĕ and sūrya.
adv. purely, merely, only, solely, exclusively (Gr.M.).
(? spelling and gend.) a certain edible fungus found on the bark of the elm, Agaricus flammans (L. 73).
m. vinegar (El. sirka). -ṭang m. a kind of pear (L. 350, sirkatang).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. sīryōv), to go round, circulate (Gr.Gr. lxxx).
m. a stone or iron weight for weighing three-quarters of a sēr (of about two pounds); (grain or other article) weighing this amount.

adj. (f.sīriñᵘ̈), (a vessel) containing or holding a sēr (about two pounds) of grain or the like (Gr.Gr. 147); a vessel which holds exactly a sēr (by measure) and is used for measuring, a sēr measure.

(also written sīr) f. (pl. nom. sērĕ, Gr.Gr. 62) a brick (for building) (cf. atha-sᵒ, p. 62b, l. 33; ranga-sᵒ, p. 837a, l. 24; surki-sᵒ, p. 935a, l. 28) (El. sír; Gr.Gr. 15, 62; Gr.M.; L. 458; Śiv. 1033; Rām. 568). A brick may be either a baked brick (pücᵘ̈ sīrᵘ̈), or an unbaked brick of sundried mud (ömᵘ̈, or khām, sīrᵘ̈) (cf. khām sᵒ, p. 400a, l. 21). --bĕhanāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to lay a brick; met. to unite former enemies in friendship, to reconcile; (of disordered conditions) to set in order, make good arrangements, to appease (a quarrel), and the like. --bĕhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a brick to be laid; met. reconciliation of former enemies to be effected; (disordered conditions) to be put in order (as ab.). --ḍalüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a brick to be displaced; met. mutual enmity among relations, etc., to occur; a business to go out of order through some piece of carelessness or the like, good arrangements to become disarranged. ¶ sērĕ-kajāba m. a pyramid-shaped pile of bricks. -kölib m. a brick-mould (cf. قالب). -kō̃da f. a brick-kiln. -lürᵘ̈ f. a brick house, a house built of baked bricks. -pōr m. a brick story, i.e. an upper story of a house. In Kashmīr, if the lowest story of a house is built of stone, the upper stories are generally of brick. -tūrᵘ̈ f. a bricklayer's tool, used for trimming bricks. -ʦyūnᵘ m. a brick pillar, a pillar built of bricks.

f. a finger-shaped roll of clean cotton prepared for spinning into thread (Śiv. 1014); a wad of cotton for medicinal purposes (cf. gĕv-sᵒ, p. 316b, l. 10; phamba-sᵒ, p. 698a, l. 39; thañi-sᵒ, s.v. thañⁱ). ¶ sīri-tulᵘ m. a stick about a span long, and as thick as the thumb, on which this cotton is wound and made ready. -tāsa m. a covered jar in which the cleaned cotton is stored for the purpose of making these rolls.

f. N. of the daughter of Zanakh (Skt. Janaka) King of Mithilā and wife of Rām (Skt. Rāma) (Śiv. 701, 852, 1140, 1419, 1481; Rām. 36, 66, 120, 135, 183, 198, 224, 228, 312, 319, 322, 334, 363, 369, 374, 378, etc.).
m. tyranny (K.Pr. 101). -gar ستم گر (YZ. 17) or -gār ستم گار (YZ. 44) m. a tyrant, oppressor.
m. controversy, altercation, quarrelling, dispute; (in Ksh.) abuse, vituperation, invective, contumely (Rām. 963, 1239).
m. (sg. dat. sitas), (in speaking) a mere breath (without intelligible words), a mere inarticulate whisper (El. sít f. a sound); a whisper (Gr.Gr. 13).
m. boiling, in the following:-- siwa-hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), vegetables boiled in water. Cf. siwun.

or sīwā or sēwā f. service, servitude (Gr.M. sēwā; Śiv. (sēwā) 102, 970, 1073; (sīv) 1314; K. (sīwā) 782, 1094). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to do service (to, dat. or gen.), to serve, do homage (to) (Śiv. (sīv) 366, 477, 488, 527; Rām. 395, 423, 1533, 1641-3 ff., 1663; K. (sīwā) 460, 503, 526, 780, 928, 979, 1069, 1132).

adj. c.g. tame, domesticated (as a beast). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become domesticated, tamed (of a beast or the like); (of a human being) to become tamed, subjugated, dependent. --karun -- m.inf. to tame, domesticate; to tame (a person), subjugate, make dependent.
or (q.v.) siwāh postpos. (governing dat. or abl.) with the exception (of), except, save, but, besides; without, deprived of (Rām. 196). Cf. siwāh and siwöyⁱ.
postpos. (governing dat. or abl.) with the exception (of), except, save, but, besides (H. v, 9, governing dat.), see siwā and siwöyⁱ.
or sēwākār m. one who does service (e.g. out of respect, or as a pupil to his teacher) (Śiv. (sē˚) 9).
m. (sg. dat. sīwakas; f. sīwakĕñ, q.v.), a servant, servitor, follower (K. 335, 384).
n.ag. (siwavüñᵘ̈), one who serves; one who honours, worships. N.ag. of siwun, q.v.
prep. and postpos. (governing dat. or abl.) with the exception of, except, save, besides, other than, over and above, further than, but (W. 97, sivöi; YZ. 101, siwöy). Cf. siwā and siwāh.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. syuwᵘ), to serve, wait or attend on, do service to, minister to, obey; to honour, worship (cf. pād siwȧnⁱ, p. 681a, l. 6); to stew, cook in water, boil (vegetables and the like); met. to tame, domesticate (an animal) (cf. aḍa-syuwᵘ, p. 12a, l. 18). ¶ siwan-lë̆jᵘ̈ f. a saucepan or cooking pot for stewing (vegetables, etc.), a stewing-pan (small in size and made of earthenware). -phakh m. (sg. dat. -phakas), the evil smell remaining in an emptied stewing-pot after cooking. -thöjⁱ f. a large stewing-pan (of metal). -wôñᵘ m. the waste water in which vegetables, etc., have been stewed. ¶ siwana yunᵘ pass. to become soft by boiling or stewing; (of the limbs) to become exhausted or relaxed by steam, perspiration, a close atmosphere, or the like; (of an animal) to become tamed, domesticated. ¶ syuwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sivᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), served, ministered to; honoured, worshipped; boiled in water (Śiv. 1328); tamed, domesticated.
or (Rām. 1042) siyā adj. c.g. black (YZ. 44, 141, 144). -pōsh سیاہ پوش adj. c.g. clad in black (El. siyah-posh).
f. management, conduct (of affairs), right ordering (K.Pr. 216).

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. sīʦᵘ̈-ladiñ), an epileptic, one who suffers from epilepsy; (esp. of a child) one who is naughty, disobedient, annoying, and destructive; (of some work) arduous of accomplishment, to be accomplished only by the expenditure of great bodily and mental labour (cf. arsīʦᵘ̈lad and arasīʦᵘ̈lad, p. 45a, ll. 6, 8). Cf. sētalad and sēth.
m. remembering, remembrance, recollection (Śiv. 106, 195, 372, 383, 983, 1726); memory. Cf. sŏran.
smarath, or sumᵃrath f. (sg. dat. smrë̆ʦᵘ̈, smarüʦᵘ̈, or sumᵃrüʦᵃ), remembering, remembrance, recollection, memory (Śiv. 1860 (smrĕth); 274, 1478, 1572, 1593 (smarath)).

m. bathing, washing (the body), ablution of the whole body, immersion in water (K. 270); purification by bathing, religious or ceremonial ablution (L.V. 32, 46; K. 335, 410, 484, 971). Cf. shrān, srān.

or su a common prefix borrowed from Skt. signifying 'well', 'good', etc., as in (e.g.) sŏ-shīl, well-mannered. Words with this prefix will be found in their alphabetical order. Its opposite is kŏ or ku, q.v.
an honorific suffix, as in rājĕ-söb, His, or Your, Majesty, H. x, 7, 8; Khŏdā-Söb, God, H. iii, 8; x, 5; K.Pr. 61, sābō, voc.
or f. N. of the sister of Krushna (Kṛṣṇa), who became the wife of Arjuna (in Skt. Subhadrā) (K. 1017).

m. nature, innate or peculiar disposition, personal character (Gr.M.; Śiv. 513, 736, 740, 997, 1080, 1144, 1546, 1712, 1904; Rām. 1768; K. 15, 231, 239). kaṭhini sŏbāwa-sostᵘ, possessing a ard nature, fierce by nature (Gr.M.). ¶ sŏbāwa-kinⁱ adv. by nature, naturally, by natural disposition (Gr.M.). -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), full of (a good) nature, good-tempered, amiable, of a lovable character.
adj. c.g. patient (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 85, sābirah, as proper N.).
f. (sg. dat. sŏbŏ̈zᵘ̈ 1, for 2, see subọ̆dᵘ), good understanding, clear intelligence, sharp discernment (Rām. 16, 1645, 1648).
adj. (f. sŏbŏ̈zᵘ̈ 2), possessing good understanding, very intelligent, of excellent discernment.
m. good understanding, good information, good acquired knowledge.
adj. (f. sŏbūdᵘ̈), one who has acquired good knowledge, one who is well-versed or well-taught.

m. (sg. dat. sŏchas), cheapness, plenty and cheapness, cheapness and abundance (El. suchh; YZ. 402, sôchah, obl. sg.; K.Pr. 204, suchh). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. cheap abundance to occur, general cheapness and plenty to take place. ¶ sŏchas-kyutᵘ adv. at a time of cheapness and plenty.
or sō̃ch m. (sg. dat. sōcas or sō̃cas), thought, reflection, consideration.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. sōcyōv), to consider, reflect, ponder, deliberate.
adj. c.g. virtuous, good, well-behaved; (of an animal) quiet, tame, gentle.
or said (= سید) m. a Saiyid, a descendant of Muḥammad, a holy man, a saint (El., Gr.Gr. 22).

m. goods, wares (of trade), merchandise (esp. such articles as salt, oil, spices, or the like) (H. viii, 9; YZ. 58, saudā; K.Pr. 78, 218); trade, trafficking, marketing (El. also sauda) (H. iii, 1; v, 10; K.Pr. 153 (sᵒ nyunᵘ, to buy goods), 70, 94). ¶ (With suff. of indef. art.) sōdāh, a transaction, traffic, bargain or agreement between two or more parties (cf. dȧpⁱ dȧpⁱ sōdāh, p. 233b, l. 44; priʦhⁱ priʦhⁱ sōdāh, p. 771a, l. 42) (Gr.M.).
or sudām m. N. of a Brāhmaṇa, a friend of Krushna (Kṛṣṇa) (in Skt. Sudāmā) (Śiv. 702, 1434, 1474; K. 423, 1075-1175; K.Pr. 204).
or sōzüñᵘ̈ f. a mason's square (the sādhanī of Hindōstān).
or sudarshĕn m. the N. of Viṣṇu's discus (Śiv. 710; K. 881-2, 1059); N. of a Vidyādar (Skt. Vidyādhara) who was cursed by Aṅgiras and changed to a serpent (K. 347).
f. a drain through a wall (e.g. for carrying off the waste water of a cook-room, etc.).
f. the conduct of a holy man or saint, or devotee (cf. sād 2).
m. a lucky day, a day suitable for a festival; a great day, a festal day occurring at regular intervals (e.g. Christmas day, New Year's day, the Śivarātri, and so on). Cf. sŏdüshᵘ̈.
or sọ̆durᵘ adj. (f. sŏdörᵘ̈ or sọ̆dᵘ̈rᵘ̈), prosperous, affluent, rich (of a person, or, met. of a work, crop, etc.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sūdᵘ, f. sūdᵘ̈ (not sūzᵘ̈)), to consider, reflect on, ponder over, scrutiny (e.g. opposing arguments, etc.), come to a decision after mature consideration. sūdᵘ-motᵘ (sometimes wrongly written sôdᵘ-motᵘ, see sādun) perf. part. (f. sūdᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), considered, reflected, pondered over. (The f. is sūdᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, not sūzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, apparently to avoid confusion with sūzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, sent, see sōzun.)
adv. on a lucky day, on a day suitable for a festival. Cf. sŏdŏh.
ord. (f. söḍimᵘ̈), 'one-and-a-halfth', of, or belonging to, one and a half (e.g. the word might be used in counting units, each divided in half).

or (Gr.M.) sudar m. (sg. dat. sọ̆dras), the sea, ocean (Gr.M.; Śiv. 5, 1191, 1551; K. 491; K.Pr. 46, 155). ¶ sọ̆dra-(sudara-)boṭhᵘ  m. the sea-shore (Gr.M.). -könzᵘ̈ m. a certain spiced dish made from rice water or congee (see könzᵘ̈) mixed with mustard-seeds, cumin-seeds, ginger, pepper, grape-juice, and other condiments, fermented in the heat of the sun (K.Pr. 14). -könzᵘ̈- (or -kānz-)pôwᵘ  m. the jar in which this congee is prepared (K.Pr. 26); see könzᵘ̈. -pav m. a sea-channel, a narrow channel (suitable for boats) in the sea, a narrow strait.
in dūnᵘ-sôdᵘ, p. 223b, l. 27, i.q. swād 2, q.v.
in sŏdⁱ wôñᵘ m. N. of a merchant (in Skt. Sudarśana) who was granted a vision of the child Krushna (Kṛṣṇa) (Śiv. 240, 1876 ff.).
or sōgand or saugand f. (sg. dat. sŏgünzᵘ̈), fragrance, odour, perfume (Gr.M.; Śiv. 47; K. (so˚) 114, 583, 924); scent, things giving forth scent (K. 973).
adj. c.g. scented, full of odour, fragrant (El. sogandar, Gr.M.).
f. cheapness; (of something formerly expensive) the becoming cheap, the becoming a drug in the market.

or sugrīv m. 'well-necked', N. of a monkey-chief (in Skt. Sugrīva). He was cruelly treated by his brother Vāli. Rāma killed Vāli and installed Sugrīva on his throne. In return Sugrīva, with his army of monkeys helped Rāma to recover Sītā (Śiv. 704; Rām. 39, 452 ff., 477, 481 ff., 747, 749, 833, 856, 916, 925, 928, etc.).
or (q.v.) srŏgun  conj. 3 (2 p.p. sŏgyōv), to become cheap, to fall in price. sŏgyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sŏgyē-müʦᵘ̈), become cheap.
or (q.v.) srọ̆gᵃñār m. clearness of the sky on the stoppage of the rain and snow (resulting in cheapness of food).
f. (sg. dat. sọ̆gᵃrüñᵃ), the making a thing cheap and plentiful; making (something) a drug in the market (e.g. by abusive criticism, or by making it unfashionable, etc.), depreciation, disparagement.
f. (sg. dat. sö̃gᵃrüñᵃ), the causing a thing to become congealed or coagulated; letting a thing (by neglect) become dry and hard.
or (q.v.) srọ̆gᵃrāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. sọ̆gᵃrôwᵃ), to make cheap, to cheapen, to fix a fair price; to make of small account, to cry down, depreciate, disparage; cf. sọ̆gᵃrun and sọ̆jᵃrāwun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sö̃gᵃrôwᵃ), to cause a thing to become congealed; to cause it to become dry and hard (by neglect, or the like).

conj. 1 (sọ̆gᵒrᵒ) to make a thing cheap and plenty; to cause a thing to become a drug in the market (e.g. by abusive criticism, making it unfashionable or the like), to depreciate, disparage. Cf. sọ̆gᵃrāwun.

or (q.v.) srọ̆gᵘ (f. sö̆jᵘ̈ or sŏjⁱ), cheap, costing a low price. sọ̆gᵘ shuphᵘ ta panādār adj. c.g. cheap, strong, and wide and long (of something for sale). ¶ sŏgi mŏlukᵘ gen. (f. --mŏlücᵘ̈ --), cheap, low-priced. ¶ sŏjⁱ (or sö̆jᵘ̈) milawan  f. (sg. dat. --milavüñᵘ̈ --), great cheapness. --mŏlawan -- f. (sg. dat. --mŏlavüñᵘ̈ --), id.
m. a mimic, actor, player; one who (with the object of cheating) pretends sickness, etc. (see sã̄g).

a Sanskrit phrase (in Skt. sō 'ham) meaning 'I am that', i.e. 'I am one with God' or 'God and I are one'; cf. hams 2. It is much used by Śaiva Hindūs as a mantra, or mystic formula (Śiv. 1019, 1378, 1488, 1578, 1681, 1769, 1780, 1805, 1841). ¶ sōhamsa, i.q. sōham (Śiv. 1222). Cf. the next. ¶ sō-'ham-sō, i.q. sōham (Śiv. 984, 1882).
f. (sg. dat. sŏhbüʦᵘ̈), companionship, society, association (Gr.M.).
f. rule, command, sway, influence (cf. cashma-söᵒ, p. 177a, l. 10).
or (q.v.) srŏjĕr m. cheapness, low price. sojĕrukᵘ gen. (f. sŏjĕrücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, cheapness; hence, bought at a time of cheapness, bought when at a low price.
or sôjuv m. the husband of a wife's sister, a wife's brother-in-law.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sọ̆jᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. sọ̆jᵃrun, q.v. Cf. srọ̆gᵃrāwun, sọ̆gᵃrāwun.
or (q.v.)srọ̆gᵃrun conj. 1 (1 p.p. sọ̆jᵒrᵒ), to make (something which is dear) cheap, to cheapen, to bring down the price (of something).
or (q. v.)srọ̆jᵃran f. (sg. dat. sọ̆jⁱrüñⁱ), making cheap, bringing down the price of something dear.
in sok pachin, the pintail duck, Dafila acuta (L. 129).

m. a prosperous time, a time of great prosperity (for a person or country); a time free from calamity or the like; general cheapness of food, etc., a time of plenty. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. cheapness to come into existence; to become cheap (of something previously dear). ¶ sŏkālukᵘ gen. (f. sŏkālücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a time of prosperity, welfare, or the like.
m. a pious action, a good work, a holy deed (Śiv. 426).
f. (sg. dat. sŏkathi), a pleasing speech, pleasant words, kindly language.
m. (sg. dat. sŏkaṭas; f. sŏküṭᵘ̈, q.v.), a good son, a virtuous and charming boy (Gr.Gr. 132).
adj. c.g. easy, not difficult, practicable, feasible (Gr.M.); as adv. (or sŏkhāla-pöṭhⁱ) easily (Gr.M.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sŏkhanôwᵘ), to make happy, make comfortable, cause to feel secure, put in good cheer, cheer up; cf. sŏkhawun. sŏkhanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sŏkhanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), rendered secure.

conj 1 (1 p.p. sŏkhowᵘ), to make happy, to cheer, enliven, put at ease, make comfortable (by the removal of obstacles, etc.); cf. sŏkhanāwun. sŏkhowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sŏkhüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), put at ease, not troubled by obstacles.

or sŏkhith adj. c.g. full of happiness, comfortable, entirely free from care (K. 633, 959, 1166); producing happiness, causing or producing comfort. --bĕhun -- m.inf. 'to sit happy', to be or continue cheerful, happy. --rōzun -- m.inf., id.
adj. c.g. happy, contented, blessed with health, wealth, children, security, etc. (Śiv. 1438, 1459, 1679).
f. witness, testimony (oral or written), signature as witness to a document or the like (Rām. 1054, 1065, 1600, 1686, 1706).

or (Gr.M.) sökshī c.g. one who sees, an observer, an eye-witness (Rām. 1782); met. the Observer of everything, the Supreme Being (Śiv. sökshī, 306, 1277, 1339, 1415, (f.) 1513). A witness (to a document, in a law-court, or the like) (El. sákhí, saukhí; Gr.M.); one who, or that which gives testimony, who or which gives proof (of anything) (Śiv. 672).
adj. c.g. scorched, burnt, consumed to ashes (Rām. 298, YZ. 39).

m. i.q. sŏkāl, q.v. sŏkölⁱ, adv. at a good time, in a time of prosperity; at a time of cheapness, in a time of plenty. ¶ sŏkālyukᵘ gen. (f. sŏkālicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, cheapness, bought at a cheap time, bought cheaply (esp. of something usually expensive).
adj. (f. sŏköjᵘ̈), bought in a time of cheapness.
adj. (f.sọ̆kürᵘ̈), easy, facile, feasible, practicable; lax, uneven, discontinuous (cf. sọ̆kᵒrᵒ 1).
f. (sg. dat. sö̃krönʦᵘ̈), i.q. sankarāth, q.v.
f. (sg. dat. sŏkacĕ; m. sŏkaṭh, q.v.), a good daughter, a virtuous and charming young girl.
f. (sg. dat. sọ̆kᵃrüñᵃ), levelling (of land in preparation for cultivation).

or sukᵃrāwun 1 conj. 1 (1 p.p. sọ̆(u)kᵃrôwᵃ ), i.q. sọ̆kᵃrun, q.v. sọ̆(u)kᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ  perf. part. (f. sọ̆(u)kᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ ), (of wild, uncultivated land) roughly levelled as a preliminary to preparing for cultivation.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sọ̆kᵒrᵒ 2, for 1, see s.v.), to level (uncultivated land in preparation for cultivation), to make the first breaking of the soil and general levelling. Cf. sọ̆kᵃrāwun.

(for 2, see sọ̆kᵃrun) or sukᵒrᵒ adj. (f. sọ̆kᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or sukᵘ̈rᵘ̈), uneven owing to being only half ready (e.g. something being pounded, or a dish being cooked), incomplete; cf. sọ̆korᵘ. sọ̆kᵒruy thawun m.inf. carelessly to leave something only half, or partly, completed; to join up incompletely.

or sail 2 (= سیر) (for 1, see sail 1) m. strolling, a stroll, ramble, walk, excursion, tour, pleasure trip (cf. nāwa-sᵒ, p. 666b, l. 21) (Gr.Gr. 22; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1363; K. 701-2, 992; H. ii, 2, 4, 8; iii, 1; viii, 7; K.Pr. 233). Cf. sair.
or (Śiv.) sulab adj. c.g. easy to be obtained, easy of attainment, attainable, feasible (Śiv. 1758, 1869).
m. a good, or distinct, mark; an auspicious mark, sign, or omen.
f. mutual affection, long standing brotherly love, love based on generations of affectionate intercourse.

or sulanāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. sŏ(u)lanôwᵘ ), to fondle, lovingly to take (a child, pet animal, or the like) into one's lap, to dandle, rock in one's arms, to hug or clasp to one's bosom (Rām. 1129); cf. sŏlawun and sulawun. sŏ(u)lanôwᵘ-motᵘ  perf. part. (f. sŏ(u)lanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caressed, etc., as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sŏlowᵘ), to establish in a happy position (u.w. reference to a child who has been lovingly brought up and cared for); cf. sŏlanāwun and sulawun. sŏlowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sŏlüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), established (as ab.) in a happy position.

f. 'good union', intimate association with pious people, pious actions, pious conduct, and the like; a certain plant, Plectranthus rugosus (El. solei; L. 76, sulai, a medicinal herb used for preparing an eyewash). sŏlayĕ-kāṭh m. (sg. dat. -kāṭhas), the wood of this plant (good for making charcoal).
or (q.v.) sŏrahāl f. a kitchen, a cookhouse (El. sulahar m.).
m. a head cook, chef de cuisine, cordon bleu.
in sōli-gārē, m.c. for suli gari, see sul.
m. a kind of fine red cloth, Turkey red. sölⁱ-dastār m. a turban made of this cloth (usually worn by boys, or, to distinguish caste, by adults).
or suman 1 m. a flower; esp. the great-flowered jasmine (L.V. 68). -sŏy f. 'a flower-nettle', a certain stinging plant; a nettlish woman, a woman of a waspish disposition, a shrew.
or suman 2 adj. c.g. good-minded, of a good disposition, benevolent, gracious. sŏmana adv. graciously, benevolently; piously (Rām. 993).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sŏmbôrᵘ), i.q. sọ̆mbᵃrun, q.v. to collect together, to gather (things or people) together (Rām. 777).

or sumbul سنبل m. (sg. dat. sọ̆mbulas), a certain plant of sweet odour, spikenard (the hairs of a mistress are often compared to it) (cf. bēkh-sᵒ, p. 99b, l. 18) (Śiv. 55 (sŏmbul); Rām. (sŏmbul) 279, 649, 676, 1021; YZ. 69, 476, 565).
f. (sg. dat. sọ̆mbᵃrüñᵃ), the act of bringing together, collecting (articles) together; making level, levelling.
f. wages for collecting; wages for levelling.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sọ̆mbᵃrôwᵃ) (i.q. sọ̆mbᵃrun, q.v.; causal of samun, q.v.) to collect (things) together (cf. bawan sọ̆ᵒ, p. 147a, l. 32) (El. súmráwun; Gr.M.; Śiv. 25, 113; Rām. 1675; K. 1138; H. xii, 21, 24); gradually to save up, to make savings, earn, make (a fortune) (Gr.M.); to acquire, gain (El. somráwun); to lie with (a man with a woman) (only El. sombráwun); to make level (rough ground or the like). sọ̆mbᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. sọ̆mbᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), collected, saved up (YZ. 408); levelled, made level.
n.ag. (f. sọ̆mbᵃravüñᵃ) one who collects together, one who gathers (scattered articles) together.

or (q.v.)sọ̆mbᵃrāwun conj. 1. (caus. of samun, q.v.) (1 p.p. sọ̆mbᵒrᵒ), to collect together, to gather (scattered articles) together (cf. bawan sọ̆ᵒ, p. 147a, l. 31) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1559; Rām. 1463; K. 204, 415, 769, 1033, 1065, 1085-6; H. ix, 9; xi, 7; xii, 21; K.Pr. 48); gradually to save up, to make savings (Gr.M.); to make level (Gr.Gr. 8, K. 1037). ¶ sọ̆mbᵃ̇rᵃ̇ sọ̆mbᵃ̇rᵃ̇ thawun m.inf. to collect or save up little by little. ¶ sọ̆mbᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. sọ̆mbᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), collected together, etc., as ab.

or sombᵘ adj. (f. sümᵘ̈), equal (to, dat.) (in size, weight, extent, usefulness, ability, etc.) (cf. shāl gübᵘ̈ hāka-ʦar sȧmⁱ, p. 879b, l. 36) (L.V. 1, 5, 16; K. 795; H. (sumbᵘ) xii, 4, 5; K.Pr. 80 (khĕni sümᵘ̈, enough for eating cf. wayĕs sombᵘ, p. 1174b, l. 45), 156 (sumb)); like, similar, resembling (Rām. 1656; K. 543; K.Pr. 20 (suṅmb), 206); even, level, flat, smooth (El. sum, Gr.M.); level, even, parallel (of lines) (Gr.M.); impartial, fair; medium, average; agreeing, unanimous (of opinions) (Gr.M.). --pahān -- adj. (f. sümᵘ̈ pahān), about equal, etc., as ab. somᵘ somᵘ gaʦhun m.inf. to become completely fulfilled (at the right time and place) (e.g. a blessing, a curse, or a business undertaken). somᵘ somᵘ karun m.inf. completely to fulfil, as ab. ¶ sami kada adj. c.g. or adv. of the same stature, of the same form, exactly alike. ¶ samis somᵘ adj. (f. --sümᵘ̈ --), (a person) just like another (e.g. in age, occupation, qualities, conduct, and so on). ¶ somuy adj. (f. sümᵘ̈y), the exact mean, neither excessive nor too little, neither of the very best quality nor of bad quality, and so on.

m. gold (cf. dȧgⁱ dȧgⁱ sŏn banun, p. 196a, l. 42; dȧsⁱ dȧsⁱ sŏn, p. 255b, l. 25; payith sŏn, p. 817b, l. 13) (Gr.Gr. 41, 51, 94, 148, 161; Gr.M.; W. 6, 111; L.V. 100 (= K.Pr. 46); Śiv. 169, 430, 544, 983, 1041, 1060, 1077, 1081, 1196, 1227, 1233, etc., 1345, 1903; Rām. 18, 58, 141, 568, 570, 682, 736, 738, 1066-7, 1203, 1378, 1418, 1495, 1678, 1735, 1747; K. 28, 60, 97, 183, 555, 590, 671, 692, 831, 843, 914; YZ. 214, 286, 375; K.Pr. 46, 122, 143, 186, 206, 236, 246, 259); riches (El.); met. anything very valuable or excellent (cf. krĕhna-sᵒ, p. 469b, l. 5). ¶ sŏna-bāna m. a gold dish vessel, or the like. -cucurᵘ m. a certain mountain bird (described as having gold-coloured wings, and a long tail). -ḍaba m. a box full of gold (Gr.Gr. 73); a box for holding gold. -hôrᵘ adj. (f. -hörᵘ̈), covered or painted with a pattern of gold, or with a pattern of a colour suggesting gold such as ruddy brown; cf. sŏnahȧrⁱ. -hörⁱ adj. c.g., id. -hörⁱ sāban f. (sg. dat. -hörⁱ sābüñᵘ̈), 'mottled soap,' hence (of some otherwise clean cloth) the being covered, as by a pattern, with dirty marks. -hārĕr m. the being covered with a golden or ruddy brown pattern. -kömᵘ̈ f. gold-work, the work or trade of a goldsmith. -kan m. (1) a small fragment or speck of gold; (2) an ear decked with a gold ornament (H. vii, 11). -kᵒtᵒ adj. (f. -kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), coloured with liquid gold paint. -lö̃kh f. (sg. dat. -lö̃ki), 'the golden island,' N. of an island in the Ḍal lake near Śrīnagar (El. sónalãuk; RT. Tr. II, 417, sunᵃlānk) (Śiv. 1820). -löṭᵘ̈ f. a longish piece of gold, (for manufacture). -mahö- nyuwᵘ m. a gold statue of some individual. -mŏhar f. a gold seal (such as a signet ring); a gold coin, a 'gold mohur'; a piece of gold of the weight of a gold mohur. -mahārĕñ f. a bride decked with gold on all her limbs. -marg f. N. of a mountain plateau in the Sĕnd Valley of Kashmīr, famous for its flowery meads (H. xi, 3). -murg m. the Monaul Pheasant, Lophophorus refulgens (L. 119); cf. sunal. -pingan f. (sg. dat. pingüñᵘ̈), the pipe-shaped mould into which melted gold is cast. -pạthᵃr m. (sg. dat. pạtras), gold leaf. -shọ̆dᵘ adj. (f. -shö̆zᵘ̈), made of pure, unalloyed gold. -sondᵘ gen. (f. -sünzᵘ̈), made of gold (Gr.Gr. 41; Rām. 890, 1143j; K. 401, 920, 1007, 1037; H. v, 1, 3-5; K.Pr. 183, 206); cf. sŏnukᵘ, bel. -sôwᵘ adj. (f.-sövᵘ̈), filled with gold (e.g. a mining plot, a treasury, or the like) (Rām. 1784); replete with gold, incalculably wealthy (Śiv. 58). -warukh m. (sg. dat. -warakas), thin leaf gold (eaten as a medicine), gold-leaf. -wasth m. (sg. dat. -wastas), a gold ornament (cf. sŏnⁱ-wⁱ, bel.). ¶ sŏnⁱ-ḍaba m. a box made of gold, a gold casket. -kĕsürᵘ̈ f. 'a golden beard of corn,' a kind of gold flower or boss attached to an ornament. -lar f. a necklace set with gold bosses, flowers, or the like. -māl f. a long garland-like necklace set with gold, with or without other beads. -pōsh m. N. of a certain flower. -sāga-lar f. a kind of necklace worn by Musalmān women, adorned with gold amid pearl, coral, and similar beads. -ʦürᵘ̈ f. N. of a certain small bird. -wasth (sg. dat. -wastas), a gold ornament (cf. sŏna-wᵒ, ab.). ¶ sŏnukᵘ gen. (f. sŏnücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, gold (Śiv. 1235, 1238, 1283, 1726; Rām. 542, 1087, 1372). Cf. sŏna-sondᵘ, ab., which means 'made of gold'.

f. (sg. dat. sŏni, Gr.Gr. 70), a co-wife, a contemporary wife, a rival wife (Gr.Gr. 16, 144; Rām. 82, 280; K.Pr. (sun) 119, 158, 194). Cf. sọ̆ñᵘ. ¶ sŏna-bodᵘ m. the condition between co-wives, the mutual hostility between co-wives (cf. bodᵘ 2, p. 84a, l. 39) (Gr.Gr. 144). -küṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kacĕ), a co-wife's daughter (esp. when used contemptuously or with disrespect). -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a co-wife's son (esp. used contemptuously, etc., as ab.). -pöthᵃr m. (sg. dat. pöthᵃras), a co-wife's conduct, i.e. the conduct between two women who are not co-wives (i.e. mutual hostility and rivalry). -tônᵘ m. the mutual hostility between co-wives, or such similar conduct between women who are not co-wives. -wāzᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. co-wife worry, the worry caused in a household by the existence of co-wives. ¶ sŏnⁱ-hondⁱ gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a co-wife. -pĕṭhⁱ dyunᵘ m.inf. to give (a girl in marriage) to a man who already has a wife. -pĕṭhⁱ karun m.inf. to marry a second wife during the lifetime of the first.
adj. c.g. gilt, golden (Gr.M.). Cf. sŏna-hôrᵘ, p. 917a, l. 18.
adj. f. (a woman) who has a co-wife (sŏn 2). Cf. sata-sᵒ, s.v. sath 3.
f. a female goldsmith (Gr.Gr. 39); a woman of the goldsmith caste; a goldsmith's wife. Cf. sŏnᵃr.
or sunashā f. N. of a certain goddess (Śiv. 1165, 1238).
adj. c.g. 'called blessed'; hence (of a person who has no children, or who has only daughters), one who has (at length) got a son.

m. the confluence of two rivers (cf. sọ̆nᵘ 1 and sand), used in the following compound:-- sŏnda-brörᵘ̈ f. N. of one of the holiest of Kashmīr holy places, the sacred spring of the goddess Sandhyā, called in Sanskrit Trisaṁdhyā. It is said at certain periods in the early summer to flow intermittently, three times during the day, and three times during the night. It is situated in the Bring Pargana in the south-east of the Valley (RT. Tr. II, 469, Sundᵃ̣brạ̄r, El. Sundabrãr, Śiv. 1168).

f. a Hindū festival held after a babe is bathed on (usually) the sixth day after birth, on which day, also, offerings and worship are offered to the goddess Shĕshṭhī (L. 259, says that the festival is on the ninth, not the sixth, day after birth) (cf. shrān-sᵒ, p. 893b, l. 20).

adj. c.g. lovely, beautiful, handsome, charming (cf. mahā-sᵒ, p. 557a, l. 3) (Gr.M.; W. 21, sundar; Śiv. 384, 788, 896, 940-1, 959, 1130, 1266, 1468, 1499; Rām. 342, 351, 1570; K. 134, 428 (sŏndarāh, a beauteous damsel), 766, 783; YZ. 342, 547); cf. shyāma-sᵒ, p. 903a, l. 13. --māl -- f. a lovely garland; met. a lovely charming woman (Śiv, 436, 573; Rām. 1194). --māl hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. --māl hishᵘ̈ --), like a lovely garland, very beautiful and charming.
f. a beautiful woman (K. 238, sŏndari; K.Pr. 207, sundari); a title of Pārvatī (Śiv. 1512, 1691, 1728).
m. N. of the preceptor of Krushna (Kṛṣṇa) and Balarāma (see K. 483-498) (K. 485). In Skt. Sāndīpani.

or sondūkh صندوق m. (sg. dat. sondu(ū)kas ), a box, trunk, chest, coffer, case (Gr.M.; Rām. (sandūkh) 16, 623; K.Pr. 14). sonduka-han f. a small box or chest, a casket. -ṭhāna m. the lid of a box (Gr.M.).

adj. (f. sünzᵘ̈), a postposition of the genitive case, used with m.sg. animate nouns. It governs the dative case. Its original form was hondᵘ. Every masculine dative singular ends in s, as in ʦūras, to a thief; mölis, to a father. When hondᵘ was suffixed to such a word, the h was elided, so that the postposition apparently became sondᵘ, as in ʦūra-sondᵘ of a thief, for ʦūras-hondᵘ, or mölⁱ- sondᵘ, of a father, for mölis-hondᵘ (Gr.Gr. 40). See hondᵘ. ¶ This word has the usual meaning of the genitive, viz. 'of', 'belonging to' (Gr.Gr. 40; L.V. 105, 108; Rām. 271, 509, 510, 538, 631, 957, 1332, 1439, etc.; K. 7, 30, 35, 47, 49, 66, 190, 323, 344; H. ii, 5, 6, 7, 9, etc.). ¶ As has been seen sondᵘ is used with masculine animate nouns. Hondᵘ is used with all feminine nouns and with all plural nouns. Masculine singular nouns which indicate proper names of persons, however, take unᵘ while masculine inanimate nouns take ukᵘ (Gr.Gr. 41). There are, nevertheless, occasional exceptions. Thus, the gen. of Brahmā, the N. of a god, is Brahmā-sondᵘ, p. 121a, l. 34; so Vishṇu-sondᵘ, Rām. 23; Yindrāza-sȧndⁱ pöṭhⁱ, Rām. 1737. ¶ Again, sondᵘ is used with certain inanimate nouns to indicate 'made of' (Gr.Gr. 41). Thus, sŏna- sondᵘ chạthᵃr, an umbrella (made) of gold, while sŏnukᵘ chạthᵃr, would mean 'an umbrella belonging to gold'; so marīna-sondᵘ, made of merino; pash- mīna-sᵒ, made of cloth (p. 781a, l. 30); rŏpa-sᵒ, made of silver (p. 840a, l. 25) (Rām. 890, 1143j; K. 401, 920, 1007, 1037; H. v, 1, 3-5).
f. a co-mother-in-law (the mothers of a bride and bridegroom are sŏñĕñs to each other) (cf. dŏda-sᵒ, p. 190a, l. 23; nĕcivⁱ-sⁱ, p. 621b, l. 43; putᵃ̇rᵃ̇-sᵃ̇, p. 804b, l. 2) (Gr.Gr. 39). Cf. sọ̆ñᵘ.
adj. (f. sọ̆ngalüvᵘ̈), made of sọ̆ngᵒlᵒ 1 (q.v.) wood.
adj. c.g. made of sọngᵒlᵒ (q.v.) wood. Cf. sọ̆ngᵒlᵒ 2.

m. N. of a certain tree, the yew, and its wood (El. sangal, sungal, Taxus baccata); the Himalayan spruce, and its wood (El. sungal, Abies Smithiana; according to L. 79, sungal is the Himalayan silver fir, Abies Webbiana. Cf. budulᵘ).
adj. (f. sọ̆ngᵘ̈lᵘ̈), made of sọ̆ngᵒlᵒ 1 (q.v.) wood. Cf. sọ̆ngȧlⁱ.
m. a kind of round box for holding small articles.
m. (sg. dat. sọ̆ñⁱṭhis), the home of a co-father-in-law (sọ̆ñᵘ, q.v.). sọ̆ñⁱṭhyukⁱ gen. adj. (f. sọ̆ñⁱṭhicⁱ), of, or belonging to, a co-father-in-law's home.
adj. (f. sŏnüvᵘ̈), made of gold, golden.

or (Gr.Gr. 58) sŏnurᵘ (sg. ag. and pl. nom. sŏnᵃ̇rᵃ̇, sg. obl. sŏnar. The fem. is sŏnarĕñ, q.v.; his wife is also sŏnar-bāy, see bel.); a goldsmith, a worker in precious metals (Gr.Gr. 34, 39, 148; W. 111; Śiv. 1652; Rām. 1066; H. v, passim (sŏnar); K.Pr. 207); a man of the goldsmith caste. ¶ sŏnar-bāy f. a goldsmith's wife (Gr.Gr. 34); cf. sŏnarĕñ. -kār m. the goldsmith's art, working in gold. -koṭᵘ m. a real son of a goldsmith, a good goldsmith (Gr.Gr. 132). -thöjᵘ̈ f. a goldsmith's crucible. -wān or sŏnᵃ̇rᵃ̇-wān or sŏnȧrⁱ-wān m. a goldsmith's shop or workshop.

possessivepron. (f. söñᵘ̈), our, of us (Gr.Gr. 56, 87; Śiv. 13, 46, 100, 103, 105, 157, 955, 963, etc.; Rām. 1104, 1784; K. 173, 266, 306, 458, 466, 472, 907, 958, etc.; H. viii, 11, 13; x, 5, 12); (as subst. m.) our house, our home (Rām. 1108a, K. 157). This word is used as the genitive of the plural of the personal pronoun bŏh, I. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. (impve. sg. 2 --wŏla --), to come to our house (used in hospitable invitation) (Rām. 673, 1107, 1765, 1784-5). sāni adv. in our house, at our home.

m. (f. (Gr.Gr. 39) sŏñĕñ), a co-father-in-law (the father of a husband and the father of the husband's wife are sọ̆ñᵘ to each other) (cf. dŏda-sᵒ, p. 190a, l. 22; nĕcivⁱ-sⁱ, p. 621b, l. 38; putᵃ̇rᵃ̇-sᵃ̇, p. 804a, l. 49) (Gr.Gr. 39). Cf. sŏn 2. ¶ sŏñⁱ-dorⁱ m. the row of people belonging to a co-father-in-law, the relations or people of a co-father-in-law (who would ordinarily be invited to a family gathering). -gara m. the home of a co-father-in-law; meton. his family. -kūrᵘ̈ f. the daughter of a co-father-in-law (other than a son's wife), a son's sister-in-law or a daughter's sister-in-law. -mahönyuwᵘ m. the servant of a co-father-in-law (esp. such a servant as is used in communications between the two houses); cf. mahanyuwᵘ. -nĕcyuwᵘ m. the son of a co-father-in-law, a son's or daughter's brother-in-law. -pokhᵘ m. the people of the family of a co-father-in-law. -paʦay f. entering into the relationship of co-father-in-law (caused by the marriage of the respective son and daughter). -sāmaṭh m.pl. (pl. dat. -sāmaṭan), a collection, assembly, or party of co-fathers-in-law. -wath f. (sg. dat. -wati), the road to a co-father-in-law, i.e. to the home of a co-father-in-law. ¶ sŏñĕn-hondᵘ pl. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, co-fathers-in-law.
m. the confluence of two rivers (cf. sand and sŏnd) used in the following compound:-- sŏnⁱ- golᵘ m. the deep hole in the bed at the confluence of two rivers (caused by the meeting of the currents).

or sonᵘ adj. (f. süñᵘ̈), deep, profound (e.g. a lake, a pit, or the like) (Gr.M.; L. 459, sun; Śiv. 330, 1191, 1201, 1755; Rām. 517, 958; H. v, 6); (of a tract of country) low-lying; (of a human being) grave, profound; sagacious, serious, inscrutable (Śiv. 1195, K.Pr. (sun) 138). --wŏgonᵘ -- adj. (f. süñᵘ̈ wŏgüñᵘ̈), deep and shallow, here deep and there shallow, up and down (e.g. a lake, a road) (Śiv. 1681, 1892, cf. 1757; Rām. 1715; YZ. 542); (of a tract of country) undulating; (of an act or business) partly suitable and partly unsuitable. --wŏgonᵘ bōzun -- m.inf. to consider the suitability and unsuitability, to consider the merits (of any act, etc., as ab.); so (with zānun) to know, or (with wuchun) to examine, the merits (as ab.). ¶ sȧñⁱ-wôrⁱ or süñᵘ̈-wôrᵘ̈ m. low land always waterlogged (owing to its being in the neighbourhood of a marsh or the like) (the use of sȧñⁱ instead of sȧnⁱ in this word is not explained); cf. sañĕ-wörᵘ̈, s.v. sañ. -wāryukᵘ adj. gen. (-wāricᵘ̈), (crops, work, etc.) of, or belonging to, waterlogged land.

conj. 2 (1 p.p.sö̃ponᵘ, f. sö̃püñᵘ̈) i.q. sapanun, q.v., to become (cf. dara-dar söpanüñᵘ̈, p. 241a, l. 38; māra sö̃panun, p. 587b, l. 9; māray söpanüñᵘ̈, p. 595a, l. 36, where sö̃pünᵘ̈ is a misprint; and tēr sᵒ, s.v. tēr) (L.V. 5; Śiv. 43, 63, 318, 326, 328, 348, 384, 394, 409, 492, 510, 600, etc.; Rām. 35, 47, 100, 107, 141, 173, 343, 702, etc.; K. 111, 133, 269, 793); to be made, produced, formed, completed, effected (Śiv. 510, 1087; Rām. 1070); to arise, come into being (Śiv. 118, 979, 1465, 1707; Rām. 309, 436-7, 606, 730, 819, 1291, 1501; K. 725); to happen, occur, take place (Rām. 888, 973, 1098, 1108f, 1170, 1235, 1265, 1308, 1755; K. 123, 235, 533, 568, 637, 649); (with. dat. of possession) there is (to so-and-so), (he) has. In the past tense, 'I became,' etc., are used to mean 'I became and am now'; hence, 'I am,' etc. (Rām. 1561). Cf. sampanun, sapadun, sapanun, and sapazun.
m. (sg. dat. sŏpātras), one who is a worthy person, a good man, a respectable person; esp. a son of good character.
or sūphⁱ2 f. (sg. dat. sōpi), an iron-mine; a tract in the south-east of Kashmīr in which there are iron-mines (cf. El. Sof Ahun).
adj. c.g. very fruitful, very productive (Śiv. 1536, 1622), very fertile.
f. a cloth through which liquids are strained; a cloth or rag for cleaning, rubbing, or wiping, a wiper, a duster, a dish-clout.
m. N. of a town on the river Vĕth or Jehlam, about a mile below the point where the latter leaves the Wulur lake. The ancient Suyyapura (RT.Tr. v, 118, Sōpūr; K.Pr. 180, Sopúr).
m. (sg. dat. sŏpŏtras), i.q. sŏpūtᵘ, q.v. (Rām. 1446).
adj. c.g. self-evident; self-luminous; (subst. m.) self-illumination, personal gloriousness (Śiv. 108, 226, 657, 1063, 1124, 1192, 1269, 1413, 1574, 1820).

adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, or produced in Sōpōr (q.v.). --māzarath -- f. (sg. dat. māzarüʦᵘ̈), 'a Sōpōr welcome,' i.e. an empty welcome, a welcome correct in outward form, but not heartfelt (K.Pr. 203).
m. a good son, a son who is born of excellent parents and of excellent qualities and character (K.Pr. 174); a good son, a son devoted to his parents.

or (Rām. 77-8) sŏpan m. (sg. dat. sọ̆pᵃnas or (Śiv.) sŏpnas), a dream, a vision in sleep (Gr.M.; Śiv. 923, 1755 (pl. nom. sŏpna); Rām. 76-8, 1138; K. 802, 806, 1154). --ḍēshun -- m.inf. to see a dream, to see a vision in sleep, to dream. --wuchun -- m.inf., id. (El.). ¶ sọ̆pᵃna-māyā f. dream-delusion, an action which appears unreal, as in a dream. ¶ sọ̆pᵃ̇nᵃ̇ yunᵘ m.inf. to appear in a dream (K. 800).

m. a noise, sound (esp. a musical sound) (cf. atha-sᵒ, p. 62b, l. 26) (El. sor, slow music) (Śiv. 374, 394, 408, 1017, 1323, 1348, 1455, 1761, 1771, 1779, 1803, 1827, 1847); a note of the musical scale (they are seven in number) (Śiv. 1455, 1771); a vowel. --phirun -- m.inf. to play music, make musical sounds (Śiv. 1612, with pun on meaning of sŏr 2).

m. (f. sūriñ, q.v.), a male pig, a hog (cf. dyāra-sōr, a money-pig, a miser, p. 270b, l. 47; sŏrbān-sōr, p. 933a, l. 34) (Gr.Gr. 22; K.Pr. 203, 227, 236). ¶ sōra-buthᵘ m. pig-faced, having a face like that of a pig; impudent-faced, brazen-faced, bold-faced. -buthörᵘ̈ f. a face like that of a pig; impudence, brazen-facedness. -ʦam f. pigskin, pig leather; met. a man's skin which is rough and hard. -ʦomᵘ adj. (f. -ʦümᵘ̈), made of pigskin; having skin like that of a pig.

m. recollection, memory (cf. bē-sŏr, p. 135a, l. 1) (Śiv. 348, 351; Rām. 1693; K. 604); thinking of, calling to mind, carefulness, watchfulness (El.); consciousness (K. 66, 413); (esp. of someone in a faint or the like) motion (of the limbs, etc.), effort, movement (as a sign of returning consciousness) (Gr.M. bē-sŏr, lifeless). --ḍalun -- m.inf. the memory to fail. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to remind (Śiv. 107, (with pun on meaning of sŏr 1) 1612). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. (of someone in a faint or the like) movements of the limbs to occur, signs of returning consciousness to appear. --karun -- m.inf. to make movements, to show signs of returning consciousness; to show watchfulness, be careful (K.Pr. 77, sur); to think (El.). --rōzun -- m.inf. memory to remain, memory to be borne in mind; consciousness to remain (in a person), consciousness to exist (K. 69, 511); (of a fainting person) nothing but movements of the limbs to remain (K. 263). --sŏr gaʦhun -- m.inf. involuntary movements (in a senseless person) to occur. --sŏr karun -- m.inf. (after a faint) to begin a succession of involuntary movements. --thawun -- m.inf. to keep memory, to bear (something) in mind, to watch carefully. ¶ sŏra-boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), one who has a good memory, mindful. -ḍolᵘ adj. (f. -ḍüjᵘ̈), one who has lost his memory; one whose power of movement has been lost. --ḍalun -- m.inf. to lose one's memory; to lose power of motion. --phērun --  m.inf. to begin to remember; to begin to show signs of motion (K. 659). --phirun -- m.inf. to cause (a heedless or forgetful person) to remember and bear in mind, to remind (Śiv. 1750; cf. sŏr ph˚, Śiv. 1612). --phirawun -- m.inf. to recall (a person) to memory, to cause to remember; to rouse a senseless person. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), devoid of memory, forgetful, forgetting (Śiv. 335); motionless (in a swoon). --rōzun -- m.inf. to bear firmly in the memory, to continue remembering (Śiv. 1689, 1803); to remain firm in consciousness. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come into memory, to remember (intr.) (K. 461, 744); to come to oneself, to return to consciousness. ¶ sŏras pyonᵘ m.inf. to come into remembering, to become composed, collected, calm (Śiv. 1170).

f. (sg. dat. sūrᵘ̈), a strong wall built of blocks of stone, a stone-wall; a river-wall, sea-wall, pier-wall. ¶ sōra-lāday f. the act, or work, of building such a wall; wages for building such a wall. ¶ sūrᵘ̈-küñᵘ̈1 (for 2 and 3, see sūrⁱ) f. a large block of stone, used in numbers for strengthening and reinforcing the base of a river-wall to protect it from the violence of the strong current. -pĕṭh thawun m.inf. to carry off and disappear, to run away with (stolen property or the like).
m. collyrium; met. a fine powder (Śiv. 1731). Cf. sŏrma.
f. inconsiderateness, the habit of acting without due deliberation (esp. when marked by ill-timed anger, troubling others, mischievous interference, or the like).
or (q.v.) sŏlhār f. (sg. dat. sŏrahöjᵘ̈), a kitchen, a cookhouse. See sŏlhār (? another form of the same word).
m. one's own kingdom, one's own glory (Rām. 77).
m. remembering, calling to mind (cf. dyāna-sᵒ, p. 268a, l. 16) (Śiv. 155, 983, 1266, 1557). Cf. smaran.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sŏranôwᵘ), to cause to be remembered, to call to mind (K. 358).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sōranôwᵘ), to cause (something) to be used up, finished, exhausted, to use up (Rām. 1454); to spend (time or the like) without profit, to waste (another's time).
n.ag. (f.sŏravüñᵘ̈), one who remembers, recollects, one who has a good memory.
n.ag. (f. sōravüñᵘ̈), that which is nearly finished, or nearly used up; that which is usually used up or finished at the proper time or place.
m. the Ksh. form of the Skt. Svarbhānu, a N. of Rāhu (see Rāh 2), the demon of eclipse. sŏrbān sōr m. 'a Sŏrbān pig', a gruff fellow who keeps himself to himself and refuses to answer questions.

m. heaven, Indra's paradise (El. sorag, paradise, súrug, heaven; Gr.M.; L.V. 62; Śiv. 419, 646, 1132, 1539; Rām. 571, 1167, 1567; K. 1124; K.Pr. 233, surug); met. (in this world) a delightful place, a heaven upon earth (K. 1005, sŏrgāh, with suff. of indef. art.). ¶ sŏrga-būñᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -bōñĕ), 'a plane-tree of heaven' (very shady and pleasant); hence, a woman who in her lifetime sees many children and grandchildren; a woman who (as a plane-tree gives shade) supports numerous dependents in happiness and comfort, a Lady Bountiful. -dwār m. the gateway of heaven (Śiv. 972, 1074; Rām. 1072); meton. i.q. sŏrg, heaven and all that it contains (Śiv. 64, 1154); a heaven upon earth, a delightful place (Rām. 597). -lūkh m. Indra's paradise (Rām. 342; K. 300, 770, 773). -wās m. an inhabitant of heaven, a celestial being, a god (Rām 1599). -wösī m. one who lives in heaven, one whose soul is in heaven; (politely) one who is dead, deceased (Rām. 507). -wothᵘ adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), one who descended from heaven (cf. wasun); hence, met. an angel, one of angelic beauty or character. -zyūnᵘ adj. (f. -zīñᵘ̈), one who has conquered heaven, one who, by his virtuous conduct, has earned a title to an abode in heaven after his death. ¶ sŏrgukᵘ gen. (f. sŏrgücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, heaven (Rām. 519, 651, 1072, 1212, 1234).
m. (K. 771) or sŏrgāpurī f. (Śiv. 197) heaven, Indra's paradise (Śiv. and K., as ab.); met. a heaven upon earth, a delightful place.
adj. c.g. produced or instituted in heaven; met. delightful or charming as if produced in heaven.
adj. c.g. an inhabitant of heaven, a person who, owing to virtuous conduct, attains to heaven.
f. gradual transporting and depositing in another place, accumulation (cf. pā̃-sᵒ, p. 748a, l. 14).

f. feeling, touching, testing by feeling (e.g. feeling something in the dark to find out what it is) (Gr.Gr. 120); finding out or worming out another's secret intentions or opinion (cf. phȧlⁱ-sⁱ, p. 694b, l. 20).--hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (by question or the like) to worm out another's secrets.

m. powdered antimony or lead-ore; collyrium for the eyes (made of the ab.) (YZ. 261; K.Pr. (surmah) 2, 95, (sarmah) 153); fine powder, dust (Rām. 500); a disease of wheat, which turns the grain into a black powder with an offensive smell (L. 342); cf. sŏr 4. --karun -- m.inf. to reduce to an unpalpable powder (like collyrium). -shrünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -shranjĕ), a small box for holding collyrium (usually egg-shaped and made of crystal, silver, or the like). -srünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -sranjĕ), id. -tᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a needle for applying collyrium. -tᵃl f., id. -tᵃlḍālüñᵃ f.inf. to apply collyrium to the eye with such a needle.
f. a woman whose eyes are coloured with collyrium; a woman whose face is of a darkish grey colour (looked upon as a beauty).
adj. c.g. of the colour of collyrium, darkish grey.
adj. c.g. of the colour of collyrium, greyish.
f. a pipe, clarion, hautboy (K. 1009, K.Pr. (suranai) 207, 261).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sŏrshôwᵘ), to wash (i.q. sŏrshun 2, q.v.); to cause to be washed.
m. (sg. dat. sŏrshĕnas), water for washing, etc. (as in sŏrshun 2).
conj. 1 (1 p.p.sọ̆rshᵘ), to wash, clean (e.g. the hands, feet, a dish, a cloth) (cf. atha sᵒ, p. 62b, l. 35). sọ̆rshᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sö̆rshᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), washed, wet after washing.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sọ̆rᵘ), to remember, recollect, call to mind (cf. dörᵘ̈ bar sŏrun, p. 238a, l. 40) (L.V. 91; Śiv. 107, 164-5, 211, 249, 1165, 1170, 1708, 1723, 1726, 1749, 1751, 1757, 1760-1, 1763, 1770, 1772, 1777, 1857, 1901; Rām. 3, 57, 173, 1489, 1753; K. 50, 565, 1062-3, 1168); to call to mind, to remember affectionately, meditate upon (L.V. 45, 65; Śiv. 249, 309, 757, 798, 1383; K. 202, 499, 512, 588, 1125); to be conscious, to be in a state of consciousness (K. 61); to think upon, meditate upon (K. 180, 555, 1112, 1158); to experience, meet with, encounter, undergo (K.Pr. 256, surih for sŏri). Cf. sarun. ¶ sŏrⁱ sŏrⁱ pakun m.inf. to act after taking full precautions. ¶ sọ̆rᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sö̆rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), remembered, recollected. ¶ sŏrani pyonᵘ m.inf. to fall into memory, to call previous experience to remembrance (and act accordingly); to come to one's right mind (K. 88). ¶ sŏranas pyonᵘ m.inf. to call previous experience to remembrance, to remember, call to mind (K. 64, 122, 180); to profit by experience, to understand the surrounding circumstances (K. 209, 211, 526); to become conscious, to cease to be unconscious (K. 230). ¶ sŏrith bĕhun m.inf. to settle oneself, after calling to mind previous experience. --pakun -- m.inf. to act according to previous experience, to act cautiously (remembering one's powers or capabilities) (cf. atha sŏrith pakun, p. 62b, l. 37). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain remembering, to remain carefully in charge (of anything). --thawun -- m.inf. to care for with due regard to the future.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. sūrᵘ; 2 p.p. sōryōv), to be spent, exhausted, used up, run short (of things, e.g. when being divided out) (Gr.Gr. 19, 205; Rām. 919; K. 157, 1025; K.Pr. 259); to become used up, to become worn out, to fade away (Rām. 200, 295); (of a period of time, of age, of life, or the like) to pass away, elapse (esp. vainly, or without profit), expire (Rām. 661, 908, 950, 1089, 1625, 1634, 1636; K.Pr. 128); (of longings, efforts, or the like) to become exhausted, to be overspent, to cease, to be given up as hopeless, to be in vain (cf. tamanāh sᵒ) (Rām. 711, 953, 1053, 1586, 1628; YZ. 22, 474; K.Pr. 187). ¶ sūrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sūrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), used up, exhausted. ¶ sōran-vil f. the time of being used up, of being finished. -vizᵘ̈ f., id. ¶ sōrān yunᵘ m.inf. gradually to become used up. ¶ sōryō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. sōryē-müʦᵘ̈), used up, exhausted.
(or swarṻph, cf. swa) m. (sg. dat. sŏrṻpas), one's own form, natural state, condition, or character, true constitution (Śiv. 153, 346, 1069, 1277, 1565, 1844). See also swa-rṻph, s.v. swa.

m. (sg. dat. sŏrzanas), the final ceremony of the Śivarātri festival, beginning in Kashmīr on the 12th of the dark half of the month of Phāgun (February-March), lasting for five days, and ending on the first lunar day of the light half of the month, i.e. the day of the new moon. Cf. wagurᵘ. ¶ sŏrzan okᵘ dŏh m. the first lunar day (i.e. the day of the new moon) of the light half of Phāgun on which the festival ends. -māwas f. according to some, the festival begins on the 11th of the dark half of Phāgun, not the 12th. These call the day of the new moon by this name.
adj. (f.sö̆rᵘ̈), one who has a good memory, remembering.
m. in sȧrⁱ-pholⁱ m. a mustard seed; (as an example of minuteness) (L.V. 47).

adj. (f. sörᵘ̈ 1), essential, that which is the essence (of anything or quality); (in Ksh.) indestructible, imperishable, everlasting, permanent (Śiv. 189, 738, 1582, 1644); trustworthy (El.); all, the whole (in this sense generally used at the present day with emph. y, Gr.Gr. 92; see bel.) (Gr.Gr. 154, Gr.M.; without emph. y, we have in sg. (for pl. see bel.) Śiv. 32, 414, 913, 934, 1154; Rām. 7, 276, 282, 515, 587, 642, 717, 1098, 1136, 1381, 1573, 1603, 1682, 1761; K. 14, 56, 84-5, 91, 100, 162, 263, 268, 329, 447, 467, 500, 584, 586, 627, 762, 815, 817, 1102; YZ. 177. With emph y, see bel.). --nērun 1 -- m.inf. to attain to a condition of indestructibility, to turn out (to be) permanent. --nērun 2 -- adj. (f. --nērüñᵘ̈--), one who, or that which, attains a condition of permanence. ¶ sāri ranga adv. in every way (Gr.Gr. 154). ¶ sörⁱ m.pl. (f. sārĕ), all, every (when employed with emph. y, see bel.) (L. 458, soré; Śiv. 25, 127, 924, 981, 1221, 1500, 1509; Rām. 8, 141, 194, 667, 692, 751, 857, 916, 1003, 1085, 1108c, 1595, 1641, 1690). ¶ sāriy pöṭhⁱ adv. in every way (Gr.Gr. 153). ¶ sôruy adj. (for pl. see söriy bel.; sg. dat. sörisᵘ̈y, sometimes written sörisạy; f.sg. sörᵘ̈y, abl. sāriy), all, the whole, quite the whole, the entire (cf. sôruy kã̄h, etc., p. 390a, l. 1) (Gr.Gr. 92, 153; Gr.M.; L.V. 31, 42-8, 84, 95; Śiv. (sôruy) 42, 117, 207, 363, 369, 419, 588, 636, 641, 677, etc.; (sörisạy), 284, 1153; (sörᵘ̈y), 769; (sāriy) (f.), 1240; Rām. (sôruy) 56, 60, 162, 172, 177, 182, 313, 429, 514, 516, 594, 597, 653, etc.; (sörⁱsạy) 156, 320, 556, 737, 739, 844, 981, 1013, 1234, 1442; (sörᵘ̈y) 178, 442, 571, 595, 994, 1703; K. (sôruy) 128, 469, 1150, etc.; (sāriy) 5-6, etc.; (sörisᵘ̈y) 100; (sörᵘ̈y) 560, 570, 839, etc.; YZ. (sôruy) 99, 236; H. (sôruy) iii, 1; v. 7, 9; xi, 9, 20; xii, 19). ¶ söriy (sometimes written sörī) m.pl. (dat. sārĕnᵘ̈y, sometimes written sārĕnạy, sārĕniy, or sārĕnⁱ; ag. abl. sārĕvᵘ̈y, sometimes written sārivạy; f. sārĕy), all, every (Gr.Gr. 92; Śiv. (söriy) 193, 195, 213, 224, 235, 285, etc.; (söri) 720, 733, 1047, 1511, 1532; (sārĕnᵘ̈y) 162, 170; (sārĕniy) 202, 1170; (sārĕy) 1861; Rām. (söriy) 2, 4, 68, 142, 207, 399, 615, etc.; (sörī) 972; (sārĕnⁱ) 465, 1228, 1463; (sārĕniy) 579, 835, 1359, 1476, 1492; (sārĕvᵘ̈y), 142; (sārĕy) 307; K. (söriy) 40, 85, 182, 235, 340, 418, 633, etc.; (sārĕnᵘ̈y) 513, etc.; (sārĕnⁱ) 304, 706, etc.; (sārĕvᵘ̈y) 566; (sārĕy) 98, 238, 299, etc.; H. (söriy) iii, 4; v, 9; vi, 16; YZ (sörī) 173, 189; (sarĕnạy) 26); ¶ all people, everybody (Śiv. (söriy) 65, 206, 360, 385, 507, etc.; (sörī) 622, 624, 783, 1507, 1523, 1890; (sārĕnᵘ̈y) 123; (sārĕnạy) 41, 89, 99; (sārĕniy) 8, 74, 212, 443, 839, 1225, 1235, 1239, 1335; (sārivạy) 843, 1508; Rām. (söriy) 2, 53, 127, 204, 341, 404, 722, etc.; (sörī) 137; (sārĕnⁱ) 586, 998, 1112, 1243-4, 1311, 1751, 1762; (sārĕniy) 92, 815, 985, 1278; (sārĕniy-hondᵘ) 63; (sārĕvᵘ̈y) 90, 796, 1108c; K. (söriy) 108, 173, 236, 415, 1151, etc.; (sārĕnᵘ̈y) 99, 402, 404, 407, 466, etc.; (sārĕnⁱ) 467, 706, etc.; (sārĕvᵘ̈y) 266, 292, 369, 534, 561, 701, 750; (sārĕy) 301, 511, 765, etc.; K.Pr. (sárí for söriy) 150). ¶ sāryukᵘ or sāryukuy gen. (sāricᵘ̈ or sāricᵘ̈y), of, or belonging to, the whole or everything. (Without emph. y) (Siv. 729 (f.); Rām. 1756); (with emph. y) (Śiv. 911; Rām. 126, 815, 1136, 1387, 1757; K. 6, 1100).
adj. said to mean 'absorbed', 'vanished'. Noted only as a supposititious original of the word sȧlⁱ-alam, p. 24b, l. 27. Possibly connected with sȧrⁱ 2, q.v.

(f. sörᵘ̈ 2), 1 p.p. of sārun, q.v., used --˚, collected, brought together by degrees from one place to another, transported in instalments (cf. aḍ-sᵒ, p. 10b, l. 10, and aḍa-sᵒ, p. 11b, l. 5) (K.Pr. 200).

m. gradual transportation from one place to another, accumulating, accumulation of something (cf. atha-sᵒ, p. 62b, l. 27; athi-sᵒ, p. 66a, l. 15; börᵘ̈-sᵘ̈, p. 118b, l. 27; dajĕ-sᵒ, p. 203a, l. 45; dȧlⁱ-sⁱ, p. 211b, l. 48; dana-sᵒ, p. 222a, l. 13; dāñĕ-sᵒ, p. 231a, l. 4; khal-sᵒ, p. 397a, l. 4; lada-sᵒ, p. 508b, l. 4; laṭa-sᵒ, p. 537a, l. 18; mȧṭⁱ-sⁱ, p. 603a, l. 11; nȧṭⁱ-sⁱ, p. 660a, l. 3; nāwa-sᵒ, p. 666b, l. 26; phal-sᵒ, p. 692a, l. 14; phȧlⁱ-sⁱ, p. 694b, l. 17; phŏṭⁱ -sᵒ, p. 715b, l. 21; pajĕ-sᵒ, p. 724a, l. 11; pȧlⁱ-sⁱ, p. 730a, l. 32; pā̃-sᵒ, p. 748a, l. 13; potᵘ-sᵘ, p. 788a, l. 3; piṭhⁱ-sⁱ, p. 818b, l. 29; thapa-sᵒ, s.v. thaph; tal-sᵒ and tȧlⁱ-sⁱ, s.v. tal 1); the being accumulated, being amassed or collected (cf. aḍ-sārĕ-maḍ-sārĕ, p. 10b, l. 13; gagar-sᵒ, p. 28a, l. 5; khaṭa-sᵒ, p. 421a, l. 28; lāka-sᵒ, p. 517b, l. 48).

f. touching, feeling (with the hand or the like) (cf. nama-sᵒ, p. 635b, l. 48) (Gr.Gr. 122); testing by touch or by feeling (cf. ȧnⁱ-sⁱ, p. 30, l. 38; lata-sᵒ, p. 537a, l. 4); met. testing secretly, putting to a private test.
m. one who reminds, one who calls things to another's memory.
m. N. of a sacred site (in Skt. Surêśvarī) on the north-east side of the Ḍal lake near Śrīnagar. It is of great sanctity (RT.Tr. II, 455).

m. the iris, Iris nepalensis (El.; L. 75, 248; Rām. 397, 403, 648, 1018, 1091; YZ. 13, 96, 150). According to El. it is the great graveyard flower with the Musalmāns of the Valley and is of four species, yellow, white, red, and blue. In Rām., however, it is always alluded to as a typically dark-coloured flower, in contrast, e.g., to the rose. The root of the red species is used as a remedy for amenorrhœa, and for noises in the ear. According to L. the plant is used medicinally as a stimulant and expectorant.
m. good progeny, a fine child or fine children (Rām. 1258).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. sŏsaryōv), to decay internally (e.g. wood) (Gr.Gr. 121); (of a person) to suffer internally (from sorrow, desire, etc.). sŏsaryō-motᵘ perf. part. (sŏsaryĕ-müʦᵘ̈), decayed internally.
adj. c.g. suffering from internal decay.
m. excellent character, good behaviour, gentlemanliness; cf. shāna 1. sŏshānukᵘ gen. (f. sŏshānücᵘ̈), (esp. of a child or one not of full age) well-mannered, gentlemanly (f. lady-like).
adj. c.g. well-mannered, well-behaved, well brought up.
f. N. of the wife of Sŏdām (Sudāmā), q.v., (in Skt. Suśīlā) (Śiv. 1473; K. 1175, 1180, 1193-4, 1197 ff.).

or sŏsur m. internal decay (e.g. something worm-eaten or a fruit going badinside) (Gr.Gr. 121). --aʦun -- m.inf. internal decay to occur; (of a person) internal suffering (due to grief or the like) to occur. --lagun -- m.inf., id. ¶ sŏsar-hĕma f.pl. lines or creases on a bean or the like caused by decay. -lôdᵘ m. a pile of decay, a pile of grain, fruit, or the like much decayed.
interj. (a corruption of the Skt. svasti, 'it is well') welcome! hail! (used esp. by Brāhmaṇas in benediction) (K. 977); adieu! farewell! Cf. sŏstĕstu.
interj. (a corruption of the Skt. svastyastu, 'may it be well'), i.q. sŏst, q.v. (K. 934).
m. N. of a certain holy mantra or text recited at the auspicious moment of beginning a sacrifice (in Skt. svastibhadra) (K. 1038).

or (q.v.) sosᵘ adj. (f. süʦhᵘ̈. The opposite of this word is rostᵘ, q.v.) accompanied by, possessed of, possessing, endowed with (Gr.M.). Very common --˚, as in āyĕ-sᵒ, p. 73a, l. 23; bala-sᵒ, p. 103a, l. 36 (Śiv. 1259); bāwa-sᵒ, p. 147a, l. 4; bayĕ-sᵒ, p. 148b, l. 30; dā̃di-sᵒ, p. 187b, l. 31; dādi-sᵒ, p. 191a, l. 42; dŏkha-sᵒ, p. 206b, l. 4; dana-sᵒ, p. 222a, l. 15; darma-sᵒ, p. 245a, l. 1; dūshĕ-sᵒ, p. 253a, l. 50; māna-sᵒ, p. 573a, l. 22; nēma-sᵒ, p. 637a, l. 23; nyāyĕ-sᵒ, p. 675a, l. 12; phala-sᵒ, p. 692b, l. 3; pŏñĕ-sᵒ, p. 746b, l. 28; prayĕma-sᵒ, p. 774a, l. 43; pāyĕ-sᵒ, p. 812b, l. 15; rāga-sᵒ, p. 828a, l. 15; röni-süʦhᵘ̈, p. 835b, l. 22; rǖpa-sᵒ, p. 840b, l. 4; shŏba-sᵒ, p. 869a, l. 15; shūbi-sᵒ, p. 869a, l. 44; santāpa-sᵒ, p. 923b, l. 25; and many others (Śiv. 237, 580, 587, 806, 840, 891, 983, 985, 1050, 1438, 1566, 1628, 1648, 1785; Rām. 242, 1259, 1783 (nawa-dwāra-sostᵘ (a house) with nine doors; cf. p. 664a, l. 27); K. 10, 231, 242).
adj.(f. sösiñᵘ̈), costing or worth, a thousand (rupees, etc.) (cf. dyāra-sᵒ, p. 270b, l. 49; sata-sᵒ, s.v. sath 3); one whose wages are a thousand (rupees, etc.).
adj. iris-coloured, purple, lilac; as subst. f. purple colour (L. 459).
i.q. sostᵘ, q.v. as in shūbi-sᵒ, p. 869a, l. 44.

adj. (f.sösᵘ̈), amounting to a thousand, consisting of a thousand; worth a thousand (rupees or the like), costing a thousand; earning (wages of) a thousand (rupees, etc.). Often --˚, as in ʦu-sôsᵘ, consisting of four thousand; pönʦa-sᵒ, consisting of five thousand, and so on. ¶ sāsi-mŏkha adv. with a thousand mouths (Śiv. 735, alluding to the thousand heads of the serpent Shēsh (Śēṣa)). -ranga adv. of a thousand kinds, in a thousand ways. -rȧngⁱ adj. c.g. of a thousand kinds. -wati adv. in a thousand ways; for a thousand reasons or causes.
adj. (f. sösᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, lentils or porridge (sas), used in compounds such as sata-sᵒ, made of seven kinds of lentils, etc., s.v. sath 3.
m. a staff, club, cudgel, truncheon (K.Pr. 179).

f. (sg. dat. sö̆ʦᵘ̈), deep and prolonged sleep (cf. nĕta-sŏth, p. 661a, l. 1) (Rām. 1182; K. 55, 65, 77, 79, 91). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. deep sleep to fall (involving insensibility). ¶ sŏta-sövᵘ̈ f. deep and prolonged sleep. -sövᵘ̈ pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. deep and prolonged sleep to fall; to fall into coma when at the point of death (so sŏta-sövᵘ̈ ʦhunüñᵘ̈, to die).

m. (sg. dat. sōṭas), concord, association, agreement. --karun -- m.inf. (of former enemies) to make concord, to make it up, become friends. --rōzun -- m.inf. concord to continue. --thawun -- m.inf. to keep up intimacy for the future (esp. with some powerful person in the hope of future help).

or sōnth m. (sg. dat. sō̃tas), the spring season, spring time [considered as covering two months, viz. Ṯs̱ithᵃr (in Skt. Caitra = March-April) and Wāhĕkh (in Skt. Vaiśākha = April-May), and hence as covering the period when the sun is in Pisces and Aries (Skt. Mīna and Mēṣa)] (L. 326, sont; Śiv. 1573, 1651, 1848; Rām. 678; K. 100; H. ix, 7; K.Pr. 78, 203); the spring festival held on the day of the sun's entry into Pisces (called in Skt. the Caitra-saṁkrānti), spring-day (L. 265, 464, sont). -kāl m. spring time (Rām. 1661). -kölⁱ adv. in the spring. -kālukᵘ gen. (f. -kālücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the spring. -kālyukᵘ gen. of -kölⁱ (f. -kālicᵘ̈), id. --karun -- m.inf. to carry out the spring festival. -mās m. the spring month, springtide. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. spring to come. ¶ sō̃ta-bôgᵘ m. the spring-gift, the present sent on the spring festival to a bride and her husband by her parents. -dŏy f. the second day after the spring festival. -kani adv. at or about spring time. -kanyukᵘ gen. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, about spring time. -mās m. a spring month, i.e. one of the two months Ṯs̱ithᵃr and Wāhĕkh (see ab.); the spring season, spring time. -mösⁱ adv. in the spring time. -māwas m. the day before the spring festival (held on the sun's entry into Pisces), i.e. the last day of the sun's stay in Aquarius. On the evening of this day a large basket is filled with paddy, on the top of which are placed jewelled ornaments of silver and gold, curds, flowers, rice-cakes, walnuts, lights, and other articles. This is deposited on the east side of the bed of the head of the household, and on the morning of the next day (i.e. of the spring festival) it is greeted with hymns and blessings by every member of the family, great and small. Each then takes one of the fruits or flowers, bathes, and casts it into the river. -phal m. a spring crop (e.g. barley, wheat, mustard, etc.); the astrological result of the conjunction of planets occurring on the occasion of the spring festival. -phulay f. the spring-flowering, the blooming of flowers in the spring. -sul f. a spring-dawn, the beginning of the year (on the occasion of the spring festival); met. a very early time, a time coming very quickly (e.g. for the early completion of some prolonged work). -suli adv. very quickly, very soon, very early. -tray f. the third day after the spring festival, i.e. the third day of the sun's residence in Pisces (on which a festival and worship are held). -wôñᵘ m. spring-water, the river floods after the spring melting of the winter snow. ¶ sō̃tukᵘ gen. (f.sō̃tücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, spring. ¶ sō̃tunᵘ adj. (f. sō̃tüñᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, spring (Rām. 14, 1089). ¶ sō̃tas-kyutᵘ adv. in the spring.
m. (sg. dat. sŏṭhᵃkas), crystal, quartz (El. soṭka, Śiv. 1657, Rām. 571, K. 921). sŏṭhᵃka-ṭujᵃ f. a splinter, or piece, of crystal.

m. an embankment, a river embankment (often used as a road, or even as a bridge) (cf. sum-sᵒ, p. 911b, l. 6; sĕmanz-sŏthi, p. 913b, l. 45; swa-mana-sᵒ, s.v. swa) (El. suth; L. 458, sut; L.V. 74, 98 (= K.Pr. 18); Śiv. 371, 1143, 1829; Rām. 36, 794-7, 1749).
m. a comrade, associate, companion, ally, accomplice, mate, assistant (El. also söth; Gr.M. söthī; Śiv. söthī, 1552).
f., i.q. sŏth, q.v. deep sleep, in nĕta-sŏtī, p. 660b, l. 50.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. sŏtyōv), to be tranquillized, assuaged, appeased, composed, quelled, cooled, extinguished (e.g. a blazing fire, fever, rage, hunger, weariness, tyranny, and so on, or a person suffering from any of these); cf. sŏth and wāh 1. sŏtyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sŏtyē-müʦᵘ̈), tranquillized, etc., as ab.

adj. (f.sö̆ʦᵘ̈), appeased, allayed, calmed, pacified (El. sút, lazy); extinguished (of fire), subsided (of heat, etc.); become gentle (of a flooded stream); calm (of the sea) (Gr.M. sotᵘ); slow (W. 20). --sọ̆tᵘ -- adj. (f. sö̆ʦᵘ̈ sö̆ʦᵘ̈) calm, extinguished, quieted; as adv. slowly (W. 96). --tab -- m. long continued worry, pain, trouble, etc. ¶ sö̆ʦᵘ̈y tĕmbᵘ̈rᵘ̈ wŏshĕlüñᵘ̈ f. 'an extinguished spark to become red'; used met. with reference to any woman, fem. thing, quality, act, or condition, who or which, from small beginnings rises to great eminence, prosperity, or exaltation.

or (as first member of acompound) sütᵘ̈ m. or (q.v.) sütᵘ̈ f. the flour of barley, gram, etc. (parched before it is ground), parched gram (or popcorn) reduced to meal, 'suttoo' (cf. dachilⁱ-sⁱ, p. 186, l. 7; lāyĕ-sᵒ, p. 543b, l. 5). (El. saut.) ¶ sütᵘ̈-phĕkh f. (sg. dat. -phĕki), a very small amount of suttoo. -pholᵘ m. a quantity of suttoo taken as provision on a journey, a viaticum of this meal.

m. a group of seven, a seven (Gr.Gr. 83). ¶ sȧtⁱ m.pl. the form used for sath 3, seven, in multiplication, as in zᵃh sȧtⁱ ʦŏdāh, two sevens are fourteen (Gr.Gr. 86); cf. sāḍa sȧtⁱ, p. 863b, l. 43, which owing to its special meaning is treated as sing. f. -sataway card. (pl. dat. sȧtⁱ-satawanī orsȧtⁱ-satawȧnⁱ), even the seven, all the seven (Gr.Gr. 85). ¶ sotwāh khaṇḍā about seven but a little less, nearly seven (Gr.Gr. 83).
m. a happy time, a time of prosperity, good times.
or suvĕʦār m. (cf. swa-vĕʦār, p. 952b, l. 18) good, or wise discrimination (Śiv. 950, 1272).
f. an auspicious moment or occasion, see vizᵘ̈.
f. of the preceding, used as subst. f. to mean 'sleep', in the phrase sŏta-sᵒ, p. 946a, l. 32; sāvi-sān adv. quietly (El. sáwísan).
f. (sg. dat. sŏwöñᵘ̈), a lucky word, a word or sentence of good omen (heard at the beginning of a work, or accidentally in any other connexion).
m. a pleasant winter (without much snow, rain, cold winds, and the like).

f. a lucky week-day (fortunate for beginning any work). (Each week-day is under a special planet, and the luckiness consists in the day having the special planet which is auspicious for the particular work.)
f. a pious resolution or determination (e.g. to act virtuously, to benefit others, to endow a holy place, or the like).
f. a woman whose husband is alive (and of respected character).
f. (sg. dat. sŏwati), a good road, i.e. a holy way (such as that followed on a pilgrimage).
adj. (f. sŏwöcᵘ̈), well-voiced, kindly-voiced, saying kindly or consoling words.
adj. c.g. of a kindly disposition. sŏwŏnda 2 adv. in a kindly way, amiably, affectionately.
f. (sg. dat. sŏwāñĕ), i.q. sŏwān, q.v.

adj. (f. sövᵘ̈), rich in, abounding in, possessing abundantly (frequent --˚; cf. bala-sᵒ, p. 103a, l. 39; bata-sᵒ, p. 137b, l. 2; dana-sᵒ, p. 222a, l. 17; dyāra-sᵒ, p. 217a, l. 5; māla-sᵒ, p. 565a, l. 28; mǖ̃thri-sᵒ, p. 606a, l. 36; māyā-sᵒ, p. 612b, l. 31; phala-sᵒ, p. 692b, l. 6; pŏñĕ-sᵒ, p. 746b, l. 31; rūma-sᵒ, p. 834a, l. 35; ǖnⁱ-sövⁱ, p. 835b, l. 35; rǖpa-sôwᵘ, p. 840b, l. 5; sŏna-sᵒ, p. 917b, l. 7) (Śiv. 58, Rām. 1784); rich, wealthy (El. sáó, sov; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 125, sáv for sövᵘ̈); plenteous, abounding (of a crop) (L.V. 66); also met. --˚, as in atha-sᵒ, with hands full (of money), liberal (p. 62b, l. 46); āyĕ-sᵒ, long-lived, healthy (p. 73a, l. 25); mŏla-sᵒ, of great price, of high value (p. 566a, l. 45); mana-sᵒ, firm-minded (p. 572a, l. 43); panāh-sᵒ, (of cloth) fine and broad (p. 740a, l. 45). sövᵘ̈ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to cause a woman to be endowed with wealth, virtues, learning, and the like; to endow her with such.
1 p.p. of sāwun (f. sövᵘ̈), used --˚ put to sleep, caused to sleep (cf. aḍa-sôwᵘ, p. 12a, l. 10) (K.Pr. 154).

f. the common nettle (cf. bŏta-sᵒ, p. 138b, l. 32; ganda-sᵒ, p. 289b, l. 46; suman-sᵒ, p. 913b, l. 31); (El. só,e; L. 75, urtica dioica; 462, soi; 76, sooi, a stomachic medicine; K.Pr. 13, suí); useless action, vain efforts, unprofitable exertions; peppermint (El. sóí). --āsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. vain efforts to exist, to be in the habit of making useless actions (worrying other people). --chāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to beat or flog with nettles (a naughty boy or the like). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a nettle to touch (a person), to be stung by a nettle; to become engaged in fruitless actions (worrying other people). ¶ sŏyĕ-dŏph m. (sg. dat. -dŏpas), a nettle-plant. -ṭūpᵘ m. the nettle-flower. -zanḍ m. a bunch of nettles; a nettle-plant.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. sŏyĕladiñ) (a child or other) who worries others by fruitless actions.

or pron. (a borrowed Skt. word), self, oneself (cf. swa-swayĕm, p. 952b, l. 26) (L.V. 33; Śiv. 1020, 1843, 1850); by oneself; of oneself, of one's own accord; (or subst. m.) N. of a site in the Mạchⁱpur Pargana of Kashmīr where volcanic phenomena are observed. At certain periods vapour issues from fissures in the ground. The Skt. name was Svayambhū. See RT.Tr. i, 34 (note). According to Stein (l.c.) the place is now called 'Sayam' (Śiv. 305, 1121, 1174, 1425). sŏyĕm-bū  m. the Self-existent, a title of the Supreme Deity, esp. in the character of Brahmā, Vishnu, or (Śiv. 835) Shiwa (Śiva). sŏyĕm sō m. the name given in schools to the Śāradā character equivalent to the Nāgarī sva (in Kāshmīrī sŏ). It is the first syllable of the Skt. word svasti, which is part of the Skt. phrase ōṁ svasti ēkaṁ siddhaṁ, which is uttered before enunciating the alphabet (see JRAS., 1916, p. 681).
m. (a borrowed Skt. word) the public selection of a husband by a maiden of rank at an assembly of suitors held for the purpose (Śiv. 45, 629, 684; K. 709-10, 730, 893-4).

f. (sg. dat. sŏyë˘ʦᵘ̈), a lamp-wick (El. soyet, a wick; soyat, a candle; as a city term, sãt, i.e. söth, a wick; as used out of Srīnagar, set, a lamp; saiyat, a lamp). sŏyë˘ʦᵘ̈ f. pl. inf. 'to make into wicks,' i.e. (in anger, or the like) to tear up a garment or cloth into little pieces.
f. (sg. dat. -yĕʦhi), a good wish, a pious wish, pious intentions, good purpose, good resolves.
or (q.v.) söyīsth m. a groom, a horse-keeper (El. sá,ís; Rām. 1337).
m. a groom, a horse-keeper, a syce (El. sá,ís; H. xii, 3, 4). Cf. söyis.
m. a certain wild plant used in cooking (? El. swoi, tamarisk).
adj. c.g. burning, inflaming, used --˚, as in dil-sōz, p. 215a, l. 31; as subst. m., heat, burning (YZ. 1).
m. a symphony, a musical concert, a triple symphony (Rām. 1572). Cf. sāz 1.
m. a well-to-do and virtuous man, a gentleman, a respectable and benevolent man (K.Pr. 202).

f. a needle; (in Ksh.) tambour-work; cloth with tambour-work pattern; cf. sōzüñᵘ̈ 2. -tūpⁱ f. a cap ornamented with tambour-work. The tambour- work must be of the same colour as the cloth of the cap. Otherwise it is a cikȧnⁱ ṭūpⁱ, see cikan.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sōzanôwᵘ), to cause to be sent (El., K. 982).
m. (sg. dat. sŏzātas), one (esp. a boy) of good caste; hence, met. one of good family, well brought up, well educated, and well conducted.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sūzᵘ), to send (a person, message, or the like), dispatch (cf. athi sᵒ, p. 66a, l. 19; phīrith sᵒ, p. 706b, l. 25; pata sᵒ, p. 793a, l. 46) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 157, 638-9, 1218, 1670; Rām. 81, 147, 161, 195, 294, 304-5, 451, 489, 495-6, 505, etc.; K. 42, 105, 127, 305, 308, 485, 500, 554, 591, 640, 645, etc.; H. v, 1; x, 4; YZ. 28, 91, 246, 427; K.Pr. 128). sūzᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sūzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), sent, dispatched. Cf. sōdun.
f. a kind of coverlet of tambour-work.
f. a kind of bag or purse closed by a string (K.Pr. 236).
f. mallows (El.) (cf. gurⁱ-sⁱ, p. 299a, l. 9; sinⁱ-muhima sᵒ, s.v. syunᵘ) (L. 75 sutsal, Malva rotundifolia, used medicinally as an expectorant; K.Pr. 201, 208).
f. in the following:-- sŏʦüñᵘ̈- (also written sŏʦᵃñĕ-)tulᵃ (-) m. a hollow straw (fitting over the iron spindle) on which thread is wound while being spun.
m. calmness, quietness; the condition of being extinguished. Cf. sọ̆tᵘ.
adj. c.g. one who is uncontrolled, one who acts entirely at his own pleasure; hence, a N. of Shiwa (Śiva) (Śiv. 30, 48, 775, 1273).
f. (sg. dat. sọ̆ʦᵃrüñᵃ), appeasing, calming, extinguishing (e.g. of fire, fever, grief, or the like).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sọ̆ʦᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. sọ̆ʦᵃrun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 8). sọ̆ʦᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. sọ̆ʦᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), appeased, calmed, extinguished.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sọ̆ʦᵒrᵒ), to appease, calm, extinguish (e.g. fire, fever, grief, or the like) (causal of sŏtun, q.v.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sporshᵘ), to touch (dat. of obj.) (L.V. 37).
in the following:-- srag-alag m. inconsistent behaviour, sometimes respectful and sometimes the reverse, occasional failure in courtesy (a phrase used in apologies for accidental discourtesy).

or srĕh m. affection, love, tenderness (El. sré; Gr.Gr. 147; Śiv. (srah) 1758, 1843; (srĕh) 1033, 1112, 1688; K. (srĕh) 157, 266, 409, 743; K.Pr. (srĕh) 99); moistness, dampness, (Śiv. 1610 (srah); H. viii, 7 (srĕh); K.Pr. (srĕh) 17 187); cf. sᵃnih. --barun -- m. to practise loving, to show affection, to be in love with (K. 462). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. love to be born, to come into existence; moisture to occur, dampness to be experienced. --karun --  m.inf. to moisten, make humid; moisture or humidity to occur. --rōzun -- m.inf. moisture to remain, (of something being dried) a little moisture to remain. ¶ sraha-borutᵘ adj. (f. -barᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), full of love, very loving (Śiv. 1806), lovable, adorable, attractive, seductive. -vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), moist, damp, (after a course of drying) still moist.

or srĕhulᵘ or srihyulᵘ adj. (f. sra(ĕ)hᵘ̈jᵘ̈ ), loving, full of love, affectionate, of a loving disposition (Gr.Gr. 147); causing love, arousing affection, attractive, captivating; moist, damp (El. sirhúl, Gr.M.).
f. (sg. dat. srüñᵘ̈), sweat, perspiration (cf. srônᵘ).

m. bathing, ablution, immersion in water (El. srán, adj. clean; H. v, 9; xii, 6, 7; YZ. 162, 537); ceremonial bathing. Cf. shrān, snān. ¶ srāna-gorᵘ m.(f. -gürᵘ̈), a bathing man; a man who washes or bathes a helpless invalid; the man who bathes the corpse of a man. -püṭᵘ̈ f. the board on which a corpse is placed for bathing, as ab. -paṭh m. (sg. dat. paṭas), a piece of cloth worn round the privities in bathing, a bathing dress, a loin-cloth (K.Pr. 91).
or (q.v.) shranḍa m. a fat, corpulent, strapping fellow; a buffalo (El., K.Pr. 203, both sranḍah).
or (qq.v.) shrāñĕr, sāñĕr m. moistness, dampness (cf. atha-sᵒ, p. 62b, l. 33); freshness, juiciness. Cf. shrônᵘ, srônᵘ.
or (q.v.) shranz m. pincers, nippers, a forceps; a blacksmith's tongs.
m. a small hole, a pin-hole (such as those bored for an earring or the like, or appearing in a dish, etc.); cf. shrav. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to make such a hole.
adj. c.g. perforated, having a pin-hole (e.g. a leaking vessel). See srav.
n.ag. (f. srawavüñᵘ̈), that which oozes, that which drips; (of a vessel) leaking. Cf. shrawawunᵘ.

conj. 2 (2 p.p. srowᵘ. According to Gr.Gr. lxxxi, this verb is conj. 3, with 2 p.p. sravyōv), to drip, ooze, drop forth, trickle; cf. shrawun. srowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. srüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), dripped, oozed forth.
or srŏdⁱlözⁱ f. commonalty, the condition of being joint property or the like.

or (q.v.) sryodᵘ adj. (f. srö̆zᵘ̈), common (to two or more), joint (cf. man-srᵒ, p. 572a, l. 23); cf. sryodᵘ. --bōzun -- m.inf. to consider in common, (of a number of people) to be unanimous. ¶ srŏdi bĕhun m.inf. to sit in commonalty, (of a number of people with distinct occupations) to occupy a joint locality or place of business for mutual convenience or profit. --rōzun -- m.inf. to abide in common, (of a number of persons) to dwell in commonalty or partnership; (of a number of people of the same trade) to dwell or work in the same locality. --thawun -- m.inf. to put into commonalty, to put things together for joint use, to put into partnership for mutual profit. ¶ srŏdyukᵘ gen. (f. srŏdicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, commonalty (e.g. property in common, or a shareholder).
m. sharing, participation, coparcenary, property held in common, community of interests.
n.ag. (f. srŏgavüñᵘ̈), that which is (gradually) becoming cheap, becoming cheaper and cheaper.
or (q.v.) sŏgun conj. 3 (2 p.p. srŏgyōv), to become cheap, to fall in price. srŏgyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. srŏgyē-müʦᵘ̈), fallen in price.
or (q.v.) sọ̆gᵃñār m. general cheapness (esp. of food) (esp. when due to favourable weather, etc.).

or (q.v.) sọ̆gᵃrāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. srọ̆gᵃrôwᵃ), to make (something dear) cheap, to cheapen, to bring down the price (of something); to fix a fair price (after bargaining); to make of small account, to cry down, depreciate, disparage; cf. sọ̆jᵃrāwun and srọ̆gᵃrun. srọ̆gᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. srọ̆jᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), made cheap; made of small account.
or (q.v.)sọ̆jᵃrun, i.q. srọ̆gᵃrāwun, q.v. (1 p.p. srọ̆gᵒrᵒ).

or (q.v.) sọ̆gᵘ adj. (f. srö̆jᵘ̈ or srŏjⁱ), cheap, costing a low price (El. srug, srang; Gr.Gr. 30, 140; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1284, 1290; K.Pr. 204 srug). ¶ srŏgi bāzara adv. at a low price, cheaply. --drŏgi -- adv. cheaply or dearly, (e.g. in srŏgi drŏgi gaʦhi hyonᵘ, it must be got at any price, whether cheap or dear). --mŏlukᵘ -- adj. (f. --mŏlücᵘ̈ --), cheap, low-priced.
or (q.v.) sŏjĕr m. cheapness, low price (Gr.Gr. 30, 140). srŏjĕrukᵘ gen. (f. srŏjĕrücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, cheapness; hence, bought at a time of cheapness, bought when at a low price.
or (q.v.)sŏjⁱran f. (sg. dat. srọ̆jᵃrüñᵃ), making cheap, bringing down the price (of something dear).
m. (El.), see sawölī (L. 79, sarul or kanzal, Alnus nitida).
(? spelling and gend.) or mahz-nĕnd (p. 557a, l. 28) the second weeding of a rice crop (L. 463).
or (q.v.) shrŏng f. a very narrow passage, lane, tunnel, or the like.
or (q.v.) shrônᵘ adj. (f. sröñᵘ̈), wet, moist; succulent, not dry, green, juicy; (of a story or the like) soft, tender. Cf. sāñĕr, srāñĕr, and shrônᵘ.
m. community (of property, opinions, etc., between two or more persons), co-partnership, joint participation (cf. man-sᵒ, p. 572a, l. 20). Cf. srọ̆dᵘ and sryodᵘ.
or(q.v.) shrünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. sranjĕ) a tiny box or casket (cf. sŏrma-sᵒ, p. 935b, l. 6).
or (q.v.) srọ̆dᵘ adj. (f. srë̆zᵘ̈), common (to two or more), joint. Cf. srọ̆dᵘ.
m. place, situation, used --˚ in Persian compounds as in pīra-stān, p. 753a, l. 3. Cf. sthān.
f. a spot of ground, in such Skt. compounds as dēva-sthalī (p. 261b, l. 47), a god-spot, i.e. a spot of ground sacred to the gods or hallowed by their presence (Śiv. 1170).
m. a place, spot, site, position, locality (cf. nābi-sᵒ, p. 619b, l. 14; parama-sᵒ, p. 760a, l. 21) (L.V. 57, 82; Śiv. 20, 1050, 1601, 1654, 1659, 1700). Cf. stān.
adj. c.g. fixed to one spot, stationary, unmovable, inanimate (opp. to zangam) (Śiv. 1631).
adj. c.g. large, great, big, bulky, huge (opp. to sṻkshm, q.v.) (Śiv. 1026, 1198, 1853).
f. a woman. -warna f. a person of the woman class, a female; a woman (Rām. 1205).
f. praise, a hymn of praise (K. 331, 337). Cf. tŏtā, tŏth 2, and tōth.
m. the governor of a province, viceroy (Śiv. 1798); (in Kashmīr) a district officer (K.Pr. 114); any officer of high rank (K.Pr. 187, subahdár).
m. (sg. dat. subūtas), proof, testimony, conviction (Gr.M.).

m. dawn, daybreak, morning (sometimes written suba) (cf. prath subᵃh, p. 769a, l. 34) (El. subah, subh, morning from sunrise to 9 o'clock) (Gr.Gr. 157; Gr.M.; Śiv. 157, 275, 1113, suba; Rām. 92, 119, 1257; H. x, 8; xii, 9; K.Pr. 176, 204). ¶ subᵃha adv. from the morning (e.g. in subᵃha tā shām, from morn till eve, Rām. 259). ¶ subᵃhai adv. very early in the morning (Gr.Gr. 22). ¶ subᵃhukᵃ gen. (f. subᵃhücᵃ), of, or belonging to, the early morning (Śiv. 1360, Rām. 439). ¶ subᵃhan m. the early dawn (El. subhan, subhán); adv. at early dawn (cf. az suᵒ, p. 74a, l. 24) (Gr.Gr. 157; Gr.M.; Rām, 884, 1636; H. x, 11). ¶ subᵃhanukᵃ gen. (f. subᵃhanücᵃ), of, or belonging to, the early dawn. ¶ subᵃhanas adv. at early dawn (El.; W. 95; H. xii. 12). --bögⁱ -- or --bögin -- adv. at about early dawn. ¶ subᵃhas adv. at early dawn (El.; W. 95; Śiv. 332; Rām. 143; H. xii, 5). prath subᵃhas, adv. every morning (Gr.M.). --bögⁱ -- or --bögin -- adv. at about early dawn.

m. profit, gain (L. 459, sud; Śiv. 375, 1812; Rām. 1576; K.Pr. 146, 245, (sud) 109); interest, usury (El.). --nērun -- m.inf. gain to issue, profit to come from anything. ¶ sūda-dyār m.pl. wealth of usury, money earned by lending money at interest; money increased by lending at interest. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), not resulting in any great profit; one whose business is without profit, owing to working on borrowed capital or the like.
m. an obstruction in the nose, coryza; (pl.) scybala, small hard balls into which the fæces are formed in certain deranged conditions of the colon (in the sg. a single one of these balls).
m. N. of a son of the King of Kāśī (Skt. Sudakṣiṇa) (K. 875, 882).
m. (f. sūdarĕñ, q.v.), a usurer, money-lender. -bāy f. his wife.
m. forcible insertion, forcible thrusting into a narrow orifice (cf. sukun). --dyunᵘ 1 -- m.inf. to strike a blow with the closed fist, or with the point of club.

m. want of food, not eating, abstinence (voluntary or involuntary) from food; cf. sakolᵘ. --dyunᵘ 2 -- m.inf. not to eat food, to abstain (voluntarily or involuntarily) from food, to fast, starve. --lagun -- m.inf. a fast, owing to want of food or famine, to be experienced, to starve.
in nika-suka, p. 627b, l. 31, q.v. Cf. nyukᵘ sukᵘ, p. 670a, l. 38.
f. (sg. dat. sukarüñᵘ̈), causing (something) to contract, making smaller (e.g. a piece of cloth by crushing it up, or by sewing it), shrinking (something), reducing the width or size (of something).

conj. 1, noted only in the following:-- sukorᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sukürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), drawn together (by someone), caused to be shrunk up, made smaller or contracted (e.g. a cave, path, or wall made artificially smaller, a piece of cloth made shrunken in size, or an ornament made tighter). Cf. sukᵃrāwun 2.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. sukaryōv), to become contracted, to contract, shrink. sukaryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sukaryē-müʦᵘ̈), contracted, shrunken.
adj. c.g. minute, fine, thin, delicate (opp. to sthūl, q.v.) (Śiv. 368, 1026, 1198, 1525, 1853, 1872).
f. the buttock (El. sukúj). Cf. mandul.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sukᵘ; f. according to some sucᵘ̈ (Gr.Gr. lxxx, and reported for this dictionary as sukᵘ̈) to squeeze into, to force something into a tight orifice; met. (of a man) to have sexual intercourse; cf. shrŏkun 2 and suka 1. sukᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sukᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), forced into a tight place, squeezed into.
