conj. 1 (1 p.p. sukᵃrôwᵃ), to cause to be contracted, artificially to make smaller, to cause to be shrunken; cf. sukarun 1. sukᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (sukᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ) contracted (by some one), made smaller, shrunken (by some one).
m. (sg. dat. sūktas), a good or wise saying; a Vedic hymn (K. 15).
in nyukᵘ-sukᵘ, p. 670a, l. 38, q.v. Cf. nika- suka, p. 627b, l. 31.

or (Gr.Gr. 156) sulᵘ̈) f. good time, early time, the time before the appointed time (Rām. 674, 1648); early dawn (cf. sō̃ta-sᵒ, s.v. sō̃th) (L.V. 99 (= K.Pr. 46), 100); spare time (El.). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the being in good time to occur, to be before the appointed time, to be in good time. --karüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to make earliness, to be in good time, to be in plenty of time. ¶ suli adv. early, betimes (cf. sō̃ta-sᵒ, s.v. sō̃th) (Gr.Gr. 156; Gr.M.; L. 460; Śiv. 163, 628, 1883; Rām. 73, 436, 884); at dawn (H. xii, 23; K.Pr. 87). --bögi -- or --bögin -- adv. early, approximately early, pretty early, more or less beforehand. --gari -- adv. at dawn time (H. v, 7, sōli-gārē, m.c.). --vili -- or (Śiv. 1135) --wuli -- adv. exactly early, promptly early (Śiv. 1135). ¶ sulyukᵘ gen. of suli (f. sulicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, an early time.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. sulowᵘ), to take into one's lap, to cherish, fondle (a child, pet animal, or the like) (Rām. 1105); cf. sulanāwun and sŏlawun. sulowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. sulüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), fondled, as ab.
m. N.P. Solomon (the son of David) (H. xii, 17).
f. an impaling stake.--diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to impale; to crucify (El.).
f. the Himalayan poplar, Populus ciliata (El. sulálí). Cf. bagnū; dūd-phras, p. 191b, l. 15; saphēdār.
m. a sultan, king, emperor (H. i, 1).
m. a hoof, a hoofed foot (W. 139, K.Pr. 71).

f. a bridge (L. 457; W. 13; L.V. 34, 50, 96, 98; Śiv. 1793; K.Pr. 46, 47); the parting of the hair. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to pull up a bridge', to lay down a boundary line (i.e. after having fixed a boundary, to lay it down definitely in detail). -sọ̆thᵘ m. bridge and mole; met. the observance of the rules of religion and good conduct (Rām. 1749). -sọ̆thᵘ dyunᵘ m.inf. to perform acts of pious liberality (e.g. providing works of irrigation, building a bridge, providing food for the hungry, and so on). -sọ̆thᵘ ʦaṭun m.inf. to cut off, put an end to, good old customs such as observances of rules of religion or conduct. --ʦaṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cut a bridge (K.Pr. 8); (pl.) to cut bridges (of a mischievous and extravagant wife who hinders her husband from crossing over to the other side, where peace and prosperity are to be had) (K.Pr. 70). ¶ suma-küṭᵘ̈ f. a small bridge.

or sŏmīr or samīr m. N. of the sacred mountain Mēru (allegorically represented as composed of gold and gems, the centre of the universe, and the abode of the gods) (Hindū) (Śiv. 1302, 1306, 1314, 1440, 1456, 1505; Rām. 558, 933, 1013, 1418); met. anything firm and immovable; firm and inexhaustible resources or wealth; a polite term used by the satisfied recipient in thanking the donor of some small gift; the large, or central, bead of a rosary (Śiv. 1314). ¶ sŏ(su)mīra-parbuth  m. (sg. dat. -parbatas), Mount Mēru. ¶ sŏ(su)mīrüñᵘ̈-sath f. (sg. dat. sŏ(su)mīrañĕ süʦᵘ̈ ), the hope or expectation of certain and inexhaustible resources; a sure and certain hope or expectation of gaining these resources.
f. N. of one of the wives of Daśaratha and mother of Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna (Rām. 40, 84, 278, 280, 1101, 1108a, 1118, 1143a).
or m. (sg. dat. sumuhūrtas), an auspicious period, time, or moment (for any rite, etc.) (K. 1037).

or (Śiv. 162, 1314) sumaran f. (sg. dat. sumᵃrüñᵃ), remembering, remembrance, recollection, memory (Śiv. 1500, 1785); a rosary, or string of beads used for religious purposes (Śiv. 162, 1293, 1314). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause a person to remember, to call to a person's memory, to remind (of). --phirüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to remember, recall to one's memory (something forgotten) (either automatically or by someone reminding); to tell one's beads (on a rosary). --rōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. memory (of something) to abide or persist. ¶ sumᵃrüñᵃ-pholᵃ m. a bead of a rosary (the large, central bead of a rosary is sumīr, q.v.).
f. in sumᵃrī-māwas f. the lunar day of the new moon (see māwas) when it falls on a Monday. Pious acts performed on this day are believed to give great merit.
(? spelling) m. the Monaul Pheasant, Lophophorus refulgens (L. 119). Cf. sŏna-murg.
m. a court messenger, a policeman, constable.
adj. c.g. patient (El. santushi. Cf. the preceding).
m. a peach, Amygdalus persica (El.). Cf. ʦūnū.
adj. c.g. entrusted, consigned, assigned, made over (Gr.M.).
m. the betel-nut, the nut of the Areca catechu (Śiv. 577, 970). suphārĕ-khünḍᵘ̈ f. a piece (or paring) of areca-nut.
m. a Ṣūfī, one of a peculiar sect of Muslim devotees (they are looked upon as unorthodox); (in Ksh.) a religious pupil (who always dwells near his master to receive instruction).
f. a kind of woollen cloth; an iron-mine (i.q. sōph, q.v.); a tract in the south-east of Kashmīr in which there are iron-mines (i.q. sōph, q.v.).
a by-form of suphörⁱ, q.v. In sīla-sᵒ, see sīla.

or (Śiv.) sŏr 3 m. a god (Śiv. 859). sura-guru m. the preceptor of the gods, (in Skt.) Bṛhaspati; the chief of the gods; hence, sura-guru-nāth, the lord of the chief of the gods, the Supreme Deity (L.V. 5, 65).

m. (pl. dat. sūran, Gr.Gr. 51), ashes (cf. aḍa-sᵒ, p. 13b, l. 5; brana-sᵒ, p. 124a, l. 33; daba-sᵒ, p. 181b, l. 26; ṭŏka-sᵒ, s.v. ṭŏkh) (Gr.Gr. 51; Śiv. 319, 326, 815, 875, 878, 893, 900, 932, 1063, 1287, 1292, 1608, 1685, 1778; Rām. 47, 457, 554, 682, 740, 767, 978, 1081, 1113, 1234, 1263, 1597; H. v, 9; xii, 23; YZ. 234-5; K.Pr. 64, 207); powder, dust (Rām. 933; K. 111, 441; H. vii, 13; K.Pr. 207); hoar-frost (El.; L. 460, sur; Śiv. 325, 334, 1208). --sās -- m. a heap of ashes (e.g. such as is left after a conflagration) (Śiv. 818 (sūra-s˚), 833 (id.), (1355 sūr-s˚); K.Pr. 262 (na sūr na sās)). -zamīn f. a kind of soil, dark in colour (L. 320, surhzamin). ¶ sūra-dag f. (El. m.) dew (El., Gr.M.); the pain caused to the bare feet by walking in the hoar-frost (K.Pr. 26; cf. p. 193a, l. 37). -kᵒtᵒ adj. (f. -kᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), 'wet with ashes', i.e. smeared all over with ashes. -lŏbur m. a lump of the ashes of dried cowdung. -manan f. (sg. dat. -manüñᵘ̈), a boatman's brazier full of ashes (see manan). -motᵘ adj. (f. -müʦᵘ̈), 'ashes-mad', one who is in the constant habit of smearing the body with ashes (Śiv. 88, 114, 154, 270, 370 (sūray-m˚), 579, 1292, 1564, 1608, 1610; Rām. 1602). -më̆ʦᵘ̈ f. 'ashes-earth', a kind of earth, white like ashes, used for rubbing on the body (Śiv. 353). -pholᵘ m. a heap of ashes (such as is left by a burnt-out fire). -sās, see sūr-sās, ab. -ṭās m. the crash of (falling) ashes, i.e. hardly any sound at all; hence, met. entire disappearance, as in the phrase tath drāv na sūra-ṭās (on its disappearance or destruction), there was not even the crash of its ashes.
in sur-chö̃ch f. a certain fruit-bearing bramble, Rubus lasiocarpus (L. 73, sur chánch). Cf. suru krilu, p. 933a, l. 26.
m. joy, pleasure (noted only in YZ. 494, 547).
m. (sg. dat. sūrākhas), a hole, opening, orifice (Rām. 269, 716); a perforation; a perforated wound (in the body), a wound (Rām. 1235, 1251).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. suranôwᵘ), to clean or scour a (metal) vessel or the like with ashes; i.q. surawun, q.v. suranôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. suranövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), cleaned, scoured, as ab.
f. (sg. dat. surüʦᵘ̈), occupation, means of subsistence; adequate means (for anything), means of accomplishment. In the latter sense, i.q. sūrath.

f. or (YZ. 224-5) m. (sg. dat. (Śiv.) sūrüʦᵘ̈; (YZ. 47) sūrati صورتہ; or (m.) sūratas صورتس), form, fashion, figure, appearance, aspect (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1276; Rām. 1366; YZ. 18, 47, 224-5); face, countenance; prospect, probability; state, condition (of a thing), case; effigy, image, portrait, statue, picture (Rām. 1159); mental image, idea; beauty, loveliness (YZ. 67, 160); (in Ksh.) occupation, means of subsistence, adequate means (for anything), means of accomplishment (i.q. surath, q.v.); ba- sūrath, adv. in the appearance (of), in the guise (of), in appearance, outwardly (Rām. 1149); cf. surath. --āsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. means of accomplishment to be within reach. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ --गछ़ु॑ञू॒ । साधनसंपत्समागमः f.inf. means of accomplishment to occur, i.e. to be obtained. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to collect means of accomplishment. --rōzun -- m.inf. means of accomplishment to remain over and above (after use).
f. (sg. dat. suraṭi), a certain root used for making black dyes.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. surowᵘ), to clean or scour (a vessel, mirror, etc.) with ashes (cf. ös sᵒ, p. 46b, l. 17) (Rām. 47); i.q. suranāwun, q.v. surowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. surüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), cleaned, scoured, as ab.

m. N. of a particular artery of the human body (Skt. suṣumṇā) (Śiv. 1655).

onomat. f. a rustling sound (H. xii, 23).

adj. (f. sūsᵃmārĕñ), a vile hypocrite, wicked dissembler, a malicious person, a wolf in sheep's clothing (K.Pr. 116).

f. a kind of striped cloth. -palav m. a garment made of this cloth.
(?), in sut pakun, to creep (El.). Cf. sọ̆tᵘ.

m. (sg. dat. sutakas), the ceremonial lustration with incense of the house and family performed by the midwife on the sixth day after a Hindū child's birth (Skt. sūtaka) (K.Pr. 123).

[also written sǖtⁱ or (m.c. Rām. 1594, 1611) sṻtī ] or sṻtin adv. and postpos. governing dat. or abl. (El. set, seth; W. 98, sötⁱ). ¶ A. adv. with, together, in company, as a companion [(sṻty) Rām. 870, 953, 1686, 1756; K. 780; H. vii, 5; x, 14; xii, 2, 16; (sṻtin) Rām. 855; K. 727]. Cf. also bel. ¶ B. Postpos. governing dat., with, together with, associated with, (striving) with, it being implied that the person or thing accompanied is the principal, and he who (or that which) accompanies is the appendage. Thus in mölis-sṻty (or sṻtin) āv, he came with the father, it is implied that the father is the principal, while the son who came is the appendage, i.e. that the father brought the son along with him. If the superiority of the parties is reversed, we must use sān (q.v.) instead of sṻty. Thus mölis-sān āv, indicates that the father is the appendage so that it is implied that the other brought his father along with him [Gr.Gr. 44; Gr.M.; (sṻty) L.V. 57, 92; Śiv. 12, 23, 38, 69, 84, 114-5, 164, 182, 196, 240, 278, 353, 432, 519, 593, etc.; Rām. 35, 73, 88, 103, 120, 171, 176, 327, 330, 428, 435, 448, 484, 530, 611, 690, 705, 803, 848, 904, 943, etc.; (in Rām. 152, 701, the postpos. governs a pron. suff. attached to a verb); K. 200-1, 211, 279, 286 (pron. suff.), 287-8, etc.; H. iii, 7, 8; v. 7, 10; vii, 6; viii, 3, 7, 11, etc.; YZ. 93, etc.; (sṻtin) Śiv. 160, 527, 799, 1460, 1664, 1688; Rām. 361, 1027, 1639, 1647-8, 1677, 1691 (in the foregoing in Rām. the postpos. governs a pron. suff. attached to a verb), (governing dat.) 31, 90, 94-5, 106, 142, 317, 469, 488, etc.; K. 727 (pron. suff.), 748; H. i, 7; YZ. 23]. ¶ Occasionally, in poetry, we find this word governing the dat., when we should expect the abl. Thus (sṻtin) Rām. 33, satas sṻtin pūrᵘ, filled with truth; 838, tas sṻtin (for tami s˚) for that reason, therefore. ¶ C. Governing abl., with, by means of (indicating the instrument). Thus, shrāki-sṻtin, (cut) with a knife (cf. ami-(amiy-)sṻty, p. 55a, l. 12, p. 55b, l. 8; atha-sᵒ, p. 62b, l. 40) [Gr.Gr. 20, sṻtin; 47; Gr.M.; (sṻty) L.V. 25; Śiv. 13, 17-19, 27, 51, 92, 170, 191, 239, 254, etc.; Rām. 6, 16, 47, 233, 449, 479, etc.; K. 5, 154, 165, 171, 232, 247, etc.; H. v, 4; vii, 19; viii, 7; x, 8; xii, 12, 16, 17; YZ. 35, 50; (sṻtin) Śiv. 23-4, 130, 191, 269, 281, 505, 590, 746, 992, etc.; Rām. 409, 435, 457, 478, 480, 582, 703, 839, 1006, 1176, 1200, 1376, 1411, 1648; K. 646; H. ix, 5, 12; YZ. 79]; of, resulting from, with (denoting material, race, stock, etc.), in accordance with; sērĕ mĕʦi sṻty, bricks (made) of clay; āba-sᵒ (filled) with water, Gr.M.) [(sṻty) Śiv. 58, 512, 919, 1200, 1245, 1474; Rām. 285, 1022; K. 231, 350, 414, 921; (sṻtin) K. 984]; in consequence of, by reason of, on account of, owing to, with, by, of, through (bŏchi sṻty, dying of hunger, Gr.M.) [(sṻty) L.V. 83; Śiv. 26, 102, 110, 165, 167, 207, 214, 229, 248, 251, etc.; Rām. 230, 377, 533, 781, etc.; K. 13, 51, 61, 91, 175, 230, 301, etc.; (sṻtin) Śiv. 128, 170, 471; Rām. 96, 199, 200, 603, 655, 828, 1117, 1189, 1192, 1194, 1210, 1221, 1374, 1377, 1379, 1545, 1567, 1618; K. 424, 625]. ¶ Instead of the ablative, we may use the ablative masculine of the genitive. Thus (from ḍĕka) ḍĕkaki sṻtin, by means of the forehead; guri-sṻtin or guri-sandi sṻtin, by means of a horse [Gr.Gr. 47; (sṻty) Śiv. 361, 1018, 1509, 1592-3, 1642; Rām. 176; K. 583; H. i, 3; v, 5; vi, 16; vii, 10, 13; x, 4; (sṻtin) Śiv. 171; H. i, 4]. ¶ In this sense, it sometimes forms a kind of adverb or other indeclinable, as in avë̆zᵘ̈-sṻty, with incorrectness, i.e. wrongly, p. 71a, l. 5; bükʦᵘ̈ sᵒ, courteously, K. 574; devotedly, K. 704; dayāyⁱ-sⁱ, with kindness, i.e. please! p. 267a, l. 3; Śiv. 1223, 1319; gŏḍa-sᵒ, with the beginning, i.e. from the first, p. 277a, l. 41; lōla-sᵒ, affectionately, K. 523; mana-sᵒ, with the heart, cordially, p. 572a, l. 42; [(sṻtin) Śiv. 192, 438, 504, 1411]. ¶ Occasionally, in poetry, we find this word governing the abl., when we should expect the dat. Thus:-- (sṻtin) Rām. 1097, pōshau-s˚ kulᵘ, a tree with flowers. ¶ sṻtin suv postpos. (governing dat.) in close contact with, (of place) right inside, in (or into) the very heart of (Rām. 606). ¶ sṻtinạy, emph. form of sṻtin, with, in company with (Śiv. 647, 684). ¶ sötiy or sṻtiy, emph. form of sṻty, as in tim chih bāzi-sṻtiy dŏh nibāwān, they live only by deceit (Gr.M.; so L.V. 25; Śiv. 1611; K.Pr. 107, suĕtí; id. 208, sutí dugah (i.e. sṻtiy dŏga), by means of pounding, by continued pounding, by blow after blow). ¶ sṻty(sṻtin) anun  m.inf. to bring with one, to bring along ((sṻty) Śiv. 717, 1670; K. 494; (sṻtin) Rām. 971). -bôjᵘ m. one who accompanies, a companion, friend, associate (Śiv. 1832); a follower, a servant (Śiv. 169). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take a person (along) with oneself, to bring (a person) along, to bring in one's train [(sṻty) Śiv. 169, 629, 805, 955, 1116, 1172, 1419-20, 1456, 1459, 1581, 1672 (pānas sṻty hyonᵘ), 1836; Rām. 1039, 1100, 1323, 1554, 1698, 1758; K. 14, 24, 28, 83, 203, etc.; H. ii, 1; v, 6; YZ. 88; (sṻtin) Rām. 1322; K. 647]. --nyunᵘ -- m.inf. to take (a person) with one, to take a person along (Śiv. 1380, 1676 (pānas sṻty nyunᵘ); Rām. 953; K. 69 (pānas sṻty n˚), 196 (id.), 203 (id.), 283 (id.), etc.). --pakun -- m.inf. to go along in company, to accompany, be a fellow traveller (with, dat.) (Rām. 870). --pakawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --pakavüñᵘ̈ --), a fellow traveller (El. set-pakawun). ¶ sṻty-sṻtin adv. accompanying, in company (with a person) (Śiv. 1115, 1134). sṻty-sṻtinạy, id. (Śiv. 636). sṻty-sṻtin hyonᵘ m.inf. to take (a person) along with one. sṻty-sṻty adv. and postpos. with, together (with, dat.), in one company, in society (with) (Śiv. 94, 986, 1054, 1154, 1362, 1445, 1581; Rām. 871, 1779; H. vii, 5; YZ. 25). sṻty-sṻtiy adv., i.q. sṻty-sṻty (Śiv. 1186). ¶ The word sṻtin is naturally scanned in poetry as two long syllables (¯ ¯) as in Rām. 96, dapan sᵃh bīma-sṻtin gāsa hĕth āv, but occasionally it is scanned as ̆ ¯, as in Rām. 95, korukh hārĕn- sṻtin brāryau vĕsápônᵘ. In both these lines the metre is ̆ ¯ ¯ ¯ ̆ ¯ ¯ ¯ ̆ ¯ ¯. In 95 the scansion of vĕsapônᵘ is irregularly ̆ ¯ ¯. Other examples of ̆ ¯ are Rām. 469, 530, 606, 626, 917, 1097, 1163, 1189, 1200, 1280, 1389.
f., i.q. sotᵘ 1 m. q.v., see tᵃla-sᵃ, s.v. tᵃl.
m. the condition of fitting closely (e.g. a cover on dish). Cf. suwa 2.

or (Rām. 606) suv adj. c.g. united, joined together, closely adhering, firmly fixed to, closely fitting together (e.g. a dish and its cover, a bottle and its cork, or the like) (cf. sṻtin-suv, p. 951a, l. 13); cf. suvyō-motᵘ. suwa bĕhun m.inf. (of two things, actions, etc.) to fit closely together, to be intimately united (Rām. 606).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. suwanôwᵘ), to cause to sew, to set a person sewing.

or sawār adj. c.g. and subst. m. mounted, riding (on a horse, etc., dat.) (H. xii, 1, sa˚); embarked (on a ship), riding (in a carriage), etc.; a rider, horseman (cf. shĕh-sᵒ, p. 873a, l. 43), (El. sawār; Gr.M., id.); (pl.) cavalry (Rām. (sa˚) 1323, 1373, 1435). --gaʦhun -- or --sapadun -- m.inf. to ride (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. (sa˚ sö̃panun) 394, 409).
f. wages paid for sewing, a tailor's wages.
n.ag. (f. suwavüñᵘ̈), one who sews, one who is occupied in sewing; a professional sewer, a tailor.

or sawörī f. riding (cf. ratha-sᵒ, p. 847a, l. 17); horsemanship; anything in or on which one rides, a vehicle; retinue, cavalcade, suite (Śiv. (sa˚) 580, 629, 724, 729, 783, 786, 958, 1356; Rām. 1756).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. suwᵘ), to sew (El. siwun, suwun) (Gr.Gr. 22; Gr.M.; L. 463, sivun; K.Pr. 208, 257, 'sow' misprint for 'sew'); to sew together, stitch together; met. to fasten one thing to another as if by sewing (Rām. 448, 1408, 1564). suwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. suvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), sewn, that of which the sewing has been completed.
f. (sg. dat. suwᵃrüñᵃ), fitting (something) closely, fitting or forcing tightly (into something). Cf. suwa 2.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. suwᵃrôwᵃ), to fit tightly together, to join closely together (e.g. a dish and its cover or a bottle and its cork); cf. suwa 2. suwᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. suwᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), closely joined together, as ab.

m. relish, flavour, taste, enjoyment (of food, story, music, or the like) (cf. pā̃-sᵒ, p. 748a, l. 19) (K. 1147; K.Pr. 167, 200); prudence based on experience (of the results of dissipation, or of suffering from robbery, or from heedlessness, or the like). (Cf. sād 1.) ¶ swādas pyonᵘ m.inf. to fall into experience, to act cautiously as the result of unfortunate experience. --wātun -- m.inf. (after acting heedlessly) to adopt a cautious attitude born of experience.
m. with a quarter, increased by a fourth, a quarter more (than) (cf. dūnᵘ-sôdᵘ, three-quarters and one and a quarter, p. 223b, l. 27) (W. 105). Cf. sawā.
adj. (f. swādüjᵘ̈), having a taste, flavoured (sweet, bitter, sour, or so on) (of food, a story, a song, or the like).
m. (a borrowed Skt. term) the ejaculation of the word swāhā, which is an exclamation used in making oblations to the gods (Śiv. 8).
i.q. sāl 1 m. an invitation (L. 460, sawálá; K. 402-4, 638).
m. heaven (a word borrowed from Skt.) (L.V. 9).

adj. and pron. own; self. This is a Skt. word, and occurs only in borrowed Skt. compounds. Owing to the fact that wa following a consonant, and u in borrowed words, are both, in Ksh., pronounced as ŏ, this word is frequently employed to suggest a double meaning, as in the following:-- swa-darshĕna-myūlᵘ m. union with the Self (i.e. God) (brought about) by visiting (holy places), or union (brought about) by the excellent visiting (of holy places) (sŏ-darshĕna-myūlᵘ) (L.V. 36). swa-man-bāg m. the garden of one's own heart, or a jasmine garden (sŏman-bāg) (L.V. 98 = K.Pr. 18). swa-mana-sọ̆thᵘ m. the embankment of (the illusions of) one's own mind, or (suman-sọ̆thᵘ) an embankment with crazy bridges (sum) (L.V. 98). swa-para-vĕʦār m. discrimination regarding the Self and the Supreme or discrimination regarding Him who is excellently supreme (sŏ-para-vĕʦār) (L.V. 28). swa-vĕʦār m. discrimination on one's own Self, or sŏ-vĕʦār good discrimination (L.V. 71, 79). Cf. sŏ-vĕʦār. ¶ swa-rṻph m. own form, i.e. the nature (of anything), identity with, as in kha-swarṻph, He who is identical with absolute vacuity, the impersonal Supreme Deity (L.V. 15); niza-swarṻph, the nature of what is one's own, the nature of Self (L.V. 67). swa-swarṻph m. (sg. dat. -swarṻpas), a person's own form or nature (cf. sŏrṻph) (Śiv. 12, 1069). swa-swayĕm m. one who is one's own self, one who is the Self (an epithet of the Deity) (Śiv. 1850).
f. (a borrowed Skt. term) freedom of will, free will, independence (Śiv. 1484).

f. (sg. dat. swöʦᵘ̈), a certain auspicious constellation, the star Arcturus (as forming the fourteenth Nakṣatra or lunar asterism, in Skt. Svāti). swöʦᵘ̈-tārukh m. (sg. dat. -tārakas), the star Arcturus.
or swātmā m. (a word borrowed from Skt.) one's own self; hence, the Self recognized as identical with the Supreme (L.V. (˚mā) 39, 40, 61; Śiv. (˚ma) 606).
adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, heaven (see sŏrg), heavenly; met. worthy of heaven, magnificent, luxurious (of garments or the like) (K. 925, 1046).

adj. (f. së̆zᵘ̈ 2), straight, not crooked, direct, even (cf. syodᵘ dastār, p. 256b, l. 20 (Gr.M.; W. 113 (siud), 123, 139; Śiv. 1018; K. 71; YZ. 298; K.Pr. 34, 39, 137, 191); opposite, facing (cf. sĕda syodᵘ, p. 864a, l. 39) (H, viii, 6, 13); straightforward, honest, fair, candid, sincere (Gr.M.; Śiv. 471; K. 1021; K.Pr. 83); kindly (K. 384); plain, simple, easy, not difficult; straight, upright (YZ. 532; K.Pr. 78, 208); straight, regular (Gr.M.); direct (of a road) (Gr.M., K.Pr. 188); cf. sĕda. --anun -- m.inf. to bring straight, to correct, rebuke (a naughty child, or the like) (K. 140). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go straight and unopposed to one's object (K. 433, 1059). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain straight and facing (something); to act in agreement with, be favourable to. --sāda -- adj. (f. --së̆zᵘ̈ sāda --), simple, straight- forward, artless (Śiv. 1218, 1305); (of clothes, ornaments or the like) moderate, not extravagant and not bad, decent, becoming, suitable. --syodᵘ -- adv. without delay, straightway, at once and without impediment. ¶ syoduy adv. straightway, without impediment (Śiv. 86, 432); truthfully, honestly (Śiv. 1295). ¶ sĕzi wati pakun m.inf. to go on a straight road, to go on the highway (not by byways) (cf. Śiv. 1805, 1830); met. to lead an honest, straightforward life. ¶ së̆zᵘ̈ müñᵘ̈ f. 'the straight pupil of the eye'; hence, a straight, open, countenance (K.Pr. 60); met. successful accomplishment. --müñᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. successful accomplishment to occur (esp. when unexpected and a matter of good luck).

or syombᵘ m. (sg. dat. sĕmis or sĕmbis), sediment, silt (cf. nambala-sᵒ, p. 637b, l. 19); a power of causing slight intoxication. --bĕhun -- m.inf. sediment or silt to settle (at the bottom of water).

adj. (f. së̆ñᵘ̈), soft, tender (as food by prolonged cooking) (cf. aḍa-sᵒ, p. 12a, l. 13); slow, dull-witted, dull, soft; (of cooked food) without salt, insufficiently salted or seasoned (cf. aḍa-sᵒ, as ab.; atha-sᵒ, p. 62b, 48); (of a hard-hearted person) rendered tender-hearted (by adversity, sorrow, or the like); cf. sĕnun. --kyonᵘ -- adj. (f. së˘ñᵘ̈kë˘ñᵘ̈), (of food or the like) gone bad and corrupt for want of salt.
adj. (f. së̆pᵘ̈), having a swollen face; slow, dilatory, lazy.
adj. (f. së̆sᵘ̈), slow-natured, inert, inactive, torpid; a pimp, pander.
(W. 156) (i.q. سید) m. a lord, chief, prince; any descendant of Ḥusain (who was the grandson of Muḥammad), a Saiyid (W. 156).

m. (sg. dat. sīlis, abl. sēli), N. of a game formerly played by boys in Kashmīr. It is said to be extinct for half a century. In it a peg or post to which a long rope is fastened, is firmly fixed in the ground. One boy holding the other end of the rope taut, runs round in a circle, while the others try to catch him. He wards them off by kicking. If any boy succeeds in catching him, the captor takes his place, and so on till each has had his turn. The winner is the boy who succeeds in making the greatest number of complete circles.
m. (sg. dat. sindis), the river Sindh, one of the three principal rivers of Kashmīr. Its waters are sacred (L.V. 81).

m. (sg. dat. sinis. With the suff. of the indef. art. this word takes the form sinwāh, cf. gŏgᵃji-sᵃ, p. 279a, l. 25), a vegetable sauce, broth, stew (cf. böʦᵘ̈-sᵘ̈, p. 146a, l. 25; dŏda-sᵒ, p. 190a, l. 25; gŏgᵃji- sinwāh, as ab.; hŏkha-sᵒ, p. 327a, l. 36; nadȧrⁱ- sᵒ, p. 623a, l. 43) (K.Pr. 8, 42 (sun), 87 (id.) 93, 155, 201, 205, 219); what is eaten along with rice, and is either vegetables, meat, or fish (El. sun, syun; Gr.Gr. 163); a dish of food (L. 459, sun); a flesh-broth; flesh for broth (cf. nījĕ-sᵒ, p. 626b, l. 43). ¶ sinⁱ-bạrⁱg m. a single leaf of a vegetable suitable for making broth; met. a very little of vegetables and other materials for broth; -dĕv m. (f. -dĕviñ), one who eats much broth, a soup-gobbler. -gāsh m. cheapness or plenty of vegetables and other materials for broth; plenty of broth. -köñᵘ̈ f. a few vegetables (this word cannot be employed if meat is included in the idea) (Gr.Gr. 163). -lë̆jᵘ̈ f. a saucepan for making broth; a vessel full of broth, a full soup-tureen. -lakta m. a large lump of meat (such as a lump of a shoulder of mutton) for making broth. -muhim m. dearness or scarcity of materials for making broth, or of broth. -muhima sŏʦal f. 'mallows when soup is dear'; met. (when something necessary is unobtainable) an inferior substitute (K.Pr. 201). -milawan f. (sg. dat. -milavüñᵘ̈), a custom between neighbours of exchanging broth (indicating intimacy and similarity of caste). -myulᵘ m. 'soup-terms', a state of friendship between neighbours in which they are on terms of exchanging broth. -pholᵘ m. a tasty morsel in broth. -rān f. (for dat., see rān) the thick part of a leg of mutton or goat, suitable for making broth. -thaph f. (sg. dat. -thapi), a gobbet (or as much as can be taken up by all the fingers) of the solid part of broth. -thôpᵘ m., i.q. -köñᵘ̈, ab. (Gr.Gr. 164). -tulᵘ m., i.q. -köñᵘ̈, ab., a small amount of vegetables for making broth (cf. Gr.Gr. 164). -zanḍ m., i.q. köñᵘ, ab. (Gr.Gr. 163).

m. (sg. dat. siris), powdered rice, rice flour (Śiv. 702-3, K. 1118). ¶ sirⁱ-lôdⁱ m. a heaped up pile of rice-flour. -pholᵘ m. a small amount of rice-flour (K. 1144). -wugra m. porridge of rice-flour.

m. (sg. dat. sīris, abl. sēri), giddiness, vertigo, dizziness (cf. gyūrᵘ syūrᵘ, p. 318a, p. 16). sīrⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. dizziness to happen, to be dizzy; met. to become torpid (from heavy eating or the like).

adj. (f. sīrᵘ̈ 4, for 1-3, see s.vv.; m. sg. dat. sīris, abl. sēri), weighing (so many) seers (nominally of two pounds each), used --˚, as in daha-syūrᵘ, p. 199a, l. 16; dusyūrᵘ, p. 257a, l. 1; ḍāyĕ-syūrᵘ, p. 266b, l. 29; pönʦa- syūrᵘ, p. 743b, l. 1; shĕ-syūrᵘ, p. 874a, l. 19).
1 p.p. of siwun, q.v. cooked, domesticated, etc. (cf. aḍa-sᵒ, p. 12a, l. 18; ʦūra-sᵒ, s.v. ʦūr).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sᵒḍᵒ; 2 p.p. sᵃjyōv), to bear, endure, suffer patiently (abuse or the like).

sometimes written sᵘ̈h m. (f. sīmiñ, q.v.), a lion (cf. dȧngⁱ-sⁱh, p. 226b, l. 44; khar-sᵃh, p. 407a, l. 31; pādar-sᵃh, p. 682b, l. 7; shīnuwᵘ-sᵘh, s.v. shīnuwᵘ) (Śiv. 1854; Rām. 16, 96, 807, 862, 971, 1108d, 1301, 1332, 1630; K. 222, 661, 673-4, 678; K.Pr. 30, 49, 64, 172, 215); a tiger (El. sah, suh; Gr.M.); a leopard (Gr.M.; L. 109 suh, Felis pardus; K.Pr. 249). In modern Ksh. the word apparently means only 'leopard', lions or tigers not being found in the Valley. In Rām. the word probably means 'lion'. Cf. simh. ¶ sᵃha-gŏph f. (sg. dat. gŏphi), a lion's den. -grazun m. (sg. dat. -grazanas), a lion's roar. -gō̃ʦh f. (sg. dat. gō̃ʦhi), the lion's whiskers; met. the bristly bitter leaves of a certain plant. -musla m. a lion's skin (Śiv. 816, 894 (in both -musala)). -nam m. a tiger's claw. -pūtᵘ m. a tiger's whelp; met. a brave intelligent boy.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sᵒhᵒ; f. sᵘ̈hᵘ̈), to bear patiently, endure, suffer; cf. sahun, of which the 2 p.p. is sashyōv. sᵒhᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. sᵘ̈hᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), borne patiently.

or sanīh m. affection, love; liking for, a taste for (some thing, occupation, etc.); cf. srah. --barun -- m.inf. to feel affection, to love; to be of an affectionate disposition. ¶ sᵃniha-(sanīha-)vyotᵃ  adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), full of love (for some one), enamoured (of), fond of, of an affectionate disposition; (of some thing, quality, occupation, or the like), causing love, attractive, captivating, arousing feelings of love.

m. a breaking of wind without noise, a silent fart (cf. ḍĕkⁱ sᵃs trāwȧnⁱ, p. 204b, l. 46) (El. sis, f.). --ʦalun -- m.inf. such wind to abscond (i.e. escape and disappear); hence, met. braggard boasting to result (at the time of action) in feeble futility. ¶ sᵃsa-phȧṭᵃ gaʦhun m.inf. be destroyed silently (or privately) and become dissipated, quietly to go bad and become worthless (for the idiom cf. kŏla-phȧṭⁱ gaʦhun, p. 716a, l. 5). -phȧṭⁱ karun m.inf. privately (or silently) to render something worthless as ab.
adj. c.g. one who suffers from inability to retain wind (see sᵃs).

f. heat, great warmth, fervent heat, boiling heat (El. sȧsar, sisar); lightning in rain, rain (believed to be boiling) accompanied by lightning; cf. bᵃsar. --aʦüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of water) the boiling point to be reached. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. rain accompanied by lightning (believed to be boiling) to fall. --ʦhunüñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to throw boiling water (on a person). ¶ sᵃsari-gŏgᵃjᵃ f. a kind of turnip cooked by long boiling. sᵃsari-wôñᵃ m. boiling or very hot water.
n.ag. (f. sᵃsavüñᵃ), one who owing to disease or having eaten certain food is unable to retain his wind (see sᵃs).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sᵒsᵒ; 2 p.p. sᵃsyōv or sᵃsōv, Gr.Gr. 208. This verb is impersonal) to break wind, fart (esp. without noise) (Gr.Gr. 208); met. to talk boastfully and do nothing.

m. (sg. dat. sᵃtras or sᵃtᵃras), thread (cf. paṭa-sᵒ, p. 793b, l. 33) (El. sathir, thread); string, line, cord; a bunch, or hank, of thread; an aphoristic rule, a technical or memorial rule; cotton which has been carded and cleansed, but not yet spun into thread (El. sathir, cotton, sithar, cotton without seeds; K.Pr. 214, situr). --trāwun -- m.inf. to set the thread (on the loom); hence, to make the preliminaries for a work to be undertaken. ¶ sᵃtra-(or sᵃtᵃra-)dōr  f. a long stretch of cotton cloth as issuing from the loom, a 'thān' of cloth, cloth in the piece. -dōra m. a loom for weaving. -kônᵘ m. the roll or ball of cotton thread as wound on the distaff (El.). -kāñᵉ̆r f., id. -poṭᵘ m. a kind of cloth, in which the woof is of cotton and the warp of wool. -ʦādar f. a sheet of a cloth of which the woof is of cotton and the warp of wool.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. sᵒtᵒ, f. sᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈; 2 p.p. sᵃʦōv), to force into, violently to push into, crowd into. sᵒtᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. sᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), forced into, pushed into.

m. a tailor (cf. janda-sᵒ, p. 375a, l. 28; ṭŏpa-sᵒ; ṭōpi-sᵒ, s.v. ṭūpⁱ) (Gr.Gr. 32; L. 464, suts; W. 18, sats; L.V. 103; Rām. 911). -mŏzūrⁱ 1 f. the amount paid to a tailor for work done, a tailor's wages.

m. a large strong needle (such as is used for sewing sacks. An ordinary needle is sᵃʦan 2, q.v.); cf. suwa 1, and Waḵẖī siʦ, a needle. -muʦᵘ m. the bits of cloth that are left over and unused after a tailor has cut out and made a garment; met. a tailor's profits; cf. muʦᵘ and mŏʦun. -mŏzūrⁱ 2 f. a living made by the needle, the livelihood or profession of a tailor.
m. (sg. dat. sᵃʦanas), warning, informing, esp. by hinting, private indication, gestures, or the like.

f. (sg. dat. sᵃʦüñᵃ), a needle (for sewing) (a large needle is sᵃʦ 2, q.v.) (cf. janda-sᵒ, p. 375a, l. 21; phȧlⁱ-sⁱ, p. 694b, l. 22); ṭōpi-sᵒ, s.v. ṭūpⁱ (Gr.M.; L. 462, satzan; K.Pr. 208). ¶ sᵃʦüñᵃ- (also written sᵃʦᵃñĕ-)kömᵃ  (usually written by Hindūs) f. 'needle-work', i.e. silk embroidery. -mŏzūrⁱ f. needle-work, a livelihood gained by needle-work, a tailor's profession, tailoring. -pohᵘ m. 'a needle's spleen', i.e. a needle's eye. -powᵘ or -pôwᵘ m. a needle's eye (K.Pr. 190, sĕʦanih páwih, by the eye of a needle). Like pohᵘ, -powᵘ also means 'spleen'. -pyotᵘ m. the point of a needle.
f. a festival indicating (see sᵃʦan 1) some event, as in sŏkh-sᵃʦan, p. 905b, l. 4, a festival in honour of some happy event.

. The seventeenth (or, if we count the aspirates ch, kh, and ph, and also the sibilant sh, as separate letters, the twenty-first) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet when written in the Roman character, the sixteenth (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z as separate letters, the nineteenth) consonant when written in the Śāradā or in the Nāgarī character, and the fourth consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. Its Kāshmīrī name is tōv tö. It is sounded nearly like the dental t of India proper, but the dental colour is not so decided, and the letter is liable to be confounded with the cerebral ṭ (q.v. bel.). It is also used to represent the Arabic letter t̤ ط (t̤ōē), which, in Kāshmīrī, occurs only in words borrowed directly or indirectly from that language. In such cases, the t̤ ط is pronounced in Kāshmīrī like an ordinary t. ¶ The aspirate of t is th تہ, which is the seventeenth (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z as separate letters, the twentieth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet when written in the Śāradā or in the Nāgarī character. Its Kāshmīrī name is thöshⁱ thö. ¶ When the letter t is followed, in a Kāshmīrī word, by ü-mātrā (but not when followed by i or i-mātrā) it is changed to ʦ. Thus, the nominative plural of the base rāt-, night, is röʦᵘ̈. Similarly, ty becomes ʦ, and tĕ becomes ʦa. Thus, the 2 p.p. of katun, to spin, is kaʦōv (for *katyōv), and from the base tat-, hot, we have the abstract noun taʦar (for *tatĕr), heat. In the same way, the aspirate th becomes ʦh, as in wọ̆thᵘ, arisen, feminine wö̆ʦhᵘ̈; the 2 p.p. of wŏthun, to arise, is wŏʦhōv (for *wŏthyōv); and from the base wath-, free, we have the abstract noun waʦhar (for *wathĕr), freedom. See Gr.Gr. 28; Gr.M., p. 22. ¶ For the interchange of t and ṭ, see bel. s.v. ṭ.

. The eighteenth (or, if we count the aspirates ch, kh, and ph, and also the sibilant sh, as separate letters, the twenty-second) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet when written in the Roman character, the eleventh (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z as separate letters, the fourteenth) consonant in the Śāradā or in the Nāgarī character, and the fifth consonant in the Perso-Arabic character. Its Kāshmīrī name is ār mã̄ṭa. It is sounded approximately like the cerebral ṭ of India proper, but it is not so decidedly cerebral, being more nearly post-alveolar, so that it is liable to be confused with the dental t dealt with in the preceding article. ¶ The aspirate of ṭ is ṭh, the twelfth (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z as separate letters, the fifteenth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī language when written in the Śāradā or in the Nāgarī character. Its Kāshmīrī name is sar mã̄ṭha. ¶ When the letter ṭ is followed in a Kāshmīrī word by i, ĕ, or y (but not when followed by i-mātrā or ü-mātrā) it is changed to c. Thus, the base paṭ-, a board, has its nominative singular püṭᵘ̈, but its ablative singular is paci, its nominative plural is pacĕ, and its ablative plural pacyau. Similarly, in such cases, the aspirate ṭh becomes ch. Thus, kāṭh-, a stalk, nominative singular köṭhᵘ̈, ablative singular kāchi, nominative plural kāchĕ, and ablative plural kāchyau. See Gr.Gr. 29; Gr.M., p. 22. ¶ Allusion has been made above to the tendency observable in Kāshmīrī to confuse the dental t and th with the cerebral ṭ and ṭh, respectively. So strong is this tendency that Kāshmīrī poets do not hesitate to rhyme a word containing a dental letter with another containing a cerebral. For instance, in Rām. 699, the word Yindᵃrzīth is rhymed with ḍīṭhᵘ̈, and, in 872, with bīṭhᵘ̈,--rhymes which would be unthinkable in India Proper, where there is a sharp distinction between the sound of th and that of ṭh. In the following words there is confusion between initial t (th) and ṭ (ṭh):--tāḍav or ṭāḍav, swelling; tō̃g or ṭō̃g, an elephant-goad; thŏba or ṭhŏbba, a sherd; ṭhēla, a bag, compared with the Hindī thailā; thanḍ, cool, compared with the Hindī ṭhaṇḍā; thingun or ṭhingun, a pretty child; thāpēra or ṭhāpēra, a slap; tālun or ṭālun, to displace; tŏṭh or ṭọ̆ṭᵘ, cotton-seed; tö̃th or ṭē̃ṭh, self-conceit; tö̃th or ṭö̃ṭhᵘ̈, a filament; tōṭhun or ṭōṭhun, to be pleased; tatarārav or ṭaṭarārav, pattering; ṭyoṭhᵘ, bitter, as compared with Skt. tikta-, H. tītā. The following are a few examples of the same tendency in regard to letters that are not initial:--phī˜tun or phī˜ṭun, a rag; pitun or pīṭun, to become weary; musht-, a fist, compared with Skt. muṣṭi-; and pāthun, to become, compared with pāṭhi (p. 794a, l. 13), may it become. There are many other similar cases that have not yet been collected.
preposition, to, until, as far as (Rām. 259, 797, 1058 tā ba-ī˜-hāl, up to the present time); adv. as long as, whilst (YZ. 7).

conjnct. and (W. 99 tạ; L.V. 3, 4, 13, etc.; Śiv. 12, 13, 39, 43, etc.; Rām. 22, 68, 85, 87, 98, etc.; K. 18, 21, 24, 31, 36, 53, etc.; H. i, 5; iii, 5; v, 4, 9, 12, etc.). ¶ This conjunction is used to connect single words in the singular number, as in suh ta ʦᵃh, he and thou. For connecting plural words, ti (q.v.) is used in preference to ta, as in mahanivⁱ ti gupan ti āy, both the men and the cattle came (Gr.Gr. 255); but this distinction is not always observed in conversation. ¶ If it is required to connect clauses, instead of words, biyĕ is generally used (El. s.v. tah; so Śiv. 163, 799; YZ. 82), but ta is also occasionally employed for this purpose (see Gr.M., s.v. for examples; so, e.g., Rām. 123, 135-6, 221, 867, and elsewhere). ¶ ta sometimes has a slightly adversative sense, almost equivalent to 'but' as in jism chuh fönī, ta rūh chuh bökī, the body is mortal, and (or but) the soul is immortal (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 152, 178). ¶ na-ta 1, and not, nor (see p. 618a, l. 3); yā... na ta, either... or (W. 153); na... ta na, neither... nor (W. 153); na... na... ta, not... nor... nor (L.V. 15). ¶ ta biyĕ, conjnct. and also, moreover, (this) as well as (that) (Gr.M.; Rām. 124, 1389, 1534). ta... biyĕ..., conjnct. both... and (H. viii, 9). ta... ta..., conjnct. both... and. ¶ With emph y, ta becomes tay 1 or töy 1, qq.v.

conjnct. then, so, accordingly, therefore (L.V. 21, 30, 33, 42, etc.; K.Pr. 173); then, and then, and next, thereupon (L.V. 1, 4, 19, 23, etc.); then, and then, thereafter, but (L.V. 98); then, so that (L.V. 66); ¶ then, indicating the apodosis of a conditional, or quasi-conditional, sentence (Gr.M.; L.V. 2, 27, 55, 87; H. ii, 7; iii, 4; vii, 9; viii, 10); or the antecedent clause of a relative clause (L.V. 61). ¶ Sometimes ta connects a conjunctive participle with the main verb of a sentence, as in yĕḍ phŏllavith ta mŏyĕ, having distended her belly, (then) she died (Gr.M.). This last idiom is especially common in K. Typical examples will be found in K. 553, 582, 838. ¶ Added to an Imperative, something like the Hindī tō, ta makes it polite, as in kar, do; kar-ta, please to do (Gr.Gr. 249. Cf. K. 201, 1174; K.Pr. 238, tai for tay 2, see bel.). ¶ This word is often almost untranslatable, or equivalent to 'in fact', 'forsooth' and so on, as in bŏh ta suh zānan-na, (how can I judge him) I, in fact, don't know him (Gr.M.; H. viii, 9). Sometimes it has the force of 'still', 'nevertheless' as in katiy rūzⁱtan, ta nākhŏshᵘ̈y chuh, stay where he may, still he is unhappy (Gr.M.; so L.V. 60). It is sometimes a pure expletive, as at the end of two lines of every verse in K. ¶ With emph. y, ta becomes tay 2 or töy 2, qq.v. ¶ na-ta 2 or na-tay is used to mean 'or else' 'otherwise' (see p. 618a, ll. 4, 11); yā-tay... na-ta, either... or else (K.Pr. 239).

m. heat; ague, fever (cf. khām tᵒ, p. 400a, l. 23; lōsa tᵒ, p. 533a, l. 26; pokᵘ tᵒ, p. 724b, l. 49; sọ̆tᵘ tᵒ, p. 943a, l. 23) (El.; L. 458; H. v, 3, 10). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. fever to occur; to be filled with great anger (so that, as in a fever, one does not desire to converse, to hear, or even to eat). --karun -- m.inf. fever to appear, signs of fever to become evident.
heat, warmth; power, ability, in bē-tāb, q.v.; enduring, brooking (Śiv. 584, Rām. 1324); heat of the sun (= tāv, q.v.) (H. 397). Cf. bē-tāb.
m. a lattice, window; (in Ksh.) an umbrella, sunshade; met. a leaf hut (which is merely a protection from the sun) (Rām. 1253). Cf. tāpa-dāna, s.v. tāph.
adj. c.g. ruined, destroyed. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be ruined; (of a ship or boat) to be wrecked (Gr.M.).

or tabukh m. (sg. dat. tabakhas), a cover, lid; a large dish or plate, a tray (cf. dachĕ-tᵒ, p. 186a, l. 9); a basin, bowl; a large jar (cf. mā̃ch-tᵒ, p. 547b, l. 10); a vessel for kneading dough in; (in Ksh.) a certain severe disease involving intestinal tumour. -bata m. a great festival dinner served in large dishes. -nāl m. a kind of coat-collar (the same shape in front and behind, so that, as required, it can be worn back to front); met. one who always agrees with the majority (e.g. who follows, as occasion demands, the religion of the people among whom he finds himself:-- a Śaiva among Śaivas, a Vaiṣṇava among Vaiṣṇavas, a Jain among Jains, and so on). --püṭᵘ̈ -- f. (sg. dat. -pacĕ), a kind of shelf close up to the edge of the ceiling, forming a recess in which articles can be placed or kept. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. intestinal tumour to occur in a person.
m. a large drum; a drum, a tambourine; (esp.) a kettle-drum (Rām. 831, 975).

f. a hatchet, an axe (Rām. 934, 1096, 1176). tabar-dār تبردار m. an axe-bearer, armed with an axe (L. 458 tabadár); a wood-cutter, a woodman (El., K.Pr. 137). -dārĕñ f. a female wood-cutter; a wood-cutter's wife. -dörī f. the profession or occupation of a wood- cutter. tabar-tēg تبرتیغ m. a kind of axe with a long edge, and a sharp spike on the upper side.
f. the sugar of the bamboo, bamboo-manna (a siliceous deposit on the joints of the bamboo).
töbīdār (= تابعدار) adj. c.g. obedient, subject (to), submissive (Gr.M.; Śiv. 340, tābē˚); servant, etc.
(sg. dat. tabīyĕtas), nature, personal character, disposition (Gr.M.). tabīyĕta-kinⁱ adv. by nature, naturally, by natural disposition (Gr.M.).
m. abuse (El.). --kaḍun -- or -- m.inf. to abuse (El.).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. tābyōv), to be brilliant, to shine (of the sun or moon) (Rām. 1002, 1278, 1372).
(? gend.) a bier, a kind of temporary coffin used at Moslem funerals (L. 271 tabut); an oblong case put over a grave.

tabᵘ̈cᵘ̈, or tabücᵘ̈ f. a kind of earthenware dish or saucer (cf. diwᵃʦa-tᵃ, p. 265a, l. 49; mala-tᵒ, p. 565a, l. 2). Cf. tabakh. tabacĕ pĕñĕ f. pl. inf. saucers (of abuse) to fall, i.e. (of a son, a servant, or the like) to become subjected to scolding (by an angry parent, master, or the like). --parañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to recite saucers (of scolding), to scold, as ab.
m. a kind of turban made up of a long narrow strip of cotton or woollen cloth.
f. a small axe useful for splitting firewood or the like (Śiv. 860).
m. forwardness, boldness, insolence, daring; sharpness, keenness (Gr.Gr. 139). Cf. ṭokᵘ.
m. N. of a remedy for eye disease, made of the flour of a certain grain (cf. nẹ̆ndᵃri-tᵃ, p. 642b, l. 16).
m. a certain tender grass, a favourite fodder for horses.

f. (sg. dat. tachi), scratching (Gr.Gr. 125); itchiness, itch. Cf. tüchᵘ̈ 1. ¶ tacha-bacha m. a means of employment, livelihood (esp. as a master). -bacha karun m.inf. to work at such a means of livelihood. -tacha m. longing, desire, great anxiety (for something lost or beyond reach, but very necessary; quasi, scratching about to find it); cf. tachun. -tacha karun m.inf. 'to scratch about', (when something in a house has disappeared and it is feared that it has been carried off by rats or the like) to go about searching in every little hole or hollow in the walls.
m. love, affection (for anything animate or inanimate) (Gr.Gr. 139). Cf. ṭôṭhᵘ.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. tochᵘ, f. tüchᵘ̈ 2, for 1, see s.v.), to pare, shave, scrape; to plane (wood or the like) (Gr.Gr. 121, 125); to excoriate (cf. khōrĕ tachañĕ, p. 412a, l. 40); to scratch (with the nails or the like) (K.Pr. 82); to scratch (the ground, as a fowl) (Rām. 97, K.Pr. 118). tochᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tüchᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), pared, planed, excoriated, scratched, etc., as ab.
f. scratching, a scratch (with the nails etc.) (cf. gala-tachañĕ, p. 282b, l. 1).
m. embezzlement, peculation, squandering property entrusted to one (e.g. in gambling, in in wantonness, or the like). --karun -- m.inf. to embezzle, as ab.
f. a vile unchaste woman, a low strumpet.
f. angry admonition (of a naughty boy, or the like), angry reproof (including, if necessary, slapping or the like).
m. puffing with the cheeks blown out; arrogant puffing.
m. slight swelling of the face, eyelids, etc., due to indigestion; met. pride, arrogance.
adv. then only, then and not till then (L.V. 77).

m. (this word is fem. in Urdū) a device, contrivance (Gr.M.; Rām. 349, 360, 823, 869, 882); counsel, advice, as in cyāni tadbīra mūjūb, according to thy advice (Gr.M.; so Rām. 117). --karun -- m.inf. to consult, take mutual advice (Rām. 544); to consider, take counsel with oneself (Rām. 1413).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. tôḍᵘ, f. töḍᵘ̈, f. sg. dat. tājĕ; 2 p.p. tājyōv, or (Gr.Gr. xxxiv), according to some, tāḍyōv), to admonish angrily, to reprove in anger or slap (a naughty boy, or the like), to punish (by beating). tôḍᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. töḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, with sg. dat. tājĕ-maʦĕ), reproved, punished, etc., as above.
m. glory, brilliancy (of the sun, or the like) i.q. tāph, q.v. (YZ. 174).

f. a long line or row. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cast (grain, or the like) in lines. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to become laid in rows (automatically). ¶ tȧgⁱ-tagay f. a complete row. ¶ tagi tagi adv. in rows, in lines (Śiv. 1857). tagi tagi bĕhun m.inf. to sit in rows. --tagi rōzun -- m.inf. to remain in lines. --tagi thawun -- m.inf. to arrange in rows.

or tö̃g f. the braying of an ass (cf. khar-ṭᵒ, p. 407a, l. 26) (Gr.M.); the lowing of cattle (El.). Cf. ṭū̃g. ṭã̄ga-ṭã̄g f. loud and excessive braying of asses; similar cries uttered by other animals.
m.pl. inflamed or bloody bruises (resulting from a blow). Cf. tō̃g or ṭō̃g.
c.g. one who howls in anguish (cf. ṭã̄gun 1).

a platter, pail, bucket, tub, trough; a mason's mud- or lime-pit (cf. rabi-tᵒ, p. 823b, l. 5). --karun -- m.inf. to make mud plaster or mud mortar; to make liquid mud (to serve the purpose of writing or daubing large letters or the like).
f. 'uttering repeated cries like the braying of an ass', i.e. the utterance of cries of alarm or pain by cattle.
m. a man who makes mud plaster or mortar.
f. a large tub or trough, a kneading trough.

conj 2 (1 p.p. togᵘ, f. tüjᵘ̈ 1, for 2, see talun; 2 p.p. tajyōv 1, for 2, see id.) to be known how to be done, to be possible (in this sense,--as compared with hĕkun, which means, generally, to be physically able,--tagun, on the contrary, implies skilled knowledge, as in kamis tagi wanunᵘ, to whom is saying possible? i.e. who can tell) (cf. mangun tᵒ, p. 579a, l. 30) (Gr.Gr. 204; Gr.M.; W. 86; L.V. 24, 37; Śiv. 1276, 1727, 1852; Rām. 325, 360, 988; K. 364; H. i, 15; v, 3, 8, 9; viii, 9; x, 5; K.Pr. 208). togᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ 1, for 2, see talun), done by being known how to be done, done successfully.
conj. 1 impers. (1 p.p. ṭō̃gᵘ; 2 p.p. ṭã̄jyōv), to emit a loud cry or roar, (esp.) to bray (of an ass) (Gr.Gr. xxx); to howl in anguish.
m. a small horse, a pony.
or tāgᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the thread (of silver or gold and ornamented) worn round the waist by Hindū women, a woman's girdle.
(f. ṭã̄givᵘ̈), made of pear-wood. Cf. ṭang.

cf. تاہ) ground, site, floor; bottom, underneath, foundation; layer, stratum; fold plait, ply, the fold of a folded garment, etc. (Śiv. 129); a fold or sheet of paper or the like (Gr.M.). --karun -- m.inf. to fold, to fold up (W. 143); to arrange in folds or layers; (generally) to put into neat order (Śiv. 1148); to take care of (K.Pr. 173). --karith thawun -- m.inf. to fold up; carefully and neatly to put by. ¶ tāha bĕhanāwan m.inf. to leave at the bottom, throw into the background, surpass. tāha tāha thawun m.inf. to put one over the other, to pile up in an orderly manner. ¶ tāhas bĕhanāwun m.inf. to put at the bottom, put in the background; (by showing superiority), to cause another to abandon work on which he is engaged.
m. the noise made in driving away crows.
tahkīkāt تحقیقات m. (sg. dat. tahakikātas), an inquiry, investigation, inquest (Gr.M.).
f. service, attendance; esp. attendance on a human being, on cattle, horses, etc., similar service (El. ṭohul).
m. a servant, attendant, a groom, cowherd, shepherd, or the like (El. tahalyí (sic), a groom).
f., i.q. ṭahal, q.v. esp. personal attendance on a person, the duties of a valet.
? m. (among Musalmāns) ceremonial ablution, the ablution before prayers (K.Pr. 63).
(for تحقیق) adv. of a certainty, certainly, assuredly (H. x, 12; xi, 13; xii, 3).
m. a servant, attendant; (esp.) a groom (H. x, 5, 12).

f. boiled rice cooked with turmeric, salt, and oil, and yellow in colour (eaten by Kāshmīrīs, and used in oblations cast forth to be consumed by birds and animals) (cf. tīla-tᵒ, s.v. tīl, ʦaka-tᵒ, s.v. ʦaka) (tahar, in El. (m.); L. 463; K.Pr. 29, 55). ¶ tahāri-phakīr m. (f. -phȧkⁱröñⁱ), a beggar who takes and eats such yellow rice, which has been cast forth in oblation; met. one who is miserably poor. --pholᵘ -- m. a small quantity of yellow rice which has been cast forth as an oblation. -thapul m. (f. -thapüjᵘ̈ or -thapȧjⁱ), a plunderer of oblations of yellow rice.
(? spelling) m. a certain deer, the Hemitragus jemlaicus (L. 114).

m. a collector of revenue, a tax-gatherer (commonly looked upon as an example of inevitableness and mercilessness) (K.Pr. 56); (in Ksh.) the chief magistrate of a tahsīl, or large division of Kashmīr (El.; L. 401, 450). The Ksh. form of this word is tösildār, q.v.
another spelling of tay 1, 2, and 3, qq.v.
(? spelling) f. a chattering woman (El. ṭȧirṭair). Cf. tartȧrⁱ.
tītĕn, tötĕn, and tṻtĕn, see tyūtᵘ.
taiʦi, tīʦa, tīʦi, töʦa, töʦi,tṻʦa, tṻʦi, see tyūtᵘ
(? spelling) m. the bark of the Cinnamomum albiflorum (El.). Cf. pạtᵃr, p. 802b, l. 11; patraj, tejpat, and tamāla.

(sometimes written tājy) m. a crown, diadem, tiara (cf. dyuv tāj, p. 272a, l. 16; pōshĕn-hondᵘ tᵒ, p. 779b, l. 5; shēr-tᵒ, p. 889a, l. 32; takht-ō-tᵒ, s.v. takht) (Śiv. 704, 1012, 1484, 1715; Rām. 260, 274-5, 819, 821-2, 830, 1001, 1127, 1132, 1143d, 1462, 1466; K. 450; YZ. 236; K.Pr. 134, 203); a high-crowned cap; a crest, tuft, plume (cf. nīlijⁱ-tⁱ, p. 634b, l. 18) (Śiv. 1815); met. royalty, imperial power (cf. rājy-tᵒ, p. 830a, l. 39) (Rām. 143). -tārukh m. (sg. dat. -tārakas), a 'tiara-star', a comet with the tail pointing upwards (see p. 535b, l. 45).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -dārĕñ), crowned, diademed; crested; a crowned head, king, sovereign.
m. approval, permission (Gr.M.); view, opinion, decision, judgment (Gr.M.); a scheme, plan, device (Gr.M.).
m.pl. mutual collisions, concussions, repeated striking on each other, chattering (of the teeth) (cf. dan-ṭᵒ, p. 221a, l. 1; dand-ṭᵒ, p. 224a, l. 42; ḍanṭakar, p. 228b, l. 12). Cf. the next.
m. (from whatever cause) prominently visible, clearly manifest. -pöṭhⁱ adv. clearly, prominently, manifestly.

or (Śiv. 711) tāgath m strength, vigour, power (El. tákat, f.; Gr.M.; W. 129; Śiv. 711, 741, 848, 921-2; Rām. 169, 543, 547, 814, 967, 989, 1183, 1531, 1625). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), powerless, unable (El.).
(? gend.) repeating the Muhammadan creed, or saying 'God is great' upon particular occasions (L. 270).

m. (sg. dat. ṭakas), a crunch (with the teeth) (Gr.Gr. 122); the blow of an axe (in cutting wood, lopping a tree, or the like) (K.Pr. ṭak 257, 260; ṭukhā 155); a piece (severed from anything); watching impatiently or jealously (for something longed for); keenness, vehemence. --āsun -- m. impatient watching or vehemence as ab. to exist. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to cut or lop (a tree's branches or the like) (so W. 149, ṭak dāwun); to cause a misunderstanding. --rōzun -- m.inf. watching impatiently to continue. -ṭokᵘ adv. (in a discussion, speaking) unrestrainedly, fluently, volubly, vehemently. -ṭücᵘ̈ f. a kind of long-shaped loaf. --ṭakh -- m. volubility, fluency. ¶ ṭaka muñᵉ̆rith adv. regarding or looking (at something) jealously or impatiently (with eyes half turned down). --muñĕrith -- adv. (with verbs indicating discussion, conversing, or the like) vehemently (esp. of one previously timid).

m. (sg. dat. tākas), an arch, cupola, vault; a recess (in a wall), niche (Gr.Gr. 10); a cornice, ledge, projecting part (cf. nar-māda-tᵒ, p. 646b, l. 20); a window, balcony (cf. bālā-ĕ-tᵒ, p. 104b, l. 18; linga-tᵒ, p. 326b, l. 30; panjara-tᵒ, p. 741a, l. 2; potᵘ tᵒ, p. 788a, l. 21; shēra-tᵒ, p. 889a, l. 50) (K.Pr. 4); (in Ksh.) a door-frame (or similar construction) (cf. dachĕ-tᵒ, p. 186a, l. 3; dutôkᵘ, p. 258b, l. 12). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. 'to put (on) a ledge', to make an accomplished fact, to confirm; hence (in Ksh.) (after the details of a marriage arrangement have been informally settled) to carry out the formal ceremony of signifying the agreement of both parties to the terms so arranged. Cf. Hindōstānī t̤āq baiṭhnā. ¶ tāka-dörᵘ̈ f. an upper story window-balcony (Śiv. 1360). -patᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. the floor-mat of a window-balcony.
m. (sg. dat. ṭākas), N. of a certain caste, the members of which generally act as physicians (Gr.Gr. 10).
adj. c.g. single; (of numbers) uneven, odd (cf. juph-kina-tᵒ, p. 376b, l. 1); singular, rare, unique, unmatched, unequalled, unrivalled.
m. an underground apartment where goods and valuables are stowed away (El.).
m. defect, failure, omission, shortcoming (Rām. 360); a fault, offence, crime, misdemeanour (Gr.M.; Śiv. 324; Rām. 160, 823; H. viii, 10; x, 12); sin, vice (El. taksīr).
adj. c.g. blamable, culpable, criminal, guilty (Gr.M.); as subst. m., a criminal, delinquent (Gr.M.).

(sometimes written takta) (for 2, see takhth) m. a plank, board, slab (W. 120); a platform; a table; a bench, stool; a sheet of paper; a sheet or expanse of cloth (cf. jāma-takta, p. 373b, l. 32). -bôrᵘ m. a load of boards, planks, or slabs of wood (tied in a bundle, and carried from the forests for sale in the towns). -püṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -pacĕ), a sawn plank of wood; a small board.

m. (sg. dat. takhtas), a throne, chair of state (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1484; Rām. 168, 712, 1108f; K. 540; YZ. 236; K.Pr. 227); a seat, stage, platform; a sofa, bed; any place raised above the ground for sitting, reclining, or sleeping. --karun -- m.inf. 'to make a throne', (in battle) utterly to defeat the opposing forces. ¶ takht-i-rāwun m. (Rām. 1099) the throne of Rāvaṇa, but also meant for takht-i-rawān تختِ روان m., (Rāvaṇa's) travelling throne or magic car. There is a pun on the two words 'Rāwun' and 'rawān'. takht-ĕ-sulaimān, or takht-i-sulaimān تختِ سلیمان m. 'Solomon's throne', N. of a lofty hill lying on the south side of the city of Śrīnagar. Its ancient Sanskrit name was 'Gōpâdri' (El.; RT.Tr. II, 452). takht-ō-tāj تخت و تاج m. throne and diadem; met. royal state (Rām. 260). ¶ takhta 2 in takhta-pōsh m. a covering for a throne, seat, etc.; a cloth or cushion to sit upon; a covered stage or platform. ¶ takhtas bĕhun m.inf. to sit down upon a throne, (of a new king) to assume sovereignty, to be crowned king.
m. a small recess, a small niche; a small shelf, window, etc. (see tākh 1); (in Ksh.) a recess or niche in the upper part of a doorway, or high up in a wall (cf. ʦū̃ṭhⁱ-tⁱ, s.v. ʦū̃ṭhᵘ).
f. a kind of round cap, embroidered with silk and silver thread.
m. (in sickness, etc.) a heated object applied to an affected part, a cataplasm, poultice.
adj. c.g. contentious, fond of argument; a subject of contention. --jamā تکرآری جمع m. an item of village revenue disputed by the villagers (L. 406, 449).
m. (sg. dat. takshĕkas), N. of one of the principal Nāgas, or serpents, of Pātāla or Hell (the abode of Yama, the god of death) (Rām. 310).
in ṭakulᵘ wŏhav m. a heart-striking curse, a curse uttered against the hearer's children or other beloved objects. Cf. ṭakh.
adj. (f. tākᵘ̈jᵘ̈), having an odd (i.e. uneven) number, (in counting) that (or those) which has (or have) uneven numbers (cf. tākh 2).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭokᵘ, f. ṭücᵘ̈; 2 p.p. ṭacyōv) to gnaw, crunch (a bone or the like) (Gr.Gr. 122); met. to speak unsuitably (esp. when uttering words without sense). ṭokᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ṭücᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), gnawed, crunched. ṭakith ʦhunun m.inf. (when engaged in conversation) to overwhelm (the other person) with abuse. Cf. ṭukun.
adj. difficult to be borne or suffered (Rām. 1011).

or ṭakara m. collision, the striking of two things (e.g. two swords) against each other. ¶ ṭakᵃra dyunᵘ m.inf. to balk, or interpose an obstacle before, another who is on the point of success. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to be balked when on the point of attainment, to be tantalized. --lagȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the eyes to become inflamed. --lagun -- m.inf. balking to occur, disappointment (caused by some obstacle) to be experienced. --pyonᵘ -- m. a collision (as ab.) between two bodies to occur.
f. a kind of large, wide and deep, basket (El. ṭokur).

m. a pillow, bolster, cushion (Śiv. 1825); anything upon which one leans, prop, support (lit, and met.), reliance, trust; help, backing; a place of repose; the stand or abode of a faqīr (temporary or permanent). ¶ takiyĕ-dār تکیہ دآر m. a faqīr, wandering ascetic, darwēsh, or the like, who has taken up his stand or abode in some specific place; an abbot, prior (of a monastery, or the like). takiyĕ-dörī تکیہ دآری f. the condition of such a settled ascetic. takiyĕ dyunᵘ m.inf. to give (one) a pillow (to recline against); to receive with respect; to lean or rest (upon or against); to depend upon the help or backing of some powerful person. ¶ tȧkⁱyĕs bĕhun m.inf. to sit in an ascetic's stand, to adopt the life of a settled ascetic.
m. deferring, neglecting, evading (some task). Cf. the next.

m. the bottom, lowest part (of anything or place) (cf. bāl-tal, p. 104a, l. 1); the place underneath, the underneath part (bhū-tal, the whole earth (as opposed to the sky), the surface of the earth (L.V. 22, 42); (as adv.) below, down (H. ix, 6; K.Pr. 187); (as postpos., governing dat., or occasionally the acc. in the form of the nom.) below, to below, down, beneath, under (cf. (with dat.) babi-tᵒ, p. 77a, ll. 41, 43; bayĕs-tᵒ, p. 148b, ll. 39, 42; carbas-tᵒ, p. 175a, l. 27; minüʦᵘ̈-tᵘ̈, p. 582b, l. 23; nazari-tᵒ, p. 676b, ll. 11 ff.; pajĕ-tᵒ, p. 724a, ll. 20 ff.; paran-tᵒ, p. 750b, l. 13; (with acc.) boṭhᵘ-tᵘ, p. 140a, l. 44; nakha-tᵒ, p. 628b, l. 18; nam-tᵒ, p. 635a, ll. 49 ff.) (Gr.Gr. 152, 155, 159; Gr.M.; W. 97; Śiv. 178, 500, 575, 818, 910, 1078, 1176, 1179, 1562, 1752 talạy, 1754, 1813; Rām. 141, 193, 197, 353, 410, 475, 506, 508, 585, 601, 697-8, 978, 988, 1007, 1017, 1088, 1329, 1355, 1414, 1418, 1529, 1552; K. 94, 158, 310, 346, 988, 1026; H. ii, 3; v, 4; viii, 6, 7, 13; x, 7, 8; YZ. 165; K.Pr. 150, 156, 206). --anun -- m.inf. to bring down (El.). --dọ̆bᵃri -- adv. buried below, buried down, very secretly, in a hidden place (of burying treasure or the like); cf. tȧlⁱ-dọ̆bⁱri, bel. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go down, descend (Rām. 87, 116, 300, 562, 738, 1224); to go to the foot of, to go close to the bottom (of something) (Rām. 500, 940). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take below (oneself), to put beneath one's feet; (of an elephant) to crush beneath the feet (K.Pr. 150). ¶ tal-kun adv. to below, towards beneath (u.w.vbs. of depositing or the like (Rām. 1199). -kun gaʦhun m.inf. to go to below, to become underneath, (of something or some person usually exalted) to become lower than the low, to go to the bottom. -kun karun m.inf. to put to the bottom, to defeat (in a dispute, by abuse, or the like), bring low. -kun thawun or -kun thāwun m.inf. to put below, i.e. to conceal something, to hide carefully. -kun ʦhunun m.inf. to throw below; to forget an injury done by another, to forgive and forget, think no more of (a wrong done), to let bygones be bygones. ¶ tal karun m.inf. to bring down to the bottom, to defeat (cf. talphas tal karun, s.v. talᵃph) (Rām. 1409); to put (something) under (something) (Rām. 1417). --küñᵘ̈ pĕṭh küñᵘ̈ karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to put a stone below and to put a stone above'; hence, to call down curses on, to curse, to utter maledictions on. -podᵘ m. the sole of the foot (El. tálpód); cf. tala-podᵘ, bel. -pȧdⁱ-mal  m. 'the dirt on the sole of the foot', anything utterly vile and worthless; cf. tala-pȧdⁱ-mal, bel. --pĕṭh -- subst. m. and adv. the below and the above, the entirety; that which (moves) up and down (Śiv. 1352); (adv.) up and down; one above and the other below; secretly and thoroughly. --pātāl -- the lowest hell, the hell at the bottom of the lowest hell (see pātāl) (Śiv. 985). --raṭun -- m.inf. to hold down, keep down (K. 236, 1026). -sörᵘ̈ f. secretly purloining and gradually carrying away (from another's store); cf. tȧlⁱ-sörⁱ, bel. --tal thawun -- m.inf. gradually to save up (for the time of need). -zadal f. a libidinous unchaste woman. ¶ tala adv. and postpos. governing abl. from below, from under (cf. canga-tᵒ, p. 173a, l. 16; drĕshṭi-tᵒ, p. 249a, l. 11; mūla-tᵒ, p. 567a, l. 47; pajĕ-tᵒ, p. 724a, l. 14) (Śiv. 27, 1343, 1445, 1597, 1621, 1623, 1828; Rām. 21, 621, 1075, 1257, 1672; K. 153, 207, 233, 566; H. vii, 7; K.Pr. 231); below, beneath (K. 151); from near, from close proximity (Śiv. 1750); secretly, privately; (adv.) below, beneath (K.Pr. 210). -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, below, produced or born in below, coming from below; situated below, lower. -podᵘ m. the sole of the foot; cf. tal-podᵘ, ab. -pȧdⁱ-mal m. the dirt on the sole of the foot, anything utterly vile and worthless; cf. tal-pȧdⁱ-mal, ab. -pĕṭhan adv. from the bottom to above, from bottom to top. -pĕṭha wŏthun m.inf. 'to rise from below', (in an attack of rage or the like) to lose control of oneself. -shutᵘ or -shutun  adv. beginning from the bottom, from the root, from the beginning (u.w.vbs. of inspecting or the like). --tala -- adv. (with vbs. of raising or the like) from below and from below, in order from along the bottom; down to the very bottom (K.Pr. 210). --tala pala bāh shĕth -- m. one who secretly acts without self-control. -trọ̆shᵘ adj. (f. -trö̆shᵘ̈), possessing secretly a hard or fierce nature, fierce at bottom. ¶ tȧlⁱ adv. and postpos. (usually governing the agent case) from beneath, from below (cf. ȧchⁱ-tⁱ yunᵘ, p. 8b, ll. 31 ff.; dī̃jĕ-tᵒ, p. 202a, ll. 48 ff.; khurⁱ-tⁱ, p. 410b, l. 26; nakha-tᵒ, p. 628b, l. 29) (Śiv. 1807; K.Pr. 111, 162); to below, to beneath (cf. khurⁱ-tⁱ, p. 410b, l. 26; kȧnⁱ-tⁱ, p. 448b, ll. 32ff.; kȧʦhⁱ-tⁱ, p. 493a, l. 1; tȧngⁱ tᵒ yunᵘ) (YZ. 32); below (Gr.Gr. 155; Gr.M.; Śiv. 870; H. iii, 3; xii, 14). tȧlⁱ bȧlⁱʦhȧlⁱ  adv. in some way or other, by one means or another (by ingenuity, by force, or dishonestly, but necessarily somehow) (cf. our 'beg, borrow, or steal', which has much the same force). -dọ̆bᵃri adv. buried below, buried down, very secretly, in a hidden place (below ground); cf. tal-dọ̆bᵃri, ab. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go down; hence, to become destroyed, ruined. --kinⁱ -- adv. from below (Gr.Gr. 159, Rām. 1410, K. 154); below (Gr.M., governing dat.) (Rām. 1147). -sörᵘ̈ f. secretly purloining and gradually carrying away (from another's store); cf. tal-sörᵘ̈, ab. --tȧlⁱ -- adv. below the below, at the extreme lowest place, right at the bottom (Śiv. 474). -ṭāri wuchun m.inf. to look with the eyelids down, to look under the eyelids, glance, spy (esp. censoriously). Cf. ṭȧlⁱ ṭörⁱ wuchun, p. 1000a, l. 11. ¶ tali-tal adj. c.g. very much below, right at the bottom. ¶ talī, postpos. below, i.q. tal, ab. (YZ. 124, K.Pr. 234). tal talī adv. down to the very bottom (K.Pr. 209). ¶ talukᵘ gen. adj. (f. talücᵘ̈ 1, for 2, see s.v.) of, belonging to, or produced below (cf. dara-tᵒ 1, p. 234b, l. 26; and 2, p. 236a, l. 21; nakha-tᵒ, p. 628b, l. 31); thana-tᵒ, p. 978a, l. 3) (K.Pr. 183 talikis for talakis). --pĕṭh -- adv. upside down. --pĕṭh gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be turned upside down (and so to be destroyed) (e.g. by an earthquake). --pĕṭh karun -- m.inf. to turn upside down (and so destroy). ¶ talay adv. (emph. form of tala, ab.) even under, right under (K.Pr. 54 talai).

m. (but sometimes f. as in tᵒ mārüñᵘ̈, bel.) snapping the fingers (in beating time in music, measuring rhythm, or the like) (Śiv. 1731); clapping the hands (in time to music); a cymbal (El.) --mārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to snap the fingers or clap the hands (as ab.) (Śiv. 276, 374, 1323, 1456, 1689); to beat a cymbal (El.). ¶ tāla-horᵘ m. a pair of small cymbal-like musical instruments.
m. tala-buz m. roasting in grease, frying. Cf. talun.
m. the palmyra tree or fan palm, Borassus flabelliformis. ¶ tāla-kulᵘ m. the palmyra palm tree. -phal m. its fruit (with its gelatinous pulp).

f. (but sometimes m., see bel.) the palate, esp, the hard palate (but also including the uvula) (El. tál, m.); the upper part or capital of a column, pillar, or the like; the part of the skull below the Brahmarandhra (p. 121a, l. 8) (? the parts of the cranium in the neighbourhood of the coronal and sagittal commissures), the crown of the head (cf. ṭĕkⁱ-tāl, s.v. ṭyokᵘ) (El. m.; Rām. 728; K.Pr. 10, 70, 210). This word is m. in Hindī. Cf. tālyunᵘ. --dazüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'the cranium to burn', mental disquietude (caused by opposition to one's wishes). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. the palate (or uvula) to fall, a certain disease of the palate or uvula (esp. of a child) commonly following diarrhœa, to occur. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. a disease of the palate to come (in which the palate is covered by small boils). --zāl -- f. 'a palate net', crafty conciliatory language (to obtain an object). --zāl wahārun -- or --zāl wahārüñᵘ̈ -- m. or f.inf. to employ such conciliatory language (quasi, spreading a net). --zāl wanüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to use such conciliatory language. ¶ tāla-pharhongᵘ m. an ulcer or gathering on the palate. -raz f. a kind of jewelled chain or string, used as a support for a heavy earring, so as to take the weight off the ear (cf. pushᵉ̆ṭᵉ̆-tᵉ̆-rᵉ̆, p. 783a, l. 25). -ʦokᵘ m. a circular ornament worn on the top of a woman's headdress (made of silver, silken thread, or the like). -zodᵘ gaʦhun m.inf. a certain disease (involving a cleaving or hole in the palate) to occur. -zövⁱjyār or -zöyⁱjyār m. (of voice or language) delicateness; softness, gentleness, sweetness, tenderness (esp. when referred to as a habit). -zövyulᵘ or -zöyyulᵘ adj. (f. -zövijᵘ̈ or -zöyijᵘ̈), having a delicate palate; hence, soft-tongued, one whose language or words are soft, sweet, gentle, tender, or the like. -zöyilī f. the habit of using gentle language, as ab. ¶ tāli-gulⁱ ladith wadun m.inf. (when a work or business has turned out badly) to lament over having ever under- taken it. -ganḍ m. tying (a load, bundle, or the like) on the top of the head. -kinⁱ wasun m.inf. (by entering into conversation) to endeavour to worm out a person's private intentions. --tāli wasun -- m.inf. rain to drip or stream down through a roof or ceiling. -ʦĕl m. an impediment at the time of making an effort. -ʦĕl dyunᵘ m.inf. to obstruct a naturally energetic person, to curb or restrain another's impetuosity. -ʦĕl lagun m.inf. to be obstructed when making an effort, to have one's effort- curbed. -ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ʦanjĕ), stopping a person's efforts. --wasun -- m.inf., i.q. tāli-kinⁱ wasun, ab

f. deferring, neglecting, evading (some imposed task) (Gr.Gr. 128); cf. the preceding. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to signify refusal to do some imposed task (by shaking the head, shrugging the shoulders, or the like).
m. inquiry, request, demand; sending for, summons; pay, wages, salary (Gr.M.).
m. a fee paid to a peon for serving a process; the fee payable to a witness (K.Pr. 4); daily pay to constables, etc. (paid by those they guard).
m. a seeker, a searcher, one who is eagerly desirous (of, gen.) (Śiv. 409).
m. (not f. as in Hindōstānī) divorcing (a woman), divorce, repudiation. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to divorce, put away (a wife).
m. (sg. dat. talaranas), shaking, waving (e.g. of the hair, a sheet, the fringe of a garment, etc.).

m. (not f. as in Hindūstānī), search, quest (Gr.M.); scrutiny, study, research; effort, exertion (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to search (for, dat.), to seek (Gr.M.; Rām. 1104, talāshĕ, m c.); to explore; to endeavour (El., Gr.M.). --thawun -- m.inf. to set (a person) asearch, to set a search going.
interj. O!, Ho! (addressed to a male) (H. v, 5; x, 1).
m. an artificial pond, a tank (El. taláo, K.Pr. 209).

m. the ceiling (of a room) (cf. laṭᵃri-tᵃ, p. 538b, l. 45; pacĕ-tᵒ, p. 791a, l. 47) (L.V. 85; K.Pr. 102; Rām. 569, 570; K. 155, 210; H. viii, 6); the roof of a house (El. tálau, Śiv. 1246); --ē -- m. the name given in schools to the Śāradā character corresponding to the Skt. ē; cf. tölī ai. -püṭᵘ̈ f. one of the boards that form a ceiling for one story of a house and, at the same time, the floor of the story above. ¶ tālawa pyonᵘ m.inf. to fall from the ceiling; hence, a sudden and unexpected calamity to befall; suddenly to stand up (e.g. when hearing of some unexpected occurrence).
adj. c.g. nervous, tremulous, apprehensive, fearful (by nature); fickle, changeable (Gr.M., wrongly subst. m. talawulᵘ); restless, fidgety; versatile.
(? spelling) m. in talawūl karun m.inf. to harass (El.). Cf. tulatāl and the preceding.
destiny (El. tálai; K.Pr. sg. obl. tálie, 114); success, fortune (El., as ab.). I.q. tālē, q.v.
m. destiny, fate; prosperity, good fortune, happiness, welfare (Śiv. 1651). I.q. tālay, q.v.
adj. c.g. bitter, acrid (cf. bādām tᵒ, p. 86b, l. 26); as subst. m. Colchicum illyricum (El.).

m. bitterness; acrimony, malice, rancour; (in Ksh.) indignation or annoyance caused by disappointment or non-fulfilment of hopes. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to cause disappointment, as ab. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to suffer disappointment, as ab. --thawun -- m.inf. (by another) to keep such disappointment alive.
in talōr (i.e. talorᵘ)-dach (El. m., but probably f.) the vine (Vitis). Cf. tanorᵘ.
or talᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a certain dish made up of chopped vegetables fried in oil, ghī, or the like (cf. nadȧrⁱ-tⁱ, p. 623a, l. 44).
or tŏlöyⁱ f. a counterpane or coverlet (made with quilted cotton) (cf. nadȧrⁱ-tⁱ, p. 623a, l. 46, and tolᵘ 2).

(for1, see tal) or tŏlücᵘ̈ f. defeat (in a game, such as chess, gambling, or the like) when at the point of victory. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. defeat to be suffered, as ab.; to become the servant of a servant (e.g. when a person in authority is superseded by one of his subordinates who is put over him). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to defeat a person (as ab.) when he is at the point of victory.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. tolᵘ 3 (for 1, see tọ̆lᵘ, for 2, see s.v.), f. tüjᵘ̈; 2 p.p. tajyōv), to fry (Gr.Gr. 117). tolᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), cooked in oil, fried. talana yunᵘ m.inf. pass. to be fried.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. ṭalyōv), to move, stir; (of time or a period of time) to lapse, be passed, to pass by or away; to be displaced; to retire, get out of the way. Cf. ṭolᵘ and ṭālun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. tôlᵘ, f. töjᵘ̈; 2 p.p. tājyōv), to lift up, erect (esp. to move from one place and set up in another); cf. ṭālun and tulun. tôlᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. töjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), removed and set up elsewhere, erected.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭôlᵘ, f. ṭöjᵘ̈; 2 p.p. ṭājyōv), to pass over, go beyond, exceed (a fixed time); to put off, defer, postpone (Gr.Gr. 128); to pass over with indifference; to move (something) from one place to another, remove, displace, put out of the way, avert; (of speech or the like, when addressing one person) to change the direction of one's speech and address someone else; cf. ṭalun and tālun. ṭôlᵘ-motᵘ  perf. part. (f. töjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈) (of a period of time) passed over, exceeded; deferred, postponed; passed over with indifference; (of some thing) moved from one place to another, put aside, moved out of the way; (of speech or the like) addressed to a new person, having its direction changed.
talwāsa تلواسہ m. commotion, restlessness; anxious grief, trouble, anxiety, terror (Śiv. 1352, 1463; Rām. 54, 98, 382, 937, 1340); astonishment.

adj. (f. talimᵘ̈), belonging to the lowest part, nether, situated beneath (Gr.Gr. 152, K.Pr. 18). --pĕṭh karun --m.inf. to turn upside down. --pĕṭh thawun -- m.inf. to set upside down (esp. with the object of confusing or misleading a person).
m. cooking in oil, frying (Gr.Gr. 117). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to fry (in oil, etc.).

m. (sg. dat. tālinis), the upper half of the head (from the roof of the mouth upwards); cf. tāl 3. --dazun -- m.inf. distress, heartache (e.g. that caused by a child's misconduct, inability to marry off a daughter on account of poverty, and so on) to be experienced (Rām. 1620; cf. tᵒ zālun, Rām. 195). Cf. tāl dazüñᵘ̈, p. 997a, l. 32.
m. perishing, ruin, wasting, in talphas tal karun m.inf. to reduce (another) to extreme poverty.

m. (sg. abl. tama 1; for 2, see s.v.), darkness; weariness, fatigue (from travelling) (cf. ạndᵃrᵃ-tᵃ, p. 32b, l. 19; phraṭa-tᵒ, p. 709b, l. 33; potᵘ-tᵘ, p. 788a, l. 23; wölinja-tᵒ, s.v. wölinj) (Śiv. 1752, 1770, 1849); spiritual darkness (L.V. 74); asthma. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give, or cause weariness (H. vii, 17); to rest (on the way) owing to fatigue, to sit down for a rest (on a journey). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take a rest, as ab. --kaḍun -- m.inf., id. ¶ tama-hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), (on a journey) overcome with fatigue.
(cf. طعام) m. food, victuals; (in Ksh.) a dinner party (given to friends, relations, etc.).
a jingle of bram in bram-tam, p. 123a, l. 41, q.v.

adv. and postpos. as far as, up to, including (cf. az-tᵒ, p. 74a, l. 25; ȧzⁱ-tⁱ, id., l. 40; kotᵘ-tᵘ, p. 484a, l. 47; pagāh-tᵒ, p. 683a, l. 46; totᵘ-tᵘ, s.v. totᵘ 2) (Gr.M.; L.V. 57 (governing dat.); Śiv. 681, 1439 (with dat.); Rām. 240, 260, 782, 1412, 1550, 1605, 1677, 1719; K. 1058); then, just then, in the meantime (W. 93; Rām. 147, 945, 1178, 1354); indeed (to emphasize an expression), really, truly, completely (Rām. 728); as a correlative of yāmath (as far, or long, as ----) so far, or so long (Rām. 761). ¶ With an interrogative, tām gives a meaning of indefiniteness, as in kȧhⁱ-tⁱ, somehow or other, p. 388a, l. 2 (K. 1119); kar-tᵒ, at some time or other, p. 465a, l. 28; kati-tᵒ, somewhere, anywhere, p. 483b, l. 41; kotᵘ-tᵘ, id., p. 484a, l. 49; kūtᵘ-tᵘ, of some indefinite quantity, p. 485a, l. 18. In all these, the underlying idea is a doubtful interrogative, as we should say 'is so-and-so anywhere?' (Gr.Gr. 256; Gr.M.; L.V. 86; Śiv. 1725, 1861; Rām. 1417). ¶ Used by itself, as an adv. tām means 'for a short time', 'a little', as in 'rest a little'. ¶ Synonyms of this word are tāmath, tāñ, and tāñĕth, qq.v.
adj. c.g. very covetous, in khām-tamā, p. 400a, l. 26, q.v. (K.Pr. 103, tama). Cf. tamöyī.

or tamah, or (q.v.) tamāh m. covetousness, greed, vehement desire (El.); (in Ksh., of food, or the cooking pot containing it) excessive heat, the condition of being too hot to be touched; met. arrogance; cf. also tamā. --karun -- m.inf. to covet (El.). tama-tāv طمع تاو m. extreme pride, arrogance, haughtiness (due to wealth, position, learning, or the like). tama wasun m.inf. arrogance to descend, to become humbled (owing to the disappearance of the ground for pride); (in cooking) excessive heat to depart, slight cooling to take place. tama-wothᵘ adj. (f. --wüʦhᵘ̈ --) (food, etc.), that has lost its extreme heat, slightly or partly cooled. tama-wothᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), one whose arrogance has descended, humiliated, humbled (as ab.). ¶ tamahukᵘ gen. adj. (f. tamahücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, vehement desire; obtained after vehement desire (e.g. a long-delayed son).

or (q.v.) tama 2 m. covetousness, vehement desire; greediness, greed, avarice; avidity; ambition; longing (for, gen.) (H. vii, 26). --kala kaḍun -- m.inf. to become eager to misappropriate another's property (with which one is entrusted). --karun -- m.inf. to covet, to hanker (after). --nērun -- m.inf. eager desire or ambition to be attained, a longing to be satisfied. ¶ tamāhas tāwan pyonᵘ m.inf. the loss of (something obtained after) great longing to befall (a person).
adj. c.g. one who suffers from asthma (see tam 1).
m. the leaves of the Cinnamomum albiflorum (El.). Cf. pạtᵃr, p. 802b, l. 11; patraj, taj, and tējpat.
adj. c.g. complete, whole, perfect. --karun -- m.inf. to complete, conclude, finish (Gr.M.).

tamanā, or tamannā تمنا m. wish, desire, longing, longing desire (El. tamanná, Rām. 1350, K.Pr. 87); request, prayer, supplication. --nērun -- m.inf. a longing desire to be fulfilled (Śiv. tamannā, 923; tamanā, 1104-5, 1140; tamanāh, 1235; Rām. 1127, 1573, 1633, 1763). --rōzun -- m.inf. a longing desire to remain unfilled, desire to be frustrated (even on the point of success) (Rām. 1530). --sōrun -- m.inf. desire to be exhausted, (hence) efforts to be found unavailing, efforts to be abandoned as useless, to be given up as a bad job (Rām. 711, 953, 1053, 1586, 1628).
m. blackness, darkness or swarthiness of complexion (cf. buthⁱ-tⁱ or -tamañĕr, p. 143a, l. 1) (Gr.Gr. 140).
adj. c.g. sooted, sooty; met. having the face blackened (by public disgrace, disrespect, frustration of hope, disease, or the like).
f. a ripe date, a date (El. tamarī, m.). (In Hindī this word is m.)
m. an attack of anger, wrath (whether spontaneous or due to some external cause).

m. entertainment, exhibition, show, sight, spectacle (Gr.M., Śiv. 422); sport, amusement, pleasure, fun, jest, joke; anything strange or curious (H. iii, 7). --wuchun -- m.inf. to see a sight or spectacle, to see what is to be seen (K.Pr. 171, 215); to look on at fun or sport, etc.; to look on unmoved, encouragingly, or provocatively at some evil action.

adv. and postpos. as far as, up to, including (cf. az-tᵒ, p. 74a, l. 26; ȧzⁱ-tⁱ, id., l. 41; dupaharan tᵒ, p. 233b, l. 4; kotᵘ-tᵘ, p. 184a, l. 47; shāmas tᵒ, p. 882b, l. 16) (Śiv. 1756; Rām. 26, 306, 374, 423, 559, 972, 998, 1137, 1233, 1541; K. 910); just then, in the meantime (Rām. 436, 526, 652, 793, 982, 1358, 1390, 1405, 1738; Y.Z. 177); indeed (to emphasize an expression), really, truly, completely; as a correlative to yāmath (as far, or long, as ----) so far, or so long (Rām. 703-4; H. xi, 20). ¶ With an interrogative, tāmath gives a meaning of indefiniteness, as in kȧhⁱ tᵒ, somehow or other, p. 388a, l. 3; kar tᵒ, at some time or other, p. 465a, l. 32; kati tᵒ, somewhere, anywhere, p. 483b, l. 42; kotᵘ tᵒ, id., p. 484a, l. 49; kūtᵘ tᵒ, of some indefinite quantity, p. 485a, l. 18. In all these, the underlying idea is a doubtful interrogative, as we should say, 'is so-and-so anywhere' (Gr.Gr. 256). ¶ Used by itself, as an adv., tāmath means 'for a short time', 'a little', as in 'rest a little' (Rām. 78). ¶ Synonyms of this word are tām, tāñ, and tāñĕth, qq.v. ¶ tāmathᵃy adv., even then (W. 93 tāmatai).

f. irresoluteness, vacillation (Gr.Gr. 128); (of a cow, horse, or the like) sudden jumping, capering, curveting, caracolling. --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to curvet, caracole. ¶ tambala tulañĕ f. pl. inf. to become sportive, to become wanton.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. tambalôwᵘ), to distract, make distraught, frighten, threaten (Śiv. 1623; Rām. 1438, 1623, 1780); to perplex, deceive (El., L. 459, Śiv. 1884); to agitate with desire, to excite desire in a person, to make anxious for something (Rām. 362, 593); to challenge (an opponent) (K. 232).
n.ag. (f. tambalavüñᵘ̈), one who is bewildered, perplexed, distracted.
m. (sg. dat. tambalanas), perplexity, irresolution, agitation, distraction; delirium (Gr.M.).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. tambalyōv), to be perplexed, irresolute, vacillating (owing to fear, hesitation, or the like), to change one's mind (from sudden grief or joy), to become agitated, distracted, bewildered (Gr.Gr. 128; Śiv. 312; Rām. 889, 1143h; YZ. 15); to be deceived (El., YZ. 212); to astonish (El. tr.). tambalyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tambalyē-müʦᵘ̈), agitated, distracted.
m. a kind of mandoline, or Turkish guitar, with strings of brass wire.
m. a professional player on the tambūra, q.v.
f. reason (as opposed to instinct), discernment, judgment, discrimination (cf. bē-tamīz, p. 144b, l. 28) (Gr.M., W. 110); civility, courtesy (El.).
in tamō-gŏn m. one of the three properties belonging to all created things, the property of darkness or ignorance (see p. 857b, l. 27) (Śiv. 447). Cf. tam 1.

m. tobacco (Nicotiana tabacum and rustica) (Gr.Gr. 126; Gr.M.; L. 330, tamák; K.Pr. 86). --cyonᵘ -- m.inf. to smoke tobacco (Gr.M.; cf.
