K.Pr. 241). ¶ tamökⁱ-bāna m. a hookah (for smoking tobacco through water). -dām m. as much tobacco smoke as is sucked in one inspiration, a single whiff of tobacco smoke. -gul m. the amount of partly-burnt tobacco in the bowl of a hookah after only a little has been smoked. -kulᵘ m. the tobacco plant. -köṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kāchĕ), the upright stem of a hookah. -shōda m. a confirmed tobacco smoker (a slave to the habit). -wạthᵃr m. tobacco-leaf.

tamun 2 or tamunᵘ 2 adj. (f. tamüñᵘ̈ or tamᵘ̈ñᵘ̈), sooty, blackened with soot or the like (cf. buthⁱ-tⁱ, p. 142b, l. 49; wölinja-tᵒ, s.v. wölinj) (Gr.Gr. 140); met. dirty, blackened generally (c.g. of the face having its beauty spoilt) (cf. ala-tamonᵘ, p. 25b, l. 38); publicly disgraced. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become black; (of some hope, etc., on the point of fulfilment, or the like) to come to nothing, be frustrated. --karun -- m.inf. to make black, to frustrate (as ab.). ¶ tamᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ katᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a sooty potsherd; met. blackness or darkness of the face (caused by public disgrace, disrespect, frustration of efforts, disease, or the like). --katᵘ̈rᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such blackness of the face to occur, to be subjected to public disrespect, to disease, to disappointment, or the like. --katᵘ̈rᵘ̈ phērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the face to become generally blackened (e.g. by over-exertion, disease, frustration of efforts, or the like cause). --lë̆jᵘ̈ -- or --lë̆jⁱ -- f. a cooking pot encrusted with soot from long use.
adj. c.g. covetous, greedy (El. tamáí). Cf. tama 2 and tamā.
m. comparison, similitude; an allegory, fable, apologue (Gr.M.).
or tamunᵘ 1 m. (sg. dat. tamanas), soot (or similar black substance). taman-lyolᵘ m. a cooking-pot encrusted with soot or the like (from long use).

m. a thread, a fibre; a tone, tune (in music); stretching, extension; a stretched or tight cord or rope (cf. dŏbⁱ-tⁱ, p. 182b, l. 37); a rigid rod or bar; a beam, or the like, of a house (cf. hāka-tᵒ, p. 327a, l. 7; mal-tᵒ, p. 564a, l. 27; prövishĕ-tᵒ, p. 773b, l. 3) (K.Pr. 87); (in Ksh.) a limb, member, or part of the body (cf. āyĕs-tᵒ, p. 73a, l. 32) (H. viii, 7); one who is suitable as a bridegroom (owing to his freedom from faults and possessing excellent qualities); a certain measure in paying a marriage dowry. So many tōlās (about half-an-ounce each) of gold are paid, one tān is usually ten or fifteen tōlās, and the dowry is then said to be of so many tāns. --kaḍȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to tear out the limbs; hence, to break the limbs by a violent beating. ¶ tāna-bāgay f. division of limbs, (hence, of any person or thing consisting of members, in putting the members in correct order, or in counting them) dividing out the members. --tāna -- adv. limb by limb, member by member. --tāna kaḍun -- m.inf. to dismember, to pull off limb after limb, to tear limb from limb (Rām. 698, 1405). --tāna karun 1 -- m.inf. to put members apart, to dismember (Rām. 468). --tāna muʦarun -- or --tāna muʦarāwun -- m.inf. to loosen the members, (of something the members of which are tightly united) to undo the members, separate the joints.
onomat. m. the sound of a slap on the face, a smack or similar sound.

adv. and postpos. as far as, up to, including (cf. önthas-tᵒ, p. 32a, l. 4; az-tᵒ, p. 74a, l. 27; ȧzⁱ-tⁱ, id., l. 41; kalpāntas-tᵒ, p. 440b, l. 33; pagāh-tᵒ, p. 683a, l. 46; par tāñ pāwun, p. 750b, l. 11; shām tᵒ, p. 882a, l. 29; totᵘ-tᵘ, s.v. totᵘ 2) (Gr.Gr. 154, 256; Śiv. 738, 1486, 1505, 1627, 1635, 1829, 1877; Rām. 285, 303, 334, 769, 787, 885, 899, etc.; K. 6, 41, 111, 211, 400, 599, 606, 740, 782, 797, 815, 1024, 1027, 1079, 1096, 1148; H. v, 6; x, 4, 6, 7, 8; xii, 6, 20); just then, in the mean- time (Śiv. 92, 388; Rām. 80, 194, 318, 499, 507, 554, 590, 694, 781, 783, 854, etc.; K. 262, 612, 890; H. v. 7; xi, 20; xii, 1; YZ. 29); indeed (to emphasize an expression), really, truly, completely (Rām. 698); as a correlative to yāmath, etc. (as far, as long, as ----) so far, or so long (Rām. 1779; K. 140, 597), or (no sooner did he) than (K. 151, 240, 628; YZ. 31). ¶ Used by itself, as an adv., tāñ means 'for a short time', 'a little', as in 'rest a little' (Rām. 235). ¶ With an interrogative, tāñ gives a meaning of indefiniteness, as in kahⁱ-tⁱ, somehow or other, p. 388a, l. 4 (K. 740); kar-tᵒ, at some time or other, p. 465a, l. 33. In such cases the underlying idea is a doubtful interrogation, as if we should say 'is so-and-so anywhere?', or 'what in the name of goodness!' (Gr.Gr. 256; Śiv. 85; Rām. 129, 146, 432, 1012, 1243, 1397, 1417; K. 88, 181, 366; H. v, 4; viii, 10). ¶ Synonyms of this word are tām, tāmath, and tāñĕth, qq.v.
m. the bosom, breasts (of a woman); the dugs, udder (of a female animal) (El. tana, the nipple; K. 109-10).

f. (sg. dat. tani, Gr.Gr. 70), the body, person (of man or beast) (cf. gal-tᵒ, p. 202a, l. 13; hiyĕ-tᵒ, p. 363a, l. 39; potᵘ-tan, p. 788a, l. 27 (W. 156; L.V. 76, 93; Śiv. 47, 168, 225, 445, 619, 815, 946, 1008, 1438, 1459, 1679, etc.; Rām. 186, 233, 247-8, 274, 279, 345, 354, 1233-4, etc.; K. 423, 425; YZ. 74, 96, 106, 234, 344; K.Pr. 239, 240); one's own person, self (cf. āyĕ-tᵒ, p. 73a, l. 27). --nāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bathe one's (own) body, to bathe (Śiv. 24, 1397, 1711; Rām. 676, 1235, 1625, 1772; K. 973). --tanhā تن تنہا or tan-ĕ- tanhā تنِ تنہا adj. c.g. alone, utterly alone (Rām. 1200). ¶ tana-mana or (Śiv. 241) mana-tana adv. with body and soul, with one's whole self (Śiv. 241, 1073, 1422, cf. tan-man, 493; K. 630, 1001). -mana karun m.inf. to accomplish with body and soul. -mana lagun m.inf. to become devoted body and soul (K. 4, 509, 524, 595, 612, 1030, 1141).

adv. from that time forward, since that time, ever since (Gr.M.; L.V. 83, 93; Rām. 1162; K. 504, 1100; K.Pr. 194, tanahdai for tana day (p. 265b, l. 34)). -pĕṭha or -pĕṭhan adv. beginning from that time, ever since (Rām. 1715, K. 244). -pĕṭhukᵘ adj. (f. pĕṭhücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, from that time, (of something existing now) beginning at that time (and continuing till now). -shutᵘ or -shutun adv. beginning from that time, ever since then (K. shutᵘ, 822, 1093). -yōr-kun adv. from that time up to now, ever since then. ¶ tanukᵘ adj. (f. tanücᵘ̈), of from then, existing ever since then.
f. reproach, disapprobation, chiding, blame. --diñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to blame, reproach. -tāna karun 2 m. (sic) inf. to despise (El.).
f. a long wide hall or building.
f. a strong rope of many strands; a tent-rope; a long rope for measuring land.
m. (sg. dat. tanagᵃtas), false appearance, disguise, pretending to be someone else.
f. (sg. dat. tanaki), a string or cord made of fine twisted silver wires. tanaki-dār adj. c.g. (of a garment) trimmed or embroidered with this silver cord.
(? spelling and gend.), land on the slope of the mountains, reclaimed from the forest (L. 321).
in ṭanḍa-gᵃnḍam m. (esp. when poor) making a great show of prosperity, by collecting valuables from various directions, in order to impose on people.

f. a line, row, range, series; a group, collection, flock, troop, large number (cf. gŏbᵃra-tᵃ, p. 275a, l. 50; pŏtra-tᵒ, p. 799b, l. 36; wāka-tᵒ, s.v. wākh 2); a row of people (of the same caste) sitting down to a meal, a company or party of the same caste at dinner. ¶ tandali rōzun m.inf. to stay or keep in a row (esp. of caste-fellows), as ab. tandali thawun m.inf. to set in a row, as ab., (at a dinner-party) to set people in proper order of precedence.

f.pl. skewers or spits for roasting meat, etc. Cf. tọ̆nᵃjĕ. ¶ tȧndⁱjĕn lagun m.inf. to be fixed on roasting-spits; (met.) to become distraught, at one's wits ends owing to some calamity, to be on thorns of anxiety. --lāgun -- m.inf. to make a person distraught, as ab.
m. thinness, slenderness, emaciation (Gr.Gr. 29, 140; Śiv. 766); fineness, delicateness. Cf. tonᵘ 2.
m. elegance and grace in a woman's language (cf. töñᵘ̈ and tawāza).

adv. and postpos. as far as, up to, including (cf. az-tᵒ, p. 74a, l. 28; ȧzⁱ-tⁱ, id., l. 41; pagāh-tᵒ, p. 683a, l. 47) (Rām. 547); just then, in the meantime; indeed (to emphasize an expression), really, truly, completely; as a correlative to yāmath, etc. (as far, as long, as ----) so far, or so long (Rām. 538). ¶ Used by itself, as an adv., tāñĕth means 'for a short time', 'a little', as in 'rest a little'. ¶ With an interrogative, tānĕth gives a meaning of indefiniteness, as in kȧhⁱ-tāñĕth, somehow or other, p. 388a, l. 5; kar-tāñĕth, at some time or other, p. 465a, l. 34. In such cases the underlying idea is a doubtful interrogation, as if we should say 'is so-and-so anywhere?' (Gr.Gr. 256). ¶ Synonyms of this word are tām, tāmath, and tāñ, qq.v.

adj. c.g. contracted, confined, straitened, strait, narrow, tight (cf. atha-tᵒ, p. 63a, l. 48) (El.; Gr.M.; Rām. 403, 523-4; K.Pr. 153); wanting, scarce, scanty, stinted, barren; distressed, poor, badly off; distracted, troubled, vexed (cf. dil-tᵒ, p. 215b, l. 1); dejected, sad, sick (at heart); angry (Śiv. 879). --anun -- m.inf. to distress, vex, worry, harass. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be distressed or incommoded (by), to be in distress or difficulty (Rām. 1074); to be troubled, vexed, or harassed (by) (Śiv. 834); to be utterly weary or sick (of), to have one's patience exhausted (by); to be in straits, be badly off, penniless; to be enraged (against, upari) (Śiv. 571). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. i.q. --gaʦhun; esp. to become distressed and utterly weary of life (owing to anxiety, disease, or the like).

m. a pear, Pyrus communis (for various kinds, see El. s.vv. ṭang and ṭangakul) (cf. hāpath-ṭᵒ, p. 342b, l. 46; jajīri-ṭᵒ, p. 372a, l. 47; mŏkhta-ṭᵒ, p. 561a, l. 17; mama-ṭᵒ, p. 570b, l. 27; nāba-ṭᵒ, p. 619b, l. 8) (El. ṭang and táng, tan; L. 73, 79, 348, 350, 351; W. 17, 21; L.V. 92; K.Pr. 7, 78, 115, 119, 138); cf. ṭö̃cᵘ̈ and ṭö̃jᵘ̈, which are small varieties of the fruit. -kujⁱ or -kujᵘ̈ f. a small pear-tree, a pear-vine. -kulᵘ m. a pear-tree. ¶ ṭanga-chã̄ṭa or -chỗṭᵘ f. an inferior pear (small, juiceless, and with no flavour). -hüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -hacĕ), a piece of pear which has been cut up and dried, a slice of dried pear. -lünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -lanjĕ), a branch of a pear tree laden with fruit. -loṭᵘ m. the narrow end of a pear; met. a certain ornament so shaped (turned up, thick, and long). -lȧṭⁱ-dār m. an ornament set, or adorned, with the foregoing ornaments. -phulay f. the blossoming of pears, pear-blooming. -pōsh m. the pear-flower. -shīra m. pear juice (commonly expressed from the fruit). -vüñᵘ̈ f. a grove of pear-trees (usually planted in lines) (W. 144, -wanⁱ; K.Pr. 135, -waní). ¶ ṭȧngⁱ-tȧlⁱ yunᵘ m.inf. to come under a pear (-tree); met. to obtain success comfortably and easily. ¶ ṭangan ras pyonᵘ m.inf. sexual desire to become first apparent in a youth coming to the age of puberty.

m. the projecting spike that acts as a bolt at one corner of a door (cf. darwāza- ṭᵒ, p. 250b, l. 51). ¶ ṭanga āmotᵘ adj. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), flurried, distracted (by some unbearable calamity or the like). --anun -- m.inf. to flurry, fluster, distract (someone for one's own purposes) (Śiv. 382). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be flurried, flustered, alarmed, scared, dismayed (by some unbearable task) (Śiv. 1258; K. 13, 240).
m. a horse-belt, girth (El. tang). --cārun -- m.inf. to tighten a girth, to girth (a horse); met. to make (someone) ready to set forth.
f. straitness, narrowness; tightness, closeness; scantiness, scarceness; distress, difficulty, want, poverty; stinginess, parsimony.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. tangyōv), to be, or become, tight, too narrow, contracted (e.g. of a place, or of the hand).
تنہا adj. c.g. solitary, lonely (El. tanha; Rām. 1200, tan-ĕ-tanhā, see p. 1008a, l. 18).
f. (sg. dat. tanīki), a slim, slender, woman.
m. contraction, narrowness; (of some receptacle) being too small, the being too narrow, the not allowing room enough; narrowness of income, poverty. Cf. tang.
f. the consisting of Him, identity with Him (i.e. the Supreme) (Śiv. 1858). This word is a technical term borrowed directly from Skt.

in tanna-nanna (K.Pr. 135) (cf. tānana, tanᵃna tanānay in H. v, 12) onomat. a sound supposed to represent the sound of the Ksh. sitār or guitār; hence, rejoicing (K.Pr. 135). In H. v, 12 the words are translated 'taradiddle', which is suitable for the context.
m. the vine (Vitis) (El. tanaur). Cf. talorᵘ.

m. (sg. obl. tạntra or (in composition) optionally tạndra-) a religious treatise; esp. a sacred book of the Śaiva religion (L.V. 11, 58); the regular order of ceremonies or rites, ritual. ¶ tạntra-tārakī or tạndra-tārakī f. the profession of a superintendent of ritual (see the next). -tārukh m. (sg. dat. -tārakas), a professional or skilled superintendent of ritual at a sacrifice or similar religious ceremony. -tārakh-bāy f. the wife of a superintendent of ritual. -tārakh-pūthⁱ f. the guide-book or hand-book of a superintendent of ritual. -tārakĕñ f. a female superintendent of ritual, i.e. a woman who guides in singing, etc., the women assembled at a sacrifice or the like, the conductor or leader of the female choir. -tāraközᵘ̈  f. the profession or condition of a superintendent of ritual; the skill acquired and employed by him.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. tanyōv), to be, or become, thin, slender, wasted away (Gr.Gr. 173; Śiv. 415, 1006). tanyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tanyē-müʦᵘ̈), become thin.
m. an oven, a stove (K.Pr. 210). Cf. tọ̆ndūra.
(? spelling and gend.) the young leaves of the red poppy, much esteemed as a vegetable (L. 72).
m. extreme and urgent desire (to finish some work or the like).
f. (sg. dat. tạñᵉ̆rüñᵉ̆), the making thin or slender.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. tạñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), i.q. tạñᵉ̆run, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 173). tạñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. tạñᵉ̆rövᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), made thin, thinned.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. tạñᵒrᵒ), to make thin, make slender, to thin (Gr.Gr. 7); to dilute (Gr.Gr. 121).
adj. c.g. (of a horse) a kicker, one which kicks. Cf. ṭaph.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. tapaladiñ), attacked by fever, fevered, wasted by fever.
f. an extravagant housewife, a woman who spends more money than she can afford.
m. one who talks nonsense, an idle or foolish talker.
f. penance, religious austerity, mortification (Rām. 969). Cf. tapasy.
m. asceticism, devotion (El. tapasia; L.V. 35, sg. abl. with emph. y, tapasiy). Cf. tapasī.
or tapōwan m. an austerity grove, a sacred grove in which ascetics practise austerities (Śiv. (tapa˚) 441; (tapō˚) 672, 1409). Cf. taph.

m. (sg. dat. tapas), devout austerity, religious austerity, the practice of mental or personal self-denial or self-infliction of bodily torture (L. V. 62; Śiv. 51, 255, 310, 441, 540, 554, 556, 633, 650, 652-3, 678, 680, 757, 1062, 1220, 1448, 1582, 1591, 1618, 1717; Rām. 62, 100-1, 226, 521, 592, 618, 760-1; K. 31, 67, 243, 358, 455, 612, 619, 624, 670, 703-4, 755, 876); fever (Gr.M., K. 822). --khārun -- m.inf. to cause fever (e.g. by giving a person too much work, by distressing him, by making a false accusation, terrifying, or enraging, and so on). --khasun -- m.inf. fever to come on or be brought about (e.g. by excessive exertion). ¶ tapa-bal m. the power acquired by religious austerities. -dār m. (f. -dārĕñ), the headman or leader of a group of villages or of a society, the chairman of a meeting (honoured on account of his wide lands, great flocks, or generous offerings at sacrifices, and so on). -ryoshᵘ m. a holy man who practises austerities (Śiv. 36); a man of the world of saintly character. -rĕshⁱ-bāy f. such a saint's wife; a woman whose character is that of a saint's wife. -ʦhĕway f. slight relief of hunger (by giving a little food). -ʦhĕway gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f. slight relief of hunger (by receiving a little food) to occur. ¶ tapukᵘ adj. gen. (f. tapücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, religious austerities (Śiv. 267, Rām. 552); produced by, or due to, religious austerities.

m. (sg. dat. ṭapas), a blow, esp. a kick (from a horse, or the like) (cf. gurᵘ-ṭᵘ, p. 299a, l. 13; kŏ-ṭapa, p. 491a, l. 23; ʦō̃ca-ṭᵒ, s.v. ʦō̃ca) (Gr.Gr. 123); met. a sudden misfortune (K.Pr. 246); sudden, quick, death (e.g. from epilepsy, cholera, plague, or the like); the fear of such quick death. Cf. ṭāph. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. a kick to be received from a horse; rapid death to ensue (from epilepsy, cholera, plague, or the like). ¶ ṭapa-ṭaph f. (sg. dat. -ṭapi), kick upon kick, mutual kicking (like that of horses fighting). For the gender of this compound, see Gr.Gr. 75.

m. (sg. dat. tāpas), warmth, heat, burning (Śiv. 346, 1291, 1297, 1733; Rām. 533, 536, 700); sunshine, heat of the sun (cf. gagar-tᵒ, p. 280a, l. 10; gaṭa-kārunᵘ tᵒ, p. 310a, l. 38; lari-tᵒ, p. 529b, l. 38) (El.; Gr.Gr. 52, 72, 137; Gr.M.; W. 111; L. 464; Rām. 172, 532; H. i, 11; K.Pr. 250); distress, torment, anguish (Rām. 195, 1620, 1730). -gaṭa f. sun-heat and darkness combined; a time marked by darkness and sunheat. ¶ tāpa-dāna m. an umbrella, sunshade (El. tápadán, tápdán; W. 111, tapạdāna; Śiv. 1145); cf. tāba-dāna. --drāmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. drāmüʦᵘ̈) (of something requiring drying) dried in the sun (e.g. fresh grain requiring drying before husking). --drāv -- adj. c.g., id. -gilan f. (sg. dat. -gilüñᵘ̈), the piercing of a clouded sky by a small amount of sunshine, a ray of sunshine piercing a clouded sky. -hŏchĕr m. dryness (esp. of something moist) caused by sun-heat. -họ̆khᵘ adj. (f. -hö̆chᵘ̈), dry owing to sun-heat (and not to the application of fire, etc.). -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), scorched, heated, inflamed, or tormented by sun-heat (Gr.Gr. 137, Śiv. 1813). -haʦar m. the being scorched, etc., as ab. by sun-heat. --koḍᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --küḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --) (of some moist article) purposely dried (by someone) in the sun. --kaḍun -- m.inf. purposely to dry (something moist) in the sun. -krāy f. 'a sun-heat boiling pan', very severe, burning sunshine. -lĕlⁱ m.pl. 'jars of sun-heat', long-continued sun-heat. -lawa f. sprinkling of sunshine, very slight sunshine. -ṭĕkh f. (sg. dat. -ṭĕki), a drop or trace of sunshine, a spot of sunshine (coming through an interstice). -totᵘ adj. (f. -tüʦᵘ̈), hot from exposure to the sun. -taʦar m. heat due to exposure to the sun; the heat caused by sunshine. -ṭyokᵘ m. (in a shaded place) a spot of sunlight (filtering through the cause of shade). -ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ʦanjĕ), violent, unbearable, sun-heat (such as that at midday in summer). -yāwa m. 'a hot-weather rake', a dandy who wears summer clothes even in winter. ¶ tāpukᵘ gen. adj. (f. tāpücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or due to, the sun's heat. ¶ tāpas bĕhun m.inf. to sit in the sun (to warm oneself), to bask in the sun. --bĕhanāwun -- m.inf. 'to cause to sit in the sun'; hence, to dismiss a person from work, and make him one of the unemployed.
f. (sg. dat. -ṭāpi), a slap with the open hand (cf. kala-ṭᵒ, p. 435a, l. 50; ṭīph-ṭᵒ, l. 47 bel.). Cf. ṭaph.
m. great exhaustion caused by the difficult nature of some work which one must complete. --tulun -- m.inf to exhaust a person (by urging on to the completion of some difficult work).
tafāwut تفاوُت m. difference, distinction, discordance (Śiv. 644; Rām. 488, 1270, 1295; K.Pr. 89). --thāwun -- m.inf. to differ (El.).
(cf. تافتہ) m. a certain kind of spiced cake. --ʦaṭȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. 'to cut cakes', to speak or chat amusingly, to use diverting or pleasing language.
f. a woman endowed with long and copious hair. Cf. ṭopᵘ 1.
m. heat, warmth (Gr.Gr. 128); distress caused by heat; (in Ksh.) intense thirst (due to fever or the like).
m. an ascetic, one who has become perfected or sanctified by austerities (Śiv. 671, 1456; Rām. 98, 610, 1134, 1684). Cf. taph.

f. a pestilence, plague, general outbreak of cholera, or the like. ¶ tapāli-dĕv m. (f. -dĕviñ), the demon of plague (believed to capture and kill human beings at sight). tapāli-buḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -bujĕ), 'a pestilence old woman'; hence, a pestilence which has grown old, i.e. that has continued for a long time. -hünzᵘ̈ capāth or -hünzᵘ̈ cĕpāth f. (sg. dat. --ca(cĕ)pöʦᵘ̈ --) 'a pestilence slap', i.e. a sudden attack of pestilence. -ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ʦanjĕ), a pestilence-blow, an outbreak of deadly pestilence.
adj. (f. tapörimᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or produced in, that (out of sight) direction (see tapörⁱ) (Gr.Gr. 151).

adv. in that (out of sight) direction (with vbs. of placing, going, etc.) (Gr.Gr. 159); from that (out of sight) direction (Gr.Gr. 159); cf. tami pörⁱ, p. 968a, l. 11. -kinⁱ adv. from that (out of sight) direction (u.w. vbs. of coming, etc.).
m. sunshine (when thought of with pleasure).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭopᵘ), to criticize another unfavourably in his absence, to backbite.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. tôpᵘ), to heat, cause to be hot, (of the sun) to shine upon (L.V. 53).
m. (sg. dat. tapanas), a heap of charcoal (collected for winter use). tapan-phȧlⁱ m.pl. a small amount of such charcoal.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. topᵘ), and conj. 3 (2 p.p. tapyōv), (conj. 1) to take (e.g. a brazier) for the purpose of warmth; (conj. 3) to warm oneself (at a fire or the like), to bask (in the sun or before a fire) (cf. nāra-jōsh tᵒ, p. 647b, l. 22) (Gr.Gr. 128). ¶ topᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tüpᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), taken, or used, for warmth (e.g. a burning brazier). ¶ tapyō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. tapyē-müʦᵘ̈), warmed (e.g. a room warmed by a fire, or a brazier lighted).
adj. (f. ṭapijᵘ̈), endowed with long, copious, well-tended hair (Gr.Gr. 146). Cf. ṭopᵘ 1.
f. a woman (esp. a young unmarried girl) whose hair is habitually in disarray (unkempt, dirty, thick, harsh, and short). Cf. ṭopᵘ 1.

or ṭĕr m. an invented story, fiction, a romance, fable (esp. when told for entertaining others). -bāz adj. c.g. (as subst., f. ṭar-bāzĕñ), one who is in the habit of telling fictions, etc., as ab. --lāyun -- m.inf. to spread a fiction (or invented story) abroad. ¶ ṭara-gĕl f. a long piece of fiction, romance, invented tale, or the like.

(cf. تر) m. a seedling, shoot, sprout. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to pull up the sprout (and examine the root); hence, to examine critically and ascertain the source of some secret affair, and, having done so, to publish it. --nērun -- m.inf. the sprout to come forth; hence, the source of some secret affair to become published. ¶ tara drāmotᵘ perf. part. (f. -drāmüʦᵘ̈) (of a seed or the like) sprouted, sprouting. --drāv -- adj. c.g., id. --nērun -- m.inf. (of a seed) to issue from the sprout, to sprout forth.

m. passing over, crossing (a river or the like) (cf. kŏla-tᵒ, p. 437b, l. 27; nāwa-tᵒ, p. 666b, l. 28; ṭᵃka-tᵃ, p. 991b, l. 31; tika-tᵒ, p. 992b, l. 7) (Gr.Gr. 123; W. 114, wrongly translated 'side, bank'; Rām. 544; K.Pr. 138); a means for taking a person across (a river or the like) (L.V. 96; K.Pr. 46, 47; Śiv. 1023; Rām. 780 (tārāh, with suff. of indef. art.), 1307); a fee paid to a ferry-man (L.V. 98; K.Pr. 18; Śiv. 1201, 1788); crossing (the Ocean of Existence), salvation (L.V. 72; Śiv. 14, 381, 957; Rām. 53); power or ability (both by intelligence and availability of the necessary means) to carry out any work (cf. mĕcĕ-tᵒ, p. 601b, l. 46; nĕcĕ-tᵒ, p. 659b, l. 25); a niche or shelf in a wall for holding a lamp (cf. mĕʦi-tᵒ, p. 609a, l. 14) (K. 921). --āsun -- m.inf. power to carry out any very difficult task to exist. --bōzun -- m.inf. (before attempting any very difficult task) to estimate the power available for its performance. --bōzana yunᵘ -- m.inf. ability to be recognized; to be assured in oneself that one has ability and power to carry out some very difficult work. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to convey (a person) across (a river or the like), to ferry across (L.V. 106; Śiv. 253, 415, 737, 1576, 1578); to enable another to carry out some work; to reach or extend across (Rām. 632). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to have oneself ferried across. --karun -- m.inf. (in distributing food, money, or the like) to arrange that there is sufficient for everyone, to see that each one gets his proper share. --lagun -- m.inf to reach the other side; (of some work) to be completed; to reach the other side (of the Ocean of Existence), to gain salvation (Rām. 1573). --wuchun -- m.inf. to consider beforehand whether there are sufficient means, etc., to carry out any work. --zānun -- m.inf. (in the case of some work still to be carried out) to know that one (i.e. oneself) has the power to carry it out. ¶ tāra-kānᵃ̇jᵃ̇ f. connexion (e.g. caused by intercourse, mutual visiting, conversation). -kānᵃ̇jᵃ̇ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. (of a go-between) to arrange connexion (e.g. between the parties to a marriage, for settling some necessary business, or the like). -nôrᵘ  m. a pipe for conveying water across a gap or chasm. -nāv f. a ferry-boat. --tarun -- m.inf. to pass over, cross over (esp. some difficult river); to get through and carry out (some important work) (Rām. 127 (tārun, causal)); to cross over (the Ocean of Existence), to obtain salvation (Rām. 1575). --torᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --türᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), crossed over, passed over; (of some important work) carried through and carried out.
in tara-tar f. repeatedly crossing a river (by boat, etc.), crossing backwards and forwards; a strong fondness for crossing, as ab. Cf. tār 1.

f. thread, string (Śiv. 1077, 1872); wire, cord, string of a musical instrument (Śiv. 669); the electric telegraph, a telegraphic message, a telegram; a thin spikelet (e.g. as an engraving tool) (Śiv. 1373). --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to draw wire. ¶ tāra-tyuzᵘ or -tuzᵘ m. a kind of radish with a long wire-like root (L. 75, tarituz, a medicinal plant, used as a diuretic). -tizⁱ-bọ̆dⁱ m. a bunch of these radishes. -tizⁱ-caṭiñ or -tizⁱ-ʦyūṭⁱ f. a chutnee or pickle made of these radishes pounded.

adj. c.g. new, fresh; green; young, tender, soft; juicy, moist, damp, wet (Śiv. 1210). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become moist. --karun -- m.inf. to moisten. --pahān -- adj. c.g. a little moist, rather moist, rather juicy, somewhat succulent.
f. (pl. nom. tārāyĕ, Śiv. 38) a star (Śiv. 38, 198, 1663); N. of the wife of Wölī (Skt. Vālī), king of the monkeys, and mother of Angad (Rām. 492). Cf. tāra 1.
f.pl. stars (cf. nabacĕ tāra wālañĕ, p. 619a, l. 43; nabañĕ tᵒ, id., l. 49) (Śiv. 1076; Rām. 1484, 1486). Cf. tārā.
m. garden herbs, pot-herbs, greens (K.Pr. 255, where it is translated 'spices and other rich things'). Cf. shĕh-tarra, p. 873a, l. 49.
f.pl. about three, approximately a triad (Gr.Gr. 82; Śiv. 393, 956, 1671, 1898; K. 1118; YZ. 53 (?); K.Pr. 153).
m. manner, mode (Gr.M.), used in the sing. abl. in adverbial phrases, such as prath taraha, of every kind (p. 769a, l. 42).
m. (sg. dat. tarākas), fasting (from want of food), starvation. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to fast or abstain from food (owing to anger or the like).
f. the profession of one who passes or conducts over (cf. tạntra-tᵒ, p. 1012a, l. 15).
f. elevation, promotion, progress, improvement, prosperity (Gr.M.).
f. the profession of one who passes or conducts over (cf. tạntra-tᵒ, p. 1012a, l. 28).
adj. c.g. a habitual teller of invented stories, a habitual liar.
or tarala m.pl. wanton acts, amorous frolics. ¶ tarala karȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to display amorous frolics, etc. --wanȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to use wanton language; to talk frivolously in order to cause delay.
adj. c.g. one who habitually frolics amorously or wantonly, wantonly sportive.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. tāranôwᵘ), to get (someone or something) passed over (by someone else). Causal of tārun, and double causal of tarun, qq.v.

m. a wave, billow, ripple; emotion, rapture, transport, ecstasy; fancy, conceit, whim, caprice; conception, idea, opinion, surmise. --wŏthȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. (about some one affair) many different opinions to arise.

m. a long strip of cotton cloth about three inches wide, wound three or four times round the head of a Brāhman grown up married woman (as an indication that the marriage has been consummated) (L. 262). taranga-gürᵘ̈ f. a woman who makes these head-dresses. -mŏhᵃra or -mŏhara m. polishing this head-dress (it is first dressed with a starch-like substance, and then rubbed with a hard, smooth, polishing-stone).

m. (not f. as in Hindōstānī) limit, term; region, district, quarter, tract (Śiv. 1684); side, direction (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1498; Rām. 1683; H. xi, 5); a point of the compass, direction (sometimes as the four, N., S., E., and W., and sometimes as ten, the four cardinal points, the four intermediate points, the Zenith, and the Nadir (Śiv. 199, 515); (as postposition with gen.) towards (W. 98). ¶ tarpha or tarạpha  adv. from (such and such) a direction (cf. ami tᵒ, p. 55a, l. 13; amiy tᵒ, p. 55b, l. 9; prath tᵒ, p. 769a, l. 41) (Rām. 434); from towards (W. 98). ¶ tarphukᵘ gen. (f. tarphücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, (such and such) a direction (cf. ami tᵒ, p. 55a, l. 15; amiy tᵒ, p. 55b, l. 11).
adj. c.g. and subst. m. one who takes a side, a party man, a partisan (cf. bē-tarafdār, p. 145a, l. 49); a follower; a sectary.
f. the act of taking a side, partiality, partisanship (Gr.M.); party-spirit; favouring, assistance.
adj. and subst. c.g. sharp-tongued, fluent of speech, eloquent; a boaster, braggart, a lying vaunter.
(? spelling) m. an official whose duty it is to weigh the grain when the government's share is taken from the cultivators (El.). ? for tarāzdār, q.v.
f. a fee paid for crossing, a bridge-toll, ferry-fare, or the like.
adj. (f. taravüñᵘ̈ 1), (in weighing) somewhat overweight, weighing a little more than the amount in the other pan. Cf. trāyĕ tōlun, p. 1035a, l. 40.
n.ag. (f. taravüñᵘ̈ 2), one who crosses (a river), a ferry passenger; one whose business or occupation is to cross; (of a debt or the like) ripe or ready for repayment.
n.ag. (f. tāravüñᵘ̈), a ferryman (El., Śiv. 1191); a means of crossing (someone) over (Śiv. 1201, 1755). See tārun.
(cf. Prs. ترازو) m. a weighman (L. 411). Cf. taraugdar.

or (q.v.) tārüʦᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. tāraʦhi), a small pair of scales (such as is used for weighing precious metals or the like); a pair of scales genl. (such as would be used for weighing salt or the like) (K.Pr. 153). ¶ tāraʦhi-dünḍᵘ̈ or -ḍunḍᵘ̈ f. the beam of such scales. -pôturᵘ m. a pan of such scales.
m. (H. ii, 4), education, tuition, instruction. [According to some, this word is f.]
adj. c.g. in man gav tārĕ, the mind became devoted (to) (Śiv. 1362).
a kind of fodder grass (L. 71). ? türᵘ̈, q.v.
or tarīkh طریق m. mode, manner, method, fashion (Gr.M.).
f. freshness, juiciness, ripeness; moisture, dampness, humidity, wetness; low lands on the bank of a river, etc., land covered with water, moist soil, marsh, swamp.

m. interpretation, translation. tarjama khārun m.inf. 'to raise an interpretation', (in the presence of another) to show great honour (to), utter profuse praises or the like (to a person, esp. when he is unworthy of it). --karun -- m.inf. to interpret, translate (El. tarjuma k˚, Gr.M.). --karan-wôlᵘ -- n.ag. (f.--karan-wājĕñ --), an interpreter, translator (El. tarjuma k˚, Gr.M.).
m. a plot (El. tarkajár). --karun -- m.inf. to plot (El.). Cf. tarkh.
m. (sg. dat. tarkas), discussion, consideration, examination, deliberation, investigation.
adj. and subst. c.g. fluent of speech, eloquent; a boaster, a vaunter.
m. a certain grain, a kind of rape, Brassica campestris, sub-sp. (L. 330, taruz).
m. (sg. dat. tarpanas), (among Hindūs) a daily religious ceremony consisting in offering a libation of water to the spirits of deceased ancestors or to the gods (Śiv. 1430, K. 971).
in shĕh-tᵒ, p. 873a, l. 49, q.v. I.q. tara 2, q.v.

or tarᵃsun conj. 2 or 3 (1 p.p. torᵒsᵒ; 2 p.p. tarᵃsyōv), to be, or become, frightened, terrified, alarmed, to fear, be afraid (at the sight of some terrific or formidable personage, or due to anxiety as to some future danger). Cf. trasun and traʦun. ¶ torᵒsᵒ-motᵒ 1 perf. part. (f. türᵘ̈sᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), frightened, terrified (esp. used with regard to some child, or the like, at some unseen fear). ¶ tarᵃsyō-motᵃ 2 perf. part. (f. tarᵃsyē-müʦᵃ), (of an animal or man, who has experienced terror at some previous time) filled with fear thereabout (at the present time, also).

m. onomat. a snap, crack, crackle, fizz, whiz; the patter of dropping, clatter. --karun -- m.inf. unceasingly to prate, prattle, chatter, gabble (like the patter of rain). --lagun -- m.inf. much chattering or gabbling to occur (as ab.). --lāgun -- m.inf. to prate unceasingly, gabble, talk nonsense.
adj. c.g. and subst. m. a gabbler, prater (who talks as unceasingly as the patter of falling rain).
m. order, arrangement, in bē-tartīb, p. 145b, l. 1. tartība-waröy adv. disorderly (El. misprinted tarbíbawaráí).

m. (sg. dat. tārakas; f. tārakĕñ), one who passes or conducts over (cf. tạntra-tᵒ, etc., p. 1012a, l. 17 ff.). N. of a Daitya, or demon (in Skt. Tāraka), who oppressed the gods, and was finally killed by Kārttikēya, the seven-day old son of Śiva (Śiv. 677, 679, 680-1, 1581).

m. (sg. dat. tārakas), a star (cf. gāshĕ-tᵒ, p. 308b, l. 44; kŏl-tᵒ, p. 437a, l. 8; lȧṭⁱ-tⁱ, p. 535b, l. 41; shölⁱ-tⁱ, p. 880b, l. 26; swöʦᵘ̈-tᵘ̈, p. 955a, l. 33; tāj-tᵒ, p. 535b, l. 45, and p. 990a, l. 7) (Gr.M.; W. 115; Śiv. 1145; Rām. 197, 569, 1013, 1017; YZ. 82, 555; K.Pr. 193). ¶ tārakh-gŏgᵃjĕ f.pl. a kind of turnip stew (in which the turnips are cut up and boiled in water, then cooked in oil, and finally in sauce). --gạnzᵃrȧnᵃ -- m. pl. inf. to count stars; met. (in the case of separation from a beloved, or the like) to get through the time by diverting one's attention to something else. -gāsh m. starlight (i.e. the light of the stars when there is no moon). -nab m. a star-sky (i.e. a star-lit sky free from clouds). -naba m., id.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. torᵘ), to cross over, pass over (a river or the like) (cf. apôrᵘ tᵒ, p. 39a, l. 25; mȧnzⁱ tᵒ, p. 584b, l. 1; tāra tᵒ, p. 1018a, l. 19) (Gr.Gr. 175, 204; Gr.M.; W. 459; Śiv. 155, 254, 1165, 1191, 1386, 1487, 1564, 1589, 1637, 1780, 1891; Rām. 42, 544-5, 556, 778, 797, 1590; K. 70, 75); to cross over (the Sea of Existence), to gain salvation (Rām. 1575); to be spread out, extended (cf. buthᵘ tarith pyonᵘ, p. 142a, l. 20; narĕ tarañĕ, p. 650a, l. 9); to pass through and through (Rām. 1612); to become impressed on the mind, senses, feelings, or the like (cf. phikiri tᵒ, p. 690b, l. 39); (of the mind, intelligence, etc.), to pass over, grasp, understand thoroughly (Śiv. 1752); (of some experience) to be thoroughly experienced (cf. bözⁱ tarüñᵘ̈, p. 153a, l. 2; lāg tarüñᵘ̈, p. 511b, l. 2). ¶ torᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. türᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), crossed over; spread out; impressed on the mind; experienced. ¶ tarith gaʦhun m.inf. to be crossed over (of a river or the like); to be passed (as an examination), to be completed (of some business, action, course of study, or the like); to become impressed on the mind, etc., as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. tôrᵘ 2, for 1, see s.v.; f. törᵘ̈ 2, for 1, see s.v.), to enable (one) to cross, to pass (another) across (a river or the like) (cf. apörⁱ tᵒ, p. 39a, l. 43; bōñĕ- muhulᵘ tᵒ, p. 115b, l. 19; mȧkⁱ tārȧnⁱ, p. 559a, l. 25) (Gr.Gr. 123, 175, 197-8; W. 114; Śiv. 516, 930, 1488, 1607, 1739, 1750, 1840, 1910; Rām. 898; K.Pr. 14, 138); to carry (another) through difficulties, to help, save, rescue (K.Pr. 165, 262); to deliver, save, absolve, free from further transmigration (Śiv. 951, 1052, 1487, 1516, 1753, 1845); to benefit, assist (El.); to free, rid of; to impress (something) on the mind (of another) (cf. phikiri tᵒ, p. 690b, l. 41); to pass (a quality) on to another, to infect (Śiv. 1903); to pass (a thread, lace, or the like) (through a hole) (cf. dab tᵒ, p. 181a, l. 41; kāha tārañĕ, p. 387b, l. 43); to pass (something) through (cf. barma tᵒ, p. 123b, l. 9) (zodᵘ tārun, to bore a hole through (something), H. viii, 25; trŏmbⁱ tārȧnⁱ, to prick holes with a needle, p. 1026b, l. 1); to thread (a needle); to put (a roof or the like) across the top of a house, to fix (a roof, ceiling, etc.) (cf. bām tᵒ, p. 107a, l. 1; dalav tᵒ, p. 215b, l. 5; pahurᵘ tᵒ, p. 703b, l. 3); to complete an arrangement (cf. tᵃjĕ tārañe, p. 990a, l. 32); to carry through (some business); to cause (something) to be experienced (cf. bözⁱ tᵒ, p. 153a, l. 4; köḍⁱ tārüñᵘ̈, p. 384b, l. 36; lö̃ph tārüñᵘ̈, p. 528b, l. 42; mĕkhal tārüñᵘ̈, p. 560a, l. 36; pūrᵘ tᵒ, p. 755a, l. 9; tāra tᵒ, p. 1018a, l. 21) (Rām. 127, YZ. 123); to put something across, or through (e.g. ʦhāl tārüñᵘ̈, to jump across, Rām. 555, 556; surākh tārun, to bore a hole through, Rām. 716); bāj tārun, to take tribute (from a subordinate king, etc.) (H. x, 10; xi, 2). ¶ tôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. törᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), passed over (by someone); impressed on the mind (by someone); and so on, as ab. ¶ tāran-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a ferryman (El.).
or (q.v.) tāraʦh f. a small pair of scales (such as is used in weighing precious metals or the like). ¶ tāraʦi-dünḍᵘ̈ or -ḍünḍᵘ̈ f. the beam of such scales. -pôturᵘ m. the pan of such scales.
f. a sword, a 'tulwar' (Gr.M.; K. 33, 447, 811). tarwāri-bardār m. a sword-bearer, a swordsman.
m. form, shape, fashion (Śiv. 1326 (of the lie of a garland on the breast)); way of acting, style of conduct, manner, way.
m. a legacy, bequest; inheritance (by succession or bequest); effects or estate of a deceased person.
f. a kind of earring worn by women (light and made of gold). ¶ tȧrⁱki-horⁱ m. a pair of these (one for each ear). -kan m. an ear adorned by such an earring; a single one of a pair of these earrings.

onomat. m. a sudden loud or explosive sound, bang (e.g. of a gun), crack (e.g. of a whip), smack (e.g. of a slap), crash (e.g. of the fall of a building) (cf. barawañĕ-ṭᵒ, p. 130a, l. 13; dura-ṭᵒ, p. 239a, l. 28; ṭᵒ kaḍun, p. 386a, l. 14, and bel.; kura-ṭᵒ, p. 467a, l. 44; potᵘ ṭᵒ, p. 788a, l. 29; shōra-ṭᵒ, p. 890a, l. 6) (W. 3); hence, something attended by a crashing sound (cf. rūda-ṭᵒ, p. 826b, l. 14); a sudden sound (such as a snap of the fingers or a smack of the lips) (K.Pr. 59, 138); what is indicated by a crash, utter destruction, going crash (cf. sūra-ṭᵒ, p. 932b, l. 37). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to make the sound of a slap, of cracking a board, or the like; to smack the lips (?) (K.Pr. 138); to spend (esp. extravagantly) to the last farthing or grain (of food, etc.). -pŏṭās or -puṭās m. 'crash flop', speaking aloud and plainly (esp. of proclaiming one's own or another's hidden fault), gossiping, tattling, scandal-mongering. -pŏṭösⁱ adj. c.g. one who is in the habit of speaking clearly as above, a scandal-monger, tale-teller. --trāwun -- m.inf. to make the sound of the crack of a whip on a person's body, to crack a whip on a person. ¶ ṭāsa-pholᵘ m. the seed of a certain plant (said to grow and ripen at the base of the flower, after the flower has been plucked). -ṭās f. crashes all round (as in a salvo of artillery).
m. an omen, a prognostic indication, sign. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. a good omen to happen (esp. the presage of future great possessions by meeting a great herd of cattle, horses, or the like).
m. a certain musical instrument, a kind of kettledrum or tabor (Śiv. 1455).

m. a drinking-cup, goblet, bowl; a vessel in which water is cooled; (in Ksh.) a covered earthen vessel for containing cotton or the like, prepared ready for spinning (cf. phamba-tᵒ, p. 698a, l. 50; sīri-tᵒ, p. 931a, l. 45).
m. a playing card; a game of cards.
adj. c.g. making or emitting a sudden explosive sound (or habitually doing so) (see ṭās) (cf. okᵘ-ṭᵘ, p. 19a, l. 49; sata-ṭᵒ, p. 944b, l. 46) (K.Pr. 209).

or tasallī تسلی m. consolation, comfort, solace (cf. dilas tasallī diñᵘ̈, p. 211a, l. 14) (El. f., H. vi, 16). tasalī gaʦhun m.inf. consolation to happen, to become consoled, comforted (K.Pr. 103); to be satisfied, have sufficient (W. 143, tasallā g˚) (Rām. 953, 1565; K.Pr. 170, tasallá); consolation to go (i.e. to depart), to be disappointed, lose all hope (of accomplishing some task). --karun -- m.inf. to console, comfort, solace; to render (a person) hopeless, to destroy (a person's) hope, disappoint (as ab.).
f. a multitude of crashes, bangs, or similar loud explosive noises, sounding in all directions (cf. ṭās).
f. (among Moslems) a string or chaplet of beads, a rosary (El. tasbíh, W. 463; K.Pr. 29, 63, 212); a Moslem necklace (El. tasbí).
m. settlement, adjustment, disposal (of a case) (Gr.M.).
tashᵉ̆th f. (sg. dat. tashti), a cup, bowl, basin, charger, salver, platter (Gr.M., tashti-kĕth, in a basin; YZ. 375, tashtā, with suff. of indef. art.); (in Ksh.) a spittoon.
m. ridicule, a jest, (as a joke) charging another with some non-existent quality or fault; cf. ṭasᵃna. --trāwun -- m.inf. to spread abroad ridicule, as ab.
adj. (f. ṭāsᵘ̈rᵘ̈), (of some eating vessel or the like) shallow, not deep.
? f. a picture, a painting, drawing (Rām. 130).
m. a jest, a joke, (as a joke) charging another with something (e.g. telling him that he is hiding away something wanted). Cf. ṭasōla.
m. the scrotum (including the testes) (cf. pōsh, p. 778a, l. 42).
m. a false or invented tale, esp. when designed to injure another's character.
onomat. m. thunder; any thunderous sound.
or ṭaṭarāray f. (of rain, --˚) noisy torrents, pattering, pouring. Cf. tatarāy.
or ṭaṭarāy f. (of rain, --˚) a pouring continuous torrent (esp. when accompanied by noise). Cf. tatarāray.

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. tatȧrⁱladiñ), suffering from the anguish caused by the smarting of a wound; suffering from the pains or smart of anger; (of a drug-fiend) suffering from unsatisfied craving for the drug.
see tati, s.v. totᵘ 2, p. 1040a, l. 38.

adv. there in that place (out of sight) (u.w.vbs. of placing or the like) (Gr.Gr. 155); in addressing a woman, this word takes the form tatĕnī. ¶ tatinukᵘ adj. (f. tatinücᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or produced there (out of sight). ¶ tatĕnan or tatĕnas adv. there, in that place (out of sight) (u.w.vbs. of standing or the like) (Gr.Gr. 155). ¶ tȧtⁱnas adv. in that very place (out of sight), even there (u.w.vbs. of placing or the like). ¶ tȧtⁱnⁱy adv. in that very place (out of sight), even there (u.w.vbs. of placing or the like).
m. (sg. dat. ṭaṭhas), a kind of large earthen dish. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat the contents of such a dish, to eat a great quantity, to gobble, devour. Cf. ṭuṭha.

ṭaṭhᵘ̈jᵘ̈ or ṭaṭhüjᵘ̈, sometimes (e.g., p. 692a, l. 15) spelt ṭhaṭhüjᵘ̈ f. a wooden trough, a tub (cf. gᵃsa-ṭᵃ, p. 307a, l. 31; kö̆mᵘ̈-ṭᵘ̈, p. 443b, l. 18; phal-ṭhᵒ, p. 692a, l. 15) (Gr.Gr. 36, 145; Gr.M.); cf. ṭọ̆ṭhᵘ. This word is fem. of ṭaṭhulᵘ, q.v.
m. loving conduct, fondness (esp. that of a parent who spoils his child by such) (Gr.Gr. 139).

m. a basket for holding grain or the like (made of wood, cane, or bamboo, and sufficient to hold a ṭọ̆ṭhᵘ (q.v.) of grain) (Gr.Gr. 36, 145); a tray (commonly made of elm-wood and used by Moslems) (L. 80, tattul). Cf. ṭaṭhȧjⁱ.
tatĕnan, tatĕnas, tȧtⁱnas, tȧtⁱnⁱy, see tatĕn.
adv. in that place (out of sight), there (El.); cf. tȧtⁱ, p. 1040a, l. 20. tȧtⁱthiy adv. even there, in that very place (Rām. 1635).
adv. (a word borrowed from Skt.) at that moment, at that time (K. 660, 870).
see panʦa-tatŏ, p. 742b, l. 6. See also tattwa, the Skt. form of the word (Śiv. 1033).
m. Artemisia Indica and vestita (El. tataur). Cf. tatwen.
m. (a form directly borrowed from the Skt. tatpada, 'that expression') (Śiv. 1851, where the expression referred to is the Skt. formula 'sō'ham', 'I am He', i.e. 'I am one with the Supreme').
(? tatūr), m. Datura stramonium (El.). Cf. daturᵘ.

m. a Skt. technical term (tattva), an element, (pl.) the fundamental and general factors of which the universe consists (L.V. 20, Śiv. 1850). In Ksh. also spelt tatŏ; cf. panʦa-tatŏ, p. 742b, l. 2 (Śiv. 1033). Another form of the same word is tŏth 1 (Śiv. 1498, 1585, 1831).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. tatyōv), to be, or become, hot (cf. bāra tᵒ, p. 117b, l. 4) (Gr.Gr. 173; L. 464, to be warm); to be, or become, hot with rage, to be filled with anger. --tṻrun -- m. (sg. dat. tatanas tṻranas), (in fever) cold and heat together (one internal and the other external). ¶ tatyō-motᵘ perf.part. (f. tatyē-müʦᵘ̈), become hot; filled with anger.
m. a burning sensation, a smart (caused e.g. by fire, or by the application of caustic or the like to a sore place) (El.; Gr.Gr. 33, 35). --wŏthun -- m.inf. such a burning sensation to arise.
adj. (f. ṭaṭᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or ṭüṭᵘ̈rᵘ̈), (of man or beast) wasted from old age, decrepit, stricken in years (cf. buḍa-ṭᵒ, p. 85b, l. 3).
(? spelling) m. Artemísia sacrorum and vulgaris (El.). Cf. tatorᵘ.
adj. c.g. (as subst., tạtᵃrĕladiñ), i.q. tatȧrⁱlad, q.v.

or tütᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. agitation, disquietude, anguish (such as is felt by one in a rage) (Gr.Gr. 33, 35); unsatisfied craving for an intoxicating drug (felt by a drug-fiend) (cf. shōda-tᵒ, p. 871a, l. 12); cf. taturᵘ. --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause internal disquietude (as ab.). --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. craving to arise (in a drug-fiend, when unable to get his drug at the usual time). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such craving to attack (a drug-fiend).
a jingle of ātᵘ̈y in ātᵘ̈y-tātᵘ̈y, p. 69b, l. 6.
f. (sg. dat. ṭacĕ), a privy, jakes.
or tōba m. repentance, repenting, penitence (Gr.M.); as interj. repent! shame! fie! (W. 101). --karun -- m.inf. to repent (Gr.M., W. 149, K.Pr. 260).
m. state, condition, quality; manner, mode, way (Gr.M.). Cf. ba-taura, p. 145a, l. 35.
onomat. m. a single bark of a dog (cf. hūnⁱ-ṭⁱ, p. 337a, l. 16). ṭãv ṭãv onomat. m. the barking of a dog; a similar sound uttered by a human being; used met. in bīra-ṭãv-ṭãv, p. 117a, l. 41.

m. extreme heat (Gr.Gr. 124, 137); roasting, frying, baking (cf. hŏkha-tᵒ, p. 337a, l. 45) (Rām. 1626); parching due to drought (cf. hŏkha-tᵒ, p. 377a, l. 43); parching dryness (cf. āma-tᵒ, p. 29b, l. 1); a method of ploughing for rice, dry ploughing (L. táo, 332, 463); ardour, zeal, eagerness (for accomplishing some task); distress, suffering (from weariness or the like) (Śiv. 1824); exhaustion (H. xi, 13); the burning of hunger, fever, etc. (esp. when the sufferer is wasted away by famine), famine-fever (cf. hŏkha-tᵒ, p. 377a, l. 44); pride, conceit (in one's own learning, beauty, wealth, high office, etc.) (cf. tama-tᵒ, p. 1005a, l. 10); contortion, twist, coil, curl. This word combines the meanings of both tawun and tāwun. --anun -- m.inf. to dry something moist; to bring zeal (to oneself), to apply zeal; to bring zeal (to another), to fill with zeal. --āsun -- m.inf. ardour, or zeal, to come into existence (for the accomplishment of some difficult task). --dyunᵘ --, m.inf. to twist, curl (something, dat.) (K.Pr. 239). --karun -- m.inf. to do parching, i.e. parching, or drought, to exist, e.g. drought to occur in a field, or parching fever in the body. --lagun -- m.inf. famine-fever to attack (a person). --wŏthun -- m.inf. famine-fever to come into existence. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. drought to come; eagerness, ardour, zeal (esp. when due to rivalry) to come into existence. ¶ tāwa-bọ̆ḍᵘ adj. (f. -bö̆ḍᵘ̈, dat. -bŏjĕ), 'sunk by frying,' merely cooked in deep oil or the like (and not subsequently cooked with flavouring matter) (chiefly u.w. reference to pieces of fish); cf. bŏḍun and tövⁱ-gāḍa, p. 1047a, l. 47. -chŏkh m. (sg. dat. -chŏkas), a severe and painful wound. -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), smitten with heat, hot (Gr.Gr. 137); smitten with pride or self-conceit (such as incites to ardour). -mujⁱ or -mujᵘ̈ (sometimes written -mujy) f. large radishes or the like, cut up and slightly fried in oil, and then boiled with spices. --wālun -- m.inf. to bring down from conceit, to lower another person's self-conceit. --wasun -- m.inf. to descend from self-conceit, to become deprived of, or freed from, self-conceit. -wothᵘ adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), (from henceforth) freed from self-conceit. --wothᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --wüʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), one whose self-conceit has departed.

onomat. m. a single caw of a crow; met. ridicule, derisive sarcasm (esp. when broadcast), public deriding (exciting angry reprisals) (K.Pr. 107, translated 'news'). --ṭāv -- onomat. m. the repeated caws of a crow, the cawing of a crow. --tulun -- m.inf. to raise ridicule; (esp. among a number of boys) to shout (at another) in ridicule (and so excite his anger). --wŏthun -- m.inf. such anger raising ridicule to be uttered.
m. the alloying of gold with copper (in order to harden it). Cf. tôwᵘ 1.
f. inward wrath, secret anger, secret hatred; cf. tüvᵘ̈. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such anger or hatred to come to a person.
m. the parching of grain or the like, toasting.
m. a certain gold coin used in Tibet.
m. an iron plate or pan on which cakes and the like are toasted or grain is parched. -buzᵘ̈ f. half-frying, half-baking (on such a griddle) (so that the article cooked is just browned outside).
adj. c.g. (of crops or the like) withered by the heat of drought.

m. burning jealousy, consuming envy, heart-burning, rancour; burning sorrow, sorrow caused by the death of one very dear; (in trading, instead of making a profit) loss of part of the capital (cf. tamāhas tᵒ pyonᵘ, p. 1006a, l. 44). --āsun -- m.inf. jealousy to obsess a person. --pyonᵘ -- , m.inf. burning sorrow to fall, (of a woman) to lose her husband by death, to become a widow; (in trade, instead of profit) serious loss of capital to be incurred (YZ. 553 (met.)). -zad m. (of a man) smitten by burning sorrow due to the death of, or separation from, a beloved one. -zadiñ f. (of a woman) distraught by the burning sorrow due to the death of a husband.
(for 2, see tawun) f. (sg. dat. tavüñᵘ̈), the belly (a word used in cursing abuse).
adj. c.g. a loving guardian (esp. of an orphan child). Cf. tāwan.
adj. (f. tāwanüñᵘ̈) (in trading) that which is of small value, or has lost or is losing its value (Śiv. 1566). Cf. tāwan.

m. civility, courtesy, politeness (usually pl. in this sense) (Gr.M.); (in Ksh.) cleverness in speech, smartness of language, aptness of retort (esp. called forth by another's interruption, heckling, abuse, or the like). Cf. tāñĕr.
m. (sg. dat. tawörīkhas), histories, a history, chronicle (Gr.M.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. towᵘ), to roast, toast, parch (grain) (burning only the outer surface) (cf. sĕkh tavüñᵘ̈, p. 904b, l. 36) (K.Pr. 213); to display impudence, show impertinence, act audaciously, have no shame before one's betters or equals. ¶ towᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), parched, toasted, as ab. ¶ tawan 2 (for 1, see s.v.) in tawan-phash m. a very slight parching, as ab. ¶ tavith wawun m.inf. 'having parched to sow', to sow (grain) that has been parched, and is hence dead; (met.) to sow seeds of enmity (i.e. by opposing a person so as to render his actions fruitless for ever).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. tôwᵘ), to warm, to heat (Gr.Gr. 124, L. 464, K.Pr. 75); to make to glow, make red-hot; to heat (a person) (in a Turkish bath or the like). tôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), heated, warmed, etc., as ab.
m. a marriage dowry, a nuptial present. tāyĕ-kani or -kanĕn adv. (given, etc.) as a nuptial present.

see ta 1, of which it is the emph. form (see p. 961a, l. 33) (Śiv. 46, 55, 108, 187, etc.); used in poetry as a purely pleonastic word (H. iv, 1, etc.; YZ. 31, 76). Cf. töy 2, and also wūr taishūr, s.v. wūrᵘ 2.

see ta 2, of which it is the emph. form (see p. 961b, l. 10) (K.Pr. 238, 239, written tai). na- tay, or else, otherwise (see p. 618a, ll. 4, 11, and p. 961b, l. 11) (Śiv. 76, 168, 354-8, etc.); yā tai... na ta, either... or else (K.Pr. 239). Cf. töy 2.

m. folding, rolling up. --karun -- m.inf. to fold, roll up; to wind up, to bring to a conclusion, to close, dispose of; to traverse, pass over, cross over (Śiv. 1700); to exercise authority (H. xi, 3). Cf. tᵃy 1.

adj. c.g. prepared, ready, finished, completed, complete (Gr.M.; W. 140; Śiv. 721, 1071, 1582, 1792; K. 571; K.Pr. 41, 215); in full vigour, fully developed, robust; (of fruit) ripened, ripe. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be, or become, ready, prepared; to get ready, be on the alert. --karun -- m.inf. to make, or get, ready, to prepare (cf. tōph tᵒ kᵒ, p. 1015b, l. 29) (H. iv, 2; xii, 18, 22); to provide, arrange, put in order; to train; to fatten. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain ready, keep ready (awaiting help or the like). --thawun -- m.inf. to set (a person or thing) ready (for any task or duty).

f. the state of being prepared; preparedness, readiness; preparation, getting ready, making arrangement (Gr.M.; Śiv. 631, 720, 724, 729, 1244, 1356; Rām. 5, 1675, 1756); show, pomp, splendour; plumpness, fatness; robustness.
adj. c.g. fresh, new, recent (W. 112, YZ. 71); fresh, not stale (Śiv. 1072; Rām. 188, 318); fat, plump, in good condition (YZ. 393); as adv. recently (El.).
f. freshness, newness (W. 112); renewal, renovation, revival, being refreshed (Gr.M.); good condition, plumpness.
m. recording, commemoration; a biographical memoir, a biography (Gr.M.).
m. (sg. dat. tāzanas), a kind of whip or goad (for driving plough-bullocks) (El. a horsewhip). Cf. Persian تازیانہ.
m. heat (esp. great heat), fervour, calidity (cf. tāpa-taʦar, p. 1015a, l. 22) (Rām. 532); fever (El. tazzar). See totᵘ 1.
f. (sg. dat. tạʦᵃrüñᵃ), making hot, heating, calefaction.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. tạʦᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. tạʦᵃrun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 173). tạʦᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. tạʦᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. tạʦᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, ab., q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. tạʦᵒrᵒ), to heat, make hot, make red-hot (Gr.Gr. 173); cf. tatun. tạʦᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. tạʦᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), heated, made red-hot.
f. awaiting a particular occasion (e.g. even when hungry waiting for the proper meal- time), patient waiting, enduring. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show patience, wait patiently, endure.

f. a stitch (in sewing) (El. tĕb, m.); sewing, stitching. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to sew (esp. in mending a tear, putting on a patch as a repair, or the like). -ṭö̃kh f. (sg. dat. -ṭö̃ki) slight or little sewing (in some particular place, e.g. in mending a tear, or in making some slight alteration to a finished garment).
adj. c.g. spotted, marked with spots (cf. machĕ-ṭᵒ, p. 547a, l. 43). Cf. ṭë˘cᵘ̈.
m. bitterness (W. 112 techar); pungency (cf. marʦa-ṭᵒ, p. 594b, l. 25); anger, wrath (at someone or something). Cf. ṭyoṭhᵘ. --nērun -- m.inf. wrath to issue, a quarrel to arise.

f. a spot (differing in colour from the article on which it occurs) (cf. machĕ-ṭĕcĕ, p. 547a, l. 41); a certain kind of small edible bird (El. tech, a species of waterfowl, and ṭaich, a bird of Kashmīr; L. 122, téch, the water hen (Gallinula chloropus). Cf. ṭyokᵘ. ¶ ṭĕcĕ-āyirᵘ̈ f. 'hunting these birds'; hence, obstruction on all sides (of some body of persons surrounded by another more powerful). -hôrᵘ adj. (f. -hörᵘ̈), spotted with white, covered with white spots (El. techihor, spotted). -hôrᵘ sᵃh, m. a leopard (El. techihór suh). -shikār m. 'hunting these birds,' attacking and dispersing a number of people (as one disperses a flock of these birds with a shot-gun).
m. (sg. dat. ṭĕḍākaras), eructation of undigested food. ṭĕḍākar-pȧnḍith m. a conceited ignoramus who imagines himself a learned man (quasi, who eructates undigested learning).
m. a boaster, braggard (without due ground for so acting).
m. a sword, scimitar, cutlass, dagger (W. 119, K.Pr. 54); (in Ksh.) the blade of a sword or the like (cf. tabar-tᵒ, p. 963a, l. 5) (Rām. 431; H. viii, 6, 13).

m. rising ground, hillock, eminence (cf. rĕyĕ-ṭᵒ, p. 854b, l. 44; shihȧlⁱ-ṭⁱ, p. 875a, l. 14) (Śiv. 1245); ostentation (El.). ¶ ṭē̃ga pĕṭha hāwun m.inf. to run away, abscond (esp. with someone else's property). -pĕṭhukᵘ adj. gen. (f. -pĕṭhücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or produced on high ground.

f. (sg. dat. tĕhi), pride, haughtiness, arrogance (whether proper or improper) (K.Pr. 254); cf. tēh and thēh. --mōrüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. pride to become mitigated. ¶ tĕhi-wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is arrogant.
in ṭĕhṭĕh m. the sound emitted by the flames of burning straw, dry wood, or the like.
f. fire, passionateness, crossness, acrimony, sharpness; arrogance; cf. tĕh. tēhi-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one of a passionate, arrogant nature.

(? spelling and gend.) (in a Moslem marriage ceremony) the marriage night (after the bridegroom has brought his bride home) (L. 269); ? cf. the Hindī ṭēhlā, a marriage ceremony. -jōr, the clothes given to the bride by her father-in-law after she has remained seven days in her husband's house and has put off her bridal dress. In these clothes she sets off to visit her father's house (L. 269). Cf. jōra 2.
m. (? tēj-pạtᵃr f.), the leaves of the Cinnamomum albiflorum (El.). Cf. pạtᵃr, p. 802b, l. 11; patraj, taj, and tamāla.
in ṭēka-baṭañ f. N. of a flower (described as yellow) of Kashmīr (El. teka batain) (Rām. 678, 1091).

f. (sg. dat. ṭĕki), a mere drop or trace of any thick liquid (such as gruel, clarified butter, honey, or the like) (cf. añĕma-ṭᵒ, p. 37b, l. 15; gĕv-ṭᵒ, p. 316b, l. 15; tīla-ṭᵒ, s.v. tīl 1; tāpa-ṭᵒ, s.v. tāph). Cf. ṭyokᵘ.
f. a horoscope, an astrological record of nativity.
f. a small earthen cooking-pot, a pottle (cf. lë̆jᵘ̈-ṭᵘ̈, p. 516b, l. 39) (El. ṭikar; K.Pr. ṭĕkur, 125; ṭĕkar, 254).
f. pride, haughtiness, putting on fine airs (even when one is not entitled to do so).

m. the sesamum-seed, Sesamum indicum, sesame, oil-seed (El. tél, til; L. 330, til; L.V. 45 (used as an offering to a god); K.Pr. 188, 213). -dȧjⁱ or -düjᵘ̈ f. a sesame-field. -khüjᵘ̈ f. oil-cake. -loḍᵘ m. a sweetmeat made of parched sesame-seeds in sugar. -tīl m. sesame-oil. -vüñᵘ̈ f. a large sesame-field; N. of a village in Kashmīr, in Anantanāg Pargana. -worᵘ m. a kind of thick round cake, of wheat, mixed with sesame.
m. (sg. dat. tĕlakas), an ornamental mark; a sectarian mark or marks made with coloured earth, sandal-wood, or unguents, on the forehead, or between the eyes.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. tēlanôwᵘ), to cause to exude (or to melt to) oil; to cause to give smarting pain. This verb is causal of tēlun 2, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 174).

adj. c.g. a soldier (i.e. originally one of the soldiers from the Tailanga country, who were the first to be drilled and clothed in European fashion); (in Ksh.) (esp. of a boy or the like) impudently clever in effecting one's purpose.
f. cleverness in securing the accomplishment of one's purpose.
conj. 1, to cause to expand, to make manifest, display (Śiv. 1429 (pres. part. tēlan), 1844).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. tēlyōv), (of some greasy solid) to exude oil (on the application of heat), to melt, turn to oil (from heat); (of water in a receptacle) to leak, or ooze, away (L.V. 78-9); (of a boil or the like just ripened) to give intolerable pain (Gr.Gr. 174). The causal of this verb is tēlanāwun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 174). tēlyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tēlyē-müʦᵘ̈), melted, as ab.

adv. at that very time (Gr.Gr. 156; El.; Rām. 114, 1186, 1309, 1411). ¶ tĕli adv. then, at that time (El. tili, tilih; Gr.Gr. 156; Gr.M.; W. 94; L.V. 49, 82; Śiv. 159; Rām. 45, 99, 204, 356, 417, 471, 474, 619, 658, 719, 947, 957, 1234-6, 1321, 1386, 1719; K. 6, 20, 181, 520, 700; H. ii, 3; v, 5, 6; xii, 3); at that (former) time, in those days (Rām. 1628); tĕli-ti, conj. nevertheless (El. tilih tih). Frequently used to introduce the apodosis of a conditional sentence, as in ʦᵃh hĕkakh-a... tĕli, canst thou (do so-and-so)... then (Gr.M.). ¶ tĕliy adv. even then, at that very time, just then (Rām. 1111). ¶ tĕlyukᵘ adj. (f. tĕlicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or produced at that time (esp. of past time) (Rām. 1404; K. 197, 915; K.Pr. 214).

m.pl. cataract (of the eyes) (cf. ȧchⁱ-tⁱ, p. 8b, l. 36; kāʦa-tᵒ, p. 493a, l. 36). -kônᵘ adj. (f. -köñᵘ̈), blind (by cataract) of one eye; totally blind (by cataract). -kāṭh m. (sg. dat. -kāṭhas), a kind of tree. --pĕnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. cataract suddenly to befall (a person).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. tĕmbarladiñ), one who is afflicted by cataract (cf. kāʦa-tᵒ, p. 493a, l. 38).
adj. (f. tĕmbürᵘ̈), afflicted with cataract (cf. ȧchⁱ-tⁱ, p. 8b, l. 38).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. f. tĕmbyēyĕ. This verb is impersonal, and is conjugated in the feminine, with the subject in the dat., as in tĕmbyēyĕs, there was looking jealously to him, i.e. he looked jealously, Gr.Gr. 239), to look jealously (at), look with jaundiced eyes; to look eagerly (cf. achĕ tĕmbañĕ, p. 8b, l. 35) (Gr.Gr. 182, 188, 215, 234, 240, 248).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. ṭĕmbyōv), to cause to disappear, to efface, obliterate.
or tĕmbᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a spark (of fire) (cf. nāra-tᵒ, p. 648a, l. 40; sö̆ʦᵘ̈y tᵒ wŏshĕlüñᵘ̈, p. 943a, l. 25) (El. tembir, timbar; Gr.M.; Rām. 1613).

or tyọ̆ngul, or tyū̃gul m. (sg. dat. tĕngalas, tyŏngalas, or tē̃galas), a spark of fire (cf. bȧṭhⁱ- tyọ̆ngul, p. 140b, l. 40; nāra-tyū̃gul, p. 648a, l. 50; ʦᵃñĕ-phŏti tyọ̆ngul nērun, s.v. ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈); a mere spark, a piece of smouldering charcoal (giving but a dim shine) (El. tungul, a live coal; W. 151, id.); fire (El.; L. 460, tungal; Rām. 621; K.Pr. tungul, 30, 161). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. a smouldering charcoal to fall; a spark to fall (on someone) (Rām. 1082); met. the hot weather or summer to begin; sadness or anxiety to be caused by some sudden thought. ¶ tĕngal m.pl. sparks; a heap of smouldering charcoal. -gāsh m. the dim light given out by smouldering charcoal; met. a little learning, very slight knowledge of some branch of science, a smattering of some subject. --tulȧnⁱ -- m.pl.inf. to raise sparks; met. tormenting and urging a pupil, in order to make him acquire knowledge. --wŏthȧnⁱ -- m.pl.inf. sparks to rise; met. to be tormented, worn out, or worried (e.g. in searching for something destroyed, in attempting to complete an impossible task, or in severe and constant study).
m. the son of an adultress by a father other than her husband, a bastard, a son of adultery (cf. kŏ-ṭᵒ, p. 491a, l. 28).
adj. c.g. full, filled up (e.g. a cooking-pot). ṭēpā-ṭēph adj. c.g. brimful.
m. a commentary, gloss, explanation of the meaning of words or passages in a book.
m. (sg. dat. ṭĕpanas), fish-guts, the entrails etc. taken out of a fish when preparing it for cooking (cf. gāḍa-ṭᵒ, p. 276b, l. 29). ṭĕpan-gāḍa f.pl. tiny fish-fry (just hatched).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭyopᵘ), to fill (a receptacle) forcibly (till it can contain no more), to fill so that the contents are pressed down and all but running over. ¶ ṭĕpⁱ ṭĕpⁱāsun m.inf. to be entirely filled (so that the least addition will cause running over). --ṭĕpⁱ thawun -- m.inf. to fill in this way. ¶ ṭĕpith āsun m.inf. to be brimful (pressed down and running over). --thawun -- m.inf. to fill to the brim (pressed down and running over). ¶ ṭyopᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ṭë˘pᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), filled to the brim, as ab.

m. a victor, a conqueror (in a battle, dispute, gambling, etc.); cf. tērun. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become a conqueror, win (a game, etc.). --sapadun --, --sö̃panun --, or --sapazun -- m.inf. to become a conqueror, to become a victor.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. tēryōv), (in an argument or dispute) to conquer, and thereby to become influential or powerful, to gain prestige; cf. tēr. tēryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tēryē-müʦᵘ̈), become powerful, as ab.

m. N. of the eighth lunar asterism (in Skt. Tiṣya or Puṣya) (Śiv. 1550; Rām. 124, 1259-60); pride, haughtiness, arrogance. --karun -- m.inf. to display arrogance or imperiousness. ¶ tēshĕ-tēshĕ adv. at each Tēsh; hence, now and then, occasionally.
adj. (f. ṭĕsᵘ̈rᵘ̈), (esp. after eating) satiate, sated, glutted, gorged.
in tet gad, tet shakr, see ṭyoṭhᵘ.
in ṭĕṭam-ṭôrᵘ hyuhᵘ adj. (f. --hishᵘ̈ --), suddenly appearing upright.
f. (sg. dat. and pl. nom. tīʦᵘ̈ 1, as if from tēth), a lunar day, the time between two risings of the moon (Rām. 1259).

f. (sg. dat. ṭĕṭhi), intense desire, intolerable craving (esp. for opium or similar intoxicating drug, felt by one addicted to its consumption, and not getting it at the usual time) (El. ṭĕṭ, intoxication; Gr.Gr. 126, according to which it is a verbal noun of ṭĕṭhun, q.v., with a special meaning). --khārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause intolerable craving, as ab. --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. impatient and unendurable craving (for a drug, as ab.) to arise (e.g. when the drug becomes unobtainable). --mōrüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such craving to be allayed (e.g. by the obtainment of some small quantity of the drug). --mōravüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to allay another's craving (as ab.) (e.g. by providing some small quantity of it).

f. (sg. dat. tīʦᵘ̈ 2, for 1, see tĕth, for 3, see tyūtᵘ), a certain present (of a fixed multiple of five rupees) given to the relations of the bride or bridegroom. According to L. 262, the sum varies from eight annas to five rupees, and is paid to the bridegroom whenever the bride's father invites her on a visit. tīʦᵘ̈ f.pl. a present (of a multiple of seven rupees) paid to the bride on the occasion of her second entrance to her husband's house, after visiting her parents' house for the first time after her marriage.

or (qq.v.) ṭīṭhⁱ, ṭī˜ṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. ṭē̃ṭi), self-pretension, self-confidence, self-conceit; cf. tö̃th 2. --khārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to raise self-confidence, to fill another with a good opinion of himself. --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (in doing another's work) self-confidence to rise, self-conceit or independence to be shown. Cf. ṭīṭhⁱ khᵒ. ¶ ṭē̃ṭi-wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), a self-confident or arrogant person.
or (q.v.) ṭẹ̆ṭhᵃrāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭẹ̆ṭhanôwᵘ), i.q. ṭẹ̆ṭhᵃrāwun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 174).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ṭĕṭhyōv), to become bitter or acrid, (of food) to become bitter (and gone bad) (El. ṭiṭhun; Gr.Gr. 126, 174; W. 113, tėtun; K.Pr. 5, 62); met. to become angry (at something); cf. ṭyoṭhᵘ. ṭĕṭhyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ṭĕṭhyē-müʦᵘ̈), become bitter, as ab.; become angry (at something).
m. the fry of a certain fish. It is said to have a bitter taste. Cf. ṭyoṭhᵘ.
or (q.v.) ṭĕṭhanāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭẹ̆ṭhᵃrôwᵃ), to make bitter, render bitter (Gr.Gr. 174); to render (a person) angry (by some undesired conduct).
see tȧtⁱ, s.v. totᵘ 2, p. 1040a, l. 22.
m. the top or summit of anything (e.g. a treetop, a mountain summit).
a jingle of bētri, p. 145a, l. 46, q.v.
or ṭĕvürᵘ̈ f. a pretty and pert damsel (esp. aged between sixteen and twenty-four) (cf. ranga-tᵒ, p. 837a, l. 31).

adj. c.g. and adv. sharp, keen, acute; hot, pungent, strong, acrid; fiery, passionate, impetuous (Rām. 29, 206); (of a glance) piercing, penetrating; swift, fleet, quick, rapid (Gr.M.); quick, apt, intelligent, keen-witted; sharp (of a knife, claw or the like) (Gr.M., Rām. 37); (as adv.) swiftly, quickly, impetuously (Rām. 127).

or (more usually) tīz m. light, lustre, radiance, glory (Śiv. 166, 346, 434, 467, 523, 575, 666, 836, 904-5, 936-7, 1126, 1155, 1742; Rām. 1014, 1080; K. 133, 449, 657, 1059); the radiance of personal beauty (Śiv. 653, 888, 922); energy, strength, power (Śiv. 919, 1501; Rām. 1123; K. 621, 959, 987); ardour, fire (Śiv. 1804, 1844); fury (K. 436). ¶ tīza-barith adj. c.g. full of glory (Śiv. 919). -lôdᵘ m. a pile, or mass, of radiance. -rṻph or (Śiv. 305) tēzōrṻph adj. c.g. possessing a radiant form (Śiv. 1609, 1685). -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), abounding in radiance, beauty, glory, or energy (Śiv. 580, 806).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. tyozᵘ, f. të̆zᵘ̈), to abandon (L.V. 55, Śiv. 1818).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. tēzyōv, Gr.Gr. 226; m.pl. tēzöy, tēzēy or tēzyēy, Gr.Gr. 227; 3 and 4 p.p. tēzyāv, Gr.Gr. 240); to be or become sharp (of a sword, knife, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 173, 226, 227, 240); to be or become sharp, intelligent, expert; (of a conflagration) to become more fierce, to blaze up with greater intensity; (of a disease) to become exacerbated; to become still more enraged, to have one's anger intensified. tēzyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tēzyē-müʦᵘ̈), sharpened (as ab.); become sharp, intelligent, expert; (of fire) intensified, as ab.; (of disease) exacerbated; (of an angry person) still more infuriated.
adj. c.g. artificial, unreal (and worthless on that account), fictitious, imitation.
adj. c.g. one who habitually fabricates, one who habitually acts artificially.
m. (sg. dat. thabanas), a lump (cf. mĕʦi-thᵒ, p. 609a, l. 11).
adj. c.g. (of cereal food, or the like) insufficiently cooked, (on that account) hard, not soft.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. thadyōv), to be or become high or elevated, to become higher, to become taller (El. thadun, Gr.Gr. 173, K.Pr. 173); to become erect; to become elevated; to become elevated (in position, wealth, power, or the like). ¶ thadith bĕhun m.inf. 'having risen to sit', to achieve a high position (in wealth, fortune, good qualities, children, etc.) and remain secure there. ¶ thadyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. thadyē-müʦᵘ̈), become high; elevated; raised (to power, etc.).

m. (f. ṭhagiñ q.v.), a deceiver, impostor, cheat, knave, sharper, plunderer (K.Pr. 221); a robber, assassin, cut-throat. ¶ ṭhaga-bāba m. 'Sir ṭhag', an impostor who swindles in the character of a highly-respectable old gentleman. -bāpār m. the conduct or actions of an impostor, swindling conduct. -bāy f. a swindler's wife. -pav m. the practice, exercise, or frequent use of swindling.
f. fatigue, lassitude, exhaustion (resulting from exertion); cf. thã̄kh or thö̃kh. --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make fatigued (by imposing some exhausting labour). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. fatigue to be felt.
f. in order to appropriate the results, dishonestly to induce another to abandon work on which he is engaged.
f. habitual swindling, knavery, cheating, imposture, the profession or actions of an impostor, etc.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭhagôwᵘ), to deceive (Gr.Gr. xxxi).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭhogᵘ f. ṭhüjᵘ̈), to cheat, deceive, beguile, impose upon, trick, dupe, swindle (Gr.M.); conj. 3 (2 p.p. ṭhagyōv) to be deceived, cheated (Gr.Gr. xxxi, Gr.M.). ṭhogᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ṭhüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), deceived, cheated, imposed upon.

f. casting oneself into water, plunging (oneself) into water. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to plunge into water, to dive; to jump down (Rām. 1335). --mārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to dive (Rām. 546). --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to plunge into water and swim, to swim. --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (in order to secure the fruits) suddenly to plunge into another's work.
in ṭhāha-ṭhāh onomat. m. loud laughter, a peal of laughter.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭhaharôwᵘ. This verb is the casual of ṭhaharun, q.v., in all its senses) to make steady, make firm (cf. pūrᵘ ṭhᵒ, p. 755a, l. 2) (El. thaharanáwun (sic), Gr.M.) to cause to stop, to cause to tarry, and so on, as in ṭhaharun; to ascertain, decide, determine (Gr.M.).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ṭhaharyōv), to become fixed, firm (of something previously unsteady) (cf. pūrᵘ ṭhᵒ, p. 754b, l. 50) (K. 623); to become or be steady (cf. atha ṭhᵒ, p. 63a, l. 4); to stand still (Śiv. 1539, K. 1023); to stop, rest, pause, halt (Gr.M.); to stay, remain, abide (Śiv. 1650; K. 1107; H. ii, 4); to wait tarry, (Gr.M.); to wait for, tarry for (K. 1105); to be settled, fixed, determined. ¶ ṭhạhᵃrith derived from conj. part., as adv. behind time, late, retarded, after the right time, unpunctually; slowly, leisurely, deliberately. ¶ ṭhaharyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ṭhaharyē-müʦᵘ̈), become fixed, firm, steady, etc.
m. fixture; pause, rest, stop, halt (esp. for a short time).
m. N. of a Kashmīr village where there is a site sacred to Shiva (Śiv. 1161, 1895).
in ṭhaka-ṭhaka m. covered with ashes (e.g. a man's body), dusty, sooty.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. thakanôwᵘ), to make weary, cause to be weary, to fatigue (Gr.Gr. 176). Cf. thạkᵃrawun.

m. (sg. dat. thakas), weariness, fatigue, exhaustion, lassitude (Gr.Gr. 122); resting on account of weariness; cessation on the conclusion of anything (e.g. of long singing, a long bout of lecturing, or the like). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to take a rest (e.g. in the course of a long journey to recline for a time in a shady place). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to rest, take a rest, as ab.; to take a rest at the conclusion of any wearying task or action. ¶ thaka-būñᵘ̈ f. a weariness-plane, a plane-tree under which a weary person can rest (on a journey in the hot season); met. a genial, kindly woman, who gives rest and comfort to others (cf. K.Pr. 7, 102 for the same simile for a kindly wife). -büṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -bachĕ), a weariness-hearth, a place to which a person goes for rest, or where he finds rest; met. a genial, kindly man, who gives help and rest to others.
m. (sg. dat. ṭhākas), ordering some work to be stopped, stopping any piece of work.
or thö̃kh f. (sg. dat. thã̄ki or thö̃ki), distress resulting from extreme fatigue (esp. when this is fruitless). Cf. thã̄g 1.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. thokᵘ, f. thücᵘ̈; 2 p.p. thacyōv), to be, or become, wearied, tired, fatigued, exhausted, jaded (Gr.Gr. 30, 122, 204, 209, 224; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1770, 1824; Rām. 546; K. 164, 961; YZ. 417). The causal of this verb is thakanāwun or thạkᵃrāwun, qq.v. (Gr.Gr. 174); El. also gives the infinitive thakun as noun subst. meaning 'fatigue'. --aʦun -- m.inf. fatigue to enter, fatigue to overcome (a person), fatigue to be suffered. --nērun -- m.inf. fatigue to exit, i.e. to depart, rest to be attained, to become rested. --nīrith yunᵘ -- m.inf. fatigue to come out, fatigue to become manifest (by the usual signs). --ʦalun -- m.inf. fatigue to depart, to become rested. ¶ thokᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. thücᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), wearied, fatigued (YZ. 134, K.Pr. 12). ¶ thakith pyonᵘ m.inf. to become utterly wearied or exhausted (YZ. 92).

conj. 1. (1 p.p. ṭhôkᵘ, f. ṭhöcᵘ̈; 2 p.p. ṭhācyōv) to prohibit, command to desist (from any work); to hammer into, knock into; cf. ṭhāsun and ṭhukun. ṭhôkᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ṭhöcᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), stopped (by a command) or prohibited (from carrying out any work), caused to desist.
f. (sg. dat. thạkᵃrüñᵃ), the causing of fatigue, weariness.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. thạkᵃrôwᵃ, f. thạkᵃrövᵃ or thücᵘ̈rövᵘ̈), to fatigue, to weary (e.g. by heavy work, long journeying, delay, etc.) (Gr.Gr. 174, Śiv. 1394); cf. thakanāwun. thạkᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. thạkᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ, or thücᵘ̈rövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), wearied by (someone or something, as ab.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. thạkᵒrᵒ), to cause to be fatigued, to fatigue, weary (by hard work, by delay, etc.).

f. a place, spot, site (L.V. 53; Śiv. 1026, 1570-1); (esp.) a place in a book, lesson, or the like; a strip of ground used as a garden- bed, or for cultivating vegetables (cf. hāka-thᵒ (reported as masc.), p. 326b, l. 33; pōshĕ-thᵒ, f., p. 779a, l. 2) (Śiv. 1853); a seed bed; hence, rice seedlings (cf. dā̃-thᵒ, p. 231a, l. 7) (L. 463); land (as opposed to water) (Śiv. 1537, 1741). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to plant vegetables (in such a strip of land). ¶ thala-bāgay f. dividing a piece of ground into such long strips for planting vegetables, so as to facilitate irrigation or watering. --karañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to divide a piece of ground, as ab. ¶ thȧlⁱ thȧlⁱ wuchun m.inf. to examine (e.g. a picture, a dress, or a book) in different places (i.e. here and there). For thȧlⁱ thȧlⁱ wālun, see s.v. thalun. ¶ thali thali wuchun m.inf. to look over in detail and admire some loved one (e.g. a darling child or wife).

m. (f. thöjⁱ or thöjᵘ̈, q.v., means a larger sized tray), a plate of metal used by Hindūs for eating, etc., a platter, trencher (cf. dã̄-thāl barun, p. 231a, l. 9; khakari thᵒ, p. 396a, l. 13; khira-thᵒ, p. 409a, l. 42) (Śiv. 207, 283, 374, 1152, 1169, 1202, 1247, 1524, 1748; YZ. 422, 427); cf. trömⁱ. ¶ thāla-bāgay f. distribution (of food) in numerous platefuls. -bata m. food served (at a dinner) in metal plates. As a rule at a large dinner, such as that given at a wedding, or the like, owing to the number of guests, food is served in earthenware plates. When at such a dinner the guests are served on metal plates, the feast is called by this name. -dạndᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the edge of a metal platter, etc. -khŏn f. (sg. dat. -khŏni), a pile of metal platters. -khünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -khanjĕ), a bit of a broken metal platter used as such. -khạpᵘ̈ṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. khạpᵃcĕ), a worn-out damaged little metal platter. -mŏy f. a small metal platter. -phuṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -phucĕ), a chipped or broken little metal platter. -raʦh f. (sg. dat. -raʦi), a small, light, metal platter. ¶ thālas-kĕth adv. in a platter (Gr.Gr. 43).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. tholᵘ, f. thüjᵘ̈ 2 (for 1, see s.v.) or thȧjⁱ; 2 p.p. thajyōv), to trim the branches of a tree or the like, to lop, prune (Śiv. 1573); met. to scold loudly, abuse (esp. a perverse servant), to give (someone) a dressing down. ¶ tholᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. thüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), lopped, pruned, as ab.; scolded, as ab. ¶ thȧlⁱ thȧlⁱ wālun m.inf. to lop a tree from the top downwards; met. to destroy a powerful enemy (quasi climbing to his head, and so humbling him, and then lopping off his friends and helpers one by one). For thȧlⁱ thȧlⁱ wuchun, see p. 975a, l. 47. ¶ thalith wālun m.inf. to lop off branches (and cast them down).
f. a small plate or platter; one of a pair of cymbals (or similar instrument) (Śiv. 1729).

m. (the stem of a tree used as) a pillar, column, post, pile (Śiv. 1846, 1850; Rām. 568, 1104; K.Pr. 24, 214); a prop (L. 462, W. 3). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to put a pillar, to support (e.g. a cross-beam) by a pillar. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. (in building a house, or the like) to plant, to set up, a pillar. --lagun -- m.inf. paralysis (of the neck) to occur, i.e. to get a stiff neck. ¶ thama-kŏlay f. 'a pillar-wife', a woman who is subject to all the people of a house, and who is hence, the object of much abuse; a household drudge. -tham karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. (for gend., see Gr.Gr. 75) (in building a large house) to set up all the pillars or piles for supporting the bottom storey.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. thamowᵘ), to cause to stop, to stop, to prevent going on (L.V. 38).
f. a small upright post (like one of the uprights of a spinning wheel, or the like) (El. thaimij).

or thāmun conj. 3 (2 p.p. thamyōv or thāmyōv), to become stopped, impeded, arrested (e.g. of some business in progress, of a current of water, and so on); (of someone) to be stopped, halted, impeded; to be, or become, at rest, to be without employment, to find oneself with nothing to do (cf. atha thᵒ, p. 63a, l. 11). thamyō-motᵘ or thāmyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tha(thā)myē-müʦᵘ̈ ), stopped, arrested, etc., as ab.
adj. c.g. supplied with, or having, a small upright post, as in the preceding.

m. a dish-cover, pot-lid (cf. pata ṭhᵒ karun, p. 793a, l. 48) (K.Pr. 25, 75); a cork (El.), a plug for stopping a hole; cf. ṭhāna. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to put on a lid; to cork (El.), to stop a hole with a plug (Rām. 464).

m. cloth, silk, etc., in the piece (cf. kapar-thᵒ, p. 463b, l. 36; pȧṭⁱ-thⁱ, p. 789b, l. 31; pöṭⁱ-thⁱ, p. 790a, l. 13) (W. 122, Rām. 911). ¶ thāna-poṭᵘ m. fine woollen cloth or 'puttoo' (cf. poṭᵘ 2) in the piece. --wọ̆thᵘ -- adj. (f. --wö̆ʦhᵘ̈ --), (of cloth, etc.) 'risen from the piece', just (cut off) from the piece, unused, new, fresh; met. (of some other article, such as a dish or a cooking-pot) unused, new, fresh. --wothᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --wüʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --) (of cloth, a made-up garment, or the like) 'descended from the piece', bran-new. ¶ thānukᵘ 1 (for 2, see thāna) gen. (f. thānücᵘ̈), made out of, or from, an entire piece of cloth (e.g. a garment).

m. the udder (of a cow, etc.), dug (Śiv. 1006, 1368). ¶ thana pyonᵘ m.inf. (of a human being or other animal) to be actually in the condition of being born, to be issuing from the womb. -talukᵘ adj. (f. -talücᵘ̈), 'of under the udder', freshly milked, just issued from the cow, (milk) fresh from the cow.

m. a place, site (cf. thāna) (Śiv. 242, 486, 1599, 1603, 1730); a place of abode (K. 527); esp. a sacred spot, a site holy to some deity (K. 619). al-thān, the place of the wine (of bliss), the abode of bliss, i.e. union with the Supreme (L.V. 60).

m. a dwelling-place, a place where people dwell (Śiv. 85, 1122, 1152, 1846, 1857); a sacred spot, a place hallowed by a god, a place of pilgrimage; the quarters of the officials of a town, village, or the like; a police-station; cf. thān 2. -dār the resident head official of a village or pargana (group of villages) who collects the Government revenue, the chief magistrate of a pargana (El.). -dörī f. the office or duties of the head official of a village or pargana, as ab. -dār-bāy f. the wife of the head official of a village, etc., as ab. -dārĕñ f. a female head official of a village, etc., as ab.; the wife of a head official, as ab. -gām m. the village in which the resident official head of a pargana, as ab., has his permanent office. -hūnᵘ m. 'the hound of a thāna', a surly malicious fellow permanently resident in the head- quarters of an official headman, or at a place of pilgrimage. -pȧtⁱ m. the professional priest (purōhita) or minister at a place of pilgrimage, holy place, temple, or the like (cf. RT.Tr.
