II, 380). -pȧtⁱ-bāy f. his wife. -rôchᵘ m. the appointed paid guardian or caretaker of the office of the head official of a village, or of a sacred spot. -röchⁱ 1 m., id. -röchⁱ 2 f. the office or duties of such a guardian. ¶ thānukᵘ 2 (for 1, see thān 1) gen. m. (f. thānücᵘ̈) of, or belonging to, or born or produced in a sacred spot, or in the headquarters of a head official, as ab.

m. a dish-cover, a pot-lid; the lid of a box, or the like (cf. sonduka-ṭhᵒ, p. 919a, l. 46) (Gr.M.); a cork (El. ṭhān), the stopper of a bottle (Gr.M.), a plug to fill a hole (Rām. 468); cf. ṭhān. -bāh m. steam (issuing) from a cover; met. the divulging of some secret action or scandal. Cf. bahāṭhāna, p. 97a, l. 19 -bāh gaʦhun m.inf. a scandal to be divulged. -dār adj. c.g. having the lid or cover on, (of a box) shut up. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to cork, to plug a hole (Rām. 467). --karun -- m.inf. to put the cover or lid on (a dish, box, or the like); to cover, hide, conceal, throw a veil over. --wothᵘ -- adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), having had the lid removed, opened, uncovered.
adj. c.g. cold, cool, chill (to the touch); (of a person's character) cool, cold.
f. coolness, coldness (to the touch, or in character).
f. a cooling drink; the intoxicating potion made of bhang (Śiv. (ṭhanḍöi) 231, 283; with suff. of indef. art. ṭhandāyāh, 90).
adj. c.g. a habitual swindler, a professional cheat.

m. a stain, obloquy, disrepute. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to put a bad mark against (a person), to give (a person) a bad name, to spread reports (of so-and-so's) evil conduct; to disgrace one's own family by bad conduct or the like. --lagun -- m.inf. disgrace to attach to a family, clan, or the like, owing to the bad conduct of one of its members; (owing to such a disgrace) to be barred by one's caste-fellows from intermarriage.

m. a seal, stamp (K.Pr. 127, ṭhap). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to apply a seal, to stamp, to put a seal (to a document). --karun -- m.inf. to mark (a document or the like) with a seal, to stamp (a document). --trāwun -- m.inf. to use a seal, to stamp, to seal.

m. a plunderer, looter, ravager, dacoit. --bāpār -- m. the business or occupation of a plunderer or dacoit, sack, dacoity. --hūs -- m. 'a plunderer outcry', general widespread plundering, dacoity, pillage, sack.
f. the practice or occupation of plundering, looting, dacoity.
f. the act of erecting an image for worship; the site at which such an image is erected (Śiv. 868).
or thāpēra or ṭhāpēra f. a slap (on another's face), a box on the ear (cf. thāpᵘ̈rᵘ̈).

f. (sg. dat. thapi 2, for 1, see thopᵘ) grasping by the hand, taking by the hand, a hold (cf. ȧnⁱ-thapa, p. 30b, l. 42) (Śiv. 1222, 1562, 1564; K. 680; H. xii, 12); (of vegetables, food, or the like) as much as can be held, or taken, in the hand (cf. ala-thᵒ, p. 22b, l. 31; pȧñⁱ-thⁱ, p. 746a, l. 43; sinⁱ-thⁱ, p. 957b, l. 26); a lump of this size (cf. añĕma-thᵒ, p. 37b, l. 14; öṭⁱ-thⁱ, p. 53a, l. 37; rabi-thᵒ, p. 823b, l. 8; thañi-thᵒ, p. 979b, l. 35); possession, hold (of anything); the handle, or hilt, of a sword or the like, or of a plough or the like, or met. (Śiv. 1021); plundering, looting (cf. brörⁱ-thⁱ, p. 125b, l. 44, which is reported as m.). --āsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a hold to exist; hence, to have a small share in someone else's property or business. --athi lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. possession to come into the hand, possession (esp. by scheming for an opportunity) of another's property to be obtained. --aʦüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. grasping to enter, i.e. to suffer interference at the hands of another (who has been scheming for an opportunity). --diñᵘ̈ --  f.inf. to give a grasp, to put the hand upon, to seize with violence, snatch at (Rām. 623, 1333; K. 206; H. viii, 7; xii, 12; K.Pr. 56). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'grasping to happen', i.e. possession by an evil spirit to occur, an attack of epilepsy or the like to occur; to be filled with furious rage at some untoward occurrence. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to grasp by the hand, to catch hold of (e.g. something falling) (cf. alāndĕn-thapa karañĕ, p. 25a, l. 2; khŏni thᵒ karüñᵘ̈, p. 402b, l. 9) (L.V. 4; Śiv. 598, 1220, 1493, 1861, 1877; Rām. 518, 1252, 1519; K. 596, 845; H. iii, 4, 8, 9; v, 6, 9; vi, 9; viii, 7, 9; xii, 11; K.Pr. 184). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'grasping to attack', sudden and unexpected destruction to happen (esp. to long and gradually accumulated wealth). --lāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to seize by the hand, grasp (Rām. 919, YZ. 362). --thö̆sᵘ̈ -- f. plundering and robbery, robbery and the like. --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to raise the grasp, i.e. to give up following or persecuting, to let alone (K. 366). --tulawañ -- f. the price for letting alone, blackmail or consideration given to induce a person to cease persecuting or the like, indemnity paid to a conquering foe. --ʦānüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause grasping to enter, i.e. to seize (a schemed for) opportunity for interfering in someone else's affairs. --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f. a grasp to be lifted up, persecution or following to be given up; a plague of insects or caterpillars to appear on the leaves of a crop of vegetables or the like. ¶ thapa-sār f. a banister, baluster, stair-rail (cf. sār 2). -sörᵘ̈ f. steady accumulation of stolen property, plundering over and over again and accumulating the property. -thaph f. plundering on plundering, general rapine. ¶ thapi anun m.inf. to bring by a grasp, to snatch something floating down a river. --nyunᵘ -- f.inf. to pounce down upon and carry off (K. 205). -pĕṭh rōzun m.inf. to dwell on plunder, to make a livelihood by plundering. --thapi -- adv. (with verbs of taking or the like) by plundering by a number of people, by general pillage. --thapi karun -- m.inf. to cause to be carried off in the hand by a number of people (e.g., in the free distribution of food as an act of charity, to allow the assembled people each to carry away as much as he can hold in his hand). --thŏsi -- adv. (with verbs of taking, or the like) by plundering and sacking, by pillage.

onomat. m. (sg. dat. ṭhapas), the noise made by some soft substance (such as mud or the like) rubbing against something else, swish. --karith -- adv. without obstruction. --ṭhaph -- onomat. m. the sound made by two soft substances, such as mud or the like, colliding, plop.
in ṭhāph-ṭhīph adj. c.g. or adv. duly, fitly, proper, as it ought to be.
a jingle of aphari in aphari thaphari, p. 38a, l. 42. Cf. thapēra.
adj. c.g. suffering from pain in the eye (see thapᵘ̈rᵘ̈).
m. (f. thapüjᵘ̈ or thapȧjⁱ), a plunderer, looter, dacoit, i.q. thapal, q.v. (cf. nāra-thᵒ, p. 648a, l. 35; tahāri-thᵒ, p. 983b, l. 36); snatching (El.).
f. (sg. dat. thapri), the pain caused by disease in the eyes.
or ṭhāpᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a slap (on another's face), a box on the ear, i.q. thapēra, q.v. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to slap (another) on the face.
f. in ṭhȧpⁱ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. (without preliminary bargaining) to agree (on the spot) to purchase.
f. trepidation, perturbation, ruffle, hurry, fuss, flurry, fluster (cf. thörᵘ̈, thārun, and thö̃tharun).

or (vill.) thaḍ f. (sg. obl. thürᵘ̈ 1 (thüḍᵘ̈), Gr.Gr. 70-1; for 2, see s.v.), the back (of the body) (Gr.Gr. 70, Gr.M., W. 18, Rām. 918, K.Pr. 47). --āsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a backing to exist, i.e. help to be provided to someone (e.g. by a master to a servant) endeavouring to finish some very difficult work. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to give the back', to retire into the background (out of humiliation, on finding one's skill etc. surpassed by another). --dith bĕhun -- m.inf. to turn the back (on something) and sit down, to abandon all work and do nothing; successfully to appeal for help and in consequence to remain at ease. --dith rōzun -- m.inf. successfully to appeal for help and in consequence to remain at ease. --dārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of a horse, or the like) to offer the back, to place the back at (so-and-so's) disposal (L.V. 88). --phuṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the back to be broken, i.e. help or support on which one has long depended to become destroyed or to vanish. ¶ thürᵘ̈-ḍakha m. a support to the back (when sitting,--such as a pillow behind the back, the back of a chair, or a wall). -ḍokhᵘ m., id.; (in a quarrel or the like) a backer, a supporter. -kọ̆bᵘ adj. (f. -kö̆bᵘ̈), hump- backed (El. thar-kaub). --kani --, adv. towards the back, backwards (H. v, 4, both thüḍᵘ̈ and thürᵘ̈). -konḍᵘ m. the spinal column (El. thar kúnḍ).
m. a sitting place (of brick or stone, round a shrine, house, tree, or the like).

f. shaking, trembling, quivering, shivering, quaking (cf. atha-thᵒ, p. 63a, l. 15) (Śiv. 1296, thar, m.c.). --āsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. trembling to occur, i.e. fear to be experienced, to be filled with fear. --aʦüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. trembling to enter, i.e. to attack (a person) (K. 439). --thara -- f. general trembling (of the body), shivering (esp. that of ague, etc.) (Śiv. 343, 864). --ʦānüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause trembling to enter (a person), to dismay, alarm, scare.
adj. c.g. (of woven material) strong, tough.
adj. c.g. a hasty person, excitable, impulsive.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. tharyōv), to tremble, shake, quake, quiver (from anxiety, timidity, or the like); cf. thara. tharyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tharyē-müʦᵘ̈), one who is trembling, as ab.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. thāryōv), to tremble, quiver, be in trepidation (owing to anxiety, haste, etc.) (Rām. 763, K. 81); to be in a hurry, to fuss, flurry, be in a fluster (Gr.Gr. 122); cf. thö̃tharun and thār. thāryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. thāryē-müʦᵘ̈), one who is all of a quiver as ab., one who is in a flurry, flustered.

onomat. m. the noise made by pieces of stone or by metal articles knocking against each other, bang, clash, knock (cf. chāna-ṭhᵒ, p. 162a, l. 25) (W. 140, K.Pr. 178); met. a person's fault to become a matter of public talk. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become an object of public censure, owing to the divulging of some fault. --karun -- m.inf. to make the noise of 'bang', 'crash', and so on. --ṭhas -- onomat. m. to knock, or tap, on a door, on the ground, or the like (K.Pr. 219). --ṭhis -- onomat. m. the noise made by repeatedly striking a gong, bell, or the like (esp. when out of sight and not loud). Cf. ṭhis ṭhis, l. 12, bel. ¶ ṭhasa-bar m. a door which shuts itself with a bang. -baran f. (sg. dat. -barüñᵘ̈), a doorway with doors of this description.
onomat. m. the noise made by something solid flung down forcibly to the ground and smashed, crash, smash.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭhôsᵘ; f.pl. ṭhāsĕ or ṭhāsa, Gr.Gr. 208; 2 p.p. ṭhāsyōv or ṭhāsōv, Gr.Gr. 225), to hammer, or drive, forcibly into the ground, into a log, or the like; to smash against the ground (cf. bāna ṭhāsȧnⁱ, p. 110a, l. 3); cf. ṭhākun and ṭhukun. ṭhôsᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ṭhösᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), driven in, hammered in, as ab.
or ṭhāsarāray f. a series of sounds of crashing (see ṭhās) (such as that caused by the falling of houses in an earthquake, of trees being felled, of rocks being hurled down, and so on).
in thatha matha adj. c.g. very fat, very plump, corpulent.

in ṭhaṭh-bakürᵘ̈ f. internal hollowness with outside strength, unsubstantiality, apparent strength with internal weakness. ṭhaṭha-bạkᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f., id.; unsubstantial conduct (e.g. after giving notice of distribution of much property, to make a habit of distributing things of little value).

m. (? dat.) trust, confidence, intimacy; design, scheme, plan; arrangement, adjustment; splendid apparel, magnificence, the wearing handsome clothes etc., adornment, decoration. --bĕhanāwun -- m.inf. to set in order, (of some business which has become weak or slack) to pull (it) together, to set (it) on a firm basis. --thawun -- m.inf. to keep up appearances, somehow or other to make a good show before the world (even when really poverty-stricken, unsuccessful, or the like).

m. a jest, joke, ridicule (Gr.M., Śiv. 73). -böshⁱ f. resemblance to a joke, i.e. conducting any business as though it were a joke, acting as if in jest. -bāz adj. c.g. jocular, facetious, waggish, a wag. --karun -- m.inf. to jest (with, dat.), to play tricks with (e.g. having promised something, at the time due for performance to pretend to deny the promise) (Śiv. 1390; K. 617, 989). -motᵘ adj. (f. -müʦᵘ̈), addicted to jokes, one who is a confirmed or habitual joker (K. 989).
i.q. ṭaṭhȧjⁱ, q.v. Cf. phal-ṭhᵒ, p. 692a, l. 15.

m. (sg. dat. ṭhaṭharas), a part of the wall of a house, supporting the main beams of the roof, etc., and formed of logs laid horizontally upon each other; cf. ṭhoṭhᵘ. ṭhaṭhar-mŏ̈ndᵘ̈ f. one of these logs.
f. a kind of grass, said to cut the skin at a mere touch, and to have sharp tips (Rām. 1631); grass and briars used as fuel (L. 460, thathri).
(for 2, see ṭhoṭhᵘ), in ṭhȧṭhⁱ anun m.inf. to reason with (an angry person or the like), coax, conciliate. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. (of an angry person or the like) to become conciliated, coaxed to reason.

m. the place where something (esp. something hidden or lost) is, the place to which one seeks to be directed by a clue (in searching). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to find such a place by means of a clue; to endeavour to find by such a clue. --nērun -- m.inf. the place of deposit (as ab.) to be discovered after tracing a clue. -pata m. a clue to such a place; the place for which such a clue is required.
m. the first beginning (in making something, e.g. in building a house). --lāgun -- m.inf. to set to work at the very beginning (as ab.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. thāwanôwᵘ), to cause to be put or placed (El.). Causal of thawun or thāwun, q.v. in all its senses (Śiv. 1393).
or thāwawunᵘ n.ag. (f. tha(thā)wavüñᵘ̈ ), one who puts, one who places, etc., in all the meanings of thawun, q.v. (Śiv. 861 (thā˚), 945 (tha˚)).

or thāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. thowᵘ or thôwᵘ), to put, place, set, lay (upon or before), apply (cf. anda thᵒ, p. 32a, l. 7; ȧndⁱ thᵒ, p. 31b, l. 33; athi thᵒ, p. 66a, l. 22; bāl thᵒ or bölⁱ thᵒ, p. 104a, ll. 10, 24; bôrᵘ thᵒ, p. 118a, l. 28; börⁱ thᵒ, p. 118b, l. 3; baṭhi thᵒ, p. 140b, l. 18; boṭhᵘ thᵒ, p. 140a, l. 41; buthi thᵒ, p. 143b, l. 14; bayĕs tal thᵒ, p. 148b, l. 39; dubari- shāh thᵒ, p. 184b, l. 10; dāg thᵒ, p. 194a, l. 15; dashĕ thawañĕ, p. 252b, l. 31; khōr thᵒ, p. 410a, l. 22; lyobᵘ ṭhᵒ, p. 543a, l. 23; nam tal thᵒ, p. 635b, l. 9; naphᵃs manz thᵒ, p. 645b, l. 11; nyāra thᵒ, p. 673a, l. 44; nazar thavüñᵘ̈, p. 676a, l. 25; pajĕ-tal thᵒ, p. 724a, l. 30; pali thᵒ, p. 730a, l. 41; parda thᵒ, p. 756b, l. 10; pēshĕs thᵒ, p. 778a, l. 10; path path thᵒ, p. 792a, l. 36; shĕchⁱ thavüñᵘ̈, p. 870a, l. 48; sūrᵘ̈-pĕṭh thᵒ, p. 931a, l. 38; srŏdi thᵒ, p. 933b, l. 4; tāha tāha thᵒ, p. 966a, l. 3; ṭhŏli ṭhŏli thᵒ, p. 976a, l. 23; tal-kun thᵒ, s.v. tal 1; talyumᵘ pĕṭh thᵒ; tandali thᵒ, s.v. tandal; ʦapi thᵒ, s.v. ʦaph 2 (Gr.M.; L.V. thā˚, 70; Śiv. tha˚, 189, 704, 1084, 1089, 1098, 1632, 1715; thā˚, 169, 353, 1090, 1257, 1815; Rām. tha˚, 27, 69, 120, 175, 587, 603, 662, 688, 795, 1178, 1269, 1436; thā˚, 440, 705, 707, 757, 1443, 1552; K. tha˚, 82, 118, 151, 357, 366, 389, 427; H. tha˚, iii, 1; x, 5, 10; xii, 9; thā˚, ii, 4; iii, 5, 9; v, 11; vi, 5; viii, 9, 11; ix, 4; x, 12; xii, 4, 12, 15, 23; YZ. thā˚, 265; K.Pr. 135, where tahwizen is a misprint for thȧvⁱzĕn); ¶ to put into a certain condition (and leave there) (cf. brôrᵘ mörith thᵒ, p. 125b, l. 11; brö̃ʦᵘ̈ thᵒ, p. 127b, l. 41; lōla thᵒ, p. 523a, l. 20; phih thᵒ, p. 686a, l. 42; thodᵘ thᵒ, p. 970b, l. 40; ʦūri thᵒ, s.v. ʦūrᵘ̈) (Gr.M.; Śiv. tha˚, 738; thā˚, 1756; YZ. thā˚, 114); to found (upon), base (upon) (cf. bāzĕ-pĕṭh thᵒ, p. 153a, l. 6); ¶ to put down (and go away), to leave (there), to allow to remain (cf. gōr thᵒ, p. 297b, l. 16; nām thawȧnⁱ, p. 636b, l. 8; nāv thᵒ, p. 665b, l. 10; rāza-kaṭh thᵒ, p. 857a, l. 29; shĕyĕ thᵒ, p. 902b, l. 39; sọ̆kᵒruy thᵒ, p. 907b, l. 17) (Gr.M.; L.V. thā˚, 27; Śiv. tha˚, 1302; Rām. tha˚, 7, 950, 1283, 1292; thā˚, 416, 742, 942, 951, 1103; K. tha˚, 71, 812, 827; H. tha˚, viii, 7); to put down (and give to someone), to make over (to someone, as a gift) (Rām. tha˚, 5); to put down, lay down, show as proved (pharkh thᵒ, p. 704b, l. 21); ¶ to put in a certain condition, to cause to be so-and-so (cf. prasan thᵒ, p. 767b, l. 46; rum rum shĕrmanda ṭhᵒ, p. 833b, l. 41; rözⁱ thᵒ, p. 858a, l. 21) (Gr.M.; Śiv. tha˚, 182, 572, 604, 1492, 1554, 1777; thā˚, 23, 1531, 1732, 1785); ¶ to deposit (e.g. earnest money), lay down, stake, pledge (cf. band thᵒ, p. 111a, l. 36; bȧndⁱ thᵒ, p. 111b, l. 16; nyās thᵒ, p. 674a, l. 10; say thᵒ, p. 955b, l. 40); to put by, put aside (cf. batas thᵒ, p. 137b, l. 34; tal tal thᵒ, s.v. tal 1) (Gr.M.; YZ. thā˚, 405); ¶ to fix, arrange, found, establish (hŏb thᵒ, p. 321a, l. 21; langar thᵒ, p. 527a, l. 31; nēb thᵒ, p. 619b, l. 27; nākh dōla thᵒ, p. 629b, l. 5; nōkh thᵒ, p. 629b, l. 43; nēm thᵒ, p. 637a, l. 6; nĕyĕm thᵒ, p. 671a, l. 6; niyāz thᵒ, p. 675a, l. 25; phēra thᵒ, p. 701b, l. 1; pariʦar thᵒ, p. 771b, l. 46; pȧṭⁱñĕ thᵒ, p. 802a, l. 42; pay thᵒ, p. 812a, l. 24; rāy thavüñᵘ̈, p. 854b, l. 19; sag thᵒ, p. 866b, l. 38; shĕkh thᵒ, p. 876b, l. 44; sĕka thᵒ, p. 904a, l. 39; sŏkha thᵒ, p. 905b, l. 28; salāh thᵒ, p. 909b, l. 39; sār thᵒ, p. 928b, l. 38; ṭhāṭh thᵒ, p. 986a, l. 41; thüzᵘ̈ thavüñᵘ̈, s.v. thüzᵘ̈ 2; talkha thᵒ; tanzi thᵒ, s.v. tünzᵘ̈) (Gr.M.; Śiv. tha˚, 70, 357, 436, 709, 864, 1311; Rām. tha˚, 73, 311, 627, 696, 941-2, 1095, 1253, 1505; thā˚, 1739, 1783; K. tha˚, 720; YZ. thā˚, 26; K.Pr. tha˚, 44, 92); ¶ to impose, put upon (a person) (cf. bīm thᵒ, p. 107a, l. 30; bayĕ thᵒ, p. 148b, l. 31; dāba thᵒ, p. 182a, l. 32; lādan thavüñᵘ̈, p. 509a, l. 44; minath thavüñᵘ̈, p. 582b, l. 15; myondᵘ thᵒ, p. 613b, l. 33; pyāda thᵒ, p. 813b, l. 29; ṭö̃ṭa thᵒ, s.v. ṭö̃ṭa 1) (Gr.M.; Rām. tha˚, 190, 639, 1143, 1741; thā˚, 211; K. tha˚, 719); ¶ to set (something) in action, to set (a procedure) going (cf. magar thᵒ, p. 552b, l. 24; pachān thᵒ, p. 679b, l. 27; phāka thᵒ, p. 688a, l. 29; pakhyāg thᵒ, p. 727b, l. 38; praʦaras thᵒ, p. 771b, l. 35; pata-thüzᵘ̈ thᵒ, p. 795a, l. 50; rōza thawañĕ, p. 858a, l. 4; shĕr thᵒ, p. 889a, l. 16; talāsh thᵒ) (Gr.M.; Śiv. tha˚, 759, 1015, 1166, 1832; thā˚, 1878; Rām. tha˚, 468; H. thā˚, viii, 3; YZ. thā˚, 38, 231; K.Pr. thā˚, 87); ¶ to apply, ascribe, impute (cf. bāv thᵒ, p. 146b, l. 47) (K. tha˚, 823, 903); ¶ to engage, employ, appoint, take into service (cf. bandēla thᵒ, p. 111b, l. 50) (Gr.M.; Śiv. tha˚, 341, 1148; Rām. tha˚, 395; K. tha˚, 1163; H. thā˚, ii, 11; viii, 14; xi, 6); to put into use, utilize, use, exercise (a faculty, etc.) (cf. bāsh thᵒ, p. 132a, l. 40; cĕth thᵒ, p. 177b, l. 28; hōsh thᵒ, p. 353a, l. 20; khabar thavüñᵘ̈, p. 391a, l. 28; kan thᵒ, p. 447b, l. 16; mag thavüñᵘ̈, p. 551b, l. 18; thopᵘ and thapi thᵒ, p. 980a, ll. 33, 44) (Gr.M.; L.V. thā˚, 91; Śiv. tha˚, 40, 584, 637, 697, 765, 807, 821, 906, 988, 1194, 1227, 1293, 1361-2, 1365, 1558, 1726, 1873; thā˚, 420, 533, 544, 596, 644, 880, 1594, 1668, 1803; Rām. tha˚, 29, 55, 60, 209, 334, 455, 500, 1108, 1195, 1208, 1284, 1286, 1460, 1602; thā˚, 83, 486, 523, 1366, 1758; H. tha˚, ii, 7; thā˚, viii, 6, 8, 11; ix, 1, 4; YZ. thā˚, 556); ¶ to utilize (a door, lock, or the like, by opening or shutting), (hence, either) to open (a door, etc.) (cf. darwāza thᵒ, p. 250b, l. 41; kuluph thāᵒ, p. 440b, l. 10) (Gr.M.; H. thā˚, iii, 8; viii, 4, 12); (or) to shut (a door) (Rām. tha˚, 16, 22, 1557); ¶ to keep, maintain, retain, hold (cf. āsh thavüñᵘ̈, p. 47b, l. 2; brã̄th thavüñᵘ̈, p. 127b, l. 37; dörī thavüñᵘ̈, p. 237b, l. 22; lang thᵒ, p. 526b, l. 12; mēl thᵒ, p. 565b, l. 28; manas thᵒ, p. 572b, l. 20; maʦhi-ganḍas thᵒ, p. 609a, l. 43; māwas thavüñᵘ̈, p. 612a, l. 8; nam thawȧnⁱ, p. 635a, l. 47; nyāl thᵒ, p. 670b, l. 10; niyĕth thavüñᵘ̈, p. 674b, l. 12; nazari-tal thᵒ, p. 676b, l. 20; phikir thavüñᵘ̈, p. 690b, l. 25; phir-mal thᵒ, p. 701b, l. 46; prāy thavüñᵘ̈, p. 773b, l. 19; prayĕm thᵒ, p. 774a, l. 31; paʦh thavüñᵘ̈, p. 807a, l. 38; shē̃kh thavüñᵘ̈, p. 877a, l. 40; samaʦār thᵒ, p. 915b, l. 14; sir thᵒ, p. 929b, l. 33; sŏr thᵒ, p. 930b, l. 33; sarmāyĕ thᵒ, p. 935b, l. 29; sōṭh thᵒ, p. 946a, l. 48; ʦĕtas thᵒ, s.v. ʦĕth 2) (Gr.M.; Śiv. tha˚, 693; thā˚, 556-7; Rām. tha˚, 736, 994, 1231, 1764; thā˚, 626, 1574-5, 1656, 1728, 1773; H. thā˚, v. 10; xii, 25); ¶ to keep back, reserve, leave (unused) (cf. bökⁱ thᵒ, p. 98b, l. 26; dã̄d wöyith thawȧnⁱ, p. 187a, l. 26; path thawun, p. 792a, l. 48) (Gr.M.; K. tha˚, 237; H. thā˚, x, 17); to put away, conceal (cf. ṭhari thᵒ, p. 983a, l. 16) (K. tha˚, 1143); ¶ to give up, cease (cf. bākh thavüñᵘ̈, p. 99a, l. 45); ¶ to deem, esteem, consider (cf. bas thāv, enough! p. 131a, l. 41; lŏkoṭᵘ thᵒ, p. 521b, l. 16; nishcay thᵒ, p. 655b, l. 50; ṭôṭhᵘ thᵒ) (Gr.M.). ¶ This verb is frequently used with the conj. part. or freq. part. of another verb, to form an intensive compound. The force is that of the main verb, to which is added the idea of thorough and final completion. Thus, bögᵃrith thᵒ, p. 93a, l. 3; būzith thᵒ, p. 154a, l. 26; cĕth thᵒ, p. 179b, l. 13; cövith thᵒ, p. 178b, l. 40; dȧbⁱ dȧbⁱ thᵒ and dabith thᵒ, p. 183b, ll. 38, 40; dọ̆bᵃrith thᵒ, p. 184b, l. 45; dabavith thᵒ, p. 185a, l. 25; dagith thᵒ, p. 196b, l. 6; ḍölith thᵒ, p. 214a, l. 17; ḍölⁱ ḍölⁱ thᵒ and ḍölith thᵒ, p. 214a, ll. 24, 27; khaṭith thᵒ, pp. 423a, l. 9, and 423b, l. 26; latörit thᵒ, p. 539a, l. 30; napith thᵒ, p. 645b, l. 48; phirith thᵒ, p. 707b, l. 29; pövith thᵒ, p. 810b, l. 45; rachĕ karith thᵒ, p. 824b, l. 7; rᵃsith thᵒ, p. 844a, l. 21; rᵃsavith thᵒ, p. 844b, l. 27; shīrith thᵒ, p. 894a, l. 23; sọ̆mbᵃ̇rᵃ̇ sọ̆mbᵃ̇rᵃ̇ thᵒ, p. 912a, l. 33; sŏrith thᵒ, p. 936b, l. 41; tāh karith thᵒ, p. 965b, l. 48; tŏh karith thᵒ, p. 970a, l. 5; thodᵘ tulith thᵒ, p. 970b, l. 46; ṭhīkᵃrövith thᵒ, p. 975a, l. 25; thipith thᵒ, p. 981b, l. 49; ṭĕpⁱ ṭĕpⁱ thᵒ and ṭĕpith thᵒ, s.v. ṭĕpun; tōr dith thᵒ, s.v. tōr 1; trȧpⁱ trȧpⁱ thᵒ, s.v. trapun; trọ̆pᵃrith thᵒ, s.v. trọ̆pᵃrun; so trọ̆pᵃrövith thᵒ; ʦĕlith thᵒ, s.v. ʦĕlun; ʦörith thᵒ, s.v. ʦārun) (so Rām. tha˚, 23, 197, 1772; thā˚, 887, 1266-7; K. tha˚, 816; H. thā˚, x, 3; YZ. thā˚, 158-9). ¶ thowᵘ-motᵘ or thôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. thüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ or thövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), put, placed, etc., as ab. (Rām. tho˚, 175, 587, 1269, 1253, 1557; thô˚, 757, 887; K. tho˚, 720, 903); put down and left; hence, remaining over, still remaining, unexhausted (K. tho˚, 237).
m. (sg. dat. thāwaras), a mountain-range, a mountain (Śiv. 1259).
m. highness, height, loftiness, elevation. Cf. thodᵘ.

m. height, loftiness, highness (Gr.Gr. 29, 140; Gr.M.); the upstream (of a river) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1052, 1878; YZ. 450); met. highness of qualities, dexterity (cf. atha-thᵒ, p. 63a, l. 32); an acclivity (El.); a high, or elevated, place (K. 372, 443). Cf. thodᵘ.
f. (sg. dat. thạzᵃrüñᵃ), making high, making higher, elevating (materially or morally).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. thạzᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. thạzᵃrun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 173). thạzᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. thạzᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. thạzᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, s.v. thạzᵃrun, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. thạzᵒrᵒ), to make high, make higher, to raise, elevate (either materially or morally) (Gr.Gr. 7). thạzᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. thạzᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), raised, elevated, as ab.
(or ṭhī˜ca) pakun  m.inf. (of blood, or the like), to flow in a violent torrent (cf. rath ṭhī˜ca wasun, p. 845b, l. 29).
in the following:-- ṭhĕcĕ-pholᵘ m. treasure gradually and secretly collected, a secret hoard. Cf. ṭhī˜ṭh.
m.pl. airs, ostentation used in the following (cf. tĕh):--thēh dinⁱ or --mārȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to put on airs and graces (owing to pride in youthful beauty, wealth, or the like).

m. in the following:--ṭhēka āsun m.inf. urging (esp. one who is unwilling to go on with or complete some work) to occur. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to accept urging, to agree to continue with, or to complete, some work at another's urging. --karun -- m.inf. to agree or assent to undertake the completion of some work. --nyunᵘ -- m.inf., i.q. ṭhēka hyonᵘ, ab.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. thĕkanôwᵘ), to cause to boast, to praise, applaud (Śiv. 1653); to be, or become, praiseworthy (Rām. 1441, n.ag. thĕkanāwunᵘ).
n.ag. (f. thĕkavüñᵘ̈), a boaster; a fop (El.).
f. praise (Gr.Gr. 120); flattery, adulation; esp. self-praise, self-commendation (without due reason).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. thyokᵘ, f. thë̆cᵘ̈; 2 p.p. thĕcyōv), to boast, brag, vaunt, praise oneself (whether entitled to do so or not) (Gr.Gr. 120; W. 132; K. 330, 647; K.Pr. 101, 107, 236 (thuktam for thyokᵘtham)); to praise, commend, applaud, magnify, exalt (Śiv. 1627); to vie with, emulate, rival (dat. of obj.) (Rām. 1099). thĕkun lāyĕkh adj. (f. thĕküñᵘ̈ lāyĕkh, see lāyĕkh) worthy of praise, fit to be praised, commendable. Cf. thĕkanas lāᵒ, bel. ¶ thĕkan-thöjᵘ̈ f. 'a platter of boasting', a self-applauding woman, a woman who habitually boasts or praises herself. ¶ thĕkanas lāyĕkh adj. c.g. (see lāyĕkh) praiseworthy, i.q. thĕkun lāᵒ, ab. ¶ thyokᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. thë̆cᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), praised, glorified, commended.
adj. c.g. a habitual flatterer, a habitual adulator (Gr.Gr. 120); esp. a habitual self-praiser, a habitual boaster, a braggart (without due reason).
f. loftiness, height (of some part of the body, such as the brow) (cf. ḍĕka-ṭhᵒ, p. 204b, l. 26). Cf. ṭhŏla.

m. a large bag, a sack (El., K. 953); a sack-like part of the intestines (cf. garba-ṭhᵒ, p. 300a, l. 5; pēshābukᵘ ṭhᵒ, p. 780a, l. 49); cf. ṭhīlⁱ. -kapur m. (sg. dat. -kaparas), sackcloth, coarse cloth for making sacks.
adv. here and there, all about, everywhere (inside and outside, up and down) (u.w.vbs. of seeking or the like).
adj. c.g. firm, steady; permanent, eternal, everlasting (Śiv. 243, thĕrāh, with suff. of indef. art.).
m. a kind of mantle, cloak, wrapper, made of woollen cloth.
f. (sg. dat. thë̆ʦᵘ̈), stability, permanence, continuance in existence (Śiv. 977, 1587; K. 615, 623).
m. N. of a village on the shore of the Ḍal lake, about a mile from Gupakār (q.v.), where there is a sacred site. Its ancient name was Thēda (RT.Tr. II, 454).
m. a fixed place or abode (Gr.M.); the proper place (for anything); dwelling-place, residence, home; certainty, absence of doubt (Gr.M.).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ṭhīkyōv), to stand firmly, to be steady, remain steady (cf. atha ṭhᵒ, p. 63a, l. 9) (Gr.Gr. 173, Siv. 1752, Rām. 1659); to come to a firm stand, to become steady (cf. prān ṭhīkȧnⁱ, p. 761a, l. 30; shāh ṭhᵒ, p. 873a, l. 13). ṭhīkyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ṭhīkyē-müʦᵘ̈), made to stand firmly, come to a steady stand.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭhīkᵃrôwᵃ), to set up firmly, to fix firmly, to make steady (something unsteady) (Gr.Gr. 173); to establish firmly. ¶ ṭhīkᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. ṭhīkᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), made firm, fixed, established (by someone). ¶ ṭhīkᵃrövith thowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. --thüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), fixed, established, installed. --thawun -- m.inf. to fix, establish, instal.

f. the fashion in which a turban is wound round the head; a blow at a ball in hockey, polo, or the like (cf. potᵘ ṭhil kaḍᵘ̈ñᵘ̈, p. 788a, l. 18). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'the blow of the ball to come', (by one engaged in a hard struggle for victory) sudden and decisive defeat to be experienced. ¶ ṭhila kaḍañĕ f. pl. inf. 'to pull out blows of the ball', (of one previously in subjection) to conquer over and over again, to win repeatedly. ¶ ṭhilan gindun m.inf. 'to play at ball-blows', to strive for the mastery.
f. (sg. abl. ṭhēli) a small sack (cf. ṭhēla), a bag, purse (El., Gr.M., Śiv. 1079, K.Pr. 86).
onomat. m. the noise made by a bell or the like, tinkle, ting (Śiv. 1847); cf. ṭhañ. ṭhiñ-ṭhiñ onomat. m. the gentle sound of repeated ringing of a bell, cymbals, or the like, tinkling.

f. (sg. dat. thipi, or, in some connexions, thēpi), a number of slaps delivered on any part of the body by another with the palm of the hand, a slapping (cf. atha-thᵒ, p. 63a, l. 13). ¶ thēpi thēpi dyunᵘ m.inf. to give a thorough slapping (as a punishment); met. to give a severe scolding. --thēpi korᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --thēpi kürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --) (usually of some dependent) one who has received slappings (as a punishment) from a number of people. --thēpi karun -- m.inf. to cause someone (esp. a dependent) to be slapped by a number of people.
in ṭhiph dith or --karith -- adv. suddenly, unexpectedly, unawares, all at once (esp. of recovery from illness).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. thyupᵘ), to slap another with the palm of the hand; to pat (something into shape) (cf. dramba thipañĕ, p. 245a, l. 46); cf. thiph. thyupᵘ-motᵘ  perf. part. (f. thipᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), slapped (of some part of the body); patted (as ab.). thipith thawun m.inf. to cow by a slapping.
f. (a portable brazier or the like) filled up with charcoal, etc. (cf. nāra-ṭhᵒ, p. 648a, l. 38).

f. (sg. dat. thērĕ), a kind of twig broom or besom, used for sweeping out the dung from a cow-house (cf. gĕv-thᵒ, p. 316b, l. 12) (Śiv. 1032). ¶ thēri-dŏph m. (sg. dat. -dŏpas), a certain shrub that grows in the hill-forests. --khôrᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --khörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), caused to become prosperously successful (of a person, thing, occupation, or the like), perfected by being endowed with good qualities, education, wealth, etc. --khārun -- m.inf. to cause (a pupil or other person by proper instruction and bringing up) to be prosperously successful, to cause (a thing, business, or the like) to become prosperously successful. --khasun -- m.inf. to mount on the broom, to become prosperously successful (by being endowed with wealth, health, prosperity, offspring, etc.). --khotᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --khüʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), become prosperously successful, as. ab. -laʦhüjᵘ̈ f. a broom. --tᵘ̈jᵘ̈ -- f. a twig used in making these brooms.

onomat. m. the noise made by a single stroke on a bell, gong, or the like, ting, tinkle (Gr.Gr. 13). --ṭhis -- onomat. m. the subdued noise of reiterated gentle strokes on a bell, gong, or the like. Cf. ṭhas ṭhis, p. 984b, l. 49.

ṭhisurᵘ, or ṭhusurᵘ m. a ripened boil or similar gathering (cf. pāka-ṭhᵒ, p. 725b, l. 15). --hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. --hishᵘ̈ --) (of someone who has eaten to repletion, a leather bag or similar receptacle, and so on) full, bursting full (like a ripened boil).
f. in ṭhī˜ṭh mī˜ṭh f. a person's entire household property (including money, articles, etc.). Cf. ṭhĕcĕ.
adv. in front of, in the presence of.

or ṭhŏbba m. (pl. dat. thŏban or ṭhŏban), a round piece of earthenware or shaped piece of potsherd, about the size and shape of a rupee. A number of these are used as pieces by children in a certain game. thŏba-katᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or ṭhŏbba-katᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a piece of potsherd shaped like a rupee used as ab. The pl. -katrĕ is used for the stock of sherds used in a game. thŏban (or ṭhŏban) gindun  m.inf. to play this game.
m. a short thick tree, without branches, a bush, scrub; met. (in this sense, f. thŏbüñᵘ̈), a stout squat-figured person.
m. a plug, in lyobᵘ-thobᵘ, p. 543b, l. 21, q.v. Cf. thopᵘ.
f.pl. thrusts, or thrusting, with the toes; cf. ṭhukun. --diñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to push, or thrust (someone or something) with the toes (in order to set him or it in motion).

adj. (f. thüzᵘ̈ 1, for 2, see s.v.), high, tall, lofty (cf. pōra-thᵒ, p. 753b, l. 9) (El. thŏd, thaud; Gr.Gr. 9, 29, 140; Gr.M.; W. 20; Śiv. 784, 1050, 1811; Rām. 600; YZ. 409; K.Pr. 165); upright, erect (cf. kāri-thᵒ, p. 467a, l. 31) (Śiv. 971, of the neck, see p. 1167a, l. 31; so, 1363; H. vii, 11; YZ. 64, 146); elevated, on a high place (Śiv. 985, 1068); high (in price) (Gr.M.); high-minded, on one's dignity, on the high horse (K.Pr. 258). --karun -- m.inf. to exalt (El.). --rōzun -- m.inf. (of something previously bent or prone) to remain or continue erect (YZ. 298). --thawun -- or --thāwun -- m.inf. to put in a higher position, to raise (and leave raised); to set upright, to erect. --tulun -- m.inf. to raise (e.g. someone from a sitting position) (El., Śiv. 1812, YZ. 184); to erect; to lift up (and remove) (Rām. 123, 1417, 1495). --tulith thawun -- or --tulith thāwun -- m.inf. to raise and put down (elsewhere); hence, to remove a person (from an office, or the like). --tulith ʦhunun -- m.inf. to raise (once for all); to raise and carry off; to raise and put away, to wipe off, sweep off. --wŏthun -- m.inf. to stand up (El.; Śiv. 321; Rām. 707, 903, 942, 952, 961, 1384; H. ii, 3, 5, 6; v, 6, 9; xii, 14, 15; K.Pr. 165). ¶ thadi adv. on high (K. 154, 446); from on high; (of a voice, or the like) high, loudly. --pala -- adv. with great nobility, with great magnanimity; with great superiority. --thadi -- adv. high (in every respect), at a great height (in every particular); from a great height (in every particular); (of a voice, or the like) loudly (i.e. with each word loud). --thodᵘ -- adj. (f. --thüzᵘ̈ --), lofty in every respect. ¶ thadam-thodᵘ adj. (f. -thüzᵘ̈), very high, very lofty; very elevated.
m. one who is in the habit of dishonestly interfering with another's work, so as to appropriate its results.

or thöjᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. thājĕ), a large-sized metal plate, dish, or tray for food, etc. (cf. diva-gōn-thᵒ, p. 261b, l. 18; diwath-thᵒ, p. 265a, l. 26; siwan-thᵒ, p. 954a, l. 30; thĕkan-thᵒ, s.v. thĕkun) (K. 154, 161-2; K.Pr. 132, 163, misprinted tha˚ for thā); a crucible (for melting gold, etc.) (cf. payĕn-thᵒ, p. 817b, l. 2; sŏnar-thᵒ, p. 923a, l. 43); a lapidary's polishing wheel (cf. manᵃr-thᵃ, p. 581b, l. 5). Cf. thāl, which is equivalent to our 'plate'.
adj. c.g. a spitter, one who habitually spits.
adj. c.g. one who is the leading person in a company or community (cf. ṭhōkh, ab.).

f. (sg. dat. thŏki), spittle, saliva (cf. lĕkh-thᵒ, p. 518a, l. 16; shāla-thᵒ, p. 880a, l. 17; tīla-thᵒ, s.v. tīl) (K.Pr. 26, 63, 215, 258, 262); spitting. ¶ thŏka-bāna m. a spitting-pot, a spittoon. -buthᵘ m. a 'spit-face', one whose face should be spit upon, i.e. one who is engaged in some very vile or blameworthy occupation. --hĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to receive spittings, to be an object of general scorn on account of vile occupation or of blameworthy actions. --khĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to eat spittles, to become an object of scorn, as ab. -lôdᵘ m. a pile or accumulation of spittle. -lọ̆ʦhᵘ m. a lump of thick spittle, a clot of phlegm expelled from the mouth. -mūnᵘ m. an accumulation of spittle, as it were, plastered on a wall or the like. -nūn m. spittle-salt, one's own spittle mixed with salt (applied as a remedy to a blister on the foot caused by walking). --rāʦavith -- conj. part. used as adv. (with verbs of giving, etc.) with much ignominy, most insultingly (as if the gift was daubed with the giver's spittle). --trāwañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to reject with scorn (as if one ejects spittle at it) (K.Pr. 166). --ʦhunañĕ --  f. pl. inf. to spit (upon, dat.) (K.Pr. 12); to eject spittles, to make the noise of spitting; hence, to abuse some committer of a vile or despicable action. ¶ thŏki thŏki gōmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --thŏki gömüʦᵘ̈ --), one who has become an object of universal blame and contempt, on account of vile or despicable conduct. --thŏki gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become the object of universal blame and contempt, as ab. --thŏki korᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --thŏki kürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), spat upon by everyone, i.e. universally despised and blamed on account of vile or despicable conduct. --thŏki karun -- m.inf. to make (a person) an object of universal blame and contempt, as ab.

m. in ṭhōkh-dār m. the head of a company or community, the leading man of a village (whose position is due to rank, generosity, virtue, good family, or similar reason) (cf. ṭhōkal). -dörī f. the office or position of the head man of a community (see the preceding).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. thọ̆kᵘ, f. thö̆cᵘ̈; 2 p.p. thŏcyōv), to spit, expectorate. ¶ thokᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. thö̆cᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), spit out; spit at or on; disgraced by vile abusive language; one whose conduct or occupation is very vile; one who has fallen under an utterly evil fate, despised and rejected. ¶ thŏkan atha dārun m.inf. 'holding the hand to be spit upon', to be utterly subservient (to); met. to show entire loving subserviency (to a friend, master, servant, or the like).

m. (sg. dat. ṭhôkuras, Rām. 952), an idol, an image for worship (Gr.M.; L. 264; Rām. 580, 585, 944-5, 950, 952; K. 974). ṭhôkur-brôhmun m. (sg. dat. -bröhmanas), an idol Brāhmaṇ, a paid Brāhmaṇ in attendance on an idol, who conducts the worship. -dwār or ṭhōkura-dwār m. an idol-house, temple (Gr.M.). -kuṭhᵘ m. the room or shrine in a house in which the image of a god is set up for worship (El. ṭhokur-kuṭ. According to El. it is generally on the second floor of a house). -söb m. the image of a god.

adj. (f. thücᵘ̈), wearied, tired, fatigued, exhausted, jaded (cf. thakun, of which this is the 1 p.p.). --bokᵘ -- adj. (f. thücᵘ̈ bücᵘ̈), wearied and hungry (e.g. a person on a pilgrimage); worn out, troubled, confounded.

f. a blow or thrust with the horns (given by a horned animal) (cf. nẹ̆ndᵃri-ṭhŏla, p. 642b, l. 18) (Gr.Gr. 134). Cf. ṭhũ̄̈kh. ¶ ṭhŏla diñĕ f. pl. inf. to thrust with the horns, to gore, to butt. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a ram that butts, a ram kept and trained for fighting other rams. --lāyĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to strike blows with the horns, to horn, gore, butt; met. to display arrogance. -ṭhŏl f. mutual striking with the horns, a fight between horned animals, a butting contest between rams (Gr.Gr. 75). ¶ ṭhŏli dyunᵘ m.inf. (in a fight or quarrel) to give before (i.e. in advance of) (the adversary). --ṭhŏli thawun -- m.inf. to set (two posts or the like) head joining head. --thawun -- m.inf. to set in front (of another).
adj. c.g. possessing a lofty forehead, high-browed. Cf. ṭhĕl and ṭhŏl.

adj. c.g. a horned animal which is habitually addicted to attacking with its horns, or (of a ram) to butting (Gr.Gr. 134). --kaṭh -- m. (sg. dat. --kaṭas --), a ram which is addicted to attacking anyone (or any other animal) by butting.
m. partaking of, affected by, a recipient of, used --˚ with words implying abuse, or the like, as in wŏhav-tholᵘ, a recipient of a curse.
1 p.p. of thalun, q.v. (f. thüjᵘ̈ 2, for 1, see s.v.) trimmed (of the branches of a tree) used --˚ as in aḍa-thᵒ, p. 12a, l. 21.
m. the amount (of liquid, or the like) contained in the palm of the hand stretched out and hollowed, a handful (cf. pā̃-thᵒ, p. 748a, l. 21).
m. Allium sativum (El. thóm. Cf. lasam).

m. in the following:-- thāmi gōmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), stopped, made to cease (any work by some impediment); halted (by some impediment), stopped (when in motion); cf. thamun or thāmun and tham. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be stopped, to be made to cease (in any work by some impediment); to be made to stand still, to stand still, to stop (when in motion), halt. --korᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --kürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), caused to stop, made to cease (in any work by someone impeding); halted, caused to stop (when in motion, by someone impeding). --karun -- m.inf. to cause someone to stop (some work, by impeding it) (Śiv. 1728); to halt, cause to stop (something in motion, by impeding). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain, or continue, stopped, to stay halted, to be made to stay motionless (K. 75).

f. fraud, swindling (Śiv. 1529); a trap (Gr.M., Śiv. 1310); a kind of fish-net or fish-trap fixed in a running stream. --lāgüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to set a fish- trap; to set a trap with the object of swindling. --wahārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to spread a net, set a trap (Gr.M.). ¶ ṭhāñĕ bĕhun m.inf. to abide in permanence, to be comfortably settled. -gorᵘ m. (f. -gürᵘ̈), a habitual deceiver, swindler. --rōzun -- m.inf. to abide carefree, comfortably, and permanently (cf. rāñĕ ṭhāñĕ rōzun, p. 839b, l. 34).
m. a certain part of a silk-weaver's loom.
m. the head or leader of a group of people, of a number of relatives, or the like, honoured and respected on that count. Cf. thọ̆ngᵘ.

m. (sg. abl. thapi 1, for 2, see thaph), a cover, blind, shutter, stop (over or in an aperture, e.g. to prevent the light passing through, or a sound or liquid from issuing) (cf. ös thᵒ, p. 46b, l. 22; ʦũ̄̈ṭh trövith thᵒ, s.v. ʦũ̄̈ṭh (El. thup, closing); a plug (El. thaup); a cover (in the sense of a preventive), a check (K.Pr. 139, thup). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to cover, or close (the mouth of a vessel, or the like). --thawun -- or --thāwun -- m.inf. to cover a hole, plug (a hole to prevent a liquid issuing), close a tap; to stop (bleeding or the like), to apply a surgical bandage. --wŏthun -- m.inf. a plug, cover, blind, or the like, to come away, the covering of an aperture to be removed, a tap to become open. ¶ thapi dyunᵘ m.inf. to apply as a cover, as a plug, or the like. --lagun -- m.inf. to serve as a shutter, plug, or the like. --thawun -- or --thāwun -- m.inf. to apply a cover, plug, or the like (to prevent liquid flowing).

m. patting (another) with the palm of the hand, a pat, repeated gentle slapping; (of any grass, vegetable, or similar article) as much as can be grasped in the hand, a fistful, bunch, small quantity (cf. gāsa-thᵒ, p. 307a, l. 48; guyan-thᵒ, p. 317b, l. 47; hāka-thᵒ, p. 326b, l. 35; handi-thᵒ, p. 337b, l. 7; muji-thᵒ, p. 558b, l. 6; nĕhölⁱ-thⁱ, p. 626a, l. 15; prāji-thᵒ, p. 757b, l. 48; pōshĕ-thᵒ, p. 779a, l. 20; sinⁱ-thⁱ, p. 957b, l. 28) (Gr.Gr. 164). --thôpᵘ -- m. patting or stroking a person on the shoulders, back, or other parts of the body, as a method of consolation or conciliation. --thôpᵘ dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to console, conciliate, encourage.

f. a potter's trowel, the wooden instrument with which a potter pats unbaked vessels after forming them on the wheel, in order to correct their shape; a similar trowel used for applying plaster, etc., to a wall or the like. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to spread plaster, as ab.

m. a bone (such as the knee-cap, or the globular part of a bone in a joint) to which no flesh is attached. ¶ ṭhōra-pholᵘ m. a globular-shaped bone of this kind. -ras m. a soup made by digesting such fleshless joint-bones. It is used as a regimen in sickness.
m. in atha-thörĕr, p. 63a, l. 25; i.q. thörᵘ̈, q.v.
in phērun thōrun, p. 706a, l. 38, q.v. Cf. also thurᵘ.
m. the fig-tree, Ficus reticulata (El. thaur ? cf. thurᵘ̈ 1).

m. hiding one thing by another, covering, screening (cf. pȧtⁱ-ṭhⁱ, p. 789a, l. 39) (El. ṭhúr, a partition; Śiv. 1063); a lid, cover (cf. gajĕ-ṭhᵒ, p. 281b, l. 14). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become concealed, hidden, to become invisible. ¶ ṭhari rōzun m.inf. to remain under cover, to keep or remain concealed in something. --thawun -- m.inf. to hide (something in something), to conceal, screen something from sight.

f. (in the performance of any work) hurry, flurry, fluster (caused by fear or the like) (cf. atha-thᵒ, p. 63a, l. 19; hŏkha-thᵒ, p. 327a, l. 29; khĕna-thᵒ, p. 402a, l. 8) (Gr.Gr. 122); cf. thār, thārun. --pāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. causing (a work or the like) to be completed in a hurry (by telling perturbing news). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such hurry or fluster to occur in the completion of any work. --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to urge on (someone) to hurry on the completion of a work (raising fear of danger coming).

f. (of something loose, such as carded cotton or snow) so much as can be taken up by the united tops of the fingers of one hand, the fingers' full (cf. yēra-thᵒ, p. 1202b, l. 32); a small amount, a little bit (cf. phamba-thᵒ, p. 698a, l. 43) (K.Pr. 87 thus). ¶ thŏsi āmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --) (of cloth or the like which has decayed) gone into shreds. --onᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --üñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), (of cloth, thread, etc.), shredded (by someone), pulled to shreds. --anun -- m.inf. to shred or pull to pieces (cloth, thread, etc.). --thŏsi gamotᵘ -- or --thŏsi gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --thŏsi gamüʦᵘ̈ -- or --thŏsi gömüʦᵘ̈ --) (of cloth or the like) fallen into little scraps (owing to an accident, being spoilt, or the like). --thŏsi gaʦhun -- m.inf. (of cloth which has been spoilt) to fall into scraps, as ab., at a mere touch. --thŏsi korᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --thŏsi kürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --) (of spoilt cloth, etc.), torn, or broken, or shredded by hand into little scraps; (of carded cotton) picked out into little portions. --thŏsi karun -- m.inf. to tear, or shred, cloth; to spoil wool or carded cloth by taking out pinches. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. (of decayed cloth) to go into shreds.
(? spelling) m. the name of the goat from which the finest shawl-wool is obtained (El.).
m. the name used in schools for the Śāradā letter corresponding to the Nāgarī tha.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. thŏsiladiñ), wearied, fatigued; (some work which is) full of fatigue.

m. a fat clot or lump of snow or the like (cf. phamba-thᵒ, p. 698a, l. 44; shīna-thŏsⁱ, p. 885a, l. 8; ʦitra-thᵒ, s.v. ʦithᵃr 1; and yēra-thᵒ, p. 1202b, l. 34). ¶ thŏsⁱ anȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. a heavy fall of snow (in clots or lumps) to begin to fall, a heavy hailstorm to begin. --pĕnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. a heavy fall of snow (in clots or lumps) to fall, a heavy hailstorm to occur. --pĕwawunᵘ -- adv. at (or in) the time of heavy snow or hailstorm (u.w. vbs. of arriving, etc.), (coming) in a snowstorm. --pĕwañĕn -- adv., id. --pĕwawañĕn -- adv., id.
f. weariness, distress, fatigue (cf. thaph thᵒ, p. 981a, l. 9, and thapi thŏsi, p. 981a, l. 44). --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause fatigue (to someone). --yiñᵘ̈ -- fatigue to come (to someone).

f. (? dat.) anger, sulkiness (at some contretemps); cf. ṭhū̃ṭh. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. inward anger to be felt (e.g. indicated at a meal by refusing to take food), sulkiness to come to a person. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. anger to come to a person (e.g. indicated as ab.).

m. (sg. dat. thŏthas), blue vitriol, sulphate of copper (cf. nīla-thᵒ, p. 634a, l. 26); the prickly refuse after cleaning or carding cotton, wool, etc.; nettle-rash (El. thŏt, cf. thŏthawāy); an interruption, impediment (during a consultation, in reflection, conspiracy, sleep, or the like) (cf. thŏth 2); (in doing independent work) stoppage, restraint, check, restriction; a kind of turban. --āsun -- m.inf. likelihood of check, restraint, to occur. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. (in a consultation, consideration, etc., as ab.) an impediment to occur. --karun -- m. to cause an impediment, as ab.; to stop, blockade (dat.) (K. 729).
f. (sg. dat. thŏti, Gr.Gr. 70), an impediment (Gr.Gr. 70). Cf. thŏth 1.
adj. c.g. (of cloth, clothes, etc.) coarse, rough (owing to little prickles of the original cotton, wool, etc., not having been entirely removed). Cf. thŏth 1.
f. (sg. dat. thö̃tharüñᵘ̈), flurry, nervousness, hurry (from fear or the like).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. thö̃tharôwᵘ), to hurry (a person), to cause flurry (through fear or the like). thö̃tharôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. thö̃tharövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), put in a flurry.
m. flurry, nervousness, hurry (from fear or the like) (cf. atha-thᵒ, p. 63a, l. 30).
f. a condition of hurry or flurry, etc. (due to fear or the like).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. thö̃tharyōv), to be flurried, hurried, nervous (Gr.Gr. 127); cf. thārun. thö̃tharyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. thö̃tharyē-müʦᵘ̈), flurried, hurried.
m. a certain skin disease accompanied by an eruption on the trunk of the body, ? nettle-rash (cf. thŏth 1).
or thö̃thorᵘ adj. (f. thö̃thürᵘ̈), one flurried by nature, nervously hurried (from haste or fear) (cf. atha-thᵒ, p. 63a, l. 27).
or ṭhö̃ṭhur m. a maker of hardware or metal pots and pans, a copper-smith, a brazier (El. ṭhánṭhir). -bāy or ṭhö̃ṭharĕñ f. his wife. ¶ ṭhö̃ṭhar-wān m. a copper- smith's shop or workshop.

m. (pl. ṭhȧṭhⁱ 2, for 1, see s.v.), the pier (made of logs piled horizontally upon each other) of a river bridge (as distinct from the end buttresses) (cf. kạdᵃla-ṭhᵃ, p. 385a, l. 41); cf. ṭhaṭhur. ṭhȧṭhⁱ gaʦhȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. an excess of people, etc., to assemble (for any business), a great crowd to come together.
adj. i.q. ṭôṭhᵘ, q.v. beloved, liked, an object of affection (Rām. 1332; H. vii, 4).
m. depositing (with another person, for safe custody, as a pledge, or as a stake, and so on), pledging, pawn.
m. Grislea tomentosa (El. tháí). Cf. tövī.
f. weakness, laxness of the limbs, debility (caused by hunger). --wasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. languor to descend (on a person), to languish, be weak, infirm (from hunger).
f. the skin of the head, the scalp. --wālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to scalp.
f. a kind of grass mat (a word used in the north-west of the Valley) (cf. mĕndⁱ-thⁱ, p. 613b, l. 41).
(? spelling and gender) a certain plant (Barbarea sp.) eaten in time of famine (L. 71).
m. a kind of clumpy grass (used as a fodder).

m. N. of an ancient festival which still survives in the Marāz Pargana, in the south-east of the Valley, and which is held on the full moon of the month of Ṯs̱ithᵃr (Skt. Caitra = March-April), and is celebrated by lighting bonfires of grass and wood. The tradition is that in former days all the inhabitants of Kashmīr used to leave the country on the full moon of Öshid (Skt. Āśvina = September-October) and stay away for the winter. The festival is held to commemorate their return on the full moon of Ṯs̱ithᵃr, i.e. on the beginning of spring. The bonfires are supposed to destroy the darkness of winter. --zālun -- m.inf. to celebrate this festival by kindling bonfires, and so destroying the winter darkness.

f. dry ground, land fit for cultivation, arable land, esp. land suitable for seed-beds; a wooden receptacle in which the articles necessary for the worship of an idol are kept, a casket (for this purpose), a pyx (L.V. 33). -dāñĕ m. rice plants (paddy) which have been trans- planted, paddy sown in seed-beds and subsequently transplanted. --nār -- m. a nursery for rice (cf. nār 2) (L. 462 thajnár).
adj. c.g. (a horned animal which is) in the habit of attacking with its horns (Gr.Gr. 134).

m. (sg. dat. ṭhukas), hammering into, knocking in, driving into (the ground a stake, peg, etc., with a mallet or the like) (cf. atha-ṭhᵒ, p. 63a, l. 6) (Gr.Gr. 122, W. 140, K.Pr. 41); the Skt. given above as the meaning of this word usually signifies 'digging up', but here it is certainly used to mean the ab. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to hammer in (as ab.). --ʦhunun -- m.inf. 'to thrust in (a wedge)', i.e. (for one's selfish object) to interfere or obstruct some other's work (by offering some pretended reason), to put a spoke in another's wheel.
m. (sg. dat. ṭhū̃kas), the tip of anything pointed (e.g. the nib of a pen) (Gr.M.). I.q. ṭhū̃kᵘ 1, q.v.

f. (sg. dat. ṭhũ̄̈ke), (by a horned animal) striking with the horns, thrusting or piercing with the horns, goring (Gr.Gr. 134). Cf. ṭhŏl. ¶ ṭhũ̄̈ka diñĕ f. pl. inf. to give gorings, attack with the horns; met. arrogantly and threateningly to display wrath. ṭhũ̄̈ka-ṭhũ̄̈kh f. mutual goring (as in a fight between horned animals) (Gr.Gr. 75, ṭhū̃ka-ṭhū̃kh).
adv. persistently, determinedly, resolutely. Cf. ṭhũ̄̈kh.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭhukᵘ f. ṭhucᵘ̈; 2 p.p. ṭhucyōv), to hammer, drive in (e.g. a stake, peg, etc., into the ground, etc.), thrust forcibly into (cf. dŏh ṭhᵒ, p. 199b, l. 50) (Gr.Gr. 122; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 1); cf. ṭhākun and ṭhāsun. Regarding the meaning of the Skt. translation, see ṭhukh. ¶ ṭhukᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ṭhucᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), knocked in, driven into (the ground, etc.), as ab. ¶ ṭhukith conj. part. 'having hammered in'; hence, as adv. under compulsion (of someone), perforce; dŏh ṭhᵒ, having hammered in the day, i.e. having finished the day's work (K.Pr. 131).
m. a fall due to a blow, kick, knock, stumble, or the like (W. 7 ṭhokar). --lagun -- m.inf. to come into collision (with), to knock (against an obstacle); to trip, stumble.

m. rapping the tip of the fingers with a strip of wood (a punishment for boys, etc.), slapping the hands in this way; a mistake in a book, a scribal error in a manuscript or the like, a printer's error, a misprint; cf. ṭhū̃kh. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to detect scribal errors or misprints, to check a manuscript, correct a proof, etc. --trāwun -- m.inf. to scratch out, erase (an error in a manuscript or the like); to trim the point of a pen.
adj. (f. ṭhṻkᵘ̈), one who is attacked by the horns of any animal, gored (Gr.Gr. 20).

m. an egg (whether of bird or insect) (cf. gānda-ṭhᵒ, p. 289a, l. 23; gö̃ṭa-ṭhᵒ, p. 311b, l. 47; kakav-ṭhᵒ, p. 433a, l. 8; pachin-ṭhᵒ, p. 679b, l. 40; pinḍi-ṭhᵒ, p. 739a, l. 29; rĕyĕ-ṭhᵒ, p. 854b, l. 46; ʦari-ṭhᵒ, s.v. ʦürᵘ̈ 4) (El.; Gr.M.; W. 21, 129, 144, ṭhul; L. 460, tul; K.Pr. 93, 108, 111, 117, 120-1, 147, 163); anything shaped like an egg (cf. bangi-ṭhᵒ, p. 113a, l. 14); used --˚, as a term of disparagement (cf. khŏjĕ-ṭhᵒ, p. 395a, l. 18). --trāwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to lay eggs (K.Pr. 120, 163). --vẹ̆zᵃrȧnᵃ -- m. pl. inf. 'to examine eggs', to give out publicly, and cast reproach upon, anothers secret defects. ¶ ṭhūla-bāha m. 'egg-steam', i.e. slight, or insufficient, boiling (applied to water, rice-milk, and so on). -kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a small, light, elegant kind of brazier or kāngrī (see kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈). -kŏkᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. 'an egg-hen', a hen that lays many eggs, a good layer. -kala m. a man with a head shaped like an egg. -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. a certain kind of dish, prepared by poaching the contents of eggs with spices in heated clarified butter (Gr.Gr. 75). -māyĕ m. varnishing or coating (cloth, a wall, etc.) with white of egg. -phāh m. 'egg cherishing', to sit on eggs (whether one's own or another bird's) in order to hatch them. -ʦūr m. an egg-thief; met. a cat. -zambūra m. a certain dish made with unbroken eggs, i.q. zambūra, q.v. -zain f. a kind of basket in which eggs are kept, an egg-basket. ¶ ṭhūlan bĕhun m.inf. 'to sit on eggs'; hence, to sit and do nothing, to have lost one's employment, etc. --bĕhanāwun -- m.inf. to dismiss (a person) from (his) employment. ¶ ṭhūlas hyuhᵘ adj. (f. --hishᵘ̈ --), like an egg, oval (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. large, gross, coarse (as opposed to subtile) (Śiv. 1019, 1525).
adj. c.g. one (man or beast) who does absolutely nothing.
f. (sg. dat. thurüñᵘ̈), the forming or making earthen vessels on the potter's wheel (cf. atha-thᵒ, p. 63a, l. 24). Cf. thurᵘ̈ 3.
m. ability to form (on the potter's wheel) (cf. atha-thᵒ, p. 63a, l. 26). Cf. thurun.
m. in phira-thurĕr, reversal, p. 702a, l. 19. Cf. thurungᵘ.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. thurᵘ), to form (earthenware vessels on the potter's wheel, or metal vessels on a lathe or the like) (cf. bāna thurȧnⁱ, p. 109b, l. 50) (K.Pr. 234, where parmāna thuri is translated 'he will throw about (? cause to revolve) the scales'). thurᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. thurᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), formed on a potter's wheel or lathe. thurith anun m.inf. to search for and bring something non-existent (quasi, forming it out of nothing on a potter's wheel).

m. turning, whirling (in dancing or the like, or similar whirling in the case of inanimate things). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf to whirl, as ab.; (of something, such as an action, quality, disease, and so on, which has gone) to come back, return.

m. a turn, or twist, in dancing (cf. naʦan thᵒ, p. 663b, l. 36) (K.Pr. 44); a sudden turn or twist round (e.g. of an animal, a ball, or the course of a river). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to make a sudden turn or twist (cf. naʦan-thᵒ dᵒ, p. 663b, l. 37); (of something animate or inanimate, action, occupation, etc., which has gone) to come back, return.
see phira-thᵒ, p. 702a, l. 11; and phyurᵘ-thᵘ, p. 722a, l. 34. Cf. thōrun.
f. a kind of climbing plant or grass, with thread-like thorny leaves (? cf. thorᵘ).

f. blame, aspersion, accusation, a charge (regarding something that has been spoilt, lost, or the like). --khārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring such a charge (whether the person is guilty or not). --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a charge to be incurred. ¶ thuri khasun m.inf. to become an object of dislike or blame (on account of naughtiness, impertinence, or the like) (esp. of a child). --khotᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --khüʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), (a child or the like) who has become an object of dislike or blame, an eyesore of a child.

(for 1, see thar) f. a bush, shrub, esp. a creeping shrub, but not necessarily so (cf. bāra-thᵒ, p. 117a, l. 45; dönᵘ̈-thᵘ̈, p. 223b, l. 16; hiyĕ-thᵒ, p. 363a, l. 38; kēla-thᵒ, p. 436a, l. 49; kȧnḍⁱ-thⁱ, p. 455a, l. 33; krǖḍa-thᵒ, p. 468b, l. 44; pōshĕ-thᵒ, p. 797a, l. 23) (El. thur; L. 282, 458; L.V. 96; Śiv. 165, 345, 1061, 1727, 1760, 1848; H. ii, 3; YZ. 32, 66, 543; K.Pr. 47, 215); met. lattice-carving resembling a creeper (cf. linga-thᵒ, p. 526b, l. 28); met. a graceful girl (cf. nāza-thᵒ, p. 675a, l. 41; ranga-thᵒ, p. 837a, l. 29). ¶ thari-kȧnḍⁱ m.pl. thorns on such a shrub or creeper. -pōsh wari gaʦhȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. the flowers on the shrub to become abundant; met. (a person's) offspring to be copious, to have abundant descendants.
in atha-thᵒ, p. 63a, l. 22. Cf. thurun.

m. a quarrel, dispute (affecting the people assembled at a wedding or other festival). --tulun -- m.inf. to raise a quarrel, i.e. out of enmity in order to impede another's festival to seek for an opportunity of setting people at variance. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to spoil a festival by setting the people at variance. --wŏthun -- m.inf. a festival to be impeded by people being set at variance.
f. a female spoil-sport (one of the feminines of ṭhūsurᵘ, q.v.).
m. (f. ṭhūsarĕñ or ṭhūsᵘ̈rᵘ̈, qq.v.), one who, on the occasion of some festival, impedes it by setting the people at variance, a spoil-sport. Cf. ṭhūs.
f. a female spoil-sport (cf. ṭhūsurᵘ, of which it is one of the feminines).
f. in ṭhū̃ṭh lagüñᵘ̈ f.inf. anger against a person doing a kind action (e.g. offering a dish of food or the like) to be felt. Cf. ṭhō̃ṭh.
m. a great supply of food, a well-spread table.
m. neglect, ceasing to take care of, showing no love for, showing aversion to (esp. with reference to a baby or the like).
adj. (thutrövᵘ̈), one who habitually feels aversion or disgust on seeing another's squalor, unsightliness, or the like.
in thuyē thuyē m. spitting (as a token of disgust or blame).
f. height, loftiness, in pata-thüzᵘ̈, p. 793a, l. 50. --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to praise oneself, boast of one's own excellence (cf. pata thüzᵘ̈ thavüñᵘ̈, p. 793a, l. 50).
in thyorᵘdorᵘ adj. (f. thë̆rᵘ̈ dürᵘ̈), very firm, stable, fixed, steady.

m. (sg. dat. ṭhipis), a bird-cage (Gr.Gr. 17); a cage-like apparatus in which live fish are kept (cf. gāḍa-ṭhᵒ, p. 276b, l. 37) (Gr.Gr. 17). --ṭhôrᵘ -- m. a hidden hoard of treasure or the like. ? Cf. ṭhorᵘ.

or ṭhyūrᵘ m. (sg. dat. ṭhiris or ṭhīris), a kind of ulcer on the eyeball (cf. achⁱ-ṭhⁱ, p. 8b, l. 30). ṭhirⁱ-kônⁱ or ṭhīrⁱ-kônⁱ adj. (f. ṭhirⁱ-köñⁱ), one-eyed (caused by the bursting of the eyeball due to this ulcer).
f. surfeit, a feeling of repletion (from eating, drinking, or the like). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a feeling to be experienced.
or thulmulᵘ̈ f. offspring (in the sense of all one's sons, grandsons, and so on), descendants. --navüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. offspring to flourish, to have a large and increasing number of descendants.

m. a secondary suffix indicating the relationship of nephew, as in bābathᵃr a brother's son; bĕnathᵃr a sister's son (Gr.Gr. 133); the corresponding feminine termination is za, as in bāwᵃza a brother's daughter; bẹ̆nᵃza a sister's daughter (Gr.Gr. 133).
f. the fruitless mulberry tree, the leaves of which are considered the best of all varieties of mulberry leaves for silk-worms (El. thuj).
f. N. of the female of the Mallard (Anas boscas) (L. 129, thuj).

adv. and conjnct. also, indeed, even, as in suh ti ʦᵃh ti, he also, thou also (Gr.Gr. 255); tō-ti (Hindī tau bhī), even then, etc., see tōti; kari-ti, he will indeed make (Gr.Gr. 180; Gr.M.; W. 99, 153; L.V. 32, 48, 106; Śiv. 3, 21, 73, 119, 171, 211, 364, 498, 582, 622, 656 (tī m.c.), 704, and elsewhere; Rām. 166, 216, 236, 262, 295, etc.; K. 18, 20, 26, 48, 61, etc.; H. ii, 4; vi, 11; viii, 5, 8, etc.; K.Pr. 146). ¶ ti is also used as a conjnct. connecting plural words (ta 1, q.v., being used to connect singular words), as in mahanivⁱ ti gupan ti āy, both the men and the cattle came (Gr.Gr. 255; W. 153; Śiv. 1776; H. iii, 8). ti na... ti na, neither... nor (W. 153). ti ta conjnct. and also (K. 611). ti ti 1, that also (K. 582), see tih, but ti... ti 2,..., conjnct. both... and (H. x, 13; xii, 12). ¶ Added to an indefinite pronoun, it strongly emphasizes the indefiniteness, as in kã̄h ti, anyone even, anyone at all (p. 390a, l. 12; H. i, 5; vii, 23); kē̃h ti nā, nothing at all (L.V. 9, 11; so Śiv. 1072, 1476; Rām. 710, 1295, 1492; K. 78, 87, 97, etc.); kã̄ʦh ti nō sath, no substance at all (L.V. 41); kö̃h ti na khĕth, no harm at all (L.V. 77); so kã̄h ti (Rām. 164, 1497); kĕ˜h ti (H. viii, 9).
or tī˜brū m. Xanthoxylon hostile (El. tímbar, tímbrú).
m. a kind of tilak or sectarian mark on the forehead of a Hindū.
f. the upper part of a turban (which lies on the crown of the head) (K.Pr. 156).

pron. dem. (in a compound, or in an idiomatic phrase approaching the nature of a compound, this word sometimes takes the form ti; for examples, see bel.) that (not within sight). ¶ [sg. nom., an.m. suh, f. sŏh or sa; inan. tih, also written ti. Acc.-dat., an. c.g. tamis or tas; inan. tath. Ag., an.m. tȧmⁱ, f. tami; inan. tȧmⁱ. Abl., an. and inan. c.g. tami or tawa. Gen., an. m. and f. tȧmⁱ-sondⁱ or tasondᵘ; inan. c.g. tamyukᵘ or tawukᵘ. ¶ In the plural there is no distinction between an. and inan., and gender is distinguished only in the nominative case. Thus, nom., m. tim, f. tima. Acc.-dat. c.g. timan. Ag. and abl. c.g. timau. Gen. timan-hondᵘ or tihondᵘ. For most of the above forms, see Gr.Gr. 88 and Gr.M. See also the references bel. ¶ In the sing. this pronoun is an. or inan., and the an. forms in some cases distinguish between the masc. and fem. genders. As regards the plural, see above. ¶ When this word is used as an adjectival pronoun, the inanimate forms, with one exception, are not employed. The only exceptions are tath, the inan. dat. sing., and (very rarely) tih, the inan. nom. sing. The former is used only as an adjective when agreeing with an inan. noun of either gender in the dative singular. In other cases, when an adjectival use is required, the animate forms are used, according to gender, even when agreeing with an inan. noun, except that the adjectival feminine dative is tami as well as tamis, although, when used substantively, only the an. form tamis is used for the feminine as well as for the masculine. When agreeing with a genitive, the usual rule for adjectives is observed. When the genitive is the genitive of a masculine singular inanimate noun, and therefore ends in ukᵘ, etc., the pronoun is put into the ablative singular, and, when the genitive is not of this description, the pronoun is put into the dative singular. Thus, suh (not tih) jahāza, that ship; sa (not tih) shĕlph, that art; but tath (not tas or tamis) kulis, to that tree (inan. m. sg. dat.); tath kāmĕ, for that work (inan. f. sg. dat.); tami (m. sg. abl.) cīzukᵘ, of that thing; tas (m. sg. dat.) söhiba-sondᵘ, of that gentleman; tami (not tamis) jyāyĕ-hondᵘ, of that place. ¶ It therefore follows that the nominative singular inanimate form tih, it, that, is hardly ever used as an adjective, but is used almost always as a substantive. But suh and sa, the masculine and feminine forms, are also used as substantive inanimate forms, instead of tih, when the pronoun is correlate to a preceding adjective pronoun that (as all these pronouns follow the same rules) is used, though inanimate, in the animate masculine or feminine gender, as explained above for adjectival suh and sa. The preceding pronoun is usually the relative, as in yus asbāb tŏhĕ hyotᵘwa, suh (not tih) chuh drọ̆gᵘ, what property you purchased, that is dear; yĕmi murāda khötᵃra ʦĕ sōzōthas bŏh, suh (not tih) sapodᵘ pūra, the purpose for which you sent me has been fulfilled; ʦĕ yŏssa kitāb mĕ lüzᵘ̈th, sa (not tih) āyĕ mĕ khŏsh, the book which you sent me, was acceptable to me. The preceding pronoun is not necessarily a relative; thus, suh phal chuh ʦọ̆kᵘ, suh (not tih) ma khĕh, that fruit is sour, do not eat it. ¶ When, however, the demonstrative pronoun is correlate to a substantive inanimate pronoun, tih is used, as in yih bŏh wanān chus, tih chwā pozᵘ kina apozᵘ, is what I say true or false? Also, as the pronoun yih, this (not the relative pronoun yih, what), in the direct singular, is the same in form for both genders, whether animate or inanimate, when the substantive demonstrative pronoun is correlate to it, it is, in the direct singular, always tih, not suh or sa. Thus, yih (adj. m. inan.) sôruy kurᵃkoṭᵃ kyāzi chuh yiti pyō-mot? tih nih tulith, why is all this refuse here? take it away. ¶ In the plural nominative the masculine agrees with all masculine nouns, and the feminine agrees with all feminine nouns, without any distinction between animate and inanimate. But, if the adjective pronoun agreeing with a feminine nominative plural is separated from it by some word that does not indicate its gender by its form, then the masculine form of the plural pronoun is used instead of the feminine. Thus, tim (not tima) zᵃh pacĕ (fem. plur. nom.), those two boards, but tima pacĕ, those boards. The other cases of the plural are all of common gender, and make no distinction between animate and inanimate. [For ab. generally, see Gr.M. s.v. tih.] ¶ sa or sŏh f. sg. nom., f. of suh, bel., q.v. (Śiv. 434, 493, 651, 691, 903, 1090, etc., sa; Rām. 113, 115, 116, 137, etc., sa; K. sa, she, 290, 694, 703, 738, 806, 1080; adj. 72; H. sa, v, 5, 9; viii, 11; x, 14, etc.; sŏh, xii, 5; (adj.) sa, x, 1, 6, 12; sŏh, iii, 5; (adj. inan. f.) sa, viii, 7; x, 10; sŏh, xii, 26). ¶ suh dem. that (not within sight), both pronoun and pronominal adj. The corresponding dem. for persons or things within sight is huh, q.v. It is also used as a pronoun of, the third person, meaning 'he', 'she', or 'it', (not within sight); (as pronoun) (Śiv. 1035, 1225, 1229, etc.); (as pron. adj.) (L.V. 104; Śiv. 495, 531, 681, 903, 920, etc.; Rām. 62, 81, 287, 344, 362, 385, 388, etc.; H. ii, 8, 9; viii, 7, 10, 13; x, 12, 14; K.Pr. 205); (as personal pron.) (L.V. 8, 24, 31, 33; Śiv. 536-7, 554, 578, 585, 619-20, etc.; Rām. 18, 26, 29, 72, 78, etc.; K. 6, 26, 40, 43, 261, 335, 370, 521, 571, 576, 672, 678, 686, 691, etc.; H. ii, 8, 11; v, 9, 10, etc.; (inan.) xii, 4, 11, 14, 15). ¶ say or sŏy f. that (fem.) verily, that very, that indeed, she verily (L.V. 52, 81, (sŏy); Śiv. 37, 46, 93, 105, 210, 439, 669, 881, etc., say; Rām. 44, 255, 424, 872, 1514, 1516, say; K. 683, 850, say; 39, sŏy; H. say, iii, 1, 4; xii, 14; say, (adj. inan.) ii, 6; viii, 7, 10, 13; ix, 4; xi, 5; sŏy, vii, 16). ¶ suy m. (f. say or sŏy), that (masc.) verily, that very, that indeed, he verily (L.V. 3, 15, 31, 34, 37; Śiv. 48-50, 56, 91, 247-8, etc.; Rām. 15, 178, 316, 909, 958, etc.; K. 41, 52, 213, 321, 492, 607, 640, 684, etc.; H. i, 4, 8; iii, 3; v, 1; vi, 16, etc.; adj. xii, 19; (inan.) ii, 4; vii, 8, 13; ix, 11). ¶ ti, in ti karith adv. having done that; hence, as adv., even then, still, yet, nevertheless. --warā karith -- adj. having done without that; hence, as adv., otherwise, or else. ¶ tī, see tiy, bel. ¶ tih, sg. nom. inan. it, that, (pron.) (L.V. 24, 37, 70, 107; Śiv. 41, 308, 533, 893, 999, 1007, 1086, 1757, 1852; Rām. 45, 60, 93, 162, 172, etc.; K. 296, 506, 569, 610, 676, 1089; H. iii, 4, 9; viii, 3, 9, 11, etc.); (rarely as a pron. adj.) (Śiv. 1836; Rām. 292, 1133, 1419). ¶ tihondᵘ or (q.v. bel.) timan-hondᵘ pl. gen. (f. tihünzᵘ̈), of them (an. or inan., c.g.) (L.V. 71; Śiv. 499, 1073, 1083, 1209, 1257, 1519, 1665; Rām. 1156, 1379, 1764; K. 62, 290, 310, 312, 453, 1002, etc.; H. viii, 3, 11; xii, 16). ¶ tȧmⁱ instr. sing. an. m. and also inan. c.g. (an. f. tami), by him, by that, (as pronoun) (Śiv. 41, 121, 449, 536, 636, etc.; Rām. 8, 62, 71, 78-9, 102, 106, 110, 113, etc.; K. 233, 254, 383, 438, 492, 550, 635, etc.; H. ii, 1; iv, 3-6; x, 3, 12). tȧmⁱ-sondⁱ or (q.v. bel.)tasondᵘ sg. gen. adj. (f. -sünzᵘ̈. This form may refer to any an. m. or f. noun, but not to an inan. noun, in which case the sg. gen. is tamyukᵘ, q.v. bel.) of him (Śiv. 505, 995, 997, 1000, 1003, 1020, 1666; Rām. 386, 657, 697, 1577, 1644; K. 573; H. i, 3; vii, 6, 13); of her (Śiv. 433; Rām. 355, 775, 1289, 1694; H. xii, 15). ¶ tami 1 f. sg. ag. an. of tih, see ab. (Śiv. 431, 496 (pron. adj.), 635, 654, 837, 870, 1114; Rām. 149, 153, 165, 184-9, 190-7, 233, etc.; K. 428, 537, 583, 601, 709-10, 803, 1146). ¶ tami 2, f. sg. dat. of tih, when used as an adj., see ab. (H. x, 10). ¶ tami 3, or (q.v. bel.) tawa abl. sg. c.g. an. andinan. of tih; (as pron. an.) (Śiv. 31 (f.); Rām. 804 (m.)); (as pron. inan.) (Śiv. 102, 239 (f.), 1191, 1422; Rām. 1581; K. 601, 775); (as pron. adj.) (Śiv. 673, 708, 741, 1315, 1344, 1428; Rām. 233, 822, 829; K. 920; H. ii, 7; iii, 9; v, 5; viii, 9; x, 10, 12, 14; xii, 4, 6); (used adverbially) for that reason, on that account, therefore (Śiv. 1287). Frequently used in phrases, such as the following:-- tami dŏha adv. on that day. --gari -- adv. at that hour, at that time. --khŏta --, --khōta --, or --khŏtan -- adv. (in comparison) than that (not within sight) (as in 'better than that') (Rām. 1581; K. 319, 935). --kani -- or --kanĕn -- adv. for that (not within sight) reason, on account of that, therefore (Gr.Gr. 159). --mŏkha -- adv. on that (not in sight) account, for that reason, therefore. --nishĕ -- adv. (with signification of abl. sg.) from that (not within sight); than that, rather than that; in exchange for that. --phiri -- adv. at that time, on that occasion (past or future, but not present). --pörⁱ -- or (q.v.) tapörⁱ adv. in or from that (not within sight) direction (Gr.Gr. 151, 159). --pata -- or --patan -- adv. after that (not within sight), after then (Gr.Gr. 159; Śiv. 131; K. 873; H. x, 12; xii, 16). --path-kun -- adv. behind that (not within sight). --patukᵘ -- adj. (f. --patücᵘ̈ --), of, or belonging to, what is behind that (not within sight); cf. tamis-patukᵘ, bel. --patyumᵘ -- adj. (f. --patimᵘ̈ --), of, or belonging to, or produced in what is behind that (not within sight); cf. tamis patyumᵘ, bel. --puʦhⁱ -- or --putshy -- adv. with that (not within sight) purpose, for that. --ranga -- adv. in that manner (Gr.Gr. 154); on account of that (not within sight), for that reason, therefore. --wushötⁱ -- adv. for that (not within sight) cause, for that reason, therefore. --vizi -- adv. at that time, then (Gr.Gr. 157). ¶ tim m. pl. nom. (f. tima), they (L.V. 6, 76, 77; Śiv. 72, 78, 81, 129, 132, 433, etc.; Rām. 2, 54-5, 68, 94, 108, etc.; K. 64, 67, 200, 414, 452, 468, etc.; H. v, 438; viii, 3, 4, 11, etc.); (f.) (Śiv. 1453, 1667); (as adj.) those (L.V. 28; Rām. 133, 466, 542, 634, 856, 864, etc.; H. viii, 13; x, 12); f. (Śiv. 38, 1664; K. 766, 768; H. viii, 11; xi, 9; adj. xii, 19). ¶ timau pl. ag. and abl. by them (pron.) (Śiv. 695, 1084; Rām. 7, 81 f., 82, 142, 445, 517, 528, 540, 542, etc.; H. vi, 11; x, 12; xii, 7); from them (pron.); by those (pron. adj.); from those (pron. adj.) (Rām. 1209). -pĕṭha adv. (with signification of abl. pl.) from those; than those. ¶ timan, pl. dat. c.g. to them (pron.) (Śiv. 498, 639, 675-6, 679, 694, 706, 1094, 1184, 1187; Rām. 18, 54, 56, 87, 134, 235, etc.; K. 213, 478, 842, 863, 981, 1002, 1071; H. viii, 1; xi, 8; xii, 1; fem. xii, 6, 17); to those (pron. adj.) (Rām. 138, 586, 710-1, 864, 1463, 1553; H. x, 6; xi, 6); with emphatic y, we have timanạy (Śiv. 20, 34, 1209, 1361; K. 290 (timanᵘ̈y); H. (timanᵘ̈y) viii, 11; xii, 1). -hondᵘ or (q.v. ab.) tihondᵘ pl. gen. adj. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of them, of those (not within sight) (K. 67). ¶ tamis or (q.v. bel.) tas, acc.-dat. sg., c.g., an. of tih, see ab.; (pron. m.) (Śiv. 30 (tamisạy), 432, 641, 645, 670, 708-9, 742, etc.; Rām. 72, 74, 113, 233, 287, 308, 313, 351 (tamisạy), etc.; K. 519 (tȧmⁱsⁱy); H. ii, 7; viii, 9; (tamisᵘ̈y) ii, 1; viii, 9; xii, 1); (pron. f.) (Śiv. 532, 844; Rām. 419, 563, 665-7, 754, 761, 878, etc.); (pron. adj.) (f. -patücᵘ̈), i.q. tami patukᵘ, ab. --patyumᵘ -- adj. (f. -patimᵘ̈), i.q. tami patyumᵘ, ab. --saṭh -- adj. c.g. like that (or it) (not within sight), (indicating non-identity, but similarity, as if to the question 'is it that?' we should reply 'no, but it is like it'). ¶ tamiy 1, emph. form of tami 1, 2, and 3, ab., as in tamiy röʦᵘ̈, on that very night (p. 848b, l. 12) (L.V. 25, Rām. 147; so Rām. 149 (m. adj.), 311 (id.), 377 (f. adj.), 839 (m. pron. abl.), 1145 (f. pron. instr.), 1709 (f. adj.); K. 841 (m. adj.), 1004 (id.); H. If the noun is an. the form is tȧmⁱ-sondⁱ, q.v. ab., or tasondᵘ, q.v. bel.) of that (not within sight) (Śiv. 920-1; Rām. 17, 61, 161, 282, 464, 667, etc.; K. 589; H. vii, 12; K.Pr. 248, tamukuí, for tamyukᵘ with emph. ī). ¶ tas i.q. tamis, ab. (cf. tas pata, p. 792b, l. 28) (pron. m.) (L.V. 20, 34, 37, 105; Śiv. 33, 38, 51, 58-9, 65, 72, 83, etc.; Rām. 57-8, 59, 71, 76, etc.; K. 2, 6, 15, 22, 35, 39, 41, etc.; H. i, 5, 8; ii, 8; iv, 2, etc.); (pron. f.) (Śiv. 35, 435-8, 508, 530, 653-7, etc.; Rām. 84, 120, 336, 350, etc.; K. 535; H. xii, 2, 15, 25); (pron. adj.) (Śiv. 319, 683, 1155, 1232, 1599; Rām. 28, 83 f., 488, 537-8, 576, etc.; K. 8, 10, 50, 88, 102, etc.; H. ii, 7; vii, 4; viii, 7, etc.). The word is occasionally used with the meaning of the genitive, as in K. 147, or of the accusative, as in K. 165, 382, 441, 747, 836. An emphatic form is tȧsⁱ, to him or her only, etc. (L.V. 65; Śiv. 883, 1366, 1578; Rām. 308, 1760; K. 321, 448, 598, 621, etc.). tas-kun adv. i.q. tamis-kun, ab. (Śiv. 596, 1196; Rām 79, 148, 258, 411, etc.). ¶ tasondᵘ or (q.v. ab.) tȧmⁱ-sondⁱ sg. gen. adj. (f. tasünzᵘ̈. This form may refer to any an. m. or f. noun; but not to an inan. noun, in which case the sg. gen. is tamyukᵘ, q.v. ab.); of him (Śiv. 46, 214, 247-8, 597, 639, 744, 798, 919, 1173, 1496, 1619; K. 3, 95, 101, 117, 126, 395, 582, 601, 621, 1111, 1124, etc.); of her (Śiv. 100, 102, 105, 433-4; Rām. 61, 240, 304-5, 474, 705, 894, etc.; K. 114, 520; H. ix, 3). tasȧndⁱ pöṭhⁱ adv. like, in the manner of, that person (not within sight), like him, like her (or other an. noun) (Gr.Gr. 154). tasonduy (f. tasünzᵘ̈y), his or hers only, even his or hers, even of that animate being (Gr.Gr. 92; L.V. 72; Śiv. 49, 599, 651, 724, 1121-2; Rām. 110, 115, 805, 1442, 1448; K. 321, 448, 598, 625, 720, 764, 882, 1082, 1084, 1088, 1146). ¶ ti ti, that also (K. 582). ¶ tath inan. sg. dat. to it, to that (not within sight) (inanimate thing) (cf. tath-pata, p. 792b, l. 26) (as pron.) (Śiv. 353, 367, 474, 476, 509, etc.; Rām. 26, 118, 122-3, 343, 477-8, etc.; K. 162, 261, 377, 673, 686, 1150, 1153, etc.; H. ii, 1; v, 4; vii, 27, 28, etc.); (as pron. adj.) (L.V. 47; Śiv. 63, 85, 319, 357, 412, 494, etc.; Rām. 121, 128, 188, 738, 1294, etc.; K. 16, 24, 60, 62, 85, 94, 126, 139, etc.; H. (inan.) ii, 1; v, 5; viii, 9; x, 12, etc.; (inan. f.) xii, 15). tath-kun adv. towards that (inanimate thing, place, etc., not within sight); in that direction (Gr.Gr. 160, Rām. 536). ¶ tȧthⁱ or tathy, emph. form of tath, ab., as in Rām. 314, etc.; K. 23, 279, 429, 925, etc.; H. iii, 8; xii, 4, 11, 14). tathy-kun adv. even in that direction (not within sight) (Gr.Gr. 160). ¶ tawa i.q. tami 3, ab. q.v. (cf. tawa pata, p. 792b, ll. 27-8), from that, by that (YZ. 186); (used adverbially) for that reason, on that account, therefore (L.V. 57; K. 318, 895). tawa bāpath adv. for the sake of that (inan. c.g., not within sight), for that; on that account (Śiv. 709, taway-b˚). --khŏta --, --khōta --, or --khŏtan -- adv. i.q. tami khŏta, etc., ab. (Rām. 1239). --kani -- or --kanĕn -- adv. i.q. tami kani, ab. (Gr.Gr. 159; K. 231). --kinⁱ -- adv. on that account, for that cause. --kārana -- adv. for that reason, for that cause. --mŏkha -- adv. i.q. tami mŏkha, ab. --nishĕ -- adv. i.q. tami nishĕ, ab., q.v. (Rām. 352, rather than that; 1234). --pata -- or patan -- adv. i.q. tami pata, ab., q.v. (Gr.Gr. 159, 200; Śiv. 1792; Rām. 1644; K. 135-6, 190, 256, 297, 458, 628, 759, 870, etc.). --path-kun -- adv. i.q. tami path-kun, ab., q.v. --patukᵘ -- adj. (--patücᵘ̈ --), i.q. tami patukᵘ, ab., q.v. --patyumᵘ -- adj. (--patimᵘ̈ --), i.q. tami patyumᵘ, ab., q.v. --puʦhⁱ -- or --puʦhy-- adv. i.q. tami puʦhⁱ, ab., q.v. -ti or (q.v.) tōti conj. nevertheless (Gr.M.). --wushötⁱ -- adv. i.q. tami wushötⁱ, ab., q.v. ¶ tawukᵘ gen. adv. (tawücᵘ̈), i.q. tamyukᵘ, ab., q.v. ¶ taway adv. emph. form of tawa, ab. only from that, even from that, verily from that, only for that reason, therefore (El. tawai; L.V. 69, 90, 94; Śiv. 192, 372, 422, 430, 506, 512, 709, 754, 762, 839, 864, 1122, 1133; Rām. 228, 400, 475, 487, etc.; K. 358; YZ. 251); by that means (L.V. 75, K. 676). ¶ tiy (often written tī) inan. m. sg. nom. emph. form of tih, ab. that verily, only that, even that (L.V. 20, 21; Śiv. 121, 312, 317, 319, 348, 538, etc.; Rām. 14, 50, 133, 162, 335, 592, etc.; K. 323, 422, 574, 576, 606, 621, 796, etc.; H. tiy, vii, 1; iii, 9; tī, xi, 1); (for tih + ay) if that (H. iii, 4, 9). ¶ tiyĕ  inan. m. sg. m. inter. is it really that (the answer expected being in the negative)? tiyĕ bā ? inan. m. sg. inter. pol. id., but a respectful query, addressed to a male. tiyĕ biñ ? inan. m. sg. inter. pol. id., but a respectful query addressed to a female. tiyĕ sö ? inan. m. sg. inter. pol. id., addressed to a much-respected male. ¶ tiyō, i.q. tiy, ab., with respectful suffix ō, that verily Sir (Śiv. 226).
or tihijᵘ̈ f. a slender sprout, a fine plant filament (cf. kŏng-tᵒ, the tip of the stigma of the saffron-flower, p. 456b, l. 21); met. anything fine and delicate (cf. kana-tᵒ, p. 448a, l. 35).

or tyuhorᵘ (sg. dat. tĕharis), top, summit, peak, apex (e.g. of mountain, tree) (cf. kulⁱ-tⁱ, p. 439a, l. 6) (Śiv. 747 tyu˚). ¶ tĕharĕn khasun m.inf. to mount to peaks; met. to show arrogance, insolence, audacity. --khārun -- m.inf. to cause (someone) to rise to peaks; met. highly to praise, to eulogize, extol, glorify. ¶ tĕharyau-pĕṭhⁱ wŏṭatrāwañĕ f. pl. inf. to take jumps over peaks; met. to show daring, courage, spirit, valour, intrepidity.
f. trade, commerce (cf. bē-tᵒ, p. 144a, l. 39) (K.Pr. 216).
f. a commentary, annotation, gloss; a translation (El. ṭíka). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to commentate, annotate; to translate (El.).

(for 2, see under ṭᵃkh) m. a certain ornament worn on the forehead (commonly of gold and studded with jewels) (cf. ḍĕka-ṭᵒ, p. 204b, ll. 19, 28) (Śiv. 467, K. 734); a caste-mark on the forehead of a Hindū (L. 264, 461); a mark of distinction; met. that which, or he who, is the essential, the chief, or the most honoured, among its or his fellows or associates (cf. ḍĕkukᵘ ṭᵒ, p. 205a, l. 8). Cf. ṭyokᵘ.
adj. c.g. a mean fellow (who in distributing food at a dinner party helps each guest to small scraps of meat). Cf. tikh.

f. (sg. dat. ṭikaṭi), a ticket (railway, etc.), a postage-stamp; a visiting-card. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a ticket to be applied, a mark (indicating quality, goodness, defect, reputation, etc.) to be put (on something).

m. (sg. dat. tikas), a small piece of flesh (cf. māz-tᵒ, p. 615a, l. 2; shīshĕ-tᵒ, p. 897b, l. 33; ʦhŏka-tᵒ, s.v. ʦhŏkh) (K.Pr. 128, nāra-tᵒ, a bit of fire). ¶ tika tika adv. in small pieces, in little bits (used with vbs. of dividing or the like). --tika khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to eat up in little bits; met. (of a strong person) to beat (a weak person) mercilessly. -tār m. (also ṭᵃka-tār or ṭika-tār, p. 991b, l. 31) the N. of a certain game, in which potsherds (or the like) are thrown along the surface of the water of a river in an endeavour to make them reach the other side, a kind of 'Ducks and Drakes'.

m. oil (expressed from sesame, mustard-seed, walnut kernels, etc.) (cf. ala-tᵒ, p. 22b, l. 35; ȧlⁱshi-tⁱ, p. 25b, l. 13; ā̃cĕ-tᵒ, p. 53b, l. 16; bȧṭhⁱ-tⁱ, p. 140b, l. 37; ḍūnⁱ-tⁱ, p. 224a, l. 21; gōjĕ-tᵒ, p. 281b, l. 6; khām tᵒ, p. 400a, l. 29; kāji-tᵒ, p. 430a, l. 28; kwöjⁱ-tⁱ, p. 495b, l. 37; manạñĕ-tᵒ, p. 580b, ll. 26, 29; sȧndija-tᵒ, p. 919a, l. 31; tēl-tᵒ, l. 10 ab.) (El. tíl, til, cf. tēl; Gr.M.; L. 330, til, sesame, see tēl; Rām. 717; K. 973; K.Pr. 11, 50, 55, 66, 109, 159, 189, 190, 204, 213, 262). --anun -- m.inf. 'to bring oil' (quasi, to squeeze oil out of a person); hence, to exhaust a person by causing him to search for something hidden or destroyed (when he has no idea as to its whereabouts); cf. --yunᵘ, bel --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give oil; hence, (in the obsequial rites for a deceased father or other relation) suspending a lamp for the benefit of his spirit; cf. tīla-aiṭham and tīla-shrād, bel. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be exhausted in searching for something hidden or destroyed (when one has no idea of its whereabouts). Cf. --anun, ab.; the eyes to be dazzled or dazed (by sudden bright light), or to be made to swim (by prolonged reading small writing, etc.). ¶ tīla-aiṭham f. (sg. dat. -aiṭhümᵘ̈), the eighth lunar day of the bright half of the month of Phāgun (Skt.
