Phālguna = February-March), on which obsequial lamps are hung up for the benefit of deceased relatives; cf. tīl dyunᵘ, ab. and tīla-shrād, bel. -basta f. a kind of large leather bag for holding oil. -chakh f. (sg. dat. -chaki), sprinkling with oil, pouring oil in a stream of fine drops. -chikh f. (sg. dat. -chiki), sprinkling oil, splashing a very little oil (esp. to some distance). -char f. an explosion of drops of boiling oil (caused by drops of water coming into contact with it); a certain disease, accompanied by long dark marks on the back of the hands. -dāg m. an oil-mark, a stain caused by oil. -dāra  f. a fine stream of oil; met. a very small quantity of oil. -gŏgul m. (sg. dat. -gŏgalas), a certain oil-seed, rape (Brassica campestris) (L. 330, 440, tilgoglu). -gurun m. a kind of small fish, which itself exudes oil when being fried. -khȧjⁱ or -khüjᵘ̈ or -khal f. oilcake. -kanᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a certain part (an upright pin on the left side) of a spinning-wheel, on which the little wheel rests. -kọ̆pᵘ m. a kind of leather bag for holding oil. -kronḍᵘ m. a kind of ladle for taking out oil from a vessel. -krāy f. a cauldron (usually of iron) filled with hot oil. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), acridity of oil (caused by contact with something tainted). -köʦᵘ̈ f., i.q. -kanᵘ̈rᵘ̈, ab. -kyomᵘ m. a certain insect (? a glow-worm). -nörᵘ̈ f. a vessel for measuring oil. -noṭᵘ m. an oil-jar; a jar full of oil. -phal m.pl. oil-seeds. -phyorᵘ m. a drop of oil. -phyūrᵘ m., id. -pöjⁱ or -pöjᵘ̈ f. a certain measure (six seers, or twelve pounds) of oil. -palim or -palimᵘ̈ f. oil sediment. -pyotᵘ m. the gall-bladder; bile (El. tilapyut). -rājy m. a certain kind of mendicant (of the Aghōra sect) who begs oil from householders on Saturdays, his clothes being at the time soaked in oil. -shrād m. the obsequial ceremony on which lamps are suspended for the benefit of a deceased relative. See tīl dyunᵘ and tīla-aiṭham, ab. -thŏkh f. (sg. dat. -thŏki), a very small amount of frothy oil (like a spurt of saliva). -tahörᵘ̈ yellow boiled rice mixed with oil, offered to spirits on Tuesdays and Saturdays. -ṭĕkh f. (sg. dat. -ṭĕki), a mere drop or trace of oil, a very small amount of oil. -ṭö̃ṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ṭã̄chĕ), a thin stream of oil. -ʦŏcĕ f.pl. (of ʦŏ̈ṭᵘ̈), cakes cooked in oil offered at the tīla-shrād (q.v. ab.). -ʦoḍᵘ m. a wide-mouthed vessel for holding oil (used in oil-shops for containing the oil sold in retail). -wã̄-dã̄d m. an oil-press bullock. -wã̄-kanz m. an oil-press. -wôñᵘ or tilawôñᵘ m. an oilman, an oil-seller (El. telawoin, tilawóin) (H. xi, 20, tila˚; K.Pr. tīla˚, 229, 244). -wāñĕñ f. an oilman's wife; a certain Himalayan mountain plant (believed to shine at night and to turn copper into gold). -wörᵘ̈ f. a small vessel for serving oil. -wã̄- ʦakh m. (sg. dat. -wã̄-ʦakas), the revolving bar of an oil-mill attached to the bullock's neck. ¶ tīlukᵘ gen. adj. (f. tīlücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or produced in oil.
in tīl-pathᵃr (? spelling) m. the maple (Acer) (El. tílpatar). Cf. kīl-pathᵃr.
in tila-bilav m. apparent stability accompanied by real instability, outward strength and hollowness within.
m. (sg. gen. tilāwukᵘ), gold. ¶ tilāwukᵘ gen. adj. (f. tilāvücᵘ̈), made of gold (Rām. 370).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. tīlanyōv), (of walnut-kernels or the like) to become oily, to become putrid (exuding oil, and of acrid taste). tīlanyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tīlanyē-müʦᵘ̈), become putrid, as ab.

f. (sg. dat. tilmi), a narrow strip (of cloth, a wooden board, or the like) (cf. burza-tᵒ, p. 131a, l. 5; kapar-tᵒ, p. 463b, l. 38; pacĕ-tᵒ, p. 791a, l. 45; ʦŏcĕ-tᵒ, s.v. ʦŏ̈ṭᵘ̈) (El. tilyim; Gr.Gr. 163, compounds with this word are smaller than those formed with chal, q.v., p. 160b, l. 49); cf. tilyunᵘ. tilmi tilmi karun m.inf. to divide into small pieces or strips (of land, cloth, a wooden board, or the like).
m. a fragment (El. tilyun). Cf. tilim.
in ṭīm-ṭām m. dress, show, ostentation (El.).

m. tin. ¶ ṭīna-chal f. a piece of tin. -gorᵘ m. a tinman. -khünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -khanjĕ), a piece of tin. -püṭᵘ̈ f. a sheet of tin. ¶ ṭīnukᵘ gen. adj. (f. ṭīnücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, tin; made of tin.
or ṭiñᵘ̈ f. a certain horse's pace, described as a kind of gallop (cf. gurⁱ-ṭiñ, a strong taste for equitation, p. 299a, l. 12). ṭiñĕ-gurᵘ m. a horse that practises this gait.

m. the crown of the head, the top of the skull; a well-bucket (cf. gagar-ṭᵒ, p. 280a, l. 14). -wôrᵘ m. a well-bucket. --zᵃlun -- m. 'to scratch the top of the head', to shave the head (a contemptuous term).
m. making a horse proceed in the pace called ṭiñ, q.v., riding at this pace.
f. unsteadiness, unsettledness (of the body, due to the mind being perplexed).
f.pl. tiny bits, scraps (e.g. of thread, paper, or the like); motes, particles.
m. (cf. Hindī tīn-tērah) three and thirteen (regarded as unlucky numbers); hence, scattered, dispersed, broken; distracted; ruined, destroyed; squandered, dissipated, wasted.
adj.(f. ṭīnüvᵘ̈), made of tin, tin.

m. (sg. dat. ṭīpas), detraction (of the merits of others), carping criticism, disparagement. --kaḍȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to disparage (making out even another's virtues to be faults). --ṭāph -- m. (sg. dat. ṭīpas ṭāpas), frequent disparagement (of someone making out even his virtues to be faults) (a jingle of ṭīph, not a compound with ṭāph, q.v.).

m. animals of the sheep or goat kind (as a flock, class, or kind) (El. ter, sheep; K.Pr. 224, 232); a flock of sheep (L. 463, tir); cf. tyūrᵘ. -ḍangij f. the closet over the sheep-pen of a house; (in Kashmīr, in winter the sheep and goats are crowded into the ground floor of a house. The small room or locker immediately over this sheep-pen is called the tīr-ḍangij, and, for the sake of its warmth, children sit, and guests sleep in it (cf. L. 249, 363)). --gạnzᵃrȧnᵃ -- m.pl.inf. to count sheep or goats for purposes of taxation (L. 363, it is collected as the sheep go up in flocks to the mountain pastures when winter is over); met. to be utterly bewildered (quasi trying to count the sheep in a moving flock). -khĕjⁱ or -khë̆jᵘ̈ f. a flock of sheep or goats collected in one spot. -khyolᵘ m. a large flock of sheep or goats; cf. tīrⁱ-khyolⁱ, s.v. tyūrᵘ. -rôchᵘ m. a shepherd or goat-herd (i.q. cōpān, q.v.) (for these people, see L. pp. 361 ff.); cf. tīrⁱ-rôchⁱ, as ab. -röchⁱ-bāy f. his wife. -wôrᵘ m. a sheep- or goat-fold. ¶ tīra-ḍang m. a hobble for sheep or goats; foot-shackles (for a man).

m. an arrow (Gr.M.; Rām. 233, 340, 348, 371, 448-9, 781, 783, 891, 898-9, 919, 1299, 1363, 1376, 1398, 1411, 1564, 1612; YZ. 6, 70, 208). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to discharge an arrow (at, dat.) (Rām. 43, 160, 232, 310, 315, 357, 502, 869, 890, 897, 1214, 1352, 1361, 1375-6, 1378, 1406, 1408, 1410, 1612). --lāyun -- m.inf. to discharge an arrow (at, dat.) (Rām. 376, 982, 1399); to hit, or strike with an arrow (obj. dat.) (Rām. 248, 1353, 1368, 1418). --rāwȧnⁱ -- m.pl.inf. arrows to be lost; agitation or bewilderment to occur (causing one to forget or neglect one's other occupations, etc.). --sẹ̆zᵃrun -- m.inf. to aim an arrow straight (at, pĕṭh) (Rām. 999). --trāwun -- m.inf. to discharge an arrow (Rām. 123, 867); to draw a bow (Rām. 117). --trāwan-wôlᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --trāwan-wājĕñ --), an archer (El.). ¶ tīra-dag f. the blow of an arrow, the flight of an arrow straight at the mark. -dag-hyuhᵘ adj. (f. -dag-hishᵘ̈), like an arrow's path, straight as an arrow. --mārun -- m.inf. to strike with an arrow (Rām. 1042). --mōrüñᵘ̈ -- f. (of clothes, ornaments, or met. of strength) slight wearing out to occur, slight signs of wear to become visible (Rām. 490). -nôrᵘ m. a quiver. ¶ tīr-i höricᵘ̈ (Rām. 109) or --hörinjᵘ̈ -- (Rām. 344) (= تیر ہارج) m. an arrow with a crescent-shaped head. tīr-i jādō تیرِ جادو m. a magic arrow (Rām. 873).
m. the bank of a river (Rām. 1754).

or tīrᵘ̈ 1 f. (sg. dat. tīrĕ), a bird's feather, plume (cf. braga-tᵒ, p. 120a, l. 31; gŏndⁱ-tⁱ, p. 290a, l. 15; kŏkar-tᵒ, p. 432a, l. 44; mōr-tᵒ, p. 587b, l. 47; pachin-tᵒ, p. 679b, l. 41) (El. tihir; Gr.M. tīrᵘ̈; L. 460, tir; Śiv. 1012). ¶ tīrĕ lāgañĕ f.pl.inf. to apply feathers; to proffer instruction to one's teacher, 'to teach one's grandmother to such eggs,' to give silly advice to one's teacher (and so put him to shame) (cf. kŏkar-tᵒ lᵒ, p. 432a, l. 45). --yiñĕ -- f.pl.inf. 'feathers to come', to be reduced to poverty (by the loss of one's means of subsistence) (cf. kŏkar-tᵒ-yᵒ, p. 432a, l. 49). ¶ tīri-gọ̆ndᵘ m. a plume of heron's feathers bound up with pearls, precious stones, and gold and silver wire, worn on a turban on state occasions (i.q. gŏndⁱ-tīrⁱ, p. 290a, l. 15). -gŏndurᵘ m. a bunch of feathers tied together by their stems.
m. an archer, a bowman (H. ii, 7; YZ. 50).
in bangi-ṭᵒ, the female bhang blossom, p. 113a, l. 17. Cf. ṭīrᵘ̈.
m. a sacred bathing-place, a place of pilgrimage (L.V. 36, 46; K.Pr. 201, tirt; Śiv. 524, 1080, 1089, 1159, 1166, etc.); the actual place on a river bank where such bathing takes place (K. 971).

f. (pl. nom. ṭīrĕ, Gr.Gr. 62) a lump or 'shape' of any soft cooked food, or of liquid boiled down to a solid but soft condition (cf. bata-ṭᵒ, p. 137b, l. 9; ʦāmañĕ-ṭᵒ, s.v. ʦāman; wŏgra-ṭᵒ; wāṭa-ṭᵒ, s.v. wāṭh 2), cold pudding (Gr.Gr. 62, Śiv. 1020, K.Pr. 249). ṭīri-bata m. a lump or shape of boiled rice (i.q. bata-ṭīrᵘ̈, as ab.).
(f. of tyūrᵘ, q.v.) a ewe (Gr.M., s.v. tyūrᵘ).

or ṭīs onomat. m. the sound caused by cracking the joints of the fingers, backbone, etc. (an accompaniment of massage); the crack of the breaking of a dried branch of a tree, or similar sound. ṭis (or ṭīs) kaḍun  m.inf. to make the joints of the fingers or of the backbone give out a cracking sound (in massage); to cause the sound of the crack of a dried branch of a tree. ṭis-ṭis m. the crackling sound of burning wood, straw, or the like. ¶ ṭisa-bọ̆kᵘ or -bokᵘ m. 'a handful of cracks', a number of simultaneous cracks of the joints of the fingers, backbone, etc. (in massage). -paparāray f. 'a pattering of cracks', i.q. the preceding. -paparāy f., id.
f. a multitude of crackling sounds, such as those emitted by burning dry firewood, or the like (cf. ṭis).
f. the Himalayan honeysuckle (Lonicera quinquelocularis) (El.). Cf. pākhorᵘ.
m. a certain measure in music (consisting of three beats and a rest).
or tītar m. the francoline partridge (Perdix francolinus).
in tī̃tar-gūjⁱ f. a certain section of the female private parts (obsc.).
in ṭī˜ṭar-kônᵘ or ṭī˜ṭᵃram-kônᵃ adj. (f. -köñᵘ̈), blind of one eye, owing to inability to move the eyelids. Cf. ṭī˜ṭh.
f. (sg. dat. ṭī˜ṭi), the moving of the eyelids up or down, a wink, blink (cf. ȧchⁱ-ṭⁱ, p. 8b, l. 44). Cf. ṭī˜ṭar.

adv. in that manner, so (Gr.Gr. 153, Gr.M., Rām. 1500, K. 432); yitha titha, in any way, in some way or other, somehow (Śiv. 75; K. 138, 1098, 1114, 1119, 1126); cf. tyuthᵘ. titha pöṭhⁱ or --pöṭhin -- adv. in that manner, in that way (Gr.Gr. 153, Śiv. 52). ¶ tithay adv. in that very manner, exactly so (El. tithai, tithúí; Gr.Gr. 92; Gr.M.; L.V. 100; Śiv. 432; Rām. 59, 74, 111, 113, 156, 167, 236, 372, 404, 482, etc.; K. 58, 77, 582, 847, 863, 902, 1173-4); from that very moment (u.w. vbs. of going and the like) (Śiv. 691, 696, 780, 782, 784, 790, 879, 1300, 1336; Rām. 208); at that very moment (K. 339, 645). --pöṭhⁱ -- adv. in that very manner, in such a way that (Gr.M.; Śiv. 240, 439, 713-4; H. xii, 22).
f. (sg. dat. ṭī˜chĕ), pride (Gr.Gr. 62), i.q. ṭē̃ṭh, q.v.
inṭīṭhⁱ khasüñᵘ̈ f.inf. i.q. ṭē̃ṭh khasüñᵘ̈, s.v. ṭē̃ṭh, q.v.
in titī tī the call of a hen to her chicks (W. 129, K.Pr. 118).
m. (sg. dat. ṭiṭaras), N. of a certain bird, (?) the sandpiper, peewit, lapwing (Tringa vanellus).
adj. (f. tītimᵘ̈), (of things not within sight) consisting of so many of the same number as that (out of sight) (Gr.Gr. 150).

adj. (f. tītiñᵘ̈), weighing so much, measuring so much, so much, so long; costing so much, worth so much (Gr.Gr. 148); aged so much, of the same age as (that, etc.). In all these meanings the thing with which comparison is made must be out of sight.

in ṭī˜ṭᵃram-kônᵃ adj. (f. -köñᵘ̈), i.q. ṭī˜ṭar-kônᵘ, s.v. ṭī˜ṭar, q.v. -nay f. N. of an enclosed forest in the western mountains of Kashmīr, into which the ancient kings used to sentence criminals to life-long banishment.
f. zeal, determination (in endeavouring to accomplish some work, even if it is impossible).
adj. c.g. intense, severe, acute, violent, extreme (Śiv. 1208, 1744, 1797, all of asceticism).
subst. and adj. c.g. a group of three, a triad.
adj. c.g. radiant, glorious (Śiv. 806, 808, 919, 1155); (of a beautiful face, etc.) radiant (Śiv. 794, 944).

sharpness, keenness; energy, fervour, ardour; boldness, courage, confidence; anger, fury; speed (Rām. 745). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to aggravate (anger, etc.), exaspirate, exacerbate, add fuel to the fire. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of sickness or the like) to become increased, exacerbated; (of authority, any special quality, etc.) to become enhanced; to display vigour, show great energy (Rām. 915).
f. a certain kind of mare, noted for its swiftness.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. tīzᵃrôwᵃ), to sharpen, whet (Gr.Gr. 173); (by training, etc.) to make a person expert; to increase, aggravate (fire, disease, etc.); to incite, exasperate (someone already angry), to add fuel to the flames; i.q. tīzᵃrun, q.v. tīzᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (tīzᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ),sharpened, whetted; made expert; aggravated; exasperated.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. tīzᵒrᵒ or tyūzᵒrᵒ), to sharpen, whet (Gr.Gr. 173); (by training, etc.) to make a person expert; to increase, aggravate (fire, disease, etc.); to incite, exasperate (someone already angry), to add fuel to the flames; i.q. tīzᵃrāwun. tīzᵒrᵒ-motᵒ or tyūzᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. tīzᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), sharpened, whetted; made expert; aggravated; incited, exasperated.
m. so muchness, the measure, quantity, or amount (of anything). Cf. tyūtᵘ.
i.q. ta, in tōti, s.v. ti 2, q.v.
m. interpretation, explanation (particularly of dreams) (cf. khābukᵘ töbīr, p. 390b, l. 44) (H. vi, 11-16).
m. (sg. dat. ṭŏbaras), a kind of large drinking-vessel.
or töbi (= تابع) adj. c.g. dependent (on, dat.) subject (to), subdued (Gr.M.); f. (with suff. of indef. art.) töbⁱyāh (H. xii, 18). --rōzun -- m.inf. to be submissive (to, dat.) (Gr.M.).

f. (sg. dat. ṭã̄chĕ), guilt (of some crime, or the like); cf. ṭũ̄̈. --khārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring a charge of guilt cf. ṭũ̄̈ khārun, p. 962a, l. 2; (in a discussion) to argue out the fallacies in a statement.
(sg. dat. ṭācĕ), a kind of cap, round in shape and embroidered (cf. ʦạndra-ṭᵒ, s.v. ʦạndᵃr).

f. a kind of small pear, similar to ṭö̃jᵘ̈, q.v. (cf. khar-ṭᵒ, p. 407a, l. 34; phaka-ṭᵒ, p. 689a, l. 20) (W. 17 ṭạnch); cf. ṭang. ¶ ṭã̄cĕ-kujⁱ or -kujᵘ̈ f. a small or dwarf tree of this pear. -kulᵘ m. a large-sized tree of the same.
m. care, trouble, distress (caused by loss or damage). --wātanāwun -- m.inf. to bring trouble, to cause distress to a person (by doing injury), to cause loss or damage (to a person).

or ṭō̃g m. a bruise, tumour, or swelling on the forehead, etc., caused by a blow (cf. nīla-tᵒ, p. 634a, l. 21); an elephant-goad, the iron hook with which elephants are driven. --khārȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to cause bruises by a blow or blows. --khasȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. such bruises to occur. ¶ tō̃ga-(ṭō̃ga-)wôlᵘ  n.ag. (f. tō̃ga-(ṭō̃ga-)wājĕñ ), an elephant driver.
f.pl. secret agreement, private consultation, conspiracy.

tōh or tuh m. the husk, or chaff of grain, chaff, bran (El. tŏh, tuh; L. 461, toh; K.Pr. 7, 128, 238, tŏh; 224, tuh; 87, thoh). --karun -- m.inf. to reduce to chaff; to reduce to powder or tiny scraps (e.g. cloth destroyed by white ants); to abuse violently or grossly. --karith thawun -- m.inf. to reduce to powder or tiny scraps (as in the preceding); to abuse violently or grossly. --karith trāwun -- m.inf. to overwhelm with gross abuse. -nār m. a fire of burning chaff (which is very fierce). --nār muh nār -- m. profusion of ornaments (worn on the person). -pholᵘ m. a collection (esp. when small) of chaff. -shīn  m. a fall of light fine snow (like chaff). ¶ tuhukᵘ adj. (f. tuhücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, chaff; filled, or stuffed, with chaff, made up of chaff, and so on.
in ṭŏha-ṭŏha m. the noise made in coughing, the sound of a cough.

تہمت f. suspicion; allegation, accusation, aspersion, calumny, slander (esp. when false). --khārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bring an accusation (against someone). --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an accusation to be brought. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an accusation to be brought (against someone). --lāgüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to accuse falsely, to belie, calumniate, slander, asperse, traduce. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (during an investigation into a crime) a suspicion (that so-and-so has committed it) to arise, a charge (of a crime) to be made (against a person).
or tôshᵘ, the form taken by tāh, q.v., when used adjectivally --˚. In such a case, its fem. is töshᵘ̈. Cf. okᵘ-tôhᵘ, p. 19a, l. 43, and okᵘ-tôshᵘ, id. l. 47.
f.pl. the inner part of the eye, the eyeballs (cf. ʦūra-ṭᵒ, s.v. ʦūr). Cf. ṭŏlⁱ, of which this is the fem. form.
adj. c.g. one who has prominent eyeballs.
f. haste, quickness, speed (El. tajíl; K.Pr. 103, tájíl).

f. a kind of small pear (usually acid in flavour, and with a thick skin. According to El., s.v. ṭánj, the country people cook it in warm water) (cf. gura-ṭᵒ, p. 298b, l. 27; mŏdᵘ̈rᵘ̈ ṭᵒ, p. 550b, l. 14; phaka-ṭᵒ, p. 689a, l. 21; sīhra ṭᵒ, p. 890b, l. 48; ʦŏ̈kᵘ̈-ṭᵘ̈, s.v. ʦọ̆kᵘ) (W. 110, tānj). Cf. ṭö̃cᵘ̈ and ṭang.
(for 2, see ṭŏkh) adj. c.g. (of some metal article or the like) very strong, very tough (made so by hammering, annealing, forging, or the like); cf. ṭŏkh. -rudr m. a kind of coral (Śiv. 1310).
f. a kind of water-lizard. (According to dictionaries the Skt. word nihākā means 'alligator', but that is certainly not the meaning here).
f. a mallet, pestle, or similar instrument for pounding; a club used in playing hockey on horseback, a polo-club (El. ṭúkin).
adj. c.g. crook-backed, having the back bent by rheumatism, etc.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭŏkowᵘ), to hammer (some metal article) into shape on an anvil or the like (Gr.Gr. 122, where the meaning given is a misprint); cf. ṭŏka 1 and ṭŏkh. ṭŏkowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ṭŏküvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), hammered into shape on an anvil or the like.

m. (sg. dat. ṭŏkas), hammering, pounding (with a hammer, mallet, pestle, or the like) (cf. atha-ṭᵒ, p. 63a, l. 36; chāna-ṭᵒ, p. 162a, l. 27; drāʦi-ṭᵒ dyunᵘ, p. 250a, l. 35) (Gr.Gr. 122, where the meaning given is a misprint; K.Pr. 135, 231 ṭuk). ¶ ṭŏka 2 (for 1, see s.v.) in ṭŏka-sūr m. ashes of crushing, powder; crushing to powder (H. vii, 13). -sūr gaʦhun m.inf. (of something hard) to become, or be reduced to, powder, to become pulverized. -sūr karun m.inf. (of the same) to reduce to powder, to pulverize.
or ṭö̃khā in shē̃kh-ṭö̃kh or shē̃khā-ṭö̃khā, p. 877a, l. 41, q.v. (a jingle).
f. (sg. dat. ṭö̃ki), a stitch, in ṭēb- ṭö̃kh, p. 962a, l. 33, q.v.
adj. (f. ṭö̃kiñᵘ̈), worth, or costing, two pice. Cf. ṭū̃kᵘ.
adj. (f. ṭücᵘ̈), bold, courageous, confident; (in any work) habitually keen, vehement, energetic (cf. ṭakh-ṭokᵘ, p. 992a, l. 6) (Gr.Gr. 139).

m. an earthen shallow dish for eating from, a platter, plate, dining-plate, tray (cf. ômᵘ ṭᵒ, p. 27a, l. 29; khira ṭᵒ, p. 409a, l. 44; sāla-ṭᵒ, p. 909a, l. 1) (L.V. 106; H. viii, 4, 12; K.Pr. 2, 24, 253). --trāwun -- m.inf. to beg shamelessly (i.e. even without necessity, at improper times or on improper occasions, from sheer greediness, and so on). ¶ ṭökⁱ-bata m. food (at dinner party, wedding feast, or the like) served to each guest in separate platters. ṭökⁱ-dạndⁱrⁱ f. the rim of a platter. -har f. (sg. dat. -hürᵘ̈), 'a platter fight,' a fight among the seated guests at a dinner-party, in which they hurl their platters at each other. -katarĕ f.pl. broken bits or sherds of platters. -tünzᵘ̈ f. a pile of platters (one over the other). -ʦhürᵘ̈ f. a basket for carrying platters. -ʦürᵘ̈ f. a pile of platters (one over the other).
a jingle in mŏl-tŏl, p. 566a, l. 19, q.v.

m. weighing, i.q. tul 3, q.v. (cf. atha-tᵒ, p. 63a, l. 37; mēna-tᵒ, p. 573b, l. 11; māvi roṭᵘ-tᵘ, p. 611a, l. 20) (Gr.Gr. 124); weight (El., Gr.Gr. 23, W. 114); a machine for drawing water from a well or stream, the irrigation-lever of India, consisting of a lever supported on one or two long posts, having a bucket suspended at one end, and a weight of stone or earth at the other (El.). -trạngᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a kind of hanging shelf (like the pan of a balance hung on strings) on which dishes, etc., are stored one above the other. ¶ tōla-bār m. a weight by weighment, esp. the gift (for pious purposes) of grain or similar articles, equivalent in amount to the weight of a man. This is a religious ceremony, in which the grain is weighed against the giver, in order to avoid the consequences of some evil omen or unlucky astrological conjuncture. -brôrᵘ m. the cross-bar on which an irrigation-lever swings as on a fulerum. -kijᵘ̈ f. the bar which joins the two upright posts of an irrigation-lever. -kānüjᵘ̈ f. (of the next), the swinging cross-bar of an irrigation-lever, if it is not a heavy beam. -kānul m. the same swinging beam, if it is of heavier make. -mēn f. (sg. dat. -mīñᵘ̈), measurement by scales (i.e. by weight) (cf. mēna-tōl, p. 573b, l. 11). -raz f. the rope attached by one end to the free end of the swinging beam of an irrigation-lever, and to the other end of which the bucket is fastened. -ʦaḍ m. the fixed upright post of an irrigation-lever. -wān m. the site of a well irrigation-lever. -wôrᵘ m. the earthenware bucket of an irrigation-lever, a well-bucket (Gr.M., Śiv. 1027). ¶ tōlas khārun m.inf. to elevate (a person) on to an irrigation-lever (and leave him there); met. after having agreed to give the necessary help to a person engaged on some impossible task, and so inducing him to undertake it, to drive him to distraction by recognizing the impossibility and, at the critical moment, withdrawing the promised help; loudly to reproach and blame (a person). --ladun -- m.inf. to blame with harsh abuse.
f. the sign Libra of the Zodiac (Śiv. 481, K. 132).
m. any clan of high-caste Hindūs.
f. the holy basil (Ocymum sanctum), the sacred tulasī shrub of India (Śiv. 498, 1058); the leaves of this plant (Śiv. 1400).
f. a kind of bead necklace in four or five strands, and with a jewelled central ornament.
f. wages for weighing, a weighman's fee.
f. the profession or duties of a weighman.
n.ag. (f. tōlavüñᵘ̈), one who weighs, a weighman.
m. the name used in schools for the Śāradā form of the letter ai. Cf. tālav ē, s.v. tālav.

f. teaching, instruction (El. tãlím); copying finely, writing accurately; m. the paper on which are depicted the characters denoting the different coloured threads to be used by a shawl-maker at each step of his work (cf. gul-i-tᵒ, p. 283b, l. 29, and ganḍan-wôlᵘ, p. 290b, l. 38) (El. tálím; L. 462, tálim).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. tūlᵘ; f. tūjᵘ̈, sg. dat. tōjĕ; 2 p.p. tōjyōv), to weight, measure by weight (cf. hᵒrᵒ hāyẹ̆ka tᵒ, p. 346a, l. 35; hᵃri tᵒ, p. 346a, l. 39; trāyĕ tᵒ, s.v. trāy) (Gr.Gr. 18, 124; 197, conj. part. tūlith; 246, impve. 3, tūlin; Gr.M.; W. 114; L.V. 23; Śiv. 1476, 1827 (met.); H. ix, 10; K.Pr. 63); to measure (length, etc.) (Śiv. 1565). ¶ tūlᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (sg. abl. tōli-mati; f. tūjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, sg. dat. tōjĕ-maʦĕ), weighed. ¶ tūlⁱ tūlⁱ katha karañĕ f. pl. inf. to speak coquettishly, affectedly, wantonly.
adj. (f. tōlᵘ̈rᵘ̈), loud-voiced, one who habitually speaks loudly (even when speaking on private matters).
m. a professional weighman, a man who is skilled in weighing.
or tolᵘ 1 m. a mattress, the wadded quilt on which a sleeper lies.
m. in ṭŏlⁱ m.pl. the sockets of the eyes (cf. ʦūra-ṭᵒ, s.v. ʦūr 1) (K.Pr. 159); cf. ṭŏjĕ, of which this is the mase. form. -vyoṭhᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ṭhᵘ̈), a man with prominent eye-sockets.
(cf.) in ṭȧlⁱ ṭörⁱ wuchun m.inf. (when engaged on some work) secretly to glance obliquely under the eyelids at some other person's work. Cf. tȧlⁱ-ṭāri wuchun, p. 996b, l. 34.

(for 3, see talun) m. the inner lining (containing cotton padding) of a warm mantle, quilt, or the like (cf. gaba-tᵒ, p. 274b, l. 14; guni-tᵒ, p. 288b, l. 36; lēphi-tᵒ, p. 528b, l. 28). Cf. also tọ̆lᵘ or tolᵘ 1, tul 3, and talöyⁱ.
m. the nest of wild bees, or other stinging insects.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. tọ̆mbᵘ), to pull out, pluck open by hand (cotton, wool, or the like), to card by hand. Cf. tọ̆mbᵘ 2.
m. a stinging insect, such as a gadfly; a wild bee.
f. a honeycomb or other receptacle for wild honey.
f. a kind of gourd (Lagenaria vulgaris). It is used for cupping. ¶ tŏmbĕ hĕñĕ f. pl. inf. to cup, as ab. --lāgañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to apply a gourd for this cupping.
m. a pencil-shaped piece of cleaned cotton held in the left hand for spinning (cf. phamba-tᵒ, p. 698a, l. 46) (K.Pr. 244).

or tŏmul m. (sg. dat. tŏmᵃlas), husked rice, uncooked rice (cf. bēlⁱ-tⁱ or byölⁱ-tⁱ, p. 150a, l. 50; gŏsöñⁱ-tⁱ, p. 309b, l. 50; ʦari-tᵒ, s.v. ʦürᵘ̈ 4) (El.; Gr.Gr. 51, 75, 164; Gr.M.; Śiv. 841 (tŏmal, pl. nom.); K.Pr. 7, 225). ¶ tŏmᵃla-ôṭᵃ m. rice-flour (El. tumla-óṭ). -kạtᵃra m. a very small amount of husked rice. -mọ̆nḍᵘ m. a thick cake made of rice-flour (Gr.Gr. 75). -pholᵘ m. a single grain of husked rice (in the pl., only in this sense; Gr.Gr. 164); a small quantity (esp. enough for subsistence) of husked rice (Gr.Gr. 164). -ṭọ̆ṭhᵘ m. fifteen seers (thirty pounds) of husked rice (see ṭọ̆ṭhᵘ). -ʦŏ̈ṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ʦŏcĕ), rice-bread (El., Gr.Gr. 74). -wôñᵘ m. a seller of husked rice. -worᵘ m. a cake made of rice-flour.
m. onomat. a chink, jingle, in chŏñ-ṭŏñ, p. 163a, l. 38, q.v.

f. the pounding end of a rice-pestle; a lump, or bump on the upper part of the forehead; (when loss in business has occurred, esp. when due to carelessness) an evil report, scandal. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such an ill report to occur.
adj. c.g. one who has a bump, or lump, on the upper part of the forehead.
adj. c.g. one who (owing to his carelessness) is an object of scandal.
m. an oven; a stove; cf. tanūr. -ʦrüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ʦracĕ), the circular cover of an oven. -ʦŏ̈ṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ʦŏcĕ), bread or a cake baked in an oven.
adj. c.g. one who has a lump, bump, boil, or tumour on the forehead. Cf. ṭŏnḍ and tō̃g or ṭō̃g.
tọ̆ngᵘ, or (q.v.) thọ̆ngᵘ m. the peak of a mountain or the like (El. túng, a mountain pass; K. tŏng, 629, 631-2).

m. a kind of hoe, a hand-hoe (cf. pötᵃri-tᵃ, p. 804a, l. 13) (El. tongur and tungarú. The latter he describes as a small pickaxe, the iron part of which is placed at an angle of forty-five degrees to the wooden handle; L. 460, tongru, a hand-hoe). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become a hoe; hence, met., to become bent and broken down by disease or the like. --trāwun -- m.inf. to follow and importune persistently. --trövith bĕhun -- m.inf. obstinately and persistently to follow, as ab. ¶ ṭŏngȧrⁱ-pürⁱ f. the handle of a hoe. -pôturᵘ m. the blade of a hoe.
in tŏnna-kạtᵃra m. a small amount of husked rice. -pholᵘ m. a small amount or small parcel of husked rice.
m. a certain seed (imported from the north) used as a remedy for insect-bites, boils, and the like.

f.pl. spits or skewers for cooking meat; cf. tȧndⁱjĕ. tọ̆nᵃjĕn lagun m.inf. to be fixed on roasting-spits; met. to be on thorns of anxiety (e.g. through fear of the consequences of having lost money entrusted to one).
f. a charming woman expert in fluent, graceful, and tender language. Cf. tawāza.
m. the belly below the navel, the pubes, region of the bladder. Cf. tūnᵘ.
m. a turban (for males) (according to El. s.v. tón, this is an old word).

adj. (f. tüñᵘ̈ 2, for 1, see s.v.), thin, not thick (El. tŏn, tun; Gr.Gr. 29, 57, 62, 140; Śiv. 336); thin, lean, emaciated; thin, delicate, slender; thin, liquid (as compared with solid) (Gr.M., K.Pr. 205 tun). --pahān -- adj. (f. tüñᵘ̈ pahān), somewhat thin, a little thin, rather thin, thinnish.

m. a secondary suffix, like pônᵘ, q.v., forming abstract nouns denoting general relationship, state, or condition. The relationship indicated is more intimate than that indicated by pônᵘ (q.v.) (Gr.Gr. 143-4) (cf. baba-tᵒ, fatherhood, p. 77a, l. 20; bācabaṭh-tᵒ, the condition of a priest-brāhman, p. 79a, l. 42; buhᵃ̇rᵃ̇-tᵃ̇, the profession of a druggist, p. 66b, l. 32; bĕnüñᵘ̈-tᵘ̈, sisterhood, p. 114a, l. 37; brahma-tᵒ, brāhmaṇhood, p. 121a, l. 20; bröhman-tᵒ, id., p. 121b, l. 34; bārȧnⁱ-tⁱ, brotherhood, p. 124a, l. 48; böyⁱ-tⁱ, brotherhood, p. 149b, l. 11; bȧyⁱ-kākañĕ-tⁱ, the relationship of sisters-in-law, p. 150a, l. 13; drikākañĕ-tᵒ, the mutual relationship between brothers' wives, p. 243a, l. 45; mājĕ-tᵒ, motherhood, p. 557b, l. 31; nāñĕ-tᵒ, grandmotherhood, p. 644a, l. 28; nŏshĕ-tᵒ, daughter-in-lawship, p. 655b, l. 32; pŏtra-tᵒ, sonhood, p. 799b, l. 34; pāyĕchⁱ-tⁱ, the occupation of an outcaste Brāhmaṇ, p. 813b, l. 6; rĕshⁱ-tⁱ, anchorite-hood, p. 856a, l. 2). ¶ This suffix is also used to indicate conduct like that of the principal word, as in bācabaṭh-tᵒ, a condition like that of a priest-brāhmaṇ, see ab.; buhᵃ̇rᵃ̇-tᵃ̇, conduct like that of a druggist, see ab.; böyⁱ-tⁱ, brotherly conduct, see ab.; bȧyⁱ-kākañĕ-tⁱ, conduct like that of sisters-in-law, see ab.; kŏlayĕ-tᵒ, conduct like that of a wife, humble obedience, p. 442a, l. 23; kanjar-tᵒ, conduct like that of a souteneur, p. 457a, l. 26; mājĕ-tᵒ, motherly conduct, see ab.; nāñĕ-tᵒ, affectionate conduct like that of a grandmother, see ab.; pōshĕ-tᵒ, gentle conduct, like that of one who tends flowers, p. 779a, l. 33; pitᵃ̇rᵃ̇-tᵃ̇, the mutual hostility natural among kinsfolk, p. 803a, l. 45; pŏtra-tᵒ, conduct like that of a son, see ab.; pāyĕchⁱ-tⁱ, conduct like that of an outcaste Brāhmaṇ, see ab.; sŏna-tᵒ, mutual hostility like that between co-wives, p. 917b, l. 48.

m. (the pl. nom. of ṭŏph, q.v., also has the form ṭŏpa), a kind of embroidery (made by forming a pattern with thread, etc., on cloth). ṭŏpa-dār adj. c.g. embroidered in this way. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to embroider, as ab. -sᵃʦ m. an embroiderer. -sᵃʦan f. (sg. dat. sᵃʦüñᵃ), an embroidering needle; met. a woman who (like this needle) pierces to the vitals, one who uses spiteful language.
m. a kind of cap or head-dress, worn under the turban, and reaching down to the back of the neck.
adj. c.g. (of a snake or the like) accustomed to bite, (of a stinging insect) accustomed to sting.
adj. (f. -kijᵘ̈), a darling child, one treated and tended with much affection.

f. (sg. dat. ṭŏpi), a bite or sting (of a serpent, or a biting or stinging insect, or the like) (cf. bicⁱ-ṭⁱ, p. 149b, l. 30; mö̃kan- ṭᵒ, reported as m., but possibly incorrectly, p. 562a, l. 19; pishⁱ-ṭⁱ, p. 818a, l. 36; ʦara-ṭᵒ, s.v. ʦar 2) (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 122, 150, ṭop; 217, 250, ṭuph); a lancet (El.); the pulsation or beating of an abscess (El.); itch, itchiness; sexual fury, intense desire for sexual intercourse, oestrum; a Moslem's lock of hair (cf. ṭopᵘ 1) (El.; K.Pr. 33, 62). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of a serpent or biting insect) to bite; (of a stinging insect) to sting (W. 134). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. urgent desire for sexual intercourse to be experienced. --lāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to sting (El.). --mōrüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a sting to be calmed or allayed; met. any intensity to be calmed (e.g. the heat of boiling water to be cooled, unbearable hunger to be allayed by giving a little food, and so on). --mōravüñᵘ̈ -- f. to allay a sting; to calm an intensity, as ab. ¶ ṭŏpa mārñĕ (for --mārañe --) f.pl. to allay itching by light scratching.

f. (sg. dat. tōpi), a gun, a cannon, a field-piece (El. tŏp, m., a gun). --lāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to aim and fire a gun (at a person or thing). --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to explode, or fire, a gun (e.g. as a time signal). --tayār karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to load a gun (? cannon) (El. taiyár karun, m.). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'a cannon to come'; hence (of some sharp order, objectionable command, or the like) to be extremely unpleasing.
in okᵘ-tôpᵘ, p. 19a, l. 45; dutôpᵘ, p. 259a, l. 1; trᵃtôpᵃ, s.v. Cf. tāph.

m. long plentiful hair (of the head) or ringlets, esp. that of a woman (El. taup, a ringlet; ṭŏp, a Musalmān's lock of hair; Gr.Gr. 146). Cf. ṭŏph, ṭapil, and ṭapᵘ̈rᵘ̈. ¶ ṭȧpⁱ-chüʦⁱ f. a white-haired, or grey-haired, woman. -khakhürᵘ̈ f. dragging (esp. a woman) by the hair along the ground. -kaḍa-kaḍ f. mutual pulling of each other's hair (in a fight between women). -kôsᵘ adj. (f. -kösᵘ̈), having the head shaved, a shaveling. -lang m. a small compressed lock of hair (quasi, a branch from the whole head of hair). -tulᵘ m. a small wisp of a woman's hair.
m. a blow on a ball (as in hockey, etc.). ṭapĕn gindun m.inf. to play at striking balls (as in hockey, etc.).

m. a side, a party (e.g. at a wedding, the bridegroom's family, or the bride's family); one of several sources (of wealth, honour, help, disgrace, or punishment, and so on). This word is usually the second member of a compound word, as in du-ṭopᵘ sāl, an invitation to a wedding, a twofold invitation (cf. p. 258b, l. 46); ʦu-ṭopᵘ danḍ, a punishment for four reasons; so sāsa-ṭᵒ, p. 941a, l. 11; sata-ṭᵒ, p. 944b, l. 45; trᵃṭopᵃ, s.v.

m. hindrance, obstruction, check (esp. of some work nearly completed); cf. tôrᵘ 1. --dith thawun -- m.inf. to obstruct and stop completely (someone else's work which is nearly completed). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to stop or obstruct (another engaged on any work, esp. by declaring it to be fruitless).

adv. there (of some place out of sight) (El. thither; Gr.Gr. 155; W. 94, thither; 139, tur, there; Śiv. 42; Rām. 293-4; H. x, 3; YZ. 91). -kun adv. towards that place (out of sight), thither, in that direction (Gr.Gr. 160); in that place (out of sight), there. ¶ tōra adv. from there, thence (of a place out of sight) (Gr.Gr. 156; W. 94; Śiv. 81, 117, 1792; Rām. 425, 1055; H. i, 6, 8; v, 4, 9; viii, 11; xii, 1, 11; K.Pr. 154); in reply (to a question or the like) (Śiv. 66, 88, 310, 312, 630, 636, 837, 1249; Rām. 150, 193, 256, 356, 365, 383, 613, 657, 660, 681, 811, 816, 823, 946, 1621-2, 1650, 1703; YZ. 138, 389). -kani or -kanĕn  adv. from. that direction (out of sight) (Gr.Gr. 159); in that direction (out of sight). -kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, that (out of sight) direction, produced in that direction. -pĕṭha adv. from there, from that place (out of sight) (u.w. vbs. of coming or the like). -yōr adv. from there (out of sight) to here and (back again) from here to there, i.e. over the whole intervening space, or (with vbs. of motion) backwards and forwards. ¶ tūrⁱ also written tūry adv. in that very place (out of sight), only in that place, even there (Gr.Gr. 156; L.V. 19, 61; Śiv. 283; H. vii, 20; x, 3; K.Pr. 84 túr); to that very place, thither (Rām. 661). -kun or tūry-kun adv. only in that very place (Gr.Gr. 160); thither only, only to there (Rām. 1254); only in that direction, hence (met.) only in thy direction, only towards thee (Rām. 650); in those very conditions, only in respect, or in regard to, that (K. 867, 1142). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give in that very place; to give (something) at the very place (where it is received); hence, to return, give back immediately on receipt (K. 687). ¶ tōrukᵘ adj. (f. tōrücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or produced in, there (out of sight).

m. hair, a fringe of hair; an ornamental tassel, a border; an ornament worn on a turban (K.Pr. 225, turah); (in Ksh.) a tassel or the like made of very fine silver wire. -dār طرہ دار (of the hair) fringed, crested, etc.; (in Ksh. esp.) (of a turban or the like) fringed with fine silver wires. -dastār طرہ دستار m. a turban fringed, as ab.

or (q.v.) tōrüʦᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. tōraʦhi), a carpenter's chisel (L. 370, túrats). -wôrᵘ m. a fine chisel, esp. for cutting narrow holes. ¶ tōraʦhi-dan m. the wooden handle of a chisel. -mūrᵘ̈ f. the cutting edge of a chisel.

f. the cucurbitaceous plant and the vegetable, Luffa acutangula (El. turela, m. one of the Cucurbitaciae). tŏrēla-hüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -hacĕ), a dried piece of the fruit of the plant (cut up and stored to dry for winter).
m. (sg. dat. törīkhas), a date, era, epoch (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. dark, obscure; (in Ksh.) subst. m. (sg. dat. törīkas), obscurity, darkness, gloom (Rām. 798).
tārīf تعریف m. praise (El.; W. 18; H. vi, 17). --karun -- m.inf. to praise (El., Gr.M.).

in tŏrka-chān m. a private carpenter, a village carpenter who works on his own account, a cabinet maker (H. vii, 17, 20); cf. chān 1. -chān-bāy f. his wife. -chönil f. the occupation of a cabinet maker. tŏrka-chöñᵘ̈ f. a cabinet maker's wife.
m. wearing disguise, etc. (for the purpose of deception).

तोर॑च़ू॒ or (q.v.) tōraʦh f. (sg. dat. tōraʦĕ), a carpenter's chisel (Gr.M.); ? a wedge for splitting wood (cf. ʦōras). ¶ tōraʦi-dan m. the wooden handle of a chisel. -mūrᵘ̈ f. the cutting edge of a chisel.

m. the eyelid (cf. ȧchⁱ-ṭörⁱ, p. 8b, l. 39; añĕma-ṭörⁱ, p. 37b, l. 17; añĕma-ṭôrᵘ, id., l. 18; ȧshⁱ-ṭörⁱ, p. 47b, l. 50; tȧlⁱ-ṭāri wuchun, p. 996b, l. 34; ṭȧlⁱ ṭörⁱ wuchun, p. 1000a, l. 11; ṭĕṭam- ṭôrᵘ, s.v. ṭĕṭam) (El. ṭár, ṭór. El. gives also ṭáryí f. with the same meaning). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. the eyelid to fall; extreme desire or longing for something seen to be felt. --wŏtalun -- m.inf. the eyelid to rise, urgent desire, as ab., to be satisfied. ¶ ṭāri khasun m.inf. to be, or become, entirely pleasing, to be satisfying. --khotᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --khüʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈--), become pleasing, as ab. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. satisfaction to be experienced. ¶ ṭörⁱ ȧchⁱ dôdᵘ m. disease of the eyelids. --yinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. disease of the eyelids (accompanied by intumescence) to occur. ¶ ṭāricᵘ̈ zih f. the edge of the eyelid (El. ṭárich zih, ? ṭāricᵘ̈ zēh).

(for 2, see) or tôḍᵘ m. a bolt (of a door or window) (cf. ʦhala-tᵒ, s.v. ʦhal) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 207, 1503, 1646, 1747, 1890; K. 69, 73, 77; K.Pr. 164); a door-bar; met. check, obstruction (Śiv. 1369). Cf. tōr 1. ¶ törⁱ-hüṭⁱ f. (sg. dat. -hacĕ), the wooden bar of a door-bar, the wooden bolt of a door-bolt. -khünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -khanjĕ), the lower jaw (El. tárkhanḍ, K.Pr. 120).

(for 2, see tārun) f. delay, lateness, tardiness, slowness (cf. dŏha-tᵒ, p. 200a, l. 24; khĕna-tᵒ, p. 402a, l. 10; katha-tᵒ, p. 486b, l. 18; lama-tᵒ, p. 524a, l. 46; nāwa-tᵒ, p. 666b, l. 32; rōṭa-tᵒ, p. 845a, l. 8) (El. tãr, tardiness, slowness, delay; Gr.M.; W. 13; Śiv. 728, 1682, 1739; Rām. 586; K. 355, 633, 719). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. delay to occur. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause delay, make delay, to delay (Śiv. 52; K. 364, 378, 580). ¶ tāri sg. abl. by delay, in a delayed manner; --gaʦhun -- (of the mind, etc.), to become confused (H. v. 7, tārē, m.c.; YZ. 132, id.); to fade, wither, die (of a plant) (K.Pr. 58).

m. thirst (esp. when caused by eating something saline, acrid, pungent, or the like, and no water is available). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. such thirst to occur. --lagun -- m.inf. parching thirst to attack a person (esp. when wandering on an arid desert in the hot season). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. thirst to be experienced by a person (esp. when caused by saline, etc., food, and no water is available). --wŏthun -- m.inf. thirst caused as ab., or by sickness, to arise.
in ṭōsa-ṭōs f. a mutual struggle or fight (with fists or the like). ṭōsa-ṭōs wŏthüñᵘ̈ f.inf. such a fight between two parties to arise. Cf. ṭūsᵘ.

m. popularly imagined to be a kind of bird, from the hair (? down) of which a valuable cloth is made, and said to live in the country to the north of Kashmīr (? Khōrāsān); a fine kind of shawl-wool, popularly supposed to be the hair (? down) of this bird; the cloth (which is a fine kind of pashmīna) made from this wool; cf. tūsⁱ and tōsakh. -pō̃bürᵘ̈ f. a shawl of this cloth (Rām. 1120).
m. (sg. dat. tōsakas), a valuable cloth popularly believed to be made from the hair (? down) of the tōsa-bird (see tōsa), a fine kind of pashmīua.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. tōshĕnôwᵘ), to cause to be pleased, to cause to be satisfied (Gr.Gr. 174).

conj. 2 or 3 (1 p.p. tūshᵘ; 2 p.p. tōshyōv or (Gr.Gr. xxxv) tōchyōv), to be pleased (by another's conduct), satisfied, gratified (e.g. of a master in regard to a servant) (Gr.Gr. 174, 206; Śiv. 44, 1690; Rām. 1094, 1580; K. 20, 95, 103, 139, 194, 293, 308, 330, 467, 477, 594, 643, 714, 750, 752, 963, 1133, 1163, 1165; YZ. 31, 114; K.Pr. 72, 153, 214); to show kindness (to) (K.Pr. 193); cf. tōṭhun and ṭōṭhun. tūshᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tūshᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, sg. dat. tōshĕ-maʦĕ), pleased, satisfied.
(= tahsīldār تحصیلدار q.v.) m. a certain revenue official, a collector of revenue (Gr.M.).
m. effect, operation, mode of operating (e.g. the operation or effect of a medicine) (Gr.M.).

m.pl. long thin strips of skin or leather, leather straps, thongs. --tulȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to raise strips of skin, to flog a person so as to flay him. --wuḍāwȧnⁱ -- m.pl.inf. to cause strips of skin to fly, to flog, as ab.
m. a plausible knave, one who swindles by means of clever language. Cf. ṭŏṭākh.

f. praise, commendation (Gr.M.; Śiv. 733, 756, 1117, 1334, 1907; Rām. 1108c; K. 53, 412, 610, 962); with suff. of indef. art. tŏtāh, a praise, i.e. a song of praise (K. 1152). I.q. stutā, tŏth 2, and tōth, qq.v.

m. a parrot (Gr.Gr. 94; Gr.M.; W. 3; Śiv. 962, 1362; H. ii, 4-17; K.Pr. 78). -cashm adj. c.g. 'parrot-eyed', faithless, false, treacherous. -kolᵘ adj. (f. -küjᵘ̈), 'parrot dumb', i.e. not speaking clearly, mumbling, inarticulate (esp. of a child).
m. (under another's orders) determination, persistence, zeal (in completing some work).

m. employment on a very troublesome and difficult work, which must, somehow or other, be accomplished. --rōzun -- m.inf. such work to remain to be done, i.e. not completed, and still waiting to be finished. --thawun -- m.inf. to leave such work to be finished by someone else. ¶ ṭö̃ṭi-wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), a miser, skinflint, niggard.
m. a beam or rafter for supporting the roof of a house.
m. loss, damage (incurred in a sale or the like). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. such loss to befall (a person).

f. (sg. dat. ṭŏṭākas), telling lies, fabricating a cock-and-bull story (either as a joke, or with intent to cheat). Cf. ṭŏṭa. ¶ ṭŏṭakā-mȧnzil m. chattering impossibilities, telling tall or impossible yarns (as if one were a lunatic).

(c.g.) or ṭŏṭolᵘ (f. ṭŏṭᵘ̈jᵘ̈) adj. one who is in the habit of charging others with untruthfulness, even when their words are true, a contradictor, one who habitually gives the lie to others. Cf. ṭŏṭañ.
adj. c.g. 'beaky' (cf. tō̃th), (of a bird) sharp-beaked; (of a stone, spike, or the like) sharp-pointed.
f. N. of a mountain goddess worshipped in Kashmīr, a form of Pārvatī (Śiv. 1162).
m. forcible tyrannous conduct (compelling a weaker to surrender property, do some work, act as a slave, or the like). Cf. ṭŏṭun.
or tutām, or tŏ(tu)tāmath  adv. up to then, as far as that (El., W. tutām); then (El. tutām). Cf. tŏtāñ.
in ṭōṭam-nay f. (in a famine or the like) utter poverty (due to such); cf. ṭŏṭun. ṭōṭam-nayĕ wātun m.inf. to arrive at (i.e. fall into) such utter poverty.
f. a woman who is in the habit of giving the lie to others, even when they are speaking the truth, one who habitually contradicts, or gives the lie to, others. Cf. ṭŏṭal.
or tutāñ, or tŏ(tu)tāñĕth  adv. up to then, as far as that (i.q. tŏtām, q.v.) (K.Pr. 101, 197, 257, tután).
m. (sg. dat. tŏṭas), a small atom of dirt or seed remaining in cotton after it has been carded. Cf. ṭọ̆ṭᵘ and ṭŏṭh.

m. (sg. dat. ṭŏṭas), a boll, or capsule, on the cotton-plant, which has gone bad (and contains no cotton fit for spinning), or which refuses to ripen (cf. kapasi-ṭᵒ, p. 464a, l. 44); met. a deceiver, one who uses language (pleasant to hear, but) deceitful. Cf. ṭọ̆ṭᵘ and tŏṭh.
m. (sg. dat. tōtas), praise, eulogy; cf. tŏtā and tŏth 2. --karȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to sing the praises (of), to eulogize publicly.

f. (sg. dat. tō̃ti, Gr.Gr. 70) the beak (of a bird or the like) (El. tónt; Śiv. 1064; Rām. 604; K. 191; K.Pr. 34, tuṅth); the fore-finger; i.q. tyū̃thᵘ in lashi-tyū̃thᵘ, p. 533b, l. 47. tō̃ta-krĕhonᵘ adj. (f. -krĕhüñᵘ̈ or tō̃ʦa-krĕhüñᵘ̈), black-beaked; (of a pen) black-nibbed; (of a human being) weak-faced (gentle-faced) but nevertheless inwardly secret (esp. when he or she has power to crush another), fair-faced but sly.
in pānʦ tŏth, see p. 742b, ll. 6, 14. This word is another form of tattwa, q.v. (Śiv. 1498, 1685, 1831).
f. (sg. dat. tö̃ʦᵘ̈), a fine thread, fibre, filament; catgut, a sinew; wire; the string of a musical instrument; a thin filament of strong syrup or other glutinous liquor). Cf. ṭö̃ṭhᵘ̈.
f. (sg. dat. tö̆ʦᵘ̈), praise, eulogy (K. 15, 62, 386, 1048). I.q. stutā, tŏtā, and tōth, qq.v.

f. self-conceit, overweening pride (i.q. ṭē̃ṭh, q.v.), in tö̃th khārüñᵘ̈ f.inf. by praise or flattery to fill (a person) with overweening pride (so that he refuses to listen to reason). --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.pl. to be filled with overweening pride (as ab.) (so that one is insensible to reason).
adj. c.g. one who is impudent, quick-witted and expert.
n.ag. (f. tōṭhavüñᵘ̈), one who is pleased, gratified, appeased (see tōṭhun) (Śiv. 1199).

conj. 2 or 3 (1 p.p. tūṭhᵘ; f. tūṭhᵘ̈, dat. tōchĕ; 2 p.p. tōṭhyōv (Śiv. 701, 705, 735) or tōchyōv), to become satisfied, pleased, gratified (by another's conduct) (Śiv. 1043, 1403, 1406; Rām. 537; K. 16, 239, 310, 1104, 1172); (of a god) to be pleased or appeased (by worship or the like) (Śiv. 309, 484, 982; Rām. 75, 226, 940, 1274; K. 269, 611, 621, 792, 877, 1173-4); (as vb. trans.) to be pleased with, gracious to (dat. of person) (Śiv. 75, 115, 190, 205, 488, 660, 701, 705, 734-5, 1045, 1341, 1378; Rām. 125, 508; K. 309, 671); cf. tōshun and ṭōṭhun. tūṭhᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. tūṭhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, dat. tōchĕ-maʦĕ), pleased, gratified, appeased, as ab. tōṭhyō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. tōṭhyē-müʦᵘ̈), id.

conj. 2 or 3 (1 p.p. ṭūṭhᵘ; f. ṭūṭhᵘ̈, dat. ṭōchĕ; 2 p.p. ṭōṭhyōv), i.q. tōṭhun, q.v. (Śiv. 1471 to be pleased, satisfied). ṭūṭhᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ṭūṭhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, dat. ṭōchĕ-maʦĕ), i.q. tūṭhᵘ-motᵘ, s.v. tōṭhun, q.v. ṭōṭhyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ṭōṭhyē-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. tōṭhyō-motᵘ, s.v. tōṭhun, q.v.
adj. c.g. clever, sharp, smart, intelligent (esp. of a boy).

or ṭoṭhᵘ adj. (f. ṭüṭhᵘ̈), (of rice or the like) weighing two and a half trakhs (see trakh 2) of six Kāshmīrī seers each, or fifteen seers in all (cf. tŏmᵃla-ṭᵃ, p. 1006b, l. 31) (Gr.Gr. 145). Cf. ṭaṭhulᵘ.

or (q.v.) ṭhôṭhᵘ adj. (f. ṭöṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat ṭāchĕ), dear, beloved, precious, darling (cf. kāmi-ṭᵒ, p. 444a, l. 17; mājĕ-ṭᵒ, p. 557b, l. 34) (Gr.Gr. 139; Gr.M.; W. 20, ṭoṭ; Śiv. 7, 435, 1547; Rām. 510, 628, 729, 1737; K. 289, 728, 803, 1133; H. iv, 4; ṭhôṭhᵘ, vii, 4; YZ. ṭôṭ, 77, 131, 263; K.Pr. 29, 166, 215); favourite, liked (e.g. dainty food); generous (El.); venerable (El.); magnificent, splendid (El.); extreme, very great (K. 551, of grief). --thāwun -- m.inf. to prefer (El. ṭóṭ th˚). ¶ ṭāṭhi, vocative, Dear One!; (politely) Sir! (Rām. 268). ¶ ṭöṭhⁱ-dag f. the smart of a beloved one, the sorrow caused by the loss or death of a beloved one (such as a wife or son). -dag pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. such sorrow to befal. -dagal adj. c.g. afflicted with such sorrow. -khāv m. devouring a beloved, a man who devours (i.e. destroys) those whom he loves (an expression used in cursing). -khāwal f. a woman who devours those whom she loves (used in curses, as ab.). -ponᵘ m. mourning for a beloved, sorrow at the sudden death of a beloved son or the like. ¶ ṭöṭhᵘ̈ dag f. 'beloved sorrow', the feeling of terrible sorrow experienced by some unbearable grief. Cf. K. 551, ab.

f. (sg. dat. ṭã̄chĕ), a thin filament or stream of some liquid (such as oil, melted butter, honey, or even milk) (cf. dŏda-ṭᵒ, p. 190a, l. 41; khira-ṭᵒ, p. 409a, l. 41; tīla-ṭᵒ, p. 999a, l. 15); cf. tö̃th 1, q.v. --khārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to spin a long yarn, make a prolix statement or criticism. --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of a statement or criticism) to become prolix. ¶ ṭö̃ṭa-kĕlam m. the trickling resin exuding from a fir-tree.
conj. nevertheless, still, yet, even so, even then (Gr.M.; L.V. 29; Śiv. 1353-4; Rām. 1601; K.Pr. 70, 165 (totih); K. 781, 1117, 1124). I.q. tawa-ti, p. 969b, l. 22.
? f. neglecting, abandoning; nyāyĕs tötīl, slowness in quarrelling (K.Pr. 103).

m. (sg. dat. ṭö̃ṭakas), a foul-mouthed, ill-natured fellow. ¶ ṭö̃ṭakh f. (sg. dat. ṭö̃ṭaki), an abusive ill-natured woman. -nôrᵘ adj. (f. -nörᵘ̈), a noisy child, one who for little or no reason is always ready to make a noise.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. tọ̆tᵘ, f. tö̆ʦᵘ̈), to praise, eulogize, sing praises to (K. 14, 63, 255, 384, 387, 681, 934).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ṭŏṭyōv), to have insufficient room (e.g. in a house or for sitting), to be crowded; to have (or find oneself with) insufficient means of livelihood (cf. atha ṭᵒ, p. 63b, l. 18) (L.V. 13). ṭŏṭun yunᵘ m.inf. one's livelihood to become insufficient. ¶ ṭŏṭan-wād m. distress caused by insufficient profits (from one's livelihood); worry, distress (caused by another's oppression). -wād anun m.inf. to cause another's livelihood to give insufficient profits; to cause worry or distress to another. -wād yunᵘ m.inf. loss of profits (as ab.) to occur; worry, or distress, as ab., to occur. ¶ ṭŏṭyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ṭŏṭyē-müʦᵘ̈), crowded, oppressed by want of room; having insufficient means of livelihood.

(Gr.Gr. 156) tatuth, or totuth adv. to that place (out of sight), thither (u.w.vbs. of going or the like); in that place (o. of s.), there (Gr.Gr. 156); cf. totᵘ 2. tatuthᵘ̈y adv. even there (Gr.Gr. 156).

f. (sg. dat. ṭọ̆ṭᵃrüñᵃ), crowding (other things, such as houses in a street) close together (Gr.Gr. 121). ṭọ̆ṭᵃran-wād m. a habit or custom of crowding things together (e.g. by stopping traffic on a road); agitation, anxiety, or distress, of mind (caused by another's frequent anger, persistent enmity).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭọ̆ṭᵃrôwᵃ), to crowd (things) together (e.g. houses on a public road). ṭọ̆ṭᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. ṭọ̆ṭᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), crowded together (by someone) (as ab.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭọ̆ṭᵒrᵒ), to cause to have insufficient room, to crowd (things or persons) together (Gr.Gr. 121); to cause (a person) to have insufficient means of livelihood. Cf. ṭŏṭun.

m. a seed of cotton, a single cotton-seed (cf. kapasi-ṭᵒ, p. 464a, l. 43) (El. ṭuṭ; L. 459, tudth); met. a very small, or microscopic, quantity of anything (cf. thañi-ṭᵒ, p. 979b, l. 37). Cf. tŏṭh and ṭŏṭh. ¶ ṭŏṭⁱ m.pl. cotton-seeds (in quantity); (of a servant or the like) fatigue, weariness, worry (caused by being sent hither and thither, and never having any rest). -ã̄cār 'worry-pickles', (to a servant or the like) worry caused by not being allowed to come and go (i.e. by being kept at his work, etc.). --anȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to cause worry (to a servant, etc.) by constantly sending him hither and thither. -byôlᵘ m. a single cotton-seed as found amid cotton which has been extracted from the husk. -carkh m. (sg. dat. -carkas), an instrument for extracting the seeds from cotton, a cotton-carder. -honḍᵘ hyuhᵘ m. 'like a ram (fattened) on cotton-seeds', hence, a simple-minded, cool-tempered person (who is not affected by abuse or the like). -khŏyĕ f.pl. 'microscopic politenesses', the want of manners of a rude, ill-mannered, child, or the like. --yinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. weariness to come (caused by searching in vain for something lost or the like). -yẹ̆ndᵃr m. a machine for carding cotton (freeing it from the seeds).

m. (f. ṭüṭᵘ̈ 1 (for 2, see s.v.), sg. dat. ṭacĕ), a horse, esp. a pony (cf. gurⁱ- tüṭᵘ̈, p. 299a, l. 15) (El. ṭaṭ, a pony mare; W. 121, ṭoṭ; K.Pr. 11, 174). ¶ ṭȧṭⁱ-khŏyĕ f.pl. 'horse-habits', conduct like that of a brute-beast, insolent and foolish conduct. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ. His wife is ṭȧṭⁱ-wölⁱ-bāy), a horse-keeper, one who lives by conveying loads on horse-back, a horse-carrier.

adj. (f. tüʦᵘ̈), very hot, red-hot (El. taut, tŏt, hot; Gr.Gr. 29, 140; Śiv. 1870; Rām. 723, 1587); hot, not cold (cf. tāpa-tᵒ, p. 1015a, l. 21) (L.V. 56-7; K.Pr. 213); fervent, zealous; passionate, wrathful; (in f.) (of soil) rendered too warm by the presence of large stones (L. 321, tats); (as subst. m.) a burnt place on the body, a scar caused by burning (cf. nāra-tᵒ, p. 648a, l. 44). ¶ tata-bād m. N. of a certain disease affecting the skin, and accompanied by a burning sensation and fainting. --gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), indignant, in a bad temper. --grọ̆dᵘ -- m. a furious vulture (pouncing on an unsuspecting dove); hence, sudden unexpected destruction (cf. grad and grọ̆dᵘ). --grọ̆dᵘgaʦhun -- m.inf. sudden unexpected destruction to occur. --gaʦhun-- m.inf. to become hot; (of some old or venerable person) to become angry or indignant (at some contrary happening). --hār -- m. a boiler for heating water. (In the centre is a tube filled with burning charcoal.) --khāna -- m. a heated room, a room made hot; a room specially heated in which a criminal (or enemy) is shut up as a torture. --khānas ladun -- m.inf. to put (a criminal or enemy) into a heated room (as ab.). --karun -- m.inf. to enrage (a person), to make furious. --phū -- f. a hot expiration, emitting a hot breath. --phū karawunᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --karavüñᵘ̈ --) (of food or the like) steaming hot, pouring forth hot steam. --pạtᵃran lagun -- m.inf. 'to find oneself on red-hot leaves (or sheets of iron)'; hence, to be in acute distress and at one's wits' ends (e.g. in endeavouring to find means for recovering property for which one is responsible, or for securing the recovery from sickness of one near and dear). --tövᵘ̈ -- f. 'a red-hot frying-pan', intense hot weather. --tövᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. intense heat to be felt (e.g. in fever, or in hot weather). --tövᵘ̈karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause extreme heat to be experienced (e.g. by inducing violent fever, or compelling a person to journey in the hot weather). --wôñᵘ -- m. hot water, boiling water. ¶ tȧtⁱ kala-pushⁱ dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to apply hot caps (as a cure for indigestion). (Woollen caps are heated and applied to the painful part.) ¶ taʦa kañĕ hĕñĕ f. pl. inf. 'to take up hot stones', (when ordered to go somewhere) to show obstinate unwillingness (cf. our 'dropping a thing like a hot potato'). --katᵃrĕ hĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. 'to take up hot potsherds', insolently and peremptorily to refuse (to do some work). Cf. the preceding. ¶ taʦi tāvi gaʦhun m.inf. 'to go on to a red-hot frying pan', to become utterly distraught, to be at one's wits' ends. ¶ tüʦᵘ̈ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to use hot (abuse), i.e., when one is too lazy to do a work oneself, to abuse and threaten another to make him do it. --rŏpay -- f. a hot rupee, a rupee hot from the mint, a newly-coined rupee. --tövᵘ̈ -- f. a red-hot frying pan, the extreme midday temperature in the hot weather.

adv. there, in that place (out of sight) (cf. yutᵘ kĕhō totᵘ, p. 390b, l. 1) (El. tut; Gr.Gr. 113, 156; W. 94, to˙t, tut; Rām. 152, 583, 885, 952, 1336; K. 593, 1117; H. xii, 16-7; K.Pr. 102, 237); to that place, thither (Gr.M.; Śiv. 65, 722, 1880; Rām. 119, 543, 602, 770, 814, 854, 1100, 1108c, 1143g, 1480, 1503, 1535, 1542, 1676, 1688, 1707, 1752; K. 42, 128, 1140; H. v, 1); from there (H. iii, 9); (yotᵘ totᵘ, wherever, Rām. 1776; everywhere, Rām. 99). -kun adv. towards there (out of sight), thither, towards that direction (Gr.Gr. 160). -tām or -tāñ adv. up to there, as far as that place (Rām. 1677, 1719, -tām; 885, -tāñ); as far as then, up to that time (Śiv. 681, -tām; Rām. 303, 1233, 1236, -tāñ; K. 797, 815, -tāñ; 1058, -tām). ¶ tȧtⁱ adv. even there, in that very place (out of sight) (u.w. vbs. of placing or the like) (El. tati, there; W. 94, tati and teti; L.V. 48, 49, 68; Śiv. 305, 1035, 1108); there, in that place (as ab.) (Gr.Gr. 154; Rām. 109, 546, 625, 941, 1258, 1294, 1719; K. 68, 604, 678; H. ii, 1; v, 1, 7, 9; viii, 9; YZ. 38); from that very place, only from there (Śiv. 635). ¶ tati adv. from there (out of sight), thence (El. tatih; Gr.Gr. 155; Rām. 80, 462, 942; K. 491, 496, 604, 627, 699, 758, 1060; H. iv, 2; vii, 17); there, in that place (out of sight) (u.w. vbs. of placing or the like) (Gr.Gr. 150; Gr.M.; L.V. 70, 88; Siv. 77, 120, 130, 318, 412, 674, 908, 910, 972, 1197, 1316-7, 1328, 1357, 1892; Rām. 298, 310, 363, 381, 409, 564, 582, 586-7, 641, etc.; K. 71-2, 219, 220, 223, 230-1, 235, 244, 263, 405, 411, 598, etc.; H. iv, 7; v, 7; x, 5; xii, 4, 6, 14, 16); there, under those circumstances (L.V. 41, m.c. tatē). -ōtra or --ūtra -- adv. on the day before the day before yesterday, two days before yesterday, i.e. three days ago. -ōtrukᵘ or -ūtrukᵘ adj. (f. ō(ū)trücᵘ̈ ), of, or belonging to, or produced three days ago. -ōtra-kani or -ūtra-kani adv. perhaps, probably, or about, three days ago. -ōtra-kanyukᵘ or -ūtra-kanyukᵘ adj. (f. -ō(ū)tra-kanicᵘ̈ ), of, belonging to, or produced, about three days ago. -kölⁱ-kĕth adv. on the day after the day after to-morrow, two days after to-morrow, three days hence (Gr.Gr. 157); cf. kölⁱ-kĕth, p. 434b, l. 8. -kölⁱ- kĕthukᵘ adj. (f. kölⁱ- kĕthücᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or produced, three days hence. -kölⁱ-kĕth-kani adv. perhaps, probably, or about, three days hence. -kinⁱ adv. thence, from that direction (out of sight) (u.w. vbs. of going, looking, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 158). -pĕṭha adv. from there (out of sight), thence (u.w. vbs. of coming or the like) (Gr.Gr. 155, K. 493). -yōr-kun adv. ever since then, from then up to now. ¶ tatī, see tatiy, bel. ¶ tatĕy or tatyĕy (for tati + ay 2) if there (Rām. 1547). ¶ tatiy or tatī adj. even there, in that very place (out of sight) (u.w. vbs. of placing, remaining, or the like) (Śiv. 112, tatī; 1614, tatiyĕ, m.c.; Rām. tatī, 1588, 1605, 1616; tatiy, 230, 265, 315, 335, 376, 397, 588, 642, etc.; K. tatiy, 80, 409, 774; H. id., v, 9); even then, at that very time (L.V. 104; Rām. tatiy, 144, 1752-3; K. tatiy, 217, 879); from that very place (Rām. tatiy, 575); from that very time (Rām. tatī, 1607, 1610); for that very cause (K. 618); in that very way, just so (Rām. tatiy, 910, 1256, 1634). ¶ tȧtiy adv. even there, in that very place (out of sight) (u.w. vbs. of placing or the like) (L.V. 51). ¶ totuy adv. to that very place (out of sight), even thither (u.w. vbs. of going or the like) (L.V. 47; Śiv. 675, 1101; Rām. 321, 575, 1738; K. 619); in that very place (o. of s.), even there (Gr.Gr. 156; Rām. 746, 1327). ¶ tatyukᵘ adj. (f. taticᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or produced, there (out of sight) (Gr.Gr. 150; Śiv. 1087, 1099; K. 714).
in tōv-tö m. the name used in schools for the Śāradā character equivalent to the Nāgarī letter ta.
m. Grislea tomentosa (El. táwí). Cf. thöyī.
m. an ornament worn on the head-dress by Muslim women.

or tövᵘ̈ 3 f. a frying-pan or similar cooking vessel (cf. gāḍa-tᵒ, p. 276b, l. 20; hŏkha-tᵒ, p. 327a, l. 46; tata-tövᵘ̈ and taʦi tāvi gaʦhun, p. 1039b, ll. 24, 44; tüʦᵘ̈ tövᵘ̈, p. 1040a, l. 2; ʦŏcĕ-tᵒ, s.v. ʦŏ̈ṭᵘ̈) (Rām. 723; K.Pr. 38, wrongly written thov, 91 tāv, 107 tov); met. drought (cf. hŏkha-tᵒ, as ab.); burning fever (cf. hŏkha-tᵒ, as ab.). Cf. tāv. ¶ tövⁱ-gāḍa f.pl. fish cut up into pieces and fried in deep oil, before making them into a stew; cf. tāwa-bọ̆ḍᵘ, p. 1046b, l. 46. -gāḍa-lawās or -gāḍa-lawāsa m.pl. pancakes made with pieces of this fried fish offered to a bridegroom and bride on the occasion of the Śiva-rātri festival. ¶ tāvi kaḍun m.inf. to fry pieces of fish, meat, curds, etc., in oil, as ab. --kraʦhi ladun -- m.inf. 'to raise from the griddle and hot shovel', to vituperate, abuse, curse.
m. a charm, amulet (esp. such as is worn by children and others as a protection from evil spirits) (L. 270, 458).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. tōwarôwᵘ), i.q. tōwarun, q.v. tōwarôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tōwarövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. tōworᵘ-motᵘ, q.v. s.v. tōwarun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. tōworᵘ), to make red-hot, to heat (metals) (El.); to look fiercely or threateningly (K.Pr. 26); to look obliquely, to take a sidelong look (cf. ȧchⁱ tōwarüñᵘ̈, p. 8b, l. 43; p. 116b, l. 16); cf. tōwarāwun. tōworᵘ- motᵘ perf. part. (f. tōvürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), looked at threateningly or fiercely.
adj. (fem. tövᵘ̈ 1, for 3, see tövⁱ) (of gold) alloyed with copper (this hardened alloy being used for ornaments, etc.).
adj. (f. tövᵘ̈ 2, for 3, see tövⁱ) heated, made hot, used --˚, as in aḍa-tᵒ, p. 12a, l. 29; okᵘ-tᵘ, p. 19b, l. 1.

emph. form of ta 2 (p. 961b, l. 10), then, and then, thereafter, thereupon (L.V. 9, 11, 16); then, therefore, accordingly (L.V. 24, 53); then, introducing the apodosis of a conditional sentence (L.V. 12).

m. (sg. dat. tŏyĕnas) in tŏyun tŏyun m. small scraps of cloth, paper, or the like. --tŏyun gaʦhun -- m.inf. (of a garment, cloth, paper, or the like) to be torn into scraps and scattered. --tŏyun karun -- m.inf. (as ab.) to tear into scraps and scatter abroad.

adj. c.g. fast-running, fleet; subst. m. a hunting dog, a greyhound. --hūnᵘ -- m. a greyhound. -pĕṭhⁱ kān gaʦhun m.inf. (?) 'the arrow to go over the greyhound', to succeed by accident, to achieve the results of any work without taking any trouble.
f. ability, power (to endure adversity, etc.), power of endurance (K.Pr. 13, tuṯs̱).
m. a man who is dull-witted, stupid.
m. a pond (artificial, circular in shape, and overgrown with vegetation) (cf. aza- bābunᵘ tᵒ, p. 74b, l. 7); a lake (L.V. 84).

c.g. or tragunᵘ or trĕgunᵘ (f. tra(trĕ)güñᵘ̈ ), adj. (of a string, rope, or the like) having three strands; threefold, triple, three times repeated (cf. lacha-trᵒ āy, p. 506b, l. 50) (W. 105, trèguṇ; Rām. 1767).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. trạgᵃnôwᵃ), i.q. trạgᵃnun, q.v. trạgᵃnôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. trạgᵃnövᵃ-müʦᵃ), made threefold, trebled.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. trạgᵒnᵒ), to make threefold, triplicate, multiply by three.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. traharyōv), to become alarmed, or agitated, by an ill-omen, or the like (Śiv. 1295). traharyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. traharyē-müʦᵘ̈), alarmed (as ab.).
interj. protect! save! (Borrowed from Skt., where it is a 2nd pers. sg. imperative) (Śiv. 130; Rām. 1403; K. 554, 880, 997).

(pl. dat. trailōkan) or trailōky m. the three worlds (Heaven, Earth, and Hell), the universe (Śiv. 472, trailūkh; 60, 130, 651, 731, trailōky; K. 766, trailōky). trailōkyĕ-nāth m. the Lord of the Universe, a title of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 37, 514, 979). Cf. trilōka-nāth, trizagath, and (s.v. trayĕ 3) trayĕ-lūkh.
hardness (of any substance); met. hardness (of human nature); hardness of price (of food-grains or the like). Cf. trakajyār.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. trakarôwᵘ), to harden, to cause (something soft) to become hard; to reproach abusively (one who is about to act in opposition). ¶ trakarôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. trakarövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), hardened (as ab.); reproached (as ab.). ¶ trakarāvüñᵘ̈ f.inf. looking angrily at (some person or thing, esp. when done by a person ordinarily of a gentle temper).

conj. 3 (trakaryōv 1), (of something formerly soft) to become hard; (of one formerly energetic) to become indolent, slothful. trakaryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. trakaryē-müʦᵘ̈), become hard (as ab.), become indolent (as ab.).
(sg. dat.), in byākh trākh, anyone else, someone else (p. 150a, l. 1). The word is a jingle of byākh, formed on the basis of trĕh, three, as byākh is based on bi, another.

m. (sg. dat. trakas 1. As the first member of certain compounds, this word takes the form traka or trakha. In two cases it takes the form trika, see bel.) a group of three, a triad (cf. trica); the lowest part of the backbone (where three bones are said to meet) (El. trak, trek, the back). ¶ traka-band or trakha-band m. disease of the lower part of the backbone, (?) lumbago. -phuṭᵘ or trakha-phuṭᵘ adj. (f. -phuṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. -phucĕ), one with the lower part of the backbone broken or bent, hunch-backed. ¶ trika-bāg m. that which consists of three parts, i.e. the Hindū triad of Brahmā, Vishnu (Viṣṇu), and Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 1695) (cf. trĕkāran); N. of a village in Kashmīr from which there is a view of Mount Haramŏkh (p. 343a, l. 31). It is said to be free from poisonous snakes (Śiv. 1695). -vüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -wacĕ), the connexion (by marriage) between three families (as when A gives his daughter in marriage into B's family, and B gives his daughter into C's family, the word then indicates the mutual connexion between the respective families of A, B, and C).

m. (sg. dat. trakas 2), a measure (esp. for grain) consisting in six Kāshmīrī seers, equivalent according to some to about twelve, and according to others to about nine and a half pounds (cf. lakh-trᵒ, p. 517b, l. 35; pā̃-trᵒ, p. 748a, l. 22; trȧkⁱ-trakh, col. a, l. 12) (Gr.Gr. 31, 52, 147; W. 134; Śiv. 1828; K.Pr. 42, 162, 208, 216). Cf. man 3, and, for the value of a trakh, see khār 3. --khanḍ -- m. about a trakh (W. 103). ¶ traka-bọ̆dᵘ or -bodᵘ adj. (f. -bö̆zᵘ̈ or -büzᵘ̈), (of something to the amount of which reference is made) weighing, or measuring, many trakhs (see bọ̆dᵘ 2). -phyurᵘ m. (in weighing grain trakh by trakh) the making a mistake in counting the number of trakhs (during the process of weighment). --traka -- adv. (in weighing, distributing, etc.), trakh by trakh. -wād m. (in weighing trakh by trakh) the sum of all the trakhs.

or trakurᵘ adj. (f. trakürᵘ̈ 1 or trakᵘ̈rᵘ̈), dried, hard, harsh, rough, coarse, stiff (of any thing, action, or quality) (cf. aḍa-trᵒ, p. 13b, l. 8; buthⁱ-trⁱ, p. 143a, l. 5) (Gr.Gr. 141, Gr.M.); harsh, cruel, merciless, ferocious; passionate, irascible (K.Pr. 7); dissolute (El. trakkur).
m. (sg. dat. trakanas), a weaver's shuttle.
f. a pair of scales, a balance (El. trakȧr, trakir, trakur); Libra (the sign of the Zodiac) (El. trakur, m.). ¶ trakari-ḍünḍᵘ̈ f. the beam of a pair of scales. -pôturᵘ m. a scale-pan.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. trạkᵃrôwᵃ), to elevate; lift up (e.g. a fallen post, a house which has fallen down).
or trakarun 2 conj. 3 (2 p.p. trạkᵃryōv or trakaryōv 2), to become elevated, to be raised (cf. nam trᵒ, p. 635b, l. 27, and trạkᵃrāwun).
f. a lump of earth or similar substance, a clod (cf. nūna-tᵒ, p. 641a, l. 19). trala-ha r f. a clod fight, a fight in which the opponents hurl clods at each other.

m. N. of a town about twenty miles south-east of Śrīnagar, in which there is a large colony of Sikkhs said to have been settled by Ranjit Singh. For further particulars, see El. s.v. trāla-ʦŏdāh f. (sg. dat. -ʦŏdüshᵘ̈), the fourteenth lunar day of the dark half of the month of Phāgun (Skt. Phālguna = February-March), i.e. exactly a month after the Shiwa-rāth (see p. 901b, l. 46) fast. -ʦŏdāh lagüñᵘ̈ f. violent diarrhœa to attack a person (quasi, such as is caused by indigestion experienced by greedy eaters on the expiry of the fast of the Shiwa-rāth).

f. a hole (esp. bored in a plank of wood or the like); esp. the hole in the prow of a boat into which the peg is fitted to which the tow-rope is attached. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to bore a hole. --tārun -- m.inf. to bore a hole right through a board or the like (Śiv. 1845).
m. copper (Gr.M.; L. 459, tram; Rām. 1054, 1412, 1418, 1724; K.Pr. 186). ¶ trāma-poṭᵘ m. a sheet or plate of copper. -püṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -pacĕ), id., but small in size.
three mans, or four and a half seers (see p. 572b, l. 29).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. tramanôwᵘ), to bore holes (into wood or the like). Cf. tramawun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. tramowᵘ), to bore holes through a board or the like. Cf. tramanāwun.
f. a small copper vessel (see trömⁱ); a certain disease (involving poisonous sores on the back of the hands). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. this disease to befall.
adj. (f. trāmüvᵘ̈), made of copper, copper (Rām. 565; K.Pr. 216, pl. dat. trámahwĕn for trāmarĕn).

m. protecting, preserving; defence, shelter, help, protection; (in Ksh.) strength, courage, vigour (Rām. 200, 907; YZ. 22); power, faculty, attribute, virtue, property (Rām. 1069); understanding, comprehension (= Skt. cētana) (K. 680, 682).
m.pl. 'threes' used as a multiplicative, as in trĕh trāna nav, three threes are nine (Gr.Gr. 86, W. 104).

or trĕng f. copious evacuation, diarrhœa (esp. of children) (cf. gᵃsa-tᵃ, p. 307a, l. 28). ¶ tranga f.pl. repeated diarrhœa (esp. that caused by terror or the like); met. extreme terror, extreme apprehension. --wasañĕ -- f. pl. inf. such attacks of diarrhœa to come down; hence, to experience such extreme terror or apprehension.
m. a collection, row (cf. aḍiji-trᵒ, p. 14a, l. 41).

or trangürᵘ̈ f. (in a shop or the like) a collection of small articles (salt, turmeric, and the like); a vessel used for holding all these articles; --˚ a collection or row of anything (cf. lari-trᵒ, p. 531b, l. 11; tōl-trᵒ, p. 999b, l. 3). trạngᵃri-wôñᵃ m. a travelling pedlar (who sells such small articles).
m. ophthalmia (El. trápajár); fierceness, eager violence (Rām. 602).

m. compression into a narrow space; the sensation of oppressive and suffocating heat engendered by the ab.; cf. trapun. -tṻrun m.inf. oppressive heat and chill, i.e. the beginning of an attack of fever (marked by a feeling of internal heat, accompanied by external chill). Cf. trūrᵘ. ¶ trapa-traph f. (sg. dat. trapa-trapi. For gender, see Gr.Gr. 75), mutual oppressive crowding (as when a number of people are crowded into too small a space).

or trĕphᵃth adj. c.g. satiated, satisfied, content (El. traft, full); cf. trupti. traphᵃth gaʦhun m.inf. to become satisfied or satiated (of someone hungry, poverty-stricken, or the like) (Śiv. trĕ˚, 386, 1073; Rām. 1108b). --karun -- m.inf. to satiate, satisfy (Śiv. trĕ˚, 1678).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. tropᵘ), to crowd (articles or persons) into a narrow space, to cram in; to shut tightly, close, cover up tightly (cf. darwāza tᵒ, p. 250b, l. 45) (Rām. 23; H. viii, 3, 11). ¶ trȧpⁱ trȧpⁱ thawun m.inf. forcibly to keep on cramming (things into a confined space) till there is no more room whatever. ¶ tropᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. trüpᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), crammed in; closed tightly, tightly covered.

m. fear, terror (e.g. caused by an enemy's attack, or by the appearance of an epidemic). --karun -- m.inf. to put fear (into a person), to thunder abuse (e.g. at a servant guilty of some fault) (Śiv. 593, 1461).

onomat. m. the sound of breaking or falling of some large hard object, such as a great tree, a wooden pillar, or the like, 'crash'; cf. trᵃs, tris. --milawun -- m.inf. to cause to fall, or cut down, with a crash.

f. an instrument for cutting, a knife, scissors (cf. jigar-tᵒ, p. 371b, l. 48; kalam-tᵒ, p. 439b, l. 47) (Rām. 1268, 1539); a piece cut off, a cutting. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- or --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cut off the edges of anything (such as paper, cloth, or the like), to trim.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. trasyōv), to become afraid or alarmed (at some terrifying sight), to fear; cf. traʦun, and tarsun. trasyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. trasyē-müʦᵘ̈), overwhelmed with fear, as ab.
conj 1 (1 p.p. trạsᵃrôwᵃ), to cause to fear, terrify (by some terrifying spectacle) (Gr.Gr. 7). trạsᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. trạsᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), terrified, as ab.

f. (sg. dat. traṭi 2, for 1, see trọ̆ṭᵘ), lightning, a thunderbolt (cf. hĕnga-tᵒ (met.), p. 339a, l. 49; naba-tᵒ, p. 619a, l. 22; nȧbⁱ-tⁱ, ib., l. 34; nāra-tᵒ, p. 648a, l. 42; pā̃-tᵒ, p. 748a, l. 25; rūda-tᵒ, p. 826b, l. 11) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1558, Rām. 458, K. 110, K.Pr. 253); a meteorite (El.). Note that hār-tᵒ, N. of a place (p. 344a, l. 19), is m., while, when it means 'lightning in the month of Hār' (ib. l. 21), it is f.
in trāwa-trāv m. (of some vessel) brimful (El. tráwa-tráwa; Śiv. 520, 1802).
f. the act of depositing (and leaving there), the act of abandoning (cf. tula-trāv, p. 1000a, l. 36). See trāwun.
m. leaving, letting go, abandoning; emission, pouring forth; scattering (cf. dȧlⁱ-tⁱ, p. 212a, l. 3). This word is the abs. noun of trāwun (q.v.) in all its meanings.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. trāwanôwᵘ), to cause to let go, or to cause to be let go (El.). Causal of trāwun (q.v.) in all its meanings (Śiv. 1849, cause to put forth; 1896, cause to abandon).
n.ag. (f. trāwavüñᵘ̈), one who lets go, etc. (in all the meanings of the verb trāwun, q.v.) (cf. nār-tᵒ, an incendiary, p. 647a, l. 22) (Śiv. 861, betake oneself to (rest)).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. trôwᵘ), to let go, let loose, loose, let go hold of, release (cf. atha tᵒ, p. 63b, l. 15; mŏṭh trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 604a, l. 44) (Gr.M.; L.V. 70, 88; Śiv. 1565; Rām. 808; K. 162; H. iii, 4; x, 5, 12); to set free, release, liberate (cf. dã̄d trāwȧnⁱ, p. 187a, l. 19; phrith tᵒ, p. 709b, l. 49) (Rām. 1322; K. 560, 564, 566, 664); to unharness, set free (harnessed horses, etc.) (Śiv. 1699); to leave (a limb or the like) loose, to let (it) hang comfortably (K. 972); to leave (e.g. space between lines) (Gr.M.); to spare, forgive (a sin, etc.), pardon, let off, discharge (a person), acquit (a person under trial) (Śiv. 425); to leave, let alone, leave alone (cf. kañi-küñᵘ̈ tᵒ, p. 461b, l. 11); ¶ to leave, quit (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 57; YZ. 218, 232); to leave behind (at death) (Gr.M., Rām. 260); to forsake, abandon, desert (cf. dolᵘ dᵃnith tᵒ, p. 211b, l. 40); path tᵒ, p. 792b, l. 1) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 452, 513, 554, 557, 572, 585, 1445, 1450, 1543, 1624, 1635, 1851, 1901, 1909; Rām. 385-6, 394-5, 427, 529, 612, 625, 757, 767, etc.; K. 265, 281, 290, 417, 860-1; YZ. 139, 151); to relinquish, resign, renounce, give up (Gr.M.; L.V. 27, 30; Śiv. 553, 576, 583, 884, 890, 893, 898, 973, 1021, 1057, 1271, 1352, 1545, 1757, 1815; Rām. 8, 31, 45, 52, 178-9, 211, 322, 453, 555, 657, etc.; K. 500, 505, 672, 869, 1029; H. ii, 10; xi, 11; YZ. 236, 238, 515; K.Pr. 46); to abstain from (Śiv. 786, 992, 1539); to get rid of (cf. mal tᵒ, p. 564a, l. 28; phrakh tᵒ, p. 704a, l. 35; ṭhū̃kᵘ tᵒ, p. 972b, l. 24) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1017, 1246, 1435, 1810); to divorce (El., Rām. 328); to rid (cf. mĕʦi murⁱ trāwȧnⁱ, p. 608b, l. 41); to complete and leave finished, to leave after completion, to complete entirely (cf. chŏkh tᵒ, p. 159b, l. 10; ciṭha tᵒ, p. 177b, l. 38) (Śiv. 1235); to perform, carry out, complete (cf. khāka tᵒ, p. 395a, l. 48); to leave (it, after passing along it), to traverse completely (a road or the like) (L.V. 82); to put or lay aside; to put down, place, deposit (Śiv. 1475, 1516); ¶ to discharge, shoot, fire (an arrow, gun, etc.) (cf. tōph trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 1015b, l. 27; tīr tᵒ, p. 1019a, l. 8) (Gr.M.; Rām. 117, 123, 867, 1271); ¶ to take to, put on, or adopt (a course of conduct), perform (cf. ḍã̄b tᵒ, p. 182a, l. 17; ḍocᵘ tᵒ, p. 185a, l. 50; ḍŏcurᵘ trövith bĕhun, p. 186b, l. 38; ḍula tᵒ, p. 212a, l. 29; ḍulagunᵘ tᵒ, p. 213a, l. 27; ḍāph tᵒ, p. 232b, l. 5; ḍēra tᵒ, p. 236b, l. 30; gēra tᵒ, p. 296b, l. 37; lam-lisar tᵒ, p. 524a, l. 24; lisar tᵒ, p. 534b, l. 29) (Śiv. 1811, 1834-5; K. 995); to carry out, carry on, do some action (cf. dōr trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 237a, l. 10; khᵃr trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 406b, l. 42; lö̃pa trāwañĕ, p. 528b, l. 45; rav tᵒ, p. 852a, l. 39; shŏy tᵒ, p. 903a, l. 3; thāh trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 971b, l. 28; tĕharyau-pĕṭhⁱ wŏṭa trāwañĕ, p. 983b, l. 49; ṭᵃkh trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 991b, l. 20) (Śiv. 410; Rām. 1756; K. 825); to bring into action, employ (a limb of the body, or some instrument) (cf. kọ̆ṭhᵘ tᵒ, p. 489a, l. 15; kŏra tᵒ, p. 466b, l. 8; lar trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 529b, l. 10; mŏhar tᵒ, p. 556a, l. 14; nār tᵒ, p. 647a, l. 24; patang tᵒ, p. 802a, l. 27) (Gr.M., Śiv. 506); ¶ to take to (rest, sleep, or the like) (cf. nẹ̆ndᵃr trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 642b, l. 44; shŏng trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 885b, l. 14 (Śiv. 1702, 1826; H. iii, 3, 7; viii, 5); ¶ to emit, give forth, pour forth, eject (cf. bākh trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 99a, l. 47; ḍĕkⁱ sᵃs trāwȧnⁱ, p. 204b, l. 46; khᵃr tᵒ, p. 406b, l. 29; lahar trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 516a, l. 50; marʦa-pŏnda trāwañĕ, p. 594b, l. 20; phakh tᵒ, p. 689a, l. 6; phukār trāwȧnⁱ, p. 691a, l. 7; pharyād tᵒ, p. 711a, l. 3; pŏnd trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 739a, l. 35; pọ̆sᵘ tᵒ, p. 777a, l. 25; rās tᵒ, p. 842a, l. 49; thŏka trāwañĕ, p. 973a, l. 29; ṭās tᵒ, p. 1037a, l. 1; ʦũ̄̈ṭh trāvüñᵘ̈) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 905, 1389; Rām. 295, 1386, 1636; K. 38, 90, 502, 926, 936, 984-5, 987-8, 1047; H. i, 5; xii, 2, 12; YZ. 19, 33, 130, 440, 484; K.Pr. 31, 124, 166, 216); to pour out, pour forth, spill (cf. oshᵘ tᵒ, p. 47b, l. 22; grŏkh tᵒ, p. 302a, l. 29; phukār tᵒ, p. 691a, l. 9; phyār tᵒ, p. 721b, l. 5) (Śiv. 1250, 1252, 1255, 1551, 1688, 1893, 1910; Rām. 1222, 1433, 1618; K. 162; H. v, 4); to lay (eggs) (cf. ṭhūl trāwȧnⁱ, p. 976a, l. 44) (W. 144; K.Pr. 120, 163); to keep pouring forth, to do something persistently (cf. chŏkañ trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 160a, l. 34; ḍŏcurᵘ tᵒ, p. 186b, l. 40; ḍuṭhay trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 258b, l. 2; nāla trāwañĕ, p. 683a, l. 45) (Rām. 242, 292, 376, 875, 893, 1551); ¶ to cast, throw, cast down (cf. cīrⁱ trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 174b, l. 31; pashĕ-pĕṭhⁱ shīn trāwun, p. 777b, l. 8) (Śiv. 1015; Rām. 358, 426, 480, 485, 914, 929, 947, 1368; K. 124, 450, 595; H. viii, 7; xii, 11, 16, 17); to throw away (K.Pr. 64); to throw forth, put forth, thrust forth (cf. kadam tᵒ, p. 385b, l. 7; nazar trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 676a, l. 30; pūrⁱ trāwȧnⁱ, p. 755a, l. 13; ṭôkᵘ tᵒ, p. 991a, l. 28) (Śiv. 17, 496, 509, 514, 902, 918, 958, 1034, 1088, 1099, 1820, 1878; Rām. 370, 711, 1287, 1294, 1371; H. iv, 5; YZ. 32, 224); to spread out, lay out (cf. sᵃthᵃr trāwun, p. 947b, l. 15); dȧlⁱ trāwȧnⁱ, m. pl. inf. to throw out the skirts (from the body), i.e. to sit with bended knees (L.V. 49); but cf. dȧlⁱ-trôwⁱ, p. 1033a, l. 22; to strew, scatter, spread abroad (cf. dāba tᵒ, p. 182a, l. 24; pāh trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 683b, l. 37; phukⁱ trāwȧnⁱ, p. 688b, l. 35; phᵃr tᵒ, p. 701a, l. 8; phë̆ṭᵘ̈ trāvüñᵘ̈, p. 715a, l. 31; ṭasōla tᵒ, p. 1038a, l. 22) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 125; YZ. 10, 168); ¶ to doff, put off (clothes, ornaments, etc.) (cf. pŏshākh tᵒ, p. 780b, l. 39) (Śiv. 1725; Rām. 201, 274, 654, 828, 990, 1467, 1576, 1634; H. v, 9; x, 2; xii, 6, 7); ¶ This verb is commonly used with the conjunctive participate of another verb to form an intensive compound, as in bakith tᵒ, p. 102a, l. 22; cīrith tᵒ, to wring out (water from a cloth), Gr.M.; chala karith tᵒ, p. 161a, l. 9; dali dᵃnith tᵒ, p. 212a, l. 10; dᵃnith tᵒ, p. 228a, l. 16; dasith tᵒ, p. 255b, l. 32; lath dith tᵒ, p. 536b, l. 22; tŏh karith tᵒ, p. 970a, l. 7; tᵃʦha karith tᵒ, s.v. tᵃʦh; ʦaṭith tᵒ, s.v. ʦaṭun) (Śiv. 23, 353, 1666; Rām. 1310; H. ii, 5; x, 7, 8). ¶ trôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. trövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), let go, abandoned, etc., as ab. (cf. kövⁱ tᵒ, p. 495a, l. 45); laid (of an egg) (K.Pr. 163). ¶ trövith, conj. part. having abandoned, etc.; hence, used as an adverb, save, except, putting (such and such) out of consideration (K. 1054). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to abandon and depart; met. to abandon one's possessions to heirs and depart; hence, to die. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to throw away (El., Gr.M.); to give up, abandon (any work).

or trĕy 1 f. (sg. dat. tra(trĕ)yĕ 1 , for 2, see trĕh 1, for trayĕ 3, see s.v.), the third lunar day of a lunar fortnight (cf. achin-tᵒ, p. 9b, l. 1; gōra-tᵒ, p. 305b, l. 17; nawa- rĕh tᵒ, p. 665a, l. 6; sō̃ta-tᵒ, p. 947a, l. 3) (Rām. 1767); esp. the third lunar day of the nawa-rĕh festival (see p. 665a, l. 6) (L. 265, treh). trayĕ-hondᵘ or trĕyĕ-hondᵘ gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, belonging to, produced on, or begun on the third lunar day.

f. the inner nature (of any person or thing) (Śiv. 1239, 1622); favouring, assistance, partizanship (cf. rāyĕ-trāyĕ, p. 854b, l. 25). --wuchüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to inspect the inner nature, to test the inmost character (of any person or thing). ¶ trāyĕ tōlun m.inf. to weight out over and above the fixed amount (Śiv. 1476). Cf. tarawun.

i.q. trĕh 1, q.v., in the following:-- trayĕ-gŏn m. the three qualities (Śiv. 237, 514; cf. trĕ-gŏn). -lūkh m. the three worlds taken collectively (Śiv. 957); cf. trailūkh, trizagath. --lōʦan m. he who has three eyes, N. of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 1044), i.q. trilōʦan, q.v.
or trĕyĕshīth card. eighty-three (Gr.Gr. 79, El. trȧshīt).
or trĕyĕ˚ ord. (f. tra(trĕ)yĕshītimᵘ̈ ), eighty-third (Gr.Gr. 79, El. trȧshityum).
or trĕyĕ˚ adj. (f. tra(trĕ)yĕshītiñᵘ̈ ), costing, or worth, eighty-three (rupees, etc.); earning wages of eighty-three (rupees, etc.).
card. thirteen (Śiv. 524, Rām. 1771). This is the borrowed Skt. word trayōdaśa; the Ksh. word is truwāh 1, q.v.

trĕyumᵘ or triyumᵘ ord. (f. tra(trĕ, tri)yimᵘ̈ ), third (Gr.Gr. 76; Śiv. 863, tri˚; Rām. trĕ˚, 84, 180, 381, 385, 466, 1051, 1139, 1151, 1205, 1259-60, 1277, 1564, 1716; K. tra˚, 1145-6; trĕ˚, 27; H. trĕ˚, viii, 7, 8; xii, 19; YZ. 14, 104; K.Pr. 70). trayimi or trȧyⁱmi adv. for the third time.

conj. 2 or 3 (1 p.p. troʦᵘ; 2 p.p. traʦyōv), to fear, be afraid, terrified (esp. when caused by some formidable sight) (Gr.Gr. 226). Cf. trasun and tarsun. ¶ troʦᵘ-motᵘ 1 p.p. (f. trüʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), terrified, as ab. ¶ traʦyō-motᵘ 2 p.p. (f. traʦyē-müʦᵘ̈), terrified as ab. into a swoon.
