conj. 1 (1 p.p. trạʦᵃrôwᵃ), to terrify, fill with fear, cause to be afraid (esp. by displaying some formidable spectacle) (Gr.Gr. 7). trạʦᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. trạʦᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), caused to be terrified.
m.pl. the three guṇas, qualities, or constituents of existing things, viz. goodness, passion, and darkness (see p. 857b, l. 35) (Śiv. 1643, Rām. 1774). See trayĕ-gŏn, s.v. trayĕ 3.

sometimes written trĕ, try, or trih card. (pl. dat. trĕn; pl. abl. trĕyau, Gr.Gr. 82. In composition, this word takes the form trᵃ, tra, trĕ, or tri, as in tra-man, p. 572b, l. 29; trᵃbāra or tribāra, p. 1021b, l. 6; trĕgunᵘ, p. 1021b, l. 40. In various idiomatic uses (see bel.) it is treated as a singular, in agreement with a singular noun, and then takes the form trayĕ 1 or trĕyĕ 1. For trayĕ 2, trĕyĕ 2, see tray, for trayĕ 3, see s.v.); ¶ three (Gr.Gr. 76, 82, 86, 154; Gr.M.; L.V. (in the old Ksh. form trᵃh) 16, 75; Śiv. 118, 159, 196, 779, 978, 1521, etc.; Rām. 797, 1774; K. 384, 688, 795; H. x, 1, 12, 20; xii, 5, 6, 11, 19; YZ. (trah) 112). Cf. trayĕ 3. ¶ In Śaivism, there are three impurities (mala) of the soul, which impede its final release (L.V. 75). These are called in Skt. āṇava, māyīya, and kārma. The first is the state or character of the soul deeming itself to be finite; the second is that born of cosmic illusion; and the third is the impurity that results from action (see L.V. s.v. trᵃh). There are also three worlds (heaven, earth, and hell) (cf. Śiv. as ab. and trĕbuwan); and three qualities (gŏn) (see trĕ-gŏn). ¶ trayĕ 1 (for 2, see tray, for 3, see s.v.), adv. thrice, three times, on three occasions (K. 136); cf. trĕyĕ, bel. -manza sg. abl. (one, etc.) from among, or out of, three (K. 1022). -phiri adv. on three occasions, three times, thrice (K. 63). Cf. trĕyĕ-phᵒ, bel. ¶ trĕy card. only three, exactly three. Cf. triy 1, bel. ¶ trĕyĕ 1 or trĕyi (for trĕyĕ 2, see tray) in trĕyĕ (or trĕyi) ali kaḍun  m.inf. to drag (i.e. plough) with three-plough, i.e. to plough three times (esp. with ref. to a bean-field or the like being prepared for sowing). --laṭi -- adv. three times, thrice. -nĕngi adv., id. --phiri -- adv., id.; cf. trayĕ-phᵒ, ab. --ranga -- adj. c.g. of three kinds (cf. trĕyi- ranga, p. 836b, l. 44) (Gr.Gr. 154). --vizi -- adv. three times, thrice. ¶ triy 1 (for 2, see s.v.) only three, exactly three (Gr.Gr. 82). Cf. trĕy, ab.
m.pl. the three causes, the Hindū triad of deities,--Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva,--the respective causes of the creation, preservation, and destruction of the universe (Śiv. 99; Rām. 1061, 1715).
(for 2, see trēkyunᵘ) f. a scale-weight for weighing one trakh (see trakh 2), a trakh-weight. Cf. the next.

adj. (f. trēkiñᵘ̈ 2, for 1, see s.v.), of the weight or measure of one trakh (see trakh 2), (of some one thing) weighing a trakh; (of a vessel) having a contents of one measured trakh. Cf. trökyunᵘ 2.

f. an apple (cf. ambȧrⁱ-tⁱ, p. 27b, l. 5; batpurī-tᵒ, p. 145a, l. 32; khar-tᵒ, p. 407a, l. 36; nābȧdⁱ-tⁱ, p. 620a, l. 1; sil-tᵒ, p. 909a, l. 25 (L. 349)). ¶ trēla-kujⁱ or -kujᵘ̈ f. a small apple-tree. -kulᵘ m. a kind of apple-tree (El.). -mŏrba m. apple-jam.
or (q.v.) trĕshĕway card. emph. even all three (Gr.Gr. 85; Śiv. 1168 (dat. trinawȧnⁱ); Rām. 201, 1565; H. xii, 25).
(? spelling and gend.) a certain food plant eaten in time of famine (L. 71).

(by Paṇḍits also written) f. (or, according to some, m.) thirst (cf. achĕn-tᵒ, p. 9a, l. 17; kakav-tᵒ, p. 433a, l. 9; nūna-tᵒ, p. 641a, ll. 20, 25) (El. m.; Gr.Gr. 136, m.; Gr.M.; L.V. 37; K. 1092; K.Pr. 63); strong desire, greed, avidity, covetousness (Gr.M.); drinking-water (for quenching thirst) (cf. phŏṭⁱ-tⁱ or phȧṭⁱ-tⁱ, p. 715b, l. 43; shō̃ṭh-tᵒ, p. 899b, l. 34) (Śiv. 342; Rām. 235-6, 1174, 1393-5, 1439; K. 230, 702; H. viii, 7; K.Pr. 155); any liquid for drinking (Rām. 398); water poured in libations to ancestors (cf. pŏtra-tᵒ, p. 799b, l. 38); soil that will not hold irrigation water (L. 321); cf. trĕshnā. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. thirst to be experienced, to be thirsty (with dat. of person thirsty) (El. m.inf.; K. 835; H. viii, 7). --wēsh -- f. thirst (a jingle of trēsh) (El., who makes the word m., but we should expect it to be f.). ¶ trēshĕ-hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), smitten by thirst, thirsty (cf. shurāh-yāra trēshĕ-hotᵘ anun, p. 891b, l. 27) (Gr.Gr. 136; W. 113; Śiv. 1559, 1585; YZ. 406, 411). trēshĕ- kulᵘ m. a tree of libations, i.e. a son (who offers libations for deceased ancestors). trēshĕ trēshĕ karān gaʦhun m.inf. to die without male descendant (who can offer libations for one's benefit).
or (q.v.) trĕnaway card. emph. even all three (Gr.Gr. 85; Śiv. 64 (trᵃsh˚), 977, 1168 (dat. trĕshĕwȧnⁱ), 1529; K. 1031, trashĕway; K.Pr. 142).
or trushnā or, as written by Paṇḍits, f. (the Skt. form of trēsh, q.v.), thirst (Śiv. 1584); greed, avarice (Gr.M.; Śiv. 341, 754, 1237, 1313, 1559, 1755, 1815).
trĕyĕ, trĕyau, see trĕh 1 and tray.
(? spelling) m. matting (El., who says that it is used towards Bārāmūla). Cf. patᵘ̈jᵘ̈ and wagowᵘ.
m. a nominal coin now worth three times eight cowries, i.e. 24 cowries. Cf. bahāgañ and bahāgoñunᵘ.

m. the three worlds (earth, heaven, and hell) (Śiv. 99, 898, 1623; Rām. 1334; K. 134, 361, 1041). ¶ tribuwana-nāth  m. the Lord of the three worlds, a title of the god Shiv (Skt. Śiva) (Śiv. 320). -rāza m., id. (Śiv. 1133, 1363). -sār m. the Essence of the three worlds (another title of Shiv) (Śiv. 37, 62, 91, 178, 180, 412, 514, 850, 942, 1799); applied to the gods generally (or possibly pluralis majestatis) (Śiv. 395).
m. a group of three, a triad, trio (Gr.Gr. 82). Cf. trakh 1 and trila.
or truchĕr m. sharpness, sharp-wittedness, acuteness (Gr.Gr. 30, 140). Cf. trukhᵘ.
adj. c.g. possessing the three qualities (see the preceding) (Śiv. 367, 846, 1119).
m. (of a tree) having a triple stem ascending from one trunk, three stemmed; (of a pillar or the like) branching into three.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. triköshⁱladiñ), one who fasts (religiously), or goes without food (owing to want, illness, or the like), for three days (see köshⁱlad, p. 481a, l. 3).
card. thirty millions, three crores. There are said to be this number of gods (Śiv. 433, 635, 698, 719, 723, 1520; Rām. 68, 88, 1054).
m. a group of three, a triad, trio (Gr.Gr. 82). Cf. trica and trakh 1.
m. the Lord of the three worlds (Heaven, Earth, and Hell), a title of Shiv (Śiva) (i.q. trailōkyĕ-nāth, ab.) (Śiv. 387). Cf. trizagath.
m., id. (Śiv. 832). The Skt. form of this word is Trilōkêśvara.
m. He who has three eyes, a title of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 363, 976, 1345). Cf. trinētr.

adj. (f. trimüñᵘ̈), weighing or measuring three mans of one and a half seers (or three pounds) each (see man 3); as subst. a vessel containing, or suitable for measuring, this amount; a weight (of stone or iron) for weighing this amount. Cf. tra-man.
m. He who possesses three eyes, a title of Shiv (Śiva) (the three eyes being respectively the sun, the moon, and fire) (Śiv. 153, 514). Cf. trilōʦan.
m. the figure '3', the written sign for the numeral three.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. trinyōv), to be, or become, prosperous in having many sons, grandsons, etc., to be blessed with many descendants. trinyō-motᵘ  perf. part. (trinyē-müʦᵘ̈), become prosperous (as ab.).
a medicine composed of the three myrobalans, Terminalia chebula, T. bellerica, and Phyllanthus emblica.
adj. c.g. (of a mattock, hoe, spade, knife, or the like) possessing three blades.
m. he who is the three Pushkaras (Pushkara, being the name of three different places of pilgrimage), a title of Shiv (Śiva) (Skt. tripuṣkara) (Śiv. 1172).

onomat. m. 'snap', 'crack' (cf. trᵃs and trās 2), used in the following:-- tris gaʦhun m.inf. the sound caused by breaking, felling, or striking such things as a dried branch, a piece of wood, or the shoulder-blade to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to make this sound (e.g. by tearing a dried branch off a tree). --milawun -- m.inf. breaking, etc., with such a sound to occur.
f. the old N. of a sacred spring in Kashmīr, the modern Sŏnda-brörᵘ̈ (q.v., p. 918b, l. 32) (RT.Tr. 469, Śiv. 1496).

or trᵃsh f. a small piece of dry wood, a thin twig or splinter of dry wood (such as might be used for fuel), a fire-stick (cf. lᵃsh-trᵃsh or lish-trish, p. 533a, l. 45) (El. trushi, Gr.M.). trishĕ-hürᵘ̈ f. a small chip of such wood.
or (El.) trashūl m. a trident (Śiv. 620). trishūla-dar  m. the Trident-bearer, a title of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 1171).

a woman, a female (as distinguished from a male of man or beast) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 957, 974, 1044, 1103, 1345, 1436, 1822; Rām. 624, 773, 848, 1151, 1238, 1575, 1767; K. 52, 273, 288, 435, 617, 986); a wife (El. tréí, trí; Śiv. 339, 711, 1438; Rām. 81, 1260, 1641, 1643, 1652, 1686; K. 48, 744, 918, 946, 1107). ¶ triyĕ-bāv m. woman's nature, womanhood (Śiv. 960, 1130; Rām. 629; K. 747, 1105); effeminacy. --karañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to marry wives, i.e. to marry many wives, to have a large seraglio (K. 132). ¶ trī-warna f. an individual of the woman kind, a woman (with all the characteristics of a woman) (Rām. 1051).

m. the three worlds (Heaven, Earth, and Hell). This is the Skt. word trijagat, borrowed. Cf. trailūkh, and (p. 1035a, l. 45) trayĕ-lūkh. -mātā f. a title of Pārvatī, the Śakti, or Energic Power, of Shiv (Śiva), personified as his wife, also called Shiwā (Skt. Śivā) (Śiv. 1138). ¶ trizagat-pāl m. (borrowed from Skt. trijagatpāla), the protector of the three worlds, a title of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 179, 266, 965, 1221, 1254, 1321, 1697); a title of Vishnu (Śiv. 1381, 1436). Cf. trilōka-nāth.
(for 2, see trökyunᵘ 2) f. a stone or iron weight (for weighing) equivalent to one trakh (see trakh 2). Cf. ab. and trökyunᵘ 1.
m. (sg. dat. trökinis), a vessel of which the content is one measured trakh.
adj. (f. trökiñᵘ̈ 2 for 1, see s.v.) (of some single object) weighing one trakh (see trakh 2) (Gr.Gr. 147); (of some vessel) measuring or holding a trakh (Gr.Gr. 147). Cf. trēkyunᵘ.

adj. (f. trücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, so many trakhs (see trakh 2), used --˚ (cf. aiṭha-trᵒ, p. 66b, l. 45; daha-trᵒ, p. 199a, l. 20; pönʦa-trᵒ, p. 743b, l. 4; shĕ-trᵒ, p. 874a, l. 23) (K.Pr. 162). ¶ trȧkⁱ traka adv. trakh by trakh (each trakh being about six seers of about two pounds each). -trakh m. a full trakh (not under weight).
adj. (f. tröjᵘ̈), ugly, misshapen, disfigured, deformed.
adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, or produced in Trāl (q.v.).
m. N. of a certain food-grain, buckwheat (cf. ʦṻna-trᵒ, s.v. ʦṻn) (El. trúmba, Fagopyrum esculentum; L. 76, 330, 338, trumbá).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. trŏmbowᵘ), to prick (with a needle); cf. trŏmbun. trŏmbowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. trŏmbüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), pricked (as ab.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. trọ̆mbᵘ), to prick with a needle; cf. trŏmbawun. trọ̆mbᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. trö̆mbᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), pricked (with a needle).
f. a circle (of people). -- karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to sit in a circle, to form a circle of seated persons.

m. a needle-prick, used in the following:--trŏmbⁱ dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to prick (holes, e.g. in the tough skin of a fruit). trŏmbⁱ tārȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to prick holes at a distance from each other in the skin of the egg-plant fruit or similar fruit preparatory to cooking. Cf. trusᵘ.

or trömᵘ̈ f. a copper dish (used only by Musalmāns) out of which food is eaten (El. trām, 'it corresponds to the thāl of the Hindū'; H. iii, 1; viii, 3, 11); cf. thāl. trāmi-bata m. (at wedding feasts or the like) the food contained, or served, in copper vessels for the Musalmān guests.

m. a bundle or collection of rags (esp. bits of old worn-out clothes). Cf. trongᵘ and zacĕ-trᵒ, s.v. züṭᵘ̈. ¶ trŏngⁱ wālȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to wear (clothes, etc.), to rags. --wasȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. (of clothes) to become very ragged, to be a mere collection of rags.
m. a kind of pocket-cloth, a cloth (usually an old worn rag) in which various articles are knotted separately. Cf. trọ̆ngᵘ.

m. a dark hole or chasm (in the ground); a dark recess or closet (in a house or the like) (cf. hēri-trᵒ, p. 345b, l. 16); in daba-tronᵘ, p. 181b, l. 32, tronᵘ is apparently confounded with tryūnᵘ, q.v.
adj. c.g. sewed, stitched (cf. barma-tᵒ, p. 123b, l. 15).
f. N. of a certain medicinal plant (described as somewhat poisonous and having very bitter leaves).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. trọ̆pᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. trọ̆pᵃrun, q.v. to cover tightly, obstruct, shut (Śiv. 1703). trọ̆pᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. trọ̆pᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. trọ̆pᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, s.v. trọ̆pᵃrun. trọ̆pᵃrövith thawun m.inf. i.q. trọ̆pᵃrith thawun, s.v. trọ̆pᵃrun.

trŏparun, or trupurun conj. 1. (1 p.p. trọ̆pᵒrᵒ or trupurᵘ), to cover tightly, obstruct (e.g. by hanging a curtain over a window), to shut an orifice by covering it (cf. dārĕ trọ̆pᵃrȧnᵃ, p. 238a, ll. 44, 48; lᵃyĕ trọ̆pᵃrañĕ, p. 542b, l. 40) (L.V. 101); to close tightly any opening (cf. ȧchⁱ trọ̆parañĕ, p. 8b, l. 40) (Rām. 1769). Cf. trapun. ¶ trọ̆pᵒrᵒ-motᵒ or trupurᵘ- perf. part. (f. trọ̆pᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ or trupurᵘ̈-), covered, shut tightly, as ab. trọ̆pᵃrith thawun m.inf. to shut up or cover tightly (a door, window, etc.).

m. sewing, stitching (cf. barma-tᵒ, p. 123b, l. 11; kanjĕ-tᵒ, p. 455b, l. 32; mū̃ṭhⁱ-tⁱ, p. 605a, l. 20; māwȧlⁱ-tⁱ, p. 611b, l. 27). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to sew, to stitch (with dat.). ¶ trŏpⁱ kaḍȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to sew in a particular way, to quilt, sewing together two layers of cloth with cotton between.
f. a crowding together in a confined space, a cramming together, used --˚ lari-tᵒ, p. 531b, l. 13. Cf. trapun and the next.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. trōryōv), (of a sore or wound) to dry up, form a scab (cf. krôrᵘ). trōryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. trōryē-müʦᵘ̈), become dry, as ab.

or m. hardness, harshness, roughness (esp. of something once soft and tender, but become dry) (cf. atha tᵒ, p. 63b, l. 12); irascibility of temper (cf. atha-tᵒ, as ab.); conjunctivitis, ophthalmia (El. trŏshĕr, trŏshur).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. trŏshyōv), (of something soft or tender) to become rough, hard. trŏshyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. trŏshyē-müʦᵘ̈), become rough or hard, as ab.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. trọ̆shᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), to make (something soft or tender) rough or hard (Gr.Gr. 7).

adj. (f. trö̆shᵘ̈), hard, rough (e.g. as wood or the like) (cf. aḍa-tᵒ, p. 12a, l. 26; atha-tᵒ, p. 63b, l. 10; tala-tᵒ, p. 996b, l. 7); passionate, irascible (esp. only so externally, but inwardly mild-tempered) (K.Pr. 216).

or troṭᵘ m. (sg. abl. traṭi 1, for 2, see traṭh), a necklace of several strands, and adorned with moonshaped gold beads (cf. māla-tᵒ, p. 565a, l. 44; rachi-tᵒ, p. 824b, l. 10) (El. trauṭh, ṭruṭ; Śiv. 1557; Rām. 512; K. 85; H. xii, 5; YZ. 374 (ṭroṭ)).
in trowa-nĕnd (L. 463, trowanind), f. the fourth and last weeding of a rice crop. Perhaps trowa is incorrect for trāwa; cf. trāwun. See nĕnd 2.

1 p.p. of trāwun, q.v. (f. trövᵘ̈), used --˚ in such compounds as atha-trôwᵘ, free-handed, liberal (p. 63b, l. 14); dȧlⁱ-tⁱ, loose-skirted, wasteful, extravagant, uneconomical (the skirt being used for holding things) (p. 211b, l. 50).
f. a footpath (for a single person to walk on). trŏyĕ trŏyĕ phērun m.inf. strolling about in lanes (without object, or for passing the time).
(? spelling) m. balsam (Balsamina impatiens) (El.). Cf. tatūre, and (?) the preceding.
m. (sg. dat. trukas), the act of crunching with the teeth (cf. trukun) (Gr.Gr. 122).

or tryukhᵘ adj. (f. truchᵘ̈ or (Gr.Gr. 72) trichᵘ̈), quick, clever, ingenious, acute, sharp-witted, intelligent (El. truk; Gr.Gr. 30, 72, 140, tryukhᵘ; Gr.M.; K.Pr. truk, 76, 146, 160, 216). Cf. tryukhᵘ.
in trū̃khᵘ dyunᵘ m.inf. to stir up, instigate, stimulate (esp. to arouse or stir up again some anger that had subsided).

f. the act of crunching up hard food (such as grain) between the teeth, chewing, mastication (Gr.Gr. 120). trukiñĕ-pholᵘ m. 'crunch-grain', grām, pease, or other such hard grain that, when eaten, is crunched between the teeth.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. trukᵘ, f. trucᵘ̈; 2 p.p. trucyōv), to crunch (something hard, such as grām or other grain) between the teeth, to chew, masticate (Gr.Gr. 120, 122); to gnaw or cut (like a rat) (cf. borᵘ trᵒ, p. 118a, l. 20); cf. ṭukun and trukᵘ. trukᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. trucᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), crunched with the teeth, as ab.; gnawed or cut, as ab.
m. the noise of chewing or gnawing hard or dry food, the sound of a crunch (cf. aḍa-trᵒ, p. 12a, l. 23); cf. trukun and ṭukh. --trukᵘ -- m. crunching, a sound of repeated crunches.
N. of a certain poisonous plant, Impatiens Roylei (L. 76). ? Cf. the next.
m. (sg. abl. trōli), weariness, or exhaustion, caused by excessive exertion or labour.
m. a kind of lute with wire strings.
m. (sg. dat. trunāwartas), 'the whirler of straws', N. of the Demon of the Whirlwind (in Skt. Tṛṇâvarta) who attempted to carry off Krushna (Kṛṣṇa), but was slain by him (K. 123, 180).
or trungᵘ m. distress, harassment, persecution (caused by stinging language uttered by another). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to provoke, irritate, re-arouse former anger.
m. a panther (El. trúnts). Cf. trū̃zᵘ.
(? spelling and gend.) the planting of rice-seedlings (L. 463, trupai).
f. contentment, satisfaction (L.V. 12, Śiv. 1430). Cf. traphᵃth.

m. the initial stage of fever (marked by chilly ague with a high temperature); cf. traph-tṻrun, p. 1029a, l. 18. --nīrith yunᵘ -- m.inf. fever to be relieved by its 'coming out' (i.e. sweating, etc., produced by exercise).

m. a prick or pierce with a pointed instrument, such as a needle, skewer, a thorn, or the like; cf. trọ̆mbᵘ. --dyunᵘ -- m. to prick or pierce, as ab.; met. to use stinging language. --lagun -- m.inf. a prick, as ab., to be experienced, to be pierced or pricked.
card. (pl. dat. truwāhan), thirteen (Gr.Gr. 76). Cf. trayōdashĕ.

(sg. dat. truwöshᵘ̈ or truvüshᵘ̈), the thirteenth lunar day of a lunar fortnight (cf. hērüʦᵘ̈-tᵘ̈, p. 351a, l. 4). truvüshᵘ̈-hondᵘ̈ gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or born, or produced on this day (Śiv. 524).
m.pl. 'thirteens', used as a multiplicative with numerals above ten, as in kāh truwöhⁱ akh hath ta tĕyĕtöjih, eleven thirteens are a hundred and forty-three (Gr.Gr. 86).

m. votive oblations made on behalf of a woman on the fourth day after delivery of a child. --khārun -- or --khasun -- m.inf. (if the woman is delicate or weak) a slight quartan feverish attack to come to her on this day.
m. a kind of panther (El. trúṅts, trúnts). It is believed to try to eat the moon, by jumping up towards whenever it sees it. Cf. trunzᵘ.
in likha-tryukhᵘ, p. 518b, l. 12, and lyukhᵘ-tryukhᵘ, p. 543b, l. 41, qq.v.; cf. trukhᵘ of which it is an alternative form (Gr.Gr. 30, 72, 140).

(sg. abl. trēli), threefold, of three kinds (noted only in Śiv. 1844, abl. trēli, which is probably m.c. for trila, q.v.). trēli-karm m. the threefold (class of) actions (all actions being either virtuous (Skt. puṇya), sinful (Skt. pāpa), or of mixed character (Skt. miśra)) (Śiv. 1844).

or trūnᵘ m. (sg. dat. trīnis, abl. trēni), the covering of a limb (such as a glove or stocking) (cf. atha-trᵒ, p. 63b, l. 16; khŏra-trᵒ, p. 409b, l. 35). In daba-tryūnᵘ or -tronᵘ (p. 181b, l. 32) the word seems to mean 'injury to a limb'.
or tribāra adv. for the third time, the third time.

card. (pl. dat. trᵃhan), thirty (Gr.Gr. 77; El. trȧh; Rām. 547, 1301; K. 553). ¶ trᵃ̇hᵃ̇ m.pl. 'thirties', used as a multiplicative, with numerals above ten, as in kāh trᵃ̇hᵃ̇ trĕh hath ta trᵃh, eleven thirties are three hundred and thirty (Gr.Gr. 86).
in old Ksh. the equivalent of trĕh 1, q.v. (L.V. 16, 75).
card. (pl. dat. trᵃhaiṭhan), sixty-three (Gr.Gr. 78, El. treheṭ).
trĕhath, or trihath card. (pl. dat. trᵃ(trĕᵃ, triᵒ)hatan ), three hundred (Gr.Gr. tri˚, 80, 84, 85; Rām. 600); three pice (see p. 357b, l. 8) (Gr.Gr. 85).
adj. (f. trᵃhatiñᵃ), costing three hundred (rupees or the like).
adj. c.g. (of a twist of the sacred kuśa-grass (see kush) or of the sacred thread worn by high-caste Hindūs) possessing three strands (cf. köñᵘ̈ 2 and 5); met. (of the body) very strong, powerful.
f. a drink made up of milk, curds, and water mixed in equal parts.
adj. (f. trᵃkhörᵃ), weighing or measuring three khārs (see khār 3 and khôrᵘ 2), each khār consisting of 16 trakh; (of some receptacle) suitable for containing the above amount.
f. (trᵃlürᵃ), (of a necklace or the like) of three strands.
adj. (f. trᵃmösiñᵃ), three months old, produced three months ago; produced after three months, taking three months to be produced.
adj. (f. trᵃmösᵃ), of, or belonging to, three months; three months old, produced three months ago (YZ. 367); produced after three months, taking three months to be produced.
adj. (f. trᵃnamatiñᵃ), costing ninety-nine (rupees, etc.), having wages of ninety-nine (rupees, etc.).
adj. (f. trᵃpȧjᵃ or trᵃpüjᵃ), consisting of three pals (of about two ounces each) (see pal 2); (usually of cloth or the like) (a head-dress or the like) made of three pals of thread.
adj. (f. trᵃpövᵃ), weighing or measuring three-quarters of a sēr (cf. pôwᵘ 3) or one and a half pounds.

adj. (f. trᵃpūrᵃ), (a house or the like) with three stories, three storied; (of an ornament or the like) three storied, having three sections one above the other; (of a field) bearing the same crop three times successively.

onomat. m. the noise of something hard (such as dry wood) breaking, 'crack', 'snap'; cf. trās 2, tris. --mēlun -- m.inf. 'a crack-sound to be joined', i.e. to break with such a sound, such a sound (indicating such a break) to be heard. --milanāwun -- m.inf. to break (dry wood or the like) and so cause such a sound. --milawun -- m.inf., id. --trᵃs tra-pũ̄̈ʦhī -- m. 'snap, snap, three little bits', making a living in a very humble way (cf. pũ̄̈ʦhī).
adj. (f. trᵃsatatiñᵃ), costing or worth seventy-three (rupees, etc.); earning seventy-three, as ab.

or trishākal adj. c.g. three-branched, having three segments (esp. of something such as a tree, which has ordinarily two branches, or as a walnut, which has ordinarily two segments) (K.Pr. 229, trĕhshákal).
(for 2, see trᵃsyūrᵃ) f. a weight of three seers (of about two pounds each) for weighing.
(f. trᵃsīrᵃ 2, for 1, see s.v.), weighing three seers (of two pounds each); (m. or f.) a vessel or receptacle containing or measuring three seers.

or trith m. (sg. dat. trᵃtas or tritas), a slit rent, fissure, tear (in a garment) (El. trit, trȧt; K.Pr. 51, trit); a made slit in a garment (to allow it to be put on or taken off) (cf. nāla-tᵒ, p. 632b, l. 40). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to rend, tear (El.). --wālun -- m.inf. to tear, or rend, a garment, or the like. --wasun -- inf. a long rent or tear to be made in a garment, or the like.
adj. (trᵃṭüpᵃ), for three parties, from three points of view, and so on, see ṭopᵘ 3.
adj. (f. trᵃtöpᵃ), three times put in the sun, thrice spread out in the sun to dry (of damp grain or the like). Cf. tôpᵘ and tāph.
adj. (f. trᵃtrücᵃ), measuring three trakhs (of six Kāshmīrī seers, see trakh 2); (m. or f.) a receptacle containing, or measuring, three trakhs.
adj. (f. trᵃtröcᵃ), measuring three trakhs as in the preceding; (m. or f.) an appliance for measuring this amount; (m. or f.) a receptacle containing, or measuring, this amount.
adj. (f. trᵃwörᵃ), having three covers, trebly wrapped up, trebly enclosed.
adj. (f. trᵃwörᵃshiñᵃ), of, or belonging to, three years; three years old.
adj. (f. trᵃwöṭᵃ, sg. dat. trᵃwācĕ), having three joints, joined in three places. Cf. wôṭᵘ.
or trĕwuh card. (pl. dat. trᵃ(trĕ)wuhan ), twenty-three (Gr.Gr. 77).
adj. (f. trᵃwarishᵃ), of three years, produced three years ago, three years old.
in tū-tū m. (onomat.), noise in the ears (El.).
in ṭū̃-ṭū̃ m. pretended weeping, e.g. as when a child cries in order to get something from a parent.

m. false accusation, falsely charging (one) with a crime, aspersion, detraction, calumny, slander; cf. ṭö̃chᵘ̈. --khārun -- m.inf. to accuse (falsely), to charge (someone) with having caused harm (e.g. to charge someone who has merely touched an article with being the cause of its breaking, when really it had been broken in some other way); cf. ṭö̃chᵘ̈ khārüñᵘ̈. --khasun -- m.inf. such a charge as the ab. to be brought against a person.
m. widespread destruction (e.g. that caused by an earthquake or inundation) (cf. naba-ṭᵒ, p. 619a, l. 19). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. such destruction suddenly to occur.
(for 2, see tachun) f. itchiness, itch; scratching (Gr.Gr. 121); cf. tach 2. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an attack of itchiness to come on.
m. the glans penis (cf. kŏla-ṭᵒ, p. 437b, l. 25).
see ṭokᵘ, ṭakun, and ṭakh-ṭücᵘ̈, s.v. ṭakh.

m. a heap, mound (Śiv. 1289); a stack; a granary (El.); a butt for shooting at; cf. tözⁱ. --gaʦhȧnⁱ --  m. pl. inf. heaps or piles to arise (e.g. of grain, of rubbish, and so on); great accumulation to occur. --karȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to make piles (e.g. of grain); to accumulate great wealth.

f. a trumped-up story (esp. when told with intent to deceive), a cock-and-bull yarn (invented by the teller). ṭuḍi-gorᵘ m. (f. -gürᵘ̈), one who is in the habit of inventing and telling such trumped-up stories.
or (q.v.) ṭung f. the cry of a jackal (El.). Cf. ṭã̄g. ṭū̃ga-ṭū̃g f. a concert of jackals' cries.
m. the yew-tree, Taxus baccata (cf. brāhmī and pōstal) (El. túng); Picea Webbiana (cf. birre, budulᵘ, and röyil) (El. túng).
m. (sg. voc. ṭō̃gi), a man who has a tumour, etc. (see tō̃g or ṭō̃g) (K.Pr. 74, voc. written ṭoṅi).
possessive pron. (f. tuhünzᵘ̈), your (not 'thy'), of you (pl.). The word is used as the gen. pl. of the personal pron. ʦᵃh 2, thou, q.v. (Śiv. 838, 883, 1249, 1295; H. ii, 2; xii, 15).
f. reawakening (by words or other suggestion) anger over an ancient grudge.
any very minute grain (such as millet) (cf. shölⁱ-tⁱ, p. 880b, l. 37). Cf. tūjⁱ.
f. in pinga-tūjⁱ, a husked millet seed, i.q. tū̃j, q.v.

or ṭujᵘ̈ f. a small globular object, a small ball, pebble, marble, pill, or the like (cf. gȧnⁱshĕ-ṭⁱ, p. 293a, l. 36; nūna-ṭᵒ, p. 641a, l. 14; shuhⁱ-ṭⁱ, p. 874b, l. 13; sŏṭhᵃka-ṭᵃ, p. 947a, l. 43); a clod (El. tuj); a kind of small deep-seated globular tumour (cf. naphka-ṭᵒ, p. 646a, l. 25). Cf. ṭulᵘ, of which this is a feminine form. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to indicate (e.g. by signs or gestures), point out, intimate (something to another) (e.g. to induce him to begin some work, or to set him quarrelling).
m. an arrow without a head, but with a button or knob at the point. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to be very unpleasant, to prove very disagreeable (like being hit by an arrow).
adj. c.g. (a cloth or similar article) having holes (gnawed in it by mice, moths, or the like).
adj. c.g. full of holes, all holes (as in ṭukal, q.v.).

m. (sg. dat. ṭukas), a hole (cut or gnawed by some animal such as a mouse, moths, or the like, in cloth, or the like) (cf. ạthᵃri-ṭᵃ, p. 67b, l. 2; gagar-ṭᵒ, p. 280a, l. 7) (El. ṭuk, cutting; Gr.Gr. 122); a fragment (of salt, sugar, or similar crystallized substance) (cf. nūna-tᵒ, p. 641a, l. 16).
m. grain for seed, seed-grain. --musāda -- (for تخم مساعدہ) seed-grain aid, an advance of grain made to a village for seed (L. 407).
m. that which is a piece, or part, of something (e.g. a piece of leather or of wood, or a son as a piece of the father).

c.g. (1 p.p. ṭukᵘ, f. ṭucᵘ̈; 2 p.p. ṭucyōv), to crunch (something hard) with the teeth; to gnaw or cut (like a rat) (cf. borᵘ ṭᵒ, p. 118a, l. 14) (Gr.Gr. 17, 122). Cf. ṭukh, ṭakun, and trukun. ṭukᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ṭucᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), crunched, gnawed.
(cf. تقوی) m. fear of God, piety; (in Ksh.) trusting hope, hope based on trust.

m. a piece, bit, morsel, scrap (of something hard) (cf. dāsa-ṭᵒ, p. 252a, l. 14) (El. ṭukar, a part; ṭukra, a bit, piece; K.Pr. 247). -bāgay f. division of something hard divided into parts or morsels (such as land, a metal, wood, etc.). --karȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to break or cut into pieces (H. viii, 6, 13).

m. (sg. dat. ṭũ̄̈kis, abl. ṭē̃ki or ṭö̃ki, pl. nom. tǖ̃kⁱ), anything in quantities worth two pice (or about a halfpenny) each; copper coins, pice (genl.) (K.Pr. 122). ¶ ṭē̃ki or ṭö̃ki adv. to be bought or sold, for two pice, a ha'pporth (K.Pr. 153). ¶ ṭũ̄̈kⁱ-wād m. a quantity of two-pice pieces.
f. a kind of small basket. Cf. ṭākᵘ̈rᵘ̈.
m., i.q. tᵃl 1, a mulberry, q.v., in shĕh-tᵒ, p. 873a, l. 45.
m. length, longness, prolixity (Śiv. 747, Rām. 768). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. (in a legal or other argument) to display prolixity, to argue at length (Rām. 1638).

(for 1 and 2, see tᵃl 1 and 2) m. weight, measure (El. túl, L.V. 23); weighing, measurement (cf. atha-tᵒ, p. 63a, l. 39). Cf. tōl 1. --karun -- m.inf. to weight (something) in the hand, feel the weight of (cf. atha-tōl, p. 63a, l. 37).
m. cotton-wool in tūla-paryö̃kh a bed (the pillows of which are stuffed) with cotton-wool, a luxurious bed (L.V. 73). Cf. tolᵘ 2.

or (q.v.) tulᵘ 2 (cf. tulun), raising, used in the following:-- tula-tāl f. lifting up and putting down (e.g. to find the right place for an object); met. (of a speech, literary work, or the like) arranging one's arguments in good order, and after discussion of all the pros and cons; cf. tālun and tulun. tula-tāl ās üñᵘ̈ f.inf. rising and falling to occur, (of one at the point of death) very slight expiration and inspiration to exist. tula-tāl thavüñᵘ f.inf. to complete a work or carry out a profession carefully, skilfully, and thoroughly (understanding it from top to bottom, and taking all necessary precautions). tula-tul f. lifting up again and again. tula-trāv f. taking up, and putting, and leaving there (e.g. in arranging things); (in a speech, literary work, or the like) settling all the pros and cons, discussing thoroughly and decisively.
adj. cold (El.). Cf. tᵃla-katurᵃ, p. 995b, l. 7, and tṻr.

adj. c.g. weighing (so much), used --˚ (cf. pōshĕ-tᵒ, p. 779a, l. 37), so rudra-tula, worth its weight in coral (Śiv. 1871). tula-tula adj. c.g. of equal weight, of weight equal to the weight of something else.
in tulā-kūṭᵘ m. the beam or standard of a large weighing balance; hence, such a balance (L.V. 23).

m. N. of a site (in Skt. Tūlamūlya), in the Delta of the Sind River, about ten miles north-west of Śrīnagar, and sacred to Mahārājñī, a form of Durgā (see RT.Tr. II, p. 488) (El. Tulamul; Śiv. 1135, 1175, 1519).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. tulanôwᵘ), to cause to lift (El.). Causal of tulun, q.v., in all its meanings (Śiv. 1777, cause to experience).
(? spelling) in tulatāl karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to harass (El.). Cf. talawūl.
f. wages for raising, removing, etc. (see tulun) (cf. dŏkha-tᵒ, p. 206b, l. 10; thaph tᵒ, p. 981a, l. 13).
or tulicᵘ̈ f. a deep earthenware eating dish (used esp. by Muslims). Cf. tulukᵘ.
or tulöñᵘ̈ f. prompt beginning, beginning at once, starting at once (on some work, owing to skilled practice, to eagerness, or the like).
in tūlönⁱ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to go into useless details, act or speak diffusely or at needless length, to waste time in prolonging needlessly (some work).
m. a wide deep earthen- ware dish for eating (used chiefly by Muslims) (cf. phakīr-tᵒ, p. 690b, l. 5). Cf. tulic.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. tulᵘ, f. tujᵘ̈; 2 p p. tujyōv), to lift, take up, raise, raise up, hoist (cf. tālun, and atha tᵒ, p. 63a, ll. 41 ff.; ḍachĕ tulañĕ, p. 186a, l. 20; kadam tᵒ, p. 385b, l. 5; kangan tulȧnⁱ, p. 457a, l. 8; palav tulȧnⁱ, p. 732b, l. 1; pūrᵘ tᵒ, p. 755a, l. 5; shĕmshēr tulüñᵘ̈, p. 884a, l. 34; thodᵘ tᵒ, p. 970b, ll. 42ff.) (Gr.Gr. 17; Gr.M.; L. 461; L.V. 99; Śiv. 1117, 1715; Rām. 123, 232, 315, 464, 480, 489, 781, 795, 888, 899, 982, 999, 1398, 1411, 1415, 1417, 1421, 1468, 1520, 1573, 1625, 1648; K. 399, 429, 1144; H. ii, 7; iii, 1, 2, 7, 9; v. 4; x, 7, 12; xii, 2, 4, 6, 9, 17; K.Pr. 143, 224); to exalt; to heighten, cause to become stronger (cf. brēh tulüñᵘ̈, p. 120b, l. 16) (Rām. 532); to cause to become erect (cf. brag tulȧnⁱ, p. 120a, l. 18; lüṭᵘ̈ tulüñᵘ̈, p. 536a, l. 43) (Śiv. 1812, Rām. 1495, YZ. 184); to raise, cause to rise (a blister or the like) (cf. bargölⁱ tulȧnⁱ, p. 120b, l. 1; dĕl tulȧnⁱ, p. 210b, l. 40; murĕn māz tᵒ, p. 589a, l. 31; phala tulañĕ, p. 692b, l. 50; tōsma tulȧnⁱ) (L.V. 101; H. vii, 14); ¶ to take up (for the purpose of using) (cf. banga tulüñᵘ̈, p. 112b, l. 32) (Śiv. 713, Rām. 1132, K. 561); to erect, build up, construct (cf. brang tᵒ, p. 124b, l. 50) (Rām. 1289); to draw (a map, picture, or the like) (cf. nakshĕ tᵒ, p. 631b, l. 15); ¶ to cause to rise, arouse, to cause to come into existence (cf. bĕgarun tᵒ, p. 92b, l. 3; bambar tulȧnⁱ, p. 108a, l. 12; dôdᵘ tᵒ, p. 191b, l. 3; dag tulüñᵘ̈, p. 193a, l. 49; drāg tᵒ, p. 241b, l. 1; gānd tulüñᵘ̈, p. 289a, l. 13; khad tulüñᵘ̈, p. 391b, l. 32; phȧrⁱ-dag tulüñᵘ̈, p. 702b, l. 22; phȧrⁱshĕr tᵒ, p. 708b, l. 37; tĕngal tulȧnⁱ, s.v. tĕngul; taphar tᵒ); to raise, excite, stir up, instigate (cf. dīn tᵒ, p. 223a, l. 14; dūñᵘ̈ tulüñᵘ̈, p. 231b, l. 13; hūs tᵒ, p. 352a, l. 48; huy tulüñᵘ̈, p. 363a, l. 44; mulᵃkh tᵒ, p. 568a, l. 6; maĩshĕr tᵒ, p. 598a, l. 47; nyāy tᵒ, p. 675a, l. 7; ṭhūs tᵒ, p. 985b, l. 14; ṭāv tᵒ); to arouse, excite, cause (something dormant) to become active (cf. dödⁱ-wōv tulüñᵘ̈, p. 191b, l. 11; phȧrⁱ-wōv tulüñᵘ̈, p. 702b, l. 40; phutang tulȧnⁱ, p. 718b, l. 28) (Rām. 602, K. 981); to start, cause to begin, set in action (cf. dav tulüñᵘ̈, p. 260b, l. 3; prasang tᵒ, p. 768a, l. 22; parwāz tᵒ, p. 773b, l. 11; tambal tulüñᵘ̈ and tambala tulañĕ, s.v. tambal; ʦingara tulañĕ, s.v. ʦingar) (L.V. 99; Śiv. 699; Rām. 417, 531, 549, 1684; K. 294; H. ii, 9; K.Pr. 46); to cause to begin, hatch, breed (a quarrel or the like) (cf. phasād tᵒ, p. 712a, l. 14; phutūra tᵒ, p. 718b, l. 46); ¶ to turn aside (one's own or another person's) attention, divert, distract (cf. dŏkha tᵒ, p. 206b, l. 5); ¶ to hold up, sustain (Śiv. 701, 994); to support (pain, etc.) (Rām. 761, YZ. 570); to take up and carry, bear, carry (cf. bôrᵘ tᵒ, p. 118a, ll. 29 ff.; jajīrᵘ̈ tulanwôlᵘ, p. 372a, l. 42) (Gr.M.; Rām. 402, 601; K. 73, 124; H. xii, 2); to take up and carry away, to take up and appropriate (H. x, 6, 7); to bear the responsibility of, undertake (cf. shĕrtal tulüñᵘ̈, p. 896a, l. 5) (Gr.M.); to undergo, experience, suffer, endure (cf. hān tulüñᵘ̈, p. 336a, l. 38; mazrath tulüñᵘ̈, p. 616b, l. 16) (Gr.M., Rām. 1489); ¶ to contract (debts), to obtain (money or goods) on credit (cf. karᵃz tᵒ, p. 479a, l. 29); to derive, acquire, get, gain (as the result of labour) (phöyida tᵒ, to derive profit, Gr.M.; Rām. 505a); ¶ to withdraw, remove (from on or from before) (cf. buthi-pĕṭha tᵒ, p. 143a, l. 48; dīna tᵒ, p. 223a, l. 19; phakas wurun tᵒ, p. 689a, l. 30; parda tᵒ, p. 756b, l. 11) (Śiv. 1849, Rām. 434); to lift up, root up (cf. kānᵃjĕ tulañĕ, p. 457b, l. 8; nam tulȧnⁱ, to lift the nails, torment, p. 635b, l. 12; to pare the nails, H. v, 6; ṭĕnḍⁱ tulȧnⁱ, s.v. ṭyonḍᵘ; tūz tulȧnⁱ); to efface, erase, expunge, abolish, cause to disappear, do away with (cf. barm tᵒ, p. 123a, l. 48; das tᵒ, p. 251b, l. 24; diwath tulüñᵘ̈, p. 264b, l. 50; khay tulüñᵘ̈, p. 426a, l. 7; lawa tulüñᵘ̈, p. 541a, l. 7; mālay tulüñᵘ̈, p. 570a, l. 19; shāph tᵒ, p. 887b, l. 50; thaph tulüñᵘ̈, p. 981a, l. 10) (H. xii, 15); ¶ to eject, pour forth (cf. dᵃh tᵒ, p. 198a, l. 13); to give forth (a loud sound), raise (a roar) (cf. graz tulüñᵘ̈, p. 306a, l. 6; pharyād tᵒ, p. 711a, l. 1; shōr tᵒ, p. 889b, l. 43) (Gr.M.; Rām. 445, 1143k, 1161; K. 153, 366); to give forth (a smell or the like) (cf. bŏy tulüñᵘ̈, p. 149a, l. 20; phakh tᵒ, p. 688b, l. 50). ¶ This verb is looked upon as the causal of wŏthun, to rise, q.v., in the special sense of 'raising' or 'lifting up', but not in the sense of 'causing to rise', for which wŏthanāwun is used (Gr.Gr. 176). ¶ tulᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tujᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), raised, etc., as ab. ¶ tulith thawun m.inf. to take up and put down (in its proper place, for concealment, or otherwise); to remove (a person) from his work or post, to dismiss from (his) post.
adj. (f. tulüvᵘ̈), made of mulberry wood (see tᵃl 1).

m. a small lump (e.g. of salt, sugar, or the like, or a muller for grinding colours, etc.) (cf. lāran-ṭᵒ, p. 531b, l. 43; nūna-ṭᵒ, p. 641a, l. 18; ranga-ṭᵒ, p. 857a, l. 26; shīna-ṭᵒ, p. 885a, l. 10 (K.Pr. 147). Cf. ṭujⁱ.

m. a single blade of grass or similar long thin vegetable straw (cf. sŏʦüñᵘ̈-tᵘ̈, p. 952a, l. 24) (K.Pr. 125); a thin rod (cf. hama-tᵒ, p. 333a, l. 24; sīri-tᵒ, p. 930a, l. 43); a very small quantity (of vegetables, wood, or the like) (cf. darbi-tᵒ, p. 240a, l. 42; draman-tᵒ, p. 245b, l. 36; gāsa-tᵒ, p. 308a, l. 1; guyĕn-tᵒ, p. 317b, l. 48; hāka-tᵒ, p. 326b, l. 37; kāṭha-tᵒ, p. 487b, l. 17; muji-tᵒ, p. 558b, l. 45; pana-tᵒ, p. 735a, l. 21; pōshĕ-tᵒ, p. 779a, l. 29; pĕʦi-tᵒ, p. 806b, l. 44; sinⁱ-tⁱ, p. 957b, l. 29; ṭȧpⁱ-tⁱ, s.v. ṭopᵘ 1; tari-tᵒ, s.v. türᵘ̈; ʦhĕṭh-tᵒ, s.v. ʦhĕṭh; ʦhĕyĕ-tᵒ, s.v. ʦhĕy; zinⁱ-tⁱ, s.v. zyunᵘ) (Gr.Gr. 164). Cf. tᵃl 2 or tul 2 and tᵃ̇jᵃ̇. ¶ tulⁱ pilanȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. 'to hand out straws', i.e. out of indolence to abandon some urgent work, and waste time instead in a useless occupation. --prānȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. 'blades of grass to become old', to waste time over some unnecessary work (in order to show off one's skill). --prinȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. out of indolence to waste time on some useless work. --ʦārȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to gather blade by blade, or leaf by leaf; to work lazily or indolently.
m., i.q. tul 4, raising, elevation, height (cf. alam-tᵒ, p. 24b, l. 22).
m. a certain ornament, shaped like a half-moon, and worn over the forehead. -kalapushᵘ m. a cap embroidered with a row or rows of these ornaments; hence, a head so adorned.

m. a kind of gourd (Lagenaria vulgaris) (cf. tö̆mbᵘ̈); a hollowed gourd (in which mendicants carry water, etc.). -wôrᵘ m. a kind of well-bucket (of equal width at bottom and top). -wörᵘ̈ f. id., but with a contracted mouth.
m. (sg. dat. tumbakas), in tumbakh-nörᵘ̈ f. a kind of musical instrument, shaped like a jar with a long neck, used by women at festivals.
f. the belly (esp. of a child); cf. tuphücᵘ̈. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the belly (esp. of a child) to become filled.
m. (sg. dat. tumanas), one who is lean and inscrutable, one who is lanky in appearance, and secretly false at heart, gaunt and blackhearted (cf. tamun 2, with which the word is said to be connected).
in tun-kóḍ (? spelling) m. the cerebellum (El.). Cf. kôḍᵘ 1.
m. one who has naturally a withered or a crooked arm (i.e. who has been born so).
m. (sg. dat. ṭunḍākas), provocative language, words (esp. when false) used to incite a quarrel.

f. swiftness; briskness, activity; sharpness, severity (e.g. of a disease); impetuosity, violence, fierceness, fury (Rām. 376, 497); (in Ksh.) zealous assiduity, smartness combined with ardour, alacrity.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. tundyōv), to be, or become, hot; (of a disease) to be, or become, aggravated; to be, or become, heated, hot-tempered, angry. tundyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tundyē-müʦᵘ̈), (of disease) aggravated; heated, angered, enraged.
adj. (f. tunzᵘ̈), quick, swift; brisk, active; hot, sharp, acrid; impetuous, hasty; fierce, violent; (in Ksh., esp. of a child) active and intelligent, sharp, keen-witted (YZ. 5).
or (q.v.) ṭū̃g f. the cry of a jackal (El. ṭúng; K.Pr. 83, 192); the lowing of a cow (sic, L. 456, tongan, dat. pl., and so translated). ṭungan aʦun m.inf. to make cries like those of a jackal.
m. a swelling, bump, or tumour on the forehead (cf. the preceding).
m. sharpness; alacrity, keenness; severity (of a disease); dearness, high price. Cf. tundᵘ.

f. a pile of articles (e.g. dishes, or plates, or rubbish) one on the top of the other (cf. bāna-tᵒ, p. 110a, l. 2; ṭökⁱ-tⁱ, p. 991a, l. 40). --khārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to pile articles, as ab. (esp. when done forcibly). --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf.articles to be piled, as ab. ¶ tanzi thawun m.inf. to arrange in a pile, as ab.

f. (sg. dat. tṻnʦhi), a kind of tiny earring (usually of gold). ¶ tṻnʦha f.pl. the muscles of the back of the neck. --galañĕ -- f. pl. inf. the muscles of the neck to melt; hence, the body to become wasted away (owing to long-continued grief, long-continued sickness, or the like).
m. (sg. abl. tōni), the navel (El. tún; Gr.Gr. 18, 20). Cf. tonᵘ 1.

(for 2, see tonᵘ 2) f. the string or fastening of a garment (as of a pair of drawers, or of the neck of a garment) (Rām. 749); the leathern girth of a horse (fastening the saddle and the blanket under it); the collar-band of a garment. tañĕ-nāl  m. (a garment) fitted with a collar-band.
tūfān طوفان m. a storm (El.); a disastrous flood (K.Pr. 180).
m. a tube through which a thing is propelled; a musket, gun; a pea-shooter; a pop-gun.
f. the belly (esp. when fat and protuberant), 'corporation'. Cf. tumücᵘ̈.

m. (sg. abl. ṭōpi), the button-like blossom of the male Indian hemp (bhang) (cf. banga-ṭᵒ, p. 113a, l. 16); any similar blossom (cf. sŏyĕ-ṭᵒ, p. 956a, l. 28); a button. ¶ ṭūpⁱ-pholⁱ m. a button. -wöjⁱ or -wöjᵘ̈ f. a button-hole.

f. (sg. dat. ṭōpĕ), a skull-cap (worn chiefly by Moslems) (cf. phamba-ṭᵒ, p. 698a, l. 49; phȧtⁱla-ṭⁱ, p. 717a, l. 46; phĕtⁱ-ṭⁱ, p. 723a, l. 20; prāji-ṭᵒ, p. 757b, l. 49; rōt-ṭᵒ, p. 847b, l. 42; sōzan-ṭᵒ, p. 958b, l. 39) (El. ṭópi, Gr.Gr. 73, Gr.M.). -gorᵘ m. a cap-seller (El. ṭopagar). ¶ ṭōpi-gorᵘ m. a cap-maker (El. ṭopagar, ṭopigur). -janda m. a worn-out skull-cap. -khỗṭᵘ m. one of the four triangular pieces, which, sewn together, form a skull-cap. -korᵘ m. the circular border round the edge of a skull-cap. -pholᵘ m. a band round the edge of a skull-cap (Gr.Gr. 73). -shikhurᵘ m. an old worn- out skull-cap. -salay f. a metal spike used for packing cotton into a wadded cap. -sᵃʦ m. a cap-sewer, a man who sews caps, a cap-tailor. -sᵃʦan f. (sg. dat. sᵃʦüñᵃ), a cap-needle, a needle for sewing caps. --ṭōpi kaḍun -- m.inf. to abuse or reproach publicly (i.e. before others). -wār m. sufficient cloth to make a skull-cap. -züṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -zacĕ), an old ragged skull-cap.

or tūrᵘ̈ f. (sg. abl. tōri), an adze, an axe, hatchet, half-adze (cf. sērĕ-tᵒ, p. 930a, l. 34) (El. tor, m., túr, f.; W. 13, thūrᵘ; L. 370, 460; Śiv. 1776, tūrᵘmᵃcr; H. vii, 18 (id.)); tōri-dab m. the blow of an axe (K.Pr. 114, 236).

or tǖrᵘ̈ f. (pl. nom. tṻrĕ, Gr.Gr. 62, or, as in the following, tṻra), cold, coldness, chill (cf. gŏlāb-tᵒ, p. 284b, l. 10; hŏkha-tᵒ, p. 327a, l. 40; māga-tᵒ, p. 551b, l. 47; pŏha-tᵒ, p. 684a, l. 44; pōshĕ-tᵒ, p. 779a, l. 35; rūda-tᵒ, p. 826b, l. 9) (Gr.Gr. 20, 62, 127, 137; Gr.M.; W. 9; L.V. 16, 28; Śiv. 336, 343; K. 276; K.Pr. 154, tar); esp. the cold shivering of ague (El. tu̇r, fever; K.Pr. 160, túr); cf. tūl 4. --aʦüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. cold to enter (the body), bodily coldness to be experienced; (esp.) the chill of ague to attack a person; cf. tṻra aʦañĕ, bel. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. cold to be felt (e.g. when wearing too thin clothes). -zāl f. 'cold fever', in which the body is outwardly hot but is chilly within. ¶ tṻra anañĕ f. pl. inf. to put a person in terror (quasi, so that he is all of a tremble, and subsequently shivers at the mere memory). --aʦañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to become terrorized, as ab.; cf. tǖrᵘ̈ aʦüñᵘ̈, ab. --khasañĕ -- m. pl. inf. the cold shivers (at the beginning of an attack of fever) to start. --ʦānañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to put a person in terror (quasi, in cold shivers). --yiñĕ -- f. pl. inf. shivering terror to come (to a person). ¶ tṻri-al f. a gourd shrunken up by the cold of winter. -ala m. shivering due to cold. -ala aʦȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. shiverings (from cold) to attack (a person). -bambar m. pl. stinging shivers due to cold (quasi, as if one is stung by bees). -bambar wŏthȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. such stinging cold to be felt (by a person) (e.g. from contact with snow). -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), afflicted by cold, chilled to the bone (Gr.Gr. 137). -kŏkur m. (pl. nom. -kŏkar; sg. f. -kŏkürᵘ̈), 'a cold-cock,' i.e. one who feels cold severely (and cowers and is pinched like a fowl in a winter frost). -kakav m. 'a cold-bartavelle', i.q. the preceding. -konḍᵘ m. cold-prickles, the down of the body standing on end on account of cold; hence, generally, bristling of the down, horripilation, thrill. -kȧnḍⁱ anȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to cause thrills (in another, by terrifying or the like). -kȧnḍⁱ aʦȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. shivering thrills (from exposure to cold, or from ague) to attack (a person). -kȧnḍⁱ yinⁱ m. pl. inf. thrills of fear to come (to a person, at the memory, or the like, of some past terror). -lĕḍ adj. c.g. 'defeated by cold', one who is filled with fear merely by experiencing a feeling of cold.
m. of, or belonging to, or produced in Turkey, or in Turkestan. (Cf. El. truk, a Turk.)
f. a trumpet, a clarion, i.q. turī, q.v.
f. a kind of trumpet, a clarion, i.q. turay, q.v. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a player on this instrument, one skilled in playing it.
or tṻrun 1 adj. (f. tǖrüñᵘ̈), (of hot food, etc.), become cool or cold, cold (Gr.Gr. 140); cold (genl.) (K.Pr. 236, f. voc. turuni). Cf. tᵃronᵃ.
m. (sg. dat. ṭuranas; pl. nom. ṭuran), the bough of a tree cleared of all its shoots and branches, a bare bough (fit only for firewood or the like); (m.pl.) a collection or pile of such boughs.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. tṻryōv), to be, or become, cold, frigid (esp. of the body or some limb) (cf. atha tᵒ, p. 63b, l. 4; traph tᵒ, p. 1029a, l. 18; tatun tᵒ) (L. 459, túrun; L.V. 16); (of water) to freeze (L.V. 16); cf. tᵃranun. tǖryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. tǖryē-müʦᵘ̈), become cold, as ab.
adv. i.q. tūrⁱ, q.v., p. 1019b, l. 48.

f. (a word borrowed from Skt.) the fourth state or condition (Skt. avasthā) of existence, the first three being waking (Skt. jāgṛti), waking sleep (Skt. svapna), and deep sleep (Skt. suṣupti); the fourth state of the soul, in which the spiritual subsists alone by itself, contrasted, like a spectator, as a substance undifferentially set free from all existing things (Śiv. 1488, 1623, 1826, 1866). There is a final stage called turyātīth, in which there is complete union with the Supreme (Śiv. 1757).
f. the final stage of emancipation, beyond the fourth stage (see turyā) (Śiv. 1757). A word borrowed from the Skt. turyâtītā.
m. a certain bird, the red-crested Pochard, Branta rufina (L. 130).
m. (sg. abl. ṭūri), a dish like ṭūrᵘ 2, but smaller (cf. öriʦi-ṭᵒ, p. 45b, l. 14; kŏng-ṭᵒ ʦhunüñᵘ̈, p. 456b, l. 24) (K. 528, 710).

f. a plant-fibre, a flower-filament (cf. muji-tᵒ, p. 558b, l. 11); (in carpentry) a tenon (cf. brörⁱ-tⁱ, p. 126a, l. 6; hāki-tᵒ, p. 327a, l. 4; kūṭⁱ-tⁱ, p. 485b, l. 22) (H. x, 5, 12); met. a projecting point (like a tenon) (cf. kangȧvⁱ-tⁱ, p. 457a, l. 28). ¶ tari-bọ̆dᵘ m. a bundle, tied together by the roots, of the acid fibrous leaves of a kind of radish-like vegetable. -caṭiñ f. a condiment made of the pounded roots and leaves of this vegetable. -tulᵘ m. a single one of these vegetables. -ʦyūṭᵘ m. i.q. -caṭiñ, ab.
m. (sg. abl. ṭōri), a flower-bud (cf. pōshĕ-ṭᵒ, p. 779a, l. 36).
m. (sg. abl. ṭōri), the dish out of which Hindū women eat (it is round, deep, and brazen) (cf. khira-ṭᵒ, p. 409a, l. 45; wŏgra-ṭᵒ) (Gr.Gr. 18, 19, 56; K.Pr. 183).

m. (sg. abl. ṭōsi, pl. nom. ṭūsⁱ), m. a blow with the clenched fist (cf. lĕki-ṭᵒ, p. 518a, l. 49, and ṭōs); met. a threatening gesture (cf. achirwāl-tūsⁱ, p. 9b, l. 23). ṭūsⁱ dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to strike blows with the fist; met. without excuse to afflict (another).
adj. c.g. having the colour of a certain woollen cloth made in the city of T̤ūs in Khōrāsān, a kind of purple. Cf. tōsa.
m. a mulberry (El.; cf. shah tút, L. 348). Cf. tᵃl.
in tuta-mö̃ch m. (sg. dat. mö̃chas), the honey, or nectar, found in the flower of a certain plant. People suck the flower by its lower end or tail. ? Cf. tūt.
or ṭū̃ṭh m. in --ganḍun -- m.inf. to expel, banish, exile (a son, servant, or other member of a family).
m. a great meal, a large quantity of food eaten at one time. Cf. ṭaṭh.
m. a certain aquatic fish-eating bird (cf. baḍa-ṭyū̃ṭhᵘ, p. 82b, l. 30, and kŏla-ṭyū̃ṭᵘ, p. 437b, l. 29, and (?) tuzukh).
adj. (f. tuʦᵘ̈), long faced, having the nose and other features thin and long (cf. shōga-tᵒ, p. 872a, 1. 19). --hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. tuʦᵘ̈ hishᵘ̈), lean-faced (from disease, anxiety, or the like).
f. (sg. dat. ṭacĕ), worrying (a person engaged in urgent work) by continually dogging or interrupting him.

in tūtⁱ-lambukh m. (sg. dat. -lambakas), a long prolix involved story, a story with a number of others emboxed in it, and without any clear ending; cf. tǖ̃tⁱ. -zĕv f. rapid (but still appropriate and logical) speaking or rhetoric. -zĕwal adj. c.g. an eloquent, rapid, speaker, as ab.
or tǖ̃thⁱ adj. c.g. in tǖ̃tⁱ (or tǖ̃thⁱ)-korⁱ m. catgut (used for stringing the bow of a cotton-carder). -pürᵘ̈ f. long, unseasonable, unrestrained garrulity. Cf. tūtⁱ.
f. (sg. dat. ṭō̃cĕ), a spout, esp. (in Ksh.) the mouthpiece of the long stem of a hookah.

f. shutting up, closing; (of a flower) the closing of the petals (Gr.Gr. 120); mean-heartedness. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. mean-heartedness, stinginess, niggardliness (esp. on the part of a master towards his household) to affect a person. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such niggardliness to come (to a person).
f. inward wrath, secret anger; cf. taviñ. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such anger to come to a person.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭuwanôwᵘ), to cause to be closed (e.g. of the eyes) (K. 256).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭuwᵘ), to close, shut up (the hand, eye, mouth, or the like) (cf. atha ṭᵒ, p. 63b, l. 22; dan or dand ṭuwȧnⁱ, p. 221a, l. 6; p. 224a, l. 45) (K. 138; H. xii, 22); firmly to close up any orifice genl.; (of a flower) to close the petals (Gr.Gr. 120). ṭuwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ṭuvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), closed, as ab.

m.pl. the tips of the fingers or toes (as a whole); cf. ṭyonḍᵘ. --tulȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to harass (someone by imposing an impossible task, or by urging him to the completion of some difficult one, quasi, causing him to wear off the tips of his fingers and toes); cf. ṭĕnḍⁱ tulȧnⁱ, p. 1049 b, l. 48. --wŏthȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the finger- and toe-tips to be worn away; hence, to be harassed, as ab. Cf. ṭĕnḍⁱ wŏthȧnⁱ, p. 1050a, l. 3.
adj. c.g. (esp. of a child) intelligent, sharp (in study). Cf. tundᵘ.
m. (sg. dat. tuzakas), regulation, ordinance, institute; retinue, pomp, state, dignity; (in Ksh.) N. of a certain fish-eating bird (described as having a long sharp beak). Cf. ṭū̃ṭhᵘ.
the Skt. word for 'thou', quoted in Śiv. 1851. So twamēvạy for Skt. tvam-ēva, thou only, even thou (Śiv. 1761).
m. leaving, forsaking, abandoning (Śiv. 1031, 1268, 1351, 1525, 1744; Rām. 225); resigning, renouncing (things of this world) (Śiv. 272, 587, 735, 1047, 1355, 1448, 1531, 1691, 1749, 1821, 1829).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. tyôgᵘ, f. työjᵘ̈, L.V. 62), to let go, let loose; to abandon, relinquish, give up (Śiv. 1713, 1850); (hence) to wield, to draw (a sword) (L.V. 62).
adj. c.g. one who abandons; one who performs religious ceremonial rites disinterestedly, and not for the sake of any reward attached to them (Śiv. 201).

m. (sg. dat. ṭĕkis), a ṭīkā, or sectarian mark worn on the forehead by Hindūs (cf. agᵃna-ṭᵃ, p. 16b, l. 46; bādām-tᵒ, p. 86b, l. 27; basma-ṭᵒ, p. 133a, l. 50; chata-ṭᵒ, p. 166a, l. 20; ciwa-ṭᵒ, p. 178b, l. 19; gangājalī-ṭᵒ, p. 292a, l. 36; rakh-ʦandan-ṭᵒ, p. 830b, l. 23) (El. ṭyuk, K. 926); an ornamental patch (of gold, silver, tinsel, colour, or the like) worn on the forehead (Śiv. 1155); (on white cloth or the like) a dirty mark, a small stain, a blot; an ornamental spot (in a pattern); a spot (generally) (cf. tāpa-ṭᵒ, p. 1015a, l. 24); a drop, a very small quantity of some liquid (e.g. of curdled milk). Cf. ṭika 1. ¶ ṭĕkⁱ-büdⁱrⁱ f. a forehead-patch of a coloured pattern, made with saffron and vermilion embellished with spots of white sandal- wood (cf. büdᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 2). -küñᵘ̈ f. a stone on which sandal for forehead-marks is ground. -pūʦᵘ̈ f. a woman's veil ornamented with spots and a coloured pattern (worn on festive occasions, such as a son's marriage). -tāl f. a similar veil, patterned in fine spots (worn on the top of the head). -vürᵘ̈ f. a small case (used by women) for containing materials for making these ornamental forehead-patches; a kind of toilet-box.

m. (sg. dat. tĕlis) a water blister (of the skin), blister (esp. when suddenly occurring) (cf. nāra-tᵒ, p. 648b, l. 1) (L.V. 108); met. any sudden evil (cf. rāwan-tᵒ, p. 853a, l. 24); met. inability to endure another's prosperity, enviousness, envious jealousy (cf. vebar-tᵒ). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. envious jealousy to fall (on a person), i.e. to be acutely felt.
adj. (f. të̆mbᵘ̈), under weight, below the expected weight; under measure, below the proper measure.

m. (sg. dat. ṭĕnḍis), the tip of a finger, toe, or similar limb (cf. ongᵘji-ṭᵘ, p. 33b, l. 32; atha-ṭᵒ, p. 63b, l. 25; khŏra-ṭᵒ, p. 409b, l. 36; khōra-tᵒ, p. 410a, l. 13); the tip of the nipple of the breast (cf. babi-ṭᵒ, p. 77a, l. 48) (El. babiṭunḍ); met. a mere trace of something, a tiny morsel (esp. of vegetables, or similar food) (cf. myonḍᵘ-tyonḍᵘ, a gobbet and a tiny bit; hence, a collection of moderate-sized gobbets, p. 614a, l. 3, and Gr.Gr. 95. I.K. VIII, i, 32, looks upon this compound as a jingle. Cf. also thañi-ṭᵒ, p. 979b, l. 38; wŏgra-ṭᵒ). Cf. tūz. ¶ ṭĕnḍⁱ-bọ̆kⁱ m. the finger-tips of one hand, or toe-tips of one foot, when pressed or collected together. -khāv m. a certain water-insect, popularly supposed to bite the finger- or toe-tips; a certain disease in which the tips of the fingers are eaten away by sores (K.Pr. 153). -khāv pyonᵘ m.inf. this disease to attack (a person). --tulȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to raise, (i.e. smite) the tips of the fingers (esp. as a punishment of boys); to give (a person) great trouble in the accomplishment of some work (e.g. involving him in constant journeys, searches, etc.); cf. tūz tulȧnⁱ. --wŏthȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to be involved in great trouble, as ab. Cf. tūz wŏthȧnⁱ.

adj. (f. të̆ṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat. ṭĕchĕ), bitter (cf. khĕna-ṭᵒ, p. 402a, l. 11) (Gr.Gr. 25, 26; Gr.M.; W. 20, 116, tio˙t); pungent (K.Pr. 214 (m. sg. dat. ṭĕṭis), 106); cf. ṭĕchĕr. --zahar hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. ṭë˘ṭhᵘ̈ zahār hishᵘ̈), 'bitter like poison', unbearably or very extremely bitter. ¶ ṭĕṭha-gāḍ f. a certain small river-fish (L. 158, tet gad). -khôlᵘ hyuhᵘ adj. (f. --hishᵘ̈ --), 'like a bitter kernel'; hence, easily extracted, easily taken out. -mĕṭha m. persuasion (esp. of an unwilling person); cf. myūṭhᵘ. -shĕkȧrⁱ adj. c.g. (of a fruit or the like) bitter-sweet (cf. El. ṭeṭha shakir tsúnṭ, a kind of apple, said, s.v. tsúnṭ, to be very unpalatable; according to L. 350, tet shakr, is very refreshing). -ʦēra m. (? pl.f.) a species of bitter apricot (El., W. 116). -vĕna m. N. of a certain medicinal plant used as a remedy for indigestion, etc. (W. 115; L. 67, 75, tetwán); according to L. 67, a drug known as ibsántin is distilled from its leaves. ¶ ṭë˘ṭhᵘ̈ zahārhishᵘ̈ f., see ṭyoṭhᵘ zahar hyuhᵘ, ab.
m. (sg. dat. ṭibis), N. of a certain bird.
or tyọ̆ngul m. (sg. dat. tē̃galas), i.q. tĕngul, q.v.

m. (sg. dat. tikis), a follower of the Trika form of Śaivism current in Kashmīr (Gr.Gr. 131). ¶ tikⁱ-bāy f. his wife. -pūtᵘ m. his son (Gr.Gr. 131). -ʦōram f. (sg. dat. -ʦōrümᵘ̈), the fourth lunar day of the light half of the month of Māg (Skt. Māgha = January-February), on which followers of this religion hold a special worship.

m. (sg. dat. tīris, abl. tēri), an animal of the sheep or goat kind (without regard to sex) (El. ter; Gr.Gr. 19, 152; Gr.M.); a ram, a male sheep (a ewe is tīrᵘ̈ 2) (Gr.M.; W. 19, tiör; Śiv. 1030); (El. tyúr) a flock of sheep (cf. nījĕ-tᵒ, p. 626b, l. 46). Cf. tīr 1. ¶ tīrⁱ m.pl. a number, or flocks, of sheep or goats. -khyolᵘ m. a flock of sheep or goats (Gr.Gr. 152); cf. tīr-khyolᵘ, p. 1018b, l. 35. -loṭᵘ m. one who possesses only a single miserable little sheep or goat (esp. of one who was once a large flock-master); cf. loṭᵘ 1, p. 535b, l. 22. -röchⁱ f. the occupation of herding sheep or goats, shepherding, goatherding. -rôchᵘ m. a shepherd, a goatherd (i.q. cōpān, q.v.) (for these people, see L. pp. 361 ff.). Cf. tīr-rôchᵘ, p. 1018b, l. 37.
in lashi-tyū̃thᵘ, p. 533b, l. 47, q.v. Cf. tō̃th 1.
in baḍa-ṭyū̃ṭhᵘ, p. 82b, l. 30, q.v. Cf. ṭū̃ṭhᵘ.

pron. adj. [masc. sg. dat. tṻtis or (Gr.M.) tītis; ag. tǖtⁱ or (Gr.M., K. 779) tītⁱ; pl. nom. tǖtⁱ or (Śiv. 1329) tītⁱ; dat. taitĕn, tötĕn, tṻtĕn, or tītĕn; ag. taityau, tötyau, tṻtyau, or tītyau; fem. sg. nom. tǖʦᵘ̈ (Gr.M.) or tīʦᵘ̈ 3 (for 1, see tĕth and for 2, see tēth) (Gr.M.); ag. taiʦi, töʦi, tṻʦi, or tīʦi; pl. nom. taiʦa, töʦa, tüʦa, or (Gr.M.) tīʦa. Cf. Gr.Gr. 59]; ¶ so much (in measure, weight, or the like) (of something within sight compared with something not within sight) (Gr.Gr. 59, 91, 148, 150; Gr.M.; W. 94; Śiv. 1303; Rām. 403, 488, 497, 1546, 1603; K. 478); yūtᵘ... tyūtᵘ, as much... so much, the more... the more (Gr.M., Śiv. 1559), (adv.) as soon as... so soon (H. xii, 2; YZ. 192, 454; K.Pr. 34). ¶ tītⁱ m.pl. so much (of more things than one), so many (as ab.) (Gr.Gr. 59, Gr.M., Śiv. 1329, K. 779). ¶ tītis m. sg. dat. used as adv. (in price) for so much (as ab.). ¶ tīʦi phiri adv. for so many times, so often (of some action within sight compared with some action not within sight).
m. porridge, in makāyi-tyū̃tᵘ, p. 563b, l. 8, q.v.
in kŏla-ṭyū̃ṭᵘ, p. 437b, l. 29, q.v. Cf. ṭū̃ṭhᵘ.
or tuzᵘ m. a kind of radish, see tāra-tᵒ, p. 1018a, l. 33.

or tᵘ̈jᵘ̈ (also spelt tᵃj), tujⁱ tujᵘ̈ f. a small stick, thin rod, pin, spike, anything needle-shaped (such as e.g. a piece of straw or a toothpick, the hair of a brush, the fine end of a boring instrument) (cf. ashéd-tᵒ, p. 48b, l. 12); barma-tᵒ, p. 123b, l. 8; dȧnⁱ-tⁱ, p. 221a, l. 10; danda-tᵒ or dȧndⁱ-tⁱ, p. 225a, ll. 1, 34; darba-tᵒ, p. 240a, l. 40; gāsa-tᵒ, p. 307b, l. 49; kȧnⁱ-tⁱ, p. 448b, l. 29; laʦhajĕ-tᵒ, p. 540a, l. 12; nakha-tᵒ, p. 628a, l. 13; nakha-tᵃjĕ, p. 628b, l. 15; nȧmⁱ-tⁱ, p. 636a, l. 15; rŏpⁱ-tⁱ, p. 840a, l. 30; sŏrma-tᵒ, p. 935b, l. 10; thēri-tᵒ, p. 982b, l. 47) (Gr.Gr. 16); esp. (El. túj) a wooden spike on which the shawl-wool thread is wound for weaving shawls (cf. khanḍawāv-tᵒ, p. 403a, l. 35). Cf. tᵃl 2, of which this is a f. form. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to use a toothpick, to pick the teeth. ¶ tᵃjĕ-gorᵃ m. a maker of shawl-weaver's spikes (see ab.) (El. tújigur). -kabāba m. collops or meat roasted on skewers. -kaböbⁱ m. a seller of skewered collops. --tārañĕ -- f. pl. inf. (a shawl-weaver) to arrange the spikes for weaving, to weave (shawls).
adj. c.g. one who is naturally a good runner.

or ṭikān adv. (properly pres. part. of ṭᵃkun, to run) quickly, speedily, at once (u.w. vbs. of going, doing, eating, or the like) (Gr.M.; L. 462, tikán; Rām. 365, 371, 391, 489, 560, 599, 716, 836, 857, 886, 930, 932, 978, 1100, 1327, 1330, 1357, 1384, 1693, 1712; K. 38, 106, 138, 1041, 1145-6); El. also gives the word as subst. m., meaning quickness, celerity, swiftness, haste. --karun -- m.inf. to make haste, be quick, hasten. --ṭᵃkān -- adv. very quickly, quickly all the time (W. 96, 151).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭᵃkanôwᵃ), to cause to run, to set running, to set on the run (El. ṭukanáwun).

or ṭikh or ṭīkh f. (sg. dat. ṭᵃki, ṭiki, or ṭīki), running (cf. shāla-ṭᵒ, p. 880a, l. 20) (Gr.Gr. 125; K.Pr. 217 ṭak, 231 ṭuk). --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to bring running', i.e. to come running. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to run away (owing to fear, astonishment, or the like) (El. tak, K. 939). --niñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to go away at a run (from any work). --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to run away (esp. in terror). --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to run very fast. ¶ ṭᵃka or ṭika 2 (for 1, see s.v.) in ṭᵃka-nörᵃ f. the muscle of the heel, the tendo Achillis (El. takanár). -phĕran m. a running garment, a short dress (not reaching below the knee, and suitable for running in). -ṭᵃkh f. (sg. dat. -ṭᵃki), great speed (in going or the like), fast running (K. 658). -tᵃkh gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. great speed to occur (in the performance of any work). -tār or (q.v.) tika-tār m. N. of a certain game in which potsherds (or the like) are thrown along the surface of the water of a river in an endeavour to make them reach the other side, a kind of 'Ducks and Drakes'; see tika-tār, p. 992b, l. 7. -wāwᵃ̇jᵃ̇ or -wāwᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a certain toy, like our children's 'windmill', consisting of vanes fixed on the end of a rod, which are set in motion by the holder running. ¶ ṭᵃki, etc., adv. at a run, quickly, hurriedly. ṭᵃki gaʦhun m.inf. to go at a run, to go at speed (K. 700). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come at a run, to come running, to come at speed.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. ṭᵃkyōv), to run, go quickly (El. ṭukun) (Gr.Gr. 125, L. 463).

or tul 1 (for 2, see tᵃl 2; for 3, see s.v.) m. a mulberry fruit (Morus indica) (cf. bĕdāna-tᵒ, p. 87b, l. 6; bŏṭa-tᵒ, p. 138b, l. 34; chata-tᵒ, p. 166a, l. 18; ʦari-tᵒ, p. 1081b, l. 40) (El. túl, q.v., s.v., for an account of the mulberry in Kashmīr; L. 73, 79, 348, tul, morus sp.; K.Pr. tul, 9, 224). Cf. tūt. ¶ tᵃla-ḍölᵃ f. a kind of basket-tray, or shallow basket, filled with mulberries, or a similar basket by which they are measured and sold; a complimentary present ('dalee') of mulberries carried in such a tray. -dŏph (sg. dat. -dŏpas), a mulberry-bush. -gᵃs m. fæces (said to resemble mulberries) caused by eating mulberries. -hüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -hacĕ), mulberry-wood in general; a piece of mulberry timber. -khorᵘ m. (f. -khürᵘ̈), 'a mulberry scald-head', i.e. a gluttonous eater of mulberries. -khāv m. a mulberry-eater, one who is fond of eating mulberries. -kulᵘ m. a mulberry-tree (cf. bĕdāna-tᵃla-kᵃ, p. 87b, l. 6) (El. tulakul, q.v. for the different varieties of the tree in Kashmīr; K.Pr. 116). -lünḍᵘ̈ f. the branch of a mulberry-tree. -lang m. the trunk or main branch of a mulberry-tree. -mūl m. the root of a mulberry-tree. -mọ̆nḍᵘ a post, or pillar, of mulberry-wood. -mūrᵘ̈ f. a twig of a mulberry-tree (used as fuel in sacrificial fires and the like). -pan m. a mulberry leaf. -popᵘ m. a ripe mulberry. -sütᵘ̈ f. meal of dried and ground mulberries. -ʦᵃñᵃ f.pl. charcoal made of mulberry-wood. -vüñᵘ̈ f. a mulberry grove (planted in regular lines). -zain f. a kind of basket for holding mulberries; such a basket full of mulberries. -zyunᵘ m. mulberry fire-wood, mulberry-wood fuel.

or tul 2 (for 3, see s.v.) f. a needle, a stylus (esp. such as is used for applying collyrium to the eyes or for similar uses), a painter's brush (cf. sŏrma-tᵃl, p. 935b, l. 12) (El. tul, collyrium); a fault, delinquency, culpability (causing loss to another); cf. tᵃ̇jᵃ̇ and tulᵘ. --khārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to impute, or bring a charge of such a fault (esp. when committed by someone other than the person charged). --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a fault to be imputed. ¶ tᵃla-(or tula-)katurᵘ  m. sheet-ice, a piece of sheet-ice (El. talakatur, tulakatar, túlakutur; L. 461, tulr katr; Śiv. 337 (tula˚). With tᵃla, in this connexion, cf. tṻr and tūl 4.
m.pl. a swarm of wild bees (or similar stinging insects); cf. tᵃlᵃrᵃ. --pĕnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. a swarm of bees to attack (a person), to be stung by a swarm of bees.

tᵃlürᵃ or tulᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a bee (esp. a wild bee) (cf. chamba-tᵒ, p. 161b, l. 25; mā̃ch-tᵒ, p. 547b, l. 13; pōshĕ-tᵒ, p. 779a, l. 31) (El. tilur, m.; Gr.M. tᵃlᵃrᵃ; L. 461, tilr) (H. ix, 1, 3-6; K.Pr. 155); a wasp (El. tular). Cf. tᵃlar. tᵃlari-ôlᵃ m. a bee's nest; a beehive.
m. spluttering sound from the anus at the time of defecating. ṭᵃr-ṭᵃr m. (met.) senseless continued chattering. ṭᵃr-ṭᵃr lāgun m.inf. to worry people by continuous frivolous talk.

f. relationship, affinity. tᵃra kaḍañĕ 1 f.pl.inf. to drag out relationships, (in discussing a proposed marriage) carefully and minutely to examine the good and bad qualities of the relations of both parties.

f. a rag, a piece of cloth (esp. one long and narrow), a strip (cf. dajĕ-tᵒ, p. 203a, l. 47; kapar-tᵒ, p. 463b, l. 40; pȧṭⁱ-tⁱ, p. 789b, l. 32). --wasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a strip to descend (i.e. to be torn off a cloth). ¶ tᵃra kaḍañĕ 2 f.pl.inf. to use a cloth or garment till it is worn into strips. --wālañĕ -- f.pl.inf. to tear or cut into strips. --wasañĕ -- f.pl.inf. to become torn or cut into strips.
tᵃrañĕr, or tṻrañār m. coolness, coolth (cf. atha-tᵒ, p. 63b, ll. 8, 9) (Gr.Gr. 140); coldness; met. poverty (K.Pr. 237, sg. dat. turneras for tᵃrañĕras).

or tṻranāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. tᵃ(tṻ)ranôwᵃ ), to cool, make cool (hot food); to cool (generally); to extinguish (a fire) (L.V. 38, tᵃr˚). tᵃ(tṻ)ranôwᵃ-motᵃ  perf. part. (tᵃ(tṻ)ranövᵃ-müʦᵃ ), cooled (by someone), etc., as ab.

or tṻranun conj. 3 (2 p.p. tᵃ(tṻ)ranyōv ), to become cold (esp. of some hot eatable), to go cold; (of anything else) to become cold, to become cool (cf. atha tᵒ, p. 63b, l. 7); to be cold (genl.) (K.Pr. 40, 114); cf. tṻrun 2. tᵃ(tṻ)ranyō-motᵃ  perf. part. (f. tᵃ(tṻ)ranyē-müʦᵃ ), become cold, become cool, as ab.
or tᵃrun adj. (f. tᵃrüñᵃ), cool, cold, frigid (cf. atha-tᵒ, p. 63b, l. 1) (El. turun; L.V. 56, 57, tᵃrunᵃ); (esp. of food) cooled, become cold (El. tirun). Cf. tṻr and tǖronᵘ.
m. a wrench or dislocation (of a limb) (cf. zanga-tᵒ, s.v. zang 1). Cf. ʦᵃs.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭᵃsonᵃ, f. ṭᵃsüñᵃ; 2 p.p. ṭᵃsañōv), forcibly to thrust into or pierce, to stab, poke into, prod (e.g. a nail, a dagger, the finger, etc.) (cf. hĕng tᵃsanȧnᵃ, p. 339a, l. 38); cf. ṭᵃsun. ṭᵃsonᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. ṭᵃsüñᵃ-müʦᵃ), thrust into, forced into, as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ṭᵒsᵒ; 2 p.p. ṭᵃsōv, Gr.Gr. 208, 224), forcibly to thrust into or pierce, to stab, poke into, prod (e.g. with a nail, a dagger, the finger, etc.); cf. ṭᵃsanun. ṭᵒsᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. ṭᵘ̈sᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), thrust into, forced into, etc.

f. folding, folding up, rolling up; a fold, crease; a plait; (in Ksh.) a fine, thin, stream of liquid; a very fine thread, filament (L.V. 102). Cf. tay 3. ¶ tᵃyĕ pakun m.inf. to go in a fine stream, (of blood or the like) to issue from a wound in a thin stream. --wasun -- m.inf. to descend in a fine stream, (of blood, etc.) to issue, as ab.
f. a woman who makes a speciality of spinning very fine thread, a delicate spinner (L.V. 102, Śiv. 1872). Cf. tᵃy 1.

f. (sg. dat. tᵃʦhi), anything small, little, trifling; (in Ksh.) a dirty rag, a clout (cf. atha-tᵒ, p. 63b, l. 20; mal-tᵒ, p. 564a, l. 31). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to wipe off (with a clout) (cf. mal-tᵒ kᵒ, p. 564a, l. 33); (in boiling milk or the like, when it is on the point of boiling over) to wipe the outside of the vessel with a rag dipped in cold water (to stop the boiling over). ¶ tᵃʦha kaḍañĕ f.pl. inf. to wear (clothes, etc.), to rags; to tear (a person) to rags, i.e. to abuse someone (who is an object of anger) root and branch, including his progenitors up to his first ancestor; to wear oneself to rags by intense study. --karith trāwañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to tear up into small fragments. ¶ tᵃʦhi añĕmaʦhunun m.inf. to feed (some very exhausted invalid) by (squeezing) a rag dipped in gruel or the like (into his mouth). -palav m. a rag for wiping dishes, a dish-clout.
m. a garment (esp. of thin material). tᵃ̇thᵃ̇ m.pl. clothes (esp. used with regard to clothes for the wash).
sometimes used instead of tᵘ̈jᵘ̈, see tᵃ̇jᵃ̇ (cf. ashĕd-tᵒ, p. 48b, l. 12).

This is the regular u of Hindī, pronounced like the u in 'full'. It is represented in Nāgarī by and in the Persian character by pēsh. Thus, کُس, kus, who? This vowel is not affected by any mātrā-vowel. ¶ The sound of u cannot commence a word. In such a position u always becomes wu. Thus, uḍar, a plateau, becomes wuḍar. In the Nāgarī character it is optionally spelt or, but the word is always pronounced wuḍar, and will be so written in this dictionary. In the Persian character it is always وُڈَر. ¶ The letter u is quite often interchanged with ŏ, both in speaking and in writing. Most Kāshmīrīs seem to be unable to distinguish between the two sounds.

This is the long ū of Hindī, pronounced like the ū in 'rule'. It is represented in Nāgarī by, and in the Persian character by wāw preceded by pēsh. Thus, چھور, ʦūr, a thief. Like u, this ū is not affected by any mātrā-vowel. ¶ As in the case of u, the sound of ū cannot commence a word. In such a position it becomes wū. Thus, ū̃ṭh, a camel, becomes wū̃ṭh. In the Nāgarī character it is optionally spelt or, but the word is always pronounced wū̃ṭh, and will be so written in this dictionary. In the Persian character it is always وُونتھہ. ¶ The letter ū is quite often interchanged with ō, both in speaking and in writing. Most Kāshmīrīs seem to be unable to distinguish between the two sounds.

This is the sound which a takes when followed by ᵘ̈. It is nearly the same as the short German ü. It is represented in Nāgarī by and in the Persian character by zabar. Thus, بَڈ, büḍᵘ̈, great (fem.). When in the process of declension or conjugation or for any other reason the ᵘ̈ disappears, the raison d'être for the ü disappears also, and it reverts to the original a, as explained under the head of o, q.v.

This letter, which is peculiar to the Kāshmīrī, is pronounced something like a long-drawn German ü. It is represented in the Nāgarī character by, and in the Persian usually by yē, as in, سیت, sṻty, with. The vowel often represents the diphthong ai, followed by ⁱ or ᵘ̈. Thus, from the base kait- we have a fem. sing. kǖʦᵘ̈, how much? and a pl. masc. dir. kǖtⁱ.
f. saying 'yes and no', assenting and dissenting, indecision, hemming and hawing; the groaning of a sick person, or any imitation of it. Cf. ũ̄̈ʦᵃh-pũ̄̈ʦᵃh.
(f. ᵘ̈jᵘ̈), a secondary suffix forming adjectives, as in gāṭa, skill, gāṭulᵘ (f. gāṭᵘ̈jᵘ̈), skilful (Gr.Gr. 145).
f. the throwing away and scattering of a powder or anything minutely subdivided, so that to all intents and purposes it ceases to exist.
(for 1 see under onᵘ 3). A sec. suff. indicating condition, only noted in mait-un, the condition of a corpse (Gr.Gr. 144).

m. (f. anziñ), a male swan; a male goose, a gander (Śiv. 1810; K.Pr. 220); the grey goose (L. 128, ans). -borᵘ m. or -baran f. a goose-door, a small door in the wall of a courtyard or of a vegetable garden, by which the larger quadrupeds cannot enter, but which men can enter by bending their bodies or 'ducking' as a goose ducks his head to go through a low hole. -böwᵘ̈ f. the upper leg of a goose, especially when boiled down to a broth. -gardan f. a swan's neck; met., a long thin neck of a man. -würᵘ̈ f. the name of a certain soup or sauce made of the pounded flesh of a goose boiled in water.
etc. See onᵘ and also anun 2.

(f. üñᵘ̈), a suffix forming the genitive, used mostly with masc. proper names, as in rāmunᵘ (f. rāmüñᵘ̈), of or belonging to Rāma, and with the word pāna self, forming the adj. panunᵘ (f. panüñᵘ̈), own (Gr.Gr. 42, 152). For unᵘ 1 see onᵘ 3.
a feminine suffix forming abstract nouns. It is the fem. form of onᵘ 3, etc. See Gr.Gr. 118.
a sec. suff. used with the words kūṭᵘ, a beam, and dag, a blow. Thus, kūṭunᵘ, a small beam; dagunᵘ, a club, a mace (Gr.Gr. 148).
(f. irᵘ̈), a secondary suffix only occurring in the word köshurᵘ (f. köshirᵘ̈), of or belonging to Kashmīr (see Gr.Gr. 150).
(f. ūrᵘ̈), a secondary suffix as in nastūrᵘ, having an ugly nose (nast) (Gr.Gr. 137).
f. a title, a nickname; esp. an abusive title given in the course of a verbal altercation.
f. the large saw used for cutting logs into planks and the like. Cf. ar 3 and ara- litᵘ̈rᵘ̈ under ara 1.
a sec. suff. forming adverbs of time, indicating the year in which a thing occurred, as in yih-us, this year; par-us last year (Gr.Gr. 158).
m. a sec. suff. appearing in the words mŏnḍ-us, widowhood, and dŏb-us, a washerman's club (Gr.Gr. 144).
m. (sg. dat. utas), a secondary suffix forming abstract nouns, as in band-uth, relationship (Gr.Gr. 144).
c.g. (as subst., m. sg. dat. ūṭas), secondary suff. forming adjectives, as from lĕkh (base lĕk), abuse, lĕkal or lĕkal-ūṭh, abusive (Gr.Gr. 138).
m.pl. groups of eight, used in the multiplication table, as in ʦōr ǖṭhⁱ dŏyĕtrᵃh, four eights (are) thirty-two (Gr.Gr. 84, 86). W. 104 spells the word öṭhⁱ.

f. (sg. dat. acĕ), a bundle, hank, or skein of thread, arranged for twisting into string or rope. Usually the second member of a compound, as in sǖtra-üṭᵘ̈ a skein of thread, yēra-üṭᵘ̈ a skein of worsted, kēsha-ütᵘ̈ a wisp of hair. Cf. aṭh 2. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to form a skein; to become of one mind, to conspire.
adj. (f. üvᵘ̈), a sec. suff. added (like the gen. term. ukᵘ) to nouns, and signifying 'composed of'. Thus, from sŏn, gold, sŏnuvᵘ, made of gold; see Gr.Gr. 161.
m. assenting and dissenting, hemming and hawing, hesitation. Cf. ũ̄̈hᵘ̈-ṭũ̄̈hᵘ̈.
m. (in Hindū tradition) 'common to all mankind', a title of fire; esp. the fire of digestion (in the stomach) (Śiv. 306).
m. (of the four main Hindū castes) a Vaiśya, or man of the third caste, whose business is agriculture or trade (K. 982).
f. N. of a necklace worn by Vishnu, in Skt. Vaijayantī (Śiv. 1326).
m. with the trunk curved, an epithet of the god Gaṇêśa (see Ganēsh), who is represented with the head of an elephant (Śiv. 6).
(? spelling and gender) a certain fibre-yielding rush (L. 68).
m. profession, trade, occupation, business; esp. the business of buying and selling, trade, commerce.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. worzᵘ), to leave, relinquish, give up, abandon (cf. paph wᵒ, p. 748b, l. 43). ¶ worzᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vürzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), given up, abandoned, as ab. ¶ warzith conj. part. having abandoned; hence, as adj. free from, devoid of, as in pāph wᵒ, sinless (Rām. 1620). Cf. pāpa-warzan, p. 749a, l. 15.
m. division, partition, apportionment (of inheritance or the like); a part or share, as ab.
in vĕbar-tyolᵘ m. extreme jealousy, extreme envy (cf. tyolᵘ, a blister).
m. greatness, glory, grandeur, magnificence, splendour, wealth; power, might.
f. (sg. dat. vĕböjᵃrüñᵃ), division, partition (of property, money, an inheritance, or the like).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. vĕböjᵒrᵒ), to divide, partition (property, an inheritance, or the like).
adj. (f. vĕböshᵘ̈), lit. 'one who speaks a corrupt language'; hence, stupid, void of understanding, clumsy.
f. (sg. dat. vĕbūsüʦᵘ̈), N. of a certain disease involving a dry, frothy, evil-smelling mouth.
m. ornament, decoration; (in Ksh.) (of a person, a place, etc.), great wealth of, or richness in, possessions or articles of various kinds.
f. (sg. dat. vĕbṻʦᵘ̈), riches, wealth, plenty, might, power.
m. fatness, thickness, stoutness, bulkiness (cf. pĕlⁱ-vⁱ, p. 814a, l. 43). --pōchĕr -- m. stoutness and thickness, excessive, or great, stoutness, great thickness.

f. (sg. dat. vë̆zᵘ̈), a rule, commandment, enjoining precept; a sacred rule, ordinance, injunction; a religious rite, or ceremony (cf. böshᵘ̈- vᵒ, p. 94a, l. 1) (Śiv. 1000). ¶ vĕdi (for Skt. vidhi), in the following:-- vĕdi-pūrwakh adv. according to due ceremony, ritely (K. 971). -vë̆zᵘ̈ adv. id. (K. 494, 715, 726, 770, 1046).

m. complaint, reproach, censure, accusation (made to one person regarding another's action). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to make such a complaint. --phirun -- m.inf. to complain (to one's own people) about some old grievance (suffered by oneself or by another) which one has continually borne in mind, to grumble over an old grievance.
m. headstrongness, addiction, foolish obstinacy (in censurable conduct). --aʦun -- m.inf. addiction to a censurable course of conduct to be acquired.
m. a rite, ceremony, performance of prescribed acts or rites (cf. bali-vᵒ, p. 104b, l. 24).
f. a widow (El. ? should the word be vĕdawa ?).
adj. c.g. obstinately addicted to a censurable course of conduct, headstrong.

or vidyā f. knowledge (Gr.M., Śiv. 109); learning (Gr.Gr. 187, Gr.M., Śiv. 1471); a branch of learning, a science (Gr.M.; Śiv. 707; K. 485-6, 488). -dachin, -dachiñᵘ̈, -dakshinā , or -dakhĕnā f. a fee paid to a teacher (K. 488 dakhĕnā). ¶ vidyāyi-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), void of knowledge, ignorant (Gr.M.).
(or viᵒ) m. a certain kind of demi-god or semi-divine being, in Skt. Vidyādharu (K. 346); a man learned in sacred lore (Śiv. 50, 626, 862).
f. freezing cold (after a fall of snow, with a clear sky and bitter wind) (K.Pr. 226).
f. (sg. dat. vẹ̆dᵃrüñᵃ), looseness, slackness (e.g. of the knot of a load); slackness, weakness, feebleness.
f. (sg. dat. (?) vẹ̆dᵃraṭhi), a kind of painful abscess. --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such an abscess to come on.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. vẹ̆dᵃrôwᵃ), to loosen, slacken; to make feeble (by opposition, assisting in defeat, robbing, or the like). vẹ̆dᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. vẹ̆dᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), loosened, slackened (by someone); made feeble (as ab.).
m. unsteadiness (of character), fickleness, inconstancy; opposition, antagonism.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. vẹ̆dᵃryōv), to be, or become, loose, slack (of the knot of a load or the like) (Gr.Gr. 8); to be, or become, slack, weak, feeble. vẹ̆dᵃryō-motᵃ perf. part. (f. vẹ̆dᵃryē-müʦᵃ), become loose, slack; enfeebled, become slack, weak.
m. the state or conditions prevailing at any particular time, the times, the state of affairs (at such a time). -phyurᵘ m. the course or lapse of time, the march of time, the tide of events.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. vĕgalôwᵘ), to cause to melt, to liquify (something) (Śiv. 27).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. vĕgalyōv), to melt, deliquesce (L.V. 69); (met.) to melt, become dejected (Rām. 1557).

vign (also written), or vigᵃn m. an obstacle, impediment (Gr.M., Śiv. 1118, Rām. 1570, K. 1064); a difficulty, trouble (K. 696). ¶ vigna-hartār  m. the remover of obstacles, N. of Gaṇēśa (see ganēsh) (Śiv. 1). -nĕwār m. the warder off of obstacles, N. of id. (Śiv. 7 (-niwār), 1081).

or (H.) vih 1 m. poison, venom, virus (El. vih; Gr.M.; Śiv. 122, 1055; Rām. 268, 387, 972, 1159, 1173; K. 231, 284, 889; H. v, 6); jealousy, heart burning, malice, spite, rancour (K. 83, 190, 350, 889, 1052; K.Pr. 99). --barun -- m.inf. to feel jealousy, rancour (at another's good fortune or prosperity) (e.g. between co-wives). --ganḍᵘ̈rᵘ̈ -- f. the very poisonous globular root of a certain wild poisonous plant. vĕha-borutᵘ adj. (f. -barᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), filled with poison, poisonous, venomous; filled with jealousy, rancorous, malevolent, malicious. -gŏgᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a certain plant with a very poisonous root. -ṭö̃jᵘ̈ f. a certain poisonous fruit, resembling a small pear, found in the hill forests; (met.) one who is of a very malevolent nature.
adj. c.g. poisonous, toxic. Cf. vĕh.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. vĕhaladiñ), poisonous, toxic; of a jealous disposition, jealous. Cf. vĕh.

or vĕhawath f. (sg. dat. vĕhᵃvüʦᵃ), high regard, respect, or deference to the opinion of one's family, neighbours, respectable people, or the like. (Cf. dīshĕ-vᵒ, p. 253a, l. 25; lūka-vᵒ, p. 519a, l. 30.)

m. N. of a famous holy place about thirty miles east of Śrīnagar, the ancient Vijayêśvara (RT.Tr. II, 463, Vijᵃ̣brōr; El. Vijibrór; Śiv. 1161; K.Pr. 230); cf. ʦakadar and vizayēshŏr. vĕjabrāri adv. at Vĕjabrôrᵘ.
adj. c.g. born, produced, transacted, etc., in Vĕjabrôrᵘ.

in vĕjē-satam f. (sg. dat. -satümᵘ̈), the seventh day of the bright half of a month falling on a Sunday in certain asterisms classed as 'male' (in Skt. vijayā-saptamī). On such days in Kashmīr, oblations are made at Mārtaṇḍa to the Manes.

or vikār m. change for the worse, deterioration, becoming spoiled, turning bad (e.g. of a man through disease, or food by corrupting) (Gr.M., K. 1154). vĕkāra-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without change, unchanging (Gr.M.).
adj. (f. vĕkaröjᵘ̈), formidable, frightful, dreadful-looking, hideous, horrible, terrible.
adj. (f. vë̆khᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), individualistic, singular (in dress or conduct); unconventional, habitually acting contrary to custom or to good manners, of generally irritating habits.
f. (sg. dat. vë̆khᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), an individual, one (out of a number) considered separately.
adj. c.g. manifested, displayed, evident, plain, clear.
m. the condition of having become manifested, apparentness.
individuality, singularity; unconventionality, acting contrary to custom or the rules of good manners; a threatening gesture (Rām. vĕkhʦār, 335, 393).
adj. (f. vĕküjᵘ̈), wanting a limb (mostly used --˚, after the mention of the limb missing, as in khōra-vᵒ, wanting a foot; narĕ-vᵒ, wanting an arm; nasti-vᵒ, noseless).
in vĕla-boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈) (of a human being, horse, bull, or the like) very untractable, unmanageable, refractory, disobedient, violently contumacious.

or (q.v.) vēra m. (sg. dat. vēli), a time, season, opportunity, the proper time, point of time, time (for anything) (cf. kŏ-vᵒ, p. 496a, l. 21; mimizⁱ-vⁱ, p. 571b, l. 25; prath-vᵒ, p. 769a, l. 44; pĕwan-vᵒ, p. 811a, l. 9; rūda-vᵒ, p. 826b, l. 25; sahār-vᵒ, p. 890b, l. 32) (El. vélah; Gr.M.; Śiv. 511, 698, 1081, 1131, 1718, 1720); cf. vil and viz. --vēla -- adv. at different times, from time to time.
f., i.q. vēla, q.v. It is the Skt. form of the word, and is occasionally used. See K.Pr. 177.
or vilāph m. (sg. dat. vĕlāpas), wailing, lamentation, a wail (K. 453, 480).
f. (sg. dat. vĕlarüñᵘ̈), decrepitude, etc., as in the next.
