conj. 1 (1 p.p. vĕlarôwᵘ), to cause to become decrepit, etc. (as in vĕlarun, q.v.). vĕlarôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vĕlarövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to become decrepit, etc.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. vĕlaryōv), (of a house, pillar, tree, or the like) to become decrepit, insecure (from old age, loosening of supports, or the like); (of the body) to become decrepit, worn out (owing to ill-health or the like) (K. 381); to become unnerved, unmanned (e.g. at hearing disastrous news) (Rām. 907; K. 51, 80). vĕlaryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vĕlaryē-müʦᵘ̈), become decrepit, as ab.
m. sport, play, pastime; amorous or wanton gesture, wantonness, coquetry, gay manners, fashionableness, fine array.
m. (sg. dat. vĕlāyĕtas), an inhabited country, a region; a foreign country; esp. England or Europe (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. English, European, see the next.
m. (f. vĕlāsĕñ), a wanton, a voluptuary, sensualist, pleasure-seeker.
? conj. 3 (of a road or way) to be lost, noted only in K.Pr. 231.

also written viᵒ m. a heavenly car, a vehicle used by the gods for travelling in the air (Śiv. 921, 967, 1149, 1494, 1736, 1913; Rām. 281, 1712, 1761; K. 851); an aeroplane, balloon; the board on which the corpse of a Hindū is carried to cremation (El.).
vĕna 1, or vĕnā, postpos. without, free from (L.V. 12, vĕnā); apart from, distinct from (L.V. 13, vĕn). Another form of this word is vin, q.v.

m. N. of a certain medicinal plant, a kind of peppermint, and of its leaf (cf. ṭĕṭha-vᵒ, p. 1051a, l. 3) (L. 73, venna = Mentha; El. vien = Mentha incana and roylana; W. 115, vien; Śiv. 187-9, 190, 192, 1041, 1196, 1406; K.Pr. 106, 248). -caṭiñ f. a chutnee, or preserve, made of its leaves. -dŏph m. (sg. dat. -dŏpas), its plant. -pōsh m. its flower.
m. destruction, ruin, utter loss, decay. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. destruction to come, i.e. the time for destruction, or change of character, to have arrived.
or viᵒ f. (sg. dat. vĕnüʦᵘ̈, Śiv. 1668), i.q. vĕnatī, q.v., a respectful statement or communication, a request (Gr.M. vinath; Śiv. 703, 880, 916, 1227, 1300, 1668; K. 15, vi˚).
or (q.v.) vĕnath f. a respectful statement or communication, a request (Gr.M. vinath).

or vinay m. polite conduct, good breeding or manners; modesty, humility (Gr.M. vinay). --pranay -- m. (esp. of a boy or youth) excellent manners united with good education (Śiv. 1342 vinay ta pranay). ¶ vĕnayĕ-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), void of good manners, unmannered, ill-mannered, insolent, rude, impertinent (Gr.M.). -raʦhar m. want of good manners, insolence, rudeness. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), well-behaved, gentlemanly, refined; modest. -sṻty adv. politely (Gr.M.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. vyondᵘ, f. vë̆nzᵘ̈), to behave (towards someone), conduct oneself, practise (a course of conduct) (El. vyendun) (L.V. 64, Rām. 1148); to revere, show courtesy (to); to obtain, get, gain, acquire (something wanted, looked for, or worked for, coming at the expected time) (cf. nāṭa vĕndañĕ, p. 660b, l. 17); to look upon as, consider as (L.V. 43, Śiv. 1561). vyondᵘ-motᵘ perf. part (f. vë̆nzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), practised (as ab.); acquired (as ab.).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. vĕngyōv) (of anything animate or inanimate, or of any work, or the like) to become deficient in a member, to become maimed, defective, mutilated, defective. Cf. vyongᵘ and wongᵘ.
or vẹ̆ngᵃrāwun conj. 1 (1 p.p. vẹ̆ngᵒrᵒ), to maim, mutilate (anything animate or inanimate, or a work, or the like). See vĕngun.
m. a condition of mutilation, defectiveness, deficiency of a member (of anything animate or inanimate, or of any work, or the like). Cf. vyongᵘ.
for vẹ̆ñᵒrᵒ, 1 p.p. of vẹ̆ñᵉ̆run, q.v. --˚, in aḍa-vᵒ, p. 12b, l. 2.
adj. c.g. (of anything animate or inanimate, or any work, etc.) on the point of destruction, perishing, being destroyed.

f. (sg. dat. vẹ̆ñᵉ̆rüñᵉ̆), the act of picking to pieces with the fingers, unravelling, separating, pulling to pieces, shredding (string, straw, vegetables, a bunch of leaves, etc., as in vẹ̆ñᵉ̆run, q.v.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. vẹ̆ñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), i.q. vẹ̆ñᵉ̆run, q.v. vẹ̆ñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. vẹ̆ñᵉ̆rövᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), i.q. vẹ̆ñᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, q.v. s.v. vẹ̆ñᵉ̆run.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. vẹ̆ñᵒrᵒ), to pick to pieces with the fingers, unravel, dismember, separate, pull to pieces, take to pieces, shred (string, vegetables, a bunch of leaves, a mass of straw, or similar compact, dense, or intertwisted object) (Gr.Gr. 7). vẹ̆ñᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. vẹ̆ñᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), picked to pieces, as ab.
f. a calamity, misfortune, adversity, distress.

f. (sg. dat. vĕpüʦᵘ̈, but cf. vĕpüʦhᵘ̈lad bel.), a calamity, misfortune, adversity, distress. ¶ vĕpüʦᵘ̈ wolᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. --vüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), enveloped in misfortunes, surrounded by misfortunes. vĕpüʦᵘ̈-wôlᵘ̈ m. (f. -wājĕñ), involved in calamity (and by contact, etc.) causing calamity to others.

n.ag. (f. vĕpavüñᵘ̈), (of anything inanimate) that which fits into or finds room in a receptacle; (of instruction, command, or the like) that which is firmly fixed in the mind; (of a human being) he who finds a place in any society, position, or locality (even if not originally suitable for it).
m.pl. a jingle of phĕphar in phᵒ-vᵒ (p. 700b, l. 35).
adj. (f. vĕphüjᵘ̈), fruitless, bearing no, or imperfect, fruit (L.V. 55).
adj. (f. vĕpüzᵘ̈), subject to calamity, unfortunate, afflicted, distressed, fallen into adversity.
adj. (f. vĕpüṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. vĕpacĕ), oppressive, tyrannical, irritating, infuriating; contaminating, debasing (by association).
adj. (f. vĕpüʦhᵘ̈), incredulous, unbelieving, sceptical; untrustworthy, not to be relied on, unreliable; hard to believe, incredible.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. vĕpyōv), (of anything rational or irrational) to be firmly situated in some place, and yet to have no definite location, to be diffused through, pervade, permeate, fill up, fill exactly; (of something such as a command, conversation, circumstance) to be firmly fixed in the mind. Cf. vyāpun 1. ¶ vĕpan-bāna  m. large-mindedness, the having a capacious intellect; (of a vessel or the like) the being sufficiently large to contain some specified substance. ¶ vĕpana-gatā adj. c.g. (of a man or rational being) gone away never to return (lit. or fig. 'dead'). Cf. gata. ¶ vĕpyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vĕpyē-müʦᵘ̈), that which has pervaded, etc., as ab., pervading, etc.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. vĕpüʦhᵘ̈ladiñ), full of, or pervaded by calamity, in evil plight; calamitous, disastrous. See vĕpath.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. vẹ̆pᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. vẹ̆pᵃrun, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. vẹ̆pᵒrᵒ), to cause to find room in anything, to cause to pervade, permeate; to hide, conceal (a thing, a person, conduct, or the like). See vĕpun.
in ʦēra-vēr, p. 1079a, l. 13, very late. Cf. vēla and vēra.

f. loving desire, desire on account of affection, loving motive (e.g. when one wishes to give something desired to a beloved friend, child, wife, or the like) (Śiv. 1024); cf. vīrᵘ̈ 2. vēri 1 postpos. (used --˚) for, for the sake of, on account of (e.g. when one gives or places something, or goes somewhere, merely for the sake of some loved person) (cf. ʦᵃhan-vᵃ, p. 1058b, l. 26) (Rām. 1484, cyāñĕ v˚, on thy account; 1577, tȧmⁱ-sanzi v˚, for his sake; 1591, in exchange for, in place of, instead of).
or (q.v.) vēla f. a time, season, etc., as s.v. vēla, q.v. (Rām. 986, sg. obl. vēri). Cf. also vēr 1.
m. (sg. dat. vĕrakas), one who has subdued all his passions and desires, and has taken to an ascetic life. Cf. virakth.
adj. c.g. incidental, occasional; in small quantity, a little.
m. the condition of one who has lost all his relations, the condition of being alone in the world. Cf. vĕrostᵘ.
adj. (c.g. vĕrüʦhᵘ̈), one who has lost all his relations (without father, wife, or children, etc.), one who is alone in the world.
adj. (f. vĕrüsᵘ̈), sapless, without juice; tasteless, flavourless; (met.) insipid, without charm.
adj. c.g. useless, vain, fruitless, unprofitable.

f. (sg. voc. vĕsī, H. ix, 1; visⁱyiy, H. ix, 11) a girl's female friend (of the same age), crony, close companion, comrade, play-fellow, chum, confidante (cf. ganga-vᵒ, p. 292a, l. 8) (El.; Gr.Gr. 25, 144; Rām. 1778; K. 803; H. ix, 1, 11; xii, 14; K.Pr. 167, 194); cf. vyosᵘ. --sö̆drᵘ̈ --  f. such a companion who is also related by blood and has been a play-fellow and comrade from childhood; a woman who has been admitted to close friendship like the above (whether by another woman or by a man). ¶ vĕsa-pônᵘ m. close comradeship (between women, as ab.) (Gr.Gr. 144, K.Pr. 102); met. similar close friendship or comradeship (between other female creatures) (Rām. 95). -pônᵘ lāgun m.inf. to form such a comradeship.
m. unevenness, roughness, ruggedness (lit. and met.) (Gr.Gr. 139, visamĕr).

m. assiduous practice in, or application to (an art, course of study, or the like); debauchery, dissipation, licentiousness. --aʦun -- m.inf. to enter debauchery, become a debauchee, plunge into dissipation.
or vĕsᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 1 f. slackness, feebleness (cf. asara-vĕsar, p. 51a, l. 30; mada- vĕsar, p. 584b, l. 9); instability, unsteadiness, precariousness (cf. atha-vĕsar, p. 64b, l. 38).
f. for vĕsarüñᵘ, f. of vĕsarun, to become slack, q.v. In dāl vᵒ, p. 210a, l. 28.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. vĕsarôwᵘ), to loosen, relax (something); to make frail, enfeeble (YZ. 72); to render unstable; to let fall; to terrify, fill with fear. vĕsarôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vĕsarövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), loosened, relaxed, enfeebled, etc., as ab.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. vĕsaryōv), to become loose, relaxed, untied (cf. dasta vĕsarȧnⁱ, p. 256b, l. 1); to fade (as a flower); to become slack, frail, feeble, to fade (El., Śiv. 335); to waste away, vanish, disappear (Rām. 1579); to become unstable, unsteady (cf. atha vᵒ, p. 64b, l. 41); to fall down; to be nervous, timid, timorous. vĕsaryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vĕsaryē-müʦᵘ̈), relaxed, fallen down, slackened, etc., as ab.
m. casting off, quitting, abandoning. --karun -- m.inf. to cause casting off, to destroy (gen. of obj.) (Śiv. 1431).
conj. 3, to take one's leave, depart (L.V. 9).
m. dejection, sadness, grief, sorrow. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to cause dejection (to another). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. dejection or grief to come (to a person from some cause).
f. (sg. dat. vĕshākhi), N. of a certain constellation, the 16th lunar mansion (in Skt. viśākhā).

postpos. governing dat. on, upon (El. véshih); (in special meanings) in, as in strī-lingas vēshĕ, (of some word) in the feminine (it means so-and-so); nākaḥ ākāshĕs-vēshĕ, (the Sanskrit word) nākaḥ (is used) in (the meaning of) 'the sky'.
in vĕshĕmatyunᵘ sŏrg m. a fleeting heaven, momentary bliss, wealth, or the like (disappearing almost at once, as if it were in a dream). Cf. vĕshĕy.

or (Śiv.) viᵒ , m. scene of action, ground of action, basis (L.V. 71, vishĕy); worldly enjoyment, the pleasures of sense, worldly prosperity and ease of life (Śiv. 339, 1082, 1351); debauchery, sensuality, evil habit; sudden, or unexpected, loss or destruction (of a thing, of the results of work, of an occupation, or the like). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such sudden, or unexpected loss to occur. ¶ vĕshĕyĕ-būg m. devotion to the enjoyment of earthly pleasures, worldly-mindedness.

adj. c.g. peculiar, special (Gr.M. vishēsh, Śiv. 1725); excellent, distinguished, preeminent, choice. --karith -- adv. especially, specially, only (for this purpose) (Gr.M.) so, L.V. 54, kari vishēsh, she has a special character.
m. taking rest, resting oneself (esp. after a long and tiring journey, labour, or the like).

m. a seat, a mat for sitting or sleeping on, esp. the seat of the presiding priest at a Hindū sacrifice; (in Hindū worship) a wisp of kush-grass (see p. 480a, l. 47) used as a substitute to represent a god or a Brāhman. --wahārun -- m.inf. to spread out one's mat-seat; met. to settle oneself tenaciously near another (for the sake of protection or to obtain some object).
f. cholera; met. fainting or swoon with symptoms resembling those of cholera.
f. unconsciousness, oblivion, loss of memory or of consciousness, insensibility (e.g. from intoxication, possession by a demon, epilepsy, fainting, grief, or the like) (Śiv. 937).

vĕsmrath, or vismrĕth adj. c.g. one who has lost memory or consciousness, unconscious, insensible (as in vĕsmar 1). vĕsmar gaʦhun m.inf. to become unconscious or insensible, as ab., so vismrĕth gaʦhun (K. 505).
adj. (f. vĕsümᵘ̈), uneven, rough, rugged (lit. and met.) (Gr.Gr. 139, visomᵘ); difficult, hard to understand or to carry out.
or vĕsurᵘ adj. (f. vĕsürᵘ̈ or vĕsᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 2), loose, relaxed, untied; slack, frail, feeble (cf. hȧṭⁱ-vⁱ, p. 356a, l. 31); nervous, timid, timorous; unstable, unsteady (cf. mada-vᵒ, p. 548b, l. 14).

(or viᵒ) m. extension, amplitude, breadth, expanse (of country, time, circumstance, action, sheet of cloth, etc.) (Śiv. 523, 1102); (of speech) prolixity, diffuseness, fullness of detail; the broad, or general, condition or arrangement of anything (Śiv. 18, 1158). --anun -- m.inf. (of something disarranged) to put in proper order. --bōzun -- m.inf. to consider, or examine, an opportunity (as to whether it is suitable or not). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to explain fully or comment on (some concise statement or literary work); to put in order (something previously disarranged). --wuchun -- m.inf. to examine, or deliberate upon, a state of affairs (as to its suitability in regard to place, time, availability of materials, or the like). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. a suitable state of affairs to present itself.

(or viᵒ ᵒ) conj. 1 (1 p.p. vĕstôrᵘ), to explain, comment upon, expand (some complicated or concise statement, treatise, or the like) (Śiv. 64, 1158, 1580); to expand, diffuse widely (Śiv. 9, 100). vĕstôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vĕstörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), explained, commented upon (as ab.).
or vĕst adj. c.g. dispersed, scattered, in asta-vĕsth, p. 52a, l. 8.

adj. c.g. calm, quiet, of a tranquil disposition; free from passions; cool, free from heat, of low temperature. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become appeased, allayed, calmed; to become abated, put an end to, extinguished. --karun -- m.inf. to calm, tranquillize, appease, allay; to abate, put an end to, extinguish; to cool (anger, pride, etc.).

m. (in a discussion) a captious objection, idle carping, fallacious argument, false objections; wrangling, captious criticism. --tulun -- m.inf. to raise captious objections, use false arguments; to spread abroad false rumours (causing public agitation).
adj. c.g. one who habitually makes captious objections, etc., when engaged in a discussion (see the preceding).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. vĕtarôwᵘ), i.q. vĕtarun, q.v. vĕtarôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vĕtarövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of any work, esp. when very difficult, and in the face of obstacles), carried on, carried through.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. vĕtorᵘ), to carry on or through (esp. some very difficult work in the face of obstacles).
or vitastā f. N. of the principal river of Kashmīr, i.q. vĕth, q.v. (Śiv. 1495, vi˚).
m. pl. dat. of vyotᵘ, q.v.

f. (sg. dat. vĕthi, Gr.Gr. 70), the N. of the principal river of Kashmīr, in Skt. Vitastā. In India it is known as the Jihlam (vulgo Jhelum) (El. vĕṭh (sic), vyĕt; Gr.Gr. 25, 70; W. 149; Śiv. 1588; K.Pr. 9, 227, 233). In K.Pr. 102, treated as a symbol of prosperity. Cf. vĕtastā. -shikhurᵘ pārun m.inf. to cast a certain bet, ordeal, or test. In this, a wet mark is put on one side of a potsherd, piece of grass, or the like. It is tossed into the air, and, as in our 'head or tail', the side that turns up decides the contest. ¶ vĕtha-bal m. any local ghāṭ on the bank of this river, where people bathe, or embark and disembark (Gr.Gr. 165). -boṭhᵘ m. a bank of this river. -göḍᵘ̈ f. a fish of this river (cf. gād). -krünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kranjĕ), N. of the country on both banks of this river. -truwāh f. (sg. dat. -truvüshᵘ̈), the thirteenth lunar day of the bright half of the month of Bādᵃrapĕth (Skt. Bhādrapada = August-September), being the anniversary of the day on which Pārvatī, the Energic Power of Śiva, descended to the earth in the form of this river. A festival is held on this date, during which Hindūs worship and make offerings to the river. -truvüshᵘ̈-bôgᵘ̈ m. a present made to a bride by her husband's people on the occasion of this festival. -wôñᵘ m. the water of the river Vĕth (as distinct from that of neighbouring streams) (El. veṭhawóiṅ; Gr.Gr. 73; W. 115, v ėthạwonⁱ, river-water). -woturᵘ m. the source of the river Vĕth. -wāv m. the breeze that blows from the Vĕth, or from a place where it has a confluence with another river or with the Wular lake.
f. in gar-vēṭh, household utensils, p. 296a, l. 36, q.v.
adj. c.g. excessively stout, corpulent, obese; cf. vyoṭhᵘ. vĕṭha-pan m. a carpenter's rule or gauge.

f. (sg. dat. vĕtharüñᵘ̈), a kind of sack made of string formed by twisting paddy-straw (used for carrying paddy and the like) (cf. māz-vᵒ, p. 615a, l. 6, where there is also possible confusion with vẹ̆ṭhᵃran, q.v.) (El.; L. 463, vetran; K.Pr. 124); a mat made of this string, a straw mat. ¶ vĕtharüñᵘ̈-patᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a mat woven from twisted rice-straw; an old, worn-out, mat like the ab. -sāban f. (sg. dat. -sābüñᵘ̈), 'soap on such a straw-mat', wasting one's substance on useless labour (K.Pr. 190).
f. a woman who is too stout, too fat, made ugly by fatness, gross. Considered to be the fem. of vyoṭhᵘ, q.v., but used in a bad sense (Gr.Gr. 38).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. vĕṭhyōv), to become stout, fat, corpulent, to swell (cf. rĕkh vĕṭhüñᵘ̈, p. 830b, l. 43) (El.; Gr.Gr. 108, 110, 173, 196); (of something originally thin, by undergoing the necessary processes) to become thick, etc.; to increase (El.); to exult, rejoice (on the attainment of one's desires, etc.) (Rām. 1109; K. 61, 96, 255, 330, 337, 418, 461-2, 569, 585, 633, 648, 659, 682, 725, 749, 771, 857, 902, 949, 964, 986, 1133, 1158). vĕṭhyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vĕṭhyē-müʦᵘ̈), become stout, fat, thick, as ab.
m. a certain bird, described as small, dark-coloured, and living in swampy land; a certain smooth wood found in root-shaped lumps in barren hill-country.
adj. (f. vĕṭhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 1), stout, plump, bouncing (usually with reference to a boy or girl).
f. (sg. dat. vẹ̆ṭhᵃrüñᵃ), making stout, making fat; fostering (a human being, a tree, or the like). See māz- vĕtharan, s.v. vĕtharan.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. vẹ̆ṭhᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. vẹ̆ṭhᵃrun, q.v. (El., Gr.Gr. 173); to increase (tr.) (El.). vẹ̆ṭhᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. vẹ̆ṭhᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. vẹ̆ṭhᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, q.v. s.v. vĕṭhᵃrun.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. vẹ̆ṭhᵒrᵒ), to make stout, to fatten, to foster (e.g. a man by food, etc., or a tree by horticultural care, watering, etc.) (Gr.Gr. 8); to increase (tr.). vẹ̆ṭhᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. vẹ̆ṭhᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made stout, fattened, as ab.
(for 1, see vĕṭhurᵘ 2) f. N. of a certain small fish, generally found in forest torrents.
m. a collection of seed-grain (for sowing).
f. the roe of a fish, i.q. wav, q.v.

f. the act of scattering or casting all round one (rice, seed for sowing, dust, or the like) (cf. dāñĕ-vᵒ, p. 231a, l. 23). --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to throw up (seeds, etc.) from a winnowing-basket or the like, in order to cleanse them from dust and other foreign matter.

(sometimes written viᵒ) m. (sg. dat. vĕ(vi)vīkas ), discrimination, just judgment, discernment (Śiv. 1016, 1482, 1488, 1695, 1754, 1826). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give discrimination (to), to advise, reason with, warn; to explain, teach the way of true knowledge or of practising some fine art. --karun -- m.inf. to do discrimination, to consider thoroughly, investigate.
adj. c.g. one who discriminates, a discriminating person; one who shows compassion to every creature, compassionate.

(sometimes written viᵒ) m. marriage (El. veva); a marriage ceremony and all its customary procedure (Śiv. 411; Rām. 627; K. 901, 950); a wedding festivity. --karun -- m.inf. to carry out the marriage ceremony, to marry (so-and-so to so-and-so) (El.; Śiv. 39; Rām. 425; K. 726, 830, 912).

m. trade, trading, commerce, traffic (El.); mutual behaviour, social intercourse, mutual conduct (between relations, friends, or the like) (Śiv. 27, 587); conduct, behaviour (general) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 586, 829, 1790, 1799, 1816, 1839); usage, custom, an established rule or practice (Śiv. 9, 33, 56, 80); carrying out (of some business), performance (Śiv. 72, 504, 523, 1099, 1696).

m. a professional trader, a business man; one who is busied in worldly affairs (as opp. to one free from worldly attachments) (Śiv. 201, 579, 587, 1047); (adj. c.g.) busy, occupied (L.V. 65; Śiv. 1051, 1509, 1513).
m. explanation, gloss, comment, interpretation (of some obscure passage or statement).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. vyowᵘ), to scatter, throw about, strew (seed for sowing, dust, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 8); to sow broadcast; to toss up (grain, etc.) in a winnowing-basket or the like (in order to cleanse it). vyowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vë̆vᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), scattered about, as ab.; sown broadcast; winnowed, as ab.
f. (sg. dat. vẹ̆wᵃrüñᵃ), the act of scattering or strewing (seeds, dust, etc.); tossing up (grain, etc.) in a winnowing-basket, or the like, to cleanse it.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. vẹ̆wᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. vẹ̆wᵃrun, q.v. vẹ̆wᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. vẹ̆wᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. vẹ̆wᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, s.v. vẹ̆wᵃrun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. vẹ̆wᵒrᵒ), to scatter, throw about, strew (seed for sowing, dust, powder, or the like) (i.q. vĕwun, q.v.); to sow broadcast; to toss up (grain, etc.) in a winnowing-basket (in order to cleanse it); to pull apart (with the fingers), tease out (a mass of cotton, tangled twigs, straw, or the like). vẹ̆wᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. vẹ̆vᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), scattered, thrown about, strewn; (of seed) sown broadcast; winnowed; pulled apart, as ab.
m. a secret place, a private spot.
m. complete knowledge (of anything), full cognizance, familiarity (with). Cf. vyodᵘ.
also written viᵒ m. victory, conquest (K. 1018).
f. (sg. dat. vẹ̆zᵃrüñᵃ), acquiring full knowledge (of something), making oneself master of something, studying something, minutely examining something.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. vẹ̆zᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. vẹ̆zᵃrun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. vẹ̆zᵒrᵒ), to acquire full knowledge (of something), to master (a subject) (cf. nāṭa vẹ̆zᵃrañĕ, p. 660b, l. 19); to examine, prove, (in a dispute) to examine the rights and wrongs of both parties in order to decide (cf. ṭhūl vẹ̆zᵃrȧnᵃ, p. 976a, l. 45) (Gr.Gr. 7). vẹ̆zᵃrith dyunᵘ m.inf. to consider a dispute and decide as above.

m. the condition of possessing, being well supplied with, naturally full of, used --˚, as in dana-vᵒ, p. 222a, l. 26; hayāh-vᵒ, p. 364a, l. 27; mōda-vᵒ, p. 549a, l. 33; mandacha-vᵒ, p. 575b, l. 15; phala-vᵒ, p. 692b, l. 25; pranayĕ-vᵒ, p. 764b, l. 9. Cf. vyotᵘ.

(also writtenviᵒ) m. deliberation, consideration, examining, discriminating judgment, decision (cf. sadvᵒ, p. 866b, l. 6; swa- para-vᵒ, p. 952b, l. 14; sŏ-vᵒ, p. 955a, l. 47) (El.; Gr.M.; L.V. 28-9, 71, 79; Śiv. 19, 331, 950, 1023, 1032, 1342, 1512, 1579, 1589, 1595, 1612, 1670, 1706, 1715, 1776, 1780, 1788, 1820, 1858, 1898); esp. wise discrimination, virtuous resolves, wise and virtuous conduct (Rām. 42, 95; K. 543). --karun -- m.inf. to pay attention, consider carefully (Gr.M., Śiv. 1751, Rām. 241); to fancy, imagine (El., Gr.M.). -nāg m. N. of a sacred spring in the environs of Śrīnagar, and on the north side of the city (RT.Tr. II, 457, Vícār Nāg; K.Pr. 134, 233). -nögⁱ adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, this spring (Rām. 244). ¶ vĕʦāras lagun m.inf. to become engaged in deliberation; to become the object of deliberation, to be brought into consideration (Rām. 2).

(also written viᵒ) conj. 1 (1 p.p. vĕʦôrᵘ), to consider (about something), deliberate (upon), exercise discrimination (concerning), decide (about) (Gr.M.; L.V. 30; Śiv. 1364, 1788). vĕʦôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vĕʦörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), considered about, deliberated upon, decided about.

f. (sg. dat. vĕʦüʦᵘ̈) (of a vessel or the like) room for conveniently containing, the being of the right size for holding (something); the condition of having the mind or heart filled or pervaded with some experience (such as joy, sorrow, learning, etc.). Cf. vĕʦun.
n.ag. (f. vĕʦavüñᵘ̈), that which fits into (a vessel or the like); that which pervades.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. vĕʦhanôwᵘ), i.q. vĕʦhanun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. vĕʦhonᵘ, f. vĕʦhüñᵘ̈; 2 p.p. vĕʦhañōv), to separate, tease out (a lump of cotton or wool, straw, or a bunch of anything) (El. vetsanun); to explain word by word (any difficult passage or book), to compose a full detailed commentary. vĕʦhonᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vĕʦhüñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), teased out, fully explained, as ab.

f. the being without (something) (cf. mālinⁱ-vⁱ, p. 570b, l. 15); being without the necessary materials or appliances for some urgent work (? cf. El. wutsai, necessity). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- such absence of necessary materials to happen. --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause necessary materials to be wanting, at the critical moment to cause such to disappear. ¶ vĕʦhȧyĕ-röchⁱ adj. c.g. that which guards against such want of necessary materials, some small object that completes the supply of such materials (which by its coming enables the work to be carried out).
1 p.p. of vĕʦhanun, q.v., used as adj. in aḍa-vĕʦhonᵘ (f. -vĕʦhüñᵘ̈), half teased out, p. 12b, l. 10.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. vyoʦᵘ; 2 p.p. vĕʦyōv), to fit into, be conveniently contained or held in (El.; Gr.Gr. 204; L.V. 47; K.Pr. 64, 227); to pervade (Gr.Gr. 204, 224); to be agreed to, consented to, liked, approved of (Śiv. 1873); (of a person) to be contained in oneself; hence (with negative or the like) not to be able to contain oneself (for joy or the like) (Śiv. 1044 (vĕʦana for veʦān, m.c.), 1290; cf. K.Pr. 156). Cf. vyotᵘ. ¶ vĕʦan-bāna m. the condition of being a full receptacle (of learning, property, good qualities and good fortune), worthiness, dignity. ¶ vĕʦyō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. vĕʦyē-müʦᵘ̈), thoroughly filling, pervading (the mind) (of such things as joy, sorrow, anger, a secret, a quality, or the like). ¶ vyoʦᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. vë̆ʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), conveniently contained in (a receptacle), fitting into.
m. N.P. of the brother of Rāvaṇa (in Skt. Vibhīṣaṇa) (Śiv. 704, 1421; Rām. 32, 39, 637 (his birth), 704, 708, 822, 868, 879, 882, 901, 904, 960, 962, 1001).
f. a fit or proper opportunity, occasion; cf. vil. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an opportunity for revenge to come.

or (as written by Paṇḍits) vēd m. the sacred scriptures of the Hindūs, the Vēda (Śiv. 8, 50, 64, 77, 82, 109, 200, 276, 394, 446, 515, 538, 582, 626, 672, 688, 757, 800, 803, 847, 851, 979, 1006, 1077, 1115-6, 1118, 1158, 1164, 1169, 1186, 1287, 1323, 1368, 1527, 1580, 1753, 1763, 1796, 1837, 1865; Rām. 101, 637, 1140, 1643; K. 96, 568, 666, 1039). ¶ vīda-pāṭh m. (sg. dat. -pāṭhas), reading, or studying, of the Vēda; reciting a text or texts of the Vēda at some religious rite. -pöṭhⁱ m. a professional reciter of vedic texts, as ab. -pūthⁱ f. (sg. dat. -pōthĕ), a book of one or more of the Hindū scriptures. -sökshī m. the evidence of, or proof from, the Vēda (Śiv. 672). -wān m. one well versed in the Vēdas, with their supplementary writings, so as to be able to recite, read, and teach them.
m. (sg. dat. vīdāntas), N. of one of the six systems of Hindū philosophy (Skt. vēdânta), claiming to teach the ultimate aim and scope of the Vēda (Śiv. 1417).
m. N. of a Province in India, the modern Berar (Skt. Vidarbha) (K. 639, 648).
m. N. of a hero of the Mahābhārata. He was the younger brother of Pāṇḍu, and was noted for wisdom, righteousness, and impartiality (Śiv. 1328, K. 1035).

(also written vēg) speed, velocity, rapidity (Śiv. 1867); stream, current. vīga-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), wanting speed, slow; (of a river or the like) having a gentle current, easy, sluggish; inactive, slow, dull, remiss. -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), speedy, rapid; (of a river or the like) having a quick current; quick, apt, intelligent, keen-witted. -woṭᵘ m. the becoming ready, holding oneself in readiness, the being fully equipped (for any work).

f. a certain hill goddess, who wanders through the forests singing and dancing. In the good old times she is said to have been visible to mortal eyes, but nowadays, alas, she is invisible (cf. wan-vᵒ, s.v. wan 1) (El. viganí, a fairy; Śiv. 942, 966, 1454; H. v, 9).
m. the invisible male leader of a company of woodland hill goddesses (see vigiñ).

also written by Paṇḍits vijñān m. knowledge, wisdom, intelligence; discrimination, discernment (Śiv. 1012, 1014, 1695, 1747, 1760); esp. worldly or profane knowledge derived from personal experience (as opposed to gyān, or knowledge of the Supreme) (Śiv. 1063, 1418, 1600, 1660, 1765).

or (Rām. 380) vīh m. dress, appearance; sudden change of condition or appearance, change in a moment from an ordinary state to another (cf. potᵘ vih, p. 788b, l. 15) (Rām. 287, 380; K. 245, 439); airs and graces, affectation (K.Pr. 132). In the old Ksh. of L.V. this word has the form vyuhᵘ, q.v. --gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. successive changes of condition to occur (e.g. a person first moribund, then unconscious, and then reviving, or something first visible, then momentarily invisible, and then again momentarily visible, or sudden colour changes). --dārun -- m.inf. to take a (certain) form, to appear as (such-and-such) (K. 108, 190, 224, 867). --hāwun -- m.inf. to display a change of appearance, (magically) to take on (such-and-such) a form, to change oneself into (such-and-such), disguise oneself (Rām. 362, 985). --hihⁱ hāwȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. as it were to show changes of appearance, to display airs and graces (Rām. 332). --karȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. 'to make changes of condition'; hence, to exhibit coquettish actions (e.g. in dress, in displaying joy or sorrow, anger or serenity, wantonness, amorous sport, artful wiles, and so on, in turns) (Rām. 1143g); to change one's form or appearance (by magic) (Rām. 861). --lāgun -- m.inf., i.q. --dārun, ab. (K. 251).
c.g. coquettish, flirtatious, affected. Cf. vih 2.
m. (f. vihatᵃrĕñ), an old friend, a friend from childhood (? cf. El. vehatir, m. neighbourhood). -bāy f. his wife.
in vijĕ-wāv m. a contrary and stormy wind opposing boats on a navigable river.

m. expansion, wide extent; sa-vikās, that which has wide expanse, the total expanse of creation, the visible creation (L.V. 1); blooming, blossoming. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to cause to expand or to blossom, to cause to rejoice, make happy (Śiv. 1434, 1446).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. vikāsyōv), to become widely expanded, to widen out and extend to some distant limit (L.V. 22).
adj. c.g. frightful, horrible, dreadful; great, huge, broad. vikaṭa-rṻph adj. c.g. huge in form, gigantic (Śiv. 8).
adj. c.g. expanding, blossoming; cheerful, happy (Śiv. 1759).

f., i.q. vēla, q.v. (cf. dŏhᵃ̇lᵃ̇-vᵃ̇, p. 200b, l. 46; naʦan-vᵒ, p. 663b, l. 39; potᵘ vil, p. 788b, l. 19; shāma-vᵒ, p. 882b, l. 1; sōran-vᵒ, p. 937a, l. 9; wadan-vᵒ, p. 1098a, l. 32) (according to El. this word is used toward Islāmābād); a short space of time (Gr.Gr. 13); cf. viz. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the right time, opportunity, or season to come. ¶ vili or (after the word suli) wuli, adv. at (such-and-such) a time (cf. suli vili or suli wuli, p. 909b, l. 14) (K.Pr. 87).
or vilinjᵘ̈ 1, for 2, see vilyungᵘ f. a hanging rail, a rail suspended by both ends from the ceiling of a room (on which garments, blankets, etc., are hung) (K.Pr. 112, 233).
or vilⁱñĕr m. inaccessibility (owing to a tortuous or difficult approach, or to distance); met. difficulty (in performance, intelligibility, or the like). Cf. vilyunᵘ and vilyungᵘ.

f.pl. dejection, disappointment, mortification (caused by the non-receipt of something greatly desired). --wanañĕ -- f.pl.inf. to utter lamentations, to lament (Rām. 276, 1558, 1594). -zār m. repeatedly imploring (for something very necessarily or urgently required, or for the appeasement of a master or member of one's family who is in a rage) (Śiv. 408); cf. villa ta zār, Rām. 276, 1558, and zāra-villa, s.v. zār 1. -zörⁱ m.pl., id.

adj. (f. vilinjᵘ̈ 2, for 1, see vilinj), approached by a tortuous or winding road, inaccessible, difficult of approach; (of some task) difficult to perform, unintelligible, complicated; cf. vilyuñᵘ. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. (of some place formerly accessible) to become accessible with difficulty (owing to some obstacle, or to want of means of access); (of some task, formerly easy and simple) to become difficult, unintelligible, complicated, or the like.

adj. (f. viliñᵘ̈), (of some place) difficult of access (owing to a bad or tortuous road, or to distance); (of a task) difficult (in performance, intelligibility, complexity, or the like). Cf. vilyungᵘ.
m. consideration, reflection, examination, discussion (L.V. 16; Śiv. 1122, 1346, 1858).

or vina postpos. (governing abl. or, in the case of persons, optionally the dat.) without, free from (Śiv. vin, 1215 (abl.), 1451 (dat.), 1624 (dat.); K. vina, 285 (governing nom.)); apart from, distinct from (K. vina, 525 (dat.)). See vĕn.
f. a kind of guitar, the Indian lute. --wāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf., to play the lute (K. 296, 340, 964).
m. (sg. dat. vināyĕkas), a N. of Ganēsh (q.v.), in Skt. Vināyaka. vināyĕka-bal m. N. of a certain site sacred to him (Śiv. 2).
adj. c.g. reversed. --hāwun -- m.inf. to show reversed, to misrepresent (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. vīpⁱladiñ), inundated, flooded; (of a human being) ruined by flood, one whose entire property, house, land, or the like, has been destroyed by flood. Cf. vyūpᵘ.
(? gend.) a fine (in money). Noted only in H. v, 7.

a hero, one who is brave, bold, valiant, courageous (cf. bala-vᵒ, p. 103a, l. 41; dīra-vᵒ, p. 236b, l. 38) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1062, 1487, 1673, 1675, 1694, 1819; Rām. 43, 119, 122, 511, 620, 882, 1299, 1360, 1399, 1401; K. 34, 360, 376, 430, 436, 441, 625, 720, 797-8, 1024); one who is strong, muscular, brawny, stalwart (K. 367); a kind of Bhairava (see börav) who is the local godling of a cemetery or place for burning corpses. ¶ vīra-bạdᵃr or m. N. of a powerful hero created by Shiva (Śiva) from his matted hair (Skt. Vīrabhadra) for the destruction of Daksh's (Dakṣa's) sacrifice (Śiv. 106, 118 ff., 1120, 1562); (in Ksh.) a great hero, champion, mighty man. -pŏrush m. a stalwart man of great strength and determination, a hero (K. 360, 751). ¶ vīrȧnⁱ kār m.pl. a champion's deeds (arduous, formidable, and completely carried through).

or vīrᵘ̈ 1 f. (sg. dat. vīrĕ), the white willow (see El., s.v. vīr for its varieties and the uses to which it is put in Kashmīr) (cf. bŏṭa-vᵒ, p. 138b, l. 48; mushka-vᵒ, p. 597b, l. 27) (El. salix alba; Gr.Gr. 15; L. 68, 70, 79 (Salix tetrasperma); W. 7, 149; Śiv. 1013, 1039, 1553, 1573; Rām. 1634; K.Pr. 7, 257, 260). ¶ vīri-bāman m.pl. the flowers of the willow. -kujᵘ̈ f. a willow tree. -mọ̆nḍᵘ m. the thick, bare, trunk of the willow tree. -māv f. a large branch of the willow tree (suitable for planting as a cutting) (Śiv. 1819, vīrĕ-). -pan m.pl. willow leaves (used medicinally for heart-disease, etc., and as a sudorific). -tīl m. oil extracted from burnt fresh willow twigs (used medicinally for skin diseases). -wār m. a willow grove, a piece of ground planted with lines of willows. -zyunᵘ m. willow firewood.
subst. and adj. c.g. (sg. obl. virakta), one who is free from passion, or worldly attachment (Śiv. 58, 819, 889, 1021, 1540, 1568). Cf. vĕrakh.
f. a roof beam, a ceiling rafter (El. a beam). ¶ virāma-godᵘ m. the empty space between such beams or rafters. -tāh m. a row or series of these beams or rafters.
m. (sg. dat. virāṭas) (in Hindū philosophy) N. of a mystic Being, looked upon as the Supreme Intellect pervading the aggregate of created beings (Skt. Virāj-, sg. nom. Virāṭ).
or (H.) virⁱd, or virud m. (pl. nom. virdⁱ, Rām. 557), habitual practice, regular drill (in any particular subject) (Rām. as ab.); magic skill, magic power (H. ii, 3, 4).

or wuriñ f. a certain forest tree, the hazel (Corylus Colurna, L. 74, 79); its nut (L. 460). ¶ viriñĕ-(wuriñĕ-)hüṭᵘ̈  f. (sg. dat. -hacĕ), the wood of the hazel (noted for its hardness, and used for making household articles, esp. pattens and spoons, see L. 81). -kulᵘ m. the hazel-tree. -tīl m. the oil of the hazel-nut (used as an embrocation for rheumatism, etc.).
or wurⁱñuwⁱ adj. (f. viriñivᵘ̈ or wurⁱñivⁱ), made of the (hard) wood of the viriñ-tree (used for making caskets, stools, or the like).

in virkum-pōsh or virⁱkimⁱ-pōsh m. a certain sweet-smelling yellow flower appearing in early spring on the joints of the hollow stems of a certain creeping plant before the leaves have sprouted. The plant is found on the wuḍars or high plateaux of the Valley.
m. (sg. dat. vīratas), heroism, valour, courage (Śiv. 1819); muscularity, stalwartness, virility.
adj. (f. vīrivᵘ̈), made of willow-wood (e.g. a stool or casket). Cf. vīr 2.
f. (sg. dat. vēri), great liking, enthusiasm, or love (for any thing or work) (Śiv. 1039, K.Pr. 139). Cf. vēr 2.
f. (sg. obl. vēri) (?) a time, occasion; in duka vīrᵘ̈, a twofold occasion; hence, a twin birth (p. 207a, l. 25), so duka-vēri, adv. (id., l. 25).
f. in gar-vīrᵘ̈, a house-lizard (p. 296a, l. 34), q.v.
f. in yāwan-vīrĕ (s.v. yāwun) f.pl. a group of small pimples on the face in the time of youth.
n.ag. (f. visavüñᵘ̈), one who exhibits pleasure, one who becomes pleased or delighted, as in visun, q.v.

or vishwāmithᵃr m. (sg. dat. vishāmitras), N. of a celebrated Hindū sage (in Skt. Viśvāmitra). He was the companion and counsellor of the youthful Rāma, and secured his marriage with Sītā (Rām. 101, 110-1, 124, 135, 1247, 1589, vishā˚; K. 1039, vishwā˚; K.Pr. 233, wĕshámitar).
(usually spelt or) m. an offering made to Vishnu (q.v.) (Śiv. 1069, 1378, 1431, 1635, 1668, 1697).

(but usually spelt vishṇu), or (q.v.) vishn  m. (sg. gen. vishn(ṇ)unᵘ, Śiv. 1200, but vishn(ṇ)u-sondᵘ, Rām. 23) the second deity of the Hindū Triad, Brahmā, Vishnu (Skt. Viṣṇu), and Shiv (Śiva). His duty is that of the preservation of the universe, Brahmā being the Creator, and Shiv (Śiva) the Destroyer. He had ten incarnations, the most celebrated being those of Rām (Rāma-candra) and Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) (Śiv. 6, 31, 77, 96-7, 127, 159, 188, 236, 421, 447, 581, 625, 699, 716, 778, 851, 863, 977, 1141, 1200, 1299, 1433, 1487, 1762; Rām. 23, 47, 368, 589, 1759; K. 4, 10-1, 21, 49, 78, 92, 320, et passim). See also vishn.
or vishŏkarm m. (in Hindū mythology) N. of the architect of the gods (in Skt. Viśvakarman) (Rām. 572, 593, ˚kam; K. 589, 1149, ˚karm).
m. 'He who sustains the universe', a title given to Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 1021, 1162); a title given to Vishnu (Viṣṇu) (Śiv. 1334, 1400). Skt. Viśvambhara.
adj. (f. vishümᵘ̈), uneven, not level; tangled, complicated (L.V. 6).
m. 'the Lord of the Universe', a title of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 153, 1410).

m. 'He whose form is the universe', He who is omnipresent, a title given to Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 903, 1021, 1177, 1622); a title given to Vishnu (Viṣṇu) (Śiv. 1399, 1492); the entire universe in manifest form (K. 159, 160, 411).
m. 'the Lord of the universe', a title given to Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 858, 936, 1177, 1400; K. 876).
for words beginning thus, see under vishŏᵒ.
adj. c.g. one who has trust or faith, confiding, trustful (Śiv. 1759).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. visyōv), to become pleased, delighted (e.g. at obtaining something wished for, or at the successful accomplishment of something).
in viṭa-viṭa adv. dilatorily, by slow degrees, little by little (u.w. vbs. of giving, taking, doing a task, and the like).

m. a kind of Börav (see p. 129b, l. 44) or local godling who acts as a Khitra-pāl (p. 423b, l. 6) or guardian of cultivated fields (Śiv. 1683); met. a Brāhmaṇ who is a greedy eater of oblations (cf. the next). -brôhmun m. (sg. dat. -bröhmanas), a low-class Brāhmaṇ (not allowed to intermarry with members of the caste of more respectable employment) who conducts the worship of such a Vitāl, and who lives on the offerings, etc., made to it. -kāv m. 'a Vitāl-crow', a mean beggar (greedy, persistent, and clamorous in begging). ¶ vitāla-shēṭh f. (sg. dat. -shīṭhᵘ̈), the sixth lunar day of the dark half of the month of Pŏh (December-January) on which a festival is held and offerings are made to a local Vitāl. -sondᵘ m. N. of a tract said to be haunted by Vitāls lying between Śrīnagar and the Ḍal lake; cf. the next. ¶ vitālüñᵘ̈ marg f. N. of a site near Śrīnagar where a Vitāl is said to have helped King Pravarasēna II to found that city (see RT.Tr. iii, 340 ff., and II, 442).

f. a certain disease, the symptoms of which are said to be small pustules on the throat, palate, and tongue. In the case of children and cattle it is said to be easily curable, but in the case of invalids seriously ill, it is generally incurable.

or vizᵘ̈ f. (sg. abl. vizi), a time, a particular moment of time (mostly --˚) (cf. khĕñi-vizi, p. 428a, l. 41; kŏ-vizi, p. 496b, l. 22; lạgᵃna-vizi charun, p. 512b, l. 15; nina-vizᵘ̈, p. 672b, l. 46; pönʦi vizi, p. 743b, l. 25; prath vizi, p. 769a, ll. 48 ff.; pĕwan-vizᵘ̈, p. 811a, l. 17; sahār-vizᵘ̈, p. 890b, l. 32; sōran-vizᵘ̈, p. 937a, l. 10; tami vizi, p. 968a, l. 30; trĕyĕ vizi, p. 1022b, l. 14; ʦōri vizi, p. 1079b, l. 45; yīʦi vizi, s.v. yūtᵘ 2; dŏyĕ vizi, s.v. zᵃh) (Gr.Gr. 157-8; Gr.M.; W. 149; Śiv. 287, 1331; K. 575, 1027; YZ. 146; K.Pr. 31, 51, 77, 83, 153, 260); a period of time (cf. hĕchan- vᵒ, p. 321b, l. 36; paran vᵒ, p. 762b, l. 28) (El. viz or, in Śrīnagar, vis, a short space of time; Rām. 1709); a time, a season (H. ix, 8). Cf. vēla and vil. ¶ vizi na-ta kŏzi adv. at the wrong time instead of the (right) time. ¶ vizan 1 (for 2, 3, see s.vv.) adv. at (such-and-such) a time (of the day), as in köjⁱ vizan, in the forenoon; pĕshᵉ̆n vizan, in the early afternoon; digar vizan, in the late afternoon. --bögⁱ -- or --bögin -- adv. id., but rather more indefinite, as in digar vizan bögin, in the late afternoon.
(for 1, see viz) m. the obtainment of the proper or expected result of any action or course of action.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. vizanôwᵘ), to cause (grain, etc.) to be winnowed; to winnow, sift (grain, etc.). vizanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vizanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), winnowed, sifted.
f. Indian hemp, bhang (cf. banga); the intoxicating drink made from this (Śiv. 189, 1017).
m. N. of Shiv (Śiva), in Skt. Vijayêśvara, as the presiding deity of Vĕjabrôrᵘ (q.v.) (R.T.Tr. II, 463; Śiv. 1161).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. vyuzᵘ, f. vizᵘ̈), to winnow, sift (grain, etc.). vyuzᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vizᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), winnowed.
or wōvᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 1 (for 2, see wōwᵃrun) f. a female weaver (Gr.Gr. 35).
m. an old man (El.), i.q. vrĕdd, q.v.

m. (sg. dat. vratas), a religious act of devotion or austerity (esp. a vow of fasting), a vowed observance (Śiv. 285, 526, 758-9, 1168, 1408, 1583, 1905; Rām. 7; K. 274). --dārun -- m.inf. to take or keep a vow (of fasting, etc.) (K. 266, 1168).
adj. c.g. old, aged, advanced in years (El. vrad, an old man; Rām. 548).
or (Śiv., Rām. 1108g, and K.) vrush f. the zodiacal sign Taurus (El. warish; Śiv. 475; Rām. 1108g, 1280; K. 57, 130).
or (Śiv.) vrushĕb m. a bull (El. vrĕshib; Śiv. 394, 409, 618, 817, 894, 1188, 1564, 1877).
or (Śiv.) vrushĕbāsan m. he who is seated on, or rides upon, a bull (Skt. Vṛṣabhâsana), a N. of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 160, 193, 363, 975, 1040, 1407).
m. (sg. dat. vrĕttāntas), a topic, subject (Gr.M.); condition, state (Gr.M.); a story, tale, narrative (Gr.M.).
m. a tree, in kalpa-vruksh, p. 440b, l. 39. It is a borrowed Skt. (vṛkṣa) word (Śiv. 1013, 1213, 1553).
m. N. of a forest in India, one of the scenes of the youthful exploits of Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) (Śiv. 1375, 1440; K. 182).
f. (sg. dat. vrushciki), the zodiacal sign Scorpio (Skt. Vṛścika) (K. 132). I.q. warcakh, q.v.
m. N. of a demon in the form of a bull, who was killed by Krushn (Kṛṣṇa), in Skt. Vṛṣabhâsura (K. 350).

f. (sg. dat. vrĕʦᵘ̈), conduct, behaviour (which may be either active, see pravruth, or inactive, see nivruth) (Śiv. 1022, 1048, 1054, 1057, 1369, 1427 (the vruth which is nivruth, contrasted with pravruth), 1437, 1469, 1753, 1821, 1860, 1864).

f. (sg. dat. vruttiyĕ), noted only in Śiv. 1694, where it is translated by the Skt. taralavāsanā, i.e. transient emotion or transient desire. It seems, however, merely to be another form of vruth, q.v.
f. (sg. dat. wanjĕ) (a woman who is) lame, crippled, halt. Cf. wongᵘ, f. vünjᵘ̈, f. sg. dat. also wanjĕ.

(for 4, see wanun), sometimes written wañᵘ̈ f. a wood, or grove, of trees (esp. when all of the same kind), an orchard, a fruit garden (cf. kulⁱ-vⁱ, p. 439a, l. 8; mĕwa-vᵒ, p. 611a, l. 37; tᵃla-vᵃ, p. 995a, l. 40; tēl-vᵒ, p. 998a, l. 11; ṭanga-vᵒ, p. 1010b, l. 12; ʦēra-vᵒ, p. 1079b, l. 7; wath-vᵒ and wata-vᵒ, s.v. wath) (Gr.Gr. 37; W. 144, wanⁱ; K.Pr. 135, 246, wani); a mountain path (cf. dōla-vᵒ, p. 211b, l. 18). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to plant and keep up an orchard or fruit garden (esp. as a work of religious merit). ¶ wañi-rāwul adj. (f. -rāvüjᵘ̈), 'one who leads astray in a fruit-garden'; hence, one who has taken to vicious ways, and leads others astray by his example.

(for 4, see wanun) f. (between two persons) similarity, or equality, of condition (such as happiness, misery, gain, loss, sickness, health, sudden death, and so on) (K.Pr. 91); cf. wanan. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such similarity of condition to occur (as when one person's condition becomes the same as that of another).

f. of worᵘ 1, q.v. a small lump of pulse, beans, or the like, pounded, fried in oil or clarified butter, spiced, and used as a condiment to season cooked food (cf. ünzᵘ̈-wᵘ̈, p. 36b, l. 23; khal-wᵒ, p. 397a, l. 38; mahā-vᵒ, p. 553a, l. 18; masāla-vᵒ, p. 599b, l. 15) (El. wȧir; Gr.Gr. 10; L. 260, wari, describes three varieties; K.Pr. 66, 220); a ball of rice (like a rissole) fried in grease, and eaten on festive occasions (cf. zanga- vᵒ, s.v. zang 2). In these senses, the word is naturally mostly used in the plural (warĕ); cf. worᵘ 1. --bazüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to fry one of these lumps; met. to busy oneself in helping on another's work. ¶ warĕ-āra m. a number of these fried lumps strung together like a necklace. -bata m. rice-rissoles prepared as ab. -pholᵘ m. a single one of these lumps. warĕ ta wadạvĕ karañĕ f.pl.inf. 'to make rissoles and festivities', to make great rejoicings (e.g. on the reappearance or regainment of something destroyed, or the like) (K. 173, wari for warĕ).
f. a small receptacle, box, jar, in ṭĕkⁱ-vürⁱ, p. 1049b, l. 4, q.v. Cf. worᵘ 3, the m. form.
a jingle of lürᵘ̈ in lürᵘ̈-würᵘ̈, p. 531a, l. 32, q.v.

f. (sg. dat. wacĕ), a collection of separate things brought together, an assemblage (of things), a lobulated mass (cf. bŏka-wᵒ, p. 99b, l. 46; hirⁱ-wⁱ, p. 367a, l. 49; phã-vᵒ, p. 698a, l. 15; trika-vᵒ, p. 1023b, l. 10; ʦȧkⁱ-vⁱ, p. 1067b, l. 5; esp. a cob of maize or the like (cf. dŏda-wᵒ, p. 190b, l. 8; makāyi-wᵒ, p. 563b, l. 12); a bringing together, joining up (cf. lata-wᵒ, p. 537a, l. 7); a groove (in a beam) into which other boards fit (cf. kura-wᵒ, p. 467a, l. 40); (in a garment or the like) a gusset, slit (cf. cāka-wᵒ, p. 169b, l. 13; gal-wᵒ, p. 282b, l. 15; kaʦha-wᵒ, p. 492b, l. 49). ¶ wacĕ f.pl. an assembled group of distinct things (cf. kŏṭhⁱ-wⁱ, p. 489a, l. 30); esp. the total of the seeds in a cob of maize or the like; a wheel-like article with spokes united at the hub. -kônᵘ f. the ball of thread as formed on a spinning wheel. -kāñᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. id., but smaller than the preceding, and somewhat long. -yẹ̆ndᵃr m. a machine for twisting two strands of thread (as formed on a spinning wheel) into one, and forming the doubled thread into a new ball.
f. (sg. dat. wacĕ), a measure of weight, a weight weighing two seers (or four pounds) (cf. Hindī bāṭ); anything weighing two seers.
f. (sg. dat. -wacĕ), a small round stone, a pebble (cf. kah-wᵒ, p. 425b, l. 36, and Rām. 1607, not 1609, as there misprinted; nal-vᵒ, p. 632a, l. 3). Cf. waṭh.

(for 1, see wasun, for 2, 3, see wothᵘ 2, 3) f. opening, uncovering, in the following:-- vüʦhᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. revelation to occur, (a secret) to become revealed or published abroad. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to publish (a secret) abroad, to reveal (a secret). Cf. wothᵘ 2.

f. (sg. dat. vyözᵘ̈), disease, illness, distress, suffering (Śiv. 447, 813; Rām. 20, 114, 293, 770, 994, 1570, 1604, 1630, 1686). --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. distress to mount (on a person), to suffer distress or tribulation (e.g. from being charged with another's fault, from having to perform a too difficult task, or to carry a too heavy burden). --lārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. tribulation to adhere, (owing to bad association or infection) to suffer, through gaining a reputation for immorality, dishonesty, or the like, or through being attacked by some contagious disease, and so on. --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to raise suffering', to relieve another from distress or suffering (such as calumny, bad repute), to rescue him (from debauchery or from some serious disease); some public calamity (such as famine, general immorality, general evil repute, epidemic, etc.) to occur. --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. general tribulation (such as epidemic, drought, floods, pillage, thieving, anarchy, evil report, etc.) to arise. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. distress to come (esp. from calumny, false accusations, a reputation for debauchery or the like).
m. grammar (according to the Hindū system; a word borrowed from Skt. vyākaraṇa) (Gr.Gr. 199, Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. pervading, diffused, widely spread, extending all over, or through, any thing or place (Śiv. 105, 115, 156, 212, 739, 884, 1369, 1510, 1518).

n.ag. (f. vyāpavüñᵘ̈) (of a law, order, command, skill in, or knowledge of, any subject) pervading, spread over a wide area, universally prevailing (cf. vyāpun 1); one who (from small beginnings) has become able to succeed in the accomplishment (of some difficult work) (cf. vyāpun 2).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. vyôpᵘ), to pervade, to be widely distributed through or over (esp. of the Supreme Deity, of a command, or of some branch of knowledge) (K. 320, 509); cf. vĕpun. vyôpᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vyöpᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), pervaded, etc., as ab.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. vyāpyōv), to become able to reach to (e.g. a dwarf trying to, and succeeding in, reaching something high aloft), to become able to carry out some very difficult work, to travel over a very arduous and lengthy road, and so on. vyāpyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vyāpyē-müʦᵘ̈), become able to reach to, become able to attain to success, etc., as ab.

f. (sg. dat. vyāpᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), pervading, general spreading over, or through, a wide area (cf. vyāpun 1); the becoming able to succeed (in some very difficult work) (cf. vyāpun 2); (in the series of exercises of a Yōgī ascetic) the time, or turn, for any one of them.
in dyār-vyār, p. 270a, l. 38, a jingle of dyār, q.v.

m. N. of a celebrated Hindū saint and author (Skt. Vyāsa), said to have compiled the Vēdas, the Mahābhārata, and the Purāṇas (Śiv. 1077, 1355, 1376, 1433, 1466; Rām. 1681; K. 990, 1038, 1176); met. any man of great and wide learning, who is a master of many branches of knowledge.
adj. (f. vë̆dᵘ̈rᵘ̈), (of some thing or action) hostile, adverse, antagonistic (to another's actions, character, or the like).

adj. (m. sg. dat. vĕdis; f. vë̆zᵘ̈), known (by recognition or experience) (L.V. 56, K.Pr. 229); --˚, one who knows, as in tattwa-vᵒ, one who knows and understands the tattwas (see tattwa) (L.V. 20). -motᵘ adj. (f. vë̆zᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), become known, ascertained, realized (by memory, testing, or the like). --rōzun -- m.inf. to continue well known (from recognition or previous experience), not to be forgotten, to be familiar. --thawun -- m.inf. to impress the knowledge (of something) on oneself, to note carefully. ¶ vĕdⁱ-prāh m. fickle-mindedness, heedlessness of warning or instruction.
m. N. of a demon killed by Krushn (Kṛṣṇa), in Skt Vyōmâsura (K. 388).
adj. (f. vë̆ngᵘ̈ or vë̆njᵘ̈), wanting a limb, maimed; (of some thing or work) wanting an essential part. Cf. wongᵘ and vĕngun.

f. (sg. dat. vyöpᵃrüñᵃ), causing to pervade (from small beginnings), causing to become widely spread (esp. of some person originally of petty influence), gradual extension (of power and authority) over a wide area (as a conflagration may spread from a single spark of fire).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. vyöpᵒrᵒ) (of some person or thing originally petty) to cause to pervade or be widely spread, to cause (one's own power and authority) gradually to spread over a wide area, (of a spark or little fire) to cause (a conflagration) to spread over a wide area, and so on.
m. (sg. dat. vĕsis), a man's friend, comrade, chum, crony, pal (usually of the same age); N. of a village of Kashmīr near Islāmābād. Cf. vĕs.

adj. (f. vë̆ṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat. vĕchĕ; vĕṭhiñᵘ̈ (q.v.) is also said to be a fem. of this word, but is used only in a bad sense, Gr.Gr. 38), fat, plump, stout, corpulent (cf. buthⁱ-vⁱ, p. 143a, l. 14; gala-vᵒ, p. 282b, l. 4; mandal-vᵒ, p. 576a, l. 46; nala-vᵒ, p. 632a, l. 36) (El. vyauṭh, vyuṭ, vyuṭh; Gr.Gr. 38, 93; Gr.M.; L. 460, viot; W. 20, vio˙t); big, bulky, great, large (cf. ȧchⁱ-vⁱ, p. 9a, l. 5; kala-vᵒ, p. 435b, l. 30; pĕlⁱ-vⁱ, p. 814a, l. 44; wuṭha-vᵒ, p. 1159b, l. 10) (Rām. 976, K. 686); gross, coarse (El. vyuṭ vyuṭh, with the additional meaning of 'swift'); (of cloth) coarse (Gr.M.); cf. vĕṭha. --pahān -- adj. (f. vë̆ṭhᵘ̈ pahān), somewhat, or a little, stout, big, etc. (as compared with others) (Gr.Gr. 93). --pūṭhᵘ -- adj. (f. vë̆ṭhᵘ̈ pūthᵘ̈), (of a garment or the like) too stout, too thick, too coarse. --vyoṭhᵘ -- adj. (f. vë̆ṭhᵘ̈ vë̆ṭhᵘ̈), in every respect stout, fat, big, coarse, etc. (e.g. of a man, or of grain).

adj. (f. vë̆ʦᵘ̈) [this word is used only --˚. I.K. (iv, 26, 27) treats it as a secondary suffix signifying possession, when the thing possessed accompanies the possessor, but does not actually form part of him or it. Cf. Gr.Gr. 137, read with suff. No. 9 on p. 136] possessing plentifully, richly endowed with (cf. barsā-vᵒ, p. 127a, l. 45; dana-vᵒ, p. 222a, l. 26; rǖnⁱ-vⁱ, p. 835b, l. 48; sāwayĕ-vᵒ, p. 955b, l. 15) (Gr.M.); (more usually) possessed by, pervaded by, suffused with, full of (cf. bāwa-vᵒ, p. 147a, l. 7; bayĕ-vᵒ, p. 148b, l. 36; dŏkha-vᵒ, p. 206b, l. 21; drāga-vᵒ, p. 241b, l. 35; dūshĕ-vᵒ, p. 253b, l. 2; gardi-vᵒ, p. 300b, l. 2; hayāh-vᵒ, p. 364a, l. 29; mōda-vᵒ, p. 549a, l. 35; māna-vᵒ, p. 573a, l. 27; mandacha-vᵒ, p. 575b, l. 17; marga-vᵒ, p. 590b, l. 22; mātama-vᵒ, p. 607a, l. 16; phala-vᵒ, p. 692b, l. 27; pāpa-vᵒ, p. 749a, l. 18; prāha-vᵒ, p. 757b, l. 7; pranayĕ-vᵒ, p. 764b, l. 10; prayĕma-vᵒ, p. 774a, l. 49; rāga-vᵒ, p. 828a, l. 17; rūga-vᵒ, p. 828b, l. 3; sŏbāwa-vᵒ, p. 862b, l. 32; shīla-vᵒ, p. 880b, l. 18; shurⁱ-vⁱ, p. 890b, l. 19; shĕrmi-vᵒ, p. 893a, l. 39; sᵃniha-vᵃ, p. 921b, l. 29; sraha-vᵒ, p. 934b, l. 44; wuprīda-vᵒ, p. 1132b, l. 41). Cf. vĕʦun.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. vyözᵘ̈ladiñ), suffering from disease, distress, etc. Cf. vyād.

m. (sg. dat. vīgis), a figure or picture drawn on the ground with turmeric and coloured powder used at weddings and at the investiture of a boy with the sacred thread. At a wedding the bride and bridegroom are, and, at the investiture, the boy after purificatory ceremonies is, seated on it. A ceremony of lustration round them or him is then performed (L. 261, 461, wegu; Śiv. 668, 971, 1089-90, 1097, 1152, 1492; Rām. 765; K.Pr. 130-1, sg. obl. wígi). ¶ vēgi-wothᵘ adj. (f. -vüʦhᵘ̈) (just) descended from the vgūgᵘ, i.e. one who is just married, one whose marriage has just been completed (cf. Rām. 765). --wothᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. vüʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), a married man (or woman).

m. (pl. nom. vihⁱ), sudden change from one condition to another; hence, the sudden 'sport' (līlā) of the Divinity, by which He manifests Himself in creation (L.V. 109). This is an old word, its modern representative is vih, q.v.

m. (sg. dat. vīpis, abl. vēpi), an inundation, flood. ¶ vīpⁱ-dĕv m. 'an inundation-devil', a deluge, a violent inundation (causing loss of life and property, supposed to resemble the work of an infuriated demon). ¶ vīpis-kyutᵘ adv. at, or in, the time of a deluge (e.g. born at such, or departed, or given, at such a time).
m. (sg. dat. vīris, abl. vēri), flower-nectar (H. ix, 2); --˚ any similar plant-exudation (cf. samaki-vᵒ, p. 913a, l. 2).

m. (sg. dat. viʦis), the collection of what remains over after meeting the necessary expense of any work, saving up such remains (Gr.Gr. 95); saved up wealth, savings. --karun -- m.inf. to save up, put by, store up what (money or goods) one receives. --pôʦᵘ -- or --pūʦᵘ -- m. money or goods saved up from old times, old savings (either inherited or accumulated by oneself, or both); a collection of odds and ends, an omnium gatherum (Gr.Gr. 95). --thawun -- m.inf. to put by savings, to save up. ¶ viʦis thawun m.inf. to put by for saving, to store up as savings.

و. The twentieth (or, if we count the aspirates ch, kh, ph, th, ṭh, and ʦh, and also the sibilant sh as separate letters, the twenty-seventh) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet when written in the Roman character, the twenty-ninth (or, if we count ʦ, ʦh, and z as separate letters, the thirty-second) consonant when written in the Śāradā or in the Nāgarī character, and the thirty-third consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. Its Kāshmīrī name is washĕ wö. It is generally sounded like the bi-labial w of Panjābī, not like the dento-labial w of English, but, as in Panjābī, the sound fluctuates between that of a sound approaching that of the English w and that of a sound approaching that of an English v. As a rule, the v-sound is heard before a palatal vowel or semi-vowel, such as e, i, ü, or y, or when it is final, while the w-sound is heard in all other cases. Thus, the name of the chief river of Kashmīr (the Jehlam of India) is Vĕth, not Wĕth; 'he will become' is bŏvi, not bŏwi; karawunᵘ, a doer, has its feminine karavüñᵘ̈; 'he became' is bŏvyōv, not bŏwyōw; and the word for 'wind' is wāv, not wāw. Examples of the w-sound are the first letter in wāv, just quoted; rawa, a blanket; wŏpazun, to become; and rāwun, to be lost. In this dictionary, I have endeavoured throughout to represent the w-sound by w, and the v-sound by v, but I fear that I have not always been consistent, and that, especially in the earlier pages, I have sometimes written w when I should have written v, but such slips can easily be corrected by paying attention to the foregoing rules. ¶ The character wa is also used to represent the vowel-sound of ŏ or, when modified by a mātrā-vowel, of ọ̆ or ŏ̈ (see page 4b, ll. 3 ff.). This only occurs when the wa immediately follows a consonant, in which case it has this force alone and is never used with a consonantal force. Thus, to become, is bŏwun, not bwawun; a wound, is chŏkh, not chwakh; milk, is dŏd, not dwad, and so on, whenever wa immediately follows a consonant. If, however, a wa is initial, or immediately follows a vowel, it retains the sound of wa, as in wawun, to sow; korᵘwa, he was made by you. ¶ As explained on pp. 4b, ll. 11 ff., and 5a, ll. 47 ff., the sounds of ŏ and u are interchangeable in Kāshmīrī, both in speaking and writing. Indeed, most Kāshmīrīs seem to be unable to distinguish between the two, the sound that to English ears appears to be that of ŏ being that most commonly used for both. Hence, when a word containing the letter ŏ is not found in the present work, it should be looked for as if it had u instead of ŏ, and vice versa. ¶ In Kāshmīrī, neither ŏ nor u can begin a word, a w being prefixed to these sounds when they occur in such a position, though often omitted in writing. Thus, the Skt. upâya, a device, becomes in Ksh. wupāy or wŏpāy, and the Skt. udāharaṇa, an example, becomes wudāharan or wŏdāharan.
conj. and (cf. hörⁱ-wa-harȧdⁱ, p. 344a, l. 39) (H. x, 14).
conj. or (L.V. 64). wā... wā, either... or (L.V. 8).
m. wā wā interj. O fie! (W. 101).

(? cf. wöñᵘ̈ 5) in the following:--wã̄-dab m. a sudden fall backwards (either accidental or caused by another's action). wã̄ yiñᵘ̈ f.inf. an evil repute or bad name (whether deserved or undeserved) to be acquired. Cf. wāman 2.
m. an epidemic disease, plague, cholera, pestilence (K.Pr. 227). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. such an epidemic to come (i.e. occur).
m. the arrival at, or attainment to, any state or condition.

m. internal tightness, the having the contents tightly held (e.g. a walnut the kernel of which is tightly contained within the shell and is difficult to extract); met. the tightness (of a miser or of a secretive person).

m. (sg. dat. wachas), the breast, chest, bosom (El wach and wachh; Śiv. 797, 1445; K. 124, 491; K.Pr. 148. 166, 199). -dọ̆gᵘ m. a blow on the chest, repeated beating of one's own breast (in token of envy or jealousy on hearing of another's success). -dọ̆gᵘdyunᵘ m.inf. to beat one's breast, as ab. -dọ̆gᵘ lagun m.inf. a reason for beating one's own breast (as ab.) to happen. --ʦēṭun -- m.inf. to beat one's own breast (in sorrow, etc.). --ʦēṭay -- f. beating one's own breast (in sorrow). ¶ wacha-dara m. stoutness and broadness of the chest (of a man). -kāñĕ f.pl. the ribs (El. wachakányi, the hypochondrium). -kāñĕ nērañĕ f. pl. inf. the ribs to stand out, the chest to look like a skeleton (from disease, starvation, or the like). -phāh m. 'chest warmth', taking a child and cuddling it to the breast; met. affectionate nurture, loving protection and support. --wacha -- m.pl. the act of beating one's own breast (in sorrow, terror, or the like). --wacha dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to display sorrow by such beating. --wacha lagȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. a cause (such as another's tyranny, etc.) for beating one's own breast, as ab., to arise.
m. unwillingness to return a thing deposited, an intention to misappropriate property held in trust (K.Pr. 161). --karun -- m.inf. to misappropriate property held in trust.

f. (sg. dat. vüḍᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 71), profit (in a mercantile transaction); (in a sale) discount, an agreed reduction in price (to complete a speedy sale). In H. v, 1, the word is translated 'crookedness', said with regard to a ring by the person to whom it is offered for sale, apparently to cheapen it. vüḍᵘ̈-pĕṭhdyunᵘ̈ m.inf. to invest money in the hope of profit.

m. speech, words, talk (cf. öhī-wᵒ, p. 17b, l. 13) (Śiv. 1460, K.Pr. 15); an answer, reply (Śiv. 449, K.Pr. 199); a discussion, dispute, controversy (cf. ʦŏʦan-wᵒ, p. 1090a, l. 12); a habit, custom (cf. ṭọ̆ṭᵃran-wᵃ, p. 1045a, l. 41); --˚ irritating, causing annoyance (cf. phāṭawan-wᵒ, p. 719b, l. 25; pōrawan-wᵒ, p. 772b, l. 35; ṭŏṭan-wᵒ, p. 1044b, l. 11; ʦānan-wᵒ, p. 1075b, l. 14; wŏthan-wᵒ, s.v. wŏthun); --˚ measuring, weighing or counting out (cf. nika-cirna-wᵒ, p. 627b, l. 1; phuṭa-wᵒ, p. 717a, l. 10; pājĕ-wᵒ, p. 723b, l. 41; paĩsa-wᵒ, p. 777a, l. 10; pushĕran-wᵒ, p. 782b, l. 30; pī̃ʦa-wᵒ, p. 807b, l. 28; sēra-wᵒ, p. 929b, l. 2; ṭũ̄̈kⁱ-wⁱ, p. 991b, l. 5; traka-wᵒ, p. 1023b, l. 34; ʦringa-wᵒ, p. 1082b, l. 47); clapping the hands (in tune to music or the like) (see --tulun, bel.); clapping the hands (in derision, or to startle) (K. 222, 232); --˚ one who is employed in any very petty matter or affair (cf. phĕka-wᵒ, p. 689a, l. 49; phȧlⁱ-wⁱ, p. 694b, l. 26; phĕrⁱ-wⁱ, p. 721b, l. 32); see also wád, s.v. wāda. --aʦun-- m.inf. (in an argument) to become agitated by an opponent's words. --karun -- m.inf. to argue mutually, discuss (concerning, pĕṭh) (Gr.M.); to quarrel or argue (with someone) (Rām. 1210; K.Pr. 64, 116); (in an argument) to abuse each other (K.Pr. 147). --tulun -- m.inf. to raise speech, to raise conversation, to hold discourse (concerning, gen.) (K. 981); to clap the hands (in tune to music, etc.) (K. 294). --ʦānun -- m.inf. (in an argument) to cause an opponent to become agitated by one's language. -wād m. answering (a teacher or the like) insolently (El. wádwád karun, to answer). -wād-kuʦurᵘ adj. (f. -wād-kuʦürᵘ̈), 'an answering-back puppy', a pupil who insolently answers his teacher's, or his superior's, animadversions. -wād-lŏgulᵘ adj. (f. -wād-lŏgüjᵘ̈), a pupil (or the like) who habitually answers his superiors insolently. --wŏthun -- m.inf. (in an argument) to become annoyed, or agitated, by the opponent's language.

m. cheating (at gaming or the like); an inguinal bubo. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. (in gambling) cheating, or an accidental breach of the rules (favouring one party as against the other) to occur. --karun -- m.inf. dishonestly to dispute the result (in gambling).
in wada-wad f. the weeping together of a number of assembled persons.

m. a promise, agreement, guarantee (Gr.M., Rām. 1711, K.Pr. 178) (wāda- y-Khŏdā, a vow by God, H. xii, 7, 15); (esp.) an agreement entered into for borrowing money (L. 387, wád); an appointment, assignation (e.g. an agreement about a particular time or place) (Rām. 661); a pre-determined occurrence, that which is pre-destined (Rām. 222, 681, 1492); a time, or period, fixed by agreement or by fate (Rām. 950, 1143h). --karun -- m.inf. to promise (Gr.M.). --thawun -- m.inf. to make an appointment (for something), to fix a time (for doing something). --wātun -- m.inf. the agreed time to arrive; esp. the destined moment of death to come.
in adal-wadal, etc., p. 14b, l. 18, i.q. badal, q.v. (K.Pr. 2, 102).

f. distress, pain, trouble (from extreme exertion, insult, abuse, or the like) (cf. ganḍȧrⁱ-wⁱ, p. 291a, l. 39; khĕji-wᵒ, p. 305a, l. 1; waṭha-wᵒ, s.v. waṭha). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such distress to be experienced.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wadanôwᵘ), to cause to weep, to cause to wail, lament, etc. (caus. of wadun, q.v. in all its meanings) (El., Śiv. 1394, K.Pr. 166). wadanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wadanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to weep, etc., made to weep, etc. (by someone).
n.ag. (f. wadavüñᵘ̈), one who laments, wails, weeps (El. wadawun); one who is ready to cry on the slightest provocation, a cry-baby.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wodᵘ, f. vüzᵘ̈; 2 p.p. wazōv. This verb is impers. in the tenses formed from the p.p.) to lament, wail, cry, weep, sob, mourn (cf. bāki wᵒ, p. 99b, l. 12; hamāl wᵒ, p. 334a, l. 15; mājĕ-wᵒ, p. 557b, l. 36; tāli-gulⁱ ladith wᵒ, p. 997b, l. 17) (El.; Gr.M.; L.V. 67; Śiv. 707, 832; Rām. 64, 157, 167, 183, 198-9, 200, 220-1, 226, 229, 234, 253, 258-9, 261, 264, 267, 277-8, 283, 358, 378, 388, 430, 439, 465-6, 538-9, 648, etc.; K. 289, 454, 479, 507, 801-2, 857, 859; H. vii, 16, 25; ix, 1; xi, 5; YZ. 43, 55, 125, 156, 183, 455; K.Pr. 36, 145); to be abundant, to abound, to be more than sufficient (Śiv. 1565). ¶ wadan-bāpār m. (of a number of assembled people) united lamentation or wailing, etc. -bāṭh or -bã̄ṭh m. (sg. dat. -bāṭas, etc.), long continued crying or wailing (esp. of children or women after a scolding or abuse). -biṭh or -biṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -bichĕ), a wailing-assembly, i.e. (in time of grief) a number of persons assembled together and weeping; the place where such persons assemble. -vil f. the time, or proper occasion, for wailing (e.g. a loss, grief, fear, or the hungriness of a child). -vil lāgüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to start a time of wailing (for any of the ab. causes). ¶ wadān riwān pres. part. used as adv., with great wailing or lamentation. ¶ wadani bĕhun m.inf. to sit down to wail, to weep and wail (in presence of some calamity). ¶ wadanas aʦun m.inf. 'to enter weeping', i.e. to become absorbed in weeping (at some injury done by another), to begin violent and prolonged weeping (K. 82, 91, 236, 407). --ʦānun -- m.inf. to set (a person) weeping, to give cause for weeping (by opposition, terrifying, blaming, attacking, or the like).

or (K. 669) wānur m. (sg. dat. wã̄daras, Gr.Gr. 51; f. wā̃dürᵘ̈ or wã̄darĕñ), a monkey (El. wándur, a monkey; wándúr, a bear; cf. ponzᵘ 1, which also means both 'monkey' and 'bear'; Gr.Gr. 51; Gr.M.; L. 108, wândar; Rām. 68, 444, 452, 459, 466, 542, 746, 778, 785, 794, 832, 864, 916, 931, 965, 983, 990, 996, 1003, 1070, 1134, 1143k, 1408; K. 19, 155, 888; also 669, 679, where it can only mean 'bear'. wã̄dar-bacĕ m. a young monkey. -rāj m. 'monkey-rule'; hence, a time of utter irreligion and great oppression (K.Pr. 9).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wạḍᵃrôwᵃ), to bury in the ground (e.g. in order to hide something); to bury, inter (a corpse); to hide, conceal (an action, quality, or the like). wạḍᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. wạḍᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), buried (as ab.); interred (as ab.); concealed (as ab.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wạḍᵒrᵒ), to bury in the ground; to hide, conceal (an action, quality or the like).

or wadạv f. (sg. dat. wadạvi. The pl. nom., wadạvĕ, is often written wadạvi. The pl. dat. is usually written wadạvĕn); (on the occasion of some happy event, such as the birth of a son, his marriage, the receipt of an honour, recovery from illness, safe arrival after a difficult journey, or the like) rejoicing, festivity, congratulations (Rām. 1274; K. 99, 103, 113, 173, 567, 833; K.Pr. 218, wadiwih). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to offer congratulations (as ab.) (cf. warĕ ta wadạvĕ karañĕ, s.v. vürᵘ̈ 1). --ladüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to distribute gifts on such an event; (esp. at a marriage, the bride's relations) to make presents (to the bridegroom's relations). ¶ wadạvi-bôgᵘ m. a present made on such an occasion. -bata m. a dinner given, or a present of dainty food sent, on such an occasion.

f. an iron clamp holding a box, or the like, together. -rūg or wạdᵃri-rūg m. continual irritation caused by the ill-temper or abuse (or the like) of one's own closely-related people (e.g. wife, husband, father, father-in-law, and so on). -rūg aʦun m.inf. such irritation to begin to be felt.
(? spelling and gender) i.q. pát, q.v. (L. 68).

f. a bridle (W. 150; Śiv. 1562, K.Pr. 257); a rein; a tether. --raṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to seize the bridle', to coax (some wayward person) to subjection, to tame, civilize (Śiv. 1854, caus.). --zānüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to acknowledge the bridle', to recognize (from previous experience) that so-and-so is the only source from which a desired object can be obtained. ¶ waga-ḍolᵘ m. a gradual depression or low spot (e.g. in the ground, or on the roof of a house). ¶ wagi anun m.inf. to bring under or to the bridle, to bring under subjection (L.V. 37). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take (a horse) by the bridle (L.V. 69). --raṭun -- m.inf. to hold (a horse) by the bridle (L.V. 26).
adv. and the rest, etcetera, and so forth (Gr.M.).
f. a woman who (for want of a home of her own) lives in another's house; the wife of a man who (for similar reasons) lives in another's house.
f. a slip of thin iron or other metal fastened round the corners, etc., of a box or the like, to strengthen it.
m. a cowherd, göwālā; a milk-seller. -bāy f. his wife.

or waguwᵘ m. a reed mat, matting (cf. dā̃-wᵒ, p. 231a, l. 16; khañi-wᵒ, p. 405b, l. 13; phŏhari-wᵒ, p. 687b, l. 4; rāda-wᵒ, p. 825a, l. 38; wāwᵃjĕ-wᵃ, s.v. wāvᵘ̈jᵘ̈) (El. wagú (the Śrīnagar word), patij (i.e. patᵘ̈jᵘ̈) (Islāmābād), and trhas (? spelling) (Bārāmūla); Gr.M.; L. 69, waggu; W. 141; Śiv. 1833; K.Pr. 7, 109, 171, 227). --waṭun -- m.inf. to roll up a mat; hence (of an entire family, work, field, or the like) to be utterly destroyed (either spontaneously or by another). ¶ wagȧvⁱ-gorⁱ m. (his wife is wagȧvⁱ-gȧrⁱ-bāy), a mat-maker, a mat-seller (El. wagívgur, wagivigur). -phard m. a small, light, mat. -patᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. an old worn-out mat. -pë̆ʦᵘ̈ f. a reed used for making mats. -rād m. a long narrow mat. -tᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a single mat-reed; a brush or pencil made of this reed. -tᵃjĕn lārun m.inf. to become thin, lean, meagre, to become a mere skeleton (from disease, starvation, or the like, so that one is bed-ridden). -wōnanwôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wōnanwājĕñ), a mat-weaver (El.).

m. (f., q.v., wã̄gajĕñ), one who lives (whether with the owner's consent or not) in another's house (K.Pr. 95, 228). --anun -- m.inf. to allow an outsider to live in one's house; met. to admit another to one's own secrets, work, opinions, or the like. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause another to enter a house (one's own or a third person's); to cause another to be admitted to one's secrets; to cause disease, fear, or some course of conduct to be experienced by an opponent. ¶ wā̃gȧjⁱ-wôrⁱ m. (esp. of one who is homeless) the taking up residence in the house of another (not as a paid servant) (Śiv. 1065, K.Pr. 187). -wôrᵘ kaḍun m.inf. (owing to poverty, helplessness, or the like) to take up a permanent residence in another's house.

m. (sg. dat. wã̄ganas), the egg-plant (Solanum melongena), and its fruit, brinjal (cf. ala-wã̄gan, p. 22b, l. 40; bŏṭa-wᵒ, p. 138b, l. 41; buza-wᵒ, p. 155a, l. 16; marʦa-wᵒ, p. 594b, l. 26; phŏṭa-wᵒ, p. 716b, l. 35; rū-wã̄gan, p. 823a, l. 31; röṭh-wᵒ, p. 849b, l. 3) (L. 346, wángan; YZ. 404; K.Pr. 10, 156). ¶ wã̄gan-hacĕ f.pl. a collection of pieces of dried brinjals (preserved for winter use); cf. wã̄gañĕ-hacĕ, s.v. wā̃güñᵘ̈. -kulᵘ m. the brinjal-plant. -nĕhölⁱ f. a collection of brinjal seedlings; the planting out or transplanting of such seedlings (also wᵒ-nᵒ karüñᵘ̈). -nowᵘ m. the festival of eating the new brinjals (i.e. the first of the new season); a present made to a bride's father-in-law's people on this occasion; cf. nowᵘ 1. -nȧvⁱ-bôgⁱ m. the similar present made by the relations of a bride's father to the relations of a bridegroom on this occasion. -nȧvⁱ-sāl m. the invitation to partake in the feast on this occasion. --pã̄gan -- m.pl. (a jingle) brinjals and the like (Gr.Gr. 95).
f. a piece of dried brinjal or egg-plant (preserved for winter use); cf. wã̄gun. wā̃gañĕ-hüṭᵘ̈ f. (pl. nom. -hacĕ), id. (generally used in the pl.). Cf. wã̄gan-hacĕ, col. a, l. 7, ab.
m. a person's circle of friends and relations when assembled together.

m. (pl. nom. wāgȧrⁱ), a kind of earthenware cup, esp. used for offerings at the ceremony of consecration of the image of a god on the occasion of the Śivarātri festival in Phāgun (Skt. Phālguna = February-March). Cf. sŏrzun for details. ¶ wāgȧrⁱ-bāh f. (sg. dat. -böshᵘ̈), the twelfth lunar day of the dark half of the month of Phāgun (Skt. Phālguna = February-March), on which the image of the goddess Vāgīshŏrī (Skt. Vāgīśvarī) is consecrated in preparation for the festival of the Śivarātri on this and the four following days. -pūzā f. the worship at this consecration ceremony.

f. palpitation, or throbbing (of the heart, etc., and marked by panting breath). --sŏtüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such palpitation (e.g. due to fainting, fatigue, hunger, or the like) to be quieted or to cease (e.g. by death). --thaküñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'palpitation to become weary' (one's) strength or power to become weary by exertion, to become exhausted (Rām. 546).
interj. bravo! well done! excellent! (L.V. 68). --wāh -- interj. id. (Śiv. 870). --wāh karun -- m.inf. to cry 'bravo!' (Śiv. 434).
m. mistletoe, Viscum album (El., cf. ahalū).
m. a vehicle, conveyance, carriage (Śiv. 14, K. 746).

m. (sg. dat. wahᵃras or waharas), a year (Śiv. 1443, 1465; K. 170, 211, 374; K.Pr. 2, 72, 161, 195, 204). In the printed edition of K. 374, the word is wrongly translated 'rainy season'. Cf. warih. ¶ wahᵃra-bal m. the annual offering made (on a fixed date) to the household god or similar deity. -bata m. the store of rice-grain, etc., collected for the whole year's consumption of a household. -byūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -bīṭhᵘ̈), (of a field, tree, or the like) bearing no crop, or fallow, for one year, after a year of crop-bearing; (of a cow or the like) bearing a calf or giving milk in one year, and not doing this in the next, and so on for similar cases. -gāv  f. (sg. dat. -gövᵘ̈ or, among Paṇḍits, gôvᵘ̈), a cow bearing a calf every year. -kujᵘ̈ f. a fruit-shrub, or fruit-tree, that bears fruit every second year. -wôdᵘ or wahōra-wôdᵘ m. an anniversary festival (cf. nētra-wᵒ-wᵒ, p. 662a, l. 41); esp. a birthday festival (L. 258, wehrawari; K.Pr. 232, wahrawud); a birthday. -wödⁱ bāgĕ c.g. a birthday present. -wödⁱ-bôgⁱ m., id. -wödⁱ bāgyukᵘ adj. gen. (f. -wödⁱ bāgë˘cᵘ̈) (a present) made to a son-in-law on his birthday by his wife's relations. -wödⁱlad m. one who is associated with each birthday of a person as it comes round. -wödis-kyutᵘ adv. on a birthday, on the occasion of a birthday. -wörᵘ̈ f. (among high-caste Hindūs) the srāddha, or obsequial ceremony, performed in honour of certain deceased relatives at the end of a year after the death of such a relative. -wārĕ-shrād m. the obsequial rite performed by a son or other heir each year on the anniversary of a person's death. ¶ wạhᵃ̇rᵃ̇ or wạhȧrⁱ adv. after a year, in a year's time (cf. hȧtⁱ-wⁱ, p. 357b, l. 40) (Rām. 462). --wạhᵃ̇rᵃ̇ -- adv. year by year, on each anniversary. -wahᵃras or -wȧrⁱhĕs adv. for an entire year, during an entire year, throughout the whole year, from year's end to year's end (L.V. 46, -wahᵃras). ¶ waharukᵘ adj. gen. (f. waharücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a year (cf. drāga- waharukᵘ, p. 241b, l. 29); of one particular year (i.e. of last year, of this year, of next year). ¶ waharas adv. for a year, for an entire year (K. 211, wᵒ-tāñ, for a whole year). --wuḍith wālañĕ vizi dab -- m. 'after flying for a year, a flop when coming down', i.e. after spending much energy, time, and money on some object, when on the brink of success to give it up.

f. (sg. dat. wahārüñᵘ̈ 1, for 2 see s.v.) the act of spreading or stretching out, opening out, expanding, loosening out; driving away, causing to disappear (flies or the like, with a fan, etc.); --˚ an instrument for driving away (flies, etc.) (e.g. a fan or fly-whisk) (used after a word signifying flies, etc.) (cf. machĕ-wahārun, p. 547a, l. 46).

f. (sg. dat. waharöʦᵘ̈), the rainy season, the rains, the monsoon (El. wahrát, waiharát, wiharát; Gr.M.; L. 326, wairat = July 15-September 15; Śiv. 1550; K. 841, 1087; K.Pr. 59, 229). --dŏshüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the due quantity of rain to fall in the rainy season, there to be a full rains. ¶ waharöʦᵘ̈-hondᵘ̈ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, belonging to, produced in, or relating to, the rainy season. -rūd m. a fall of rain in the rainy season; met. a merely transient friendship, enmity, or the like.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wahārôwᵘ), i.q. wahārun, q.v. (El. waharáwun, to spread; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1795, see wahārun). wahārôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wahārövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. wahôrᵘ-motᵘ, s.v. wahārun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wahôrᵘ), to spread out, stretch out, open, expand (cf. boṭhᵘ wᵒ, p. 140b, l. 20; dand wahārȧnⁱ, p. 224a, l. 50; dramba wahārañĕ, p. 245a, l. 50; murᵘ wᵒ, p. 588b, l. 29; marēd wahārüñᵘ̈, p. 589b, l. 44; nār wᵒ, p. 647a, l. 33; pāh wahārüñᵘ̈, p. 683b, l. 41; prāʦa wahārañĕ, p. 771a, l. 29; ṭhöñᵘ̈ wahārüñᵘ̈, p. 980a, l. 1; tāl zāl wᵒ, p. 997a, l. 42; vẹ̆shᵉ̆ṭurᵉ̆ wᵒ) (El. wáharun; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1795, ösᵘ̈ waharāwun, to open wide the mouth, so K. 193); to spread abroad, publish (cf. pöthᵃr wᵒ, p. 800a, l. 38; sã̄g wᵒ, p. 867a, l. 22); to shed over (a place) (e.g. the sun's rays) (Gr.M.); to stretch out, extend (cf. atha wᵒ, p. 64b, l. 6; khōr wᵒ, p. 410a, l. 30) (K. 605; K.Pr. 236, wrongly waharun); to spread out, set (a trap) (cf. zāl wᵒ, s.v. zāl 1; zŏnz wahārüñᵘ̈; zāpaṭh wᵒ) (Gr.M.); to spread out and arrange (the appliances necessary for any work); hence, to make full preparations (for some work) (cf. bakhēra wᵒ, p. 100b, l. 26; biṭh wahārüñᵘ̈, p. 140a, l. 4; dāthur wᵒ, p. 258a, l. 41; kalush wᵒ, p. 441a, l. 37; yë̆ñᵘ̈ wahārüñᵘ̈); to scatter, in the sense of widely practising some conduct (cf. bāṭh wᵒ, p. 139b, l. 3; mạkhᵃra wᵒ, p. 560b, l. 13; pakhanḍ wᵒ, p. 726b, l. 46); to cause to be scattered, to drive away (flies, or the like, with a fan, fly-flapper, or the like) (cf. machĕ wahārun, p. 547a, l, 46; machĕ wahārañĕ, ib., l. 49). wahôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wahörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), spread, scattered, driven away, etc., as ab.
(see also wahāran and wahārun)  f. an instrument for driving away flies or the like (e.g. a fan, or a fly-flapper), used --˚, being preceded by the name of the insect driven away.
n.ag. (f. wahavüñᵘ̈), (of a river) flowing, in full flood (L.V. 57, 96).

or wahāy f. the N. used in Kashmīr schools for the Śaradā form of the non-initial letter ā, corresponding to the Nāgarī. Its form is changed to a circle after the letter ṅ, j, or ṭ. See kŏnḍali-wᵒ, p. 456a, l. 20.

m. (sg. dat. wahĕkas), N. of the second month of the Hindū year (Skt. Vaiśākha = April-May) (cf. bēlⁱ-wⁱ, p. 150b, l. 7) (El. wahek, f., wáhyik, m.; W. 106, vạhek; Śiv. 470; K.Pr. 171, wahik). ¶ wahikⁱ adv. in this month. ¶ wahikukᵘ adj. gen. (f. wahikücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, this month.
m. imagination, idea, fancy; distrust, anxiety, apprehension, fear (YZ. 401).
in wahōra-wôdᵘ, see ab. under wahar.

wahurᵘ, wuhorᵘ, or wuhurᵘ adj.
