(f. wȧrishᵘ̈), of (so many) years, (so many) years old (cf. aiṭha-wᵒ, p. 66b, l. 47; bāhi waharĕ, p. 94a, l. 45; daha-wᵒ, p. 199a, l. 32; duwohurᵘ, p. 262b, l. 47; hata-wᵒ, p. 357b, l. 30; nawa-wᵒ, p. 664b, l. 5; pönʦa-wᵒ, p. 743b, l. 7; shĕ-wᵒ, p. 874a, l. 27; shēṭha-wᵒ, p. 899a, l. 43; sata-wᵒ, p. 944b, l. 49; wuha-wᵒ, p. 1104a, l. 28) (El. wuhur; Gr.M. wuhurᵘ; Śiv. 578 (f.); K. 185 wahurᵘ).
1 p.p. of wahārun. Used --˚ as in aḍa-wᵒ, p. 12a, l. 48, half-spread out.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. wahyōv), to flow (as water in a river or the like) (K. 563).

noted only in the following idiom:-- wöhith na hĕkun m.inf. to be dumb before abuse or rudeness and make no retort; (in the course of conversation) out of jealousy to be unable to bear the praise applied to some particular person.

or wāhⁱ interj. a cry indicating sickness, pain, or sorrow; Ah! (cf. wuhⁱ wāhy, p. 1104a, l. 41) (El. váí, Oh!, wöe, wöe, alas!; W. wāi, alas!; Rām. 195, 465, 975). --wāhy karun -- m.inf. to utter this cry.

or wödy or (see wöd) wödᵘ̈ m. a physician, a doctor (Gr.M., Śiv. 1855). wai(wö)dĕ-ʦaʦᵃr  f. anxiety felt (by the members of an invalid's family) in regard to the propriety of sending for a doctor, his fee, and so on.
or wör m. enmity, hatred, animosity, hostility, rancour (El. vãr, spiteful; Gr.Gr. 22; Śiv. 338 wör, 1806 wair; Rām. 1146, 1361 wör; K. 240, 897, 1051, 1061-3; K.Pr. 187).
or wairāna ویرانہ adj. c.g. waste, laid waste, desolate (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to lay waste, ruin (El.).
m. an enemy, a hater (either by nature, or due to some cause).

or wö̃s (also written wöms) f. age, time or period of life (El. vãṅs, wãṅs, wens in which ã = ö; Gr.Gr. 22, 137; Gr.M.; Rām. 535, 1780; YZ. 7, 510); (with suff. of indef. art.) waĩsāh (night will be long as) a whole lifetime (Rām. 196). --barüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to live (all) one's life (in some place or condition) (Śiv. 1730). --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to enjoy a full (i.e. long) life (a phrase used in blessings or the like). ¶ waĩsi (wö̃si)āmotᵘ  perf. part. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈m --), come into (old) age, become old and decrepit. --boḍᵘ -- adj. (f. büḍᵘ̈), an elder, one who is venerable on account of age, a grey beard; but waĩsi bajĕ, (lived) to a great age (K. 604). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. in idioms such as hath waĩsi gav, in age he went a hundred (years), i.e. he lived for a hundred years (H. ii, 12). --pūrᵘ -- adj. (f. --pūrᵘ̈ --), one who has lived a full lifetime, a centenarian. --somᵘ -- adj. (f. sümᵘ̈), equal in age, of equal age (e.g. two friends, a bride and bridegroom, and so on); one who is not yet adult, not fully grown up. --sŏrun -- m.inf. to remember all one's life, never to forget (K. 1062). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come into (old) age, to become old and decrepit.
a jingle of paĩsa in paĩsa-waĩsa, p. 777a, l. 12, q.v.
or wö̃saṭh adj. c.g. (of a human being) of ripe age, aged (say, roughly, over sixty years of age).
(Rām.) or wöshrawan m. a N. of Kubēra, the god of wealth and Guardian of the North (Skt. Vaiśravaṇa) (cf. dana-wᵒ, p. 222a, l. 21, q.v.) (Rām. 637, K. 172).

or wötaran f. (sg. dat. wai(wö)tarüñᵘ̈ ), N. of the Hindū Styx, the river that flows between the earth and the lower regions, which has to be crossed by spirits of the departed (Skt. Vaitaraṇī) (Śiv. 1910); N. of a Kashmīr river (RT.Tr. II, 274); a man's entire possessions, saved up and collected from his earnings, as his means of support throughout life. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make gifts (e.g. a cow to a Brāhmaṇ) in order to secure the passage of the spirit of a dying relative, or the like, over this river; to carry off, or plunder, a man's entire possessions, as ab. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. destruction or loss of one's entire property, as ab.
or wötāranī f. N. of the hell past which the river mentioned in the preceding article flows; the ceremony of making gifts, as in the preceding, in order to help a spirit across this river.
adj. c.g. wearing a finger-ring. Cf. wöjⁱ.
f. the vulva (El. Cf. Ar.-Prs. وُجود, penis).

m. a cause, reason, pretext (esp. for some sudden, unexpected, or unforeseen occurrence) (El., Rām. 146). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such a reason, cause, or pretext to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to make a cause; hence, a cause suddenly to arise (e.g. a momentary illness as an explanation for a sudden death) (Rām. 608).

m. (sg. dat. wākas), speech, words, language (cf. ku-wôkᵘ, p. 496a, l. 2) (in this sense sometimes fem.); voice, the power of expression by word. [In Śaiva philosophy this is one of the five karmêndriyas, or faculties, or powers, of action] (L.V. 2); a clause, sentence, a stanza, verse (cf. ölⁱ-wⁱ, p. 26a, l. 27; wāky) (Gr.M., Śiv. 959); esp. the mystic formula confided to a disciple by his preceptor, a guiding principle (L.V. 94); a magic spell (uttered) (Rām. 789-90); a saying, an aphorism (L.V. 104); a thing said, a brief sentence or statement (Śiv. 693; Rām. 103 (bad-w˚, a curse), 1608 (a decree of fate), 1709); a promise (K. 576, 628, 722). -dān m. the giving (one's) word, the formal promise (to give a girl in marriage, made by the parents and relations of a bride to those of a bridegroom). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to utter a sentence, make a brief statement (K. 1092); to give (one's) word, to promise, agree (to some proposal). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to utter a spell (Rām. 1299). --muchun -- m.inf. to begin to speak, after the completion of a vow of silence, or after a long spell of silence. --pālun -- m.inf. to keep one's word, carry out a promise (Rām. 154, 291). -sĕd f. (sg. dat. -së̆zᵘ̈), fulfilment, or coming true, of a word (i.e. of a curse, blessing, or the like). --waʦun -- m. the coming true of a casual word (e.g. such as that uttered in the course of conversation, or otherwise). ¶ wāka-tandul f. 'a procession of words'; hence, a continued stream of abuse.
a jingle of hākh, in hākh-wākh, p. 326b, l. 11, q.v. (K.Pr. 163).
adj. c.g. fitting, suitable, accordant, tallying.
f. unrestrained explanation, explanation at great length and in great detail (Gr.Gr. 129).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wakhonᵘ 2; 2 p.p. wakhañōv), to lecture, to explain (some book) to others, tell (Gr.Gr. 128); to recite (holy writ or the like) (Śiv. 582, 979, 1077). wakhonᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (wakhüñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), previously explained, as ab.

(for 2, see wakhanun), or wakhun, or wŏkhunᵘ m. (sg. dat. wa(wŏ)khanas ), a reading, recitation; a lecture read or made by a teacher to a pupil, esp. one of a regular course of readings or lectures (Rām. 1491); an exercise, a subject of study (Gr.M.); a tale, a story (L.V. 84). --darun -- m.inf. the substance of a lecture to become learnt by heart (by a pupil). --dạrᵃrun -- or --dạrᵃrāwun -- m.inf. to deliver one of a course of such lectures (extemporarily, and not by reading from a written document). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. a lecture or reading to come, i.e. to reach its object, to be thoroughly understood and accepted by the hearers.
m. (sg. dat. wakharas), a cake offered in sacrifice, a sacrificial cake (L.V. 10, 77).

or wakth (= وقت) m. (sg. dat. wakhtas or waktas), time, a particular time (cf. bĕgā-wᵒ, p. 90a, l. 33; daphul-wᵒ, p. 233a, l. 30; köjⁱ-wⁱ, p. 430a, l. 12; mimizⁱ-wⁱ, p. 371b, l. 23) (El. wakt; Gr.M.; Rām. 487 (dar-wakt-i در وقتِ, at the time of); H. vi, 16, wakth); a space of time (Gr.M.); season (Gr.M.). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. occasion to arise (for something); adversity or misfortune to befall, distress to be experienced. --wātun -- m.inf. time to be spent, as in kōtāh wᵒ wôtu-y, how much time was spent for thee, how much time did you spend? (Gr.M.). ¶ wakta adv. at (such-and-such) a time (cf. dŏyĕ wakta, s.v. zᵃh) (Gr.M., Rām. 806). wakta wakta adv. from time to time. ¶ waktukᵘ adj. gen. (f. waktücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or produced at, some particular time; of, or done at, the right time (K.Pr. 227). ¶ waktan or wakhᵃtan وقتن adv. at (such-and-such) a time (cf. bĕgā-wᵒ, p. 90a, l. 36; köjⁱ-wⁱ, p. 430a, l. 14) (Rām. 575). ¶ waktas or wakhᵃtas adv. at (such-and-such) a time (cf. bĕga-wᵒ, p. 90a, l. 37; köjⁱ-wⁱ, p. 430a, l. 16) (K.Pr. 227). --āsun -- m.inf. to be at the (right) time; esp. (of a pregnant woman) to come near her time. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain at the time; esp. (of a pregnant woman) to be near her time.

m. an agent, deputy, substitute (El.); a representative in a law-court, an attorney (Gr.M.); an advocate, pleader on behalf of another (Śiv. 872); a hanger-on at a law-court, or the like (K.Pr. 29, wakīl-i, with iẓāfat).
m. a phrase, period, sentence, i.q. wākh 1, q.v. (Gr.M.).

f. retrograde motion (of a planet) (Rām. obl. wakri, 418); a storm of anger, rage (of some person in power against a subordinate or some helpless person). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of a planet) to show retrograde motion; (of an employee, in the course of some work, and in order to hinder it) after a display of anger, to draw back, or retire from it (i.e. to go on strike). ¶ wạkri gaʦhun m.inf. (of some person in power) to display great anger (against some subject, subordinate servant, or helpless person). --gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), become angry, as ab.
adj. c.g. oblique, crooked; of a crooked nature, dishonest, fraudulent. --müñᵘ̈ -- f. an oblique pupil of the eye, a downcast look (K.Pr. 60, wukar). (Cf. së̆zᵘ̈ müñᵘ̈, p. 956b, l. 15.)
f. (pl. wạkᵃrüñᵃ), in shẹ̆tᵃrüñᵃ-wạkᵃrüñᵃ, p. 900a, l. 30, q.v.

m. a crease (in paper, cloth, etc.), hair-line mark, mark of a crack; an impediment (caused by another to one who is on the point of success). -ʦhal m. an obstacle or impediment (caused by another, as ab.); habitual swindling, cheating. -woṭᵘ m. secret hoarding of one's earnings (unknown even to the hoarder's relations). -woṭᵘ bōzun m.inf. to keep an eye on, to watch, guard one's secret savings, as ab. ¶ wala-zobᵘ m. a kind of small fish found in ponds and marshes.

m. hair, down (of the human body) (cf. achar-wᵒ, achir-wᵒ, p. 9b, ll. 20, 22; buḍa-wᵒ, p. 85b, l. 8; dāri-wᵒ, p. 238a, l. 30; kīhi-wᵒ, p. 390b, l. 12; kaʦha-wᵒ, p. 492b, l. 48; mō-yĕ-wᵒ, p. 546b, l. 38; mas-wᵒ, p. 595b, l. 36) (El.; Gr.Gr. 51; Gr.M.; Rām. 1293, 1350); hair, fur (of a lower animal) (cf. gurⁱ-wⁱ, p. 299a, l. 18; puy-wᵒ, p. 813a, l. 1); a single hair (cf. zọ̆kⁱ-wⁱ, s.v. zọ̆kᵘ) (L.V. 24; Rām. 118, 735, 1271, 1415); a filament, fibre (cf. nadȧrⁱ-wⁱ, p. 623b, l. 2; phã-wᵒ, p. 698a, l. 10); met. a very small quantity, as in mŏyĕ-wᵒ, p. 613a, l. 20. In Rām. this word is found only --˚. ¶ wāla-borᵘ m. a kind of springe for catching small birds (a horse-hair noose at the end of an elastic switch) (K.Pr. 245). -bürᵘ̈ f. the orifice of the vulva (esp. used in abuse imputing unchastity). -guna f. a sack, a bag, made of animal hair, esp. one of the sacks fastened on each side of the back of a beast of burden. -gorᵘ m. a felt-maker. -khāv m. N. of a certain disease, owing to which the hair of the beard, etc., comes off. -phamb m. a certain soft kind of pashmīna wool, mixed with coarse hair of no value. -raz f. a hair rope (used for tethering horses, etc.); the cord binding together the spokes of the large wheel in a spinning-wheel (El.). -wāsh, -wöshⁱ, or -wöshᵘ̈ f. a kind of horse-hair net, used for trapping small game or small birds (cf. khurᵘ̈-wᵘ̈, p. 412a, l. 19) (H. v, 2; K.Pr. 112); often used met., as in Śiv. 250, 1693, 1783; Rām. 1103, 1595. -wôshᵘ m. a trapper, a fowler, who uses this net.
f. a flower (cf. āra-wᵒ, p. 41a, l. 49; lẹ̆dᵃrĕ-wal-pōsh, p. 510a, l. 38).

or wāla, c.g. a suffix added to substantives to form nouns implying possession or relation generally (cf. Hindī wālā) (cf. bĕha-wāl, p. 94b, l. 9; jȧmⁱ-wāla, p. 373b, l. 38; prūnʦh-wāla, p. 764a, l. 33; wuphal-wāl; wŏphar-wāl, s.v. wŏphurᵘ; zᵃla-wāl, s.v. zᵃl).
the form taken by pal 2 (q.v.) in the compound ad-wal, p. 15b, l. 45, q.v.
f. (sg. dat. wöjᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 69), the hole (of a snake, rat, mongoose, or the like) (cf. gagar-wᵒ, p. 280a, l. 20) (El.; Gr.Gr. 31, 69; K.Pr. 64, 188). Cf. wöjⁱ.

f. bringing down, lowering down, putting away, in phala-wāl, p. 692b, l. 18, and in the following:-- ¶ wāla-wāl f. the act of continually or regularly causing to descend, bringing something down whenever it becomes high or exalted. -wālay f., id. esp. of bringing down honour (by abuse or the like).

f. (sg. dat. walüzᵘ̈) connexion, affinity, relationship, association, familiar intercourse (such as we find in close friendship, consanguinity, or the like) (cf. wath-wᵒ, s.v. wath). walüzᵘ̈-wôlᵘ̈ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is intimately associated, as ab.
f. (sg. dat. wālaki), dirt (dust, chaff, straw, etc.) mixed up in a heap of grain. Cf. wālath and wūlⁱ.
f. (sg. dat. wālüñᵘ̈), the act of bringing down, the causing to descend (etc., see wālun).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. walanôwᵘ), to dress (another), to cause another to dress, to cause to be clothed (El., YZ. 559). Cf. walun.
f. the act of bringing or putting down (cf. shīna-wᵒ, p. 885a, l. 14); met. humiliating, disgracing, putting to shame (a person of rank by public abuse or insult) (H. vii, 15; K.Pr. 25).
m. in walās karun m.inf. to flatter (El.).
f. (sg. dat. wālüʦᵘ̈), dirt (dust, chaff, straw, etc.) mixed up in a heap of grain. Cf. wālakh and wūlⁱ.
f. wages for bringing down (e.g. for carrying a load down from a mountain, or similar elevated situation); wages for pulling down (a house or the like).
n.ag. (f. wālavüñᵘ̈), one who causes to descend, who brings down, who lowers (something) (Śiv. 857); one who degrades or humiliates (another by abuse or the like); one who skins, flays. See wālun.
m. a time when it is raining, a shower of rain (such as prevents one from going out), an occasion when rain falls.

f. the act of causing to descend, bringing down (Gr.Gr. 128); degrading, abusing, humiliating (a person) (cf. mōda-wᵒ, p. 549a, l. 28; māna-wᵒ, p. 573a, l. 25); taking down, putting away, putting off (responsibility or the like) (cf. nakha-wᵒ, p. 628b, l. 46); stripping off, skinning, flaying (cf. basta-wᵒ, p. 135b, l. 7; pōsta-wᵒ, p. 784b, l. 3); (of rain, etc.), a shower, a fall, an occasion or time of falling (the rain, etc., being looked upon as being rained down by someone) (cf. rūda-wᵒ, p. 826b, l. 27; shīna-wᵒ, p. 885a, l. 17).
conjnct. but, yet, however, for all that (Rām. 1533).

m. (sg. dat. walgatanas), the act of bending back or curving back (something long); the act of winding round (a rope for tying on a load). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to bend back or twist (a rope, a long withy, or the like); (or intrans.) (of some disease, difficulty, fault, or the like, which has been cured or done away with) to return, come back again.
m. a master, lord, prince, governor; a helper, defender; a favourite of God, a saint; (in Ksh.) a good man, a true gentleman.
f. a Skt. word meaning 'a beloved woman', used in Śiv. 12 and 1142 to indicate the śakti (see shĕktⁱ), or Energic Power, of Śiva.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wolᵘ, f. vüjᵘ̈; 2 p.p. wajyōv), to wrap up, roll up in something (Gr.M.; L. 465; Śiv. 104, 323; Rām. 717; H. viii, 6, 13); to roll up, wrap up, wind up (cloth, string, or the like) (El., Gr.Gr. 22); to encircle, bind, entangle, envelop (cf. gulⁱ walun hyuhᵘ, p. 284a, l. 33; nāl wᵒ, p. 632b, l. 1) (El. walun, wŏlun; Śiv. 17, 110, 227, 424, 874, 893, 1055, 1282, 1474; Rām. 257, 346, 553, 724, 913, 1073, 1191, 1496, 1614; H. ix, 7; K.Pr. 152); to cover, to clothe (El., Gr.Gr. 5; Rām. 786, 805 pass., 1726; K. 976; YZ. 106, 257); to put (clothes) on oneself (El., Śiv. 529, 752, 793, 801, 816, 894, 1326, 1350, 1540, 1570, 1574, 1651; Rām. 5, 201, 976, 979, 1087, 1758; YZ. 170, 234). ¶ wȧlⁱ wȧlⁱ freq. part. as adv. hurriedly, quickly, speedily (El. walwal). Cf. wȧlⁱ. ¶ wolᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), wrapped up, rolled up, etc., as ab.; enveloped, entangled (cf. vĕpüʦᵘ̈ wᵒ, s.v. vĕpath); put on, worn (of clothes) (Śiv. 344). ¶ walana yunᵘ m. inf. pass. of walun in all its senses, and (also, esp.) to follow, pursue, persecute (in order to harass or to urge on someone to complete some work, either by bodily action or by abuse or by charging with some fault, or the like); to adhere to, stick to (K.Pr. 154); to be attached to, devoted to (K. 502).

(occasionally, as in Gr.Gr. 177, written wārun) conj. 1 (1 p.p. wôlᵘ, f. wöjᵘ̈; 2 p.p. wājyōv. This word is the causal of wasun, q.v., Gr.Gr. 177. Its opposite is khārun, cf. khārañĕ wālañĕ, p. 415a, l. 24, and Śiv. 1017, 1753), to cause to descend, to bring down, to lower (something) (cf. atha wᵒ, p. 64b, l. 18; dŏd wᵒ, p. 188a, l. 48; dam wᵒ, p. 216b, l. 23; haṭi wᵒ, p. 356b, l. 7; kö̆bᵃrĕ wᵒ, p. 382b, l. 5; khyolᵘ wᵒ, p. 426a, l. 48; nabacĕ tāra wālañĕ, p. 619a, l. 43; rath wᵒ, p. 845b, l. 31; wuyᵘ wᵒ) (Gr.Gr. 23, 128, 149, 150; L.V. 104; Śiv. 324, 971, 973; Rām. 1431, 1458; K. 33, 450; H. iii, 9; iv, 7; vii, 17; viii, 1; x, 8; xi, 11; YZ. 162; K.Pr. 72, 99); met. to lower, abase, render of no account, degrade (cf. dĕmāg wᵒ, p. 219a, l. 37; khras wālüñᵘ̈, p. 415b, l. 48; mada wᵒ, p. 548b, l. 5; mōda wᵒ, p. 549a, l. 25; mada-māza wᵒ, p. 615a, l. 10; nāv wᵒ, p. 665b, l. 12; phūdᵃr wālüñᵘ̈, p. 685a, l. 43; pāvi wᵒ, p. 810a, ll. 36 ff.; tāwa wᵒ, p. 1047a, l. 7; yīrī pīrī wālüñᵘ̈, s.v. yīrī) (Śiv. 69, 125, 421, 1758; K. 31, 829, 869); ¶ to pour down, rain (something) down, drop (something), let (something) fall (cf. brö̃ṭⁱ wālȧnⁱ, p. 127b, l. 10; nāba ṭang wālȧnⁱ, p. 619b, l. 11; raḍa wᵒ, p. 825a, l. 47) (Śiv. 713, 1233, 1245, 1250-1, 1259, 1391; Rām. 863, 1546; K. 318-20, 325, 1087, 1137); to lead or bring down (from the shore into the river, or into a boat), to embark (a person), load (cargo) (cf. nāvi wᵒ, p. 667a, l. 13) (K.Pr. 227); to bring down, i.e. draw in (the breath) (Śiv. 1017, 1750; Rām. 17); ¶ to bring down (a tool or the like) on something (in order to bring it into action), to begin working with (a tool) (cf. ara wālañĕ, p. 41a, l. 20; litᵘ̈rᵘ̈ wālüñᵘ̈, p. 539a, l. 13) (Śiv. 167; H. v. 4); ¶ to take down, take off, put away (cf. bôrᵘ wᵒ, p. 118a, l. 32; laʦh wālüñᵘ̈, p. 539b, l. 14; nakha wᵒ, p. 628b, l. 35, so p. 92a, l. 26; p. 166b, l. 27; p. 249b, l. 10) (L. 459 hōrun nakha w˚, to discharge a debt; Śiv. 199, 1208, 1506; Rām. 291; YZ. 95; K.Pr. 80, to take a pot off the fire); to ruin, make useless, make unable to act, wear out (cf. nakh wālȧnⁱ, p. 628a, l. 35; pŏṭh wālüñᵘ̈, p. 796b, l. 19) (Śiv. 838); to bring down, or cause (some bad condition) (cf. trŏngⁱ wālȧnⁱ, p. 1028a, l. 18; trᵃth wᵒ, p. 1032a, l. 22; wuka wᵒ, p. 1108a, l. 18); to pull down (a building), dismantle, reduce to ruins (Rām. 740, 800); ¶ to tear off, strip off, peel, flay, trim (cf. ala-hacĕ wālañĕ, p. 22b, l. 4; basta wālüñᵘ̈, p. 135b, l. 5; dĕl wālȧnⁱ, p. 210b, l. 43; drūrᵘ wᵒ, p. 218a, l. 16; nakha-chala wālañĕ, p. 628a, l. 45; phala wālañĕ, p. 693a, l. 5; phīs wᵒ, p. 711b, l. 30; parca wālȧnⁱ, p. 756a, l. 25; pōst wᵒ, p. 784a, l. 47; randa wālañĕ, p. 836a, l. 20; thȧlⁱ thȧlⁱ wᵒ, p. 977a, l. 18; thalith wᵒ, p. 977a, l. 24; thras wālüñᵘ̈, p. 984b, l. 15; tᵃra wālañĕ, p. 1017a, l. 24) (Rām. 374, 382, 433, 707, 843; H. viii, 6); to take off, doff (a garment or the like) (Gr.M.); to pluck, collect, and deposit (flowers or the like) (Śiv. 273, 662). ¶ wôlᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wöjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to descend, etc., as ab. ¶ wölith ʦhunun m.inf. 'having brought down, to cast away'; hence, to terrify (as the result of threats or the like).
m. a son (esp. a darling only boy).
m. leavings of food from the table (partaken of by Musalmān servants, persons of low caste, or given to dogs); second-hand garments (worn by a person other than the original wearer). Cf. wulash.
m. something wrapped or twisted round (something else) (cf. kala-wᵒ, p. 435b, l. 25). Cf. walun.
adv. quickly, speedily, soon (Rām. 1782, 1785). Cf. wȧlⁱ wȧlⁱ, s.v. walun.
f. an abusive nickname, a by- name (given for some improper action, whether innocently done or not).
f. the action of fanning (to produce coolness, ward off flies, or the like).
adj. c.g. left (not right). ¶ wāma-bāg, the left direction, the left side, the left (K. 59). -hast, the left hand (K. 838).
m. a name of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 1136, 1179); N. of a famous Indian sage (K. 1039).
m. fanning (to revive a fainting person, to cool, to drive away flies, or the like).
f. (sg. dat. wāmüñᵘ̈), disgustingness, the property of not only being disgusting, but also, by contact, defiling another.
m. nausea, a feeling of nausea (e.g. caused by a noisome smell, or a disgusting sight).

m. the left-hand doctrine or ritual of worshippers (of Śiva), according to the Tantras, i.e. the worship of the Female Energy, or Śakti (see shĕktⁱ) of Śiva, in which the eating of flesh, drinking of spirits, etc., is practised.
m. a follower of the preceding ritual.
adj. (as subst., f. wāmiladiñ), he or that, who or which, is an object of abuse and by contact renders another also an object of abuse, disgusting.
m. a race, family, dynasty, lineage (K. 829).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. wamyōv), to vomit; (of food, etc.), to be vomited.

m. (sg. dat. wāmanas), a dwarf, pigmy. wāman 3 or wāman-ōtār m. the dwarf incarnation of Vishnu, when he became a dwarf to humble the demon Bali (cf. Śiv. 739, 859; K. 27 wāman); met. a very short man, a dwarf.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wômᵘ), to cause a current of air (by a fan or the like, to cause coolness, ward off flies, or the like) (cf. machĕ wāmañĕ, p. 547b, l. 1).

m. a forest, wood (cf. düdᵘ̈wan, p. 191a, l. 16; danḍakh-wᵒ, p. 226a, l. 32; pöshⁱ-wⁱ, p. 779b, l. 46) (Gr.Gr. 37; Gr.M.; L. 460; L.V. 25, 28; Śiv. 365, 409, 439, 493-4, 534, 556, 585, 598, 662, 739, 817, 999, 1030, 1037, 1062, 1195, 1222, 1286, 1375, 1411, 1419, 1440, 1561, 1602, 1617, 1650; Rām. 148, 173, 206, 230, 341, 391, 404, 756, 785, 883, 1025, 1143g-44, 1156, 1165, 1167, 1198, 1207, 1253, 1283, 1328, 1389, 1426-7, 1622, 1674; K. 182-3, 186, 193, 207-8, 217-9, 223-4, 256, 282, 305, 318, 382, 398, 673, 677-8, 1083, 1085, 1087-8, 1137; H. vii, 10; ix, 1, 3-5; K.Pr. 154, 156, 227, 229, 248); a cluster, group, a quantity (of something) (cf. dāra-wᵒ, p. 235a, l. 37; dyāra-wᵒ, p. 271a, l. 10; nörⁱ-wⁱ, p. 649b, l. 10); esp. a large quantity, a large amount, as in bata-wᵒ, a great deal of boiled rice; sinⁱ-wⁱ, a lot of vegetables, etc. (syunᵘ); wana-wan, bel.; zinⁱ-wⁱ, a great deal of firewood (zyunᵘ); met. (like a forest) one who is unfathomable, profound, incomprehensible, inscrutable (Śiv. 773). Cf. vüñᵘ̈ 1. ¶ The following forests are mentioned in Rām.:--Ashukh-wan, the forest of Aśōka trees near Laṅkā, where Rāma was encamped (900); Danḍakh-wᵒ, see p. 226a, l. 32; Kazal-wᵒ (584), the same as the Kajalī ban of India. The last is a mysterious forest, a stock subject of reference in Indian literature, into which various famous local heroes have disappeared instead of dying. In Rām. it is merely named as a famous forest. Tradition as to its locality varies. According to some, it is near Hardwār, in Audh, and, according to others, it is in Assam. ¶ wan-ölicᵘ̈ f. clematis (L. 459 wan alach). -babᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. forest, i.e. wild, basil (L. 76, Mentha sp.). -gām m. a forest village. -gömⁱ adj. c.g. a forest villager, one who is born in, or dwells in, a forest village. -ganḍa c.g. 'a forest tied up (cf. ganḍ) bundle of firewood'; hence, a great big clumsy lout, a looby, Tony Lumpkin, clumsy clown. -hūnᵘ m. (f. -hūñᵘ̈), a forest dog, a wild dog. -hand f. wild chicory (reported to be used as a medicine for application to broken limbs. An infusion of it is also given as a regimen to a lying-in woman. The same infusion is also used in offerings made to the goddesses called Mātṛkā). -hörᵘ̈ or (Rām. 4) wana-hörⁱ  f. a wild starling (Śiv. 962, 1362, 1365; Rām. 4). -kŏkur m. (f. -kŏkürᵘ̈), a kind of wild bird resembling a barndoor fowl. -lay f. any delightful woodland level spot in the hills (cf. lay 2). -mahönyuwᵘ m. (sg. dat. -mahönivis), a forest man (looked upon as rude, uncouth, and ugly, usually a charcoal burner). -mujᵘ̈ f. a kind of wild radish (of acrid taste, a paste made from it is used for wounds). -mawal f. wild cockscomb. -prān m. a wild onion (L. 75, allium sp., used as a stimulant and expectorant). -rahun m. (?) wild garlic (L. 72, wan ruhan). --raṭun -- m.inf. to take to a forest life, to lead the life of a hermit (Śiv. 981; Rām. 207, 249). -sōr m. (f. -sūriñ), a wild boar. -ʦhāwulᵘ (f. -ʦhāvüjᵘ̈), 'a forest goat', an animal described as resembling a large goat, found in inaccessible spots in the hills north of Kashmir. -ʦᵃñĕ f.pl. forest charcoal, charcoal prepared in the forests and brought into the city for sale. -vigiñ f. a certain forest goddess (see vigiñ) (cf. Śiv. 966, vanücᵘ̈y vi˚). -wās m. living in the forest (in preference for solitude, or as an anchorite), exile to the forest (L.V. 55, 64; Śiv. 596, 818, 948, 953, 1349, 1439, 1454, 1713, 1822; Rām. 41, 155, 161, 660, 765, 1143f, g); i.q. wan- wösⁱ, bel. (Rām. 228, 425). -wösⁱ adj. c.g. a dweller in the forest; esp. a forest hermit, ascetic, anchorite (Śiv. 529, 1759; Rām. 215). -zyunᵘ m. forest firewood. ¶ wana 1 in wana-hörⁱ, see wan-hörᵘ̈, ab. -māl f. a garland of wild flowers (Śiv. 1436); a row of forests, one after the other, along the hill tops. -marg f. a mountain table-land, a plateau high up among the hills (full of flowers and flowering shrubs, and with a pleasant climate). -phal m. wild fruit. -rôchᵘ m. a road guardian, a guard against highway robbers; a weapon taken by a traveller for his protection. -thal f. a wooded country, a woodland glade. -wan m. a great, wide, forest; a forest within another forest. [To be distinguished from wanawan 1 and 2, qq.v., s.vv.] -wothᵘ adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), come down from the forest (to civilization); hence, a fine healthy stalwart person (quasi, an ox or sheep that has come down to the towns, after long grazing in the forests).

m. a shop, a place where a man makes or/and sells his goods or where goods are sold, the headquarters, or office, of a professional man (cf. ashĕd-wᵒ, p. 48b, l. 16; barbuzⁱ-wⁱ, p. 119a, l. 48; bōzagȧrⁱ-wⁱ, p. 152b, l. 5; bazāza-wᵒ, p. 155b, l. 23; carsa-wᵒ, p. 176b, l. 21; guzar-wᵒ, p. 319a, l. 23; hakīm-wᵒ, p. 328b, l. 30; hȧrⁱsa-wⁱ, p. 350a, l. 49; khāra-wᵒ, p. 407b, l. 50; krālā-wᵒ, p. 470b, l. 26; mahᵃladār-wᵃ, p. 554b, l. 19; manᵃr-wᵃ, p. 581b, l. 7; mĕnzar-wᵒ, p. 585a, l. 6; nāstigȧrⁱ-wⁱ, p. 658b, l. 46; nöyid-wᵒ, p. 670a, l. 17; phalgȧrⁱ-wⁱ, p. 691b, l. 35; pujⁱ-wⁱ, p. 723b, l. 48; pīra-wᵒ, p. 753a, l. 8; pasörⁱ-wⁱ, p. 783b, l. 43; potᵘ wᵒ, p. 788b, l. 30; pȧṭⁱ-wⁱ, p. 789b, l. 35; puywöñⁱ-wⁱ, p. 813a, l. 13; rangȧrⁱ-wⁱ, p. 838a, l. 46; shĕrāb-wᵒ, p. 891a, l. 1; sŏnar-wᵒ, p. 923a, l. 43; ṭhö̃ṭhar-wᵒ, p. 987a, l. 15; wöda-wᵒ, p. 1097a, l. 31; wöñⁱ-wⁱ, s.v. wôñᵘ 2; wāwᵃ̇rᵃ̇-wᵃ̇, s.v. wôwurᵘ; wāza-wᵒ) (El.; Gr.Gr. 10; Gr.M.; L. 464; W. 114; L.V. 102; K.Pr. 102; Śiv. 531, 1211, 1248; H. i, 2; xi, 17; K.Pr. 102, 107, 138, 159, 177-8); a place where people work or carry on manufacture, etc., a factory, workshop, mine, or the like (cf. dŏbⁱ-wⁱ, p. 182b, l. 39; dūnⁱ-wⁱ, p. 223b, l. 39; nūna-wᵒ, p. 641a, l. 31; payĕn-wᵒ, p. 817b, l. 8; tōla-wᵒ, p. 999b, l. 28; wŏkhal-wᵒ, p. 1109a, l. 36) (El.); a place where people collect, or are collected, for any purpose (cf. bö̃dⁱ-wⁱ, p. 83b, l. 36; gāna-wᵒ, p. 288a, l. 29; kŏla-wᵒ, p. 437b, l. 31; kana-wᵒ, p. 448a, l. 43; kanjar-wᵒ, p. 457b, l. 27; phĕshĕl kā̃daryunᵘ wᵒ, p. 713a, l. 6; pyāda-wᵒ, p. 813b, l. 31; shōda-wᵒ, p. 871a, l. 15; wātal-wᵒ, s.v. wātul; zāra-wᵒ, s.v. zār 2; zörⁱ-wⁱ, s.v. zörⁱ 1) (K. 36, 40, 51, 53, 365-6, 896, 997, 1005, 1028, all böndⁱ-w˚ for bö̃dⁱ-wⁱ, as ab.). --bĕhun -- m.inf. to set up a shop, to start a business of shop- keeping; to be a shopkeeper, to keep shop (Śiv. 240). --kamanāwun -- or --kamawun -- m.inf. to keep shop, live by shopkeeping; (esp. of a woman) to practise prostitution, to live as a harlot. --wuṭhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to lampoon, satirize. ¶ wāna-dĕlⁱ m.pl. a kind of rush used by merchants for tying up small parcels (El. wándelí); cf. dyolᵘ and wā̃-dyolᵘ, p. 1128a, l. 28. -kirāy f. a shopkeeper's fee, the amount, or rent, paid to the owner of a shop, for permission to sell in it. -mọ̆nḍᵘ m. a carpenter's bench, a heavy block of wood in a carpenter's shop, on which other wood is chopped or worked. -pë̆nḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -pĕnjĕ), a quadrangular spot in the front of the shop, or wooden platform, for the convenience of customers, on which they can wait till served. -püṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -pacĕ), the door, or shutter, of a shop. -rôchᵘ m. a shop guard, a shop caretaker. -wôlᵘ m. (a female shopkeeper is wāna-wājĕñ, a shopkeeper's wife is wāna-wölⁱ-bāy) a shopkeeper (El., Śiv. 1248). -wölī f. shopkeeping, the profession of a shopkeeper. -wothᵘ adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), come down from the shop, fresh from the shop, just purchased, brand-new.

obl. wana 2 in wana-pürᵘ̈ f. 'speech-recitation'; hence, unrestrained speech in lecturing, explaining, or the like; cf. wanun parun, s.v. wanun 1. wana-pürᵘ̈ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to speak at great length (in instructing, reproving, abusing, or the like); to pour out a flood of angry talk.

a suffix added to a substantive to form an adjective of possession, as in bö̆zᵘ̈-wān, possessing wisdom, wise, p. 83b, l. 25; bāgi-wᵒ, prosperous, p. 91a, l. 2; gŏna-wᵒ, possessing good qualities, p. 288b, l. 13; pŏñĕ-wᵒ, one who has the results of good actions, p. 746b, l. 32; shūba-wᵒ, possessing beauty, p. 369a, l. 38; vīda-wᵒ, possessing (i.e. versed in) the Vēdas, p. 1096b, l. 25) (Gr.M.). Cf. wônᵘ 2.
(f. wöñᵘ̈ 2), suffix signifying 'keeper', 'man', etc., as in bāg-wān, a gardener, p. 89b, l. 38; ḍīḍⁱ-wⁱ, a doorkeeper, p. 188a, l. 21. Cf. wôñᵘ 2, 3.

or (q.v.) wöñᵘ̈ 4 f. (sg. dat. and pl. nom. wöñᵘ̈ 4. For 1-3 and 5-7, see s.vv.) speech, words, language (cf. sŏwān, s.v.; zan-wān, s.v. zan 1) (El. wányi, sound, proverb); a dirge, elegy, threnody (sung by women, under a leader, each morning for ten days after a death, esp. after the death of an old man or woman) (El. wŏiṅ; Rām. 429, wöñī for wöñᵘ̈, m.c.). Cf. wönī 1. ¶ wāna-gürᵘ̈ f. the woman who leads the singing in such an elegy. ¶ wöñᵘ̈ 4 f.pl. such a dirge, as ab. --diñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to utter cries of lamentation, to call to in grief (YZ. 542). --tulañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to utter loud lamentations (YZ. 570).
in hana-wana, a jingle of hana, q.v., p. 335b, l. 48 (Śiv. 1347, 1411).
in wana munda, 'the log harrow over which rice is threshed' (sic. L. 464; ? wana-mọ̆nḍᵘ).

f. (sg. dat. wanüñᵘ̈), similarity of condition (e.g. when one person is dead, ruined, or disgraced, another person to be in the same condition); a necessary consequence, outcome (K. 677). Cf. vüñᵘ̈ 2.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wananôwᵘ), to cause to be spoken (Śiv. 129, 161, 1130); to inform someone through another, to send a message; to call, summon, invite (Śiv. 74); to say, sing, declare, recite (Śiv. 867-8, 960, 966, 974); to cause (another) to speak; hence, to converse with (dat.) (Rām. 1110).
f. backbiting, slandering, slander. -lŏgolᵘ adj. (f. -lŏgüjᵘ̈), a backbiter, slanderer, calumniator.

(for 2, see wanawun) f. (sg. dat. wanavüñᵘ̈), rumour, report, on dit. [To be distinguished from wana-wan, p. 1120a, l. 39.] --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a rumour to occur, i.e. to learn (something) by rumour. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to say over and over again (so as to get something done, or to explain something).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wanowᵘ) (of women at a festival, such as a marriage) to sing in chorus (L. 269, wani wani, for wanawȧnⁱ, inf.pl.; Śiv. 830, 941-2, 959, 966, 1074, 1132, 1223, 1345, 1440, 1640, 1690); to arrange for such a chorus, to teach the singers, to rehearse the chorus. ¶ wanawan 2 in wanawan-dyār m.pl. the fee or remuneration paid to the chorus of women friends singing at a festival, such as a wedding or the like. --grākañ -- f. one of the chorus of women friends singing on such an occasion. -hurᵘ m. the words of a song sung by the chorus of women friends on such an occasion. -hurᵘ trāwun m.inf. to start, or begin, such a song. -kākañĕ f.pl. the chorus of these singing women friends. -wājĕñ f. one of the members of the above chorus of women friends. -waʦun m. the words of one of these chorus songs.
n.ag. (f. wanavüñᵘ̈), one who says, one who speaks, etc., in all the meanings of wanun 1, q.v.; an instructive or narrative statement.
m. a forest dweller; esp. a hermit, recluse, anchorite (who has abandoned home life and taken to the wilds) (Rām. 7).
a jingle of and, in anda-wand, p. 32a, l. 9, q.v.

m. a part, a share (e.g. of a piece of land, or of a pile of grain). ¶ wanḍa-bāgay f. the process of dividing out, sharing out, as ab. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), a person who allots shares, a superintendent of a sharing out or partition.

m. the cold season, winter (El. wanda, wandah, wanduh; Gr.M.; L. 326, wandh = November 15-January 15; Śiv. 327 (read wanda tay), 333, 973; Rām. 1010; K.Pr. 81 (m.pl. of gen., wanduni)). -gaṭa f. the gloom or darkness of winter; suffering or torment caused by intense cold. -kölⁱ adv. in the winter season. -mās m. a winter month, winter time. -môsᵘ adj. (f. -mösᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or suitable to be used in winter time. -phĕran m. a wadded coat for winter use. -röʦᵘ̈ f.pl. the winter nights (long, dark, and bitterly cold); cf. wandañĕ-röʦᵘ̈, bel. -röʦᵘ̈n pl. dat. used as adv. in the winter nights. -wôñᵘ m. winter water, the intensely cold water flowing in the rivers, etc., in that season. -züṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -zacĕ), an old much-worn wadded garment or coverlet for use in winter. ¶ wȧndⁱ or wandi adv. in the winter time. ¶ wandukᵘ adj. gen. (f. wandücᵘ̈), of, belonging to, produced in, or intended for use in winter (Rām. 1005, 1009, 1011). ¶ wandañĕ röʦᵘ̈ f.pl. the long winter nights = wanda-rᵒ, ab. ¶ wandas adv. in the winter (Śiv. 1687; Rām. 1006; K.Pr. 30, 86, 180, 228, 242). -kyutᵘ adv., id.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wondᵘ; f. vünzᵘ̈; 2 p.p. wanzōv), to dedicate, devote (a victim), offer (in sacrifice) (e.g. for the appeasement of some deity, or in order to cause some public calamity to be abated) (cf. rath wᵒ, p. 845b, l. 24) (Rām. 34, 163, 169, 243, 246, 251, 639, 672, 952, 1079, 1128, 1143, 1143a, b, d, 1144, 1490, 1494, 1632, 1640, 1675; K. 60, 150, 184, 246, 250, 278, 292, 309, 394, 511, 515, 523, 688, 731, 859, 927, 986-7, 1123; YZ. 22, 57, 140, 152, 541; K.Pr. 66, 75, 155, 178, 194). wandun kyutᵘ adj. (f. wandüñᵘ̈kiʦᵘ̈), for devoting, (intended to be offered) as a sacrifice, a sacrificial victim (before being offered) (Śiv. 51, 156, 191, 205, 226, 235, 237, 316, 362, 1161, 1168-9, 1417, 1435, 1537, 1594, 1613, 1742, 1744, 1767). ¶ wondᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vünzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), that which has been offered as a victim. ¶ wandana āmotᵘ perf. part. pass. (f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), become devoted as a sacrificial victim (as ab.). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. pass. to become devoted as a sacrificial victim (as ab.). ¶ wandith dyunᵘ m.inf. to offer (something) as a sacrificial victim, to devote. wandith lagun m.inf. to become devoted (as ab.); met. to become sacrificed, i.e. to be reduced to a state of ruin (by some other's action). wandith thawun m.inf. to deposit, or place ready, (a victim) for sacrifice.
f. (sg. dat. wạnḍᵃrüñᵃ), division, distribution, portioning out.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wạnḍᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. wạnḍᵃrun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wạnḍᵒrᵒ), to apportion, distribute, portion out, parcel out, divide into shares (e.g. a tract of land or other property). ¶ wạnḍᵃrith dyunᵘ m.inf. to divide out, apportion, among shareholders, to give each his share. --nyunᵘ -- m.inf. to participate, go shares in, take one's share.
f. the wife of a shopkeeper (wôñᵘ 2, q.v.) (El wányain; Gr.Gr. 38); a decent, respectable woman, who is mistress of a household. See also wôñᵘ 3.

m. that which (in bartering) is given in exchange for the object bought, price, equivalent, consideration. --barun -- m.inf. to make good the value (of something destroyed, which belongs to another), to compensate for, indemnify. -baröyⁱ f. compensation, indemnification, giving an equivalent, making good (as ab.). See waröyⁱ.
m. lameness, crippledness, haltingness, limping. Cf. wongᵘ.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wonᵘ 2, for 1, see s.v.; f. vüñᵘ̈ 4, for 1, 2, 3, see s.vv. 2 p.p. wañōv), to say, speak (cf. apozᵘ wᵒ, p. 40a, l. 44; bad-rad wᵒ, p. 88a, l. 15; bã̄g wanüñᵘ̈, p. 90a, l. 18; bŏh-tāna wanȧnⁱ, p. 95a, l. 11; banda wᵒ, p. 111b, l. 2; bayāth wanüñᵘ̈, p. 152b, l. 3; ḍūlⁱ wanüñᵘ̈, p. 212a, l. 49; dāy wᵒ, p. 266a, l. 39; hyotᵘ wᵒ, p. 367b, l. 39; kȧnⁱ-tȧlⁱ wᵒ, p. 448b, l. 36; kapas wanüñᵘ̈, p. 464a, l. 27; lọ̆tᵘ wᵒ, p. 535a, l. 48; nañĕr wᵒ, p. 644b, l. 8; phᵃr wᵒ, p. 701a, l. 10; phuraki wanañĕ, p. 704a, l. 21; phīrith wᵒ, p. 706b, l. 26; salām wanüñᵘ̈, p. 910a, l. 28; tāl zāl wanüñᵘ̈, p. 997a, l. 45; waʦun wᵒ; zŏnz wanüñᵘ̈; zĕv wanüñᵘ̈) (El.; Gr.Gr. 5; Gr.M.; L.V. 89, 94; Śiv. 47, 69, 79, 81, 83, 86, 131, 286, 311-2, 322, 355, 358, 384, 394-5, 408, 429, 449, 502-7, 743-5, 870, 1003, 1758, etc., passim; Rām. 26, 51, 64, 70, 97, 102, 107, 114, 133-4, 144, 157-8, 198, 202, 209, 220-2, 234, 242, etc., passim; K. 15-6, 38, 141, 223, 290, 385, 471, 516, 544, 560, 651, 722-3, etc., passim; H. passim, see Vocabulary; YZ. 20, 33, 36, 46, 60, 135, 206, 231, 260, etc.; K.Pr. 163, 228); ¶ to tell (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 47, 93, 116-7, 634, 683, 686, 693, 743, 764, 792, 804-5, 807, 811, 820, 893, 1121, 1446, 1653; Rām. 50, 90, 113, 135, 171, 234, 238-9, 258, 290, 337, 342, 414, 442, 527, etc., passim; K. 9, 11, 104, 156, 175, 304, 358, 386, 402-3, 511, 584, 592, 609, 643, 646, 689, 741, 704, etc., passim; H. iii, 5; vi, 15; x, 1, 6, etc.; YZ. 14, 187-9, 239, 456, etc.); ¶ to mention, refer to, tell of, describe, (sometimes with gen. of thing spoken about, as in jāyĕ-hondᵘ wᵒ, to speak about a place) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 91, 160, 203, 225, 434-5, 494, 496-7, 528, 653, 711, 742-5, 748, 770, 781, 848, 870, 895, 901, 909, 917, 921, 938, 1037, etc., passim; Rām. 313, 396, 403, 412, 424, 430, 537-8, 581, 631, 711, 896, 997, 1761, 1776; K. 97, 264, 290, 296, 300, 306, 332, 453, 487, 501, 511, 535, 546, 551, 589, 614, 637, 749, 783, etc., passim; YZ. 83, 196, 215, 249; K.Pr. 91); to explain (cf. nĕmath wanüñᵘ̈, p. 639b, l. 12) (El.; Śiv. 82, 584, 591, 594, 640, 650, 697, 837, 843, 912, 1226, 1295, 1355, 1753; Rām. 967, 1015, 1138, 1320, 1702; K. 47, 129, 508, 575-6, 991, 1176; YZ. 128, 157); to tell (in the sense of ordering, persuading, advising, etc.) (cf. wöyⁱ wöyⁱ wᵒ, s.v. wāyun) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 110, 393-4, 716-8, 1005, 1232, 1301, 1303; Rām. 5, 11, 169, 704, 1247); ¶ to call, name (as in 'people call this so-and-so'), recognize as (Gr.M.; L.V. 15; Śiv. 809, 903, 1210, 1498; Rām. 501, 1220, 1243); to say (to oneself), to consider (Śiv. 580; Rām. 580, 1124, 1194, 1250, 1306, 1346, 1348, 1366, 1391, 1421-2). --parun -- m.inf. to explain. Cf. wana-pürᵘ̈, p. 1120a, l. 47. ¶ wȧnⁱ wȧnⁱ kȧnⁱ pȧtⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. although frequently reminded to keep forgetting (K.Pr. 229). wȧnⁱ wȧnⁱ ʦandan adj. c.g. uncontrolled, independent. ¶ wonᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vüñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), said, told. ¶ wanan wanan (Śiv. 902, 904) or wanān wanān (Śiv. 490) pres. part. as adv. while speaking, as (he) said (this).
or wanunᵘ m. (inf. or verbal noun or 1) a speech, a thing said, a saying (L.V. 108; Śiv. 682, 824, 900; Rām. 1151, 1629; K. 506).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. wanyōv), to become wet, moist (Rām. 1117, 1189, 1603). Cf. wazawun.
m., i.q. wã̄dur, q.v. a monkey (? a bear, see wã̄dur) (K. 669, as N.P., sg. gen. wānarunᵘ).
a shopkeeper, esp. a travelling shopkeeper, a pedlar, a 'boxwallah' (cf. wôñᵘ wāñurᵘ, p. 1128a, l. 16); a certain small bird, haunting marshes.
m. (sg. dat. wāñĕtas), the profession of shopkeeping, trade (esp. as a grocer, or the like) (cf. puy-wᵒ, p. 813a, l. 18); the conduct of a decent, respectable man. Cf. wôñᵘ 2.
a jingle of anwār, q.v., p. 36a, l. 37.
(sic) (? wö̃ʦᵘ̈ or wö̃ʦh), a curse, partiality (El.).
(cf. also wonᵘ 1 for another word of the same form), in wȧnⁱ-wath f. a forest path, or road (esp. in mountainous country). Cf. wan 1.
adv. back, back again. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give back, return (K.Pr. 106).
m. (sg. dat. wāpaṭas), cleansing a large quantity of winnowed paddy by shaking it up in a sheet.
m.pl. a certain pox, principally affecting children, ? measles.

m. (sg. dat. wāpas), sowing (seed, etc.) (cf. bēlⁱ-wⁱ and byölⁱ-wⁱ, p. 150b, l. 10; dā̃-wᵒ, p. 231a, l. 18; harᵃda-wᵃ, p. 348a, l. 16) (Śiv. 1291); sowing-time, seed-time, the sowing season, the proper time for sowing any particular seed (L. 463). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. 'sowing to come', i.e. (of a field) to become prepared and ready for sowing. ¶ wāpa nērun m.inf. 'to issue from sowing', i.e. (of a field or the like) to have been completely sown. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. 'to come from sowing', i.e. (of a field or the like) the seeds to sprout (after sowing).

m. a place where (in accordance with a religious endowment) food is distributed free, an almshouse; cf. wŏpha. -bata m. 'almshouse rice', the practice of living on food distributed at almshouses (a lazy, heedless, life).

or wŏphā ? f. observation of good faith, faithfulness, fidelity (cf. bē-wafā, p. 147a, l. 18; bē-wŏphā, p. 148a, l. 1) (El., K.Pr. 72). --karan-wôlᵘ -- n.ag. (f. --karan-wājĕñ --), one who is faithful (El.).
or wŏphādār adj. c.g. faithful, trustworthy (El., K.Pr. 101); faithful (to), devoted (to), loyal (Rām. 773).
or wŏᵒ f. fidelity, loyalty, faithfulness (El. (wa˚); H. (wŏ˚) ii, 2-7, 10, 12).

or wŏphöyī f. fidelity, loyalty, sincerity (cf. bē-wᵒ, p. 148a, l. 4); trustworthiness, dependableness (K.Pr. 5, wafáí). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to make firm friendship (with, sṻty), become a faithful ally (Rām. 94).
(? spelling and gend.) a kind of large pear (L. 350, note).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wôpᵘ), to sow (a field), to plant (a field) with seed (Gr.M.); to sow (seed) in a field, to scatter seed; cf. wawun. wôpᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wöpᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈) (of a field) sown; (of seed) sown (in a field).

m. twisting (as in twisting together the strands of a string between the palms of the hands) (cf. atha-wᵒ, p. 64b, l. 21; khŏshⁱ-wⁱ, p. 418b, l. 40; khŏshⁱ-wȧrⁱ, id., l. 44; muʦaran-wᵒ, p. 610b, l. 25) (Śiv. 1014, 1217 (pun on war 2), 1643, 1646, 1872; K.Pr. 219, gō̃ʦhan war, twisting, or twirling, the moustaches).

m. a time, occasion, opportunity (cf. angȧlⁱ-wⁱ, p. 33b, l. 47; yīshĕr-wᵒ, s.v. yīshŏr); esp. a favourable opportunity, the right, or propitious, time (for something) (Śiv. 1790, K.Pr. 102); a day of the week, a week day (including Sunday. They are āth-wᵒ, Sunday, p. 67b, l. 13; ʦạndra-wᵒ, Monday, p. 1074b, l. 14; bōm-wᵒ, p. 107b, l. 2, or mangal-wᵒ, p. 578b, l. 50, Tuesday; bŏd-wᵒ, Wednesday, p. 83b, l. 3, and K. 57; gŏra-wᵒ, p. 297b, l. 7, or bras-wᵒ, p. 127a, l. 42, Thursday; shọ̆kᵃr-wᵃ, Friday, p. 879a, l. 36; and baṭa-wᵒ, Saturday, p. 145b, l. 36) (cf. zā-wār, s.v. zā; zāhna-wār); a flock, herd, troop (cf. sĕnda-wᵒ, p. 918b, l. 29). ¶ wāra-phyurᵘ m. the passage of time (counted in days of the week). --wāra -- adv. over and over again, repeatedly (K. 474).

m. a boon, blessing, favour (cf. pīra-wᵒ, p. 753a, l. 11) (Śiv. 448, 851, 934, 1166, 1173, 1217 (pun on war 1), 1219, 1651, 1697, 1738, 1761; Rām. 565; K. 16, 67, 268, 278, 330, 423-4, 537, 574, 577, 604, 606, 611-2, 620-1, 625, 655, 705, 739, 792, 795-6, 876-7, 965, 1029); used --˚ to indicate the excellence of anything, esp. as an indication of respect, as in gŏra-war, a revered preceptor (Śiv. 1022).

m. putting or piling things over each other (e.g. courses of bricks in building a wall, or pieces of material or embroideries on cloth, etc.) (cf. hanga-wᵒ, p. 338b, l. 50; kȧmbⁱ-wⁱ, p. 444a, l. 35; nȧrⁱ-wⁱ, p. 649a, l. 30; phȧlⁱ-wⁱ, p. 694b, l. 28; palang-wᵒ, p. 731b, l. 17; ṭōpi-wᵒ, p. 1014a, l. 25; ʦökⁱ-wⁱ, p. 1067b, l. 22; zamba- wār) (Rām. 1301, a pile of bones); winding or twisting a string, or the like, over and over into a ball. --anun -- m.inf. to build (as ab.) in courses, one above the other; to wind up string, etc., into a ball, as ab. --thawun -- m.inf. to keep, retain (K.Pr. 206). --trāwun -- m.inf. to throw away (K.Pr. 206).
m. inward anger (due to wishes being thwarted), resentment, displeasure, umbrage, dudgeon (cf. būta-wᵒ, p. 141b, l. 18).
m. a hedge (of thorns or the like round a garden, etc.) (El. wár, or towards Islāmābād, wáḍ).
m. pretended reluctance, coquetry, coquettish behaviour (cf. göñᵘ̈-wᵘ̈, p. 294a, 1. 2).
m. a long strip of land (generally near a lake or the like) grown over with willows and similar shrubs (cf. vīri-wᵒ, p. 1136a, l. 16).
m. in war-kulᵘ the banyan or Indian fig-tree, Ficus indica.
m. in gar-wār, a taste for housekeeping (p. 236a, l. 32).
a suff. borrowed from Persian (āwar, war, or wār) implying possession, as in nāma-war (= نام آور, or نام ور, or نام وار), possessing a name, famous, p. 636b, l. 23. See warī.
f. a sacrificial rite, used --˚ in māsa-wᵒ, p. 596a, l. 3; pacha-wᵒ, p. 679a, l. 12.

adj. c.g. fitting, suitable; fitting accurately together, intimately united; (as subst.) fitness, suitability, accurate fitting together; a fitting result, satisfactory condition (Śiv. 1795, 1797); cf. wār 8 and wāra. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be, or become fitting or suitable, to fit into place, to fit conveniently in with some work. --wath gaʦhun -- m.inf. (circumstances, e.g. relations, residence, worldly condition, or the like) to become suitable, or as one would wish; cf. wāra wati, etc., p. 1135a, l. 25. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. suitability, or fitness, to occur; fitness for union (or friendship, etc.) to occur (Rām. 327); (of two things) fitting together accurately, or suitably, to occur.
a Persian suffix used in revenue terms, as in asömī-wār, p. 50a, l. 18, and here meaning 'after, or according to, the details of'. This suffix also indicates suitability or fitness. Cf. wār 7.
m. i.q. wôrᵘ 2 or wörᵘ̈ 1, in ʦȧkⁱ-wār, p. 1067b, l. 4.
in ti warā karith, p. 967b, l. 5; i.q. waröy, q.v.

adj. c.g. and adv. in good condition, doing well (Rām. 1423, 1443); comfortable, at ease; healthy, well; (adv.) easily, comfortably (K. 1120, YZ. 21); fittingly, suitably, thoroughly, completely (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 23, 26, 159, 369, 481, 675, 752, 906, 1073, 1304, 1307, 1655; Rām. 386, 527, 707, 1170, 1511; K. 36, 122; H. vii, 24; YZ. 35, 128, 206, 236, 262, 269); excellently, in an excellent manner (El.; Gr.M.; W. 96; Śiv. 1638, 1859); attentively (El.; Śiv. 113, 157; Rām. 797, 806); carefully, properly (Rām. 625-6); skilfully (El., W. 96); cf. wār 7 and wārāh. --āsun -- m.inf. to be comfortable and in good health, to thrive in health and circumstances or in either; to be in good spiritual health, to be piously disposed (Śiv. 375). --kāra -- adv. prosperously, continually and steadily without opposition or impediment, steadily and securely, in good condition, safe and sound (H. x, 8); auspiciously (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1080, 1097); cf. wāray, bel. --pöṭhⁱ -- or --pöṭhin -- adv. correctly, well and thoroughly, carefully and effectively (Śiv. 70, Rām. 1292, K. 645). --rōzun -- m.inf. to be and continue right, in good condition, prosperous, etc., as ab. --wāra -- adv. without undue haste, gently, slowly, gradually, by slow degrees (El. warawara, slowly; W. 96, 151; Śiv. 394, 1081, 1097, 1686; Rām. 800, 1183, 1568, 1624, 1676, 1731; YZ. 100; K.Pr. 262); over and over again, repeatedly; gently, softly (Rām. 102). --wati -- adv. on the prosperous road, prosperously, thrivingly, happily flourishing; cf. wār 7. --wati rōzun -- m.inf. to be and continue on the prosperous way, to prosper, thrive, flourish in happiness. ¶ wāray adj. c.g. prosperous indeed, very happily thriving (Śiv. 578, 949, 1074); adv. thoroughly, completely (Śiv. 13, 1533 (kāray is a misprint), 1898; Rām. 957); very attentively (Śiv. 954, Rām. 1108a); comfortably, happily (Rām. 1632). wāray-kāray adv. very auspiciously (Śiv. 55, 392).
in āra-wara, like a hill-stream (āra), p. 41b, l. 2; kŏ-wara, in a bad way, by a wrong method, p. 496a, l. 36.
an adjectival form, based on war 2 (q.v.), in pīra-wara, p. 753a, l. 13.
in wara-kúr (El.), see wōra-kūrᵘ̈, p. 1136b, l. 17.
m. one who grants boons, a bestower of boons (K. 705).
m. a boar, pig (wild or domesticated); the third, or boar, incarnation of Vishnu (Śiv. 856).
m. N. of an important town at the west end of the Valley of Kashmir, called Bārāmūlā by foreigners. Its Sanskrit name was Varāha-mūla (El. Waramúl, K.Pr. 229). See RT.Tr. II, 482.
f. a coquette, flirt. Cf. war 4.
adj. c.g. twisted (and so no longer straight). Cf. war 1.
one who readily takes umbrage, resentful, irascible, irritable. Cf. war 3.
f. a fine, handsome, house, a mansion, palace.
n.ag. (f. waravüñᵘ̈), one who chooses or selects (see warun 2) (Śiv. 850, K. 705).

adj. c.g. very much, excessive (L. 462 wárujáh; Śiv. 33, 423, 877; Rām. 101, 459, 497; H. iii, 1; viii, 2); (as adv.) excessively, exceedingly (Śiv. 656, 696, 714, 728, 784, 873, 1294; Rām. 226, 350, 1020). Cf. wārāh.
m. (? f.) the zodiacal sign Scorpio (El. warchak m.). Cf. vrushcikh.
in wardā-budav m. a man (esp. an impudent young fellow) who, for his own purposes, habitually swindles others, a regular swindler, a dishonest fellow.

m. a bridal garment (worn by the bride at the ceremony, and provided by her parents) (cf. maʦa-wᵒ, p. 602b, l. 18) (Śiv. 996, 1219, 1651; Rām. 763, 1591); handsome garments given by the bridegroom's relations after the weddiṇg.

m. (of a stick, rope, or the like) wrapped round, lapped round; (of some incident) puzzling, complicated; (of some work or business) in which obstacles are apprehended, expected to be difficult. Cf. war 1.
m. a contrivance, plan, device (for carrying out some very difficult work).
f. a midwife (cf. māra-wᵒ, p. 587a, l. 5) (El. wāryin; L. wárin, 270, 462; K.Pr. 231, sg. obl. wáriní).

m. usage, custom, established practice (as handed down from former times), approved moral conduct (cf. rǖnⁱ-wⁱ, p. 835b, l. 46); polite and virtuous conduct, good manners; the intelligent carrying out of any work or business (by one who understands it thoroughly). --raṭun -- m.inf. to adopt established practice, to take to polite and virtuous conduct. --rāwarun -- m.inf. (of some respected and reverend person) to abandon customary politeness (for some temporary reason). ¶ warga bĕhun m.inf. (of one formerly leading an irregular habit) to adopt and continue in established and virtuous customs, to lead a reformed life. --dapun -- m.inf. to give advice to another in a circumlocutory manner, e.g. to advise in parables, or by talking to a third person on some apparently different matter. --raṭun -- m.inf. to take, or make obedient, a person, that he may receive moral training. --rōzun -- m.inf. (after receiving good moral instruction) to continue in good conduct. --thawun --  m.inf. to put (a pupil, servant, or the like) in the proper line of conduct for the performance of any task; to fix anything in its right order or position. ¶ wargas aʦun m.inf. (when one has come to full age and years of discretion) to take or engage in a livelihood by carrying on some business.

adj. (f. warhüjᵘ̈), crooked, bent, or distorted inside (e.g. a sheaf, or a cloth, tightly wrapped up) (K.Pr. 231, of a log); (of a man, met.) having the heart or inner feelings awry (owing to anger or the like).

f. (1) in nām-warī, reputation, p. 636b, l. 10, Persian termination indicating possession, formed from war 6, q.v. ¶ (2) in nāma-warī, reputation, p. 636b, l. 25, a corruption of the Persian āwarī آوری, also indicating possession.
see not only worᵘ, but also wurᵘ.
(K. 173), for warĕ, see warĕ ta wadạvĕ karañĕ, s.v. vürᵘ̈ 1.

or warihy or wȧrⁱhy m. (sg. dat. wȧrⁱhis or warihĕs), a year (cf. aki warihĕ aki, p. 20b, l. 30; dahi dŏhⁱ warihĕ pĕṭha, p. 200b, l. 11; drāga-wᵒ, p. 241b, l. 26; nīla-wᵒ, p. 634a, l. 28; prath warihĕ, p. 769a, l. 47) (El. weri; Gr.Gr. warihy, 148, 158; warihĕ path warihĕ, year by year, 158; Gr.M.; Rām. 7, 466-7, 787; H. xii, 20; YZ. 394, 402, 406; K.Pr. 176, warih, 231 warí). Cf. wahar. ¶ wȧrⁱhi-bata m. a year's food, all the food-grain grown or stored in a particular year. -sôwᵘ m. a prosperous year (with abounding crops, free from disease or other calamities, and with a happy prosperous people). ¶ wȧrⁱhyukⁱ adj. gen. (f. wȧrⁱhicⁱ), of, belonging to, born in, or produced in (such-and-such) a year (cf. drāga-wᵒ, p. 241b, l. 32); taking a year to grow, accomplished in a year, or taking a year for accomplishment.

conjnct. a particle indicating an option or alternative, as in bata nay khĕkh, ʦŏcĕ warish khĕh, if thou wilt not eat boiled rice, as an alternative eat bread; ʦᵃh nay gaʦhakh, suh warish gaʦhin, if you will not go, let him go instead.
f. of wahorᵘ, q.v. Cf. okᵘ-wȧrishᵘ, p. 19b, l. 8; sata-wȧrⁱshiy, Śiv. 578.
m. a swelling (such as a tumour, etc.) (El.).

or warᵃn m. (sg. dat. warnas), a colour, hue (L.V. 15, Śiv. 1558); a caste (among Hindūs), a class, race, tribe (cf. rāza-wᵒ, p. 857b, l. 9; trī-warna, p. 1035b, l. 14) (Rām. 1261); the general appearance of a person (other than the speaker) (Śiv. 600, 840, 1266, 1386; Rām. 223, 369, 861); nature, character (Rām. 25, 109). --dārun -- m.inf. to assume a certain general appearance (Śiv. 840); to assume the general appearance of another, to disguise oneself.
f. condition, state, in nānā-warnā, a condition of diversity, a condition of varying existence (Śiv. 1492). Cf. warn.
m. the small coins given in exchange for (and equivalent in value to) a coin or coins of large value, small change.

waröi, waröyi, or warā postpos. governing abl., without, bereft of (cf. atha-wᵒ, p. 64b, l. 23; kharca-wᵒ, p. 413a, l. 36; mōta-wᵒ, p. 604b, l. 6; ti warā karith, p. 967b, l. 5) (El. veráí, waráí; W. 113, waröi); except (El., Gr.M., W. 97). In wōda-baröyⁱ (p. 1097a, l. 10) and wanga-baröyⁱ (p. 1124a, l. 37) this word is spelt with an initial b instead of w.
m. a year (Śiv. 924, YZ. 190). warshĕ-phal m. the fruit of the year, i.e. a kind of horoscope, or paper showing a man's fate during the current year.

or warshunᵘ m. (sg. dat. warshĕnas), raining, rain, showering (cf. akölⁱ-wⁱ, p. 21a, l. 36; kŏ-kölⁱ-wⁱ, p. 431b, l. 5; pōshĕ-wᵒ, p. 779a, l. 43) (El. also gives the meaning 'rest') (Śiv. 167, 345, 508, 903, 1038, 1146, 1243, 1252-3, 1410, 1550, 1913; Rām. 1714, 1723, 1777; K. 56, 451, 567, 771, 874).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. worshᵘ), to rain down (something), to shower (something) down (cf. pōsh wᵒ, p. 778b, l. 10) (K. 196, 255). Cf. washun.

m. repeated practice or exercise (in order to become perfect in any act or business) (Śiv. 1218); occupation, profession; manner of living, mode of life (Śiv. 1619, 1649); mutual close association or fellowship between two persons; earnings, hire, wages. --āsun -- m.inf. full and complete practice to be acquired. --thawun -- m.inf. to set up a close fellowship (with some person) (e.g. with some influential person in the hope of future profit). -müʦᵘ̈ f. a woman who (after falling from a high station) has taken to humble work (e.g. the wife of a great man who for some cause has sunk to being a maidservant). ¶ wartanas bĕhun m.inf. to sit at earning, i.e. (of some well-to-do person, compelled by some misfortune) to take to a humble occupation (such as household service). --rōzun -- m.inf. (of some well-to-do person, as ab.) to carry on such a humble occupation. --thawun -- m.inf. to compel some person (esp. one of a status equal to one's own, such as a wife, son, parent, or brother) to take a humble occupation.
m. use, custom (Gr.M.); conduct, behaviour (Gr.M.); circulation or currency (of a coin) (Gr.M.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wartôwᵘ), to use, employ, apply, put (something) to use, occupy oneself in (some work) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1211); to enter into close association or fellowship with (another); (of some quantity of anything that has to be distributed) to distribute the respective shares (to the recipients) (H. xi, 7); to dispense, expend (an allotted sum, such as household expenses) (Gr.M.). wartôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wartövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), put to its proper use, employed; distributed (as ab.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wortᵘ, f. vürʦᵘ̈; 2 p.p. warʦōv), to practise, repeatedly exercise oneself in (any act or business); to use, apply, occupy oneself in (any thing or work). --bartun -- m.inf. (a jingle of wartun), to practise close association or fellowship with (another). ¶ wortᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vürʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), used, employed (for its proper purpose), practised. ¶ wartani bĕhun m.inf. (when a quantity of anything has to be distributed) to set to work at distributing the respective shares (to the recipients).

m. (sg. dat. warakas), a leaf (of a tree, or of a book, or of silver, or gold, etc.) (cf. dyāna-wᵒ, p. 268b, l. 18; nĕchapatri-wᵒ, p. 621a, l. 36; sŏna-wᵒ, p. 917b, l. 10) (El., Gr.M.). --phērun -- m.inf. 'the leaf to be turned over', i.e. when just on the point of success to meet unsuccess. --phirun -- m.inf. 'to turn over a leaf', i.e. to cause unsuccess to one who is on the point of success.
adj. (f. wārᵘ̈jᵘ̈ or wārüjᵘ̈), (of anything animate or inanimate) in sound condition, strong, and of good quality or virtuous.

also written warunᵘ, and, by Paṇḍits, m. N. of a certain deity; the regent of the ocean and of the western quarter (Skt. Varuṇa) (Śiv. 1154; Rām. 583, 780-4, 792; K. 335-6, 591); met. water generally (L.V. 53). waruna lūkapāl m. the regent of the western quarter. Cf. worᵘnorᵘ 2.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wôrᵘ), to move out of the way, put aside; to drive away (e.g. flies with a fan); to wipe off, erase (writing, a picture, design, or the like). wôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), put aside, etc., as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. worᵘ 2, for 1, see s.v.), to choose, select (esp. a husband, a wife, a friend, or a servant) (Śiv. 45, 114, 413, 629, 635, 661, 668, 711, 714, 995, 1128, 1135-6, 1218, 1491, 1608, 1722, 1727, 1740, 1752, 1760, 1772, 1809; Rām. 326, 328; K. 206, 268, 613, 655, 705, 730, 766, 768, 778, 781, 807, 918); to choose (a person as the recipient, acc., of a boon, abl.), grant a boon (to), to put (a person) in receipt of a boon (K. 206, 521, 1029); to accept, (graciously) to deign to accept (Śiv. 1534, 1851); to ask a boon, petition for (K. 422). worᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), chosen, selected, as ab.
m. a certain bird of prey (like a kite or falcon. It is said to kill smaller birds, such as crows, starlings, or sparrows, in a single swoop).
m. a cultivator, in warza-bāgay f. (at a harvest-home, when the entire crop has been collected) the apportionment of their shares among the owner of the field and the cultivators.
f. (sg. dat. warzüñᵘ̈), leaving, giving up, abandoning (cf. pāpa-wᵒ, p. 749a, l. 15).
f. (sg. dat. warzüʦᵘ̈), putting away, expelling, banishment (of a thing, work, etc.); ostracizing, excommunicating (a person).

m. (sg. dat. warzakas; f. warzücᵘ̈), he (or she) who provides all the necessaries for carrying on a household, a housewife, housekeeper, the earning member of a house (cf. gar-wᵒ, p. 296a, l. 38; pāna-wᵒ, p. 736a, l. 9; par-wᵒ, p. 751a, l. 29).
in warzunᵘ wāv m. poverty, neediness, destitution. -wāv pyonᵘ m.inf. poverty to fall (on someone rich).

f. marrow (Śiv. 191, 316); brain (El.). ¶ wasi āsun m.inf. 'to be in the marrow'; hence, (of some work) to have a place in the heart, to be cherished, be loved, prized. --nūn pyonᵘ -- m.inf. 'salt to fall on the marrow', great distress to be experienced (e.g. by the loss or destruction of some cherished object, or by the receipt of bad news). -pĕṭh adv. 'on the marrow', (something that should be carried out) voluntarily, eagerly, ardently, with all one's heart.

m. dwelling, resting, living, residing (cf. wan-wās, p. 1120a, l. 20) (L.V. 55; Śiv. 818, 1432, 1439, 1452, 1472, 1713; K. 1115); pressing, grasping, holding (in atha-wās, p. 64b, ll. 23 ff.) (L.V. 92; Śiv. 956, 1010, 1432, 1441, 1442 (athav-wᵒ, mutual hand-grasping), 1460, 1467, 1676; Rām. 737, 1779-80; K. 400, 666, 1130); one who dwells, inhabits (i.q. wösⁱ, in sŏrga-wās or -wösī, p. 934a, l. 26) (Śiv. 1257, 1354). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take up an abode (L.V. 18, Śiv. 955).

f. a board or panel with a carved pattern, used in the ceiling of a room between each joist (Rām. 577). ¶ wasa-püṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -pacĕ), a single one of these boards. -tālav m. a ceiling ornamented with these boards (K. 922). -tān a joist supporting these boards.
m. dress, clothes, a garment (mal-wās, p. 564a, l. 42; wạsᵃtra-wᵃ, s.v. wạsᵃtᵃr).

f. in wasa-khas f. descent and ascent, falling and rising (e.g. of the breath, or of the vital airs going upwards and downwards) (Śiv. 1027, 1682); fluctuations (in prosperity), vicissitudes; (in comparing two similar objects) unevenness, lowness and height; cf. khasa- was, p. 417a, l. 8. wasa-was f. gradual descent (from a high position, lit. and met.).
in was-vihurᵘ m. the whole collection of a person's ornaments, bijouterie, jewelry.
f. (sg. dat. wasamüʦᵘ̈), the entire property (of a wealthy person) (K.Pr. 80). --khë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (under the guise of friendship) to steal or misappropriate the entire property (of some one).

or wāsanā f. (sg. dat. wāsanāyĕ), fancy, imagination, idea (Rām. (-nā) 315, 682, 847); expectation, inclination; intention, determination (to accomplish something) (cf. rākhĕs-wᵒ, p. 832a, l. 3) (Śiv. (-nā) 182, 237, 239, 371, 755, 984, 1421, 1524, 1811; Rām. (-nā) 38, 52); wish, desire (generally) (Śiv. (-nā) 158, 165, 452, 1311, 1341, 1472, 1655, 1677, 1815, 1833; Rām. (-nā) 100, 1660, 1776, 1779). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. longing or desire (esp. for something unobtainable, or when inopportune) to occur.
m. (sg. dat. wasantas), the spring, the vernal season, the Skt. word corresponding to sō̃th, q.v. -ādĕkh m.pl. spring and the other (five seasons), all the six seasons (Rām. 573).

f. (sg. dat. wasüʦᵘ̈), a place of permanent abode, a home (cf. wāri-wᵒ, p. 1138a, l. 17); the locality in which a man's ancestors have dwelt and in which his descendants are born, the family home (cf. wāri-wᵒ, p. 1138a, l. 17).

n.ag. (f. wasavüñᵘ̈), that which comes down, descends, falls (lit. and met.), and so on in all the meanings of wasun, q.v. (El.; Śiv. 499, 1560; YZ. 108); (of a road, ground, or the like) that which descends gradually, that which slopes down (cf. the preceding) (K.Pr. 72).
f. the making (a person) subject to influence, bringing under subjection, used --˚, as in būta-wash, p. 141b, l. 20.

m. (of a cloth, sheet of paper, or the like) unevenness, the being crushed or crumpled; a crease caused by crushing or crumpling, as ab. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. crumpling to occur; met. impatience, indignation, or grudging to be felt (esp., at a meal, of anger felt against the server when one does not get served as one wishes). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to smooth out creases, etc., as ab., to spread out straight, stretch out (Rām. 531, where korᵘ is for koḍᵘ); to rub down or massage (a wearied leg or other member). --karun -- m.inf. (Rām. 531), see the preceding (korᵘ, here being a vill. form of koḍᵘ). --nērun -- m.inf. crushing or creases to be smoothed out.

adj. c.g. obedient (to), submissive (to), under the influence or control (of), under the power (of) (Gr.M.); charmed, fascinated; subdued by charms, incantations, or the like. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become subject to the influence (of), to become fascinated by (esp. used of a woman becoming subject to love) (Śiv. 1454). --karun -- m.inf. to make subject, to bring under subjection, bring under one's influence (e.g. by persuasion, conciliation, or by charms, etc.). ¶ washĕ-wö m. the term used in schools for the Śāradā character corresponding to the Nāgarī wa.
wöshⁱ, or wöshᵘ̈, in wāla-wᵒ, p. 1112a, l. 3, q.v.

m. (sg. dat. washạpas), forgetfulness, heedlessness, carelessness, inattention (e.g. when one carelessly drops something, so that it breaks, or, when doing some work, carelessly neglects some important action, so that the result is not what is wanted).

(? cf. واشکافتن) m. (? dat.) the divulging of some secret (occurrence, secret formula, thing, action, or the like) (? with شکافتن, cf. the slang English, 'to split'). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. sudden or unexpected divulging (as ab.) to occur.
adj. c.g. (of a cloth, sheet of paper, or the like) uneven, crushed, crumpled, creased; (of a human being) impatient, indignant, having a grudge.
m. bringing (a person) under one's own influence, subduing, subjugating. Cf. wash 1.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. woshᵘ), to rain (water from the clouds), drizzle, shower. Cf. warshun 2.
or washĕwunᵘ m. the occurrence of long-continued gentle rain, a long gentle shower. Cf. woshᵘ.
m. support, prop, help, aid, resource (Rām. 1425); as postpos. governing gen., by means of (W. 98). -sṻty, as postpos., id. (W. 98).

m. (sg. dat. wasishṭhas), N. of a celebrated Hindū sage, in Skt. Vasiṣṭha or Vaśiṣṭha. He was the family priest of Dashĕrath (Daśaratha), Rāma's father, and of Rāma himself (Rām. 104, 222, 1109, 1140, 1143c, 1308, 1310, 1681).
m. (in Ksh.) a meeting, interview (El., YZ. 524).
m. a powder made from the leaf of a certain shrub, and used as a hair dye.
m. motive, reason; account, sake; relationship, connexion. --thawun -- m.inf. to have to do (with), to concern, to bear (upon).

wast or wasᵃth m. (sg. dat. wastas), a thing, article, chattel (cf. banda-wᵒ, p. 111a, l. 41) (Gr.M.; K. 952; H. v, 1); a certain ornament (cf. haṭi-wᵒ, p. 356b, l. 18; sŏna-(or sŏnⁱ-)wⁱ, p. 917b, ll. 12, 27); a garment, (pl.) clothes genl. (cf. dŏbⁱ-wⁱ, p. 182b, l. 45) (K.Pr. 231).

or wạsᵃtᵃr m. (sg. dat. wạsᵃtras), a garment, clothes, raiment (Gr.M.; Śiv. 10, 58, 752, 801, 889-90, 1037, 1047, 1329, 1411; Rām. 784, 1087, 1189, 1758; K. 227, 418-9, 1046). --pairun -- m.inf. to put on clothes, to dress oneself (Gr.M., Śiv. 1440); to put clothes on another, to dress a person (K. 422, 843). wạsᵃtra-wās m. flimsy raiment. wạsᵃtᵃra-wan m. N. of a certain sacred site and grove (Śiv. 1037, 1411).
in wȧstⁱ pyonᵘ m.inf. to fall down (from a height through the air), to drop. Cf. wȧsⁱ.
m. N. of the father of Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) (Skt. Vasudēva) (Śiv. 1385; K. 1, 17, 23-5, 28, 33, 37, 44, 50, 53, 75, 127, 356, et passim).
m. a N. of Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) as the son of Wasudēv (q.v.) (Śiv. 1325, 1369, 1472, 1850).

or wāsakh-nāg m. (sg. dat. wāsakas), N. of a celebrated serpent, the king of snakes (in Skt. Vāsuki) (Śiv. 169, 360, 504, 1040, 1153, 1170, 1557); (in Ksh.) N. of site in Kashmīr where there is a spring sacred to Vāsuki (cf. RT.Tr. II, 470).
m. arrival (El.); a kind of drum (Śiv. 1729).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. wothᵘ 1, f. (Rām. 10, 111) vüʦhᵘ̈ 1, for 2, 3, see wothᵘ 2, 3, for 4, see s.v.; 2 p.p. waʦhōv. The 1 p.p. should be distinguished from wọ̆thᵘ, 1 p.p. of wŏthun, to rise, q.v. The two words are almost identical in sound, but have opposed meanings. The causal of this verb is wālun, to bring down, q.v. sometimes written wārun (Gr.Gr. 175). The opposites of this verb are khasun and wŏthun, qq.v. both meaning 'to rise'); to descend, come down, dismount (cf. bŏn wᵒ, p. 110b, l. 14; bēli wᵒ, p. 150b, l. 23; dŏbas wᵒ, p. 182b, l. 3; guri wᵒ, p. 299a, l. 28; hȧṭⁱ wothᵘ, p. 356a, l. 35; haṭi wᵒ, p. 356b, l. 14; phīrith wᵒ, p. 706b, l. 28; wŏl wasüñᵘ̈, p. 1112b, l. 12) (El.; Gr.Gr. 175, 205, 210; Gr.M.; L.V. 69; Śiv. 182, 509, 788, 966, 1074, 1300, 1664, 1686, 1874; Rām. 10, 111, 280, 1055, 1078, 1461, 1713, 1716; K. 278, 335, 396, 411, 656, 851; H. iii, 2, 5, 9; v, 7, 9; vi, 16; viii, 4, 6, 13; ix, 4, 6; x, 5; xii, 2, 6, 7, 11, 14-5; K.Pr. 72, 82, 87, 158, 252); (of some condition or season) to come down upon (a person), to be very near (cf. lônᵘ wᵒ, p. 525b, l. 10); to come down (from a boat), to land (Gr.M.); ¶ to become lowered, abased, to fall (in price, value, estimation, dignity) (cf. dĕmāg wᵒ, p. 219a, l. 39; drŏbas wᵒ, p. 239b, l. 49; phūdᵃr wᵒ, p. 685a, l. 45; yĕṭh wasüñᵘ̈, s.v. yĕṭh 1); to become taken down, lowered, reduced, disgraced, degraded (cf. mada wᵒ, p. 548b, l. 7; mōda wᵒ, p. 549a, l. 30; pāvi wᵒ, p. 810a, l. 45; tama wᵒ, -wothᵘ, wothᵘ- motᵘ, p. 1005a, ll. 17, 20; tāwa wᵒ, p. 1047a, l. 7); ¶ to be dropped, let fall, (of rain) to fall, to be showered or scattered (cf. arshĕ wᵒ, p. 44b, l. 21; brö̃ṭⁱ wasȧnⁱ, p. 127b, l. 12; lānath wasüñᵘ̈, p. 528a, l. 11; pathar wᵒ, p. 798b, l. 39; tāli tāli wᵒ, p. 997b, l. 24; wojᵘ wᵒ, p. 1107a, l. 10) (Śiv. 501, 1532); to fall suddenly or en masse, to fall in overwhelming quantity (e.g. an avalanche) (cf. lam wasith yunᵘ, p. 524a, l. 15; mȧtⁱ-wôñⁱ wᵒ, p. 602b, l. 5; raḍa wᵒ, p. 825a, l. 50; wŏbⁱ wasȧnⁱ, p. 1093a, l. 1) (Rām. 402); (of a liquid) to flow down, or out (cf. dŏd wᵒ, p. 188a, l. 50; dāri dāri wᵒ, p. 235b, l. 1; rath ṭhī˜ca wᵒ, p. 845b, l. 29; tᵃyĕ wᵒ, p. 1048b, l. 28) (Śiv. 618, 1212, 1588; Rām. 1587, 1616); (of food) to go down (the throat), be swallowed (K. 213, 1101; K.Pr. 250); ¶ (of disease, defect, injury, or the like) to come down (on a person or thing), to attack (cf. bŏchi- gaṭa wasüñᵘ̈, p. 80a, l. 24; brikh wasüñᵘ̈, p. 122b, l. 11; brᵃs wasüñᵘ̈, p. 126a, l. 43; khōla wasañĕ, p. 398a, l. 4; khras wasüñᵘ̈, p. 416a, l. 1; myondᵘ wᵒ, p. 613b, l. 39; phsara wasañĕ, p. 714a, l. 15; parkölⁱ wasȧnⁱ, p. 758a, l. 45; tranga wasañĕ, p. 1028a, l. 11; trŏngⁱ wasȧnⁱ, p. 1028a, l. 19; trᵃth wᵒ, p. 1032a, l. 24; wuka wasüñᵘ̈, p. 1108a, l. 20; wuna wasüñᵘ̈, p. 1122a, l. 43) (Śiv. 1296, 1752; K.Pr. 99, 167); ¶ to go down (from the shore to a boat), to embark, go aboard, to go down (into the water, to bathe) (cf. nāvi wᵒ, p. 667a, l. 17) (K. 270-1, 971); ¶ (of a tool or the like) to come down (on to something, in order to be brought into action), to begin to be worked or to be set working (on something), to begin to work (on) (cf. nĕndi wᵒ, p. 641b, l. 50); to come down (upon), meddle (with); hence, pilfer (from) (K.Pr. 246); ¶ to be taken down (from), to be taken off, put away (cf. nakha wᵒ, p. 629a, l. 1, and Śiv. 1562); (of a debt) to be paid off (K. 460); to be torn off, stripped off, peeled off (cf. drūrᵘ wᵒ, p. 248a, l. 19; tᵃr wasüñᵘ̈, p. 1017a, l. 20; tᵃra wasañĕ, ib., l. 25) (Rām. 603, K.Pr. 213); ¶ to be ruined, made useless, worn out, brought to a bad condition (cf. bāna wᵒ, p. 110a, l. 12; nakh wasȧnⁱ, p. 628a, l. 38; nala-nakha wᵒ, p. 632a, l. 27; pỗdᵘ wᵒ, p. 682a, l. 3; phĕkⁱ wasȧnⁱ, p. 721a, l. 3; pŏṭh wasüñᵘ̈, p. 796b, l. 22; rās wᵒ, p. 842b, l. 3; yĕḍ wasüñᵘ̈); to wane, fade, become wasted, decline, (of a heavenly body) to set (cf. buthi wᵒ, p. 143b, l. 17; dŏh wᵒ, p. 200a, l. 4; drē̃ṭh wᵒ, p. 249b, l. 21; rasa wᵒ, and -wothᵘ, p. 842a, ll. 18, 23; sṻrĕ wᵒ, p. 933a, l. 12; thras wasüñᵘ̈, p. 984b, l. 11); to go down, subside (e.g. something swollen) (cf. lal wasüñᵘ̈, p. 521b, l. 36); (of a door or the like) to be opened, unlocked (Śiv. 340). ¶ wȧsⁱ wȧsⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to keep descending little by little; to become gradually subject to ever-increasing fear; to become gradually weaker and weaker owing to increasing hunger or starvation. wȧsⁱ wȧsⁱ pyonᵘ, see wasith pyonᵘ, bel. See also wȧsⁱ and wȧstⁱ, s.vv. ¶ wasith bata m. soft boiled rice in which (owing to the water not being carefully poured away) the grains are clotted together and not separate (cf. phali wᵒ bᵒ, p. 694b, l. 33). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to descend, or drop, in one single fall (and not in stages) (lit. and fig.) (Rām. 604, 1713, 1718-9); (the ground, etc.) to fall in, a cavity or crater to appear (in the ground) (K. 632); boiled rice to clot, as ab. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall down, tumble down, be knocked down (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1630; Rām. 156, 239, 287, 290, 322, 399, 454, 483, 500, 504, 518, 527, 712, 897, 916, 922, 933, 1111, 1115, 1201, 1309, 1352, 1354, 1401, 1578 (so wȧsⁱ wȧsⁱ pyonᵘ, 1180, 1252, to fall down again and again); K. 110, 212, 329, 798; H. ii, 3, 6; YZ. 194). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come down, descend (Rām. 112). ¶ wothᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vüʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, Śiv. 1752), descended, come down, etc., as ab. (cf. rasa wothᵘ-motᵘ, p. 842a, l. 25; vēgi wothᵘ-motᵘ, s.v. vyūgᵘ, to be compared with vēgi- wothᵘ, s.v. wothᵘ 3) (Rām. 400); (of hair) reaching down to (the knees) (Rām. 285).
m. palpitation of the heart (from fear, apprehension, or the like), fluctuation of mind, wavering, nervousness, perturbation (El. waswas, sorrow; YZ. 93). ? Cf. waswö.
(? spelling) (? waswās, q.v.) m. surprise (El. waswã). waswa trāwun (sic) m.inf. to surprise (El.).
adj. c.g. apprehensive, dreading, nervous, timorous.
n.ag. (f. was-vüñᵘ̈), (of a road, sloping land, or the like) gradually descending, with a downward slope. Cf. the next.
m. a thing, article, esp. such a thing as an ornament, a vessel, a spade or other tool (cf. dŏbⁱ-wⁱ, p. 182b, l. 42).

in wȧsⁱpyōmotⁱ perf. part. (f. --pyömüʦᵘ̈ -- or --pyēmüʦᵘ̈ --), fallen down (from a height) (lit. and met.). pyonᵘ or wȧstⁱpyonⁱ m.inf. to fall down (from a height) (lit. and met.) (Śiv. 967, 1778, wȧsⁱ). Cf. wasun and wȧstⁱ.
(i.e. wāṭ), a seam (W. 114), see wāṭh 1. In W. 115, wāt, a seam, is a mistake for wāṭh 2, q.v.
a jingle of bata, in bata-wata, p. 137b, l. 15, q.v.

m. a stain, stigma, disrepute (causing general censure, expulsion from society, or the like). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to put a stigma (on a person or thing), to give a bad name (to). --lagun -- m.inf. a stigma to attach to a person or thing, (of a person) to get a bad character, (of a thing or action) to become considered useless or vile.

adj. c.g. in full original form (i.e. not divided up or incomplete) (e.g. a rupee which has not been changed into its equivalent in coins of smaller value). --korᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --kürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), merged into one whole, as in the next. --karun -- m.inf. to combine, merge, a number of parts into one whole (e.g. to exchange a number of small coins for one coin corresponding to their total value, such as giving 16 annas for a rupee, or 12 pence for a shilling). -pūnʦhuwᵘ m. N. of a certain copper coin, of the value of a quarter pice, see pūnʦhuwᵘ. ¶ wȧṭⁱ-waṭa adj. c.g. full, complete (genl. with reference to a silver or gold coin).
adj. c.g. possessing joins; hence (of something once broken or torn) pieced together, repaired, mended.
(? spelling and gender), the first of the four khushābas or weedings by hand of a rice field, i.q. arīʦar, kachh-nĕnd, and pangrai, qq.v. (L. 463, cf. 327).
f. in wāvüñᵘ̈ wātal, etc., q.v. s.v. wāv 1.
adj. c.g. possessing joins, mended, repaired (e.g. a metal or wooden article, or an article of clothing).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. waṭaladiñ), stained in repute, in disrepute. Cf. waṭa 1.
f. the conduct of a Wātul, or scavenger; conduct like that (marked by evil habits, abusive language, plaguing, disregard for life, general impurity, and so on).

f. (sg. dat. watüñᵘ̈), a small circular, or wheel-shaped, piece of leather, wood, or metal, used for fastening the chain of a bolt or the like; cf. watüñᵘ̈. watᵃñĕ-gurᵃ m. 'a wheel-horse', a little carriage on wheels for a baby, a perambulator.
n.ag. (f. wātanāwavüñᵘ̈), one who causes to arrive, etc. (as under wātun, q.v.); one who conveys, delivers, a conveyer (El.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wātanôwᵘ), to cause to arrive (K. 338, 1150), to bring, etc. [Causal of wātun, q.v. in all its meanings (cf. tödī wᵒ, p. 964a, l. 36) (El.; Śiv. 1004, 1090, 1656, 1756, 1880; Rām. 21, 129, 409, 416, 626, 705, 899, 1449, 1478, 1666, 1707; K. 469; H. viii, 9; YZ. 158)]; to convey, to deliver (El.; Gr.M.; Rām. 680, 1676, 1691; H. iii, 9); to conduct (a person to a certain place) (K. 401, 1164; H. v, 9, 10; YZ. 38, 249, 251, 434). wātanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wātanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to arrive, brought, etc., as ab.
m. N. of a certain flower (Rām. 647, 1008, 1092).

adj. c.g. (cf. waṭh 1) in waṭȧsⁱ gōmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), turned to stone (of some human being, or the like, so turned by a curse, or the like). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to be turned to stone, as ab.; met. to be overwhelmed with unbearable grief. --karun -- m.inf. to turn (so-and-so) to stone, as ab.; (met.) to cause (a person) to be overwhelmed with misery by a curse.

m. (sg. dat. waṭatas), earnings, gain, amassed profits (resulting from any work on which one is engaged) (Gr.Gr. 128); cf. waṭun and waṭiñ. --anun -- m.inf. to collect together (parts into a whole), to piece together. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to become pieced together (as ab.).

f. in wātawan karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to finish, or accomplish something anyhow (e.g. in fitting together the parts of a whole, to fix the parts wrongly, or, in distributing gifts, doing it hurriedly and incompletely).

n.ag. (f. wātavüñᵘ̈), one who arrives, one who has been (in such-and-such a place) (Rām. 1255); one who acts with discrimination and thorough knowledge; (as adv.) immediately on arrival (K. 394, 523; H. xii, 15, with emph. y, wātawunuy; so YZ. 32).

m. (sg. dat. wã̄ṭas), the belly, stomach (cf. ā̃ṭa-wᵒ, p. 69a, l. 38) (K.Pr. 218). ¶ wã̄ṭa-buḍay f. (immediately on seeing something) violent longing, impetuous hankering (for it, so that one is even ready to take it by force). --phērun -- m.inf. to experience pleasure in giving or leaving (esp. something of great value or much loved) to another.

f. (sg. dat. wati, Gr.Gr. 70), a road, way, track, path (cf. ajĕ wati, p. 13b, ll. 38 ff.; ala-wᵒ, p. 23a, l. 37; ȧndⁱ- wati, etc., p. 31b, ll. 34 ff.; bölⁱ-wⁱ, p. 104a, l. 26; drustĕ wati, p. 249a, l. 26; kŏ-wᵒ, p. 496b, l. 9; maharājī wᵒ, p. 556a, l. 49; nörⁱ-wⁱ, p. 649b, l. 21; nina-wᵒ, p. 672b, l. 43; pā̃-wᵒ, p. 748a, l. 35; potᵘ wᵒ, p. 788b, l. 28; rāza-wᵒ, p. 857b, l. 10; sangar-wᵒ, p. 921a, l. 44; sŏñⁱ-wⁱ, p. 924b, l. 48; sŏ-wᵒ, p. 955a, l. 36; wȧnⁱ-wⁱ, p. 1121b, l. 3) (El. wat, wath; Gr.Gr. 66, 70; Gr.M.; L. 463; L.V. 41, 98; Śiv. 371, 535, 1067, 1247, 1253, 1312, 1450, 1626, 1824, 1861, 1895; Rām. 30, 48, 140, 181, 244, 337, 403, 1171, 1598 (voc.); K. 112, 195, 425, 1010-1, 1124; H. ii, 2; v, 7; vii, 17; x, 1; xii, 14, 15; YZ. 38, 279, 418; K.Pr. 1, 87, 91, 132, 232); route, course, way by which one travels (cf. nāvi-wᵒ, p. 667a, l. 19) (Śiv. 1700, 1805; K. 75, 431, 1120, 1161-3; H. ii, 1; x, 4; K.Pr. 26); (met.) a way, manner of life, method, habit (cf. hūnⁱ-wⁱ brörⁱ-wⁱ, p. 337a, l. 31; prāñĕ wati pakun, p. 762a, l. 7; pata-wᵒ, p. 793b, ll. 3 ff.; sĕzi wati pakun, p. 956b, l. 14; wār wath gaʦhun, p. 1134b, l. 21; wāra wati, p. 1135a, l. 25) (El. method, K.Pr. 77); a way, manner, means, cause (cf. nina-wᵒ, p. 672b, l. 45; sāsi-wati, p. 941a, l. 44; dŏyĕ wati, s.v. zᵃh); teaching, instruction (which shows how to acquire some knowledge or carry out some act) (cf. ath-wath, p. 67b, l. 16) (Śiv. 16, 538). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give a path, to make way (for a person), to allow to pass (K. 70); to give means (for accomplishing something) (K. 579). --hë̆ñᵘ̈-- f.inf. to take the road, set forth, depart (Rām. 680, 1598). --hāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show the way, point out the right course, to conduct, guide (lit. and fig.) (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 109, 236, 518, 623, 1625, 1759, 1885; Rām. 178, 989; K. 578; H. v, 9; K.Pr. 14, 165); (of one who has gone wrong) to direct (him) along the right way (lit. and fig.). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to make a way', to search for, and find, help for the successful accomplishment of any work. -pĕṭh dyunᵘ m.inf. 'to put upon the way', to dedicate, or devote, to public use (e.g. a private garden, tank, hospice, or the like). -pĕṭh ṭôkᵘ trāwun m.inf. (of a respectable person) to solicit like a mean beggar (quasi, like a sorry mendicant seated at a cross-roads with a bowl before him, proclaiming his destitution, and accepting the most trivial charity). -pĕṭh yōñĕʦhunun m.inf. (amongst Brāhmaṇs) a fictitious investiture of the sacred thread, performed in some public place such as the bank of a river, or a place where four ways meet.
