It is performed when a Brāhmaṇ has died, and when his heir has not yet been so invested, in order to enable the latter to perform the funeral rites. --rāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a road to be lost; the way to be missed (Rām. 1222); to become hostile to proper knowledge, morality, conduct, or discrimination, and attach oneself to the opposite, to become immoral, etc., be led astray (Śiv. 553); cf. wati-rāwun, bel. --rāwarüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause a way to be lost, to cause (a person, dat.) to lose (his) way (Śiv. 1625; Rām. 1362, 1616 (rāwarāvüñᵘ̈), 1620 (id.); K.Pr. 226); to seduce into evil practices, mislead, as ab. --ʦaṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cut, or break, a road; to break faith (with a creditor, an ally, and so on). --wuchüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to inspect a road; before beginning any work, to consider carefully its nature, propriety, results, etc. (Rām. 95, 1000); to watch the way, expect, wait for (a person) (Gr.M.; K. 643, 647, 1001, 1005; YZ. 253 (pl.)); to watch (a person's) way, to follow (his) footsteps (Rām. 1486). --wuchith pūrᵘ trāwun -- m.inf. 'to advance the foot after (first) inspecting the road', not to undertake a work without previous consideration, as ab. -walad f. (sg. dat. -walüzᵘ̈), 'road-companionship', (in the carrying out of a work) a large number of friendly helpers. -vüñᵘ̈ f. 'a road-grove', (in any work) a crowd of friends and relations, etc., to help; cf. wata-vᵒ, bel. -vüñᵘ̈ karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to seek for a full supply of helpers for the successful completion of a work. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a way to come, an opportunity to turn up, a method to present itself (Rām. 838, K. 242). ¶ wata-gām or -gômᵘ m. a roadside village (esp. when existing only at rare intervals on a long lonely road). -gömⁱ m. an inhabitant of such a village. -gotᵘ m. one who goes along a road, a wayfarer; one who travels, proceeds along (some route) (L.V. 57). -gath m. (sg. dat. -gatas), one who travels on a road, a wayfarer (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1485, 1829); a passenger (on a ship) (Gr.M.). -hāwukh m. (f. -hāvücᵘ̈), one who shows a road, a guide, a guide-post, any action or quality that guides (lit. and fig.) (El., Gr.M., YZ. 432). -kharc m. road-expense, the cost of a journey; money for a journey, provision (of funds) for a journey (Gr.M.). -kŏl f. a stream or canal of running water met on a road (esp. in a forest or wild). -kulᵘ m. a shady tree, or tree with fruit (met on a desolate and usually treeless road). -kāman f. (sg. dat. -kāmüñᵘ̈), 'scarcity of road', inability to go to some place or house (owing to fear, anxiety, or some obstacle). -kônᵘ subst. m. and adj. (f. -köñᵘ̈), 'one who is one-eyed on the road', i.e. who breaks the rules of good conduct (by misappropriating a deposit or the like), one who leads others astray (from virtue, etc.) (cf. K.Pr. 1); a bad or winding road, a road that is not straight (K.Pr. 1). -kāñĕr m. misappropriation of a loan or deposit, as ab.; leading others astray, as ab.; -krim (? spelling) m. a certain sweet pot-herb, Lychnis sp. (L. 72, cf. krim). -kôs m. distortion of a road, crookedness of a road; crookedness of conduct, etc. -lürᵘ̈ f. a road-house, an inn, a traveller's rest-house on a long road, a caravanserai, a tent at a stage on a road (El. vatalur, watalar). -nôshᵘ m. a road-destroyer, a highway robber (L.V. 43). -pūrᵘ m. a footpath; a narrow path in the hills or cut through the snow, passable by only one person at a time; cf. wati-pᵒ, bel. -pūrᵘ kaḍun m.inf. (of one recovering from illness) to begin to attempt to walk, (of a baby) to begin to toddle. -pö̃than m. a traveller on the road, one who is travelling on a long journey (esp. when he is doing so against his will or under some necessity). -rôchᵘ m. a road guardian, a road watchman; anything which would help on a journey (such as money, food, dress, house), viaticum, travelling money, etc. -sāmāna, m. travelling expenses (El.). -söthⁱ m. a road companion, a fellow-traveller. -törᵘ̈ f. delay on the road. -vüñᵘ̈ f. a grove by a long dreary road (esp. one planted as a pious act for the use of the general public); cf. wath-vᵒ, ab. -yār m. a road-friend, a friend made in the course of a journey. -yārᵘ̈zᵘ̈ f. such friendship; friendship caused by travelling on similar occupations. ¶ watā-wath f. (sg. dat. -wati), having something (which one should do himself) done by another. ¶ wati āsun m.inf. to be, or become, a helper, to be of assistance, to show favour to another's efforts, to take his side. --karun -- m.inf. to make (some powerful person) show favour to oneself (in case of a dispute, quarrel, or some unpopular act or business), to bring a person over to one's own side. -kọ̆ʦhᵘ  m. a bribe to bring a person over to one's own side, a bribe (to a judge) to gain a favourable decision. --lagun -- m.inf. to get on the (right) way, to become confirmed in a worthy course (of conduct, courtesy, zeal in learning, or the like); (of a thing, quality, or action) to become established in a good condition. --lāgun -- m.inf. to confirm, or establish, a person, thing, etc., as in the preceding. --nērun -- m.inf. to emerge on (or from) a road, to approach, come near (Rām. 1143k). --pakun -- m.inf. to go along a road (Śiv. 1654; Rām. 42; K.Pr. 99, 232); to live a well-conducted life (in peace, contentment, affection, and the due carrying out of religious duties). -pūrᵘ m. a footpath; one who leads a well-conducted life; cf. wata-pᵒ, ab. -pĕṭh anun m.inf. to bring on to the (right) way, start (a person) in the right direction (Śiv. 154). -pĕṭh bĕhun m.inf. to sit (as a beggar) on the road, to be plunged into sorrow by the loss of one's entire possessions. -pĕṭh bāna-khörᵘ̈ phuṭarüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to reveal one's own, or another's private character, or affairs, or secret (cf. bāna-khörᵘ̈ phuṭarüñᵘ̈, p. 109b, l. 39). -pĕṭh thawun m.inf. to dedicate property for the free use and enjoyment of the public. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), impassable (El.). -rôwᵘ adj. (f. -rövᵘ̈), one who has lost his way, one who has deviated from the right road (lit. and fig. of morals, etc.). -rāwul m. (f. -rāvüjᵘ̈), one who causes another to lose his way, one who, or that which, misleads (lit. and fig., as ab.). --rôwᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --rövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), one who has lost his way, been misled (lit. and fig., as ab.). --rāwun -- m.inf. to lose one's way (lit. and fig. of morals, etc.); cf. wath rāvüñᵘ̈, ab. -rāwurᵘ m. (f. -rāvürᵘ̈), one who leads others on to the wrong way, one who misleads (lit. and fig., as ab.). --rāwarun -- m.inf. to mislead (El.). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain firm and persistent in helping or showing favour to another. --thawun -- m.inf. (before beginning a dispute, some unpopular work, etc.) to bring over an influential person to one's own side. -ʦolᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüjᵘ̈), one who, while en route with a number of companions or caravan, absconds from the company; one who has abandoned the rules of good conduct or education, and has taken to a disreputable life. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who has powerful help (in accomplishing some object); a powerful person who takes side with another and helps him. --wati -- adv. along the proper road, in the right manner (the whole time), carefully and thoroughly (K.Pr. 232); along the whole way, continually as one goes along (Rām. 1766). -wôtᵘ adj. (f. -wöʦᵘ̈), one who has traversed the road and reached the end, one who has completed a journey; met. one who has gone through the whole course, one who has mastered all the rules (of good conduct, of some branch of learning, or the like). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come by, or along, a road (K.Pr. 18); to come on the way, to occur during a journey (K. 74, 729); to come on to the right way, to become a reformed character, (of a thing, work, or the like) to become in prosperous condition.

m. (sg. dat. waṭas), a stone (globular and smooth, such as is found in a river-bed), a large pebble, a boulder, rock (cf. khāra-wᵒ, p. 408a, l. 2; kāji-wᵒ, p. 430a, l. 31; kañi-wᵒ, p. 461b, l. 44; kwöji-wᵒ, p. 495b, l. 38; nal-wᵒ, p. 632a, l. 6; nīla-wᵒ, p. 634a, l. 29; phāla-wᵒ, p. 693a, l. 22) (L.V. 17, K.Pr. 190); met. any smooth globular object, like such a stone (cf. khŏna-wᵒ, p. 402a, l. 43). Cf. vüṭᵘ̈ 3. ¶ waṭa-gŏgul m. 'a sphere-turnip'; hence, some object globular in shape (esp. used with regard to the stone, etc., on a ring); hence, met. something thick, bulky, stout. --khorᵘ -- m. the circular leaf (or a collection of leaves) of a certain aquatic plant (used as a food for horses). -khūrᵘ̈ f. N. of a certain disease in the heel, caused by a blow or the like, and involving painful internal gatherings difficult to cure; cf. khūrᵘ̈ 1. -khürᵘ̈ f. a certain medicinal creeping plant with long delicate leaves, and growing in the ground at the foot of the hills. -kram f. N. of a certain wild vegetable with long, thick, and closely packed leaves. -rᵃkh [] f. (sg. dat. -rᵃkhi), a line or mark deeply and permanently engraved or marked on a rock; met. anything (such as a condition, promise, or the like) which is fixed, irrevocable, absolutely unchangeable. --thawun -- m.inf. to keep secret, hold one's tongue about, not to mention (something heard, known, secretly imparted, or the like). --thowᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --thüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), kept secret, or private, as ab. -tövⁱ adj. c.g. (of chick pease or the like) only half-parched, parched only on one side, badly roasted (and hence hard as gravel). -tövⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to be badly cooked, as ab.

m. (sg. dat. wāṭas), union, uniting, the act of joining up two separate things, tying up together, piecing together (cf. atha-wᵒ, p. 64b, l. 44; banga-dĕli-wᵒ, p. 112b, l. 49; ganḍa-wᵒ, p. 289b, l. 22; hanga-wᵒ, p. 339a, l. 2; hōnza-wᵒ, p. 341a, l. 20; lara-wᵒ, p. 529a, l. 42; nakha-wᵒ, p. 629a, l. 4; phöda-wᵒ, p. 685a, l. 23; phĕkⁱ-wⁱ, p. 721a, l. 6; pakhᵃca-wᵃ, p. 726a, l. 38; pȧnⁱ-wⁱ, p. 737b, l. 32; rĕla-wᵒ, p. 832b, l. 41) (Gr.Gr. 123); a joining or joint (of limbs) (cf. banda-wᵒ, p. 111a, l. 28); joining together, construction; hence, the material of which a thing is constructed (L.V. 17); a seam (W. 114, wāt); repairing (by joining broken pieces, uniting broken limbs, causing the edges of a wound to unite by a surgical operation, and so on) (cf. dīri-wᵒ, p. 271a, l. 28; ʦaṭh-wᵒ (m.), ʦaṭa-wᵒ (f.), p. 1085b, ll. 39, 45); the union, or forming the union, of personal friendship or relationship with another. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to repair (by joining up broken pieces or the like). --karun -- m.inf., id. (H. x, 12). --sapadun -- m.inf. to cling (El., W. 88). ¶ wāṭa-pūrᵘ m. a certain method of walking (in which the toe of the hinder foot is placed against the heel of the foot in front,-- foot throughout touching foot, as is done in measuring land). -wāṭh f. (sg. dat. -wāṭi), intimate union, close joining up, mutual exact fitting together. ¶ wāṭukᵘ 1 adj. gen. (f. wāṭücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, close union of two or more things or persons.
adv. (borrowed from Skt. vat, and used as a suffix) like, as in mastāna-wath, like one who is drunk (Śiv. 1450).
m. the extreme, unbearable, heat experienced in the summer at midday.

m. (sg. dat. wāṭas), a lumpy kind of porridge of coarsely broken grain (such as maize, barley, etc.) (cf. kạnᵃka-wᵃ, p. 457b, l. 40; makāyi-wᵒ, p. 563b, l. 14; pingi-wᵒ, p. 740a, l. 25; shölⁱ-wⁱ, p. 880b, l. 38; wushki-wᵒ, p. 1147a, l. 12) (W. 115, wāt, mistranslated 'seam'). ¶ wāṭa-koshᵘ m. the bran of pounded maize (as sifted from the broken grain). -lŏkhᵃr or -lŏkhürᵘ̈ f. a large coagulated lump of the material of this porridge, when cold and stale. -mujᵘ̈ f. a certain kind of radish, small and pungent (El. wáṭamúj). -pholᵘ m. 'a grain in porridge', a hidden hoard (hitherto unknown and now discovered), treasure trove. -ṭīrᵘ̈ f. a large coagulated lump of the material of this porridge when cold and stale. ¶ wāṭukᵘ 2 adj. gen. (f. wāṭücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, such porridge (e.g. a particular grain suitable for making it, or a dish for holding it).

in waṭha-wadal f. distress, fever, or the like caused to a respectable person by abuse publicly directed at him; cf. waṭhal 1. -wadal gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. such distress or fever to be experienced. -wadal karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to cause such distress, etc., by offering such abuse.
f. disrespect (shown to another by abusing him before respectable people); cf. waṭha. --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such disrespect to happen, i.e. to be shown (to a person).
f. secret collection (of money, goods, results of work, or the like), secret hoarding. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. secretly to hoard, secretly to pile up one's earnings or the like.
m. or f. the act or condition of spreading, becoming diffused, in wuna-wathar, f., p. 1122a, l.47, and wö̃ʦha-wᵒ, m., s.v. wö̃ʦh 1, q.v. Cf. watharun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. watharôwᵘ), i.q. watharun, q.v. (El., Gr.M.) (El. also has watharawun, to spread (a carpet)) (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 57, 1850; Rām. 1783; YZ. 343).

m. a level piece of ground, a field, i.q. pathur, q.v., and (like wạthᵃr, q.v.) used only --˚ (cf. baḍ-watharū, p. 81b, l. 48; lar-watharū, p. 529b, l. 41); a field in which rice is sown broadcast (L. 331, watrú, 463, wattru).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wathorᵘ), to spread out (a carpet, mat, or the like, on the ground), lay out flat (Śiv. 500, 1468; Rām. 1495; H. xii, 18, 21; YZ. 235); to throw (a person) flat and spread out on the ground (for execution). wathorᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wathürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), spread out, as ab. (Rām. 569, 579).

m. a mat, rug, or the like spread out (for sleeping on or for sitting on), a bed (Gr.M.; L. 458, wathran; K. 925; H. xii, 24); a carpet (El.). ¶ watharȧnⁱ-palav m. a rug (used like a mattress) spread (on a bed for being lain upon. Usually some old worn-out garment). ¶ watharani pyōmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --pyēmüʦᵘ̈ --), filled with agitation, as in the following. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to become extremely agitated (by fear, disease, loss, anxiety, or the like, to such a degree that the person affected is not able even to stand up).

m. destruction or ruin (of a house or other place of refuge, e.g. by decay, or by being pulled down and the materials being scattered) (Śiv. 120); met. destruction of any refuge or means of help. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such destruction or decay to occur.

f. destruction or ruin of anything animate or inanimate (by decay or violent removal from its site, and the constituents being scattered in different directions) (Śiv. 5); the causing of such destruction or ruin.

m. great fatigue, weariness, distress (from excessive labour, journeying, or the like). Cf. wutra. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such fatigue to be experienced; to become exhausted by exposure to extreme heat, a rainstorm, or the like; to experience mental distress (from being abused, from grief, or similar cause).

m. (sg. dat. wạtᵃras). (This word is the form taken by pạthᵃr 1, when it is the second member of a compound. It therefore occurs only --˚) a leaf (cf. ala-wᵒ, p. 22b, l. 44; bōñĕ-wᵒ, p. 115b, l. 31; dachĕ-wᵒ, p. 186a, l. 16; datᵃ̇rᵃ̇-wᵃ̇, p. 259a, l. 23; gula-wᵒ, p. 284a, l. 1; hāka-wᵒ, p. 326b, l. 46; kā̃bayĕ-wᵒ, p. 382b, l. 50; khēla-wᵒ, p. 397b, l. 23; khȧrⁱ-wⁱ, p. 410b, l. 49; muji-wᵒ, p. 558b, l. 30; pampōshĕ-wᵒ, p. 734a, l. 28; pana-wᵒ, p. 735a, l. 23; pōshĕ-wᵒ, p. 779a, l. 47; tamökⁱ-wⁱ, p. 1006b, l. 12; ʦᵃnȧnᵃ-wᵃ, p. 1075a, l. 26; ʦū̃ṭhⁱ-wⁱ, p. 1087a, l. 21) (El. wȧthar, wathir; Gr.Gr. 51; Śiv. 1802); any leaf-like object (cf. pilⁱ-pilⁱ-wⁱ, p. 814b, l. 2). Cf. wạtᵃr 2. ¶ wạtᵃra-horᵃ m. a pair of certain leaf-like ear-ornaments. -kan m. a single one of a pair of these ornaments.
m. the condition of being without a screen, or of being exposed (either above or all round) (e.g. of a house, a courtyard, or a garden).
adj. c.g. (of a house, meeting place, courtyard, garden, or the like, or of a dish, vessel, etc.) without a screen, exposed (either above or all round), uncovered, unfenced.
f. N. of a certain hard wood found in the forests (L. 79, 82, wutil, (?) Rhus Wallichii). According to L. 82, it is used for making spoons and combs, and the tree has a red berry. Cf. waṭyulᵘ.
f. earning only for oneself (and not for the benefit of others), saving up one's earnings (Gr.Gr. 120). Cf. waṭun and waṭath.

m. a way, path, track; fashion, mode, custom, habit; disposition, conduct, behaviour; (in Ksh.) careful conduct, circumspection, caution, forethought. --bĕhun -- m.inf. to settle oneself in a favourable position (for carrying out some laudable purpose in a satisfactory way). --rōzun -- m.inf. (of someone or something previously not in a satisfactory condition) to be settled in a favourable condition. --thawun -- m.inf. to put in order in a favourable condition.
adj. c.g. affectionate towards, fondly loving, kind or compassionate towards (Śiv. 1036, 1204, 1535, 1673, 1675, 1740; K. 400, 1102).
m. N. of a demon, who, disguised as a calf, attempted to kill Krushn (Kṛṣṇa), but was killed by him (in Skt. vatsâsura) (K. 186).
in waṭuka börav (or bhairav)  m. N. of a certain Börav (Bhairava) (see p. 129b, l. 44), a partial form of Śiva, said to have been born as a mental son of Pārvatī (Śiv. 1552). Cf. waṭukh.

m. (sg. dat. waṭakas), N. of a certain wide-mouthed bowl set up during the five days of the festival of the Śivarātri, beginning with the 12th lunar day of the dark half of the month of Phāgun (February-March), for the worship of Waṭuka Börav (see ab.); meton. a general term for all the vessels accompanying this bowl, and used in this worship. Cf. waṭuka. ¶ waṭạka-pūz f. the performance of the worship on this festival; the body of rules laid down for this worship. ¶ waṭakh-ḍulᵘ m. a bowl used in this worship. It is employed to contain the various oblations made each day to Waṭuka Börav. -ḍulijᵘ̈ f. id., but smaller in size. -ḍūnᵘ m. a walnut used in this worship; the whole supply of these walnuts. A number of walnuts are put as offerings into the above bowl, and after the conclusion of the ceremony these are distributed mutually, one to another, by the assembled relations and friends, in order to secure successful results from the worship. -nörᵘ̈ f. a small bowl used at this worship, in which oblations of water and fruit, etc., are deposited. It is also called Rāma-goḍᵘ, q.v., p. 833b, l. 8. -noṭᵘ  m. i.q., -ḍulᵘ, ab. -pröpyunᵘ m. the oblations of food offered at this worship. They are consumed by the officiating priest and his assistants. -pūzā f. i.q., waṭạka-pūz, ab. -rāza m. the god Waṭuka Börav worshipped at this ceremony; the collection of apparatus used in this worship. -wôñᵘ m. the water remaining over from the offerings at this worship.

m. (sg. dat. wāṭakas), he who, or that which, joins together, a man who joins up broken articles, a professional mender, or one skilled in mending, a repairer; a process that unites together things broken (cf. anga-wᵒ, p. 33b, l. 2); one who brings together persons (e.g. a married couple or two friends) who have quarrelled, a reconciler.

m. (sg. dat. wātalas; f. wātᵘ̈jᵘ̈, H. xi, 14-5), a man of the lowest and most degraded caste in Kashmīr, a sweeper, a Mihtar, a scavenger, leather-worker (cf. hāra- wātᵘ̈jᵘ̈, a kind of bird, p. 344b, l. 14; māra-wātul, p. 587b, ll. 12 ff.; pöshⁱ-wⁱ, p. 780a, l. 1; shupⁱ-wⁱ, p. 887b, l. 34) (Gr.Gr. 36, 58; Gr.M.; L. 418; W. 17; H. xi, 14-5; K.Pr. 9, 231-2); met. one who acts like one of this degraded caste, a filthy fellow (cf. lĕka-wᵒ, p. 518a, l. 44). ¶ wātal-bāpār m. the natural condition of a Wātul; hence, foulness, filthiness (e.g. of a kitchen or its utensils, of garments or ornaments, of the body internally or externally). -mahāsas m. porridge of butter and beans (p. 553a, l. 13) (a dainty) for a Wātul; hence, incompatibility (e.g. fine ornaments on a dirty limb, or on the wrong and inappropriate limb). -phukh f. (sg. dat. -phuki), a kind of plate or tray, on which a Wātul who works as a shoe-cobbler keeps his tools. -wān m. a place where Wātuls and other foul and polluting people congregate or herd together. -wāza m. a cook of this caste, a low-caste cook who deals only with foul food (cf. hūnⁱ-māzas wātal-wāza, p. 337a, l. 5) (K.Pr. 84).
m. in burza-wᵒ, a large thin sheet of birch-bark (p. 131a, l. 9), and phã-wᵒ, a square sheet of cotton wool (p. 698a, l. 17), qq.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. woṭᵘ 3 (for 1, 2, see s.vv.); f. vüṭᵘ̈ or wüṭᵘ̈ 4 (for 1, 2, 3, see s.vv.); f.pl. wacĕ; 2 p.p. wacyōv), to bring together (a number of things), to collect (things scattered), to assemble (tr.) (Gr.Gr. 120, 128); to close up (something open, e.g. the eye, the mouth, or the hand) (cf. atha wᵒ, p. 65a, l. 3) (Śiv. 168; Rām. 522-3, 1266-7, 1509); to join up, unite (L.V. 80); to fold up, or roll up (something spread out) (cf. dāman wᵒ, p. 219b, l. 44; lonḍᵘ wᵒ, p. 525b, l. 43; wagowᵘ wᵒ, p. 1103a, l. 22) (Gr.Gr. 5, 10; Śiv. 1301-3, 1308, 1568); to wind up into a ball (cf. ḍyū̃gᵘ wᵒ, p. 267b, l. 4); to collect another person's property and appropriate it (e.g. in sharing out to get hold of other persons' shares as well as one's own). woṭᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wüṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, pl. wacĕ-maʦa), brought together, etc., as ab.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. wôtᵘ, f. wöʦᵘ̈ (Rām. 147); 2 p.p. wāʦōv), to arrive (at, dat. or dat. with pĕṭh), to reach the end of a journey (cf. and wᵒ, p. 31b, l. 15; bīgis-pĕṭh wᵒ, p. 91a, l. 23; bakām wᵒ, p. 102a, l. 15; manzilas wᵒ, p. 584b, l. 31; pānas wᵒ, p. 736a, l. 48; pata wᵒ, p. 793b, l. 8; pĕtis-pĕṭh wᵒ, p. 818a, l. 50; shĕchⁱ wātüñᵘ̈, p. 870b, l. 1) (El.; Gr.Gr. 204, 208; Gr.M.; L.V. 51, 60, 82; Śiv. 65, 85, 279, 328, 631, 675, 781, 783, 930, 973, 1029, 1101, 1131, 1163, 1173, 1176-7, 1233, 1505, 1550, 1772, 1909; Rām. 121, 147, 284, 436, 471, 522, 531, 542, 575, 586, 652, 779, 836, 854, 887, 1072, 1100, 1198, 1330, 1412, 1542, 1565, 1648, 1688, 1699; K. 2, 17, 53, 76-7, 79, 94, 100, 213, 234, 256, 337, 376, 394, 396, 398, et passim; H. ii, 8; iii, 1-4, 7, 9, et passim, as in Vocab.; YZ. 30, 33, 39, 112, 126, 391; K.Pr. 111, 178, 260); to arrive at, find (something sought for) (cf. nēbas wᵒ, p. 619b, l. 38) (Śiv. 1877, K. 599, YZ. 525); to arrive at, reach, be able to reach up to (some condition) (cf. aṭāṭayis wᵒ, p. 69a, l. 32; pulan wᵒ, p. 730b, l. 31; sŏkhas wᵒ, p. 905b, l. 40; ṭōṭam-nayĕ wᵒ, p. 1044a, l. 23) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 42, 214, 986; Rām. 1281, 1666, 1748, 1750; K. 395, 597, 656, 1120, 1140; YZ. 190, 228); ¶ to arrive at (a person, dat.), get at (him), circumvent (him) (H. xii, 13); to arrive at (some condition), be at the point of (e.g. death) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1631); to come into the possession (of), be obtained (K. 625, 646, 705, 730, 742, 777, 1146); ¶ (of time) (a certain moment of time) to arrive (cf. samay wᵒ, p. 915b, l. 38; wāda wᵒ, p. 1096a, l. 42) (Śiv. 511, 1081; K. 8, 46, 68, 238, 242, 355, 607, 626, 690, 799, 847, 1169); (of time) to come and pass on, to elapse (cf. kāl wᵒ, p. 434a, l. 16) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 110; Rām. 896; K. 489, 704, 1111); to come (to a person), happen (e.g. harm, good luck, etc.) (Gr.M.; L.V. 60; Rām. 128, 881, 1299; K. 50, 86-7, 362, 536, 684, 711, 841); ¶ to be proper, be suitable [in fut. with pres. sense, wātakh, thou art suitable (Rām. 849), wāti, it is proper; and in past cond. with sense of past ind., wātahö, I was suitable (Rām. 1185)] (Śiv. 318; Rām. 241, 647, 708, 735, 849, 1185, 1237-8, 1576; H. viii, 3, 6, 8, 11); relationship or connexion to exist (with, dat.) (fut. used in pres. sense, etc., as ab.) (Rām. 528, 681; K.Pr. 178); ¶ to fit, go into, not to be excessive but to be just enough to fill (of the quantity necessary to fill a vessel of limited size), to extend over a certain space (Gr.M.; K. 111, 478); to pervade, permeate, be diffused through (Śiv. 368, 515, 626, 641, 1225, 1567; Rām. 1617; K. 777, 862); ¶ (of food being cooked) to be cooked and ready, to be completely cooked, to be ready for serving; ¶ thoroughly to acquire the understanding of a difficult subject, to acquire the mastery of such (cf. panan wᵒ, p. 734b, l. 14) (Śiv. 46, 743, 821, 937, 1332, 1486; K. 35, 607); to have the power of discrimination (cf. swādas wᵒ, p. 953b, l. 9). ¶ wôtᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wöʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), one who has arrived, etc., as ab. (K. 339, 356, 593, 645). ¶ wātan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who arrives, an arrival; one who arrives without delay, one who has made no delay on the road, one who will arrive very soon, one who is expected immediately; one who acts with discrimination and thorough knowledge. ¶ wötith āsun m.inf. to become a thorough master (of some difficult subject). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to arrive all of a sudden, to arrive there and then (K. 446, 648, 805, 832, 870). --rōzun -- m.inf. to arrive and settle down (somewhere); to have previously mastered (some difficult subject).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wôṭᵘ; f. wöṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. wācĕ; 2 p.p. wācyōv), to join, unite, fasten permanently together, to fix together (cf. pholᵘ wᵒ, p. 694a, l. 46) (Gr.Gr. 123; Gr.M.; L. 461, wútun); to join, unite (things broken), to mend, repair (K.Pr. 80); to join broken limbs, act as a bone-setter; met. to unite (persons who are separated by a quarrel), to bring together, reconcile; to make (something) ready for action (e.g. drawing a bow) (Rām. 1428). ¶ wôṭᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wöṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), joined, repaired, etc., as ab. ¶ wāṭan-gorᵘ m. (f. -gürᵘ̈), a professional joiner, repairer, mender, bone-setter, etc., as ab. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), id.
f. a small circular piece of leather, wood, or metal, with a hole in the centre, used as a toy. Cf. watan 2.
f. of wāṭun, q.v., also occurring in āṭüñᵘ̈-wāṭüñᵘ̈, p. 68a, l. 46, q.v.
m. a kind of wooden box or casket, partitioned inside and with a movable cover.
or woturᵘ 1 m. casting, flinging, hurling (i.q. wotᵘ 1, q.v.), used --˚, as in data-wᵒ, p. 257b, l. 7; lȧlⁱ-wⁱ, p. 523a, l. 29; pāma-wᵒ, p. 733b, l. 9.

or woturᵘ 2 m. a leaf (of paper, or the like, a slip (of paper), a document, memorandum (i.q. pạthᵃr 1, q.v.), used --˚, as in dārath-wᵒ, p. 249b, l. 43; ganĕth-wᵒ, p. 293a, l. 48; mal-wᵒ, p. 564a, l. 44; pīri-wᵒ, p. 753a, l. 31; pashṭa-wᵒ, p. 783a, l. 14; patha-wᵒ, p. 791b, l. 14; ʦĕtas-wᵒ, p. 1089b, l. 8.
m. (sg. dat. wȧṭilis), a certain tree with a hard wood found in the forests; (when felled) its wood. Cf. waṭil 1.
or wạtᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 1 or wütᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 1 f. of waturᵘ 1, flinging, hurling, used --˚, as in dȧdⁱ-wⁱ, p. 191a, l. 13; lȧlⁱ-wⁱ, p. 523a, l. 31.
or wạtᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 2 or wütᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 2 f. of waturᵘ 2, a leaf (of paper), a memorandum, used --˚, as in atha-wᵒ, p. 65a, l. 6. Cf. wạthᵃr.
or wạtᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 3 f. in ạgᵃna-wạtᵃr, p. 16b, l. 48, a general name for all the articles offered in oblation at a fire-sacrifice.
f. in the following:-- wạtᵃri-nūn m. (in food) an intolerably excessive flavour of salt, brininess; met. tormenting and unbearable distress (due to the loss of something loved or desired).
adj. (f. wȧṭⁱlivⁱ), made of waṭil-wood, see waṭil 1.

or (q.v.) vĕv 2 f. the mass of eggs, or roe, of a fish. ¶ wavi-göḍᵘ̈ f. a certain kind of fish, which is said always to have a roe inside it. -gurun m. N. of another kind of fish, small in size and found in forest streams. Even the males, as well as the females, are said always to contain roes. It is said to have a very delicate flavour. Cf. gurun 1.

m. a current of air, wind (cf. brō̃ṭha-wᵒ, p. 128a, l. 46; buthi-wᵒ, p. 143b, l. 19; pakha-wᵒ, p. 725a, ll. 39, 47; vijĕ-wᵒ, p. 1106b, l. 40; wŏpal-gŏndi-wᵒ, p. 1131b, l. 49; vĕtha-wᵒ, p. 1158a, l. 33) (El. wáo; Gr.Gr. 162; Gr.M.; L. 465, wawa; W. 147; L.V. 24, 83; Śiv. 268, 738, 746, 994, 1151, 1632, 1706, 1801, 1809; Rām. 582, 686, 745, 886, 889, 917, 1190, 1658-9; K. 378, 970, 1125; K.Pr. 230); a strong wind, a wind-storm, hurricane, whirlwind (El.; Śiv. 253, 1558, 1833; Rām. 403, 461, 550, 563, 601, 891, 1336, 1338; K. 1087; K.Pr. 76, 80); air, climate (Gr.M.); (pl.) the five vital airs, i.q. prān 1, p. 760b, l. 36, q.v. (L.V. 69; Śiv. 527, 1014, 1546); poverty, indigence, penury, helplessness, misery (cf. bata-wᵒ, p. 137b, l. 18 ff; warzunᵘ wᵒ, p. 1145a, l. 19) (Śiv. 1831; Rām. 267, 1207; K.Pr. 59, 205, 232, 235, 255); an epidemic, pestilence (cf. kāʦa-wᵒ, p. 493a, l. 15); the god of wind (Skt. Vāyu), who is the regent of the north-west quarter (cf. ludr-wᵒ, p. 510b, l. 17) (Śiv. 1147, 1301; Rām. 737, 855, 906; K. 538); courtesy, politeness (noted only in ʦhĕndⁱ ta wāv, p. 1066a, l. 42). --dᵃnun -- m.inf. to state, or proclaim, one's poverty. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give wind, to make a breeze (e.g. with a fan or the like); to display or divulge some hidden thing or secret for a very short time, to expose such for but a moment. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to experience poverty, to get along somehow or other in a state of poverty. --lagun -- m.inf. an (unwholesome) wind to attack (a person, e.g. causing a chill to a sweating body, or the like); cf. wāwa-zar, bel. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. poverty to fall (on a person, e.g. when a rich man loses all his possessions) (W. 143; Rām. 283, 621). ¶ wāwa-dab m. a fall of the wind, a check or suppression of a violent wind-storm. -ḍūnᵘ m. a walnut with a small kernel (that a mere touch of wind blows from the tree), a windfall walnut. -golᵘ m. 'a wind-mouth', a place (such as a cave or a room) out of which there continually issues a strong draught or blast of air, as it were through a door. -hāl f. (sg. dat. -höjᵘ̈), 'a wind-hall', a place (e.g. a road, or a room) where strong wind is always continually blowing. -khal f. a room (in a house), or the like, in which there exists a strong, bitterly cold, draught. -kār m. when in a state of poverty to carry out (an expensive) festivity (such as a son's marriage); met. to carry something out against one's own wishes. --karun -- m.inf. to carry on some work in a state of poverty and want of the necessary materials. -kaṭh m. (f. -küṭᵘ̈), a child of poverty, a child born to poverty-stricken parents, a child brought up without proper food and clothing; a child born to parents who have no other children, an only child. -māl f. a sail (of a ship) (El. m.; Gr.M. f.; Śiv. 1834). -mŏyā f. a slight wind (Gr.Gr. 164). -nāv pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. extreme poverty to fall (upon some formerly rich person). -phungur m. (sg. dat. -phungaras), a short violent gust of wind, a smart puff (strong enough to extinguish, not encourage, fire). -paṭh m. (sg. dat. -paṭas), a sheet used in winnowing. -ring f. a slight gentle breeze (cf. p. 837b, l. 28) (Gr.Gr. 162). -tab m. a slow lingering fever caused by an unwholesome wind. -ṭhūl m. an empty egg (whose sole content is wind); met. a very thin weak child. -ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ʦanjĕ), a puff of wind, a gust (Gr.M.). -woshᵘ m. a shower of rain accompanying a gale of wind. -zar m. a fever caused by the impact of cold wind on a sweating body, a chill. Cf. wāv lagun, ab. ¶ wövⁱ karun m.inf. to carry out somehow or other some necessary festivity, or other expensive proceeding, when in a state of poverty. ¶ wāwukᵘ adj. gen. (f. wāvücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or due to wind (e.g. terror at a storm) (K. 1087); of, belonging to, or due to poverty. ¶ wāvüñᵘ̈ wātal f. (of a body or number of persons) fleeing in all directions, scattered flight (e.g. in terror, or from some calamity). --wātal gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a condition of such scattered flight to occur. --wātal karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (by an attack or the like) to put to scattered flight, to rout (an army). ¶ wāwas nāwa-söl m. 'a pleasure-cruise in poverty', e.g. to become engaged in heavy and complicated commercial dealings, without possessing any of the necessary stock or appliances. --wāv pyonᵘ -- m.inf. poverty to fall on poverty, i.e. further poverty to fall on one who is already poverty-stricken.
m. in danda-wāv, a tooth-file, p. 225a, l. 30, and phahᵃra-wāv, a file, p. 687a, l. 30, yẹ̆ndra-wāv, s.v. yẹ̆ndᵃr. Cf. wōwᵃrun.
m. in khanḍa-wāv, a shawl-weaver, p. 403a, l. 21. Cf. wôwurᵘ.
f. in khanḍa-wāvil, the profession of a shawl-weaver, p. 403a, l. 33. Cf. wāv 3.

wāwᵃ̇jᵃ̇, or wāvüjᵘ̈ f. a fan, a hand-pankhā (cf. ṭᵃka-wᵃ, p. 991b, l. 36) (Śiv. 1151; K. 652, 1164); met. something that cools (cf. ạshᵉ̆ka-wāwüjᵉ̆, p. 48b, l. 42). wāwᵃjĕ-wagowᵃ m. a kind of mat (woven of bamboo-leaves, or date-palm-leaves). wāwᵃji-dan m. the handle of a hand-pankhā.
f. (of a fish) full of roe. Cf. wav.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. wāwaladiñ), poverty-stricken (esp. of one all his life in this condition).

f. (sg. dat. wāvüʦᵘ̈), borax (used as a flux for melting precious metals) (El.). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. flux to fall, to become melted; met. (of possessions) sudden vanishing to happen, to be suddenly ruined and lost (through bad companionship or the like).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wowᵘ), to sow (seed), to scatter or plant seed (cf. tavith wᵒ, p. 1047b, l. 50) (El. wawun, vauwun; L. 464, wáwun; L.V. 66; Śiv. 1110, 1476, 1530, 1532; Rām. 14, 1364, 1504, 1512, 1661; H. ix, 9; K.Pr. 84, 187, 190, 232, 256); to sow (a field, etc.), to plant (a field, etc.) with seed (Gr.M.); to plant a cutting. Cf. wāpun. ¶ wowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), sown (of seed, etc.); planted as a cutting; (of a field, etc.) sown. wȧvⁱ-matis krāv m. the harvesting of that which has been sown; reaping the fruits of one's former actions, (esp.) enjoying the results of former kindly actions; to live comfortably on one's accumulated earnings. ¶ wavith thawun m.inf. to sow the seed (and leave it there); met. to do some kind, or unkind, action, which will ultimately bear fruit in the shape of pleasant or unpleasant results.
m. in dōla-wạy, a zigzag path, p. 211b, l. 20.

m. sufficient rice for the food of a whole household, the allowance of rice issued (at stated intervals or on any occasion) for such food (K.Pr. 44 (wai), 192 (wáí)). --mọ̆ʦᵘ -- m. a store saved up and collected out of the allowance of rice issued at intervals for feeding a household. ¶ wayĕs sombᵘ adj. (f. --sümbᵘ̈ --), sufficient for the daily allowance of rice, etc., issued for the consumption of a household.

m. wind (cf. wāv and mal-wᵒ, p. 564a, ll. 46 ff.) (El. wáyí); (usually) rheumatism, gout, or similar pain (cf. baba-wᵒ, p. 77a, l. 38; dada-wᵒ, p. 187b, l. 45; danda-mal-wᵒ, p. 224b, l. 42; cf. mal-wᵒ, ab.); ? palsy, see we. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. an attack of rheumatism to come on. ¶ wāyĕ-bĕmörⁱ f. rheumatism. -phŏtᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. 'a basket of rheumatism', rheumatism pervading the whole body (which is thereby shrunken up like a basket). -patᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. 'a rheumatism mat', an attack of severe and permanent rheumatism.

f. N. of a certain semi-aquatic medicinal plant, the root of which is used as a stomachic and for diminishing phlegm, the Sweet-flag, Acorus calamus; the root of this flag. -bọ̆dᵘ m. a bunch of the stems of this flag. -ganḍᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the root of this flag. -gāsa m. the sheathed grass-like stem of this flag. -kala m. the knob, or bulb, at the bottom of this flag. -laḍur m. the sheathed stem of this flag. -rāṭh f. (sg. dat. -rāṭhi), a long and widespread collection of the roots of this flag, all sprung from a single original root. -sar m. N. of a lake in Kashmīr (Śiv. 1826).
f. the profession of playing (a musical instrument) (cf. sāza-wāy, p. 959b, l. 23). See wāyun.

f. a suffix indicating the wages paid for anything, as in börᵘ̈way, p. 118b, l. 31, or böraway, p. 130a, l. 23, the wages of a porter; chānaway, p. 163a, l. 6, the wages of a carpenter; dŏsilway, p. 255b, l. 17, the wages of a plasterer; gānaway, p. 288a, l. 30, a harlot's fee; hŏnjĕ-way, p. 337b, l. 46, commission on a bill of exchange (Gr.Gr. 143).

m. respect, deference, modesty (equivalent to لحاظ). wāyĕ barun m.inf. to abstain from undertaking any intended difficult work out of modesty in the presence of another respected person. --karun -- m.inf. out of such modesty to cease from such a work. Cf. bēwāyĕ, without hesitation, carelessly, fearlessly, p. 148a, l. 39, and Rām. 108, 1300.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wāyĕnôwᵘ), to cause to be plied or used, to enable to be plied or used (Śiv. 1877, ʦhã̄ṭh wāyĕnāvüñᵘ̈, to enable swimming to be done, to enable to swim); to cause to row (a boat), to enable to row (Śiv. 1780, 1804).
n.ag. (f. wayĕvüñᵘ̈) (food) that is wholesome, or that is a good regimen; (teaching or advice) that is agreeable and acceptable to the hearer.
n.ag. (f. wāyĕvüñᵘ̈), one who propels, uses, wields; one who rows a boat; one who plays (a musical instrument) (Śiv. 1441, 1779).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. woyᵘ 2 (for 1, see s.v.) (of food) to be or become wholesome, to agree with, be or become a suitable regimen (for an invalid) (esp. of something of which the wholesomeness was doubtful, but which consumption has shown to be wholesome) (Gr.Gr. 204); (genl.) (of food) to be wholesome, suitable (Śiv. 1086). woyᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vüyᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), that which has turned out to be a wholesome regimen, as ab., a tonic; met. (teaching or advice) which is agreeable or acceptable to the hearer.

conj. 1 impers. (1 p.p. wôyᵘ), to ply, use, wield (a tool, weapon, or the like) (cf. dukörᵘ̈ wāyüñᵘ̈, p. 209a, l. 30; litᵘ̈rᵘ̈ wāyüñᵘ̈, p. 539a, l. 16; makᵃʦ wāyüñᵘ̈, p. 563a, l. 29; shrākh wāyüñᵘ̈, p. 892a, l. 21) (K. 928, 980, 1132); to row, propel, paddle (a boat) (cf. atha wᵒ, p. 65a, l. 14; druba-wᵒ, p. 240a, l. 9; nama wᵒ, p. 635b, l. 50; wŏra wᵒ, p. 1136a, l. 33) (L. 462; Śiv. 1488, 1683, 1805); to wave (the arms), throw (the arms) up and down (cf. narĕ wāyĕñĕ, p. 650a, l. 15); to perform an action involving throwing the arms backwards and forwards (e.g. swimming) (cf. ʦhã̄ṭh wāyüñᵘ̈, p. 1163a, l. 19) (Gr.M.); (in cultivating) to drive (bullocks), to plough (cf. dã̄d wāyȧnⁱ, p. 187a, ll. 24 ff.) (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1530; K.Pr. 49, 187 (wái, impve.)); to play (a musical instrument) (cf. nay wāyüñᵘ̈, p. 669b, l. 46; pōg wᵒ, p. 683a, l. 36; shiriñ wāyüñᵘ̈, p. 894b, l. 40; vīnā wāyüñᵘ̈, p. 1121b, l. 27) (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 107, 450, 669, 732, 782, 796, 1323, 1336, 1453, 1779; K. 260-2, 270, 275, 280, 282, 296, 340, 412, 964, 1031; YZ. 372; K.Pr. 156); to beat a drum, gong, or similar instrument, or, e.g., the breast (cf. ḍābᵘ̈rᵘ̈ wāyüñᵘ̈, p. 184a, l. 34; ḍam-ḍam wᵒ, p. 218b, ll. 41 ff.; nagāra wāyĕnwôlᵘ, p. 624b, l. 50; sāz wᵒ, p. 958b, l. 5) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1029, Rām. 183) (beating the breast), 831 (a drum), 974 (id.); to ring (a coin, to see if it is genuine) (L. 462). L. 464 adds the meaning 'to suit', probably wrong for wuyun, q.v. wāyun dã̄d lāyun kān m. 'a bullock to plough, and an arrow to be shot', a man (esp. a servant) who has to do all the hard work of an establishment (at one time doing heavy work like a plough bullock, and at another time sent on long messages like an arrow). ¶ wöyⁱ wöyⁱ wanun m.inf. as if with indifference, or unconcern, to direct, or give orders to another; when a person wants anything done, to bring someone else to him to do the work (instead of doing it oneself). ¶ wôyᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wöyᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), plied, used, etc., as ab.; esp. wöyᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ zamīn, arable land (El. wáímats z˚).
waz' وضع f. placing, fixing, laying down; a gesture, action (with suff. of indef. art. waziyāh, Rām. 824); a dignity, that which confers honour (K.Pr. 261, wazah).
m. a sermon (Moslem) (H. xii, 1). wāz- khwān وعظ خوان m. a Moslem preacher (L. 462).

m. a cook (cf. aṭa-wᵒ, p. 56a, l. 34; baṭᵃñĕ-wᵃ, p. 145a, l. 22; hūnⁱ-māzas wātal-wᵒ, p. 337a, l. 5; nöṭⁱ-wⁱ, p. 660a, l. 7; wātal-wᵒ, p. 1164b, l. 8; wuʦan-wᵒ, p. 1171a, l. 10) (El.; Gr.Gr. 95, 132; Gr.M.; L. 459, waza; L.V. 83; Śiv. 1072; Rām. 581; K. 737-8; K.Pr. 54, 84, 106). -bāy f. his wife. -gara m. a cooking house, kitchen (El. -gar). -küṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kacĕ), his daughter (by tradition, naughty, impudent, and abusive). -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a cook's son (a term used contemptuously or in anger) (Gr.Gr. 132); used abusively to indicate anyone of similar conduct (ill-conducted, impudent, and abusive). -mahanyuwᵘ m. a servant who does cook's work, a house-cook. -pacĕ c.g. a cook-person, one who is a cook by profession, and comes of a line, or caste, of cooks. -pônᵘ m. cookship, the profession of a cook (practised by one who has not previously been a cook). -pāza m.pl. cooks and the like, cooks etc. (a jingle) (Gr.Gr. 95). -tônᵘ m. the conduct or actions of a new cook, i.e. of one who has not acted as a cook previously. -tᵃʦh f. (sg. dat. -tᵃʦhi), a cook's dirty rag, the filthy rag or cloth used for wiping out vessels and the like; any similar rag. -wān m. a cookshop, cookroom, kitchen (K.Pr. 159). -yĕṭh f. (sg. dat. -yĕṭi), the pride (or arrogance) of a skilled cook (see yĕṭh).
f. the profession or condition of a cook.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wazanôwᵘ), to moisten, make wet, wet (El.); cf. wazawun. wazanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wazanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), moistened, wetted.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wazanôwᵘ), to cause to give forth a sound (e.g. to strike a bell, or to crack a whip) (cf. dura wazanāwȧnⁱ, p. 239a, l. 31).
f. (sg. dat. wazārüʦᵘ̈), the office, or dignity, of a vizier or high minister of state (see wazīr); the dignity or position of an heir apparent to a king (Rām. 509).
f. the act of moistening, wetting (Gr.Gr. 120).
f. (sg. dat. wazavüñᵘ̈ 1, for 2, 3, see wazawunᵘ 1, 2), the action of making moist, moistening, wetting.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wazowᵘ), to moisten, make wet; cf. wazanāwun 1 and wanun 3. wazowᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wazüvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), moistened, wetted.

n.ag. (f. wazavüñᵘ̈ 2, for 1, see wazawan), that which is put in water to get wet, that which is being soaked; (of any work, circumstance, story, etc.) that which is being delayed (in order to postpone the result). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain in a condition of delay, be in a state of suspense (esp. of some work that should be done at once). --thawun -- m.inf. to delay, cause delay (to something, esp. to something that should be done at once).
n.ag. (f. wazavüñᵘ̈ 3), that which gives forth a sound (e.g. a bell, a musical instrument, or any article of wood or metal) whether on being struck, etc., or spontaneously.

m. a minister of state, a vizier (El.; Rām. 465, 1756; K. 819, 823; H. ii, 1, 4, 5, etc.; viii, 1, 4, 11, 12, 14; xii, 1, 2, 4, 5, etc.; K.Pr. 210, 246); (at chess) the queen (Rām. 1314). -wazārat وزیر وزارت m. (in Ksh.) a district officer (L. 401, 421).
f. the dignity or office of a vizier (El., a counsellor; H. xii, 26).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wozᵘ, 2 p.p. wazōv), to give forth a sound, to sound, ring (as a musical instrument, or as a whip being cracked, or some metal or wooden thing when knocked) (cf. dura wazȧnⁱ, p. 239a, ll. 24, 29; dŏyĕ atha ʦürᵘ̈ wazüñᵘ̈, s.v. zᵃh) (El. wajun, wazun; Śiv. 327, 725, 1638, 1729, 1779; K. 1009; K.Pr. 42, 60); (of a human being) to speak in a roar, to roar out (something).
or wāzᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. worry, annoyance, being distracted from one's work by another (cf. sŏna-wᵒ, p. 917b, l. 50). --lāgüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to worry, distract, as ab.
f.pl. in potᵘ waʦa phērañĕ, to be struck senseless with terror, p. 788b, l. 30, q.v.

f. (sg. dat. wāʦaki), reading out fluently and correctly (from a book or the like). --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the power of such reading to come into existence, i.e. to be gained (by a person). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of some child or the like) the power of fluent reading aloud to come, i.e. to be acquired. ¶ wāʦȧkⁱ parun m.inf. to read without attending to the meaning (for the purpose of learning mnemonical rules, such as those of grammar, by rote).
m. one who habitually uses (censurable) language, a calumniator, contradictor, reviler, or the like.
m.pl. in shīth waʦan, p. 899b, l. 14, q.v.

m. 'arrival'; hence, the turning up, or being got, just when required (of something laboured for or desired), the coming of an opportunity to complete some work; the acquisition of some quality, the mastery of some acquirement, branch of art, or learning, the gaining of skill or dexterity.

or wö̃ʦar m. (of a river, lake, pit, or the like) shallowness; shallowness of intellect, readiness to let out, or divulge, secrets; absence of profundity, simplicity and clearness of language. Cf. wỗtᵘ.

m. (sg. dat. wāʦas), words, speech; a promise, undertaking, pledge (K. 279). --dyunᵘ --, m.inf. to promise, plight one's word (K. 520). --hyonᵘ --, m.inf. to take a word, i.e. to obtain (a person's) assent (Rām. 151); to take up a word, to make a petition (K. 575, wāc hyonᵘ). ¶ wāʦa-band or -bandan m. word-binding, a promise (to perform, etc.) (K. 278-80, -band). -bandan dyunᵘ m.inf. to promise, vow (to do something).

m. (of two things usually, or which can be, joined together) the being slightly apart, openness, the condition of being open (e.g. the eyelids, a clasp, a garment) (cf. ȧchⁱ-wⁱ (p. 8b, l. 50); (of something that can be closed or shut up) openness (cf. atha-wᵒ, p. 65a, l. 13) (Gr.Gr. 29, 140).
m. eager, ardent, affection (for a son, wife, brother, friend, or the like).

or waʦhurᵘ m. (f. waʦhᵃr or waʦhürᵘ̈), a calf (cf. dŏda- waʦhürᵘ̈, p. 190b, l. 11; khinda-wᵒ, p. 403a, l. 42) (El. watsir, f.; Gr.Gr. 33, 37, waʦhᵃr, f.; K.Pr. 81, 171, f.). ¶ This word, with an interjection, is used in the vocative fem., with emphatic y, waʦhariy, in addressing a female junior or inferior, as in hāy (hatay, or hatöy) waʦhariy! (Gr.Gr. 99).

m. (sg. dat. waʦanas), the reading out of some sacred book; a verse sung in a song, a song (cf. wanawan-wᵒ, p. 1126b, l. 40) (Śiv. 1044, 1454, 1662); a saying, a sentence of instruction, precept (cf. wākh-wᵒ, p. 1108b, l. 13) (L.V. 94). --wanun -- m. (at a wedding or similar festival, the chorus of women) to start singing auspicious songs. ¶ waʦan-pad m. a line (of a stanza) of one of such auspicious songs.
m. or we-naṭh ? f. (El. both m.) shaking palsy, paralysis agitans. (Noted only in El. Probably we is incorrect for wāy 1, q.v. See also naṭh.)
(? spelling and gender) N. of a certain medicinal plant, used as an anthelmintic (L. 75).
in washĕ-wö, the letter. See wash 2.

or (H. v, 2) wŏbāl (= وبال) m. a crime, sin, fault; blame-worthiness, a guilty condition (H. v, 2). This word is old, and is now little used, but is still generally understood. --khasun -- m.inf. (another's) guilt to rise (upon a person), (another's) wickedness to infect a person (through association).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏbarôwᵘ), to finish, complete (Gr.Gr. 170); (with conj. part. of another verb) to finish (doing something), end (some action) completely (Rām. wanith w˚, to finish speaking, 414, 469, 1344, 1389, 1698); cf. wŏbarun. wŏbarôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏbarövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), finished, completed (by someone).

conj. 1 and 3 (1 p.p. wŏborᵘ; 2 p.p. wŏbaryōv) (with conj. part. of another verb) to finish (doing something), stop (doing something) (Rām. wanith wŏborun, he stopped speaking, 442, 507) (cf. wŏbarāwun); (conj. 3) to be finished, completed (Gr.Gr. 170). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. 'finishing to come', decrepitude from old age to come (to a person). ¶ wŏbarān yunᵘ m.inf. (of strength, accumulated property, etc.), gradually to waste away, (of a person) to approach decrepitude from old age. ¶ wŏbaryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏbaryē-müʦᵘ̈), finished, completed.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏbasôwᵘ), to cause to swell, to cause food being cooked to swell, or foam, up; to cause any work to have prolific results; (of foam or the like) to become widely scattered abroad.

conj. 2 or 3 (Gr.Gr. 205-6) (1 p.p. wŏbosᵘ; 2 p.p. wŏbasyōv, Gr.Gr. 226) to be very prolific, to have copious fruit, to pullulate, to have great or many results; (of food being cooked) to swell greatly in size, to swell up, increase in size (Gr.Gr. 206); to become divided into innumerable parts, to be scattered widely. ¶ wŏbosᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏbüsᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), increased, etc., as ab. ¶ wŏbasith yunᵘ m.inf. to become prolific; (of food being cooked) to swell or foam up.
in wŏbayĕ-brạshᵉ̆ṭh adj. c.g. fallen from both, i.e. (of a person trying two alternatives) failing to succeed in either (e.g. trying to combine worldly conduct with piety), fallen between two stools.

m. a small hole or window in a wall for admitting air or light, or for letting out smoke, a ventilating hole, a smoke-hole (cf. dᵃha-wᵃ, p. 198a, l. 40; gāshĕ-wᵒ, p. 308b, l. 46; hēri-wᵒ, p. 345b, l. 20; pashĕ-wᵒ, p. 777b, l. 11). ¶ wŏbⁱ-dörⁱ f. such a hole (generally in the top of a wall). -gāsh m. the light coming in through such a hole. -ʦôkᵘ m. the wooden frame of such a hole. --wasȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. the ventilating holes to come down; hence (on the occasion of a festival or the like) an unexpected obstacle to occur.
f. a jingle of kö̆bᵘ̈rᵘ̈, q.v. in kö̆bᵘ̈rᵘ̈-wᵘ̈, p. 382b, l. 3.

f. the upper part of the head, the brain-pan, crown of the head (El.; Śiv. 1012; H. iii, 1; xi, 12, 16; K.Pr. 203); a head of hair (Gr.Gr. 16, scalp). --pārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (of a woman) to braid the hair. --shērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to comb, or arrange, the hair. ¶ wŏḍa-nonᵘ adj. (f. -nüñᵘ̈), bare-headed, with the head uncovered (K. 825; K.Pr. 86, wuḍah nun). ¶ wŏḍi rab f. mud on the head, used in ḍab-ḍab wŏḍi-rab, a practical joke, p. 183a, l. 41, q.v. -ʦünḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ʦanjĕ), a slap on the (uncovered) head; met. a gross insult, insulting abuse, bullying. -ʦünḍᵘ̈ lagüñᵘ̈ f.inf. gross and insulting abuse to be experienced, to be treated with insult (e.g. on account of one's want of merit, or having no protector), to be bullied. -ʦanjĕ-kūrᵘ̈  f. a girl who (on account of her want of merit, or because she has no one to protect her) is habitually bullied, insulted, or treated with contempt; met. a grown-up woman who is so treated. --wŏḍi dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to give several slaps on a person's head; met. frequently to bully, abuse, or insult someone who has no protector. --wŏḍi lagȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. such bullying to be experienced.

wödᵘ̈, or waid m. a physician, a doctor, i.q. waidy, q.v. (cf. phĕla-wödᵘ̈, p. 693b, l. 5) (El. waid, Gr.Gr. 22). wöda-wān m. a doctor's place of business, where he receives patients (K.Pr. 138, vedah-wán); a place to which sick persons come for treatment, a hospital.

m. a gift, or present (offered to a superior, or, on a festal occasion, to a friend or relation). Cf. wôdᵘ. ¶ wōda-baröyⁱ f. the offering of such a gift in return for a similar gift given to the offerer on a previous occasion. See waröyⁱ. --nērun -- m.inf. to give (some near relation) a helping hand by making him a present on a festal occasion (esp. when the present is non-obligatory).

f. sickness, ailment, disease, illness. --hōrüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to pass through a sickness, to recover after suffering from illness. ¶ wōda-ʦaʦᵃr f. general anxiety felt by many of a person's relations and family on the occasion of his suffering from illness.
adv. from there (H. xii, 23). I.q. ōra, p. 41b, l. 20, q.v.
m. abusive disgrace, dishonour, disgrace (referring to a person, beast, thing, or action).
or wŏdĕm m. zeal, energy (Gr.M.); exertion (El. wadam, wadĕm).

adj. c.g. and adv., standing up, erect, standing permanently on end (Rām. 951; H. iii, 1, 8; viii, 6; xii, 1; K.Pr. 145, wudanih); risen up (to a standing position) (Rām. 332, 431, 524, 672, 819, 1374); (as adv.) very quickly speedily (u.w.vbs. of motion, eating, giving, etc.); cf. wŏthadañĕ. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain standing (Gr.M.; H. xii, 1); to be at attention, always ready to obey, to be constant in attendance or service; to receive (a guest) hospitably.
adj. c.g. generous, liberal, munificent. -ʦĕth adj. c.g. noble-minded, magnanimous; intelligent, discriminating.
adj. c.g. indifferent, apathetic, listless; one who has no passion for anything; bewildered, perplexed, distracted (Śiv. 1434, 1453).

m. rising (e.g. of a heavenly body) (Rām. 1265); exaltation, grandeur, splendour, nobility (K. 1072). ¶ wŏdayĕs yunᵘ m.inf. to come to rising, to become highly exalted, to reach a very high pitch (K. 426, 1048, 1096, 1108).

m. production, creation; (in Ksh.) energy (in any work), strenuous effort; independence, autonomy. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to encourage (a person) to practise independence (whether good or bad). --lagun -- m.inf. 'independence to be acquired', i.e. to get freedom to deal with property or business hitherto under the control of another.
m. an exalted person, one of high degree, eminent, magnanimous, and of great wealth.
adj. c.g. a speaker, one who speaks, used --˚, as in satya-wödī, p. 950a, l. 17 (Śiv. 518).
m. one who is indifferent, unconcerned, taking no part (in).

m. i.q. wŏdās 2, esp. one who has abandoned all passion for things of this world, an anchorite, hermit, ascetic (Śiv. 1759); separated (from), apart (from) (Rām. 507); sorrowful, mournful, forlorn (Gr.M., Rām. 1213); bewildered, perplexed, distracted (Śiv. 779). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to abandon worldly desires and passions, to take to indifference to the world, to become an ascetic; to become distraught (Śiv. 779, Rām. 524). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain apart, take no part (in something), show oneself unconcerned (in). Cf. the next.

m. (sg. dat. wŏdaras), the womb (L.V. 51); the belly, abdomen (El. also waḍur, Śiv. 1817). wŏdar-dôdᵘ m. (of a childless person) yearning for offspring; (of a person with children) sympathy, loving fellow-feeling with one's children; anxiety for a child's future (moral or material).
m. (sg. dat. wōdaras), a robber with violence, highway robber, marauder (cf. gözⁱ-wôⁱ, p. 318b, l. 27).
adj. raised, lifted up, exalted (K. 424); ready, prepared, eager, bent on, intent on.
or wŏdyōg m. exertion, effort (El. wadhyug, wadyúg; Śiv. 1015, 1709, 1766, 1804). --karun -- m.inf. to endeavour, make effort, exert oneself (El., Śiv. 1708, K. 586).
adj. c.g. industrious, diligent, persevering, zealous (at work) (Gr.M.).
or wŏdurᵘ  m. an otter (El. udur; L. 111, wudar; W. 9, vo˙dur). wŏdȧrⁱ-musla m. otter-skin (used by the wealthy as a kind of cloak in cold weather).
m. in nētra-wahara-wôdᵘ, p. 662a, l. 41, and wahᵃra-wôdᵃ, s.v. wahorᵘ. Cf. wōd 1, of which it is probably another spelling.
(also spelt wödᵃr) f. a bubo (e.g. in the armpit) (cf. kȧʦhⁱ-wⁱ, p. 493a, l. 4) (K.Pr. 128, wádar, translated 'sickness'). --pë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a bubo to come on (K.Pr. 128, as ab.).
in wahᵃra-wᵃ, s.v. wahar. Cf. wôdᵘ.

m. a roofed window or other aperture in the roof of a house (for entrance or exit on to the roof) (El.); cf. wuga. -borᵘ m. the exit on to the roof of a house through a roofed window or otherwise). -baran f. (sg. dat. barüñᵘ̈), the doorway of such an aperture. -morᵘ m. a hut or shelter in the roof of a house. -pash m. the thatch of a roof-aperture; met. (of rice or the like in a dish) the condition of being a very high pile.

m. deafness. -phrath m. (sg. dat. -phratas), an ill-bred, ill-mannered fellow (in appearance, dress, speech, listening, standing, walking, and every other action), a boor, clown, uncouth person. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. deafness to come on (a person).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. wŏgaladiñ), one who suffers from deafness.
or wŏgañĕr m. shallowness, etc., as in wŏgunᵘ, q.v.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. wŏganyōv), to become shallow (of something previously deep; e.g. a river becoming silted up, or a dish by accumulation of dirt); (of something sunk or fastened deep down) to rise to the surface, become manifest (cf. shāna wŏganȧnⁱ, p. 884b, l. 5) (Rām. 1122). wŏganyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏganyē-müʦᵘ̈), become shallow, as ab.; risen to the surface, as ab.

wŏgᵃra, or wugra m. a kind of thin rice gruel or porridge (thinned with the water in which it has been boiled, and suitable for mixing with other edibles) (cf. dŏda-wᵒ, p. 190b, l. 5; gāri-wᵒ, p. 298a, l. 14; machĕ-wᵒ, p. 547a, l. 44; pingi-wᵒ, p. 740a, l. 22; sirⁱ-wⁱ, p. 957b, l. 43; ʦēra-nȧmⁱ-wⁱ, p. 1079a, l. 49) (L. 462; K.Pr. 147, 205, 255). When cold it becomes a jelly, hence:---ṭīrᵘ̈ f. a lump of this jellied rice-porridge; met. a poor weak man (K.Pr. 249). -ṭūrᵘ m. a kind of round, deep, dish for holding this jellied porridge. -ṭyonḍᵘ m. (sg. dat. -ṭĕnḍis), a very small lump of this jellied porridge.

adj. (f. wŏgüñᵘ̈) (of a body of water) fordable, shallow, not deep (cf. danda-wᵒ, p. 225a, l. 2; sonᵘ wᵒ, p. 918a, l. 21) (Śiv. 1638, 1681, 1892, see sonᵘ wᵒ, as ab.; Rām. 1715, YZ. 542); (of a person or his intellect) open, shallow, unreserved (Śiv. 1757).
adv. now, a vill. form for wŏñ, q.v. (H. iii, 9).

(cf. wŏhav) in wŏha-wŏha hë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. to become an object of general and frequent vituperation (owing to bad conduct, or to causing damage whether knowingly or unknowingly); cf. wŏhav. -wŏha-khë˘ñᵘ̈ f.inf. to suffer such vituperation. -wŏha karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to vituperate (something that has gone wrong or someone who makes it go wrong). -wŏha pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. such vituperation to occur (e.g. when things go wrong, or someone acts badly or rudely).

m. a curse, cursing, imprecation, malediction, vituperation (cf. bab-wᵒ, p. 77a, l. 3; lȧlⁱ-wⁱ, p. 523a, l. 26; ṭakulᵘ wᵒ, p. 993a, l. 45) (El. wohau; Gr.Gr. 124; K.Pr. 72, sg. obl. wohawah). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take a curse, accept a malediction; (esp. of a naughty child) to accept a severe scolding for bad conduct (and to cease therefrom). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to utter a curse or malediction against someone. --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. to suffer a malediction, to be cursed; (esp. of a naughty child) to be severely scolded. -tholᵘ adj. (f. -thüjᵘ̈), one who lies under a curse; esp. one who (on account of bad conduct) is an object of general abuse. --ʦārun -- m.inf. to select, i.e. utter, a curse or malediction; (esp.) severely to scold (a naughty child).

conj. 1, impers. (1 p.p. wŏhowᵘ), to curse (Gr.Gr. 124, K.Pr. 132); to vituperate, to abuse. ¶ wŏhawan-lŏgulᵘ adj. (f. -lŏgüjᵘ̈), one who habitually utters curses or vituperations. ¶ wŏhawȧnⁱ bĕhun m.inf. to set to work at cursing or vituperation, to pour forth a flood of vituperation.
adj., c.g. broken, crazy, in wöhⁱ taböhⁱ (= واہی تباہی) adj. c.g. in broken condition or circumstances; crazy, insane. --taböhⁱ bāshun -- m.inf. to talk nonsense.

m. general longing, eagerness (for something, on account of its rarity, worth, excellence, or the like), high estimation. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to enhance the value (of something) (Rām. 1313, but probably here for wôjᵘ dᵒ, s.v. wôjᵘ, q.v.). khōj m. contrariety, opposition, adverseness, oppositeness (occurring in some thing or action, or in the medical treatment of an invalid). --lagun -- m.inf. to become of great value, to become an object of general desire (owing to becoming rare or the like).
wujāpȧtⁱ, wŏjāpath, or wujāpath adj. c.g. unfit, improper, unsuitable, inefficient, unfit to be done, acting unfitly.

or wujāra adj. c.g. laid waste, devastated, demolished, ruined, spoiled; waste, desolate, deserted, abandoned. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become utterly ruined, demolished, wasted, ravaged, plundered, spoiled; to become deserted, desolate, wasted. --karun -- m.inf. to ruin, lay waste, devastate, destroy, spoil, plunder, depopulate.
m. unsteadiness of temper, the having an uncertain temper (Gr.Gr. 31, 41); esp. the being easily moved to anger, irascibility, irritability. Cf. wūlᵘ.
adj. c.g. necessary, expedient, proper, worthy (of) (Gr.M., W. 110).

m. the edge of a thatch or roof, an eave (Rām. 570, wōj m.c.); the water falling from the eaves of a house. --pashpun -- m. water to trickle from the eaves of a house. --wasun -- water to fall, as ab. ¶ wȧjⁱ-asta m. the sheltered space (usually about a cubit wide) under the eaves of a house (see asta). -pashpun m. the trickle of water from the eaves of a house. -rāṭh f. (sg. dat. -rāṭhi) a violent torrent of rain falling from the eaves. -wôñᵘ m. water which is falling, or which has fallen, from the eaves. -wôrᵘ m. a small hut, useful as a shelter from the rain.

m. (after a sound coming from a lute, drum, or similar musical instrument) reverberation, resonance. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give forth a reverberation; met. (after another has made a short statement) to repeat it at length and with diffuseness; (of another's good or bad quality of small importance) to dilate upon it at great length (cf. wōj dᵒ, s.v. wōj 2 and Rām. 1313).

or wöjᵘ̈ 1 a finger-ring, a ring (generally) (cf. aina-wᵒ, p. 30b, l. 11; gö̃ḍa-wᵒ, p. 277b, l. 2; kana-wᵒ, p. 448a, l. 39; krē̃ka-wᵒ, p. 470a, l. 19; mŏhara-wᵒ, p. 556a, l. 21; nasta-wᵒ, p. 658b, l. 15; pampōshĕ-wᵒ, p. 734a, l. 26; yēran-wᵒ, s.v. yērun) (El. wáj. wãj; Gr.Gr. 31; Gr.M.; L. 463, waj; W. 13, vöj, 17 vöz; Śiv. 414, 994, 1043, 1095, 1373, 1760; Rām. 670-2, 1125, 1294; K. 926, 1047; H. v, 1; x, 8; xii, 14, 15; K.Pr. 227); a hole (e.g. of a rat, mouse, snake, etc.) (cf. nūla-wᵒ, p. 634b, l. 9; sarpa-wᵒ, p. 937b, l. 38) (Gr.Gr. 31; W. 139, wāj; K.Pr. 3) (see also wāl 3); a button-hole or similar orifice (cf. parcan-wᵒ, p. 756a, l. 32). Cf. wôlᵘ 1, of which this word is the fem. ¶ wājĕ-atha m. a hand with rings on each finger. -krē̃kh m. (sg. dat. -krē̃kas), a jewel of a ring, or suitable for a ring (Rām. 609, wājĕ-hondᵘ kr˚). -phuṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -phucĕ), a small, broken, worn-out ring.

in wŏka wŏka karun m.inf. (owing to the influence of a drug) mental confusion to overcome (a person), mental muddling to be experienced. --wŏka lagun -- m.inf. such a state of mental confusion to come on; hesitation as regards the inception of any work to be felt. -wôrᵘ m. 'wobbly foundation', i.e. commencing a work without due preparation or before one is ready for it. Cf. wŏkish.
adj. c.g. having the hair hanging down the back in plaits (cf. wö̃kh).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏkowᵘ), noted only in K. 132, where it means 'to cool down (milk that is boiling over)', and in H. vi, 16, where it has the same meaning, but is wrongly translated 'to draw forth, bring out'.

f. (sg. dat. wö̃ki), a plait of long braided hair hanging down behind (worn by women). [Kashmīr women wear their hair in a peculiar arrangement of many plaits, in which black wool or silk is interwoven. While a girl is undeveloped these are separate, but after puberty, they are gathered together and fastened with a heavy tassel (cf. L. 251, where the distinction is said to be between married and unmarried women)] (cf. khanjȧrⁱ-wö̃ka, p. 404a, l. 27; mas-wᵒ, p. 595b, l. 34; phĕtⁱ-wö̃ka, p. 723a, l. 21; zölⁱ- wö̃ka, s.v. zôlᵘ 1) (El. wánk, also 'a curl'; Gr.Gr. 11; L. 462 wank; YZ. 155, pl. dat. wrongly written wânikan; K.Pr. 25); the silken cord used in binding these plaits; a kind of long rope-like construction consisting of vegetables stored dry in this condition for winter use (cf. gŏgᵃjᵃ-wᵃ, p. 279a, l. 33; mulⁱvĕñĕ-wⁱ, p. 570a, l. 13). Cf. wǖ̃kⁱ-dār, col. a, l. 30. ¶ wö̃ka-loṭᵘ m. the silken string tied at the end of these braided plaits, or their tassel. -laṭhurᵘ m. (after combing or cleaning the hair) the whole mass of hair gathered together, as ab. -laṭurᵘ m., id. -laṭᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the end of a braided plait farthest from the head. -mahārĕñ f. a girl bride wearing her hair now arranged as that of a married woman. -mŏnjĕ f.pl. the bases of the plaits of the braided hair close to the head. -pan the silken cord or tassel with which the end of a plait is tied (of a married or grown-up woman) (El.; L. 462, wankopan; K.Pr. 131). -patulᵘ the whole set of plaits of the hair (of an undeveloped girl). -ʦhar f. the arrangement of the separated plaits of an undeveloped girl. ¶ wö̃kan-pĕṭh adv. 'on braided plaits', i.e. a bride who is in the age-period for wearing these separately braided plaits, i.e. a young girl still undeveloped.

adj. c.g. unwell, indisposed, sick; (owing to anger, hate, strife) out of sorts, unbalanced, indisposed; terrifying, terrible, fearsome (Rām. 635). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become unwell, indisposed, suffering from illness (used esp. with reference to someone looked upon with respect or affection).

f. the being unwell, indisposition, sickness; ill-humour, irritability, petulance; (in any action) the occurrence of an obstacle (such as difficulty, unintelligibility, ugliness, dreadfulness). Cf. wōkhajyār.
m. i.q. wōkhagī, q.v., but El. wokhajár, a plot; wokhajár karun, to plot.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏkharôwᵘ), i.q. wŏkharun, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏkhorᵘ), to turn upside down (esp. the contents of a vessel, e.g. to stir up the fire in a brazier, or to stir up a mass of powder).
f. great cheapness, great reduction in price (owing to the thing sold being damaged or gone stale). wŏkhayĕ-hondᵘ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), much cheapened (for the above cause).

or wŏkhul m. (sg. dat. wŏkhalas), a large mortar (for pounding grain, salt, etc.) (El.; K. 151, 168-9, 171; K.Pr. 112, 216, 233); a stone trough (esp. one in which cloth is trodden for cleaning purposes) (cf. manḍan-wŏᵒ, p. 577a, l. 10; nāra-wŏᵒ, p. 648b, l. 14) (El.); cf. wŏkhüjᵘ̈. wŏkhal-wān m. the place where such a cleansing trough is kept (usually on the bank of a river).
m. scraping out and emptying a pot with a ladle or spoon, taking out the food to the last scrap (L.V. 95).
f. a small mortar (of stone, etc., used for pounding salt or the like) (cf. wŏkholᵘ) (El. wokhij).

m. overturning, bringing the bottom to the top, stirring up (e.g. the burning coals of a fire), used --˚, as in atha-wŏᵒ, p. 64b, l. 13; nāra-wŏᵒ, p. 648b, l. 17. Also met. in the following phrases:-- --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to remind (a person) of something he has forgotten (esp. something such as wrath or sorrow). --lagun -- m.inf. something (e.g. wrath, sorrow) previously forgotten, after the lapse of time, to come to memory.
(f. wüchᵘ̈), in pönʦa-wokhᵘ, p. 743b, l. 14, q.v.

f. (owing to the influence of a drug or the like) mental confusion (cf. wŏka); (in some work upon which one is engaged) confusion, unsteadiness, uncertainness; an attack of throbbing pain in some member of the body (due to rheumatism or the like) (cf. wŏkun).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. wŏkyōv), throbbing pain to be felt in some limb (from rheumatism or the like) (cf. wŏka and wŏkish).
adj. (f. wöcᵘ̈), used --˚, having (such-and-such) a voice (cf. kŏ-wôkᵘ, p. 496a, l. 2). Cf. wākh 1.
f. great fatigue, weariness. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. great fatigue or weariness to come, or be experienced.

f. the undeveloped foetus with its surrounding membrane; dregs of ghī (Gr.Gr. 16); cf. wölⁱ. --wasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the foetus to come down before its time, a miscarriage to occur; an appearance similar to that of a miscarriage to occur owing to extreme fatigue.

in wōla-bôrᵘ m. an insecurely or crookedly tied load, hanging awkwardly on the back and interfering with walking. -dōla adj. c.g. (any thing or action, etc., which is) habitually in an improper and awkward place or condition, so as to get into the way of others.

or (affectionately) wŏlō (used as an imperative of yunᵘ, to come, see Gr.Gr. 247) come! come here! (El. walô, wŏlo; Gr.Gr. 247, wŏla; Gr.M.; YZ. 270, 439; K.Pr. 21, wulah). wŏla-wŏla karun m.inf. to do (i.e. say) 'come, come', affectionately to address a pretty child or pet animal when inviting it to eat, etc. (W. 140, wula wula k˚).
m. children, descendants, offspring, progeny (El. walád, a son; H. iv, 3). -dôdᵘ 'offspring-pain', longing for offspring, longing for a child; sympathy with another in such longing.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏlogᵘ), i.q. wŏlangun, q.v., to pass over, to get through (something difficult), to endure right to the end (cf. sankaṭh wᵒ, p. 922a, l. 45).
(?) m. fine apparel, grand clothes, ornaments, etc. (Gr.Gr. 128, and I.K., IX, ii, 80, where it is noted as f.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏlolᵘ; 2 p.p. wŏlalyōv, Gr.Gr. lxxv), to adorn, put on fine clothes (on oneself or another) (Gr.Gr. 128).
m. reproach, blame, denunciation, accusation, imputation (due to bad conduct or the like). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. such reproach, etc., to come (to a person), to become an object of such reproach, etc.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wōlanôwᵘ), to cause (a person) to be nervous, to put (him) into agitation, to perturb, fluster. wōlanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wōlanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), agitated, etc. (by someone).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏlangôwᵘ), i.q. wŏlangun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏlongᵘ, f. wŏlünjᵘ̈), to pass over, pass through, complete, get through somehow or other (e.g. a difficult mountain climb, a long journey, a difficult task, or hard times) (cf. dŏh wᵒ, p. 200a, l. 1) (Śiv. 876, 1217, 1457, 1643). Cf. wŏlagun. ¶ wŏlongᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏlünjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), got through with difficulty, etc., as ab. ¶ wŏlangith gaʦhun m.inf., i.q. wŏlangun; also (of a thing or action) to become dissociated (from its usual concomitants).
m. beauty (of person) due to ornament, ornateness, adornment, decoration. Cf. wŏllās.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏlasôwᵘ), to put fine clothes on, dress up (esp. a child, image of a god, or the like); (by praise, kindly words, or the like) to encourage another (to a course of action).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏlosᵘ), to adorn (oneself or another), put on fine apparel; (by praise or kindly words on the part of a master, parent, or the like, or in consequence of advice, as to probable pleasant results) to become encouraged (to a course of action), to display zeal; to become happy, to rejoice (L.V. 14, Śiv. 1242). ¶ wŏlosᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏlüsᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), adorned, finely dressed (as ab.); (esp. of some child) encouraged as ab. ¶ wolasana yunᵘ m.inf. pass. (esp. of a child) to be encouraged (by a parent, teacher, or the like) to become happy (Śiv. 1262, 1347, 1509). ¶ wŏlasanas yunᵘ m.inf., id. (Śiv. 1224).

f. calamity, outrage, violence, plundering, havoc, ravaging, epidemic, or the like (caused, e.g., by invasion, by an enemy, bad government, injustice, robbers, and so on). --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to raise outrage', to ravage, plunder, rule unjustly, and so on; to start an epidemic. --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a calamity to rise or occur; an epidemic to start.
m. N. of a celebrated monkey-chief, who was slain by Rāma (Rām. 444-512). In Skt. Bāli, Bālin, Vāli, or Vālin (Rām. 456, 460-1 etc., 497, 777, 808-9, 1473).

(or wölinjᵘ̈) f. the heart (cf. carbas-tal wᵒ gaʦhüñᵘ̈, p. 175a, l. 27) (El.; Rām. 963, 1608, 1612; H. v, 6; viii, 3, 4, 11, 12; x, 5; K.Pr. 54); the heart (as the seat of the affections) (cf. waʦhi-wölinjĕ, s.v. woʦhᵘ) (L.V. 25; Śiv. 191, 316, 1197; Rām. 163, 430, 529, 730, 771, 1110, 1181, 1214, 1428, 1485, 1523; K. 442, 1127; YZ. 188, 557). -bŏḍüñᵘ̈ f.inf. the heart to sink, i.e. to faint, become insensible; to become replete with food (quasi, the belly is so full that the heart is drowned in the contents). ¶ wölinja (or wölinjĕ)-boḍᵘ  adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), great-hearted, firm-hearted, steadfast. -dôdᵘ m. pain in the heart (e.g. heart-burn or angina pectoris). -dam m. a spasm in the heart (from obstruction of breath or the like). -khỗṭᵘ m. a half (? ventricle) of the heart (looked upon as a seat of the affections, etc.). -krĕhonᵘ adj. (f. -krĕhüñᵘ̈), dark-hearted, i.e. one who obstinately refuses to answer or speak (even though pressure is put upon him or though he is abused) and who keeps his opinion concealed. -mọ̆nḍᵘ m. 'lump-hearted,' i.e. unconcerned, callous, disregarding what others say, unblushing, unabashed, insolent, a curmudgeon. -tam m. a certain disease of the heart, due to excessive exertion, and accompanied by stoppage of breath. -tamunᵘ adj. (f. -tamüñᵘ̈), soot-hearted, black-hearted, malevolent. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), patient, tolerant, stoical. -wothᵘ adj. (f. -wüʦhᵘ̈), open-hearted, magnanimous, noble-hearted, generous. Cf. wothᵘ 2.
m. happiness, joy, delight; ornateness, adornment, decoration (Śiv. 1355, 1438, 1447). Cf. wŏlās.
m. one who habitually wears ornaments, a well-dressed person, dandy, fop (Śiv. 1759). Cf. wŏlösⁱ.
m. a leading man in his own class or family (distinguished by family descent, wealth, high position, good qualities, and learning).

(Rām. 1255) or wölmīkh m. N. of a celebrated sage (Skt. Vālmīki) the author of the Skt. Rāmâyaṇa. According to the Ksh. Rām. 1255 he was the guru, or spiritual preceptor of Janaka, Sītā's foster-father. When Sītā was banished by Rāma he gave her shelter and brought up her son Lava. He also (Rām. 1286 ff.) created for Sītā a twin brother for Lava, named Kuśa (Rām. 1255, 1544, 1699, 1732).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. wŏlāsĕñ), one who habitually wears ornaments, a well-dressed person, fop. Cf. wŏllösī.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. wōlyōv), to be of an uncertain temper, to be easily moved to anger, or to be nervous, to become agitated, perturbed; cf. wūlᵘ and wōjĕr. wōlyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wōlyē-müʦᵘ̈), one who has become of an uncertain temper, etc., as ab. (cf. El. wolyómut, drunk). wōlan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is habitually of an uncertain temper, irritable, nervous.

m. (sg. dat. wŏlaras), N. of a large lake, about thirty miles north-west of Śrīnagar, commonly known as the 'Woolar' lake (see RT.Tr. II, 423 ff.). In Sanskrit it was called the Mahāpadmasaras (El. Wular Ráza, see bel.; Śiv. 591); the word is also the name of one of the Parganas (the ancient Hōlaḍā) of the Marāz Division of Kashmīr (RT.Tr. II, 436, 460; Gr.Gr. 15, ular). ¶ wŏlar-göḍᵘ̈ f. N. of a certain fish found in the ab. lake. It is described as having a long dark-coloured body, and a red face. -hönzᵘ̈ m. (f. -hānzañ), a boatman who plies on the above lake. They are accustomed to storms, and live by fishing, collecting water-chestnuts (gôrᵘ 1), and capturing water-fowl. -rāza m. another N. of this lake. Being the largest lake in Kashmīr, it is called rāza or 'king' (El.). ¶ wŏlarukᵘ adj. gen. (f. wŏlarücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, or produced in the ab. lake.
m. (sg. dat. walatas), a string or long piece of cloth or the like, for wrapping round and round anything so as to form a covering, or for packing up as a parcel. Cf. wolyutᵘ.
m. (sg. dat. walitas), binding round, wrapping up; stuff for wrapping up, a wrapper. Cf. wolutᵘ.

m. a large earring (a smaller earring is wöjⁱ or wöjᵘ̈ 1, q.v.) (cf. kana-wᵒ, p. 448a, l. 41, but cf. kȧnⁱ-wⁱ, s.v. wôlᵘ 2) (Gr.Gr. 31, 36, 56; W. 17, vol; K. 60, 755, 770, 926, 1047); a fish-hook; angling (L. 458, wol). Cf. wöjⁱ and wôrᵘ 5. ¶ wölⁱ-baĩs m. fishing with the hook, as opposed to fishing with the net (zölⁱ-baĩs, q.v., s.v. zôlᵘ) (L. 159, wail bans). -horᵘ m. a pair of earrings (Gr.Gr. 81). wölⁱ-kan m. an ear adorned with an earring; an earring.

(f. wājĕñ, Śiv. 1882), a secondary suffix added to substantives to derive nouns implying possession or relation generally, when the thing possessed accompanies the possessor, but does not actually form part of him or it, as in dyārawôlᵘ, wealthy; lariwôlᵘ, one who possesses a house; shāyiwôlᵘ, one who possesses a place; kōriwôlᵘ, one who possesses a daughter; nĕcivⁱwôlⁱ, one who possesses a son, and so on. Exceptional are garwôlᵘ, the master of a house, as contrasted with garawôlᵘ, one who possesses a house; gupanwôlᵘ (from gupun, a quadruped), one who owns herds (cf. Gr.Gr. 136) (cf. anga-wᵒ, p. 33a, l. 48; āshi-wᵒ, p. 47b, l. 8; atha-wᵒ, p. 64b, l. 15; būda-wᵒ, p. 85a, l. 27; bāga-wᵒ, p. 90a, l. 3; banda-wᵒ, p. 110b, l. 48, and p. 111a, l. 25; bĕñĕ-wᵒ, p. 115a, l. 40; bāra-wᵒ, p. 117a, l. 14; and many others) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1029, hōshĕ-w˚; 1067, dana-w˚; 1248, wāna-w˚, etc.). ¶ It is also added to a substantive or adjective to indicate that which is characterized by the main word, as in böshᵘ̈-wᵘ̈, one who (eats only once) on the twelfth lunar day, p. 94a, l. 2; bāja-wᵒ, cessable (bāj, a cess), p. 97b, l. 25; bukᵃ̇rᵃ̇-wᵃ̇, rude (bukurᵘ, rudeness), p. 102b, l. 4; bāna-wôlᵘ, a maker of pots (bāna), p. 110a, l. 5; bāna-wôlᵘ, one who experiences (good or bad) fate (bāna), p. 110a, l. 25; bāñĕ-wôlᵘ, one who carries goods in slings (böñᵘ̈), p. 115b, l. 3; bāra-wājĕñ, a woman who deals in bāra-fruit, p. 117a, l. 46; kȧnⁱ-wⁱ, p. 452a, l. 18 (but cf. kana-wᵒ, p. 448a, l. 41); and many others (Gr.M.; L.V. 86; K. 178, phala-wājĕñ; 431, hȧstⁱ-wôlⁱ; 556, 825, 984-5, ratha-wôlᵘ; 1007, chērĕ-wôlᵘ).

(f. wājĕñ) a suffix added to an oblique form (ending in an) of the infinitive of any verb, and forming a noun of agency (see p. vi), as in karan-wôlᵘ, a doer (cf. Gr.Gr. 193) (cf. āsan-wᵒ, p. 51a, l. 4; bacan-wᵒ, p. 80b, l. 45; bēchan-wᵒ, p. 80a, l. 44; baḍan-wᵒ, p. 87a, l. 2; bŏḍan-wᵒ, p. 87a, l. 2; bögᵃran-wᵃ, p. 92b, l. 50; baharan-wᵒ, p. 96b, l. 40; bakhᵃcan-wᵃ, p. 100a, l. 33; bōlan-wᵒ, p. 106a, l. 24; and many others) (Gr.Gr. 106, 193; Gr.M.).
in wölⁱ biñ f. a pregnant female (human or other). Cf. wŏl 2.

in wŏm-kār m. the sacred syllable ōm, uttered (by Hindūs) at the beginning and end of a reading of the Vēda, or before beginning a prayer, sacred work, the alphabet, or similar passages. -kārā wŏm m. the name of the syllable ōm as uttered by children at the beginning of the recitation of the alphabet. -poṭᵘ or -pôṭᵘ m. (in teaching to write the alphabet) the first line (commencing with ōm) written by the teacher for the pupil to copy. ¶ wŏmā wō m. the word ōm as used at the beginning of the alphabet; meton. the alphabet itself (El. wamáwo).
f. (sg. dat. wŏmözᵘ̈), a foul smell, a stink (cf. dᵃha-wᵃ, p. 198a, l. 42; dᵃ̇hᵃ̇-wᵃ̇, p. 198b, l. 30; ʦara-wᵒ, p. 1078b, l. 40).
in the following:-- wŏman-horᵘ m. a pair of ladles used in sacrifices. -hȧrⁱ-lünḍⁱ f. a single one of these ladles.
m. disrespect, contempt, disregard. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. disrespect to be experienced (by some respectable person).

or wuᵒ (= امید) f. (sg. dat. wŏmīzᵘ̈), hope, expectation (cf. nā-umēd, p. 638a, l. 6; nā-wŏmēd, p. 668a, ll. 14, 16) (El. ummed; Gr.Gr. wummēd; Rām. 1515, 1627; YZ. 39, omêd). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without hope, hopeless, desperate (El.). --thavüñᵘ̈ -- or (El.) --thāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to expect, to hope (Rām. 696).
m. want of circumspection, imprudence, imprudent folly.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. wŏmözᵘ̈ladiñ), emitting a foul smell, stinking; met. one defiled by abuse, bad repute, or the like. Cf. wŏmād.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. wọ̆mᵘ, 2 p.p. wŏmyōv), exhaustion to be experienced (by being unable to complete something, e.g. a journey, a piece of writing, or a speech). wŏmyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏmyē-müʦᵘ̈), exhausted, as ab.
or womᵘ m. one who acts imprudently, imprudent, wanting in circumspection. wŏmⁱ-pöthⁱr or wȧmⁱ-pöthᵃr m. want of circumspection, acting imprudently.

m. wool (cf. wōnun 1) (K.Pr. 237, sg. obl. wunah). ¶ wōna-chath f. (sg. dat. -chüʦᵘ̈), wool-waste, the waste discarded after clearing or carding wool. -ḍī˜jᵘ̈ f. a twisted up ball of wool (after cleansing); a ball of spun wool, a ball of worsted. -ḍyū̃gᵘ m. (sg. dat. -ḍī˜gis), a similar ball, but larger in size. -kônᵘ m. the ball of worsted as ready twisted on the spinning machine. -pan m. worsted. -sᵃthᵃr m. (sg. dat. -sᵃtras), the worsted threads as arranged on the loom for weaving.

or (vill.) wŏh (q.v.) adv. now, at this time (El. woin, wúin; Gr.Gr. 156; Gr.M.; W. 94, woni; Śiv. 11, 69, 70, 72, 91, 131, 202, 335, 361, 378, 415-6, 425, 539, etc., passim; Rām. 114, 126, 161, 164, 199, 200, 271, 334, 395, 468, 490, 506, etc., passim; K. 307, 473, 587, 796, 1023; H. v, 6; vii, 26; viii, 7; YZ. 94, 230). The underlying implication of this word is that the action referred to has not previously existed, but is now begun, and, if the verb is in a future tense or in the imperative, will be carried on in future. Thus wŏñ kari implies that (he has hitherto not done it) but will now do it (so Śiv. 69, 70, 72, etc.; Rām. 202, 234, 241, 293-4, 300, 340, 475, 489, etc.; K. 89, 471). ¶ wuñ or wuñĕ adv. even now, at this very time (excluding all implication of past or future time), now (El. wunyi; Gr.Gr. 156; Gr.M.; W. wun; L.V. 99, wuñĕ; Śiv. 318, 943, wuñ; 210, 1217, 1294, 1598, wuñĕ; Rām. 146, 150, 173, 268, 361, 365, 505, 553-4, 556, etc., wuñ; 216, 289, 357, 674, 691, 1488, 1490, 1495, 1523, 1622-3, wuñĕ; K. 66, 264, 357, 363, 565, 633, wuñĕ; H. (wuñ) ii, 5; iii, 1, 2; v, 5, 6, 8; viii, 7, 10-1; ix, 4, 6; x, 5-7; xii, 6, 15, 18-9; (wuñĕ) x, 1; YZ. (woñih) 546; K.Pr. 13 (wúini)). -kĕn adv. now at present, etc., see wuñᵉ̆kĕn. ¶ wuñᵘkuy adj. (f. wuñᵘ̈cᵘ̈y), of, or belonging to, the present time, of nowadays. ¶ wuñis-tām or -tāmath adv. up to now, hitherto (in time) (W. 94, wuniuktām, for wuñukᵘ tām; K.Pr. 236, wunuktám).
or wŏnnatun conj. 3 (2 p.p. wŏnatyōv), to become lofty, to become elevated.
f. the fee paid for weaving, a weaver's wages.
f. height, loftiness, elevation, altitude (Gr.M.); stature (of a man) (Gr.M.).

m. a person's innate disposition, heart, feelings, character (El. wanda; W. 35, id.; L.V. 49, 72; Rām. 1126, 1320, 1461, 1581, 1583, 1624, 1633, 1775-7; K. 94, 536; K.Pr. 43, 253); a person's inner intention, determination, resolve (Śiv. 85, 333, 1201, 1682); imagination (Rām. 1611); mā̃gayi-wᵒ, a heartfelt prayer (K. 488). --āmotᵘ -- perf. part.
