(f. --āmüʦᵘ̈ --), (of some action or business) carried out according to one's own private intentions. -boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), of a noble character (characterized by nobility, discretion, patience, sobriety, etc.), magnanimous; cf. -sôwᵘ, bel. --bāwun -- m.inf. to display (to another) one's inner intentions or feeling; cf. wŏndukᵘ bāᵒ, bel. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to enquire into, or test, another's intentions or feelings; cf. --shāh hyonᵘ, and wŏndas hyonᵘ, bel. -khŏsh adj. c.g. cheerful, happy, comfortable (El.). -khŏsh karun, m.inf. to comfort (El.). -kumolᵘ, adj. (f. -kumüjᵘ̈), gentle (El. wandakumal). -môrᵘ adj. (f. -mörᵘ̈), one whose intentions or secret thoughts are hidden, one who keeps his intentions to himself. -narm adj. c.g. kind (El.). --phoṭᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --phüṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), born from one's inner self, etc., as in the next. --phaṭun -- m.inf. the heart to be broken (YZ. 150); disease of the heart to be experienced; to germinate from one's own inner self, (of a cock-and-bull story) to be produced from one's own imagination; met. (of a child) to be begotten from one's own loins. -prasand adj. c.g. glad, joyful. -prasand karun m.inf. to gladden (El.). -prasand sapadun m.inf. to rejoice, be glad (El.). --rūdᵘ-motᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --rūzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ --), disgusted (El.); cf. wŏndas rōzun, bel. --shāhhyonᵘ -- m.inf. to test or pry into another's intentions or inner thoughts; cf. --hyonᵘ, ab. -sôwᵘ adj. (f. -sövᵘ̈), noble-minded, magnanimous; cf. -boḍᵘ, ab. --wuchun -- m.inf. to watch for, or test, a person's intention. --yunᵘ --  m.inf. one's private intentions to be carried out; agreement (with one's own intentions, or opinions) to be reached. ¶ wŏndukᵘ  adj. gen. (f. wŏndücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, one's heart, feelings, or character (Rām. 72, 674, 1088, 1127, 1267, 1492, 1559, 1572, 1635, 1763, 1775); of, or belonging to, one's own private intentions; secret, private, mysterious. --bāwun -- m.inf. to display one's own secret intentions. Cf. wŏnda bāᵒ, ab. ¶ wŏndas hyonᵘ m.inf. to conceal in one's own heart, to bear or endure silently (grief, trouble, wrongs, or the like); cf. wŏnda hᵒ, ab. --raṭun -- m.inf. to keep as a secret, to keep to oneself (some scandal, secret, wicked action, or the like). --rōzun -- m.inf. (some scandal, secret, etc., as in the preceding) to remain hidden in the mind, to remain untold (by one who knows); cf. wŏnda rūdᵘ-motᵘ, ab. --thawun -- m.inf. to hide in the heart, to keep (some story or fact) to oneself (as a secret not to be revealed) (Rām. 1773 thāwun).
adj. (f. vünzᵘ̈), (1 p.p. of wandun, q.v.), offered as a victim, dedicated to sacrifice, made an offering to a god.

adj. (f. vünjᵘ̈, sg. dat. wanjĕ), lame, crippled, halt (due to misshapen legs); crippled (in regard to some other limb, e.g. the hand) (Gr.M.). Cf. vünḍᵘ̈ (of which the sg. dat. is also wanjĕ) and vyongᵘ.
f. the profession of a shopkeeper (wôñᵘ 2), shop selling, shopkeeping as a livelihood (cf. puy-wᵒ, p. 813a, l. 15).
a suffix, indicating possession, forming abstract nouns from adjectives ending in wān 2, as in bögi-wönī, possession of good fortune, prosperity, p. 91a, l. 3.
f. the business of a shopkeeper (esp. of a grocer) (cf. nūna-wᵒ, p. 641a, l. 36; puy-wᵒ, p. 813a, l. 17).
or adj. c.g. mad, furious (El. wanmat, Śiv. 1649); (as subst. m.) a madman (El.).

or wōnöjᵘ̈ f. the windpipe and gullet, i.q. ōh-nöjᵘ̈, p. 18a, l. 12, q.v. wōnöjin gaʦhun m.inf. (of food) to go the wrong way (when eating) (i.q. ōh-nöjᵘ̈n gaʦhun, p. 18a, l. 16, q.v.); hence, met., to suffer distress, have a bad time.
(sg. dat. wōnanas), a kind of short wool, cf. wōn; the woof (in weaving) (K.Pr. 249).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wūnᵘ; f. wūñᵘ̈, sg. dat. wōñĕ; 2 p.p. wōñōv), to weave (cf. wagȧvⁱ-wōnanwôlⁱ, p. 1103a, l. 37) (Gr.Gr. 20, 22; Gr.M.; L. wanun; W. 7; Rām. 1781). wūnᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wūñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), woven.
adj. (f. wŏnüʦᵘ̈), raised, elevated; high (lit. and fig.), tall, lofty, eminent (El. wanut).

(for 2, see wanun) m. a thing said (cf. wanun); hence, understanding, knowledge after experience (Śiv. 1192); a message (H. xi, 20). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to meditate upon, reflect upon, take into consideration, contemplate (something wanted or to be tested) (Śiv. 1207, 1423); to send a message (H. xi, 20); cf. wȧnⁱ dinⁱ, bel. --rōzun -- m.inf. to be remembered (of something once seen), to be recognized. --thawun -- m.inf. to show and explain something, or someone, to another, in order that he may recognize it when he again comes across it, to bring under notice, call attention to. ¶ wȧnⁱ dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to think about, give consideration to, dwell upon, search for (something hidden, or now perceived after long non-observance) (Śiv. 251, 439, 810, 1052, 1183, 1327, 1595, 1666, 1681; Rām. 249, 439, 1715, 1766). Cf. wonᵘ dyunᵘ, ab. ¶ wani kaḍun m.inf. to gain thorough experience (of something), to recognize (as such-and-such) (p. 386 a, l. 18) (Śiv. 950). --rōzun -- m.inf. (of something only once seen) to continue in a state of recognition, to be thoroughly remembered. --thawun -- m.inf. to impress (something shown once) on a person's memory. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come into cognition, to be recognized (as such-and-such) (Śiv. 1011, 1038, 1106-7, 1343, 1669, 1878, 1892).

m. the form which pôñᵘ, water, takes when it is the second member of a compound word. See p. 746b, ll. 37 ff. Numerous examples are there given, and the following are here given in addition:--gölin-wᵒ, p. 285b, l. 36; mȧtⁱ-wⁱ, p. 602a, l. 50; pāñĕ-wᵒ, p. 748a, l. 46; rasᵃri-wᵃ, p. 844a, l. 40; sābüñᵘ̈-wᵘ̈, p. 862b, l. 5; shĕkar-wᵒ, p. 878b, l. 44; shīna-wᵒ, p. 885a, l. 18; shrāna-wᵒ, p. 893b, l. 39; shrōʦi-wᵒ, p. 896a, l. 43; shō̃ṭh-wᵒ, p. 899b, l. 37; sĕki-wᵒ, p. 905a, l. 16; sĕnda-wᵒ, p. 918b, l. 28; sᵃsari-wᵃ, p. 942a, l. 17; sō̃ta-wᵒ, p. 947a, l. 7; siwan-wᵒ, p. 954a, l. 31; tata-wᵒ, p. 1039b, l. 31; ʦhĕṭⁱ-wⁱ, p. 1066b, l. 7; ʦitra-wᵒ, p. 1087a, l. 46; wuga-wᵒ, p. 1101b, l. 15; wȧjⁱ-wⁱ, p. 1107a, l. 18; wanda-wᵒ, p. 1122b, l. 28; vĕtha-wᵒ, s.v. vĕth; waṭakh-wᵒ, s.v. waṭukh) (W. 115, wonⁱ). ¶ wã̄ 1 (for 2, see wôñᵘ 2, for 3, see s.v.). We have seen above that pôñᵘ becomes wôñᵘ when the second member of a compound word. As explained on p. 746b, ll. 35 ff. when pôñᵘ is the first member of a compound word, it becomes pã̄, as in pã̄-aṭh, a water-flood, and numerous other examples given on p. 747a, ll. 25 ff. There remains the case when pôñᵘ is not only the second member of a compound word, but is followed by a third member,--when in fact it falls in the middle of a compound word. In such case it becomes wã̄ 1. Examples are kȧnḍⁱ-wã̄-ḍulⁱ, a cauldron-water-cistern, i.e. a vat for storing water for cooking purposes, p. 455a, l. 4; kȧnḍⁱ-wã̄-manḍulⁱ, pot-water-scouring, i.e. scouring out a pot with water, p. 455a, l. 7; ʦhĕṭⁱ-wã̄-ḍulⁱ, a tub for dirtied water, p. 1066b, l. 3.

f. ploughing, cultivation by plough. ¶ wāñĕ-dã̄d m. a plough-bullock. -drāv m. one who has come out of ploughing, a bullock that has been trained to plough. --kaḍun -- m.inf. to train a bullock to the plough. --lagun -- m.inf. to become attached to ploughing, (of a bullock) to be taken to the plough (before he is trained); met. (of some weak or incapable person) to be set to some hard piece of work. --lāgun --  m.inf. to put a bullock to the plough (for the first time, as ab.); met. to set an incapable person to hard work, as ab. --nērun -- m.inf. (of a bullock) to become trained to the plough.

a suffix forming nouns of agency or possession, as in pruthi-wônᵘ, p. 770a, l. 35; shūba-wônᵘ, p. 896a, l. 38; shruta-wônᵘ, p. 896a, l. 14. So also (L.V. 26) brama-wônᵘ, a wanderer. All the other examples also come from L.V. Cf. wān 2.

m. (sg. abl. wāñi. When this word is the first or middle member of a compound word it generally takes the form wã̄ 2 (Gr.Gr. 74); for wã̄ 1, see wôñᵘ 1, for 3, see s.v. For examples, see bel. The fem. of this word is wāñĕñ, q.v.) a shopkeeper (cf. wān 1), trader, merchant (cf. ashĕd-wᵒ, p. 48b, l. 17; bọ̆ngᵃri-wᵃ, p. 113a, l. 45; burza-wᵒ, p. 131a, l. 7; bŏṭa-wᵒ, p. 138b, l. 44; kapar-wᵒ, p. 463b, l. 49; mŏkhta-wᵒ, p. 561a, l. 19; nūna-wᵒ, p. 641a, l. 35; pȧṭⁱ-wⁱ, p. 789b, l. 37; puy-wᵒ, p. 813a, l. 5; tīla-wôñᵘ, p. 999a, l. 24; tŏmla-wᵒ, p. 1006b, l. 34; trạngᵃri-wᵃ, p. 1028b, l. 3. Although the idea of 'shopkeeper' or 'seller' is always present in the above, these compounds often also include the idea of 'manufacturer, who sells his products'. Thus, tīla-wôñᵘ is not only an 'oil-seller', but also a man who prepares oil for sale) (El. wányi, wŏiṅ, an oilman, shopkeeper; Gr.Gr. 38, 74; L. 387, 464, wáni; W. 136, wonⁱ; Śiv. 240, 1876; YZ. 67; K.Pr. 20, 31 (waṅi), 154, 228-9); ¶ met. a decent respectable man (of a quiet, self-restrained, and patient character). wôñᵘ wāñurᵘ m. a man whose profession is shopkeeping, esp. a seller of such articles as oils, spices, or the like, a grocer. ¶ wã̄ 2. Examples of this word used as the first member of a compound word are:-- wã̄-burza m. shopkeeper's birch-bark, birch-bark used for paper, as sold in shops, a superior kind of birch-bark, smooth, clean, and wide, suitable for wrapping up parcels; cf. burza-wôñᵘ, p. 131a, l. 7. -chān m. a head carpenter, the foreman carpenter (or architect-builder) employed in building a house. -dyolᵘ m. a kind of grass used by shopkeepers for tying up parcels of condiments or the like; cf. wāna-dĕlⁱ, p. 1121a, l. 1. -ganḍ m. the tying up of a load or parcel, when it is securely done. -pacĕ m. one who is born in a family whose occupation is shopkeeping; one who is of decent respectable family (in this sense used esp. in discussing proposals of marriage or the like). -phuṭȧjⁱ or -phuṭüjᵘ̈ f. a shopkeeper's parcel, a parcel wrapped up in birch-bark, or the like, as delivered to a customer by a shopkeeper; met. a similar unopened parcel. -tônᵘ m. (in reference to some particular person) decent, respectable character (in all dealings). -ṭaṭhulᵘ m. a tub or trough in which a shopkeeper stores for sale his supply of flour or the like. ¶ Examples of wã̄ used as the middle member of a compound word are:-- tīla-wã̄-dã̄d, an oilman's bullock, p. 999a, l. 22; tīla-wã̄-kanz, his oil-press, id., l. 23; tīla-wã̄-ʦakh, the revolving bar of his press, id., l. 31. ¶ wāñe-wôñᵘ m. a decent, respectable man, as ab. ¶ wöñⁱ-dān m. 'a shopkeeper's fireplace'; hence, met. a miserly or very indigent form of living. -wān m. a shopkeeper's (esp. a grocer's) shop. -yār m., id.
f. the feminine of wān 3 and wôñᵘ 3, indicating a female keeper, etc., and not his wife, as in guzar-wöñᵘ̈ a female octroi collector (not his wife), p. 319b, l. 1.
(f. wöñᵘ̈ 3), inḍīḍⁱ-wôñⁱ or ḍīḍⁱ- waacr;n, a doorkeeper, p. 188a, l. 21, i.q. wān 3, and probably due to confusion with wôñᵘ 2. Like that word, it has also a f. wāñĕñ, p. 188a, l. 24.

the obl. form and pl. nom. of wān 4. Also i.q. wān 4, in lĕla-wöñᵘ̈, p. 522b, l. 2; lila- wöñᵘ̈, ib., l. 8; and sŏwöñᵘ̈, s.v. In Rām. 429, wöñī is for wöñᵘ̈, m.c. In K. 522 wöñᵘ̈ pālüñᵘ̈ means 'to keep one's word, to keep a promise'.
f. earnings, in pĕṭhⁱ-wⁱ, p. 796a, l. 8. Cf. wöñī 1.
in pathȧrⁱ-wöñⁱ, adv. on, or all over, the floor or bare ground, p. 799a, l. 10. ? Cf. wã̄ 3.
in wöñᵘ̈-döñᵘ̈ f. (of one reduced to poverty) the small broken or worn articles of jewelry that remain in his possession (probably a jingle of döñᵘ̈, q.v.).
or vüñᵘ̈ 3, an adjectival suffix, c.g., as in wŏphar-wöñⁱ, wŏphar-vüñᵘ̈, s.v. wŏphurᵘ, q.v.
f. (sg. dat. wŏpüzᵘ̈), birth; creation, production; origin, rise.

or wŏpād f. (sg. dat. wŏpüzᵘ̈ or wŏpözᵘ̈), a personal defect (such as disease, debauchery, making false charges, or other criminality) which is contagious, or which infests others by association (Śiv. 1441, 1746, 1764). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a defect to taint or contaminate (a person, dat.).
n.ag. (f. wŏpadāwavüñᵘ̈), one who causes (something) to come into existence (Śiv. 854).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏpadôwᵘ), to cause to spring up or come into existence, to bring into existence, be the producer of, to create (El. wopúdáwun, who says the word is peculiar to remote mountain districts; Śiv. 33, 59, 60, 99, 100, 582, 803, 1241; K. 131, 618); to cause to occur or happen. Cf. wŏpazāwun.
m. instruction, advice (Gr.M., Śiv. 23, Rām. 1171); esp. true instruction, right teaching (L.V. 1, 2, 51-4, 66, 80, wŏpadēsh; Śiv. 1704; Rām. 41, 171).
m. widespread misfortune, a general calamity (such as famine, lawlessness, drought, floods, epidemic, pillage, conflagrations, etc.), national distress, national disturbance, insurrection.
adj. c.g. (any man or beast) that causes such widespread calamity as in the preceding.

or (q.v.) wŏpazun conj. 2 (1 p.p. wŏpodᵘ; f. wŏpüzᵘ̈), to arise, spring up, come into existence, be born, come into being, be produced (Gr.M.; L.V. 56; Śiv. 1230, 1559; K. 878); to occur, take place; cf. wŏpanun, wŏpazun. wŏpodᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏpüzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), sprung up, come into existence; occurred, happened. Cf. wŏpüzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, f. of wŏpozᵘ-motᵘ, s.v. wŏpazun.
f. a certain wild shrub, the long dagger-shaped sub-acid leaves of which are used as a vegetable. Cf. wŏpal-hākh, s.v. wŏpal.
m. a kindly action, benefit, assistance, help (Gr.M.; Śiv. 236; K. 578, 1120; K.Pr. 219). sarwa-wŏᵒ adj. c.g. one who grants help or benefits to all (Śiv. 4, 39; K. sarŏ wŏ˚, 2, 21, etc.).
adj. c.g. helping, serving, kindly (cf. par-wᵒ, p. 751a, l. 27) (Śiv. 587, 1051). sarwa-wŏᵒ adj. c.g. one who grants help or benefits to all (Śiv. 194, 1510, 1886).

(cf. wŏpȧjⁱ), in the following:-- wŏpal bāṻ m. the name used in schools for the Śāradā character corresponding to the Nāgarī letter ū. -gŏndi-wāv m. 'the wind of a wŏpal-posy', i.e. a very slight impediment, a mere nothing of an impediment (cf. the next). -hākh (sg. dat. -hākas), a certain wild vegetable leaf (eaten on the occasion of an obsequial fast or the like) (L. 347, Dipsacus inermis; Rām. 766, 1283). --wō -- m. the name used in schools for the Śāradā character corresponding to the Nāgarī letter u.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. wŏponᵘ, f. wŏpüñᵘ̈), to arise, spring up, come into existence, be born; to occur, take place; cf. wŏpadun, wŏpazun. wŏponᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏpüñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), sprung up, born; occurred.

adj. c.g. another (H. v, 4, kus-tāñ wŏ˚, someone else); other, different, alien (Rām. 732); not one's own, others' (Śiv. 341, 624, 1172, 1862); jealous (El.); (as subst. m.) a foreigner, stranger (El.; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 119, 236). --bĕha -- m. an alien residence (e.g. among strangers or people of a different caste). --gạnzᵃrun -- m.inf. to look upon or consider (someone, esp. one of one's own kin) as alien. -ʦŏpar adj. c.g. other, different, alien (or something of the sort). (A jingle.)
m. help, assistance, kindness, favour (shown to a person).
f. alienness, the condition of being foreign or alien (e.g. belonging to a different caste).

m. not getting food, not eating food, fasting, famishment, starvation (W. 111). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to fast, abstain from food (owing to obstinacy, parsimony, or the like, and even when food is available). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. famishment, as ab., to occur. -röchⁱ c.g. something which relieves famishment (such as a little fruit, a scrap of bread, etc.).
f. service, attention, attendance, waiting on; adoration, worship (Śiv. 1620, 1655).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. wŏpasladiñ), hungry, famishing, starving (W. 111, K.Pr. 236).
f. (sg. dat. wŏpüʦᵘ̈), profuse production, great fruitfulness, great fecundity, pullulation.
m. one who fasts (as a religious discipline).
f. a certain shrub, the juice and leaves of which are used for healing wounds or the like.

m. a means, expedient (Śiv. 17, 42, 110, 1242, 1299, 1472, 1478, 1488, 1743; Rām. 475; K. 576, 875, 1019); mode, way, device (for doing something) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1516; Rām. 300, 1767); a remedy, cure (El. wapáí, wŏpáí f.; wapáí karinyi, to cure) (Śiv. 1758).
f. (sg. dat. wŏpazüʦᵘ̈), coming into existence, birth, springing up (Gr.Gr. 128).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏpazôwᵘ) to cause to spring up or come into existence, to bring into existence, to be the producer of (Gr.Gr. 171); to cause to occur, to cause to happen. Cf. wŏpadāwun.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. wŏpozᵘ), to arise, spring up, come into existence, be born, become (Gr.Gr. 28, 128, 171, 204, 212; YZ. 397); to occur, take place; cf. wŏpadun, wŏpanun. wŏpozᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏpüzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), sprung up, come into existence; occurred, happened. wŏpüzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ is also f. of wŏpodᵘ-motᵘ, q.v. s.v. wŏpadun.
f. in hūnⁱ-wŏph, p. 337a, l. 23, i.q. wuph, q.v.

m. the making a livelihood by begging food and clothing from others, professional begging; a professional beggar; cf. wapha. -bata m. rice obtained in this way; hence, plenty of food obtained regularly from others. -bata lagun m.inf. such food to be obtained, to become fat on the obtainment of easy and regular food from others, and hence to become audacious and insolent. -bata pyonᵘ m.inf. such rice to fall to a person, i.e. food in plenty to be regularly received from others. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. the proceeds of begging to fall (to a person), i.e. to get a living by professional begging (and so to be comfortable, happy, without care, audacious and insolent).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏpharôwᵘ), to loosen the foundations of anything, make loose (lit. and fig., as in wŏpharun, q.v.).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. wŏpharyōv) (of some stone, column, brick) to become loose in its position (e.g. by pulling or by digging round the base, etc.); similarly, fig. of a secret, a disease, a bad habit, or the like. wŏpharyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏpharyē-müʦᵘ̈), loosened, as ab.
(for وافر) adj. c.g. abundant, plentiful, copious (H. vi, 14).

adj. (f. wŏphürᵘ̈), loose, insecure, not firmly fixed. --lagun -- m.inf. to become loose, to become insecure in its place, to have (its) foundations loosened (lit. and fig.). ¶ wŏphar-ḍünjᵘ̈ f. looseness, instability (of something that should be firmly fixed, e.g. a stone in a wall, or pillar); cf. ḍünḍᵘ̈ and wŏphara-ḍanjĕ, bel. -wāl adj. c.g. unsteady-minded, (of one engaged in any duty) not persevering, one whose attention is readily distracted, unsteadfast, capricious; cf. wuphal-wāl, p. 1130b, l. 49, and wŏpharun. -wöñⁱ adj. c.g. not firmly fixed in its place, insecure. -vüñᵘ̈ adj. c.g. not having a secure foundation, fixed to something insecure. ¶ wŏphara-ḍanjĕ adj. c.g. not firmly fixed in its seat or foundation, loose, unsteady. Cf. wŏphar-ḍünjᵘ̈, ab.
adj. c.g. (as subst., wŏpözᵘ̈ladiñ), possessing a defect (as described s.v. wŏpad or wŏpād, q.v.).

m. a kind of long heavy oar, used for propelling large heavy boats in turning them, or against wind or stream. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to ply such a heavy oar (which requires considerable force). --wāyun -- m.inf., id.

adj. c.g. 'step' (cf. ōr 2), i.e. of, or belonging to, a stepmother or stepfather (K.Pr. 203). Used in the following:-- wōra-bab m. a stepfather, i.e. a mother's second husband. -bĕñĕ  f. a stepsister. -bāpār m. the conduct or attitude of a stepmother to her stepchildren, or of stepchildren to their stepmother. -bôyᵘ m. a stepbrother (YZ. 84, 97-8, 103, 138, 452) (so wōra-bāpathᵃr, the son of a stepbrother; wōra-bāpath- nŏsh, his (the son's) wife; wōra-bāwᵃza, the daughter of a stepbrother; and wōra-bȧyⁱ-kākañ, the wife of a stepbrother). -dorᵘ m. the relations or family of a co-wife (from the point of view of the other wife); the relations or family of a stepmother (from the point of view of the stepson). -dyārath-nŏsh f. the daughter-in-law of a husband's stepbrother, the wife of a husband's stepbrother's son. -dyārathᵃr m. the son of a husband's stepbrother. -dyārᵃza f. the daughter of a husband's stepbrother. -dryuyᵘ m. a woman's husband's stepbrother. -gọ̆bur m. (sg. dat. gọ̆bᵃras), the son of a co-wife, a stepson (esp. when beloved) (K.Pr. 236, wurah-g˚); (in the case of a woman who has married a second time, from the point of the second husband) her son by her first marriage, a man's stepson (esp. when beloved); cf. -nĕcyuwᵘ, bel. -hahar m. a wife's stepbrother. -hash f. the co-wife of a mother-in-law. -kūrᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kōrĕ), the daughter of a co-wife, a woman's stepdaughter; a daughter by a husband's first wife (El. wara-k˚). -möjᵘ̈ f. a stepmother (H. viii, 1, 11; K.Pr. 181, wurah-m˚). -môlᵘ m. the father of a co-wife (K.Pr. 144, worah-m˚; 236, wurah-m˚). -mālyunᵘ m. the original home of a woman's mother-in-law's co-wife, i.e. of a husband's stepmother. -mātāmāl m. the original home of a stepmother, i.e. the home of a stepmother's father. -nĕcyuwᵘ a stepson (i.e. the son of a co-wife, or the son of a wife by her former marriage) (cf. -gọ̆bur, ab.) (H. viii, 3). -nŏsh f. the wife of a woman's stepson, a stepdaughter-in-law. -pĕcĕñ f. the wife of a father's step-brother, a step-aunt. -pokhᵘ m. the family or relations of a stepmother. -pakhy adj. c.g. of, or belonging to, the relations or family of a stepmother (e.g. those members who should be invited to a festivity, or their profession, etc.). -pẹ̆tᵃr or pẹ̆thᵃr m. a father's stepbrother, a step-uncle on the father's side. -rag f. the consanguinity or kindred between step-relations, step-relationship (as affecting funeral rites or the like). -rᵃsh f. the mutual enmity between stepbrothers or between their descendants. --zām -- f. (sg. dat. zömᵘ̈ or (among Paṇḍits) -zōmᵘ̈), a stepsister-in-law, the stepsister of a woman's husband. (So wōra- zömith-nŏsh, the daughter-in-law of a husband's stepsister; wōra-zömiyĕ, the husband of a husband's stepsister; wōra-zömiza, the daughter of a husband's stepsister.) -zāmaturᵘ m. the son-in-law of a co-wife, a co-wife's daughter's husband.
adj. c.g. born of a woman who has married a second time.

f. the condition and conduct of either of the spouses or of both of them, in the case of a woman having been married a second time. This state of affairs is condemned among high-caste Hindūs, is looked upon as disgraceful, and involves expulsion from caste.
or m. absence of worldly desires or passions, indifference to the world, asceticism (Śiv. 587, 735, 1268, 1532, 1573, 1744, 1753, 1797, 1803, 1829; Rām. 37).
f. (sg. dat. wōrüʦᵘ̈), a cloth or other covering of the body or part of the body, etc. (cf. mȧṭⁱ-wⁱ, p. 603a, l. 15; sạtᵃra-wᵃ, p. 948b, l. 9). Cf. wurun 2.
f. a general chorus of barking (by dogs) (as when they are warning against some calamity about to happen, or giving warning about thieves).

n.ag. (f. wōravüñᵘ̈), a barker, a dog which is given to barking; (a human being) who prates, chatters, jabbers; one who keeps on wailing without cessation (in order to obtain some thing or attain some object). --rōzun -- m.inf. to keep on wailing or talking (in the hope of obtaining some thing, or attaining some object). --thawun -- m.inf. to set a person wailing (at the disappointment of his hopes) or speaking incoherently (by more than satisfying his hopes).
f. the barking of a dog (cf. hūnⁱ-wⁱ, p. 337a, l. 25); a similar sound made by a human being.
m. (f. wŏrdüchᵘ̈), a child of adultery, an illegitimate child.
(? gend.) an incident, occurrence; a catastrophe (H. xii, 19).

m. an awl or needle for piercing leather for embroidery; patterned embroidery on leather or the like (sewn on the leather through holes previously made with the above awl). -gorᵘ m. one who does such embroidery, an embroiderer on leather. --tārun -- m.inf. to sew such embroidery.
or m. one who has abandoned all worldly passions or desires (Śiv. 1507, 1523; Rām. 352).

m. a certain Moslem religious ceremony celebrating the union of the soul of a deceased with the Supreme Spirit (cf. urs nabi in L. 268); met. (sarcastically) a competition in telling lying stories, practised on certain occasions by dyers (cf. rangᵃ̇rᵃ̇-wᵃ̇, p. 838a, l. 35) (K.Pr. 177).
(also written wörshyunᵘ) or wörⁱshunⁱ adj. (f. wörshiñᵘ̈ (also written) or wörⁱshüñⁱ) of, or belonging to, the past year, one year old (cf. okᵘ-wörshiñ, p. 19b, l. 9) (Gr.Gr. 148, wörshyunᵘ).
m. a man who is in a permanent post or situation (as distinct from one in temporary service). Cf. wôrᵘ 1.

m. (sg. ag. wŏrȧdⁱ 2, for 1, see s.v.), the second husband of a woman who has married twice (Gr.Gr. 37, K.Pr. 191); cf. wŏrᵘ̈zᵘ̈. --karun -- m.inf. to take a second husband. ¶ wŏrȧdⁱ-bāpār m. (when a woman has married a second time) the mutual relations of the spouses, and their general conduct (esp. in regard to religious duties). -gāth m. (sg. dat. -gātas), the disgrace to a family in which a female member has contracted a second marriage. -küṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kacĕ), a daughter of a woman who has contracted a second marriage. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. kaṭas), the son of such a woman. -nēthᵃr m. the marriage rite joining a man to a woman who is taking him as a second husband. -pöthᵃr m. the conduct (esp. in regard to religious duties) of one or other of the spouses of such a marriage; similar conduct by another person not so married.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wūrᵘ. This verb is impers. in the tenses formed from the p.p.) to bark (as a dog) (Gr.M.; K.Pr. 84, 171); to talk disconnectedly in one's sleep, to babble or utter inarticulate sounds in a fit of insensibility; to talk inarticulately, utter words without sense; prate, chatter, jabber, make inarticulate noises, howl (Gr.M.; K. 907, 1051). ¶ wūrⁱ wūrⁱ wŏthun m.inf. (whenever remembrance of some former terror, pain, injury, or the like recurs) the terror, etc., to be experienced afresh over and over again. ¶ wōran-gāth m. (sg. dat. -gātas), shameful, abusive, or unworthy speech; (of anything inanimate) worthless, uncommendable, useless. -gāṭh m. (sg. dat. gāṭhas) or adj. c.g. (of speech, esp. where public) shameful, abusive, improper; (of something inanimate) worthless, useless.

m. (sg. dat. wörivis), a husband's father's house, the home of a woman's father-in-law (cf. baḍa-wᵒ, p. 82b, ll. 32, 35) (L. 458, wáreo; H. x, 3, where the vocabulary wrongly refers it to a man's father-in-law's house); pl. (wörivⁱ) the people of this house, a husband's relations (Rām. 1620). ¶ wörivⁱ-böʦⁱ m. a relation in the house of a husband's father (such as her husband's brother, that brother's wife, or the husband's sister). -dorᵘ m. a woman's husband's relations (spoken of as a whole group of people). -krônᵘ m., id. ¶ wörⁱvyukⁱ adj. gen. (f. wörⁱvicⁱ), of, or belonging to, a husband's family (Śiv. 1233, Rām. 764).

(for 2, see warun) m. a kind of spiced cake (cf. batās-wᵒ, p. 145b, l. 15; kö̃kañĕ-wᵒ, p. 431b, l. 41; kulicĕ-wᵒ, p. 439a, l. 27; kö̆mᵘ̈-wᵘ̈, p. 443b, l. 21; krȧʦhⁱ-wⁱ, p. 478a, l. 33; mahā-wᵒ, p. 553a, l. 15; makāyi-wᵒ, p. 563b, l. 11; mŏnga-wᵒ, p. 578b, l. 39; maʦhi-wᵒ, p. 609b, l. 6; pakhyāg-wᵒ, p. 727b, l. 41; pạtrakh-wᵒ, p. 804b, l. 13; shō̃ṭh-wᵒ, p. 899b, l. 40; tēl-wᵒ, p. 998a, l. 12; tọ̆mᵃla-wᵃ, p. 1006b, l. 35; ʦŏcĕ-wᵒ, p. 1085b, ll. 25 ff.; yāji-wᵒ, s.v. yöjᵘ̈) (Gr.M.). Cf. vürᵘ̈ 1. ¶ wȧrⁱ-babar m.pl. the whole collection of small cakes, etc., of various kinds prepared for a religious offering. -pojᵘ m. (f. -püjᵘ̈) (on the occasion of a marriage) the person employed to carry a large basket (püjᵘ̈) filled with varieties of spiced cakes from the bridegroom's people to the house of the bride's father. He precedes the bridegroom's procession. -püjᵘ̈  f. the ab. mentioned large basket. -rôchᵘ (at a marriage, among all the other cakes) one very large (thick and wide) cake of special shape (like our wedding-cake).

m. the being firmly fixed in position, fixed dwelling, the having a permanent residence, the having a permanent post (cf. wā̃gȧjⁱ-wⁱ, p. 1101b, l. 31; wȧjⁱ-wⁱ, p. 1107a, l. 20; wŏka-wᵒ, p. 1108a, l. 15; wŏṭa-wᵒ, s.v. wŏṭh). --karun -- m.inf. to adopt some position or residence permanently.

m. an earthenware jar or pot (the m. form of this word is wôrᵘ 2, q.v.) (cf. dŏda-wᵒ, p. 190b, l. 6; diwạta-wᵒ or diwaʦa-wᵒ, p. 265a, l. 41; dŏyĕn-wᵒ, p. 269b, l. 49; graka-wᵒ, p. 301b, l. 44; guras-wᵒ, p. 304a, l. 7; kalashĕ-wᵒ, p. 441a, l. 49; kŏlaʦh-wᵒ, p. 441b, l. 19; mīli-wᵒ, p. 566a, l. 4; mila-wᵒ or milᵃri-wᵃ, p. 569a, l. 41; macĕ-wᵒ, p. 603b, l. 5; namūna-wᵒ, p. 638a, l. 47; phira-wᵒ, p. 702a, ll. 22 ff.; parmāna-wᵒ, p. 760a, l. 34; ranga-wᵒ, p. 837a, l. 49; tīla-wᵒ, p. 999a, l. 29; tumba-wᵒ, p. 1005b, l. 3; ʦȧrⁱ-wⁱ, pp. 738b, l. 50; 769b, l. 37; 891a, l. 37, and 1080a, l. 3; wahᵃra-wᵃ, p. 1105a, l. 17; zūgⁱ-wⁱ) (El. wãr; W. 13, vör; K. 425, wörāh, with suff. of indef. art.; H. xi, 13). ¶ wāri-dān m. a kind of cooking-stove (dān), for preparing oblations for several deities at the same ceremony. (It has several openings, for several pots, each for cooking a separate oblation.) -kronḍᵘ m. a kind of ladle with a deep cup and a long handle, used for ladling oil in cooking. -tīl m. oil in a jar kept ready for constant use near a cooking-stove (as distinct from the main store of oil kept elsewhere).
adj. having (so many) twists or folds (cf. wār 2), used --˚, as in okᵘ-wôrᵘ (p. 19b, l. 5); okᵘ-wāri okᵘ-wāri (id., l. 7); shĕ-wôrᵘ (p. 874a, l. 30).

m. a jar, bucket (the m. form of wörᵘ̈ 1, q.v.), used --˚, as in mȧṭⁱ-wⁱ, p. 603a, l. 13; naṭa-wᵒ, p. 663a, l. 38; saga-wᵒ, p. 867a, l. 7; tōla-wᵒ, p. 999b, l. 30; tumba-wᵒ, p. 1005b, l. 1; ṭinḍa-wᵒ, p. 1009b, l. 11; ʦaḍa-wᵒ, p. 1054a, l. 3); (Śiv. 1368, wārĕ for wāri, m.c.; 1502 wörīyĕ for wörⁱ, m.c.); a kind of covered box or receptacle, used --˚ (cf. worᵘ 3), as in kranḍa-wᵒ, p. 474a, l. 21.

f. a plot of ground near a house, a garden (the m. form of this word is wôrᵘ 3, q.v.) (cf. ala-wᵒ, p. 22b, l. 43; ārᵃm-wᵃ, p. 43b, l. 33; gŏgᵃji-wᵃ, p. 279a, l. 36; ganḍa-wᵒ, p. 289b, l. 20; khŏḍa-wᵒ, p. 392b, l. 30; kŏng-wᵒ, p. 456b, l. 32; maĩshĕr-wᵒ, p. 598b, l. 2; pīra-wᵒ, p. 753a, l. 15; pōshĕ-wᵒ, p. 779a, l. 42; potᵘ wᵒ, p. 788b, l. 26; rǖnⁱ-wⁱ or rǖnⁱ-wôrⁱ, p. 835b, l. 40) (El. wãr, m. and f., or, towards Islāmābād, wãḍ, m.; Gr.Gr. 13, 72, 161; L.V. 63; Śiv. 132, 255, 1028, 1363, 1782; H. v, 7). ¶ wāri-gŏgᵃ̇jᵃ̇ or -gŏgᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a garden turnip (i.e. one which is well-flavoured, etc., and carefully cultivated in a garden). -hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), green-vegetables grown in a garden close to the house. -muṭhᵘ m. garden pulse (Phaseolus). -wasath f. (sg. dat. -wasüʦᵘ̈), 'a garden-home', a home in which religious duties are carried out and from which many descendants come; hence, a family containing a virtuous wife and daughter-in-law; met. the complete and satisfactory accomplishment of any work; the becoming well-established in any position (? cf. wāra).
in sȧnzⁱ-worⁱ, a certain large box for holding smaller caskets, p. 924a, l. 35, q.v. Cf. wôrᵘ 2 and vürᵘ̈ 2.

m. an enclosed space, garden (m. form of wörᵘ̈ 2, q.v.) used --˚ as in rǖnⁱ-wôrⁱ or -wörᵘ̈, N. of a place (p. 835b, l. 40), sȧñⁱ-wôrⁱ (p. 918a, l. 31); a place where cattle, etc., congregate, a fold, cattle-yard (cf. dā̃da-wᵒ, p. 187b, l. 28; tīr-wᵒ, p. 1018b, l. 40).
f. a kind of boat, a sort of small barge (cf. ḍakha-wᵒ, p. 205b, l. 5; dā̃-wᵒ, p. 231a, l. 20; gāḍa-wᵒ, p. 276b, l. 33; ʦhaṭa-wᵒ, p. 1062b, l. 26; ʦāka-wᵒ, p. 1068a, l. 31) (L. 313, 381, 458, wár).
m. a paper, document, used --˚, as in khalās-wᵒ, p. 399b, l. 7. ? Cf. wạthᵃr, s.v. pạthᵃr.
f. in hīta-wörᵘ̈, a slight pretext (hīth, a pretext), p. 358b, l. 11.
m. in naka-wôrᵘ, a nostril, p. 627a, l. 38. Cf. wôlᵘ 1, a ring.
f. in pakha-wörᵘ̈, the plump part of a fowl's wing (pakh), p. 725a, l. 38, q.v.
adj. in prāna-wôrᵘ, old, worn out (p. 761b, l. 45).
f. of wôrᵘ 8-10. Also, in mạkhᵃr-wörᵃ, a coquette, where it is f. of *wôrᵘ, i.q., wôlᵘ 2.
m. in tōraʦh-wôrᵘ, a narrow chisel (p. 1032b, l. 42).
adj. possessing coverings, used --˚, as in pönʦa-wᵒ, p. 743b, l. 16.
adj. occurring (so many) times (cf. wār 1), used --˚, as in pönʦa-wᵒ, p. 743b, l. 17. Cf. ʦᵃhan- wāri, by gradual tastes, p. 1058b, l. 24.
(for 1, see wurᵘ 1) N. of a certain deity, the regent of the western quarter. See warun 1.

(or wŏrüzᵘ̈) f. (sg. dat. wŏrᵃzĕ; pl. nom. wŏrᵃza, Gr.Gr. 63), a woman who has married a second husband, after losing her first (Gr.Gr. 37, 63); the second wife of a widower (H. viii, 1, 11); cf. wŏrudᵘ. wŏrᵃza-pöthᵃr m. the conduct of a woman who has made a second marriage (condemned among respectable Hindūs); conduct resembling the above, the conduct of a woman who is unchaste, shameless, etc.
adj. c.g. a secondary suffix indicating 'belonging to', 'having such-and-such an origin,' i.q. wôlᵘ 2, q.v., in añĕch-wörⁱ, p. 37a, l. 33.

f. (sg. dat. wŏsaröʦᵘ̈), a night passed in waking or sleeplessness (e.g. caused by amusement, worship, festivities, grief, fear, disturbing noise, or so on). --gaʦüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a waking or sleepless night to occur. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to pass such a waking or sleepless night.

or (H.) wōsh m. sighing, a sigh (El., Gr.M.) (El. adds wosh, as an interj. meaning 'Oh!'. Cf. wush). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to sigh (El., W. 88). --trāwun -- m.inf., id. (Gr.M.; K. 502, 998; H. i, 5, wōsh, probably m.c.).
m. (sg. dat. wŏshĕlāwanas), the being caused to flush, flushing, reddening of the complexion (see the next).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏshĕlôwᵘ), to cause a person to flush (from anger, etc.).
m. (sg. dat. wŏshĕlanas) (of the complexion, etc.) becoming red, flushing (as in wᵒ 2, bel.). --khasun -- m.inf. flushing to mount, i.e. occur, as ab.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. wŏshĕlyōv) (of the complexion, etc.) to become red, flushed (from anger, fever, exposure to heat, or the like); (of a fruit or the like) to become red (owing to ripeness or the like). wŏshĕlyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏshĕlyē-müʦᵘ̈) (of the complexion) flushed, as ab.; (of a fruit or the like) reddened (by ripeness).

m. fatigue, exhaustion, depression (due to heavy labour, suffering, or the like); inward anxiety, apprehension (of outrage, tyranny, riot, rebellion, or the like). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to obtain relief from such fatigue or depression (e.g. by success, joining in festivity, being praised for one's work, or so on); to become relieved from such apprehension (by the removal of its cause, etc.).
m. breathing out, expiration (as opp. to shwās, inspiration, q.v.) (Śiv. 1437).
m. pronunciation, utterance (Gr.M.). I.q. wŏʦʦār, q.v.
m. a shower of rain (esp. when light or gentle) (cf. wāwa-wᵒ, s.v. wāv 1). Cf. washun.

in the following:-- wŏsi anun m.inf. to spoil (a child or the like) so as to cause it to be disobedient, unruly, impatient of restraint, self-willed, etc.; cf. wŏsun. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to become disobedient, etc., through spoiling.
f. (sg. dat. wösiyüʦᵘ̈), a will, a testament (Gr.M. wösiat).

(cf. استاد) m. a master, esp. a craftsmaster, a teacher of some craft (El. a teacher; K.Pr. 131); a skilful craftsman, an adept (El. adj. skilful); esp. a barber. -bāy f. a wife of one of the ab. -hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), N. of a certain vegetable, described as growing in the spring, and as having long, delicate leaves (cf. nĕndun-(or nĕndan-)wᵒ-hᵒ, p. 642a, ll. 26, 31) (cf. El. wasta, a kind of vegetable; K.Pr. 41). -hāka-nal m. the stalk of the preceding (K.Pr. 41, where it is translated 'cabbage-stalk'). -kār m. an expert master-craftsman (at the head of a number of others).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. wọ̆sᵘ) or (according to some) conj. 3 (2 p.p. wŏsyōv), to become redundant, to result in excess, to have lavish or extravagant outcome (e.g. of food being prepared for cooking, and turning out too much, or seed bearing an unexpectedly large crop). Cf. wŏsi. ¶ wọ̆sᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vüsᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), become excessive or redundant, as ab. ¶ wŏsan-hār n.ag. c.g. that which usually becomes excessive or too much (e.g. some particular rice which in cooking turns out to be more than is required or expected).
f. expertness, or uncommon skill in craftsmanship; the livelihood earned by, or the occupation of, a skilled craftsman. Cf. wŏsta.

or wösī adj. c.g. (as subst., f. wāsĕñ), one who inhabits (some country or other place), a dweller, inhabitant, resident (cf. naraka-wösⁱ, p. 651a, l. 13; sŏrga-wösī, p. 934a, l. 27; wan-wösⁱ, p. 1120a, l. 25) (Śiv. 195, 529, 779, 1435). Cf. wās 1.
adj. c.g. (of food badly cooked, fruit imperfectly ripened, or the like) hard inside, having a hard centre or kernel. Cf. wỗṭᵘ and wö̃ṭh.

adj. c.g. one who habitually leaps; one who habitually walks in leaps, one who habitually leaps along; one who is easily put into a state of excitement by joy, fear, or the like, excitable, easily excited. Cf. wŏṭh and wŏṭun.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏtalôwᵘ), to raise, elevate (lit. and met.) (causal of wŏtalun in all its senses). wŏtalôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏtalövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), raised, etc., as ab.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. wŏtalyōv) (of something depressed or sunk) to rise, become high (cf. ṭôrᵘ wᵒ, p. 1020a, l. 30); met. to rise (in wealth, honour, in bodily health, or the like); to become prominent. wŏtalith yunᵘ m.inf. (of something hidden, e.g. a seed sown in the earth, a fault, a change) suddenly to become prominently manifest. wŏtalyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏtalyē-müʦᵘ̈), risen, become prominent, etc., as ab.
or wŏttam adj. c.g. excellent, of the highest quality, best (Śiv. 1087, 1449, 1864, wŏtt˚; K. 1040, 1054, wŏtt˚). Cf. wŏttomᵘ.
f. excellence, in wŏtamatā karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to praise, commend, eulogize, show honour (to).
m. incarnation of a deity; the incarnate form or personality taken by a deity; (met.) a child, or descendant, who exactly resembles his parent, or ancestor, in every particular.

f. (sg. dat. wŏṭi), a leap, jump (pĕṭhⁱ (a jump) over) (cf. kala-pĕṭhⁱ wᵒ, p. 435a, l. 42; kŏli-wᵒ, p. 437b, l. 48) (El. woṭ, wŏth; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1567; K.Pr. 63). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give a jump, to jump, (esp.) to jump down from on high, or to jump to a height from below (Rām. 554, 558, 1369; K.Pr. 146). --dāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause to jump, make (a person) leap (cf. p. 263a, l. 49) (Śiv. 1815). --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give a jump, to jump up suddenly, to jump (from sudden fear, surprise, or the like) (cf. p. 386a, l. 22) (Śiv. 998); (of something low down) to jump up, be propelled upwards. --lāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take a jump, to leap, to leap (into), leap (upon) (El.; Rām. 212, 250; K. 233, 237, 446, 491, 632). --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to leap up, to leap to a height (Rām. 549; H. ii, 9). --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take a series of jumps, esp. down from, or over, a height (cf. tĕharyau-pĕṭhⁱ wŏṭa trāwañe, p. 983b, l. 49). --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to jump down, hurl oneself down, plunge (into) (H. iii, 4; K.Pr. 109); (on seeing something going on which interests) suddenly to plunge into the middle (of it). ¶ wŏṭa-bari ʦhŏṭa-borᵘ m. jumping about (from one thing to another), trying resource after resource (used of someone helpless and without resources and making despairing efforts to accomplish some work). -pūrᵘ m. going along, or progressing, by jumps; a road or path over which it is necessary to pass with great speed. --tulañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to leap about, to leap, make leaps (Gr.M.). -wôrᵘ m. a place which should be reached, or which can be reached, by very quick going (quasi, in a leap). -wôṭᵘ m. a path which can be traversed only by jumping (owing to rocks, uneven surface, hollows, torrents, or the like). -wŏṭh f. continued leaping (K. 448, 1127); progressing by uninterrupted leaps; (in doing any work) habitually acting rashly and without consideration of results. ¶ wŏṭi anun m.inf. to bring with a leap, to cause (someone) to come at once before oneself, to summon hastily (K. 367).
m. (sg. dat. wö̃ṭas) (of grain, fruit, etc., badly cooked) internal hardness, toughness, or grittiness. Cf. wỗṭᵘ.

adj. c.g. standing up, erect (K. 980); standing permanently on end; cf. wŏdañĕ. --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain standing; to be at attention, always ready to obey, to be constant in attendance; to receive (a guest) hospitably. --thawun -- m.inf. to set standing, set erect; to set (a person) continually standing, i.e. perpetually on duty, without a moment's rest.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏthanôwᵘ), to cause (so-and-so) to rise (as distinguished from tulun, to raise or lift up, both words being looked upon as causals of wŏthun, q.v.) (Gr.Gr. 176).
f. (sg. dat. wŏtharüñᵘ̈), wiping, making clean by wiping; anything used for wiping, a wiper, a duster.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏtharôwᵘ), i.q. wŏtharun, q.v. (Gr.M.). wŏtharôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏtharövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. wŏthorᵘ-motᵘ, s.v. wŏtharun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏthorᵘ), to wipe, make clean by wiping, to wipe clean (H. viii, 6, 13). wŏthorᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏthürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), wiped clean. wŏtharan-palav m. a wiping cloth, a cloth for wiping off dirt, (for a human being) a bathing towel.
m. anything for wiping off dirt, or for wiping dry, a wiper, towel.
m. rising from one's seat to show honour (to another), rising in honour of; met. to show respect to another by complimenting him, or by praising his good qualities.
n.ag. (f. wŏthavüñᵘ̈), one who (or that which) stands up, or is on the point of rising, or becoming prosperous; one who is zealous and ready to work.
m. (sg. dat. wŏthpātas), any public calamity (such as drought, flood, epidemic, etc.). Cf. wŏtpāth.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. wọ̆thᵘ, f. wö̆ʦhᵘ̈; 2 p.p. wŏʦhōv. The 1 p.p. should be distinguished from wothᵘ, 1 p.p. of wasun, to descend, q.v. The two words are almost identical in sound, but have opposed meanings); ¶ to rise, go up, ȧscend (cf. dᵃh wᵒ, p. 198a, l. 21; parda wᵒ, p. 756b, l. 13; tala-pĕṭha wᵒ, p. 996a, l. 46; tĕngal wŏthȧñⁱ, p. 1011a, l. 29; ṭĕnḍⁱ wŏthȧnⁱ, p. 1050a, l. 3) (El. wŏthun, wótun, wuthun; Gr.Gr. 26, 29, 111, 176, 209, 225, 227; Gr.M.; L.V. 1; Rām. 344, 561, 563, 595, 820, 886, 900, 1099, 1127; K. 873); esp. to rise suddenly, or unexpectedly (cf. manza wᵒ, p. 584a, l. 36; wūrⁱ wūrⁱ wᵒ, p. 1141b, l. 37) (Rām. 1475); to rise up, stand up, become erect (cf. lüṭᵘ̈ wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 536a, l. 46; mĕnga wŏthañĕ, p. 578a, l. 44; thodᵘ wᵒ, p. 971a, l. 2) (Gr.Gr. 204; L.V. 10, 75; Śiv. 65, 321, 392, 842, 879, 1357; Rām. 114, 173, 391, 431, 484, 554, 598, 662, 672, 692, 707, 819, 903, 252, 955, 1107, 1110, 1374, 1384, 1388, 1402, 1462, 1493, 1559, 1604, 1691, 1712, 1741; K. 69, 80, 235, 443, 446, 461, 475, 600, 608, 814-5, 870, 890, 895, 897, 930, 1000, 1041, 1097, 1118; H. ii, 3, 5, 6; iii, 1, 8; v, 6, 9; viii, 11; xii, 3, 14-5, 20; YZ. 532; K.Pr. 63, 237); to rise up and stand, to be standing, erect (El. wathun, to stand; Rām. 332); to rise, get up (from bed, sickness, or the like), to awake, recover from illness (cf. bĕmāri wᵒ, p. 109a, l. 2; nẹ̆ndᵃri wᵒ, p. 642b, l. 24) (Gr.M.; L.V. 105; Śiv. 163, 628; Rām. 73, 622; K. 592, 801 (wö̆ʦᵘ̈ is a misprint for wö̆ʦhᵘ̈), 968, 971, 1163; H. xii, 23); to swell (as a river, a vein, a bruise, or the like) (cf. nahöjⁱ wŏthañĕ, p. 625b, l. 38; rag wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 827b, l. 23); ¶ to rise for the purpose of leaving, to rise up and go, to take leave (cf. brag wŏthȧnⁱ, p. 120a, l. 22; dŏkha wᵒ, p. 206b, l. 17; mala wᵒ, p. 564b, l. 21); to depart (from a place, or this world) (buthi-pĕṭha wᵒ, p. 143b, l. 3); to be lifted off, to be done away with, be abolished, discontinued (lawa wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 541a, l. 10; thopᵘ wᵒ, p. 980a, l. 32; thaph wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 918a, l. 20) (Śiv. nakha w˚, to be lifted off the shoulder, i.e. to be completed, 1758, the reference to wasun, on p. 629a, l. 4 being incorrect); todisappear, cease to exist (cf. bögⁱ wŏthȧnⁱ, p. 91a, l. 20; banga wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 112b, l. 37; barm wᵒ, p. 123b, ll. 1 ff.; das wᵒ, p. 251b, l. 27; dọ̆shᵘ wᵒ, p. 253a, l. 33; diwath wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 265a, l. 3; mālay wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 570a, l. 20; mandach wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 575b, l. 12; satyā wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 950b, l. 29) (Śiv. 1290); to rise (owing to friction or the like) from the surface, to be worn away, (of skin) to be worn off, flayed (cf. bargölⁱ wŏthȧnⁱ, p. 120b, l. 5; nam wŏthȧnⁱ, p. 635b, l. 38; tūz wŏthȧnⁱ, p. 1051b, l. 41); ¶ to spring up, sprout, shoot, grow; to break out (as an epidemic, mutiny, etc.), to arise suddenly (as a storm, disturbance, etc.), to burst forth (as fire) (cf. brēh wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 120b, l. 18; dūñᵘ̈ wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 231b, l. 18; drāg wᵒ, p. 241b, l. 4; hūs wᵒ, p. 352b, l. 2; huy wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 363a, l. 46; khad wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 391b, l. 36; mājĕ-wadun wᵒ, p. 557b, l. 40; maĩshĕr wᵒ, p. 598a, l. 49; mazhar wᵒ, p. 615b, l. 10; naba-nār wᵒ, p. 619a, l. 11; nār wᵒ, p. 647a, l. 35; phȧrⁱshĕr wᵒ, p. 708b, l. 41; phãwār wŏthȧnⁱ, p. 720b, l. 4; pönʦa-grishᵘ̈ wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 742b, l. 33; tāv wᵒ, p. 1046b, l. 37; wŏlharish wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 1113b, l. 38) (El. wothun, to blow (of the wind); Śiv. 1614, 1843; Rām. 404, 693, 740, 835, 1761; K. 451, 762; H. iii, 3; vi, 12-3, 15; YZ. 396; K.Pr. 128); to spring up, come into existence, begin, occur (cf. bādwôrᵘ wᵒ, p. 89a, l. 42; brᵃs wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 126a, l. 47; bŏy wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 149a, l. 22; dôdᵘ wᵒ, p. 191b, ll. 6 ff.; dọ̆dᵃsa wᵒ, p. 193a, l. 7; gānd wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 289a, l. 16; mȧchⁱ wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 547a, l. 35; muh wᵒ, p. 553b, l. 17; mŏshᵉ̆kh wᵒ, p. 597b, l. 18; nyāy wᵒ, p. 675a, l. 8; phakh wᵒ, p. 689a, l. 8; phasād wᵒ, p. 712a, l. 16; phutūra wᵒ, p. 718b, l. 49; pralāb wᵒ, p. 759a, l. 35; prasang wᵒ, p. 768a, l. 23; sĕy wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 956a, l. 7; ṭōsa-ṭōs wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 1037a, l. 38; ṭāv wᵒ, p. 1047a, l. 22; ʦan wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 1073b, l. 23; wucāpa wᵒ, p. 1095b, l. 1; wād wᵒ, p. 1096a, l. 26; wuṭh-paṭã̄g wᵒ, p. 1159b, l. 18; wāʦakh wŏthüñᵘ̈; wŏʦrāṭh wᵒ; vyād wŏthüñᵘ̈) (Gr.M.; Rām. 281, 407, 1142, 1290; K. 1114); to come on, begin (as pain, disease, etc.) (cf. bĕgarun wᵒ, p. 92b, l. 6; bambar wŏthȧnⁱ, p. 108a, l. 14; brikh wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 122b, l. 10; dạdᵘ̈rᵘ̈ wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 192a, l. 38; dag wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 193b, l. 5; phȧrⁱ-wōv wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 702b, l. 43; phutang wŏthȧnⁱ, p. 718b, l. 29; pyās wᵒ, p. 818a, l. 15; rĕy wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 854b, l. 34; tṻri- bambar wŏthȧnⁱ, p. 1021a, l. 27; tōs wᵒ, p. 1037a, l. 34; taturᵘ wᵒ, p. 1044b, l. 46); to proceed (from), originate, issue, emanate, result (cf. prawa wŏthañĕ, p. 772a, l. 13; rāy wŏthüñᵘ̈, p. 854b, l. 21; tarang wŏthȧnⁱ, p. 1028a, l. 32); to rise (upon), fall (upon), attack (Gr.M., K. 1056, K.Pr. 85). ¶ This verb is used with the conjunctive participle of another verb, to indicate the hastiness, impulsiveness or suddenness of the act expressed by the latter, as in phīrith wŏthun, equivalent to our 'to up and answer' (K. 755; H. viii, 6; x, 2, 6; xxii, 11). ¶ wọ̆thᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wö̆ʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), risen, etc., as ab. ¶ wŏthan-wād m. disappearing, i.e. total destruction (of a kingdom, of one's entire property, or the like). -wād yunᵘ m.inf. the time of such destruction to come near. ¶ wŏthith gaʦhun m.inf. (by some overwhelming calamity, an entire kingdom, property, or business) to disappear, i.e. to be totally destroyed.

adj. (f.wö̆ʦhᵘ̈), 1 p.p. of wŏthun, q.v. (This word is to be distinguished from wothᵘ 3, which has the opposite meaning.) Used as adj., risen, standing up, erect; he who, or that which, is steadily and continuously rising (lit. and met.); risen (from bed, sickness, or the like) (cf. bĕmāri-wᵒ, p. 108b, l. 50; huri-wᵒ, p. 347a, l. 45); prepared, ready (cf. byāli-wᵒ, p. 150b, l. 40); risen (from), been done with, been got rid of (cf. mūni-wᵒ, p. 573b, l. 47); originated, issued, emanated (cf. manza wᵒ, p. 584a, l. 30); risen from its origin, just issued, fresh from the source (cf. thāna-wᵒ, p. 978a, l. 10. Here there has possibly been confusion with wothᵘ 3, q.v.); and so on, through all the meanings of wŏthun. ¶ wŏtha-bēṭh f. (of some thing or action) the continuously and repeatedly rising up and settling down. -bēṭh lagüñᵘ̈ f.inf. (of a human being) to begin repeatedly rising and sitting; to become restless, fidgetty, etc.; (of some action) to become uncertain, at one time in action, at another time not, or at one time definite and at another time indefinite, and so on; cf. wŏthāsan. -dān m. a movable fireplace or cooking stove (capable of being moved safely from one place to another). ¶ wŏthā-bīṭhī f. rising up and sitting down; esp. (as a punishment to a school boy) continuous repeated standing up and sitting down.

(for 1, see wasun) (f. vüʦhᵘ̈ 2, for 1, see wasun) (of a thing or action) open, unclosed, not shut up (cf. ȧchⁱ-waʦha gāshĕ-raʦha, p. 9a, l. 2; aḍa-wᵒ, p. 12b, l. 7; atha-wᵒ, p. 64b, l. 47; ṭhāna-wᵒ, p. 978b, l. 29; wölinja-wᵒ, p. 1115b, l. 48) (Gr.Gr. 29, 140; Gr.M. wọ̆thᵘ; K.Pr. 1, 105, 245); exposed, bare, uncovered, naked; not tied up, unfastened; loose, not connected (with); free, unrestricted, unrestrained (cf. bukᵃ̇rᵃ̇-wᵃ̇, p. 102b, l. 6). --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to throw (a door or the like) open (Rām. 1734).

(f. vüʦhᵘ̈ 3, for 4, see s.v.). (This word is to be distinguished from wọ̆thᵘ, which has the opposite meaning), 1 p.p. of wasun, used --˚ as adj., in the following meanings;--descended, come down, [as in hȧṭⁱ-wⁱ, p. 356a, l. 35; nakha-wᵒ, p. 629a, l. 7; nēri-wᵒ, p. 673b, l. 18; sŏrga-wᵒ, p. 934a, l. 30; wana-wᵒ, p. 1120a, l. 42]; just come (from), fresh (from) [as in dōri-wᵒ, (cloth) fresh from the loom, p. 237a, l. 34; hĕli-wᵒ, p. 364b, l. 21; wāna-wᵒ, p. 1121a, l. 20; so dāna-wᵒ, (of cooked food) fresh from the oven (cf. thāna-wọ̆thᵘ, p. 1158b, l. 49); vēgi-wᵒ, one who is just married (s.v. vyūgᵘ), as compared with vēgiwothᵘ-motᵘ (p. 1150b, l. 18), a married person]; declined, faded, wasted, waned, (as in buthⁱ-wⁱ, p. 143a, l. 10; nashĕ-wᵒ, p. 654b, l. 41; rasa-wᵒ, p. 842a, l. 23); fallen (from some former condition), abased (as in mada-wᵒ, p. 548b, l. 16; mōda-wᵒ, p. 549a, l. 32); and so on for other meanings of wasun.
wŏthⁱñĕr or wŏthⁱñēr m. habitual readiness to undertake (any work) at once and without delay, industrious activity, zealous quickness.
adj. c.g. (a deity), who has become incarnate, an incarnate deity; (met.) (a child, or descendant), who exactly resembles his parent, or ancestor, in every particular.
m. (sg. dat. wŏtpātas), a portent, any portentous or unusual phenomenon boding calamity (K. 181); any public calamity (e.g. an eclipse or earthquake). Cf. wŏthpāth.
f. (sg. dat. wŏtpüʦᵘ̈), i.q. wŏtpatti, q.v. (Śiv. 763, Rām. 113).
adj. c.g. created (Śiv. 681, 913, 1231). --karun -- m.inf. to create (Gr.M., Śiv. 1278).
f. creation, the act of creating. -kāran m. the cause of creation, the First Cause, the Creator (Gr.M.). Cf. wŏtpath 1.
m. energy, strenuous effort, perseverance; encouraging, inciting. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to encourage (Gr.M.).
m. a joyous or festive occasion, a festival (K. 24, 56, 568, 715, 752, 771, 776, 833, 950, 1065). I.q. wŏʦhav, q.v.
f. incitement (Gr.M. wŏtshöish). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to incite (Gr.M.).
m. an answer (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 623, 1348, 1653); the north (i.q. wŏturᵘ, q.v.) (Śiv. 1412, 1589).
m. (sg. dat. wŏttarāpathas), the way to the North, the north country (K. 612).
adj. (f. wŏttümᵘ̈), excellent, of the highest quality, best (L.V. 53). I.q. wŏtam, q.v.

adj. (f. wŏtüjᵘ̈), high, lofty, elevated (as compared with others, in form, position, fortune, qualities, occupation, or the like). ¶ wŏtal-bujĕ f.pl. risings and sinkings, repeated ups and downs (e.g. in the flood of a river, in a state of health, or in indecision of mind); cf. bŏḍun. -ḍēmb m. a floating island, such as are common on the Ḍal lake.
conj. 3 to leap, jump; to go along in leaps, to leap along. [This word is hardly ever used as a verb, such phrases as wŏṭh diñᵘ̈, etc. (see wŏṭh) being preferred.]

m. the north (cf. wŏttar) (El. wattúr, wŏtur; Gr.M. wŏttorᵘ; Śiv. wŏttar, q.v.); a country situated to the north; (in some phrase, see bel.) left (not right). -kun adv. in the north (cf. wŏtarā-khanḍ-kun, Rām. 783); to the north, as far as the north (Rām. 632). ¶ wŏtara-khōwurᵘ adj. (f. -khōvürᵘ̈), that which goes in the reverse direction, that of which the action or existence is the reverse (of something alluded to). [The word khōworᵘ usually means 'north' (see p. 425a, l. 43), and certainly does so in Rām. 516; but here it seems to mean 'south', and is also so translated in El. s.v. kháwur.] ¶ wŏtarā-khanḍ m. the north country, the north. -khanḍ-kun adv. in the north country (Rām. 783). ¶ wŏtari-kani adv. on the left. -kanyukᵘ adj. gen. (f. -kanicᵘ̈, of, or belonging to, of (a place), on the left. ¶ wŏtȧrⁱ-kinⁱ adv. on the north (side) (Rām. 1682). ¶ wŏtaryukᵘ adj. gen. (f. wŏtaricᵘ̈), of, belonging to, born, or produced in the north.
m. in vĕtha-wᵒ, p. 1158a, l. 32, the source of the Vĕth, ? the same as waturᵘ 1.

m. the room on the ground floor of a house, in which the tenants live in the winter for the sake of warmth (El. wauṭ, Śiv. 1567, Rām. 572). wȧṭⁱ-nakawôrⁱ m. a narrow closet or small room on this ground floor.

1 p.p. of wātun, q.v. (f. wöʦᵘ̈), as adj. arrived (cf. aza-wᵒ, p. 74a, l. 34; wati-wᵒ, s.v. wath 1); (met.) arrived at a condition of readiness for use, (of a man) one who has passed through childhood and is now able to make himself useful, (of a thing) ready for use after due preparation. --prôtᵘ -- adj. (f. wöʦᵘ̈ pröʦᵘ̈), become quite ready for use, as ab.

1 p.p. of wāṭun, q.v. (f. wöṭᵘ̈), as adj. joined up, united (cf. phuṭa-wᵒ, p. 717a, l. 12; wŏṭa-wᵒ, s.v. wŏṭh); (added to a numeral) containing (so many) joins, as in duwôṭᵘ, p. 264b, l. 35 (e.g. duwöṭᵘ̈ pīr, a stool with two joints, or joined in two places; trᵃwôṭᵃ bāna, a dish joined in three places; ʦuwôṭᵘ phĕran, a coat with four seams). ¶ As subst. m. the act of joining, an agreement (cf. saṭa-wᵒ, p. 942b, l. 41; ʦoṭᵘ wᵒ, p. 1085a, l. 40); a person who joins pieces together, as in anga-wᵒ, a mender of a broken limb (cf. anga-wāṭukh, p. 33b, l. 2); bāna-wᵒ, a mender of dishes. ¶ wöṭⁱ-hāl f. N. of a certain kind of rice-plant, or paddy, with a large white grain in a thin husk (L. 463, watihal).

m. (of a river, lake, pit, or the like) shallowness (cf. ỗtᵘ-wᵘ, p. 53a, l. 48) (Śiv. 1755). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. 'to take the shallowness'; hence, to find out (after enquiry) another's intentions. --wuchun -- m.inf. to sound the depth (of a body of water); to test (another's) intentions. ¶ wö̃tⁱ-gāv 1 or -gôvᵘ m. (f. -gövᵘ̈), one who shows contempt for his own people (by the way he supports those whom he ought to support, or by the way he neglects to help those whom it is his duty to help); cf. gāv 1. -gāv 2 f. a cow that gives milk (i.e. that is not dry) (K.Pr. 126, wánti-g˚). Cf. gāv 2.

adj. (f. wö̃ṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. wã̄cĕ) (of a shell-fruit, such as the walnut) having the kernel hard and difficult to extract, close-shelled (cf. El. wónṭ dúṅ, i.e. wỗṭᵘ ḍūnᵘ, a kind of walnut, s.v. dun; L. 352, wantu and vont) (K.Pr. 229); as subst. m. and f. a mean miserly person from whom it is difficult to extract anything. Cf. wö̃ṭh.
f. the act of joining up, bringing close together, used --˚ in saṭa-wöṭᵘ̈, p. 942b, l. 37. Cf. wôṭᵘ.

m. casting, flinging, hurling (stones, dust, mud, or the like) at (someone or something animate or inanimate) (cf. kañi-wᵒ, p. 461b, l. 43). --karun 1 -- m.inf. to harass, torment, or damage (by flinging showers of such missiles, at someone, or something, as ab.). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. a flinging (of such missiles) to happen (to someone), to be tormented by a shower of such missiles; met. to be subjected to a torrent of abuse, etc.

m. a collection of things clustered together, a lump, pad, used --˚, as in danda-wᵒ, p. 225a, l. 8; hirⁱ-wⁱ, p. 367a, l. 47; kana-wᵒ, p. 448a, l. 46; naka-wᵒ, p. 627a, l. 39; nal-wᵒ, p. 631b, l. 49; vīga-wᵒ, p. 1101a, l. 40); wal-wᵒ, p. 1111b, l. 16). Cf. vüṭᵘ̈ 1 (of which this is the masc. form) and waṭun.

m. a method of marking linear figures on silk or fine woollen cloth by impressing it with a heated sickle-shaped instrument of iron. --karun 2 -- m.inf. to impress such figures. ¶ wȧtⁱ-gorⁱ m. a man whose profession it is to mark such figures. -ṭūpⁱ f. (sg. dat. -ṭōpĕ), a cap ornamented with such figured silk or the like.
adj. (f. vüṭᵘ̈), of (such-and-such) a weight, used --˚, as in raṭa-wᵒ, p. 847a, l. 1). Cf. vüṭᵘ̈ 2.

adj. (f. vüʦᵘ̈), having (so many) roads or ways of approach or exit, used --˚, as in daha-wᵒ, approached by ten roads, p. 199a, l. 24; shᵉ̆wᵉ̆, s.v.; sata-wᵒ, approached by seven roads, p. 944b, l. 50; ʦŏwotᵘ, s.v. a place where four ways meet. Cf. wath 1.

(by Paṇḍits usually written wōv or wōvᵘ̈), f. pain, ache, in dödⁱ-wōv, p. 191b, ll. 10 ff.; danda-wōvᵘ̈, p. 225a, l. 11; phȧrⁱ-wōv, p. 702b, ll. 36 ff.; prāna-wövᵘ̈, p. 761a, l. 49, qq.v. ? Cf. wāv 1 or 2.

m. (sg. dat. wōwaras; a female weaver is wōvᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 1, q.v., Gr.Gr. 35. In the old Ksh. of L.V. 102, wôwurᵘ has the form bôwurᵘ), a weaver (cf. pō̃bᵃri-wᵃ, p. 678b, l. 28; pȧṭⁱ-wⁱ, p. 789b, l. 38) (El. wáûr, wãwur, wôwúr; Gr.Gr. 23, 35; L. 316, 464, wáwar; K. 420); hence, a seller of made-up cloth (cf. pūʦa-wᵒ, p. 807a, l. 18) (K.Pr. 237). ¶ wōwᵃ̇rᵃ̇-bāy f. a weaver's wife (Gr.Gr. 35). -dōra m. a weaver's loom (cf. dōr 3 f. a loom, dōra 3 m. the cloth as it issues from the loom). -khᵃʦh m. (sg. dat. -khᵃʦas), the comb-like implement or brush used by weavers for cleaning off the fluff from the threads on the loom. -wān m. a weaver's shop, or place where he has his loom (L.V. 102, bōwᵃ̇rᵃ̇-wᵃ̇).
f. (sg. dat. wōwᵃrüñᵃ), the act of paring, scraping, grinding, or polishing (some metal article in order to furbish it after manufacture) (Gr.Gr. 121).
f. (sg. dat. wöwᵃrüñᵃ), the act or business of weaving.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wōwᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. wōwᵃrun, q.v. wōvᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. wōvᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. wōwᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, s.v. wōwᵃrun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wōwᵒrᵒ, or wūwᵒrᵒ; f. wōvᵘ̈rᵘ̈ 2, for 1, see s.v., or wūvᵘ̈rᵘ̈), to scrape, grind, or polish (a metal article in order to furbish it after manufacture) (Gr.Gr. 121); cf. wāv 2. wōwᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. wōvᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), furbished, as ab.
(for 2, see wayun) adj. (f. vüyᵘ̈), other, another, different (from), unconnected with.
m. loss, damage (occurring to anything or in any work). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. loss to come to a person, thing, or work (through censure, blame, disparagement, etc.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏzalôwᵘ), to make red, dye red, redden (Gr.Gr. 171). wŏzalôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏzalövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made red, dyed red, reddened.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. wŏzalyōv), to become red (Gr.Gr. 171). wŏzalyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wŏzalyē-müʦᵘ̈), become red, reddened.

m. vomiting. --gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. vomitings to begin, an attack of vomiting to come on. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. a single occurrence of vomiting to happen, to vomit once for all (e.g. on experiencing a stink, or eating or drinking something disgusting).
f. the profession of a cook.

or wŏzulᵘ adj. (f. wŏzüjᵘ̈), red-coloured, red (cf. aḍa-wᵒ, p. 12b, l. 13; gala-wᵒ, p. 282b, l. 5) (El. wazul; Gr.Gr. 16, 138, 141; Gr.M.; L. 459; W. 20; Śiv. 68, 98, 113, 801; Rām. 203, 1022, 1097, 1210, 1266, 1379, 1502; YZ. 75, 147, 213, 527; K.Pr. 116, 166, 238). --prazolᵘ -- adj. (f. wŏzüjᵘ̈ prazüjᵘ̈), brilliantly beautiful.
m. an excuse (El. uzr, Gr.M.). Another form of ozur, q.v.

adj. (f. wŏzümᵘ̈), that which is subject to loan, that which has been borrowed, or which is suitable to be borrowed, or may be borrowed; a loan (El. wazum; Gr.M.; L. 461, wazam; K.Pr. 238); (as subst. m.) the practice or transaction of borrowing (money or other articles). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to lend (El., K.Pr. 228). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to borrow (El.). --thāwun -- m.inf. to owe (El.). --ʦaṭun -- m.inf. (f. wŏzümᵘ̈ʦaṭüñᵘ̈), to borrow (money), to take a loan. (When the thing borrowed is feminine, the f. form is used) (Gr.M.). --wŏrudᵘ -- adj. (f. wŏzümᵘ̈ wŏrüzᵘ̈), subject to loan, that which is borrowed or may be borrowed, or is liable to be borrowed; (as subst. m.) (on some necessary occasion) a borrowing transaction.
f. (sg. dat. wö̃ʦüñᵘ̈), cheating, swindling, misleading; disappointing, disappointment.

m. (sg. dat. wö̃ʦas or (see bel.) wö̃ʦhas), the being defrauded; deceit, cheating (Gr.Gr. 11, 123); non-fulfilment of hopes, disappointment (cf. dayĕ-wᵒ, p. 266a, l. 29). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. disappointment to occur, hopes not to be fulfilled. ¶ wö̃ʦha-wathar m. total disappointment (when a work, etc., is on the point of successful completion, total destruction of the expected results). See wathar.
f. (sg. dat. wōʦhaṭi), fainting, insensibility, the being stunned (e.g. caused by disease, agony, loss, terror, grief, or a blow). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such insensibility to occur.
or wŏʦhuwᵘ m. a joyous occasion, a festival (cf. khā̃dar-wᵒ, p. 393b, l. 6) (K. 637, wŏʦhuwāh, with suff. of indef. art.). I.q. wŏtsav, q.v.

m. a male calf (cf. dŏda-wᵒ, p. 190b, l. 10) (El. wuts; Gr.M.; Śiv. 705, 1393, 1464, 1837; K. 185-6, 203, 210-2, 261; K.Pr. 49, 68-9, 72, 158, 171, 232, 251, 256). For the fem. of this word, waʦhᵃr or waʦhürᵘ̈ is used, see waʦhorᵘ (Gr.Gr. 33, 37). ¶ wȧʦhⁱ-guhⁱ m. the dung of a calf (used for purificatory purposes and as a medicine). -khinda f.pl. the sportive leaping of a young calf (cf. khinda-waʦhorᵘ, p. 403a, l. 42). ¶ waʦhi-wölinjĕ adv. 'calf-heartedly', with great tenderness, very affectionately (u.w. vbs. of speaking, distributing, accomplishing, or the like).

m. (sg. dat. wŏʦrāṭas), censurable, wicked, or vile conduct (including neglect of religious observances, general immorality, and libertinism). --tulun -- m.inf. to take to such vile conduct. --wŏthun -- m.inf. such conduct to begin to be practised.
adj. c.g. one who practises such vile conduct, as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wū̃ʦᵘ (Śiv. 1475); 2 p.p. wö̃ʦōv. This verb is impersonal), cheating to be done (by so-and-so); hence, to cheat, swindle, rob another of the result of his labours (Gr.Gr. 123, Śiv. 1475); (in a distribution or sharing out, dishonestly or not) to prevent (a person) getting what he is entitled to, to disappoint (cf. dayĕ wᵒ, p. 266a, l. 29). wū̃ʦᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. vǖ̃ʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), cheated, swindled, robbed of the result of one's labours; disappointed, as ab. (cf. dȧyⁱ wᵒ, p. 266a, l. 33).
adj. c.g. high; (as subst. m.) the apex of the orbit of a planet (Śiv. 481).
(sometimes written wŏshʦār, q.v.) m. utterance, pronunciation.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏʦʦorᵘ), to utter, pronounce (L.V. 58).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wŏʦʦôrᵘ), to utter, pronounce, i.q. wŏʦʦarun (Śiv. 1375, 1753, 1845).

m. a pair of forceps or tweezers (esp. those used by barbers for plucking out hairs) (El. wauts, m. forceps, f. pincers). ¶ wŏʦⁱ dinⁱ m. pl.inf. 'to apply tweezers'; hence, to torment a person by pricking him with a pointed instrument; to torment, or pierce to the vitals, by threats, abuse, intimidation, or the like. ¶ wŏʦi wŏʦikhyonᵘ m.inf. to cause torment, as ab.
m. partial, or imperfect, cooking (as when food is under-boiled, owing to the heat ceasing or becoming insufficient). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such partial cooking to occur.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wubalôwᵘ), to cause to boil up; (of a river or piece of water) to cast up waves (W. 149, K.Pr. 260). ¶ [The intransitive form of this verb has not been noted, we should expect wubalun, conj. 3.]

m. an unreal or groundless dispute or objection (e.g. arising in some act of giving or taking, or in calculating). -gorᵘ m. one who is in the habit of raising such groundless disputes or objections. --karun -- m.inf. to dispute, or object, groundlessly, as ab. --tulun -- m.inf. to intervene by raising a groundless dispute or objection. --wŏthun -- m.inf. such an intervention to occur.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wuchanôwᵘ), to cause to be seen, to show (Śiv. 16, 1397); to cause to be considered, to explain.
f. the cost paid for looking, an inspection fee.
n.ag. (f. wuchavüñᵘ̈), one who sees, a beholder, looker on; one who inspects, examines, tests; and so on as in wuchun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wuchᵘ), to see, behold, look at, view, perceive, regard (cf. dōla dōla wᵒ, p. 211b, l. 11; khāb wᵒ, p. 390b, l. 41; khwāb wᵒ, p. 425a, l. 2; mōj wᵒ, p. 557a, l. 42; nĕdarsh wᵒ, p. 623a, l. 28; pȧtⁱ ta brū̃ṭhⁱ wᵒ, p. 789a, l. 34; pata brō̃ṭhas wᵒ, p. 792a, l. 50; tȧlⁱ-ṭāri wᵒ, p. 996b, l. 34; tamāshĕ wᵒ, p. 1007b, l. 15) (Gr.M.; L.V. 3, 68, 83, 98; Śiv. 347, 349, 424, 436, 509, 584, 618, 654, 656-7, 712, 758, 784-5, 794, 811, 839, 872, 874, 879, 881, 907-8, 911, 916, 918, 922-3, 935-6, 949, 957, 964, 967, etc.; Rām. 3, 22, 25, 28, 35, 46, 89, 174-5, 202, 233, 240, 285-6, 314, 322-3, 335, 337, 345, 369-70, 392, 400, 406, 444-5, 462-3, 473, 477, etc.; K. 25, 96, 108, 201, 263, 295, 312, 340, 412, 436, 480, 546, 593, 609, 648, 650, 678-9, 703, 716, 804, 930, 949, 964, 986, 1016, 1111-2, 1116, 1133; H. iii, 1; viii, 6, 9; YZ. 12, 42, 48, 52, 99, etc.; K.Pr. 150); ¶ to look at, examine, inspect, weigh well, prove, try (cf. bāzar wᵒ, p. 154b, l. 29; ḍĕka-lônᵘ wᵒ, p. 204b, l. 9; danjĕ-kun wᵒ, p. 226a, l. 8; mŏl-tŏl wᵒ, p. 568a, l. 21; mö̃thᵃr wuchüñᵘ̈, p. 606a, l. 29; myāda wᵒ, p. 613a, l. 40; maza wᵒ, p. 614b, l. 12; phāl wᵒ, p. 693a, l. 27; ray wᵒ, p. 854a, l. 36; sāth wᵒ, p. 945b, l. 25; thȧlⁱ thȧlⁱ wᵒ, p. 975a, l. 47; tār wᵒ, p. 1018a, l. 3; trāy wuchüñᵘ̈, p. 1035a, l. 37; wŏnda wᵒ; vĕstār wᵒ; wath wuchüñᵘ̈, s.v. wath 1; zang wuchüñᵘ̈, s.v. zang 2) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 23, 422, 499, 586, 698, 730, 760, 768, 829, 895, 1063, 1261, 1288, 1367, 1543, 1593, 1676, 1719, 1737, 1756, 1851, 1902; Rām. 125, 129, 289, 357, 429, 499, 515-6, 536, 544, 551, 567, 579, 590, 595-6, 623, etc.; K. 149-50, 160, 179, 194, 232, 286, 372, 384, 416, 438, 475, 524, 526, 536, 543, 629, 643, 647, 677, 918, 935, 948, 978, 1001, 1005, 1156; H. v, 5; vii, 18, 24; viii, 1, 3; YZ. 27, 225; K.Pr. 150, 178); to look for, seek for (dat.) (Śiv. 425, 1465, 1469; Rām. 433, 441, 525, 944, 1143c; K. 656, 693, 1034; YZ. 116); ¶ to see, to try (if one can do so-and-so) (Gr.M.); to consider (if one can do so-and-so), hesitate about (K. 1116); ¶ to look out for, watch for, wait for, await cf. gō̃ʦhi wᵒ, p. 313a, l. 11; hīth wᵒ, p. 358b, l. 5; prashᵉ̆n, p. 767a, l. 50; rōgi wᵒ, p. 828a, l. 36; rugᵘ wᵒ, p. 828b, l. 10) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1118, 1706; Rām. 10, 69, 1169); ¶ to see, find, discover (Gr.M.; Śiv. 340, 554, 1656, 1748, 1853; Rām. 95, 508, 608, 630, 1000, 1557, 1720; K. 94, 231, 286, 288, 811, 910, 1037, 1104); to see, understand, be of opinion (Gr.M.; Siv. 728, 1068, 1774, 1802, 1807, 1818, 1820, 1834; Rām. 12, 26, 222, 652, 1302, 1420, 1522-3, 1560; K. 135, 237, 295, 435, 960, 1061); ¶ to experience, suffer, endure (cf. nĕshⁱkāl wᵒ, p. 656a, l. 21; pās wᵒ, p. 776b, l. 35) (Rām. 24, 825, 1005, 1520); El. also gives the inf. wuchun, as meaning 'eyesight'. ¶ The impve. of this verb is often used as an interjection, or semi-interjection with the meaning of 'behold' (e.g. wuch, Rām. 122, 155, 741, 1092, 1762); more commonly in the plural (as in wuchiv, Rām. 271, 556, 585, 602, 621, 629, 637, 654, 891, 943, 951, 1220, 1222, 1228, 1268, 1326, 1334, 1336, 1338, 1452, 1546, 1751; wuchⁱtav, Rām. 604, 1147, 1160, 1298, 1409, 1538, 1547, 1549, 1613, 1689). ¶ wuchᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wuchᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), seen, etc., as ab. ¶ wuchan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who sees, beholds (Śiv. 916); one who examines, tests. ¶ wuchith-kār m. action taken after due consideration. --karun -- m.inf. to act after due consideration. --rōzun -- m.inf. to keep on the watch, to keep an eye on. --thawun -- m.inf. to observe and keep in mind.
m. looking at, observation, inspection (of another's property or work); (El. wuch) sight. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. a secret to become revealed (by the revealer observing the hidden property or action).
f. the practice of raising or entering into groundless disputes or objections.
adj. c.g. one who is in the habit of raising groundless disputes or making groundless objections.
or m. the country of which Ayōdhyā was the capital, the modern Awadh or Oude (Rām. 888).

m. N. of a certain seed, which, when ground and made into a plaster with water, is used as a cure for headache. It is burnt as a protection against demons (Śiv. 1150). -zālay f. the burning of this seed. When a bridegroom or bride are about to set forth for the wedding (or on similar occasions) this seed is burnt before them with appropriate spells, in order to ward off the evil eye, demons, ghosts, or similar evils.
pres. part. of wuḍun, to fly, q.v., used as adv., quickly, speedily (L. 462, wudan).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wuḍanôwᵘ), to cause to fly, set flying (e.g. a tame bird, an airplane, or the like) (Gr.M., K. 947); to carry (a load on the head) (Gr.M.; ? cf. wŏḍ). wuḍanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wuḍanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to fly, set flying (by someone).

f. (sg. obl. wuḍürᵘ̈, Śiv. 1813), a plateau, raised a little above the level of the valley (cf. nyövⁱ-wⁱ, p. 674b, l. 34; pö̃par-wᵒ, p. 749b, l. 48) (El. uḍar, wuḍar; Gr.Gr. 15; L. 461, udar; Śiv. 1813).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. wudaryōv), to feel sorrow in separation or owing to loss. wudaryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wudaryē-müʦᵘ̈), become sorrowful, as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wuḍôwᵘ), to cause to fly; to cause to fly away, to cause to move away (cf. tōsma wuḍāwȧnⁱ, p. 1038a, l. 30); to cause to move speedily, to speed up; to destroy; to carry off, take away entirely (cf. banga wuḍāvüñᵘ̈, p. 112b, l. 24). ¶ wuḍôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wuḍövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), caused to fly; caused to fly away; speeded up (by someone); destroyed; carried off. ¶ wuḍövith ʦhunun m.inf. to squander, dissipate.
n.ag. (f. wuḍavüñᵘ̈), one who flies, soars; a speedy rider or driver; anything which is on the point of destruction.
or m. one who rescues, a deliverer (a title given to Śiva, as the Rescuer from rebirth, voc. wuddara, Śiv. 1584).
or m. N. of a Yādava, uncle and friend of Krushn (Kṛṣṇa), in Skt. Uddhava (Śiv. 992, 1005; K. 500 ff. to 531, 898-9, 985, 1003, 1020).
f. a woman's sheet or mantle (according to El., s.v. wóḍín, it is the marriage veil, and is made of finer materials than the ordinary veil or pūʦᵘ̈).
m. food (esp. cooked grain). --tulun -- m.inf. to eat such food.

conj. 2 or 3 (1 p.p. wudᵘ, f. wuzᵘ̈; 2 p.p. wudyōv), to be wide awake; to become wide awake, to wake from sleep, to come to one's senses out of a faint (K. 600); met. to come forth out of obscurity, to become actively manifest (L.V. 25); cf. wudᵘ. wudᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wuzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), awakened, come to out of a faint.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. wuḍyōv), to fly, to soar (El.; W. 115; K. 747, 807); (met.) to fly away, disappear, be destroyed, vanish, become nothing, (of a human being) to gain final emancipation (after death). [In this latter meaning only, the conj. part. is wujith, not wuḍith, see Gr.Gr. 104, 198.] ¶ wuḍyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wuḍyē-müʦᵘ̈), flown away, disappeared, destroyed (e.g. by time, change, character, calamity, expenditure). ¶ wuḍith gaʦhun m.inf. to fly away (Gr.Gr. 104, 198; Gr.M.). ¶ wujith gaʦhun m.inf. to disappear, vanish, be utterly destroyed and not leave a trace; to give up the ghost, die (Rām. 260); to obtain final emancipation (Gr.Gr. 198).
(? spelling) conj. 1 (1 p.p. wudᵃrôwᵃ), to wet (El. udaráwun). Cf. wazanāwun 1.

adj. (f. wuzᵘ̈ 1, for 2, see wuzun), awake, awakened from sleep (cf. nẹ̆ndᵃri-wᵃ, p. 642b, l. 20) (L.V. 32); met. wide-awake, sharp-witted, clear-witted; skilled, accomplished (in somework). Cf. udun. ¶ wuda-sāway f. broken sleep, sleep from which one wakes over and over again. -sāway gaʦhüñᵘ̈  f.inf. broken sleep to occur to a person.

(? spelling and gender) (in a Kāshmīrī house) an opening from the ground floor to the first floor, through which the heated breath of the cattle kept on the ground floor passes to the first floor, and so keeps the whole house warm (L. 461, cf. 249). ? i.q. wŏga 1.
in wuga-wôñᵘ m. the water that falls from the eaves of a house (Gr.Gr. 73); met. anything that comes suddenly and lasts only a very short time. Cf. wŏga 1.

(also written), m. N. of a king of Mathurā (Skt. Ugrasēna). He was father of Kans (Kaṁsa), who deposed him. Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) slew Kans, and restored Wugrasēn to the throne (K. 22-3, 40, 377, 445, 464-6, 569, 672, 901 ff.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wugᵃrôwᵃ), to recover a debt, to be repaid a loan, to receive payment of a loan. wugᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. wugᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ) (of a loan) recovered, received in payment.
f. the demanding repayment of a loan, dunning a creditor.

card. twenty, a score (Gr.Gr. 15, 77, 149; Gr.M.; Rām. 410, 551, 630; K. 766, 913, 998, 1028). ¶ wuha-wuhurᵘ adj. (f. -wȧrishᵘ̈), twenty years old, twenty years of age. ¶ wuhan-andar adj. c.g. in twenty, i.e. (a person) in his (or her) twentieth year. -hondᵘ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of twenty, costing, or worth, twenty (rupees, etc.); of, or belonging to, twenty (persons, etc.).
f. (sg. dat. wuhüñᵘ̈), smouldering, keeping alight (Gr.Gr. 121), cf. the next; a certain disease of the rice-plant, in which the grain turns to powder (L. 335, wohan).
(? spelling) adv. thither, towards that direction (noted only in K.Pr. 236, uharin). Cf. yuhariñ, wuharyundᵘ, and yohuryundᵘ.
adv. a short distance from here, a short way off (u.w. vbs. of going, placing, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 94). Cf. wuhariñ, ohᵘryundᵘ, yohuryundᵘ.
f. the roar of a lion or tiger.
n.ag. (f. wuhavüñᵘ̈), that which glows, smoulders, keeps burning; met. one who feels a burning sensation (from anger, fever, thirst, or the like).
f. an old form of wūhᵘ̈, q.v.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. wuhyōv), to glow, smoulder, to keep burning without being extinguished (both lit. and also met. of anger, jealousy, thirst, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 121).
or ǖhᵘ̈ f. heat, calidity, high temperature. In L.V. 82, this word has the form wuhī, and is translated 'red hot coal'. wūha-wān or ṻha-wān m. a Turkish bath, sudatory, hammām.
pl. nom. (so many) twenties, the form used by wuh, twenty, q.v., in multiplication, as in kāh wuhⁱ zᵃh hath ta wuh, eleven twenties are two-hundred-and-twenty (Gr.Gr. 86).
or wuhy interj. indicating distress, Oh! Ah! --wāhy -- interj. id.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wujôrᵘ), to destroy utterly, raze to the ground, ruin; to lay waste, ravage, plunder, spoil; to depopulate. wujôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wujörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), razed to the ground; wasted, ravaged; depopulated.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wujᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. wujārun, q.v.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. wujᵃryōv), to be utterly destroyed, razed to the ground, ruined; to be laid waste, ravaged, plundered, spoiled; to be depopulated, be devoid of inhabitants.
in wūjᵘ khujᵘ adj. (f. wūjᵘ̈ khujᵘ̈), unfit, improper, unsuitable.

f. fatigue, weariness, exhaustion; cf. wukurᵘ. --wālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause exhaustion (by hard work) to be experienced. --wasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. fatigue to descend (upon a person), exhaustion (from hard work) to be experienced.
f. a destitute, unfortunate, woman, a poverty-stricken widow; cf. wuka and (l. 6, ab.) wukᵘ̈rᵘ̈.

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. wukȧrⁱladiñ) (of a man) exhausted and helpless owing to one's work or occupation having become futile; (of a woman) suffering great distress (due to widowhood, childlessness, poverty, and so on).
m. change for the worse, disease, malady; (of food, etc.) going bad, corruption, fermentation. --mukhāl -- m. cold in the head.

adj. (f. wukᵘ̈rᵘ̈), unfortunate, unsuccessful in work, in distress, poverty-stricken (K.Pr. 7); damaged, dented (of some thing) (K.Pr. 75); cf. wuka. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. (of a man) his occupation or work to become fruitless, profitless, futile, unsuccessful (and so to become exhausted, etc.); (of a woman) to be thrown into distress (by becoming a widow or other calamity). --dukurᵘ -- adj. (f. wukᵘ̈rᵘ̈ dukᵘ̈rᵘ̈), unfitting, unbecoming, improper, non-conforming, unsuitable. ¶ wukᵘ̈rᵘ̈  f. a widow (poverty-stricken, childless, etc.); cf. wukaröñᵘ̈.
(? spelling) adj. separate, apart (noted only in K.Pr. 106).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wukᵃrôwᵃ), to make crooked, to crooken (Gr.Gr. lxxii). Cf. wạkᵃr 2.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. wukᵃryōv), to be crooked (Gr.Gr. lxxii). Cf. wạkᵃr 2.

m. (sg. dat. wũ̄̈kis; abl. wō̃ki), a carved arch or curvature over and round a doorway, a carved doorframe with a pointed curved top (quasi niche-shaped), a similar pattern on a cloth, a paper, or the like. -tū̃kᵘ adj. overwhelmed by misery, poverty, ridicule, or the like. Reported as in very rare use. ¶ wǖ̃kⁱ-dār adj. c.g. (a cloth, paper, etc.) bearing the above pattern; a woman's hair braided in this shape. Cf. wö̃kh.
in wula-gāsa m. a kind of marsh grass which is used for making grass sandals.
f. a kind of paddy, the rice from which is a small, clean, fragrant grain (El. wúlag). wulȧgⁱ-byôlⁱ m. (sg. dat. -byölis), the same (esp. when kept for seed).
m. the remains of a meal (K.Pr. 109). Cf. walūsa 2.
in wulaṭh pulaṭh m. (sg. dat. wulaṭas pulaṭas), reversal, the being turned upside-down (of a thing, action, or condition); (among relatives or the like) reversal of friendly conditions. Cf. wulᵃṭa.

f. (sg. dat. wulaṭhüñᵘ̈), obstinacy, perverseness, refractorines (shown by a person asked or engaged to do some work); an obstacle (suddenly presenting itself in any work). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such obstinacy to be exhibited; such an obstacle to present itself.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. wulaṭhañĕladiñ), one who shows obstinacy or perverseness when asked to undertake any particular work, a disobliging fellow.
f. love, affection, being fond (for, or of, some special thing or work).
f. a meteor; a firebrand, torch; (in astrology) one of the eight principal daśās or aspects of planets indicating a person's fate (Skt. ulkā) (Rām. 420).
m. wages (of a workman, servant, or the like, paid regularly at fixed intervals, such as a month), pay, salary. -dar m. (f. -dariñ), a servant paid on such wages.

adj. c.g. and adv. reversed, turned back; upside-down, topsy-turvy; reverse, perverse; contrary, opposite (K. 38); of a contrary temper, cross-grained; (of a disease) refusing to yield to appropriate remedies, obstinate; (of a time, astrological moment) opposing, unpropitious, unlucky (Śiv. 1477). Cf. wulaṭh.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wulᵃṭôwᵃ), to reverse, put back to front, overturn, turn upside-down (K. 910). wulᵃṭôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. wulᵃṭövᵃ- müʦᵘ̈) (by someone) reversed, put back to front, overturned, turned upside-down.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. wulᵃṭyōv), (of a thing, action, etc.), to be reversed, put back to front, overturned, be turned upside-down; to reverse one's action, alter one's conduct in the opposite direction (K. 359); (conj. 1) to overturn (for wulᵃṭāwun, q.v.) (K. 909). wulᵃṭyō-motᵃ perf. part. (f. wulᵃṭyē-müʦᵃ), become reversed, put back to front, turned upside-down.
m. a small hole for ventilation or light (Gr.Gr. 17). Cf. wọ̆bᵘ.
adj. (f. wūjⁱ or wūjᵘ̈, dat. wōjĕ), one who has an uncertain temper, one who is easily moved to anger, irascible, irritable, nervous (Gr.Gr. 31, 141). Cf. wōjĕr and wōlun.
in wūlⁱyā gāsa adj. c.g. (of thread, flowers, vegetables, etc.), mixed with dirt or foreign matter (and hence valueless).

f. N. of the daughter of Daksh (Dakṣa) and wife of Shiv (Śiva) (in Skt. Umā). Being insulted at Dakṣa's sacrifice, she threw herself into the fire, and was subsequently reborn as Pārvatī, the whole story being the subject of Śiv. She is Śiva's śakti (see shĕktⁱ) or Energic Power (Śiv. 34, 888, 1115, 1143, 1165, 1186, 1617, 1762; Rām. 590, 1181, 1513 ff., 1527). wumādar m. N. of Śiva (Śiv. 1165). wumādēvī f. c.g. Wumā (Śiv. 63, 196). wumānāth m. N. of Śiva (Śiv. 760, 768). wumāpati m., id. (Śiv. 154, 370). wumārudr m. Umā and Rudra (i.e. Śiva) looked upon as one, Śiva together with his Energic Power, as one conception (Śiv. 39, 57, 62).
a neg. adv. (vill.) not now (cf. wŏñ, wõ̆h) (H. ii, 11).

or wumürᵘ̈ (= عمر) f. (sg. obl. wumri, Rām. 1780), lifetime, period of life (K.Pr. 56, wumr; Śiv. 423; K.Pr. 41, 56, 87, 143, 204); age, time of life (El. umr, umar, m.; Rām. 1740 wumar, m.c.; 1781). ¶ wumarĕ-boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), senior, of great age, old (as compared with contemporaries). -zyūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈), aged, old, long-lived; (in blessings or the like) long-lived, having a long life.

f. blindness, want of sight (K. 449); bad luck, failure (cf. wunun) (Gr.Gr. 122). --wasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. blindness to descend (on a person); met. to become distracted (e.g. from overwork, fear, anxiety, or the like); to be, or become, devoid of respect (to one's superiors). -wathar f. 'spreading of blindness', i.e. extreme agitation, distraction, or alarm (quasi, as if caused by a sudden attack of blindness). -wathar gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. such extreme agitation to occur (to a person).
f. mist, fog (El. wunar, wunir, m.), i.q. wunar, q.v.
f. mist, fog (cf. pŏhⁱ-wunar, p. 684b, l. 9) (El. wunar, wunir, m.) (Gr.Gr. 15, Gr.M., Śiv. 331), i.q. wunal, q.v.
m. ill-luck, want of success after long and strenuous effort. Cf. wunun.
m. a dog's howl (cf. shāla-wung, p. 880a, l. 24) (Gr.Gr. 122, 125).
m. the howl of a dog (i.q. wung, q.v.).
