f. sleeplessness (caused by anxiety or the like) (Gr.Gr. 122, where it is connected with wunga 1, 125). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such sleeplessness to occur (to a person).
adj. c.g. (of a dog) given to howling, a howler; (of a man) given to uttering howling cries, or one whose ordinary speech resembles a howl.
n.ag. (f. wungavüñᵘ̈) (a dog or the like) who keeps on howling; (of a human being, esp. a child or one ignorant) one who howls (e.g. for something he wants but doesn't get).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wungᵘ, f. wunjᵘ̈; 2 p.p. wunjyōv), to howl (of a dog or the like) (cf. shāla-wᵒ, p. 880a, l. 25) (Gr.Gr. 122, 125; cf. W. 2, ūngān, the cry of a fox); (of a human being or the like) to utter a similar sound.
m. the time occupied in opening the eye, the twinkling of an eye, an infinitesimal moment of time; opp. to nimēsh, q.v., the time occupied in closing the eye (Śiv. 1069, 1427).
adv. now, at the present time (cf. wŏñ), used in the following:-- wuñukh-tām, or -tāmath, or -tāñ, or -tāñĕth adv. up to now, till now, up to the present time.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. wunyōv), fate to be against one, to be unlucky in result, success to fail after long and strenuous effort; to be ill-starred (cf. döv wᵒ) (Gr.Gr. 122, Rām. 1603). wunyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wunyē-müʦᵘ̈) (of some labour, journey, exertion, or the like) ill-fated, having disastrous result, having fate against it in the result; ill-starred.

m. (sg. dat. wunībis), delusion, mistake, error (when something is expected or longed for, and something else turns up and is mistaken for it). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such a delusion to occur (esp. over and over again). --karun -- m.inf. to distress by (over and over again) deluding, as ab.

or wuñᵉ̆kĕnas adv. now, at the present time, at this time (e.g. 'at this time to-morrow') (cf. wŏñ) (Śiv. 634, 841, 1713, 1718-9; Rām. 150, 492, 680, 791, 808, 852, 997, 1155, 1204, 1220, 1222-3, 1228, 1460, 1527, 1702; K. 1099, 1112, wuñkĕn). -bögⁱ or -bögin adv. about now, at about the same time as now on some other day. ¶ wuñᵉ̆kĕnukᵉ̆ adj. gen. (f. wuñᵉ̆kĕnücᵉ̆), of, or belonging to, the present time, contemporary.
m. (sg. abl. wōni), a kind of dish made of fried uncrushed kernels of the water-chestnut, eaten when, owing to a vow, the eating of rice and other similar food is forbidden.
(f. wūñᵘ̈), 1 p.p. of wōnun, q.v., used --˚, as in aḍa-wūnᵘ, half-woven, p. 12a, l. 50.

m. (of something inanimate) inward burning or heat, internal smouldering; inward rotting (due to fermentation and consequent heat); (of a human being) inward anger, resentment; cf. wupun. --khasun -- m.inf. spontaneous internal combustion or rotting to occur (e.g. in a pile of grain, or a heap of wood, a pile of uncared-for garments). -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), burnt or rotted internally, as ab.; full of resentment. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. (of a heap of grain, a pile of wood, or the like which has been allowed to become damp) to begin to rot or burn from internal heat; (of a human being) to begin to feel resentment.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. wupaladiñ) (of a pile of paddy or the like) gone bad by internal fermentation or internal spontaneous combustion. Cf. wupa.
m. N. of certain mystic writings of the Hindūs (Śiv. 21). Borrowed from Skt. upaniṣad.
adv. above, up. -cūṭī adv. superficially, without going into (a matter) thoroughly, skimming over the surface, cursorily. (Said not to be a genuine Ksh. word, but to be borrowed from India.)

(occasionally spelt wŏph, q.v.) f. (sg. dat. wuphi), the act of flying or soaring, flight (Gr.Gr. 127; Śiv. 1052, 1607); met. moving, or going, rapidly or quickly. --tulüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to fly up (Rām. 531). wuphi adv. very quickly, speedily (u.w. vbs. of going, coming, seeing, beginning, completing, or the like).
in wuphal-wāl m. i.q. wŏphar-wāl, s.v. wŏphurᵘ, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wuphalôwᵘ), to encourage (an ignorant child or the like) to persevere (in acquiring skill), incite (Gr.Gr. 170). wuphalôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wuphalövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), encouraged in perseverance, as ab. See wuphun.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. wuphalyōv) (of some ignorant boy or the like) to be, or become, persevering or energetic (by continual practice).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wuphanôwᵘ), to cause to fly (Gr.Gr. 170; Śiv. 351, 1064, 1396, 1693, 1783, 1811); (of a mother-bird) to teach (her chicks) to fly; to fly (a kite, etc.) (Gr.M.); to drive (a horse or vehicle) at great speed. wuphanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wuphanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), taught to fly, as ab.; driven very fast, as ab.
m. a bird (El. upháún, ? wuphawunᵘ, q.v.).

f. the act of flying, or going swiftly in wuphawañĕy raṭañĕ f.pl. (with emph. y) (simultaneous) flyings and stoppages, i.e. imagining impossibilities, describing or asking someone to believe an impossibility, attempting an impossible task.
n.ag. (f. wuphavüñᵘ̈), one who flies, (a bird or the like) which habitually flies (K. 922; K.Pr. 235, m. pl. nom. wufawane); (a man, horse, vehicle, or the like) which moves with great rapidity.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. wuphyōv), to fly, soar, go flying (Gr.Gr. 15, 127; conjugated, 224, 234, 237, 239, 240-1, 245-6; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1516, 1694, 1811); to go, or move, rapidly or quickly; (of a human being or the like) to become intoxicated (by drugs, or pride, or the like). ¶ wuphān pres. part. used as adv. flying; hence, as adv., very quickly or rapidly (u.w. vbs. of going, arranging, eating, and so on). ¶ The causal of this verb is either wuphanāwun, which means 'to cause to fly', or wuphalāwun which means 'to incite' (Gr.Gr. 170).

f. (of a heap of dried cowdung, wood, grain, or the like) internal combustion, internal fermentation, or the like (i.q. wupa, q.v.) (Gr.Gr. 120); (of dried cowdung on a hearth) taking fire (from contact with the burning coals). --ʦhunüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to set burning internally (a pile of dried cowdung, straw, or the like, or fuel on a hearth).

m. affectionate respect (such as might be paid to an elder, a friend, or relation). --barun -- m.inf. to show such respect (by appropriate conduct). ¶ wuprīda-vyotᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ʦᵘ̈), one who is the worthy object of such respect; one who habitually shows such respect.

conj. 2 or 3 (see Gr.Gr. 204-5) (1 p.p. wupᵘ, 2 p.p. wupyōv), (of a heap of dried cowdung, a pile of wood, straw, paddy, clothes, or the like) to burn internally (by spontaneous combustion, or otherwise), to smoulder internally, ferment internally (Gr.Gr. 120, 204-5); met. to rot, or decay internally (owing to fermentation and consequent heat); (of a human being) to feel inward wrath, to be filled with resentment; cf. wupa. wupyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wupyē-müʦᵘ̈), internally burnt or fermented, as ab.; filled with resentment, as ab.
or in wūr-taishūr (Śiv. 871), see wūrᵘ shūrᵘ, s.v. wūrᵘ 2, bel. The words should probably be written wūrᵘ tay shūrᵘ, in which tay is the conjunction 'and'.
m. a big, fat, fool, an oaf. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), an entire (uncastrated) ram (as distinct from bāla- kaṭh, a castrated ram) (L. 463, wur).

f. a kind of large, long, cooking-stove, with many openings (usually set up temporarily on the occasion of feasts or the like, when much cooking is necessary) (cf. nāra-wᵒ, p. 648b, l. 19) (Gr.Gr. 165 wur, K.Pr. 85). -bal m. the place where this long cooking-stove is set up (Gr.Gr. 165); the presents given by the guests at such a festival as a wedding, boy's tonsure, or the like. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to set up such a long cooking-stove; (met.) (in complimentary speech to the host or the like) to give a large dinner party. -tāv m. the intense heat of such a cooking-stove; hence, enthusiasm, zeal, ardour, or vehemence (which after a while quickly cools down).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wuranôwᵘ), to cause (beads, etc.) to be strung (on a thread, etc.) (K. 954). Causal of wurun 1, q.v.

in wurāṭh purāṭh na bōzun m.inf. not to consider the beginning and the end, not to consider the past and the future, to show rashness, to act precipitately or without discrimination (cf. rāṭh wurāṭh bōzun, p. 848b, ll. 45 ff.).
m. (a borrowed Skt. expression) the act of going upwards, ascending into the sky (L.V. 38).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wurᵘ), to thread or string (beads or the like) (Śiv. 338); to thread (a needle or the like); to thrust (a person, etc.) into a hollow or narrow space (lit. or met.). wurᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. wurᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of a bead or the like) threaded, strung; (of a needle, etc.) threaded; (of a person, etc.) thrust into a narrow space (lit. or met.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wurᵘ) (of a person lying on a bed) to cover with bed-clothes, to pull up the bed-clothes, wrap oneself up in bed-clothes (cf. phakas wurun tulun and ʦhunun, p. 689a, ll. 30, 33) (El. wurun, m. bed-clothes; K.Pr. 155, 205, 236); cf. Hindī ōṛhnā. wurᵘ-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. wurᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), having the whole body covered, or wrapped up, in bed-clothes.
m. (sg. dat. wuranis), bed-covering, bed-clothes, a quilt, blanket. ¶ wurȧnⁱ-palav m. a light bed-blanket (or the like). -züṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -zacĕ), an old ragged blanket (or the like).

m. (sg. dat. wuranis), a kind of prop carried on a long journey by a laden coolie on which, when resting, he supports the weight of the load on his back without removing it. wurȧnⁱ-mȧnzil m. a stage, or the length of a journey, between two such rests.
f. a kind of light movable partition for dividing up a room into sections as required.
f. N. of a famous Apsaras or nymph of Indra's heaven (Skt. Urvaśī) (Śiv. 1454).

or, also written wūrⁱ or adv. even there (Gr.Gr. 156); to or at some indicated place, here, there, hither, thither (as in wūry yima, we shall come here; wūry gaʦhav, we shall go there); there (in the sense of 'back again') (u.w. vbs. of bringing, and the like); cf. ōr 1 and Gr.Gr. 156. wūry na yūry (with variant spellings as ab.) adj. c.g. '(neither) there nor here'; hence, one who is bewildered, distracted, unable to make up his mind.
f. (sg. dat. wōrĕ), a washable cover put outside a wadded (and hence unwashable) quilt to keep it clean (cf. lēphi-wᵒ, p. 528b, l. 29). wōri-tolᵘ m. a wadded quilt (protected as ab.).

or (sometimes, as bel.) worᵘ 4 adj. (m. abl. sg. wari; f. nom. wurᵘ̈), thriving, stout, flourishing, in good state, well (cf. orᵘ wurᵘ, p. 42a, l. 21); (of metal, wood, cloth, or the like) stout, strong. --khurᵘ -- adj. (f. wurᵘ̈ khurᵘ̈), (of something, such as a rope or cloth, made of thread) badly put together (i.e. badly twisted or woven, or sewn together) and hence useless; met. an action which gives rise to objectionable results (such as agitation, some accusation, or scandal). ¶ wurⁱ-kyulⁱ m. (sg. dat. -kilis), inconsiderate boldness, disobedient audacity, audacious mischievousness. ¶ wari gōmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), (of some one formerly emaciated, or of some work or business formerly failing) become stout and sturdy, become flourishing. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become flourishing, as ab. (cf. thari-pōsh wari gaʦhȧnⁱ, p. 983b, l. 16) (Śiv. 1061, K.Pr. 215). --karun -- m.inf. to cause to flourish, to make stout and well. ¶ worᵘ norᵘ 1 (for worᵘnorᵘ 2, see s.v.) adj. (f. vürᵘ̈ nürᵘ̈), good in some particulars and not good in others, of mixed or varying quality (e.g. a garment, a coverlet, or a house).
m. the small shoulder round the open mouth of a cooking-stove, on which the cooking-vessel rests (made of half-baked earth).
m. rice boiled dry (cf. vürᵘ̈ 1) (Gr.Gr. 17). --bata -- m. well-cooked rice (in which the grains are separate, and not clotted together) (K.Pr. 205, wura bata).

also written, in the following:-- wūrᵘ shūlᵘ adj. agitated, distracted, overwhelmed by trouble (esp. used of some person not grown up, under the influence of anger, grief, sickness, rash conduct, or the like). --shūrᵘ -- adj. one who is agitated, distracted, talking incoherently, etc., as ab. (esp. used as ab.); cf. wūr taishur (probably wūrᵘ tay shūrᵘ, tay being the conj. 'and') in Śiv. 871, where it means 'incoherent speech', 'nonsense'. Cf. wūry na yūry, s.v. wūry.
in wus-gagar (El. and W. us˚) for wuʦha-gagur, q.v., s.v. wuʦha.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wusarôwᵘ), i.q. wusarun, q.v. wusarôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wusarövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), i.q. wusorᵘ-motᵘ, q.v. under wusarun. wusarāwana yunᵘ m.inf. pass. i.q. wusarana yunᵘ, under the same.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wusorᵘ), to open, untie (a tied-up load, parcel, or the like); cf. wusuṭᵘ. wusorᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wusürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), untied, as ab. wusarana yunᵘ m.inf. pass. to become untied, as ab.
m. (sg. dat. wusatas), breadth, width, expanse, vastness (of surface, time, quality, action, etc.).

m. a slight cry of pain (esp. when uttered by a woman on receiving a minor injury such as a scratch or a light blow) (cf. El. wosh, interj., Oh!); cf. wŏsh. El. also gives ush, tears; ush pakun, tears to flow; and ush tráwun, to weep.

f.pl. barley, a collection of grains of barley (cf. hūnⁱ-wⁱ 1 and 2, p. 337a, ll. 28 ff.) (El. m. oats, barley. It is mostly eaten by Moslems. Kāshmīrī Hindūs eat the grain only in times of scarcity; W. 114, 115 wushuk; L. wiska, 330, Hordeum vulgare, 458; K.Pr. 84, 251). ¶ wushki-ôṭᵘ m. barley meal. -pholᵘ m. a single grain of barley; a few grains of barley. -pröjⁱ or -pröjᵘ̈ f. chopped-up barley straw and chaff (used as an ingredient of wall-plaster, etc.). -ʦŏ̈ṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ʦŏcĕ), barley bread (used as a remedy for rheumatism or pain in the side) (Gr.Gr. 74). -wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), barley porridge or gruel; coarsely ground barley (W. 115, wushuk wat, where wat is wrongly translated 'seam'). Cf. wāṭh 2.
or wushⁱnēr m. heat, warmth, warmness (cf. atha-wᵒ, p. 64b, l. 33; sŏkha-wᵒ, p. 905b, l. 33) (K.Pr. 51, 237).

postpos. (governing abl., and used with pronouns) for (such-and-such) a reason, for (such-and-such) a cause (cf. ami-wᵒ, p. 55a, l. 17; tami-wᵒ, p. 968a, l. 28; tawa-wᵒ, p. 969b, l. 23). ¶ Occasionally when added to a noun it forms an adj. c.g. as in sŏkha-wᵒ, causing happiness, p. 905b, l. 34.
or wushyunᵘ adj. (f. wushüñᵘ̈ or wushiñᵘ̈), warm, hot (cf. aḍa-wᵒ, p. 12b, l. 4; sŏkha-wᵒ, p. 905b, l. 30) (El. wushun; Gr.Gr. 94; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 236, f. sg. voc. wushini).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wushᵉ̆nôwᵉ̆), to heat, make hot, to warm, make warm (cf. atha wᵒ, p. 64b, l. 36) (El., Gr.Gr. 171, K.Pr. 9). wushᵉ̆nôwᵉ̆-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. wushᵉ̆növᵉ̆-müʦᵉ̆), heated, warmed (by someone or something).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. wushᵉ̆nyōv), to become warm, to be warm, be hot (El. wushnun). The causal of this verb is wushᵉ̆nāwun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 171). wushᵉ̆nyō-motᵉ̆ perf. part. (f. wushᵉ̆nyē-müʦᵉ̆), become warm.
m. a teacher, professor, master (Gr.M.; Rām. 1491; H. i, 13; ii, 1, 5, etc.; K.Pr. 170, 257); (in Ksh., esp.) a teacher of shawl-weaving apprentices (El.). Cf. wŏsta.
m. a garland used at sacrifices on the occasion of various Hindū festivals. Such garlands are used for decorating the jars, dishes, etc., containing the offerings.
adj. (f. wusüṭᵘ̈) (of a tied-up load, parcel, or the like) untied, loosened, opened, taken to pieces (El. wusuṭ, loose). Cf. wusarun.
m.pl. sweatings, perspiration (due to excessive exertion, pain, weakness, fear, or the like) (El. wúsawás).
f. the nature or condition of a camel, camelhood; (of a human being) acting like a camel (involving stupidity, and heedlessness in gait, eating, and general conduct). Cf. wū̃ṭh.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. wutāwalladiñ), one who is precipitate, hasty, rash.
m. haste, hurry, quickness; precipitancy, eagerness, impatience; restlessness, fidgetiness (El. utáwul, fickleness of disposition).

m. (sg. dat. wū̃ṭas, Gr.Gr. 51; f. wū̃ṭiñ, q.v., Gr.Gr. 38), a camel (cf. muji-wᵒ, p. 558b, l. 17) (El. unṭ, wúnṭ; Gr.Gr. 18, 38, 51; W. 134, wunṭh; K.Pr. 78, 235). ¶ wū̃ṭa-bār (sometimes spelt wū̃ṭha-) m. a camel's load, the goods loaded on a camel (H. i, 9, wū̃ṭa-bār; YZ. 420, wûnṭhah-b˚); met. an excessively heavy burden imposed upon a man (even if it is beyond his strength). -cŏbur adj. (f. -cŏbᵘ̈rᵘ̈), a camel lout, a hulky boor (described as a long-necked, tall, bulky fellow, who is brainless in what work he does, whose gait, manner of speech and of eating, and other forms of conduct are objectionable). The word is not confined to the male sex. -kö̆bᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a camel's hump (traditionally said to represent the grave of an ancient Moslem saint); met. any hump-shaped article fixed firmly on its base. -naʦun m. (sg. dat. -naʦanas), 'a camel's dance', useless labour, lost labour, labour in vain. -raz f. a rope of camels, i.e. a line of camels connected together by a rope running through the nose-ring of each; a collection of people all mutually united by one reason (such as mutual friendship, relationship, common occupation, and so on). -ʦolᵘ m. one who walks like a camel (without heading hollows and heights, shortest or longest way, and so on); hence, one who acts without discrimination, one who acts unreflectingly. -ʦopᵘ m. 'camel-bitten'; hence, one, unable himself to think or understand, who acts properly or improperly only in obedience to another, one who is a mere docile machine.

m. (sg. dat. wuṭhas; obl. wuṭha 1), the lip (of the face) (cf. shĕkar-wᵒ, p. 878b, l. 45) (El. wuṭ, wuṭh; Gr.Gr. 15; Gr.M.; Śiv. 66, 539, 830; Rām. 724, 1266, 1393, 1708; YZ. 75). ¶ wuṭha-ʦhyonᵘ adj. (f. -ʦhë˘ñᵘ̈), one who has a torn lip, or a gap in the lip (owing to some wound or accident). -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), one who (by a surgical operation, or by some accident) has a cut lip, or a piece of lip cut off; hare-lipped. -vyoṭhᵘ adj. (f. -vë̆ṭhᵘ̈), thick-lipped, swollen-lipped.

(cf. wuṭhun) in wuṭh-paṭã̄g m. extreme harassment of another, violence (e.g. by making him give something, goading him into doing something impossible, or making charges against him). -paṭã̄g tulun m.inf. to harass in this way. -paṭã̄g wŏthun m.inf. such harassment to happen (e.g. by violence, attacks, uproar, etc.). -paṭö̃gⁱ adj. c.g. one who habitually harasses, as ab.
adj. c.g. one who has a deformed lip.

f. (sg. dat. wuṭhüñᵘ̈), the act of twisting (cf. atha-wᵒ, p. 64b, l. 49) (Gr.Gr. 121); a screw (El.). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give a twist (to something loose or lax, such as a rope or the like, in order to tighten it up). --yiñᵘ̈-- f.inf. 'twisting up to come (to a person)', to show more and more persistence the more one's entreaties are refused.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wuṭhanôwᵘ), to cause (a rope or the like) to be twisted; to harass (a person) by causing the police, etc., to bring accusations (of theft or the like) against him.

f. twisting, coiling; twisting a rope or the like; a twist, coil (El. wuṭhin, Gr.Gr. 120, K.Pr. 178); persistence or obstinacy (in insisting in undertaking some work in spite of another's objections). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. obstinacy or persistence in carrying out some work to occur.
adj. c.g. reckless, inconsiderate (in urging others to carry on work, while inactive oneself).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. wuṭhᵘ, f. wuṭhᵘ̈, f.dat. wuchĕ; 2 p.p. wuchyōv), to twist, screw, wring (cf. atha wᵒ, p. 64b, l. 50; gō̃ʦha wuṭhañĕ, p. 313a, l. 6) (Gr.Gr. 15, 120-1); to twist (as in making a rope or the like) (cf. anga wᵒ, p. 33b, l. 14; atha wuṭhüñᵘ̈, p. 65a, l. 2) (Gr.M., L.V. 107); to coil round and round (something to strengthen it, or to strengthen a joint); to entangle; (met.) to wring (a person's feelings), to hurt his feelings by subjecting him to violent abuse or accusations, no matter how much he shows humility and entreats (cf. wān wuṭhȧnⁱ, p. 1120b, l. 49). ¶ wuṭhᵘ-motᵘ (f. wuṭhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), twisted, etc., as ab.; hurt in the feelings, as ab. ¶ wuṭhana yunᵘ m.inf. pass. to become twisted, as ab.; to become the subject of violent abuse or accusations, as ab., the more one pleads and shows humility; (of a disease or the like) the more remedies are applied, to entangle (i.e. get hold of) the patient the more.
m. a cross-beam supporting the upper floor or roof of a house. wuthȧrⁱ-mọ̆nḍⁱ m. the block of wood that supports this beam and keeps it in its place.

m. (during a shower of rain) the water that drips from the eaves of a house (Gr.Gr. 15, wuth; Śiv. 338). ¶ wuthⁱ-dag f. the fall of a torrent of water from the eaves. -dāra f.pl. a stream of water from the eaves.
1 p.p. of wuṭhun, q.v. used --˚ as adj. in aḍa-wuṭhᵘ, half-twisted, p. 12b, l. 8, q.v.
(sometimes, e.g. p. 595b, l. 21, spelt wū̃ṭᵘ̈) f. (sg. dat. wṻchĕ or, sometimes, wū̃cĕ), a kind of large earthenware jar or vat (cf. masa-wū̃ṭᵘ̈, p. 595b, ll. 21 ff.) (K.Pr. 139).
(sometimes written wū̃ṭhiñ) f. of wū̃ṭh, q.v., a she-camel (El. unṭín, wútinyi; Gr.Gr. 38; YZ. 419, 421, wûṁṭhiñ).

in wutra-buñulᵘ m. utter prostration, the being rendered exhausted by attempting to perform excessive labour beyond one's power, or by too severe a strain; the being stunned (by a blow on the head or other violence). Cf. wathurᵘ. -buñulᵘ mēlun m.inf. such prostration or stunning to be experienced. -buñulᵘ milanāwun m.inf. to cause such prostration to another (e.g. by imposing too heavy a load upon him), to stun (by a blow on the head), etc., as ab. -buñulᵘ milawun m.inf., id. -buñulᵘ tulun m.inf. to cause such prostration by a blow or other violence.

adv. on the day before yesterday, i.q. ōtra, q.v. wūtra-kani adv. about, probably, the day before yesterday (Gr.Gr. 159, ṻtra-kani). See ōtra-kani or ṻtra-kani, p. 68b, l. 21. wūtrukᵘ (f. wūtrücᵘ̈), of, belonging to, born, or produced on the day before yesterday.
m. twisting, wrenching, sprain, dislocation of the foot, knee, or other lower limb. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such twisting, etc., to occur.
in mas-wū̃ṭᵘ̈, etc., p. 595b, ll. 21-2, i.q. wū̃ṭhᵘ̈, q.v.
n.ag. (f. wuyĕvüñᵘ̈), that which becomes sufficient, as in wuyun, q.v.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. wuyyōv), to be sufficient, to be the right amount (e.g. sufficient goods for division among a number of people, or sufficient materials or appliances for completing any work, and so on); cf. way 1 and L. 464 wáyun, ll. 11 ff. ab. wuyyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wuyyē-müʦᵘ̈), become, or found to be, sufficient, as ab.
m. an udder. --wālun -- m.inf. (of a cow) 'to bring down the udder', to show signs of being about to calve (by the udder becoming swollen).

m. the doorway, or entrance, of a house (Śiv. 1080). -bar m. the door of such a doorway. -nyās m. the lintel of such a doorway. ¶ wuza-baran f. (sg. dat. -barüñᵘ̈), a lightly built door in such a doorway.
m. brilliancy, lustre, radiance; (of a human being) comeliness united with brilliancy of intellect, brilliance, illustriousness (K. 987).

or (Rām. 1545) wuzamala f. lightning (cf. nāra-wᵒ, p. 648b, l. 22) (El. uzmal, wuzmal, wuzmala, all m., and wuzamal, f., a flash; Gr.Gr. 15; Gr.M.; L. 461; Śiv. 268, 575, 1374, 1538, 1558, 1742, 1868; Rām. 482, 862, 1017, 1545; K.Pr. 253). Cf. wūz.

also written wŏᵒ conj. 1 (1 p.p. wuzanôwᵘ), to awaken (a person from sleep), rouse (a person from a faint, unconsciousness, or the like) (El. woz˚; Gr.Gr. 171; Gr.M.; L.V. 105; Śiv. 352, 1478, 1631, 1709, 1883; Rām. 486, 909; K. 605; K.Pr. 64); cf. wuzawun. wuzanôwᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. wuzanövᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), awakened, aroused, as ab.
possessing radiance, radiant, lustrous, brilliant; (of a human being) beautiful and at the same time illustrious and brilliant in intellect. Cf. wūz.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. wuzowᵘ), i.q. wuzanāwun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 171).

f. a spontaneous issuing forth (of water from a mountain source), a spring (cf. nāga-wᵒ, p. 624a, l. 45) (Gr.Gr. 120); met. the first appearance or manifestation (of something) (cf. nāra-wᵒ, p. 648b, l. 23).

conj. 2 or 3 (1 p.p. wuzᵘ 2, for 1, see s.v.; 2 p.p. wuzyōv or wuzōv, Gr.Gr. 226) to spring forth, appear or issue spontaneously (as water from a mountain source, or steam appearing from something) (Gr.Gr. 17, 120, 171; Śiv. 191, 1592, 1842); (of a thought or circumstance) to appear spontaneously to the mind, to strike one (Gr.Gr. 226; L.V. 39, 40; K. 266); (of desire) to become aroused (H. viii, 11); to become wide awake, to awake from sleep, to come to one's senses out of a faint (cf. wudun) (El., Gr.Gr. 226, Rām. 674, K.Pr. 95); (of wind or the like) to be aroused, to rise (Śiv. 1706). ¶ wuzᵘ-motᵘ 1 perf. part. (f. wuzᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ 1), awakened from sleep, come to out of a faint. ¶ wuzō-motᵘ or wuzyō-motᵘ 2 perf. part. (f. wuzyē-müʦᵘ̈), sprung forth, issued spontaneously, as ab.; (a thought, etc.) which has spontaneously occurred to the mind, as ab. See Gr.Gr. 226.
(for 2, see wudun and wuzun), f. of wudᵘ, q.v.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. wuʦanladiñ) (of food) somewhat burned (in the cooking); (of a human being) resentful (cf. wuʦüñᵘ̈).
m. alertness, in atha-wᵒ, q.v. p. 65a, l. 7.

adj. c.g. alert and industrious, energetic (cf. atha-wᵒ, p. 65a, l. 11); cf. wuʦun. -gagur m. (f. -gagᵘ̈rᵘ̈), the flying fox (El. usgagar, flying fox or flying squirrel, wútsagagar or wutsah-gagur, flying fox; L. 112, wutsagagar, flying fox; W. 115, wuʦagagur, flying fox, usgagur, flying squirrel). --prang -- m. a flying couch, equivalent to the flying carpet of fairy-tales (H. xii, 18).
f. alert energy (esp. for one's own benefit, or in cheating others), smartness.
f. the occurrence of burning or scorching of food in the process of cooking (K.Pr. 150). Also, another form of wuʦüñᵘ̈, q.v.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. wuʦyōv, Gr.Gr. 224) (of food being cooked) to be burnt or scorched by exposure to too great heat (cf. K.Pr. 150); cf. wuʦüñᵘ̈ (see Gr.Gr. 192). --khasun -- m.inf. such burning to occur. --karun -- m.inf. to give evidence of being burnt in the cooking (e.g. when the smell betrays the fact). ¶ wuʦan-lôdᵘ m. 'a lump of burning', (of food) the being burnt through and through by exposure to too hot a fire, the being spoiled by being over-burnt. -wāza m. a cook who habitually burns the food in cooking, a bad cook; met. one who habitually spoils work entrusted to him.

conj. 1. (This verb is throughout impersonal, and in tenses formed from the past participle is always in the feminine gender. The person is indicated by a pronominal suffix in the dative. Thus, wuʦĕs, there will be resentment to him, i.e. he will feel resentment; wuʦᵘ̈s, there was inward resentment to him, he felt resentment, see Gr.Gr. 120, 182, 188, 192, 203, 215, 220, 234, 248-9, 254. 1 p.p. f. wuʦᵘ̈), 'burning to occur'; hence (between persons hitherto friendly) resentment, enmity, hostility, a quarrel to spring up (Gr.Gr. as ab.). Cf. wuʦun.

. The twenty-first (or, if we count the aspirates ch, kh, ph, th, ṭh, and ʦh, and also the sibilant sh, as separate letters, the twenty-eighth) consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet when written in the Roman character, the twenty-sixth (or, if we count ʦ, tsh, and z, as separate letters, the twenty-ninth) consonant when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the thirty-fifth consonant when written in the Perso-Arabic character. Its Kāshmīrī name is yāwa yö, and it is sounded like the y in the English word 'yes'. ¶ As in the case of the letters ñ and sh, the inherent vowel of this letter is ĕ, not a, so that must be transliterated yĕ, not ya. Thus, for example, bad, is in this Dictionary transliterated yĕch, not yach; yesterday, is transliterated yĕwa; and, a rule, is transliterated niyĕm. ¶ When the syllable yĕ immediately follows a consonant, it is sounded as ĕ, not as yĕ, and is, in fact, the usual representative of the vowel ĕ in writing. Thus, is the only way of spelling Vĕth, the Ksh. name of the River Jihlam, and represents bĕñĕ, a sister. For the further changes of this ĕ under the influence of mātrā-vowels, see p. 3a, ll. 14 ff. In the Perso-Arabic character, the sound of ĕ is represented by zēr, so that for these two words we have وِتہ and بِنِ, respectively. ¶ In Kāshmīrī, the sounds of ĕ, i, and ī cannot begin a word or syllable. Even if they are so written, they are always, in such a position, sounded as if a y was prefixed. Thus, initial ē is sounded as yē, initial i as yi, and initial ī as yī. In this way ēr, wool, is pronounced yĕr; ih, this, is pronounced yih; and ĩran, an anvil, is pronounced yīran. In the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, such an initial letter is optionally written with or without the, so that these three words may be written or, or or or, respectively, but they are always pronounced with the initial y, as yēr, yih, and yīran, and are so spelt in the Roman character in this Dictionary. In the Perso-Arabic character, the initial y is usually written as in یِیرن، یِہ، ییر, respectively. The only exceptions occur in the transliteration of a few Sanskrit words, as in اِیشُر, for yīshŏr, i.e. Skt. īśvara. ¶ Kāshmīrī follows other Dardic languages in optionally inserting a y-sound before a non-initial u-sound, exactly as in English the word 'duty' is pronounced 'dyuty'. As the insertion of this y-sound is optional, and largely depends upon the personal equation of the speaker, it is rarely indicated in writing, but written doublets do occasionally occur, such as tuzᵘ or tyuzᵘ, a radish, and ṭū̃ṭhᵘ or ṭyū̃ṭhᵘ, a certain bird. Extreme instances of this are found in the Kāshmīrī words for 'thou' and 'two'. The original word for 'thou' was *tū. This became *tyū, but under the ordinary phonetic rules of the language (cf. p. 960a, l. 26) the ty became ʦ, so that *tyū became *ʦū. Then, under another phonetic rule, ū became ᵃ (cf. mᵃtra- mūtra-, sᵃtra- sūtra-, and the Persian pronunciation of tū, thou, and dū, two, as tŭ and dŭ, respectively), so that the next stage was *ʦᵃ. To this, in order to aid the pronunciation, hā-ĕ-nuḵẖtafī was added, and the final Kāshmīrī form is ʦᵃh. It may be added that, while this word is usually written or in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, in some MSS. we find the word regularly written or. The history of the word for 'two' follows exactly the same lines, viz. *dū > *dyū > *zū > *zᵃ > zᵃh.

or yi 1, a representation of the Persian iẓāfat when following a vowel, as in hawāla-y-khŏdā, in the care of God (H. x, 7); wāda-y-khŏdā, an oath of (i.e. by) God (H. xii, 7, 15); dwā-yi-khör, a prayer for welfare (H. i, 3); hawā-yi-asmān, the air of heaven (H. ii, 6).

conjnct. or (cf. wūlⁱ yā gāsa, p. 1113a, l. 43) (Gr.M.; W. 152; Śiv. 1015, 1907; Rām. 845, 863, 1067, 1069; K. 617; H. ii, 12; viii, 1). yā-na یا نہ conjnct. or not (Rām. 272); used as a particle to emphasize a question, as in yā-na gōkh-a, didst thou go?; yā-na wuchum-a, did I see?; yā-na bōzy-ā, will he hear? yā... na-ta... (cf. na-ta 2, p. 618a, l. 4), either... or (W. 153). yā-ta یا تہ conjnct. if, supposing, as in yā-ta kara bŏh, ada kari suh, if I do (it), then he will do (it); yā-ta wuchakh ʦᵃh, ada zānakh, if thou wilt look, thou wilt know, and so on. yā-tay conjnct. a particle implying contrast, indicating ability (as contrasted with another's inability), as in yā-tay korum, nata kȧrⁱzi-hē, note that I did (it), otherwise thou shouldst have done (it) (implying that the speaker had been able to do it, but that the person addressed had been unable); so, yā-tay khyōn, na-ta khĕta, note that he ate (it), otherwise eat (it thyself) (implying that while he could eat it, the person addressed could not) (El. yátai, or, and, (?) yátu, except; W. 99 yātai, either, or; K. 869). yā... yā..., either... or (W. 152; Rām. 371, 1364; H. x, 3, 7; xii, 9).
interj. O! Oh! yā bār sāhibō یا با صاحبو O Great God! (K.Pr. 210).
adj. finding, getting, used --˚, as in kam-yāb, hard to get, scarce, p. 442b, l. 24; kām-yāb, obtaining one's object, p. 447a, l. 25.

f. (sg. dat. ? yāci) (in some business conducted openly) the secret employment of means to effect the result (e.g. a bribe, secret commission, or the like). --hë̆ñᵘ̈ --  f.inf. to take a bribe, a secret commission, or the like. --hāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take secret revenge (e.g. to conceal one's power to interfere with some work on which an enemy is engaged, and on its completion suddenly and secretly to attack it).

m. remembrance, recollection (cf. yād pāwun, p. 810b, l. 38; yād pāwanāwun, p. 811a, l. 42) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 117, 1506, 1598; Rām. 289, 509, 667, 756, 833, 835); memory (Rām. 561; H. i, 7). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. memory to occur, to be remembered, to be learnt by heart; cf. --karun, bel. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take in mind, bear in mind (H. xii, 17). --karun -- m.inf. to recollect, remember, call to mind (El., Gr.M.); to commit to memory, repeat from memory (without having to read from any paper), to learn by heart; cf. --gaʦhun, ab. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. memory to fall (to a person), remembrance to be aroused (El. to remember (intrans.); Śiv. 73 caus., 440, 1002, 1002 caus., 1822 caus., 1884 caus., 1909 caus.; Rām. 431, 658, 771, 1535, 1630 caus.; H. iii, 5; vii, 20, 26; xii, 15; caus. vi, 11; K.Pr. 102). --thawun -- or --thāwun -- m.inf. to bear in mind, keep in memory, to remember, not to forget (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 596; Rām. 27, 994). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. memory to come to a person (El. to remember (intrans.); W. 88).
f. in the following:-- yād gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. punishment to be experienced (by a child, for the sake of correction). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to punish, correct, as ab.
(? spelling) conjnct. although (El., W. 99, 100). Cf. yȧd, yĕd.
m. a descendant of Yĕdu (Yadu), q.v. (Śiv. 1322; K. 18, 362, 438, 444, 464, 466-7, 615, 670, 686, 835, 852, 988, etc.); esp. a title of Krushn (Kṛṣṇa), who was one of these.

f. calling to mind; remembrance, recollection. --rōzüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. remembrance to continue, i.e. to remember one's own people by helping or supporting them in case of poverty; to arrange for the support of one's dependents after one's death. --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to bear (previous kindnesses) in mind, to arrange for doing kind actions in return for benefits previously received (e.g. when the original giver of the benefits is now in poverty), to show practical gratitude.
m. (among Hindūs) a sacrifice, sacrificial rite; a coloured circle, marked with mystic pictures and signs, employed in the worship of a god.
in yāgar pachiñ f. a legendary bird of monstrous size, capable of carrying away animals as large as a horse, like the roc of the Arabian Nights (Rām. 316, 694).
an old form of yūtᵘ 2, q.v., in L.V. 81.

f. the mane (of a horse) (W. 139, K.Pr. 71); met. fine dress, handsome apparel, good turn-out and general appearance (of a man) (K.Pr. 156). -cāl f. handsome dress, general appearance, and carriage (of a man). --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cut off a horse's mane (supposed to strengthen or increase the size of the neck). ¶ yāla-gupāl m. a dissipated dandy (cf. gōpāl, a N. of Kṛṣṇa, p. 294b, l. 19).
or (qq.v.) yāmath, yāmathᵘ̈y adv. even when, at the very time when, at the moment when, as soon as (El. yám; W. 93; Śiv. 1000, 1622; Rām. 706, 1634; YZ. 164, 229). Cf. yāñ and yāñĕth.

or yāmathᵘ̈y adv. i.q. yām, q.v., at the very time when, just when, as soon as (El. yámat; W. 93 yāmatai; Śiv. yāmath 767; Rām. id. 112, 239, 498, 538, 654, 703, 761, 1374, 1382, 1501, 1521, 1687, 1708, 1733, 1741; K. id. 1145); cf. yāñĕth and yāñ. tāmath.... yāmath.... so long.... as (H. xi, 20).
or yānī یعنی adv. that is to say, viz., i.e., to wit (El. yáne, Gr.M., Rām. 1015).
adv. when, at the time at which (i.q. yāñ, q.v.) (El. yányít). Cf. yāmath and yām.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. yāpanôwᵘ), caus. of yāpun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 175).

conj. 2 or 3 (1 p.p. yôpᵘ; 2 p.p. yāpyōv. The causal of this verb is yāpanāwun, not yöpᵃrāwun, Gr.Gr. 175), to be sufficient, be competent, to succeed in completing (some very difficult task), to be able (cf. atha yᵒ, p. 65a, l. 18); (in the distribution of food, etc., among a number of people, the food, etc.) to be sufficient, to be adequate, to go all round, to be enough. yôpᵘ-motᵘ  1 perf. part. (f. yöpᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), one who has competently carried out (a task or the like); (of food, etc., being distributed) found to be adequate for all. Cf. vyāpun 2.

m. a friend (cf. ādan-yᵒ, p. 14b, l. 46; atha-yᵒ, p. 65a, l. 21; bāla-yᵒ, p. 104b, l. 9; jāni yᵒ, p. 374b, l. 31; kana-yᵒ, p. 448b, l. 2; wata-yᵒ, p. 1156a, l. 5) (El.; W. 7, 114; L.V. 99, 100; Śiv. 1613, 1616, 1687, 1790; Rām. 93, 643, 833, 898, 1066, 1112, 1766; K. 1076, 1126-7; H. iv, 4, 7; v, 9; vi, 1; vii, 6; x, 1, 4, 6, 11; K.Pr. 46, 101, 137-8, 187, 240-1); a companion, comrade (cf. banga-yᵒ, p. 112b, l. 33; carsa-yᵒ, p. 176b, l. 22; pĕnji-yᵒ, p. 729a, l. 21) (El.); a lover, a beloved (YZ. 15, 29, 33, 37-8, 40, 43, 238, 245, 248-9, 260); (of a married woman) a husband (K.Pr. 194, sg. ag.); a place where friends (i.e. people in general) meet (such as a shop, a bathing-place on the bank of a river, or the like) (cf. wöñⁱ-yⁱ, p. 1128b, l. 6); met. 'The Friend', i.e. the spirit or soul of a man or woman, cf. 'hospes comesque corporis' (K.Pr. 50). --lāgun -- m.inf. to pretend to be a friend, show pretended friendship. --sapadun -- m.inf. to befriend (El.); to connive (at), to share, to be a party (to) (El.). ¶ yāra-bojᵘ m. a man (of any caste) who attends on the bathers at a bathing-place, and who is paid by fees or salary. -bal m. a bathing-place on the bank of a river or the like (where the people of the neighbourhood meet daily, and also where libations of water are offered to ancestors) (Gr.Gr. 165; W. 112; Śiv. 178, 1683, 1686; K. 971; K.Pr. 11); a quay, landing-place (El., Gr.M., Śiv. 1719, K.Pr. 178); cf. bal 3. -bal brôhmun m. (f. -bröhmüñᵘ̈, his wife), a low-class Brāhmaṇa who attends at bathing-places, and takes fees from the people on the occasion of eclipses and similar occurrences. -bal-kākañ f. a bathing-place sister-in-law; hence, a crony whose friendship was formed at a bathing-place (where women meet and gossip). -bal karun m.inf. (of a Hindū) to perform the daily ceremony of bathing at a bathing-place, as enjoined by the scriptures. -bal-pôwᵘ m. a single step in the flight of steps at a bathing-place. -bȧlⁱ gaʦhun m.inf. to bribe secretly (a judicial officer or the like). -bȧlⁱ yunᵘ m.inf. to bring a person over to one's own side by bribing (as ab.). -lay f. a friend's affection, loving companionship, loving devotion to a friend (K. 1076). -müʦᵘ̈ f. an adultress, a woman who is addicted to associating with lovers, a wanton. ¶ yār-i-jönī (m.c. for یار جان) m. a beloved friend (Rām. 14).
m. the town of Yārkand, in Central Asia (H. xi, 1).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. yôrᵘ), to be friendly (W. 114); hence in various metaphorical senses, such as to repay an obligation or kind action by another (Śiv. 954); to pay by set off, to take credit in account; to give credit for something not done, or a debt not paid (Śiv. 1582); to accept something of small value as the equivalent of something of great value (Śiv. 1687); to accept a small fine as requital for an offence that should be met with a long term of imprisonment; to ward off an approaching calamity by performing appropriate penances, sacrifices, or the like (and so satisfying fate). ¶ yôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. yörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), paid by set off (etc., as ab.). ¶ yörith dyunᵘ m.inf. to make over something or some work to the entire control of another person (as an equivalent for something else, or in order to gratify him). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. (a god, or some powerful person) to show mercy (to someone threatened with calamity, as a result of his prayers, repentance, or the like). --nyunᵘ -- m.inf. to take in exchange, or as an equivalent; to take something or some work entirely under one's own control (as ab.). --ʦhunun -- m.inf. forcibly to make over some difficult work to another (even if it is beyond his powers).

or yārᵘ̈zᵘ̈ f. friendship, affection (cf. atha-yᵒ, p. 65a, l. 24; gāna-yᵒ, p. 288a, l. 32; hāpath-yᵒ, p. 342b, l. 47; muṭhⁱ-phȧlⁱ-yⁱ, p. 605a, l. 15; nönⁱ-yⁱ, p. 640a, l. 34; wata-yᵒ, p. 1156a, l. 6) (El., L. 111, W. 21, K.Pr. 77); boon-companionship (cf. banga-yᵒ, p. 112b, l. 40; pĕnji-yᵒ, p. 739a, l. 23) (Gr.M. yārüzᵘ̈). --lāgüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to form or make a friendship.

f. a share of money given for help in the accomplishment of some particular work, a bribe, inducement to help. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take a gift as an inducement (i.e. as a bribe, as blackmail, or to abstain from an accusation).
for yĕth, see yih 2; for yith, see yih 1.
or yötᵃrā f. a journey, pilgrimage (Gr.M., Śiv. 1485); a company of pilgrims. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a large number of people to assemble in some place in order to set out on a pilgrimage.
m. N. of a king of Kābul (Skt. Yauvanâśva). He was father-in-law to Garga, and, through him, grandfather of Kālayavana (K. 622).

m. a dandy, fop, who is at the same time a debauchee, a fast gentleman, a rake (cf. tāpa-yᵒ, p. 1015a, l. 28). yāwa yö m. the name of the Śāradā character corresponding to the Nāgarī letter ya. -yĕṭh f. (sg. dat. -yĕṭi) fop-conceit, i.e. ostentation, posing as a wealthy person (esp. when one is not). Cf. yĕṭh 1.
f. foppish debauchery, loose living with fine apparel, libertinism.

f. assistance, aid; friendship; favour; (in Ksh.) fullness, completeness (such as fulfilling the demands of a lifelong friendship (Rām. 837), of the return made for a kind action, of the working out in this life of the results of actions performed in a former existence, or of welfare and prosperity lasting unbroken throughout one's life); indestructibility, the property of being everlasting.

m. (sg. dat. yāwanas), youth, prime or bloom of youth (of human being, beast, tree, etc.) (Śiv. 736, 1039, 1061, 1566; Rām. 554-5; K. baḍi yāwanas, in the full bloom of youth, 636; YZ. 517; K.Pr. 128, 257); adolescence, puberty (Śiv. 1791); beauty, adornment (W. 149, K.Pr. 260). --lagun -- m.inf. youth to be obtained, i.e. (of an old man, animal, tree, or the like) to become young again, to enjoy a second youth; the age of puberty to be reached. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. youth to be obtained (as ab.); the age of puberty to be reached (Rām. 629). ¶ yāwan-mad m. the intoxication, wantonness, or frolicsomeness of youth. -madun m. (sg. dat. -madanas), a youth who is, or was, the beloved of a girl's young days, a girl's first love; youthful days (looked upon as if they were as darling as a beloved). -müʦᵘ̈ f. a beautiful girl full of the frolicsomeness of youth. -rāy m. 'King Youth', a young man glorious in his youthfulness; the wealth, or fortune, of youth (i.e. beauty of form, strength, ability, joy, etc.). -vīrĕ f.pl. a group of small spots or pimples that appear on the face in the time of youth. ¶ yāwanas tāwan f. (so reported, but tāwan is masc.) sorrow in youth, i.e. terrible sorrow suddenly to befall one in the midst of happiness (quasi, the condition of a young beautiful wife, suddenly condemned to widowhood) (YZ. 553). --ʦhaṭa mārañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to bound up, or leap up, in youth, to display the frolicsomeness of youth.

or yāyum m. (sg. dat. yāyĕmas), employment on another person's business (instead of one's own). ¶ yāyĕm-gürᵘ̈ f. a maid-servant, i.e. an independent female working in another person's (and not in her own) house. -müʦᵘ̈ f. a woman who habitually and willingly does another's work as if it were her own.
m. a sacrificial ceremony, a sacrifice. In grāma-yāz, p. 303a, l. 18.
conj. 1. (1 p.p. yôzᵘ), to adore, worship (K. 416).
f. (see yāʦakh), a female beggar; the wife of a male beggar.
m. (sg. dat. yāʦakas, f.nom. yāʦakĕñ q.v.), a mendicant, beggar, suppliant. yāʦaka-bāv m. the condition, or occupation, of a beggar or suppliant (K. 1122).
f. request, solicitation, entreaty; begging, mendicancy.
interj. O! (L.V. 56 yē gŏrā, O teacher!).

m. concealment, or denial, of knowledge, evasion, going back from one's word. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to conceal, or deny, knowledge of something, to practise evasion, to go back from one's word. --karun -- m.inf., id. ¶ yĕba-dub m. evasion, as ab., esp. evasion of the return of something entrusted to the evader.
in yĕba-ʦüṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ʦacĕ), a clod-crusher, a maul or heavy club for breaking clods of earth (Śiv. 1531). Cf. yĕṭa- phürᵘ̈, s.v. yĕṭh 2.
m. (sg. dat. yĕbūsatas), dryness, acridity; (in Ksh.) dryness of the mouth (including throat, palate, tongue, and lips) (owing to disease).
c.g. one who conceals or denies knowledge of something, one who evades, one who goes back from his word.
m. and adj. c.g. a basket-bearer, a bearer who carries loads on his back in the basket called yüṭᵘ̈, q.v.; anything which is bent, humped, or crooked in the middle. Cf. yüṭᵘ̈.

or yẹ̆ch m. (sg. dat. yẹ̆chas; f. sg. nom. yẹ̆chiñ), a kind of demi-god attendant on Kubēra, the god of riches, and employed in guarding his treasures, etc. (Skt. yakṣa) (Rām. 1475, K. 123); (in Ksh.) a kind of fairy or Kobold (cf. bŏdⁱ-yⁱ, p. 83b, l. 46; gᵃsa-yᵃ, p. 307a, l. 34; pā̃-yᵒ, p. 748a, l. 38; ʦhŏṭa-yᵒ, p. 1063a, l. 50) (K. 299, spelt yĕʦhy); a hyena (El. yachh, K.Pr. 134). ¶ yẹ̆cha-(or yĕcha-)gaṭa  f. the pitch darkness of the night of the dark half of the winter month of Pŏh (December-January) (believed to be particularly haunted by these Kobolds). -khĕv m. a man (esp. a boy) who is deformed by having a limb or other member of the body missing (quasi, bitten off and eaten by one of these Kobolds). -phal adj. c.g. (of a crop or the like) bearing a great harvest (even though a very small amount of seed has been sown). -phū̃sⁱ f. a Yĕch's cap (see phū̃sⁱ, p. 711b, ll. 45 ff., where the legend on the subject is given) (K.Pr. 141). -phyār m. one (esp. a boy) who is very ugly, but at the same time sharp and intelligent. -pūtᵘ m. a Kobold's boy child; a human child who is ugly. -rṻph m. (sg. dat. -rṻpas), adj. c.g. deformed (El. yach-rúp). -shĕkᵃl adj. c.g. deformed (El. yach-shakl). -thaph f. (sg. dat. -thapi), a blow from a Kobold, i.e. an attack of epilepsy or the like (believed to be due to such demoniac possession). -ʦhyoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦhë˘ṭᵘ̈), 'a Kobold's leavings', a deformed morose person (quasi, who has been tormented and left crippled by a Kobold). -ʦọ̆lᵘ m. one who (esp. a boy) is hideous, ugly.
m. N. of one of the Parganas, or fiscal divisions, of Kashmīr (famous for its rice) (El. yach).

adj. c.g. wicked, bad, dissolute, depraved (El. yach; W. 21 yachh; Rām. 62, 64); hideous, ugly (Gr.M.); bad, unpleasing, horrid, terrible (Rām. 326, 437; K. 235). --khār -- adj. c.g. bad (and) vile, very bad, thoroughly base, utterly contemptible. --khār hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. --khār hishᵘ̈ --), thoroughly blameworthy, utterly vile. --khār karun -- m.inf. to disgrace (another, by abusing him publicly and proclaiming his vices or defects). --kömᵘ̈karawunᵘ̈ -- n.ag. (f. --kömᵘ̈ karavüñᵘ̈ --), an evil doer (El.). --karun -- m.inf. to disable (El.).

or yẹ̆chiñ f. of yĕch 1, q.v. a female fairy or Kobold; a Kobold's wife. ¶ yĕchiñĕ-(or yẹ̆chiñĕ-)pūtᵘ  m. a female Kobold's boy child (supposed always to accompany her); a human child who has been born as the result of worshipping a female Kobold. -ʦŏdāh f. (sg. dat. ʦŏdüshᵘ̈), the fourteenth lunar day of the light half of the month of Māg (January-February) on which worship is performed and offerings are made to a female Kobold.
(? spelling and gender) N. of a certain fibre plant, Abutilon Avicennae (L. 68 yechkar, 458 yechkár).
f. (sg. dat. yẹ̆chᵃrüñᵃ), the act of making bad, spoiling (a thing, work, etc.).

yid, yŏd 1 (for 2, see s.v.), yodᵘ, or yudᵘ, conjnct. if (El. yud; L.V. 18 yid; 23, 24 yudᵘ; Rām. yodᵘ, 33, 881, 1067, 1432, 1508, 1529, 1532, 1769, 1780; YZ. 27 yod); although, notwithstanding (El. yȧd, W. 100 yod). ¶ yŏd-nai conjnct. if not (Rām. 604). ¶ yĕd-wanay, yŏd-wanay, or yodᵘ-wanay conjnct. if, in case, provided that (El. yúduwane, yudwanai; L.V. 10 yodᵘ˚); although, notwithstanding (W. 100 yadwanai). ¶ yodwah, yĕduway, yidᵃway, yŏdwai or yodway conjnct. if (El. yudwai; Gr.M. yĕduwai; L.V. yidᵃway 64; Śiv. yŏdwai 558, 841, 1251; Rām. yodwai 151, 174, 326, 328, 330, 363, 366-7, 471, 504, 666, etc.; YZ. yodwah 198); although, notwithstanding (W. 100 yadwai; Rām. yodwai 18, 118).

f. (sg. dat. yë̆ḍᵘ̈ or yüḍᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 70), the belly, stomach, abdomen (cf. hȧsⁱ-yüḍⁱ gāsa-gë˘ḍᵘ̈, p. 354b, l. 31; nicᵘ̈ yĕḍ, p. 670a, l. 46) (Gr.Gr. 10, 70-1, 134; Gr.M.; L. 458 yad; W. 18 yad, 111, 123 yaḍ; Śiv. 200; K. 1091; H. ix, 7; K.Pr. 14, 16, 28, 80, 156, 239, 257). --aʦüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a habit of craving for food to arise, habitual greediness to take its rise (in a person). --barith -- adj. c.g. having the belly full, full (El.). --phaṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. rupture or bursting of the intestines to occur (due to violent flatulence, to a blow, or the like) (Gr.M. 254, K. 381). --raṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a chronic incurable disease of the intestines to attack (a person); to be satisfied with a small amount of suitable food, to live in good health by avoiding unwholesome food. --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. habitually to eat any kind of food that one sees (without considering propriety, or whether the food is wholesome or not). --ʦalüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. diarrhœa to occur. --wasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the belly to sink, i.e. extreme hunger to be experienced. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the belly to come, i.e. to be comfortably replete with nice food, to have had a good dinner (K.Pr. 199). ¶ yĕḍa-boḍᵘ adj. (f. -büḍᵘ̈), having a swollen belly (e.g. owing to a hearty meal); big-bellied, corpulent (El. yaḍabauḍ, Gr.Gr. 75); a glutton (El. yeḍabauḍ). ¶ yë̆dᵘ̈- or yüḍᵘ̈-dôdᵘ̈ m. bellyache, colic. -dödⁱlad adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -dödⁱladiñ), suffering from bellyache, colicky. --hᵃy -- f. the pain in the abdomen experienced by a woman after childbirth. -motᵘ adj. (f. -müʦᵘ̈), gluttonous, voracious. -nyukᵘ adj. (f. -nicᵘ̈), lean-bellied, small-bellied (i.e. satisfied with little food). -rᵃkh karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to practise fasting; to eat meagrely, starve oneself (e.g. out of miserliness). -ʦāl f. a form of indigestion usually caused by emptiness of the belly. -ʦolᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüjᵘ̈), one (esp. a child) who is suffering from chronic or frequent diarrhœa. --yüḍᵘ̈ dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to cry out that one is hungry, proclaim one's hunger, protest against insufficient supply or non-supply of food.
m. (sg. dat. yĕdakas), a led horse; (in Ksh.) a horse of a very swift kind, a race-horse.

adj. c.g. bellied (in the sense of 'rotund in the middle', 'swollen or thick in the middle',--e.g. a jar or post--or 'bent out in the middle'), big-bellied (Gr.Gr. 134, where it is distinguished from yẹ̆ḍᵃl; K.Pr. 239).
yidbār ادبار m. turning back, going back; disloyalty, treachery (Rām. 155, 1319); ill-fortune, ill-luck; (in Ksh.) defeat (El. idabár).
m. N. of a celebrated ancient king (Skt. Yadu), eldest son of Yayāti, and ancestor of Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) (K. 618, 620). Cf. yādav.
yodway, yŏdwai, yudwai, see yĕd, p. 1184b, l. 32.
adj. c.g. (of a human being) pot-bellied, gluttonous, a glutton (El. yiḍal; Gr.Gr. 134, where it is distinguished from yĕḍal; L. 460 yadal; W. 111 yiḍal).
m. (sg. dat. yĕgarāwanas), the evil smell of burning oil or the like.
(K.Pr. 35), for yihön, cond. past pl. 3 of yunᵘ, q.v.

f. (sg. dat. yĕhānüʦᵘ̈), contempt, disdain (cf. kŏl-kōrĕ-yᵒ, p. 436b, l. 41) (El.); affront, indignity, insult, slight; slander, calumny. --khë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to suffer indignity (from loud abuse or the like). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to contemn (El.); to abuse another loudly and publicly (El.). --pëñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such abuse to befall (a person).

or yihāta احاطہ m. surrounding, enclosing; enclosed space, enclosure, premises, precincts; (in Ksh.) the exercise of might, power, authority, sway (due to wealth, high office, or the like). --karun -- m.inf. to exercise such power; hence (esp. of a low person suddenly promoted) to become highly exalted, to become invested with great authority, power, wealth, or the like.

m. oneness, unanimity, (of a number of persons) the being all of one mind; the ace (at cards, etc.); a kind of one-horse vehicle, the ekkā of India; cf. also yĕka under yĕkh 1 and 2. --karun -- m.inf. (of a number of people) to unite as one, to show united determination. -gurᵘ m. an ekkā-pony, or a pony suitable for harnessing to an ekkā. -wôlᵘ m. an ekkā- driver, one who drives an ekkā for hire.
m. (sg. dat. yēkadantas) (an elephant) possessor of only one tusk; a N. of Gaṇêśa, see Ganēsh.
or yēkādashĕ card. eleven, i.q. kāh 1, q.v. (a word borrowed from Skt. ēkādaśa). The god Rudra is said to appear under eleven forms, see p. 387b, l. 21 (Śiv. 522, Rām. 1770).
or yikrār اقرار m. agreement, consent, acquiescence, confirmation (Śiv. 1796 yĕ˚); confession, acknowledgment, admission.
f. oneness, unity, identity (borrowed from Skt.) (Śiv. 1485, 1490).
card. (sg. obl. yēka; emph. yēkᵘ̈y, Śiv. 993), one (i.q. akh, q.v., borrowed from Skt. ēka) (Śiv. 993, 1134, 1370, 1405, 1486, 1695).

m. (sg. dat. yĕkas), frozen snow, ice formed from frozen snow (El. yakh; Śiv. 27, 333, 342). ¶ yĕka-muhulᵘ m. a long icicle (such as is pendent from the eaves of a house). -ṭujⁱ f. a ball of ice formed from frozen snow. -wôñᵘ m. the intensely cold water that issues from frozen snow.
f. (sg. dat. yĕki), vomiting. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to vomit. ¶ yĕka yiñĕ f. pl. inf. vomitings to come, an attack of vomiting to occur.
adj. c.g. intensely cold (to touch), freezingly cold; cf. yĕkh 1. --lagun -- m.inf. (of anything animate or inanimate) to become intensely cold, to suffer from intense cold.

card. one, i.q. akh, q.v., e.g. ba yĕkh tīr, with a single arrow (Rām. 340). -bār یک بار adv. at the same time, at once, simultaneously; at once, all at once, immediately (Śiv. 781, 912; Rām. 405, 860, 887); together, not separately (Rām. 460); altogether, entirely, the whole (Rām. 470, 1130, 1684). -dam یک دم adv. in one breath, in a moment, at once, all at once (Rām. 898, ba-yĕkh- dam). -jā یک جا, -jāh, or -jyāh, adv. in one place, together (cf. El. yakjazámut (i.e. yĕkh-jā zāmotᵘ, equal in age); Śiv. yĕkh-jyāh 203, 905, 1302, 1556, 1831; Rām. -jāh 49, 466, 573, -jā 1108d; H. -jāh, x, 12; yĕg-jāh, ii, 4); all together, unanimously (Rām. 1685, ba-yĕkh-jā). -lakh (= یکلخت) adv. all at once, all together, altogether (K. 561). -pāṭh f. (sg. dat. -pāṭi), a cloth or other garment only just long enough to go once round the body; cf. paṭa. -rah یک رہ adv. by one road; once; at once, at one glance, at first sight (El. has yakrah, in the east, which his reverse vocab. shows to be a misprint for 'in the least'). -sö (= یکسو) adv. on one side, aside, apart from others (YZ. 242). -sān یک سان adj. c.g. and adv. the same, identical with (Rām. 1203, 1499); like, similar (Śiv. 1241); associated only (with, sṻtin), having only (...) for a companion (Rām. 1200). -tôrᵘ adj. (f. -törᵘ̈) (of a cloth or the like) that of which the warp and woof consist of single threads. Cf. tār 2.
f.pl. a kind of dish (consisting of meat cooked with spices in curdled milk).
m. expulsion, ejection, eviction. --karun -- m.inf. to evict, expel, banish (from) (Rām. 32 (yĕkrāj), 822).
subst. m. and adj. c.g. belief, faith, true faith, conviction (K.Pr. 170); (as adj.) certain, sure. --zānun -- m.inf. to be certain, to know for certain, be assured (Gr.M.).
adv. certainly, surely, in truth (W. 96, yaqīnan).
m. Sunday (a word borrowed from Persian), i.q. āthwār, q.v.

m. a certain small bird with a very disgusting smell (K.Pr. 240, where it is wrongly described as a plant). yĕkurᵘ mörith athan phakh (a proverb) a stink on the hands after killing this bird, i.e. great damage all for nothing. The flesh of the bird is uneatable, the hands of the killer become stinking, he incurs the sin of killing a living being, and all for no profit.
card. one. An old form of okᵘ and akh, qq.v., in yēka-wāṭh, of one construction, of the same material (L.V. 17); gôrum yēkuy dēh, I have loved only one body (i.e. nothing but my body) (L.V. 7).

m. the motion of the body in making a violent pull or drag, a pull (El. yal, jolting, yala, assault). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to move or bend the shoulders, back, etc. in the act of pulling, to give a strong pull.

or adj. c.g. (of an untamed beast) tamed, brought under control (Gr.Gr. 21, subst. m., subjection); obedient, loyal (K.Pr. 245). --anun -- m.inf. to tame, bring under control (a violent or wild beast, a stubborn naughty boy, and so on). --karun -- m.inf., id. (Rām. 16). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to become tamed, as ab.

adj. c.g. free, set free, set at liberty; turned loose, allowed to roam or pasture at liberty. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become perverse, self-willed, unruly, unrestrained, to break loose (of a woman, child, horse, or the like). --rōzun -- m.inf. to break loose and remain so, to be independent, unrestrained, continue at liberty. --trāwun -- m.inf. to cause (a child, animal, or the like) to become unrestrained (by faulty teaching, etc.); to render uncontrolled, unruly, ungoverned, or the like; to let go (a person seized) (H. iii, 4; x, 5, 21). -wôlᵘ n.ag. one who (on the ground of wealth, qualifications, good fortune, or the like) behaves, or acts, arrogantly.
yilāj علاج m. a medicine, remedy, cure (El. iláj, Rām. 275). --karun -- m.inf. to heal, to cure (El.). yilāja-rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), incurable (El.).
m. (sg. dat. yĕlākas), a mountain table-land, a high plateau. Sheep are here pastured (L. 362 ilák).

or yillath (= علت) f. (sg. dat. yĕlüʦᵘ̈), a disease, sickness, malady, infirmity, weakness (El. yalat); a fault, vice (K.Pr. 88 illat); a bad or worthless thing (cf. arzöni-yᵒ, p. 46a, l. 20); a defect, flaw, detrimental effect (Rām. 110); a pretext, pretence, excuse; a charge, count (of an indictment) (Gr.M. yillath m.). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. harm or damage (such as blame, accusation, evil conduct, or the like, due to evil association) to be incurred. --lārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. some vice (such as being a slave to drugs) difficult to relinquish, or disease difficult to be got rid of to become attached to (i.e. affect) a person. ¶ yĕlüʦᵘ̈-wôlᵘ̈ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who has been affected by one of the above defects, vices, etc.
adj. c.g. of, belonging to, born or produced on, a mountain plateau (see the next).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. yĕlüʦᵘ̈ladiñ), one who is affected by a defect, disease, or vice as in the preceding.
(for 3, see yolᵘ) adj. c.g., in yĕlⁱ kaṭh m. (sg. dat. --kaṭas --), a castrated ram fattened up and plump.

or yĕli rel. adv. of time, when, at what time, at the time when, as soon as (El. yili, yilih; Gr.Gr. 156; Gr.M. yĕli; W. 94 id.; L.V. yĕli 31, 44, 49, 82, 102, 103; Śiv. id. 3, 40, 53, 63, 78, 81, 85, 106, 159, 268, 313, etc.; Rām. id. 15, 45, 62, 88, 102, 114, 141, 144, 147, etc.; K. 8, 12, 24-5, 32, 46, 50, 55, 58, etc.; H. ii, 3, 7; iii, 8; iv, 7; v, 5, 6, 9; vi, 11, etc.; YZ. yĕly 157, yĕlih 172. This word sometimes has the force of 'if', as in H. v, 8). yĕli tĕli adv. now and then, occasionally (El. yili tili). ¶ yĕlyukᵘ adj. (f. yĕlicᵘ̈), of when, of, born, or produced at the time when.

m. N. of the god who rules the spirits of the dead (men or beasts) (Skt. Yama) (El. yam, an angel; Śiv. 931, 1843, 1908); the Angel of Death (K.Pr. 6, 175, 240). -brôhmun m. a low kind of Brāhmaṇ who acts as priest for this god, and who carries through the various funeral ceremonies. -bayĕ m. the fear of this god; hence, fear of death (L.V. 27 yĕma-bayĕ). -hāl f. (sg. dat. -höjᵘ̈), the abode of Yama, the limbo of the departed; the place where the relations and friends of a deceased meet to lament his death. -hēr f. Yama's stairway; N. of a certain long, difficult, and dangerous mountain path in Ksh. (Śiv. 931). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. Yama to fall (on a person), the sudden unexpected death (of a person) to occur. -rāth f. (sg. dat. -röʦᵘ̈), Yama's night, the long grievous night passed by the family when a person dies early in that night. -ruth m. (sg. dat. -rutas), Yama's fast, the ten days' fast observed by the members of the family after a death. -rāza or yĕma-rāza m. N. of the god Yama (Gr.M. yĕmarāza; Śiv. id. 864; Rām. 175, 474, 587, 1740). ¶ yĕma-baṭh m. (sg. dat. -baṭas), Yama's apparitor, who drags away the soul of a dying person to judgment (usually in pl.) (L.V. 74). -dār or -dwār m. the world, or abode, of Yama, the limbo of the dead (men or beasts) (Śiv. dw˚ 1911); cf. dwār. -dūth m. (sg. dat. -dūtas), a messenger of Yama, who carries off the deceased to the limbo, an angel of death (Śiv. 483). -guma m.pl. the sweat denoting the imminence of death (Rām. 1587, 1616). -naṭh f. (sg. dat. -naṭi), the quivering or trembling of a person at the point of death. -pö̃than m. the journey of a deceased to the limbo.
m. self-control, self-restraint, observance of moral duty (Śiv. 269, 1213).

m. N. of a Vidyādhara, or demi-god, in Skt. Yamala. He and Arzŏn (Skt. Arjuna) were sons of Vaiśravaṇa, or Kubēra, the god of wealth. They were cursed by Nārada to become two trees, and so they remained until they were released by Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) (K. 169-70).
m. N. of a certain wild flower described as sweet-scented and somewhat dark in colour; N. of a certain small-sized variety of ruby.

yẹ̆mbürᵘ̈-zal, or yẹ̆mbᵃra-zal f. a certain white flower blooming in the early spring, the narcissus (El. yimbarzal, yimberzal; K.Pr. 56; Śiv. yẹ̆mbürᵘ̈˚ 55, 1008; Rām. 184, 197, 353, 645, 655, 676, 1031, 1494 (read yẹ̆mbᵃr-zala, voc.), etc.; YZ. 153, 184, 209, 274, 565); cf. Arabic عنبر, ambergris. -dāñĕ m. N. of a variety of the rice-plant or paddy (El. yimbirzal dányi; L. 248, 333, 463 imbrzal, a good white rice).
m. N. of one of the three divisions of the Valley of Kashmīr,-- Marāz (p. 595a, l. 48), Kamrāz (p. 446b, l. 16), and Yĕmrāz (commonly spelt 'Yamrāz'). The last is the city of Śrīnagar (K.Pr. 138).
f. N. of a river, the 'Jumnā' (Skt. Yamunā) (K. 410).
yĕmi, yim 2, yima 2, yimau 2, see yih 2.
(for 2, see yë̆ñᵘ̈ 1) m. a small field or plot of land (with an irregular surface) (Śiv. 1213, K.Pr. 248, translated 'river bank'). Cf. yĕnodᵘ.

adv. and postpos. without (as in mĕ yᵒ, without me; ʦĕ yᵒ, without thee; tas yᵒ, without him; karana yᵒ, without doing); in exchange (for), instead (of) (as in tas yᵒ, instead of him; tath yᵒ, instead of it; karana yᵒ, instead of doing; khĕna yᵒ, instead of eating. yĕnay adv. and postpos. without, as ab. (El. yanai, gratis).

adv. from the time when, since, ever since the time when (Rām. 348, 535; K. 1062, 1100; K.Pr. 194 yanah). -pĕṭha id. (Gr.M.; Śiv. 527, 1340). -shutᵘ or -shuth adv. id. (K. 740). --ta tana -- adv. after a long time, a long time after, a long time since; but yĕna tana, and ever since then (Rām. 1162). ¶ yĕnukᵘ adj. (f. yĕnücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, since the time when.

(sometimes written yĕndᵃr or yindᵃr 1) m. (sg. dat. yẹ̆ndras, etc.) an instrument, machine, appliance (cf. dŏsa-yᵒ, p. 252a, ll. 43 ff.; ködⁱ-yⁱ, p. 384b, l. 48; ṭŏṭⁱ-yⁱ, p. 1039a, l. 32; wacĕ-yᵒ, p. 1154a, l. 37); esp. a spinning-machine, a spinning-wheel (cf. pakhᵘ̈cᵘ̈, p. 726a, l. 40; pacĕ-yᵒ, p. 791a, l. 49; ranga-yᵒ, p. 837b, l. 7) (Gr.Gr. 13, yindᵃr; W. indar, a wheel; Śiv. 1014, (with pun on yindᵃr 2) 1217; K.Pr. 87). yẹ̆ndᵃr ta ʦạndᵃr naʦun m.inf. 'the spinning-wheel and the moon to dance', i.e. great festivity to be performed or carried out. --katun -- m.inf. to work a spinning-wheel, to spin (K.Pr. 65, 253). ¶ yẹ̆ndra-(or yẹ̆ndᵃra-)bĕha  m. the board on which a spinning-wheel stands and is supported, the base board of a spinning-wheel. -ḍȧchⁱ f. one of the upright supports of the axle of either of the wheels of a spinning-wheel. -dŏs f. a mud wall (in which the mud is pressed and pounded into a long trough as a mould) (cf. dŏsa-yᵒ, p. 252a, l. 43, and L. 249). -katawañ f. the profession or livelihood of spinning. -kanᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the part of a spinning-wheel on which the little wheel rests (see kanᵘ̈rᵘ̈, p. 458b, l. 24). -köʦᵘ̈ or -kāʦan f. (pl. nom. -kāʦa or -kaʦüñᵘ̈), one of the three supports of the iron spike that acts as the distaff of a spinning-wheel. -lūrᵘ̈ f. the driving handle of a spinning-wheel. -muhulᵘ m. a kind of long heavy pestle-machine for pounding and husking rice. It is a kind of beam, resting horizontally on a fulcrum, with the pestle at one end, while the other end is moved up and down by the feet of one or more workers (El. indar-muhul; L. 463 indr mohl, a rice lever mill; W. 114 indarmo˙hal). -māl f. a woman who is skilled in and devoted to working a spinning-wheel. -pakhucᵘ or pakhᵃch m. (sg. dat. pakhᵃcas), the side (or one of the flat spokes together forming the side) of the large wheel of a spinning-wheel (cf. pakhᵘ̈cᵘ̈). -shikhürᵘ̈ f. an old worn-out spinning-wheel. -tulᵘ m. the metal spike (performing the office of a distaff) attached to the small wheel of a spinning-wheel (El. yandar-tul and yindertul). -ʦakᵃj or ʦakᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. the large wheel of a spinning-wheel. -ʦạkᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the handle-part (or part held by the fingers) of the handle used for revolving the large wheel of a spinning-wheel. -wāv m. a certain goldsmith's tool, a furbisher or shaper. -yōñĕ m. the driving-band of a spinning-wheel. ¶ yẹ̆ndras bĕhun m.inf. to sit at the spinning-wheel, to be an industrious spinner.
m. a goldsmith's draw-plate, the plate perforated with holes of different size through which a length of precious metal is drawn for gradual conversion into wire.

or yindrāza or (q.v.) yindᵃr 2 m. N. of the king of the gods, the regent of the visible heaven, the god of rain and of thunder (Skt. Indra-rāja) (Śiv. yindrāza, 201, 213, 810, 1148, 1249; yindrāz (m.c.) 446; yindra-rāza 3; Rām. yindrāza 147, 398, 574, 620-1, 1058, 1737; K. yindra-rāza 330, 538, 755-7, 770, 774).

or yongᵘ m. Asafoetida (El. yang, yanga, yangú, Ferula Assafoetida). According to El. it is imported from the Panjāb, and is eaten by Hindūs (not by Moslems) as a condiment. ¶ yĕnga-bagāra m. Asafoetida sauce. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give asafoetida; met. to avoid or abandon (someone or something) so as to cause (him or it) to be ruined or destroyed. --lagun -- m.inf. asafoetida to be experienced; to look upon a kind action as an injury (and to abuse the doer of it). -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -mŏnjĕ), an asafoetida root. -phakh m. (sg. dat. -phakas), the stink of asa˚. rôchᵘ m. N. of a certain small medicinal plant growing in submontane tracts, and described as having small round leaves. -röchⁱ-mūl m. the root of the foregoing, from which a tea is prepared as a remedy for rheumatism and similar diseases.

or yĕngurᵘ a charcoal-burner, a man who prepares charcoal in the forest and sells it in the city; a kind of coarse charcoal (cf. ʦᵃñĕ-yᵃ, p. 1076b, l. 48) (El. yangar; H. xi, 17). yĕngar-ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ f. a kind of charcoal used by goldsmiths and blacksmiths (which burns only under artificial draught).

f. the people, or company, that attend, or are members of, a wedding party; cf. yë̆ñᵘ̈ 3. --hōrüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to carry out the duties of hospitality, etc., at a wedding party. ¶ yĕñili-grākh m. (sg. dat. -grākas), an attendant, steward, or manager at or of a wedding party (his business being to welcome and look after the comfort, etc., of the guests).
m. an irrigated plot in a large area of rice-fields. Cf. yĕn 1.

f. the warp (in weaving) (El. yain, yĕn; W. 145 yenⁱ; K.Pr. id. 171, 219, 249). --wahārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to spread out the warp (on the loom); (met.) to lay a net, set a snare, spread the toils (to injure another). --yērüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to lay out or sort the warp for the loom (a row of sticks is set upright in the ground, and the thread, carried along through a ring fastened at the end of a short stick held in the right hand, is led backwards and forwards, up and down the whole row, zigzagging from stick to stick) (El. yaïn yerinyi, Śiv. 1808). ¶ yĕñĕ-gab m. the twisting turn of the thread when being carried zigzag round one of the above upright sticks. -kônᵘ m. one of the sticks in this row (cf. gaba- kᵒ, p. 274b, l. 1).

f. anxiety, distraction of the mind (regarding the support of one's family, carrying out some very difficult work, or the like). --khārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause mental anxiety (as ab., or by some accusation). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. mental anxiety (as ab.) to come (caused by some impediment, opposition, accusation, or the like). ¶ yĕñĕ-gorᵘ m. one who causes such anxiety, a mischief-maker (who starts others quarrelling, or causes obstruction or impediment to others).

in yĕñĕ-wôlᵘ m. the assemblage of the relations of the bridegroom at a wedding, (from the bride's point of view) a wedding party (cf. kāwa-yᵒ, p. 495a, l. 40) (H. xii, 15, 17, 18; K.Pr. yanihwol, 100; yeniwol, 197).
or yipöᵒ adj. (f. yĕ(yi)pörimᵘ̈ ), of, belonging to, or produced on the near side (of a river, mountain range, wall, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 151, K.Pr. 15).
adj. (f. yĕpörimᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or produced on the side which (cf. the preceding) (Gr.Gr. 151).

(also written yipôrᵘ) m. this side, the near side (of a river, mountain range, wall, or the like) (cf. apôrᵘ-yᵘ, p. 39a, l. 26) (El. yipor; W. 95, id., adv.). -kun adv. to, or in, this side (W. 95). ¶ yĕpāri or yipāri adv. on this side, on the near side (Śiv. 968 yipārĕ m.c.; K.Pr. 14, 240, (yapárí for yĕpāriy) 261). ¶ yĕpörⁱ 1 or yipörⁱ adv. from this side, from the near side (cf. apörⁱ-yⁱ, p. 39a, ll. 44 ff.) (Gr.Gr. 151; Śiv. 1460; H. v, 4). -kinⁱ 1 adv. from hither, from this side (cf. apörⁱ-yⁱ-kⁱ, p. 39a, l. 46). ¶ yĕpāryukᵘ or yipāᵒ adj. gen. (f. yĕ(yi)pāricᵘ̈ ), of, belonging to, or produced on this side or the near side (of a river, etc., as ab.).
m. which side, the side which. ¶ yĕpörⁱ 2 adv. in or from the side which (Gr.Gr. 151). -kinⁱ 2 adv. from which side, the side from which.

or m. wool (cf. raza-yēr, p. 856b, l. 8) (El. f.; Gr.Gr. 21, m.; L. 465). ¶ yēra-dastār m. a woollen turban. -dāv f. woollen thread, worsted. Note that dāv, p. 260b, l. 23, is m. -jŏrāba m. a woollen stocking or sock. -kônᵘ m. the ball of worsted as wound on the distaff in the process of spinning. -kangañ f. a wool-comb, a comb-like instrument for teasing out wool, a teasel. -kānul m. a long string of wool like a plaited braid (not so thick as -lav, bel.). -kataway,  f. the profession or employment of spinning wool; the wages, or fee, paid for spinning wool. -lav m. a long, thick rope or cable of wool (cf. -kānul, ab.). -pan m. a quantity (large or small) of woollen thread or worsted. -thŏs f. as much wool as can be taken up by one hand, a fistful of wool. -thọ̆sᵘ m. a lump of so much wool as can be taken up by the fingers of one hand. -ʦādar f. a woollen shawl.
a marriage feast (L. 460, probably a misprint for yë̆ñᵘ̈ 3, q.v.).
conj. 1, caus. of yērun, q.v. (1 p.p. yēranôwᵘ), to cause warp to be arranged for the loom; (of a bird's nest) to cause to be put together, to cause to be built (Śiv. 1784).
m. an amble (the pace of a horse).
in yĕri-lūkh m. (sg. dat. -lūkas), this world or life, the world of mortals, as opp. to the future world or life. Cf. yōr 1.
m. a crowd or throng (of people, collected with some object, or come together for some reason).
(? spelling) m. a flower of Kashmir (El. ering).

or yŏrma m. a kind of fancy embroidery or rich needlework (e.g. adorning a woollen mat). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to embroider as ab. -gorᵘ m. an embroiderer (of this kind of work). --tārun -- m.inf. to embroider as ab.

or conj. 1 (1 p.p. yyūrᵘ, f. yīrᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 15) (in weaving) to sort, or arrange, the warp for the loom (cf. yë̆ñᵘ̈ yērüñᵘ̈, p. 1200b, l. 23) (Gr.Gr. 21, Śiv. 1808, K.Pr. 249); met. (of a bird) to put together, i.e. build (a nest) (cf. ôlᵘ yᵒ, p. 23b, l. 13) (Śiv. 1025, 1049, 1440; Rām. 1445). ¶ yyūrᵘ-mōtᵘ perf. part. (f. yīrᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of warp) arranged, sorted (as ab.). ¶ yēran-wöjᵘ̈, yīran-wöjᵘ̈, or yīriñᵘ̈-wöjᵘ̈ f. the ringed stick used for arranging the thread for the warp (as described under yë̆ñᵘ̈ yērüñᵘ̈, as ab.). ¶ yīran-dolᵘ or yīrin-dolᵘ m. the whole contrivance of upright sticks for arranging the warp, as described under yë̆ñᵘ̈ yērüñᵘ̈. In distributing the thread with his ringed stick the weaver walks continually up and down the whole row of sticks. -dolᵘ lāgun m.inf. (met.) to walk continually backwards and forwards till some work is completed. ¶ yīriñᵘ̈-wöjᵘ̈ f., see yēran-wᵒ, ab.
adj. (f. yērivᵘ̈), made of wool, woollen (K.Pr. 18). Cf. yēr 1.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. yĕsākaladiñ), poverty-stricken.
m. (sg. dat. yĕsākas), utter or abject poverty (i.e. want of every necessity of life). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. such poverty to befall (a person). --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to reduce (another) to utter poverty.

m. a kind of dish composed of various articles (such as lotus filaments, water chestnuts, beans, and pieces of fish) made up with a paste of rice-flower and fried in oil. -gorᵘ m. a man who makes and sells this.

m. fame, reputation, glory, renown (Śiv. 1678; K. 2, (yĕshāh, with suff. of indef. art.) 1169). --gĕwun -- m.inf. to sing the glory (of anyone or anything, gen.), to sing the praises (of), to commend, praise (Gr.M.; K. 842, 981). --kaḍun -- m.inf. to endeavour to gain a great reputation (by excessive liberality on some great occasion, or the like). --nērun -- m.inf. reputation to issue, (a person's) fame to become widespread. ¶ yĕshĕ-wôlᵘ adj. (f. -wājĕñ), famous, glorious, renowned.

f. N. of the wife of the cow-herd Nanda and the foster mother of Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) (Skt. Yaśōdā) (Śiv. 702, 990, 1141, 1371, 1385, 1395, 1399, 1435, 1461; K. 48, 66, 94, 98, 109, 115, 136, 139, 143, 156, etc.).
m. 'the Joy of Yĕshōdā' (q.v.), a N. of Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) (Śiv. 1382, 1838).
adj. c.g. suffering from continual and abject poverty, poverty-stricken.

f. great physical toil, manual labour, heavy toil, labour beyond one's powers, severe exertion. --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (out of enmity, or the like) to cause a person to exert himself in heavy toil beyond his powers, to exhaust another by putting him to hard labour. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such heavy toil to fall upon a person (esp. when it consists in doing some useless work).
m. poverty, indigence, destitution (marked by meanness and squalor of appearance, dress, intelligence, qualities, and acts). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. such poverty to come (to a person).
adj. c.g. (as subst. f. yĕtabārᵃladiñ), poverty-stricken (as in the preceding).
adj. c.g. (a person or horse) who when rising, going, or the like is in the habit of swinging round or twisting his shoulders and back. Cf. yĕṭh 1.

or yitĕn pron. adv. here, in this place (El. yiten; Gr.Gr. 155). ¶ yitĕnī pron. adv. emph. even here, in this very place; (also, in addressing a woman) here, in this place. ¶ yĕtĕnukᵘ 1 adj. gen. (f. yĕtĕnücᵘ̈ 1), of, produced in, or born in this place, of here. ¶ yitinan or yitinas pron. adv. here, in this place (Gr.Gr. 155).

f. (sg. dat. yĕṭi), raising of the shoulders, shaking the shoulders, a shrug (indicating arrogance, conceit, or the like) (cf. buñilⁱ-yⁱ, p. 115b, l. 49; wāza-yᵒ, p. 1178b, l. 26; yāwa-yᵒ, s.v. yāwa); a similar motion by a horse. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take a person by the shoulders and shake him (with the intention of throwing him down). --hāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show (unwarranted) pride or conceit (e.g. as regards undertaking some task which one is finally unable to complete). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf.id. --wasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. conceit to come down, to become humiliated (by want of success in what one has undertaken); pride to be brought low (by loss of wealth, resources, or the like).
in yĕṭa-phürᵘ̈ f. (in agriculture) a clod-crusher (K.Pr., sg. abl. yaṭahpurih 187). Cf. yĕba-ʦüṭᵘ̈, p. 1183a, l. 31.

or yitha 1 rel. pron. adv. as, in like manner as, just as, as if, how (Gr.Gr. 153; Gr.M.; L.V. 100; Śiv. 52, 994, 1430; Rām. 32, 74, 354, 372, 698, 807, 917, 998, 1165, 1266, 1297, 1475, 1500; K. 55, 65, 378, 432, 438, 484, 524, 651, 726, 971, 1046; YZ. 107); just as, at the very time that, while; (as conjnct.) so that, in order that (K. 358, 989). --pöṭhⁱ 1 -- or --pöṭhin 1 -- rel. pron. adv. how (Gr.M.; Śiv. --pöṭhⁱ, 714; Rām. --pöṭhⁱ, 59, 1007). --titha -- pron. adv. in some way or other, somehow (cf. p. 1041b, l. 48) (Śiv. 75; K. 138, 1098, 1114, 1117, 1119, 1126). ¶ yĕthay or yithay 1 rel. pron. adv. emph. just as, in precisely the same manner in which (Rām. 807, 1179; K. 77, 902, 1173-4). -kana 1 or -kȧnⁱ 1 pron. adv. id.; as, in like manner as. --pöṭhⁱ 1 -- or --pöṭhin 1 -- pron. adv. just as, in precisely the same manner in which (Śiv. --pöṭhin 790; H. --pöṭhⁱ xii, 22).
in yĕṭha-lôrᵘ m. a severe pummelling or beating. ? Cf. yĕṭh 2.

m. (sg. dat. yĕṭharas, pl. nom. yĕṭhar), a certain shrub growing in barren uplands, and used as firewood. yĕṭhar-nār m. fire from this wood; met. a person of a mild disposition who is suddenly moved to quick and fierce anger.
or yĕtᵃn m. effort, exertion, endeavour (Gr.M. yĕtn); persevering or continued effort, perseverance.
m. a fatherless child, an orphan (cf. baba-yᵒ, p. 77a, l. 22; mājĕ-yᵒ, p. 557b, l. 43; mölⁱ-yⁱ, p. 566b, l. 31) (Gr.M., K.Pr. 160).

pron. adv. where, in the place which (Gr.Gr. 156; W. 93 yotut); (with emph. y) yĕtuthᵘ̈y, even where, in the very place which (Gr.Gr. 156). yĕtȧtⁱ adv. i.q. yĕtuthᵘ̈y ab. even where, in the very place where (H. xii, 6).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. yẹ̆tᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. yẹ̆tᵃrun, q.v. yẹ̆tᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. yẹ̆tᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. yẹ̆tᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, ab., q.v.

(f. yẹ̆tᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), completely carried out to the best of one's ability (as ab.); supported, maintained (as ab.).

(sg. dat. yĕzatas), honour, rank, dignity, respect (cf. bē-yiᵒ, p. 152a, l. 29) (El. yazat m., izzat f.; L. 283; W. 18 'izzat, m.; K.Pr. 51, 90 izzat, m.). --karun -- m.inf. to show honour (to), pay respect (to). --thawun -- m.inf.
