m. abundance, excess, redundancy. Cf. yë̆ʦᵘ̈.

or yiʦh f. (sg. dat. yĕ(yi)ʦhi ), wish, desire (cf. sŏ-yĕʦh, p. 958a, l. 34) (El. yatsha, decision; yatshá, will; yetsa, wish, intention; yetsha, resolution; yitsha, desire; Gr.Gr. 126; Gr.M.; L.V. 29, 40, 45; Śiv. 190, 286, 307, 795, 1308; Rām. 20, 173, 590, 1029, 1582, 1670, 1723; K. 709, 894; K.Pr. 2); hope, trust, faith, confidence (cf. paʦh-yᵒ, under yᵒ-paʦh, bel.); (esp.) the will of God, God's power (El. yetsa); affection, love (Śiv. 1371; K. 109, 743, 964); intention, purpose, resolution, determination (to do a thing) (Gr.M., Rām. 514); cf. yiʦʦhā. --barüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show great love or affection (Rām. 35; K. 427, 1036, 1081); to show honour or respect (K. 526). -paʦh or (p. 807a, ll. 46 ff.) paʦh-yĕʦh f. (sg. dat. yĕʦhi-paʦhi), hope and affection, complete confidence (in), excessive trust (in) (e.g. when making a deposit on trust) (Śiv. 309, 1071; K. 10, 1002, 1036, 1044). -paʦh thavüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to put such complete confidence (in). --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to feel a desire for, long for. ¶ yĕʦhi-kār m. an act performed with much love and affection, an affectionate act. --karun -- m.inf. to do (a thing) with a wish (i.e. of one's own accord, and not in compliance with another's order).
or yiʦhawunᵘ or n.ag. (f. yĕ(yi)ʦhavüñᵘ̈ ), one who wishes (for), desires, one who is eager (Śiv. 1452, K. 1044); one who has a liking (for), one who loves (cf. pānas yᵒ, p. 736b, l. 3).
or yĕʦhukh adj. (f. yĕʦhücᵘ̈), wishing for, desirous on behalf of, used --˚, as in pāna-yᵒ, self-interested, p. 736a, l. 11.

or or conj. 1 (1 p.p. yoʦhᵘ or yuʦhᵘ ), to wish (Gr.Gr. 14, 126; Śiv. 634, 826-7, 882; Rām. 1026, 1445, 1448, 1507); to wish (for), desire, long for (El. yatshun, yetsun; Gr.M.; Rām. 1127; K. 639, 798); to choose, desire (to do anything) (Gr.M.); to choose, prefer, select (anything) (Gr.M., K. 1171); to express a wish, request, demand, ask for (Gr.M.); to determine, intend, propose (to do anything) (Gr.M.; Rām. 78, 1157). ¶ yo(yu)ʦhᵘ-motᵘ  perf. part. (f. yüʦhᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), wished for, desired. ¶ yĕ(yⁱ)ʦhan-wôlⁱ  n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who desires, one who is eager (El. yatsanwol, eager; Gr.M.).
adj. (f. yĕʦürᵘ̈), zealous (noted only in f. sg. voc. yĕʦarī, K.Pr. yaʦarih 245). ? Cf. the preceding.

adj. c.g. and adv. (pl. dat. yĕʦan, K.Pr. 250), much, very (El. yat, yȧts, yits; Gr.Gr. 154; Gr.M.; W. 96 yaʦ, more; L.V. 102-3; Śiv. 190, 1639, 1860; Rām. 29, 64, 101-2, 197, 445, 525, 539, 664, etc.; K. 192, 721, 964, 1053, 1103; YZ. yaʦ 240; K.Pr. yiʦ 39, yĕʦ and pl. dat. yĕʦan 250, yaʦan 245). --kāl -- m. a long time (past, present, or future) (Śiv. 81; Rām. 306, 972, 1137, 1297, 1541; K. 489, 685, 704, 1111); delay (Gr.Gr. 157); (as adv.) for a long time (Śiv. 1209; Rām. 313, 895, 1411, 1772; K. 794; H. ii, 4 yüʦᵘ̈-kôlᵘ̈, cf. yĕʦa-kôlᵘ, bel.). --kölⁱ -- adv. after a long time (Śiv. 343, K.Pr. yĕʦkáli 157); late (Gr.Gr. 157). -kālukᵘ or -kālyukᵘ adj. gen. (f. -kālücᵘ̈ or -kālicᵘ̈), of a long time ago, of olden times, ancient. ¶ yĕʦa-kôlᵘ adj. (f. -köjᵘ̈), i.q. yüʦᵘ̈ kālukᵘ, ab.; (as adv.) for a long time (Gr.M.). Cf. yüʦᵘ̈-kôlᵘ̈ under yüʦᵘ̈ kāl, ab. ¶ yĕʦi-ranga adv. in many ways (Gr.Gr. 154).
f. (sg. dat. yibādüʦᵘ̈), religious service, worship, devotion. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to worship (with gen. of obj.) (Gr.M.).
m. N.P., Iblīs, the Devil, Satan (H. iv, 2).

(? spelling and gender) a drug distilled from the leaves of the ṭĕṭha-vĕna (p. 1051a, l. 3) (L. tetwan, Artemisia) (L. 67 ibsántin, 'a name no doubt derived through the Arabic from the Greek absintha' (i.e. apsinthion)).

f. (sg. dat. yīzᵘ̈, K.Pr. 58), any periodical Muslim festival, a festival, feast-day (El. íd; L. 268; K.Pr. 58); the Muslim Easter ('īdu'l-fit̤r) (Gr.Gr. 14); great festivity and rejoicing, festivity, revelry (K.Pr. 82). Cf. yīdⁱkāh.
m. this (world) (H. vii, 16), a corruption of the Skt. idam, this.
or yiday adv. indeed, certainly, truly, verily. yidav is used in addressing a man, and yiday when addressing a woman.
m. copious discharge of urine, diabetes; (in Ksh.) urine (El. idrâr).
m. a place (outside a town) where the appropriate Moslem service of the yīd ('īd) and similar festivals is held, an 'īd-gāh (El. ídgá; L. 288 idgah; H. vi, 16; K.Pr. idgáh, 87). Cf. yīd.
in yigīr bigīr f. catching hold of a person in order to stop him (either a habit of doing this or a single occasion).

pron. dem. this (within sight). ¶ [Sg. nom. an. and inan. c.g. yih or (vill.) yuh 1, yuhᵘ 1 or yühᵘ̈, also (in compounds) written yi. Acc.-dat. an. c.g. yimis, or nŏmis, or (vill.) nĕmis; inan. yith, or nŏth, or (vill.) nĕth. Ag. an. and inan. m. yimⁱ or nŏmⁱ, f. yimi or nŏmi. Abl. an. and inan. c.g. yimi, yiwa, or nŏmi. Gen. an. c.g. yimⁱ-sondⁱ, yisondᵘ, or nŏmⁱ-sondⁱ; inan. yimyukᵘ or nŏmyukᵘ. In the plural there is no distinction between an. and inan., and gender is distinguished only in the nominative case. Thus, nom. m. yim, f. yima; or m. nŏm, f. nŏma. Acc.-dat. yiman or nŏman. Ag. and abl. yimau or nŏmau. Gen. yiman-hondᵘ or yihondᵘ, or nŏman-hondᵘ or nŏhondᵘ. For most of the above forms, see Gr.Gr. 89, 90, and Gr.M. See also the references below.] ¶ In the sing. this pronoun is an. or inan., and the an. forms in some cases distinguish between the masc. and fem. genders. As regards the plur., in this respect, see ab. In both numbers, it will be observed that, except in the nom. sing., an otherwise obsolete base nŏth, etc., can be used instead of the more regular forms yith, etc. This is most common in the sing., and is chiefly colloquial. ¶ When written in the Nāgarī character, all the forms of this pronoun are usually written with an initial (instead of) in order to distinguish it from the Relative Pronoun yih 2. ¶ When this word is used as an adjective pronoun, the inan. forms yith and nŏth are employed when agreeing with an inan. noun of either gender in the dative singular. Thus, yith kulis or nŏth kulis, to this tree. When agreeing with a genitive, the usual rule for adjectives is observed. Thus, yimis (or nŏmis) söhiba-sondᵘ  of this gentleman, but yimi (or nŏmi) cīzukᵘ  of this thing. ¶ In the plural nominative the masculine agrees with all masculine nouns, and the feminine agrees with all feminine nouns, without any distinction between animate and inanimate. But, if the adjective pronoun agreeing with a feminine nominative plural is separated from it by some word that does not indicate its gender by its form, then the masculine form of the plural pronoun is used instead of the feminine. Thus, yim (not yima) zᵃh pacĕ (fem. nom. plur.) (not), these two boards, but yima pacĕ, these boards. The other cases of the plural are all of common gender, and make no distinction between animate and inanimate. [For ab. generally, see Gr.M., s.v. yih 1.] ¶ nŏm pl. nom. and acc. (f. nŏma), these; (as pron. adj. m.) (H. x, 5); (as pron. adj. f.) (H. viii, 4). I.q. yim, bel. ¶ nŏmau (also spelt nŏmav), pl. ag. and abl. c.g. by these, from these; (as pron. adj. m.) (H. x, 12). I.q. yimau, bel. ¶ nŏmⁱ instr. sg. an. m. and also inan. c.g. (an. f. nŏmi), by this, i.q. yimⁱ, bel., q.v. -sondᵘ sg. gen. an. of this, i.q. yimⁱ-sondⁱ, bel., q.v. ¶ nŏmi, i.q. yimi 1 and 2, bel., q.v. ¶ nŏman pl. acc. dat. c.g. for these, to these; these (acc.) (H. viii, 1); (as pron. adj.) (H. x, 12). I.q. yiman, bel. ¶ nŏmis or (vill.) nĕmis sg. acc.-dat. an. c.g., to this; (as pron. adj. an. m.) (H. ne˚ v, 9; xii, 15). I.q. yimis, bel. ¶ nŏmyukᵘ sg. gen. inan. (f. nŏmicᵘ̈), of this (without life), i.q. yimyukᵘ, bel., q.v. ¶ nŏth sg. dat. inan. to this (inanimate thing), i.q. yith, bel., q.v. ¶ yi 2, (for 1, see y 2) for yih 1 bel., in compounds, such as yi-ti, this also (K. 326; H. x, 8). ¶ yī, i.q. yiy 1, bel., q.v. (H. vi, 8). ¶ yih 1 or (vill.) yuh 1, yuhᵘ 1, yühᵘ̈, sg. nom. and acc., an. and inan., c.g. this (within sight), he, she, it (within sight) (Gr.Gr. 13, 89, 90, 113, 115, 153, 158, 194, 213; Gr.M.). (An. m.) (L.V. 26; Śiv. 820; Rām. 105, 161, 366, 413, 505, 667, 726-7, 734, 880, etc.; K. 133, 135, 141, 358, 608; H. yih ii, 9, 11; iii, 7, 8; v, 5; viii, 6, 13; x, 1, 2, 5, 6, 12; xii, 1-3, etc.; yuh xii, 5; yüh, for yühᵘ̈, ii, 9; x, 12; K.Pr. 250-1); (an. f.) (Śiv. 874; Rām. 424-5, 668, 1030, 1032, 1034-5, 1148, 1150, 1649; H. ii, 8; iii, 4; v, 6, 10, 12; viii, 3; x, 8; xii, 4, 15, 20, 25); (inan.) (L.V. 84-5; Śiv. 92, 532, 640, 686, 696, 710, 716, 792, 805, 957, etc.; Rām. 157, 159-60, 222, 280, 293, 469, 592, 597, etc.; K. 275, 672, 773, 1161; H. iii, 4, 8, 9; vi, 16; viii, 7, 11; x, 4, 5, 7, 13, etc.); (as pron. adj.) (L.V. 7, 28; Śiv. 10, 13, 18, 697, 802, 815, 838, 899, etc.; Rām. 267, 289, 340, 385, 395, 473, 592, 708, 733, 1667, etc.; K. 1063; H. yih ii, 3, 8, 9, 10; iii, 1, 3, 4; v, 5-7, 11; viii, 1, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 13, etc.; yüh, for yühᵘ̈, ii, 11; YZ. yih 23, 84, etc.; K.Pr. 244). ¶ yihondᵘ 1 or (q.v. bel.) yiman-hondᵘ pl. gen. (f. yihünzᵘ̈), of these (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1005; K. 30; H. viii, 1; K.Pr. yihunduí for yihonduy 253). ¶ yihuy or yuhuy or yŏhay (f. yihay), sg. nom. and acc. this very, even this, only this (El. yihoi, yihuí); (an. m.) (Śiv. 796, 798, 809, 813, 821-3, 835, 849 ff., 1659, 1714; Rām. 1313; K. 38; H. yihuy x, 7; xii, 15; yuhuy x, 1; yŏhay x, 8); (an. f.) (L.V. 52; H. xii, 20); (inan.) (Śiv. 642; K. 72, 114; H. yihuy, viii, 10); (as pron. adj.) (L.V. yuhuy 13; Śiv. m. 646; f. 358, 693, 718, 1194, 1225, 1902; Rām. m. 1620; f. 147, 181, 1388; K. f. 268, 274, 394, 878; H. yuhay, xi, 2; yihōy, v, 10). ¶ yim pl. nom. and acc. (f. yima), these (El., Gr.Gr. 89, Gr.M.); (m.) (L.V. 109; Śiv. 583; Rām. 334, 384, 445-6, 448, 450, 1295, 1383, 1397, etc.; yimay (? yimạy) 588; K. 17, 175, 201; H. ii, 3; viii, 1, 3, 13; x, 1, 2, 12; xii, 2, 3, 18, 23; (f.) Rām. 555, 1438; K. 275; H. viii, 4; K.Pr. 253); (as pron. adj.) (H. v, 9, 12; viii, 1, 3, 5, 11; x, 12; xii, 6; (f.) iii, 8; v, 8; viii, 4; x, 1, 2, 6; with emph. y; f. yimay, xii, 3, 23). ¶ yimau or yimav or (vill.) yimōv pl. ag. and abl. c.g. (Gr.Gr. 90; Gr.M.; Rām. 1413, 1434; H. yimau ii, 3; viii, 1, 3, 5; xii, 1, 17, 22; yimav v, 8; viii, 11; x, 6, 12; yimōv x, 1); (as pron. adj.) (H. yimau v, 7; viii, 3, 9; yimav iii, 1; x, 1, 5, 12); with emph. y, yimavᵘ̈y (H. iii, 7; viii, 6). ¶ yimⁱ or (see ab.) nŏmⁱ sg. instr. an. m. and also inan. c.g. pron. rel. who, which, that. ¶ [Sg. nom. an. m. yus or yusᵘ; f. yŏssa or (vill.) yĕssa; inan. yih, also (in compounds) written yi, or (old) yuhᵘ2 or yuh 2. Acc.-dat. an. c.g. yĕmis or yĕs; inan. yĕth. Ag. an. m. yĕmⁱ; f. yĕmi; inan. yĕmⁱ. Abl. an. and inan. c.g. yĕmi or yĕwa. Gen. an. c.g. yĕmⁱ-sondⁱ, yĕsondᵘ, or yĕs; inan. yĕmyukᵘ. In the plural there is no distinction between an. and inan., and gender is distinguished only in the nominative case. Thus, nom. m. yim, f. yima. Acc.-dat. c.g. yĕman or yiman. Ag. and abl. yĕmau or yimau. Gen. yĕ(yi)man-hondᵘ  or yihondᵘ. For most of the above forms, see Gr.Gr. 88-9 and Gr.M. See also the references below.] ¶ In the sing. this pronoun is an. or inan., and the an. forms in some cases distinguish between the masc. and the fem. genders. As regards the plural, see ab. ¶ When this word is used as an adjectival pronoun, the inanimate forms, with one exception, are not employed. The exception is yĕth, the inan. dat. sing. It is used as an adj. when agreeing with an inan. noun of either gender in the dat. sing. In other cases (except in the old language of L.V.), when an adjectival use is required, the animate forms are employed, according to gender, whether agreeing with an animate or inanimate noun, as in yus söhib, what gentleman, i.e. the gentleman who; yŏssa triy, the woman who; yus (not yih) jahāza, the ship which; yŏssa shĕlph, the art which, but (L.V. 8) yuh nām (not yus nām), the name which. An exception is that the adjectival feminine dative is yĕmi, not yĕmis, although, when used substantively, the an. form yĕmis or yĕs is used for the feminine as well as for the masculine. Thus, yĕmis söhibas, to the gentleman who; yĕmi triyĕ, to the woman who. When agreeing with a genitive the usual rule for adjectives is observed. When the genitive is the genitive of a masculine singular inanimate noun, and therefore ends in ukᵘ, etc., the pronoun is put into the ablative singular. Thus, yĕmi cīzukᵘ, of what thing, i.e. of the thing which. When the genitive is not of this description, the pronoun is put into the dative singular, as in yĕmis (or yĕs) söhiba-sondᵘ, of the gentleman who. ¶ For the use of the demonstrative pronoun tih, as the correlative of this pronoun, see p. 966b, ll. 22 ff. ¶ In the plural nominative the masculine yim agrees with all masculine nouns, and the feminine yima with all feminine nouns, without any distinction between animate and inanimate. But if the adjective pronoun agreeing with a feminine nominative plural is separated from it by some word that does not indicate its gender by its form, then the masculine form of the pronoun is used instead of the feminine. Thus, yima pacĕ, the boards which, but yim (not yima) zᵃh pacĕ, the two boards which. For ab. generally, see Gr.M., s.v. yih 2. ¶ This pronoun is often repeated in various idiomatic senses, as in yusᵘ yih dapay, he who will say what to thee, i.e. whoever will say anything to thee (L.V. 20); yĕs yih rōʦē, to whom what is pleasing, i.e. whatever is pleasing to each (L.V. 21); yih yih karm, whatever work (L.V. 58); yuhᵘ yih karm, whatever act (L.V. 61); yĕmⁱyus zônᵘ, he who knew whom (Śiv. 449); yĕmis yĕmicᵘ̈ yiʦʦhā, whoever has a wish for anything (Śiv. 1085); prayĕn ôsᵘ yĕs yih, to whomever anything was pleasing (Śiv. 1086); yus yiy mangiy, whoever would ask anything from thee (Śiv. 308); yus yus, whoever (K. 430, 992); yih yih (K. 863) or yiy yiy (K. 323), whatever; yus yus yĕth yĕth kāmi lagihē, whoever was allotted to each particular work (K. 1067); yĕs yus gaʦhi, that which is necessary for a particular person (K.Pr. 243); yus yĕs zāni, he who knows a particular person (K.Pr. 256). So yĕmⁱ yitha wuchᵘ, as each one looked (K. 438); pazi yuthᵘ yĕs, as is proper for each (K. 1071); yus yuthᵘ kari, as each one does (so will he reap) (K.Pr. 256). ¶ yi 3, for yih 2 bel. in yi-(or yih-)kē̃h  pron. indef. inan. whatever, whatsoever (Rām. 45, 256, 470, 790, 1660, 1745; K. 422, 569, 1055, 1057, 1166); cf. yus-akhāh, bel. yi-(or yih-)kē̃ʦhāh  pron. indef. inan. i.q. yi-kē̃h (Śiv. 117, 695, 1184, 1529; Rām. 20, 162, 587, 653); (as pron. adj. inan.) Cf. yīrun.
m. a desire, wish, will, intention, resolve (Gr.M.).
f. (sg. dat. yīrüñᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 69), an anvil (El.; Gr.Gr. 14, 29, 69; H. xi, 16).
m. Iran, Persia (El. irán; Gr.Gr. 150; Gr.M.; H. ii, 1).

n.ag. (f. yīravüñᵘ̈), one who floats, floating (Rām. 973); one who is unstable, fickle, capricious; one who is distracted, perplexed, distraught, confused. ¶ yīravüñᵘ̈ nāv f. a floating, or drifting, boat (K.Pr. 254); great distraction, agitation, confusion (due to fear or the like). --nāv gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. great distraction, as ab., to occur. ¶ yīrawañĕ nāvi gaʦhun m.inf. 'to go into a drifting boat', hence to become distraught, agitated.
in yīrīpīrī wālüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to disregard, neglect, show disrespect to (esp. to one who is haughty or self-conceited).
adj. (f. yīrāni, Gr.Gr. 150), of or relating to Persia, Persian (El. irání). --gurᵘ -- m. a Persian horse (Gr.Gr. 150).
m. direction, instruction, order, command, bidding (Rām. 718, where yīrshād is a misprint).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. yīryōv), to float about, drift (up in the air, or on the surface of water) (El.; Gr.Gr. 14; Rām. 620, 790, 1078); to drift whirling about (Śiv. 1551); to be distracted, perplexed, distraught (Śiv. 1023).

m. a species of mustard seed (employed in rheumatism and colds, and also burnt at marriages, births, and other festivals to drive away evil spirits, or to avert the mischievous effects of the evil eye) (L. 75 isband, Peganum Harmala; Rām. 1358).
m. a certain white ointment made by mixing up a certain metallic powder in hot oil.
m. a ruler, master, lord; a N. of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 1145).

m. a sign, token, hint, signal (El. ishára, K. 646, K.Pr. 202); a slight movement (of the hand, etc., as a sign, command, or the like) (Rām. 478). --karun -- m.inf. to point out, signal, beckon (El., Gr.M.).
f. N. of a village in Kashmīr (Rām. 677). It has a famous and holy spring, which is said to be a portion of the Ganges. For the legend connected with it, see K.Pr. 120 (Ishíbarí).

m. a lord, master (Śiv. 48, 162, 853; Rām. 770); the Supreme Deity (Gr.Gr. 199, 200; Śiv. 20, 31, 60, 241; Rām. 32, 180, 220, 252, 525, 991, 993, 1260, 1284, 1477, 1570, 1670, 1705; K. 385); a N. of Shiv (Śiva), connoting his power and supreme lordship (L.V. 43; Śiv. 81, 132, 386-7, 429, 487, 493, 599, 676, etc.; Rām. 607; K. 796, 877). ¶ yīshĕr-wār f. (in astrology) N. of a certain period of three months, viz. the months during which the sun passes through the zodiacal sign under which a man was born, and also through the signs immediately preceding and following it. Thus, if a man is born under Aries, the period is the three months taken by the sun in passing through Pisces, Aries, and Taurus. Each year the man is particularly affected by the sun during these three months. ¶ yīshĕrav yī m. the name used in schools for the character in the Śāradā alphabet corresponding to the Nāgarī ī.
(? spelling) m. Ipomaea coerulea or Pharbites nil, i.q. kāladāna, p. 435b, l. 43 (El. ishpecha).

adj. c.g. wished, desired, longed for; beloved, agreeable, liked; worshipped, reverenced. yishṭa-dēv m. (f. yishṭa-dēvī), a specially reverenced god (or goddess), one's tutelary deity (Śiv. 113 fem.). yishṭa-dyunᵘ m. (sg. obl. -dina), the giving of that which is desired, giving all that is wanted, lavish generosity (Rām. 4).
m. the seed of the fleawort or plantain, Plantago ispaghul (El. isaphgol).
adj. c.g. standing, erect (Śiv. 497; Rām. 950, 1443, 1697); rearing (as a horse) (Rām. 921); standing ready (for anything) (Rām. 1420, 1452).

in yita-gaʦh m. or f. repeated coming and going (necessitated in performing some work). -gaʦh karun (or karüñᵘ̈) (or) m. or f.inf. to come and go repeatedly (as ab.). -gaʦh lagun (or lagüñᵘ̈) (or) m. or f.inf. repeated coming and going to be attached (to a person), i.e. (in the performance of some work) fatigue caused by frequent coming and going to be experienced (esp. when the person continues coming and going in ignorance that the work has already been completed).
for yĕtha in yith-nay conj. so that not, in order that not (H. ix, 12).

pron. adv. thus, in this manner, in this way (Gr.Gr. 153, Gr.M., K. 393); without motive, without reason, casually (in this sense usually with an interrogative verb, as in yitha gachyā suh, will he go without motive?, i.e. he certainly will go with a motive). --pöṭhⁱ 2 -- or --pöṭhin 2 -- pron. adv. in this manner, in this way, thus (El. yithah pãṭ, also yithapãt, translated 'again'; Gr.Gr. 153; Gr.M.; W. 96 yiti pöṭh; Śiv. --pöṭhⁱ 571, 683). ¶ yithay 2 pron. adv. emph. in this very manner, exactly so (Rām. 69, 688, 691, 704); without cause, motive, or reason, for no particular reason, on the spur of the moment (Śiv. 652); without resistance, without price, gratis (El. ithai, yithai; Gr.Gr. 13 ithai; Gr.M.). --hyuhᵘ -- pron. adj. (f. --hishᵘ̈ --), exactly like this, such (El. yithanhyú); ill at ease, feeling unwell, out of sorts, only so so; distraught, agitated (by fear of anxious times, of illness, or the like); El. also gives as adv. ithinyu, thus. --hyuhᵘ gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become angry (at), resent, take umbrage. --hyuhᵘ karun -- m.inf. to make (a person, esp. a member of one's own family) angry. -kana 2 or -kȧnⁱ 2 pron. adv. in this very manner, thus. --pöṭhⁱ 2 -- or --pöṭhin 2 -- pron. adv. in this very manner, in this very way, exactly so (Gr.M.; Śiv. --pöṭhⁱ 490, 684, 810, 837, 843, 869, 924, 1251, 1336; --pöṭhin 672, 1668; Rām. --pöṭhin 1016, 1311, 1315; H. --pöṭhin viii, 3). --rōzun -- m.inf. to wait for (some result soon to happen); to sit doing nothing, hence be without employment, to sit apart from one's fellows, to remain unmarried, not to join the company at a meal, and so on. --thawun -- m.inf. to set a person aside and inactive, to keep him apart from others, not to put him to his proper use (e.g. at meal times to abstain from giving food, to keep (a son) at home and unmarried, to keep money and not to put it to a profitable use, to have a coat and not wear it, and so on).
m. a history, legend, historical tradition (Śiv. 1457).
m. agreement, accord, combination, confederacy; an accident, chance (El. ittifák, Gr.M.).
pron. adv. here, in this very place (El. yitit, yutut; Gr.Gr. 156; W. 93 yatit, yetit, yitit, in this very place, just here).
adj. c.g. et cetera, and so forth, and others, and the rest (Rām. 98). Borrowed from Skt. ityādika.
pron. adj. (f. yītimᵘ̈), (in counting) this much or many, so much or many (Gr.Gr. 150).
rel. pron. adj. (f. yītimᵘ̈), (the one) which (out of many) (Gr.Gr. 149).
pron. adj. (f. yītiñᵘ̈), costing this (or so) much, worth this (or so) much (Gr.Gr. 148); earning this (or so) many (rupees, etc.) in wages, etc.
rel. pron. adj. (f. yītiñᵘ̈), costing how much, worth as much as (Gr.Gr. 148).
m. a woman's first child-birth. yiwanukᵘ adj. gen. (f. yiwanücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, a woman's first child- birth, a woman's first child.

n.ag. (f. yiwavüñᵘ̈), he who or that which comes or becomes (and so on in all the meanings of yunᵘ, q.v.) (cf. ȧchⁱ- tȧlⁱ yᵒ, p. 8b, l. 33; ȧchⁱ yᵒ, p. 9a, l. 7; bakā yᵒ, p. 102a, l. 29; drē̃ṭh yᵒ, p. 249b, l. 28) (Gr.Gr. 105; Rām. 247, 1039); that which is coming, the future (El. yiwawun); as an adv., as in gāsh yᵒ, immediately on dawn coming (p. 308b, l. 31); paʦh yᵒ, persuasively (p. 807b, l. 1); khosh yiwawunᵘ, even while he is pleasing to (her) (Śiv. 1462). ¶ yiwawunuy adv. immediately on coming (Gr.M.).
adv. for this very reason, therefore (cf. yiwa, p. 1188b, l. 40) (El. yawai, therefore).
n.ag. (f. yivüñᵘ̈), i.q. yiwawunᵘ, q.v. (cf. khŏsh yᵒ, p. 418b, l. 14) (Rām. 128, 353; YZ. 9).
m. molestation, annoyance, pain, trouble, harm, hurt, injury (El. yiza, nuisance); distress, poverty and suffering (K.Pr. 29). --dyunᵘ -- m. inf. to torment (El. íza dyun).
f. drawers, trousers (esp. the flowing or wide trousers of Moslems) (El. yezár). -ḍūrᵘ̈ f. the string with which drawers are tied, trouser-strings (El. ezárdúr, m.).
m. agitation, perturbation, anxiety, trouble. --karun -- m.inf. to disturb (El. iztaráb karun).
m. a statement or deposition made in a court of justice (Gr.M.).
m. so much, this much (as a fixed measure or quantity). Cf. yūtᵘ 1.
m. the measure or quantity which. Cf. yūtᵘ 2.

f. (i.q. yĕʦh, q.v., of which it is the Skt. form), wish, desire, will (Śiv. 31-2, 70, 100, 367, 538, 635, 811, 833, 846, 894, 979, 1071, 1139, 1218, 1238, 1275, 1478, 1766, 1907). ¶ As the first member of a compound this indicates something wished for, loved, favourite, as in yiʦʦhā-būzan, favourite food, a dainty (Śiv. 1071, 1084-5, 1087); yiʦʦhā-pọ̆thᵃr, a beloved, or favourite, son (Śiv. 9).

or yŏdd m. fighting, a fight, battle (war or fisticuffs) (El.; Gr.M.; Rām. yŏd 310, 337, 619, 621, 831, 864, 910, 971, 975, 1428, 1436, 1451; K. yŏdd 452, 580, 599, 662, 745, 775, 795, 818-21, 827, 870, 897, 1023-4). gaʦhȧnⁱ -- m.pl. inf. fighting (including mutual abuse, etc.) to take place. --karun -- m.inf. to fight, to make war (El.; Rām. 350, 450, 476, 600, 701, 1450).
yŏdwanay, yodᵘwanay, etc., see yĕd, p. 1184b, ll. 28 ff.
f. the pine tree, i.q. yörᵘ̈, q.v. According to El. (s.v.) this is the form of the word used about Islāmābād and about Bārāmūla (El. yãḍ, m.).

m. an age of the world. According to Hindū belief there are four of these, called in Skt. the Satya-yuga or Kṛta-yuga, Trēta-yuga, Dwāpara-yuga, and Kali-yuga, lasting, respectively 1,728,000; 1,296,000; 864,000; and 432,000 years. The present age is the Kali-yuga (cf. dwāpar-yᵒ, p. 264a, l. 20; kali-yᵒ, p. 436a, l. 12; satya-yᵒ, p. 950a, l. 18) (Śiv. 1444, 1521, 1712-4; Rām. 51; K. 6, 7, 12, 606); hence, any very long period of time (Śiv. 32, 1714). --phērȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. ages to revolve; hence, in the performance of any long work many impediments and delays to occur. ¶ yŏga-phyurᵘ or yōga-phyurᵘ m. the revolution of the ages; the revolution of times, past, present, and future; the passing of a very long period of time.
in yōga-phyurᵘ m. i.q. yŏga-phyurᵘ, s.v. yŏg, q.v.

m. (sg. gen. yūgukᵘ, Śiv. 1458, 1776), concentration of the thoughts, deep and abstract contemplation, meditation, mental absorption in the Supreme Spirit (cf. dyāna-yᵒ, p. 268b, l. 21; rāza-yᵒ, p. 857b, l. 13) (L.V. 14; Śiv. 21, 24, 247, 442, 597, 735, 756, 1028, 1067, 1215, 1270, 1312, 1418, 1448, 1458, 1485, 1512, 1531, 1591, 1654, 1671, 1689, 1696, 1742, 1747, 1765, 1776, 1782, 1825-6, 1833, 1835, 1841, 1854, 1857, 1865, 1915; K. 424, 437, 969); the Yōga system of philosophy (teaching the means whereby the human soul may obtain complete union with the Supreme Being) (Śiv. 1848). -abyās  (Śiv. 1448) or yōgābyās  (Śiv. 1264) m. regular practice of deep and abstract contemplation, etc., as ab. (borrowed from Skt. yōgâbhyāsa). ¶ yōga-kal f. skill in the practice of abstract contemplation or of mental absorption (L.V. 14). -māyā f. the power of abstract meditation; the śakti (see shĕktⁱ) or Energic Power of God in the creation of the world, personified as a deity (Rām. 66).

or yōgīshŏr m. one who is an adept in, or master of, deep and abstract contemplation, and who has thereby obtained superhuman faculties (K. yögī˚ 437); a name, or title, or Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. yōgē˚ 866, 1215, 1639; K. yōgī˚ 969).
or yūgī m. one who practises the religious system of mental absorption (yōg, q.v.) (L.V. 14; Śiv. 442, 1001, 1377, 1514, 1591; K. 61).

f. a certain female attendant on Shiv (Śiva). There are sixty-four of these, and they are all invoked, under the title of 'mothers', at the religious ceremony called Diva-gŏn (q.v. p. 261b, l. 2) (L. 260, Śiv. 730).
adj. c.g. fitting, worthy, proper (as in karunᵘ yᵒ, worthy to be done; danḍas yᵒ, worthy of punishment) (Gr.M.).
(? cf. یاغی) adj. c.g. daring, arrogant, insolent, audacious, brazen. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become insolent, etc., as ab.

or (q.v.) ohᵘryundᵘ adv. a short way off (u.w. vbs. of coming, putting, sitting, standing, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 94); cf. yuhariñ and wuharyundᵘ. --pahān -- adv. somewhat in this direction, an indefinite short way off (Gr.Gr. 94).

adj. (f. yöjᵘ̈ 1), one who conducts himself unsuitably or improperly, unmannerly, rude (e.g. in speech, listening, thinking, appearance, dress, walk, etc.). --hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. yöjᵘ̈ hishᵘ̈), one who (usually well-mannered) on some occasion acts like such a person. ¶ yāji-paijāma m. 'with misfitting breeches'; hence, one who is ugly or unmannerly in form, appearance, speech, etc.

f. (sg. dat. yājĕ), a kind of cup-shaped cake or biscuit, made of rice-flour cooked in oil. It is offered by women to a god on various festivals (cf. kö̆mᵘ̈-yᵘ̈, p. 443b, l. 23; kana-yᵒ, p. 448a, l. 50) (El. yáj, a biscuit; K.Pr. 3, 105, 190, 239). ¶ yāji-lĕji-pĕṭh nẹ̆ndᵃr pë̆ñᵘ̈ f.inf. 'sleep to fall on the cake-saucepan', (owing to abundance of all that one needs) freedom from care to exist, to rest secure, be free from anxiety; to be careless, thoughtless, heedless. -worᵘ m. i.q. yöjᵘ̈; a piece or fragment of such a cake.
f. (sg. dat. yọ̆khᵘ̈ʦᵘ̈), a means, expedient, plan, device (Śiv. 993, 1747, 1823).
m. (sg. dat. yôkūtas), a certain precious stone, a kind of ruby (Rām. 569).
m. (sg. ag. yĕlⁱ 3), solder. yĕlⁱ-wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), the mending a metal vessel or the like with solder.
m. a square thick piece (of gold, silver, or the like), used --˚.

m. the sacramental or sacred thread worn by Brāhmaṇas and other high-caste Hindūs (cf. wath-pĕṭh yᵒ ʦhunun, p. 1155a, l. 10) (El. yónyi, Śiv. 1077); the driving-band of a spinning-wheel (cf. yẹ̆ndra-yᵒ, p. 1199b, l. 2) (El., Śiv. 1014); a bow string (El.). -kāñᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or kāñᵉ̆r f. a ball of fine thread suitable for making this sacred thread; cf. kônᵘ 1, of which kāñᵘ̈rᵘ̈ is a dim. -lāg f. the fee paid to the officiating priest at the ceremony of investiture with this thread. -lar f. a strand of this thread (before marriage it has three strands and after marriage six). -pan m. cotton thread suitable for this thread; the festival of investing with this thread (usually applied to a modest festival of people who are not wealthy); the driving-band of a spinning-wheel (cf. yẹ̆ndra-yᵒ, p. 1199b, l. 2). -pôrutᵘ m. (sg. dat. -pōratas) (during a marriage ceremony) a present of gold and silver coins made to the bridegroom by the person who gives away the bride. --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to invest with the sacred thread; (as subst. m.) the festival on the occasion of this investiture (K. 483). -wôlᵘ m. (at this ceremony) the boy who is to be invested. -zang f. the present given for good luck to the maiden who spun the thread.
m. (sg. dat. yöpis) (in some difficult or apparently impossible task) one who is competent to carry it through to its completion. See yāpun.

pron. adv. here, in this place (cf. ōr na yōr, p. 41b, l. 14; ōr-yōr, id., l. 16, ōrukᵘ yōr, id., l. 32; tōra yōr, p. 1019b, l. 43) (El. yór, yúr, yúri, hither; Gr.Gr. 155; W. 94; Rām. 288, 450, 881; K. ōr yōr, there and here, round about, in all directions, 656; H. ii, 2; viii, 5; ix, 6, 8, 10, 12; x, 4). yiti-yōr, hence- forth, from now on (Śiv. 42, 69, 72, 375, 378, 417, 598). -kun 1 adv. in this direction, hither (Gr.Gr. 160); on this side, on the near side; up to now, up to this time (cf. tana yōr-kun, p. 1008b, l. 22; tati yōr-kun, p. 1040b, l. 11). yimi-yōr-kun, from this time forth, henceforth (Śiv. 311). ¶ yōra 1 adv. from this side, from the near side, from here, hence (cf. ōra yōra, p. 41b, l. 27) (Gr.Gr. 156; W. 94; K. 818; H. v, 8). yōra tōra, from this side and that (Śiv. 117). -kani 1 or -kanĕn 1 adv. from this side, hence (Gr.Gr. 159, K. 653). -kanyukᵘ 1 gen. adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or produced in this direction or on this side. ¶ yūrⁱ 1 (also written yūry) pron. adv. emph. in this very place, exactly here (cf. wūry na yūry, p. 1144b, l. 7) (Gr.Gr. 156; W. 93 yuri; Śiv. 283, 450, 638; Rām. 166, 262, 294, 382, 560, 1748, 1785; H. x, 12; YZ. 44, 180, 418, 459); to this very place, hither (H. x, 5; xii, 15, 23). -hondᵘ wŏla, come here (vill.) (H. v, 5). -kun 1 adv. even in this direction, in this very direction. ¶ yōrukᵘ gen. adj. (f. yōrücᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or produced here (cf. ōrukᵘ yōrukᵘ, p. 41b, l. 34).

rel. pron. adv. where, in the place in which (Gr.Gr. 155, W. 94, 139 yur). -kun 2 adv. in the direction which, whither (Gr.Gr. 160); on the side which, where. ¶ yōra 2 adv. from the side which, from what place, whence (Gr.Gr. 156; W. 94; L.V. emph. yōray, 19; H. i, 6 (correl. tōra)). -kani 2 or -kanĕn 2 adv. in the place which, where; from the place which, from where, whence (Gr.Gr. 159). -kanyukᵘ 2 gen. adj. (f. -kanicᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or produced where, or in the place which. ¶ yūrⁱ 2 (also written yūry) rel. pron. adv. emph. even where, even in the place which, in the very place which (Gr.Gr. 156, W. 93 yuri, L.V. 61, K.Pr. yúr 84). -kun 2 adv. even in the direction which, in the very direction which (Gr.Gr. 160); even where (K.Pr. 254).
pron. adv. up to here, as far as this place (W. 93); up to now, until now (W. 93).
rel. pron. adv. up to where, as far as the place which (W. 93); up to when, until the time when (W. 93).

f. friendship (Rām. 1052); assistance, help (El. yárí). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to show friendship (to), to show kindness (to), to do a favour (to), to help, relieve, assist (El.; Śiv. 202, 1504; Rām. 1220).

or (q.v.) yöḍᵘ̈ f. a fir-tree, the blue pine (cf. dōla-yārĕ, p. 211a, l. 40) (El. yãr, yór, yárí, pinus longifolia, or yãḍ; also yero, m.; L. 78, 80, yár, pinus excelsa; W. 12; Śiv. 1908; K.Pr. yár 58, 114, 229). Its wood is called kāyorᵘ, etc., q.v. ¶ yāri-kĕlam m. the resin, or tar, that exudes from a pine-tree (El. yãri kilum). -kang m. a pine-cone. -kā̃golᵘ m. (sg. dat. -kã̄galas), the root of a certain wild plant, which, when powdered and mixed with clarified butter, etc., so as to form an ointment, is used as a remedy for rheumatism and the like. -lang m. another wild root used in the same way for similar purposes. -pan m. a spray or twig of a pine-tree.
m. the lilac (L. 461, yosmun). Cf. hiy-āsmān, p. 363a, l. 28.

rel. pron. adv. where, in the place which (Gr.Gr. 156; Gr.M.; W. 94 yo˙t, yut; Rām. 471). -tām, -tāmath, -tāñ, or -tāñĕth pron. adv. as far as, until, so long as (Gr.M.; Śiv. 681; Rām. -tām 240, 782, 1550, 1605; -tāmath 26, 374, 423, 559, 1233; -tāñ 303, 334, 899, 1002; K. -tām 1058, -tāñ 6, 1079, 1096; H. -tāñ, xii, 6); cf. yutām, yotāñ, s.v. yutāñ 2. --totᵘ -- adv. here and there, promiscuously, all about, everywhere (Rām. 30, 99); wherever (Rām. 21, 152); cf. p. 1040a, l. 12. --yotᵘ -- adv. wherever (Rām. 1776). ¶ yĕtⁱ 1 (for 2, see s.v. yutᵘ) pron. adv. where, in the very place which (Gr.Gr. 154; W. 93-4 yati, yeti). ¶ yĕti pron. adv. from where, from the place which, whence (Gr.Gr. 150, 155; L.V. 57); where, in the place in which (Gr.M.; L.V. 88; Śiv. 908, 1101, 1316-7, 1376, 1880; Rām. 363, 602, 942, 1100; K. 1028, 1124; H. viii, 11; x, 7; K.Pr. 58). -kinⁱ (Gr.Gr. 158) or -pĕṭha (Gr.Gr. 155) adv. from the place which, whence. ¶ yĕtiy or yotuy pron. adv. emph. even where, in the very place which (Rām. 1244, 1707, 1730). ¶ yĕtyukᵘ 1 (for 2, see yityukᵘ, s.v. yutᵘ) pron. adj. gen. (sg. f. yĕticᵘ̈), of where, of, belonging to, or produced in the place which (Gr.Gr. 150).
adj. (f. yöʦᵘ̈ 1), gone long ago, long gone, long ago departed.

or (q.v.) ôtᵘ adj. (f. yöʦᵘ̈ 2), alone, mere, sole, only (as in nĕcyuwuy yôtᵘ, only a boy) (El. yót; W. 96 yot; K. 560, 756; K.Pr. 85); (as adv.) only, merely, nothing but (Gr.M.; Rām. 854 pānasạy yôtᵘ, (read a letter) only to himself, i.e. privately); (with a word indicating number or quantity) only (so much) (as in akh yôtᵘ, only one), merely.
m. a league (the measure of distance, about eight miles, more or less) (K. 588); hence, any indefinite long distance (L.V. 26).

m. (f. yüzᵘ̈), a foolish fellow who dresses wrongly (wearing his outer garments as inner, and vice versa) (cf. kŏlayĕ-yᵒ, p. 442a, l. 24). yĕza-mām m. 'a muddler uncle', i.e. a man (esp. one employed in the kitchen) who stupidly and heedlessly leaves things in disorder and topsy-turvy.

m. N. of the eldest of the five Pāṇḍava princes, in Skt. Yudhiṣṭhira (he was celebrated for his truthfulness and righteousness, and was the leader of the Pāṇḍavas in the great war, described in the Mahābhārata, between them and the Kauravas) (Śiv. 1178; K. 540, 1031, 1033, 1044-5, 1048, 1072).
m. a pair, a couple (borrowed from Skt. yuga) (Śiv. 14).
(? spelling) adv. hither, towards this direction (noted only in K.Pr. 236 yuharin). Cf. wuhariñ, wuharyundᵘ, and yohuryundᵘ.

m. (pl. nom. yindⁱ), an organ of sense or action, in Skt. indriya (L.V. 79). In the Śaiva philosophy of Lal Dĕd there are five organs of sense (Skt. buddhîndriya or jñānêndriya), viz. the organ of smell (ghrāṇêndriye), of taste (rasanêndriya), of sight (darśanêndriya), of touch (sparśêndriya), and of hearing (śravaṇêndriya); there are also five organs of action (karmêndriya), viz. the organ of generation (upasthêndriya), of excretion (pāyvindriya), of locomotion (pādêndriya), of handling (hastêndriya), and of voice (vāgindriya). In L.V. 79 it is probably the latter five to which reference is made.
(? spelling) f. the leaf of the Rhododendron campanulatum, which when dry is mixed with snuff to increase the sternutatory action (L. 82). ? Cf. yĕnga or yongᵘ.

. The twenty-second consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character, the thirteenth when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the sixteenth when written in the Perso-Arabic character. The Kāshmīrī name for the character is zȧyⁱ zö, which is also used for the character (ja). It is pronounced like z in the English word 'zeal'. The characters z and are also used to represent the sound of the Persian or Arabic ذ (ẕāl), ض (ẓād), and ظ (z̤ā), which, in Kāshmīrī written in the Perso-Arabic character, occur only in words borrowed from one or other of these languages. In such cases they are pronounced in Kāshmīrī like an ordinary z. ¶ Regarding the relationship between j and z, see Art. j, p. 369a, ll. 28 ff. As there explained, it is difficult to formulate any general rule according to which, in Kāshmīrī, an original j remains as j or becomes z, or vice versa. As a rough guide it may be stated that, in the case of words borrowed from Persian, an original j or z usually remains unchanged, but that, when such a word becomes thoroughly incorporated into the Kāshmīrī, j tends to become z. The same is true of words borrowed from Sanskrit, so far as regards the change of j to z. It thus happens that there are several words in an intermediate stage of adoption, in which both sounds are employed at option in the same word. Thus, the Persian word judā, apart, becomes, in Kāshmīrī, both judā and zudā, and jigar, the liver, becomes both jigar and zigar. As a rule, however, in most words borrowed from Persian or from Arabic through Persian, a j is preserved unchanged. As exceptions may be noted such words as jūlān, fetters, which appears in Kāshmīrī as zōlāna, and maujūd, existing, Ksh. mūzūd. As regards words borrowed from Sanskrit, the case is different. While in many instances an original j of that language is preserved, in many other words directly borrowed from that language, an original j becomes z. Such, for instance, are:--Skt. jagadīśvara-, Ksh. zagadīshŏr, the lord of the world; Skt. jagat, Ksh. zagath, the world; Skt. jambukêśvara-, Ksh. zambukēshŏr, N.P.; Skt. jāmbavān, Ksh. zāmbawān, N.P.; Skt. janaka-, Ksh. zanakh, N.P.; Skt. jaṭā, Ksh. zaṭh, matted hair; Skt. jitêndriya-, Ksh. zitēndriy, one who has conquered his passions; Skt. jīva-, Ksh. zīv (compared with true Ksh. zuv), life; Skt. jīvana-, Ksh. zīwan, life; Skt. jvālā, Ksh. zwālā, glow; Skt. jyēṣṭhā, Ksh. zyēshṭhā, N.P.; Skt. ajāmila-, Ksh. azāmil, N.P.; Skt. ajapā, Ksh. azapā, silent prayer; Skt. bhuja-, Ksh. bŏz, the arm; Skt. bhōjana-, Ksh. bōzan, food; Skt. dhvaja-, Ksh. dŏz, a flag; Skt. kujāta-, Ksh. kŏzāth, baseborn; Skt. lajjā, Ksh. lazzā (compared with the true Ksh. laz), shame, and many others. ¶ The letter z is often of secondary origin. If a dental d (not the cerebral ḍ) is followed by ü-mātrā, it becomes z. Thus the Nominative Plural of grand, counting, is grünzᵘ̈, and the 1 p.p. of √lad-, build, is lodᵘ, with a feminine lüzᵘ̈. When it is followed by ĕ (i.e. ya) or by y, it also becomes z, the ĕ becoming a, and the y being dropped. Thus the base thad-, high, forms its abstract noun by adding ĕr (yar), and becomes thazar, height, and the 2 p.p. of √lad-, formed by adding yōv, is lazōv. For further particulars, see Gr.Gr. 28 ff. and Gr.M. p. 22.

adj. c.g. full of holes (either made so, as a sieve, or of something worn out).
? gend., saffron (cf. bēkh-zᵒ, m., p. 99b, l. 19; shöhī-zᵒ, f., p. 874b, l. 2) (W. 155, K.Pr. 180).

adj. c.g. and subst. m. reddish, rusty-coloured, dirty red; (as subst.) a certain kind of rice with a reddish grain (the word applies both to the grain and to the plant) (cf. baḍa-zᵒ, p. 82b, l. 37; kĕvⁱ-zⁱ, p. 502b, l. 41; nika-zᵒ, p. 627b, l. 24; shāla-zᵒ, p. 880a, l. 27) (L. 463, Śiv. 1032); cf. zagiñ and zạgᵃr. -anzun m. (sg. dat. -anzanas), a certain kind of rice with reddish soft full-shaped well-savoured grain. -bāsᵃmath f. (sg. dat. -bāsᵃmüʦᵃ), a similar rice but with a longish grain. -dönᵘ̈ adj. c.g. (of rice or the like) having a dark red colour.

f. watching, guarding (cf. khal-zᵒ, p. 397a, l. 8) (Gr.Gr. 125, Śiv. 1691, Rām. 337, K. 968). --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to guard, watch (e.g. against thieves) (Śiv. 272, 1382). --thavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to watch carefully (dat.), pay attention (to), heed (dat.) (Rām. 1286). ¶ zāga-zāg f. careful, or heedful, watching (esp. if mutual). ¶ zāgi bĕhun m.inf. to remain secretly and vigilantly guarding (e.g. against theft). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to go on guard (esp. of watching a ripe field of corn or a full threshing floor against theft).
f. black, blacking, black powder used as such (YZ. 212).
m. the Lord of the Universe, a title of Śiva (Śiv. 87, 190, 233, 929, 1104, 1176).
f. the Lady of the Universe, a N. of Durgā (Śiv. 1524).
m. (sg. dat. zāgalanas), a foul smell, a stink (like that of rotting flesh).
f. the mother of the universe, a N. of Durgā (Śiv. 96).
? f. alms, the portion of a Moslem's property given in charity (K.Pr. 133).
m. a protector of the world (Śiv. 1252, used as an epithet of Śiva).
f. the wages for watching or guarding (esp. that paid a secret watch- man of a ripe paddy-field, or the like).
n.ag. (f. zāgavüñᵘ̈), one who watches, one who guards, a watchman.
f. watching or guarding (night and day) of a ripe paddy-field, a full threshing-floor, or the like (cf. brörⁱ-zⁱ, p. 125b, l. 48; khala-zᵒ, p. 397a, l. 22) (Gr.Gr. 128).
f. a certain kind of rice with a small red grain (cf. zag 1 and the next).
m. a fetter, shackle. Cf. zōlāna.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. zôgᵘ, f. zöjᵘ̈ 2 (for 1, see s.v., for 3, see zālun 2); 2 p.p. zājyōv), to be watchful, to watch, guard (e.g. property against theft) (Gr.Gr. 125, 128; Gr.M.; L.V. 48; Rām. 1529); to watch (something or someone), stare at, to keep an eye on (Rām. 1407-8; K. 152; H. ii, 5; K.Pr. 128, 164); to be watchful, vigilant, keep wide awake, watch for (an opportunity of doing something) (in this sense, impersonal in past tenses) (L.V. 78, 79; Śiv. 1311, 1692, 1850; Rām. 498, 601, 861; K. 547, 653, 810; YZ. 92, 309, 329, 334, 416; K.Pr. 112, 241, 258); wuchith zāgun, to stare at (Gr.M.). zāgan-jāy f. a place for watching, a hidden place from which to watch (against thieves, enemies, or the like).
or zạgᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or zügᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a kind of paddy bearing a dusky red grain (cf. baḍa-zᵒ, p. 82b, l. 38; nika-zᵒ, p. 627b, l. 37). Cf. zag 1 and zagiñ.
m. (sg. dat. zāgᵃratas), watching, guarding, vigilance (whether by day or night); the condition of being wide awake (Śiv. 1866).

or (see bel.) zah زہ adv. at all, ever, at any time (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1010, 1569, 1676, 1743; Rām. 967, 1057; K. 470, 829, 849, 852, 858, 1140, 1147, 1167; H. xi, 14; K.Pr. 66, 82, 92, 182, 255); ever, always (El., W. 95 za). In the Persian character this word is often written zah زہ. Cf. zāth 3. --kāli -- or --kölⁱ -- adv. ever, at any time; some time, at some day, once upon a time. --na -- or na zāh adv. never, at no time (W. 95, 158; Rām. 787, 956, 1148, 1336, 1602, 1630, 1649, 1655). --na-ta zāh -- adv. some time or other (W. 95 za nata za).

zahr زہ٘ر or zahār m. poison, venom, virus (cf. ṭyoṭhᵘ zahar hyuhᵘ, p. 1050b, l. 39) (El.; Rām. (zahr) 42, 827, 876, 1656; H. viii, 6, 7, 13); met. poison (in the sense of something intolerably bitter, salt, or the like) (cf. nūna-zahār, p. 641a, l. 38). zahar khasun m.inf. poison to rise (to a person), i.e. rage, fury, to be felt (H. viii, 7). zahār-mŏhᵃra (= زہر مہرہ) m. bezoar, looked upon as an antidote to poison.
f. 'the never day', an indefinite day (used sarcastically in making an appointment). Cf. zāh.
f. (sg. dat. zahᵃmüʦᵃ), disquietude, indisposition; pain, affliction, trouble, sickness; (in Ksh.) indolence, want of energy, apathy, indigence or affliction caused by such.
adj. c.g. one who is lazy, indolent, apathetic (esp. when also indigent).
or zay 2, q.v. interj. victory!, i.q. jai, q.v. (Śiv. 1698, 1701, 1714, 1729).

m. a contraction of Zainu 'l-'ābidīn زین العابدین N. of a famous Sultan of Kashmīr who came to the throne in A.D. 1417 (L. 191). His name frequently appears in local names in Kashmīr, as in the following:--zaina-gīrᵘ̈ f. N. of a district (pargana) in the north of Kashmīr (El. zainager, m.; RT.Tr. II, 487). zaina-kadᵃl m. N. of the fourth bridge across the river Vĕth or Jehlam in the town of Śrīnagar. It was built by Zainu 'l-'ābidīn. The word is also used to designate the quarter of the town in the vicinity of the bridge (RT.Tr. II, 449; El. zenah kadal; K.Pr. 258). zaina-pōr m. N. of a village and tract south of Śrīnagar in the Divᵃsar Pargana (RT.Tr. II, 471).
f. a kind of basket or withy tray for holding flowers, fruit, or the like (cf. tᵃla-zᵃ, p. 995a, l. 42; ṭhūla-zᵒ, p. 976b, l. 16) (El. zen, Gr.Gr. 22). Cf. zönᵘ̈ 1.
m. the olive tree, an olive (El.).
m. a flint (for striking fire) (El. zakhmakh, Gr.M.).
m. a treasure, hoard; (in Ksh.) a warehouse, storehouse, godown (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. wounded, hurt (Rām. 233, 1453). zakhmi hayat (? زخمی حیات) N. of a certain medicinal plant used 'internally in ulcer' (L. 76).
m. a wound, cut, scar, gash, sore (El.; Rām. 357-8, 1651; YZ. 74).
f. a child's penis, or a small one like such.

m. water (cf. ganga-zᵒ, p. 292a, l. 10; nāga-zᵒ, p. 624a, l. 49; pādĕ-zᵒ, p. 683a, l. 11) (El.; Gr.Gr. 28, 38, 72; L.V. 38-40, 45, 47, 81; Śiv. 179, 330, 348, 929, 1022, 1026, 1056, 1096, etc.; Rām. 426, 533, 543, 546, 597, 759, 781, 1334; K. 70, 75, 231, 233, 244-5, 271-2, 411, 413, 758, 836, 931, 946, 1045); any water-like liquid (cf. mad-zᵒ, p. 548a, l. 49) (K. 973); urine (a polite term) (Rām. 948). -gurᵘ m. a sea-horse (a mythical horse, said to be able to fly). -mal m. 'water and dirt', i.e urine and fæces (referred to together). --lagun -- m.inf. an urgent desire to urinate to be felt (Rām. 944). -mal band gaʦhun m.inf. a certain disease (constipation combined with suppression of urine) to occur. -ʦürᵘ̈ f. 'a water-sparrow', a polite name for fish for cooking. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. i.q. --lagun, ab. (Rām. 945, 949). -zīv m. any aquatic creature. ¶ zala-hostᵘ m. a water-elephant, a sea-elephant (a mythical animal) (L.V. 47).

m. (in some compounds, noted below, thisword is f., perhaps due to confusion with zāl 2 and 3) a net, snare, noose (cf. khurⁱ-zⁱ, p. 412a, l. 11; māyā-zᵒ, p. 612b, l. 35) (El.; Gr.M.; L. 462; Śiv. 158, 227, 277, 424, 711, 876, 1206, 1332, 1516, 1693; Rām. 340, 422, 614, 1103, 1496, 1614, 1781; K. 737; H. i, 6-8; ix, 7; YZ. 11, 65, 68, 210, 364, 475; K.Pr. 63); a web, spider's web, cobweb (cf. zalȧrⁱ-zⁱ, s.v. zalurᵘ) (El., Gr.M.); any web-like texture (cf. garba-zᵒ, p. 300a, l. 6; mādri-zᵒ f., p. 550a, l. 37); a collection, mass (cf. pā̃-zᵒ f., p. 748a, l. 43; rag-zᵒ, p. 827b, l. 25); esp. a mass of clouds (cf. hāra-zᵒ f., p. 344a, l. 36; mīga-zᵒ, p. 552a, l. 9; naba-zᵒ, p. 619a, l. 27); (esp.) a collection, or thicket, of trailing plants (cf. bāra-zᵒ, p. 117a, l. 48; kȧnḍⁱ-zⁱ, p. 465a, l. 40; krǖḍa-zᵒ, p. 468b, l. 45) (Śiv. 1568, 1686, 1854; Rām. 1252; YZ. 257) (in this meaning, the word is possibly confused with zār 3, q.v.); illusion, deception; a bunch of unblown flowers. -tāl m. artful, or deceitful, conciliatory language (cf. tāl-zāl m. or f., p. 997a, ll. 40 ff.). --wahārun -- m.inf. to spread a net; met. to spread a net (of deceit), to lay a trap (to deceive another).

or (q.v.) zālay f. (sg. dat. zöjᵘ̈), shivering (from cold); the shivering of ague (cf. tǖr-zᵒ, p. 1021a, l. 7) (Śiv. 287; K. 822, zāla; K.Pr. 68, zálah); fever (El.; Śiv. 165, 373, 1248, 1257). In Gr.Gr. 69 this word is confounded with zāl 1. ¶ zāla dᵃnañĕ f. pl. inf. 'to flaunt shiverings', (even if one is well off) to make a show of poverty when it is necessary to incur expenditure. -dĕv m. (f. -dĕviñ), 'a shiver demon', one who is unable to endure great cold. --hārañĕ -- f. pl. inf. 'to shed shivers', to be perished with cold (the whole body shivering and the teeth chattering). -patᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. 'a mat of shivers', one who is violently attacked by ague throughout his whole body. -satam f. (sg. dat. -satümᵘ̈), N. of a festival held on the seventh lunar day of the dark half of the month of Phāgun (= February-March). --yiñĕ -- f. pl. inf. shivers to come, an attack of ague to come on.
f. a disease of the eyes, involving a membranous growth over the eyeballs. Cf. zāl 1.
f. a certain disease involving a crop of small boils on the upper lip and neighbourhood. Cf. K. 822, where zāla is used for zāl 2.

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. zālaladiñ), one whose body is suffering from shivering cold or from ague; one who shivers from fear, a coward, one who shivers (out of miserliness) at the idea of expenditure; that which is intolerably cold.
adj. c.g. composed of water; (as subst. m.) the waste of waters (which is all that is left at the destruction of the universe) (L.V. 93) (El. zalamaì m., a storm).
f. (sg. dat. zālamŏkhi), N. of a sacred site, sacred to Durgā, about sixteen miles east of Śrīnagar, in Skt. Jvālāmukhī.
m.inf. (1 p.p. zālanôwᵘ), to cause to burn, to cause to be burnt (El.).

f. (sg. dat. zalüʦᵘ̈), baseness, meanness, vileness; humiliation, abasement; (in Ksh.) a condition of filthy or sordid misery (K.Pr. 7, 52, zallat). --pôñᵘ -- m. filthy water, i.e. semen virile (Rām. 1517).
n.ag. (f. zalavüñᵘ̈), warm, hot (esp. of things eatable or drinkable) (El.); burning, fiery hot, blazing (L.V. 57).
n.ag. (f. zālavüñᵘ̈), one who sets ablaze, consumes with fire (e.g. the person who sets alight a funeral pyre) (K.Pr. 122).
f. shivering of ague or the like, i.q. zāl 2, q.v. (cf. buthⁱ-zⁱ, p. 143a, l. 16); burning (in wuda-zᵒ, q.v., p. 1097a, l. 45).
(H.), zulaikhā زلیخا (YZ.), f. N. of the wife of Potiphar (in the story of Joseph) (H. vi, 1 ff.; YZ. 59, 177, 309, etc.).
adj. c.g. mean, vile, wretched; brought low, abased, humbled (H. i, 4).
f. the sweat of the feet (Gr.Gr. 38). In atha-zᵒ, p. 65a, l. 42, the word refers to sweaty hands.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. zalyōv), to taste like water; watery eructations to come into the mouth from the stomach (K.Pr. 154); the mouth to water (from desire of some dainty food).
or zālunᵘ m. (sg. dat. zālanas) fuel (firewood, cowdung cakes, or the like) (El. firewood). According to El. this word is in use towards Bārāmūla.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. zôlᵘ 2 (for 1, see s.v.), f. zöjᵘ̈ 3 (for 1, see s.v., for 2, see zāgun); 2 p.p. zājyōv), to burn (something), to kindle, set on fire (cf. krünḍᵘ̈ zālüñᵘ̈, p. 474a, l. 33; rum-rāṭh zālüñᵘ̈, p. 834a, l. 1; ʦhāy zālüñᵘ̈, p. 1065b, l. 32) (Gr.M.; L.V. 49; Śiv. 125, 268, 377, 426, 973, 1150, 1422, 1482; Rām. 77, 159, 186, 279, 333, 449, 715, 726-7, 733, 744, 800, 802, 826, 956, 1006, 1202, 1236, 1358, 1387, 1471, 1474, 1497, 1595, 1626, 1657, 1663, 1706; K. 114, 631, 879; H. ii, 12; iii, 1, 4; K.Pr. 41, 251); to light (a fire) (cf. nār zᵒ, p. 647a, l. 37) (Śiv. 305, 1205, 1758; Rām. 839, 958, 1069, 1601, 1769; K.Pr. 138); to burn away something, to burn to nothing, utterly to destroy (sin, or the like) (Śiv. 105, 420, 928, 1063, 1156, 1685, 1746; Rām. 781; YZ. 19, 35, 41, 55, 200, 307); to set on fire, torture (Rām. 157, 163, 195). This verb is considered to be the causal form of dazun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 176). ¶ zālan-kūṭunᵘ m. a straight stick for stirring up a fire, a wooden poker. ¶ zôlᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. zöjᵘ-müʦᵘ), set on fire, kindled; burnt (by some one) (Śiv. 888).
m. (sg. dat. zalaris), a spider (El. zalur, Gr.M., Śiv. 277). ¶ zalȧrⁱ-zöjⁱ f. a spider's net-like egg-cocoon. -zāl m. a spider's web.
m. blame, censure, reproach, disparagement, detraction (Rām. 282).

f. (sg. dat. zömᵘ̈, commonly written by Pandits or), a husband's sister, a wife's sister-in-law (cf. ōra-zᵒ, p. 42a, l. 8; māsatᵘ̈rᵘ̈ zᵒ, p. 601a, l. 48; pitᵘ̈rᵘ̈ zᵒ, p. 803b, l. 30; wōra-zᵒ, p. 1136b, l. 46) (Gr.Gr. 66, 72; Rām. 1145, 1154, 1163, 1171, 1611; K.Pr. 119, 259); nŏshĕ- hünzᵘ̈ zām, the sister-in-law of a daughter-in-law, i.e. a daughter (Rām. 848). ¶ zömᵘ̈-(zōmᵘ̈-)brānd  m. when a bride first enters her husband's house her way is barred by her husband's sister and others to whom she has to pay a fee, called by this name (L. 262 zámbránd). -kākañĕ f.pl. husband's sister and a brother's wife (i.e. the two kinds of a woman's sister-in-law) (Gr.Gr. 72).

m. a bandage, fillet, kerchief (bound upon a wound); dressing, poultice, plaster; application of ointment, liniment, balm, or the like (Śiv. 652, zamādāh, with suff. of indef. art., see p. 1219b, l. 11).
f. (sg. dat. zāmüñᵘ̈), a yawn, yawning. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to yawn; to prevaricate concerning or deny (the making away with property entrusted to one), to equivocate.
m. time, period; an age (cf. dōr-ĕ zᵒ, p. 237a, l. 3) (Śiv. 726; K.Pr. 184, zamán).
m. (sg. dat. zamānatas), guarantee, security, surety, bail (Gr.M.).

m. (sg. dat. zāmataris), a son-in-law (cf. bẹ̆nᵃza zᵒ, p. 115a, l. 7; bāwᵃza zᵒ, p. 148a, l. 45; dyārath zᵒ, p. 271a, l. 46; wōra-zᵒ, p. 1137a, l. 2) (El.; L. 464, zamtur; K. 727, 813, 816; K.Pr. 65, zámuthur; 259, zámatur). ¶ zāmatȧrⁱ-bŏkutⁱ m. a child son-in-law, one who is less than ten years of age. -nĕcyuwᵘ m. (sg. dat. -nĕcivis), a youthful son-in-law (over ten years, but below puberty).

in the following:--zamba-drölid adj. c.g. (as subst., f. -drölⁱdĕñ), one who is dirtied by mud or the like; met. one whose clothes, body, and conduct are foul. -wār m. encrustation of thick dirt (e.g. in a cooking pot fouled with long exposure to fire); a pile of crusted or solidified mud (cf. zamwār in Rām. 700). Cf. zamüñᵘ̈lad.

m. the white jasmine, Jasminum sambac; the iris, Iris germanica or I. sambac (cf. bēkh-zᵒ, p. 99b, l. 19) (L. 249, the yellow iris; Rām. 1094). -pōsh m. its flower. -tīl m. an oil extracted from its flower.
m. one of the forms used in K. (674) for zāmbawanth, q.v.

m. (sg. dat. zāmbawantas), N. of a king of the bears, who helped Rāma at the siege of Lankā. In Skt. his name was Jāmbavat. He also appears later as a friend of Krushna (Kṛṣṇa) to whom he gave his daughter Jāmbavatī in marriage. His name appears in various forms in Ksh.; in Śiv. it appears as zāmbawanth (Śiv. 1677). In Rām. we usually find zāmōwan, but also zāmawanth and zāmōwanth. In K. we have (674) zāmbawān and (669, 679, 680, 683) zāmbawanth. See all these s.vv. In K. 669, 679, he is stated to be a monkey, not a bear.
(Śiv.) or zāmbawatī (K. 683) or zāmbawath (K. 688), f. N. of the daughter of Zāmbawanth (q.v.) who married Krushna (Kṛṣṇa). The Skt. form of the word is Jāmbavatī (Śiv. 1677).
(K. 683) or zāmbawath (K. 688), f., i.q. zāmbawantī, q.v.
or zĕmbakēshŏr m. a N. of Shiwa (Śiva), in Skt. Jambukêśvara (Śiv. 1138 zĕ˚, 1167 za˚).
m. a solution of gold (employed for gilding); a certain dish made with eggs (cf. ṭhūla-zᵒ, p. 976b, l. 13).

f. (sometimes m., see bel.) (sg. dat. zamīni), the earth (El.; Gr.M.; Rām. 1242 (m.), 1723 (m.); soil, land, ground (cf. bīṭhᵘ̈ zᵒ, p. 140a, l. 26; dā̃-zᵒ, p. 231a, l. 24; narm zᵒ, p. 651b, l. 24; sūr-zᵒ, p. 932b, l. 19; zabal zᵒ, p. 1215b, l. 30) (El.; Gr.M.; Rām. 454, 519, 1141, 1455, and as bel.; H. ix, 9; K.Pr. 16, 111, 246, 259, and as bel.) (masc. in Rām. 300, 435, 448, 676, 1564; K.Pr. 94); the world, land (as opposed to the sky) (H. iii, 8); the floor (of a room) (Gr.M.). --khanan-wôlᵘ -- n.ag. m. a ploughman (El.). ¶ zamīni-kand m. a certain edible root, generally growing in marshy ground. -path m. (sg. dat. -pathas), a certain piece of land, of such a size that six seers of paddy-seed are required for sowing it. See path 1. -pathᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a small level field.
zāmawanth, and zāmōwanth m. the forms taken in Rām. by zāmbawanth, q.v. (zāmōwan, Rām. 39, 512, 548, 777, 865, 1402, 1409; zāmawanth, Rām. 906; zāmō- wanth, Rām. 856, 865).
or zömpāna m. a palanquin (cf. aina-zᵒ, p. 30b, l. 12) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 84, 787, 921, 1147).
m. an emerald, but in Ksh. used loosely for any precious stone of great value (K. 922-3).
conj. 1 (this verb is impersonal, 1 p.p. zômᵘ), to yawn (L.V. 46).
adj. c.g. covered or defiled with clotted mud or dirt. Cf. zamba.
m. i.q. zamba-wār, p. 1223a, l. 36, q.v. (Rām. 700).
or (q.v.) zanzam m. N. of a celebrated well at Mecca, called Hagar's well; (in Ksh.) intense freezing cold (when the ground is frozen over).

f. (sg. dat. zöñᵘ̈ 2, for 1, see s.v.), knowledge, apprehension, opinion (cf. brahma-zᵒ, p. 121a, l. 26; darma-zᵒ, p. 245a, l. 5; gör-zᵒ, p. 296b, l. 25; pȧshⁱ-zⁱ, p. 779b, l. 26) (Gr.Gr. 106, 127; Śiv. 49, 241, 437, 1378, 1604, 1876, 1880, 1899; Rām. 1459-60, 1502, 1534, 1642; H. vii, 29); acquaintance, familiarity (Śiv. 240, 1030; Rām. 73; K.Pr. 260); discovery, ascertaining (El.); true knowledge (of the Supreme) (L.V. 31; Śiv. 16, 61, 285, 314, 331, 350, 369, 425, 451, 776, 1193, 1314, 1533, 1586, 1595, 1604, 1738, 1765, 1805, 1891); knowledge, senses, clearness of thought (as opposed to insensibility) (Rām. 761). In many of the examples quoted above, the first meaning or the fourth is equally applicable. -kar adj. c.g. (of a person) acquainted, familiar, recognized (from previous meetings), an acquaintance. Cf. zöñᵘ̈-kār, p. 1229b, l. 2. -pachān f. acquaintance, familiarity. ¶ zöñᵘ̈-grākh n.ag. (f. -grākañ), i.q. -wôlᵘ, bel. (Gr.Gr. 106). -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), without knowledge, ignorant; unknown. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who possesses understanding, full of knowledge, wise (Gr.Gr. 106).

m. a man, person, individual (cf. kŏ-zan, p. 503, l. 5; sath zᵒ or sazzan, p. 945a, l. 44; sŏ-zan, p. 958b, l. 34) (Śiv. 1717; K. 197, 915, 1162); mankind (L.V. 31; K. 56, 822). kunuy zan, only one person; hence, alone, lonely (Rām. 1328; K.Pr. 161, kunuí zaná). zan srọ̆dᵘ man srọ̆dᵘ m. 'man in common (and) heart in common', mutual pleasure in affectionate partnership in any work. zan-wān f. (sg. dat. -wöñᵘ̈), a general rumour (of something new or unexpected). zan-zö̃puṭᵘ m. man and beast, the animal creation. ¶ zana-baca m.pl. 'a man's children', an entire family, a family taken as a whole unit.
m. a beater, a striker, used --˚ to signify a wielder (of some tool, or the like) (cf. kalam-zᵒ, p. 439b, l. 48) (K.Pr. 92).
f. a woman (H. x, 13; K.Pr. 103); marda-zan, man or woman (H. vii, 23).

m. (sg. dat. zanakas), N. of a celebrated king of Mithilā (or Vidēha, the modern north Bihār), in Skt. Janaka. He was the foster-father of Sītā, the wife of Rām-ʦandar (Rāma-candra). After Sītā's abandonment by Rām, he became an anchorite, indifferent to pleasure or pain (Śiv. 735, 1822; Rām. 4, 115, 124, 137, 428, 1206, 1220, 1588, 1672).
m. the chin (cf. cāh-ĕ zᵒ, p. 157b, l. 34); the pit of the chin.

f. a woman, a female human being (cf. zanāna-dāy, p. 266a, l. 45; khāsa zᵒ, p. 417a, l. 33; prath zanāni, p. 769b, l. 2) (El. zenána, zenánah; Gr.Gr. 152; Gr.M.; L. 465; W. 18; Śiv. 941, 1129, 1223, 1358; Rām. 1668; K. 286; H. ii, 1; iii, 4, 5, 9; v, 5, 11, 12, etc.; YZ. 241; K.Pr. 174, 250, 260); a wife (H. iii, 1; v, 1, 4, 7, 9, 10; x, 5, 12, 13; K.Pr. 7, 72, 204, 221, 260). zanāna dahyumᵘ dŏh m. the tenth day after a death, on which the women of the household put off their ceremonial impurity and arrange their hair, etc. -khyolᵘ m. a collection of women, a crowd of women, a group of women (Gr.Gr. 152). -mahanyuwᵘ m. a woman person, a woman (referred to politely). -morᵘ m. a woman's body, the female form.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. zānanôwᵘ), to cause to be known, to explain (to so-and-so) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1009, 1019).
m. a N. of Vishnu or Krushna (Kṛṣṇa), in Skt. Janârdana (Śiv. 1416).
n.ag. (f. zānavüñᵘ̈), one who knows, recognizes, or understands (see zānun) (Śiv. 1545, Rām. 1143m, K. 839).

m. a small shrub, a small bush (cf. pạtri-zᵒ, p. 802b, l. 21; sŏyĕ-zᵒ, p. 956a, l. 29). zanḍa-kakav m. a partridge which dwells hidden under low bushes, and lives on their fruit; met. a person who habitually lives hidden from others.

or (once, see bel.) zạnḍ m. a word added to other words signifying vegetables or wood, to signify 'a little' (cf. darbi-zạnḍ, p. 240a, l. 43; draman-zanḍ, p. 245b, l. 40; gāsa-zᵒ, p. 308a, l. 4; guyan-zᵒ, p. 317b, l. 49; hāka-zᵒ, p. 326b, l. 48; kāṭha-zᵒ, p. 487b, l. 20; muji-zᵒ, p. 558b, l. 21; niran-zᵒ, p. 653a, l. 46; pana-zᵒ, p. 734b, l. 25; pōshĕ-zᵒ, p. 779a, l. 50; payĕ-zᵒ, p. 812a, l. 45; sinⁱ-zⁱ, p. 957b, l. 31; zinⁱ-zⁱ, s.v. zyunᵘ) (Gr.Gr. 163).

f. the leg, the shank (of man or animal, or of a stool, table, or the like) (cf. bāma-zᵒ, m., p. 107a, l. 4; khara-zang hyuhᵘ, p. 407b, l. 11; khōvürᵘ̈ zᵒ, p. 425b, l. 24; kŏkar-zᵒ, p. 432b, l. 1; potᵘ zᵒ, p. 788b, l. 37; rabi-zᵒ, p. 823b, l. 10) (El., in common parlance, the lower extremity; Gr.Gr. 65, erroneously translated 'thigh'; W. 144; Śiv. 1309; Rām. 343, 603, 632, 711; K. 147, 419, 563, 1026; H. ii, 11; K.Pr. 57, 95, 102, 117, 171, 236, 246-7, 253, 261). ¶ zanga-horᵘ m. the two legs, the pair of a person's legs (El.). -rôdᵘ adj. (f. -rözᵘ̈), long-legged, a long-shanks, a runner (K.Pr. 261); one who, by habitually going and coming, accomplishes his own object without regard to others. --trövith bĕhun -- m.inf. to sit having let go the legs, i.e. to sit with the legs hanging down, and not tucked cross-legged (K. 972). -tᵃs m. dislocation of the leg. zanga-(or zangi-)ʦᵃs  m. a wrench or dislocation of the leg (K. 1026, zangi-). zanga-zang f. 'leg on leg', much coming and going. -zang karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to do much coming and going (in the accomplishment of any work). -zyūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈), long-legged, long-shanked (K.Pr. 76); one who habitually walks much. ¶ zȧngⁱ zȧngⁱ karun m.inf. to do anything with much use of legs, to accomplish something by dint of much coming and going. ¶ zangi-tȧlⁱ trāwun m.inf. 'to deposit under the leg (quasi, making an offering before the feet of a bound enemy)', hence, to show mercy to a conquered foe (by carrying out his desires). -ʦᵃs, see zanga-, ab. -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈), having one leg amputated.

f. an omen, a sign of good or bad luck (cf. diwa-gōn zang, p. 261b, l. 23; liwa-zᵒ, p. 541b, l. 13; liwan-zᵒ, p. 542a, l. 27; nawa-rĕh zᵒ, p. 665a, l. 10; phira-zᵒ, p. 702a, l. 34; phĕshĕl zᵒ, p. 713a, l. 14; potᵘ zᵒ, p. 788b, l. 38) (Śiv. 1092); a present to bring good luck (cf. bāma-zᵒ, m., p. 107a, l. 5; dŏda-zᵒ, p. 190b, l. 15; dāna-zᵒ, p. 221a, l. 43; dŏsil zᵒ, p. 255b, l. 6; dastār-zᵒ, p. 256b, l. 31; nöyid-zᵒ, p. 670a, l. 27; pĕwan-zᵒ, p. 811a, l. 17; yōñĕ-zᵒ, p. 1201a, l. 30) (L. 260, Śiv. 1152). --anüñᵘ̈ -- f. to bring something (e.g. a dish of curds, or a girl, on the right hand) that serves as an omen of good luck before a person on his beginning some operation (such as a journey, a festal ceremony, etc.). --wuchüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (at the beginning of a journey, or the like) to test an omen (to see if it is lucky). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (in similar circumstances) an omen (good or bad) suddenly to present itself. ¶ zanga-vürᵘ̈ f. a ball of spiced bean-meal used for luck at weddings and similar festivities. ¶ zangi anun m.inf. to bring (something) for a good omen (e.g. when a person is starting on a journey to bring a dish of curds on his right side). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. (at the beginning of any action) an omen (good or bad) to be manifested (K.Pr. 142).
adj. c.g. legged, i.q. zongᵘ 2, q.v. (as in okᵘ-zangal, p. 19b, l. 13); one who is in the habit of doing much coming and going, a great walker.
adj. c.g. capable of independent motion, a living being (as opposed to sthāwar, the inanimate creation) (Śiv. 1431).

m. verdigris; (in Ksh.) the green colour of verdigris, verdigris-green; rust (El.); accumulated dirt of decay (like rust) (Rām. 1657). --khasun -- m.inf. verdigris to rise, (milk, curds, or the like, in a metal vessel) to become spoilt by a scum of verdigris appearing on the surface. --lagun -- m.inf. verdigris to appear, (of milk, etc., as ab.) to be spoilt by verdigris scum.
c.g. an Ethiopian, a negro, blacka- moor (YZ. 67).
adj. c.g. 'leggy'; i.e. a man noted for stout or long legs, or for quickness of gait. People of the north country are said to be of this kind.

zanᵃm, or (q.v.) zarm m. birth, nativity (cf. bröhman-zᵒ, p. 121b, l. 35; bröhmana-zᵒ, p. 121b, l. 40; brahma-zᵒ, p. 121a, l. 30) (Śiv. 34, 431, 527, 1536, 1748; Rām. 65, 68, 418, 1143f, 1248; K. 26, 72, 98,130, 356, 614, 681); origin, rise, production (Śiv. 1593, 1670, 1754, 1879); life, existence (Śiv. 228, 320, 599, 928, 984, 1899; Rām. 208, 225, 347, 442; K. 6, 20); cf. zarm. --būgun -- m.inf. to suffer the fruits of (one's) birth, to endure (one's) fate (Rām. 1010, 1016). ¶ zanma-aiṭham or -öṭham f. (sg. dat. -ai(ö)ṭhümᵘ̈ ), the festival of the birth of Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) celebrated on the eighth lunar day of the dark half of the month of Bādᵃrapĕth (Skt. Bhādrapada, = August-September). -chapath f. (sg. dat. -chapüʦᵘ̈), throwing away one's existence, leading a worthless life; (of something inanimate, such as a water-jar, or the like) throwing away, or losing, its form (by being broken, or the like); cf. zarma-chᵒ, p. 1232b, l. 1. -drölid m. (as subst., f. -drölⁱdĕñ), indigent (owing to incompetence, etc.) from birth (to old age); cf. zarma-dᵒ, p. 1232b, l. 6. -satam f. (sg. dat. -satümᵘ̈), the seventh lunar day of the dark half of Bādᵃrapĕth (see ab.), on which, in some localities, the birth of Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) is celebrated. Cf. zarma-sᵒ, p. 1232b, l. 9. ¶ zanmas yunᵘ m.inf. to come to birth, to be born (Rām. 2, 76, 178, 223-4, 1108e, 1275 (zanmas- pĕṭh), 1447, 1473, 1672, 1729; K. 4, 17-19, 27, 46, 51, 55, etc.).
m. (in the Hindū doctrine of transmigration) the preceding life, a former birth (Skt. janmântara) (K. 1168).
m. intense freezing cold (i.q. zamzam, q.v.) (Śiv. 1842); purity of nature, a pure nature (Śiv. id.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. zapanôwᵘ), to cause (a holy passage, a name of a deity, mystic prayer) to be muttered (Śiv. 1489).
m. (sg. dat. zāpaṭi), false wheedling, false blandishment; cf. zŏnz. --wahārun -- m.inf. 'to spread such blandishment', deceitfully to wheedle.
n.ag. (f. zapavüñᵘ̈), one who mutters or repeats (holy passages, the name of deity, or the like, see zapun) (Śiv. 646).

m. (sg. dat. zapas), muttering prayers, repeating prayers, etc., in an undertone, repeating holy passages, names of deities, or the like (Gr.Gr. 123; Śiv. 8, 72, 255, 441, 1426, 1789; K. 484, 943); silently counting the beads of a rosary, etc. (Śiv. 1250). --karun -- m.inf. to perform such muttered prayers, etc. (Rām. 957, 961, 1680; K. 974). -māl f. a rosary of beads (for such prayers) (Śiv. 1220, 1489 zapu- m˚). -taph or taph-zaph m. (sg. dat. zapas-tapas, etc.), muttered prayers and religious austerities combined (Śiv. 51, 540, 1448, 1582). ¶ zapa-hum m. a sacrifice or oblation offered in connexion with muttered prayer, etc. -kŏthᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a bag for holding a rosary. -wôlᵘ m. one who, under some vow, performs muttered prayers. ¶ zapas bĕhun m.inf. to set oneself to muttering prayers.

m. (sg. dat. zāphas), weakness, feebleness, debility; fainting, a fainting fit, swoon (Rām. 290, 1181, 1354). --anun -- m.inf. to bring fainting, to cause fainting (Rām. 290, 1354, 1385). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. fainting to come to a person, an attack of fainting to occur. ¶ zāpha-hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), in a swoon, in a faint.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. zāphaladiñ), suffering from faintness, in a swoon.
m. victory, triumph, success. --tulun -- m.inf. persistently goading on another to complete some work. -janga (cf. ظفر جنگ) m. (in carrying out any work) very impetuous, eagerly industrious.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. zopᵘ), to utter muttered prayers, to repeat prayers in an undertone (Gr.Gr. 123); to repeat holy passages, names of deities, or the like (Śiv. 154, 313, 541, 632, 645-6, 983, 1426, 1512, 1567; K. 877); to count silently the beads of a rosary (Śiv. 474).

m. deafness (El.); cf. zorᵘ. -kakav m. a pheasant (El. zar kakû) (it is said to fly high in the air in circles, uttering shrill cries); a certain toy (swung round in the air it makes a sound like a pheasant's cry) (Rām. 922). -tᵃl m. a mulberry, unripe and, therefore, unwholesome. ¶ zara-kutāl m. a disobedient person (esp. a boy) (who, though he hears, is, as it were, deaf to orders). -porᵘ adj. (f. -pürᵘ̈), one who is merely hard of hearing, but who, when at work, takes advantage of his known infirmity and acts (for his own purposes) as if he were stone deaf.

m. groan, plaint, lamentation, wailing; (in Ksh. esp.) a lamentable, or piteous, appeal (cf. lila-zᵒ, p. 522b, l. 11; phĕnzār, p. 700a, l. 36; villa-zᵒ, p. 1114a, l. 3) (El. zár, respect; Śiv. 408; Rām. 64, 209, 494, 725, 788, 991, 1028, 1112, 1143l, 1208, 1380, 1400, 1479, 1481, 1701; K. 239; H. i, 13; iv, 1; YZ. 20, 260); a polite request (Rām. 297, 947, 1130). ¶ zāra adv. respectfully (El. zárah); zāra zāra, adv. with many lamentations (YZ. 43). zāra-pāra m. (sg. dat. -pāras), a lamentable appeal (in order to persuade, or conciliate, another) (El. zárapár, an excuse; zárpár, intercession, request; zárah-párah, adv. respectfully) (Śiv. 113, 396, 429; Rām. 1107, 1144, 1568; K. 33, 35, 40, 136, 156, 238, 272, 275, 345, 663, 827, 912; H. ix, 1; x, 5, zāra-pār; YZ. 269); an apology, asking for forgiveness (El., Śiv. 6); an entreaty, coaxing request (H. ii, 3, 5, zāra-pāra). zāra-villa f. much lamentable appealing (cf. zār ta villay, Rām. 276; villa ta zār, Rām. 1558).

m. fever (with chill and internal burning) (cf. lōsa-zᵒ, p. 533a, l. 27; wāwa-zᵒ, p. 1172b, l. 48) (K.Pr. 255); (esp.) the ephemeral fever of children (El.). -jōsh m. the burning heat of fever. -phakh m. (sg. dat. -phakas), the foul smell of the mouth and breath that accompanies fever.

m. gambling (cf. hār-zᵒ, p. 344b, l. 50; nika-zᵒ, p. 627b, l. 38). --gindun -- m.inf. to gamble (El.; K.Pr. 137, zāras g˚). ¶ zāra-biṭhᵘ̈ f. a meeting of gamblers, a gaming party. -manḍȧjⁱ or -manḍüjᵘ̈ f. a group, or assemblage, of gamesters (for the purpose of gambling). -pav m. the vice, practice, or bad habit of gambling. -wān m. a gambling hell.
m. gold, money, riches, wealth (Śiv. 430, 703; YZ. 185); zar-ĕ-caupān زر چوپان m. a tax collected on flocks (L. 363).

m. a collection, multitude, crowd (cf. mĕwa-zᵒ, p. 611a, l. 39). --˚ a place where anything grows in abundance, -garden, -place, -bed (cf. gul-zār, p. 283b, l. 32; pŏshĕ-zᵒ, p. 779b, l. 2) (W. 112). Cf. zāl 1.
in zár batchi (? spelling and gend.), a woodcock, Scolopax rusticula (L. 125).

m. the hair on the scalp (esp. of an infant). -ḍūnⁱ m.pl. walnuts used at the ceremony of a boy's tonsure. -kôpᵘ m. 'a hair-brainpan', a boy's hairy scalp before tonsure. -kāsun m.inf. to perform the ceremony of tonsure on a boy (usually when he is at least three years of age) (cf. L. 260, zar kasa, the ceremony of tonsure) (K. 483). -kāsay f. the festival of a boy's tonsure.
in zara-zara m. sympathetic sorrow, grief or heart-burning at the sight of another's sorrow or pain.

f. a mote, atom, particle, a little, a tittle, jot (Śiv. 331, 935; Rām. 674; YZ. 41, 231). --zara -- adv. by every atom, entirely (Śiv. 347, 1586). ¶ zarāh or zarā f. i.q. zara (with suff. of indef. art.) (Rām. 41, 1506).
m. harm, injury, hurt, damage (El., Gr.M.); defect, deficiency; affliction, distress, anguish. --karun -- m.inf. to hurt (El.).

m. N. of a celebrated king of Magadha (in Skt. Jarāsandha), two of whose daughters were married to Kams. When Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) slew Kams these fled to their father, who attacked Krushn seventeen times unsuccessfully, but on the eighteenth attack, with the aid of Kālayavana, compelled him to retreat to Dwārakā. He afterwards imprisoned many kings, but Bhīmasēna overpowered and slew him in single combat, and so released them (K. 550 ff., 628 ff., 995 ff., 1019 ff.).
m. a blow, a stroke, a wound (Rām. 1429); stamping, sealing, coining (money); coined money, coin (Gr.M. zarᵃb). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to stamp, coin.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. zardyōv), to be, or become, yellow (Rām. 1520).
m. deafness (El.); (of a gong, or the like) silentness, giving no sound (even when struck).
adj. c.g. woven with gold thread, embroidered with gold (K.Pr. 199).
in zarka-barkh (= زرق برق) adj. c.g. glaring, glittering, magnificent, splendid.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. zarladiñ), suffering from fever, feverish.

m. birth, nativity (cf. bröhman-zᵒ, p. 121b, l. 35); origin, rise, production; life, existence. Cf. zanm. ¶ zarma-chapath  f. (sg. dat. -chapüʦᵘ̈), throwing away one's existence, leading a worthless life; (of something inanimate, such as a water-jar, or the like) throwing away, or losing, its form (by being broken, or the like); cf. zanma-chᵒ, p. 1228a, l. 14. -drölid m. (as subst., f. -drölⁱdĕñ), indigent (owing to incompetence, etc.) from birth (to old age); cf. zanma-dᵒ, p. 1228a, l. 19. -satam f. (sg. dat. -satümᵘ̈), the seventh lunar day of the dark half of the month of Bādᵃrapĕth (see zanma-aiṭham, p. 1228a, l. 9) on which, in some localities, the birth of Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) is celebrated; cf. zanma-sᵒ, p. 1228a, l. 22. -zyuṭhᵘ adj. (f. -ziṭhᵘ̈), elder (by birth) (of brothers or the like). ¶ zarmas yunᵘ m.inf. to come to birth; to have great good fortune, to be very prosperous.
(? spelling) (L. 459) (? cf. زردک) adj. c.g. yellow.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. zorᵘ), to bear, endure (El. gives the meaning 'be', which is perhaps a misprint) (Gr.Gr. 5; Śiv. 157; Rām. 645, 1500, 1571; YZ. 142). Cf. zᵃrawun.
adj. c.g. necessary, needful, requisite (Gr.M.); urgent, important (Gr.M.).
f. (sg. dat. zarūrüʦᵘ̈), need, necessity (Gr.M.); urgency, importance (Gr.M.).

f.pl. the back teeth, grinders. --bĕhañĕ -- f. pl. inf. the back teeth to become stuck, fixed, or immovable, or clenched (e.g. from eating something hard, from drinking very cold water, from fainting, and so on).
m.inf. to become much fatigued, to become exhausted.
or zasuth m. (sg. dat. zastas), zinc, spelter, pewter (cf. Hindī jast).
f. a false statement, misrepresentation, deceitful talk.
c.g. one who habitually makes deceitful statements, a prevaricator.
zötⁱ (cf. zāth), in the following: --zātĕ-sᵃmar adj. c.g. one who has memory of one's former births (in the scheme of transmigration) (cf. smaran). zötⁱ-onⁱ adj. (f. -üñᵘ̈), blind from birth.
f. (sg. dat. zaṭi), the loose hair found in the hand or comb when dressing hair, hair-combings (El.); a clotted lump of hair on the head; the cleaned lump of a ginger- or similar root.

f. (sg. dat. zöʦᵘ̈ 1, for 3, see s.v.), race, family, lineage, tribe (cf. manᵃshĕ-zᵃ, p. 581b, l. 40; parī-zᵒ, p. 752a, l. 19; pȧshⁱ-zⁱ, p. 779b, l. 29; sarpa-zᵒ, p. 937b, l. 40; zīwa-zᵒ, p. 1236a, l. 35; zŏwa-zᵒ, p. 1236b, l. 19; zuwa-zᵒ, p. 1237a, l. 3) (Śiv. 1304; H. xii, 16); caste (cf. kam-zᵒ, p. 442b, l. 28; kŏ-zᵒ, p. 503b, l. 13; sankar-zᵒ, p. 922a, l. 6); the true nature (of anything) (L.V. 4); (in pl.) things, articles (Gr.M.); dēwa-zāth, of divine race, a deity (Rām. 1268); manushĕ-zāth, a human being (Rām. 1167, 1498); cf. zātĕ. -būth gạnzᵃrāvüñᵃ f.inf. to discuss regarding, or estimate, the good or bad qualities (of some one). (Here būth is the equivalent of the Skt. bhūti, birth.) -būth nạñᵉ̆rāvüñᵉ̆ f.inf. to lay bare good and bad qualities, to criticize; esp. to lay bare only defects, to decry, defame, calumniate. ¶ zöʦᵘ̈-kam adj. c.g. of inferior race, caste, kind, etc. (YZ. 24).

f. (sg. dat. zöʦᵘ̈ 2, for 3, see s.v.), nature, disposition (W. 110; K.Pr. 43, 199); breed, tribe, caste (cf. zāth 1, and parī-zᵒ, p. 732a, l. 19); a person, individual (YZ. 182); bad-zāth, a vile creature, miscreant, villain, wretch (Rām. 980, 1667).
adj. (f. zaṭᵘ̈jᵘ̈), one who habitually makes deceitful statements, mendacious.

m. (sg. dat. zātakas), the astrological calculation of a nativity, a horoscope (L. 259, zátuku; Rām. 86, 666, 1275; K. 129, 134, 734). ¶ zātakh-kŏnḍȧjⁱ or -kŏnḍüjᵘ̈ f. the circular diagram in a horoscope in which the positions of the planets at the time of a person's birth are indicated. -phuṭᵃ̇jᵃ̇ or phuṭᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. the bag or cloth case in which all the horoscopes of a household or family are stored. -ṭĕkiñ f. a horoscope, (esp.) an abstract of a full horoscope.
m. delight, joy, voluptuousness; love (El. zauk, zók).

m. the dried powdered lac-resin (or seed lac) that remains after extracting the dye; (in smelting metal) the impurities extracted by the process (Rām. 736). -māl m. ordure involuntarily evacuated at the moment of death. -mīl f. (sg. dat. -mīli), a kind of indelible ink made of lamp-soot mixed with liquid lac-dye. -ras m. lac-juice, lac-dye.
(f. zāyĕ), 2 p.p. of zyonᵘ, q.v., born, used also --˚ as adj., as in sada-zᵒ, p. 863b, l. 2. Cf. also zôwᵘ.

m. conquest, triumph, victory, success, winning (in battle, gaming, or a lawsuit) (i.q. jai, jay, qq.v.) (Śiv. 224, 233, 962, 1136, 1732; Rām. 1274, 1748; K. 569, 659, 711, 765, 915, 959). zayĕ-sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), victorious, triumphing (Śiv. 1628, 1648).
f. a birth, the festival at a birth, used --˚ (cf. pŏtra-zᵒ, p. 799b, l. 42) (K. 95, 102, 129). Cf. zā.
or (q.v.) zai interj. victory! bravo! all hail! (i.q. jai, jay, qq.v.) (Śiv. 204); zayā 1, a single cry of 'victory' (Śiv. 1534, 1851).
f. a daughter. Noted only in the voc. zāyi (YZ. 20, 25).
f. N. of a subordinate goddess, who acted as an attendant to Pārvatī (Śiv. 1495).

adj. c.g. perishing, becoming lost or destroyed; lost, wasted, fruitless, abortive. --gōmotᵘ -- perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), unused, not brought into use, lying without a claimant or user, lying lost and unwanted, lying waste, (of a woman) unmated, (of learning) not drawn upon, (of beauty) not appreciated, and so on; wasted away (by disease, or the like). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to perish; to be or become lost; to be wasted, to be fruitless (owing to not being used, as ab.) (YZ. 547); to waste away (from disease or the like). --karun -- m.inf. to cause to fade, cause to waste away, etc., as ab. (Rām. 212, 1571; YZ. 544).
n.ag. (f. zayĕvüñᵘ̈), conquering, victorious, a conqueror.
m. that which is connected with birth (cf. mölⁱ-zⁱ, p. 566b, l. 33); the festival or rejoicing in honour of the birth of a son.
in zȧyⁱ zö m. the name of the letter ja (which includes za) when written in the Śāradā character.
adj. c.g. very old (of a man or woman), aged, an ancient, greyhead (cf. buḍa zᵒ, p. 85b, l. 10).
f.pl. rupees (a word used principally by plasterers, masons, carpenters, and the like).
adj. (f. zazaryĕ-müʦᵘ̈), (of leaves, or the like) withered, turned yellow; (of an animate being) withered from old age, decrepid. Cf. zazurᵘ and zŏzarun.

m. grass, leaves, or vegetables that have become decayed, withered, yellow, or stale (and are hence fit only to throw away) (Gr.Gr. 121). Cf. zŏzurᵘ. ¶ zazȧrⁱ-köñⁱ f. a small bunch, or wisp, of such leaves (thrown away in the process of preparing vegetables for cooking, or in cleaning or sorting them). -tulᵘ m. id.
(= اذ), prep. from (another form of az 2, q.v.) (Rām. 49, zĕ brahmāh, from Brahmā).
n.ag. (f. zēbavüñᵘ̈), beautiful, lovely, graceful (in form, apparel, or carriage).
(cf. زیب) conj. 3 (2 p.p. zēbyōv), to be beautiful, lovely (in form, apparel, or by graceful carriage).

m. length, longness (cf. atha-zᵒ, p. 65a, l. 26; phala-zᵒ, p. 692b, l. 30) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1598, Rām. 796); stature (El., Rām. 230); cf. zyūṭhᵘ. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give length, to make long, cause to continue for long (e.g. a narrative, hatred, a battle).
(cf. زہ) f. a border, edge; a crescent-shaped fold below the front of a turban over the forehead; the edge or parapet of a roof.
f. intelligence, sagacity; (in Ksh.) ardent desire, eagerness (Rām. 530).
or zĕliñ f. (sg. dat. zĕli), cream (esp. cream of tyre) (cf. dŏda-zᵒ, p. 109b, l. 14) (El., Gr.Gr. 25). zĕli-khôsᵘ m. a dish, or cup, of cream.
f. (sg. dat. zë̆ñᵘ̈), mud (cf. odurᵘ zĕn-hyuhᵘ, p. 15a, l. 38). zë̆ñᵘ̈-thaph m. (sg. dat. -thapas), a handful of mud, such as is taken up in plastering.
f. the payment for winning (at gambling or the like), i.e. the amount or stake paid to the winner by the loser.
n.ag. (f. zēnavüñᵘ̈), one who conquers or defeats; one who wins (a stake iu gambling, booty, or the like); one who earns (K.Pr. 12).
m. (in plastering a wall or the like) the man whose business it is to prepare the mud plaster (cf. zĕn 2).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. zyūnᵘ; 2 p.p. zēñōv), to conquer, defeat (in war, gambling, etc.) (cf. ȧsⁱ gaʦhav zēnȧnⁱ, p. 95a, l. 20) (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 170, 1455, 1674, 1792, 1796, 1835; K. 729, 823, 1019); to win (as the result of conquering, or hard work); to gain (at play), to gain possession of (cf. lās zᵒ, p. 532b, l. 48; nāv zᵒ, p. 665b, l. 17) (El.; Rām. 62, 1263; K. 812; H. x, 1, 6, 7; xi, 1 ff.; xii, 25); to earn, make good profit (cf. pŏñ zᵒ, p. 746b, l. 12; sĕng zᵒ, p. 920a, l. 50) (El.; Gr.Gr. 21; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 262, zĕnun).
