This verb has a ben. form, zēñyĕn, may he conquer! (Gr.Gr. 251). ¶ zēnan-kulᵘ m. 'an earning-tree', a prosperous earner, one of a family or the like who makes more money than the others. ¶ zyūnᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. zīñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), conquered, defeated.
(? spelling) in zer-gŏgul m. N. of a food-plant, a turnip-rooted Umbellifer, the root of which gives a warm food (L. 72 zergogal).
adv. and prep. under, below, beneath (Rām. 1725).

m. ashes with fire still in them, live ashes, embers; cf. zitiñ, zᵃʦ. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to give embers; hence, to incite a person to anger, to provoke to anger, inflame (e.g. by tale-bearing or the like). -katurᵘ m. an ember-sherd; a potsherd on which live embers are placed. -nār m. fire sprung from embers. --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. embers to fall, i.e. suddenly to fall into great affliction (e.g. by loss of property, or hearing bad news). --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to afflict (a person) as ab.; to provoke to anger, enrage.
m. (sg. dat. zēṭhas), N. of the third month of the luni-solar year (in Skt. Jyaiṣṭha), equivalent to May-June (W. 106, Rām. 1634, K.Pr. 128).
in zēṭham zyūṭhᵘ adj. (f. --zīṭhᵘ̈ --), very long, extra long (see zyūṭhᵘ).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. zēṭhyōv), to become long, be lengthened, be long (Gr.Gr. 21, 226; W. 113, zetun; Śiv. 1565, zēṭi misprint for zēṭhi). zēṭhyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. zēṭhyē-müʦᵘ̈), lengthened.

f. the tongue, the organ of speech (cf. ösa-zᵒ, p. 47a, l. 10; dŏda-zᵒ, p. 190b, l. 19; danda zᵒ gaʦhüñᵘ̈, p. 225a, l. 14; gali zᵒ, p. 283b, l. 1; gᵃsa zᵒ, p. 307a, l. 37; zᵒ kaḍüñᵘ̈, p. 386a, l. 23; mŏdᵘ̈rᵘ̈ zᵒ, p. 550b, l. 26; par zᵒ, p. 751a, l. 33; potᵘ zᵒ gaʦhüñᵘ̈, p. 788b, l. 46; tūtⁱ-zⁱ, p. 1041a, l. 20) (El. zeo; Gr.Gr. 134, 138; Gr.M.; W. 139; Śiv. 241, 354, 434, 741, 986, 1908; Rām. 271, 684, 894, 936, 1207, 1615, 1746; K. 193-4, 544, 1152; K.Pr. 175, 188, 229, 253, 262); a tongue, language, dialect (cf. köshirᵘ̈ zᵒ, p. 482a, l. 2) (Gr.M., Śiv. 1796). --dᵃnüñᵃ -- f.inf. 'to shake out the tongue', hence, to take a solemn vow before a god. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give a tongue, endow with speech (Śiv. 378); to promise (K. 829); to agree to, to consent. --dapüñᵘ̈ --, --karüñᵘ̈ --, or --wanüñᵘ̈ --, f.inf. to speak a language (El.). --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to thrust out the tongue, to begin speaking (K. 508). --phirüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to turn the tongue, to change one's speech, adopt another line of argument, change the subject of one's talk (K. 1108). --phaṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the tongue to burst; met. to feel disgraced by overwhelming defeat (Rām. 483, 1091). --ʦaṭüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. rudely to interrupt and silence (another). ¶ zĕwa-pŏrān m. the telling a long story with great prolixity, verbose expatiation. -rôdᵘ adj. (f. -rözᵘ̈), 'long of tongue,' one who, by dint of talking, gets something done by another; cf. zĕvi-rᵒ, bel. -ʦaturᵘ m. (f. -ʦatᵘ̈rᵘ̈), a smart speaker, one who is clever and prompt in reply. -zyūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈), long in tongue, one who possesses a tongue ready and skilled (e.g. in giving orders, instructing, abuse, etc.). ¶ zĕvi-dagi adv. 'at a stroke of the tongue', (of some story, recitation or the like) bursting forth like a flood at the tip of the tongue. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take on the tongue, to utter (a word, etc.), to mention (K. 675, 1055). -rôdᵘ adj. (f. -rözᵘ̈), i.q. zĕwa-rᵒ, ab. (K.Pr. 261). -sostᵘ adj. (f. -süʦhᵘ̈), endowed with a tongue, a ready speaker, one quick in reply or the like (Gr.Gr. 134). -ʦoṭᵘ adj. (f. -ʦüṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. -ʦacĕ), one whose tongue, or that the tongue of which, has been cut off. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who is eloquent (Gr.Gr. 134). ¶ zĕvⁱ zĕvⁱ karun m.inf. to urge another by word of mouth (without doing anything oneself).
or zĕviṭh c.g. (sg. dat. m. zĕvĕ(vi)ṭas ), an informer, tale-bearer, traducer, traitorous betrayer, calumniator (Gr.Gr. 138).
adj. c.g. endowed with tongue, eloquent, a great talker, garrulous (cf. lĕka-zᵒ, p. 518a, l. 47; tūtⁱ-zⁱ, p. 1041a, l. 22) (K.Pr. 263); a calumniator (Gr.Gr. 134).
m. N. of a village about six miles east of Śrīnagar, the ancient Jayavana, where there is a pool sacred to the Nāga Takṣaka (see RT.Tr. i, 220; vii, 607) (Śiv. 928).
m. ornament, jewels (cf. kālī-zᵒ, p. 436a, l. 23).
n.ag. (f. zĕwavüñᵘ̈), one who is being born. zĕwawunuy adv. immediately on being born (Rām. 1587).

conj. that (W. 100). Employed with various forces (see Gr.M. for details). ¶ It is used as a declarative conj. annexing the substance of a speech, etc., to the principal sentence, as in tȧmⁱ mônᵘ zi yi chuh pozᵘ, he affirmed that this is true; tas priʦh zi cyônᵘ nāv kyāh chuh, ask him what is his name (lit. ask him that what is your name). Note that in such cases, as in India Proper, the subordinate sentence is introduced in direct narration. Similarly after verbs expressing necessity, propriety, doubt, intention, and many others for which see Gr.M. s.v. (Śiv. 679, 1232; Rām. 360, 1108, 1137, 1671; K. 9, 63, 65, 66, 104, 113, etc.). ¶ As a consecutive conj., that, so that, as in bŏh dōryōs tyūtᵘ zi shāh gōm band, I have run so much that I have lost my breath (so L.V. 48; Rām. 261, 671, 737, 1133, 1400, 1546, 1659; K. 97, 295, 405, etc.; K.Pr. (zih) 95). ¶ As a final conj., that, in order that, as in sa chĕh mĕhᵃnath karān, zi pananis pānas rachi, she labours in order that she may support herself (K. 19, 38, 127, 163, etc.). ¶ As a causal conj., that, because that, as in kyāh sabab chuh zi ʦᵃh rōzakh-na, what is the reason that thou wilt not remain; so yimi-kinⁱ zi, for this that, i.e. for which reason, wherefore (Śiv. 794, 841; Rām. 382; K. 169, 289, 694, etc.). ¶ As a temporal conj., that, since, as in kē̃h dŏh gay zi suh āv, some days have passed since he came. ¶ As a conj. introducing a subordinate question, as in wuch zi ʦᵃh hĕkakha būzith, see if thou canst understand. ¶ When zi is added to kyāh, the compound kyā-zi, what that? means 'why?', see s.v., p. 502b, l. 44. ¶ When zi is prefixed to a relative pronoun, which is preceded, not followed, by its antecedent, it is almost pleonastic in its force. If anything, it gives a certain indefiniteness to the pronoun, as in zi yus, quasi 'anyone who' or 'whoever'. Thus tim chih timan ṭhagān zi yiman ṭhagith hĕkān chih, they cheat anyone they can. ¶ As an adv. verily, forsooth, (almost pleonastic) (Śiv. 602-3, 619, 1818; Rām. 361, 363, 804, 857, 977, 1096, etc.; K. 448, 460, 640, 717, etc.; K.Pr. (zih) 25, 29, 33, 43, 87, 93, 233). ¶ zi yĕmi-sṻty conj. so that (Gr.M.). --yitha -- conj. so that (Gr.M.). --yuthᵘ -- conj. to such a degree that (Gr.M.).
interj. a form of address, a term of endearment or respect, Sir, Master, Madam (cf. bāba-zī, p. 77b, l. 9) (Śiv. 132).
m. seniority (in age, learning, qualities, social precedence, or the like) (El. zichhar). Cf. zyuṭhᵘ.
zidd ضد f. (El.), m. (Gr.Gr.), contrariness, persisting, insistence; (in Ksh.) envy, hatred, spite, revenge (El.; Gr.Gr. 13; H. vi, 10).

f. gambling, gaming, dicing. --pālüñᵘ̈ -- m.inf. (when a course of gambling has been interrupted) to keep the gambling up (e.g. to fill up the time by a little independent gaming). ¶ zigi-pūnʦhuwᵘ m. 'the gambling half-pice' (see pūnʦhuwᵘ), i.e. (in a gambling contest) the portion of the stake taken from the winner by the other gamblers who are spectators.
m. i.q. jigar, q.v. the liver (LV. 49).
f. a kind of thumb-ring worn by women.
in zikh zikh m. slackness in doing anything, want of energy in the performance of any task.
m. (sg. dat. zīkhas), painful difficulty of breathing, asthma. --lārun -- m.inf. an attack of asthma to come on.
? m. remembering, remembrance; the praise and glorification of God or of a saint, esp. (in Ksh.) a certain Moslem religious exercise with this object and inducing a religious ecstasy (L. 289).
m. a district, or division, of a province (El. zillah).

m. obligation, responsibility, burden of proof. I.q. zimah, q.v. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take responsibility, accept responsibility (for), admit, confess (H. xii, 15). --khālun -- or --khārun -- m.inf. to cause responsibility to mount (on a person), to prove (a person) to be responsible, to prove (a person) guilty (H. x, 12). --khasun -- m.inf. responsibility to mount, i.e. to be proved, guilt to be proved (H. iii, 3). --karun -- m.inf. to make responsibility, to put responsibility (upon, dat.), to put (a person, dat.) in charge (H. viii, 5).
or zimma ذمہ m. responsibility, trust, charge, i.q. zima, q.v.; (in Ksh., adj. c.g.) necessary (El.).
m. a Jina, i.e. the Buddha (L.V. 8).

m. a saddle (El.; Gr.M.; Rām. 978; H. xi, 9; YZ. 238; K.Pr. 74); a staircase. (According to El., s.v., the present kind of leather saddle is said to have been introduced into Kashmīr by the Emperor Akbar.) --ganḍun -- or --ladun -- m.inf. to saddle (El.). --karith -- in gurᵘ zᵒ kᵒ, a horse ready saddled (H. iii, 8). ¶ zīna-köṭhⁱ or -köṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kāchĕ), the wooden frame of the Kāshmīrī saddle. -pôwᵘ m. a single step in a staircase.
f. life, living, existence (Rām. 840, 1500; K.Pr. 149); lifetime (Gr.M. zindagiyĕ-tāmath, during life, as long as one lives).
f. life, living, existence (Rām. 1514); maintenance, livelihood; a condition of (continuous) living, long life (Rām. 1133).
m. N. of a certain wild flower, red in colour and sweetly scented (Rām. 647, 1008, 1092).

or (q.v.) zingarun conj. 3 (2 p.p. zingalyōv), (of a person or thing) to waste away, to become thin, worn to a rag, decayed, ineffective, useless (from disease, from being worn out, or the like). zingalyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. zingalyē-müʦᵘ̈), become thin, as ab.

pl. m. in zingar aʦȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. 'wastings away to enter (a person)', hence, apprehension or alarm (due to memory of former perils or molestations) to attack (a person); cf. zingarun. --ʦānȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to cause such apprehension or alarm to be experienced.

or (q.v.) zingalun conj. 3 (2 p.p. zingaryōv), (of a person or thing) to waste away, to become thin, worn to a rag, decayed, ineffective, useless (from disease, from being worn out, or the like); cf. zŏngarun. zingaryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. zingaryē-müʦᵘ̈), wasted away, become thin, as ab.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. zīñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), to cause (or aid) another to be victorious (in fighting, gambling, etc.).
f. of zyūnᵘ, 1 p.p. of zēnun, q.v.

f. sleepiness, drowsiness (in the midst of work). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'drowsiness to occur', work to be neglected, dereliction of duty or negligence to occur. ¶ zipa karañĕ f. pl. inf. to neglect one's work, show dereliction of duty. ¶ zipan aʦun m.inf. 'to enter drowsiness', to fall into coma (when at the point of death).
m. food and other edible supplies provided for an official when visiting a village.

m. a fine, soft, or low sound; the treble in music; (in Ksh.) (in accompanying a song) the side of the drum struck by the palm of the right hand. ¶ zīra-bam (= زِیروبم) m. low and high notes; a pair of small kettle-drums (Śiv. 1689, 1847); (in Ksh.) the two ends of a drum. Cf. bam-zīra, p. 106b, l. 47.
m. cummin-seed (cf. kāla zᵒ, p. 435b, l. 49). Cf. zyurᵘ and L. 67, zirah siyah, red caraway, Carum sp.
m. (sg. dat. zirātas), a cultivated field (El. zirát).
f. (sg. dat. zirⁱshĕ), a certain fruit, described as a kind of small grape. zirⁱshĕ-shīr m. a drink expressed from this fruit, used as a remedy for dysentery.

sometimes written zīr f. (sg. dat. zērĕ), a nudge, a shove, a poke with the hand or finger (cf. atha-zᵒ, p. 65a, l. 45; gĕv-zᵒ, p. 316b, l. 18; hama-tulⁱ zᵒ, p. 333b, l. 25; prāha-zᵒ, p. 757b, l. 8; potᵘ zᵒ, p. 788b, l. 41; pata-zᵒ, p. 793b, l. 14) (Gr.Gr. 15; Śiv. 1847; Rām. 1410; K. 171, 175); shoving (some inanimate object), making to rock; inciting (Śiv. 1027, 1630); a suggestion, inspiration (esp. an evil suggestion) (Rām. 847). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give a push or shove (K. 428); to nudge (dat.) (H. x, 7); to incite, excite, provoke to rage (dat.). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a nudge or incitement to anger to occur, anger to occur. --zīrᵘ̈ f. inciting to anger by a number of signs, nudges, or the like; shoving (something inanimate) over and over again (so as to make it rock and finally fall).
or f. (sg. dat. zishṭhi), the name of the eighteenth lunar mansion, called in Skt. Jyēṣṭhā.
adj. c.g. (a word borrowed from Skt. jitêndriya) one who has conquered his passions, one who has subdued his senses (Śiv. 1264, 1513, 1601).
f. in zīṭh gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. (in gambling, esp. when one is on the point of winning) losing to occur through some piece of carelessness or blunder.
f. (in a polygamous household) the senior (i.e. first married) wife.

f. (sg. dat. zīṭhᵃrüñᵃ), the act of making longer, lengthening, (esp.) making too long, lengthening more than necessary (Gr.Gr. 121); the condition of being or becoming long (or too long), lengthiness.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. zīṭhᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. zīṭhᵃrun, q.v. zīṭhᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. zīṭhᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. zīṭhᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, ab. q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. zīṭhᵒrᵒ or zyūṭhᵒrᵒ; 2 p.p. zīṭhᵃryōv), to make long, to make longer, to lengthen, to extend (cf. atha zᵒ, p. 65b, l. 1) (Gr.Gr. 121). zīṭhᵒrᵒ-motᵒ or zyūṭhᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. zīṭhᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), made long, extended, lengthened.
in zīṭhⁱ-pōsh m. N. of a certain flower that blooms in the month of Zēṭh (q.v.) (Rām. 205).
f. a spark (of fire); cf. zĕta, zᵃʦ. ¶ zitiñĕ-gāsh m. a spark light, a distant tiny gleam of light. -kyomᵘ m. a spark-worm, a fire-fly.
m. an astrologer (cf. zȧrⁱ-zⁱ, p. 1231b, l. 37) (El.).

m. the principle of life, life, existence (cf. zuv) (Śiv. 993, Rām. 418, K. 196); the individual or personal soul of a living being (Śiv. 559, 980); a soul, in the sense of a living creature, a thing with life (cf. zal-zīv, p. 1220b, l. 39) (Gr.M.; L.V. 12; Śiv. 162, 202, 335, 744, 1051, 1299, 1304, 1509, 1719, 1816). ¶ zīwa-gāth m. (sg. dat. -gātas), killing life, taking life, slaying. -zāth f. (sg. dat. -zöʦᵘ̈), a living creature (i.q. zuwa-zᵒ, p. 1237a, l. 3).
m. a suffix of respect added to a proper name, as in Krushna-zīv (Śiv. 1325, 1761; K. 1, 119, 226, etc.), Rāma-zīv (Rām. 288) (so K. 915). Cf. jī, juv.
m. N. of a certain mantra or spell, the utterance of which restores a corpse to life (Śiv. 321).
m. life; life, mode of existence, livelihood, profession (Gr.M.); --˚ a living creature (Śiv. 739). --karun -- m.inf. to earn one's living (Gr.M.).
adj. c.g. living, alive. -mŏkth adj. c.g. 'liberated while living', one who, being purified by a true knowledge of the Supreme, is freed from future birth while yet alive.
m. the individual soul enshrined in the human body (as opposed to the Supreme Soul) (Śiv. 1064).
adj. living, while yet alive, during lifetime (L.V. 12). zīwȧntⁱ mọ̆khᵃ̇tᵃ̇, men who obtain final release while yet alive (L.V. 6).
m. (sg. dat. zīwatas), the condition of a living being, the condition of life, life (Śiv. 1340, 1767).

f. victory (Gr.Gr. 129; I.K. IX, ii, 49); income, earnings, profits of work (El. zí; Śiv. 232, ziyō m.c.; K.Pr. 70, 138, 204, 262, zí). ziyi-kulᵘ m. 'the income-tree', (in a family) the member who by good conduct and industry earns the largest income.
ziyāfat ضیافت f. an entertainment, feast, banquet (El. zí,áfat, m.; H. x, 4, 11); hospitality, entertainment; a dish of food brought as a present, a present of dainty food (H. x, 5, 10).
(? spelling) (L. 463), the season for sowing rice. Cf. wāph.
adj. (f. zŏbürᵘ̈), having the lower part of the cheek swollen (by disease or other cause).
m. paddy that grows in marshy land.

m. a marsh reed-bed (cf. wala-zᵒ, p. 1111b, l. 21), a paddy-field in a marsh or similar land. ¶ zabi-gāsa m. a kind of reed used for making mats. -kukᵘ m. a kind of small bird haunting sheets of water (Śiv. 1812). -wôñᵘ m. the water in a flooded paddy-field, or flowing from it.
m. one who is clothed in rags. Cf. züṭᵘ̈.

m. a hole, cavity, aperture (cf. atha-zᵒ, p. 65a, l. 30; athas-zᵒ, p. 66b, l. 8; nadarinⁱ zȧdⁱ, p. 623b, l. 4; phaka-zᵒ, p. 689a, l. 26; tāla-zᵒ gaʦhun, p. 997b, l. 5) (El. zud, Śiv. 1018, K. 154); cf. zad 1. --karun -- m.inf. to pierce (El. zúd kᵒ). ¶ zȧdⁱ gaʦhȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. 'holes to occur', to become full of holes (e.g. of a metal vessel, clothes, etc.) (cf. parininⁱ zᵒ gᵒ, p. 774b, l. 42).
(f. zözᵘ̈), i.q. zāda, q.v., in harām-zᵒ, p. 348b, l. 43.

or zrôḍᵘ m. a hollow, low-land, or ravine perennially full of water, a pond, lake (El. zóḍ or zróḍ, a ferry, a ford). ¶ zöḍⁱ-babⁱrⁱ f. a certain medicinal plant growing in marshy soil, and described as having long and sweet-scented leaves. It is used as an expectorant (L. 75 zadibabr). -nāwa f.pl. 'pond-boats', i.e. a very heavy torrential fall of rain (quasi, so much water that the ground is changed into a navigable pond).
in zȧḍⁱ-bal m. N. of a site north of Śrīnagar behind the Hāra-parbuth (q.v.).
adj. (f. züḍᵘ̈, sg. dat. zajĕ), dull, stupid, i.q. zaḍ 3 (El.).
adj. (m. sg. dat. zö̃galis; f. zö̃güjᵘ̈), (wood, or the like) grown in the forest, forest (timber, etc.).

m. (in a Hindū sacrificial ceremony) N. of a certain mystic sign marked over the fire-receptacle or on the head-dress of the wife of the person for whom the sacrifice is being performed, in Skt. called jvālā-liṅga, or 'flame-liṅga' (cf. Kathāsarit-sāgara, i, 28).
adj. (of a man) lanky, very long and thin.

adj. c.g. manifest, evident, plain, visible (El. záhir; Gr.M.; Śiv. 328, 652, 682). --karun -- m.inf. to make manifest, publish, display (El., Gr.M.). --pöṭhⁱ -- adv. visibly, openly (Śiv. 235); ostensibly (El.). --sapadun -- m.inf. to become manifest, become evident, be revealed, to appear (Gr.M.); (?) to exist (only El.). -zamāda (= ظآہر ضماد) m. 'a visible balm', hence (in Ksh.) outward show, formality, formal example of conduct (Śiv. 652, -zamādāh, with suff. of indef. art.). ¶ zöhirā ظآہرا adv. outwardly, manifestly (Gr.M.).
the planet Venus, in zŏhᵃra-khōtan f. 'a Venus', a lovely, delicate-limbed, woman. Cf. khôtūn.

(for 2, 3, see zāgun and zālun 2) f. a fine, delicate, net (such as a spider's web, or other fine net) (cf. zalȧrⁱ-zⁱ, s.v. zalurᵘ). Cf. zāl 1. ¶ zāji-pulahorᵘ m. a kind of woman's shoe, woven of very fine string made of a special kind of grass. ¶ zöjⁱ-obur m. a light cloud (resembling a delicate net, and not causing rain).
in zŏka-wörᵘ̈ f. a light club used in a game in which another club thrown on the ground is hit to a distance.
in zŏkarambã̄ḍē m. a vile fellow (used in censorious reference). Cf. zọ̆kᵘ and bã̄ḍē.
f. a woman with much hair on the privities. --kākañ -- f. a dissolute woman, a strumpet (obsc. abuse).
m. the hair of the female privities. ¶ zọ̆kⁱ-khūrⁱ m. a razor for shaving this hair. -wāl m. a single one of these hairs.
f. brief drowsiness (Gr.Gr. 16). According to El. this word is a rural name for a woman's head-dress.

f. a brief doze (e.g. of a sick person, or of some one taking a brief rest) (cf. nẹ̆ndᵃri-zᵃ, p. 642b, l. 26) (El. zŏlah, drowsiness; Rām. 679; YZ. 153, 566). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'drowsiness to occur', (in some delicate enquiry) a careless blunder to occur (when one is at the point of success), negligence to occur, one's eyes not to be kept open (Rām. 1037, zŏli gaʦhun; 1229, zŏla g˚; K.Pr. 263, zulih gaʦhun). ¶ zŏlan aʦun m.inf. to fall into coma (e.g. when at the point of death).
adj. c.g. habitually drowsy, lazy, negligent.
m. a fetter, shackle. Cf. zāgnūl.
adj. c.g. tyrannical, unjust, cruel (El., Gr.M.).
m. the foundation trench of a house.

(for 2, see zālun) m. the joining place of two tree-branches (cf. duzôlᵘ, p. 272b, l. 29, and Rām. 603); the space (including the web) between two adjacent fingers or toes (cf. atha-zᵒ, p. 65a, l. 40; sandija-zölⁱ dinⁱ, p. 919a, l. 38) (K.Pr. 184, 259); an interstice (between teeth, or the like) (cf. danda-zᵒ, p. 225a, l. 13); a cluster of flower-buds, or the like (cf. pōshĕ-zᵒ, p. 779a, l. 49); network; met. kāla-zᵒ, the efflux, or passing, of time (L.V. 64). ¶ zölⁱ-baĩs m. fishing by net (cf. zāl 1), as opposed to fishing with hook and line (wölⁱ-baĩs, q.v., p. 1112b, l. 37) (L. 159, zail bans). -hār f. (hiding) a cowry between the fingers (a method of cheating in gambling). -panjara m. lattice-work (for a window or the like). -pīr f. N. of a certain serious disease, involving boils or sores at the root of the spaces between the fingers or toes. -pushĕṭh f. (sg. dat. -pushᵉ̆ṭi), a network sandal-lace. -trọ̆pᵘ m. a method of sewing, in which the edges of two pieces of cloth are apart, and connected by a kind of net- work. -wö̃ka f.pl. (among girls) a method of dressing in a netted pattern the long plaited hair that hangs down behind (YZ. 155, K.Pr. 25). --yinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. itchiness to come between the fingers or toes.
adj. (f. züjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), (of dainty food) eagerly desired. Cf. zalun.
adj. c.g. ornamented with a net pattern.
m. one who is accountable or responsible (for), a surety, guarantor (Gr.M., K.Pr. 67).

in zömith-gŏbur m. (sg. dat. -gŏbaras), the son of a husband's sister (see zām). -nĕcyuwᵘ m. (sg. dat. -nĕcivis), id. -nŏsh f. the daughter-in-law of a husband's sister (cf. wōra-zömith-nŏsh, p. 1136b, l. 49).
m. the husband of a woman's husband's sister, the husband of a wife's sister-in-law (cf. pŏphaturᵘ zᵒ, p. 749a, l. 40; piturᵘ zᵒ, p. 803b, l. 15; wōra-zᵒ, p. 1136b, l. 50).
f. the daughter of a husband's sister (cf. pitᵘ̈rᵘ̈ zᵒ, p. 803b, l. 33; wōra-zᵒ, p. 1137a, l. 1).
adj. c.g. very lean in body, very thin, a mere skeleton, skin and bone.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. zŏngaryŏv), (of a person or thing) to waste away, to become thin, worn to a rag, become languid, etc., as in zingarun, q.v. zŏngaryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. zŏngaryē-müʦᵘ̈), wasted away, become thin, as ab.
m. a kind of anklet or wristlet furnished with hollow balls filled with pieces of stone, etc., so as to make a ringing sound.
adj. (f. zŏngürᵘ̈), (of a man or woman) long, lean, but strong, long and wiry (cf. zọ̆ngᵘ).
m. a long, lean, but strong man, a wiry fellow. Cf. zŏngurᵘ.
m. fire (esp. when a great blaze).
adj. (f. zünjᵘ̈), legged, endowed with legs, used --˚, as in oku-zᵒ, p. 19b, l. 12; aiṭha-zᵒ, p. 66b, l. 49; ʦŏ-zongᵘ, p. 1091b, l. 33.
(? spelling and gend.), N. of a certain plant, the powdered roots of which, mixed with butter, are used to strengthen the hair (L. 74).

f. hypocritical or deceitful soothing, conciliation, appeasing, blandishment, wheedling; cf. zāpaṭh. --wahārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to spread (the net) of blandishment', i.e. (with the object of swindling) to begin wheedling. --wanüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (with the same object) to use false wheedling words. ¶ zŏnzi-gorᵘ adj. (f. -gürᵘ̈), a dishonest wheedler.
adj. c.g. one who is a dishonest wheedler, a swindler.
f. a kind of tall narrow withy basket, used for holding flowers, fruit, or the like. Cf. zain 2.

m. (f. züñᵘ̈, q.v., s.v.), a man, a male person, an individual (esp. used in enumeration, as in kunᵘ zᵒ, p. 453b, l. 38; kunuy zᵒ, p. 454a, l. 9) (El. zaun, zŏn; Gr.Gr. 85; Śiv. 1199; Rām. 355, 856, 1462; K. 887; H. viii, 5, 11; x, 1, 2, 5, 6, 12; K.Pr. 95, 132). kunᵘ or kunuy zonᵘ, only one person, a single person, one who is all alone (Rām. 973, 1744; K. 563; H. viii, 7). ¶ zani path zani adv. person by person, man by man, each person in order (Gr.Gr. 158). ¶ zanis-züñᵘ̈ f. a man's woman, a woman living as his wife with a man not her wedded husband, a kept woman, or else one made over in marriage to a man by her people, but without the customary dowry, etc.

(for 2, see s.v. zān) adj. c.g. acquainted, familiar, recognized (from frequent meetings); (as subst. m.) an acquaintance, a person with whom one is acquainted (Gr.M.). zöñᵘ̈-kār adj. c.g. (of a person) acquainted, familiar, recognized (from previous meetings), an acquaintance. Cf. zān-kār, p. 1225a, l. 15.
m. a kind of sharp-pointed mattock used like a plough in preparing wet rice fields (Śiv. 1531).
m. a tax office (where market dues, octroi, or the like, are collected).
or zābita ضابطہ m. established practice, custom (El. zápitah).

m. strength, force, power, vigour, virtue (cf. atha-zᵒ, p. 65a, l. 48; dana-zᵒ, p. 222a, l. 28; hāra-zᵒ, p. 345a, l. 4; kam-zᵒ, p. 442b, l. 26; maʦha-zᵒ, p. 609a, l. 41) (Gr.Gr. 22; Gr.M.; Śiv. 3, 123, 214, 738, 1303, 1562, 1670, 1734; Rām. 409, 477, 479, 480, 490, 522, 559, 647, 696, 710, 808, 852, 881, 954, 997, 1115, 1237, 1343, 1393, 1454, 1748); az-zōr, violently (Rām. 819). --karun -- m.inf. to use force, make an effort (El.; Śiv. 1636); to use moral force, insist (H. viii, 2; xii, 15). ¶ zōra or zōra-sṻty, or -sān adv. strongly (El. zórah, Gr.M.); violently, forcibly, energetically (Gr.M.; W. 156; Śiv. 1672, 1674; Rām. 278, 499, 531, 562, 822, 875, 949, 1399, 1455; K. 1125, zōr of printed text is a misprint; YZ. 455, -sān; K.Pr. 135, 166, 187, 262). ¶ zōras-sṻty anun m.inf. to force (El. zoras set anun).
or zōrawörī f. power, force (Rām. 699, 1343, zōrāwarī; 972, zōrawörī).
f., i.q. zār 1, q.v. (Śiv. 215, 385; Rām. 1546). Cf. zörⁱ 2.
or zōrāwar زوراور or zōrāwār adj. c.g. strong, overcoming, powerful (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 14; Rām. 530 (zōrāwar), 1302 (-wār); H. xi, 2 (-wār)).

adj. (f. zürᵘ̈), deaf (cf. kan zᵒ, p. 447b, l. 24) (El. zȧr, zu̇r; Gr.Gr. 8, 10; Gr.M.; W. 17; K.Pr. 34, 191, 234, 261); (of a gong, or the like) without sound, silent. Cf. zar 1. ¶ zȧrⁱ asun m. the laugh of a deaf man (who does not himself hear a joke, but who laughs perfunctorily because he sees some one else smile). -dĕv m. (f. -dĕviñ), 'a devil for deafness,' one who is very deaf, one who is stone deaf. -zitish m. a deaf astrologer (who does not hear the questions asked him and yet is venturesome enough to give predictions in reply that, of course, are wrong).
m. a gambler, gamester (i.q. zörⁱ 1, q.v.) in katari-zᵒ, p. 491b, l. 20, q.v.
f. in ʦūr zörᵘ̈, p. 1080b, l. 23, i.q. zār 2, q.v.

m. a gambler, gamester (cf. hāra-zᵒ, p. 345a, l. 5; nika-zᵒ, p. 627b, l. 41; narda-zᵒ, p. 650a, l. 43) (El. zãr, zãrí; K.Pr. 261); cf. zôrᵘ. -biṭhᵘ̈ f. a meeting of gamblers, a company or society of gamesters. -dĕv m. a professional gamester, the head or proprietor of a gambling hell. -khorᵘ adj. (f. -khürᵘ̈), 'a gambler-scald-head,' head,' a mean young gamester. -manḍȧjⁱ or -manḍüjᵘ̈ f. a group, or assembly, of gamesters. -phash m. 'a gambler-cyclone', a very rapid kind of gambling (in which dice, etc., are not used, and there are only rapid wagers on the gambling board). -wān m. a gambling hell.

or zörī in lila-zᵒ, p. 522b, l. 13, i.q. zār 1, a lamentable, or piteous, appeal (cf. villa-zᵒ) (Rām. 220, 252, 316, 938, 1540, 1673; YZ. 303); a polite request, supplication, conciliatory words (Rām. 1107, 1637, 1692, 1735). Cf. zöriy.
in lōsa-zörⁱ marun, p. 533a, l. 29. ? Cf. zar 2.
f. a cough (cf. Gr.Gr. 112, where it is stated to be m.).
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. zŏsaladiñ), afflicted with coughing, suffering from a cough.
m. the name used in schools for the aspirated sonant palatal letter in the Śāradā character, corresponding to the Nāgarī jha.
conj. 1 (this verb is impersonal. 1 p.p. zọ̆sᵘ; 2 p.p. zŏsōv), to cough (Gr.Gr. 122, Gr.M., L.V. 46).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. zōtyōv), to shine, gleam, glitter (e.g. of a lamp, a jewel, a polished metal) (El.; Gr.Gr. 174; Śiv. 434, 470, 792, 815, 946). The causal form of this word is zōtanāwun (Gr.Gr. 174); it also has a passive zōtana yiwān chuh, he is shining, equivalent in meaning to zōtān chuh (Gr.Gr. 169).

(sometimes written zuv 1) f. a louse (cf. khŏshāl khānas zuv aʦun, p. 419a, l. 7; kapar-zŏv, p. 463b, l. 50) (El. zauv) (K.Pr. 10, 86, 169, 217). ¶ zŏwa-kach m. a certain medicinal grass. -khorᵘ adj. (f. -khürᵘ̈), a louse-scaldhead, a child or other person so afflicted with lice that he is apparently a scaldhead, or bald from that reason; hence, used as a term of abuse. -kala m. one (usually a boy) whose (unshaven) head is full of lice. -kān m. 'a mine of lice', N. of a bulrush (? Phragmites communis), from the head of which the cottony fluff (kalaronᵘ, q.v.) used in plastering is obtained. This head is supposed to resemble a louse, and as they are very numerous, the plant is called 'a mine'. -kŏnḍal f. 'a brazier-bowl of lice', i.e. a dirty girl or other female (who suggests lousiness) (used abusively). -kŏnḍul m. a dirty boy or other male (as ab.). -kôpᵘ m. 'a louse-skull', a lousy head of a woman or (unshaven) boy. -lạgᵃn m. 'a louse-wedding', a wedding secretly performed and maimed of its full rites (on account of poverty, etc.). -polᵘ m. 'a basket of lice', i.e. a number of lice collected on one spot or person. -ṭapürᵘ̈ f. a woman whose hair is full of lice, used as a term of abuse. -zāth f. (sg. dat. -zöʦᵘ̈), 'a lousy birth', a vile place of origin, (of some person) an ignoble birthplace, a mean, or base, origin.

adj. (f. zövijᵘ̈), minute, delicate, fine, (of cotton goods, or the like) soft (cf. tāla-zᵒ, p. 997b, l. 10) (YZ. 73, 289). Cf. zöyyulᵘ. zövilⁱ-wôlⁱ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a smart trickster, an insidious cheat.
m. minuteness, delicacy, fineness (cf. tāla-zᵒ, p. 997b, l. 7). Cf. zöyⁱjyār.
m. (sg. dat. zōwaranas), the amount of curd kept back for adding to fresh milk (like rennet) to turn it into curd. Cf. the preceding.
m. N. of a certain sacred spot and spring in Kashmīr (Śiv. 928, 929).
f. (sg. dat. zōwᵃrüñᵃ), the act of setting agoing, starting (something) (cf. nāra zᵒ, p. 648b, l. 27).
conj. 1, i.q. zōwᵃrun, q.v. zōwᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. zōwᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. zōwᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, s.v. zōwᵃrun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. zōwᵒrᵒ), to beget, to bring to birth, to give a start to, set agoing (e.g. a fire, a quarrel, etc.); to cause (milk) to curdle, to curdle (milk) (cf. zōwarun; El. zaorun). This verb is the causal of zyonᵘ, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 175). zōwᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. zōwᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), set going (by some one), started.
(f. zövᵘ̈), i.q. zāv, 2 p.p. of zyonᵘ, q.v., sometimes used --˚ as in aḍa-zᵒ, p. 12b, l. 21. Cf. also zāv.
f. delicateness, fineness (cf. tāla-zᵒ, p. 997b, l. 13).

(also written zöyulᵘ) adj. (f. zöyijᵘ̈), minute, delicate, (of thread or the like) fine, (of paper or the like) thin, (of cotton goods or the like) soft (cf. tāla-zᵒ, p. 997b, l. 11) (El., Gr.Gr. 141, Gr.M., L.V. 102, K.Pr. 183); cf. zövyulᵘ. zöyilⁱ-wôlⁱ m. (f. -wājĕñ), one who acts delicately (e.g. in consolation, in bargaining, in reproaching, and so on).
m. minuteness, delicacy, fineness (cf. tāla-zᵒ, p. 997b, l. 7) (Gr.Gr. 141, zöyᵉ̆jyār). Cf. zövⁱjyār.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. zŏzaryōv), to become withered, (of leaves, or the like) to turn yellow (Gr.Gr. 121); (met.) (of a human being) to wither from anxiety, sorrow, or the like. zŏzaryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. zŏzaryē-müʦᵘ̈), withered (as ab.). Cf. zazaryō-motᵘ.

adj. (f. zŏzürᵘ̈), (of grass, vegetables, or the like) withered, decayed, turned yellow; cf. zazurᵘ. --aʦun -- m.inf. to become withered, as ab.; (of a human being) to become withered from sorrow or the like. --ʦānun -- m.inf. to cause (a person) to become withered as ab. ¶ zŏzȧrⁱ-tulⁱ m. (in cleaning or sorting vegetables) the collection of withered or yellow leaves thrown away as refuse. ¶ zŏzürᵘ̈ köñᵘ̈ f. id.
adj. c.g. of good caste, of good birth, of good breed; (of something inanimate) of good quality. Cf. zāth 1.
(for 1, 2, see zāth 1, 2) adj. c.g. having such and such a nature, used --˚, in bicⁱ-zⁱ, p. 149b, l. 28. Cf. zāth 2.
adj. c.g. weak, infirm; (in Ksh.) bad, wicked, faulty (El.).
adj. c.g. quick, swift, in zūdā-zūd adv. (with vbs. of going, or the like) very quickly, very speedily.
adj. c.g. separated, apart, etc., i.q. judā, q.v.
or zūrĕ in zᵒ lagun, to acquire, or fall into, bad habits (L.V. 70).
or zudöī (= جدآی) f. separation, parting, absence (Gr.M.), i.q. judöyⁱ, q.v.
f. (pl. nom. zadĕ), a small hole (H. vii, 25). Cf. zodᵘ.
in the following: zūgⁱ-lö̃kar m. N. of an island in the outfall of the Ḍal lake near Śrīnagar. -wörᵘ̈ f. a kind of jar or basket used for containing cleaned cotton-wool ready for spinning.

or zūjⁱ, f. (sg. dat. zōjĕ), a long piece of cloth worn by Brāhmaṇ women, extending from the crown of the head down to the small of the back (cf. kana-zᵒ, p. 448b, l. 5) (El., K.Pr. 167); a cover, curtain, veil (Śiv. 1807); the delicate network covering the seed-vessel of a lotus. ¶ zōjĕ-astar m. a kind of cotton cloth woven like a net, muslin, net. -loṭᵘ m. a short zūjᵘ̈. -mahārĕñ f. a bride ceremonially invested with a zūjᵘ̈ (this being done when she emerges from childhood). -sᵃʦ m. a tailor whose profession it is to make these head-dresses.
or zulf زلف m. a curl, lock of hair, ringlet (El.; YZ. 64, 65, 565).
or zulm ظلم m. tyranny, violence, cruelty, oppression (El.; Gr.M.; H. ix, 1, 6; K.Pr. 118). --karun -- m.inf. to oppress (El.; W. 88; H. ix, 1).
(L. 74), zamb-chule (El.) m. Prunus padus (Bird cherry) (L. 79 also gives zonb).

or zumutᵘ adj. (f. zumüʦᵘ̈), half alive, half dead, having only a feeble spark of life (cf. aḍa-zᵒ, p. 12b, l. 15); (of something naturally juicy) half dried; (of something being cooked) half cooked, half raw.

or zūnᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. zūni), moonlight (cf. brāri-zᵒ, p. 125b, l. 24; kāʦa-zᵒ, p. 493a, l. 40; potᵘ-zᵘ, p. 788b, l. 35) (Gr.Gr. 20, zūnᵘ̈; Gr.M.; L. 462, zun; W. 7, 13, id.; L.V. 9; Śiv. 166, 470, 525, 583; Rām. 187, 431, 1075, 1084, 1391, 1589, 1629, 1771; K. 280, zūnᵘ̈; YZ. 4, 80, 82, 145, 159; K.Pr. 34); potᵘ zūn, the end of the moonlight, the last hours of the night (L.V. 105). --khĕni khasun -- m. 'to rise to eat the moonlight', to be intoxicated with self-conceit. --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'moonlight to attack a person', i.e. to become wasted away and exhausted (from disease, over exertion, starvation, or the like, as if one were suffering from phthisis) (cf. Rām. 1201). ¶ zūna-ḍab f. a kind of covered balcony (in which people sit to enjoy the moonlight) (H. viii, 1). -gāsh m. the light of moonlight, the light of the moon. -nẹ̆ndᵃr f. sleep with the eyes remaining open. -pach m. the light fortnight of a lunar month (Rām. 1108g). -pȧchⁱ-zāmotⁱ perf. part. (f. -pȧchⁱ-zāmüʦⁱ), 'born in such a lunar fortnight,' one who is universally disliked or unpopular. ¶ zūni-grohun or -grônᵘ m. an eclipse of the moon (YZ. 268).

f. (f. of zonᵘ 1, q.v.), a woman (cf. kuñᵘ̈ zᵒ, p. 453b, l. 39; kuñᵘ̈y zᵒ, p. 454a, l. 10) (Śiv. 534, 1663-4; H. xii, 6, 7); kuñᵘ̈y züñᵘ̈, only one woman, a single woman, a woman all alone (Rām. 1051 (küñᵘ̈y, misprint for kuñᵘ̈y), 1200, 1225; H. xii, 15).
(cf. زرق) f. detraction, insinuation; an ill-natured hint, i.e. a hint or sign designed to remind a person of some former wrong, and so to rouse his anger.
f. progeny, offspring; (in Ksh.) the offspring (of God), the whole world (H. vii, 8).

m. a daughter's son, a grandson (cf. par-zᵒ, p. 751b, l. 8) (Gr.Gr. 17). ¶ zurⁱ-karm m. the obsequial rite performed by a daughter's son on behalf of his grandparent. -pĕnḍ m. the piṇḍa, or ball of rice, offered by him at this rite.
f. a daughter's daughter, a granddaughter (cf. par-zᵒ, p. 751b, l. 9) (Gr.Gr. 17); N. of a certain bone, the great trochanter of the femur (El. zur, m.).

f. (sg. dat. zacĕ), a rag, a worn or old patched cloth (cf. üdᵘ̈rᵘ̈ zᵒ, p. 15a, l. 42; dajĕ-zᵒ, p. 203a, l. 49; dastār-zᵒ, p. 256b, l. 36; kam-zᵒ, p. 442b, l. 47; löchⁱ-zⁱ, p. 507b, l. 15; lō̃gi-zᵒ, p. 512a, l. 10; mal-zᵒ, p. 564b, l. 3; phĕran-zᵒ, p. 705b, l. 30; pula-hȧrⁱ-zⁱ, p. 730b, l. 19; pöʦhⁱ-zⁱ, p. 808a, l. 16; paizār-zᵒ, p. 820b, l. 38; rawa-zᵒ, p. 852a, l. 48; ṭōpi-zᵒ, p. 1014a, l. 26; ʦādari-zᵒ, p. 1054b, l. 27; wanda-zᵒ, p. 1122b, l. 30; wurȧnⁱ-zⁱ, p. 1142a, l. 18) (El. zaiṭ; Gr.Gr. 10; Gr.M.; W. 8 zạṭh, 12 zaṭ; K. 1118-9, 1143; H. xi, 9; K.Pr. 74, 152, 178, 261). -püṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. zacĕ-pacĕ), 'rag and sheet', a general name for clothes of all kinds. ¶ zacĕ pl. nom. rags, a collection of rags. -chal f. a piece of rag. -gūdᵘ m. blameable, censurable, reprehensible (see gūdᵘ). -gorᵘ m. a rag-buyer, a man whose profession it is to go about buying rags. -hurᵘ m. a lump of rag (e.g. such as would be used for applying plaster) (see hurᵘ 2). -hurᵘ̈ f. id. -lọ̆ʦhᵘ m. a large globular shaped lump of rags. -mahādīv m. one who, even though well off, out of humility or the like, habitually wears patched or ragged garments (cf. mahādēv). --nērañĕ -- f. pl. inf. rags to issue, to turn into rags, to become worn out (of a garment, book, or the like). -palav m. a ragged sheet or cloak. -pura nonᵘ gaʦhun m.inf. that which is (under) a ragged cloth to become revealed, i.e. anything concealed (such as a shameful action or a secret) to become public property (cf. pura 2). -purra m. a long strip of rag (such as would be used for a turban or the like). -shikhurᵘ or -shukhurᵘ m. a mass of rags (of one piece of cloth not in separate pieces, but hanging together like a number of loops) (cf. shikhurᵘ 1). -tilim f. a little bit of rag. -trọ̆ngᵘ m. a tied-up bundle of rags. -züṭᵘ̈ f. 'rag to rag', i.e. (in arranging a marriage) mutual equality (in family, religion, property, relationships, and so on) of both parties. ¶ zacĕn-pacĕ-phyurᵘ m. clearing out rags, selecting the useful ones out of a collection of rags.

m. (voc. zuwā, written zúah, K.Pr. 67) (i.q. zīv, q.v.), the principle of life, life, existence (to be distinguished from juv, the term of respect, see art. j, p. 369a, l. 39, and juv, p. 379b, l. 1) (cf. orᵘ zᵒ, p. 42a, l. 24; kam-zᵒ, p. 442b, l. 30) (El. zú; Gr.Gr. 124; Gr.M.; W. 124, 156, zu; L.V. 54; Śiv. 191, 226, 316, 984, 1279, 1446; Rām. 151, 163, 177, 271, 306, 427, 496, 671-2, 850, 1094, 1121, 1143, 1490, 1507, 1673, 1737; K. 56, 187, 346, 432, 573, 674; YZ. 33, 558; K.Pr. 111, 262, zú); the soul, spirit (Gr.M.; L.V. 106; Rām. 299; K. 110, 506; H. ii, 4; K.Pr. 17); a person's self (Śiv. 51; K. 60, 986; K.Pr. 67); the body, the material personality. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take life, to destroy life (L.V. 54, 810, 858). ¶ zuwa-dādi adv. for (the protection of) the body from pain, as a preventive, as a prophylactic (cf. the next). -dôdᵘ m. bodily pain. -ḍanḍ m. a life substitute, the giving something (one's own self, an animal, a material offering) in sacrifice to relieve another. -larza m. fear for the body (caused by attack of disease, an enemy, something terrifying, and so on); cf. larzun. -röchⁱ f. preservation of the body, anything (e.g. armour or an amulet) that protects the body. -rostᵘ adj. (f. -rüʦhᵘ̈), insensible, lifeless (El. zúrust). -zāth (f. (sg. dat. -zöʦᵘ̈), a living creature (i.q. zīwa-zᵒ, p. 1236a, l. 35); the animate world (as opposed to the inanimate). --zuwa lagun -- m.inf. (in time of epidemic or general calamity) to be filled with constant apprehension for one's life. ¶ zuvücᵘ̈ shĕkᵃlkarüñᵃ f.inf. to take precautions for one's future, self-protection.
f. a lamp-stand (usually of wood) (cf. dᵃpa-zᵃ, p. 232a, l. 19; dupa-zᵒ, id., l. 35) (El. zúr m.; Gr.Gr. 20; W. 13, zur). Cf. zuwulᵘ. zuwᵃri-bĕha m. the support, or base, of a lamp-stand.

or (Rām. 839) zuwūlᵘ m. an illumination, festal arrangement of lights (El. zúl). ¶ zuwal-māl f. 'an illumination-garland', i.e. a beautiful woman. ¶ zuwȧlⁱ-nāv f. a boat illuminated with thousands of lights and set floating on festal occasions.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. zuvyōv), to live, to be alive (Gr.Gr. 22, 124; Gr.M.; Śiv. 944; K.Pr. 258); to make a living, carry on life, support oneself (K.Pr. 257); to come to life, revive.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. zuwᵃrôwᵃ), to cause to be alive, give life to, bring into (living) existence (e.g. a seed), to cause, to start (e.g. a quarrel or a blaze of fire) (Śiv. 1678, zuwarāwun).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. zuwᵒrᵒ), to revive (someone or something), to give new life to, to restore to life, to restore to good order (something that had been rendered useless or broken), to revive (a nearly extinguished fire), and so on.
m. an island, isle, islet (Rām. 596, 606 zuv).

f. blaze, flame, glare, effulgence; a N. of Pārvatī or Durgā (Śiv. 95, 99, 1137, 1180). zwālā-rṻph m. 'he whose form is blazing', a N. of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 346). zwālāyĕ-rṻph m. id. (Śiv. 93, 97, 314).

m. a volcano. zwālamŏkha-rṻph m. 'She whose form is of fire like a volcano', a title of Pārvatī or Durgā (Śiv. 92), cf. zwālā; the form of, or resemblance to, a volcano, i.e. the form taken by her (Siv. 99).

or ziyāda زیادہ adj. and adv. more, additional (cf. dahi warihĕ zᵒ, p. 200b, l. 10) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 497; Rām. 265, 1697); too much, excessive, very (Gr.M.; Śiv. 444, zyād, m.c.); many, much, a great deal (Śiv. 1596).
f. N. of the goddess of misfortune (in Skt. Jyēṣṭhā) (Śiv. 1474).

conj. 3. [The causal of this verb is zōwᵃrun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 175). ¶ Inf. and fut. pass. part. zyonᵘ (Śiv. 342, Rām. 813); sg. instr. zĕnan (Śiv. 991); dat. zĕnas (Śiv. 1384, K. 18); abl. zĕna (Śiv. 659) or zĕni; gen. zĕnukᵘ; pl. nom. zĕnⁱ; f. sg. nom. zë̆ñᵘ̈; pl. zĕñĕ. ¶ Pres. part. zĕwān (Śiv. 928); impers. fut. part. zĕnī; conj. part. zĕth (Gr.Gr. 198, Śiv. 1194, YZ. 311); neg. conj. part. zĕnay; freq. part. zĕ zĕ (Gr.Gr. 105, 198), or zĕth zĕth (Gr.Gr. 105, 198); adverbial part. zĕwöni; n.ag. 1 zĕwawunᵘ (Gr.Gr. 105, 192; Rām. 1587); 2 zĕnawôlᵘ (Gr.Gr. 106, 193). ¶ Fut. (Gr.Gr. 202) sg. 1 zĕma (Rām. 67); 2 zĕkh; 3 zĕyi (L.V. 37, Śiv. 243, Rām. 1597) (to him, zĕyĕs, K. 52): pl. 1 zĕmav; 2 zĕyiv; 3 zĕn (L.V. 47, Śiv. 1373). ¶ Cond. past (Gr.Gr. 253) sg. 1 zĕmahö; 2 zĕhökh; 3 zĕyihē: pl. 1 zĕmahöv; 2 zĕyⁱhīv; 3 zĕhön. ¶ Impve. pres. (Gr.Gr. 247) sg. 2 zĕh; 3 zĕyin (Rām. 1597): pl. 2 zĕyiv; 2 zĕyin. Pol. (Gr.Gr. 249) sg. 2 zĕta; 3 zĕyⁱtan: pl. 2 zĕyⁱtav; 3 zĕyⁱtan. Fut. zĕzi (Gr.Gr. 250); past zĕzihē (Gr.Gr. 251). ¶ 2 Past (Gr.Gr. 229, 236) m.sg. 1 zās (Rām. 1442, K. 63); 2 zākh (Rām. 803); 3 zāv (Śiv. 527, Rām. 83-4) (for me, zām, Śiv. 1110; from her, Rām. 1258): pl. 1 zāy; 2 zāwa; 3 zāy (Rām. 85-6, K. 785-6): f.sg. 1 zāyĕs (Rām. 1586); 2 zāyĕkh (Śiv. 664); 3 zāyĕ (Śiv. 35) (to them, zāyĕkh, K. 78): pl. 1 zāyĕ; 2 zāyĕwa; 3 zāyĕ (K. 785) (to him, zāyĕs, Śiv. 34). ¶ 3 Past (Gr.Gr. 229, 241) m.sg. 1 zāyōs; 2 zāyōkh; 3 zāyōv: pl. 1 zāyēy; 2 zāyēwa; 3 zāyēy: f.sg. 1 zāyēyĕs; 2 zāyēyĕkh; 3 zāyēyĕ (Śiv. 33): pl. 1 zāyēyĕ; 2 zāyēyĕwa; 3 zāyēyĕ. ¶ 4 Past (Gr.Gr. 229, 241) m.sg. 1 zāyās; 2 zāyākh; 3 zāyāv (Rām. 337): pl. 1 zāyāy; 2 zāyāwa; 3 zāyāy (L.V. 51): The fem. is the same as in 3 past. ¶ The perf. part. is (Gr.Gr. 110) m.sg. zāmotᵘ (K. 86, etc.); pl. zāmȧtⁱ: f.sg. zāmüʦᵘ̈ (K. 66); pl. zāmaʦa (K. 357).] ¶ to be born, to come to birth, to come into existence (cf. phāgun zᵒ, p. 685b, l. 22) (El. zyun; Gr.Gr. 26, 110, 167, 175, 198, 229; Gr.M.; L.V. 37, 45, 47, 51; Śiv. 33-5, 243, 432, 527, 659, 664, 928, 990-1, 1000, 1194, 1197, 1340, 1373, 1384, 1424, 1477, 1544, 1584; Rām. 67, 83-5, 337, 598, 629, 633-4, 637, 803, 813, 915, 1109, 1206, 1258, 1264, 1321, 1338, 1347, 1369, 1442, 1464, 1517, 1586, 1597, 1702; K. 18, 37, 41, 47, 52, 63, 78, 539, 624, 734, 785, 950; YZ. 149, 311; K.Pr. 47, 76, 137, 263 read zĕyi); (of seeds or the like) to sprout, to spring up, germinate (cf. drāmun zᵒ, p. 245b, l. 19) (Śiv. 1110, K. 318); (of milk, in the preparation of curds) to crack, to curdle, to turn (El. zyun; cf. zōwarun). --marun -- m. (sg. dat. zĕnas maranas), birth and death (Śiv. 342, 1424); death at the time of birth. ¶ zāmotᵘ (f. zāmüʦᵘ̈), born, come into existence (cf. zūna-pȧchⁱ-zⁱ, p. 1226a, l. 10) (Rām. 28, 115, 145, 351, 424, 428, 493, 665, 760, 1125, 1359, 1470, 1631; K. 66, 86, 357, 550, 751, 764); (of seeds, etc.) sprouted, sprung up, germinated (cf. aḍa-zᵒ, p. 12b, l. 15); (of milk, etc.) curdled (cf. ômᵘ zāmotᵘ dŏd, p. 27a, l. 23). --dŏd -- m. curdled milk, curds (L. 462, zamat). ¶ zĕna-gürᵘ̈ f. the time of birth (used in astrological calculations). -jāy f. a birth place (El. zenajáe).

m. (sg. dat. zinis), wood fuel, firewood (cf. aga-zᵒ, p. 16a, l. 31; bana-zᵒ, p. 109b, l. 1; börᵘ̈-zᵘ̈, p. 118b, l. 32; brana-zᵒ, p. 124a, l. 35; ḍūnⁱ-zⁱ, p. 224a, l. 22; mŏnḍⁱ-zⁱ, p. 574b, l. 34; phal-zᵒ, p. 692a, l. 19; phala-zᵒ, p. 693a, l. 8; phrȧsⁱ-zⁱ, p. 709a, l. 8; pöshⁱ-zⁱ, p. 779b, l. 47; tᵃla-zᵃ, p. 995a, l. 44; wan-zᵒ, p. 1120a, l. 28; vīri-zᵒ, p. 1136a, l. 17) (El. zún; Gr.Gr. 163; Gr.M.; W. 115, ziun; Śiv. 973; K. 280, 1083, 1137; H. ii, 12; xi, 7; xii, 20-2, 24; K.Pr. 41, 155, 159, 164). ¶ zinⁱ-ambār m. a pile, or stack, of firewood (Śiv. 68). -banna f. a stack of firewood. -bôrᵘ m. a load of firewood (as carried about for sale, or the like). -gë̆ḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -gĕjĕ), a tied-up bundle of firewood (Rām. 584). -gĕḍürᵘ̈ f. such a bundle of small size. -gurᵘ m. a horse-load of firewood, so much as would be, or is, carried on a horse (for sale, or the like). -hönzᵘ̈ m. a firewood boatman, a boatman who collects firewood in the forest and transports it by boat for sale (W. 115). -hürᵘ̈ f. a little (two or three chips) of firewood (Śiv. 1085-6, 1138). -köñᵘ̈ f. a little firewood, so much as would be sufficient only for a day or so (cf. köñᵘ̈ 5, p. 461a, l. 21) (Gr.Gr. 163). -laṭürᵘ̈ f. a single stoutish piece of firewood. -lö̆ʦhᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a small tied bundle (about a handful) of small firewood. -mọ̆nḍᵘ m. a log for firewood. -mŏnḍᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a small log, as ab. -mĕnzur m. (sg. dat. -mĕnzaras; f. mĕnzarĕñ, either his wife, or a female firewood-seller), a professional seller of firewood. -tulᵘ m. a small amount of firewood (Gr.Gr. 164). -thôpᵘ m., i.q. -tulᵘ (Gr.Gr. 164). -zanḍ m., i.q. -tulᵘ (Gr.Gr. 163).
f. zīñᵘ̈, 1 p.p. of zēnun, to conquer (cf. sŏrga-zyūnᵘ, p. 934a, l. 33).

(sg. dat. ziris), caraway-seed, cumin-seed (cf. baḍa-zᵒ, p. 82b, l. 40; dā̃-zᵒ, p. 231a, l. 27; kāla-zᵒ, p. 436a, l. 3; phaka-zᵒ, p. 689a, l. 27) (W. 144, K.Pr. 43); flower-pollen (cf. gŏlāb-zᵒ, p. 284b, l. 12). Cf. zīra 2, and L. 67, zirah siyah, red caraway, Carum sp. ¶ zirⁱ-gŏgⁱjⁱ or -gŏgᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. its globular root (cf. L. 76, ziri gogul, a certain diuretic medicinal plant). -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -mŏnjĕ), id. -mushᵉ̆kh m. a whiff of cumin, a very small amount of cumin. ¶ ziri-kiñ f. a very small amount of anything (cf. kāñ 1).

m. (sg. dat. zisis), a hole in the ground, a pit; (esp.) a pit in which grain is concealed (L. 411 zusu, 462 zús). zisⁱ-ʦö̃gijⁱ f. a mat (for sitting on) over a pit, a seat, as a trap, over a pit (so that the sitter is at once precipitated into it).

adj. (f. ziṭhᵘ̈ or (H. xii, 6) zë̆ṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat. zichĕ), elder (by birth), senior (cf. garba-zᵒ, p. 300a, l. 8; zarma-zᵒ, p. 1232b, l. 15) (El. zúṭh; Gr.Gr. 58, declined; Gr.M.; Rām. 629, 1736; K. 1012; H. xii, 6); an elder, a chief, principal (El. zyúṭ; K. 466, 919; H. v, 1); superior in rank, taking precedence (K. 904); (as subst. m.) a magistrate (El. zyút). El. confounds this word with zyūṭhᵘ, q.v. --bôyᵘ -- m. the eldest brother in a family of brothers and sisters (Rām. 330, z˚ barādar; --bôyᵘ, 336, 456). --hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. ziṭhᵘ̈ hishᵘ̈), the elder (among others), the oldest (Rām, 699, 859; H. viii, 5). --karun -- m.inf. to superannuate (El. zyút k˚). --pahān -- adj. (f. ziṭhᵘ̈ pahān), a little older (than the others), somewhat senior. ¶ ziṭh ʦāṭh m. (sg. dat. --ʦāṭas --), the head, or senior, boy of a school or class. ¶ ziṭhi-paksh adj. c.g. belonging to the elder branch (of a family, or the like). ¶ ziṭhᵘ̈ bĕñĕ f. an elder sister, the eldest sister in a family of brothers and sisters.

adj. (f. zīṭhᵘ̈, sg. dat. zēchĕ), long (in time or space), lengthy, tall (cf. atha-zᵒ, p. 65b, l. 6; āyĕ-zᵒ, p. 73a, l. 29; buthi-zᵒ, p. 143b, l. 24; dāri-zᵒ, p. 238a, l. 32; hĕnga-zᵒ, p. 339b, l. 2; khōra-zᵒ, p. 410b, l. 19; lā̃ga-zᵒ, p. 511b, l. 14; lȧṭⁱ-zⁱ, p. 535b, l. 49; nala-zᵒ, p. 632a, l. 37; nȧri-zᵒ, p. 649a, l. 36; narĕ-zᵒ, p. 650a, l. 17; pȧdⁱ-zⁱ, p. 681b, l. 38; phala-zᵒ, p. 692b, l. 31, and p. 693a, l. 10; rāda-zᵒ, p. 825a, l. 29; wumarĕ-zᵒ, p. 1119a, l. 27; zanga-zᵒ, p. 1226b, l. 29; zĕwa-zᵒ, p. 1236a, l. 6) (El. zyúṭ, zyúṭh, zúṭh; Gr.Gr. 19, 75; Gr.M.; Śiv. 842, 847, 912; Rām. 600, 1489; K. 926; K.Pr. 76, 143, 159, 219, 257, 262); (of a room, area, or the like) long, spacious (Gr.M.; Śiv. 1084, 1733). El. confounds this word with zyuṭhᵘ, q.v. --karun -- m.inf. to make long, make longer, extend, draw out (El. zúṭh k˚, W. 88). ¶ zēṭhi-zyūṭhᵘ adj. (f. -zīṭhᵘ̈), very long, extra long, too long. ¶ zīṭhⁱ atha dārȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. to stretch out the arms (H. vii, 25).

m. (sg. dat. zitis), sudden, or unexpected, gain; gaining or getting possession of something looked upon as unobtainable (e.g. accidentally finding hidden treasure). ¶ zitⁱ-onⁱ adj. (f. -üñᵘ̈), (even though possessing sight) one who acts as if he were blind, one who pretends blindness. -añĕr m. sham, or pretended, total blindness (whether one is merely dim-sighted or can see well).

card. (sg. obl. dŏyĕ or dŏyi; pl. dat. dŏn, abl. dŏyau), two (cf. atha-zᵃh, p. 65a, l. 36; khōr-zᵃh, p. 410a, l. 33) (Gr.Gr. 76, 81; El. záh, zih; Gr.M.; W. 101, 105, zạ, zạh; L.V. 75; Śiv. 1285, 1663, 1756; dŏyĕ, 513, 933, 1405; dŏn, 169, 500, 1370, 1621; Rām. 14, 138, 460, 530, 631, etc.; dŏn, 18, 138, 160, 279, 280, 646, etc.; dŏyau 1380; K. 166, 170, 550, 555, 819, 1026, 1145; dŏyĕ, 136, 309, 1003; dŏyi, 27, 864; dŏyĕv for dŏyau, 171; H. v, 3-5, 8-10; viii, 1, 3-5, 8, 11-13; x, 1, 4; xii, 1, 3; dŏyi, viii, 7; dŏn, viii, 1, 4, 6, 11; x, 11; xii, 11, 14, 15, 19; dŏyau, iii, 1; v, 7; viii, 2, 3, 5; x, 5). ¶ In the sg., with a sg. noun, this word means 'two', as in the pl. (cf. dŏyi rĕti, after two months, K. 864; dŏyi kāmi, (one) out of two actions, K. 1003; and bel.). ¶ dŏn-hondᵘ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, two (Rām. 1781); costing two (rupees, etc.). dŏn-judöyⁱ f. separation of a pair (e.g. the death, or absence on a journey, of one of a married couple). dŏn ta trĕn manz gaʦhun m.inf. 'to go into two and three', hence, to be at one's wits' end, to fall into a dilemma, not to know which way to turn (so dŏn- trĕn andar gaʦhun, Śiv. 779). ¶ dŏnⁱ-hondⁱ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, only two. ¶ dŏyĕ (or dŏyi) atha ʦürᵘ̈ wazüñᵘ̈  f.inf. to clap with both hands, a quarrel or fight for which both sides are responsible, i.e. in which one is as bad as the other. --kunuy -- m. a single action with two results, i.q. our 'killing two birds with one stone'. --phiri -- adv. on two occasions, twice. --ranga -- adv. in two ways, in two different manners (Gr.Gr. 154). --wakta -- adv. at two times, on two occasions, twice. --wati -- adv. by two roads, i.e. for two reasons, on two accounts. --vizi -- adv. at two times, twice. ¶ zᵃy card. only two (Gr.Gr. 81, Rām. 1384); exactly two, a complete two (Śiv. 1333); the two (Śiv. 198).

f. a certain tiny longish insect, similar to an ant, which by contact with the skin causes irritation and scratching (cf. zᵃlun). --lāgun -- m.inf. contemptuously to abuse or refer to the minuteness of a transaction (such as making or receiving a gift, or buying or selling); met. to put a tax on people.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. zᵃjᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. zᵃjᵃrun, q.v. zᵃjᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. zᵃjᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), harassed, as ab.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. zᵃjᵃrᵃ), to pare, scrape; to harass by frequent annoyance or distressing (quasi, by skinning a person alive). Cf. zᵃlun.
(cf. زک) f. defeat, humiliation; (in Ksh.) revenge (El. zak, m.). zᵃka raṭüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to keep up a private grudge, to maintain inward resentment.
f.pl. two khār or ass's loads (cf. khār zᵃkhörᵃ, p. 408a, l. 46).

m. scratching (with the finger-nails) (cf. atha-zᵒ, p. 65a, l. 37; hŏkha-zᵒ, p. 327a, l. 47); the act of paring, scraping (Gr.Gr. 124). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to scratch (another) (with the nails or the like) (H. xii, 17). ¶ zᵃla-bọ̆kᵃ m. unintentional or accidental scratching (oneself or another) with all the nails of one hand (cf. bọ̆kᵘ) (K.Pr. 54 zulahbuk). -ponzᵘ m. a scratch made by all the five nails of one hand (cf. ponzᵘ 2). -wāl adj. c.g. one who is needlessly persistent in doing to no profit any work (such as buying, selling, giving, or receiving). -wölī f. needless persistence as above. -wālay f. the being needlessly persistent as ab.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. zᵒlᵒ f. zᵘ̈jᵘ̈; 2 p.p. zᵃjyōv), to pare, shave, scrape off the surface (cf. ṭinḍa zᵒ, p. 1009b, l. 12) (El. zilun, zulun; Gr.Gr. 124; Gr.M.); to peel, skin (cf. ala zᵒ, p. 22b, l. 45) (K.Pr. 78, neg. conj. part. written zulahnai); to scratch (with the nails); to cut (a pen) or sharpen (a pencil) (Gr.M.); cf. zᵃjᵃrun. zᵒlᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. zᵘ̈jᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), pared; skinned; scratched.
in zᵃnāra ʦhunun m.inf. to offer oneself as a sacrifice (on behalf of some one), to show absolute self-sacrifice (for some one).

m. (esp. in response to encouragement given by another) determination, perseverance, zeal, ardour. --tulith nyunᵘ -- m.inf. to become encouraged or determined in a course of evil conduct, by observing the forbearance of the person (e.g. a master) affected by it.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. zᵃrowᵃ), to bear, endure, show forbearance (to bad conduct of a servant or the like) (W. 156, zur˚; K. 200, 202, 479, 540, 542, 662, 1051; K.Pr. 239); cf. zarun. zᵃrowᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. zᵃrüvᵃ-müʦᵃ), one to whom, or an act to which, forbearance is shown as ab., borne with.
card. (pl. dat. zᵃtôwuhan), twenty-two (Gr.Gr. 77; El. zatáwuh, zatówuh, zitáwuh).
m. a ray of light (e.g. of the sun), a gleam, shine (e.g. of a jewel or the like) (El. zitsah, ziza; Śiv. 836; K. (fem.) 926, 936, 985, 1047). Cf. zĕta, zitiñ.

The nineteenth consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet in the Roman character, the eleventh when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character, and the ninth when written in the Perso-Arabic character. The Kāshmīrī name for the character, as well as for (ca), is ʦāṭuv ʦö. It has approximately the sound of ts in the English word 'catsup', but is more dental. The aspirate of ʦa is ʦha چھہ, called in Kāshmīrī ʦŏṭiñ ʦhö, the twelfth consonant of the Kāshmīrī alphabet when written in the Śāradā or Nāgarī character. The sound is approximately that of tsh in the English words 'cat's head', not that of 'cat-shark', but is more dental. ¶ In some books printed in the Persian character, the letters ژ and ژہ, instead of چھ and چھہ, respectively, are used to represent these sounds. ¶ Regarding the relationship existing between c, ch, and ʦ, ʦh, respectively, see Art. c, p. 156a, ll. 9 ff. To this may be added that it is difficult to formulate any general rule according to which, in Kāshmīrī, an original c, ch, remains as c, ch, or becomes ʦ, ʦh. As a very rough rule, it may be said that, in the case of words borrowed directly from other languages, such as Persian or Sanskrit, an original c, ch, is preserved unchanged, but that when the word becomes thoroughly incorporated into the language, it tends to become ʦ. It thus happens that there are several words in an intermediate stage of adoption, in which both sounds are used at option in the same word. An example of this is the Persian word camca, a spoon, which becomes both cō̃ca and ʦō̃ca in Kāshmīrī. As a rule, however, in most words borrowed from Persian the c is preserved unchanged. As regards words borrowed from Sanskrit, the case is different, an original c being in many instances changed to ʦ. Thus, Skt. canḍī > Ksh. ʦanḍī, N.P.; candra- > ʦạndᵃr, the moon; candana- > ʦandan, sandalwood; caraṇa- > ʦaran, a foot; cit > ʦĕth, the mind; carâcara- > ʦarāʦar, the whole creation; ācamana- > āʦaman, sipping; ācāra- > āʦār, behaviour; gōcara- > gōʦar, range; kāca- > kāʦh, glass; mucukunda- > muʦukund, N.P. On the other hand, Skt. chatra- > Ksh. both chạthᵃr and ʦhạthᵃr, an umbrella; and chala- > both chal and ʦhal, deceit. Similarly, in pure Ksh. words, we have both chapun and ʦhapun, to be hidden; chörᵘ̈ and ʦhörᵘ̈, hurry; cīrⁱ and ʦyūrᵘ (for ʦīrᵘ), a certain plant, and other such pairs. ¶ The letters ʦ and ʦh are often of secondary origin. When a dental t or th (not the cerebral ṭ, ṭh) is followed by ü-mātrā, it becomes ʦ or ʦh, respectively. Thus, the base of rāth, night, is rāt-, and this becomes röʦᵘ̈ in the Nominative Plural; the √kat-, spin, forms its 1 p.p. kotᵘ, with a feminine küʦᵘ̈; the Nominative Plural of kŏth, a hank, is kö̆ʦhᵘ̈; and the √wŏth-, rises, has its 1 p.p. wọ̆thᵘ, fem. wö̆ʦhᵘ̈. Again, when these letters are followed by ĕ (i.e. ya) or by y, they also become ʦ and ʦh, respectively, and at the same time ĕ becomes a, and y is dropped. Thus, the adjective totᵘ, hot, has for its base tat-. The abstract noun is formed by adding ĕr (i.e. yar) to the base, and is therefore taʦar, heat, with ĕ becoming a; the 2 p.p. of √wŏth- is formed by adding yōv, so that it is wŏʦhōv, with drooping of the y. For further particulars, see Gr.Gr. 18 ff., and Gr.M. p. 22.
(? ʦhã̄) m. according to El. (s.v. tsáṅ) this word means 'salt' (which is imported into Kashmīr from Ladakh and the Panjāb). The word is a corruption of the Ladakhī Tibetan tsha.
m. the upright post on the top of which swings a well-lever (cf. tōla-ʦᵒ, p. 999b, l. 27).
in ʦaḍa-wôrᵘ m. an earthenware vessel for milk or the like, the same as ʦoḍᵘ, q.v., but smaller in size (Śiv. 1368, 1502).
f. need, requirement, necessity. --ʦalüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. need to depart, competent provision to be secured, means for carrying out to become available.

f. a fringed woollen shawl, mantle, sheet (worn over the shoulders and back and reaching low) (cf. bŏṭa-ʦᵒ, p. 128b, l. 26; kapar-ʦᵒ, p. 463b, l. 42; pā̃-ʦᵒ, p. 748a, l. 29; pȧṭⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 789b, l. 33; rugölⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 828b, l. 21; sᵃtᵃra-ʦᵃ, p. 947b, l. 27) (El. also, a veil; K.Pr. 126). --gilavüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to flourish the shawl', (of some invisible power) to grant suddenly or unexpectedly a favour (esp. suddenly and unexpectedly curing the sickness of an invalid). ¶ ʦādari-baṭa m. a Brāhmaṇ or Paṇḍit who (even though placed in high authority) habitually wears only a woollen shawl (i.e. who is of a modest, unostentatious character). -jōr m. a pair of shawls joined together, a double shawl (cf. jōr 1). -püṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -pacĕ), a narrow shawl (made of a single width of cloth). -shikhurᵘ m. (sg. dat. -shikharas), a rag of a shawl, a dirty piece of an old worn out shawl. -züṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -zacĕ), a worn out ragged dirty old shawl. ¶ El. also gives tsádir-wádir (ʦādᵃr-wādᵃr), m. a shawl.
m. (sg. dat. ʦã̄ganas), N. of a certain medicinal fruit. ʦã̄gan-kulᵘ m. the tree on which it grows.
in ʦȧhⁱ ta ʦatajihi adv. very slowly, with difficulty and delay (u.w. vbs. of producing or the like).
or ʦöl m. a garment (borrowed from Skt.) in the word kŏ-ʦail (Śiv. 750), p. 494a, l. 9, q.v.

m. (sg. dat. ʦaitanĕs), consciousness, feeling, sensation (Śiv. 194, 1525); (in Śaiva mysticism) the Supreme Consciousness, the Supreme Experiencing Principle, a N. of the Supreme (L.V. 16; Śiv. 1043, 1406, 1415, 1515, 1545, 1548).

obl. form of ʦakh 1 and 2. Also used in the following:-- ʦaka-lār f. speedy running (after a person), speedy pursuit. -pal m. i.q. ʦŏka-pal, s.v. ʦọ̆kᵘ, q.v. -tahörᵘ̈ f. a funeral feast. -ʦürᵘ̈ f. a very industrious woman (quasi, as busy as a sparrow, see ʦürᵘ̈ 4).

m. N. of an alluvial plateau below Vijᵃbrôrᵃ, q.v. where there was once a famous temple dedicated to Viṣṇu Cakradhara (RT.Tr. II, 461); a wielder of a discus (cf. ʦakhᵃr); hence, a N. of Vishnu (Viṣṇu) (cf. Śiv. 710) or (Śiv. 1161) Shiv (Śiva).
adj. c.g. wheel-shaped, circular and flat. Cf. ʦakᵘ̈jᵘ̈ and ʦakul.
or ʦākav m. a certain bird, the ruddy sheldrake or Casarca rutila (L. 128 tsakáo).

m. (sg. dat. ʦakas), a round clod of earth with grass, etc., growing on it, a round lump of turf (suitable for building an embankment), peat (cf. ḍēmba-ʦᵒ, p. 217b, l. 38; hili-ʦᵒ, p. 331a, l. 10) (L. 62, Rām. 42). ʦaka-nāv f. a barge for carrying peat or vegetable manure gathered from the Ḍal lake (K.Pr. 66).

m. (sg. dat. ʦākas), a group of four, a four, a double pair (cf. dūra-ʦᵒ, p. 239a, l. 4) (Gr.Gr. 83); used as a multiplicative, as in trih ʦākh bāh, three fours (are) twelve (cf. Gr.Gr. 86, W. 104); cf. ʦula. --pĕnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. loving longing to befall a person, or to be experienced. ¶ ʦāka-wörᵘ̈ f. a state barge with rowers seated before and behind the raised canopy for the passenger (El. tsákawár, m.; Śiv. 1363). Cf. contra, ʦhaṭa-wörᵘ̈, p. 1062a, l. 26. ¶ ʦākhāh khanḍā m. a group of a little less than four, about four, four or so (Gr.Gr. 83).
m. (sg. dat. ʦakas), the revolving bar of an oil-press to which the bullock's neck is attached (cf. tīla-wã̄-ʦᵒ, p. 999a, l. 30).

f. (sg. dat. ʦakhi), rage, passion, anger (cf. potᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 788a, l. 43) (El. tsak; Gr.M.; Śiv. 203, 1462; K. 139, 847, 908; H. vii, 2; YZ. 405). --anüñᵘ̈ --, f.inf. to bring anger (to a person), to cause anger to be felt (by, dat.), to provoke, anger, enrage (Rām. 460). --khasüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. anger to rise (to, dat.), anger to be felt (by, dat.) (El.; Rām. 309, 473, 785, 865, 917, 1377, 1453; K. 443). --karüñᵘ̈ --, f.inf. to be in, or fly into, a passion (Gr.M., K. 359). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. anger to come (to, dat.), anger to be felt (by, dat.), to be provoked (subject, dat.) (El.; Rām. 532, 551; K. 325, 441, 680; K.Pr. 115). ¶ ʦakhi gaʦhun m.inf. to go into anger, to become angry (K. 40, 163, 192, 233); -hotᵘ adj. (f. -hüʦᵘ̈), smitten by wrath, full of rage (H. vii, 14).
m. a piece of dried plaster (that has fallen off a wall on drying).

or (q.v.) ʦakr m. (sg. dat. ʦakras), a wheel; a circle; a discus (the missile) (cf. ʦakadar) (Śiv. 710; Rām. 224; K. 59, 872, 881-2, 884, 1059); a circle of individuals, a group of individuals (L.V. 63); a wide extent of country extending from sea to sea; (in astrology) a particular part of a person's fate (e.g. lönⁱ-ʦⁱ, the part of a woman's fate concerned with her marriage) (Rām. 421); (in mystic Śaivism) one of the seven circles or convolutions (Skt. cakra) along the spinal cord (Skt. suṣumnā) (see L.V. pp. 12 ff.) (Śiv. 1891). ¶ ʦakras phērun m.inf. to walk in a circle (e.g. round someone or something) (Śiv. 1221).
f. a feigned cough (e.g. to warn a thief, or to awake a sleeper) (Gr.Gr. 33, 37). Cf. ʦās.
f. anger (esp. that of a child or of a subordinate). --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to vent such anger (on someone).
f. a potter's wheel. Cf. ʦakᵘtᵒdjᵘtᵒd.
or (q.v.) ʦakhᵃr m. a circle (a corruption of Skt. cakra), used in the compound shailā-ʦakr, p. 880a, l. 38, q.v. See ʦakhᵃr for other uses.
m. the shape of a discus, a mark resembling a discus (K. 397); as adj. c.g. wheel-shaped. See ʦakhᵃr.

adj. c.g. (sg. dat. ʦakrawartas), (as an epithet of a king) ruling a wide tract of country (extending from sea to sea, cf. ʦakhᵃr), ruling as a universal monarch, ruling as an emperor (Rām. 1280; K. 5, ˚wart).
m. 'Lord of the discus' (cf. ʦakhᵃr), a N. of Vishnu (Viṣṇu) (cf. Śiv. 710); a N. of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 1179, 1221, 1508).

or ʦakulᵘ m. (sg. dat. ʦakalas, Gr.Gr. 58), a flat circular piece (of something), a disc (cf. dāla-ʦᵒ, p. 210b, l. 24; gŏgᵃji-ʦᵃ, p. 279a, l. 18; muji-ʦᵒ, p. 558b, l. 12; nadȧrⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 623a, l. 47; rāma-ʦᵒ, p. 833b, l. 25; shömⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 882b, l. 48; ʦāmañĕ-ʦᵒ, p. 1072b, l. 32) (Gr.Gr. 35); a flat piece of land (cf. drāman-ʦᵒ, p. 245b, l. 38). Cf. ʦakᵘ̈jᵘ̈ and ʦakajal.

m. (sg. dat. ʦākatas), circumambulation, going round, circuit; going round (someone or something) (keeping him or it on the right, as a token of reverence). --lagun -- m.inf. (instead of going by the direct route) to have to go a long way round.

or ʦaküjᵘ̈ f. (f. of ʦakul, q.v., Gr.Gr. 35), a single wheel of a wheeled vehicle or machine (cf. ratha-ʦᵒ, p. 847a, l. 18; yẹ̆ndra-ʦᵒ, s.v. yẹ̆ndᵃr); a circular, flat, revolving object, such as a millstone or a potter's wheel (cf. graṭa-ʦᵒ, p. 305a, l. 1; krāla-ʦᵒ, p. 470b, l. 25; and ʦạkhᵘ̈rᵘ̈) (K.Pr. 18); a single buttock, a hip (El. tsakij; K.Pr. 38, 235); cf. ʦakajal and ʦakul. ʦakᵃjĕ-horᵃ m. a pair of buttocks, the buttocks, the hips.

f. the handle for moving the large wheel of a spinning-wheel (cf. yẹ̆ndra-ʦᵒ, s.v. yẹ̆ndᵃr) (El. tsakar m.; K.Pr. 131); sexual intercourse (of man or of beast) (esp. when violent). ¶ ʦạkᵃra-mã̄ḍay f. stirring up mud at the bottom of clear water; met. to sully virtuous qualities by sinful conduct. ¶ ʦạkᵃri-madun m. one habitually addicted to venery, a libertine.
adj. c.g. (of dish, bowl, or the like) possessing a circular, or ring, base.

f. (sg. dat. ʦāli), the palm of the hand stretched out and hollowed (cf. atha-ʦᵒ, p. 64a, l. 16; yë̆ḍᵘ̈-ʦᵘ̈, s.v. yĕḍ); the amount contained in such a palm, a handful of this nature (cf. ȧshⁱ-ʦāla, p. 48a, l. 1; nūna-ʦāl, p. 641a, l. 26; pã̄-ʦāl, p. 748a, l. 33) (Śiv. 662, 702, 1250, 1255, 1688; Rām. 1039).
f., in pötra-ʦāl (p. 804a, l. 29, and Rām. 612) and in yë̆ḍᵘ̈-ʦāl, a form of indigestion, s.v. yĕḍ, qq.v.

(cf. ʦalun) in ʦala-lār m. (lit.) running in flight (from someone); hence (in reading or the like) hastily running (through the matter), galloping through (a book, a recitation, or the like). -ʦitta sg. voc. O restless mind! (L.V. 72).

adv. a particle used to emphasize a prohibitive negative. Thus ma gaʦh, do not go, but ʦala ma gaʦh, do not go on any account; so ʦala ma kar, do not do (it) at all. --bā -- adv. id., but used in addressing a male person of equal rank. --biñ -- adv. id., but used in addressing a female of equal, or superior, rank. --sö -- adv. id., but used in addressing an elder male, or a male of superior rank.

f. (sg. dat. ʦālüñᵘ̈), a small shovel, or spoon-like instrument, used for stirring up a fire (El. used in a kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈, or portable brazier; K.Pr. 129); anything of a similar shape (cf. pamba-ʦᵒ, p. 733b, l. 37).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦalanôwᵘ. This verb is one of the causals of ʦalun. The other is ʦạlᵃrāwun, q.v., see Gr.Gr. 174), to cause to run away, to put to flight (Rām. 867, K. 999).
n.ag. (f. ʦālavüñᵘ̈), one who bears, one who endures (Śiv. 1254).

conj. 2 (1 p.p. ʦolᵘ, f. (L.V. 33) ʦüjᵘ̈. The causal of this verb is ʦalanāwun or ʦạlᵃrāwun, qq.v., Gr.Gr. 174), to run away, to flee, abscond, to escape (cf. hĕth ʦᵒ, p. 366b, l. 41; pānas ʦᵒ, p. 736a, l. 47; path ʦᵒ, p. 792b, l. 3; shāl ʦalith, etc., p. 879b, l. 40) (El.; Gr.Gr. 5, 28, 108, 194, 205, 209; Gr.M.; L.V. 28, 31, 33, 75, 86; Śiv. 279, 1064, 1539, 1663; Rām. 33, 92, 172, 375, 498, 529, 913, 1198, 1207, 1257, 1329, 1717; K. 138, 151, 239, 242, 468, 559-630 passim, 658, 661, 691, 761, 823, 825, 882, 999; H. ii, 7-9; v, 6; vi, 8; viii, 4, 11, 13; ix, 1, 4; xii, 25; K.Pr. 147, 154, 173, 239); to depart, go away, disappear (cf. bŏcha ʦalüñᵘ̈, p. 80a, l. 18; bōm ʦalun, p. 107a, l. 40; dŏd ʦᵒ, p. 188a, l. 44; shē̃kh ʦᵒ, p. 876b, l. 46; sankaṭh ʦᵒ, p. 922a, l. 44; thakun ʦᵒ, p. 974a, l. 1; ʦaḍ ʦalüñᵘ̈, p. 1054a, l. 7; ʦrṻṭh ʦᵒ) (Śiv. 165, 287, 424, 585, 661, 794, 804, 871, 922, 930, 962, 1112, 1118, 1153, 1162, 1239, 1241, 1283, 1463, 1571, 1627, 1632, 1775, 1813, 1844, 1848, 1895; Rām. 10, 23, 31, 60, 98, 114, 124-6, 302, 387, 461, 674, 678, 901, 994, 1008, 1065, 1080, 1085, 1088, 1110, 1126, 1173, 1177, 1192, 1264, 1321, 1361, 1364, 1398, 1461, 1492, 1494, 1559, 1572, 1641, 1703, 1782; K. 174, 413, 464, 696; YZ. 31, 402; K.Pr. 17, 60, 62, 160, 187); to go away (from), depart (from), abandon (obj. in abl.) (Rām. 27, 838-9, 965, 1031, 1121; K. 202, 513; YZ. 28, 141, 273, 519-20, 525); to go, proceed, move along, be in motion (Rām. 889-90, K. 375); to disappear, be worn away (cf. nam ʦalȧnⁱ, p. 635b, l. 30); to come away, be removed (suddenly) (cf. nüʦᵘ̈ ʦalüñᵘ̈, p. 663b, l. 11; ʦokᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 1067a, l. 47); (of some evacuation) to run out quickly, be suddenly discharged (cf. dāl ʦalüñᵘ̈, p. 210a, l. 25; dasth ʦalȧnⁱ, p. 256a, l. 48; dāth ʦalun, p. 257b, l. 21; yĕḍ ʦalüñᵘ̈, s.v. yĕḍ); to depart, go suddenly, be suddenly accomplished (cf. nȧmⁱ ʦalun, p. 636a, l. 27; rakañ or rikiñ ʦalüñᵘ̈, p. 832a, ll. 38, 49). ¶ hĕth ʦalun to take and run off, to carry off, elope with (K. 653); to take away (YZ. 17, 33, 508). nīriṭh ʦalun (words, etc.) to emerge and become suddenly uttered (p. 721b, l. 2) (Śiv. 1187, K. 239, YZ. 465). trövith ʦalun, to abandon (YZ. 151). ¶ ʦolᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦüjᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), fled, departed, etc., as ab. (Gr.Gr. 109, K. 468). ¶ ʦalan-shāy f. a place of refuge, asylum (El.). -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), an absconder, a (military) deserter (El.). ¶ ʦalān gaʦhun m.inf. to go along, proceed (cf. ʦalith gᵒ, bel.) (Rām. 403). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come hurriedly, to flee home (cf. ʦalith yᵒ, bel.) (Rām. 1184). ¶ ʦalith gaʦhun m.inf. to run away (to a distance), abscond (Rām. 336, 1089, 1112, 1379, 1551, 1725); cf. ʦalān gᵒ, ab. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. having absconded to come, to arrive as an absconder (from somewhere else) (Rām. 339, 1369). Cf. ʦalān yᵒ, ab. ¶ This verb is sometimes used impersonally, as in dushmanan ʦolᵘ, by the enemies it was fled, i.e. the enemies fled (Gr.M.).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦôlᵘ, f. ʦöjᵘ̈; 2 p.p. ʦājyōv), to bear, endure (cf. atha ʦᵒ, p. 64a, l. 20) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 271, 419, 824, 1247, 1253, 1446, 1758; Rām. 196, 203, 218, 291, 617, 643, 1027, 1289, 1386, 1570, 1575, 1581, 1711; YZ. 60, 346; K.Pr. 239, 241). ¶ ʦālan-bāna m. the habit, or nature, of endurance, endurance, patience, long-suffering. -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who bears or endures, resigned, long-suffering, unruffled by nature, imperturbable.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦạlᵃrôwᵃ. This verb, like ʦalanāwun, is a causal of ʦalun, see Gr.Gr. 174) to cause to run away, to put to flight (K. 1023).

f. skin, hide, bark, rind (of man, beast, tree, fruit, or the like) (cf. hāpath-ʦᵒ, p. 342b, l. 47; khar-ʦᵒ, p. 407a, l. 38; nuñᵘ̈ ʦᵒ, p. 641a, l. 47; potᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 788a, l. 45; shĕza-ʦᵒ, p. 903b, l. 13; samūr-ʦ, p. 914a, l. 45; sōra-ʦᵒ, p. 931a, l. 23) (El.; Gr.Gr. 148; W. 111 ʦo˙m; Śiv. 166, 816, 894; Rām. 635; K.Pr. 217); according to El. the word also means 'volume'; cf. ʦarmun. --mã̄ḍi yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the skin to be kneaded (p. 548b, l. 40), i.e. to become hardened, or toughened, by practice; hence, genl. to become hardened to heavy labour by continued practice. --phalüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. the skin to become worn away (phalun 2) (esp. by helping to carry a heavy load or the like). ¶ ʦama-dȧjⁱ (or -düjᵘ̈) f. (out of friendship or the like) telling or recounting a person's good qualities even when he is patently committing a fault; pretending a virtue when one has it not (cf. gāna-ʦamadüjᵘ̈, p. 288a, l. 25); -ḍanḍ m. bodily help, i.e. help given by a friend with some part of his body (such as his hands, feet, or back); -dorᵘ adj. (f. -dürᵘ̈) (of anything animate or inanimate) hard-skinned, tough-skinned, hard-barked. -ʦürᵘ̈ f. 'a skin-sparrow', i.e. a bat. ¶ ʦami āsun m.inf. 'to remain on the skin', i.e. the responsibility of carrying out (some duty) to lie (upon someone).
m. something possessing a skin or bark; hence, the felled trunk of a tree from which the branches have been lopped (esp. when still retaining its bark).
adj. c.g. possessing a skin, as in nūna-ʦᵒ, p. 641a, l. 28; esp. hard-skinned, tough-skinned.

f. (sg. dat. ʦāmüñᵘ̈), cheese (El. m., Gr.M. f.). ¶ ʦāmañĕ-(or ʦāmüñᵘ̈-)mŏ̈nḍᵘ̈  f. a ball of cheese, an entire cheese, a cake of cheese (Gr.Gr. 75). -ṭīrᵘ̈ f. a large mass of curds before making into cheese. -ʦakul m. (sg. dat. -ʦakalas), a circular piece of cheese (prepared as a relish).
in ʦamar-gāv f. the Yak (Bos grunniens) (highly valued for its bushy tail, used as a fly-whisk); ʦamar-wôlᵘ m. a maker of fly-whisks (see ʦāmar).
m. the tail of the Bos grunniens (used over a god or a great person as a ceremonial fly-whisk) (L.V. 73; Śiv. 1175, 1515; K. 932, 985, 1132, 1151). See ʦamar.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦamaṭhyōv) (of something naturally juicy) to dry up, wither (cf. ʦamun) (El. to wither, decay). ʦamaṭhyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦamaṭhyē-müʦᵘ̈), dried up, withered, as ab.
m. admiration, surprise; a show, spectacle, wonderful object (Śiv. 1777).

perf. part. of aʦun, q.v. (f. ʦāmüʦᵘ̈), entered (lit. and met.) (cf. brēshĕs aʦun and brēshĕn ʦāmüʦᵘ̈, p. 126b, ll. 40, 36; mã̄ḍi aʦun and mã̄ḍi ʦāmotᵘ, p. 548b, ll. 33, 37; pȧtⁱ aʦun, and pȧtⁱ ʦāmotᵘ, p. 789a, ll. 8, 41; path aʦun, p. 791b, l. 28, and path ʦāmotᵘ, p. 792b, l. 5) (Gr.Gr. 110; Rām. 652, 686).
or (q.v.) ʦã̄ph m. (sg. dat. ʦampi), persuasion, cajolery, blandishment, inducement (to another to do something). Cf. ʦã̄ph.

conj. 2 (1 p.p. ʦomᵘ), and conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦamyōv. The causal of this verb is ʦọ̆mᵃrāwun, q.v.) (of some liquid or juice in a green plant) to be reduced in amount (by drying, evaporation, boiling down, or the like) (cf. ras-mas ʦᵒ, p. 844a, l. 3); (of advice or the like) to be agreed to, adopted. Cf. ʦamaṭhun. ¶ ʦomᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦümᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), reduced (by cooking, evaporation, etc.), as ab. ¶ ʦamith gaʦhun m.inf. to become abashed or ashamed (owing to being tongue-tied); to be disgraced (in the eyes of respectable people by the circulation of evil reports). ¶ ʦamyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦamyē-müʦᵘ̈), become reduced, as ab.; (of advice or the like) agreed to, adopted.
m. (his wife is ʦamarĕñ or ʦamᵃr-bāy), a worker in leather, currier, shoemaker, cobbler, harness-maker (El. tsamar, tsomor; Gr.Gr. 148; W. 111 ʦo˙mūr). -bāy f. his wife.
f. the odour of a cowhouse (arising from the mixture of fodder, cowdung, and urine). --wŏthüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such an odour to arise.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦānanôwᵘ), i.q. ʦānun, q.v., to cause to enter (Śiv. 126).
m. a garment (noted only in YZ. 234, 541). Cf. canda, a pocket.
in wȧnⁱwȧnⁱ ʦandan, s.v. wanun 1, q.v.
f. 'The Furious', a N. of Durgā, the wife, or energic form, of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 1515); a hasty, impetuous woman (L.V. 77).
f. (sg. dat. ʦȧnḍiki), a meeting, assembly (esp. of gamblers or similar reprobates).
or ʦāndrāyĕn in ʦạndrāyĕn ʦāpun m.inf. to keep a certain very severe fast for an entire lunar month. It is called in Skt. cāndrâyaṇa, which appears as ʦāndrāyĕn ʦāpun in Śiv. 595.

m. (sg. dat. ʦandanas), sandal-wood (cf. rakh-ʦᵒ, p. 830b, l. 15; rakta-ʦᵒ, p. 831b, l. 34) (El.; L. 78 tsandum, probably a misprint; L.V. 42; Śiv. 973, 1080, 1155, 1613, 1902; Rām. 692, 739, 1080; K. 425-6, 528, 926, 976; K.Pr. 159, 229). ¶ ʦandan-bura m. the bark of the sandal tree (cf. bura 2); a powder made from a bark-like strip of sandal-wood (cf. bura 1). -dār adj. c.g. bearing sandal-wood, i.e. sprinkled, or covered, with sandal-wood (YZ. 57, of a bed). -hār m. a kind of necklace of three, five, or seven strands (the candra-hār of India, of which name this word is a corruption) (L. 262 chandanhár). -köjᵘ̈ f. a flat stone on which sandal-wood is ground to powder. -kwöjᵘ̈ f., id. -küñᵘ̈ f., id. -mỗkun m. a small lump of sandal-wood used for being reduced to powder on a grinding stone.
(El. ts˚), a common misspelling for ʦhāḍun, q.v.

or ʦandᵃr m. (sg. dat. ʦạ(a)ndras ), the moon (cf. bāla-ʦᵒ, p. 104a, l. 42; phal-ʦᵒ, p. 692a, l. 18; punimᵘ̈-ʦᵘ̈, p. 741a, l. 40; yẹ̆ndᵃr ta ʦᵒ naʦun, s.v. yẹ̆ndᵃr) (El. tsandar, the new moon, crescent-shaped moon; L.V. 9, 22, 109; Rām. 406, 575, 1484, 1486, 1774; YZ. 34; K.Pr. 253); a moon-shaped ornament worn on the head (used esp. by children). ¶ ʦạndra-grohun m. (sg. dat. -grahanas), an eclipse of the moon. -hāl m. a kind of paddy with a soft white grain. -kalā f. a digit of the moon; the crescent of the moon immediately before or after the new moon (Śiv. 98 (N.P.), 1490). -kalādār m. he who wears the crescent moon, i.e. who has it for his crest, a N. of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 75). -kalapushᵘ m. a kind of round cap ornamented with moon-shaped pieces of gold, silver, etc. -shēkhar m. he who has the moon for his crest, a N. of Shiv (Śiva) (Śiv. 1586). -ṭöcᵘ̈ f. a kind of child's cap ornamented as ab. -ʦṻḍ m., i.q. -shēkhar, ab. (Śiv. 976, 1035, 1538, 1574); a N. of Vishnu (Śiv. 740). -wār m. Monday (El. tsandarwár, Gr.M., W. 106 ʦandawār). Cf. sūmwar.
m. (sg. dat. ʦạndᵃrakas), one of the moon-shaped marks, or eyes, on the expanded tail of a peacock (cf. mōr-ʦᵒ, p. 587b, l. 49).
m. a receiver of blows, i.e. an obstinate boy, or the like, who refuses to learn or obey orders, and is hence subject to frequent chastisement. Cf. ʦünḍᵘ̈.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦônᵘ, f. ʦöñᵘ̈; 2 p.p. ʦāñōv. This verb is the causal of aʦun, q.v.), to cause to enter, to bring in, put into (dat.) (cf. atha ʦᵒ, p. 64a, l. 24; bāzar ʦᵒ, p. 154b, l. 36; khaphari phamb ʦᵒ, p. 406a, l. 13; khyolᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 426a, l. 47; wā̃gujᵘ ʦᵒ) (El.; Gr.Gr. 12, 13; Gr.M.; W. 65; Śiv. 1645, 1911; Rām. 416; K. 36, 365-6, 816, 896); to invite (into), lead into (cf. gara ʦᵒ, p. 295b, l. 3; jin ʦᵒ, p. 375a, l. 11) (K. 298, 494, 715, 900, 1130; H. iii, 7); to bring into existence (in something) (cf. phuṭh ʦānüñᵘ̈, p. 717a, l. 5; dāg ʦᵒ, p. 194a, l. 19; khrọ̆lᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 412b, l. 46; kᵃṭh ʦᵒ, p. 486a, l. 17); ¶ to cause some condition to occur (in) (esp. when the condition is new or unexperienced) (cf. ala ʦᵒ, p. 23a, l. 49; baṭha ʦᵒ, p. 139b, l. 29; chag ʦānüñᵘ̈, p. 158b, l. 8; cār ʦᵒ, p. 174b, l. 4; dŏdurᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 192b, l. 7; khurᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 411b, l. 45; lār ʦānüñᵘ̈, p. 530a, l. 25; lōsa ʦᵒ, p. 533a, l. 16; maza ʦᵒ, p. 614b, l. 9; nēkh-pūrᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 629b, l. 18; naṭh ʦānüñᵘ̈, p. 660a, l. 25; pȧtⁱ ʦᵒ, p. 789a, l. 50; potᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 788a, l. 49; path ʦᵒ, p. 792b, l. 9; pay ʦᵒ, p. 812a, l. 1; rāshĕ ʦᵒ, p. 843a, l. 35; shram ʦᵒ, p. 893a, l. 28; tṻra ʦānañĕ, p. 1021a, l. 17; ʦᵃkar ʦānȧnⁱ, p. 1069a, l. 50; ʦᵃkȧṭᵃ ʦānȧnⁱ, p. 1070a, l. 9; ʦingar ʦānȧnⁱ, p. 1074b, l. 49; ʦāph ʦānüñᵘ̈, p. 1077b, l. 31; zingar ʦānȧnⁱ; zŏzurᵘ ʦᵒ) (Gr.M.; Rām. 470; K. 620; H. ix, 2); to cause something to begin working, to start in action, to set going (into something) (cf. drôtᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 249a, l. 44; khalas ʦᵒ, p. 397a, l. 26; khayāl ʦᵒ, p. 426b, l. 27; nakh ʦᵒ, p. 628a, l. 33; pĕd ʦānüñᵘ̈, p. 681b, l. 12; panḍa ʦᵒ, p. 738b, l. 5; pöthᵃr ʦᵒ, p. 800a, l. 35; thaph ʦānüñᵘ̈, p. 981a, l. 17; wād ʦᵒ, s.v. wād; wadanas ʦᵒ, s.v. wadun) (Gr.M.; K. 326, 331); to apply (a patch or the like) (cf. düjᵘ̈ ʦānüñᵘ̈, p. 203a, l. 24). ¶ ʦānan-wād m. harassing, oppression, annoyance (to compel someone to undertake something difficult).
adj. c.g. unsteady, restless, unstable, inconstant, changeful, volatile, fickle (Gr.M.; Śiv. 334, 1340, 1539; Rām. 74, 1624); tremulous, agitated (Rām. 173, 986, 1285).
f. unsteadiness, restlessness, instability, inconstancy, volatility, fickleness.
adj. c.g. one who habitually bites, a biter (a man, dog, horse, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 134).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦāpanôwᵘ), to cause to gnaw (caus. of ʦāpun, q.v.) (so El., ? really 'to cause to be gnawed').

m. or f. (sg. dat. ʦāpas or ʦāpi. This is the verbal noun of ʦāpun, q.v., and may be either m. (Gr.Gr. 123) or f. (Gr.Gr. 127)), the act of gnawing, biting, chewing (cf. atha-ʦᵒ, p. 64a, l. 28) (Gr.Gr. 66); mumbling with the gums (cf. atha-ʦᵒ, as ab.). --aʦüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. masticating to enter, i.e. a flavour (of some eatable) to be experienced for the first time (used esp. of children). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give mastication, to chew (something); met. to ponder over, meditate upon, ruminate upon (e.g. upon some advice or the like, given by another). --ʦānüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause the flavour (of some eatable) to be experienced for the first time.

or (q.v.) ʦamph f. (sg. dat. ʦã̄pi), coaxing, wheedling, blandishment, cajolery (to induce another to do something) (Gr.Gr. 66). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to coax, wheedle, to speak kindly words to, send salutations to (K. 982). Cf. ʦamph.

(sg. dat. ʦapi), the bowels (of man or beast) (cf. ḍọ̆mbᵘ-ʦᵘ, m., p. 217b, l. 50) (K.Pr. 61). ʦapi nūn pyonᵘ m.inf. 'salt to fall on the bowels', to become distraught, overwhelmed with grief, out of one's mind for sorrow (caused by the loss or destruction of property or the like).

f. (sg. dat. ʦapi), a paddy-field, a field in which rice is grown, and where the paddy is deposited as it is reaped (El. a sheaf of grain); cf. dā̃-ʦᵒ, a single paddy-plant, p. 231a, l. 14. --güñᵘ̈ āsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'the paddy-plot to be dense'; hence, to be very prosperous or well-to-do (esp. with reference to one who lives by cultivation or some other profession). ¶ ʦapi-dāñĕ m. reaped paddy, as laid down on the field to dry. --thawun -- m.inf. to lay down the reaped paddy on the field to dry (as each handful of the plant is cut, it is so laid down).

the act of biting, a bite (Gr.Gr. 134), in the following:-- ʦapa-ʦaph m. or f. (sg. dat. -ʦapas or -ʦapi), mutual biting (as in a dog fight, or when horses fight). Note that this word may be m. or f. Cf. ʦāph.
(? spelling) f. a kind of sandal (i.q. pulahorᵘ, p. 730b, l. 5) (L. 251). Borrowed from Hindī cappal.
or ʦapul adj. (f. ʦạpᵘ̈jᵘ̈), i.q. ʦapal, q.v. (cf. atha-ʦᵒ, p. 64a, l. 31).
