conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦôpᵘ), to gnaw, bite, chew, masticate (cf. atha ʦᵒ, p. 64a, l. 36; gār ʦᵒ, p. 295a, l. 20; marʦ ʦᵒ, p. 594b, l. 10; maʦha ʦāpañĕ, p. 609a, l. 39; nār ʦᵒ, p. 647a, l. 31; ʦᵃmaruwᵃ kara ʦᵒ, p. 1073a, l. 33; ʦạndrāyĕn ʦāᵒ, p. 1074b, l. 28) (El.; Śiv. 577, 595; Rām. 724, 921, 936, 1538, 1573, 1578, 1656; K.Pr. 120); to mumble with the gums. ¶ ʦôpᵘ-motᵘ (sic) perf. part. (f. ʦöpᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), crushed with the teeth, chewed, masticated, gnawed. ¶ ʦöpith ʦhunun m.inf. to overwhelm (some subordinate) with abuse.
m. motion, or progression (esp. of a heavenly body) (cf. graha-ʦār, p. 301a, l. 30).
m. a bed-bug (L. 156). ʦara-gānd f. the evil smell emitted by bugs. ʦara-ṭŏph f. (sg. dat. -ṭŏpi), a bug-bite. -wŏmād f. 'a bug-stink'; hence, an outburst or swarming forth of many bugs.

m. a kind of rope into which green vegetables are twisted up in the autumn, so as to be preserved for consumption in the winter months (cf. hāka-ʦᵒ, p. 326b, l. 42, and p. 879b, l. 36; pañi-ʦᵒ, p. 746a, l. 45) (L. 463 tsaráh, with suff. of indef. art.; K.Pr. 192). The word phari-ʦᵒ, p. 703a, l. 12, means a certain preparation of roasted fish. Cf. ʦürᵘ̈ 2.
m. in parinⁱ-ʦar, p. 774b, l. 39 (K.Pr. 166). Cf. ʦᵃran.
ʦara, in ʦar-aʦar, ʦara-aʦara, see ʦarāʦar.
f. the profession, or employment, of a spy, detective, or the like. See ʦar 1.

m. a foot (a corruption of the Skt. caraṇa, as in shŏba-ʦᵒ, p. 869a, l. 25) (Śiv. 155-6, 169, 191, 228, 381, 628, 798, 987, 1266; K. 398, 1000). ʦarana-kamal m. a lotus-foot, a foot beautiful as a lotus, (as a reverential term) a foot (cf. pāda-kamal, p. 681a, l. 8) (Rām. 1644).
m. (sg. dat. ʦaranāmrĕtas), 'foot-nectar', the water in which the feet of a god or venerated person have been washed (borrowed from Skt. caraṇâmṛta) (Śiv. 1398). Cf. ʦaran.
m. a foot-lotus, a lotus-like foot (borrowed from the Skt. caraṇâravinda) (Śiv. 1424). Cf. ʦaran.
m. a certain bird (described as having black wings and a red beak).

or (Śiv. 624) ʦara-aʦara, or (K.) ʦar-aʦar m. that which is movable and that which is immovable, the animate and the inanimate, i.e. the whole universe (borrowed from Skt. carâcara) (L.V. 16; Śiv. 105, 155, 370, 624, 868, 935; K. 320, 509).
m. increase, abundance, excess (cf. phala-ʦᵒ, p. 692b, l. 16) (El. tsarir, m. increase, and tsirir, f. abundance; Gr.Gr. 138, Gr.M., Rām. 1152).

or ʦarith m. (sg. dat. ʦarĕtas), behaviour, act or acts, deeds, conduct, goings on (El. tsareṭ, f. a spectacle); Gr.M. ʦarith; L.V. 38; Śiv. 711; K. 3, 35, 139, 247, 324, 332, 505, 607, 615, 638, 688, 731, 919, 936, 940, 981); a biography, account of adventures, history (of a person) (K. 749); an account of any particular appearance, dress, or the like (of a person).
f. a very delicately formed woman (with each limb delicate and soft).
f. inward wrath, jealousy (Gr.Gr. 117, 118). Cf. ʦarüñᵘ̈.
m. (sg. dat. ʦarmanas), a skin, a hide (L.V. 66). Cf. ʦam.
m. a kind of condiment made of sheep's or goat's liver spiced with very hot pepper, etc., and salt; an offering to demons, etc., made of this condiment.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦôrᵘ), to gather, collect, pick (as a bird), pick up (cf. dŏdas kȧnḍⁱ ʦārȧnⁱ, p. 190b, l. 40; lĕkh ʦārüñᵘ̈ and lĕka ʦārañĕ, p. 518a, ll. 15, 41; tulⁱ ʦārȧnⁱ, p. 1000b, l. 33; wŏhav ʦārun) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 193, 526, 1183, 1515, 1913; K.Pr. 61, 106); to select, separate, sort (cf. chȧtⁱ krĕhȧnⁱ ʦārȧnⁱ, p. 166a, l. 42) (Gr.Gr. 11, 12; Gr.M.; L. 464; Śiv. 1032, 1579, 1845; H. vi, 14); to clear (from dirt or the like), pick out, weed, purify (by picking out impurities). ¶ ʦôrᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦörᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), picked, selected, etc., as ab.; cleaned, cleansed, purified, etc., as ab. ¶ ʦörith conj. part. (see also s.v.) in ʦörith kaḍun m.inf. to extract, select out (from its surroundings); quote (from a book) (Gr.M.). --thawun -- m.inf. to select and put (aside); to select, choose (e.g. a name) (Śiv. 436); to cleanse (from impurities) and put (aside).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦorᵘ; 2 p.p. ʦaryōv), to do, perform, carry out (meditation, austerities, or the like) (Śiv. 312; K. 612, 619, 704).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦaryōv), to go forward, progress, walk (L.V. 38).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦaryōv), to increase, become more than sufficient, to be larger than required, remain over and above (cf. nam ʦarȧnⁱ, p. 635b, l. 34) (Gr.Gr. 118; K. 7, 1025); cf. ʦorᵘ 2. ʦaryō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦaryē-müʦᵘ̈), more than is required, remaining over and above.

(sometimes written ʦariñ, Gr.Gr. 192) conj. 1 (this verb is throughout impersonal, and in tenses formed from the past participle is always in the feminine gender. The person is indicated by a pronominal suffix in the dative. Thus, ʦarĕs, there will be inward anger to him, i.e. he will be inwardly angry. ʦürᵘ̈s, there was inward anger to him, he was inwardly angry. See Gr.Gr. 118, 182, 188, 192, 203, 215, 220, 234, 248-9, 254; 1 p.p. f. ʦürᵘ̈), inward wrath, hidden resentment, jealousy, to occur or be (to a person) (Gr.Gr. 117). ʦürᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ perf. part. f. hidden resentment that has occurred (to a person).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦorʦᵘ), to discuss, consider, investigate; to watch, wait for expectantly (K. 149, 653, 920); (in Ksh. esp.) malevolently to spy on another, secretly to hunt out another's defects (cf. potᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 788b, l. 11). ʦorʦᵘ-motᵘ p.p. (f. ʦürʦᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), malevolently spied upon.
disrespect, insult, humiliation, public abuse (Gr.Gr. 33, 37, 134; Rām. 1665); terror, great fear or sorrow (Rām. 798); a hole, aperture, cavity, chasm (Rām. 1169, K. 111).

f. a cough (cf. ʦākhᵃr) (El. tsás, m. and tsaṅs, f.; Gr.Gr. 33, m., and so, also, to be inferred from I.K. vi, 18; K.Pr. 109). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to conceal or deny knowledge, show evasion, esp. to deny that one has property which has been entrusted to one. --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a cough to come, to be attacked by a cough, or disease involving such.
I entered, or he entered for him, see aʦun, p. 70a, l. 23.
adj. c.g. afflicted with coughing, subject to coughing (Gr.Gr. 134).
(also by Paṇḍits written) m. astringency (Gr.Gr. 138, 141). Cf. ʦôhᵘ and ʦôshᵘ.
adj. c.g. (as subst., f. ʦāsiladiñ), id. (Gr.Gr. 135).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦosᵘ, 2 p.p. ʦasyōv. This verb is impersonal, as in ʦosun, it was laughed by him, he laughed) to laugh long and loudly, to go into a fit of laughing (Gr.Gr. 208, 225; Rām. 332, 1094, 1457). ¶ ʦȧsⁱ ʦȧsⁱyunⁱ m.inf. (of a number of people) all to laugh loud and long. ¶ ʦasith yunᵘ m.inf. to come in fits of laughter; hence, to come joyfully (K. 24); to come, or be, assembled in multitudes (more than there is space for), (of fruit) to be produced in great quantities (so that there is not sufficient room on the tree), and so on (Rām. 282).
ord. (ʦtajihimᵘ̈), fortieth (Gr.Gr. 77). Cf. L. 264 chat jihun, the fortieth day after the appearance of an attack of smallpox.
m.pl. forties, the form of ʦatajih used in multiplication, as in kāh ʦatajihⁱ ʦōr hath ta ʦatajih, eleven forties (are) four hundred and forty (cf. Gr.Gr. 86).
in ʦātakh pachin m. the pied cuckoo, Cuculus melanoleucus, the papīhā.
m. (in a narration or the like) disputing at length, or interrupting at length with irrelevant details (esp. by someone other than the narrator).
f. in ʦāṭan kaḍüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to pick out, remove (dirt from cotton); met. carefully and repeatedly to revise, or edit, some written composition, story, or the like.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦaṭanôwᵘ), to cause to be cut, etc. (see ʦaṭun) (cf. pōn ʦᵒ, p. 737a, l. 29).
in ʦaṭaph-ʦaṭh f. cutting or dividing relationship (e.g. when discords separate a husband and wife).
m. cleverness, skilfulness, sharpness, ingenuity (cf. atha-ʦᵒ, p. 64b, l. 5; shāma-ʦᵒ, p. 882a, l. 49) (Gr.Gr. 139).
f. wages for cutting (esp. for cutting down trees, sawing wood, or the like). See ʦaṭun.
n.ag. (f. ʦaṭavüñᵘ̈), one who cuts, a cutter, etc. (in all the senses of ʦaṭun, q.v.) (El.); esp. a woodcutter, a sawman; (of a road or the like) not long, short.

m. (sg. dat. ʦaṭas), cutting (Gr.Gr. 146) used in the following:-- ʦaṭh-kapaṭh m. 'cutting and cutting out' (cf. kapaṭun) (amongst tailors, carpenters, and the like) the calculation of material used in cutting away and adding pieces (to form the completed whole). ʦaṭh-wāṭh m. (sg. dat. -wāṭas), 'cutting and joining,' id. ʦaṭaph-ʦaṭh, see s.v. ʦaṭaph. ¶ ʦaṭa-ʦṻr m. cutting to powder, tearing a garment or the like to tiny rags. -ʦaṭh f. cutting or tearing apart; setting at variance (two people). -wāṭh f. (sg. dat. -wāṭi), cutting and joining, i.e. tailoring (cutting out the cloth and sewing it up properly); surgery, a surgical operation.

m. (sg. dat. ʦāṭas), a pupil (in a school or of a tutor), an apprentice (of some artisan or the like), a pupil (of a spiritual preceptor) (cf. kū̃sᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 479b, l. 35; pĕnji-ʦᵒ, p. 739a, l. 19; ziṭh ʦᵒ, s.v. zyuṭhᵘ) (Gr.M.; W. 146; Śiv. 1887 ʦāṭa, pl.; K. 1083, 1088; H. v, 1; K.Pr. 257). ʦāṭh ʦö or (q.v.) ʦāṭuvʦö m. the name used in schools for the Śāradā letter corresponding to the Nāgarī letter, whether it represents ca or ʦa. ¶ ʦāṭa-bôjᵘ m. a fellow-pupil, a school-fellow (K. 1084, 1086). -bāy f. the wife of a pupil (of a teacher, or of a spiritual preceptor). -gạdᵃra m. 'a beloved little pupil', a very young pupil (under seven years of age). -hāl m. (sg. dat. -hālas, Gr.Gr. 69), a school, a college (El.; Gr.Gr. 69; Gr.M.; L. 463; K. 485, 1076, 1078, 1136; H. viii, 4, 11). -kūrᵘ̈ f. a girl pupil (of a teacher, or of a religious preceptor); the wife of a male pupil, as ab. -kọ̆ṭhᵘ m. 'the pupil's knee', a certain posture in sitting (in which thighs, knees, shanks, and feet, all rest on the ground). -nĕcyuwᵘ m. the son of a pupil (of a teacher, or of a religious preceptor). -pȧnḍⁱtözⁱ f. 'pupil's paṇḍitship', little by little to interfere with another's means of livelihood, in order dishonestly to capture it.
m. (f. ʦaṭᵘ̈jᵘ̈), a dishonest fellow, a swindler, a cutpurse, a thief, a robber (cf. ʦūr ʦᵒ, p. 1080b, l. 21) (Gr.Gr. 146). Cf. ʦaṭh.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦoṭᵘ; f. ʦüṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. ʦacĕ; 2 p.p. ʦacyōv), to cut, tear (cf. bôrᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 118a, l. 18; tāphtāna ʦaṭȧnⁱ, p. 1015b, l. 47) (Gr.Gr. 5, 9, 10; Gr.M.; W. 145; L. 459; L.V. 66; Rām. 388, 636; K.Pr. 171); ¶ to cut, wound (cf. dasta ʦaṭȧnⁱ, p. 256a, l. 49; kȧchⁱ ʦᵒ, p. 507a, l. 9; mȧchⁱ ʦaṭüñᵘ̈, p. 547a, l. 32) (Rām. 410, 820, 1373, 1422; H. v, 5, 7; YZ. 150; K.Pr. 155, 218); to cut asunder, sever, divide, tear apart (cf. dȧlⁱ ʦaṭȧnⁱ, p. 212a, l. 6; hoṭᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 356a, l. 18; haṭi-pholᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 356a, l. 50; kadᵃl ʦᵒ, p. 385a, l. 30; nāna ʦaṭüñᵘ̈, p. 639b, l. 47; prāʦa ʦaṭañĕ, p. 771a, l. 16; pō̃th ʦaṭüñᵘ̈, p. 796b, l. 36; sum ʦaṭüñᵘ̈, p. 911b, l. 15; wath ʦaṭüñᵘ̈, s.v. wath 1) (Śiv. 711, 1432, 1558, 1563, 1783, 1833; Rām. 703, 911, 914, 919, 1103, 1176, 1305, 1582; K. 124, 191, 390; YZ. 159, 194, 233, 505; K.Pr. 70, 139, 165, 174); to cut off, tear away (cf. khōr ʦᵒ, p. 410a, l. 27; kala ʦᵒ, p. 435b, l. 23; nam ʦaṭȧnⁱ, p. 635b, l. 36; sar ʦᵒ, p. 928a, l. 45) (Gr.M.; L.V. 80; Śiv. 124-5, 319-20, 1568; Rām. 37, 335, 411, 997; K. 693, 746, 759, 762, 791, 827, 829, 872-3, 883, 1059; H. iii, 2; v, 7; viii, 6, 11; ix, 5; K.Pr. 214); ¶ to dissect, cut (as a surgeon) (Gr.M. ʦ˚-wāṭun, cutting and uniting, surgery); to cut off, throw away, give up, abandon (Rām. 1268); to clean (grain) (El.); ¶ to pluck, gather (flowers or fruit) (Gr.M.; Rām. 1082, YZ. 376); ¶ to cut out, strike out, erase; to interrupt (speech) (cf. ös ʦᵒ, p. 46b, l. 35; cỗṭᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 177a, l. 36; zĕv ʦaṭüñᵘ̈); ¶ to traverse, get over (a road or the like) (cf. manzila ʦᵒ, p. 584b, l. 29) (Rām. 207, K.Pr. 45); to clear land (of jungle) (cf. banjĕr ʦᵒ, p. 113b, l. 8) (L.V. 25, K.Pr. 246); ¶ to make ashamed, put to the blush (cf. phalakh ʦaṭȧnⁱ, p. 695a, l. 37); ¶ to take a loan, incur a debt (from) (cf. wuzumᵘ ʦᵒ) (Gr.M.). ¶ ʦoṭᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦüṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, sg. dat. ʦacĕ-maʦĕ), cut, etc., as ab.; taken on loan, borrowed (as a debt) (cf. wŏzumᵘ ʦᵒ). ¶ ʦaṭith dyunᵘ m.inf. to cut to pieces, to cut up (L.V. 104). --trāwun -- m.inf. to cut away, to cut off and throw away, finally to get rid of (Rām. 45). --ʦhunun -- m.inf. to tear to pieces (H. xii, 15).
or ʦạtur adv. quickly, speedily, at once (cf. ʦaturᵘ 2). ʦạtur ʦạtur adv. quickly (all the time), rapidly (Gr.Gr. 76). Cf. ʦaturᵘ ʦatur, s.v. ʦatur 2.

or ᵒbŏz m. (a corruption of Skt. caturbhuja) a group of four arms, the four arms (of a four-armed god or the like) (Śiv. 100, ʦaturbuza; 1117); a title of various gods (Śiv. 10 (Ganēsh), 515 (Shiv), 732 (Vishnu, cf. 1117); 47 (Vishnu); K. 58, 594 (Vishnu)).
m. (a corruption of Skt. caturvēda) the four Vēdas (Śiv. 801).
or ʦạturᵘ adj. (f. ʦa(ạ)türᵘ̈ ), clever, skilful, ingenious, sharp-witted (cf. atha-ʦᵒ, p. 64b, l. 3; shāma-ʦᵒ, p. 882a, l. 46; zĕwa-ʦᵒ, s.v. zĕv) (Gr.Gr. 139). Cf. ʦŏturᵘ.
in ʦaturᵘ ʦatur adv. very quickly (see ʦatur).
or (q.v., p. 1086a, l. 4) ʦāṭh ʦö m. the name used in schools for the Śāradā letter corresponding to the Nāgarī letter, whether it represents ca or ʦa.
he entered, 2 p.p. of aʦun, see p. 70a, l. 22 (Gr.Gr. 230, 236).
f. the amount of paddy land which (at the time of weeding) can be measured as the area within extended arms with the fingers of each arm touching.
f. (sg. dat. ʦāvünᵘ̈), worrying (by a beggar) by frequent begging.
m. N. of a village lying to the north-east of the Ḍal lake, near Śrīnagar (El. tsátsa, N. of a village where paper is made).
f. in wōda-ʦᵒ, s.v. wōd 2, q.v., and in waidĕ ʦᵒ, s.v. waidy.

f. (sg. dat. ʦĕḍi or ʦë˘ḍᵘ̈), patience, endurance, bearing patiently (another's anger, a calamity or the like) (El. tsĕḍ, f., tseda, m.; Gr.Gr. 25; W. 123; K.Pr. 28); waiting patiently, patient expectation. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take patience, to wait patiently (for). --karüñᵘ̈ --  f.inf. to bear patiently; to await patiently (for), be patient (El.). ¶ ʦĕḍi- (or ʦë˘ḍᵘ̈-) wôlᵘ  m. (f. -wājĕñ), patient, long-suffering (in character).
m. a mark, sign, emblem, distinguishing mark (K. 397).
f. (a woman) who has vile pudenda, an unchaste woman (cf. ʦē̃kh).

f. (sg. dat. ʦē̃ki), a woman's pudenda (used in obsc. abuse) (cf. kŏ-ʦᵒ, p. 493b, l. 39). ʦē̃ka-phŏkh m. (sg. dat. -phŏkas), 'a puff, or breath, from this'; hence, (on the part of a woman) lascivious feelings, shameless immodesty.
f. (sg. dat. ʦē̃ki), a kind of small mattock used in vegetable gardens and the like, a vegetable hoe.
conj. 1 (this verb is impersonal. 1 p.p. ʦĕkholᵘ; 2 p.p. ʦĕkhajyōv), to jest with a smile, to smile with, or at, a joke (K. 139, 179, 222).

m. forcing something additional into a receptacle already full, stuffing into, cramming into (cf. atha-ʦᵒ, p. 64a, l. 18) (Gr.Gr. 124); (of a number of persons) the being crowded together (in, e.g., a small room, where the bodies are in close contact to each other and there is no space even to sit down); squeezing, crushing, pressing (K.Pr. 10); squeezing, shampooing (El.); impediment, obstruction (due to crowding) (cf. tāli-ʦᵒ, p. 997b, l. 26); inward anger, taking offence, umbrage, soreness, resentment (at some piece of rudeness or disrespect). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to force, stuff, cram, into a receptacle. --gaʦhun-- m.inf. the being crowded together to occur, crowding to happen; umbrage or resentment to be experienced (on account of some piece of disrespect). ¶ ʦĕla-mŏ̈nḍᵘ̈ f. the being spoiled by being crushed, the being squeezed out of shape. ʦĕla-ʦĕjⁱ or ʦĕlam-ʦĕjⁱ adv. crowdedly, with mutual crowding, closely packed. ʦĕla-ʦĕl f. (sg. dat. -ʦë˘jᵘ̈), the being crowded together, crowding (e.g. a number of people packed together in too small a room).
adv. i.q. ʦĕla- ʦĕjⁱ, p. 1070b, l. 29, q.v.

(by some written ʦĕllun) conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦyolᵘ, f. ʦë˘jᵘ̈; 2 p.p. ʦĕjyōv), to force (something) into (a receptacle), to stuff into, cram into (Gr.Gr. 25, 26, 124); to train with vigorous practice, to train intensively (cf. English 'cram') (L.V. 69). ¶ ʦĕlⁱ ʦĕlⁱ freq. part., as adv. with continued forcible cramming. ¶ ʦĕlith manḍith conj. part. as adv. having crammed having trampled, cramming in and trampling down. --thawun -- m.inf. to cram into, force into (and leave there).
or ʦĕmĕr m. shortness, (esp. in the sense of shorter than proper) being too short.

or ʦĕmburᵘ, or ʦĕmorᵘ, ʦĕmurᵘ adj. (f. ʦĕmbürᵘ̈, ʦĕmürᵘ̈) (of any member of the body, esp. the nose) having it too short, flat-nosed, squat-nosed, snub-nosed (cf. nas-ʦᵒ, p. 654b, l. 9); met. (of the eye) flat and dull without eyelashes (cf. ȧchⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 8b, l. 45). Cf. ʦĕpoṭᵘ.
or ʦĕmurᵘ adj. (f. ʦĕmürᵘ̈), i.q. ʦĕmborᵘ, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦēnanôwᵘ), to cause to recognize, or to be recognized, by a sign, to indicate by a sign, wink, or the like (cf. ʦēnun, ʦīñᵉ̆run, and ʦīñᵉ̆rāwun) (Śiv. 1884).
f. making known, information, indication, pointing out. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to point out, show (El. tsenawain dinyi).

n.ag. (f. ʦēnavüñᵘ̈), one who recognizes, distinguishes, identifies (Śiv. 1515); esp. the Supreme, considered as the source of all sensation (Śiv. 1342); (as adv.) by identification, by recognition, by means of identification.
f. in ranga-ʦᵒ, p. 837a, l. 39, q.v.
m. (sg. dat. ʦĕnganas), happiness, jollity, the being amused. --hyonᵘ --, m.inf. to take happiness, to be amused (K.Pr. 249).
conj. 1 (this verb is impersonal; 1 p.p. ʦyongᵘ, f. ʦë˘njᵘ̈; 2 p.p. ʦĕnjyōv), to rejoice, to exult, show happiness (on succeeding in carrying out one's intentions) (El. to be happy). Cf. ʦring 1.
(? spelling) m. a funeral pyre (El.). ? Cf. Skt. citā. ʦintabal m. the place of a funeral pyre, a funeral pyre (El.).
or ʦintā f. thinking, thought; thought, care, anxiety (Rām. 555; K. 500, 1158); i.q. ʦinth, q.v. --barüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be anxious, to be full of care (K. 65).
conj. 1, i.q. ʦēnun 2, q.v. to meditate upon, think upon (K. 408, 505); mani ʦᵒ, to consider in one's mind, to determine (on a particular course of conduct) (K. 410).
or ʦēnunᵘ m. (sg. dat. ʦēnanas), consciousness, understanding, intelligence (Śiv. 1043, 1339, 1406, 1415, 1592; K. 212, 301, 311).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦyūnᵘ, Gr.Gr. 19; 2 p.p. ʦēñōv. The causal of this verb is ʦēnanāwun or ʦīñᵉ̆rāwun, Gr.Gr. 174), to know by a sign, to recognize, distinguish, identify (K. 186, 195, 210); to recognize (as such-and-such), to understand (a thing to be such-and-such) (L.V. 28, Śiv. 1545, Rām. 627, K. 141, YZ. 421); hence, to accept when seen, to experience, gain the experience (of anything) (L.V. 6); to recognize as authoritative, to meditate upon (instruction given) (L.V. 51-4, 80; Śiv. 1704). Cf. ʦēntun.
adj. c.g. marked with surface cuts.
m. (too much) shortness, the condition of being too short (e.g. when one arm is shorter than the other, and so on). Cf. ʦĕmborᵘ, ʦĕpoṭᵘ, and ʦyopᵘ.

f. (sg. dat. ʦĕpi), a skin wound, a wound skin-deep, a cut on the outside only, a surface cut (esp. when accidental). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to wound, cut (as ab., also on clothes,cloth, or the like). --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cut (as ab.) the skin, one side of a cloth, or the like (with a knife or the like). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to have the mark of a cut or the like made (on the skin, cloth, etc., as ab.) (K.Pr. 224, ʦyap); met. (in accomplishing some task) loss in one particular to be experienced.
f. (sg. dat. ʦē̃pi), a very small part of anything. ʦē̃pi-ʦē̃pi adv. little by little, scrap by scrap, morsel by morsel (u.w. vbs. of giving or the like).
adj. (f. ʦĕpüṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. ʦĕpacĕ), having a flat nose, flat-nosed (cf. ʦĕmborᵘ, ʦĕpĕr, and ʦĕpyuṭᵘ; also nas-ʦĕpoṭᵘ, p. 654b, l. 11).
adj. (f. ʦĕpiṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. ʦĕpicĕ), shortened, shrunken and globular, snub (e.g. of the nose). Cf. ʦĕpoṭᵘ.

m. a long time, lateness, delay (El. f.; Gr.Gr. 21; Gr.M.; W. 93; Śiv. 1709; Rām. 1721; H. v, 6; K.Pr. 3); cf. ʦrēṭh. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. a very long time to occur, delay to occur (to a person) (i.e. to be late) (Gr.M.; Rām. 946, 1153, 1561; H. iii, 1; v, 9). ¶ ʦēra-vēr adv. even very late (in the day spoken of; u.w. vbs. of coming or the like). ¶ ʦīrⁱ adv. late in the day, in the latter part of the day; after delay, with delay (Rām. 237; H. iii, 1). --onᵘ -- adj. (f. --üñᵘ̈ --), a little blind, dim-sighted (on account of inflamed eyelids or the like). --bögin -- adv. somewhat late in the day, in the afternoon. --hŏgᵃ̇rᵃ̇ -- adv. late in the day, after evening. --pahān -- adv. somewhat late in the day, in the afternoon, after some time (Gr.Gr. 94). --pahānas -- adv., id. ¶ ʦērukᵘ adj. gen. (f. ʦērücᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, the later part of the day; born, or produced, long ago, of long standing.

f. (according to El. and W. there is also ʦēra, m., q.v.), an apricot, Prunus Armeniaca (cf. bāla-ʦᵒ, p. 104b, l. 9; bŏṭa-ʦᵒ, p. 138b, l. 39; phaka-ʦᵒ, p. 689a, l. 24; papa-ʦᵒ, p. 748b, l. 25; ʦŏka-ʦᵒ, p. 1067a, l. 32) (Gr.Gr. 21; L. 348; L.V. 92; K.Pr. 12, 119, 214). ¶ ʦēra-ö̃ṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -ã̄cĕ), the stone of the apricot fruit, an apricot stone. -hāputh m. (sg. dat. -hāpatas), a bear (who eats) apricots; met. one who habitually eats mixed food (regardless of its dirtiness or cleanness). -kujⁱ or -kujᵘ̈ f. an apricot shrub. -kulᵘ m. an apricot-tree. -krē̃kh m. (sg. dat. -krē̃kas), the gum that exudes from an apricot-tree (looked upon as resembling a jewel in a ring). --mēṭhañĕ -- f. pl. 'the (sour) apricots to become sweet', hearty mutual affection to succeed mutual hostility. -nomᵘ m. a dried apricot (looked upon as dried skin). -nȧmⁱ-wugra m. a sweet dish made by cooking dried apricots in water with spices, etc. -phulay f. the season of apricot-blossoms. --papañĕ -- f.pl. the apricots to ripen, the ripening of apricots; met. the ripening of (the prospect of obtaining) great profits. -pōsh m. the apricot-flower. -wugra m. apricot stew. -vüñᵘ̈ f. an apricot orchard. ¶ ʦīrⁱ-hüṭⁱ f. (sg. dat. -hacĕ), apricot wood (used for making knife-handles, fancy boxes, or the like).

m. an apricot, i.q. ʦēr 3, q.v., which is fem. Noted only in El. (who gives both tser, f., and tséra, m.), in ʦokạ-ʦera (W. 116), p. 1067a, l. 33, and ṭeṭha-ʦera (W. 116), p. 1051a, l. 2. Possibly the word is really fem. plur. nom. of ʦēr 3.
f. sense, consciousness, understanding, intelligence (Śiv. 171, Rām. 322).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦēṭanôwᵘ), to cause to pulverize (? to cause to be pulverized) (El.) (see ʦēṭun).

(for 1, 2, 3, see ʦĕth, 1, 2, 3) m. full consciousness, full perception, attention; remembrance, continuance in memory (of something not forgotten), recollection (El. f.). --karun 2 -- (for 1, see p. 1086b, l. 5) m.inf. to remember, recollect (Gr.M., Rām. 754). -waturᵘ m. the possession of a good memory, power of remembering accurately past events (owing to a habit of careful observation) (cf. pạthᵃr 1, a leaf of paper, which becomes wạthᵃr, as the second member of a compound). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. memory to come (to a person), to be remembered (by, dat.) (El. tsetas yenyi, to remember, recollect).
f. in wach ʦᵒ, s.v. wach 1, q.v. Cf. ʦēṭun.

m. (sg. dat. ʦēṭas), pounding crushing, reducing to powder (cf. atha-ʦᵒ, p. 64a, l. 50) (Gr.Gr. 115, 123). --dyunᵘ -- to pound, crush, reduce to powder; met. to beat severely, thrash, pummel, trounce (a person); to exhaust a person (by continually pressing him on to complete some work) (cf. ʦrēṭh dyunᵘ, p. 1083b, l. 37). -mār m. a thrashing, pummelling, trouncing. ¶ ʦēṭa-gŏgᵃ̇jᵃ̇ f. a severe beating or trouncing (in which the skin is not cut, but limbs are injured or broken, quasi, as one pounds a turnip). -körⁱ f. beating, trouncing.
f. (sg. dat. ʦē̃ti, Gr.Gr. 70), tumbling head over heels (as by an acrobat). See ʦith gaʦhüñᵘ̈, bel. ʦē̃ta-ʦē̃th f. repeatedly tumbling head over heels, a series of such tumbling.

m. (sg. dat. ʦĕtas 2), consciousness, sensation, understanding, intelligence (Skt. cētanā, caitanya) (Śiv. 268, 1043, 1069, 1311, 1374, 1426, 1484, 1538, 1562; K. 11, 78, 168); memory, remembrance, recollection. ¶ ʦĕtas 2, sg. dat. commonly used to mean 'in memory' or 'in so-and-so's memory' (K. 858, 999, 1135, 1139, 1161). For ʦetas 4, see s.v. --anun -- m.inf. to bring to (one's) memory, to call to mind, remember (K. 503, 1140). --pyonᵘ -- m.inf. to fall to the memory, to come to remembrance, be remembered (El. tsetas pyinye; L.V. 87; Rām. 793, 936, 1138, 1390, 1392, 1555; K. 499, 504). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain in memory, always be remembered (K. 336). --thawun -- or --thāwun -- m.inf. to bear in mind, keep in memory, remember, recollect (Gr.M.; Rām. 662, 1296, 1574). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to come to (a person's) memory, to be remembered.

or (q.v.) ʦitt m. (sg. dat. ʦĕtas 3, for 4, see s.v.) the organ of thought, the mind, intellect (Skt. citta) (cf. wudār-ʦᵒ) (L.V. 9, 11, 70; Śiv. 352, 596, 637, 693, 866, 906, 986, 1011, 1035, 1194, 1346, 1361, 1612, 1617). ¶ ʦĕtas karun 1 m.inf. to impress upon the mind (L.V. 34). For 2, see s.v. ʦĕtas 4.
or ʦitt m. the organ of thought, mind, intellect, i.q. ʦĕth 3, q.v. (cf. ʦala-ʦitta, p. 1070a, l. 37) (L.V. 22, 26, 28, 36, 67, 69, 72; Śiv. 1122, 1038, 1350, 1406, 1437, 1592, 1841, 1884).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦyūṭᵘ, f. sg. dat. ʦēcĕ; 2 p.p. ʦēcyōv; conj. part. ʦīṭith, Gr.Gr. 197), to pound, crush, reduce to powder, mince (cf. nūn ʦēṭani bĕhun, p. 640b, l. 7, wach ʦᵒ, s.v. wach 1) (Gr.Gr. 105, 115, 197). ʦīṭⁱ ʦīṭⁱ ʦhunun m.inf. thoroughly to master (some branch of learning, art, lesson, or the like) (cf. Gr.Gr. 105).

m. (sg. dat. ʦētanas), the thinking principle, the mind; thinking of, remembering, reflecting on (Śiv. 1267); (in religion) calling to mind and realizing (the nature of the Supreme) (L.V. 26, 77). Cf. ʦītan.
m. (sg. dat. as in 1), i.q. ʦaitany, q.v. ʦētana-Shiv m. the god Shiv (Śiva) in his quality of Supreme Spirit, as opposed to his more material manifestations (L.V. 79).
conj. 1 (this verb is impersonal, 1 p.p. ʦẹ̆tᵒrᵒ), to look at with indifference, to show want of appreciation for.
f. searching, seeking, i.q. ʦhöḍᵘ̈ or ʦhö̃ḍᵘ̈, q.v., but the corresponding form, ʦhāḍ, is not used (Gr.Gr. 121, 126).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhāḍanôwᵘ), to cause to seek (El. tsáḍanáwun).
m. searching for, seeking; (esp.) seeking for (an absconding criminal by the police, and so on), trailing, quest. --ʦhunun --  m.inf. to set (the police, etc.) to seek for (a criminal, etc.).
f. i.q. ʦhöḍᵘ̈, q.v. in gar-ʦhᵒ, searching in a house (p. 296a, l. 21).

or ʦhã̄ḍun conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhôḍᵘ or ʦhỗḍᵘ; f. ʦhöḍᵘ̈ or ʦhö̃ḍᵘ̈, dat. ʦhā(ã̄)jĕ ), to search for, seek for (cf. hīth ʦhāḍȧnⁱ, p. 358b, l. 3; môwᵘ ʦhᵒ, p. 611b, l. 9) (El. tsáḍun, tsánḍun, tshánḍun; Gr.Gr. 121, 126; Gr.M.; W. 136, ʦāṇḍ˚; L. 463, id.; L.V. ʦhāḍ˚, 44, 69; ʦhã̄ḍ˚, 99, 100; Śiv. ʦhāḍ˚, 97, 272, 370, 481, 517, 660, 665, 1680, 1758, etc.; Rām. ʦhāḍ˚, 181, 214, 243, 344, 379, 446, 546, 566, 640, 697, 699, 755, 901, 934, 964, 1005, 1175, 1187, 1285, 1422, 1598, 1668, 1716; K. ʦhāḍ˚, 271, 602, 615, 738, 740, 835, 845, 875, 1019, 1160; H. ʦhāḍ˚, xii, 15; YZ. ʦāḍ˚ (sic), 25, 224, 227, 238; K.Pr. ʦhã̄ḍ˚, 153, 257, 258; ʦānḍ˚ (sic), 8, 10, 46); to search (a place for something), explore (for), ransack (for), rummage (for) (L.V. ʦhāḍ˚, 3, 48; Śiv. 1214, 1419; Rām. 515; K. 677, 1143; H. ʦhã̄ḍ˚, vii, 26); to request, demand (El. tsádun, sic). Cf. ʦhanḍun, ʦhārun 1. This verb is commonly misspelt ʦāḍun, ʦānḍun, etc., when written in the Roman character. Examples are noted ab.
m. (sg. dat. ʦhāgalanas), the odour of raw flesh, or similar odour due to corruption.
m. a goat, in ʦhạgᵃla-dān m. the religious release of a goat for the prevention of evil caused by the planet Mars or the like; the sacred books describing this rite. See ʦhāwul.
or ʦhāgulᵘ m. (sg. dat. ʦhāgalas), the testicle of a sheep or goat.

m. fraud, deceit, deception, roguery, knavery (Gr.Gr. 124; Gr.M.; Śiv. 874; Rām. 944, 1417; K. 209, 1020; K.Pr. 218, 241); a clever device or expedient (Rām. 410, 585, 697, 988; K. 653, 1025; YZ. 172); a device (for accomplishing something), a machine (cf. gagar-ʦhᵒ, p. 280a, l. 12; pā̃-ʦhᵒ, p. 748a, l. 31 (f.); Rām. 44); (in a machine or tool, etc.) a pin, handle (for turning a wheel, or otherwise setting in action) (cf. atha-ʦhᵒ, p. 63b, l. 33) (Śiv. 1747, 1828, 1914). -borᵘ m. a door which by secret mechanism shuts itself so that it cannot be opened by one not in the secret. -tôrᵘ m. a kind of bolt for fastening a pair of doors opening in the centre. ¶ ʦhala bala adv. by fraud and force, by trickery, by stratagem (K. 821). -ʦhidᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. fraud, knavery, trickery, imposture (cf. Hindī chal-chidr). -ʦhidrözᵘ̈ f. fraudulent, or knavish, conduct (cf. ab.). -wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who habitually deceives, a cheat (by nature or habit), a dishonest rogue. ¶ ʦhȧlⁱ bȧlⁱ adv. by fraud or force, by stratagem, by trickery (cf. tȧlⁱ bȧlⁱ ʦhȧlⁱ, p. 996a, l. 18); whether one wills or not (K.Pr. 111, 203).

f. a jump, leap, spring (El. tshál, running). --anüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take a jump, make a leap (Śiv. 1528). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give a jump, make a single leap (generally with the idea of leaping off something) (Śiv. 709; Rām. 562, 745, 1408). --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take a leap, make a single jump (Rām. 561). --mārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to leap, to jump over (Rām. 778). --niñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take a leap, make a single jump (Rām. 548). --tārüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to jump across (something) (Rām. 553, 555). ¶ ʦhāla diñĕ f. pl. inf. to give jumps, to leap about (e.g. as in pleasure or the like) (Śiv. 267, 660, 1680). --hĕñĕ -- f. pl. inf. to take leaps, to go along leaping (Rām. 886). --mārañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to make many jumps, to jump over and over again, to progress in leaps, to leap along (Śiv. 528, 764, 820, 972, 1322, 1380, 1615; Rām. 820, 1097, 1328).
n.ag. (f. ʦhalavüñᵘ̈), a deceiver, one who is in the act of deceiving or cheating, one who is crafty (Gr.M.).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦholᵘ, f. ʦhüjᵘ̈ or ʦhȧjⁱ), to deceive, defraud, cozen, cheat (Gr.Gr. 28, 124; Gr.M.). ʦholᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦhüjᵘ̈- (or ʦhȧjⁱ-)müʦⁱ ) deceived, cheated.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhạlᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. ʦhalun, q.v. (Śiv. 189, Rām. 951, K. 1020).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhạlᵒrᵒ), i.q. ʦhalun, q.v. (K. 39, 209, 283, 289, 355).

f. that which is uneatable (e.g. ordure, filth, or polluted or dirty food). ¶ ʦhamba-khāv m. one who habitually eats ordure or the like. -ʦhŏy f. a certain skin disease, accompanied by red blisters and itching.
a form used in villages instead of ʦhunanāwun, q.v. (H. x, 13).
or ʦhŏnḍ f. searching for, seeking. Cf. ʦhã̄ḍ, ʦhöḍᵘ̈ or ʦhö̃ḍᵘ̈.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhonḍᵘ; 2 p.p. ʦhanjyōv), to search for, seek (El. ʦhándun, Rām. 594); to search (a place for something), to explore (for), ransack (for), rummage (for) (Rām. 514, 516; YZ. 134 chhanḍit for ʦhanḍith); to traverse, pass over (L.V. 26; Rām. 1325-6, 1591); to pervade (Rām. 1096); cf. ʦhāḍun, ʦhārun 1. ʦhonḍᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦhünḍᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, sg. dat. ʦhanjĕ-maʦĕ), searched for, sought, etc., as ab.
a form sometimes used in villages instead of ʦhunun, q.v. (Impve. fut. ʦhȧnⁱzi, H. xii, 16; Pres. m.sg. 3, ʦhanān chuh, xii, 17; 1 p.p. ʦhonᵘ, xii, 7).
m. protection (i.q. chapan, p. 164a, l. 17) (El. tsepan).

f. (sg. dat. ʦhã̄pi), dimness of vision (El. tsámp); mistake as to the relative equality of two things (i.e. when comparing one thing with the memory of another). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. dimness to come, to be dimsighted (dat. of person), to have dim vision (El. tsámp yun).
conj. 3, to be hidden, to hide (El. tsipun); to take refuge (with). This verb is really the same as chapun, q.v., which is, however, treated as transitive.
f. a kind of basket (described as round and deep, but according to El., s.v. tshar, a small basket which is generally carried on the head) (cf. wö̃ka-ʦhᵒ, s.v. wö̃kh) (K.Pr. 101); cf. ʦhürᵘ̈ 2.
n.ag. (f. ʦhāravüñᵘ̈), one who searches, etc. (see ʦhārun 1) (Śiv. 206, 1534).
m. (of a vessel or the like) emptiness (cf. phala-ʦhᵒ, p. 692b, l. 14); the condition of being emptied of all one's property, poverty (cf. atha-ʦhᵒ, p. 63b, l. 50).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦharyōv), (of a vessel formerly full) to become empty; met. (of a human being) to become moneyless, beggared, to lose one's fortune; to lose one's capabilities, qualities, health, or the like. ʦharyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦharyē-müʦᵘ̈), become empty, emptied; beggared; emptied of capabilities, etc.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. as ab.), to let go, drop, scatter (Rām. 1245).
adj. c.g. free from a load (lit. or fig.).
adj. c.g. an experienced swimmer, a good swimmer (El. tsánṭul, f. tsánṭal, a swimmer).
f. wages for winnowing, the cost of winnowing.

f. (sg. dat. ʦhã̄ṭi), swimming (El. tsánt, Śiv. 1755); crossing (a river or the like) by swimming. --lāyüñᵘ̈ --, f.inf. to swim (El.). --wāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf., id. (El.; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1877, caus.). ¶ ʦhã̄ta-ʦhã̄ṭh f. the swimming of a great number of people backwards and forwards; the swimming of one person backwards and forwards a great number of times (as in bathing or for amusement) (K. 946).

f. (sg. dat. ʦhaṭi), a freezing wind-storm, a blizzard (lit. and met.) (cf. bayĕ-ʦhᵒ, p. 148b, l. 23; kala-ʦhᵒ, p. 435b, l. 2; pŏhⁱ-ʦhⁱ, p. 648b, l. 7; par-ʦhᵒ, p. 751a, l. 23; shīna-ʦhᵒ, p. 885a, l. 11) (Rām. 206); a wind-storm genl. (cf. nāra-ʦhᵒ, p. 648b, l. 2) (Rām. 1610, nārañĕ ʦhaṭa = flaring flames). ¶ ʦhaṭa-rūd m. a rainfall blown about by a violent wind-storm (and not falling straight down). -shīn m. snow falling during a blizzard (i.e. blown about in violent whirls and not falling straight down). -wörᵘ̈ f. a certain kind of small boat capable of withstanding violent wind-storms (El. tsáṭawãr, 'the smallest, lightest, and swiftest of all the boats used on the Kashmīr lakes. It is so light and small that it is not at all endangered by the prevalent wind-storms which are often very violent on the Wulur and other lakes. It has but one or two boatmen in it.' L. 381 tsatawar; Śiv. 1682, 1804). Cf. contra ʦāka-wörᵘ̈, s.v. ʦākh.

f. (sg. dat. ʦhaṭi), shaking up and down (as in shaking out a garment to drive out the dust); winnowing grain (cf. atha-ʦhᵒ, p. 64a, l. 8; potᵘ-ʦhᵘ, p. 788a, l. 32) (Gr.Gr. 126); cf. ʦhraṭh. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give a winnowing (to); to examine something carefully in order to remove dirt, to pick, sift. --kaḍüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to shake out dust, etc., from anything. ¶ ʦhaṭa mārañĕ f. pl. inf. to bound up, fly up, bounce up, shoot up (cf. yāwanas ʦhᵒ māᵒ, s.v. yāwun). --ta grāyĕ mārañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to move the body in a swaggering fashion, to strut swaggeringly, bridle (due to pride in wealth, etc.). ¶ ʦhaṭi baṭi nērun m.inf. to become dexterous, adroit, skilled, skilful.

f. in the following:-- ʦhaṭh anüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to give a short preliminary boiling, stewing, or the like. ¶ ʦhaṭa-büzᵘ̈ f. slight cooking in water, slight boiling or stewing; cf. ʦhĕ-bazyunᵘ, p. 1055a, l. 21. -gŏgᵘ̈jᵘ̈ (or -gŏgᵃ̇jᵃ̇)  f. a kind of soup made by slightly stewing turnips in oil and water. -hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), green vegetables similarly stewed. -ras m. gravy extracted from meat by long cooking and flavoured only with a little salt and pepper (given to a sick person).

m. (sg. dat. chạtᵃras, abl. chạtᵃra, and so on, but pl. nom. chạthᵃr), an umbrella, esp. a large umbrella held over kings or a small silver umbrella put over the idol in a temple; a sort of umbrella made of flowers, etc., used at festivals (an ordinary umbrella is chạtᵃ̇rᵃ̇, q.v.); (?) a certain pot-herb, Megacarpœa polyandra (L. 72, chattr). ¶ chạtᵃra-būñᵃ f. an umbrella plane-tree; hence, met. a woman with many children, grandchildren, and other relations. -gulᵘ m. N. of a well-known village in Lār (Lahara) Pargana, close to Rāmarādan, for which see RT.Tr. I, 114 (iii, 467 n.). -hāl f. (sg. dat. -höjᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 69), a certain kind of rice with a soft white grain, which is very fruitful.
m. (sg. dat. ʦhạtᵃras), an umbrella, sunshade, i.q. chạthᵃr, q.v. (cf. ʦhāyĕ- ʦhạthᵃr, s.v. ʦhāy, and ʦhatradörⁱ).
m. 'one who carries an umbrella', i.e. one before whom an umbrella is carried as a mark of dignity, a king, monarch, emperor (K. 904). Borrowed from Skt. chatradhārī. Cf. chạthᵃr and ʦhạthᵃr.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhoṭᵘ; f. sg. dat. ʦhacĕ), to shake up and down; to winnow (Gr.Gr. 126); to throw up into the air, to cast abroad (L.V. 4); to do something suddenly and violently (cf. bākh ʦhaṭüñᵘ̈, p. 99b, l. 1) (Rām. 1519, 1694; K. 78); (of fire or the like) to flare up (Śiv. 1563). ʦhoṭᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦhüṭᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈, sg. dat. ʦhacĕ-maʦĕ), winnowed, etc., as ab.
or ʦhaṭüjᵘ̈ f. a fly-whisk, or chowry, used as a fan (K. 652, 1164).
m. a young shoot, sprout, scion (esp. when unexpectedly sprouting with branches from a felled tree); the young of a domestic animal (e.g. a colt, calf, lamb, kid, or the like).
or ʦhāvüjᵘ̈ f. a she-goat, a nanny-goat (cf. hurⁱ-ʦhⁱ, p. 347a, l. 22) (El. tsáwij and tsháwij; L. 460 tsáwaj, a goat). ʦhāwᵃji-mŏngurᵃ m. (f. -mŏngᵘ̈rᵘ̈), a kid.

or ʦhāwulᵘ m. (sg. dat. ʦhāwalas, the f. is ʦhāwȧjⁱ, q.v.) a he-goat, billy-goat, buck-goat (cf. buḍa ʦhᵒ, p. 85b, l. 5; wan-ʦhᵒ, s.v. wan 1) (El. tsáwúl and tsháwúl; Śiv. 313, 319, 354-5, 358, 361; H. iii, 5). ¶ ʦhāwȧlⁱ-basta f. goatskin. -māz m. goat's flesh (El. tsáwil-m˚).

f. shade, shadow (cf. gagar-ʦhᵒ, p. 280a, l. 13) (El. tsáí, tsáya; Gr.M.; Śiv. 104, 1063, 1433; Rām. 532; K.Pr. 2, 102, see bel.); a shadow (cf. potᵘ-ʦhᵘ, p. 788a, l. 40) (El. tsháe; L.V. 67; Śiv. 896, 1133, 1479; Rām. 212); a shady place; a reflected image, a reflection; resemblance; a shadowy fancy, hallucination, illusive form (Rām. 1077); a shadowy figure, an object faintly or indistinctly seen (Rām. 231); colour of the face, complexion; beauty (Śiv. 1742). zadal ʦhᵒ, 'a shade full of holes'; hence, a roof-thatch full of holes, a leaky or worn-out thatch (K.Pr. 2, 102). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. an accidental mistake of identification to occur (whether real or pretended), mistaken recognition to take place (K. 285); mental derangement to occur (believed to be due to possession by an evil spirit). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to shade; to cover, shelter (e.g. a person from rain) (K. 74). --kāsüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take away the shadow, to remove the false shame that prevents reconciliation of a person who has quarrelled with another. --zālüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. 'to burn the shadow', ceremonially to pace round a straw fire (on the conclusion of mourning for a death, or to ward off convulsions from a child or the like). ¶ ʦhāyĕ-gyutᵘ m. the illusion caused by the appearance of a shadow (esp. of something itself unseen). -holᵘ m. a hidden, or secret, place; as adj. or adv. hidden, concealed (Rām. 653) (cf. holᵘ 2). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain in the shade, to stay hidden (Rām. 1571). -ʦhạthᵃr m. 'a shade umbrella', a person of importance who supports many people.
adj. c.g. shaded, shady (Gr.M. ʦhāyi-dār, a mere matter of spelling).
f.pl. the front soft part of the thighs.
in ʦhĕ-bazyunᵘ m. (sg. dat. -bazinis), slight frying, insufficient frying (so that the taste of oil remains). Cf. ʦhaṭa-büzᵘ̈, s.v. ʦhaṭh 3.
m. the condition of being leavings; (of food or the like) uneatableness, untouchableness, impureness, abominableness, impurity (Gr.Gr. 142). Cf. ʦhyoṭᵘ.
m. (sg. dat. ʦhĕdanas), a roof, thatch; materials for roofing, thatching-grass, etc.

m. cutting, a cut, cleft, incision, scission (cf. atha-ʦhᵒ, p. 63b, l. 35, and ʦhenna-ʦhᵒ) (Gr.Gr. 123; Śiv. 984, 1619); a cutting off, severance, destruction (K. 30, 849); cf. ʦhiñ 1. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to cut, divide (in two). ¶ ʦhĕna-ʦhĕn f. separation, putting apart (combatants, and so stopping a fight).
or ʦhẹ̆ñᵃrāwun conj. 1, causal of ʦhĕnun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 174).

sometimes written ʦhĕna, adj. c.g. cut off, separated by cutting, in the following:-- --āsun -- m.inf., i.q. the next (Śiv. 1437, ʦhĕna). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become cut off (Śiv. 1340, 1439, ʦhĕna; Rām. 1501, id.) esp. (on a journey in company with others) to become separated (from the others). --karun -- m.inf. to sever; to tear asunder (K. 191, ʦhĕna). --kūṭun -- m. a short piece cut off a long string, rope, or the like. -ʦhidöy f. total severance, or dissolution, of relationship (e.g. of marriage, or the like, owing to some quarrel). -ʦhĕn f. cutting on cutting, tear on tear; (of garments or the like) the condition of being in rags and tatters; severance, or dissolution, of relationship, as ab.

or ʦhĕnnun conj. 2 (1 p.p. ʦhyonᵘ or ʦhyonnᵘ; f. ʦhë˘ñᵘ̈ or ʦhë˘ññᵘ̈; 2 p.p. ʦhĕñōv or ʦhĕññōv), to be, or become, cut, cut off, severed (cf. khōr ʦhᵒ, p. 410a, l. 25) (Gr.Gr. 123, 204; L.V. 83); to be torn, split (Gr.Gr. 174, 204; Gr.M.; Rām. 749); to be cut off (e.g. the head in decapitation) (Rām. 471); (of thread or the like) to be cut, broken (El.); to be cut off, brought to an end (cf. mūl ʦhĕnȧnⁱ, p. 567a, l. 6; pankᵃth ʦhĕnüñᵘ̈, p. 741a, l. 22; pö̃th ʦhĕnüñᵘ̈, p. 796b, l. 31; rūzi ʦhĕnun, to be cut off from one's livelihood, p. 858a, l. 35) (Śiv. 415, 1424; Rām. 768, 1052, 1340, 1749; K.Pr. 233); to become exhausted, or worn out (by a long journey, excessive labour, or the like) (Śiv. 589, 1001, 1770); to become separated, apart (Śiv. 1341, 1676, 1752, YZ. 83). ʦhyonᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦhë˘ñᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), cut, torn, cut off, etc., as ab.; exhausted, as ab. ¶ The causal of this verb is ʦhĕñᵃrāwun or ʦhĕnanāwun (Gr.Gr. 174).
or ʦhĕnᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. the blade of a small knife, the blade of a penknife (cf. shrāki-ʦhᵒ, p. 892a, l. 34).
or ʦhĕnanāwun, conj. 1, causal of ʦhĕnun, q.v. (Gr.Gr. 174).
or ʦhipal adj. c.g. (of something animate) in the habit of hiding, a skulker, stealthy, a lurker, one who lies in ambush; (of something inanimate) habitually hidden, seldom findable.

f. (sg. dat. ʦhĕpi), remaining hidden, hiding, concealment of oneself; cf. ʦhiph. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to give concealment, to be or become hidden (cf. pānas ʦhĕpa dāwañĕ, p. 263a, l. 7, Śiv. 1756; dēv ʦhĕpa diwanövin, p. 263b, l. 39, Śiv. 123; both with causal meanings) (Śiv. 913; Rām. 1007, 1089, 1273). --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take concealment, (esp. of an inanimate object) to become closely hidden. -- ʦhyunᵘ ta grāy -- m. (in order to puzzle or deceive another) hiding and revealing oneself alternately. ¶ ʦhĕpa-chörᵘ̈ f. a certain children's game, a kind of blind man's buff (in which the blindfolded player has to find another who is hidden. When he succeeds, the rôles are reversed) (Śiv. 1374, ʦhĕpa-ʦh örᵘ̈); cf. chörᵘ̈. --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to hide oneself, conceal oneself (K. 600). -ʦhĕph f. hiding oneself (wandering from one place of concealment to another) (Rām. 1426). ¶ ʦhĕpi adv. secretly, in hiding, hidden (K. 244). For ʦhĕpi ʦhĕpi, see ʦhĕpun.

conj. 3, to hide oneself, conceal oneself (noted only in the following forms):-- ¶ ʦhĕpⁱ ʦhĕpⁱ freq. part., hiding oneself frequently, or in various places; hence, as subst. f. (in this sense also ʦhĕpi ʦhĕpi), the children's game of hide and seek (K. 220). ¶ ʦhĕpith conj. part. used as adj. c.g. hidden, concealed, secret (L.V. 60). Cf. ʦhĕph.

(cf. ʦhĕwun and ʦhĕzun), adj. c.g. extinguished, quenched (YZ. 515, of sorrow). Usually found in the following:-- ʦhĕta gōmotᵘ perf. part. (f. --gömüʦᵘ̈ --), (of fire or the like) become extinguished, quenched (H. xii, 23; YZ. 524); (of a person) extinguished, i.e. famished with hunger, starving; (of a period of time) elapsed, wiped off (YZ. 7). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. (of fire) to become quenched, extinguished (cf. nār ʦhᵒ gᵒ, p. 647a, l. 24) (Rām. 58, 1028, 1784; YZ. 148). --karun -- m.inf. to quench, extinguish (El. tseta k˚; Śiv. 122, 417; Rām. 731). -kāyurᵘ m. kāyurᵘ, or wood of the Himalayan blue pine (p. 501a, l. 50), a fire of which is not lasting, but quickly goes out (see K.Pr. 101); any wood with similar properties.

m. (sg. dat. ʦhĕṭas), food fallen from the dish on to the ground at the time of eating, remnants of food, leavings of a meal, orts; cf. ʦhyoṭᵘ. --sīrᵘ̈ -- f. the portion of the lump of cotton-wool left over in the fingers on the conclusion of spinning (see sīrᵘ̈ 2). --tulᵘ -- m. the leavings of grass- fodder after a cow, or the like, has been fed. ¶ ʦhĕṭa-pholᵘ m. a grain of cooked rice or the like thrown from or fallen from the dish on to the ground at the time of eating.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦhĕṭyōv), to become impure, to become unclean, to become refuse and untouchable (Rām. 1049). ʦhĕṭyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦhĕṭyē-müʦᵘ̈), become impure, etc., as ab.
f. (sg. dat. ʦhẹ̆ṭᵃrüñᵃ), rendering impure, causing impurity to occur.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhẹ̆ṭᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. ʦhẹ̆ṭᵃrun, q.v. ʦhẹ̆ṭᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. ʦhẹ̆ṭᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q.ʦhẹ̆ṭᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, s.v. ʦhẹ̆ṭᵃrun, q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhẹ̆ṭᵒrᵒ), to render impure, to cause something previously pure to become impure, to defile (cf. ös ʦhᵒ, p. 46b, l. 28) (Gr.Gr. 7, K. 136); met. to render (pure food or the like) impure (by putting it into the mouth and eating it). ʦhẹ̆ṭᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. ʦhẹ̆ṭᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), rendered impure (as ab.).
f. (of something previously pure), the condition of being, or having become, impure or unclean (Gr.Gr. 142, spelt ˚yārᵘ̈z).
adj. (f. ʦhĕṭⁱyārĕñ), one who deals in impure or unclean food, a seller, or maker of such; one whose conduct is impure or unclean.
f. the condition of being impure or unclean (Gr.Gr. 142).
m. (of fire) the being on the point of being extinguished, the being nearly out.
f. (of rain or the like) cessation (cf. rūda-ʦhᵒ, p. 826b, l. 16). ʦhĕviñĕn adv. at the time of such cessation (cf. rūda-ʦhᵒ, p. 826b, l. 18).
m. (of rain or the like) cessation (cf. rūda-ʦhᵒ, p. 826b, l. 21). ʦhĕwawạñĕn adv. at the time of cessation (cf. p. 826b, l. 23).

f. the being extinguished, extinguishment (cf. ʦnāra-hᵒ, p. 648b, l. 11); (of rage, hunger, thirst, or the like) allayment, appeasement, abatement, cessation (cf. dᵃh-ʦhᵃ, p. 198a, l. 16; dᵃha-ʦhᵃ, p. 198b, l. 28; rūda-ʦhᵒ, p. 826b, l. 24; tapa-ʦhᵒ, p. 1014b, l. 10).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦhĕvyōv), (of fire) to be extinguished (cf. nār ʦhᵒ, p. 647a, l. 25); (of rage or the like) to be allayed, appeased; cf. ʦhĕta and ʦhĕzun. ʦhĕvyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦhĕvyē-müʦᵘ̈), extinguished; allayed.
f. (sg. dat. ʦhẹ̆wᵃrüñᵃ), the act of extinguishing (a fire or the like) (cf. nāra-ʦhᵒ, p. 648b, l. 7); allaying (rage or the like).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhẹwᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. ʦhẹ̆wᵃrun, ab., q.v. (cf. nār ʦhᵒ, p. 547a, l. 28). ʦhẹ̆wᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. ʦhẹ̆wᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), i.q. ʦhẹ̆wᵒrᵒ-motᵒ, ab., q.v.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhẹ̆wᵒrᵒ), to extinguish (a fire, conflagration, or the like) (Gr.Gr. 7); to allay, appease (rage, etc.), quench (thirst), etc. (Gr.M.). ʦhẹ̆wᵒrᵒ-motᵒ perf. part. (f. ʦhẹ̆vᵘ̈rᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), extinguished (by someone), as ab.; appeased (by someone), as ab.

f. a kind of thatching grass (Śiv. 338). ¶ ʦhĕyĕ-ḍēmb m. an artificial or floating island on which this grass grows spontaneously. -gorᵘ m. a professional thatcher. -horᵘ m. a long thin strip of wood (cf. hürᵘ̈ 1, of which this is a masculine form), used in the tying of a thatched roof. -kān m. an arrow made from a stem of this grass. -lürᵘ̈ f. a thatched house (of brick or stone and two or three stories high). -nār m. a fire of this grass (which burns fiercely and is extinguished with difficulty). -pahörᵘ̈ f. a thatched hut. -tulᵘ m. a single stem of this grass; a very small amount of this grass.
conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦhĕzyōv), to become extinguished, (of daylight) to fade away, become extinct (L.V. 22). Cf. ʦhĕta and ʦhĕwun.

m. cutting off, cessation, stoppage (of something going on steadily, e.g. a river, a flow of water or of speech, income, progression of a person walking, and so on). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. such a cessation to occur.
f. in ʦhĕnna-ʦhidöy, s.v. ʦhĕnna. Cf. ʦhid.
f. in ʦhala-ʦhidᵘ̈rᵘ̈ and ʦhidrözᵘ̈ f. in ʦhala-ʦhidrözᵘ̈, both s.v. ʦhal, q.v. Cf. Hindī chidr.
in ʦhih ʦhih m. dandling (a baby), i.q. ʦhīh, bel.
f. dandling (a baby), tossing it playfully up and down, i.q. ʦhih ʦhih ab.

m. (sg. dat. ʦhilivis), an artful pretext (made up for bringing an accusation against some one). --raṭun -- m.inf. (in picking holes in a person's character) to seize upon such a pretext (for an accusation).

f.pl. faint or dull sunlight, dusk. -milawan f. (sg. dat. -milavüñᵘ̈), the union of the two dusks (evening and nightfall), twilight. --milawun -- adv. at the time of twilight. --milawạñĕn -- adv. id. (used esp. with verbs indicating coming or the like).
m. a cut (caused by a knife or the like). Cf. ʦhĕn.

onomat. the explosive spluttering sound caused by water, gravy, or similar liquid being added in cooking to heated oil, ghī, or the like; cf. ʦhᵃr. -baz m. cooking involving such spluttering (e.g. when gravy is added to hot oil as ab.). See bazun 1.
ʦhīnʦhⁱ, ʦhīnʦhᵘ̈ and ʦhūnʦhᵘ, see ʦhī˜ʦh and ʦhyū̃ʦhᵘ 1 and 2.
f. (sg. dat. ʦhipi), i.q. ʦhĕph, q.v.
f. (sg. dat. ʦhī˜ʦhi), a woman very slim from birth, a naturally slender woman (cf. ʦhyū̃ʦhᵘ 2).
m. (of a human being) natural slimness, slenderness (cf. ʦhyū̃ʦhᵘ 2).
m. a thin stick, a twig (cf. ʦhyū̃ʦhᵘ 2).

m. shortness (esp. shorter than usual, e.g. a man shorter than usual, a rope too short, a short tree which is usually tall, and so on), dwarfness, undersizedness (cf. atha-ʦhᵒ, p. 63b, l. 29) (El. tsŏchar; W. 112, ṯs̱o˙char); abridgedness, compressedness, conciseness, brevity (Śiv. 1598). Cf. ʦhọ̆ṭᵘ.

or ʦhö̃ḍᵘ̈ (sometimes written ʦhöḍ, ʦhöḍ) f. (sg. dat. ʦhājĕ or ʦhã̄jĕ), searching for, seeking (cf. atha-ʦhᵒ, p. 63b, l. 31) (Gr.Gr. 121, 126); searching (a place for something), exploring (for), rummaging, ransacking (for) (cf. gar-ʦhᵒ, p. 296a, l. 19). Cf. ʦhã̄ḍ, ʦhanḍ or ʦhŏnḍ. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to institute a search, to search (something for something), to hunt for (in) (esp. of a thief or the like searching in receptacles, etc., for plunder).

m. a lock of hair worn on the crown of the head of a Hindū, a topknot (cf. hanga-ʦhᵒ, p. 338b, l. 44) (El. tsog, Śiv. 124); the arrangement of the hair, plaited with silk, worn hanging down behind by Ksh. girls (El.); the tasselled head of a cob of Indian corn or maize. --bŏḍun -- m.inf. 'the topknot to be sunken', hence, to become utterly unworthy (owing to inherent viciousness and consequent disrepute). ¶ ʦhögⁱ-laṭⁱrⁱ f. 'a topknot-tail', hence, a long topknot (Śiv. 124). ʦhögⁱ-monḍⁱ m. the root (or base) of a top- knot (where it joins the skull).

m. i.q. ʦhōh, q.v. in the following: ʦhŏh dinⁱ m. pl. inf. to act zealously and happily, to apply oneself heart and soul (to any task) (Rām. 791, 794); esp. to seek with zeal, zealously and unceasingly to search for (Śiv. 341, 493; Rām. 514); to roam through, to wander ceaselessly through and through (Śiv. 422); to act fearlessly and without restraint, to give free rein (to one's feelings, etc.) (cf. lŏkacyāras ʦhŏh dinⁱ, p. 517b, l. 27). --dyunᵘ -- m. sg.inf. to give happiness, to cause to feel unrestrained rapture (L.V. 44). --mārȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to act fearlessly and without restraint.

m. after entering into the midst of any business (e.g. into a position of authority, or into expenditure of money) acting fearlessly and without restraint, becoming zealously and busily engaged in any task; happiness, pleasure, rest in the midst of occupation (K.Pr. 59, 171). Cf. ʦhŏh.
adj. c.g. filled with conceit in one's own shrewdness, proud of one's own cleverness.

adj. c.g. (as subst., f. ʦhŏkaladiñ), blemished or disfigured by marks of scorching or parching, (esp. of food) spoiled and made useless (by this cause); filled with conceit in one's own shrewdness, proud of one's own cleverness (Gr.Gr. 135, sly).

m. (sg. dat. ʦhŏkas), semi-combustion, (of food, or the like) the being half-burnt; speechlessness (cf. ʦhŏkun) (Gr.Gr. 123); conceit in one's own shrewdness, pride in one's own cleverness (Gr.Gr. 135, slyness). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to burn or heat half (i.e. partially). --khyonᵘ -- m.inf. (of food being cooked or fried) to be half cooked, to be partly cooked, to be partly burnt. --lagun -- m.inf. partial, or slight, burning or parching to occur (to something); burning or harrowing (of the heart or feelings) to be felt (due to grief, sickness, hunger, or the like). ¶ ʦhŏka-shikār m. killing for sport (and not for food). -tikh m. (sg. dat. -tikas), a small piece of goat's flesh toasted (over burning charcoal, and not thoroughly cooked).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦhŏkyōv), (at the beginning of a discussion, or when busy in some work, or when being instructed or trained, and so on) to become obstructed, stopped, hindered, to become powerless, become silenced, speechless (Gr.Gr. 122). ʦhŏkyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦhŏkyē-müʦᵘ̈), obstructed, hindered, as ab.; (of a human being, horse, or the like) (in studying, carrying out some work, walking, or the like) stopped, hindered, unable to proceed.
f. apprehension, fear, terror (esp. of something unseen or expected).
f. secret knowledge (by which the accomplishment of some difficult task is rendered easy), private experience.
or (q.v.) ʦhyondᵘ m. a mark of punctuation, the mark.

f. silence, muteness (El. tshŏpah and tsŏpah; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1598, 1639; K.Pr. 219). -dab m. keeping silence (esp. under the influence of fear or the like). -dam m. obstinate silence (even under provocation), obstinate muteness. --karüñᵘ̈ --, f.inf. to keep silence (El.; Gr.M.; W. 88 ʦo˙pah karaṇⁱ; Śiv. 81, 1638; Rām. 1465; YZ. 83, 439, 452). --karith --, conj. part., as adv. silently, without saying anything (Gr.M.; H. xii, 4). ¶ ʦhŏpi sg. obl. by silence, esp. by silent meditation (L.V. 2). -manthᵃr m. the mystic formula of silence, i.e. the Śaiva mystic formula (Skt. ajapamantra) in which no words are uttered, but which consists only in a number of exhalations and inhalations (L.V. 40).
m. taciturnity, slowness of speech, reticence; (in work or action) slowness, slackness (cf. atha-ʦhᵒ, p. 63b, l. 44).
f. secret conduct, secret, or underhand, dealing.
adj. (f. ʦhŏ̈pᵘ̈), habitually silent, taciturn, slow of speech (El, tsŏpah, dumb; Gr.Gr. 27; K.Pr. 219); slow in action, slack at work (cf. atha-ʦhᵒ, p. 63b, l. 42).

adj. (f. ʦhürᵘ̈ 1), empty, void, devoid (of), deprived (of), free, or freed (from), without (cf. atha-ʦhᵒ, p. 63b, l. 45; phala-ʦhᵒ, p. 692b, l. 10; ruma-ʦhᵒ, p. 834a, l. 23) (Gr.Gr. 10; Gr.M.; Śiv. 1806; K.Pr. 219, 239); empty (of property), beggared. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. (of something previously full) to become empty, to be emptied. ¶ ʦhariy (Rām. 364) or ʦhoruy (Rām. 986) uselessly, in vain; only, merely, nothing but (K.Pr. 132, ʦhurui).
in ʦhĕpa-ʦhörᵘ̈, Śiv. 1374. See ʦhĕpa-chörᵘ̈, col. a, l. 7.

m. a short stick, club, walking stick (according to El. s.v. tsoṭa, this is the word employed in Śrīnagar, elsewhere ḍã̄g, q.v. is more usual) (cf. ranga-ʦhᵒ, p. 837a, l. 34) (H. iii, 1, 2); a pestle.
m. one who is very dwarfish, a tiny dwarf, a pigmy.
m. a very small dwarf, a pigmy, Lilliputian.

m. (sg. dat. ʦhŏṭas), rubbish, sweepings, dust, ashes, or the like (cf. kala-ʦhᵒ, p. 435b, l. 6; wŏṭa-bari ʦhŏṭa-borᵘ, s.v. wŏṭh); a place where such sweepings are collected, a rubbish-heap, a dust-heap, ashpit (El. tsoṭ). Cf. ʦhŏ̈ṭᵘ̈ 2 and ʦhyoṭᵘ. ¶ ʦhŏṭa-pachin m. 'a rubbish-bird', one who is unworthy of respect, a person of no account among his fellows. -phakīr m. (f. -phȧkⁱröñⁱ), 'a rubbish-beggar', one who is in extreme indigence, or in great distress. -shikār m. 'a chase for rubbish', a pursuit of which the result is worthless. -yĕch m. (sg. dat. -yĕchas), 'a rubbish-demon', one who goes about, or occupies himself amid refuse and rubbish.

f. a little, or dwarfish, woman (f. of ʦhọ̆ṭᵘ, q.v., used only with reference to human beings, Gr.Gr. 35). --ʦhö -- m. the name used in schools for the letter cha (or ʦha) when written in the Śāradā character.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦhŏṭyōv), to become small or short, to turn out to be too short (e.g. a garment when being tried on) (El. tshuṭun, to be low; Śiv. 1565); to be shortened, cut off (cf. pō̃th ʦhŏṭüñᵘ̈, p. 796b, l. 34). ʦhŏṭyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦhŏṭyē-müʦᵘ̈), become short, shortened.
f. (sg. dat. ʦhọ̆tᵃrüñᵃ), making shorter, abridging, condensing (Gr.Gr. 121).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhọ̆ṭᵃrôwᵃ), i.q. ʦhọ̆ṭᵃrun, q.v. ʦhọ̆ṭᵃrôwᵃ-motᵃ perf. part. (f. ʦhọ̆ṭᵃrövᵃ-müʦᵃ), shortened, abridged, condensed.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhọ̆ṭᵒrᵒ), to make (something long) short, to shorten, abridge, condense, abbreviate (Gr.Gr. 7, 121). ʦhọ̆ṭᵃrith āsun m.inf. (of the head of a family) to have to do with a very small number of members of the family, (of a thing) to belong to a very small group, to be one of a very small number.

sometimes written ʦhoṭᵘ adj. (f. ʦhŏ̈ṭᵘ̈ 1 sg. dat. ʦhŏcĕ), short, not long, small (cf. atha-ʦhᵒ, p. 64a, l. 1; khōra-ʦhᵒ, p. 410b, l. 14; nāla-ʦhᵒ, p. 632a, l. 32; nȧrⁱ-ʦhⁱ, p. 649a, l. 25; narĕ-ʦhᵒ, p. 650a, l. 11) (El. tsouṭ, tsút, K.Pr. 219 (f. sg. dat.)); (of an animate being) short, dwarfish, low, the reverse of tall (Gr.Gr. 35, see ʦhŏṭiñ; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 257); too short, not long enough, too small (Gr.M.; Rām. 743; K.Pr. 156, ʦuṭ). --goṭᵘ -- m. darkness or (temporary) blindness (due to terror, agony, or the like). --karun --, m.inf. to shorten (El. tsauṭ karun). --mọ̆ṭᵘ -- adj. (f. ʦhŏ̈ṭᵘ̈ mö̆ṭᵘ̈), short and fat, short and stout, squat (cf. ʦhọ̆ṭᵘ̈rᵘ̈ mọ̆ṭᵘ̈rᵘ̈, p. 1063b, l. 49). ¶ ʦhŏṭi ganḍa raṭun m.inf. to seize with a little knot, to interrupt or stop another in midst of work (e.g. by asking difficult questions).

f. (sg. dat. ʦhŏcĕ), refuse, offal (i.q. ʦhŏṭh, q.v.) in the following:-- ʦhŏci-ʦūr m. a thief of offal; hence, a rude boorish low-caste fellow, one who has no reputable employment. ¶ ʦhŏcĕn sūr kāsun m.inf. to console oneself in difficulties with pleasant hopes.
f. that which is short, dwarfish (of a woman, or of any feminine inan. object). --mọ̆ṭᵘ̈rᵘ̈ -- f. that which is short and stout (as ab.). Cf. ʦhọ̆ṭᵘ mọ̆ṭᵘ, p. 1062a, l. 47.
f. in ʦhamba-ʦhŏy, p. 1058a, l. 45, q.v.
m. emptiness, hollowness (e.g. as in the case of a walnut with no kernel) (cf. atha-ʦhᵒ, p. 64a, l. 13) (Gr.Gr. 141; Śiv. 1474, 1753, 1806). Cf. ʦhọ̆ʦᵘ.
m. lightness, relief from a burden (of the bodily form of man or beast); (esp.) relief (from anxiety or the like).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhö̃ʦhanôwᵘ), to cause to be lightened, to relieve from a burden (Gr.Gr. 171).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦhö̃ʦhanyōv), (of an animate being) to become lightened (by the removal of a burden) (Gr.Gr. 171); met. to become lightened (by the removal of anxiety or the like). ʦhö̃ʦhanyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦhö̃ʦhanyē-müʦᵘ̈), lightened, as ab.
adj. (f. ʦhö̃ʦhüñᵘ̈), lightened, become light (by the removal of a burden, lit. or met.).

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦhŏʦyōv, Gr.Gr. 226) to become hollow, empty, of no internal strength (esp. of something previously solid) (Gr.Gr. 226); met. to become of no value, to become deprived of wealth, of virtue, etc. ʦhŏʦyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦhŏʦyē-müʦᵘ̈), become hollow, as ab.

adj. (f. ʦhŏ̈ʦᵘ̈), (of something, e.g. a fruit, apparently solid and full) empty, hollow, unsound, worthless (cf. atha-ʦhᵒ, p. 64a, l. 11) (Gr.Gr. 141; Śiv. 1551, 1639, 1667, 1779); met. deprived of all one's virtue, property, or the like; an empty walnut, a walnut with no kernel (cf. the next) (K.Pr. 229). ¶ ʦhŏʦa-kônᵘ m. (f. -köñᵘ̈), utterly empty, worthless, without any value (of result, qualities, etc.); esp. an empty walnut, a walnut with no kernel (K.Pr. 156, 229, 236); cf. kônᵘ 5. ʦhŏʦa-könⁱ mashwara m.pl. worthless advice.

m. (sg. dat. ʦhraṭas), tossing or rolling on the ground in pain, a throe, convulsion (cf. mōtȧnⁱ ʦhᵒ, p. 604b, l. 8) (El. tsrát, f. trembling); cf. ʦhaṭh 2. --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to toss or roll on the ground (in pain or through laziness). --lagȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. throes to attack (a person), pain or fretting (due to unwillingness to carry out another's orders) to be felt. -lāṭh m. (sg. dat. ʦhraṭas-lāṭas), rolling and turning (as a symptom of pain or of laziness). ¶ ʦhraṭa-ʦhraṭh f. (sg. dat. -ʦhraṭi), rolling or tossing in pain; met. being distraught or at one's wit's end.

or (vill.) ʦhanᵒ, q.v. conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhunanôwᵘ), to cause to be thrown or cast (Śiv. 67, of a net; H. x, 13, ʦhan˚); to cause to be thrown away (Rām. 1587); to cause to be clothed, or clothe another (El. tsunanáwun); and so in other causal meanings of ʦhunun, q.v.

or (vill., as in H. xii., 17; K.Pr. 92, 146, 262) ʦhanun conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦhunᵘ, f. ʦhuñᵘ̈; 2 p.p. ʦhuñōv. In books edited in the Roman character, this verb is sometimes (e.g. K.Pr. 26, 44) incorrectly written ʦunun), to throw down, hurl down, drop (cf. ḍula ʦhᵒ, p. 212a, l. 35; tal-kun ʦhᵒ, p. 995b, l. 50) (El. ʦunun, Śiv. 754, YZ. 118-9); to cast or fling away (cf. mal-katürᵘ̈ ʦhunüñᵘ̈, p. 563b, l. 47; sĕkh ʦhunüñᵘ̈, p. 904b, l. 39; ʦhĕṭⁱ-wôñⁱ ʦhunun, s.v. ʦhyoṭᵘ) (Rām. 1037); to leave, abandon (Rām. 1167, 1622); to throw, fling, cast, hurl (cf. kŏli ʦhᵒ, p. 437b, l. 44; sᵃsar ʦhunüñᵘ̈, p. 942a, l. 14) (Gr.M.; L. 464, ʦunnun; Rām. 692, 787, 790, 1319, 1588; YZ. 287; K.Pr. 114, 146); to put down, drop down, lower (cf. bŏn ʦhᵒ, p. 110b, l. 12); to put down, set, arrange (cf. byonᵘ ʦhᵒ, p. 151a, l. 29; khŏras-pĕṭh khŏr ʦhᵒ, p. 409b, l. 39; phakas wurun ʦhᵒ, p. 689a, l. 33; pāna-môrᵘ ʦhᵒ, p. 736a, l. 4; shrukᵘ ʦhᵒ, p. 892a, l. 6) (H. v, 6); darwāza ʦhunun wothᵘ, to throw a door open (Rām. 1734); ¶ to shed, pour (cf. kŏng-ṭūrᵘ̈ ʦhunüñᵘ̈, p. 456b, l. 24); to eject, vomit (cf. thŏka ʦhunañĕ, p. 973a, l. 31) (K.Pr. 12, 262); ¶ to place, or lay, before, submit, present (cf. nētra- katha ʦhunañĕ, p. 662a, l. 19); to put (on), impose (upon) (cf. bār ʦhᵒ, p. 117a, l. 12) (YZ. 551, K.Pr. 153); to put on, throw on, don (a garment, ornaments, etc.) (cf. basta ʦhunüñᵘ̈, p. 135b, l. 2; kapar ʦhunȧnⁱ, p. 463b, l. 44; nölⁱ ʦhᵒ, p. 633a, ll. 2, 6; yōñĕ ʦhᵒ) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 163, 194, 360, 793, 814, 891, 1709, 1794; Rām. 189, 512, 715; K. 483; H. v, 9; viii, 10; x, 4; xii, 7; K.Pr. 26, 102); to put, deposit, place (cf. phyorᵘ ʦhᵒ, p. 721b, l. 28; rachani ʦhᵒ, p. 824b, l. 45; tᵃʦhi añĕma ʦhᵒ, p. 1046a, l. 25) (Gr.Gr. 17; H. viii, 6; x, 7; YZ. 267; K.Pr. 26, 92, 44); ¶ to scatter, sow broadcast (cf. lūṭh ʦhᵒ, p. 538a, l. 26; pāh ʦhunüñᵘ̈, p. 683b, l. 39) (Śiv. 691); to sow (discord, etc.) (cf. phās ʦhᵒ, p. 711b, l. 8; phë̆ṭᵘ̈ ʦhunüñᵘ̈, p. 715a, l. 32; phūṭh ʦhᵒ, p. 717a, l. 21; ṭhūs ʦhᵒ, p. 985b, l. 17); ¶ to thrust, thrust into (cf. atha ʦhᵒ, p. 63b, l. 38; mushᵉ̆th ʦhunüñᵘ̈, p. 599a, l. 10) (Rām. 963, 1509); ¶ to apply, set in action, wield (cf. cĕth ʦhᵒ, p. 171b, l. 31; nilyuwᵘ ʦhᵒ, p. 635a, l. 19; rachun ʦhᵒ, p. 824b, l. 8; sĕki kroʦhᵘ ʦhᵒ, p. 905a, l. 7; ṭhukh ʦhᵒ, p. 973b, l. 12) (Śiv. 1531; K. 209, 822; H. v, 6); to cause, occasion, produce, excite (cf. bam ʦhᵒ, p. 106b, l. 43; būth ʦhᵒ, p. 141a, l. 37; cōka ʦhᵒ, p. 169a, l. 16; dab ʦhᵒ, p. 181a, l. 42; dag ʦhunüñᵘ̈, p. 193b, l. 3; dŏkh ʦhᵒ, p. 206a, l. 41; dōr ʦhunüñᵘ̈, p. 237a, l. 11; jogᵘ ʦhᵒ, p. 371b, l. 3; khrang ʦhᵒ, p. 415b, l. 10; lār ʦhᵒ, p. 530a, l. 22; muh ʦhᵒ, p. 553b, l. 16; muhim ʦhᵒ, p. 555a, l. 7; piʦh ʦhunüñᵘ̈, p. 807b, l. 15; shĕhalath ʦhunüñᵘ̈, p. 857b, l. 13; thörᵘ̈ ʦhunüñᵘ̈, p. 983a, l. 29; ṭᵃkh ʦhunüñᵘ̈, p. 991b, l. 20; ʦhāḍav ʦhᵒ, p. 1056b, l. 30; vĕshād ʦhᵒ; vĕʦhay ʦhᵒ) (Rām. 267); ¶ to carry out (hurriedly or quickly) (cf. thāh ʦhunüñᵘ̈, p. 971b, l. 30; wŏṭh ʦhᵒ) (Rām 747; H. ii, 9; iii, 4; K.Pr. 109). ¶ With the conjunctive or frequentative participle of another verb this verb forms an intensive compound, usually with an idea of violence, hurry, or totality (cf. bakith ʦhᵒ, p. 102a, l. 23; chakith ʦhᵒ, p. 160a, l. 16; chalith ʦhᵒ, p. 161b, l. 7; dọ̆bᵃrith ʦhᵒ, p. 184b, l. 46; dith ʦhᵒ, p. 204a, l. 1; dᵃnith ʦhᵒ, p. 212a, l. 12; ḍuvith ʦhᵒ, p. 263b, l. 26; kaḍith ʦhᵒ, p. 386a, l. 32; muhith ʦhᵒ, p. 555b, l. 6; nĕngalith ʦhᵒ, p. 643a, l. 30; napith ʦhᵒ, p. 645b, l. 48; pihⁱ pihⁱ ʦhᵒ, p. 699a, l. 14; phirⁱ phirⁱ ʦhᵒ, p. 707b, l. 12; phirith ʦhᵒ, p. 707b, ll. 26, 31; p. 715a, l. 27; phuṭᵃrith ʦhᵒ, p. 719a, l. 27; pushᵉ̆rith ʦhᵒ, p. 782b, l. 33; pushᵉ̆rövith ʦhᵒ, p. 782b, l. 44; rᵃsavith ʦhᵒ, p. 844b, l. 29; hodᵘ tulith ʦhᵒ, p. 970b, l. 49; ṭakith ʦhᵒ, p. 993b, l. 37; trövith ʦhᵒ, p. 1034b, l. 28; ʦöpith ʦhᵒ, s.v. ʦāpun; ʦīṭⁱ ʦīṭᵘ ʦhᵒ, s.v. ʦēṭun; wuḍövith ʦhᵒ; wölith ʦhᵒ, s.v. wālun) (Gr.M.; Śiv. 124, 1625, 1635; Rām. 16, 148, 232, 257, 382, 413, 703, 711, 898, 947, 985, 1163, 1165, 1310, 1368, 1376, 1391, 1414, 1499, 1532, 1608, 1631, 1674, 1693, 1695; K. 124, 244; H. ii, 5; iii, 5; viii, 7, 10; x, 9; xii, 4, 15-7). ¶ ʦhunan-wôlᵘ n.ag. (f. -wājĕñ), one who throws down, etc., as ab.; esp. a dissolute fellow, a habitual adulterer.
f. a kind of open basket (cf. atha-ʦhᵒ, p. 63b, l. 47; ruma-ʦhᵒ, p. 834a, l. 36) (Gr.Gr. 10). Cf. ʦhar.
another spelling of ʦhyū̃ʦhᵘ 1 and 2, q.v.

or (q.v.) ʦhondᵘ m. (sg. dat. ʦhĕndis), a certain mark of punctuation, the mark equivalent to our semi-colon. ¶ ʦhĕndⁱ m.pl. affectionate respect, politeness. -jōrāh m. a certain mark of punctuation, the double mark. equivalent to our full stop. --karȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to show great politeness and hospitality. --ta wāv -- m. affectionate politeness.

(f. ʦhë˘ñᵘ̈), 1 p.p. of ʦhĕnun, q.v. Used --˚, in the sense of 'cut', 'cut off', as in ösa-ʦhᵒ, p. 46b, l. 32; atha-ʦhᵒ, p. 64a, l. 14; māwȧlⁱ-hʦⁱ, p. 611b, l. 28; nȧrⁱ-ʦhⁱ, p. 649a, l. 26; narĕ-ʦhᵒ, p. 650a, l. 12; nasta-ʦhᵒ, p. 658b, l. 12; nyŏṭha-ʦhᵒ, p. 674a, l. 31; pakha-ʦhᵒ, p. 725a, ll. 21, 33; para-ʦhᵒ, p. 751a, l. 43; wuṭha-ʦhᵒ, s.v. wuṭh 1.

adj. (f. ʦhë˘ṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. ʦhĕcĕ), (of food) remaining over (after eating) (and hence defiled) (cf. gagar-ʦhᵒ, p. 280a, l. 16; kāwa- ʦhᵒ, p. 495a, l. 34; yẹ̆cha-ʦhᵒ, s.v. yẹ̆ch) (El. ʦhuṭ, m. remainder; Gr.Gr. 26, 142; Gr.M.; H. x, 3, 5, 12; K.Pr. 220, ʦhuṭ); cf. ʦhŏ̈ṭᵘ̈ 2 and ʦhĕṭh. ¶ ʦhĕṭⁱ-khāv m. (f. -khāvĕñ), one who is habitually an eater of (another's) leavings. -wā̃ḍulᵘ m. a large tub (see ḍulᵘ 1) for receiving water that has been rendered impure (e.g. by being used for washing up dishes after food, for rinsing out the mouth, or the like). -wôñᵘ m. water that has been rendered impure, as ab. (K.Pr. 101). -wôñᵘʦhunun m. inf. to throw out the dirty water; to cast away like dirty water; hence, to destroy or render valueless another's work when on the point of success or completion.

m. (sg. dat. ʦhīlis), N. of a certain game, in which a rope is attached to a stake fixed in the ground. The player holds the other end of the rope and runs round the post, while the others try to hit him with sticks. For a fuller description, see K.Pr. 44, where the game is called ʦihul.
m. (sg. dat. ʦhinis), a goldsmith's cutting instrument or chisel (cf. ʦhĕph ʦhyunᵘ ta grāy, p. 1061a, l. 3).
or (also written ʦhū̃ʦhᵘ) m. (sg. dat. ʦhī˜ʦhis), a man of very low or degraded caste, an outcaste (said to be so vile as to feed on dog's flesh). ʦhī˜ʦhⁱ-bāy f. his wife.
or (also written ʦhū̃ʦhᵘ) adj. (f. ʦhī˜ʦhᵘ̈ or ʦhī˜ʦh), naturally thin and slender; (of something inanimate) naturally slender, thin, fine. Cf. ʦhī˜ʦh.

in ʦhᵃr ʦhᵃr m. the explosive spluttering sound caused by water or the like being added in cooking to heated oil or ghī; cf. ʦhiñ 2. ʦhᵃra-ʦhᵃra m. the being consumed by pity (e.g. at the spectacle of another's misery).
m. pure spirit (Skt. ʦit) and joy (Skt. ānanda); hence, as a name of the Deity (the Self which is compact of) pure spirit and joy (a word borrowed from Skt. cidānanda) (L.V. 6).

m.pl. (but sometimes ʦingara, f.pl.), leaping, bounding (in joy). --ʦānȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. 'to cause jumps to enter'; hence, to terrify or intimidate (a child, servant, or the like, by frequent beatings, scoldings, or the like). ¶ ʦingara tulañĕ f. pl. inf. to leap or jump for joy.
f. (sg. dat. ʦinti), care, anxiety; i.q. ʦĕntā, q.v. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to care (for, gen., as in cyöñᵘ̈ ʦᵒ karān, caring for thee) (L.V. 72).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦīñᵉ̆rôwᵉ̆), i.q. ʦīñᵉ̆run, q.v.; cf. Gr.Gr. 174 (El. to point out, to show).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦīñᵒrᵒ), to cause to be known by a sign, hint, point out, indicate by a hint, wink, or the like (caus. of ʦēnun 2. Cf. ʦēnanāwun, Gr.Gr. 174).
f. to nip, or pinch, between the nails of the thumb and forefinger.
adj. (f. ʦīrivᵘ̈), made of apricot-wood (cf. ʦīrⁱ-hüṭⁱ, p. 1079b, l. 9).
f. a bird (El. tsíri). Cf. ʦürᵘ̈ 4.
f. sense, consciousness; remembering, reflecting on some previous occurrence. Cf. ʦētun 1.

or ʦitth (Gr.Gr. 70) f. (sg. dat. ʦiti, ʦitti, Gr.Gr. 70), sudden cramp in the muscles of the back and legs (arising in mountain-climbing, running, sudden excitement, etc.), loss of use of the limbs (Gr.Gr. 13, 70). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such cramp to occur (K.Pr. 36, translated 'to tumble down', apparently incorr. for ʦē̃th, q.v.).

m. (sg. dat. ʦitras 1, for 2, see ʦitᵃr). N. of the twelfth luni-solar month (in Skt. Caitra) (March-April) (El. tsitar, m., for Hindūs, and tsithar, f., for Musulmāns; W. 107 tsitạr; Rām. 1108g; K.Pr. 128, 171, 220). ¶ ʦitra-thŏsⁱ m.pl. large lumps of snow or hail falling (like those that usually fall in this month). -wôñᵘ m. the snow-water that comes down in the mountain torrents in this month (looked upon as very pure, cool and, owing to its origin among the mountain plant wholesome).
f. (sg. dat. ʦitri), N. of the fourteenth lunar mansion, in Skt. citrā.

f. a kind of pickle or sauce, 'chutnee' (the solid ingredients of which are chopped up or reduced to a pulp and retained in the vinegar). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to reduce to a state of chutnee, to reduce to a pulp, mash, destroy (lit. and fig.). --gaʦhüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to be mashed, reduced to pulp like the ingredients of chutnee (e.g. of a worm or a beetle trodden upon).
f. any condiment made with something pounded and mixed with spices (cf. caṭiñ and ʦyūṭᵘ).
f. N. of a friend and companion of Wushā (Uṣā), daughter of Bānāsŏr (Bāṇa) (K. 803, 805, 807).
m. (in painting a wall or the like) the parts intentionally left unpainted (e.g. in making a pattern).

m. (sg. dat. ʦitras 2, for 1, see ʦithᵃr 1), a picture, painting, delineation. ʦitra-kār m. 'the deed of a picture' (as if a picture had come to life and done something), see mōni ʦitra-kār, p. 574a, l. 8.
m. division into four, dividing into four shares.
m. a fourth share, a fourth part, a quarter.
m., i.q. cō̃ca, q.v., a wooden-handled ladle. ʦō̃ca-ṭaph m. (sg. dat. -ṭapas), a blow dealt with a ladle.
card. (pl. dat. ʦŏdāhan), fourteen (Gr.Gr. 76, 83; Śiv. 525, 855; Rām. 7, 535).

f. (sg. dat. ʦŏdüshᵘ̈), the fourteenth day of a lunar fortnight (cf. hāra-ʦᵒ, p. 244a, l. 25; lāwasa-ʦᵒ, p. 542b, l. 13; trāla-ʦᵒ, p. 1025b, ll. 12 ff.; yĕchiñĕ-ʦᵒ, s.v. yĕchiñ) (Śiv. 525; Rām. 187, 379, 1083, 1655, 1771). ʦŏdüshᵘ̈-hondᵘ̈ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or produced in the above.

m.pl., the form taken by ʦŏdāh 1, fourteen, in multiplication, as in kāh ʦŏdöhⁱ akh hath ta ʦŏwanzāh, eleven fourteens (are) one hundred and fifty-four. This form can only be used with a numeral above ten (Gr.Gr. 86).
m. (sg. dat. ʦŏdisis), the obsequial rite performed by the daughter, or daughter's son, of the deceased, on the fourth day after death (see shrād).

m. a large earthenware vessel for milk or the like (El. tsȧu̇ḍ, as ab., and tsuḍ, m. a middle-sized water-vessel) (cf. dŏda-ʦᵒ, p. 190a, l. 45; dŏyĕn-ʦᵒ, p. 269b, l. 47; guras-ʦᵒ, p. 304b, l. 4; gĕv-ʦᵒ, p. 316b, l. 17; prīta-ʦᵒ, p. 769b, l. 33; tīla-ʦᵒ, p. 999a, l. 19) (Gr.Gr. 9, Śiv. 1837, K. 146, K.Pr. 73). Cf. ʦaḍ 2.
adj. e.g. fourfold, four times as much (cf. mŏnga-ʦᵒ, p. 578b, l. 18).
m. fourfoldness, the property of being fourfold.
f. train, retinue, suite, courtiers; the persons of a household, family. ʦö̃giji-munish m. a bullying head of a house, a house-despot.
f. a round piece of grass matting (cf. zisⁱ-ʦⁱ, s.v. zyusᵘ) (El. tsángij, K.Pr. 38, 254).
f. in rạtna-ʦᵘ lustration by waving a lamp (p. 849b, l. 32) (Śiv. 1093). Cf. ʦỗgᵘ.
adj. (f. ʦọ̆gᵘ̈ñᵘ̈), fourfold, consisting of four (strands of thread, widths or layers of cloth, or the like) (W. 105).
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦọ̆gᵃnôwᵃ), to make fourfold (e.g. to make a rope in four strands, to lay a cloth in four layers, and so on).

m. a lamp (consisting of a wick in oil) (cf. nyŏṭhas ʦᵒ dazun, p. 674a, l. 36) (El. tsong and sóng; Gr.Gr. 162; Gr.M.; W. 11, ʦoṇg; Rām. 1659; K. 921; K.Pr. 11, 67, 138). Cf. ʦö̃jᵘ̈, the dim. form of this word. ¶ ʦö̃gⁱ-gāsh m. the (dim) light of such a little lamp. -lᵃth f. (sg. dat. -lᵃti), a very dim little oil lamp (Gr.Gr. 162). -rĕh f. the flame of a lamp (K.Pr. 262, ʦāngi-rĕh).
or ʦuhaiṭh card. (pl. dat. ʦŏ(u)haiṭhan ) sixty-four (El. tshúheṭ; Gr.Gr. 78; K. 485-6). This word is often pronounced ʦŏ(u)höṭh , Gr. Gr. 78.
or ʦuhaiṭhyumᵘ ord. (f. ʦŏ(u)haiṭhimᵘ̈ ), sixty-fourth (Gr.Gr. 78). This word is often pronounced ʦŏ(u)höṭhyumᵘ , and so in the fem.
or ʦuᵒ ord. (f. ʦo(u)hatimᵘ̈ ), four-hundredth (Gr.Gr. 80). The corresponding card. is ʦōr hath (Gr.Gr. 80).
or ʦuᵒ adj. (f. ʦŏ(u)hatiñᵘ̈ ), costing four hundred (rupees, etc.), worth four hundred.
or (q.v.) ʦôshᵘ adj. (f. ʦöshᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 31) (of something edible or drinkable, etc.) astringent, acrid (Gr.Gr. 31); (as subst. m.) anything edible or drinkable which is astringent, an astringent.
f. a lamp (dim. form of ʦỗgᵘ, q.v.) (YZ. 44, 140).

m. sourness, acidity (El.; Gr.Gr. 30, 140); mutual animosity (e.g. occurring between friends or the like), opposition, hostility. Note that this word is not ʦŏcĕr, as we might expect; see ʦọ̆kᵘ (Gr.M.). --nērun -- m.inf. such mutual hostility to arise (between people).
adj. c.g. (of some whole) in four parts, divisions, or sections (cf. khã̄ṭh).
adj. (f. ʦŏkhrövᵘ̈), (of cloth) woven with four shuttles (see khrāv).
m. 'four leg', a certain disease accompanied by rheumatic pains in the waist and thighs, so that the sufferer has to walk on all fours, ? a kind of lumbago.
adj. (f. ʦŏkhūrᵘ̈), four-legged (usually of something inanimate).
f. a certain wild herb the leaves of which have a pleasant acid taste (? Indian sorrel).
f. sourness, acidity; angry sourness, angry moroseness (Gr.Gr. 128).
adj. (f. ʦŏköjᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, four times, occurring at four times (e.g. a meal).
adj. c.g. four-cornered, rectangular, square (Gr.M. ʦŏkūnjal). Cf. ʦŏkūnal.

conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦŏkyōv), to become sour, acid, acrid (K.Pr. 146); to be sour, acid (El., W. 113); (of someone usually mild in temper) to become angered (Gr.Gr. 128). ¶ In the sense of 'acidity', the causal of this verb is ʦọ̆kᵃrāwun, but in the sense of 'anger', its causal is ʦukᵃrāwun (Gr.Gr. 174). ¶ ʦŏkyō-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦŏkyē-müʦᵘ̈), become sour; become angered, indignant.
adj. c.g. four-cornered, quadrangular, (of, e.g. a stool, a board, or a piece of land). Cf. ʦŏkū̃jal.
m. a certain kind of sour cake. ʦŏkra-bākar f. noise of tumult, uproar, Babel.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦọ̆kᵃrôwᵃ), to make sour, acidify, cause to turn sour; to make (the face, etc.) angry, to show an angry face (as in scolding a child) (cf. buthᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 142a, l. 24) (in this sense ʦukᵃrāwun, q.v., is to be preferred, Gr.Gr. 174). Regarding the distinction between ʦọ̆kᵃrāwun and ʦukᵃrāwun, see ʦŏkun.
or ʦukᵃrun conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦọ̆(u)kᵒrᵒ ), to make sour, acidify, cause to turn sour; to make (the face, etc.) angry, to show an angry face, to frown, scowl, show moroseness (Gr.Gr. 7).

adj. (f. ʦŏ̈kᵘ̈, Gr.Gr. 36), sour, acid-tasting, tart (cf. kanda-ʦᵒ, p. 454a, l. 46) (El. tsauk; Gr.Gr. 30, 36, 140; Gr.M.; W. 21, 113, 115; K. 979; K.Pr. 30, 71, 146, 170). In derivatives from this word, k does not become c (cf. ʦŏkĕr, and Gr.Gr. as ab.) (Gr.M.). --bam-ʦū̃ṭhᵘ -- m. a sour kind of quince (see p. 109a, l. 27) (El. tsŏk bamtsúnṭ; W. 116 tso˙k-bamʦunt). --dönᵘ -- m. a sour kind of pomegranate (see p. 223a, l. 46) (El. tsŏk dáṅ). --nār hyuhᵘ -- adj. (f. --nār hishᵘ̈ --), like acid fire, so sour as to be uneatable or undrinkable, unbearably acid (cf. K.Pr. 137). ¶ ʦŏka-ala f.pl. a kind of sour pickle made of pieces of gourd, pumpkin pickle. -bata m. boiled rice which has fermented till it is sour. -crã̄ṭh adj. c.g. very tart, very sour. -hākh m. (sg. dat. -hākas), a kind of pickle made of vegetables boiled and mixed with the juice of sour grapes and condiments, and then fermented to acidity by exposure to the sun, pickled greens. -laḍur m. a certain vegetable found in the hills, used like rhubarb, and medicinally as an astringent (cf. laḍur) (El. tsokalaḍar; W. 115 tso˙kạ ladur; L. 72 tsok laddar, Polygonum polystachyum; tsoka ladar, 76). -pākh m. (sg. dat. -pākas), the pain of a gathering bruise. -pal m. (owing to fatness, heaviness of body, or the like) inability to rise (of an entire body, or of a particular limb); cf. ʦaka-pal, s.v. ʦaka. -poṭᵘ m. wet cloth which has been dipped in a preliminary dye before dyeing it crimson. -rath m. (sg. dat. -ratas), blood which has gone sour, i.e. bloody pus in a deep swelling. -ʦᵘ̈ñᵘ̈ f. a certain wild herb used in the preparation of a sour condiment. -ʦēr f. a sour species of apricot (El. tsoki-tsera, m.; W. 116 ʦokạ-ʦera). -ʦū̃ṭhᵘ m. a kind of apple (described by El. as sour and small) (W. 116). ¶ ʦŏ̈kᵘ̈ ṭö̃jᵘ̈ f. a sour kind of small pear (see ṭö̃jᵘ̈) (El. tsŏk ṭánj; W. 116 ʦo˙kạ-ṭānj).

m. (lit.) something circular; hence (esp.) the circular base or bottom of a receptacle, or its support, such as the ring under a cup, rose-bowl, or the like (cf. güḍᵘ̈wa-ʦᵘ̈, p. 278b, l. 21; khösⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 417b, l. 22; phŏhari-ʦᵒ, p. 687b, l. 1; tāla-ʦᵒ, p. 997b, l. 2 (El. tsuk). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. the base of a bowl, cooking vessel, or the like, to be broken, the bottom to be burnt (K.Pr. 216). --ʦalun -- m.inf. id. --yunᵘ -- m.inf. this part of a bowl, cooking-pot, or the like to become worn out. ¶ ʦȧkⁱ-gav m. (a jar, etc.), of which the lower part is gone (i.e. broken). -khôsᵘ m. a drinking cup with a ring base. -püṭᵘ̈ f. the rudder of a ship (Gr.M.). -wār m. a bowl with a ring base (cf. narakunᵘ ʦȧkⁱwār, p. 651a, l. 21). -vüṭᵘ̈ f. a little ball of thread on the spindle of a spinning-wheel. ¶ ʦaki bĕhun m.inf. (of a cup or the like) to sit, or remain steady, on its base; met. to lose one's employment. --phērun -- m.inf. to be cast down from its base (lit. and met.). --yunᵘ -- m.inf. to become worn out or decayed at the base.

m. a rectangular frame (large or small, of wood or other material) (cf. dŏsa-ʦᵒ, p. 252a, l. 39; görⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 298a, l. 46; kañi-ʦᵒ, p. 461b, l. 34; linga-ʦᵒ, p. 526b, l. 32; lari-ʦᵒ, p. 431b, l. 15; wŏbⁱ-ʦⁱ, s.v. wọ̆bᵘ). ¶ ʦökⁱ-ganḍ m. the fastening at the corners of the rectangular frame used for the foundation in building a house. -wār m. the rectangular framework used for the foundation in building a house.
adj. (f. ʦŏ̈kᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), soured; hence, harassed, afflicted (by distress, fatigue, or the like). Cf. ʦŏkun.
f. a fireplace, hearth (esp. a temporary arrangement for immediate use) (cf. kañi-ʦᵒ, p. 461b, l. 36) (El. a fireplace, Gr.Gr. 16).
m. a simple-natured child, a little simpleton.

m. a screen, cover (for concealment) (cf. bōma-ʦᵒ, p. 107a, l. 48; būta-ʦᵒ, p. 141b, l. 15; dᵃhi-ʦᵃ, p. 198b, l. 34); a kind of small fish (described as having a large head); a kind of insect (described as swarming in cold water in the hot season); used as a pejorative suffix in khanḍa-wāv-ʦᵒ, p. 403a, l. 37; yẹ̆cha-ʦᵒ, s.v. yĕch 1.

adj. (f. ʦüjᵘ̈) (1 p.p. of ʦalun, q.v.) used --˚ to indicate 'departing from', 'abandoning' as in dŏdⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 190b, l. 24; nȧmⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 636a, l. 17; ranga-ʦᵒ, p. 837a, l. 36; rötⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 847b, l. 46; wati-ʦᵒ, s.v. wath 1; yë̆ḍᵘ-ʦᵘ, s.v. yĕḍ; so wū̃ṭa-ʦᵒ, moving like a camel s.v. wū̃ṭh (El. tsaul, escaped).

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦọ̆mbᵘ), to pierce, bore (e.g. a pearl, the nose, or the lobe of the ear) (cf. kan ʦᵒ, p. 447b, l. 22; nas ʦŏmbüñᵘ̈, p. 654b, l. 8) (El., L.V. 75, Śiv. 1290); ʦọ̆mbᵘ-motᵘ perf. part. (f. ʦŏ̈mbᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈), bored, pierced, as ab.
m. having four faces, four-faced; (of a mountain or the like) four-peaked.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦọ̆mᵃrôwᵃ. This verb is the causal of ʦamun, q.v.) to reduce (the amount of some liquid, or of the juice in a green plant, or the like, by drying, evaporating, boiling down, or the like); to cause (some advice, or course of conduct) to be agreed to, assented to, adopted.
adj. (f. ʦümᵘ̈), made of skin, used --˚ as in sōra-ʦᵒ, made of pigskin, p. 931a, l. 25.
adj. (f. ʦümᵘ̈) (of some liquid) reduced to a small amount (by evaporation or the like), used --˚, as in aḍa-ʦᵒ, p. 12a, l. 31; ras-ʦᵒ, p. 841b, l. 33. See ʦamun, of which this word is 1 p.p.
or ʦunamath card. (pl. dat. ʦŏ(u)namatan ), ninety-four (Gr.Gr. 80).
card. even four, the four, all four (Gr.Gr. 85). See ʦōr.
m.N. of a celebrated wrestler in the service of Kams (Kaṁsa), who was killed by Krushn (Kṛṣṇa) (K 368, 440), in Skt. Cāṇūra.
