or ʦŏ̈nzᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. ʦŏnzi), a female slave, a (household) slave-girl, a housemaid (El. tsúns, tsŏns; Śiv. 437, 1237; Rām. 1038; K. 29, 637, 727, 913, 928, 979, 1132, 1150). ʦŏnza-küṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -kacĕ), the daughter of a slave-girl. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), the son of a slave-girl.
m. a male slave or male servant (esp. one employed as a messenger).
adj. c.g. bulky on all four sides, having the lower part bulky and heavy (so that he or it is too heavy to be lifted) (cf. pacĕl).
or ʦŏpĕndurᵘ m. confined in four directions; hence (of a man or beast) confined by the two hands, or fore legs, and the two feet, or hind legs, being seized by hand or bound by ropes.
m. a place where four ways meet, a cross-roads (Śiv. 1625).

or (q.v.) ʦŏwā-pôrᵘ adj. and adv. in all four directions, all round (u.w. vbs. of progression, searching, etc.) (Śiv. 641, 1529, 1641 (ʦapôr, m.c.); H. ii, 3, 5). ʦŏpörⁱ or (q.v.) ʦŏwā-pörⁱ adv. in all four directions, all round (Gr.Gr. 160; Śiv. 729, 764, 805, 810, 1183, 1460, 1515; H. xii, 21, 24); from all four directions, from all round (u.w. vbs. of going, coming, and the like) (Gr.Gr. 160, Śiv. 582).
(sic) m. the refuse of chewing, what is discarded or expelled from the mouth after chewing.

m. a bite (with the teeth, and on someone else) (cf. drᵃka-ʦᵃ, p. 243a, l. 3; gali-ʦᵒ, p. 283a, l. 50; guli-ʦᵒ, p. 284a, l. 32; hūnⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 337a, l. 19; kāwa-ʦᵒ, p. 495a, l. 37; wū̃ṭa-ʦᵒ, s.v. wūṭh) (El. tsúp, Gr.M.); when --˚, this word is sometimes used to mean a small amount of something eatable, as we should say 'a bite of something', see dŏda-ʦᵒ, p. 190a, l. 50; nūna-ʦᵒ, p. 641a, l. 29; the compound nāvi-ʦᵒ, p. 667a, l. 7, means 'a little worn-out uncomfortable boat'. --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take a bite, to bite (Gr.M.; H. x, 7). --kaḍun -- to take a (single) bite (out of something, e.g. from an apple, or similar fruit) (K.Pr. 238); to swallow in a single bite. ¶ ʦapis yunᵘ m.inf. to attack in order to bite (e.g. a dog attacking a person).
(f. ʦöpᵘ̈) 1 p.p. of ʦāpun, q.v., gnawed, chewed, masticated, used --˚, as in aḍa-ʦᵒ, p. 12a, l. 34; ôpᵘ-ʦôpᵘ, p. 40a, l. 18.
(El. ts˚) in tsor karun, to conquer (El.) and tsor karanwôlᵘ, a conqueror (El.). Cf. ʦorᵘ 2.

card. (f. ʦōra, Rām. 136; pl. dat. ʦōran or ʦŏn), four (Gr.Gr. 23, 76, 83 (declined), 160; Gr.M.; Śiv. 12, 200, 515, 800-1, 1594, 1642, 1695, 1712, 1768; Rām. 355, 568, 634, 740, 796; K. 185, 649, 827, 1018; H. iv, 4 (ʦŏn); vii, 5; viii, 5 (ʦŏn); x, 1, 2, 5 (ʦŏn), 6, 12 (ʦŏn); xii, 1, 23; YZ. 158 (ʦōn for ʦŏn)). --hath -- card. (pl. dat. ʦŏn hatan, Rām. 536), four hundred (Gr.Gr. 80). ¶ ʦŏn-hondᵘ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of, or belonging to, four. ʦŏn-kun nazar f. vision, or view, in (all) four (directions), seeing in every direction (K.Pr. 38, ʦun˚). ¶ ʦŏnaway or (q.v., s.v.) ʦŏshĕway card. emph. i.q. ʦōray bel., q.v. (Gr.Gr. 85, Śiv. 1716). ¶ ʦōri-laṭi adv. four times. -māsi adv. for four months, during four months (K. 43). --phiri -- adv. four times. -pörⁱ adv. in, or from, four directions only (Gr.Gr. 160). --rĕti -- adv. in four months, after four months (K. 832). --vizi -- adv. on four occasions, at four times. ¶ ʦōray or ʦōrạy card. emph. the four, all four, even four, only four (Gr.Gr. 83; Śiv. 803, 1529).
f. (sg. dat. ʦōrümᵘ̈), the fourth lunar day of a lunar fortnight (cf. shrūka-ʦᵒ, p. 892a, l. 39; sankaṭa-ʦᵒ, p. 922a, l. 48; tikⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 1049b, l. 12) (Rām. 1767, K. 676).
(El. tso˚) or ʦōraʦh (El. tsorats), f. a wedge (as for splitting wood) (El.; ? i.q. tōrüʦᵘ̈ and tōraʦh, qq.v.); a certain tool for cutting leather (H. xi, 14, ʦōraʦh).
m. an essence (El. tsorit, where only it has been noted. The spelling is doubtful). Cf. ʦārun.
m. a chessman, draughtsman, or piece in a similar game (Śiv. 280, 1644). ʦŏrȧngⁱ-püṭᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. -pacĕ), a chequered cloth or board used in gambling, a chess board, a draught board.

adj. (f. ʦŏrüñᵘ̈), one who has lost both his hands and both his feet, or who is so crippled (by disease or fracture) that he cannot use any of these four limbs. A compound of ʦōr and ronᵘ, qq.v. --gaʦhun -- m.inf. to become so maimed or crippled.
(El. ts˚), incorr. for sôruy, p. 931b, l. 24, q.v.

m. (sg. dat. ʦörinis), that which is picked off or out, i.e. the refuse picked off or out and thrown away in preparing vegetables, etc., for use (cf. gŏgᵃji-ʦᵃ, p. 279a, l. 30; muji-ʦᵒ, p. 558b, l. 13; phamba-ʦᵒ, p. 698b, l. 2; pōshĕ-ʦᵒ, p. 779a, l. 40; puyĕ-ʦᵒ, p. 813a, l. 27).

m. an oblation (such as grain, clarified butter, etc., offered to a deity or spirit and cast into the sacrificial fire) (cf. prīta-ʦᵒ, p. 769b, l. 36). ¶ ʦȧrⁱ-wörⁱ f. a kind of earthen vessel in which such oblations or similar food is cooked or contained (cf. pĕnḍa-ʦᵒ-wᵒ, p. 738b, l. 50; prīta-ʦᵒ-wᵒ, p. 759b, l. 37); meton. the actual oblation (as ab.) (cf. shrāda-ʦᵒ-wᵒ, p. 891a, l. 38); a certain dish consisting of rice cooked with ghī and salt. ʦȧrⁱ-wāri-pholⁱ m. a dish of rice cooked with turmeric, offered on a Saturday or on a Tuesday, or on some other occasion, to Bhūtas (see būth 1), Bhairavas (see börav) or the like. ʦȧrⁱ-wāri-lë˘jⁱ f. the pot in which this dish of rice, ghī, and salt is cooked.

m. the opening on the top of a cooking-stove, on which the cooking-vessels are placed (cf. okᵘ-ʦᵘ, p. 19b, l. 3; dāna-ʦᵒ, p. 221a, l. 40; potᵘ-ʦᵘ, p. 788b, l. 3); met. a similar-shaped rimmed depression on the body (cf. ȧchⁱ-ʦörⁱ, p. 8b, l. 48; ȧshⁱ-ʦörⁱ, p. 48a, l. 3; mĕnga-ʦörⁱ, p. 578a, l. 43). ¶ ʦāri-wôlᵘ m. one who cooks very little food, i.e. a man who (owing to the smallness of his family) cooks only small meals. ¶ ʦörⁱ-pākh m. (sg. dat. -pākas), (of meat or the like) thorough cooking (till tender).

adj. (f. ʦürᵘ̈ 1) and adv., copious, abundant, very much, too much, excessive (cf. phala-ʦᵒ, p. 692b, l. 15) (El. tsaur, much, more, tsŏr, adv. very, and tsur, abundant, superfluous; Gr.Gr. 9, 138; Gr.M.; W. 21, 22, 96; Rām. 775, 1137, 1617, 1632, 1701; K. 7, 12, 68, 133, 179, 190, 250, 263, 341, 362, 364, 527, 532, 572, 579, 583, 704, 722, 741, 747, 798, 919, 1052, 1080, 1087, 1102, 1142, 1168; K.Pr. 94, 217-8, 245, 250). ¶ ʦạrⁱ-pöṭhin adv. in great abundance, abundantly, copiously, excessively. ¶ ʦoruy adj. and adv., very much, very, exceedingly (El. tsŏruí; Rām. 420 fem.).
(f. ʦörᵘ̈), 1 p.p. of ʦārun, q.v., gathered, collected, selected; used --˚, as in aḍa-ʦᵒ, p. 12a, l. 38.
or ʦusatath card. (pl. dat. ʦŏ(u)satatan ), seventy-four (Gr.Gr. 79).
adj. c.g. (of cloth) woven with four hundred threads.
card. even all four (Gr.Gr. 83, 85; Śiv. 1521). See ʦōr.

or (q.v.) ʦôhᵘ adj. (f. ʦöshᵘ̈), (of something edible or drinkable) acrid, astringent (cf. aḍa-ʦᵒ, p. 12a, l. 40) (Gr.Gr. 138); (as subst. m.) anything edible or drinkable which is astringent, an astringent.
m. long continued conversation (esp. when scandal or criticism of others) (cf. katha-ʦᵒ, p. 486b, l. 19); slandering, tale-bearing, backbiting.

f. (sg. dat. ʦŏti, Gr.Gr. 70), the anus, podex (obsc.) (cf. khar-ʦᵒ, p. 407a, l. 39) (El. tsot, m.; tsut, f.; Gr.Gr. 70, 146); the pudendum (usually, but not always, muliebre) (obsc.) (cf. khar-ʦᵒ, as ab.; kŏ-ʦŏth, p. 494b, l. 16) (El. f.). Cf. ʦŏ̈ʦᵘ̈. ¶ ʦŏta-büṭhᵘ̈ f. the side of the pudendum muliebre (obsc.). -bachĕ f.pl. the thighs of an unchaste woman. -ʦūr m. a secret adulterer, a secret profligate. -ʦūrᵘ̈ f. the (legal) offence, or crime, of such secret unchastity. -ʦŏth f. (sg. dat. -ʦŏti), undisguised frequent acts of unchastity. ¶ ʦŏtⁱ-nonⁱ adj. (f. -nüñᵘ̈), (owing to poverty or to shamelessness) a man whose anus is uncovered (f. a woman whose garments are so torn that her private parts are exposed).
f. the condition of being a pupil (see ʦāṭh).
or ʦuṭopᵘ adj. (f. -ʦŏ(u)ṭüpᵘ̈ ), having four different reasons, capable of being done, or disposed of, in four different ways, having four different meanings, and so on (see ṭopᵘ 3).
adj. (f. ʦŏtrökiñᵘ̈), measuring, or weighing, four trakhs (see the preceding) (Gr.Gr. 147).
ʦŏtrôkᵘ, or ʦutrokᵘ adj. (f. ʦŏtrücᵘ̈, ʦŏtröcᵘ̈, or ʦutrücᵘ̈), of four trakhs, each equivalent to six Kāshmīrī seers (see trakh), (a vessel) holding four trakhs, measuring four trakhs (Gr.Gr. 147).

m. (f. ʦŏtᵘ̈jᵘ̈, q.v. which is used in a special sense), a sodomite (cf. ʦŏth) (Gr.Gr. 146); used as an abusive adj. (K.Pr. 224). In compounds this word also means a fornicator, adulterer, or, generally, one utterly vile. ¶ ʦŏtal-bāpār m. the general (vile) conduct of a sodomite; conduct like that of such a person. -damölⁱ f. a vile fellow who stamps on the ground (see damölⁱ), such a one who without reason raises an uproar. -pöthᵃr m. conduct like that of a sodomite, general vile conduct.
adj. (f. ʦŏtūjᵘ̈), weighing four (Indian) tōlās of half an ounce each.
adj. (f. ʦŏtürᵘ̈), clever, skilful, sharp-witted (K.Pr. 193). Cf. ʦaturᵘ 1.

f. (sg. dat. ʦŏcĕ), bread, a cake, a small flat loaf (cf. atha-ʦᵒ, p. 64a, l. 42; bĕbi-ʦᵒ, p. 77b, l. 27; kö̆mᵘ̈-ʦŏcĕ, p. 443b, l. 20; kạnᵃka-ʦᵃ, p. 457b, l. 39; krǖla-ʦᵒ, p. 470b, l. 44; kȧshⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 480a, l. 38; kŏṭhⁱ-ʦŏcĕ, p. 489a, l. 27; makāyi-ʦᵒ, p. 563b, l. 9; mᵃtra-ʦᵃ, p. 605b, ll. 26 ff.; pana-ʦᵒ, p. 734b, l. 3; pōsh-ʦᵒ, p. 778b, l. 8; pithⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 818b, l. 12; tīla-ʦŏcĕ, p. 999a, l. 17; tŏmᵃla-ʦᵃ, p. 1006b, l. 32; tọ̆ndūra-ʦᵒ, p. 1010a, l. 19; wushki-ʦᵒ, s.v. wushka) (El. tsŏṭ, ʦuṭ; Gr.Gr. 74, 162, 163; Gr.M.; L. 458; W. 113; H. v, 7, 8; K.Pr. 77, 103, 224). -mö̆nḍᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. ʦŏcĕ-mŏnjĕ), cakes and the like, bread etcetera, used --˚. ¶ ʦŏcĕ-bạrᵃg m. a thin cake, a pancake. -chal f. a piece of cake (generally about half) (Gr.Gr. 162); cf. -tilim, bel. -han f. a little loaf (W. 113). -kā̃durᵘ m. a bread-baker, one who bakes and sells bread. -katurᵘ m. a bread-sherd, a large sherd or earthenware platter, on which loaves are baked. -mọ̆nḍᵘ m. a thick fat kind of loaf or cake. -mŏnjĕ f.pl. globular shaped cakes cooked with ghī, etc. -mǖ̃thᵃr f. cakes presented to his schoolmaster and his school-fellows, on the occasion of a boy completing his learning of the alphabet (see mö̃thᵃr 1). -tilim f. a small piece of a loaf (less even than a quarter; cf. -chal, ab.) (Gr.Gr. 163). -tövᵘ̈ f. an iron griddle or the like for baking bread. -worᵘ m. a kind of small-sized loaf or cake (K.Pr. 220). -wȧrⁱ-har f. 'a quarrel about little cakes', i.e. a quarrel among mean-hearted, beggarly, or low people about some petty matter. -wȧrⁱ-ʦūr m. 'a thief of little cakes', i.e. a mean, beggarly, or low fellow.

m. a kind of Hindū oblation or offering scattered into the air before the house door or on to the roof of the house, intended for the Yōginīs, or female attendants on Shiv (Śiva), as they travel in the air. It is supposed to ward off, or carry away, misfortune. It consists mainly of rice with pieces of sheep- or goat-liver or -heart, and is generally offered on Tuesday or Saturday. --khitra-pāl -- m. this offering united with a similar offering to certain Bhairavas, see khitra-pāl and börav. ¶ ʦȧṭⁱ-khāv m. an eater of these offerings, a man who habitually eats them. ¶ ʦaṭi-kani lagun m.inf. for the relief of another from calamity, to offer oneself as an oblation.

1 p.p. of ʦaṭun, q.v. (f. ʦüṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. ʦacĕ), cut, cut off, used --˚ (cf. aḍa-ʦᵒ, p. 12a, l. 42; ösa-ʦᵒ, p. 47a, l. 6; atha-ʦᵒ, p. 64a, l. 46; dȧlⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 212a, l. 4; gulⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 284a, l. 23; khōra-ʦᵒ, p. 410b, l. 17; kala-ʦᵒ, p. 435b, l. 16; kana-ʦᵒ, p. 448a, l. 36, Gr.Gr. 75; lȧṭⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 535b, l. 46; murⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 588b, l. 43; māwȧlⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 611b, l. 30; nala-ʦᵒ, p. 632a, l. 34; nȧrⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 649a, l. 28; narĕ-ʦᵒ, p. 650a, l. 14; nas-ʦᵒ, p. 654b, l. 13; nyŏṭha-ʦᵒ, p. 674a, l. 35; pakha-ʦᵒ, p. 725a, l. 35; panja-ʦᵒ, p. 740b, l. 25; wuṭha-ʦᵒ, s.v. wuṭh 1; yĕba-ʦüṭᵘ̈, s.v. yĕba; zangi-ʦᵒ, s.v. zang 1; zĕvi-ʦᵒ, s.v. zĕv) (El. tsuṭ); (of a loan) taken, borrowed; ʦoṭᵘ wôṭᵘ m. the action of taking a loan (to provide funds for a feast or the like). ¶ El. gives tsauṭ, torn, to which, by confusion with ʦhọ̆ṭᵘ, q.v. he also gives the meanings 'little, short'.

or ʦŏtᵃ̇jᵃ̇ f. (f. of ʦŏtul, but in a special sense), a wanton woman, an incontinent slut (cf. ʦūra-ʦᵒ, p. 1081a, l. 17) (Gr.Gr. 146). ʦŏtᵃjĕ-khāb m. 'a wanton's dream'; hence, a statement unworthy of belief.

in the following:-- ʦŏwā-pôrᵘ or (q.v.) ʦŏpôrᵘ adv. in all four directions, all round (Śiv. 515, 1567; Rām. 1255, 1767). -pöri or (q.v.) ʦŏpörⁱ adv. (Gr.Gr. 160) in all four directions, all round (Gr.M.; Śiv. 626, 1052, 1504, 1891); from all four directions, from all round (Rām. 1679).
or ʦuwahurᵘ, or ᵒwuhurᵒ adj. (f. ʦŏ(u)warishᵘ̈ ), born, or produced, four years ago, four years old; existing for four years, lasting four years.
or ʦuwanzāh card. (pl. dat. ʦŏ(u)wanzāhan ), fifty-four (Gr.Gr. 78, Śiv. 328).
or ʦuwotᵘ m. a place where four ways meet, a cross-roads.
or ʦuwôṭᵘ adj. (f. ʦŏ(ʦu)wöṭᵘ̈ , sg. dat. ʦŏ(ʦu)wācĕ ), having four joints, joined in four places.
card. (pl. dat. ʦŏwuhan), twenty-four (El. tsawuh, tsŏwuh; Gr.Gr. 77, 83).

f. tale-bearing, backbiting, slandering, slander. --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to slander, backbite (esp. in order to sow discord). ¶ ʦŏyĕ-gorᵘ (f. -gürᵘ̈), one in the habit of backbiting or sowing dissention by slander. -wôlᵘ m. (f. -wājĕñ), a backbiter, slanderer.
he entered for thee, ʦöy, they entered for thee, see aʦun (Gr.Gr. 241).
m. a certain area of land, the area that requires four trakhs (see trakh 2), of six Kāshmīrī seers each, of paddy-seed for sowing.
or ʦu-zongᵘ m. (f. -ʦŏ(u)zünjᵘ̈  or -jⁱ), four-legged, a quadruped (as distinct from a biped) (K.Pr. 61).

conj. 3 (ʦŏʦyōv, Gr.Gr. 236) (of a merchant's business or the like) to become contracted, to fall off, become insufficient for livelihood. ʦŏʦan-wād m. (in a business, as ab., in the hands of partners) a falling off (of profits, etc.) owing to want of unanimity among the partners.

f. adultery, fornication, esp. rape (cf. ʦŏth) (El. tsóts, m. adultery, with tsóts karun, to commit adultery). --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to have sexual intercourse with a woman, esp. to rape. --dāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. (causal of --diñᵘ̈, ab.) to cause or induce a man to have sexual intercourse with a woman, esp. to induce him to commit rape. -dyār m.pl. a harlot's fee; a harlot's earnings from her profession. -madun m. (sg. dat. -madanas), a profligate man, one addicted to venery, a lecherous fellow. -madüñᵘ̈ f a profligate woman, one who is incontinently licentious.

m.pl. palpitations, quivering, writhing, in the following:-- --barȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to suffer palpitations; hence, to be in great anguish (mental or physical). --dinⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to writhe in anguish.

m. N. of a place in Kashmīr, where there is a shrine of the saint Nūru'd-dīn (L. 250, 293, Chhrar Sharif, see chrār sharīf, p. 165b, l. 43; K.Pr. 220). Here pretty painted portable braziers, or kāngrīs (see kā̃gᵘ̈rᵘ̈), which are often given as presents, are made. ʦrāra-kã̄gᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. a brazier made in this place.
m. name of the place which holds the shrine of Kashmīr's greatest saint, Nūr Dīn (L. 250, 293; not mentioned in RT.Tr. or by El.).

m. (sg. dat. ʦraṭas), the noise caused by falling from a height on to the ground or on to water, smash, splash (cf. atha-ʦᵒ, p. 64a, l. 40; nāwa-ʦᵒ, p. 666b, l. 33, the splash of a boat on the water; hence, sea-sickness) (L.V. 1); cf. ʦröṭⁱ and ʦrŏṭh. ʦraṭa bĕhun m.inf. to be hopelessly without employment (of one whose business, official position, possessions, or the like has been so destroyed that it is impossible to set it up again).
m. (cf. ʦēr 1) delay, procrastination, excessive time (occupied in the performance of something) in the following:-- --lagun -- m.inf. delay (in the accomplishment of some work) to occur.

m. i.q. ʦēṭh, q.v. pounding, crushing, reducing to powder, in the following:-- ʦrēṭh dyunᵘ m.inf. to exhaust a person (by continually pressing him on to complete some urgent work) (cf. ʦēṭh dyunᵘ, p. 1086b, l. 9).
m. exultation, delight, skipping for joy, etc. Cf. ʦĕngun 2.
in ʦringa-wād m. distribution little by little, using little by little in giving away.
(often written ʦröj) f. a leather-worker's wife (see ʦrôlᵘ); the wife of a city police-spy or a female doing this work (see ʦrôlᵘ) (Gr.Gr. 36).

m. (f. ʦröjᵘ̈, q.v.) a leather-worker, carrier, shoemaker (of untouchable caste) (Gr.M.); a kind of police-spy or detective (there being usually one in charge of each quarter of a town. A woman (ʦröjᵘ̈) may sometimes occupy the post) (Gr.Gr. 36; H. v, 7; K.Pr. 107, 221, 224); a jailor (YZ. 370, 381). According to K.Pr. 144, the word is the name of a Moslem sect, which has the choice of three employments. They can become, jailors, or bootmakers, or beggars. Moslems outside the sect do not eat with them. For their origin, see K.Pr. 98. ʦrölⁱ-zāphal m. a nutmeg brought in former times to a house by a friend or relation, as a harbinger of good luck, on the occasion of a festival (such as that on the birth of a son).
m. a certain measure of grain, flour, or the like, half a handful, half as much as can be contained in the hollow of the hand (i.e. the palm stretched out and hollowed) (El. chrong).
m. the noise of falling from a height, esp. the noise caused by the buttocks or thighs coming into contact with the ground in a fall on a slippery or muddy road, flop, plop. Cf. ʦröṭⁱ and ʦraṭh.
m. the condition of being wheel-shaped; anything wheel-shaped; a potter's wheel (El. tsruṭ m.). Cf. ʦrüṭᵘ̈.
f. the noise caused by one thing falling repeatedly on a similar thing, esp. the noise produced in sexual intercourse. Cf. ʦraṭh, ʦrŏṭh.
in ʦrṻṭh ʦalun m.inf. the wits to become clouded (e.g. owing to the weakness of old age).

f. (sg. dat. ʦracĕ), a potter's wheel (El. tsrauṭ f.); any circular disc, large or small, a round cake, a tabloid (cf. hanga-ʦᵒ, p. 338b, l. 47; lācha-ʦᵒ, p. 507a, l. 30; mīli-ʦᵒ, p. 565b, l. 51; nāga-ʦᵒ, p. 623b, l. 49; nöhⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 625b, l. 23; tŏndūra-ʦᵒ, p. 1010a, l. 18); cf. ʦroṭᵘ. ʦrüṭᵘ̈ gaʦhüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to become a disc, to be squashed flat by a blow from above, to be struck by a blow from above and so destroyed.

f. the hair on the top of the head, a single lock on the crown of the head; a crest, plume, diadem (Śiv. 740, 976, 1035, 1538, 1574, all in the compound ʦandra-ʦᵒ, he who has the moon for his diadem. See ʦạndᵃr).
m. a place in a tree or the like where it spreads out into four branches (united at the base).
adj. (f. ʦukhörᵘ̈), weighing four khārs (see khār 3); able to contain four khārs; suitable for carrying, or able to carry, four khārs.
adj. c.g. one who fasts for four days, one who has eaten nothing for four days.
m. a sulky or angry-natured man, with a frowning forehead, a scowler.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦukᵃrôwᵃ), to make angry, to anger (see ʦŏkun) (Gr.Gr. 174); to make (the face) angry (as in scolding a child) (see the preceding).

m. the light burning pain caused (e.g.) by contact with a spark; the mark caused by such a burn; the burning sensation caused by eating something pungent; loving sympathy. ʦukⁱ lagȧnⁱ m. pl. inf. little burns, as ab., to occur (to someone); burning in the mouth from eating something pungent to occur.
m. a group of four, a four. Cf. ʦākh.

or ʦumᵘ̈ṭhᵘ̈ or ʦumüṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. ʦumᵃṭi or ʦumᵃṭhi), a nip, a pinch (cf. kapar-ʦᵒ, p. 463b, l. 46; phĕkⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 720b, l. 48); a kind of red ant. --hë̆ñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to take a nip, to draw a person's attention by pinching him.
in tāzak-ʦun, q.v.; in ʦun-kun (K.Pr. 38), see ʦōr.

m. powder (cf. khanḍa-ʦᵒ, p. 403a, l. 2) (El. tsún, broken filings) (Gr.Gr. 20); filings (El. tsúṅ, i.e. ʦū̃). ¶ ʦṻna-mŏṭh karüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to make (something) a fistful of powder, to crush to powder (and so destroy). -trŏmba m. N. of a certain food-grain (? a variety of buckwheat) (cf. trŏmba).

f. (sg. dat. ʦanjĕ), a blow, stroke, hit (cf. atha-ʦᵒ, p. 64a, l. 22; cö̃ṭⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 177a, l. 44; dŏbiñĕ-ʦᵒ, p. 184a, l. 21; kala-ʦᵒ, p. 435b, l. 8; kañi-ʦᵒ, p. 461b, l. 38; lōri-ʦᵒ, p. 531a, l. 17; macilⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 548a, l. 35; nala-ʦᵒ, p. 632a, l. 33; phĕkⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 720b, l. 50; para-ʦᵒ, p. 750a, l. 49; shĕmshēri-hünzᵘ̈ ʦᵒ, p. 884a, l. 37; wŏḍi-ʦᵒ, s.v. wŏḍ) (Gr.M.; Rām. 969; K.Pr. 62); (of wind) a sudden blow, gust (cf. wāwa-ʦᵒ, s.v. wāv 1) (Gr.M.); met. a sudden, violent, unbearable calamity (cf. nāra-ʦᵒ, p. 648b, l. 11; tāli-ʦᵒ, p. 997b, l. 33; tāpa-ʦᵒ, p. 1015a, l. 26; tapāli-ʦᵒ, p. 1016a, l. 20). --lāyüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to strike a blow (e.g. with a sword) (on, dat.) (H. iii, 5, 6). --yiñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. a blow to come, a blow, or hurt from a blow, to be received (K.Pr. 261). ¶ ʦanjĕ ʦanjĕ karun to enfeeble (a person, esp. a child) by repeated blows, or by blows given by a number of people.
m. the figure 4, the written sign for four.
(El. ts˚), see ʦᵃnunᵃ and incorr. for ʦhunun.
f. silence, inability to retort (in an argument).
adj. (f. ʦupüjᵘ̈), weighing four pals of about two ounces each (cf. pal 2).
m. having four leaves, four-leaved (of a plant or the like).
adj. (f. ʦupūrᵘ̈, sg. dat. ʦupōrĕ), (of a house) four-storied; (of a box or the like) four-shelved.
m. powder, fine fragments. In ʦaṭa-ʦṻr, s.v. ʦaṭh.

m. a thief, burglar (cf. canda-ʦᵒ, p. 172b, l. 45; dŏda-thañi-ʦᵒ, p. 190a, l. 39; dŏda-ʦᵒ, p. 190b, l. 2; dŏhᵃ̇lᵃ̇-ʦᵃ̇, p. 200b, l. 42; gar-ʦᵒ, p. 296a, l. 23; gurⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 299a, l. 16; hāra-ʦᵒ, p. 344b, l. 47; khŏḍa-ʦᵒ, p. 392b, l. 40; kāmi-ʦᵒ, p. 444a, l. 20; mandĕñ-ʦᵒ, p. 577b, l. 48; nȧmⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 636a, l. 29; par-ʦᵒ, p. 751a, l. 25; potᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 788b, l. 5; süñᵘ̈-ʦᵘ̈, p. 916a, l. 23; ṭhūla-ʦᵒ, p. 976b, l. 12; ʦhŏci-ʦᵒ, p. 1062b, l. 5; ʦacĕ- wȧrⁱ-ʦūr, s.v. ʦŏ̈tᵘ̈) (El. tsúré; Gr.Gr. 18, 28, 50, 51; Gr.M.; W. ʦur, 7, 11, 18; L.V. 43, 101; Śiv. 279, 328, 1067, 1311, 1321, 1381; Rām. 1426; K. 148; H. iii, 3; viii, 9; x, 12; xii, 1; YZ. 180, 257, 281; K.Pr. 66, 74, 77, 125, 168, 176, 221 ff., 236); met. one who secretly does prohibited actions (cf. gᵃsa-ʦᵃ, p. 307a, l. 32; ʦŏta-ʦᵒ, s.v. ʦŏth); (facetiously, or quasi-facetiously) a person, an individual, in phrases such as nömⁱ ʦᵒ, p. 637a, l. 40; any person or thing that causes violent damage or destruction (cf. buñulⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 115b, l. 47; lönⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 525b, l. 33; nāra-ʦᵒ, p. 648b, l. 12) (H. vii, 12); met. a deadly wasting disease (cf. ạndᵃ̇rᵃ̇-ʦᵃ̇, p. 32b, l. 22; rata-ʦᵒ, p. 846b, l. 30); (in cultivating crops) weeding and clearing out the roots (cf. ala-ʦᵒ, p. 22b, l. 38). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to weed and clean the roots of a crop. --ʦaṭulᵘ -- m. thief-swindler, a man who is a thief and also a swindler, a thoroughly bad lot. --zörᵘ̈ -- f. thieving and gambling, a life of profligacy and criminality. ¶ ʦūra-bāy f. a thief's wife. -buzⁱ or -buzy adj. c.g. dependent on theft, i.e. liable to theft, liable to be stolen. -gūdᵘ m. the vulva of a thief, the pudendum of an unchaste woman who is a thief, or who works in conspiracy with thieves; hence, meton. such a woman (in this meaning f.). -hāʦh f. (sg. dat. -hāʦi), a false charge of theft; cf. ʦūri-hᵒ, s.v. ʦūrᵘ̈. -khŏḍ m. the cavity at the back of the throat, behind the uvula. -khoḍᵘ m. 'a thief vulva', the pudendum of a woman who is secretly unchaste. -kọ̆kᵘ̈rᵘ̈ or -kükᵘ̈rᵘ̈ f. huddling up the limbs (in cold weather or the like) (cf. kakürᵘ̈ or kükᵘ̈rᵘ̈). -kal f. looking longingly (at something, as if one wished to steal it). -kŏnḍal f. (sg. dat. -kŏnḍüjᵘ̈ or -kŏnḍali) 'a thief fire-bowl', a woman who habitually acts like a thief, a thoroughly dishonest woman. -kāphürᵘ̈ f. secret intrigue or plotting (esp. among thieves in order to rob someone); cf. köphir, of which kāphürᵘ̈ is the abs. noun. -kaṭh m. (sg. dat. -kaṭas), a thief's son (an abusive term) (Gr.Gr. 132); met. any badly-conducted or naughty boy. -nagörᵘ̈ f. a woman who associates with thieves (usually unchaste, shameless, and dishonest). -pūtᵘ m. a thief's son (Gr.Gr. 131); a term of affection used playfully by elders to a baby (Gr.Gr. 131). -pav m. the artful practices of a thief, a thief's dexterity. -syuwᵘ m. 'domesticated by a thief', an apprentice thief, a boy adopted by a thief and taught the profession. -ṭŏjĕ f.pl. or -ṭŏlⁱ m.pl. 'thief's eyeballs', bloodshot eyes (K.Pr. 159, -ṭŏlⁱ); cf. ṭŏjĕ and ṭŏlⁱ.-ʦⁱñⁱ f. 'a thief-coal', a woman who habitually conducts herself like a thief, a trollop, trull. -ʦūr f. thief upon thief, the appearance of a number of thieves (in some locality, due to bad government). -ʦŏtᵃ̇jᵃ̇ or -ʦŏtᵘ̈jᵘ̈ f. a loose woman who is at the same time a thief.
f. theft, thieving, the practice of thieving.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦṻranôwᵘ), to cause (a man) to have violent sexual intercourse, etc. (with oneself or with another woman).
adj. (as subst., f. ʦūrladiñ), suffering from a deadly wasting disease (cf. rata-ʦᵒ, p. 846b, l. 34).
(El.) in lānĕ-ʦūrū, Xanthium strumarium, p. 525b, l. 13, i.q. ʦyūrᵘ, q.v.
conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦṻrᵘ), to have violent sexual connexion, etc., with a woman, esp. to rape a virgin.

or (q.v.) ʦūrⁱ or ʦūrī f. theft (cf. dŏhᵃ̇lᵃ̇-ʦᵃ̇, p. 200b, l. 44; khŏḍa-ʦᵒ, p. 392b, l. 12; potᵘ ʦᵒ gaʦhüñᵘ̈, p. 788b, l. 8) (El. tsúri; Gr.M.; Śiv. 852, 1393; K. 148-51; H. xii, 1); the secret doing of forbidden actions (cf. nȧmⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 636a, l. 34; ʦŏta-ʦᵒ, p. 1086b, l. 42). --karüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to steal (El. tsúrik˚; H. xii, 1; K.Pr. 207, 237). --karanāvünᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause theft to be committed (K.Pr. 149). ¶ ʦūri adv. by theft (Rām. 683, 1162); stealthily, secretly, furtively (El.; Rām. 411, 659, 760, 861, 1143i, 1196, 1206, 1292, 1415, 1781-2; K. 158, 389, 642; YZ. 422). --bĕhun -- m.inf. 'to sit furtively', to remain hidden, keep concealed (from fear of another or the like). -hāʦh f. (sg. dat. -hāʦi), a false accusation of theft (YZ. 422); cf. ʦūra-hᵒ, p. 1080b, l. 32). --hyonᵘ -- m.inf. to take by theft, to steal (something) (K. 736). --nyunᵘ -- m.inf. to carry off by theft, to steal (El. tsúri ninyi, Gr.M., YZ. 416). -- pöṭhⁱ -- or --pöṭhin -- adv. stealthily, secretly, furtively (H. iii, 1 (pöṭhin); xii, 6, 7, 17 (pöṭhⁱ)). --rōzun -- m.inf. to remain hidden, to abide in safe concealment. --thawun -- m.inf. to put away in hiding, to hide (something). --ʦūri -- adv. stealthily, secretly, furtively (all the time).

(for 1, see ʦorᵘ 2) f. a handful, or wisp, of grass, straw, or the like, used --˚ (cf. dĕlⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 268, l. 3); a wisp as ab. fashioned for some use (cf. bumbⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 107b, l. 48; nakha-ʦᵒ, p. 628b, l. 33; cf. ʦar 3); a number of articles (such as plates) piled one over the other (cf. ṭökⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 991a, l. 41).

f. clapping the hands together (in sport, in keeping time to music, etc.) (cf. dŏyĕ atha ʦürᵘ̈ wazüñᵘ̈, to clap with both hands, s.v. zᵃh) (K.Pr. 60). ¶ ʦari-mŏ̈nḍᵘ̈ tulüñᵘ̈ f.inf. to clap the hands in derision, publicly to ridicule (a person) (cf. mö̆ndᵘ̈ 2) (cf. K. 222, 232). -popᵘ m. a kind of game consisting in clapping the hands.

f. a hen-sparrow (cf. ranga-ʦᵒ, p. 837a, l. 44; sŏnⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 917b, l. 26; ʦaka-ʦᵒ, p. 1066b, l. 41; ʦama-ʦᵒ, p. 1072a, l. 37) (El. tsar; Gr.M.; W. 18, ʦar; L. 282, tsari; Rām. 694; K.Pr. 31, 217-8, 240). A cock sparrow is könṭur, q.v. ¶ ʦari-ôlᵘ m. a sparrow's nest. -bacĕ  m. a young sparrow, a sparrow-chick. -dŏd m. 'sparrow's milk', i.e. something very difficult or impossible to obtain (like our 'pigeon's milk'). -laʦhȧjⁱ or -laʦhüjᵘ̈ f. 'sparrow's broom', N. of a certain medicinal seed, commonly found growing on house roofs, and used as a remedy for indigestion and as an antiperiodic (L. 76). -nam m. a sparrow's claw; met. any similar shaped small object. -puribⁱ m. 'the second husband of a sparrow's widow', a scarecrow for frightening small birds from ripened crops. -ṭhūl m. a sparrow's egg. -tᵃl m. a kind of mulberry (described as small and of unpleasant taste). -tŏmul  m. (sg. dat. -tŏmalas), 'sparrow's rice', the N. of a certain creeping plant, used medicinally.
or ʦūrī, f. i.q. ʦūrᵘ̈, q.v., in the following:-- canda-ʦūrⁱ, pocket-picking, p. 172b, l. 47; nȧmⁱ-ʦūrī, stealing with the nails (in gambling), p. 636a, l. 33.
adj. c.g. made up of four parts, sections, branches, compartments, or the like (cf. p. 878a, l. 30) (K.Pr. 229, of a walnut).
adj. (f. ʦusīrᵘ̈, sg. dat. ʦusērĕ), weighing four seers (of about two pounds each).
adj. c.g. one who habitually breaks wind (see ʦũ̄̈ṭh) (Gr.Gr. 134).
f. a woman whose advice is not worthy of being attended to, a woman who is not worth listening to (whose words are worth nothing but contempt, cf. ʦũ̄̈ṭh).
adj. c.g. emitting four crashes or bangs (not all at once, but one by one) (e.g. a gun fired four times in succession, see ṭās).

also written ʦũ̄̈ṭhᵘ̈ f. (sg. dat. ʦũ̄̈ṭi), breaking wind, a fart (cf. khar-ʦᵒ, p. 407a, l. 42) (El. tsenṭh; Gr.Gr. 126, 134); met. boasting without valid reason (cf. ḍĕka-ʦᵒ, p. 204b, l. 35); met. an unpleasant obnoxious person (cf. dĕwa-ʦᵒ, p. 261a, l. 20). --trāvüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to let a fart, to fart. --trövith thopᵘ -- m. 'a plug after doing this', after telling a scandal to wish to conceal it. ¶ ʦũ̄̈ṭa-dĕv m. a shameless fellow, who on a single occasion breaks wind several times. -gurᵘ adj. (f. -gurᵘ̈), one who habitually ever and anon breaks wind. -pônᵘ m. an anus that frequently allows farts to issue. -paparāy f. an uninterrupted series of farts (cf. paparāray).

or ʦū̃ṭh (incorrectly written ʦū̃ṭᵘ, p. 568a, l. 49) m. an apple (El. see tsúnṭ, for a list of varieties) (cf. ambȧrⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 27b, l. 6; bam-ʦᵒ, p. 109a, l. 24 and p. 510a, l. 25; kuli-pĕṭhukᵘ ʦᵒ, p. 439a, l. 13; mālamuhⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 568a, l. 49; ʦŏka-ʦᵒ, p. 1067a, l. 38) (El. tsúnṭ; Gr.Gr. 56, 163; W. ʦunṭ, 21, 115-6; L. tsunt, Pyrus malus, 73, 79, 348, 458; L.V. 92; YZ. 376, 535, ʦûṁṭh; K.Pr. 36, 78, 138, 214, 220). ¶ ʦū̃ṭhⁱ-bēra m. 'the apple-hedge', a small ridge-shelf, or niche, for receiving small light articles, made with the plaster, in plastering the inner wall of a house; cf. -tākhucᵘ, bel. -hacĕ f.pl. dried apple-chips. -kŏl f. N. of a canal connecting the Ḍal lake with the river Vĕth or Jehlam close to Śrīnagar. Its ancient Skt. name was Mahāsarit. See RT. Tr. II, 416. -kulᵘ m. an apple tree (El. tsunṭ-kul, W. id. 115). -rēmph f. (sg. dat. -rēmpi), a small apple for its kind, an apple smaller than the average of its kind (Gr.Gr. 163). -tākhucᵘ m. i.q. -bēra, ab., q.v. -wạthᵃr m. an apple leaf.
conj. 1 (this verb is impersonal, 1 p.p. ʦũ̄̈ṭᵘ; f.sg. dat. ʦũ̄̈cĕ; 2 p.p. ʦũ̄̈cyōv), to break wind with noise, to fart (Gr.Gr. 126).

f. mutual quarrelling (esp. between two persons, and instigated by a third) (Gr.Gr. 119, 192); cf. ʦuvüñᵘ̈. --diñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. to cause a quarrel to blaze up, to inflame a quarrel (i.e. when there is some hidden seed of anger between two persons, a third person to stir it up into bursting forth). --lagüñᵘ̈ -- f.inf. such a quarrel to burst forth (on some excuse or exciting cause).

(sometimes written ʦuviñ; Gr.Gr. 119, 192) conj. 1 (in the tense formed from the past participle, and in these tense only, this verb is impersonal and is only in the feminine gender, the subject being in the case of the agent. Thus ʦuvᵘ̈th, it was quarrelled by thee, i.e. thou quarrelledst. In the plural, it indicates many quarrels, as in ʦuvĕth, thou quarrelledst many times. See Gr.Gr. 188, 214, 220, 233. 1 p.p. f. ʦuvᵘ̈), to quarrel, esp. of a verbal quarrel or mutual abuse (cf. har ʦᵒ, p. 343b, l. 17) (Gr.Gr. as ab. and 117, 119, 192; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 37). ʦuvᵘ̈-müʦᵘ̈ perf. part. f. a quarrel been made (between so-and-so). ʦuvith diñᵘ̈ f.inf. to instigate a quarrel. ¶ [Although technically impersonal, the grammatical subject of this verb is really some fem. word, such as har 4, meaning a quarrel, which is understood. Thus ʦuvᵘ̈th, ab., is literally '(a quarrel) was quarrelled by thee'.]
adj. (f. ʦuwörᵘ̈), (of a necklace or the like) having four coverings, wrapped round with four similar coverings.
m. (sg. dat. ʦuwanas), mutual quarrelling, a quarrel. Cf. ʦuviñ and ʦuvüñᵘ̈.
m. the immature root of the first young leaf sprouts of a plant such as a radish which when mature has globular roots.
m. (sg. dat. ʦĕlis), a certain fish; a certain insect, or worm, found in mountain lakes.
adj. (f. ʦë˘mᵘ̈), become short, shrunken, shortened (e.g. by disease, or drying up). Cf. ʦyopᵘ.

adj. (f. ʦë˘pᵘ̈), short, too short (e.g. of a limb compared with its fellow); cf. ʦyomᵘ. ʦĕpi nūn pyonᵘ m.inf. 'salt to fall on such a deformed limb', to become much distressed or dejected (in searching for some lost valuable).

or (q.v.) ʦyuwᵘ m. (sg. dat. ʦihĕs), a certain period of time, a period of 24 seconds, the sixtieth part of a ghaṛī (see gürᵘ̈ 1), and said to be 60 twinklings of an eye (see nimēsh) (K.Pr. 176). ʦihĕn-hondᵘ adj. gen. (f. -hünzᵘ̈), of this short space of time, lasting only an instant; (of a sudden death) a death in an instant; (of one at the point of death or the like) having only an instant to live; (of something nearly complete) about to be finished in an instant.

m. (sg. dat. ʦīnis, obl. ʦēni), a pillar, or wall acting as a pillar (kañi-ʦᵒ, p. 461b, l. 40; shēra-ʦᵒ, p. 889b, l. 3; sērĕ-ʦᵒ, p. 930a, l. 36) (El. tsyun; Gr.Gr. 21, 26, 59 (declined); Gr.M.; W. 19 ʦion; Śiv. 749). ʦēnyukᵘ gen. adj. (f. ʦēnicᵘ̈), of, belonging to, or on, a pillar or such a wall.

m. (sg. dat. ʦīris, abl. ʦēri), a certain shrub with spiny burrs (El. tsúr, Xanthium strumarium); a medicinal plaster prepared from its oil and used as a remedy for rheumatism; cf. cīrⁱ 3, and lānĕ-ʦūrū, p. 525b, l. 13. ʦīrⁱ-konḍⁱ m. the spiny burr of this plant (it adheres to the clothes of passers by).

adj. (1 p.p. of ʦēṭun, q.v.; sg. dat. ʦīṭis, abl. ʦēṭi; f. ʦīṭᵘ̈, sg. dat. ʦēcĕ), anything pounded, esp. a condiment, sauce, chutnee, or pickle made by pounding something edible (cf. aḍa-ʦᵒ, p. 12a, l. 46; handi-ʦᵒ, p. 337b, l. 9; muji-ʦᵒ, p. 558b, l. 16; nadȧrⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 623a, l. 49; rōṭa-ʦᵒ, p. 845a, ll. 12, 14; tāra- tizⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 1018a, l. 38; tari-ʦᵒ, p. 1020b, l. 44) (Gr.Gr. 19).
m. (sg. dat. ʦivis), a certain very short space of time, i.q. ʦyuhᵘ, q.v.
m. suction, sucking (esp. of a juicy fruit or food) (cf. atha-ʦᵃh, p. 63b, l. 27) (Gr.Gr. 124). --dyunᵘ -- m.inf. to suck (a juicy fruit, or the like), (of a baby) to suck (the breast).

pron. of the second person, thou (El. tsih, tsuh; Gr.Gr. 6, 87; Gr.M.). ¶ Sing. nom. ʦᵃh (Gr.Gr. 87; L.V. 7, 13, 44, etc.; Siv. 3, 157, 159, 162, etc.; Rām. 14, 22, 27, 29, 30, 35, 37, etc.; K. 106, 144, 868, 1107; H. ii, 11; iii, 2, 9, etc.); ¶ Acc.-Dat. ʦĕ (Gr.Gr. 87; L.V. 13, 44, 56, 72; Śiv. 449, 585, 708, 780, etc.; Rām. 191, 326, 493, 656, etc.; K. 86-7, 360, 552, 722, etc.; H. v, 10; vi, 11, etc.); (in old Ksh. there is also tŏyĕ, L.V. 13); ¶ Ag. ʦĕ (Gr.Gr. 87; L.V. 64; Śiv. 87, 360, 410, 594, etc.; Rām. 154, 195, 214, 256, 576-7, 744, etc.; H. i. 12; ii, 11; xii, 20; YZ. 59); ¶ Gen. cyônᵘ (Gr.Gr. 12, 56, 87; L.V. 72; Śiv. 153, 156, 168, 197, etc.; Rām. 567, 662, 771, 782, 791, 810, 845, 850; K. 30, 38, 86, 137, 356, etc.; H. v, 9; vi, 3; viii, 3, 11, etc.); ¶ Plur. nom. tŏhⁱ (Gr.Gr. 27, 87; L.V. 91; Śiv. 393, 683, 693, 883; Rām. 270, 476, 514, 528, etc.; H. viii, 3, 5, 13; xii, 1; YZ. 198); ¶ Acc.-Dat. tŏhĕ (Gr.Gr. 26, 87; Śiv. 881; K. 54, 63, 89, 274, 473, 1140; H. x, 5, 12); ¶ Ag. tŏhĕ (Gr.Gr. 87; Śiv. 82, 1249, 1447; Rām. 126, 1474; H. x, 12); ¶ Gen. tuhondᵘ (Gr.Gr.; Śiv. 838, 883, 1249, 1295; Rām. 270, 1299; K. 54, 274, 460; H. ii, 2; xii, 15). ¶ Of the above forms, cyônᵘ and tuhondᵘ are really possessive pronouns, and are dealt with separately, s.vv., qq.v. ¶ As in the case of other personal pronouns, this pron. has a series of pronominal suffixes used with verbs. The suff. of the sing. nom. is kh, of the acc. and ag. is th, and of the dat. y. If the verb is in the third person, the suff. of the sing. acc. is y, not th. For all cases of the plur. the suffix is wa. These are added directly to forms ending in vowels, but, when added directly to forms ending in a consonant, the suffixes of the singular take a as a junction vowel. Examples are, in order, poku-kh, thou wentest; kara-th, I shall make thee; kari-y, he will make thee; koru-th, made by thee; karān chu-y he makes for thee; korᵘ-wa, made by you; korᵘ-m-akh, thou wast made by me; karān chus-ath, I make thee; karān chus-ay, I make for thee; karān chus-wa, I make you. The suffix kh when followed by another pronominal suffix beginning with a vowel becomes h as in karān chu-h-as (for chu-kh-as), thou makest for him. For all these, see Gr.Gr. 184 ff. In villages v is sometimes substituted for wa, as khĕyĕ-v, she was eaten by you (H. x, 12), and in karĕm-av, I made them for you (H. x, 6). ¶ This pronoun is peculiar in that whenever it is the subject of, or is governed by, a finite verb, even if fully expressed, it must always also be represented by a suffix. It should, however, be understood that, in regard to the suffixes of the nominative case, the future indicative, the present conditional, the past conditional, and the present imperative, being already supplied with terminations indicating the person of the subject, never take any additional pronominal suffixes of the nominative. In all other circumstances the use of the suffixes of this pronoun, and of this pronoun alone, is compulsory, not optional. If, however, the pronoun is not directly governed by the verb, but is governed by a postposition, the use of the suffix is not compulsory. For examples, see Gr.M. s.v. ʦᵃh. ¶ tŏhⁱ c.g. pl. you (pl.) (as ab.), sometimes used respectfully for the singular, as in K. 933. ¶ ʦᵃy, emph. form of ʦᵃh, even thou, thou alone (El. tsĕí; L.V. 42, 109; Śiv. 24, 42, 120, 168, 201, etc.; Rām. 1030, 1061, 1123-4; K. 384, 466, 560, 792, 1110; H. i, 10; xii, 15). ¶ ʦĕy, or (K. 469) ʦĕyⁱ emph. form of ʦĕ, even thee (Rām. 196, 423, 830, 1038, etc.; K. 466, 756, 1138, 1173; YZ. 57).
f. (sg. dat. ʦᵃhüñᵃ), sucking, suction; sipping, tasting.
n.ag. (f. ʦᵃhavüñᵃ), one who sucks (cf. mȧchⁱ ʦᵒ, p. 547a, l. 30); one who sips, tastes.

conj. 1 (1 p.p. ʦᵒhᵒ, f. ʦᵘ̈shᵘ̈; 2 p.p. ʦᵃshyōv, Gr.Gr. 225), to suck up, suck (cf. mȧchⁱ ʦᵃhüñᵃ, p. 547a, l. 26) (El. tsihun; Gr.Gr. 124, 210, 225; Gr.M.; K.Pr. 234); to sip, taste (El. tsáhun, tsuhun). ¶ ʦᵃhan-wāri adv. by gradual tastes, by a series of tiny sips or bites (u.w. vbs. of eating) (cf. wôrᵘ 9). -vēri adv. for tasting, merely for tasting (not for eating) (used ˚--). ¶ ʦᵃhith nyunᵘ m.inf. to suck dry, to dry up (something juicy, by sucking, or by leaving in the sun, or by cooking, or the like).
m. one who is in the habit of eating the savoury relish named ʦᵃkh (q.v.).
m.pl. alarm (caused by apprehension of the recurrence of former injury); cf. ʦᵃkȧṭᵃ. --ʦānȧnⁱ -- m. pl. inf. to cause such alarm (esp. in threatening or scolding a child).
f. (sg. dat. ʦᵃkaṭüñᵃ), (from cold or the like) shrinking, withering, shrivelling.
f. (sg. dat. ʦᵃkaṭi), shrinking, withering, shrivelling (e.g. a limb from cold, or a flower, or leaf).
conj. 3 (2 p.p. ʦᵃkaṭyōv), to shrink, shrivel, wither (e.g. from cold). ʦᵃkaṭyō-motᵃ perf. part. (f. ʦᵃkaṭyē-müʦᵃ), shrivelled, shrunken, as ab.
m.pl. in ʦᵃkȧṭᵃ ʦānȧnⁱ m.pl.inf. to intimidate (a child or the like, by scolding, punishment, or the like, so that he shrinks from another interview). Cf. ʦᵃkar, and the next.
m. (sg. dat. ʦᵃkas), the act of setting on fire, kindling, setting alight; N. of a certain greasy uncooked sweet relish eaten with food. ʦᵃka-khāv m. one who is in the habit of eating this relish.

adj. (f. ʦᵃmarüvᵃ), made of iron, iron (see ʦᵃmurᵃ) (Rām. 631; H. xii, 16, 17, ʦamruwᵘ; K.Pr. 190). ʦᵃmaruwᵃ kara ʦāpun m. to chew peas of iron; hence, met. to be occupied in some very difficult work (cf. H. as ab.). In H. xii, the word is explained by the pandit as 'leathern', but the meaning 'made of iron' is certainly the correct one. So also in K.Pr. 190. In the modern language it is confused with ʦam, leather.
m. iron (this is a Burushaskī word, and in various forms is current over the whole Dard country. In Ksh. it is reported as an old word, now seldom used).

the internal malleolus (El. tsanun); the ankle (El. tsunun); a peach (the fruit) (cf. bŏṭa-ʦᵒ, p. 138b, l. 38) (El. tsúnú, tsunun, Amygdalus Persica; W. 116 ʦunun; L. 348 tsunnan, 462, tsannan). ʦᵃnȧnᵃ-ö̃ṭᵃ f. a peach-stone. -wạthᵃr m. a peach leaf.

m. a stain, blot, stigma, disrepute (due to some sin, blame, or the like). --gaʦhun -- m.inf. a stigma to arise (in the course of any procedure, between two persons or actions mutually connected or the like). ʦᵃr-ʦᵃr m. repeated interruptions interfering with another's work. ¶ ʦᵃra-gāḍ f. N. of a certain game played with cowries.
adj. c.g. stained or marked (in regard to some particular quality), in disgrace or bad repute (for something). Cf. ʦᵃr.
f. (sg. dat. ʦᵃrüñᵃ), a hole, chink (cf. bar-ʦᵒ, p. 116b, ll. 30, 32; mᵃtra-ʦᵃ, p. 605b, l. 24) (El. tsiran, K.Pr. 251). Cf. ʦar 4.
m. a tearing blow, a wrench (to a limb or the like) (cf. zanga-ʦᵃs, s.v. zang 1; K. 1026, zangi-ʦ˚, a wrench given (in wrestling) to a leg). Cf. ʦᵃsta and tᵃs.
adj. c.g. wrenched off, torn off (Rām. 603). Cf. ʦᵃs.

f. a lump of charcoal, charcoal (when a single lump is not referred to, the pl. ʦᵃñĕ (see below) is generally used in this sense) (cf. boṭhⁱ-ʦⁱ, p. 140b, l. 44; lasa-ʦᵒ, p. 532b, l. 35; mal-ʦᵒ, p. 564a, l. 35; ʦŏka-ʦᵒ, p. 1067a, l. 30; ʦūra-ʦᵒ, s.v. ʦūr 1; yĕngar-ʦᵒ, s.v. yĕngur) (Gr.Gr. 164, Gr.M.); a black mark made by charcoal (cf. ḍĕka-ʦᵒ, p. 204b, l. 30); anything small and black and hard (like a little bit of charcoal) (cf. rŏnga-ʦᵒ, p. 837b, l. 47); self-conceit, self-complacency, vanity (cf. ḍĕka-ʦᵒ, p. 204b, l. 32; gāṭa-ʦᵒ, p. 310b, l. 2). ¶ ʦᵃñĕ, f.pl. charcoals, a collection of charcoal (e.g. for fuel) (cf. khāra-ʦᵒ, p. 407b, l. 48; kāṭha-ʦᵒ, p. 487b, l. 19; küʦhᵘ̈-ʦᵘ̈, p. 493b, l. 22; pana-ʦᵒ, p. 735a, l. 32; payĕn-ʦᵒ, p. 817b, l. 4; tᵃla-ʦᵃ, p. 995a, l. 39; wan-ʦᵒ, s.v. wan 1) (El. tsinya m., tsinyin; Rām. 621, 1081, 1495). -āshnāv = چھنہ آشنا m. 'a charcoal relation', i.e. a mere acquaintance, one only slightly known, or a distant cousin (K.Pr. 159, 'people from the villages often pay a visit to the city during the winter season bringing with them charcoal for sale. They sell their load, put up for a night in some person's house, and are off again the following morning'). -bôrᵘ m. a load of charcoal (carried in leather bags from the forests to the towns). --gaʦhañĕ -- f. pl. inf. to become charcoals, to be burnt to charcoal; met. anguish, mental pain (due to someone else's evil conduct) to be experienced. -hāgurᵘ m. (sg. dat. -hāgaras), a certain bird (said to resemble a crow, and to be edible). -hanā f. a single piece of charcoal. -khikhur or -khikhurᵘ m. a kind of withy or straw basket, in which small charcoal is brought from the forest into the towns for sale. --karañĕ --  f. pl. inf. to turn into charcoal; to destroy; to cause mental anguish (by injuring another by evil conduct). -mŏnḍurᵘ m. a large block of charcoal. -mŏndürᵘ̈ f. a lump of coarse charcoal. -müṭᵘ̈ f. The sound represented by this letter does not occur in Kāshmīrī, although the character is often met with in borrowed Persian words, written in the Perso-Arabic character. Except by Persian scholars, the character is usually pronounced ph, or, when initial, sometimes as p. When Persian words occurring in Kāshmīrī are written in the Śāradā or Roman character the letter ف is represented by ph. Hence, for all words commencing with f ف, see under ph.

This vowel (a-mātrā), which also occurs in Pᵃshtō and other languages of the North-West Frontier, is pronounced as an extremely short a. It never begins a word. In the Nāgarī and Śāradā characters it is not represented at all, the consonants between which it occurs being compounded into one character. Thus, the word ʦᵃh, thou, is written, literatim ʦ-h, as if with no vowel. In the printed text of the Kaśmīraśabdâmṛta it is represented by virāma, thus. In the Persian character it is represented by zabar, thus چھَہ. ¶ This vowel occurs under two sets of circumstances. In the first it is an original vowel, inherent in the word in which it occurs, and in such cases it modifies the vowel of the preceding syllable, if any, and if that vowel is liable to modification. Thus, a followed by ᵃ becomes ạ, ā becomes ö, ē becomes ī, ō becomes ū, and so on. Examples will be found under the respective vowels. In the second set of circumstances ᵃ is not original, but is merely a helping vowel inserted between the members of an original compound consonant to make the pronunciation more easy (what Sanskrit grammarians call svarabhakti). In such a case a preceding vowel is not modified. Thus the Sanskrit word śastra, iron, becomes in Kāshmīrī, شِس٘تَر, shĕstᵃr, and the Arabic word جَل٘د, jald, active, becomes jald, or jalᵃd, quickly. As in the latter case, the insertion of this ᵃ is often optional and depends upon the personal equation of the speaker. ¶ Every final a in the language is pronounced very shortly, as if it were ᵃ, but this distinction is not marked in writing, nor is the preceding vowel affected by it.

This vowel bears the same relation to ᵃ that ȧ does to a (see ȧ). When ᵃ is followed by ⁱ it becomes ᵃ̇. Like the ᵃ it is omitted in the Nāgarī character. In the Persian character it is represented by zabar. Thus, from, ان٘دَرَ, ạndᵃra, from inside, we have, ان٘دَرِ, ạndᵃ̇rᵃ̇. It is sounded like an extremely short ȧ.

This mātrā-vowel bears the same relation to ᵃ that ĕ does to a. That is to say, when ᵃ follows ñ it becomes ᵉ̆. Thus, بَنیَراوُن or بنیِراوُن, bạñᵉ̆rāwun, to cause to be. It is pronounced as a very short e, like the second e in 'ceremony'.

This bears the same relation to ᵃ that o does to a. When ᵃ is followed by ᵘ it becomes ᵒ. Like ᵃ it is omitted in the Nāgarī character. In the Persian character it is represented by pēsh. Thus, from the root dᵃn, shake out, we have the past participle, دُن, dᵒnᵒ.

This is the u-mātrā vowel. At the end of a syllable it is silent, but when followed by a consonant in the same syllable it becomes an ordinary u. Thus, korᵘ, pronounced kor; korᵘ-thas, pronounced korthas, and korᵘn, pronounced korun. Under most circumstances it affects the pronunciation of the vowel of the preceding syllable, e.g. changing ᵃ to ᵒ, a to o, ā to ô, ĕ to yo, i to yu, ī to yū, and ō to ū. A preceding u or ū, however, it leaves unchanged. It is represented, when final, in Nāgarī by, and is usually omitted in the Persian character. Thus, کُر, korᵘ, done; بُڈ, boḍᵘ, great. When medial, it is represented as an ordinary u. Thus, کُرُن, korun, he did.

This is the ü-mātrā vowel. At the end of a syllable, like ᵘ, it is silent; and when followed by a consonant in the same syllable, it is pronounced as a very short German ü. Thus, kürᵘ̈, pronounced kür; kürᵘ̈-thas, pronounced kürthas; kürᵘ̈n, pronounced kürᵘ̈n, with the second syllable short; and gāṭᵘ̈jᵘ̈, pronounced gāṭᵘ̈j. Under most circumstances, when original, it affects the pronunciation of the vowel of the preceding syllable, e.g. changing ᵃ to ᵘ̈, a to ü, ā to ö, ĕ to ë˘, ē to ī, ō to ū. A preceding i, ī, u, or ū, however, it leaves unchanged. When ᵃ is changed to ᵘ̈, under the influence of a following ᵘ̈, this new, secondary, ᵘ̈ does not, in its turn, affect a preceding vowel. Thus, gāṭᵃjᵃ becomes gāṭᵘ̈jᵘ̈, not göṭᵘ̈jᵘ̈. It is represented in Nāgarī by, and, when final, is generally omitted in the Persian character. When not final it is sometimes represented by zabar and sometimes by zēr. Thus, گر, kürᵘ̈; یَڈ, büḍᵘ, کرَن or گرن, kürᵘ̈n.

This is the i-mātrā of the Kāshmīrī alphabet. It has the sound of a very slightly pronounced i, and it also affects the pronunciation of the vowels of the preceding syllable, as explained under the head of each vowel. It is represented in Nāgarī by, and in the Persian character by zēr. Thus, میآنِ, myönⁱ, my (masc. pl.).

or ⁱlözⁱ f. a secondary suffix used to form nouns of condition from substantives or adjectives. Thus, motᵘ, a madman, mȧtⁱlöz, the condition of a madman; brēṭh, ignorant, brīṭhⁱlöz, ignorance (Gr.Gr. 143).
